negative_highlights: FY2007 net loss of $87.5 million ($5.42 per share) including $78.3 million of impairments and a $28.7 million valuation allowance ($1.78 per share)
Auditors included going-concern language; about $60 million of debt maturities remain for the balance of 2008
Homebuilding gross margin ex-impairments fell 260 bps to 9.3%, homebuilding revenue declined 3%, and a $4.8 million Atlanta loan is in foreclosure
positive_highlights: Total debt reduced by more than $124 million, from over $295 million to about $171 million at year-end, and about $161 million post-restructuring
Senior unsecured notes restructured at a 50% discount, generating about $15 million of reportable income expected in Q1 2008
Operating cash flow of $116.5 million and a $13.9 million federal/state tax refund received; SG&A targeted down at least $10 million in 2008
summary: Comstock reported FY2007 net loss of $87.5 million ($5.42 per share) on total revenue of $266.2 million, up 8% but only because bulk/land sales rose 476% to $33.4 million while homebuilding revenue fell 3% to $232.8 million. Impairments totaled $78.3 million and a $28.7 million deferred-tax valuation allowance added $1.78 per share to the loss; Q4 revenue was $53.2 million and homebuilding gross margin ex-impairments compressed 260 bps to 9.3%. The company cut total debt from over $295 million to about $171 million (about $161 million after the note restructuring) received a $13.9 million tax refund, and had Q4 revenue of $53.2 million. Auditors included going-concern doubt, about $60 million of 2008 maturities remain, and management guided to at least $10 million of SG&A reduction in 2008 with an Atlanta loan ($4.8 million) in foreclosure.

negative_highlights: Portfolio yields compressed in both segments, with life down to 3.89% from 4.17% and home service down to 4.47% from 4.65%
Realized gains fell versus 2010 and 2009, alongside a $70,000 American Airlines bond impairment and a $561,000 real estate write-down
Taiwan growth was flat and management called the Asian market 'disappointing'
positive_highlights: Premium growth continued, with life segment premiums of $118.2 million representing 88% of 2011 growth and home service adding $43.2 million
General expenses declined to $26.9 million from $27.1 million in 2010 and $28.4 million in 2009
Death claims fell year over year (down 6.9% in life and 7.6% in home service), and persistency improved
summary: Citizens reported 2011 life segment premiums of $118.2 million (88% of premium growth) and home service premiums of $43.2 million (12%), but the call did not disclose total revenue, EPS, or net income figures. Portfolio yields declined across both segments (life 3.89% vs 4.17%; home service 4.47% vs 4.65%), driving a $0.8 million reserve increase and roughly $1 million of additional fourth-quarter DAC amortization from lower long-term yield assumptions. General expenses fell to $26.9 million from $27.1 million in 2010, and the company recorded a $70,000 American Airlines bond impairment plus a $561,000 real estate write-down; no formal 2012 guidance was issued, with management describing a cautiously optimistic outlook on rates and continued acquisition interest.

negative_highlights: Life pretax income declined due to Q4 2011 reserve assumption changes (higher reserves from low rates) not present in the prior-year period
Average portfolio yield fell to 3.76% from 3.94% a year ago, with $92M of bond calls in the quarter
New business growth lagged in Latin America, and U.S. Life book continues to run off modestly
positive_highlights: Net investment income increased 3.8% despite the low-rate environment
Home Service segment provided the majority of profitability, helped by a ~$500K IBNR reserve release and lower property claims
Life segment premium growth of 4.4%, with endowment products representing 80% of first-year premiums
summary: Citizens reported a 'consistent, predictable' Q1 2012 with no surprises; Life segment accounted for ~75% of premiums with 4.4% premium growth, but pretax income was lower due to Q4 2011 reserve assumption changes (higher reserves from low rates) and a mix shift toward renewals. Home Service contributed $10.9M in premiums (1% growth) but the majority of profitability, aided by a ~$500K IBNR reserve release and lower property claims. Net investment income rose 3.8% but the average portfolio yield fell to 3.76% from 3.94% a year ago amid $92M of bond calls; management guided to no new rate increases and expects rates to stay low through 2012-2013.

negative_highlights: The Life segment reported a loss for both the 3 and 6 months, driven primarily by reserve increases
Fixed-maturity calls of roughly $220M in the first half forced reinvestment at lower yields, compressing the portfolio yield
AA-rated holdings fell from 65.1% at year-end to 51.1%, shifting into A and BBB categories; Home Service death claims rose to $3.9M from $3.0M
positive_highlights: Premiums rose 5.5% for the quarter and 5.8% for the 6 months, with renewal premium up $1.9M and $4.3M respectively over 2011
Book value increased 2.9%, driven by unrealized gains on available-for-sale securities, with no other-than-temporary impairments identified
Persistency remained exceptionally strong, and ordinary surrenders held at 0.05% for the past several years
summary: Citizens reported a loss in its Life segment for both the 3 and 6 months ended June 30, 2012, driven primarily by reserve increases tied to improved persistency, lower interest rates, and the endowment-heavy product mix; premiums still rose 5.5% (3mo) and 5.8% (6mo) on renewal growth of $1.9M and $4.3M. Home Service premiums contributed about $11M, aided by a late-2011 book acquisition, though death claims rose to $3.9M from $3.0M for the quarter. Investment income grew on a larger asset base, but roughly $220M of fixed-maturity calls in the 6 months forced reinvestment at compressed yields, and the AA-rated share of the portfolio fell from 65.1% to 51.1%. No explicit guidance figures were given; management called the quarter a 'coincidental convergence' of events and expects results to return to a more conventional track.

negative_highlights: Hurricane Isaac drove expected Home Service losses of about $750,000, with 634 claims submitted and 227 declined or closed by quarter-end
Investment yield declined to 3.74% at quarter-end from 3.92% at December 31, 2011, with new money rate at 3.1%
Management said year-to-date profitability was slightly lagging 2011 despite sales growth
positive_highlights: International life segment direct premiums earned grew 7.9% in the quarter and 7.2% for nine months versus 2011
Realized gain of approximately $6 million on sale of a previously impaired equity mutual fund, with no other-than-temporary impairments in the quarter
Home Service premiums rose about 10% to roughly $11.1 million, bucking industry contraction, with commission expense down 1.5% for the quarter and 2.4% year-to-date
summary: Citizens reported Q3 2012 direct premiums earned growth of 7.9% (7.2% for nine months) in the international life segment, and Home Service premiums of about $11.1 million. Hurricane Isaac produced roughly $750,000 in expected Home Service losses, with about 500 claims anticipated at an average cost near $1,500. Net investment yield fell to 3.74% from 3.92% at year-end 2011, partly offset by a roughly $6 million realized gain on an equity mutual fund sale. No explicit EPS, net income, or formal guidance figures were provided, and management described year-to-date profitability as slightly behind 2011.

negative_highlights: Life segment investment yield fell to 3.61% from 3.89% in 2011 as low rates pressure reserves and tax assumptions
First-year premium growth decelerated to 6.1% in 2012 from 6.6% in 2011
A $1.3 million realized loss was recorded in Q4 from impairment of the Ameren Energy security, which fell to a 72.50 price
positive_highlights: General expenses decreased 7.5% in 2012 versus 2011 on reduced actuarial, accounting and employee benefit costs
First-year premiums rose 6.1% for full-year 2012, driven by the international life segment
Goodwill was confirmed unimpaired at the 12-31 review, with no valuation issues
summary: Citizens reported full-year 2012 first-year premium growth of 6.1%, decelerating from 6.6% in 2011, with the life segment producing $126 million of premiums and the Home Service segment $44 million (1-2% growth). The life segment investment yield fell to 3.61% from 3.89%, death claims rose 5.3% to $7.1 million, and a $1.3 million impairment on Ameren Energy was recorded in Q4. Management gave no quantitative 2013 guidance, citing low rates and a Venezuela transition unknown, while noting general expenses fell 7.5% and reiterating interest in acquisitions. Rick Riley acknowledged earnings growth is 'not what we would like' and 'modest at best.'

negative_highlights: A $50 million inventory write-off was recorded for RETAVASE due to stability issues and FDA Complete Response Letter.
An $11.5 million impairment charge was taken on LIXAR (lixivaptan) development costs.
The relaunch timeline for RETAVASE has been pushed back to 2015, eliminating expected upfront payments and milestones.
positive_highlights: Net product sales grew 15% year-over-year to $116.1 million in 2012, driven by strong performance in CARDENE and ZYFLO.
CUROSURF achieved a 52% market share in Q4 2012 and grew 2% despite a slowing market decline.
The company successfully integrated the EKR transaction within 90 days and secured a 15-year agreement extension with Chiesi for CUROSURF.
summary: Net product revenues grew 15% year-over-year to $116.1 million for the full year and 92% quarter-over-quarter to $34.9 million in Q4 2012. However, the company recorded significant charges including a $50 million write-off of RETAVASE inventory due to FDA stability issues and an $11.5 million impairment on LIXAR, resulting in a GAAP net loss of $11.9 million for the year. Management raised concerns about the timeline for relaunching RETAVASE to 2015 following a Complete Response Letter from the FDA.

negative_highlights: Kiwi product sales fell 41% to $9.2 million as both volumes and average note price declined
Apple-related product sales declined 8% to $22.9 million with volumes down 15%
CFO said fruit juice beverage gross margin may decline further and declined to provide Q1 2013 guidance
positive_highlights: Revenue rose 22% to $102.4 million and operating income rose 33% to $25.2 million
Concentrated pear juice sales more than doubled, up 116% to $28.9 million
Fruit juice beverage sales increased 29% to $27.1 million on reduced prices to gain market share
summary: SkyPeople Fruit Juice reported fiscal 2012 revenue of $102.4 million, up 22% from $84 million, with operating income up 33% to $25.2 million and net income attributable to shareholders of $18.2 million versus $13.2 million in 2011. Growth was driven by a 116% increase in concentrated pear juice sales and a 29% increase in fruit juice beverages, offsetting a 41% decline in kiwi products and an 8% decline in apple products. Management issued no explicit 2013 revenue or EPS guidance, said it would not project Q1 2013 results, and indicated fruit juice beverage gross margin could decline further. The Board is evaluating large new investment projects and has not decided on any dividend or buyback, with only $14-15 million of its $30 million cash available for such projects after working capital needs.

negative_highlights: Home service property claims rose to $551K from $364K on Louisiana weather activity
Life death claims were lower by $751K versus Q1 2012, a favorable variance unlikely to repeat
Domestic life premiums declined on aging books and the A&H premium assumption change
positive_highlights: Net investment income rose 10% on portfolio growth and improved yield
Portfolio yield improved to 3.86% from 3.76% year-over-year and 3.81% at year-end
Venezuela direct premium reached $6.4M, overtaking Colombia's $6M as the top Latin American market
summary: Citizens reported Q1 2013 with life segment premiums of $30.1M (73.6% of total), net investment income up 10%, and portfolio yield of 3.86% versus 3.76% a year earlier and 3.81% at year-end. Home service premiums were ~$10.8M with property claims of $551K versus $364K, driven by Louisiana weather, and a $500K IBNR release flattered prior-year comparison. No explicit EPS or formal guidance was provided; management described results as consistent with year-end trends and cited the low-rate environment as a continuing headwind.

negative_highlights: Swing to a $8.1 million net loss from $2.3 million net income in the prior-year quarter
Deferred revenue recognition declined $19.1 million year over year, and TC-1734/3480 revenue recognition has now concluded
No public detail on AstraZeneca's development plans for licensed alpha4 beta2 compounds beyond early pre-clinical candidates
positive_highlights: Revenue of $3.5 million exceeded the prior $2.4 million guidance assumption
R&D expense fell $9.5 million year over year due to conclusion of a Phase 3 program and 2012 workforce reductions
Recruitment completed in the Phase 2b TC-5619 schizophrenia study, with top-line results expected toward end of 2013
summary: Targacept reported a Q1 2013 net loss of $8.1 million versus net income of $2.3 million in Q1 2012, driven by a $19.1 million decrease in deferred revenue recognition partly offset by a $9.5 million reduction in R&D expense. Revenue came in at $3.5 million, above the prior $2.4 million guidance assumption, because the restructuring of the AstraZeneca arrangement accelerated recognition of remaining deferred revenue tied to TC-1734. Management reaffirmed prior expense guidance of $48-54 million, year-end cash of at least $135 million, and a cash runway through at least 2015. Pipeline milestones were unchanged: Phase 2b TC-5619 recruitment complete with data expected toward year-end, Phase 2b TC-5214 in overactive bladder on track for Q2 start, and TC-1734 Alzheimer's data expected mid-2014.

negative_highlights: SG&A costs increased 20% to $13.1 million due to sales force growth and promotional expenses.
Management declined to comment on the Chiesi buyout process or timeline, citing lack of involvement.
Pipeline product RETAVASE faces ongoing FDA regulatory issues regarding raw material suppliers.
positive_highlights: Net revenues reached $38 million, marking the highest quarterly revenue in company history.
Gross margins increased 7 percentage points to 68%, driven by CARDENE addition and improved CUROSURF performance.
Non-GAAP net income per diluted share reached $0.24, a significant improvement over the prior year.
summary: Cornerstone Therapeutics reported Q1 FY2013 net revenues of $38 million, a 71% year-over-year increase driven by the addition of CARDENE and growth in CUROSURF and ZYFLO. Gross margins expanded to 68%, up from 61% in the prior year quarter, while non-GAAP net income per share rose to $0.24. Management raised the outlook for the PERTZYE acquisition, projecting peak sales exceeding $40 million in the CF market.

negative_highlights: Total revenue fell 53% year-over-year.
Internet advertising revenue declined 12%.
Operating income swung to a loss of $0.1 million.
positive_highlights: Gross margin improved to 36.6% from 16%.
Brand management and sales channel revenue up 254% year-over-year.
Paying customers increased 40% to approximately 800.
summary: In Q1 2013, total revenue declined 53% to $7 million due to a strategic reduction in TV advertising, but gross margin improved from 16% to 36.6% and gross profit rose 8% to $2.6 million. Internet advertising revenue fell 12% to $3.8 million, while brand management sales jumped 254% to $0.53 million. Operating loss was $0.1 million versus an operating income of $0.1 million a year ago. The company expects full-year 2013 revenue of $36 million and net income of $1.2 million, with increased R&D spending toward mobile and social products.

negative_highlights: Gross margins in the Ground Equipment Sales segment remained under pressure from a highly competitive environment and low-margin military contracts.
Overnight Air Cargo operating income growth was offset by increased management labor and administrative costs associated with adding key personnel.
Ground Support Services operating margins faced headwinds from significant startup costs incurred while opening new large stations.
positive_highlights: Consolidated revenue increased 15% to $103 million driven by all three operating segments.
Net income grew 24% to $1.7 million, marking the 10th consecutive year of profitable operations.
Ground Support Services segment revenues surged 44% to $12.9 million due to new customers and locations.
summary: Consolidated revenues increased 15% to $103 million and net income rose 24% to $1.7 million ($0.68 per diluted share) for fiscal 2013 compared to the prior year. The company reported its 10th consecutive year of profitable operations, with significant growth driven by a 26% increase in ground equipment sales and a 44% rise in ground support services revenues. Management highlighted improved production efficiencies at the Global Ground Support subsidiary and announced a 20% dividend increase to $0.30 per share.

negative_highlights: Swung to a Q2 net loss of $12.4 million from net income of $14.5 million in the prior-year quarter, driven mainly by lower deferred revenue recognition.
Six-month net loss of $20.4 million versus net income of $16.8 million for the first half of 2012.
No product revenue was reported and no new financial guidance beyond the cash balance and runway was provided.
positive_highlights: Cash and investments of $164 million at quarter end, with guidance reaffirmed for at least $135 million at year-end 2013 and runway through at least end-2015.
Recruitment completed in the Phase IIb TC-5619 schizophrenia study, with top-line results expected in late December or January.

Recruitment completed in the Phase IIb TC-1734 Alzheimer's study, with top-line data still anticipated in mid 2014, and the TC-5214 overactive bladder Phase IIb study initiated in May targeting approximately 750 patients.
summary: Targacept reported a Q2 2013 net loss of $12.4 million versus net income of $14.5 million in Q2 2012, with the swing driven primarily by lower deferred revenue recognition, partly offset by lower R&D spend and the non-recurrence of 2012 restructuring charges. Six-month net loss was $20.4 million versus net income of $16.8 million a year earlier. The company ended the quarter with $164 million in cash and investments and reaffirmed guidance for a year-end 2013 balance of at least $135 million and a cash runway through at least the end of 2015. No product revenue or EPS figures were disclosed; clinical timelines were reiterated with TC-5619 data expected late December or January, TC-5214 in the first half of 2014 and TC-1734 in mid 2014.

negative_highlights: SG&A expenses increased significantly by 55% to $13.8 million due to growth in sales force and promotional spending.
Cash balance decreased by $700,000 to $55.5 million primarily due to a $10 million upfront payment for the PERTZYE license agreement.
positive_highlights: Net revenues reached a record $40.4 million, an 88% increase year-over-year.
Gross margin increased 16 percentage points to 75%, driven by the addition of CARDENE and improved margins on CUROSURF and ZYFLO.
CUROSURF posted record quarterly revenues of $11.3 million, a 21% increase over the prior year quarter.
summary: Cornerstone Therapeutics reported Q2 FY2013 net revenues of $40.4 million, representing an 88% year-over-year increase and a record quarterly revenue for the company. Net income per diluted share was $0.19, compared to a loss of $0.17 in the prior year quarter, driven by strong performance from CARDENE, CUROSURF, and ZYFLO. Management highlighted that gross margin expanded 16 percentage points to 75% due to product mix changes and improved margins on existing products.

negative_highlights: Total revenue down 32% year-over-year to $8.9 million
TV advertising revenue fell nearly 60% year-over-year
Cash and equivalents dropped to $3.4 million from $5.5 million at year-end 2012
positive_highlights: Gross margin up 1,100 basis points to 40.5%, driven by mix shift to higher-margin internet advertising
Paying internet advertising clients grew from 855 to 1,368 year-over-year
Entered partnership with China Business Journal and joint product development with Baidu
summary: ChinaNet reported Q2 2013 revenue of $8.9 million, down 32% year-over-year, while gross margin expanded to 40.5% from 28.7%. Net income fell to $0.4 million from $0.9 million, with EPS of $0.02. The decline was driven by a 60% drop in TV advertising revenue, partially offset by growth in internet advertising clients from 855 to 1,368. Management reiterated FY2013 guidance of $36 million revenue and $1.2 million net income, and highlighted new initiatives including a joint product with Baidu and a mobile app platform.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to $12.9 million in Q3 2013 from $7.9 million in Q3 2012
Nine-month net loss of $33.3 million versus net income of $8.9 million a year earlier, a $42.2 million swing
No update provided on AstraZeneca's strategic review of licensed program 1446
positive_highlights: Cash and investments of $155.1 million with reiterated year-end balance of at least $135 million and runway through at least end-2015
Patient recruitment completed for the Phase IIb TC-5619 schizophrenia study, with top-line results expected December or January
TC-5214 overactive bladder study enrollment progress exceeded additional planning assumptions
summary: Targacept reported a Q3 2013 net loss of $12.9 million versus a $7.9 million net loss in Q3 2012, driven by a $3.9 million increase in R&D expenses. Cash and investments totaled $155.1 million, and management reiterated year-end cash of at least $135 million and runway through at least end-2015. No revenue was reported; the quarter was defined by pipeline execution, with Phase IIb data for TC-5619 expected December/January and TC-5214 and TC-1734 data in 2014. Management declined to comment on AstraZeneca's strategic review of the partnered 1446 program.

negative_highlights: RETAVASE faces a stability failure requiring new process development, with a target relaunch delayed to late 2015.
CARDENE sales are currently supported by generic manufacturer shortages, which management expects will end at an unknown future date.
SG&A costs increased 27% to $16.4 million due to legal fees for patent litigation and promotional expenses.
positive_highlights: Net revenues reached $53.7 million, up 43% from Q3 2012, marking the highest quarterly revenue in company history.
Gross margin expanded to 76%, an increase of 14 percentage points over the prior year quarter.
Successfully launched generic equivalent of Tussionex on September 23 and initiated sales for PERTZYE.
summary: Cornerstone Therapeutics reported Q3 FY2013 net revenues of $53.7 million, a 43% year-over-year increase driven by CARDENE sales growth and new product launches like PERTZYE and Tussionex. Net income per diluted share jumped to $0.31 from $0.05 in the prior year quarter, with gross margins expanding to 76%. Management highlighted record revenue for the third consecutive quarter but noted a patent litigation stay regarding CARDENE generics and stability issues delaying the RETAVASE relaunch.

negative_highlights: Total revenue down 27% YoY to $7.5 million.
TV advertising revenue declined 83% YoY.
Full-year revenue guidance reduced to $30 million.
positive_highlights: Internet advertising revenue grew 7% YoY and customer count increased 27%.
Gross margin expanded to 55% from 40.1% YoY.
Operating cash flow for nine months improved to $2.8 million from $2.5 million.
summary: Q3 2013 total revenues fell 27% YoY to $7.5 million, but gross profit was flat at $4.1 million with gross margin up to 55% from 40.1%. Internet advertising revenue grew 7% and customer numbers increased 27%, while TV advertising revenue dropped 83% to $0.6 million. Net income was $1.2 million (EPS $0.05), and management lowered full-year revenue guidance to $30 million with net income of $1.2 million. The company cited strategic shift away from low-margin TV advertising and continued growth in higher-margin internet services.

negative_highlights: Full-year 2013 net loss widened to $46.7 million from $7 million in 2012, driven by a $53.9 million decrease in deferred revenue recognition
2014 guidance calls for minimal operating revenue against $40-45 million in operating expenses, implying continued losses
Year-end 2014 cash is now expected at a minimum of $100 million, below the $143.8 million starting balance
positive_highlights: Q4 2013 net loss narrowed to $13.4 million from $15.9 million in Q4 2012 on lower R&D expense and non-recurrence of restructuring charges
Both Phase-IIb programs (TC-5214 for overactive bladder, TC-1734 for Alzheimer's) remain on track for mid-2014 top-line results
Ended 2013 with $143.8 million in cash and investments; cash runway affirmed at least through end-2015
summary: Targacept reported a Q4 2013 net loss of $13.4 million, narrower than the $15.9 million loss in Q4 2012, helped by a $1.6 million R&D reduction and the non-recurrence of $1.4 million in 2012 restructuring charges; full-year 2013 net loss widened to $46.7 million from $7 million, largely on a $53.9 million decline in deferred revenue recognition. The company ended 2013 with $143.8 million in cash and guided 2014 operating expenses to $40-45 million with minimal operating revenue. Management described both Phase-IIb trials (TC-5214 in overactive bladder, TC-1734 in Alzheimer's) as on track for mid-2014 top-line data and affirmed cash covers operations at least through end-2015; a year-end 2014 cash figure was corrected on the call to at least $100 million.

negative_highlights: Film Products Q4 operating profit fell $4 million to $16 million on flexible packaging volume and pricing declines
2013 included a $14 million after-tax ($0.43/share) environmental charge to discontinued operations at divested Bonnell Canada
Guidance calls for slightly lower Film Products margins in 2014, continued flexible packaging weakness, Q1 surface protection slowdown, and $1-2 million more 13D spending
positive_highlights: Surface protection films posted record 2013 sales, up 30% year-over-year, and personal care sales rose 4%
Bonnell full-year operating profit improved $9 million to $18 million including ~$4.8 million of AACOA synergies; Q4 operating profit up $4 million
Pension expense expected to fall to ~$7.5 million in 2014 from $13.7 million; quarterly dividend raised 16% and net debt/EBITDA at 1.39x
summary: Q4 ongoing EPS was $0.27 and full-year ongoing EPS $1.15, with segment operating profit essentially flat in Q4 and up 13% for the year on 9% higher net sales (AACOA-driven). Film Products Q4 operating profit fell $4 million to $16 million on weak flexible packaging pricing and volumes, while Bonnell operating profit rose $4 million. Management guided 2014 to modest ~2% Film Products volume growth and ~9% Bonnell growth, but flagged slightly lower Film Products margins, continued flexible packaging pressure, a slow start with surface protection weakness through Q1, and elevated 13D costs of $1-2 million. The company also recorded a $14 million after-tax charge ($0.43/share) to discontinued operations tied to an environmental claim at divested Bonnell Canada.

negative_highlights: Pretax loss widened to $11.6 million in Q1 2014 from $8.1 million in Q1 2013
Loss increase driven principally by a $3.5 million decrease in recognized deferred revenue from collaboration agreements
positive_highlights: Ended Q1 2014 with $132.1 million in cash and investments and reaffirmed expectation to end 2014 with at least $100 million
Both Phase 2b trials (TC-5214 for OAB and TC-1734 for Alzheimer's) remain on track for top-line results around mid-2014
TC-6499 exploratory trial for diabetic gastroparesis remains on track for mid-2014 initiation
summary: Targacept reported a Q1 2014 pretax loss of $11.6 million versus a $8.1 million pretax loss in Q1 2013, with the wider loss attributed principally to a $3.5 million decrease in recognized deferred revenue from collaboration agreements. Cash, investments, and marketable securities totaled $132.1 million as of March 31, 2014, and management reiterated its expectation to end 2014 with at least $100 million in cash. The two ongoing Phase 2b trials (TC-5214 in overactive bladder and TC-1734 in Alzheimer's disease) remain on track for top-line results around mid-2014, and an exploratory trial of TC-6499 for diabetic gastroparesis is on track for mid-2014 initiation.

negative_highlights: Pipeline revenues dropped significantly from $9.2 million in Q1 2013 to $0.7 million in Q1 2014
Biofuels gross profit fell sharply from $8.3 million to $0.6 million due to margin squeezes and the absence of a $1.00 blender's credit
positive_highlights: Biofuels demand increased despite the lack of the blender's credit
Chemical margins remained relatively stable at roughly 30% despite volume declines due to price-volume curves on bleach activator
summary: FutureFuel reported Q1 FY2014 revenue of $82.2 million, down 11% year-over-year to $92.2 million in the prior period. Adjusted EBITDA was $10.1 million versus $17.7 million last year, and net income decreased to $6.3 million from $14.1 million due to lower sales volumes, reduced refined petroleum product sales on common carrier pipelines, and the absence of a blender's credit in the biofuels segment.

negative_highlights: TC-1734 missed the primary objective of superiority to donepezil in Alzheimer's disease on cognitive and global function, and the program was discontinued.
TC-5214 failed its co-primary incontinence endpoint (p=0.379) and development in overactive bladder was discontinued, leaving no clinical-stage revenue-bearing programs.
Operating expense guidance was reset downward alongside a 25% workforce reduction versus year-end 2013 and no significant operating revenues expected for 2014.
positive_highlights: Net loss before income taxes narrowed to $8.1 million in Q2 2014 from $12.4 million a year earlier, aided by lower R&D expense.
TC-5214 showed a statistically significant reduction in micturition frequency (p=0.033) at the highest dose, with several secondary endpoints also significant.
Cash and marketable securities of $122.8 million as of June 30, 2014, with a projected ~$107 million at year end and 2014 opex guided to $32-36 million.
summary: Targacept reported a Q2 2014 net loss before income taxes of $8.1 million versus $12.4 million a year ago, with the improvement driven by lower R&D spend as the company ended development of two lead programs. Both Phase IIb readouts failed: TC-1734 did not beat donepezil in Alzheimer's disease on cognition or global function, and TC-5214 hit one co-primary endpoint in overactive bladder (micturition frequency, p=0.033) but missed the other (incontinence, p=0.379); development of both was discontinued. Guidance was cut, with 2014 operating expenses now seen at $32-36 million and year-end cash of roughly $107 million after a 25% workforce reduction versus year-end 2013. The company has no revenue programs and is refocusing on business development and an early gastroparesis trial of TC-6499, which may read out in 2015.

negative_highlights: Death claims increased in both the life and home service segments for the three and six month periods, which management called unfavorable claim experience
First year life premiums fell 7.4% for the quarter, and home service premiums were essentially flat excluding $700K quarterly and $900K year-to-date from the Magnolia acquisition

Lower persistency in the home service block raised amortization of deferred acquisition costs, and the Magnolia acquisition is expected to contribute only about $300K to full-year net operating income
positive_highlights: Life segment renewal premiums rose 7.6% for the quarter and 5.9% for the six months, with renewals over 86% of total premiums
Investment yield improved to approximately 4.21% from a prior low of about 3.6%, and net unrealized bond gains reached $40.4 million at June 30 versus $5.1 million at year-end 2013
Life surrender expense fell 12.6% for the quarter, and surrenders held steady at roughly 0.6% of ordinary in-force
summary: Citizens reported life segment insurance premiums up 5.7% for the quarter and 5.4% year-to-date, driven by renewal premiums up 7.6% and 5.9% respectively, while first year premiums fell 7.4% in the quarter but rose 2.7% year-to-date. Results were muted by unfavorable death claim experience in both the life and home service segments, partially offset by a 12.6% quarterly decline in life surrender expense; general expenses were roughly flat. Investment yield improved to about 4.21% from a prior low near 3.6%, and net unrealized bond gains rose to $40.4 million at June 30 from $5.1 million at year-end 2013. No explicit financial guidance or prior guidance comparison was provided, and management said the outlook remains positive while noting economic stress in Argentina and roughly 60% inflation in Venezuela.

negative_highlights: Films 2014 volume target cut from 2% growth to a 7-10% year-over-year decline
Brazil flexible packaging line ramp pushed to Q4 from Q2, creating a sizable volume miss, and Cabo operational issues remain unresolved
Bonnell volume target lowered to 6-8% from 9% as nonresidential construction grew only about 2% versus the 4% industry expectation
positive_highlights: Bonnell adjusted EBITDA of $10.7M was over 60% above Q2 2013, with EBITDA margin up more than 400 bps to 12.7%
Ongoing-operations EPS of $0.34 was $0.04 favorable to 2013 and net income from ongoing operations rose 14% to $11.1M
New automotive press is exceeding expectations, with customer commitments for over half its capacity
summary: Tredegar reported Q2 FY2014 diluted EPS of $0.11, including a $10M one-time 3M litigation settlement charge; ongoing-operations EPS was $0.34, up $0.04 YoY, with net income from ongoing operations of $11.1M up 14%. Combined segment operating profit was flat at $23M, as Bonnell's adjusted EBITDA rose over 60% to $10.7M while Films EBITDA fell $5M to $23.2M (15.9% margin) on a $2.2M baby-care volume impact and surface-protection inventory correction. Management lowered Films' 2014 volume target from 2% growth to a 7-10% decline, cut Bonnell's volume target to 6-8% from 9%, and pushed the Brazil flexible packaging line ramp into Q4 from Q2; ROIC target held at 8-9% and 2016 targets affirmed.

negative_highlights: Biofuels segment posted a gross profit loss of $0.6 million, down from income of $12.8 million last year.
Chemical revenues decreased 22% primarily due to lost sales to a substantial customer and reduced volumes on discontinued products.
New proprietary herbicide intermediate plant is not yet at full rate production despite strong demand.
positive_highlights: Feedstock prices for biodiesel have recently loosened significantly after being tight earlier in the year.
The company holds substantial storage capacity, positioning it well if feedstock dislocations persist or RIN values improve later in the year.
Deferred revenue related to shortfall fees from an intermediate anode powder customer is expected to be realized in Q3.
summary: Q2 FY2014 revenues decreased 36% to $68 million and adjusted EBITDA fell 74% to $6.7 million compared to the prior year quarter. The decline was driven by a severe drop in biofuels revenue (-45%) due to weak market conditions, loss of RIN value, hedging losses, and reduced sales volumes across key chemical segments including proprietary herbicide intermediates (-51%). Management noted that while some new product lines are ramping up, execution challenges with new plants and a lack of regulatory clarity on the EPA's Renewable Volume Obligation (RVO) continue to weigh heavily on results.

negative_highlights: Comprehensive net loss widened to $488,000 from a $142,000 loss in the prior-year quarter
No financial guidance was provided for future periods
The prior-year quarter included a $200,000 benefit from a decrease in warrant liabilities, versus a $30,000 increase this year
positive_highlights: Direct sales bookings increased 663% year-over-year to $802,000, the fourth consecutive quarterly increase
Total revenue grew 5.7% to $1,032,000 despite the loss of $500,000 in LinkedIn revenue from the prior-year period
Acquisition agreement for NAPW, which generated $19.7 million in revenue and $2.3 million in operating cash flow last year
summary: PDN reported Q2 2014 GAAP revenue of $1,032,000, up 5.7% from $977,000 a year earlier, despite the termination of the LinkedIn agreement that had provided $500,000 in past quarters. Direct sales bookings rose 663% year-over-year to $802,000, the fourth consecutive quarterly increase. However, the comprehensive net loss widened to $488,000 from a $142,000 loss in the prior-year quarter, driven by costs of building a direct sales force and the lower-margin events division. The company announced a definitive merger agreement to acquire the National Association of Professional Women (NAPW), which generated $19.7 million in revenue and $2.3 million in operating cash flow last year, but provided no formal financial guidance for the upcoming quarters.

negative_highlights: Adjusted net loss per share widened from $0.39 to $0.73 year-over-year due to increased R&D expenses and non-recurring finance charges
Cash burn remains elevated at an estimated range of $1.5 million to $2 million per month for the next two to four quarters
positive_highlights: Completed patient recruitment for DFU Phase III trial months ahead of schedule
Achieved goal of having 25 clinical sites open and actively enrolling subjects in VLU study by October 1st
Secured FDA agreement to remove blood matching requirements, enhancing scalability
summary: Macrocure reported a net loss of $10.1 million ($0.70 per share) for Q3 FY2014 compared to a prior year loss of $10.2 million, with adjusted EPS widening from $0.39 in the current quarter to $0.73 last year due to increased R&D costs and non-recurring finance expenses. The company achieved key clinical milestones including completing patient recruitment for its diabetic foot ulcer trial early and reaching enrollment goals for its venous leg ulcer study, while securing an agreement with the FDA to remove blood matching requirements that enhances scalability.

negative_highlights: No product revenue reported; net loss continued at $24.5M for the nine months ended September 30, 2014
No new NNR studies will start prior to determining strategic direction, per CEO
Prior full-year cash guidance of approximately $107M at year-end was reiterated without update, indicating continued cash burn
positive_highlights: Cash and investments of $114.5M at quarter end provides a substantial runway
Q3 net loss narrowed to $4.9M from $12.9M in Q3 2013 on lower R&D expense
Returned AstraZeneca rights give unencumbered ownership of TC-1446 and other NNR compounds for possible out-licensing
summary: Targacept reported Q3 2014 cash and investments of $114.5M, a net loss of $4.9M versus $12.9M a year ago, and a nine-month loss of $24.5M versus $33.3M, the improvement driven by lower R&D spend. No revenue was disclosed; the company is a clinical-stage biotech running a strategic review and expects to identify preferred options—strategic combination, in-licensing, or a substantial cash return—before year-end 2014. Prior cash guidance of roughly $107M at year-end was unchanged, and the exploratory TC-6499 diabetic gastroparesis trial is expected to report headline results in the first half of 2015.

negative_highlights: Surrender expense rose 19.8% for the quarter and 9% year-to-date versus 2013
Home Service segment had no real organic premium growth excluding Magnolia; lower persistency there is pressuring DAC amortization
Domestic life sales were flat to slightly below 2013 levels
positive_highlights: Life segment insurance premiums grew 7.8% for the quarter and 6.2% year-to-date, with first year premiums up 9.1%
Death claims decreased 13.2% for the three months ended September 30, 2014
Investment income yield rose to 4.22% from a prior low around 3.6%
summary: Citizens reported double-digit net income increases for Q3 and year-to-date 2014, with life segment premiums up 7.8% for the quarter and 6.2% year-to-date, driven by strong renewals (>85% of premiums) and 9.1% growth in first year premiums. Home Service premiums rose over 5% but only due to the Magnolia acquisition, with no organic premium growth in the segment. Death claims fell 13.2% in the quarter but surrender expense rose 19.8% and Home Service persistency weakened, lifting DAC amortization. Investment yield improved to 4.22%, and no explicit forward guidance was provided.

negative_highlights: Biodiesel revenue plummeted 25% to $58.2 million due to severely weakened market conditions, the absence of the dollar blender's credit, and a narrow spread on feedstock prices.
Gross profit for biodiesel collapsed from $12.2 million in Q3 last year to just $3 million this quarter as industry profitability suffered without government support mechanisms.
positive_highlights: Chemical segment gross profit increased 29% to $17.9 million inclusive of a one-time shortfall revenue item, driven by improved margins on the new herbicide intermediate and performance chemicals.
The company maintains an extremely strong balance sheet with approximately $200 million in cash, no debt, and low-cost feedstock advantages allowing profitability despite industry-wide challenges.
summary: Q3 revenue decreased 15% to $103.1 million and adjusted EBITDA fell 44% to $15.9 million due to weak biodiesel market conditions driven by the absence of the blender's credit and lower RVO volumes. Chemical revenues declined 13% excluding a one-time shortfall revenue item, while gross profit dropped 20%. Management highlighted strong liquidity with nearly $200M in cash but noted significant industry headwinds regarding renewable fuel mandates.

negative_highlights: $11.8 million non-cash VirtualAgility impairment drove an $8.1 million net loss, or $0.19 per share, versus $6.5 million net income a year ago.
Technology sales, services and licensing revenue fell $103,000 to $475,000 due to no Q3 2014 settlements.
Technology management division posted a $424,000 adjusted EBITDA loss, and corporate adjusted EBITDA loss widened 8% to $541,000.
positive_highlights: Printed products revenue rose 22% to $4.5 million on plastic and packaging sales, and printed products adjusted EBITDA rose 160% to $603,000.
Company-wide adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed to $362,000 from $556,000 a year ago on 17% revenue growth and cost controls.
Excluding this year's impairment and last year's $9.2 million tax benefit, net loss shrank to $2.19 million from $2.7 million.
summary: Total revenue rose 17% to $5.0 million, with printed products up 22% to $4.5 million and adjusted EBITDA loss improving to $362,000 from a $556,000 loss a year ago, though technology sales fell $103,000 to $475,000 on the absence of settlements. GAAP results swung to an $8.1 million net loss ($0.19 per share) versus $6.5 million net income ($0.15) last year, driven by an $11.8 million non-cash impairment on the VirtualAgility investment. Management gave no specific numeric guidance but said printed products is positioned for continued revenue and EBITDA growth in Q4 and 2015, and disclosed IP litigation setbacks including an adverse summary judgment in the Coupons.com breach-of-contract case. Cash and restricted cash stood at $2.3 million at quarter end.

negative_highlights: Total operating expenditures rose 50% to $2.158 million from $1.439 million
Only about 60,000 of NAPW's roughly 600,000 members are paid members
No formal forward guidance or consensus comparison was provided despite a heavily Q4-weighted recruitment business
positive_highlights: E-commerce revenue increased 174% to $45,000 from $16,000 a year ago
Recruitment revenue exceeded the prior-year quarter despite the loss of the LinkedIn contract
Identified approximately $3 million in annual cost savings across both entities, including a $300,000 sub-lease saving
summary: Professional Diversity Network reported Q3 FY2014 results following its September 24, 2014 merger with NAPW, with total operating expenses up 50% to $2.158 million versus $1.439 million a year ago, of which only $349,000 came from post-merger NAPW operations. E-commerce revenue rose 174% to $45,000, the events division booked $198,000, and recruitment revenue exceeded the prior-year quarter despite the loss of the LinkedIn contract. NAPW generated $18.9 million of revenue in the first nine months of 2014, roughly 80-85% from membership, and the company identified about $3 million in annual cost savings. Management cited a strong October with retention, new members, and revenue all up but offered no formal forward guidance.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined sequentially from Q2, which management attributed to no new wells being added, natural shale decline, and the produced-water disposal bottleneck
Many D-J Basin wells, including the company's, were shut in for extended periods during the quarter waiting on disposal capacity, depressing Q3 volumes

Debt stands at $29.4 million with $8.1 million current against $8.9 million cash, and no EPS or formal financial guidance was provided; the 500 BOE/d exit rate and Loomis well results remain forward-looking
positive_highlights: Sales volume grew to 16,984 BOE (185 BOE/d), over 200% year-over-year growth, with revenue of $1.1 million up roughly 450-500% YoY
The November 3 salt-water disposal agreement lifted net Red Hawk production to nearly 3,400 BOE in the 27 days ended November 5 versus 975 BOE during the prior shut-in 27-day period, a ~350% increase

Wattenberg acreage was acquired at ~$1,000/net acre versus recent basin transactions at $4,500-$8,800/net acre, and the company holds $8.9 million cash plus ~$1 million net available on its debt facility
summary: PEDEVCO reported Q3 FY2014 revenue of $1.1 million, up roughly 450-500% year over year, on sales volume of 16,984 BOE (185 BOE/d, over 200% YoY growth), but revenue declined sequentially versus Q2 because no new wells were added and many wells were shut in for extended periods due to a produced-water disposal bottleneck in the D-J Basin. Management reiterated an exit-2014 target of roughly 500 net BOE/d (about double current levels), a $40-$60/bbl breakeven at a ~15-16% rate of return, and ~$30 million of discretionary capex over the next 12 months, but gave no formal revenue or EPS guidance and reported no EPS figure. The key change versus the prior quarter is the November 3 salt-water disposal agreement, which management says restored full production and lifted Red Hawk net production to nearly 3,400 BOE in the 27 days ended November 5 from 975 BOE during the shut-in August-September period. Balance sheet: $8.9 million cash, $29.4 million debt of which $8.1 million current.

negative_highlights: Gross profit grew 41% versus 79% revenue growth, indicating margin contraction
Working capital declined to $31.3 million from $71.9 million at fiscal year-end
Nine-month operating cash flow fell to $12.9 million from $31.4 million, and kiwi facility production was delayed
positive_highlights: Revenue rose 79% YoY to $34.8 million on growth across nearly all product lines
Operating income grew 57% to $7.2 million and net income rose 45% to $4.7 million
Operating expenses fell to 9% of sales from 13%, with G&A down 19% to $1.3 million
summary: Revenue rose 79% YoY to $34.8 million, driven by broad gains across apple, pear, and juice-beverage lines, with net income up 45% to $4.7 million and EPS of $0.17 versus $0.11 a year ago. Gross profit rose 41% to $10.2 million, implying margin compression given the faster revenue growth, while operating expenses fell as a percentage of sales. The text gives no explicit forward guidance and notes the kiwi processing facility production has been delayed; working capital fell to $31.3 million from $71.9 million at fiscal year-end.

negative_highlights: Film Products full-year net sales fell 7% to $579 million and operating profit dropped 18% to $58 million, with EBITDA margin of 15.3% below the 16% target
2016 Film Products adjusted EBITDA margin target lowered to 17%-18% from original 18% due to competitive pricing and lower volumes
Noncash pension expense to increase $5.6 million in 2015 to approximately $12.3 million, and effective tax rate rose to 35% from 31%, a $0.07 EPS headwind
positive_highlights: Bonnell operating profit rose 40% to $26 million with 7% volume growth and EBITDA margin of 10.3%, at the high end of target range
Bonnell Q4 net sales up 24% and operating profit up 20%, with volume growth of 13% year over year
New flexible packaging line came in on budget with ramp-up pace exceeding expectations, and Brazil operational issues were resolved by year-end as committed
summary: Tredegar reported Q4 ongoing EPS of $0.23 and full-year ongoing EPS of $1.13, down from $1.15 in prior year. Film Products net sales fell 7% to $579 million for the year with operating profit down 18% to $58 million, driven by the loss of baby care elastic laminate volume, competitive pricing pressures, and Brazil operational inefficiencies. Bonnell was a standout with full-year net sales up $35 million to $344 million, operating profit up 40% to $26 million, and volume growth of 7%. Management guided to difficult Film Products market conditions in the first half of 2015, restated 2016 Film Products adjusted EBITDA margin target down to 17%-18% from the original 18%, and expects pension expense to increase $5.6 million in 2015.

negative_highlights: Total revenues decreased 30% year-over-year as biofuel revenue fell 44% due to reduced note prices and volumes.
Biofuels gross profit declined significantly on a full-year basis (down 56%) compared to the prior year period.
Management stated Q1 biodiesel demand remains challenging with no final mandate or dollar credit in place.
positive_highlights: Net income increased 14% to $30.1 million driven by net benefit of retroactive reinstatement of one dollar blenders tax credit ($10.3M profit recognized).
Chemical segment revenue grew 7% year-over-year, with the new proprietary herbicide intermediate contributing significantly.
Gross profit from biofuels improved 39% quarter-over-quarter to $46 million despite lower sales volumes.
summary: Net income increased to $30.1 million due to a retroactive reinstatement of the blender tax credit, while revenues decreased 30% year-over-year driven by lower biofuel watching prices and volumes. Management noted that Q4 was challenging for biodiesel demand without a final mandate or dollar credit in place throughout the year, though they expressed optimism about building momentum on their chemical side with new products like the herbicide intermediate.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened significantly from $3.9M in Q4 FY2013 to $7.6M in Q4 FY2014 due to increased R&D ($5.7M vs $3.3M) and G&A expenses.
Full year net loss expanded from $18.3M in 2013 to $25.5M in 2014.
positive_highlights: DFU Phase III trial on track to complete treatment period with last patient out by June 2015, allowing database lock in early September and data reporting in October.
summary: Macrocure reported a net loss of $7.6 million ($0.42 per share) for Q4 FY2014 and $25.5 million ($2.15 per share) for the full year, driven by increased R&D expenses of $5.7M in Q4 due to patient recruitment acceleration. Management provided no financial guidance but reiterated clinical milestones: DFU Phase III results expected October 2015, VLU futility analysis in Q3 2015 with full results anticipated H1 2016, and a BLA submission targeted for the second half of 2016. The company maintains $47.4 million in cash as of year-end.

negative_highlights: No GAAP EPS, net income, or cash flow figures were disclosed
The quarter included $565,000 of non-cash stock compensation and over $700,000 of amortized intangibles
$8.3 million of Q4 revenue is described as 'bookings' that only 'closely matched revenues', and Q1 2015 figures are unaudited
positive_highlights: Q4 2014 revenue rose to $8.3 million from $1.5 million a year earlier
Q1 2015 booked revenue reached $11.2 million (unaudited) versus $1.6 million in the prior-year period
Noble Voice gross margins were stated as north of 60%, and subletting one NAPW facility is expected to save over $300,000 annually
summary: Q4 2014 revenue rose to $8.3 million from $1.5 million a year earlier, with NAPW contributing just over $6 million of that total, and Q1 2015 booked revenue reached $11.2 million (unaudited) versus $1.6 million a year prior. Management cited over $300,000 in annual savings from subletting one NAPW facility, $565,000 of non-cash stock compensation and over $700,000 of amortized intangibles in the quarter, and a Noble Voice gross margin north of 60%. Registered users grew from 37,000 in March 2014 to 218,000 in March 2015, and Noble Voice is processing roughly 4,000 inbound job-seeker calls daily. No formal EPS, net income, or cash flow figures were disclosed and no specific forward guidance was given beyond expectations of expense flattening and continued revenue growth.

negative_highlights: Gross margin fell from 45.3% to 17%
Operating loss of $14.6M vs. prior $0.6M net income
Brand management revenue dropped to $0.9M from $2.6M
positive_highlights: Total revenue up 28% YoY to $38.9M
Search engine marketing revenue up 51% to $31.3M
Cash and equivalents increased to $5M from $3.4M
summary: ChinaNet reported FY2014 revenue of $38.9M, up 28% YoY, driven by search engine marketing (up 51% to $31.3M), but gross margin collapsed from 45.3% to 17% due to lower-margin new services and higher Internet resource costs. Operating loss widened to $14.6M from $0.6M net income in 2013; net loss per share was $0.61. Management guided 2015 revenue to $48M (+25-28%) but expects losses to continue, improving toward profitability by Q1 2016. They are launching Business Direct 3.0 with Baidu and made small investments (e.g., O'Yummy) to diversify, but admit Q1 2015 slow start due to Chinese New Year.

negative_highlights: Consolidated revenue fell sharply due to a $32 million decline in biofuels sales driven by regulatory uncertainty and energy price declines.
Bleach activator business declined 27%, with management confirming an early termination of the P&G supply contract at year-end.
Biofuel segment revenues dropped 62% compared to the prior year quarter.
positive_highlights: Chemicals segment revenue grew 13% year-over-year despite significant declines in legacy businesses.
Net income increased to $8.1 million, a 29.6% rise from the prior period driven by LIFO reserve benefits and improved chemical execution.
Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded significantly to 24% compared to 12% in the prior year quarter.
summary: Consolidated revenue declined 34.2% to $54.1 million due to a significant drop in biofuels sales driven by regulatory uncertainty and lower energy prices, though the chemicals segment grew 13%. Net income increased 29.6% year-over-year primarily due to a favorable change in LIFO reserve rather than operational volume growth. Management expressed cautious optimism for later quarters but highlighted headwinds including contract terminations with P&G and industry-wide capacity idling.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened significantly year-over-year due to elevated clinical trial expenses for the new Phase III studies in DFU and VLU.
G&A expenses increased from $0.7M to $1.6M, reflecting costs of being a public company including stock-based compensation and recruiting.
positive_highlights: Completed patient recruitment for the VLU Phase III trial in record time (under 12 months) with over 250 patients across 25 sites, accelerating timelines by approximately six months compared to initial plans.
Received extremely positive feedback on mechanism of action data presented at SAWC and ARVO conferences regarding angiogenesis and cell proliferation.
summary: Macrocure reported a net loss of $6.9 million for Q1 FY2015 compared to $3.4 million in the prior year quarter, driven by increased R&D expenses ($5.3M vs $2.7M) and G&A costs associated with being public. The company reiterated its 2015 operating expense cash burn guidance of $21-25 million but did not provide specific revenue figures as it is a pre-revenue clinical-stage biotech firm.

negative_highlights: Net cash used in operations was $465,000 in the quarter
Company does not disclose NAPW paying subscriber count for competitive reasons
Severance and integration-related costs are still flowing through, delaying full realization of expense reductions until Q3
positive_highlights: Revenue rose to $10.7 million from $1.2 million in Q1 2014 and $7.8 million in Q4 2014
Total annualized cost savings target raised to over $4 million from the initial $3 million goal
Registered users grew from about 3 million to over 10 million, with monthly new registrations up to 250,000+ from roughly 40,000 a year ago
summary: Revenue for Q1 2015 was $10.7 million versus $1.2 million a year ago and $7.8 million last quarter, driven by acquisitions; gross margin exceeded 80%. Management raised its cost-savings target to over $4 million annualized versus the original $3 million goal, citing $500,000 already realized plus $3.5 million more by the end of Q3, and expects the expense run rate to fall about $300,000 per month from the end of Q1 to the end of Q3. Registered users grew from roughly 3 million to over 10 million, with new registrations running over 250,000 per month versus about 40,000 a year ago. Q1 used $465,000 of cash in operations, and $4.4 million net was raised in an April offering.

negative_highlights: Consolidated gross margin contracted to 23% from 31% a year ago
Operating expenses rose to 24% of sales from 17%, with G&A up 150% to $3 million including a $1.5 million bad debt allowance
Apple-related product sales fell 99% to approximately $25,000 from $274,000
positive_highlights: Revenue rose 41% YoY to $16.6 million from $11.8 million
Net income increased 164% to $1.7 million and EPS doubled to $0.06 from $0.02
Concentrated pear juice revenue grew 111% to $7 million and now represents 50% of total revenue
summary: SkyPeople Fruit Juice reported Q1 2015 revenue of $16.6 million, up 41% from $11.8 million a year earlier, with net income of $1.7 million (EPS $0.06) versus $0.6 million ($0.02) in Q1 2014. However, consolidated gross margin fell to 23% from 31%, operating expenses rose to 24% of sales from 17%, and a $1.5 million bad debt allowance was recorded tied to slower accounts receivable collection following sales-team turnover. Concentrated pear juice sales grew 111% to $7 million and now represent 50% of total revenue, while apple-related sales collapsed 99% to roughly $25,000. No explicit forward guidance was provided beyond noting new processing projects expected to reach trial production by end of June.

negative_highlights: Gross margin declined to 20.4% from 26.3%
Operating loss widened from $0.7M to $3.1M
Cash and equivalents fell to $2.2M from $5M end of 2014
positive_highlights: Search engine marketing revenue up 56% YoY
Partnership with Baidu for Direct 3.0 and cross-note
Full-year loss guidance improved to $5-6M from $14M last year
summary: In Q1 2015, ChinaNet's revenue grew 13% year-over-year to $5.8 million, with search engine marketing services up 56% to $5.6 million, but gross profit fell to $0.9 million and margins declined from 26.3% to 20.4%. Operating loss widened to $3.1 million and net loss per share was $0.07. Management lowered full-year guidance to a net loss of $5-6 million, an improvement from prior year's $14 million loss, while highlighting new partnerships such as Baidu Direct 3.0, an investment in O'Yummy, and a planned credit product with Shanghai Pudong Development Bank.

negative_highlights: Recognized revenue declined year-over-year from RMB92.9 million to RMB73.7 million.
Advanced payments from customers decreased due to a tight credit environment in China and shifts toward direct sales models.
The company explicitly stated it does not typically provide guidance, citing lack of variance over recent years.
positive_highlights: Deferred revenues increased to RMB373.4 million ($61.1 million), indicating strong underlying demand and order flow expected to be recognized in the fourth quarter.
summary: Origin Agritech reported Q3 FY2015 recognized revenue of RMB73.7 million ($12.0 million), a decrease from the prior year's RMB92.9 million, while deferred revenues rose to RMB373.4 million. The company posted an operating loss of RMB8.4 million and a net loss attributable to Origin of RMB11.9 million, representing improvements over last year but still reflecting weak quarterly performance due to accounting recognition policies where most revenue is booked in Q4.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened significantly year-over-year from $4.4M ($0.59/share) to $6.7M ($0.37/share), reflecting elevated clinical trial costs.
General and administrative expenses increased by $0.7 million in Q2 due to payroll, stock-based compensation, and public company-related costs.
Commercial launch is delayed until early 2018 following FDA approval expected around the end of 2017.
positive_highlights: Company remains on-track to report top-line results from the Diabetic Foot Ulcer (DFU) Phase III trial in October and Venous Leg Ulcer (VLU) trial in H1 2016.
Management expects a favorable DSMB recommendation with probability of success anticipated between 46% and 100%, indicating strong separation between treatment and control arms.
The company secured no debt outstanding while maintaining $35.9 million in cash, providing liquidity to fund the upcoming BLA filing scheduled for H2 2016.
summary: Macrocure reported a net loss of $6.7 million ($0.37 per share) for Q2 FY2015 and $13.6 million ($0.74 per share) for the six months ended June 30, 2015, driven by increased R&D expenses of $4.8M in Q2 due to Phase III clinical trials. The company reiterated an expected operating expense cash burn range of $21-25 million for 2015 and confirmed it has no debt outstanding with approximately $35.9 million in cash and short-term investments as of June 30, 2015.

negative_highlights: Net income decreased to $3.8 million from $5.3 million in the prior year
Gross profit in biofuels segment declined to a loss of $4.5 million, up from a smaller loss previously
Softness observed in product sales to energy exploration and ag chemistry markets
positive_highlights: Revenue increased 53.7% to $104.6 million compared to Q2 2014
Chemical segment revenue remained flat at $32.7 million with gross profit up 40%
Biofuels sales volume for biodiesel blends increased by 75%
summary: FutureFuel reported Q2 FY2015 revenue of $104.6 million (up 53.7% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $9.3 million (up 39%), but net income decreased to $3.8 million due to derivative losses, RIN inventory buildup, and reduced marketable securities gains. Management noted softness in ag chemistry and energy exploration markets for chemicals, while biofuels revenue grew significantly despite a gross profit loss of $4.5 million driven by the aforementioned non-operating factors.

negative_highlights: Net loss of $788,000 in the quarter
Revenue roughly flat sequentially at $10.4 million
Management declined to provide guidance on Q3 trends or profitability timing
positive_highlights: Operating expenses reduced by nearly $1.5 million sequentially, with EBITDA deficit narrowing 71% to $454,000
Gross margin above 85% in Q2
Added over 1.5 million new registered users and signed NAPW corporate membership contracts including with Manpower Group
summary: Professional Diversity Network reported Q2 2015 revenue of $10.4 million, roughly flat sequentially but up 907% year-over-year due to acquisitions, with gross margin above 85% and a net loss of $788,000. Operating expenses fell nearly $1.5 million from Q1 and the EBITDA deficit narrowed 71% from $1.568 million to $454,000, as management prioritized profitability over revenue growth. Management did not provide guidance, stating it would not comment on Q3 trends or future profitability timing, but reiterated a goal of reaching positive EBITDA. The company reported $6.4 million in cash and short-term investments and $527,000 in notes payable with no long-term debt.

negative_highlights: Total revenue fell 18% year-over-year primarily due to a decline in metals business and silicon nitride sales dropping $0.3 million.
Gross margins declined from 73% to 71%, partially attributed to lower-margin private-label sales.
FDA request for additional two years of clinical data delays the commercialization timeline for the cervical composite device until late Q4 or early Q1 2016.
positive_highlights: GAAP net loss decreased by $7.3 million year-over-year to $5.9 million due to reduced operating expenses and stock-based compensation.
Operational cash burn declined by 37% year-to-date, with quarterly operational cash flow improving significantly in Q2 compared to the prior period.
Production yields increased beyond 97.5%, up from the low 90s during the same period last year.
summary: Second quarter revenue declined 18% year-over-year to $4.8 million driven by lower metals business and a loss of key surgeons for silicon nitride products. Gross margins contracted slightly to 71%, while operating expenses fell significantly due to restructuring, resulting in an improved GAAP net loss of $5.9 million compared to the prior period's $13.2 million. Management maintained full-year revenue guidance of $19-20 million but noted silicon nitride sales growth is likely at the lower end of expectations.

negative_highlights: Apple concentrate sales fell 94% to ~$50,000 (11 tons vs. 480 tons), attributed to intense price competition and low margins
Total revenue grew only 2% to $12.2 million, with fruit juice beverages up just ~1% to $11.1 million
Major orange (Yidu, ~$48 million) and kiwi (Mei County, ~$72 million) projects remain behind schedule with no firm completion dates
positive_highlights: Gross margin expanded to 42% from 38%, with gross profit up to $5.1 million from $4.6 million
Net income attributable to SkyPeople jumped to $2.1 million ($0.08 EPS) from $0.05 million (nil EPS)
Operating income rose 64% to $3.6 million and first-half operating cash inflow rose to $36.7 million from $22.4 million
summary: Revenue rose 2% to $12.2 million as fruit juice beverages held 91% of sales (up slightly to $11.1 million) while apple concentrate collapsed 94% to ~$50,000. Gross margin expanded to 42% from 38%, operating income rose 64% to $3.6 million and net income jumped to $2.1 million ($0.08 EPS) from $0.05 million, driven partly by a reversal of a doubtful-debt provision. Management gave no formal earnings guidance and flagged that major projects in Mei County, Yidu and Suizhong remain behind schedule. The stock fell after a same-day S-3 shelf filing enabling up to $100 million in financing, which management acknowledged as a dilution concern.

negative_highlights: Total revenue declined 7.1% YoY to $9.6 million
TV advertising revenue fell to $1 million from $1.8 million
Company reported an operating loss of $1.8 million and net loss of $1.2 million
positive_highlights: Gross margin improved to 23.7% from 16.4% year-over-year
Internet advertising revenue increased 16% to $5.8 million
Balance sheet solid with cash up to $4.6 million and $0.9 million operating cash flow
summary: ChinaNet reported Q2 2015 revenue of $9.6 million, down 7.1% YoY, but gross margin improved to 23.7% from 16.4% due to higher-margin Internet advertising. Net loss narrowed to $1.2 million from $1.3 million a year ago. Management maintained full-year 2015 revenue guidance of $48.75 million despite a weak first half and expects net loss of about $6 million for the year, a 50% decrease from last year. They highlighted strategic investments and partnerships, including Dongsys Innovation and Beijing Saturday, as growth drivers.

negative_highlights: Net income declined 57% YoY from $11.5 million to $4.9 million due to a one-time termination payment and inventory adjustments
Chemical segment revenue fell 30% ($13.3 million decline) driven by lower volumes, unfavorable product mix, and the non-recurring contract termination charge
Gross profit in biofuels declined despite volume growth as energy prices dropped significantly
positive_highlights: Revenue increased 4% YoY driven by higher sales volumes offsetting lower prices
Biofuel segment revenue grew 30% due to volume increases of biodiesel and diesel blends
Amendment with P&G extended bleach activator product sales through 2018
summary: FutureFuel reported Q3 FY2015 revenue of $107.1 million (up 4% YoY) and net income of $4.9 million ($0.11/share), both significantly lower than the prior year quarter due to a one-time contract termination payment, inventory adjustments under LIFO accounting, and declining energy prices in its biofuel segment. While revenue grew on volume, gross profit contracted 58% primarily because of an $8.8 million non-recurring charge related to a graphite material contract that did not recur in the prior year.

negative_highlights: Total revenue declined by 19% compared to the prior year quarter.
Non-silicon nitrate sales dropped sharply by 27%, driven by a lack of sufficient diversity and activity decline among key surgeons.
GAAP net loss increased substantially due to an $8 million increase in fair value derivative liabilities.
positive_highlights: Year-to-date operational cash burn decreased significantly by 38% from the prior year period.
Production yields increased beyond 97%, representing a sizable increase over last year's same period.
Company finalized definitive agreements to raise up to $15 million in equity financing.
summary: Third quarter revenue was $4.8 million, down 19% year-over-year primarily due to declines in the metals business and silicon nitrate sales of $300k (down 10%). GAAP net loss widened to $10.1 million from a prior period loss of $4.9 million driven by an $8 million increase in fair value derivative liabilities, though adjusted EBITDA improved slightly to a loss of $2.1 million versus $2.3 million previously.

negative_highlights: OEM revenue from largest customer fell 69% sequentially, more than forecast
Gross margin contracted to 29.2% from 31.5% in Q2
Net loss widened to $10.2M from $8.9M in Q2
positive_highlights: Revenue grew sequentially from $18.4M to $18.8M despite OEM shortfall
OEM bookings in Q4 are ahead of same point in Q3, expecting recovery
New products like Glassware 2.0 and Exosphere commercially available in Azure
summary: Sphere 3D reported Q3 2015 revenue of $18.8 million, up slightly from $18.4 million in Q2, despite a $1.3 million OEM revenue shortfall. Gross margin declined to 29.2% from 31.5% in Q2, and net loss widened to $10.2 million from $8.9 million. Management highlighted progress on strategic initiatives, including new products with Microsoft, but noted the OEM headwind was larger than expected and margins remain under pressure.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined sequentially from Q2 to $9.3 million due to deliberate cuts in low-margin business and sales headcount reductions.
Q3 adjusted EBITDA deficit of about $900,000 was wider than the $1.5 million deficit in Q2, attributed to non-recurring expenses and staffing adjustments.
GAAP net loss was $29.7 million including non-cash goodwill impairment and deferred tax valuation allowances, with pro forma loss of $1 million or $0.07 per share.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 493% year-over-year to $9.3 million, reflecting the combined company acquisitions.
Gross margin held at 84%, up from 73% in the year-ago quarter.
Adjusted EBITDA deficit narrowed to less than $50,000 in September, the best month since the March 2013 IPO, with $6 million in annualized cost cuts already achieved.
summary: Professional Diversity Network reported Q3 2015 revenue of $9.3 million, up 493% year-over-year but down sequentially from Q2, which management attributed to a planned pullback from low-margin business and sales force reductions. Gross margin was 84%, but adjusted EBITDA deficit widened to about $900,000 from $1.5 million in Q2, with September reaching near-breakeven at less than $50,000 deficit. GAAP net loss was $29.7 million due to non-cash goodwill impairment and deferred tax valuation allowances, with pro forma loss of about $1 million or $0.07 per share. Management touted $6 million in annualized cost cuts and expects another $1 million in savings, targeting profitability in early 2016, but provided no specific revenue or EPS guidance and acknowledged the revenue decline was baked into plans.

negative_highlights: Total revenues declined 9.3% year-over-year due to lower volumes from market oversupply and increasing competition
Net loss for the fiscal year was RMB13.8 million, an increase in absolute terms compared to a net loss of RMB9.5 million in 2014 (excluding tax liability reversals)
Headcount reductions were necessary as part of cost reduction efforts amid market challenges
positive_highlights: Operating income turned positive at RMB1.3 million, reversing the prior year's loss of RMB24.5 million
Net cash provided by operating activities reached RMB52.2 million from a negative outflow of RMB85.6 million in 2014
General and administrative expenses decreased by 12% year-over-year to improve cost structure
summary: Total revenues for fiscal year 2015 were RMB376.3 million, a decrease of 9.3% year-over-year due to lower volumes in corn and rice seeds caused by market oversupply and competition. Operating income turned positive at RMB1.3 million from an operating loss of RMB24.5 million the prior year, driven primarily by expense control efforts that reduced general and administrative expenses by 12%. Net cash provided by operating activities improved to RMB52.2 million compared to a negative outflow of RMB85.6 million in fiscal 2014.

negative_highlights: Total revenue declined 15% year-over-year, with metal cell sales dropping due to a decline in activity for key surgeons and an outdated system.
Silicon nitride cells decreased by $0.7 million (6%) attributed to restructuring consequences and the loss of several key surgeons during early 2015.
Management declined to provide specific numerical guidance or revenue targets for 2016, citing a lack of established historical patterns.
positive_highlights: Full-year loss narrowed from $32.6M in 2014 to $23.9M primarily due to lower non-cash stock-based compensation and reduced operating expenses.
Adjusted EBITDA improved significantly, moving from a loss of $11.9 million in 2014 to a loss of only $9 million in 2015.
Operational cash burn decreased by $5.5 million (38% reduction) compared to the prior year period.
summary: Full year 2015 revenue was $19.5 million, a decrease of 15% from the prior year driven by lower metal sales and silicon nitride cell declines due to restructuring and surgeon attrition. The company reported an improved financial position with cash burn reduced by $5.5 million compared to the prior year period and total debt obligations decreasing to $17.8 million. Management expressed optimism for 2016 following regulatory clearance of a spinal fusion device, but explicitly declined to provide specific numerical guidance.

negative_highlights: Gross margin declined to 28.5% in Q4 from 37.6% a year ago
Top-line growth not yet robust, with Q4 revenue essentially flat sequentially
Management declined to provide specific revenue growth guidance for 2016
positive_highlights: Revenue increased 99% YoY in Q4 to $18.9 million
Full-year revenue grew to $76.2 million from $13.5 million
Pipeline up 10x since VMware partnership launch
summary: Sphere 3D reported Q4 2015 revenue of $18.9 million, up from $9.5 million a year ago, and full-year revenue of $76.2 million versus $13.5 million in 2014, driven by acquisitions. Gross margin for Q4 was 28.5% (39.1% excluding amortization), down from 37.6% a year ago. Management expects modest growth in Q2 2016 and more significant growth in the second half, citing a ten-fold increase in pipeline since the VMware partnership and continued Microsoft Azure collaboration. They also plan to eliminate 100% of short-term debt.

negative_highlights: Cash of $9.4 million funds operations only through Q3 2016, with management openly evaluating alternatives to raise capital
Full-year revenue of approximately $0.5 million remains immaterial, derived from legacy gene therapy sublicensing, not the phage pipeline
Both active clinical programs are early Phase I safety studies with no efficacy data yet reported
positive_highlights: Full-year operating loss narrowed to $10.2 million from $14.1 million in 2014
R&D expense declined to $4 million from $5.8 million, aided by a $0.5 million Australian government research grant and lower non-clinical spending
Dosed first patient in the Adelaide AB-SA01 chronic rhinosinusitis study in January 2016 and cleared to initiate a second Phase I study with the U.S. Army
summary: AmpliPhi reported FY2015 revenue of approximately $0.5 million, up from $400,000 in 2014, with a full-year operating loss of $10.2 million versus $14.1 million in the prior year. R&D expense fell to $4 million from $5.8 million and G&A to $6.4 million from $6.9 million. Cash and cash equivalents totaled $9.4 million, and management said existing resources are sufficient only through Q3 2016, with the company evaluating options to raise additional capital. The company remains pre-revenue in its phage platform, with two Phase I programs — the Adelaide Staph study and the U.S. Army skin study — expected to complete enrollment in the middle and first half of 2016, respectively, and no formal financial guidance was provided.

negative_highlights: Q4 GAAP net loss widened to $3.8 million from $2.0 million in Q4 2014; full-year net loss was $35.8 million versus $3.7 million in 2014
Q4 adjusted EBITDA deficit was about $2 million, including roughly $850,000 of office-closure expenses and a $795,000 goodwill impairment charge
New membership sales came in below plan, and management stated it failed to achieve its near-term profitability goal in 2015
positive_highlights: Full-year revenue rose 232% to $38.6 million in 2015 from $11.6 million in 2014
Gross margin expanded to 85.6% for 2015 from 81.5% in 2014, and Q4 gross margin was 88.6%
Registered users more than doubled to 7.5 million, up 114% from 3.5 million at year-end 2014
summary: Q4 2015 revenue was $8.2 million, up 4.8% YoY, with gross margin of 88.6%; full-year 2015 revenue was $38.6 million, up 232%, with gross margin of 85.6% versus 81.5% in 2014. Q4 GAAP net loss was $3.8 million versus a $2.0 million loss in Q4 2014, and full-year net loss was $35.8 million versus $3.7 million. Q4 adjusted EBITDA deficit was about $2 million, including roughly $850,000 of office-closure expenses, and management said it was very close to adjusted EBITDA breakeven in February 2016.
