The company entered a $5 million credit facility, is absorbing my Footpath in April 2016, and reported over 80 licenses sold for its new hired product, with a target of 500 active diversity recruitment subscribers within twelve months.

negative_highlights: Life insurance profitability essentially flat at ~$8.4 million versus 2014's record, with Q4 investment income nearly $2 million below Q4 2014
Preneed cemetery sales remained weak through 2015 and require a reorganized sales effort
No cash dividend anticipated in the foreseeable future, with management citing capital intensity and principle-based reserve increases of ~20%
positive_highlights: Pre-tax earnings of $19.8 million, up 59% on a 25% revenue increase — second-best year in company history
Mortgage originations up ~38-40% to just under $3 billion versus ~18% industry growth, with 212% higher segment profitability and 93% retail mix
Death care operating earnings up 38% (excluding REO effects) on flat revenue; retained mortgage servicing rights valued at $12.6 million on ~$1.8 billion originated balance
summary: 2015 revenue rose 25% to drive pre-tax earnings of $19.8 million, up 59% YoY and the company's second-best year ever behind only 2012's $21.35 million. Mortgage funding grew ~38-40% to just under $3 billion (vs. ~18% industry average) with a 212% profit increase, while life insurance profitability was roughly flat at ~$8.4 million and death care operating earnings improved 38% on flat revenue. Total assets grew ~$79 million to just shy of $750 million and stockholders' equity passed $100 million. No numeric guidance was given; management reiterated no cash dividend and framed capital as reserved for growth.

negative_highlights: Revenue fell to $7.3 million from $10.7 million a year earlier, a $3.4 million year-over-year decline
No explicit forward guidance was provided, and the company declined to give a bookings figure for the quarter
Q1 2016 included a $500,000 one-time litigation settlement charge within operating expenses
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA deficit narrowed to $474,000 from $1.4 million a year ago, the best quarter on that basis since the IPO
Gross margin expanded to 88% from 84%, and operating expenses fell $4 million versus Q1 2015
Corporate renewal rates exceed 75%, and PDN Recruits is pacing about 20% ahead of internal plan with an average sale of $712
summary: Q1 2016 revenue fell to $7.3 million from $10.7 million a year earlier, a $3.4 million decline management attributed to planned sales-staff reductions and a focus on profitable revenue. Gross margin rose to 88% from 84%, operating expenses fell $4 million to $9.2 million, and the adjusted EBITDA deficit narrowed to $474,000 from $1.4 million, excluding a $500,000 litigation settlement charge. Net loss per share was $0.10 versus $0.12 a year ago. Management gave no formal guidance but cited favorable corporate renewal rates above 75%, a 20% pacing advantage for PDN Recruits versus internal plan, and an 8% sequential increase in revenue per monetized session early in Q2.

negative_highlights: No updated figures on Microsoft joint marketing progress
Seasonality remains in Europe and government business
CEO acknowledged backing away from prior guidance
positive_highlights: Revenue up to $19.6 million from $18.9 million last quarter
Non-GAAP gross margin up 140 bps to 33.3%
Adjusted EBITDA loss nearly halved to $3.1 million
summary: Sphere 3D reported Q1 2016 revenue of $19.6 million, up from $18.9 million in Q4 2015, with systems revenue up 8% sequentially to $12.2 million. Non-GAAP gross margin expanded to 33.3% from 31.9%, and adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed to $3.1 million from $6.1 million year-over-year. Management highlighted progress with VMware and Microsoft partnerships, including Azure Government validation, but provided no specific guidance and noted that pipeline updates are limited. They expect some sequential growth in the second half of the year.

negative_highlights: Total revenue declined by $400,000 (or 16%) compared to the same period in 2015.
Silicon nitride specific sales decreased due to timing of large initial private label orders last year versus replenishment orders this quarter.
Revenue decrease was attributed partly to continued market pricing pressure and hospital vendor consolidation.
positive_highlights: Debt obligations decreased by approximately $11.4 million (or 47%) from June 2015 levels to under $13 million.
Operational cash burn improved by $1.5 million, representing a 51% reduction compared to the prior year period.
Gross profit margin expanded significantly to 88% excluding inventory provisions due to lower private label sales and medical device excise tax refunds.
summary: First quarter revenue decreased by 12% to $4.2 million and silicon nitride sales fell by 16%, primarily driven by lower private label orders and the implementation of a new commercial sales plan that impacted Q1 results. Net loss narrowed from $5.4M in the prior year period to $3.4M due to significant reductions in operating expenses, while cash burn improved by 51% as debt was reduced significantly.

negative_highlights: Cash of $6.2 million at March 31, 2016 is only sufficient to fund planned operations into the third quarter of 2016, with capital raising alternatives under evaluation
Operating loss widened to $4.5 million from $2.3 million a year earlier, driven by R&D rising to $2.0 million from $1.0 million and G&A rising to $2.6 million from $1.4 million
Sequential single- phage manufacturing capacity may delay C. difficile production by roughly a quarter and constrain trial timelines
positive_highlights: First cohort of the Australian AB-SA01 chronic rhinosinusitis Phase I trial completed dosing with no drug-related adverse events, and the second cohort has begun dosing
AB-PA01 showed in vitro activity against 87.2% of 429 clinical Pseudomonas isolates and activity comparable to meropenem in a mouse lung infection model
Series B convertible preferred stock converted into approximately 1.5 million common shares in April 2016, streamlining the capital structure to about 8.2 million common shares outstanding
summary: AmpliPhi reported Q1 2016 revenue of approximately $0.1 million from legacy sublicensing, flat versus the prior-year period, with R&D expenses rising to $2.0 million from $1.0 million and G&A to $2.6 million from $1.4 million. The operating loss widened to $4.5 million from $2.3 million, while the net loss was $3.1 million, including a $1.4 million non-cash derivative gain. Cash stood at $6.2 million as of March 31, 2016, and management said current resources fund operations only into the third quarter of 2016, with capital raising alternatives under evaluation. On the clinical side, the first cohort of the Australian AB-SA01 Phase I trial completed dosing with no drug-related adverse events, the second cohort began dosing, and management reiterated two Phase I data readouts in Q3 2016.

negative_highlights: Net interest income fell $4.4 million and net interest margin contracted 17 bps to 4.1%
Non-performing assets increased $19 million to $756 million, driven by a $35 million commercial relationship that filed bankruptcy
Net charge-offs rose to $24.7 million (1.11% annualized) from $23.6 million (1.05%), and the allowance to non-performing ratio fell to 39.2% from 41%
positive_highlights: Non-interest expenses fell $3.5 million, with reductions of $1.2 million in occupancy and $1 million in compensation and benefits
30-89 day delinquencies fell 13% to about $212 million from roughly $245 million at March, the lowest level in many years
Tangible book value rose $0.17 to $7.83 and tangible common equity reached 13.55% with Tier 1 at 17.12%
summary: First BanCorp reported Q2 net income of $22 million, or $0.10 per share, down from $23.3 million ($0.11) in Q1 and described as 'very close to consensus.' Net interest income fell $4.4 million as NIM contracted 17 bps to 4.1%, partly offset by a $3.5 million reduction in operating expenses; non-performing assets rose $19 million to $756 million, including a $35 million commercial relationship that filed bankruptcy. Management gave no formal guidance but targets pre-tax pre-provision earnings near $50 million and says the loan pipeline looks stronger for the second half, while flagging elevated prepayments ($51 million in Q2, $145 million YTD) and pending OREO sales.

negative_highlights: Total planted corn acres in China are expected to decline by approximately 10% for the full year, impacting revenue volume.
Net loss per diluted share widened on a GAAP basis from RMB0.52 to RMB0.8 due to timing differences and one-time expenses.
Advances from customers decreased significantly (RMB47.3 million vs RMB128 million prior year) reflecting industry oversupply, low commodity prices, and delayed farmer payments.
positive_highlights: Net revenue grew 12.1% YoY to RMB82.6 million driven by strong sales of corn hybrid Liyu-16 due to yield and disease resistance.
Operating loss decreased on an adjusted basis (excluding one-time stock comp) from RMB13.4 million to RMB10.2 million, a 23.9% reduction.
Inventory levels improved significantly with a decrease of RMB90.6 million due to better forecast demand efforts.
summary: Origin Agritech reported Q3 FY2016 net revenue of RMB82.6 million (up 12.1% YoY) driven by corn hybrid Liyu-16 sales, partially offset by lower rice discount sales and a broader market decline in planted acres expected to impact full-year volume. Operating loss narrowed on an adjusted basis due to one-time stock compensation timing differences but remained at RMB10.2 million excluding these items; the company reported positive operating cash flow of RMB39.6 million (implied from balance sheet changes) and reduced debt by RMB17.5 million, though deferred revenues increased as final returns are pending in Q4.

negative_highlights: Gross margin declined to 29.6% from 30.4% sequentially
Net loss widened to $9.6 million and adjusted EBITDA worsened to negative $4.6 million
Cash fell to $4.3 million after $8.5 million operating cash burn
positive_highlights: Second quarter revenue up 6% YoY to $19.6 million, flat sequentially
V3 GA launch introduced ten appliances with NVIDIA and VMware partnerships
Partner pipeline includes deals from $60,000 to over $1 million
summary: In Q2 FY2016, Sphere 3D reported revenue of $19.6 million, up 6% year-over-year and flat sequentially, with gross margin contracting to 29.6% from 30.4% sequentially. Net loss widened to $9.6 million ($0.19 per share) from $8.1 million in the prior quarter, and adjusted EBITDA was negative $4.6 million, worse than the prior quarter's negative $3.1 million, partly due to FX and one-time G&A. Cash dropped to $4.3 million from $8.7 million in December, with $8.5 million used in operations. Management highlighted the GA launch of the V3 VDI product family, growing POCs and partner pipelines, and the Azure Government validation for SnapCLOUD, while reiterating expectations for a second-half revenue ramp.

negative_highlights: Total revenue was $4 million, a decrease of $800,000 from Q2 2015.
Silicon nitride sales decreased by $500,000 compared to the same period in 2015.
positive_highlights: Operating cash burn decreased to $2.4 million for the six months ended June 30, 2016 compared to $5.3 million in the prior year period.
summary: Second quarter revenue was $4 million, a decrease of $800,000 year-over-year driven by lower private label sales and weaker commercial performance in a key geographic area during the implementation of new sales strategies. Operating cash burn decreased to $2.4 million for the six months ended June 30, 2016 (down from $5.3M), aided by a recent $12.7 million public offering that reduced total debt obligations below $9.5 million.

negative_highlights: Q2 revenue declined 3% year over year to $4.1 million
Technology sales, services, and licensing revenue fell 23% year to date, partly due to the absence of a $150,000 one-time license fee from Q2 2015
Technology management adjusted EBITDA losses increased 222% in Q2 2016
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA turned positive at approximately $112,000 in Q2 2016, the first profitable adjusted EBITDA quarter and positive for the first half
Net loss improved 70% to $318,000, or $0.01 per share, from $1 million, or $0.02 per share, in Q2 2015
Printed products adjusted EBITDA profit rose 93% in Q2 and 85% for the first half, with year-to-date printed product sales up 15%
summary: DSS reported Q2 2016 revenue of $4.1 million, down 3% year over year, but first-half 2016 revenue rose 10% versus the prior year. Adjusted EBITDA turned positive at approximately $112,000, marking the first profitable adjusted EBITDA quarter and a positive first half, with net loss narrowing to about $318,000, or $0.01 per share, a 70% reduction from the $1 million loss in Q2 2015. Operating expenses fell 18% in the quarter and 10% for the first half, while printed product sales rose 15% year to date and technology sales fell 23% due to reduced low-margin hardware sales and the absence of a $150,000 one-time license fee from Q2 2015. The company provided no explicit forward guidance, announced a 1-for-4 reverse stock split effective August 25, and highlighted ongoing investments in AuthentiGuard and other anti-counterfeiting products.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to $3.9 million from a $2.6 million loss from operations in the prior-year period, with G&A rising to $2.5 million from $1.6 million.
Cash of $7.1 million is only sufficient to fund operations into Q4 2016, requiring an additional capital raise in the second half of the year.
Burn rate is expected to expand in 2017 as the company starts CF Phase 1 studies, with revenue remaining flat at approximately $0.1 million.
positive_highlights: AB-SA01 Phase 1 trial in chronic rhinosinusitis showed no drug-related adverse events in the first cohort and the topical skin Phase 1 trial is fully enrolled.
AB-PA01 demonstrated in vitro activity against 87.2% of 429 global clinical isolates and showed activity similar to meropenem in a lung infection model.
Two new patents were granted covering phage-antibiotic sequential treatment for antibiotic-resistant infections, including a Japanese patent for Pseudomonas.
summary: AmpliPhi reported Q2 2016 revenue of approximately $0.1 million, flat year over year, and a net loss of $3.9 million compared to a $2.6 million loss from operations in the prior-year period. R&D rose to $1.2 million and G&A to $2.5 million, driving a higher operational loss, while cash stood at $7.1 million with management stating resources only fund operations into Q4 2016. The company highlighted clinical progress in its AB-SA01 Phase 1 trials and AB-PA01 preclinical data, and expects to complete both Phase 1 studies before year-end, but it must raise additional capital in the second half of 2016 with the burn rate expected to expand in 2017.

negative_highlights: Gross margins contracted year-over-year, decreasing by 0.2% (or 20 basis points) due to reductions in high-margin grinders and service parts.
Art's Way Scientific sales fell 17% for the quarter compared to last year ($910k vs $1.1M).
Year-to-date ag revenue remains down significantly at a loss of 23% or $3.85 million due to cyclical industry headwinds.
positive_highlights: Q3 ag sales increased 2% compared to last year, signaling stabilization in the second half after severe first-half declines.
Income before tax for the agricultural segment improved by $106,000 YTD (from a loss of $83k) due to Vessels discontinuation and beet harvester sales.
Successfully reduced gross inventory levels by 2.1 million dollars or 11%, exceeding the corporate goal.
summary: Q3 revenue grew 2% year-over-year to an implied level where QoQ growth was negative due to a severe ag economy decline in the first half of FY16 (YTD sales down 23%). Gross margins decreased by 0.2 percentage points or 20 basis points, though income before tax improved significantly as Vessels operations were discontinued and beet harvester pass-through items boosted revenue. Management expressed cautious optimism for the remainder of the year while emphasizing a strong balance sheet achieved through debt reduction ($9.9M to $7.6M) and inventory cuts.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined by $1.4M primarily due to lower private label sales and weaker commercial metals sales during an expansion strategy implementation phase.
Silicon nitride ceramic sales decreased by $700,000 compared to the same period in 2015 due to timing of initial orders versus replenishment.
International revenue decreased slightly as costs were offset by lower private label and OEM partner activity.
positive_highlights: Net loss decreased from $10.1M in the prior year period to $4.3M due to lower costs and improved gross profit margins of 82% (excluding inventory provisions).
Operating cash burn for nine months ended September 30, 2016 was $5.3 million, a decrease from $7.1 million in the prior year period.
Total principal debt obligations were reduced to less than $9 million following a successful public offering.
summary: Third quarter revenue decreased by $1.4 million to $3.4 million compared to the prior year period due to lower private label sales and weaker commercial metals sales. Net loss narrowed significantly from $10.1 million in Q3 FY2015 to $4.3 million, driven by improved gross margins of 82% (excluding inventory provisions) and reduced operating expenses following a headcount reduction that saved approximately $2 million annually.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to $43.3 million due to $34.4 million non-cash impairment
Gross margin declined to 28% from 29.6% sequentially
Total cash dropped to $5 million from $8.7 million at end of 2015
positive_highlights: Signed term sheet for $25 million financing with minimal dilution
Disk systems business grew 22% to $35.1 million for nine months
Expanded Microsoft relationship to Managed ISV Program with dedicated support
summary: Sphere 3D reported Q3 FY2016 revenue of $18.5 million, slightly down 1.6% year-over-year and down from $19.6 million in Q2, affected by OEM partner merger activity but with signs of recovery. The company reduced operating expenses by $1.2 million year-over-year and planned to achieve at least $4 million in annual savings, while recording a $34.4 million non-cash impairment charge leading to a net loss of $43.3 million. Management announced a signed term sheet for $25 million financing with minimal dilution, and highlighted late-stage negotiations for large agreements and a new term sheet expected to add $6 million annually to virtualization revenue from early 2017. The tone is upbeat with focus on new partnerships, proof-of-concept conversions, and expected 2017 growth.

negative_highlights: No explicit financial guidance was provided for Q4 or full-year 2016
Investor questioned the lack of press releases and communication, and management acknowledged a 'paucity of information' and that the stock has 'performed awfully'
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA of approximately $397,000, or 8% of sales, marking the second straight quarter of positive adjusted EBITDA and fifth consecutive quarter of improvement

positive_highlights: Adjusted OIBDA rose to $86M from $44M a year ago, including a $30M net RHC appeal benefit and $12M of operational improvement
Consumer revenue up 3% on data growth, with 1,400 paying cable modem net adds plus 3,600 promotional adds
Business revenue up about 6% ex-RHC on education and health care growth; leverage at 4.4x versus 6.5x max with $267M revolver capacity
summary: GCI Q1 adjusted OIBDA roughly doubled to $86M from $44M, helped by a $30M net RHC appeal benefit (lapping a $21M prior-year reserve plus $9M of previously unrecognized revenue) alongside a $12M operational improvement. Revenue details were partial: consumer revenue rose 3% and business revenue about 6% ex-RHC, with 1,400 paying cable modem adds. Management repeatedly stressed the business is defensive and the network held up, but flagged Alaska economic risk with 70,000 jobless claims in six weeks and a higher doubtful-accounts allowance. No explicit revenue or OIBDA guidance was given; CapEx may come in a bit below plan while the Anchorage 5G build stays on track.

negative_highlights: COVID-19-related delays slowed enrollment, though operations are improving
Biomarker data at three months require additional analyses; no maximal dose achieved
Company is reducing spending and may need to extend cash runway based on outcomes
positive_highlights: Statistically significant P1NP increases with EB613 1.5 mg dose at one month
No serious product safety related adverse events or dropouts in Phase 2 trial
Cash runway into Q2 2021, with 2020 operating loss expected at $10 million or less
summary: Entera Bio reported Q1 2020 financial results with a net loss of $2.9 million and cash of $13.3 million, expecting to fund operations into Q2 2021. The key highlight is interim Phase 2 data for EB613 showing statistically significant P1NP increases at the 1.5 mg dose and a dose response, but no maximal dose reached. The company plans to study higher doses within current 2020 spend and expects six-month BMD data in Q3 2020, with Phase 3 targeted for late 2021 or 2022. COVID-19 caused moderate enrollment delays, but operations are resuming.

negative_highlights: Revenue fell 58.5% year-over-year to RMB 272.1 million, with total closed-loop GMV down 46.5% to RMB 17.9 billion
Swung to a net loss of RMB 136.4 million from net income of RMB 14.8 million a year earlier, and non-GAAP net loss was RMB 110 million
Operating expenses rose 62.7% to RMB 189.4 million, including a RMB 32 million increase in doubtful-debt provisions due to slower developer settlements
positive_highlights: Active agents grew 42.8% year-over-year to 218,400, with February active agents up 64.4% on the prior-year period
New primary housing property projects on the platform rose 54.8% year-over-year to 2,400
Gross margin held roughly flat at approximately 18.2% despite the sharp revenue decline
summary: Fangdd reported Q1 FY2020 revenue of RMB 272.1 million, down 58.5% year-over-year, with gross margin roughly flat at 18.2%. The company swung to a net loss of RMB 136.4 million from net income of RMB 14.8 million a year earlier, driven by the COVID-19 disruption, higher operating expenses including RMB 26.4 million in share-based compensation, and a RMB 32 million increase in doubtful-debt provisions. Management guided Q2 revenue to RMB 660–720 million, citing an expected steady recovery after May transaction volumes improved, and noted active agents grew 43% year-over-year to 218,400.

negative_highlights: Wireless subscriber counts remain slightly lower than last year, with revenue growth of 6% coming from higher-value plan mix rather than subscriber adds
Sale of the broadcast television business will slightly reduce GCI business video revenue going forward
No explicit numeric forward guidance was provided, and regulatory visibility on rural subsidies was described as uncertain with an undetermined timeline
positive_highlights: Adjusted OIBDA grew 18% on total revenue growth of 5%, with dollar-for-dollar revenue flow-through driven by data demand and cost containment
Consumer revenue up 5% with 6,500 paying cable modem adds and 4,400 new revenue-generating wireless lines versus Q1
Business revenue up about 6% on growth in government, health and education, with no uptick in bad debt expense and lower health care costs
summary: GCI Liberty reported Q2 FY2020 GCI revenue up 5% YoY and adjusted OIBDA up 18%, with consumer revenue up 5%, business revenue up about 6%, and dollar-for-dollar OIBDA flow-through from data demand and cost containment. Management gave no explicit numeric forward guidance, but noted the Anchorage 5G build is over 85% complete and on track for later this year, and that the pending Liberty Broadband-GCI Liberty merger is expected to close in H1 2021. The quarter also included the July 31 sale of GCI's broadcast television business, which was immaterial to adjusted OIBDA, and 4,400 net new revenue-generating wireless lines versus Q1 with paying cable modem adds of 6,500.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to $1.8M from $0.9M year-over-year
Patient classified as progressive disease per RECIST at 8 weeks
No mention of revenue or EPS versus consensus
positive_highlights: Reduction in target lesions in a refractory Ewing sarcoma patient treated for 6 months
Cash and equivalents up from $3.7M to $7.2M plus $6.2M offering
Plasma drug levels at or above preclinical activity levels
summary: For Q2 FY2020, Salarius Pharmaceuticals reported a net loss of $1.8 million ($0.13 per share), wider than the prior-year loss of $0.9 million ($0.30 per share) due to higher R&D and G&A costs. Cash stood at $7.2 million at quarter-end, supplemented by a $6.2 million offering in August and up to $9.1 million in grant funding, extending runway to late 2021. Early seclidemstat data show dose-proportional plasma levels and a reduction in target lesions in one patient, though RECIST classified the patient as progressive disease. The company plans to expand its Ewing sarcoma trial to include Ewing-related sarcomas, increasing expansion cohort from 20 to 50 patients, with early data expected in the second half of 2021.

negative_highlights: Q2 revenue was RMB737.7 million, well below the prior-year period as implied by the cost of revenue decline, due to COVID-19 impact
Gross margin was only 16.4% in Q2 2020
Net cash used in operating activities was RMB62.2 million in the quarter
positive_highlights: June single-month revenue increased 35.9% year over year to RMB390 million
Non-GAAP net income of RMB11.9 million, with net loss narrowing to RMB14 million
Active agents rose 26.9% year over year to 265,000 and new construction projects increased 24.9% year over year to 2,918
summary: FangDD reported Q2 2020 revenue of RMB737.7 million, down from RMB869.4 million implied by the 15.1% decline in cost of revenue, with gross profit of RMB121 million and a 16.4% gross margin. Net loss was RMB14 million, while non-GAAP net income (excluding share-based compensation) was RMB11.9 million, and net cash used in operating activities was RMB62.2 million. Management guided Q3 2020 revenue to RMB1.05–1.15 billion and said June revenue rose 35.9% year over year to RMB390 million. Active agents grew 26.9% year over year to 265,000, and new construction projects rose 24.9% year over year, even as overall quarterly revenue declined.

negative_highlights: The 1.5 mg group's BMD increase did not reach statistical significance (p=0.08)
Cash on hand only sufficient to support operations into Q2 2021
Six-month biomarker data showed no significant changes versus placebo, differing from injectable PTH profile
positive_highlights: EB613 generated a placebo-adjusted increase in lumbar spine BMD of 2.15% at the 1.5 mg dose
Significant dose-dependent trend in lumbar spine BMD across all EB613 groups
Enrollment back on track at 131 subjects, up from 106, with no serious drug-related adverse events
summary: Entera Bio reported interim six-month data from the Phase 2 trial of EB613, showing a placebo-adjusted 2.15% increase in lumbar spine BMD at the 1.5 mg dose (p=0.08) and a significant dose-dependent trend across all doses. The company added a higher 2.5 mg dose group and discontinued lower doses, aiming to start a Phase 3 trial in late 2021 or 2022. H1 2020 revenue was $94,000 from the Amgen collaboration, with total operating expenses of $6.4 million and cash sufficient into Q2 2021. Enrollment was back on track with 131 subjects, and no serious drug-related adverse events were reported.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened significantly year-over-year due to a nearly doubling of R&D expenses, primarily from increased clinical trial costs.
COVID-19 caused chemotherapy cycles to drop by an average of 20% in the first three months of the pandemic before recovering.
Management explicitly stated no intention for Expanded Access Program (EAP) use as a revenue driver due to cost concerns.
positive_highlights: PROTECTIVE-2 Phase 3 interim analysis met both new primary endpoint (Grade 4 neutropenia prevention) and old criteria, with patient enrollment completed ahead of schedule in July.
DSMB recommended continuation of the DUBLIN-3 non-small cell lung cancer trial based on favorable benefit-risk ratio after reviewing data from over 500 patients.
Company raised $33.9 million via public offering and private placement to strengthen balance sheet for commercialization.
summary: BeyondSpring reported a net loss of $12.8 million for Q2 FY2020 compared to $7.4 million in the prior year period, driven by R&D expenses rising from $5.2M to $11M and SG&A increasing slightly due to pre-launch preparation costs. The company raised gross proceeds of $33.9 million through a public offering and private placement at $13 per share during June and July 2020, bringing cash on hand to $38.1 million as of the quarter end. Management provided no financial guidance but indicated that current resources are sufficient for approximately three quarters while clinical trial expenses decline.

negative_highlights: Phase III study did not achieve its primary objective on negative symptoms (Marder NSFS).
Company has no approved treatment for schizophrenia's negative symptoms and faces significant regulatory uncertainty.
Management indicated they are preparing for potential scenarios including running another Phase III trial if requested by the FDA.
positive_highlights: Net loss narrowed to $8.1 million from $14 million in Q3 last year due to lower R&D and G&A expenses.
Collaborative revenue of $41.2 million recognized for the nine-month period ended Sept 30, 2020.
summary: Minerva Neurosciences reported a net loss of $8.1 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2020, compared to a prior year loss of $14 million, driven by R&D expenses of $4.6 million and G&A expenses of $3.5 million. Collaborative revenue was $41.2 million in the nine months ended Sept 30 due to an opt-out from its Janssen agreement for seltorexant. The company's primary focus remains on a Type C meeting with the FDA scheduled for November 10 regarding roluperidone, following Phase III results that missed their primary objective but showed functional improvements.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to $27.9 million or $0.50 per share from $23.2 million or $0.68 per share a year ago.
SG&A expenses increased to $23.9 million from $15.3 million a year ago, with Q4 expected consistent with Q3, due to launch preparation.
Medicare unrestricted access for INVELTYS remains low at 23%, versus 80% for commercial payers, pressuring gross-to-net.
positive_highlights: INVELTYS net revenue increased to $2.2 million in Q3 2020 from $1.5 million in Q3 2019.
INVELTYS prescriptions rose 84% quarter-over-quarter to approximately 38,000, with branded NRx share at 11.6% as of October 23.
FDA approval of EYSUVIS as the first prescription therapy for note weakness in-term dry eye disease, with launch planned and sales force expansion underway.
summary: Kala reported Q3 2020 INVELTYS net revenue of $2.2 million, up from $1.5 million a year ago, with INVELTYS prescriptions growing 84% quarter-over-quarter to approximately 38,000 and branded NRx share of 11.6%. The company received FDA approval for EYSUVIS for short-term dry eye disease treatment and is expanding its sales force to about 90 representatives by year-end and targeting shipping to wholesalers by end of 2020. Operating loss widened to $25.8 million from $21.6 million a year ago, and net loss was $27.9 million or $0.50 per share. Cash and investments were $159.1 million as of September 30, with runway into at least Q3 2022; revenue guidance for INVELTYS remains uncertain due to COVID-19.

negative_highlights: Consumer video revenues would have been down absent the reclassification of cable advertising sales revenue from the sold broadcast business
Corporate and other expenses were elevated due to costs related to the proposed GCI Liberty/Liberty Broadband combination
Two lawsuits were filed against GCI Liberty over the transaction; one dismissed, the second proceeding with expedited discovery
positive_highlights: Adjusted OIBDA grew 27%, faster than the 11% revenue growth, on data demand, cost containment and lower healthcare costs
Consumer revenue up 8% and business revenue up 13%, with 3,300 sequential cable modem adds and 200 sequential wireless subscriber adds
FCC approved the GCI Liberty/Liberty Broadband combination on October 23, with a special shareholder vote scheduled December 15 and expected close by Q1 2021
summary: GCI revenue rose 11% ($23 million) to roughly $232 million with adjusted OIBDA up 27% ($20 million), driven by data growth, consumer revenue up 8% and business revenue up 13%. Management gave no formal forward guidance beyond expecting full-year CapEx similar to last year and a GCI Liberty/Liberty Broadband deal close by Q1 2021, with FCC approval received and the shareholder vote set for December 15. Cash was $553 million consolidated, $105 million at GCI, with leverage at 3.7x versus a 6.5x max, and the Anchorage 5G build is effectively complete.

negative_highlights: Lumbar spine BMD increase p-value was 0.08, not statistically significant
Cash runway only into Q2 2021, requiring additional capital
Total femur and femoral neck BMD showed no significant treatment effect
positive_highlights: Phase 2 enrollment completed at 161 patients despite pandemic
Six-month interim data showed dose-dependent increase in lumbar spine BMD
No serious drug-related adverse events in the trial
summary: Entera Bio completed enrollment of its Phase 2 EB613 trial with 161 patients despite COVID-19. Six-month interim data showed a mean placebo-adjusted lumbar spine BMD increase of 2.15% (p=0.08) for the 1.5 mg dose, with a dose-dependent trend. The company expects final biomarker data including the new 2.5 mg dose in Q1 2021 and final BMD data in Q2 2021. Cash of $7.1 million at September 30, 2020 is expected to fund operations into Q2 2021, with an anticipated 2020 operating loss of approximately $11 million.

negative_highlights: Q4 2020 revenue guidance of RMB 600-700 million implies a decline from Q3's RMB 819.1 million
Revenue fell 13.6% year-over-year to RMB 819.1 million
Management guided to higher offline costs and no near-term gross profit improvement due to subsidy-competition impact and Centaline joint venture investments
positive_highlights: Gross margin expanded to 23.5% from 21.0% in Q3 2019, despite revenue decline
Net income of RMB 21.9 million improved sequentially from a RMB 14 million net loss in Q2 2020
Active agents on platform exceeded 276,000, up 21.98% year-over-year, with September hitting a record monthly high of 185,000
summary: Fangdd reported Q3 2020 revenue of RMB 819.1 million, down 13.6% year-over-year but up 11% sequentially from RMB 737.7 million. Gross margin expanded to 23.5% from 21.0% a year ago, while net income came in at RMB 21.9 million versus RMB 18.3 million in Q3 2019, aided by share-based compensation of RMB 26.1 million. Management guided Q4 2020 revenue to RMB 600-700 million, below the Q3 level, explicitly citing the decision to stop offering subsidies and commissions advances to agents, which will hurt closed-loop new construction transactions, and warned of higher operating costs from offline investments with the new Centaline joint venture. Active agents exceeded 276,000, up 21.98% YoY, and new construction projects on the platform rose 11.26% YoY to 3,479.

negative_highlights: Q4 net product revenues of only $2.2 million (including just $300,000 from EYSUVIS) and no forward revenue guidance provided
Net loss widened to $31.1 million in Q4 2020 from $22.0 million a year ago; non-GAAP operating loss grew to $24.7 million from $17.6 million
Management said INVELTYS net revenues could continue to be negatively impacted in 2021 due to COVID-19 pressure on elective ocular surgeries, with inability to project timing
positive_highlights: EYSUVIS generated over 2,200 filled prescriptions and more than 550 prescribing eye care professionals in the first six weeks post-launch

EYSUVIS added to Express Scripts' National Preferred, Basic and High Performance Formularies one month after launch; over 1,200 additional prescriptions in the patient hub awaiting prior authorization
INVELTYS Q4 prescriptions of ~41,000 rose 8% sequentially; full-year 2020 prescriptions of ~143,000 rose 11% vs 2019; branded new prescription market share ~11.5%
summary: Kala reported Q4 2020 net product revenues of $2.2 million, up from $1.2 million a year ago, with $1.9 million from INVELTYS and $300,000 from newly launched EYSUVIS. The company gave no financial guidance, citing COVID-19 uncertainty, and expects INVELTYS revenue to remain negatively impacted in 2021; INVELTYS prescriptions rose 8% sequentially in Q4 and 11% for full-year 2020, while EYSUVIS generated over 2,200 filled prescriptions and 550 prescribers in its first six weeks. Cash of $153.5 million at year-end, plus $18.2 million raised in January, is expected to fund operations into at least Q4 2022. EYSUVIS received Express Scripts formulary coverage one month into launch, but the broader surgery market remains depressed and no annual sales guidance was provided.

negative_highlights: Phase 3 study did not meet statistical significance for negative symptoms of schizophrenia
Cash, cash equivalents, and restricted cash declined from $46 million in Dec 2019 to approximately $25.5 million at year-end 2020
$19 million impairment charge taken on IN-process R&D related to MIN-117
positive_highlights: $60 million cash payment received from Royalty Pharma in January 2021
Phase 3 trial showed improvement at both 32mg and 64mg doses despite missing primary endpoint significance
FDA confirmed willingness to consider modified ITT population excluding the outlier site
summary: Minerva Neurosciences reported a significant decrease in R&D expenses to $3.6 million for Q4 FY2020 compared to $19 million the prior year due to an impairment charge taken in December 2019 and trial completions, while cash reserves dropped from $46M to $25.5M before a subsequent $60M royalty payment. Management disclosed that their Phase 3 study did not meet statistical significance for negative symptoms of schizophrenia but remains encouraged by promising signals seen in the open-label extension data expected later this year.

negative_highlights: Interim BMD data from earlier doses showed p=0.08, not statistically significant
No final BMD data yet; expected in Q2 2021
COVID-19 pandemic risks noted but enrollment completed despite challenges
positive_highlights: EB613 Phase 2 met primary endpoint with significant P1NP increase (p<0.04) at 2.5mg
Significant decrease in CTX (p<0.015) suggests potential positive impact on BMD
Cash sufficient to fund operations into Q2 2022
summary: Entera Bio reported positive Phase 2 results for EB613, meeting the primary endpoint with significant increases in bone formation biomarkers and a decrease in resorption marker. The company has sufficient cash into Q2 2022, plans an End of Phase 2 meeting later in 2021, and anticipates starting Phase 3 in 2022. Management expressed confidence in the platform, highlighting multiple partnering opportunities and an ongoing collaboration with Amgen.

negative_highlights: Net loss for full-year 2020 increased to $7.4 million from $6.9 million prior year
Increased R&D costs driven by drug manufacturing costs
Details of clinical data restricted by embargo, limiting transparency
positive_highlights: Completed dose escalation and moved to recommended Phase II dose in three patient populations
Strong clinical signals observed in myxoid liposarcoma and FET-translocated sarcomas
Cash position strengthened to approximately $37 million, described as strongest to date
summary: Salarius Pharmaceuticals reported Q4 2020 net loss of $1.8 million and full-year net loss of $7.4 million, with per-share losses improved year-over-year. Cash reached $37 million after recent financing, strengthening the balance sheet. Seclidemstat completed dose escalation in Ewing sarcoma and is advancing to phase II in three populations, with strong activity signals in myxoid liposarcoma and FET-translocated sarcomas. Management expects readouts around end of Q4 2021 or Q1 2022 and plans multiple new trials by mid-2021.

negative_highlights: Q4 gross margin fell to 8.3% with gross profit of RMB51.8 million, and full-year gross margin was 16.9%
Q4 net loss was RMB92.8 million (non-GAAP net loss RMB68.5 million) and full-year net loss was RMB221.4 million
New-construction closed-loop GMV fell 6.25% sequentially in Q4 and 23.6% year-over-year for full-year 2020 to RMB107.9 billion, with Q4 operating cash outflow of RMB225.9 million
positive_highlights: Active agents on the platform exceeded 283,000 in Q4, up 19% year-over-year, with SaaS-active agents up 30.2% to 557,000 (85% from small/medium agencies)
Closed-loop resale property GMV rose 15.26% year-over-year in 2020 to RMB73.1 billion and 15.4% sequentially in Q4
New property sales SaaS solution launched with pilot partnerships with more than 30 top developers, targeting a 60-80% gross margin model
summary: Q4 2020 revenue fell to RMB622.4 million with gross margin down sharply to 8.3% from typical levels, and net loss was RMB92.8 million (non-GAAP net loss RMB68.5 million). Full-year revenue was RMB2,451.3 million with a 16.9% gross margin, a net loss of RMB221.4 million, and Q4 operating cash outflow of RMB225.9 million. New-construction closed-loop GMV fell 6.25% sequentially in Q4 and 23.6% for the full year to RMB107.9 billion, while resale closed-loop GMV rose 15.26% year-over-year to RMB73.1 billion. Management guided Q1 2021 revenue to RMB270-290 million, guided new-property commission gross margin at 15-20% and new SaaS gross margin at 60-80%, and expects overall gross margin to rise as SaaS penetrates.

negative_highlights: Net loss increased to $17.6M in the quarter due to a significant rise in G&A expenses.
No commercial revenue guidance provided; launch timing is contingent on regulatory approval expected in 2022.
DUBLIN-3 Phase III trial data not yet available for presentation at ASCO, with final results guided only for mid-year.
positive_highlights: Filed NDA with FDA and China NMPA for plinabulin combination therapy to prevent chemotherapy-induced neutropenia (CIN).
Received Breakthrough Therapy Designation from both U.S. and Chinese regulators.
Completed $86.3 million equity financing in Q4 2020, extending cash runway by approximately 15 months.
summary: BeyondSpring reported a net loss of $17.6 million in Q4 FY2020 and $61.0 million for the full year, driven by increased R&D expenses ($8.4M vs $12.6M prior YoQ) and G&A costs ($10.4M vs $2.7M). The company successfully filed NDAs in the U.S. and China for its lead asset plinabulin but provided no financial guidance, noting that commercial launch is contingent on regulatory approval expected in 2022.

negative_highlights: INVELTYS prescriptions fell to ~37,000 in Q1 2021 from ~41,000 in Q4 2020 due to COVID-19 impact on elective ocular procedures
Net loss widened to $30.4 million from $22 million a year ago, with SG&A up to $27.7 million from $15.4 million on EYSUVIS launch costs
Most Q1 EYSUVIS prescriptions required prior authorization and lacked insurance coverage, limiting near-term volume
positive_highlights: EYSUVIS launch traction: >11,600 prescriptions and >2,000 unique prescribers within four months
Commercial coverage for EYSUVIS already at ~43% of lives (69 million) with Express Scripts and Cigna wins
Cash strengthened to $156 million via new $125 million credit facility and $34.7 million ATM proceeds
summary: Kala reported Q1 2021 net product revenues of $3.3 million, split roughly evenly between INVELTYS ($1.63 million, up ~$500k YoY from $1.1 million) and newly launched EYSUVIS ($1.64 million). EYSUVIS launch metrics showed 11,600+ prescriptions from 2,000+ prescribers by late April, ~43% commercial coverage (69 million lives), and ~50% treatment-naive patients. INVELTYS prescriptions fell to ~37,000 from ~41,000 in Q4 2020 due to COVID impacts on elective ocular surgery. Cash was $156 million after a new $125 million credit facility and $34.7 million in ATM proceeds, extending runway to at least two years; guidance was not formally raised.

negative_highlights: No efficacy data released yet; trial outcomes pending ASCO presentation.
Management declined to consider share buyback, focusing capital on R&D.
Company has not pursued CNS indications due to lack of blood-brain barrier penetration.
positive_highlights: Net loss improved to $1.9M from $2.1M YoY, with operating loss down $0.6M.
Completed dose escalation in Ewing sarcoma trial, with data to be presented at ASCO.
Cash of $36.6M expected to fund trials through completion and beyond.
summary: Salarius Pharmaceuticals reported Q1 2021 net loss of $1.9 million ($0.06 per share), improved from $2.1 million ($0.22 per share) in Q1 2020, with operating loss decreased by $0.6 million due to lower G&A costs. The company highlighted progress in its clinical programs for seclidemstat, including completion of dose escalation in a Ewing sarcoma trial with data to be presented at ASCO, and plans for up to three trials in five patient populations. Cash and equivalents stood at $36.6 million at quarter end, which management says is sufficient to fund ongoing trials through completion. Management expressed confidence in the drug's potential in hematologic cancers, citing a differentiated safety profile from other LSD1 inhibitors.

negative_highlights: Net loss of $8.8M reported for the quarter
Potential need for longer double-blind placebo-controlled studies if FDA requests additional Phase 3 trials post-approval data review
positive_highlights: Net loss narrowed significantly to $8.8M from $12.2M due to completion of Phase 3 core study costs
$60 million cash upfront payment received from Royalty Pharma providing non-dilutive funding
Open-label extension data showed continuous improvement in negative symptoms and functioning, described as unique compared to literature
summary: Minerva Neurosciences reported a net loss of $8.8 million for Q1 FY2021 compared to $12.2 million in the prior year quarter, driven by R&D expenses of $3.3 million versus $8.1 million previously due to the completion of Phase 3 core studies. The company received an immediate $60 million cash upfront payment from Royalty Pharma and has potential for up to a further $95 million in milestone payments. Management expressed strong confidence that current data supports submission to the FDA, noting no need for additional placebo-controlled trials at this stage.

negative_highlights: Net loss increased to $2.1 million from $874,000 year-over-year, driven by higher R&D costs.
Cash burn expected to increase for the rest of 2021 as clinical trials ramp up.
Management provided limited near-term milestones; interim data for PCS499 only expected in first half of 2022.
positive_highlights: Cash position of $23 million with $10.2 million raised in Q1, supporting operations through 2023.
First patients being screened for Phase 2b trial of PCS499 (ulcerative NL) this week.
Completed pre-IND meeting for PCS12852 (gastroparesis) and advancing IND preparations.
summary: Processa Pharmaceuticals reported a Q1 2021 net loss of $2.1 million ($0.14 per share), wider than the $874,000 loss in Q1 2020, due to increased R&D expenses for clinical trial preparations. As of March 31, 2021, the company had $23 million in cash and cash equivalents, after raising $10.2 million gross from a private offering. Management highlighted progress in advancing its pipeline, including patient screening for the Phase 2b trial of PCS499 and site initiation for the Phase 1b trial of PCS6422. However, they expect increased cash burn for the rest of the year and provided limited near-term catalysts, with interim data for PCS499 expected in the first half of 2022.

negative_highlights: Gross margin compressed to 11.4% from 18.2% a year earlier, and gross profit fell 32.6% to RMB33.3 million
Net loss of RMB104.8 million and non-GAAP net loss of RMB93 million, with RMB4.8 million net cash used in operating activities
New construction distribution revenue was RMB270 million and management conceded that opting out of advanced commission payments caused a direct decline in new construction revenue growth
positive_highlights: Resale property segment revenue reached RMB18.8 million, up 183.6% sequentially, with closed-loop resale GMV up 81.8% YoY to RMB13.56 billion
Operating expenses fell 25.9% YoY to RMB140.3 million on cost controls and lower share-based compensation
Partnerships through the property cloud SaaS solution reached 24 of China's top 100 developers, including 22 of the top 30
summary: Fangdd reported Q1 2021 revenue up 6.9% YoY to RMB291 million, but gross profit fell 32.6% to RMB33.3 million as gross margin compressed to 11.4% from 18.2% a year earlier, and the net loss remained RMB104.8 million (non-GAAP loss RMB93 million). Resale property GMV rose 81.8% YoY to RMB13.56 billion, yet the core new construction distribution business declined because management chose not to fund advance commission payments, a move it tied directly to lower revenue growth. Q2 2021 guidance was introduced at RMB380-420 million total revenue, with new construction at RMB314-370 million and resale at RMB40-50 million, and management said gross margin should improve sequentially without giving a breakeven target.

negative_highlights: Still reporting operating and net losses ($536K and $546K, respectively)
Cash decreased to $1.2M and debt rose to $7M due to inventory build
Chipset supply challenges expected to continue, including potential price premiums
positive_highlights: Record revenue of $15.0M, up 26% YoY, third consecutive record quarter
Gross margin improved to 34.0%, up 810 bps YoY and 120 bps sequentially
Adjusted EBITDA turned positive at $380,000 on a normalized basis
summary: Minim reported record Q1 2021 revenue of $15.0 million, up 26% year-over-year, with gross margin expanding to 34.0%, up 810 basis points from 25.9% a year ago. The company introduced deferred software subscription revenue of $265,000 and reported an improved operating loss of $536,000, nearing breakeven. Management raised its ASP target to 10-20% for bundled products, announced plans to uplist to NASDAQ, and expects profitability in 2021, while acknowledging chipset supply challenges and managing inventory accordingly.

negative_highlights: Revenue is still minimal ($157k) and operating expenses were $2.5 million in Q1
Full 6-month BMD data not yet released; final results awaited
No disclosed specific partnership milestones or timing for Amgen next step
positive_highlights: EB613 Phase II met primary endpoint: P1NP increase at 2.5mg, p<0.04 vs placebo
Osteocalcin increased (p<0.01) and CTX decreased (p<0.015) at 3 months, indicating bone-building potential
Cash runway extended into Q2 2022; three MTAs signed for platform validation
summary: Entera Bio reported Q1 2021 revenue of $157,000, up from $42,000 a year ago, primarily from Amgen R&D services. The Phase II EB613 trial met its primary endpoint with a significant increase in P1NP biomarker at 2.5mg (p<0.04); osteocalcin and CTX also showed significant favorable changes. The company expects final 6-month BMD data in Q2 2021 and believes Phase III could begin in 2022. Cash is sufficient into Q2 2022, and the company signed three MTAs for potential partnerships.

negative_highlights: Net loss increased slightly from $16.1 million in Q4 FY2020 to $17.0 million in Q1 FY2021
G&A expenses more than doubled year-over-year, rising from $2.9 million to $6.4 million due to pre-commercialization activities and personnel costs
positive_highlights: FDA granted Priority Review for the NDA filing
Phase 3 DUBLIN-3 study achieved two successful interim analyses with final analysis criteria (439 death events) reached as of Q1 FY2021
NCCN guideline updates expanded the addressable market by more than 100% due to inclusion of intermediate-risk patients
summary: BeyondSpring reported Q1 FY2021 R&D expenses of $11.3 million (down from $13.7M) and G&A expenses of $6.4 million (up from $2.9M), resulting in a net loss of $17.0 million compared to $16.1 million last year. The company confirmed it has reached the 439 death events required for final analysis on its Phase 3 DUBLIN-3 study, with top-line data expected mid-year (August/September). Management highlighted FDA priority review status and a PDUFA date of November 30, 2021.

negative_highlights: No financial results or revenue/EPS figures disclosed in the transcript text
Management explicitly stated open-label extension data has NOT yet been discussed with FDA regarding specific feedback points, indicating ongoing regulatory friction
Clinical trial expansion plans are on hold pending a pre-NDA meeting
positive_highlights: Open-label extension data successfully obtained and presented at medical meetings
FDA acknowledged mITT analysis as a valid approach for primary endpoint confidence
summary: Minerva Neurosciences provided a Q&A update on its Phase 3 roluperidone trial and regulatory path for the NDA submission in H1 2022 but did not report specific financial results or guidance changes. Management clarified that open-label extension data has been published to the FDA, confirmed bioequivalence study design with healthy volunteers, and stated they are prioritizing R&D preparation before considering expanded indications.

negative_highlights: EYSUVIS revenue was essentially flat at $1.7M in Q2 vs $1.6M in Q1 despite 93% prescription growth, due to inventory destocking and gross-to-net dynamics
INVELTYS revenue declined $0.2M q/q with a $0.5M product returns reserve tied to COVID-related elective surgery disruptions
GAAP net loss widened to $36.5M ($0.57/share) from $23.3M ($0.42/share) as SG&A rose to $28M from $15.3M
positive_highlights: EYSUVIS prescriptions rose 93% q/q to 15,632, and refills have surpassed 2,500 since launch
Commercial formulary coverage reached ~56% (~96M lives), including OptumRx, with Medicare Part D adding 3.2M lives
62% of Q2 EYSUVIS prescriptions were for patients new to prescription dry eye therapy, supporting first-line use
summary: Q2 FY2021 net product revenue was $3.1M, comprising $1.7M EYSUVIS and $1.4M INVELTYS; EYSUVIS revenue rose only $0.1M q/q despite prescriptions growing 93%, and INVELTYS revenue fell $0.2M q/q due to a $0.5M returns reserve. GAAP net loss widened to $36.5M ($0.57/share) from $23.3M ($0.42/share) on higher SG&A ($28M vs $15.3M). No formal guidance was given; management noted the Salesforce expanded to 105 reps, Medicare Part D coverage for 7% of the Medicare population began July 1, and inventory levels are still normalizing.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to $3.1 million from $1.8 million a year ago
Increased R&D costs drove higher operating loss
No new clinical data readouts in quarter; data expected later this year
positive_highlights: Cash increased to $33.1 million from $7.2 million YoY
Completed dose escalation and initiated enlarged Phase 2 sarcoma trial
Seclidemstat showed single-agent activity in FET-rearranged sarcomas
summary: Salarius Pharmaceuticals reported Q2 FY2021 net loss of $3.1 million, slightly higher than year-ago, but closed the quarter with $33.1 million in cash, up from $7.2 million. The company highlighted clinical progress: completing dose escalation in the advanced solid tumor trial, expanding the sarcoma trial to three subgroups, and initiating a hematologic cancer trial. Data at ASCO showed seclidemstat's single-agent activity in FET-rearranged sarcomas, supporting expansion. Management believes the company is undervalued and funded through 2023.

negative_highlights: CD19 RPM CAR-T program requires further process development before additional patients can be infused, with timeline possibly up to 12 months
COVID-19 restrictions in Taiwan are slowing manufacturing facility operations, adding uncertainty to the CAR-T timeline
Company is seeking broader partnership for the CD19 RPM CAR-T program, signaling a strategic pullback from the asset
positive_highlights: Announced a $50 million venture debt facility with Silicon Valley Bank, with an immediate $25 million drawdown extending cash runway into Q4 2022, beyond expected initial TCR-T clinical data
Completed commissioning of the Houston cGMP clinical production unit and aseptic process validation, enabling the facility for the Phase 1/2 TCR-T library trial
Two patients in the Taiwan CD19 RPM CAR-T trial were dosed and evaluated with no serious adverse safety events reported
summary: Ziopharm ended the first half of 2021 with approximately $76.7 million in cash and announced a $50 million venture debt facility with Silicon Valley Bank, drawing an initial $25 million tranche that extends cash runway into Q4 2022; the tranche was not included in the quarter-end cash balance. The company completed commissioning and aseptic process validation of its Houston cGMP clinical production unit and remains on track to dose the first patient in its Phase 1/2 TCR-T library trial in Q4 2021, with initial readouts expected in the first half of 2022. On the CD19 RPM CAR-T program in Taiwan, two patients were dosed with no serious adverse safety events, but the team concluded further process development is required before infusing additional patients, a delay that may take up to 12 months and is compounded by COVID-19 restrictions in Taiwan.

negative_highlights: Retail segment collected only 81% of billed rent and contributed ~$90,000 of COVID-related rent abatements (~2% of quarterly rents)
Model home acquisitions slowed to six properties for ~$2.9 million in H1 2021 versus 11 acquired in H1 2020, as prices surged
No explicit financial guidance was provided; capital deployment is expected to slip into Q4, and retail remains the most challenged segment
positive_highlights: Core FFO rose to $1.7 million in H1 2021 from $1.5 million in H1 2020, aided by elimination of expensive mezzanine debt and lower interest expense
Collected 97% of billed consolidated rent, with Model Homes and Office Properties at 100% of budgeted revenue; these two segments were 83% of quarterly rents
Closed $23 million of preferred gross proceeds in June and $10 million of common/warrant gross proceeds in July, plus sold 32 model homes for about $15.1 million with over $2 million of gain in H1
summary: Presidio Property Trust reported Q2 2021 core FFO of $1.7 million for the first half versus $1.5 million a year earlier, with 97% of billed rent collected company-wide and 100% collection in its Model Homes and Office segments, which accounted for 83% of quarterly rents. The company raised $23 million gross via a new preferred series in June and an additional $10 million gross via common shares and warrants in July, and sold four properties totaling $33 million of transaction volume in the first half; 32 model homes were sold for roughly $15.1 million with over $2 million of gain recognized. Management did not provide formal financial guidance but said it expects to deploy recently raised capital into acquisitions through the remainder of Q3 and into Q4, citing one property in escrow and an active pipeline. Retail remained the weakest segment with 81% of billed rent collected, and the company noted a $200 million S-3 shelf that it may access over time.

negative_highlights: Preliminary net loss widened to $8.5 million, or $0.68 per share, from $3.3 million, or $0.37 per share, a year earlier
Development and commercialization expenditure climbed to $3.8 million from $0.6 million, and employee benefits expense rose to $1.7 million from $1.1 million
Stated cash runway extends only into the fourth calendar quarter of 2022 with no product revenue reported
positive_highlights: Cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities rose to approximately $12.7 million as of June 30, 2021 from about $430,000 a year earlier, after roughly $19.7 million in net IPO proceeds
Awarded a $4.7 million grant from the Australian Federal Government to fund a high-tech biosensor manufacturing facility
Voice-of-customer survey showed 9 of 10 patients responded positively to the biosensor platform and 7 of 10 were seriously interested in purchasing
summary: GBS reported a FY2021 preliminary net loss of $8.5 million, or $0.68 per share, widening from a $3.3 million loss ($0.37 per share) a year earlier, driven by rising development and commercialization spend ($3.8 million versus $0.6 million). Cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities were approximately $12.7 million as of June 30, 2021, versus about $430,000 a year earlier, following $19.7 million in net IPO proceeds, and management said resources fund operations into the fourth calendar quarter of 2022. The company is pre-revenue with no product sales, and management outlined FY2022 milestones including an FDA EUA submission for the SARS-CoV-2 antibody test, clinical protocols for the Saliva Glucose Biosensor, and completion of a biosensor manufacturing facility (awarded a $4.7 million Australian government grant) expected in the first half of next year.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened significantly to $3.2 million from $733,000 year-over-year
Only 2 patients enrolled in PCS499 Phase 2B, with 10 pre-screened patients not qualifying
Clinical trial costs expected to continue increasing for remainder of year
positive_highlights: In-licensed PCS3117 with orphan designation for pancreatic cancer and patent life to 2036
PCS6422 enrolled first patient in Phase 1B
PCS499 Phase 2B study underway with sites being initiated
summary: Processa Pharmaceuticals reported Q2 2021 net loss of $3.2 million or $0.20 per share, wider than the prior-year loss of $733,000, driven by clinical trial costs and the in-licensing of PCS3117. R&D expenses rose to $1.6 million from $427,000, and G&A expenses increased to $1.3 million. The company had $20.8 million in cash and cash equivalents. Pipeline progress includes 2 patients enrolled in the PCS499 Phase 2B trial, first patient enrolled in PCS6422 Phase 1B, IND planned for PCS12852 by end of September, and PCS3117 biomarker development underway. Management expects costs to increase as trials expand and noted clinical trial costs in the $3-5 million range per study.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to RMB139 million from RMB104.8 million in Q1, with non-GAAP net loss of RMB127.9 million.
Provision for doubtful accounts surged to RMB79.1 million from RMB20 million in Q1 due to developers' weakened financial conditions.
Q3 revenue guidance of RMB250-300 million implies a sharp sequential decline from RMB401.4 million, citing COVID-19 and market uncertainty.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 37.9% sequentially to RMB401.4 million, driven by new property transaction services up 32.1% and resale property revenue up 114.4%.
Gross margin expanded 420 basis points sequentially to 15.6% from 11.4%.
Active agents on platform increased 13% sequentially to 250,000, and new property GMV rose 15.7% to RMB18.9 billion.
summary: Fangdd reported Q2 FY2021 revenue of RMB401.4 million, up 37.9% sequentially, with gross margin expanding to 15.6% from 11.4% in Q1. However, the company posted a net loss of RMB139 million (widening from RMB104.8 million in Q1) and a non-GAAP net loss of RMB127.9 million, largely due to a RMB79.1 million provision for doubtful accounts from developers with weakened financial conditions. Management guided Q3 revenue to RMB250-300 million, a significant sequential decline, citing COVID-19 impact on core markets and near-term business uncertainty. The quarter was also marked by a shift away from subsidy-driven competition toward margin focus, but the large bad debt reserve and weak guidance overshadowed top-line and margin gains.

negative_highlights: No revenue or earnings figures reported as the company remains pre-commercial
Full safety and efficacy data for patients 10-12 withheld due to ESMO embargo, limiting disclosure
positive_highlights: Approximately $40 million in cash provides runway for the next couple of years
Blast reductions of 33%, 61%, 63%, and 50% observed in four of twelve patients treated with GTB-3550
Dose escalation continuing to 200 mcg with no dose-limiting toxicities observed to date
summary: GT Biopharma held its first earnings call as a public company, reporting no revenue or EPS figures as a clinical-stage biotech. Management highlighted that 12 patients have been treated in the GTB-3550 Phase I trial, with dose escalation continuing to 200 mcg next week, and reported blast reductions of 33%, 61%, 63%, and 50% in four patients. The company has approximately $40 million in cash to fund operations for the next couple of years, was added to the Russell 2000, and expects to present updated safety and efficacy data at ESMO in September, with final Phase I data expected later this fall.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA was negative $300K vs positive $300K in Q1
Incurred $500K one-time scrap expense and higher component/airfreight costs
Chipset supply challenges expected to persist through at least Q2 2022
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 45% YoY, accelerating from 26% in Q1
Gross margin exceeded 30%, showing significant year-over-year improvement
Cash flow from operations improved to negative $400K from negative $5M in Q1
summary: Minim reported Q2 FY2021 revenue growth of 45% YoY, up from 26% in Q1, with gross margin over 30% and adjusted EBITDA of negative $300K (including a one-time $500K scrap charge). Deferred revenue ratio rose to 7% from 2%, and cash flow from operations improved to negative $400K from negative $5M. Management raised $22.7M in a secondary offering and sold trademark assets for $4M, and expects chipset supply challenges to persist through at least Q2 2022 but sees minimal operational impact.

negative_highlights: Management explicitly stated that regulatory environments 'do not support' their e-commerce plans at scale, effectively ruling out a major revenue stream.
The company terminated its relationship with Valqari for contract manufacturing services because it was deemed 'not accretive to our growth strategy'.
Revenue of $1.9 million is largely attributed to new contributions from MicaSense and Measure acquisitions rather than organic business expansion.
positive_highlights: Net loss declined to $4.7 million compared to a net loss of $10.3 million in the prior year period due to lower non-cash charges associated with financing activities.
Cash position strengthened to $39.2 million as of June 30, 2021 from approximately $23.9 million at the end of 2020 following capital raised via an ATM offering totaling $28.6 million in Q2.
summary: AgEagle reported Q2 FY2021 revenue of approximately $1.9 million and a net loss of $4.7 million ($0.07 per share), driven by acquisitions made earlier in the year rather than organic growth from legacy operations. Management terminated its relationship with Valqari for contract manufacturing services, dismissed shareholder lawsuits as frivolous, and raised concerns that regulatory environments abroad do not support their e-commerce plans at scale.

negative_highlights: Operating loss expected to be approximately $13 million in 2021.
Financial expenses increased $9.9 million due to higher warrant fair value.
Only $266,000 in revenues, reliant on Amgen collaboration.
positive_highlights: EB613 Phase 2 met primary and key secondary endpoints, with lumbar spine BMD increased 3.78% vs placebo (p<0.008).
Cash balance strengthened to $28.1 million, funding operations into Q4 2022.
Signed material transfer agreements with three companies for platform feasibility.
summary: Entera Bio reported H1 2021 revenues of $266,000 (up from $94,000) from Amgen R&D services, with total operating expenses of $5.2 million. The company highlighted positive Phase 2 results for EB613, an oral PTH for osteoporosis, which met primary and key secondary endpoints with significant BMD increases. Cash stood at $28.1 million as of August 8, 2021, sufficient into Q4 2022, and management expects an end-of-Phase 2 meeting with FDA in H2 2021 and potential partnerships by year-end.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to $19.3 million from $12.8 million year-over-year.
G&A expenses surged by $6.4 million compared to the prior quarter due to pre-commercialization costs and stock-based compensation.
positive_highlights: DUBLIN-3 trial data showed significant improvement in overall survival for plinabulin plus docetaxel versus docetaxel alone.
summary: BeyondSpring reported a net loss of $19.3 million in Q2 FY2021 compared to $12.8 million the prior year, driven by R&D expenses rising to $11.3 million and G&A increasing significantly due to pre-commercialization activities for plinabulin. The company highlighted positive top-line data from its DUBLIN-3 trial showing improved overall survival in non-small cell lung cancer but noted that detailed subset analyses are pending the ESMO presentation on September 20. Management confirmed a strategic partnership with Hengrui involving an upfront payment of approximately $30 million and potential milestones up to $170 million, providing additional cash runway.

In Q3 FY2021, Minim reported net revenue of $15.0 million, up 25% year-over-year, but gross margin declined to 29.9% from 32.2% a year ago due to component inflation. Net income was $1.7 million, helped by a one-time $4 million Zoom trademark sale. Management acknowledged margin pressure and expects cost increases to persist, prompting a 6% average price increase on 60% of products. The company raised capital via secondary offering and expanded its credit facility to fund inventory and growth initiatives. Full-year guidance was not provided, but Q4 shipments of new products and expected growth in deferred revenue suggest an optimistic outlook.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to $3.7 million from $1.7 million in the prior year period
No CPRIT grant revenue recognized in Q3 2021 versus $1.4 million in prior year
Limited clinical data reported; no new efficacy results in the quarter
positive_highlights: Cash position improved significantly from $9.6 million to $31.9 million year-over-year
Completed enrollment in Ewing sarcoma safety lead-in cohort, with Phase 2 dose expected early 2022
Increased sarcoma trial sites from 8 to 13, expected to accelerate patient enrollment
summary: Salarius Pharmaceuticals reported a Q3 2021 net loss of $3.7 million ($0.08 per share), compared to a net loss of $1.7 million ($0.10 per share) last year. Operating losses increased due to the absence of CPRIT grant income ($1.4 million in prior year) and higher R&D and G&A costs. Cash and cash equivalents totaled $31.9 million as of September 30, 2021, up from $9.6 million a year ago, with management stating this is sufficient to fund operations through 2022 and beyond. Clinical progress included completing enrollment in the Ewing sarcoma safety lead-in cohort, adding 5 new trial sites (bringing total to 13), and establishing a research partnership with Fox Chase Cancer Center. Potential clinical data readouts are expected later this year and throughout 2022.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to $22.7 million ($0.11 per share) from $20.3 million ($0.10 per share) in Q3 2020.
Total operating expenses rose 12% year over year to $22.7 million, with G&A up from $6.4 million to $8.2 million.
First patient dosing in the TCR-T library study remains contingent on FDA IND clearance and is not expected before H1 2022.
positive_highlights: Cash and cash equivalents of $91.7 million as of September 30, 2021, with runway expected into Q2 2023.
Completed engineering and process qualification runs at the in-house CGMP clinical production unit in October, supporting planned first patient dosing in H1 2022.
Expected forward cash burn of less than $15 million per quarter following restructuring, reducing the expense trajectory.
summary: ZIOPHARM reported a Q3 2021 net loss of $22.7 million, or $0.11 per share, versus a $20.3 million loss ($0.10 per share) a year earlier, with total operating expenses up 12% to $22.7 million and R&D up 4% to $14.5 million. Cash and equivalents were $91.7 million at September 30, 2021, and management guided to a cash runway into Q2 2023 with quarterly burn expected below $15 million, down from recent levels. The company is awaiting FDA clearance of its TCR-T library IND and completed engineering/process qualification runs at its in-house CGMP facility in October, reiterating first patient dosing in the first half of 2022. The quarter included a strategic restructuring and operational progress, but no new clinical data or financial outperformance versus prior periods.

negative_highlights: FDA denied request for pre-NDA meeting, proposing a Type C guidance meeting instead.
Net loss widened to $9.2 million due to non-cash interest expense of $1.7 million related to the Royalty Pharma royalty stream sale.
positive_highlights: Bioequivalence study results met key pharmacokinetic objectives (AUCinf and AUCs) for roluperidone formulations.
summary: Minerva Neurosciences reported a net loss of $9.2 million for Q3 FY2021 compared to an $8.1 million loss in the prior year period, driven by non-cash interest expense on its royalty agreement with Royalty Pharma and lower R&D spending following Phase III trial completion. Management maintained guidance for NDA submission in H1 2022 despite FDA denial of a pre-NDA meeting request, which was downgraded to a Type C discussion focused primarily on monotherapy data.

negative_highlights: No revenue was reported for the quarter as the company remains pre-revenue in its clinical stage.
The registrational trial design is still being finalized with the FDA, with timing dependent on regulatory discussions.
positive_highlights: Phase Ib/IIa study of ATYR1923 showed dose-dependent improvement in lung function (FVC) with 2.8% to 3.3% gains at higher doses versus placebo.
Patients treated with ATYR1923 achieved an average steroid reduction of 58% from baseline, with three patients completely tapering off steroids.
Company raised $80.6 million in net proceeds via a public offering in September 2021, strengthening its balance sheet.
summary: aTyr Pharma reported Q3 FY2021 financial results with $116.4 million in cash, cash equivalents, and investments as of September 30, 2021, following the successful completion of a Phase Ib/IIa study for ATYR1923 in pulmonary sarcoidosis. The company demonstrated clinical proof-of-concept with significant steroid reduction (up to 58% from baseline) and lung function improvements compared to placebo, supporting advancement to a registrational trial next year. R&D expenses were $5.1 million and G&A expenses were $2.6 million for the quarter.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened significantly to $18.4 million from $10.4 million in Q3 FY2020.
R&D expenses increased substantially to $15.3 million, primarily due to a $5.5 million milestone fee and Phase III trial costs.
G&A expenses rose to $3.2 million from $0.6 million in the prior year quarter.
positive_highlights: MANTRA-2 basket study is now active and open to enrollment across approximately ten sites in the U.S.
Preclinical models demonstrated robust anti-tumor activity of milademetan in patient-derived organoids and graphs, supporting the rationale for the new trial strategy.
Dedifferentiated liposarcoma shows high MDM2 amplification (approx. 17 copies per cell) with a very low p53 mutation rate (approx. 2%), validating the target population.
summary: Rain Therapeutics reported a net loss of $18.4 million for Q3 FY2021, compared to a loss of $10.4 million in the prior year quarter, driven by R&D expenses of $15.3 million and G&A expenses of $3.2 million. The company provided no financial guidance but projected full-year 2021 operating spend between $50M-$60M and a year-end cash balance of $137M-$147M. Clinically, the company announced the reprioritization of its Phase III MANTRA-3 study from intimal sarcoma to Merkel cell carcinoma based on new preclinical data and market size.

negative_highlights: GAAP gross margin declined 12 percentage points to 20.2% from 32.2% in Q3 2020.
Operating loss widened 57% to $443,000 and adjusted net loss widened 95% year-over-year.
Supply-chain disruptions delayed shipments into Q4 2021 and possibly Q1 2022, with no specific dollar impact disclosed.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 127% year-over-year to $3.7 million and 106% year-to-date to $10.6 million.
Bookings were approximately $5.6 million, the second highest in company history and up 509% from Q2 2021.
Excluding non-recurring 2020 items, gross margin improved by two percentage points year-over-year.
summary: Surna Inc. reported Q3 2021 revenue of $3.7 million, up 127% year-over-year, and a GAAP gross margin of 20.2% versus 32.2% in Q3 2020, which management said was flat-to-up 2 points excluding non-recurring 2020 benefits. Bookings were approximately $5.6 million, the second highest in company history and up 509% sequentially, though the quarter included $500,000 of cancellations, and supply-chain delays pushed some shipments into Q4 2021 and possibly Q1 2022. The company posted a net loss of $408,000 and used $1.8 million in operating cash flow year-to-date; no forward revenue or earnings guidance was given beyond pursuing an uplisting and a capital raise.

negative_highlights: SCYNERGIA study enrollment slower than projected due to COVID-19, timelines extended into 2022
First partial launch quarter had 1,006 total prescriptions, but this was in line with expectations
Patient education and activation efforts not starting until early next year
positive_highlights: 1,100 BREXAFEMME prescriptions in October alone, showing upward trajectory
Coverage of BREXAFEMME grew to over 30% of commercial lives and still growing
IV formulation Phase 1 showed no serious adverse events; tolerability clearly better than previous formulations
summary: SCYNEXIS reported Q3 2021 as the first quarter after FDA approval of BREXAFEMME in June and the launch began in August. In the partial launch quarter, IQVIA data showed 1,006 total prescriptions, with nearly 700 in September, and 1,100 in October alone, indicating a promising upward trajectory. Payer coverage reached over 30% of commercial lives, and the company is on track for its Tier 3 coverage goal. The CANDLE Phase 3 trial for prevention of recurrent VVC is on target for topline results in early Q2 2022, with a potential approval by end of 2022. The IV formulation Phase 1 showed improved tolerability with no serious adverse events. However, the SCYNERGIA trial for invasive pulmonary aspergillosis experienced slower enrollment due to COVID-19, with timelines extended into 2022.

negative_highlights: Same-store occupancy was down a few percent in 2021 compared to 2020, which management called transitory.
Industrial property rent collections were 81% of budgeted rents due to the timing of tenant turnover.

Model Home acquisitions slowed sharply to 6 properties for about $2.9 million in the first three quarters of 2021, versus 25 properties in the same period of 2020, as builders struggled with labor and material shortages.
