positive_highlights: Core FFO rose 8% to $1.67 million for the first three quarters of 2021 versus $1.55 million in the same period of 2020, aided by lower interest expense.
Model Homes collected 100% of billed rents in the first three quarters, and Model Homes plus Office Properties collected 197% of budgeted revenues, together representing 94% of quarterly rents.
The company sold 39 Model Homes for approximately $19 million in the first three quarters, recognizing a gain of about $2.9 million, and has repurchased shares under a $10 million buyback program.
summary: Presidio Property Trust reported core FFO of $1.67 million for the first three quarters of 2021, up 8% from $1.55 million in the prior-year period, with consolidated rent collections of 96% for Q3 2021. Model Homes and Office Properties both collected 197% of budgeted rents, while industrial lagged at 81% due to tenant turnover; COVID-related rent abatements were about $90,000, or 2% of billed rents. The company sold four properties for $33 million in 2021, acquired a net lease daycare property in Houston, and repurchased some shares under a new $10 million plan. Management said it expects same-store occupancy to improve from a few-percent decline versus 2020, called the industrial weakness transitory, and said it expects to deploy nearly all its cash into acquisitions by the next call; no explicit numeric guidance was given.

negative_highlights: Full-year guidance lowered on all key metrics, including paid subscribers to 970,000 from 1.08 million and GAAP revenue to $540 million from $560 million.
Billings decreased 8% to $238.1 million from $149.9 million in the prior-year quarter (as reported).
Adjusted cash flow from operations fell to $34.7 million from $55.0 million, and the adjusted cash flow margin declined to 25.2% from 36.7%.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 43.1% YoY to $140.7 million from $98.1 million.
October landing page visits rose 17.5% over the June-September average, with early improvement in paid subscriber additions and lower acquisition costs.
Board authorized a $35 million share repurchase program and the company closed a $150 million revolving credit facility.
summary: Q3 2021 revenue rose 43.1% YoY to $140.7 million, but billings fell 8% to $238.1 million versus a prior figure of $149.9 million (as stated in the transcript), and paid subscribers declined by 30,000 sequentially to 965,000. Management lowered full-year 2021 guidance: paid subscribers to 970,000 from 1.08 million, billings to $740 million from $750 million, adjusted cash flow from operations to $210 million from $212 million, and GAAP revenue to $540 million from $560 million. Adjusted cash flow from operations fell to $34.7 million from $55.0 million a year ago, and net loss widened to $366.2 million on a $339.1 million increase in stock-based compensation. Management cited a travel-and-leisure-driven engagement slowdown persisting about five months, but pointed to October landing page visits up 17.5% and an uptick in new paid subscriber additions as early signs of normalization.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to $1.4 million from $1.0 million in the prior-year period due to higher development and commercialization expenditure
Government support income fell to zero from $55,427 a year earlier
CEO transition announced, with an interim CEO and a permanent search expected to take three to six months
positive_highlights: Awarded a US$4.7 million non-dilutive manufacturing grant from the Australian government to fund a biosensor manufacturing facility
Cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities of approximately $12.6 million, essentially flat versus $12.57 million at June 30, 2021, with runway stated into the first half of 2023
Saliva SARS-CoV-2 antibody test showed comparable specificity and sensitivity to commercially available tests in a preliminary Wyss Institute study, with sample-to-answer time under 10 minutes
summary: GBS Inc. reported a preliminary Q1 FY2022 net loss of $1.4 million, or $0.10 per share, compared with a net loss of $1.0 million, or $0.12 per share, in the prior-year period, with the increased loss attributed to accelerated development and commercialization spending. Government support income fell to zero from $55,427 a year earlier. Cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities were roughly flat at $12.6 million versus $12.57 million at June 30, 2021, and management said resources should cover expenses into the first half of 2023. Leadership changes were announced, with the CEO transitioning to President of Asia Pac and an interim CEO in place while a permanent search proceeds.

negative_highlights: 6422 DPD inhibition was transient, not lasting seven days after a single dose
499 Phase 2b enrollment slower than expected, interim analysis pushed to Q1 2022
Net loss increased $1.9 million on an acquisition-adjusted basis due to higher clinical costs
positive_highlights: Interim 6422 data showed at least 50x higher potency than capecitabine, up to 100x in some patients
Cash increased $3.7 million in nine months, ending at $19.1 million
Received FDA study-to-proceed letter for 12852 Phase 2a
summary: Processa Pharmaceuticals reported Q3 2021 net loss of $3 million ($0.19 per share), similar to prior year; R&D costs rose to $1.7 million due to clinical trial progress. Cash was $19.1 million with $3.7 million increase in first nine months. Interim Phase 1b data for next-generation capecitabine showed high potency but short-lived DPD inhibition, leading to protocol modification; enrollment for 499 Phase 2b is slower than expected, with interim analysis expected in Q1 2022. Management maintains timelines for Phase 3 and approval.

negative_highlights: Clinical development of lead asset MarzAA stopped; Crimson-1 could slip to late 2023, which management called a financing hurdle it could not overcome without a partner
Enrollment described as very slow due to pandemic logistics and competition for subjects from approved and late-stage prophylaxis therapy
Company pivots from late-stage hemophilia to earlier-stage complement, with MarzAA/DalcA now being explored for licensing or sale and no near-term revenue driver
positive_highlights: Cash of $64.5 million as of September 30, 2021 supports continued operations
Halting MarzAA development expected to cut burn by approximately 40% and extend runway to about one year
First 2 complement factor I-deficient subjects enrolled in the ConFIdence natural history study; IND for CB 4332 planned for 2022
summary: Catalyst Biosciences used its Q3 FY2021 call to announce it is halting clinical development of MarzAA and pivoting to an earlier-stage complement/protease platform, citing very slow enrollment and estimating Crimson-1 could not complete until late 2023. The company reported cash of $64.5 million as of September 30, 2021, and guided to a roughly 40% reduction in burn and approximately one year of runway. It plans to submit an IND for CB 4332 in 2022 and initiate first-in-human dosing, while seeking a partner or buyer for MarzAA and DalcA. No revenue, EPS, or conventional financial guidance was reported; the prior expectation of a MarzAA submission by year-end and pivotal data in 2022 was effectively abandoned.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined year-over-year to $219k due to consolidation of Birmingham center expenses ($515k) and limited Atlanta operations
GAAP net loss increased significantly to $2.2 million driven by pre-revenue startup labor costs at new centers
Deferred license revenue recognition timing remains uncertain with approximately $3 million outstanding
positive_highlights: Regained full rights to INVOcell distribution after terminating Ferring agreement
Birmingham center ran ahead of plan in first month with strong patient flow and pregnancy rates
International expansion progressing with centers operational or under development in Mexico, Malaysia, Pakistan, Spain, Africa
summary: Revenue for the quarter totaled $219,000 compared to $336,000 in the prior year period, while GAAP net loss widened to $2.2 million from $1.8 million last year due to startup costs at two new INVO centers (Birmingham and Atlanta). The company terminated its Ferring agreement but expressed confidence in regaining control of the U.S. market with three operating centers and a fourth planned for Q1 2022, anticipating breakeven by early 2022.

negative_highlights: Gross profit margin contracted by 400 bps to 39% from 43%
Net loss widened significantly to $3.8 million ($0.05/share) compared to a prior year net loss of only $575,000
Management acknowledged ongoing supply chain constraints impacting delivery schedules
positive_highlights: Total revenues climbed 169% YoY to approximately $2.0 million
Cash position increased significantly to approximately $32.2 million from $23.9 million in the prior year period
Successful integration of senseFly and Measure Ground Control with new product launches including RedEdge-P
summary: AgEagle reported Q3 FY2021 total revenues of approximately $2.0 million, representing a 169% increase year-over-year driven by acquisitions and new product launches like the RedEdge-P sensor. Gross profit margin decreased to 39% from 43% in the prior period due to shifts in product mix toward lower-margin acquired entities. The company reported a net loss of $0.05 per share compared to a smaller loss of $0.01 last year, while cash position strengthened to $32.2 million following capital raises.

negative_highlights: EYSUVIS launch described as slower than expected, with only about half of prescriptions being filled at the pharmacy due to lack of insurance coverage
INVELTYS prescriptions fell to ~37,410 from 41,103 QoQ, with CVS moving to a generic ophthalmic surgical steroid formulary and removing INVELTYS coverage
EYSUVIS revenue grew only ~10% QoQ versus 19% volume growth, as co-pay assistance pressured gross-to-net
positive_highlights: EYSUVIS prescriptions rose 19% QoQ to 18,537 and retail prescriptions grew 94% QoQ to 3,115
EYSUVIS refills increased 94% in Q3 versus Q2, and about two-thirds of Q3 prescriptions were for patients new to prescription dry eye therapy
Commercial coverage reached ~60% of lives after adding 4.5 million covered lives in Q3, with cash runway guided into Q2 2023
summary: Kala reported Q3 2021 EYSUVIS prescriptions of 18,537, up 19% QoQ, while EYSUVIS revenues rose only ~10% QoQ as more scripts filled through co-pay assistance. INVELTYS prescriptions fell to ~37,410 from 41,103 in Q2 and were hit by removal from the CVS formulary. Management called the EYSUVIS ramp 'slower than expected,' with about half of prescriptions rejected for lack of coverage (60% commercial, 10% Medicare Part D), and announced a patient-facing digital DTC campaign by year-end. Separately, Kala acquired Combangio, adding KPI-012, a clinical-stage secretome therapy for persistent corneal epithelial defect, with an IND planned for 3Q next year. Cash runway was guided into Q2 2023, including some revenue growth and flat OpEx in 2022 versus 2021.

negative_highlights: Revenue fell 57.8% sequentially to RMB169.2 million from RMB401.4 million
Gross margin contracted sharply to 3.5% from 15.6% in Q2
Q4 revenue guidance of RMB138-150 million implies further sequential decline, with management citing 'great uncertainty'
positive_highlights: SaaS solution revenue rose 38.8% sequentially to RMB3.2 million from RMB2.3 million
Net cash used in operating activities improved to RMB12.8 million from RMB53 million in Q2 2021
Cash, restricted cash and note weakness in-term investments stood at RMB632.9 million with unutilized bank facilities of RMB180 million
summary: Revenue fell 57.8% sequentially to RMB169.2 million from RMB401.4 million in Q2 2021, driven by a 48.5% sequential decline in closed-loop GMV. Gross margin collapsed to 3.5% from 15.6%, and G&A surged to RMB267.5 million due to RMB201.9 million in impairment provisions, producing a net loss of RMB355 million (RMB4.13 per ADS) versus a RMB139 million loss in Q2. Management guided Q4 revenue to RMB138-150 million, citing continued market downturn and 'great uncertainty,' while making strategic cuts to the new property distribution and Yuancui resale businesses.

negative_highlights: Gross margin was only 13.4%, and management indicated higher margins would only come once the Highsharp joint venture is set up
Only 880 machines (approximately 1.3% of total orders) were recognized as revenue in Q3, leaving substantial execution and delivery risk
No formal financial guidance was provided for Q4 2021 or 2022, and R&D investment in crypto mining machines had not yet begun as of September 30, 2021
positive_highlights: Revenue of $5.34 million versus minimal prior-year revenue, with gross profit of $0.71 million compared to $21,138 in Q3 2020
Net income of $0.2 million, turning profitable from a $0.32 million net loss in the prior-year quarter
Secured purchase order for 67,500 crypto mining machines, far exceeding initial expectations
summary: AGM Group reported Q3 2021 revenue of $5.34 million, driven by its new ASIC crypto mining machine business, with total computing power of 79,200 TH/s versus nil a year earlier. Gross profit was $0.71 million at a 13.4% gross margin, operating income was $0.37 million, and net income was $0.2 million, reversing a $0.32 million net loss in Q3 2020. The company has secured a purchase order for 67,500 mining machines but recognized revenue on only 880 units (about 1.3% of orders) in the quarter, with the remainder to be delivered in future periods. No explicit financial guidance was provided for Q4 or 2022, though management said Q4 will focus on fulfilling deliveries and expects the semiconductor supply crunch to ease in mid-2022.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to $3.46 million in Q2 FY2022 from $1.9 million in the prior-year quarter, driven by $2.6 million of prepaid R&D expense
FDA feedback on the breakthrough device designation application indicated further data generation was advisable before advancing the submission
Cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities fell to $11.19 million at December 31, 2021 from $12.57 million at June 30, 2021
positive_highlights: $4.7 million non-dilutive Australian Federal Government grant awarded to fund a high-tech biosensor manufacturing facility
Clinical trial protocol submitted to the Mills Peninsula Medical Center IRB for a 40-subject saliva glucose study, with first-stage completion expected by July 2022
Management states cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities of $11.19 million are sufficient to cover expenses and capital requirements into the first half of 2023
summary: GBS Inc. reported a Q2 FY2022 preliminary net loss of $3.46 million, or $0.23 per share, versus a $1.9 million net loss in the prior-year period, driven largely by $2.6 million of prepaid R&D expensed in the quarter. Government support income fell to $177,791 from $233,218 a year earlier, and cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities declined to $11.19 million as of December 31, 2021 from $12.57 million at June 30, 2021, with management stating resources cover requirements into the first half of 2023. No formal revenue or EPS guidance was provided; the FDA responded to the licensor's breakthrough device designation application that further data generation is advisable, and the first-stage 40-subject saliva glucose clinical trial is expected to complete by July 2022. The key change versus the prior period is the near-doubling of the net loss on accelerated development spending and the FDA feedback requiring added data before advancing the submission.

negative_highlights: Company remains in a loss position despite record revenue growth.
Operating cash flow was negative $3.8 million, showing a significant decrease from previous periods due to working capital dynamics and R&D investments.
positive_highlights: Revenue surged 7,016% year-over-year driven by the scaling of 5G messaging services to over 100 institutional clients.
summary: Datasea reported Q2 FY2022 revenue of $9.6 million, representing a massive 7,016% increase year-over-year and over 900% growth quarter-over-quarter driven by the rapid expansion of its 5G messaging business. Despite this explosive top-line growth, the company remains unprofitable due to significant R&D spending but guidance indicates an expectation to breakeven in Q3 FY2022 and turn profitable in Q4 FY2022 with a projected total revenue from Q1-Q3 of $36 million.

negative_highlights: Ecommerce Vehicle GPPU missed guidance by ~$600 in Q4, with adjusted EBITDA loss of $120M versus guidance; roughly half of the GPPU variance tied to premium auction vehicles over $30,000 bought in Q3 for Q4 sale
Q1 2022 guidance implies sequential decline (revenue ~$875M, units 18,000-19,000) and a ~$130M adjusted EBITDA loss, with FY2022 guidance withheld
~20-24% of reconditioning capacity sits with ADESA, whose announced acquisition creates reconditioning capacity uncertainty that management deferred to Analyst Day
positive_highlights: Q4 revenue rose 130% YoY to $934M and ecommerce units of 21,243 rose 93% YoY, exceeding the high end of guidance
Ecommerce Product GPPU increased 14% YoY to $1,075; full-year SG&A per transaction improved 18% to $3,818 from $4,633
Consumer-sourced units were 76% of Q4 retail units (up from 40% in 2020); reconditioning centers doubled to 38 and last-mile reached over 60% of deliveries, above the 50% target
summary: Q4 revenue rose 130% YoY to $934M with ecommerce units up 93% to 21,243, but ecommerce GPPU came in ~$600 below guidance on premium-vehicle depreciation, higher reconditioning costs, and year-end warranty/inventory accruals, driving a $120M adjusted EBITDA loss versus guidance. Q1 guidance implies a further step down to ~$875M revenue, 18,000-19,000 units, ~$1,500 GPPU, and a ~$130M adjusted EBITDA loss, with full-year 2022 guidance withheld citing the just-announced ADESA acquisition (~20-24% of reconditioning capacity) and pending UACC purchase accounting. Management said it expects Q1 to be the EBITDA trough with sequential improvement through the year, but repeatedly deferred specifics to the spring Analyst Day, and the Q4 miss was explained in detail under repeated analyst pushback on the GPPU shortfall.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened significantly to $18 million from $5.4 million year-over-year.
R&D expenses increased substantially to $14.7 million, driven by Phase 3 trial costs.
Management explicitly declined to provide a timeline for the top-line data readout, stating they will not refine guidance yet.
positive_highlights: Exceeded site activation goals for the pivotal Phase 3 MANTRA study ahead of expectations.
First patient dosed in the tumor-agnostic MANTRA-2 basket trial in November 2021.
Cash balance of $140.2 million provides sufficient runway to complete all ongoing and planned clinical trials.
summary: For the fourth quarter of 2021, Rain Therapeutics reported a net loss of $18 million compared to $5.4 million in the prior year, with R&D expenses rising to $14.7 million and G&A to $3.4 million. The company has $140.2 million in cash providing runway into the first half of 2024 but explicitly stated it will not refine guidance for the Phase 3 MANTRA trial data readout, maintaining only that final data is anticipated in 2023. Management emphasized a prudent capital strategy to prioritize the flagship liposarcoma trial while controlling expenses on subsequent basket trials.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to $12.2M from $11.2M
Cash sufficient only into Q4 2022, implying need for additional funding
No Phase 3 start yet; timeline is H2 2022 with continued operational setup
positive_highlights: Phase 2 EB613 met primary and key secondary endpoints with p<0.001 for biomarker dose response
FDA agreed on BMD as primary Phase 3 endpoint
Engaged Torreya for EB613 partnering; strong regional interest especially in Asia
summary: Entera Bio reported FY2021 revenues of $571k (up from $365k YoY), a net loss of $12.2M, and year-end cash of $24.9M, sufficient into Q4 2022. The Phase 2 study of EB613 met primary and key secondary endpoints with significant dose response; FDA endorsed BMD as primary Phase 3 endpoint. Phase 3 start is expected in H2 2022, with 600-800 patients. Management highlighted progress in Amgen collaboration, growing MTA activity, and hiring Torreya for EB613 partnering.

negative_highlights: Q4 billings decreased 4.4% to $151.4 million from $158.4 million a year earlier, attributed to lower customer engagement and rescheduled campaigns.
Adjusted cash flow from operations fell to $5.0 million in Q4 from $16.0 million, with margin contracting to 3.3% from 10.1%.
Management discontinued forward-looking guidance and said it does not expect year-over-year growth in Q1 2022 versus a record Q1 2021.
positive_highlights: Full-year revenue grew 51% to $549 million and adjusted cash flow from operations rose 47% to $197.1 million.
Q4 revenue increased 37.3% year-over-year to $146.7 million, driven by a $25.7 million rise in term subscription revenue and $15.3 million in lifetime subscription revenue.
Paid subscribers grew 13.4% to 972,000, with high-value and ultra-high-value subscribers up 19% and 32% respectively year-over-year.
summary: MarketWise reported Q4 2021 revenue of $146.7 million, up 37.3% year-over-year, but billings declined 4.4% to $151.4 million and adjusted cash flow from operations fell to $5.0 million from $16.0 million a year earlier. For the full year, revenue rose 51% to $549 million and adjusted CFFO grew 47% to $197.1 million. Management announced it will no longer provide forward-looking financial guidance, reversing prior expectations, and stated it does not expect year-over-year growth in Q1 2022 versus a record prior-year quarter. Paid subscribers grew 13.4% to 972,000, while ARPU declined to $742 from $759.

negative_highlights: Q4 net loss widened to $4.1M from $1.8M year-over-year
Full-year net loss increased to $12.8M from $7.4M
R&D costs rose due to higher personnel and clinical trial expenditures
positive_highlights: Cash and equivalents nearly tripled to $29.2 million from $11.1 million
SP-3164 acquisition expands pipeline into targeted protein degradation
Cash runway expected to cover ongoing programs through second half of 2022 and into early 2023
summary: Salarius Pharmaceuticals reported Q4 FY2021 net loss of $4.1 million, up from $1.8 million year-over-year, with R&D costs rising and grant revenue absent. Full-year net loss widened to $12.8 million from $7.4 million, but cash position strengthened to $29.2 million versus $11.1 million at year-end 2020, supported by $28.3 million raised in 2021. Management highlighted the acquisition of SP-3164 for targeted protein degradation and expects interim sarcoma data and preclinical data for SP-3164 in late 2023. Guidance is qualitative: management projects a cash runway covering ongoing programs through the second half of 2022 and into early 2023.

negative_highlights: No revenue reported for the quarter as the company is pre-revenue
R&D expenses increased to $23.3 million for the year due to preparation for registrational trials
positive_highlights: FDA granted orphan drug designation for efzofitimod for sarcoidosis
Positive end-of-Phase 2 meeting with FDA leading to planned registrational study initiation in Q3 2022
Demonstrated steroid reduction of 58% and FVC improvement of 3.3% vs placebo in Phase 1b/2a
summary: aTyr Pharma reported Q4 FY2021 financial results with $107.9 million in cash and $23.3 million in R&D expenses for the full year. The company received FDA orphan drug designation for efzofitimod and plans to initiate a registrational study in Q3 2022 following a positive end-of-Phase 2 meeting. Management expressed confidence in the clinical data, noting steroid reduction of 58% and FVC improvements compared to placebo.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to $54.9 million from $19.9 million in the prior year due to increased R&D and G&A expenses.
Phase 3 LIFT-AD enrollment expansion adds complexity with a target completion of Q3 2022.
positive_highlights: Enrollment in Phase 2 ACT-AD completed with 77 participants, on track for Q2 topline data.
Discontinuation rate in ACT-AD was approximately 14%, significantly below the modeled 20% expectation.
Company ended FY2021 with $319.7 million in cash, cash equivalents, and investments.
summary: Athira Pharma reported full-year 2021 financial results with R&D expenses of $42.8 million and a net loss of $54.9 million ($1.49 per share), driven by increased clinical trial activities and personnel expansion. The company ended the year with $319.7 million in cash, providing liquidity to support its lead programs including the Phase 2 ACT-AD study (topline expected Q2) and Phase 3 LIFT-AD study (enrollment completion targeted Q3). Management expressed confidence in the clinical data readout and the potential for fosgo to address mild-to-moderate Alzheimer's disease.

negative_highlights: Q4 revenue declined slightly due to supply chain constraints limiting material availability.
Management explicitly stated they will not issue annual guidance for 2022, citing a volatile environment and slowing Chinese demand (GDP forecast ~5.5%).
Raw material costs like steel peaked over 200% in 2021, creating headwinds expected to persist into the first half of 2022.
positive_highlights: Full-year revenue reached $98.8 million with 48% year-over-year growth, surpassing the top-line guidance of $100 million mentioned in context (though slightly under the specific $100M target cited as a goal to be surpassed).
Gross margin expanded by 7 basis points YoY to 19.8%, driven by higher-value transmission sales.
Cash and cash equivalents nearly doubled from $9.4 million in 2020 to $17.8 million at year-end.
summary: GTEC reported full-year revenue of $98.8 million (up 48% YoY) and Q4 revenue of $22.9 million (down slightly from the prior year). While annual results beat guidance, management explicitly stated they would not issue formal 2022 guidance due to volatile supply chain constraints and a slowing Chinese market. The company highlighted record gross profit margins but noted that raw material costs remain high.

negative_highlights: Management gave no numeric revenue or EPS guidance, only general expectations of future revenue and profitability growth
The Bitcoin mining operation, with close to $10 million invested and 1,000 machines, ran only about 1.5 months in 2021 after a late start and was described as facing 'difficulties to start'
Revenue growth was driven primarily by the Q4 CBD merchant portfolio acquisition rather than organic expansion
positive_highlights: FY2021 revenue rose ~82% to $16.7 million from $9.8 million, with processing fees up $7.5 million to $15.8 million
Merchant base expanded from ~8,500 to ~10,500 and merchant processing volume reached a ~$1.3 billion run rate, aided by the Q4 CBD/DBA portfolio acquisition
Company is debt free after raising $6 million in August and $25 million in November 2021, with total assets up $30.4 million to $40.6 million
summary: OLB Group reported FY2021 total revenue of $16.7 million, up about $6.9 million (~82%) year over year, with transaction and processing fees rising from $8.3 million to $15.8 million. Total assets grew about $30.4 million to $40.6 million, largely from property/equipment and intangibles tied to the Bitcoin mining build-out. Merchant count rose from roughly 8,500 to 10,500 and processing volume reached a ~$1.3 billion run rate, driven mainly by a Q4 CBD merchant portfolio acquisition; the company has no short- or long-term debt following an August $6 million and November $25 million capital raise. Management gave no numeric guidance, citing broad revenue and profitability growth expectations for the coming year and noting the Bitcoin mining operation began only about 1.5 months before year-end.

negative_highlights: Total Q4 net product revenue fell to $1.9 million from $3.1 million in Q3, with EYSUVIS down to $1.2 million and INVELTYS down to $0.7 million.
About 50% of commercial and 70% of Medicare Part D EYSUVIS prescriptions were not being filled, and gross-to-net worsened due to heavy co-pay assistance reliance.
Cash position fell to $92.1 million from $124.5 million at September 30, 2021, with runway only into Q2 2023 absent the targeted $25 million expense reduction.
positive_highlights: EYSUVIS prescriptions rose 21% quarter-over-quarter to 22,460, with the uptick continuing into early 2022 and total prescriptions of about 87,000 since launch.
Commercial coverage reached approximately 118 million lives (70% of U.S. commercial) after securing UnitedHealthcare (~13 million lives) in March 2022, with CVS Caremark bids submitted.
KPI-012 Phase 1b showed significant improvement in 7 of 8 PCED patients with complete healing in 6 of 8, and a Phase 2/3 trial is targeted for Q4 2022.
summary: Q4 2021 net product revenue fell to $1.9 million from $3.1 million in Q3, with EYSUVIS at $1.2 million (down from $1.8 million) and INVELTYS at $0.7 million (down from $1.2 million), even as Symphony-reported EYSUVIS prescriptions rose 21% to 22,460 quarter-over-quarter. The revenue decline was driven by a heavier mix of lower-priced patient-assistance/co-pay prescriptions (watch-down from $485 WAC to a $60 acquisition fee), while INVELTYS was hurt by higher returns reserves. Cash was $92.1 million at year-end and management targets roughly $25 million of 2022 expense reductions to extend runway beyond Q2 2023; no formal revenue guidance was given, but commercial coverage reached about 118 million commercial lives (70%) plus roughly 7.1 million Medicare lives (15%) after the UnitedHealthcare and Cigna Medicare wins.

negative_highlights: Q4 revenue modest at $600,000; initial launch scale still small
January 2022 softness due to COVID-related office closures
MARIO study completion anticipated early 2024, including potential approval late that year
positive_highlights: Q4 net revenues $600,000; 3,674 prescriptions in Q4, solid growth over Q3
Coverage for more than 48% of commercial lives, tracking ahead of expectations
Positive Phase 3 CANDLE results; sNDA on track for Q2 submission
summary: In Q4 2021, SCYNEXIS reported BREXAFEMME net revenues of $600,000 and over 4,600 total prescriptions since launch, with 1,600 new prescribers in Q4. They announced positive Phase 3 CANDLE data for recurrent VVC prevention and expect sNDA submission in Q2 2022. Commercial insurance coverage reached 48% of U.S. lives, ahead of expectations. Company ended 2021 with over $100 million cash, runway into Q2 2023, and reiterated franchise potential of $700–800 million annual U.S. sales.

negative_highlights: Q4 revenue was impacted by supply chain disruptions that delayed shipments and pushed contract revenue beyond original timelines
FY2021 operating loss of $1.98 million and net loss of $1.34 million, despite improvement over 2020
Management declined to provide any revenue or earnings guidance and gave no timing detail on potential acquisitions
positive_highlights: FY2021 revenue of $13.6 million rose 60% over 2020 and was the second best in company history
Gross margin expanded 330 bps to 21.5% from 18.2% in 2020
Net bookings of approximately $16 million rose 116% versus 2020, with record second-half bookings of $9.6 million
summary: CEA Industries reported FY2021 revenue of $13.6 million, up 60% versus 2020, with gross margin expanding 330 bps to 21.5%. Full-year net bookings were approximately $16 million, up 116%, including a record $9.6 million in the second half. However, Q4 revenue was held back by supply chain disruptions that delayed shipments, and FY2021 still produced an operating loss of $1.98 million and a net loss of $1.34 million. Management provided no forward revenue or earnings guidance and would not detail M&A timing, while noting the February 2022 NASDAQ uplisting and approximately $24 million capital raise leaving roughly $21 million in cash as of mid-March 2022.

negative_highlights: Adjusted net loss increased by $5.1 million due to clinical trial costs
PCS499 Phase 2b enrollment slow; some patients died from COVID
Cash raised via private placement and Lincoln Park equity facility signals market uncertainty
positive_highlights: Net loss narrowed to $11.4 million from $14.4 million in 2020
Cash balance increased to $16.5 million from $15.4 million
Five pipeline drugs each target >$1 billion market with early efficacy evidence
summary: Processa reported Q4/2021 net loss of $11.4 million or $0.75 per share, improved from $14.4 million or $2.54 per share in 2020, but adjusted for IPR&D the net loss increased by $5.1 million due to higher clinical trial costs. Cash balance at year-end was $16.5 million, increased by $1.1 million from 2020, and the company secured a $15 million equity facility as financing. Multiple clinical milestones are expected in 2022, but patient enrollment in the PCS499 trial has been slow due to COVID. The company faces uncertainty in capital markets.

negative_highlights: Management declined to guide on enrollment pace or timing of initial clinical data, citing likely below-nameplate manufacturing utilization and the possibility of a scientific conference rather than a defined release.
Chief Medical Officer Raffaele Baffa departed effective the day after the 10-K filing, with the company engaging a consultant and relying on a board member for clinical development expertise.
TCR library expansion is not expected until the second half of 2022 at the earliest, with each added TCR taking six to 12 months to qualify and amend into the IND.
positive_highlights: Q4 R&D expense fell 41% to $8.2 million and G&A fell 76% to $2.1 million versus Q4 2020.
2022 operating cash flow guided to $40–$45 million, a significant reduction from $61.5 million in 2021 burn, with runway into Q2 2023.
IND amended in December to add four TCRs, bringing the library to 10 TCRs across eight HLAs, and first patient has been consented in the Phase 1-2 TCRT library trial.
summary: Alaunos reported Q4 2021 net loss of $11.8 million, or $0.05 per share, compared to a $22.8 million loss, or $0.11 per share, in Q4 2020; R&D expense fell 41% to $8.2 million and G&A fell 76% to $2.1 million. Full-year net loss was $78.8 million, or $0.37 per share, versus $80.0 million, or $0.38 per share, in 2020. Cash and equivalents stood at $76.1 million with full-year burn of $61.5 million, and management guided 2022 operating cash flow to $40–$45 million, sufficient to fund operations into Q2 2023. Key changes: first patient consent in the Phase 1-2 TCRT library trial with dosing expected in Q2 2022, a CMO departure effective the day after filing, and an IND amendment adding four TCRs for a 10-TCR library.

negative_highlights: The Atlanta joint venture incurred approximately $0.6 million in operating expenses for only $44,000 of revenue due to one-time startup costs.
Mexico and Alabama JVs generated a combined net loss of roughly $1M including pre-revenue startup labor and other one-time expenses.
The company stated it will need to source additional capital to support INVO Center expansion plans despite having sufficient liquidity for near-term needs.
positive_highlights: Revenue increased significantly from $1 million in FY2020 to $4.2 million in FY2021 driven by the resumption of distribution business and new center openings.
Net loss narrowed from $8.3 million to $6.7 million, with adjusted EBITDA improving from a $3.7M loss to a $2.8M loss (or $2.1M excluding JV non-cash items).
All three new INVO Centers are operational and treating patients; Birmingham clinic achieved 67% positive pregnancy tests in the most recent series.
summary: For the full year ended December 31, 2021, INVO Bioscience reported revenue of $4.2 million (up from $1 million in FY2020) and a net loss of $6.7 million compared to an $8.3 million loss prior year; adjusted EBITDA was a loss of $2.8 million versus $3.7 million last year, excluding non-cash charges. The company opened three new INVO Centers (Birmingham, Atlanta, Monterrey) in FY2021 with the Georgia JV contributing only $44k revenue and operating expenses of approximately $0.6M for the year due to startup costs; total cash on hand was $5.7 million after debt repayment but additional capital is needed for expansion.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA swung to -$4.5M from +$1.7M in 2020
Q4 revenue and EBITDA hit by supply chain disruptions and inventory rebalancing
Cash expected to drop from Q4 to Q1 2022 due to COVID-related supply disruptions
positive_highlights: Revenue up 16% YoY to $55.4M, outperforming market decline of 7%
Amazon channel grew 57% and share rose to 41%, #1 position
Gross margin improved 328 bps to 31.6%
summary: Minim's FY2021 GAAP revenue grew 16% to $55.4M, but Q4 underperformed due to supply chain and demand normalization, leading to adjusted EBITDA of -$4.5M versus +$1.7M in 2020. Gross margin improved 328 bp to 31.6%. Management expects Q1 2022 revenue to rebound 20-30% quarter-over-quarter, though cash will decline from Q4 to Q1. Amazon share grew to 41%, and the company became #1 in Amazon modem/gateway market share.

negative_highlights: No explicit forward guidance or consensus comparison provided on the call.
Model Home acquisitions slowed in 2021 versus 2020, with only 18 properties acquired for about $8 million during the year.
positive_highlights: Core FFO rose to $2.5 million in 2021 from $1.5 million in 2020, with interest expense down 45% year-over-year.
Collected more than 100% of billed rent in 2021 as tenants brought past-due 2020 accounts current.
Completed $33 million of property sales plus approximately $21 million of Model Home sales with a $3 million gain, while adding a Johns Hopkins-leased property.
summary: Presidio Property Trust reported 2021 core FFO of $2.5 million versus $1.5 million in 2020, with interest expense down 45% year-over-year. The company executed 50 leases totaling about 217,000 square feet in 2021, sold three Colorado office properties and one California retail asset for $33 million, and sold 44 Model Homes for roughly $21 million with a $3 million gain. Management also highlighted a new acquisition of a 30,000-square-foot building 100% leased to Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health and the sponsorship of a SPAC, but provided no explicit forward guidance or specific quarterly figures.

negative_highlights: Consolidated gross profit margin decreased from 45% in 2020 to 44% due to increased costs of components and parts.
Cash position declined year-over-year, dropping from $23.9 million at end-2020 to $14.6 million at end-2021 primarily due to investing activities for acquisitions.
HempOverview business slowed following the news cycle perspective regarding hemp regulations.
positive_highlights: Revenue increased significantly by 659% YoY to $9.8 million due to successful integration of MicaSense, Measure Global, and senseFly acquisitions.
eBee TAC drones were added to the DIU Blue UAS cleared list for use with US government agencies and military branches.
Raised approximately $30.9 million via ATM between May and December 2021 to fund integration and growth initiatives.
summary: AgEagle reported full-year FY2021 revenue of $9.8 million (up from $1.3M in prior year) driven by three acquisitions including MicaSense and senseFly, resulting in a net loss of approximately $30.1 million ($0.43/share). Gross margin contracted to 44% from 45%, primarily due to supply chain constraints on components. Management indicated that while the acquisition strategy fueled growth, they are now pivoting toward organic revenue generation and cash flow positivity for 2022.

negative_highlights: Company incurred a net loss of $924,718 for the full year and $1.1 million in Q4.
Significant one-time charges included $4.3M depreciation on closed factories and cancellation of deferred tax assets.
Chemical and natural gas segments sustained losses of $2.5M and $167k respectively with no operations in 2021.
positive_highlights: Full-year revenue increased 95% YoY to approximately $5 million.
Gross margins expanded significantly to 50.7% from 31.2% in the prior year.
Bromine segment gross profit surged 182% to $26 million due to volume and pricing increases.
summary: Gulf Resources reported full-year 2021 revenues of approximately $5 million (up 95% YoY) and a net loss of $924,718, driven by one-time charges including $4.3M in depreciation for closed factories, $2.7M in deferred tax asset cancellations, and $3.1M in compensation. The fourth quarter specifically saw a revenue increase of 76.7% to $20.9 million but resulted in a net loss of $1.1 million due to similar one-time accounting impacts. Management provided no specific full-year 2022 guidance but noted Q1 2022 would be weak due to winter closures, with expectations for reduced losses and higher revenues thereafter.

negative_highlights: US FDA requires additional data for CIN approval, necessitating a second Phase 3 study.
FDA discussions indicate that non-small cell lung cancer filing in the US is delayed until at least late 2022 due to concerns over patient population relevance (87% of DUBLIN-3 data from China).
Full year net loss increased slightly to $64.2M compared to $61.0M prior year.
positive_highlights: Positive top-line data presented for Plinabulin plus docetaxel in non-small cell lung cancer (DUBLIN-3), showing significant improvement in overall survival compared to standard of care.
Strategic partnership with Hengrui Pharmaceuticals secured, including an upfront payment estimated at $31 million and potential milestones up to $171 million for commercialization in Greater China.
Cash balance stood at $41.6M plus note weakness in-term investments of $30.7M ($72.4M total), deemed sufficient to support operations over the next year.
summary: BeyondSpring reported a net loss of $9.5 million in Q4 FY2021 and $64.2 million for the full year, driven by R&D expenses of $36.9M (down from $41.8M) but offset by higher pre-commercialization costs. The company confirmed that its US filing timeline for non-small cell lung cancer is off until at least late 2022 due to FDA discussions regarding the relevance of data derived primarily from Chinese patients, and a second Phase 3 study in CIN will be required before potential approval.

negative_highlights: No full-year 2022 revenue guidance was provided; CFO Steven Sim said full-year projection is 'almost impossible' amid China lockdowns and supply chain disruption.
Q4 gross margin of 18.8% remains thin for a hardware business, and operating expenses more than tripled year-over-year with SG&A quadrupling to about $0.82 million.

Cryptocurrency mining demand is exposed to volatile digital asset prices and North America relocation involves execution and cost risk that management acknowledged is still only in the planning stage.
positive_highlights: Full-year revenue jumped to $36.71 million from roughly $0.05 million in 2020, with $31.37 million generated in Q4 alone.
Full-year net income turned positive at $3.53 million versus a $1.07 million net loss in 2020.
Q4 gross margin expanded 5.4 percentage points quarter-over-quarter to 18.8%, and working capital rose to $24.48 million from $3.23 million, aided by a $20 million December capital raise.
summary: AGM Group reported Q4 FY2021 revenue of $31.37 million versus roughly $0 in the prior-year quarter, driving full-year revenue to $36.71 million and swinging full-year net income to $3.53 million from a $1.07 million loss in 2020. Q4 gross margin was 18.8%, up 5.4 percentage points from the prior quarter, with Q4 net income of $3.84 million and operating income of $5.06 million. Management declined to give full-year 2022 revenue guidance, citing COVID lockdowns and supply chain disruption, but said quarter-to-quarter trends should be positive as the company pursues a joint venture with HighSharp and a North America relocation of headquarters and manufacturing.

negative_highlights: Total revenue declined 17% YoY to $68.4 million, and telematics products revenue fell 43% YoY to $27.1 million due to supply chain constraints.
Adjusted EBITDA fell to $5 million (7% margin) from $9.9 million (12% margin) in the prior-year quarter.
The company did not provide quarterly guidance, citing difficulty projecting revenue timing, and expects continued pressure on free cash flow from shipment delays and subscription transitions.
positive_highlights: Software and subscription services revenue grew 19% YoY and 13% sequentially to a record $41.2 million, 60% of total revenue.
Remaining performance obligations rose 47% YoY to $200 million, with over $90 million expected to be recognized in fiscal 2023.
Subscriber base increased to 1.1 million from 954,000 a year ago, and the company converted about one-fifth of eligible device customers to recurring contracts in the quarter.
summary: CalAmp reported Q4 FY2022 total revenue of $68.4 million, flat sequentially but down 17% year over year, with software and subscription services revenue rising 19% YoY to a record $41.2 million (60% of total). Telematics products revenue fell 43% YoY to $27.1 million, and adjusted EBITDA dropped to $5 million (7% margin) from $9.9 million (12%) a year ago, due to component shortages and a transition to subscription contracts. Remaining performance obligations surged 47% YoY to $200 million, and the company added over 100,000 subscribers. Management gave no quarterly guidance, citing supply chain uncertainty and the subscription transition, but said it hopes to resume guidance in the latter half of fiscal 2023; it also targets 1.2–1.5 million subscribers and 10–15% organic growth.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened significantly to $17.4 million compared to $6.8 million in Q1 2021.
R&D expenses increased substantially to $13.6 million from $5.3 million year-over-year.
positive_highlights: Phase III MANTRA study enrollment is over halfway complete with a target of 160 patients.
Top-line data for the pivotal Phase III MANTRA study is anticipated in the first half of 2023, which is earlier than previously guided.
Enrollment for the tumor-agnostic Phase II MANTRA-2 study remains on track with an interim readout expected in Q4 2022.
summary: Rain Therapeutics reported a net loss of $17.4 million for Q1 FY2022, an increase from $6.8 million in the prior year quarter, driven by R&D expenses of $13.6 million and G&A of $3.9 million. The company confirmed ample cash runway extending into the first half of 2024 based on its existing balance of $123.2 million as of March 31, 2022. Management provided an earlier-than-guided update on the Phase III MANTRA study, anticipating enrollment completion by year-end and top-line data in H1 2023.

negative_highlights: The new nutritionally enhanced corn (NEC) business model contributed zero sales in H1 FY2022 as the crop had not yet been harvested.
Supply constraints limited revenue potential for the top-performing hybrid, forcing management to turn away orders.
positive_highlights: Sales grew impressively by 300% to RMB46.4 million driven by a new disease-tolerant corn variety that outperformed competitors during severe weather events.
Operating expenses were leveraged effectively, growing only 14% despite the tripling of revenue.
Management indicated they ran out of inventory for their top-performing hybrid and are ramping up production to meet anticipated demand.
summary: Origin Agritech reported first-half FY2022 sales of RMB46.4 million (USD$7.3 million), representing a 300% increase from the prior period to RMB11.6 million, driven by strong demand for its disease-tolerant corn variety which ran out of inventory. Despite rapid revenue growth and operating expenses rising only 14%, the company generated earnings of RMB1.3 million (USD$0.03/share) due to sub-lending income from a Beijing headquarters property sale; notably, zero contribution came from its new nutritionally enhanced corn (NEC). Management expressed high confidence in exceeding full-year sales guidance of 300% and stated they are ramping up seed production for the coming season.

negative_highlights: No revenue reported as the company is pre-commercial; all expenses are R&D focused.
positive_highlights: Received FDA orphan drug designation for Efzofitimod for the treatment of systemic sclerosis (scleroderma).
Clinical proof-of-concept demonstrated for Efzofitimod in pulmonary sarcoidosis with positive Phase 1b/2a results.
Company maintains a clean balance sheet with no debt and approximately $100 million in cash.
summary: aTyr Pharma reported Q1 FY2022 results with $98.7 million in cash and $13.4 million in total expenses ($8.9M R&D, $3.5M G&A). The company confirmed it is on track to initiate a registrational study for Efzofitimod in pulmonary sarcoidosis in the third quarter of 2022 following a positive Endo Phase II meeting and accepted data presentation at ATS. Management also highlighted receipt of FDA orphan drug designation for scleroderma and plans to initiate a Phase 1 study for ATYR2810 in cancer in the second half of 2022.

negative_highlights: Billings fell 47% YoY to $136M and 10% sequentially, with overall conversion rate down ~16 bps QoQ
Adjusted cash flow from operations was $1.1M versus $98M a year ago, including an $18.1M working-capital drag
Paid subscribers fell 9% to 909,000 and ARPU declined to $636 from $825, with an estimated 60,000 additional churn from the outsized Q1 2021 cohort
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 14.3% YoY to $136.8M, driven by an $11.3M increase in lifetime subscription revenue and $7.2M in term subscription revenue
High-value and ultra-high-value subscriber counts rose 9% and 21% YoY, with cumulative conversion rates hitting all-time highs
Free subscriber base grew 33% to 14.5 million, and the company repurchased 2.1 million shares for ~$11.5 million in the quarter
summary: Revenue rose 14.3% YoY to $136.8M, but billings fell 47% YoY to $136M and 10% sequentially from Q4's $151M, as the D2P conversion rate dropped 16 bps QoQ on low-ARPU subscriber hesitancy. Adjusted cash flow from operations collapsed to $1.1 million from $98 million a year ago, with $18.1 million of the decline attributed to working-capital timing. Paid subscribers fell 9% to 909,000 while the free base grew 33% to 14.5 million, and ARPU dropped to $636 from $825. Management reaffirmed it will not provide guidance and declined to commit to a minimum free cash flow level for the year, despite acknowledging it has flexibility to cut marketing and G&A.

negative_highlights: Company reported a net loss of $22.5 million and an operating loss of $19 million for FY2021.
FY2021 gross margin was only 27%, temporarily impacted by aggressive distribution discounts to secure partners.
Life Sciences division is not included in current revenue projections despite clinical trial progress.
positive_highlights: Audited revenues grew from ~$100k (FY2020) to $9M (FY2021), with Q4 up 229% over Q3 and H2 up 329% over H1.
Colombian cultivation facility secured a new export quota of over 43,000 kg for high-THC products following regulatory changes in March 2022.
Cash balance strengthened to $37.6M as of Dec 31, 2021 from $14.9M the prior year.
summary: Flora Growth reported FY2021 audited revenues of approximately $9 million (up from ~$100k in 2020) and a net loss of $22.5 million driven by an operating loss of $19 million including over $8M in one-time issuance and acquisition expenses. Management reiterated FY2022 revenue guidance of $35-45 million, citing the activation of House of Brands (60-70% contribution) and Wholesale pillars while Life Sciences remains off-book for now. Gross margin was 27%, with management expecting expansion to over 50% in 2022 as higher-margin brands like JustCBD scale.

negative_highlights: Full-year ecommerce unit guidance of 45,000-55,000 represents a decline from the Q1 annualized rate of ~78,000 units, signaling a significant growth slowdown
Titling and registration issues have caused customer problems, strained DMV relationships, and are expected to drive $17M-$27M in non-recurring costs in 2022
Q1 included a $202M non-cash goodwill impairment and a GAAP net loss, with continued cash burn expected through 2022
positive_highlights: Q1 revenue of $924M came in 6% above guidance, with ecommerce GPPU of $1,763, 18% ahead of guidance and up 26% sequentially
Adjusted EBITDA loss of $107M beat guidance by $23M, aided by a $30M gain on the first UACC securitization
Realignment plan targets $135M-$165M in cost reductions and operating improvements for 2022, with $180M-$220M on a fully annualized basis, and year-end liquidity guided to ~$500M
summary: Vroom reported Q1 2022 total revenue of $924M, 6% above guidance, with ecommerce units up 26% YoY to 19,473 and ecommerce GPPU of $1,763, 18% above guidance; adjusted EBITDA loss of $107M beat guidance by $23M. However, the company issued full-year ecommerce unit guidance of 45,000-55,000, a steep reduction from the Q1 annualized run rate of ~78,000, along with an adjusted EBITDA loss of $325M-$375M, as it prioritizes unit economics over growth amid titling/registration problems. A realignment plan targets $135M-$165M in 2022 cost reductions, including a 14% workforce cut, and year-end liquidity is guided to $450M-$565M. The quarter included a $202M non-cash goodwill impairment and a $30M securitization gain, but operational execution issues and a growth slowdown drove a cautious, defensive tone.

negative_highlights: Management expects a slight decline in Q2 2022 operating results versus the prior-year quarter due to sale timing relative to partner buyouts
CEO said rent growth is not expected to continue at the current rate, and cap rates could see a slight increase as financing-dependent buyers drop out
The $13 million gain on the San Antonio property sale (over 18% IRR) was a major driver of net income and is non-recurring
positive_highlights: Same-store NOI grew 15.9% and same-store revenue grew 10.6% year over year on the 7,729-unit same-store pool
AFFO per diluted share rose 30% to $0.39 from $0.30; net income swung to $11.5 million from a $3.8 million loss
Debt to enterprise value fell to 59% at March 31, 2022 from 72% a year earlier, and new leases signed at 12.6% spreads
summary: BRT reported Q1 FY2022 net income of $11.5 million, or $0.62 per diluted share, versus a net loss of $3.8 million ($0.22) a year earlier, driven largely by a $13 million share of gain on a property sale. AFFO rose to $7.2 million ($0.39/share) from $5.1 million ($0.30), a 30% per-share increase, on same-store revenue growth of 10.6% and same-store NOI growth of 15.9%; average occupancy was 96.4% and average rents rose 9.2%. Management gave no formal numeric guidance but flagged a possible slight decline in Q2 operating results as dispositions (Retreat at Cinco Ranch, The Vive) may close before partner buyouts, and it is acquiring remaining JV partner interests in nine properties for about $89 million with roughly $187.7 million of assumed non-recourse mortgage debt. Debt to enterprise value fell to 59% from 72% a year earlier.

negative_highlights: Gross margin down to 31.5% from 33% in Q4
Adjusted EBITDA still negative at -$1.7 million
Cash decreased to $10.5 million, down from $13.1 million
positive_highlights: Revenue up 27% quarter-over-quarter to $13.3 million
100%+ growth in Q1 orders compared to last quarter
Held number one market share on Amazon with ~40% share in core category
summary: In Q1 2022, Minim reported GAAP revenue of $13.3 million, up 27% quarter-over-quarter, while gross margin declined to 31.5% from 33% in Q4. Adjusted EBITDA improved from a $3.1 million loss to a $1.7 million loss, and cash decreased to $10.5 million from $13.1 million due to inventory payments, with expectations of improvement over the year. The company noted a return to normal retail order levels, strong Amazon market share, and progress on supply chain diversification, though mesh category entrance has been challenging.

negative_highlights: RDOF subsidy revenue expectations were cut by about $11 million versus the de-SPAC deck, with no subsidy revenue recognized in Q1
Adjusted EBITDA loss guidance of $125 million implies significantly higher spending than prior estimates even excluding the RDOF timing shift
The de-SPAC raised only about $155 million net, roughly half of what was originally expected, and management said the business will require more capital with no specific update on funding plans
positive_highlights: Revenue rose 63% year-over-year to $7.4 million and customer relationships reached roughly 71,000, up 72% year-over-year
Serviceable households increased 20% year-over-year to 5.5 million, and MDU penetration reached 25% in year one, 28% in year two, and over 30% in year three
Customer growth of more than 8,000 net adds in the quarter marked the second consecutive quarter above that level, with FY22 guidance of at least 100,000 customers
summary: Starry's first earnings call as a public company reported Q1 2022 revenue of $7.4 million, up 63% year-over-year, with customer relationships of approximately 71,000 (up 72%) and a net loss of $53.6 million versus $41 million a year earlier. Full-year 2022 guidance calls for revenue of at least $50 million (125% growth) and customer relationships above 100,000 (at least 58% growth), but the revenue outlook includes more than $15 million of RDOF subsidy revenue and the company now expects adjusted EBITDA losses of $125 million. Relative to the de-SPAC deck, RDOF revenue expectations were pushed down by roughly $11 million and the EBITDA loss guidance implies greater spending than previously outlined, while the de-SPAC raised only about $155 million net versus roughly half the originally expected proceeds. ARPU fell 7.9% to $36.4 due to promotional periods and customer mix, and management said additional capital will be needed with no specific update on the funding outlook.

negative_highlights: Winter growth trends slowed due to Omicron wave
Net revenue of $700,000 is modest for a launch quarter
Commercial coverage at 55% of commercial universe, leaving room for improvement
positive_highlights: Q1 2022 net revenues reached $700,000 with nearly 4,000 prescriptions
Repeat prescribers grew to 56% of volumes in Q1 versus 20% in Q4 2021
Over 80% of FURI and CARES patients showed clinical benefit in interim analysis
summary: In Q1 2022, SCYNEXIS generated $700,000 in net revenue and about 4,000 prescriptions for BREXAFEMME, with a 10% growth in prescriber base and repeat writers tripling versus Q4 2021. The company reported positive interim data from FURI and CARES with over 80% clinical benefit, and expects to file an sNDA for recurrent VVC this quarter with approval by end of 2022. Cash position was over $95 million, extended by a $45 million offering to fund operations into Q1 2024. Management highlighted commercial momentum but also acknowledged winter slowdown due to Omicron.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined 26% year over year to $1.7 million, with supply chain delays preventing conversion of backlog to revenue on the original contract timelines
Gross margin fell to 5.2% from 14.6% a year earlier on lower recognized revenue against a partially fixed cost base
Net bookings of ~$2.1 million fell 61% versus Q1 2021, and operating loss widened to $1.6 million from $686,000
positive_highlights: Approximately $22 million in net proceeds raised from the sale of ~5.8 million shares and ~6.6 million warrants, ending Q1 with about $22 million in cash versus $2.2 million at December 31, 2021
Backlog of $11.2 million at March 31, 2022, up $361,000 or 3% from the prior quarter-end
Successful uplisting of common shares and warrants to the NASDAQ Capital Market; management said no previously signed contracts were canceled
summary: Q1 2022 revenue fell 26% year over year to $1.7 million due to supply chain-driven shipping delays that prevented conversion of contract backlog to revenue; gross margin compressed to 5.2% from 14.6% on the lower revenue against a partially fixed cost base, and net loss widened to $1.4 million from $793,000. Net bookings were approximately $2.1 million, down 61% versus the prior-year quarter, while backlog rose 3% to $11.2 million. The company completed a NASDAQ uplisting and raised about $22 million in net proceeds from a common stock and warrant offering, ending the quarter with roughly $22 million in cash (about $2.83 per share). Management cited no contract cancellations and said it is seeing an early Q2 bounce-back in orders.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to $6.1 million from $1.9 million year-over-year
No grant revenue in current period contributed to the increased loss
R&D expenses increased by $2.7 million year-over-year
positive_highlights: Completed pre-IND meeting with FDA for SP-3164, receiving clear guidance
Plans to release interim seclidemstat clinical data in the second half of 2022
Cash position of $24.2 million expected to fund operations into 2023
summary: Salarius Pharmaceuticals Q1 FY2022 reported net loss of $6.1 million, compared to $1.9 million loss a year ago, due to higher costs and absence of grant revenue. Cash was $24.2 million. The company highlighted the acquisition of the SP-3164 targeted protein degradation program from DeuteRx and completed a pre-IND meeting with the FDA, aiming for an IND submission in first half of 2023. Seclidemstat clinical programs are enrolling patients, with interim data expected in the second half of 2022.

negative_highlights: Net loss of $1.4 million remained despite positive adjusted EBITDA, largely from depreciation and amortization.
Bitcoin mining contributed only about 3% of revenue and the $6.5 million mining outlook depends on today's Bitcoin price and 1,000 miners being fully installed.
Company plans to hold mined Bitcoin rather than note, subjecting future revenue to crypto price volatility.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew roughly 4x year over year to $8.7 million from $2.2 million, with management citing both the acquired portfolio and organic growth.
Adjusted EBITDA swung positive to about $550,000 from negative $689,000, a $1.2 million improvement.
Balance sheet shows about $4 million cash and no debt, with only roughly $750,000 of open miner leases.
summary: Q1 2022 revenue rose to $8.7 million from $2.2 million a year earlier, with gross profit up to $1.5 million from $463,000. Adjusted EBITDA turned positive at roughly $550,000 versus a negative $689,000 in Q1 2021, though the company still posted a $1.4 million net loss driven mostly by depreciation and amortization. Management guided to about $36 million of 2022 revenue from fintech products, plus an additional $6.5 million from Bitcoin mining once 1,000 miners are running, and said it expects net income positive by year-end. Merchant services accounted for 97% of revenue while Bitcoin was only about 3%, and the company ended the quarter with roughly $4 million cash and no debt.

negative_highlights: Net loss increased to $3.2M from $2.1M year-over-year
PCS499 enrollment heavily impacted by COVID, only one patient in screening
Biomarker for 3117 not yet validated, only assays in development
positive_highlights: 12852 enrollment of five patients with confidence to complete enrollment by September/October
Amended Phase 1b protocol for next-gen capecitabine and enrollment started
Cash runway into Q3 2023 supports completion of three ongoing trials
summary: Q1 FY2022 net loss widened to $3.2M ($0.20/share) from $2.1M ($0.14) a year ago on higher clinical trial costs. Cash of $14.3M is expected to fund operations into Q3 2023; cash used in operations was $1.8M. Enrollment is progressing: 12852 has 5 of 24 patients with completion expected Sept/Oct, while 499 faces COVID-related delays with only 1 in screening and 5 awaiting pre-screening. Management expects key data on three trials by year-end and FDA meeting for 3117 in December.

negative_highlights: Cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities declined to approximately $10.7 million from $12.5 million on June 30, 2021.
No revenue reported for the quarter; results were driven by timing of development spend and government grant income.
Runway guidance was unchanged from last quarter, with no new financing or partnership revenue disclosed.
positive_highlights: Net loss narrowed to $1.34 million, or $0.09 per share, from $3.14 million, or $0.27 per share, in the same period last year.
Government support income rose to $192,500 for the quarter, an increase of $158,210 versus the same period in 2021.
Lead saliva-based glucose study enrolled 10 of approximately 40 adults, with data collection expected to complete around May and analysis by end of June.
summary: GBS Inc. reported a Q3 FY2022 preliminary net loss of $1.34 million, or $0.09 per share, compared with a net loss of $3.14 million, or $0.27 per share, in the prior-year period. Cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities totaled approximately $10.7 million versus $12.5 million on June 30, 2021, with management stating the runway remains unchanged from last quarter and sufficient into the first half of calendar 2023. The company reported no commercial revenue and instead highlighted clinical progress, including IRB approval at Sutter Health, 10 of 40 patients enrolled, and manufacturing construction expected to break ground in the second half of next quarter.

negative_highlights: Net product revenue fell to $1.4 million in Q1 2022 from $1.9 million in Q4 2021, with EYSUVIS sales down to $1.0 million from $1.2 million.
INVELTYS prescriptions declined to 34,690 in Q1 from 36,700 in Q4 2021, and revenue fell to $0.4 million from $0.7 million.
Cash declined to $70.2 million from $92.1 million at year-end 2021, and management expects runway only into Q2 2023.
positive_highlights: EYSUVIS prescriptions rose 18% sequentially to 26,518 in Q1, accelerating to 31% growth in early Q2.
Payer coverage expanded to 92% of commercial lives (155.3 million) after CVS Caremark added EYSUVIS effective May 2, and Medicare coverage doubled to 14.1 million lives with Humana starting June 1.
Copay assistance program utilization dropped from as high as 70% of EYSUVIS scripts in Q4 2021 to 54% in the most recent week, already improving net ASP.
summary: Kala reported Q1 2022 net product revenue of $1.4 million, down from $1.9 million in Q4 2021, with EYSUVIS sales of $1.0 million and INVELTYS $0.4 million. EYSUVIS prescriptions grew 18% sequentially to 26,518, but net revenue fell due to heavy reliance on patient assistance programs following CVS Caremark coverage restrictions. Payer coverage improved significantly in Q2 with CVS Caremark commercial and Humana Medicare wins, which management expects to reduce copay assistance use and lift net average watching price, mainly in the second half. Cash was $70.2 million, with runway into Q2 2023; KPI-012 Phase 2/3 trial remains on track for Q4 2022.

negative_highlights: No revenue or earnings guidance; future depends on clinical trial outcomes
Manufacturing capacity limited to approximately one patient product per month
Management explicitly indicated the company will not have a patient per month in 2022
positive_highlights: First patient dosed in Phase 1/2 TCR-T Library trial and cleared the 28-day safety window
Q1 2022 net loss narrowed to $9.8 million ($0.05/share) from $21.6 million ($0.10/share) in Q1 2021
Cash and cash equivalents of $68.3 million, with runway into Q2 2023
summary: Alaunos reported a Q1 2022 net loss of $9.8 million, or $0.05 per share, versus a $21.6 million loss in Q1 2021, with R&D down 58% to $5.6 million and G&A down 57% to $3.5 million. The company ended the quarter with $68.3 million in cash, guided 2022 operating cash burn of $40-45 million, and expects an operating cash runway into Q2 2023. Clinical progress included dosing the first patient in the Phase 1/2 TCR-T Library trial, with initial data expected at a medical meeting in the second half of 2022; no revenue or earnings guidance was provided.

negative_highlights: Electric industrial equipment deliveries impacted by supply interruptions and component shortages lengthening wait times
Global headwinds including COVID-related shutdowns, China shipping disruptions, high logistics costs, and geopolitical instability in Eastern Europe expected to remain challenging over the near term
Cost of goods sold rose 18% due to inflationary pressures
positive_highlights: Record Q1 revenue of $29.3 million representing a 19% year-over-year increase
Net income grew 19% to $2.9 million with gross margin expanding 100 bps to 21.7%
Cash balance increased by 30%, providing flexibility for R&D and investments
summary: GTEC reported Q1 FY2022 revenue of $29.3 million (up 19% YoY) and net income of $2.9 million (up 19% YoY), driven by record unit deliveries despite global supply chain disruptions, material shortages, and geopolitical instability in Eastern Europe. Management noted that while the quarter was a success, significant headwinds including COVID shutdowns affecting suppliers/clients and longer installation times for charging stations persist into the near term. The company is executing its long-term strategy to capture market share in electric industrial vehicles with new product introductions (HEVI brand) and an upcoming Maryland assembly site.

negative_highlights: Management explicitly stated they would not provide second quarter or full-year guidance for 2022.
Chemical segment remains closed with commercial production delayed until potentially 2023 due to electricity restrictions and winter shutdowns.
Natural gas project in Sichuan lacks government approval, leaving the business line inactive.
positive_highlights: Revenue increased 70% YoY to $8.9 million despite facility closures for over half the quarter.
Gross profit expanded 306% to $4.4 million, with bromine gross margins expanding to 51.8% from 27%.
Strong cash flow generation of $8.5 million from operating activities and a cash balance of $105.7 million.
summary: Gulf Resources reported Q1 FY2022 revenue of $8.9 million, a 70% increase year-over-year driven by bromine and crude salt segments operating for only 39 days due to environmental closures. Gross profit surged 306% to $4.4 million, though net loss from operations narrowed significantly to $65,100 after excluding shutdown costs and foreign exchange losses. Management explicitly declined to provide full-year or Q2 guidance, instead announcing a six-year strategic plan to be released later in the month.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined significantly year-over-year to $163,000 due to the absence of Ferring's one-time purchase and license revenue
Adjusted EBITDA loss increased from $1 million last year to approximately $2 million (or $1.8M excluding JV charges)
Expansion timelines remain subject to regulatory registration processes in China taking 18-24 months
positive_highlights: China distributor agreed to annual minimums totaling just over $14 million over the initial five-year period
Atlanta INVO Center consistently achieving targeted patient flow of 40-50 consultations per month via marketing programs
Birmingham clinic achieved a 57% clinical pregnancy rate with all patients testing positive post-transfer
summary: Revenue for Q1 FY2022 totaled $163,000 compared to $685,000 in the prior year period due to a one-time purchase by Ferring last year and consolidation of Atlanta INVO Center costs. The company reported a net loss of $2.8 million versus $2.5 million previously, with adjusted EBITDA losses widening slightly from $1M to $1.8M (excluding JV charges). Management provided no specific financial guidance but expressed confidence in growth trends at existing centers and new distribution agreements.

negative_highlights: No financial results disclosed on the call
Phase III plans and FDA dialogue not finalized
Partnership timing only, no confirmed deal
positive_highlights: Appointed new CBO/CFO with 25 years of biotech experience
Market study shows payers favorable to EB613 as oral anabolic
Filed multiple U.S. patent applications to extend patent life
summary: Entera Bio reported Q1 2022 financial and operational results with no specific financial figures provided in the call. The company highlighted progress on EB613, its lead oral anabolic for osteoporosis, and announced the appointment of Miranda Toledano as CBO and CFO. A market study suggested favorable reception from clinicians and payers for EB613, and the company plans to initiate Phase III. Management expressed interest in global partnership, expecting to finalize a deal by year-end. However, the call provided no quantitative updates on revenue, EPS, margins, or cash position.

negative_highlights: First-year premiums of life insurance dropped year-over-year amid COVID-19 and a high 2021 base.
Claims adjusting business almost ground to a halt in COVID-hit areas and recorded a loss in Q1 2022.
No full-year guidance provided, with management citing COVID-19 and regulatory uncertainty and expecting the double-recording requirement to impact the whole industry including Fanhua.
positive_highlights: Life insurance GWP grew 10.1% year-over-year, outperforming a 3.1% industry decline.
G&A expenses excluding digitalization investment fell 17.2% year-over-year on staffing and outlet optimization.
Open platform first-year premiums reached about RMB40 million, up 62.3% quarter-over-quarter.
summary: Fanhua reported Q1 2022 operating income of RMB20.6 million, which management said met expectations, and life insurance GWP grew 10.1% year-over-year even as industry life GWP fell 3.1%. First-year premiums of life insurance declined, however, the 13-month persistency ratio held above 91%, and G&A expenses excluding digitalization investment fell 17.2% year-over-year. Management declined to provide full-year guidance, citing COVID-19 uncertainty and upcoming double-recording regulatory requirements in Hebei starting June, but said it remains confident of making an operating profit in Q2 2022. A stock dividend of CNFinance shares was announced, valued at approximately $31.4 million or $0.58 per Fanhua ADS.

negative_highlights: Total revenue declined 19% year-over-year to $64.7 million and 5% sequentially, missing prior expectations due to supply chain constraints.
Adjusted EBITDA margin contracted to 3% ($1.9 million) from 11% ($8.4 million) a year ago, driven by lower revenue and higher product costs.
Gross margin declined to 40% from 41% a year ago, remaining under pressure from higher product costs and freight charges; cash and cash equivalents fell to $59 million from $79 million last quarter.
positive_highlights: Software and subscription services revenue grew 13% year-over-year to $39.6 million, representing 61% of total revenue, the second consecutive quarter above 60%.
Remaining performance obligations (RPO) increased to approximately $215 million from $202 million at fiscal year-end, with 37% (~$80 million) expected to be recognized over the next 12 months.
Subscriber base grew 25% year-over-year and 13% sequentially to 1.2 million; approximately one-third of eligible telematics device customers have been converted.
summary: CalAmp reported Q1 FY2023 revenue of $64.7 million, down 19% year-over-year and 5% sequentially, missing prior expectations due to supply chain constraints, particularly COVID-related lockdowns in China. Software and subscription services revenue was $39.6 million (61% of total), up 13% year-over-year but down 4% sequentially. Adjusted EBITDA fell to $1.9 million (3% margin) from $8.4 million (11% margin) a year ago. The company did not provide formal quarterly guidance but expects mid-to-high single-digit sequential revenue growth in Q2, citing easing supply chain pressures and conversion progress; gross margin was 40%, down from 41% a year ago, with a long-term 50% target.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to $17.6 million from $8.2 million in the prior year quarter.
R&D expenses increased significantly to $14.3 million compared to $5.5 million in Q2 2021.
positive_highlights: Completed enrollment in the Phase 3 MANTRA trial with 175 patients, exceeding the 160-patient target and finishing five months ahead of prior guidance.
Demonstrated clear acceleration in enrollment since the Q1 update, surpassing expectations at both management and physician levels.
Maintained a strong balance sheet with $106 million in cash, cash equivalents, and note weakness in-term investments.
summary: Rain Therapeutics reported a net loss of $17.6 million for Q2 FY2022, an increase from $8.2 million in the prior year quarter, driven by R&D expenses of $14.3 million primarily for its lead candidate milademetan. The company announced it completed enrollment in the Phase 3 MANTRA trial with 175 patients, exceeding its target and finishing five months ahead of prior guidance. Management maintains a strong balance sheet with $106 million in cash, providing runway into mid-2024.

negative_highlights: Total revenue declined 9.7% YoY to $19.5M from $21.6M.
Net loss widened to $31.7M versus $24M in the same quarter last year.
EDP-938 failed to meet primary and secondary antiviral endpoints in the Phase IIb RSVP trial in low-risk adults, limiting its near-term potential in that population.
positive_highlights: EDP-235 Phase I data showed exposure multiples 3-6x over EC90 for Alpha and Delta variants at 200mg and 400mg without ritonavir boosting, with projected 4x lung-to-plasma ratio.

EDP-938 demonstrated statistically significant antiviral effect (undetectable RSV RNA) in a low-risk adult population despite missing primary endpoint, with ~500 subjects exposed showing favorable safety.
Cash position of $292.7M expected to cover existing programs for two years.
summary: Enanta reported Q3 FY2022 revenue of $19.5M, down from $21.6M YoY, and a net loss of $31.7M or $1.53 per diluted share, wider than the $24M loss in the prior year. R&D expenses decreased to $39.1M from $47M, while G&A rose to $12.9M from $8.4M. The company highlighted positive Phase I data for COVID-19 candidate EDP-235, with planned Phase II initiation in Q4 2022, and expects cash to fund operations for two years.

MarketWise reported Q2 FY2022 revenue of $128.0 million, down 9.9% YoY from $142.1 million, with billings plunging 36.5% to $117.5 million from $185.1 million and adjusted cash flow from operations falling to $26.8 million from $59.4 million. The company gave no formal guidance, but announced roughly $37 million in annualized overhead reductions (~15% of budgeted overhead) plus a targeted ~$37 million cut to second-half direct marketing spend, while landing-page conversion remained ~20% below Q4 2021 levels. Paid subscribers fell 9.7% to 898,000 and ARPU dropped to $580 from $823, though net income swung to $34.0 million from a $8.4 million loss on lower Class B stock comp and high-value conversion rates hit all-time highs of 42% and 32%. Management framed the weakness as macro-driven retail hesitancy with a historical recovery analogy, but the quarter showed sharp billings decline and defensive cost actions.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to $4.7 million from $3.1 million year-over-year
R&D expenses increased $0.8 million due to new degrader program
Absence of grant revenue in 2022 quarter
positive_highlights: Expanded seclidemstat trial to 15 sites, 23 locations, with more to come
Cash of $22.6 million expected to fund operations into 2023
Completed pre-IND meeting with FDA for SP-3164; on track for IND submission
