summary: Salarius Pharmaceuticals reported a Q2 2022 net loss of $4.7 million, wider than the prior-year loss of $3.1 million, with R&D expenses up due to the new protein degrader program and no grant revenue. Cash stood at $22.6 million as of June 30, expected to fund operations into 2023. The company highlighted progress in its seclidemstat trials (adding new sites) and its SP-3164 program, with interim clinical data expected later this year and an IND submission planned for the first half of 2023. No revenue was reported; the company is pre-commercial.

negative_highlights: Total revenue fell 49% sequentially to $475 million and ecommerce units dropped 53% to 9,233
Full-year ecommerce units now expected at the low end or below prior guidance
Adjusted EBITDA excluding securitization gain per unit decreased 32% quarter-over-quarter as expenses did not fall as fast as units
positive_highlights: Ecommerce GPPU more than doubled sequentially to a record $3,629, with vehicle GPPU up 264% to $2,166
Adjusted EBITDA excluding securitization gain improved $51 million sequentially, or 38%
Adjusted SG&A reduced by $52 million sequentially, including $20 million logistics, $15 million marketing, and $12 million fixed costs
summary: Vroom reported Q2 FY2022 total revenue of $475 million, down 49% sequentially, as ecommerce units were intentionally cut 53% to 9,233 and ecommerce GPPU more than doubled to a record $3,629. Adjusted EBITDA loss improved by $51 million sequentially excluding securitization gain, and adjusted SG&A fell $52 million. Management guided full-year ecommerce units to the low end or below its forecast, adjusted EBITDA loss to $325–$350 million (near or better than the midpoint), and year-end liquidity to ~$500 million, while declining to provide a unit outlook for 2023 until year-end.

negative_highlights: Same-store expenses rose 10.7%, outpacing 10% revenue growth and compressing NOI growth to 9.4%
Debt to enterprise value remained elevated at 63%, and available liquidity fell to about $31.4 million at August 5 from $57 million cash plus $35 million facility availability at quarter end
Transaction market volume has slowed and cap rates rose 25-50 bps, limiting near-term external acquisition activity
positive_highlights: AFFO per share rose 19% to $0.37 from $0.31 on improved operating margins and lower interest expense at unconsolidated subsidiaries
Average rents up 10.9% YoY to $1,252/month with new lease spreads of 15.1% and renewal spreads of 10.7%
Completed all 11 announced JV buyouts for $105.9 million, expanding the wholly-owned portfolio by roughly 3,800 units YoY to 5,420 units
summary: BRT reported Q2 2022 net income of $35.6 million ($1.91/diluted share) versus $6 million ($0.34) a year earlier, driven mostly by a $40.1 million share of gains on two property sales; AFFO was $6.9 million ($0.37/share), up 19% per share from $0.31. Same-store revenue rose 10%, expenses 10.7% and NOI 9.4%, with average rents up 10.9% to $1,252 and occupancy at 96.1%, up 80 bps. Management completed all 11 announced JV buyouts ($105.9 million) and most dispositions, growing the wholly-owned portfolio to 21 properties/5,420 units, and raised the quarterly dividend 8.7% to $0.25. No formal forward guidance was given; management expects transaction pricing to widen and activity to pick up in the fall.

negative_highlights: Cash on hand decreased from $55.1 million at year-end 2021 to $46.5 million as of June 30, 2022.
R&D expenses increased slightly to $2 million compared to $1.9 million in the prior year quarter.
positive_highlights: Narazaciclib Phase 1 trials advanced to cohort five in both US and China studies with no dose-limiting toxicities observed to date.
Rigosertib monotherapy showed a sustained complete response in a patient with dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa-associated squamous cell carcinoma for over one year.
Preliminary data from the Rigosertib plus nivolumab trial in KRAS mutated NSCLC showed two partial responses and one instance of stable disease in seven evaluable patients.
summary: Onconova reported a net loss of $4 million ($0.19 per share) for Q2 FY2022, compared to a net loss of $4.2 million in the prior year quarter, driven by R&D expenses of $2 million and G&A of $2.1 million. The company maintains a cash position of $46.5 million, sufficient to fund operations for over 18 months. Management provided no financial guidance but reiterated that clinical progress on lead assets narazaciclib and Rigosertib is on track, with an anticipated determination of the context phase 2 dose for narazaciclib potentially occurring before the end of the year.

negative_highlights: Net loss was $36.3 million and adjusted EBITDA loss was $33.9 million, despite revenue growth.

The company has a funding gap of roughly $200 million (versus original target of $340-370 million, raised only ~$155 million in IPO) and is pursuing dilutive financing options including a $100 million equity facility.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 52% YoY to $7.8 million and customer relationships increased 69% YoY to nearly 81,000, with record net adds of over 9,700 in the quarter.
Serviceable homes grew 20% YoY to 5.7 million, and the company achieved cohort-level profitability for 2020 and Q1 2021 building launches within 3-4 quarters.
Adjusted EBITDA margin improved by 25 percentage points YoY, and gross margin showed operating leverage as cost of revenues grew 56% YoY, slower than revenue growth.
summary: Starry reported Q2 FY2022 revenue of $7.8 million, up 52% year-over-year, with record net customer additions of over 9,700 bringing total customer relationships to nearly 81,000 (up 69% YoY). However, the company reported a net loss of $36.3 million and an adjusted EBITDA loss of $33.9 million, while maintaining its full-year 2022 customer guidance of >100,000 (unchanged) but deferring clarity on RDOF regulatory revenue that was included in prior guidance. Management highlighted positive cohort-level profitability and progress on a committed equity facility (up to $100 million) and potential additional investments, but acknowledged the need for further capital to reach breakeven.

negative_highlights: Cash position declined to $44.6 million at June 30 from $92.1 million at December 31, 2021, primarily due to operating cash use
No commercial revenue stream following the EYSUVIS/INVELTYS divestiture, leaving the company dependent on pipeline success
KPI-012 Phase II/III trial not yet started; topline data not expected until Q1 2024
positive_highlights: Completed sale of EYSUVIS and INVELTYS to Alcon for $65 million upfront plus up to $325 million in commercial milestones
Operating expense reductions: SG&A fell to $22.7M from $27M in Q1; planned >50% cut in H2 2022 and 60-70% cut in 2023 non-GAAP opex
Cash runway into Q2 2024 extends beyond the planned Q1 2024 KPI-012 Phase II/III data readout
summary: Kala reported Q2 2022 cash of $44.6 million, down from $92.1 million at Dec 31, with SG&A of $22.7 million (non-GAAP $20.4 million) versus $27 million (non-GAAP $24.7 million) in Q1, and R&D of $4.5 million. The quarter was defined by the July sale of EYSUVIS and INVELTYS to Alcon for $65 million upfront plus up to $325 million in milestones, transforming Kala into a pure R&D company. Management guided to a Phase II/III trial start for KPI-012 in PCED in Q4 2022 with topline data in Q1 2024, and a >50% reduction in non-GAAP opex versus H1 2022 and 60-70% for full year 2023. Cash runway is guided into Q2 2024, beyond the KPI-012 data readout.

negative_highlights: Q2 revenue declined to $20.6 million due to COVID restrictions in China causing client shutdowns and order delays.
H1 net income decreased by approximately 5% year-over-year despite gross profit growth.
Operating expenses rose significantly, with general and administrative expense increasing 52%.
positive_highlights: Gross margin expanded by 330 basis points to 23.5% driven by cost savings and shift to higher-value products.
Company secured $10 million in proceeds from a direct registration and private placement offering.
Heavy division launched the GEL-5000 front loader and opened its first assembly site in Baltimore, Maryland.
summary: GTEC reported Q2 FY2022 revenue of $20.6 million and H1 FY2022 revenue of $49.9 million, representing a decline from the prior year due to COVID-19 shutdowns in China that delayed client orders. Net income for the first half was $5.3 million compared to $5.6 million previously, while gross margin expanded 330 bps to 23.5%. Management characterized the quarter as challenging but noted a strong backlog and raised guidance expectations for the second half of the year.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to $8.4M from $5.3M year-over-year
499 enrollment significantly affected by COVID, with completion pushed to later timelines
6422 delayed due to regulatory hoops and protocol modifications
positive_highlights: 12852 trial almost completely enrolled, final top-line results expected before end of 2022
Management seeing increased patient screening for 6422 after enrollment programs
Cash runway into Q3 2023 supports ongoing trials
summary: Processa reported a net loss of $8.4 million for H1 2022, up from $5.3 million in the prior year, with R&D costs increasing by $2.1 million. Cash stood at $12.1 million, expected to fund operations into Q3 2023. Clinical progress is mixed: 12852 is nearly fully enrolled with top-line results expected before end of 2022, while 6422 and 499 experienced delays due to regulatory hurdles and COVID. Management provided no financial guidance, focusing on pipeline updates and potential licensing or partnerships.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined to $3.0 million from $4.5 million a year ago on supply chain and project delays
Gross margin compressed to 10.2% from 28.4% as fixed cost of goods sold weighed on profitability with lower revenue
Net loss of $1.8 million (negative $0.23 per share) versus prior-year net income of $300,000, and a $2.3 million contract cancellation due to a customer's loss of funding
positive_highlights: Backlog increased 21% to $9.7 million versus $8 million a year ago, and net bookings rose to $1.5 million from $900,000
Cash and cash equivalents reached $20.6 million (from $2.2 million at year-end) after ~$21.7 million in net equity proceeds, and the company remains debt-free
Signed a $1.2 million initial contract with Green Brothers Farm under a potential $10 million, 2-3 year project, plus a preferred-provider partnership with Merida Capital
summary: Q2 revenue fell to $3.0 million from $4.5 million a year ago on supply chain and project delays, gross margin compressed to 10.2% from 28.4% due to fixed costs and lower volume, and the company swung to a net loss of $1.8 million (negative $0.23 per share) from net income of $300,000 ($0.17 per share). Backlog rose 21% year over year to $9.7 million and Q2 net bookings grew to $1.5 million from $900,000, though both were partly offset by a $2.3 million contract cancellation. Management cited a more challenging macro and interest-rate environment, with no formal guidance beyond an expectation to recognize delayed revenue and drive growth and margin improvement in the second half, alongside a debt-free balance sheet and $20.6 million of cash after a February equity raise.

negative_highlights: No revenue, EPS, or formal forward guidance provided; company remains pre-revenue with a net loss of $9.9M
Management declined to clarify whether a second patient has been dosed, citing conference restrictions
Solasia darinaparsin royalties described as low single digits and not materially impactful to capital needs
positive_highlights: R&D expenses fell 56% to $5.9M and G&A fell 62% to $3.4M versus Q2 2021, due to restructuring and lower headcount
Cash runway of ~$60M expected to fund operations into Q2 2023, with Q2 burn down 62% to $8.2M
TCR-T Library trial advanced to the second dose level (~40B cells) after first patient dosed in May, with early data expected in Q3 2022
summary: Alaunos reported Q2 2022 net loss of $9.9M ($0.05/share) versus $22.7M ($0.11/share) in Q2 2021, with R&D down 56% to $5.9M and G&A down 62% to $3.4M. Cash of ~$60M is expected to fund operations into Q2 2023, with Q2 operating burn of $8.2M. The TCR-T Library Phase 1/2 trial is progressing to the second dose level (~40B cells) after the first patient was dosed in May; management declined to confirm whether a second patient has been dosed and said early data will be presented in Q3 at a scientific/medical meeting. Management provided no revenue, EPS, or formal forward guidance, and the quarter's key change was cost efficiency as the company is pre-revenue and clinical-stage.

negative_highlights: Revenue base remains small in absolute terms
Macro environment headwinds noted
Commercial execution still in early stages
positive_highlights: Revenue nearly doubled quarter-over-quarter to $1.3 million
Prescriptions grew 29% quarter-over-quarter to over 5,100
PDUFA date set for November 30, 2022 for second indication
summary: SCYNEXIS reported Q2 2022 revenues of $1.3 million from BREXAFEMME, nearly double Q1, with 5,100 prescriptions, a 29% quarter-over-quarter increase. The company raised $45 million in April, ending with over $118 million in cash, and maintains a runway into Q1 2024. FDA granted priority review for the supplemental NDA for recurrent VVC with a PDUFA date of November 30, 2022. Management expressed confidence in upcoming catalysts, including the VANQUISH and MARIO studies.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined year-over-year by approximately $62,000 (from ~$208k to ~$146k) due to the timing of batch cycles and full amortization of prior deferred revenue.
Net loss widened significantly from a net loss of $1.8 million in Q2 FY2021 to approximately $2.8 million in Q2 FY2022, excluding non-cash charges.
Adjusted EBITDA loss increased from $1.3 million last year to $2.2 million this quarter (or $1.9 million on an apples-to-apples basis).
positive_highlights: Patient trends and activity (inquiries, consults) expanded sequentially by approximately 20% from Q1 despite muted revenue recognition timing.
Management signed a non-binding LOI for the acquisition of an established profitable practice with over 15 years in operation to accelerate scale via 'build and note' strategy.
FDA submission data collection completed successfully, validating outcomes to support a five-day clinical label enhancement expected within coming days.
summary: INVO Bioscience reported Q2 FY2022 revenue of approximately $146,000 compared to $208,000 in the prior year period and a net loss of $2.8 million versus $1.8 million last year. Management highlighted that while quarterly revenue was muted due to batch cycle timing, patient activity (consults) grew sequentially by approximately 20% from Q1, with expectations for higher third-quarter revenue as batches complete more frequently. The company announced a new 'build and watch' strategy including the signing of a non-binding letter of intent to acquire an established fertility practice.

negative_highlights: Gross margin contracted to 70% from 74% on sales mix
Non-GAAP adjusted EBITDA loss widened to $9.9 million from $6.3 million a year earlier
Net loss attributable to stockholders was $19.9 million versus prior-year income of $14.8 million, with no formal guidance and cost/budget adjustments under evaluation
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 37% YoY to $4.7 million and 55% for the six-month period, primarily organic growth
Industrial/RTLS business booked its strongest new-booking quarter since the beginning of last year
Avg contract value for experience app products cited at over $135,000, with some deals in the seven digits
summary: Inpixon reported Q2 FY2022 revenue of $4.7 million, up 37% YoY, with gross profit of $3.3 million; gross margin fell to 70% from 74% on sales mix. Net loss attributable to stockholders was $19.9 million versus a $14.8 million gain a year earlier, and non-GAAP adjusted EBITDA worsened to a $9.9 million loss from a $6.3 million loss. Pro forma non-GAAP loss per share was $0.07, flat with the prior year, and the company ended with $65.8 million in cash. No explicit forward revenue or earnings guidance was issued; management flagged inflation, a stronger dollar, and supply chain and labor challenges, and said a strategic-alternatives review remains ongoing with no decisions made.

negative_highlights: No revenue reported; company remains pre-revenue biotech dependent on cash reserves and milestone payments.
Phase 3 study design includes a forced steroid taper to zero over 12 weeks, requiring careful patient selection to avoid excluding too many candidates.
positive_highlights: Received FDA Fast Track Designation for efzofitimod for the treatment of pulmonary sarcoidosis.
Phase 3 study EFZO-FIT is projected to be the largest interventional study for patients with sarcoidosis to date.
Regulatory alignment achieved with US, EU, and Japan authorities regarding steroid reduction as a primary endpoint.
summary: aTyr Pharma reported Q2 FY2022 financial results with $89.3 million in cash and restricted cash as of June 30, 2022. The company incurred $9.1 million in R&D expenses and $3.4 million in G&A expenses for the quarter. Management highlighted the successful initiation of the global Phase 3 EFZO-FIT study for efzofitimod in pulmonary sarcoidosis, with plans to enroll the first patient in Q3 2022.

negative_highlights: Recorded an adjusted EBITDA loss of $8.2 million for H1 FY2022, compared to a net loss of $32.7 million.
Recognized a significant one-time goodwill impairment charge of $16 million and a write-down on the Hoshi investment due to market valuation declines.
Cash balance decreased from $37.6 million at year-end 2021 to only $10.3 million as of June 30, 2022.
positive_highlights: Revenue surged 604% year-over-year driven by full integration of JustCBD (acquired H1) and Vessel contributions.
Gross profit margin expanded significantly with household brands at 43% gross profit and Flora Labs exceeding 54%, aided by a tactical shift away from low-margin food categories.
Company remains debt-free while executing major operational milestones including the completion of its Colombian cultivation facility build-out.
summary: Flora reported H1 FY2022 revenue of $14.9 million (up 604% YoY) and gross profit of approximately $7 million (up 547%), driven by acquisitions JustCBD and Vessel, though operating expenses surged to $37.7 million due to integration costs and a $16 million goodwill impairment charge resulting in an adjusted EBITDA loss of $8.2 million. Management reiterated full-year revenue guidance between $35 million and $45 million despite acknowledging significant regulatory delays on Colombian dry flower exports until April 1, supply chain complexities, and the need to manage cash burn diligently with a balance sheet reduced from $37.6M to $10.3M.

negative_highlights: Production volume decreased slightly to 1,795 tonnes due to unannounced government COVID inspections causing facility shutdowns.
Chemical segment remains non-operational with zero revenue and a net loss of $475,000 due to equipment delivery delays.
Foreign currency translation resulted in a negative adjustment of $16.4 million due to RMB depreciation.
positive_highlights: Revenue increased 41% to $15.7 million driven by a 38% rise in bromine revenue ($13.9M).
Gross profit expanded 80% to $7.6 million as average note prices rose to $7,740/tonne.
Operating income swung from a loss of $2.4M to a profit of $5.1M despite higher allocated costs.
summary: Gulf Resources reported a strong Q2 FY2022 with revenue of $15.7 million (up 41% YoY) and EPS of $0.37, reversing a prior quarter loss. Gross profit surged 80% to $7.6 million driven by bromine price increases and supply constraints, while operating income turned positive at $5.1 million. Management noted that guidance for the full year is not yet provided as they wait for Q3 results before issuing new projections.

negative_highlights: Loss from operations increased to $5.39 million due to decreased gross margins caused by supply chain constraints.
Software subscription sales declined to $158,000 compared to $229,000 in the prior year quarter.
Management emphasized a need for hyper budget consciousness and achieving cash flow breakeven as the key priority.
positive_highlights: Total revenues increased significantly by 173% YoY due to senseFly acquisition inclusion and strong demand for Altum-PT/RedEdge-P sensors.
Sensor sales rose 23% to $2.10 million, with a backlog of approximately $1 million included in contract liabilities.
eBee TAC received design verification from EASA for BVLOS operations over people and was added to the DoD Blue UAS Cleared List.
summary: AgEagle reported Q2 FY2022 revenues of $5.29 million (up 173% YoY) and a net loss of $5.6 million ($0.07/share), driven by the inclusion of senseFly acquisition revenue but offset by supply chain constraints reducing gross margins. Management highlighted strong demand for new sensors with an order backlog of approximately $1 million, yet explicitly stated that achieving cash flow breakeven is the main priority to unlock future growth and weather economic headwinds.

negative_highlights: Revenue down 3% sequentially, with consumer spending cooling on home networking equipment
GAAP gross margins fell to 19.7% due to restatement-related inventory costing errors
Cash decreased to $4.7 million, down from $10.5 million prior quarter; NASDAQ minimum bid price deficiency noted
positive_highlights: Prime Day gross sales up 53% year-over-year, maintaining number one position on Amazon.com
Won additional sales space at Target and surpassed goal of 100,000 Minim Intelligent Network in Q3
Deferred revenue grew to $1.1 million
summary: Minim's Q2 2022 revenue was $12.9 million, down 3% sequentially, with gross margins dropping to 19.7% due to a restatement-related inventory costing correction. The company posted a net loss of $4.4 million (or $3.1 million before restatement) and adjusted EBITDA of negative $3.4 million. Inventory remained high at $34.4 million and cash fell to $4.7 million, though management expects improvement in the second half. The company also noted strong Prime Day sales (up 53% YoY) and a NASDAQ compliance risk due to a low stock price.

negative_highlights: Operating income of RMB31 million was below prior-year levels, with a RMB7 million loss in the claims-adjusting segment and RMB15 million loss from Yuntong branch investment

Product mix shifted toward lower-margin note weakness in-term savings products, with whole-life and annuity at 79% of first-year premiums vs. 68% a year earlier, while critical illness products fell to 7% from 20%
Total performing agents decreased 37.6% YoY, and management flagged ongoing COVID-19 and double-recording regulatory pressures into Q3
positive_highlights: Life insurance first-year premiums rose 43.7% YoY and 25% QoQ to RMB615.7 million
High-performing agents grew, with 100,000 Premium Agents up 41.2% YoY and per capita productivity among 3-month 10,000 Premium Agents up 33.3% YoY
Agents using digital tools showed productivity nearly 1.5x that of others, and active agents on the Lan Zhanggui 3.0 platform increased about 50%
summary: Fanhua reported Q2 FY2022 insurance gross written premiums up 12.2% YoY to RMB2.9 billion, with life first-year premiums up 43.7% YoY and 25% QoQ to RMB615.7 million. Operating income was RMB31 million, below the prior-year level, largely due to a RMB7 million claims-adjusting segment loss, a RMB15 million loss from Yuntong branch investment, and RMB10.3 million in IT infrastructure spending; excluding these, operating income would have been about RMB63 million, up 34%. Management guided to H2 2022 operating income of no less than RMB30 million, noting continued investment and COVID/double-recording pressures, while pointing to a shift toward lower-margin short-term savings products (whole-life and annuity at 79% of first-year premiums vs. 68% a year earlier) as a drag on commission income.

negative_highlights: Currency headwinds: weighted average depreciation of 19% in operating countries, impacting top-line guidance.
Guided to lower end of top-line guidance at 90%-100% of $141 million, though still a beat on constant-currency basis.
Adjusted EBITDA still negative at -$3.9 million per month in July.
positive_highlights: Total ticket sales up 3x YoY to $29 million; bookings up 3.5x YoY to $22.6 million.
Contribution margin breakeven achieved in July, ahead of plan; Egypt turned EBITDA positive in August.
M&A synergies delivering: Turkey and Argentina revenues at 2.0x and 2.1x pre-integration levels, with contribution margin improvements of 9% and 32%.
summary: Q2 2022 total ticket sales hit an all-time high of $29 million, up 3x year-over-year, with bookings of $22.6 million up 3.5x. Contribution margin reached breakeven in July, and adjusted EBITDA burn improved to -$3.9 million in July. Management guided to 90%-100% of the initial $141 million top-line target, mostly due to FX headwinds, and expects to beat the adjusted EBITDA target of -$87 million by 5%-10%.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to $8.4 million in FY2022 from $7.3 million in FY2021
Cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities fell to ~$8.2 million from ~$12.6 million a year earlier
Government support income declined to $437,000 from $1.98 million, and no formal revenue guidance was provided
positive_highlights: Completed sample collection and analysis in the ~40-patient Type II diabetes saliva/blood glucose study, with results described as encouraging and consistent with prior studies
Selected the University of Newcastle site for the Biosensor manufacturing facility, with first equipment on site and ~60% of equipment expected delivered by year-end at no construction capital outlay
Executed an exclusivity agreement with Intelligent Fingerprinting for fingerprint sweat-based drug screening, seen as a path to revenue growth
summary: GBS reported a preliminary FY2022 net loss of $8.4 million, or $0.57 per share, versus a $7.3 million ($0.65) loss in FY2021, with cash, equivalents and marketable securities falling to approximately $8.2 million from $12.6 million a year earlier. Government support income dropped to $437,000 from $1.98 million. R&D spend was flat at $3.8 million while employee benefits rose to $2.3 million from $1.9 million on commercialization hiring. Management provided no formal revenue or EPS guidance, said existing cash funds operations into the second half of calendar 2023, and reported continued negotiation of the Intelligent Fingerprinting exclusivity/acquisition, with equipment deliveries staged and no construction capital outlay as the university builds the Newcastle facility.

negative_highlights: Total revenue declined ~8% year-over-year to $72.8 million from $79 million
Gross margin fell to 39.8% from 42.2% a year ago, with management noting product and logistics cost pressure not yet fully offset by price increases
Cash and cash equivalents dropped to ~$48 million from $59 million sequentially on the Omega legal settlement, lower revenue from supply constraints, and deferred billings
positive_highlights: Software and Subscription Services revenue rose 13% sequentially and 7% year-over-year to $44.5 million, now 61% of consolidated revenue
Total global subscribers increased 9% sequentially and 32% year-over-year to 1.3 million
Adjusted EBITDA improved sequentially to $4.8 million (7% margin) from $1.9 million (3% margin) in Q1
summary: CalAmp reported Q2 FY2023 revenue of $72.8 million, up ~13% sequentially from $64.7 million but down ~8% year-over-year from $79 million; Software and Subscription Services revenue rose 13% sequentially and 7% year-over-year to $44.5 million (61% of total). Non-GAAP adjusted EBITDA was $4.8 million (7% margin), up from $1.9 million (3%) last quarter but down from $8.3 million (11%) a year ago, and gross margin of 39.8% fell from 42.2% a year ago. The company reiterated it will not provide quarterly guidance but expects low- to mid-single-digit sequential revenue growth in Q3, with no full-year guidance and difficult shipment visibility. Cash fell to $48 million from $59 million on the Omega settlement, lower revenue tied to supply constraints, and rising deferred billings from multiyear subscription conversions.

negative_highlights: Gross margin is extremely low at 5.6% as the company proceeds into the later stage of its new business model.
The Q&A session was abruptly cut note weakness in after only three questions, preventing management from addressing investor concerns regarding financials or specific guidance updates.
positive_highlights: Revenue surged $16.9 million year-over-year driven by the expansion of the 5G messaging business platform.
Secured a major procurement agreement for ultrasonic air disinfection equipment valued at no less than RMB35 million ($5M) with delivery scheduled by end of 2022.
summary: Datasea reported FY2022 revenue of $17.08 million, a massive 96% increase from the prior year driven entirely by new 5G messaging services ($17.02M), while gross margin contracted to just 5.6%. Management provided no EPS or GAAP/Adjusted earnings figures and offered only qualitative guidance for future growth in acoustic intelligence and Smart City sectors, with a Q&A session that was cut short due to time constraints.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA remained negative at $0.95 million pro forma, reflecting heavy investment in growth infrastructure.
Management explicitly stated it would not pursue further acquisitions before year-end due to a conservative market approach.
Operating expenses increased significantly to $10.86 million pro forma, driven by stock-based compensation and IPO preparation.
positive_highlights: Pro forma revenue grew 17.2% year-over-year, outpacing global education market growth.
Campus revenue increased by 48%, driven by the gradual lifting of COVID-19 restrictions.
Group gross margin expanded to 29.97% due to improved results from the campus business.
summary: Genius Group reported H1 FY2022 pro forma revenue of $16.57 million, representing a 17.2% year-over-year increase driven by campus and digital education segments. The company posted negative adjusted EBITDA of $0.95 million on a pro forma basis, citing increased investments in marketing and senior leadership positions. Management maintained its 2022 guidance at the lower revenue range and adopted a more conservative approach to acquisitions for the remainder of the year.

negative_highlights: Billings declined 23.9% YoY to $105.1M and 11% sequentially from Q2, driven by lower entry-level subscriptions and conversions
Adjusted CFFO fell to $13.1M from $34.7M a year ago; adjusted CFFO margin contracted to 12.5% from 25.2% YoY
Paid subscribers fell 7.4% to 894,000 and ARPU dropped 28% to $556 from $772 on a 31% decline in trailing billings
positive_highlights: Adjusted CFFO margin improved to 12.5% in Q3 from 11% in the first half as a direct result of the cost-cutting initiative
Overhead reduced by nearly $8M ($31M annualized) versus Q1 2022 run rate, with total annualized overhead savings of $37M identified
Direct marketing spend cut by $18M (~$6M/month), in line with the targeted $37M reduction for the second half
summary: Revenue fell 14.7% YoY to $119.9M and billings dropped 23.9% to $105.1M; adjusted CFFO declined to $13.1M from $34.7M, though its margin improved to 12.5% from 11% in the first half on cost cuts. Paid subscribers fell 7.4% to 894,000 and ARPU dropped to $556 from $772. Management cited persistent macro-driven subscriber hesitancy, cut overhead and direct marketing to hit stated savings targets, and gave no explicit forward revenue or billings guidance beyond expecting cost-savings trend to continue in Q4.

negative_highlights: Cash declined to $29.4 million at September 30 from $99.7 million at June 30
Management is pursuing a full or partial sale via PJT Partners and said the company requires more capital to reach breakeven
Cost actions include eliminating approximately 50% of the workforce and pausing Las Vegas expansion
positive_highlights: Net customer additions exceeded 10,000 in the quarter, a first for the company
Serviceable footprint grew 18% year-over-year and customers grew 66%, with total activated units above 450,000
Withdrawal from RDOF freed up approximately $17 million in restricted cash
summary: Starry reported Q3 FY2022 net customer additions of more than 10,000, serviceable footprint growth of 18% year-over-year, and activated units of over 450,000 with roughly 20% penetration; no revenue, EPS, or margin figures were disclosed. Cash fell to $29.4 million at September 30 from $99.7 million at June 30, and the company hired PJT Partners to advise on M&A, capital raising, and balance sheet alternatives including a full or partial sale. Management outlined cost cuts including a roughly 50% workforce reduction, withdrawal from the FCC RDOF program, and a pause on Las Vegas expansion, citing macro-driven financing challenges. Guidance was effectively withdrawn, with no Q4 or full-year outlook provided and no Q&A taken due to the ongoing PJT process.

negative_highlights: Interim analysis of IMU-935 in moderate-to-severe psoriasis showed no benefit for the two active doses compared to placebo, with an unexpectedly large decrease in PASI in the placebo arm.
Net loss widened to $21.2M in Q3 2022 from $19.3M in Q3 2021.
R&D expenses increased to $16.5M from $15.5M year-over-year, driven by external development costs and higher personnel expense.
positive_highlights: Strengthened balance sheet with a $60 million private financing in October 2022, extending cash runway into Q4 2024.
IMU-856 received a U.S. Notice of Allowance for a key composition-of-matter patent, expected to provide protection into at least 2038.
IMU-856 Phase 1 SAD/MAD data showed favorable safety, tolerability, and pharmacokinetics with no maximum tolerated dose reached.
summary: Immunic's Q3 2022 results showed net loss of $21.2M, or $0.69 per share, versus a $19.3M loss in Q3 2021. R&D expenses rose to $16.5M from $15.5M, driven by its three clinical programs, while cash stood at $72.8M before a $60M PIPE in October that extends the runway into Q4 2024. The key negative was an interim analysis of IMU-935 in psoriasis where group-level mean data showed no benefit over placebo, with an outsized placebo response; the company will provide next steps in Q1 2023. Positive pipeline updates included an IP allowance for IMU-856 and favorable Phase 1 SAD/MAD data for that candidate.

negative_highlights: Total revenue fell 28% sequentially to $341 million as Ecommerce units declined 30%
Q4 GPPU expected to fall sharply to roughly $2,500-$3,500 from $4,206 due to aged inventory and declining used-car prices
Expected full-year Ecommerce unit volume below prior forecasted range after a third-party sales staff reduction cut contracts 32% in the four weeks after late August
positive_highlights: Ecommerce gross profit per unit rose 16% sequentially to $4,206
Adjusted EBITDA loss, excluding non-recurring costs, improved $20 million sequentially to $57.5 million
Restricted cash reduced by $59 million sequentially, driven by titling and registration improvements
summary: Vroom reported Q3 FY2022 total revenue fell 28% to $341 million as Ecommerce units dropped 30%, while adjusted EBITDA loss excluding non-recurring costs improved by $20 million sequentially to a $57.5 million loss and Ecommerce gross profit per unit rose 16% to $4,206. Net loss was $51 million, helped by a $38 million debt extinguishment gain from repurchasing $56 million face value of convertible notes for $18 million and a $16 million UACC securitization gain; liquidity ended at $510 million with year-end liquidity still guided near the midpoint of the $450-$565 million range. Management said it expects full-year Ecommerce unit volume below its prior forecasted range, adjusted EBITDA loss better than the midpoint of its guided loss range, and warned Q4 GPPU could fall to roughly $2,500-$3,500 from $4,206 due to aged vehicle sales and declining used-car prices. The quarter was also pressured by a large unexpected reduction in third-party sales staffing in late August that cut contracts 32% over the following four weeks, and the sales function is not expected to be fully staffed until Q1 2023.

negative_highlights: Total Q3 revenue decreased to $2.6M from $2.7M in the prior year.
Cost of revenue increased by 45% due to specimen mix changes, offsetting volume declines.
COVID-19 revenues declined significantly and are expected to continue declining unpredictably.
positive_highlights: Non-COVID revenue hit an all-time high record at $2.3 million (88% of total).
Company successfully mobilized operations following executive departures without missing a beat on core business continuity.
summary: iSpecimen reported Q3 FY2022 revenue of $2.6 million, a decrease from the prior year's $2.7 million driven by declining COVID-19 specimen sales and geopolitical impacts in Russia/Ukraine. Non-COVID revenue reached an all-time high record at 88% of total ($2.26M), but overall performance was weighed down by higher costs per unit due to mix changes, resulting in a miss relative to the prior year's comparable period.

negative_highlights: Net income fell to $7.06 million ($0.37/share) from $28.11 million ($1.54) on a smaller prior-year gain on sale
Transaction volume 'way, way down' and cap rates up at least 125 bps, with bid-ask spread delaying seller repricing
Rent growth velocity has slowed and management flagged emerging affordability concerns among renters
positive_highlights: AFFO per share rose to $0.38 from $0.31 a year ago on improved operating margins and partner buyouts
Same-store NOI grew 18.3% with revenue up 11.4% and expenses up only 3.6%
New lease spreads of 16.1% and renewal spreads of 10.8%, with average rents up 13% to $1,301
summary: BRT reported Q3 FY2022 net income of $7.06 million ($0.37/diluted share) versus $28.11 million ($1.54) a year ago, the decline driven by a larger prior-year gain on sale at an unconsolidated property; AFFO rose to $7.17 million ($0.38/share) from $5.66 million ($0.31). Same-store revenue grew 11.4%, expenses 3.6%, and NOI 18.3%, with average monthly rents up 13% to $1,301 and occupancy flat at 96.2%. Management gave no formal forward guidance, noted transaction volume has slowed considerably and cap rates have risen at least 125 bps, and said rent growth remains positive but has decelerated from prior quarters.

negative_highlights: Q4 revenue guidance was reduced to $48M due to a combination of foreign exchange impacts and slowing customer orders.
Customer order intake fell by approximately 14% quarter-over-quarter compared to Q3 last year.
Demand for the acquired FrontRow audio solutions has declined as school districts have exhausted initial post-pandemic spending.
positive_highlights: Record gross profit margin expanded to 31% (up from Q1's 25%) due to lower supply chain costs and FrontRow integration benefits.
Adjusted EBITDA grew significantly year-over-year, reaching $9.9 million despite FX headwinds.
Company generated positive cash flow from operations for the first time in its history.
summary: Boxlight reported Q3 FY2022 revenue of $68.7 million (up 12.7% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $9.9 million (up 38% YoY), beating prior guidance due to favorable foreign exchange impacts that would have otherwise pushed results above the original guide. Management revised Q4 guidance down to $48M revenue and $2M adjusted EBITDA, citing a mix of FX headwinds in Europe and a temporary slowing of demand across both regions. Despite this caution for the near term, management maintains confidence in double-digit growth for 2023 driven by market share gains.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA was negative $45.2 million, a steep loss despite landing within guidance
Prepaid block sales fell year-over-year in Q3 after the June price increase pulled sales into Q2
Plans to cut SG&A from 16% of revenue to low double digits imply roughly $40 million of EBITDA benefit needed over 12-18 months
positive_highlights: Revenue of $420 million rose 39% year-over-year, ahead of 25%+ growth guidance
Adjusted contribution margin of 5.1% exceeded the high end of the 4.5%-5% guidance range
Pro forma cash and equivalents of $545 million including the EETC debt financing
summary: Wheels Up reported Q3 FY2022 revenue of $420 million, up 39% year-over-year and ahead of its 25%+ growth guidance, driven by a 20% increase in flight revenue per live leg and a $35 million year-over-year jump in aircraft sales. Adjusted contribution margin came in at 5.1%, above the high end of the 4.5%-5% guide, while adjusted EBITDA was negative $45.2 million, within the negative $42 million to $47 million range. Q4 guidance calls for revenue up approximately 15% year-over-year, adjusted contribution margin of 4.25%-4.75%, and adjusted EBITDA of negative $40 million to negative $45 million. Management outlined cost cuts targeting SG&A from 16% of revenue to low double digits and reaffirmed a path to positive adjusted EBITDA in 2024, while Q3 prepaid block sales fell year-over-year after a Q2 pull-forward from a June price increase.

negative_highlights: Expected disruption to prescription growth in Q4 due to ending in-person promotion
note, general and administrative expenses up 9% YoY
Non-cash loss of $6.5 million on warrant liabilities
positive_highlights: Q3 net product revenue up 23% QoQ to $1.6 million
Cash runway extended into Q2 2024
FURI enrollment reached target of 200 subjects
summary: SCYNEXIS reported Q3 2022 net product revenue of $1.6 million, up 23% sequentially and up from $1.3 million in Q2, while total cash was $96.1 million with runway extended into Q2 2024. The company is executing a strategic shift toward hospital-based invasive fungal indications, ending in-person promotion and pursuing a partner for BREXAFEMME; it expects disruption to prescription growth in Q4. Pipeline progress is mixed: FURI enrollment reached 200 (larger than planned), CARES and SCYNERGIA are closing, MARIO enrollment active with data expected early 2024, and an sNDA for recurrent VVC has a PDUFA date of November 30, 2022.

negative_highlights: FDA issued a Refusal to File (RTF) letter for roluperidone NDA, preventing substantive review
Non-cash interest expense increased by $0.9 million Y/Y due to accruing royalties on the Seltorexant deal
positive_highlights: Net loss narrowed sequentially to $6.9 million from $9.2 million last year
R&D expenses decreased by approximately $2.1 million QoQ and Y/Y primarily due to the completion of Phase 3 trial extensions in 2021
summary: Minerva Neurosciences reported a net loss of $6.9 million for the third quarter ended September 30, 2022, compared to a prior year loss of $9.2 million, driven by lower R&D and G&A expenses but offset by increased non-cash interest expense on royalty liabilities. The company received a Refusal to File (RTF) letter from the FDA regarding its NDA for roluperidone in October 2022 and has requested a Type A meeting before year-end, with no new financial guidance provided due to this regulatory uncertainty.

negative_highlights: Strategic decision to pause internal clinical development of ATYR-2810 due to current market conditions and capital prioritization.
No new financial guidance provided for cash runway or revenue, relying on milestones from partner Kyorin.
Oncology program 2810 will rely on non-dilutive funding sources like academic collaborations rather than internal spend.
positive_highlights: First patient dosed in EFZO-FIT Phase 3 study in September, meeting aggressive timelines and guidance.
Received FDA Fast Track designation for efzofitimod for the treatment of systemic sclerosis (SSc).
Published full results from Phase 1b/2a study in CHEST showing substantial benefit including steroid reduction.
summary: aTyr Pharma reported Q3 FY2022 results with $79.6 million in cash and restricted cash as of September 30, 2022. The company initiated the global pivotal Phase 3 study (EFZO-FIT) for its lead candidate efzofitimod in pulmonary sarcoidosis, dosing the first patient in September and meeting aggressive timelines. Management announced a strategic decision to pause internal clinical development of the oncology asset ATYR-2810 to prioritize capital for EFZO-FIT, while retaining the IP value through potential academic collaborations.

negative_highlights: Cash, equivalents and marketable securities declined to approximately $5.74 million as of September 30, 2022 from $8.24 million at June 30, 2022
Management stated cash resources cover expenses and capital commitments only into the first half of 2023
Net loss improvement was driven by $0.31 million of government support income rather than operating performance
positive_highlights: Closed acquisition of Intelligent Fingerprinting Limited on October 4, adding fingerprint drug-testing technology and manufacturing capability
Reported preliminary FY2022 net loss improved to $1.21 million ($0.08/share) from $1.43 million ($0.10/share) a year earlier
Announced new client relationships with Goldstar Transport, Eastern Airways, and The Glass Systems Group, plus CE marking for a saliva-based COVID-19 rapid antigen test
summary: Intelligent Bio Solutions reported a preliminary FY2022 net loss of $1.21 million ($0.08/share) versus a $1.43 million ($0.10/share) loss in the prior year, with the improvement driven primarily by $0.31 million of government support income rather than operations. Cash, equivalents and marketable securities fell to approximately $5.74 million as of September 30, 2022 from $8.24 million at June 30, 2022, and management guided to a cash runway sufficient only into the first half of 2023. The quarter's main event was the October 4 close of the Intelligent Fingerprinting acquisition, which added a fingerprint drug-testing platform, a CE-marked saliva COVID antigen test, and new customer wins including Goldstar Transport, Eastern Airways, and The Glass Systems Group. No formal revenue guidance was issued; management targeted first IFP sales in Australia in Q1 2023 and framed U.S. FDA market entry as a two-year plan requiring an estimated $2 million to $3 million of funding.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined due to foreign exchange shifts and pandemic lockdowns in China delaying deliveries
Management warned that new territories are being shut down by zero COVID policy impacting global market access
HEVI business faces challenges securing the first fleet deal amidst a need for significant market education
positive_highlights: Net income surged 67% year-over-year despite headwinds
Gross margin maintained at 22.1% with a shift toward higher-value products
Opened first U.S.-based assembly site outside Baltimore, targeting production of 500 units annually
summary: GTEC reported Q3 FY2022 revenue of $21.8 million, a slight decrease from the prior year's $23.1 million due to foreign exchange impacts and pandemic-related shutdowns in China that delayed deliveries despite record unit production of 31,303 drivetrains. Net income surged 67% to $2.1 million driven by improved operating efficiency (operating expenses down 10%) and lower tax rates rather than top-line growth. Management expressed caution regarding Q4 delivery timelines due to the uncertainty of China's zero COVID policy while highlighting progress in their HEVI electric equipment division.

negative_highlights: Decided to discontinue planning for the MANTRA-3 study in Merkel cell carcinoma, representing a strategic retreat from an indicated opportunity.
Net loss of $18 million driven by R&D expenses of $14.5 million and G&A expenses of $3.9 million.
Management explicitly stated they will not provide additional guidance on subsequent milestones for the MANTRA-2 basket trial.
positive_highlights: Completed enrollment of the pivotal MANTRA trial with 175 patients five months ahead of schedule.
Raised guidance for top-line data from H1 2023 to Q1 2023.
MANTRA-2 interim data showed early antitumor activity including two unconfirmed partial responses and tumor regressions in a diverse patient population.
summary: Rain Therapeutics reported a net loss of $18 million for Q3 FY2022, slightly better than the prior year's $18.4 million loss, with R&D expenses decreasing to $14.5 million. The company raised its guidance for top-line data from the pivotal MANTRA trial from the first half of 2023 to the first quarter of 2023 following accelerated enrollment completion. However, management announced a strategic pivot to deprioritize Merkel cell carcinoma (MANTRA-3) and focus on larger market opportunities like MANTRA-4, citing a need for prudent cash management despite raising $50 million in new capital.

negative_highlights: October Prime Day sales were lighter than hoped
Cash position thin at $1.9 million with only $0.5 million credit availability
Going concern language expected in 10-Q due to line maturity
positive_highlights: Revenue up 8% sequentially to $13.8 million
Gross margin expanded to 22.3% from 19.7%
Inventory reduced by $4 million in the quarter
summary: Q3 FY2022 revenue was $13.8 million, up 8% sequentially, with gross margin improving to 22.3% from 19.7%, but net loss widened to $4.1 million. Inventory reduced to $30.3 million from $34.3 million, and cash stood at $1.9 million with minimal credit availability. Management flagged October Prime Day underperformance, aggressive pricing, and a plan to exit the ISP business, while expanding e-commerce channels and launching new WiFi 6E products. They expect inventory to fall further and cash to remain about flat year-end, but acknowledged a going concern issue ahead of the 10-Q filing.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to $14.4 million from $8.2 million year-over-year
Gastroparesis symptom data not yet available until year-end
Only 6-9 patients per group limit trial conclusions
positive_highlights: NGC potency increased to 50 times greater than FDA-approved capecitabine
12852 showed statistically better gastric emptying vs placebo (p<0.1)
Cash runway into Q3 2023 sufficient to complete three ongoing trials
summary: Processa reported Q3 2022 results highlighting positive Phase 1B data for Next Generation Capecitabine (NGC) showing well-tolerated regimens and 50x greater potency than capecitabine, and positive Phase 2A proof-of-concept for 12852 in gastroparesis with gastric emptying significantly improved (p<0.1) at 0.5 mg. Cash of $9.1 million is expected to fund operations into Q3 2023, while net loss widened to $14.4 million for nine months. The company plans to initiate Phase 2B trials for both programs in 2023.

negative_highlights: Q3 revenue declined roughly 6% YoY to $4.2 million on delayed IIoT shipments and lower sales in that product line
Gross margin fell to 70% from 73% on sales mix, and non-GAAP adjusted EBITDA loss widened to $8.2 million from $6.7 million
Net loss attributable to stockholders was $17.6 million, including a $7.6 million goodwill impairment, with no quantitative forward guidance provided
positive_highlights: Nine-month revenue rose approximately 30% to $14.1 million from $10.9 million in the prior year period
Definitive agreement signed to spin off and note the enterprise apps business to KINS Technology Group at a $69 million pre-transaction value
Global head count reduced by approximately 20% to streamline operations and accelerate the path to profitability
summary: Q3 FY2022 revenue fell ~6% YoY to $4.2 million versus $4.5 million, which management attributed to delayed IIoT shipments and lower sales in that product line, while nine-month revenue rose ~30% to $14.1 million. Gross margin contracted to 70% from 73% on sales mix, net loss attributable to stockholders was $17.6 million (including a $7.6 million goodwill impairment), and non-GAAP adjusted EBITDA loss widened to $8.2 million from $6.7 million. Cash stood at approximately $53.2 million as of September 30, 2022, after a $45.8 million Series A preferred redemption, and was subsequently increased by $15 million in gross proceeds from a registered direct offering. Management gave no quantitative forward guidance, citing market volatility, customer uncertainty and supply chain challenges, while noting a ~20% headcount reduction, a definitive KINS spinoff at a $69 million pre-transaction value, and a nonbinding LOI for the remainder of the business on which it declined specifics.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA loss widened to $2 million from $1.6 million year-over-year due to equity compensation and JV losses
Opening of Tampa, Bay Area, Kansas City clinics delayed into the New Year rather than by year-end
Financing options limited pending audit completion on material acquisition
positive_highlights: Three operating INVO Centers combined revenue increased sequentially and over the prior year period
Clinics have become cash flow self-supporting with no significant funding required since Q2 2022
First baby born in Malaysia partnership; LOI signed for acquisition of a profitable mid-sized practice
summary: Revenue for Q3 FY2022 was approximately $235,000 (up from ~$219k prior year), while the company reported a net loss of $2.5 million and an adjusted EBITDA loss of $2 million compared to losses in the same period last year. Management highlighted progress at existing clinics which are becoming self-funding but noted delays on new center openings into early 2023 due to focus on closing a pending acquisition LOI.

negative_highlights: Cash balance decreased from $55.1 million at year-end 2021 to $42.6 million as of September 30, 2022.
R&D expenses increased significantly to $3.6 million in Q3 2022 compared to $1.8 million in Q3 2021.
Management indicated that quarterly cash burn will increase upon entering the new Phase 1/2a combination study.
positive_highlights: Announced initiation of a Phase 1/2a clinical trial for narazaciclib combined with letrozole in low-grade endometrioid endometrial cancer starting Q1 2023.
Encouraging safety data for narazaciclib showing no significant bone marrow suppression or diarrhea, allowing for continuous daily dosing unlike competitors.
Rigosertib combination therapy showed a complete response in a patient with RDEB-associated skin cancer on therapy for over 15 months.
summary: Onconova reported a net loss of $5.4 million ($0.26 per share) for Q3 FY2022, an increase from the $3.5 million loss in the prior year quarter, driven by R&D expenses rising to $3.6 million. Management provided no specific financial guidance but stated that current cash reserves of $42.6 million are sufficient to fund operations and clinical trials through 2024. The call focused on positive clinical updates, including plans to initiate a Phase 1/2a trial for narazaciclib in endometrial cancer in Q1 2023 and updated efficacy data for rigosertib in lung cancer.

negative_highlights: Second patient (colorectal cancer, dose Level 2) achieved only stable disease and progressed at 12 weeks due to new liver and lung lesions
Cash runway guided only into Q2 2023, with management citing the ATM and shelf as financing options
Collaboration revenue of ~$2.9 million was driven by a one-time milestone that management said will be the most meaningful payment over the next few years
positive_highlights: Confirmed partial response in first patient at the lowest dose level with 51.2% target lesion reduction at week 12 and six-month progression-free survival
TCR-T cell persistence observed at ~30% of all T cells at 24 weeks and infiltration of both helper and killer TCR-T cells into the tumor
Operating cash burn reduced 36% to ~$6.1 million and R&D expense down 46% to ~$7.9 million versus Q3 2021
summary: Alaunos reported Q3 2022 collaboration revenue of ~$2.9 million (vs ~$0.4 million in Q3 2021) from Solasia's darinaparsin sales milestone, a net loss of ~$8.9 million ($0.04/share) versus ~$22.7 million ($0.11/share) a year ago, R&D expense down 46% to ~$7.9 million and G&A down 60% to ~$3.3 million. Cash and equivalents were ~$37.8 million with restricted cash of ~$13.9 million, and operating cash burn was ~$6.1 million versus ~$9.6 million a year ago; management guided to cash runway into Q2 2023. Clinical highlights included a confirmed partial response in the first patient at the lowest dose level, a second patient with stable disease that progressed at 12 weeks, TCR-T persistence to six months, and planned dosing of the next patient in Q4 2022 plus an IND amendment for two new TCRs and a shift to cryopreserved product. No formal EPS or revenue guidance was provided; the key change versus prior periods was the first-in-human clinical validation and a materially lower cost structure.

negative_highlights: Gross margin contracted to 11.8% from 20.2% on higher variable costs and expense reallocation
Net bookings fell to $2.2 million from $5.6 million and quarter-end backlog declined to $6.8 million from $9.9 million
Net loss widened to $1.0 million from $0.4 million; operating expenses rose to $1.7 million from $1.2 million
positive_highlights: Revenue up 37% YoY to $5.1 million from $3.7 million
Cash and cash equivalents of $21.1 million as of September 30, 2022 versus $2.2 million at December 31, 2021, driven by $21.7 million of equity financing proceeds
New non-cannabis contracts signed with indoor produce farms in New York and Florida plus a strategic alliance with Hydrobuilder Holdings
summary: Q3 2022 revenue rose 37% to $5.1 million from $3.7 million a year ago on supply-chain recovery, but gross margin fell to 11.8% from 20.2% and the net loss widened to $1.0 million (negative $0.13 per share) from $0.4 million. Net bookings dropped to $2.2 million from $5.6 million and quarter-end backlog fell to $6.8 million from $9.9 million, though backlog is expected to convert over 18 months. Cash rose to $21.1 million (from $2.2 million at year-end) on $21.7 million of equity financing, and the company remains debt-free. Management gave no numeric guidance, cited growth initiatives including a Hydrobuilder alliance and water treatment products, and said partnership benefits should arrive in 2023.

negative_highlights: Loss from operations increased significantly to $5.1M due to supply chain constraints and higher G&A/R&D costs
Gross profit margins contracted in Q3 specifically attributed to ongoing supply chain issues
Cash position declined materially to $5.3M compared to $14.6M at the end of 2021
positive_highlights: Revenue surged 172% YoY to $5.5M driven by senseFly acquisition integration and sensor sales growth
Net income turned positive at $1.7M due to a $6.5M gain on extinguishment of debt from satisfying hold-back amounts
eBee drones achieved FAA approval for operations over people/vehicles, creating new commercial use cases
summary: AgEagle reported Q3 FY2022 revenues of $5.5 million (up 172% YoY) and net income of $1.7 million driven by a one-time gain on extinguishment of debt, while the loss from operations widened to $5.1 million due to supply chain constraints and increased G&A costs related to acquisitions. Management highlighted strong demand for eBee drones following FAA approvals over people/vehicles but noted that gross profit margins contracted in Q3. The company raised approximately $14.6 million via financing activities during the first nine months, leaving a cash position of $5.3 million.

negative_highlights: COVID pandemic caused softening of bromine prices and delays in equipment delivery for the chemical factory.
Factory number eight is not yet producing; revenue from it will be recognized in Q4 2022.
Government approval is still pending for factories number two and ten, with no clear timeline.
positive_highlights: Revenues increased 29% YoY to $22.8 million; profit before tax rose 68% to $12.4 million.
Gross margin expanded significantly to 63% from 56% in the prior year.
Full-year guidance for bromine and crude salt segments was raised, with projected profits of $22.4M-$22.8M.
summary: Gulf Resources reported Q3 FY2022 revenues of $22.8 million (up 29% YoY) and EPS of $0.86 (up 65%), significantly exceeding prior guidance for both revenue ($20-21.8M) and profit before tax ($9-10.3M). Management raised full-year guidance for the bromine and crude salt segments, projecting revenues of $62.7M-$64.1M and profits of $22.4M-$22.8M despite COVID-related price softening and production delays. The company noted that while it cannot currently watch back shares or pay dividends due to capital controls, it is exploring mechanisms like executive share repurchases in RMB.

negative_highlights: Net loss from continuing operations widened to $2.7 million versus a net income of $511,000 a year earlier.
Gross margin declined to 52% from a prior period (exact prior margin not stated) due to distributor mix and discounts.
Guidance of $100 million for calendar 2023 remains unchanged, and the current quarter was affected by delays in closing acquisitions.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 199% year-over-year to $11.6 million, driven by four acquisitions.
Gross profit increased by $3.4 million to $6 million.
Completed $23.5 million sale of select CBD assets, reducing debt and interest expense by ~$900,000 annually.
summary: Upexi reported Q1 FY2023 revenue of $11.6 million, up 199% year-over-year from $3.9 million, driven by recent acquisitions. Gross profit rose to $6 million but gross margin declined to 52% due to distributor sales and discounts. The company posted a net loss from continuing operations of $2.7 million, versus a net income of $511,000 in the prior year. Management guided to calendar 2023 revenue of $100 million, the same baseline as previously projected.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined 14% YoY to $20.3 million due to falling MAVIRET sales.
Net loss per share increased to $1.27 from $1.22 in the prior-year quarter.
R&D expense guidance for fiscal 2023 increases to $210-$230 million, reflecting higher clinical investment.
positive_highlights: Initiated SPRINT, a Phase 2 trial of EDP-235 in COVID-19 patients, with data expected in H1 2023.
Cash of $278.5 million expected to fund operations into Q4 fiscal 2024.
Early RSV season in Northern Hemisphere may accelerate enrollment in ongoing EDP-938 trials.
summary: Enanta reported Q4 FY2022 total revenue of $20.3 million, down from $23.6 million year-over-year due to lower AbbVie MAVIRET sales. Net loss widened to $26.3 million ($1.27 per share) from $24.6 million ($1.22 per share) in the prior-year quarter. R&D expenses decreased to $34.8 million from $48.9 million, while G&A increased to $12.6 million from $8.4 million. The company initiated SPRINT, a Phase 2 trial for COVID-19 candidate EDP-235, and provided fiscal 2023 guidance for R&D expense of $210-$230 million and G&A of $46-$52 million.

negative_highlights: Q4 operating income guidance of no less than RMB30 million implies a sequential decline from Q3's RMB32.2 million.
Total number of performing agents declined, and agent recruitment slowed due to stricter standards and COVID-19.
Industry life insurance gross written premiums grew only 1.3% YoY, a sharp deceleration from Q2.
positive_highlights: Operating income of RMB32.2 million grew 14.2% YoY and beat expectations.
Life insurance premiums grew 6.2% YoY to RMB2.8 billion; regular first-year premiums up 9.1% YoY.
Number of 100,000 premium agents grew 46% YoY, contributing 48% of first-year premiums, up from 39%.
summary: Fanhua reported Q3 2022 life insurance premiums up 6.2% YoY to RMB2.8 billion, with regular first-year premiums up 9.1% YoY to RMB529.7 million, and operating income of RMB32.2 million, up 14.2% YoY, which beat management's expectations. However, total performing agents declined, and the company guided Q4 operating income to no less than RMB30 million, implying a sequential decline from Q3's RMB32.2 million. High-performing agent productivity improved, with per capita productivity up nearly 20% YoY and 100,000 premium agents growing 46% YoY, contributing 48% of first-year premiums. The macro and COVID-19 headwinds remain significant, and agent recruitment has slowed.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to $7.4 million compared to a net loss of $3.6 million last year
Operating expenses increased substantially from $4.2M to $10M due to acquired businesses and infrastructure expansion
Cash balance decreased significantly to $5.9 million, down from $37.6M at end-2021
positive_highlights: Revenue reached an all-time quarterly record of approximately $10.8 million
Gross margin significantly improved to 46.2% from 29.6% in the prior year period
Colombian cultivation facility is fully operational with high-THC harvesting underway
summary: Flora Growth reported Q3 FY2022 revenue of $10.8 million (up 414% YoY) and gross margin expansion to 46.2%, driven by the integration of acquired brands JustCBD, Vessel, and No Cap. Despite a net loss widening to $7.4 million due to OpEx increases from acquisitions and M&A activities, management reaffirmed its full-year 2022 revenue guidance range of $35M-$45M without raising it.

negative_highlights: Estimated 2022 revenue will be under EUR2 million, a very low base for a company with a EUR61 million asset base.
Q3 operating loss of EUR5.5 million driven by EUR4.6 million of operating expenses, with adjusted admin expenses guided to EUR4-4.5 million per quarter.
Continued use of the ATM facility, note 300,000 shares in Q3 at an average price of $7.35 and 400,000 shares in Q4 at an average price of $4.
positive_highlights: Secured an additional EUR30 million grant, bringing total approved grants to about EUR49 million.
Announced two tech sale contracts totaling EUR7 million in Portugal and Spain, plus a 50-50 JV for a 75 MW Bakersfield, California project.
Introduced the HEVO-Chain centralized PEM electrolyzer, with production planned for 2024 and a target of 500 MW annual capacity by end of 2025.
summary: Fusion Fuel reported a Q3 FY2022 operating loss of EUR5.5 million on operating expenses of EUR4.6 million, with no material revenue; management guided 2022 revenue to under EUR2 million and targeted over EUR40 million for 2023. Adjusted administration expense guidance was set at roughly EUR4-4.5 million per quarter, and the company disclosed new commercial wins including a EUR30 million grant, entry into the U.S. and Italian markets, and the HEVO-Chain product. The quarter showed continued pre-revenue losses and expenses above prior run-rate, but management emphasized pipeline progress and a Benavente sale-leaseback expected to close in December.

negative_highlights: Management explicitly revised full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance to a larger loss range of $4M-$5M.
CEO stated the company is taking a 'cautious approach' to future acquisitions due to market conditions and cash requirements.
Negative adjusted EBITDA widened on a standalone basis despite revenue growth, driven by increased marketing and infrastructure investments.
positive_highlights: Standalone revenue grew 16.68% YoY, outpacing the global Edtech market growth of 16.3%.
Gross margin expanded to 33.96% on a standalone basis and 47.33% pro forma.
Adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed from -$1.59 million in the prior year period to -$3.89 million.
summary: For the nine months ended September 30, 2022, Genius Group reported standalone revenue of $14.42 million (up 16.68% YoY) and pro forma revenue of $24.67 million. The company maintained its full-year 2022 guidance for pro forma revenue between $35 million and $38 million but revised adjusted EBITDA guidance to a loss between $4 million and $5 million due to higher planned investments in acquisitions and infrastructure.

negative_highlights: SOP delayed to Q1 2024 due to reduced funding speed in a challenging macro environment with rising interest rates.
Company faces high capital needs (€130 million) for the next milestone, requiring a community fundraising campaign as an alternative to dilutive equity raises.
Hiring freeze implemented since November and operational expenses controlled despite strong growth.
positive_highlights: Revenue accelerated six-fold in Q3 compared to the previous quarter due to strong Sono Solar growth (130% YoY).
Secured a first purchase order for solar body panels from one of the world's largest car manufacturers for high-volume production integration.
Raised €70 million total liquidity via convertible debentures, ATM inflows, and existing cash reserves.
summary: Sono Motors reported Q3 FY2022 revenue of €138,000 (six times the prior quarter) and year-to-date revenues of €180,000 driven by its Sono Solar licensing business. Management disclosed a significant delay in Series Production on Delivery (SOP), pushing it from H2 2023 to Q1 2024 due to reduced funding speed and high inflation/interest rates impacting capital markets. To bridge the remaining €130 million gap needed for pre-series vehicles, management announced a non-dilutive 'Save Sion' campaign seeking upfront payments equivalent to 3,500 vehicle down-payments from its community.

negative_highlights: Consolidated gross margin fell to 33.7% from 39.8% in the prior quarter and 40.7% a year ago, with spot-market component purchases reducing margin by $5.7M (~700 bps)
Adjusted EBITDA was flat at $4.7M versus $4.8M last quarter despite the revenue growth, as gross margin compression offset lower operating expenses
Telematics products revenue declined 8% YoY; Q4 revenue guided roughly flat sequentially and detailed quarterly guidance was not provided
positive_highlights: Software & subscription services revenue rose 11% sequentially and 35% YoY to a record $49.3M, representing 62% of consolidated revenue
Remaining performance obligations increased 20% sequentially and 72% YoY to $252M, with subscribers up 12% sequentially to 1.5M
Non-GAAP operating expenses fell 6% sequentially and 10% YoY; converted two large customers (Michelin, Navman) to recurring contracts and added Ford North America
summary: CalAmp reported Q3 FY2023 revenue of $78.9M, up 8% sequentially and 15% YoY, exceeding expectations, with software & subscription services revenue up 11% sequentially and 35% YoY to $49.3M (62% of total). Consolidated gross margin contracted sharply to 33.7% from 39.8% last quarter and 40.7% a year ago, as $5.7M of spot-market component buys to fulfill aged backlog (including Verizon 3G-to-4G upgrades) cut roughly 700 bps from margin and pressured adjusted EBITDA, which was flat at $4.7M. The company maintained its policy of not giving detailed quarterly guidance but said Q4 revenue would be roughly flat sequentially, with meaningful gross margin recovery expected in Q4 and normalization early next fiscal year. Subscribers rose 12% sequentially to 1.5M and remaining performance obligations climbed 20% sequentially to $252M, while telematics products revenue fell 8% YoY.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined 14.5% YoY to $23.6M as MAVYRET royalties fell to $22.6M due to lower patient volumes.
G&A expenses increased 33.7% YoY to $12.7M, driven by higher headcount and stock comp.
HBV program appears stalled with no new partners or data, as management adopts a 'watching and analyzing' approach.
positive_highlights: Enrolled beyond target in Phase 2 SPRINT study for COVID-19 antiviral EDP-235, with topline expected in May.
Preclinical ferret model shows EDP-235 reduces viral load and prevents transmission of COVID-19.
Cash runway extended into Q4 fiscal 2024, providing timeline coverage for key milestones.
summary: Fiscal Q1 2023 (ended Dec 31, 2022) revenue fell to $23.6M from $27.6M YoY, driven by lower MAVYRET royalties due to COVID-related patient volume declines. Net loss narrowed to $29M ($1.39 per share) from $30.1M ($1.48) YoY. R&D spending declined to $40.9M from $48.5M, while G&A rose to $12.7M from $9.5M. Cash reserves of ~$241.4M are expected to fund operations into Q4 FY2024. Management highlighted key upcoming data readouts: SPRINT COVID-19 Phase 2 topline in May, EDP-323 Phase 1 RSV data next quarter, and preclinical presentations. They provided no revised full-year guidance, but reiterated plans for a Phase 3 COVID trial in H2 2023.

negative_highlights: Q4 revenue declined slightly YoY due to Canadian closure.
Operating income decreased 5% in Q4 and 7% for full year 2022.
Total recurring contract value growth rate declined due to lower new client sales.
positive_highlights: Core offerings grew 7% YoY in 2022.
Received Best in KLAS 2023 Award for Patient Experience Improvement.
Returned $48.6 million to shareholders via dividends ($21M) and buybacks ($27.6M) in 2022.
summary: Q4 2022 revenue decreased slightly YoY due to Canadian closure, with core offerings up 7% and net 2022 revenue up 2%. Operating income fell 5% in Q4 and 7% for the full year. Effective tax rate rose to 30% due to a $2.6M non-deductible FX translation reclassification. Total recurring contract value (TRCV) was $146.8M at year-end; the company noted lower new client sales, with growth driven by price increases and upsells.

negative_highlights: Gross margin declined sequentially due to lower-margin E-Core and Cygnet businesses, though branded products still see 70-80% margins.
Operating expenses rose 83% YoY, with sales and marketing up 100% due to increased ad spend.
Despite revenue growth, net loss from operations was $2.1 million, though improved 16% YoY.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 444% YoY to $27.1 million, exceeding internal expectations of $20-23 million.
Adjusted EBITDA turned positive at ~$119,000, the first positive quarter after divesting Infusionz.
Gross profit increased 141% YoY to $10.3 million; debt from E-Core acquisition was fully paid off.
summary: Upexi reported record Q2 FY2023 revenue of $27.1 million, up 444% YoY from $4.9 million and up 134% sequentially, driven by acquisitions (Cygnet, LuckyTail, E-Core/Tytan Tiles) and year-end sales. Gross profit rose 141% to $10.3 million, but net loss from operations improved 16% to $2.1 million. Adjusted EBITDA turned positive at approximately $119,000 versus a $971,000 loss in the prior quarter. Management maintained calendar 2023 revenue guidance of over $100 million and expects EBITDA margin to reach 8%-12% by year-end.

negative_highlights: Q4 2022 GAAP net loss available to common shareholders was $59 million, or $2.08 diluted loss per share, versus $62 million of net income, or $2.08 diluted EPS, in Q4 2021
Full-year 2022 net loss available to common shareholders was $168 million, or $5.95 diluted loss per share, compared with net income of $438 million, or $15.09 diluted EPS, in 2021
Full-year operating adjusted EBITDA declined to $366 million from $422 million in 2021
positive_highlights: Q4 2022 operating revenues, excluding investment marks, rose to $450 million from $353 million in Q4 2021
Full-year recurring operating EBITDA of about $325 million exceeded the roughly $310 million needed to fund dividend, taxes, and overhead
Communications segment revenues increased over 150% to $236 million in 2022 and generated $30 million of segment income
summary: B. Riley Financial reported Q4 2022 total revenues of $327 million, down from $422 million in Q4 2021, and a net loss available to common shareholders of $59 million, or $2.08 diluted loss per share, versus $2.08 diluted EPS a year earlier; the loss was driven by $124 million of investment markdowns. Excluding investment marks, operating revenues were $450 million, up from $353 million in Q4 2021, with operating adjusted EBITDA of $102 million versus $106 million. Full-year 2022 operating revenues were $1.3 billion with operating adjusted EBITDA of $366 million, down from $422 million in 2021, and recurring operating EBITDA of roughly $325 million. Management guided 2023 recurring EBITDA to a run-rate in the low $300s and an upside case in the high $300s, and noted that 2022 recurring EBITDA covered the approximately $310 million needed for dividend, taxes, and overhead.

negative_highlights: North America Interactive reported negative $6 million in EBITDA for the quarter
Management expects consumer weakness starting in Q2, anticipating a pullback from current trends
Japan market experienced slowed sentiment with new traffic issues before recovering
positive_highlights: International Interactive UK business grew 12% year-over-year on a constant currency basis in Q4
Casinos & Resorts core portfolio (excluding AC and Tropicana) achieved EBITDA margins of high thirties, including $96 million total EBITDAR
Asia region showed positive year-on-year performance with improving ARPUs and visitation
summary: Bally's reported Q4 FY2022 results with Casinos & Resorts EBITDAR of $96 million and International Interactive EBITDA of approximately $89 million at a 39% margin; however, North America Interactive posted negative $6 million in EBITDA. Management updated its full-year 2023 financial forecast to reflect current FX rates and the reset in North America Interactive losses, projecting revenues between $2.5 billion and $2.6 billion with adjusted EBITDA of $660 million to $700 million.

negative_highlights: Recorded a $33 million noncash goodwill impairment in Q4 2022 related to the IMU-935 psoriasis program.
The Phase 1b trial of IMU-935 in psoriasis failed to show a benefit of active doses over placebo, with the placebo arm experiencing a greater-than-expected decrease.
Full-year net loss widened to $120.4 million from $92.9 million in 2021, driven by increased R&D and G&A expenses.
positive_highlights: Ended 2022 with $116.4 million in cash and investments, sufficient to fund operations into Q4 2024.
Plan to report top-line data from Part C of the Phase 1 trial of IMU-856 in celiac disease patients in mid-2023.
summary: Immunic reported a full-year 2022 net loss of $120.4 million, or $3.78 per share, with R&D expenses rising to $71.3 million from $61.1 million in 2021. The company ended the year with $116.4 million in cash and investments following a $60 million private placement in October, which it expects to fund operations into Q4 2024. A $33 million noncash goodwill impairment was recorded in Q4 after the Phase 1b trial of IMU-935 in psoriasis failed to show a benefit over placebo due to an unexpectedly high placebo response. Management provided timelines for upcoming data readouts but did not issue formal financial guidance.

negative_highlights: Q4 operating loss of €13 million increased by €5 million from Q3, driven by €2.5 million Exolum impairments and a €2.9 million inventory provision.
Full-year 2022 operating costs were around €18 million versus prior guidance of around €14 million, due to one-off items including a €1.5 million production capacity charge.
Revenue recognition for the Exolum project is pending commissioning, and management noted it is too early to forecast development fees or equity returns.
positive_highlights: Secured €36 million C-5 grant and €10 million C-14 grant, with a total of nearly €65 million in grants awarded.
Contracted €13 million of technology sales for 2023 and provided 2023 revenue guidance of €25 million, with 2024 at €80 million and 2025 over €140 million.
Signed first green hydrogen offtake contract in Portugal with Dourogás and was selected for a €2.5 million tech sales tender in Spain.
summary: Fusion Fuel reported a Q4 2022 operating loss of €13 million, up €5 million from Q3, driven by €2.5 million of Exolum-related impairments and a €2.9 million inventory provision; full-year 2022 operating costs were around €18 million versus prior guidance of around €14 million.
