Q4 revenue was not provided, but the company has contracted €13 million of technology sales for 2023 and set a 2023 revenue target of €25 million, with 2024 and 2025 targets of €80 million and over €140 million. The quarter included non-cash charges and one-off costs that pushed results below the previously guided cost base, while management pointed to a growing development pipeline and secured grants as support for future revenue.

negative_highlights: Q4 revenue of $73.8 million rose only about 3% sequentially and contribution margin fell to $17.4 million from $17.8 million as Q3 included $2.3 million of higher shortfall revenue
Q4 net income of $2.6 million was slightly below Q3's $2.7 million, and full-year 2022 was still a net loss of $0.7 million

Full-year 2022 free cash flow was negative $13.9 million after $19.3 million of capex and the Blair acquisition, and Q1 2023 volume guidance of 1.0-1.2 million tons implies a step down from Q4's 1.175 million
positive_highlights: Full-year volumes hit an annual record 4.33 million tons, up 36% from 3.19 million in 2021
Full-year adjusted EBITDA swung to $29.3 million from negative $30.5 million in 2021
Signed an extension with the Marcellus customer that extends the contract term and increases volumes, and industrial sales volume grew 30% in the quarter
summary: Smart Sand reported Q4 2022 revenue of $73.8 million, up from $71.6 million in Q3, on 1.175 million tons sold (up 6% sequentially). Full-year revenue was $255.7 million versus $126.6 million in 2021, with 4.33 million tons sold (up 36% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $29.3 million versus negative $30.5 million in 2021. Q4 adjusted EBITDA of $10.7 million and free cash flow of $2.4 million marked the third consecutive quarter of positive adjusted EBITDA and second of positive free cash flow; net income was $2.6 million ($0.06/share), roughly flat sequentially. Management guided Q1 2023 volumes to 1.0-1.2 million tons with contribution margin per ton in the low double-digit range, is spending approximately $5 million to bring Blair online in Q2 2023 to address Canada, and bought back Clearlake's 5.18 million shares (approximately 11.3% of outstanding) for approximately $8.85 million.

negative_highlights: E-commerce GPPU fell 71% sequentially to $1,233, driven by aged inventory, market depreciation, and EV inventory reserves.
Total revenue declined 39% sequentially to $209 million as e-commerce units fell 36% due to intentionally slowed transactions.
Full-year 2023 adjusted EBITDA loss guidance of $200 million to $250 million includes a $45 million headwind from no assumed securitization gain on sale, versus gains in 2022.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA loss excluding securitization gain and non-recurring costs improved by $3 million sequentially to $70.5 million.
Reduced adjusted SG&A by $31 million sequentially and cut headcount by 20% in January, expecting $27 million in annualized savings.
Inventory available for sale or pending sale rose to 87% at year-end from 52% in Q3, and over 95% currently, after titling process improvements.
summary: Vroom reported Q4 2022 total revenue of $209 million, down 39% sequentially, with e-commerce units down 36% and e-commerce GPPU down 71% to $1,233. Adjusted EBITDA loss excluding securitization gain and non-recurring costs was $70.5 million, a $3 million sequential improvement. For full-year 2023, guidance calls for an adjusted EBITDA loss of $200 million to $250 million (or $150 million to $225 million if a securitization gain on sale is recognized), with ending cash of $150 million to $200 million. The company expects continued GPPU pressure in the first half from watching through aged inventory, a transitory headwind of roughly $21 million for the year.

negative_highlights: Q1 FY2023 EBITDA is expected to drop double-digits YoY due to revenue mix changes as high-margin pandemic projects conclude.
Marketing Services segment saw both revenue (-6.8%) and EBITDA (-18.4%) decline, primarily driven by the end of direct mail campaigns.
Customer Care revenue declined 12.9% year-over-year as anticipated rolling off of COVID-related project work.
positive_highlights: Fulfillment & Logistics segment grew 34.4% in Q4 driven by a large logistics client and new contracts with an international investment firm.
Customer Care achieved significant margin expansion, increasing EBITDA to $3.2 million from -$2.6M despite revenue decline due to pandemic project roll-off.
Company ended the year debt-free with over $10 million in cash after redeeming preferred shares and paying down credit line.
summary: Harte Hanks reported Q4 FY2022 revenue of $54.8 million (up 5.4% YoY) and EBITDA of $4.4 million (up from $3.5M), driven by a 34.4% surge in Fulfillment & Logistics offsetting declines in Customer Care (-12.9%) and Marketing Services (-6.8%). Management noted that Q1 FY2023 will face an abnormally strong YoY comparison due to the expiration of high-margin pandemic projects, leading to expected double-digit EBITDA decline for the quarter despite modest revenue growth.

negative_highlights: G&A expenses rose to $2.9 million in Q4 2022 from $2.1 million in Q4 2021 on higher legal and accounting costs
2023 operating cash burn guidance of $35–40 million exceeds the 2022 burn of $29.2 million, implying an acceleration in spending
Outstanding debt of approximately $16.7 million with principal repayments ongoing through August 2023
positive_highlights: Q4 operating cash burn fell 53% to $7.1 million from $15.1 million in Q4 2021
Full-year 2022 net loss narrowed 52% to $37.7 million from $78.8 million in 2021
First objective clinical response in a solid tumor with non-viral TCR-T reported, with translational data showing TCR-T persistence without exhaustion markers
summary: Alaunos reported a Q4 2022 net loss of $9.2 million ($0.04/share) versus an $11.8 million loss in Q4 2021, with R&D down 32% to $5.6 million and operating cash burn down 53% to $7.1 million. Full-year 2022 net loss narrowed 52% to $37.7 million, and collaboration revenue rose to $2.9 million on darinaparsin milestones. Management provided no revenue or EPS guidance, but said cash of $53 million funds operations into Q4 2023 with 2023 operating cash burn of $35–40 million, and reiterated expectations to treat 12–15 Phase 1 patients and become Phase 2 ready by year-end.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened slightly in absolute terms compared to the prior year's adjusted performance due to increased G&A expenses as the team builds out.
Arbitration award from Turkey dispute is only $1.3 million, which management noted was disappointing despite a favorable ruling on merits.
positive_highlights: Completed optimization study doubling Phase I production capacity from original targets to approximately 16,000 metric tons per annum throughput (7,500 CSPG).
Signed a non-binding indicative term sheet for $150 million of private debt to cover remaining capital requirements.
Secured an agreement with a Tier-1 EV battery producer to potentially purchase all Phase I output.
summary: Westwater Resources reported a net loss of $11.1 million for FY2022 (or Q4 context), down from $16.1 million in the prior year due to lower product development and arbitration costs offset by higher G&A expenses, resulting in EPS of $(0.25) versus $(0.49). Management announced a significant optimization study that more than doubles Phase I throughput capacity to 7,500 metric tons per annum (from ~3,700), increasing the estimated pre-tax NPV threefold and raising the projected cumulative cash flow for Phases I & II combined.

negative_highlights: FDA issued a Refuse to File letter (RTF) for roluperidone, maintaining its stance despite additional data submissions.
Phase 3 study did not meet primary end point; only highest dose hit P-value of 0.05 using Hochberg correction.
positive_highlights: Company secured a $3.1 million refund of the NDA filing fee from the FDA due to small business status.
summary: Minerva Neurosciences reported a net loss of $32.1 million for the year ended December 31, 2022 (vs. $49.9M in 2021) and Q4 2022 cash balance was approximately $36.2 million following an FDA refund of filing fees. The company received a Refuse to File letter from the FDA regarding its roluperidone NDA, which remains in effect despite ongoing dialogue addressing concerns about Phase 2b applicability and Phase 3 statistical endpoints.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened significantly year-over-year to $75.7 million for the full year.
Company terminated the RAD52 preclinical research program citing lack of meaningful probability of success.
Management withdrew cash runway guidance, stating prior estimates may be irrelevant pending MANTRA results.
positive_highlights: MANTRA Phase 3 study completed enrollment of 175 patients five months ahead of prior year-end guidance.
Phase 1 data showed median PFS of 8.0 months in a specific DDLPS cohort, compared to ~2 months for standard of care.
Raised $50 million via registered offering, bringing cash position to approximately $130.5 million.
summary: Rain Oncology reported a net loss of $22.7 million for Q4 2022 and $75.7 million for full year 2022, compared to losses of $18 million and $51.4 million respectively in the prior year periods. The company terminated its preclinical RAD52 program due to assay limitations and withdrew cash runway guidance pending the upcoming MANTRA top-line data readout in Q2 2023. Management expressed high confidence in the Q2 timeline for the pivotal MANTRA trial results despite not disclosing if the required progression events have been met.

negative_highlights: 2023 revenue guidance of $1.55–$1.6 billion implies roughly flat to down versus 2022's $1.6 billion, with Q1 revenue growth only mid-single-digits after a slower-than-expected January.
Live flight legs declined 5% year-over-year and new membership sales weakened; management cited macroeconomic headwinds and a conscious pullback in sales/marketing.
Full-year 2023 adjusted EBITDA is guided to a loss of $110–130 million and GAAP net loss to $300–320 million, alongside $30 million of annualized headcount cost cuts announced last week.
positive_highlights: Q4 revenue of $408 million was a record and at the high end of guidance, up nearly 20% year-over-year; full-year revenue was a record $1.6 billion, up over 30%.
Adjusted EBITDA loss of $43.7 million came within the $40–45 million guidance range, and adjusted contribution margin of 4.7% was at the high end of the 4.25–4.75% guide.
Prepaid block sales exceeded $1 billion for the year, a record, and cash rose to $586 million from $285 million in Q3 after the October debt financing.
summary: Wheels Up reported Q4 2022 revenue of $408 million, up nearly 20% year-over-year and at the high end of guidance, but adjusted EBITDA was a loss of $43.7 million and adjusted contribution margin fell to 4.7%. Full-year 2022 revenue was a record $1.6 billion, up over 30%, yet membership revenue growth decelerated to 13% and live flight legs fell 5%. For 2023, management guided revenue to $1.55–$1.6 billion (implying roughly flat to down versus 2022), Q1 adjusted EBITDA loss of $45–50 million, and a full-year adjusted EBITDA loss of $110–130 million, with January slower than anticipated and improvement only from February onward. The quarter was essentially in line on revenue but included flight leg declines, bad debt charges, and a 2023 revenue guide that does not show growth.

negative_highlights: Management explicitly stated 'Tough tape today' and 'tough day to put out earnings'
Company will reduce spend on late-stage preclinical activities by over 30% compared to prior year
Future quarterly results will be released by press release only, reducing analyst access
positive_highlights: Received $10 million milestone payment from Kyorin for initiation of EFZO-FIT study in Japan
Generated gross proceeds of approximately $52 million from public offering of common stock
Expanded clinical program to include Phase 2 study in scleroderma-associated ILD, doubling market opportunity
summary: aTyr Pharma reported Q4 FY2022 financial results with R&D expenses of $42.8 million and G&A of $14 million for the full year, ending with $69.3 million in cash and a runway extending into 2026. The company received a $10 million milestone payment from Kyorin related to the initiation of the EFZO-FIT study in Japan and raised approximately $52 million from a public offering. Management announced that future quarterly results will be released via press release only, streamlining reporting while focusing on advancing the Phase 3 sarcoidosis trial (expected Q1 2025 readout) and initiating a new Phase 2 study in scleroderma-associated ILD.

negative_highlights: Total revenue declined by approximately 7% compared to full-year 2021 due to the loss of COVID-related demand.
Average note price per specimen decreased by roughly 29% ($157) driven by a shift in product mix away from high-margin COVID items.
Cash balance dropped significantly from $27.7 million at end-2021 to $15.3 million at end-2022, with average quarterly burn of ~$2.2M.
positive_highlights: Non-COVID revenue hit a record $9.5 million representing an 18.6% increase over FY2021.
Total specimens shipped increased by approximately 6,703 units (32%) to reach ~27,503 for the year.
Average cost per specimen decreased significantly from $252 in FY2021 to $173 in FY2022.
summary: Full year 2022 revenue was $10.4 million (down 7% YoY) and non-COVID revenue reached a record $9.5 million (+18.6%), while total specimens shipped increased by 32%. Management noted that Q4 FY2022 revenue of $3.2M was an all-time high but declined from the prior year due to COVID headwinds, with guidance for full-year growth explicitly deferred until H2 2023.

negative_highlights: Full-year FYP growth was only 3.5% year-over-year to RMB2.9 billion, or about 20.1% excluding the January 2022 high base impact
Total performing agent count declined as the company shifted toward higher-performing agents, implying continued contraction of the traditional sales force
positive_highlights: Q4 total GWP grew 11.7% year-over-year to approximately RMB3.6 billion, with FYP up 19.6%
Q4 operating income of RMB84.9 million came in 'far ahead' of guidance; non-GAAP net income attributable to shareholders rose 76.1% year-over-year to RMB70.9 million
2023 target of no less than 50% year-over-year growth in both life insurance first year premiums and operating income
summary: Fanhua reported Q4 FY2022 total gross written premiums of approximately RMB3.6 billion, up 11.7% year-over-year, with first year premiums growing 19.6% year-over-year. Q4 operating income came in at RMB84.9 million, described as far ahead of guidance, and non-GAAP net income attributable to shareholders grew 76.1% year-over-year to RMB70.9 million. For full year 2022, total GWP grew 10.3% to RMB12.9 billion and FYP reached RMB2.9 billion, up 3.5% (up approximately 20.1% excluding a January 2022 high base). Management set a 2023 target of no less than 50% year-over-year growth in both life insurance first year premiums and operating income, and outlined plans to acquire 10 insurance intermediaries in 2023 contributing at least RMB1 billion in first-year premiums.

negative_highlights: Revenue missed guidance and declined sequentially due to FX headwinds and industry demand slowdown
Q1 2023 revenue guidance was cut from prior expectations (implied higher levels)
Order intake decreased by 4.6% year-over-year
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA of $2.6 million exceeded internal guidance of $2 million
Gross margin expanded to a record high of 34% (or 33.6% reported), up significantly from the prior year
First full year of positive operating cash flow ($8M) allowing debt paydown
summary: Boxlight reported Q4 FY2022 revenue of $43 million (or $42.8M per CFO), missing guidance and showing a slight decline from the prior year due to FX headwinds and slowing demand, though constant currency growth was +7%. Adjusted EBITDA came in at $2.6 million, beating its own guidance of $2 million but falling short of full-year expectations relative to recent trends. Management lowered Q1 2023 revenue guidance to $40M (down from prior implied levels) and expects modest single-digit growth for FY2023 driven by school safety spending deadlines.

negative_highlights: AFFO per share declined to $0.37 from $0.41 a year ago, and net loss widened to $0.22/share from $0.08
Combined portfolio NOI grew only 0.7% in Q4 as expenses rose 19.7% versus 8.5% revenue growth, with weather costs subtracting 3.5 points from NOI

New lease spreads decelerated sharply to 3.4% in January-February 2023 from 9.5% in Q4, guidance assumes property revenue growth moderates to 5.7%, and the Chatham disposition cuts 2023 FFO by ~$0.05/share with no assumed redeployment
positive_highlights: Average monthly rents rose 9.2% YoY and Q4 blended lease spreads were 9%, with renewal spreads holding at 8% through January-February

Balance sheet improved: full $75.3 million liquidity as of March 1, all mortgage debt fixed at a 3.99% weighted average rate, no maturities until 2025, and a new $21.2 million Silvana Oaks loan at 4.45% fixed for 10 years, 300 bps below the credit facility debt it replaced
Dividend raised 8.7% to $0.25 per share, with 2023 payout ratio guided to a covered 62%-67% of AFFO, plus a new 3%-discount DRIP
summary: BRT reported Q4 2022 FFO of $0.40/share vs $0.35 a year ago, but AFFO fell to $0.37 from $0.41, with a net loss of $0.22/share vs $0.08, driven by higher depreciation from partner buyouts, weather costs of ~$549k ($0.03/share), and ~$367k ($0.02/share) of added interest expense. Combined portfolio NOI rose just 0.7% as revenue grew 8.5% but expenses jumped 19.7%, with weather costs alone cutting NOI by 3.5 points. Initial 2023 guidance calls for AFFO of $1.50-$1.61 (2.3% growth at midpoint), FFO of $1.08-$1.19, and combined portfolio NOI growth of 3.1% at the midpoint, with insurance assumed up 50.4% and real estate taxes up 9.8%. Average occupancy fell to 94.7% from 96.4%, and new lease spreads decelerated to 3.4% in January-February from 9.5% in Q4.

negative_highlights: Net loss increased year-over-year from $16.2 million to $19 million due to higher spending on narazaciclib development and drug manufacturing.
Cash and cash equivalents declined by $16.3 million over the last 12 months, reducing the financial runway.
Management explicitly stated it is impossible to provide specific timeframes for completing future dose escalation cohorts or starting Phase II trials.
positive_highlights: Narazaciclib Phase I trial completed the fifth dose escalation cohort with a favorable safety profile showing no clinically meaningful cases of neutropenia or diarrhea.
Rigosertib achieved a complete clinical response in the second evaluable participant for RDEB-associated squamous cell carcinoma after only 4 cycles of therapy.
The company plans to seek guidance from the FDA on an expeditious path towards approval for rigosertib in the ultra-orphan indication of RDEB-associated squamous cell carcinoma.
summary: Onconova reported a net loss of $19 million for FY2022 compared to $16.2 million in the prior year, driven by increased R&D spending on its lead asset narazaciclib. The company's cash position decreased from $55.1 million at the end of 2021 to $38.8 million at the end of 2022, with management projecting this runway will fund operations into Q1 2024. While clinical progress was highlighted for narazaciclib and rigosertib, no financial guidance was provided.

negative_highlights: Total Q4 revenue was essentially flat at $61.7M versus $61.2M a year ago
Digital subscription revenue fell 36% YoY to $4.6M, with TheStreet digital subs down 39% since Jim Cramer's departure
Senior notes due at year-end are classified as current and the 10-K was delayed with an extension filing
positive_highlights: Digital advertising revenue grew 47% YoY to $34.5M, representing over two-thirds of total revenue
Licensing and syndication revenue increased 129% YoY to $6.1M with near-zero associated cost
Q4 adjusted EBITDA improved to $5.4M from $1.1M a year ago, and full-year adjusted EBITDA turned positive at $3.1M
summary: Q4 revenue was $61.7M, up only slightly from $61.2M a year ago, as 47% growth in digital advertising to $34.5M and a 129% rise in licensing/syndication to $6.1M offset a planned print decline to $16.5M from $27.9M and a 36% drop in digital subscription revenue to $4.6M. Q4 net loss narrowed to $13.7M from $19.9M and adjusted EBITDA swung to $5.4M from $1.1M; full-year revenue rose 17% to $221M and full-year adjusted EBITDA was positive $3.1M versus a $12.1M loss. Management guided FY2023 revenue to $255M-$270M and adjusted EBITDA to $30M-$35M, and flagged that senior notes come due at year-end with refinancing or extension expected in the near term, while the 10-K filing was delayed via a 15-day extension. The quarter's flat top line versus strong digital growth and the unresolved debt maturity are the key changes versus the prior period.

negative_highlights: Spot charter rates temporarily moderated in the first part of Q1 2023 due to winter weather and product stockpiling in Europe
Q1 2023 booked TCE rate of $28,000 per day is below Q4 2022's $33,182 per day
Weighted average interest rate rose to 7.25% due to increases in LIBOR
positive_highlights: TCE revenues rose to $13.8 million, up $10 million YoY and 16% sequentially
MR daily TCE reached $33,182, up 14.2% QoQ and 3.8x YoY
Announced sale of Pyxis Malou for $24.8 million, netting ~$18 million cash and an expected $8 million non-cash gain in Q1 2023
summary: Pyxis Tankers reported Q4 2022 TCE revenues of $13.8 million, up $10 million year-over-year and 16% sequentially, with net income of $6.5 million ($0.61 basic EPS) versus a $5.6 million loss in Q4 2021. MR daily TCE averaged $33,182, up 14.2% sequentially and 3.8x year-over-year, while adjusted EBITDA reached $9.7 million. For Q1 2023, 80% of available days are booked at an average estimated TCE of $28,000 per day, and the company announced the sale of its oldest vessel, Pyxis Malou, for $24.8 million, expecting an $8 million non-cash gain in Q1 2023. The primary change versus the prior period is the significant strengthening in charter rates, though management noted some temporary moderation in spot rates early in Q1 2023.

negative_highlights: Cost of revenues surged to RMB 89.3 million, driven by inventory write-downs, far exceeding revenue of RMB 12.7 million.
Net loss remained substantial at RMB 132.8 million, nearly flat versus the RMB 135.5 million loss in Q4 2021.
Cash and cash equivalents declined to RMB 87.8 million as of December 31, 2022 from RMB 233.9 million at end-2021.
positive_highlights: Net revenues increased to RMB 12.7 million (USD 1.8 million) in Q4 2022 from RMB 3.2 million in Q4 2021.
R&D expenses decreased to RMB 39.2 million from RMB 99.6 million year-over-year.
Basic and diluted loss per share narrowed to RMB 1.19 from RMB 1.32 in the prior-year period.
summary: Nano Labs reported Q4 2022 net revenues of RMB 12.7 million (USD 1.8 million), up from RMB 3.2 million in Q4 2021, but cost of revenues surged to RMB 89.3 million due to inventory write-downs, driving an operating loss of RMB 136.9 million and a net loss of RMB 132.8 million (RMB 1.19 loss per share). Cash and cash equivalents fell to RMB 87.8 million from RMB 233.9 million at end-2021. Management did not provide formal guidance but stated it expects 2023 financial performance to be 'well improved compared to the fourth quarter of 2022.' The quarter was heavily impacted by Ethereum's conversion from proof-of-work to proof-of-stake in September 2022 and declining cryptocurrency prices, and the company highlighted strategic shifts toward overseas markets and new products including AIGC, ZKP computing, and the iPollo Metaverse.

negative_highlights: No revenue guidance provided; management said it is 'still a ways away' from giving sales guidance
R&D expense increased to $9.4 million in Q4 from $7.2 million a year earlier, and SG&A rose to $11.1 million from $9.7 million
Net loss of $13.9 million in Q4 and $60.5 million for the full year
positive_highlights: Q4 FYARRO net product sales rose 23% QoQ to $5.2 million
Full-year 2022 sales of $15.2 million surpassed estimates in just 10 months on the market
More than 120 unique ordering accounts at year-end, up 34% from the prior quarter, with a reorder rate above 85%
summary: Aadi Bioscience reported Q4 FYARRO net product sales of $5.2 million, up 23% quarter-over-quarter, bringing full-year 2022 sales to $15.2 million in the first 10 months of launch. The company ended the year with approximately $172.6 million in cash, cash equivalents, and short-term investments, including proceeds from a $72.5 million financing, expected to fund operations into 2025. Management reaffirmed its expectation to complete enrollment in the PRECISION 1 trial by spring 2024 and said preliminary data from a double-digit number of patients will be shared in Q2 2023; no formal revenue guidance was provided. R&D and SG&A expenses increased year-over-year as the company built out its commercial and clinical infrastructure.

negative_highlights: Revenue fell to $1.5 million from $3.1 million a year earlier
Net bookings dropped to $206,000 from $4 million, and backlog fell to $5.6 million from $10.8 million
Gross margin contracted to 10.3% from 18.1% on lower revenue and higher variable costs
positive_highlights: Operating expenses decreased 13% sequentially from Q3 2022 to $1.4 million, reflecting early cost-saving benefits
Cash and cash equivalents rose to $18.6 million from $2.2 million a year earlier after ~$22 million in stock and warrant proceeds; company is debt free
Signed a third consecutive contract with a Northeast cultivation facility and two non-cannabis engineering contracts in Q4, plus more in early 2023
summary: Q4 FY2022 revenue fell to $1.5 million from $3.1 million a year earlier, with net bookings of $206,000 versus $4 million and backlog down to $5.6 million from $10.8 million, reflecting delayed or cancelled cannabis cultivation CapEx. Gross margin contracted to 10.3% from 18.1%, operating expenses declined 6% YoY and 13% sequentially to $1.4 million, and net loss was $1.3 million or $0.18 per share versus a $0.25 per share loss a year ago. Management gave no formal guidance, said it expects lower OpEx in 2023 from current levels, and noted the company remains debt free with $18.6 million of cash and equivalents at December 31, 2022.

negative_highlights: Q4 revenue down 23.2% sequentially
Gross margin down to 19.9% from 22.3%
Cash at $1 million and $38,000 credit availability
positive_highlights: Cost reduction actions expected to generate 20% annual savings
Inventory reduced 26% since Q2 to $25.4 million
Signed non-binding term sheet for $12 million asset-backed credit facility
summary: Minim reported Q4 2022 revenue of $10.6 million, down 23.2% sequentially but up 1.4% year-over-year. Full-year revenue declined 9% to $50.6 million. Gross margin fell to 19.9% from 22.3%, partly due to a $1.2 million inventory reserve charge. The company initiated cost cuts expected to yield 20% annual savings and aims for adjusted EBITDA profitability in the second half of 2023, but cash is low at $1 million and a reverse stock split is planned to regain NASDAQ compliance.

negative_highlights: Q4 revenue declined 17% year-over-year primarily due to decreased sales volume from pandemic restrictions in China.
Net income turned into a loss of $0.8 million as operating expenses increased by over 50% YoY to invest in HEVI expansion.
positive_highlights: Gross margin expanded 380 basis points to 19.9% driven by a strategic shift toward higher-value products like lithium-powered integrated drive train units.
HEVI electric equipment demos and pilots received extremely positive feedback, with the company fully booked for product demonstrations through May.
summary: GTEC reported Q4 FY2022 revenue of $19.1 million, a decrease of 17% year-over-year due to pandemic lockdowns in China and foreign exchange impacts. The company posted a net loss of $0.8 million compared to income in the prior period, with gross margins expanding slightly but operating expenses rising significantly as they invested in HEVI infrastructure.

negative_highlights: Deal excludes Greater China and other prior agreement regions, limiting full global scope
Milestones are success-based and not guaranteed; only upfront payment is certain at close
No specific Q4 FY2022 revenue or EPS figures were provided in the transcript
positive_highlights: Upfront payment of $90 million expected in Q2 2023, providing non-dilutive capital and >2-year cash runway
Total potential deal value of $593 million plus royalties with GSK, an established infectious disease player
Capital will repay Hercules and Silicon Valley Bank debt, strengthening balance sheet
summary: SCYNEXIS announced an exclusive global license agreement with GSK for ibrexafungerp, excluding Greater China and prior agreement regions. The deal includes a $90 million upfront payment, potential total deal value of $593 million plus tiered royalties (mid-single to mid-teen percent on annual sales). Funds will repay debt and extend cash runway to over two years, while SCYNEXIS retains rights to next-generation fungicides like SCY-247, with GSK having right of first negotiation. Q4 FY2022 financials were not provided, but the deal removes perceived financing overhang and validates the asset's potential.

negative_highlights: Q4 billings fell to $100.9 million from $151.4 million a year ago, and full-year billings dropped 37% to $459.5 million
Paid subscribers fell 13.4% to 841,000 and ARPU declined to $519 from $742
Q1 conversion rates have deteriorated below Q4 levels, with management unable to quantify the outlook and no numeric guidance provided
positive_highlights: Adjusted CFFO margin expanded to 18.2% in Q4 2022 from 3.3% in Q4 2021 on cost cuts
Direct marketing spend was cut $40 million in H2 vs a $37 million target, and overhead run-rate savings reached $36 million annualized
Free subscriber base grew 2 million (+14.6%) in 2022 and cumulative active subscriber spend hit an all-time high
summary: MarketWise reported Q4 2022 GAAP revenue of $127.7 million, down 13% YoY, with billings of $100.9 million versus $151.4 million a year ago and sequentially down 4%. Full-year revenue fell 6.7% to $512.4 million and billings dropped 37% to $459.5 million; paid subscribers declined 13.4% to 841,000 and ARPU fell to $519 from $742. Cost cuts exceeded targets ($40 million marketing vs $37 million goal; $36 million annualized overhead savings), lifting adjusted CFFO margin to 18.2% in Q4 from 3.3% a year ago, but management gave no numeric guidance and flagged continued weak Q1 conversion. Management did not provide formal forward guidance and cited continued macro-driven subscriber hesitation.

negative_highlights: Gross margin declined to 72% from 73% on sales mix
No explicit forward revenue or EPS guidance provided; only directional commentary on cost cuts and the pending second LOI
Net loss of $63.4 million and adjusted EBITDA loss of $26.6 million remain substantial relative to $19.4 million revenue
positive_highlights: Revenue rose 21% to $19.4 million, with $2.6 million from smart office apps and $900,000 from real-time location technologies
Adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed to $26.6 million from $29.6 million and net loss improved by $5.8 million to $63.4 million
Cash of $20.2 million with expected operating expense reduction of approximately 50% following the CXApp sale
summary: Inpixon reported FY2022 revenue of $19.4 million, up 21% from $16.0 million, with gross margin of 72% versus 73% prior year and net loss of $63.4 million versus $69.2 million. Non-GAAP adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed to $26.6 million from $29.6 million, and cash stood at $20.2 million. The company completed the spin-off of its CXApp workplace business to KINS Technology Group in March 2023 and expects operating expense reductions of roughly 50% over coming quarters, but provided no explicit revenue or EPS guidance for 2023.

negative_highlights: GAAP net loss widened to $27.4 million in 2022 on a non-cash impairment
Discontinued 499 gastroparesis trial due to enrollment difficulties
Phase 2b costs uncertain and dependent on FDA discussions
positive_highlights: Next-gen capecitabine at all doses evaluated so far causes no catabolite adverse events
Cash positioned to fund operations into Q3 2024 with $12.9 million total
Expect to initiate Phase 2b capecitabine trial in H2 2023
summary: Processa reported a GAAP net loss of $27.4 million ($1.70 per share) for FY2022, up from an $11.4 million loss, partly due to a non-cash impairment. Cash was $6.5 million at year-end, supplemented by $6.4 million raised post-period, funding operations into Q3 2024. Management prioritized three next-generation chemotherapy drugs, highlighted favorable Phase 1b capecitabine data with no catabolite adverse events, and expects to meet with FDA mid-April and initiate Phase 2b in H2 2023. The company discontinued a gastroparesis trial due to enrollment difficulties.

negative_highlights: Bromine prices have dropped approximately 40% since the end of the fiscal year due to economic slowdowns and lockdowns.
Management explicitly stated they are unable to make revenue or earnings projections for fiscal year 2023 until bromine pricing stabilizes.
The Yuxin chemical factory opening is delayed by strict government environmental requirements, pushing commercial production into an uncertain timeline.
positive_highlights: Revenue increased approximately 20% to $66.1 million driven by higher bromine prices earlier in the year.
Gross profit increased 34% to $37.4 million and operating profit surged 216% to $16.5 million.
Company generated cash flow from operations of approximately $51.1 million, making free cash flow positive after investing $37.6 million.
summary: Gulf Resources reported an excellent fiscal year 2022 with revenue increasing approximately 20% to $66.1 million and EPS of $1 versus a prior loss of $0.09. Management noted that while bromine prices have dropped approximately 40% since year-end, they believe prices have reached a bottom and will recover in 2023. No specific guidance for fiscal year 2023 was provided due to the uncertainty surrounding future bromine pricing.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to $52.6 million compared to $21.4 million in FY2021 due to a one-time impairment charge of $26.2 million
Adjusted EBITDA remained negative at -$18.3 million, with Q4 specifically impacted by year-end sales campaigns and discounts reducing gross profit
Cash position decreased from $37.6 million in December 2021 to $9.5 million due to acquisitions (JustCBD) and higher operating expenses
positive_highlights: Record full-year revenue of $37.2 million representing a 314% increase from the prior year
Gross margin expanded significantly to 39%, up from 27% in the prior period, driven by high-margin acquired businesses
Q4 was identified as the highest revenue-generating quarter and year for the company to date
summary: Flora reported full-year FY2022 revenue of $37.2 million (up 314% YoY) and gross profit of $14.4 million, driven by the integration of acquired brands JustCBD and Vessel. The company recorded a net loss of $52.6 million due to significant non-cash charges including a $26.2 million impairment on House of Brands assets and M&A-related transaction costs. Management provided 2023 revenue guidance of $90M-$105M, noting that Q4 results were impacted by year-end sales campaigns and discounts.

negative_highlights: Revenue remains negligible at $5,000 for the full year with no revenue generated prior to Q4 FY2021
General and administrative expenses surged from $290k to $1.2 million in Q4 due to IPO preparation costs and public company reporting requirements
Expansion into European markets is delayed until next year pending CE marking approval
positive_highlights: Net loss narrowed significantly from $5.6 million in Q4 FY2021 to $1.7 million in Q4 FY2022 due to lower interest expense and reduced stock-based compensation
CyPath Lung commercial launch in Texas is proceeding with positive feedback on ease of use, sample collection quality, and actionable results from physicians
Clinical trial data published showing 92% sensitivity and 87% specificity for detecting lung cancer in high-risk patients
summary: bioAffinity Technologies reported Q4 FY2022 revenue of approximately $2,500 and full-year revenue of roughly $5,000, both driven by royalties from its CyPath Lung test sold through partner Precision Pathology Services. The company posted a net loss narrowing to $1.7 million in the quarter (from $5.6M prior year) due to lower interest expense on convertible notes and reduced stock-based compensation compared to 2021 levels, though R&D expenses increased slightly to $429k. Management highlighted successful early commercial testing in Texas with positive physician feedback but noted that full EU expansion is not expected until next year.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened materially to $58.3 million due to a one-time goodwill impairment of $41.7 million
Cash position declined from $14.6M at end-2021 to $4.3M at end-2022 despite raising ~$17.9M in financing
Operating loss increased to $22.8 million before the impairment charge
positive_highlights: Total revenues climbed to a new company record of $19.1 million, up 96% YoY
Sensor sales increased 27% to $8.7 million driven by adoption of Altum-PT and RedEdge-P sensors
Drone (eBee) revenue grew significantly from $2.4M in 2021 to $9.8M in 2022 following the senseFly acquisition
summary: AgEagle reported full-year FY2022 revenue of $19.1 million (up 96% YoY) and a net loss of $58.3 million compared to $30.1 million in the prior year, driven by non-cash goodwill impairment charges totaling $41.7 million. Management provided no specific financial guidance for FY2023 but expressed confidence that cost synergies from integration will flow through to profitability later in 2023 while maintaining strict cash discipline.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined significantly to $822k from $4.2m prior year due to the removal of a one-time Ferring license order ($3.6M) that inflated FY2021 results.
Net loss widened to $10.9 million (vs $6.7M last year), with adjusted EBITDA losses increasing from $2.8M to $8.4M.
positive_highlights: Acquisition of Wisconsin Fertility Institute signed with binding agreement, bringing approximately $5.5 million in trailing revenue and ~$1.9M net income upon consolidation.
summary: INVO Bioscience reported Q4 FY2022 revenue of approximately $822,000 (down from ~$4.2M prior year) and a net loss of $10.9 million compared to $6.7 million in the prior period. The company announced an acquisition agreement for Wisconsin Fertility Institute with trailing 12-month revenues of roughly $5.5 million and projected full-year contribution starting next fiscal year, while existing INVO Centers generated ~$1.4M combined revenue. Management noted delays in finalizing the annual 10-K due to the audit process but expressed excitement about the acquisition strategy adding scale.

negative_highlights: Q4 net loss attributable to common stockholders was $15.8 million ($20.46 per share), heavily impacted by a non-cash impairment charge of $9.7 million.
Revenue declined year-over-year in Q4 due to reduced advertising spend and the lack of wholesale revenue from Bailey 44, which moved online-only in June.
The company is still paying off an MCA loan used for acquisitions, with weekly payments expected to cease only after mid-October.
positive_highlights: Gross margin expanded significantly from 24.6% in FY2021 to 42.6% in FY2022, an increase of 18 percentage points driven by operating leverage and reclassification adjustments.
Sales and marketing expense ratio declined sharply from 50.2% a year ago to 35.4%, illustrating strong cost discipline despite revenue volatility.
Cross-merchandising strategy proved successful with Sundry e-commerce daily revenue increasing an additional 50% over four days following the launch of Stateside products.
summary: Digital Brands Group reported a net revenue decrease of 15.8% to $3.4 million in Q4 FY2022 and a full-year increase of only 82.4%, driven by the delayed acquisition of Sundry which closed on December 30, 2022. The company recorded a significant one-time impairment charge of $9.7 million ($12.56 per share) in Q4 and an interest expense of $3 million related to MCA financing. Management emphasized that these results are backward-looking and do not reflect the positive working capital cycle transition or EBITDA positivity expected starting this fall.

negative_highlights: Q4 gross margin fell to 35.3% from 41% in the prior year despite a 160-basis-point sequential improvement
Full-year adjusted EBITDA declined to $18.1 million from $24.7 million in the prior year
Annual recurring software application subscription revenue fell from $94 million to $80 million, and S&SS remaining performance obligations were down 7% quarter over quarter
positive_highlights: Software and subscription services revenue reached a record $51.4 million, up 25% year over year and 65% of total revenue
Adjusted EBITDA increased 44% sequentially to $6.8 million, or approximately 9% of revenue
Restructuring announced in late January expected to deliver $10–12 million in annualized cash savings
summary: CalAmp reported Q4 FY2023 revenue of $78.5 million, flat sequentially and up 15% year over year, while full-year revenue of $295 million was flat versus the prior year. Software and subscription services revenue reached a record $51.4 million, up 25% year over year, and adjusted EBITDA rose 44% sequentially to $6.8 million, but gross margin fell to 35.3% from 41% a year ago. Guidance for Q1 FY2024 is $72–78 million in revenue and $5–9 million in adjusted EBITDA, implying a sequential decline. The company announced a restructuring expected to save $10–12 million annually and said it aims to return to year-over-year revenue growth by the end of FY2024.

negative_highlights: Operating income decreased approximately $2.8 million (down 73% YoY) due to revenue mix shifts toward lower margin logistics.
Customer Care revenue declined 18.8% as pandemic-related projects ended and streaming client interactions were lighter than anticipated.
Marketing Services revenue fell 13% driven by the roll-off of direct mail campaigns and reduced spend from B2B tech customers.
positive_highlights: Company maintained positive EBITDA of $2.1 million despite lower revenue levels, demonstrating resilience against macroeconomic headwinds.
Fulfillment & Logistics segment grew revenues by approximately $3.1 million (up 16.7% YoY) and generated $0.5 million in EBITDA from the InsideOut acquisition.
Balance sheet strengthened with a $5.3 million federal tax refund, no debt on books, and authorization of a new share repurchase program.
summary: Harte Hanks reported Q1 FY2023 revenue of $47.1 million (down 4% YoY) and a net loss of $0.8 million ($0.11/share), compared to prior year income of $3.3 million, driven by the end of pandemic-related projects in Customer Care and reduced spend from financial services clients. Management stated that previously shared fiscal year expectations are no longer relevant due to macroeconomic headwinds stronger than expected and limited visibility beyond Q2. The company announced a new segment combining Marketing Services and Customer Care into 'Customer Experience' and authorized a $6.5 million share buyback program.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined 5% year-over-year.
Operating income decreased 23% year-over-year.
Marketing expenses increased by $1.3 million to support brand recognition and sales development.
positive_highlights: Core solutions TRCV increased 1% year-over-year.
Operating expenses were kept consistent through cost containment and workforce automation.
Company continued capital allocation with dividends and share repurchases.
summary: Revenue declined 5% YoY in Q1 2023, partly due to the scheduled closure of the Canadian location and focus on core offerings. Operating income fell 23% YoY, driven by revenue decline and a $1.3 million increase in marketing expenses. TRCV grew 1% for core solutions, but total TRCV was $146.7 million. The company funded $2.9 million for innovation, $3 million in dividends, and $2 million in buybacks. No forward guidance was provided.

negative_highlights: Operating adjusted EBITDA declined slightly to $80 million from $84 million in the prior-year quarter
Targus downturn was larger than expected, with management noting COVID-related benefits fading and prior-year freight costs elevated by $20 million
Episodic capital markets and liquidation businesses contributed minimally, and management said the macro environment has not improved
positive_highlights: Total revenues rose 75% YoY to $432 million
Security lending revenue grew over 140% YoY and Fixed Income revenue rose ~65%
Wealth Management returned to profitability with revenues up sequentially to $50 million
summary: B. Riley reported Q1 2023 total revenues of $432 million, up 75% YoY, with net income available to common shareholders of $15 million or $0.51 per diluted share and adjusted EBITDA of $95 million. Operating revenues rose 43% to $381 million, but operating adjusted EBITDA slipped slightly to $80 million from $84 million a year earlier. Management emphasized diversification and recurring cash flow amid weak capital markets and episodic deal activity, noting no explicit forward guidance and a Q2 macro that has not improved. A quarterly dividend of $1.00 per share was affirmed and $54 million of buybacks were completed, but no formal guidance figures were provided.

negative_highlights: Average note price per assessment decreased by 30%, falling from approximately $489 to $342.
Cash burn accelerated to $4.3 million, higher than usual due to significant technology spend and slower accounts receivable conversion.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 17% year-over-year despite a challenging macro environment for biotech funding.
summary: iSpecimen reported Q1 FY2023 revenue of approximately $3 million, a 17% year-over-year increase driven by a 75% rise in specimen volume to 8,629 units. However, average watching price per assessment declined 30% from the prior year due to market headwinds and competitive pressure on pricing. Management noted that while Q1 results met internal expectations reflecting seasonality, cash burn increased to $4.3 million primarily due to heavy technology investments of $1.9 million.

negative_highlights: No virologic effect on viral RNA decline in the overall population; placebo arm showed rapid viral clearance.
Revenue fell to $17.8 million from $18.7 million year-over-year on lower MAVYRET patient volumes.
Net loss widened to $37.7 million from $33.6 million year-over-year.
positive_highlights: SPRINT met primary endpoint with favorable safety and tolerability; no serious adverse events or discontinuations.
EDP-235 400mg showed statistically significant symptom improvement at all time points in patients enrolled within 3 days of onset, with hazard ratio 1.9 for time to symptom improvement.
Closed $200 million royalty sale to OMERS, extending cash runway to calendar 2026.
summary: Enanta reported Q2 FY2023 revenue of $17.8 million, down from $18.7 million a year earlier due to lower MAVYRET patient volumes. Net loss widened to $37.7 million or $1.79 per share from $33.6 million or $1.63 per share in the prior year. Top-line SPRINT data showed EDP-235 met primary safety endpoint and improved symptoms, but missed virologic endpoints; management is focusing on partnership for Phase 3 and considering a Phase 2 in long COVID. The company raised $200 million via a royalty sale, extending cash runway into 2026.

negative_highlights: Adjusted contribution margin of 1.8% missed the guided 3.5%-4% range, which management attributed to lower demand and prior-period charge cleanup.
Flight revenue declined 2% year-over-year as live flight legs fell, and management guided Q2 organic revenue down 15%-19%.
Full-year 2023 guidance was suspended, with management citing higher-than-normal financial variability from program changes and macro softness.
positive_highlights: OpEx was down more than $7 million sequentially and $12 million versus the Q3 2022 run rate, better than guidance for a slight decline.
Prepaid blocks were $100 million for the quarter, reflecting continued customer commitments despite being lower year-over-year.
G&A expenses fell 16% sequentially in dollar terms as spending reductions accelerated.
summary: Q1 FY2023 revenue came in with membership revenue up 5% YoY and flight revenue down 2% YoY, while adjusted contribution margin of 1.8% fell well below the 3.5%-4% guidance. Adjusted EBITDA loss was $48.9 million, near the high end of the $45-$50 million loss range, and the company suspended its full-year 2023 guidance, providing only Q2 revenue of $350-$360 million and adjusted EBITDA loss of $39-$44 million. Management framed the quarter around a pending member program overhaul and cost cuts aimed at positive adjusted EBITDA in 2024, but acknowledged macro softness and transitional churn.

negative_highlights: FFO fell to $0.28 per diluted share from $0.35 and AFFO to $0.36 from $0.39 year-over-year
Combined portfolio NOI grew only 1% as total expenses rose 15.2%, with non-controllable expenses up 21.5%
Average occupancy declined to 94.2% from 96.4%, and blended lease spreads slowed from 5.3% in Q1 to 4.6% in April
positive_highlights: Average monthly rents for the combined portfolio rose 10.9% year-over-year
Chatham Court sale expected to close in Q2 at a sub-5% cap rate, generating a 22% IRR over a seven-year hold and $19 million of net proceeds
Recurring and replacement CapEx totaled roughly $217 per unit, below the $300 per unit assumed in NOI guidance
summary: BRT reported Q1 FY2023 FFO of $0.28 per diluted share versus $0.35 a year ago and AFFO of $0.36 versus $0.39, with a net loss of $0.21 per diluted share compared with prior-year net income of $0.62 that had included a $0.70 property sale gain. Combined portfolio NOI rose 1% as revenue grew 7.1% but total expenses rose 15.2% (non-controllable up 21.5%), with $396,000 of storm/insurance-cancellation costs cutting NOI by 2.6 points and $678,000 of higher interest expense also weighing. Full-year 2023 guidance and assumptions were affirmed unchanged, and the Chatham Court sale at a sub-5% cap rate plus the $62.5 million Richmond acquisition remain on track for Q2 and year-end respectively. Average occupancy fell to 94.2% from 96.4%, while blended lease spreads slowed to 5.3% in Q1 and 4.6% in April.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA fell to $8.4 million from $10.7 million in Q4 on seasonal production costs, higher freight, bonus payments and Blair staffing
Q2 volume guidance of 1.0-1.2 million tons with management pointing to the lower end; Appalachia demand expected to moderate on low natural gas prices
Shortfall revenue of $1.9 million supported Q1 revenue and will be lower in Q2, with the related contract expiring in Q3
positive_highlights: Sales volume of 1.195 million tons rose 40% YoY, the fourth consecutive quarter above 1.1 million tons
Contribution margin per ton improved to $14.89 from $14.77 sequentially; Q2 guided to remain mid-double-digit
Third consecutive quarter of positive free cash flow at $1.1 million; Blair facility began shipping sand this month
summary: Smart Sand sold 1.195 million tons in Q1 FY2023, up 40% YoY and slightly above Q4's 1.175 million tons, on revenue of $82.4 million versus $73.8 million prior quarter. Contribution margin was $17.8 million and adjusted EBITDA $8.4 million, down from $10.7 million in Q4 on seasonal production costs, higher freight, bonus payments and Blair staffing; free cash flow was $1.1 million. Management guided Q2 volumes to 1.0-1.2 million tons, flagging possible moderation in Appalachia on low natural gas prices and April weather/rail issues, with Q2 contribution margin per ton expected mid-double-digit and full-year free cash flow positive. Shortfall revenue will be lower in Q2 and the related contract expires in Q3, while the Blair mine began shipping this month.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined by approximately 19% year-over-year (or 18.6% per CFO) due to softer demand across the industry.
Order intake fell significantly, with Q1 orders down roughly 35% compared to the prior period.
Management warned that current high gross margins are likely an anomaly and expect them to compress in coming quarters as pricing pressure increases.
positive_highlights: Gross profit margin expanded significantly to 36.8%, an increase of 1,190 basis points over Q1 2022 and exceeding management's conservative guidance.
Adjusted EBITDA improved by 171% year-over-year as lower manufacturing costs and freight expenses offset revenue declines.
Company maintained a strong balance sheet with $11.3 million in cash, reduced debt to $49.8 million, and paid down an $8.5 million balloon payment early.
summary: Boxlight reported Q1 FY2023 revenue of $41.2 million and adjusted EBITDA of $3.3 million, representing a decline in both metrics compared to the prior year quarter due to softer demand and foreign exchange headwinds. Management maintained full-year guidance for modest single-digit growth but noted that H1 2023 would be down approximately 17% from last year before expecting a rebound in the second half driven by government-funded tenders.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to ~$10M from ~$9.8M in Q1 2022, with operating cash burn rising to ~$9.4M from ~$7.8M
Cash runway of ~$37.4M extends only into Q4 2023, with the Q3 interim data readout falling close to the runway horizon
Management repeatedly declined to give patient counts, dose-level detail, or substance of the Q3 readout, and specific efficacy for patient three was not confirmed
positive_highlights: Eliminated all commercial sales-based royalties and milestone obligations to Precigen, representing potential savings of over $160M
Fully prepaid the remaining $11M SVB term loan, releasing $13.9M of restricted cash back to the company
Enrollment accelerated with a fully booked manufacturing schedule; total patient target for Phase 1 unchanged at 12-15 when including 3 previously treated patients
summary: Alaunos reported Q1 2023 net loss of ~$10M, or $0.04 per share, versus a $9.8M net loss, or $0.05 per share, in the prior-year period. R&D expenses rose 17% to ~$6.5M while G&A fell 10% to ~$3.2M, and cash burn increased to ~$9.4M from ~$7.8M a year earlier. The company ended the quarter with ~$37.4M in total cash and reiterated 2023 operating cash outflow guidance of $35M-$40M, expecting runway into Q4 2023. Management confirmed 9-12 patients dosed this year (plus 3 previously treated, unchanged from prior 12-15 guidance) and reiterated an interim Phase 1 readout in Q3 plus ASCO translational data in June.

Vroom reported Q1 2023 revenue of $197 million, down 6% sequentially, with e-commerce units down 5% and an adjusted EBITDA loss excluding non-recurring costs of $64 million, an improvement of $10 million sequentially. E-commerce gross profit per unit rose 107% to $2,552 sequentially, but 77% of units sold were aged over 180 days, pressuring margins, and management guided Q2 GPPU to be roughly flat with Q1 before improving in the second half as aged inventory clears. The company reaffirmed its 2023 year-end cash outlook of $150 million to $200 million and cited $42 million in annualized cost savings from reductions in force, while UACC securitization losses led to waiving servicing fees and consolidating an off-balance-sheet securitization. The key change versus the prior quarter was the recasting of adjusted EBITDA to include finance receivable fair value adjustments, which increased reported losses and altered comparability.

negative_highlights: Sequential sales growth of 12% marked a slowdown from the 20%+ rates seen in prior quarters, which management attributed to launch-curve flattening in the small PEComa indication.
Net loss widened to $15.2 million from $13.9 million in the prior-year quarter.
No financial guidance was provided, and PEComa market size remains uncertain with the estimated patient population at only 100 to 300.
positive_highlights: FYARRO Q1 sales of $5.9 million rose 12% sequentially, bringing cumulative sales to more than $21 million in 13 months on the market.
Unique ordering accounts exceeded 145, up 21% sequentially, with 26 new accounts and a reorder rate above 90%.
Cash, cash equivalents and note weakness in-term investments of $151 million are expected to fund operations into 2025.
summary: Aadi Bioscience reported Q1 FY2023 FYARRO sales of $5.9 million, a 12% sequential increase over Q4, with more than 145 unique ordering accounts (up 21% sequentially) and a reorder rate above 90%. Net loss widened to $15.2 million from $13.9 million a year earlier, while R&D rose to $11 million and SG&A to $11.2 million; the company ended the quarter with $151 million in cash, expected to fund operations into 2025. No financial guidance was given, and management noted the 12% growth was slower than the 20%+ sequential rates seen in prior quarters as the launch curve matures. Clinical updates included a PRECISION 1 enrollment update with more than 15 tumor types and no new safety signals, and the company continues to target full enrollment by spring 2024 with interim efficacy data on 40 patients expected later in 2023.

negative_highlights: Two patients labeled as PRs in the clinical study report may actually be CRs, but are recorded as PRs due to investigator labeling.
STS PFS data are preliminary and subject to change with more patient enrollment.
Clinical costs are trending downward, but R&D expense increased by about $1 million due to technology rights acquisition.
positive_highlights: In the last eight AML patients, four had blast counts fall to less than 5%, a 50% complete response rate.
Preliminary median PFS in soft tissue sarcoma with lung mets approaching three months, nearly doubling historical norms.
No cardiac toxicity observed across all Annamycin trials despite many patients exceeding lifetime anthracycline limits.
summary: In Q1 2023, Moleculin reported continued clinical progress in its Annamycin programs for AML and soft tissue sarcoma. The company emphasized strong preliminary efficacy data, including a 50% complete response rate in a subset of AML patients and progression-free survival improvement in STS patients with lung metastases. Management highlighted the absence of cardiotoxicity in all trials, with over $37 million cash runway into Q3 2024. Guidance remains focused on advancing to Phase 2 in AML later this year and announcing additional data readouts.

negative_highlights: Billings fell 28.5% year-over-year to $97.2 million and 3.7% sequentially
Paid subscribers dropped 14.5% to 777,000 and active free subscribers fell 11.5% to 4 million
ARPU declined to $493 from $636 as conversion rate fell roughly 15 basis points quarter-over-quarter
positive_highlights: Net income from operations rose $13.1 million or 75.7% year-over-year to $30.6 million on cost discipline
Adjusted cash flow from operations improved to $3.9 million from $1.1 million, a 4.0% margin versus 0.8%
Initiated a $0.01 per share quarterly dividend representing a 2.4% annual yield
summary: MarketWise reported Q1 2023 GAAP revenue of $126.2 million, down 7.7% year-over-year, with billings plunging 28.5% to $97.2 million and paid subscribers down 14.5% to 777,000. Cost cuts drove net income from operations up 75.7% to $30.6 million and adjusted cash flow from operations to $3.9 million from $1.1 million a year ago. No forward financial guidance was provided; management said billings and subscriber pressure will persist until macro conditions improve, and it initiated a $0.01 quarterly dividend. ARPU fell to $493 from $636, and active free subscribers declined 11.5% to 4 million.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA loss widened to $4.5M from $1.1M in the prior year quarter
Digital subscription revenue declined $2.6M to $3.9M as resources shifted to free ad-supported content
$102.7M in term debt and bridge notes are due at year-end, and refinancing discussions are ongoing with no final solution announced
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 7% YoY to $51.4M, with digital advertising up 9% to $23.5M and licensing/syndication up 49% to $4.6M
Gross margin expanded to 42% from 41%, and operating expenses rose only 2% despite acquired businesses
Net cash used in operations improved by $11.6M YoY to $1.7M, and cash rose to $16M from $13.9M at year-end
summary: Arena Group reported Q1 2023 revenue of $51.4M, up 7% YoY from $48.2M, with gross margin expanding to 42% from 41% and opex up only 2% to $35.9M. However, adjusted EBITDA loss widened to $4.5M from $1.1M, net loss grew to $19.4M from $18.4M, and digital subscription revenue fell $2.6M to $3.9M. Full-year 2023 guidance was maintained at $255-270M revenue and $30-35M adjusted EBITDA as the company works to refinance $102.7M in term debt and bridge notes due at year-end. The quarter was mixed, with revenue growth and cost discipline offset by expanding losses and no guidance raise.

negative_highlights: Net loss increased to $20.5 million from $17.4 million year-over-year.
R&D expenses rose to $16.7 million due to higher clinical trial costs for milademetan.
Management declined to provide guidance on cash runway or specific timelines for MANTRA-2 readout.
positive_highlights: Achieved required number of events to trigger primary endpoint analysis in global Phase 3 MANTRA study.
Top-line data from MANTRA expected to be released this quarter.
Cash position of $109.8 million provides runway to complete all ongoing and planned clinical trials.
summary: Rain Oncology reported a net loss of $20.5 million for Q1 FY2023, an increase from $17.4 million in the prior year quarter, driven by higher R&D expenses ($16.7M vs $13.6M) and G&A costs. The company achieved the required number of events to trigger the primary endpoint analysis in its Phase 3 MANTRA study for milademetan, expecting top-line data release this quarter. Management provided no financial guidance or cash runway updates, citing the pending clinical readout as a priority.

negative_highlights: Casinos & Resorts EBITDAR was negatively impacted by material weather disruptions in Lake Tahoe (unprecedented snowfall) and Evansville (tornadoes), causing a $3.5 million shortfall at those two properties.
Corporate expenses were $3.5M higher than expected due to one-time costs, though management noted this is not indicative of the run-rate which they expect to normalize back to $13-$14M.
North America Interactive reported a loss of negative $10.5 million EBITDAR for the quarter as it scales operations in New Jersey and Ontario prior to launching in Pennsylvania.
positive_highlights: Casinos & Resorts segment generated record Q1 revenues of $329 million, up 9.4% YoY, with core portfolio EBITDAR margins expanding to 37.8% excluding lower-margin Atlantic City and Tropicana properties.

International Interactive grew revenue by 9.6% in the UK on a constant currency basis while maintaining positive contribution from North American iGaming operations (New Jersey generating over $1M monthly profit).
Strategic partnerships with Kambi and White Hat announced to transition sports betting infrastructure to a variable cost model, reducing fixed costs and economic risk.
summary: Bally's reported Q1 FY2023 revenues of $598.7 million (up 9.2% YoY) and Adjusted EBITDA of $126.4 million (up 10.2% YoY), driven by strong Casinos & Resorts performance ($329M revenue, record segment result) despite weather headwinds in Tahoe and Evansville. Management upgraded full-year guidance to a range of $665-$700 million EBITDAR citing FX tailwinds and confidence in the business following new technology partnerships with Kambi and White Hat that shift sports betting costs from fixed to variable. The company repurchased 1M shares for $19.8M and reduced full-year CapEx guidance by $10M.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to $25.3 million from $20.8 million in the year-ago quarter as R&D expenses rose to $23.0 million from $17.4 million
No revenue and no product commercial stage, with operations funded entirely by cash reserves
Follow-up data on the Phase Ib IMU-856 celiac patients is not planned, limiting longer-term durability evidence
positive_highlights: Reported highly positive Phase Ib Part C data for IMU-856 in celiac disease showing clinical improvements versus placebo across four dimensions of disease pathophysiology
Reported positive, statistically significant maintenance-phase data for vidofludimus calcium versus placebo in the Phase IIb CALDOSE-1 ulcerative colitis trial
Cash and investments of $97.1 million with stated runway into Q4 2024
summary: Immunic is a clinical-stage biotech with no product revenue; Q1 2023 R&D expenses were $23.0 million versus $17.4 million a year earlier, G&A was $4.3 million, and the net loss widened to $25.3 million ($0.58 per share) from $20.8 million ($0.74 per share on more shares). The company ended the quarter with $97.1 million in cash and investments and guided to runway into Q4 2024. The call's focus was clinical, not financial: management reported positive Phase IIb CALDOSE-1 maintenance data for vidofludimus calcium in ulcerative colitis, highly positive Phase Ib Part C data for IMU-856 in celiac disease, and guided to an interim biomarker analysis from the Phase II CALLIPER trial in progressive MS in the second half of 2023, with top-line CALLIPER data at end-2024 and the first Phase III ENSURE readout at end-2025.

negative_highlights: The company remains unprofitable with an adjusted EBITDA loss of roughly $1.7 million despite revenue growth.
Management explicitly stated they are taking a 'measured pace' on acquisitions due to resource constraints, limiting the speed of scale-up.
One planned Bay Area clinic opportunity was put on hold indefinitely.
positive_highlights: Revenue increased by approximately 113% YoY and grew 46% sequentially, reflecting building patient awareness at existing clinics.
Gross margin expanded significantly from 60% to 79% driven by improved efficiencies at the Atlanta INVO Center.
Adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed from $2 million in Q1 FY2022 to approximately $1.7 million.
summary: Q1 FY2023 revenue totaled approximately $348,000 (up from $163,000 in the prior year), driven by consolidated service revenue of roughly $297,000 and product sales. The company reported an adjusted EBITDA loss improvement to a net loss of $1.7 million compared to $2 million last year, with gross margins expanding from 60% to 79%. Management reiterated that the Wisconsin acquisition is on track for closing in Q2 but noted they are taking a measured pace due to resource constraints.

negative_highlights: Operating loss widened to $7.2 million from $6.9 million year-over-year.
Cash burn remained at $6.1 million, consistent with the prior five quarters.
No specific financial guidance provided for the quarter.
positive_highlights: Raised $7.5 million in gross proceeds and $2.8 million net via ATM facility, ending Q1 with $14.3 million cash.
Completed first round of beta programs with four partners including Novant Health and Stanford University.
FDA 510(k) submission for heart rate and SpO2 planned for June with clinical data showing <1 bpm error.
summary: Movano Health reported an operating loss of $7.2 million in Q1 FY2023, an increase from the prior year's $6.9 million loss, driven by accelerated R&D and commercialization efforts for the Evie Ring. The company raised $7.5 million in gross proceeds via a public offering and $2.8 million net via its ATM facility, ending the quarter with $14.3 million in cash. Management provided no specific financial guidance but confirmed plans to launch the Evie Ring in September 2023 for $269 without a subscription.

negative_highlights: Net loss increased from $4.1 million in Q1 2022 to $5.8 million in Q1 2023.
Cash and cash equivalents decreased from $38.8 million at year-end 2022 to $34.2 million at quarter-end 2023.
positive_highlights: First patient dosed in the Phase I/IIa trial of narazaciclib combined with letrozole in low-grade endometrioid endometrial cancer.
Rigosertib demonstrated durable complete clinical responses in patients with RDEB-associated SCC, leading to a request for an FDA Type B meeting.
Narazaciclib monotherapy showed acceptable safety profiles with no clinically meaningful cases of neutropenia or diarrhea at the 240-milligram cohort.
summary: Onconova reported a net loss of $5.8 million ($0.28 per share) for Q1 FY2023, an increase from the prior year's loss of $4.1 million, primarily driven by narazaciclib clinical development expenses. The company closed the quarter with $34.2 million in cash, sufficient to fund operations into Q1 2024. Management highlighted significant clinical progress, including the first patient dosed in the Phase I/IIa trial of narazaciclib combined with letrozole for endometrial cancer and a request for an FDA Type B meeting for rigosertib in RDEB-associated SCC.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to approximately $7 million in Q1 FY2023 versus a prior year miss context (though absolute numbers improved)
Non-cash interest expense increased by $0.2 million due to royalty liability amortization
No commercial launch timeline or sales hiring plans provided for 2024
positive_highlights: FDA confirmed review will proceed on standard timeline without an advisory committee
Roluperidone NDA filed with a PDUFA goal date of February 26, 2024
Company received $3.1 million refund from FDA filing fees
summary: Minerva Neurosciences reported a net loss of approximately $7 million for Q1 FY2023 compared to $9.8 million in the prior year quarter, driven by reduced R&D and G&A expenses but increased non-cash interest expense on royalty liabilities. The company confirmed FDA acceptance of its roluperidone NDA with a PDUFA date of February 26, 2024, noting no advisory committee is planned. Management indicated that existing cash reserves are sufficient for at least the next 12 months.

negative_highlights: Net loss from continuing operations widened to $12.3 million from $10.8 million, including a ~$2.5 million deferred tax provision
No quantitative forward guidance provided; RTLS LOI remains nonbinding with no timeline for a definitive agreement
Disclosed NASDAQ bid-price compliance notice received in mid-April, and ATM usage has diluted shares outstanding
positive_highlights: Revenue rose 17% YoY to $3.1 million from $2.6 million on stronger Indoor Intelligence sales (Aware and RTLS lines)
Gross margin expanded to 75% from 70%, and gross profit grew 25% to $2.3 million
Operating expenses fell $0.6 million YoY to $10.5 million; adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed to $7.7 million from $8.8 million
summary: Inpixon reported Q1 2023 continuing-operations revenue of $3.1 million, up 17% YoY from $2.6 million, with gross margin expanding to 75% from 70%. However, net loss from continuing operations widened to $12.3 million from $10.8 million, driven partly by a ~$2.5 million deferred tax provision, and non-GAAP adjusted EBITDA remained a $7.7 million loss (improved from $8.8 million). The quarter was dominated by the March 14 spin-off of the Workplace Experience business to CXApp, and management gave no quantitative guidance, declining to provide a timeline for a definitive RTLS transaction. Cash stood at $15.3 million, and the company disclosed a NASDAQ bid-price compliance notice received in mid-April.

negative_highlights: Drone sales declined sharply to $2M from $27M YoY as the company transitions focus to the new eBee VISION model.
Operating loss increased to -$4.2M compared to a smaller loss in Q1 FY2023, indicating ongoing cash burn despite top-line growth.
Software subscription revenue decreased year-over-year from $170k to $121k.
positive_highlights: Gross margin improved significantly to 48.8% from 35.5% YoY due to supply chain optimization and cost reductions.
Sensor segment revenue doubled year-over-year driven by strong demand for RedEdge-P and Altum-PT sensors.
Signed a two-year supply agreement with WingTra representing approximately $2 million in future revenue.
summary: AgEagle reported Q1 FY23 revenue of $4.1 million (up 5.6% YoY) and a gross margin expansion to 48.8%, but operating loss widened from -$7.5M in the prior year period due to lower drone sales ($2M vs $27M). Management raised no new guidance, noting that while sensor demand is strong with a signed WingTra deal worth ~$2M over two years, overall profitability remains elusive as they work toward cash flow breakeven.

negative_highlights: Vessel operating expenses rose and inflation remains a concern, partially offsetting higher charter revenues.
Weighted average interest rate increased to 8.15% due to higher LIBOR/SOFR.
Share price has not reflected the increase in net asset value, per management.
positive_highlights: TCE revenues rose 139% YoY to $9.2 million and net income to common shareholders was $8.7 million ($0.81 basic EPS) versus a $3.7 million loss in Q1 2022.
MR daily TCE reached $23,508, more than double the prior-year period, and Q2 2023 bookings were at an estimated $29,160 for 70% of available days.
Sale of the Pyxis Malou generated an $8 million gain and almost $19 million in net cash proceeds, raising total cash to $30.5 million with net funded debt at 23% of total capitalization.
summary: Pyxis Tankers reported Q1 FY2023 TCE revenues of $9.2 million, up 139% YoY, and net income to common shareholders of $8.7 million ($0.81 basic EPS), versus a $3.7 million loss in Q1 2022. The quarter included an $8 million gain on the sale of the oldest tanker, the Pyxis Malou, for $24.8 million, with $19 million in net cash proceeds. Daily TCE for MRs was $23,508, more than double the year-ago period, and adjusted EBITDA improved to $4.2 million. For Q2 2023, 70% of available days were booked at an estimated average TCE of $29,160, sequentially higher than Q1; no formal earnings guidance was provided.

negative_highlights: Backlog fell to $1.9 million from $11.2 million a year ago
Net bookings declined to $800,000 from $2.1 million year over year
Received a NASDAQ minimum bid price deficiency notice; no assurance of regaining compliance
positive_highlights: Revenue grew to $4.7 million from $1.7 million in the prior-year quarter
Gross margin expanded to 18.2% from 5.2%, and operating expenses fell 24% year over year to $1.3 million
Net loss narrowed to $0.4 million ($0.05 per share) from $1.4 million ($0.41 per share); debt-free with $15.9 million cash
summary: Q1 revenue rose to $4.7 million from $1.7 million a year ago, driven by completion of previously delayed projects, while gross margin expanded to 18.2% from 5.2% and net loss narrowed to $0.4 million ($0.05 per share) from $1.4 million. However, net bookings fell to $800,000 from $2.1 million and backlog collapsed to $1.9 million from $11.2 million on reduced cannabis capital spending. Management expects OpEx to fall further from the $1.3 million quarterly level but gave no quantitative revenue guidance, citing a prolonged cannabis construction lull and a NASDAQ minimum bid price notice.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to $557,000 from $119,900 due to bromine prices plunging by the highest percentage in memory.
Gross margin contracted significantly to 27% from 52% YoY as bromine note prices fell 48%.
Chemical and natural gas segments generated no revenue due to factory closures and equipment delays.
positive_highlights: Revenue increased 4% YoY to $9.3 million despite severe market headwinds.
Company generated $4.8 million in free cash flow and maintained a strong cash position of $115.8 million.
Crude salt segment turned profitable with $42,930 profit compared to a loss last year.
summary: Gulf Resources reported Q1 FY2023 revenue of $9.3 million (up 4% YoY) but a net loss of $557,000 and EPS loss of $0.05, driven by a 48% drop in bromine prices and winter shutdowns closing production facilities. Management stated that while the quarter was weak due to these headwinds, they generated $4.8 million in cash flow and ended with $115.8 million in cash. Guidance for the year remains cautious regarding price timing but optimistic about a potential rebound and future facility openings.

negative_highlights: No revenue, EPS, or margin figures were reported for the quarter.
AMP-270 pancreatic cancer enrollment has been slower than expected, with possible first dosing slipping to Q3 2023.
Two site dropouts occurred due to inability to pay per-patient costs.
positive_highlights: Cash runway stated to extend through the end of 2024.
Received over $600,000 for Ampligen supplied to the Dutch Early Access Program.
Ovarian cancer Phase 2 interim report expected in June 2023.
summary: AIM ImmunoTech's Q1 FY2023 call contained no reported revenue, EPS, or margin figures. Management said cash is sufficient to fund operations through the end of 2024, citing over $600,000 received for Ampligen supplied to the Dutch Early Access Program and external funding for several studies through grants from Merck, NIH, and DoD. Key program updates included the AMP-270 locally advanced pancreatic cancer study, where the first site opened in Q4 2022 but enrollment has been slower than expected, with first patient enrollment still expected in Q2 2023 and possible first dosing in Q3. The DURIPANC metastatic pancreatic cancer study with AstraZeneca is expected to commence in Q4 2023, potentially earlier. The company noted an interim report for the advanced recurrent ovarian cancer study expected in June.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined sharply by 24% compared to Q1 FY2022, primarily attributed to logistical hurdles from post-zero-COVID policies in China and pent-up travel demand.
Sales volume dropped as the company sold only 36,841 transmission units versus 41,902 a year ago.
Operating income decreased by nearly $1 million despite margin expansion due to lower sales volumes.
positive_highlights: Gross margin improved significantly by 320 bps driven by a strategic shift toward higher-value lithium-powered transmission products.
HEVI electric machinery pilot programs with United Rentals received positive feedback, leading to an extension of the pilot and requests for additional demos.
Balance sheet strengthened with cash on hand increasing 125% year-over-year to $15.4 million.
summary: Total revenue decreased by 24% year-over-year to $22.1 million due to supply chain challenges and a stronger dollar, though gross margins expanded 320 basis points to 24.9%. Net income fell to $2.5 million from $2.9 million in the prior period as operating expenses rose slightly despite cost-cutting efforts.

negative_highlights: Net loss attributable to common stockholders was $6.2 million ($1.08 per diluted share), compared to $7.8 million last year.
Non-cash expenses in G&A totaled $3.1 million, significantly impacting reported profitability and cash flow metrics.
EBITDA positivity is not expected until this fall due to ongoing MCA payments ending only in early October.
positive_highlights: Net revenues surged 48.4% YoY to $5.1 million driven by the Sundry acquisition integration.
