Management reaffirmed fiscal 2024 guidance early, expecting Q1 to be the largest revenue quarter in company history, though it cited ongoing operational disruptions from slower Amazon processing and the Bloomios default. The sale of Interactive Offers and reclassification of discontinued operations are expected to improve profitability.

negative_highlights: Net profit declined 17.7% year-over-year primarily due to higher tax provisions and depreciation from spectrum acquisition.
Market share decreased by 0.2 percentage points to 43.5% compared to the previous quarter.
Bundle revenue experienced degrowth as management shifted focus to personalized offers.
positive_highlights: Subscriber base returned to growth momentum with 0.8 million net additions in Q3.
Data revenue accelerated with 26.2% year-over-year growth, driven by 7 GB average usage per user.
Service ARPU increased 8.5% year-over-year due to higher data segment contribution.
summary: Grameenphone reported Q3 FY2023 revenue growth of 6.3% year-over-year and EBITDA growth of 5.7%, maintaining an EBITDA margin of 61.9%. The quarter saw a return to subscriber base growth with 0.8 million net adds, though market share dipped slightly to 43.5%. Management noted that lower bundle revenue was due to personalized offers and higher depreciation/tax provisions impacted net profit.

negative_highlights: Intermodal segment posted an operating loss of $4.3 million, with California drayage operations losing $6.5 million and dragging consolidated EPS down by $0.19.
Trucking segment revenues fell 2.5% to $97.1 million as load counts dropped 13.1% due to inventory destocking and UAW disruptions.
Company-managed brokerage turned negative with a loss of $1.1 million, operating margins contracting to -3.8% from 2.7% last year.
positive_highlights: Contract Logistics segment maintained a record 16.9% operating margin, matching last year's performance despite volume challenges.
Trucking segment achieved a 13.3% increase in revenue per load due to wind energy volumes offsetting declines in other sectors.
Company-managed brokerage improved operating income by $1.8 million to $6.6 million despite a 2.5% drop in top-line revenue.
summary: Universal Logistics Holdings reported Q3 FY2023 earnings of $0.88 per share on total operating revenue of $421.3 million, both metrics coming in line with guidance but significantly below the prior year's peak due to a freight recession and UAW strikes. Operating income decreased to $36.8 million from $69.8 million last year, driven by a massive $67.8 million revenue decline in Intermodal and losses in California drayage operations. Management reiterated Q4 guidance of $350-$375 million in top-line revenue and 7%-9% operating margins, noting that the UAW strike could impact these forecasts.

negative_highlights: Management expects Q4 residential origination to decline versus Q4 last year, with Q1 possibly also showing weakness depending on BoC policy
Q4 commercial outlook is similar with relatively fewer transactions as buyers and sellers grapple with valuations
Residential 30-day arrears rose to 14 bps from 12 bps at the end of Q2
positive_highlights: Pre-fair-market-value income of CAD 95.5 million was 98% higher than the same quarter last year
Residential origination rose 26% YoY to CAD 8.3 billion and commercial origination rose 30% to CAD 3.3 billion
Board raised annualized dividend CAD 0.05 to CAD 2.45 and approved a special dividend; 17th distribution increase since IPO
summary: Q3 2023 pre-fair-market-value income of CAD 95.5 million was up 98% year-over-year, with residential origination of CAD 8.3 billion up 26% and commercial origination of CAD 3.3 billion up 30%, driving MUA to CAD 141.9 billion (residential +8%, commercial +14% YoY). Excluding fair-value gains, net revenue was CAD 254 million, up 21% sequentially, and the Board raised the annualized common dividend by CAD 0.05 to CAD 2.45 plus approved a special dividend. However, management guided to a year-over-year decline in Q4 residential origination (with Q1 weakness possible) and fewer commercial transactions, citing decelerating applications after the July Bank of Canada hike. Residential 30-day arrears ticked up to 14 bps from 12 bps, while 90-day arrears were unchanged at under 6 bps.

negative_highlights: Domains retail gross margin up only 2% net of high-value domain sales; aftermarket weakness persists
Negative cash from operations of $7.1 million in Q3, worse than -$1.0 million a year ago
Macroeconomic environment has not improved and is expected to weigh on markets for years
positive_highlights: Wavelo revenue up 174% YoY and adjusted EBITDA of $4.2 million, its strongest quarter since launch
Ting added 2,600 net subscribers, best quarter in seven quarters, with total subs up 26% YoY
Repaid net $6.5 million on syndicated debt in Q3 and signed improved credit agreement
summary: Tucows Q3 2023 total revenue rose 11.4% to $87.0 million, with Wavelo revenue up 174% to $11.1 million and Ting revenue up 17% to $12.9 million, adding 2,600 net subscribers. Domains revenue grew 1% to $61.1 million with adjusted EBITDA up 5% to $10.9 million. Management affirmed FY2023 guidance of $55-60 million EBITDA for TCX and a Ting loss of $42-45 million, while noting continued macroeconomic headwinds and a significant gap between public valuations and intrinsic business value.

negative_highlights: Full-year revenue guidance lowered by $100 million to the range of $2.4 billion-$2.5 billion.
North America Interactive reported a loss of negative $18 million in adjusted EBITDAR for the quarter, with an expected total annualized loss of approximately $60 million.
Tropicana Las Vegas revenue faces pressure due to uncertainty surrounding Oakland A's relocation plans and lack of reinvestment.
positive_highlights: Consolidated revenues grew 9.4% YoY driven by strong performance in Rhode Island, Kansas City, Black Hawk, and Quad Cities segments.
International Interactive segment net revenues increased 13.1% YoY with margins stabilizing at low-to-mid-30%s.
Chicago Temporary Casino achieved a successful soft launch with week-over-week volume growth despite operating only 20 hours per day.
summary: Consolidated revenues rose 9.4% year-over-year to approximately $633 million, while adjusted EBITDAR increased 6% to roughly $173 million for the third quarter of FY2023. Management updated full-year guidance downward due to a delayed Chicago Temporary Casino opening and reduced reinvestment plans at Tropicana pending MLB's decision on the Oakland A's relocation. Despite these headwinds, management expressed high confidence in 2024 execution following the completion of growth projects in Kansas City and Twin Rivers.

negative_highlights: TV media advertising revenue declined 14% YoY due to weaker demand in tech and pharma categories, reduced political spend, and international headwinds.
Q4 D2C losses are expected to be similar to the year-ago period rather than showing immediate improvement, driven by higher sports costs and marketing for Western European launches.
Filmed Entertainment OIBDA was a loss of $49 million impacted significantly by SAG-AFTRA strike-related idle costs totaling nearly $60 million.
positive_highlights: D2C subscription revenue grew 46% in Q3 driven by Paramount+ subscriber additions and global ARPU expansion of 16%.
Free cash flow delivered at $377 million, with management expecting strong FCF continuation into Q4 despite strike impacts.
Paramount Plus crossed 63 million subscribers globally while domestic monthly churn continued to improve year-over-year.
summary: Paramount Global reported Q3 FY2023 revenue of $7.1 billion and adjusted OIBDA of $716 million, driven by a 46% growth in D2C subscription revenue and strong free cash flow of $377 million. Management highlighted progress on the path to streaming profitability with narrowed losses but noted that Q4 D2C losses will remain similar to the prior year due to higher sports costs and marketing spend for new international launches. The company closed a major asset sale (Simon & Schuster) generating ~$1.6B proceeds, which it intends to use for debt paydown.

negative_highlights: Average note price per specimen decreased by $16 (3%) to $518 in Q3, contributing to a lower nine-month run rate.
Cash and cash equivalents dropped significantly from $15.3 million at year-end FY2022 to $2.7 million as of September 30, 2023.
Management explicitly stated they do not provide financial guidance for the current period.
positive_highlights: Revenue increased by $195,000 (8%) YoY driven by an 11% increase in specimen count to 5,367 units.
The new sequencing procurement program generated a pipeline of 20-30 projects with customer response rates nearing 75%-100%.
Cost reductions are significant: monthly headcount expenses expected down ~29% and other operational costs down ~52% for the remainder of FY2023.
summary: iSpecimen reported Q3 FY2023 revenue of $2.8 million (up 8% YoY) and a slight miss in the trailing nine-month run rate compared to last year due to lower average watching prices ($518 vs $534). Management highlighted significant cost-cutting measures, including a ~29% reduction in headcount-related expenses following a workforce reduction of approximately 20%, but explicitly stated they do not provide financial guidance. The company remains cash-flow neutral through October despite the revenue miss.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined 6.5% year-over-year to $892.8 million due to lower ethanol and distillers grains prices.
MSC protein construction at Madison and Fairmont remains delayed pending permits, which management said are taking longer than expected.
Summit Carbon pipeline startup is now indicated for 2026, a delay from prior expectations.
positive_highlights: EBITDA swung to positive $52 million from negative $35.6 million in the prior-year quarter.
Ultra-High Protein production reached record levels in Q3 and the company began commercial deliveries of 60% protein, achieving up to 62.3% protein content.
Plant utilization improved to 93.9% from 81.5% in Q2 and 90.9% a year ago, with 2024 Ultra-High Protein EBITDA guided to $80–120 million.
summary: Green Plains reported Q3 2023 revenue of $892.8 million, down 6.5% year-over-year, net income of $22.3 million or $0.35 per diluted share, and EBITDA of $52 million, a swing from negative $35.6 million a year ago. Plant utilization rose to 93.9% from 90.9% a year ago and 81.5% in Q2, and Ultra-High Protein production reached record levels with commercial 60% protein output beginning. Management guided to Q4 performance above Q3, 2024 Ultra-High Protein EBITDA of $80–120 million and corn oil contribution of $130–160 million, while noting permitting delays for MSC installations at Madison and Fairmont and a Summit carbon pipeline startup slipped to 2026.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined 6.5% YoY to $892.8 million on lower ethanol and dried distillers grains prices.
SG&A rose to $35.5 million from $29.1 million, driven by legal fees tied to the GPP note-in.
MSC construction at Madison and Fairmont remains pending permitting outcomes, with management noting permitting 'continues to take longer than we thought'.
positive_highlights: Swung to net income of $22.3 million ($0.35 diluted EPS) from a $73.5 million loss a year ago, with EBITDA of $52 million versus negative $35.6 million.
Record Ultra-High Protein production in Q3, with yields over 4 lbs per bushel at Shenandoah, and 60% protein achieved up to 62.3% at Wood River.
2024 guidance introduced for protein EBITDA of $80M-$120M and renewable corn oil contribution of $130M-$160M, with the Tharaldson JV on track for Q1 2024 startup.
summary: Green Plains reported Q3 2023 revenue of $892.8 million, down 6.5% YoY, but swung to net income of $22.3 million ($0.35 diluted EPS) from a $73.5 million loss, with EBITDA of $52 million versus negative $35.6 million a year ago and a 93.9% plant utilization rate. Management guided to stronger Q4 free cash flow and outlined 2024 EBITDA contributions of $80M-$120M from five MSC protein facilities plus a partial year from the Tharaldson JV, alongside renewable corn oil at $130M-$160M. Ultra-High Protein production hit record levels, 60% protein commenced commercial sales, and the GPP merger is targeted to close before year-end, though Madison and Fairmont MSC permitting delays and a soft corn oil pricing environment temper the outlook.

negative_highlights: Significant class flooding impacted production for several days during Q3.
Lease operating expenses increased by $2.2 million versus the prior quarter due to restart costs and flooding events.
Net loss of $13.4 million widened from a net income of $9.8 million in the previous quarter.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA of $19.5 million beat internal projections by $1.9 million due to higher commodity prices.
Production volumes exceeded initial projections following the restart of Beta operations in late April.
Net debt reduced significantly, with liquidity at approximately $31 million and net leverage ratio improving.
summary: Amplify Energy reported a net loss of $13.4 million in Q3 FY2023 compared to prior quarter income, driven by noncash unrealized losses on commodity derivatives despite adjusted EBITDA beating expectations at $19.5 million. Management reaffirmed full-year guidance for both Adjusted EBITDA ($80M-$100M) and Free Cash Flow ($30M-$50M). The company announced strategic initiatives including a marketing process to monetize Bairoil assets starting Q1 2024, restarting development at Beta in H1 2024, and launching Magnify Energy Services.

negative_highlights: Cash balance decreased from $27.6 million to approximately $12.7 million due to $14.9 million used in operating activities.
No active grants were received during the period, with Project NextGen funding remaining uncertain despite ongoing discussions.
positive_highlights: Gedeptin Phase 1 data presented at AACR-AHNS showed the therapy was safe, feasible, and demonstrated tumor size reduction in initial patients.
summary: GeoVax reported a net loss of approximately $18 million for the nine-month period ended September 30, 2023, compared to an $8.6 million loss in the prior year period, driven by increased R&D expenses of $14.5 million versus $5.4 million and G&A expenses rising from $3.4 million to $4.6 million due to clinical trial activity for CMO4S1 and Gedeptin programs.

negative_highlights: RBC ratio declined to 400-420% from 430-450%, driven by interest rate hedge losses and reduced admitted deferred tax assets.
Life segment reported an adjusted loss of $2 million, driven by lower underwriting margin.
positive_highlights: Annuity sales of $2.6 billion, up 5% sequentially, with Shield sales up 15% sequentially.
Adjusted earnings excluding notable items of $275 million, in-line with expectations despite $30 million lower alternative investment income.
Holding company liquidity robust at $900 million; year-to-date share repurchases of $216 million through November 3.
summary: Brighthouse Financial reported Q3 2023 adjusted earnings excluding notable items of $275 million, roughly in-line with expectations and up from $271 million in Q2. Annuity sales totaled $2.6 billion, up 5% sequentially, driven by strong Shield sales. The estimated RBC ratio declined to 400-420% from 430-450% due to interest rate hedge losses and DTA reductions, but management expects a partial recoupment in Q1 2024 via an increased mean reversion point. Holding company liquidity remained robust at $900 million, and share repurchases continued.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA loss widened by $8.2 million sequentially to $64.5 million.
Full-year adjusted EBITDA loss guidance was updated to $225–245 million, reflecting higher realized losses and negative mark-to-market at UACC.
Year-end cash and cash equivalents guidance was reduced to $137–162 million.
positive_highlights: E-commerce units grew 11% sequentially and e-commerce GPPU improved 6% to $3,144 from $2,954.
Adjusted SG&A was reduced $3.1 million sequentially despite the 11% increase in unit volume.
Aged inventory (units held >180 days) fell to 34% of units sold from 80% in Q2, with less than 20% expected in Q4.
summary: Vroom reported Q3 2023 revenue of $236 million, up 5% sequentially, with e-commerce units up 11% and e-commerce GPPU rising 6% to $3,144. Adjusted EBITDA loss widened 15% sequentially to $64.5 million, driven by a $13.3 million headwind from higher net losses and an unfavorable mark-to-market on UACC finance receivables. The company lowered its full-year 2023 adjusted EBITDA loss guidance to $225–245 million and cut its year-end cash and cash equivalents forecast to $137–162 million. Management also disclosed plans to pursue raising capital to scale the business, with no specific structure yet.

negative_highlights: Operating income decreased 10% YoY due to costs exceeding revenue growth
Revenue grew only slightly YoY; Q3 revenue not specified numerically
Net debt of ~$20 million at quarter-end
positive_highlights: 91 health care provider systems adopted Human Understanding Program, 18% from new logos; contract value growth from existing clients averaging 13%
Sales force increased 19% since beginning of year; two consecutive quarters of double-digit sales growth YoY
Operating margin grew 8.3% sequentially over Q2 2023
summary: In Q3 2023, National Research Corporation reported revenue that increased slightly year-over-year, but operating income fell 10% due to costs outgrowing revenue, including marketing, cybersecurity, and nonrecurring tax adjustments. TRCV was $144.3 million at quarter-end. Management highlighted a 19% increase in sales force, two consecutive quarters of double-digit sales growth, and an 11% reduction in FTEs, expecting margin expansion and revenue acceleration in future quarters. Guidance was not explicitly provided.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to $16.3 million from $14.4 million in the prior-year quarter.
R&D expenses increased 35% to $11.9 million, and SG&A rose to $11.2 million, driving higher operating costs.
No explicit financial guidance for revenue or EPS was provided for the full year or next quarter.
positive_highlights: FYARRO sales grew 40% year over year to $6 million in Q3 2023, with $80 million cumulative sales in the first nine months.
Cash balance of $119.3 million is expected to fund operations into 2025.
PRECISION 1 trial enrollment is progressing rapidly, with more than 150 sites available and a first interim data readout expected by mid-December.
summary: Aadi Bioscience reported Q3 2023 FYARRO sales of $6.0 million, up 40% year over year, with cumulative 2023 sales of $80 million. R&D expenses rose to $11.9 million from $8.8 million a year earlier, and net loss widened to $16.3 million from $14.4 million. The company ended the quarter with $119.3 million in cash, expected to fund operations into 2025. Management highlighted progress in the PRECISION 1 trial, now with two planned interim analyses (first by mid-December 2023, second in Q3 2024), and reaffirmed timelines for full enrollment by spring 2024 and study completion by end-2024. No formal financial guidance was provided.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined significantly due to softer industry demand and missed market share expectations in key geographic markets.
A goodwill impairment charge of approximately $13.2 million impacted the bottom line, contributing to a net loss of $17.8 million.
Management lowered Q4 guidance from prior optimistic outlooks citing slower-than-expected second-half performance.
positive_highlights: Gross profit margin improved by 570 basis points to 36.3% driven by lower manufacturing costs and freight reductions.
Order intake increased by 11% for Q3, marking a sequential improvement despite revenue decline.
Company reduced debt facility by $15 million over the last 12 months with an additional $4 million payment subsequent to quarter end.
summary: Boxlight reported Q3 FY2023 revenue of $49.7 million, a decline of approximately 28% year-over-year compared to $68.7 million in the prior period. Adjusted EBITDA was $4.9 million versus $9.9 million last year, while gross margin expanded to 36.3%. Management guided for Q4 revenue and adjusted EBITDA to be flat with the same quarter of the previous year.

negative_highlights: Contribution margin per ton declined sequentially to $17.20 from $17.57 despite higher volumes
Q4 guidance of 900,000-1.1 million tons and $12-16/ton contribution margin represents a clear step down from Q3's ~1.2 million tons and $17.20/ton
Revenue increase to $76.9 million from $74.8 million was driven primarily by contractual shortfall revenue recognition, not underlying price or volume strength
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA rose to $13.3 million from $11.4 million in Q2 and contribution margin to $21.0 million from $19.0 million
Year-to-date free cash flow of $17.5 million, with management stating the company will be cash flow-positive for 2023
Approximately 50% of expected 2024 sales volumes already contracted, plus a stated expectation of at least 10% higher 2024 volumes than 2023
summary: Smart Sand sold ~1.2 million tons in Q3, up 12% sequentially from 1.1 million tons, with revenue of $76.9 million, contribution margin of $21.0 million ($17.20/ton), and adjusted EBITDA of $13.3 million, up from $11.4 million in Q2. Revenue growth was attributed primarily to contractual shortfall revenue recognition rather than pricing, and contribution margin per ton actually fell sequentially from $17.57. Q4 volumes are guided to 900,000-1.1 million tons with contribution margin of $12-16/ton on seasonal Bakken slowdown and customer budget exhaustion, while management expects full-year 2024 sand volumes at least 10% above 2023 and reaffirmed full-year free cash flow positivity ($17.5 million YTD).

negative_highlights: 2023 adjusted EBITDA guidance includes approximately $200 million of gains on asset sales, introducing timing and execution risk.
No incremental FLNG units beyond FLNG1 and FLNG2 are planned, limiting near-term growth from new liquefaction capacity.
Ireland terminal project faces regulatory setback, with an appeal refiled after the government's ruling disagreed with the company's position.
positive_highlights: Downstream operating margin reached $195 million, up from $49 million in Q2 and $15 million in Q1, driven by contracted customer volumes.
Full-year 2023 adjusted EBITDA guidance reaffirmed at $1.6 billion, with Q4 expected to more than double Q3's $208 million.
FLNG1 mechanically complete and first gas introduced, with commissioning expected by year-end; both Puerto Rico power plants completed and operating above 97% reliability.
summary: NFE reported Q3 FY2023 total segment revenue of $514 million, operating margin of $250 million, and downstream operating margin of $195 million, up 4x QoQ and 13x Q1. Net income was $62 million, or $0.30 per diluted share, and the company reaffirmed its full-year 2023 adjusted EBITDA guidance of $1.6 billion, including ~$200 million of asset sale gains, with Q4 adjusted EBITDA expected to 'double or more' Q3's $208 million. The quarter was highlighted by the mechanical completion and first gas introduction at FLNG1, completion of both Puerto Rico power plants, and nearing operational status of two Brazilian LNG terminals. Management expects 2024 adjusted EBITDA of $2.4 billion, over 85% from downstream customers and nearly 90% already contracted.

negative_highlights: Net sales declined 27% year-over-year due to a 22% drop in volume and promotional activity.
Management lowered full-year capital expenditure expectations to $4.5-$5.5 million from the prior $7-$9 million range.
Sales experienced pullback in key western states like California, though partially offset by Midwest strength.
positive_highlights: Adjusted gross margin expanded over 1,200 basis points to 23% driven by restructuring and brand mix.
Proprietary nutrient sales grew over 20% year-over-year, contributing significantly to profitability.
Positive free cash flow of $6.9 million generated despite lower sales levels.
summary: Net sales for Q3 FY2023 were $54.2 million, down 27% year-over-year driven by a 22% decrease in volume and a 5% price/mix decline. Despite the revenue miss, adjusted gross margin expanded significantly to 23% (up 1,200 bps YoY) due to restructuring savings and brand mix, resulting in positive adjusted EBITDA of $0.5 million for the second consecutive quarter. Management reaffirmed full-year net sales guidance at $230-$240 million but noted results will likely be around the lower end of that range.

negative_highlights: GAAP net loss of $76 million driven by unrealized investment losses on equity holdings
$35.5 million noncash goodwill and trade name impairment at Targus due to PC market weakness
Operating adjusted EBITDA of $107.5 million was only up from $106.2 million YoY, despite 48% revenue growth, and management did not provide quantitative forward guidance
positive_highlights: Operating revenue of $473 million was the highest quarterly total in the firm's history
Auction and Liquidation segment generated $78 million revenue and $18 million segment income, led by engagements like Bed Bath & Beyond
Investment banking fee revenue up over 100% from Q2 and Wealth Management revenues increased to $51 million
summary: B. Riley reported Q3 2023 total revenues of $462 million, up 48% YoY, with operating adjusted EBITDA of $107.5 million (up 34% QoQ but only slightly above the prior year's $106.2 million). A GAAP net loss of $76 million was driven by unrealized investment losses and a $35.5 million noncash impairment at Targus. The quarter included record operating revenue and strong Auction/Liquidation and Financial Consulting results, while management did not provide quantitative forward guidance and spent substantial time addressing concerns about the FRG investment.

negative_highlights: Revenue of $320 million declined YoY, with flight revenue down 23% YoY and 9% sequentially
GAAP net loss of $144.8 million including a $56.2 million non-cash goodwill impairment
Prepaid blocks of $79 million pressured by program coverage changes and market speculation over financial position
positive_highlights: Underlying adjusted contribution margin of 9.2% (ex-one-time items) up sequentially to the highest level in over two years
Adjusted EBITDA loss ex-items narrowed to $30.4 million, the smallest in almost two years, on lower OpEx (down 10% YoY)
Closed $350 million term loan from Delta and new investors, ending with $365 million total liquidity
summary: Wheels Up reported Q3 revenue of $320 million, down year-over-year (flight revenue fell 23% YoY and 9% sequentially) as it shifted to a regional model. Adjusted EBITDA loss was $18.5 million, but that included $5.9 million of one-time software license revenue and roughly $6 million of aircraft-sale gains; excluding those, the loss was $30.4 million, described as the narrowest in almost two years. Underlying adjusted contribution margin was 9.2% (11% reported), up sequentially and the highest in over two years. GAAP net loss was $144.8 million including a $56.2 million goodwill impairment; liquidity was $365 million after the $350 million Delta/investor term loan, with $50 million of the $500 million raise still in discussion, and management reiterated confidence in reaching positive adjusted EBITDA in 2024.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined across all three segments year-over-year due to decreased streaming services, project conclusions, and reduced budgets in consumer products
Net income dropped significantly from $7.2 million last year primarily because the prior period included a one-time gain of $2.5 million from note unused IP addresses which is not recurring
Customer Care revenue fell 19.4% sequentially due to decreases in streaming services and consumer product budgets
positive_highlights: Fulfillment & Logistics Services revenue increased sequentially by 15% driven by work from largest customers
Company maintains a strong balance sheet with $13.3 million cash, no debt, and a positive operating income/EBITDA despite the miss
Appointment of new leadership (Kelly Waller for Sales & Marketing; Ron Lee for Inside Sales) to address pipeline gaps
summary: Third quarter revenues were $47.1 million, down 12.6% year-over-year and effectively flat sequentially, while net income fell to $600,000 from $7.2 million in the prior year due to a lack of other income compared to last year's IP sale. All three operating segments—Customer Care, Fulfillment & Logistics Services, and Marketing Services—experienced revenue declines ranging from 4% to 19%. Management provided no updated guidance for Q3 or FY2023 but reiterated that the second half baseline remains applicable while outlining a transformative 'Project Elevate' plan with Kearney targeting cost reductions and sales improvements starting in early 2024.

LanzaTech reported Q3 FY2023 revenue of $19.6 million, up 52% sequentially and 143% year-over-year, with gross margin expanding to 27% from 16% and gross profit up 150% QoQ to $5.2 million. The company now targets full-year 2023 revenue at the low end of its $80-100 million range, citing opportunities that slipped into next year, and expects adjusted EBITDA at the high end of the negative $65-75 million range; reaching the low end implies roughly doubling Q4 revenue versus Q3. Net loss was $25.3 million and adjusted EBITDA negative $19.1 million, while cash burn fell to $24.2 million from $33.8 million in Q2. The quarter also included an FPA accounting change requiring restatement of Q1 and Q2 2023 financials, which management said is isolated and does not affect earnings or cash flow.

negative_highlights: Zola distribution declined at the end of 2022 due to retailer challenges in the CBD category.
Cash and note weakness in-term investments declined $2.8 million quarter-over-quarter to $15.7 million.
Inventory increased $1.2 million year-over-year, with production runs paused until Q2 2024.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 2% year-over-year to $1.6 million driven by GoodWheat expansion.
Gross margins expanded 300 bps to 31%, with YTD margins up nearly 1,500 bps.
SG&A expenses reduced 18% year-over-year to $3.4 million, the lowest level since 2019.
summary: Arcadia Biosciences reported Q3 FY2023 continuing operations revenue of $1.6 million, a 2% year-over-year increase driven by GoodWheat growth despite Zola distribution losses. Gross margins expanded to 31% from 28% in the prior year, while SG&A expenses fell 18% year-over-year to $3.4 million due to headcount reductions following the exit of the body care business. Management expressed confidence in scaling GoodWheat across three categories and maintaining double-digit growth in 2024.

negative_highlights: Revenue from South Korea dropped to zero due to ongoing third-party reimbursement disputes
Macro environment and high interest rates are headwinds for large capital purchases, likely increasing reliance on leasing models in the future
Operating expenses were artificially suppressed by a one-time $1.4 million employee retention credit
positive_highlights: Revenue increased 26% YoY driven by robust system sales of ALLY
Gross margin held steady at 50%, matching low-50s guidance
Installed base reached 39 systems with a backlog of 8 pending installation
summary: Third quarter revenue was $9.8 million (up 26% YoY) and net income was $2.6 million ($0.13/share), driven by strong ALLY system sales despite a complete loss of South Korean revenue due to third-party reimbursement issues. Gross margin remained flat at 50%, matching guidance, while operating expenses decreased primarily due to an employee retention credit offsetting costs. Management expressed caution regarding the macro environment and interest rates affecting capital demand for large purchases.

negative_highlights: Revenue fell 22% compared to the prior-year period due to persistent inventory destocking and sluggish demand.
Adjusted operating income declined from $1.7 million last year to $0.6 million this quarter as growth investments weighed on results.
positive_highlights: Gross margin expanded significantly by 530 basis points (from prior year) despite a sharp decline in top-line sales.
summary: FGI reported Q3 FY2023 revenue of $29.9 million, a decrease of 22% year-over-year driven by inventory destocking and macro headwinds in the home improvement market. Gross margin improved to 26.2%, expanding 530 basis points due to product mix shifts toward higher-margin categories despite lower revenues. Management lowered its full-year 2023 guidance, revising revenue expectations to $115 million-$120 million and adjusted operating income to $2 million-$2.8 million.

negative_highlights: U.S. revenue declined following the termination of the PTAP program on June 30, reverting sales to cash-pay prices.
Cost of revenue increased to $187,000 from $101,000 in the prior year due to fixed overhead increases.
Net loss per share widened to $5.49 compared to $2.90 in the prior year period.
positive_highlights: Revenue in Canada increased 29% year-over-year to $72,000 driven by an exclusive distribution agreement with HealthTech Connex.
Operating loss improved significantly to $3.2 million from a prior year loss of $4.9 million.
Cash runway is expected to extend into the second quarter of 2024.
summary: Total revenue for Q3 FY2023 was $143,000, a decrease of $53,000 compared to the prior year quarter due to the expiration of the Patient Therapy Access Program (PTAP) in the U.S., partially offset by increased Canadian sales. Operating loss narrowed to $3.2 million from $4.9 million in the prior year period, and net loss was $3.7 million or $5.49 per share. Management highlighted progress on reimbursement pathways, including FDA breakthrough designations and a letter of intent from the Quebec Ministry of Health for 30 units.

negative_highlights: Combined portfolio NOI decreased 0.4% YoY as total expenses rose 10.1%, with non-controllable expenses up 19.1% and insurance up 67%
October new lease rents turned negative at -0.7% and blended rent growth slowed to 2.7%, with management more cautious on new lease trends heading into 2024 budgeting
Occupancy fell to 94.4% from 96.2% a year ago, and Alamo Ranch and Bells Bluff cost roughly 200 bps of NOI growth
positive_highlights: FFO rose to $0.31/share from $0.29 and AFFO to $0.41/share from $0.38 a year ago
Average monthly rents for the combined portfolio were up 6.8% YoY and revenue grew 4.1%
Repurchased 671,000 shares for $12.5 million at a weighted average of $18.58, cited as accretive on AFFO yield
summary: BRT reported Q3 FY2023 combined portfolio NOI down 0.4% YoY as revenue rose 4.1% but total expenses jumped 10.1%, with non-controllable costs up 19.1% and insurance up 67%. FFO was $0.31/share vs $0.29 a year ago and AFFO $0.41 vs $0.38, while GAAP net loss was $0.08/share against prior-year income of $0.37 that included a $0.61 gain. Average occupancy held at 94.4% (down from 96.2% a year ago), blended rents rose 3.5% in Q3 but new lease rents turned negative at -0.7% in October. Guidance for 2023 was affirmed, not raised; the company purchased 671,000 shares for $12.5 million at $18.58 average and cited a very quiet transaction market.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined 13% year-over-year, partly due to currency effects.
Q4 2023 expected to be negatively impacted by the Israel-Hamas war.
Slow-moving inventory discounts reduced average note price to $4.35 per gram.
positive_highlights: Gross margin improved to 22% from 20% year-over-year.
Adjusted EBITDA loss decreased 65% to $1.3 million.
Operating expenses reduced by 34% year-over-year.
summary: In Q3 2023, IM Cannabis reported revenues of $12.4 million, down 13% from $14.2 million in Q3 2022, with 6.4% of the decline attributed to unfavorable currency effects. Gross margin before fair value adjustments improved to 22% from 20%, and adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed by 65% to $1.3 million. Operating expenses fell 34% year-over-year, but the company faced headwinds from slow-moving inventory discounts, a delivery transition, and the onset of the Israel-Hamas war, which is expected to negatively impact Q4. Management remains focused on sustainable profitability and anticipates regulatory changes in Germany and Israel, but notes delays due to the war.

negative_highlights: Data are preliminary and from small cohorts (8 AML patients, 17 STS patients)
STS PFS of 3.4 months is modest compared to other agents
Pivotal trial costs estimated at $18M (AML) with no guarantee of external funding
positive_highlights: AML: 38% complete response rate in heavily pre-treated patients
STS: 78% response rate at optimal dose in pre-treated patients
Cash runway into Q3 2024 with no debt
summary: Moleculin reported preliminary Phase 2 data for Annamycin in AML and STS, showing a 38% complete response rate in heavily pre-treated AML patients and a 78% response rate with 56% 3-month PFS in STS at the optimal dose. The company ended Q3 with about $25 million cash, no debt, and expects runway into Q3 2024. Management is planning end-of-Phase 2 meetings with FDA/EMA and expects to start pivotal trials in 2024, with potential external funding for the STS pivotal trial.

negative_highlights: No Q3 FY2023 financial results (revenue, EPS, margins, cash flow) were presented on the call.
Management stated Inpixon is not being adequately valued in the market and cited market-cap challenges, motivating the strategic transactions.
Both transactions remain subject to closing conditions including SEC clearance, stockholder approval, and Nasdaq listing approval.
positive_highlights: XTI transaction S-4 declared effective, with shareholder meeting scheduled for December 8, 2023 and closing targeted for the current quarter.
Damon Motors reported over $85 million in credit-card-backed consumer reservations for the HyperSport and over $70 million raised to date.
XTI cited over 700 conditional pre-orders and expressions of interest representing more than $7 billion in potential gross revenue at a $10 million list price.
summary: This call was a business-update presentation on two strategic transactions (the XTI Aircraft merger and the Grafiti/Damon Motors spin-off) rather than a review of Q3 financial results; no revenue, EPS, margin, or cash flow figures were discussed. Management stated it does not believe Inpixon is adequately valued in the market and is pursuing the deals to address that. The XTI S-4 was declared effective, with a shareholder meeting set for December 8, 2023, and the XTI merger targeted to close in the current quarter; the Grafiti spin-off registration was confidentially filed, with the Damon combination expected to close in Q1 2024. Damon's CEO cited over $85 million in consumer reservations and over $70 million raised to date.

negative_highlights: The company swung to a net loss of $748,000 from net income of $595,000 a year earlier, driven by operating expenses rising to $3.8 million from $1.6 million.
Cash used in operating activities was $225,000 versus $1.97 million of cash provided a year earlier.
Safe Harbor program licensing income fell 81% to $7,000, and no detailed forward guidance was provided beyond full-year revenue.
positive_highlights: Revenue rose 79% year-over-year to $4.3 million from $2.4 million.
Investment income increased 111% to $1.19 million, and loan interest income grew 119% to $906,000.
Average active accounts rose 49.6% to 986, with deposit balances up 36.5% to $216.9 million.
summary: Safe Harbor reported Q3 2023 revenue of $4.3 million, up 79% year-over-year, with deposit/onboarding income up 65% to $2.2 million and investment income up 111% to $1.19 million; however, a net loss of $748,000 replaced prior-year net income of $595,000. Adjusted EBITDA was roughly flat at $1.05 million versus $1.02 million, and operating expenses rose to $3.8 million from $1.6 million. The company set full-year 2023 revenue guidance of $16 million to $16.5 million and said it intends to provide more detailed guidance in the coming year.

negative_highlights: Net loss per diluted share was $14.55, up from $223.83 a year ago but still representing significant losses
G&A expenses increased 25.3% YoY to $3.7 million due to noncash items like depreciation and amortization of loan discounts
Management confirmed the Board is reviewing strategic alternatives, indicating potential delisting or sale
positive_highlights: Net revenues increased 22.5% YoY to $3.3 million
Gross margin expanded significantly from 36% a year ago to 52.3%
Sundry wholesale bookings tripled in Q1 FY2024 compared to the prior quarter
summary: Net revenues increased 22.5% to $3.3 million and gross margins expanded significantly to 52.3%, driven by Sundry's turnaround following design changes in September. However, the company reported a net loss of $14.55 per diluted share due to high G&A expenses including noncash items, resulting in an overall operating miss relative to typical profitability expectations for this revenue level. Management explicitly stated they are actively pursuing strategic alternatives and reviewing options given the dislocation between public market value and intrinsic asset value.

negative_highlights: Total page views declined 8% YoY, with pronounced weakness at The Spun and HubPages
Digital subscription revenue fell 31% YoY to $3.2M and print revenue declined 9% YoY to $17.6M
Net cash used in operating activities was $5.9M; credit line borrowings rose to $17.3M from $14.9M at June 30
positive_highlights: Total revenue grew 11% YoY to $63.4M with digital ad revenue up 29% and total RPMs up 46%
Adjusted EBITDA rose 86% YoY to $6.4M and gross margin expanded ~140 bps to 44%
E-commerce revenue grew 637% YoY and Creator Network generated 7-figure revenue since August launch
summary: Arena Group reported Q3 FY2023 revenue of $63.4M, up 11% YoY, with digital advertising up ~29% (digital revenue $45.8M, 72% of total) and gross profit $28.2M at a 44% margin. Adjusted EBITDA was $6.4M, up 86% YoY, and net loss improved to $11.2M from $16.5M. Total page views fell 8% YoY, digital subscription revenue declined 31% to $3.2M, and print revenue dropped 9% to $17.6M. Management gave no formal guidance, citing the pending Bridge Media Networks/SIMPLIFY transaction and active proxy period; the deal is expected to close in Q4 2023 or Q1 2024, subject to shareholder approval.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to $22.8 million ($0.51 per share) from $21.2 million ($0.69 per share) in Q3 2022, with shares outstanding rising to 44.6 million from 30.6 million.
Cash position of $59.7 million is expected to fund operations only into September 2024, with no financial guidance and reliance on partnering or financing.
R&D expenses increased 20% YoY to $19.8 million, driven by external development costs for ongoing clinical trials.
positive_highlights: Interim Phase 2 CALLIPER data showed a 22.4% improvement in serum NfL for vidofludimus calcium over placebo at week 24 (p=0.01), with consistent effects across progressive MS subtypes.
Received a USPTO notice of allowance for a patent covering vidofludimus calcium in relapsing MS, expected to provide protection into 2041.
Completed enrollment of the Phase 2 CALLIPER trial with 467 progressive MS patients across more than 70 sites.
summary: Immunic reported Q3 FY2023 R&D expenses of $19.8 million, up from $16.5 million YoY, and a net loss of $22.8 million, or $0.51 per share, versus a $21.2 million loss in the prior-year period. The company ended the quarter with $59.7 million in cash, funding operations into September 2024. Management highlighted positive interim Phase 2 CALLIPER data (22.4% NfL improvement over placebo, p=0.01) and a new U.S. patent allowance extending protection to 2041. No formal financial guidance was provided; the company is pursuing partnering and non-dilutive financing options.

negative_highlights: Net loss increased slightly to $4.7 million from $5.4 million in the prior year
R&D expenses rose to $2.5 million from $3.6 million in Q3 FY2022
G&A expenses increased to $2.7 million from $2.1 million in Q3 FY2022
positive_highlights: Cash runway projected to be sufficient through Q3 FY2024
Narazaciclib showing potential for continuous dosing without the standard one-week off period required by other CDK4/6 inhibitors
Initial safety data suggests narazaciclib may avoid difficult adverse events like diarrhea
summary: Onconova reported a net loss of $4.7 million ($0.23 per share) for Q3 FY2023, compared to a $5.4 million loss in the prior year period, driven by higher G&A costs and timing of manufacturing expenses. The company's cash position decreased to $25.2 million as of September 30, 2023, but management projects this runway is sufficient through Q3 FY2024. Clinical progress for lead programs narazaciclib and rigosertib was highlighted, with the Phase 1/2 trial for narazaciclib extending into Q1 FY2024 to define an optimal dose.

negative_highlights: Net loss of $1.8 million in the quarter, with adjusted EBITDA of only $60,000
Cash on hand is just approximately $1.2 million
DMint spinoff timing is unresolved pending multiple rounds of SEC comments, and no 2024 EBITDA guidance was provided
positive_highlights: Q3 revenue rose 55% year over year to $9.69 million, with payment processing up 39% to $8.3 million
Company reports no debt and a run rate of roughly $31 million excluding bitcoin mining
Electricity cost locked at about $0.0489 per megawatt hour for 5 years at the Selmer, Tennessee DMint facility
summary: Q3 2023 revenue was $9.69 million, up 55% from $6.22 million a year earlier, with payment processing up 39% to $8.3 million; year-to-date revenue was $24.7 million versus $23.4 million, a 5.4% increase. The company reported a net loss of $1.8 million, attributed mainly to depreciation and amortization, with adjusted EBITDA of just $60,000 and cash on hand of about $1.2 million. Management gave no 2024 EBITDA guidance because the timing of the DMint spinoff, filed via S-1 and still in SEC comment rounds, remains uncertain; the 1,000 miners in Selmer are not yet fully powered.

negative_highlights: Operating loss widened to $9.1 million from $8.7 million due to accelerated commercialization costs.
Cash burn remained at $7 million, consistent with the prior seven-quarter run rate.
No revenue guidance provided for the Evie Ring launch quarter.
positive_highlights: Evie Ring launch imminent with orders opening November 20; management expects shipping before year-end.
FDA submission for pulse oximetry is progressing with no showstoppers despite additional cybersecurity requirements.
Cuffless blood pressure trial results demonstrated accuracy of 5.9 mmHg, meeting or exceeding FDA standards.
summary: Movano Health reported an operating loss of $9.1 million in Q3 FY2023, compared to a loss of $8.7 million in the prior year period, with cash burn of $7 million. The company raised approximately $200,000 on its ATM facility and announced a new $3.6 million underwritten public offering priced at $0.85 per share. Management expressed confidence in the upcoming launch of the Evie Ring, citing over 120,000 engaged leads and significant interest ahead of the November 20 order date.

negative_highlights: No revenue, EPS, or margin figures reported; the company remains pre-commercial
AMP-270 first patient enrollment remains pending despite prior focus on site activation; 30 sites in activation but no patients enrolled
Manufacturing costs increased due to inflation, with no offsetting revenue
positive_highlights: Cash and marketable investments of approximately $22.4 million as of September 30, with management stating ability to fund through key milestones
DURIPANC combination trial on track for Q4 patient recruitment after receiving EU QP release and import approval
summary: AIM ImmunoTech reported no revenue or EPS figures, only a cash and marketable investments position of approximately $22.4 million as of September 30. Clinical milestones were discussed: AMP-270 first patient enrollment is 'imminent' with 30 sites in activation and 18 in preselection visits; the DURIPANC study with durvalumab is on track to open in Q4; and the long COVID Phase 2 trial is fully enrolled with top-line data expected in early Q1. Management expressed confidence in funding through key milestones and highlighted new manufacturing of Ampligen (approximately 9,000-10,000 vials) and the addition of Azenova for business development.

negative_highlights: Total revenue declined year-over-year from $15.6 million to $13.5 million
Net loss widened significantly to approximately $2.1 million compared to a net loss of $3.7 million in the prior period
Cash balance decreased substantially to approximately $2.6 million as of September 30, 2023 from $7 million a year ago
positive_highlights: Gross profit surged from $37,000 to approximately $163,000 YoY driven by higher-margin TAZTE channel focus
TAZTE platform achieved a notable 1.5x increase in gross merchandise value (GMV) and 2x growth in total transactions during the quarter
Paid user base grew by 4.7% with over 2,66 million registered users on ZCITY as of November 6
summary: Treasure Global reported Q1 FY2024 revenue of $13.5 million, a year-over-year decline from $15.6 million in the prior period as management shifted focus to higher-margin channels like TAZTE. Gross profit improved significantly to approximately $163,000 compared to $37,000 last year due to this strategic pivot and margin expansion initiatives. The company reported a net loss of approximately $2.1 million versus $3.7 million in the prior year quarter.

negative_highlights: Proact 1 Phase III trial enrollment delayed to H1 2024 due to eGFR range change from 20-50 to 20-35 mL/min, with only approximately 50 of over 80 enrolled patients meeting new criteria
Manufacturing paused following EU qualified person audit that identified deficiencies in quality management system documentation, with resumption not expected until H1 2024
Management could not be confident on durability of REACT effect, noting possible need for redosing at 18-24 months and that Phase II lacked a control group beyond 18 months
positive_highlights: Phase II RMCL-002 data showed 37% of 73 injected patients had no or minimal eGFR decline over 30 months, with 56% of those being stage 4 CKD patients
In stage 4 CKD patients with severe albuminuria, eGFR declined only 0.2 mL after REACT injection over 18 months versus a 6.0 mL decline in the prior 12 months on standard of care
Company stated it is well capitalized into 2025 and plans to report 007 interim data in mid-2024 and final 002 data in H1 2024
summary: ProKidney's Q3 FY2023 call was a clinical and corporate update rather than a traditional financial results discussion, with no specific revenue, EPS, or margin figures stated for the quarter. Management highlighted updated Phase II RMCL-002 data showing eGFR stabilization in high-risk diabetic CKD patients, with 37% of 73 injected patients having no or minimal eGFR decline and stage 4 patients showing a -1.6 mL/min change versus -6.0 mL/min for standard of care over 12 months. The company announced a modification to the proact 1 Phase III trial eGFR range from 20-50 to 20-35 mL/min, delaying enrollment resumption to H1 2024, and a manufacturing pause due to EU qualified person audit findings on quality management system documentation, also expected to resolve in H1 2024. ProKidney reported being well capitalized into 2025 with no financing details provided.

negative_highlights: GAAP operating loss of $378 million driven by noncash impairments and credit loss charges.
Net book value declined from $2.7 billion as of March 31, 2023 to $1.2 billion as of September 30, 2023.
Ben Custody fee revenue fell to $6.5 million from $7.8 million year-over-year.
positive_highlights: Ben Liquidity interest income rose to $13.0 million from $10.9 million in the prior-year quarter.
Closed a $25 million three-year term loan to meet obligations and provide working capital.
Since inception, financed 376 distinct funds and private interests with $1.2 billion of collateral NAV.
summary: Beneficient reported Q2 FY2024 with Ben Liquidity interest income of $13.0 million (up from $10.9 million YoY) and Ben Custody fee revenue of $6.5 million (down from $7.8 million YoY). The quarter included noncash goodwill impairments of $306 million and a $61 million credit loss charge, driving a GAAP operating loss of $378 million and a $1.45 fully diluted loss per share; adjusted operating loss was $12 million. Net book value fell to $1.2 billion from $2.7 billion at March 31, 2023. Management closed a $25 million three-year term loan and disclosed the first financing collateral NAV of $1.2 billion, while noting macro uncertainty but not providing formal forward guidance.

negative_highlights: Revenue growth was flat at +0.2%, masking a significant negative foreign exchange impact of approximately -8% from the weakening yen.
Operating expenses rose sharply by 26.5% YoY to $3.4 million, primarily due to increased shipping fees and R&D investments in new product lines.
The heavy machinery business (Heavy Corp) remains a revenue driver for future quarters rather than current earnings.
positive_highlights: Gross margins expanded significantly from 22.1% in Q3 FY2022 to approximately 30.7% (calculated as $6.3M gross profit / $21.8M revenue) due to higher-value product mix and operational efficiency.
Operating income increased by 35% year-over-year, driven by the strategic focus on high-margin drivetrain products.
Cash position strengthened with cash equivalents rising 32% YoY to $21.5 million.
summary: GTEC reported Q3 FY2023 revenue of $21.8 million (up 0.2% YoY) and GAAP EPS implied by the beat on operating income ($2.8M vs prior year), though gross margin expansion was offset by a significant negative currency impact (-8%) which masked underlying organic growth (~4.6%). Management raised full-year revenue guidance to over $90 million despite FX headwinds, citing strong demand for transmissions and drivetrains.

negative_highlights: TCE revenues declined $2.7 million year-over-year to $9.3 million in Q3 2023
Net income fell to $3.1 million ($0.29 basic EPS) from $5.1 million ($0.48 basic EPS) in Q3 2022
Adjusted EBITDA decreased $5.1 million year-over-year to $5.5 million
positive_highlights: Q4 2023 MR bookings at 84% of available days at an average estimated TCE of $29,600 per day, a 6% sequential increase over Q3's $28,000 per day
Sale of Pyxis Epsilon for almost $41 million, a 10-year high, expected to net approximately $26.4 million in cash and realize a $17.1 million gain in Q4
Adjusted EBITDA of $5.5 million with a low consolidated leverage ratio of 27% and total cash of $34.1 million as of September 30, 2023
summary: Pyxis Tankers reported Q3 2023 time charter equivalent revenues of $9.3 million, down $2.7 million year-over-year, with net income of $3.1 million ($0.29 basic EPS) versus $5.1 million in Q3 2022, and adjusted EBITDA of $5.5 million. The decline was due to lower spot chartering activity and fewer operating vessels, though results improved sequentially from Q2 2023. Management announced the sale of the Pyxis Epsilon for approximately $41 million, expecting a $17.1 million gain in Q4, and a $6.8 million investment in a dry bulk joint venture. Forward guidance points to a constructive product tanker outlook with Q4 MR bookings at 84% at an average TCE of $29,600 per day, a 6% sequential increase.

negative_highlights: Q4 revenue fell 7% YoY to $18.9M and full-year revenue fell 8% to $79.2M due to declining MAVYRET sales.
Net loss widened in Q4 and full year; full-year loss per share increased to $6.38 from $5.91.
Paused hMPV/RSV dual-inhibitor program and stopped RSVTx study, reducing pipeline breadth.
positive_highlights: Initiated Phase 2a challenge study for EDP-323, an L-protein inhibitor for RSV, with data expected in Q3 2024.
FY2024 R&D guidance set at $100-120M, down from $163.5M in FY2023, extending cash runway through fiscal 2027.
Cash position of ~$370M at quarter end, including $200M from royalty sale, supports runway through fiscal 2027.
summary: Enanta reported Q4 FY2023 revenue of $18.9M, down from $20.3M YoY, with FY2023 revenue of $79.2M versus $86.2M in FY2022, reflecting declining AbbVie MAVYRET sales. Net loss for Q4 was $28.1M ($1.33/share) versus $26.3M ($1.27/share) in the prior year; full-year loss widened to $133.8M ($6.38/share) from $121.8M ($5.91/share). Management cut FY2024 R&D guidance to $100-120M (from $163.5M in FY2023) to extend cash runway through fiscal 2027, and reiterated expected data readouts for EDP-938 and EDP-323 in Q3 2024. The company paused its dual-inhibitor program and stopped RSVTx to conserve cash, while announcing future non-virology programs but providing no specifics.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined by 74% to $5.9 million, with bromine revenue falling 75% to $4.9 million.
Net income swung from a profit of $9.0 million in the prior year to a loss of $1.8 million.
Gross margin contracted significantly to 7% for the nine-month period compared to 57% previously.
positive_highlights: Bromine market price increased approximately 7.4% since quarter-end to $3,477 per tonne based on sensors.com data.
Management expects a return to profitability in the fourth quarter as bromine prices recover.
Flood prevention initiative aims to mitigate future risks and enhance probability of reopening factories.
summary: Gulf Resources reported a significant miss in Q3 FY2023 with revenue declining 74% to $5.9 million and net income turning into a loss of $1.8 million compared to a prior profit of $9.0 million, driven by a 75% drop in bromine revenues due to lower volumes and prices. Management disclosed a substantial one-time expense of approximately $15.15 million incurred in Q3 for flood prevention initiatives, with an additional $35 million projected for completion in Q4. While management expressed optimism about long-term demand and noted a recent uptick in bromine prices, they maintained production restrictions to await price recovery.

negative_highlights: Management expects the anticipated commission cap implementation in Q4 to bring note weakness in-term challenges across the industry.
The 382% YoY net income increase was largely due to a one-off unrealized gain from the Cheche investment, which management noted is non-recurring and could cause future volatility.
Sales slowed in August and September after the August pricing-rate change as insurance partners adjusted product offerings, with customer demand restoration expected to take time.
positive_highlights: Total life insurance premium grew 23% YoY to RMB3.4 billion and first-year premium rose 10.3% to RMB584 million.
Adjusted operating expense ratio improved to 30% from 32% YoY despite higher IT investment.
MDRT agent count increased 29% YoY and monthly productivity of MDRT agents rose 27% to RMB600,000.
summary: Fanhua reported Q3 FY2023 total life insurance premium up 23% YoY to RMB3.4 billion and first-year premium up 10.3% to RMB584 million, with net income attributable to shareholders of RMB117.7 million, up 382% YoY largely due to a one-off unrealized gain on its Cheche Technology stake. The adjusted operating expense ratio improved to 30% from 32%, and MDRT agent count rose 29%. Management guided to short-term pressure in Q4 from expected commission rate caps and slower demand after the August pricing-rate change, while positioning these regulatory shifts as a catalyst for its open platform strategy. No explicit quantitative guidance was provided.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined to $15.9 million from $17.1 million year over year
Operating expenses rose to $3.6 million from $3.3 million, including a $0.2 million one-time marketing promotion
Management noted a very tough retail environment with consumers concentrating on essentials and karaoke demand arriving later than usual
positive_highlights: Gross margin expanded 40 bps to 23.2% from 22.8%, helped by product mix and lower inbound ocean container prices
Target shelf presence increased to 4 SKUs from 2 last year, and Costco Canada sold 13,000 pieces versus an 8,700-piece forecast
The 3PL transition eliminated a large percentage of the workforce and avoided significant rent increases, with hundreds of thousands in annual cost mitigation expected
summary: Q2 FY2024 revenue fell to $15.9 million from $17.1 million a year earlier, which management attributed to late-September shipping delays that shifted into October plus roughly $900,000 in added co-op incentive accruals for holiday promotions. Gross margin edged up to 23.2% from 22.8% on product mix and lower ocean container costs, while operating expenses rose to $3.6 million from $3.3 million. Cash stood at approximately $3.2 million, with working capital to be funded by vendor financing, cash on hand and operating cash flow. Management gave no explicit forward revenue or EPS guidance, and the quarter's key change was the completed shift from a 100% in-house logistics model to a fully outsourced 3PL during peak shipping season.

negative_highlights: Gross margin compressed to 38.9% from 52.4% last year, driven by NETi gross margin down to 10% from 17% and brand ad investments.
Cash balance was only $417k as of 9/30, with a $2 million note payment and ongoing working capital needs.
Management acknowledged near-term EBITDA margins may miss the top of the prior range as they invest in growth.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 140% YoY and 53.5% sequentially, ahead of prior guidance.
G&A as a percentage of revenue dropped to 8.2% from 19% YoY; operating expenses fell to 29% of revenue from 56.5%.
Tytan Tiles Disney Frozen launch achieved 115 units/day run rate, ranking rose from 20,000 to 4,000 on Amazon.
summary: Upexi reported fiscal Q1 2024 revenue growth of ~140-144% YoY and 53.5% sequentially, reaching $26.4 million, but gross margin declined to 38.9% (from 52.4% last year) due to NETi lower margins and brand investments. Management reaffirmed calendar 2023 revenue guidance of $100 million but tempered near-term EBITDA margin expectations, citing investment in brand launches and a challenge to reach the top of the prior margin range. The company paid $2 million on acquisition notes and restructured remaining debt over 12 months, with cash at only $417k. Brand investments in Disney Frozen Tytan Tiles and VitaMedica are highlighted as long-term growth drivers.

negative_highlights: Q3 revenue was only $43,000, down $66,000 from $109,000 in Q3 2022.
Q3 GAAP net loss was $4.4 million (-$0.38 per share), roughly flat versus the $4.4 million loss a year earlier.
Operating expenses rose to $4.4 million from $4.3 million, and the collaboration with Tel Aviv University and Sheba Medical Center for Gut-on-a-Chip was terminated after one year.
positive_highlights: Nine-month revenue rose to $10.7 million from $241,000, driven by the $10 million AbbVie milestone payment booked in Q3.
Cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash were $29 million with a stated runway of at least two years, excluding potential future milestone payments.
Q3 operating cash flow was positive $6.8 million versus a $3.2 million use a year earlier, reflecting the AbbVie receipt.
summary: Q3 2023 GAAP revenue fell to $43,000 from $109,000 a year earlier, while the nine-month figure jumped to $10.7 million from $241,000 thanks to a $10 million AbbVie milestone payment. GAAP net loss was $4.4 million (-$0.38 per share) versus a $4.4 million loss (-$0.40) in Q3 2022; cash stood at $29 million, described as a runway of at least two years excluding any future milestones. Management noted the Israel war began in October, about 10% of staff were drafted, and that production and development were minimally affected, with budget adjustments and a planned December 2023 large-animal breast implant study.

negative_highlights: Q3 revenue of just EUR2.5 million, with the full quarter tied to a single project, the Madrid plant

Reversed EUR0.5 million of previously recognized revenue after a customer's POSEUR grant project was abandoned, and added EUR0.5 million to the legacy HEVO-Solar inventory impairment (total provision now EUR7.7 million against that inventory)
Bank balance of only EUR1 million at September 30, with cash flow breakeven not expected until sometime in 2025
positive_highlights: Entered an agreement with Macquarie for a financing facility of up to $20 million to fund 2024 objectives
Set a 2024 revenue target of EUR34 million, with five projects already signed and confirmed and Sines 1 in negotiation
Operating cost base declined for a third consecutive quarter, with personnel costs down EUR0.26 million QoQ and a target of roughly 20% reduction to FY2023 SG&A
summary: Fusion Fuel reported Q3 2023 revenue of EUR2.5 million tied to the Madrid green hydrogen project and a pre-tax loss of EUR4 million, with a EUR1 million bank balance at September 30. The company reversed EUR0.5 million of prior revenue after a Portuguese POSEUR-funded customer project failed to meet its grant deadline, and added EUR0.5 million to the EUR7.2 million HEVO-Solar inventory impairment. Management kept FY2023 guidance unchanged and set a 2024 revenue target of EUR34 million, backed by five confirmed projects plus the pending Sines 1 sale, and secured a Macquarie convertible facility of up to $20 million (ATM cancelled as a condition), while targeting cash flow breakeven in 2025 and roughly a 20% cut to FY2023 SG&A.

negative_highlights: No commercial revenue or earnings reported as production has not yet started.
Management noted that some potential customers are taking a wait-and-see approach based on the evolving geopolitical climate regarding domestic versus imported graphite sourcing.
positive_highlights: PEA for Coosa Deposit indicates estimated pretax NPV of $229 million and IRR of 26.7%.
summary: Westwater Resources provided no financial results for Q3 FY2023 as the company has not yet commenced commercial production or reported revenue/earnings in this period. Management presented a Preliminary Economic Assessment (PEA) for the Coosa Deposit indicating an estimated pretax NPV of $229 million and IRR of 26.7%, while noting that negotiations on off-take agreements with Kellyton continue to be active but no specific deal was finalized in this quarter.

negative_highlights: Revenue of $53.6 million declined 32% year-over-year and 13% sequentially and fell below the expectations from October 5
Gross margin contracted to 33% from 36% sequentially on unfavorable mix, lower volumes, higher E&O accruals, and warranty expenses
Recognized a $74 million goodwill impairment due to significant TSP revenue declines
positive_highlights: Industrial segment had an extraordinarily strong quarter, particularly with a large OEM customer
Closed a $45 million term loan with Lynrock Lake, providing additional liquidity and no financial covenants
Early signs of TSP recovery: order volumes up, improved internal forecast, and more favorable customer commentary
summary: CalAmp reported Q3 FY24 revenue of $53.6 million, down 32% year-over-year and 13% sequentially, and adjusted EBITDA of $1 million, both below the expectations set on October 5. Gross margin fell to 33% from 36% in the prior quarter on unfavorable mix, lower volumes, and higher E&O and warranty costs, and the company recognized a $74 million goodwill impairment tied to TSP segment weakness. Management guided Q4 consolidated revenue down slightly with stable adjusted EBITDA, citing early stabilization in TSP orders, a return to normal industrial levels, and a new $16 million annualized cost reduction program targeting adjusted EBITDA breakeven at roughly $42 million in quarterly revenue.

negative_highlights: Loan growth was flat as $36M of originations were offset by a $36M loan sale; pipeline of $210M was essentially unchanged from $212M at September 30
Reported net income was $8.4M ($0.33/share), hit by a $3.8M loss on the commercial loan sale and $0.9M on securities sales, versus $12.4M ($0.49/share) adjusted
GAAP-to-adjusted gap also reflects nonrecurring tax adjustments that will revert to a 23-25% effective rate in 2024, and no explicit 2024 revenue or earnings guidance was provided
positive_highlights: Net interest margin expanded 32 bps QoQ to 3.68%, with ~17 bps of core improvement as earning-asset yields rose ~30 bps versus a 15 bp rise in funding costs
Return on tangible common equity reached 15.75%, the highest since Q1 2021, and adjusted ROA was 1.38%
New loan originations carried an 8.35% weighted average rate versus 4.89% on loans sold, and cost of deposits rose only 16 bps versus 28 bps in Q3
summary: First Bank reported Q4 net income of $8.4M ($0.33/diluted share), or $12.4M ($0.49/share) adjusted, which excludes merger costs and $0.9M of investment-sale losses plus $3.8M of loan-sale losses. NIM rose 32 bps QoQ to 3.68%, though ~15 bps of that came from $3.9M of acquisition accounting accretion, leaving ~17 bps of core improvement. Loans were roughly flat as $36M of originations were offset by a $36M non-strategic commercial loan sale; deposits were flat and return on tangible common equity hit 15.75%. Management said it met Malvern cost-save targets, expects deposit pricing pressure to subside in 2024, and guided the effective tax rate back to 23-25% — but gave no explicit numeric EPS or revenue guidance.

negative_highlights: Data usage per user declined in Q4 due to rising inflation, preelection political instability, and the discontinuation of lower validity packs.
OpEx grew 19.2% year-over-year primarily due to energy price increases, though like-for-like growth was only 9%.
Dividend payout ratio dropped to 51% as management adopted a prudent approach given macroeconomic uncertainty.
positive_highlights: Data revenue grew 20% year-over-year to contribute approximately 31% of subscription and traffic revenue.
EBITDA margin held steady at 61.3% despite energy price hikes and inflation pressures.
Total subscriber base reached 82 million, a 3.6% increase driven by strong data user growth.
summary: Grameenphone reported Q4 FY2023 revenue growth of 6.9% year-over-year and EBITDA margin expansion to 61.3%, driven by a 20% increase in data revenue despite macroeconomic headwinds like inflation over 9%. The company delivered solid earnings per share of BDT 4.35 (up 58.2% YoY) and proposed a final dividend of BDT 12.50 per share, representing 51% of the year's profit. Management noted that while Q4 data usage was impacted by lower validity packs and political instability, underlying momentum remains strong for 2024.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined 24% YoY to $18M, reflecting lower MAVYRET royalties.
Net loss widened to $33.4M from $29M in the prior-year quarter.
Management provided no specific efficacy thresholds for moving RSVPEDs or RSVHR to Phase 3, citing only directional trends in virology as the go/no-go.
positive_highlights: Cash position of approximately $337M is expected to fund operations through fiscal 2027.
RSV portfolio advancing with two Phase 2 studies (RSVPEDs and RSVHR) enrolling across over 15 countries and over 100 sites.
Preclinical data for CSU KIT inhibitor showed potent, selective activity with favorable ADME properties, positioning for a development candidate announcement this year.
summary: Q1 FY2024 revenue was $18M, down from $23.6M in the prior-year period, with a net loss of $33.4M ($1.58 per share) versus a $29M loss ($1.39 per share) a year earlier. The company reiterated RSV study timelines, expecting top-line results from the EDP-323 challenge study and the RSVPEDs Phase 2 study in Q3 2024, while noting guidance on RSVHR would come later. Management highlighted progress in the new CSU immunology program and planned to announce a development candidate this year, alongside a second immunology program. Financial guidance for FY2024 OpEx was reaffirmed.

negative_highlights: NAV declined to $13.01 per share from $14.03, primarily due to $1.36 per share of net unrealized depreciation on investments.
Three portfolio companies remained on nonaccrual status, unchanged from the prior quarter.
Net expenses, excluding the prior quarter's large incentive fee, still included higher borrowing costs.
positive_highlights: Total investment income rose to $23.1 million from $20.3 million in the prior quarter, driven by new debt investments and higher dividend and success fee income.
Adjusted NII per share increased $0.02 to $0.26, with net investment income swinging to $9.7 million from a $1.7 million loss.
Credit facility expanded to $200 million with over $120 million available, and ATM program raised $28.7 million at accretive prices.
summary: Gladstone Investment reported Q3 FY2024 total investment income of $23.1 million, up from $20.3 million in the prior quarter, and net investment income of $9.7 million versus a $1.7 million loss last quarter. Adjusted NII was $0.26 per share, up $0.02 from $0.24, while NAV fell to $13.01 per share from $14.03 due to $1.36 per share of unrealized depreciation and $1.24 per share of distributions. The company paid a $1.00 per share supplemental distribution alongside its $0.08 monthly distribution, expanded its credit facility to $200 million, and expects deal flow to pick up modestly.

negative_highlights: Q4 2023 adjusted earnings excluding notable items were $189 million, below the average quarterly run rate due to lower alternative investment income ($0.95 per share below expectations) and seasonally higher expenses.
New statutory requirement created a negative unassigned funds balance of approximately $1.1 billion at BLIC, requiring regulatory approval for any 2024 dividends from that entity.
Full-year 2023 statutory earnings were approximately $200 million loss, a significant decline from $1 billion in 2022, reflecting volatility and the accounting change.
positive_highlights: Full year 2023 total annuity sales were $10.6 billion, exceeding the 2023 target; Shield annuity sales hit a record $6.9 billion, up 17% YoY.
Estimated combined RBC ratio was approximately 420% at year-end, up 10 points sequentially, with $1.3 billion liquid assets at the holding company.
Corporate expenses were only up 2% to $885 million in 2023, below core inflation of approximately 4%; management expects them to decline in 2024.
summary: Brighthouse Financial reported Q4 2023 adjusted earnings of $177 million, with a $12 million unfavorable notable item, and $189 million excluding that item, below its average quarterly run rate due to lower alternative investment income and seasonally higher expenses. Full-year 2023 total annuity sales were $10.6 billion and life insurance sales were $102 million, both exceeding targets, with Shield annuity sales up 17% to $6.9 billion. The estimated RBC ratio was approximately 420% at year-end, and the company repurchased $250 million of stock in 2023. The new statutory requirement to reflect all anticipated future hedging had an insignificant impact on the RBC ratio but resulted in a negative unassigned funds balance at BLIC, potentially requiring regulatory approval for 2024 dividends; management expects corporate expenses to be down in 2024.

negative_highlights: Recorded $883 million non-cash goodwill impairment, bringing total write-downs to over $2 billion since the 2019 transaction
Ben Liquidity base interest revenue fell 13.4% sequentially and Ben Custody fee revenue fell 9.1% sequentially, with custodied NAV down 13.0%
Management stated further goodwill impairment is anticipated at March 31, 2024 if the stock price does not improve
positive_highlights: Adjusted operating income turned positive in Ben Liquidity at $2.5 million versus a $4.7 million loss last quarter
Cash and cash equivalents rose to $11.2 million from $2.4 million in the prior quarter
PLP program grew to 19 participating funds with $1.5 billion in committed capital as of December 31, 2023, up from seven funds and $300 million a year earlier
summary: Beneficient reported Q3 FY2024 with Ben Liquidity base interest revenue of $11.3 million, down 13.4% sequentially, and Ben Custody fee revenue of $5.9 million, down 9.1% sequentially, with custodied NAV declining 13.0% to $432.5 million. Total segment operating loss was $894.6 million, driven primarily by an $883 million non-cash goodwill impairment, with GAAP loss per share of $1.98. Adjusted operating income was positive at $2.5 million for Liquidity and $4.8 million for Custody, and cash rose to $11.2 million while total debt fell to $128.2 million. Management highlighted scaling initiatives through the PLP program, which grew to 19 funds and $1.5 billion in committed capital, and noted that additional goodwill impairment is possible if the stock price does not improve.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined 18.4% YoY to $21.8 million, driven by re-commerce slowdown
Adjusted EBITDA fell sharply to $29,000 from $750,000 prior quarter
Net loss widened to $2.4 million from net income of $2.7 million a year earlier
positive_highlights: Gross margin expanded 620 bps sequentially to 38%
Brand product sales increased 16.7% sequentially to $7.7 million, 35.1% of total revenue
Expected $450k-$550k quarterly G&A savings from facility consolidation by end of April
summary: Upexi's fiscal Q2 2024 revenue fell 18.4% YoY to $21.8 million and gross margin expanded to 38% from 31.8% sequentially. Brand product sales rose 16.7% sequentially to $7.7 million, but adjusted EBITDA dropped to $29,000 from $750,000 in the prior quarter, and net loss deepened to $2.4 million. Management is prioritizing higher-margin brands, expects the manufacturing consolidation to yield $2 million annual G&A savings, and anticipates continued sequential margin expansion.

negative_highlights: Total revenue decreased slightly for both Q4 and full year 2023; operating income fell 4% (Q4) and 14% (FY) YoY.
TRCV declined, primarily due to focus on core digital solutions and lower net sales, though the trend improved late in 2023.
2024 guidance calls for relatively flat revenue and earnings; higher tech, sales, and executive expenses will weigh on margins until revenue conversion later in the year.
positive_highlights: Recurring new sales up 18% YoY in Q4 2023; full-year recurring new sales grew 24% ($3 million) over 2022.
Sequential operating margin expansion for three consecutive quarters; Q4 operating margin up 5% over Q3.
Customer NPS hit 75, an all-time high; ROE improved to 51% from 40%, with $55 million returned to stockholders in 2023 and another $18 million in January 2024.
summary: NRC's Q4 2023 revenue decreased slightly YoY, while diluted EPS rose to $0.36 from $0.27 a year earlier, helped by margin expansion and buybacks; full-year EPS fell to $1.25 from $1.27. Management guides 2024 revenue and earnings to start relatively flat, with higher tech, sales, and executive expenses pressuring margins until the expanded product suite converts later in the year. Recurring new sales rose 18% YoY in Q4, and operating margin expanded sequentially for the third straight quarter, but TRCV declined and operating income fell 4% YoY in Q4.

negative_highlights: Total revenue fell sharply by approximately 67% year-over-year, dropping from $20.4 million.
Paid users declined significantly by 64%, attributed to the intentional move away from lower-margin e-voucher products.
Cash balance decreased substantially to approximately $1.2 million compared to $4.7 million in the prior year.
