positive_highlights: Gross profit increased by $112,000 year-over-year despite lower total revenue due to strategic focus on higher-margin offerings.
Company raised $4 million via a public offering and retired remaining convertible notes of $2.1 million to fortify its financial position.
summary: Treasure Global reported Q2 FY2024 revenue of $6.7 million, a significant year-over-year decline from $20.4 million in the prior period. Gross profit improved to approximately $346,000 compared to $234,000 last year due to a strategic shift toward higher-margin business channels like TAZTE and AI-driven solutions for ZCITY'. The company posted a net loss of approximately $1.2 million versus $2 million in the prior quarter.

negative_highlights: Intermodal segment posted an operating loss of $944,000 due to $4.5 million in losses at West Coast operations.
Trucking segment revenue decreased $13.8 million to $75.2 million with operating margins contracting to 3.3%.
Company-managed brokerage revenue fell 29% to $28.1 million as spot loads were very low and many opportunities operated at or below breakeven.
positive_highlights: Contract logistics segment delivered exceptional results with operating income increasing $1.9 million to $32.1 million and margins expanding to 15.9%.
Dedicated transportation group remained stable with five new launches in 2023, including a major customer launch in Mexico.
Company reported its second best year ever for operating income and EPS despite the challenging quarter.
summary: Universal Logistics Holdings reported Q4 FY2023 operating revenues of $390.9 million and net income of $21.4 million ($0.81 EPS), missing prior year figures of $458.7 million revenue and $33.4 million net income. The company cited depressed freight rates, a UAW strike impact costing approximately $2.2 million in mixed operating income, and significant losses in West Coast intermodal operations totaling $4.5 million as primary drivers of the decline. Management provided 2024 guidance for top-line revenues between $400 million to $420 million for Q1 and full-year margins in the 8% to 10% range, noting a 'murky' outlook dependent on import volume recovery.

negative_highlights: North America Interactive generated an adjusted EBITDA loss of $9.8 million for the quarter with a full-year projected loss of approximately $30 million.
Tropicana Las Vegas will close on April 2nd, impacting revenues and contributions beginning in Q2 FY24.
January revenue was impacted by severe weather across most U.S. markets.
positive_highlights: Casinos & Resorts achieved a robust 7% revenue increase for the quarter with strong performance across Rhode Island and Kansas City properties.
International Interactive delivered record adjusted EBITDA of $93.2 million, driven by double-digit growth in the UK market despite regulatory headwinds.
Chicago Temporary facility ramped successfully to over $10 million GDR in January 2024, exceeding initial expectations.
summary: Bally's reported Q4 FY2023 revenues of $612 million (up 6% YoY) and full-year revenue growth of 9%, driven by strong performance in Casinos & Resorts (+7%) and International Interactive. Adjusted EBITDA margins remained solid across the portfolio, though North America Interactive posted a loss as it ramps up Bally Bet operations. Management provided FY2024 guidance for revenues between $2.5B-$2.7B and adjusted EBITDA of $655M-$695M, incorporating assumptions regarding Tropicana's closure in April 2024.

negative_highlights: Ting Adjusted EBITDA was -$12.4M in Q4, up from -$6M in Q4 2022
Ting workforce reduced by 13% (72 employees) and Mesa partner market ceased
Consolidated Adjusted EBITDA down 62% YoY; Wavelo Q4 revenue and EBITDA down sequentially
positive_highlights: Wavelo 2023 revenue $38.7M, Adjusted EBITDA $10.6M vs upgraded guidance of $4M-$6M
Consolidated revenue grew 10% YoY; operating cash flow improved to $9M in Q4 from $2.9M
Repaid $11.5M on syndicated loan, reducing leverage to 3.42x for third consecutive quarter
summary: Tucows reported Q4 2023 consolidated revenue up 10% YoY and Adjusted EBITDA of $2.6 million, down 62% YoY due to continued investment in Ting, which posted -$12.4 million Adjusted EBITDA. Wavelo beat its upgraded 2023 guidance with $10.6 million Adjusted EBITDA, but expects much lower growth in 2024. Domains grew revenue and gross margin modestly, while the company reduced Ting's workforce by 13% and ceased activity in Mesa, Arizona, with $4 million restructuring charges. 2024 guidance for Domains, Wavelo, and Corporate totals $53M-$57M Adjusted EBITDA; Ting guidance to be refined, with intention to reduce EBITDA loss.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to $93.6M in FY2023 from $120.4M in FY2022 (though per-share loss improved due to higher share count)
R&D expenses increased 17% to $83.2M, driven by ongoing clinical trial costs
First Phase III ENSURE readout timeline shifted from end of 2025 to Q2 2026, reflecting recruitment pace
positive_highlights: Closed first tranche of up to $240M private placement, receiving $75M in net proceeds, with top-tier investors including BVF Partners, Avidity Partners, and Janus Henderson
Phase II CALLIPER interim data showed 22.4% improvement in serum NfL for vidofludimus calcium over placebo at week 24 (p=0.01)
Cash runway extended into Q3 2025, funding operations through multiple clinical milestones
summary: Immunic reported FY2023 R&D expenses of $83.2M (vs $71.2M in 2022) and a net loss of $93.6M, or $2.11 per share, versus a $120.4M loss ($3.78/sh) in 2022. The company ended 2023 with $46.7M in cash and, combined with the $75M first tranche of a January 2024 private placement of up to $240M, expects runway into Q3 2025. Management highlighted positive Phase II CALLIPER interim NfL data in progressive MS and reiterated upcoming catalysts, including CALLIPER top-line data in April 2025, a Phase III ENSURE futility analysis in late 2024, and first ENSURE readout now guided to Q2 2026.

negative_highlights: INVOKE-2 trial observed an incidence of ARIA-E and ARIA-H of approximately 20% (mostly asymptomatic) with clinically serious events just under 1%
Full-year collaboration revenue ($97.1M) was significantly lower than the prior year ($133.6M)
AL002 study design relies on a common closed trial where placebo patients will be titrated to active doses in an open-label extension, delaying definitive efficacy readout
positive_highlights: FDA granted Breakthrough Therapy designation to latozinemab for FTD-GRN based on Phase 2 data
INVOKE-2 (AL002) completed enrollment ahead of schedule with a robust biomarker package including tau PET and plasma p-tau assays
Cash runway extended through 2026 following $75 million follow-on financing in January
summary: Alector reported Q4 FY2023 collaboration revenue of $15.2 million and full-year revenue of $97.1 million, alongside R&D expenses of $47.7M for the quarter ($192.1M annually) which were lower than prior periods due to trial completions. The company highlighted significant clinical milestones including FDA Breakthrough Therapy designation for latozinemab in FTD-GRN and enrollment completion for pivotal Phase 3 trials, while noting a ~20% incidence of ARIA-like events (mostly asymptomatic) in the AL002 Alzheimer's study. Management provided forward guidance estimating $60M-$70M collaboration revenue and cash runway through 2026.

negative_highlights: Total company advertising declined 11% due to strikes, political ad headwinds (-400 bps), and unfavorable FX.
Affiliate revenue in TV Media declined 1%, continuing trends from the first three quarters of 2023.
International subscriber growth is expected to slow as management rightsizes investment in local content that does not travel globally.
positive_highlights: D2C subscription revenue grew 43% in the quarter driven by Paramount+ subscriber additions of 4.1M and global ARPU expansion.
Paramount+ domestic price increase flow-through contributed to a full-quarter growth of nearly 80% in D2C sub revenue.
Content slate momentum remained strong with Mean Girls and Bob Marley: One Love opening at #1 domestically.
summary: Paramount Global reported Q4 FY2023 revenue of $7.6 billion and adjusted OIBDA of $520 million, navigating significant headwinds from labor strikes that impacted linear advertising (down 11%) and political spend. Management provided forward guidance for low to mid-teens ad growth in Q1 driven by the Super Bowl but noted sub-growth expectations are lower than 2023 due to strike delays and a strategic shift away from local content investment internationally. The company announced an approximately $1 billion programming and restructuring charge expected in Q1 FY2024, including roughly $200 million for workforce reductions.

negative_highlights: Full-year revenue of $62.6 million was well below the $80-$100 million guidance, driven by CarbonSmart offtake shortfalls.
2024 adjusted EBITDA guidance of a $65-$55 million loss, with positive adjusted EBITDA timeline reset from late 2024.
Q1 2024 revenue expected to be similar to Q1 2023 (~$10 million), roughly half of Q4 2023, reflecting a back-half-weighted year.
positive_highlights: Q4 revenue grew 77% YoY to $20.5 million, with core Biorefining revenue up 103% to $14.2 million.
Full-year gross margin expanded ~400 bps to 28%, and Q4 gross profit rose 62% QoQ to $8.5 million.
Cost actions reduced annualized operating expenses by $5.3 million and cut executive cash bonuses by 80%, saving ~$3 million.
summary: LanzaTech reported Q4 2023 revenue of $20.5 million (up 77% YoY) but full-year revenue of $62.6 million, well below the $80-$100 million guidance due to CarbonSmart offtake shortfalls. Q4 gross margin was 41% and full-year gross margin 28% (up ~400 bps), with adjusted EBITDA loss of $13.7 million in Q4 and $80.1 million for the year. For 2024, management guided revenue to $90-$105 million and adjusted EBITDA loss of $65-$55 million, while resetting the timeline for positive adjusted EBITDA beyond late 2024. The company announced a reorganization reducing the executive team by 33%, cutting ~5% of headcount, and lowering 2023 executive cash bonuses by 80%.

negative_highlights: Net loss, though reduced, remains substantial at $20.8 million for 2023
No revenue reported; company remains pre-commercial with ongoing clinical spend
Enrollment completion timelines for some trials (e.g., iGoLSTA) depend on external funding from WARPNINE, which is not fully secured
positive_highlights: ASCEND trial fully enrolled (158 patients); top-line cohort A data expected Q4 2024, full data mid-2025
Operating expenses decreased 55.4% YoY due to merger-related in-process R&D not repeating; R&D costs fell 2.5% to $12.7 million
Cash runway extended to early 2026 based on current plans
summary: Lisata reported full-year 2023 operating expenses of $25.7 million, down 55.4% from $57.6 million in 2022 (down 5.5% excluding merger-related in-process R&D). Net loss narrowed to $20.8 million from $54.2 million. Cash and marketable securities stood at $50.5 million, expected to fund operations into early 2026. The ASCEND trial reached full enrollment with top-line data for cohort A expected in Q4 2024; BOLSTER enrollment is on track to complete by end of 2024, but no milestones were met for the quarter.

negative_highlights: Net loss attributable to common stockholders of $31.3 million in Q4 and $193.7 million for full year; AFFO per share negative $0.36 in Q4
No common dividend anticipated for some time; reinstatement tied to paying off the strategic financing
Unable to provide timing estimate on KEYS A and KEYS B loan pool consensual transfers, and some marketed asset sales previously fell through
positive_highlights: RevPAR grew 1.6% in Q4 on 3.4% ADR increase, the 11th straight quarter of YoY RevPAR growth
Group room revenue exceeded prior year by 16% for the full year, with 2024 and 2025 group pacing up 8% and 13%
Food and beverage margin improved 284 bps in Q4 and F&B revenue grew 18% for the full year
summary: AHT reported Q4 net loss attributable to common stockholders of $31.3 million (-$0.90/diluted share) and negative AFFO of $0.36 per diluted share, with full-year AFFO of $0.72. Q4 comparable RevPAR rose 1.6% on a 3.4% ADR increase, marking an 11th consecutive quarter of YoY RevPAR growth, and January total revenue grew 5.3%. The strategic priority is retiring the $183 million Oaktree strategic financing, funded by asset sales (six assets totaling ~$225 million, including Hilton Boston Back Bay at $171 million for ~$70 million net proceeds), mortgage refinancings, and non-traded preferred raising (~$105 million to date). No common dividend reinstatement is expected for some time, and the KEYS A and B loan pool transfers remain in progress with no timing estimate.

negative_highlights: Fast LNG 1 slipped from prior schedule; first LNG now expected late March and first cargo in April.
No explicit revenue or EPS figures disclosed in the transcript, limiting visibility on top-line performance.
CEO described the company's shares as 'very undervalued at these levels,' without providing a specific valuation metric.
positive_highlights: Full-year 2023 FFO per share of $3.56 versus $1.61 in 2022, with 2024 guidance of over $6 per share.
Barcarena and Santa Catarina terminals completed and hooked up, with Barcarena projected to generate $500 million in contracted EBITDA at run rate by 2027.
FLNG 2 fully financed at $700 million; construction begins April with expected Q1 2026 start-up.
summary: NFE reported Q4 2023 EBITDA of $388 million and full-year EBITDA of $1.3 billion, with funds from operations (FFO) of $3.56 per share in 2023 versus $1.61 in 2022, and guided 2024 FFO to over $6 per share. Management highlighted the completion and hook-up of the Barcarena and Santa Catarina terminals in Brazil and reiterated first LNG from Fast LNG 1 in late March with first cargo in April. CapEx is expected to decline roughly 90% in 2024 from 2023 levels, and FLNG 2 was announced as fully financed with construction starting in April. No explicit revenue or EPS figures were provided on the call.

negative_highlights: Q4 net sales fell note weakness in of guidance range due to industry softness in the US specialty retail channel.
Full year 2024 revenue guidance implies a low to high teens percentage decline, with implied lost revenue between $27 million and $39 million.
Dilution among distributor brands created a drag on total company performance, keeping overall sales below desired levels.
positive_highlights: Proprietary nutrient brands sales grew in Q4 and for the full year of 2023 compared to 2022.
Adjusted gross profit margin expanded significantly to 24.3% in Q4 from 14.7% a year ago, driven by favorable brand mix and lower freight costs.
International and non-cannabis sales increased to approximately 25% of total 2023 sales, up from 22% in the prior year.
summary: Fourth quarter net sales were $47.2 million, down 23.2% year over year due to an 18.7% volume decrease and a 4.5% price mix decline. Despite the revenue miss, the company achieved positive adjusted EBITDA for the full year 2023 and expects positive adjusted EBITDA in 2024, though it provided guidance for net sales declines of low to high teens for the upcoming year. Management noted that while they believe they have reached a bottom in industry demand, the path to recovery depends on regulatory catalysts like federal descheduling and legalization in major states like Florida and Pennsylvania.

negative_highlights: Q4 net loss of $70 million, or $2.32 per diluted share, driven by a non-cash Targus impairment and unrealized investment losses.
Q4 operating revenues declined to $395 million from $449 million in the prior-year period; operating adjusted EBITDA fell to $79 million from $110 million.
Annual report on Form 10-K filing delayed; management declined to comment on auditor sign-off.
positive_highlights: Capital Markets segment revenues increased 75% to $575 million in 2023, with segment income up to $198 million from $82 million.
Full-year total revenues rose 52% to $1.65 billion, and operating revenues increased 25% to $1.63 billion.
Wealth Management returned to profitability with $198 million in revenues and $3 million segment income; assets under management grew to $25.4 billion from $24 billion.
summary: Q4 FY2023 total revenues were $347 million with a net loss of $70 million, or $2.32 diluted loss per share, driven by a non-cash Targus impairment and unrealized investment losses. Operating revenues were $395 million, down from $449 million in Q4 2022, and operating adjusted EBITDA fell to $79 million from $110 million. Full-year total revenues rose 52% to $1.65 billion with operating adjusted EBITDA of $368 million, but the company delayed its 10-K filing, cut its dividend by 50% to $0.50 per share, and retained Moelis to review strategic alternatives for Great American. Management cited strong growth in several core segments, including a 75% increase in Capital Markets revenues to $575 million, while acknowledging continued weakness in Targus.

negative_highlights: FY2023 preliminary unaudited financial and operational results were delayed and not discussed on the call, leaving revenue, EPS, and margin figures unreported
Additional 15% headcount reduction announced on top of the prior 10% cut, with the later part of the year expected to be significantly stronger than the first half
Analyst noted 4Q '23 volume declined sequentially and January retail sales appeared weaker year-over-year, with the loan covenant requiring roughly $5.4 billion revenue or about 100,000 units in 2024
positive_highlights: $950 million of the $1.3 billion funding requirement secured through a three-year loan facility from a syndicate of global banks
Polestar 3 production started in Chengdu and Polestar 4 production started in China, with U.S. (South Carolina) and South Korea (Busan) manufacturing milestones reached
Guidance for double-digit gross margin in the later part of 2024 and high-teens gross margin with cash flow breakeven in 2025
summary: Polestar delayed its preliminary FY2023 financial results and did not report revenue, EPS, or margins on the call, citing first-year Sarbanes-Oxley compliance. Management announced roughly $950 million of a $1.3 billion funding need secured via a three-year bank loan facility, guided to a double-digit gross margin in the later part of 2024 and high-teens gross margin with cash flow breakeven in 2025. The company also disclosed a 15% headcount reduction, building on a prior 10% cut, and noted Polestar 3 and 4 production starts with global deliveries beginning in summer 2024. The call was dominated by funding, covenant, and share-price concerns rather than reported results.

negative_highlights: Cash balance decreased significantly to approximately $6.5 million from $27.6 million at year-end.
$25 million used in operating activities with no active grants received during the period.
No award has been made under Project NextGen despite ongoing discussions, creating uncertainty regarding future financing.
positive_highlights: Positive interim data from Phase 2 trial of GEO-CM04S1 demonstrated statistically significant increases in neutralizing antibodies against multiple SARS-CoV-2 variants including Omicron XBB.1.5 without reconfiguration.
summary: GeoVax reported a net loss of $14 million in Q4 FY2023 (or full year depending on context interpretation, text says 'net loss for '23 was [$265] million' which implies annual figure or typo correction needed but clearly indicates financial distress) with no active grants and cash balances dropping to approximately $6.5 million from $27.6 million at the end of 2022 due to operating activities usage of $25 million. Management provided positive interim clinical data for GEO-CM04S1 showing robust immune responses in immunocompromised patients but explicitly stated no award has been received yet under Project NextGen despite ongoing discussions, and raised capital is expected opportunistically.

negative_highlights: Gross margin decreased sequentially to 43% in Q4 due to higher proportion of system sales and inventory roll-off.
Revenue growth was constrained by a freeze in the South Korea market, which represented less than 1% of revenue.
positive_highlights: Fourth quarter revenue grew 18% YoY to $12.1 million with full year revenue up 19%.
summary: Fourth quarter revenue grew 18% year-over-year to $12.1 million driven by strong ALLY system placements (44 total in FY23) and procedure volume increases of nearly 20%. Full year revenue increased 19%, with gross margins at 50% for the full year, consistent with guidance despite a quarter-to-quarter dip due to higher proportion of lower-margin system sales. Management raised expectations for future growth driven by US expansion and anticipated European clearance in H2 FY24.

negative_highlights: Q4 revenue was only €1.6 million, and the company recorded a pretax loss of €12.3 million
Impairment charges totaled €9.7 million, including a €6.4 million inventory write-down and €3.3 million for a development project, closing the HEVO Solar legacy chapter

Bank balance was just over €1 million on December 31, and the company must seek shareholder approval at an upcoming EGM to issue securities beyond the existing 20% cap, with management unable to specify dilution or timing
positive_highlights: HEVO-Portugal portfolio received IPCEI designation, enabling bilateral funding agreements and European Investment Bank discussions
2024 revenue guidance of €34 million maintained, with €7.3 million already contracted and €10 million expected from balance-of-plant equipment plus €2 million from engineering services
Operating costs decreased for the fourth consecutive quarter, and Q1 2024 ATM raise of €5.9 million net, mostly on February 16, improved liquidity
summary: Fusion Fuel reported Q4 revenue of just €1.6 million, with a pretax loss of €12.3 million driven by €9.7 million of noncash impairments, including a €6.4 million inventory write-down and a €3.3 million development project charge. The company reiterated its 2024 revenue guidance of €34 million, of which only €7.3 million is contracted, and guided to approximately 15% gross margin, with SG&A of €14–16 million and CapEx of €8–10 million. The quarter included a key post-period development: its HEVO-Portugal project received IPCEI designation, which management says opens bilateral funding and EIB discussions but will not drive 2024–2025 results. Cash burn remains a concern, with the December 31 bank balance just over €1 million, partially addressed by a €5.9 million ATM raise in February.

negative_highlights: Cash sales were down 3% year-over-year due to high interest rates impacting residential dealers and delaying C&I capital purchases.
Q4 operating expenses increased 10% including $90,000 in SG&A and $53,000 in R&D primarily reflecting personnel-related increases.
positive_highlights: Full year profitability achieved with net income of $119,000 ($0.05 per share) after reversing stock split expenses.
Gross profit margin improved to 74.5% in 2023 from 72.4%, driven by higher-value new products and custom units.
Monitoring revenue returned to growth with a 9% increase, recovering above pre-3G sunsetting levels.
summary: Full year revenue rose 15% to $8.1 million with hardware sales up 23%, while Q4 revenue increased 22% to $2.25 million driven by a new product launch and custom units. The company achieved full-year profitability with net income of $119,000 ($0.05/share) after reversing stock split expenses, supported by gross margin expansion to 74.5%. Management raised expectations for double-digit monitoring revenue growth in 2024 following the recovery from legacy hardware sunsetting.

negative_highlights: Revenue of $246 million declined year-over-year and adjusted contribution margin was only 1.2%
Adjusted EBITDA loss of $38.1 million deteriorated sequentially from the prior quarter
GAAP net loss of $81.1 million remained large, and management gave no numeric revenue or EBITDA guidance, only a qualitative target of positive adjusted EBITDA this year
positive_highlights: Prepaid blocks were $207 million, up over 150% sequentially and the strongest quarter of the year
Cash balance rose to $264 million with total liquidity plus reserve deposits of $384 million, supported by $490 million of committed capital led by Delta in 2023
Charter volumes grew approximately 20% year-over-year and opex fell $14.7 million sequentially to the lowest level since Q1 2022
summary: Wheels Up reported Q4 revenue of $246 million, down year-over-year, with more than half the decline attributed to lower aircraft sales revenue and the divestiture of the aircraft management business. Adjusted EBITDA loss was $38.1 million, improved year-over-year but worse sequentially, and adjusted contribution margin was just 1.2% on underutilized fixed assets plus non-recurring maintenance adjustments. GAAP net loss was $81.1 million, better than last year primarily on the absence of a prior goodwill impairment, while prepaid blocks of $207 million rose over 150% sequentially and cash ended at $264 million with $384 million total liquidity. Management reiterated the goal of positive adjusted EBITDA this year, citing charter volumes up ~20%, a new $1.2 billion FTV metric, and a cost base with opex down $14.7 million sequentially, but no numeric EBITDA or revenue guidance was provided.

negative_highlights: GAAP net loss of $35.5 million ($1.29 per diluted share) driven by mark-to-market losses on RMBS.
Book value per common share fell to $4.53, down 9.2% from September 30 due to negative duration positioning and lower MSR marks.
MSR portfolio net CPR averaged approximately 4.2%, modestly down from the prior quarter's 5.6%.
positive_highlights: Earnings available for distribution (non-GAAP) covered quarterly distributions at $4.5 million ($0.17 per share).
Management successfully repurchased over $6 million in Series B preferred shares to improve the capital structure before they transitioned to floating rates.
Raised $11.8 million through aftermarket common share programs early in 2024.
summary: Cherry Hill reported a GAAP net loss of $35.5 million ($1.29 per share) for Q4 FY2023 due to portfolio positioning impacts from rate declines and lower MSR marks, though non-GAAP earnings available for distribution were positive at $4.5 million ($0.17 per share). Book value declined 9.2% year-over-year primarily driven by negative duration exposure during the Fed pivot in late 2023. Management utilized capital to repurchase Series B preferred shares and raised funds via an aftermarket program, while maintaining a leverage ratio of approximately 4.2 times.

negative_highlights: Full-year interest expense ($16.3M) exceeded guidance due to rising rates, though Q4 declined $0.7M.
Cost inflation driven by regulated power costs (some double-digit increases) and industry-wide liability insurance rate hikes.
2024 production volumes are projected nearly flat year-over-year at 19k-21k BOE/day.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA increased to $25.2 million in Q4 from a prior quarter loss of $13.4M due to non-cash derivative gains and lower LOE.
Full-year 2023 adjusted EBITDA ($88M) met the midpoint of guidance despite steep declines in natural gas prices throughout the year.
Beta development program forecasted to generate IRRs exceeding 100% with payback periods under one year.
summary: Amplify Energy reported Q4 FY2023 adjusted EBITDA of $25.2 million and free cash flow of $14.4 million against a full-year 2023 backdrop where production averaged 20,800 BOE/day (up 1% sequentially) but LOE declined 7%. Management provided explicit 2024 guidance for adjusted EBITDA between $90M-$110M and free cash flow of $20M-$40M based on WTI at $75/bbl, noting that the Bairoil asset monetization is ongoing with an update expected by mid-summer.

negative_highlights: Q4 revenue declined 14.5% to $72 million and gross margin contracted to 38.0% from 43.1% a year ago, reflecting planned promotional activity
FY2024 revenue guidance of $190-$210 million implies organic sales down mid-teens to mid-single digits, with $32-$37 million of headwinds from store closures and international distributor transitions
Adjusted EBITDA profitability may take longer than initially communicated, with FY2024 adjusted EBITDA loss guided at $63-$78 million
positive_highlights: Inventory reduced 51% year-over-year to $58 million, entering 2024 with a healthy mix of core franchise goods
Full-year operating cash use narrowed to $30 million from $91 million in 2022, ending with $130 million in cash and no outstanding revolver borrowings
Q4 adjusted EBITDA came in ahead of expectations and revenue was at the high end of the guided range, marking the fourth consecutive quarter of meeting or exceeding guidance
summary: Q4 revenue of $72 million declined 14.5% year-over-year and gross margin fell to 38.0% from 43.1%, though results came in at the high end of guidance and adjusted EBITDA exceeded expectations. Management issued FY2024 revenue guidance of $190-$210 million (organic down mid-teens to mid-single digits) and an adjusted EBITDA loss of $63-$78 million, citing $32-$37 million of headwinds from 10-15 US store closures and international distributor transitions. The company stated that reaching adjusted EBITDA profitability may take longer than previously communicated. Inventory fell 51% year-over-year to $58 million and full-year operating cash use narrowed to $30 million from $91 million, with $130 million of cash and no revolver borrowings.

negative_highlights: Q4 2023 net loss of $4.8 million compared to net income of $6.7 million in Q3 2023.
Q4 2023 revenue fell to $61.9 million from $76.9 million sequentially, with sales volumes down to ~1.0 million tons from 1.2 million tons.
Q4 2023 free cash flow was negative $9.6 million, and management guided to potentially negative free cash flow in Q1 2024 due to higher working capital.
positive_highlights: Record full-year 2023 revenue of $296 million, up 16% YoY, and record sales volume of 4.5 million tons.
Q1 2024 volume guidance of 1.25-1.4 million tons, implying 25-40% sequential growth from Q4 2023.
Full-year 2023 free cash flow of $8 million and a $34.1 million adjusted EBITDA, up from $29.3 million in 2022.
summary: Smart Sand reported Q4 2023 revenue of $61.9 million, down from $76.9 million in Q3, and a net loss of $4.8 million versus net income of $6.7 million in the prior quarter. Full-year 2023 revenue was a record $296 million with adjusted EBITDA of $34.1 million, but Q4 volumes fell to ~1.0 million tons from 1.2 million tons sequentially due to seasonal slowdown and customer budget exhaustion. Management guided Q1 2024 volumes to 1.25-1.4 million tons (up 25-40% QoQ) and full-year 2024 volumes 5-10% above 2023, with contribution margin per ton in the mid-teens and positive free cash flow expected for the year.

negative_highlights: Net revenue fell 40.3% year-over-year to $32.8 million, with sustained revenue down $15.6 million.
Q1 2024 revenue guidance of $18-$21 million implies roughly a 45% year-over-year decline.
Fourth-quarter contribution margin was negative 0.8%, and sustained product contribution margin declined to 6.9% from 8.3% a year ago.
positive_highlights: Gross margin expanded to 51.0% from 37.1% in the prior-year quarter, driven by product mix and lower high-cost liquidation.
Adjusted EBITDA loss improved 65.4% to $5.6 million from $16.2 million a year ago.
Inventory declined to $20.4 million from $43.7 million a year ago, and the credit facility was extended to December 2026 with the minimum liquidity covenant reduced to $6.8 million.
summary: Aterian reported Q4 2023 net revenue of $32.8 million, down 40.3% year-over-year, with sustained revenue at $25.2 million versus $40.8 million, due to SKU rationalization, reduced discretionary spending, and competitive pricing. Gross margin improved to 51.0% from 37.1% a year ago, and adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed 65.4% to $5.6 million. Q1 2024 guidance calls for revenue of $18-$21 million (about a 45% year-over-year decline) and an adjusted EBITDA loss of $2.5-$3.5 million, with management still targeting second-half 2024 adjusted EBITDA profitability. Inventory fell to $20.4 million and the credit facility was extended to December 2026 with reduced covenants.

FYARRO Q4 net product sales were $6.3 million, up 6% QoQ and 21% YoY, with full-year 2023 sales of $24.4 million, up 60% from $15.2 million; management guided FYARRO 2024 sales to roughly the $6.0-6.5 million quarterly range, saying the ultra-rare PEComa market is nearing saturation. Q4 net loss widened to $16.3 million from $13.9 million a year ago, and full-year net loss was $65.8 million versus $60.5 million, with R&D up to $48.9 million from $32.7 million. In the PRECISION 1 interim readout, the TSC1 arm showed a 26% overall response rate (early, deep, durable, four tumor types) while the TSC2 arm showed a lower response rate; full enrollment is expected by May, the next two-thirds interim readout (80 patients, independent assessment) in Q3 2024, and study completion by end-2024. Cash of $108.8 million plus 2024 cost-reduction measures extend runway into Q4 2025.

negative_highlights: 2024 outlook projects new supply limiting rent growth, continued occupancy pressure and inflationary impact on operating margins
No specific earnings targets provided for 2024
Transaction market described as 'very, very quiet' with cap rates in the mid-5s below financing costs, keeping BRT in a hold posture

summary: BRT's Q4 call gave no explicit quarterly figures — revenue, EPS, FFO and margins were not stated on the transcript, with management directing listeners to the prior night's release. Management said it is not providing specific earnings targets, and the 2024 outlook anticipates new supply limiting rent growth, continued occupancy pressure and inflationary headwinds compressing operating margins. On the positive side, BRT repurchased $16.7 million of shares during the year and into 2024, has no significant mortgage maturities until early 2026, and expects better conditions by early-to-mid 2025 as new units are absorbed.

negative_highlights: Q4 revenues decreased by $4 million year-over-year, driven by a 9.3% drop in total sales as pandemic-related demand moderated.
Gross profit margin contracted to 31.7%, down 190 basis points from the prior-year period due to non-recurring adjustments and market maturation.
The company reported an adjusted EBITDA loss of $1.1 million compared to income in Q4 FY2022, with full-year guidance lowered to flat revenue.
positive_highlights: Management eliminated approximately $3 million in annualized fixed costs over the last two months through headcount reductions.
Early indications for Q1 suggest a modest return to order growth in the U.S. market following four consecutive quarters of decline.
The company is introducing new Google-certified EDLA interactive panels and enhancing legacy devices with compatible software.
summary: Boxlight reported Q4 FY2023 revenues of $38.8 million, a decrease of approximately 10% year-over-year compared to the prior period's $42.8 million. The company posted an adjusted EBITDA loss of $1.1 million versus income in the prior quarter and expects full-year 2024 revenue to remain flat with gross margins declining by 100-200 basis points due to market maturation. Management highlighted a strategic pivot including cost reductions targeting approximately $3 million in annualized fixed costs, leadership realignment, and debt refinancing efforts.

negative_highlights: Q3 2023 financials were restated due to incorrect classification of transaction-related costs in the cash flow statement.
2024 guidance refers to exit run rate revenue of $47 million-$53 million, a projection metric rather than a full-year revenue forecast.
positive_highlights: FY2023 net revenue grew 1,097% to $5.7 million, with marketplace revenue up 529%.
EveryLife contributed over $2.7 million in revenue since its Q3 2023 launch, 70% of which was subscription-based.
Balance sheet remained debt-free with $16.4 million in cash and $17.2 million in working capital at year-end.
summary: PublicSquare reported FY2023 net revenue of $5.7 million, up 1,097% year over year, driven by marketplace growth of 529% and over $2.7 million from the EveryLife brand launched in Q3 2023. The quarter included the launch of the e-commerce marketplace on November 1, with traffic up 549% and average order value above $70, and the company ended the year with $16.4 million in cash and zero debt. Management guided to a year-end 2024 exit run rate revenue of $47 million to $53 million from existing businesses before synergies, and announced the all-stock acquisition of Credova, a name-now-pay-later firm with 2023 net revenues of $15.5 million, adjusted EBITDA of $2.3 million, and positive free cash flow. Credova adds over 4,800 merchants and 2.8 million applicants, with management expecting it to remain cash flow positive in 2024.

negative_highlights: No revenue beat or EPS guidance raise was reported; the company maintained prior financial guidance despite strong clinical progress.
Expanded Access Program logistics will be handled on a case-by-case basis with centers bearing some financial burden, limiting immediate commercial upside visibility.
The Phase 2 EFZO-CONNECT study in SSc-ILD is still in early enrollment and no data is expected until later in 2024.
positive_highlights: Phase 3 EFZO-FIT study enrollment is on track to complete by Q2 2024 at the target of 264 patients.
Strong patient demand for Efzofitimod led to the implementation of an Expanded Access Program (EAP) prior to data unblinding, serving as a positive clinical signal.
The company maintains sufficient cash runway to fund operations through the BLA filing without needing additional dilutive financing.
summary: aTyr Pharma reported fourth quarter and full year 2023 financial results with $101.7 million in cash, restricted cash, and investments at period end. The company maintained its prior financial guidance for the full year, citing sufficient cash runway to fund operations through the filing of a biologics license application (BLA) for Efzofitimod. Management highlighted significant progress on the Phase 3 EFZO-FIT study in pulmonary sarcoidosis, with enrollment expected to complete in Q2 2024, and noted strong patient demand leading to an early Expanded Access Program.

negative_highlights: Consolidated DSO spiked to 90.7 days, significantly above management's target of low-70s due to a large client payment delay
Engineering segment revenue declined YoY following a major contract reduction by approximately 30%
DSO is expected to remain elevated through Q1 before improving in subsequent quarters

Life Sciences Data & Solutions gross profit expanded by 19% compared to the prior year
summary: RCM Technologies reported Q4 FY2023 results with consolidated gross profit growing 5.7% to $21.6 million and adjusted EBITDA rising 18.5% to $8.9 million. Adjusted diluted EPS increased significantly by 37.5% from $0.52 to $0.71, driven largely by a normalized view of the healthcare segment which grew over 28% year-over-year after removing COVID impacts. Management provided forward guidance for fiscal 2024 anticipating at least low double-digit consolidated adjusted EBITDA growth compared to FY2023.

Net loss widened to $6.5 million from $6.1 million, with operating expenses of $8.5 million for the quarter and $24.6 million year-to-date including $3.2 million of Paragon litigation costs; cash and short-term investments totaled $9.1 million with no bank debt. Orders were $3.4 million year-to-date with backlog of $3.3 million, and management expects order activity and revenue to ramp meaningfully in the final quarter and to reach profitability during calendar 2025. Management cited a $77 million pipeline, over 5x year-over-year, and roughly $4.5 million in annual run-rate savings from the R&D-to-commercial pivot.

The cancer sequencing initiative secured a pipeline of approximately $1.5 million in new business opportunities with confirmed orders from 25 investigated projects.

summary: Pyxis Tankers reported Q4 2023 TCE revenues of $12 million, down 13.6% year-over-year due to operating one fewer tanker and lower spot exposure, while average daily TCE for eco-MR2 fell 8% to about $30,500. Net income of $21.6 million, or $2.04 basic EPS, surged versus $6.5 million last year mainly because of a $17.1 million gain on the December sale of a 2015-built tanker. Adjusted EBITDA declined $2 million to $7.7 million, though Q4 TCE was up sequentially from Q3. Management gave no explicit quantitative guidance but noted constructive sector outlooks; as of March 12, 2024, 92% of Q1 tanker days were booked at $30,300 per day and 70% of dry bulk days at $19,600 per day, and the company has deployed $1.4 million to watch back 375,000 shares, about 7.5% of the public float.

negative_highlights: Q4 Adjusted EBITDA was just below breakeven due to a $7 million net one-time estimated litigation settlement expense recorded in operating expenses.

summary: Katapult reported Q4 FY23 gross originations of $67.5 million (up 13% YoY) and revenue of $56.7 million (up 16%), exceeding the pre-announced guidance range of 13%-15%. Adjusted EBITDA was just below breakeven, representing a $4.9 million improvement over Q2022 despite including a one-time estimated litigation settlement expense that impacted operating expenses. Management raised full-year 2024 revenue growth expectations to at least 10% and noted strong performance from new direct integrations like Wal-Mart via Katapult Pay.

The company has not yet secured debt financing to complete Phase I construction of its Kellyton Graphite Plant despite having multiple term sheets on the table and signing a multiyear off-take agreement with SK On. Management raised production guidance for Phase I from 7,500 metric tons per annum (announced in March) to an anticipated 12,500 metric tons based on debottlenecking studies.

summary: Fanhua reported FY2023 total life insurance premiums of RMB16.1–16.4 billion, up roughly 29–30% year-on-year, with first year premiums up 30.3% to RMB3.8 billion, operating income up 16.1% to RMB195.8 million, and net income attributable to shareholders up 179.7% to RMB280.4 million. Q4 industry-level results turned negative amid the pricing rate change, and management explicitly declined to give 2024 annual targets given uncertainty over the pending independent-intermediary commission cap (rumored April implementation, consensus 30–40% commission cut). End-market demand forecasted as flat or down modestly for repair and remodel spending.

Gross margin expanded strongly by roughly 550 bps to 29.2%, driven by higher-margin product mix, but operating expenses increased as management continued investing in growth initiatives like new geographies and digital tools. Management provided initial full-year 2024 guidance for revenue between $115M-$128M (implying a miss on prior year levels) and adjusted net income of $1.2M-$2M, citing flat-to-slightly-down end-market demand.

STS data still immature; median OS not yet reached

summary: Moleculin Biotech reported clinical data from its Annamycin program in relapsed/refractory AML, with a 60% CRc rate (50% CR, 10% CRi) in second-line patients from the MB-106 trial. The company highlighted the drug's lack of cardiotoxicity across 82 treated subjects and plans to initiate a pivotal registration study in AML this year, targeting an FDA end-of-Phase 2 meeting by summer. Management also mentioned interest from European sarcoma experts for an externally funded trial, while the company ended 2023 with $24 million in cash, sufficient into Q4 2024. The tone is confident, emphasizing superior efficacy versus approved targeted therapies and a clear regulatory pathway.

Management remains confident in market fundamentals, citing low order books and supportive demand, and highlighted a strong cash balance of $35.6 million with no bank debt.

The company projects 2024 revenue of approximately $7 million based on a backlog that grew to $10.8 million as of March 20, 2024. Management declined to provide specific gross margin guidance, noting that profitability is driven by product mix and fixed overhead absorption.

negative_highlights: Net loss increased year-over-year from $40.9 million to $42.9 million.
Operating burn rate remains high at approximately $8 million per quarter without commencing the pivotal trial.
VERSATILE-003 Phase 3 trial is being shelved in favor of the new triple combination strategy.

In the refractory (ICI-resistant) group, the triple combination achieved a 63% overall survival at 12 months compared to approximately 30% with current approaches.
Safety profile confirmed as acceptable in over 300 patients treated with PDS01ADC and over 170 with Versamune HPV.
summary: PDS Biotech reported a net loss of $42.9 million for the year ended December 31, 2023, compared to $40.9 million in the prior year, driven by increased operating expenses and interest costs despite R&D spending decreasing slightly. The company raised approximately $10.5 million via ATM sales during Q4, leaving a cash balance of $56.6 million sufficient for operations through late 2025 absent new financing or trial initiation. Management announced a strategic pivot to prioritize the triple combination (Versamune HPV + PDS01ADC + KEYTRUDA) in head and neck cancer over the previously planned VERSATILE-003 Phase 3 trial, citing superior efficacy data from NCI-led studies.

Operating loss widened slightly to $2.2 million compared to $2.7 million in the prior year.
positive_highlights: CMS assigned unique HCPCS codes for PoNS controller and mouthpiece effective April 1st, 2024, enabling case-by-case claims submission.
A letter of intent was received from the Quebec Ministry of Health to purchase 30 PoNS devices for stroke validation.
Cash runway extended into Q3 2024 following $1.3 million raised under the ATM program since year-end.
summary: Helius Medical reported Q4 FY2023 revenue of $134,000, a significant decrease from $282,000 in the prior year quarter, driven by the expiration of the PTAP program and lower Canadian sales. The company posted an operating loss of $2.2 million and a net loss of $1 million, though cash burn decreased to $2 million. Management noted that revenues will likely remain low until CMS reimbursement is secured, expected in October 2024.

negative_highlights: Client count fell from 1,040 as of March 2023 to 721 at year-end after the Central Bank agreement termination, with the deposit-fee impact first recognized in Q4
Full-year operating expense jumped to $38.3 million from $11.7 million on goodwill and developed-technology impairment charges, producing a $17.3 million net loss
Cash used in operations was $832,000 versus $1.7 million provided in 2022, cash fell to $4.9 million from $8.4 million, and a $135,000 working capital deficit remains
positive_highlights: Full-year revenue rose 85.3% to $17.56 million from $9.48 million, with loan interest income up 163% to $2.97 million and investment income up 175.6% to $5.84 million
Loan book grew 194% year-over-year to $55.66 million from $18.9 million
Average monthly fee revenue per account increased 35% to $8,298 from $6,154, and Q4 net income was $2.5 million versus a $37 million loss a year earlier
summary: Safe Harbor reported Q4 2023 revenue up more than 25% to $4.5 million from $3.6 million, including $549,000 of retroactive interest-method revenue recognized in the quarter. Full-year revenue rose 85.3% to $17.56 million with adjusted EBITDA of $3.6 million versus $1.3 million in 2022, but the company posted a full-year net loss of $17.3 million driven by Abaca-related impairments and restructuring. The July 2023 termination of the Central Bank agreement cut clients from 1,040 in March to 721 at year-end, with the deposit-fee impact first hitting Q4. Management gave no explicit numeric guidance, citing optimism about 2024 and potential regulatory catalysts (SAFER Banking Act, Schedule III rescheduling) while noting a $135,000 working capital deficit.

negative_highlights: No revenue, EPS, or quantitative financial results disclosed on the call; only qualitative runway statement
G&A elevated, including $6.5 million in legal expenses for the year, with ongoing Delaware Supreme Court litigation
AMP-270 U.S. enrollment constrained by standard-of-care differences pending a Type D FDA meeting; first U.S. patient dosing not confirmed
positive_highlights: Cash runway stated as sufficient to fund programs for 'the next year and a half or longer'
Ovarian cancer Phase 2 preliminary data showed objective response rate better than the April 2022 AACR preliminary data, described as 4x-5x greater ORR than pembrolizumab alone in KEYNOTE 100
DURIPANC Phase 1 first three patients enrolled with no reported adverse events to date, Phase 1 completion expected summer 2024
summary: AIM's FY2023 update call contained no reported revenue, EPS, or quantified financial results beyond a qualitative claim of cash runway for 'the next year and a half or longer,' with G&A noted as elevated largely due to $6.5 million in legal expenses. Clinical updates were the focus: the ovarian cancer Phase 2 interim report is pending, the AMP-518 post-COVID topline data (reported February) was described as showing positive signals though not statistically significant, and the DURIPANC Phase 1 portion is expected to complete in summer 2024. AMP-270 enrollment in the U.S. is stalled pending a Type D FDA meeting on inclusion criteria, while EU enrollment is targeted for Q3/Q4 2024. No formal financial guidance was provided.

negative_highlights: Statutory loss after tax was US$145 million, heavily impacted by non-recurring acquisition costs.
Significant non-cash fair value adjustments of US$47 million and warrant valuation changes of US$22 million hit the P&L.
Operational improvements like ventilation debottlenecking will not impact production until next year.
positive_highlights: ASX IPO raised approximately A$325 million (US$214 million) providing a strengthened balance sheet for debt repayment.
Copper revenue per shipment increased from US$18-19 million to US$24 million due to higher commodity prices.
Company repaid deferred consideration of US$83 million and reduced interest-bearing liabilities including senior facilities.
summary: Metals Acquisition reported a statutory loss after tax of US$145 million for FY2023, driven by one-off acquisition costs including US$79 million in administration expenses and US$48 million in stamp duty. The company clarified that results reflect only the first six months of ownership following the mid-year acquisition of the CSA copper mine, with underlying earnings representing roughly half a year of operations. Management noted significant non-cash fair value adjustments totaling around US$47 million related to warrants and derivatives.

negative_highlights: Q4 2023 GAAP net loss widened to $4.7 million, or $0.41 per share, from $4.4 million, or $0.39 per share, in Q4 2022.
Q4 2023 GAAP cost of revenues rose to $773,000 from $62,000 a year earlier, including inventory write-offs and royalty expenses.
The gut-on-a-chip program was put on hold, with no timeline for reinitiation.
positive_highlights: Full-year 2023 revenue reached $11 million, up $10.7 million from $299,000 in 2022, driven by a $10 million milestone payment from AbbVie.
Cash and cash equivalents of $26.7 million as of December 31, 2023, provided a runway into at least 2025 by management's estimate.
AbbVie reported expected meaningful growth and a ramp-up in the U.S. filler market after multiple quarters of decline, supporting prospects for the partnered dermal filler program.
summary: CollPlant reported Q4 2023 GAAP revenue of $299,000, up from $58,000 in Q4 2022, and full-year 2023 revenue of $11 million versus $299,000 in 2022, driven mainly by a $10 million AbbVie milestone payment. The company remains pre-commercial with a Q4 GAAP net loss of $4.7 million, or $0.41 per share, and full-year net loss of $7 million versus $16.7 million in 2022. Cash and cash equivalents stood at $26.7 million as of December 31, 2023, which management projects funds operations into at least 2025. The company put its gut-on-a-chip program on hold to focus resources on its aesthetics and breast implant programs, and it anticipates reporting breast implant large animal study data in Q4 2024 and Q1 2025.

negative_highlights: Company paused order intake due to capital constraints and operational challenges hindering volume production.
Revenue will be nominal in Q1 FY2024 as the company builds inventory before relaunching orders.
Customer service and delivery response times were impacted by initial launch setbacks.
positive_highlights: Operating loss narrowed to $6 million from $8 million in the prior year period.
Raised $24 million in private placement including a strategic seed investment from a Tier 1 medical device company.
Clinical trial data for pulse oximetry achieved a root-mean-square error of 2.46%, exceeding FDA guidance.
summary: Movano Health reported an operating loss of $6 million for Q4 FY2023, a reduction from the $8 million loss in the prior year period, with cash burn of $5.4 million offset by a $24 million private placement closed during the quarter. The company paused new order intake to resolve production and customer service challenges following its November launch, resulting in nominal revenue recognition for Q4 as shipments commence in 2024. Management expressed confidence in clinical data supporting FDA clearance for pulse rate and blood oxygen monitoring by July 2024.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to $23.3 million ($0.65 per share) from $8.2 million ($0.56 per share) in 2022
Operating expenses rose to $54 million from $39 million, including a $12.9-$13 million impairment that was nearly 60% of the loss
Q4 revenue declined sharply versus Q4 2022 as the FFS portfolio was wound down and large merchants were turned off
positive_highlights: Revenue was essentially flat year-over-year at $30.6 million versus $30.4 million, a 0.7% increase
Company reported no debt and approximately $19 million in assets
Insurance/entertainment expansion: added three baseball/entertainment teams and now serves roughly 1,800 Bodega distribution locations out of 32,000
summary: OLB reported FY2023 revenue of $30.6 million, essentially flat versus $30.4 million in 2022, with operating expenses rising to $54 million from $39 million and the net loss widening to $23.3 million ($0.65 per share) from $8.2 million ($0.56 per share). The loss was driven largely by a $12.9-$13 million impairment of the FFS portfolio acquired in Q4 2021, which was shut down in Q1 2024, plus increased legal, SG&A and salary costs. Management withdrew prior guidance on the DMINT spin-off timing, now pointing to completion around the filing of Q2 results subject to SEC review, and is pursuing litigation against FFS and Clear Fork Bank while planning a reverse split and insider share purchases. Management said it expects to stabilize the company in Q1 2024.

negative_highlights: Q4 net loss of $600k after removing audit charges reflects low revenue from the Sundry turnaround
Sundry's wholesale revenues hit a lowest point during the second half of FY23
Net income was only breakeven due to non-cash expenses, masking underlying weakness
positive_highlights: Gross margin increased 10.2% YoY due to significant non-cash audit write-downs that will not recur
Operating expense structure significantly lowered, with G&A excluding non-cash items down 35.7%
Management expects meaningful revenue re-acceleration in Q1 and Q2 based on wholesale bookings
summary: Net revenues increased 6.8% to $14.9 million for the full year and were flat excluding non-cash charges in Q4 ($3.5M vs $3.4M). Gross margins expanded significantly due to one-time audit-related write-downs, but underlying operating performance was weak with a net loss of only $600k after removing these specific charges on low revenue driven by the Sundry turnaround.

negative_highlights: NIM compressed to 3.24% and ROA fell to 0.65% as deposit costs rose, with cumulative cycle deposit beta at 61%
Avenue is well note weakness in of its $225 million deposit goal, now expected in Q3/Q4 with small Q2 progress at best
Published slide-deck error listed multifamily weighted-average LTV at 90% versus the correct 69%
positive_highlights: Net loans increased $22 million and total deposits $47 million in the quarter
Credit quality strong: net charge-offs of 0.03% of gross loans, non-performing loans at 0.5% of gross loans, criticized/classified at 2.12%
Legacy Avenue deposits produced $619,000 in interest and fees in Q1, covering almost two-thirds of Avenue's expenses
summary: Q1 EPS was $0.36 with an efficiency ratio of 76%, ROA of 0.65%, ROE of 5.97%, and NIM of 3.24%; results were down slightly quarter-over-quarter due to rising deposit costs, with cumulative cycle deposit beta at 61%. Net loans grew $22 million and total deposits $47 million, non-performing loans are 0.5% of gross loans with net charge-offs at 0.03%. Guidance calls for a 1.2% monthly expense run rate, low-single-digit loan growth, and an Avenue goal of $225 million in deposits and $2 million in fees for 2024, with breakeven targeted around $225 million in deposits. Management acknowledged Avenue deposits remain far from the 2024 goal and pushed the timeline to the second half, while a slide-deck error corrected multifamily weighted-average LTV from 90% to 69%.

negative_highlights: Net interest margin declined to 3.64% from 3.68%, with an estimated 9 bps decline excluding acquisition accounting accretion, and management expects continued pressure.
Total loans fell $29.1 million as $74 million of payoffs (55% from asset sales) offset $78 million of new fundings.
Non-interest-bearing deposits declined 1.1% and total cost of deposits rose 20 bps amid continued deposit pricing pressure.
positive_highlights: Loan pipeline increased to $300 million of probable fundings at March 31, up from $212 million at December 31, spread across 266 loans.
Efficiency ratio stayed below 60% for the 19th consecutive quarter at 55.6%, and tangible book value per share rose 3.2%.
Investor CRE loans fell $42.8 million while owner-occupied CRE and C&I loans grew a combined $15.4 million, advancing the balance-sheet repositioning.
summary: First Bank reported Q1 2024 net income of $12.5 million, or $0.50 per diluted share, with a 1.41% return on average assets. Adjusted diluted EPS was $0.49, essentially flat versus the prior quarter's $0.49, and the net interest margin compressed to 3.64% from 3.68% (down ~9 bps excluding acquisition accounting). Loans declined $29.1 million on $74 million of payoffs, largely asset sales, while the loan pipeline rose to $300 million from $212 million at year-end. Management offered no explicit EPS or revenue guidance, expected continued margin pressure from deposit costs, and reiterated a ~5% loan growth target for the year.

negative_highlights: Accrued a preliminary wildfire liability of $215 million related to the Smokehouse Creek fires in Texas.
Year-to-date electric sales decreased by 0.3% due to declining use per customer and timing delays for large C&I expansions.
positive_highlights: Earnings beat prior period by $0.12 due to rate reviews and lower O&M expenses including gains from a land sale.
summary: Xcel Energy reported Q1 FY2024 earnings of $0.88 per share versus the prior year's $0.76, driven by rate reviews and lower O&M expenses but offset by higher depreciation and interest charges. Management reaffirmed its full-year 2024 EPS guidance range of $3.50 to $3.60 per share despite a significant wildfire liability accrual in Texas. The company noted that year-to-date electric sales decreased slightly while natural gas sales increased, with revised projected annual growth expectations.

negative_highlights: Consolidated operating income down 29% in Q1, with HDMC down 29%
EMEA retail sales down 11% and APAC down 12%, with APAC declining for 3rd consecutive quarter
HDMC Q1 revenue down 5% due to lower wholesale volumes and pricing, with dealer inventory up 26% YoY
positive_highlights: North America retail sales up 6% in Q1, driven by new Street Glide/Road Glide touring models
LiveWire retail sales up 86% YoY and became #1 on-road EV motorcycle brand in the U.S.
Company returned $773M in buybacks and $214M in dividends since 2022; planned similar trajectory in 2024
summary: Harley-Davidson's Q1 2024 results were in line with expectations, with consolidated revenue down 3% and EPS of $1.72. North America retail sales grew 6% driven by new touring models, but EMEA and APAC declined 11% and 12% respectively. HDMC revenue fell 5% due to lower wholesale volume and pricing, partially offset by favorable mix. The company maintained its full-year HDMC guidance, while LiveWire improved its operating loss guidance to $105-115 million from $115-125 million.

negative_highlights: OpEx increased 7.9% YoY primarily due to a 3x increase in electricity prices starting February.
Mobile data users decreased by 1 million from December 2023 levels, reflecting industry-wide cooling.
Macro challenges including point-to-point inflation of 9.8% continue to strain customer purchasing power.
positive_highlights: EBITDA margin remained strong at 60.8% despite rising energy costs and inflation.
4G subscriber base grew significantly by 5 million (15.2%) to reach 38.2 million.
Total revenue growth of 5.3% YoY marks the 12th consecutive quarter of top-line growth.
summary: Grameenphone reported a solid Q1 FY2024 performance with total revenue growing 5.3% YoY and EBITDA rising 5% to maintain an industry-leading margin of 60.8%. The company added 2.9 million subscribers, reaching 83 million total, driven by a 15.2% increase in 4G data users despite macroeconomic headwinds like inflation and energy price hikes. Reported EPS stood at BDT 9.91, boosted by a one-off tax provision reversal.

negative_highlights: Combined ratio increased to 102.4% from 101.2% due to large fire losses
Strategic nonrenewals in Georgia and Alabama caused Commercial Lines growth to be slightly negative at -1%
Workers' compensation incurred $2.9 million of unfavorable reserve development
positive_highlights: Net premiums earned increased 5.8% to $227.7 million
Investment income rose 16.1% to $11 million with an average tax equivalent yield of 3.40%
Personal lines retention remained very strong at 107.2%
summary: Net premiums earned increased 5.8% to $227.7 million, driven by rate increases averaging 12% in total and 14% excluding workers' comp. However, the combined ratio deteriorated to 102.4% from 101.2% due to large fire losses and unfavorable reserve development in workers' compensation, resulting in an underwriting loss offset only by investment income. Management noted that strategic nonrenewals in Georgia and Alabama prevented achieving targeted underwriting profit levels.

negative_highlights: Intermodal revenue decreased 30.9% to $76.7 million due to a 14.1% volume decline and rate pressures.
Trucking segment revenues fell 12.6% with load haul down 7.1% and revenue per load excluding fuel surcharges down 6.2%.
Company-managed brokerage segment reported an operating loss of $2.5 million, compared to a smaller loss in the prior year.
positive_highlights: Contract logistics segment delivered outsized results with revenue increasing 48.4% to $313.5 million.
Record quarterly EPS of $1.99 and operating margin of 15.3%, the best in company history.
Management expects the new contract program to be substantially complete by January 2025.
summary: Universal Logistics Holdings reported Q1 FY2024 revenue of $491.9 million and EPS of $1.99, driven by a 48.4% surge in contract logistics revenue to $313.5 million due to a new program award. However, transactional segments faced significant headwinds with intermodal revenue down 30.9% and trucking revenue down 12.6%. Management provided Q2 guidance of $450-$475 million in revenue and 9%-11% operating margins, reflecting the ramp-down of the temporary contract logistics program.

negative_highlights: TV Media affiliate revenue declined 3% due to Pay-TV ecosystem declines
Domestic ARPU growth was negatively impacted by lower engagement following last year's strikes
Cash dividend will be reduced by approximately $55 million annually upon preferred stock conversion
positive_highlights: Total company revenue grew 6% to $7.7 billion
Adjusted OIBDA surged 80% year-over-year to $987 million
D2C subscription revenue expanded 22%, with Paramount+ adding 3.7M subscribers
summary: Paramount Global reported Q1 FY2024 total revenue of $7.7 billion (6% YoY growth) and adjusted OIBDA growing 80% to $987 million. The company highlighted strong advertising growth driven by the Super Bowl, with D2C subscription revenue up 22% led by Paramount+ adding 3.7M subscribers. Management expressed confidence in their new leadership team's strategic plan focused on hit content and balance sheet strengthening.

negative_highlights: Federal funding release in March means procurement timing likely pushes opportunities to Q3/Q4
Expected full-year cash burn of approximately $30 million
Bioprocessing recovery still awaited
positive_highlights: Revenue up 8% year-over-year in Q1
Acquisition of RedWave expected to be accretive to revenue, gross margins, and cash flow
Full-year revenue guidance raised to $63-$65 million, up 25%-29%
summary: First quarter revenue was $10 million, up 8% year-over-year, with robust demand for handheld devices. The company announced the acquisition of RedWave Technology, which is expected to add 2024 revenue and improve margins and cash flow breakeven. Full-year revenue guidance was raised to $63-$65 million (25%-29% growth), but management noted federal funding procurement timing is pushing some opportunities to Q3/Q4. Cash used in Q1 was $10 million, with full-year burn expected around $30 million.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined 7% year-over-year, driven specifically by a decrease in the number and average size of construction design-build projects.
Backlog decreased sequentially by $11 million (or 10%), with no new material contracts signed in Europe during Q1.
Management explicitly excluded potential upside from cannabis rescheduling or banking legislation changes from their full-year guidance.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA loss of $0.3 million beat quarterly guidance and represented a sequential improvement from the prior quarter's negative cash flow position.
Gross margin expanded significantly to 20% in Q1, driven by improved delivery on services projects and higher margins on new construction design-build work.
Operating expenses decreased sequentially by $1.2 million due to optimization efforts initiated in late 2023.
summary: Urban-Gro reported Q1 FY2024 revenue of $15.5 million (down 7% YoY) and an adjusted EBITDA loss of $0.3 million, which beat guidance but represented a sequential decline from the prior quarter's positive cash flow. Management maintained full-year 2024 revenue guidance at more than $84 million with no change to the outlook for returning to positive adjusted EBITDA by year-end. While CEO Brad Nattrass highlighted significant industry catalysts like potential cannabis rescheduling, he explicitly stated that these developments are not factored into current financial projections due to timing unknowns.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to $18 million in FY2023 from $12 million in FY2022
Auto Service segment growth was only 8% year over year, to $215 million from $199 million
No quantitative 2024 guidance was provided, only a general expectation of growth
positive_highlights: Total revenue rose 29% year over year to $364 million from $282 million
Auto e-Insurance revenue grew 79% to $149 million, including over 100% year-on-year growth tied to EV makers such as Tesla, NIO, XPeng and Li Auto
Adjusted EBITDA improved by $7.2 million to positive $1.6 million for FY2023
summary: SunCar reported FY2023 total revenue of $364 million, up 29% from $282 million in 2022, with Auto Service revenue up 8% to $215 million and Auto e-Insurance revenue up 79% to $149 million; e-Insurance Intermediation rose 75% to $118 million and Technology Service rose 98% to $31 million. Net loss widened to $18 million from a $12 million loss in 2022, though adjusted EBITDA turned positive at $1.6 million, an improvement of $7.2 million year over year. Management gave no explicit quantitative guidance, saying only that it expects another year of growth in 2024 and that e-Insurance should become the larger segment over time. The key change versus the prior period was the revenue growth and swing to positive adjusted EBITDA, offset by the larger net loss.

negative_highlights: Casino & Resorts adjusted EBITDA fell 15% YoY due to adverse January weather and bridge construction disruptions affecting Rhode Island visitation.
International Interactive revenue declined 4% YoY as the company strategically reduced marketing spend outside of its core U.K. market.
North America Interactive is expected to incur an adjusted EBITDA loss of approximately $30 million for FY2024.
positive_highlights: North America Interactive revenue surged 70% YoY to $41.5 million driven by strong iGaming performance in New Jersey, Pennsylvania, and Rhode Island.
International Interactive adjusted EBITDA margin expanded approximately 290 basis points to 36%, supported by robust U.K. operations which grew revenues 12% on a USD basis.
Chicago temporary facility GGR ramped significantly to over $13 million in March, representing greater than a 50% increase compared to December.
summary: First quarter revenues increased by 3% year-over-year to $618 million, driven by a 4.1% rise in the Casino & Resorts segment and a substantial 70% growth in North America Interactive, though International Interactive declined 4%. Management reiterated full-year guidance for revenue of $2.5B-$2.7B and adjusted EBITDAR of $655M-$695M despite challenges including January weather impacts on margins ($89.4M segment loss vs prior year) and the closure of Tropicana.

negative_highlights: Wireless revenue declined 2.3% YoY to $18.6 million, and management said wireless demand will continue to decline on a secular basis
Adjusted operating expenses rose $1.3 million YoY to $28.5 million, including a $0.6 million increase in cost of revenue and higher R&D
Full-year guidance was only reiterated, not raised, with Q2 facing a tough comparison against last year's $5 million single deal
positive_highlights: Software operations bookings of $7.9 million, up 39% YoY, with 19 six-figure contracts and 4 multi-year engagements
Software revenue up 15.3% to $16.3 million, with growth across maintenance, license, professional services and hardware
Adjusted EBITDA up 9.2% to $7.5 million, covering the $6.3 million returned to stockholders; net unit churn fell to 1.6% from 2.5% in the prior quarter
summary: Spok reported Q1 2024 revenue of $34.9 million, up 5.1% YoY from $33.2 million, with software revenue up 15.3% to $16.3 million while wireless revenue fell 2.3% to $18.6 million. GAAP net income was $4.2 million or $0.21 per diluted share versus $3.1 million or $0.15 a year ago, and adjusted EBITDA rose 9.2% to $7.5 million. Software operations bookings of $7.9 million grew 39% YoY, the second-highest Q1 in company history, including 19 six-figure contracts. Management reiterated full-year 2024 guidance of $136-144 million revenue and $27.5-32.5 million adjusted EBITDA, and said it still expects double-digit full-year software bookings growth.

negative_highlights: Fee-paying AUM declined in both private equity and credit, with elevated outflows in credit.
Net accrued carry balance of $2.2 billion declined from the prior quarter due to realizations and lower appreciation; CP VII fell out of carry.
G&A expenses of $80 million benefited from one-time items and seasonality, and are expected to rise back toward normal run-rate, implying lower FRE margin in future quarters.
positive_highlights: Record quarterly FRE of $266 million, up nearly 40% year-over-year, and record FRE margin of 47%, up from 35% in Q1 2023.
DE of $1.01 per share, the best quarterly result since 2022; realized proceeds of $5.9 billion, the highest since Q4 2022.
AUM of $425 billion, up 12% year-over-year, with $5.3 billion of new capital raised, in line with expectations.
summary: Carlyle reported record Q1 FY2024 FRE of $266 million, up nearly 40% year-over-year, and record FRE margin of 47%, up from 35% in Q1 2023. DE was $431 million or $1.01 per share, the best quarterly result since 2022. Assets under management reached $425 billion, up 12% year-over-year, with $5.3 billion raised in the quarter, in line with expectations; management reiterated its full-year 2024 targets of $1.1 billion FRE, 40-50% FRE margin, and $40 billion of inflows. Management expects fundraising, deployment, and realization to accelerate through the year, though the fundraising environment for Global Private Equity remains somewhat challenging.

negative_highlights: Management explicitly stated there is a 'lull' in acquisition opportunities and less inventory being shown compared to the prior year.
The company has no ATM open for share repurchases or new capital raising at this time, citing market conditions requiring patience.
positive_highlights: Rental income increased 15.4% year-over-year driven by portfolio growth from industrial manufacturing property acquisitions.
summary: Modiv Industrial reported Q1 FY24 rental income of $11.9 million (up 15.4% YoY) and adjusted funds from operations (AFFO) of $3.3 million (up 6.6% YoY). Management provided no specific financial guidance but described the quarter as 'straightforward' while emphasizing a strategic focus on partnership discussions rather than active acquisitions due to market volatility.

negative_highlights: Subscription revenues declined 4% year-over-year due to a higher mix of lower-priced commitment periods and fewer sign-ups for behavioral offerings.
The company recorded noncash impairment charges totaling approximately $258 million related to franchise rights acquired balances, impacting GAAP EPS significantly.
Full-year adjusted operating income guidance remains flat at $100-$110 million with no raise despite margin expansion.
positive_highlights: Adjusted gross margin hit a record high of 68%, up from 57.1% the prior year, driven by fixed cost reductions and mix shift.
Activation rate trended positively with Q1 reaching its highest level since 2020, indicating improved engagement in core programs.
Clinical subscribers grew to 91,000 at quarter-end, exceeding guidance of 85,000 despite supply constraints on GLP-1 medications.
summary: WW reported Q1 FY2024 revenue of $207 million and adjusted gross margin of 68%, driven by a record high margin but offset by subscription revenues declining 4% year-over-year due to mix shifts. The company recorded significant noncash impairment charges of approximately $258 million related to franchise rights, resulting in an adjusted operating loss of $6 million for the quarter. Management maintained full-year revenue guidance between $830-$860 million and clinical subscriber targets despite softness in new sign-ups attributed to intentional marketing spend shifts.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined year-over-year from $17.8M to $17.1M.
R&D expense guidance increased, reflecting higher spending on immunology and RSV acceleration.
Management remains vague on exact enrollment status for RSV studies and declined to provide specific efficacy thresholds for upcoming data.
positive_highlights: Net loss narrowed year-over-year from $37.7M to $31.2M.
Cash position remains strong at ~$300M, with runway through fiscal Q3 2027.
RSV pediatric study RSVPEDs nearing completion of final cohort, with data expected in H2 2024.
summary: Enanta's fiscal Q2 2024 revenue was $17.1M, down from $17.8M in the prior year, with a net loss of $31.2M ($1.47 per diluted share), an improvement from the $37.7M loss a year earlier. R&D expenses decreased to $35.6M from $43.5M, partly due to reduced COVID spending, but G&A rose to $14.2M. Management updated FY2024 expense guidance upward, with R&D now expected between $125M and $145M and G&A between $50M and $60M. Key upcoming data readouts include EDP-323 Phase IIa challenge data in Q3 2024 and RSVPEDs data in H2 2024.

negative_highlights: Book value per common share declined modestly from $4.53 to $4.49, and was estimated down an additional 3% by Friday.
EAD ($0.13/share) remained under the dividend level of $0.15/share in the near term due to market environment constraints.
positive_highlights: Repurchased approximately $9.3 million of Series B preferred shares to stabilize equity profile and reduce dividend obligations as the series transitions to floating rate.
MSR portfolio net CPR averaged 3.9% with a low recapture rate of ~1%, indicating minimal refinancing incentive in the high-rate environment.
summary: For Q1 FY2024, CHMI reported GAAP net income of $9.7 million ($0.32 per share) and earnings available for distribution (EAD) of $4 million ($0.13 per share), resulting in a book value decline to $4.49 due to market volatility from the Fed pausing rate cuts. Management maintained financial leverage at 4.5x while repurchasing Series B preferred shares, but also announced a special committee exploring strategic alternatives without providing specific guidance on future dividends or capital structure changes.

negative_highlights: Net revenue fell 42% YoY to $20.2 million, with sustained revenue down 36% YoY to $18.2 million
Q2 2024 revenue guidance of $20–23 million implies a ~39% YoY decline at the midpoint
Q2 adjusted EBITDA is still guided to a loss of $1–2 million, no product launches in Q1, and pricing pressure persists in discretionary categories
positive_highlights: Gross margin expanded to 65.1% from 54.8% a year ago and 51% in Q4 2023, the highest as a public company
Net loss improved 80% YoY to $5.2 million, and adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed 38.4% YoY to $2.6 million
Inventory reduced to $18.5 million from $40.4 million a year ago, and credit facility balance cut to $9.4 million from $19.1 million
summary: Aterian reported Q1 FY2024 net revenue of $20.2 million, down 42% YoY, with gross margin expanding to 65.1% (vs. 54.8% a year ago and 51% in Q4 2023) and contribution margin of 14.1% (vs. 5.9% YoY). Net loss improved 80% to $5.2 million and adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed 38.4% to $2.6 million, but no guidance was provided for Q2 adjusted EBITDA profitability until H2 2024. Q2 revenue guidance of $20–23 million implies a ~39% YoY decline at the midpoint, though on a SKU-rationalized basis the decline would be ~15%. The company reaffirmed its target of adjusted EBITDA profitability in H2 2024 and expects gross margin to moderate to the high 50s/low 60s as seasonal products re-enter the mix.

negative_highlights: Revenue decreased by approximately $700,000 year-over-year due to a sharp decline in specimen volume.
Average cost per specimen increased by 44% from $133 to $191 despite lower volumes.
Cash and cash equivalents declined significantly from $5 million at December 31, 2023 to approximately $2.6 million as of March 31, 2024.
