positive_highlights: Next-Day Quotes Program conversion rate increased to 50% in Q1 from 34% in Q4, with prospective purchase order dollar value up 190% quarter-over-quarter.
Supplier network refresh reduced the supplier count from 243 to 140 while maintaining or increasing supply capabilities through deeper collaboration.
Cash burn excluding one-time charges improved significantly to approximately $1.2 million for the quarter.
summary: iSpecimen reported Q1 FY2024 revenue of approximately $2.3 million, a decrease from the prior year's $3 million due to a 39% drop in specimen count (5,241 vs 8,629), partially offset by an average watching price increase of 28%. Management highlighted significant cost reductions and improved cash burn but noted that revenue guidance for H2 is not explicitly raised despite operational improvements.

negative_highlights: Heart failure revenue decreased 38% due to lower utilization and console sales
Capital sales lower than expected in Q1
Cash only $1.4 million at quarter end, requiring financing
positive_highlights: Pediatric revenue grew 40% with consumable utilization up 54%
Gross margin improved to 64.1% from 58.4%
Operating loss narrowed by $1.1 million year-over-year
summary: Nuwellis reported Q1 2024 revenue of $1.9 million, up 2% year-over-year, driven by an 11% increase in consumable utilization despite lower console sales. Pediatric category grew 40%, while heart failure revenue declined 38%. Gross margin improved to 64.1% from 58.4%, and operating loss narrowed to $4.7 million from $5.8 million. The company ended the quarter with $1.4 million cash and raised $2.4 million net in an April offering, expecting cash runway into early fall. Management cited robust pipeline for capital sales in 2024 but noted continued lumpiness.

negative_highlights: Financial results were flat year-over-year, indicating no growth in Q1.
Sales from new products and additional sales associates are expected to ramp a few quarters behind initial cost, pressuring near-term margins.
Net debt of $40 million expected to increase through the year due to planned investments.
positive_highlights: Operating cash flow increased 50% YoY to $12 million from $8 million.
Returned $18 million to stockholders through dividends and stock repurchases in Q1.
Management outlined a clear strategy to double TAM via expanded product portfolio and generative AI overlay.
summary: Q1 FY2024 results were consistent with expectations and relatively flat year-over-year. Operating cash flow increased to $12 million from $8 million in the prior year. The company returned $18 million to stockholders via dividends and buybacks and had $40 million in net debt at quarter end. Management reiterated its long-term goals of doubling TAM, achieving double-digit revenue growth, and expanding margins, while noting increased IT/AI investment and a sales force build over the next 2-3 years.

negative_highlights: A pipe fracture inside the FLNG 1 cold box on April 26 released perlite and delayed first LNG, which had been expected within roughly 72 hours of the incident.
Q1 capex was about $680 million, including roughly $140 million on FLNG 1, keeping full-year gross capex near the prior $1.5 billion expectation.
Management declined to give clear earnings guidance, saying investors are 'probably a quarter away' from country-by-country data and that modeling the transition period is difficult.
positive_highlights: Q1 EBITDA of $340 million came in on top of management's estimates and kept full-year guidance on track (unchanged).
New Puerto Rico contract lifts contracted volumes from 25 TBtu to 105 TBtu with a longer (4-year) term, versus the ended 40 TBtu FEMA arrangement.
Brazil now runs 12 MTPA of LNG import capacity across two online terminals, supporting about $500 million of contracted 2026 run-rate EBITDA, with a planned minority sale and possible IPO in 2024.
summary: NFE reported Q1 2024 EBITDA of $340 million, which management said was right on top of estimates and tracking toward full-year guidance, with no change to that guidance. The quarter's biggest developments were structural rather than financial: a new 80 TBtu island-wide Puerto Rico gas contract (lifting total contracted volumes to 105 TBtu) replacing the ended FEMA arrangement, two Brazil LNG terminals now online carrying about $500 million of run-rate 2026 contracted EBITDA, and FLNG 1 in final commissioning with first cargo targeted for June. Management flagged a pipe fracture inside the FLNG 1 cold box on April 26, expected to be repaired within roughly a week, delaying first LNG by a short period. No updated EPS, revenue, or full-year EBITDA figures were given on the call.

negative_highlights: Domains EBITDA declined 3.2% YoY due to cybersecurity and timing costs
Ting EBITDA remains negative at -$9.5 million, with Q1 operating cash flow negative $5.7 million
Net loss widened to $26.5 million ($2.42 per share) from $19.1 million a year ago
positive_highlights: Consolidated revenue up 8.7% YoY, with all three businesses contributing to dollar gains
Adjusted EBITDA up 38.7% YoY to $4.2 million, driven by Wavelo
Ting added 2,700 net subscribers, up 25.6% YoY, reaching 46,000 total
summary: Tucows reported Q1 2024 revenue of $87.5 million, up 8.7% YoY, with gross margin up 30.3% to $18.3 million and adjusted EBITDA up 38.7% to $4.2 million. Domains grew modestly but EBITDA fell 3.2%, Wavelo's EBITDA surged on DISH migration, and Ting subscriber growth was strong but EBITDA remained negative. Management remains cautious on public market capital for fiber, moderating capital spending and highlighting deleveraging while signaling a focus on cash-generating businesses.

negative_highlights: FYARRO net product sales fell 8.8% year over year to $5.4 million
Net loss widened to $18.3 million from $15.2 million a year ago
R&D expenses increased to $13.6 million from $11 million a year ago
positive_highlights: PRECISION1 trial now fully enrolled, with the next interim analysis (80 patients, independent assessment) expected in Q3 2024
Cash, cash equivalents and note weakness in-term investments of $88.3 million fund operations into Q4 2025
SG&A declined to $10.6 million from $11.2 million a year ago on lower legal and consulting costs
summary: Aadi Bioscience reported Q1 FY2024 FYARRO net product sales of $5.4 million, down 8.8% year over year, which management attributed to distributor ordering patterns and fewer new commercial patient initiations. R&D expenses rose to $13.6 million from $11 million a year ago on PRECISION1 and Phase II progress, while SG&A fell to $10.6 million from $11.2 million, and net loss widened to $18.3 million from $15.2 million. Management said it expects a return to FYARRO sales growth in Q2 and remains on track for the PRECISION1 interim readout in Q3 2024, with cash runway into Q4 2025. The company also terminated its adagrasib collaboration with Mirati/BMS to prioritize the EEC and NETs Phase II programs.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined 28% year-over-year to $39 million, reflecting lower demand, full-price transition, and distributor/store changes.
Adjusted EBITDA remained negative at a loss guided for Q2 of $20-17 million and full year of $78-63 million.
Operating cash use was $26 million in the quarter, including $4 million inventory build and $2 million lease exit costs.
positive_highlights: Gross margin expanded 680 basis points year-over-year to 46.9% on cost savings, healthier inventory, and reduced promotions.
Inventory fell 45% year-over-year to $61 million, and the company closed the quarter with $102 million in cash and no outstanding borrowings.
The Tree Runner Go launch had the highest two-week performance of any product in almost two years, with robust conversion in men's and women's.
summary: Q1 revenue of $39 million fell 28% year-over-year, but gross margin expanded 680 basis points to 46.9% and adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed despite the sales decline, with results meeting revenue guidance and exceeding adjusted EBITDA guidance. Full-year guidance was reiterated: revenue of $190-210 million, gross margin of 42-45%, and adjusted EBITDA loss of $78-63 million, incorporating a $32-37 million headwind from store closures and international distributor transitions. Q2 revenue is guided to $48-53 million with adjusted EBITDA loss of $20-17 million; management expects a Q4 top-line inflection from new product and marketing, and noted heavy promotional activity was avoided. The key change is the continued strategic shift to full-price watching and a distributor model, which is intentionally pressuring near-term sales.

negative_highlights: Total revenue declined 2% year-over-year due to a 17% drop in Watsons/other B2B sales
New vertical product launches are taking longer than initially anticipated per management commentary
Net loss widened slightly to $0.5 million compared to the prior quarter's adjusted performance
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA turned positive at $0.7 million for the fourth consecutive quarter
Gross margins expanded 80 basis points to 60.7% driven by a shift toward higher-margin e-commerce sales (58% of total)
New retail partnerships with Sprouts Farmers Market and Vitamin Shoppe launched in Q1, expanding distribution beyond previous channels
summary: ChromaDex reported Q1 FY2024 revenue of $22.2 million, a 2% decline year-over-year driven by lower B2B sales and the absence of a major Amazon brand campaign compared to last year. The company achieved positive adjusted EBITDA of $0.7 million but reiterated full-year guidance unchanged from prior expectations despite acknowledging that new vertical launches are taking longer than anticipated. Management emphasized cost discipline, improved marketing efficiency, and strong cash flow while noting R&D investments will remain heavy in the first half before moderating.

negative_highlights: Net loss increased to approximately $29.6 million from $25.3 million in the prior-year quarter.
A $4.8 million noncash charge was recorded for the change in fair value of tranche rights related to the January 2024 financing.
Other income swung to negative $2.1 million from positive $1.2 million in the prior-year period, partly due to $1.7 million in financing-related costs.
positive_highlights: $97.3 million in cash and cash equivalents at March 31, 2024, expected to fund operations into Q3 2025.
R&D expenses decreased to $18.7 million from $22.9 million in the prior-year quarter, mainly due to lower clinical development costs.
Interim CALLIPER analysis showed separation from placebo in serum neurofilament light chain levels across all PMS patients and subtypes, supporting neuroprotective potential.
summary: Immunic reported Q1 2024 R&D expenses of $18.7 million (down from $22.9 million in Q1 2023) and a net loss of approximately $29.6 million, or $0.30 per share, versus a net loss of $25.3 million, or $0.58 per share, in the prior-year period. The company ended the quarter with $97.3 million in cash and cash equivalents, which it expects to fund operations into Q3 2025. No revenue or product guidance was provided, as the company is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical firm, but management reiterated timelines for key clinical readouts: Phase II CALLIPER top-line data expected April 2025, a Phase III ENSURE interim futility analysis later this year, and the first ENSURE trial readout in Q2 2026.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined 9.9% YoY to $37.1M with gross margin contracting by 230 bps to 34.5% due to product mix shifts.
Net loss widened from -$2.9M in Q1 FY2023 to -$7.1M, including ~$940k in severance charges and $2.6M net other expense.
Management lowered full-year revenue outlook expectations citing a maturing market with declining global IFPD shipments.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA of +$0.2M significantly exceeded the prior negative expectation of -$3M due to cost savings and operational focus.
CEO Dale Strang delivered his first full quarter as CEO, confirming beliefs in company execution despite market softness.
Primary lender extended an additional $2 million bridge loan for seasonal working capital needs.
summary: Q1 FY2024 revenue was $37.1 million (down 9.9% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA beat guidance at +$0.2M versus a prior expectation of -$3M, driven by cost reductions including ~$5M in fixed costs eliminated and severance charges recorded. Management maintained full-year flat revenue guidance but lowered Q2 revenue expectations to $43-45 million (down from implied higher levels) while keeping adjusted EBITDA guidance at $2-3 million.

negative_highlights: Comparable RevPAR decreased 1% YoY and AFFO per diluted share was negative $0.35
March RevPAR was down ~300 bps, with softness in Northeast destination markets and airport hotels; April's ~3% revenue growth was partly calendar-shift driven
Company does not anticipate reinstating a common dividend in 2024, and it transferred possession/control of KEYS loan pool hotels to a receiver, eliminating further economic interest
positive_highlights: Group rooms revenue for the balance of 2024 is pacing up 8% YoY, and 2025 group pace is ahead by 15%
Non-traded preferred offering has raised ~$122 million gross to date, including $23 million in Q1, with 43 dealer agreements signed
Asset sales and refinancings progressing: three assets sold, three under PSA and five under LOI, representing roughly $625 million combined, with ~50% of the ~$107 million strategic financing repaid
summary: Q1 2024 comparable RevPAR fell 1% YoY and AFFO per diluted share was negative $0.35, though GAAP net income was $67.4 million ($0.60/share) and adjusted EBITDAre was $59.5 million. Management emphasized deleveraging progress on the ~$107 million remaining strategic financing, with about 50% repaid, three assets under PSA and five under LOI totaling roughly $625 million in potential proceeds, plus ~$122 million raised in the non-traded preferred offering to date. March was soft (RevPAR down ~300 bps) with April revenue up ~3%, attributed partly to calendar shifts and weather; group pace for the remainder of 2024 is up 8% and 2025 group pace is up 15%. The company does not anticipate reinstating a common dividend in 2024 and continues to transfer assets via foreclosure (KEYS loan pools) and refinance several loans.

negative_highlights: Adjusted loss of $98M includes a $366M unfavorable notable item from a retroactive reinsurance premium rate increase, reducing TAC by ~$300M.
Normalized statutory earnings were pressured by actual-to-expected changes in the in-force annuity block and by SHIELD growth now consuming capital.
Annuity net outflows were ~$1.5B in the quarter, with elevated surrenders expected to continue through 2024.
positive_highlights: SHIELD annuity sales grew 20% YoY to $1.9B, with total annuity sales up 3% YoY to $2.9B.
Holding company liquid assets remain robust at $1.3B, with no debt maturities until 2027.
Excluding notable items, adjusted EPS of $4.25 was in line with expectations and above the company's normal run-rate of ~$4.
summary: Q1 2024 adjusted loss was $98M including a $366M unfavorable notable item from a retroactive reinsurance premium rate increase; excluding notables, adjusted earnings were $268M ($4.25/share), in line with expectations. Annuity sales totaled $2.9B, up 3% YoY, with SHIELD sales up 20% YoY to $1.9B. Management expects 2024 full-year corporate expenses to be lower than 2023. Statutory TAC fell ~$300M to $6B, and RBC ratio is estimated at 415%-435%.

negative_highlights: Adjusted NII declined to $1.00 per share for the fiscal year from $1.10 in the prior year
Quarterly net investment income fell to $5.3 million from $9.7 million, and adjusted NII per share declined to $0.24 from $0.26
Two portfolio companies remained on nonaccrual status, and management described deal opportunity quality as spotty with competitors paying 8x-9x EBITDA versus its 6x-7.5x target range
positive_highlights: Portfolio fair value increased to $921 million from $754 million at the prior year-end, driven by $184 million of investments versus $134 million in the prior year
NAV per share rose to $13.43 from $13.01 in the prior quarter
Total distributions of $2.20 per share for the fiscal year, with monthly distributions at a $0.96 per share annual run rate and $1.24 per share in supplemental distributions
summary: Fiscal Q4 FY2024 total investment income was $23.6 million, up modestly from $23.1 million in the prior quarter, but net investment income fell to $5.3 million from $9.7 million due to a $4.1 million increase in accrued capital gains-based incentive fees; adjusted NII was $8.8 million or $0.24 per share versus $9.1 million or $0.26 per share. Full-year total investment income rose to $87.3 million from $81.5 million, while adjusted NII declined to $34.5 million or $1.00 per share from $36.7 million or $1.10 per share. NAV increased to $13.43 per share from $13.01, the portfolio fair value grew to $921 million from $754 million, and the company paid $2.20 per share in total distributions for the year. Management cited a strong deal pipeline and backlog but noted competitive pricing and did not provide formal forward guidance.

negative_highlights: Gross margin was pressured by a significant increase in employment taxes in New York, which impacted the year-over-year comparison.
positive_highlights: Consolidated gross profit grew 7.1% YoY from $19.0 million to $20.4 million despite a deliberate reduction in Health Care services revenue.
Adjusted EBITDA increased 11.1% YoY, reaching $6.8 million, with Engineering segment showing strong double-digit growth of 27.1%.
School revenue grew by 19.1% to $31.9 million after removing COVID impact from the prior year comparison.
summary: RCM Technologies reported Q1 FY2024 consolidated gross profit growth of 7.1% to $20.4 million and adjusted EBITDA growth of 11.1% to $6.8 million. Adjusted diluted EPS grew by 30.4% from $0.41 to $0.53, driven largely by Engineering gross profit up 27.1%, while Health Care was impacted by a deliberate reduction in services to a slow-paying client and employment tax increases. Management raised full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance expectations to at least low double-digit growth compared to fiscal 2023.

negative_highlights: Gross profit was slightly below prior quarter and prior year due to product mix.
GoodWheat expansion requires significant upfront investment in promotions and slotting.
Management described retailer execution results as 'mixed' with some accounts struggling.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew sequentially by 7% and year-over-year by 2%.
Loss from continuing operations dropped to approximately $3.1 million, the lowest in six years.
Zola coconut water unit sales and dollar sales increased 10% versus last year.
summary: Q1 FY2024 revenue was approximately $1.3 million, representing a 7% sequential increase and a 2% year-over-year increase driven by GoodWheat and Zola sales. Gross margins remained healthy at 35%, while operating expenses declined 21% year-over-year to $3.5 million, resulting in a loss from continuing operations of approximately $3.1 million, the lowest level in six years. Management reaffirmed guidance for 2024 net operating losses under $10 million and reiterated that cash use will remain in single digits.

negative_highlights: Comparable RevPAR was flat year-over-year at $368, with urban assets down slightly and a challenging comparison from a $2.2 million prior-year property tax refund at Sofitel Chicago.
Four Seasons Resort Scottsdale RevPAR fell 1.4% due to difficult comparisons from last year's Super Bowl and Phoenix Open occurring in the same week.
Cameo Beverly Hills and Yountville (Napa) markets showed softness, with LA market occupancy, ADR, and RevPAR all down, and Napa pressured by tech layoffs and aggressive luxury rate discounting.
positive_highlights: Ritz-Carlton Reserve Dorado Beach RevPAR grew 23.4% year-over-year to $2,162 with 65% occupancy and $3,302 ADR, and achieved a 10.7% trailing 12-month yield on cost.
Group rooms revenue for the full year is pacing 3% ahead of last year, with Q2-to-Q4 pacing up 7% and 2025 group pace ahead by 10%.

Announced $165 million sale of Hilton La Jolla Torrey Pines with a non-refundable $6 million deposit, plus $50 million preferred redemption and $50 million common buyback, and refinanced/extended almost all 2024 debt maturities.
summary: Braemar reported Q1 2024 comparable RevPAR of $368, essentially flat year-over-year, with net income of $3.5 million ($0.05 per diluted share) and AFFO per diluted share of $0.42. Hotel EBITDA was $71 million, with luxury resorts delivering $65 million and positive RevPAR growth, though urban assets were pressured by a prior-year $2.2 million property tax refund and softness in Los Angeles and Napa. Management announced a shareholder value creation plan including the $165 million sale of the Hilton La Jolla Torrey Pines, a $50 million preferred redemption, and a $50 million common buyback, and has refinanced or extended nearly all 2024 debt maturities. Guidance was not explicitly updated, with management expressing optimism on group pace and margin expansion.

negative_highlights: Total revenue decreased 9% to $70.5 million due to high interest rates suppressing transaction volume.
Real Estate division adjusted EBITDA declined by $0.5 million to $0.8 million following the sale of DIA and internal technology charges.
The company continues to operate with a cash burn, reducing operational cash burn to approximately $974,000 in Q1.
positive_highlights: Gross profit margin expanded 160 basis points to 10.3% due to fee resets and ancillary business growth.
Encompass Lending Group revenue surged 55% to $2.3 million with file starts up 114% year-over-year.
Verus Title revenue increased 9.5% to $652,000 following the launch of a joint venture.
summary: Fathom Holdings reported Q1 FY2024 total revenue of $70.5 million, a 9% year-over-year decline driven by a 10.6% drop in brokerage revenue and lower transaction volume (7,703 transactions vs 8,532 last year). Gross profit margin expanded 160 basis points to 10.3%, aided by fee resets and ancillary business growth, while GAAP net loss narrowed slightly to $5.9 million. The company sold its DIA insurance business for approximately $8 million upfront cash and provided Q2 guidance of total revenue between $86 million and $89 million with adjusted EBITDA expected to turn positive in the range of $0.2 million to $0.5 million.

negative_highlights: Total consolidated revenues declined by 2.1 million year-over-year, driven primarily by a drop in Marketing Services and Fulfillment & Logistics segments.
Fulfillment & Logistics revenue fell to $19.4 million due to cost compression from reduced overall market demand in the logistics space.
Cash balance decreased significantly to $11.5 million from $18.4 million at year-end 2023, though no debt was drawn on the line of credit.
positive_highlights: Adjusted operating margin expanded to 3.9% from 3.4% in the prior year due to cost savings and efficiency initiatives under Project Elevate.
Same-store revenue performance improved significantly, marking the best result among the past five quarters at a decline of only 3.5%.
New Sales Services segment generated $4.7 million in revenue with growth potential estimated up to $9 million over the next couple of years.
summary: Harte Hanks reported Q1 FY2024 revenue of $45.4 million, a decline of 3.5% year-over-year compared to $47.1 million in the prior period. Adjusted operating income was $1.8 million versus $1.6 million last year, while adjusted EBITDA grew slightly from $2.7 million to $2.8 million despite higher restructuring expenses related to Project Elevate.

negative_highlights: Management expects gross margin percentage to decrease in future quarters due to higher concentration of ALLY sales (currently priced lower than legacy systems).
Company does not provide forward financial guidance for the full year or subsequent quarters.
Cash balance declined from $24.6M at year-end to $19.1M as of March 31, reflecting seasonal cash usage.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 28% YoY to $10.6M driven by strong procedure volume and system placements.
Gross margin expanded to 53%, up from 52% in the prior year quarter.
Net loss narrowed significantly to $2.2 million, a 50% decrease compared to Q1 FY2023.
summary: Revenue reached $10.6 million in Q1 FY2024, representing a 28% year-over-year increase driven by ALLY system placements and procedure growth exceeding 25%. The company reported a gross margin of 53% on the quarter while reducing its net loss to $2.2 million from $4.3 million in the prior year period. Management expressed confidence in sustaining top-line growth expectations despite noting that future margins may compress as ALLY sales concentration increases.

negative_highlights: Core FFO fell to $0.36 per share from $0.45 a year earlier, and revenue declined to $47.2 million from $50.2 million
Occupancy was 75.8% at quarter end, with management expecting to carry substantial vacancy for the foreseeable future
Management could not forecast when or if the 694,000-square-foot, roughly $46 million Deerfield sale will close, and the Arch Street JV may be unable to satisfy extension conditions
positive_highlights: Year-to-date leasing reached 522,000 square feet of new and renewal deals, more than double the prior year
The U.S. government exercised a 4-year renewal option on all 413,000 square feet at the Covington, Kentucky property
Total liquidity of $258.3 million after a credit facility amendment rightsized borrowing capacity and modified covenants
summary: Q1 revenue fell to $47.2 million from $50.2 million a year earlier, and core FFO dropped to $0.36 per share from $0.45, while the net loss widened to $26.2 million (-$0.47 per share) from $8.9 million. Results included $3.8 million of one-time revenues, of which $1.6 million of tax reimbursements had not been expected until next year. Management reaffirmed full-year core FFO guidance of $0.93-$1.01 per share, G&A of $19.5-$20.5 million, and net debt to adjusted EBITDA of 6.2x-7.0x. Positives included 522,000 square feet of leasing year-to-date, more than double last year, and a 4-year, 413,000-square-foot U.S. government renewal at Covington, Kentucky, but management continued to flag a difficult leasing environment, elevated vacancy, and the Deerfield sale timing as uncertain.

negative_highlights: Bath Furniture segment faced subdued demand and trade-downs
GAAP operating income turned negative $0.3M due to higher growth investments
Operating expenses increased significantly from $7.2M to $8.7M
positive_highlights: Revenue grew robustly 13.2% YoY to $31 million
Gross margin expanded 90 bps to 27.4%
Pro Sanitaryware business rebounded as inventory levels moderated
summary: FGI reported Q1 FY2024 revenue of $31 million (up 13.2% YoY) and gross margin expansion to 27.4%, driven by growth in Shower Systems and pro Sanitaryware segments, while Bath Furniture remained weak due to trade-down trends. Management maintained full-year guidance for adjusted operating income ($2.8M-$3.8M) despite GAAP operating loss of $0.3M caused by increased investment expenses.

negative_highlights: Net loss of $5.4 million persists, though improved from $6.2 million in the prior year
BOLSTER trial arms for head/neck and esophageal cancers terminated due to feasibility issues
Funding for iGoLSTA trial pending partner funding; timelines subject to change
positive_highlights: Cash runway extended into early 2026, covering all planned data milestones
Enrollment in BOLSTER cholangiocarcinoma arm expected to complete by year-end, possibly sooner
Received orphan and rare pediatric disease designations for osteosarcoma, adding potential priority review voucher
summary: Lisata reported Q1 2024 operating expenses of $6.6 million, down 3.6% YoY, and a net loss of $5.4 million, improved from $6.2 million a year ago. Cash stood at $43.3 million, with funding expected into early 2026. Management highlighted progress across multiple clinical trials, with top-line data from the Phase 2b ASCEND trial expected in Q4 2024, and emphasized increased partner interest as data approaches.

Revenue rose to $72.3 million from $71.5 million, but nightclub same-store sales fell $2.9 million and Bombshells revenue declined $1.5 million YoY with segment operating margin collapsing to 5.5% from 12.4%. GAAP EPS of $0.08 reflected an $8 million impairment; non-GAAP EPS was $0.90, near the high end of analyst expectations. Non-GAAP operating margin fell to 33.4% from 39.3% on lower service revenue, higher insurance, Texas patron tax and wage inflation, and management gave no formal guidance while flagging that April was down and the Central City gaming timeline is 18 months to 2 years out. Management is refocusing on capital allocation, rebranding underperforming clubs, and targeting under 9 million shares outstanding through buybacks.

negative_highlights: Revenue fell 44% year-over-year to $197 million and adjusted contribution margin was only 1% on lower fixed-asset utilization
Adjusted EBITDA loss was $49 million and GAAP net loss was $97 million in the quarter
Total private jet Flight Transaction Value declined 26% year-over-year with demand described as weak in January and February
positive_highlights: Prepaid blocks rose 14% year-over-year to $114 million, with corporate block sales the highest share of total blocks in company history
Total charter FTV grew 25% year-over-year and reached 54% of total flight transaction value
Operational metrics hit internal goals: 98% completion rate, 87% on-time performance, and 27 brand days (highest in over two years)
summary: Revenue fell 44% year-over-year to $197 million, driven by exit of aircraft management and sales, reduced programmatic flying areas, and weaker industry demand; total private jet Flight Transaction Value was down 26% and adjusted contribution margin was just 1%. Adjusted EBITDA loss was $49 million, roughly flat year-over-year, with a GAAP net loss of $97 million and liquidity plus reserve deposits of $301 million. Prepaid blocks rose 14% year-over-year to $114 million with corporate blocks at the highest percentage of total blocks in company history, and charter FTV grew 25%, but management again deferred the positive adjusted EBITDA target to later this year without explicit numeric guidance.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened significantly from a prior quarter's income due to non-cash unrealized losses on commodity derivatives as prices increased.
Q1 lease operating expenses rose to $38.3 million, driven by one-time adjustments and scheduled maintenance costs.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA of $24.9 million exceeded expectations, demonstrating resilience despite a net loss from derivative accounting impacts.
Free cash flow guidance was raised following the generation of $2.3 million in Q1 free cash flow.
Sinking fund obligations were successfully restructured to lower annual payments by approximately $7 million.
summary: Amplify Energy reported Q1 FY2024 adjusted EBITDA of $24.9 million and free cash flow of $2.3 million, both exceeding expectations despite a net loss driven by unrealized derivative losses due to rising crude prices. Management increased its annual guidance for WTI at $78/bbl and Henry Hub at $2.25/MMBtu based on the strong quarter and higher forecasted commodity prices. The company accelerated certain capital projects in Q1 but maintains that full-year LOE will remain within original ranges as one-time costs normalize.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA loss increased quarter-over-quarter to $22.1 million; total cash burn was $29.2 million, including large annual payments.
Biorefining revenue declined year-over-year to $5.0 million due to the uneven nature of early-stage project revenues.
A registration statement on Form S-3 with a $100 million at-the-market offering was filed, despite the company stating no current plans to utilize it.
positive_highlights: Gross margin expanded to 34%, up approximately 570 basis points over the full year 2023 gross margin, driven by higher-margin engineering services and JDA/contract revenue.
Gross profit improved 87% year-over-year to $3.5 million.
Full year 2024 revenue guidance of $90-$105 million was reiterated, with a projected 20-40% quarter-over-quarter revenue increase in Q2.
summary: LanzaTech reported Q1 2024 revenue of $10.2 million, up 6% YoY, with gross margin of 34% (up ~570 bps vs FY2023) and gross profit of $3.5 million, up 87% YoY. Adjusted EBITDA loss widened to $22.1 million and cash burn was $29.2 million, with cash of $92.3 million. Management reiterated FY2024 guidance of $90-$105 million revenue and a negative $65-$80 million adjusted EBITDA, expecting a 20-40% QoQ revenue ramp in Q2 and a back-half-weighted year. A $100 million ATM shelf was filed, and no plans to utilize it were stated.

negative_highlights: Owned & Operated revenue declined 35% year-over-year and 13% sequentially, driven by a 12% sequential drop in advertising spend.
Q2 guidance explicitly forecasts an 8-9% decline at the midpoint for both revenue and adjusted gross profit compared to Q1.
Owned & Operated cost per session declined $0.01 sequentially as note-side pricing volatility compressed spreads.
positive_highlights: Delivered results above the high end of guidance for revenue ($84.9M), gross profit ($31.2M), and adjusted EBITDA ($422k).
International revenue share increased to approximately 29% of Owned & Operated, up from 25% in Q4.
Organic traffic for MapQuest and CouponFollow saw a significant increase starting in March due to favorable Google Search algorithm changes.
summary: System1 reported Q1 FY2024 revenue of $85 million and adjusted EBITDA of $423,000, both exceeding the high end of prior guidance despite a sequential decline in Owned & Operated revenue driven by Google volatility. Management provided specific Q2 guidance expecting revenue between $88-90M (down 16% YoY at midpoint) and adjusted EBITDA between $5-7M, declining sequentially but anticipating growth in the back half of the year.

negative_highlights: Gross margin fell to 15% from 23% YoY
Adjusted EBITDA loss widened 10% YoY
Cash reduced to $1.0M from $1.8M; Oranim purchase canceled with $2.8M loss
positive_highlights: April Germany sales about double prior six-month monthly average
G&A expenses decreased 28% YoY
Regulatory reform in Israel and Germany legalization expected to drive patient growth
summary: Q1 2024 revenue declined 3% YoY to $12.1M with gross margin down to 15% from 23% due to price cuts, slow-moving inventory provisions, and FX. Adjusted EBITDA loss widened 10% to $2.1M, net loss from continuing operations was $6.0M, and cash fell to $1.0M. Management highlighted regulatory catalysts in Germany and Israel effective April 1, noting April German sales roughly doubled the prior six-month monthly average, but emphasized early-stage impacts and ongoing uncertainty.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined due to lower capital spending and shipment timing delays
Adjusted EBITDA loss increased from $700k to $1.4m, exacerbated by a one-time warranty expense
note and administrative expenses rose significantly including severance costs
positive_highlights: No known lost customers or orders to competition despite macro pressure
Launch of new private label program with another top-tier forklift OEM
summary: Flux Power reported Q3 FY2024 revenue of $14.5 million, a decrease from the prior year's $15.1 million and following its record high in Q2. Adjusted EBITDA widened to a loss of $1.4 million compared to a $700k loss last year, driven by lower gross profit ($4.4M) and increased operating expenses including severance costs. Management cited delays in forklift deliveries from OEMs and higher interest rates as primary headwinds but noted signs that the market may abate later this calendar year.

negative_highlights: Executed a workforce reduction of 29%, including contractors, as part of a rightsizing initiative to conserve cash.
Deferred various CapEx items, such as construction at Kabanga, to prioritize the delivery of the feasibility study.
Stopped exploration drilling to focus capital allocation on critical work streams.
positive_highlights: Successfully closed a $50 million non-brokered private placement of convertible debentures, with net proceeds of $44.3 million received post-quarter-end.
Received $1.5 million subscription proceeds from Glencore for a 6% stake in the US recycling subsidiary.
Maintained strong relationships with anchor partners BHP and Glencore, confirming no impact on project timelines despite Western Australia challenges.
summary: Lifezone Metals reported a net loss of $4 million for Q1 FY2024, narrowing from the prior year's loss of $0.10 per share, driven by cash outflows of $15.4 million focused on advancing its flagship Kabanga Nickel project and Glencore recycling partnership. The company raised $44.3 million in convertible debentures and $1.5 million from Glencore, bringing the total cash balance to $79.6 million at quarter-end. Management confirmed it remains on track for a definitive feasibility study (DFS) completion by the end of Q3 2024 for Kabanga and expects the Glencore recycling project to reach Final Investment Decision (FID) in Q3.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to $905,000 from $807,000 YoY.
Cash declined to $2.4 million from $2.7 million despite a $1 million insider-led offering.
MDR compliance for European sales not yet achieved, with first sales expected only later this summer.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 104% YoY to $1.27 million, above the $1.25 million guidance.
Gross margin turned positive to 21.9%, up from -9.2% YoY and 14.6% sequentially.
Consumer branded products revenue increased 178% YoY, boosted by first full quarter of Kenkoderm.
summary: NEXGEL reported Q1 FY2024 revenue of $1.27 million, up 104% YoY and exceeding guidance of $1.25 million, with gross profit margin improving to 21.9% from negative in the prior year. Net loss widened to $905,000 from $807,000 in Q1 FY2023, reflecting investments in capacity expansion and MDR compliance. Management expects to launch RESONIC gel pads with AbbVie by year-end, begin European sales of Hexagels later this summer, and sees expenses normalizing in H2 2024.

negative_highlights: The Unidompedro acquisition is expected to dilute margins in 2024, though management anticipates improvement from 2025 onward.
Medical Practice Solutions B2B revenue was impacted by postponed invoices; underlying B2B growth would have been 20-30% instead of the reported 9% segment growth.
Net debt increased to R$1.577 billion, and pro forma for the acquisition, net debt/adjusted EBITDA is expected to rise to 1.6x from 1.2x in Q1 2024.
positive_highlights: Net revenue grew 13% YoY to R$804 million, driven by a 6.4% increase in medical school average ticket and seat expansion.
Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 300 bps to 49.5%, with gross margin expansion in all three segments (Undergrad ~1.5 pp, Continuing Education ~4 pp, Medical Practice Solutions >5 pp).
Adjusted EPS jumped 54% YoY to R$2.74, supported by a 51% increase in adjusted net income and lower financial expenses.
summary: Afya reported Q1 2024 net revenue of R$804 million, up 13% year-over-year, with adjusted EBITDA of R$398 million (margin 49.5%, up 300 bps) and adjusted EPS of R$2.74, up 54-55%. Adjusted net income rose 51% to R$251 million, and operating cash flow was R$429 million with 110% conversion. Guidance for full-year 2024 adjusted EBITDA of R$1.3-$1.4 billion and net revenue of R$3.15-$3.25 billion was reaffirmed; no change. The company announced the acquisition of Unidompedro (300 medical seats in Salvador) for R$660 million, expected to close July 1, 2024, which will slightly dilute margins in 2024 before synergies materialize.

negative_highlights: Revenues remain muted due to cash-pay basis and high price point ($25,700) not feasible for most patients.
Cash burn from operations remains at $3 million despite the financing round.
PoNS sales are currently limited to MS indications pending stroke authorization.
positive_highlights: Revenue increased $24,000 YoY to $135,000 driven by sales in both the U.S. and Canada.
Operating loss narrowed to $3.4 million from $3.8 million in the prior year period.
CMS established HCPCS codes for PoNS effective April 1, enabling third-party payer negotiations.
summary: Helius Medical Technologies reported Q1 FY2024 revenue of $135,000, an increase of $24,000 compared to the prior year period, with operating loss narrowing to $3.4 million from $3.8 million. The company raised its cash runway into 2025 via a $6.4 million financing round and expects revenues to significantly boost later in the year following CMS reimbursement approval anticipated by October 1. Management expressed confidence in achieving widespread reimbursement for PoNS and FDA authorization for stroke by early-to-late 2025.

negative_highlights: Cash balance of $17M with market cap of only $13M
Average daily trading volume at 30,000 shares
Cash runway only extends into Q4 2024, with planned expenditures pushed to 2025
positive_highlights: Reported 60% CRc rate in second-line AML patients
Treated over 80 patients with 0 cardiotoxicity
Endpoint of Phase II meeting with FDA expected by end of June
summary: Q1 FY2024 R&D expense decreased to $4.3M from $5.7M, G&A to $2.4M from $2.6M; cash remains roughly $17M with runway into Q4 2024, though market cap is about $13M with only 2.5M shares. The company emphasizes a 60% CRc rate in second-line AML patients, has treated over 80 patients with no cardiotoxicity, and plans an End of Phase II meeting with the FDA in Q2, expecting feedback in early Q3. Guidance is to initiate a pivotal trial in H1 2025, and management asserts the data are sufficient for approval if repeated.

negative_highlights: Total revenue was flat to slightly down at $4.1 million versus $4.2 million, with declines in investment income and deposit activity offsetting lending growth.
Depository fees fell 28% to $1.62 million from $2.25 million, and client accounts dropped to 757 from 1,040 after the Central Bank of Arkansas agreement termination.
Full-year 2024 guidance is only 'slightly better' adjusted EBITDA on 'modestly higher' revenue than 2023's $3.6 million on $17.6 million.
positive_highlights: Operating expense fell more than 35% to $3.7 million from $5.8 million, producing net income of nearly $2 million versus a $1.4 million loss.
Loan interest income rose 250% year-over-year to $1.6 million and represented just over 40% of revenue, with the loan book nearly tripling.
Adjusted EBITDA rose to $1.0 million from $409,000, and operating cash flow was $1.4 million versus $232,000 of cash used in the prior-year period.
summary: Safe Harbor Financial reported Q1 2024 total revenue of $4.1 million, essentially flat versus $4.2 million a year ago, as deposit and onboarding income fell and loan interest income rose over 250% to $1.6 million. Operating expense fell more than 35% to $3.7 million, driving net income of nearly $2 million versus a $1.4 million loss, and adjusted EBITDA rose to $1.0 million from $409,000, with operating cash flow of $1.4 million. Client accounts dropped to 757 from 1,040 after the July 2023 termination of the Central Bank of Arkansas agreement, and depository fees fell 28% to $1.62 million. Full-year 2024 guidance calls for slightly better adjusted EBITDA on modestly higher revenue compared to 2023's $3.6 million adjusted EBITDA on $17.6 million revenue.

negative_highlights: Mytesi prescription volume decreased 7% sequentially from Q4 2023 due to deductible resets
No specific financial guidance or earnings targets were provided for the full year
OnTarget trial results remain blinded and timing is described as 'imminent' rather than confirmed
positive_highlights: Combined net revenue increased approximately 20% versus Q1 2023
Non-GAAP recurring EBITDA loss narrowed from $9 million in Q1 2023 to $7.5 million in Q1 2024
Net loss attributable to common shareholders decreased by approximately $2.9 million year-over-year
summary: JAGX reported Q1 FY2024 combined net revenue of approximately $2.4 million, representing a 20% year-over-year increase but a 7% sequential decline from Q4 2023 due to annual Medicare deductible resets. The company posted a GAAP loss from operations of $8.2 million (down from $9.9 million in the prior year) and a net loss attributable to common shareholders of $9.2 million. Management upgraded the timing for OnTarget trial results to 'imminent' but provided no specific financial guidance or earnings targets.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined year-over-year due to fewer product discounts and updates to revenue recognition methodology extending customer lives.
Gross margin contracted by 400 basis points to 57% from 61% in the prior year.
Management stated that current growth initiatives are not yet generating material top-line sales needed to eliminate monthly burn.
positive_highlights: G&A expenses decreased by $1.6 million or 25% year-over-year due to cost-cutting initiatives.
Operating loss improved by $1.2 million (24%) compared to the prior year period.
Cash burn from operations decreased to $2.5 million, a reduction of $1 million versus the prior year.
summary: Vivos Therapeutics reported Q1 FY2024 revenue of $3.4 million, a decrease from $3.8 million in the prior year period, driven by lower VIP enrollment revenue and appliance sales despite higher estimated customer lives. Gross margin contracted to 57% from 61%, while operating loss narrowed to $3.8 million due to significant G&A reductions of $1.6 million (25% YoY). Management expressed cautious optimism about a new strategic channel initiative targeting medical groups and sleep testing centers, which they expect to materially broaden revenue sources and reduce dependence on the dental channel.

negative_highlights: Cash balance significantly declined to $769,000 from $6.5 million year-over-year.
No grant revenues or government contracts were recognized during the first quarter of FY2024.
Research and development expenses increased by 57% (or $1.6 million) compared to Q1 2023.
positive_highlights: Positive interim data reported from the heterologous booster trial showing statistically significant increases in neutralizing antibodies against multiple SARS-CoV-2 variants including Omicron XBB.1.5 and JN.1.
Robust immunogenicity demonstrated in Phase II stem cell transplant/immunocompromised randomized trials with results published in peer-reviewed journals.
summary: GeoVax reported a net loss of $5.6 million (or $2.47 per share) for Q1 FY2024 compared to a loss of $4 million in the prior year period. The company had no grant revenues or government contracts during the quarter, with cash balances declining from $6.5 million at end-2023 to approximately $769,000 by March 31 due to operating activities and clinical trial spending. Management noted active discussions regarding a potential BARDA award under Project NextGen but provided no specific financial guidance or revenue projections for the quarter.

negative_highlights: Total revenue grew just 2% year-over-year to $5.8 million
Authentication segment revenue fell to $0.1 million from $0.2 million as a large order slipped to Q2/Q3
Precision Logistics same-customer shipping volumes declined about 2%, with pricing pressure flagged
positive_highlights: Gross margin expanded to 39% from 27%, lifting gross profit 49% to $2.3 million
Adjusted EBITDA turned positive at $0.1 million, the third consecutive positive quarter
Net loss narrowed to $0.6 million ($0.05 per diluted share) from $1.6 million ($0.17 per diluted share)
summary: Q1 2024 revenue rose 2% to $5.8 million from $5.7 million, with Precision Logistics up 4% to $5.6 million and Authentication down to $0.1 million from $0.2 million as a large order slipped. Gross profit rose 49% to $2.3 million, gross margin expanded to 39% from 27%, net loss improved to $0.6 million from $1.6 million, and adjusted EBITDA was a positive $0.1 million, a third straight positive quarter. Management affirmed prior guidance for double-digit revenue growth in both segments and the company overall, weighted to H2, and reiterated expectations for positive 2024 cash flow, though it flagged softer parcel volumes, potential pricing pressure, and longer Authentication sales cycles.

negative_highlights: Net sales declined 12.9% year-over-year due to a 12.6% decrease in volume/mix driven by oversupply.

Adjusted EBITDA was $0.3 million, significantly below the prior year's loss of $2.1 million but still far from management's stated goal of $2.7 million positive adjusted EBITDA over the last 12 months.
Free cash flow was negative $3.7 million for the quarter, though management notes this is a seasonally low period.
positive_highlights: Adjusted gross margin expanded 80 bps to 23.4% of net sales, marking the fifth consecutive quarter of expansion.
Sequential net sales growth achieved for five consecutive months (October through March), the longest string since the IPO.
Non-cannabis and non-North American revenue sources increased to an estimated 32% of sales, a 360-basis-point increase from the prior year.
summary: Net sales declined 12.9% year-over-year to $54.2 million, driven by a 12.6% decrease in volume/mix due to oversupply in the cannabis industry, though adjusted gross margin expanded 80 bps to 23.4%. Management reaffirmed full-year guidance for net sales (low to high teens decline), positive adjusted EBITDA, and positive free cash flow, noting sequential revenue growth for five consecutive months but cautioning against raising guidance early in the year.

negative_highlights: R&D expenses increased due to trial completions
SUNRISE-3 data readout pushed to H2 with no precise timing
Phase III HCV timelines depend on regulatory alignment
positive_highlights: Completed SUNRISE-3 enrollment ahead of schedule
98% SVR4 rate in HCV leading cohort
Cash runway extended into 2027
summary: Atea Pharmaceuticals reported Q1 2024 with strong clinical execution: SUNRISE-3 Phase III COVID trial enrollment completed ahead of guidance with 2,221 patients in the monotherapy cohort and 74 in combination. HCV Phase II leading cohort showed 98% SVR4 and enrollment for full Phase II ongoing; Phase III expected around year-end. Cash at $541.5 million extends runway into 2027, and guidance includes costs for two Phase III HCV trials. Top-line SUNRISE-3 data expected in H2 2024.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined 35.5% year-over-year driven by lingering effects of the RV market downturn.
Gross margin contracted from 29.4% to 22.9%, primarily due to decreased sales volume increasing fixed overhead costs per unit.
Home Energy Storage solutions require installation through certified dealers and are not available for self-installation.
positive_highlights: Substantial pre-orders received for next-generation Group 27 and GC2 Series batteries with Vertical Heat Conduction technology, beginning shipment in May.
New Edge battery launched featuring a slim profile (4.2 inches height) designed to maximize space without compromising performance.
Secured vendor contract with Tractor Supply, expanding retail footprint across 2,232 locations starting June.
summary: First quarter revenue decreased to $1 million from $1.5 million in the prior year period due to an RV market downturn and customer order limitations ahead of new product launches. Gross profit declined to $200,000 (22.9% margin) compared to $400,000 previously as lower sales volume drove higher fixed overhead costs per unit. Net loss increased to $2.2 million ($0.31 EPS).

negative_highlights: Q2 volume guidance steps down to 1.0-1.2 million tons from 1.3 million on Marcellus demand pullback tied to low natural gas prices
Free cash flow was negative $5.5 million in Q1 on working capital build
Industrial sand is only ~5% of volumes and remains a multi-year build toward a 10% target
positive_highlights: Sales volumes up 31% to a record 1.3 million tons, lifting revenue to $83.1 million from $61.9 million in Q4
Contribution margin per ton improved to $13.85 from $9.07, and adjusted EBITDA rose to $9.3 million from $0.7 million
Wet plant and hydraulic mining changes expected to yield $1-2 per ton or more in cost savings
summary: Smart Sand reported record Q1 sales volumes of 1.3 million tons, up 31% sequentially, driving revenue to $83.1 million from $61.9 million in Q4 2023. Contribution margin rose to $18.5 million ($13.85/ton) from $9.2 million ($9.07/ton), and adjusted EBITDA jumped to $9.3 million from $0.7 million. Management guided Q2 volumes down to 1.0-1.2 million tons on Marcellus pullback from low natural gas prices, partially offset by Bakken and Canada, with contribution margin of $13-16/ton and capex of $15-20 million; Q1 free cash flow was negative $5.5 million on working capital, but full-year positive FCF is still expected.

negative_highlights: Net income fell to $4.6 million from $13.8 million and diluted EPS dropped to $0.19 from $0.54 as the legacy CECL provision reversal shrank from $9.0 million to $1.6 million
Interest expense rose to $42.0 million from $32.7 million, and core operating expenses rose to 6.0% of the average managed portfolio from 5.7%
Annualized net charge-offs of 7.84% rose from 5.20% a year ago, and originations remain below the $415 million in Q1 2023
positive_highlights: Revenue increased 10% YoY to $91.7 million, with the fair value portfolio at $2.8 billion yielding 11.3%
Originations rebounded to $346 million from $301 million in Q4, and the portfolio reached a record $3.02 billion, up from $2.86 billion a year ago
QoQ delinquency and net charge-off metrics improved, and the Gen 8 origination model cut delinquency 200 bps in the October 2023 vintage test
summary: Q1 FY2024 revenue rose 10% YoY to $91.7 million, but pretax earnings fell to $6.6 million from $18.4 million and diluted EPS dropped to $0.19 from $0.54. The decline was driven by a $9.3 million smaller loss-provision reversal on the legacy CECL portfolio ($1.6 million vs $9.0 million) and interest expense rising to $42.0 million from $32.7 million. Originations of $346 million rose from $301 million in Q4 but were below $415 million a year earlier, and management said new paper is performing better while flagging net charge-offs of 7.84% vs 5.20% a year ago. Management gave no explicit numerical guidance but said Q1 is a turning point for growth capital, including $50 million in new residual funding and a renewed $200 million warehouse line.

negative_highlights: Net loss attributable to common shareholders was $51 million, driven by approximately $59 million of investment-related losses, versus $23 million of investment gains in the prior-year quarter.
Operating adjusted EBITDA declined to $66 million from $88 million in Q1 2023, and operating revenues fell to $379 million from $389 million.

Consumer Products (Targus) posted a segment loss of $3 million amid continued softness in global PC and laptop sales, and the quarterly dividend was reduced to $0.50 per share from prior levels, implying roughly $30 million in annual savings.
positive_highlights: Advisory Services (B. Riley Advisory Services) delivered a record first quarter with segment revenues up 40% to $35 million and operating income up 62% to $6.1 million.
Wealth Management revenues rose to $52 million, surpassing prior-year and sequential levels, with operating margins continuing to improve and assets under management at $25.8 billion.
Services and fees revenue increased 9% year-over-year to $257 million, and the company redeemed approximately $115 million of senior notes during the quarter.
summary: B. Riley reported Q1 FY2024 total revenues of $343 million and a net loss attributable to common shareholders of $51 million, driven by roughly $59 million of investment-related losses plus incremental 10-K and investigation costs. Operating adjusted EBITDA fell to $66 million from $88 million a year earlier, and operating revenues declined to $379 million from $389 million, though service and fee revenue rose 9% to $257 million. Management declared a $0.50 quarterly dividend — halved from prior levels to align with operating EBITDA — and said it expects to exit 2024 with ample liquidity, while discussing a Great American sale process that may slip toward early Q3 and continued weakness in Targus and Franchise Group. The quarter was pressured by noncash investment marks and late-filing costs, with management expressing confidence in the operating businesses but acknowledging a tough consumer and small-cap environment.

negative_highlights: Consolidated revenues declined year-over-year due to the company's deliberate decision to discontinue several unprofitable product lines.
The business faced regulatory headwinds in Florida which hurt both top-line and bottom-line results for the quarter, though issues are now resolved.
Management explicitly stated they do not feel comfortable providing specific sales mix forecasts or guidance breakdowns at this time.
positive_highlights: German operations sales increased significantly to $11.3 million from $8 million YoY driven by new medical cannabis legislation effective April 1, 2024.
Total operating expenses decreased by $1.4 million (18%) year-over-year and net cash used in operating activities improved by $3 million (70%).
JustCBD added 200 new wholesale customers to its network while maintaining a gross profit margin of 41%.
summary: Flora Growth reported Q1 FY2024 revenues of $18 million, a decrease from $19.3 million in the prior year quarter primarily due to the deliberate discontinuation of unprofitable product lines and regulatory issues in Florida. Operating expenses decreased by $1.4 million (or 18%) YoY to $6.3 million as the company cut costs, resulting in an operating loss improvement from $2.4 million to $1.6 million before noncash items. Management provided no specific financial guidance for future quarters but expressed optimism regarding upcoming regulatory changes in Germany and potential U.S. rescheduling.

negative_highlights: Wayfair business declined approximately 5% YoY due to reduced app flow from the merchant side.
Q2 gross originations guidance was lowered to 3-5% growth reflecting continued macro headwinds in home furnishings.
Management noted uncertainty regarding Federal Reserve interest rate cuts and potential tightening by prime creditors.
positive_highlights: Gross margin expanded nearly 380 bps YoY to 25%, driven by strong collections and lower lease inventory costs.
Adjusted EBITDA turned positive at $5.6 million, a significant improvement from the loss in Q1 last year.
Katapult Pay added Lowe's as a new retailer partner following successful integrations with Best note, Home Depot, and Lenovo.
summary: Katapult reported Q1 FY2024 gross originations of $55.6 million (up 1.6% YoY) and revenue of $65.1 million (up 18.1% YoY), slightly beating expectations for flat performance due to strong collections and a tax season tailwind. Gross margin expanded nearly 380 bps to 25%, while write-offs remained within the target range at 8.4%. Management reiterated full-year guidance of approximately 10% growth but lowered Q2 gross originations outlook to 3-5% citing ongoing headwinds in home furnishings.

negative_highlights: Q1 included $5.9 million in share-based compensation expenses and $2.3 million in one-time Credova transaction costs
No explicit profitability metrics (EPS, margins) were provided in the transcript
2024 revenue guidance was only reaffirmed, not raised, despite the strong top-line growth
positive_highlights: Net revenue increased 817% year over year to $3.5 million
Pro forma Q1 net revenue of $6.4 million exceeded full-year 2023 revenue by 12.2%
Marketplace monthly average users grew 314% year over year
summary: PublicSquare reported Q1 FY2024 net revenue of $3.5 million, up 817% year over year, with pro forma revenue of $6.4 million including Credova. The company reaffirmed its March 14, 2024 guidance for a 2024 exit run-rate of $47–$53 million revenue and expects to exit the year with $8–$10 million in cash. Q1 included $5.9 million in share-based compensation and $2.3 million in one-time Credova transaction costs, and the company provided no explicit EPS or margin figures. Management highlighted continued growth in Marketplace users (up 314%), EveryLife subscription revenue (75% of segment revenue), and new fintech initiatives, but the quarter's profitability picture remained unclear.

negative_highlights: No product revenue recorded in the quarter versus $1.2 million net product revenue in the prior-year period following the Vyleesi divestiture
Net cash used in operations widened to $8.6 million from $1.4 million a year earlier, attributed mainly to working capital changes
Operating expenses increased to $9.2 million from $8.5 million on higher Melanocortin program spending
positive_highlights: Positive Phase 3 MELODY-1 results for PL9643 in dry eye disease, with pain and 7 of 11 secondary symptom endpoints reaching statistical significance at two weeks
Vyleesi worldwide rights sold to Cosette Pharmaceuticals for up to $171 million in December 2023, eliminating related note expenses
Cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities of $10 million as of March 31, 2024, sufficient to fund operations into the second half of calendar 2024
summary: Palatin reported Q3 FY2024 with zero product revenue after watching Vyleesi worldwide rights to Cosette for up to $171 million in December 2023, versus $3.4 million gross product sales and $1.2 million net product revenue a year earlier. Operating expenses rose to $9.2 million from $8.5 million on greater Melanocortin program spending, net loss narrowed to $8.4 million ($0.53 per share) from $8.7 million ($0.76 per share), and cash plus marketable securities stood at $10 million versus $9.5 million plus $2.3 million of receivables at December 31, 2023. Management highlighted positive Phase 3 MELODY-1 dry eye results for PL9643, an upcoming FDA Type C meeting, planned MELODY-2/3 studies, mid-2024 interim data for oral PL8177 in ulcerative colitis and top-line data for the diabetic kidney disease study, and two new Phase 2 programs in obesity and erectile dysfunction. Cash is expected to fund operations into the second half of calendar 2024.

negative_highlights: Revenue was negatively impacted by order cancellations due to unexpected manufacturing delays and delivery timeline issues.
Operating loss of $5.8 million reflects early launch inefficiencies and costs associated with the Evie Ring launch.
Company is holding on taking new orders until inventory controls are optimized, delaying D2C revenue growth.
positive_highlights: Raised $24 million in gross proceeds from a strategic private placement including a Tier 1 medical device investor.
FDA submission for Evie Med pulse oximeter feature achieved RMSE of 2.46%, exceeding the 3.5% guidance benchmark.
Strategic partners expressed immediate interest in continuous, secure medical-grade data solutions.
summary: Movano Health reported $852,000 in revenue and an operating loss of $5.8 million for Q1 FY2024, driven by a launch of the Evie Ring that resulted in order cancellations due to delivery delays. The company raised $24 million via a private placement in April 2024, bringing cash on hand to $24.8 million pro forma. Management indicated they will pause taking new orders until inventory levels are secured to ensure reliable delivery timelines.

negative_highlights: Total revenue fell by approximately 76% compared to the second quarter of fiscal year 2024
Cash balance decreased significantly from $4.1 million as of March 31, 2023 to approximately $0.3 million as of March 31, 2024
Quarterly active users declined compared to the previous quarter
positive_highlights: Gross profit increased substantially by 47% year-over-year despite revenue decline
Net losses narrowed significantly from approximately $2.9 million in Q3 FY23 to approximately $1.7 million in Q3 FY24
ZCITY Premium Store exceeded sales expectations and sold over 6,000 Bill Saver Bonanza Packs within four months
summary: Treasure Global reported Q3 FY24 gross profit of $217,000 (up 47% YoY) and a net loss reduction to approximately $1.7 million from $2.9 million in the prior year quarter. However, total revenue declined significantly by approximately 76% compared to Q2 FY24 due to a strategic shift away from lower-margin offerings like e-vouchers toward higher-margin channels. Management noted cash reserves dropped to ~$0.3M but secured an ATM offering of up to $2.99 million.

negative_highlights: No revenue or EPS figures were disclosed; the only financial metric provided was $10.9 million in cash at quarter-end.
G&A expenses increased year over year, while R&D expenses were described only as 'consistent' with no specific amounts.
No timing estimate was given for the next IND submission in the post-COVID fatigue program, pending biomarker analysis.
positive_highlights: Interim data from the ovarian cancer trial showed a 45% objective response rate in 21 evaluable patients, compared with 8% for pembrolizumab alone in KEYNOTE-100.
DURIPANC safety evaluation for the first dose level found no severe adverse events or dose-limiting toxicities, and escalation to the next dose level was approved.
The company completed cGMP manufacturing of 9,042 clinical vials of Ampligen, supporting ongoing trials and partner discussions.
summary: AIM ImmunoTech's Q1 FY2024 call was almost entirely clinical and operational, with minimal financial disclosure: the company ended the quarter with $10.9 million in cash, R&D expenses were consistent with prior periods, and G&A expenses rose year over year. Management reported positive interim ovarian cancer data (45% objective response rate in 21 evaluable patients) and DURIPANC safety clearance to the next dose level, but provided no revenue guidance or updated financial outlook. The key change versus prior periods was continued pipeline progress and manufacturing of 9,042 clinical vials of Ampligen, while the absence of revenue or earnings figures leaves the quarter's financial performance unmeasurable from the transcript.

negative_highlights: The company remains unprofitable on a GAAP basis with a net loss of $0.8 million.
Revenue guidance relies heavily on the pending OpenExO acquisition closing later in the quarter.
Student base growth is projected to be organic only, without specific new product revenue drivers mentioned.
positive_highlights: Pro forma revenue grew 150% YoY to $70.4 million driven by the FatBrain AI acquisition.
Gross margin expanded significantly to 51.7% (up 420 bps) due to digital delivery focus.
Net loss reduced by 90% to $0.8 million, with a path to positive adjusted EBITDA of over $6 million in 2024.
summary: Genius Group reported full year 2023 pro forma revenue of $70.4 million (up 150% YoY) and a net loss reduction to $0.8 million following the acquisition of FatBrain AI. Management raised 2024 pro forma revenue guidance to above $105 million, representing a 50% increase from the prior year's pro forma revenue. The company also anticipates becoming profitable on an adjusted EBITDA basis with over $6 million in 2024.

negative_highlights: BDC-1001 discontinued after Phase 2 expansion cohorts failed to reproduce the ~30% ORR bar set from dose escalation
Leadership turnover: CEO Willie Quinn, CMO Edith Perez, and two board directors (Engleman, Miller) all transitioning
50% workforce reduction and program shutdown signal a materially narrowed pipeline reliant on early-stage assets
positive_highlights: Workforce cut of ~50% extends cash runway into 2H 2026, funding BDC-3042 and BDC-4182 data readouts with existing resources
BDC-3042 has cleared the first three dose-escalation cohorts with no dose-limiting toxicities; the fourth cohort is fully enrolled
Preclinical data show next-gen ISACs outperform MMAE-based ADCs and retain activity at lower antigen density; BDC-4182 advancing to IND-enabling studies
summary: Bolt used its first-ever earnings call to discontinue all development of lead ISAC BDC-1001 after the Phase 2 expansion cohorts failed to reproduce the ~30% overall response rate seen in dose escalation. The company is cutting roughly 50% of its workforce, narrowing the board by two directors, and replacing its CEO and CMO, actions it says extend cash runway into the second half of 2026. Remaining priorities are the Phase 1 Dectin-2 agonist BDC-3042 (three dose cohorts cleared with no DLTs, fourth fully enrolled, safety/enrollment update expected in 2H) and next-gen Claudin 18.2 ISAC BDC-4182, which is in IND-enabling work with a planned 2025 trial start. No revenue, EPS, or margin figures were reported; the Q1 release is a pipeline and strategic update.

negative_highlights: Q1 revenue was negatively impacted by a one-off customs delay at L.A. port that shifted majority of March shipments into April.
Company raised equity in Q4 to address Nasdaq delisting risk regarding shareholder burn and compliance, contradicting prior 'no raises' stance.
Significant noncash charges including $368,000 income tax charge impacted GAAP results.
positive_highlights: Gross margin profit increased 48.1% compared to a year ago due to fixed cost leverage from higher revenues.
Net operating loss improved dramatically, dropping from $3.7 million last year to $225,000 in the current quarter.
New store opened mid-April is already generating healthy week-to-week revenue increases with no additional product manufacturing costs.
summary: Net revenues were $3.6 million compared to $4.4 million a year ago due to wholesale shipments shifting from March into April. Net operating loss narrowed significantly to $225,000 from $3.7 million last year as gross margin increased to 48.1% and G&A expenses decreased by $1 million following the Sundry acquisition synergies.

negative_highlights: Net income to common shareholders fell to $3.4 million from $8.7 million a year ago, which included an $8 million vessel sale gain
Basic EPS declined to $0.33 from $0.81 in Q1 2023
G&A expenses were lower by $600,000, suggesting cost reduction may not be sustainable
positive_highlights: TCE revenues increased 10.2% year-over-year to $10.2 million
Adjusted EBITDA increased $1.8 million to $6 million
83% of Q2 available days for MRs booked at average TCE of $32,500 per day, above Q1 average of $31,719 per day
summary: Pyxis Tankers reported Q1 FY2024 TCE revenues of $10.2 million, up 10.2% year-over-year, driven by higher spot rates and the addition of dry bulk carriers. Net income to common shareholders was $3.4 million or $0.33 basic EPS, down from $8.7 million a year ago which included an $8 million gain on vessel sale. Adjusted EBITDA rose $1.8 million to $6 million. Management provided a bullish near-term outlook for product tankers and a balanced view for dry bulk, citing healthy charter rates, booked Q2 coverage, and announced fleet expansion and capital return actions including a new Kamsarmax acquisition and $1 million additional buyback authorization.

negative_highlights: Received Nasdaq deficiency notice due to share price below $1; executed reverse stock split
Interest and finance costs of $543K and unrealized loss on warrants of $630K
Financial liability of $39 million due in July 2024
positive_highlights: EBITDA increased 301% to $5.7 million and net income up 475%
TCE more than doubled to $36.5K from $15.9K in Q1 2023
Fleet capacity expanded 234% and cash balance grew 285%
summary: C3is reported a strong Q1 2024 with EBITDA of $5.7 million, up 301% YoY, and net income of $3.8 million, up 475% YoY, driven by the Aframax tanker addition. TCE more than doubled to $36.5K. Cash increased 285% to $34.9 million, aided by public offerings, and fleet capacity expanded 234% with the delivery of the Eco Spitfire in May. The outlook remains positive with low order books, healthy demand growth, and no bank debt, though the company completed a reverse stock split to regain Nasdaq compliance and has a $39 million liability due in July 2024.

negative_highlights: GAAP revenue fell to $98,000 from $433,000 in the prior-year quarter, a decline of $335,000
GAAP cost of revenue rose to $545,000 from $325,000, mainly due to fixed production facility costs against low revenue
GAAP net loss widened to $4.2 million ($0.37 per share) from $3.7 million ($0.33 per share) a year earlier
positive_highlights: Cash and cash equivalents of $23.2 million with no debt, providing a runway at least until the end of 2025 based on current plans
Net cash used in operating activities was $3.3 million, roughly flat versus $3.4 million in Q1 2023
Advancing large animal study with commercial-size breast implants (including a 200 cc implant) initiated in December 2023, with data expected in Q4 2024 and Q1 2025
summary: CollPlant reported Q1 2024 GAAP revenue of $98,000, down $335,000 from $433,000 in Q1 2023, with cost of revenue up to $545,000. GAAP net loss widened to $4.2 million ($0.37 loss per share) from $3.7 million ($0.33 loss per share), while non-GAAP net loss was $4 million ($0.35 per share) versus $3.3 million ($0.29 per share). Cash and equivalents stood at $23.2 million with no debt, which management believes provides runway at least until the end of 2025, excluding any potential partnership revenue. No formal revenue or EPS guidance was given; the company outlined upcoming clinical milestones, including large animal study data in Q4 2024 and Q1 2025 and ongoing work with AbbVie, but did not specify timing for the next AbbVie milestone payment.

negative_highlights: No revenue recognized in Q1 2024; pre-tax loss of €5.1 million.
NASDAQ deficiency notice for failing to maintain $10 million in shareholders' equity; bank balance of only €1.5 million at quarter-end.
2024 revenue guidance unchanged but still dependent on monetizing the Sines portfolio, with no formal update on timing.
positive_highlights: Operating cost base reduced by €1.5 million sequentially (excluding Q4 grant credits), the fifth consecutive quarter of reduction.
Pipeline of over 200 MW of offers and tenders across 16 markets, with 73% of projects under 5 MW and an average size of 3 MW.
Received provisional €5 million grant approval for the 25 MW HEVO-Aveiro project and a €1 million Work Package award from H2tALENT; IPCEI designation for Sines 630 MW project.
summary: Fusion Fuel reported no revenue in Q1 FY2024 and a pre-tax loss of €5.1 million, while maintaining its 2024 guidance that remains weighted to H2. Management cited a €0.7 million revenue deferral, a fifth consecutive quarter of operating cost reductions (down €1.5 million excluding prior grant credits), and a bank balance of just over €1.5 million. The company received a NASDAQ shareholders' equity deficiency notice in May, is finalizing a compliance plan within 45 days, and continues to explore strategic financing to address its capital position. On the commercial side, it progressed its 200+ MW pipeline across 16 markets and prepared to commission its first commercial HEVO-Chain system for a cement client in Spain.

negative_highlights: No specific revenue or cash flow guidance provided for the upcoming quarters.
R&D expenses remain elevated at $20 million annually due to ongoing Phase 3 trials.
Company remains unprofitable with a net loss of $29.4 million.
positive_highlights: PALISADE-2 Phase 3 study achieved positive results, marking the first successful Phase 3 for an acute SAD treatment candidate.
PALISADE-3 trial launched with enrollment on track and improved operational efficiencies compared to prior studies.
Net loss narrowed significantly to $29.4 million from $59.2 million in the prior year.
summary: Vistagen Therapeutics reported fiscal year 2024 results with R&D expenses of $20 million (down from $44.4M) and a net loss of $29.4 million (improved from $59.2M). The company highlighted positive Phase 3 data for fasedienol in SAD, the launch of PALISADE-3 with mid-2025 readout expectations, and a new repeat-dose study to inform labeling. Management expressed confidence in execution but provided no specific financial guidance or revenue figures.

negative_highlights: Consolidated revenue declined 3% sequentially to $124.3 million, which management attributed to seasonal softness and two fewer note days.
E-commerce revenue fell 37% year-over-year, described as facing intense top-line pressure.
Management explicitly warned that the ramp-up pace for new stores has considerably slowed and not met internal standards.
positive_highlights: Free cash flow reached a record $9.4 million, exceeding the prior two quarters combined, with $22.7 million generated over the trailing twelve months.
Adjusted EBITDA rose 52% year-over-year to $10 million, maintaining an 8.1% margin for the second consecutive quarter.
Market share in the five operating provinces increased to 10.9% from 10.4% in Q1 and 9.9% a year ago.
summary: High Tide reported Q2 FY2024 revenue of $124.3 million, up 5% year-over-year and down 3% sequentially, with positive net income, record free cash flow of $9.4 million, and adjusted EBITDA of $10 million (8.1% margin). Gross margin reached a nine-quarter high of 28.4%, and market share expanded to 10.9%. Management reaffirmed its 20-30 organic store target for the year and highlighted a new $15 million debt financing, but cautioned that the ramp-up pace of new stores has slowed and that same-store sales growth is moderating amid a softer industry backdrop.

negative_highlights: Gross profit margin declined due to inventory write-downs incurred during the transition to order-driven production.
Received $0 revenue from EPA-funded deals despite substantial award announcements, citing slow contract issuance.
Significant headwinds remain regarding charging infrastructure readiness at many school districts, delaying qualified leads.
positive_highlights: Delivered first all-electric Type D purpose-built school buses from the new West Virginia facility.
Commercial EV Star upfitted sales increased nearly 50% year-over-year, rising from 79 to 117 vehicle deliveries.
Secured financing via a $5 million term loan and $5 million in EDC guarantees specifically for production pursuant to customer orders.
summary: GreenPower reported fiscal year 2024 revenues of $39.3 million and gross profit of $5.4 million, with a decline in gross margin attributed to inventory write-downs associated with the ramp-up of its new West Virginia facility. Management highlighted a transition from manufacturing to inventory toward a production plan driven by customer orders, noting that while live orders exceed 100 units, significant delays persist due to EPA contract issuance and charging infrastructure challenges at school districts. The company delivered 222 vehicles total, including the first Type D school buses from West Virginia, but explicitly stated it received $0 revenue from EPA-funded deals despite substantial announcements.

negative_highlights: Q1 2024 revenue fell about $200 million with gross margin negative around 9%
2023 booked a ~$450 million non-cash impairment and ~$1.9 billion operating cash outflow
Updated guidance was deferred and cash-flow breakeven pushed to late 2025 amid tariffs and pricing pressure
positive_highlights: Q2 deliveries reached 13,000 cars with retail order intake up 169% year-over-year
SG&A expenses declined 1% in Q1 2024 despite Polestar 3 and 4 marketing spend
