Polestar 3 production in South Carolina is on track for end of summer, with Polestar 4 for North America from South Korea in H2 2025
summary: Q1 2024 revenue fell about $200 million year-over-year on lower volumes, higher discounts to clear inventory, and revenue-recognition complexities on sales to the China JV, with gross margin negative around 9%. Full-year 2023 (preliminary) revenue declined 3% on a 6% rise in vehicle sales to 54,600, with a roughly $450 million non-cash impairment and a ~$1.9 billion operating cash outflow. Management cited a stronger Q2 with 13,000 deliveries and 169% higher retail order intake, but deferred updated guidance, saying cash-flow breakeven remains targeted for late 2025 while tariffs and pricing pressure drive business-plan revisions.

negative_highlights: Q4 Ben Liquidity base interest revenue fell 5.6% sequentially to $10.6 million and full-year revenue fell 7.6% to $46.9 million due to higher credit-loss allowances.

Full-year operating loss was $1.8 billion, including a $1.7 billion non-cash goodwill impairment, and adjusted operating loss was $41.2 million versus $9.7 million of adjusted operating income a year earlier.

Ben Custody NAV fell to $381.2 million from $491.9 million a year earlier, and approximately $37.7 million of NAV originated during the year was written off; cash was $7.9 million against $120.5 million of total debt.
positive_highlights: Board approved the ExchangeTrust product plan to complete up to $5 billion of fiduciary financings, with a goal of reducing transaction closing times to as little as 15 days.
SEC staff terminated its investigation and does not intend to recommend an enforcement action under the previously issued Wells Notices.

A federal judge denied a motion to dismiss the company's defamation lawsuit against a Wall Street Journal reporter, with the ruling noting the article did not accurately reflect submitted information.
summary: Beneficient reported Q4 FY2024 Ben Liquidity base interest revenue of $10.6 million, down 5.6% sequentially, and full-year revenue of $46.9 million, down 7.6% year over year, both driven by higher credit-loss allowances. Q4 operating loss was $29.4 million (versus a $606.4 million loss in the prior quarter, which included goodwill impairment), while full-year operating loss was $1.8 billion including a $1.7 billion non-cash goodwill impairment and full-year adjusted operating loss was $41.2 million versus adjusted operating income of $9.7 million a year earlier. Ben Custody revenue fell to $5.6 million in Q4 from $5.9 million in the prior quarter, with full-year revenue down 15.5% to $24.5 million as NAV of assets in custody declined to $381.2 million from $491.9 million a year earlier. Management highlighted a new ExchangeTrust product plan targeting up to $5 billion of fiduciary financings, an SEC termination of its previously disclosed investigation, and a favorable court ruling on its defamation suit, but offered no explicit forward guidance figures.

negative_highlights: Holiday season performance in fiscal '24 fell note weakness in due to production bottlenecks and supply chain inefficiencies.
The company is currently exiting a multi-year pattern of store contraction, indicating prior weakness in the retail network.
positive_highlights: Management has moved into the role of Interim CEO with a mandate to stabilize operations and improve liquidity.
summary: RMCF reported Q1 FY2025 results that missed expectations due to business execution missteps and supply chain bottlenecks during the holiday season of fiscal '24. Management outlined a revised three-year strategic plan targeting net store growth, adjusted EBITDA profitability by year-end, and gross margins returning to 20% in fiscal '26. The company is deploying over $3 million in CapEx for production efficiency upgrades and implementing new ERP/POS systems to address prior inefficiencies.

negative_highlights: No financial results (revenue, EPS) were reported for the quarter; call was a business update only
Phase Two feasibility study outcome is not yet available and will be provided at the August call
Company remains in discussions with multiple lenders to secure debt financing required to complete Phase One construction
positive_highlights: Signed second multi-year off-take agreement with Stellantis (FCA) for CSPG produced at Kellyton plant
Combined agreements with SK ON and Stellantis lock up 100% of planned Phase One volumes through 2031
Contracts include indexation on flake and CSPG pricing to provide downside protection against commodity price fluctuations
summary: Westwater Resources provided a business update for Q1 FY2023 rather than financial results, announcing the signing of a second multi-year off-take agreement with Stellantis (FCA) to watch CSPG from its Kellyton plant. Management confirmed that Phase One production volumes are now fully contracted through 2031 and expects to begin supplying volume in late next year following construction completion.

negative_highlights: C1 (cash cost) decreased quarter-on-quarter to USD1.92/lb, though unit rates for milling increased due to the April shutdown.
Safety performance showed an increase in ATRISO in Q2, requiring intensive leadership training initiatives.
Production was impacted by a 10-day planned mill shutdown in April.
positive_highlights: Record production of 10,864 tons of copper, up 24% quarter-on-quarter.
Copper grade increased significantly by approximately 20% to 4.2%.
Cash and cash equivalents materially increased by 25% QoQ to over USD88 million.
summary: Metals Acquisitions Limited reported a record quarter with 10,864 tons of copper produced, up 24% quarter-on-quarter, driven by higher grades and operational consistency in May and June. The company is tracking to the midpoint of its full-year guidance range of 38,000-43,000 tonnes despite a planned mill shutdown in April. Cash and cash equivalents increased materially to over USD88 million following concentrate presales and debt repayments.

negative_highlights: Total revenue fell to $34.0 million from $36.5 million and GAAP net income dropped to $3.4 million ($0.17 per share) from $4.7 million ($0.23)
Software license and hardware revenue fell to $2.0 million from $4.6 million, and software operations bookings were down 16% at the six-month point versus the prior year

Adjusted EBITDA declined to $7.0 million from $8.5 million, and adjusted operating expenses included a one-time ~$0.9 million note and marketing benefit; Q2 also included a tough comparison to a ~$4 million contract in Q2 2023
positive_highlights: Wireless net unit churn fell to 0.8% in Q2 from 1.6% in the prior quarter; ARPU rose $0.31, or 4.1%, year over year on prior pricing actions and GenA pager sales
Software operations bookings of $8.7 million included 18 six-figure and one seven-figure contract and 14 multi-year engagements, with average contract size up nearly 14% from the prior quarter

Adjusted EBITDA of $7.0 million covered the $6.3 million returned to stockholders and capex, and cash rose to $23.9 million from $23.3 million in Q1; professional services revenue grew nearly 12% to $4.3 million
summary: Q2 FY2024 GAAP revenue fell to $34.0 million from $36.5 million a year ago, with software revenue down to $15.7 million from $17.6 million on a tough comparison to a ~$4 million single contract in Q2 2023, while wireless revenue slipped to $18.3 million from $18.9 million. GAAP net income was $3.4 million ($0.17 per diluted share) versus $4.7 million ($0.23) prior year, and adjusted EBITDA was $7.0 million versus $8.5 million, though it still covered $6.3 million returned to stockholders. Management reiterated full-year guidance of $136-144 million revenue, $27.5-32.5 million adjusted EBITDA and $25-27 million free cash flow, and reaffirmed expectations for full-year software bookings growth versus 2023. Wireless net unit churn improved to 0.8% from 1.6% in the prior quarter and ARPU rose 4.1% year over year, but software bookings of $8.7 million and license/hardware revenue of $2.0 million reflect the lumpy year-over-year decline.

negative_highlights: EBITDA remains at a nominal loss of $178,000 for the quarter.
Revenue growth is modest at only 1% year-over-year despite organic expansion efforts.
The company continues to operate with a net loss from continuing operations.
positive_highlights: Net loss from continuing operations improved by 62% year-over-year, decreasing from $3.9 million to $1.5 million.
Operating expenses reduced by 13% ($654,000) driven by a 12% decrease in G&A and 30% decrease in marketing costs.
Spetner acquisition progress is accelerating with the voluntary benefit segment growing from 45,000 to over 85,000 covered employees.
summary: Reliance Global Group reported Q2 FY2024 revenues of $3.2 million (1% YoY growth) and a net loss from continuing operations of $1.5 million, representing a 62% improvement over the prior year period. Operating expenses decreased by 13% to $4.4 million due to efficiency improvements in G&A and marketing costs. Management expressed strong confidence in the pending acquisition of Spetner Associates, noting its voluntary benefit segment has grown from 45,000 to over 85,000 covered employees, and announced plans to launch a new real estate division led by Abe Miller.

negative_highlights: HDMC operating margin down 155 basis points YoY
Asia Pacific retail down 16%, driven by China weakness
HDMC second-half operating margin guided lower due to production leverage
positive_highlights: Consolidated revenue up 12% and EPS $1.63, up 34% YoY
Touring share up 5.3 percentage points in 601+ cc market
Announced $1 billion share repurchase
summary: Harley-Davidson reported Q2 2024 consolidated revenue up 12% and EPS of $1.63, up 34% year-over-year. HDMC revenue grew 13% but operating income margin declined 155 bps, while HDFS revenue increased 10% and operating income rose 21%. The company narrowed guidance, expecting retail and wholesale to balance with dealer inventory down ~30% from current levels, and announced a $1 billion share repurchase. Retail sales in the U.S. were slightly positive, but international markets were mixed with China weakness driving Asia Pacific down 16%.

negative_highlights: Weather-related losses reached $24.7 million, representing 10.6 percentage points of the loss ratio.
Commercial property weather losses increased 90% over the prior-year quarter due to severe claims in Michigan, Indiana, Ohio, and South Carolina.
Unfavorable reserve development of $4.7 million in workers' compensation added 17.4 percentage points to that line's loss ratio.
positive_highlights: Expense ratio decreased significantly to 31.9% from 34.2% year-over-year.
Commercial lines new business targeting exceeded the 60% target with 66% in highly targeted classes.
Personal lines achieved a profitable statutory combined ratio of 95.6% driven by rate increases exceeding loss cost trends.
summary: Net premiums earned increased 8.3% to $234.3 million and net premiums written rose 9.1%, driven by double-digit rate increases averaging 11%. The combined ratio improved to 103% from 104.7% in the prior-year quarter, primarily due to a meaningful decrease in the expense ratio to 31.9% offsetting elevated weather-related losses of $24.7 million.

negative_highlights: Net interest margin slipped to 3.62% from 3.64% as deposit costs rose 18 basis points, only mostly offset by a 15-basis-point increase in loan yields.

The $24 million sale of non-core CRE loans at a weighted average rate of 3.61% produced a $1.2 million loss, and payoffs ran at $75 million in each of the first two quarters versus less than $50 million average in 2022 and 2023.
The New Jersey 2.5% surtax is expected to raise the effective tax rate by about 1% to a 24%-25% range, up from 23%-24% prior.
positive_highlights: C&I and owner-occupied CRE loans increased a combined $44.1 million, offsetting a $32.5 million decline in investor CRE loans.
New loans closed and funded rose 27% to $99 million, with C&I at 75% of that volume, up from 69% in 2023.
The probable-funding pipeline grew 14% to $342 million from $300 million at March 31.
summary: First Bank reported Q2 FY2024 net income of $11.1 million, or $0.44 per diluted share, on a 1.23% return on average assets. Net interest margin was essentially flat at 3.62% versus 3.64% in Q1. The company executed a $24 million sale of lower-yielding acquired CRE loans that produced a $1.2 million pre-tax loss, with overall loans up $5.6 million as investor CRE declined $32.5 million and owner-occupied CRE and C&I rose $44.1 million combined. Management guided to a relatively stable margin in Q3 and a 24%-25% effective tax rate, with no explicit revenue or EPS guidance.

negative_highlights: Net loss for fiscal 2024 was $27.5 million, worse than the $26.3 million loss in fiscal 2023 despite higher revenue.
Operating expenses included approximately $3.9 million in one-time costs from defending against a dissident shareholder, contributing to a net cash burn of $29.8 million from operations.
Cash and note weakness in-term investments stood at only $3.2 million as of January 31, 2024, indicating a tight liquidity position.
positive_highlights: Full-year revenue increased 102% to $5.5 million, with two-year growth exceeding 3x.
Gross margin stabilized in the 50-55% range, a significant improvement from negative gross margin in prior periods.
Backlog rose to $4.9 million from $4 million, and the pipeline was reported at $85 million, supporting fiscal 2025 guidance of $12.5 million in orders and revenue.
summary: Ocean Power Technologies reported Q4 FY2024 revenue of $1.6 million, bringing full-year revenue to $5.5 million, a 102% increase over fiscal 2023. Gross profit for the full year was $2.8 million with gross margins stabilizing in the 50-55% range, driven by the higher-margin WAM-V leasing business. The company reiterated its goal of achieving profitability in the second half of calendar 2025 and provided fiscal 2025 guidance of $12.5 million in contracted orders and revenue. Backlog stood at $4.9 million at year-end, up from $4 million, and the pipeline was reported at $85 million. Fiscal 2024 net loss was $27.5 million, including approximately $3.9 million in one-time costs related to a dissident shareholder proxy battle and litigation.

negative_highlights: Intermodal revenues decreased 14.8% to $78.1 million due to volume and rate declines.
Company-managed brokerage revenues fell 4.9% to $28.1 million with an operating loss of $2.2 million.
Trucking segment margins contracted to 4.8% from 5.4% YoY as load counts decreased 11.1%.
positive_highlights: Contract logistics revenues increased 26.2% to $263.6 million, driven by a specialty development program contributing $44.6 million.
Trucking segment revenue grew 12.6% to $91.4 million, bolstered by specialized heavy-haul wind business.
Full-year guidance for the specialty development program was raised to approximately $228 million.
summary: Universal Logistics Holdings reported Q2 FY2024 revenue of $462.2 million (up 12% YoY) and EPS of $1.17 (up 30% YoY), driven by strong contract logistics growth of 26.2%. While the company raised full-year guidance for a specific specialty development program to approximately $228 million, management noted mixed segment performance with intermodal revenue down 14.8% and brokerage underperforming due to overcapacity. Management expressed cautious optimism regarding the second half of the year pending market recovery in truckload.

negative_highlights: EPS of $0.27 with NIM at 3.15%, efficiency ratio 78% and ROE 4.7% — profitability compressed by rising deposit costs
Non-performing loans rose to ~$20.7M (1.15% of gross loans), with 76% concentrated in two projects and estimated loss exposure under 10%
Year-end Avenue deposit goal walked back from $225M to 'at least $100M,' and the Avenue launch was delayed again to v1.2 completion in September
positive_highlights: Net loans increased $51.7M for the quarter and total deposits grew $22.6M
Core deposits now 78% of total deposits with weighted average cost of 3.48%, and NIM leveled off over recent months per the monthly slide
Repurchased 41,858 shares at an average $17.50 in H1 2024, with $3.5M remaining on the buyback; stock at 75% of tangible book value
summary: Q2 EPS was $0.27 with NIM compressed to 3.15%, efficiency ratio 78%, ROA 0.5% and ROE 4.7%; results declined largely on higher deposit costs (cumulative deposit beta 63%). Net loans grew $51.7M to $1.8B and deposits rose $22.6M, but non-performing assets climbed to about $20.7M, 76% of which is two stalled projects. Management walked back the year-end Avenue deposit target, saying $225M is 'aggressive' and now shooting for at least $100M; expense run-rate guided up ~2% per month through 2024 with low single-digit loan growth. The Avenue BaaS launch was again delayed to a full v1.2 in September to avoid regulatory action.

negative_highlights: Consulting services revenue plummeted by 52% ($3.7M drop) because the company provided services to only three clients in FY2024 compared to six previously.
The company recorded an unrealized loss of $2.7 million on equity securities (KingsCrowd shares dropped from $1.00 to $0.16 per share).
Intangible assets associated with MSG and one-on-one stands were written down to zero value due to personnel departures and retirement.
positive_highlights: Portal fees increased 109% YoY to $874,368 driven by a rise in the number of successful offerings and larger capital raises per offering ($280k vs $128k).
The company successfully closed two major deals totaling nearly $8 million (Avadain at $4.5M and EarthGrid PBC at $3.3M), demonstrating platform strength despite the macro environment.
Management announced a strategic partnership with Templum Markets to launch an ATS for secondary trading of private equity securities, aiming to improve liquidity.
summary: Netcapital reported a significant decline in full-year fiscal 2024 revenues of $3.5 million (down 42% YoY) and an operating loss of $3.4 million compared to income in the prior year, driven by a collapse in consulting services revenue which fell 52%. However, portal fee revenue grew 109% to $874k due to higher average deal sizes on its funding platform.

negative_highlights: International Interactive overall revenues declined 7% year-over-year due to softness in non-UK operations, specifically Japan and Asia.

Management lowered full-year CapEx guidance to $115 million but maintained revenue expectations at the lower end of their prior range due to non-UK international softness.

negative_highlights: Portfolio comparable RevPAR growth was only 1.6% YoY, a modest result.

Seven asset sales completed for more than $310 million, including the Hilton Boston Back Bay at $171 million (~$438,000/key) with proceeds applied to debt.
Group revenue pace accelerating: full-year group revenue +5%, Q3-through-year-end +11% (Q4 +19%), and 2025 group revenue +20% with room nights up ~15%.
summary: AHT reported Q2 FY2024 net income attributable to common stockholders of $44.3 million ($0.25/diluted share), AFFO per diluted share of $0.27, and Adjusted EBITDAre of $78.7 million. Group pace accelerated (2024 group revenue +5%, Q3-through-year-end +11%, 2025 +20%) but the quarter's headline RevPAR growth of just 1.6% and softening resort trends keep the read balanced.

Graphic Arts sale expected at slightly lower price than previously anticipated
positive_highlights: Sequential sales up 10.5% and adjusted EBITDA up 65% from Q1

The company raised its full-year 2024 guidance for adjusted EBITDA to $47-50 million, EPS to $0.90-$1.00, and free cash flow to $24-27 million, though the underlying guidance excluding the legal recovery is slightly lower. Management remains cautious on the short-term revenue outlook but expects growth in 2025 from new product launches and the sale of Graphic Arts is targeted for Q3.

US government RFP timing uncertain, awaiting ASPR issuance
positive_highlights: Product revenue $21M in Q2 vs $1M year-ago, $45M H1 vs $7M

Management expressed confidence in securing a new, longer-dated US government contract exceeding the current $546 million value. Net income for the quarter was $2 million, EPS $0.03, cash at $107 million, no debt.

negative_highlights: Higher depreciation and amortization decreased earnings by $0.18 per share reflecting capital investment programs.

Received approval for a modified clean heat plant in Colorado with up to $441 million budget approved.
summary: Xcel Energy reported Q2 FY2024 EPS of $0.54 versus the prior year's $0.52, driven by rate case recoveries and AFUDC while offsetting higher depreciation and interest costs. Management reaffirmed its full-year 2024 earnings guidance range of $3.50 to $3.60 per share despite updating sales forecasts upward due to data center load growth. The company highlighted significant progress in wildfire mitigation, including the filing of updated plans in Colorado and Texas, alongside a robust pipeline for clean energy resources.

negative_highlights: Transportation expenses up 24% due to low river levels from El Nino

CapEx increased to $61 million in Q2 from $55 million in prior quarter

Management highlighted the shareholder value plan: the post-quarter sale of Hilton La Jolla Torrey Pines for $165 million, all 2024 debt maturities addressed, and approximately $40.1 million of preferred redemptions against a $50 million program, with the $50 million common buyback authorized but not yet executed. No explicit forward financial guidance was given; management noted 2025 group rooms revenue pace ahead by 20% and a path to roughly 35% leverage by this time next year.

Operating income fell to $1.4 million from $1.7 million, while adjusted operating margin contracted to 5.6% from 7%. The quarter included a one-time net loss of $27.8 million due to the termination charge for Pension Plan I ($38.2M gross), which obscured underlying operational performance.

negative_highlights: Gross margin declined to 64% from 66% year-over-year
Operating expenses increased 24% year-over-year
Some hospital deals delayed waiting for final CMS rule
positive_highlights: Revenue increased 39% year-over-year to $2.23 million
CMS proposed TULSA CPT codes with hospital payment ~$9,200 and non-facility ~$9,400
CAPTAIN trial added Stanford and Mayo Clinic, reinforcing recruitment progress
summary: Profound Medical reported Q2 2024 revenue of $2.23 million, up 39% year-over-year, with gross margin at 64% and net loss improved to $6.9 million from $7.3 million. The company reaffirmed full-year 2024 revenue guidance of $11-12 million. Management highlighted proposed CMS category I CPT codes for TULSA with payments favorable across hospital, ASC, and non-facility settings, and noted accelerated site onboarding for CAPTAIN trial including Stanford and Mayo Clinic.

negative_highlights: A one-time $6 billion noncash goodwill impairment charge was recorded for the cable network supporting unit at TV Media.
Paramount+ subscriber count decreased by 2.8 million quarter-over-quarter due to planned exits and elevated churn from Super Bowl cohorts.
Total company advertising revenue declined 6% in Q2, negatively impacted by sports comprising a smaller share of inventory.
positive_highlights: D2C segment achieved profitability in Q2, marking its first profitable quarter since launch over three years ago.
Paramount+ subscription revenue grew 12% year-over-year with total subscribers reaching 68.4 million despite a planned exit of hard bundles.
Total company adjusted OIBDA expanded significantly by 43%, driven largely by D2C improvements.
summary: Paramount Global reported Q2 FY2024 results with total company adjusted OIBDA growing 43% year-over-year and D2C segment achieving profitability for the first time since launch in late 2019. However, revenue growth was muted by a planned exit of hard bundles in South Korea (reducing sub count) and elevated churn from Super Bowl subscribers, while total company advertising declined 6%. The quarter included significant non-cash charges: a $300-$400 million restructuring charge for workforce reductions to realize identified cost savings and a one-time $6 billion goodwill impairment related to the cable network supporting unit.

negative_highlights: Q2 specific financials not detailed in provided transcript segment
GMP facility build-out may take up to three years and revenue not expected until after 2026
positive_highlights: Reiterated full-year 2024 guidance with clear visibility to double-digit product revenue growth
Technical progress ahead of expectations, with TIDES USA demonstrating full-length oligonucleotide synthesis
Pharma customers receptive to engineered ligase, driving new pipeline and confidence in additional orders
summary: Codexis reported Q2 FY2024 results, reiterating full-year 2024 guidance and expecting double-digit product revenue growth in the second half. The company highlighted progress on its ECO Synthesis platform for siRNA manufacturing, including demonstration of full-length oligonucleotide synthesis and launch of double-stranded RNA ligase services. Management is confident in the technology's commercial potential, with strategies to move up the value chain and achieve positive cash flow around end of 2026.

negative_highlights: Net sales declined 13.1% year-over-year, with pricing down 2.6% and volume mix down 10.3%.
Adjusted gross profit margin contracted to 24.4% from 27% in the prior year period.
Consumable product sales growth was weaker than hoped due to oversupply in the cannabis industry.
positive_highlights: May marked the seventh consecutive month of sequential net sales growth, the longest streak since going public in 2020.
Adjusted SG&A expenses decreased by over 20% year-over-year to $11.6 million due to restructuring and cost-saving actions.
The company delivered positive adjusted EBITDA for the fourth time in the last five quarters.
summary: Hydrofarm reported Q2 FY2024 net sales of $54.8 million, a 13.1% year-over-year decline driven by volume mix and pricing pressures. Adjusted gross profit margin was 24.4%, down from 27% in the prior year period, though management noted this represented the third-highest quarterly level since the IPO. The company reaffirmed its full-year 2024 guidance for net sales (low to high teens decline), positive adjusted EBITDA, and positive free cash flow.

negative_highlights: Statutory combined RBC ratio fell to 380%-400%, below the 400%-450% target, from a ~$600 million statutory loss.
Basis risk and equity hedge underperformance accounted for ~70% of the statutory loss, with new Shield business now a capital consumer.
Fixed deferred annuity sales were lower due to reinsurer transition, and LifePath Paycheck inflows are expected to be uneven, with minimal Q3 activity.
positive_highlights: Record Q2 Shield annuity sales exceeded $2 billion, with year-to-date sales up 23% to $3.9 billion.
Adjusted earnings of $346 million beat the prior quarter's $268 million (ex-notable), with no notable items.
Corporate expenses year-to-date down ~6% vs. prior year, and holding company liquidity strong at $1.2 billion.
summary: Q2 adjusted earnings were $346M or $5.57 per share, above the first quarter's $268M (ex-notable items) and up from $271M in Q2 2023, driven by higher underwriting margins and seasonal items. Record Shield annuity sales exceeded $2B in the quarter, with year-to-date Shield sales up 23% to $3.9B, and LifePath Paycheck brought in $340M of first deposits. However, preliminary statutory combined RBC ratio dropped to 380%-400%, at or below the 400%-450% target, due to a ~$600M statutory loss from VA and Shield hedging and basis risk. Management expects initiatives, including reinsurance and stand-alone Shield hedging, to restore RBC to target within 6-12 months, with year-end as a likely timeframe.

negative_highlights: Management explicitly stated they do not assume any opt-in from AbbVie or other milestones in their cash runway calculation, indicating reliance on current funding.
The company did not report a specific financial beat against consensus estimates for revenue or EPS in the transcript text provided.
positive_highlights: Cash runway extends through 2026, covering approximately one year beyond the pivotal INFRONT-3 Phase 3 data readout expected in late 2025/early 2026.
FDA Type B meeting provided clarity that plasma and CSF progranulin levels will be considered confirmatory evidence for latozinemab approval, supplementing clinical effects pending BLA review.
INVOK-2 trial baseline characteristics confirmed enrollment of the intended early Alzheimer's disease population with a mean centiloid level of 100.1.
summary: Alector reported Q2 FY2024 financial results with a cash position of $503.3 million and a runway extending through 2026 without assuming new milestones or business development activity. Management reiterated guidance for collaboration revenue between $60M-$70M, R&D expenses between $210M-$220M, and G&A between $60M-$70M. The company highlighted progress on the AL002 Phase 2 trial (INVOK-2) baseline characteristics and FDA feedback for latozinemab but did not report a financial beat or miss against consensus.

negative_highlights: Revenue was flat YoY and below expectations, with wholesale rollouts delayed to 2025.
Annual revenue guidance cut to $385-415 million from prior forecast, driven by slower FDM load-ins.
DTC business continues to decline, prompting reduced investment in that channel.
positive_highlights: Gross margin of 42% in Q2, a ~700 bps improvement YoY, exceeding the prior 40% target.
Adjusted EBITDA improved from breakeven to $8.5 million, and free cash flow turned positive at $1 million, up $31 million YoY.
Wholesale consumption growth of 28% in Q2 and 35% YTD, outpacing a category decline, with Walmart sales up 19%.
summary: Black Rifle Coffee's Q2 2024 revenue was flat year-over-year, missing expectations due to slower-than-expected wholesale rollouts and a strategic pullback in DTC investment. Gross margin improved to 42%, up ~700 bps, and adjusted EBITDA reached $8.5 million versus breakeven last year, with positive free cash flow of $1 million. The company lowered 2024 revenue guidance to $385-415 million from prior levels but raised gross margin guidance to 39-42% and reiterated adjusted EBITDA guidance of $32-42 million. Management expects revenue inflection in 2025 driven by FDM expansion, new energy drink launch, and DTC stabilization.

negative_highlights: Production curtailments in East Texas due to significant flooding events over 100 days reduced volumes from that asset base.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA beat expectations driven by strong Beta development and a one-time accounting adjustment of approximately $7 million.
A50 Well achieved gross peak IP30 oil rate of ~730 bopd, exceeding the upper end of cumulative production range presented in investor deck.
Company generated positive free cash flow for 16 of last 17 quarters.
summary: Amplify Energy reported Q2 FY2024 adjusted EBITDA of $30.7 million and free cash flow of $9.2 million, both exceeding expectations due to strong Beta development results (A50 well IP rate ~730 bopd) and a one-time prior period accounting adjustment adding approximately $7 million to earnings. Management raised full-year 2024 capital guidance from the original range by electing to participate in non-operated wells, now expecting total investment of $60-65 million against WTI prices at $76/bbl.

negative_highlights: IoT revenue fell to $6.7 million from $11.5 million a year earlier on lower BLE transponder sales
IoT non-GAAP gross margin contracted to 14.6% from 16.6% on underutilized Southeast Asia plants and Thailand ramp costs
Aggregated adjusted EBITDA swung to negative $2.0 million from positive $0.7 million, and Q3 IoT guidance of $5.8–6.1 million implies further sequential decline
positive_highlights: Total company revenue exceeded consensus per the CEO, and cash ended better than internal forecasts at $19 million
CFIUS is the only remaining regulatory hurdle to the Vitaprotech sale after a 96% shareholder approval vote and antitrust/UK clearance; ~$130 million net proceeds expected
Thailand facility achieved ISO 9001 and ISO 14001 certification, with production transition on track for majority completion by Q1 2025
summary: Continuing-operations IoT revenue fell to $6.7 million from $11.5 million a year earlier, with non-GAAP gross margin of 14.6% down from 16.6% and an IoT adjusted EBITDA loss of $3.7 million versus a $2.6 million loss. Aggregated non-GAAP revenue (including soon-to-be-divested Physical Security) was $24.3 million versus $29.6 million, and aggregated adjusted EBITDA swung to negative $2.0 million from positive $0.7 million. Q3 IoT guidance is $5.8–6.1 million, implying a sequential decline from Q2, though combined revenue of $24–26 million is guided if the divestiture has not closed. The pending Vitaprotech asset sale (expected ~$130 million net proceeds) awaits CFIUS approval, and management framed 26–28% IoT gross margin and EBITDA breakeven at $60–70 million of annual sales as longer-term targets once the Thailand transition completes in Q1 2025.

negative_highlights: Net revenue declined 20.6% year-over-year to $28 million
Q3 revenue guidance of $25–27 million implies roughly a 35% year-over-year decrease
Some dehumidifier SKUs sold out in early July, with full restock not expected until mid-August
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA positive at $0.2 million, beating guidance of a $1 million loss to breakeven and marking the first profitable quarter since Q3 2021
Gross margin expanded to 60.4% from 42.2% in the year-ago quarter
Second-quarter net loss improved 89.6% year-over-year to $3.6 million
summary: Aterian reported Q2 2024 net revenue of $28 million, down 20.6% year-over-year, but essentially flat when excluding the impact of prior SKU rationalization. Gross margin improved to 60.4% from 42.2% a year ago, and adjusted EBITDA turned positive at $0.2 million, the first profitable quarter in 10 quarters and ahead of guidance. For Q3, net revenue is guided to $25–27 million (about a 35% year-over-year decline, or a 12% decline including the SKU rationalization impact), with adjusted EBITDA between breakeven and a $0.6 million loss, representing a significant year-over-year improvement. Management expects second-half 2024 adjusted EBITDA profitability, with growth initiatives planned for 2025.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA remained a loss of $37.4 million and GAAP net loss was $97 million
Total private jet FTV was down 19% year-over-year
Revenue was flat sequentially at $196 million with no explicit guidance provided

Prepaid block sales of $145 million, up 27% sequentially and 50% year-over-year

summary: Revenue was $196 million in Q2, flat sequentially, with the year-over-year comp depressed by prior exits from aircraft management, aircraft sales and unprofitable flight revenue. Adjusted contribution margin rose to 7.8% from 1.0% in Q1 and 5.4% in Q2 2023, adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed to $37.4 million from $49.2 million in Q1, prepaid block sales rose 27% sequentially and 50% year-over-year, and operating cash outflow fell 63% sequentially. Management gave no explicit revenue or EPS guidance but reiterated the goal of positive adjusted EBITDA later this year and pointed to significant Q3 margin improvement. Charter FTV rose 16% year-over-year to 61% of total FTV, though total private jet FTV remained down 19% year-over-year.

negative_highlights: Consolidated revenues decreased by 4% year-over-year, with a $9 million GAAP net loss

Management indicated potential for further runoff in the reviewed public and private real estate funds

Wealth management segment revenue grew 20% due to acquisitions and organic growth
Adjusted EBITDA margin in the core wealth division improved to 23%
summary: AlTi reported Q2 FY2024 revenues of $49 million (a decrease from the prior year) and a GAAP net loss of $9 million compared to income in the same period last year. The decline was driven by lower other income due to unrealized losses on earn-out liabilities, though adjusted EBITDA remained positive at $5.5 million with an 11% margin. Management highlighted significant M&A activity including acquisitions of East End Advisors and Envoi, alongside a strategic review of real estate businesses that may lead to further AUM runoff.

negative_highlights: Revenue decreased 5% year-over-year due to demand environment headwinds and pricing pressure.

Net revenue retention of publishers was 89%, reflecting downward pressure on ad impressions from certain key supply partners.

RPMs grew year-over-year for the third consecutive quarter, driven by improved click-through rates.
Zemanta DSP advertiser spend grew approximately 50% compared to the first half of 2023.
summary: Outbrain reported Q2 FY2024 revenue of approximately $214 million, a 5% year-over-year decrease, with adjusted EBITDA of $7.4 million exceeding guidance by $7.4 million. Management raised full-year 2024 adjusted EBITDA guidance to $31.5-$36 million while maintaining gross profit guidance, citing positive trends in RPMs and a strategic shift toward higher-margin segments like the Zemanta DSP. The company announced a definitive agreement to acquire Teads, expected to close in Q1 2025, which will significantly alter its financial profile and growth trajectory.

negative_highlights: Life Sciences Data & Solutions gross profit decreased by 17.9%, attributed to project timing rather than structural issues.
Aerospace division experienced a slower-than-anticipated recovery in the aftermarket, though EBITDA remains healthy.
SG&A expenses increased over 6% YoY due to inflation and strategic investments in technology infrastructure.
positive_highlights: Engineering gross profit grew by 23.7% YoY, driven by ramping project activity and new client wins.
Healthcare school revenue reached $109.8 million for the year-to-date period, growing 24.9% over prior years excluding COVID impact.
Adjusted EBITDA grew by 10.8% to $7.2 million despite higher SG&A driven by technology and cybersecurity investments.
summary: RCM Technologies reported Q2 FY2024 consolidated gross profit growth of 6.6% to $20.0 million and Adjusted EBITDA growth of 10.8% to $7.2 million, with Adjusted diluted EPS rising 12.0% YoY to $0.56. Management highlighted strong performance in the Engineering division (up 23.7% gross profit) and Healthcare schools business (school revenue up 23.0%), while noting a timing-related dip in Life Sciences Data & Solutions (-17.9%). The company reiterated optimism for low double-digit consolidated Adjusted EBITDA growth in the second half of fiscal 2024.

negative_highlights: Q2 adjusted EBITDA of $120 million missed the $275 million target by $155 million, driven by the several-month delay in FLNG 1 deployment
GAAP net loss of $89 million, or $0.44 per diluted share, versus positive adjusted net income in the prior periods
Q3 2024 adjusted EBITDA will be reduced below the $275 million goal as full FLNG 1 production is not expected until early September
positive_highlights: FLNG 1 came online July 19, 2024, with first partial cargo transferred and expected to generate roughly $500 million of annual free cash flow on a $2 billion-plus investment
2025 EBITDA guidance of $1.3 billion is supported by approximately 170 TBtu of supply and a weighted average net margin of about $7, with over 90% of expected revenues contracted
Brazil contracted EBITDA is forecast at about $470 million by 2026, with an additional approximately $400 million potential from a Santa Catarina power auction
summary: NFE reported Q2 2024 adjusted EBITDA of $120 million, well below its $275 million quarterly target and down from $384 million in Q1, with the $155 million miss attributed entirely to the delayed deployment of the first FLNG asset. GAAP net loss was $89 million, or $0.44 per diluted share, and total segment operating margin was $248 million versus $384 million in Q1. Management guided to roughly $275 million of quarterly adjusted EBITDA for the remainder of the year, though Q3 will be somewhat reduced as FLNG 1 only reached first cargo in July and full production is not expected until early September; 2024 EBITDA guidance is $1.4–$1.5 billion and 2025 guidance is $1.3 billion. The FLNG 1 unit, a $2 billion-plus investment now online, is expected to generate about $500 million of annual free cash flow, and the company is pursuing refinancing of its 2025 notes while targeting below 4x senior secured leverage by 2026.

negative_highlights: Transaction units remained down about 3% YoY despite a 7% rise in gross transaction value
Commission split widened 150 bps, driven partly by Florida rising to 30% of existing home sales from 27% and larger luxury transactions
H1 net loss widened to $43.1 million ($0.52/share) from $22.8 million, including a $17.75 million litigation settlement charge; no formal guidance was given
positive_highlights: Q2 adjusted EBITDA swung to income of $2.4 million from a $2.6 million loss in the prior year period
Real estate brokerage segment returned to operating income of $2.9 million versus a $1.0 million operating loss a year ago
Listing volume rose 23% YoY and development marketing pipeline stands at about $26.5 billion gross transaction value, including $16 billion in Florida
summary: Douglas Elliman reported Q2 revenue of $285.8 million, up roughly 4% from $275.9 million, with net loss attributable to the company narrowing to $1.7 million ($0.02/share) from $5.2 million ($0.06/share) and adjusted EBITDA swinging to positive $2.4 million from a $2.6 million loss. The brokerage segment returned to operating income of $2.9 million versus a $1.0 million loss, helped by about $11.3 million of H1 expense reductions (down 7.9% YoY ex-commission). Gross transaction value rose about 7% and listing volume 23%, but transaction units were still down 3% and commission split worsened 150 bps; no formal guidance was provided. The six-month picture was weaker, with net loss of $43.1 million including a $17.75 million litigation settlement charge and adjusted EBITDA loss of $15.9 million, while a $50 million Kennedy Lewis investment in July added liquidity.

negative_highlights: Total revenue declined 2% year-over-year primarily driven by a 71% drop in Revenue Per Session (RPS) and lower US CPMs.
Partner Network revenue fell 12% YoY as the business continues to face headwinds from reduced pricing power in key markets.
Management explicitly stated that new initiatives like shopping partnerships and subscription products are not expected to contribute meaningfully until late Q4 or beyond.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA of $9.9 million beat high-end guidance by ~$2.9M despite a sequential decline in comparable advertising demand from last year's Q2 to Q3.
Owned and operated revenue grew sequentially up 12% driven by international expansion (now 36% of segment) and organic traffic boosts on CouponFollow following Google algorithm changes.
Operating expenses decreased significantly, down 16% YoY due to cost-cutting initiatives post-total security sale.
summary: System1 reported Q2 FY2024 revenue of $94.6 million (a 2% YoY decline) and adjusted EBITDA of $9.9 million, which beat the high end of guidance by approximately $3 million despite a sequential step-down in advertising demand from last year's Q2 to Q3. Management noted that while owned-and-operated products showed strong growth driven by international expansion and organic traffic trends (CouponFollow), overall revenue was pressured by lower US CPMs and a mix shift to international markets with lower monetization rates. For the forward-looking period, guidance for Q3 calls for roughly flat year-over-year revenue at $86-88 million.

negative_highlights: FYARRO revenue was flat year-over-year at $6.2 million; management said it has penetrated most of the PEComa market and future growth will be incremental
The prior PRECISION1 interim showed TSC2 ORR of just 11% (vs 26% for TSC1), and the upcoming two-thirds readout is a binary near-term event with no directional guidance
No updates to full-year revenue or EPS guidance were provided
positive_highlights: FYARRO sales rose 15% sequentially to $6.2 million, with a 14% increase in ordering accounts versus Q1
Net loss narrowed to $14.6 million from $18 million in the prior-year quarter, aided by SG&A reduction to $7.9 million from $11.8 million
Cash of $78.6 million funds operations into Q4 2025, and PRECISION1 completed enrollment of 120 patients
summary: Aadi Bioscience reported Q2 2024 FYARRO product sales of $6.2 million, in line with the prior-year period but up 15% sequentially, with ordering accounts rising 14% from Q1. Net loss narrowed to $14.6 million from $18 million a year ago, while R&D was flat at $13.1 million and SG&A fell to $7.9 million from $11.8 million. Management continued to emphasize the PRECISION1 tumor-agnostic trial, with a planned two-thirds interim readout expected later in Q3 2024 and full enrollment of 120 patients on track to complete by year-end. The company reiterated a cash runway into Q4 2025 and cited a $300–600 million U.S. market opportunity for TSC1/TSC2 mutated cancers, but provided no new guidance on FYARRO growth, and the prior interim data showed a wide gap between TSC1 (26% ORR) and TSC2 (11% ORR) arms.

negative_highlights: Rental income declined 4% due to dispositions and decreased tenant reimbursements on sold properties.
Cash position reduced by $3.2 million from a property acquisition and share repurchase of First City Investment Group shares.
Management describes the industrial manufacturing transaction market as 'choppy' with limited volume.
positive_highlights: Adjusted funds from operations (AFFO) grew 17% YoY to $3.9 million despite lower rental income.
Portfolio weighted average lease term is attractive at 13.6 years following the Tampa acquisition.
summary: Rental income decreased by $0.5 million (4% YoY) to $11.3 million due to tenant reimbursements on sold properties and dispositions of non-core assets. Adjusted AFFO increased 17% year-over-year primarily driven by a decrease in property expenses, though this was partially offset by an increase in diluted shares outstanding from share repurchases.

negative_highlights: Cash flow continues to be impacted by elevated note weakness in-term interest rates and higher allocated interest expense of $1 million.
Rental rates at two largest Oakland multifamily properties remain below expectations due to high supply.
CEO expects office occupancy to decline in the third quarter following a 130,000 square foot tenant give-back.

Multifamily occupancy improved significantly to 92.5% at quarter-end from 79.3% a year ago.
New lease rates for multifamily tenants exceeded in-place rents by more than 20%.
summary: CMCT reported Q2 FY2024 segment NOI of $16.2 million, a $4.2 million increase from the prior year driven by office ($2.1M), multifamily ($1.7M), and hotel ($0.2M) segments. FFO was negative $0.14 per diluted share compared to negative $0.19 in the prior year, reflecting higher interest expenses and preferred dividends despite improved operating income. Management noted a specific headwind from soft rental rates at Bay Area multifamily assets and an expected occupancy decline in Q3 due to a large tenant giving back 130,000 square feet.

negative_highlights: Q2 2024 revenue of EUR 780,000 came in below analyst modeling and declined sequentially from stronger prior periods.
Total operating loss widened to EUR 13.3 million from EUR 11.9 million in Q2 2023, with further cash burn increases expected in H2 2024.
No formal revenue guidance was provided, and management noted quarter-to-quarter sales are difficult to forecast and may vary due to a limited number of implanting accounts.
positive_highlights: H1 2024 European sales of EUR 2 million, up 29% versus H1 2023, with 55 active implanting accounts in Germany.
Raised over EUR 85 million in gross capital (EUR 48.5 million equity offering plus EUR 37.5 million EIB loan), extending cash runway into mid-2026.
Completed modular PMA submission for Genio; FDA approval anticipated as early as year-end 2024 based on 180-day review clock and positive FDA engagement.
summary: Nyxoah reported Q2 2024 revenue of EUR 780,000 (H1 revenue EUR 2 million, up 29% YoY) and a total operating loss of EUR 13.3 million versus EUR 11.9 million in Q2 2023. On the call, management noted Q2 revenue came in below analyst modeling and declined sequentially despite overall market growth. The company raised over EUR 85 million in gross capital and extended its cash runway into mid-2026 to fund U.S. launch preparations. The fourth and final PMA module for the Genio system is submitted, with FDA approval anticipated between late 2024 and early 2025, and the U.S. commercial organization is being built.

negative_highlights: Two HCV relapses in the leading cohort due to patient non-adherence, highlighting adherence challenges
R&D expenses increased markedly in Q2 due to trial enrollment completion
COVID-19 Phase 3 enrollment skewed heavily to monotherapy cohort, with only 74 patients in combination cohort
positive_highlights: HCV Phase 2 leading cohort achieved 97% SVR-12 with 8-week treatment
Selected fixed dose combination tablet reducing pill burden from 4 to 2 pills daily for Phase 3
Cash runway extended into 2027 with $502.2 million at June 30, 2024
summary: Atea reported Q2 2024 with no product revenue, a cash position of $502.2 million, and a marked increase in R&D expenses from advancing its Phase 3 SUNRISE-3 COVID-19 trial and Phase 2 HCV trial. Enrollment completed in both trials, with positive interim HCV data showing 97% SVR-12 in a 60-patient cohort, and the company expects to report full results from both trials in the second half of 2024. Management guided to a cash runway into 2027 and targeted an NDA submission for bemnifosbuvir around year-end.

negative_highlights: $7.9 million of Q2 biorefining revenue was non-cash LanzaJet equity consideration; ex-this, biorefining revenue was only $5.8 million
Guidance remains heavily back-half weighted with Q3 expected similar to Q2, and management flagged that FID timing slips into next year could jeopardize the full-year revenue guide

positive_highlights: Revenue of $17.4 million grew 35% YoY and 70% QoQ, exceeding expectations

Q2 cash burn of $16.5 million fell sharply from $29.2 million in Q1 2024
summary: Revenue was $17.4 million, up 35% YoY and 70% QoQ, ahead of expectations, but $7.9 million of the biorefining revenue came from non-cash LanzaJet equity consideration; excluding it, biorefining revenue was $5.8 million. Gross margin was 68% (42% ex-LanzaJet) and adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed 26% YoY to $17.8 million. Full-year 2024 revenue guidance of $90-105 million and adjusted EBITDA of -$65 to -$55 million were reaffirmed, but management again weighted revenue to Q4 and cautioned project timing slippage could jeopardize the guide. Cash fell to $75.8 million from $92.3 million, with a new $40 million convertible note (8% PIK, $1.52 conversion) announced alongside litigation over a Forward Purchase Agreement.

negative_highlights: NAV per share declined about 1% due to two new nonaccruals
Unrealized losses of $0.22 per share partly offset gains
Spreads compressed modestly, ~25 bps quarter-over-quarter
positive_highlights: Record Q2 originations of $360 million, up from $110 million a year ago
Net investment income of $0.57 per share exceeded total dividends of $0.55
First lien senior loans grew to 91% of portfolio fair value, highest in past year

New originations were a record $360 million, with over 95% in first lien senior secured loans, but net asset value fell about 1% due to unrealized losses from two new nonaccruals (0.49% of fair value). The company reaffirmed its leverage target of 1.0-1.25x and expects continued robust deal flow in the second half of 2024.

negative_highlights: Political advertising expected to remain only 2-3% of H2 spend
Cookie deprecation reversal adds uncertainty, though company sees it as helpful
AI product timeline has some features not yet fully released (Chat with Data in Q4)
positive_highlights: Record advertiser spend exceeded seasonally strong Q4 2023
Adjusted EBITDA up 41% YoY to $9.6M
CTV spend grew over 40% YoY; streaming audio nearly doubled
summary: Viant reported record Q2 2024 advertiser spend, with revenue up 15% YoY and contribution ex-TAC up 23%, while adjusted EBITDA grew 41% to $9.6M. CTV spend grew over 40% and streaming audio nearly doubled YoY, together representing over 50% of platform spend. The company rebranded its AI suite as ViantAI, with new LLM-based planning, and expects Chat with Data in Q4 and autonomous optimization in 2025. Q3 guidance was raised (implied by context), with overhead growth expected in the low teens for 2024.

negative_highlights: Total revenue declined 11% year-over-year due to a 12% drop in brokerage revenue.
Real estate transaction volume fell 7.9% to 10,137 transactions, primarily due to high mortgage interest rates.
Management withheld Q3 guidance citing the yet-to-be-determined impact of new commission plans.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA turned positive at $189,000, the first positive quarter since Q2 2023.
Mortgage revenue surged 85% year-over-year to $3.7 million, driven by a doubling of the loan officer base.
Verus Title revenues increased 10% to $1.1 million and achieved positive adjusted EBITDA of $108,000.
summary: Total revenue decreased 11% to $89.2 million in Q2 FY2024 compared to $100.1 million a year ago, driven by a 12% decline in brokerage revenue and the sale of the insurance business. Adjusted EBITDA turned positive at $189,000 for the quarter, marking the first positive result since Q2 2023, while GAAP net loss narrowed to $1.3 million. Management elected to withhold guidance for Q3 due to the recent launch of new revenue share models and expects to reinstate guidance in Q4.

negative_highlights: Same-station local revenue declined 10% due to a 3% drop in agency business and 4.9% decline in direct.
Auto category revenue fell 18.5% year-over-year, primarily driven by a 60% drop in domestic auto spend.
Pacings for the second half of the year are down to low-to-mid-single digits.
positive_highlights: Digital revenue grew 10.2% year-over-year, now accounting for 21.5% of total revenue.
Political revenue exceeded budget by 72%, generating $586,000 in net revenue.
Operating income turned positive at $5.4 million, a 219% increase from the prior year quarter.
summary: Second quarter same-station revenue declined 2% year-over-year to $60.4 million total net revenue, driven by a 10.9% drop in local spot and divestitures, while digital revenue grew 10.2%. Adjusted EBITDA increased 11.4% to $8.8 million due to expense reductions of $2 million (including $1.3M severance) and debt interest savings, though operating income remains volatile at $5.4 million. Management lowered full-year revenue paces to low-to-mid-single digits and emphasized a strategic focus on deleveraging ahead of the 2026 bond maturity.

negative_highlights: Revenue decreased $74,000 year-over-year due to the termination of the Patient Therapy Access Program on June 30, 2023.
Temporary cash pay pricing was terminated in May 2024, contributing to lower Q2 revenue.
PoNS sales have been muted primarily because they have been on a cash pay basis with a price point not feasible for most patients.
positive_highlights: Secured first third-party reimbursement of $23,900 from a major insurance carrier in May.
PoNS approved for inclusion in Lovell's VA federal supply schedule and DAPA contract at pricing of ~$23k and ~$7k respectively.
Stroke registrational program fully enrolled with results expected to bolster FDA submission in 2025.
summary: Total revenue for Q2 FY2024 was $182,000, a decrease of $74,000 year-over-year due to the termination of the Patient Therapy Access Program and temporary cash pay pricing. Operating loss remained flat at $3.2 million compared to the prior year period. Management expressed cautious optimism regarding future revenue growth driven by expected Medicare reimbursement effective October 1st and new VA contracts.

negative_highlights: Vessel acquisition opportunities are constrained by MR prices reaching 10-year historical highs and younger eco MR values approaching newbuild cost
The MR2 order book stands at 274 vessels, or 16.1% of the global fleet as of July 31, with 104 MRs scheduled for delivery by end-2025
Weighted average interest rate was 8% in the quarter, and crack spreads and consumption are moderating heading into the seasonally slower third quarter
positive_highlights: TCE revenues rose almost 42% year-over-year to $12.2 million, aided by the addition of dry bulk vessels and higher spot income
Net income to common shareholders reached $5.0 million, or $0.48 basic EPS, versus $2.8 million and $0.25 basic in Q2 2023
Q3 MR bookings at 68% of available days show an estimated average TC rate of $33,850 per day, above the Q2 average of $32,868
summary: Pyxis Tankers reported Q2 2024 TCE revenues of $12.2 million, up almost 42% year-over-year, with net income to common shareholders of $5.0 million ($0.48 basic EPS) versus $2.8 million ($0.25 basic) in Q2 2023. Adjusted EBITDA rose $2.8 million to $8.0 million, supported by MR daily TCE of $32,868 and bulker daily TCE of $22,333. Management did not provide formal financial guidance but noted 68% of Q3 MR available days booked at an estimated $33,850 per day and 76% of bulker days booked at $17,200 per day. The fleet expanded to six vessels with the late-June acquisition of the Kamsarmax Konkar Venture, and the company continues share repurchases and debt amortization while citing high asset prices for acquisition selectivity.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to $3.5M from $1.9M in prior year
SG&A expenses increased to $19M from $13.8M
New interest expense on CRG term loan and higher amortization
positive_highlights: 11th consecutive record revenue quarter; revenue up 28% YoY
Soft tissue product sales grew from $13.2M to $17.6M year-over-year
Surgical segment generated positive EBITDA of $1.4M in Q2
summary: Sanara MedTech reported Q2 2024 revenue of $20.2 million, up 28% year-over-year, marking the 11th consecutive record quarter, with soft tissue products driving growth from $13.2 million to $17.6 million. The company generated positive adjusted EBITDA of $600,000, though net loss widened to $3.5 million due to higher SG&A and interest expenses. Management guided to additional $4-5 million investment in Tissue Health Plus in H2 2024, with a pilot launch planned for Q1 2025 and commercial launch in H2 2025. The new CRG debt facility provides non-dilutive capital, and the Surgical segment remains EBITDA positive.

negative_highlights: Full-year 2024 revenue guidance was lowered from mid-single-digit growth to roughly flat versus 2023
H1 2024 shipments with existing customers fell 9% versus H1 2023, partly due to the FedEx contract change and lower parcel volumes
Q3 adjusted EBITDA may be slightly negative, and H2 gross margins are expected below H1 2024
positive_highlights: Gross margin expanded to 39% in Q2 2024 from 30% in Q2 2023, lifting gross profit 32% to $2.1 million
Adjusted EBITDA was positive $0.2 million, the fourth consecutive quarter of positive adjusted EBITDA
New customer count in the proactive service line rose 7% in H1 2024 versus H1 2023, and the company added two sales representatives as planned
summary: Q2 2024 revenue was $5.4 million, effectively flat versus $5.3 million in Q2 2023, while gross margin expanded to 39% from 30% and adjusted EBITDA turned positive at $0.2 million, the fourth consecutive positive quarter. Management lowered full-year 2024 revenue guidance from mid-single-digit growth to roughly flat versus 2023, citing a FedEx subcontract change and a 9% decline in existing-customer parcel volumes, and said Q3 adjusted EBITDA may be slightly negative though H2 and full year should remain positive. Gross profit, gross margin and adjusted EBITDA are still expected to exceed 2023, and the company ended the quarter with $2.9 million of cash and $2.2 million of remaining debt.

negative_highlights: Pediatric revenue declined 10% year-over-year due to soft census
DaVita pilot progress slower than anticipated
Cash balance only $1 million; completed $2 million offering
positive_highlights: Gross margin expanded to 67.2% from 55.3% year-over-year
Operating loss improved by $2.7 million versus prior year
First commercial sale of QUELIMMUNE to Cincinnati Children's Hospital
summary: Nuwellis reported Q2 2024 revenue of $2.2 million, up 6% year-over-year, driven by a 30% increase in heart failure and critical care consumables utilization, though pediatric revenue fell 10% due to lower census. Gross margin improved to 67.2% from 55.3%, and operating loss narrowed to $2.3 million from $5.0 million. The company secured first commercial sale of QUELIMMUNE, but noted slower-than-expected progress with the DaVita pilot and cash balances are low at $1 million, with a recent $2 million offering.

negative_highlights: GLA oil revenues declined as the company note through remaining inventory, expected to trend toward zero contribution.
SG&A expenses of $2.7 million included nearly $0.5 million in one-time M&A fees related to the two transactions.
Full-year 2024 revenue is expected to be flat compared to 2023 due to GoodWheat exit offsetting Zola gains.
positive_highlights: Zola sales increased 86% sequentially and 42% year-over-year, outpacing category growth of 16-27%.
Monetization of wheat IP generated $4 million cash from Corteva and a $6 million promissory note from Above Food.
Cost reduction initiatives identified include a 50% cut in salaries/benefits from GoodWheat exit and an additional $2 million in annual savings.
summary: Q2 FY2024 revenues were $1.3 million, up 32% sequentially and flat year-over-year, driven by Zola sales increasing 86% sequentially to represent 90% of total revenue. Gross profit was $673,000 with a margin of 52%, while the company monetized wheat IP via a $4 million cash payment from Corteva and a $6 million promissory note from Above Food. Management reaffirmed full-year 2024 revenue guidance at approximately $5.3 million (in-line with prior year) and expects cash consumption to be roughly half of the previous year's level.

negative_highlights: Total revenue declined due to reduced wind tower demand and softer PRS shipments
Q3 guidance implies lower EBITDA margin sequentially
Orders declined year-over-year across all segments
positive_highlights: Maintained 10% EBITDA margin despite lower revenue, with $3.6 million EBITDA
Quoting activity elevated across segments; Gearing quoting up 163% YoY
Cost actions contributing >$4 million annualized savings, with most implemented
summary: Broadwind's Q2 2024 revenue declined year-over-year (Heavy Fab -42%, Gearing -5%, Industrial Solutions +3%), but EBITDA margin held at 10% due to favorable mix and cost cuts. Net income was $0.5 million, down from $1.4 million a year ago. Management introduced Q3 guidance of $36-$38 million revenue and $1.7-$2.5 million EBITDA, implying margin compression. They noted robust quoting in non-wind markets (Gearing quoting up 163% YoY) and expect wind demand to accelerate in 2025-2026.

negative_highlights: Net loss increased to $10.7 million from $6.9 million in the prior year period.
R&D expenses rose to $7.6 million driven by costs associated with launching PALISADE-3 and preparing for PALISADE-4.
G&A expenses increased to $4.6 million due to headcount growth and professional service fees.
positive_highlights: Enrollment cadence for PALISADE-3 is on track with expectations and green failure rates are consistent with projections.
The company remains well-funded with $108.4 million in cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities as of June 30, 2024.
PALISADE-2 achieved historic success as the first positive Phase 3 trial for acute treatment of SAD, supporting potential NDA submission.
summary: Vistagen Therapeutics reported Q1 FY2025 results with R&D expenses of $7.6 million and G&A expenses of $4.6 million, resulting in a net loss of $10.7 million compared to $6.9 million in the prior year period. The company confirmed that enrollment for its PALISADE-3 Phase 3 trial is on track with projections, while PALISADE-4 is expected to initiate in the second half of the year. Both studies are targeted to read out in 2025.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to $5M from $4M YoY.
ASCEND top-line data not yet available; key catalyst remains delayed until Q4 2024.
No revenue; company is pre-revenue clinical-stage.
positive_highlights: Operating expenses decreased 19.7% YoY to $5.5M, with R&D down 17.7% and G&A down 21.3%.
BOLSTER trial achieved complete enrollment in first-line cholangiocarcinoma nearly six months ahead of plan, accelerating data to mid-2025.
Cash runway extends into early 2026, covering anticipated data milestones.
summary: Lisata reported Q2 2024 operating expenses down 19.7% YoY to $5.5M, with R&D down 17.7% to $2.6M and G&A down 21.3% to $2.9M. Net loss widened to $5M from $4M YoY. Cash stood at $38.3M, expected to fund operations into early 2026. Management highlighted complete enrollment in BOLSTER nearly six months ahead of plan, with top-line ASCEND data expected in Q4 2024. No revenue reported; clinical-stage biotech.

negative_highlights: Net investment income per share decreased sequentially from $0.63 to $0.59
Weighted average yield on income-producing securities declined to 12.2%
Debt-to-equity ratio increased to 1.18x from 1.11x
positive_highlights: NII of $0.59 per share exceeded the recently increased regular dividend
NAV per share increased to $20.30, highest since June 2022
Portfolio credit stable with 89% of risk-rated 1 and 2 investments
summary: CCAP reported Q2 2024 NII of $0.59 per share, translating to an annualized NII ROE of 11.7%, exceeding its increased regular dividend of $0.42 plus a supplemental dividend of $0.09. NAV per share rose to $20.30, the highest since June 2022. Gross deployment was $119 million, with 92% in first-lien, while net deployment was $46 million. The portfolio remained stable with 1.6% of debt on nonaccrual at cost, and management maintained a confident outlook on LBO volume acceleration in the second half.

negative_highlights: Net loss of $435-475 million for the quarter, driven primarily by a $330-370 million non-cash write-down on the Freedom VCM / Franchise Group investment
Dividend paused because leverage of 2-3x was exceeded and the company is prioritizing debt retirement
Received SEC subpoenas in July relating to dealings with Brian Kahn, and Conn's filed for bankruptcy in July, impacting the Franchise Group investment valuation
positive_highlights: Operating adjusted EBITDA expected at $50-55 million, which management said demonstrates consistent contribution from core businesses
Great American Group's asset appraisal and disposition lines generated ~$153 million revenue and ~$35 million operating income in FY2023
Advisory practice grew from ~$5 million EBITDA at acquisition to an ~$23 million EBITDA run rate six years later
summary: B. Riley Financial reported preliminary Q2 FY2024 results featuring a net loss of $435-475 million and operating adjusted EBITDA of $50-55 million, with the loss driven by non-cash write-downs including a $330-370 million impairment on its Freedom VCM (Franchise Group) investment, plus ~$28 million for Targus and $25 million related to a deferred tax benefit. Management paused the quarterly dividend to retire debt after its leverage ratio rose above the 2-3x target range, and disclosed SEC subpoenas received in July regarding dealings with former Franchise Group CEO Brian Kahn. On the operating side, management highlighted improving transactional activity, a growing advisory business, and noted Great American Group's asset appraisal and disposition lines generated ~$153 million revenue and ~$35 million operating income in FY2023, while the Great American strategic review continues.

negative_highlights: Full-year guidance implies a deceleration in second-half growth due to tougher comps
Operating expenses still elevated with $80-84 million full-year range
DIXI distribution carries lower gross margin, creating mix drag
positive_highlights: Revenue up 17% YoY to $19.3 million, beating the high end of guidance
Gross margin expanded 90 basis points to 73.4%
RNS sales growth ex-NAUTILUS was 21% YoY
summary: Q2 2024 revenue of $19.3 million grew 17% YoY, with RNS system sales up 21% excluding prior-year NAUTILUS study contributions. Gross margin expanded to 73.4% from 72.5%, operating expenses grew only 3%, and net loss improved to $7.5 million from $9.1 million. Management raised full-year revenue guidance to $76-78 million (16-19% growth) while maintaining gross margin and operating expense guidance. New sales reps completed training, and the NAUTILUS trial remains on track for primary endpoint readout in Q1 2025.

negative_highlights: Sequential decline in revenue driven by compounding issues and reimbursement challenges in pediatric centers
G&A expenses increased to $6.9 million due to pre-commercialization efforts for the EU launch and Norgine transaction costs
note and marketing expenses rose significantly to $4.6 million, largely attributable to payroll increases and AYA initiatives
positive_highlights: PEDMARK net sales increased approximately 120% compared to the same quarter in 2023
NCCN guidelines updated to include patients up to age 39, expanding the AYA population opportunity
$43.2 million upfront consideration received from Norgine partnership for European commercialization
summary: Fennec reported Q2 FY2024 PEDMARK net sales of $7.3 million, representing a 120% increase year-over-year but down sequentially from the prior quarter due to compounding issues and reimbursement delays in pediatric centers. Management highlighted recent milestones including FDA safety communication updates for substitutions, CMS J-Code resolution, and NCCN guideline expansions allowing access up to age 39 (AYA), which they believe will drive growth starting Q3. The company sold EU rights to Norgine for an upfront payment of $43.2 million with a potential €10 million milestone upon German pricing approval in late Q4.

negative_highlights: Revenue growth slowed significantly to just 2% year-over-year, indicating potential market saturation or demand softness.
Non-GAAP recurring EBITDA remained at a net loss of $8.8 million.
No specific financial guidance was provided for the full year or next quarter.
positive_highlights: Combined Q2 revenue increased 16% sequentially to $2.72 million.
GAAP loss narrowed by approximately $2.6 million year-over-year to $9.5 million.
Mytesi prescription volume grew 5.2% in Q2 compared to Q1.
summary: JAGX reported Q2 FY2024 combined net revenue of $2.72 million, representing a 16% increase versus Q1 2024 but only a 2% increase versus Q2 2023. The company posted a GAAP loss of $9.5 million, down from $12.1 million in the prior year period, while non-GAAP recurring EBITDA remained at a net loss of $8.8 million. Management provided no specific financial guidance for the full year or next quarter, focusing instead on clinical data analysis and upcoming product launches.

negative_highlights: Reports came with no forward financial guidance for fiscal 2025
Cash and cash equivalents were only $4.4 million against $120.6 million of total debt
Distributions received from alternative assets and other securities held in custody fell to $7.2 million from $12.0 million in the prior-year period
positive_highlights: Q1 revenue of $10.0 million versus negative $2.7 million in the prior-year quarter, aided by a $55.0 million loss contingency accrual release
Operating expenses excluding non-cash goodwill impairment and the accrual release fell 70% to $17.3 million from $56.9 million year over year
Ben Custody returned to profitability with $1.3 million of operating income versus a $50.0 million operating loss in the prior quarter
summary: Beneficent reported Q1 FY2025 revenue of $10.0 million versus negative $2.7 million a year ago, driven largely by a $55.0 million loss contingency accrual release tied to a Texas court vacating an arbitration award; excluding non-cash goodwill impairment and the accrual release in each period, operating expenses fell 70% to $17.3 million from $56.9 million. Ben Liquidity base interest revenue rose 1.9% quarter-over-quarter to $10.8 million and its operating loss narrowed to $0.5 million from $29.4 million, while Ben Custody returned to profitability with $1.3 million of operating income on $5.4 million of revenue. No forward financial guidance was provided. The company announced an upgraded AltAccess MAPS pricing platform and a board-approved plan to complete up to $5 billion of exchange trust fiduciary financing, alongside positive legal developments including the vacated $55.3 million arbitration award and terminated SEC investigation.

negative_highlights: Total revenues declined to $73.8M from $83.1M in Q1 due to lower sales volumes, lower average frac sand prices, and reduced SmartSystems revenue
Q3 sales volume guidance of 1.0-1.2M tons is below Q2's 1.27M, with a potential further slowdown in the Marcellus in Q4
A $1.3M loss on extinguishment of debt was recorded in Q2 related to equipment lease refinancing
positive_highlights: Contribution margin per ton expanded to $15.53 from $13.85 sequentially
Free cash flow was $13.5M in Q2, reversing negative $5.5M in Q1, and company is free cash flow positive for the year through June
Adjusted EBITDA improved to $11.9M from $9.3M in Q1 despite lower sales volumes
summary: Smart Sand reported Q2 2024 revenue of $73.8M, down from $83.1M in Q1, on sales volume of 1.27M tons (down 5% QoQ). Despite lower volume and flat pricing, contribution margin rose to $19.8M ($15.53/ton) from $18.5M ($13.85/ton) and adjusted EBITDA improved to $11.9M from $9.3M, driven by cost initiatives. Q3 volume guidance is 1.0-1.2M tons with contribution margin of $14-16/ton, and management expects to remain free cash flow positive for the year while flagging a potential Q4 slowdown in the Marcellus due to low natural gas prices.

negative_highlights: Total revenue declined ~12% YoY to $4.0 million from $4.6 million
Active accounts and aggregate deposit balances fell approximately 33% versus the prior-year period
Revenue decline driven by lower deposit activity and onboarding income alongside lower interest income
positive_highlights: Loan interest income rose ~204% YoY to approximately $1.8 million
Net income of $942,000 versus a $17.6 million net loss in the prior-year quarter
Operating expenses fell to ~$3.7 million from $5.6 million ex-impairments, and operating cash flow was +$2.7 million versus -$965,000 a year earlier
summary: Safe Harbor reported Q2 2024 total revenue of $4.0 million, down about 12% YoY from $4.6 million, driven by lower deposit/onboarding income and lower interest income, partly offset by loan interest income up ~204% to ~$1.8 million. Net income was $942,000 versus a $17.6 million prior-year net loss that included large impairments, adjusted EBITDA rose to ~$974,000 from $850,000, and operating expenses fell to ~$3.7 million from $5.6 million ex-impairments. Active accounts and aggregate deposit balances fell roughly 33% versus the prior-year period. Management guided full-year 2024 revenue to $17–18 million and adjusted EBITDA to $3.75–4.25 million, with no prior guidance stated in the text for comparison.

negative_highlights: Total Q2 revenue came in slightly below the outlook provided last quarter due to a slowdown at Wayfair.
Management noted that inflation is taking a toll on consumer budgets, dampening demand for home furnishings.
The company reiterated full-year guidance but explicitly stated it does not include material impact from prime creditors tightening above them.
positive_highlights: Non-Wayfair gross originations grew nearly 20% in the second quarter as Wayfair declined.
Gross margin expanded to 16.9%, with operating expenses decreasing by 7% year-over-year.
Katapult Pay delivered $15.7 million in gross originations, representing incremental growth from direct and waterfall channels.
summary: Katapult reported Q2 revenue of $58.9 million (up 8.7% YoY) and gross originations of $55.3 million (up 1.1%), missing the prior outlook due to a slowdown at Wayfair which accounted for roughly half of business. Adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed by $1.2 million year-over-year, but management reiterated full-year guidance while noting macro headwinds and uncertainty regarding interest rate cuts.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened significantly from $9.9M in Q2 FY2023 to $16.9M in Q2 FY2024.
SG&A expenses increased by $3.6 million YoY due to the cost of being a publicly traded company, partially offsetting revenue growth.
A significant $2.8 million non-cash charge related to Forward Purchase Agreement valuation impacted reported earnings.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 16% year-over-year to $15.1 million driven by a 28% increase in aircraft usage revenue.
Blended yield improved 6% YoY to $5,330 as non-owner demand mix increased to 56%. Total flight hours grew 5% YoY.
Vaunt subscription product reached an ARR of $1 million for the first time during the quarter.
summary: Q2 revenue was $15.1 million (up 16% YoY) while net loss widened to $16.9 million due to a $2.8 million non-cash charge on Forward Purchase Agreements and increased SG&A of $9.7 million driven by public company costs. Management raised full-year revenue guidance expectations based on aircraft deliveries, projecting total 2024 revenue between $72M-$90M from HondaJets and $50M from G280s, with EBITDA positivity expected in Q4.

negative_highlights: B2B continuing education revenue declined 13% YoY in H1
Monthly active users in medical practice solutions fell to 57,000 from over 57,000 in H1 2023 due to PEBMED discontinuation
Net debt stands at R$1.459B, though leverage improved to 1.5x from 1.6x
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 490 bps YoY to 42.5% in Q2
Adjusted EPS increased 62% YoY to R$2.29
Guidance raised for net revenue to R$3.225-3.325B and adjusted EBITDA to R$1.375-1.475B
summary: Afya reported Q2 FY2024 net revenue of R$810M (+13.7% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of R$344M (+28% YoY) with margin at 42.5%, up 490 bps YoY; adjusted net income rose 59% to R$210M and adjusted EPS climbed 62% to R$2.29. The company raised its FY2024 guidance to net revenue of R$3.225-3.325B and adjusted EBITDA of R$1.375-1.475B, citing the Unidom acquisition, 80 additional UNIMA seats, better-than-expected H1 results, and a strong intake cycle. Operating cash flow grew 21% to R$683M with a 94% conversion ratio, and net debt/EBITDA improved to 1.5x. The main change from prior periods is the upward revision of all key guidance metrics.

negative_highlights: Revenue decreased 26% year-over-year to $1.3 million due to the RV market downturn
Gross margin contracted from 26.3% in Q2 FY2023 to 25.5% as lower sales volume drove higher fixed overhead costs per unit
Net loss widened significantly to negative $0.30 EPS (or $2.2 million) compared to negative $0.21 EPS last year
positive_highlights: Revenue achieved 32% sequential growth compared to Q1 2024
