Gross margin above 33% in the quarter, with full-year guidance of at least 30%.
Remained debt-free with no credit line drawdown at quarter end.
summary: Q3 2024 was a seasonally strong quarter with net sales slightly above the prior year, as all three toy/consumer product divisions grew. Adjusted EPS was $4.79 for the quarter, down from $4.75 last year, with gross margin above 33%, and trailing 12-month adjusted EBITDA of $58.5 million (8.5% margin). Management reiterated full-year gross margin guidance of at least 30% and highlighted continued debt-free status, but flagged soft industry watch-through and concerns about retailer creditworthiness, with about 1% of sales decline from credit issues. Capital allocation plans remain undecided.

negative_highlights: Total revenue declined to $34.9M from $35.4M a year ago, with GAAP EPS down to $0.18 from $0.22
Adjusted EBITDA fell to $7.5M from $8.4M in the prior-year period
Full-year churn guidance raised to 4.5%-6% from the previously stated 4%-5%, with net unit churn higher than anticipated
positive_highlights: Software operations bookings of $10.4M grew nearly 65% YoY with 24 six-figure contracts, doubling the second quarter's count
Software backlog increased to $63.6M, up more than 19% from the prior-year quarter
Professional services revenue rose 26.1% YoY to $4.8M, with managed services growing almost 133% and comprising ~20% of professional services
summary: Total GAAP revenue fell to $34.9M from $35.4M a year ago, with wireless revenue down to $18.3M from $19M and software roughly flat at $16.6M; GAAP EPS slipped to $0.18 from $0.22 and adjusted EBITDA declined to $7.5M from $8.4M (though up $0.5M sequentially). Software operations bookings rose 65% YoY to $10.4M with 24 six-figure contracts (double the prior quarter) and backlog grew 19% to $63.6M, while professional services rose 26.1%. Management reiterated full-year guidance of $136-144M revenue and $27.5-32.5M adjusted EBITDA, but raised full-year wireless churn expectations to 4.5%-6% from the prior 4%-5%. Cash grew to $27.8M from $23.9M.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined 2.6% year over year to $104.7 million
Annualized recurring revenue fell 3.6% year over year to $401.5 million
GAAP net loss was $43.1 million, or negative $0.47 per diluted share, driven by a $58.5 million Oracle litigation accrual
positive_highlights: Billings rose 7.7% year over year to $65.2 million, led by North America and Asia Pacific
Non-GAAP EPS was $0.22 versus $0.13 in the prior-year quarter
Gross margin expanded 160 basis points sequentially to 60.7%, exceeding 60% for the first time this year
summary: Q3 2024 revenue was $104.7 million, down 2.6% year over year, with annualized recurring revenue of $401.5 million (down 3.6%) and billings of $65.2 million (up 7.7%). Gross margin was 60.7% versus 62.7% a year ago but up 160 basis points sequentially, and non-GAAP EPS was $0.22 versus $0.13, while GAAP EPS was negative $0.47 due to a $58.5 million Oracle litigation accrual. The company suspended guidance amid ongoing Oracle litigation and announced a ServiceNow partnership for enterprise application modernization. Revenue retention was 89%, and the Oracle PeopleSoft wind-down and prior large renewal terminations continued to weigh on top-line growth.

negative_highlights: Provision for credit loss rose to $20.2 million from $14.5 million in the prior-year quarter, and management said core provision could trend closer to $22 million.
Net charge-offs were $13.4 million, or 2.18% of average portfolio, up from 1.88% a year ago; consumer loans 90+ days past due rose to 0.39% from 0.34%.
Net interest margin was 8.11%, down 24 bps YoY, with cost of funds up 77 bps YoY to 4.05% and new CD issuance at 3.95%–4.15%, above the 3.68% weighted deposit cost.
positive_highlights: Net interest income grew 8% YoY and 6% QoQ to $52.7 million.
Recreation loan originations of $139 million were up 50% from Q3 last year; total loans grew 13% YoY to $2.5 billion.
Board raised the quarterly dividend 10% to $0.11 and net book value per share rose to $15.70 from $15.25 in the prior quarter.
summary: Medallion Financial reported Q3 FY2024 net income of $8.6 million, or $0.37 per share, with net interest income up 8% YoY to $52.7 million and total loans up 13% YoY to $2.5 billion. Net interest margin was 8.11%, down 1 bp QoQ and 24 bps YoY, while the provision for credit loss rose to $20.2 million from $14.5 million a year ago. The board raised the quarterly dividend 10% to $0.11 and the company repurchased $1 million of stock at an average of $7.89, leaving over $15 million on the buyback authorization. Management characterized the quarter as clean aside from elevated taxi medallion recoveries that added a couple of cents to EPS, and guided to a potentially flat-to-slightly-down Q4 portfolio before a Q1 reacceleration.

negative_highlights: Full-year sales guidance lowered to low end of $450-$460 million range
Q3 sales down 2.4% (excluding non-recurring) and adjusted EPS down to $0.77
XTRATUF inventory shortages left several million dollars in sales on the table
positive_highlights: Adjusted gross margin up 110 basis points to 38.1%
Durango and XTRATUF US growth double-digit; Lehigh sales up double-digits with 200 new accounts
Spring bookings robust for Durango and XTRATUF; strong Q4 start for Muck
summary: Rocky Brands reported Q3 sales of $114.5 million, down 2.4% excluding non-recurring items, and adjusted EPS of $0.77, below prior-year's $1.09. Management lowered full-year sales guidance to the low end of the $450-$460 million range, citing warm weather, less promotional activity, and XTRATUF inventory shortages. Durango, XTRATUF, and Lehigh saw double-digit growth, but Muck and Georgia were weak. Gross margin improved 110 bps to 38.1%, and interest expense fell to $3.3 million from $5.8 million.

negative_highlights: Occupancy declined to 94.4% as the 535,000 sq ft Indianapolis property went vacant in July, and neither it nor the 2.2 million sq ft Hawaii parcel is expected to be leased before 2025
NOI fell 0.7% YoY and GAAP NOI took a $1.3 million non-cash charge from an early tenant termination in Hawaii
Dividend held at $0.01 per share with no timeline for an increase; net debt to total assets was 68.1% and net debt coverage 12.1x
positive_highlights: FFO rose 1.5% YoY to $8.1 million ($0.12 per share) and cash basis NOI increased 1.1% to $82.5 million
Executed 2.7 million sq ft of leasing at rents 7% above prior leases, including 13 FedEx renewals over 2 million sq ft with no free rent or tenant improvement concessions
Extended the $1.2 billion loan one year and bought the cap for $17 million, less than previously expected, with Q4 interest expense guided down to roughly $72 million from $73.9 million
summary: Q3 FFO came in at $8.1 million or $0.12 per share, up 1.5% YoY, while NOI slipped 0.7% to $84.7 million and cash basis NOI rose 1.1% to $82.5 million. Occupancy fell slightly to 94.4% following the July vacancy of a 535,000 sq ft Indianapolis property, and GAAP NOI absorbed a $1.3 million non-cash charge from a Hawaii tenant termination; leasing totaled 2.7 million sq ft at 7% higher rents, anchored by 13 FedEx renewals covering over 2 million sq ft with no concessions. Management kept the quarterly dividend at $0.01 per share, citing the absence of a credit facility and the need to preserve liquidity for leasing costs, capex and debt obligations, and flagged American Tire Distributors (1.6% of annualized revenue) filing Chapter 11 last week. The $1.2 billion floating-rate loan was extended one year via a $17 million interest rate cap with a 2.78% SOFR strike, and Q4 interest expense is guided to approximately $72 million from $73.9 million.

negative_highlights: EAD fell to $0.24 per share from $0.51 in Q2, with a $0.14 decline in real estate operations and a $0.04 run-rate NII decline from net payoffs
Loans rated 4 or 5 rose 2 points to 23% of par, and two loans were foreclosed, including a $9.3 million Memphis multifamily asset

Loan portfolio shrank $134.4 million on $118.1 million of payoffs and $23.7 million of foreclosures against only $7.4 million of fundings, with earnings constrained until the CLOs are paid down and a new securitization issued
positive_highlights: GAAP book value per share rose to $27.92 from $27.20 at June 30
CECL reserves decreased $291,000 ($0.04 per share) versus a $1.3 million increase in Q2, driven by payoffs, modifications, and improved property performance
Repurchased 114,000 shares for $1.7 million at roughly a 46% discount to book, with $2.3 million remaining on the program
summary: ACR reported Q3 GAAP net income of $2.8 million, or $0.36 per diluted share, including a $2.8 million unrealized gain on an Austin office foreclosure conversion, but earnings available for distribution fell to $0.24 per share from $0.51 in Q2. The EAD decline reflected a $0.14 drop in real estate operations, a $0.06 preferred dividend change, and a $0.04 run-rate decline in net interest income from net payoffs. The loan portfolio fell $134.4 million to $1.6 billion as $118.1 million of payoffs and $23.7 million of foreclosures outpaced $7.4 million of fundings, and loans rated 4 or 5 rose 2 points to 23% of par. Management gave no formal guidance but said book value per share should be flat to better over the next two quarters as REO and equity assets are monetized and capital is redeployed into new loans.

negative_highlights: Americas segment sales declined sequentially due to Hurricane Helene impacts, which pushed approximately $1.5 million in revenue into Q2.
Asia segment net sales fell 2% year-over-year driven by struggling economic conditions in China and pricing pressure.
Adjusted EBITDA for the upcoming quarter is expected to be negative ($4M-$2M) due to holiday seasonality.
positive_highlights: Consolidated net sales grew 6% year-over-year to $147.4 million, driven by strong performance in the Brazil segment (up 15% YoY).
Beyond Apparel initiatives are gaining traction with significantly better margins than traditional apparel products.
New REPREVE innovations like ThermaLoop received overwhelmingly positive customer and media response.
summary: Consolidated net sales were $147.4 million, up 6% year-over-year but down 6% sequentially due to seasonality and a ~2% impact from Hurricane Helene in the Americas segment. Management reiterated fiscal 2025 guidance for top-line growth of approximately 10%, citing cost reductions and new product traction as drivers despite softness in Asia.

negative_highlights: Insurance underlying loss ratio rose year-over-year, partly due to MidCorp diluting the loss ratio by 60-70 bps and the prior-year DAC benefit adding 1.9 points
Mortgage new insurance written of $13.5 billion reflected a soft origination market, and management said growing market share would likely require price cuts
positive_highlights: Operating EPS of $1.99 and 14.8% annualized operating ROE, with book value per share up 8.1% to $57
Reinsurance net premiums grew 24.5% (22.4% ex-reinstatement) and mortgage delivered a 14.8% combined ratio
Catastrophe losses of $450 million from Helene and other events remained within the company's seasonally adjusted cat load
summary: Arch Capital reported Q3 2024 after-tax operating income of $1.99 per share and a 14.8% annualized operating ROE, with book value per share up 8.1% to $57. Underwriting income was $538 million on an 86.6% combined ratio (78.3% underlying ex-cat), while $450 million of catastrophe losses from Hurricane Helene and other events came in within the seasonally adjusted load. All three segments contributed, with reinsurance net premiums up 24.5% and insurance up 20% including the MidCorp acquisition; mortgage remained highly profitable at a 14.8% combined ratio. Management gave no formal guidance but signaled continued favorable P&C market conditions and floated potential capital return after wind season. The quarter was a solid operational beat with no major negatives, though it lacked a formal guidance raise.

negative_highlights: FY2024 revenue guidance was cut to $119-121 million from a prior ~$126 million midpoint after Q3 revenue came in flat and organic recurring growth was only 5%
Adjusted EBITDA fell to $5.4 million from $6.2 million year over year, with adjusted EBITDA margin down to 19% from 21% and GAAP gross margin down to 67% from 73%
Management attributed the shortfall to timing on large enterprise tax deals (roughly 50+ accounts tied to one integrator), a slower new-product ramp and an acquisition slipping to 2025
positive_highlights: Recurring revenue grew 20% year over year and reached 98% of total revenue, up from 81% a year earlier as ERTC revenue was replaced
Backlog rose to over $67 million, up 35% sequentially and 250% year over year, supporting the double-digit organic growth implied in 2025 guidance
Sales bookings increased 141% year over year, and 12 acquisitions over four quarters added roughly $15 million in recurring revenue at an average ~2.6x multiple
summary: Q3 FY2024 revenue was $29.3 million, flat year over year, as an approximately $5 million decline in non-recurring ERTC revenue offset 20% recurring revenue growth; recurring revenue reached 98% of total versus 81% a year earlier. Organic recurring growth of just 5% missed internal expectations, and adjusted EBITDA fell to $5.4 million (19% margin) from $6.2 million (21%). Management cut FY2024 revenue guidance to $119-121 million (from a prior ~$126 million midpoint), citing delayed large enterprise tax deals, slower new-product ramp and a slipped acquisition, while initiating FY2025 guidance of $134-138 million revenue and 23-24% adjusted EBITDA margin. CEO Pat Goepel acknowledged the shortfall, saying 'I own the timing and I screwed up,' while pointing to sales bookings up 141% and backlog up 250% year over year.

negative_highlights: Consolidated revenue declined 10% and Gourmet Foods & Gift Baskets revenue fell 14.4% to $84M
BloomNet revenue dropped 20.1% to $23.1M on a partner merger, and segment contribution margin fell to $6.8M from $9.4M
Adjusted EBITDA loss of $27.9M and consumer floral segment contribution margin declined to $4.9M from $8.8M on marketing investment
positive_highlights: E-commerce order decline improved to 6.5% from 11.5% in Q4 and 16.1% a year ago
Gross margin expanded 20 bps to 38.1% and operating expenses fell $4.3M excluding non-recurring charges
Wholesale revenue expected to increase about $20M over prior year in Q2, with strong pear crop more than double last year
summary: FLWS reported fiscal Q1 revenue down 10% to roughly $242M, with e-commerce revenue down 8% on a 6.5% order decline and 1.5% AOV decline, in line with internal expectations. Adjusted EBITDA loss was $27.9M, gross margin improved slightly to 38.1%, and opex fell $4.3M excluding non-recurring items. Full-year guidance was unchanged: revenue flat to down mid-single digits, adjusted EBITDA $85-95M, and free cash flow $45-55M. Management cited improving order trends versus down 11.5% in Q4, a $3M wholesale timing shift into Q2, and expected $20M wholesale revenue increase versus prior year in the holiday quarter.

negative_highlights: O&M expenses increased by $58 million YoY due to wildfire mitigation and storm damage.
Full-year O&M forecast revised upward to a 3%-4% increase relative to 2023 levels.
Interest charges decreased earnings by $0.08/share driven by rising rates.
positive_highlights: Ongoing earnings beat at $1.25/share driven by rate case outcomes (+$0.25) and AFUDC (+$0.04).
Reaffirmed 2024 guidance of $3.50-$3.60 EPS despite higher O&M costs.
Initiated strong 2025 earnings guidance range of $3.75 to $3.85, implying ~7% growth from the prior year's midpoint.
summary: Xcel Energy reported Q3 ongoing earnings of $1.25 per share, beating the prior quarter's $1.23 and reaffirming its full-year 2024 guidance range of $3.50 to $3.60 while initiating a new 2025 guidance range of $3.75 to $3.85 representing approximately 7% growth from the prior year's midpoint. Management updated their five-year capital investment plan to $45 billion, reflecting annual rate base growth of 9.4%, and raised long-term EPS growth objectives to a range of 6% to 8%. The company noted that O&M expenses increased by $0.09 per share due to wildfire mitigation and storm costs, leading to a revision in the full-year O&M forecast.

negative_highlights: Oilsands revenue declined year-over-year, with scope changes and deferred work limiting visibility; 2025 oilsands guidance is withheld pending contract finalization.
Canadian utilization target of 75% was pushed off by a year to end-2025.
Free cash flow was only $11 million due to a $32 million working capital draw and $12 million spent on capital work in progress.
positive_highlights: Record Q3 EBITDA of $106 million, up 75% from the prior Q3 record, with a 29% margin.
Backlog increased ~$300 million sequentially to $3.1 billion, with bid pipeline exceeding $10 billion.
Australia fleet utilization hit 84% in Q3, peaking at 88% in July, and 25 trucks moved to Australia are expected to contribute $10-20 million incremental EBITDA in 2025.
summary: Q3 2024 delivered record EBITDA of $106 million (29% margin) and adjusted EPS of $1.17, driven by Australia (MacKellar) achieving 84% utilization and operating at above 20% gross margins. Canadian utilization recovered to 51% from 42% in Q2, but oilsands revenue remained down year-over-year. Backlog rose about $300 million quarter-over-quarter to $3.1 billion, with management expecting year-end backlog to stay above $3 billion. Guidance for 2024 is unchanged, and management expects 2025 EBITDA to increase meaningfully on Australia growth and stable oilsands, while Canadian utilization is targeted to reach 75% by end-2025.

negative_highlights: DSCR slipped to 1.36x, which management attributed to the unleased A-life senior loan (SOFR+900) and modest SFR slippage
Multifamily exposure fell again in the mix while Life Sciences rose above a quarter of the portfolio, reflecting paybacks shrinking the overall book
Management noted rising rate volatility causing retrades and a paused transaction market, plus heavy competition clustering at SOFR+250-300 for stabilized deals
positive_highlights: Earnings available for distribution rose to $0.75 per diluted share from $0.43 in Q3 2023, and CAD of $0.67 covered the $0.50 dividend 1.34x
Book value per share increased 2.6% to $16.95, and debt-to-equity was reduced to 1.52x from over 2x in Q1 via roughly $40 million of repo line paydowns
Q4 EAD guidance of $0.79 at the midpoint implies sequential growth from Q3's $0.75, and management flagged possible 2025 storage monetization
summary: NREF reported Q3 2024 net income of $0.74 per diluted share versus a $0.90 net loss in Q3 2023, with interest income up $5.6M to $23.6M and earnings available for distribution of $0.75 versus $0.43 a year earlier. Cash available for distribution was $0.67, covering the $0.50 quarterly dividend 1.34x, and book value per share rose 2.6% to $16.95. Q4 guidance is for EAD of $0.79 per share at the midpoint (range $0.75-$0.83) and CAD of $0.50 at the midpoint ($0.45-$0.55). The balance sheet was deleveraged to 1.52x debt-to-equity from over 2x in Q1, and management highlighted a more active multifamily pipeline and an early storage monetization.

negative_highlights: Q3 U.S. seasonality was more pronounced than the prior year's 'anomaly'.
Management not guiding to 2025 yet, suggesting growth catalysts are later.
LungTraX platform not yet generating direct revenue; adoption will take time.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 15% year-over-year, with U.S. up 17% and international up 12%.
Added 15 new U.S. accounts, ending Q3 with 280 active accounts.
Year-to-date patient engagement up 150% to over 34,000 potential patients.
summary: Pulmonx reported Q3 2024 worldwide revenue of $20.4 million, up 15% year-over-year (15% constant currency), with U.S. revenue of $13.8 million (up 17%) and international revenue of $6.6 million (up 12%). Gross margin was 74%, flat year-over-year. Total operating expenses increased 3% to $29.2 million. The company reaffirmed full-year 2024 revenue guidance of $81-84 million, implying ~20% growth at the midpoint, and noted the launch of LungTraX Connect and Detect pilots into select centers. Management expressed confidence in commercial execution but highlighted early innings for strategic initiatives and expects material contributions from Japan only in 2026.

negative_highlights: Gross margin declined 70 bps to 37.5% due to mix shift from cushioning to void-fill
Europe/APAC environment remains uneven and sluggish, especially in Germany and Poland industrial sectors
Input cost environment expected to rise in coming quarters as paper indices increased mid-single-digits
positive_highlights: Net revenue up 10.5% constant currency; volumes up 14.7% YoY
North America revenue up 15.5% on strong strategic account activity and plastic-to-paper switch
Automation bookings year-to-date up 60%; Q4 expected to set record; 2025 visibility highest ever
summary: Ranpak reported Q3 FY2024 with strong double-digit top-line and adjusted EBITDA growth, marking the fifth consecutive quarter of volume growth. North American net revenue surged 15.5% (constant currency) driven by strategic accounts and e-commerce plastic-to-paper switching, while Europe/APAC grew 7.1% with volumes up 9%. Gross margin came in at 37.5% (down 70 bps YoY) due to mix shift toward void-fill and pricing pressure, but adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to 21.6%. The company reiterated full-year guidance, highlighted record automation bookings expected in Q4, and noted strong progress on deleveraging (net leverage down to 4.0x). Management expressed optimism about 2025, citing robust backlog and visibility.

negative_highlights: Operating profit decreased significantly due to one-time pension termination expense of $7.6 million and stock-based comp increase
Net income dropped from $10.3M YoY to $1.9M primarily driven by the non-cash charges mentioned above
Global commercial revenue declined due to soft international markets, specifically in China
positive_highlights: Gross profit margin expanded by 190 bps to 28% driven by favorable mix and lower product costs
Revenue growth achieved despite expected average price decreases, indicating volume strength
HealthBeacon integration progressing with revenue increasing quarterly
summary: Hamilton Beach reported Q3 FY2024 revenue of $156.7 million (up 2% YoY) and gross profit margin expansion to 28%, but operating income fell to $10.6 million due to non-cash pension termination charges ($7.6M) and higher equity incentive compensation ($2.9M). Management reaffirmed full-year revenue growth expectations while noting that comparisons are now normalizing, which will likely moderate reported results in the back half of 2024.

negative_highlights: Offshore segment margin fell to $72 million in Q3 from $97 million in Q1 due to rare technical issues.
Soda ash production challenges and higher maintenance spending at Westvaco; export prices expected lower in Q4.
Fourth quarter results negatively impacted by delays in offshore repairs.
positive_highlights: Offshore expansion project on schedule, with Shenandoah and Salamanca expected online in Q2 2025.
Management reiterates confidence in 2025 adjusted EBITDA growth and turning cash flow positive.
No growth capital projects identified; committed to debt reduction and preferred redemption.
summary: Genesis Energy reported Q3 2024 results that were well below original expectations due to multiple operational and technical issues in offshore and soda ash segments. Offshore segment margin dropped to $72 million from $97 million in Q1, driven by rare mechanical failures at producer fields, with repairs delayed to year-end, impacting Q4. Soda ash faced production challenges at Westvaco and softer export prices. Management reiterates confidence in 2025 growth from offshore startups (Shenandoah and Salamanca) and expects to turn cash flow positive next year, though soda ash headwinds persist.

negative_highlights: R&D revenue declined to $1.7 million from $3.9 million due to discontinued program
Total revenue growth partially driven by timing of customer orders
Forward-looking growth still dependent on ongoing customer adoption and milestones
positive_highlights: Product revenue increased to $11.2 million from $5.4 million in Q3 2023
Product gross margin improved to 61% up from 58%
Net loss reduced to $20.6 million from $34.9 million
summary: Codexis reported Q3 2024 revenue of $12.8 million, up from $9.3 million in Q3 2023, with product revenue increasing to $11.2 million from $5.4 million. Product gross margin improved to 61% from 58%. The company reiterated full-year guidance, ended the quarter with $90 million in cash, and continues to target profitability by end of 2026. Management emphasized progress in ECO Synthesis platform, including upcoming TIDES presentations and a planned GMP scale-up partnership for 2025.

negative_highlights: Consolidated sales down 20.2% YoY driven by hurricanes and high interest rates.
Labor Day event sales were down in the mid-teens compared to last year.
Closing rates remain below last year's levels due to a more deliberate consumer.
positive_highlights: Traffic improvement observed over the last month following election conclusion.
Design business grew 19% for the quarter as a percentage of total business.
Company remains debt-free with $121.2 million in cash and equivalents.
summary: Consolidated sales fell 20.2% to $175.9 million and EPS dropped to $0.29 from $1.02 year-over-year due to a cautious consumer, high interest rates, and hurricane disruptions. Gross margin decreased 60 bps to 60.2%, while SG&A expenses rose as a percentage of sales to 57.4%. Management noted traffic is improving but remains below prior levels, with closures in Florida and North Carolina impacting the quarter.

negative_highlights: Full-year revenue guidance cut to ~$900 million midpoint from the prior ~$1 billion, with EBITDA guidance lowered to $43 million from a prior $67 million midpoint
Adjusted EBITDA margin fell 250 bps sequentially to 4.3%, and adjusted operating margin fell 200 bps to 0.3%
Electronics sales fell ~12% sequentially with adjusted operating margin down ~480 bps to 2.8%; Control Devices sales fell 8.1% with margin down 150 bps to 3.1%
positive_highlights: Year-to-date cash generation of $13.3 million, a $31.3 million improvement versus the same period in 2023, driven by an $11.3 million inventory reduction

MirrorEye announced as standard equipment on several DAF and Volvo European truck platforms and a new DTNA Freightliner Cascadia program launching mid-2025, with take rates expected to exceed original expectations
First-ever leak detection module award with a Chinese OEM for a hybrid vehicle platform, targeting start of production in Q4 2025
summary: Q3 sales came in at $213.8 million, down 9.8% sequentially, as production headwinds hit all primary end markets. Adjusted operating margin fell 200 bps to 0.3%, and adjusted EBITDA margin fell 250 bps to 4.3%. Management lowered full-year 2024 revenue guidance to a midpoint of $900 million (from prior ~$1 billion) and cut EBITDA expectations accordingly, citing a $34 million reduction tied to a 3.6% weighted end-market decline plus softer MirrorEye aftermarket and off-highway sales. Offsets included $13.3 million of year-to-date cash generation ($31.3 million better than prior year) from an $11.3 million inventory reduction, and new MirrorEye factory-installation wins.

negative_highlights: Non-GAAP economic earnings fell to $0.13 per share from $0.80 a year ago and GAAP EPS fell to $0.01 from $0.41
Intermediary channel had quarterly net outflows of $325 million and wealth management lost $44 million net
Share repurchases were minimal at roughly $273,000 for 21,879 shares
positive_highlights: AUM rose 5% sequentially to $17.7 billion, the highest level in six years, driven by $1.1 billion of market appreciation
Institutional channel posted net inflows of $197 million with gross sales over $1 billion year-to-date and a pipeline of nearly $2 billion
The MDST energy ETF crossed $50 million in AUM and exceeds 10,000 daily shares traded, thresholds for broader platform inclusion
summary: Westwood reported Q3 2024 revenue of $23.7 million, up from $22.7 million in Q2 and $21.9 million a year ago on higher average AUM. GAAP comprehensive income was $0.1 million or $0.01 per share versus $3.4 million or $0.41 per share a year ago, and non-GAAP economic earnings fell to $1.1 million or $0.13 per share from $6.5 million or $0.80. AUM reached $17.7 billion, up 5% sequentially and the highest in six years, on $1.1 billion of market appreciation partly offset by $0.1 billion of net outflows, with intermediary outflows of $325 million and wealth management outflows of $44 million. The institutional pipeline is nearly $2 billion and the board declared a $0.15 regular dividend, but no formal forward guidance figures were given.

negative_highlights: Guidance for Q4 implies a sequential decline in revenue ($132-142M) and EBITDA due to seasonality and budget exhaustion.
Natural gas prices remain challenging (averaging ~$2 year-to-date), pressuring activity in Haynesville and Northeast.
International tool sales increased in Q3 but are expected to decrease in Q4, and full-year international sales are tracking lower year-over-year.
positive_highlights: Revenue of $138.2M exceeded guidance ($127-137M) and grew ~4% QoQ.
Adjusted EBITDA increased ~47% QoQ to $14.3M with incremental margins of ~79%.
Cementing market share grew ~23% QoQ in operating areas, with revenue up 12% despite lower rig count.
summary: Q3 revenue was $138.2M, beating guidance of $127-137M, with adjusted EBITDA up ~47% QoQ to $14.3M despite a 3% decline in US rig count. Cementing drove growth, increasing jobs ~9% and revenue ~12% on market share gains, while total revenue grew ~4% QoQ. Management expects Q4 revenue of $132-142M, down sequentially due to seasonality and budget exhaustion, but views Q3 results as repeatable and anticipates a moderate activity pickup in 2025 if gas prices support it. Adjusted EBITDA margins improved significantly, with incremental margins of ~79%.

negative_highlights: Biopharma services revenue fell 17% due to project completion shifting from late Q3 into early October.
Hurricanes in Florida and the Southeast disrupted testing volumes for approximately two weeks at the end of the quarter, causing a slight miss on expectations.
Sales team expansion was slightly slower than planned with an average of 63 contributing reps versus guidance to catch up by year-end.
positive_highlights: Lung diagnostic testing revenue grew 40% year-over-year driven by test volume expansion and new payer coverage additions.
Gross margins remained robust at 77.0%, consistent with the upper-70s target despite biopharma timing shifts.
Net loss narrowed to $10.3 million, representing a 6% improvement versus the prior year quarter.
summary: Biodesix reported Q3 FY2024 revenue of $18.2 million (up 35% YoY), driven by a 40% increase in lung diagnostic testing revenue to $17.2 million, while biopharma services revenue declined 17%. Management reaffirmed full-year 2024 guidance of $70-72M and expects adjusted EBITDA breakeven in H2 2025, noting that Q3 growth was slightly below expectations due to hurricanes affecting the Southeast sales territory. The company anticipates a sequential recovery in lung volumes for Q4 as hurricane impacts subside.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined year-over-year by $0.7 million driven by a $7.1 million sales decline in semi.
Front-end semi market is currently paused with deliveries anticipated only in the second half of 2025.
Full-year revenue guidance was tightened, implying lower Q4 results compared to prior expectations.
positive_highlights: Sequential gross margin expansion of 570 basis points driven by favorable product mix and cost actions.
Back-end semi orders showed sequential improvement for the third consecutive quarter, signaling recovery from the trough.
Alfamation contributed $5.4 million in revenue and strengthened positions in automotive and life sciences.
summary: Revenue decreased $3.7 million sequentially to $30 million due to $2 million in shipment delays and a decline in semi revenue, partially offset by growth in auto EV from the Alfamation acquisition. Management tightened full-year 2024 revenue guidance to a range of $128-$131 million, implying Q4 revenue of $34-$37 million with gross margins expected at approximately 42%. While sequential gross margin expanded 570 bps due to mix and cost actions, the front-end semi market remains paused until late 2025.

negative_highlights: New loan coupons fell below 8% for the first time, with the five-quarter weighted average at 7.98%
Nonperforming loans increased $2 million to 0.14% of the portfolio due to one consumer loan relationship in collection
Provision of $837,000 was recorded, and the allowance for credit losses remained at 1.19% of loans
positive_highlights: EPS of $0.35 rose 82% YoY from $0.19 and 13% QoQ from $0.31, marking a record quarter
Average loans increased 16.6% YoY and deposits grew 10.7% YoY to $2.1 billion, with deposit-aggregating verticals now 31% of total deposits
Net interest margin improved 9 bps in the quarter to 3.03%, with September NIM at 3.09%, and management expects further expansion
summary: USCB reported Q3 FY2024 net income of $6.9 million, or $0.35 per diluted share, up from $0.31 last quarter and $0.19 a year ago, with ROA of 1.11% and ROE of 13.38%. Deposits rose 10.7% YoY to $2.1 billion and average loans grew 16.6% YoY, while the net interest margin improved 9 basis points to approximately 3.03% for the quarter, with September's NIM at 3.09%. Management guided to continued high single to low double-digit loan growth, further NIM expansion, and a 40–50% deposit beta on rate cuts, and declared a $0.05 dividend while repurchasing 10,000 shares. Credit quality remained clean with zero net charge-offs and nonperforming loans at 0.14% of the portfolio.

negative_highlights: Non-performing loans rose $8.4 million to $13.4 million on a single secured commercial relationship placed on non-accrual
A $500,000 provision for credit losses was recorded versus none in the prior quarter, with net charge-offs of $9,000
30-89 day past due loans rose $5.4 million to $7.3 million (0.73% of gross loans), driven by a $3.5 million agricultural loan
positive_highlights: Net interest margin expanded 9 bps to 3.30% and net interest income rose 5.7% ($630,000) sequentially
Net income of $3.9 million grew 30.5% over the prior quarter and 36.6% year-over-year, with EPS up 36.5% YoY to $0.72
Gross loans crossed $1.0 billion for the first time, up $21.3 million (8.6% annualized), while noninterest expense fell $536,000
summary: Landmark reported Q3 FY2024 net income of $3.9 million ($0.72 diluted EPS), up 30.5% from the prior quarter and 36.6% year-over-year, with ROA of 1.0% and ROE of 11.82%. Gross loans rose $21.3 million (8.6% annualized) to a record $1.0 billion, net interest margin expanded 9 bps to 3.30%, and noninterest income grew $533,000 while noninterest expense fell $536,000. A $500,000 provision was recorded versus none in Q2, and non-performing loans jumped $8.4 million to $13.4 million on a single secured commercial relationship placed on non-accrual. Management said rate cuts should be accretive to margin going forward but gave no formal numeric guidance; the Board declared a $0.21 dividend and a 5% stock dividend.

negative_highlights: Revenue rose only ~2% YoY ($0.7M) while expenses increased 12% ($2.8M), with compensation up 11% ($1.9M)
Management reported discretionary outflows during the quarter (characterized as revenue neutral) and said most business metrics are down on higher expenses
positive_highlights: Discretionary AUM increased $1.0 billion to $22.6 billion, up 5% QoQ and 10% YoY, providing forward revenue visibility
New institutional business pipeline rose 20% to $1.2 billion, and excludes the new Global Equity strategy which management says has high capacity
Total AUM reached $35.1 billion, up 13% year-over-year, with broader market participation across market caps benefiting the diversified business
summary: Silvercrest reported Q3 revenue of $30.4 million, up about 2% year-over-year, with expenses up 12% ($2.8M) driven by an 11% rise in compensation, pushing reported net income to $3.7 million (Class A $0.24 per share) and adjusted EBITDA to $6.3 million (20.9% of revenue, down from 22.9% YTD). Discretionary AUM rose $1.0 billion to $22.6 billion (up 5% QoQ, 10% YoY) and total AUM reached $35.1 billion (up 13% YoY), with the institutional pipeline up 20% to $1.2 billion. Management guided optimistically toward significant net organic inflows over the next two quarters, though noted most metrics are down due to higher investment spending and no formal guidance was raised. Repurchased $1.4 million of Class A shares under the up-to-$12 million plan.

negative_highlights: B2B sales declined due to Watsons channel weakness in Hong Kong
Cash flow from operations decreased year-over-year ($3.5M vs $6.5M) driven by working capital changes
positive_highlights: Revenue beat expectations with $25.6M reported, up 31% YoY
Gross margins expanded to 63.5%, a significant improvement over the prior year's 60.8%
Management raised full-year revenue growth guidance from a range of 10-15% to approximately 15%
summary: ChromaDex reported Q3 FY2024 revenue of $25.6 million, a 31% year-over-year increase driven by record ingredient sales ($14.8M) and e-commerce growth. The company achieved profitability with net income of $1.9 million and positive adjusted EBITDA of $2.9 million, marking the sixth consecutive quarter of operational cash flow generation. Management raised its full-year 2024 top-line guidance to approximately 15% year-over-year growth from a prior range of 10-15%, citing strong momentum in Niagen Plus and e-commerce.

negative_highlights: Consolidated net loss of $18 million ($0.26/share) and ~$24 million cash consumed in the quarter, with net working capital up ~$36 million
Roughly 71,000 tons of pulp production lost to unplanned downtime across three mills, an estimated ~$20 million EBITDA impact
Hardwood realizations fell $69 to $632/ton, prompting a CAD 4 million non-cash inventory impairment at the Peace River Mill
positive_highlights: Operating EBITDA improved to $50 million in Q3 from $30 million in Q2, aided by fewer planned maintenance days (20 vs 37)
Softwood pulp sales realizations held steady at $814/ton vs $811/ton, and the NBSK list price rose $65 to $1,762/ton
Lumber production rose 10% sequentially to 122 million board feet, and mass timber generated strong margins with a $33 million order file
summary: Mercer reported Q3 2024 operating EBITDA of $50 million, up from $30 million in Q2, but a consolidated net loss of $18 million ($0.26 per share) and cash consumption of about $24 million. Results were pressured by roughly 71,000 tons of lost pulp production from unrelated unplanned downtime (a ~$20 million EBITDA hit) and weaker hardwood prices, partly offset by fewer planned maintenance days. Softwood realizations held at $814/ton, while hardwood fell to $632/ton and management flagged a CAD 4 million hardwood inventory impairment. Management expects strong Q4 pulp results and says the operational issues are behind them, though Q4 already includes 12 days of unplanned downtime at Peace River; no formal guidance was provided beyond directional commentary and the $95–120 million CapEx range.

negative_highlights: Total revenue declined YoY to $38.8M; OA Pain Management decreased 2% due to lower U.S. JNJ sales.
OEM channel (including JNJ) guided down 8-10% for 2024 and 12-18% for 2025 due to competitive pricing and reduced market access.
Recorded a $27M non-cash impairment on Arthrosurface assets; $3-$5M restructuring costs expected.
positive_highlights: Commercial channel revenue expected to grow 14-19% in 2024 and 12-18% in 2025, driven by Integrity and international OA pain sales.
Integrity surgeries grew >40% sequentially to nearly 200, with over 20% of surgeons new to Anika.
First module of Hyalofast PMA filed; company remains on track for U.S. launch by 2026.
summary: Anika's Q3 2024 total revenue was $38.8M, down $2.7M YoY, with adjusted gross margin of 65% (down 1 point) and an adjusted EBITDA of $5.4M. The quarter included a $27M impairment on Arthrosurface, recorded in Q3, as the company executed a strategic pivot: watching Arthrosurface (~$10M) and planning to divest Parcus Medical. Management lowered 2024 guidance for the OEM channel (down 8-10%) due to JNJ U.S. pricing and market access pressures, but guided commercial channel growth of 14-19% in 2024 and 12-18% in 2025. The company also announced planned headcount reduction from ~325 to ~225.

negative_highlights: Gas Cylinders sales down 4.7% year-over-year due to timing of SCBA projects
Graphic Arts divestiture delayed to H1 2025 as original buyer did not meet valuation
Pull-forward from customers (hurricane/port strike) may create demand timing uncertainty
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA up 22.7% year-over-year to $13.5 million, with margin up 260 bps to 14.8%
Adjusted EPS up 35% to $0.27
Raised full-year 2024 adjusted EBITDA guidance to $45M-$47M (excluding legal recoveries)
summary: Luxfer reported Q3 2024 sales of $91.4 million, up 1.2% year-over-year, with adjusted EBITDA up 22.7% to $13.5 million and a margin of 14.8%, the third consecutive quarter of margin growth. Adjusted EPS rose 35% to $0.27. The company raised full-year 2024 guidance, now expecting adjusted EBITDA between $45M-$47M (excluding legal recoveries) and $52M-$54M including recoveries, with adjusted EPS of $0.88-$0.94 excluding and $1.09-$1.14 including recoveries. Management remains optimistic about operational efficiency and strategic investments, while the Graphic Arts divestiture is expected to close in H1 2025 after the original buyer failed to meet valuation expectations.

negative_highlights: EPS was breakeven versus $0.01 in the year-ago quarter; net income fell to about $200,000 from $700,000 on a swaps mark-to-market loss
Recorded Music revenue declined 1% to $10.7 million, lapping prior-year De La Soul physical releases and a Sinead O'Connor streaming spike
Sync revenue benefited from timing of licenses that management said is 'not necessarily indicative of a run rate'
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA rose 11% to $17.6 million and OIBDA rose 34% to $16.6 million, a record high
Music Publishing revenue increased 10% to $28.6 million, driven by catalog acquisitions and streaming price increases
Guidance raised: revenue to $150-153 million and adjusted EBITDA to $59-62 million, implying about 5% and 9% growth at the midpoint
summary: Reservoir reported Q2 FY2025 revenue of $40.7 million, up 6% YoY (5% organic), with adjusted EBITDA up 11% to $17.6 million and OIBDA up 34% to $16.6 million. Music Publishing revenue grew 10% to $28.6 million while Recorded Music declined 1% to $10.7 million due to lapping De La Soul releases. Net income was about $200,000 and EPS was breakeven versus $0.01 a year ago. Management raised revenue guidance to $150-153 million (from $148-152 million) and adjusted EBITDA guidance to $59-62 million (from $58-61 million).

negative_highlights: Southwest region adjusted EBITDA decreased significantly by 16%, attributed to a note weakness in-term shift in product service line mix driven by customer scheduling issues.
Q4 outlook anticipates a sequential revenue decline of approximately 10% to 14% due to winter holidays and budget exhaustion.
Rockies segment incremental revenue was predominantly from lower margin coiled tubing and wireline services.
positive_highlights: Q3 consolidated adjusted EBITDA margin remained stable at 15%, consistent with Q2 despite a sequential decline in average U.S. land rigs of 7%.
Northeast Mid-Con segment revenue increased by 7% sequentially, driven largely by pressure pumping and frac rentals activity.
Rockies segment revenue grew 10.6% sequentially due to incremental activity.
summary: KLX reported Q3 revenue of $189 million (up 5% sequentially) and adjusted EBITDA of $27.8 million with a margin of 15%. Management noted that while the quarter was strong, they expect a sequential decline in Q4 revenue of approximately 10-14% due to seasonality and budget exhaustion. For 2025, management expressed optimism but declined to provide specific guidance numbers until after the Q4 results.

negative_highlights: North American Mining swung to an approximately $0.5M operating loss from $0.9M profit, driven by a $900K receivable reserve after a phosphate customer temporarily ceased operations.
Minerals Management operating profit and adjusted EBITDA are guided down for Q4 and full year 2024 on natural gas and oil price expectations, with a moderate 2025 production decline anticipated.
Full-year 2024 cash flow before financing is expected to be a use of cash; company ended the quarter with $70M debt against $63M cash.
positive_highlights: Consolidated operating profit of $19.7M versus a $6.3M operating loss a year ago; net income of $15.6M ($2.14/share) versus a $0.51 loss per share.
Excluding the $13.6M insurance recovery, consolidated operating profit still increased over 197% from last year's Q3 loss.
Minerals Management operating profit rose 71% to $6.2M on revenue up 54% to $8.8M, helped by late-2023 acquisitions; Coal Mining segment operating profit of $19.9M versus a $4.7M loss.
summary: NACCO reported Q3 FY2024 operating profit of $19.7M and net income of $15.6M ($2.14/share), versus an operating loss of $6.3M and net loss of $0.51/share in the prior-year quarter. Results included $13.6M of business interruption insurance income at Mississippi Lignite; excluding it, consolidated operating profit still rose over 197% from last year's loss. Management guided to significantly higher Q4 and full-year 2024 operating profit and adjusted EBITDA, with Coal Mining and North American Mining up but Minerals Management down on lower oil and gas prices and expected 2025 production decline. The quarter also carried a $900K receivable reserve tied to a phosphate customer that temporarily ceased operations.

negative_highlights: Net income fell to $4.8M ($0.20 diluted EPS) from $10.4M ($0.41) a year ago; pre-tax earnings dropped to $6.9M from $14.2M
Annualized net charge-offs rose to 7.53% from 6.86% and 30+ day delinquencies rose to 14.04% from 12.31% YoY
Net interest margin declined 7% YoY to $50.5M as interest expense rose with a larger securitization and credit line debt balance
positive_highlights: Q3 originations of $446M, up 38% YoY from $322M, with October the second-best origination month in company history
Large dealer group originations of $119M, up 21% over Q2 and 40% over Q1, raising their mix from 21% to ~28% of originations
Vintage-over-vintage CNL improvements from 2022 through the first three quarters of 2024, aided by the Gen 8 credit model and ~$4M in estimated fraud-loss savings
summary: Revenue rose 9% YoY to $100.6M and Q3 originations jumped 38% to $446M, with the fair value portfolio at $3.1B yielding 11.3%. But pre-tax earnings fell to $6.9M from $14.2M and net income dropped to $4.8M ($0.20 diluted EPS) from $10.4M ($0.41), while net interest margin declined 7% to $50.5M and expenses rose to $93.7M from $77.9M. Credit deteriorated YoY with annualized net charge-offs of 7.53% versus 6.86% and 30+ day delinquencies of 14.04% versus 12.31%, though management noted vintage-over-vintage CNL improvement from 2022 through 2024. Management gave no formal numeric guidance but signaled confidence in an 18-20% origination growth rate for the year and positioning for growth in 2025, tied to a strengthening ABS market and expected Fed rate cuts.

negative_highlights: Total revenue declined 7% YoY to $178.5M due to government program expirations and construction slowdowns.
US Telecom segment recorded a non-cash goodwill impairment charge of $35 million reflecting market multiple compression.
Operating income turned negative at -$38.4 million, down from $6.8 million in the prior year.
positive_highlights: International segment achieved double-digit Adjusted EBITDA growth of 17.3% to $32.2 million despite flat revenue.
Strong free cash flow generation from operations totaling $97.4 million for the first nine months, up year-over-year.
High-speed data subscribers in international markets increased by 4% compared with last year.
summary: ATN International reported Q3 FY2024 revenue of $178.5 million (down 7% YoY) and a net loss of $32.7 million ($2.26/share), driven by the conclusion of government programs, construction revenue declines, and a non-cash goodwill impairment charge of $35.3 million in the US Telecom segment. Management updated its full-year guidance downward to revenues of $720-$730M (from $730-$750M) and Adjusted EBITDA of $182-$188M (from $190-$200M). While the International segment showed double-digit adjusted EBITDA growth, overall performance was weighed down by US headwinds.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined 40.6% year-over-year driven by a 36.3% drop in active earning OPTAVIA Coaches.
Income from operations fell sharply to $2.1 million (1.5% of revenue) compared to $25.5 million in the prior year period.
Q4 guidance indicates continued decline with an expected loss per share ranging from $0.10 to $0.65.
positive_highlights: EPS of $0.10 per diluted share beat the high end of the guidance range of $0.10 to $0.65 loss.
Revenue met the upper end of the provided guidance range.
Gross profit margin improved 20 basis points to 75.4% despite lower volumes.
summary: Third quarter revenue was $140.2 million, a decrease of 40.6% year-over-year, while EPS beat the high end of guidance at $0.10 per diluted share. Management provided Q4 revenue guidance of $100 million to $120 million and expects a loss per share between $0.10 and $0.65 due to continued pressure on customer acquisition from GLP-1 competition. The company canceled its credit facility to save fees, citing a strong cash position of $170 million.

negative_highlights: Hurricane-related infrastructure damage caused delays in deliveries and procedural volumes for customers, impacting Q3 results.
Patient eligibility backlog within Patient Direct continues to shrink slowly but remains a headwind compared to prior year levels.
Adjusted EPS was flat with the prior year despite revenue growth.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew across both segments with Patient Direct up 6% YoY driven by strong demand in diabetes and sleep supplies.
Gross margins expanded approximately 20 basis points sequentially, though they remain lower than the prior year due to a LIFO credit last quarter.
The company reduced total debt by nearly $200 million during the quarter.
summary: Owens & Minor reported Q3 FY24 revenue of $2.7 billion (up 5% YoY) and adjusted EPS of $0.42 (flat vs prior year). Management provided full-year guidance for revenue between $10.6B-$10.8B, adjusted EBITDA between $540M-$550M, and adjusted EPS between $1.45-$1.55. The company acknowledged that hurricane-related supply chain disruptions and patient eligibility backlogs negatively impacted Q3 performance relative to prior expectations.

negative_highlights: Oil sales down 9% QoQ due to lower prices and wider discounts
Operating netback down 12% to $34.18 per barrel
Cash balance expected to drop by ~$170 million due to i3 funding
positive_highlights: Funds flow from operations up 31% from prior quarter to $60 million
Completed i3 Energy acquisition, increasing 2P reserves by 119%
Sixth consecutive discovery in Ecuador with Charapa-B7 initial 30-day rate of 2,043 bopd
summary: Gran Tierra reported Q3 2024 with $60 million funds flow from operations (up 31% QoQ), $93 million adjusted EBITDA, and net income of $1 million. Production was flat at 32,764 bopd, while oil sales fell 9% due to lower Brent prices and wider differentials. The company completed the i3 Energy acquisition on October 31, significantly boosting reserves and adding Canadian assets, with management reaffirming 2024 guidance and expecting to issue 2025 guidance in early January.

negative_highlights: Net loss of $36 million due to high development expenses and R&D activities.
Certification timeline pushed to 2027, with flight test campaigns starting in 2026.
Production facility investment peak expected in 2026, implying increased cash burn next year.
positive_highlights: Raised $236 million in new capital since July, resulting in record pro forma liquidity of $445 million.
Completed assembly and testing of full-scale engineering prototype; flight campaign expected to start early next year.
ANAC published the basis of certification for eVTOLs in Brazil, a key regulatory milestone.
summary: Eve Air Mobility reported a net loss of $36 million for Q3 FY2024, driven by $32 million in R&D and $9 million in SG&A, partially offset by interest revenues and mark-to-market gains. The company raised $236 million in new capital since July, bringing pro forma liquidity to $445 million, which covers approximately three years of current cash consumption. Management reaffirmed its 2024 cash guidance of $130 million to $170 million, noting that higher Brazilian currency helped stay at the low end of this range.

negative_highlights: Arcadia sales down 19% YoY and adjusted EBITDA margin down 13pts to 5.8%
DynaEnergetics roughly breakeven due to $5M bad debt and inventory charges
Adjusted EPS attributable to DMC was -$0.49; guided Q4 sales and EBITDA below Q3
positive_highlights: NobelClad adjusted EBITDA margin improved to 23.2% on favorable project mix
Leverage ratio remains low at 1.18, below covenant threshold of 3.0
Automation of DynaStage assembly phase one complete; phase two early next year
summary: DMC Global's Q3 FY2024 sales fell 11% sequentially and year-over-year to $152.4 million, with adjusted EBITDA at $5.7 million (4% of sales) and an adjusted net loss of $9.6 million (EPS -$0.49). Weakness was driven by lower construction and energy activity, with Arcadia sales down 19% YoY and EBITDA margin collapsing to 5.8% from 18.8%, and DynaEnergetics roughly breakeven due to $5 million in bad debt/inventory charges. The company halted its strategic review, wrote off $142 million of goodwill, and provided Q4 guidance of $138-148 million sales and $5-8 million adjusted EBITDA, reflecting continued market challenges.

negative_highlights: Senior approved policies were stable YoY in Q1, with revenue growing modestly due to lower policy volume offset by higher LTVs.
SelectRx membership growth slowed sequentially to 5%, with management expecting more modest growth in the first half of fiscal 2025.
Healthcare Services profitability expected to temporarily step down in Q2 due to seasonal investments and the new Olathe facility.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 26% YoY to $292 million in Q1.
Guidance raised: adjusted EBITDA guidance up $10 million at midpoint to $100-$130 million.
Healthcare Services delivered record quarterly adjusted EBITDA of $5 million with SelectRx members up 64% YoY to over 86,000.
summary: SelectQuote reported Q1 FY2025 revenue up 26% YoY to $292 million, with consolidated adjusted EBITDA improving by nearly $10 million YoY. Senior revenue was up modestly to $93 million with adjusted EBITDA of $8 million, and Healthcare Services revenue reached $156 million with record adjusted EBITDA of $5 million. The company raised its full-year fiscal 2025 revenue guidance to $1.425-$1.525 billion (from $1.4-$1.5 billion) and adjusted EBITDA to $100-$130 million (from $90-$120 million). Early AEP performance exceeded expectations, driven by higher agent productivity, close rates, and marketing efficiency, and the company completed a $100 million securitization to improve its balance sheet.

negative_highlights: Local core advertising revenue declined approximately 9% YoY due to displacement in over one-third of the footprint.
Scripps Networks division revenue fell 6% YoY, with Q4 guidance expecting a mid-single-digit decline continuing into next year.
No pay-TV contract renewals occurred in the quarter or prior two quarters, contributing to distribution revenue declines.
positive_highlights: Local Media revenue beat guidance with a 26% YoY increase driven by record political ad spending ($125M).
Company significantly exceeded EBITDA expectations due to tight expense management and strong political cash flow.
Leverage ratio improved rapidly from 6x in Q2 to 5.1x at quarter-end, with a plan to reach high-4s by year end.
summary: Scripps reported Q3 FY2024 revenue of $1.7 billion (implied from segment data) with Local Media up 26% YoY driven by record political advertising ($125M), while Scripps Networks revenue declined 6% and core local ad revenue fell 9%. Management raised full-year political revenue guidance to over $340 million but maintained Q4 guidance for a decline in network revenues. The company significantly exceeded EBITDA expectations, paid down $115M of debt, reduced leverage from 6x to 5.1x, and expects further deleveraging to the high-4s by year-end.

negative_highlights: Total revenue declined 4%, with connected machines down 11% due to Q4 promotional planning
90-day engaged users decreased 3% as pandemic cohorts aged without sufficient new user acquisition offsetting attrition
Gross margin contracted slightly to 46.1% from 46.8% in the prior year
positive_highlights: Paid subscriber count grew 5% year-over-year to over 2.8 million
New user onboarding success improved by nearly 50% compared to a year ago in machine connection time
Cash flow from operations increased significantly to $70 million, up from $36 million the prior year
summary: Cricut reported Q3 FY2024 revenue of $167.9 million, a 4% year-over-year decline driven by an 11% drop in connected machines and lower accessories/materials sales on favorable comps. Operating income fell 55% to $10.6 million as higher marketing spend and increased hosting fees pressured margins despite paid subscribers growing 5%. Management maintained full-year guidance, reiterating expectations for continued revenue declines but anticipating slight platform growth and incremental operating margin improvement.

negative_highlights: Total net revenue declined 4.6% year-over-year driven by the divestiture of WJBR and closure of Guarantee Digital.
National advertising revenue dropped 15.3% ex-political due to advertiser hesitation post-election.
Auto category revenue fell 11% year-over-year reflecting industry-wide profit squeezes from high inventory levels.
positive_highlights: Debt reduced from $300 million to $220 million pro forma following a successful exchange offer and tender.
Digital revenue grew 11.7% on a same-station basis for the quarter as the company shifts mix away from agency business.
Political revenue exceeded budget with $8.2 million booked in Q4 year-to-date, up 23% relative to last year.
summary: Q3 same-station revenue grew 0.5% sequentially but declined 1.6% year-over-year on a same-station basis and 4.6% for total net revenue due to divestitures and the closure of Guarantee Digital. Operating income swung from negative $85.5 million in Q3 last year to positive $1.2 million this year, driven by an impairment reversal and debt reduction, though Adjusted EBITDA declined 6.9% to $5.6 million. Management noted that national advertising remains constrained with advertisers hesitant to book inventory until after the election.

negative_highlights: Operating profit declined 40% due to lower production volumes and higher costs
Global bookings down 36% year-over-year to $370 million
Full-year tax rate increased to 32% from 31%, and Nuvera revenue fell to $0.3 million
positive_highlights: Revenue grew year-over-year with average sales prices up 25%
Bolzoni operating profit improved more than 100% year-over-year
Debt-to-capital ratio improved 500 basis points to 46%
summary: Hyster-Yale reported Q3 FY2024 revenue of $1 billion, up year-over-year, but operating profit fell to $33 million and net income to $17 million from $36 million a year ago, missing expectations due to supply chain constraints and product introduction issues that reduced production volumes. Bookings dropped 36% year-over-year to $370 million, and the company guided to a global market decline in Q4 and a modest decrease in 2025. Management maintained its full-year outlook for significant improvement and expects 2025 shipments roughly in line with 2024, supported by a $2.3 billion backlog, but warned production may moderate without share gains.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined 13% year-over-year driven by a 13% reduction in volume mix, with nearly half of that decline attributed to customers trading down to more affordable products.
Full-year revenue guidance was cut significantly as the anticipated core revenue decline worsened from 5%-9% to 13%-14%.
The company lost a Midwest retailer business worth approximately $20 million to $25 million in sales impact for 2024 due to the customer sourcing windows from China.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA margin remained resilient at 8.7% despite significant volume and mix headwinds.
The company is exceeding its targeted annual cost savings, now expecting approximately $115 million versus a prior target of $100 million.
Significant progress was made in improving quality for door skin production compared to the previous quarter.
summary: Third quarter revenue was $935 million, down 13% year-over-year, with adjusted EBITDA of $82 million and a margin of 8.7%. Management revised full-year 2024 guidance downward to net revenue of $3.7 billion to $3.75 billion (from $3.9B-$4.1B) and adjusted EBITDA of $265 million to $280 million (from $340M-$380M), citing softer demand, mix shifts toward lower-priced products, quality issues, and the loss of a Midwest retailer.

negative_highlights: Q3 production and LOE impacted by a 100-year flood, causing ~800 BOE/d shut-ins and higher LOE
LOE slightly above midpoint due to storm remediation, but offset by reaffirming LOE guidance
Infrastructure projects mostly complete; Q4 capital is primarily D&C, but CapEx guidance reaffirmed at $540-580 million
positive_highlights: raised full-year production guidance by over 5% versus August and 10% above initial 2024 guidance
fifth consecutive quarter of positive free cash flow with debt paydown and share buybacks
Kallus Middle Spraberry well IP of ~1,500 BOE/d, outperforming Wolfcamp A type curve; identified ~300 Middle Spraberry locations
summary: HighPeak Energy reported Q3 2024 production averaging over 51,000 BOE/d, beating expectations and raising full-year production guidance by over 5% versus the prior August guide, to 48,000-51,000 BOE/d. The company generated positive free cash flow for the fifth consecutive quarter, paid down debt, and repurchased shares. Costs were elevated due to a 100-year flood, but LOE guidance is reaffirmed. Strong well results include a 1,500 BOE/d IP from the first Middle Spraberry well, and the company highlighted sub-$50 breakeven inventory of over 1,150 locations.

negative_highlights: Total revenue declined 2.5% year-over-year to $15.9 million.
Biopharma revenue dropped over $2 million due to budget constraints and elongated sales cycles.
Latin America churned a large account acquired earlier in the year, partially offsetting growth elsewhere.
positive_highlights: Cash burn reduced by 39% year-over-year to $9.6 million due to strong cost management.
Adjusted gross margin expanded 60 basis points to 73.1% despite soft revenue.
MSK-ACCESS adoption accelerated with 18 customers signed globally, including recent implementations in Q4.
summary: SOPHiA reported Q3 revenue of $15.9 million, a year-over-year decline of approximately 2.5% driven by material weakness in the biopharma segment which fell over $2 million. Despite this miss, clinical volume reaccelerated with 16% growth (17% excluding COVID), gross margin expanded to 73.1%, and cash burn improved significantly by 39% year-over-year. Management reaffirmed full-year 2024 revenue guidance of $65M-$67M and adjusted operating loss guidance despite the quarterly miss.

negative_highlights: B2B co-issue channel decreased quarter-over-quarter due to unanticipated price changes by GSEs Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac.
Lock volumes are trending lower in the fourth quarter as mortgage rates sit in the high 6s/low 7s compared to Q3 levels.
Ongoing negotiations with Rithm regarding renewal terms for a portion of their subservicing contract.
positive_highlights: Adjusted pre-tax income of $35 million with a 31% adjusted ROE, up from negative returns in prior years.
MSR hedge delivered a net favorable benefit of $10 million this quarter and offset all but $12 million of MSR value changes over the last 12 months.
Total servicing additions reached $60 billion year-to-date with consumer direct recapture volume up 52% versus Q2.
summary: Onity Group reported Q3 FY2024 net income of $21 million and adjusted pre-tax income (PTI) of $35 million with a 31% adjusted ROE, representing sequential improvements in both metrics. The company executed significant debt restructuring transactions reducing corporate and MSR debt by over $180 million year-to-date to close the quarter at a pro forma leverage ratio of roughly 2.9:1 (down from nearly 4x). Management provided forward guidance anticipating slightly improved originations markets but noted potential servicing PTI declines due to lower float, while maintaining an early estimate for full-year adjusted ROE around 15%.

negative_highlights: Net sales declined 15.8% YoY and full-year 2024 sales guidance was lowered to down approximately 17% from a prior ~15% decrease
Gross margin contracted to 16.9% from 17.6% and operating margin fell to 4.9% from 6.8%, with lost fixed-cost leverage of 150 bps
Volvo truck transition will negatively impact sales through 2025, with most significant impact expected next year; two customers also insourced products previously produced as overflow
positive_highlights: Over $45 million in new business secured year-to-date and a pipeline of $270 million in active opportunities, with more than $100 million in the final negotiation stage
Year-to-date free cash flow of $23.1 million and cash of $42.3 million with debt-to-trailing-EBITDA under 1x
Approximately $2.6 million in expected annual savings from a Q3 fixed-cost and SG&A reduction in force; year-to-date gross margin of 18.1% sits within the 17%-19% target range
summary: Q3 FY2024 net sales fell 15.8% YoY to $73 million (product sales down 11.9%), with gross margin of 16.9% versus 17.6% a year ago and operating income of $3.6 million (4.9% of sales) versus 6.8%. Diluted EPS was $0.36 versus $0.49, and adjusted EBITDA was $7.4 million (10.3% of sales) versus $9.8 million (11.3%). Management lowered full-year 2024 sales expectations to down approximately 17% from a prior ~15% decrease, citing customer demand schedule changes around the holidays, while maintaining full-year gross margin guidance of 17%-19%. The Volvo truck model transition began this quarter and is expected to pressure sales through 2025, though the company cited over $45 million in new business won year-to-date and a pipeline of more than $270 million.

negative_highlights: Non-GAAP gross margin fell to 23.2% from 36.2% year-over-year
Adjusted EBITDA of -$7.7 million and non-GAAP EPS loss of -$0.87
Full-year revenue guidance midpoint lowered by $20 million and adjusted EBITDA by $14 million
positive_highlights: Q2 orders shaping up to be even stronger; record bookings possible
Trailing 12-month book-to-bill above 1
summary: Aviat Networks reported Q1 FY2025 revenue of $88.4 million, up 1.7% year-over-year, but with non-GAAP gross margin of 23.2% (down from 36.2%) and adjusted EBITDA of -$7.7 million. The company lowered its full-year FY2025 guidance to $430-$470 million revenue and $30-$40 million adjusted EBITDA, citing US Tier 1 CapEx weakness, project timing issues, and execution distractions. Management noted a book-to-bill over 1 for the trailing twelve months and expects a V-shaped recovery with Q2 orders tracking strong, potentially record bookings. They remain optimistic about private network growth, including ProVision Plus software opportunity and Aprisa 5G wins.

negative_highlights: Total revenue declined 2% YoY, with DTC and Outpost channels down due to shifting consumer preferences
Energy launch will be a drag on gross margins in 2025 (below 40%) due to slotting and trade expenses
Higher green coffee prices pressuring margins, with Q4 gross margin expected in high 30s
positive_highlights: Gross margin improved over 8 points YoY to 42.3% YTD, exceeding 40% target for third consecutive quarter
FDM ACV increased 18 points sequentially to 41%, with wholesale revenue ex-barter up 12% in Q3
Adjusted EBITDA up 15% YoY to $7.1 million and free cash flow improved $60 million YTD
summary: Q3 revenue declined 2% YoY to $100.7 million (not stated, but ex-barter up 2%), with wholesale segment revenue growing 3% YoY and 17% YTD. Adjusted EBITDA rose 15% YoY to $7.1 million, with gross margin expanding over 8 points YoY to 42.3% YTD. Management narrowed revenue guidance and raised EBITDA midpoint to $35-40 million, while lowering free cash flow expectations to positive (from 80% conversion). FDM ACV increased 18 points sequentially to 41% and RTD ACV rose 5 points YoY to 47%, but DTC and Outpost channels remain under pressure.

negative_highlights: Total advertising revenue decreased 10% year-over-year driven by an unusual high mix of harder-to-monetize G and PG rated movies in July
National attendance declined 8% year-over-year, contributing to lower national revenue per attendee (down 3%)
Q4 guidance reflects a challenging comparable due to the absence of Taylor Swift's Eras Tour demand pull from last October
positive_highlights: Revenue of $62.4 million beat guidance range of $56-58 million; adjusted OIBDA of $8.8M beat guidance of $6-8M
Scatter market revenue per attendee increased year-over-year as advertisers shifted spend closer to campaign dates
New programmatic self-serve offering saw sales up 96% quarter-over-quarter with its biggest quarter since launch
summary: NCM reported Q3 FY2024 revenue of $62.4 million and adjusted OIBDA of $8.8 million, both exceeding guidance ranges but representing a year-over-year decline in total advertising revenue (down 10%) due to lower attendance and an unfavorable mix of G/PG-rated films. Management raised Q4 FY2024 guidance for revenue ($82-86M) and adjusted OIBDA ($28-30M), citing challenges from the Taylor Swift event in October last year and a soft December film slate, while expressing optimism about 2025.

negative_highlights: Total revenue fell to RMB27.0 million from RMB353.6 million year-over-year, a 92% decline.
Q4 revenue guidance of RMB15-17.5 million is a further sequential decline from Q3's RMB27.0 million.
General and administrative expenses rose to RMB45.2 million from RMB34.7 million, outpacing revenue.
positive_highlights: Net income swung to RMB67.9 million from a loss a year ago, with operating profit of RMB35.2 million.
Overseas platform AutoCango.com accumulated over 370,000 page views and nearly 60,000 registered users since launch.
Net recovery on credit provisions was RMB74.4 million, helping profitability and balance-sheet improvement.
summary: Cango's Q3 2024 revenue was RMB27.0 million, down sharply from RMB353.6 million a year ago, but the company swung to operating profit of RMB35.2 million from a loss of RMB87.8 million, and net income was RMB67.9 million. Non-GAAP adjusted net income was RMB71.3 million, with basic non-GAAP EPS of RMB0.69 per ADS. The company guided Q4 2024 revenue to RMB15-17.5 million, implying continued sequential decline, but highlighted growth in its international used-car platform AutoCango.com and continued diligence on credit risk, with M1+ at 3.17% and M3+ at 1.76%.

negative_highlights: Net interest income decreased from the prior quarter due to projecting increased prepayment speeds on the residential loan portfolio given recent rate moves.
EAD per share declined from $0.19 in Q2 (implied) or previous levels to $0.17, with Arc Home contributing a specific loss of $0.02 for the quarter.
Management indicated they will likely commit less capital to agency-eligible investor loans over the next few quarters due to increased competition and stretching MBS execution channels.
positive_highlights: Book value increased by approximately 2% to $10.58 per share driven by hedge-adjusted mark-to-market gains on securitized loan and non-Agency RMBS portfolios.
Successfully retired the $86 million WMC convertible note maturity after issuing $100 million in investment grade unsecured bonds earlier in the year.
Initiated a new home equity lending segment with acquisitions of approximately $150 million and commitments for another $200 million, targeting an attractive market size.
summary: MITT reported GAAP EPS of $0.40 and EAD per share of $0.17 for Q3 FY2024, driven by mark-to-market gains but offset by a projected increase in prepayment speeds due to rate rallies which reduced net interest income compared to the prior quarter. The company deleveraged its balance sheet from 2.5 turns to 1.5 turns following the maturity of WMC convertible notes and sold Agency RMBS, ending with $120 million in liquidity. Management expressed caution regarding near-term volatility around elections but maintained confidence in their credit book resilience.

negative_highlights: Net income declined 66% YoY primarily due to $8.8 million of pretax debt refinancing costs associated with retiring Senior Notes.
Free cash flow generation was lower than the prior year period, impacted by increased working capital usage for contactless chip inventory and CEO transition-related costs.
positive_highlights: Net sales increased 18% YoY with product sales growing 25%, driven by eco-focused contactless cards and Card@Once instant issuance solutions.
Gross margins expanded 170 basis points from the prior year quarter to 35.8% due to operating leverage.
Adjusted EBITDA increased 18% YoY, with income from operations in the Debit and Credit segment rising 30%.
summary: CPI Card Group reported Q3 FY2024 net sales growth of 18% and adjusted EBITDA growth of 18%, driven by a 25% increase in product sales led by eco-focused contactless cards. Management raised its full-year outlook for both net sales (to mid-to-high single-digit) and adjusted EBITDA, citing strength across the portfolio despite ongoing channel inventory normalization. The company also updated free cash flow expectations to be slightly below 2023 levels due to working capital improvements.

negative_highlights: Fourth quarter guidance implies lower servicing revenue and absence of one-time insurance benefit
Management notes expected ongoing market challenges and inflationary vendor costs
Mortgage market volumes remain historically low, though forecast to recover in 2025
positive_highlights: First profitable quarter since Q1 2022, with adjusted net income of $7 million
Pull-through weighted rate lock volume up 19% YoY, near high end of guidance
Gain on sale margin of 329 bps, above guidance of 280-300 bps
summary: In Q3 2024, loanDepot returned to profitability with adjusted net income of $7 million, versus a $29 million adjusted net loss in the prior year, driven by higher volume and improved margins. Pull-through weighted rate lock volume was $6.7 billion (up 19% YoY), at the high end of guidance, and gain on sale margin of 329 bps exceeded guidance of 280-300 bps. The company completed its Vision 2025 cost program (reducing annualized non-volume expenses by over $730 million) and launched a new multi-year strategic plan, Project North Star. For Q4, management guides to rate lock volume of $5.5-7.5 billion and gain on sale margin of 285-305 bps.

negative_highlights: Full-year SHOP NOI guidance lowered to $102-107 million; Q4 implied SHOP NOI drops to roughly $24 million on ~$4 million of hurricane costs
Year-end occupancy now expected just below 80% versus the original ~400 bps ramp assumption, with Q3 ending at 79.4%; sequential SHOP NOI declined despite YoY growth

Medical office/life science same-store occupancy fell 150 bps to 87.8% on the Valley Durham vacate, with ~9% of annualized revenue expiring through year-end 2025 and a 233,000 sq ft St. Louis tenant vacate in Q1 2025
positive_highlights: Consolidated SHOP NOI rose 32.6% YoY on 6.4% revenue growth, with same-store margin expansion of 240 bps YoY and average monthly rate up 5.4%
Annual insurance program renewed effective July 1 with $6.8 million, or 26%, reduction in premiums to be realized in upcoming quarters

Under agreements or LOIs to note 28 properties for ~$348 million, including the 18 triple-net senior living communities at over $150,000 per unit and a 7.3% in-place cap rate, with ~$300 million earmarked to partially redeem the zero-coupon secured notes
summary: DHC reported Q3 normalized FFO of $4.0 million, or $0.02 per share, with same-property cash NOI of $65.8 million, up 16.1% YoY but down 1.5% sequentially. SHOP NOI of $27.4 million rose 32.6% YoY but declined sequentially as expenses climbed 140 bps on wages, seasonal utilities and $2.5 million of one-time fire and hurricane costs. Management lowered full-year SHOP NOI guidance to $102-107 million, citing Q3 shortfall, roughly $4 million of Q4 hurricane costs, and year-end occupancy now expected just below 80% versus a prior ~400 bps ramp, and cut CapEx guidance to $180-190 million. The company is expanding its SHOP disposition program to 32 communities (2,422 units, negative $2 million NOI) and pivoted its $440 million June 2025 maturity refinancing to smaller tranches and diversified lenders after agency financing proved slower than expected.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA margin contracted 350 bps to 3.5%, with net loss of $0.03 per diluted share versus $0.14 of income a year ago
Full-year 2024 revenue guidance cut to $710–740 million from $730–780 million and adjusted EBITDA cut to $20–25 million from $28–36 million
Electrical Systems revenue fell 19% and adjusted operating income dropped $5 million; Vehicle Solutions revenue fell 16% with operating income down $4.5 million
positive_highlights: Year-to-date new business wins reached approximately $95 million, including $18 million in Q3
Free cash flow from continuing operations was $17 million versus $11 million in the prior-year quarter, aided by $20 million from the Cab Structures sale
Headcount reduced by approximately 1,200 roles, or 15% of the continuing-operations workforce
summary: CVG reported Q3 2024 continuing-ops revenue of $171.8 million, down from $202.9 million, with an adjusted net loss of $0.01 per share versus $0.14 of income a year ago. Adjusted EBITDA fell to $4.3 million (3.5% margin) from $12.2 million (6.0%) on lower volumes, inflation, and operational inefficiencies. Management cut full-year 2024 revenue guidance to $710–740 million from $730–780 million and adjusted EBITDA to $20–25 million from $28–36 million, and CEO James Ray said he was "not happy" with the results. The quarter was framed around portfolio reshaping, including Cab Structures, Chillicothe, and Industrial Automation divestitures, but leadership declined to quantify the benefit and indicated Q4 would be seasonally weakest.
