RNG production rose to 1.0 million MMBtus from 0.7 million, a more than 40% year-over-year increase, and management kept 2024 guidance unchanged, calling results in line with expectations. The company commissioned Sapphire and Polk, lifting operating design capacity to 8.8 million MMBtus, and has six projects in construction totaling 2.6 million MMBtus of OPAL's share, including newly announced Kirby. Management expressed confidence that the election outcome is neutral-to-positive for RNG policy, and noted first ITC monetization of $8.6 million not included in adjusted EBITDA.

negative_highlights: FinTech vertical declined by 13% YoY due to changing client payment support models.
Free cash flow decreased to $4.1 million compared to $6.6 million last year, driven by higher capital expenditures and longer DSOs of 75 days.
positive_highlights: Record Q1 revenue of $129.7M representing a 4.1% YoY increase, ending a period of flat-to-down performance.
Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to 12%, marking the ninth consecutive quarter of year-over-year improvement in this metric.
Raised full-year FY2025 revenue guidance lower bound from $510M to $515M, signaling confidence in momentum.
summary: IBEX reported record Q1 FY2025 revenue of $129.7 million (up 4.1% YoY) and adjusted EPS of $0.52 (up 30% YoY). Management raised the full-year fiscal 2025 revenue guidance range to $515-$525 million from a prior lower bound of $510 million, while maintaining an adjusted EBITDA outlook of $67-$69 million. The quarter featured margin expansion driven by offshore growth and new AI wins.

negative_highlights: Total revenue declined sequentially by 6% to $88.8 million, driven by a significant drop in marketing-driven business lines.
RPS for the Partner Network decreased 68% year-over-year and 7% quarter-over-quarter due to Google Search Partner Network volatility.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA of $10.3 million exceeded the high end of guidance by approximately $600k-$700k combined across key metrics.
summary: System1 reported Q3 FY2024 revenue of $88.8 million (up 1% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $10.3 million, exceeding the high end of guidance by approximately $600k-$700k combined across metrics despite a sequential decline in total revenue driven by marketing-driven business volatility. Management highlighted strong performance from owned-and-operated products like MapQuest (record usage) and CouponFollow, which offset declines in Google Search Partner Network-dependent segments where RPS fell 68% YoY due to watch-side policy changes. Due to ongoing market uncertainty regarding the SPN rebound timing and holiday season dynamics, management decided not to provide Q4 guidance.

negative_highlights: Revenue down 16.8% YoY and gross margin fell to 12.5% due to $3.4M inventory charge
Sluggish growth in Germany, Italy, Netherlands; continued macro headwinds
Q4 guidance includes potential additional inventory charges and EBITDA loss remains
positive_highlights: Sequential revenue growth of 12.1% and continued momentum over three quarters
Market share gains: DC optimizer share up from 9% in 2022 to 13% in 2023
New contracts and ARR growth in EI software; strong growth in newer markets
summary: In Q3 FY2024, Tigo Energy reported revenue of $14.2 million, down 16.8% YoY but up 12.1% sequentially. Gross margin fell to 12.5% due to a $3.4 million battery inventory charge; adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed to $8.3 million. Management raised market share gains and strong growth in newer regions like Czech Republic and Australia, but noted sluggishness in Germany, Italy, and Netherlands. Q4 guidance is $14-17 million revenue and $6.5-8.5 million adjusted EBITDA loss, with potential additional inventory charges. EBITDA breakeven is expected in 2025, likely H2.

negative_highlights: Total revenue fell 1.5% to $14.3 million due to non-recurring ICFA revenue in Q3 2023
Management stated high inflation and cost drivers 'have caught up with us' and are impacting earnings growth
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA rose 7.2% to $8.2 million from $7.6 million in Q3 2023
Net income increased to $2.9 million or $0.12 per diluted share from $2.6 million or $0.11
Active service connections grew 4.7% to 63,889, with Maricopa multifamily permits up 281% year-to-date to 1,200 units
summary: Global Water Resources reported Q3 2024 total revenue of $14.3 million, down 1.5% year-over-year, as ICFA revenue recognized in Q3 2023 did not recur; regulated revenue rose 2.2% to $14.3 million. Operating expenses declined 3.3% to $10.3 million, and net income improved to $2.9 million or $0.12 per diluted share from $2.6 million or $0.11. Adjusted EBITDA grew 7.2% to $8.2 million, and active connections rose 4.7% to 63,889. No formal guidance was issued; management flagged that inflation is impacting earnings growth and that the two largest utilities will file a rate case in the first half of 2025.

negative_highlights: GAAP gross margin contracted sharply to 0.9% due to a one-time inventory write-down of $2.8 million.
A large Clinical Solutions order was canceled for Q4 delivery, expected to lower fourth-quarter revenue.
Lab Essentials revenue decreased 2% YoY despite sequential customer growth.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 17% YoY driven by a 229% increase in Clinical Solutions revenue ($0.6M -> $2.0M).
Free cash outflow improved significantly to $2.4 million, the lowest level since Q2 2021.
Operating expenses declined sequentially and reached their lowest level since IPO.
summary: Teknova reported Q3 FY2024 revenue of $9.6 million (up 17% YoY), driven by a surge in Clinical Solutions sales ($2.0M) and stable Lab Essentials growth despite specific customer headwinds. However, GAAP gross margin collapsed to 0.9% due to a one-time $2.8 million non-cash inventory write-down; excluding this charge, margins would have been 29.8%. The company reiterated full-year revenue guidance of $35M-$38M and lowered its free cash flow outflow forecast for the year from an implied higher level to less than $16 million.

negative_highlights: Spreads continued to compress in Q3, albeit at a slower pace
Watch list increased slightly to 5.6% of fair value
Repurchase activity remains modest relative to program size ($14M of $100M)
positive_highlights: NII of $0.58 per share fully covers regular and special distributions
Net asset value increased to $18.15 per share from $18.03
No new non-accruals during the quarter; non-accruals stable at 1.5% of fair value
summary: NCDL reported Q3 2024 net investment income of $0.58 per share, fully covering its regular and special dividends of $0.45 and $0.10 per share, with total GAAP net income of $0.67 per share including $0.09 of net realized and unrealized gains. Net asset value rose to $18.15 per share from $18.03, and the company originated $226 million of new investments, with no new non-accruals and non-accruals at roughly 1.5% of fair value. Management expressed optimism for 2025, citing moderate spread compression, expected M&A pickup, and a large repurchase program with $14 million used of a $100 million authorization.

negative_highlights: SUNRISE-3 trial did not have desired outcome
COVID-19 variants trended milder, limiting drug impact
Market research shows 94% of prescribers not satisfied with current treatments
positive_highlights: Cash runway projected into 2027
Phase II HCV lead-in cohort showed 97% SVR12
Phase III HCV program expected to start early next year
summary: Atea reported Q3 2024 results with cash of $482.8 million, down from $492.8 million at the start of Q4, and expects cash runway into 2027. The key event was the failure of the SUNRISE-3 COVID-19 trial, which did not meet expectations due to milder disease and no hospitalizations. The company is pivoting to its HCV program, with Phase II top-line results expected in early December and Phase III planned for early 2025. R&D expenses decreased mainly due to lower COVID-19 spending.

negative_highlights: GAAP net loss of $2.2 million (-$0.16 per diluted share) driven by a $6 million non-cash impairment charge related to MRI Network assets.
System-wide sales declined to $148.6 million from $151.2 million, with professional recruiting and staffing brands down $6.5 million.
Permanent placement market described as 'incredibly tough' for seven consecutive quarters, with no clear recovery yet.
positive_highlights: Adjusted net income increased 29% YoY to $2.8 million, or $0.20 per diluted share, versus $2.2 million or $0.16 per diluted share in Q3 2023.
Adjusted EBITDA rose to $4.9 million from $3.7 million, with margin expanding to 52% from 40%.
SG&A expenses decreased 15.3% to $5.4 million and net workers' compensation expense fell to approximately $499,000 from $1.5 million.
summary: HireQuest reported Q3 FY2024 total revenue of $9.4 million, up 1.6% YoY, with franchise royalties of $9.0 million versus $8.9 million. GAAP net loss was $2.2 million (-$0.16 per diluted share) due to a $6 million non-cash MRI impairment charge, while adjusted net income rose 29% to $2.8 million ($0.20 per diluted share) and adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to 52% from 40%. System-wide sales fell to $148.6 million from $151.2 million, as temporary staffing grew 3.6% but professional recruiting declined $6.5 million. SG&A fell 15.3% and workers' compensation expense dropped nearly 67%. Management gave no explicit quantitative guidance but expressed optimism for stabilization and improved results into 2025, citing lower interest rates, normalized immigration policy, and franchisee productivity.

negative_highlights: Total revenue declined 3% year-over-year reflecting lingering macroeconomic headwinds and reduced customer expansion in the prior period.
Average paid members were flat quarter-over-quarter but decreased 5% compared to last year, indicating continued pressure on subscription growth.
positive_highlights: Total revenue beat street consensus with a $35.4M quarter-over-quarter increase driven by strong performance in adjusted EBITDA ($9.7M).
Interchange revenue from the Expensify Card surged 48% year-over-year to $4.6 million as migration to the new program accelerated.
Full-year free cash flow guidance was raised sequentially for a third time, now set at $19-$20 million.
summary: Expensify reported Q3 FY2024 revenue of $35.4 million (6.3% QoQ increase) and adjusted EBITDA of $9.7 million, beating consensus forecasts despite a 3% YoY decline in revenue due to lingering macro challenges. Management raised full-year free cash flow guidance from the previous range up to $19-$20 million, citing strong performance driven by higher interchange take rates on the new card program and operational efficiencies. The company highlighted that 94% of existing card spend has migrated to the new Expensify Card program, which generates 20% more interchange revenue.

negative_highlights: Total transaction volume decreased 9.5% year-over-year to 9,331 transactions due to higher mortgage rates and home prices.
GAAP net loss widened significantly to $8.1 million from $5.5 million in the prior year quarter.
Management elected to withhold Q4 guidance entirely, citing uncertainty regarding interest rates and acquisition impacts.
positive_highlights: Ancillary business revenue increased 44% year-over-year by $1.6 million to offset some brokerage declines.
Real Estate division gross profit margin expanded to 5.7% from 5.1% due to fee increases and new high-value property fees.
Mortgage division revenue surged 52% year-over-year to $2.9 million driven by loan officer base growth.
summary: Third quarter revenue declined 10% year-over-year to $83.7 million, driven by an 11% drop in brokerage transactions and the absence of insurance business revenue following its sale in May. Adjusted EBITDA widened to a loss of $1.4 million compared to a $250,000 loss in the prior year quarter. Management explicitly withheld Q4 guidance due to interest rate uncertainty and the integration impact of the My Home Group acquisition.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to $24.4 million in Q3 2024 from $22.8 million a year earlier.
R&D expenses increased to $21.4 million from $19.8 million year over year.
No revenue or earnings guidance was provided, as the company remains clinical-stage with no approved products.
positive_highlights: Independent Data Monitoring Committee recommended the Phase 3 ENSURE trials continue as planned without changes after an interim analysis.
CALLIPER topline data in progressive MS is expected in April 2025, a near-term clinical catalyst.
Cash of $59.1 million expected to fund operations into Q3 2025.
summary: Immunic reported a Q3 2024 net loss of $24.4 million, or $0.24 per share, with R&D expenses rising to $21.4 million from $19.8 million a year earlier and G&A increasing to $4.4 million from $3.8 million. Cash and equivalents stood at $59.1 million, which management expects to fund operations into the third quarter of 2025. The quarter contained no revenue or earnings guidance; the main updates were clinical, including a favorable IDMC context for the Phase 3 ENSURE program and an expected April 2025 topline readout for the Phase 2 CALLIPER trial. Management discussed partnering interest and peak sales potential but gave no specific new financial guidance or partnership terms.

negative_highlights: SaaS ARPU declined sequentially to $307 from $333 due to introductory pricing for migrated customers.
Marketing Services billings fell 35% year-over-year as customers convert to the SaaS platform.
Recorded a noncash impairment charge of $83.1 million related to the structural decline of the marketing services business.
positive_highlights: SaaS revenue beat guidance at $87.1M, representing a 29% year-over-year increase.
Net dollar retention expanded significantly to 101%, up 900 bps year-over-year.
Raised full-year EBITDA guidance range to $33.5-$34.5 million following the Keap acquisition.
summary: Thryv reported Q3 FY2024 SaaS revenue of $87.1 million (up 29% YoY) and Marketing Services revenue of $92.8 million, beating guidance on both fronts. The company raised its full-year consolidated EBITDA guidance to $33.5-$34.5 million following the acquisition of Keap, which added over 15,000 customers and $80+ million in annualized revenue. Consolidated adjusted gross margin expanded 480 bps YoY to 65%, driven by SaaS mix and the transition of marketing services clients to higher-margin SaaS products.

negative_highlights: Direct-to-consumer sales declined 23.2% year-over-year to $19.2 million due to a downsized sales force.
Rental revenue fell 13.1% to $13.9 million driven by lower average billing rates and a shift to private payers.
Operating expenses increased 3.2% (excluding one-time charges) due to higher advertising costs and personnel expenses.
positive_highlights: Total revenue grew 5.8% year-over-year to $88.8 million.
Domestic business-to-business revenue surged 35.1% to $23.4 million.
Gross margin expanded significantly to 46.5%, up 630 basis points from the prior year.
summary: Inogen reported Q3 FY2024 revenue of $88.8 million, a 5.8% year-over-year increase driven by strong business-to-business growth, partially offset by declines in direct-to-consumer and rental channels. The company raised its full-year 2024 revenue guidance to a range of $329-$331 million (approx. 4-5% growth) and achieved positive adjusted EBITDA for the second consecutive quarter. Management expressed confidence in the path to profitability, citing gross margin expansion to 46.5% and improved cash flow generation.

negative_highlights: The Phase Ib ADCT-601 solid tumor program targeting AXL was discontinued after failing to demonstrate a favorable benefit-risk profile during dose optimization.
Management noted that bispecifics have penetrated significantly in the academic setting and made inroads into the community, taking over about one-third of the overall third-line plus market share.
No specific revenue guidance or quantitative sales targets were provided for the current indication beyond a peak potential of $80-plus million.
positive_highlights: ZYNLONTA net product revenues increased year-over-year to $18.0 million in Q3 2024 driven by volume and net price increases.
Year-to-date ZYNLONTA revenues reached $52.9 million, maintaining stability despite competitive pressure from bispecifics which captured approximately one-third of the market share.
Non-GAAP operating expenses decreased year-to-date by 12% versus the prior year due to efficiencies, partially offset by investments in LOTIS-5.
summary: ADC Therapeutics reported Q3 FY2024 net product revenues of $18.0 million for ZYNLONTA, representing a year-over-year increase to $52.9 million year-to-date versus $52.4 million in the prior year period. The company maintained its disciplined capital allocation strategy with cash and equivalents of $274.3 million at quarter-end, funding operations into mid-2026. Management highlighted progress in LOTIS-5 enrollment nearing completion and interim data expectations for LOTIS-7 in December, while discontinuing the AXL solid tumor program due to an unfavorable benefit-risk profile.

negative_highlights: IP&S segment continued outflows (~R$1.2 billion), with management flagging that high SELIC rates make significant inflows difficult
Management fees grew only 2% YoY as reported, and retroactive fees fell to R$3 million versus larger impacts in prior comparable periods
Q4 will carry roughly R$35 million of one-time M&A transaction costs tied to Compass and Lacan closings
positive_highlights: Adjusted distributable earnings of R$1.08/share rose 12% YoY and FRE of R$1.02/share rose 7% YoY
Private markets momentum: R$0.5 billion of new commitments in the quarter, VICC at R$1.5 billion toward a R$2 billion target, and SPS IV first close expected above the ~R$1 billion size of Fund III
Compass combination closed with combined AUM of $54 billion, plus the Lacan acquisition (R$1.5 billion AUM) expected to be immediately accretive to FRE and DE per share
summary: Vinci reported Q3 2024 FRE of R$53.8 million (R$1.02/share, up 7% YoY per share) and adjusted distributable earnings of R$57.1 million (R$1.08/share, up 12% YoY per share), with AUM of R$70 billion up 8% YoY. Fee-related revenues rose 5% YoY to R$112.7 million, and management fees grew 9% excluding catch-up fees; retroactive fees were only R$3 million this quarter versus larger impacts in Q2 and Q3 2023. The quarter was dominated by strategic news rather than an operational beat: the Compass combination closed (combined AUM of $54 billion) and the Lacan forestry acquisition was announced (R$1.5 billion AUM), both expected to be accretive to FRE/DE per share starting Q4. IP&S continued to see outflows of roughly R$1.2 billion on high Brazilian real rates, partially offset by positive public equity net inflows and continued private markets fundraising.

negative_highlights: Weighted average portfolio yield declined to 18.3% from 18.7% at June 30 due to repricing amendments and the 50 bps prime rate cut
Loan number 9 remains on nonaccrual status carrying a $1.4 million CECL reserve
Florida adult-use legalization fell note weakness in of the 60% threshold, and the MSOS ETF fell more than 25%, limiting a potential source of new investment opportunities
positive_highlights: Net interest income rose to $14.5 million from $13.2 million in Q2 and adjusted distributable EPS increased to $0.56 from $0.50
Portfolio credit quality improved with 72% of loans risk-rated 2 or better versus 61% at June 30, and the CECL reserve fell to $4.1 million from $5.1 million
Liquidity exceeds $75 million, with a new $50 million unsecured term loan at 9% and a BBB+ rating from Egan-Jones, plus full repayment of Loan 11 at par
summary: REFI reported Q3 net interest income of $14.5 million, up from $13.2 million in Q2, with adjusted distributable earnings of $0.56 per diluted share versus $0.50 in the prior quarter. The loan portfolio stood at $362 million across 29 companies with an 18.3% weighted average yield, down from 18.7% at June 30 on repricing amendments and a 50 bps prime rate cut. Book value rose to $15.05 per share from $14.92, the $0.47 dividend was unchanged, and the company affirmed its previously issued March 12 guidance. Credit metrics improved, with 72% of the portfolio risk-rated 2 or better versus 61% prior quarter, though the portfolio yield declined and Florida adult-use legalization failed while the MSOS ETF dropped over 25%.

negative_highlights: General and administrative expenses surged year-over-year from $3.8M to $6.1M due to non-cash stock comp for the new CEO, severance payments ($0.7M), and IP litigation costs.
Operating cash flow decreased by approximately $2 million (excluding one-time items) despite revenue growth.
Management declined to provide specific Q4 guidance or financial targets, citing ongoing uncertainty regarding business development priorities.
positive_highlights: Net product sales of $7.0M beat Q3 FY2023 ($6.5M) and H1 2024 total sales (~$22M) exceeded full-year 2023 revenue.
Achieved >90% reimbursement rates in the AYA population, validating commercial viability for a new growth segment.
Secured partnerships with major health plans (via Orsini) and academic centers to drive adoption over compounded alternatives.
summary: Fennec reported Q3 FY2024 net product sales of $7.0 million compared to $6.5 million in the prior year quarter and total H1 2024 sales of approximately $22 million, exceeding full-year 2023 revenue but missing analyst expectations for a profitable or cash-positive quarter due to significant G&A increases driven by CEO severance ($0.7M) and IP litigation expenses. Management highlighted positive momentum in the Adolescent/Young Adult (AYA) segment with >90% reimbursement achieved and new customer adoption, while noting that operating cash decreased by approximately $2 million for the period excluding one-time items.

negative_highlights: Comparable RevPAR fell 1.6% YoY to $261 and AFFO per diluted share was negative $0.24 with a net loss of $1.4 million
Resort leisure demand declined YoY and Ritz-Carlton Lake Tahoe renovation disrupted results; 77% of debt is effectively floating at a 7.6% blended rate
Hurricanes Helene and Milton caused an estimated $500K-$700K impact at the Sarasota property with some October group cancellations; no common share buybacks executed yet
positive_highlights: Urban portfolio RevPAR grew 6% to $213 and total urban hotel revenue rose 8% with occupancy up 4%
October Comparable RevPAR increased 7.5% with Comparable Total Revenue up almost 11%, and Q1 2025 group pace is up nearly 40%
Hilton La Jolla Torrey Pines sold for $165 million ($419,000 per key) at a 7.2% cap rate; $407 million CMBS refinancing extended maturity to 2029 at SOFR + 3.24%
summary: Braemar reported Q3 2024 Comparable RevPAR of $261, down 1.6% YoY, with Comparable Hotel EBITDA of $24.7 million, a net loss of $1.4 million ($0.02 per diluted share), and AFFO per diluted share of negative $0.24. Urban hotels grew RevPAR 6% (to $213) and group revenue rose 14%, while resorts softened and Ritz-Carlton Lake Tahoe renovation weighed on results. October Comparable RevPAR rose 7.5% with total revenue up nearly 11%, Q1 2025 group pace is up nearly 40%, and full-year 2025 group revenue pace is up 13%, but the quarter itself saw a RevPAR decline and negative AFFO. The company closed the $165 million Hilton La Jolla Torrey Pines sale, refinanced a $407 million five-hotel CMBS loan, redeemed roughly $50 million of non-traded preferred, and has not repurchased any common shares.

negative_highlights: Consolidated adjusted gross profit margins decreased by 40 basis points YoY due to the partial quarter impact of acquiring Plastiq in Q3.
SMB segment margins contracted as higher credit losses and a mix shift with top resellers offset revenue growth.
positive_highlights: Revenue increased by more than 20% YoY driven by organic growth in SMB, B2B, and enterprise segments.
Adjusted EBITDA reached a new quarterly record of $54.6 million with an increase of over 18% from the prior year quarter.
Plastiq acquisition is now profitable after integration, contributing to sequential margin expansion when excluding timing impacts.
summary: Priority Technology Holdings reported Q3 FY2024 revenue of $227 million (up >20% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $54.6 million (a record). Management raised full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance to a range of $200-$204 million, citing strong organic growth in B2B and enterprise segments which now contribute nearly 60% of gross profit. The company affirmed revenue and gross profit guidance while noting that the reported consolidated margin decline was primarily due to the partial quarter impact from the Plastiq acquisition.

negative_highlights: Realized PA gas price of $1.54/Mcf with curtailments continuing through the quarter
PA operating costs rose approximately 40% in the quarter due to Auburn-area plugging and abandonment
Q4 liquids production expected to decline quarter-over-quarter until drilling resumes in 2025, and no incremental PA drilling is forecast for 2025
positive_highlights: Permian seventh Ector well drove 19% quarter-over-quarter oil production growth
Permian contributed approximately $8.5 million of adjusted EBITDA year-to-date, 70% of the total company figure
Three of seven deferred PA TIL wells put on flowback, adding about 8 MMcf/d net at a ~13% net revenue interest
summary: Epsilon called Q3 the trough for its Pennsylvania business, with production curtailed and realized gas prices at $1.54/Mcf, while P&A activity in the Auburn area lifted PA operating costs roughly 40% for the quarter. The Permian's seventh Ector well drove 19% quarter-over-quarter oil production growth and contributed about $8.5 million of adjusted EBITDA year-to-date, 70% of the company total. Management guided to Q4 liquids declines until drilling resumes in 2025, but expects natural gas volume growth in Q4 as curtailments lift and deferred TILs come online, and it entered Alberta via two JVs with roughly $10 million of CapEx planned over 12 months starting December. No formal guidance figures or consensus comparisons were provided.

negative_highlights: Capital expenditures were elevated at $2.9 million due to equipment purchases for oncology and wound care growth.
Negative pressure wound therapy equipment sales were lower due to a difficult comparison with a surge in leases from the prior year.
Chemo Mouthpiece revenue is not expected to contribute meaningfully until next year (2025).
positive_highlights: Revenue exceeded $35 million for the first time ever with strong sequential growth of nearly 5%.
Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded significantly to 22.3%, exceeding the prior year's 19.8%.
Operating cash flow surged to $9.8 million, more than double the prior year quarter.
summary: InfuSystem reported Q3 FY2024 net revenue of $35.2 million, representing an 11% year-over-year increase and nearly 5% sequential growth. Adjusted EBITDA margins expanded to 22.3%, driven by higher-margin oncology and rental mix, while operating cash flow reached a record $9.8 million. Management reaffirmed full-year 2024 guidance for high single-digit revenue growth and adjusted EBITDA margins in the high teens.

negative_highlights: Private jet gross bookings fell 20% year-over-year and total gross bookings fell 16%
On-time performance of 82% was below the company's target for the quarter
Guidance shifted to positive adjusted EBITDA for full-year 2025 only, with Q4 2024 absorbing fleet modernization costs; adjusted EBITDA loss remained $20 million and GAAP net loss $58 million
positive_highlights: Adjusted contribution margin of 14.8%, up from 7.8% in Q2 and 1% in Q1, the highest since going public in 2021
Prepaid block sales rose 86% year-over-year to $147 million, with corporate block sales up over 50%
Operating cash flow improved 44% sequentially and 94% year-over-year to a $15 million outflow from $250 million a year ago
summary: Revenue was $194 million in Q3, roughly flat sequentially after seven quarters of prior decline, with adjusted contribution margin at 14.8% (up from 7.8% in Q2 and a record since going public) and adjusted EBITDA loss of $20 million, improved $17 million sequentially. Prepaid block sales rose 86% year-over-year to $147 million, but private jet gross bookings fell 20% year-over-year and on-time performance of 82% missed target. Management guides to sequential Q4 adjusted EBITDA improvement but flagged fleet modernization costs as a headwind, and now expects positive adjusted EBITDA for full-year 2025 rather than Q4 2024. The fleet modernization plan (Phenom 300 and Challenger 300, $332 million BofA facility, $105 million GrandView acquisition) is the key change versus the prior period.

negative_highlights: Net sales declined 18.8% year-over-year due to a 13.7% decrease in volume mix and 4.9% pricing decline.
Free cash flow was negative $5.3 million, impacted by investments in new partner brands and working capital delays.
Industry headwinds persist with oversupply in cannabis and closures of large retailers.
positive_highlights: Adjusted gross profit margin expanded 130 bps to 24.3% due to higher-margin proprietary brand mix and productivity gains.
Six consecutive quarters of adjusted gross profit margins at or above 23%.
Adjusted EBITDA more than doubled compared to 2023, demonstrating profitability at lower sales levels.
summary: Hydrofarm reported Q3 FY2024 net sales of $44 million, a decline of 18.8% year-over-year driven by volume mix and pricing pressures. Adjusted gross profit margin expanded to 24.3%, marking the sixth consecutive quarter above 23%, while adjusted EBITDA turned slightly positive at $2.1 million. Management reaffirmed full-year 2024 guidance for net sales (low to high teens decline), adjusted EBITDA, and free cash flow.

negative_highlights: GAAP net loss widened slightly to $1.2 million ($0.10/share) from a prior year loss of $1.4 million due to nonrecurring litigation and business combination expenses related to the ADA Site Compliance acquisition.
Operating expenses on a GAAP basis increased 9% YoY, though this was partially driven by one-time items rather than core spend increases.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew sequentially from $8.47 million to $8.93 million, representing a 21% annualized growth rate and exceeding high-end guidance.
Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded significantly from 17% in Q2 to 23% in Q3 as non-GAAP operating expenses were reduced by 10%.
The company achieved its first-ever Rule of 40 status, with both Enterprise and Partner/Marketplace channels growing organically around 5% sequentially.
summary: AudioEye reported Q3 FY2024 revenue of $8.9 million (up 14% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of a record $2 million, beating both prior guidance and consensus estimates. Management raised full-year 2024 revenue guidance to $35.2M-$35.3M and increased Q4 adjusted EBITDA guidance by approximately $675k (to $2.2M-$2.3M) while maintaining the Rule of 40 milestone for the first time.

negative_highlights: Gross margin contracted from 50% in Q3 2023 to 46% due to a higher mix of system sales.
Net loss widened slightly to $1.5M ($0.13/share) compared to net income of $2.6M last year, though this is attributed to the absence of favorable warrant valuation swings seen previously.
Q4 OUS system placements are expected to be 'one or two systems shy' of Q3 levels as backlog clears.
positive_highlights: Revenue beat expectations with a 38% year-over-year increase to $13.5 million, fueled by international expansion.
Adjusted EBITDA swung positive at $429k compared to a negative $1.4M in the prior year quarter.
Trailing twelve-month recurring revenue grew 22% to $38 million as new systems ramp up.
summary: LENSAR reported Q3 FY2024 revenue of $13.5 million (up 38% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $429k (a turnaround from -$1.4M prior year), driven by the sale of 24 ALLY systems globally, including 11 outside the U.S. following regulatory clearances in Europe and Taiwan. Management expects Q4 OUS system sales to approximate the strong Q3 volume but notes difficulty beating that specific number due to backlog depletion; procedure volumes are expected to remain robust despite seasonal holidays and hurricane disruptions.

negative_highlights: Full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance lowered from $760M-$800M range to approximately $750M.
Non-political advertising spending slowed leading up to election day, impacting Q4 outlook and full year expectations.
Multiplatform Group revenues declined 1.1% YoY (2.9% ex-political) with adjusted EBITDA down significantly due to Olympic timing.
positive_highlights: Digital Audio Group revenue grew 12.7% YoY with podcasting EBITDA margins remaining accretive at 33.2%.
Audio & Media Services Group revenues surged 45.3% YoY, driven by digital growth and political advertising tailwinds.
Successfully entered a Transaction Support Agreement extending ~$4.1B of debt maturities to 2029-2031 while keeping annual cash interest expense flat.
summary: iHeartMedia reported Q3 FY2024 consolidated revenues of $1 billion (up 5.8% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $205 million, which was in-line with guidance but missed the top end due to a slowdown in non-political advertising near election day. Management lowered full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance from a range of $760M-$800M to approximately $750M and expects Q4 revenues to be up high single digits, excluding political which is expected to rise slightly but not match the prior cycle peak.

negative_highlights: Revenue fell $5.2 million year-over-year, driven by lower BLE transponder and mobile product sales
Non-GAAP gross margin contracted to 9.3% from 14% a year earlier on production underutilization in Southeast Asia
Non-GAAP adjusted EBITDA loss widened to $4.5 million from $2.3 million, and Q4 revenue guidance of $6.0–6.3 million implies a further sequential decline
positive_highlights: Q3 revenue of $6.5 million came in $0.4 million above the upper end of guidance
Cash and equivalents reached $145.7 million, up $121.4 million since December 31, 2023, following the Physical Security sale netting ~$135 million
Board approved a $10 million share repurchase program and proposed governance changes including eliminating the classified board
summary: Identiv reported Q3 FY2024 revenue of $6.5 million, $0.4 million above the upper end of guidance but down $5.2 million year-over-year, with GAAP gross margin of 3.6% and non-GAAP gross margin of 9.3% versus 11.2% and 14% in Q3 2023. GAAP net loss from continuing operations was $9.3 million or $0.40 per share, and non-GAAP adjusted EBITDA loss was $4.5 million. Q4 2024 IoT revenue guidance is $6.0–6.3 million, and management expects approximately 75% of production to transition to Thailand by year-end, targeting a 26%–28% non-GAAP gross margin once complete. The company completed the sale of its Physical Security business, ended with $145.7 million in cash, and announced a $10 million share repurchase program alongside a new Perform, Accelerate, Transform strategy.

negative_highlights: Surgical glaucoma revenue missed expectations with a sequential decline of 8% and lower-than-anticipated recovery from LCDs.
Dry eye pricing increase effective October 1 is expected to have a significant negative impact on cash pay procedure volumes in Q4, capping dry eye revenue below $0.5M for the quarter.
Final Medicare rule denied device-intensive status for CPT code 66174 as reported costs fell just under the 30% threshold.
positive_highlights: Adjusted operating expense guidance lowered to $104M-$106M from prior range, reflecting improved leverage and lower legal costs.
Dry eye revenue ($1.5M) was ahead of expectations despite a sequential decline due to fewer new accounts and the upcoming price increase.
Cash flow turned positive at $0.4 million in Q3 compared to cash burn of $10 million in the same period last year.
summary: Sight Sciences reported Q3 FY2024 revenue of $20.2 million (1% YoY growth), missing internal expectations due to slower-than-expected recovery in surgical glaucoma utilization following LCD finalization and a sequential decline driven by seasonality, partially offset by dry eye demand ahead of an October 1 price increase. Management maintained full-year 2024 revenue guidance but lowered adjusted operating expense guidance from $107M-$109M to $104M-$106M due to lower legal expenses and improved working capital management, while reiterating the expectation for double-digit surgical glaucoma growth in Q4. The company ended with $118.6 million in cash and generated positive operating cash flow of $0.4 million.

positive_highlights: Loan production grew 64% YoY to $476.8 million, driven by strong demand for new loans.
Net interest margin expanded 26 bps YoY to 3.6%, supported by a portfolio yield increase of 80 bps.
October securitization was six times oversubscribed on AAA bonds with a cost of funds of approximately 6%.
summary: Velocity Financial reported a record Q3 FY2024 with loan production of $476.8 million (up 13% QoQ) and net portfolio growth of $876 million. Net interest income increased 29% YoY, earnings grew 31%, and the weighted average coupon on new held-for-investment originations was 10.8%. Management highlighted a healthy pipeline with over 900 applications in October alone and raised the portfolio goal to exceed $5 billion UPB by 2025.

negative_highlights: Q3 net income of $0.07 per share was flat versus the prior-year quarter despite the 8% net income increase
CEO stated the 26.4% NOI CAGR is 'unsustainable' and that NOI growth rate should moderate going forward
DC multifamily faces supply pressure on vacancies and revenue growth; apartment occupancy 91.9% and retail occupancy 79.4%, with new Perryman delivery expected to weigh on Industrial NOI until leased
positive_highlights: Pro rata NOI up 39% to $11.3 million in Q3 and up 28% to $29 million year-to-date, driven by all six stabilized multifamily projects plus Mining and Industrial contributions
Mining NOI rose 79.9% to $5.1 million, including a one-time $1.9 million catch-up royalty payment covering 24 months of owed minimums
Year-to-date net income rose 94% to $4.7 million ($0.25/share) versus $2.4 million ($0.13/share) prior year; Industrial segment occupancy at 95.6%
summary: FRP reported Q3 net income up 8% to $1.4 million, or $0.07 per share, unchanged EPS versus the prior-year quarter; year-to-date net income rose 94% to $4.7 million ($0.25/share). Pro rata NOI rose 39% to $11.3 million in Q3 and 28% to $29 million year-to-date, but Q3 was boosted by a one-time $1.9 million minimum royalty back payment caught up from 24 months of prior shortfalls. CEO John Baker said the 26.4% three-year NOI CAGR is unsustainable and growth should moderate as the mix shifts toward stabilized assets, while the DC multifamily submarket faces vacancy pressure from new supply.

negative_highlights: Wavelo revenue down 9% YoY and EBITDA down 18.5% YoY
Ting workforce cut by over 40% and no common equity partner found
Cash flow from operations was negative $4.6M in Q3
positive_highlights: Consolidated adjusted EBITDA up 94% to $8.7M in Q3
Ting adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed to $5.1M from $12.2M YoY
Domains gross margin up 8% YoY, value-added services margin up 26%
summary: Consolidated Q3 revenue grew 6.1% YoY to $92.3M, gross profit up 32.4% to $22.2M, and adjusted EBITDA nearly doubled to $8.7M from $4.5M, driven by Domains and Ting improvements. Domains revenue rose 5.9% to $64.7M with EBITDA up 5.6% to $11.5M, while Wavelo revenue declined 9% to $10.1M and EBITDA fell 18.5% to $3.4M. Ting revenue grew 19% to $15.3M, EBITDA loss narrowed to $5.1M from $12.2M, and net additions were 1,400. Management reduced Ting workforce by 40% to cut ~$22M in cash costs, stopped expansion, and expects Ting to be near adjusted EBITDA breakeven in 2025. Consolidated adjusted EBITDA year-to-date exceeded $22M, on track to approximately double from 2023's $15.5M.

negative_highlights: Total revenue fell ~13% YoY to $28.9 million, with airtime and service revenue down $5 million to $24.4 million
Full-year revenue guidance narrowed to $114-117 million and adjusted EBITDA to $8.5-11.5 million, citing Coast Guard reductions and ARPU pressure
Management expects airtime margins to compress slightly over time from new custom Starlink data plans; Q3 gross profit was negative $0.2 million
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA rose to $2.9 million from $2.6 million in Q2, with adjusted EBITDA less CapEx of $1.4 million versus zero in Q2
Airtime gross margin improved sequentially to 36.5% from 36.0% on strong LEO/Starlink data margins
Record antenna shipments for a third consecutive quarter and subscribing vessels up ~2% QoQ to just below 6,800
summary: KVH reported Q3 revenue of $28.9 million, down roughly 13% year over year, with airtime and service revenue of $24.4 million, down $5 million, attributed to continued VSAT product and service decline; results were in line with prior expectations. Adjusted EBITDA was $2.9 million versus $2.6 million in Q2, airtime gross margin rose to 36.5% from 36.0%, and total subscribing vessels grew about 2% sequentially to just below 6,800. Full-year 2024 guidance was narrowed to $114-117 million revenue and $8.5-11.5 million adjusted EBITDA, driven by U.S. Coast Guard contractual reductions and ARPU pressure. Management flagged an anticipated slight airtime margin compression over time from new custom Starlink plans and noted the October 19 Intelsat IS-33e satellite anomaly, with service largely restored.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to $13 million from $6.6 million year-over-year due to increased clinical and development expenses.
R&D expenses surged to $10.2 million, primarily driven by the PALISADE Phase 3 program costs.
G&A expenses increased to $4.2 million due to headcount growth and professional services fees.
positive_highlights: PALISADE-3 and PALISADE-4 Phase 3 trials initiated on time with no site overlap, addressing previous variability concerns.
Significant excitement and engagement from Principal Investigators (PIs) across the research community for the new intranasal therapies.
Enhanced surveillance capabilities through in-person investigator meetings and site initiation visits reducing attrition rates.
summary: Vistagen Therapeutics reported a net loss of $13 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2024, compared to a loss of $6.6 million in the prior year period, driven by R&D expenses rising to $10.2 million and G&A expenses increasing to $4.2 million. The company confirmed it is on track with its guidance for initiating PALISADE-3 and PALISADE-4 Phase 3 trials for fasedienol in mid-2024, aiming for NDA submission in early 2026 if successful. Management also outlined plans to submit an IND for the PH80 hot flash program in the second quarter of 2025.

negative_highlights: Q4 revenue guidance of $60-61 million implies a 7-9% year-over-year decline and a sequential drop from $62.7 million
Preliminary 2025 outlook calls for revenue below 2024 and adjusted EBITDA margin contraction of at least a few hundred basis points
NDR for calendar 2024 is expected at 85-87%, with churn still elevated and CRPO down 4% year-over-year, driving 2025 revenue pressure
positive_highlights: Q3 revenue, adjusted EBITDA, and EPS all exceeded the high end of guided ranges
Unlevered free cash flow was $85.2 million on a trailing 12-month basis, up 58% year-over-year, and represented 105% of TTM adjusted EBITDA
Board authorized a $100 million expansion of the share buyback program, expected to be completed by end of 2025
summary: Definitive Healthcare reported Q3 FY2024 revenue of $62.7 million, down 4% year-over-year, but above the high end of guidance; adjusted EBITDA was $20.6 million (33% margin) and non-GAAP EPS was $0.10, also above guidance. Q4 guidance calls for revenue of $60-61 million (down 7-9% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $16-17 million (26-28% margin), with full-year NDR of 85-87%. Management said 2025 revenue will be less than 2024 and adjusted EBITDA margin will contract by at least a few hundred basis points, with a return to sequential revenue growth targeted for the second half of 2025. The company authorized a $100 million buyback expansion and announced CFO Rick Booth will leave by June 2025.

negative_highlights: Net loss for the quarter was approximately $837,000, though this improved significantly from the prior year's adjusted loss.
Commission expense rose 13% due to higher first-year commissions.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 5% YoY to $3.4 million driven by organic growth.
Total operating expenses decreased 16% to $3.9 million due to the OneFirm strategy.
Adjusted EBITDA turned positive at approximately $42,000, a 121% improvement over the prior year.
summary: Revenue grew 5% to $3.4 million while total operating expenses declined 16% to $3.9 million, significantly improving the loss from operations by 64%. The company reported a positive adjusted EBITDA of approximately $42,000, marking a turnaround from prior losses and a 121% increase year-over-year. Management expressed strong confidence in the pending acquisition of Spetner Associates, which is expected to double consolidated revenues upon closing.

negative_highlights: GAAP net loss widened to $27.2 million ($0.33 per share) from $4.9 million ($0.06 per share), including a $20.2 million non-cash derivative charge
Adjusted net loss was $6.5 million ($0.08 per share), worse than the $4.7 million ($0.06 per share) adjusted loss a year ago
Nine-month brokerage segment operating loss widened to $31.9 million from $20.3 million, including a $17.75 million litigation settlement charge
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed to $1.4 million from $3.0 million in the prior-year quarter
Real estate brokerage segment reported operating income of $454,000 versus an operating loss of $2 million in Q3 2023
Listing volume increased 6% and average price per transaction rose to $1.6 million from $1.57 million
summary: Douglas Elliman reported Q3 FY2024 revenue of $266.3 million, up from $251.5 million a year ago, alongside a net loss attributable to the company of $27.2 million, or $0.33 per diluted share, versus a $4.9 million loss in the prior-year period; the loss included a $20.2 million non-cash charge from the change in fair value of the embedded derivative in the convertible debt. Adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed to $1.4 million from a $3.0 million loss, and the brokerage segment swung to operating income of $454,000 from a $2.0 million loss. Average price per transaction rose to $1.6 million from $1.57 million, listing volume increased 6%, and the development marketing pipeline stands at approximately $26.8 billion, with another $4.7 billion expected to come to market through 2025. No formal forward guidance was provided, and the new CEO emphasized diversification, an M&A unit, and ROI discipline.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to $9.4 million in Q3 from $5.6 million
Operating expenses up 42% YoY to $10.8 million
Transition from recurring-only to capital sales adds near-term revenue uncertainty
positive_highlights: Q3 revenue up 64% YoY to $2.83 million
CMS reimbursement set at $12,992 hospital / $10,728 ASC, higher than robotic prostatectomy
CAPTAIN trial recruiting faster, adding Cleveland Clinic, readout in H1 2025
summary: Profound Medical reported Q3 2024 revenue of $2.83 million, up 64% YoY, with recurring revenue of $2.65 million and $179k capital equipment. Net loss widened to $9.4 million ($0.38/share) from $5.6 million, with cash at $27.1 million. CMS final rule set TULSA reimbursement at urology APC Level 7, with average facility payment of $12,992 in hospitals and $10,728 in ASCs, both above other prostate procedures. Management reaffirmed FY2024 revenue guidance of $11-12 million and highlighted increasing CAPTAIN trial recruitment including Cleveland Clinic, with data expected by AUA 2025.

negative_highlights: Net loss remained substantial at $13.4 million, and cash burn was $11.5 million in the quarter.

Guidance for key catalysts is vague: no specific FDA decision date for the cardiac surgery PMA supplement, CE Mark timing depends on EU regulators, and revenue growth is expected to be chunky and unpredictable quarter to quarter.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew to $0.8 million from $0.2 million in the prior-year quarter, and management noted a run rate closer to $875,000 with further hospital starts after October 1.
Hospital clients increased by over 60% quarter-over-quarter, which management said reflects new marketing and customer education initiatives.
Cash runway extended to about 18 months following a $20.6 million equity raise, extinguishment of the Avenue Capital loan for $17.85 million, and an $11.5 million royalty funding agreement.
summary: Beyond Air reported Q2 FY2025 revenue of $0.8 million versus $0.2 million a year earlier, a four-fold increase, but gross margin was negative $1.1 million as cost of revenue exceeded sales due to $0.7 million of device upgrade costs and $0.8 million of non-cash charges. Net loss narrowed to $13.4 million ($0.28 per share) from $16.2 million ($0.51 per share), and cash burn was $11.5 million, which management expects to cut by at least one-third in Q3. Guidance is qualitative: hospital clients rose over 60% quarter-over-quarter, gross margins are expected to turn positive in the March 2025 quarter, and international shipments should begin in the first half of calendar 2025. The company raised $20.6 million in equity, extinguished a $17.85 million Avenue Capital loan, and secured an $11.5 million royalty funding agreement to extend cash runway to about 18 months.

negative_highlights: Total revenue declined 2% year-over-year
Heart failure and critical care categories down 36% and 25% respectively
Operating loss still at $1.5 million in Q3
positive_highlights: CMS reimbursement to increase 297% to $1,639 per day effective Jan 1, 2025
Gross margin improved to 70% from 57.3% year-over-year
Pediatric revenue up 28% with three new pediatric accounts
summary: Nuwellis reported Q3 2024 revenue of $2.4 million, down 2% year-over-year but up 8% sequentially, with a 28% surge in pediatric category. Gross margin improved to 70% from 57.3%, while operating loss narrowed to $1.5 million from $3.2 million, though net income was driven by a $3.9 million warrant revaluation benefit. The company highlighted a significant CMS reimbursement increase effective January 1, 2025, raising the facility fee from $413 to $1,639 per day (297% increase), which management expects to accelerate growth. Cash balance was $1.9 million at quarter end, with additional $5.1 million raised from warrant exercises after quarter end.

negative_highlights: Cash on hand only $9.4 million, sufficient into Q1 2025, implying near-term funding need
High per-patient costs in US and reliance on lower-cost regions could affect timelines
No formal guidance; financial runway limited
positive_highlights: Phase 2 CR rate of 50% in second-line AML patients, more than double existing therapies
Median durability of responses now 8 months and still climbing; 78% MRD-negative
FDA-specified adaptive design and early unblinding reduce approval risk
summary: Moleculin reported Q3 2024 with $9.4 million cash on hand, sufficient to fund operations into Q1 2025. The company highlighted its Phase 2 data for Annamycin in AML, including 50% complete remission in second-line patients, median durability of 8 months, and 78% MRD-negative responses. The Phase 3 MIRACLE trial is underway with adaptive design, and management emphasized de-risking via early unblinding and the possibility of accelerated approval if interim results are strong. Financial guidance was not provided; cash runway is short.

negative_highlights: Net revenue fell 34% year-over-year to $26.2 million, with a 27% decline expected in Q4 (or 4% adjusted for SKU rationalization).
Dehumidifier sales missed expectations due to stockouts and weather, and kitchen appliance products showed softness.
Q4 adjusted EBITDA is guided to approximately breakeven, with revenue guidance implying a significant year-over-year decline that will pressure overall profitability.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA turned positive at $0.5 million, a 111% improvement from a loss of $4.4 million in Q3 2023, marking the second consecutive profitable quarter.
Gross margin expanded 1,090 basis points to 60.3% from 49.4% year-over-year, driven by SKU rationalization and lower liquidation of high-cost inventory.
Contribution margin improved to 17% from 3% in the prior-year quarter, and operating loss narrowed 73.4% to $1.7 million.
summary: Net revenue declined 34% year-over-year to $26.2 million in Q3 2024, with adjusted EBITDA of $0.5 million representing the second consecutive quarter of profitability and a 111% improvement from the prior-year loss of $4.4 million. Despite the revenue decline, gross margin expanded to 60.3% from 49.4%, contribution margin improved to 17% from 3%, and operating and net losses narrowed significantly. Q4 guidance of $22.5–$25.5 million implies a 27% year-over-year decline (or 4% adjusted for SKU rationalization), with adjusted EBITDA expected to be approximately breakeven; management reiterated its goal of adjusted EBITDA profitability for the overall second half of 2024. The quarter was characterized by a substantial revenue decline due to SKU rationalization and dehumidifier stockouts, but was offset by margin expansion and cost-reduction benefits, resulting in a mixed performance.

negative_highlights: Q3 net income of $6.9 million came in marginally below Q2, with revenue essentially flat due to straight-line rent accounting
2025 guidance assumes no new 2025 deals and depends on closing ~$110 million of Q4 acquisitions that have not yet closed
ATM share sales acknowledged by management as a near-term EPS drag ('it's going to be a drag on earnings by definition') until proceeds are deployed
positive_highlights: Dividend raised $0.01 to $0.14 per share, the fourth increase in nine quarters of paying
100% of contractual rents collected; YTD net income up 37.8% to $19.9 million

Pipeline of roughly $110 million of acquisitions expected to close in Q4 (including an $87.5 million Missouri portfolio and ~$24 million Kansas deal), underpinning 2025 revenue guidance of ~$125 million and FFO of ~$75 million
summary: Strawberry Fields reported Q3 2024 net income of $6.9 million, marginally below the prior quarter, with revenue and expenses 'mostly in line' with Q2 due to straight-line rent treatment; YTD net income of $19.9 million was up 37.8% YoY. Total assets rose 4% QoQ to $661.5 million on five acquired properties and the August Series A bond raise. Management guided to roughly $125 million of revenue and $75 million of FFO for 2025 assuming no new deals, contingent on closing about $110 million of acquisitions in Q4, and raised the quarterly dividend $0.01 to $0.14 (ninth consecutive quarter, fourth increase). The company collected 100% of contractual rents and cited a 47% payout ratio and ~50% leverage.

negative_highlights: Cost of revenues increased to $23 million due to higher utilization, inflationary pressures on parts and travel, and expenses related to Spanish scooper return-to-service work.
Management noted they have not fully realized benefits from targeted cost structure reductions estimated a year ago.
Inflationary pressures in salaries, wages, benefits, travel, and small parts replacement impacted margins.
positive_highlights: Revenue increased approximately 20% YoY to $64.5 million driven by higher flight hours and record wildfire activity.
Net income surged to $27.3 million ($0.31 diluted EPS) compared to $17.5 million in the prior year quarter.
Management raised full-year 2024 revenue guidance significantly to a range of $90-95 million, exceeding the initial guidance of $70-86 million.
summary: Bridger Aerospace reported Q3 FY2024 revenue of $64.5 million (up ~20% YoY) and net income of $27.3 million ($0.31 diluted EPS), driven by record wildfire activity including 8 million acres burned nationally. Management raised full-year 2024 revenue guidance to a range of $90-95 million (from an initial $70-86 million) and adjusted EBITDA guidance to $35-40 million, citing strong Q3 results and continued dry weather extending the season into November. The company expects positive free cash flow for the first time in its history.

negative_highlights: Brick-and-mortar retail sales were only about 2% of total sales, indicating early-stage adoption in this channel.
positive_highlights: Gross margins expanded to a record 65%, up from 49% in Q3 2023.
Adjusted EBITDA reached its best quarterly performance in company history with a 21% improvement YoY.
Operating expenses decreased 12% year over year due to revenue growth and efficiency.
summary: SenesTech reported record Q3 FY2024 revenue of $1.4 million for the nine-month period (vs $898k YoY), driven by Evolve Rat (52% of revenue) and Evolve Mouse (17% of revenue). Gross margins expanded significantly to a record 65%, up from 49% year-over-year, while operating expenses decreased 12% YoY. Management raised guidance for profitability, projecting cash flow breakeven next year following the lowest EBITDA loss in company history.

negative_highlights: Q3 adjusted EBITDA loss of $4.4 million and cash and cash equivalents of only $5.7 million, of which $1 million was restricted
Cash flow positivity milestone pushed from 2024 to 2025, with full company cash flow positivity now targeted for the latter half of 2025
Workforce reduced by over 35% as part of a strategic reorganization, indicating significant cost pressures
positive_highlights: Net revenue grew 222% year-over-year to $6.5 million, with EveryLife up 126% year-over-year to $2.6 million
Gross margin expanded from 27% to 64% year-over-year due to high-margin credit products
Signed contracts for over $1 billion in annualized GMV on PublicSquare Payments, ahead of the Christmas shopping season goal, and activated first $100 million-plus merchant
summary: PublicSquare reported Q3 2024 net revenue of $6.5 million, up 222% year-over-year, with $3.2 million from Fintech (watch now, pay later only) and $2.6 million from EveryLife, up 126%. Overall gross margin expanded from 27% to 64% year-over-year, driven by high-margin credit products. The company did not provide formal revenue or EPS guidance, but said it expects over $1 billion in contracted annualized GMV to be integrated between Q4 2024 and Q1 2025, realizing full revenue impact in early Q2 2025 at a blended take rate of 1.9%-2.3%, and reaffirmed its expectation to reach positive cash flow in the latter half of 2025 following a 35% workforce reduction expected to save $11 million annually. Notably, cash flow positivity was pushed out from 2024 to 2025 due to the Credova acquisition and Fintech investment, and the quarter included a $4.4 million adjusted EBITDA loss and $5.7 million in cash and equivalents.

Management reiterated Q4 guidance of $43-$47 million revenue (midpoint +25% YoY) and $3-$4 million adjusted EBITDA from continuing operations only.

summary: RumbleOn reported Q3 FY2024 revenue of $295 million, down 12.7% year-over-year, and adjusted EBITDA of $6.8 million, down 26.1%, with Powersports dealership revenue down 13.6% on a 13.2% decline in major unit volumes. $142 million non-cash income tax expense associated with the C-Corp conversion impacted net loss

Management reiterated full-year 2024 revenue guidance of $190-$195 million but declined to provide specific EBITDA guidance for FY2024 or FY2025, noting that visibility will improve upon year-end results.

summary: James River reported a Q3 FY2024 net loss from continuing operations of $1.07 per share and an adjusted net operating loss of $0.74 per share, driven by a $76.3 million E&S reserve charge tied to its detailed valuation review and the State National reinsurance transaction. The E&S segment combined ratio was 136.1% versus a 92.6% current accident year ratio, while Specialty Admitted produced a 91.3% combined ratio. The company announced a $12.5 million Enstar equity investment, conversion of $37.5 million of Gallatin Point preferred to common, a new $75 million adverse development cover with Enstar, a cut to the quarterly common dividend to $0.01 per share, and the conclusion of its strategic review process. No explicit forward guidance was provided beyond commentary on loss trends and expense ratio expectations.

negative_highlights: Sales of GLA oil continued to decline as the company note through remaining inventory.

Management declined to provide forward guidance due to the timing of new distribution shipments but expressed optimism for full-year retail distribution growth exceeding 80%.

Management reiterated full-year 2024 guidance for revenues between $200M-$205M and plans to open 10-11 new restaurants, maintaining an adjusted EBITDA margin target of approximately 18%. While same-store sales declined 9.6% YoY due to weather events (hurricanes) and extreme heat, management noted significant improvement in October/November comps.

Gross margin fell to 35% from 37%, and a $2.3 million goodwill and intangible impairment drove a net loss of $2.4 million, or $0.23 per diluted share; adjusted EBITDA was flat at $0.2 million. Management said full-year 2024 revenue will be slightly below 2023 and gross margin will still exceed 2023, but Q4 gross margin will be below Q3, and 2025 gross margin is expected to be roughly flat. The company plans to exit the code portion of the Authentication segment, ending the Amazon Transparency relationship by the end of 2024 and redirecting investment toward ink and Precision Logistics.

Full-year 2024 revenue will fall well note weakness in of the $200 million potential cited a year ago; 2025 guidance was not provided, and the DHS protest remains unresolved

TSA PreCheck enrollment footprint more than doubled from 83 to 173 locations in three months, on track for 500 in 2025
summary: Telos reported Q3 FY2024 revenue of $23.8 million, near the top end of the $22–$24 million guidance range, and an adjusted EBITDA loss of $4.1 million, better than the guided $8 million to $6.5 million loss. GAAP gross margin was 13.2%, depressed by a $13.1 million noncash impairment and restructuring charge, while cash gross margin expanded 250 basis points year-over-year to 44%, the highest since the 2020 IPO. Q4 revenue guidance of $24.5–$26.5 million implies 3–11% sequential growth driven by Security Solutions, with an adjusted EBITDA loss of $4.5–$3.5 million; Secure Networks revenue is expected to decline sequentially. The key change was resolution of the DMDC protest in Telos's favor, with the program now generating revenue, and continued rapid expansion of TSA PreCheck enrollment locations from 83 to 173, though Secure Networks backlog continues to decline and the DHS protest remains unresolved.

Management framed the quarter's larger operating-loss figure as including roughly $10.6 million of non-cash items plus $2.7 million of onboarding costs and $1.3 million of relocation costs; they said the effective 'guidance increase' to $79-84 million operating income reflects folding in $17 million of non-cash items rather than a true raise. Cash from operations was $22.9 million and net bank debt fell to $114.3 million from $136.3 million at June 30.
