summary: Q3 2024 revenue rose 40% year-over-year to $667,000 from $477,000, with unit sales up roughly 50% and gross margin down 50 bps to 85.4%. Operating loss narrowed to $1.7 million from $3 million, and net loss improved to $1.8 million versus $8.6 million, with cash of only $261,000 at quarter-end supplemented by a $5 million life sciences fund investment expected to close mid-November. Management cited a new category one CPT code effective January 1, 2026, an FDA age expansion to 8-21 years, and covered lives growing to about 35 million from 4 million, and it expects Q4 revenue growth and continued acceleration into 2025 toward cash flow breakeven, with RED commercialization expected in late 2024 or early 2025. The key change versus prior periods is the swing from year-over-year revenue declines of 20% in Q1 and 5% in Q2 to 40% growth in Q3.

negative_highlights: Cash position low at $5.7 million, including restricted cash.
Stock-based compensation expense of $5.8 million in Q3.
Workforce reduction of over 35% indicates cost pressures.
positive_highlights: Net revenue increased 222% to $6.5 million in Q3.
Signed contracts with potential for over $1 billion in annualized GMV ahead of schedule.
EveryLife revenue grew 126% year-over-year in Q3.
summary: PublicSquare reported Q3 FY2024 net revenue of $6.5 million, up 222% year-over-year, with Fintech contributing $3.2 million from watch now, pay later only, as payments revenue starts in Q4. Gross margin expanded to 64% from 27%, driven by high-margin credit products. Management signed contracts potentially exceeding $1 billion in annualized GMV for its payments platform, ahead of schedule, and activated its first enterprise merchant expected to process over $100 million annually. The company reduced workforce by over 35% to save an estimated $11 million annually, aiming for segment and overall cash flow positivity in 2025.

negative_highlights: Beef verification business faces persistent headwinds expected to continue until herd cycles improve.
Gross profit declined slightly to $2.8 million, leading to an 18% drop in operating income year-to-date.
SG&A expenses increased 13% year-over-year due to higher marketing, personnel, and travel costs.
positive_highlights: Product revenue rose 9% to $1.3 million, compensating for declines in other segments.
Cash from operations increased 6% year-over-year to $2.8 million over the first nine months.
summary: Total revenue increased slightly to $7.1 million in Q3 FY2024, driven by a 9% rise in product revenue but offset by declines in professional services and persistent headwinds in the beef verification business. Net income fell 32% to $0.5 million ($0.09 per share) due to higher SG&A costs of $2.2 million and lower gross profit. Management reiterated that beef-related revenue slowdowns will persist until herd downsizing cycles back up and drought conditions subside, though they view the shift to electronic RFID tags as a long-term growth opportunity.

negative_highlights: Q3 revenue declined 13% year-over-year, subscribers fell 13% to 3.8 million, and October non-subscriber traffic dropped 37% year-over-year
Company no longer expects to meet 2025 goals of 30% adjusted EBITDA margin and $100 million free cash flow
Additional restructuring cuts 21% of headcount (319 employees), with $22-$26 million in charges expected, mostly in Q4
positive_highlights: Q3 revenue of $137 million and adjusted EBITDA of $22 million exceeded prior guidance
Questions asked increased 79% year-over-year, and monthly retention for Chegg Study and Study Pack rose 30 basis points year-over-year
Board authorized a $300 million increase to the securities repurchase program; free cash flow was $24 million in Q3
summary: Chegg reported Q3 FY2024 revenue of $137 million, down 13% year-over-year, with subscription services revenue of $120 million (down 14%) and adjusted EBITDA of $22 million (16% margin). The company exceeded its Q3 guidance on revenue and adjusted EBITDA, but non-subscriber traffic declined sharply: down 8% in Q2, 19% in Q3, and 37% year-over-year in October. Management no longer expects to meet its 2025 goals of 30% adjusted EBITDA margin and $100 million free cash flow, citing Google's AI Overviews and student adoption of generative AI. Chegg announced an additional 21% workforce reduction, expecting $60-$70 million in 2025 savings, and guided Q4 revenue to $141-$143 million with adjusted EBITDA of $32-$34 million. A $300 million increase to the securities repurchase program was also authorized.

negative_highlights: Gross margin contracted to 58.4% from 61.3%, driven by reduced throughput from the delayed internally produced stem cell launch
Adjusted EBITDA fell to a $193,000 loss from $458,000 positive in Q3 2023
Net loss of $5 million, or $0.04 per share, versus net income of $9.2 million (which included a $13.3 million bargain purchase gain) a year earlier
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 12% YoY to $27.9 million, and year-to-date revenue is up 36%
Full-year revenue guidance of $116-$120 million was reaffirmed, implying ~27-31% annual growth
Signed a wound-care licensing deal in October with a $1.5 million upfront payment and minimum $3.75 million in 2025 licensing/royalty revenue at little incremental cost
summary: Q3 2024 revenue rose 12% YoY to $27.9 million, but gross margin fell to 58.4% from 61.3% and adjusted EBITDA swung to a $193,000 loss from $458,000 positive a year ago. Management reaffirmed full-year revenue guidance of $116-$120 million and expects to be adjusted EBITDA positive in Q4 2024. The quarter was held back by delayed launches of OsteoVive Plus (validation delays) and the Cortera pedicle screw system (supplier issues), both released in late September, plus a summer procedure slowdown, while October brought a wound-care licensing deal with a $1.5 million upfront payment and minimum $3.75 million in 2025 licensing/royalty revenue.

negative_highlights: IP revenue fell to $0.5 million from $5.8 million in Q2, driving consolidated revenue down sequentially from $25.8 million to $23.3 million
GAAP net loss of $14 million ($0.14 per share) versus $1.6 million net income a year ago, including $4.1 million of unrealized equity losses
Book value per share declined to $5.85 from $5.95 at June 30, and industrials revenue fell to $7 million from $8.3 million YoY on lower printer sales
positive_highlights: Deflecto acquired for $103.7 million, expected to add $128-136 million revenue and $17.5-19.5 million EBITDA for 2024
Energy segment revenue rose 12% QoQ to $15.8 million with adjusted EBITDA of $8.4 million
Repurchased approximately 3 million shares for about $14 million at an average price of $4.65 under the $20 million program
summary: Acacia reported Q3 revenue of $23.3 million, up 131% YoY on the Benchmark acquisition but down from $25.8 million in Q2 due to a drop in lumpy IP revenue to $0.5 million from $5.8 million. Adjusted EBITDA was $1.7 million, with operated segment adjusted EBITDA of $6.9 million and include-IP-excluded operated EBITDA of $9 million; GAAP net loss attributable to Acacia was $14 million or $0.14 per share, and book value per share slipped to $5.85 from $5.95 at June 30. The quarter's main event was the $103.7 million Deflecto acquisition ($48 million debt, $55.7 million equity), guided to $128-136 million 2024 revenue and $17.5-19.5 million EBITDA, leaving roughly $280 million of cash. No formal EPS or EBITDA guidance was given for the core business, and IP revenue variability drove the sequential decline.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA missed significantly due to approximately $35 million in retroactive adjustments and negative prior period development of about $10 million.
Management expects a revenue decrement in 2025 as they rationalize the payer network, impacting roughly 20,000 members.
positive_highlights: Top line revenue grew 26% year-over-year to $362.1 million driven by a 22% member base expansion exceeding 128,900 members.
summary: P3 Health Partners reported Q3 FY2024 revenue of $362.1 million (up 26% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA loss of $71 million ($184 PMPM), driven by approximately $35 million in retroactive adjustments, elevated medical utilization of $5-10 million, and negative prior period development. Management provided no formal guidance for the quarter but indicated a recalibrated step-off point closer to an annualized quarterly loss run rate of ~$30 million versus Q3's reported impact, while noting expected revenue decrements in 2025 due to network rationalization affecting roughly 20,000 members. The company outlined $130+ million in improvement initiatives targeting profitability starting in late 2024 and accelerating in 2025.

negative_highlights: Gross margin declined 60 bps year over year to 14.3% from 14.9% on a mix shift away from conversion cars
CFO guided gross margin to decrease sequentially from Q3 to Q4 due to changeover timing and mix, with full-year margin only materially in line with 2023
A $110 million non-cash charge for warrant liability was recognized due to share price appreciation during the quarter
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 83% year over year to $113.3 million on 961 railcar deliveries versus 503 in the prior-year quarter
Adjusted EBITDA rose to $10.9 million from $3.5 million, and the full-year adjusted EBITDA midpoint was raised to $38 million (89% year-over-year increase at the midpoint)
Second consecutive quarter of positive operating cash flow at $7.2 million, with $44.8 million cash and no outstanding revolver borrowings
summary: FreightCar America reported Q3 2024 revenue of $113.3 million, up 83% year over year from $61.9 million, on 961 railcar deliveries versus 503 a year earlier. Gross margin was 14.3%, down 60 bps from 14.9% a year ago on mix but up 180 bps sequentially, and adjusted EBITDA rose to $10.9 million from $3.5 million; the company reaffirmed full-year revenue and delivery guidance (4,300-4,500 cars) and raised the midpoint of its adjusted EBITDA range to $37-39 million, an 89% year-over-year increase at the midpoint. Operating cash flow was $7.2 million, a second consecutive positive quarter, with $44.8 million cash and no revolver borrowings, and backlog stood at 3,611 railcars valued at roughly $372 million. Management flagged a slower industry quarter but noted share gains of 3% sequentially on a trailing 12-month basis against a roughly 20% industry order decline.

negative_highlights: Full-year 2024 revenue guidance was narrowed down from prior expectations.
Q3 results lacked anticipated year-end seasonality, leading to a lower annual forecast.
Net loss of $10.3 million ($0.14/share) remains significant despite margin improvements.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 56% year-over-year driven by sales of Swoop portable imaging systems.
Gross margin expanded over 270 basis points sequentially to a record 52%.
FDA clearance received for ninth-generation AI-powered software reducing acquisition times.
summary: Hyperfine reported Q3 FY2024 revenue of $3.6 million, representing a 56% year-over-year increase and sequential gross margin expansion of over 270 basis points to a record 52%. The company narrowed its full-year 2024 revenue guidance to a range of $14 million to $14.5 million (midpoint ~30% YoY growth) and updated the full-year gross margin outlook to 47%-50%, citing reduced seasonality in Q3 as a reason for the lower annual forecast.

negative_highlights: Net loss of $29.8 million and operating loss of $32.3 million in the quarter, with R&D up to $27.2 million on ALTITUDE-AD spending
Net cash burn of approximately $23 million in the quarter with no product revenue
Management declined to specify next steps for subcutaneous sabirnetug or confirm whether Phase II plus Phase I data would suffice for a subcutaneous pivotal study, pending Phase I PK data
positive_highlights: Cash and marketable securities of approximately $259 million with runway into the first half of 2027
ALTITUDE-AD enrollment progressed faster than expected, with enrollment completion now anticipated in the first half of 2025
pTau 217 enrichment screening cut the incidence of negative amyloid PET scans by about 50% versus the Phase I study
summary: Acumen reported Q3 2024 R&D expenses of $27.2 million and G&A of $5 million, driving an operating loss of $32.3 million and a net loss of $29.8 million, with net cash burn of roughly $23 million. Cash and marketable securities stood at approximately $259 million, with runway expected into the first half of 2027. Management said ALTITUDE-AD enrollment has progressed faster than expected and now anticipates completing enrollment in the first half of 2025, while subcutaneous Phase I top-line PK results are expected in Q1 2025. As a clinical-stage company with no product revenue, results are measured against trial timelines and spend rather than a financial beat or miss.

negative_highlights: GBM trial enrollment slower than expected; Latvian sites several months behind schedule
Second-line cholangiocarcinoma cohort recruiting slower due to rapid disease progression in eligible patients
Management expressed frustration with share price and negative enterprise value
positive_highlights: BOLSTER first-line cholangiocarcinoma enrollment completed 6 months ahead of schedule, accelerating top-line readout to mid-2025
ASCEND Cohort A preliminary analysis accepted for presentation at ASCO GI January 2025
Cash runway extended into early 2026 with reduced operating expenses
summary: Lisata reported Q3 2024 net loss of $4.9 million, improved from $5.3 million a year ago, with R&D expenses down 24.8% to $2.5 million. Cash stood at $35.9 million, sufficient into early 2026. Key upcoming data includes ASCEND Cohort A preliminary results at ASCO GI in January 2025, BOLSTER first-line top-line mid-2025, and iLSTA preliminary results at ASCO GI. GBM trial enrollment is slower than expected, with Estonian site at 5 patients and Latvian sites not yet initiated.

negative_highlights: Company still reports an operating loss of approximately $3.3 million despite cost reductions.
Total operating expenses remained high at $4.850 million, though down from the prior year.
Revenue growth is modest (7% YoY) relative to a company transitioning into profitability.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew to $1.89M with a net retention rate exceeding 106%.
Cash-based losses narrowed by 43%, dropping from $2.36 million in Q3 2023 to $1.324 million.
Successfully launched the first end-to-end AI pilot platform for a leading financial services customer.
summary: CXAI reported Q3 FY2024 revenue of $1.89 million (up from $1.76M prior quarter) and recurring revenue increased to 88% with a net retention rate above 106%. While the company highlighted its best financial quarter ever, it remains in an expansion phase as cash-based losses narrowed significantly but were not eliminated ($1.324 million loss). Management emphasized strategic milestones like AWS Marketplace listing and AI product launches rather than profitability.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to approximately $16.7 million in the first nine months of FY24 compared to $18.4 million in the prior year period.
Revenue remains minimal at only $3.1 million for the 9-month period with no comparable revenues reported during the same periods in 2023.
positive_highlights: Announced a major BARDA Project NextGen award valued at almost $400 million for GEO-CM04S1, validating MVA technology and supporting a comparative trial against an mRNA vaccine.
summary: GeoVax reported $2.8 million in Q3 revenue and a net loss of approximately $16.7 million for the first nine months of FY24, driven by manufacturing costs associated with its BARDA Project NextGen award which began mid-June. Management highlighted significant clinical progress including the initiation of an expanded Phase 2 trial for Gedeptin in head and neck cancer and cGMP production milestones for their Mpox vaccine candidate GEO-MVA. While no financial guidance was provided, management indicated that revenue from the BARDA contract is expected to be approximately $3 million per quarter as it runs through its current phase.

negative_highlights: Consumer Payments gross profit growth decelerated to 2% from 6% YTD, with management citing ~2-3 points of consumer spending softness, RCS client loss, and enterprise implementation delays
Full-year revenue, gross profit, and adjusted EBITDA guidance was left unchanged, with no framework for FY2025 given ahead of the Q4 call
Reported free cash flow conversion benefited from ~$20 million of net working capital timing, of which ~$15 million is expected to reverse in Q4
positive_highlights: Business Payments gross profit grew 67% YoY, aided by political media spending and new enterprise wins like University of Florida Health Systems
Q3 free cash flow of $48.8 million and conversion of 139%, with the full-year reported conversion outlook raised from 60% to 65%
Instant Funding transaction volume up ~24% YoY; balance sheet at $419 million total liquidity with net leverage of ~2.5x
summary: Q3 revenue was $79.1 million, up 6% YoY, with gross profit up 9% to a 44% adjusted EBITDA margin and adjusted net income of $21.2 million ($0.23/share). Consumer Payments gross profit grew only 2% (vs 6% YTD) on consumer spending softness, RCS client loss, and enterprise implementation delays, while Business Payments grew 67% on core AP, political media, and new client ramps. Full-year guidance was reiterated (revenue $314-320M, gross profit $245-250M, adjusted EBITDA $139-142M), with only reported free cash flow conversion raised from 60% to 65% due to ~$20M net working capital timing benefits. Management cited mid-to-high single-digit Consumer organic growth and declined to provide FY2025 specifics beyond qualitative bridges.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined to $203.6 million from $210.8 million a year earlier
Q4 project/charter work is expected to lower EBITDA margins sequentially even as gross margin dollars rise
Operating cash flow was near breakeven at $205,000, with large acquisition-related outflows
positive_highlights: Net income attributable to Radiant rose 28.8% to $3.376 million from $2.622 million a year ago
Adjusted EBITDA increased 3.1% to $9.452 million from $9.167 million a year earlier
Closed the acquisition of Foundation Logistics and converted the Focus Logistics operating partner, with a maturing pipeline of tuck-ins
summary: Radiant reported Q1 FY2025 revenue of $203.6 million, down from $210.8 million a year earlier, while net income rose 28.8% to $3.376 million ($0.07 per diluted share) and adjusted EBITDA edged up 3.1% to $9.452 million. Adjusted net income rose 20.4% to $7.883 million. Management said the slower freight market persists and expects industry headwinds into 2025, but guided to a stronger-than-usual December quarter on project/charter and storm-related work, while warning that project margins will be lower. Operating cash flow was roughly breakeven at $205,000, with cash outflows driven by acquisitions.

negative_highlights: Houston facilities faced multi-day utility outages from Hurricane Beryl, resulting in estimated production losses of approximately 100,000 MMBtus for the first 9 months
Blue Granite RNG project commissioning delayed to 2027 due to Hurricane Helene remediation efforts
Landfill hosts are delaying wellfield collection infrastructure installation, a trend expected to continue through 2025
positive_highlights: Total revenues increased 18.4% YoY to $65.9 million
RIN self-marketing volumes increased by 2 million units (14.5%) to 15.8 million
Adjusted EBITDA grew 31.3% to $29.4 million
summary: Total revenues increased 18.4% to $65.9 million in Q3 2024, driven by higher RIN self-marketing volumes and pricing, while RNG production remained flat at 1.4 million MMBtus due to weather outages. Management provided an updated full-year 2024 outlook with RNG revenues expected between $175 million and $185 million, citing landfill-driven delays that will impact production timing through 2025. No specific guidance was provided for Q4 or 2025 due to market uncertainty regarding pathway renewals.

negative_highlights: Full-year revenue guidance midpoint cut to $143M from $148M prior (range narrowed to $140M-$146M)
CINVANTI declined sequentially on the loss of a large account, in a highly competitive ASP-driven market
ZYNRELEF and APONVIE revenue remains small ($6.3M and $1.1M) and VAN benefit is not expected to meaningfully materialize until Q1 2025
positive_highlights: Product gross margin of 71% vs 42% a year ago, and 73% year-to-date vs 41%, with gross profit doubling to $75.1M
Adjusted EBITDA swung to positive $1.4M operating income and net loss narrowed to $4.8M from $25M
ZYNRELEF CrossLink accounts have ordered nearly 40,000 units (~$4.4M net revenue) since April, and VAN was FDA-approved September 24 with launch targeted for the first week of December
summary: Heron reported Q3 2024 total acute care net revenue of $7.4M (ZYNRELEF $6.3M, APONVIE $1.1M), CINVANTI $22.6M and SUSTOL $2.8M, with product gross margin of 71% vs 42% a year ago (boosted by the absence of prior-year inventory write-offs). The net loss narrowed to $4.8M from $25M, year-to-date cash burn was under $10M, and adjusted EBITDA was a positive $1.4M. Full-year revenue guidance was narrowed to $140M-$146M from $138M-$158M, adjusted OpEx to $101M-$105M from $107M-$111M, and adjusted EBITDA to $2M-$5M from -$10M to +$3M; management also guided Q4 revenue to $37M-$43M. CINVANTI fell sequentially on the loss of a large account, which management expects to reverse in Q4.

negative_highlights: Management explicitly warned of continued inflation in capital equipment and construction costs compared to the previously provided guidance of $1.1 billion for Project Permian.
Cash flow used in operations increased from prior periods due to ramping up activity at La Porte, with expectations that this usage will continue increasing as they build out the organization.
positive_highlights: Phase 1 of the Baker Hughes validation testing at La Porte commenced successfully with no recordable injuries during over 140,000 hours of work by contractors and partners.
Air Liquide was selected as the air separation unit supplier for Project Permian FEED, securing a major equipment component milestone.
summary: NET Power reported a cash flow used in operations of approximately $8 million and total capital expenditures of roughly $22 million for the third quarter of FY2024, with no revenue or EPS figures disclosed as the company remains pre-commercial. Management confirmed Project Permian is on track for initial power generation between late 2027 and early 2028, though they noted expected inflation in capital equipment costs that will offset previously provided guidance estimates.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined 9.5% sequentially to $3.8 million from $4.2 million and 15.6% year-over-year from $4.5 million.
GAAP gross margin fell to 47.0% from 55.5% in Q2, and non-GAAP gross margin fell to 61.7% from 68.8%, hurt by a $0.3 million millimeter-wave inventory write-down and lower royalty revenue.
Q4 guidance of $3.6-$4.0 million suggests further sequential decline at the midpoint, and management pointed to Q1 2025 rather than Q4 for the anticipated revenue inflection.
positive_highlights: Non-GAAP operating expenses fell to $3.3 million from $4.9 million in Q2 and $4.0 million in the prior-year quarter, with GAAP opex down almost 20% year-over-year.
Memory IC shipments rose sequentially to approximately $3.7 million from $3.4 million, with $5.7 million of remaining backlog scheduled to ship by the end of Q1 2025.

New millimeter-wave traction: 82 customer engagements, 23 active evaluations, 28 evaluation kits shipped in Q3 (a record), a $1.4 million DUNE follow-on order from a South African WISP, a Kenya WISP order, and an initial military order.
summary: Peraso reported Q3 2024 revenue of $3.8 million, down 9.5% sequentially from $4.2 million and 15.6% year-over-year from $4.5 million, with GAAP gross margin of 47.0% (down from 55.5% sequentially) and a GAAP net loss of $2.7 million ($0.98/share). Management guided Q4 revenue to $3.6-$4.0 million, implying continued softness, though it reiterated expectations for second-half 2024 revenue to grow double-digits over the prior-year period. The main positive change was operating expense reduction, with non-GAAP opex down to $3.3 million from $4.9 million sequentially and GAAP opex down nearly 20% year-over-year, alongside new millimeter-wave design wins and a $1.4 million follow-on DUNE order. Management expressed confidence in an inflection in Q1 2025 tied to design-win conversions and memory backlog, but the reported quarter showed sequential revenue and margin declines.

negative_highlights: Total operating expenses rose to $76.6 million from $56.9 million in Q3 2023, a roughly $19.7 million increase
Management declined to confirm KOASTAL-1 enrollment completion or final sample size, citing policy to disclose at top-line
Company explicitly will not comment on the competitor's negative M4 readout, leaving that overhang unaddressed
positive_highlights: Cash of $341.3 million with runway expected into mid-2026, covering five clinical catalysts over the next 18 months
KOASTAL-1 top-line data reaffirmed for around end of 2024, with KOASTAL-2/3 in 1H 2025
KOASTAL studies powered at approximately 90% with built-in ability to increase enrollment up to 25% without a protocol amendment
summary: Pre-revenue clinical-stage biotech's first earnings call; no product revenue or EPS reported. Q3 total operating expenses rose to $76.6 million from $56.9 million a year earlier, driven by the navacaprant Phase 3 program and broader portfolio spend, and the company ended the quarter with $341.3 million in cash expected to fund operations into mid-2026. Management reaffirmed timing for KOASTAL-1 top-line data around year-end 2024 and KOASTAL-2/3 in the first half of 2025, and confirmed it intends to commercialize navacaprant itself in the U.S. pending two positive Phase 3 studies. No financial guidance was given; the key change versus prior periods is the ramp in R&D spend as the Phase 3 readouts approach.

negative_highlights: Instrument revenue fell 39% YoY to $2.4M with no concrete signs of recovery expected until early 2025.
Asia-Pacific region revenue declined 34%, while Europe remained flat at +2% growth.
Diagnostics enablement partner revenue was immaterial for the quarter, though up from prior quarters.
positive_highlights: Accelerator lab revenue grew 36% YoY to $10.5M, now comprising ~30% of total business with recurring characteristics.
Non-GAAP gross margin expanded approximately 160 bps sequentially and 280 bps vs prior year due to operational improvements and Advantage Plus transition.
Strong demand for Simoa technology in neurology trials continues despite instrument softness, evidenced by double-digit growth across six consecutive quarters.
summary: Quanterix reported Q3 FY2024 revenue of $35.7 million (up 13% YoY) and non-GAAP gross margin expansion to 53.4%, driven by a 36% surge in Accelerator lab services which offset a sharp decline in instrument sales (-39%). Management reaffirmed full-year 2024 revenue guidance of $134-$138 million despite the restatement of prior period financials and continued macro headwinds for capital funding.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA declined by approximately $4 million compared to last year as market volatility flattened margins
Arctic demand expected to be less than last year in Q4 due to wetter and warmer weather conditions
Charter-in cost per day increased significantly, squeezing the margin on chartered fleet from ~$4,000/day in prior period to $1,800/day
positive_highlights: TCE rates exceeded prevailing market by 19% driven by strong utilization in Arctic trade routes
Total cash from operations increased $12.1 million year-over-year to approximately $28.5 million due to improved working capital
Company solidified position in ice class niche by acquiring remaining 50% interest in post-panamax vessels
summary: Pangaea Logistics Solutions reported Q3 FY2024 adjusted EBITDA of $23.9 million and GAAP net income of $5.1 million ($0.11/share), representing a decline from the prior year due to higher charter hire expenses offsetting market rates, though TCE premiums remained strong at 19%. Management noted that Arctic demand in Q4 is expected to be lower than last year due to wetter weather conditions and anticipates typical seasonal slowing in dry bulk. The company announced an agreement to acquire 15 handysize vessels from M.T. Maritime pending shareholder approval, which will expand the fleet but introduce a transition period for integration.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EPS declined YoY to $0.51 primarily due to a higher effective tax rate (35%) including BEAT expenses.
Merchant gross margin was impacted by exiting high-risk merchants and lower interest revenue ($3M headwind).
SMB direct book growth decelerated slightly compared to prior periods as the company pruned its portfolio.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 8% YoY to $427M, with Merchant Solutions up 11% driven by e-commerce/iGaming growth.
Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 70 bps sequentially from H1 due to portfolio optimization and derisking actions.
Net leverage ratio improved significantly to 4.7x at quarter-end, ahead of the full-year target.
summary: Paysafe reported Q3 FY24 revenue of $427 million (up 8% YoY) and Adjusted EBITDA of $117.8 million (up 1%), though the margin declined 170 bps to 27.6%. Management reaffirmed full-year guidance for revenue ($1.713B-$1.729B) and adjusted EBITDA margins (27.5%-28%) despite a $3 million headwind from interest rates and portfolio optimization investments.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to $754,000 in Q3 from $552,000 a year ago, due to higher SG&A including advertising and marketing costs.
Cash balance at quarter-end was only $1.1 million, prompting a $2 million insider-led offering for working capital.
Q4 guidance excludes AbbVie revenue, which remains delayed to Q1 2025, and management could not provide specific Q4 revenue figures for Silly George's holiday performance.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 141% year-over-year to $2.94 million, with gross margin expanding 1540 bps to 43.6%.
Silly George brand run rate increased from approximately $2 million at acquisition to $5 million heading into the holidays.
Adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed from $788,000 in Q2 to $347,000 in Q3, with Q4 expected to approach cash flow positive.
summary: NEXGEL reported Q3 2024 revenue of $2.94 million, up 141% year-over-year and 104% sequentially, with gross margin expanding to 43.6% from 28.2% a year ago. Adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed to $347,000 from $788,000 in Q2, and the company expects Q4 revenue to exceed $3 million with cash flow approaching positive. Management cited strong growth from the Silly George brand, now at a $5 million run rate, and the Cintas partnership beginning to ship in Q4, while AbbVie revenues remain slated for Q1 2025.

negative_highlights: Reported net loss was heavily impacted by $16M in non-cash warrant fair value adjustments, accounting for 77% of the total reported loss.
Operating expenses increased due to significant ground lease payments at San Jose and new amortization recognition on signed leases ahead of cash payment dates.
Management stated they are not thinking about dividends yet as growth opportunities outweigh capital returns.
positive_highlights: Revenues experienced a step-function increase driven by the San Jose campus opening and optimization of three other campuses.
Management revised guidance to add one additional airport, increasing total portfolio target to 23 airports by end-2025 from previous estimates.
Actual revenues are exceeding conservative 'Sky Harbour Equivalent Rent' forecasts significantly due to strong demand for semiprivate hangars.
summary: Sky Harbour reported Q3 FY2024 results where revenues increased due to the opening of the San Jose campus and optimization of existing sites, though specific consolidated revenue figures were not explicitly stated in the transcript text provided. Operating expenses rose significantly driven by non-cash ground lease amortization ($1.3M-$3.3M) at Addison and other new leases, alongside $16M in warrant fair value adjustments which comprised 77% of reported net loss for the quarter. Management revised their full-year guidance upward to include an additional airport (totaling 23 by end-2025), but reiterated that consolidated breakeven cash flow is not expected until next year.

negative_highlights: Full-year 2024 adjusted EBITDA guidance was cut to $170-175 million, implying Q4 of roughly $43-48 million versus the $43.2 million just reported.
Construction segment revenue fell $41.4 million organically to $262.3 million, with new and used equipment sales down $40.6 million YoY and $31.8 million sequentially.
Construction rental revenue was flat sequentially, breaking the typical pattern of Q3 outpacing Q2, on lower-than-expected physical utilization.
positive_highlights: Product support revenue rose 7.8% to $140.2 million, with parts and service up 4% organically, providing a high-margin buffer against equipment weakness.
Funded debt was reduced by $39 million in the quarter via an $18.2 million rental fleet reduction and working capital optimization, holding leverage at 4.6x.
SG&A fell to approximately $111 million from about $115 million in the prior two quarters, and the Board expanded the share buyback program to $20 million.
summary: Alta reported Q3 FY2024 revenue of $448.8 million, down $17.4 million YoY and $39.3 million sequentially, with the miss concentrated in new and used equipment sales as construction equipment revenue fell $41.4 million organically and new/used equipment sales dropped $44.5 million (29.5%). Adjusted EBITDA was $43.2 million, down $7.8 million YoY, and full-year 2024 EBITDA guidance was cut to $170-175 million from the prior range, implying Q4 EBITDA of roughly $43-48 million. Product support revenue grew 7.8% to $140.2 million and the company paid down $39 million of funded debt while trimming rental fleet by $18.2 million, holding leverage at 4.6x. Management cited election and interest-rate uncertainty for the demand softness but said post-election sentiment has improved and expects normalization in the first half of 2025, and the Board expanded the buyback program to $20 million.

negative_highlights: revenue declined 35% year-over-year due to wind tower pause
Q4 guidance implies softer sequential performance
oil and gas softness continues to impact gearing
positive_highlights: orders up 45% year-over-year, driven by all segments

summary: Broadwind reported Q3 2024 revenue of $35.9 million, down 35% year-over-year due to lower wind tower demand, but delivered near double-digit EBITDA margin (9.5%) and its seventh consecutive profitable quarter. Orders increased 45% year-over-year, with industrial orders up 52% and gearing up 46%, though gearing orders remain below desired levels. Management introduced Q4 revenue guidance of $31-$33 million and adjusted EBITDA of $1-$1.5 million, while expecting 2025 wind volumes to be similar to 2024 with an uptick in activity later in the year.

summary: Sanara MedTech reported Q3 FY2024 revenue of $21.7 million, up 35% year-over-year, marking the 12th consecutive record quarter. Adjusted EBITDA improved to $800,000 from $300,000 in the prior year, with the Surgical segment generating positive EBITDA. The company invested $5 million in ChemoMouthpiece LLC for a 6.6% stake and exclusive distribution through its InfuSystem JV, while Tissue Health Plus remains on track for a mid-2025 commercial launch.

negative_highlights: Q3 revenue fell 35% year-over-year to $6.1 million, including a $500,000 write-down on aged receivables tied to discontinued clinical services.
GAAP gross margin turned negative 139% from 30% a year ago, driven by $9.8 million in one-time charges flowing through cost of goods sold.
Q4 revenue guidance of $6-$7 million and full-year $28-$30 million implies a significant step-down from prior-year levels, with system placements slowing to about 5-7 per quarter.
positive_highlights: Flow cell sales rose 27% year-over-year to 7,835 units, signaling growth in consumable utilization after flat Q2 comparisons.
Operating cash burn fell 46% year-over-year to approximately $14 million, and non-GAAP operating expenses were cut 49% to $16.1 million.
OGM installed base reached 368 systems, up 22% from 301 a year earlier, and a new CPT code (81195) for OGM in hematologic malignancies is set to take effect in January 2025.
summary: Q3 2024 revenue was $6.1 million, down 35% year-over-year, with non-GAAP gross margin of 26% versus 32% a year ago and a GAAP gross margin of negative 139% due to $9.8 million of one-time inventory and related charges. The company guided Q4 revenue to $6-$7 million and full-year 2024 revenue to $28-$30 million, implying continued softness, while OGM installed base grew 22% to 368 systems and flow cell sales rose 27% year-over-year. Management attributed the decline to discontinued clinical services and a deliberate shift away from capital equipment sales toward cash preservation and consumables utilization. Cash and equivalents stood at $23.4 million, with operating cash burn reduced 46% year-over-year to about $14 million.

summary: Smart Sand sold 1.19 million tons in Q3, down 7% sequentially, with revenue of $63.2 million versus $73.8 million in Q2 on lower volumes and lower average watching prices. Contribution margin fell to $13.2 million ($11.09/ton) from $19.8 million ($15.53/ton), and adjusted EBITDA dropped to $5.7 million from $11.9 million, partly reflecting $1.1 million in Canada fab closure and $1.3 million in refinancing costs. Free cash flow was $3.7 million and the company paid a $0.10 special dividend plus announced a $10 million buyback. Guidance calls for Q4 volumes of 1.1-1.4 million tons and Q1 2025 demand consistent to potentially higher than Q1 2024, with pricing improvement only expected over 2025 rather than now.

Nine-month net income fell to $12.5M ($0.35 EPS) from $14.5M ($0.41), with unit OpEx up 21% to $7.84/BOE. The three 1.5-mile Alicia Renee wells were drilled in 14 days, under budget, and are producing over 2,800 BOE/d; no further drilling is planned in 2024 and 2025 guidance has not yet been set. Buybacks began in October with about 104,000 shares repurchased under a 1.75M-share program funded from cash flow.

Operating expenses improved to $5.9 million (down $3.9 million YoY) and cost fell $3.9 million YoY to $2.8 million, but net loss was $11.4 million and adjusted net loss was $11.4 million versus $9.0 million in Q2. Management gave no specific revenue or EPS guidance, instead pointing to an emerging 2025 backlog, a second Aquanaut vehicle expected in Q1 2025, and a goal to watch the first Toolkit license in 2025.

Ethics committee approval was obtained from Medanta Medicity Hospital in India for a separate 9-18 patient safety, feasibility and dose-finding trial, and the company expects to qualify for Australia's 43% cash rebate on Australia-based trial spending.
summary: Aethlon Medical reported no product revenue for its fiscal Q2 2025 (quarter ended September 30, 2024), consistent with its pre-commercial status. Operating expenses declined 9% to approximately $2.9 million from $3.2 million a year earlier, and net loss narrowed to approximately $2.8 million from $3.0 million; cash stood at approximately $6.9 million as of September 30, 2024. The quarter's key development was clinical: the first and second patients were enrolled in the Australian Hemopurifier oncology trial, a second site (Pindara Private Hospital) opened for enrollment, and ethics approval was obtained for a separate India trial, though it awaits CDSCO import approval. Management guided to first safety data around January 2025 and first EV/T-cell data by summer 2025; it did not provide financial guidance.

The company repaid a $4 million bridge loan early but remains in the process of finalizing a waiver for its senior credit agreement due to missing an interest coverage covenant ratio.

Net income swung to $354,000 from a $748,000 loss, helped by a 13% reduction in operating expenses and 48% growth in loan interest income to $1.3 million. The company guided full-year 2024 revenue to $15.0-$15.5 million, a range versus no prior guidance in the text, and flagged challenging cannabis market conditions.

Book value per share was $9.42, with a CECL reserve of $25.3 million (10.7% of loans) and unrealized losses on loans widening by $4.6 million to $19.6 million. Management characterized federal reform, including rescheduling and SAFE Banking, as likely slower under a Republican sweep, framing scarcity of capital as favorable for lender deployment.

summary: Xos reported Q3 2024 revenue of $15.8 million, up 1.6% sequentially, with GAAP gross margin of 18.1% (15% excluding clean energy credits), marking the fifth consecutive quarter of positive margins. Unit deliveries were 94 units, up 4.4% sequentially, and the company achieved low-volume series production of its hub product, shipping nearly 12 hubs. Non-GAAP operating loss improved to $6.6 million from $9.7 million in Q2, and free cash flow improved to negative $11.7 million from negative $26.1 million. However, the company lowered its full-year 2024 revenue and unit delivery guidance, now expecting revenue of $54.1-$67.6 million and deliveries of 320-400 units, while narrowing non-GAAP operating loss to $33.7-$42.2 million, citing infrastructure and customer delays. Cash stood at $9.2 million, and inventory increased to $42.4 million, with over $25 million in incentive receivables backlog.

Inventory fell to $138 million and debt to $85 million, while no formal guidance was provided; management attributed the margin decline to clearing overstock and pointed to licensing mix, automation savings, and acquisitions as future margin drivers.

Management updated full-year 2024 guidance, lowering annual revenue expectations to between $88 million and $92 million while maintaining adjusted EBITDA guidance at $8-10 million. Despite the miss on top-line growth relative to internal targets, management highlighted strong legacy HCP business performance, a gross margin expansion of 60 basis points year-over-year, and significant cash flow generation.

summary: EARN reported Q3 FY2024 net income of $0.21 per share and adjusted distributable earnings (ADE) of $0.28 per share, resulting in an annualized economic return of 10.8%. Management expressed confidence in the pipeline, citing strong demand for 5G assurance and AI capabilities, and announced a new CEO starting December 1.

summary: Worksport reported Q3 2024 revenue of approximately $3.1 million, up 581% year-over-year from $458,000 and up 63% from Q2 2024, driven by B2C online sales that reached $1.59 million (51% of total revenue). Gross profit was $247,000, with the company attributing margin erosion to a strategic production slowdown. Management said it expects to exceed its prior full-year 2024 revenue guidance of $6-8 million and issued 2025 guidance of $25-34.5 million, with a goal of becoming cash flow positive in 2025. The company also announced upcoming launches of the AL4 tonneau cover, COR/SOLIS energy systems, and Terravis heat pump line.

KORU reported Q3 revenue of $8.2M, up 17% YoY and the third straight quarter of double-digit growth, with gross margin up 140 bps to 63.4%; domestic core grew 12% to $6.4M, international grew 5% (about 25% normalized for BSI destocking), and Novel Therapies grew 276% to $0.6M. The company raised FY2024 revenue guidance to $32.75-33.25M (15-17% growth) from $32-32.5M (12-14%), lifted gross margin guidance to 62-63% from 61-62%, and increased its year-end cash target to at least $8.8M from $8M, while OpEx guidance rose to $24.5-25M. The next-generation device 510(k) was pushed to mid-2025 from Q4 2024 and the rare disease biologic filing to sometime in 2025, both described as having no material 2025 revenue impact. Cash usage was $1.7M in the quarter and $2.7M year-to-date, a 60% improvement over 2023, with Q4 breakeven targeted.

Management disclosed ReMEDy2 protocol changes including newly eligible thrombolytic non-responders and an interim analysis sample increase from 144 to 200 participants, which pushes interim results from summer 2025 to Q4 2025. Management guided to positive cash flow in Q4 2024 and positive adjusted EBITDA in early 2025, but issued no explicit full-year revenue or EPS guidance and gave no prior guidance to compare against.

While management highlighted a strategic partnership with Quanta Computer involving a $10 million investment tranche received in Q3 and cost reductions totaling 28%, these positives were overshadowed by the sharp decline in top-line performance.

Management indicated that updated margin guidance for Germany will be provided in Q1 2025 as they stabilize their business model.

summary: Fiscal Q4 FY2024 revenue decreased 16% to $378 million and full year revenue fell 8%, primarily due to Hurricane Helene disruptions in Florida which impacted sales during a typically strong period. Gross profit declined 24% to $91 million for the quarter, while operating income improved slightly from a loss of $117 million to an adjusted EBITDA of $8 million driven by cost reductions and lower interest expenses despite restructuring charges. Management provided cautious guidance for FY2025 with total sales expected between $1.7 billion and $1.85 billion.

negative_highlights: Net revenues declined to $2.4M from $3.3M year-over-year
Gross margin fell to 46% from 52.3% due to fixed costs and lower digital revenue
Sales and marketing expense cut by over half, limiting near-term growth
positive_highlights: VAYNERCOMMERCE partnership drove 34% increase in daily digital revenues over 17 days
G&A decreased $1.3M year-over-year and $500K sequentially
2025 earnings benefit of $4.5M from non-cash and interest expense amortization ending
summary: Q3 net revenues fell to $2.4M from $3.3M YoY, largely due to dropping a wholesale account that was net-negative on cash contribution, and limited digital ad spend. Gross margin contracted to 46% from 52.3%, but G&A dropped $1.3M and net loss improved to $3.5M from $5.4M. Management highlighted a new VAYNERCOMMERCE partnership that drove a 34% increase in daily digital revenues during a 17-day period, and expects a $4.5M earnings benefit in 2025 from non-cash expense amortization ending and interest expense declining, plus a wholesale price increase at Sundry adding over $500K annually. The company is pivoting from debt repayment to growth initiatives.

negative_highlights: Streaming audio and CTV combined represent ~50% of spend, but streaming audio growth is not quantified in the excerpt
Q4 guidance implies deceleration from Q3 growth rate
Political contributed ~3% of CxT in Q4, a headwind for 1H next year
positive_highlights: Revenue and contribution ex-TAC grew 34% and 21% YoY, respectively
Record Q3 adjusted EBITDA of $14.7 million
CTV spend up nearly 50% YoY, with Direct Access representing over half of CTV spend
summary: Viant delivered a strong Q3 2024, with revenue and contribution ex-TAC up 34% and 21% YoY respectively, and record adjusted EBITDA of $14.7 million. CTV spend grew nearly 50% YoY, driven by Direct Access and the newly announced IRIS.TV acquisition, which enhances content-level targeting. Management raised Q4 guidance, and expects continued above-market growth. Expense growth is expected to remain below contribution ex-TAC growth in 2025.

negative_highlights: Company remains unprofitable with an operating loss of $7.4 million and cash burn of approximately $5.6 million.
D2C sales are in a very early stage with only 339 units shipped since resuming orders on September 17.
Management explicitly stated they will remain 'judicious' with capital spending and manage resources carefully.
positive_highlights: Operating loss narrowed to $7.4 million from $9.1 million in the prior year period.
Successful relaunch of Evie Rings with 339 units shipped in the sub-period following a back-in-stock announcement.
FDA 510(k) clearance for EvieMED is in the final stages, with active discussions secured for B2B pilots and clinical trials.
summary: Movano Health reported an operating loss of $7.4 million for Q3 FY2024, a reduction from the $9.1 million loss in the prior year period, with cash and equivalents at $11.3 million. The company shipped 339 Evie Rings during the sub-period following its September 17 relaunch, noting that marketing spend remained entirely organic for this initial phase. Management highlighted progress on FDA 510(k) clearance for the EvieMED Ring and upcoming Android app launch, while emphasizing a continued focus on managing capital deployment and cash burn.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened significantly from a profit of $0.1 million in the prior period due to a $3 million settlement charge.
Adjusted EBITDA remains negative at -$0.1 million despite revenue growth, indicating high cost absorption.
Progress on ZTAC integration is described as 'slower than anticipated'.
positive_highlights: Revenue surged 93% year-over-year to $2.2 million driven by mobile gaming integration with ZTAC and strong arena demand.
summary: Q3 FY2024 revenues reached $2.2 million, representing a 93% year-over-year increase driven by mobile gaming and arena events, though total costs rose to $3.3 million due to ZTAC integration expenses. The company reported an adjusted EBITDA loss of $0.1 million compared to the prior quarter's $0.3 million loss, while net income turned negative at -$4.0 million primarily due to a one-time settlement charge and foreign currency losses. Management provided no updated financial guidance for FY2024 but expressed optimism about upcoming initiatives like the World Mahjong Tour.

negative_highlights: License/R&D services revenue decreased $0.1 million (50%) YoY
R&D expenses increased slightly to ~$3M despite lower R&D spend in prior year due to Fabry program completion, though S&A dropped significantly
positive_highlights: Revenue increased $7.6 million (75% YoY) to $17.8M driven by Chiesi sales
Net income turned positive at ~$3.2M due to debt repayment and lower R&D spend
Company is now fully debt-free after repaying the 7.5% senior secured convertible notes
summary: Protalix reported Q3 FY2024 revenue of $17.8 million from goods sales and $0.1 million from license/R&D services, representing a 75% year-over-year increase driven by Chiesi sales but offset by lower Brazil sales. The company recorded net income of approximately $3.2 million ($0.04 basic EPS) compared to a Q3 2023 loss of $1.9 million, aided significantly by the full repayment and extinguishment of its senior secured convertible notes in September. Management confirmed that all eight cohorts for the Phase 1 trial of PRX-115 are complete with data analysis ongoing, while plans for a Phase 2 study remain pending regulatory discussions.

negative_highlights: No product revenue recorded in the quarter versus $2.1M net product revenue a year ago after the Vyleesi sale
Net loss widened to $7.8M from $5.2M a year ago, and net cash used in operations rose to $7M from $5.9M
Cash and cash equivalents fell to $2.4M at September 30, 2024 from $9.5M at June 30, 2024
positive_highlights: BMT-801 obesity study fully enrolled as of October, upsized from 60 to approximately 115 patients, with top-line data expected in Q1 2025
Phase 2 PL8177 ulcerative colitis top-line data expected in Q1 2025, with management citing five or six large companies under CDA and re-engagement ahead of data
Operating expenses declined to $7.8M from $8.2M a year ago, mainly from elimination of Vyleesi note expenses
summary: Palatin reported Q1 FY2025 revenue of zero product sales following the December 2023 sale of Vyleesi to Cosette, versus $2.1M net product revenue and $4.6M gross product sales in the prior-year quarter, with net loss widening to $7.8M from $5.2M and cash falling to $2.4M as of September 30, 2024 from $9.5M at June 30, 2024. Operating expenses were $7.8M versus $8.2M a year ago, and net cash used in operations rose to $7M from $5.9M. The company said it will focus going forward on MCR-4 obesity assets, retained an investment bank to explore strategic options for non-obesity programs, and guided to multiple data readouts: the Phase 2 BMT-801 bremelanotide/tirzepatide obesity study fully enrolled at ~115 patients with top-line data in Q1 2025, PL8177 ulcerative colitis Phase 2 top-line data in Q1 2025, and bremelanotide diabetic kidney disease data this quarter or Q4 2024.

negative_highlights: Total revenue fell to $12.6 million from $17.5 million in Q3 2023 due to lower North America processing, and full-year 2024 revenue guidance was cut to $56-$60 million.
Adjusted EBITDA swung to negative $1.7 million from positive $50,000 in Q3 2023, while other expense rose to $2.1 million from $600,000 on debt discount accretion and derivative fair value changes.
Two European software integrations were postponed to Q4 2024, and the company declined to provide specific 2025 guidance, citing an incomplete planning process and many moving parts.
positive_highlights: International revenue grew 96% year-over-year to $9.8 million, with international processing volume up from $781 million in Q2 2024 to $952 million in Q3 2024.
North America processing volume rose 12% sequentially to $171 million, and U.S. revenue grew more than 10% sequentially, which management said points to a return to growth.

The company reached a memorandum of understanding to restructure its balance sheet, paying $16.5 million to terminate its 8% senior convertible note and redeem its Series B convertible preferred stock.
summary: Ryvyl reported Q3 2024 revenue of $12.6 million, down from $17.5 million a year earlier, with GAAP gross margin of 38.5% versus 38.2% and adjusted EBITDA of negative $1.7 million compared to positive $50,000 in Q3 2023. International revenue grew 96% to $9.8 million and total processing volume rose 31% year-over-year to $1.123 billion, but management cut full-year 2024 revenue guidance to $56-$60 million from the previously reiterated expectation, citing delayed European software integrations and U.S. softness. Management said the integration issues were resolved in October and expects U.S. business to have bottomed with double-digit sequential growth, while declining to issue specific 2025 guidance until January planning is complete.

negative_highlights: FY2025 guidance calls for only modest revenue growth; no specific numerical ranges were provided
Oil and gas water deliveries were stronger in the first three quarters and weaker in Q4, which management called atypical
The company remains early-stage, with only 2% of water assets, 18% of land development, and 7% of planned rentals in production
positive_highlights: Record FY2024 revenue of $28.7 million and net income of $11.6 million, or $0.48 per share
Gross margin near 70% on $20 million gross profit, benefiting from low historical land and water rights basis
Water utility segment had a record year, with oil and gas revenue over $5.5 million and 21% CAGR in utility customer connections
summary: Pure Cycle reported record FY2024 results: revenue of $28.7 million, gross profit of ~$20 million (~69% margin), and net income of $11.6 million, or $0.48 per share, driven by delivery of 194 for-sale lots (plus 17 retained) in Phase 2D and record oil and gas water sales of over $5.5 million. Q4 revenue was about $12.5 million. Management provided forward guidance for the first time, expecting revenues to increase modestly in FY2025 with higher margins, and noted the single-family rental portfolio should grow from 14 units toward 100 over the next 18-24 months. The prior year was characterized as an anomaly due to rapid interest rate increases affecting homebuilder lot inventory.

negative_highlights: Q3 cash burn was approximately $11 million, though management expects a reduction to $4M-$4.5M in Q4.
PERIO-03 pancreatic trial enrollment increased beyond target, pushing data readout to mid-2025 without immediate efficacy confirmation.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 42% YoY to $7.3 million with gross margin expanding to 86%.
R&D expenses dropped 56% QoQ as PERIO Phase 1 trials completed enrollment.
Management raised full-year 2025 sales guidance range to $28M-$30M.
summary: TriSalus reported Q3 FY2024 revenue of $7.3 million, representing a 42% year-over-year increase driven by TriNav device sales in the US. Gross margin remained robust at 86%, while R&D and G&A expenses decreased significantly due to trial completions and de-SPAC cost normalization. Management provided full-year 2025 guidance of $28M-$30M, projecting over 50% growth and a path to EBITDA positivity in 2025.

negative_highlights: Gross margin dipped to 71.7% from 74.3% due to hardware mix
Monitoring revenue from the wireless contract not yet recognized until units are installed
CP segment (pipeline) sales were lower in the quarter
positive_highlights: Q3 revenue up 46.1% to $3.05 million, EPS up to $0.29 from $0.01
Excluding the material contract, Q3 revenue still grew double-digits over prior year
Operating cash flow for nine months improved to $739,000 from $366,000
summary: Acorn Energy reported record Q3 2024 revenue of $3.05 million, up 46.1% YoY, with EPS of $0.29 versus $0.01 a year ago. The quarter benefited from an initial $724,000 hardware shipment under a two-year, ~$5 million contract with a national wireless telecom provider. Excluding that contract, revenue still grew double-digits. Management expects operating expenses to rise as they invest in IT and engineering, but remains confident in double-digit growth and operating leverage.

negative_highlights: Traceability contributed only 6% of revenue, so the doubling thesis remains unproven in reported numbers
Operating expenses rose 3% to $4 million on sales, marketing, and automation investment while revenue grew 8%
No formal numeric revenue or EPS guidance was provided for the fiscal year
positive_highlights: Revenue up 8% to $5.4 million and recurring revenue up 6%, with recurring at 98% of total
Operating income up 23% to $1.5 million, net income up 21% to $1.7 million, EPS up to $0.09 from $0.07 on 8% revenue growth
Queue of 4,000 companies being actively enrolled represents roughly $10 million of incremental ARR over 18-24 months
summary: ReposiTrak reported Q1 FY2025 revenue of $5.4 million, up 8% YoY, with recurring revenue up 6% at 98% of total. Operating income rose 23% to $1.5 million, GAAP net income rose 21% to $1.7 million, and basic EPS was $0.09 versus $0.07, with operating cash flow up 23% to $1.9 million and $25.8 million in cash. Traceability was only 6% of revenue, but management cited 4,000 companies (~5,000 facilities) in the enrollment queue representing roughly $10 million of incremental ARR over 18-24 months and reiterated a goal to double the revenue run rate in a few years. No formal numeric guidance was given; the dividend was raised 10% to $0.0726 per share annually and another ~70,000 preferred shares ($750,000) were redeemed.

negative_highlights: Israel revenue declined due to Oranim deal cancellation and 10% drop in patients
Gross margin for nine months fell to 14% from 25%
Net loss widened to $10.6M for nine months
positive_highlights: German revenue up 278% to $5.8M in Q3
Adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed 82% to $0.2M
Operating expenses ratio improved to 30% from 40%
summary: Q3 2024 revenue grew 12% YoY to $13.9M, driven by a 278% surge in German revenue to $5.8M, but Israel declined due to the Oranim deal cancellation and a 10% drop in medical cannabis patients. The company continued to clean slow-moving inventory with a $0.6M charge, and gross margin improved to 23% from 21% YoY. Adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed to $0.2M from $1.3M, but the company remains loss-making and is focused on building supply chain and integration for accelerated German growth in 2025.

negative_highlights: VIP enrollment revenue fell 6% to $900,000 due to a strategic shift away from the VIP model and lower contract completions.
Cash burn from operations increased slightly to $9.8 million for the nine months ended Sept 30, primarily due to changes in working capital.
Management expressed disappointment with the DME initiative and noted that most dentists are not adopting the sleep treatment model.
positive_highlights: Revenue increased 17% quarter-over-quarter to $3.9 million, driven by a 34% rise in product revenue.
Gross margin expanded significantly to 60% from 53% year-over-year.
Operating loss decreased 27% quarter-over-quarter as cost-cutting initiatives continued.
summary: Vivos Therapeutics reported Q3 FY2024 revenue of $3.9 million, a 17% quarter-over-quarter increase driven by higher appliance sales and lower discounts, while VIP enrollment revenue declined 6% due to a strategic pivot away from that model. Gross margin expanded to 60%, and operating expenses decreased for the ninth consecutive quarter as the company reduced cash burn. Management indicated Q4 will be a transition period with expectations of flat-to-slight growth before significant accretion in 2025 under the new sleep-center alliance model.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened slightly to $10.7 million with R&D expenses rising to $6.8 million.
VERSATILE-003 trial design was modified to reduce cost and time, focusing on a two-arm study first before pursuing the triple therapy arm involving PDS01ADC dose optimization.
No revenue or cash flow from product sales; reliance entirely on existing capital reserves of ~$50 million.
positive_highlights: VERSATILE-002 matured data shows Median Overall Survival at 30 months with a lower bound CI improving to ~20 months versus pembrolizumab's ~18 months.
Objective Response Rate improved from 26% to 36%, and Complete/Partial Responses increased significantly (9% complete response vs 3% prior year).
IMMUNOCERV Phase 2 data demonstrated a 100% 36-month overall survival rate in patients receiving all five doses of Versamune HPV versus 82.6% for Keytruda plus CRT.
summary: PDS Biotech reported a net loss of $10.7 million for Q3 FY2024, compared to $10.8 million in the prior year quarter, driven by increased R&D expenses despite lower operating costs and G&A fees. The company has no revenue-generating products yet; VERSATILE-003 is a Phase 3 trial expected to initiate enrollment early Q1 2025 with an interim readout estimated for roughly mid-to-late 2026, while IMMUNOCERV data showed promising survival rates in cervical cancer but next steps are undecided. Management expressed confidence in the clinical pipeline's potential against competitors like Merus and Keytruda, citing superior durability of response in HPV-positive patients.

negative_highlights: Net sales fell to $6.8 million from $11.9 million, with roughly $4.4 million of the gap attributed to liquidity-driven inventory constraints and note weakness in shipments
Gross margin contracted to 18% from 34% on higher trade spend and increased COGS as a percentage of net sales; operating loss widened to $3.1 million from $0.1 million
Full-year 2024 outlook withdrawn due to year-to-date inventory challenges, with management acknowledging note weakness in shipments and production problems have been a repetitive message
positive_highlights: Over 5,000 new points of distribution secured in aggregate, including Safeway Albertsons' national secondary display (1,800+ points) and Giant Eagle's 7 new items (1,100+ points)
New $10 million one-year revolver with Whitebox plus largest shareholder D&D Source of Life's purchase of all outstanding secured debt, which management says deleverages the balance sheet
Operating cash flow turned positive at $1.1 million versus $1.8 million used in the year-ago quarter, driven by lower inventory purchases
summary: Net sales fell to $6.8 million from $11.9 million a year ago, with management attributing roughly $4.4 million of the shortfall to liquidity-constrained inventory purchases and short shipments. Gross margin contracted to 18% from 34%, operating loss widened to $3.1 million from $0.1 million, and modified EBITDA was a $3 million loss versus $0.2 million a year ago. Reed's withdrew its previously issued full-year 2024 outlook and announced a $10 million one-year revolver with Whitebox plus D&D Source of Life's purchase of all outstanding secured debt from Whitebox. Management cited over 5,000 new points of distribution and a functional beverage launch planned for early 2025, but said it will take until year-end to be fully stocked.

negative_highlights: R&D expenses decreased $0.6 million YoY, partly due to lower OPC1 program spending, reflecting delayed study initiation
No OPC1 patient dosing yet; enrollment awaits FDA review of IND amendment expected in Q1 2025, following prior delays
Ongoing operating loss of $3.8 million in the quarter, with the company still dependent on external funding and partnership milestones
positive_highlights: Total revenues rose to $3.8 million from $1.2 million YoY, primarily from more collaboration revenue recognized under the Roche agreement
Net loss narrowed to $3.0 million ($0.02 per share) from $7.1 million ($0.04 per share) YoY
Cash runway guidance extended to Q1 2026, one quarter longer than previously guided, with $32.7 million in cash and marketable securities as of September 30, 2024
summary: Lineage reported Q3 2024 total revenues of $3.8 million, up $2.5 million YoY, driven by increased collaboration revenue from Roche, while net loss narrowed to $3.0 million ($0.02 per share) from $7.1 million ($0.04 per share). Operating expenses decreased $0.3 million to $7.6 million. Management extended its cash runway guidance to Q1 2026, a quarter longer than previously guided, citing fiscal discipline and OPC1 startup activities completed while awaiting FDA input. The company also disclosed a recent FDA meeting that it believes provides a clear path to initiating the DOSED study for OPC1, with enrollment expected after the agency completes its review in Q1 2025.

negative_highlights: Revenue fell 85% YoY to $9.1 million; Colossus SSP revenue was down 96% to $2.2 million
Swung to a $3.7 million operating loss, $6.4 million net loss and $2.9 million adjusted EBITDA loss from prior-year profits
FY2024 revenue guidance slashed to $60-70 million from the prior $170-190 million target, with FY2025 guided at $90-110 million
positive_highlights: Gross margin expanded to approximately 39% from 23% a year earlier on a higher note-side mix
Operating expenses were held roughly flat at $7.2 million versus $7.3 million despite the revenue collapse
Signed two leading DSP partners expected to go live later in 2025 under the new Colossus Connections initiative
summary: Q3 FY2024 revenue was $9.1 million, down 85% YoY from $59.5 million, driven by a 96% collapse in Colossus SSP revenue to $2.2 million after the May Adalytics blog post caused a major customer to pause and volumes to fall; watch-side revenue declined 12% to $6.9 million. Gross profit fell 70% to $3.5 million while gross margin rose to about 39% from 23% on a mix shift toward the watch side. The quarter swung to a $3.7 million operating loss from $4.5 million operating income and a $2.9 million adjusted EBITDA loss from $5.4 million income; cash ended at $4.1 million. Full-year FY2024 revenue guidance was cut to $60-70 million (from the original $170-190 million target) with FY2025 guidance of $90-110 million; the company cited cost reductions, a $20 million equity reserve facility with New Circle, and new DSP partnerships (two signed, live later in 2025) aimed at rebuilding.

negative_highlights: Nine-month revenue declined to $5.5 million from $5.9 million YoY
Exit from a European service agreement creates near-term revenue headwind
Q3 gross margin benefited significantly from a prior-year $1 million hardware reserve
positive_highlights: Revenue up 18% YoY to $2.1 million; license revenue up 52% to $1.4 million
Net loss improved to $0.7 million from $1.8 million YoY
Large orders from defense ministry, British Columbia, and banking customer support Q4 and beyond
summary: BIO-key reported Q3 FY2024 revenue of $2.1 million, up 18% YoY and up from $1.1 million sequentially, driven by higher license and hardware revenue. License revenue rose 52% to $1.4 million, and gross margins improved significantly, partly due to a prior-year hardware reserve and a higher mix of license revenue. Net loss narrowed to $0.7 million from $1.8 million a year ago. Management expects 2024 revenue to meet or exceed 2023's $7.75 million, implying Q4 revenue of at least $2.3 million, supported by multiple large orders received after quarter end.

negative_highlights: The company could not close liquidity or primary capital transactions in the quarter pending shareholder approval to increase authorized shares, with deal closings not expected until later in Q3.
Distributions from alternative assets in custody declined to $5.3 million from $14.3 million a year earlier, roughly a 28% decline in the distribution rate versus beginning NAV.
Segment adjusted operating loss was $2.3 million for the quarter, and Ben Liquidity and Ben Custody segment revenue growth was flat to modest.
positive_highlights: GAAP revenues turned positive at $8.6 million versus negative $42.8 million in the prior-year quarter, with GAAP net income of $9.7 million and basic EPS of $2.98.

Permanent equity deficit narrowed to $13.2 million from $148.3 million after reclassifying $126 million of preferred equity, moving toward Nasdaq's $2.5 million positive permanent equity listing requirement.
Operating expenses excluding impairment fell 31.9% to $22.0 million, and comp and benefits dropped to $7.1 million from $15.4 million.
summary: Beneficient reported Q2 FY2025 GAAP revenues of positive $8.6 million versus a negative $42.8 million a year ago, GAAP net income of $9.7 million and basic EPS of $2.98, and a second consecutive quarter of positive fully diluted EPS. However, the company was unable to close liquidity and primary capital transactions during the quarter pending shareholder approval to increase authorized shares, which it received in October; segment-level results showed a $2.3 million adjusted operating loss. Operating expenses excluding impairment declined 31.9% to $22.0 million and permanent equity deficit narrowed to $13.2 million from $148.3 million after a $126 million preferred reclassification, but distributions from collateral fell to $5.3 million from $14.3 million a year earlier and management described industry distribution rates at 8% of NAV versus a 12-20% historical band.

negative_highlights: Average realized price per BOE decreased, offsetting some of the volume-driven revenue growth.
Operating costs were elevated due to an eight-month CO2 purchase pipeline shutdown and compressor issues at Delhi before resumption in October.
Production in Williston Basin was temporarily impacted by high-volume wells going down during Q1.
positive_highlights: Total production increased 16% YoY to 7,478 net barrels of oil equivalent per day driven by SCOOP/STACK and Chaveroo wells performing above initial expectations (approx. 65% above acquisition type curves).
Net income surged 40% year-over-year due to increased revenue volumes and reduced operating costs.
Cash flow from operations materially improved to $7.6 million compared to $4.3 million in the prior year period.
summary: Evolution Petroleum reported fiscal Q1 FY2025 revenue of $21.9 million (up 6% YoY) and net income increasing 40% to $2.1 million driven by record oil production from SCOOP/STACK acquisitions and new Chaveroo wells, partially offset by lower realized prices. Management reiterated full-year CapEx guidance at approximately $12-14 million while maintaining a consistent dividend program for the 45th consecutive quarter.

negative_highlights: Full-year 2024 revenue guidance was reduced to $315–320 million from $325–335 million due to new product certification delays.
Hardware revenue growth was only 15% YoY, impacted by certification delays which are expected to persist into early 2025.
Sequential growth in activated devices slowed, which management attributed to lower hardware sales in Q1 2024.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 38% YoY to a record $83 million, with recurring revenue up 49% to $60 million (72% of total).
Gross margin expanded to 45.7% from 38.1% YoY, with hardware margin at 34.4% (up from 20.5%) and recurring margin at 50.1% (up from 46.9%).
Achieved first positive net income of $0.7 million and record adjusted EBITDA of $11.1 million, with free cash flow of $10.1 million.
summary: Nayax reported Q3 2024 record revenue of $83 million, up 38% YoY, with recurring revenue up 49% to $60 million (72% of total) and a first-ever net income of $0.7 million. Gross margin expanded to 45.7% from 38.1%, adjusted EBITDA reached a record $11.1 million, and free cash flow was $10.1 million. Full-year 2024 revenue guidance was lowered to $315–320 million from $325–335 million due to new product certification delays, while adjusted EBITDA guidance of $30–35 million was kept with an expectation of the higher end, and hardware margin guidance was raised to exceed 30% from 27–29%. Management also introduced a 2025 adjusted EBITDA margin target of at least 15%.

negative_highlights: Gross profit margin was lower than anticipated at 8.6% due to negative margins in the Truck Body division.
Truck Body division suffered from lower throughput compared to prior periods, dragging down overall profitability.
Management stated uncertainty regarding the extent of changes to federal programs following the recent election.
positive_highlights: Revenue increased 78% sequentially to $5.3 million driven by deliveries of 11 Type D buses, 6 EV Star Cargo Plus, and 5 EV Stars.
SG&A costs declined by $630,000 (12.1%) due to reductions in professional fees and share-based payments.
The company has over 300 live orders and qualified leads for its all-electric school buses.
summary: GreenPower reported Q2 FY2025 revenue of $5.3 million (a 78% increase over Q1) and generated a gross profit of approximately $460,000, resulting in a gross margin of 8.6%. Management explicitly noted that the lower-than-anticipated gross profit margin was primarily due to negative margins in the Truck Body division caused by lower throughput compared to prior periods. The company raised $3 million via an underwritten share offering and finished the quarter with approximately $850,000 in available liquidity from its EDC facility.

negative_highlights: GAAP operating income declined to a loss of -$0.1 million, down from +$0.5 million in the prior year.
Adjusted net income guidance was lowered significantly to negative $1 million to breakeven (missed positive prior guide).
Gross margin contracted 40 bps YoY to 25.8% due to higher freight costs and promotional expenses.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 20.6% YoY driven by strong performance across all geographies (Europe +39%, US +21%).
Gross profit hit a record $9.3 million, an increase of 18.9% compared to the prior year.
Management raised full-year revenue guidance significantly from $115-$128M to $127-$131M.
summary: FGI reported Q3 FY2024 revenue of $36.1 million (up 20.6% YoY) and gross profit of a record $9.3 million, though GAAP operating income turned negative at -$0.1 million due to higher expenses and margin compression from freight/promotions. Management raised full-year 2024 revenue guidance to $127-$131M (from $115-$128M) but lowered adjusted net income guidance to a loss of up to breakeven (from positive $1.2-$2M). The outlook remains cautious with industry growth expected at muted levels, though the company expects margins and operating leverage to improve in Q4.

negative_highlights: Net loss from operations increased to $7.3 million compared to $8.8 million in Q3 2023.
Non-GAAP recurring EBITDA showed a net loss of $9.2 million, widening the loss from $6.2 million in Q3 2023.
Net loss attributable to common shareholders increased by approximately $2.1 million to $9.9 million.
positive_highlights: Net revenue increased 14% QoQ to $3.1 million and 11% YoY to $2.8 million.
Phase III OnTarget trial achieved meaningful clinical signals in breast cancer subgroup, accepted for poster presentation at San Antonio Breast Cancer Symposium.
Successfully launched Gelclair, the company's third commercialized prescription product, in the United States.
summary: JAGX reported Q3 FY2024 net revenue of $3.1 million, representing a 14% increase quarter-over-quarter and an 11% increase year-over-year. The company achieved significant clinical signals in breast cancer from its Phase III OnTarget trial, with results accepted for presentation at the San Antonio Breast Cancer Symposium on December 11, 2024. Management also announced the recent US launch of Gelclair, a new prescription product for oral mucositis.

negative_highlights: Company is disputing and negotiating $4.9 million in accounts payable
A D&O insurer has failed to pay a $2.5 million secondary coverage layer, cited alongside payables as major going-concern and stockholder equity issues
Active proxy fight: activist investors nominated four directors to replace the entire board, with management claiming the group seeks over $5 million in reimbursement
positive_highlights: DURIPANC combination showed 5 of 6 patients (83%) with stable disease at three months versus 20% in historical controls
Manufacturing optimization with Sterling cut polymer production time by about 40% and is expected to save roughly $2 million in method transfer plus about $200,000 per batch
AMP-518 complete data supports statistically significant response in moderate-to-severe post-COVID fatigue patients, enabling a targeted follow-up trial
summary: AIM ImmunoTech's Q3 FY2024 call contained no reported revenue, EPS, or margin figures and no explicit financial guidance; management instead detailed clinical progress on Ampligen, including preliminary DURIPANC data showing stable disease in 5 of 6 patients at three months versus 20% historical controls. The company disclosed it is disputing and negotiating $4.9 million in accounts payable and that a D&O insurer has failed to pay a $2.5 million secondary layer, both cited as major factors in going-concern and stockholder equity issues. Management also described a manufacturing optimization expected to save about $2 million in validation and roughly $200,000 per batch, and highlighted an activist investor campaign seeking to replace the entire board.

negative_highlights: Feline test milestone not yet achieved, with ongoing test optimization
Many clinical manuscripts and licensing deals still pending
Cash neutrality target remains a goal for 2025, not yet reached
positive_highlights: Q3 revenue up 187% YoY, year-to-date revenue up 96% to $1 million
Nu.Q Vet test revenue up 307% in Q3 and 100% YTD, with 110,000 tests sold
Signed 500-patient lung cancer validation study in Taiwan; sepsis data predicted higher mortality and organ failure risk
summary: VolitionRx reported Q3 2024 revenue of $475,000, up 187% YoY, with year-to-date revenue of $1 million, up 96%. Nu.Q Vet test revenue grew 307% in the quarter and 100% YTD, with over 110,000 tests sold in the first nine months.
