Management highlighted significant clinical progress in lung cancer and sepsis, including a large prospective study in Taiwan and positive sepsis data. Operating expenses were reduced, and the company reiterated its goal of cash neutrality in 2025.

negative_highlights: Total revenue fell 10% year-over-year to $21.8 million and non-GAAP EPS declined to $0.04 from $0.12
Gross margin contracted to 70% from 73% a year ago and adjusted EBITDA margin fell to 6% from 12%
Total RPO declined 15% year-over-year with note weakness in-term RPO down 9%, and total SaaS ARR decreased 4% year-over-year
positive_highlights: Knowledge customer SaaS ARR grew 16% year-over-year, with LTM dollar-based net retention up to 103% from 98% last quarter
Q1 revenue of $21.8 million landed at the high end of guidance, and both revenue and EPS came in ahead of consensus
New bookings were up significantly year-over-year off a seasonally light quarter and a weak year-ago base, with management noting post-summer RFP pickup in October
summary: eGain reported Q1 FY2025 total revenue of $21.8 million, at the high end of guidance but down 10% year-over-year, with non-GAAP EPS of $0.04 versus $0.12 a year ago, both ahead of consensus. Management reiterated full-year revenue guidance of $92-$93 million and non-GAAP EPS of $0.17-$0.20, with Q2 revenue guided to $22.2-$22.6 million and non-GAAP net income of breakeven to $0.5 million. Knowledge SaaS ARR grew 16% year-over-year and Knowledge net retention improved to 103% from 98%, while total SaaS ARR fell 4% and total net retention was 90%, reflecting prior Conversation and Analytics customer losses and the Cisco OEM revenue recognition timing deferral of approximately $1.3 million. Q1 bookings improved off a weak year-ago base but management characterized the quarter as seasonally light, with deal momentum picking back up in Q2.

negative_highlights: No explicit Q4 numeric revenue or EPS guidance provided on the call; figures deferred to the Shareholder Letter
Growth remains modest at low-single-digit rates after a two-year technology spending downturn
Rising tech customer R&D spend is not yet converting to sales and marketing budgets, delaying a broader recovery
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 2% year-over-year in Q3, the second consecutive quarter of growth after 1% in Q2
Management expects continued similar low-to-mid-single-digit revenue growth in Q4 and into early 2025
Multiple 2024 product launches (Account Insights Feed, Market Monitor, Priority Engine Demand, IntentMail AI) positioned for the Informa Tech combination ahead of 2025
summary: TechTarget reported modest year-over-year revenue growth of 2% in Q3, following 1% growth in Q2, marking a second consecutive quarter of growth off a two-year depressed technology spending cycle. Management expects similar low-to-mid-single-digit growth in Q4 and into early 2025 but provided no explicit numeric guidance or EPS and margin figures on the call, referring instead to the separately filed Shareholder Letter. The dominant forward item is the pending combination with Informa Tech's digital business, expected to close shortly after the November 26 special meeting, with management citing an improved interest rate environment and post-election certainty as tailwinds.

negative_highlights: Ending ARR declined $900k year-over-year to $18.7 million, including a $5.8 million reduction from the delayed contract
Free cash flow usage was $7.3 million versus $400k in Q3 last year, due to delayed cash receipts
Operating expenses increased 5% to $17.3 million, including $600k in one-time severance costs
positive_highlights: Subscription gross profit margin improved to 86% from 85% year-over-year
Service gross profit margin improved to 61% from 54% year-over-year
Gift card revenue recorded in Q3, expected to contribute significantly in 2025
summary: DMRC reported Q3 FY2024 revenue of $9.4 million, up 5% year-over-year, with subscription revenue up 9% to $5.3 million. However, ending ARR fell to $18.7 million from $19.6 million, a $900k decline driven primarily by a $5.8 million impact from a delayed contract renewal. The quarter's results were heavily impacted by this delayed contract, which also caused free cash flow usage of $7.3 million and no revenue or cash collection from the deal. Management emphasized the contract's transformational potential and expects to close it in Q4, but provided no formal financial guidance for the quarter or full year. The CFO did indicate that Q4 free cash flow usage is expected to be significantly improved from Q3, and could be significantly positive if payment is received before year-end.

negative_highlights: Fleet operational utilization declined to 90.6% from 93.6%
Non-cash warrant fair value loss of $10.35M for 9M 2024
Cash balance reduced to $8M after large capital payments
positive_highlights: Revenues up 120% to $32.9M for 9M 2024; adjusted net income up 106%
Fleet capacity tripled since inception to 213,000 dwt with no bank debt
TCE up 24% YoY to $23,000 per day
summary: C3is reported strong Q3 FY2024 results with nine-month voyage revenues of $32.9 million, up 120% YoY, adjusted net income of $7.7 million (up 106%) and adjusted EBITDA of $13.5 million (up 92%). The company took delivery of its fourth vessel, the Eco Spitfire, increasing fleet capacity by 234% since inception, and has no bank debt. Fleet utilization was 90.6% for the nine months, slightly down from 93.6% last year. Management remains cautious on geopolitical and tariff risks but expresses confidence in sustained growth and market conditions.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to $6.9 million from $4.4 million in Q3 2023, with basic loss per share increasing to $0.31 from $0.20
U.S. cinema revenue declined 19% year over year, driven by a 10% screen count reduction and a 32% drop in specialty circuit box office
Cash used in operations increased to $11.8 million for the nine months, and cash balance stood at $10.1 million against $215 million in total borrowings
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA turned positive at $2.9 million, the first positive result in four quarters
Global operating loss narrowed to $246,000 from a $4.35 million loss in Q2 2024
Australian cinema revenue reached a record AUD37 million for a third quarter, with highest-ever F&B spend per patron
summary: Reading International reported Q3 2024 total revenue of $60.1 million, down 9.8% year over year but up 28% sequentially from Q2. The company posted a net loss of $6.9 million (-$0.31 per share) versus a $4.4 million loss in Q3 2023, with global operating loss narrowing to $246,000 and adjusted EBITDA turning positive at $2.9 million. U.S. cinema revenue fell 19%, Australia rose 2%, and New Zealand declined 11%, while real estate operating income rose 52% to $1.4 million. No formal guidance was provided; management pointed to a stronger 2025 film slate and ongoing asset sales to reduce debt, with liquidity pressure remaining a key concern.

negative_highlights: Q4 bookings at $24,630/day are about $5,000 below Q3's $22,000 fleet average (and MR rates)
Q3 was sequentially lower than Q2 in both product tanker and dry bulk segments on softer charter rates
Asset values near ten-year highs have made accretive MR acquisitions difficult; no compelling opportunities identified
positive_highlights: TCE revenues rose to $11.7 million, up about 24-25% YoY
MR daily TCE improved 6% YoY to $29,826
Net income of $3.6 million vs $3.1 million a year ago; adjusted EBITDA $6.7 million, up $1.2 million
summary: Pyxus Tankers reported Q3 2024 TCE revenues of $11.7 million, up roughly 24-25% year over year, with adjusted EBITDA of $6.7 million and net income of $3.6 million ($0.34 basic / $0.31 diluted EPS) versus $3.1 million a year earlier. Fleet average TCE was about $22,000/day, with MRs at $29,826/day (up 6% YoY) and dry bulkers at $13,841/day. Results were sequentially lower than Q2 in both segments on softer charter rates. Forward bookings show Q4 TCE rates below Q3: 69% of product tanker days booked at $24,630/day (about $5,000 lower) and 65% of bulker days at $13,190/day (nearly 5% lower). Management struck a guardedly optimistic tone, citing a manageable order book and supportive long-term fundamentals, while noting elevated asset prices have limited acquisition opportunities and that they continue watching back stock and amortizing debt.

negative_highlights: Net sales declined slightly from Q2 due to limited inventory caused by liquidity challenges.
The company remains in a legal struggle regarding the ABG Tapout lawsuit after deciding not to continue with that license.
Funding inflows have been delayed, impacting working capital and acquisition timelines.
positive_highlights: Gross margins expanded significantly to 30% from 23% in the prior quarter.
EBITDA loss narrowed to $1.7 million from $2.2 million in Q2, driven by margin improvement and lower SG&A spending.
Cash balance improved to $457,000 compared to a nominal amount at the end of Q2.
summary: Q3 FY2024 net sales were $381,000, down slightly from Q2 2024 due to liquidity constraints limiting inventory and sales. Gross margins improved significantly to 30% (up from 23% in Q2) driven by lower wine costs and the restart of the high-margin Qplash resale business. The company raised approximately $8 million in capital since August but continues to face headwinds regarding funding timing and a technical default on a note.

negative_highlights: Time charter equivalent dropped significantly to $15,353 per day compared to $15,800 in the same period last year.
Operating expenses increased to approximately $5,904 from $5,621 due to higher fuel costs and other operational pressures.
Smaller segments weakened significantly while Capesize strength was insufficient to offset broader market declines.
positive_highlights: Fleet utilization reached a high of 99.7% in the nine-month period ending September 30, highlighting effective vessel management.
The company successfully secured favorable time charters for nine vessels during Q3, achieving an overall average rate higher than previous fixtures despite market disconnects.
Balance sheet remains robust with cash and restricted cash increasing to $186.8 million from $161 million in December.
summary: Diana Shipping reported a miss in Q3 FY2024 with time charter revenues declining to $57.5 million from $62.1 million and net income falling to $3.7 million from $7.4 million the prior year, driven by lower rates on smaller segments despite strength in Capesize vessels. Management provided no specific forward guidance but noted that secured revenue for 2024 covers only 78% of remaining days while 2025 outlook remains uncertain due to supply growth outpacing demand and geopolitical risks like the Red Sea disruption.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA remains negative at $2.8 million, though improving towards the target of breakeven by end of 2026.
Integration delays for certain major airline partners due to IT challenges on their side are expected in Q4.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew at fastest pace since IPO with a 29% YoY increase in Platform revenue to $2.3 million.
Adjusted EBITDA improved significantly by $1.3M year-over-year, outperforming guidance range of negative $3.4m to -$3.3m.
Gross margins expanded materially with IFRS gross margin rising 10 percentage points YoY from 54.9% to 65%.
summary: Freightos reported Q3 FY24 revenue of $6.2 million (up 21% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of negative $2.8 million, beating guidance by outperforming the range of -$3.4M to -$3.3M. Management raised full-year transaction volume guidance upwards while narrowing ranges for Gross Booking Value ($257m-$265m) and Revenue ($6.4m-$6.5m). The quarter highlighted record transactions, strong platform growth driven by elevated market rates (air cargo up 11% volumes), and successful integration of the Shipsta acquisition.

negative_highlights: Cash burn of $596 million in Q3 against $79 million in ending cash, leaving liquidity dependent on the announced $3.5 billion related-party capital injection through 2026
ASP fell over 10% to $21,000 from $24,000 in Q2 as VF 3 entered the mix, with management expecting ASP to remain range-bound
Only 55% of the 80,000 delivery target was achieved through nine months, requiring roughly 40,000 deliveries in Q4, and formal 2025 guidance was deferred
positive_highlights: Gross loss margin improved sharply to minus 24% from minus 62.7% in Q2 2024, driven by an 8.3% decline in unit bill-of-material costs and a 20.1% decline in unit production costs
EV deliveries rose 66% QoQ and 115% YoY to 21,912, with Vietnam retail sales up 504% YoY and VinFast becoming the top-note OEM in Vietnam
SG&A fell 10% QoQ and dropped to 28% of sales from 44% in Q2, and R&D declined 21% QoQ to 17% of sales
summary: VinFast reported Q3 2024 net revenue of $512 million, up 42% QoQ and 49% YoY, with EV deliveries of 21,912 up 66% QoQ and 115% YoY. Gross loss narrowed to $123 million (negative 24% margin) from a negative 62.7% margin in Q2, and net loss improved 29% QoQ to $550 million. Management reiterated the 80,000 full-year 2024 delivery target, citing October and November momentum, and disclosed a $3.5 billion capital injection from Vingroup and founder Pham Nhat Vuong through 2026; formal 2025 guidance was deferred to year-end. Q3 ended with only $79 million in cash plus $968 million in credit facilities against $596 million of quarterly cash burn.

negative_highlights: FY2024 revenue guidance cut to $20M from prior $24M, driven by reduced BARDA development services revenue and DoD contribution postponed to 2026
Q3 revenue declined to $4.4M from $4.8M and gross margin contracted to 16% from 19% on revenue mix
Nine-month net loss widened to $26.3M ($2.72/share) from $5M ($0.56/share), largely on warrant revaluation expenses tied to a 78% YTD share price increase
positive_highlights: FDA approved NexoBrid for pediatric use (newborn to 18 years), aligning the US label with the EU and Japan
Secured $25M PIPE led by Mölnlycke plus €16.25M in European Innovation Council funding for EscharEx in diabetic foot ulcers
New GMP manufacturing facility construction complete, commissioning underway, expected to increase manufacturing output six-fold by end-2025; Vericel reported 43% QoQ NexoBrid revenue growth
summary: Q3 2024 revenue fell to $4.4M from $4.8M a year earlier, with gross profit of $0.7M (16% of revenue) versus $0.9M (19%), and the company lowered full-year 2024 revenue guidance to $20M from a prior $24M. The cut reflects the FDA pediatric approval requiring no post-approval BARDA-funded activities and a Type C meeting that pushed temperature-stable NexoBrid clinical work with the US Army to 2026. Offsets include FDA pediatric approval, a Category III CPT code, WHO inclusion of enzymatic debridement, a $25M PIPE led by Mölnlycke, and €16.25M from the European Innovation Council for the EscharEx DFU program. NexoBrid demand is said to exceed manufacturing capacity, with the new facility targeted for full operation by end-2025 and a six-fold capacity increase.

negative_highlights: Q3 2024 revenue of $4,000 versus $43,000 in Q3 2023, with no deliveries planned or made to the largest customer
Nine-month revenue fell to $351,000 from $10.7 million, driven by the absence of the $10 million AbbVie milestone received in 2023
Nine-month cash used in operating activities rose to $10.6 million from $418,000 a year earlier, and Q3 gross loss widened to $268,000
positive_highlights: Preclinical breast implant study showed significant implant vascularization and native tissue ingrowth of about 1 cm per month at three months post-implementation
Cash and cash equivalents of $15.4 million expected to fund operations at least through the end of 2025
Company expects to supply rhCollagen to its largest customer in December 2024, and targets signing another collaboration agreement in 2025
summary: CollPlant reported Q3 2024 GAAP revenue of just $4,000 versus $43,000 a year earlier, as no rhCollagen deliveries were made to its largest customer during the quarter; nine-month revenue fell to $351,000 from $10.7 million because 2023 included a $10 million AbbVie milestone payment. Q3 GAAP net loss was $4.3 million ($0.38 per share), with gross loss of $268,000 and nine-month operating cash use of $10.6 million, leaving $15.4 million in cash and a runway into at least the end of 2025. Management gave no numerical guidance but said it aims to sign another collaboration agreement in 2025 and is preparing a December 2024 rhCollagen delivery to its largest customer. Preclinical breast implant data at three months showed vascularization and tissue ingrowth of roughly one centimeter per month.

negative_highlights: Daily time charter equivalent declined 37% QoQ to $22,000
Operational utilization was only 65.6%, burdened by drydocking and the idling of the Magic Wand for the entire quarter
Global tanker ton-mile demand fell 4.8% and spot rates for product tankers fell 57% QoQ; management expects Q4 rates below last year's levels
positive_highlights: Adjusted net income rose 142% YoY to $10.9 million, despite a weak market
Cash position of $200 million with zero debt and $68 million operating cash flow in the first nine months
summary: Imperial Petroleum reported Q3 2024 revenue of $33 million, up 12.2% YoY, net income of $10.1 million ($0.29 EPS), and adjusted net income of $10.9 million (up 142% YoY). However, daily time charter equivalent fell 37% to $22,000 from the prior quarter, operational utilization was only 65.6%, and management does not expect Q4 to match prior-year levels, citing weak spot rates for product tankers down 57% QoQ. The company maintains a strong liquidity position with $200 million in cash, zero debt, and $68 million in nine-month operating cash flow, but provided no formal guidance for the coming quarter.

negative_highlights: Inventory write-downs of $28.5 million on the 2023-2024 harvest and $19.5 million on the 2024-2025 harvest due to lower pound solids from reduced Early, Mid-Season and Valencia production.
Management provided no fiscal 2025 forecast, stating it cannot forecast crop size or expected revenues, and said fiscal 2024 fruit production did not return to pre-Hurricane Ian levels.
Hurricane Milton in October 2024 caused measurable fruit drop in Polk and Hardee County groves, with the amount of additional drop not reliably estimable.
positive_highlights: New three-year Tropicana orange purchase agreement prices are approximately 33% to 50% higher over the contract life than last season's average price.

Balance sheet strengthened: the 17,229-acre Ranch sale for $77.6 million gross funded repayment of the credit line and $19.1 million of MetLife debt, cutting required principal payments through fiscal 2029 to under $1.5 million per year, and the MetLife revolving line maturity was extended to 2034.
Adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed to $3.8 million in FY2024 from $16.1 million in FY2023.
summary: FY2024 net income attributable to common stockholders was $7.0 million ($0.91/diluted share) versus $1.8 million ($0.24) a year earlier, but the increase came from an $81.4 million gain on land sales, while adjusted EBITDA remained a loss of $3.8 million (improved from a $16.1 million loss). The company recorded $28.5 million of inventory write-downs on the 2023-2024 harvest plus a $19.5 million impairment on the 2024-2025 harvest, and management explicitly declined to provide any fiscal 2025 forecast given no visibility on crop size following Hurricane Ian and Hurricane Milton's October 2024 fruit drop. The principal positive is a new three-year Tropicana orange supply agreement at prices roughly 33%-50% above last season's average, and a strengthened balance sheet from the Ranch sale proceeds and MetLife credit amendment.

negative_highlights: Q4 net income fell to $141,000 ($0.01/share) from $1.0 million ($0.10/share) in the prior-year quarter
Equity and earnings of unconsolidated affiliates fell $689,000 pre-tax as AFUDC from MVP construction ended

Interest expense rose $305,000 YoY on floating-rate debt supporting the MVP investment and the Roanoke Gas line of credit; Q4 volumes fell 5% on warm weather and a temporary large commercial customer shutdown
positive_highlights: Rate case settlement with staff provides a $4.08 million annual revenue increase reflecting a 9.9% ROE, with final approval expected in fiscal Q2
Full-year FY2024 net income grew $462,000 to $11.8 million ($1.16/share) despite inflation and higher interest costs
First MVP cash distribution of approximately $800,000 received in October, with about $3.2 million expected for FY2025 and dividend raised just under 4% to $0.83 annually
summary: Q4 FY2024 net income fell to $141,000 ($0.01/share) from $1.0 million ($0.10/share) a year ago, driven by a $689,000 decline in equity earnings from MVP (AFUDC ended with construction completion) and $305,000 higher interest expense. Full-year FY2024 net income rose to $11.8 million ($1.16/share) from $11.3 million ($1.14/share), and the rate case settlement with staff provides a $4.08 million annual revenue increase at a 9.9% ROE. FY2025 EPS guidance is $1.18-$1.25, modest growth off FY2024, with capital spending of $21.6 million and a resumed dividend increase of just under 4% to $0.83 annually.

negative_highlights: Operating cash flow decreased by approximately 12% year-over-year compared to prior period levels
No specific quantitative production guidance provided for FY2025, only qualitative statements about higher throughput in H2
Stock price declined following the earnings release despite record financial results and positive exploration news
positive_highlights: Mill expansion completed on time and on budget at approximately $6 million for capacity increase to 2,000 tonnes per day
Record revenue of over $40 million and record EBITDA achieved in FY2024 despite lower grade production late in the year
Discovery of Stamford Bridge shear zone with drill holes returning well over 150 gram tonne meters
summary: TRX Gold reported record revenue and EBITDA for FY2024 driven by a new mill expansion to 2,000 tonnes per day that came online in Q4, though operating cash flow decreased year-over-year. Management highlighted the discovery of the Stamford Bridge shear zone but provided no quantified production guidance or specific financial targets for 2025 beyond vague statements about higher throughput later in the year. The call was mixed as management defended its nondilutive growth strategy while acknowledging significant market headwinds, including a depressed stock price and challenges with their joint venture structure.

negative_highlights: Operating cash outflow was $7.9 million in Q2 due to a $17 million increase in accounts receivable
Gross margin is expected to decline to roughly 45% in Q3 due to amortization of tariff and freight variances and delayed promotions
Inventories increased $4.9 million and are expected to end FY2025 at approximately $110 million, higher than previously discussed
positive_highlights: Net sales rose 4% to $60.2 million, with growth across every sales channel and both product categories
Gross margin expanded 230 basis points to 48%
Adjusted EBITDAS increased 43% to $7.5 million and FY2025 adjusted EBITDAS guidance was raised to 6.6%-7.1% of sales
summary: American Outdoor Brands reported Q2 FY2025 net sales of $60.2 million, up 4% year over year, exceeding expectations, with GAAP EPS of $0.24 versus $0.01 and non-GAAP EPS of $0.37 versus $0.25. Gross margin expanded 230 basis points to 48%, and adjusted EBITDAS rose 43% to $7.5 million. Management raised FY2025 net sales guidance to $205-$210 million (3.2% growth at midpoint) from up to 2.5%, and increased adjusted EBITDAS guidance to 6.6%-7.1% of sales ($13.5-$15 million); it also provided initial FY2026 net sales guidance of $220-$230 million (8.4% growth at midpoint). The primary change versus the prior period is the improved outlook driven by strong line reviews, early load-in orders, and new product launches.

negative_highlights: Consolidated net sales fell 5.2% year over year to $55.7 million, with adjusted operating loss widening to $2.6 million from $2.2 million a year ago.
Upholstery fabrics sales declined 6.4% year over year and 10% sequentially, with a large customer's order reduction expected to also pressure Q3 sales.
Cash flow from operations and free cash flow were negative $2.6 million and negative $3.4 million for the first half, and management expects potential net debt in Q3.
positive_highlights: Mattress fabrics segment sales rose 7.1% sequentially to $30.1 million, driven by higher order levels and new program wins.
Mattress fabrics operating loss narrowed to $1.0 million from $3.5 million in Q1, a 70.7% sequential improvement.
Hospitality contract business remained solid, representing 35% of upholstery fabrics sales and offsetting residential weakness.
summary: Culp reported Q2 FY2025 net sales of $55.7 million, down 5.2% year over year, with a GAAP net loss of $5.6 million ($0.45 per diluted share) versus a $2.4 million loss in the prior-year period. Adjusted operating loss was $2.6 million, including $2.8 million in restructuring charges, though this improved sequentially from Q1. The mattress fabrics segment saw sequential sales growth of 7.1% and narrowed its operating loss to $1.0 million, while the upholstery fabrics segment was pressured by a significant temporary order reduction from a large residential customer and is expected to remain weak in Q3. Management provided limited guidance, expecting flat-to-slightly-down Q3 sales and a return to positive adjusted operating income in Q4, contingent on restructuring savings and no demand recovery.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA margin of 12.3% missed the 13-15% guidance on lower other revenue
Gross margin fell to 34.7% from 41.1% in Q2 and was flat YoY, held back by higher rental product costs
Average active subscribers declined 2.9% YoY to 130,796, and FY revenue guidance was narrowed to 2-4% from 2-6%
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA of $9.3 million (12.3% of revenue) versus $3.5 million (4.8%) a year ago
Free cash flow negative $3.4 million, a $14 million YoY improvement, with FY24 breakeven reiterated
Reserve orders up ~23% and new Reserve customers up ~36% YoY; Resale up 23% YoY
summary: Q3 revenue was $75.9 million, up 4.7% YoY and at the midpoint of the $75-77 million guide, a fourth consecutive quarter of accelerating growth. Adjusted EBITDA of $9.3 million (12.3% of revenue) came in below the 13-15% margin guidance on lower other revenue, while gross margin was flat YoY at 34.7% and down sharply from 41.1% in Q2. Free cash flow was negative $3.4 million versus negative $17.7 million a year ago, and management reiterated FY24 guidance for 2-4% revenue growth (narrowed from 2-6%), 15-16% adjusted EBITDA margin, and free cash flow breakeven. Reserve grew 21% YoY and Resale 23%, but average active subscribers fell 2.9% YoY even as ending subscribers returned to 0.6% growth.

negative_highlights: Total net sales fell 4.7% to $80.2 million, below expectations, with DTC down 8.3% and wholesale down 2.2%
Lower international wholesale reorders and Outlet sales negatively impacted sales growth by 300 basis points
Store closures added a 163 basis point headwind to DTC, and FY2024 inventory is now expected up high-single-digits
positive_highlights: Gross margin expanded to 50.0% from 44.2%, a ~580 basis point improvement, driven by ~480 basis points of lower product/freight costs and 80 basis points from reduced promotions
Operating income rose to $5.8 million from $2.8 million, with adjusted operating margin up ~350 basis points
Full-price customer file growth accelerated to high-single-digits, outperforming first-half trends
summary: Vince Holding reported Q3 FY2024 net sales of $80.2 million, down 4.7% year-over-year, below expectations due to lower international wholesale reorders and weaker Outlet sales, which together cost about 300 basis points of growth. Profitability was in line with guidance, driven by gross margin expansion of roughly 560 basis points to 50.0%, yielding operating income of $5.8 million and EPS of $0.34 versus $0.08 prior year. Q4 guidance calls for total net sales down mid-single-digits to up low-single-digits with operating margin up 200-300 basis points, while the full-year FY2024 outlook remains for low-single-digit sales decline and adjusted operating margin up 25-50 basis points versus 1.4% last year. Management noted the quarter was slightly below top-line expectations but ahead on transformation savings, and remains cautious on the shortened holiday season and consumer uncertainty.

negative_highlights: Gross margin down 2.9 points for the fiscal year
Q4 gross margin impacted by ~2.5 points promotional pricing, ~1 point inventory reserves
Operating expenses up $12.2 million, including $11.2 million goodwill impairment
positive_highlights: Inventory down $51.7 million from last year's Q4
Operational cost savings positively impacted gross margin by about 2 points
Company remains debt-free and continues paying a meaningful dividend
summary: Fiscal 2024 was challenged by soft consumer demand and competitive pressures, with gross margin down 2.9 points for the year. Q4 gross margin fell 6 points due to promotional pricing, mix, and inventory reserves, partially offset by cost savings. The company cited a goodwill impairment and other charges, but maintains a debt-free balance sheet and reduced inventory by $51.7 million.

negative_highlights: Consolidated revenue declined to $80.6 million from $115 million, with a $7.5 million net loss versus $6.1 million net income last year
Full-year guidance implies an operating loss of about $9 million and a $0.25 EPS loss compared with $0.54 EPS income in FY2024
Pura Vida revenue fell 42.9% to $10.1 million due to e-commerce and wholesale declines and higher digital marketing costs
positive_highlights: Vera Bradley gross margin expanded 80 basis points from reduced liquidation and clearance mix
Brand awareness rose 700 basis points, the first increase since 2021, with 35-54 customer acquisition up 9 points
The Urban Outfitters partnership expanded significantly for holiday and new outlet stores opened at Simon Premium outlets
summary: Q3 FY2025 consolidated revenue was $80.6 million versus $115 million a year ago, with a non-GAAP net loss of $7.5 million or $0.27 per diluted share versus $0.19 income last year. Vera Bradley Direct fell 27% to $52.5 million, Indirect fell 28% to $18 million, and Pura Vida dropped 42.9% to $10.1 million. Full-year guidance was cut to roughly $385 million in revenue, about 52.5% gross margin, roughly $9 million operating loss and about $0.25 EPS loss versus $0.54 EPS income in FY2024. The main swing factor was weaker clearance-unit migration into outlets and lower specialty and key-account orders, partly offset by Vera Bradley gross margin improving 80 basis points.

negative_highlights: Total company comparable sales decreased 0.8% in Q3, with softer full-price note in the direct channel and ~$800k negative impact from hurricanes
Q4 revenue guidance implies a 4%-6% decline, including an $8 million impact from the extra week in the prior year
Full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance was narrowed downward to $105-$107 million, representing a 5%-7% year-over-year decline
positive_highlights: Delivered a healthy gross margin of 71.4% despite targeted promotions and markdowns to normalize inventory
Adjusted EBITDA margin remained high at 17.7% of sales, marking a fourth consecutive year of high-teens margin
Board authorized a new $25 million share repurchase program, the first since the 2017 IPO
summary: J.Jill reported Q3 FY2024 sales of ~$151 million, up 0.3% YoY, with comps down 0.8% and adjusted EBITDA of $26.8 million (17.7% of sales). Gross margin was 71.4%, down 60 bps, due to promotions, markdowns, and elevated ocean freight costs. Q4 guidance calls for total revenue down 4%-6% (worsened by calendar shift and extra week), though comps are expected up 1%-3%; FY2024 adjusted EBITDA guidance was narrowed to $105-$107 million, reflecting a 5%-7% YoY decline. The company announced a $25 million share repurchase program and is managing through a soft full-price consumer environment.

negative_highlights: FY2025 adjusted EBITDA guidance is only low single-digit growth
Traditional search has seen a 'precipitous drop' over the last nine months, with Gartner predicting a 25% decline in Google general search
Print revenue is on a declining secular trend and remains a drag on overall margin
positive_highlights: Digital revenue reached 51% of total operating revenue, up 7 points year-over-year
Digital subscription revenue grew 41% on a same-store basis, reaching the 771,000 unit target
Amplify Digital Agency grew 21% in the quarter and is approaching $100 million annually
summary: Lee reported Q4 FY2024 with digital revenue reaching 51% of total operating revenue, a 7-point improvement year-over-year. Digital subscription revenue grew 41% same-store and Amplify Digital Agency grew 21% in the quarter, with digital subscriptions hitting the 771,000 unit target. FY2025 guidance calls for total digital revenue growth of 7% to 10% and adjusted EBITDA growth in the low single digits. The company announced AI partnerships with Perplexity, ProRata, and AWS, with early economics expected this fiscal year, while citing $82 million in FY2024 cost savings and $13 million in asset sales.

negative_highlights: Bombshells same-store sales fell 16.2% and segment operating income swung to a $2.5 million loss from $1.2 million income a year ago
Total company sales declined $2 million and adjusted EBITDA fell $2.3 million, with GAAP EPS at $0.03
Impairments totaled $12.5 million in the quarter and $38.5 million for the fiscal year, tied to underperforming locations and higher discount rates
positive_highlights: Nightclub same-store sales rose 2.2%, the second consecutive quarter of positive comps and the first back-to-back gain since the first half of fiscal 2023
Share count reduced 4.7% year-over-year to 8.955 million, with $7.8 million of buybacks in the quarter and a 16.7% dividend increase
Debt fell $7.2 million sequentially to a 3.28x debt-to-trailing-EBITDA ratio, with the Playmate note paid down $1.5 million early
summary: Q4 FY2024 total sales fell $2.0 million as nightclub revenue slipped $307,000 (with 2.2% same-store sales growth offset by 10 hurricane closure days) and Bombshells revenue fell $1.643 million on a 16.2% same-store sales decline; GAAP EPS was $0.03, though non-GAAP EPS rose $1.63, operating cash flow increased $3.5 million, free cash flow rose $2 million, and adjusted EBITDA declined $2.3 million. Management introduced a 'Back-to-the-Basics' five-year plan targeting $400 million revenue, $75 million free cash flow, 7.5 million shares or fewer, and about $6 million of acquired club EBITDA per year, funded 50/50 between club acquisitions/debt paydown and buybacks/dividends. Share count fell 4.7% to 8.955 million, a 16.7% dividend increase was declared, and four underperforming Bombshells locations plus the Denver food hall were exited. No formal numeric FY2025 guidance was issued beyond the 2029 plan targets.

negative_highlights: Revenue decreased by approximately $1.9 million or ~92% year-over-year to $170,528
Operating loss of $2.2 million compared to an operating profit of $52k in the prior year period
positive_highlights: Received FINRA approval for Netcapital Securities Inc. to operate as a registered broker-dealer
Broker-dealer license enables fee-based revenue models on larger fundraises (Reg A/Reg D) rather than flat fees
summary: Netcapital reported a significant miss in Q2 FY2025 with revenues dropping approximately $1.9 million (or ~92%) to $170k due to the cessation of consulting services for equity securities and an operating loss widening from profit to roughly $2.2 million. Management highlighted that while FINRA approval was received for their broker-dealer subsidiary, they are not providing specific revenue forecasts or timelines for new streams like Reg A offerings, noting a delay in launching the Templum ATS exchange due to regulatory details.

negative_highlights: Q4 product revenue fell to $1.3 million from $1.7 million a year earlier on a cancelled Zimmer Biomet purchase order
FY2024 net loss widened to $12.3 million from $11.9 million in FY2023
Cash and equivalents declined to $1.5 million from $5.3 million a year earlier, and working capital fell to $2.4 million
positive_highlights: FY2025 product revenue guidance of $8-10 million implies 132-190% growth over FY2024's $3.5 million
FY2025 gross margin guided to 47-51% versus 31% in FY2024
24 epilepsy centers requested proposals for OneRF, doubling from last quarter, with 12 patients treated across five centers
summary: Product revenue fell to $1.3 million in Q4 FY2024 from $1.7 million a year earlier, which management attributed to a cancelled Zimmer Biomet purchase order during the transition to the OneRF product line; full-year product revenue rose 77% to $3.5 million. FY2025 guidance calls for product revenue of $8-10 million (132-190% growth) and gross margins of 47-51%, up from 31% in FY2024, supported by the expanded Zimmer Biomet partnership that included a $3 million upfront license payment. The company ended the fiscal year with $1.5 million in cash, down from $5.3 million a year earlier, and a $12.3 million net loss. OneRF Ablation has been used in 12 patients across five centers, and 24 epilepsy centers have requested proposals, double last quarter's count.

negative_highlights: Backlog declined sequentially to about $3.6 million from prior levels
Cash, restricted cash, equivalents and note weakness in-term investments fell to $2.3 million from $3.3 million in the prior quarter
YTD operating cash burn remained $10.9 million despite the 30% improvement
positive_highlights: Revenue hit a record $2.4 million, up 170% year-over-year and 142% sequentially
Operating expenses cut 41% to $4.7 million and net loss narrowed 46% to $3.9 million
Latin America accounted for roughly one-third of revenue and the pipeline remained near $90 million
summary: Ocean Power Technologies reported record Q2 FY2025 revenue of $2.4 million, up 170% year-over-year and 142% sequentially, with Latin America contributing roughly one-third of sales. Operating expenses fell 41% to $4.7 million, net loss narrowed 46% to $3.9 million, and YTD operating cash use improved 30% to $10.9 million. Management reiterated its target of reaching positive cash flow by the end of calendar 2025 and cited a pipeline still near $90 million, though backlog slipped sequentially to about $3.6 million.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to a $5.4 million deficit in Q4 compared to a net income or smaller loss context due to impairment charges related to PP&E and goodwill recorded during the quarter.
The reported adjusted EBITDA of $5.9 million is lower than the full-year run rate implied by prior guidance, as it was impacted by one-time impairments not present in Q4 FY2023.
Canadian market growth forecast to slow to approximately 4% for fiscal 2025 due to regulatory headwinds and potential excise tax changes under a new Conservative government.
positive_highlights: Net revenue grew sequentially by 10% to $44.7 million driven by international sales and domestic recreational growth of 17.6%.
Adjusted gross margin expanded significantly year-over-year from 20% in Q4 FY2023 to 37% in Q4 FY2024 due to higher yields (record 187g/plant) and operational efficiencies.
Successfully achieved $9.1 million of the targeted $10 million annual cost savings, with synergies from the Motif acquisition expected to begin realization.
summary: Organigram reported Q4 FY2024 net revenue of $44.7 million (up 10% sequentially and 22% YoY) with adjusted gross margins expanding to 37%. Adjusted EBITDA was $5.9 million, representing a sequential increase but missing the implied full-year guidance trajectory due to significant impairment charges recorded in Q4 FY2023 that impacted year-over-year comparisons. Management reiterated fiscal 2025 expectations of stabilizing gross margins above 35% and generating positive adjusted EBITDA, noting that while they delivered on their annual cost savings target, the quarter's headline earnings were dragged down by prior period impairments.

negative_highlights: Cash balance remains thin at $266,000
Company is actively pursuing additional financing
Adjusted operating loss still significant at $3.6 million
positive_highlights: Q4 revenue grew 44% sequentially, exceeding guidance midpoint
Adjusted gross margin improved 16.3 points sequentially to 56.6%
LOI to acquire Spacecraft Components expected to be immediately accretive
summary: Q4 fiscal 2024 revenues were $2.95 million, up 44% sequentially and up 426% YoY, surpassing the midpoint of guidance. Adjusted gross margin improved 16.3 percentage points sequentially to 56.6%, with a full-year adjusted gross margin of 45%. The adjusted operating loss narrowed 12% sequentially to $3.6 million. Management guided Q1 FY2025 revenues to $3.05-3.15 million and announced a letter of intent to acquire Spacecraft Components, expected to be immediately accretive.

negative_highlights: Total revenue decreased by approximately $0.7 million due to the sale of the Lori Goldstein brand.
HSN revenues were impacted by two hurricanes, causing show cancellations and fulfillment disruptions.
GAAP net loss widened to $9.2 million compared to a prior year loss of $5.1 million.
positive_highlights: Non-GAAP net loss improved by approximately 56% year-over-year to $1.3 million.
C. Wonder brand retail sales grew 60% over last year despite September disruptions.
Judith Ripka business achieved nearly 500% year-over-year growth in the third quarter.
summary: Total revenue declined by approximately $0.7 million to $1.9 million in Q3 FY2024, driven by the sale of the Lori Goldstein brand and hurricane disruptions at HSN. The company reported a GAAP net loss of $9.2 million ($0.39/share) but achieved a non-GAAP net loss improvement of 56% to $1.3 million ($0.06/share). Management anticipates improved EBITDA in Q4 due to cost reductions and recovery from hurricane impacts, though they do not confirm a return to profitability.

negative_highlights: Q4 net loss applicable to common stock was $2.0 million, or $0.11 per diluted share
Q4 fresh lemon cartons sold fell to 470,000 from 550,000, with average price down to $17.95 from $20.39 per carton
FY2025 avocado volume guidance of 7–8 million pounds represents a significant decline from FY2024's 15.1 million pounds
positive_highlights: Full-year adjusted EBITDA swung to $26.7 million from a loss of $224,000 in FY2023
Full-year net revenue rose 6% to a record $191.5 million
Avocado volume of 15.1 million pounds in FY2024 was the most in almost 15 years
summary: Limoneira reported Q4 FY2024 net revenue up 6% to $43.9 million and full-year revenue up 6% to a record $191.5 million, with FY adjusted EBITDA swinging from a loss of $224,000 in FY2023 to $26.7 million in FY2024. Q4 net loss per diluted share narrowed to $0.11 from $0.20, and Q4 adjusted EBITDA improved to $1.2 million from a loss of $1.3 million. The company guided FY2025 fresh lemon volumes to 5.0–5.5 million cartons and avocado volumes to 7–8 million pounds, lower than FY2024's 15.1 million pounds due to the alternate-bearing nature of avocados. Management emphasized water monetization and real estate value, projecting $180 million in total Harvest joint-venture proceeds over seven fiscal years, with $15 million received in FY2024.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to $6.6 million ($0.25 loss per share) compared to net income of $14.2 million last year.
SG&A expenses increased to $11.1 million, driven by a $1.8 million rise in non-cash stock-based compensation.
Manufacturing gross profit decreased $0.5 million due to manufacturing variances.
positive_highlights: Revenues increased 8% YoY to $32.6 million driven by a $1.9 million increase in CDMO revenues and manufacturing timing.
Gross profit expanded $1.1 million YoY due to price increases and favorable sales mix, partially offset by manufacturing variances.
Adjusted EBITDA grew 20% sequentially to $6.5 million, reflecting improved leverage over overhead costs.
summary: Lifecore reported Q2 FY2025 revenues of $32.6 million, an 8% increase year-over-year, with gross profit rising to $11.1 million and adjusted EBITDA reaching $6.5 million. The company successfully closed a $24.3 million PIPE financing and restructured its credit facility, significantly strengthening its balance sheet. Management maintained full-year revenue guidance of $126.5 million to $130 million despite the strong quarter.

negative_highlights: The water utility segment was softer this quarter, which management attributed to the anticipated pullback in oil and gas activity and timing of tap fee monetization.
Oil and gas revenue was weaker as operators work through permits and pad site infrastructure for roughly 180 wells on Lowry Ranch, pushing more activity to late 2025 and beyond.
Commercial development at Sky Ranch is not expected to generate codified transactions until around 2026, with real monetization in 2027.
positive_highlights: Net income nearly doubled year over year to almost $4 million, with EPS of $0.16, up about 78% versus the prior-year quarter.
Gross margin came in at about 64% on $5.7 million of revenue, with oil and gas royalties contributing about $2.6 million from six new wells.
Tap fees rose about 150% and recurring customer revenue grew about 12%, while rental income rose about 14%.
summary: Pure Cycle reported Q1 FY2025 record revenue of about $5.7 million, up nearly 7% year over year, gross profit of roughly $3.67 million at a 64% gross margin, and net income of almost $4 million or $0.16 per share, with EPS up about 78% year over year. Management said it remains on pace with prior FY2025 guidance of roughly $31 million in total revenue, about $23 million in gross profit, and $0.52 in EPS versus $0.48 in FY2024. Oil and gas royalties contributed about $2.6 million from six new wells, tap fees rose about 150%, customer revenue grew about 12%, and rental income rose about 14%. Water segment results were slightly weaker as anticipated due to timing of oil and gas activity, with operators expected to accelerate drilling in late 2025 through 2030.

negative_highlights: Franchise and royalty fees decreased to $1.1 million from $1.2 million in the prior period
Gross margins declined slightly to 10% driven by higher supply, third-party vendor, and labor costs
Total costs and expenses increased to $8.6 million compared to $8.5 million last year
positive_highlights: Total revenue grew year-over-year by approximately 2.6% to $7.9 million
EBITDA turned positive at $41,000 compared to negative $300,000 a year ago
Fulfilled nearly 100% of franchisee and specialty market demand during the holiday season
summary: Total revenue increased to $7.9 million from $7.7 million in the prior year period, while franchise and royalty fees declined slightly to $1.1 million from $1.2 million. Gross margins contracted marginally to 10% due to higher supply, vendor, and labor costs, resulting in a net loss of $0.8 million ($0.10-$0.11 per share). Management highlighted the launch of a new ERP system on January 6 and secured a $6 million credit facility but noted substantial work remains to accelerate growth.

negative_highlights: Loan shrinkage in Q4 driven by unscheduled principal payoffs from energy and hospitality exits totaling over $160 million for the full year
No M&A deals closed in 2024 despite active pursuit of opportunities, described as disappointing
Potential note weakness in-term pressure on NIM due to loan redeployment following excess liquidity
positive_highlights: NIM stability maintained through various rate cycles, currently at approximately 450 bps
C&I loan segment grew over 5% for the full year as a highlight of portfolio redeployment
Strong liquid position with two meaningful sources of additional liquidity including a second backstop
summary: Bank7 Corp reported Q4 FY2024 results where loan shrinkage in the energy and hospitality segments was driven by unscheduled principal payoffs from business exits rather than organic demand issues. Management noted that while deal flow slightly improved, they are drawing a hard line on new loan rates amidst uncertainty regarding Fed interest rate cuts which may cause NIM compression. The company highlighted strong capital levels and liquidity but admitted to missing M&A targets in 2024 with no material closures.

negative_highlights: Q3 financial statements do not reflect the €20.8M financing proceeds received just before quarter-end
Recorded a write-down of polymerization equipment purchased for the Ulsan project due to accounting rules, though physical assets remain in good standing
Canceled joint venture with SKGC and departure of Board member Jonghyuk following parent company reorganization
positive_highlights: Finalized €20.8M financing deal with Societe Generale including a $10M upfront payment and technology license for an European facility
Cash burn reduced to $2.8 million in Q3, below the prior quarter's $2.9 million run rate
India joint venture on track to break ground in Q2 2025 with engineering services revenue expected to start flowing back immediately
summary: Loop Industries reported a cash burn of $2.8 million in Q3 FY2025 and finalized the Reed transaction with Societe Generale for €20.8 million (€10M upfront) prior to quarter-end, which will be reflected in Q4 results rather than this period's financials. Management lowered its full-year head office expense guidance from $12 million ($1M/month) to a high watermark of $10 million due to reduced R&D and G&A costs as the production facility transitions out of testing phase. The company canceled its joint venture with SKGC in South Korea, citing strategic alignment toward low-cost manufacturing regions like India.

negative_highlights: Head grade profile was below average at approximately 1.25-1.29 g/t compared to 2.5 g/t in Q1 FY24
Recovery rates declined meaningfully due to the lower grade ore and higher proportion of waste rock processed during the strip campaign
Q2 production is expected to be slightly down as maintenance on ball mills occurs before returning to full capacity
positive_highlights: Processing cost per ton decreased significantly to $12.60 due to the expanded plant operating at capacity
Realized gold price of $2,653/oz was $700 higher than Q1 FY24, driving growth in revenue and EBITDA despite lower grades
Throughput increased by over 100% year-over-year to exceed 1,700 tons per day
summary: TRX reported Q1 FY2025 results where production was effectively flat year-over-year due to a lower grade profile (approx. 1.29 g/t) and reduced recovery rates during the first strip campaign of the expanded plant, though revenue grew on record gold prices ($2,653/oz). Management confirmed Q2 head grades will be slightly lower before improving in H2 as higher-grade ore blocks are accessed. The company highlighted a 100%+ increase in throughput to over 1,700 tons/day with processing costs per ton down by 111% year-over-year.

negative_highlights: $1.2 million loss recorded from note approximately $12 million of investment securities
Provision for credit losses increased to $1 million due to qualitative factors regarding debt service coverage ratios
New credit opportunities have slowed somewhat, requiring a more selective approach
positive_highlights: Net income beat the prior quarter at $7.1 million versus $6 million
Core deposit balances increased 8.3% in Q4, facilitating a reduction of over $200 million in expensive wholesale funding
Credit quality remains pristine with zero past dues over 30 days and only 0.26% on the watch list
summary: West Bancorporation reported a $1 million provision for credit losses in Q4 FY2024 and recorded a one-time $1.2 million loss on the sale of investment securities. Net income was $7.1 million compared to $6 million in the prior quarter, with net interest margin expanding seven basis points driven by deposit repricing following Fed rate cuts. Management declared a quarterly dividend of $0.25 and expressed confidence that 2025 improvement is already underway due to strong deposit gathering.

negative_highlights: Net charge-offs to average loans were 91 basis points, with $9.4M in charge-offs
Non-performing loans increased due to additions in franchise finance and small business lending
SBA gain on sale revenue dipped slightly due to timing of loan closings
positive_highlights: Net income and EPS up sequentially, with net interest income up 8% QoQ and 17% YoY
SBA originations up 45% YoY to $540M, targeting $600M in 2025
Full-year adjusted revenue growth of 30% outpaced expenses, creating operating leverage
summary: First Internet Bancorp reported Q4 2024 net income of $7.3M and diluted EPS of $0.83, up 5% and 4% sequentially, respectively. Net interest income grew 8% quarter-over-quarter and 17% year-over-year, with net interest margin expanding 5 basis points. The company took $9.4M in net charge-offs, largely in SBA and franchise finance, but non-performing loans remained low. Management guided to a strong 2025 with SBA originations target of $600M and expects earnings to reach around $4.20 per share for 2025, starting in the low-mid-$0.80 range in Q1.

negative_highlights: Tangible book value per share declined $0.09 to $10.81 on higher AOCI mark and increased share count
Swap fee income, a key driver with over $3 million booked in 2024, is expected to decline in 2025
A $650,000 provision was tied to a repossessed yacht and vessel relationship, and nonrecurring expenses reduced EPS by $0.04
positive_highlights: Diluted EPS more than doubled to $0.34 from $0.14 in Q4 2023; adjusted EPS was $0.38 excluding nonrecurring items
Net interest margin expanded 13 bps QoQ to 3.16% and 54 bps over three quarters
Board doubled the quarterly cash dividend to $0.10 per share
summary: USCB reported Q4 2024 net income of $6.9 million, or $0.34 per diluted share, up 153.7% from $0.14 in Q4 2023; adjusted EPS was $0.38 excluding over $1 million in nonrecurring expenses. Net interest margin rose 13 basis points quarter-over-quarter to 3.16% and 54 basis points over three quarters, while average loans grew 15.3% YoY and average deposits rose 11.8% YoY. The board doubled the quarterly dividend to $0.10 per share and management guided 2025 loan growth to high single-digits to low double-digits, with Q1 2025 expenses around $12 million before rising. NIM is expected to hover near current levels near term and expand in 2025 if the yield curve normalizes.

negative_highlights: Loan pipeline fell 11% to $245 million at quarter-end from September 30
Noninterest income declined to $2.2 million from $2.5 million in Q3, and management does not expect a significant increase entering 2025
Noninterest expenses rose to $19.1 million from $18.6 million in Q3 on higher salaries, branch activity and technology spend; effective tax rate steps up to 25-26% from a 23-24% run rate
positive_highlights: NIM expanded 6 bps to 3.54% as interest-bearing deposit costs fell 20 bps, outpacing an 11 bp decline in loan yields
Fourth-quarter ROAA rose to 1.10% from 0.88% in Q3 and 0.93% in the year-ago quarter
NPAs to total assets fell to 0.46% from 0.69% at year-end 2023, with net recoveries in Q4 and ACL coverage of nonperforming loans at 323%
summary: First Bank reported Q4 FY2024 net income of $10.5 million, or $0.41 per diluted share, with ROAA of 1.10% up from 0.88% in Q3 and 0.93% a year ago. Full-year net income was $42.2 million or $1.67 per diluted share, with ROAA of 1.15% and return on average tangible common equity of 12.5%. Loans grew 7.3% annualized in the quarter ($56.8 million) and 4% year-over-year, while net interest margin expanded 6 bps to 3.54% on a 20 bp decline in interest-bearing deposit costs. Management guided to flat-to-improving margin, a 25-26% effective tax rate (up from a 23-24% run rate due to the New Jersey corporate transit fee), roughly flat noninterest income to start 2025, and 2025 loan growth approximating the Q4 pace.

negative_highlights: Full impairment of the Venue capitalized intangible drove FY2024 EPS to -$1.60 and ROAE to -4.44%; impairment alone cost $2.14/share after tax
Credit actions cost $0.67/share, 24 bps of ROAA and 8 bps of NIM, with $4.5 million of net charge-offs and $2.9 million of additional provision
Venue has one fully live FinTech client that is onboarding slowly, and 2025 depends on an estimated $135 million of average deposits to reach profitability
positive_highlights: Non-performing assets reduced 62% over the year to $21.7 million, with principal loss of just 10% on loans resolved in 2024
Classified loans fell from 4.31% to 2.94% of total gross loans in the quarter, and 30-day past dues trended to virtually zero
Net interest income grew about 4-4.5% quarter-over-quarter in dollars, and $60 million of callable CDs were exercised, with $122 million more available to lower funding costs
summary: MainStreet Bancshares reported FY2024 EPS of -$1.60, ROAA of -0.47%, ROAE of -4.44% and NIM of 3.13%, with Q4 hit by a full impairment of the capitalized Venue software intangible ($2.14/share after tax for the year) plus $4.5 million of net charge-offs and $1.9 million of reversed interest income. Pre-impairment credit actions cost $0.67/share, 24 bps of ROAA and 8 bps of NIM; the impairment actually added $0.48 to tangible book value, which stood at $23.77. Management guides FY2025 to low-single-digit loan growth and a non-interest expense run rate of 83 bps per month (~$51.9 million base), describing that as roughly a 40% reduction in run rate versus 2024, with Venue estimated at $135 million of average deposits for the year. Non-performing assets fell 62% to $21.7 million and classified loans dropped from 4.31% to 2.94% of gross loans, while CRE concentration remained at 375% of capital, at the board limit.

negative_highlights: Revenue recognition delayed by a month due to a concentrate shipment sitting at port before year-end, impacting Q4 cash flow.
Refinancing of senior debt and Sprott facility repayment timeline is estimated at six to eight weeks, creating temporary uncertainty on the balance sheet structure.
positive_highlights: Record copper production of 11,320 tonnes achieved in Q4.
C1 cash costs dropped to a record low of US$1.66/lb, with an additional ~US$0.16/lb saving expected from January onwards due to TCRC improvements.
Net gearing delevered massively to 15% (down from 41%) with US$213 million in liquidity.
summary: MAC Copper reported Q4 FY2024 production of 11,320 tonnes at a grade of 4.1%, landing just above the mid-point of its prior year guidance. The company achieved record low C1 cash costs of US$1.66/lb and total cash costs of US$2.31/lb, driven by improved dilution control and favorable exchange rates. Management highlighted a significantly strengthened balance sheet with net gearing reduced to 15% and liquidity at US$213 million, while confirming the early repayment of Sprott debt and ongoing refinancing discussions.

negative_highlights: Reported pre-tax loss of $17.4 million for Q4 2024
Consumer loan cleanup included $20.8 million provision and $2.5 million interest reversal
Digital platform margin was only 140 bps (6.47% asset yield vs 5.07% deposit cost)
positive_highlights: Core bank loan pipeline doubled year over year; over 80% from new customers
Panacea loans grew to $435 million and funding to ~$100 million, with 30-40% growth rates
Pre-tax core profitability potential ~$10 million after removing one-time charges and drags
summary: Primis Financial reported a Q4 2024 pre-tax loss of $17.4 million, driven by a $20.8 million provision for the consumer loan book, $2.5 million interest reversal, and $1.25 million fraud losses. Excluding these and other non-recurring items, core pre-tax profit was approximately $6.2 million, with potential closer to $10 million after adjusting for temporary drags. Management repositioned the balance sheet by moving the consumer book to held for sale, watching the Life Premium Finance business, and reducing digital deposit rates, aiming for cleaner earnings and margin expansion to 3.25%-3.50% in 2025. Core bank loan pipeline doubled year over year, and Panacea grew to $435 million in loans with $100 million in low-cost funding.

negative_highlights: Gross profit declined 8% to $84 million due to lower margins on exiting brands and new/pre-owned pricing.
Net loss widened to $14 million ($0.81 per share) compared to a net loss of $8 million in the prior year period.
Sales in hurricane-impacted Florida areas were down mid-single digits, though difficult to quantify lost sales recouped.
positive_highlights: New unit sales significantly outpaced the industry, which was down approximately 14% in relevant categories.
Same-store sales increased 4%, with new boat units up double-digits (approx. 12-13%).
Inventory levels decreased year-over-year by over 9% to $637 million.
summary: Revenue increased 3% to $376 million and same-store sales rose 4%, driven by double-digit growth in new unit volumes despite a challenging industry environment. Gross profit declined 8% due to lower margins on exiting brands, while SG&A expenses decreased 1%. Management reaffirmed full-year guidance for total sales of $1.7 billion to $1.85 billion and adjusted EBITDA of $80 million to $110 million.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined 5.7%; e-commerce fell 8.3%, with OMS issues estimated to have cut e-commerce revenue by about $20M.
Adjusted EBITDA dropped to $116.3M from $130.1M, and full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance was reset to $65M-$75M.
Corporate gifting fell ~17.5% to about $70M from $84M, with lower AOV, fewer items per order, and weaker marketing efficiency in free/branded search channels.
positive_highlights: Gross margin of 43.3% held flat year over year (43.5% excluding OMS costs), recovering toward the low-40s historical average.
Wholesale gift basket business grew in the teens with a broader new mass/club retail customer base.
Adjusted operating expenses fell $2.9M to $239M on Work Smarter initiatives, and $25M term loan was prepaid with no revolver borrowings.
summary: Q2 FY2025 revenue declined 5.7% with e-commerce down 8.3%, AOV down 1.2%, and adjusted EBITDA falling to $116.3M from $130.1M. Management attributed the shortfall to softer consumer demand, a pullback in corporate gifting (roughly $70M vs $84M, down 17.5%), and an OMS implementation breakdown at Harry & David estimated to have cut e-commerce revenue by about $20M and EBITDA by roughly $6.3M, with about $8M of lost EBITDA from foregone revenue. Net interest income rose to $15.5 million from $14.8 million sequentially as NIM widened to 10.0% from 9.70%, but noninterest income fell to $5.6 million from $6.1 million. The provision for credit losses increased to $3.9 million from $2.2 million, net charge-offs rose to $3.2 million, and NPAs are expected to migrate roughly $12 million in Q1. Originations were $1.3 billion in Q4 and $5 billion for FY2024, up 16% YoY, with credit enhancement balances guided to rise $50 million-$100 million by the end of 2025.

summary: High Tide reported record Q4 FY2024 revenue of $138.3 million, up 9% year-over-year and 5% sequentially, with full-year revenue of $522.3 million up 7%. Adjusted EBITDA was $8.2 million, down 1% year-over-year and 14% sequentially, with adjusted EBITDA margin of 6% versus 6.6% a year ago, reflecting drag from 29 new store openings. Free cash flow was $5.9 million in Q4 (up 4% YoY) and $22 million for the year (up 217%), with cash reaching a record $47.3 million. The company guided to 20-30 new organic stores in 2025 and expected lower e-commerce gross margins from the global Cabana Club launch, offset by the accretive Purecan acquisition.

Credit card activities generated a $1.1 million pretax loss for 2024.

summary: GBFH reported Q4 2024 net income of $5.2 million ($0.36 per diluted share), up from $5.0 million in Q3, and full-year net income of $18.6 million ($1.37 per diluted share), a 71% year-over-year increase. Credit card transaction volume surged 272% quarter-over-quarter to $51.7 million, with the program achieving breakeven in Q4. Management noted NIM compression from accelerated CD costs but expects repricing benefits in Q1 2025. Nonperforming assets rose to $14.2 million, but most are SBA-guaranteed, and the bank remains confident in working through them.

Gross margin was negatively impacted by increased promotional pricing, unfavorable overhead absorption, and product mix. The company highlighted a $14 million acquisition in diving for vertical integration, progress in cost savings, and a debt-free balance sheet, but remains cautious about near-term market conditions.

summary: CVRx reported Q4 FY2024 total revenue of $15.3 million (up 36% YoY) and US Heart Failure revenue of $14.3 million (up 41%), driven by expansion to 223 active centers from 178 in the prior year. Gross margin was 83%, slightly down from 85% last year, while SG&A expenses rose 19% due to increased headcount and stock-based compensation. Management provided full-year 2025 revenue guidance of $63-65 million with gross margins expected between 83%-84%. The company noted a Q1 seasonality dip is anticipated but expects consistent growth thereafter.

summary: Aviat Networks reported Q2 FY2025 revenue of $118.2 million, up 26.2% year-over-year, with non-GAAP EPS of $0.82, adjusted EBITDA of $14.8 million (a record) and operating cash flow of $20.8 million, the best in at least seven years. Book-to-bill was 1.08 for the quarter, and the company reaffirmed its prior guidance, citing potential upside from U.S. Tier 1 recovery and Pasolink momentum.

Management cites continued inflationary pressure on COGS and a fluid tariff situation as ongoing risks.

China delivered over 50% revenue growth year-over-year with a 10-point market share gain despite macro headwinds.

Despite the top-line miss, management maintained adjusted EBITDA guidance at $40-$42 million, citing an expected improvement in margins as the company accelerates investments in high-margin recurring revenue streams.

The company identified $40 million in annualized cost reductions to execute by the end of Q2, closed over $5 million of asset sales in the quarter, and flagged an additional $25 million of non-core assets to monetize. The key change versus prior messaging is heavier emphasis on AI monetization and cost actions to back up unchanged guidance rather than any reported top-line improvement.

Management reaffirmed FY2025 EBITDA guidance of R900-1 billion and raised FY2026 guidance to R1.35 billion, citing a 42% YoY increase driven by organic growth and acquisitions.

summary: Universal Logistics Holdings reported Q4 FY2024 revenue of $465.1 million (up 19% YoY) and EPS of $0.77, beating consensus estimates driven by strong Contract Logistics growth (+52.7%) and specialized Trucking results. The company added six new hospital starts and two renewals, received CE Mark approval for LungFit PH in Europe, and expects sequential revenue growth through the year. Formal revenue guidance for fiscal 2026 will be provided in June; no specific quarterly guidance was given.

positive_highlights: Nightclub same-store sales rose 3.7% with total segment revenue up $0.7 million (1.1%)
