summary: Radiant reported Q2 FY2025 revenue of $264.5 million versus $201.1 million a year earlier, net income of $6.47 million (up 556.5% to $0.14 basic/$0.13 diluted), adjusted net income of $10.70 million (up 94.6%) and adjusted EBITDA of $12.02 million (up 55.9%) versus $7.71 million in the prior-year period. Management attributed the outperformance largely to project activity tied to Hurricane Milton (49 charter flights moving ~8 million units of IV fluid), plus a modest tariff-related pull-forward, while noting same-store results were 'relatively flat, best case flat.' The company explicitly cautioned that the quarter should not be annualized, citing soft freight markets, the seasonally weakest March quarter, and recently introduced tariffs on China, Mexico and Canada as near-term headwinds. No specific quantitative guidance was issued; Todd Macomber indicated Q3 would play out similar to last year with a potential uptick by Q4, and the company completed the acquisitions of Foundation Logistics, TCB Transportation and the conversion of Focus Logistics in the quarter, with no buyback activity.

negative_highlights: Organic net sales declined 7% year over year, led by a 9% decline in North America
Adjusted EBITDA fell to $38 million from $47 million, and adjusted EPS fell to $0.08 from $0.12
Full-year organic net sales guidance cut to down 2% to 4%, with adjusted EBITDA now expected flat
positive_highlights: Free cash flow of $25 million in the quarter vs. $15 million a year ago and a $17 million outflow in Q1
Net debt reduced by $12 million, with interest costs down 21% to $13 million
Away-from-home net sales grew 38% in North America and 52% internationally
summary: Hain Celestial reported fiscal Q2 2025 organic net sales down 7% year over year, with a five-point decline in volume/mix and a two-point decline in price, driven primarily by a 9% drop in North America; adjusted EBITDA fell to $38 million from $47 million, and adjusted EPS was $0.08 versus $0.12. Adjusted gross margin contracted about 60 bps to 22.9% on cost inflation and higher trade spend. Management lowered full-year guidance to organic net sales down 2% to 4% and adjusted EBITDA flat year over year, while still expecting H2 growth; they also pushed the sustainable 3%+ organic growth exit rate to fiscal 2027. Free cash flow was $25 million, and net debt was reduced by $12 million.

negative_highlights: Equity in earnings of unconsolidated affiliates fell to $854,000 pre-tax from $1.5 million, and management said the apples-to-oranges comparison will persist for two more quarters
Interest expense up $143,000 on higher line-of-credit balances and higher midstream debt rates
positive_highlights: Net income rose to $5.3 million ($0.51/share) from $5.0 million ($0.50) on higher Roanoke Gas margins from July rate increases
Total delivered volumes up 16% YoY and residential/small commercial volumes up 4% on 10% more heating degree days
Hearing examiner recommended the $4.08 million stipulated revenue requirement; first MVP cash distributions received (~$800,000 in October plus another quarterly distribution)
summary: Net income was $5.3 million or $0.51 per share versus $5.0 million or $0.50 a year ago, aided by July rate increases at Roanoke Gas that offset lower equity in earnings from MVP ($854K vs $1.5 million) and $143K higher interest expense. Total delivered gas volumes rose 16% on a fuel-switching transportation customer, with residential/small commercial volumes up 4% on 10% more heating degree days. FY2025 capital spending guidance held at ~$21.6 million ($21.5-22 million range) and the EPS forecast of $1.18-$1.25 was reaffirmed as unchanged. The hearing examiner context adoption of the $4.08 million stipulated rate increase, with a final commission order pending.

negative_highlights: Q3 revenue of $19.6M was down 24.6% YoY, below expectations
FY25 revenue outlook cut to $77-83M from prior expectations
Management and board taking 10% salary/retainer cuts and annual cost reductions planned
positive_highlights: Gross margin improved 490 basis points to 29.4% (second highest in 7 years)
Landed 7 new contracts with $100-200M revenue potential over 5 years
EV Charging revenue up 48% year-to-date and pipeline grew sequentially
summary: Q3 FY2025 revenue was $19.6M, down from $26M year-over-year, with results impacted by project timing delays and reduced lighting distribution activity. Gross margin improved 490 bps to 29.4%, and adjusted EBITDA was slightly positive. Management reduced FY25 revenue guidance to $77-83M and expects double-digit revenue growth and positive adjusted EBITDA in FY26, supported by $100-200M of new contracts and cost reductions. The company is reorganizing into two business units and management/board are taking 10% salary cuts.

negative_highlights: Full-year 2024 gold production at Mount Milligan was below guidance due to lower grades in phases six and nine
2025 consolidated AISC guidance of $1,400-1,500/oz is up from 2024 actual AISC of $1,148/oz
The Goldfield project was shelved after an impairment charge and does not meet near-term development thresholds
positive_highlights: Mount Milligan Q4 AISC fell 15% quarter-over-quarter to $1,114/oz, driven by lower sustaining capex
Q4 free cash flow was $47 million, with cash balance rising to $625 million and total liquidity over $1 billion
$88 million returned to shareholders in 2024 via $44 million in buybacks and $44 million in dividends
summary: Centerra Gold reported Q4 2024 adjusted net earnings of $37 million ($0.17/share), produced 73,000 oz gold and 12.8 Mlb copper, and generated $93 million operating cash flow ($47 million free cash flow). Full-year 2024 gold production of ~367,000 oz came in below the low end of guidance at Mount Milligan due to lower grades, with 2025 consolidated gold guidance of 270,000-310,000 oz and AISC of $1,400-1,500/oz, up from $1,148/oz in 2024. Mount Milligan gold guidance for 2025 is 165,000-185,000 oz, with a pre-feasibility study now targeted for Q3 2025, while the Goldfield resource was shelved after an impairment and Thompson Creek restart remains on track for first production in H2 2027. Earnings release preceded the call, but the transcript provides detailed figures and guidance.

negative_highlights: Gross loss of negative 72.7% due to a $19.5 million inventory reserve charge
Adjusted EBITDA loss widened to $22.1 million from $11.6 million a year ago
Go ESS storage business only 6% of sales, down from 9%, with weak demand and falling battery prices
positive_highlights: Revenue up 86.8% YoY and 21.3% sequentially to $17.3 million, fourth consecutive quarter of sequential growth
Excluding inventory charge, gross margin was 40.2% in Q4, up from 36.5% in Q3 (ex-reserve)
Predict Plus platform grew to 140,000 meters under management, ARR above $1 million
summary: Tigo Energy reported Q4 2024 revenue of $17.3 million, up 86.8% year over year and 21.3% sequentially, marking four consecutive quarters of sequential growth. However, the quarter included a $19.5 million inventory reserve charge, resulting in a gross loss of negative 72.7% and an operating loss of $24.1 million. Excluding the charge, gross margin was approximately 40%. The company guided Q1 2025 revenue to $17-19 million and full-year 2025 revenue to $85-100 million, expecting adjusted EBITDA profitability in the second half of 2025. Predict Plus ARR now exceeds $1 million, with 140,000 meters under management.

negative_highlights: Adjusted gross margin declined sequentially from 37% to 33% due to seasonally lower volume and competitive forces in the gummy category.
Edibles segment faced headwinds with market share declines attributed to low-cost single count competitors and price compression.
Net loss widened to $23 million (vs. $15.8M prior year), though adjusted net loss was manageable at $4.1 million after fair value adjustments.
positive_highlights: Net revenue increased 17% year-over-year driven by flagship brands and a 2.3x increase in international sales ($3.3M).
Adjusted gross margin expanded sequentially to 33%, with management reiterating stabilization around 35% for the full fiscal year.
Organigram achieved #1 market share position nationally in vapes (over 22%) and pre-rolls, expanding national market share by 600 bps YoY.
summary: Organigram reported Q1 FY2025 net revenue of $42.7 million (up 17% YoY) and adjusted gross margin expanding to 33%. The company reiterated fiscal guidance for margins stabilizing around 35%, noting that while the quarter was seasonally soft, profitability is expected to ramp significantly in H2 as Motif synergies flow through.

negative_highlights: Q4 underwriting income declined 13% YoY to $625 million due to cat losses
California wildfires expected to result in net losses of $450-550 million
Effective tax rate projected to rise to 16-18% in 2025 from 8.2% in 2024
positive_highlights: Net premium written up 17% YoY to $3.8 billion in Q4
Full-year operating ROE of 18.9% and net income ROE of 22.8%
Record reinsurance segment underwriting income of $1.2 billion for the year
summary: Arch Capital reported Q4 2024 net premium of $3.8B (up 17% YoY) but underwriting income fell 13% to $625M due to elevated catastrophe losses in the quarter. Full-year after-tax operating income was $3.5B, operating ROE 18.9%, and book value per share rose 13% to $53.11 after a $5 special dividend. Management guided to a 2025 cat load of 7-8% of net earned premium, a higher effective tax rate of 16-18% due to Bermuda's 15% corporate tax, and estimated $450-550M net losses from the California wildfires. Competitive pressures in public D&O and cyber, along with a modest increase in MI delinquencies, were balanced by record reinsurance underwriting income and strong investment income.

negative_highlights: Net income from continuing operations fell to $2.7 million from $8.7 million
Cash and cash equivalents dropped to $1.2 million from $3.3 million
Operating cash flow usage increased by $2.1 million
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 24.6% to $16.2 million
Received GMO safety certificate for BBL2-2 corn in May 2024
Gene-editing breakthrough published in Nature
summary: Origin Agritech reported fiscal 2024 revenue of $16.2 million, up 24.6% year-over-year, driven by higher corn seed volume. Net income from continuing operations fell to $2.7 million from $8.7 million, largely due to one-time gains in the prior year and increased G&A and R&D spending. Cash and cash equivalents declined to $1.2 million from $3.3 million, while operating cash flow used increased $2.1 million. Management outlined a three-phase strategy targeting cash flow breakeven by 2026, and highlighted a new GMO safety certificate and gene-editing breakthrough, but did not provide revised revenue guidance.

negative_highlights: Total revenue growth of 7% to $5.5 million is below the company's stated 10-20% full-year target, requiring a significant second-half acceleration
Recurring revenue grew only 5% to $5.4 million, and the recurring share of total revenue slipped to 98% from 99%
Sales and marketing expenses rose 15% and total opex rose 7%, matching or exceeding the 7% revenue growth rate
positive_highlights: Deferred revenue grew 70% to $4.2 million since June 2024, representing $1.7 million in incremental subscription revenue over the next 12 months
Cash from operations year-to-date was $5.3 million, up 117% from the prior-year period, with $28 million cash and no bank debt
GAAP EPS rose 14% to $0.08 and year-to-date EPS rose 21% to $0.17 basic, while net income to common shareholders grew 12%
summary: ReposiTrak reported Q2 FY2025 revenue up 7% to $5.5 million and GAAP EPS of $0.08, up 14% from $0.07, roughly in line with the company's baseline growth trajectory. Management guided to accelerating to double-digit revenue growth in the second half, bringing full-year growth to a 10-20% range, citing $4.2 million in deferred revenue (up 70% since June 2024) that will add ~$1.7 million of incremental subscription revenue over the next four quarters. The company also highlighted a 5,500-facility enrollment pipeline representing nearly $10 million in incremental annualized revenue over 18-24 months, while acknowledging a likely FDA enforcement delay that management views as favorable for orderly onboarding.

negative_highlights: Full-year revenue fell 4.3% YoY to $3.176 billion and finished below expectations
Government segment revenue fell ~10% and adjusted EBITDA dropped 35%, with margin down ~8 points
Full-year new business ACV declined 20% versus 2023; Q4 ACV was flat and slightly below internal expectations
positive_highlights: Full-year adjusted EBITDA margin of 3.9% finished at the high end of expectations, with Q4 at 4%
Net ARR activity was positive at $92 million, helped by improved client retention
Net leverage reduced to 1.6 turns after $639 million of term loan prepayments and 52 million shares repurchased
summary: Conduent reported Q4 adjusted revenue of $800 million and full-year 2024 revenue of $3.176 billion, down 4.3% YoY and slightly below expectations; full-year adjusted EBITDA was $124 million at a 3.9% margin, at the high end of guidance. New business ACV was $137 million in Q4, flat YoY, and full-year ACV fell 20% versus 2023. 2025 guidance calls for revenue of $3.1-3.25 billion (roughly flat at the midpoint), adjusted EBITDA margin of 4.5-5.5%, and adjusted free cash flow of $0-40 million, with an exit-rate margin around 8%. The company framed 2024 as a trough and expects sequential improvement through 2025, aided by lapping government headwinds in mid-2025.

negative_highlights: Statutory capital declined by $300 million in TAC during Q4, with a $350 million negative impact from interest rates and a $200 million increase in asset adequacy testing reserves.
Estimated combined RBC ratio was approximately 400% at year-end, at the low end of the target range, requiring a $100 million capital contribution from the holding company.
positive_highlights: Record Shield annuity sales of $7.7 billion in 2024, up 12% year-over-year.
Life insurance sales grew 18% to $120 million for the full year.
Corporate expenses down over 7% year-over-year in 2024.
summary: Brighthouse Financial reported Q4 2024 adjusted earnings of $304 million, which included a $48 million unfavorable notable item; excluding that, adjusted earnings were $352 million, up from $243 million in Q3 2024 and $189 million in Q4 2023. However, statutory capital weakened: total adjusted capital fell $300 million in the quarter to $5.4 billion, and the estimated combined RBC ratio was approximately 400% at year-end, at the low end of the 400%-450% target, requiring a $100 million capital contribution from the holding company. Management guided that RBC is expected to be 'relatively stable' over the next few years without additional holding company support, but they delayed the long-term free cash flow projections, which were previously expected by mid-2025.

negative_highlights: Total revenues declined 4% year over year due to lower realized commodity prices down approximately 12%.
Temporary downtime of ~90 BOE per day occurred at Williston and Chaveroo, with natural gas sales impacted by a compressor failure.
Production at the three producing wells in Block One was temporarily reduced by gas interference issues requiring pump adjustments.
positive_highlights: Total production grew 10% year over year to 6,935 BOE per day despite lower commodity prices and temporary downtime.
SCOOP/STACK wells are performing approximately 10% above type curves for gas volumes.
Company maintains a strong financial position with $22.2 million in total liquidity including cash on hand.
summary: Evolution Petroleum reported Q2 FY2025 total revenues of $20.3 million, a decline of approximately 4% year over year driven by realized commodity prices down roughly 12%. Production volumes increased 10% to 6,935 BOE per day due to acquisitions and new wells, partially offsetting the price drop but resulting in lower overall revenue. Management maintained its quarterly dividend at $0.12 per share for the 46th consecutive quarter while noting temporary production downtime issues resolved by January.

negative_highlights: Product revenue is expected to decline sequentially in Q2 FY2025 after the initial stocking order to Zimmer Biomet was completed in December
Cash and cash equivalents fell to $1.1 million as of December 31, 2024 from $1.5 million as of September 30, 2024
Full-year gross margin guidance of 47-51% is well below the 58.9% reported in Q1, implying margin compression in coming quarters
positive_highlights: Product revenue rose 235% YoY to a record $3.3 million, with product gross margin expanding to 58.9% from 27.2%
Q1 net income of $1.8 million ($0.06 per share) versus a $3.3 million net loss ($0.14 per share) in the prior-year quarter, aided by a $3 million Zimmer Biomet license payment

Total operating expenses fell 12% YoY to $3.2 million, and the company expects a 510(k) submission for its trigeminal nerve RF ablation system in H1 calendar 2025, a potential revenue driver not in guidance
summary: NeuroOne reported record Q1 FY2025 product revenue of $3.3 million, up 235% from $1 million a year earlier, plus $3 million in license revenue from the expanded Zimmer Biomet agreement, for total revenue of $6.3 million. Product gross margin expanded to 58.9% from 27.2%, and the company posted net income of $1.8 million ($0.06 per share) versus a $3.3 million net loss ($0.14 per share) a year ago. Management reiterated FY2025 guidance of $8-10 million product revenue (132-190% growth) and 47-51% product gross margin, but noted product revenue will decline sequentially in Q2 after the initial Zimmer stocking order before ramping through the year. Cash stood at $1.1 million with no debt, and the company regained NASDAQ share price compliance.

negative_highlights: GAAP net loss of $10.7 million ($0.20 per share) and distributable earnings loss of $8.3 million ($0.15 per share) in Q4.
Realized losses of $18 million ($0.33 per share) included the full write-off of a subordinated loan on a New Jersey office property and loss on sale of a California REO.
Outstanding principal balance of risk-rated 4 and 5 loans increased by 12% or $37 million in Q4 due to reclassification of a Massachusetts life science loan.
positive_highlights: Collected $350 million in repayments for full year 2024, nearly double the amount collected in 2023.
Reduced outstanding borrowings by $172 million in Q4 and $444 million (27%) for the full year of 2024.
Net debt-to-equity ratio excluding CECL declined to 1.6 times at year-end, down from 1.9 times in 2023.
summary: ACRE reported a GAAP net loss of $10.7 million ($0.20 per share) and a distributable earnings loss of $8.3 million ($0.15 per share) for Q4 FY2024, driven by an $18 million realized loss on the write-off of a New Jersey office loan and the sale of a California REO property. Full year 2024 results showed a GAAP net loss of $35 million ($0.64 per share) and distributable earnings loss of $44.6 million ($0.82 per share). Management highlighted strong repayment collections totaling $350 million for the full year (nearly double 2023 levels) and a significant reduction in leverage, with net debt-to-equity declining to 1.6x. The Board adjusted the quarterly dividend to $0.15 per share to align with strategic objectives of resolving underperforming assets.

negative_highlights: AUM experienced $0.8 billion of net outflows over the year, offset only by $1.9 billion of market appreciation
Full-year economic earnings fell to $7.0 million ($0.82/share) from $18.3 million ($2.26/share) in 2023
Intermediary channel saw net outflows of $229 million
positive_highlights: Institutional team won and funded eight mandates totaling over $600 million, roughly double the prior year
Q4 revenues rose to $25.6 million from $23.7 million in Q3 and $23.2 million a year earlier
MDST ETF reached $73 million in assets by year-end, far exceeding its first-year target
summary: Westwood reported Q4 2024 total revenues of $25.6 million, up from $23.7 million in Q3 and $23.2 million in the prior-year quarter, driven by higher average AUM and performance fees. Q4 comprehensive income was $2.1 million ($0.24/share) versus a prior-year net loss of $2.6 million, and non-GAAP economic earnings were $3.4 million ($0.39/share). Full-year economic earnings fell to $7.0 million ($0.82/share) from $18.3 million ($2.26/share) in 2023, and AUM saw $0.8 billion of net outflows offset by $1.9 billion of market appreciation, ending at $17.6 billion in total AUM and advisement. The board declared a $0.15/share dividend, and management cited a robust institutional pipeline, ETF launches, and a cautiously optimistic 2025 outlook without providing explicit numeric guidance.

negative_highlights: Only 1 of 3 enrolled patients received Hemopurifier treatment; two were excluded by pre-specified stopping criteria (one responded to anti-PD-1 alone, one had toxicity)
Cash balance of ~$4.8 million leaves limited runway
India trial remains blocked pending CDSCO approval amid new documentation requirements, and no enrollment timeline was given for reaching the 9-18 treated-patient target
positive_highlights: Operating expenses fell ~50% to $1.8 million from $3.6 million, driven by a $1.3 million payroll reduction and $300,000 lower professional fees
Net loss narrowed to ~$1.8 million from ~$3.5 million year over year

HREC and RGO approved the protocol amendment at all three Australian sites; Royal Adelaide and Pindara can enroll now and Genesis Care/Royal North Shore begins enrollment after a Feb 14 site initiation visit
summary: Aethlon reported Q3 FY2025 operating expenses of $1.8 million, down ~50% from $3.6 million a year earlier, and net loss narrowed to ~$1.8 million from ~$3.5 million, with cash of ~$4.8 million as of December 31, 2024. The clinical update showed only one of three enrolled patients actually received Hemopurifier treatment; a protocol amendment approved at all three Australian sites removes the two-month run-in and broadens eligibility to speed enrollment, while the India trial still awaits CDSCO approval. No revenue or earnings guidance was given, and management said opex will ramp up as trials progress, so the cost decline is not a durable run rate.

negative_highlights: No product sales recorded in the quarter versus $4.3 million in gross product sales and $2 million in net product revenue in the prior-year quarter
Cash and cash equivalents declined to $3.4 million at December 31, 2024 from $9.5 million at June 30, 2024
Total operating expenses rose to $2.6 million net of a $2.5 million gain from $0.9 million net of a $7.8 million gain a year earlier, as the CoSette gain shrank
positive_highlights: Net loss narrowed to $2.4 million from $7.8 million in the prior-year quarter, driven by a warrant liability fair value change and the elimination of leasing product revenue and note expenses
Net cash used in operations fell to $4.8 million from $10.5 million in the prior-year period
Cash of $3.4 million at December 31, 2024 excludes $4.3 million of net proceeds raised in an equity offering that closed in February 2025
summary: Palatin reported no product revenue in Q2 FY2025 versus $4.3 million in gross product sales and $2 million in net product revenue a year earlier, reflecting the completed sale of female sexual dysfunction rights to CoSette. Operating expenses were $2.6 million net of a $2.5 million gain on the sale versus $0.9 million net of a $7.8 million gain in the prior-year quarter, and the net loss narrowed to $2.4 million from $7.8 million. Cash and cash equivalents stood at $3.4 million as of December 31, 2024, excluding $4.3 million of net proceeds from an equity offering that closed in February 2025, and management said it is actively engaged with multiple potential funding sources. No formal financial guidance was issued; the principal catalysts are Phase 2 data for the obesity combination study later this month and for the ocular program in Q1 calendar 2025.

negative_highlights: Soda ash market conditions expected to remain challenging in early 2025
Producer mechanical issues in offshore fields continue to impact volumes
Cash costs of running business remain high at $600-625 million per year
positive_highlights: Offshore segment expected to deliver upwards of 20+% sequential growth in 2025
Marine transportation segment expected to deliver record results in 2025
Management sees significant supply rationalization in soda ash, which could improve prices
summary: Genesis Energy reported Q4 2024 results, highlighting that major offshore projects (Shenandoah and Salamanca) remain on schedule for first production in Q2 2025, which is expected to drive over 20% sequential growth in offshore segment margins. Management guided 2025 adjusted EBITDA to around $700 million and 2026 to around $800 million, with cash costs of $600-625 million. Soda ash market remains challenged, but management sees supply rationalizations (UK, Spain, Poland) as positive for future price recovery. Marine transportation is expected to deliver record results in 2025 due to strong market fundamentals.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to $14.1 million from $6.4 million year-over-year due to increased R&D spending.
R&D expenses rose to $11.3 million, up from $4.5 million in the prior year period.
positive_highlights: Top-line data from Palisade 3 and Palisade 4 expected later in 2025 with no change to guidance.
Positive efficacy signals observed across five clinical-stage pherine product candidates including fasedienol, itruvone, and PH80.
Enhanced internal execution capabilities reducing reliance on CRO surveillance for Phase 3 trials.
summary: VistaGen Therapeutics reported a net loss of $14.1 million for the third quarter ended December 31, 2024, compared to $6.4 million in the prior year period, driven by increased R&D expenses of $11.3 million primarily due to its Palisade Phase 3 program for fasedienol. Management provided no financial guidance but confirmed that top-line data from both Palisade 3 and Palisade 4 are expected later in 2025 with no change to prior expectations. The company highlighted positive efficacy signals across five clinical-stage pherine product candidates, including the recent initiation of a repeat-dose study for fasedienol.

negative_highlights: Net revenue declined to $393.7M from $425.6M in the prior-year quarter
Net income fell to $7.1M from $8.9M, and adjusted EBITDA declined to $16.1M from $17.9M
Gross margin of 10.7% reflected unfavorable product mix and promotional activity
positive_highlights: Physical movie sales rose 23% year-over-year to $86M, and vinyl grew 12% to $109M
Operating expenses declined 6% to $27.5M with distribution and fulfillment costs down 18% on automation and the Minnesota warehouse closure
Revolver balance reduced $31M year-over-year to $70M, raising liquidity availability to $50M from $19M
summary: Q2 FY25 net revenue fell to $393.7M from $425.6M a year ago, with gross margin of 10.7% and net income of $7.1M versus $8.9M, the latter dented by a $2.5M noncash warrant revaluation; adjusted EBITDA was $16.1M versus $17.9M. Offsetting the top-line decline, vinyl rose 12% to $109M and physical movie sales surged 23% to $86M, while operating expenses fell 6% to $27.5M and distribution/fulfillment costs dropped 18% on automation and warehouse consolidation. The revolver balance was cut $31M year-over-year to $70M, lifting availability to $50M from $19M. No formal guidance was issued, but management cited the new exclusive Paramount home entertainment license (Gladiator 2 street date March 4 with a 150,000-unit initial forecast) and the Handmade by Robots acquisition as catalysts for 2025.

negative_highlights: Full-year revenue guidance lowered to $88.5–$90 million from $92–$93 million
Non-GAAP EPS guidance cut to $0.14–$0.16 from $0.17–$0.20
Non-GAAP net income fell to $1.3 million from $3.4 million, and adjusted EBITDA margin contracted to 7% from 16%
positive_highlights: AI knowledge hub ARR increased 17% year over year
AI knowledge customers represented 55% of total SaaS ARR, up from 46% a year ago
Total SaaS ARR rose 2% sequentially and SaaS revenue was ahead of internal expectations
summary: eGain reported Q2 FY2025 total revenue of $22.4 million, down 6% year over year, within guidance. Non-GAAP net income fell to $1.3 million or $0.05 per share from $3.4 million or $0.11 per share a year ago, with adjusted EBITDA margin down to 7% from 16%. Management lowered full-year revenue guidance to $88.5–$90 million from $92–$93 million and cut non-GAAP EPS guidance to $0.14–$0.16 from $0.17–$0.20, citing a $2 million reduction in professional services revenue and longer sales cycles for large AI knowledge deals. Offsetting the weakness, AI knowledge hub ARR rose 17% year over year and accounted for 55% of total SaaS ARR, up from 46% a year earlier.

negative_highlights: GAAP net loss of $29 million driven by the one-time debt restructuring charge of $41 million
Fourth quarter adjusted ROE was negative 25% due to the non-recurring costs
positive_highlights: Adjusted pretax income of $90 million in full year 2024, up 84% versus the prior year
Total servicing additions increased by 70% over 2023 to reach $25 billion in Q4 alone
Raised adjusted ROE guidance for 2025 to a range of 16% to 18%
summary: Onity Group reported fourth quarter results consistent with prior guidance, delivering adjusted pretax income of $11 million and full-year adjusted ROE of 20%, which exceeded the previous year's result but was in line with current expectations. The GAAP net loss for the quarter included a one-time charge of $41 million related to corporate debt restructuring costs. Management raised its adjusted ROE guidance range for 2025 from prior levels (implied below) to 16% to 18%, citing improved balance sheet positioning and deleveraging progress.

negative_highlights: Ting recorded a $28.2 million one-time restructuring and impairment charge in Q4
Wavelo Q4 revenue down 1.9% sequentially to $9.9 million
2025 guidance includes a $9 million one-time charge for winding down Verizon MVNO agreement
positive_highlights: Consolidated revenue up 19% YoY and Adjusted EBITDA more than doubled to $34.9 million in 2024
Ting improved Adjusted EBITDA from a $12.3 million loss to a $1.5 million loss in Q4, with December slightly positive
Wavelo Adjusted EBITDA for 2024 was $13.8 million, well above guidance of $8-10 million
summary: Tucows reported Q4 2024 consolidated revenue up 19% year-over-year, with Adjusted EBITDA of $34.9 million for the year, up 126% from $15.5 million in 2023. Excluding Ting, Adjusted EBITDA hit $57.4 million, above guidance. Ting reduced Adjusted EBITDA loss to $1.5 million in Q4 from $12.3 million a year ago, turning slightly positive in December. Management guided 2025 Adjusted EBITDA to approximately $56 million before a $9 million one-time Verizon wind-down charge, up 75% over 2024.

negative_highlights: Pound solids harvested fell to approximately 4.0 million from 4.7 million due to Hurricane Milton fruit drop
Net loss of $9.2 million (-$1.20 per diluted share) versus prior-year net income of $42.9 million
Management expects fiscal 2025 harvest volumes to be lower than fiscal 2024 and is exiting citrus production after the current crop
positive_highlights: Revenue increased 21% to $16.9 million from $14.0 million, driven by a 38.9% higher price per pound solid ($3.69 vs $2.66)
Adjusted EBITDA turned positive at $0.7 million versus a $2.3 million loss in the prior-year quarter
Expects ~$20 million of land sale proceeds in fiscal 2025 and $73.5 million of remaining credit availability
summary: Q1 FY2025 revenue rose 21% to $16.9 million from $14 million, but this was driven by a 38.9% higher price per pound solid ($3.69 vs $2.66) under a new Tropicana agreement, while pound solids harvested fell to 4.0 million from 4.7 million on Hurricane Milton fruit drop. The company reported a net loss of $9.2 million (-$1.20 per diluted share) versus last year's $42.9 million gain, which had included a $77 million Alico Ranch land sale; adjusted EBITDA improved to $0.7 million from a $2.3 million loss. Management reiterated its strategic wind-down of citrus operations after the current harvest, expects fiscal 2025 harvest volumes below 2024, and reiterated ~$20 million of land sale proceeds expected this fiscal year. Guidance implies a soft volume outlook with liquidity supported by land sales and $73.5 million of credit availability.

negative_highlights: Q4 revenues of $26.2 million fell $3.5 million year-over-year on lower market rates
Q4 net income of $3.9 million was eroded by a $3.3 million foreign exchange loss
Standard product tanker rates fell to about $22,000/day from roughly $33,000/day a year earlier, and Suezmax rates to about $30,000/day from near $60,000/day
positive_highlights: Full-year 2024 net income of $50.2 million, or $1.54 per share, with operating cash flow of roughly $78 million
Q4 operational utilization of 86% and time charter coverage up 180% year-over-year, cushioning weaker spot rates
Debt-free balance sheet with cash near $207 million (up 67% in 2024) generating $6.7 million of interest income
summary: Q4 2024 revenues came in at $26.2 million, down $3.5 million year-over-year on lower market rates, with net income of $3.9 million depressed by a $3.3 million non-operating FX loss; full-year 2024 net income was $50.2 million (EPS $1.54) and EBITDA $59.2 million. Q4 operational utilization was 86% and time charter coverage rose 180% YoY, offsetting weaker spot rates, while voyage costs fell 39% and running costs rose $1 million on a larger fleet. No formal numerical guidance was provided; management said the focus is on executing already-announced fleet growth, with the tanker Clean Imperial delivered in January 2025 bringing the fleet to 12 vessels and remaining 2025 TC coverage around 23%. The key change versus the prior year is a materially softer rate environment — product tanker rates fell from roughly $33,000/day to $22,000/day and Suezmax from about $60,000/day to near $30,000/day.

negative_highlights: GAAP net loss attributable to common shareholders was $8.6 million, or $1.32 basic loss per share, in Q3 FY2025.

Ben Liquidity interest income fell 5.7% sequentially to $11.3 million and the segment posted a $2.9 million operating loss, down from $2.9 million operating income in the prior quarter, due to higher loans on nonaccrual and intersegment credit losses.
Cash and cash equivalents were only $4.1 million against $122.9 million of total debt, and ExchangeTrust closings have been out of the market for roughly 15 months.
positive_highlights: Permanent equity improved from a deficit of $148.3 million at June 30, 2024 to positive $14.3 million at December 31, 2024, aided by a $35 million redesignation of preferred equity and a $160.5 million temporary-to-permanent reclassification.
Operating expenses excluding prior-period noncash goodwill impairment declined 38% to $13.9 million in Q3 FY2025 from $22.5 million a year earlier.
The BCH liquidation priority revision is estimated to create $9.2 million of pro forma tangible book value attributable to Ben's public common stockholders using December 31, 2024 financials.
summary: Beneficient reported Q3 FY2025 GAAP revenues of $4.4 million versus negative $10.2 million a year ago, driven by mark-to-market adjustments rather than operational growth, while GAAP net loss attributable to common shareholders was $8.6 million, or a basic loss per share of $1.32. Ben Liquidity interest income fell 5.7% sequentially to $11.3 million due to more loans on nonaccrual, and the segment swung to a $2.9 million operating loss from $2.9 million operating income in the prior quarter. Ben Custody revenue was flat sequentially at $5.4 million with NAV of assets in custody at $385.1 million, and total debt stood at $122.9 million against $4.1 million of cash as of December 31, 2024. Management offered no formal numerical guidance but stated it expects liquidity transaction closings to pick up after the BCH proxy vote and a better 2025 on expected realization events, while noting previously disclosed capital stack changes and the pending $1.5 million Mercantile Bank acquisition.

negative_highlights: Cash balance remains thin at $405,000, requiring additional financing for acquisitions and growth
Adjusted gross margin declined to 54.1% from 56.6% in the prior quarter
Company withheld revenue guidance citing substantial near-term variability
positive_highlights: Revenue of $3.17 million exceeded guidance and marked fifth consecutive quarter of growth
Adjusted operating loss improved 28.9% quarter-over-quarter, fourth consecutive reduction
Acquisitions of Spacecraft Components and SCP Manufacturing expected to enhance margins and profitability
summary: In fiscal Q1 2025, Mobix Labs reported revenue of $3.17 million, exceeding prior guidance with a 7.3% sequential increase and an 11-fold jump year-over-year. Adjusted gross margin was 54.1%, and adjusted operating loss narrowed to $2.5 million, marking the fourth consecutive quarter of reduced operating losses. The company announced two acquisitions (Spacecraft Components Corp and SCP Manufacturing) and guided to long-term gross margin of 60% and adjusted operating margin of 30%, but withheld near-term revenue guidance due to acquisition-related variability.

negative_highlights: Revenue decreased 37.7% year-over-year primarily driven by a 34.1% decrease in active earning OPTAVIA coaches.
Operating income fell 91.8% to $700,000 as gross profit declined 37.6% and SG&A increased as a percentage of revenue.
Q1 2025 guidance implies continued losses ranging from $0.00 to a loss of $0.50 per share due to ongoing customer acquisition challenges.
positive_highlights: EPS of $0.07 came in above the company's guidance range.
Revenue per active earning coach declined only 5.5% year-over-year, a significant moderation from the 22.2% decline in Q1 2024.
The new OPTAVIA ASCEND product line launched in December received positive feedback with approximately 17% of January orders including these products.
summary: Fourth quarter revenue was $119 million, down 37.7% year-over-year, while EPS of $0.07 beat the guidance range but remained significantly below prior year levels at $0.55. Gross profit margin improved 10 basis points to 74.1%, yet operating income contracted sharply to $700,000 due to lower volumes and higher SG&A as a percentage of revenue driven by company-led marketing spend. Management provided Q1 guidance of $100 million to $120 million revenue, acknowledging continued pressure on active earning coaches and expecting losses in the first half of 2025.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined 12% driven by a 14% reduction in core revenues in North America and a 6% decline in Europe.
Adjusted EBITDA margin contracted by 150 basis points to 4.5% due to lower volume, mix, and negative price-cost dynamics.
Free cash flow was a use of $28 million, resulting in net debt leverage increasing to 3.8 times, above the target range of 2 to 2.5 times.
positive_highlights: Delivered approximately $115 million of transformation benefits in 2024.
North America interior door business remained relatively stable as the company picked up share.
Europe adjusted EBITDA improved by $1 million year-over-year due to strong productivity improvements.
summary: Fourth quarter revenue declined 12% year-over-year to $896 million, driven by lower volume and mix shifts toward affordable options, while adjusted EBITDA fell 28% year-over-year to a range of $40 million. Management lowered full-year 2025 guidance for core revenues to a 4% to 9% decline (projecting $3.2B-$3.4B) and forecast adjusted EBITDA between $215 million and $265 million, citing significant headwinds from the divestiture of Towanda and continued market weakness in North America.

negative_highlights: Q1 2025 brand advertising guidance of $30–40 million implies a 26–31% sequential decline and 13–19% annual decline.
GAAP net loss widened to $21 million in Q4 2024 from $13 million in Q4 2023, with the full-year 2024 loss at $100 million versus $66 million in 2023.
Sohu Media full-year 2024 revenues fell to $91 million from $140 million in 2023, with the operating loss widening to $287 million from $269 million.
positive_highlights: Online game revenues exceeded prior guidance, with Changyou's quarterly operating profit of $48 million, up from $47 million a year earlier.
Brand advertising revenues hit the high end of prior guidance at $19 million.
Sohu repurchased 4.2 million ADS for approximately $52 million, about one-third of the $150 million board-approved program.
summary: Sohu reported Q4 2024 total revenues of $135 million, down 5% year-over-year and 11% quarter-over-quarter, with brand advertising at $19 million (down 7% YoY) and online game revenues at $110 million (down 4% YoY). The company posted a GAAP net loss of $21 million, wider than the $13 million loss in Q4 2023 and the $16 million loss in Q3 2024. Management guided Q1 2025 brand advertising revenues to $30–40 million, implying a 13–19% YoY decline and a 26–31% sequential decline, while online game revenue is guided to $105–115 million, roughly flat sequentially. The CEO attributed the soft advertising outlook to macroeconomic weakness, noting auto advertising budgets were 'cut by half' in 2024 and AI enthusiasm has not yet translated into marketing spend; Sohu Media's full-year 2024 revenue fell to $91 million from $140 million in 2023.

negative_highlights: Gross margin was lower than target due to inefficiencies in the new West Virginia manufacturing operations and the truck body division.
SG&A expenses increased sequentially from $2.2 million to $2.9 million, primarily driven by headcount additions.
Federal funding landscape remains fluid with uncertainty regarding contract completion between EPA and dealers.
positive_highlights: Revenue increased 35% sequentially to $7.2 million driven by sales of 13 BEAST Type D buses, one Nano BEAST, and 14 EV Star models.
Gross profit improved quarter-over-quarter to approximately $1.05 million, marking the third consecutive quarter with positive gross profit.
Strong demand confirmed for vocational applications (garbage/fueling trucks) and follow-on orders for customers electrifying their fleets.
summary: GreenPower reported Q3 FY2025 revenue of $7.2 million (a 35% increase sequentially) and gross profit of approximately $1.05 million (14.6% margin). While the company highlighted strong demand for electric school buses and improved EV Star sales, it noted that lower-than-target margins from the truck body division and new West Virginia operations offset some gains. Management indicated that gross profit will improve over time as California operations consolidate and West Virginia throughput increases.

Q4 NOI fell 0.8% to $84.2 million and adjusted EBITDAre declined 1.1% to $82.2 million year over year
Indianapolis faces significant competition as new buildings come online, and lease negotiation timelines are lengthening
positive_highlights: Full-year normalized FFO rose 12.1% to $35.4 million ($0.54/share); Q4 normalized FFO of $0.13/share up about 10% sequentially and year over year
Q4 leasing of 731,000 sq ft at rents 39.3% above prior rates, with Hawaii new leases 43% higher and 21.3-year weighted average term
Q1 2025 normalized FFO guided to $0.16-$0.18 per share versus $0.13 in Q4, aided by $2.2 million lower quarterly interest expense and the new $15 million interest rate cap
summary: ILPT reported Q4 2024 normalized FFO of $8.9 million, or $0.13 per share, up roughly 10% both sequentially and year over year, while quarterly NOI fell 0.8% to $84.2 million and adjusted EBITDAre declined 1.1% to $82.2 million. Full-year normalized FFO rose 12.1% to $35.4 million ($0.54/share). Management guided Q1 2025 normalized FFO to $0.16-$0.18 per share, helped by lower interest expense, newly signed leasing, and the absence of under-$1 million of Q4 bad debt. Occupancy held at 94.4%, and two vacancies (a Hawaii land parcel and an Indianapolis property) cut occupancy 4.6% and cost $1.8 million in quarterly rent, with management targeting 2025 leases for both.

negative_highlights: Q1 2025 distributable earnings guidance of $0.30 per share is below the $0.33 reported for Q4 and below the $0.35 quarterly dividend
Six to seven loans totaling approximately $200 million expected to be repaid in the back half of 2025, versus expected net portfolio growth of only about $100 million
Total debt to equity rose to 1.6x from 1.4x quarter over quarter due to Q4 originations
positive_highlights: Total loan commitments increased to $641 million from $594 million in Q3, an 8% rise
Portfolio had no five-rated, default, or non-accrual loans, with weighted average risk rating of 3.1 and LTV at close of 67%
Office exposure reduced to 26% of outstanding loan dollars from 30% at Q3 end
summary: Seven Hills Realty Trust reported Q4 2024 distributable earnings of $0.33 per share, which management said met the high end of its guidance range, and full-year DE of $1.45 per share versus a $1.40 dividend. Total loan commitments rose to $641 million from $594 million in Q3, with the portfolio 100% floating-rate, no five-rated loans, defaults, or non-accruals, and office exposure trimmed to 26% from 30%. Q1 2025 guidance was set at $0.30 per share, below the $0.33 just reported and below the $0.35 quarterly dividend, due to a Q4 payoff and timing of new originations not closing until later in Q1 or Q2. Management expects roughly $100 million of net portfolio growth in 2025, offset by six to seven loan repayments totaling about $200 million in the back half.

Facing headwinds from USPS rate increase and two more months of large grocer loss

summary: Quad reported Q4 2024 net sales decline of 10% YoY, in line with expectations, and full-year adjusted EBITDA margin improved to 8.4% from 7.9% in 2023. Free cash flow was $56 million, with $71 million from asset sales; net debt leverage reduced to 1.6x. Management expects net sales growth between 2027-2028 and projects a 100bps EBITDA margin improvement by 2028, but faces headwinds from a large grocer loss, a likely USPS rate increase, and early 2025 divestiture of European operations. The dividend was raised 50% to $0.075 per share quarterly.

negative_highlights: Q1 FY2025 revenue guidance is lowered to a range of $30-33 million due to customer inventory burn-down from record H2 volumes, product transitions, and the expiration of a special national mobile hotspot program.
Fixed Wireless Access (FWA) revenue declined slightly YoY in Q4 as customers manage year-end inventory ahead of next-generation product launches expected mid-year.
positive_highlights: Q4 revenue grew >33% YoY with mobile solutions up 59% driven by a large carrier partner and services/other revenue up 62% on SaaS renewals.
Non-GAAP gross margin expanded to 37.4%, representing a 260 bps sequential improvement, while adjusted EBITDA reached an all-time high of $5.4 million (11.2%).
Balance sheet strengthened materially with total debt reduced from >$165M at start of year to $56M by Q4 end and cash position improved to $40 million.
summary: Inseego reported Q4 FY2024 revenue of $48.1 million (up >33% YoY) and full-year revenue of $191.2 million (up 14.3%), driven by strong carrier hotspot growth (+59%) and SaaS services expansion (+62%). The company achieved a non-GAAP gross margin of 37.4%, adjusted EBITDA of $5.4 million, and completed the sale of its Telematics business for $52 million cash to reduce debt levels significantly from over $160M in total debt at year-end.

New initiatives like LungTraX Detect show early momentum with first patient treated
summary: Pulmonx reported Q4 worldwide sales of $23.8 million, up 23% year-over-year, with record U.S. sales of $15.9 million (up 16%) and record international sales of $7.9 million (up 42%). Full-year revenue was $83.8 million, up 22%. The company guided 2025 revenue growth of 17% at midpoint, below the 20% long-term target but accelerated by new initiatives in the second half of 2025. Gross margin guidance was 74%, with R&D spending increasing for clinical trials. Management remains confident in long-term growth and highlights successful pilot programs like LungTraX.

negative_highlights: No revenue figures were disclosed, and the company remains pre-revenue or near-zero revenue with a GAAP net loss of $8.5 million in Q4.
Full-year 2025 cash burn is guided to $25 million, slightly up from 2024, with a sequential cost increase expected in Q1 due to seasonal one-time payroll costs.
GAAP operating expenses rose sequentially to $9 million from $7.6 million, and non-GAAP operating expenses rose to $6.8 million from $6.1 million, driven by higher payroll and rent costs.
positive_highlights: Q4 cash burn of $4.8 million beat guidance of $4.9 million and improved from $5.6 million in Q3, the seventh consecutive quarter of reduced net cash burn.
Raised approximately $18 million since the start of Q4 2024, extending cash runway to mid-2026 and providing nearly a full year of runway at current burn.
Apollo LiDAR met NVIDIA Hyperion specifications and received strong interest at CES, with field testing underway in China, the U.S., and Europe across non-automotive sectors.
summary: AEye reported Q4 2024 GAAP net loss of $8.5 million ($0.93/share), an improvement from $8.7 million ($1.01/share) in Q3, and non-GAAP net loss of $6.3 million ($0.69/share) versus $6.0 million ($0.70/share) in Q3. Q4 cash burn was $4.8 million, beating guidance of $4.9 million, marking the seventh consecutive quarter of reduced net cash burn, and the company ended the quarter with $22.3 million in cash plus $12.7 million raised in early 2025, extending runway to mid-2026. Full-year 2025 cash burn is guided to $25 million, slightly up from 2024, with sequential improvement expected after Q1. The quarter showed no revenue figures and no EPS consensus comparisons, but management highlighted progress on Apollo LiDAR, NVIDIA Hyperion qualification, and Tier 1 manufacturing ramp, with first Apollo units expected off the line in Q1 2025.

negative_highlights: Personal lines premiums written declined 5% in Q4 due to a pause in new business and run-off of legacy policies.
Unfavorable development of $5.1 million in commercial auto and $1.6 million in personal auto offset some gains.
positive_highlights: Net income reached an all-time high of $24 million in Q4 FY2024.
Combined ratio improved significantly to 92.9% in Q4, down from 106.8% the prior year.
Core loss ratio decreased by 9.5 percentage points quarter-over-quarter.
summary: Donegal Group reported Q4 FY2024 net income of $24 million, its highest quarterly earnings in history, driven by a combined ratio improvement to 92.9% from 106.8% the prior year. Net premiums earned grew 4.6% to $236.6 million while weather-related losses decreased significantly to $7.7 million. Full-year 2024 results showed a combined ratio of 98.6% and net investment income growth of 12.5%.

negative_highlights: GAAP net loss of $0.72 per share and distributable loss of $0.59 per share in Q4 2024
Quarterly dividend paused in December to preserve capital; total liquidity stood at just $102 million at year-end

Credit migration continued: five multifamily loans risk-rated five and slated for foreclosure with specific reserves averaging 12% of UPB, and a $390M Manhattan multifamily loan downgraded to risk rating four on a discounted payoff modification
positive_highlights: Loan sales executed near par: $30M at 99.5%, $60M at 99%, and a $101M San Diego hotel loan at par post-quarter; five of seven 2024 loan sales were at 97% of par
New York REO hotel portfolio EBITDA in 2024 exceeded 2019 pre-pandemic levels
Roughly $2 billion of gross realization proceeds underway, with one-third to two-thirds expected to close in coming quarters and ~40% of proceeds adding liquidity
summary: CMTG reported a Q4 2024 GAAP net loss of $0.72 per share and a distributable loss of $0.59 per share, with distributable earnings before realized gains/losses of $0.18. The held-for-investment loan portfolio fell to $6.1 billion from $6.3 billion as $99 million of repayments and $205 million of loan sales were partly offset by $75 million of fundings. Management paused the quarterly dividend in December and reported only $102 million of total liquidity, while guiding to just under $2 billion of gross realization proceeds with one-third to two-thirds finalized in coming quarters and roughly 40% of those proceeds adding liquidity. Credit migration continued, with five multifamily loans (50% of five-rated loans) now marked for foreclosure with specific CECL reserves averaging 12% of UPB and a $390 million Manhattan multifamily loan modified to a discounted payoff option.

Adjusted EPS fell to $3.79 from $4.62
Costume business down 7.5% for the year

summary: Q4 2024 sales were roughly in line with expectations, with toy and consumer products down 1.8% for the full year, slightly better than expected. Gross margin improved 70 bps in Q4, but full-year operating margin fell to 5.7% from 8.3%, and adjusted EPS dropped to $3.79 from $4.62. Management initiated a quarterly dividend of $0.25 and highlighted continued strength in Sonic and international growth, but acknowledged challenges in costumes and cost pressures from tariffs.

Net Revenue Retention (NRR) for enterprise accounts finished at 99%, which is below past performance and management's confidence level.
Non-enterprise ARR declined 4% to $88 million as the company pivots focus toward high-value B2B/Enterprise segments.
positive_highlights: Non-GAAP operating income exceeded $19M for FY2024, a $6M improvement over the loss in FY2023 and nearly double the original forecast.
Operating cash flow reached $26 million for the year, representing a $50 million swing from 2023's negative cash flow.
Non-GAAP sales and marketing expenses improved to 36% of revenue down from 41% in FY2023.
summary: BigCommerce reported Q4 FY2024 revenue of $87 million (up 3% YoY) and full-year revenue of $333 million (up 8%), meeting expectations but missing prior growth targets. The company significantly improved profitability with non-GAAP operating income exceeding $19M for the year ($6M loss in FY2023), driven by a ~10% headcount reduction, lower S&M spend at 36% of revenue, and restructuring costs recognized early in Q4. Management raised full-year 2025 guidance to $342-$350 million (up from prior expectations) while maintaining conservative macro assumptions.

negative_highlights: Q4 adjusted EBITDA margin deteriorated to negative 12% from negative 3% a year ago, with net loss widening to $4.3 million from $0.3 million
Services revenue declined 4% year-over-year in both Q4 and FY2024 due to lower review revenue, and Q1 guidance embeds continued review volatility
A $15.2 million non-cash impairment charge was recorded on the primary law asset and related capitalized development, excluding it from adjusted EBITDA
positive_highlights: Total DNR improved to 96% from 92%, and software DNR rose to 100% from 97%

FY2024 adjusted EBITDA improved by $7.2 million to negative $18.7 million, and operating cash flow improved to negative $8.7 million from negative $25.5 million
summary: CS DISCO reported Q4 FY2024 total revenue of $37.0 million, up 4% year-over-year, with software revenue of $30.8 million (+5%) and services revenue of $6.2 million (-4%). FY2024 revenue was $144.8 million (+5%) and adjusted EBITDA was negative $18.7 million (negative 13% margin), improved from negative $19 million. gross margin held at 75% for Q4 and FY2024, while Q4 adjusted EBITDA margin worsened to negative 12% from negative 3%; net loss was $4.3 million versus $0.3 million. FY2025 guidance was given as total revenue of $145.5 million to $257.5 million and software revenue of $124 million to $231 million, with adjusted EBITDA of negative $19 million to negative $15 million; management targets breakeven adjusted EBITDA by Q4 2026. Dollar-based net retention improved to 96% from 92%, software DNR rose to 100% from 97%, and customers with >$100,000 in revenue grew 9% to 315.

GAAP net income for Q4 declined $344,000 year-over-year
Future grants from Israel Innovation Authority are uncertain beyond first quarter 2025
positive_highlights: Q4 revenue of $16.3 million, up 16.1% year-over-year; full-year revenue up 82% to $61 million
Record net income of $13.5 million for 2024, with EPS up over 75% on a GAAP basis
Full-year 2025 revenue guidance of 12%–15% growth, indicating continued momentum
summary: RADCOM reported record Q4 2024 revenue of $16.3 million, up 16.1% year-over-year, with full-year revenue of $61 million, up 82% and above guidance midpoint, marking five consecutive years of growth. Operating income for 2024 was a record $9.5 million (16% of revenue), and net income was $13.5 million ($0.83 per diluted share). The company guided to 12%–15% revenue growth for 2025, with a midpoint of $69.2 million, and highlighted new customer wins including Norlys (Telia Denmark) and partnerships like ServiceNow.

The company declared a regular dividend of $0.42 and special dividends of $0.03 per share. Portfolio quality remained stable with non-accruals at 0.9% of fair value, but watch list names increased. Management anticipates continued pickup in LBO activity in 2025.

Net dollar retention of 103% in Q4, but closed the year at 100% indicating sub-100% yearly retention

summary: Kaltura reported record Q4 2024 total revenue of $45.6M, up 3% YoY, and record subscription revenue of $43.4M, up 6% YoY. Adjusted EBITDA was $2.7M, the sixth consecutive quarter of profitability and the highest in four years, with record gross margin and $4.3M operating cash flow. Management noted record ARR and RPO, accelerating bookings momentum, and raised expectations for 2025 with continued growth and margin expansion, targeting Rule of 30. Guidance and outlook positive, with expansion plans in sales force and AI investments.

Hardwood realizations fell to $578/ton, down $54 from Q3, and a $5 million non-cash impairment was recorded at Peace River Mill

positive_highlights: Operating EBITDA rose to $99 million in Q4 from $50 million in Q3, and full-year EBITDA grew to $244 million from $17 million in 2023

The $300 million 2026 senior notes were redeemed using $200 million of new 2028 notes and $100 million of cash
summary: Mercer reported Q4 operating EBITDA of $99 million versus $50 million in Q3, net income of $17 million ($0.25/share), and full-year 2024 EBITDA of $244 million versus $17 million in 2023, as MBSK realizations held near record levels at $794/ton and pulp sales volumes rose 29,000 tons to 405,000 tons. The solid wood segment posted negative $5 million EBITDA amid weak construction, and Q4 cash use was $54 million. Q1 2025 guidance includes 21 days of maintenance downtime at Selgar, 78 total planned downtime days versus 57 in 2024, and $100-$120 million of capex; tariffs remain the central uncertainty with no formal earnings guidance given.

negative_highlights: Total Q4 revenue was flat year-over-year at $6.7 million, indicating a lack of top-line growth.
Gross profit declined 7% to $2.8 million in the fourth quarter.
Traditional beef source and age business continues to face headwinds from cyclical herd size reductions.

Verification and certification services revenue grew 6% to $20.6 million for the full year.
Company maintains strong cash position with $2 million in cash and $2.4 million in working capital entering 2025.
summary: Q4 FY2024 revenue was flat year-over-year at $6.7 million, driven by a slight decline in verification services and a 6% increase in product revenue. Net income rose to $961,000 primarily due to an $80,000 dividend gain from Progressive Beef and a $345,000 unrealized gain on bitcoin holdings, rather than core operational expansion. Full-year revenue grew 2% to $25.7 million as growth in new service offerings offset declines in the cyclical beef source and age business.

negative_highlights: Q1 adjusted EBITDA guidance is flat at negative $3.0M-$3.2M despite revenue growth expectations.
Management explicitly stated they are 'slightly cautious' regarding global trade data and potential tariff impacts on world trade volumes.
Full-year 2025 adjusted EBITDA loss remains substantial between -$10.9M and -$10.2M.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 25% year-over-year to $6.6 million, the highest quarterly rate since going public.
Adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed significantly for Q4 ($3.1M) compared to full-year prior period (-$19M), with a path toward breakeven by end of 2026.
Added twelve new carriers in Q4, marking the strongest onboarding history and bringing total carrier count to 67.
summary: Freightos reported Q4 FY2024 revenue of $6.6 million (up 25% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA loss narrowing to negative $3.1 million from a prior year level of negative $19M for the full period, beating transaction guidance but missing high-end EBITDA expectations due to Shipster consolidation costs. Management provided Q1 FY2025 revenue guidance between $6.7m-$6.8m and adjusted EBITDA between -$3m and -$3.2m (flat vs Q4), while raising full-year 2025 revenue guidance range from the prior implied ~$29M to a new explicit range of $29M-$30.6M, citing cautiousness regarding global trade data and tariffs despite strong platform growth.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA down 8% and funds from operations down ~19% YoY due to lower Brent prices
Operating costs per BOE up 2% in 2024, impacted by removal of diesel subsidies and higher gas/electricity
2024 net income only $3 million, down from a net loss in 2023 (but still positive)
positive_highlights: Record reserves across all categories and six consecutive years of 1P reserve growth
2025 production guidance of 47,000-53,000 BOE/d, up ~35% from 2024 average
Strong reserve replacement ratios of 702% (1P), 1250% (2P), 1500% (3P)
summary: Gran Tierra reported record reserves and highest-ever quarterly production in Q4 2024, with average FY2024 production of 34,710 BOE/d (up 6% YoY) and net income of $3 million (EPS $0.10) versus a net loss in 2023. The company reaffirmed 2025 production guidance of 47,000-53,000 BOE/d, up significantly due to Canadian acquisition and development programs. CFO expects operating costs to trend down in 2025, and management is confident in 5-10% production growth into 2026. Management highlighted continued share buybacks (6.7% of shares repurchased in 2024) and plans to allocate 50% of excess free cash flow to debt reduction and 50% to buybacks, with a target net debt of $600M by end 2026 and $500M by end 2027.

negative_highlights: Q4 consolidated EBITDA down year-over-year (13.4% margin vs 7.8%)
Q1 guidance flat, with caution on tariff impacts
Arcadia high-end residential demand weak; cost structure being rightsized
positive_highlights: Q4 sales and EBITDA exceeded guidance
Extended Arcadia put option to Sept 2026, easing liquidity concerns
NobelClad Q4 sales were its second strongest in over 10 years
summary: DMC Global's Q4 2024 sales of $152.4 million and adjusted EBITDA of $10.4 million exceeded guidance, but profits fell sharply year-over-year due to weak Arcadia residential demand and lower margins across segments. Management guided Q1 2025 sales flat sequentially at $146-154 million and adjusted EBITDA of $8-11 million, citing tariff uncertainty and soft demand. The company extended the Arcadia put option to September 2026, reducing near-term liquidity risk, and is prioritizing free cash flow and debt repayment. Arcadia is being refocused on commercial products with cost cuts, while DynaEnergetics completed a product reengineering and automation phase.

negative_highlights: Total revenue fell 24% year-over-year to $143.5 million; subscriber count declined 21% to 3.6 million.
Q1 2025 revenue guidance of $114M-$116M implies a deeper year-over-year decline than Q4, with no stabilization yet.
Non-subscriber traffic plummeted 49% year-over-year in January 2025, a sharp deterioration from the 8% decline in Q2 2024.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA of $37 million (25% margin) surpassed Q4 guidance for both revenue and adjusted EBITDA.
Busuu language learning revenue grew 9% year-over-year in 2024, with enterprise revenue up 46%.
Free cash flow was positive at $4.8 million despite about $25 million in restructuring cash outlays.
summary: Chegg reported Q4 2024 revenue of $143.5M, down 24% year-over-year, with subscription revenue of $128.5M (down 23%) and 3.6M subscribers (down 21%). Adjusted EBITDA was $37M (25% margin), beating the company's own Q4 guidance, but the company initiated Q1 2025 revenue guidance of $114M-$116M, implying a continued double-digit decline, and announced a strategic review (including a possible sale) plus a lawsuit against Google over AI Overviews. Non-subscriber traffic fell 49% year-over-year in January 2025, far worse than the 8% decline reported in Q2 2024, and management explicitly stated industry challenges are causing a notable decline in traffic and subscriber acquisitions.

negative_highlights: Q4 revenue missed expectations due to a $3.5 million delay on two NYPD contracts caused by political distractions.
Adjusted EBITDA turned negative at -$1.7M for the quarter as costs were incurred without associated revenue from delayed services.
G&A expenses increased significantly year-over-year, rising 24% in absolute terms to $5.5 million.
positive_highlights: Full year 2024 revenue grew by 10% YoY to a record $102 million despite the Q4 delay.
Management raised full-year 2025 adjusted EBITDA margin guidance range from prior levels to 21%-23%.
ShotSpotter International pipeline expanded with new city captures in Brazil, South Africa, and Uruguay.
summary: Q4 FY2024 revenue decreased by 10% year-over-year to $23.4 million due to a delayed NYPD contract renewal of approximately $3.5 million, resulting in an adjusted EBITDA loss of $1.7 million compared to the prior period's profit. Despite this quarterly miss driven specifically by administrative delays rather than product failure or demand issues, management increased full-year 2025 revenue guidance to $111-$113 million and raised adjusted EBITDA margin expectations to 21%-23%. The company highlighted strong international pipeline growth in Latin America and successful pilot wins for its SafePointe weapons detection system.

negative_highlights: Revenue decreased by approximately 5% to $57.1 million compared to Q4 2023 due to softer market conditions in the back half of the year.
Diluted EPS declined significantly from $0.06 to $0.02, impacted by increased warrant gains and share count adjustments rather than operational performance.
Management warned that 2025 is projected to be a 'softer' year due to moderation in demand growth outpacing supply.
positive_highlights: Net income increased to $9.7 million from $9.4 million in Q4 2023, driven by decreased interest expense and non-operating gains.
Fleet utilization remained strong at 99.7% for the fiscal year 2024.
Company secured favorable time charters including four Capesize vessels averaging $18,312/day.
summary: For Q4 FY2024, Diana Shipping reported revenue of $57.1 million (down ~5% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $25.9 million (down from $27.1m), while net income rose to $9.7 million due to lower interest expenses but diluted EPS fell to $0.02 from $0.06. Management noted a 'year of two halves' with strong H1 rates followed by softer conditions in Q4, citing fleet efficiency gains and normalization at the Panama Canal as headwinds. Forward guidance indicates contracted revenues for 2025 are approximately $125 million (at or around breakeven) and $30 million for 2016.

negative_highlights: Non-GAAP gross margin missed expectations due to higher-than-expected scrap expense related to raw materials and a $1 million inventory reserve.
Q1 guidance midpoint is flat year-over-year, reflecting uncertainty regarding PEPFAR funding freezes affecting international diagnostics revenue (approx. 80% of which is donor-funded).
US academic/research segment exposure faces potential headwinds from NIH plans to reduce indirect research cost funding mechanisms.
positive_highlights: Core revenue grew 10% YoY driven by strong international HIV business order trends and a 14% increase in sample management solutions revenue.
Acquisition of Sherlock Biosciences completed to expand the innovation pipeline with a molecular diagnostic platform for CTNG testing expected by end of 2025.
FDA approval secured for labeling change on OraQuick HIV self-test expanding access to adolescents aged 14 and older.
summary: Q4 total revenue was $37.4 million with core revenue of $36.5 million growing 10% year-over-year to the top half of guidance range. GAAP gross margin contracted to 36.2%, while non-GAAP margins were slightly below expectations due to one-time scrap expenses and inventory reserves related to exiting a business unit. Management provided Q1 revenue guidance ranging from $27.5 million to $31.5 million, noting that the midpoint is flat year-over-year after adjusting for exited businesses.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined 18% year-over-year and 5% sequentially due to a prolonged labor market downturn with seasonally adjusted hires down for the 28th consecutive month.
Net loss widened significantly in Q4 to $10.8 million compared to net income of $5.6 million in Q4 2023, driven by revenue contraction.
positive_highlights: Job seeker web traffic grew by 30% in organic visits during 2024, demonstrating product stickiness despite macro headwinds.
summary: ZipRecruiter reported Q4 FY2024 revenue of $111 million, an 18% year-over-year decline and a 5% sequential decrease driven by soft hiring demand among SMBs. Adjusted EBITDA fell to $14.4 million (13% margin) from $42.4 million in the prior year quarter due to lower revenue volume despite disciplined cost management. Management provided Q1 FY2025 guidance of $109 million at the midpoint, representing an 11% decline versus last year but a sequential improvement over Q4.

negative_highlights: Q4 consolidated revenue declined 2% year-over-year
EPS slightly lower due to FX and discontinued operations
Europe segment operating profit decreased, with Germany revenue weakness
positive_highlights: Operating profit increased 8% year-over-year to $4.9 million
JAX Flight Club revenue grew 19% year-over-year
Q1 2025 revenue expected to grow at a higher pace with 5% incremental membership fee revenue
summary: Travelzoo Q4 2024 revenue was $20.7 million, down 2% year-over-year, but operating profit rose 8% to $4.9 million with a 24% margin. EPS was slightly lower due to FX and discontinued operations, but management expects Q1 2025 revenue to grow at a higher pace with 5% incremental growth from membership fees. Legacy member conversion to paid club membership is on track, with expectations of 50% more paying members by end of Q1. JAX Flight Club grew revenue 19% year-over-year and remains profitable.

negative_highlights: Industrial Xtreme product deployments did not materialize in FY2024 due to longer-than-expected evaluations
No meaningful revenue contribution from new industrial products until expected in 2025
Operating expenses increased 2.8% YoY primarily due to salary adjustments and benefits costs
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 10% YoY and sequentially by 25% in Q4
Gross margin expanded to 50.4% driven by higher production volumes
Operating loss narrowed significantly from $3.1M (FY) / $1M (Q3 prior) to $2.5M (FY) / $411k (Q4)
summary: Socket Mobile reported Q4 FY2024 revenue of $4.8 million (up 10% YoY) and full-year revenue of $18.8 million (up 10%), with gross margins expanding to 50.4%. The company posted a net loss per share of $0.30 for the year, narrowing its operating loss from $2.5M in FY2024 compared to $3.1M previously, though it still ended the period cash-positive without needing external financing.

negative_highlights: Direct-to-consumer sales declined 21.3% to $15.6 million due to a downsized sales force.
Rental revenue fell 16.5% to $13.8 million as the mix shifted toward private payers with lower billing rates.
DTC channel revenue is expected to remain challenged in H1 2025 while the rep count normalizes.
positive_highlights: Domestic B2B revenue surged 24.1% to $22.4 million and International B2B revenue grew 31.5% to $28.3 million.
Total gross margin expanded 821 bps to 45.3% in Q4, driven by lower raw material costs and operational efficiencies.
Adjusted EBITDA improved significantly to a negative $3.6 million in Q4 from a negative $17.3 million in the prior year.
summary: Inogen reported Q4 FY2024 revenue of $80 million (up 5.5% YoY) and full-year revenue of $335.7 million (up 6.4% YoY), driven by strong B2B growth partially offset by a deliberate DTC channel contraction. The company achieved two quarters of adjusted EBITDA profitability in 2024, with Q4 adjusted loss narrowing to $5.8 million from $19.4 million the prior year. Management provided FY2025 revenue guidance of $352-$355 million and expects gross margins between 43% and 45%, while noting that the recently announced Yuwell collaboration will not significantly impact 2025 results.

negative_highlights: Comparable store sales declined 13.7% driven by a challenging demand environment and higher mortgage rates.
EPS missed significantly at $0.49 compared to the prior year's $0.90.
Management explicitly stated they do not provide guidance for Q1 or current quarter trends.
positive_highlights: Traffic improved in Q4 with the first positive year-over-year gain in low single digits after election resolution.
Average ticket rose approximately 4% to just under $3,400 during the quarter.
Company ended the year with zero funded debt and over $120 million in cash.
summary: Haverty Furniture reported Q4 FY2024 net sales of $184.4 million, a 12.5% decrease year-over-year, with comparable store sales down 13.7%. Gross margins decreased 50 basis points to 61.9%, while operating income fell to $9.6 million (5.2% margin) and EPS dropped to $0.49 from $0.90 in the prior year quarter. Management provided forward guidance for 2025 gross margins of 60%-60.5% and fixed SG&A of $291-$293 million, maintaining a flat margin outlook despite tariff concerns.

negative_highlights: Q1 guidance flat year-over-year due to non-recurring sales and shipment shift

Recorded $4 million non-cash trademark impairment on Muck
positive_highlights: Adjusted EPS up 21% to $1.19 in Q4
Retail segment highest ever quarterly sales, up 15.3%
Full-year recurring sales up 5.3% and adjusted EPS up 31.6%
summary: Rocky Brands reported Q4 sales up 1.7% to $128.1 million, with a strong retail segment up 15.3% and wholesale up 4.5% on a recurring basis. Adjusted EPS rose to $1.19 from $0.98, and full-year recurring sales grew 5.3% with adjusted EPS of $2.54 versus $1.93. The company guided Q1 flat year-over-year due to non-recurring sales and shipment timing, despite momentum in XTRATUF, Muck, and Durango. Management remains cautious on consumer unpredictability and retailer inventory commitments.

negative_highlights: The quarter produced a net loss of $131.1 million, or $23.83 per diluted share, and AFFO per diluted share of negative $2.01.
The company carries $2.6 billion of loans at a 7.9% blended rate, with only about 23% effectively fixed.
No 2025 financial guidance was provided, leaving the Grow AHT $50 million target as a longer-term goal, and the common dividend is not expected to be reinstated in 2025.
positive_highlights: Comparable hotel EBITDA grew 6.2% year over year, with December hotel EBITDA up 12%.
Gross operating margins expanded about 141 bps in Q4, aided by cost initiatives, including a $130,000 annual food cost saving at Renaissance Nashville.

The $580 million, 16-hotel refinancing fully repaid the strategic financing, which management tied to the completion of a multi-year, $430 million-plus asset sale and $195 million preferred equity process.
summary: Q4 comparable RevPAR rose 3.1%, total revenue grew 4.6%, and comparable hotel EBITDA rose 6.2%, with gross operating margins expanding about 141 bps. However, the quarter included a net loss of $131.1 million, or $23.83 per diluted share, and AFFO per share of negative $2.01. Management emphasized its newly launched Grow AHT initiative, targeting a $50 million run-rate EBITDA uplift, and said 2025 would be a 'transformational year', though formal 2025 guidance was not provided. Subsequent to quarter-end, the company sold the Courtyard Boston Downtown for $123 million, refinanced a $580 million, 16-hotel portfolio, and fully repaid its strategic financing, while saying it does not expect to reinstate a common dividend in 2025.

negative_highlights: Total revenue declined to $137.7 million from $139 million, and adjusted EBITDA fell to $29.2 million from $30.3 million

Professional services revenue rose 21.6% and software maintenance backlog reached roughly $62 million, up nearly 22%

summary: Spok reported 2024 revenue of $137.7 million, down from $139 million in 2023, with GAAP net income of $15 million ($0.73 per diluted share) versus $15.7 million ($0.77) prior year. Adjusted EBITDA was $29.2 million, down from $30.3 million, though software operations bookings rose 13% to $34.1 million and professional services revenue grew 21.6%. 2025 guidance calls for revenue of $134-142 million (midpoint roughly flat, high end +3%) and adjusted EBITDA of $27.5-32.5 million, with the midpoint only a minor improvement over 2024. Management also noted soft Q4 wireless additions that were delayed and expects continued secular decline in pager units, offset by ARPU gains and higher-margin software license mix.

negative_highlights: Same-property cash basis NOI declined 1.4% sequentially to $63.7 million, hurt by $4.4 million of weather-related and insurance remediation costs including a $1 million Hurricane Milton deductible

SHOP expense growth of 3.9% and reliance on dispositions of 34 communities in process to improve remaining-portfolio metrics (which would have added $2.3 million of Q4 NOI and 180 bps of margin)

SHOP occupancy hit 80% (80.9% same-property) for the first time since Q1 2020, up 100 bps YoY, while average monthly rate rose 6.7%
