summary: DHC reported Q4 FY2024 total revenues of $379.6 million (up 5% YoY) and normalized FFO of $5.3 million or $0.02 per share, which management said exceeded consensus and represented a 31% sequential increase. SHOP occupancy reached 80% for the first time since Q1 2020, SHOP revenues rose 7.3% YoY with 250 bps of margin expansion, and full-year SHOP NOI of $106 million landed at the high end of revised guidance. For 2025, management guided SHOP NOI to $120-$135 million and MOB/life science NOI to $104-$112 million, with CapEx of $150-$170 million (a 16% reduction from 2024), and outlined progress on refinancing the $380 million June 2025 notes via $340 million of secured term sheets at roughly 6.5% versus 9.75% debt being repaid.

negative_highlights: Sales declined 2% to $63.9 million on continued soft consumer demand for discretionary recreational goods
EBITDA fell to $5.9 million from $6.4 million and SG&A rose 5% ($0.5 million) to $10.9 million
Q4 operating cash flow dropped to $12.3 million from $20.6 million as inventory-driven working capital benefits diminished
positive_highlights: Gross margin expanded 61 bps to 24.9%, driven by lower operational costs from footprint rationalization and workforce cuts
Full-year operating cash flow of $36 million enabled $25.3 million of debt paydown, ending at 0.8x net leverage with $25.6 million of fixed-rate debt at 2.97%
Inventory reduced 44% during 2024 and roughly 20% versus year-end 2023, with further reduction expected in 2025
summary: Escalade reported Q4 net sales of $63.9 million, down 2% year over year, with net income of $2.7 million, or $0.19 per diluted share. Gross margin expanded 61 bps to 24.9%, while SG&A rose 5% to $10.9 million and EBITDA fell to $5.9 million from $6.4 million. Operating cash flow was $12.3 million versus $20.6 million a year earlier, partly because inventory reductions contributed less as levels approached optimum. Management gave no explicit quantitative guidance, citing soft discretionary demand, ongoing footprint and workforce cuts (23% workforce reduction, ~20% square footage reduction), $25.3 million of debt paydown to 0.8x net leverage, and a $2.2 million buyback; CEO Walter Glazer is handing over to Arman Bohm on April 1.

negative_highlights: Q4 pretax earnings of $7.4 million fell 24% YoY and FY pretax earnings fell to $27.4 million from $61.1 million
FY diluted EPS fell to $0.79 from $1.80; return on managed assets dropped to 0.9% from 2.1% in 2023
Q4 net charge-offs rose to 8.02% from 7.74% YoY and 30+ day delinquencies rose to 14.85% from 14.55%; auction recoveries remain around 30% versus a historical 40-45%
positive_highlights: Q4 originations of $458 million, up 52% YoY, and FY originations of $1.68 billion, up 24%
Fair value portfolio grew 22% to $3.314 billion with yield of 11.3% net of losses; shareholders' equity reached a record $293 million

summary: Q4 revenue rose 14% YoY to $105.3 million and originations jumped 52% YoY to $458 million, but pretax earnings fell 24% to $7.4 million and diluted EPS dropped to $0.21 from $0.29 a year ago. Full-year net income fell to $19.2 million ($0.79 diluted) from $45.3 million ($1.80) in 2023, with FY expenses up 26% to $366.1 million on higher interest expense and portfolio growth. Management gave no formal numeric guidance but said 2025 should be a strong growth year with improving NIM and credit, while Q4 net charge-offs rose to 8.02% from 7.74% and 30+ day delinquencies ticked up to 14.85% from 14.55%.

negative_highlights: TV Media revenue declined 4% to $5 billion due to affiliate and advertising headwinds.
Q1 adjusted OIBDA is expected to decline year-over-year compared to last year's Super Bowl quarter.
positive_highlights: Paramount+ added 5.6 million new subscribers in Q4, the strongest quarter of sub-growth in two years.
summary: Paramount Global reported Q4 FY2024 results with Paramount+ adding 5.6 million new subscribers and achieving record engagement driven by a strong content slate including 'Landman' and the NFL season. D2C revenue grew 8% to $2 billion, while TV Media revenue declined 4% due to affiliate headwinds and fewer football games. Management raised full-year free cash flow expectations for 2025 despite Q1 being impacted by lapping last year's Super Bowl.

negative_highlights: Gross margins contracted 260 basis points year-over-year to 62.7%, attributed to test mix and timing of payments.
Adjusted EBITDA remained negative at -$1.4 million for Q4, though showing a 68% improvement over the prior period.
positive_highlights: Q4 total billable volume reached approximately 24,000 tests, up 26% year-over-year.
Tissue-based test volumes grew significantly by 50% to nearly 12,000 units in Q4.
Revenue growth of 28% was achieved without expanding the commercial sales organization.
summary: MDxHealth reported Q4 FY2024 revenue of $24.7 million, representing a 28% year-over-year increase driven by organic growth without sales headcount expansion. Gross margins declined to 62.7% from the prior year's 65.3%, primarily due to test mix and payment timing. The company confirmed its full-year 2025 revenue guidance of $108 million to $110 million, with a target for positive adjusted EBITDA in H1 2025.

negative_highlights: Adjusted distributable earnings per share fell 2% YoY to R$1.15, entirely due to a R$16 million FX loss from the 14% BRL depreciation in Q4.
The 36% Q4 FRE margin is not sustainable; management guided to a normalized run rate in the low 30% range for 2025.
Gross accrued performance fees of R$437 million may face a temporary negative impact next quarter from offshore fund mark-to-market lag and prior FX depreciation.

Performance-related earnings surged 478% YoY to R$16.5 million, driven by Argentina, Peru real estate and credit strategies.
VCP IV reached R$3.1 billion in commitments, the largest PE vintage in firm history, with domestic Brazilian investors rising to ~40% of the base versus a 30% historical average.
summary: Vinci Compass reported Q4 2024 fee-related revenues of R$218 million (up 84% YoY) and FRE of R$79 million (up 38% YoY), with management fees up 70% and performance-related earnings up 478% to R$16.5 million. Adjusted distributable earnings were R$73.9 million (R$1.15/share), down 2% per share due to a R$16 million FX hit, but would have been R$90 million (R$1.40/share, up 19%) excluding FX. The company set a normalized FRE margin expectation of low 30% for 2025 and maintained its ~80% dividend payout target. AUM reached R$327 billion, aided by the Compass combination and R$3.4 billion of gross fundraising in 2024.

negative_highlights: Automotive revenue declined 19.4% YoY due to price erosion and reduced unit sales at Mercedes-Benz
Cross-industry business (CIB) gross margin contracted from Q3 levels due to product mix shift
Full-year net loss widened significantly compared to the prior year
positive_highlights: Q4 and FY2024 revenue beat top-end of prior guidance

Adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed to $3.7M vs a wider range previously guided
summary: Valens reported Q4 FY2024 revenue of $16.7 million and full-year revenue of $57.9 million, both exceeding guidance ranges ($16M-$16.3M for the quarter; $57.2M-$57.5M for the year). Gross margins expanded to 60.4% in Q4 (guidance midpoint) but declined YoY due to product mix shifts and lower fixed cost absorption, while automotive revenue fell 19.4% YoY driven by price erosion at Mercedes-Benz. Management raised full-year 2025 guidance expectations significantly ($71M-$76M range), citing an emerging recovery from inventory digestion.

negative_highlights: 2025 revenues and profits expected to decline significantly due to soft bookings market
Q4 tax rate 55% due to non-deductible footprint charges
Bolzoni Q4 revenue down $4M YoY and operating loss below prior year
positive_highlights: Q4 revenues up 4% YoY and adjusted operating profit up 10% YoY

Early 2025 bookings show encouraging signs in EMEA and JPIC
summary: Q4 2024 revenues rose 4% YoY to $1.1B, with adjusted operating profit up 10% to $54M and adjusted EPS of $1.47. Full-year revenues reached $4.3B, up 5%, with adjusted operating profit of $267M (6% margin), the strongest in company history. Guidance calls for a significant decline in 2025 revenues and profits due to soft bookings and higher cancellations, though early 2025 bookings show encouraging signs in EMEA and JPIC. Footprint optimization programs are expected to generate $30-40M annual benefits starting in 2027, but 2025 margins are expected to be below the 7% target.

negative_highlights: Total revenue declined due to a reduction in operating weeks from 13 to 12 compared to the prior year.
Restaurant-level operating profit margin decreased 70 basis points to 11.5% primarily due to lower guest counts and increased discount levels of approximately 120 bps.
Management expects to close 10 to 15 restaurants in 2025, including three asset sales in Q1.
positive_highlights: Comparable restaurant revenue increased 3.4% excluding loyalty deferrals, led by an increase in average check.
Guest traffic trends improved sequentially in each quarter of 2024, culminating in a 600 bps improvement from Q1 to Q4.
Loyalty program revamped in May drove membership growth of approximately 1.5 million members, ending the year with 14.9 million total.
summary: Red Robin reported Q4 FY2024 total revenue of $285.2 million, a decline from the prior year due to a shift from 13 to 12 operating weeks, though comparable restaurant revenue grew 3.4% excluding loyalty deferrals. Adjusted EBITDA increased to $12.7 million driven by lower watching and G&A expenses, but restaurant-level operating profit margin contracted to 11.5%. Management provided 2025 guidance for total revenue between $1.225 billion and $1.25 billion (incorporating a ~2% headwind from closures) and adjusted EBITDA of $60-65 million.

negative_highlights: China business faces challenging environment, expected only to 'hold serve'
Hyatt integration costs and inventory step-up will affect near-term profitability
Company is not planning significant stock buybacks beyond managing dilution
positive_highlights: Q4 net sales grew 7% sequentially, exceeding expectations
Adjusted diluted EPS increased 14% sequentially
Hyatt acquisition expected to drive strong growth with revenue guidance of $145-160 million for 2025
summary: USANA reported solid Q4 2024 results with sequential net sales growth of 7% and adjusted diluted EPS up 14%, exceeding expectations. The quarter benefited from promotional activities, particularly in the US (up 16% sequentially) and Australia/New Zealand (up 9% YoY). The company completed the acquisition of an 78.8% stake in Hyatt for $405 million, which contributed minimally to 2024 results but is expected to generate $145-160 million in revenue for 2025 (29-42% growth). Management outlined 2025 plans including over 20 product launches, a global convention, and incentive enhancements, while maintaining a cautious outlook for core business growth.

negative_highlights: Aviation book contracted by more than 25% in Q4 following several quarters of rate reductions.
Significantly elevated loss activity in Q1 2025 from California wildfires and other global risks.
positive_highlights: Record core operating income of $40.9 million in Q4 and $144.8 million for the full year.
Reinsurance segment gross premiums grew more than 36% YoY with significant underwriting income growth.
Book value per share increased nearly 20% YoY to $14.85.
summary: IGIC reported Q4 FY2024 gross premiums up just under 6% YoY and a combined ratio of 77.8%, driven by strong reinsurance growth (premiums up >36%) offsetting contraction in the long tail segment. Full year net income reached a record $135.2 million with a core operating return on equity of 24.2%. Management noted that 2025 has started challenging due to elevated loss activity from California wildfires and global events, though they expect these losses to be manageable.

negative_highlights: Q4 total revenue fell 7% YoY to $8.7 million and subscription revenue fell 10% to $5.0 million
Ending ARR declined to $20 million from $22.3 million a year earlier; the $3.7 million DRS contract is expected to lapse in Q2 2025 due to a government program change
Government service revenue guided 12-14% lower in 2025 than 2024 on a smaller approved budget, and budgeting assumes increased churn plus price-aggressive renewals
positive_highlights: Reorganization targets ~$16.5 million annualized cash savings plus $5.5 million in other annualized cash cost savings, with only ~$3 million in one-time costs
Excluding the lapsed $5.8 million contract, ARR grew $3.5 million (+21%) and Q4 subscription revenue would have risen 11%
Management expects positive non-GAAP net income by no later than Q4 2025, with normalized Q1 2025 free cash flow usage of $2.7-3.2 million nearly two-thirds below Q1 2024
summary: Q4 total revenue fell 7% YoY to $8.7 million and subscription revenue slid 10% to $5.0 million, driven by zero revenue on the lapsed $5.8 million contract (versus $1.1 million in Q4 prior year); excluding it, subscription rose 11%. Ending ARR was $20 million versus $22.3 million a year ago, though management cites 21% ARR growth excluding the lapsed contract. Full-year revenue grew 10% to $38.4 million with subscription up 18%, and non-GAAP net loss per share narrowed to $0.22 from $0.28 in Q4. Management announced a reorganization cutting annualized cash costs ~$16.5 million plus $5.5 million other savings, guides to non-GAAP profitability no later than Q4 2025, and disclosed a Goldman Sachs engagement to explore options up to going private; the $3.7 million DRS contract is expected to lapse in Q2 2025.

negative_highlights: Cash used in operations and CapEx decreased to $81.4M in 2024 from $99.6M in 2023, still high
Cash burn expected to be lumpy sequentially, though lower on an annualized basis
Gross margins expected to remain lumpy
positive_highlights: Full-year 2024 revenue of $24.3M exceeded midpoint of $23.5-25M guidance
Entered into ~$80M NRE payment plan with key customers, >$40M in 2025
Q4 2024 generated gross profit for the first time
summary: Innoviz reported full-year 2024 revenue of $24.3 million, up from $20.1 million in 2023 and above the midpoint of guidance. The company secured an $80 million NRE payment plan, raised $40 million via a registered direct offering, and announced $12 million in annualized cost savings. For 2025, management guides revenue of $50-60 million, implying more than twofold growth, with positive gross margin on an annualized basis.

negative_highlights: 2025 free cash flow guided down to $20-25 million from $47.7 million
Gas Cylinders Q4 adjusted EBITDA margin down 350 bps YoY
Q1 2025 expected to be softer due to order pull-forwards and CNG headwinds
positive_highlights: Q4 adjusted EPS up 61% YoY to $0.29
Q4 EBITDA margin expanded to 14.4% from 12.2% prior year
Four consecutive quarters of margin expansion in Electron
summary: Luxfer reported Q4 2024 sales of $96 million, adjusted EBITDA of $13.8 million (14.4% margin), and adjusted EPS of $0.29, up 61% YoY, driven by defense demand and order pull-ins. Full-year adjusted EPS was $0.99 with EBITDA margin of 13.7%. 2025 guidance calls for flat revenue, adjusted EPS of $0.95-$1.05, EBITDA of $48-52 million, and free cash flow of $20-25 million, reflecting the absence of one-time benefits. Management cited near-term headwinds in clean energy and a softer Q1 2025 due to order pull-forwards, but remains confident in long-term hydrogen and CNG opportunities.

negative_highlights: Q4 gross profit margin contracted to 26.1% from the prior year's 26.8% due to expected price decreases on specific products.
International revenue declined in Q4, partially offsetting gains in North America.
Cash flow from operations decreased significantly to $65.4 million compared to $88.6 million in FY2023.
positive_highlights: Full year gross margin expanded a record 300 basis points to 26% compared to the historical range in the low 20s.
Operating profit grew 23.1% for the full year, ending with $43.2 million versus $35.1 million prior year.
Company ended FY2024 in a net cash position of $600k after repurchasing shares and paying dividends.
summary: Hamilton Beach Brands reported Q4 FY2024 revenue of $213.5 million (up 3.3% YoY) and full-year net income increasing to $30.8 million ($2.20/share). While the company achieved a record gross margin expansion of 300 bps for the year, Q4 margins contracted slightly due to planned price reductions on certain products after cost benefits were realized in late 2023. Management raised full-year revenue guidance expectations from low single-digits to mid-single digits and reiterated that operating profit is expected to grow faster than revenue driven by expense leverage.

Q4 sales of $218.9 million were pressured across all major end markets, and adjusted EBITDA of $6.0 million (2.7% of sales) came in well below prior expectations due to elevated warranty/quality costs and $2.1 million of higher engineering expense, a net $3.1 million unfavorable impact. Full-year sales of $908.3 million outperformed a weighted end market down 10.4% by 490 bps, free cash flow improved $55.5 million to $23.8 million on a $36.4 million inventory reduction, and the credit facility was amended for covenant relief through Q3 2025. 2025 guidance calls for sales of $860-890 million (down from $908.3 million) with gross margin up 135 bps and EBITDA of about $40 million (4.6% margin), plus new free cash flow guidance of $25-30 million; MirrorEye is guided to roughly $120 million (up ~$54 million). The company also set a 2026 revenue target of at least $975 million and $70 million EBITDA, and a 2029 MirrorEye target of nearly $300 million.

negative_highlights: Full-year 2025 revenue guidance is flat-to-up (+1%) due to anticipated disruption in H1 from the April 13, 2025 LCD implementation.
Operating expenses increased $12.2 million YoY (up 17%), driven by a 20% rise in SG&A and incremental clinical trial spending for ReNu BLA preparation.
Management expects a challenging operating environment throughout the first half of 2025 before stabilization begins.
positive_highlights: Q4 revenue of $126.7 million beat guidance by exceeding the upper range ($100M-$125M).
Adjusted EBITDA expanded significantly to $18.2 million (up from $7.5m prior year) and exceeded expectations.
Strong brand equity demonstrated as customers adapted quickly to delayed LCD effective dates.
summary: Organogenesis reported Q4 FY2024 revenue of $126.7 million (up 27% YoY), exceeding the high end of prior guidance and driving adjusted EBITDA to $18.2 million, which beat expectations by over $2 million. Management provided full-year 2025 financial guidance assuming a delayed LCD effective date of April 13, 2025, projecting revenue between $480 million and $535 million (flat to +11% YoY) with profitability expected to stabilize in the third quarter after challenging first-half conditions. The company highlighted strong execution despite market ambiguity but noted that customer watching behavior remains cautious due to reimbursement uncertainty.

negative_highlights: Q4 GAAP net income fell to $0.43 per diluted share from $0.73 a year earlier on an unrealized loss on common stock investments
Cash available for distribution of $0.47 covered the $0.50 dividend only 0.94x
Full-year earnings available for distribution declined 5.3% to $1.78 per diluted share from $1.88
positive_highlights: Earnings available for distribution rose to $0.83 per diluted share in Q4 from $0.44 a year earlier
Full-year cash available for distribution rose 18% to $2.42 per diluted share from $2.05
Multifamily construction starts of 37,000 units in Q4 were the lowest since Q4 2011, supporting an expected supply inflection
summary: NexPoint Real Estate Finance reported Q4 net income of $0.43 per diluted share versus $0.73 a year earlier, while earnings available for distribution rose to $0.83 from $0.44 and cash available for distribution fell to $0.47 from $0.51. The $0.50 dividend was covered 0.94x by cash available for distribution, and book value per share rose slightly to $16.97. Q1 2025 guidance is EAD of $0.45 (range $0.40-$0.50) and CAD of $0.50 (range $0.45-$0.55). Management pointed to improving multifamily fundamentals and a pipeline of roughly $75 million in construction financing plus $300 million of life science opportunities underwriting, while flagging a couple of 30-60 day delinquent loans in the Freddie Mac K B-piece portfolio.

negative_highlights: Product revenue declined quarter-over-quarter primarily due to a drop in product supply sales from global partners ($0.8M vs $7.4M)
Management forecasts an approximate 2% demand decline year-over-year for the full fiscal year 2025
Royalty revenues dropped significantly to $4.7 million compared to $24.4 million in Q3 due to China regulatory transition
positive_highlights: NERLYNX ex-factory bottle sales increased by an approximate 9% quarter-over-quarter to 2,964 bottles
Total prescriptions (TRx) grew approximately 3% year-over-year despite a decline in new patient starts
Company maintained positive net income of $19.3M GAAP and $21.1M non-GAAP due to the release of valuation allowance
summary: Puma Biotechnology reported Q4 FY2024 revenue of $59.1 million, a decline from the prior quarter driven by lower product supply sales to global partners and higher gross-to-net adjustments, though NERLYNX ex-factory bottle sales increased slightly year-over-year due to inventory builds at distributors. Management provided full-year 2025 guidance for net revenue between $192M-$198M but explicitly forecast a demand decline of approximately 2% versus the prior year and noted that royalty revenues will be lower in 2025 as China transitions regulatory ownership to Pierre Fabre.

negative_highlights: Net loss attributable to common stockholders of $31.1 million (-$0.47/share) and negative AFFO of $0.06/share for the quarter
Comparable hotel EBITDA grew only 0.7% to $41.1 million despite 5.3% revenue growth, indicating margin pressure
Los Angeles wildfire disruption caused Cameo Beverly Hills booking cancellations, group date shifts, and softened note rates, with daily volatility
positive_highlights: Comparable RevPAR rose 1.9% to $305, ending six consecutive quarters of RevPAR declines
Group rooms revenue grew 7% in Q4 and 2025 group revenue pace is up 8%, with $61 million of future group revenue booked versus $41 million in Q3
January portfolio RevPAR growth exceeded 9% excluding Capital Hilton, and urban hotels posted 3.3% RevPAR growth
summary: Braemar reported Q4 comparable RevPAR of $305, up 1.9%, ending six straight quarters of RevPAR declines, with comparable total hotel revenue up 5.3% and comparable hotel EBITDA of $41.1 million, up only 0.7%. The quarter's bottom line was a net loss attributable to common stockholders of $31.1 million (-$0.47/share) and AFFO of negative $0.06/share; full-year AFFO was $0.21/share and adjusted EBITDAre was $157.6 million. No formal 2025 guidance was issued, but management cited January portfolio RevPAR growth over 9% excluding Capital Hilton, 2025 group revenue pace up 8%, and $61 million of group revenue booked in Q4 versus $41 million in Q3. Key changes: the $193 million loan maturing June 2025 is in active refinancing talks, the Ritz Carlton Lake Tahoe loan was extended with a $10 million paydown, and roughly $80 million of non-traded preferred has been redeemed.

negative_highlights: Company had only $1 million in revenue (upfront license fee) and remains pre-commercial with no product sales.
ASCEND Cohort B and other externally controlled data timelines remain subject to investigators' schedules, limited company control.
FORFITIDE study is being restructured with no defined timeline; second-line cholangiocarcinoma enrollment only 30% complete.
positive_highlights: Net loss narrowed to $20.0 million from $20.8 million, with operating expenses down 8.9% to $23.4 million.
BOLSTER first-line cholangiocarcinoma enrollment completed six months ahead of plan, accelerating top-line data to mid-2025.
Preliminary ASCEND Cohort A data showed positive overall survival trend including four complete responses vs. none on placebo.
summary: Lisata reported no product revenue for the full year 2024 (except a $1 million upfront license fee from Kuva Labs); operating expenses fell 8.9% to $23.4 million, and net loss narrowed to $20.0 million from $20.8 million in 2023. Cash at year-end was $31.2 million, expected to fund operations into Q2 2026. Progress in 2024 included positive early ASCEND Cohort A and iLSTA data, completion of enrollment in CENDIFOX and BOLSTER first-line, and initiation of a glioblastoma study. Management expects a data-rich 2025, with ASCEND Cohort B results anticipated in the coming months and BOLSTER top-line data mid-2025, but no guidance was provided.

negative_highlights: 2025 revenue guidance of $153-163 million and adjusted EBITDA of $0-8 million implies a wide range, with EBITDA potentially flat to down from 2024's $8.6 million
Management took a more conservative CINVANTI outlook for 2025, citing increased competition and potential ASP pressure despite expected unit growth
Full-year 2024 still posted a net loss of $13.6 million, and CFO flagged lumpy EBITDA/cash flow early in 2025 from legal spend and PFS R&D
positive_highlights: Achieved Q4 net income of $3.7 million and full-year adjusted EBITDA of $8.6 million, versus a $10.7 million Q4 2023 net loss
Full-year gross margin expanded to 73.2% from 48.8% in 2023, with Q4 gross margin at 74.9% versus 71.1%
ZYNRELEF set a record at $8.5 million in Q4, up 33% QoQ and 48% YoY, with APONVIE up over 310% YoY
summary: Heron reported Q4 net income of $3.7 million versus a $10.7 million loss in the prior-year quarter, on net revenues that drove a full-year total of $144.2 million, up 14% YoY, with adjusted EBITDA of $8.6 million for the year. Gross margin expanded to 74.9% in Q4 from 71.1%, and full-year gross margin rose to 73.2% from 48.8% a year earlier, helped by the absence of prior-year inventory write-offs. ZYNRELEF hit record net revenues of $8.5 million, up 33% QoQ, and CINVANTI rebounded to $26.9 million from $22.7 million in Q3. Management issued 2025 product revenue guidance of $153-163 million and adjusted EBITDA of $0-8 million, and said it took a more conservative CINVANTI outlook given anticipated competition and ASP pressure.

negative_highlights: Revenue down 10% YoY
Behavioral subscribers down 12%
Annual interest payments of ~$100 million
positive_highlights: Clinical business grew 58% in Q4
ARPU hit record high of $4
Highest activation rate since 2020
summary: Revenue declined 10% YoY in Q4 with behavioral business down 12% but clinical up 58%. ARPU reached a record high; adjusted EBITDA margins were the highest since Q3 2022. 2025 starts with a $45 million revenue headwind and a goal to cut $100 million in run-rate costs. Management remains cautiously optimistic about stabilization and innovation, but faces uncertainty from FDA decision on compounded semaglutide and ongoing subscriber declines.

negative_highlights: Q4 net loss widened significantly to $548 million primarily due to a one-time $570 million estimated loss on the sale of discontinued operations.
Cirrata revenue in Q4 grew only 25% YoY ($44M) compared to full-year growth, impacted by softness in A&H and ESL lines.
Everspan net premiums written declined due to non-renewal of a reinsurance program and shift from retained to fully fronted programs.
positive_highlights: Cirrata revenue surged 93% YoY to $99 million driven by the Beat acquisition and strong specialty commercial auto performance.
Everspan achieved its second quarterly underwriting profit with a combined ratio improvement of 380 bps to 96.5% in Q4.
Legacy financial guarantee business sold for $420 million, providing capital relief and allowing focus on Specialty P&C growth.
summary: Ambac reported a net loss of $548 million ($10.23 EPS) for Q4 FY2024 due to a $570 million loss on the sale of its legacy financial guarantee business and acquisition-related expenses, though continuing operations generated positive adjusted earnings of $6 million. The company successfully closed the Beat acquisition driving significant revenue growth in Cirrata (+93% YoY), while Everspan achieved an underwriting profit with a 96.5 combined ratio despite some program volatility. Management indicated that forward guidance for 2025 will be revisited following the final close of the legacy business sale.

negative_highlights: Full-year 2024 revenue declined 0.6% to $428.8 million and annualized recurring revenue fell 4.1% YoY to $414.8 million
Full-year 2024 net loss was $0.40 per diluted share versus net income of $0.29 in 2023, and non-GAAP EPS fell to $0.48 from $0.54
Operating cash flow swung to a $38.8 million outflow from a $12.5 million inflow in 2023, and cash plus note weakness in-term investments fell to $88.8 million from $125.3 million
positive_highlights: Q4 billings rose 7.1% YoY to $172.1 million, and 12% excluding PeopleSoft-associated billings
Gross margin expanded to 63.7% in Q4 from 61.0% a year earlier, aided by a one-time ~$5 million revenue benefit
Ninth Circuit denied Oracle's rehearing petition on February 25, 2025, following the December 16, 2024 decision vacating much of the District Court's Rimini II trial rulings
summary: Q4 revenue was $114.2 million, up 1.9% YoY including a one-time $5 million client event that pulled forward revenue, while full-year revenue of $428.8 million declined 0.6% and annualized recurring revenue fell 4.1% to $414.8 million. Q4 GAAP EPS was $0.07 versus $0.10 a year earlier and non-GAAP EPS was $0.12 versus $0.19. Billings rose 7.1% YoY to $172.1 million (up 12% excluding PeopleSoft), and gross margin improved to 63.7% partly on the one-time revenue benefit. Guidance remains suspended pending Oracle litigation clarity, though management said it expects to return to providing guidance in 2025; the $35 million cost-reduction plan reached $18 million annualized net savings in Q4, with further restructuring charges expected in 2025.

negative_highlights: Full-year EBITDA slightly below guidance range
Jafra U.S. revenue down 17.6% in Q4 due to Shopify Plus adoption issues
Betterware Mexico EBITDA down 9.6% for the year with margin contraction
positive_highlights: Q4 revenue up 11.1% with Jafra Mexico up 22.2%
Jafra Mexico EBITDA up 15.4% for the year with margin expansion to 20.7%
Adjusted EPS up 17.3% for the full year
summary: Q4 revenue grew 11.1% with Jafra Mexico up 22.2%, but adjusted EBITDA fell 5.8% due to headwinds. Full-year EBITDA grew 2%, below the low end of guidance due to supply chain and FX pressures. 2025 guidance is mid-to-high single digit growth for revenue and EBITDA. Leadership transition announced with Andres Campos as new President and CEO.

positive_highlights: Revenue grew 5% QoQ/QoY to $37M with average paid members slightly up.
summary: Q4 FY2024 revenue was $37 million (up 5% QoQ and YoY) with average paid members slightly up to 687,000. Interchange grew significantly at 62% year-over-year to $5.1 million as the card program fully migrated. The company is now debt-free after paying down $22.7 million in debt and generated strong free cash flow of $6.3 million.

negative_highlights: Full-year 2024 revenue excluding PAXLOVID declined to $59.3M from $62M
Product gross margin declined to 56% in 2024 from 63% in 2023
First-quarter 2025 revenue expected to be slow at $8-10M
positive_highlights: Completed feasibility studies with multiple leading siRNA innovator companies
New longer-term agreement with Pfizer beyond PAXLOVID
First combined 2025 revenue guidance of $64-68M, implying double-digit growth
summary: Codexis reported Q4 2024 revenue of $21.5 million, with product revenue of $9.8 million and R&D revenue of $11.6 million. Full-year 2024 revenue excluding PAXLOVID was $59.3 million, down from $62 million, and the net loss narrowed to $65.3 million from $84.4 million. Management guided 2025 total revenue to $64-68 million, its first combined guidance, expecting double-digit growth across the entire base. The CEO expressed confidence in returning the base pharma business to growth and highlighted progress in advancing the ECO Synthesis platform, with multiple feasibility studies completed and revenue-generating contracts expected in early Q2 2025.

negative_highlights: Core income decreased by $12 million year-over-year due to the full retention loss from Hurricane Milton.
Combined ratio was elevated at 91.9% in Q4, driven significantly by catastrophe losses and lower seeded earned premiums.
Pricing is expected to decrease between 5% and 10% year-over-year on average account renewals due to favorable trends in loss costs.
positive_highlights: Remained profitable in Q4 with a full retention loss from Hurricane Milton, absorbing the event within quarterly earnings as targeted.
Successfully placed a new $200 million catastrophe bond at attractive terms featuring a cascading drop-down feature for subsequent events.
Launched a new apartment program in Florida and wrote 19 new risks totaling approximately $2.3 million of premium.
summary: American Coastal Insurance reported Q4 FY2024 net income of $4.9 million and gross premiums earned growth of approximately 13% year-over-year to $162.7 million, though core income decreased by $12 million due to a full retention loss from Hurricane Milton ($23M) which drove the combined ratio to 91.9%. Management reiterated its 2025 net income guidance range of $70-$90 million and maintained expectations for an underlying combined ratio near 65%, despite pricing decreases of 5-10% year-over-year.

negative_highlights: Full-year collaboration revenue growth is expected to decelerate significantly with guidance of only $5-15 million for FY2025.
Management explicitly stated that the Phase 3 INFRONT-3 trial will be powered primarily on symptomatic patients, excluding presymptomatics from primary analysis due to slower progression rates.
positive_highlights: Collaboration revenue surged to $54.2M in Q4, driven by the GSK partnership for Latozinemab and AL101 programs.
summary: Alector reported Q4 FY2024 collaboration revenue of $54.2 million (up from $15.2M in prior year) and full-year revenue of $100.6 million versus $97.1 million, while R&D expenses decreased to $46.5 million for the quarter ($185.9M vs $192.1M annually). Management provided 2025 guidance expecting collaboration revenue between $5-15 million and total R&D/G&A expenses of roughly $175-$185 million / $55-$65 million respectively, indicating a significant reduction in expected spend compared to the prior year's trajectory. The company highlighted strong cash reserves of $413.4 million but noted that future revenue is projected at levels significantly lower than current run rates.

negative_highlights: Consolidated Q4 revenue missed guidance due to lower political advertising than expected, both before and after the election.
Non-political advertising revenues in the Multiplatform Group were down 5% excluding politics, failing to re-express post-election optimism seen in January.
Q1 2025 adjusted EBITDA is now guided at $100M-$110M (down from prior year's $105M) due to LA wildfire impacts and macro uncertainty.
positive_highlights: Digital Audio Group generated fourth quarter revenues of $339 million up 6.7% YoY with podcasting revenue growing 6% YoY.

Multiplatform Group adjusted EBITDA grew 5.9% to $150 million despite flat consolidated revenue, driven by strong broadcast radio performance and cost savings initiatives generating net annualized savings of ~$150M.
Audio and Media Services Group revenues surged 44.7% YoY to $98 million with adjusted EBITDA up 136%.
summary: iHeartMedia reported Q4 FY2024 consolidated revenues of $1.1 billion (implied sum) up 4.8% YoY and adjusted EBITDA of $246 million, both missing the high single-digit revenue guidance and ~$290M EBITDA guidance due to lower-than-expected political advertising and a post-election slowdown in non-political ads. Management reiterated full-year 2025 consolidated revenue guidance as flat compared to 2024 with adjusted EBITDA of approximately $770 million, while warning that Q1 2025 revenues will be down low single digits due to the LA wildfires and macro uncertainty.

negative_highlights: Adjusted net loss widened in Q4 to -$22 million from -$8 million
Book value per share fell to -$40.99 from -$32.56
PREPA resolution path and timing remain largely uncertain
positive_highlights: Q4 GAAP net loss improved to -$51 million from -$138 million year-over-year
Full-year GAAP net loss improved to -$447 million from -$491 million
National's insured portfolio declined by $3.1 billion to about $25 billion at year-end
summary: MBIA reported a Q4 2024 GAAP net loss of $51 million (-$1.07 per share), improved from a $138 million loss in Q4 2023, but adjusted net loss widened to $22 million from $8 million. Full-year 2024 GAAP net loss improved to $447 million from $491 million, while adjusted net loss widened to $184 million from $169 million. Book value per share fell to -$40.99 from -$32.56, and PREPA resolution remains uncertain with an $800 million claim. National's statutory capital declined to $912 million and claims-paying resources to $1.5 billion.

negative_highlights: Marketing Services billings declined 40% year-over-year to $92 million as part of the strategic transition away from legacy services.
Net customer adds in the core SaaS business declined slightly compared to Q2 and Q3, attributed to holiday seasonality and macro caution.
Leverage ratio increased temporarily to 1.63x due to debt prepayments and costs associated with decommissioning legacy systems.
positive_highlights: Total SaaS revenue beat guidance with a 41% year-over-year increase to $104.3 million.
SaaS adjusted gross margin expanded significantly to 76%, up 620 basis points year-over-year.
Keap acquisition revenue of $13.4 million in Q4 surpassed the upper end of guidance.
summary: Thryv reported Q4 FY2024 SaaS revenue of $104.3 million, beating guidance and growing 41% year-over-year, driven by a Keap acquisition contribution of $13.4 million that exceeded the $11-12 million range. Total SaaS adjusted gross margin expanded to 76%, while quarterly SaaS EBITDA reached $17.3 million, significantly exceeding guidance by over $5 million. Management maintained full-year 2025 revenue guidance of $464.5-$474 million and EBITDA guidance of $69.5-$71 million despite the acquisition integration.

negative_highlights: GAAP net loss widened significantly due to a $17.6 million noncash charge related to warrant liabilities.
Recurring revenue mix decreased to approximately 64% in Q4 from 73% the prior year as system sales grew faster than procedure volume initially.
positive_highlights: Q4 top-line revenue increased 38% YoY to a record $16.7 million driven by 31 ALLY system placements globally.
Adjusted EBITDA turned positive at $478,000 in Q4 compared to negative $1.2 million the prior year quarter.
Company installed base of ALLY systems surpassed 135 globally with a total installed base growth of 26%.
summary: LENSAR reported Q4 FY2024 revenue of $16.7 million (up 38% YoY) and GAAP net loss of $18.7 million driven by a noncash warrant charge; the company achieved its second consecutive quarter of positive adjusted EBITDA ($478k). Management raised full-year 2025 revenue guidance to above the prior year's growth rate, citing global expansion in Europe and Southeast Asia.

negative_highlights: Total revenue declined 5% year-over-year to $235 million, primarily due to a shift to net revenue recognition on the DSP business.
Q4 results were impacted by a high single-digit headwind from one key supply partner transitioning to new bidding technology.
Legacy Teads Q1 outlook includes an expected year-over-year decline in Ex TAC gross profit due to sales force distraction and FX headwinds.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA grew 21% year-over-year to $17 million driven by margin improvements and revenue mix changes.
Ex TAC gross profit accelerated, growing 7% year-over-year for the seventh consecutive quarter.
Free cash flow reached record levels of approximately $38 million in Q4 and $51 million for the full year.
summary: Outbrain reported Q4 revenue of approximately $235 million, a 5% year-over-year decrease, while Ex TAC gross profit grew 7% and adjusted EBITDA rose 21% to $17 million. Management achieved its guidance range for the quarter but noted that total ad spend was materially flat year-over-year due to a shift in revenue recognition from gross to net on the DSP business. The company closed its acquisition of Teads on February 3rd and provided full-year 2025 adjusted EBITDA guidance of at least $180 million, acknowledging an expected pro forma decline in Q1 Ex TAC gross profit before returning to growth in H2.

Definitive Healthcare reported Q4 2024 revenue of $62.3 million, down 6% year-over-year but above the high end of guidance, with adjusted EBITDA of $17.5 million (28% margin, down 190 bps) and adjusted EPS of $0.08, up 19%. Management guided Q1 2025 revenue to $55.5-$57 million (a 10-13% decline) and full-year 2025 revenue to $230-$240 million, a 5-9% decline versus 2024's 0.3% growth, citing Q4 and January renewal rates that fell year-over-year and assuming full-year NDR in the low-to-mid 80s. Gross margin contracted roughly 400 bps to 80.7%, enterprise customers fell 21 year-over-year to 519, and a $97 million non-cash goodwill impairment was booked. Management acknowledged the return to stability and growth will take longer than anticipated 90 days ago.

negative_highlights: Q4 gross margin declined 40 bps year-over-year to 38.7%.
SG&A expenses rose to 32% of sales for the year versus 31% in 2023, with Q4 SG&A at 34% of sales.
Full-year net sales grew only 2% as reported due to the loss of ~$9 million in revenue from sold businesses.
positive_highlights: Q4 net sales rose 10% to $45.9 million and full-year adjusted sales grew 6% excluding divested businesses.
Full-year net income increased 23% to $10 million and EPS rose 10% to $2.45.
Gross margin for the year expanded to 39.3% from 37.7%, driven by over $2 million in productivity savings.
summary: Acme United reported Q4 2024 net sales of $45.9 million, up 10% from $41.9 million, and full-year sales of $194.4 million, up 2% (up 6% excluding the sold Camillus/Cuda businesses). Full-year net income rose 23% to $10 million ($2.45 per diluted share) versus $8.1 million ($2.23) in 2023, with gross margin expanding to 39.3% from 37.7%; however, Q4 gross margin dipped to 38.7% from 39.1%. Management provided no formal 2025 guidance, but expressed optimism for growth and detailed tariff mitigation via diversified sourcing, productivity savings, and price increases. The company ended the year with $21.5 million net debt and paid $2.2 million in dividends.

negative_highlights: Q4 NII declined from $0.58 in Q3 due to base rate declines and repricing
Net income per share of $0.54 was hit by $0.02 of net realized and unrealized losses from restructurings
Spread compression and competitive dynamics in private credit noted during 2024
positive_highlights: NII per share of $0.56 fully covered dividend of $0.55 for the quarter
Full-year ROE of 12.4% and NAV increased sequentially to $18.18
Portfolio nonaccruals declined to just over 0.1% of fair value after two successful restructurings
summary: NCDL reported Q4 2024 NII of $0.56 per share, fully covering the $0.55 dividend, and full-year NII of $2.26 per share with ROE of 12.4%. NAV per share rose to $18.18 from $18.15, and the company issued $300 million of unsecured notes in January 2025 to reduce debt costs. Management noted record Churchill platform origination of over $13 billion, a well-managed nonaccrual level of 0.1% of fair value, and expects continued growth in 2025, with no material policy impact anticipated.

negative_highlights: Q1 FY2025 revenue guidance of $21.7-22.8 million (down 2% to up 3%) brackets flat and implies deceleration from Q4's 9% growth.
Unique sellers fell 24% to ~5,900 due to the essential seller program retirement, with churn not expected to normalize until the first half of 2025.
Operating expenses rose 16% YoY to $23.4 million, with sales and marketing up 22% and technology development up 23%, keeping adjusted EBITDA in a $1.6 million loss.
positive_highlights: GMV grew 9% YoY to $94.5 million, the fastest pace in three years and a ~14 percentage point sequential acceleration, exceeding the high end of guidance.
Active buyers reached ~64,300, up 6% YoY, the first YoY growth since Q2 2022, with conversion rates up for a fifth consecutive quarter.
Gross margin expanded ~100 bps to 72%, and adjusted EBITDA margin improved 1 point YoY; 2024 share repurchases totaled ~5.6 million shares for $28.1 million.
summary: 1stdibs reported Q4 GMV of $94.5 million (up 9% YoY) and net revenue of $22.8 million (up 9%), both above the high end of guidance, with adjusted EBITDA margin loss of 7% versus a 7% loss last year. Q1 FY2025 guidance calls for GMV of $90-96 million (down 2% to up 5%) and revenue of $21.7-22.8 million (down 2% to up 3%), bracketing flat and below the Q4 growth rate; no full-year guidance was provided beyond an expectation for GMV growth in 2025. The quarter marks the fastest GMV growth since 2021 and the first YoY active buyer growth since Q2 2022, but unique seller count fell 24% due to the essential seller program retirement, and Q1 guidance implies a deceleration with a ~100 bp leap-year drag.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EPS of $0.55 missed last year's level due to a one-time $305 million net-of-tax goodwill impairment charge related to adverse financial market changes.
Home respiratory therapies (NIV and oxygen) declined on a year-over-year basis in Q4, though management noted encouraging signs toward a turnaround late in the quarter.
Glove pricing remained lower than prior periods, partially offsetting same-store sales growth within the Products & Health Care Services segment.
positive_highlights: Patient Direct segment outpaced market growth with mid-single-digit revenue growth in Q4 and delivered over $13 million of incremental operating income for the full year.
Gross margin expanded by 93 basis points to 21.5% compared to Q3, aided by a $10 million LIFO credit as inventory levels declined significantly at period end.
Management indicated that previously discussed cost synergy projections from the Rotech acquisition are now considered conservative regarding both value and timing.
summary: Owens & Minor reported Q4 FY2024 revenue of $2.7 billion (up 1.5% YoY) and adjusted EPS of $0.55 per share, missing the prior year's $0.69 due to a significant $305 million non-cash goodwill impairment charge recorded in the quarter. Adjusted operating income was $95 million, down from last year but up sequentially by $11 million driven by margin expansion of 93 bps versus Q3 and lower inventory levels offsetting higher SG&A expenses. Management provided full-year 2025 guidance for revenue between $10.85 billion to $11.15 billion (midpoint $11.0B) and adjusted EBITDA between $560 million to $590 million, representing approximately 10% growth over the prior year.

negative_highlights: Industry origination volumes have come down recently due to rate backups, creating a headwind for Arc Home's broader market peers.
Arc Home contributed an EAD loss of $0.02 in Q4 despite recent profitability improvements.
Book value was flat for January following the 0.6% gain in December.
positive_highlights: Book value increased by approximately 0.6% driven by gains on home equity loans and portfolio hedges.
Arc Home transitioned from negative EAD contribution to neutral/positive in December-January following investments in talent and operations.
Company successfully raised senior unsecured notes to pay off legacy WMC convertible debt.
summary: MITT reported Q4 FY2024 GAAP EPS of $0.30 and EAD of $0.18 per share against a declared dividend of $0.75 for the year (Q4 portion $0.19). Book value increased by approximately 0.6% to $10.64, driven largely by gains on home equity loans and hedges offsetting portfolio losses. Management noted Arc Home flipped from negative EAD contribution in Q3/Q4 of prior years to neutral/positive in December-January but warned that the broader market faces headwinds with industry origination volumes down due to rate backups.

negative_highlights: Navacaprant failed to show statistically significant improvement on the primary or key secondary endpoint in KOASTAL-1, the first of three Phase 3 MDD studies
Phase 2 trial of navacaprant in bipolar depression discontinued; NMRA-266 remains on clinical hold nearly a year after preclinical convulsions
Males in the non-experienced-site subgroup showed placebo response of about 15 points; total operating expenses rose to $243.8 million for full-year 2024 from $235.9 million
positive_highlights: Cash, equivalents and marketable securities of $307.6 million expected to fund operations into mid-2026
Q4 operating expenses fell to $58.8 million from $108.7 million a year earlier

KOASTAL-2 and 3 will add MGH SAFER independent diagnostic review and the VCT screening database on top of prior KOASTAL-1 measures; sites with recent positive MDD Phase 3 experience (~1/4 of KOASTAL-1 population) showed better male performance
summary: Neumora reported Q4 total operating expenses of $58.8 million versus $108.7 million a year earlier, and full-year 2024 operating expenses of $243.8 million versus $235.9 million in 2023, with $307.6 million in cash supporting runway into mid-2026. The call centered on the failure of the Phase 3 KOASTAL-1 study of navacaprant in MDD, which management called an anomaly versus prior positive kappa opioid studies, and on protocol changes (MGH SAFER diagnostic review, VCT screening database, fewer sites) for KOASTAL-2 and 3, now guided to resume with 12-15 months of enrollment. The company discontinued the Phase 2 bipolar depression trial of navacaprant and has not resolved the clinical hold on NMRA-266, citing preclinical convulsions, while advancing follow-on M4 compounds into the clinic by mid-2025.

positive_highlights: Q4 revenue and contribution ex-TAC grew 40% and 28% YoY, exceeding guidance
Adjusted EBITDA increased 31% YoY to $17.1 million, above guidance
Full-year adjusted EBITDA margin expanded ~500 bps to 25%
summary: Q4 2024 revenue and contribution ex-TAC grew 40% and 28% YoY, respectively, exceeding guidance, with adjusted EBITDA up 31% to $17.1 million. Full-year revenue rose 30% and contribution ex-TAC rose 24%, with adjusted EBITDA margin expanding 500 basis points to 25%. The company announced the acquisition of Locker, a data collaboration platform, and expects AI measurement to launch in Q2 and AI decisioning in H2 2025. Management noted temporary gross accounting for a few large customers but expressed strong market momentum and a positive outlook.

negative_highlights: Interest expense rose 33.4% ($8.2 million) to finance portfolio growth, and debt-to-market-cap of ~51-52% sits above the low end of the 45-55% target range
Management guided 2025 AFFO per share to only ~$1.20 versus a $1.11 base, roughly 8-10% growth, and hedged the figure as one it expects to beat
One 2025 lease maturity will not renew (tenant exiting), and management flagged two Chicagoland assets as potentially needing operator changes
positive_highlights: Revenue rose 17.3% ($17.3 million) while total expenses grew only 6.5%, driving net income up 30.9% to $26.5 million
Portfolio expanded from 109 to 124 facilities and 12,449 to 14,186 beds, with base rents guided to roughly $130 million in 2025 from $104 million in 2024
Dividend raised 16.6% to $0.14 per share with a 49.5% AFFO payout and 100% of contractual rents collected
summary: Strawberry Fields REIT reported FY2024 revenue up 17.3% to $117.3 million, net income up 30.9% to $26.5 million, adjusted AFFO of $55.8 million and adjusted EBITDA of $90.6 million. The portfolio grew from 109 to 124 facilities during 2024 (14,186 beds), with base rents rising from $84 million in 2020 to $104 million in 2024 and expected near $130 million in 2025. Management guided to roughly $1.20 of AFFO per share for 2025 and referenced about $150 million of acquisitions, with $80-90 million already lined up. The dividend was raised 16.6% for the year to $0.14 per share (49.5% AFFO payout), and 100% of contractual rents were collected.

negative_highlights: Consumer payments gross profit declined ~5% in Q4, and overall Q4 gross profit grew only 2% YoY
No 2025 outlook provided due to the strategic review, and management will not take questions on the review or outlook
Client losses (acquisitions and in-housing) and strategic AP migration weighed on growth, with ~$20M of favorable 2024 working capital expected to reverse in Q1 2025
positive_highlights: Business payments gross profit grew 60% YoY in Q4, driven by core AP, political media, and new client ramps
Full-year adjusted EBITDA grew 11% and free cash flow conversion improved to 75% from 42% in 2023
Instant funding transaction volumes rose ~34% YoY and supplier network grew 38% to over 360,000 suppliers
summary: Repay reported Q4 revenue of $78.3M, up 3% YoY, with gross profit growth of just 2% as consumer payments gross profit declined ~5% (offset by business payments gross profit growth of 60%). Adjusted EBITDA rose 9% to $36.5M at a ~47% margin, and Q4 free cash flow conversion was 64% versus 75% for the full year. Management refrained from providing 2025 guidance due to a newly commenced comprehensive strategic review that could include M&A, a take-private, or a sale of the company. Reported gross profit growth would have been approximately 10% excluding client losses and a strategic migration of AP clients to the total pay solution, and management expects normalized growth to build back toward mid-to-high single digits seen in early 2024.

negative_highlights: Company explicitly stated it will not launch or commercialize any new tests in 2025, limiting near-term pipeline expansion despite robust R&D progress.
Adjusted EBITDA remains a loss of $3.9 million for the quarter and $22.1 million annually; profitability is targeted only for the second half of 2025.
Cash balance decreased to $26.2 million at quarter-end, though management expects cash flow breakeven later in the year.
positive_highlights: Full-year adjusted EBITDA loss improved by 32% to a loss of $22.1 million compared to 2023, driven by revenue growth and cost discipline.
Gross margin expanded sequentially from 77.0% in Q3 to 78.7% in Q4 as volume scaled.
Pilot program successfully demonstrated the viability of leveraging primary care referral networks via pulmonologists.
summary: Biodesix reported Q4 FY2024 revenue of $20.4 million (39% YoY growth) and full-year revenue of $71.3 million (45% YoY), both in line with guidance. The company achieved a gross margin expansion to 78.7% for the quarter and improved adjusted EBITDA loss by 32% year-over-year, though it remains below profitability targets. Management reiterated full-year 2025 revenue guidance of $92-$95 million while maintaining strong margins in the mid-to-upper seventies.

negative_highlights: Continued operations posted a net loss of $178-187 million, including $73-79 million of goodwill/intangible impairment and $49 million of trading and realized/unrealized investment losses
Continuing-operations operating adjusted EBITDA was only $12-14 million for the quarter
Results are preliminary and unaudited with the 10-K at risk of a 12b-25 extension past March 17, and management said it cannot note back bonds under the new senior facility
positive_highlights: Total debt, net of cash and investments, fell $221 million sequentially to approximately $991 million as of December 31, 2024
Great American JV with Oaktree delivered ~$203 million cash upfront and a ~44% retained stake, immediately followed by a JOANN liquidation win described as one of GA Group's largest in 40 years
Closed the sale of Atlantic Coast Recycling for ~$70 million cash (~$39 million cost basis), with an expected ~$30 million gain in Q1
summary: B. Riley reported preliminary Q4 2024 net income available to common shareholders of $48-68 million ($1.57-$2.22 diluted), but that was driven by $236-247 million of income from discontinued operations tied to the Great American JV; continuing operations produced a net loss of $178-187 million including $73-79 million of goodwill/intangible impairments and $49 million of trading and investment losses. Continuing-operations operating adjusted EBITDA was only $12-14 million. No formal forward guidance was issued; management described a strategic pivot toward B. Riley Securities, Wealth Management and advisory services, backed by ~$203 million in GA JV cash, ~$236 million from brand-asset financing, a $160 million Oaktree senior secured facility, a ~$70 million Atlantic Coast Recycling sale and a ~$26 million Stifel wealth-management sale, with total debt net of cash and investments down $221 million sequentially to ~$991 million. The CEO walked back his August take-private proposal, citing the baby-bond debt structure and a desire to let shareholders participate in the recovery.

negative_highlights: Eliminated the O&M incentive fee in exchange for a $110 million payment, changing the Puerto Rico contract structure
2025 $1 billion EBITDA guidance excludes the FEMA claim, and the company is still targeting future deleveraging after $4.775 billion of recent capital-markets activity
positive_highlights: Q4 2024 EBITDA of $314 million, about 50% above prior guidance
FLNG 1 achieved roughly 120% of nameplate capacity in January and has shipped 12 cargoes (~24 TBtu)
Full-year 2025 EBITDA guidance confirmed at $1 billion, with Puerto Rico extending the island-wide contract by one year
summary: NFE reported Q4 2024 EBITDA of $314 million, roughly 50% above its prior guidance of about $209 million, with full-year 2024 EBITDA of $950 million, and it reaffirmed 2025 EBITDA guidance of $1 billion, which excludes the FEMA claim. Management said FLNG unit 1 was placed into service as of December 31, 2024, has run at roughly 120% of nameplate capacity, and shipped 12 cargoes totaling about 24 TBtu. The company extended Puerto Rico's island-wide LNG contract by one year, agreed to pay a $110 million settlement to eliminate the O&M incentive fee, and outlined low-CapEx growth opportunities in Puerto Rico and Brazil's June 2025 capacity auction.

negative_highlights: Q4 revenue declined 12% YoY (1% ex-barter) and adjusted EBITDA fell $2.2M to $9.9M
2025 adjusted EBITDA guidance of $20M-$30M is a significant drop from $39.3M in 2024
Green coffee costs are locked in 35% higher for 2025, with no price increases built into guidance
positive_highlights: FY2024 adjusted EBITDA tripled to $39.3M and gross margin expanded 950 bps to 41.2%
Free cash flow improved by over $55 million year-over-year, turning positive
Wholesale revenue grew 9% in 2024 (13% excluding barter), with FDM sales up 3.5x
summary: Q4 2024 revenue fell 12% YoY (or 1% excluding barter liquidations) as DTC and Outpost declined, while adjusted EBITDA dropped $2.2M to $9.9M. For FY2024, gross margin expanded 950 bps to 41.2% and adjusted EBITDA tripled to $39.3M, with free cash flow improving by over $55M. 2025 guidance calls for revenue of $395M-$425M and adjusted EBITDA of $20M-$30M, down sharply from 2024 due to green coffee inflation, loyalty reserve cycling, and energy launch investments. Management highlighted strong early energy distribution (17% ACV in launch month) and expects continued growth, but the first quarter will face an $11.8M revenue headwind.

negative_highlights: Supply chain issues delayed pharma-grade Niagen availability by 2-3 months
2025 G&A expected to increase by $5-6M due to Dartmouth reversal absence
Competitive threats from companies with misleading practices noted
positive_highlights: Record Q4 revenue of $29.1M, up 37% YoY
Full-year net income of $8.6M versus loss of $4.9M in 2023
Pharmaceutical-grade ingredient sales up 96% YoY in Q4
summary: ChromaDex reported record Q4 2024 revenue of $29.1 million, up 37% year-over-year, and net income of $7.2 million, versus breakeven a year earlier. Full-year revenue grew 19% to $99.6 million with net income of $8.6 million, a sharp turnaround from a $4.9 million loss in 2023. Management guided to approximately 18% revenue growth for 2025, with modest gross margin improvement, and highlighted a pending company name change and progress in pharmaceutical-grade Niagen and clinical studies.

negative_highlights: Wound care segment missed expectations due to a deliberate pause on new initiative onboarding at year-end.
Negative pressure wound therapy equipment sales were lower due to a difficult prior-year comparison including a surge in leases.
Effective tax rate spiked to 59% for the quarter due to equity compensation deduction shortages and non-cash NOL utilization.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA increased 22% YoY to $7.5 million, driven by higher treatment volumes and favorable revenue mix.
Gross margin expanded 120 bps sequentially to 53.8%, aided by high-margin oncology and rental growth.
Operating cash flow hit an all-time record of $20.5 million for the full year.
summary: InfuSystem reported Q4 FY2024 net revenue of $33.8 million (up 7% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $7.5 million (up 22% YoY), with gross margins expanding to 53.8%. The company delivered on its full-year targets, achieving an adjusted EBITDA margin of 18.8% after one-time technology upgrade costs. Management raised guidance for FY2025 revenue growth to 8-10% and expects adjusted EBITDA margins to exceed 18.8%, potentially reaching above 20% excluding the current year's ERP upgrade expenses.

negative_highlights: Gross margins declined from 34.4% to 34.1% in Q4 due to negative product mix and lower margin sales.
Adjusted EBITDA margins contracted from 19.3% to 17.5% as operating leverage was offset by increased compensation expenses.
Net income for the full year decreased 19% primarily due to $8.8 million in pretax debt refinancing costs.
positive_highlights: Prepaid segment delivered exceptional performance with a 59% Q4 increase driven by fraud-focused packaging solutions (PACS Gene) and healthcare verticals.
Debit and credit business grew 12% in the quarter, led by eco-friendly contactless cards which now represent approximately 90% of chip card volume.
Free cash flow generation was strong at $34.1 million for FY2024 despite higher capital spending.
summary: CPI Card Group reported Q4 FY2024 net sales growth of 22% driven by a 59% surge in the prepaid segment and 12% growth in debit/credit segments. Adjusted EBITDA rose 10% to $21.9 million, though margins contracted slightly from 34.4% to 34.1%. For full year FY2024, net sales grew 8%, prepaid exceeded expectations with over $100M in revenue, and free cash flow reached $34.1 million.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA declined 1% full-year and $15 million in Q4 due to a one-time increase of ~$25m in credit losses from the divested direct marketing business.
Reported revenue growth was muted at +6% (organic) because FX, interest, and disposed business headwinds offset underlying performance.
FY2025 guidance for reported revenue is flat to low single-digit (+1.7B-$1.734B), reflecting the ongoing impact of the divestiture.
positive_highlights: Full-year GAAP net income turned positive at $22 million, compared to a loss of $20 million the prior year.
Unlevered free cash flow generation remained strong at nearly $300 million for FY24 (66% conversion).
Digital Wallet segment adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 90 bps YoY to 44.3%, driven by operational execution.
summary: Paysafe reported Q4 FY2024 revenue of $420 million (up 1% YoY) and full-year revenue of $1.7 billion (up 6%), though Adjusted EBITDA declined to $103 million for the quarter ($452m full year, down 1%) due to accelerated exits in the divested direct marketing business and associated credit losses. Management provided new adjusted EPS guidance for FY2025 of $2.21-$2.51 per share with revenue growth expected between flat and +2%, citing a one-time portfolio rationalization impact that will normalize margins in 2025.

negative_highlights: Q4 net income slightly down year-over-year due to warrant impact
Full-year combined ratio of 94% above 90% target due to hurricanes
Elevated technology and State Farm investments create near-term margin drag
positive_highlights: Q4 revenue up 19% to $292 million, exceeding expectations
Full-year operating income increased sixfold to $66 million
2025 guidance calls for 30-40% net income growth and 21-29% adjusted EBITDA growth
summary: Hagerty reported Q4 2024 total revenue up 19% to $292 million, with written premiums up 13% and membership/marketplace revenue up 68%. Full-year operating income jumped to $66 million from $10 million, and adjusted EBITDA rose 41% to $124 million. Management guided 2025 total revenue growth of 12-13%, adjusted EBITDA of $150-160 million (up 21-29%), and net income of $102-110 million (up 30-40%), despite $11 million in wildfire losses and elevated technology investments. They expect accelerating growth from State Farm Classic Plus conversions and new Enthusiast Plus product, with margin expansion resuming in 2026-2027.

negative_highlights: Net loss remained at $5.3 million for the quarter
RNS growth ex-Nautilus cases was 27% vs 19% total, implying study case drag
Dixie Medical products have lower gross margins, slightly offsetting gains
positive_highlights: Fourth quarter revenue grew 19% to $21.5 million
Full-year revenue exceeded guidance at $79.9 million
Gross margin improved for RNS products on higher volumes
summary: NeuroPace reported Q4 2024 revenue of $21.5 million, up 19% YoY, and full-year revenue of $79.9 million, up 22% YoY, exceeding original guidance of $73-77 million. Gross margins were stable at 75.4% in Q4, operating expenses rose only 7%, and net loss improved to $5.3 million from $6.2 million a year ago. The company regains capital via a public offering, repurchased KCK shares, and projected cash sufficient to breakeven. Management is confident about ongoing growth, driven by record active prescribers and progress on Project CARE and clinical trials.

negative_highlights: Q4 AFFO per share ($0.37) was $0.08 below the prior year period's adjusted EPS of $0.40.
Full-year rental income decreased by approximately $400,000 due to property dispositions in Q1 2024 and corresponding straight-line rent adjustments.
Acquisition pipeline remains thin with management explicitly stating they are not compelled to note assets just for the sake of growth.
positive_highlights: Revolver debt reduced by $120 million ($150m to $30m) saving approximately $300,000 annually in unused fees while maintaining liquidity for opportunistic acquisitions.
Interest rate swaps successfully locked in a weighted average fixed interest rate of 4.27% on all indebtedness following the exercise of put options at favorable rates.
Tenant base remains resilient to tariffs with no significant pass-through issues, and two tenants have requested footprint expansions.
summary: Modiv reported Q4 FY2024 revenue of $11.7 million and AFFO per share of $0.37, which missed the prior year's adjusted EPS of $0.40 due to a property disposition in Q1 offset by straight-line rent decreases. Management maintained full-year 2025 guidance without raising it despite tariff implementation and reduced revolver availability from $150 million to $30 million for fee savings. The company emphasized patience on acquisitions, citing an opaque economic landscape and volatile market conditions as reasons for not pursuing deals that do not meet strict criteria.

negative_highlights: GAAP net loss of $15 million (-$0.65/share) on $24.4 million of unrealized portfolio losses
GAAP book value per share fell 9.8% QoQ to $10.17 and economic book value fell 6.6% to $13.10
90-day-plus delinquencies rose to 2.4% from 1.85% in Q3
positive_highlights: Net interest income rose 9% QoQ and 20% YoY to $9.9 million, with interest income up 16% QoQ
Full-year operating expenses fell ~14% YoY to $13.6 million excluding stock comp and securitization costs
Book value indicated up just over 6% from year-end (about 3% net of dividend) as of late February, recouping part of the Q4 decline
summary: Q4 GAAP net loss was $15 million (-$0.65/share) driven by $24.4 million of unrealized losses on the securitized loan portfolio, while distributable earnings were $9.9 million ($0.42/share). Net interest income rose 9% QoQ and 20% YoY to $9.9 million on 16% QoQ growth in interest income, with operating expenses down 14% for the year. GAAP book value per share fell 9.8% to $10.17 and economic book value dropped 6.6% to $13.10, both attributed to rate and spread moves; management cited book value up roughly 6% (about 3% net of dividend) quarter-to-date and expects NII to keep growing through 2025, though no formal guidance was given. Delinquencies rose to 2.4% from 1.85% but were framed as a return to normalized 2-3% levels, improving ~10 bps in January.

negative_highlights: Hardware revenue grew only 7% YoY in Q4, indicating slower growth in that segment
2025 guidance relies on ~$25 million of inorganic contribution, but only ~$10 million comes from closed deals; the rest depends on a pipeline not yet executed
Organic revenue growth was 23% in 2024 and is guided to at least 25% in 2025, but M&A contribution in recent quarters (Q3/Q4) was around 20% of growth, raising questions about the acceleration needed
positive_highlights: Q4 gross margin expanded to 46.1% from 39.9% YoY; full-year gross margin improved to 45.1% from 37.5%
Q4 adjusted EBITDA reached a record $12.8 million (14.4% of revenue), up nearly $9 million YoY
Recurring revenue grew 49% to ~$63 million in Q4 and now represents 71% of total revenue; ARPU disclosed for the first time at $215, up 12%
summary: Nayax reported Q4 revenue of $89 million, up ~34% YoY, with recurring revenue up 49% to ~$63 million (71% of total). Gross margin expanded to 46.1% from 39.9%, adjusted EBITDA hit a record $12.8 million (14.4% of revenue), and Q4 net income was $1.6 million versus a $3.3 million loss a year ago. For FY2024, revenue was $314 million (33% growth, 34% constant currency), adjusted EBITDA more than quadrupled to $35.5 million (above the $30-35 million guidance range), and free cash flow was $18 million. For 2025, the company guided revenue of $410-425 million (30-35% growth, including at least 25% organic) and adjusted EBITDA of $65-70 million, while reaffirming its 2028 targets of ~35% annual revenue growth, 50% gross margin, and 30% adjusted EBITDA margin. No major negative surprises, though M&A remains a meaningful part of the 2025 bridge (~$10 million from closed deals, with pipeline to fill the remainder).

negative_highlights: Full-year gross margin contracted to 19.2% due to a $2.8 million nonrecurring inventory charge.
Average revenue per customer declined across segments (Lab Essentials -7%, Clinical Solutions -25%).
Management noted recent softening in biopharma demand with customers delaying orders and reducing budgets.
positive_highlights: Q4 and full-year revenue grew sequentially and year-over-year respectively ($9.3M Q4 vs $7.9M prior quarter; +18%).
Free cash outflow significantly improved from -$26.7 million in FY2023 to -$13.5 million in FY2024.
Gross margin expanded sequentially to 23.0% in Q4 driven by higher Clinical Solutions mix and reduced headcount.
summary: Alpha Teknova reported Q4 FY2024 revenue of $9.3 million (up 18% YoY) and full-year revenue of $37.7 million (up 3% YoY or 11% excluding a one-time prior year order). The company reduced its annual free cash outflow to $13.5 million from $26.7 million in the prior year, finishing below guidance. Management provided FY2025 revenue guidance of $39-42 million (midpoint ~7% growth), noting that while momentum exists, macro uncertainty has caused some customers to delay orders.

negative_highlights: Net loss from continuing operations to commons of $92.7 million ($2.25/share) and adjusted operating loss of $40.8 million ($0.99/share)
Group calendar-year combined ratio of 117.6% including retroactive reinsurance effects
E&S reserve increase of $38.4 million gross ($8.9 million net) for the quarter on higher severity and frequency in primary GC and manufacturers/contractors
positive_highlights: E&S accident-year combined ratio of 89.3% excluding legacy structures versus 91.8% as reported
Specialty Admitted full-year combined ratio of 92.2% with underwriting profit up 68.6%; expense ratio improved to 14.4% from 19.6%
Record submissions in 2024 and a 9% positive renewal rate change, with 11.2% Q4 growth excluding excess casualty
summary: James River reported a Q4 adjusted net operating loss of $40.8 million ($0.99/share) and a net loss to commons of $92.7 million ($2.25/share), driven largely by $52.8 million of top-up ADC consideration and a $27 million deemed dividend on the amended Series A preferred. E&S calendar-year combined ratio was 115.1%, but on an accident-year basis was 89.3% excluding the retroactive structures, versus 91.8% reported; Specialty Admitted posted a 95.3% Q4 combined ratio and 92.2% full year. Management guided to a mid-teen 2025 operating return on tangible common equity with a similar accident-year loss ratio, and noted net investment income of $22 million in Q4. Renewal rate was 9% for 2024, submissions set a record, and E&S grew 2% in Q4 (11.2% excluding excess casualty).

negative_highlights: Q4 revenue down 9% year-over-year, and full-year revenue down 7%
Accessories and materials declined 20% for the full year
Active users down 0.7% and 90-day engaged users down 3.1% year-over-year
positive_highlights: Paid subscribers up 7% year-over-year to 2.96 million, with 121,000 sequential increase
Full-year gross margin improved to 49.5% from 44.9%
New Cricut Explore 4 and Maker 4 launched with positive initial feedback
summary: Cricut reported Q4 2024 revenue of $209.3 million, down 9% year-over-year, with full-year revenue down 7% to $712.5 million. Despite profitability growth (net income up 17% to $62.8 million for the year) and a 7% increase in paid subscribers to 2.96 million, management expressed disappointment with sales decline and soft engagement metrics, and guided for lower operating income in 2025 due to accelerated investments. New machine launches (Explore 4 and Maker 4) received positive early feedback, but the company faces pressure in accessories and materials due to private label competition.

negative_highlights: BioPharma revenue declined by approximately $4 million year-over-year due to tightened industry budgets.
Latin America volume growth was weak in Q4 following the acquisition of a top customer, though partially recovered.
2025 guidance assumes flat ASP and does not factor in material BioPharma growth.
positive_highlights: Adjusted gross margin expanded 80 bps to 74.2% in Q4 due to compute optimizations.
Record implementation of 35 new customers in Q4, significantly above the prior quarter average.
Strong pipeline visibility with MSK-ACCESS and MSK-IMPACT applications generating over 60 unique opportunities.
summary: SOPHiA reported Q4 FY2024 revenue of $17.7 million (up 4% YoY) and full-year revenue of $65.2 million (up 4% YoY), driven by clinical volume growth while BioPharma headwinds impacted overall performance. Management provided 2025 guidance for revenue between $72 million and $76 million, representing a 10% to 17% increase on a reported basis, with adjusted EBITDA loss expected to narrow to between $35 million and $39 million. The company highlighted strong new customer implementation rates in Q4 and the ramp-up of MSK-ACCESS and MSK-IMPACT applications as key drivers for the second half of 2025.

negative_highlights: Net interest margin fell to 7.84% from 8.20% a year ago, with cost of funds up 60 bps YoY to 4.12% and management declining to call a bottom
Provision for credit loss was $20.6 million versus $10.8 million a year ago; recreation net charge-offs were $16.9 million, 4.35% of the average portfolio
2025 portfolio growth guided to mid-to-high single digits, below prior years, and quarterly opex guided up to $21-21.5 million from $17.2 million
positive_highlights: Net income of $10.1 million ($0.43/share) was the highest quarter of 2024; full-year EPS was $1.52 on $35.9 million of net income
Loan originations exceeded $1 billion for the first time in company history, with total loans up 12% YoY to $2.5 billion
Quarterly dividend raised 10% to $0.11, the second increase since reinstatement in 2022; over 570,000 shares repurchased in the year at an average $8.07
summary: Q4 net income was $10.1 million, or $0.43 per share, the highest quarter of 2024, with full-year net income of $35.9 million and EPS of $1.52; net interest income rose 6% YoY to $52 million but slipped 1% QoQ. Net interest margin on gross loans fell 36 bps YoY and 27 bps QoQ to 7.84%, pressured by a 7 bp rise in cost of funds and $427,000 of reversed interest on two commercial loans placed on non-accrual. Guidance was qualitative: 2025 portfolio growth of mid-to-high single digits, below prior years, with quarterly opex stepping up to roughly $21-21.5 million from the $17.2 million reported. The dividend was raised 10% to $0.11 and the company agreed in principle to settle the SEC matter for a $3 million charge, partly offset by a $5.5 million insurance benefit.

negative_highlights: Surgical glaucoma revenue fell note weakness in of expectations due to the new Medicare LCDs effective mid-quarter which had a pronounced impact on Q4 results
Q1 2025 guidance explicitly anticipates low-to-mid double-digit decline compared to prior year due to full quarter impact of multiple MIGS procedure restrictions
Dry eye revenue declined sequentially as management shifted focus from volume growth in cash-pay SmartLids to establishing reimbursed market access
positive_highlights: Total cash used for operations improved significantly, with net cash generated in Q4 of $1.8 million versus a drawdown previously seen
Surgical glaucoma ordering accounts increased by 7% sequentially and account utilization rose by 6%
TearCare has established a commercial foundation with over 1,500 eye care facilities performing more than 65,000 procedures to date
summary: Sight Sciences reported Q4 FY2024 revenue of $19.1 million (up 2% YoY), driven by a 9% increase in surgical glaucoma but offset by an expected decline in dry eye due to price increases and strategic focus on reimbursement access rather than volume growth. Management initiated full-year 2025 guidance for total revenue between $70-75 million, explicitly factoring in headwinds from new Medicare LCDs restricting multiple MIGS procedures at the same time as cataract surgery and uncertainty regarding TearCare commercial coverage timing. The company expects Q1 2025 revenue to be down low-to-mid double digits compared to the prior year.

negative_highlights: Q4 gross margin contracted 240 bps to 47.9% from 50.3%, and operating earnings were flat at $11.5 million
Full-year sales fell 9% to $290 million, driven by a 27% decline in BOGS, with wholesale operating earnings down 5%
