New China tariffs lift the leather footwear duty from 26% to 36%, with the company average tariff around 25%; management says it will likely need to raise prices and cannot fully mitigate
positive_highlights: Legacy brands grew 8% in Q4 with Florsheim up 22% and Nunn Bush up 4%
Full-year gross margin expanded to 45.3% from 44.9% on lower inbound freight costs
Record full-year net earnings of $30.3 million ($3.16/share) with $77.3 million cash and securities and no debt, plus a $2/share special dividend paid January 2025
summary: Q4 net sales were flat at $80.5 million versus $80.6 million, with gross margin contracting to 47.9% from 50.3% and operating earnings flat at $11.5 million; net earnings rose to $10.0 million ($1.04/share) from $8.5 million ($0.90) on lower tax and higher interest income. Full-year sales fell 9% to $290 million with operating earnings down 11% to $36.6 million, while net earnings were a record $30.3 million ($3.16/share). No formal 2025 guidance was given, but management flagged new US tariffs on Chinese goods (total leather footwear duty rising from 26% to 36%) that will raise cost of goods and likely require price increases. BOGS fell 17% in Q4 on mild winter weather, offset by an 8% rise in the legacy brands and Florsheim up 22%.

negative_highlights: Q4 revenue declined 4.5% year-over-year to $498.1 million.
Full-year adjusted EBITDA fell $33 million to $168.3 million from $201 million pro forma.
Equipment gross margins compressed due to oversupply, with deliberate low-margin used-equipment sales.
positive_highlights: Sequential equipment sales rose $69 million from Q3, indicating a post-election rebound.
Reduced net debt by $61 million in 2H 2024 through a $45 million fleet reduction.
2025 adjusted EBITDA guidance of $175–$190 million implies growth over 2024's $168.3 million.
summary: Alta reported Q4 revenue of $498.1 million, down 4.5% year-over-year, with adjusted EBITDA of $40.7 million and full-year 2024 revenue of approximately $1.88 billion (flat vs 2023) and adjusted EBITDA of $168.3 million, down from $201 million pro forma. Equipment margins were weak due to an oversupplied market and deliberate low-margin used-equipment sales, while product support and rental underperformed on mild weather and reduced workdays. Management guided 2025 adjusted EBITDA to $175–$190 million, a modest step up from 2024, excluding aggressive equipment growth assumptions, and cited a $7 million margin benefit and $9 million product support improvement. The company reduced net debt by $61 million in the second half via $45 million fleet reduction and ended with $330 million liquidity.

negative_highlights: Full-year revenue declined 4% YoY due to the conclusion of Emergency Connectivity Fund (ECF) and Affordable Connectivity Program (ACP), which impacted US telecom segment revenues.
A $35.3 million goodwill impairment charge in Q1 drove a full-year operating loss of $0.8 million, reversing prior year income.
US domestic revenue fell 29% for the quarter as legacy mobile broadband customers exited and construction revenue remained lower.
positive_highlights: International segment delivered steady performance with adjusted EBITDA growing 9.7% YoY driven by high-speed data subscriber growth and operational improvements.
US business saw a 44% increase in high-speed capable customers over the three-year investment cycle, expanding fiber route miles by 32%.
Company returned capital to shareholders via $10 million in stock repurchases and maintained dividends of $14.7 million during FY2024.
summary: ATN International reported Q4 FY2024 revenue of $680.5 million (down 9% YoY) and full-year revenue of $729.1 million (down 4%), driven by the sunset of US government programs like ECF/ACP, lower construction revenue, and a goodwill impairment charge of $35.3 million that caused a full-year net loss of $26.4 million versus income in the prior year. Adjusted EBITDA declined to $184.1 million for the full year as US telecom revenues fell, while international segment adjusted EBITDA grew 9.7% YoY on modest revenue growth and margin expansion. Management provided a flat-to-slightly-down outlook for Q1 2025 due to restructuring charges similar in size to last year's first quarter.

negative_highlights: Q4 net sales declined 20.9% year-over-year driven by oversupply in the cannabis industry.
Adjusted gross profit margin contracted significantly to 9.6% from 24.3% last year due to lower sales and mix shifts.
Full-year adjusted EBITDA missed guidance primarily due to fourth quarter performance.
positive_highlights: Proprietary brand mix improved to approximately 52% in Q4 from 35% in 2020, though it slipped slightly in the quarter.
U.S. e-commerce sales increased over 25% in 2024.
Non-cannabis and non-U.S./Canadian sales mix increased by nearly 200 basis points in 2024.
summary: Hydrofarm reported Q4 FY2024 net sales of $37.3 million, down 20.9% year-over-year due to a 16.8% volume mix decrease and 3.9% pricing decline driven by industry oversupply. Adjusted EBITDA was a loss of $7.3 million in the quarter, with full-year adjusted EBITDA falling short of guidance. Management lowered its full-year 2025 net sales outlook to a decline between 10% and 20% compared to 2024 levels.

negative_highlights: Q4 revenue down 28% YoY to $33.6M
Adjusted EBITDA margin fell to 6.4% due to lower capacity utilization
Wind tower activity expected flat through 2026
positive_highlights: Orders increased 85% YoY to $37M, highest intake in nearly two years
Industrial Solutions achieved record full-year orders and revenue
Cost actions delivered ~$4M annualized savings
summary: Broadwind's Q4 2024 revenue fell 28% YoY to $33.6M, with adjusted EBITDA of $2.1M and margin of 6.4%, reflecting continued wind and oil/gas softness. Orders rebounded 85% YoY to ~$37M, the highest in nearly two years, across all segments. Full-year revenue was $143M and adjusted EBITDA $13.3M. 2025 guidance is $140M-$160M revenue and $13M-$15M adjusted EBITDA, roughly flat to slightly up. Management cites cost actions and diversification, but expects wind tower activity to remain flat through 2026.

negative_highlights: Non-GAAP gross margin turned negative at -5.2% from +19.5% in Q4 2023; GAAP gross margin was -14.9%
Non-GAAP adjusted EBITDA worsened to -$4.5 million from -$1.9 million a year earlier
Q1 2025 revenue guidance of $4.8-5.1 million is below the roughly $5.3 million consensus, partly due to the Q1-to-Q4 pull-in
positive_highlights: Revenue of $6.7 million exceeded the midpoint of prior guidance by approximately $600,000
Cash and restricted cash rose to $135.9 million, up $111 million since December 31, 2023, on strategic transaction proceeds
Thailand transition reached its year-end milestone of roughly 75% of volume moved, with the three remaining customers expected transferred by end of Q2
summary: Q4 FY2024 revenue was $6.7 million, roughly $600,000 above the midpoint of prior guidance, but only because a customer pulled Q1 2025 deliveries forward. GAAP and non-GAAP gross margins were negative 14.9% and negative 5.2%, down from positive 16.2% and 19.5% a year earlier, driven by underutilization, Thailand ramp costs, and a $0.8 million inventory write-down plus $0.2 million equipment disposal from a phased-out legacy customer. Non-GAAP adjusted EBITDA was negative $4.5 million versus negative $1.9 million in Q4 2023, with GAAP net loss of $4.3 million ($0.19/share). Q1 2025 revenue guidance of $4.8-5.1 million fell below the roughly $5.3 million consensus, reflecting the pull-in, while the 26-28% Q4 2025 gross margin target and $14-16 million cash use outlook were reiterated.

negative_highlights: Europe/APAC Q4 revenue up only 1% constant currency due to macro weakness
Automation still a negative $7 million EBITDA drag in 2024
North American paper market tightness causing margin pressure in Q1
positive_highlights: Q4 revenue up 17% constant currency, second best-quarter ever
Automation revenue grew >40% in 2024, expected >50% growth in 2025
Adjusted EBITDA full-year up 14%, at high end of guidance
summary: Ranpak reported Q4 2024 net revenue up 17% constant currency with 12% volume growth, driven by strong North America performance (36% revenue growth, ~39% volume) and automation's largest quarter ever. Full-year constant currency revenue grew 10%, and adjusted EBITDA grew 14%, hitting the high end of guidance. Management guided 2025 revenue growth of 5-11% and adjusted EBITDA of $88-97 million, with automation expected to grow over 50% and approach breakeven. They also announced a transformational agreement with Amazon and an AI partnership with Rabot.

negative_highlights: Coiled tubing revenue declined ~7% sequentially and utilization was only 44% in Q4.
U.S. rig count declined by ~30 rigs in 2024, with natural gas prices averaging $2.19, pressuring activity and pricing.
Q4 adjusted EBITDA was flat sequentially, with management attributing the shortfall to weather, holidays, and budget exhaustion.
positive_highlights: Cementing revenue increased ~20% from Q2 to Q4 2024, with Q4 being the best quarter of the year despite trough rig counts.
Q1 2025 revenue guidance of $146-152 million implies sequential growth over Q4 despite typical seasonality.
Completed one of the longest laterals to date in the Permian, showcasing technology and execution capabilities.
summary: Nine Energy Service reported Q4 2024 revenue of $141.4 million, up ~2% quarter-over-quarter and within the upper end of guidance, with adjusted EBITDA of $14.1 million, flat versus Q3. Full-year 2024 revenue was $554.1 million, net loss was $41.1 million, and adjusted EBITDA was $53.2 million. Management guided Q1 2025 revenue to $146-152 million, implying sequential growth, citing continued market share gains, cost cuts, and a rebound in natural gas activity. They expressed cautious optimism for 2025 as gas prices have improved.

negative_highlights: SMB gross margins contracted to 20.5% due to a one-time $3.5 million inventory write-down for obsolete licenses.
Operating expenses will face headwinds in 2025 from the migration of platforms to public cloud, converting CapEx to OpEx with an estimated ~$4M impact.
Interest expense increased by $2.5 million YoY due to higher debt levels following preferred stock redemption.
positive_highlights: Q4 revenue increased by more than 14% YoY, contributing to a full-year record performance with >16% growth.
Adjusted gross profit margin expanded 90 basis points in Q4 to 37.3%, driven by organic mix shifts and higher-margin B2B/Enterprise segments.
Full-year 2025 guidance raised for both revenue (range $965M-$1B) and adjusted EBITDA ($220M-$230M).
summary: Priority Technology reported Q4 FY2024 revenue of $227.1 million (up >14% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $51.7 million (up 16%). The company provided full-year 2025 guidance for organic revenue growth of 10-14% ($965M-$1B), which represents a raise from prior expectations, alongside adjusted EBITDA growth up to 13%. Management highlighted strong momentum in B2B and Enterprise segments while noting that Q4 results were purely organic following the sunset of Plastiq acquisition impacts.

negative_highlights: Full-year comparable same-store sales declined by 5.6% year-over-year.
Cost of goods sold increased by 80 basis points on an annualized basis due to premium menu and store count expansion.
Total adjusted EBITDA for the full year decreased slightly from $18.8M in FY23 to $16.7M, driven primarily by preopening costs.
positive_highlights: Full-year revenue of $208M exceeded the upper end of the prior year's guidance range ($200-205M).
Comparable sales returned to positive growth with +1.0% figures in January and February 2025.
Board approved a new stock buyback program for up to $5 million.
summary: The company delivered full-year revenue of $208 million and restaurant-level adjusted EBITDA margin of 17.7%, both exceeding the upper end of prior guidance ranges for revenue ($200-205M) and margins (17%-18%). While comparable sales declined by 5.6% in FY24, management highlighted a return to positive comp growth (+1%) in early Q1 2025 following menu price increases and new initiatives. For fiscal 2025, the company raised guidance expectations with revenue targets of $245-250 million and an adjusted EBITDA margin target of approximately 18%.

negative_highlights: Q4 gross margin contracted to 50.8% from 61.0%, with a $1.5 million inventory write-off cutting 680 bps and reduced throughput/yields cutting another 570 bps
Full-year net loss widened to $16.4 million ($0.12/share) from net income of $660,000 in 2023, and full-year adjusted EBITDA was a $2.3 million loss versus a $1.4 million loss prior year
Hardware revenue fell 10% for the year and is guided flat to modestly down for 2025, while international sales face ongoing EU supply chain issues
positive_highlights: Q4 revenue hit a record $31.5 million, +12% YoY and +28% for the full year to $117.3 million
Adjusted EBITDA swung to positive $438,000 in Q4 from a $695,000 loss in the prior-year period
Operating expenses fell to 56.8% of revenue from 74.5% a year earlier, with ~$5 million in cost reductions since August and headcount down over 13%
summary: Q4 FY2024 revenue was a record $31.5 million, up 12% year over year and 28% for the full year to $117.3 million. Q4 gross margin fell to 50.8% from 61.0%, hit by a $1.5 million Surgiline inventory write-off (680 bps) and 570 bps from reduced throughput/yields, while net loss narrowed to $3.2 million ($0.02/share) and adjusted EBITDA turned positive at $438,000. Full-year net loss was $16.4 million versus 2023 net income of $660,000, and full-year adjusted EBITDA was a $2.3 million loss. Guidance for FY2025 is $126–130 million revenue (8–11% growth) with biologics up mid-double-digits and hardware flat to modestly down, prioritizing profitability and cash flow over growth.

negative_highlights: Net sales declined 13.5% year-over-year to $52.3 million
Upholstery Fabrics sales fell 22.3% year-over-year to $23.6 million
Net loss widened to $4.1 million or $0.33 per diluted share from $3.2 million or $0.26 a year ago
positive_highlights: Mattress Fabrics operating loss reduced 58.3% sequentially to $433,000, following a 70.7% sequential reduction in Q2
Q3 adjusted EBITDA improved sequentially to negative $123,000, a $1.1 million improvement despite $3.4 million lower sequential sales
Hospitality contract business grew significantly year-over-year and rose slightly sequentially, reaching 40% of upholstery fabrics total sales
summary: Culp reported Q3 FY2025 net sales of $52.3 million, down 13.5% year-over-year, with a GAAP net loss of $4.1 million or $0.33 per diluted share and an adjusted operating loss of $1.6 million, a sequential improvement from Q2's $2.6 million loss despite $3.4 million lower sequential sales. Mattress Fabrics sales fell 4.6% YoY to $28.6 million, but the segment's restructuring drove a 58.3% sequential reduction in operating loss to $433,000, while Upholstery Fabrics sales dropped 22.3% YoY to $23.6 million on a significant customer's inventory realignment, with operating income of $679,000. Q3 adjusted EBITDA was near breakeven at negative $123,000, a $1.1 million sequential improvement, and management guided to Q4 net sales growth year-over-year with continued adjusted EBITDA improvement, targeting a return to consolidated operating income in fiscal 2026. The company announced an incremental $1 million in annualized cost savings plus a target of up to $2 million in additional fiscal 2026 savings, and expects $6-$8 million in net cash proceeds from the pending Canadian facility sale to pay down borrowings.

negative_highlights: Q4 revenue decreased 2% to $121.8 million and restaurant-level contribution margin fell to 11.2% from 14.7%
Q4 net loss widened to $9.7 million from $6.1 million
Announced closure of 12-15 company-owned restaurants in 2025
positive_highlights: Q1 2025 comp sales over 3% with positive traffic, exceeding fast-casual benchmark for last four months
January achieved largest single-month increase in overall guest satisfaction, closing 80% of gap to industry average
New menu items in test showed double-digit point increases in taste-of-food scores and attracted new guests
summary: In Q4 2024, Noodles & Company reported total revenue of $121.8 million, down 2% year-over-year, with system-wide comp sales up 0.8% and company comp traffic down 0.1%. Restaurant-level contribution margin fell to 11.2% from 14.7%, and adjusted EBITDA dropped to $4 million from $7.5 million. Company comp sales improved sequentially and accelerated to over 3% in the first eight weeks of 2025, with positive traffic, exceeding the fast-casual benchmark for four consecutive months. Management guided 2025 revenue of $503-$512 million, mid-single-digit comp sales growth, restaurant contribution margin of 12.5%-14.0%, and expects to close 12-15 company-owned restaurants while opening only two.

negative_highlights: Book value per common share declined by $0.20 ($3.82 vs $4.02) driven by RMBS mark-to-market losses
RMBS net interest spread narrowed to 2.9% lower than the prior quarter due to higher repo costs and reduced swap income
Ten-year yield ended Q4 at 4.57%, up nearly 80 bps q/q, creating a 'higher for longer' rate environment
positive_highlights: Internalization of management completed, expected to reduce operating expenses by $1.1M-$1.6M ($0.03-$0.05/share) starting in 2025
MSR portfolio net CPR averaged approximately 4.7% with recapture rates remaining low due to minimal refinance incentive
Repo costs seen coming down and benefits realized in the first quarter of 2025
summary: Cherry Hill reported GAAP net income of $0.29 per share and EAD of $10 cents per share for Q4 FY2024, impacted by approximately two cents in special committee expenses. Book value declined to $3.82 from $4.02 due to mark-to-market losses on RMBS assets amidst higher rates and volatility. Management noted repo costs were elevated at year-end but expect benefits in 1Q 2025 following the internalization of management.

negative_highlights: Workforce reduced by 20-25%
SVR12 was 88% in cirrhotic patients
17% non-adherence rate in phase two
positive_highlights: 98% SVR12 in adherent patients after 8 weeks
Phase three enrollment expected to begin in April
Cash runway expected to extend into 2028
summary: Atea reported positive phase two HCV data with a 98% SVR12 in adherent patients, initiating phase three enrollment in April. Cash stands at $454.7 million, expected to fund operations into 2028. The company is exploring strategic partnerships and reduced workforce by 20-25% to save $15 million through 2027.

negative_highlights: Revenue of $26.9 million fell ~4.5% year-over-year and declined from $29 million in Q3, with U.S. Coast Guard revenue down $1.7 million and non-Coast Guard GEO airtime down ~$1 million.
Airtime gross margin dropped to 28.2% from 36.5% in the prior quarter, and 41.4% excluding depreciation versus 48.6% prior quarter, due to GEO VSAT churn.
Q4 adjusted EBITDA less CapEx was negative $0.3 million versus positive $1.4 million in Q3, and 2025 revenue guidance of $115–125 million implies limited growth off the 2024 base.
positive_highlights: Starlink shipped over 1,000 units in Q4, the fourth consecutive quarterly record, with ~2,300 active maritime Starlink terminals and ~700 activations.
Recurring OpEx reduced ~10% for the full year, with Q4 OpEx of $9.3 million down 10% sequentially and 15% year-over-year on a like-for-like basis.
Total subscribing vessels rose ~4% sequentially to just below 7,100, and GEO bandwidth commitments fall $5 million in 2025 and another $5 million in 2026.
summary: KVH reported Q4 FY2024 revenue of $26.9 million, down ~4.5% year-over-year from Q4 2023 and down from $29 million in Q3, with adjusted EBITDA of $0.5 million and adjusted EBITDA less CapEx of negative $0.3 million. Airtime gross margin fell to 28.2% from 36.5% in the prior quarter, driven by GEO VSAT churn, though LEO margins remain strong and total subscribing vessels rose ~4% sequentially to just below 7,100. Management issued 2025 guidance of $115–125 million revenue and $9–15 million adjusted EBITDA, compared to full-year 2024 adjusted EBITDA of $8.1 million, and expects GEO bandwidth commitments to fall by $5 million in both 2025 and 2026. Starlink shipments exceeded 1,000 units in Q4 with ~700 activations and ~1,000 units awaiting activation, while OneWeb was added to the service portfolio and OpEx was cut ~10% for the full year.

negative_highlights: Q4 revenue was about half the level of Q3 2024, tied to automaker production cuts
Management could not state the Q4 loss figure on the call, saying it does not break it out
Vehicle launches previously expected in 2024 were delayed, and no timetables were given for the 2025 or 2026 programs
positive_highlights: Full-year loss per share of $0.04 was the lowest since the company went public
Revenue rose roughly 47% for the full year
Management expects a profitable quarter in the coming year and describes 2026 automotive programs as potentially dwarfing anything previously discussed
summary: Revenue fell sharply in Q4, which management attributed to automakers cutting production to clear inventory; full-year revenue rose roughly 47%. Full-year loss per share was $0.04, the lowest since the company went public, but management could not give the quarterly loss figure on the call. Management said it is looking for a profitable quarter in the coming year and that 2026 automotive programs could 'dwarf anything we've ever talked about,' while acknowledging that launches once expected in 2024 slipped and no new business press releases have been issued.

negative_highlights: CEO noted that production through February 2025 was only $429.4 million, indicating a slower start to the new year compared to the strong Q4 finish.
Management stated they do not formally forecast future production run rates, preferring to avoid putting limits on growth potential.
positive_highlights: Record quarter with core earnings of $0.60 and full-year core earnings of $2.03.
Loan production surged to $563 million in Q4, representing an 18% increase over Q3 and a 60% year-over-year gain.
NPL resolution gains totaled $5.6 million in Q4, driven by borrower refinancing or current payments rather than just REO sales.
summary: Velocity Financial reported a record Q4 FY2024 with core earnings of $0.60 and loan production of $563 million, an 18% sequential increase. The portfolio grew to $5.1 billion, while NPL resolution gains reached $5.6 million on resolved assets. Management expressed strong confidence in the business model, citing healthy demand, improved securitization spreads, and a durable source of returns from non-performing loan resolutions.

negative_highlights: Q4 revenue fell to $38.4M from $43.8M and core FFO per share dropped to $0.18 from $0.33 year over year
2025 core FFO guidance of $0.61-$0.70 per share implies a sharp decline from 2024's $1.01, with net debt/EBITDA guided to 8.0x-8.8x from 6.06x
Dividend cut to $0.02 per share from the prior quarterly payout; renewal rent spreads were down 6.6% for 2024
positive_highlights: 2024 leasing totaled about 1.1M sq ft, more than 4x the 2023 level, with 287,000 sq ft of new leases versus 21,000 sq ft in 2023
Portfolio WALT rose to 5.2 years from 4 years a year earlier
Fully backfilled the 136,000 sq ft Hasbro Providence building with an 11-year lease; G&A held flat guidance at $19.5M-$20.5M
summary: Q4 revenue fell to $38.4M from $43.8M a year earlier, core FFO dropped to $0.18 per share from $0.33, and the net loss widened to $32.8M ($0.59/sh) versus $16.2M ($0.29/sh). FY2024 revenue was $164.9M and core FFO $1.01 per share. 2025 core FFO guidance of $0.61-$0.70 per share implies a steep decline from 2024, with net debt to adjusted EBITDA guided up to 8.0x-8.8x from 6.06x, and the quarterly dividend was cut to $0.02 per share. Management characterized 2025-2026 as the bottom of revenue and core FFO declines, projecting growth only in 2027, while noting 2024 leasing totaled about 1.1M sq ft versus roughly a quarter of that in 2023.

negative_highlights: 2025 NOI guided to be flat to slightly below 2024, with management explicitly calling the prior growth rate 'not sustainable'
Commercial/Industrial NOI fell 15% in Q4 as a 50,000 sq ft tenant (10% of the segment) defaulted; Cranberry occupancy expected to fall from 96% to ~60% as all tenants roll off
D.C. multifamily concessions and vacancies pressured by new deliveries, with renewal growth limited to ~2.5% and same-store revenue up only 2%
positive_highlights: Pro rata NOI up 21% in Q4 to $9.1M and 26% for the year to $38.1M, with six stabilized multifamily projects contributing an additional $4.6M and Mining adding $2.7M
Mining and Royalty segment NOI rose 34% to $3.5M, described by management as 'as strong as it has ever been'
Annual pro rata NOI CAGR of 29.5% over the last three years
summary: Q4 net income fell 41.7% to $1.68M ($0.09/sh) versus $2.88M ($0.15/sh), though prior-year included a $1.98M one-time gain. Full-year net income rose 20.4% to $6.39M ($0.34/sh) and pro rata NOI rose 21% in Q4 and 26% for the year, with Mining NOI up 34% offsetting a 15% decline in Commercial/Industrial NOI from a tenant default. Management guided 2025 NOI to be flat to slightly below 2024, citing non-repeatable 2024 items, D.C. multifamily supply pressure, and expected vacancies at Cranberry and the new Chelsea building.

negative_highlights: 2025 consolidated operating profit guided to only a modest increase, with Coal Mining segment operating profit expected to decline modestly on lower Mississippi Lignite per-ton pricing and higher operating expenses
Net income expected to decrease moderately in 2025 excluding the anticipated non-cash pension settlement charge

Recurring inventory write-downs (including ~$6 million flagged by an analyst) in the coal segment, plus a lower Q4 operating profit trend at North American Mining in the second half on hurricane-related demand reduction
positive_highlights: Q4 net income of $7.6 million ($1.02 per share) versus a prior-year net loss of $44 million ($5.88 per share) that included a $65.9 million pretax impairment
Coal Mining segment adjusted EBITDA rose 32.6% to $4.2 million on higher Falkirk pricing and increased customer requirements; full-year adjusted EBITDA up 116% to $59.4 million
Two new contracts and one amended contract at North American Mining expected to deliver ~$20 million NPV of after-tax cash flows over 6- to 20-year terms
summary: NACCO reported Q4 2024 operating profit of $3.9 million and net income of $7.6 million ($1.02 per share), a sharp swing from the prior-year operating loss of $67.4 million ($5.88 loss per share) that included a $65.9 million impairment charge; adjusted EBITDA rose to $9.0 million from $7.1 million. For 2025 management guides to a modest year-over-year increase in consolidated operating profit, with Coal Mining operating profit down modestly on lower Mississippi Lignite per-ton pricing, North American Mining improving mostly in the second half, Minerals Management comparable, and net income down moderately excluding an expected non-cash pension settlement charge. Segment detail was mixed: coal-adjusted EBITDA up 32.6% on the Falkirk price reset, North American Mining swung to an $0.8 million operating profit, and Minerals Management's improvement was largely a prior-year impairment comparison.

negative_highlights: Q4 net loss widened due to a noncash unrealized loss on commodity derivatives compared to prior quarter gains
Production decreased by 0.5 MBoe/day driven by gas volume interruptions and residue realizations in East Texas
Beta production was significantly impacted by 10 ESP failures requiring workovers
positive_highlights: Adjusted net income was $5.1 million excluding unrealized derivative losses
Full-year adjusted EBITDA of $103 million met guidance and represented an increase from the prior year
Beta wells A50 and C59 continue to perform above pre-drill type curves with IRRs in excess of 100%
summary: Amplify Energy reported a Q4 net loss of $7.4 million versus prior quarter income due to unrealized commodity derivative losses and production downtime at Beta from ESP failures; excluding these items, adjusted net income was $5.1 million with full-year adjusted EBITDA of $103 million meeting guidance. Management provided 2025 production guidance of 19k-21k MBoe/day (midpoint up 7% YoY) and LOE guidance at the midpoint of $143M, while announcing a definitive merger with Juniper Capital expected to close in Q2 2025.

negative_highlights: Full-year net loss widened to $11.8M from $9.2M, and full-year adjusted EBITDA declined to $22.5M from $23.3M.
Full-year gross margin contracted to 69% from 72% (non-GAAP to 74% from 76%).
HR compliance group faces continued headwinds in the first half, and Q1 adjusted EBITDA guidance of $6–7M is roughly flat versus Q1 2024.
positive_highlights: Q4 adjusted EBITDA rose to $6.2M with a 20% margin, up from $2.8M and 11% in the prior-year period.
Recurring revenue reached 96% of total revenue for the full year, up from 84%, with full-year recurring revenue up 15% to $114M.
Full-year bookings grew 86% and contracted backlog reached $79M, up from approximately $20M at year-end 2023.
summary: Q4 revenue of $30.8M grew 17% YoY (22% excluding ERTC), with recurring revenue up 14%; full-year revenue was $119.8M, up 17% ex-ERTC, and recurring revenue reached 96% of total (from 84%). Q4 adjusted EBITDA was $6.2M (20% margin) versus $2.8M (11%) a year ago, but the full year net loss widened to $11.8M from $9.2M. Management reiterated 2025 revenue guidance of $134–138M (mid-teens growth) and adjusted EBITDA margins of 23–24%, and guided Q1 revenue to $33–35M. Q4 bookings grew 28%, full-year bookings rose 86%, and contracted backlog stood at $79M. Management characterized demand as steady with a flat employment outlook, flagged continued HR compliance headwinds in H1, and noted margin expansion will be back-end loaded.

negative_highlights: Total revenue fell 0.6% YoY and GAAP EPS dropped to $0.24 from $0.33 as prior-year ICFA revenue did not recur
Operating expenses rose 6.3% to $43.3 million, outpacing regulated revenue growth of 4.9%, with depreciation up $1.3 million and O&M up $1.1 million

CEO acknowledged high inflation and cost drivers have caught up with earnings growth, and the largest utilities' proposed $6.5 million rate increase is not slated for first implementation until May 2026
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA rose 5.2% to $26.7 million and adjusted net income was flat at $0.26/share, isolating recurring operations from variable ICFA revenue
Active connections grew 4.4% to 64,520 and regulated revenue rose 4.9% to $52.7 million
Farmers rate case settlement authorizes ~$1.1 million, over 85% of the request, and the ACC unanimously approved the Tucson acquisition, taking that region from 5,000 to 7,000 connections
summary: Total 2024 revenue was $52.7 million, down 0.6% YoY, as 2023 ICFA revenue did not recur; regulated revenue rose 4.9% to $52.7 million on 4.4% connection growth to 64,520. GAAP net income fell to $5.8 million ($0.24/share) from $8 million ($0.33), while adjusted net income was flat at $6.3 million ($0.26) and adjusted EBITDA rose 5.2% to $26.7 million. Operating expenses rose 6.3% to $43.3 million, driven by $1.3 million more depreciation and $1.1 million higher O&M. The company filed a Santa Cruz/Palo Verde rate case seeking ~$6.5 million (rate base ~$165 million, +47%), settled the Farmers case at ~$1.1 million (>85% of request), and won ACC approval of the Tucson acquisition; cost inflation has caught up with earnings growth.

negative_highlights: Q4 revenue declined $1 million year over year to $7.7 million from $8.7 million
Q4 gross margin contracted to 32% from 33%, and the Trust Codes Global business was divested with a $1.2 million operating loss excluding impairments in 2024
Management declined to provide 2025 guidance and said the lost customer will continue to drag on Q1 and Q2 comparatives
positive_highlights: Full-year gross margin expanded to 36% from 32% in 2023
Adjusted EBITDA was positive for the sixth consecutive quarter and rose to $1 million for the full year versus $0.4 million in 2023
Completed a $4.7 million warrant inducement raise in January 2025, retired the term loan, and reduced convertible notes from $1.1 million to $0.8 million
summary: Q4 2024 revenue fell to $7.7 million from $8.7 million a year earlier, a $1 million decline driven by a discontinued Premium services contract and a shortened peak season, while gross margin slipped to 32% from 33%. Full-year gross margin still improved to 36% from 32% in 2023, adjusted EBITDA was positive for a sixth straight quarter at $1 million for the year versus $0.4 million, and the net loss was $0.5 million, or $0.05 per diluted share. Management gave no 2025 guidance and said the previously disclosed customer loss will drag on comparables in Q1 and Q2; it declined to predict timing of capital deployment. New capital actions included a $4.7 million warrant inducement raise, retirement of the term loan, and a $15.8 million aftermarket offering; convertible debt fell to $0.8 million.

negative_highlights: Commission expense increased by $0.5 million (12%) driven by swings in revenue mix.
The company remains in a loss position with net loss of $9.1 million and adjusted EBITDA loss of $0.3 million.
positive_highlights: Net loss decreased by $2.9 million (24%) to $9.1 million versus $12.1 million in the prior year.
Adjusted EBITDA improved significantly by 39% from a loss of $0.5 million to a loss of $0.3 million.
Total operating expenses decreased by 21% or $5.9 million due to the OneFirm strategy and cost efficiency enhancements.
summary: For the year ended December 31, 2024, Reliance Global Group reported revenues of $14.1 million, an increase of $0.3 million (2%) compared to $13.7 million in 2023. Net loss decreased by $2.9 million to $9.1 million, driven by lower intangible asset impairment charges and the liquidation of contingent warrant liabilities. Adjusted EBITDA improved significantly by 39%, moving from a loss of $0.5 million to a loss of $0.3 million.

negative_highlights: Loan portfolio contracted by $81.8 million net, with $107.5 million of payoffs against only $47.9 million of new commitments.
Weighted average risk rating increased to 2.9 from 2.7, with 12 loans rated four or five representing 27% of par, up 4% sequentially.
Net interest income decreased $0.24 per share sequentially due to loan payoffs, and a $700,000 charge-off on the Orlando hotel loan is expected in Q1.
positive_highlights: Book value per share increased to $28.87 from $27.92, aided by a $7.5 million gain on an office property sale.
Repurchased 155,000 common shares at an approximate 43% discount to book value, with a new $5 million buyback authorization.
Two remaining CRE securitizations are being refinanced with a contemplated 24-month revolving period, expected to provide attractive leverage.
summary: GAAP net income allocable to common shares was $4.1 million, or $0.52 per diluted share, including an $8.6 million net interest income and a $7.5 million gain on an office property sale. EAD was $0.48 per share versus $0.24 in Q3, driven by the $0.67 per share gain, partially offset by a $0.24 decrease in net interest income from loan payoffs. Book value per share rose to $28.87 from $27.92, and the company repurchased 155,000 shares at a 43% discount to book. The $1.5 billion loan portfolio saw $107.5 million of payoffs and net contraction, with risk rating worsening to 2.9 from 2.7, and management expects EAD to trend up from a low point in early 2025 as capital is redeployed into loans.

negative_highlights: Still unprofitable with net loss of $4.9M in Q4
Install base target not met; management withholding specific numbers pending predictability
No specific revenue guidance for 2025 beyond growth percentages
positive_highlights: Q4 revenue up 108% YoY to $4.2M, a record
Gross margin improved to 71% from 52%
CAPTAIN trial enrollment completed at 201 patients
summary: Profound Medical reported Q4 2024 revenue of $4.2 million, up 108% year over year, with gross margin expanding to 71% from 52% and net loss improving to $4.9 million from $8.9 million. Management highlighted record revenue and margin, a strong balance sheet with $54.9 million cash, and the completion of CAPTAIN trial enrollment (201 patients). They are preparing for commercial growth, with expectations of 70-75% revenue growth in 2025 and 'triple-digit' growth by 2026.

negative_highlights: Personal protection product sales declined slightly, consistent with lower adjusted NICS checks
GAAP operating expenses were flat at $25.8 million, limiting operating leverage despite the sales increase
Approximately $1 million of sales shifted from Q4 into Q3, which may modestly affect the sequential growth trajectory
positive_highlights: Net sales rose 9.5% year-over-year to $58.5 million, with outdoor lifestyle up 15.1% and shooting sports up nearly 3%
Non-GAAP EPS more than doubled to $0.21 from $0.08, and adjusted EBITDAS nearly doubled to $4.7 million
Gross margin expanded 200 basis points to 44.7% GAAP, driven by higher volumes and lower inbound freight costs
summary: American Outdoor Brands reported Q3 FY2025 net sales of $58.5 million, a 9.5% year-over-year increase and ahead of expectations, with growth in both outdoor lifestyle (+15.1%) and shooting sports (+3%). Non-GAAP EPS was $0.21 versus $0.08 a year ago, and adjusted EBITDAS nearly doubled to $4.7 million. The company narrowed full-year net sales guidance to $207–$210 million and raised the midpoint and adjusted EBITDAS guidance to $14.5–$15.5 million. It also reiterated FY2026 net sales guidance of $220–$230 million, citing new product launches and expanded distribution.

negative_highlights: Automotive trading revenue collapsed to RMB15M in Q4 from RMB130.2M in Q4 2023, a 88.5% decline.
Average cash cost to mine one Bitcoin in Q4 2024 was $67,769.9, a high threshold that leaves margin vulnerable to Bitcoin price drops.
The company holds 933.8 Bitcoins and plans to mine-and-hold, exposing earnings to Bitcoin volatility.
positive_highlights: Q4 revenue surged over 400% YoY to RMB668M, with Bitcoin mining contributing RMB653M.
Net income swung to RMB55.9M from a net loss of RMB103.8M in Q4 2023.
Deployed hash rate to reach about 50 EH by end of Q1 2025, making Cango the second-largest Bitcoin miner globally.
summary: Cango's Q4 2024 total revenue surged to RMB668 million from RMB130.2 million a year ago, driven by the new Bitcoin mining business (RMB653 million). Net income swung to RMB55.9 million from a net loss of RMB103.8 million. Full-year revenue was RMB804.5 million, with net income of RMB299.8 million. Management guided to 50 EH hash rate by end of Q1 2025 (from 32 EH now) and forecasts ~6,000 Bitcoins annually from the current base, while used car exports remain a secondary focus.

negative_highlights: Full-year 2024 total attendance declined 11% year over year to 390.7 million
Q4 national advertising revenue decreased due to a 22% drop in utilization and an unfavorable mix of G/PG-rated films
First quarter FY2025 adjusted OIBDA is expected to be negative ($7.5M to -$9.5M) driven by softer box office slate
positive_highlights: Q4 revenue beat expectations at $86.3 million against a guide of $82-86 million
Adjusted OIBDA exceeded guidance significantly at $35 million versus a range of $28-30 million
Platinum advertising product sales more than doubled year over year with Q4 revenue up 28%
summary: NCMI reported Q4 FY2024 revenue of $86.3 million and adjusted OIBDA of $35 million, both exceeding their respective guidance ranges ($82-86M and $28-30M). Full-year 2024 results were slightly below prior year levels with revenue at $240.8 million versus $259.8 million in 2023. Management noted Q1 FY2025 guidance of negative adjusted OIBDA ($7.5M to -$9.5M) due to a weaker film slate and government spending delays, while expressing optimism for the second half.

negative_highlights: Q4 G&A expenses rose 18.5% ($1.3 million) on higher professional fees and portfolio/systems costs, and full-year expenses grew 7.5% versus 5.3% revenue growth
Adjusted EBITDA margin was 21.1% for 2024, well below the high-20s to ~32% levels previously reached, with management flagging more hiring and expense ahead in 2025
Management said its pipeline is becoming harder to measure as RFP-driven searches decline, making apples-to-apples comparisons to prior periods difficult
positive_highlights: Q4 revenue up 12% YoY to $32.0 million and full-year revenue up 5.3% to $123.7 million
2024 gross organic inflows of $1.5 billion, the best year since at least 2015, including a $1.3 billion global value equity seed
Total AUM grew 9.6% to $36.5 billion and discretionary AUM rose 6.4% to $23.3 billion, with the pipeline increasing to $1.6 billion from $1.2 billion
summary: Silvercrest reported Q4 revenue of $32.0 million, up 12% YoY from $28.5 million, with reported net income of $2.7 million ($0.18 per Class A share) and adjusted diluted EPS of $0.20; full-year revenue rose 5.3% to $123.7 million and adjusted EBITDA was 21.1% of revenue. Total AUM reached $36.5 billion at year-end, up 9.6%, and the firm booked $1.4 billion of gross inflows in Q4 and $1.5 billion for 2024, its best organic inflow year since at least 2015, driven largely by a $1.3 billion global value equity seed. Q4 G&A rose 18.5% and 2024 expenses rose 7.5%, with management guiding compensation and G&A to remain at these levels through 2025 as it funds new hires in Atlanta, Singapore and the global value team. No explicit revenue or EPS guidance was issued; management said a return toward high-20s EBITDA margin, and possibly 2026, depends on these investments paying off.

negative_highlights: Full-year revenue guidance lowered from prior expectations to a range of $125-$135 million.
Gross margin contracted 660 bps sequentially and 490 bps YoY due to a $1.6M inventory step-up charge.
Auto EV demand slowed with customers pushing orders into the second half of 2025.
positive_highlights: Record Q4 revenue of $36.6M and full-year revenue of $130.7M achieved despite a 26% decline in semi.
Life sciences orders more than doubled to a record $2.3 million driven by induction heating solutions.
summary: inTEST reported record Q4 revenue of $36.6 million and full-year revenue of $130.7 million, driven by the AlfaMation acquisition and growth in auto EV and defense markets which offset a severe decline in semi. Management provided cautious 2025 guidance of $125-$135 million, citing customer push-outs due to tariff uncertainty and macro headwinds, while reaffirming long-term targets.

negative_highlights: Total revenue declined 2% YoY to $57.8 million, with Europe down 15% and Asia Pacific down 16%
Recurring revenue was flat quarter-over-quarter at 45% of firm-wide revenue
GAAP EPS of $0.06 depended on a $2.3 million divestiture gain; excluding it, GAAP EPS was $0.01
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA rose 11% to $6.5 million with margin up 240 bps to 11.3% despite a 2% revenue decline
Americas revenue grew 6% to $37.9 million, led by double-digit growth in banking (up 24%), energy/utilities (up 23%) and manufacturing (up 24%)
Q1 adjusted EBITDA guidance of $6.5-7.5 million is at least 45% above the prior-year first quarter
summary: ISG reported Q4 revenue of $57.8 million, down 2% YoY excluding automation, with Americas up 6% to $37.9 million while Europe fell 15% and Asia Pacific fell 16%. Adjusted EBITDA rose 11% to $6.5 million, expanding margin 240 bps to 11.3%, and adjusted EPS was flat at $0.06; GAAP EPS of $0.06 included a $2.3 million gain on the automation divestiture, without which it was $0.01. Management guided Q1 revenue to $58-59 million and adjusted EBITDA to $6.5-7.5 million, at least 45% above the prior-year Q1, and said both Q4 revenue and EBITDA landed at the high end of guidance. The company sold its automation unit for over $20 million, cut debt by $7 million in the quarter (25% for the year), and repurchased $2.3 million of stock while paying $4.5 million in dividends.

negative_highlights: Office segment NOI declined due to a large tenant exercising a partial lease termination option in Oakland
Hotel operations NOI dropped $828,000 due to construction-related occupancy decreases
FFO turned negative at -$8.7 million compared to -$9.9 million in the prior year
positive_highlights: Credit facility balance reduced significantly to $15 million from $169 million at end of Q3
Hotel renovation on Sacramento property completed with new management agreement key money expected
Multifamily occupancy increased 240 bps year-over-year despite quarter-over-quarter decline
summary: Q4 FY2024 segment NOI decreased by $1.6 million to $9.2 million compared to the prior year, driven by declines in the Office, Multifamily, Hotel, and Lending segments. FFO turned negative at -$8.7 million (vs -$9.9M prior year) due to lower operating income partially offset by a reduction in preferred dividends. Management highlighted significant progress in refinancing office assets to retire a $15 million credit facility balance down from $169 million, but noted ongoing challenges with occupancy and lease terminations.

negative_highlights: Q4 revenue was impacted by transient supply interruptions for both UDENYCA (inventory write-downs) and LOQTORZI, limiting growth potential in a rare disease space.
Management explicitly stated they are not satisfied with the current stock price despite strong execution on balance sheet deleveraging and asset sales.
LOQTORZI revenue ramp is constrained by the rarity of nasopharyngeal cancer (1-2 new patients per physician annually) and ongoing efforts to displace off-label Keytruda use.
positive_highlights: UDENYCA net sales increased 62% year-over-year in FY2024 to $206 million, driven by supply resumption after Q3 interruptions and strong demand upon re-entry into the market.
LOQTORZI achieved NCCN preferred status for metastatic nasopharyngeal cancer following guideline updates, with new account growth of 37% in Q4 despite headwinds from divestiture uncertainty.
Strategic transformation milestones reached: SEC/CFIUS reviews completed and shareholder vote scheduled to approve the UDENYCA sale.
summary: Coherus BioSciences reported Q4 FY2024 net sales of $13 million ($46.3M for UDENYCA and $7.5M for LOQTORZI), representing a sequential decline due to supply interruptions, though full-year revenue grew significantly driven by the biosimilar franchise before divestiture. Management confirmed substantial progress on the strategic transformation, including closing conditions for the UDENYCA divestiture which is expected late Q1/early Q2 2025, leaving the company with approximately $250 million in cash post-transaction to fund oncology development. The CEO expressed dissatisfaction with current stock valuation and emphasized a focus on maximizing LOQTORZI revenue as standard of care while advancing the proprietary pipeline.

negative_highlights: Total installed cost estimate increased from a prior $950 million preliminary figure to an indicative range of $1.7 billion - $2 billion.
Project timeline delayed with best-case groundbreaking pushed to mid-2026 (if capital secured) and in-service date shifted to 2028 or later depending on FID timing.
positive_highlights: Completed FEED for Project Permian (SN1) identifying no fatal technical flaws or design issues.
summary: Net Power reported a liquidity position of $533 million at year-end Q4 FY2024, down from $580 million in Q3 due to operating cash outflows and capital expenditures for La Porte upgrades. The company completed the FEED for Project Permian (SN1) but revised its total installed cost estimate upward significantly to between $1.7 billion and $2 billion, driven by inflationary pressures and site-specific challenges like inland transportation costs in West Texas. Consequently, management pushed the project timeline with a best-case groundbreaking date of 2027 and an in-service target of 2029.

negative_highlights: The DMDC and DHS programs are now expected to contribute $50-$75 million in 2025, down from the prior estimate of $60-$85 million.
A stop work order on the DHS program was only lifted in January 2025, and revenue from that program is not expected until later in 2025.
Cash flow from operations was a $10.5 million outflow and free cash flow was a $14.8 million outflow in Q4, driven by working capital buildup and one-time CapEx.
positive_highlights: Q4 revenue of $26.4 million came in near the top end of guidance of $24.5-$26.5 million, with 11% sequential growth.
Adjusted EBITDA improved by $4 million sequentially to a $0.2 million loss, which was above the top end of guidance.
GAAP gross margin expanded nearly 600 basis points year-over-year to 40.3%, and cash gross margin reached 47%, the highest since the 2020 IPO.
summary: Telos reported Q4 FY2024 revenue of $26.4 million (up 11% sequentially), near the top of guidance, with an adjusted EBITDA loss of $0.2 million, a $4 million sequential improvement. GAAP gross margin expanded nearly 600 bps year-over-year to 40.3%, driven by a mix shift to higher-margin security solutions. For Q1 FY2025, guidance implies 7-15% sequential revenue growth to $28.2-$30.2 million and an adjusted EBITDA loss of $0.8-$1.8 million. Full-year 2025 expectations include a return to revenue growth, though the estimated contribution from the DMDC and DHS programs was reduced to $50-$75 million from $60-$85 million due to revenue recognition timing, while the existing business estimate rose to ~$70 million from $60-$65 million.

negative_highlights: Q4 consolidated adjusted EBITDA fell 2.8% to $11.1M and GRE adjusted EBITDA dropped 13% to $13.4M
Full-year adjusted EBITDA declined to $48.5M from $58.2M in 2023, and 2025 guidance of $40M-$50M implies no growth
GRE Q4 gross margin contracted 55 bps to 32.4% on electricity margin compression and a shift toward fixed-price meters
positive_highlights: Full-year adjusted EBITDA of $48.5M reached the high end of 2024 guidance
Added 23,000 net new meters in Q4 and over 60,000 for the full year, up nearly 17%
GREW gross profit rose over 120% to surpass $6M in 2024 and its operating loss roughly halved
summary: Q4 revenue fell 1.9% to $102.9M and consolidated adjusted EBITDA slipped 2.8% to $11.1M, with gross margin up 40 bps to 32.5%, though a $30.9M captive insurance loss reserve drove a $20.8M operating loss. Full-year adjusted EBITDA of $48.5M landed at the high end of 2024 guidance, down from $58.2M in 2023 on lower GRE contribution, while GRE added 23,000 net meters in Q4 and over 60,000 for the year. Management maintained 2025 consolidated adjusted EBITDA guidance of $40M-$50M, implying a step down from 2024, and cited continued investment in meter acquisition and new markets including Texas dynamic power and California gas. Net meters grew nearly 17% and GREW's operating loss roughly halved, but GRE adjusted EBITDA fell 13% in Q4 on higher acquisition spend and electricity margin compression.

negative_highlights: No OpRegen Phase 2a GAlette data timing disclosed; Lineage has received no interim data and cannot guide to timing
Full-year revenue of $5.9 million was below the $8.9 million reported for 2023
OPC1 program remains pre-pivotal with new device and manufacturing process comparability work still pending FDA review before a larger trial
positive_highlights: Q4 revenue rose to ~$2.9 million from $2.1 million a year earlier, driven by higher Roche collaboration revenue
Q4 net loss narrowed to $3.3 million ($0.02/share) from $4.8 million ($0.03/share); operating expenses fell to $7.8 million from $8.2 million
Cash of $47.8 million plus ~$5.5 million January proceeds extends runway into Q1 2027; milestone warrants could add up to $36 million if OpRegen milestone is hit and stock exceeds $0.91
summary: Lineage reported Q4 2024 total revenue of ~$2.9 million versus $2.1 million in Q4 2023, with operating expenses down to $7.8 million and net loss of $3.3 million ($0.02/share) versus $4.8 million ($0.03/share). Year-end cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities were $47.8 million, plus ~$5.5 million in January 2025 net proceeds, extending runway into Q1 2027. No new financial guidance was provided, and the company continues to await any Phase 2a OpRegen data from Roche/Genentech, which it does not control or time. Management emphasized three-year persistence of Phase 1/2a BCVA gains, competitor RPE data as mechanism validation, and unchanged plans for the OPC1 DOSED study with enrollment expected next quarter.

negative_highlights: Management explicitly declined to provide specific guidance or visibility on AYA segment contribution for Q4 or FY25
SG&A expenses increased year-over-year by $6.3 million in full year due to European pre-commercialization and Norgine transaction costs
positive_highlights: Net product sales grew approximately 13% sequentially to $7.9 million in Q4
Cash burn reduced significantly to only ~$0.6 million for the quarter following a strategic debt repayment of $13 million
PEDMARK gaining traction at major academic centers including UCLA, Fred Hutchinson Cancer Center, and Mount Sinai
summary: Fennec reported Q4 FY2024 net product sales of $7.9 million (13% sequential growth) and full-year revenue of $29.6 million versus $21.3 million in the prior year, driven by strong momentum in both pediatric and adolescent/young adult segments. The company reduced cash burn to approximately $0.6 million for Q4 after repaying $13 million of debt, while SG&A expenses decreased quarter-over-quarter due to non-cash equity compensation and a one-time severance payment. Management expressed confidence in 2H FY25 growth driven by European commercialization milestones (Norgine deal) and expanded adoption at major academic centers.

negative_highlights: Total revenue declined 21% year-over-year to $75.6 million, primarily due to a 40% drop in marketing business revenue.
Advertising spend decreased by 26% sequentially as the company adjusted payments following lower monetization from Google's Search Partner Network changes.
Google announced plans to automatically opt advertisers out of AdSense for Domains (AFD), creating note weakness in-term disruption and expected material decline in that specific line of business.
positive_highlights: Owned and operated product revenue increased 60% year-over-year driven by organic growth in private search (Startpage) and mapping (MapQuest).
Adjusted EBITDA surged 79% year-over-year to $17.9 million, demonstrating improved operational efficiency despite lower advertising spend.
Organic sessions for owned products rose over 20% sequentially from Q3 as users seek privacy-focused alternatives.
summary: System1 reported Q4 FY2024 revenue of $76 million (GAAP) and adjusted EBITDA of $17.9 million, representing a significant year-over-year improvement in profitability despite an overall top-line decline driven by marketing business volatility. Management provided specific guidance for Q1 2025 with estimated revenue between $69-71 million and adjusted gross profit growth of approximately 25%, while explicitly declining to provide full-year guidance due to ongoing Google Search Partner Network changes. The quarter highlighted strong performance in owned-and-operated products like Startpage, MapQuest, and CouponFollow, which grew significantly year-over-year.

negative_highlights: Adjusted net income down 7% to $8.7 million
TCE down 10% to $21,000 per day
Fleet operational utilization down to 90.3% from 91.6%
positive_highlights: Revenues up 47% to $42.3 million for 2024
Adjusted EBITDA up 11% to $16.4 million
No bank debt and cash balance up 39% to $12.6 million
summary: C3is reported FY2024 voyage revenues of $42.3 million, up 47% YoY, and adjusted EBITDA of $16.4 million, up 11%. Adjusted net income fell 7% to $8.7 million, and TCE dropped 10% to $21,000/day. The company ended the year with $12.6 million cash, no bank debt, and increased fleet capacity by 234% since inception. Management is cautious but confident in 2025, citing potential positive impacts from US tariffs on Chinese-built vessels (none in fleet) and 'drill baby drill' policies.

negative_highlights: Q4 CapEx came in higher than anticipated due to efficiency gains and project pull-forwards
2025 turn-in-line count slightly lower than last year
Current term loan carries a high interest rate (SOFR+750, ~13% average in 2024)
positive_highlights: Production up 10% year-over-year, beating initial flat guidance
Proved reserves up ~29% year-over-year despite lower SEC prices
LOE down 17% per BOE and CapEx 40% lower than 2023
summary: HighPeak Energy reported Q4 2024 results with production averaging over 50,000 BOEs per day and a 10% production increase year-over-year, exceeding initial flat expectations. Proved reserves increased nearly 30% year-over-year, and lease operating expenses decreased 17% on a BOE basis, while absolute debt was reduced by $120 million. For 2025, the company guides to flat production with a two-rig maintenance capital budget approximately 20% lower than 2024, including one-time infrastructure projects. Management plans to pursue a more traditional capital structure to reduce high interest costs, with a term loan refinancing expected after May 2025 co-provision expiration on March 12.

negative_highlights: Total Q4 revenue declined 9% year-over-year
Heart failure and pediatric categories down 36% and 20% respectively
Q4 console sales only 3 units vs 11 in Q3
positive_highlights: Gross margin improved to 58.4% from 54.4%
Critical Care revenue up 35% year-over-year in Q4
CMS outpatient reimbursement increased nearly fourfold to $1,639 per day
summary: Nuwellis reported Q4 2024 revenue of $2.3 million, a 9% decrease year-over-year, driven by lower console and international sales, partially offset by a 21% increase in consumables utilization. Gross margin improved to 58.4% from 54.4%, and net loss narrowed to $1.5 million from $7.9 million. The company highlighted a fourfold increase in CMS outpatient reimbursement effective January 1, 2025, and a JACC: Heart Failure publication showing a 60% reduction in heart failure events with Aquadex. Management expressed optimism about outpatient market entry and ongoing account wins, but noted limited near-term visibility on trial timelines.

Q4 revenue fell 15.7% YoY to $163.3M from $193.7M, and adjusted EBITDA collapsed to $0.9M (0.6% margin) from $8.3M (4.3%), a 370 bps contraction on lower volumes and operational inefficiencies. Adjusted net loss was $0.15 per share versus $0.06 income a year ago, with net loss of $35M including a $28.8M non-cash tax valuation allowance; full-year revenue fell to $723.4M with adjusted EBITDA of $23.2M (3.2%). 2025 guidance was initiated at $670-710M revenue and $25-30M adjusted EBITDA, implying another down revenue year but margin expansion from $15-20M of cost savings, with net leverage at 4.7x and a December covenant amendment providing relief through 2025. Management faced pointed shareholder criticism over cash burn, elevated SG&A and the lack of visible restructuring payoff, defending the 2024 portfolio actions and pointing to a second-half recovery and a 2027 debt maturity to refinance.

summary: SGC's Q4 revenue fell 1% YoY to a level within its full-year outlook, with diluted EPS of $0.13 versus $0.22 a year earlier on a tough comparison; full-year revenue and EPS grew 4% and 35% respectively. Segment results were two-sided: healthcare grew 8% and contact centers 4%, while branded products fell 5% on uniform program rollout timing. Initial 2025 guidance calls for revenue of $585-595M (up to 5% growth) and EPS of $0.75-0.82 (up to 12% growth), a back-end-weighted cadence. The board authorized an additional $17.5M buyback and net leverage improved to 1.7x from 2.0x.

Management explicitly stated they are not assuming any improvement or recovery in the macroeconomic environment within their FY2025 guidance.

SPL program-related revenue of $6.1M for the full year exceeded initial guidance provided early last year.
The company successfully integrated SeQure Dx with immaterial operating costs relative to its streamlined organization.
summary: MaxCyte reported full-year 2024 revenue of $38.6 million (down 6% YoY) and Q4 revenue of $8.7 million (down 45% YoY), driven by a one-time milestone spike in the prior year quarter rather than organic weakness. While Core business revenue grew 9% for the full year, instrument sales declined due to customer caution on capital expenditure, though Processing Assembly (PA) revenue expanded significantly. Management provided conservative guidance for FY2025 expecting Core revenue growth of 8-15%, explicitly stating they are not baking in any macroeconomic recovery.

Management provided 2025 guidance for adjusted EBITDA between $245-$280 million (inclusive of recent Moonrise acquisition) and capital expenditures between $65-$75 million, noting that the low end risks a reduction in well connections while the high end assumes customers hit timing targets.

Operating expenses fell 32% year-over-year in Q4, and full-year OpEx-to-revenue ratio dropped to 34% from 53% in 2022.
Total shipments reached a record 2 million units in 2024, up 33% year-over-year, with over 700,000 units shipped in Q4 alone.
summary: ECARX reported Q4 FY2024 total revenue of RMB1.9 billion, up 4% year-over-year and 36% sequentially, with gross margin of 21.2%; full-year revenue rose 18% to RMB5.6 billion but gross profit fell 9% and full-year gross margin slipped to 20.8%. The quarter achieved adjusted EBITDA of RMB74 million versus a loss of RMB236 million a year earlier, helped by a 32% reduction in operating expenses and a gain on partial sale of an equity investment, while loss per share narrowed to RMB0.11 from RMB0.89. Management set full-year 2025 positive EBITDA as its top priority and flagged continued hardware margin pressure, with a RMB20 million buyback announced in December and an F-3 registration filed for a potential capital raise.

summary: SIGA reported FY2024 product sales of $133 million, up ~2% YoY, with Q4 sales of $80 million driven by SNS and international deliveries, including an $11 million East Asia sale. Management expects a new SNS contract RFP in 2025 and highlighted international expansion, Japan approval, and pipeline diversification, while acknowledging mpox trial disappointments and ongoing FDA submission timeline for PEP in early 2026.

summary: Core Molding reported Q4 net sales of $62.5 million, down 15.3% YoY, with a slight net loss of $39,000 versus prior-year diluted EPS of $0.25; adjusted EPS excluding severance was $0.10 versus $0.30. Q4 gross margin rose to 15.8% from 14.8%, while operating income fell to 1.4% of sales from 3.4%. Full-year sales were $302.4 million, down 15.5%, with 17.6% gross margin, 11.2% adjusted EBITDA margin, and record operating cash flow of $35.2 million. Management guided FY2025 net sales essentially flat, but flagged first-half revenue down 5-10% and a roughly $30 million headwind from the Volvo transition, to be offset by $30-40 million of tooling revenue and a second-half truck recovery.

New RA and T-cell biomarkers launched successfully with an estimated $90 per test incremental revenue impact.
summary: Exagen reported Q4 FY2024 revenue of $14.5 million (implied from full year context and guidance) with a trailing 12-month ASP increase to $411, though total test volume declined 11% year-over-year to 123,000 units due to deliberate attrition of unprofitable channels. The company narrowed its adjusted EBITDA loss to approximately $10 million and expanded gross margins to just under 60%. Management provided Q1 2025 revenue guidance of at least $14.5 million and expects to achieve positive adjusted EBITDA in the fourth quarter of 2025.

Douglas Elliman reported Q4 2024 revenue of $243.3 million, up 13.6% from $214.1 million a year earlier, with net loss narrowing to $6 million ($0.07/share) from $14.8 million ($0.18/share). Adjusted EBITDA improved to a $5.4 million loss from a $16.1 million loss, and adjusted net income turned positive at $2.4 million ($0.03/share) versus an adjusted loss of $0.17/share. Development marketing revenue jumped to $25.5 million from $9.5 million, and full-year 2024 revenue rose to $995.6 million from $955.6 million, though the full-year net loss widened to $76.3 million ($0.91/share) from $42.6 million. Management cited a $27.7 billion active development pipeline and roughly $30% higher January-February 2025 cash receipts, but gave no formal forward guidance.

They remain focused on gaining share and maintaining margin targets.

First-quarter 2025 guidance calls for lower volumes due to seasonal decline, with margin of 320-340 bps. CEO transition announced with Anthony Hsieh returning as Executive Chairman; Project North Star continues.

Full year 2025 guidance calls for net revenue of $175-195 million (implying roughly flat to down versus 2024, or ~10% growth excluding $18-23 million of distributor-transition and store-closure impacts) and an adjusted EBITDA loss of $55-65 million, a wider loss than 2024. summary: Seaport Entertainment's inaugural Q4 FY2024 call reported total consolidated revenue of $22.8 million, roughly flat year-over-year, with consolidated hospitality revenue up 6.5% but same-store hospitality revenue down 3.5%. The company raised $270 million in fresh capital during 2024, bringing total liquidity to $429 million, which management states is sufficient to sustain operations through at least 2026. Management guided for cash consumption between $200 million and $250 million in 2025 as they accelerate eVTOL development and prepare the manufacturing facility.

Management reiterated its standard 2025 payout guidance of 90%-100% of distributable earnings with any excess taxable income paid as a Q4 special distribution. The quarter reflected steady operations against a difficult cannabis backdrop, with credit quality intact but one loan (number nine) still on non-accrual and no federal reform catalyst assumed.

Guidance was reiterated rather than changed: fresh lemon volumes of 5-5.5 million cartons and avocado volumes of 7-8 million pounds for FY2025, with FY2025 avocado volume expected below FY2024 on alternate bearing. Management said soft lemon conditions should persist through Q2 with relief expected in the second half, helped by a recent Spanish freeze shifting imports away from the U.S.

Management expressed optimism for H1 2025 but explicitly stated they will err on the side of conservatism and under-promise, avoiding specific numerical guidance.

Gross margins expanded significantly to 61%, up from 44% in the prior year period, while adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed to the company's smallest quarterly figure. Management highlighted new cost-cutting initiatives and strategic financing to accelerate progress toward cash flow breakeven.

summary: KLX reported Q4 revenue of $166 million (midpoint of guidance) and adjusted EBITDA margin above prior guidance despite a 15% YoY decline in rig count. Management successfully refinanced debt with extended maturities to 2030/2028, reducing notes outstanding by approximately 2%. Full year revenue was $709 million against expectations.

negative_highlights: Total cash from operations decreased by $4.6 million year-over-year due to a decrease in net working capital.
Q1 FY2025 demand is seasonally soft across all major trade routes with volatile market prices driven by tariff uncertainty.
Special operating expenses increased 9% year-over-year, rising from an average of $5,971 per day to $6,525 per day.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA grew by approximately $4 million year-over-year despite a 22.6% decline in market rates.
Successfully completed merger with SSI, expanding fleet to 41 owned vessels (operating range 60-70) and assuming $100 million debt.
summary: Pangaea Logistics Solutions reported Q4 FY2024 adjusted EBITDA of $23.2 million and GAAP net income of $8.4 million ($0.18/share), representing a significant year-over-year increase despite broader market rates declining by 22.6%. The company successfully closed its merger with SSI on December 30, adding 15 Handysize vessels to expand into smaller segments, though Q1 FY2025 outlook remains soft due to seasonal demand conditions and volatile trade policy uncertainty.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined 17.7% YoY due to a significant drop in case volumes and reduced marketing spend from cost-saving initiatives.
Cost of services as a percentage of revenue increased to 42.7%, up from 37.5% previously, driven by inflexible fixed costs like rent.
Customer acquisition cost rose to $3,250 per case compared to $2,600 in the prior year quarter due to lower volumes and higher lead generation expenses.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA margin of 4.7% represents a recovery from negative territory seen in prior quarters due to cost reductions.
Marketing initiatives including online video and social channels are showing encouraging early results with increased lead volume.
Company amended credit agreement to relax covenants, enhancing flexibility for investment during the transformation.
summary: AirSculpt reported Q4 FY2024 revenue of $39.2 million, a decline of 17.7% year-over-year driven by lower case volumes and reduced marketing spend. Adjusted EBITDA fell to $1.9 million (4.7% margin) from $10.1 million in the prior year quarter due to these revenue declines and elevated cost of services as a percentage of sales. Management paused de novo openings for 2025, drew down on credit facilities to maintain liquidity while increasing marketing spend, and expects Q1 same-store performance to mirror Q4's decline before sequential improvement later in the year.

negative_highlights: License and R&D service revenues collapsed by $24.7 million (98% YoY) as the Elfabrio milestone obligation was fulfilled in FY23.
Management explicitly stated it cannot provide revenue guidance for 2025 due to inventory-based sales models with Chiesi.
Net income declined from $8.3M to $2.9M, and EPS fell from $0.12 to $0.04.
positive_highlights: FY24 revenues increased $12.6 million (31%) YoY, primarily driven by Chiesi sales growth.
Company fully repaid all outstanding debt principal and interest in September 2024 using available cash reserves of ~$35M.
Phase 1 clinical trial for PRX-115 completed successfully with results supporting a planned Phase 2 initiation.
summary: Protalix reported FY24 revenues of $53 million (up 31% YoY) driven by Chiesi sales, while license and R&D service revenue dropped to $0.4 million following the completion of its Elfabrio program in prior years. The company repaid all outstanding debt with cash proceeds from warrant exercises but explicitly declined to provide FY25 guidance due to inventory-based watching arrangements that obscure future visibility.

negative_highlights: Q4 revenue missed expectations due to longer deal timing and lower average note price in international deals.
U.S. hospital critical care sales cycles are getting longer than previously anticipated.
Uncertainty remains regarding funding for deals supported by grant funds, specifically affecting the last 10 weeks.
positive_highlights: Full-year 2024 organic revenue growth was healthy at 70% excluding one-time grant revenue.
Gross margin expanded 300 basis points to 46% for the full year of 2024.
Net cash burn decreased 9% to $38.4 million, extending the cash runway to the end of 2026.
summary: Hyperfine reported Q4 FY2024 revenue of $2.3 million, a decline from $2.7 million in the prior year quarter, driven by longer U.S. hospital sales cycles and a heavier international mix. Full-year 2024 revenue grew 17% to $12.9 million with gross margin expansion of 300 bps to 46%, while net cash burn decreased 9% to $38.4 million. Management provided H1 2025 revenue guidance of approximately $6 million and full-year growth expectations of 20-30%, citing a 'tale of two halves' with significant catalysts expected in the second half.

negative_highlights: Virtual Sports revenue failed to hit the predicted inflection point during Q4 and continued to be impacted by a reduction from its largest customer.
Year-end cash balance was less than anticipated due to significant year-to-year increases in accounts receivable for equipment sales that fell late in 2024.
Virtual Sports revenue stabilization is only just beginning, with the business still recovering after a challenging full year.
positive_highlights: Interactive segment delivered strong growth with Q4 EBITDA up 105% YoY and revenue up 45% YoY.
Full-year Adjusted EBITDA margins for the Interactive segment expanded to 65%, driven by operating leverage.

Land-based gaming business achieved a significant year-over-year increase in accounts receivable due to timing, but management noted cash would have been significantly higher with a snapshot taken weeks later.
summary: Adjusted EBITDA for Q4 FY2024 was $30.9 million (up 22% YoY), while full-year Adjusted EBITDA of $100.1 million reflects minor revisions to prior results due to timing differences rather than total revenue changes. Management stated the quarter's results were 'in line with expectations' and did not raise guidance, though they noted a delay in receivables collection that reduced year-end cash below anticipated levels.

negative_highlights: Q1 FY2025 revenue guidance is down 10% to 15%, driven by a headwind of approximately 250 basis points from US academic customers.
Accelerator Lab Q1 projects are delayed, with large pharma projects expected to materialize in the second half rather than first half.
Full year FY2024 revenue guidance for 2025 is lowered significantly below consensus expectations.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew double-digits for the seventh consecutive quarter driven by robust demand for Simoa sensitivity.
Non-GAAP gross margin expanded 300 basis points YoY to 57.7% due to higher pricing and improved efficiency.
Cash usage declined significantly year-over-year, dropping from $6 million in Q4 FY2023 to $4.4 million.
summary: Quanterix reported Q4 FY2024 revenue of $35.2 million (up 11% YoY) and non-GAAP gross margin expansion to 57.7%. For full year 2024, total revenue was $137.4 million (up 12%). Management provided Q1 FY2025 guidance of a decline in revenues due to US academic paralysis and the end of the Lilly collaboration.

negative_highlights: $2.7 million impairment charge related to small molecule ion channel assets due to strategic shift to antibodies
Service revenue declined as work on certain programs completed, reducing non-cash deferred revenue recognition
Royalty revenue lower than prior year driven by competitive market dynamics in China
positive_highlights: 18% year-over-year growth in active partners reaching 91
Double-digit percentage growth (12%) in number of active programs, ending at 362 net of attrition
New platform licenses added with Incyte Corporation and Photinia Biosciences
summary: OmniAb reported Q4 FY2024 revenue of $10.8 million (up from $4.8M in prior year) driven by license and milestone payments, though service revenue declined due to completed ion channel programs. The company recorded a net loss of $13.1 million ($0.12/share), impacted by a non-recurring $2.7 million impairment charge related to small molecule assets. Management provided 2025 guidance for GAAP revenue between $20M-$25M and operating expenses between $90M-$95M, noting that the lower revenue outlook is primarily due to the amortization of deferred service revenue rather than a decline in cash flow.

negative_highlights: ReMEDy2 interim analysis delayed to first half of 2026 versus prior expectations, attributed to slower site startup and underestimated activation time
Net cash used in operations rose to $22.1 million from $18.7 million, and R&D increased to $19.1 million from $13.1 million
Site activation takes six to 12 months and enrollment remains below target, with no disclosure of current enrolling site or patient counts
positive_highlights: Cash and investments of $44.1 million with runway into Q3 2026
Preeclampsia Phase 1A dosing underway with no serious adverse events or pathological hypotension reported; data expected in Q2
DSMB completed January safety review with no significant concerns and recommended ReMEDy2 continue without modification
summary: DiaMedica's Q4/FY2024 call was a clinical update for a pre-revenue biotech, not a commercial earnings report. FY2024 net cash used in operations was $22.1 million versus $18.7 million in FY2023, R&D rose to $19.1 million from $13.1 million, and G&A fell to $7.6 million from $8.2 million, with cash and investments of $44.1 million and runway into Q3 2026. Management delayed the ReMEDy2 interim analysis to the first half of 2026 due to slower-than-expected site startup, while the preeclampsia Phase 2 Part 1A data are expected in Q2. ReMEDy2 enrollment has improved in 2025 but remains below target.

negative_highlights: Net revenue declined 25% year-over-year to $24.6 million
Full-year adjusted EBITDA remained negative at $2.1 million, though improved from a $22.3 million loss
Tariffs on China and Canada are estimated to add $3.5 million to 2025 cost of sales, of which only about 50% is expected to be mitigated through price increases
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed to $0.1 million from $5.6 million in Q4, an improvement of 98.5%
Gross margin expanded to 63.4% from 51.0% in Q4 2023
2025 revenue guidance of $104-$106 million implies 9-12% growth on a comparable basis after excluding $4 million of discontinued SKUs
summary: Q4 2024 net revenue declined 25% to $24.6 million from $32.8 million, primarily due to SKU rationalization and less liquidation, but met the high end of guidance. Gross margin expanded to 63.4% from 51%, and adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed to $0.1 million from $5.6 million. Full-year adjusted EBITDA loss improved 91% to $2.1 million. For 2025, revenue guidance of $104-$106 million implies 5-7% growth (9-12% excluding discontinued SKUs), with adjusted EBITDA targeted at break-even including $3.5 million net tariff impact. A $3 million two-year buyback was authorized.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA fell 32% year-over-year and 14% sequentially to $7.1 million
Consolidated gross margin contracted to 25% from 28% a year ago and 26% sequentially on Cabana Club e-commerce pricing and illicit market resurgence
Free cash flow was negative $1.9 million as working capital investments reached about $4 million versus a $1.1 million average positive source over the prior five quarters
positive_highlights: Record revenue of $142.5 million, up 11% year-over-year and 3% sequentially, with brick-and-mortar segment up 17% year-over-year
Same-store sales up 5% year-over-year, the fastest pace in four quarters, versus a 4% decline for the average operator since October 2021
Cabana Club members exceeded 1.76 million in Canada (up 33% year-over-year) and ELITE paid members exceeded 81,000, up 153% year-over-year
summary: High Tide reported Q1 FY2025 record revenue of $142.5 million, up 11% year-over-year and 3% sequentially, with brick-and-mortar revenue up 17% and same-store sales up 5% (the fastest in four quarters).
