Adjusted EBITDA fell 32% year-over-year and 14% sequentially to $7.1 million, and consolidated gross margin contracted to 25% from 28% a year ago, driven by the global Cabana Club e-commerce rollout and illicit market pressure in some municipalities. Free cash flow was negative $1.9 million due to roughly $4 million of working capital investment tied to new stores, though trailing four-quarter free cash flow rose 45% to $16.5 million. Management did not issue specific numeric guidance but maintained plans for 20-30 new Canadian stores in 2025, a free-cash-flow-positive fiscal year, and German medical market entry, while abandoning the previously planned €4.8 million Purecan equity purchase.

negative_highlights: Revenue decreased by approximately $890,111 (or ~85%) year-over-year due to lack of consulting service revenue
Operating loss widened from $1.2 million in the prior year quarter to $1.7 million in Q3 FY2025
Net capitalization reported a one-time impairment charge of $1.3 million related to a portfolio company
positive_highlights: Netcapital Securities Inc. received FINRA approval to operate as a broker dealer in November 2024
The company successfully engaged GenOn Neuroscience, Inc. for planned Regulation A offerings
summary: Netcapital reported a significant revenue miss for Q3 FY2025, with revenues dropping approximately 85% to $152,682 due to the cessation of equity securities consulting services. The company recorded an operating loss of $1.7 million and a net loss per share of $1.57, exacerbated by a one-time impairment charge of $1.3 million on a portfolio company. Management highlighted the successful FINRA approval for its broker-dealer subsidiary but noted that revenue from this new line is not yet realized.

negative_highlights: Q4 revenue of $3.7M was below the prior quarter's $3.8M and driven largely by $3.4M of end-of-life memory shipments
Memory IC backlog of only ~$2.3M remaining, completing in March, removing a major revenue and margin contributor
GAAP net loss of $1.6M (-$0.37/sh) and negative adjusted EBITDA of $0.4M; cash of $3.3M included ~$2.8M of financing proceeds, with operating cash burn of ~$0.8M
positive_highlights: New $3.6M purchase order from a longtime strategic FWA customer, expected to be fulfilled during calendar 2025
Q4 GAAP gross margin 56.3% and non-GAAP 71.6%, versus negative 147.3% and negative 116.6% a year ago
Q1 2025 mmWave revenue expected to exceed full-year 2024 mmWave revenue; 100+ pipeline engagements, up over 20% YoY
summary: Q4 revenue was $3.7M, up 100% YoY from $1.8M but flat to down sequentially from $3.8M, lifted by $3.4M of end-of-life memory IC shipments; full-year revenue was $14.6M versus $13.7M. GAAP gross margin rose to 56.3% (non-GAAP 71.6%) from negative 147.3% a year ago, helped by lapping a $3.2M inventory write-down, while GAAP net loss narrowed to $1.6M (-$0.37/sh) from $8.9M (-$12.48/sh). Q1 2025 guidance is $3.6M-$4.0M, with management expecting Q1 mmWave revenue to exceed all of FY2024 mmWave, and a new $3.6M FWA purchase order to ship mostly in the second half of 2025. The key shift is that the memory end-of-life tail is nearly exhausted ($2.3M backlog completing in March), so future revenue depends on ramping mmWave, where gross margins are expected to fall back toward the 40s from memory-inflated levels.

negative_highlights: Q4 net sales fell about 5% to $143 million, and gross margin contracted 120 basis points to 66.3% on higher freight and markdown mix.

FY2025 adjusted EBITDA guidance of $101-106 million is below FY2024's $107.1 million, with Q1 sales guided down 1-4% and comps down 2-5% due to soft demand, February weather, and a $1.5 million OMS cutover impact.
Reported inventories were up about 15% year over year at year-end, and management acknowledged holding somewhat too much inventory amid price-sensitive consumer behavior.
positive_highlights: Total company comparable sales rose 1.9% in Q4, driven by strong conversion and AUR in the retail channel.

FY2024 adjusted EPS of $3.47 was up 4% and Q4 adjusted EPS of $0.32 was up 14%, supported by a $4.2 million year-over-year reduction in quarterly interest expense after paying down $94 million of debt.
The quarterly dividend was increased, and $24.5 million of share repurchase authorization remained at year-end.
summary: J.Jill reported Q4 FY2024 net sales of $143 million, down about 5% year over year (against a 14-week prior-year quarter), with total company comparable sales up 1.9%. Gross margin contracted 120 basis points to 66.3% on higher freight costs and a greater markdown mix, while adjusted EBITDA fell to $14.5 million from $17.8 million; adjusted EPS rose 14% to $0.32. For fiscal 2025 the company guided sales to $617-629 million (+1% to +3%), comps flat to +2%, adjusted EBITDA of $101-106 million (versus $107.1 million in FY2024), and free cash flow of about $40 million, citing a soft start to the year, February weather, an OMS cutover impact, and tariff and macro uncertainty. The company also announced an increase to its quarterly dividend.

negative_highlights: Full-year gross margin contracted to 13% from 19.1% due to revenue mix and higher fixed costs
Q4 net loss widened to $3.9M ($0.36/share) from $1.7M ($0.19/share); full-year operating loss grew to $19.4M from $15.3M
2025 growth constrained by current manufacturing capacity, with material capacity expansion not available until 2026 regulatory approvals
positive_highlights: Q4 revenue grew to $5.8M from $5.3M and gross margin expanded to 15.5% from 13.5% YoY
2025 NexoBrid revenue guided to $24M vs $20.2M in 2024, capped only by manufacturing capacity
U.S. hospital NexoBrid orders increased 42% in Q4 2024; NexoBrid available in 90+ European burn centers and 400+ Japanese facilities
summary: MediWound reported Q4 revenue of $5.8M (up from $5.3M), with gross margin of 15.5% up from 13.5%, but net loss widened to $3.9M ($0.36 per share) from $1.7M ($0.19). Full-year revenue rose to $20.2M from $18.7M, yet full-year gross margin fell to 13% from 19.1% and operating loss expanded to $19.4M. Management guided 2025 NexoBrid revenue to $24M, with growth constrained by manufacturing capacity and dependent on EMA/FDA approvals for the new GMP facility expected in early and mid-2026. EscharEx VLU Phase 3 interim assessment is anticipated mid-2026, and R&D spending is expected to rise substantially in 2025 (~$100K per enrolled patient).

negative_highlights: Q4 net loss widened to $18.3 million from $16.3 million in the prior-year quarter
FYARRO growth was modest (7% for the full year, 14% in Q4) ahead of its divestiture to Kaken
No formal revenue, EPS, or pipeline-timeline guidance was provided for the newly launched company
positive_highlights: FYARRO Q4 net product sales rose 14% YoY to $7.2 million; full-year sales were $26 million, up 7% over 2023
Pro forma cash of $170–180 million following the $100 million PIPE and strategic transactions, expected to fund operations into 2028
Plan to submit three U.S. INDs within 15 months, including HWK-007 in H2 2025 and HWK-016 by end of 2025
summary: Q4 FYARRO net product sales were $7.2 million, up 14% YoY, with full-year FYARRO sales of $26 million (+7% vs 2023); Q4 net loss was $18.3 million (vs $16.3 million), and full-year net loss was $63.7 million versus $65.8 million. Following the December strategic transactions (in-licensing of three ADCs from Wuxi Biologics, divestiture of FYARRO to Kaken, and a $100 million PIPE), the company relaunched as Whitehawk Therapeutics with expected pro forma cash of $170–180 million, funding operations into 2028. Management outlined a plan to file three U.S. INDs within 15 months, but provided no formal earnings guidance or quantitative outlook for the ongoing ADC portfolio. This is primarily a corporate transformation update rather than a traditional quarterly results call.

negative_highlights: Net sales fell to $275.6 million from $293.5 million year-over-year, with comps down 0.8%.
Gross margin contracted 90 basis points to 33.6%.
Fiscal 2025 sales guidance of $1.080-$1.100 billion reflects a cautious outlook amid macro uncertainty.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA increased to $16.7 million from $16.4 million, with margin expanding 50 basis points to 6.1%.
Regular-price comps increased 1.6% in Q4, while clearance drag moderated toward positive territory.
Cash rose to $48.5 million from $11.7 million a year ago, and operating cash flow doubled to $77.4 million.
summary: Torrid reported Q4 FY2024 net sales of $275.6 million versus $293.5 million last year (up 1.4% excluding the extra week), with comparable sales down 0.8% but a 1.6% increase in regular-price comps. Gross margin fell 90 basis points to 33.6%, and the company posted a net loss of $3.0 million, or negative $0.03 per share, while adjusted EBITDA rose to $16.7 million from $16.4 million. For fiscal 2025, the company guided sales of $1.080-$1.100 billion and adjusted EBITDA of $100-$110 million, and Q1 sales of $264-$274 million with adjusted EBITDA of $24-$28 million, alongside a plan to close 40-50 stores.

negative_highlights: 2024 Marcellus hit by sub-$2/Mcf net wellhead pricing with curtailments of 20-25% of net production in the basin
Auction/Killam Canada well was commercially unsuccessful alongside one successful well
No incremental Marcellus drilling expected in 2025; next activity set for 2026
positive_highlights: Permian oil production up 180% year over year and Permian contributed more than 60% of 2024 cash flows
Proved reserves grew ~20% year over year despite pricing headwinds
Q1 2025 Marcellus trajectory: ~30 MMcf/d net production up 85% and realized net wellhead pricing above $3.90/Mcf, up 100% year over year
summary: Epsilon reported 2024 results framed around strategic execution: a 180% year-on-year increase in Permian oil production, which contributed over 60% of 2024 cash flows, and roughly 20% year-over-year growth in proved reserves. The Marcellus was the drag, with sub-$2/Mcf net wellhead pricing and 20-25% production curtailments in 2024. Management said the tide has turned in Q1 2025: PA net production is running at ~30 MMcf/d (up 85% vs the 2024 daily average) at realized pricing above $3.90/Mcf net to wellhead (up 100% year over year), with curtailments back online and an expectation of substantially higher 2025 Marcellus cash flows. No formal 2025 guidance ranges were given; Canada JV wells are on flowback with results too early to call.

negative_highlights: Full-year revenue growth was only 9% despite Q4 acceleration, indicating a weak first three quarters of FY2024
Full-year gross margin declined 120 basis points to 86.5% due to growth in discounted financial assistance units, which are discounted up to 65% off the $1,195 list price
Operating loss for the full year widened 7% to $7.2 million and cash used in operations was $6.1 million, leaving $3.7 million of cash on hand as of December 31, 2024
positive_highlights: Q4 revenue grew 43% year-over-year to $761,000 and unit sales rose approximately 45%
Covered lives expanded from 4 million on January 1, 2024 to approximately 51 million today
FDA label expansion for IB-Stim to ages 8-21 nearly doubles the addressable market; RED received FDA clearance on December 6 and the first order was booked in Q1 2025
summary: NeurAxis reported Q4 FY2024 revenue of $761,000, up 43% year-over-year, with unit sales up approximately 45%. Full-year revenue was $2.7 million, up 9% from $2.5 million in FY2023. Gross margin was 86.4% in Q4, flat year-over-year, but full-year gross margin declined 120 basis points to 86.5% due to a higher mix of discounted financial assistance units. Management provided no formal EPS or revenue guidance but said Q1 2025 would be a third consecutive quarter of year-over-year revenue growth and reiterated a goal of cash flow breakeven, which Tim Henrichs said would require $10-12 million in annual revenue against a roughly $6 million annual cash burn. The quarter's key strategic developments were a new FDA label expansion for IB-Stim to ages 8-21, FDA clearance of the RED device, continued insurance coverage growth to about 51 million covered lives, and an upcoming Category 1 CPT code effective January 1, 2026.

negative_highlights: Canadian fleet utilization remains low at 54% in Q4, well below the 75% target for end of 2025; Q1 2025 weather and cyclone impacts are expected to weigh on results.
Gross margin was significantly impacted by a claim extinguishment and shipping costs, with reported gross profit margin of 14.6% versus adjusted 19.7%.
Oil sands revenue declined about 30% from prior year, and the company expects flat levels in 2025, limiting near-term growth in that segment.
positive_highlights: Record annual revenue and record backlog of $3.5 billion, with $1.7 billion in new contract wins in 2024.
Australian operations achieved 82% utilization in Q4, with a target of 85% early in 2025, and MacKellar posted its highest revenue quarter ever.
Adjusted EBITDA margin of 27.8% in Q4, nearly 3% higher than last year, and cumulative margin of 27.0% since the MacKellar acquisition.
summary: Q4 revenue hit a record, driven by strong Australian growth (MacKellar's highest revenue quarter ever) and a solid oil sands performance, with adjusted EBITDA of $104M and a 27.8% margin, up nearly 3% YoY. Adjusted EPS was $1.00, and net debt rose to $856M but fell to $783M after a post-year-end convertible conversion. Guidance for 2025 calls for revenue of $1.4-1.6B, adjusted EBITDA of $415-445M, and adjusted EPS of $3.70-4.00, with backlog at a record $3.5B.

negative_highlights: Q2 FY2025 revenue declined 8% year-over-year to $16.8M due to lower demand in the material handling market and product mix shifts.
Significant one-time charges of approximately $1.7 million (restatement costs plus severance) impacted Q2 adjusted EBITDA, widening the loss compared to a prior quarter gain.
Management explicitly stated they do not provide specific guidance due to order lumpiness caused by revised OEM delivery timing.
positive_highlights: Gross margin expanded sequentially from 32% in Q1 to 33% in Q2 driven by price increases and cost reductions.
Adjusted EBITDA loss improved significantly year-over-year, narrowing from a $1.2M loss in Q1 FY204 (prior period) to a $600k loss in the current quarter before restatement impacts.
Backlog remains robust at 19.5 million as of February 28, 2025, supporting future revenue visibility.
summary: Flux Power reported Q1 FY2025 revenue of $16.1M (up 9% YoY) and gross margin expansion to 32%, but Q2 FY2025 saw a sequential decline in revenue (-8%) due to order lumpiness, with margins rising slightly to 33%. Adjusted EBITDA losses narrowed from -$1.2M to -$600k in Q1 before widening again to -$1.0M in Q2 following the recognition of $1.2M restatement costs and severance charges. Management provided forward guidance expecting Q3 revenues similar to Q2, with a 5-10% increase anticipated for Q4 as macro conditions improve.

negative_highlights: Gross margin was a loss of $1.2 million compared to a profit of $588,000 in Q3.
Carton volume fell to 338,000 from 439,000 in the prior quarter.
The company remains cash-burning and operating at a loss during the final stages of its turnaround.
positive_highlights: Total liabilities declined by over $18 million, ending the year at $17.7 million.
Net working capital improved to a positive $1.6 million from a deficit of $8.8 million in the prior year.
Cash interest paid reduced to $722,000 compared to $1.3 million in the prior year.
summary: Net revenue was $4 million in Q4 FY2024, a sequential decline from $5.9 million due to lower volume and the repricing of filtered cigar contracts which resulted in a gross margin loss of $1.2 million. The company reported a net loss with no EPS provided for the quarter, while total operating expenses remained flat at $2.8 million. Management indicated that Q4 2025 breakeven is still the outlook and that revenue stabilization is expected to begin in Q1 2025 following the completion of contract transitions.

negative_highlights: Full-year total net revenue declined 2.8% YoY to $240 million.
National ex-political revenue declined 4.9% in Q4, with national pacing down roughly 10% for Q1 2025.
Sports betting revenue decreased $1.1 million YoY to $4.1 million as the industry shifts toward retention over acquisition.
positive_highlights: Political revenue delivered $12.1 million for the full year, exceeding expectations driven by strong federal election spending.
Station operating income (SOI) increased 46% YoY to $14.1 million in Q4, excluding severance costs.
Digital revenue increased sequentially from Q3 to Q4 despite a slight decline in percentage mix due to political surge.
summary: Q4 FY2024 total net revenue was $67.3 million (up 2.3% YoY), driven by $8.3 million in political advertising which offset weakness in national and local ad spend; however, same-station revenue for the quarter grew only 4.4% while full-year revenue declined 2.8%. Management provided a specific Q1 2025 guidance step-down, pacing same-station revenue down roughly 10% starting in February due to advertiser caution and sports betting pullback.

negative_highlights: Consolidated gross margin rate declined from 51% in 2023 to 41% in 2024 due to sales mix shift.
R&D and SG&A expenses in H2 were $4.9 million, higher than the previously guided run rate of around $2 million due to unanticipated transaction fees.
Legacy GLA oil business is completely sold out with no sales expected in 2025.
positive_highlights: Zola sales increased 124% in Q4 alone and grew 80% in the second half of 2024.
Gross margins expanded to 41.3% for the full year, exceeding the low 40s guidance.
Operating cash consumption decreased 30% in the second half compared to the first half.
summary: Full year 2024 revenues reached just over $5 million (up 13% YoY) with gross profit of $2.1 million and margins of 41.3%, beating the prior guidance of low 40s. The company successfully exited legacy businesses, reducing operating cash consumption by 30% in the second half while Zola sales grew 46% for the year. Management expects the pending Roosevelt Resources transaction to complete towards the end of Q2 2025.

negative_highlights: Gross margin contracted to 91% in Q4 compared to 93% last year, primarily due to higher R&D costs during the Azure-to-AWS cloud migration.
Retail transaction volumes declined approximately 2.5% year-over-year as consumers shifted to needs-based spending and credit usage slowed.
Q1 FY2025 outlook faces headwinds with expected retail volume retractions, though management expects Q4-like strength in the back half of the year.
positive_highlights: Achieved adjusted EBITDA positive results for the full year ($520,000), a strategic milestone not met previously.
SaaS revenue grew 17% quarter-over-quarter to $5.9 million in Q4, driven by new verticals like automotive and title insurance.
Secured significant wins including a mid-seven figure annual contract with a leading bank (up ~15%) and guaranteed volume commitments from an off-price retailer.
summary: Intellicheck reported Q4 FY2024 revenue of $5.936 million, a 15% year-over-year increase driven by growth in new verticals like automotive and title insurance which offset declines in retail volumes down ~2.5%. Full-year 2024 adjusted EBITDA turned positive at $520,000 after achieving the strategic goal of profitability for the first time. Management provided a Q1 FY2025 revenue guidance estimate of approximately $4.78 million (in-line with consensus) and expects continued gross margins near 90% in 2025.

negative_highlights: No revenue or financial performance reported in the earnings call.
Cash runway only into Q3 2025, requiring future capital raises.
US enrollment expected to start later than non-EU and Middle Eastern countries.
positive_highlights: Phase 2 MB106 achieved 50% complete remission rate, double the historic control.
Median overall survival at 11 months and progression-free survival at 9 months, still climbing.
Expected first patient treated in MIRACLE Phase 3 trial in Q1 2025 and interim data readout by year-end.
summary: Moleculin Biotech provided a business update on its Phase 3 MIRACLE trial for Annamycin in relapsed/refractory AML. The company highlighted strong Phase 2 results (50% CR, 11-month OS) and expects first patient treatment in Q1 2025, with interim data unblinding by end of 2025. Cash balance of ~$13 million (including $9 million raised in February 2025) funds operations into Q3 2025. No financial results were reported; focus was on clinical milestones.

negative_highlights: Q4 gross margin declined sequentially to 37.2% from 43.6% in Q3, partly due to reclassification of Amazon commissions; CFO noted the reclassification provides more stable metrics.
Net loss widened to $3.28 million for 2024 from $3.16 million, although adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed.
One-time inventory write-offs of $243,000 negatively impacted Q4 results, but management expects no similar future charges.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 181% YoY in Q4 to $3.04 million and 112% for FY2024 to $8.69 million, with third consecutive year of >100% growth.
Gross margin expanded to 37.2% in Q4 (from 8.7% in Q4 2023) and 31.6% for FY2024 (from 9.2%).
Company issued strong 2025 guidance of at least $13 million revenue and positive EBITDA, implying continued robust growth.
summary: NEXGEL reported Q4 2024 revenue of $3.04 million, up 181% year-over-year, and full-year revenue of $8.69 million, up 112%, marking the third consecutive year of over 100% growth. Gross margin for Q4 was 37.2%, down from 43.6% in Q3 due to reclassification of Amazon commissions, and full-year gross margin was 31.6% versus 9.2% in 2023. Net loss widened to $3.28 million for 2024 from $3.16 million, including $243,000 in one-time inventory write-offs, while adjusted EBITDA loss improved to $2.43 million from $2.80 million. Management guided to at least $13 million revenue and positive EBITDA for 2025, with Q1 revenue expected at least $2.75 million.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA remained a $6 million loss in Q4, so the business was still unprofitable on the metric highlighted
Fractional sales in Q4 came in slower than expected due to external tax and election uncertainty
Challenger fleet stood at only 5 aircraft versus a target of 15 by year-end 2025, with financing facility not yet closed
positive_highlights: Gross margin expanded to 18% in Q4 from 11% in Q3 and 8% in 1H24, the highest since going public
Adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed to $6 million in Q4 from $19 million in Q1 and $10.3 million in Q3
SG&A as a percentage of revenue fell from 31% in Q1 to 27% in Q4, with outside consulting cut from $1.3 million to under $50,000 per month
summary: flyExclusive reported Q4 FY2024 revenue of ~$91 million, up 20% YoY despite a 17% smaller fleet, with flight hours up 36% and fractional revenue up ~275% YoY (though only ~$9 million). Gross margin expanded to 18% from 11% in Q3 and 8% in 1H24, while adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed to $6 million from a $19 million loss in Q1 and $10.3 million in Q3; the company did not provide specific 2025 revenue or EBITDA guidance. Management framed the year as a turnaround driven by disposing of nonperforming aircraft, cutting SG&A (consulting down from $1.3 million/month to under $50,000/month) and expanding the Challenger fleet toward 15 by year-end, with the fractional sales softness attributed to tax-policy and election uncertainty expected to convert in 1H25.

negative_highlights: Tissue Health Plus segment EBITDA loss widened to $3.1 million in Q4
OsStic U.S. launch not expected until Q1 2027
THP investment expected to be $7.5-$10 million in H1 2025
positive_highlights: Q4 net revenue up 49% YoY to $26.3 million, above prior 33% growth
Full-year adjusted EBITDA positive at $2.7 million, up $2.6 million
Sanara Surgical segment adjusted EBITDA up 73% to $9.1 million
summary: Sanara MedTech reported Q4 FY2024 net revenue of $26.3 million, up 49% year-over-year, with soft tissue repair sales up 56% and bone fusion up 8%, though $1.8 million was attributed to hurricane-related demand. Full-year net revenue was $86.7 million, up 33%, with positive adjusted EBITDA of $2.7 million. The company expanded its distributor network to over 350 partners and facilities to over 1,300, and announced a partnership for OsStic with FDA breakthrough designation, targeting U.S. launch in Q1 2027. For 2025, they expect continued investment in Tissue Health Plus ($7.5-$10 million in H1) and pilot launches in Q2, while seeking financial partners to offset investment.

negative_highlights: Net revenue fell to RMB15.86 million ($2.21 million) from RMB26.07 million a year earlier due to lower iPollo V Series sales volume.
General and administrative expenses rose 30.5% to RMB25.38 million ($3.83 million) from RMB22.38 million.
Cash and cash equivalents declined to RMB32.43 million ($4.51 million) from RMB48.16 million at December 31, 2023, and no forward guidance was provided.
positive_highlights: Gross profit of RMB11.57 million ($1.61 million) versus a gross loss of RMB40.55 million in the prior-year period, driven by lower cost of revenue of RMB4.28 million versus RMB66.62 million.
Total operating expenses fell 38.7% to RMB51.39 million ($7.15 million) from RMB83.84 million a year earlier.
Net loss narrowed to RMB60.39 million ($8.4 million) from RMB120 million in the prior-year period, with loss per share improving to RMB6.01 from RMB19.12.
summary: Nano Labs reported second half 2024 net revenue of RMB15.86 million ($2.21 million), down from RMB26.07 million in the same period of 2023, citing lower sales volumes of its iPollo V Series products. The company swung to a gross profit of RMB11.57 million ($1.61 million) from a gross loss of RMB40.55 million a year earlier, while operating loss narrowed to RMB39.82 million ($5.54 million) from RMB124.4 million. Net loss narrowed to RMB60.39 million ($8.4 million) from RMB120 million, and cash and cash equivalents fell to RMB32.43 million from RMB48.16 million at end-2023. Management provided no formal forward guidance, noting only that Cuckoo 3.0-equipped machines are shipping steadily and will have some impact on this year's performance.

negative_highlights: Gross margin was only 6.6%, and self-mining cost to mine Bitcoin rose to $47,496 from $28,200 in 2023
Bitcoin production fell ~29% to 2,537 BTC due to the halving and higher blockchain difficulty
Mining capacity under management was cut from 28 EH/s in Q1 2024 to 23.5 EH/s at year-end as procurement was deliberately reduced
positive_highlights: Total revenue rose 63.1% to $463.3 million and adjusted EBITDA more than tripled to $117.5 million
Cloud mining revenue grew 52.2% to $271 million, with 77% ($208.4 million) from recurring existing customers
Average hosting cost reduced 25% versus end-2023; secured 164 MW of power capacity with a 1 GW expansion plan
summary: BitFuFu reported full-year 2024 total revenue of $463.3 million, up 63.1% from $284.1 million, with net income of $54 million and adjusted EBITDA of $117.5 million (more than tripled from $41.7 million). Gross margin was thin at 6.6% (up from 4.5%), and self-mining cost to mine Bitcoin rose to $47,496 from $28,200. Management provided initial 2025 guidance of ~33 EH/s mining capacity and 650-800 MW hosting capacity by year-end, versus 23.5 EH/s and 551 MW at end-2024, while detailing a shift toward owned data centers and a 25% reduction in average hosting cost.

negative_highlights: Net sales fell 17% to $9.7 million from $11.7 million on note weakness in shipments tied to inventory constraints
Modified EBITDA swung to negative $0.7 million from positive $43,000, and operating cash use widened to $3.9 million from $0.2 million
SG&A rose to $4.8 million from $3.0 million, and no 2025 revenue guidance was provided, deferred to next quarter
positive_highlights: Gross margin was 30% versus 4% a year ago, helped by a $1.8 million packaging inventory write-down and $1.3 million product-hold provision in the prior-year period
Balance sheet delevered: $10.4 million cash and $9.6 million debt versus $0.6 million cash and $27.4 million debt at year-end 2023
New functional soda line secured over 8,000 points of distribution, with launches at Sprouts, Kroger, Walgreens and others between April and August 2025
summary: Q4 FY2024 net sales fell to $9.7 million from $11.7 million a year earlier, which management attributed to short shipments from inventory constraints. Gross profit rose to $2.9 million with a 30% gross margin versus 4% a year ago, but the prior-year figure included $3.1 million of one-time charges; SG&A rose to $4.8 million from $3.0 million, modified EBITDA was negative $0.7 million, and operating cash use was $3.9 million. No formal 2025 revenue guidance was given, with management deferring targets to the next quarter and citing Q1 orders trending slightly ahead of last year. A $10 million private placement closed December 30, 2024, leaving $10.4 million of cash against $9.6 million of debt, down from $27.4 million.

negative_highlights: Missed organic revenue guidance range of 14-16% for FY2024.
$1.5 million one-time ERC benefit included in GAAP net income, obscuring underlying operating performance.
No specific numerical forward guidance provided beyond qualitative 'great growth' language.
positive_highlights: Total revenue up 3% sequentially with sequential margin expansion driven by efficiency gains in Card and Output Solutions.
Record total dollars processed of $1.9 billion in Q4, a 36% increase year-over-year.
PayFac card processing volume accelerated to +28% for the full year, now accounting for ~54% of total card activity.
summary: Total revenue grew 3% sequentially and margins expanded due to productivity enhancements in Card and Output Solutions segments. The company reported GAAP net income of $600,000 ($0.02/share) including a one-time ERC benefit, marking the third consecutive quarter of positive earnings despite missing on organic growth guidance for FY24 (which was 14-16%). Management raised visibility to 'great' but did not provide specific numerical guidance updates.

negative_highlights: Q4 revenue fell to $164,000 from $299,000 a year earlier, and full-year revenue dropped to $515,000 from $11 million
Full-year GAAP net loss widened to $16.6 million ($1.45/share) from $7.0 million ($0.62/share)
Cash used in operating activities rose to $14.1 million in 2024 from $2.8 million in 2023
positive_highlights: Received a $2 million payment from AbbVie in February 2025 following a development achievement
Cash and equivalents of $11.9 million at year-end 2024 (excluding the $2 million received in Q1 2025) fund operations into Q2 2026
Preclinical breast implant study showed no capsular contracture, calcifications, or local tissue reactions at six months, with volume retention maintained in one arm
summary: CollPlant reported Q4 2024 revenue of $164,000, down from $299,000 a year earlier, and full-year revenue of $515,000 versus $11 million in 2023, which included a one-time $10 million AbbVie milestone. GAAP net loss for 2024 widened to $16.6 million ($1.45/share) from $7.0 million ($0.62/share), with cash used in operations of $14.1 million. Management said cash of $11.9 million at year-end, plus a $2 million AbbVie payment received in February 2025, funds operations into Q2 2026, and that next steps for the AbbVie dermal filler program depend on AbbVie's ongoing interim data review.

negative_highlights: Q4 netback fell 19% to $35.94/BOE from $44.40 on a 17% price decrease
2024 net income of $18.1M and EPS of $0.51 declined 6% from $19.3M and $0.54 in 2023
Full-year operating expenses rose to $7.44/BOE from $6.61, including $0.63 of prior-year true-ups
positive_highlights: Q4 production up 56% YoY to 4,440 BOE/d; full-year production up 24% to 3,478 BOE/d, both within guidance
2024 CapEx of $31.3M was $2M below the low end of guidance while revenue and adjusted EBITDA hit record highs
2025 guidance projects 29-47% production growth and 32-61% adjusted EBITDA growth, fully funded by cash flow
summary: Kolibri reported Q4 revenue of $17.4M (+29% YoY) and EPS of $0.16 (vs $0.14), with production up 56% to 4,440 BOE/d and adjusted EBITDA of $13.5M (+28%). Full-year revenue rose 60% to $58.5M with adjusted EBITDA of $44M, both within guidance, and CapEx came in $2M below the low end at $31.3M. 2025 guidance calls for production of 4,500-5,100 BOE/d (+29-47%) and revenue of $75-89M (+28-52%), with net debt held at $25-30M. Operating costs of $6.59/BOE in Q4 and netbacks of $35.94/BOE declined from $44.40 a year ago on lower prices.

negative_highlights: FY2024 operating loss widened to $16.16 million from $14.93 million in 2023, and full-year gross margin was only about 11% with cost of sales at 89% of net sales.
The 2025 revenue guidance range is unusually wide ($20–34.5 million), and reaching cash flow breakeven requires hitting the higher end of revenue guidance.
The company enacted a 1-for-10 reverse stock split in March 2025 to maintain NASDAQ listing compliance, and a warrant inducement raised net proceeds of $6.3 million.
positive_highlights: FY2024 net sales of $8.48 million rose 455% YoY from $1.53 million, with Q4 net sales of ~$2.93 million up ~250% YoY, exceeding the prior $6–8 million guidance range.
December 2024 gross margin exceeded 20% (about 21%), roughly 3x the Q3 level, versus ~11% for the full year, as branded e-commerce sales reached 58% of revenue versus 7% in 2023.
FY2025 revenue guidance of $20–34.5 million implies roughly a tripling of 2024 revenue at the midpoint, with gross margin targeted at 25–30% by late 2025.
summary: Worksport reported FY2024 net sales of $8.48 million, up 455% from $1.53 million, with Q4 net sales of approximately $2.93 million versus $839,000 a year earlier, exceeding the prior full-year guidance range of $6–8 million. Full-year gross margin was about 11%, but December gross margin exceeded 20% (21%) as the mix shifted toward branded products and away from lower-margin private label. The company issued FY2025 revenue guidance of $20–34.5 million, with the $20 million low end derived from tunnel covers alone and the incremental $15 million from roughly 5,000 SOLIS/COR units at ~$3,000 per kit, targeting gross margin of 25–30% by late 2025 and cash flow breakeven by late 2025 or early 2026. FY2024 operating loss widened to $16.16 million from $14.93 million, though loss per share improved 31% to $5.84 from $8.44.

negative_highlights: Q4 revenue fell 17.2% YoY to $8.1 million and full-year revenue declined to $34.6 million from $37.9 million
MRI network permanent placement/executive search segment declined 18.6% versus 2023 and fell note weakness in of internal expectations, prompting a $6 million impairment taken in Q3
Management said Q1 2025 has shown no real improvement from a soft December, with manufacturing and warehousing continuing to weaken
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to 47% from 44% in Q4 and full year despite the revenue decline
SG&A down 22.7% in Q4 and 12.4% for the year, with workers' comp expense down ~46% to $2 million and expected to fall further in 2025
Adjusted net income roughly flat at $9.9 million for the full year ($0.71 vs $0.72 per share) despite a 8.7% revenue decline
summary: Q4 revenue fell 17.2% YoY to $8.1 million (full year $34.6 million vs $37.9 million), with system-wide sales down to $134.8 million from $143.5 million; franchise royalties were $7.6 million vs $8.9 million. GAAP net income was $2.2 million ($0.16/diluted share) versus $15,000 a year ago, while adjusted net income was $2.6 million ($0.19) vs $2.5 million ($0.18) and adjusted EBITDA fell to $3.8 million from $4.3 million despite margin expanding to 47% from 44%. SG&A fell 22.7% in the quarter and 12.4% for the year, driven by a roughly 46% drop in workers' comp expense to $2 million, and management expects further workers' comp improvement in 2025. No formal forward guidance was issued, but management said Q1 has not improved from December and called the demand environment volatile ('three steps forward, three steps back').

negative_highlights: Q4 2024 revenue fell to $9.1 million from $41 million a year earlier, driven by note-side revenue dropping to $2.7 million from $33.4 million.
Adjusted EBITDA excluding unusual items swung to a $3 million loss in Q4 2024 from $2.2 million of income in Q4 2023.
Cash and cash equivalents ended 2024 at $1.4 million versus $5.1 million at year-end 2023, with total cash plus accounts receivable at $6.4 million versus $42.3 million.
positive_highlights: Gross margin expanded to 32% in Q4 2024 from 23% in Q4 2023 on a higher note-side revenue mix.
Operating expenses fell to $7.7 million in Q4 2024 from $18.1 million a year earlier, with roughly $2.1 million of sequential cost savings.
New note-side client wins in new verticals are expected to add $5 million to $10 million of incremental revenue in 2025, with full impact starting in Q2.
summary: Q4 2024 revenue was $9.1 million versus $41 million in Q4 2023, with watch-side revenue of $2.7 million versus $33.4 million and watch-side revenue of $6.4 million versus $7.6 million. Gross margin improved to 32% from 23% on a higher watch-side mix, and operating expenses fell to $7.7 million from $18.1 million; adjusted EBITDA was a $3.4 million loss versus a $6.6 million loss a year earlier. FY2025 revenue guidance was reiterated at $90 million to $110 million, with management expecting stronger second-half gains as new direct watch-side connections ramp and alternative pathways come online. Management attributed the revenue decline to a mid-2024 customer pause from a defamatory article and noted the customer has resumed but volumes have not returned to prior levels.

negative_highlights: Gross margin contracted by 460 basis points from 29.2% in the prior year quarter primarily due to customer marketing support costs.
Operating income swung from positive $1.2M in Q4 FY23 to negative $1.3M in Q4 FY24 as higher operating expenses ($10M vs $7.8M) and lower gross profit offset revenue growth.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 15% year-over-year to $35.6M driven by a 40.2% increase in Bath Furniture revenue and strong growth across US (14.7%), Canada, and Europe markets.
Bath Furniture segment outpaced sales expectations due to new business wins and market-aligned program pricing.
summary: FGI reported Q4 FY2024 revenue of $35.6 million (up 15% YoY) but GAAP operating income turned negative at -$1.3 million due to a gross margin decline from 29.2% to 24.6%. Management provided initial full-year 2025 guidance for adjusted net income between negative $1.9 million and positive $1 million, explicitly noting that the outlook is conservative given tariff pressures.

negative_highlights: Management explicitly stated current cash balance is insufficient to complete the Phase 3 trial, necessitating future capital raises.
Funding environment described as 'difficult and challenging', requiring a stepwise approach to raising necessary funds including equity or debt.
No specific financial guidance provided for upcoming quarters; focus remains on clinical milestones rather than revenue generation.
positive_highlights: Net loss narrowed year-over-year from $42.9M to $37.6M due to a decrease in total operating expenses of $6.7 million (R&D down $5.2M, G&A down $1.5M).
VERSATILE-003 Phase 3 trial initiated with FDA approval for the Versamune HPV + pembrolizumab combination.
Phase 2 data showed improved median overall survival of 30 months and objective response rate increased to 36% compared to prior benchmarks.
summary: PDS Biotech reported a net loss of $37.6 million for the full year ended December 31, 2024, compared to a prior-year loss of $42.9 million, driven by decreased operating expenses partially offset by increased interest expense on debt and lower cash balances. The company initiated its VERSATILE-003 Phase 3 clinical trial with an FDA-approved design for approximately 350 patients targeting HPV16-positive head and neck cancer, reducing the sample size from over 400 based on improved durability data observed in the Phase 2 study. Management indicated that current cash reserves of $41.7 million are insufficient to complete the Phase 3 trial without further capital raises via equity or non-dilutive sources.

negative_highlights: Net loss increased to approximately $25 million from $26 million due to higher manufacturing and R&D costs.
Cash balance decreased to $5.5 million at year-end, reflecting significant cash usage in operating activities.
Management stated they have 'no idea' regarding potential pauses or changes to BARDA funding following political shifts.
positive_highlights: BARDA Project Next-Gen Award valued at almost $400 million announced in June for the GEO-CM04S1 COVID-19 vaccine program.
summary: GeoVax reported a net loss of approximately $25 million for FY2024 compared to $26 million in the prior year, driven by increased R&D expenses and manufacturing costs associated with its BARDA contract. While revenues from the BARDA project reached roughly $4 million (up from zero), management provided no specific financial guidance or earnings estimates for 2025 due to ongoing uncertainties regarding government funding levels and potential trial delays. The company highlighted progress on clinical programs, including a new manufacturing process and discussions with international partners like WHO.

negative_highlights: Full-year medical margin decreased by approximately 37% year-over-year, driven primarily by elevated medical expenses including Part D costs.
Q4 adjusted EBITDA included unfavorable out-of-period true-ups of roughly $17 million related to accounting process cleanup and a single-payer partner.
Part D expense reduction is ongoing but has not yet fully offset the impact of increased facility unit costs and surgical procedure utilization.
positive_highlights: Management reaffirmed all revenue and profitability guidance metrics except slightly raising total membership expectations.
Operational efficiencies of $20 million were executed in Q4, alongside contract rationalization yielding an additional $35 million EBITDA improvement.
Early indicators for 2025 show positive trends with utilization improving following benefit design changes and a reduction in Part D risk exposure.
summary: P3 Health Partners reported Q4 FY2024 revenue of $371 million (up 7% YoY) and full-year adjusted EBITDA loss widening to $68 million in the quarter due to unfavorable out-of-period true-ups. Management reaffirmed its 2025 guidance for revenues between $1.35 billion and $1.5 billion, while slightly raising total membership expectations to a range of 109,000-119,000 members. The company reiterated an adjusted EBITDA outlook ranging from negative $35 million to positive $5 million for the full year.

negative_highlights: FY2024 net loss of $102.3 million and operating loss of $114 million with no product revenue.
R&D expense rose to $93.8 million, driven by ALTITUDE-AD spending, with no cost guidance provided.
Subcutaneous formulation still requires further formulation work and dosing planning, with no timeline disclosed.
positive_highlights: ALTITUDE-AD Phase 2 enrolled 542 participants in about 10 months, faster than planned, with topline expected late 2026.
Phase 1 subcutaneous sabirnetug showed exposure supporting continued development; injection-site reactions were 62.5% but all mild.
Cash and marketable securities of $231.5 million expected to fund operations into the first half of 2027.
summary: Acumen reported FY2024 R&D expense of $93.8 million, G&A of $20.2 million, an operating loss of $114 million, and a net loss of $102.3 million, ending 2024 with $231.5 million in cash and marketable securities with runway into 1H 2027. The key operational update was completion of enrollment of 542 participants in the Phase 2 ALTITUDE-AD trial roughly 10 months after first dosing, with topline results expected in late 2026. The company also reported Phase 1 subcutaneous sabirnetug data showing tolerability, a 62.5% injection-site reaction rate that was all mild, and exposure supporting continued development. There is no revenue or EPS, and no formal financial guidance was provided.

negative_highlights: The company filed a late Form 10-K due to errors in stock-based compensation and R&D expense timing, resulting in unaudited operating results.
Full-year operating losses widened slightly to $36.2 million from $54.5 million in the prior year due to increased sales and marketing spend.
Management noted that Q1 2025 growth may be 'lumpy' as the company shifts strategy from opening new accounts to driving utilization in existing ones.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 44% sequentially and 59% year-over-year, reinforcing a high-growth trajectory.
Gross margin remained strong at 85% in Q4 despite increased sales and marketing investments.
R&D expenses decreased by 62% quarter-over-quarter to $3 million as the company prioritized its technology platform.
summary: TriSalus reported Q4 FY2024 revenue of $8.3 million (up 44% YoY) and full-year revenue of $29.4 million (up 59% YoY), driven by TriNav adoption in new accounts and increased utilization. Gross margins remained robust at 85% for the quarter, while R&D expenses decreased significantly to $3 million due to strategic shifts. Management reiterated guidance for over 50% revenue growth in 2025, noting potential back-loading of that growth as they shift focus from account acquisition to driving utilization in existing accounts.

negative_highlights: Q4 net product revenues decreased slightly to $16.4 million from $16.6 million in Q4 2023.
Full-year revenue remained flat at $69.3 million, failing to grow despite the competitive landscape shifting.
positive_highlights: Completed enrollment for Phase 3 LOTIS-5 trial in second-line-plus DLBCL setting.
Initial efficacy data from LOTIS-7 showed a 94% best overall response rate and 72% complete response rate in the subset of patients.
Achieved double-digit reduction in operating expenses for the second consecutive year.
summary: ADC Therapeutics reported Q4 FY2024 net product revenues of $16.4 million, which was slightly below the prior year's $16.6 million, while full-year 2024 revenue remained flat at $69.3 million versus $69.1 million in 2023. The company achieved a significant operational milestone by completing enrollment for the Phase 3 LOTIS-5 trial and reporting encouraging initial efficacy data from the LOTIS-7 trial, showing a 94% best overall response rate in a subset of patients. Management maintained full-year revenue guidance at the prior year level despite competitive pressures from bispecifics.

negative_highlights: Total revenue declined 11% due to exit from Swivel Secure
Hardware revenue declined 88% in Q4
Net loss per share still $15.02 for 2024
positive_highlights: License fee revenue up 20% to $5.2 million in 2024
Gross margin improved to 78% adjusted from 64%
Cash burn reduced 23% to $2.9 million
summary: BIO-key's Q4 FY2024 revenue declined 11% to $6.9 million, with license fee revenue up 20% to $5.2 million, partially offset by lower-margin services and hardware declines after exiting a Swivel Secure agreement. Gross margin improved to 78% adjusted, and net loss narrowed to $4.3 million from $8.5 million. Management is confident about 2025 growth, citing a $910,000 contract, a tripling defense deployment, and a strengthened balance sheet with $3.8 million warrant proceeds.

negative_highlights: Q4 adjusted EBITDA missed the outlook with a loss of $1.1 million, primarily driven by front-loaded lease depreciation costs associated with rapid gross originations growth.
Write-offs as a percent of revenue increased to 9.6% in Q4 from 8.7% in Q4 FY2023 and remained elevated compared to the prior year's low single digits.
Management expressed caution regarding Wayfair, which represented 27% of total gross originations but saw application flow decline; they remain conservative on home furnishings and mattresses.
positive_highlights: Q4 revenue beat expectations with $63 million reported, representing 9.4% YoY growth and the seventh consecutive quarter of positive growth.

Gross originations grew 11.3% to $75.2 million in Q4, exceeding the internal guidance range of 6%-8%, driven by a strong holiday season with December up 24%. Excluding home furnishings/mattress, direct and waterfall gross originations grew over 50%.
The company achieved its first full-year of positive adjusted EBITDA ($4.8 million) in FY2024 after reporting losses previously.
summary: Katapult reported Q4 revenue of $63 million (up 9.4% YoY) and gross originations growth of 11.3%, both beating the company's guidance range. However, adjusted EBITDA was a loss of $1.1 million in Q4 due to front-loaded lease depreciation from strong prior-quarter growth, missing its positive outlook for the quarter but delivering full-year profitability of $4.8 million. Management raised 2025 gross originations and revenue growth guidance to at least 20% while maintaining a gross margin target range of 18%-20%, noting that Q1 margins will be impacted by continued high depreciation costs.

negative_highlights: Q4 revenue fell 27.3% sequentially due to seasonal parcel delivery delays
Guided deliveries fell note weakness in for the year
Potential tariffs could add $5,000 to $20,000 per vehicle in costs
positive_highlights: Full-year 2024 GAAP gross margin turned positive at 7.1% vs -2.9% in 2023
Secured several major orders after quarter-end, including ~200 strip chassis for UPS and 20 hubs for Caltrans
Implemented over $10 million in cost reductions in the last 12 months
summary: XOS reported Q4 2024 revenue of $11.5 million (down 27.3% from Q3) and 51 unit deliveries, missing guided deliveries due to seasonal parcel delays. Full-year 2024 revenue grew to $56 million from $44.5 million, with positive GAAP gross margin of 7.1% and non-GAAP gross margin of 18%. Management guided for continued gross margin growth in 2025, citing cost reductions and higher-margin hub mix, while flagging tariff risks and charging infrastructure as key uncertainties. The company secured major orders post-quarter, including nearly 200 strip chassis for UPS and 20 hubs for Caltrans.

negative_highlights: Financial results for the back half of FY24 did not live up to expected levels.
The Infinite Reality acquisition deal has not completed and its exclusivity period expired, forcing exploration of alternative strategic options.
Management explicitly stated that financial performance in H2 2024 was a 'speed bump' on the path to profitability.
positive_highlights: Revenue from mobile gaming expanded to roughly 16% of total revenue in Q4 with a trajectory toward 20% in Q1.
summary: Management disclosed that financial results for the back half of FY24 did not meet expectations due to micro-cap headwinds and structural shifts in the Roblox ad ecosystem. The company is executing a strategic realignment including leadership changes (CEO transition) and cost restructuring, with an aim to achieve EBITDA positivity by Q4 2025. While revenue diversification into mobile games shows promise at approximately 16% of total revenue in Q4, the immediate focus remains on reducing burn rather than reporting specific beat/miss figures.

negative_highlights: Operating expenses increased significantly due to a noncash ground lease accrual exceeding $1.4 million and hiring costs for new campuses.
Debt service coverage ratio for the Obligated Group in 2025 is projected at 1.36x, lower than the previously stated expectation of over 3x three years ago due to current revenue ramp-up status.
positive_highlights: Consolidated revenues increased 13% sequentially over Q3 driven by new leases and optimized operations at existing campuses.
Assets under construction and completed construction accelerated to reach over $250 million as of year-end.
Management confirmed they have crossed into positive cash flow from operations at the project level for Sky Harbour Capital.
summary: Consolidated revenues increased 13% sequentially in Q4 to over $250 million in assets under construction/completed construction driven by new leases and the Camarillo acquisition, while full-year consolidated revenues doubled versus 2023. Operating expenses rose due to hiring for new campuses and a noncash ground lease accrual of over $1.4 million at three airport locations. Management reaffirmed guidance to reach cash flow breakeven in Q4 but noted that the Obligated Group's debt service coverage ratio is currently lower than prior 3-year projections until later campus ramps.

negative_highlights: Ovaprene Phase III study recruitment paused at CCTN sites due to uncertainty surrounding federal contracts and funding following executive orders in Q1 2025.
Company reported a comprehensive loss of $4.5 million for the full year ended December 31, 2024.
Enrollment rate prediction impossible for Ovaprene Phase III study due to recruitment pauses at designated sites.
positive_highlights: Royalty monetization transaction with XOMA closed in Q4 2024 generating $22 million in gross proceeds to fund development activities.
Non-dilutive funding awards totaling up to $20.7 million secured from a Federal Agency and the Gates Foundation during 2024.
Significant cost reductions achieved with G&A expenses down 24% year-over-year driven by reduced headcount.
summary: Daré Bioscience reported a comprehensive loss of $4.5 million for the year ended December 31, 2024, with G&A expenses decreasing by 24% to approximately $9.2 million and R&D expenses falling by 34% to roughly $14.2 million due to reduced headcount and commercial readiness costs. The company closed a royalty monetization transaction receiving $22 million in gross proceeds from XOMA for its product candidate XACIATO, alongside up to $20.7 million in non-dilutive funding awards received during the year. Management announced a strategic pivot to utilize Section 503B compounding pathways to make their proprietary Sildenafil Cream formulation available via prescription by Q4 2025 as an interim revenue source while continuing FDA approval efforts, though they noted that recent executive orders and federal contract uncertainties have paused recruitment at key clinical trial sites for the Ovaprene Phase III study.

negative_highlights: Gross margin fell to 16% in 2024 from 20%, hit by $3.9 million inventory write-offs
Cash dropped to $0.9 million from $1.8 million year-over-year
Germany Q4 growth slower than Q2/Q3 due to supply chain delays
positive_highlights: Q4 adjusted EBITDA positive at $0.5 million, a ~$5 million improvement
German Q4 revenue up 280% YoY; Germany now 40% of H2 revenue
Operating expenses down 42% in Q4; full-year OpEx down 17%
summary: IM Cannabis reported Q4 2024 revenue of $13.3 million, up 25% year-over-year, driven by German revenue growth of 280%, and achieved positive adjusted EBITDA of $0.5 million versus a loss of $4.3 million in Q4 2023. Full-year revenue grew 11% to $54 million, but gross margin fell to 16% from 20% due to $3.9 million inventory write-offs. Management expects Q1 2025 to be the best quarter in Germany to date and sees margin improvement ahead, though it anticipates price compression and no significant Israel growth.

negative_highlights: Q4 revenue fell 24% year-over-year to $8.2 million
FY2025 revenue guidance of $29–32 million implies essentially flat growth versus $29.1 million core revenue in 2024
Cash position of $20.9 million, of which $11.4 million was restricted, with runway only into Q1 2026
positive_highlights: Non-GAAP gross margin rose to 42% in Q4 2024 from 24% a year earlier and from 22% in Q1 2023
Full-year consumables sales grew 14% to $12.8 million and software sales grew 11% to $6.2 million
AMA established a Category 1 CPT code for OGM in hematologic malignancies effective January 1, 2025, with Medicare CLFS listing at about $1,300
summary: Q4 2024 total revenue was $8.2 million, down 24% year-over-year (prior-year included $2 million from discontinued clinical services). GAAP gross margin improved to 42% from 23%, and non-GAAP operating expense fell to $10.6 million from $26.6 million, with cash of $20.9 million and runway extended into Q1 2026. FY2025 revenue guidance of $29–32 million implies roughly flat growth versus $29.1 million core in 2024, with Q1 2025 guided to $6.2–6.3 million and 15–20 new OGM system placements expected.

negative_highlights: The company reported a net loss of $38.5 million for the full year, indicating continued financial distress.
Mytesi prescription volume growth was modest at 3.9% for the full year and only 3.4% sequentially in Q4.
Management did not provide specific revenue or EPS guidance for the next quarter.
positive_highlights: Full-year 2024 net revenue increased 20% to $11.7 million versus $9.8 million in 2023.
Q4 2024 revenue grew 53% year-over-year to $3.5 million, driven by a 9.4% increase in Mytesi prescription volume over Q4 2023.
Net loss for the full year decreased by approximately $2.8 million compared to the prior year.
summary: JAGX reported Q4 FY2024 net revenue of $3.5 million, representing a 13% increase over Q3 and a 53% increase year-over-year, while full-year 2024 revenue reached $11.7 million (up 20%). The company posted a GAAP loss of $38.5 million for the year, a decrease from $41.3 million in the prior year, with Q4 operating loss narrowing to $30.8 million. Management highlighted upcoming catalysts in Q2 2025 regarding breast cancer trial data and bridge financing but did not provide specific financial guidance.

negative_highlights: Infrastructure segment revenue decreased 36.2% due to project timing and completion of large commercial construction projects
Consolidated net loss increased from $9.6 million to $16.9 million on a lower revenue base
Total cash and cash equivalents declined significantly to $48.8 million compared to $80.8 million at the end of 2023
positive_highlights: MediBeacon received FDA approval for its transdermal GFR systems
Life Sciences segment R2 delivered record top line revenues of almost $10 million, a 197% increase over 2023
Spectrum adjusted EBITDA more than doubled to $2.3 million in the fourth quarter compared to last year
summary: INNOVATE reported Q4 FY2024 consolidated revenue of $236.6 million, a decrease of 34.5% year-over-year driven by the Infrastructure segment which fell to $225.7 million from $353.8 million in the prior period. Adjusted EBITDA declined to $15 million for the quarter and net loss widened to $16.9 million compared to a narrower loss of $9.6 million last year, primarily due to project timing delays at DBM Global offset by growth in Life Sciences (R2 revenue up 173%) and Spectrum segments.

negative_highlights: Full-year revenue decreased 6% to $5.6 million due to a slowdown in the consumer market driving decreases in OEM sales.

Gross margin percentage declined from 23.9% in Q4 FY2023 to 22.1% in Q4 FY2024, with full-year margins at 20.5%, attributed to lower volumes and liquidation of non-core products increasing cost of sales.
Cash position weakened significantly with cash on hand dropping from $3.9 million at year-end 2023 to $0.5 million at December 31, 2024.
positive_highlights: Q4 Revenue surged 131% year-over-year to $2 million, primarily driven by expanding OEM relationships with major retailers like Camping World and K-Z Recreational Vehicles.
New Home Energy Storage Solutions (HESS) shipments began in January 2025 targeting a market expected to surpass $123 billion globally by 2029.
Substantial pre-orders were announced for next-generation Group 27, GC2, and Edge batteries featuring vertical heat conduction technology.
summary: Q4 FY2024 revenue reached $2 million (up 131% YoY) driven by OEM sales, while full-year revenue declined 6% to $5.6 million due to a slowdown in the consumer/RV market. Gross margins contracted slightly to 22.1% in Q4 from 23.9% prior year and averaged 20.5% for the full year as lower volumes reduced economies of scale, resulting in an annual net loss of $13.5 million ($21.03/share). Management raised incremental revenue guidance to approximately $5 million for FY2025 based on new OEM partnerships.

negative_highlights: Cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities of approximately $4 million as of December 31, 2024
Company is evaluating a potential reverse stock split to avoid NYSE American delisting
No revenue, EPS, or financial guidance figures were disclosed on the call
positive_highlights: R&D expense declined to $6.2 million in FY2024 from $10.9 million in FY2023
G&A expense declined to $13.7 million in FY2024 from $21.1 million in FY2023
Phase 2 dosing commenced in the DURIPANC pancreatic cancer trial after Erasmus Medical Center Safety Committee approval
summary: AIM ImmunoTech reported no revenue figures for Q4/FY2024, with cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities of approximately $4 million as of December 31, 2024. Full-year R&D expense fell to $6.2 million from $10.9 million and G&A to $13.7 million from $21.1 million, reflecting significant cost reductions. The call focused on clinical pipeline progress, including Phase 2 dosing in the DURIPANC pancreatic cancer trial, a planned Ampligen/FluMist influenza study, and the AMP-518 post-COVID results. Management said it is evaluating options including a potential reverse stock split to maintain NYSE American listing compliance, and will hold a special stockholder meeting within the next month or so to authorize the Board to effect such a split.

negative_highlights: Service revenue declined by $400,000 due to fewer VIP enrollments as part of the strategic shift.
The company remains a net cash user with operating cash flow used at $12.7 million, requiring additional financing in the near term.
New alliance revenues (e.g., Rebis) are not yet reflected in 2024 results and will accelerate starting in Q2 2025.
positive_highlights: Product revenue increased 26% year-over-year to $7.9 million due to higher appliance sales and reduced discounts.
Operating loss decreased by 35% to $11.2 million as the company successfully lowered its cost structure.
Cash position strengthened with total cash and equivalents rising to $6.3 million from $1.6 million.
summary: Vivos Therapeutics reported full year 2024 revenue of $15 million, a 9% increase from $13.8 million in 2023, driven by a 26% rise in product revenue to $7.9 million despite a decrease in service revenue. Operating loss narrowed significantly to $11.2 million from $17.3 million due to cost-cutting measures and higher gross profit, while the company raised approximately $17.9 million through equity transactions. Management highlighted a strategic pivot toward sleep center alliances and acquisitions, noting that 2025 is expected to be materially better than 2024 as new revenue streams from these partnerships begin to materialize.

negative_highlights: Cash at year-end only $3.3 million, with continued cash burn
No revenue guidance for 2025 due to lumpy revenues
Centralized lab automation still needed for scale; current ELISA platform manual and limited
positive_highlights: Full-year revenue up 59% to $1.2 million
Vet test volumes more than doubled to ~120,000 tests, revenue up 75%
Operating expenses down 23% full-year and 31% in H2
summary: VolitionRx reported Q4 FY2024 full-year revenue of $1.2 million, up 59% year-over-year, with vet revenue up 75% to $0.8 million and Discover revenue up 40% to $0.4 million. Operating expenses were reduced 23% year-over-year and 31% in H2, while net cash used in operations was $25.9 million. Cash at year-end was $3.3 million, with subsequent non-dilutive funding and equity sales. Management reiterated its 2025 cash-neutral goal and emphasized progress toward licensing deals in human space, but did not provide revenue guidance.

negative_highlights: Management explicitly refused to share future revenue forecasts or guidance.
Revenues are described as non-linear, with potential decreases between different periods due to project-based ordering.
Stock price dropped recently, which management attributed to a lack of information about an Indian distributor agreement rather than operational issues.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 50% year-over-year to approximately $6.1 million.
Net loss decreased by 54% from $3.7 million in 2022 to $1.2 million in 2024.
Secured a $1 million order for the Amethyst 5G platform from a U.S. customer.
summary: Maris-Tech reported a 50% year-over-year revenue increase to approximately $6.1 million in FY2024 and reduced its net loss by 54% to $1.2 million. Management highlighted significant defense contracts, including orders for armored vehicles and U.S. market penetration, but explicitly stated that future revenue forecasts are not public information at this stage. The company noted that revenues are currently non-linear due to the project-based nature of its order book.

negative_highlights: Total revenue declined slightly on a year-over-year basis for the fourth quarter.
The company explicitly stated it is not providing financial guidance or forward-looking numbers at this time.
Operating loss remained significant at $3.18 million in Q4, though flat versus last year.
positive_highlights: Subscription revenue grew 10% year-over-year, now accounting for over $6.2 million in full-year total.
Gross margin expanded to 82% from 78%, driven by a reduction in cost of revenues and the shift away from professional services.
Net retention rate improved significantly to 100% from 73% last year, supported by six major logo renewals in Q4.
summary: Q4 FY2024 revenue declined slightly to $1.66 million compared to the prior year quarter, while full-year subscription revenue grew only 10% YoY despite a shift in business model toward SaaS (87% of total). The company reported an operating loss of $3.18 million for Q4 and significantly reduced OpEx by 20%, but explicitly stated it is not providing financial guidance due to the transition period.

negative_highlights: Full-year 2024 revenue declined 5% to $210.5 million and global operating loss widened 17% to $14 million
Full-year net loss attributable to Reading increased to $35.3 million, or $1.58 per share, from $30.7 million (loss of $1.38 per share) in 2023
Interest expense rose $1.7 million for the year, and management expects Q1 2025 to be 'a disappointment' versus last year due to a softer film slate
positive_highlights: Q4 2024 adjusted EBITDA of $6.8 million, up over 400% from negative $2.2 million in Q4 2023 and the highest fourth-quarter EBITDA since Q4 2019
Global cinema revenue rose 30% YoY to $54.6 million in Q4, with cinema operating income up 191% to $3.8 million
Culver City sold for $10 million and Wellington assets closed for NZD38 million, enabling repayment of NZD18.8 million Westpac debt and $6.1 million of Bank of America debt
summary: Q4 2024 global revenue rose 29% YoY to $58.6 million, with operating income of $1.5 million versus a $7 million loss a year earlier, and adjusted EBITDA of $6.8 million versus a negative $2.2 million. Full-year revenue fell 5% to $210.5 million, operating loss widened 17% to $14 million, and net loss attributable to Reading grew to $35.3 million ($1.58 per share) from $30.7 million. Management said Q1 2025 will likely be soft versus a year ago due to a weaker film slate, but pointed to a stronger remainder of 2025. The company is prioritizing debt reduction via asset sales — Culver City sold for $10 million, Wellington closed for NZD38 million, and Cannon Park is under contract — while total borrowings stood at $202.7 million against $12.3 million of cash.

negative_highlights: Revenue decreased 2% year-over-year due to a $1.5 million decline in CDMO revenues.
Net loss of $14.8 million included $2.2 million in litigation expenses related to an activist investor matter.
Adjusted EBITDA declined $0.7 million primarily due to inventory write-downs and lower development revenue.
positive_highlights: Revenues remained on target for the fiscal year guidance.
Cash balance strengthened to over $30 million following the sale of unused filler assets.
Signed new agreements with Nirsum Laboratories and Humanetics, adding to the late-stage pipeline.
summary: Lifecore reported Q3 FY2025 revenues of $35.2 million, a 2% decrease year-over-year, and a net loss of $14.8 million compared to prior year income. Adjusted EBITDA decreased to $5.7 million from $6.4 million in the prior year period. Management reiterated full-year guidance for revenue between $126.5 million and $130 million and adjusted EBITDA between $19 million and $21 million, citing steady execution despite one-time legal expenses.

negative_highlights: No operational profitability yet; management pushed the first operational profit to 2026, relying on a 2025 development profit from a sale-leaseback rather than operations
Ford Amphitheater's $15.2 million in gross receipts are subject to the split with AEG Presents Rocky Mountains, and amphitheater net profit to Venu was only $1.66 million (9% of revenue)
No EPS, margin detail, or formal guidance figures were disclosed, leaving the profitability path dependent on unopened venues and future FireSuite sales
positive_highlights: FireSuite sales reached $77.7 million in 2024, up 250% from $22.2 million in 2023, with January 2025 at $10.4 million and February at $11.2 million toward a $200 million 2025 goal
Total annual revenue rose 42% to $17.8 million from $12.6 million, with Event Center Operations up 74% ($2.2 million) and restaurant operations up 14% ($1.3 million)
Fractional ownership financing added with banks now lending, which management said doubled sales and expanded the buyer pool to triple-net investors
summary: Venu reported fiscal 2024 revenue of $17.8 million, up 42% from $12.6 million, with FireSuite sales of $77.7 million versus $22.2 million in 2023 (a 250% increase) and total assets up 114% to $178.4 million. The Ford Amphitheater generated $15.2 million in gross receipts over 20 shows with 97,000+ tickets at a $156 average, though those receipts are subject to the AEG split. Management guided to a 2025 development profit from a Ford Amphitheater ground sale-leaseback, with the first operational profit expected in 2026 as four venues open, and reiterated a $200 million FireSuite sales target for 2025. No formal EPS, margin, or consensus comparison was provided, so the read rests on revenue growth and forward commentary.

negative_highlights: Q2 gross margin fell to about 38% from the 50%+ year-to-date level, which management attributed to percent-complete timing rather than a demand issue
Oil and gas royalty deliveries were weak as forecast, with the bulk of drilling activity pushed to late 2025/early 2026 and more meaningful volumes in fiscal 2026
No acquisition under contract or timeline for the I-70 interchange, which remains subject to a permit submission and four-to-five month CDOT review before bond issuance
positive_highlights: Year-to-date revenue of about $9.7 million with gross margin around 50%+, and year-to-date EPS of about $0.20, roughly half of the FY2025 EPS goal
Water Utilities segment had a good quarter on tap fee recognition from Filing 5, with close to 75 vertical homes and builders described as aggressive, adding recurring customers
Liquidity above $20 million including about $17 million of cash and investments, plus the approximately $25 million 2024 bond offering reimbursables supporting the note receivable
summary: PureCycle reported Q2 FY2025 revenue of about $4 million with gross margin of roughly 38%, well below the ~50%+ gross margin the company cited for the six-month year-to-date period of about $9.7 million in revenue. Management said the quarter is seasonally the softest and that a percent-complete timing shift explains the lower sequential gross profit, and it maintained FY2025 revenue guidance of roughly $30-31 million, noting year-to-date EPS of about $0.20 is just shy of half that target. Oil and gas royalty deliveries were weak as forecast, with more than 200 well permits under production expected to drive activity in fiscal 2026, and no new acquisition or interchange timeline was provided beyond a permit and bond process running to end of 2025 and into 2026.

negative_highlights: Management explicitly paused share buyback strategy, citing a 'scary time' and caution over the next few months.
Significant macro headwinds including tariffs, trade wars, government spending disruptions (DOGE), and nervous capital markets causing equity outflows.
positive_highlights: Exceptional level of earnings producing top-tier returns on equity despite capital levels being at record highs.
summary: Bank7 Corp reported a 'great quarter' with strong earnings and exceptional returns on equity despite macro uncertainty regarding tariffs and government spending disruptions. Management highlighted clean credit migration, low past dues, and successful cost management that lowered the average cost of funds to 2.58%. However, due to volatile market conditions and geopolitical risks (specifically China debt concerns), leadership decided to pause share buybacks until near-term normalcy returns.

negative_highlights: Ending active subscribers fell 4.9% YoY to 119,778 and were down from 132,518 at Q3 end, which management attributed to reduced paid marketing and seasonality
Gross margin contracted to 37.7% from 39.4% a year ago on higher revenue-share costs as Share by RTR's mix rose

FY2025 guidance implies renewed cash consumption of -$30M to -$40M with CapEx of $70-75M, and management explicitly declined to guide full-year revenue or adjusted EBITDA; Q1 revenue of $68-70M is below the $76.4M just reported
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA rose to $17.4M (22.8% of revenue) in Q4 from $11.2M (14.8%) a year earlier, and full-year adjusted EBITDA reached $46.9M (15.3% of revenue) versus $26.9M (9%)
Full-year free cash flow improved to -$7.2M from -$70.3M, and unrestricted cash at end-February 2025 was $81.2M, only $2.8M below end-FY2023
Operating expenses fell 20.8% YoY and dropped to 44% of revenue from 55.9%, and Share by RTR sourced about 50% of FY2024 inventory purchases
summary: Q4 FY2024 revenue was $76.4M, up 0.8% YoY, with subscription and reserve rental revenue down 1.2% YoY; ending active subscribers fell 4.9% YoY to 119,778 and gross margin compressed to 37.7% from 39.4%. Adjusted EBITDA rose sharply to $17.4M (22.8% of revenue) from $11.2M, and full-year free cash flow improved to -$7.2M from -$70.3M, helped by a $6.6M FY2024 cash decline versus $70.5M in FY2023. Management guided FY2025 to double-digit ending active subscriber growth and cash consumption of -$30M to -$40M, with no full-year revenue or EBITDA guidance, and gave Q1 revenue of $68-70M with adjusted EBITDA at negative 5-7% of revenue. The plan centers on roughly doubling inventory units in FY2025, with ~62% sourced via Share by RTR, funded by CapEx of $70-75M, a deliberate step-up from FY2024's near-breakeven cash posture.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA declined to $855M from $916M and adjusted EPS fell to $0.46 from $0.54 year over year
Gross margin excluding fuel and LIFO contracted 45 bps on lower-margin pharmacy mix and e-commerce delivery costs
FY2025 adjusted EBITDA guidance of $3.8-3.9B includes ~$65M from the 53rd week, implying underlying EBITDA pressure
positive_highlights: E-commerce sales grew 24% and loyalty membership exceeded 45 million, up over 15% year over year
Pharmacy revenue increased 18%, with core script volume growing year over year
Announced $1.5B productivity savings program for FY2025-2027 to fund investments and offset inflation
summary: Albertsons reported Q4 FY2024 ID sales growth of 2.3%, adjusted EBITDA of $855M (down from $916M), and adjusted EPS of $0.46 (down from $0.54). Gross margin excluding fuel and LIFO fell 45 bps, driven by lower-margin pharmacy sales and e-commerce delivery costs. Fiscal 2025 guidance was initiated with ID sales growth of 1.5-2.5%, adjusted EBITDA of $3.8-3.9B (including ~$65M from the 53rd week), and adjusted EPS of $2.03-2.16. Management framed 2025 as a year of accelerated investment in digital, media, and pharmacy that will create margin headwinds, with gradual improvement expected in the second half.

negative_highlights: FY2024 revenue fell to $1.8 million, down $4.8 million year over year, on reduced government contracts.
Net loss widened to $134.9 million from $50.7 million in 2023, including a $127.6 million debt extinguishment loss and a $106.4 million incremental restatement impact.
The company restated Q1-Q3 2024 financials for incorrect debt modification accounting, and cash at year-end was only $1.2 million.
positive_highlights: Adjusted net loss improved by $8.2 million to $26.1 million for 2024 despite a $4.8 million revenue decline.
2025 revenue guidance of greater than $16 million versus $1.8 million reported in 2024, supported by initial ROV/Aquanaut contracts including a confirmed 120-day drill support contract.
Operating expenses fell to $24.9 million, a $36.8 million reduction from 2023, and the $110.3 million Series A preferred exchange removed the debt from the balance sheet.
summary: FY2024 revenue was $1.8 million, down $4.8 million from 2023, with the decline attributed to reduced government contracts; net loss was $134.9 million including a $127.6 million debt extinguishment loss, and adjusted net loss improved to $26.1 million from $34.3 million. The company restated Q1-Q3 2024 financials and recorded a $106.4 million incremental noncash net loss impact from correcting accounting for a January 2024 debt transaction, which was subsequently exchanged into $110.3 million of Series A preferred stock, and regained Nasdaq compliance in February 2025. Management guides 2025 revenue to exceed $16 million, up from $1.8 million reported in 2024, citing an inaugural Aquanaut commercial season and the recent SeaTrepid acquisition.

negative_highlights: Total revenue excluding divested units declined 3.4% YoY to $42 million
Global airtime revenue fell 23.8% YoY to $9.3 million and the business is being de-emphasized
Full-year net loss was $38.8 million, including $20.9 million in non-cash incentive share expense
positive_highlights: Digital remittance TPV grew 13.2% YoY to $5.14 billion with transaction volume reaching 11.4 million
Remittance gross margin expanded to 62% from 58% as payout ratio declined to 0.12% from 0.15%
Management set a 2025 KPI to grow remittance revenue at least 12.5% while halting take-rate decline
summary: Currenc reported FY2024 revenue (excluding divested TNG Asia and GEA) of $42 million, down 3.4% YoY, driven by a 23.8% decline in global airtime revenue to $9.3 million, while digital remittance revenue rose 6.4% to $18.2 million on 13.2% TPV growth to $5.14 billion. Remittance gross margin improved to 62% from 58% as the payout ratio fell to 0.12% from 0.15%, though the take rate declined to 0.37% from 0.43% due to price competition. Full-year net loss was $38.8 million, heavily impacted by $20.9 million in non-cash incentive share expense and losses from divested units. Management set a 2025 KPI to grow remittance revenue at least 12.5% and expects initial AI revenue in the second half, but provided no formal full-year guidance.

negative_highlights: Management declined to provide financial guidance due to tariff uncertainty, noting even Walmart pulled guidance.
European net sales declined 4% in local currency (7% as reported) due to a non-repeating promotion.
