Westcott cutting tools sales declined, with management expecting the segment to be hit harder by consumer stress from tariffs.
positive_highlights: First aid sales increased 14% in Q1 2025, driving overall growth.
Gross margin expanded 30 basis points to 39.0% from 38.7%.
Bank debt less cash decreased to $27 million from $32 million a year earlier, aided by $12 million in free cash flow.
summary: Acme United reported Q1 FY2025 net sales of $46 million, up 2% from $45 million, with net income of $1.65 million versus $1.63 million and EPS of $0.41 versus $0.39 (up 5%). Gross margin improved slightly to 39.0% from 38.7%, and first aid sales grew 14%, though European sales declined 7% due to a non-repeating promotion and Westcott cutting tools faced a tough comparison from a large 2024 craft order. Management provided no financial guidance, citing tariff uncertainty, and noted that 40% of imports come from China with tariffs currently at 145%, causing them to postpone deliveries and plan price increases.

negative_highlights: Net income fell from a profit of USD 1.13 million in 2023 to a loss of USD 3.87 million in 2024.
Gross profit declined by 25.5% due to reduced premium pricing and increased competition following the Red Sea crisis.
Operating expenses rose significantly by 56.8% to USD 8.7 million, primarily due to business expansion and enhanced ESG initiatives.
positive_highlights: Total sales volume surged by 38.1% year-over-year driven by network expansion to over 60 ports across 4 continents.
Biofuel sales volume increased over 600% year-over-year, supported by the launch of B24 biofuel and ISCC certifications.
Revenue growth in emerging markets was robust, with South Korea up 187%, Singapore up 102%, and Europe/Asia others up 291%.
summary: CBL International reported Q4 FY2024 results for the full year ended December 31, 2024, with total revenue rising 35.9% to USD 592.5 million driven by a 38.1% surge in sales volume and network expansion. However, gross profit declined 25.5% to USD 5.37 million due to strategic pricing adjustments and increased operating expenses of 56.8%, resulting in a net loss of USD 3.87 million compared to a prior year profit. Management attributes the loss to a volume-driven strategy aimed at market share gain and biofuel adoption, with guidance for FY2025 focused on margin recovery through economies of scale and sustainable fuel development.

negative_highlights: Earnings per common share of $0.25 produced a return on average assets of only 0.46% and a return on average equity of 4.78%.
The Avenue banking-as-a-service initiative was discontinued and its intangible fully written off, with management unable to provide a precise cause beyond rising costs and timeline slippage.
Total gross loan growth was only $1 million quarter over quarter, and investor CRE lending is being slowed until political and economic stability improves.
positive_highlights: Net interest margin expanded 34 bps to 3.3%, driven by repricing $171 million of retail CDs and replacing $112 million of wholesale CDs at lower rates.
Non-interest-bearing and low-cost transactional deposits increased $74 million during the quarter.
A court-approved payoff expected in June will reduce non-performing loans from $21.7 million to $10.5 million, a 52% reduction.
summary: MainStreet reported Q1 2025 EPS of $0.25, ROAA of 0.46%, ROAE of 4.78%, and net interest margin of 3.3%, up 34 bps from the prior quarter on deposit repricing. Total gross loans grew only $1 million quarter over quarter, and the company discontinued its Avenue banking-as-a-service initiative, writing off the intangible entirely and planning a 12.5% sequential reduction in operating expenses in Q2. Management guided to margin expansion from $223 million of CD maturities through 2025 and expects NPLs to fall to $10.5 million from $21.7 million after a court-approved June payoff. The quarter reflects weak profitability (0.46% ROAA) and a strategic write-off, offset by meaningful NIM expansion and expense-reduction plans.

negative_highlights: Q2 production faced a slowdown in processing tonnes due to mining harder rock before grade improvements take full effect.
The PEA utilizes a conservative 5% discount rate for valuation rather than the analyst-standard ~10%, which may impact comparable valuations.
positive_highlights: PEA study projects $1.2 billion pretax NPV at $3,000/oz gold price with just under 18 years of mine life.
Processing costs reduced significantly from $22/t to approximately $13-14/t as the plant scaled up.
Management confirmed metallurgical recoveries are improving and sulfide ore is not refractory, addressing a key investor concern.
summary: TRX Gold reported Q2 FY2025 results driven by a robust PEA study released the prior day, projecting an average annual production of over 60,000 ounces with peak output exceeding 90,000 ounces and low cash costs around $1,000/oz. Management highlighted that processing costs have decreased from $22 to roughly $13-14 per tonne due to scale expansion at the plant's current 2,000 tonnes/day capacity. The company is transitioning into higher-grade ore in H2 FY25 following a strip campaign and plans an incremental plant upgrade to increase throughput.

negative_highlights: Consumer sentiment in key markets remains cautious
No tariff impact included in guidance due to uncertainty
India still slow roll with high hopes but no growth acceleration yet
positive_highlights: Consolidated net sales grew 12% YoY in constant currency, including Hiya contribution
Mainland China net sales and active customers grew 6% and 4% sequentially
Hiya delivering robust results with strong growth in net sales and active subscribers
summary: USANA reported Q1 FY2025 consolidated net sales up 12% year-over-year in constant currency, including the first full quarter of Hiya contribution, and results were in line with internal expectations. Direct watching net sales and active customers grew modestly sequentially for the second consecutive quarter, with Mainland China up 6% in net sales and 4% in active customers sequentially. Management reaffirmed full-year guidance, excluding any tariff impact, and highlighted strong Hiya growth and planned product launches in the second half.

negative_highlights: Provision for credit losses rose to $1.5 million from $234,000 in Q4, pushing profitability lower
An $815,000 OREO impairment reduced EPS by $0.03 and ROA by 7 bps; excluding it, earnings were only in line or slightly better
Deposit growth of $64 million lagged loan growth and included $25 million of higher-cost broker deposits; management said deposits are behind budgeted growth
positive_highlights: Net interest margin expanded 11 bps to 3.65% as interest-bearing deposit costs fell 18 bps
Loans grew $92 million, or 12% annualized, with C&I making up 81% of new fundings and investor CRE declining $12 million
NPAs to total assets declined to 0.42% from 0.46% at year-end and 0.64% a year ago
summary: First Bank reported Q1 2025 net income of $9.4 million, or $0.37 per diluted share, with a 1.0% ROA; excluding an $815,000 OREO write-down, EPS was $0.40 and ROA 1.07%. Loans grew $92 million (12% annualized) driven by C&I, while deposits grew $64 million (8% annualized) including $25 million of broker deposits, and NIM expanded 11 bps to 3.65%. Credit loss expense rose to $1.5 million from $234,000 in Q4, commensurate with loan growth, and the allowance ticked up to 1.21%. Management described a stable NIM outlook, slightly ahead-of-plan loan growth but deposit growth behind budget, and a cautiously optimistic but uncertain view on tariffs and DOGE.

negative_highlights: Paid members were slightly down less than 0.5% in April, breaking previous lockstep growth with revenue.
Management raised FCF guidance but described it as 'conservative' due to a 'tumultuous nature of the economy' and tariff uncertainty.
Customers are currently in a 'wait-and-see holding pattern,' delaying hiring and expenditures until macro impacts clarify.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 8% year-over-year despite flat paid member count due to diversified revenue streams including interchange fees which rose 43% YoY.
Expensify travel saw a massive 166% quarter-over-quarter increase in Q1, indicating strong cross-note adoption from the traditional expense product.
New simplified pricing for the 'collect' plan ($5 per member) is designed to improve conversion at the lower end of the market.
summary: Expensify reported Q1 FY2025 revenue of $36.1 million (up 8% YoY) and adjusted net income of $4.8 million, while paid members were flat at approximately 657k in April following a slight decline from the quarter end. Management raised annual free cash flow guidance to $17-$21M but explicitly adopted a conservative tone regarding macroeconomic headwinds and potential tariff impacts on customer behavior.

negative_highlights: Reported Q4 gross margin was negative 79% versus negative 24% in Q3 after a ~$242 million free-charging accounting charge; full-year net loss was $3.2 billion
Q4 ASP fell to ~$16,000 from ~$20,700 in Q3 (down 22%), driven by VF3/VF5 now at 60% of deliveries
2025 cash burn is guided to ~$2.5 billion, up from $1.9 billion in 2024, including ~$1.8 billion for CapEx and R&D
positive_highlights: Full-year deliveries of 97,399 exceeded the 80,000 target; Q4 deliveries of 53,139 rose 43% QoQ and 342% YoY
Full-year adjusted gross loss margin (ex-NRV and one-off charges) narrowed to negative 32% from negative 40% in 2023

Cash burn fell 39% YoY to $1.9 billion, with operating cash burn of just $125 million versus $2.1 billion in 2023; liquidity reached ~$3 billion after over $1.5 billion in founder/Vingroup disbursements
summary: VinFast reported Q4 2024 revenue of $678 million, up 34% QoQ and 70% YoY, with deliveries of 53,139 EVs in the quarter (+43% QoQ, +342% YoY) and 97,399 for the full year, exceeding the 80,000 target. Reported Q4 gross margin was negative 79% versus negative 24% in Q3 due to a ~$242 million free-charging accounting charge; excluding that and NRV, Q4 gross margin was flat QoQ and improved to negative 26% from negative 35% a year prior, and full-year adjusted gross loss narrowed to negative 32% from negative 40%. Full-year net loss was $3.2 billion and cash burn improved 39% YoY to $1.9 billion. Management reaffirmed 2025 guidance to at least double 2024 deliveries, expecting H1 to contribute only 25-30% of the year, with liquidity of ~$3 billion after over $1.5 billion in founder/Vingroup disbursements.

negative_highlights: Consolidated net revenues decreased 2.9% year over year
Consolidated EBITDA decreased 29.1%
Free cash flow was negative for the quarter
positive_highlights: Maintained full-year guidance of 6-9% net revenue and EBITDA growth
Board proposed a 200 million peso dividend
Business remains strongly profitable with EBITDA margin of 15.3%
summary: In Q1 2025, Betterware de México reported a 2.9% decrease in consolidated net revenues, gross margin contraction of 303 basis points, and a 29.1% decline in EBITDA, with EPS down 48.7%. The quarter was affected by softened consumer demand in Mexico and the US, a weakened peso, and China tariffs. Management maintained full-year guidance of 6-9% net revenue and EBITDA growth, despite acknowledging near-term challenges and pausing growth investments in Betterware US. The board proposed a 200 million peso dividend, reflecting prudent cash management.

negative_highlights: Q1 EPS missed expectations due to higher O&M expenses ($81M increase) and increased depreciation reflecting capital investment programs.
Updated estimated liability for Smokehouse Creek wildfires to $290 million, incorporating previously excluded categories like railroad claims and tree damage settlements.
Management noted a change in sentiment meter regarding tariffs over the last 45 days due to recent executive orders and trade actions.
positive_highlights: Electric sales increased 2% quarter-over-quarter driven by growth across most operating companies, with C&I sales up 9% year-over-year in SPS.
Management reaffirmed the ability to deliver earnings for the 21st consecutive year and remains confident in navigating tariff impacts estimated at 2-3% of capital expenditures.
Reached a constructive unanimous settlement on the Colorado wildfire mitigation plan, securing cost recovery mechanisms including insurance deferral extensions.
summary: Xcel Energy reported Q1 FY2025 earnings of $0.84 per share, missing the prior quarter's EPS by a few cents due to higher O&M and depreciation expenses. Management reaffirmed full-year 2025 guidance for EPS between $3.75 and $3.85 despite tariff uncertainties and elevated wildfire liabilities which were updated to an estimated low-end liability of $290 million.

negative_highlights: Deposit growth was flat and total deposits decreased slightly in the quarter
Commercial real estate office property sector is deteriorating with significant vacancy concerns
Management noted loan opportunities are less available than in previous years, limiting portfolio expansion
positive_highlights: Net income increased $700k quarter-over-quarter and $2 million year-over-year
No credit loss expense recorded due to excellent credit quality with no nonaccruals or OREO
Loan yields improved slightly to 5.52% as fixed-rate portfolio cash flows rolled over
summary: Net income was $7.8 million for Q1 FY2025 compared to $7.1 million in the prior quarter and $5.8 million year-over-year, driven by a net interest margin expansion of 30 basis points as deposit costs fell 38 bps. Loan portfolio growth remained modest with approximately $100 million in payoffs from asset sales and refinances replaced at better rates, while deposits decreased slightly due to ordinary cash flow fluctuations rather than relationship loss. Management noted that loan opportunities are currently less available than in previous years despite a good pipeline.

negative_highlights: Virtual Sports EBITDA declined sequentially due to Brazil tax implementation and customer onboarding friction in early quarter.
Leisure business performance was negatively impacted by the slippage of the U.K. Easter holiday from Q1 FY24 to Q2 FY25.
U.K. retail high street market showed softness with key customers Betfred and Paddy Power, though William Hill provided an offset.
positive_highlights: Interactive segment revenue grew 49% YoY while EBITDA surged 75%, expanding margins from 54% to 64%.
U.S. Interactive business grew by 90% against a market growth of only 20%, driven by new states like Delaware and strong content performance.
Debt refinancing secured with flexible terms, extending maturity to June 2026 and reducing call protection.
summary: First quarter adjusted EBITDA of $18.5 million beat the prior year by nearly 20%, driven primarily by a 49% revenue increase and 79% EBITDA growth in the Interactive segment which expanded margins from 54% to 64%. Management successfully refinanced debt with flexible terms, though they noted sequential declines in Virtual Sports due to Brazil regulatory changes. The company reiterated its deleveraging strategy via a holiday park sale and pub business restructuring.

negative_highlights: Revenue decreased 20% year-over-year to $4 million due to weakness in domestic and international businesses
Operating loss widened from $500,000 in Q1 2024 to $900,000 in the current quarter
Retail business expected to remain at current levels until tariff uncertainty resolves
positive_highlights: First green shoots observed in the industrial portion of the business
Launched Xtreme iXG and iXS Series handheld computers powered by iOS
summary: Socket Mobile reported Q1 FY2025 revenue of $4 million, a decrease of 20% year-over-year and 18% sequentially from Q4 2024. Gross margins declined slightly to 50.4%, while the company recorded an operating loss of $900,000 compared to a prior quarter's loss of $400,000. Management expressed caution regarding near-term retail demand due to tariff uncertainty but highlighted initial progress in industrial segments and new product launches.

negative_highlights: Net charge-offs totaled $9.7 million, equivalent to 92 basis points of loans
Nonperforming loans increased to 80 basis points
Net income down to $0.9 million due to elevated provision
positive_highlights: Net interest income up 6.6% linked quarter and 20% year-over-year
Total operating revenue up 22% year-over-year
Fintech revenue forecast for 2025 expected to exceed $4 million
summary: First Internet Bancorp reported Q1 2025 net income of $0.9 million and diluted EPS of $0.11, heavily impacted by $9.7 million in net charge-offs, mostly in franchise finance and small business lending. Net interest income grew 6.6% linked quarter and 20% year-over-year, with net interest margin up 16 basis points; total operating revenue rose 22% year-over-year. The company raised its 2025 fintech revenue forecast from $4 million to 'blow through' that level, and expects continued NII/NIM growth for the year. Credit quality deteriorated with nonperforming loans at 80 basis points, but management cited borrower-specific issues and no systemic stress.

negative_highlights: Trucking revenues fell 20.2% year-over-year driven by a 31.3% drop in volumes.
Intermodal segment reported an operating loss of $10.7 million, with revenue down and rates declining 8.7% excluding fuel.
Contract logistics operating margin compressed to 9.3% from 26% last year due to the completion of a specialty development project and acquisition-related depreciation.
positive_highlights: Auto production volumes rebounded significantly during the quarter, rising 67.1% in March compared to January levels.
Revenue per load in trucking increased by more than 24% excluding fuel surcharges, indicating successful strategy execution on high-yield freight.
Inventory days of supply for automotive customers decreased from 116 days to 70 days, suggesting a healthy unwinding of excess stock.
summary: Universal Logistics Holdings reported Q1 FY2025 total operating revenue of $382.4 million and net income of $6 million ($0.23 EPS), representing significant year-over-year declines compared to $491.9 million revenue and $52.5 million net income in the prior period. The company provided full-year 2025 guidance for top-line revenues between $390 million and $410 million and operating margins between 5% and 7%, which aligns with current performance but reflects a contraction from last year's levels. Management noted that while Q1 results were below historical benchmarks due to an auto production slowdown early in the quarter, they expect the second half of 2025 to look markedly different as inventory levels normalize.

negative_highlights: NIM declined 6 bps QoQ to 3.1% due to lower SOFR-linked asset yields, higher cash balances, and lower average DDA balances.
Average DDA balances fell during the quarter, driving total deposit cost up 1 bp despite a 9 bp reduction in interest-bearing deposit costs.
Nonperforming loans rose 6 bps ($1.4 million) and classified loans rose 7 bps to 0.44% of the portfolio, with the post-quarter yacht sale incurring a loss slightly above $500,000.
positive_highlights: EPS of $0.38 rose 65% year-over-year, described as the best quarter since the 2021 IPO.
Loans surpassed $2 billion, with end-of-period net loan growth of $63.4 million (13% annualized) and deposits up 25% annualized QoQ.
Net losses were zero in the quarter; nonperforming assets improve to 0.13% of total loans after the post-quarter yacht loan sale, and the efficiency ratio improved to 52.79%.
summary: USCB reported Q1 2025 diluted EPS of $0.38, up 65% year-over-year, with loans surpassing $2 billion (up 11.5% YoY on average, 13% annualized QoQ) and deposits up 8.1% YoY (25% annualized QoQ). NIM slipped 6 bps QoQ to 3.1%, ROA was 1.19%, ROE 14.15%, and the efficiency ratio improved to 52.79%. Management guides to high single-digit to low double-digit loan and deposit growth for Q2 and flat-to-slightly-up NIM, with the expense base drifting from $12.1 million toward $12.3–$12.4 million, and noted cautious optimism given tariff and rate uncertainty. The board declared a $0.10 per share dividend, doubling the prior payout.

negative_highlights: Net premiums written decreased by 1.7% due to lower new business volume and planned attrition in personal lines.
Workers' compensation experienced $1.8 million of unfavorable development, though the line remains rate adequate.
Personal lines net premiums written fell 9.9% as part of a strategic initiative to prune less profitable classes.
positive_highlights: Combined ratio improved substantially to 91.6% from 102.4% in the prior year quarter.
After-tax net income surged to $25.2 million, a significant increase compared to $6 million in Q1 2024.
Weather-related losses decreased by 2.2 million dollars and large fire losses dropped by 50%.
summary: Donegal Group reported Q1 FY2025 net premiums earned of $232.7 million (up 2.2% YoY) and a combined ratio of 91.6%, driven by a core loss ratio improvement of 4.5 percentage points to 89.1%. The company achieved record quarterly earnings, exceeding the prior year's record level, with after-tax net income rising significantly from $6 million in Q1 2024 to $25.2 million. Management raised the quarterly cash dividend and highlighted successful systems modernization milestones.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined 33.8% year-over-year due to significantly lower sales volumes and fewer active coaches.
Loss from operations widened to $1.3 million, down $9.2 million versus the prior year period.
SG&A as a percentage of revenue increased 560 basis points primarily due to loss of leverage on fixed costs.
positive_highlights: New coach cohorts are exhibiting new customer growth ahead of last year's levels.
Year-over-year decline in revenue per active earning coach moderated to only 1.4% compared to a 22.8% decline in the prior year.
ASCEND product line orders remained right in line with expectations, reaching mid-teens as a percentage of total orders.
summary: Q1 FY2025 revenue was $115.7 million, a 33.8% year-over-year decrease driven by a 32.8% drop in active earning coaches to approximately 25,400. EPS was $0.07, resulting in a net loss of $0.8 million compared to prior year income. Management provided Q2 guidance for revenue between $85 million and $105 million and a loss per share ranging from zero cents to $0.55.

negative_highlights: Operating costs and expenses rose to $500.3 million from $379.2 million, exceeding total revenue
G&A expenses increased to $47 million from $22.5 million, driven by a $31 million share-based compensation expense and a $5.4 million increase in expected credit losses on accounts receivable
Auto services revenue grew only 5.3% to $226.5 million, lagging the double-digit growth in insurance and technology services
positive_highlights: Total revenue rose 21.5% to $441.9 million, with auto insurance revenue up 44.4% to $170.5 million and technology services up 46.4% to $44.9 million
Adjusted EBITDA increased 492% to $9.8 million from $1.6 million
Tesla partnership expanded to 48 cities from an initial six, and new partnerships were signed with Xiaomi, Zeekr, and SAIC Maxus
summary: SunCar reported FY2024 revenue of $441.9 million, up 21.5% from $363.7 million, with auto insurance revenue up 44.4% to $170.5 million and technology services up 46.4% to $44.9 million; adjusted EBITDA rose 492% to $9.8 million. Growth was driven by EV partnerships including Tesla, which expanded to 48 cities from six, and new entrants such as Xiaomi and Zeekr. GAAP profitability was pressured by a $31 million one-time share-based compensation expense under the 2024 equity incentive plan, which management said will not recur. No formal guidance was issued, but management plans to provide guidance with the Q1 2025 earnings release, and U.S. tariffs are not expected to have a material direct impact.

negative_highlights: Credit card volume growth intentionally paused in Q2 for app improvements
SBA premium levels remain soft; no near-term improvement expected
Nonperforming loans up $6.2 million due to SBA loan repurchase
positive_highlights: Net revenue up 31% year-over-year to $17.4 million
Noninterest income up 127% year-over-year to $5.5 million
Book value per share up 28% to $10.27
summary: GBank Financial Holdings reported Q1 FY2025 net income of $4.5 million or $0.31 per diluted share, including nearly $1 million in one-time expenses. Net revenue was $17.4 million, up 31% year-over-year, with noninterest income up 127% driven by credit card interchange. The company completed its NASDAQ listing, downstreamed $15 million to the bank, and maintains a strong SBA/commercial pipeline of over $300 million. Management expects a temporary slowdown in credit card growth in Q2 as they enhance the app, with major marketing and product launches planned for the second half.

negative_highlights: adjusted EPS still -$0.03; Q1 smallest quarter
tariff uncertainty, holding goods, cautious view
SG&A up 1%, minimal cost growth
positive_highlights: sales up 26%, led by Sonic 3, Moana 2, Dog Man
adjusted EBITDA positive at $0.4M vs -$17.2M last year
gross margin 34.4%, product margin up, SG&A flat
summary: Q1 FY2025 sales grew 26% YoY, with dolls and role play/dress-up up 37% and action play/collectibles up 30%; adjusted EBITDA turned positive at $0.4 million, a $17.6 million improvement. Gross margin hit 34.4%, driven by product mix and favorable timing. The company remains debt-free with $59.2 million cash, but management is cautious on tariffs, holding some goods and adjusting sourcing; 2025 guidance not explicitly reaffirmed.

negative_highlights: Q2 DE guidance of $0.29-$0.31/share is below the $0.34 just reported and below the $0.35 dividend
Up to ~$145 million of loan commitments could prepay at end of Q2, and replacement originations carry lower spreads; management cited low-teens ROE on new investments
Board will continue to evaluate the $0.35 dividend rate to ensure it is sustainable, signaling potential reduction
positive_highlights: Q1 distributable earnings of $0.34/share exceeded the high end of guidance
No nonaccrual loans; weighted average risk rating improved to 2.9 from 3.1 and CECL reserve fell to 130 bps from 140 bps
Two new student housing loans closed totaling approximately $50 million at a portfolio weighted average all-in yield of 8.5%
summary: Seven Hills reported Q1 distributable earnings of $0.34 per share, exceeding the high end of guidance, driven by net earnings from loans and revenue from its one owned property, and declared a $0.35 quarterly dividend. However, Q2 DE guidance of $0.29-$0.31 per share represents a meaningful step down, as lower benchmark rates, compressed origination spreads, and an expected $145 million of Q2 repayments (loans originated at higher spreads) pressure earnings. The portfolio remains fully current with no nonaccruals, the weighted average risk rating improved to 2.9 from 3.1, and CECL reserves fell to 130 bps from 140 bps. Management explicitly flagged that the Board will continue evaluating the dividend rate to ensure it is sustainable.

negative_highlights: Gross margin expected to decrease approximately 3-4 percentage points in Q2 due to customer migration costs on upgraded platform
Net loss widened to $1.5 million from $800,000 prior year primarily driven by litigation expenses and debt extinguishment
positive_highlights: 37th consecutive quarter of record revenue
Q1 adjusted EBITDA improved by approximately $1 million year-over-year to $1.9 million
Strong pipeline building in both U.S. and EU ahead of the European Accessibility Act deadline
summary: AudioEye reported Q1 FY2025 revenue of $9.7 million (up ~34% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $1.9 million, marking the 37th consecutive quarter of record revenue. Management raised guidance for Q2 revenue to between $9.85M-$10M and reiterated full-year FY2025 revenue guidance at $41M-$42M despite a one-time gross margin impact in Q2 from platform migration costs.

negative_highlights: Total revenue fell 12% to $340.2 million from $386.7 million in 2023
Net income attributable to shareholders fell to $5.8 million ($1.30 per share) from $17.6 million ($4.46 per share)
Net cash used in operating activities was $75.7 million, and operating income fell to $3.6 million from $18.8 million
positive_highlights: Cash and cash equivalents of $45 million as of December 31, 2024, equivalent to approximately $11.11 per share
Completed a share repurchase program implemented in October 2024, leaving 4,538,358 Class A common shares outstanding
Supply chain financing services expanded into the gold industry, driving increased demand
summary: Nisun International reported FY2024 total revenue of $340.2 million, down 12% from $386.7 million in 2023, with net income attributable to shareholders falling to $5.8 million ($1.30 per share) from $17.6 million ($4.46 per share). Gross profit declined 20% to $30.9 million and operating income dropped to $3.6 million from $18.8 million, while cash and equivalents stood at $45 million ($11.11 per share) and operating cash flow was negative $75.7 million. Management gave a qualitative optimistic outlook for 2025 but did not provide specific numerical guidance, citing the KFC franchise expansion and gold-industry supply chain financing as growth drivers. The period-over-period change is a sharp contraction in both revenue and profitability versus 2023.

negative_highlights: Wholesale sales down 6.3%
Gross margin guidance pressured by tariffs
Inflationary price increases may pressure demand
positive_highlights: Record Q1 gross margin of 41.2%, 210 bps expansion
Adjusted EPS up to $0.73 vs $0.41
Retail segment sales rose 20.5%
summary: Rocky Brands reported Q1 FY2025 revenue of $114.1 million, up 1.1% year-over-year, slightly ahead of expectations, with record first-quarter gross margins of 41.2%. Adjusted EPS rose to $0.73 from $0.41 a year ago. Retail segment grew 20.5%, but wholesale declined 6.3% due to planned military reductions. Management reiterated full-year guidance despite tariff uncertainties and plans price increases in June, expecting EPS just below last year's $2.54.

negative_highlights: Operating income down 34% YoY due to member growth investments
Europe revenue up only 1%, operating margin flat at 3%
GAAP operating margin fell to 16% from 26% a year ago
positive_highlights: Revenue of $23.1 million, highest since pandemic, up 5% YoY; constant currency up 6%
Jack's Flight Club revenue up 20% YoY, premium subscribers up 13%
Expect Q2 revenue growth to double YoY, accelerating trend expected
summary: Travelzoo reported Q1 2025 revenue of $23.1 million, up 5% year-over-year, the highest quarterly revenue since the pandemic, with constant currency revenue up 6%. Operating income fell 34% to $3.7 million due to increased member acquisition investments, and non-GAAP operating profit was $4.3 million versus $6.0 million last year. Management expects Q2 revenue growth to double year-over-year and accelerate through the year as subscription fees are recognized ratably. While North America and Jack's Flight Club led growth, Europe was flat, and management acknowledged near-term EPS pressure from marketing investments.

negative_highlights: Two sizable vacancies remain unresolved: the 2.2 million square foot Hawaii land parcel (~3.6% of occupancy) and a 535,000 square foot Indianapolis property where a half-building deal fell through
Tenant decision timelines continue to lengthen, with renewals into 2026-2027 starting earlier and more parties involved
Net debt to total assets of 68.7% and net debt coverage of 11.9x keep leverage elevated, driving the disposition/refinancing evaluation
positive_highlights: Normalized FFO of $0.20 per share beat the high end of guidance by $0.02 and rose 43% year-over-year
Leasing spreads of 18.9% GAAP and 9.8% cash on 2.3 million square feet, adding $2.9 million of annualized rent
Interest expense fell $3.4 million year-over-year to $69.8 million, with Q2 expected to decline further to ~$68.5 million
summary: ILPT reported Q1 2025 normalized FFO of $13.5 million, or $0.20 per share, up nearly 43% year-over-year and 52% sequentially, exceeding the high end of guidance by $0.02 on percentage rent and a ~$750,000 Hawaii bad debt recovery. Cash basis NOI rose ~2% to $83.8 million, NOI was $87.5 million, adjusted EBITDAre $85.3 million, and occupancy rose 20 bps sequentially to 94.6% on 2.3 million square feet of leasing at GAAP/cash spreads of 18.9%/9.8%. Q2 normalized FFO guidance is $0.19-$0.21 per share, including a one-time $0.01 benefit from a lease-termination remediation payment. Management flagged elongated leasing timelines and two notable vacancies (2.2 million square foot Hawaii land parcel, 535,000 square foot Indianapolis property) while noting tariff-driven construction hesitation is aiding retention and that leverage reduction via refis or dispositions is being explored.

negative_highlights: Reinsurance net premiums written grew only 2.2% YoY, with a $147 million structured-deal nonrenewal and a cyber rate/retention headwind
California wildfires drove $547 million of catastrophe losses, producing a small underwriting loss in the Insurance segment
Management expects continued competitive pressure and rate decreases in London specialty and E&S property, and sees more casualty social inflation pain ahead
positive_highlights: Ex-cat accident-year combined ratio of 81% with all three segments improving versus Q1 2024
Insurance net premiums written up 25% YoY to $1.9 billion, with MidCorp contributing $373 million
Mortgage segment delivered $252 million of underwriting income with U.S. MI delinquency at 1.96%
summary: Arch reported Q1 2025 after-tax operating income of $587 million, or $1.54 per share, an 11.5% annualized operating ROE, with book value per share up 3.8%. Results absorbed $547 million of catastrophe losses, mostly from the California wildfires, and included $167 million of favorable prior-year development. Reinsurance net premiums written grew just 2.2% (about 6-7% adjusting for a $147 million structured-deal nonrenewal and roughly $103 million of treaty timing), while Insurance net premiums written rose 25% with $373 million from MidCorp. Management described a more competitive P&C market with pricing pressure in London specialty and E&S property, retained its 7-8 point cat load, and flagged continued capital return including $196 million of buybacks in the quarter and $100 million in April.

negative_highlights: Total revenue growth was only about 4% YoY, and the full-year guidance midpoint implies consolidated revenue in line with 2024.
Wireless revenue was roughly flat YoY and maintenance revenue declined about 2.1%; management said new maintenance is not expected to return to growth for several quarters.
Guidance was reiterated rather than raised despite Q1 outperformance, with the CFO citing macro uncertainty and a 'guarded optimism' stance.
positive_highlights: Software revenue grew 9.2% YoY to $17.8 million and professional services rose nearly 44% to $5.8 million, with managed services up more than 180% to $1.3 million.
Adjusted EBITDA rose 8.9% to $8.2 million, covering the $7.9 million returned to stockholders in the quarter.
Software backlog increased more than 15% YoY, with 22 six-figure contracts signed in Q1 including two new logos.
summary: Spok reported Q1 2025 total revenue of $36.3 million, up nearly 4% YoY, with software revenue up 9.2% to $17.8 million and wireless roughly flat at $18.5 million. GAAP net income was $5.2 million ($0.25/diluted share), up from $4.2 million ($0.21), and adjusted EBITDA rose about 9% to $8.2 million. Full-year 2025 guidance was reiterated at $134-142 million revenue and $27.5-32.5 million adjusted EBITDA, with management citing macro uncertainty and stating the Q1 outperformance does not change the midpoint outlook. Other positives include 15%+ YoY software backlog growth, 44% growth in professional services revenue, and a $1 million annualized benefit from higher disconnect fees.

negative_highlights: Total revenue down 3% YoY due to lower fuel surcharge and tonnage
LTL tonnage per day down 7.5% YoY, though outperforming the industry
Adjusted EBITDA down 3% YoY with lower fuel surcharge, tonnage, and pension income
positive_highlights: Adjusted EPS of $0.73 exceeded expectations
LTL adjusted OR improved 30 bps sequentially, better than seasonality
Yield ex-fuel accelerated to 6.9% YoY and purchase transportation costs down 53%
summary: XPO reported Q1 2025 total revenue of $2 billion, down 3% year-over-year, with adjusted EBITDA of $278 million and adjusted diluted EPS of $0.73, exceeding expectations despite a challenging freight market. LTL margins improved sequentially by 30 basis points to an adjusted operating ratio of 85.9%, with yield ex-fuel up 6.9% year-over-year and purchase transportation costs down 53%. The company lowered outsourced linehaul miles to 8.8% of total miles, a record low, and highlighted ongoing technology and AI investments aimed at further productivity gains. Management expressed confidence in continued above-market yield growth and margin expansion, while noting the uncertain macro environment and expected moderation in CapEx.

negative_highlights: Organic net sales declined 2% due to lower paper, logistics, and agency sales
Adjusted EBITDA margin contracted to 7.2%
Free cash flow was negative $100 million, worse than prior year
positive_highlights: Adjusted diluted EPS doubled to $0.20 per share
Net debt decreased by $81 million year-over-year
Growing In-Store Connect network and new client wins
summary: Quad's Q1 2025 net sales were $629 million, down 2% organically, with adjusted EBITDA down from $51 million to $46 million and margin down to 7.2%. Adjusted diluted EPS doubled to $0.20, and free cash flow was negative $100 million due to working capital timing. Management reaffirmed full-year guidance despite tariff and postal headwinds, noting limited direct tariff exposure and USPS promotional discounts for catalogers.

negative_highlights: Net interest margin fell to 8.27% from 10.0% and net interest income dropped to $14.3 million from $15.5 million
Management reiterated that NIM is expected to keep declining over time as the portfolio shifts to lower-risk, lower-yield assets
Loan originations of roughly $1.3 billion are tracking at a lower $1.2 billion quarterly rate in April
positive_highlights: Fee income increased to $7.8 million from $5.6 million in the prior quarter
NPAs declined to $29.9 million from $36.5 million, with net charge-offs falling to $2.2 million from $3.2 million
Tangible book value per common share rose to $13.42 from $13.15 sequentially, with a 22% tangible equity to assets ratio
summary: FinWise reported Q1 FY2025 net income of $3.2 million, or $0.23 per diluted share, with net interest income down to $14.3 million from $15.5 million and NIM falling to 8.27% from 10% in the prior quarter. The margin decline was attributed to seasonal softening in the three highest-yielding held-for-sale programs, repricing of variable-rate SBA loans, and the addition of roughly $40 million of lower-yielding held-for-investment loans. Fee income rose to $7.8 million from $5.6 million and NPAs fell to $29.9 million from $36.5 million, while management maintained its prior outlook for $50-$100 million of credit enhanced balances by year-end 2025 and gradual growth; no formal EPS or revenue guidance was given. Loan originations were approximately $1.3 billion with April tracking at a $1.2 billion quarterly rate, and tangible book value per share rose to $13.42 from $13.15.

negative_highlights: First quarter ROA was 66 bps, below the 1% goal
Consumer portfolio charge-offs remain high, with provision additional credit expense
Panacea consolidation reduced operating ROA by 10 bps
positive_highlights: Net interest margin up to 3.15% from 290 bps last quarter
Core community bank loan pipeline about 3 times last year; April loans up $25 million
Expect 24 bps ROA from earning assets, 15 bps from mortgage, 15 bps from tech savings
summary: Q1 FY2025 pre-tax net income was $4.5 million excluding Panacea, or $7.5 million adjusted for one-time items, equating to a 66 basis point ROA. Net interest margin improved to 3.15% from 290 basis points last quarter. Management expects to grow earning assets back to $3.75 billion, add 15 bps to ROA from mortgage growth, and reduce technology spend by 15 bps to exceed a 1% ROA goal. Panacea deconsolidation is possible with a potentially substantial gain, but not guaranteed.

negative_highlights: Q1 production trended down due to seasonal weather impacts (summer storms) and catch-up work following a strong December quarter.
Zinc off-take agreements for Merrin Mine are not yet finalized, limiting immediate revenue from that stream.
TRIFR remains 'sticky' at 7.0 despite improvements, though no reportable environmental incidents occurred.
positive_highlights: Completed debt refinance reducing net gearing to just under 20% and extending maturities to March 2028.
C1 cash costs reduced significantly to $2.47/lb, with March production dropping to $1.49/lb due to high volumes.
Merrin Mine development progressing well with independent ventilation established and significant high-grade mineralization found.
summary: MAC Copper reported Q1 FY2025 with a realized copper price of $4.04/lb and C1 cash costs of $2.47/lb, noting that the quarter was seasonally soft following a strong December. Management maintained full-year guidance for 43,000 to 48,000 tonnes of copper production and 3.8% to 4% grade, citing upcoming high-grade stopes in Q2. The company successfully refinanced its debt structure, reducing net gearing to under 20% and saving approximately $14 million annually in interest.

negative_highlights: Product gross margin contracted to 27.9% from 28.7% due to a $1.4 million deferral on China shipments.
Management expects Q4 product revenue to be negatively impacted by $10 million to $15 million due to tariffs limiting China volume.
Visibility on near-term growth is lower than just one month ago due to evolving tariff and geopolitical uncertainty.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 12% year-over-year to $113 million, with product revenue up 16% and service revenue up 9%.
Adjusted EBITDA increased significantly to $6 million from $1.1 million in the prior year quarter.
Book-to-bill ratio remained healthy at over 1.2x, indicating strong order intake relative to revenue.
summary: Accuray reported Q3 FY2025 revenue of $113 million, a 12% year-over-year increase driven by 16% growth in product revenue and 9% growth in service revenue. Adjusted EBITDA reached $6 million compared to $1.1 million last year, exceeding expectations despite a one-time margin deferral of approximately $1.4 million related to China shipments. Management maintained full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance of $28.5 million to $31 million while acknowledging potential Q4 revenue headwinds of $10 million to $15 million due to tariffs on China exports.

negative_highlights: Revenue fell to $23.3 million from $25.6 million in Q4 on lower performance-based fees
GAAP net income of $0.05 per share fell from $0.24 in Q4 and $0.27 a year ago, and non-GAAP economic EPS of $0.29 declined from $0.36 a year ago
Wealth Management had net outflows of $157 million against $56 million of gross inflows

Firm-wide AUM net inflows of $0.6 billion, partially offset by $0.3 billion of market depreciation
Two ETFs (MDST, WEEI) surpassed $100 million in combined assets, and the intermediary channel posted its best sales quarter since 2022 with $233.1 million gross sales
summary: Westwood reported Q1 2025 revenue of $23.3 million, up from $22.7 million a year ago but down from $25.6 million in Q4 on lower performance fees. GAAP net income was $0.5 million or $0.05 per share, versus $0.24 in Q4 and $0.27 a year ago; non-GAAP economic earnings were $0.29 per share versus a $0.39 loss in Q4. Firm-wide AUM/AUA totaled $18 billion, with AUM net inflows of $0.6 billion offset by $0.3 billion of market depreciation. Management cited a robust institutional pipeline exceeding $1 billion, including a ~$1 billion small-cap value sub-advisory mandate funded at quarter-end, and declared a $0.15 regular dividend; the company gave no explicit numeric guidance for the full year.

negative_highlights: Sub-servicing additions of roughly flat year-over-year due to lower subservicing additions related to the timing of bulk boardings.
Reverse servicing was up from the prior quarter but remained lower versus the prior year, primarily driven by strong asset gains in Q1 '24 and valuation adjustments on buyout loans.
positive_highlights: Adjusted pre-tax income of $25 million exceeded the full-year guidance range of 16%-18% adjusted ROE (actual annualized ROE was 22%).
Originations volume grew 53% year-over-year, significantly outpacing the industry's 8% increase.
Total servicing additions were up $17 billion versus Q1 '24, with owned MSR editions more than doubling.
summary: Onity Group reported Q1 FY2025 adjusted pre-tax income of $25 million and GAAP net income attributable to common shareholders of $21 million ($2.50 per share), exceeding full-year guidance for both metrics. The company confirmed its full year 2025 financial objectives remain unchanged, citing strong execution in originations volume (up 53% YoY) and servicing UPB growth despite a decline in subservicing additions due to timing of bulk boardings.

negative_highlights: Gross margin held at 19.8%, with total cost of revenue rising 34% year-over-year
Loss per share remained at RMB0.57 despite the improvement from RMB0.85
No explicit forward revenue or margin guidance was provided on the call
positive_highlights: Total revenue grew 30% year-over-year to RMB1.2 billion
Adjusted EBITDA loss improved to RMB105 million from RMB224 million a year earlier
Software license revenue surged 148% year-over-year to RMB187 million
summary: ECARX reported Q1 2025 total revenue of RMB1.2 billion, up 30% year-over-year, with gross profit of RMB243 million (19.8% margin) and operating loss narrowing 30% to RMB24.6 million; adjusted EBITDA loss improved to RMB105 million from RMB224 million a year earlier. Software license revenue surged 148% to RMB187 million and service revenue rose 49%, while shipments reached 684,000 units and cumulative vehicles on ECARX technology grew 35.8% to over 8.7 million. Operating expenses fell 9% year-over-year and loss per share improved to RMB0.57 from RMB0.85. Management highlighted new project wins with Geely, a Volkswagen digital cockpit sample, and a Singapore supply chain/engineering center, but did not provide explicit forward financial guidance beyond qualitative confidence.

negative_highlights: Gas Cylinders sales down 9%, margin down to 6.3% from 9%
Alternative fuel softness drove transportation sales down 23%
FX volatility noted as key sensitivity (~$1M EPS impact per $0.05 move)
positive_highlights: Sales up 8.9% to $90.5M, adjusted EPS up to $0.23
Elektron sales up 31% with 120 bps margin expansion
UGR-E demand expected to more than double in 2025; first European bulk gas module order secured
summary: Luxfer's Q1 2025 sales rose 8.9% to $90.5M, with adjusted EPS of $0.23 up from $0.20, adjusted EBITDA up 9.7% to $11.3M (12.5% margin), and operating cash flow of $5.1M. Elektron grew 31% with margin expansion, while Gas Cylinders fell 9% with margin down. Full-year guidance was reaffirmed: EPS $0.95-$1.05, EBITDA $48-$52M, and free cash flow $20-$25M. Management highlighted tariff mitigation, strong defense demand, UGR-E record backlog, and a first bulk gas transportation order, while noting FX and rare earth risks.

negative_highlights: Management suspended full-year guidance citing unpredictability from new reciprocal tariffs imposed in April, reducing visibility into near-term trends.
Gross margin expansion was driven by product mix rather than volume or pricing power as average price decreases offset some gains.
Inventory pull-forward of approximately $32 million occurred due to tariff uncertainty, impacting cash flow and working capital.
positive_highlights: Operating profit improved $3.2 million year-over-year, turning a loss from Q1 FY24 into an operating loss of only $943k for Q1 FY25.
North American consumer markets delivered solid growth led by the U.S., partially offsetting slight international declines.
HealthBeacon contributed $1.5 million in revenue and marked its third consecutive quarter of increasing patient subscriptions.
summary: First quarter revenue was $133.4 million (up 4% YoY) with operating profit improving by $3.2 million to reach a loss of only $943k compared to a prior year loss of $1.2m, driven by HealthBeacon and mix shifts. Management suspended full-year guidance due to new retaliatory tariffs in April reducing visibility into the remainder of 2025. The company is implementing price increases and accelerating sourcing diversification outside China with benefits expected to flow through starting in 2026.

negative_highlights: U.S. growth moderated over past four quarters and came in below expectations
Gross margins lower due to geographic mix
R&D expenses expected to increase with trial enrollment
positive_highlights: Worldwide sales $22.5M, up 20% YoY and 21% constant currency
International revenue grew 39% YoY, driven by China
Added 10 new U.S. accounts, ending quarter with 285 active accounts
summary: Pulmonx reported Q1 2025 worldwide sales of $22.5 million, up 20% YoY (21% constant currency), with strong international growth of 39%, but U.S. growth moderated. Management reiterated full-year revenue guidance of $96-98 million, noting that Q1 likely represents a low point for U.S. growth and expects acceleration in the back half from new initiatives. Gross margin was pressured by geographic mix, and China distributor stocking contributed to international strength.

negative_highlights: BARDA Project NextGen contract terminated via Stop Work Order in April, halting incremental spending on that specific award
Net loss increased to $5.4 million driven by R&D expenses of $5.4 million and G&A increase of $200,000
No new funding awards received from BARDA despite proposal being deemed appropriate

Encouraging interim results from CLL trial showing Pfizer arm did not meet endpoint while GeoVax study continues
cGMP production of GEO-MVA clinical batch completed with sufficient product available for upcoming evaluation
summary: GeoVax reported Q1 FY2025 revenue of $1.6 million from BARDA (up from zero in the prior year) and a net loss of approximately $5.4 million or $0.45 per share, compared to a loss of $5.9 million ($2.47 EPS) in 2024. The company disclosed that it received an unexpected Stop Work Order terminating its BARDA Project NextGen contract for convenience with less than $750,000 annual financial impact and no significant operational changes anticipated. Management remains focused on advancing GEO-CM04S1 trials in immunocompromised populations and completing cGMP production of the GEO-MVA vaccine candidate.

2025 guidance explicitly excludes any impact from the Spanish Super Scoopers, indicating uncertainty regarding their deployment timeline.
Cash balance declined to $22.3 million from $39.3 million at the end of 2024 due to winter maintenance and training activities.
positive_highlights: Record first quarter revenue of $15.6 million driven by early wildfire activity and new exclusive use contracts.
Adjusted EBITDA improved significantly to negative $5.1 million compared to negative $6.9 million in the prior year.
Secured a 5-year IDIQ contract with the Bureau of Land Management for Alaska Fire Service and an exclusive use agreement with Montana.
summary: Bridger Aerospace reported record Q1 FY2025 revenue of $15.6 million, an 184% increase year-over-year driven by early wildfire deployments and the inclusion of acquired subsidiary FMS. The company posted a net loss of $15.5 million ($0.41 diluted EPS) but improved Adjusted EBITDA to negative $5.1 million from negative $6.9 million in the prior year. Management raised 2025 guidance, projecting adjusted EBITDA growth of approximately 20% with a midpoint range of $42 million to $48 million on revenue between $105 million and $111 million.

negative_highlights: SaaS customer additions declined by 3,000 quarter-over-quarter due to holiday seasonality and a strategic shift toward expansion over new acquisition.
First quarter Marketing Services billings fell 42% YoY as the company continues converting legacy clients to SaaS.
Full-year guidance was taken with a 'cautious view' in light of recession headlines, though not materially cut.
positive_highlights: SaaS revenue beat guidance at $111.1 million with 50% YoY growth.
Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded significantly to 10% from the prior period.
Seasoned net revenue retention reached a record high of 103%.
summary: Thryv reported Q1 FY2025 SaaS revenue of $111.1 million, beating guidance with 50% year-over-year growth and a sequential increase of 7%. Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to 10%, driven by a 490 bps YoY gross margin improvement and strong subscriber growth of 37% to 111,000 total subscribers. Management raised full-year SaaS revenue guidance to $460.5M-$471M and confirmed Marketing Services EBITDA guidance, citing a conservative outlook due to macro uncertainty despite delivering a top-line beat.

negative_highlights: Revenue of $217.9 million was only in line with the prior quarter and expectations, with commercial vehicle and off-highway volumes lower
Full-year guidance was only maintained, not raised, despite Q1 outperformance, citing tariff-driven uncertainty and recently lowered third-party production forecasts
Net debt to trailing-twelve-month EBITDA remained just under 4x, well above the 2-2.5x year-end target
positive_highlights: Adjusted gross margin expanded 210 bps and adjusted operating margin 160 bps versus Q4, with operating income improving in all three segments
summary: Stoneridge reported Q1 FY2025 sales of $217.9 million, roughly in line with the prior quarter and expectations, with adjusted EBITDA of $7.6 million (3.5% of sales) up about $1.6 million or 80 bps QoQ and above prior expectations. Adjusted gross margin expanded 210 bps and adjusted operating margin 160 bps versus Q4, with operating income improving in every segment; free cash flow was $4.9 million, up $1.5 million YoY on a $28 million inventory reduction. MirrorEye set a record at +24% QoQ and SMART 2 posted a second consecutive record. Management maintained full-year guidance, expecting Q2 slightly above Q1 and EBITDA slightly back-half weighted, while flagging tariff uncertainty and reduced third-party production forecasts offset by originally conservative assumptions.

negative_highlights: North American Mining operating profit fell to $2.0M from $2.4M on reduced customer demand and higher operating expenses
Coal segment 2025 operating profit guided to a modest year-over-year decrease due to a lower contractually determined per-ton sales price at Mississippi Lignite
Pension plan termination anticipated to produce a significant non-cash settlement charge and a substantial decrease in 2025 reported net income
positive_highlights: Coal mining segment swung to $3.8M operating profit and $5.8M adjusted EBITDA from an operating loss of $0.4M and $1.8M EBITDA a year ago
Adjusted EBITDA rose to $12.8M from $11.2M and net income per share to $0.66 from $0.61
Mitigation Resources posted a second consecutive profitable quarter and is expected to be profitable for the full year
summary: NACCO reported Q1 2025 operating profit of $7.7M versus $4.8M a year ago, net income of $4.9M or $0.66 per share versus $4.6M or $0.61, and adjusted EBITDA of $12.8M versus $11.2M. The gain was driven by the coal mining segment, whose adjusted EBITDA more than tripled to $5.8M on higher Falkirk pricing and restored demand at Mississippi Lignite; North American Mining operating profit fell to $2.0M from $2.4M. Full-year guidance calls for a moderate increase in consolidated operating profit, with coal segment operating profit expected to decline modestly on lower contracted per-ton pricing at Mississippi Lignite. A pension plan termination will trigger a non-cash settlement charge and a substantial decrease in reported 2025 net income, with net income excluding the charge down moderately from 2024.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA margin contracted to 21% from 22% prior year, and GAAP net loss widened to $2.4 million from $308,000
Q2 revenue guidance of $30-32 million is below Q1's $34.9 million, implying a sequential decline
HR compliance remains depressed from the ERTC-related attachment activity in 2023, with improvement only expected in the back half
positive_highlights: Contracted revenue backlog rose 339% YoY to $82 million, with roughly $31 million expected to convert this year
New bookings increased 45% versus the prior year first quarter
Recurring revenue grew 10% to $33.2 million and reached 95% of total revenue, with non-ERTC revenue up 13%
summary: Asure reported Q1 FY2025 revenue of $34.9 million, up 10% YoY (up 13% excluding ERTC, which dragged 300 bps), with recurring revenue of $33.2 million at 95% of total. Adjusted EBITDA rose to $7.3 million from $6.8 million, but margin compressed to 21% from 22%, and GAAP net loss widened to $2.4 million from $308,000. Full-year 2025 guidance was reiterated at $134-138 million revenue and 23-24% adjusted EBITDA margin, while Q2 guidance of $30-32 million revenue and $5-6 million adjusted EBITDA implies a sequential step-down. Bookings rose 45% and contracted backlog reached $82 million, up 339%, though HR compliance remains depressed from the ERTC wind-down with recovery expected in H2.

negative_highlights: Provision for credit loss rose to $22 million from $17.2 million a year ago, including a $3.1 million allowance build on commercial loans tied to tariffs and economic uncertainty
Operating expenses increased to $20.8 million from $18.2 million YoY, with legal costs up $700,000 and technology costs expected to remain elevated
Recreation portfolio net charge-offs were $16.4 million, or 4.67% of the average portfolio, indicating continued credit stress
positive_highlights: Net income of $12 million, or $0.50 EPS, driven by a $9.4 million gain from a commercial equity investment exit
Net interest income grew 7% YoY to $51.4 million, and net interest margin expanded 10 bps sequentially to 7.94%
Quarterly dividend increased 9% to $0.12 per share, the third increase since reinstatement
summary: MFIN reported Q1 FY2025 net income of $12 million, or $0.50 EPS, with net interest income of $51.4 million (up 7% YoY and flat QoQ). The quarter included a $9.4 million gain from a commercial equity investment exit and a $1.7 million net benefit from taxi medallion recoveries, partially offset by a $22 million provision and elevated operating expenses of $20.8 million. Management characterized the results as a strong start to the year and noted that excluding non-recurring items, EPS would be around $0.35; the company also raised its quarterly dividend 9% to $0.12 per share. Guidance for full-year loan growth was set at 5-7%, and management expects one or two more commercial equity gains this year, though timing is uncertain.

negative_highlights: Same-store sales declined 2% for the quarter, driven by softer new boat sales on the West Coast.
Gross profit declined from $120 million in Q2 FY24 to $110 million due to lower margins and model mix shifts.
SG&A expenses increased 50 basis points as a percentage of revenue (to 18%) because cost savings were offset by inflationary pressures on boat shows.
positive_highlights: Adjusted net loss narrowed significantly from a prior year loss of $5 million ($0.27/share) to just $375,000 ($0.02/share).
Pre-owned boat sales increased 14% to $90 million driven by higher volumes and trade-ins.
Inventory reduction is tracking ahead of schedule with a target to end the year down 10% to 15%, exceeding initial full-year goals.
summary: Fiscal second quarter revenue decreased 1% to $484 million and adjusted EPS fell from $0.67 to $0.13 due to lower gross margins on exited brands and a challenging pricing environment. Management updated its fiscal 2025 guidance downward, forecasting total sales between $1.7 billion and $1.8 billion (downside risk) and adjusting EBITDA expectations to the range of $65 million to $95 million amidst tariff concerns and macroeconomic uncertainty.

negative_highlights: EAD swung to a loss of $0.86 per share from earnings of $0.48 per share in Q4 2024
GAAP net loss of $5.9 million or $0.80 per share, with book value per share down to $28.50 from $28.87
Recourse debt leverage ratio rose to 2.9x from 1.1x after liquidating the two CRE securitizations
positive_highlights: Loan portfolio credit quality held with weighted average risk rating of 2.9 and loans rated 4 or 5 falling to 11 from 12
Closed a new $940 million JPMorgan financing facility with a 2-year reinvestment period
Repurchased 220,000 shares for $4.4 million at an approximate 30% discount to book value
summary: ACRES reported a Q1 2025 GAAP net loss of $5.9 million, or $0.80 per diluted share, and an EAD loss of $0.86 per share versus EAD of $0.48 in Q4 2024, driven by loan payoffs, SOFR declines, $1.5 million of accelerated debt issuance costs, a $0.10 realized loss on a hotel loan sale, and seasonal REO losses. Book value fell to $28.50 per share from $28.87, while the loan portfolio declined $109.6 million net to $1.4 billion after $115.9 million of payoffs and $31.7 million of loan sales. Management guided to Q1 as a trough, reiterating expectations for $300-500 million of net portfolio growth by year-end and a second-half securitization ramp, and repurchased 220,000 shares for $4.4 million at roughly a 30% discount to book.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined 2.4% year-over-year to $104.2 million and annualized recurring revenue fell 4.7% to $396.2 million
Revenue retention rate for service subscriptions was 88%, with management flagging renewal risk under cost and cash pressure
Guidance remains suspended pending clarity on Oracle litigation, and PeopleSoft revenue continues to decline ahead of the planned wind-down
positive_highlights: Billings rose 7.2% year-over-year to $79.4 million, or 11.3% excluding PeopleSoft-associated billings
Non-GAAP operating income improved to $14.5 million (13.9% of revenue) from 8.3% of revenue a year earlier, and gross margin expanded to 61.0% from 59.8%
Deferred revenue increased to $256.4 million from $254.3 million a year earlier and operating cash flow rose to $33.7 million from $11.1 million
summary: Revenue fell 2.4% year-over-year to $104.2 million and annualized recurring revenue declined 4.7% to $396.2 million, while gross margin improved to 61% from 59.8% and non-GAAP operating income rose to $14.5 million (13.9% of revenue) from 8.3%. Billings grew 7.2% year-over-year to $79.4 million (up 11.3% excluding PeopleSoft), and non-GAAP EPS was $0.09 versus $0.08. Guidance remains suspended due to ongoing Oracle litigation, and the company confirmed it will continue winding down PeopleSoft support, with PeopleSoft revenue declining to roughly $7.0 million from $8.2 million. Deferred revenue rose year-over-year to $256.4 million while backlog dipped slightly to $553.1 million.

negative_highlights: DynaEnergetics sales down 16% year-over-year
NobelClad backlog down to $41 million from $49 million
Guidance implies lower Q2 EBITDA and sales, citing tariffs and demand disruption
positive_highlights: Consolidated sales up 5% sequentially to $159.3 million
Adjusted EBITDA attributable to DMC up 39% sequentially to $14.4 million
Arcadia adjusted EBITDA margin improved to 14.2% from 9.5% in prior year
summary: DMC Global reported Q1 FY2025 consolidated sales of $159.3 million, up 5% sequentially, and adjusted EBITDA attributable to DMC of $14.4 million, up 39% sequentially. Arcadia sales grew 9% sequentially and 6% year-over-year to $65.6 million, while DynaEnergetics sales were flat sequentially but down 16% year-over-year due to pricing adjustments. NobelClad sales were flat sequentially but up 5% year-over-year, with backlog down to $41 million from $49 million. The company guided Q2 sales to $149-157 million and adjusted EBITDA to $10-13 million, citing tariff uncertainty, lower residential demand, and softer energy markets. Management expressed cautious optimism around operational improvements but noted significant external headwinds.

negative_highlights: Comparable store sales declined 4.8% due to winter storms, inflation concerns, and high interest rates.
President's Day sales were disappointing, down roughly 10% over the two-week period.
Management reduced CapEx guidance by approximately $3 million due to tariff uncertainty affecting expansion plans.
positive_highlights: Gross margins expanded 90 bps to 61.2% driven by product selection and merchandise mix.
Operating margin improved significantly to 2.9% from 1.7% in the prior year quarter.
New store openings and inventory buildup strategies are proceeding as planned despite macro headwinds.
summary: Havertys reported Q1 FY2025 net sales of $181.6 million, a 1.3% decrease year-over-year, with comparable store sales down 4.8%. Gross margins expanded 90 basis points to 61.2%, driven by merchandise mix, while operating margin improved to 2.9% from 1.7%. Management provided full-year guidance assuming current tariffs are in effect, projecting gross margins between 60% and 60.5% and reducing CapEx expectations due to tariff uncertainty.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined 17.3% YoY driven by a 17.9% drop in cases.
Same-store revenue fell approximately 24%, with management expecting continued pressure through the year before returning to growth at year-end.
Customer acquisition cost increased to $3,130 per case due to lower volume and reduced marketing spend.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA improved by $1.9 million sequentially versus Q4 2024 due to cost discipline and workforce reductions.
Lead volume growth over Q1 last year driven by reallocated marketing spend, expanding the pipeline without increasing total ad spend.
Average revenue per case remained stable between $12,000 and $13,000 despite a challenging macro environment.
summary: AirSculpt reported Q1 FY2025 revenue of $39.4 million (down 17.3% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $3.8 million (margin 9.5%), missing the prior year's performance due to lower case volume despite a slight increase in average revenue per case ($12,799). Management provided fiscal 2025 guidance for revenue between $160M-$170M and adjusted EBITDA of $16M-$18M, maintaining the prior outlook without raising it. While management noted sequential improvement in lead generation and same-store sales trends since February, they explicitly stated that Q4-like softness is expected to persist through most of 2025.

negative_highlights: Dividend of $0.50 per share was only 0.9x covered by cash available for distribution of $0.45.
A credit loss provision rose, split about 50-50 between a CECL scenario update and a specific private preferred reserve.
Cash available for distribution fell to $0.45 per share from $0.60 a year earlier, and Q2 EAD guidance midpoint of $0.43 is below the $0.50 dividend.
positive_highlights: Net income swung to $0.70 per diluted share from a $0.83 loss a year earlier, driven by a $23.6 million increase in interest income.
Book value per share increased 1.47% to $17.22, helped by unrealized gains on preferred stock investments.
Alewife life science sponsor is negotiating leases on two-thirds of the project that would produce a roughly 10-11% debt yield across two tenants.
summary: NREF reported Q1 2025 net income of $0.70 per diluted share versus a net loss of $0.83 a year earlier, with earnings available for distribution of $0.41 per share and cash available for distribution of $0.45 per share. Q2 guidance was set at EAD of $0.43 (range $0.38-$0.48) and CAD of $0.48 (range $0.43-$0.53). Book value per share rose 1.47% to $17.22, and the $0.50 quarterly dividend was only 0.9x covered by CAD. Management flagged a CECL reserve increase split roughly 50-50 between a scenario update and a specific private preferred, while citing life science leasing delays and optimism on residential.

negative_highlights: Portfolio yield decreased 23 bps quarter-over-quarter due to high cash interest received on non-performing loans in Q4.
CEO noted that a meaningful volume boost would likely require rates to drop significantly, which is not currently expected.
positive_highlights: Record quarterly production of $640 million, a 69% increase versus the prior year.
Net revenue increased 27% and core pretax earnings rose 17% year-over-year.
Successfully completed four debt transactions in Q1 and issued three new securitizations.
summary: Velocity Financial reported Q1 FY2025 net revenue up 27% and core pretax earnings up 17% YoY, driven by record loan production of $640 million (up 69% YoY). The company raised its full-year outlook, citing strong momentum and a sustainable run rate for the remainder of 2025. Management highlighted healthy demand across property types, robust margins, and active capital markets execution including four successful debt transactions.

negative_highlights: Net loss of $6.0 million ($0.07/share) and adjusted net loss of $2.4 million ($0.03/share) means the company remains unprofitable on both bases
Management flagged continued elevated mortgage rates, low housing inventory and soft transaction volume as persisting headwinds
Cash investments declined $8.7 million in the quarter, continuing the seasonal first-quarter cash drain despite the improvement versus last year
positive_highlights: Revenue rose 27% YoY to $253.4 million, the strongest first quarter since 2022
Adjusted EBITDA turned positive at $1.1 million from a $17.6 million loss in Q1 2024
Development Marketing revenue grew 222% YoY to $21.1 million, with a $28.3 billion active pipeline and $4.2 billion more coming to market through June 2026
summary: Douglas Elliman reported Q1 2025 revenue of $253.4 million, up 27% YoY from $200.2 million and its strongest first quarter since 2022, driven by NYC existing home sales (+$17M, +34%) and Development Marketing (+$14.6M, +222%). The net loss narrowed to $6.0 million ($0.07/share) from $41.5 million ($0.50/share), and adjusted EBITDA turned positive at $1.1 million versus a $17.6 million loss a year ago. No formal revenue or EPS guidance was issued; management cited elevated mortgage rates and low inventory as persistent headwinds while noting April daily cash receipts up about 4% YoY and an active Development Marketing pipeline of roughly $28.3 billion in gross transaction value.

negative_highlights: 30-89 day past due loans rose $3.8 million to $10 million, or 0.93% of gross loans, partly from $2.2 million of SBA-guaranteed commercial loans
Noninterest income fell $13,000 QoQ and $42,000 YoY, with fees and service charges down $322,000
Management cited customer caution and tariff uncertainty with no quantified impact yet
positive_highlights: Diluted EPS of $0.81 increased 69% versus the prior-year quarter
Tax-equivalent net interest margin expanded 25 bps to 3.76% on lower deposit and borrowing costs
No provision for credit losses this quarter versus $1.5 million in Q4 2024, with net charge-offs of just $23,000
summary: Landmark reported Q1 2025 net income of $4.7 million versus $2.8 million a year ago and $3.3 million in Q4 2024, with diluted EPS of $0.81, up 69% YoY. Net interest income rose 5.8% QoQ to $13.1 million and the tax-equivalent net interest margin expanded 25 bps to 3.76%, helped by lower funding costs and no provision for credit losses versus $1.5 million in Q4. Gross loans grew $22.6 million (8.7% annualized) to a record $1.075 billion and deposits rose $7.1 million, with noninterest expense down $1.1 million QoQ and a $0.21 dividend declared. Credit metrics stayed solid, though 30-89 day past due loans rose $3.8 million to $10 million (0.93% of gross loans), and management flagged tariff-related customer uncertainty.

negative_highlights: Revenue was negatively impacted by engineering delays that pushed approximately $1.5 million of shipments out of the quarter.
Gross margin contracted 230 basis points year-over-year to 41.5% due to lower fixed cost absorption and unfavorable mix.
Management explicitly lowered Q2 guidance citing slowing receipt of orders and customer shipment delays driven by tariff uncertainty.
positive_highlights: First quarter orders increased 11% year-over-year, with industrial demand surging 47% and auto/EV demand up 25%.
The company generated $5.5 million in cash from operations and repaid approximately $3.2 million of debt to strengthen the balance sheet.
New products represented sales of $4.5 million, or approximately 17% of total revenue, supporting innovation strategy.
summary: InTest reported Q1 FY2025 revenue of $26.6 million, down $3.2 million year-over-year and $10 million sequentially, driven by a $6 million decline in semi-conductor sales and delays pushing $1.5 million of shipments into the second quarter. Gross margins tightened 230 basis points to 41.5% due to lower fixed cost absorption and unfavorable mix, resulting in an adjusted net loss of $0.11 per diluted share. Management lowered Q2 revenue guidance to a range of $27-29 million (down from prior expectations) citing tariff uncertainty and customer shipment delays.

negative_highlights: Net loss of $22 million, or $0.33 per share, compared to net income of $17 million, or $0.25 per share, in Q4
EBITDA declined to $47 million from $99 million in Q4, primarily due to maintenance downtime and weaker U.S. dollar
Mass timber order file at $24 million with expected weaker Q2 and Q3, and project start dates slipping from 2025 into 2026 due to high interest rates
positive_highlights: EBITDA of $47 million despite 22 days of planned maintenance at Selgar, which negatively impacted EBITDA by about $30 million
Pulp sales volumes increased by 26,000 tons to 478,000 tons in Q1, and lumber production rose 12% to a near-record 128 million board feet
Launched company-wide program targeting $100 million in cost savings and operational efficiency by end-2026, with $40-$50 million expected in 2025
summary: Q1 FY2025 EBITDA fell to $47 million from $99 million in Q4, driven by 22 days of planned maintenance at the Selgar mill (about $30 million EBITDA impact) and a weaker U.S. dollar. The company reported a net loss of $22 million, or $0.33 per share, versus net income of $17 million, or $0.25 per share, in Q4, with pulp sales volumes up 26,000 tons to 478,000 tons and lumber production up 12% to 128 million board feet. Management launched a company-wide $100 million cost-savings program by end-2026, targets $20 million inventory reduction and $20 million CapEx reduction in 2025, and expects Q2 pulp and lumber prices to be positive versus Q1 but mass timber to be weaker in Q2 and Q3. Key changes versus prior period include negative EBITDA impact from tariffs uncertainty, softer Chinese demand, and increased planned maintenance days for 2025 (79 vs. 57 in 2024).

negative_highlights: Consolidated net sales declined 2% year-over-year primarily due to lower volumes in Asia and foreign currency impacts.
Gross margin in Americas Segment contracted by 350 basis points driven by inflationary pressures and transition costs.
Asia Segment saw a 12% decline in net sales and 150 bps gross margin contraction amid macroeconomic pressure.
positive_highlights: Americas Segment net sales increased by 3% year-over-year driven by Beyond Apparel initiatives and Central America recovery.
Reached agreement to note Madison facility for $53.2 million, expected to close May 15th to reduce debt and retire obligations.
REPREVE represented 31% of total sales with strong brand visibility from partners like Nike, Target, and Walmart.
summary: Consolidated net sales were $146.6 million, down 2% year-over-year due to lower volumes and unfavorable mix in Asia offset by Americas growth. Gross margins contracted significantly across the board: -350 bps in Americas (transition costs) and -150 bps in Asia (macro/pricing). Management reiterated that Q4 results will improve sequentially but warned of potential 10-15% revenue downturns in Asia due to tariffs.

negative_highlights: Net loss of $19 million in Q1 2025
Adjusted EBITDA down from $95 million in Q1 2024
positive_highlights: Production up 45% YoY and 14% QoQ to 46,619 BOE/d
Ecuador wells Iguana B1/B2 averaged 1,684 bbl/d over 30 days
Simonette wells exceed budget type curves by 80%
summary: Gran Tierra reported Q1 2025 production of 46,619 BOE/d, up 45% YoY and 14% QoQ, with a net loss of $19 million (improved from $34 million loss in Q4) and adjusted EBITDA of $85 million. Capex was $95 million, funded by a heavy capital program, and the company reduced gross debt by $27 million, repurchased shares, and added a new $75 million Colombia facility. Management highlighted record drilling times, strong Ecuador discoveries, and improved Canadian well performance, while maintaining full-year production guidance of 47-53 MBoe/d.

negative_highlights: U.S. Domestic revenue declined 9.5% due to the conclusion of Emergency Connectivity Fund and Affordable Care Program subsidies.
Operating income decreased to $2.7 million, impacted by transaction-related expenses and restructuring costs.
Net loss widened slightly to $8.9 million compared to a prior year net loss of $6.3 million.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA grew 2% to $44.3 million despite lower top-line revenue.
Cash from operations increased significantly by 55% year-over-year to $35.9 million.
International segment adjusted EBITDA rose 10.6% YoY as the business stabilizes.
summary: ATN International reported Q1 FY2025 revenue of $179.3 million, down 4% year-over-year due to the wind-down of government subsidy programs in the U.S., while adjusted EBITDA grew by 2% to $44.3 million driven by international segment performance and cash from operations increasing 55%. Management reaffirmed its full-year 2025 guidance, expecting revenue flat with last year (excluding construction) and essentially flat adjusted EBITDA, citing ongoing U.S. transition costs but steady progress in international markets.

negative_highlights: Full-year guidance withheld due to tariff uncertainty; China represented 66% of cost of goods sold as of fiscal year-end
Q1 FY2025 outlook calls for sales down approximately 5% and adjusted operating margin down about 500 bps year over year
Direct-to-consumer net sales fell 8.1% with softer store traffic and planned closures, remodels and relocations
positive_highlights: Gross margin expanded 470 bps to 50.1%, driven by 320 bps from lower promotional activity and 210 bps from lower product and freight costs
