Transformation plan delivered over $10 million in savings in fiscal 2024 and full-price customer count grew double digits in Q4
summary: Vince reported Q4 FY2024 net sales up 6.2% to $80 million (about 9% excluding the prior-year 53rd week), with wholesale up 26.7% offsetting an 8.1% decline in direct-to-consumer. Gross margin expanded 470 bps to 50.1% and adjusted operating income was $2.5 million, though GAAP results included a $32 million noncash goodwill impairment from the P180 ownership change, producing a net loss of $28.3 million or $2.24 per share. Management declined to provide full-year guidance due to tariff uncertainty, noting China was 66% of COGS, and guided Q1 FY2025 sales down about 5% with adjusted operating margin down approximately 500 bps year over year.

Withdrew 2025 guidance due to tariff and macro uncertainty; tariff impact estimated at $130M-$175M
HDMC operating income declined 51% on lower volume and higher fixed costs per unit

Q1 bottom line better than expected, with operating margin at 12.1% despite environmental pressures

Retail sales down 21% globally and 24% in North America. Management withdrew full-year 2025 guidance due to tariff and macro uncertainty, citing a potential $130M-$175M tariff impact. They remain committed to reducing dealer inventory by ~10% year-end and expect productivity savings of $100M in 2025. LiveWire reduced its full-year operating loss guidance to ~$59M from $70-80M.

Diving business still very challenged
Tariffs will impact business despite U.S. manufacturing

Inventory down $69 million year-over-year

Gross margin improved slightly to 35% due to cost savings, despite marketplace discounting. Operating expenses decreased $7.7 million year-over-year. Inventory was down $69 million to $180 million. New products in fishing and camping are exceeding expectations, but overall demand remains soft and tariffs are expected to impact the business.

positive_highlights: Net interest income grew 18% YoY and over 2% QoQ to $10.1 million, with interest income up 30% YoY

summary: AOMR reported Q1 2025 GAAP net income of $20.5 million, or $0.87 per diluted share, driven largely by $18.7 million of unrealized gains on the loan portfolios; distributable earnings were $4.1 million, or $0.17 per share. Net interest income of $10.1 million grew 18% YoY and over 2% QoQ, while operating expenses ex securitization and stock comp fell 29% YoY to $2.8 million. GAAP book value rose 5.2% to $10.70 per share and economic book value rose 2.4% to $13.41, and the $0.32 dividend was maintained. No securitization closed in Q1, but AOMT 2025-4 closed shortly after quarter end (AAA at 180bps, ~13-17% yield vs the usual 15-20%), and management guided to similar opex ahead with book value roughly flat quarter-to-date.

Successful debt refinancing with Perceptive Advisors extending maturity to April 2030 and providing up to $50M in additional capacity.
Secured positive medical policy with TRICARE after a two-year review process, validating clinical evidence for active duty service members.
summary: Exagen reported record Q1 FY2025 revenue of $15.5 million, an 8% year-over-year increase driven by new biomarker launches and volume growth of 6% sequentially. The company achieved a gross margin of 58.9%, slightly down from the prior year due to transitory headwinds including partial quarter recognition of new markers and upfront lab investments, but expects steady expansion into the low 60s in H2. Management reaffirmed full-year 2025 revenue guidance of at least $65 million and raised expectations for adjusted EBITDA positivity by Q4.

positive_highlights: Free cash flow usage fell to $5.6M from $8.6M in Q1 last year; excluding $2.1M of severance paid, usage was $3.5M

summary: Total revenue fell 6% YoY to $9.4M from $9.9M, with subscription revenue down 8% to $5.3M (57% of total) versus $5.8M, and service revenue down 3% to $4.1M. Ending ARR was $20M versus $23.9M a year ago; excluding the lapsed $5.8M commercial contract, ARR grew $1.9M or 11%. GAAP net loss per share was $0.55 versus $0.50, and non-GAAP loss per share was $0.40 versus $0.27, though excluding $3.2M one-time severance both would have shown improvement at $0.40 and $0.25. Free cash flow usage improved to $5.6M from $8.6M, management said Q1 was above internal plan and still targets free cash flow positivity by Q4, but flagged higher Q2 cash usage from an external matter costing upwards of $0.5M per month plus continued churn into Q2.

negative_highlights: Net sales declined approximately 3% YoY to $55.5M amid soft discretionary spending and declining consumer sentiment.
Tariffs began impacting imported goods late in Q1, creating a little over 100 bps cost headwind with ongoing exposure tied to China sourcing.
No formal forward guidance was provided; management cited high uncertainty, changing consumer behavior, and evolving trade environment.
positive_highlights: Gross margin expanded 161 bps to 26.7% despite a ~100 bps tariff headwind, reflecting facility consolidation and cost rationalization.
EBITDA increased to $4.9M from $4.4M and operating cash flow jumped to $3.8M from $7,000 a year earlier.
Debt reduced by $1.8M in the quarter and nearly $30M over 12 months, with net leverage at 0.8x and cost of debt at 2.97%; also paid $2.1M dividend and repurchased $1.4M of shares.
summary: Escalade reported Q1 FY2025 net sales of $55.5M, down ~3% YoY, with net income of $2.6M or $0.19 per diluted share. Gross margin expanded 161 bps to 26.7% from 25.0%, driven by facility consolidation and cost rationalization, though tariffs were a ~100 bps headwind in the quarter. SG&A fell 1.2% to $10.6M and EBITDA rose to $4.9M from $4.4M; operating cash flow was $3.8M versus $7,000 prior year. The company issued no formal forward guidance, citing soft consumer sentiment and trade uncertainty, while outlining tariff-mitigation levers including sourcing shifts and surgical pricing.

negative_highlights: SHOP NOI was favorably impacted by $2.7 million of business interruption proceeds that management said should be stripped out from a run-rate basis.
Same-property MOB/life science occupancy was 90.1%, down 10 bps sequentially, with a 233,000 square foot known vacate in St. Louis.
Management guided to SHOP operating expenses increasing above 3% for 2025 versus 2024, higher than the roughly flat sequential expense trend in Q1.
positive_highlights: SHOP same-property NOI increased 42.1% year-over-year to $38.4 million with 320 bps of margin expansion to 11.2%.
Adjusted EBITDAre rose 17% year-over-year to $75.1 million and normalized FFO of $0.06 per share exceeded consensus.
Net debt to adjusted EBITDAre declined significantly to 8.8x from 11.2x at year-end following $321 million of property sales and refinancing activity.
summary: DHC reported Q1 FY2025 total revenues of $386.9 million (up 4% YoY), adjusted EBITDAre of $75.1 million (up 17% YoY), and normalized FFO of $14.3 million or $0.06 per share, which exceeded analyst consensus. Same-property cash-basis NOI rose 20.7% YoY to $71.5 million, driven by SHOP NOI up 42.1% YoY to $38.4 million, occupancy up 130 bps to 80.2%, and margin expansion of 320 bps. Management reaffirmed 2025 SHOP NOI guidance of $120-$135 million, noting a bias toward the high end and potential to raise guidance in Q2, while citing $2.7 million of business interruption proceeds and disposition timing as reasons for not raising now. The company also made progress on debt maturities, including $321 million of Q1 property sales and April/May paydowns of the 2025 and 2026 notes, reducing net debt/adjusted EBITDAre from 11.2x to 8.8x.

negative_highlights: Tariff exposure estimated at up to 2-2.5% of COGS in near term, pressuring gross margins
Q4 gross margin not expected to accelerate due to tariff and software mix
International revenue down 5% year-over-year on tough APAC comp
positive_highlights: Record adjusted EBITDA of $14.9 million, second consecutive quarterly record
Non-GAAP EPS up 13% year-over-year to $0.88
Initial sales of ProVision Plus software to Pasolink customers
summary: Aviat Networks reported Q3 FY2025 revenue of $112.6 million, up 1.6% year-over-year, with record adjusted EBITDA of $14.9 million (up 17% YoY) and non-GAAP EPS of $0.88 (up 13% YoY). Gross margins improved to 35.8% non-GAAP, driven by software and regional mix, but management expects Q4 margins to be pressured by tariffs and a softer software quarter. The company reiterated full-year guidance within the $430-$470 million range and expects to approximate consensus revenue and EBITDA, citing tariff uncertainty and a cautious Q4 outlook.

negative_highlights: Adjusted net loss of $25 million, though improved from $38 million YoY
Servicing fee income fell from $124 million to $104 million due to 2024 bulk sales
Total expenses increased 4% YoY
positive_highlights: Pull-through weighted lock volume up 15% YoY to $5.4 billion
Gain on sale margin of 355 bps exceeded guidance of 320-340 bps
Unit share market gain expanded from 145 to 187 basis points
summary: In Q1 FY2025, loanDepot reported pull-through weighted rate lock volume of $5.4 billion, up 15% year-over-year and within guidance, while adjusted revenue rose to $278 million from $231 million. Gain on sale margin came in above guidance at 355 basis points, and adjusted net loss narrowed to $25 million from $38 million. For Q2, the company guided lock volume of $5.5-8.0 billion and gain on sale margin of 300-350 basis points, noting seasonal strength offset by market volatility. CEO transition to founder Anthony Hsieh is underway.

GREW revenue fell 40% to $4.3 million from the commercial solar pivot and segment operating loss widened to $900,000 from $600,000
Full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance of $40-50 million was only confirmed, not raised, despite the strong quarter

Consolidated adjusted EBITDA increased 22.7% to $14.4 million and income from operations rose 30.3% to $12.8 million
Diversegy generated over $400,000 adjusted EBITDA versus being EBITDA negative a year ago, with record REPs up 55% YoY
summary: Genie Energy reported Q1 FY2025 consolidated revenue of $136.8 million, up 14.3% YoY, driven by a 17.8% increase in GRE revenue to $132.5 million as meters served grew by over 48,000 net to approximately 413,000. Adjusted EBITDA rose 22.7% to $14.4 million and consolidated income from operations rose 30.3% to $12.8 million, while gross margin contracted 90 bps to 27.3% on lower-margin municipal aggregation meter acquisitions. GREW revenue fell 40% to $4.3 million due to the pivot away from the commercial solar projects market and the segment loss widened to $900,000. Management confirmed full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance of $40-50 million and returned $3.9 million to shareholders via dividend and buybacks.

negative_highlights: Book value estimated down approximately 3% through April due to market volatility in early spring
Securitization spreads widened significantly, requiring a wider spread on retained securities (estimated 50-75 bps)
Existing home sales remain historically low and supply of newly constructed homes is narrowing
positive_highlights: Book value remained stable at $10.65 per share despite macro volatility
Quarterly dividend increased to $0.20, representing a 5.3% increase from the prior quarter
Arc Home achieved breakeven earnings with lock volumes increasing 50% year-over-year
summary: MITT reported Q1 FY2025 GAAP EPS of $0.21 per share and increased its quarterly dividend by 5.3% to $0.20 per share. Book value remained stable at $10.65, rising slightly despite an estimated 3% decline through April due to market volatility in early spring. Management noted that securitization spreads widened significantly (estimated 50-75 bps) and markets closed briefly before reopening by late April.

James River reported Q1 2025 net income from continuing operations of $9.0M, or $0.18 per diluted share, and adjusted net operating income of $0.19 per share, with an 11.5% annualized operating return on tangible common equity and tangible book value per share up 6.6% to $7.11. The consolidated combined ratio was 99.5% on a 66.8% loss ratio, with no catastrophe or net prior-year development; E&S produced a 91.5% combined ratio and $11.7M of underwriting income, while Specialty Admitted ran a 102.1% combined ratio and a small underwriting loss as fronting premiums fell 21%. E&S renewal rates rose 7.8% and submissions hit a record 91,000, but average premium per policy fell 8.4% and gross premium was roughly flat, with March written premium up over 9%. Management guided to a full-year 2025 expense ratio near last year's 31% (32.7% in Q1) and cited $3M-$6M of annual expense savings plus a $10M-$13M one-time benefit from the planned Bermuda-to-US redomiciliation later this year.

Net loss widened to $5.9 million ($0.35 per share) from $3.8 million ($0.22 per share), and adjusted EBITDA loss widened to $3.0 million from $1.7 million
Cash and cash equivalents of $1.8 million with active pursuit of financing to restore Nasdaq compliance
positive_highlights: note-side revenue grew 6% YoY to $6.1 million, aided by $1.2 million from customers in new verticals

summary: Q1 2025 consolidated revenue was $8.2 million, down from $22.3 million in Q1 2024, driven by watch-side revenue collapsing to $2.0 million from $16.5 million following the May 2024 Colossus SSP disruption; watch-side revenue rose 6% to $6.1 million. Gross margin expanded to 29% from 22% on mix, but gross profit fell to $2.4 million from $5.0 million, operating loss widened to $3.9 million, net loss was $5.9 million ($0.35 per share), and adjusted EBITDA loss widened to $3.0 million from $1.7 million. Operating expenses were cut 19% ($1.5 million) via a 20% staff reduction, and management maintained full-year 2025 revenue guidance of $90 million-$110 million, expecting the second half to deliver strong gains as direct DSP integrations come online. Cash was $1.8 million versus $1.4 million at year-end 2024.

negative_highlights: GAAP net loss applicable to common stockholders was $9.3 million ($0.29 per share).
Book value per common share decreased by approximately 6% from the prior quarter end.
Earnings available for distribution (EAD) are expected to trend lower moving forward due to the maturation of a large interest rate hedge.
positive_highlights: Operating expenses declined quarter-over-quarter following the elimination of the management fee upon internalization.
The company ended Q1 with $47 million of unrestricted cash on its balance sheet, maintaining a solid liquidity profile.
Prepayment speeds for both MSR and RMBS portfolios remained relatively steady despite interest rate volatility.
summary: Cherry Hill reported a GAAP net loss of $9.3 million ($0.29 per share) for Q1 FY2025, with book value declining to $3.58 from $3.82 at year-end due to mark-to-market losses on RMBS and the maturation of interest rate hedges reducing EAD. Management maintained a neutral stance on rates amidst tariff uncertainty and noted that while they have been reinvesting amortization into MBS, MSR acquisitions remain paused until potential portfolio rebalancing occurs later in 2025.

Infrastructure backlog grew to $1.4 billion, adding over $500 million of new awards during the quarter.
R2 social media engagement growth outperformed industry competitors by 774%.

The decline was driven primarily by a 14% drop in Infrastructure segment revenue due to project timing, partially offset by a strong 210% surge in Life Sciences revenue led by R2's unit sales growth.

Industry orders over the trailing 12 months were about 24,000 units, roughly 15,000 below historical replacement levels, with the order shortfall described as creating pent-up demand expected only in the second half
positive_highlights: Gross margin expanded 780 basis points year-over-year to 14.9% from 7.1% on favorable product mix and improved production efficiencies
Adjusted EBITDA rose to $7.3 million from $6.1 million a year ago despite lower revenue and deliveries
Backlog of 3,337 railcars valued at approximately $318 million was up nearly 20% sequentially, and trailing 12-month addressable market share expanded to 27% from 8%
summary: FreightCar America reported Q1 2025 revenue of $96.3 million on 710 deliveries, down from $161.1 million and 1,223 railcars in Q1 2024, with the decline attributed to planned capacity shifted to large custom fabrications and a prior-year timing benefit. Gross margin expanded sharply to 14.9% from 7.1% on favorable mix and production efficiencies, adjusted EBITDA rose to $7.3 million from $6.1 million, and adjusted EPS was $0.05 versus a $0.10 loss. The company reaffirmed full-year 2025 guidance of 4,500-4,900 deliveries, revenue of $530-$595 million, and adjusted EBITDA of $43-$49 million, with production heavily weighted to the second half. Backlog stands at 3,337 railcars valued at approximately $318 million, and operating cash flow was $12.8 million, a fourth consecutive positive quarter.

negative_highlights: Management explicitly withheld Q2 financial guidance due to uncertainty surrounding Google's AFD policy changes.
Total owned and operated revenue fell 16% YoY driven by a non-core marketing business segment decline (-35%).
Network active partners decreased 14% sequentially as the company pushes partners toward Google's new RSOC product.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA surged to $12.1 million, up significantly from just $400k in the prior year quarter.
Owned and operated product revenue grew 53% YoY with sessions up 6%, driven by CouponFollow (+160%) and MapQuest (+30%).
OpEx declined for the seventh consecutive quarter, demonstrating ongoing cost reduction efforts.
summary: System1 reported Q1 FY2025 revenue of $74.5 million (down 1% sequentially and down 12% YoY) with adjusted gross profit of $41.5 million ($33M O&O, $15M Network). While the company beat its high-end guidance on key metrics due to a one-time reversal of invalid traffic revenue in Q1, management explicitly declined to provide financial guidance for Q2 2025 or the full year citing volatility from Google's product transition (shift away from AFD) and macro uncertainty. Management highlighted strong YoY growth in owned-and-operated products (+38% share mix) but noted a sequential decline driven by seasonality.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined 19% year-over-year, with volume drops of 16% and a divestiture impact.
Free cash flow was a use of $125 million, compared to a contribution of $46 million in the prior year.
Net debt leverage ratio increased to 4.6x, exceeding the targeted range of 2.0x to 2.5x.
positive_highlights: Management expects to pass through approximately $30 million in tariff costs to customers with minimal timing impact.
New business acquisition with production builders is ahead of internal plans despite muted seasonal uptake.
Transformation initiatives are on track to deliver approximately $150 million in total benefits, with 40% realized in the first half.
summary: JELD-WEN reported Q1 FY2025 revenue of $776 million, a 19% year-over-year decline driven by volume reductions and the divestiture of Towanda operations. Adjusted EBITDA fell to $22 million (margin of 2.8%), with free cash flow turning into a use of $125 million due to lower earnings and unfavorable working capital dynamics. Management withdrew full-year guidance citing significant short-term volatility from tariffs and softer-than-expected demand, though they expect Q2 adjusted EBITDA to be slightly above Q1 levels.

negative_highlights: Total net revenue of ~$39 million was roughly flat sequentially from Q4 to Q1, with ZYNRELEF unit demand up only 2%
Gross margin is expected to step down toward the mid-70s as smaller-scale manufacturing lots are incorporated
ZYNRELEF's expected inflection is deferred to late Q3/Q4 as new accounts complete onboarding, not realized in the quarter
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA was a record $6.2 million versus a $0.7 million loss a year ago, and full-year EBITDA guidance was raised to $4-12 million from $0-8 million
APONVIE revenue grew over 432% and ZYNRELEF over 60% year over year
Net income of $2.6 million versus a $3.2 million net loss in the prior-year period; product gross margin rose to 78% from 76%
summary: Heron reported Q1 2025 total net revenues of approximately $39 million, product gross profit of $30.4 million (78%, up from 76%), net income of $2.6 million versus a $3.2 million net loss a year ago, and record adjusted EBITDA of $6.2 million. It raised full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance to $4-12 million from $0-8 million, citing Q1 strength and lower expected litigation spend. APONVIE revenue rose over 432% and ZYNRELEF 60% YoY, while total revenue was roughly flat sequentially (Q4 to Q1) as ZYNRELEF unit demand grew 2% against a market down 5.3%. Management expects a ZYNRELEF inflection in late Q3/Q4 as new accounts onboard, and expects gross margin to settle in the mid-70s as lower-scale manufacturing lots come online.

negative_highlights: SMB adjusted gross margin contracted by 30 bps YoY due to reseller mix shifts and attrition in the historical residual portfolio.
Salaries, benefits, and SG&A expenses increased significantly (SG&A up $4.1M), partially offsetting top-line growth with lower operating leverage in SMB.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 9% YoY to $224.6 million, driven by strong performance across all three business segments.
Adjusted gross margin expanded 170 bps sequentially and adjusted EBITDA improved 11% YoY to $51.3 million.
B2B revenue surged 12.1% while Enterprise revenue grew 22.2%, with recurring revenues now comprising over 62% of total gross profit.
summary: Priority Technology Holdings reported Q1 FY2025 net revenue of $224.6 million (up 9% YoY) and adjusted EPS of $0.22 (up from $0.18 in the prior year quarter). The company maintained its full-year 2025 guidance for revenue ($965M-$1B) and adjusted EBITDA ($220M-$230M), citing strong growth in higher-margin B2B (+12%) and Enterprise (+22%) segments. Management expressed confidence in achieving sequential profit growth throughout the year despite macroeconomic uncertainty.

negative_highlights: Europe and APAC combined revenue down 6% on constant currency basis, with weaker March
Adjusted EBITDA declined 7.8% (3.6% ex-warrants) on constant currency basis
Input cost pressures and production inefficiencies hurt margins; gross margin declined
positive_highlights: North America net revenue up 33.5% with PPS volume growth of 45% in Q1
7th consecutive quarter of volume growth
Management confident in 50% automation growth for 2025, with projects continuing despite tariffs
summary: Ranpak reported Q1 FY2025 consolidated net revenue up 8.8% on a constant currency basis, driven by 12% volume growth and North America PPS volume up 45% (net revenue +33.5%). However, Europe and APAC revenue fell 6% on a constant currency basis due to March weakness, and adjusted EBITDA declined 7.8% (or 3.6% excluding Amazon warrants). Management announced structural cost reductions of $8 million, expects gross margin to improve sequentially in Q2 and further in Q3/Q4, and remains confident in 50% automation growth for the year despite tariff uncertainty.

negative_highlights: Total revenue down 3% year-over-year
Accessories and materials declined 15%, including 5 points of one-time benefit
90-day engaged users declined 4% year-over-year
positive_highlights: Paid subscribers up 6% year-over-year to 2.97 million
Connected machines revenue up 4%, with both note-in and note-out units up
International revenue up 8% year-over-year
summary: Cricut reported Q1 2025 revenue of $162.6 million, down 3% year-over-year, with net income of $23.9 million (14.7% margin). Paid subscribers rose 6% to 2.97 million, but accessories and materials declined 15% and 90-day engaged users fell 4%. Management noted tariff uncertainty but cited strong machine watch-in and watch-out, and highlighted capital allocation including a special dividend and share repurchase. The company guided to an inflection point later in 2025 but acknowledged risk from tariffs.

negative_highlights: No revenue or earnings reported for Q1 FY2023 as company is pre-revenue and cash-funded
Celly Nutrition's IPO plans are ongoing subject to market conditions; listing timeline uncertain
LUCID MS Phase 2 submission targeted for latter part of year with trial start hoped for early 2026
positive_highlights: Net cash available provides an 18-24 month forecast for future burn without financing
LUCID MS Phase 1 concluded with the drug well tolerated in healthy participants; toxicity studies underway
unbuzzd sales have started in Puerto Rico following partnership with FUSION
summary: This was a shareholder update call rather than an earnings report; the company reported no revenue or EPS for Q1 FY2023 as it remains pre-revenue and cash-funded through at least late 2027. Management highlighted progress on LUCID MS (Phase 1 concluded, moving to toxicity studies) and commercial launch of unbuzzd in Puerto Rico with sales now started. The company removed the going concern uncertainty from its financials but noted that Celly Nutrition's IPO plans are ongoing subject to market conditions.

negative_highlights: Direct subscription revenue declined slightly year-over-year due to marketing spend optimization and seasonality, though management notes this is manageable.
positive_highlights: Achieved first-ever positive net income ($0.3M) and adjusted EBITDA ($1.1M), marking a landmark turnaround from losses.
Revenue grew 26% year-over-year to $15.1 million, driven by licensing revenue growth of approximately $4 million which offset slight declines in direct subscriptions.
Adjusted free cash flow reached $2 million at the high end of guidance for Q2.
summary: CuriosityStream reported Q1 FY2025 revenue of $15.1 million (up 26% YoY) and achieved its first-ever positive net income ($0.3M) and adjusted EBITDA ($1.1M). Management raised the quarterly dividend from $0.04 to $0.08 per share, citing strong cash flow generation of $2 million in free cash flow which was at the high end of guidance for Q2 (expected revenue $16-17M and FCF $2-3M).

negative_highlights: A small number of advertisers have adjusted plans, redirecting spend from Q2 to later in the year
Some concern about macro uncertainty from tariffs, though minimal impact expected
Amazon competition was addressed, but perceived as a threat by some investors
positive_highlights: Revenue increased 32% YoY, exceeding guidance
Adjusted EBITDA up 76% YoY, ninth consecutive quarter of >30% growth
AI Bidding automates 85% of ad spend, with contribution ex-TAC up 75% YoY
summary: Viant reported record Q1 2025 results with revenue up 32% YoY and contribution ex-TAC up 25% YoY, marking the seventh consecutive quarter of >20% growth in contribution ex-TAC. Adjusted EBITDA grew 76% YoY to $5.4 million, the ninth straight quarter of >30% growth. The company highlighted strong performance despite tariffs, with March being the strongest month and April continuing double-digit growth. They raised Q2 guidance and are positioned for continued strength, citing CTV, addressability, and AI as key drivers.

negative_highlights: Rental income decreased by approximately 2% year-over-year to $11.7 million due to dispositions and acquisitions timing.
Management stated they are not finding compelling acquisition opportunities, with cap rates in the low-to-mid 7s deemed insufficient for current cost of capital (~14%).
Trading volume was elevated (32k shares) but stock price declined $0.25 to close at $14.58.
positive_highlights: AFFO increased 18% year-over-year to $3.9 million driven by lower interest expense ($200k decrease) and property expenses ($140k decrease).
Preferred shares were retired, reducing leverage and saving over $400,000 annually in preferred dividends.
Weighted average lease term remains strong at 14.2 years across the portfolio.
summary: Modiv Industrial reported Q1 FY2025 rental income of $11.7 million, a decrease from the prior year period due to property dispositions and acquisitions partially offsetting each other. Adjusted Funds From Operations (AFFO) was $3.9 million per share on an annualized basis ($0.03 diluted), reflecting lower cash interest expense but no revenue beat against implied expectations given the decline in rental income. Management maintained a cautious stance, citing market volatility and lack of compelling acquisition opportunities at current pricing.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to $9.1 million from $6.1 million in prior year
Restaurant-level contribution margin down to 10.3% from 13.1%
COGS up 160 basis points to 26.6% due to new menu and one-time rollout costs
positive_highlights: Same-store sales up 4.4% system-wide in Q1, accelerating from Q4 growth of 0.5%
Post-menu launch same-store sales up approximately 5% through April despite difficult comparison
Double-digit increases in brand awareness, brand search traffic, and app sessions since relaunch
summary: Noodles & Company reported Q1 FY2025 revenue of $123.8 million, up 2% year-over-year, with system-wide same-store sales increasing 4.4% (company-owned 4.7%, franchise 2.9%). Traffic rose 1.8% and check increased 2.9% (1.3% pricing). Net loss widened to $9.1 million from $6.1 million, and adjusted EBITDA fell to $2.4 million from $5.5 million, pressured by one-time menu rollout costs and higher marketing. Management reiterated full-year guidance, widening the lower end of restaurant contribution margin by 50 basis points to account for tariffs, and noted same-store sales up ~5% through April post-menu launch. They expect free cash flow positive in Q3 and Q4.

negative_highlights: Q1 revenue missed consensus expectations due to a weaker-than-anticipated box office slate and tariff-related advertiser uncertainty.
Government advertising spend reduced significantly following policy shifts, impacting national on-screen revenue mix.
Adjusted OIBDA remained negative at $9M compared to the prior year's loss of only $5.7M.
positive_highlights: Q2 revenue guidance raised to $56M-$61M, reflecting optimism about a strong upcoming box office slate including 'A Minecraft Movie' and 'Mission: Impossible'.
Secured a five-year extension with AMC Theaters through 2042 featuring improved payment structures aligned with performance metrics.
Launched new AI-driven products Bullseye and Blueprint to enhance targeting capabilities in the NCMx suite.
summary: NCMI reported Q1 FY2025 revenue of $34.9 million, a 7% year-over-year decline driven by lower box office attendance and government ad spend reductions, which fell within the company's guidance range of $34M-$36M. Adjusted OIBDA was negative $9 million, aligning with prior guidance but reflecting reduced top-line performance. Management noted that while Q1 results were seasonally soft and impacted by specific film underperformance (e.g., Snow White), they do not view this as indicative of full-year performance.

negative_highlights: Net income and core operating income declined significantly due to higher loss activity and reinstatement premiums.
Currency revaluation negatively impacted non-U.S. dollar reserves by approximately 10 points.
positive_highlights: Combined ratio of 94.4% demonstrates resilience despite significantly elevated loss environment and macroeconomic uncertainty.
Reinsurance treaty segment showed strong top-line growth of almost 44% driven by new business in specialty lines.
Prior year development was favorable by $25.8 million, partially offsetting current accident year losses.
summary: IGIC reported Q1 FY2025 net income of $27.3 million ($0.59/share) and core operating income of $19.5 million ($0.42/share), both down significantly from the prior year due to elevated loss activity, reinstatement premiums, and currency impacts. The combined ratio was 94.4%, reflecting a 6-7 point quarter-over-quarter deterioration on a like-for-like basis after adjusting for approximately 10 points of currency revaluation impact. Management noted that while the short-tail and reinsurance segments showed growth, the long-tail segment recorded an underwriting loss of $7.5 million amidst declining rates and FX headwinds.

negative_highlights: Net interest income fell 7.3% quarter-over-quarter to $13.0 million from $14.1 million
Gross originations of $4.4 million were more than offset by $9.2 million of sales and repayments, shrinking the portfolio to $407 million
Weighted average yield to maturity declined to 16.9% from 17.2% in Q4 2024
positive_highlights: Book value per share rose to $14.87 as of March 31, 2025 from $14.83 at December 31, 2024
Total leverage decreased to 28% of book equity from 34% at year-end 2024
Loan number nine restructuring completed with dispensaries reopening, and $1.2 million of CECL reserve reversed
summary: Chicago Atlantic Real Estate Finance reported Q1 2025 net interest income of $13.0 million, down 7.3% from $14.1 million in Q4 2024, driven by lower prepayment/exit fees ($0.4M vs $1.5M) and the full-quarter impact of 50bp prime rate cuts. Distributable earnings per share were $0.47 basic / $0.46 diluted, consistent with the prior quarter, and book value rose to $14.87 from $14.83. Gross originations were only $4.4 million against $9.2 million of sales and repayments, causing the portfolio to shrink to $407 million across 30 companies, with weighted average yield falling to 16.9% from 17.2%. Total leverage declined to 28% of book equity from 34%, and the company completed the loan number nine restructuring, reversing $1.2 million of CECL reserves; management expects deployments to accelerate in Q2 and Q3 but provided no formal guidance.

negative_highlights: Core revenue decreased 2% year-over-year primarily due to a complete loss of volume from one large consumer genomics customer in the SMS segment.
Revenue from the Together Take Me Home public health program is expected to drop significantly, falling from $8 million in 2024 to approximately $4 million for fiscal 2025.
U.S. diagnostics business faces elevated uncertainty due to potential budget cuts and staffing reductions at federal agencies like HHS and CDC.
positive_highlights: International diagnostics revenue grew 8% year-over-year driven by initial orders for the WHO PQ listed hepatitis C self-test and expansion in emergency room settings.
Sample Management Solutions (SMS) revenue excluding the single large customer disruption showed organic growth, demonstrating successful diversification of the customer base.
Board authorized a new $40 million share repurchase program over two years to fund capital deployment strategy.
summary: Q1 total revenue was $29.9 million and core revenue of $29.5 million decreased 2% year-over-year due to a significant disruption from a large consumer genomics customer in the Sample Management Solutions segment. While international diagnostics grew 8%, overall results were weighed down by headwinds including an expected end to the Together Take Me Home program later this year and continued uncertainty regarding U.S. public health funding. The company raised its Q2 guidance range slightly compared to prior expectations, citing a more stable outlook for PEPFAR programs than previously feared.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined 21% year-over-year to $5.3 million from $6.7 million.
Non-GAAP gross margin contracted 260 bps to 10.8% from 13.4%, and GAAP gross margin fell to 2.5% from 7.3%.
Q2 revenue guidance of $4.9-$5.3 million implies a sequential decline from Q1, and margin guidance for Q4 was withheld due to tariff uncertainty.
positive_highlights: Q1 revenue of $5.3 million came in slightly above the company's own guidance.
Over 75% of production volume has transitioned to the lower-cost Thailand facility, with successful quality audits and final customer approvals received.
New BLE partnerships with Tag-N-Trac (pharma cold chain) and InPlay (logistics smart labels) and a wine authentication solution with ZATAP advance the accelerate strategy.
summary: Identiv reported Q1 FY2025 revenue of $5.3 million, slightly above its own guidance but down from $6.7 million in Q1 2024, attributed to the exit of low-margin business. GAAP gross margin was 2.5% (non-GAAP 10.8%), down from 7.3% (13.4%) a year ago due to dual manufacturing overhead from the Singapore-to-Thailand transition and lower utilization. GAAP net loss from continuing operations narrowed to $4.8 million ($0.21/share) from $5.4 million ($0.24/share), aided by non-recurrence of $0.9 million in prior-year strategic review costs, while non-GAAP adjusted EBITDA worsened to negative $3.9 million from negative $3.2 million. Q2 FY2025 revenue guidance was set at $4.9-$5.3 million, implying a sequential decline; management declined to provide gross margin guidance for the rest of the year pending tariff outcomes, and the stock repurchase program was paused with no buybacks made.

negative_highlights: Full-year fiscal 2025 guidance cut to organic net sales down ~5-6% and adjusted EBITDA of approximately $125 million, with the quarter's EBITDA over 20% below last year
North America organic net sales declined 10% and Snacks declined 13%, with management stating 80% of the top-line shortfall was in North America and two-thirds of that in Snacks
Free cash flow swung to a $2 million outflow from $30 million a year ago, and net leverage ticked up to 4.2x, with the credit agreement amended to allow maximum net secured leverage of 4.75x
positive_highlights: International returned to organic net sales growth of 0.5% following prior service-level challenges, with International adjusted EBITDA margin at 13.2%
Working capital improvements: DPO rose to 61 days from 37 days in fiscal 2023, and the company expects about two-thirds of its $165 million working capital goal unlocked by year-end

Cost savings and portfolio actions: over $25 million of run-rate savings expected by the second half of fiscal 2026, co-manufacturers cut 23% and vendors 13%, and lease expense reduced by over $5 million annually since fiscal 2023
summary: Hain Celestial reported fiscal Q3 2025 organic net sales down 5% (3 points volume/mix, 2 points net pricing), adjusted gross margin of 21.8% (down 50 bps), adjusted EBITDA down 23% to $34 million (8.6% of sales, down 140 bps), and adjusted EPS of $0.07 versus $0.13 a year ago. The company cut its full-year fiscal 2025 outlook to organic net sales down ~5-6%, adjusted EBITDA of approximately $125 million, gross margin of approximately 21.5%, and free cash flow of approximately $40 million, citing slower volume recovery. The Board terminated CEO Wendy Davidson effective immediately, appointed director Alison Lewis as Interim President and CEO, and launched a strategic portfolio review with Goldman Sachs; no set timetable for completion. North America organic sales fell 10% while International grew 0.5%.

negative_highlights: Revenue fell 12.8% year over year to $169.8 million and adjusted EBITDA dropped to $5.8 million from $9.7 million, a 3.4% margin
FY2025 revenue and adjusted EBITDA guidance ranges were both lowered, with the low end assuming an EPA emissions delay
Net leverage was 5x (roughly 4x on the amended covenant calculation), above the 2x target, with debt maturing in 2027 and refinancing still being explored
positive_highlights: Adjusted gross margin expanded 240 bps sequentially to 10.8% on operational and footprint actions
Free cash flow from continuing operations was $11.2 million versus negative $6.5 million a year ago, supporting $18.1 million gross debt reduction
Inventory declined $5 million versus year-end, and restructuring spend was under $1 million; reduce exposure note sequential gross margin up 290 bps
summary: Q1 2025 revenue fell to $169.8 million from $194.6 million a year ago, with adjusted EBITDA of $5.8 million (3.4% margin, down 160 bps) and an adjusted net loss of $0.08 per diluted share versus $0.08 income last year. Free cash flow swung to positive $11.2 million from negative $6.5 million on working capital and capex cuts. Management lowered FY2025 revenue guidance to $660-690 million (from $670-710 million) and adjusted EBITDA to $22-27 million (from $25-30 million), while introducing a free cash flow target of at least $20 million; the segment resegmentation and gross margin improvement to 10.8% (up 240 bps sequentially) were the main positives against a 23% Class 8 build decline and construction/ag down 5-15%.

negative_highlights: CEO noted that near-term earnings may vary quarter-to-quarter as the company executes strategy in an uncertain economic environment.
Management indicated they are being patient and selective with new lending opportunities, waiting for market volatility related to tariffs to settle before regrowing the portfolio.
The Life Science Boston project continues to struggle with negative supply growth and potential conversion back to traditional office use.
positive_highlights: Collected $307 million in repayments, double the prior quarter's amount, representing the highest percentage of outstanding principal balance in company history.
Reduced net debt to equity ratio (excluding CECL) to 1.2x from 1.9x at end of Q1 2024 by reducing borrowings $228 million.
Book value per share remained stable at $9.88, supported by a reduction in the total CECL reserve to $140 million.
summary: ACRE reported Q1 FY2025 GAAP net income of $9.3 million ($0.17 per share) and distributable earnings of $7.2 million ($0.13 per share), with no realized losses incurred. The company significantly improved its liquidity position, reducing outstanding borrowings to $946 million and increasing available capital to $147 million through loan repayments of $307 million and refinancing actions. Management declared a regular cash dividend of $0.15 per common share for the second quarter.

negative_highlights: Adjusted revenue fell 8.5% YoY to $751 million, with government segment revenue down 16% to $216 million and government adjusted EBITDA down 31%
Adjusted free cash flow was negative $74 million for the quarter and net leverage rose sequentially to 2.7 turns
Q2 2025 adjusted EBITDA margin guidance of 4% to 4.5% is below the 4.9% reported in Q1
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 50 bps YoY to 4.9% on $37 million of adjusted EBITDA despite an 8.5% revenue decline
New business ACV rose 14% YoY to $109 million and new business TCV rose 96% to $280 million, helped by an eight-year Lima, Peru transit deal
Transportation segment adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 380 bps to 4.5%, and the segment's tolling business supported New York City congestion pricing implementation
summary: Conduent reported Q1 2025 adjusted revenue of $751 million, down 8.5% YoY, driven primarily by a 16% decline in the government segment to $216 million. Adjusted EBITDA was $37 million with margin of 4.9%, up 50 bps YoY; net leverage rose sequentially to 2.7 turns and adjusted free cash flow was negative $74 million. Full-year 2025 guidance was left unchanged from February, with Q2 revenue expected sequentially higher but below Q2 2024 and adjusted EBITDA margin of 4% to 4.5%. New business ACV rose 14% YoY to $109 million and new business TCV rose 96% to $280 million, while a previously flagged large government health contract termination has now fully lapped.

negative_highlights: Total and software revenue grew only 3% year over year
Operating cash flow fell to negative $10.5 million from negative $7.3 million in Q1 of the prior year
Net loss per share of $0.08 was flat versus the prior year, with operating loss at $6.2 million
positive_highlights: Full-year 2025 total revenue, software revenue and adjusted EBITDA guidance all raised from last quarter
Q1 adjusted EBITDA of negative $5.1 million came in about $1 million above the high end of guidance
Customers spending over $100,000 grew 8% year over year to 318, representing 76% of revenue
summary: Q1 FY2025 total revenue was $36.7 million, up 3% year over year and toward the high end of guidance, with software revenue of $30.9 million (also up 3%) and services of $5.8 million. Adjusted EBITDA was negative $5.1 million (-14% margin), roughly $1 million better than the high end of guidance, while net loss per share was $0.08, flat year over year. Management raised its full-year 2025 outlook for total revenue ($146-158 million), software revenue ($125.5-131.5 million) and adjusted EBITDA (-$18 to -$15 million) versus last quarter's guidance. Customer count above $100,000 in trailing revenue reached 318, up 8% year over year and 76% of revenue, though operating cash flow worsened to negative $10.5 million from negative $7.3 million a year ago.

negative_highlights: Net loss attributable to common stockholders of $27.8 million, or $4.91 per diluted share, with AFFO per share of negative $0.98
Total revenue fell $26.5 million YoY, and softening began in February tied to DOGE-related policy actions, particularly in D.C.
Company does not anticipate reinstating a common dividend in 2025, and $2.6 billion of debt carries a blended 8.1% interest rate with 77% effectively floating
positive_highlights: Comparable hotel EBITDA grew 8.7% YoY and hotel EBITDA margin expanded approximately 131 bps
GRO AHT initiatives now expected to deliver more than $30 million of run rate EBITDA improvement toward the $50 million goal
Recent conversions delivered strong results: Le Pavillon RevPAR up 87% and La Concha RevPAR up 16% with total revenue up 27%
summary: Q1 2025 comparable RevPAR rose 3.2% and comparable total revenue grew 3.6%, with comparable hotel EBITDA up 8.7% and hotel EBITDA margin expanding about 131 bps. However, the company still reported a net loss of $27.8 million (-$4.91/share) and AFFO of -$0.98/share, with total revenue down $26.5 million YoY, though adjusted EBITDAre rose $2.2 million to $61.7 million. GRO AHT initiatives now contribute more than $30 million run rate EBITDA improvement toward a $50 million goal. Management flagged softening in some markets starting in February tied to DOGE-related policy actions and government segment weakness, primarily in D.C., while touting no common dividend reinstatement in 2025.

negative_highlights: Lift Truck revenues declined 14% year-over-year, driving significant operating profit drop
Full-year 2025 revenues, production, and profits expected below 2024's strong results
April saw customer order hesitation due to tariff effects
positive_highlights: Q1 bookings of $590 million, up nearly 50% sequentially, with book-to-bill at 100%
Nuvera realignment expected to deliver $15-20 million annualized cost savings from second half 2025
Inventory down nearly $70 million year-over-year, supporting cash flow
summary: In Q1 2025, Hyster-Yale reported a 14% year-over-year decline in Lift Truck revenues due to lower volumes, with adjusted operating profit down significantly on reduced manufacturing absorption. Management reaffirmed full-year guidance below 2024's record results, noting Q2 operating profit is expected to decline moderately due to tariff cost timing. The company announced a strategic realignment of Nuvera away from fuel cells toward energy solutions, expecting $15-20 million annualized savings. Long-term targets include a 7% operating margin through the cycle.

negative_highlights: Direct-to-consumer sales declined 21.5% to $15 million as the company operates with a smaller, more efficient team.
Rental revenue decreased 7.5% to $13.8 million due to lower average billing rates from a shift toward private payers.
Gross margin on rental revenue contracted by 33 basis points to 43.3%.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA turned positive at $36,000 in Q1 2025 compared to a negative $7.6 million in the prior year.
Domestic business-to-business revenue surged 29.9% to $21.5 million driven by increased demand from existing customers.
International business-to-business revenue grew 22.9% to $32 million, reflecting expansion into new and existing customer bases.
summary: Inogen reported Q1 FY2025 revenue of $82.3 million, a 5.5% year-over-year increase driven by strong business-to-business growth in domestic and international channels. The company achieved positive adjusted EBITDA of $36,000 for the quarter, marking its first profitable quarter since 2021, while GAAP net loss narrowed to $6.2 million from a prior period loss of $14.6 million. Management reaffirmed full-year 2025 revenue guidance of $352-$355 million and maintained expectations to approach adjusted EBITDA breakeven for the year.

negative_highlights: Royalty revenue was explicitly stated as lower in Q1 FY2025 compared to the same period last year.
Service revenue decreased due to the completion of certain small molecule ion channel programs, indicating a natural attrition cycle.
The newly launched exploration partner access program is excluded from 2025 financial guidance.
positive_highlights: Revenue increased year-over-year driven by a Phase I milestone from Genmab's 1078 clinical program.
Operating expenses declined to $23.0M due to lower stock-based compensation and reduced external costs on small molecule programs.
Net loss narrowed sequentially compared to the prior period.
summary: OmniAb reported Q1 FY2025 revenue of $4.2 million (up from $3.8M in prior year) and a net loss narrowing to $18.2 million ($0.17/share). Management provided full-year 2025 guidance for revenue between $20-25 million, which excludes the new exploration partner access program launch announced today.

negative_highlights: Revenue fell to $38.0 million from $47.2 million and core FFO dropped to $0.19 per share from $0.36 year over year
Operating property occupancy was just 74.3% at quarter end, and Q1 renewal rent spreads were roughly -18%
Net debt to adjusted EBITDA guided to 8.0x-8.8x, with debt expected to rise in coming years and 2025-2026 framed as the low point for revenue and core FFO
positive_highlights: Over 450,000 square feet of new and renewal leasing signed as of May 6 with a 7.4-year weighted average lease term, including a 160,000-square-foot 10-year Ingram Micro lease in Buffalo
Sold three vacant properties totaling 287,000 square feet for $19.1 million (~$66/sq ft), with two more under contract for $27.3 million (~$129/sq ft)
Liquidity of $244.5 million as of May 5, and full-year 2025 guidance reaffirmed at core FFO of $0.61-$0.70 per share
summary: Orion reported Q1 2025 revenue of $38.0 million versus $47.2 million a year ago, with core FFO falling to $0.19 per share from $0.36 and adjusted EBITDA of $17.4 million versus $26.7 million. The net loss narrowed to $9.4 million ($0.17/share) from $26.2 million ($0.47/share), helped by prior impairments. Management reaffirmed full-year core FFO guidance of $0.61-$0.70 per share, G&A of $19.5-$20.5 million, and net debt/EBITDA of 8.0x-8.8x, and expects the next one to two years to mark the low point for revenue and core FFO. Operating occupancy was 74.3% with a 77.4% lease rate, and Q1 renewal spreads came in at roughly -18%, though management noted new and renewal leasing of over 450,000 square feet signed as of May 6.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA margin declined by 30 basis points to 13.8% due to increased SG&A expenses related to investments in India and technology expansion.
Fintech vertical revenue decreased by 12%, though management notes this impact is expected to largely lap going forward.
positive_highlights: Record revenue of $140.7M representing an 11% YoY increase and the highest quarterly revenue ever for the company.
Adjusted EPS reached a record high of 82 cents, driven by higher margins from offshore regions (up 19%) and digital/omnichannel services growth.
Management raised full-year guidance on both revenue and EBITDA while initiating a new $15 million share repurchase program.
summary: IBEX reported record Q3 FY2025 revenue of $140.7 million (up 11% YoY) and adjusted EPS of 82 cents (up 18% YoY). Management raised full-year guidance for both revenue ($540-$545M vs prior $525-$535M) and EBITDA ($68-70M vs prior $68-69M), citing structural growth, market share gains in Q3 against seasonal trends, and the launch of a new $15 million share repurchase program. The quarter featured record profitability with adjusted EBITDA margins at 13.8% despite investments in India.

negative_highlights: Global Private Equity was 'in line with expectations' due to expected step-downs in several funds, with management fee declines in the GP segment
Transaction fee growth trajectory is uncertain and management noted the near-term market environment may slow the pace of capital markets activity
positive_highlights: Record FRE of $311 million, up 17% year-over-year
Record FRE margin of 48%, with AlpInvest FRE margin at 58%
Record AUM of $453 billion, up 6% year-over-year, with $14 billion of Q1 inflows (vs. $5 billion in Q1 2024)
summary: Carlyle reported record Q1 FY2025 results with fee-related earnings of $311 million (up 17% YoY), a record 48% FRE margin, distributable earnings of $455 million, and record AUM of $453 billion (up 6% YoY). AlpInvest FRE nearly doubled YoY to $66 million with a 58% FRE margin, and Global Credit revenue grew 28% YoY to $232 million. Management reiterated its 2025 targets of ~6% FRE growth and ~$40 billion of gross inflows, but flagged that the macro backdrop is uncertain and fluid due to new trade policies. The most notable change was the tariff-driven deterioration in market sentiment, which management said has not yet shown up in April flow data.

negative_highlights: Clinical solutions revenue declined more than 30% compared to Q1 2024 due to a large one-time order in the prior period not recurring.
Growth from biopharma custom products was lower than expected, though management maintains at least 15% growth guidance for the year.
Free cash flow remained negative ($4.3M) with an expectation of less than $12M outflow for the full year.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew low double digits for catalog products (approx 60% of total) driven by increased customer count and general demand increase.
Gross margin expanded to 30.7%, exceeding previously communicated expectations, aided by higher revenue mix and lower overhead costs.
Operating expenses decreased $900k YoY excluding the prior year's non-recurring workforce reduction charge.
summary: Alpha Teknova reported Q1 FY2025 revenue of $9.8 million (up 5% YoY), driven by low double-digit growth in catalog products but offset by a decline in clinical solutions due to the absence of one large year-ago order. Gross margin expanded significantly to 30.7%, while operating expenses decreased excluding non-recurring charges from the prior period. Management reiterated full-year revenue guidance of $39M-$42M, maintaining expectations despite macro headwinds and lower-than-guided growth in biopharma custom products.

negative_highlights: Crude oil prices have significantly reduced since early March guidance, creating potential downside exposure for the crude-oriented Rockies segment.
Natural gas volumes averaged a decrease of 2 million cubic feet per day relative to the fourth quarter in the Rockies segment due to production declines.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA increased by $1.6 million in the Rockies segment and $9.6 million in the Mid-Con segment compared to Q4.
summary: Summit Midstream reported Q1 FY2025 adjusted EBITDA of $57.5 million and capital expenditures of $20.6 million against a full-year guidance range of $245-$280 million in adjusted EBITDA and $65-$75 million in capex, which management reiterated despite recent crude price softening. The company raised an additional $250 million in senior secured notes to repay revolver borrowings and maintain over $350 million liquidity while closing the accretive acquisition of Moonrise Midstream. Management noted that if all remaining second-half wells are deferred due to lower prices, they would trend toward the low end of existing guidance.

negative_highlights: Net revenue declined year-over-year by approximately 24% to $35.7 million due to reduced store count and demand softness.
Management withdrew full-year guidance entirely, citing tariff uncertainty and potential fluctuations in consumer demand.
Store traffic dropped significantly in areas without vibrant caregiver laws as consumers walk away from retail.
positive_highlights: Proprietary product sales accounted for 32% of total revenue, up from 22.6% in the prior year period.
Gross margins expanded to 27.2%, reflecting a stronger product mix and disciplined execution on procurement.
The company ended the quarter with $52.6 million in liquidity and no debt.
summary: GrowGeneration reported Q1 FY2025 net revenue of $35.7 million, a decline from the prior year's $47.9 million due to reduced store count and softness in durables demand driven by tariff concerns. Gross margins improved sequentially to 27.2% as proprietary brand sales reached 32% of total revenue, but management withdrew full-year guidance citing macroeconomic uncertainty while providing a Q2 expectation of over $40 million.

negative_highlights: Q1 product revenues of $6 million low versus prior quarter
Pretax operating loss of $2 million and net loss of $1 million
PEP submission delayed to H1 2026 with sample analysis not expected until Q4 2025
positive_highlights: April deliveries of $62 million to SNS expected to be recognized in Q2
U.S. government exercised $26 million IV option and added $14 million manufacturing funding
Special cash dividend of $0.60 per share declared, fourth consecutive year
summary: SIGA reported Q1 2025 product revenues of $6 million from an international sale, with pretax operating loss of $2 million and net loss of $1 million. The company highlighted April deliveries of $62 million to the SNS, a $26 million IV order for 2026 delivery, and a $14 million contract modification for manufacturing. Management expressed confidence in the U.S. government partnership and expects substantial sales ahead, but provided no formal revenue guidance.

negative_highlights: Total revenue declined 9% YoY to $17.5 million, driven primarily by a 10% decrease in account utilization.
Dry eye segment revenue fell significantly from $1M to $400k due to fewer SmartLids sales following the price increase enacted in October 2024.
Surgical glaucoma revenue decreased 6% YoY as Medicare coverage for multiple MIGS procedures was restricted.
positive_highlights: Adjusted operating expenses decreased 7% YoY to $24.7 million due to lower legal fees and expense controls offsetting tariffs.
Ordering accounts increased 3% sequentially despite the new Medicare LCD restrictions on stacked MIGS procedures.
Gross margin remained flat at 86%, as tariff impacts were deferred by using pre-tariff inventory.
summary: Sight Sciences reported Q1 FY2025 revenue of $17.5 million (down 9% YoY) and adjusted operating expenses of $24.7 million (down 7% YoY). Management reaffirmed full-year 2025 revenue guidance at approximately $70-75M but lowered the adjusted expense guidance to $101-105M from a prior range of $105-107M, citing tariff impacts and fiscal discipline. The quarter was impacted by new Medicare LCD restrictions on stacked MIGS procedures in five states.

negative_highlights: Marketplace revenue fell to just over $400,000 as marketing efforts were significantly reduced ahead of the late-Q2 relaunch.
note now, pay later origination volume dipped sequentially due to seasonality and tighter AI-driven underwriting.
Revenue from the large merchant onboarding and integration backlog will not be realized until Q2 and especially the second half, leaving near-term revenue timing uncertain.
positive_highlights: Revenue increased 95% year over year to $6.75 million from $3.47 million.
Gross margin expanded to 58% from 43% a year ago.

Operating expenses decreased 10% year over year to $14 million, with sales and marketing down 48%, and the company ended Q1 with $28 million in cash plus a $2 million fully prepaid bulk EveryLife order.
summary: Q1 2025 revenue grew 95% year over year to $6.75 million, with fintech contributing $3.05 million, EveryLife $3.27 million, and the marketplace just over $400,000. Gross margin expanded to 58% from 43%, and operating expenses fell 10% year over year to $14 million, while sales and marketing dropped 48%. Management reaffirmed full-year guidance of greater than 100% revenue growth (over $46 million), a year-over-year reduction in operating expenses, and turning operating cash flow positive by year-end, but gave no new quarterly guidance and noted a marketplace revenue decline driven by a marketing halt ahead of a late-Q2 Made in America relaunch.

negative_highlights: Total revenues decreased by approximately 1.4% YoY to $34.6 million due to portfolio changes.
FFO ($0.20/share) and AFFO ($0.22/share) both declined sequentially from the prior year quarter.
Q1 lease renewal rate was lower than typical at roughly 62%, with Q2 expected volatility including a non-renewing 50,000 sq ft lease.
positive_highlights: Net income attributable to common shareholders increased significantly YoY from $800k in Q1 2024 to $2.1 million in Q1 2025 ($0.03/share vs $0.01/share).
Successfully closed a strategic five-property acquisition for $69.6 million at an attractive 9% cap rate, substantially below replacement cost.
Completed the sale of two medical properties generating aggregate gross proceeds of $8.2 million and a gain of $1.4 million.
summary: Q1 FY2025 revenue decreased by approximately 1.4% to $34.6 million due to acquisitions and dispositions, while expenses fell slightly to $32.2 million driven by non-cash compensation adjustments related to the CEO transition. Net income attributable to common shareholders was $2.1 million ($0.03/share), representing a significant YoY increase from $800k in Q1 2024 primarily due to lower prior-year comparables rather than operational expansion, as FFO and AFFO per share declined sequentially by roughly $0.01 each. Management reaffirmed full-year 2025 AFFO guidance of $0.89-$0.93 despite the CEO succession plan impacting Q2-G&A expenses.

negative_highlights: Gross margin improvement was partially offset by lower negative pressure wound therapy equipment sales ($200k decrease) and lower margin new business in Patient Services.
Chemo Mouthpiece revenue is delayed due to formulary adoption and billing logistics, with meaningful revenue expected later in 2025.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 8.5% YoY to $34.7 million, with Patient Services up 11.7% and Device Solutions up 4%.
Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded significantly to 18.2%, the highest since 2021, driven by improved collections and revenue mix.
Operating cash flow improved nearly fourfold to $1.8 million compared to the prior year quarter.
summary: InfuSystem reported Q1 FY2025 net revenue of $34.7 million, an 8.5% increase year-over-year, driven by strong growth in Patient Services and Device Solutions segments. Adjusted EBITDA reached $6.3 million (18.2% margin), representing a 64% year-over-year improvement and the highest first-quarter result since 2021. Management maintained full-year revenue guidance of 8% to 10% growth and expects adjusted EBITDA margins to exceed the prior year's 18.8%, noting that Q1 results put the company on track despite ongoing IT upgrade costs.

negative_highlights: D2C advertising revenue declined 9%, including an 800-basis point headwind from last year's Super Bowl comparison.
TV Media affiliate revenue declined 8.6% due to subscriber declines and recent deal renewals.
Digital advertising monetization is softer than expected due to increased supply, with no immediate firming observed.
positive_highlights: D2C OIBDA improved by $177 million to a loss of $109 million driven by subscriber growth and churn reduction (improved 130 bps YoY).
Paramount+ ended the quarter with 79 million global subscribers, up 11% year-over-year.
Film segment revenue grew 4% to $627m primarily due to Sonic the Hedgehog 3 box office success of nearly $500 million.
summary: Paramount Global reported Q1 FY2025 total revenue of $7.2 billion (up 2% YoY excluding the Super Bowl) and adjusted OIBDA of $688 million. D2C subscription revenue grew 16%, while TV Media advertising was flat ex-Super Bowl, with affiliate revenue down 8.6%. Management reiterated full-year guidance for Paramount+ domestic profitability but noted macro uncertainty could impact later-quarter results.

negative_highlights: Second-line Bolster cohort enrollment capped at ~20 patients, half of original target
FORTIFIDE study initiation remains on hold pending a potentially cheaper alternative
Cash runway only into Q3 2026, constraining ability to initiate new trials
positive_highlights: ASCEND Cohort A showed positive overall survival trend and 4 complete responses vs 0 in placebo
Bolster first-line enrollment completed ~6 months ahead of plan, accelerating top-line data to mid-2025
Qilu completed enrollment in 96-subject study; $10 million milestone due upon first Phase 3 patient dosing
summary: Lisata reported Q1 2025 operating expenses of $5.8 million, down 11.4% year-over-year, with R&D spend down 19.7% to $2.6 million. Net loss narrowed to $4.7 million from $5.4 million in Q1 2024. Cash and marketable securities stood at $25.8 million, expected to fund operations into Q3 2026. Management highlighted upcoming data readouts across ASCEND, Bolster, and CENDIFOX trials, with no guidance change.

negative_highlights: Gross margin rate declined from 52% in Q1 2024 to 43% in Q1 2025 as the company transitioned to a single product line.
Cash balance decreased from $4.2 million at year-end 2024 to $3.2 million at the end of Q1 2025 due to M&A expenses and operations.
R&D costs were zero in Q1 2025 compared to $6,000 in the prior year period.
positive_highlights: Zola revenue grew 90% year-over-year, significantly outpacing the 24% category growth.
Gross margins remained strong at 43%, exceeding the 30% threshold for nine consecutive quarters.
Operating expenses decreased 16% year-over-year to $1.7 million, excluding transaction fees.
summary: In Q1 FY2025, Arcadia Biosciences reported revenue of approximately $1.2 million, representing a 22% year-over-year increase driven by a 90% growth in its Zola coconut water line. The company recognized a one-time gain of $750,000 from the sale of wheat patents and eliminated a $1 million contingent liability related to soy patents. Management expressed confidence that pending tariffs will have little to no impact on Q2 results due to prior inventory replenishment.

negative_highlights: Gross margin declined 210 bps YoY to 44.8%, or about 41% excluding the $2 million gift card breakage benefit
Q2 revenue guidance of $36-41 million implies a 25% YoY decline at the midpoint
Full-year growth is back-half weighted, with return to top-line growth not expected until Q4 and tariff cost pressure building in Q3 and Q4
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA loss of $19 million beat guidance by about $5 million and improved 11% year-over-year
Inventory fell 29% YoY to $43 million, with conservative fall/holiday note preserving flexibility to chase demand
New products reached over 20% of sales in March, up from high single digits in January, with Cards on the Table generating 25 million Instagram views
summary: Q1 net revenue was $32 million, slightly above the midpoint of guidance, with gross margin of 44.8% (down 210 bps YoY) that included a ~$2 million gift card breakage benefit worth ~400 bps; adjusted EBITDA loss of $19 million beat guidance by about $5 million and improved 11% YoY. Q2 revenue is guided to $36-41 million, down 25% YoY at the midpoint, while the full-year 2025 outlook of $175-195 million revenue and $55-65 million adjusted EBITDA loss was reiterated, with expected top-line growth only in Q4. Tariff exposure on Vietnam goods, choppy consumer traffic since April, and a 29% YoY inventory reduction to $43 million frame the cautious setup ahead of the late-summer product refresh.

negative_highlights: Total revenue declined 7% year over year and subscription revenue fell 7%, with renewal rates still below the prior-year level.
Adjusted EBITDA margin contracted to 25% from approximately 31.7% in Q1 2024, and adjusted operating income fell 35% year over year.
Full-year revenue guidance implies continued decline, and management noted a lag before operational changes improve retention.
positive_highlights: Revenue of $59.2 million exceeded the high end of guidance by $3 million, and adjusted EBITDA of $14.7 million beat the midpoint by $4 million.
Professional services revenue returned to growth, up 9% year over year.
Renewal rates stabilized at levels consistent with the second half of 2024, and new logo wins were solid across all end markets.
summary: Definitive Healthcare reported Q1 FY2025 revenue of $59.2 million, down 7% year over year but above the high end of guidance by $3 million, with adjusted EBITDA of $14.7 million (25% margin) also beating guidance by $4 million. The beat was driven by professional services outperformance and deal timing, while subscription revenue declined 7% and renewal rates remained below prior-year levels though stable versus H2 2024. Full-year 2025 revenue guidance was tightened to $234–240 million (a 5–7% decline), raising the bottom end by $4 million while holding the upper end and maintaining prior profit guidance. The quarter reflected modest operational stabilization, but management cited macro uncertainty and a lag before retention improvements materialize.

negative_highlights: note and administrative expenses increased due to approximately $500k in professional fees for a multiyear financial restatement
Cash balance decreased from $600,000 at June 30, 2024 to $500,000 as of March 31, 2025 due to working capital changes
Management acknowledged tariff pressures forcing price list updates and the need for rapid supplier diversification
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 16% YoY driven by unit growth of 25% in GSE markets and 10% in material handling
Gross margin expanded to 32%, a 4.7 percentage point increase from the prior year quarter, aided by lower warranty costs
Adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed significantly to $1.1 million compared to $1.7 million last year
summary: Flux Power Holdings reported Q3 FY2025 revenue of $16.7 million (up 16% YoY) and gross margin expansion to 32%, driven by unit growth in material handling (+10%) and GSE markets (+25%). The company posted an Adjusted EBITDA loss of $1.1M, narrowing from a prior year loss of $1.7M due to higher gross profit partially offset by restatement-related S&A expenses. Management noted tariff headwinds requiring price adjustments but expressed confidence in maintaining momentum through supply chain diversification and domestic assembly expansion.

negative_highlights: Revenue performance fell note weakness in of expectations due to a sales force realignment that was 'more significant than initially anticipated'.
Full-year revenue guidance for 2025 was lowered, with management stating Q1 results set the new baseline.
Approximately half (50%) of current territory managers were hired in the last 15 months and are still ramping up productivity.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 15% YoY despite significant headwinds, driven by expansion into new territories and accounts in the US heart failure business ($11.1M revenue).
Gross margin remained stable at 84%, consistent with full-year guidance of 83-84%.
New clinical evidence presented showed an 85% reduction in heart failure hospital visits post-Barostim implantation.
summary: CVRX reported Q1 FY2025 revenue of $12.3 million (up 15% YoY) and a net loss narrowing to $13.8 million ($0.53/share). Management explicitly stated the quarter fell short of expectations due primarily to significant sales force realignment, with 25% of territory managers hired between December and March causing disruption in 'dabbler' accounts. Full-year 2025 guidance was lowered to $55-$58 million revenue (down from prior implied higher levels) while maintaining gross margin guidance at 83-84%. Q2 guidance is set at $13-$14 million.

negative_highlights: Three major offshore fields impacted by mechanical issues, volumes below normalized levels
Incremental segment margin from new projects dependent on producers hitting their numbers
No significant market impact yet from new leasing program—opportunities years away
positive_highlights: Shenandoah FPU moored, SYNC pipeline commissioning by end of May, first oil expected in June
Marine Transportation on pace to post record earnings in 2025
Cash costs reduced to $425-450 million per year from soda ash sale
summary: Genesis Energy exited its soda ash business, using proceeds to reduce debt and lower annual cash costs to $425-450 million. Offshore pipeline volumes declined due to producer mechanical issues but are expected to normalize by Q3, with Shenandoah and Salamanca startups on track and new tiebacks adding volumes. Marine Transportation is on pace for record earnings in 2025, and the company plans to allocate excess cash to redeeming preferred units, debt reduction, and potential unitholder returns.

negative_highlights: Adjusted loss from operations swung to -$0.9 million from +$5.7 million in the prior-year period
Gross margin fell to 36.1% from 40.5%, a 440 bps contraction driven by customer and product mix
Full-year 2025 guidance withheld due to tariff and macro visibility; Investor Day also cancelled
positive_highlights: E-commerce, dollar channel, and club channels posted strong gains on new product introductions, offsetting part of the mass-channel decline
International gross margin held solid at 35.3% with revenue roughly flat YoY despite challenging end markets
Identified and eliminated over $10 million in annualized costs; liquidity of approximately $90 million at quarter end
summary: Lifetime Brands reported Q1 FY2025 consolidated sales of $140.1 million, down 1.5% YoY, with the U.S. segment also down 1.5% to $128.5 million. GAAP net loss was $4.2 million ($0.19/sh), though the adjusted net loss widened to $5.3 million ($0.25/sh) from $3.2 million ($0.15/sh) a year earlier, and gross margin contracted to 36.1% from 40.5% on customer and product mix. Management declined to issue full-year 2025 guidance, citing lack of tariff visibility, and also pulled back from a formal Investor Day. The company identified over $10 million in annualized cost cuts, is on track to move 80% of manufacturing out of China by end-2025, and is implementing price increases of 6-16% effective May 15 to offset tariffs.

negative_highlights: GAAP net income guidance was cut significantly from the prior high of $38.8M down to a new range top of $34M.
Adjusted EBITDA turned negative at -$12.5M compared to +$2.6M in Q1 2024, driven by a $6.6 million write-down on assets held for sale and product expiration.
Advanced Wound Care revenue declined 23% due to the delayed LCD implementation causing customer confusion and inventory expiry.
positive_highlights: Revenue delivered in line with the previously issued guidance range despite significant market uncertainty.
Surgical and Sports Medicine segment revenue grew 11% year-over-year, providing a partial offset to Advanced Wound Care declines.
Management reaffirmed confidence in executing strategy post-LCD delay due to portfolio optionality.
summary: First quarter net revenue was $86.7 million, down 21% year-over-year due to customer demand disruption and product expiration from LCD delays, though results were in line with prior guidance range of $85-95M. Management reaffirmed full-year 2025 revenue guidance but lowered profitability expectations significantly, narrowing GAAP net income guidance by approximately half (from a high of ~$38.8M to a new high of $34M) and reducing EBITDA guidance similarly due to Q1 write-downs and margin pressure from excess inventory.

negative_highlights: First-half 2025 revenue guidance cut to down 10-15% from previous down 5-10%
Revenue fell 21.4% to $61.4 million with GAAP diluted EPS down to $0.25 from $0.43
No formal full-year 2025 revenue guidance reiterated due to macro uncertainty, and operating margin contracted to 4.6% from 6.1%
positive_highlights: Gross margin expanded 220 bps YoY to 19.2% and 340 bps sequentially despite a 21.4% revenue decline
Secured over $15 million in annual new business, including $10 million in building products and $5 million in EV battery
Free cash flow of $4.3 million on $6.1 million operating cash flow, with $94.5 million total liquidity and debt/TTM EBITDA under 1x
summary: Q1 net sales fell 21.4% YoY to $61.4 million, which management said was anticipated, driven by lower medium/heavy-duty truck and power sports demand. GAAP diluted EPS was $0.25 versus $0.43, or $0.29 ex-severance, while gross margin expanded 220 bps YoY to 19.2% and adjusted EBITDA margin rose to 11.7%. First-half revenue guidance was cut to down 10-15% from prior down 5-10% on tooling timing shifting to H2 and weaker heavy/medium-duty truck demand, and no formal full-year revenue guidance was given, though full-year gross margin is expected at 17-19%. Free cash flow was $4.3 million and the company repurchased about 63,000 shares in the quarter.

negative_highlights: Marketplace revenue declined due to intentional reduction in marketing spend
BNPL originations dipped due to seasonal shift and tightened underwriting
Fintech revenue ramp expected later in year, not immediate
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 95% YoY to $6.75 million
Operating expenses decreased 10% YoY while revenue nearly doubled
Received largest-ever $2 million bulk order from Pregnancy Resource Center coalition
summary: PSQ Holdings reported Q1 FY2025 revenue of $6.75 million, up 95% year over year, with fintech contributing $3.05 million, marketplace adding $0.4 million, and brands (EveryLife) $3.27 million. Operating expenses decreased 10% year over year to $14 million, and total margin expanded to 58% from 43%. The company highlights strong fintech onboarding, a $2 million recurring bulk order for EveryLife, and expects revenue ramp in Q3 and Q4, while noting a deliberate reduction in marketplace marketing led to lower marketplace revenue. Fintech underwriting was tightened due to a soft consumer credit environment.

negative_highlights: Q1 revenue was impacted by delayed carrier mobile broadband promotions, lower FWA purchases from a key customer transitioning inventory, and the end of a special national program.
Mobile hotspot promotion started later than anticipated in Q1.
Gross margin expected to moderate to high-30s in Q2 due to higher product revenue mix.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA of $3.7 million exceeded expectations for a fourth consecutive quarter.
Non-GAAP gross margin expanded to a record 47.5% driven by favorable revenue mix and sequential expansion.
Services revenue grew nearly 50% year-over-year on the strength of SaaS platforms.
summary: Inseego delivered Q1 FY2025 revenue within guidance and adjusted EBITDA of $3.7 million (up from the prior year quarter), driven by a record non-GAAP gross margin of 47.5% despite lower FWA purchases during a transition period. Management provided Q2 2025 guidance for total revenue between $37M-$40M and adjusted EBITDA between $2.5M-$3.5M, noting that sequential growth is expected to begin in Q2 as the company transitions from record prior-year levels.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined 12.6% (0.9% adjusted for the Easter shift), led by an 18.2% drop in Gourmet Foods and Gift Baskets
Adjusted EBITDA loss widened to $34.9 million from a $5.7 million loss a year ago; adjusted gross margin fell 350 bps to 33.1%
