Full-year guidance was withdrawn, and the OMS implementation was estimated at $20+ million of lost top line plus ~$11 million of incremental costs across two quarters
positive_highlights: BloomNet segment revenue grew 4.5%, the only segment to expand
Valentine's Day holiday demand held up, and higher-end $500-$1,500 price points sold out
Planned $40 million annualized cost reductions, with $17 million already executed
summary: Q3 FY2025 revenue fell 12.6% to a comparable-period decline, with Consumer Floral/Gift down 11.4%, Gourmet Foods down 18.2%, and BloomNet up 4.5%; adjusted gross margin contracted 350 bps to 33.1% and adjusted EBITDA swung to a $34.9 million loss from a $5.7 million loss a year ago. Management withdrew all guidance, citing tariff and consumer-sentiment uncertainty, and disclosed OMS implementation costs plus roughly $40 million in planned annualized cost cuts ($17 million already executed). The company announced a new multiyear 'Celebrations Wave' strategy and named Adolfo Villagomez CEO, while disclosing tariff exposure estimated at about $55 million.

negative_highlights: Revenue fell to $42.9 million from $72.6 million a year earlier on delayed India biodiesel contracts
Operating loss of $15.6 million and net loss of $24.5 million, with interest expense of $13.7 million
Cash balance of only $500,000 at quarter end after $15.4 million of debt repayment
positive_highlights: India biodiesel deliveries resumed in April with a $31 million order running through July after a six-month OMC purchasing pause
Keyes ethanol revenue rose $1.7 million on stronger pricing and RNG volumes grew 17% year over year
Received $19 million cash from investment tax credit sales in Q1 and expects additional ITC and 45Z sales during 2025
summary: Aemetis reported Q1 2025 revenue of $42.9 million, down sharply from $72.6 million a year earlier due to a six-month pause in India OMC biodiesel purchases, with an operating loss of $15.6 million and a net loss of $24.5 million (roughly flat YoY). Interest expense was $13.7 million and cash ended the quarter at just $500,000 after $15.4 million of debt repayment. Management framed the miss as timing-driven, citing resumed India shipments in April, expected RNG revenue starting Q3 upon CARB LCFS pathway approvals, and monetization of 45Z and additional ITC credits as the basis for a stronger second half of 2025, but offered no explicit numeric guidance. The tone is forward-looking and reassuring, though the reported quarter itself was weak.

negative_highlights: Consolidated gross margin contracted by approximately 50 basis points due to commodity input costs (nitrile) and adverse foreign currency rates.
Products & Healthcare Services revenue declined 0.8% YoY, with tariffs expected to impact annual exposure between $100M-$150M requiring price increases in June.
Q1 cash flow was the weakest of the year due to working capital consumption for inventory and costs related to Rotech acquisition discussions.
positive_highlights: Patient Direct revenue grew by 6% YoY, with sleep supplies showing high single-digit growth and oxygen therapy seeing continued recovery.
Adjusted operating income for Patient Direct expanded significantly by 31%, driven by improved collection rates and category expansion in wound/ostomy/urology.
Management reaffirmed full-year guidance despite the tariff headwinds and potential distraction from the P&HS segment sale process.
summary: Owens & Minor reported Q1 FY2025 revenue of $2.6 billion (up ~1% YoY) and adjusted net income of $18 million ($0.23/share), beating expectations with a solid beat in the Patient Direct segment which grew 6%. Management reaffirmed full-year guidance despite acknowledging significant tariff exposure estimated between $100M-$150M, primarily impacting the Products & Healthcare Services (P&HS) segment where price increases are scheduled for early June. The company noted that Q1 cash flow was weaker than usual due to inventory build and acquisition costs but expects marked improvement in subsequent quarters.

negative_highlights: Full-year revenue guidance was widened to reflect downside risks from tariffs and macroeconomic uncertainty.
Management explicitly stated that the first half of 2025 is expected to be challenging due to transformation costs and external headwinds.
Potential tariff impacts on customer supply chains remain a 'wait-and-see' risk with no material impact seen yet but acknowledged as a downside factor.
positive_highlights: Non-GAAP gross margin strengthened significantly to 80.3%, up 240 basis points year-over-year.
Pipeline growth is particularly strong in the B2B segment following sales organization realignment.
ARR reached $351 million, a 3% increase year-over-year.
summary: BigCommerce reported Q1 FY2025 revenue of $82.4 million (3% YoY) and non-GAAP operating income of $7.6 million with a margin expansion to 9.2%. Management delivered results within the previously issued guidance range but widened full-year 2025 revenue guidance from $315M-$335M to $335.1M-$351.1M and non-GAAP operating income guidance due to macroeconomic uncertainty, tariffs, and potential consumer spending shifts.

negative_highlights: Net investment income declined quarter-over-quarter due to one-time expenses and lower base rates
NAV per share declined to $17.96 from $18.18
One portfolio company was placed on non-accrual status during the quarter
positive_highlights: Net investment income excluding non-recurring items was $0.56 per share, in line with Q4 2024
Portfolio remains highly diversified with non-accruals at 0.4% of fair value
Platform investment activity up 60% year over year in Q1
summary: Nuveen Churchill Direct Lending Corp reported Q1 2025 net investment income of $0.53 per share, or $0.56 excluding one-time expenses, in line with Q4 2024. Total investment income declined to $53.6 million due to lower base rates. NAV fell to $17.96 from $18.18, driven by valuation declines in watch list names. Management expressed confidence in navigating tariff-related volatility, citing portfolio insulation and a strong pipeline.

negative_highlights: Loss ratio includes $10 million in Southern California wildfire losses
Q1 operating margins only 8% due to seasonality and tech investments
Guidance reaffirmed but not raised despite strong quarter
positive_highlights: Total revenue up 18% to $320 million
Net income up 233% and adjusted EBITDA up 45%
Membership, Marketplace and Other revenue grew 60%
summary: In Q1 2025, Hagerty reported total revenue of $320 million, up 18%, with net income of $27 million, a 233% increase, and adjusted EBITDA of $40 million, up 45%. Written premium grew 12% and commission revenue grew 13%, while membership, marketplace and other revenue jumped 60% due to strong auction results. Operating margins expanded 360 basis points to 8% despite $10 million in wildfire losses. Management reaffirmed 2025 guidance of 12-13% revenue growth and adjusted EBITDA of $150-160 million, noting technology transformation spending is on track.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to $10.7 million from $6.6 million
Operating expenses increased to $13 million from $8.7 million
Revenue pipeline expected to be back-end loaded with limited near-term deal visibility
positive_highlights: Revenue up 82% YoY to $2.6 million
Gross margin up to 71% from 60%
CAPTAIN trial demonstrates TULSA has no blood loss and no overnight stay versus robotic prostatectomy
summary: Q1 FY2025 revenue was $2.6 million, up 82% year-over-year, with gross margin improving to 71% from 60%. Net loss widened to $10.7 million from $6.6 million, with operating expenses up to $13 million from $8.7 million. Management highlighted the CAPTAIN trial data at AUA showing TULSA advantages over robotic prostatectomy, new TULSA AI BPH module release plans, and reimbursement catalyst, but reiterated a back-end loaded revenue pipeline for the year.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined year-over-year by 10% with paid employers down 11%.
Adjusted EBITDA margin contracted sharply from 17% in Q1 '24 to just 5%.
Net loss widened materially from $6.5 million in Q1 '24 to $12.8 million.
positive_highlights: Sequential revenue decline narrowed significantly from -13% in Q1 '23 and -10% in Q1 '24 to just -1%, indicating stabilization after holiday seasonality.
summary: Q1 FY2025 revenue was $110 million, representing a 1% sequential decline and a 10% year-over-year decrease compared to Q4 '24 ($111M) and Q1 '24 respectively. Adjusted EBITDA margin contracted significantly from 17% in the prior year quarter to 5%, while net loss widened to $12.8 million. Management provided Q2 guidance of $111 million at the midpoint, maintaining a cautious outlook due to macroeconomic uncertainty despite sequential growth.

negative_highlights: OEM channel revenue down 23% due to lower J&J pricing and contractually obligated rebates
Adjusted EBITDA guidance cut from 8%-10% to -3% to +3% due to pricing, manufacturing yields, tariffs, and Cingal study costs
Manufacturing yield issues for Monovisc and Cingal led to higher scrap and lower gross margin, with full-year gross margin expected to be lower
positive_highlights: Commercial channel revenue up 18% YoY, with Integrity driving 33% growth in regenerative solutions portfolio
Operating expenses down 12% YoY due to cost savings and headcount reductions
Achieved FDA alignment on Cingal bioequivalence study design, with study expected to start by year-end
summary: Anika's Q1 2025 revenue was $26.2M, down 10% YoY, with commercial channel up 18% to $11.3M and OEM channel down 23% to $14.9M due to J&J pricing pressure. Adjusted EBITDA was essentially breakeven at $100K, down from $2.7M, and gross margin fell to 56%. The company lowered full-year OEM guidance to $62M-$65M and adjusted EBITDA guidance to -3% to +3%, citing lower pricing, manufacturing yield issues, tariffs, and Cingal study costs. Management expects gross margin improvement in H2 2025 to 58%-59% and continues to see strong Integrity growth.

negative_highlights: Total prescriptions declined approximately 9% quarter-over-quarter and 8% year-over-year.
Q1 net income of $3M ($0.06/share) was significantly lower than Q4 2024's $19.3M, partly due to a one-time noncash deferred tax benefit in the prior quarter.
Cash burn increased from approximately $4.3 million earned in Q4 2024 to approximately $7.8 million burned in Q1 2025.
positive_highlights: New prescriptions increased approximately 6% quarter-over-quarter despite a decline in total prescriptions of 9% QoQ.
Demand grew about 4% quarter-over-quarter and 14% year-over-year specifically within the specialty distributor channel.
Phase I trial data for neratinib + Enhertu showed tumor regression in advanced pancreatic cancer patients, with Dose Level 3 selected as Recommended Phase II dose.
summary: Puma Biotechnology reported Q1 FY2025 net product revenue of $43.1 million, a decline from the prior quarter's $54.4 million and an increase year-over-year to $40.3 million. The quarterly miss was driven by approximately $4.7 million in inventory drawdown at specialty pharmacies and distributors rather than demand weakness alone. Management provided full-year 2025 guidance for net NERLYNX revenue between $192M-$198M, which is lower than the prior year due to expected reduced shipments from China.

negative_highlights: Book value per share fell to negative $42.22 from negative $40.99
PREPA exposure remains large and timing of resolution uncertain
Foreign exchange losses and investment fair value losses partially offset improvements
positive_highlights: GAAP net loss improved to $62 million from $86 million year-over-year
Adjusted net loss narrowed to $8 million from $24 million
National and MBIA Insurance Corp both reported statutory net income in Q1 2025 versus losses in Q1 2024
summary: MBIA reported a Q1 2025 GAAP net loss of $62 million (negative $1.28 per share), improved from an $86 million loss ($1.84 per share) in Q1 2024, with adjusted net loss narrowing to $8 million from $24 million. Losses improved due to lower PREPA-related losses and reduced operating expenses, but were partially offset by foreign exchange losses and higher RMBS losses. Book value per share deteriorated to negative $42.22 from negative $40.99. PREPA resolution remains uncertain, though the company notes litigation stays have been lifted and expresses cautious optimism about progress.

negative_highlights: Q2 adjusted EBITDA guidance of $7–8 million is below Q1's $7.4 million at the midpoint
Europe revenue down 13% and Asia Pacific down 15% year-over-year
CEO noted 'given the macro uncertainty, we will remain conservative in our outlook' and does not expect growth in Europe in Q2
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA up 68% to $7.4 million with margin expanding 554 bps to 12.4%
Americas revenue up 17% to $41 million, the largest year-over-year growth in that region in two years
Consulting utilization improved to 77.7% from 70.2% a year ago
summary: ISG reported Q1 FY2025 revenue of $59.6 million, up 5% excluding the divested automation unit, with Americas revenue up 17% to $41 million but Europe down 13% and Asia Pacific down 15%. Adjusted EBITDA rose 68% to $7.4 million, margin expanded 554 bps to 12.4%, and adjusted EPS was $0.07 versus $0.01 last year. Management guided Q2 revenue to $59.5–60.5 million and adjusted EBITDA to $7–8 million, below the Q1 EBITDA level, citing macro uncertainty and a slower European recovery expected in the second half. The quarter showed strong Americas growth and margin expansion, but guidance implies a sequential EBITDA decline and Europe/APAC remain weak.

negative_highlights: GAAP net loss widened to $14.9 million, impacted by $7.8 million in non-recurring Abliva acquisition expenses and foreign exchange/tax items
Joenja revenue growth was 9%, dampened by prior-quarter stocking and higher gross-to-net adjustments
Cash and marketable securities fell $60.5 million to $108.9 million, primarily due to the $66.1 million Abliva share purchase
positive_highlights: Total revenues increased 42% year over year, driven by RUCONEST growth of 49% to $68.6 million
Full-year 2025 revenue guidance raised to $325-$340 million from $315-$335 million
Gross margin improved 4 percentage points to 89%, and adjusted operating profit was $0.8 million excluding Abliva costs
summary: Pharming reported Q1 2025 total revenues up 42% year over year, with RUCONEST growing 49% to $68.6 million and Joenja up 9% to $10.5 million. Gross margin improved to 89%, and adjusted operating profit was $0.8 million excluding $7.8 million in non-recurring Abliva acquisition costs; GAAP net loss was $14.9 million. Management raised full-year 2025 revenue guidance to $325-$340 million from $315-$335 million, implying 9-14% growth, and announced a $10 million annual G&A cost reduction. Joenja added six new U.S. patients, the largest quarterly increase since Q2 2024, with three growth catalysts expected in the second half.

negative_highlights: Q2 GAAP gross margin guided to 32–33.5%, down from 39.8% in Q1 due to lower-margin DMDC and secure networks mix
Q2 adjusted EBITDA guided to a loss of $2.1 million to $600,000
About 600 basis points of first-half-to-second-half cash gross margin dilution expected, and secure networks revenue guided to contract low 60% to mid 70% year-over-year in Q2
positive_highlights: Q1 revenue of $30.6 million exceeded guidance, with 16% sequential growth and 3% year-over-year growth
Adjusted EBITDA of $362,000 beat the guided range of a $1.8 million to $800,000 loss
Cash gross margin expanded 313 basis points year-over-year and free cash flow was positive $3.8 million versus a $7.4 million year-over-year improvement
summary: Telos reported Q1 FY2025 revenue of $30.6 million, up 16% sequentially and 3% year-over-year, exceeding its own revenue and profit guidance with adjusted EBITDA of $362,000 versus a guided loss and positive free cash flow of $3.8 million. Security solutions grew 39% year-over-year to $25.8 million (84% of revenue) on the DMDC and TSA PreCheck ramps, while secure networks contracted. Q2 guidance calls for revenue of $32.5–34.5 million (14–21% YoY growth) but a lower GAAP gross margin of 32–33.5% and an adjusted EBITDA loss of $2.1 million to $600,000, with management flagging roughly 600 basis points of first-half-to-second-half cash gross margin dilution from lower-margin DMDC revenue streams. The full-year outlook was unchanged, and management expects year-over-year growth in revenue, adjusted EBITDA, and cash flow to accelerate in the second half.

negative_highlights: Q4 expected to show a small net loss, and the July 2024 rate increase plus MVP shipper agreements create no corresponding lift in the fourth quarter
$26.6 million of midstream debt is classified as current and pending refinancing by December 31, 2025
Capex fell ~5% to $10.7 million in the first half amid weather-driven delays in Franklin County; management flagged tariff-related macro uncertainty for its largest industrial customers
positive_highlights: EPS of $0.74 rose 17% YoY and first-half EPS of $1.26 rose 11% YoY
FY2025 EPS guidance raised to a $1.22-$1.27 range
Total delivered gas volumes up 20% in the quarter and 18% in the first half; 2.7 main miles installed already exceeds full FY2024
summary: RGC Resources reported Q2 FY2025 net income of $7.7 million, or $0.74 per share, up 17% from $6.4 million or $0.63 a year ago, driven by higher Roanoke Gas margins from rate increases that overcame lower MVP affiliate earnings and higher interest expense. First-half EPS rose 11% to $1.26 from $1.14, with total delivered volumes up 20% in the quarter and 18% year-to-date on a fuel-switching industrial customer and heating degree days up 21%. Management raised FY2025 EPS guidance to a $1.22-$1.27 range and expects a small net loss in Q4, while noting the July 2024 rate lift and MVP shipper agreements will not repeat as tailwinds in the fourth quarter. The company carries $26.6 million of midstream debt classified as current and expects to refinance before its December 31, 2025 maturity.

negative_highlights: Cash, cash equivalents, and note weakness in-term deposits declined from $131 million at end of Q4 to $112.5 million by March 31.
Working capital decreased slightly to $119.8 million compared to the prior quarter's $133.6 million.
Management stated it is too early to estimate direct or indirect impacts from new tariffs on operations.
positive_highlights: Revenue of $16.8 million exceeded the top end of prior guidance range ($16.3M to $16.6M).
GAAP gross margin expanded significantly to 62.9%, driven by automotive optimization and CIB inventory adjustments.
Secured a major design win with Mobileye for in-car sensor connectivity infrastructure.
summary: Valens Semiconductor reported Q1 FY2025 revenue of $16.8 million, exceeding the top end of guidance ($16.3M-$16.6M), with GAAP gross margin expanding to 62.9% and adjusted EBITDA loss narrowing to $4.3 million within expectations. Management highlighted significant automotive design wins including a partnership with Mobileye for EyeQ6 programs, while noting that Q2 revenue guidance remains unchanged at $16.5M-$16.8M despite ongoing tariff monitoring.

negative_highlights: Q2 GMV guided to $85-92M, down 7% to up 1%, on a conversion step-down from March to April that is expected to persist through the quarter
Unique sellers fell 23% YoY to ~5,900 due to elevated churn from subscription-pricing changes, though flat sequentially
Q2 adjusted EBITDA margin guided to a loss of 14-10%, reflecting gross margins toward the lower end of the 71-73% range and a full quarter of merit-increase costs
positive_highlights: GMV and revenue exceeded the midpoint of guidance and adjusted EBITDA margin exceeded the high end, with a loss of 8%
Active buyers rose 7% to ~64,800, the fourth consecutive quarter of sequential growth, and conversion grew YoY for a sixth straight quarter
Listings rose 5% to over 1.8M and 1stdibs became sellers' primary sales channel, surpassing their own showrooms for the first time
summary: Q1 GMV of $94.7M rose 3% and net revenue of $22.5M rose 2%, both above the midpoint of guidance, with adjusted EBITDA margin loss of 8% better than the high end of guidance. Gross margin held flat at 72% and active buyers grew 7% to ~64,800, while unique sellers fell 23% to ~5,900 on subscription-pricing churn. Q2 guidance calls for GMV of $85-92M (down 7% to up 1%) and adjusted EBITDA margin loss of 10-14%, citing a step-down in conversion from March to April concentrated in consumer furniture, softening AOV and macro-driven consumer caution. Management flagged evolving trade policy and secondary macro effects as a wide range of potential outcomes, though it noted limited direct tariff exposure.

negative_highlights: Realized RIN pricing fell 24.3% to $2.46 due to EPA regulatory delays extending the compliance period.
Operating income declined significantly from $2.4 million to $0.4 million, with a $2.0 million impairment recorded at the Blue Granite project.
Utility in February 2025 announced it would no longer accept RNG into its distribution system, contradicting previous letters of intent.
positive_highlights: Total revenue increased 9.8% to $42.6 million due to monetization of prior period RIN inventory.
RNG production volumes remained flat at 1.4 million MMBtu despite equipment failures and weather impacts.
Second Apex facility expected to complete commissioning in Q2 2025.
summary: Total revenues were $42.6 million in Q1 FY2025, a 9.8% increase driven by watching an additional 2.0 million RINs from prior period inventory, partially offset by a 24.3% decline in realized RIN pricing to $2.46. Adjusted EBITDA decreased 7.2% to $8.8 million and net loss was $0.5 million compared to net income of $1.9 million last year due to lower margins, higher O&M expenses, and a $2.0 million impairment at the Blue Granite project. Management reaffirmed full-year 2025 guidance for RNG production (5.8-6.0 million MMBtu) and revenues ($150-170 million), citing regulatory delays and utility acceptance issues as headwinds.

negative_highlights: Equity-method investment adjusted EBITDA fell to $3.4M from $6.5M, cited to prior-year RIN sale timing and startup expenses at new JVs
Q2 realized RIN price expected to be lower than Q1's ~$2.71/gal
Trade-policy uncertainty delaying investment decisions among logistics and trucking fleet customers; CNG/RNG heavy-duty adoption acceleration not yet visible
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA of $20.1M, over 30% higher YoY versus $15.2M
Fuel Station Services segment EBITDA ~$12.5M, 80% higher than Q1 2024
RNG production of 1.1M MMBtus, up nearly 40% YoY and in line with expectations
summary: Q1 2025 revenue rose to $85.0M from $64.9M and adjusted EBITDA to $20.1M from $15.2M, with net income of $1.3M versus $0.7M; RNG production of 1.1M MMBtu was up ~38-40% YoY and in line with expectations, while Fuel Station Services EBITDA grew ~80% to ~$12.5M. Management maintained full-year guidance of $90-110M adjusted EBITDA, 5.0-5.4M MMBtu RNG production (midpoint +37%), and 30-50% FFS EBITDA growth, assuming $2.60/gal D3 RINs. Offsets: equity-method adjusted EBITDA fell to $3.4M from $6.5M, realized RIN price of ~$2.71 will be lower in Q2, and trade-policy uncertainty is delaying customer investment decisions and CNG/RNG trucking adoption. Overall the quarter was described as in line, with sequential RNG production growth expected through the year.

negative_highlights: Total annuity sales declined 21% year-over-year, driven by lower fixed annuity sales
Corporate expenses were $239 million pre-tax, above run-rate (though non-trendable)
Alternative investment income was $39 million, about $0.66 below run-rate, with yield at 1.4%
positive_highlights: Holding company liquid assets were approximately $1 billion at March 31
Shield sales reached approximately $2 billion, up 3% sequentially and 5% year-over-year
Life insurance sales grew 24% year-over-year to $36 million
summary: Q1 2025 adjusted earnings were $235M including a $10M notable item; excluding that, $245M versus $268M a year ago and $352M in Q4 2024, about $15M/0.26 below run-rate. Statutory results were in line, with RBC estimated at 420-440% and holding company liquid assets near $1B. Annuity sales were $2.3B, down 21% YoY on lower fixed annuity sales, while Shield sales grew 5% YoY and life sales rose 24% YoY. Management confirmed the mid-year target for updated statutory free cash flow projections is no longer realistic and declined to give a new date.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined sequentially by 7% YoY by 12%, with Rockies revenue down 5% due to seasonality and operational downtime
Mid-Con segment missed approximately $6-7M of scheduled completions revenue due to an unforeseen operational issue driving material downtime for one frac fleet
Management explicitly stated it is difficult or impossible to provide full-year guidance, limiting forward visibility
positive_highlights: Southwest segment adjusted EBITDA reached its highest level since Q3 2023 at $11.7 million
Adjusted SG&A reduced by 12% YoY to $16.5M (excluding non-recurring items) due to cost controls and headcount reduction
New debt structure provides flexibility via PIK interest option, utilized in April during market uncertainty
summary: Q1 FY2025 revenue was $154 million (down 12% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA was $13.8 million with a 9% margin; results were in line with guidance despite sequential declines driven by seasonality and an operational issue costing $6-7M of Mid-Con completions revenue. Management provided Q2 guidance for low to mid-single digit revenue growth, citing continued Southwest strength but maintaining caution due to macro volatility and potential second-half rig count reductions.

negative_highlights: Pro forma full-quarter revenue is estimated to be down approximately 7% YoY due to the timing of the acquisition.
Management cites shortening advertiser planning and note cycles as a potential headwind.
Q2 adjusted EBITDA guidance range ($26M-$34M) reflects conservative assumptions regarding synergy capture and cross-note ramp-up.
positive_highlights: Achieved Q1 guidance for Ex-TAC gross profit and adjusted EBITDA despite the mid-quarter acquisition closing.
Legacy Teads business showed improvement in trends since deal closing, reversing Q4 headwinds.
CTV revenue grew over 50% year over year, now representing approximately 5% of total ad spend.
summary: Outbrain reported Q1 FY2025 revenue of approximately $286 million (up 32% YoY as-reported) and Ex-TAC gross profit of $103.1 million (up 98% YoY), driven primarily by the February acquisition of Teads. Management achieved its Q1 guidance for Ex-TAC gross profit and adjusted EBITDA, though they provided a wider range for Q2 guidance ($141M-$150M) citing macro uncertainty and shortening advertiser planning cycles. The company expects to realize approximately $40 million in cost synergies for full-year 2025, an increase from prior expectations.

negative_highlights: Office segment NOI declined due to a large tenant exercising a partial lease termination option in Oakland.
Multifamily segment reported an operating loss of $620,000 driven by unrealized losses on joint venture investments.
Lending division NOI decreased primarily due to loan payoffs and lower interest rates.
positive_highlights: Fully repaid and retired the $169 million recourse corporate level credit facility, enhancing balance sheet liquidity.
Hotel segment NOI increased 15% year-over-year to $4.7 million following renovation completion.
Multifamily occupancy at 701 South Hudson rose significantly from 22% at year-end to 41% by quarter end.
summary: Q1 FY2025 segment NOI decreased by $1.8 million to $11.8 million compared to the prior year, driven by declines in office and multifamily segments partially offset by a hotel improvement. FFO was negative $5.4 million per share, an improvement from the prior year primarily due to lower preferred dividends rather than operational growth. Management highlighted the full retirement of the recourse credit facility and progress on multifamily lease-ups, while noting seasonal weakness in winter months.

negative_highlights: Cost of goods sold surged by $5.6 million (215%) year-over-year to $8.2 million, significantly compressing gross margins.
Management explicitly stated that future revenues from license/R&D services will be minimal following the linear amortization of prior development costs.
No financial guidance was provided for Q2 or full year 2025.
positive_highlights: Revenues from note goods increased by $6.3 million (70%) year-over-year to $10 million.
Phase one clinical trial for PRX-115 completed all cohorts with encouraging results showing dose-dependent reduction in plasma uric acid levels.
Commercial partner Chiesi reported strong sales efforts and patient recruitment pace exceeding expectations.
summary: Protalix BioTherapeutics reported Q1 FY2025 revenues of $10 million from watching goods and $100,000 from license/R&D services, representing a 70% year-over-year increase in product sales. The company recorded a net loss of approximately $3.6 million for the quarter compared to $4.6 million in Q1 FY2024. Management provided no updated financial guidance and noted that future revenues will be minimal from license/R&D services, with potential regulatory milestones capped at an estimated $75 million.

negative_highlights: Expenses rose 9% YoY to $2.2 million more, outpacing 3.7% revenue growth and compressing margins; adjusted EBITDA margin was 20.7% of revenue
Total AUM declined in the quarter due to market volatility, and OCIO pipeline has slowed with no measurable progress
Management guided to continued market volatility pressuring note weakness in-term results and said normalized EBITDA margins in the high 20s/low 30s are not expected until at least through 2026
positive_highlights: New client organic flows of $0.4 billion in Q1 on top of $1.4 billion in Q4 2024, totaling $1.8 billion of new client accounts over two quarters
Completed a $12 million stock repurchase program and declared a $0.20 per share quarterly dividend
Global value strategy performance described as top-tier with good absolute returns despite volatile markets
summary: Silvercrest reported Q1 FY2025 revenue of $31.4 million, up 3.7% YoY, with reported net income of $3.9 million and adjusted diluted EPS of $0.27; expenses rose 9% YoY to outpace revenue growth. Total AUM fell during the quarter amid market volatility to $35.3 billion, with discretionary AUM at $22.7 billion, flat YoY. Management secured $0.4 billion in new client flows in the quarter after $1.4 billion in Q4 2024, but gave no formal numeric guidance and said continued volatility will pressure near-term revenue; margin recovery is not expected before the end of 2026. A $12 million buyback was completed and a $0.20 quarterly dividend declared.

negative_highlights: Total net revenue declined 10.1% year-over-year on an as-reported basis.
Consumer services revenue dollars declined 15% year-over-year.
National revenue excluding political declined 12.7%, with local agency revenue down 19.9%.
positive_highlights: Digital segment operating income grew meaningfully from $100,000 in Q1 '24 to $1.9 million in Q1 2025.
Digital segment operating margin expanded significantly on a same-station basis from 6.1% to 17.8%.
Adjusted EBITDA increased 28% year-over-year to $1.1 million despite lower revenues.
summary: Total net revenue was $48.9 million, down 10.1% year-over-year on an as-reported basis and 8.5% on a same-station basis, driven by softness in consumer services (-15%) and automotive (-5%). Operating income declined to a loss of $2 million from a loss of $1.1 million last year, though adjusted EBITDA improved to $1.1 million due to cost reductions and digital margin expansion. Management maintains Q2 revenue pacing at down 10% citing macroeconomic pressure but notes bright spots in Philadelphia and New Jersey.

negative_highlights: Core advertising revenue fell 3%, with automotive (low double-digits) and retail (mid-single digits) being the worst performers.
Local distribution revenue decreased 5% year-over-year, consistent with mid-single-digit subchurn trends expected to continue in Q2.
The company reported a $4 million restructuring charge that increased the loss per share by an additional $0.04.
positive_highlights: Scripps Networks achieved a record margin improvement of 870 basis points for Q1, significantly exceeding guidance of 400-600 bps.
Connected TV revenue grew strongly by 42% driven by effective sales strategies and the NWSL/WNBA partnerships.
The company successfully completed refinancing transactions to retire or extend up to $1.5 billion in debt.
summary: First quarter revenue declined approximately 1% year-over-year due to a 3% drop in core advertising and a 5% decline in local distribution revenue driven by economic uncertainty. While Scripps Networks delivered its highest margins since Q4 2022 at 32%, the company reported an EPS loss of $0.22, which was slightly better than consensus but still negative due to preferred dividends and restructuring charges.

negative_highlights: Company remains unprofitable with a net loss of $177,687 in Q1 2025
No formal financial guidance was provided, and timing for the black particle and retrofit architectural launch remains unspecified
Architectural market revenue progress is dependent on a retrofit application not yet launched, with strong second-half expectations from a licensee
positive_highlights: Royalty revenue grew over 79% YoY to $560,000 and 214% sequentially from Q4 2024
Automotive royalties rose 128% YoY and 267% QoQ, with production call-outs pointing to significantly higher GM royalties in Q2 2025
Net loss narrowed 60% YoY to $177,687, with cash of $1.4 million and no debt expected to fund operations for more than five years
summary: Research Frontiers reported Q1 2025 royalty revenue of $560,000, up over 79% YoY and 214% sequentially, driven by automotive royalties that rose 128% YoY and 267% QoQ. Net loss narrowed to $177,687 ($0.01 per share), a 60% improvement from the prior-year quarter. Cash stood at approximately $1.4 million with no debt and working capital of $2.3 million; management expects cash to fund operations for more than five years and sees revenues increasing across all market segments as new car models launch. No formal guidance figures were provided, but management indicated a new European car model was added since the March call and that Q2 automotive royalties should rise on production call-outs from GM and Ferrari.

negative_highlights: Group reported a net loss of ZAR 311 million due to the mark-to-market adjustment on MobiKwik shares.
Enterprise division EBITDA declined to ZAR 2 million from ZAR 14 million last year due to restructuring costs and exit of legacy businesses.
Merchant prepaid solutions growth slowed to 4% year-on-year due to increased competition in airtime and data sales.
positive_highlights: Consumer division delivered a standout quarter with record EPE transactional account enrollments, lending, and insurance originations.
Net revenue increased 42% year-on-year driven by the inclusion of Adumo and a 32% increase in Consumer.
Debt refinance reduced weighted average cost of debt from approximately 12% to 10.7%, saving ZAR 52 million annually.
summary: Lesaka Tech reported Q3 FY2025 revenue of ZAR 2.5 billion and net revenue of ZAR 1.36 billion, achieving guidance across all metrics despite a one-off fair value loss of ZAR 311 million on MobiKwik. Group adjusted EBITDA was ZAR 237 million, meeting the upper end of guidance after excluding approximately ZAR 20 million in reorganization costs. Management reaffirmed full-year FY25 guidance and provided positive net income guidance for FY26.

negative_highlights: GAAP net loss of $0.56 per share and distributable loss of $0.25 per share in Q1
Discounted payoff of the $183M New York land loan at 90% of par and the $88M Houston office loan at 72% of UPB imply realized losses
Liquidity of only $136M and a Term Loan B maturing August 2026, with management anticipating a meaningful principal paydown
positive_highlights: $607M of proceeds from five loan resolutions realized through April 30, progressing toward the $2B annual realization target
Reduced hospitality exposure by $326M and resolved two watch list loans, cutting land and office exposure
$214M facility closed to finance non-performing loans and hold collateral as REO through foreclosure
summary: CMTG reported a Q1 2025 GAAP net loss of $0.56 per share and a distributable loss of $0.25 per share, with distributable earnings before realized losses of $0.08 per share; REO investments contributed a $0.03 loss. The held-for-investment loan portfolio fell to $5.9B from $6.1B, and total liquidity stood at $136M. Management realized $607M of proceeds from five loan resolutions through April 30 and is targeting $2B of realizations for the year, citing tariff and policy volatility that is slowing the real estate recovery. Subsequent to quarter end, $314M of loans repaid, including a discounted payoff of an $88M Houston office loan at 72% of UPB.

negative_highlights: G&A expense guidance increased to $7-8 million from $5-6 million due to stock-based compensation
NOPARK study results may take a year or more to be public after June completion
Concerns about marketplace competitors note ineffective NAD products
positive_highlights: Revenue up 38% year-over-year to $30.5 million, record quarter
Third consecutive quarter of net income, with $5.1 million net income versus $0.5 million net loss year ago
Full-year revenue growth guidance raised to 20-25% from approximately 18%
summary: Niagen Bioscience reported Q1 2025 revenue of $30.5 million, up 38% year-over-year, with net income of $5.1 million versus a net loss of $0.5 million in the prior year. Gross margin improved to 63.4% from 60.7%. Full-year revenue growth guidance was raised from approximately 18% to 20-25% year-over-year. The company also noted strong growth in e-commerce (up 31%) and ingredient sales (up 95%).

negative_highlights: IT, Life Sciences, and Data Solutions gross profit declined 5.3% YoY to $3.6 million
Health Care consolidated gross margin compressed slightly from 29.0% to 28.2%
Engineering normalized gross margins were lower than expected due to pass-through construction revenue
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA grew 14.4% YoY to $7.8 million
Health Care gross profit increased 10.2% driven by behavioral health expansion and school district growth
Engineering segment achieved its best quarter in history with a 12.4% increase in gross profit
summary: RCM Technologies reported Q1 FY2025 consolidated gross profit of $22.0 million (up 7.9% YoY) and Adjusted EPS of $0.63 (up 18.9% YoY). Management highlighted strong growth in Health Care (+10.2%) and Engineering (+12.4%), though IT/Life Sciences declined slightly (-5.3%). The company reduced net debt by $12.0 million to $18.2 million while retiring over 300,000 shares year-to-date.

negative_highlights: Q1 EPS of $0.19 below adjusted Q4 2024 EPS of $0.31
Demand response rollout slower than expected due to complexity
Higher SG&A and R&D expenses in the quarter
positive_highlights: Revenue up 45% to $3.1M, with hardware up 78%
Operating leverage: ~50% of incremental revenue drops to operating income
New Omni/OmniPro products launching in June, Nasdaq uplisting application filed
summary: Acorn Energy reported Q1 2025 revenue of $3.1 million, up 45% year-over-year, driven by a 78% increase in hardware revenue, largely from a major cell phone provider contract. Operating income increased by $526,000, with operating expenses declining to 56% of revenue from 71% a year ago. EPS rose to $0.19 from $0.03, though adjusted for tax and audit expenses it would be $0.27. The company is launching new Omni and OmniPro monitors in June and has filed to uplist to Nasdaq, expecting completion by Q3 2025.

negative_highlights: Net sales fell 5% to $68 million and diluted EPS fell to $0.57 from $0.69, with operating earnings down 15% to $7 million
Effective China tariff rate jumped to 161% from 16% in 2024; management said at plus 145% it is 'totally unmanageable' and could not predict margin impact
Nunn Bush sales down 16% and Stacy Adams down 7% amid soft non-athletic footwear demand and conservative retailer inventories; inventory of $68.2 million is above normal for the season
positive_highlights: Florsheim brand sales rose 7% in North America, with management citing market share gains in hybrid and refined casual footwear
Dividend raised 4% to $0.27 per share; paid $2.5 million in dividends and repurchased $700,000 of stock; no debt against a $40 million revolver
Florsheim Australia same-store retail sales up 11% and operating loss narrowed to $200,000 from $400,000
summary: Weyco reported Q1 FY2025 net sales of $68 million, down 5% from $71.6 million, with operating earnings down 15% to $7 million and diluted EPS of $0.57 versus $0.69 a year earlier. North American wholesale fell 4% to $54.3 million, retail dropped 12% to $8.7 million, and Florsheim Australia declined 7%. No explicit forward guidance was issued, but management flagged that China tariffs (161% effective rate) will significantly raise future COGS, mitigated by supplier cost cuts, planned summer price increases, a temporary import pause staged via Montreal, and accelerated sourcing diversification. The dividend was raised 4% to $0.27 per share.

negative_highlights: Still reporting GAAP net loss of $7 million for the quarter
Approximately 20% of Q1 revenue exposed to reciprocal tariffs (5% at 145%, 15% at 10%)
Cash remains low at $20.3 million and converting $50 million due early 2026
positive_highlights: Revenue up 92.2% YoY and 9.1% sequentially to $18.8 million
Gross margin expanded to 38.1% from 28.2% YoY
Adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed 67.4% to $2 million; targeting positive EBITDA in Q2
summary: Tigo Energy reported Q1 FY2025 revenue of $18.8 million, up 92.2% YoY and 9.1% sequentially, marking the fifth consecutive quarter of sequential growth. Gross margin improved to 38.1% from 28.2% a year ago, and adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed 67.4% to $2 million. For Q2 2025, the company guides revenue between $21 million and $23 million and adjusted EBITDA between negative $1.5 million and positive $500,000, reiterating full-year revenue guidance of $85-$100 million. Management cited broad geographic growth, tariff exposure limited to about 20% of Q1 revenue, and confidence in continued top-line growth.

negative_highlights: Total major units sold declined 20.5% year-over-year to 13,186, with new unit sales down 23.7%.
Wholesale Express revenue fell 61.5% and gross profit dropped 68.6% to $1.1 million, due to broker departures.
Cash outflows from operating activities were $6.9 million versus inflows of $17 million in the prior year period.
positive_highlights: Adjusted SG&A expenses were $57.5 million, down 20.8% year-over-year, and represented 85.6% of gross profit versus 87.9% a year ago.
New unit gross margin improved to 13.5% from 12.5% year-over-year, and total gross profit per unit rose 5.2% to $5,365.
Total available liquidity was $171.4 million as of March 31, 2025, including $56.2 million cash and $115.2 million floor plan availability.
summary: RumbleOn reported Q1 FY2025 revenue of $244.7 million and adjusted EBITDA of $7 million, a slight decline, as total major units sold fell 20.5% year-over-year to 13,186. Powersports revenue was $239.2 million, down 18.5%, while Wholesale Express revenue dropped 61.5% and gross profit fell 68.6%, which management attributed to broker departures. CEO Michael Quartieri highlighted a 20.8% reduction in adjusted SG&A and noted that excluding Wholesale Express underperformance, adjusted EBITDA would have increased year-over-year. The company ended the quarter with $56.2 million cash, $171.4 million total liquidity, and ongoing refinancing efforts; no explicit forward guidance was provided beyond inventory expectations to end the year roughly flat with 2024.

negative_highlights: Total revenue declined approximately 6% year-over-year due to fewer cattle moving through the system.
Net income dropped significantly to $31,000 ($0.01 per share) compared to $178,000 last year.
Revenue decline in verification and certification services was exacerbated by severe drought conditions and avian influenza outbreaks.
positive_highlights: Gross margins remained fairly stable at 41.6% despite significant headwinds and volume declines.
Upcycled Certified program accelerated to 10% growth in the first quarter after a 70% increase in 2024.
Customer retention rates held steady in the high 90% range.
summary: Total revenue declined approximately 6% year-over-year to $252,000 lower than the prior period, driven by a drop in verification and certification services due to herd size reduction and drought conditions. Net income fell to $31,000 ($0.01 per share) from $178,000 last year, with a $76,000 non-cash charge on digital assets accounting for more than half of the decline; adjusted results were deemed satisfactory by management. Gross margins remained stable at 41.6% despite lower volumes, while the company continued share buybacks totaling 31,345 shares.

negative_highlights: Full-year guidance was kept unchanged despite the strong quarter, with management saying any revision would only come after the second-semester intake
Pillar Two tax rules added R$23 million to income tax expense, pressuring net income growth
Monthly active users in Medical Practice Solutions fell to 245,000 from a record 263,000, reflecting a transition from the PEBMED portal to the Afya portal
positive_highlights: Net revenue rose 16% to R$936 million and adjusted EBITDA grew 24% to R$492 million, a record 52.5% margin, up 300 bps year over year
EPS increased 23% to R$2.79 and net income reached R$257 million, up 23%
Net debt fell R$291 million to R$1,524 million, and cash flow from operations grew nearly 10% to R$470 million with a 96.8% conversion rate
summary: Afya reported Q1 FY2025 net revenue of R$936 million, up 16% year over year, with adjusted EBITDA of R$492 million and a record 52.5% margin (up 300 bps). Net income rose 23% to R$257 million and EPS reached R$2.79, up 23%. Management kept full-year revenue and EBITDA guidance unchanged despite the strong start, citing the upcoming second-semester intake and a new Pillar Two tax that added R$23 million to income tax expense. Cash flow from operations rose nearly 10% to R$470 million with a 96.8% conversion rate, and net debt fell R$291 million to R$1,524 million.

negative_highlights: Full-year 2025 cash burn guidance raised to $27-29 million from prior $25 million
Net cash used in operating activities rose to $7.8 million in Q1 from $4.8 million in Q4 2024
Revenue was not disclosed, and management provided no revenue guidance, noting it wants to see more customer pipeline progress before giving guidance
positive_highlights: First Apollo units came off LITEON's manufacturing line, marking a milestone toward high-volume production
Two proof-of-concept contracts closed in intelligent transportation systems and defense markets, with over 20 further customer engagements active
Lease dispute resolution cut potential cash liability exposure from $6.4 million to $1.4 million, and GAAP opex fell to $6.8 million from $9 million sequentially
summary: AEye reported Q1 2025 GAAP operating expenses of $6.8 million, down from $9 million in Q4 2024, and a GAAP net loss of $8 million or $0.46 per share versus $8.5 million or $0.93 in the prior quarter. Cash burn excluding financing was $8 million, with Q1 net cash used in operations rising to $7.8 million from $4.8 million, and the company ended with $25.9 million in cash. Management raised full-year 2025 cash burn guidance to $27-29 million from a prior $25 million, citing lease dispute resolution and potential cash repayment of convertible obligations, though underlying operational burn is unchanged. Positives included the first Apollo units produced at LITEON, two proof-of-concept contracts signed, and a reduction of lease liability exposure from $6.4 million to $1.4 million.

negative_highlights: Reported net loss attributable to common stockholders of $2.5 million, or $0.04 per diluted share
Resort portfolio RevPAR growth decelerated to 1.9% with resort EBITDA up only 2%
Blended average interest rate of 7.1% with approximately 77% of debt effectively floating
positive_highlights: Comparable RevPAR of $404 rose 4.2% YoY, the highest quarterly RevPAR in company history
Urban portfolio RevPAR up 11.3% (8.1% excluding Capital Hilton's inauguration lift) and urban hotel EBITDA up 39%
Q1 group revenue increased 31% YoY, with 14 of 15 hotels posting group revenue growth and 2025/2026 group pace up 7%/10%
summary: Braemar reported Q1 FY2025 comparable RevPAR of $404, up 4.2% YoY and the highest quarterly RevPAR in company history, with comparable total hotel revenue up 4.4% and comparable hotel EBITDA of $70.8 million, up 5.3%. Urban hotels drove growth with RevPAR up 11.3% versus a 1.9% gain in resorts, and hotel EBITDA margin improved 34 bps. Net loss attributable to common stockholders was $2.5 million (−$0.04/share) with AFFO of $0.40/share, adjusted EBITDAre of $63 million, and net debt to gross assets of 42.3%. The company refinanced its final 2025 debt maturity with a $363 million loan at SOFR+2.52%, redeemed ~$90 million of preferred, and cited group pace up 7% for 2025 and 10% for 2026, with no formal forward guidance range provided.

negative_highlights: Revenue fell 11.2% YoY to $7.5 million and system-wide sales dropped to $118.4 million from $134 million
Adjusted EBITDA declined to $2.8 million from $3.4 million and margin contracted 300 bps to 37%
Adjusted diluted EPS fell to $0.13 from $0.15 and management said April demand showed no improvement, with the late-year pickup having stalled
positive_highlights: SG&A down 6.5% year-over-year to $5.3 million, with continued cost reduction initiatives
Adjusted EBITDA margin held at a high 37% despite the revenue decline
Management cited a strengthening M&A pipeline with more distressed sellers becoming realistic on price after nine muted quarters
summary: HireQuest reported Q1 FY2025 revenue of $7.5 million, down 11.2% YoY from $8.4 million, with franchise royalties falling to $7.0 million from $7.8 million and system-wide sales dropping to $118.4 million from $134 million. GAAP diluted EPS was $0.10 versus $0.12, adjusted EPS $0.13 versus $0.15, and adjusted EBITDA fell to $2.8 million (37% margin) from $3.4 million (40%). Management cited continued macro headwinds with no tangible change in April demand, though noted immigration enforcement as a potential tailwind and a strengthening, more realistically priced M&A pipeline; no formal guidance was provided. SG&A fell 6.5% YoY to $5.3 million, but sequential increases were attributed to professional fee timing and a small restructuring.

negative_highlights: Revenue fell year-over-year to $25.4 million, driven by loss of U.S. Coast Guard airtime revenue (~$2.5M/quarter last year, now under $100K/quarter)
Product gross profit was breakeven and expected to remain about breakeven
GEO bandwidth commitments run through end-2026 and will continue pressuring GEO margins; Starlink terminal access charges to be passed through later this year
positive_highlights: Subscribing vessels up 5% sequentially to more than 7,400, fully recovering the 2023-2024 decline
Airtime gross margin rose to 31.5% from 28.2% in Q4, and 44.1% vs 41.4% ex-depreciation, aided by a $1.4 million lower GEO bandwidth cost and strong LEO margins
Terminal shipments exceeded 1,300 units for a fifth consecutive record quarter, with product shipments up 33% from Q4 and active CommBox Edge subscribers up 35%
summary: KVH reported Q1 FY2025 revenue of $25.4 million, down year-over-year, primarily due to lower VSAT airtime revenue including the loss of the U.S. Coast Guard business (which was roughly $2.5 million/quarter in the first three quarters of 2024). Adjusted EBITDA was $1.0 million, or negative $0.1 million after $1.1 million of capex, versus negative $0.3 million in Q4 2024; ending cash was $48.6 million, down about $2 million. Growth metrics were strong: subscribing vessels rose 5% sequentially to more than 7,400 and terminal shipments exceeded 1,300 units for a fifth consecutive record quarter, while airtime gross margin rose to 31.5% from 28.2%. Management did not raise guidance, reiterated confidence in positive cash flow, and flagged continued GEO margin pressure through 2026 commitments; product gross profit was breakeven.

negative_highlights: Reported revenue growth was dampened by approximately $400,000 in foreign exchange headwinds.
Latin America volume declined slightly due to the acquisition of a top customer by another lab.
Liquid biopsy applications (MSK-ACCESS) are still in early stages with modest initial volumes expected to ramp in H2.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 15% on a constant currency basis to $17.8 million, reaccelerating growth after a slower prior period.
Adjusted gross margin expanded 273 bps year-over-year to a record 68.7% (IFRS) / 75.7% (non-IFRS).
Adjusted EBITDA loss improved 24% year-over-year to $9.8 million, demonstrating operational leverage.
summary: Q1 FY2025 revenue grew 13% year-over-year to $17.8 million on a reported basis (15% constant currency), driven by strong new business and U.S. market expansion. Adjusted gross margin expanded significantly to a record 75.7%, while adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed 24% year-over-year to $9.8 million. Management reaffirmed full-year 2025 revenue guidance of $72-76 million and adjusted EBITDA loss guidance of $35-39 million, noting that the quarter was slightly ahead of expectations but maintaining a back-half-weighted outlook.

negative_highlights: Total revenue declined 8% YoY due to a significant drop in instrument sales ($1.4M vs $1.9M).
SPL program-related revenue fell from $3.2 million in Q1 FY2024 to $2.1 million.
Customers are exhibiting hesitation and caution regarding capital equipment purchasing decisions.
positive_highlights: Core revenue remained flat at $8.2M despite a difficult macro environment for customers.
PA (processing assembly) revenue grew 13% year-over-year to $3.9 million driven by early-stage and clinical customer activity.
Management reaffirmed full-year guidance, indicating confidence in the pipeline despite current headwinds.
summary: MaxCyte reported Q1 FY2025 total revenue of $10.4 million, an 8% decline year-over-year driven by a drop in instrument sales to $1.4 million and lower SPL program-related revenue of $2.1 million compared to the prior year quarter. Gross margin contracted slightly to 86%, while operating expenses decreased from $22.2M to $21.2M following workforce reductions and operational streamlining. Management reaffirmed full-year guidance for core revenue growth (excluding SeQure Dx) of 8% to 15% and SPL program-related revenue of approximately $5 million, citing cautious customer capital spending but confidence in executing against the pipeline.

negative_highlights: Q2 revenue guidance of $138-148M implies a QoQ decline of up to 8%.
Pricing pressure emerging in Permian, especially in cementing, and lower stage pricing in Northeast wireline.
Tariffs expected to increase costs in wireline, coiled tubing, and tool components, with uncertain pass-through.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew ~6% QoQ to $150.5M, near the top of guidance, despite flat U.S. rig count.
Coiled tubing revenue grew ~16% QoQ on 36% more days worked.
Cementing jobs grew ~11% QoQ and completion tool revenue grew ~2% on Permian market share gains.
summary: Q1 2025 revenue was $150.5M, near the upper end of guidance ($146-152M) and up about 6% QoQ. Adjusted EBITDA was $16.5M, up about 17% QoQ. Segment growth was led by coiled tubing (+16% QoQ) and cementing (+4% QoQ, jobs +11%). Management guided Q2 revenue to $138-148M, expecting declines due to oil price weakness and tariff-related cost pressure, while citing strong April and a supportive natural gas outlook.

negative_highlights: Full-year AFFO and EBITDA projections are based solely on annualizing Q1 and exclude any contribution from future acquisitions, so they are not a raised guidance
Total revenue growth of 34.1% was attributed to timing of acquisitions and the Landmark-to-Kentucky re-tenanting rather than organic same-store growth
The Landmark lease recast nets to roughly the same economics in year one, with the $1 million/month payment to the prior operator offsetting the higher rent until year five
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA rose 42% YoY to $30.4 million from $21.4 million
AFFO increased 28% YoY to $16.8 million with full-year projection of $67.3 million (+20%)
Collected 100% of contractual rents with EBITDARM coverage of ~1.89x
summary: Strawberry Fields reported Q1 2025 revenue of $37.3 million, up 34.1% YoY from $27.8 million, net income of $6.99 million ($0.13/share) versus $5.99 million ($0.12), AFFO of $16.8 million (+28%), and adjusted EBITDA of $30.4 million (+42%). Management projected full-year 2025 AFFO of $67.3 million (+20% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $128.8 million, but explicitly based these on annualizing Q1 and excluding any future acquisitions, so no true guidance raise was issued. The company collected 100% of contractual rents and closed over $40 million of acquisitions YTD, expecting to approach $100 million by end of Q2. Results were driven largely by acquisition timing (Missouri master lease, Landmark-to-Kentucky re-tenanting) rather than organic growth.

negative_highlights: Professional services revenue down 42% YoY
RPO declined 9% sequentially
Maintained revenue guidance despite outperformance, citing macro uncertainty
positive_highlights: Record total revenue of $47M, up 5% YoY, above the high end of guidance
Adjusted EBITDA reached a record $4.1M, seventh consecutive quarter of profitability
Net dollar retention climbed to 107%, highest since Q1 2022
summary: Kaltura reported record Q1 2025 total revenue of $47M, up 5% YoY, and subscription revenue of $44.9M, up 9% YoY, both above guidance. Adjusted EBITDA hit a record $4.1M, with a non-GAAP gross margin of 70%, up from 65% a year ago. Net dollar retention improved to 107%, the highest since Q1 2022, but the company maintained its full-year revenue guidance, citing seasonal slow bookings and macro uncertainty, while slightly raising adjusted EBITDA guidance.

negative_highlights: Core income decreased by $3.7 million year-over-year primarily due to increased policy acquisition costs resulting from lower seeding commission income.
Operating expenses increased significantly by $12.1 million, driven largely by a 144.8% increase in policy acquisition costs.
positive_highlights: Gross premiums written grew by over 7% compared to the same period last year, reaching a total of $68.3 million in net premium earned.
summary: American Coastal Insurance Corporation reported Q1 FY2025 net income of $21.3 million and core return on equity over 34%, while growing gross premiums written by approximately 7% year-over-year to reach a combined ratio target of 65%. However, the quarter was impacted by increased policy acquisition costs driven by lower seeding commission income due to a step-down in catastrophe share from 20% to 15% effective June 1st. Management noted that while new business growth and retention remain strong at approximately 88%, they are proceeding cautiously with their apartment building initiative as the market is more competitive than expected.

negative_highlights: Brick and mortar retail growth remains slow as retailers like Walmart prefer online performance data before shelf placement.
No international revenue was recognized in Q1 despite pending orders, as shipments await regulatory approvals in several markets.
ContraPest sales declined approximately 40% year-over-year as the company shifts focus to Evolve.
positive_highlights: Gross margins expanded 320 bps to 64.5% driven by high-margin Evolve product line adoption.
Ecommerce sales surged 107% year-over-year following expansion onto Amazon, Walmart, and Tractor Supply.
Municipal sales increased sevenfold compared to the prior year quarter due to new deployments in Chicago and New York.
summary: SenesTech reported Q1 FY2025 revenue of $485,000, a 17% year-over-year increase driven by Evolve product growth and ecommerce expansion. Gross margins expanded significantly to 64.5% from 32.5% last year, resulting in gross profit rising 132% to $313,000. Management expressed confidence in the transition to profitability, citing new cost-saving initiatives and a revised cash flow breakeven threshold of $7 million annually.

negative_highlights: Tariff-specific demand headwinds in Deflecto's transportation unit led to purchasing delays and a challenged end market.
Industrial Operations revenue declined to $7.7 million from $8.8 million year-over-year.
Parent-level G&A decreased $2 million, but consolidated G&A rose $5.7 million to $17.3 million due to Deflecto; no formal guidance was provided.
positive_highlights: Revenue of $124.4 million versus $23.6 million in the prior-year quarter (Energy $18.3M vs $1.9M; IP $69.9M vs $13.6M; Manufacturing $28.5M new).
GAAP operating income of $38.3 million versus a $2.1 million operating loss in Q1 FY2024.
Benchmark repaid approximately $21 million of debt since the April 2024 Revolution acquisition, with ~70% of production hedged through 2027.
summary: Acacia reported Q1 FY2025 revenue of $124.4 million and total company adjusted EBITDA of $50.7 million, with GAAP operating income of $38.3 million versus a $2.1 million loss in the prior-year quarter. The quarter was driven by a ~$69 million IP settlement (WiFi portfolio) and the first full quarter of Deflecto, while the IP segment contributed $69.9 million in licensing revenue. GAAP net income attributable to Acacia was $24.3 million, or $0.25 per share, and adjusted net income was $33.1 million, or $0.34 per share. Management cited tariff-related demand headwinds in Deflecto's transportation unit and did not provide formal guidance; the prior-year comparison was heavily distorted by the one-time IP settlement.

negative_highlights: Pharma Services and Clinical Trials revenue fell 39% to $0.3M as clinical trial orders slipped from Q1 into Q2
Q1 international included ~$400K of distributor stocking that management expects to weigh on Q2 international growth
Tariffs on non-U.S. supply chain are estimated at just under 100 bps of gross margin drag embedded in guidance
positive_highlights: Revenue of $9.6M rose 18% YoY and set a company record, with domestic core up 16% and international up 36%
FY2025 revenue guidance raised to $38.5M-$39.5M (15%-17% growth) from the prior $38M-$39M range
Gross margin expanded 50 bps to 62.8%, and net loss narrowed 36% YoY to $1.2M
summary: KORU reported record Q1 revenue of $9.6M, up 18% YoY, with domestic core up 16% and international up 36%; gross margin was 62.8%, up 50 bps, and net loss improved 36% to $1.2M. Management raised FY2025 revenue guidance to $38.5M-$39.5M (15%-17% growth) from a prior $38M-$39M, reaffirmed 61%-63% gross margin despite tariffs under 100 bps, and reiterated positive operating cash flow. Pharma Services/Clinical Trials fell 39% to $0.3M on order timing, and Q2 international will be pressured by ~$400K of Q1 distributor stocking pull-forward, with international growth still guided to ~30% for the year.

negative_highlights: Full-year revenue guidance cut to $550-575 million from $585-595 million, with EPS guidance withdrawn
Consolidated gross margin fell 300 bps to 36.8% from 39.8%, and EBITDA dropped to $3.5 million from $9.6 million
Healthcare Apparel revenue fell 7% and segment EBITDA declined to $1.5 million from $2.6 million
positive_highlights: Contact center segment grew revenue 3% with gross margin held flat at 53.6%
Branded Products declined less than 1%, an improvement over the prior quarter's 5% decline, with backlog strong and pipeline at record levels
Company cut approximately $13 million in annualized budgeted SG&A, beginning to impact Q2
summary: SGC reported Q1 FY2025 revenue down 1% year-over-year with a net loss of $0.05 per share versus $0.24 EPS a year earlier; consolidated gross margin fell to 36.8% from 39.8% and EBITDA dropped to $3.5 million from $9.6 million. Full-year revenue guidance was cut to $550-575 million from a prior $585-595 million, and EPS guidance was suspended entirely due to tariff uncertainty. Management cited customer watching hesitancy and April tariff announcements, offset by a $13 million annualized SG&A reduction starting in Q2 and $3.8 million of Q1 share repurchases.

negative_highlights: Guidance excludes tariff impact and macro headwinds, creating uncertainty
Free cash flow negative $10.8 million, down $28.6 million YoY
EBITDA margins down ~100 bps on normalized basis due to lower overall volume
positive_highlights: Core business grew 3.3% across all divisions, first growth in five quarters
D2C channel grew over 10% and third-party platforms grew over 50%
Gross margin up 200 bps from operational efficiencies and lower warranty costs
summary: Holley reported Q1 2025 net sales of $153 million with 3.3% core business growth, the first growth in five quarters, driven by D2C (up >10%) and B2B (up >2.5%), with third-party platforms like Amazon growing over 50%. Gross margin improved to 41.9% (up 200 bps from operational improvements) and adjusted EBITDA margin was 17.8%, but that reflects SKU rationalization; normalized EBITDA margin is down ~100 bps due to lower overall revenue. Free cash flow was negative $10.8 million due to timing. Guidance excludes any tariff impact, citing uncertainty and a price increase effective June 9; management plans to provide clearer guidance in August.

negative_highlights: Net loss of $12M in the quarter with minimal free cash flow
Cyber incident caused $2M in restoration costs and disrupted advertising, single-copy sales, and digital subscriber activations
First-half adjusted EBITDA lagged expectations; Berkshire waived March–May interest and rent payments, added to principal debt
positive_highlights: Digital subscription revenue grew 20% year-over-year; Amplified Digital Agency revenue grew 9%
Total digital revenue grew 4% to a $303M trailing twelve-month run rate despite the cyber disruption
Executed ~$40M in annualized cost reductions; ~$25M of additional non-core assets identified for monetization
summary: Q2 FY2025 revenue was $137M with a $12M net loss and minimal free cash flow; digital revenue grew 4% (digital subscription +20%, Amplified Digital +9%). Results were materially hampered by a February cyber incident with $2M of restoration costs and disruption to ad products and subscriber activation; first-half adjusted EBITDA lagged expectations. Management cited ~$40M annualized cost reductions and an updated outlook expecting digital acceleration and positive free cash flow in the second half, but no explicit numeric guidance figures were given.

negative_highlights: FY2025 revenue guidance cut by 10% to $770–$800 million, with about $50 million of the reduction from exiting the Northeast transmission and distribution business
Net loss of $3.4 million ($0.12 per share) in the quarter, though improved from a $14.6 million loss a year earlier
Process and Industrial Facilities revenue fell to $45.4 million from $65.6 million due to completion of a large renewable diesel project
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 21% YoY to $200.2 million, the highest quarterly revenue in two years
Gross margin expanded 300 bps to 6.4% from 3.4%, with under-recovery of construction overhead improving to 280 bps from 370 bps
Backlog increased nearly 8% sequentially to over $1.4 billion on $301 million of awards (book-to-bill of 1.5), with Storage and Terminal Solutions backlog at a record $848 million
summary: Matrix Service reported Q3 FY2025 revenue of $200.2 million, up 21% year over year, with a net loss of $3.4 million ($0.12 per share) versus a $14.6 million loss a year earlier, and adjusted EBITDA improved to breakeven from a $10 million loss. Gross margin expanded to 6.4% from 3.4%, helped by a 280 bps under-recovery drag that was the lowest in two years, while Storage and Terminal Solutions revenue grew 77% to $96.1 million. Management cut full-year FY2025 revenue guidance by 10% to $770–$800 million, citing the exit of its Northeast transmission and distribution business (about $50 million annual impact), project award timing, and macro/regulatory uncertainty. Backlog rose nearly 8% sequentially to over $1.4 billion with quarterly book-to-bill of 1.5, and the company expects positive adjusted EBITDA in Q4 and full-year book-to-bill around 1.0.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined sequentially by $1 million due to the active divestiture of non-core third-party resale assets classified as held-for-sale.
Full-year revenue guidance was narrowed from a range of $235-240 million down to $235-238 million, reflecting lower expected revenue in the second half.
On-premise hardware sales cycles experienced volatility and slowdowns due to tariff announcements and geopolitical uncertainty.
positive_highlights: Transformation project Diamond is complete, with the new ERP system online and efficiency savings of approximately $5 million expected over three years.
Adjusted EBITDA margin improved to 17% (excluding one-time ERP costs) as the company successfully shifted focus away from lower-margin hardware resale.
Customer loyalty metrics strengthened significantly, with NPS scores up nearly 300% and churn remaining industry-leading at below 1%.
summary: Sangoma reported Q3 FY2025 revenue of $58.1 million, a sequential decline driven by the divestiture of non-core hardware resale assets, while core platform revenue grew. Adjusted EBITDA was $9.8 million (17% margin), and the company reaffirmed its full-year 2025 adjusted EBITDA guidance of $40-42 million despite narrowing the revenue range to $235-238 million. Management highlighted a completed transformation, strong cash flow generation ($8.4M FCF), and a strategic shift toward higher-margin services as they prepare for inorganic growth.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA declined 8% to $21.2 million due to negative sales mix, higher production costs, and transition expenses for the new Indiana facility.
Gross margin decreased significantly from 37.1% in Q1 FY2024 to 33.2% in Q1 FY2025.
positive_highlights: Net sales increased 10% YoY led by strong performance from debit and credit cards and prepaid solutions.
summary: CPI Card Group reported Q1 FY2025 net sales growth of 10% driven by debit/credit and prepaid segments, but adjusted EBITDA declined 8% to $21.2 million due to negative sales mix and increased production costs including a new Indiana facility transition. Gross margin contracted from 37.1% to 33.2%, while the company affirmed its full-year organic outlook for mid-to-high single-digit growth despite tariff impacts of approximately $2 million included in guidance.

negative_highlights: Revenue fell 4.2% to $423 million, with Material Handling new equipment sales down $15.7 million year-over-year
The quarterly dividend was suspended indefinitely, with capital redirected to a buyback

Guidance is explicitly predicated on no U.S. recession and no reinstatement of 90-day pause tariffs; surcharges from OEMs range 0% to 10%, and higher increases would push the situation 'beyond manageable'
positive_highlights: Service gross margin expanded 230 bps year-over-year, with Construction up 290 bps, adding about $2.7 million in gross margin
SG&A fell $7.9 million year-over-year, with a sizable portion tied to fixed expense reductions expected to hold for the rest of the year
Adjusted EBITDA of $33.6 million was down only $0.5 million versus Q1 2024 despite the 4.2% revenue decline, and FY2025 guidance was reaffirmed organically
summary: Alta reported Q1 FY2025 revenue of $423 million, down 4.2% year-over-year, driven by $15.7 million lower Material Handling new equipment sales and strategic rental fleet reductions in Construction. Adjusted EBITDA was $33.6 million, down just $0.5 million versus Q1 2024, as a 230 bps year-over-year service gross margin improvement and $7.9 million of SG&A reductions nearly offset the revenue decline. Full-year 2025 adjusted EBITDA guidance was reaffirmed on an organic basis at $171.5 million to $186.5 million, with the range shifted only by the divestiture of the Illinois aerial rental business. The company suspended its quarterly dividend indefinitely and increased its share repurchase authorization by $10 million to $30 million, allocating $10 million to a Rule 10b5-1 plan.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to $68.0 million from $53.7 million in Q1 2024
KOASTAL-3 and KOASTAL-2 top-line data now targeted for Q1 2026 and Q2 2026, after KOASTAL-1 failed to show separation
Management acknowledged surprise at J&J's decision to terminate its aticaprant program despite prior NDA plans, adding read-through uncertainty to the KOR antagonist class
positive_highlights: $125 million K2 HealthVentures debt facility with $20 million drawn at close extends cash runway into 2027, beyond anticipated clinical readouts
KOASTAL-2/3 enrollment resumed in March with added screening measures (SAFER review, Verified Clinical Trial database) already excluding inappropriate patients
Sex mix in KOASTAL-2/3 is roughly two-thirds female, one-third male, more representative of historical MDD trials than KOASTAL-1
summary: Neumora reported a Q1 2025 net loss of $68.0 million versus $53.7 million in the prior-year period, with $249.4 million in cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities as of March 31, 2025. The company entered a $125 million debt facility with K2 HealthVentures, with $20 million drawn at close, extending cash runway into 2027. Lead asset navacaprant remains in Phase 3 KOASTAL-2 and KOASTAL-3, which resumed enrollment in March after protocol and site changes; top-line data are now guided to Q1 2026 (KOASTAL-3) and Q2 2026 (KOASTAL-2), following the KOASTAL-1 miss. NMRA-511 Phase 1b data are expected around year-end.

negative_highlights: R&D expenses were higher than expected at $45 million, with management indicating this pace will likely continue.
Cash consumption was elevated due to a working capital timing gain that slipped from Q1 to Q2, masking underlying burn rates.
Some LOIs have evolved or lapsed as customers like Zero (acquired by Norwegian) changed strategy and others went bankrupt.
positive_highlights: Backlog remains unchanged at approximately 2,800 aircraft with a total value close to $14 billion based on list price.
Full-scale prototype testing is progressing toward initial flights in 2025, including successful pusher motor and lifter motor tests.
Conforming prototype assembly site at Embraer's facility in Sao Jose dos Campos is ready to receive tooling for the certification campaign.
summary: EVEX reported a net loss of $49 million in Q1 FY2025, driven by $45 million in program development costs and $8 million in SG&A. Cash consumption was $25 million for the quarter, which management adjusted to approximately $40 million after excluding a timing shift on an invoice from Embraer. The company reaffirmed its full-year cash consumption guidance of $200 million to $250 million, noting that burn is expected to accelerate slightly from the first quarter but remain near the low end of the range.

negative_highlights: Adjusted gross margin was flat sequentially at 33%, dragged down by lower-margin Motif operations compared to the core business.

Cash used by operating activities before working capital changes was $1.6 million, primarily due to intentional inventory buildup for Q3/Q4 seasonality and a $6M Collective Project acquisition payment.
positive_highlights: Record quarter with net revenue of $65.6M (up 74% YoY) and gross sales exceeding $100M for the first time in any given quarter.
Adjusted EBITDA turned positive at $4.9 million, a swing from negative $1 million prior year due to Motif synergies and margin expansion.
International sales surged 177% YoY to $6.1 million as demand for existing customers grew in Germany and Australia.
summary: Organigram Global reported a record-breaking Q2 FY2025 with net revenue of $65.6 million (up 74% YoY) and gross sales surpassing $100 million for the first time. Adjusted EBITDA swung to positive $4.9 million from a loss in the prior year, driven by higher margins and Motif integration synergies. Management reiterated guidance that results will continue improving through Q3 and Q4 seasonality.

negative_highlights: Total revenue declined 30% YoY to $121 million, with subscriptions down 31% to $108 million.
Q2 revenue guidance of $100-$102 million implies further YoY decline and sequential softness.
New restructuring eliminates 248 jobs (22% of workforce) with $34-$38 million in charges, citing worsening business trends.
positive_highlights: Revenue of $121 million and adjusted EBITDA of $19 million both exceeded Q1 guidance.
Busuu B2B revenue grew 29% YoY; Busuu overall revenue rose 7% YoY and is expected to reach ~$48 million in 2025.
Two content licensing deals signed with top-10 tech companies, generating $4 million in Q1 and expected $7 million in Q2.
summary: Chegg Q1 2025 revenue fell 30% YoY to $121 million, exceeding its own guidance and generating $19 million adjusted EBITDA (16% margin) and $15.8 million free cash flow, though gross margin fell to 56% (down 13 points from a $16.2 million accelerated depreciation charge). Subscription revenue dropped 31% to $108 million and subscriber count declined 31% to 3.2 million, while Q2 revenue guidance of $100-$102 million implies a further sequential decline. The company also announced a restructuring cutting 248 jobs (22% of staff) with $45-$55 million 2025 savings, and is exploring strategic alternatives including a sale.

negative_highlights: Gross margin declined 400 bps YoY to 84.4% on a higher mix of discounted financial-assistance patients and higher device manufacturing and shipping costs.
Operating loss widened 25% YoY to $2.3 million, and the company settled a lawsuit for $750,000.
positive_highlights: Revenue rose 39% YoY to $896,000 and unit sales increased approximately 46%.
Covered lives expanded to about 51 million from 4 million just over a year ago.
FDA label expanded for IB-Stim to ages 8-21, and RED received FDA clearance on December 6, 2024.
summary: NeurAxis reported Q1 FY2025 revenue of $896,000, up 39% YoY from $647,000, with unit sales up approximately 46%. Gross margin fell to 84.4% from 88.4% in Q4 2024, and operating loss widened to $2.3 million from $1.8 million, though much of the increase was tied to a one-time legal settlement. No formal guidance was provided; management said Q2 2025 is expected to mark a fourth consecutive quarter of YoY revenue growth and reiterated a goal of reaching cash flow breakeven, contingent on forthcoming society guidelines and the Category I CPT code effective January 1, 2026. Covered lives grew to about 51 million from 4 million a year earlier, but revenue remains small, with 300 patients treated in the quarter.

negative_highlights: Q4 adjusted EBITDA is expected to take a 'modest step back' due to Kansas facility ramp costs and new beneficiary eligibility rules in the OEP period.
