Medicare Advantage LTV declined 8% to $915 due to shifts from upfront to ratable commission structures.
Adjusted net income expectations lowered to a range of -$1 million to $28 million reflecting warrant valuation impacts.
positive_highlights: Consolidated revenue grew 8% YoY to $408 million with SelectRx membership up 41% to 106,000 members.
Senior segment held 27% EBITDA margins despite a 26% smaller agent force, with policies down only 10% YoY.
Life Insurance adjusted EBITDA more than doubled (+103%) to $6 million with margins nearly doubling to 14%.
summary: SelectQuote's Q3 FY2025 revenue rose 8% to $408 million, with consolidated adjusted EBITDA of $38 million (9% margin). SelectRx membership reached 106,000 (+41% YoY) driving Healthcare Services revenue up 53% to $190 million, while Senior revenue fell to $169 million with a 27% EBITDA margin despite a 26% smaller agent force. Life Insurance revenue grew 13% to $46 million with EBITDA up 103%. Management maintained full-year revenue and EBITDA guidance but expects Q4 results in the lower half, citing special election period changes and Kansas facility ramp costs. Adjusted net income outlook was lowered to a range of -$1 million to $28 million due to warrant valuation effects.

negative_highlights: Revenue was flat at $7.3 million primarily due to a seasonal inventory drawdown masking the underlying 15% demand growth.
Q1 results were transitional following the divestiture of UDENYCA and significant sales force restructuring which impacted momentum.
positive_highlights: Patient demand grew 15% in Q1 driven by new patient starts and increased duration of treatment despite revenue flatness due to inventory drawdown.
summary: Coherus BioSciences reported Q1 FY2025 revenue of $7.3 million which was flat year-over-year due to a seasonal inventory drawdown despite underlying patient demand growth of 15%. The company successfully closed the divestiture of its biosimilar business (UDENYCA), generating approximately $483 million in upfront cash and realizing significant SG&A savings, though Q1 results were impacted by sales force restructuring. Management provided guidance for full-year 2025 SG&A between $90-100 million following the divestiture.

negative_highlights: Multiplatform Group revenue declined 4.2% YoY ($473M), with political advertising drag reducing the decline.
Audio & Media Services Group fell sharply, down 14.2% YoY to $59M due primarily to Katz Television impacts and high political ad spend.
Q2 revenue guidance remains negative (down low single digits) despite Q1 beat, citing macro uncertainty requiring back-half improvement.
positive_highlights: Consolidated revenue beat consensus and prior guidance, coming in up 1% YoY versus a guide for decline.
Digital Audio Group revenue surged 16% YoY ($277M), significantly above low double-digit expectations.
Podcasting revenue grew 28% YoY to $116M, well exceeding high teens guidance and expanding margins by ~300 bps.
summary: Consolidated revenue beat guidance by coming in up 1% YoY versus a guide of down low single digits, driven primarily by Digital Audio Group growth and better-than-expected March results. Adjusted EBITDA was $105 million, flat to the prior year and consistent with previously provided guidance at the midpoint range ($140M-$160M). Management reiterated full-year 2025 revenue guidance of down low single digits but noted that current macro volatility requires positive movement in the back half of the year to avoid negative impacts.

negative_highlights: GAAP net loss of $3 million for the quarter
Cost savings identification still being implemented; full benefits not yet in numbers
International real estate exit not yet finalized; definitive plan deferred to next quarter
positive_highlights: Revenue up 14% and core segment up 23% year-over-year
Adjusted EBITDA up 38% to $9 million
Private credit commitments of $240 million and Kontora won two client mandates
summary: AlTi's Q1 FY2025 revenue was $58 million, up 14% year-over-year, with core Wealth Management and Capital Solutions revenue up 23% and segment adjusted EBITDA of $19 million at a 34% margin. Consolidated adjusted EBITDA rose 38% to $9 million, and the company closed the Kontora acquisition in Germany effective April 30, with $240 million in private credit commitments since December. Management is executing a zero-based budgeting program expected to yield substantial savings fully reflected in 2026, with further cost and real estate exit details to come in August.

negative_highlights: Full-year revenue guidance lowered significantly with an expected decline of 5-13%, down from prior expectations.
Accelerator lab revenue fell sharply by 36% due to the end of Lilly collaboration and slower pipeline development in pharma projects.
European revenues declined 30% year-over-year, primarily driven by lower Accelerator performance.
positive_highlights: Consumables revenue reached record levels at $18.1 million, up 6% year-over-year driven by new assay launches and strong neurology demand.
Adjusted gross margin remained robust at approximately 50%, demonstrating pricing power in the recurring consumables business despite macro headwinds.
Accelerated cash burn reduction to $9 million from $19.4 million last quarter, representing a greater than 50% improvement.
summary: Q1 FY2025 revenue was $30.3 million, a decline of 5% year-over-year driven by softness in the Accelerator lab segment and instrument sales pressure, though consumables grew 6%. Management revised full-year 2025 guidance downward to an expected range of $120-$130 million (a midpoint reduction from prior expectations) citing macro headwinds including academic funding cuts, tariffs, and pharma spending conservatism. The company announced a strategic amendment reducing the Akoya Biosciences merger equity value by 67% while increasing Quanterix's ownership stake to 84%, alongside an announcement of $30 million in core operating cost reductions.

negative_highlights: Reported revenue declined 4% year-over-year to $77.3 million, with gross profit down 5% and adjusted EBITDA down 7%
Reported free cash flow was negative $8 million, driven by approximately $16 million of reversal and timing related to net working capital
Consumer Payments gross profit declined 5%, including roughly 6 points of full-quarter impact from prior client losses
positive_highlights: Business Payments gross profit rose 7% year-over-year, or approximately 12% excluding Q1 2024 political media contributions, despite a 12-point client loss headwind
Adjusted EBITDA margin held at 43% on $33.2 million of adjusted EBITDA
Instant Funding transaction volumes grew approximately 19% year-over-year and the supplier network expanded 40% to roughly 390,000
summary: Q1 FY2025 revenue was $77.3 million, down 4% year-over-year, with reported gross profit down 5% and adjusted EBITDA down 7% to $33.2 million (43% margin); adjusted net income was $20.3 million, or $0.22 per share. Reported free cash flow was negative $8 million, attributed to roughly $16 million of one-time net working capital reversal and about $3 million from prior client losses. Management guided to normalized gross profit growth accelerating from low single digits in Q2 to a Q4 exit rate of high single to low double digits, with free cash flow conversion above 50% in Q2 and above 60% by year-end, and announced the conclusion of the strategic review with plans to increase organic growth investment. The quarter compared unfavorably to prior periods given the decline in reported revenue, gross profit, and EBITDA, alongside an interim CFO transition.

negative_highlights: Gross margin contracted to 61.5% from 62.1% on 400 bps of inventory disposal and excess/obsolete charges, only partly offset by 390 bps of vertical-integration savings.
Spinal implant sales declined 10% YoY ($1.2 million), and hardware revenue is guided flat to modestly down as product rationalization continues.

Net income and adjusted EBITDA benefited from licensing/royalty items; the $1.5 million upfront payment is being recognized over two years (about $700,000 in 2025) rather than fully in Q1, and no additional royalty minimums are assumed.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 18% YoY to $32.9 million, including $3.6 million of licensing revenue.
Adjusted EBITDA swung to $3.0 million positive from a $1.0 million loss in Q1 2024.
Full-year 2025 revenue guidance raised to $127-$131 million, representing 8-11% growth.
summary: Xtant Medical reported Q1 2025 revenue of $32.9 million, up 18% year-over-year from $27.9 million, including $3.6 million of licensing revenue. GAAP net income was $58,000, or $0.00 per share, versus a net loss of $4.4 million, or $0.03 per share, a year ago; adjusted EBITDA was $3.0 million versus a $1.0 million loss in Q1 2024. Gross margin slipped to 61.5% from 62.1% on a 400 bps inventory charge, partly offset by 390 bps of vertical-integration savings. Management raised full-year 2025 revenue guidance to $127-$131 million (8-11% growth) from the prior range and said no additional capital raise is expected; the company also completed vertical integration of biologics manufacturing and launched Trivium and FibreX DBM products.

negative_highlights: FRE margin of 28.4% sits below the low-30s full-year target, which management reiterated rather than raised
AUM declined 7% QoQ, driven by ~7% BRL appreciation and net outflows in global IP&S, with continued equity-segment redemptions
No material corporate advisory revenue in the quarter; management said BRL10 million there would have lifted margin to ~30%
positive_highlights: Fundraising of BRL1.1 billion in capital subscriptions, described as the most active first quarter in recent years
Fee-related revenues up 117% YoY to BRL231.6 million and management fees up 15% QoQ to BRL195.5 million
PEPCO II second closing raised over BRL600 million; SPS IV first close of ~BRL200 million brought total commitments to BRL1.1 billion, matching SPS III in a single close
summary: Vinci Compass reported Q1 2025 fee-related earnings of BRL65.7 million (BRL1.04/share), up 22% YoY, and adjusted distributable earnings of BRL62.3 million (BRL0.98/share), up 26% YoY but only 6% on a per-share basis. Fee-related revenues rose 117% YoY to BRL231.6 million, aided by the first full quarter of Compass and Lacan contributions, while FRE margin came in at 28.4%, below the reiterated low-30s full-year target. AUM fell 7% QoQ on a ~7% BRL appreciation plus net outflows in global IP&S, and management kept its low-30s FRE margin guidance intact while flagging a weak corporate advisory quarter with no material revenue.

negative_highlights: Gross margin decreased from 62.0% to 60.9%, primarily due to product and channel partner mix shifts.
Net loss widened on a GAAP basis to $2.2 million ($0.12/share) compared to $6.9 million in the prior year, though this reflects non-cash stock-based compensation impacts.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 11% YoY to $21.9 million, beating consensus estimates.
Adjusted EBITDA turned profitable at $1.5 million, an improvement of nearly $2M over the prior-year quarter loss.
Committed contracted revenue exceeded $70 million, representing a greater than 25% year-over-year increase.
summary: First quarter FY2025 revenue increased 11% year-over-year to $21.9 million, while adjusted EBITDA improved nearly $2 million to a profit of $1.5 million despite gross margin contraction from 62% to 60.9%. Management raised full-year guidance for revenue ($101M-$106M) and adjusted EBITDA ($13M-$15M), citing strong contracted revenue visibility exceeding 80% year-over-end of Q1.

negative_highlights: Q2 total revenue guided to $1.8-2.0 million versus $3.9 million in Q1, reflecting the roll-off of end-of-life memory IC shipments
Cash declined to $2.8 million from $3.3 million on roughly $0.9 million operating cash burn in the quarter
positive_highlights: mmWave product revenue of $1.5 million in Q1 exceeded total full-year 2024 mmWave revenue and rose from $0.2 million in Q4
GAAP gross margin expanded to 69.3% from 56.3% in Q4 and 46.4% in the year-ago quarter
GAAP net loss narrowed to $0.5 million ($0.10/share) from $1.6 million ($0.37/share) in Q4 and $2.0 million a year ago
summary: Total Q1 revenue was $3.9 million, up from $3.7 million in Q4 and $2.8 million a year ago, with mmWave product revenue jumping to $1.5 million from $0.2 million sequentially and $0.3 million a year ago. GAAP gross margin rose to 69.3% from 56.3% sequentially (46.4% a year ago) partly on reduced amortization and favorable mix, while GAAP net loss narrowed to $0.5 million ($0.10/share) from $1.6 million in Q4, and adjusted EBITDA was negative $0.3 million. However, Q2 total revenue guidance of $1.8-2.0 million implies roughly a halving of Q1 revenue as end-of-life memory IC shipments roll off, even as management guides to double-digit sequential mmWave growth throughout 2025. Cash fell to $2.8 million from $3.3 million on roughly $0.9 million operating burn, partly offset by $0.4 million from the ATM program.

negative_highlights: Total revenue declined 21% year-over-year to $1.6 million, primarily driven by decreased smart glasses sales.
Gross margins contracted with an overall gross loss of $0.3 million compared to a smaller loss in the prior period.
positive_highlights: Net loss narrowed to $8.6 million from a prior year net loss of $10 million due to significant cost reductions in R&D and sales/marketing expenses.
summary: Vuzix reported Q1 FY2025 revenue of $1.6 million, a decrease of 21% year-over-year and an increase of 24% sequentially, driven by decreased sales of the M400 smart glasses while engineering services grew to $0.3 million. The company posted a net loss of $8.6 million ($0.11 per share), which was better than the prior year's loss of $10 million due to cost reductions and lower R&D expenses, though gross margins contracted with an overall gross loss of $0.3 million compared to $0.1 million in 2024. Management expressed confidence in upcoming milestones for Quanta investment tranches totaling $10 million expected by the end of 2025 but noted that tariff policy changes may impact margin improvement plans.

negative_highlights: Management guided the June quarter to be soft, saying it does not expect it to be the second strongest quarter and that traditional seasonality is 'out the window'
Management estimated 25% to 30% of March quarter gross margin was impacted by recently announced tariffs
Management described ocean imports ex-China as having come to a 'virtual standstill' recently and flagged near-term volatility tied to ongoing U.S. trade negotiations
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA rose 80.5% to $9.398 million from $5.208 million a year earlier, with legacy U.S. operations contributing $1.5 million and legacy Canadian operations $0.5 million of incremental adjusted EBITDA
Nine-month adjusted net income increased 62.9% to $25.459 million and nine-month revenue rose to $682.1 million from $596.4 million
Balance sheet remains strong with approximately $19 million cash on hand and only $15 million drawn on a $200 million credit facility
summary: Radiant reported Q3 FY2025 net income of $2.541 million ($0.05 diluted) on $214 million revenue, up from a $703,000 net loss on $184.6 million a year earlier, with adjusted EBITDA up 80.5% to $9.4 million and adjusted net income up 91.9% to $6.881 million. Management guided the June quarter to be soft, stating traditional seasonality is 'out the window' and it does not expect June to be the second strongest quarter, while projecting a later bullwhip recovery once tariff disputes resolve. Management estimated 25-30% of gross margin is tied to international trade exposed to tariffs, though it clarified this is exposure rather than a downside estimate, and the balance sheet held roughly $19 million cash against $15 million drawn on a $200 million facility.

negative_highlights: 2025 financial guidance was paused due to tariff and geopolitical uncertainty
Cash burn of $100-$120 million per quarter in 2024 described as unsustainable, with $4.8 billion debt against a $5.5 billion covenant
U.S. tariffs (China paused at 30% for 90 days) and model-year 2027 China connected-car ban create unresolved regulatory headwinds
positive_highlights: Retail volume grew 76% year-on-year and revenue rose 84%, driven by Polestar 3 and Polestar 4 launches
Gross margin swung positive to 7%, a 15 percentage point improvement year-on-year, on favorable model mix
Net loss improved by 31% to $190 million and adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed 46% to $115 million
summary: Polestar reported Q1 2025 retail volume growth of 76% year-on-year with revenue up 84%, gross margin swinging positive to 7% (a 15 percentage point improvement) and net loss narrowing 31% to $190 million. However, the company paused its 2025 financial guidance due to tariff and geopolitical uncertainty, while reaffirming its 30%-35% CAGR target for 2025-2027. Liquidity stood at $732 million, and the CFO described the prior $100-$120 million quarterly cash burn as unsustainable, noting active work on new equity financing with Geely.

negative_highlights: Critical care revenue fell 25% YoY due to customer inventory timing
Gross margin contracted to 56% from 64.1%
Cash position only $2.6M at quarter end
positive_highlights: Pediatrics and heart failure revenue up 38% and 28% YoY
Operating expenses down 31% and operating loss narrowed
CMS reimbursement increased nearly 4x to $1,639 per day
summary: Q1 2025 revenue was $1.9M, up 3% YoY, with consumables utilization up 4% and U.S. console sales up, offset by lower international sales. Gross margin fell to 56% from 64.1%, while operating expenses dropped 31% and operating loss narrowed to $3.1M from $4.7M. Critical care revenue declined 25% due to a one-time inventory build by a large customer, but pediatrics and heart failure grew 38% and 28% respectively. Management highlighted a new CMS reimbursement rate nearly 4x higher, an outpatient pipeline worth $773M, and plans to outsource manufacturing to cut costs.

negative_highlights: Total revenue fell 12% YoY to $16.1 million, with hospitality revenue down 16% and same-store hospitality down 12%.
Tin Building revenue fell 33% for the quarter due to closed concepts.
Entertainment operating EBITDA declined 2% on elevated winter activation programming costs.
positive_highlights: Total operating EBITDA rose 10% YoY and hospitality operating EBITDA grew 12% despite the revenue decline.
G&A fell 41% YoY to just under $10 million and adjusted net loss improved 34% to $22.8 million.
Entertainment revenue rose 18% YoY on higher Aviators ticket sales and sponsorship revenue.
summary: Total Q1 FY2025 revenue fell 12% YoY to $16.1 million on a pro forma basis, with hospitality revenue down 16% and same-store hospitality down 12%, driven by the strategic closure of restaurants and a 33% decline at the Tin Building. The GAAP net loss narrowed 28% to $31.9 million and adjusted net loss improved 34% to $22.8 million, while total operating EBITDA rose 10% and hospitality EBITDA grew 12% on better expense management. G&A fell 41% to just under $10 million, largely due to non-repeating separation costs, and cash stood at $132 million against $102.4 million of debt. Management reiterated its goal to reach breakeven in 2026 and profitability in 2027, but no numeric revenue or earnings guidance was provided.

negative_highlights: Full-year revenue guidance was lowered from prior expectations due to a one-quarter delay in hiring primary care and associate sales reps.
Sales force contraction reduced Q1 test volumes compared to the previous quarter as new territories were not yet staffed.
Adjusted EBITDA remained negative at $6.2 million, with breakeven now targeted specifically for the fourth quarter.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 21% year-over-year driven by lung diagnostics (up 16%) and development services (up 61%).
Gross margins expanded 80 basis points sequentially/annually to reach 79.4%, demonstrating operational leverage.
SG&A expenses decreased year-over-year despite adding sales headcount, reflecting successful cost containment.
summary: Biodesix reported Q1 FY2025 revenue of $18 million (up 21% YoY) and gross margins expanding to 79.4%, but adjusted EBITDA remained a loss of $6.2 million due to sales force reconfiguration delays. Management revised full-year revenue guidance down to $80-$85 million, citing that commercial expansion is approximately one quarter behind plan following the shift from pulmonology-focused reps to primary care and associate support roles.

negative_highlights: Retail credit card segment revenue fell 26% from Q1 2024 due to customer bankruptcies and economic malaise
GAAP gross margin contracted to 89.7% compared to 90.7% last year primarily due to $210 million in non-cash amortization expenses
Cash balance at quarter end ($5.1M) exceeded consensus estimates of $3.4M, indicating lower-than-expected cash generation or higher burn relative to expectations
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 5% YoY despite macro headwinds and retail contraction
Title insurance revenue surged approximately 350% year-over-year as diversification strategy takes hold
AWS platform migration completed for three large clients with plans to move all no-integration portal clients by quarter end
summary: First quarter revenue grew 5% year-over-year to a record $4.89 million driven by diversification into title insurance and banking as retail credit card business declined 26%. Adjusted EBITDA improved slightly to roughly breakeven with a small loss, while GAAP gross margin compressed due to non-cash amortization of software development costs related to the AWS migration program.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA margin of ~15.6% missed the full-year guidance target range of 17%-18%.
GAAP net loss was $2.1 million (EPS -$0.06) compared to a GAAP profit in Q1 FY2024, primarily due to one-time gains and pre-opening costs stripping out non-recurring items.
Recent macroeconomic pressures caused customer traffic reductions of 10-11% in April and May following strong January/February performance.
positive_highlights: Same-store sales declined only modestly by 0.7% in Q1, a significant improvement from the -5.6% decline seen for all of FY2024.
Gift card redemption rates have stabilized around 60-65%, outperforming the industry average, with management noting increased premium menu sales among gift card users.
summary: In Q1 FY2025, GEN Restaurant Group reported total revenues of $57.3 million, a 13% year-over-year increase driven by new store openings and same-store sales improvement to -0.7%, though this was below the full-year prior period decline of -5.6%. Adjusted EBITDA margin came in at approximately 15.6%, missing the annual guidance target range of 17%-18% due to higher costs associated with six new restaurant openings and pre-opening expenses totaling $2.6 million.

negative_highlights: Gross margin remained negative at a loss of $0.6 million due to rebuilding volume and capacity.
Cash used in operations was $2.9 million, indicating continued cash burn despite expense reductions.
The company remains dependent on future state approvals for VLN products and new branded SKUs to achieve profitability.
positive_highlights: Net revenue increased 50% sequentially to $6 million driven by CMO contract repricing and volume normalization.
Operating expenses reduced to $2 million, the lowest quarterly amount since the turnaround began in late 2023.
Net loss narrowed significantly to $3.3 million from a $4.2 million loss in the preceding quarter.
summary: First quarter 2025 net revenue was $6 million, a 50% sequential increase from Q4 2024, while gross margin remained at a loss of $0.6 million. Operating expenses decreased to $2 million, and the net loss narrowed to $3.3 million compared to $4.2 million in the prior quarter. Management indicated that breakeven EBITDA is expected in the latter half of 2025 as volume ramps up and branded products launch.

negative_highlights: Company reported a working capital deficit of approximately $9.4 million.
No revenue guidance provided for the current or upcoming quarters; first commercial revenue expected only in Q4 FY2025.
Ovaprene interim assessment is safety-only with no primary endpoint analysis, meaning sample size cannot be increased if efficacy data looks weak.
positive_highlights: G&A and R&D expenses decreased significantly by 14% ($2.3M) and 31% respectively compared to the prior year quarter.
Company secured a non-dilutive grant of up to $10.7 million in November 2024 specifically for Ovaprene Phase 3 enrollment expansion.
Received positive feedback from industry peers regarding the 'dual path' strategy (503B compounding while seeking FDA approval).
summary: Daré Bioscience reported a comprehensive loss of approximately $4.4 million for Q1 FY2025, with G&A and R&D expenses decreasing by 14% and 31% respectively due to reduced stock-based compensation and headcount. The company ended the quarter with roughly $10.3 million in cash but maintains a working capital deficit of approximately $9.4 million. Management provided no financial guidance for Q2 or full-year revenue, instead focusing on strategic updates regarding upcoming product launches via 503B compounding expected to begin generating revenue in Q4.

negative_highlights: Net loss of $28.8M and operating loss of $30.4M with no product revenue
R&D spend rose to $25.3M on ALTITUDE-AD costs and will continue ahead of a late-2026 readout
Efficacy readout for Sabirnetug is not expected until late 2026, and no specific powering assumptions were disclosed
positive_highlights: ALTITUDE-AD enrolled 542 patients in roughly 10 months, far faster than projected
Cash and securities of $197.9M expected to fund operations into early 2027
p-tau 217 pre-screening raised amyloid PET positivity to 81% vs 40% in INTERCEPT, cutting screening costs and patient burden
summary: Pre-revenue biotech Q1 2025 operating update: R&D $25.3M, G&A $5.1M, operating loss $30.4M, net loss $28.8M, and $197.9M cash expected to fund into early 2027. The key operational event was completing enrollment of the 542-patient Phase 2 ALTITUDE-AD trial in roughly 10 months, well ahead of plan, with topline data guided to late 2026. No revenue, EPS, or formal corporate guidance was reported, so the read reflects clinical execution rather than financial results; management also flagged a completed Phase 1 subcutaneous PK study and p-tau 217 screening that lifted amyloid PET positivity to 81% from 40% in INTERCEPT.

negative_highlights: Diluted EPS flat at $0.19 and net income up only 2% YoY despite 17% revenue growth
Interest expense jumped to $55 million from $42 million, driving 17% expense growth and compressing net interest margin growth to 4%
Return on managed assets fell to 0.8% from 0.9%
positive_highlights: Revenue increased 17% YoY to $106.9 million from $91.7 million
Originations rose 31.5% YoY to $451 million and portfolio grew 24% to $3.45 billion
Charge-offs fell to 7.50% from 7.84% and delinquencies to 12.35% from 12.39% YoY
summary: Revenue rose 17% YoY to $106.9 million on a $3.6 billion fair value portfolio yielding 11.4%, but expenses rose 17% to $100.1 million on higher interest expense of $55 million, leaving pretax income up only 3% to $6.8 million and diluted EPS flat at $0.19. Originations grew 31.5% YoY to $451 million and managed portfolio reached $3.45 billion (up 24%), while delinquencies (12.35%) and annualized net charge-offs (7.5%) improved slightly YoY. Flatter profitability reflected a smaller fair value markup ($3.5 million vs $5 million a year ago) and rising funding costs; no explicit forward guidance was provided beyond continued credit-conscious growth. Return on managed assets declined to 0.8% from 0.9%.

negative_highlights: Dropping one rig for May–August and pausing completions due to macro uncertainty and weak oil prices.
Tariffs on tubular goods could increase AFE by ~2%, though offset by other savings.
First quarter capital spend reached 38% of full-year budget, higher than planned, due to pulling forward activity.
positive_highlights: Production averaged over 53,000 Boe/d, beating guidance and consensus, up ~6% vs Q4.
EBITDA nearly $200 million, up ~10% QoQ on similar oil price.
Drilling efficiencies: spud-to-spud dropped from 14 to 11 days, >20% faster; simul-frac expected to be a 'dollar bill' step change in cost.
summary: HighPeak Energy reported Q1 2025 production of over 53,000 Boe/d, beating guidance and consensus, up ~6% sequentially, with EBITDA near $200 million, up ~10% QoQ. The company is taking proactive steps to manage activity in a volatile market by dropping one rig for four months and pausing completions, while still expecting to complete the same number of wells as originally guided. Guidance was narrowed with the floor raised to 48,000 Boe/d, and management highlighted significant drilling efficiencies (spud-to-spud down to 11 days) and expects further cost savings from simul-frac operations. Capital spend was 38% of the full-year budget in Q1, but the company still generated positive free cash flow.

negative_highlights: Net loss remained at -$0.71M, with SG&A nearly doubling YoY.
Cash balance low at $1.19M; financing likely needed before EBITDA positivity.
AbbVie launch delayed again, pushing to end of 2025 or Q1 2026.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 121% YoY to $2.81M, slightly above guidance.
Gross margin improved to 42.4% from 12.6% YoY and 37% sequentially.
Adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed to -$0.47M from -$0.73M YoY.
summary: Q1 FY2025 revenue was $2.81M, up 121% YoY, with contract manufacturing up 58% and consumer brands up 189% (led by Silly George). Gross margin normalized to 42.4%, up from 12.6% in Q1 2024 and 37% in Q4 2024. Adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed to -$0.47M from -$0.73M YoY. Management reaffirmed FY2025 guidance of $13M revenue and cash flow positivity, with AbbVie launch delayed again but not expected to impact guidance.

negative_highlights: Third-party technology revenues decreased to $600,000 from $800,000 in the prior year.
Mortgage and Title segments remain unprofitable with adjusted EBITDA losses of $400,000 each.
Management expressed caution regarding broader market volatility and global economic uncertainties affecting housing inventory and price trends.
positive_highlights: Total revenue rose 32.1% YoY to $93.1 million, significantly exceeding analyst expectations by roughly 12%.
Brokerage revenue climbed 36% to $88.9 million, supported by a 26% increase in transaction volume (approx. 9,715 closings).
Gross profit improved 34% YoY to $8.1 million when excluding the divested insurance business, with gross margin expanding to 8.7%.
summary: Fathom Holdings reported Q1 FY2025 revenue of $93.1 million, a 32.1% year-over-year increase driven by a 36% rise in brokerage revenue and growth in ancillary segments. The company beat analyst estimates by roughly 12%, with GAAP net loss narrowing to $5.6 million from $5.9 million due to cost-cutting initiatives. Management reiterated its guidance to achieve adjusted EBITDA profitability in the second quarter, citing strong execution despite elevated mortgage rates and shifting market conditions.

negative_highlights: Terminating SEEG distribution, which reduces product portfolio
Operating expenses up 8% due to R&D investments
Cash burn of $7.5M in the quarter
positive_highlights: Revenue up 24% YoY to $22.5M, exceeding expectations
Gross margin expanded to 77% due to RNS manufacturing efficiency
Full-year guidance raised to $93-97M
summary: NeuroPace reported Q1 2025 revenue of $22.5 million, up 24% year-over-year, with RNS System sales growing 26% (29% ex-NAUTILUS). Gross margin expanded to 77% from 73.6%, and net loss narrowed to $6.6 million from $8.9 million. The company raised full-year revenue guidance to $93-$97 million, representing 16-21% growth, and remains on track for cash flow breakeven by end of 2027. Management announced termination of SEEG distribution to focus on higher-margin RNS business, with minimal 2025 revenue impact.

negative_highlights: Organic revenue growth was only 18%, consistent with last year's Q1 but well below the reported 27% headline, relying on acquisitions for the rest
Transaction value grew ~18% YoY and was roughly flat sequentially for a third consecutive quarter, which management attributed partly to seasonality in January and February
Free cash flow was negative $5.7 million despite $1.3 million from operating activities, due to timing of processing cash settlements
positive_highlights: Gross margin expanded to 49% from 44% a year ago, with hardware margin reaching 39.5% versus 27.3% and recurring margin improving to 52% from 50%
Recurring revenue grew 35% YoY to ~$62 million, representing 77% of total revenue, up from 72% in Q1 2024
Adjusted EBITDA rose to $9.7 million (12% of revenue) from 6% of revenue a year ago, and the customer base surpassed 100,000, up over 30% YoY
summary: Nayax reported Q1 2025 revenue of $81 million, up 27% YoY (28% constant currency to $82 million), with recurring revenue up 35% to ~$62 million, now 77% of total, and adjusted EBITDA of $9.7 million (12% of revenue) versus 6% a year ago. Gross margin expanded to 49% from 44%, driven by hardware margin of 39.5% versus 27.3% and recurring margin of 52% versus 50%. However, organic revenue growth was just 18%, processing/transaction value growth decelerated to ~18% with volumes flattish for a third straight quarter, and free cash flow was negative $5.7 million. Management reaffirmed full-year 2025 guidance of 30-35% revenue growth ($410-425 million constant currency, at least 25% organic) and adjusted EBITDA of $65-70 million, expecting acceleration in the second half.

negative_highlights: Consolidated revenues declined slightly by approximately 1% year-over-year.
GAAP net loss increased to $6.7 million due to a $4.3 million non-cash accounting charge related to dust storm damage at Texas facilities reducing crop yield.
Retail branded sales in Canada were down 22% as the company intentionally shifted away from lower-margin value SKUs.
positive_highlights: International medicinal export sales grew 285% year-over-year, contributing significantly to margin expansion.
Canadian cannabis gross margins expanded to 36%, up from 25% in Q1 last year and within the targeted range of 30%-40%.
The Vanguard transaction will generate $40 million in cash proceeds while retaining a minority stake in an attractive produce opportunity.
summary: Consolidated revenues of $77 million were roughly in line with the prior year's $78 million, while GAAP net loss narrowed to $6.7 million ($0.06/share) from a prior-year loss due to lower produce sales and non-cash accounting charges rather than operational deterioration. The company announced a definitive agreement to privatize its majority fresh produce division into Vanguard Foods LP for $40 million cash, retaining 37.9% ownership while keeping Canadian cannabis assets (Delta, D1) and Texas facilities (Marfa I, Monahans). Management highlighted strong international medical export growth of 285% year-over-year in Canada but noted that retail branded sales were lower due to a strategic shift away from low-margin value offerings.

negative_highlights: Adjusted net loss widened significantly from prior year income due to market rate compression and dry docking costs increasing by $5.2M YoY
GAAP EPS declined from $0.25 per share in Q1 last year to a loss of $0.03 per diluted share this quarter
Cash flow turned negative with net cash used in operations of $4.3 million compared to prior period inflows
positive_highlights: TCE rates remained a premium of approximately 33% over prevailing market averages despite sector-wide declines
Total shipping days rose 24.6% year-over-year to 5,210 driven by the addition of SSI handy fleet vessels
Management authorized a new $15 million share repurchase program in addition to declaring a quarterly dividend
summary: Pangaea Logistics Solutions reported an adjusted net loss of $2 million and GAAP net loss of approximately $2 million for Q1 FY2025, down from prior year income due to a 37% decline in average market TCE rates. Despite the revenue miss driven by lower charter hire expenses ($14.8M EBITDA vs implied higher prior), management raised guidance expectations slightly via new share repurchase authorization and maintained dividend continuity at $0.05/quarter while integrating SSI fleet synergies.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined ~23% YoY to $4.5M, with premium services down 47%
Gross margin contracted to 33% from 39% YoY
No guidance given; Q2 comparison to remain difficult and organic revenue not expected to be positive in the second half
positive_highlights: Operating expenses reduced ~28% YoY to $2.1M, offsetting the gross margin decline
Cash balance rose to $5.7M from $2.8M at Dec 31, 2024 after $4.3M warrant exercise proceeds retired all bank debt
Proactive services gross margin improved and the service line is cited as the best organic growth opportunity
summary: Q1 2025 revenue fell ~23% to $4.5M from $5.8M, with premium services down 47% and gross margin contracting to 33% from 39%. Operating expenses were cut ~28% to $2.1M, keeping the net loss flat at $0.6M ($0.05/share), and cash rose to $5.7M after $4.3M of warrant proceeds retired all bank debt. Management explicitly declined to give revenue guidance, citing a difficult Q2 comparison and organic revenue not expected to turn positive in the second half; new customer adds slowed and are not offsetting softening in the installed base. CFO Nancy Meyers announced her retirement with an internal successor transition underway.

negative_highlights: Net sales down 25.2% YoY, driven by 22.6% volume decline.
Full-year 2025 guidance withdrawn due to tariff uncertainty.
Negative free cash flow of $12M in Q1, with operating cash flow at -$11.8M.
positive_highlights: Proprietary brand mix improved sequentially to 55% from 52% in Q4 2024.
Adjusted SG&A down 11% YoY, the 11th consecutive quarter of savings.
Adjusted EBITDA improved by $4.8M sequentially from Q4 2024.
summary: Q1 2025 net sales fell 25.2% YoY to $40.5M, with adjusted gross margin down to 21% and adjusted EBITDA a loss of $2.4M. Proprietary brand mix improved sequentially to 55% from 52%, but declined YoY. Due to tariff uncertainty and prolonged industry recession, management withdrew full-year 2025 guidance but still expects improved adjusted gross margin and lower adjusted SG&A.

negative_highlights: Total revenues of just $1.5 million and an operating loss of $6.5 million; the business remains pre-commercial and dependent on partner progress
No timeline for Genentech's decision on advancing OpRegen into a controlled study, and Lineage has no access to GAlette Study data
OPC1 dose study data is back-ended: 30-day delivery/safety readout first, with functional assessments typically 6-12 months out
positive_highlights: Net loss narrowed to $4.1 million ($0.02 per share) from $6.5 million ($0.04) a year ago, though $2.4 million of other income came from warrant fair-value changes
Cash of $47.9 million with runway into Q1 2027, plus approximately $37 million of warrant capital potentially available
Manufacturing milestone: two GMP production runs from a single pluripotent cell line sourced from master/working cell banks, claimed capable of millions of doses
summary: Lineage reported Q1 2025 total revenues of $1.5 million versus $1.4 million a year ago, with operating expenses of $8 million and a net loss of $4.1 million ($0.02 per share) compared to a $6.5 million ($0.04) loss in Q1 2024, the improvement driven largely by a $2.4 million warrant fair-value gain. Cash stood at $47.9 million with runway projected into Q1 2027, plus roughly $37 million of potential warrant capital. No financial guidance was issued; the quarter was a clinical-update call, with management highlighting a GMP manufacturing milestone (millions of doses from a single cell line), continuing Roche/Genentech investment in OpRegen, three-year Phase 1/2a data due June 21, and OPC1 dosing study enrollment targeted for June. The only measurable change versus prior periods is the smaller net loss, aided by non-operating warrant gains.

negative_highlights: Consolidated revenue down 2% YoY, with Gearing revenue down 28% and Industrial Solutions down 29%.
Adjusted EBITDA margin of 6.4% reflects low utilization and lower-margin mix.
Gearing segment posted an adjusted EBITDA loss of $0.2 million due to soft demand and operational inefficiencies.
positive_highlights: Orders increased 5% YoY to $30.5 million, with industrial solutions setting a record for bookings and backlog.
Heavy Fabrication revenue up 15% YoY and adjusted EBITDA up sequentially and YoY.
Reiterated full-year guidance with expected Q2 revenue improvement.
summary: Broadwind reported Q1 2025 revenue of $36.8 million, down 2% YoY, with adjusted EBITDA of $2.4 million (6.4% margin). Orders rose 5% YoY to $30.5 million, driven by wind repowering adapters and gas turbine demand, while gearing and Industrial Solutions revenue declined due to softness and supply chain delays. The company reiterated full-year 2025 guidance of $140-$160 million revenue and $13-$15 million adjusted EBITDA, citing improved momentum in Q2.

negative_highlights: Gross margin fell to 47% from 52% due to intangible amortization
Program revenue declined $1.4 million YoY
Operating expenses up due to noncash charge and acquisition-related costs
positive_highlights: Revenue up 59% YoY to $11.8 million, ahead of internal expectations
Adjusted EBITDA loss improved nearly 50% YoY
Reiterated full-year revenue guidance and on track for AVCAD production
summary: 908 Devices reported Q1 2025 revenue of $11.8 million from continuing operations, up 59% year-over-year driven by handheld device sales. Adjusted gross margin improved 75 basis points to 54% despite a higher mix of international distributor sales. Adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed to $4.6 million from $5.3 million a year ago. Management reiterated full-year revenue guidance, expects positive adjusted EBITDA by Q4 2025 and cash flow positivity in 2026, with the company citing strong demand in handheld markets and progress on the AVCAD program.

negative_highlights: Total expenses increased by $21 million YoY, including $15.5 million in acquisition-related costs and transactional fees.
Everspan gross premiums written declined 10% to approximately $87 million due to the non-renewal of a personal alliance reinsurance program.
Organic growth excluding acquisitions contracted by 2%, primarily driven by pullbacks in ESL and note weakness in-term medical business.
positive_highlights: Insurance Distribution and Specialty Program premium grew 70% YoY to $318 million, driven largely by the Beat acquisition contributing over $20 million in revenue.
Cirrata segment produced adjusted EBITDA of $12 million on a 29.5% margin compared to $5 million at a 28.7% margin last year.
Everspan loss ratio improved nearly 9 percentage points (to 66.9%) following the de-emphasis of assumed programs.
summary: Ambac reported Q1 FY2025 revenue of $63 million (up 27% YoY) and a net loss from continuing operations of $16 million ($0.58/share), driven by the Beat acquisition offsetting headwinds in ESL/medical lines and higher expenses at Everspan. Management provided no specific numerical guidance for future quarters, instead setting long-term targets to generate $80-90 million adjusted EBITDA by 2028 while awaiting regulatory approval for a legacy business sale.

negative_highlights: Q2 product revenue was flat year over year at $1.4 million and declined sequentially due to completed Zimmer stocking orders
Net loss of $2.3 million in Q2, though improved from $2.9 million a year earlier
Cash was only $1.3 million at March 31, 2025, before the April financing
positive_highlights: Q2 product gross margin expanded to 55.6% from 28.3% a year earlier
First-half product revenue increased 97% to $4.7 million
No debt, with $8.2 million net proceeds from an oversubscribed April raise and funding through at least fiscal 2026
summary: Q2 FY2025 product revenue was flat at $1.4 million versus $1.4 million a year ago, but Q2 product gross margin more than doubled to 55.6% from 28.3%. First-half product revenue rose 97% to $4.7 million with a $3 million Zimmer license fee; net loss improved to $2.3 million ($0.07/share) from $2.9 million ($0.11/share), and the company reported no debt with $1.3 million cash at March 31, 2025, later bolstered by an $8.2 million oversubscribed raise in April. FY2025 product revenue guidance was reiterated at $8 million to $10 million (132%-190% growth) with product gross margin of 47%-51%, excluding the $3 million license fee. Management said the sequential decline was expected due to Q1 initial stocking orders and expects revenue to ramp through the rest of the fiscal year, with upside from a trigeminal nerve ablation opportunity not included in guidance.

negative_highlights: Total revenue fell 8.9% to $65.9 million from $72.3 million; adjusted EBITDA dropped to $14.2 million from $17.2 million
Bombshells same-store sales declined 13.4% and the segment swung to an operating loss of $227,000 from $699,000 income
Nightclub same-store sales fell 3.5%, with service revenue down ~30% on weaker VIP/bottle spend; free cash flow fell to $6.9 million from $8.8 million
positive_highlights: GAAP net income rose to $3.2 million ($0.36 EPS) from $0.8 million ($0.08) on lower impairments of $2.1 million vs $8.2 million
Nightclub segment GAAP operating margin expanded to 25.4% from 18.6% on the impairment decline
Repurchased 56,875 shares for $2.9 million, reducing share count ~15% over 10 years to ~8.8 million
summary: RCI reported Q2 FY2025 revenue of $65.9 million, down from $72.3 million, with adjusted EBITDA falling to $14.2 million from $17.2 million and non-GAAP EPS of $0.65 versus $0.90. Nightclub same-store sales declined 3.5% and Bombshells same-store sales fell 13.4%, with Bombshells posting a segment operating loss of $227,000 versus $699,000 income a year ago. Management cited severe January-February weather (~$5.6 million in lost sales), divestitures of five underperforming Bombshells, and soft high-end customer spend; they noted March improvement and expect April-June to provide a clearer read. No formal guidance was issued, though management discussed long-term targets of $400 million revenue and $75 million FCF by fiscal 2029.

negative_highlights: Full-year adjusted EBITDA margin guidance was lowered from prior levels to account for tariff regime impacts and increased AI modeling/AWS costs.
Q2 revenue is expected to be lower than Q1 as the $3.5M catch-up revenue normalizes, requiring a step-down in quarterly performance before growth resumes later in the year.
One-time expenses including an all-hands meeting costing over $700k and increased AWS/Azure bandwidth usage for AI investments weighed on margins.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 12% year-over-year driven by solid new sales, renewals, and approximately $3.5M in catch-up revenue from two delayed NYPD contracts totaling over $64M in contract awards.
Adjusted EBITDA expanded significantly to $4.5 million (up 50%), highlighting operational leverage despite the one-time meeting costs.
SafePointe is gaining traction with a new California hospital mandate and early deployments at top healthcare chains, while international ShotSpotter pipeline remains robust.
summary: SoundThinking reported Q1 FY2025 revenue of $28.3 million (up 12% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $4.5 million (up 50% YoY), driven by catch-up revenue from delayed NYPD contracts. Management reaffirmed full-year 2025 revenue guidance at $111-$113M but reduced the adjusted EBITDA margin outlook to 20-22%, citing tariff impacts, AI investment costs in AWS/Azure, and a one-time all-hands meeting expense of over $700k. The company noted that Q2 is expected to be lower than Q1 as the catch-up revenue normalizes.

negative_highlights: Cash burn remained at approximately $4 million during the quarter despite lower OpEx compared to prior year.
Only ~50% of AYA patients currently complete full adherence, indicating room for improvement in patient support programs.
G&A expenses increased quarter-over-quarter due to noncash stock compensation.
positive_highlights: Net product sales grew 18% year-over-year to $8.8 million, marking the second consecutive quarter of growth.
PEDMARK launched commercially in Germany and UK with Norgine; Scottish Medicine Consortium accepted PEDMARQSI for use in Scotland.
Adherence numbers improved as Fennec HEARS program was redesigned for home administration settings.
summary: Fennec reported Q1 FY2025 net product sales of $8.8 million, representing an 18% year-over-year increase and a second consecutive quarter of growth compared to $7.4 million in the prior period. The company noted that cash operating expenses were approximately $33 million for the full year, with Q1 specifically seeing lower watching and marketing spend due to the elimination of European pre-commercialization activities from 2024. Management expressed confidence in continued momentum entering H2 2025 as new commercial initiatives mature.

negative_highlights: No revenue or earnings reported as the company is pre-commercialization; focus remains on proving technology via La Porte testing.
Management noted that Project Permian (SN1) is currently contingent upon value engineering efforts to reduce costs before a definitive cost estimate can be provided.
positive_highlights: Exited Q1 with approximately $500 million of cash and cash equivalents earning roughly 5% interest per year.
summary: Net Power reported Q1 FY2025 results with no revenue or EPS figures disclosed in the transcript as the company is pre-revenue and focused on R&D (La Porte testing) and SN1 development. Management highlighted a cash position of approximately $500 million at quarter-end, budgeting to spend roughly $190 million net of interest income during 2025 for G&A, La Porte/R&D, and project development. Guidance remains unchanged from prior periods with no specific financial targets provided other than the expectation to exit 2025 with nearly $350 million in cash.

negative_highlights: Reported revenue declined 4% YoY primarily due to FX headwinds and lower interest revenue; excluding these factors, underlying EBITDA would have been down roughly flat or slightly negative.
Attrition in the SMB segment was higher than expected (reducing revenue by ~12%), partially offsetting growth from new customers which contributed only 2% to total revenue.
Gross margin declined 190 basis points YoY due to a shift toward lower-margin ISO channel sales and reduced interest income, with Merchant Solutions margins compressing significantly.
positive_highlights: Organic revenue grew 5%, slightly better than expected, driven by double-digit growth in e-commerce (verticals like North America iGaming) and a ramping enterprise sales organization that signed over 100 new contracts.

Processing volume for Merchant Solutions increased 11% to $34.3 billion while Digital Wallet volumes rose 5%, indicating strong underlying demand despite reported revenue headwinds from FX and interest rates.
Adjusted EBITDA of $95 million was slightly ahead of expectations due to timing of cost items falling into Q2, resulting in a margin that beat the prior period's normalized run rate.
summary: Paysafe reported Q1 FY2025 revenue of $401 million (a 4% decline vs prior year) and Adjusted EBITDA of $95 million ($95M), which management noted was slightly ahead of expectations when excluding inorganic impacts from the divestiture. Management reiterated full-year guidance, citing Q1 results as 'slightly ahead' but acknowledging that underlying organic growth (excluding FX/interest/divestiture) would have been flat to down 3% without those one-offs. The company highlighted strong e-commerce and iGaming volume growth tempered by higher attrition in SMB.

negative_highlights: Revenue was impacted by the loss of several deals at large academic institutions due to significant reductions and cancellations of grant funding.
Full-year revenue guidance was lowered, implying lower second-half sales than previously anticipated.
U.S. hospital critical care deal sales cycles have lengthened to approximately one year or 1.5 years.
positive_highlights: Gross margin expanded 20 basis points year-over-year to 41.3%.
Office pilot accounts have successfully completed accreditation and are now scanning with strong enthusiasm from participating neurology practices.
NEURO PMR study enrollment is progressing well, exceeding expectations and expected to conclude ahead of the previous estimate by Q3 2025.
summary: Hyperfine reported Q1 FY2025 revenue of $2.1 million (six units sold) and a gross margin of 41.3%, which was in-line with expectations but impacted by the loss of several deals due to grant funding cancellations at academic institutions. Management lowered full-year 2025 revenue guidance to a range of 10% to 20% growth over 2024 and updated gross margin expectations to 47% to 50%, citing longer hospital sales cycles and the absence of anticipated grant-funded revenue. The company raised $6 million in financing, reducing net cash burn excluding financing to $10.1 million for the quarter.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA decreased by approximately $2.4 million compared to the prior quarter due to higher lease operating expenses and G&A costs
C48 well production underperformed initial expectations at ~100 barrels of oil per day, requiring a pivot from D-Sand to C-Sand completion
Capital program reduced with three Beta projects deferred resulting in capital savings of approximately $50 million
positive_highlights: C54 well completed with outstanding early results showing an IP20 of approximately 800 barrels of oil per day over first 20 days
Beta field production increased by approximately 35% since early 2024 after offsetting asset base decline
Completed three Haynesville acreage transactions generating $9.2 million in total net proceeds while retaining a 10% working interest
summary: Amplify Energy reported Q1 FY2025 adjusted EBITDA of $19.4 million and production of 17,900 BOE/day, a slight decrease from the prior quarter due to gas imbalance adjustments in East Texas and adverse weather. Management lowered its annual production guidance range for 2025 to 19,000-20,500 BOE/day following a comprehensive review of uncommitted capital budget triggered by material reductions in oil prices. Consequently, the company elected to temporarily defer three development projects at Beta and is exploring additional cost savings opportunities.

negative_highlights: Management guided to flat-to-slightly-negative overall NOI for 2025 versus the 21.8% three-year CAGR
A 57,000 sq ft tenant (10% of the industrial/commercial segment) defaulted and was evicted in Q1, cutting segment NOI 2%
New DC apartment deliveries will pressure vacancies, concessions and revenue growth; DC and Greenville trade-out rates were negative
positive_highlights: Net income increased 31.4% to $1.7 million ($0.09/share) from $1.3 million ($0.07) in Q1 2024
Pro rata NOI rose 10% YoY to $9.4 million; mining segment revenue and NOI up 919% over the prior year
Development pipeline of four industrial buildings (~850,000 sq ft, $146 million project cost) expected to generate $8.7-10.2 million annual NOI when stabilized
summary: FRP reported Q1 FY2025 net income up 31.4% to $1.7 million ($0.09/share) from $1.3 million ($0.07), with pro rata NOI up 10% to $9.4 million, driven mainly by mining royalties (+$524K), development (+$185K) and multifamily (+$141K). However, management explicitly guided to flat-to-slightly-negative overall NOI for 2025, citing the lapping of The Verge stabilization, industrial vacancy from the eviction of a 57,000 sq ft tenant (10% of the segment), and pressure from new DC apartment supply. The 10% NOI growth decelerates sharply from a 21.8% three-year CAGR, and guidance warns of further temporary NOI hits as the new Perryman warehouse moves from development to the industrial segment unleased.

negative_highlights: Commission expense rose $200,000 to $1.5 million, outpacing revenue growth.
Cash G&A increased quarter over quarter when excluding non-cash equity charges.
No formal guidance was provided for FY2025.
positive_highlights: Net loss decreased 68% to $1.7 million from $5.3 million YoY.
Adjusted EBITDA improved 300% to a gain of $145,000 from a loss of $74,000.
Commission income grew 4% to $4.2 million, supported by organic growth.
summary: In Q1 FY2025, Reliance Global Group reported commission income of $4.2 million, up 4% YoY, and reduced net loss by 68% to $1.7 million. Adjusted EBITDA turned positive at $145,000 versus a loss of $74,000 in the prior year. Management launched Relay Auto Leasing and expects to close the Spatner Associates acquisition, which it says will double revenue and boost profitability, though no formal guidance was provided.

negative_highlights: Full-year 2025 revenue guidance unchanged at $50-60 million, despite record quarter
Revenue expected to be back-end loaded with margin fluctuations; tariffs impact limited but uncertain
No explicit product shipment record confirmed; first Fabrinet units only expected in about a month
positive_highlights: Q1 revenues of $17.4 million, up ~3x sequentially and ~2.5x YoY, a record
Gross margin of ~40%, also a record versus 8.9% prior quarter
NRE payment plan expanded to ~$95 million; cash at $85.4 million
summary: Q1 2025 revenues were a record $17.4 million, up ~3x sequentially and ~2.5x year-over-year, with record gross margin of ~40%, driven by NRE payments and LiDAR sales. The company expanded its NRE payment plan from ~$80 million to ~$95 million, ended Q1 with $85.4 million in cash, and maintained full-year 2025 revenue guidance of $50-60 million (more than twofold YoY growth). Management highlighted a new manufacturing partnership with Fabrinet, accelerated LiDAR shipments to Volkswagen for robotaxi deployments, and expanding collaboration with NVIDIA. They expect first Fabrinet product unit shipments within a month and continue to target 1-3 new programs in 2025.

negative_highlights: GAAP net loss of $111.4 million ($14.58 per diluted share) driven by ~$119.3 million accelerated depreciation and a $25 million impairment
Harvest volumes fell to 4.7 million pounds solids from 5.8 million, reflecting Hurricane Milton impact
The $50 million land-sale upside remains uncertain and unclosed, contingent on ongoing diligence and other parties, with no guarantee on timing
positive_highlights: Land sales outlook raised to potentially more than $50 million this fiscal year, vs. prior ~$20 million guidance, a ~150% increase
Adjusted EBITDA turned to a $12.7 million gain from a $16.5 million loss a year earlier
Land Management and Other revenue rose 107% YoY on higher rock/sand royalty income and sod sales; $50 million buyback announced and workforce cut from ~200 to 25
summary: Q2 FY2025 revenue was $18.0 million, down 1% YoY, with harvest volumes falling to 4.7 million pounds solids from 5.8 million due to Hurricane Milton, partly offset by blended price per pound solids up $0.70. Results were dominated by transformation charges: a GAAP net loss of $111.4 million ($14.58 per diluted share) driven by ~$119.3 million accelerated depreciation and a $25 million tree/asset impairment, while adjusted EBITDA swung to a $12.7 million gain from a $16.5 million loss. Management raised its FY2025 land-sales outlook to potentially exceed $50 million (versus prior ~$20 million guidance), which would lift adjusted EBITDA above the ~$20 million forecast and bring net debt to roughly $60 million, though timing is uncertain pending diligence. The company also announced a $50 million share repurchase program, cut its workforce from ~200 to 25, and is winding down citrus with a final harvest on remaining groves in FY2026.

negative_highlights: FY2025 adjusted NII per share of $0.97 was slightly below the prior year's $1.00 per share, just covering the $0.96 annual distribution.
Portfolio fair value declined to $979 million from roughly $1.1 billion at the end of the prior quarter, and four portfolio companies remain on non-accrual status.
Management stated that most of the portfolio has some tariff exposure, with caution on consumer-focused companies and a direct China production footprint at a few companies.
positive_highlights: FY2025 total investment income grew to $93.7 million from $87.3 million, and Q4 investment income rose to $27.5 million from $21.4 million in the prior quarter.
The Nocturne exit generated $19.8 million in realized capital gains, and excluding the $24.3 million unrealized reversal on that exit, portfolio valuations rose $14.1 million.

NAV per share increased to $13.55 from $13.30 at the prior quarter end, and the company declared a $0.54 per share supplemental distribution in April, in addition to the $0.96 annual monthly run rate.
summary: Gladstone Investment reported FY2025 total investment income of $93.7 million, up from $87.3 million, and adjusted NII of $35.5 million or $0.97 per share, down slightly from $1.00 per share, just covering the $0.96 annual distribution. Q4 total investment income rose to $27.5 million from $21.4 million in the prior quarter, with adjusted NII of $0.26 per share versus $0.23, and NAV increased to $13.55 per share from $13.30. The year included a $19.8 million realized gain on the Nocturne exit and $221 million of new investments, with management saying it expects to close two acquisitions shortly. Management's forward view was explicitly cautious on tariff impacts across the portfolio, with four portfolio companies still on non-accrual status.

negative_highlights: Distributable earnings of $0.21 per share fell note weakness in of the $0.23 quarterly dividend.
Interest income declined to $8.5 million from $9.2 million in Q4 2024, partly due to lower income from Justice Grown.
Received a pre-discovery preliminary injunction barring enforcement of certain alleged defaults against Justice Grown, with three legal proceedings ongoing.
positive_highlights: Renewed a senior secured credit facility expandable to $100 million with an FDIC-insured bank, extending maturity to April 2028 at prime plus 50 bps.
Closed a $14 million senior secured credit facility to Standard Wellness Holdings in April 2025.
Weighted average portfolio yield to maturity remained approximately 18% as of March 31 and May 1, 2025.
summary: AFCG reported Q1 2025 distributable earnings of $0.21 per basic share and GAAP net income of $0.18 per share, with net interest income of $6.6 million. Interest income fell to $8.5 million from $9.2 million in Q4 2024, driven partly by lower income from Justice Grown ($600K vs $1.6M) and the absence of TRS dividends. Management declined to provide origination or dividend guidance, citing market volatility and pending Justice Grown litigation, but noted an active pipeline of $287 million and a portfolio yield of approximately 18%.

negative_highlights: Israel Innovation Authority grant declined to $25,000 from $209,000 year-over-year
Gross margin may vary with mix; expected range 72%-76%
positive_highlights: Record Q1 revenue of $16.6 million, up 17.5% year-over-year
Raising full-year 2025 revenue growth guidance to 15%-18%
Highest-ever non-GAAP operating income of $3.1 million and $4.4 million positive cash flow
summary: RADCOM reported record Q1 2025 revenue of $16.6 million, up 17.5% year-over-year, with non-GAAP operating income of $3.1 million (19% of revenue) and cash flow of $4.4 million, ending the quarter with $99.1 million in cash and no debt. The company raised its full-year 2025 revenue growth guidance from 12%-15% to 15%-18% year-over-year, citing strong momentum and strategic partnerships with ServiceNow and Nvidia. Management highlighted expanding agentic AI capabilities and a renewed tier-one North American contract.

negative_highlights: Net revenue growth of 15% lagged production growth of 23% as average realized prices fell 6%
Netback from operations declined to $37.55/BOE from $38.94/BOE a year ago
Management declined to quantify drilling cost savings and gave no timing for second-half drilling plans
positive_highlights: Net income up 72% to $5.8 million and basic EPS up to $0.16 from $0.09
Production averaged 4,077 BOE/d, up 23% year-over-year
Operating expense fell 15% to $7.07/BOE and drilling times on 1.5-mile laterals were cut a further 25%
summary: Kolibri reported Q1 2025 net income up 72% to $5.8 million with basic EPS of $0.16 versus $0.09 a year ago, on revenue up 15% to $16.4 million and production up 23% to 4,077 BOE/d. Adjusted EBITDA rose 24% to $12.8 million, operating expense fell 15% to $7.07/BOE, and netback slipped to $37.55/BOE from $38.94 on 6% lower realized prices. Management cited 25% faster drilling times on 1.5-mile laterals and said five wells drilled in the quarter will be completed later this quarter; no explicit production or capex guidance was given, and management declined to quantify drilling savings or second-half timing.

negative_highlights: Net cash used in operating activities rose to $7.1M from $6.7M in the prior-year quarter, and cash and investments declined to $37.3M from $44.1M at December 31, 2024.
R&D expense increased to $5.7M from $3.7M a year earlier, and management expects R&D to moderately increase in future periods.
Preeclampsia data timing remains dependent on outside laboratories finalizing the placental transfer assay, so the readout could slip within the stated window.
positive_highlights: ReMEDy2 stroke enrollment reached the 20th-25th percentile of the interim analysis cohort and management described an encouraging uptick, with interim analysis guidance reiterated for H1 2026.
Preeclampsia Part 1a top-line results are now framed with a concrete window, second half of June to first half of July, and Part 1b start is expected in Q3.
Cash and investments of $37.3M against current liabilities of $4.7M, with runway guided into Q3 2026.
summary: DiaMedica is a clinical-stage biotech with no product revenue; Q1 2025 results were purely financial. Cash and investments fell to $37.3M from $44.1M at year-end, with net cash used in operations of $7.1M versus $6.7M a year earlier, R&D up to $5.7M from $3.7M, G&A up to $2.5M from $2.1M, and runway guided into Q3 2026. On the pipeline, preeclampsia Part 1a top-line results are now expected between the second half of June and first half of July, and stroke ReMEDy2 enrollment sits in the 20th-25th percentile of the interim analysis target, with the interim analysis reiterated for H1 2026. Versus the prior update, the key changes are the enrollment uptick in stroke and the specified June-July window for preeclampsia data.

negative_highlights: Total revenue of $21 million fell 6% year-over-year and full-year FY2025 revenue guidance was cut to $88-88.5 million from $88.5-90 million
Total SaaS ARR declined 6% year-over-year and net retention for all customers was 88%, with note weakness in-term RPO down 7% year-over-year
Total gross margin contracted to 69% from 71% and adjusted EBITDA margin fell to 6% from 10% a year ago
positive_highlights: Non-GAAP net income of $765,000 or $0.03 per share came in ahead of the high end of guidance
SaaS ARR for knowledge customers increased 11% year-over-year, with FY2025 knowledge ARR growth expected in the high teens
Post-quarter close of one of the company's largest-ever deals, expanding a Big Four US bank's US Consumer Banking Group to over 100,000 users, roughly 10x the prior footprint
summary: eGain reported Q3 FY2025 total revenue of $21 million, within guidance but down 6% year-over-year, with non-GAAP net income of $765,000 or $0.03 per share ahead of the high end of guidance; adjusted EBITDA margin was 6% versus 10% a year ago. Knowledge SaaS ARR rose 11% year-over-year while total SaaS ARR fell 6%, and total RPO declined 2% with short-term RPO down 7%, both attributed to two large customer losses in the prior year. FY2025 revenue guidance was lowered to $88-88.5 million from $88.5-90 million due to extended sales cycles, though bottom-line guidance was raised to GAAP EPS of $0.09-0.10 from $0.04-0.06 on cost optimization. Management cited a post-quarter close of one of its largest-ever deals, a US mega bank US Consumer Banking Group expansion to over 100,000 users, and said sales cycles have stabilized at roughly nine to twelve months.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to $3.5 million from $1.8 million
Tissue Health Plus segment adjusted EBITDA loss deepened to $2.0 million
SG&A expenses increased 32% year-over-year
positive_highlights: Net revenue up 26% year-over-year to $23.4 million
Gross margin improved 240 basis points to 92%
Sanara Surgical segment adjusted EBITDA up $1.5 million to $2.7 million
summary: Sanara MedTech reported Q1 2025 net revenue of $23.4 million, up 26% year-over-year, with soft tissue repair products up 28% and bone fusion up 18%. Gross margin improved 240 basis points to 92%, and Sanara Surgical segment adjusted EBITDA rose to $2.7 million from $1.2 million. The company reaffirmed its growth expectations, narrowed THP cash investment guidance, and remains on track to launch the THP pilot in Q2. Net loss widened to $3.5 million due to higher SG&A and interest expense.

negative_highlights: Total revenues of $23 million missed the prior year's Q1 revenue of $23.8 million, despite a sequential increase from Q4 2024.
The ADCT-602 program targeting CD22 in B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia was discontinued based on available clinical data.
Top-line results for LOTIS-5 are uncertain regarding timing, potentially pushed to early 2026 depending on PFS event accrual.
positive_highlights: LOTIS-7 abstract data showed an exceptional 95.5% overall response rate and 90.9% complete response rate in the initial cohort of 22 patients.
No new safety signals were observed in LOTIS-7, with only low-grade adverse events reported.
Cash runway is expected to fund operations into the second half of 2026.
summary: First quarter 2025 revenues were $23 million, driven by $17.4 million in net product revenues and $5.6 million in milestone/royalty payments, which was a slight miss on the prior year's $23.8 million total revenue but met expectations for QoQ growth compared to Q4 2024. The company reported a GAAP net loss of $38.6 million, an improvement from the prior year's $46.6 million loss. Management highlighted promising LOTIS-7 data with a 95.5% overall response rate and 90.9% complete response rate in 22 patients, though top-line results for LOTIS-5 are expected later this year or early next year.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined to €1.1 million from €1.2 million year-over-year
Operating loss widened to €20.6 million from €12.2 million as U.S. launch investments accelerated
Cash position fell to €63 million from €85.6 million at December 31, 2024; runway extended only into Q2 2026
positive_highlights: FDA approvable letter received in March and final site inspection underway, with PMA approval still expected in Q2 2025
50-person U.S. commercial team fully hired and trained; established CPT code 64568 identified for launch reimbursement
First Genio implants completed in Dubai, with expansion to a second Dubai hospital and Kuwait/Saudi Arabia planned
summary: Nyxoah reported Q1 2025 revenue of €1.1 million, down from €1.2 million in Q1 2024, citing temporary softness in the international HGNS market and Genio 2.1 software upgrade-related purchase deferrals. Operating loss widened to €20.6 million from €12.2 million on U.S. commercial build-out, and cash fell to €63 million from €85.6 million at year-end 2024. Management reiterated expected FDA PMA approval in Q2 2025, noting the final manufacturing site inspection is ongoing, and said Q1 revenue factors should normalize; no formal revenue guidance was provided.

negative_highlights: Gross margin contracted 170 bps to 33.9% from 35.6% on higher cost of goods sold as capacity and inventory were increased
Operating loss widened to $1.7 million from $0.7 million; modified EBITDA loss widened to $1.6 million from $0.4 million as SG&A rose to $3.5 million from $2.6 million
Cash used in operations rose to $5.4 million from $2.4 million, and cash fell to $4.9 million from $10.4 million at December 31, 2024
positive_highlights: Net sales increased 4.5% to $10.0 million from $9.6 million on higher volumes with recurring national customers
note weakness in shipments reduced from approximately 20% at the start of the quarter to under 2% by April after the $10 million December private placement
New distribution wins including 1,100+ new points at Albertsons Safeway for Reed's Ginger Ale and national distribution at Sprouts for four functional SKUs
summary: Reed's Q1 FY2025 net sales rose 4.5% YoY to $10.0 million, but gross margin fell 170 bps to 33.9% and the operating loss widened to $1.7 million from $0.7 million. SG&A jumped to $3.5 million from $2.6 million and modified EBITDA loss widened to $1.6 million from $0.4 million, with $5.4 million of cash used in operations. Management gave no revenue guidance and flagged modest Q2 gross margin pressure from seasonal trade spend and the functional soda launch, while noting short shipments fell from ~20% to under 2% by April. The quarter mixed modest top-line growth and improved fulfillment against materially wider losses and margin erosion.

negative_highlights: Operating expenses increased moderately due to a reporting change including fuel gross at Camarillo and startup costs, obscuring underlying operational efficiency.
Management explicitly identified new competition as its 'biggest concern today' in response to analyst questions about replicators of the model.
positive_highlights: Revenues surged 133% year-over-year driven by full quarter operations at the newly acquired Camarillo campus and ramp-up in Phoenix, Dallas, and Denver.
Management reaffirmed prior guidance to achieve consolidated cash flow breakeven before year-end as leasing accelerates on new campuses over summer/fall.
Nashville occupancy remains strong at 92% (above 100% utilized space), demonstrating demand for the home basing model.
summary: Q1 FY2025 revenues increased significantly by 133% YoY and 20% sequentially primarily due to the incorporation of operations from the Camarillo campus acquisition in December 2024. Operating expenses rose moderately, driven largely by a reporting change that now includes fuel gross at Camarillo rather than net, alongside startup costs for new headcount at Phoenix, Dallas, Denver, and APA locations. Management reaffirmed guidance to reach consolidated cash flow breakeven by the end of FY25 as leasing ramps up on three new campuses.

negative_highlights: Total revenue fell sharply to $7.5M from $17.1M YoY, partly due to a one-time 2024 Roche license
Net loss widened to $20.7M from $11.5M in Q1 2024
A $2.5M pharma biocatalysis order slipped into April, missing the top of Q1 guidance
positive_highlights: Product gross margin expanded to 55% from 49% YoY
First ligase order delivered to a large pharma customer in Q1, with additional orders expected
Three CDMOs validated ligase performance in-house, supporting scalability
summary: Codexis reported Q1 FY2025 total revenue of $7.5 million, down from $17.1 million in Q1 2024, with product gross margin up to 55% from 49%. Net loss widened to $20.7 million from $11.5 million, and cash stood at $59.8 million. The company reiterated its 2025 revenue guidance of $64–68 million, noting revenue timing was affected by a $2.5 million payment shifting to April. Management highlighted early commercial progress in its ECO platform, including first orders for its ligase products and upcoming presentations at TIDES USA.

negative_highlights: Cash only $8 million, sufficient into Q3; need $15 million more
EMA approval contingent on additional GLP studies that may impact EU timeline
Phase 2 MB-106 first patient relapsed after over 600 days of complete remission
positive_highlights: First patient treated in Phase 3 MIRACLE trial with 38 sites selected
EMA approved trial in all nine EU countries
FDA feedback reduced Part B enrollment to 222 patients
summary: Moleculin Biotech reported Q1 2025 progress with its Phase 3 MIRACLE trial for Annamycin (naxtarubicin) in relapsed/refractory AML, including first patient treated, 38 sites selected, EMA approval for nine EU countries, and WHO recognition of the generic name. The company has roughly $8 million cash, enough into Q3, and needs about $15 million to reach Q1 2026 funding. FDA feedback reduced Part B enrollment to 222 patients. Final data from the MB-107 soft tissue sarcoma trial is expected soon. The company remains confident in achieving the 45-patient interim readout by end of 2025.

negative_highlights: Gross margins were softer than a year ago due to revenue mix changes, specifically the inclusion of $1 million in NYC COVID-related spoilage revenue which had no margin.
Card issuing revenues were slightly down compared to the prior year quarter primarily because the New York City COVID program provided over $1 million in revenue that is not recurring.
positive_highlights: Record numbers in first quarter revenues driven by significant increases in processing volume across all segments.
Adjusted EBITDA improved sequentially, rising from $500,000 in Q4 2024 to $700,000 in Q1 FY2025.
PayFac business continues strong growth trajectory with revenues up 25% and now accounting for approximately 59% of total card revenues.
summary: Usio reported record Q1 FY2025 revenues with a 5% increase year-over-year and adjusted EBITDA rising to $700,000 from the prior quarter's $500,000. Processing volume surged significantly across segments: total processing up 34%, ACH volumes up 36%, card transactions up 65%, and PayFac revenues up 25%. Management reiterated full-year revenue guidance of 14% to 16% growth.

negative_highlights: Total Q1 2025 revenue fell 26% YoY to $6.5 million, and flowcells sold declined 15% YoY to 6,994.
Full-year 2025 revenue guidance was updated to $26–$30 million from the prior view given on the March 31 Q4 2024 call, reflecting global trade turbulence and slowing customer decisions.

Installed base attrition is occurring as the company moves away from basic research, with some note weakness in-term contract labs returning systems; Q2 revenue guide of $6.3–$6.8 million implies limited near-term growth.
positive_highlights: GAAP gross margin expanded to 46% in Q1 2025 from 32% a year earlier, with non-GAAP gross margin also at 46% versus 34%.
GAAP operating expense fell 66% YoY to $11.4 million (non-GAAP down 65% to $8.5 million) from cost reduction initiatives including headcount cuts.
Existing-customer revenue was flat YoY at $5.8 million and flowcells sold to existing customers rose 1%, showing stability after the 2024 restructuring.
summary: Bionano reported Q1 2025 total revenue of $6.5 million, down 26% YoY, though Q1 2024 included $1.4 million from discontinued clinical services; on an apples-to-apples basis, revenue from the existing customer base was flat at $5.8 million and flowcells sold to existing customers rose 1% YoY. GAAP gross margin expanded sharply to 46% from 32% a year ago, and GAAP operating expense fell 66% YoY to $11.4 million, reflecting the September 2024 strategic shift away from new instrument placements.
