The company updated its full-year 2025 revenue guidance to $26–$30 million, citing global trade turbulence and customer tariff uncertainty, and guided Q2 revenue to $6.3–$6.8 million; the 15–20 new OGM system placements for the year were reiterated. Cash of $29.2 million ($11 million restricted) is expected to fund operations into Q1 2026.

negative_highlights: Company explicitly stated it does not currently provide financial guidance for future quarters.
Cash balance declined to $40 million from $41.7 million at year-end despite recent capital raise.
No specific revenue figures were reported as the company is pre-revenue in its clinical stage.
positive_highlights: Net loss decreased to $8.5 million from $10.6 million in Q1 FY2024 due to lower operating expenses of $9.1 million versus $10.1 million previously.
Successfully initiated the VERSATILE 003 Phase 3 registrational trial with FDA approval and added Mayo Clinic sites, targeting approximately 350 patients.
summary: PDS Biotech reported a net loss of $8.5 million ($0.21 per share) for Q1 FY2025, representing an improvement from the prior year quarter due to lower operating expenses and increased tax benefits. The company raised approximately $11 million in new capital earlier this month but did not provide financial guidance or raise its operational outlook. Management highlighted the initiation of the VERSATILE 003 Phase 3 trial for Versamune HPV plus pembrolizumab, noting that enrollment is ongoing and specific timelines are pending.

negative_highlights: Total production declined 7.5% year-over-year to 6,667 BOE/day due to planned maintenance at Delhi and weather-related downtime in Barnett.
Oil revenue fell 19%, resulting in a net loss for the quarter compared to prior year income.
Development of third Chaveroo block delayed into FY2026 to optimize timing amid low oil prices.
positive_highlights: Tex-Mex acquisition completed at an attractive valuation of approximately 3.4x forward adjusted EBITDA, adding stable low-decline production.
Natural gas revenue rose 33% year-over-year to $7.8 million and NGL revenue up 14%, partially offsetting oil weakness.
New Chaveroo wells drilled under budget with initial rates approximately 50% above expectations.
summary: Evolution Petroleum reported Q3 FY2025 revenue of $22.6 million (down 2% YoY) and a net loss of $2.2 million ($0.07/share), driven by an 8% volume decline despite higher commodity prices, though adjusted metrics showed improvement over the prior quarter. Management maintained its dividend at $0.12 per share for the 47th consecutive quarter while deferring oil-weighted development in Chaveroo to focus on gas opportunities and preserve cash flow amidst volatility. The company closed a Tex-Mex acquisition adding ~850 net BOE/day (combined with new wells) funded by cash and a modest credit facility draw.

negative_highlights: Q1 revenue proxy total segment operating margin fell to $106 million from $240 million in Q4 2024
Adjusted EBITDA of $82 million missed initial forecast due to no one-time gains and delayed items ($110 million PR incentive, Eskimo charter)
GAAP net loss of $200 million, or $0.73 per share, with no material one-time items
positive_highlights: Closed Jamaica asset sale for $1.055 billion, netting $778 million in proceeds and eliminating debt maturities until the second half of 2027
Raised full-year 2025 EBITDA-plus-gains guidance to $1.25–$1.5 billion from the previous estimate
Brazil construction on track: CELBA at 95% complete with COD expected in H2 2025, PortoCem at 54% with COD by mid-2026
summary: NFE reported Q1 2025 adjusted EBITDA of $82 million and a GAAP net loss of $200 million, or $0.73 per share, with total segment operating margin falling to $106 million from $240 million in Q4 2024. Results were below management's initial forecast primarily because a $110 million Puerto Rico incentive payment was not agreed before quarter-end and the Eskimo vessel charter sale was deferred, though both are still expected in 2025. Management raised its full-year 2025 EBITDA-plus-gains guidance to $1.25–$1.5 billion, higher than the previous estimate, and closed the sale of its Jamaica business for $1.055 billion, generating approximately $778 million in net proceeds to reduce debt and extend maturities. Core SG&A was $34 million and pro forma liquidity stood at over $1.1 billion after the Jamaica sale.

negative_highlights: The company remained unprofitable with an adjusted EBITDA loss of $6.3 million in the quarter, and no explicit numeric guidance was given.
Non-performing aircraft drag, while down roughly 80%, still costs under $600,000 per month and full removal is not complete.
Fractional sales are tempered by customer wait-and-see on the tax bill and 100% bonus depreciation, and management flagged tariff uncertainty slowing whole aircraft and fractional purchases.
positive_highlights: Revenue rose 10% year-over-year to $88 million while the fleet shrank nearly 20%, showing higher revenue per aircraft.
Gross margin expanded roughly 600 bps to about 13%, and SG&A fell nearly 700 bps to ~24% of revenue, a ~$6 million quarterly saving.
Active membership grew 38% and fractional program activity reached $16.2 million, up 100% year-over-year, with April retail charter revenue up 15%.
summary: flyExclusive reported Q1 FY2025 revenue of $88 million, up 10% year-over-year, despite operating roughly 20% fewer aircraft after disposing of non-performing jets. Gross margin was about 13%, up 600 bps, and SG&A fell to roughly 24% of revenue (down ~700 bps), but the company still posted an adjusted EBITDA loss of $6.3 million, a $13 million year-over-year improvement. Management did not provide explicit numerical guidance for revenue or EBITDA, only stating an expectation to reach positive adjusted EBITDA in 2025 and citing April retail charter revenue up 15% and Jet Club sales up 25%. Key changes versus the prior year include a 38% increase in active membership, a $59 million credit line repayment saving ~$3.6 million annually, and an extended senior note maturity to 2027.

negative_highlights: Net revenue fell 24% year-over-year to $15.4 million from $20.2 million.
Gross margin contracted to 61.4% from 65.1% and contribution margin declined to 13.4% from 14.1%.
Management withdrew its 2025 outlook and its three-year CAGR objective of at least 10-12% for 2025-2027, and paused the previously announced share repurchase program.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA loss improved slightly to $2.5 million from $2.6 million in Q1 2024 despite a 24% revenue decline, aided by prior fixed cost cuts.
Operating loss narrowed approximately 30% to $3.7 million from $5.3 million in Q1 2024.
Company stated it can navigate the environment without raising equity capital in 2025, citing cash of $14.3 million.
summary: Aterian reported Q1 2025 net revenue of $15.4 million, down 24% year-over-year from $20.2 million, driven by SKU rationalization, softer consumer demand, and reduced Amazon affiliate traffic. Gross margin contracted to 61.4% from 65.1%, and contribution margin fell to 13.4% from 14.1%, while adjusted EBITDA loss slightly improved to $2.5 million from $2.6 million. Management withdrew its previously issued 2025 outlook and its three-year CAGR target of 10-12%, citing tariff volatility, and paused its share buyback program; the company also announced a $5-6 million annualized fixed cost reduction program. Q1 results fell short on revenue and guidance was withdrawn, marking a sharp negative shift from the prior growth narrative.

positive_highlights: Revenue growth accelerated to 22% YoY with organic expansion and no new sales hires.
summary: MDxHealth reported Q1 FY2025 revenue of $24.3 million, representing a 22% year-over-year increase and organic growth without sales force expansion. Gross margins expanded to 63.8%, driven by the high-margin tissue-based segment which grew volume by 41%. Management confirmed full-year 2025 guidance of $108-$110 million, citing continued execution toward positive adjusted EBITDA in Q2.

negative_highlights: R&D expenses rose to $1.7 million from $1.3 million year-over-year, and SG&A increased to $1.6 million from $1.2 million
The company remains unprofitable with no bottom-line results provided and cash burn expected to continue until future cash flow positivity
Full TIGeR-PaC enrollment has not yet been achieved and is targeted for later in 2025, with the second interim analysis still pending
positive_highlights: Q1 revenue of ~$200,000 exceeded prior guidance for a low six-figure range
More than 10 non-TIGeR-PaC medical institutions initiated purchase orders, including high-volume academic and NCI-designated centers
Management expects sequential quarterly revenue growth for the remainder of 2025 and projects a $400 million peak U.S. annual sales opportunity for RenovoCath
summary: RenovoRx reported its first quarter of commercial revenue, with RenovoCath device sales of approximately $200,000, exceeding prior guidance of a low six-figure range. Management expects sequential quarter-over-quarter revenue growth for the remainder of 2025 and highlights strong demand from more than 10 new institutions, with a $400 million peak U.S. annual sales opportunity. R&D and SG&A expenses each rose by $0.4 million year-over-year, but the company ended Q1 with $14.6 million in cash and believes this funds both commercial scale-up and the Phase 3 TIGeR-PaC trial. The trial randomized 91 patients with 56 events as of May 2, triggering a second interim analysis expected in Q3.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined due to a shift in Roblox business resulting from changes in how the platform determines advertising revenue growth
Company remains EBITDA negative and requires further capital raises, with no specific date for breakeven other than targeting Q4 FY2025
positive_highlights: Gross margin increased from 38% (FY2024) to 44% in Q1 FY2025
Operating expense decreased approximately 25% compared to the prior year, with total cost reduction of ~30%
Net loss narrowed by 20% versus Q1 2024 despite revenue headwinds
summary: Super League reported Q1 FY2025 results where revenue met internal goals but declined due to a shift in the Roblox business following platform changes; however, net loss decreased by 20% compared to Q1 2024. Gross margin improved significantly from 38% in fiscal year 2024 to 44% in Q1 FY2025 driven by higher-margin programs and a ~25% reduction in operating expenses via cost-cutting measures including staff reductions.

negative_highlights: Total revenue fell 12% to $3.0 million due to VIP enrollment elimination
Gross margin contracted 700 bps to 50%
Cash used in operations increased to $3.8 million from $2.5 million, cash down to $2.3 million
positive_highlights: Total arches shipped grew 87% YoY from 1,996 to 3,736
Product revenue increased 8% to $1.8 million despite lower pediatric price points
Rebis alliance data shows 71% of patients chose Vivos over CPAP at $4,500 average revenue per case
summary: Vivos reported Q1 2025 total revenue of $3.0 million, down 12% YoY from $3.4 million, with a net loss of $3.9 million versus $3.8 million in the prior year. Product revenue grew 8% to $1.8 million on 87% higher arch volumes (3,736 arches), but service revenue fell due to the elimination of VIP enrollment. Gross margin declined to 50% from 57%, and cash dropped to $2.3 million from $6.3 million at year-end. Management is pivoting to a sleep-provider acquisition model, expecting to close the Sleep Center of Nevada acquisition within months, funded by a $7.5 million senior loan and equity infusion, and forecasts a Q3 accretive impact.

negative_highlights: Operating loss of RMB 155.5 million and net loss of RMB 207.3 million due to fair value decline of Bitcoin holdings.
April mining output fell 11.3% sequentially to 470 coins due to record global hash rate increase and 8% rise in mining difficulty.
Revenue concentration risk: Bitcoin mining accounts for 99% of total revenue, and power costs are relatively high under hosted model.
positive_highlights: Bitcoin mining revenue of RMB 1 billion contributed to total revenue of RMB 1.1 billion, a significant increase from RMB 64.4 million in Q1 2024.
Mined 1,541 Bitcoin in Q1 with an average effective hash rate of 30 EH/s and efficiency of 93.8%, ranking among top 3 publicly listed mining firms.
Cash and cash equivalents increased to RMB 2.5 billion from RMB 1.3 billion at year-end 2024, and credit risk exposure fell 30% to RMB 760 million.
summary: Cango's Q1 2025 revenue surged to RMB 1.1 billion (USD 145 million) from RMB 64.4 million a year earlier, driven by the new Bitcoin mining business which contributed RMB 1 billion. The company mined 1,541 Bitcoin at an average cost of USD 70,602 per coin, but recorded an operating loss of RMB 155.5 million and a net loss of RMB 207.3 million, largely due to a decline in Bitcoin prices in March. Management maintained its Mine and Hold strategy, targeting deployment of 18 EH/s of additional hash rate by end of July, bringing total capacity to 50 EH/s.

negative_highlights: Israeli revenue declined 56% YoY, partly due to supply delays and the Oranim deal cancellation.
Cash balance remains low at $1.4 million, with reliance on credit facilities and future financing.
Revenue growth was modest at 4% YoY, as German gains were mostly offset by Israeli declines.
positive_highlights: Achieved net profit of $0.2 million and positive adjusted EBITDA of $0.6 million, a ~$3M improvement YoY.
German revenue grew 569% YoY, now 62% of total revenue; 12 new strains launched in Q1 alone.
Gross profit up 94% YoY, aided by a 56% reduction in operating expenses.
summary: IM Cannabis reported Q1 2025 revenues of $12.5 million, up 4% YoY, with a net profit of $0.2 million versus a $6.0 million loss a year ago. Adjusted EBITDA turned positive at $0.6 million, improving from a $2.2 million loss in Q1 2024. German revenue surged 569% YoY to offset a 56% decline in Israel, while gross margin improved 87 percentage points. Operating expenses fell 56% YoY, driving the profitability turnaround.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to $4.46 million from $3.71 million a year ago
Operating expenses rose 26% to $4.65 million, outpacing gross profit of $396,000
Guidance for $2–3 million in COR and SOLIS revenue was removed from 2025 outlook
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 337% year over year to $2.24 million
Gross margin expanded to ~18% from 7% in Q1 2024 and 11% in Q4 2024
Active U.S. dealer network increased 64% to 151, with March B2B sales up ~70% from February
summary: Worksport reported Q1 2025 revenue of $2.24 million, up 337% from $512,000 in Q1 2024 but slightly below Q4 2024 due to seasonality. Gross margin improved to nearly 18% from 7% a year ago and 11% in Q4, while net loss widened to $4.46 million from $3.71 million, with operating expenses up 26% to $4.65 million. Management reiterated full-year 2025 revenue guidance of $20–25 million for tonneau covers but removed the previously communicated $2–3 million contribution from COR and SOLIS products, citing supply chain and geopolitical uncertainty. The company also reaffirmed its target of reaching cash flow breakeven in late 2025 or early 2026 and forecast gross margin expanding to 25–30% by late 2025.

negative_highlights: NYSE American suspended trading May 7, 2025 and commenced delisting proceedings due to low note price; shares began trading on the OTC Pink market on May 8, 2025

Cash and cash equivalents fell to $2.5 million at March 31, 2025 from $9.5 million at June 30, 2024, and the company is actively engaged with multiple potential funding sources for future operating cash requirements
No product revenue was recorded in the quarter, and the PL7737 IND submission in Q1 2026 is explicitly contingent on pending financing
positive_highlights: Phase 2 BMT-801 co-administration of Bremelanotide with Tirzepatide showed 4.4% weight reduction versus 1.6% for placebo, with 19% of combined-treatment patients losing more than 7% versus 0% on placebo and Tirzepatide alone
Net loss narrowed to $4.8 million from $8.4 million and net cash used in operations fell to $5.4 million from $8.6 million year-over-year

Oral PL-8177 produced 33% clinical remission versus 0% for placebo in moderate ulcerative colitis, and PL7737 received FDA orphan drug status; an additional ~$3.5 million of net proceeds was raised in April-May 2025
summary: Palatin reported Q3 FY2025 with no product revenue after the 2023 sale of Vyleesi to Cosette, a net loss of $4.8 million versus $8.4 million a year earlier, operating expenses of $4.8 million (down from $9.2 million), and net cash used in operations of $5.4 million (down from $8.6 million). Cash and equivalents stood at $2.5 million as of March 31, 2025, excluding roughly $3.5 million of net proceeds raised in April and May 2025, with the company actively seeking additional funding and business development. The company disclosed NYSE American delisting and suspension of trading effective May 7, 2025, with shares moving to the OTC Pink market on May 8, and noted it disagrees with the decision and is assessing options. Positive clinical readouts were reported for the MC4R obesity co-administration Phase 2 (4.4% versus 1.6% weight reduction; 19% of patients above 7% versus 0%), oral PL-8177 in ulcerative colitis (33% clinical remission versus 0% placebo), and PL-9643 dry eye responder analysis, though PL7737 IND work is explicitly contingent on financing.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined year-over-year due to shipment deferrals in the Aero and Architecture divisions caused by customer hesitation regarding tariff impacts.
Adjusted EBITDA deteriorated quarter-over-quarter from negative $4.8 million to negative $5.5 million, widening the loss despite margin expansion.
Management explicitly stated that 2025 will not be a positive free cash flow year; FCF is expected to turn positive only in 2026.
positive_highlights: Gross margin expanded 50 bps to 25.6% driven by operational efficiencies in Safety Tech (margin up from 12.8%) and Architecture segments.
Total purchase order backlog increased significantly to $36 million, indicating strong underlying demand despite timing delays.
Secured first tranche of a new debt facility with Mizrahi Bank at favorable terms ($370 bps interest rate reduction), enhancing liquidity.
summary: Gauzy reported Q1 FY2025 revenue of $22.4 million (down from $24.7M prior year) and adjusted EBITDA of negative $5.5 million (worse than the prior quarter's -$4.8M). Gross margin expanded 50 bps to 25.6%, driven by Safety Tech, while Aero revenue grew but margins contracted due to shipment timing shifts related to tariff uncertainty in March/April. Management reaffirmed full-year 2025 guidance of $130-$140 million revenue and positive adjusted EBITDA.

negative_highlights: Nine-month net revenue declined to $835.7 million from $863.5 million, which management attributed to shipment timing and product mix
Gaming revenue was pressured by tighter Microsoft hardware allocation and a difficult comparison against Q4 FY2024 promotions
Handmade by Robots production was put on complete hold during the period of 145% China tariffs, and a small arcade price increase is expected under the 30% tariff
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA grew 66% year-over-year to $4.9 million in Q3 from $2.9 million, with trailing-twelve-month EBITDA margin expanding to 2.5% from 2.2%
Net income turned positive at $1.9 million ($0.04 per share) versus a $3.4 million loss ($0.07 per share) a year earlier
Direct-to-consumer fulfillment rose to an estimated 40% of gross revenue from 33%, and distribution/fulfillment costs fell over 10% year-over-year
summary: Alliance Entertainment reported Q3 FY2025 net revenue of $213 million, essentially flat versus $211.2 million a year ago, while gross margin improved to 13.6% from 13.2%. Net income swung to $1.9 million ($0.04 per share) from a $3.4 million loss, and adjusted EBITDA rose 66% to $4.9 million; for the nine-month period net income rose 349% to $9.3 million on revenue that declined to $835.7 million from $863.5 million. Management gave no formal guidance but said EBITDA margin should exceed 3% in fiscal 2026, with a longer-term ambition near 5%, and cited the Paramount exclusive license and direct-to-consumer fulfillment (40% of gross revenue versus 33%) as growth drivers alongside tariff management.

negative_highlights: After-tax earnings fell ~42% ($7.475 million to $4.338 million) and pre-tax earnings fell ~41%, driven largely by ~$3 million of lower realized and unrealized investment income
Personnel costs rose 11.7% (~$2.2 million corporate-wide, ~$1 million or 17% in the life segment) from strategic hiring and annual compensation increases
Funeral and cemetery pre-tax earnings fell 27% to $2.21 million, and mortgage lost $1.994 million (roughly flat year-over-year)
positive_highlights: Mortgage origination volume rose 11% to $518 million versus a 2% national increase per MBA data, and the segment was profitable and cash flow positive in March
Life insurance premium margin improved roughly 14% on new premium, reflecting disciplined pricing and product refinement
Funeral home revenue grew 3.4% to $3.67 million on a 3% rise in services performed, and cemetery pre-tax earnings rose 1.2% to $815,000
summary: After-tax earnings fell roughly 42% to $4.338 million from $7.475 million in Q1 2024, with pre-tax earnings down about 41% to $5.571 million. Management attributed about 75% of the roughly $4.05 million pre-tax decline to lower realized and unrealized investment income (~$1.7 million from fewer home closings and lot sales, ~$1.25 million from stock market declines), plus about $900,000 of higher CECL bad debt reserve expense; personnel costs rose 11.7% (~$2.2 million). Segment results were mixed: life insurance GAAP earnings fell ~35% to $4.6 million despite flat premiums and an estimated ~14% improvement in premium margin, mortgage lost $1.994 million with origination volume up 11% to $518 million, and funeral/cemetery pre-tax earnings fell 27% to $2.21 million. No numeric guidance was issued; management said it remains 'cautiously optimistic' about the remainder of 2025 and described the quarter as a good one operationally.

negative_highlights: China tariffs expected to impact gross margin by approximately $1 million in the back two quarters
Physical Playboy Club development is projected as a one-to-two-year project, not immediate revenue
Licensing business excluding Byborg still grew but at a slower pace of over 50% YoY
positive_highlights: Licensing business revenue surged 175% year-over-year
Honey Birdette is ahead of plan for Q2 with an easy comparable base
Byborg deal includes a $20 million annual minimum guarantee plus additional payments
summary: PLBY Group reported Q1 FY2025 results where the licensing business grew significantly by 175% year-over-year to positive adjusted EBITDA of $2.4 million (excluding one-time personnel costs). Management highlighted strong performance in Honey Birdette with an easy comparable base and noted that Byborg contributed a significant portion of growth, though excluding it still showed over 50% YoY improvement. The company expects continued benefits from new deals in gaming and hospitality starting in the back half of the year.

negative_highlights: Total net revenue decreased by approximately 6% year-over-year to $2.2 million.
Loss from operations increased by $1.2 million, rising from $8.2 million in Q1 2024 to $9.4 million in Q1 2025.
The global Phase 3 prophylactic clinical trial for adult solid tumors did not achieve statistical significance.
positive_highlights: Dispensed prescriptions for Mytesi increased by approximately 2% year-over-year versus Q1 2024.
Initial proof-of-concept study results showed crofelemer reduced TPN requirements by up to 27% in MVID patients and 12.5% in pediatric SBS patients.
Crofelemer achieved statistically significant results in the prespecified breast cancer subgroup of the OnTarget trial.
summary: Jaguar Health reported Q1 FY2025 net revenue of approximately $2.2 million, a decrease of 6% year-over-year and 37% sequentially from Q4 2024, driven by lower distribution chain inventory purchases rather than weak product demand. While dispensed prescriptions for Mytesi increased 2% year-over-year, the company posted a net loss of $10.4 million compared to $9.2 million in the prior year. Management highlighted significant clinical catalysts, including proof-of-concept results for rare disease programs and positive breast cancer subgroup data from the OnTarget trial, but noted the failure to achieve statistical significance in the broader adult solid tumor population.

negative_highlights: Company reported a net loss of $1.2 million, though improved from the prior period.
Cash used in operating activities was $1.2 million due to prepaid inventory purchases for tariff mitigation.
positive_highlights: Revenue increased 111% year-over-year driven by RV market recovery and new HESS shipments.
summary: Revenue for Q1 FY2025 was $2.0 million, representing an increase of 111% year-over-year to the prior period's $1 million, driven by a rebound in RV sales and initial shipments from new Home Energy Storage Solutions (HESS). Gross profit margin expanded slightly to 24.5%, while SG&A expenses decreased significantly due to lower headcount and stock-based compensation. The company reported a net loss of $1.2 million but raised cash reserves to $1.1 million following a recent public offering.

negative_highlights: Near-term activity being minimized with only 0.5 net wells planned in each of Texas and Alberta, capex of $9-12 million over the balance of the year
No incremental Pennsylvania development expected this year; inventory development pushed to late 2026 or early 2027 subject to gas prices
Alberta Mannville well results not quantified; management offered no performance detail until the next quarterly report
positive_highlights: Marcellus upstream cash flows up over 200% sequentially on 58% production growth and 70% higher realized pricing
Midstream cash flows up 140% sequentially on higher throughput volumes
Roughly 45% of forecast PDP oil hedged at just over $71 WTI and about 30% of gas hedged at $3.33 NYMEX for the rest of the year
summary: Epsilon reported Marcellus upstream cash flows up over 200% sequentially on a 58% production increase and 70% realized pricing jump, with midstream cash flows up 140% sequentially on higher throughput. However, management is curtailing near-term activity given oil price volatility, planning only 0.5 net wells each in Texas and Alberta with $9-12 million of capex over the balance of the year and no further Pennsylvania investment in 2025. The first two Alberta Mannville wells were completed and began sales in April, but management declined to quantify performance, deferring detail to the Q2/Q3 update. No explicit revenue, EPS, or formal guidance figures were disclosed in the transcript.

negative_highlights: Net income fell to $0.6 million ($0.02 per share) from $0.7 million ($0.03) a year earlier
Operating expenses grew 8.3%, faster than the 7.3% revenue growth, with O&M up $403,000
Phoenix MSA single-family permits fell 15% YoY in Q1 and Maricopa permits fell 41.5%
positive_highlights: Revenue rose 7.3% to $12.5 million on 4.3% connection growth and higher consumption
Farmers rate case approved with an approximate $1.1 million annual revenue increase, effective May 1
Completed a $32 million equity raise and extended the revolver to $20 million, giving over $50 million of liquidity
summary: Global Water Resources reported Q1 2025 revenue of $12.5 million, up 7.3% YoY, driven by a 4.3% increase in active service connections and higher consumption. Operating expenses rose 8.3% to $11.2 million, outpacing revenue growth, and net income fell to $0.6 million ($0.02 per diluted share) from $0.7 million ($0.03) a year earlier; adjusted EBITDA rose 4.4% to $5.6 million. Management noted Phoenix-area single-family permits fell 15% YoY in Q1 and Maricopa permits fell 41.5%, though it called the pullback temporary and kept connection growth at a 4% annualized rate. The Farmers rate case was approved (about $1.1 million annual revenue increase) and a $6.5 million Santa Cruz/Palo Verde rate case is under review, with the Tucson acquisition targeted to close this summer.

negative_highlights: Weather reduced gross margins by 5-7% in Q1, with Australian gross margin falling to 16-17% vs normal ~25%.
Adjusted EPS of $0.52 was significantly hurt by $11 million higher depreciation, equivalent to $0.30 per share, partly due to idle equipment.
Backlog decreased by ~$300 million sequentially to $3.2 billion, though expected to recover to $4 billion by mid-year.
positive_highlights: Record trailing 12-month combined revenue of $1.5 billion, with Canadian Q1 revenue of $178 million up 45% from Q2 2024.
Canadian equipment utilization hit 68% in Q1 (best since winter 2022-23), approaching 75% year-end target.
Australian fleet capacity expanded 25% year-over-year, and bid pipeline grew to $15 billion, including $4 billion in new infrastructure opportunities.
summary: Q1 FY2025 revenue was $392 million, up 18% from Q2 2024, but adjusted EBITDA of $100 million (25.5% margin) was flat year-over-year, hit by severe weather in Australia and Canada. Adjusted EPS was $0.52, impacted by $11 million of higher depreciation ($0.30 per share). Management kept full-year 2025 guidance unchanged, expecting weather impacts to be made up in H2, with backlog expected to reach a record $4 billion by mid-year, up from $3.2 billion pro forma.

negative_highlights: Management explicitly stated it does not anticipate being EBITDA positive or cash flow positive in 2025.
Gross margin was 84%, down from 85% in Q1 2024 due to temporary factory clean room expansion costs.
Operating losses increased slightly to $7.3 million compared to the prior quarter, though still well below last year's levels.
positive_highlights: Net sales grew 42% YoY to $9.2 million driven by increased utilization and new accounts.
CMS issued HCPCS code C8004 on April 1st, enabling reimbursement for both mapping and treatment phases of radioembolization.
Adjusted EBITDA losses narrowed significantly to $5.5 million from $10.4 million in the prior year quarter.
summary: TriSalus reported Q1 FY2025 net sales of $9.2 million, representing a 42% year-over-year increase and an 11% sequential gain. The company confirmed its full-year guidance of at least 50% revenue growth but explicitly stated it will not be EBITDA or cash flow positive in 2025 due to strategic investments in commercial expansion and new clinical applications. Gross margins were 84%, slightly down from the prior year quarter due to a factory clean room expansion that is now complete.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA loss of $22 million was driven by a single underperforming contract with prior year claim impacts.
Total revenue declined 4% YoY due to the intentional reduction in membership base from exiting unprofitable plans.
One specific payer partner remains an outlier requiring collaborative resolution for performance issues.
positive_highlights: Three of four markets achieved breakeven or better performance, with the outlier being a single payer partner.
PMPM funding increased by 8% to $1,063 due to improved disease burden capture and favorable contract terms.
Utilization metrics trended positively including a 21% decrease in ED visits per 1,000 and an 11% drop in high-cost claims >$20k.
summary: Q1 FY2025 revenue was $373 million (4% YoY decrease) and membership fell 8%, both in line with expectations but reflecting an intentional strategy to exit unprofitable plans. Adjusted EBITDA reported a loss of $22 million, driven by a single outlier payer partner responsible for roughly one-quarter of the business that is being actively remediated; excluding this specific impact, the rest of the business operates at or near breakeven. Management reiterated full-year 2025 guidance despite these headwinds and noted positive trends in utilization metrics (e.g., ED visits down 21%) and PMPM funding (+8%).

negative_highlights: NII per share down $0.10 QoQ to $0.45
Non-accruals increased to 3.5% of debt at cost
Tariff uncertainty tempering near-term M&A activity
positive_highlights: New investments at 565 bps spread, above recent quarters
Portfolio weighted average interest coverage improved to 2.0x
97% floating-rate assets vs. 55% floating-rate liabilities
summary: Q1 FY2025 NII was $0.45 per share, down from $0.55 in Q4, driven by lower base rates, non-recurring income runoff, reduced Logan JV dividend, and higher non-accruals. Non-accruals rose to 3.5% of debt at cost (1.8% at fair value) with four new first-lien names. Management called this quarter 'reflective of our earnings baseline,' cited tariff-driven M&A slowdown, and noted potential tailwinds from SPV facility repricing and full-quarter portfolio impact. GAAP EPS was $0.11, NAV per share $19.62.

negative_highlights: Incremental contribution margin is only about $0.50 per revenue dollar versus a stated 70-80% goal, and marketing/onboarding spend is expected to flatten only in 12-20 months
Fiscal year-to-date revenue growth of 10.3% trails the Q3 rate of 16%, reflecting quarter-to-quarter variability management explicitly flagged
The FDA extended the enforcement deadline by 30 months, removing the regulatory catalyst some investors may have been pricing
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 16% YoY to $5.9M while operating income grew 43% to $1.8M, with opex up only 7%
GAAP net income to common shareholders rose 33% to $1.9M and EPS was $0.10 versus $0.08
Roughly two-thirds of new traceability customers onboard via the automated wizard, and deferred revenue of $3.7M is expected to convert to recognized revenue over 12-15 months
summary: ReposiTrak reported Q3 FY2025 revenue up 16% YoY to $5.9M with recurring revenue up 15% to $5.8M; operating income rose 43% to $1.8M, GAAP net income grew 27% to $2.0M, and EPS was $0.10 versus $0.08. Management reiterated its 10-20% annual revenue growth and faster earnings growth targets with no specific quarterly guidance, and reaffirmed its goal to double the historical $20M revenue base over the next several years. The clearest change versus prior periods is the FDA's 30-month extension of the food traceability enforcement deadline, which management framed as helpful to onboarding pace while noting adoption is now driven by retailer requirements rather than the regulatory date. Cash was $28.1M at March 31, with $3.7M of deferred revenue and continued capital returns via dividends, buybacks, and preferred redemption.

negative_highlights: Revenue was only $0.2 million, down $0.3 million sequentially and $0.3 million year-over-year
Net loss of $7.6 million with operating expenses still $6 million against minimal revenue
Management explicitly hedged the $16 million 2025 outlook ('I should never give forward-looking statements') and cited potential discounting pressure from larger competitors
positive_highlights: Cash rose to $10.1 million at quarter-end from $1.2 million at end-2024, aided by a $20 million at-the-market raise
Debt and associated interest were reduced by $3 million via term-loan conversion-price lowering and subsequent conversions
G&A fell $0.9 million year-over-year to $4.3 million and adjusted net loss improved to $6.8 million from $6.9 million in Q4 2024
summary: Q1 2025 revenue was just $0.2 million, down $0.3 million both sequentially and year-over-year, as the Gulf offshore season only began at the end of March. Operating expenses were flat at $6 million, net loss was $7.6 million, and adjusted net loss was $6.8 million, with cash rising to $10.1 million after a $20 million ATM raise and a $3 million debt/interest reduction. Management reaffirmed its prior ~$16 million 2025 revenue outlook, about three-quarters from day-rate utilization at roughly $50,000/day and one-quarter from software/proposals, but gave no formal guidance and repeatedly hedged that forecast with oil-price and execution caveats.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA of $2.2 million missed the outlook, primarily driven by front-loaded lease depreciation costs associated with rapid growth in Q4 and early Q1.
Loss from operations widened to a loss of $500,000 compared to income of $3.8 million in the prior year quarter.
Wayfair gross originations declined significantly (approximate volume of $17M) due to category challenges within home furnishings and mattresses.
positive_highlights: Gross originations grew 15.4% YoY to $64.2 million, beating the outlook for 11% growth.
Revenue of $71.9M came in slightly above expectations at a 10.6% increase year-over-year.
KPay originations surged 57% and now represent approximately 35% of total gross originations.
summary: Katapult reported Q1 FY2025 revenue of $71.9 million (up 10.6% YoY) and gross originations growth of 15.4%, both slightly beating guidance; however, adjusted EBITDA was $2.2 million, missing the outlook due to front-loaded lease depreciation from strong Q4/Q1 origination volume. Management reiterated full-year 2025 guidance for at least 20% gross originations growth and revenue growth of at least 20%, while projecting breakeven adjusted EBITDA in Q2.

negative_highlights: Cash position remains low at $2.6M end of quarter
Revenue guidance not provided; described as lumpy
Dependence on future financing and cost control; macro environment described as difficult
positive_highlights: Revenue up 44% year-over-year to ~$0.25M, including first human product sales
Operating expenses down 35% and cash used in operations down 48% year-over-year
Licensing discussions with over 10 companies, seven with combined market value over $600B
summary: VolitionRX reported Q1 FY2025 revenue of almost $0.25 million, up 44% year-over-year, including first-ever human product sales. Operating expenses fell 35% and cash used in operations dropped 48% to $4.3 million. Management reiterated full-year cash flow neutrality goal, emphasized confidential licensing discussions with over 10 companies, and noted a new $6.25 million convertible loan after quarter-end. Revenue remains lumpy; no FY2025 guidance provided.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined to $2.0 million from $2.4 million year over year on lower karaoke sales
Guidance that karaoke sales will decrease over the next 12 months due to tariffs on China-manufactured products
Other expenses rose to $6.5 million from $25,000 on a one-time non-cash $6.5 million warrant fair-value charge; G&A increased to $2.5 million from $2.1 million
positive_highlights: Gross margin improved to 25% from 21%, attributed to a decrease in returns
Stockholders' equity recovered to $3.3 million at March 31, 2025 from a $11.6 million deficit at year-end, restoring NASDAQ listing compliance
SemiCab India described as exclusive technology provider to the NDFE, with ~$400 million of the consortium's $1.4 billion annual freight spend identified as initial addressable market
summary: Q1 FY2025 sales fell to $2.0 million from $2.4 million a year ago, driven by lower Singing Machine karaoke sales, while gross profit held flat at $0.5 million and gross margin improved to 25% from 21% on lower returns. G&A rose to $2.5 million from $2.1 million on $0.5 million of SemiCab investment, and other expenses jumped to $6.5 million from $25,000 due to a one-time non-cash $6.5 million warrant remeasurement charge. Management explicitly guided karaoke sales to decrease over the next 12 months due to China tariffs, offset by expectations for substantially higher SemiCab revenue; stockholders' equity returned to $3.3 million and NASDAQ compliance was restored after the warrant liability was reclassified to equity. Management said it is 'all in' on SemiCab and continues to seek strategic alternatives for the Singing Machine business.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined to $1.6M from $2.2M year-over-year.
Net loss widened to $737K in Q1 '25 vs. $573K prior year.
Year-over-year comparisons hurt by $1.2M prior-year contract and EMEA transition.
positive_highlights: Revenue up 10% sequentially to $1.6 million in Q1 '25.
Gross margin healthy at 82.6%; SG&A reduced 23% year-over-year.
Cash increased to over $3 million, and debt more than halved to ~$762K.
summary: Q1 FY2025 revenue fell to $1.6M from $2.2M year-over-year due to a large financial services customer's contract timing, though revenue rose 10% sequentially. The customer upgraded to a one-to-many biometric solution, contributing $690K in Q1 and expected to generate ~$3M over two years starting Q1 2026. Gross margin dipped to 82.6%, and net loss widened to $737K due to higher share count, while cash rose to $3.1M from warrant proceeds. The company is shifting to BIO-key branded products in EMEA and highlights expanding recurring revenue over $6M.

negative_highlights: Marketing services revenues fell 15% YoY and 27% QoQ to $14M
Q2 2025 guidance implies online game revenues down 28%-35% YoY and 10%-18% QoQ
Q2 2025 net loss guidance of $20M-$30M, with marketing services down 14%-19% YoY
positive_highlights: Online game revenues of $117M were well above prior guidance and flat YoY, up 7% QoQ
Non-GAAP net loss narrowed to $16M from $22M in Q1 2024
Share repurchase of 5.5M ADS for approximately $67M as of May 15, 2025
summary: Sohu reported Q1 2025 total revenues of $136M, down 3% YoY but up 1% QoQ, with marketing services at $14M (down 15% YoY and 27% QoQ) and online game revenues of $117M (flat YoY, up 7% QoQ). GAAP net income was $182M, driven by a $199M reversal of a previously recognized uncertain tax position; excluding this, non-GAAP net loss was $16M versus a $22M loss a year ago. Q2 2025 guidance implies marketing services of $60-$70M (down 14%-19% YoY, up 17%-24% QoQ) and online game revenues of $96-$106M (down 28%-35% YoY, down 10%-18% QoQ), with a net loss of $20-$30M. The company repurchased 5.5M ADS for about $67M as of May 15, 2025, while advertising remains soft with luxury and alcohol spending declining.

negative_highlights: Management explicitly stated they are being 'cautious' on Gross Business Volume (GBV) guidance due to potential rate drops if the Red Sea reopens or tariffs impact trade lanes
CEO noted that while transaction volumes will grow, revenue growth may be dampened by flat-fee structures and external volatility in air/ocean rates
positive_highlights: Record revenue of $6.9 million representing a 30% year-over-year increase
Gross margin improved to 66.8% (IFRS) and 73.7% (non-IFRS), up from prior periods
Adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed to negative $3.0 million compared to negative $3.6 million in Q1 last year
summary: Freightos reported Q1 FY2025 revenue of $6.9 million (30% YoY growth) and adjusted EBITDA loss narrowing to negative $3.0 million from a prior year loss of $3.6 million, driven by record transactions exceeding guidance expectations. Management reiterated full-year 2025 guidance for revenue between $7.0M-$7.1M (23-25% YoY growth) and adjusted EBITDA losses of negative $2.8M to $2.9M in Q2, while noting that Gross Margin expanded significantly on an IFRS basis.

negative_highlights: Total revenue declined due to timing shifts where two major clients deferred renewal from Q1 to Q4.
Management explicitly stated they are not providing official guidance for the year, citing note weakness in-term disruption in their transition model.
Operating loss widened slightly compared to expectations despite cost reductions.
positive_highlights: Gross margin expanded significantly to record levels of 88% from Q1 2024's 82%.
Subscription revenue increased, reaching 99% of total revenue compared to 87% in the prior year.
Three large Fortune 500 customers executed expansion renewals with ARR increases.
summary: CXAI reported Q1 FY2025 results with a revenue decline driven by timing shifts where two large customers renewed in Q4 instead of Q1, rather than structural weakness. Gross margins expanded to record levels at 88% due to cost discipline and cloud savings, while operating loss narrowed despite one-time G&A costs. Management explicitly declined to provide official guidance for the year but emphasized a strategic pivot toward recurring revenue (99%) over one-time fees.

negative_highlights: Total revenue declined to $4.0 million from $5.0 million year-over-year as BARDA development services wind down
Operating loss widened to $5.2 million from $3.7 million as R&D rose to $2.9 million from $1.5 million
Adjusted EBITDA loss widened to $4.0 million from $2.9 million; cash fell to $38.7 million from $43.6 million at year-end
positive_highlights: Gross margin expanded to 19% from 12% on a favorable revenue mix
NexoBrid US revenue rose 207% year-over-year and 31% sequentially per Vericel
VALUE Phase III on track with interim analysis anticipated mid-2026; Kerecis added as a partner alongside Solventum, Mölnlycke and MIMEDX
summary: Q1 2025 total revenue fell to $4.0 million from $5.0 million a year ago on lower BARDA-funded development services as NexoBrid development nears completion. Gross margin improved to 19% from 12% on mix, but R&D jumped to $2.9 million from $1.5 million, widening operating loss to $5.2 million from $3.7 million; the reported net loss of $0.7 million ($0.07 per share) benefited from noncash warrant revaluation versus a $9.7 million loss last year. Management reiterated full-year revenue guidance of $24 million for 2025 and $30-33 million for 2026, unchanged. Operating progress continued with the VALUE Phase III on track (interim data mid-2026), the Kerecis collaboration added, and NexoBrid US revenue up 207% year-over-year per partner Vericel.

negative_highlights: Total revenue fell 11% to $40.2 million and global cinema revenue fell 12% to $36.4 million on weaker attendance in all three countries
Cash used in operating activities widened to $7.7 million from $2.8 million, and cash and equivalents stood at just $5.9 million
NAB bridge loan maturity was extended only to May 23, 2025, and the New York live-theater loan is still being negotiated for extension
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA swung to positive $2.9 million from a negative $4.0 million in Q1 2024, a 173% improvement
Global real estate operating income rose 79% to $1.6 million, the best first quarter since Q2 2018
Net loss attributable to Reading narrowed to $4.8 million ($0.21/share) from $13.2 million ($0.59/share) in Q1 2024
summary: Q1 2025 total revenue fell 11% to $40.2 million versus Q1 2024, with global cinema revenue down 12% to $36.4 million and a global operating loss of $6.9 million, though that loss narrowed 8.5% and adjusted EBITDA turned positive at $2.9 million (up 173% from a negative $4.0 million). GAAP loss per share improved to $0.21 from $0.59, aided by a $6.5 million gain on the Wellington asset sale that also eliminated NZD18.8 million of Westpac and $6.1 million of Bank of America debt. No formal financial guidance was provided; management cited improving Q2 2025 box office, the pending AUD32 million Cannon Park sale expected to close May 21, and continued lender negotiations on near-term debt maturities. The quarter marked a fifth straight stretch of strike-affected box office weakness offset by real estate monetization and cost cuts.

negative_highlights: CLO portfolio incurred mark-to-market losses of negative $0.24 per share, exceeding net interest income and modest hedge gains.
Overall economic return for the quarter was negative 3.2% due to declining prices on CLO mezzanine debt and equity.
Credit spreads widened significantly in March and April, driven by macro volatility and tariff fears, causing price declines across the board.
positive_highlights: Agency mortgage strategy generated positive portfolio income of approximately $2.55 million despite market turbulence.
Conversion to a closed-end fund was completed successfully with minimal impact on net asset value, estimated at only $0.01 per share.
European CLO equity investments outperformed US counterparts due to muted impact from credit spread widening.
summary: Ellington Credit Company reported a net loss of $0.23 per share and adjusted distributable earnings of $0.26 per share for calendar Q1 FY2025, driven by mark-to-market losses in the CLO portfolio which outweighed gains from the agency mortgage strategy. The company successfully converted to a registered closed-end fund on April 1st, liquidating its remaining agency mortgage pools with minimal impact on NAV, and has since increased its CLO portfolio size to $284 million as of late April. Management indicated that while adjusted earnings covered dividends for Q1, coverage in the upcoming quarter may be tight before resuming full coverage in Q3.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined 22% year-over-year to $32.1 million as average spot rates for product and Suezmax tankers fell about 25% and 24%, respectively
Voyage costs of $10.5 million and running costs of $7.0 million remain significant, with running costs up $1.1 million year-over-year due to fleet expansion

$129 million capital commitment for dry bulk vessel acquisitions and a $40 million April payment reduced cash from $227 million to $190 million, though management expects profitable operations to rebuild cash
positive_highlights: Net income rose 190% to $11.3 million quarter-over-quarter, with revenue up 22.5% to $32.1 million from Q4 2024
Debt-free balance sheet with cash of approximately $227 million, roughly three times the company's market capitalization

Fleet expanding from 4 to 19 vessels by Q3 2025, with seven of 13 current ships on time charter and seven of 19 vessels non-Chinese built, potentially benefiting from proposed U.S. port fees on Chinese-built ships
summary: Imperial Petroleum reported Q1 FY2025 revenue of $32.1 million, down 22% year-over-year from Q1 2024 due to lower market rates, but up 22.5% sequentially from Q4 2024; net income was $11.3 million (EPS $0.32), up 190% quarter-over-quarter. EBITDA was $14.7 million, and the company ended the quarter debt-free with cash of approximately $227 million (about $190 million after a $40 million vessel payment in April). No explicit forward guidance was provided, though management highlighted fleet expansion to 19 vessels by Q3 2025 and positive near-term dirty tanker market expectations from OPEC output increases and sanctions on Russian oil, while noting clean product tanker weakness.

negative_highlights: Q4 net income fell to $2.7 million from $2.9 million and diluted EPS was flat at $0.04 despite revenue growth, with interest expense up to $6.1 million
Net debt increased to $366.7 million from $312.7 million at prior fiscal year-end following roughly $115 million of capital deployment
Publishing performance revenue fell 13% in Q4 and recorded music physical revenue dropped 26% on a lighter release schedule
positive_highlights: FY2025 revenue of $158.7 million grew 10% and came in above the top end of previously stated guidance
Adjusted EBITDA rose 18% to $65.7 million for the year and OIBDA rose 24% to $61.4 million, aided by higher gross margin and operating leverage
Publishing sync revenue jumped 51% in Q4 to $5.5 million and recorded music digital revenue rose 19% on DSP price increases and subscriber growth
summary: FY2025 revenue rose 10% to $158.7 million, above the top end of prior guidance, with adjusted EBITDA up 18% to $65.7 million and diluted EPS of $0.12 versus $0.01. Q4 revenue grew 6% to $41.4 million with adjusted EBITDA up 14% to $18.2 million, but net income slipped to $2.7 million and diluted EPS was flat at $0.04. FY2026 guidance was initiated at $164-169 million revenue and $68-72 million adjusted EBITDA, and management said the guide does not assume a repeat of prior-year hit-driven revenue or audit recoveries. Net debt rose to $366.7 million from $312.7 million a year ago after roughly $115 million of acquisitions.

negative_highlights: Guest traffic declined 3.5% in Q1, and management expects down-4 traffic for the balance of the year.
2025 revenue guidance was reduced to $1.21B–$1.23B from $1.225B–$1.25B, with comps guided to approximately zero.
Q2 comps are expected to decline ~3%, pressured by a 240 bps loyalty revenue headwind and less price benefit.
positive_highlights: Restaurant-level operating margin improved 330 bps to 14.3% in Q1, driven by labor efficiencies.
Adjusted EBITDA more than doubled to $27.9M from $14.5M year-over-year.
Repaid $17.8M of debt using free cash flow and $5.8M from property sales, reducing principal to $171.7M.
summary: Q1 revenue was $392.4M, up from $388.5M, with comps up 3.1% on price, but traffic down 3.5%. Restaurant-level margin improved 330 bps to 14.3%, and adjusted EBITDA rose to $27.9M from $13.4M. Guidance was trimmed: total revenue now $1.21B–$1.23B (from $1.225B–$1.25B), comps expected flat for the year, Q2 comps down ~3%, and capex raised to ~$30M. Full-year EBITDA guidance held at $60M–$65M, despite absorbing tariff costs and a down-4 traffic assumption.

negative_highlights: Time charter revenues decreased by about 5% compared to Q1 2024 due to fleet size reduction and write-offs
Dry bulk contracting slumped significantly with only 0.1% of the global fleet contracted in newbuilding for H1 2025, down from record levels previously
Global seaborne dry bulk trade expected to drop by 1% this year due to softer Chinese demand and lower steel production outside India/China
positive_highlights: Fleet utilization reached 99.6% for the first quarter
Time charter equivalent rate increased to $15,739/day compared to $15,051 in Q1 2024 due to disciplined commercial strategy and better rates on fixed charters
Secured $86.8 million of contracted revenues for 66% of remaining ownership days in 2025
summary: Diana Shipping reported Q1 FY2025 time charter revenues of $54.9 million, a decrease of approximately 5% year-over-year to the prior quarter's adjusted EBITDA decline and lower fleet size due to vessel sales. Management noted that while they secured improved rates on specific charters, overall market levels are historically healthy but sentiment is lagging amidst geopolitical uncertainty and tariffs. The company declared a quarterly cash dividend of $0.01 per share.

negative_highlights: No binding offtake agreements finalized for India facility; securing contracts remains a gating item for commercial operations in late 2027.
European site selection is still ongoing with no specific country or timeline confirmed beyond Q3/Q4 targets.
positive_highlights: First quarter of material revenues with a $10.8M total beat against prior non-material reporting baseline.
India JV CapEx came in below original estimates at $176M, validating the low-cost manufacturing strategy.
Liquidity position enhanced to ~$13M cash balance following financing proceeds and debt repayment.
summary: Loop Industries reported Q4 FY2025 revenue of $10.8 million, driven by a $10.4 million upfront royalty from Reed Societe Generale Group and $600k in engineering services for the India JV. Operating expenses decreased significantly to $2.6M (down 44% YoY) as the Quebec facility transitioned to intermittent operation. Management raised guidance expectations, projecting an additional $750k in Q4 engineering revenue and anticipating $5-10 million of licensing revenue next year.

negative_highlights: Q1 revenue ($1.3M) remains roughly half of the prior year comparable period due to divestitures.
GAAP net loss widened to $7.1 million for full year 2024, driven by noncash charges including a $10 million valuation adjustment on an equity investment.
Management explicitly warns that Q3 and Q4 results will be approached with caution due to tariff impacts and HSN consolidation risks.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed to $792,000 in Q4 (improvement of $361,000 over Q4 '23) and $0.7 million in Q1 '25.
Operating costs reduced to a run rate of approximately $9 million annually through restructuring and cost-cutting measures.
Strategic transaction with United Trademark Group closed in April, providing $3 million liquidity and saving over $1 million annually in interest.
summary: Xcel Brands reported Q1 FY2025 revenues of $1.3 million, a slight increase from Q4 but significantly lower than the prior year due to the sale of the Lori Goldstein brand and exit from wholesale operations. The company posted a GAAP net loss of $2.8 million (or -$1.18 per share) and an adjusted EBITDA loss of $0.7 million, representing significant improvements over the prior year but still reflecting a miss on profitability expectations. Management provided full-year 2025 guidance for adjusted EBITDA between $1 million and $2.5 million, explicitly stating that this range includes potential negative impacts from tariffs and the HSN studio relocation.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to $22.2 million ($0.74 per share) from $19.6 million ($0.65 per share) a year ago
Gross margin contracted 120 basis points to 19.8% as note, distribution, and occupancy costs deleveraged 160 basis points
Total net sales fell 7.1% to $107.6 million, with eight fewer stores and additional closures planned
positive_highlights: Comparable sales improved sequentially to -7% in Q1 from -11.2% in Q4 FY2024, with May comps down just 2.2%
Product margins improved 40 basis points on higher initial markups, and management sees no material tariff impact for the remainder of the year
Debt-free balance sheet with $92.6 million total liquidity and continued share repurchase activity
summary: Tilly's Q1 FY2025 net sales fell 7.1% to $107.6 million with comparable sales down 7%, gross margin contracting 120 bps to 19.8%, and net loss widening to $22.2 million ($0.74 per share) from $19.6 million ($0.65). Q2 guidance calls for net sales of $150-$158 million (comp -5% to flat) and EPS of -$0.09 to +$0.07; May comps improved to -2.2%. Management highlighted improving comp trends over Q4's -11.2%, positive product margin, and no material tariff impact, but store closures continue and a full-year net loss is projected.

negative_highlights: Net sales fell to $266 million from $279.8 million and comparable sales declined 3.5%
Gross margin contracted 320 basis points to 38.1% due to planned promotional initiatives, and adjusted EBITDA margin fell to 10.2% from 13.7% a year ago
Full-year revenue guidance was cut to $1.03-$1.055 billion to reflect the footwear pause and approximately $20 million of net tariff impact
positive_highlights: Sub-brands are overachieving expectations by 2-6x, with about 90% of sub-brand purchasers also adding core Torrid products and planned penetration rising from roughly 10% to as much as 30% of the portfolio in 2026
SG&A declined $6.5 million to $70 million and leveraged 100 basis points to 26.3% of sales, driven by store optimization and contract renegotiations
Total debt was reduced by $16.2 million year over year to $284.5 million, with no borrowings outstanding under the revolver and $141 million in total liquidity
summary: Torrid reported Q1 FY2025 net sales of $266 million, down from $279.8 million a year ago, with comparable sales down 3.5% and adjusted EBITDA of $27.1 million at the high end of guidance but down from $38.2 million last year. Gross margin contracted 320 basis points to 38.1% on planned promotions, while net income fell to $5.9 million or $0.06 per share from $12.2 million or $0.12 per share. Management revised full-year net sales guidance to $1.03-$1.055 billion to reflect a $40-$45 million hit from pausing the footwear business, but maintained full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance of $95-$105 million including a $20 million net tariff impact. The company accelerated planned store closures to approximately 180 for the year, up from the prior 40-50 target, and forecast a 150-250 basis point EBITDA margin benefit in fiscal 2026.

negative_highlights: Reported GAAP net loss of $117M and combined net loss of $166M, driven by TechTarget's contribution period, integration costs and noncash impairments
Combined revenue broadly flat year-over-year with management describing the market as subdued and guiding 2025 like-for-like revenue to be broadly flat again
Value-based renewal rates flat year-on-year in Intelligence & Advisory and flat to slightly down in parts of Brand to Demand
positive_highlights: Cost synergy program tracking well ahead of the $5M year-1 target with high confidence in meeting or beating the $45M run-rate target by year 3
$490M combined-company full-year revenue came in line with previous guidance despite a subdued backdrop
Year-end cash, equivalents and note weakness in-term investments of roughly $354M; early tactical cross-note wins and larger strategic proposals noted in Q1
summary: Informa TechTarget reported 2024 reported revenues of $285M with a GAAP net loss of $117M and adjusted EBITDA of $31M, reflecting 12 months of Informa Tech and roughly one month of legacy TechTarget post-December 2 close. On a combined basis, full-year revenues were $490M, in line with prior guidance and broadly flat underlying, with combined net loss of $166M and combined adjusted EBITDA of $82M. Management guided 2025 to broadly flat like-for-like revenues and higher adjusted EBITDA, supported by overdelivery of cost synergies (tracking ahead of the $5M year-1 target against $45M by year 3) and non-recurrence of one-off combination costs. The market backdrop remains subdued with no clear improvement or deterioration versus 2024, and value-based renewal rates are flat to slightly down year-on-year.

negative_highlights: Net sales fell 12% to $102.7 million, with direct channel sales down 14.6% on lower web traffic.
Gross margin rate declined 80 bps year-over-year, and SG&A deleveraged 290 bps as a percent of sales.
Inventory rose 29% to $176.1 million versus last year, and borrowings reached $64 million versus $11 million a year ago.
positive_highlights: March and April combined gross margin improved more than 300 bps year-over-year on promotional reset and direct-to-factory sourcing savings.
Annualized expense savings initiative of approximately $15 million, with at least $10 million landing in FY2025.
New $100 million asset-based lending facility extends to 2030 with improved rates and flexibility, replacing a revolver that expired in 2027.
summary: Duluth Trading reported Q1 FY2025 net sales of $102.7 million, down 12% year-over-year (down 10.2% excluding a wholesale shipment shift), with a reported EPS loss of $0.45 and adjusted EPS loss of $0.32; adjusted EBITDA was negative $3.8 million. Gross margin fell 80 bps on February clearance, though March-April gross margin improved over 300 bps on reduced promotions and direct-to-factory sourcing. Management maintained FY2025 adjusted EBITDA guidance of $20-25 million, announced roughly $15 million in annualized expense savings ($10 million in FY2025), and cited about $14 million in added tariff costs already contemplated in that guidance. Inventory rose 29% to $176.1 million versus last year, and net liquidity stood at $45 million after transitioning to a new $100 million ABL facility.

negative_highlights: Total revenue fell 7.2% year over year to $69.6 million and 8.9% quarter over quarter, with average active subscribers down 1.8% to 133,468
Gross margin contracted to 31.5% from 37.9% a year ago, driven by higher revenue share costs and fulfillment costs at 29.3% of revenue versus 27.5%

Adjusted EBITDA swung to negative $1.3 million from positive $6.5 million a year ago, and free cash flow worsened to negative $6.4 million from negative $1.4 million on higher rental product purchases
positive_highlights: Ending active subscribers reached a record 147,157, up from 119,778 at Q4 2024 and about 1% higher year over year, with the strongest quarterly retention in four years
Q1 inventory volume received rose 24% year over year, with 36 new brands and over 1,000 new styles; new receipts are expected up over 420% YoY in Q2 and 134% for the rest of the year
Free cash flow guidance remained unchanged at negative $30-40 million for the full year, and full-year subscriber growth guidance stayed at double digits
summary: Q1 FY2025 revenue was $69.6 million, down 7.2% year over year and 8.9% quarter over quarter, with subscription and reserve rental revenue down 6.2% on lower revenue per subscriber and lower average active subscribers (133,468, -1.8% YoY). Gross margin contracted sharply to 31.5% from 37.9% a year ago and 37.7% in Q4, adjusted EBITDA swung to negative $1.3 million (-1.9% of revenue) from $6.5 million, and free cash flow was negative $6.4 million versus negative $1.4 million. Offsets came from subscriber trends: ending active subscribers reached a record 147,157 (+1% YoY, up from 119,778 at Q4), retention was the strongest in four years, and inventory receipts rose 24% YoY. Full-year guidance was unchanged (double-digit ending subscriber growth, cash consumption of negative $30-40 million), while Q2 revenue is guided to $76-80 million with adjusted EBITDA margin of negative 22%, and tariff impact is excluded from guidance.

negative_highlights: Revenue fell 46% year over year to $78 million from $144.4 million
Net loss of $16.8 million and adjusted EBITDA of negative $10.8 million, with a $19.4 million unrealized digital-asset fair value loss

Managed mining capacity of 20.6 EH/s and hosting capacity of 478 MW at quarter-end were well below 28.6 EH/s and 644 MW a year earlier, due to expired procurement contracts and supplier fleet relocations
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA excluding $19.4 million of unrealized digital-asset fair value losses would have been approximately positive $8.6 million
Managed mining capacity rebounded from 20.6 EH/s at March 31 to 28.3 EH/s by April 30 and 34.1 EH/s in May, aided by more efficient Antminer S21 series units
Average electricity price declined 18% versus Q1 2024, and the Oklahoma facility acquisition lifted self-owned hashrate to 4.2 EH/s
summary: BitFuFu reported Q1 FY2025 total revenue of $78 million, down 46% from $144.4 million a year earlier, driven by higher network difficulty, the April 2024 halving, and expired or disrupted hashrate procurement contracts. Net loss was $16.8 million and adjusted EBITDA was negative $10.8 million, though excluding $19.4 million of unrealized digital-asset fair value losses adjusted EBITDA would have been roughly positive $8.6 million. Managed hashrate fell to 20.6 EH/s from 28.6 EH/s at March 31, 2024 and hosting capacity to 478 MW from 644 MW, but management reported a rebound to 28.3 EH/s by April 30 and 34.1 EH/s in May. No numerical revenue or EBITDA guidance was issued, and the call included no Q&A session.

negative_highlights: Total net revenue fell to $35.1 million from $44.6 million a year earlier, and agribusiness revenue declined to $33.6 million from $43.3 million.
Fresh packed lemon average price per carton dropped to $14.52 from $17.85, with the company citing an oversupplied market and competitors note below cost.
Adjusted EBITDA swung to a loss of $167,000 from a gain of $16.6 million, and adjusted diluted EPS fell to a loss of $0.17 from income of $0.44.
positive_highlights: Sunkist sales and marketing merger expected to save approximately $5 million per year in note and marketing expenses and improve EBITDA by approximately $5 million annually beginning in fiscal 2026.
Avocado revenue rose to $2.8 million from $2.3 million a year ago, with average price per pound up sharply to $2.26 from $1.47.
Total costs and expenses fell 22% to $38.5 million, and operating loss improved by $1.3 million to $3.3 million.
summary: Q2 FY2025 total net revenue fell to $35.1 million from $44.6 million a year earlier, with agribusiness revenue of $33.6 million versus $43.3 million, driven by an oversupplied lemon market that cut fresh packed lemon pricing to $14.52 per carton from $17.85. The company reported a net loss of $0.20 per diluted share and an adjusted net loss of $0.17 per diluted share versus adjusted EPS of $0.44 a year ago, with adjusted EBITDA of negative $167,000 compared to a $16.6 million gain. Management lowered FY2025 fresh lemon volume guidance to 4.5-5 million cartons from 5-5.5 million and issued an early FY2026 estimate of 4-4.5 million cartons, while announcing a citrus sales and marketing merger with Sunkist Growers expected to save about $5 million annually and add roughly $5 million to EBITDA starting in FY2026. The merger will reduce top-line revenue by transitioning the $27-28 million brokered fruit business to Sunkist, but management expects improved cost structure and packing margins.

negative_highlights: Q4 swung to a net loss of $0.7M (-$0.04/share) from prior-year net income of $1.3M, including $4.6M ($0.24/share) of tariff costs
Q4 revenue growth slowed to 1.9% ($193.1M) versus 5.5% for the full year
FY26 guidance explicitly excludes recently enacted tariffs, and management declined to quantify tariff timing impact or market-share gains
positive_highlights: FY25 gross margin expanded 1.8 points to 20.3% and gross profit rose 16.1% to a record $153.8M
Operating cash flow of $45.5M and net bank debt reduced $32.6M to $81.4M, with $144.6M total cash and availability

FY25 net sales grew 5.5% to a record $757.4M and gross margin expanded 1.8 points to 20.3%, but the full year still produced a $19.5M net loss. FY26 guidance calls for $780-800M net sales (3-5.6% growth) and $86-91M operating income (4.3-10.4% growth), explicitly excluding recently enacted tariffs. negative_highlights: Total sales fell 4.9% YoY to ~$154M and comps declined 5.7%
Adjusted EPS dropped to $0.88 from $1.22 in the prior-year quarter
Full-year guidance withdrawn and most forward guidance suspended; quarter-to-date May sales still down mid-single digits
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA of $27.3M came in above the high end of previously guided range on disciplined expense management
Gross margin remained high at 71.8% despite a 110 bps YoY decline
Strong balance sheet with $31M cash, zero ABL borrowings, and continued quarterly dividend of $0.08 per share
summary: J.Jill reported Q1 FY2025 total sales of ~$154M, down 4.9% YoY, with comparable sales down 5.7% and gross margin of 71.8% (down 110 bps), while adjusted EBITDA of $27.3M exceeded the high end of prior guidance. Adjusted EPS fell to $0.88 from $1.22 a year earlier, and the company withdrew its prior full-year guidance and suspended most forward guidance, citing macro uncertainty and a new CEO's business assessment. Quarter-to-date through May, total sales remained down mid-single digits, and inventories were up 14% (or ~5% normalized), signaling near-term margin pressure.

negative_highlights: Revenue fell to $51.7 million from $67.9 million, with Direct down 23.6% and Indirect down 25.6%
Gross margin contracted 380 basis points to 47.5% from 51.3%, driven by channel shift and higher outbound freight
Prior guidance was suspended with no forward guidance provided, and the company plans to close 10 unprofitable full-line stores
positive_highlights: Indirect segment over-delivered plan by double digits, with first order shipped to Costco and a launch on Urban Outfitters Marketplace
Recently acquired customers comprised 45% of the active 12-month file versus 30% last year, skewing toward the 18- to 34-year-old demographic
