summary: Vera Bradley reported Q1 FY2026 revenue of $51.7 million, down from $67.9 million a year ago, with both segments declining: Direct fell 23.6% to $43.1 million and Indirect fell 25.6% to $8.6 million. Non-GAAP net loss from continuing operations widened to $10.0 million ($0.36 per diluted share) from $6.6 million ($0.22) last year, as gross margin contracted to 47.5% from 51.3% and SG&A rose to 74.2% of revenue from 65.7%. The company suspended prior guidance and is not providing forward guidance, citing executive and Board leadership changes and significant consumer uncertainty. Leadership transitions include CEO Jackie Ardrey's departure at end of July, an interim Executive Chairman, a new CFO, and a new Strategy and Transformation Committee.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA declined 20% year-over-year
Free cash flow of $4.9 million was down from $9.4 million in the prior-year quarter
E-commerce adjusted EBITDA declined and remains a drag on overall profitability
positive_highlights: Daily same-store sales rose 6.2% year-over-year, the fastest rate in five quarters
Adjusted EBITDA grew 14% sequentially to $8.1 million, driven by the brick-and-mortar segment
Free cash flow turned positive at $4.9 million, improving from negative $1.9 million in Q1
summary: High Tide reported Q2 FY2025 revenue of $137.8 million, up 11% year-over-year but down 3% sequentially due to three fewer days. Adjusted EBITDA was $8.1 million, down 20% year-over-year but up 14% sequentially, while free cash flow fell to $4.9 million from $9.4 million a year ago. The company achieved daily same-store sales growth of 6.2%, its fastest in five quarters, and brick-and-mortar revenue grew 16%. E-commerce continued to drag on profitability, and no formal guidance was provided, though management expressed confidence in continued margin expansion and store growth.

negative_highlights: Net loss of $4.8 million (-$0.37 per share) versus net income of $4.4 million ($0.35 per share) in the prior-year quarter.
Operating result swung to a $4.4 million loss from $5.6 million operating income last year, with adjusted EBITDA at negative $3.0 million versus negative $1.5 million.
Direct-to-consumer net sales fell 4.4%, and Q2 adjusted EBITDA margin is guided to 1%-4% versus 3.7% prior year, including ~170 bps of incremental tariff costs.
positive_highlights: Wholesale segment was relatively flat YoY, continuing to outperform the direct-to-consumer segment.
Product margin improvement: 330 bps benefit from lower product costs and higher pricing, plus 80 bps from lower promotional activity.
summary: Vince reported Q1 FY2025 net sales of $57.9 million, down 2.1% YoY, with DTC down 4.4% and wholesale roughly flat. Gross margin was 50.3%, down from 50.6% prior year, pressured by 260 bps of higher freight/duty and 120 bps of wholesale mix, partly offset by 330 bps of lower product costs/higher pricing. The company posted an operating loss of $4.4 million and a net loss of $4.8 million ($0.37 per share), versus prior-year net income of $4.4 million ($0.35 per share), and adjusted EBITDA was negative $3.0 million. Q2 guidance calls for net sales flat to down 3%, operating margin of -1% to +1%, and adjusted EBITDA margin of 1% to 4% (vs. 3.7% prior year), including ~170 bps of incremental tariff costs; no full-year guidance was provided due to tariff uncertainty.

negative_highlights: Cost of revenue of $5.4 million exceeded revenue of $3.7 million, producing a negative gross profit of $1.7 million for FY2025.
Cash and marketable securities were only $6.9 million at March 31, 2025, requiring reliance on financing vehicles to fund operations into calendar 2026.
FY2025 net loss remained large at $46.6 million ($0.69 per share), and the company continues to depend on hitting internal revenue estimates to approach profitability.
positive_highlights: FY2025 revenue rose 220% to $3.7 million from $1.2 million, all from U.S. sales, with hospitals signed in the back half driving momentum.
FY2026 revenue guidance of $12-16 million, with June quarter revenue on track for at least $1.7 million (>145% YoY growth), and guidance excludes the unapproved Gen 2 device.
Operating expenses cut 58% over six quarters to just above $7 million, cash burn down 28% to $44.1 million, and management expects further reductions in Q1/Q2 FY2026.
summary: Beyond Air reported FY2025 revenue of $3.7 million, up 220% from $1.2 million, with all growth from U.S. LungFit PH sales; gross profit was negative $1.7 million as cost of revenue of $5.4 million exceeded revenue. FY2025 net loss narrowed to $46.6 million ($0.69/share) from $60.2 million ($1.82/share), and cash burn fell 28% to $44.1 million, with period-end cash of $6.9 million. Management guided FY2026 revenue to $12-16 million and said the June 2025 quarter is on track for at least $1.7 million, up more than 145% year-over-year, while noting the guidance excludes the next-generation LungFit PH II, whose PMA supplement was just submitted to FDA.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to $51.4M from $29.4M in the prior year.
PALISADE-4 timing slipped modestly due to stricter eligibility screening and secondary review processes.
Cash position of $80.5M may require future financing to complete ongoing programs.
positive_highlights: PALISADE-3 remains on track for top-line data in Q4 2025, and PALISADE-4 expected in H1 2026.
R&D investment increased to $39.4M, supporting the PALISADE program and IND-enabling work for PH80.
Management reported strong patient and physician enthusiasm in the PALISADE program.
summary: Vistagen reported fiscal year 2025 R&D expenses of $39.4M, up from $20M, G&A of $17.1M, up from $14.1M, and a net loss of $51.4M versus $29.4M in the prior year. Cash totaled $80.5M at March 31, 2025. Management reiterated its outlook for PALISADE-3 top-line data in Q4 2025 and PALISADE-4 in H1 2026, but noted a modest timing slip in PALISADE-4 due to stricter patient eligibility screening. The company also highlighted constructive interactions with the FDA and ongoing progress in its PH80 and itruvone programs.

negative_highlights: Q1 2026 global cannabis revenue expected to be slightly lower sequentially
Adjusted EBITDA projected to be sequentially below Q4 due to lower high-margin international revenue
Poland experienced regulatory headwinds impacting prescription volumes
positive_highlights: Q4 net revenue up 34% YoY with record global medical cannabis and plant propagation revenue
Adjusted EBITDA grew 619% to a record $16.7 million in Q4
Company ended with $185.3 million cash and no cannabis debt
summary: Aurora Cannabis reported record fiscal 2025 results: net revenue up 27% to $343 million, global medical cannabis revenue up 39% to $244.4 million, adjusted EBITDA of $49.7 million, and positive free cash flow of $9.9 million. Q4 net revenue rose 34% to $90.5 million, with record adjusted gross profit of $54.2 million and adjusted EBITDA up 619% to $16.7 million, while cash at $185.3 million and no cannabis debt. Management guided Q1 2026 global cannabis to be slightly lower sequentially due to temporary international declines (notably Poland), but expects improvement in later quarters.

negative_highlights: Gross profit turned negative at -$0.8 million compared to $0.1 million last year, primarily due to sharp increases in cocoa costs.
Net loss widened significantly from a prior period of $4.9M for the full year and $1.6M for Q4 alone.
Cash balance declined to $0.7 million at year-end compared to $2.1 million previously, reflecting ongoing transformation investments.
positive_highlights: Revenue beat expectations with a year-over-year increase driven by product sales growth of $7.1 million versus $5.6 million last year.
Fulfillment reliability improved to nearly 100% for franchisee demand during the holiday season following the in-house packaging transition.
The company expects profitable contribution from e-commerce in fiscal '26 after resolving fulfillment inefficiencies.
summary: RMCF reported Q4 FY2025 revenue of $8.9 million (up from $7.3M YoY) but a net loss of $2.9 million ($-0.37/share), widening the deficit compared to last year's $1.6M loss due to higher raw material costs and brand refresh expenses. Full-year 2025 revenue grew slightly to $29.6M, yet total losses increased to $6.1M as gross profit contracted significantly from inflationary pressures on cocoa prices.

negative_highlights: No revenue was reported, and management stated the company will need to keep raising money until it can obtain grants or partner with a larger company.
Cash balance of ~$5.5 million against annual operating expenses of ~$9.3 million implies limited runway.
A $4.6 million noncash warrant inducement charge was recognized in the quarter.
positive_highlights: Operating expenses fell ~26% to ~$9.3 million from the prior year, driven by lower payroll, professional fees, and G&A.
First three oncology patients completed Hemopurifier treatments without device deficiencies or immediate complications, triggering the first DSMB meeting.
Received CDSCO approval in India to initiate a similar oncology study at Medanta Medicity Hospital.
summary: Aethlon reported FY2025 operating expenses of ~$9.3 million, down ~$3.3 million or 26% year over year, with a cash balance of ~$5.5 million as of March 31, 2025. The company recognized a $4.6 million noncash warrant inducement charge while raising ~$2.3 million in cash. Clinically, the first three oncology patients were treated with the Hemopurifier in Australia, and India's CDSCO approved a similar study, but no efficacy or revenue data were provided. Management expects DSMB review of the first cohort in July, preliminary data in about three months, and completion of the Australian study in roughly 9-12 months, and stated that additional equity financing will be needed.

Q4 net sales of $61.9 million came in nearly 34% above the prior-year quarter, but management said $8-10 million was pulled forward from FY2026 by retailers front-running tariff-driven price increases. American Outdoor Brands suspended its previously issued FY2026 net sales guidance, citing tariff uncertainty and the order pull-forward, and expects higher tariff costs to hit the income statement mainly in Q3-Q4.

summary: Culp reported Q4 FY2025 net sales of $48.8 million, roughly flat versus $49.5 million a year ago, with GAAP net loss of $2.1 million or $0.17 per diluted share (prior-year loss $4.9 million or $0.39). Non-GAAP operating loss narrowed to $704,000 from $4.0 million, helped by $10-11 million in annualized restructuring savings plus a $1.7 million inventory markdown change; full-year sales fell 5.4% to $213.2 million and full-year free cash flow was negative $17.1 million. Management did not provide specific FY2026 financial guidance, citing tariff and macro uncertainty, but expects mattress fabric sales growth and continued residential upholstery pressure, with Project Blaze integration ($3 million annualized), price increases ($2.5 million annualized) and restructuring savings phasing in from Q2 and fully effective in the back half. Q1 FY2026 is expected to remain pressured on both sales and margins due to tariff timing.

negative_highlights: LED lighting revenue down 22% in FY2025
Q4 net loss of $2.9M vs net income of $1.6M in prior year

positive_highlights: EV charging revenue up 37% in FY2025

Blended gross margin improved 170 bps to 27.5% in Q4, and adjusted EBITDA was positive in Q3 and Q4. Management cited improving revenue pacing and bookings momentum, with mid-single-digit decline expected at the half-year versus 6% in Q1.
summary: Q1 FY2025 revenue was in line with prior guidance but declined 6% year-on-year on a combined basis, with adjusted EBITDA of just $3 million. Q2 is expected to show a mid-single-digit revenue decline, putting the first half on that trajectory, while full-year revenue is guided broadly flat year-on-year with adjusted EBITDA of $85 million or more. The company reaffirmed its full-year guidance but also disclosed a pending noncash goodwill impairment and a delayed Q1 filing, and management hedged on the timing of a revenue recovery while citing no expected material change in market outlook.

negative_highlights: Gross margin remains deeply negative at -35%, and net loss was $712 million on $657 million of revenue.
Deliveries declined 32% quarter over quarter, and revenue was roughly flat versus Q4 2024.
Operating cash flow was -$607 million, worse than -$500 million a year ago; 2025 cash burn guided to $2.0–2.5 billion.

SG&A as a percentage of revenue fell to 23% from 47% a year ago; cash burn fell to 115% of revenue from 256%.
summary: VinFast reported Q1 2025 net revenue of $657 million, up 150% year over year and roughly flat versus Q4 2024, with deliveries of 36,330 EVs (+296% YoY, -32% QoQ) and 44,904 two-wheelers (+473% YoY). Gross margin was -35% (improved from -59% a year ago; -28% excluding NRV/one-offs) and net loss was -$712 million (-109% margin). Guidance was not raised: management reiterated at least doubling 2024 deliveries of 97,000 and a gross-margin breakeven target in 2026, while flagging a USD 2.0–2.5 billion cash burn for 2025. The company is closing D2C showrooms in Germany, the Netherlands, Canada and California, recording a $20 million impairment, and shifting to a dealer-led model.

summary: Pure Cycle reported Q3 FY2025 revenue of about $5 million with roughly 63% gross margin ($3.2 million) and net income of about $2 million ($0.09/share); fiscal YTD net income was about $7 million ($0.29/share). Management said revenue was slightly down quarter-over-quarter because of weighted lot deliveries in Filing 6 (about 70 lots vs. a traditional 45) and weak industrial water sales during a permitting year for its largest oil and gas operator. FY2025 guidance of about $31 million revenue and $23.7 million gross profit was not raised, with management saying results should land 'within a short part' of that guidance as roughly 220 lots close late in Q4. Share repurchases continued but were lighter in Q3 to conserve cash.

negative_highlights: Total revenue was essentially flat, masking a decline in product sales of approximately $0.6 million driven by the loss of a large specialty market customer.
Franchise and royalty fees were up only modestly ($1.7M vs $1.1M) despite higher same-store sales at existing locations.
Management indicated they are not currently planning to raise capital, leaving expansion funding contingent on future board decisions.
positive_highlights: EBITDA turned positive at $2 million, reversing from -$1.4 million in the prior year period.

Costs and expenses decreased to $6.5 million from $8 million last year due to lower G&A costs.
summary: Total revenue was $6.4 million for Q1 FY2026, essentially flat year-over-year due to the loss of a large specialty market customer that reduced sales by nearly $500,000. Despite this volume decline and dropping product sales from $5.3M to $4.7M, the company achieved positive EBITDA of $2 million compared to negative $1.4M last year due to pricing adjustments and lower G&A costs. Management expressed cautious optimism about a business transformation entering an execution phase but noted they are not currently planning to raise capital.

negative_highlights: Available liquidity ended the quarter at only $12.3 million while management states an objective to secure financing for equity contributions before start-up.
No revenue guidance provided; company is in a pre-revenue phase focused on securing off-take agreements and debt syndication.
positive_highlights: Cash operating expenses reduced by $2.2 million (46%) compared to the same quarter last year through disciplined expense management.
India facility CapEx confirmed at $176 million with a low-cost structure offering net technology cost of $0.61 per pound, significantly below competitors' estimates.
summary: Loop Industries reported Q1 FY2026 cash operating expenses of $2.6 million and a reduction in available liquidity to $12.3 million as it seeks financing for the India facility's equity contribution. Management confirmed off-take discussions are progressing with apparel and CPG brands but noted that contracts typically take time due to internal steps, while site selection is narrowing down to two locations in Gujarat pending final terms.

negative_highlights: Q3 throughput was limited to just under 1,500 tonnes per day due to scheduled maintenance and downtime before the plant reached full capacity.
The company still operates with a negative working capital ratio at quarter end, requiring focus on rightsizing payables in Q4.
Joint venture agreement remains less favorable than peers (55-45 split), which management cites as an ongoing factor impacting share price appreciation.
positive_highlights: Production increased substantially quarter-over-quarter as operations accessed higher-grade ore blocks, producing just under 4,700 ounces in Q3 versus lower prior periods.
Processing cost per tonne improved to below $15 due to economies of scale from the expanded plant capacity and optimized fleet usage.
Agreement with Bank of Tanzania secured a reduced royalty rate of approximately 4% on domestic sales compared to 7.3% for exports, providing immediate cash flow benefits.
summary: TRX Gold reported Q3 FY2025 results with revenue of $12.5 million and adjusted EBITDA of approximately $4 million, driven by production of just under 4,700 ounces at an average gold price over $3,100/oz. Management highlighted a strong quarter-on-quarter improvement in financial metrics as the company transitioned from low-grade oxide material to higher-grade sulfide ore following the completion of Stage 1 stripping. The CEO reiterated that the business is self-funding growth and focused on normalizing working capital ratios while executing plant optimizations.

negative_highlights: Expense creep observed internally, though impact on core efficiency is minimal
Oil and gas write-downs totaling $8.8 million in the quarter
M&A opportunities have not materialized despite signed LOIs over the last year
positive_highlights: Strong loan and deposit growth driven by bankers in Texas and Oklahoma
NIM maintained at the high end of historical range with low efficiency ratio
Credit quality remains strong with a continuous path toward smaller NPA numbers
summary: Bank7 Corp reported a strong Q2 FY2025 quarter with solid loan and deposit growth driven by bankers in Texas and Oklahoma, maintaining NIM at the high end of its historical range despite slight expense creep from oil and gas write-downs. Management raised guidance for core earnings efficiency to remain within the 36%-38% range while projecting full cash recovery on O&G assets by mid-next year. The company reiterated a disciplined approach to M&A, noting signed LOIs that did not close over the last 12 months.

Provision rose to $2.6 million from $1.5 million on growth and a modest uptick in net charge-offs
Lending pipeline fell 8% to $301 million of probable fundings from March 31; management expects loan growth to slow in the back half

Net interest margin held at 3.65% and PPNR rose $2.9 million, or 21% linked quarter
Noninterest-bearing deposits rose $55 million, lifting NIB to 19% of total deposits from 17% a year ago
summary: First Bank reported Q2 net income of $10.2 million, or $0.41 per diluted share, with a 1.04% ROA. Loans grew $91 million (11% annualized) and deposits rose $48 million, mostly noninterest-bearing, pushing the loan-to-deposit ratio to 105%. Net interest margin held at 3.65% and PPNR rose 21% linked quarter to $2.9 million, while the provision increased to $2.6 million from $1.5 million. Management kept its prior guidance of roughly +/-$50 million quarterly net loan growth but flagged a likely slowdown in the back half after two strong quarters, and guided to a broadly stable NIM with modest upside into 2026.

negative_highlights: Net sales declined 3% to $54 million from $55.4 million, with US segment sales down 6% on back-to-school order cancellations tied to exceptionally high April-May tariffs
Europe sales fell 6% in local currency for both the quarter and the six months, attributed mainly to shipment timing
Management declined to provide quantitative Q3/Q4 guidance and flagged uncertainty about whether broad price increases will reduce customer spending
positive_highlights: Diluted EPS rose 6% to $1.16 and net income rose 7% to $4.8 million, with management calling it a record quarterly earnings result excluding prior one-time gains
Canada segment sales rose 28% in local currency in Q2 and 21% year-to-date, driven by higher first aid product sales

summary: Acme United reported Q2 FY2025 net sales of $54 million, down 3% from $55.4 million a year ago, while net income rose 7% to $4.8 million and diluted EPS rose 6% to $1.16 from $1.09. Gross margin was flat at 41%, and SG&A fell to $15.8 million from $16.3 million. US segment sales declined 6% on canceled back-to-school orders tied to 145% China tariffs, Europe fell 6%, and Canada rose 28% in local currency. Management gave no quantitative guidance, but said it expects third- and fourth-quarter sales growth rather than declines and continued earnings strength, citing diverted orders, share gains and low-cost supply chain positioning.

negative_highlights: Production volatility noted due to sequencing of high-grade stopes in the CSA mine.
Grade expected to moderate towards the back end of the quarter as lower grade material is accessed.
Significant capital expenditure ramp-up for growth projects (Ventilation and Merrin Mine) increased total CapEx by 85% QoQ.

Record quarterly operating free cash flow of USD 42 million achieved.
C1 cost decreased significantly to USD 1.48/lb, with June reaching USD 0.94/lb.

The company achieved record quarterly operating free cash flow of USD 42 million and reduced its C1 cost to USD 1.48/lb. Management maintained full-year production guidance of 43,000 to 48,000 tonnes while announcing a sale transaction to Harmony at USD 12.25/share.

negative_highlights: Active customer count declined due to acquisition slowdown before comp plan changes
Q3 operating margin expected to be pressured by convention and rollout investments
China growth partly driven by tariff-related note-ups, not sustainable demand
positive_highlights: Consolidated net sales grew 11% year-over-year

The company repaid its line of credit used for the Hiya acquisition. Despite a drop in active customers partly due to compensation plan changes, management expressed optimism about growth initiatives, including new partnerships and product launches, and reaffirmed fiscal 2025 guidance while noting Q3 margin pressure from planned investments.

negative_highlights: Q2 sales down 20% YoY, worse than planned

U.S. customer planogram resets delayed by two months; tariff uncertainty persists

summary: JAKKS Pacific reported Q2 2025 sales down 20% YoY, with adjusted EBITDA of $2.3 million versus $12.3 million last year, and adjusted EPS of $0.03 versus $0.65. The quarter was hit by tariff-driven order cancellations and delayed retail resets, but first-half sales were down only 3% overall, with international sales up 33% and Europe up 65%. Management is cautious about the second half, citing ongoing tariff uncertainty and later shelf resets, but highlighted strong gross margins of 32.8%, a new credit facility, and continued dividend.

negative_highlights: Loan outstandings declined by approximately $50 million due to customer asset sales and refinancing activity.
Deposit costs increased by 4 basis points, partially offsetting loan yield gains which rose from 5.52% in Q1 to 5.59% in Q2.
positive_highlights: Net income improved sequentially to $8M and year-over-year to more than double the prior period's $5.2M.
summary: West Bancorporation reported Q2 FY2025 net income of $8 million compared to $5.2 million in the prior year quarter and $7.8 million in the first quarter of 2025. Loan balances decreased by approximately $50 million due to asset sales and refinancing, while core deposits increased by roughly $195 million driven largely by a municipal bond offering that offset reductions in brokered funding. Management indicated continued margin improvement opportunities through loan portfolio repricing despite slight deposit cost increases.

negative_highlights: Betterware Mexico gross margin down 127 bps YoY due to pricing
Jafra US revenue down 8.9% YoY in USD
Net debt-to-EBITDA at 1.97x, above 1.8x year-ago
positive_highlights: Betterware Mexico first net associate growth since Q1 2021, up 3.3% QoQ
Jafra Mexico revenue up 10.9% YoY, EBITDA margin 21.2%
Free cash flow MXN 592 million in Q2, 87% conversion
summary: BeFra reported Q2 2025 consolidated revenue growth of 5.1% YoY and EBITDA up 3.5% YoY to MXN 679 million, with margin at 19.1%, rebounding from a weak Q1. Betterware Mexico returned to sequential growth (+4% QoQ) and achieved its first net associate growth since Q1 2021, while Jafra Mexico grew revenue 10.9% YoY with EBITDA margin at 21.2%. Guidance for 2025 is maintained at 6-9% revenue and EBITDA growth, implying acceleration in H2. Management highlighted pricing, product, and incentive initiatives as key drivers, despite a still challenging macro environment.

negative_highlights: EPS of $0.02, well below prior periods; management acknowledges disappointment
Provision remains elevated at $10M-$11M per quarter for H2 2025, and $37M-$40M for 2026
SBA gain on sale down ~$7M linked quarter; premium softness (mid-7% vs >8% historically)
positive_highlights: Net interest income up 11.5% sequentially; NIM up 14bps to 1.96% GAAP (2.04% FTE)
SBA past dues dropped 48% linked quarter; deferral dollar value down >60% from Q4 2024
July SBA sales already $52M with $3.7M gain; Q3/Q4 noninterest income forecast ~$13.3M each
summary: Q2 2025 diluted EPS was $0.02 due to elevated credit costs, despite net interest income and margin improvement. NIM rose to 2.04% FTE, with loan yields up and deposit costs down. Guidance for Q3/Q4 shows NIM expanding to 2.20%-2.35% FTE and noninterest income recovering as SBA loan sales resume (already sold $52M in July). 2026 EPS guidance is $5.20-$6.30, with elevated provision of $37M-$40M, although management noted the provision may be padded.

negative_highlights: Nonperforming loans rose $3.7 million to $17 million, driven by two CRE credits placed on nonaccrual including a $2.6 million office building loan
Total deposits fell $61.9 million linked-quarter to $1.3 billion, with money market and checking down $50.5 million and noninterest checking down $16.5 million
A $1 million provision for credit losses was recorded versus no provision in the prior quarter, lifting the allowance to 1.23% of gross loans
positive_highlights: Diluted EPS increased 56% year-over-year to $0.75, with net income up to $4.4 million from $3.0 million
Net interest margin expanded 7 bps sequentially to 3.83% and net interest income grew 4.3% to $13.7 million
Gross loans reached a record $1.1 billion, up $42.9 million or 16% annualized, with broad-based growth across residential mortgage, commercial and CRE
summary: Landmark Bancorp reported Q2 2025 net income of $4.4 million and diluted EPS of $0.75, up 56% year-over-year, with ROAA of 1.11% and ROAE of 12.25%. Net interest income rose 4.3% sequentially to $13.7 million and net interest margin expanded 7 bps to 3.83%, driven by record gross loans of over $1.1 billion (up $42.9 million, 16% annualized). A $1 million provision was recorded and nonperforming loans increased $3.7 million to $17 million on two commercial real estate credits, one of which was brought current after quarter end. No explicit forward guidance was provided, though management noted deposit-gathering initiatives for the second half and expects nonaccrual trends to improve.

negative_highlights: Net charge-offs of 14 basis points this quarter, including a $700,000 loss on sale of a yacht and tender vessel collateral
Noninterest income was 13.8% of total revenue and 0.5% of average assets, slightly lower than the prior quarter; SBA loan sales declined from Q1
AOCI remained a negative $41.8 million, a $2.08 drag on tangible book value per share, from sub-3% yielding AFS securities purchased during the pandemic
positive_highlights: EPS up 29% to $0.40 from $0.31; ROE 14.29% and ROA 1.22%
Loans grew 15.1% annualized and deposits 13.7% annualized, with cost of deposits down 3 bp
NIM improved to 3.28% and efficiency ratio fell to 51.77%, the lowest since 2021
summary: USCB reported Q2 2025 net income of $8.1 million, or $0.40 per diluted share, up 29% from $0.31 a year earlier. Return on assets was 1.22% and return on equity 14.29%; NIM rose to 3.28%, the efficiency ratio improved to 51.77% (lowest since 2021), and tangible book value per share increased $0.30 to $11.53. Loans grew 15.1% annualized to above $2.1 billion and deposits rose 13.7% annualized to $2.3 billion, with the cost of deposits down 3 basis points. Management closed $187 million of new loan production at a 7.12% weighted-average coupon (89 bp above portfolio yield) and guided to roughly $150-180 million per quarter ahead, with 2025 expense base near the current $12.6 million and gradual increases thereafter.

negative_highlights: Trucking revenues dropped nearly 30% year-over-year due to a 22.6% decline in load volumes and an 8.9% decrease in revenue per load.
Intermodal revenues fell 13.5% year-over-year, with load volumes declining nearly 13% amid tariff impacts on imports.
Full-year guidance was lowered due to macro headwinds including tariffs, soft trucking demand, and regulatory uncertainty regarding NOx standards.
positive_highlights: Intermodal segment narrowed operating loss to $5.7 million from a $10.7 million loss in Q1, with operating ratio improving to 108.2%.
Trucking segment achieved an operating margin of 5.2%, up from 4.8% year-over-year, driven by specialized freight including wind energy.
Contract Logistics integration of Parsec contributed $55 million in revenue during the quarter.
summary: Universal Logistics Holdings reported Q2 FY2025 operating revenues of $393.8 million and net income of $8.3 million ($0.32 per share), representing significant year-over-year declines in revenue across Contract Logistics, Trucking, and Intermodal segments. Management lowered full-year guidance expectations due to tariff headwinds impacting imports and a soft trucking backdrop, while narrowing the Intermodal operating loss sequentially. The company maintained its dividend at $0.105 per share and expects top-line revenues between $390 million and $410 million for Q3.

negative_highlights: Reported net income included a $7.5 million gain, masking noise from consumer program reversals
Core expenses rose to $22.7 million from $20.4 million in Q1, though normalized to ~$21 million
Loan growth expected to slow in back half; management cautions against extrapolating 12-15% growth
positive_highlights: Core NIM expanded to 3.15%, up from 3.13% last quarter and 2.80% a year ago
Noninterest-bearing deposits increased $22 million or 19% annualized
Technology savings expected to lower run rate by $1.5 million per quarter
summary: Primis Financial reported Q2 2025 net income of $8.4 million or $0.34 per share, including a $7.5 million pretax gain from PFH, offset by new mortgage team support and consumer program reversals. Core pretax pre-provision earnings were about $8.4 million, with core net interest margin expanding to 3.15% and noninterest-bearing deposits up 19% annualized. Management expects run-rate PPNR to grow to over $13 million heading into 2026, aided by tech savings of $1.5 million per quarter starting in Q3 and continued margin expansion to mid-3.20% by year-end.

negative_highlights: Revenue of $5.9 million came in below expectations and missed the Q4 calendar 2025 profitability target
Defense procurement delays from election-related uncertainty and macro volatility slowed pipeline conversion
No explicit FY26 revenue, EPS or profitability guidance was provided despite claims of a step-function year
positive_highlights: Record funded backlog of $12.5 million entering FY26, split across buoys, vehicles and services
Operating expenses cut 27% to $23.4 million and net loss improved 22% to $21.5 million
Cash rose to $6.7 million from $3.2 million, plus a $10 million unsecured debt financing secured after year-end
summary: Fiscal 2025 revenue was a record $5.9 million, up 7% from $5.5 million, achieved alongside a 27% reduction in operating expenses to $23.4 million and a 22% improvement in net loss to $21.5 million. The company entered FY26 with record funded backlog of $12.5 million and cash of $6.7 million, later bolstered by a $10 million unsecured debt financing. However, management disclosed revenue came in below expectations and missed its Q4 calendar 2025 profitability target, citing defense procurement delays from election-related uncertainty and macro volatility. Management gave no explicit numeric guidance for FY26, only qualitative confidence in a step-function year.

negative_highlights: Net interest margin declined to 7.81% from 8.27%, driven by accrued interest reversals and lower-yielding loan additions, with management expecting further gradual decline
Net charge-offs rose to $2.8 million from $2.2 million and NPAs increased $9.9 million to $39.7 million, with up to $12 million more potentially migrating to NPA in Q3
Provision for credit losses rose to $4.7 million from $3.3 million, partially offset by matching credit enhancement income
positive_highlights: Originations of $1.5 billion rose 17% quarter-over-quarter and 27% year-over-year, with SBA 7(a) originations up 24% sequentially and over 140% year-over-year
Credit-enhanced balances reached $12 million with a reiterated $50-100 million target by Q4, a core future interest income driver
Efficiency ratio improved to 59.5% from 64.8% in the prior quarter, with positive operating leverage expected to continue
summary: FinWise reported Q2 FY2025 net income of $4.1 million, or $0.29 per diluted share, on net interest income of $14.7 million versus $14.3 million in the prior quarter. Originations reached $1.5 billion, up 17% quarter-over-quarter and 27% year-over-year, while NIM fell to 7.81% from 8.27% and net charge-offs rose to $2.8 million from $2.2 million. NPAs rose $9.9 million to $39.7 million, with up to $12 million of further migration flagged for Q3. Credit-enhanced balances reached $12 million, on track for the reiterated $50-100 million by year-end, and management offered no formal EPS guidance beyond 2027 ROA/ROE targets of over 2% and low-to-mid-teens.

negative_highlights: Operating profit down to $2.1 million from $4 million due to higher marketing expenses.
EPS reduced by $0.13 in Q2 from immediate member acquisition costs.
Travel industry demand is soft, with flight and hotel prices coming down.
positive_highlights: Revenue up 13% YoY to $23.9 million, growth across all segments.
Jack's Flight Club revenue increased 33% YoY; premium subscribers up 15%.
Management expects revenue growth to accelerate and profitability to substantially increase over time.
summary: Travelzoo reported Q2 2025 revenue of $23.9 million, up 13% YoY (12% in constant currency), but operating profit fell to $2.1 million from $4 million due to heavy investment in Club Member acquisition. Membership fees grew to $3 million and are expected to reach about 25% of revenue next year. Management expects revenue growth to accelerate in coming quarters as membership fees are recognized ratably, with profitability to increase over time. Despite near-term EPS pressure, they will continue aggressive member acquisition as long as payback remains favorable.

negative_highlights: BARDA NextGen contract was terminated as part of government efficiency programs, ending future revenue from this cost-reimbursement agreement.
Cash balance declined to $3.1 million at June 30, 2025, down from $5.5 million a year prior due to operating cash burn and the termination impact.
R&D expenses increased by approximately 16% ($1.4M) driven largely by costs associated with the terminated BARDA contract and ongoing Gedeptin/GEO-MVA programs.
positive_highlights: Received European Medicines Agency (EMA) guidance confirming a pathway to bypass Phase I and II trials via non-inferiority immunobridging for GEO-MVA against Bavarian Nordic's MVA-BN.
Completed cGMP production of the clinical batch for GEO-MVA, with plans to produce additional inventory for potential emergency use distribution discussions.
Initiated enrollment at a second site (City of Hope) for the investigator-initiated Phase II trial of GEO-CMO4S1 in chronic lymphocytic leukemia patients.
summary: GeoVax reported revenues of $2.5 million for the six months ended June 30, 2025, compared to $10.7 million in net loss versus a prior period loss of $10.9 million. Management noted that revenue from the BARDA NextGen contract has ceased due to termination under government efficiency programs and cash balances dropped significantly despite recent financing activity. While regulatory progress was made for GEO-MVA with EMA guidance allowing an immunobridging trial, clinical start dates were pushed to late 2026.

negative_highlights: Roughly $11 million of incremental tariffs on balance sheet, hitting mostly Q4
Retail gross margin down 170 bps to 45.2%
Georgia Boot finished down modestly due to tariff-related shipment delay
positive_highlights: Adjusted EPS tripled to $0.55 from $0.17 a year ago
Gross margin up 230 bps to 41.0% on strong full-price note
Guidance raised: revenue growth now 4-5% and EPS up ~10%
summary: Rocky Brands reported Q2 FY2025 net sales of $105.6 million, up 7.5% YoY, with adjusted EPS of $0.55 versus $0.17 last year, more than tripling. Gross margin expanded 230 basis points to 41.0%, driven by higher wholesale margins and a favorable retail mix. The company raised its full-year 2025 guidance: revenue growth now 4-5% (up from low single digits) and EPS up ~10% to $2.79 (vs prior down slightly), despite expecting ~$11 million of tariff headwinds. Management cited strong execution across XTRATUF, Muck, and other brands, and is ahead of schedule shifting production to lower-tariff facilities like the Dominican Republic and Puerto Rico.

negative_highlights: Quarterly dividend cut 20% to $0.28 from $0.33, tied to expected lower net interest margins on redeployed capital
Q3 guidance of $0.27-$0.29 per share is below the $0.31 just reported and below the new $0.28 dividend at the midpoint
CECL reserve rose to 150 bps of commitments from 130 bps, a $912,000 increase driven by macroeconomic factors and loan extensions
positive_highlights: Q2 distributable earnings of $0.31 per share landed at the high end of the guidance range
Credit quality intact: all loans current, weighted average risk rating steady at 2.9, no 5-rated or nonaccrual loans
Origination pipeline active with over $1 billion in average monthly loan registrations and a $34 million mixed-use retail/medical office loan in diligence
summary: Seven Hills reported Q2 distributable earnings of $0.31 per share at the high end of guidance, with $665 million in commitments across 23 first mortgage loans at an all-in yield of SOFR plus 3.64%. Management cut the quarterly dividend 20% to $0.28 from $0.33, citing a declining SOFR curve and expected redeployment of repayment proceeds at lower net interest margins, and guided Q3 distributable earnings down to $0.27-$0.29. The CECL reserve rose to 150 bps from 130 bps on a $912,000 increase, and management noted 2-3 additional loans (~$100 million) could repay in the back half, with portfolio growth to ~$700 million by year-end dependent on repayments.

negative_highlights: U.S. revenue only 17% of total, with expected market slowdown
Convertible debt of $50 million maturing January 2026, refinancing pending
Gross margin benefited one-time from reserved inventory sales
positive_highlights: Revenue up 89.4% YoY and 27.7% sequentially, exceeding guidance
Positive adjusted EBITDA of $1.1 million, improved from -$6.4 million YoY
Full-year revenue guidance raised to $100-105 million
summary: Tigo Energy reported Q2 FY2025 revenue of $24.1 million, up 89.4% YoY and 27.7% sequentially, exceeding the high end of guidance. Adjusted EBITDA was $1.1 million positive, a swing from a $6.4 million loss a year ago. The company raised full-year revenue guidance to $100-105 million and expects Q3 revenue of $29-31 million and adjusted EBITDA of $2-4 million. While U.S. revenue was only 17% of total, with Europe leading growth, management expressed confidence in sustaining growth and gaining share despite market challenges.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA loss was $1.7 million in Q2, largely flat versus $1.6 million in Q2 2024, indicating limited near-term profitability progress.
Company reduced accrual rates for new biomarkers to align with cash collections, potentially tempering near-term ASP growth.
Pipeline revenue is lumpy, with biopharma revenue ranging $100,000-$300,000 per quarter, and no near-term revenue milestones disclosed.
positive_highlights: Record quarterly revenue of $17.2 million, up 14% YoY, with AVISE CTD volume up 7% YoY and 14% sequentially.
Revenue per territory reached over $430,000, up from $285,000 two years ago, a >50% increase.
Management reiterated FY2025 revenue guidance of $65-$70 million, implying >17% growth, with adjusted EBITDA positive in Q4 at the high end.
summary: Exagen delivered record Q2 2025 revenue of $17.2 million, up 14% YoY, with AVISE CTD volume up 7% YoY and 14% sequentially. Trailing 12-month ASP rose $27 YoY to $428. Gross margin improved slightly to over 60%. Net loss widened to $4.4 million from $3.0 million YoY, partly due to one-time expenses. Management reiterated full-year revenue guidance of $65-$70 million (implying >17% growth) and expects positive adjusted EBITDA in Q4 at the high end. The company ended the quarter with $30 million in cash and is approaching cash-flow neutrality.

negative_highlights: Keep demand-generation business underperformed, leading to a modest cut in full-year SaaS revenue guidance to $460-465M.
Marketing Services billings declined 38% year-over-year, reflecting strategic shift, though at a managed pace.
SaaS subscriber count sequentially declined by 4,000, reflecting flat customer base strategy in 2025.
positive_highlights: SaaS adjusted EBITDA margin reached a record 20%, up from prior periods, with $23.4M adjusted EBITDA exceeding guidance.
SaaS adjusted gross margin expanded 430 bps year-over-year to 74%.
Net revenue retention held strong at 103%, and clients with 2+ products grew to 17,000 from 13,000 year-over-year.
summary: SaaS revenue hit $115M (up 48% YoY, incl. $17.7M from Keep), meeting guidance; SaaS adjusted EBITDA of $23.4M beat guidance with a record 20% margin. Marketing Services revenue of $95.5M and EBITDA of $27.8M beat guidance. Full-year SaaS EBITDA guidance raised to $70.5-73.5M, while SaaS revenue guidance trimmed to $460-465M due to softness in Keep's demand-gen business. Net debt fell to $274M, leverage at 2.2x, and 2 years of amortization payments were prepaid.

negative_highlights: Gas cylinders sales down 6% YoY
Automotive softness and clean energy demand subdued
FX and higher operating expenses offset gains by $2.4 million
positive_highlights: Adjusted EPS up 25% YoY to $0.30, ahead of expectations
Elektron sales up 19% YoY; defense/first response/healthcare up 43%
Guidance raised: EPS $0.97–$1.05 and EBITDA $49–$52 million
summary: Luxfer reported Q2 2025 adjusted EPS of $0.30, up 25% YoY and 30% sequentially, with adjusted EBITDA of $14 million (14.4% margin, up from 12.5% in Q1). Sales rose 5.8% to $97.1 million, driven by Elektron (+19% YoY) and a solid rebound in gas cylinders (up 14% sequentially). The company raised its full-year 2025 EPS guidance to $0.97–$1.05 and EBITDA to $49–$52 million, citing defense and aerospace momentum, while noting softness in autos and clean energy.

negative_highlights: Hyalofast Phase III trial missed statistical significance on co-primary endpoints; commercial launch pushed to 2027 with a full market release now expected in 2028.
Gross margin fell 16 percentage points YoY to 51% due to a $3M onetime scrap charge and lower J&J pricing; international OA Pain sales declined 10% due to unfilled orders.
positive_highlights: Integrity exceeded full year 2024 revenue by June and is on track to more than double in 2025, with Regenerative Solutions revenue up 41% in Q2.
Full year 2025 guidance maintained despite headwinds, including commercial channel growth of 12-18% and adjusted EBITDA of -3% to +3%.
Total operating expenses reduced 17% YoY, and cash remains strong at $53M with no debt.
summary: Q2 FY2025 revenue was $28.2M, down 8% YoY, in line with expectations. Adjusted EBITDA was -$0.2M, including a $3M onetime scrap charge from manufacturing yield issues. The Hyalofast US pivotal Phase III trial missed statistical significance on co-primary endpoints; the company will still submit the PMA in H2 2025 but extended the commercial timeline to 2027 and lowered long-term commercial channel growth guidance to 10-20% for 2026/2027 from 20-30%. Full year 2025 guidance was maintained, with adjusted EBITDA of negative 3% to positive 3%, and Integrity grew 41% in the quarter, on track to more than double in 2025.

negative_highlights: Consolidated revenue down 19% YoY
Global retail sales down 15% YoY
Touring faced headwinds with market share decline
positive_highlights: HDFS transaction expected to add $275-$300M operating income in 2025
Cash generated to accelerate $500M buyback in H2 '25
New small-displacement bike targeted below $6,000 and expected to be profitable
summary: Harley-Davidson reported Q2 FY2025 consolidated revenue down 19% YoY, with global retail down 15%, amid elevated interest rates and demand softness. The company announced a strategic HDFS partnership with KKR and PIMCO, watching equity at ~1.75x book value and generating ~$1.25B distribution, expected to boost HDFS operating income by $275-300M in 2025. Guidance for retail in North America is expected to turn positive in the second half, supported by easier comps. Management also confirmed a new small-displacement motorcycle entry price below $6,000 launching in H1 2026.

negative_highlights: Q2 was lowest volume quarter with higher organic decline in larger print product lines
Tariffs and postal rate uncertainty remain headwinds
Rising postal rates continue to challenge clients
positive_highlights: Revenue decline of 3% within the better end of 2-6% guidance range
Expecting increasing volumes and higher revenue/EBITDA in Q3 and Q4, with Q4 highest
No significant client pullback from tariffs; cautious optimism in market
summary: Quad's Q2 FY2025 results met expectations, with revenue decline of 3% year-over-year, within the 2-6% guidance range. Management reiterated FY guidance, expecting higher revenue and EBITDA in Q3 and Q4, with Q4 as the highest. They noted cautious optimism in the market, no significant client pullback due to tariffs, and highlighted growth in data-driven marketing solutions and In-store Connect. Asset sales and acquisitions (Sacramento plant sale, Enru purchase) were completed in the quarter.

negative_highlights: Total sales declined 18% driven by retailer pauses and tariff impacts on Chinese imports
Operating profit fell to $5.9 million (4.7%) compared to $10 million in the prior year period
Management refrained from reinstating guidance citing uncertainty around final tariff rates
positive_highlights: Gross margin expanded 160 basis points to 27.5% despite significant revenue decline
Core business maintained its #1 position in units sold in North America
Health segment operating loss was cut in half year-over-year, improving from a $2 million deficit
summary: Total revenue declined 18% to $127.8 million and EPS fell to $0.33 due to lower volumes in the U.S. consumer business caused by higher tariffs on Chinese imports. Gross margin expanded 160 basis points to 27.5%, driven by a favorable shift in customer mix toward commercial and health segments, while operating profit dropped significantly from $10 million to $5.9 million due to lower sales volume and an $800,000 restructuring charge. Management explicitly stated they are refraining from reinstating guidance given the uncertainty of ongoing trade negotiations.

negative_highlights: Time charter revenues declined by $1.3 million year-over-year (2%) primarily because of note vessels, not market weakness.
The broader dry bulk market saw average sector earnings down about 30% YoY amid weaker demand trends in key commodities like iron ore and coal.
Cash reserves decreased to approximately $150 million from over $207 million at year-end due to debt servicing, share repurchases ($23M), and investments.
positive_highlights: Net income turned profitable at $4.5M after posting a net loss of $2.8M in Q2 FY2024, driven by reduced debt levels and lower interest rates.
Time charter equivalent rate increased to $15,492 per day (up 3% YoY) despite the revenue decline due to fleet size reduction.
Fleet utilization remained exceptionally high at 99.5%, demonstrating effective vessel management.
summary: Diana Shipping reported Q2 FY2025 time charter revenues of $54.7 million, a decrease from the prior year's $56 million due to fleet size reduction rather than market rates. Net income improved significantly to $4.5 million compared to a loss in the same period last year, driven by lower interest costs and nonoperating gains on investments. The company declared a quarterly cash dividend of $0.01 per share.

negative_highlights: U.S. revenue growth only 6% YoY, below expectations
Full-year revenue guidance lowered from $96-98M to $90-92M
Gross margin declined to 72% from 74% due to geographic mix shift
positive_highlights: International revenue $9.1M, up 32% YoY, a record
StratX referrals rebounded to record levels in June and July
Direct-to-patient campaigns engaged 70,000 patients; TAS territories saw 19% increase in workups
summary: Q2 2025 revenue was $23.9 million, up 15% YoY and 13% on a constant currency basis, with international revenue a record $9.1 million, up 32% YoY. U.S. revenue grew only 6% to $14.7 million, missing expectations due to slower procedure volume growth, declined StratX scans, and capacity constraints at interventional pulmonology centers. Management lowered full-year 2025 revenue guidance from $96-98 million to $90-92 million, attributing the shortfall to timing rather than strategic changes and citing record StratX referrals in June/July as early signs of improvement.

negative_highlights: Q2 leasing volume fell to 171,000 square feet from 2.3 million square feet in Q1, with renewal spreads around 11%.
Net debt to total assets rose slightly to 69.9%, and the $1.4 billion Mountain JV floating-rate loan still needs refinancing with only one extension option remaining.
Occupancy was 94.3%, and lease-up of vacant Hawaii and Indiana assets remains slow.
positive_highlights: Normalized FFO of $0.21 per share came in at the high end of guidance and rose 54% year-over-year.
Refinancing $1.235 billion of floating-rate debt into $1.16 billion fixed at 6.4% is expected to save $8.5 million annually, or $0.13 per share.
Dividend raised from $0.01 to $0.05 per quarter, with Q3 FFO guidance of $0.25–$0.27 per share.
summary: ILPT reported Q2 2025 normalized FFO of $13.8 million or $0.21 per share, at the high end of guidance and up 54% year-over-year. NOI was $87.6 million and cash basis NOI $84.7 million, both up year-over-year and sequentially. Q3 normalized FFO guidance was set at $0.25–$0.27 per share, and the quarterly dividend was raised from $0.01 to $0.05. The company refinanced $1.235 billion of floating-rate debt into $1.16 billion of fixed-rate debt at 6.4%, expecting $8.5 million in annual cash savings.

negative_highlights: Excluding the acquisition, P&C Insurance organic premium growth was modest (~2%) due to competitive pressure in E&S property, excess D&O and cyber
Reinsurance net premium written growth of 5.8% was muted by a $94 million timing impact from ceded premium accruals, though this is expected to reverse next quarter
The acquired MidCorp business added 100 basis points to the accident-year ex-cat loss ratio, and program business exits will take 12-18 months on an earned basis to fully benefit results
positive_highlights: Reinsurance segment produced its best-ever pretax underwriting income of $451 million with 8.7% gross written premium growth

P&C Insurance net premium written surpassed $2 billion, up 30.7% YoY, including $451 million from the MidCorp/entertainment acquisition; annualized premium now expected slightly above the ~$1.5 billion acquisition forecast
Book value per share grew 7.3% in the quarter and 11.4% year-to-date, with net investment income up 7% sequentially to $405 million and cash flow from operations of ~$1.1 billion
summary: Arch Capital reported Q2 2025 after-tax operating income of $979 million, or $2.58 per share, with an 18.2% annualized operating ROE and book value per share up 7.3% in the quarter and 11.4% year-to-date. The Reinsurance segment produced its best-ever pretax underwriting income of $451 million, P&C Insurance net premium written rose 30.7% to over $2 billion (including $451 million from the acquired MidCorp/entertainment business), and Mortgage delivered $238 million of underwriting income, while the overall ex-cat accident-year combined ratio was 80.9%. Net investment income rose 7% sequentially to $405 million and cash flow from operations was approximately $1.1 billion. Management pointed to selective growth in casualty and Florida property cat, stabilizing D&O and cyber rates, and a higher-than-forecast ~$1.5 billion annualized premium from the acquired business, but noted competitive pressure in E&S property, D&O and cyber, and a $94 million timing-driven dip in reinsurance net premium written expected to reverse next quarter.

negative_highlights: Net loss of $13M in Q2 2025, compared to net income of $36M a year ago
Sales down 8% YoY due to 22% lower Brent prices
Guidance at lower end; first-half average of 47,000 BOE/d near the bottom of 47,000-53,000 range
positive_highlights: Record production of 47,200 BOE/d, up 44% YoY
Lowest operating cost per BOE since early 2022
Signed $200M prepayment facility mandate to address 2026 debt maturity
summary: Gran Tierra reported record production of 47,200 BOE/d (up 44% YoY), but net loss widened to $13M due to lower Brent prices. Operating costs per BOE hit the lowest since early 2022, and funds flow from operations rose 17% YoY. The company signed a mandate for a $200M prepayment facility and expects closing in Q3 2025, while maintaining 2025 production guidance of 47,000-53,000 BOE/d. Management highlighted strong results from Cohembi, Costayaco, and Simonette, and expressed confidence in ramping production in H2.

negative_highlights: Higher interest charges decreased earnings by $0.04 per share reflecting increased debt levels
Ongoing litigation regarding the Marshall Fire with trial scheduled to conclude mid-to-late November, though liability remains below insurance coverage of approximately $500 million
positive_highlights: Delivered earnings of $0.75 per share compared to $0.54 last year
Reaffirmed full-year EPS guidance range of $3.75-$3.85 despite macro headwinds
Secured 19 gas turbine reservations and identified visibility for an additional $15 billion in capital investment needs
summary: Xcel Energy reported Q2 FY2025 earnings of $0.75 per share, beating the prior year's $0.54 driven by higher revenue and AFUDC, while reaffirming full-year EPS guidance of $3.75 to $3.85 unchanged from prior levels. Management highlighted a significant incremental capital need of approximately $15 billion beyond its base plan due to data center demand and reliability requirements in Texas/New Mexico and Colorado. The company remains confident in delivering on these projects despite evolving federal policy, maintaining strong balance sheet metrics with recent equity issuance.

negative_highlights: GAAP net loss of $0.10 per share and book value per share declined to $27.93 from $28.50
Loans rated 4 or 5 rose to 13 from 11, and the general worsening in macroeconomic factors partly offset the $780,000 CECL reserve release
No dividend reinstated; management tied any payout to REO monetization and portfolio ramp without timing, and liquidity was $65 million
positive_highlights: Net interest income rose $3 million quarter-over-quarter to $8.6 million, aided by ~$1 million of financing cost savings from the new facility
EAD swung to $0.04 per share from a $0.86 loss in Q1, and net real estate operations improved $1.9 million to a loss of $77,000 on better hotel performance
Portfolio grew a net $60.5 million to $1.4 billion on a $72 million new commitment, with 272,000 shares repurchased for $5.1 million at an approximate 33% discount to book
summary: ACR reported a GAAP net loss of $732,000, or $0.10 per diluted share, on net interest income of $8.6 million, which rose $3 million quarter-over-quarter largely from lower financing costs and the non-recurrence of $1.5 million in accelerated deferred financing charges. Earnings available for distribution were $0.04 per share versus a $0.86 loss in Q1, and GAAP book value per share fell to $27.93 from $28.50. The loan portfolio grew a net $60.5 million to $1.4 billion via a $72 million new commitment, and management reiterated its goal to grow the portfolio $300-500 million through year-end, with leverage potentially reaching 3.5-4x and another CLO planned. Dividend reinstatement remains contingent on monetizing REO and ramping the portfolio, with no timing given.

negative_highlights: Management explicitly stated that material signs of growth from new partnerships will likely turn into revenue 'more so in the early part of next year' rather than H2 FY2025.
CEO noted a general market perception of a '20% drop-off in organic search' for many brands due to answer engines, creating urgency but not immediate monetization.
The rebrand is described as an intermediate step with potential disruption during the transition period before full efficacy is realized.
positive_highlights: Revenue of $84.4 million beat high-side guidance; non-GAAP operating income of $4.8 million also exceeded expectations.
Non-GAAP gross margin expanded to 80% (up 280 bps YoY) and non-GAAP operating margin improved to 6%.
ARR reached nearly $355 million with a 9% increase in average revenue per enterprise account.
summary: Commerce reported Q2 FY2025 revenue of $84.4 million (up 3% YoY) and non-GAAP operating income of $4.8 million, both exceeding the high end of guidance. The company executed a corporate rebrand to 'Commerce' and announced new partnerships with Perplexity, Google Cloud, PROS, and Accenture focused on AI-driven commerce capabilities. While Q2 results were solid, management noted that material revenue benefits from these strategic shifts are expected in early 2026 rather than the current year.

negative_highlights: Wireless revenue was essentially flat at $18.4M versus $18.3M, and management reiterated that wireless demand will continue to decline on a secular basis
Adjusted operating expenses rose to $29.4M from $28.1M, and R&D is set to accelerate ~5%-7% above prior year in H2 with further 6%-8% growth into 2026
Net unit churn of 1.6% remained within normal ranges despite sequential improvement; new logos were only ~15% of bookings
positive_highlights: Software operations bookings grew more than 34% YoY to $11.7M, including 23 six-figure and 1 seven-figure contracts; first-half bookings reached ~$20M
Professional services revenue rose nearly 25% YoY to $5.4M, driven by triple-digit managed services growth and improved resource utilization
Full-year revenue and adjusted EBITDA guidance raised, with revenue midpoint up ~$3M (2%) and EBITDA midpoint up 5% from 2024
summary: Spok reported Q2 FY2025 GAAP revenue of $35.7M, up from $34.0M a year ago, with software revenue of $17.2M (up 10%) and wireless revenue of $18.4M. GAAP net income was $4.6M, or $0.22 per diluted share, versus $3.4M or $0.17 a year earlier, and adjusted EBITDA was $7.5M versus $7.0M. Software operations bookings rose more than 34% to $11.7M, and management raised full-year 2025 guidance: total revenue of $138M-$143.5M (midpoint ~$3M/2% above prior) and adjusted EBITDA of $28.5M-$32.5M (midpoint +5% vs 2024). R&D spend is expected to accelerate in the second half, exceeding prior-year levels by ~5%-7% and rising a further 6%-8% into 2026.

negative_highlights: Comparable RevPAR declined 2.2% as government room nights fell ~26% and group revenue declined ~4%
Net loss of $39.9 million and no common dividend reinstatement in 2025
Total revenue fell over $41 million year-to-date versus 2024 following asset sales, and blended debt cost is 8.1% with ~76% effectively floating
positive_highlights: Comparable hotel EBITDA grew 2.6% despite a 2.2% RevPAR decline, with comparable margin expanding 39 bps
Other revenue rose 22% per occupied room, and renovated/repositioned hotels posted a 19% RevPAR increase (La Concha Key West RevPAR +28%, EBITDA +59%)
Highland loan extended, eliminating roughly $6.8 million of quarterly default interest, and MS 17 ($410M) plus Highland ($734M) maturities pushed to 2026-2028
summary: AHT reported a Q2 2025 net loss of $39.9 million (-$6.88 per diluted share) with AFFO of $0.78 per share, depressed by about $6.8 million of accrued default interest on the $744 million Highland loan that was eliminated by an extension; excluding it, AFFO would have been roughly $11.4 million ($1.93/share). Comparable RevPAR fell 2.2% on a 26% decline in government room nights, while comparable total revenue rose 1.3% and comparable hotel EBITDA rose 2.6% with margin up 39 bps. No numeric guidance was issued; management expects demand headwinds to subside, plans at least 3 additional asset sales, launched a follow-on nontraded preferred offering after a $212 million raise, and will not reinstate a common dividend in 2025.

negative_highlights: Revenue grew only 1% year over year to $104.1 million, and ARR declined 1.3% to $394.1 million
Billings fell 0.9% to $110.6 million and operating cash flow swung to a $17.8 million outflow from a $6.2 million inflow
Non-GAAP EPS was a loss of $0.00 versus $0.07 income a year earlier, with guidance withheld until the Q4 Analyst Day
positive_highlights: Gross margin expanded to 60.4% GAAP and 60.8% non-GAAP versus 59.1% and 59.5% a year earlier
Non-GAAP operating margin rose to 10.4% from 6.2% and adjusted EBITDA margin to 12.4% from 8.5%
Received approximately $37.9 million from Oracle; settled Rimini II litigation with no findings of infringement outstanding
summary: Rimini Street reported Q2 2025 revenue of $104.1 million, up 1% year over year but down 1.3% on ARR to $394.1 million, with billings down 0.9% and a non-GAAP net loss of $0.00 per diluted share versus $0.07 income a year earlier. GAAP net income of $30.3 million / $0.32 per diluted share was driven by a $36.2 million Oracle litigation settlement gain rather than operations. The company received approximately $37.9 million back from Oracle and settled Rimini II, while reaffirming a PeopleSoft wind-down by mid-2028; guidance was explicitly withheld until an Analyst Day expected in Q4. This is the first quarter without a formal guide, and the underlying operational picture showed gross margin expansion to 60.4% (non-GAAP 60.8%) and non-GAAP operating margin up to 10.4% from 6.2%, but headline growth and ARR remain flat to down.

negative_highlights: Full-year 2025 adjusted EBITDA guided to at or near low end of previous range
Producer mechanical issue remediation slower than expected, wells to remain down until end of Q3
Blue water marine market softened with incremental supply, limiting day rate increases
positive_highlights: Shenandoah delivered first oil, initial wells expected to meet/exceed predrill expectations
Salamanca on track for first oil by end of Q3 2025
Free cash flow generation expected to begin in Q3 2025, with 2026 outlook unchanged
summary: Genesis Energy reported Q2 2025 results in line with expectations but guided to the low end of prior adjusted EBITDA guidance due to delayed producer well remediation and slightly delayed first oil from Shenandoah and Salamanca. Shenandoah achieved first oil last week with initial wells expected to exceed predrill expectations and ramp to 100,000 barrels per day by end of September; Salamanca remains on track for first oil by end of Q3. Management reaffirmed 2026 outlook and expects free cash flow generation to begin in Q3, with focus on deleveraging and potential capital returns to unitholders.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EPS of $0.79 missed the prior year's $1.05, driven by lower new boat volumes and higher SG&A expenses.
Gross profit declined to $129 million from $133 million due to promotional activity and product mix shifts.
positive_highlights: Total revenue increased 2% to $553 million in a challenging industry environment where competitors saw declines exceeding 15%.
summary: OneWater Marine reported Q3 FY2025 revenue of $553 million (up 2% YoY) and adjusted EPS of $0.79, missing the prior year's $1.05 despite outperforming an industry that declined over 15%. Gross profit fell to $129 million due to lower new boat volumes and promotional pressure, while SG&A expenses rose 6% to $92 million. Management raised full-year revenue guidance to a range of $1.8 billion-$1.85 billion but lowered adjusted EBITDA ($65M-$80M) and EPS ($0.50-$0.75) outlooks citing macro uncertainty, tariff impacts on consumer confidence, and margin pressure.

negative_highlights: Total originations fell to $197 million from $277.6 million a year ago, with recreation originations down to $142.8 million from $209.6 million
Provision for credit loss rose to $21.6 million from $18.6 million in the prior year quarter, with recreation net charge-offs at 3.25% of the average portfolio
Operating costs increased to $21.5 million from $20 million, with technology and employee costs expected to remain elevated
positive_highlights: Net income increased 56% YoY to $11.1 million, or $0.46 per diluted share
Net interest margin remained steady at 8.09%, with total interest yield up 23 bps to 11.75%
Strategic partnership originations reached a record $168.6 million, the third straight quarter above $120 million
summary: MFIN reported Q2 net income of $11.1 million, up 56% YoY, and diluted EPS of $0.46, with net interest income up 7% to $53.4 million and NIM essentially flat at 8.09%. Book value per share rose to $16.77 from $16.36 a quarter ago and $15.25 a year ago. However, originations fell sharply to $197 million from $277.6 million a year ago, and provision for credit loss rose to $21.6 million from $18.6 million, with elevated charge-offs in the recreation portfolio. Management expressed confidence in credit improvement from newer vintages and noted ample capital after a $77.5 million preferred offering, expecting higher growth ahead; they did not provide formal numeric guidance.

negative_highlights: Book value declined 2.4% from the prior quarter due to broad market weakness following Liberation Day volatility in April.
Net interest income decreased by $1.1 million (6%) compared to the prior quarter as certain commercial loans matured and were placed on nonaccrual status.
Arc Home contributed a loss of approximately $0.13 per share ($130,000) for the quarter due to pipeline losses from April volatility.
positive_highlights: Refinanced high-cost legacy WMC repo debt, reducing cost of capital by over 50 basis points and generating approximately $40 million in additional cash for redeployment.
Acquired an additional 21.4% stake in Arc Home (total ownership now 66%) with minimal dilution expected to be earnings accretive starting in 2026.
Completed two securitizations and closed two new residential mortgage warehouse facilities designed to reduce mark-to-market risk.
summary: MITT reported a GAAP net loss of $1.4 million ($0.05 per share) and an economic return on equity that was essentially flat at negative 0.5% for the quarter ended June 30, 2025. Book value declined modestly by 2.4% to $10.39 per share due to mark-to-market losses from April volatility and commercial loan maturities placed on nonaccrual, though these were partially offset by gains on securitizations and a post-quarter refinancing that reduced debt costs by over 50 bps. The company increased its quarterly dividend by 5% to $0.21 per share.

negative_highlights: Net loss attributable to common stockholders was $16 million or $0.24 per diluted share
Government segment softness impacted Capital Hilton and D.C. market during the quarter
Two properties under renovation (Park Hyatt Beaver Creek, Hotel Yountville) muted results; excluding them, portfolio EBITDA growth was 6.3%
positive_highlights: Comparable hotel EBITDA grew 3.7% to $47.8 million with margin expansion of 11 bps
Resort portfolio EBITDA rose 6.9% to $25.7 million, led by Ritz-Carlton Lake Tahoe total revenue growth of ~39% and Dorado Beach RevPAR up 17%
Group revenue pace for full-year 2025 is up 8.6% and Q3 up 8.8%; Ritz-Carlton Lake Tahoe full-year group pace ahead 44%
summary: Braemar reported Q2 2025 comparable RevPAR of $318, up 1.5% YoY, with comparable hotel EBITDA of $47.8 million, up 3.7%, and comparable hotel EBITDA margin improving 11 bps. Net loss attributable to common stockholders was $16 million or $0.24 per diluted share, with AFFO of $0.09 per share and Adjusted EBITDAre of $38.9 million. Group revenue pace is up 8.6% for full-year 2025 and 8.8% for Q3, while the company signed a definitive agreement to watch the Marriott Seattle Waterfront for $145 million (8.1% cap rate on trailing NOI) and redeemed approximately $107 million of nontraded preferred stock. The quarter marks the third consecutive quarter of RevPAR growth, with resort EBITDA up 6.9% and urban RevPAR up 0.5%, though full-year guidance was not explicitly reiterated beyond capex range of $75-95 million.

negative_highlights: Revenue decreased 20% year-over-year to $4 million amid weak demand across all segments
Gross margin contracted slightly from 51% in Q2 FY2024 to 50%
Management lowered guidance, now expecting EBITDA neutrality instead of profitability for H2 2025
positive_highlights: Delivered first XtremeScan products to a large industrial customer with flawless deployment
Received purchase orders from multiple Fortune 50 companies in ruggedized scanning markets
Operating loss narrowed sequentially due to cost control and lower expenses
summary: Socket Mobile reported Q2 FY2025 revenue of $4 million, a 20% year-over-year decrease driven by soft demand and cautious purchasing behavior in both domestic and international businesses. Gross margins declined slightly to 50%, while operating expenses were reduced to $2.7 million through cost control measures. Management revised its full-year outlook downward, now expecting EBITDA neutrality for the second half of 2025 rather than profitability.

negative_highlights: GAAP net loss widened to $9.3 million ($0.48/share) from $8.0 million ($0.46/share) in Q1
Full-year 2025 cash burn now expected at the high end of the $27-$29 million range
Management explicitly noted top-line revenue growth 'may remain modest through the rest of the year'
positive_highlights: Contract wins tripled from 2 to 6, with over 100 engaged customers and 30 in advanced negotiations
Certified as an NVIDIA DRIVE AGX partner and selected for the GM-sponsored WinTOR project
$30 million top global transportation OEM opportunity expected to begin contributing revenue this year, plus progress with a separate top-5 global OEM
summary: AEye reported a Q2 2025 GAAP net loss of $9.3 million or $0.48 per share, wider than Q1's $8.0 million or $0.46 per share, with non-GAAP net loss of $6.7 million ($0.35/share) versus $5.5 million ($0.31/share) in Q1. No revenue figure was disclosed; management said top-line growth 'may remain modest through the rest of the year.' Cash burn fell about $1 million to $7.1 million, and quarter-end cash of $19.2 million has since been more than tripled, extending runway into 2027, though full-year 2025 cash burn is now guided to the high end of the prior $27-$29 million range. Positives included a tripling of contract wins from 2 to 6, NVIDIA DRIVE AGX certification, the GM-backed WinTOR selection, a top-5 global OEM step forward, and a ~$30 million transportation OEM opportunity expected to contribute revenue this year over 2-3 years.

negative_highlights: EBITDA swung to negative $21 million from positive $47 million in Q1, with net loss widening to $86 million or $1.29 per share
Dividend suspended by the Board due to macroeconomic uncertainty and focus on debt reduction
Pulp sales volumes fell 51,000 tonnes to 427,000 tonnes, with Chinese NBSK prices down $59 per tonne to $734
positive_highlights: Reaffirmed One Goal, One Hundred target of $100 million in cost savings by end-2026, with $25 million anticipated in 2025
Liquidity remained solid at $438 million, comprising $146 million cash and $292 million undrawn revolvers with no maintenance covenant concerns
Mass Timber backlog grew to about $68 million with potential sales inquiries exceeding $400 million over the last two quarters
summary: Mercer reported Q2 2025 EBITDA of negative $21 million versus positive $47 million in Q1, a net loss of $86 million or $1.29 per share, and cash consumption of $35 million. The decline was driven by roughly $26 million of negative FX from a weaker U.S. dollar, an $8 million pulp price impact in China, an $11 million non-cash hardwood inventory impairment, and higher fiber costs, producing negative EBITDA in both the Pulp (-$10 million) and Solid Wood (-$5 million) segments. The Board suspended the dividend, and management guided to continued soft pulp pricing through the summer with some recovery expected in Q4 2025 and into 2026. Management reaffirmed its One Goal, One Hundred program targeting $100 million in cost savings by end-2026, with $5 million achieved to date and $25 million expected for 2025, while noting no near-term pulp price recovery.

negative_highlights: FY2025 OpEx guidance was raised to $304–308 million, partly due to a $5.3 million negative FX impact.
Joenja first-half 2025 revenue was down slightly versus the last half of 2024, attributed to Q2 2024 inventory build.
The sebetralstat launch introduces potential competition in the HAE acute market, though management noted patient populations are distinct.
positive_highlights: Total Q2 revenue grew 26% year-over-year, driven by 28% RUCONEST growth to $80.4 million and 15% sequential Joenja growth to $12.8 million.
Operating profit swung to $12.9 million from a $3.1 million loss in Q2 2024, and cash increased to $130.8 million from $108.9 million in Q1 2025.
FY2025 revenue guidance was raised to $335–350 million from $325–340 million.
summary: Pharming reported Q2 2025 total revenues up 26% year-over-year, gross profit up 27% to $84.2 million, and operating profit of $12.9 million versus a $3.1 million loss a year ago. RUCONEST revenue grew 28% to $80.4 million and Joenja net revenue rose 15% sequentially to $12.8 million. Management raised FY2025 revenue guidance to $335–350 million from $325–340 million, implying 13–18% growth, while slightly increasing the OpEx outlook to $304–308 million, partly due to a $5.3 million FX headwind. The company also highlighted VUS patient reclassification (20% of 1,400 cases) and pediatric expansion as key Joenja catalysts.

negative_highlights: Fourth quarter expected to see more tariff cost flow-through
Watercraft marketplace remains weak and industry struggles
Diving marketplace challenged with uncertainties
positive_highlights: Sales up 5% to $180.7 million versus the prior year
Operating profit swung to $7.3 million from an operating loss
Gross margin up 1.8 points to 37.6%
summary: Johnson Outdoors reported Q3 FY2025 net sales of $180.7 million, up 5% year-over-year, with operating profit of $7.3 million versus an operating loss a year ago. Gross margin expanded 1.8 points to 37.6%, driven by higher volumes, pricing, and cost savings, partly offset by tariffs. Management noted strong demand for new fishing innovations and Jetboil products, but cautioned on fourth-quarter tariff costs and a still-weak watercraft market. The company remains debt-free and is focused on cost savings and tariff mitigation.

negative_highlights: Comparable store sales fell 2.3%, with EPS down to $0.16 from $0.27.
Operating margin declined 120 bps to 2.4% due to higher SG&A costs, which rose 4.1% to $107.3M.
Special order business was down mid-single digits partly due to suspended China orders after 145% tariffs; full recovery not expected until Q3.
positive_highlights: Total sales increased 1.3% to $181M, the first total written/delivered sales increase in over 2 years.
Gross margin expanded 40 bps to 60.8%, attributed to product selection and merchandising mix.
Traffic remained positive in the mid-single digits, and web sales grew 8.4%.
summary: Haverty's Q2 2025 net sales rose 1.3% to $181M, but comparable sales fell 2.3%. EPS dropped to $0.16 from $0.27 a year ago, as operating margin contracted to 2.4% from 3.6%. Gross margin improved to 60.8%, and management noted the first total written and delivered sales increase in over 2 years, though comps remain negative. Full-year gross margin guidance of 60%-60.5% and SG&A guidance were maintained, with tariffs posing ongoing uncertainty.

negative_highlights: Earnings available for distribution fell to $0.43 per share from $0.68 a year ago and cash available for distribution fell to $0.46 from $0.64
Q2 dividend of $0.50 was only 0.92x covered by cash available for distribution
Life science lab leasing remains challenging amid tariff and NIH funding uncertainty, and management flagged a few floating-rate 2021-vintage B-piece loans it is watching
positive_highlights: Net income rose to $0.54 per diluted share from $0.40 in Q2 2024, driven by a $4.6 million increase in interest income to $22.8 million
Book value per share increased 1% QoQ to $17.40, aided by unrealized gains on preferred stock investments
Q3 CAD guidance midpoint of $0.50 would restore full coverage of the $0.50 dividend, versus 0.92x coverage in Q2
summary: NREF reported Q2 2025 net income of $0.54 per diluted share versus $0.40 a year ago on interest income of $22.8 million, up $4.6 million YoY, but earnings available for distribution fell to $0.43 from $0.68 and cash available for distribution fell to $0.46 from $0.64. The $0.50 quarterly dividend was only 0.92x covered by CAD. Q3 guidance was set at EAD of $0.42 (range $0.37-$0.47) and CAD of $0.50 (range $0.45-$0.55), with book value per share up 1% QoQ to $17.40. Management flagged an active $235 million origination pipeline and an expected high-single-digit increase in the CAD run rate.

negative_highlights: Revenue fell 1% YoY to $30.7M while expenses rose 3.7% YoY, and adjusted EBITDA margin was 18.7% versus 19.7% for 1H25
Net flows were negative for the quarter, offsetting organic wins
Management said operating leverage will take time through 2026, expects management fee rate to keep declining on institutional mix, and said the OCIO pipeline has come down and could be stronger
