positive_highlights: Discretionary AUM rose 4.4% QoQ and 9.7% YoY to $23.7B; total AUM hit a firm-record $36.7B
Added $80M of organic new client accounts in Q2 and $0.5B in 1H25, roughly $2B over the past four quarters
Board raised the quarterly dividend 5% to $0.21 per share and authorized a new $25M buyback after completing the prior $12M program
summary: Revenue fell 1% YoY to $30.7M while expenses rose 3.7% YoY, compressing adjusted EBITDA margin to 18.7% of revenue; adjusted net income was $3.3M or $0.25 diluted adjusted EPS, and GAAP net income to Class A was $1.9M or $0.21 per share. Discretionary AUM rose 4.4% QoQ and 9.7% YoY to $23.7B, driven primarily by market appreciation, while net flows were negative though $80M of organic new client accounts were added ($0.5B in 1H25). Management gave no numeric guidance, said operating leverage will take time through 2026, and flagged the average management fee rate will keep declining as institutional mix grows. The board raised the quarterly dividend 5% to $0.21 and a new $25M buyback was announced after completing the prior $12M program, with $15.3M repurchased in Q2.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined 13.7% year-over-year due to lower case volume in a challenging macro environment.
Same-store revenue fell approximately 22%, indicating persistent consumer spending softness.
London facility remains cash flow negative despite outperforming the chain on comp sales.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA improved sequentially by $2 million compared to Q1, reflecting cost reduction plan impact.
summary: AirSculpt reported Q2 FY2025 revenue of $44 million, a decline of 13.7% year-over-year driven by lower case volume (down 14.1%) and same-store revenue down approximately 22%. Adjusted EBITDA was $5.8 million with a margin of 13.3%, narrowing from the prior year quarter due to soft consumer spending, though sequential improvement is noted. Management reiterated full-year FY2025 guidance for revenue between $160M-$170M and adjusted EBITDA between $16M-$18M without raising or lowering expectations.

negative_highlights: Q2 revenue declined to $271.4 million from $285.8 million year-over-year
Q2 adjusted EBITDA turned negative at a $849,000 loss versus positive $2.9 million a year earlier
Net loss widened to $22.7 million from $1.7 million, including a $17 million noncash derivative charge
positive_highlights: First-half revenue rose 8% year-over-year to $524.8 million, the strongest first half since 2022
First-half adjusted EBITDA improved to $259,000 from a $14.7 million loss in the prior year period
Year-to-date sales over $5 million rose 38% and sales over $10 million rose 32% versus the 2024 first half
summary: Q2 FY2025 revenue fell to $271.4 million from $285.8 million, with net loss widening to $22.7 million ($0.27/diluted share) versus $1.7 million ($0.02) a year earlier, driven partly by a $17 million noncash derivative charge. Adjusted EBITDA swung to a loss of $849,000 from positive $2.9 million, and adjusted net loss widened to $4.7 million ($0.06) from $532,000 ($0.01). The first half showed improvement—revenue up 8% to $524.8 million, adjusted EBITDA of $259,000 versus a $14.7 million loss—but the second quarter weakened on reduced May and early-June closings. No formal forward guidance was issued; management expressed optimism about Q3 and the second half citing luxury demand, rising average transaction values of $1.92 million, and a $28.1 billion development marketing pipeline.

negative_highlights: Net sales fell approximately 13% year-over-year to $54.3 million
Adjusted EBITDA declined $1.9 million to $3.9 million from $5.8 million in the prior year period
Management expects tariff-related expenses to increase in the second half as holiday goods are received, and cited consumers delaying or trading down plus a frozen housing market pressuring demand
positive_highlights: Gross margin expanded 56 bps to 24.7% even after absorbing $1.6 million of tariff costs (~200 bps), which would have put margin near 28% ex-tariff
Inventory reduced approximately $14 million versus the prior year quarter, supporting operating cash flow of $13.3 million
Net leverage held at 0.5x trailing 12-month EBITDA after repaying about $2 million of debt and repurchasing nearly $800,000 of shares
summary: Escalade reported Q2 FY2025 net sales of $54.3 million, down approximately 13% year-over-year, with net income of $1.8 million or $0.13 per diluted share. Gross margin expanded 56 bps to 24.7% despite a $1.6 million tariff headwind (~200 bps of margin), and SG&A fell 1.8% to $10.2 million, but adjusted EBITDA dropped $1.9 million to $3.9 million from $5.8 million. No formal revenue or EPS guidance was provided; management flagged higher tariff costs in the second half offset by targeted price increases and sourcing cost-sharing, and said Q3 seasonal inventory build will be slightly lower than prior year. Inventory was reduced ~$14 million year-over-year, debt was repaid ~$2 million, and ~$800,000 of shares were repurchased.

negative_highlights: Q2 bookings fell 53% YoY (up 15% excluding prior-year large enterprise deals), a sharp deceleration.
Organic growth was only 1% (5% excluding HR Compliance/ERTC headwind), and professional services revenue came in below plan.
Adjusted EBITDA margin guidance range was lowered at the low end to 22–24% from 23–24%, partly on near-term Lathem margin dilution.
positive_highlights: Full-year revenue guidance raised to $138–142 million from $134–138 million, including the Lathem acquisition.
Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 200 bps YoY to 17%, with adjusted EBITDA of $5.2 million versus $4.1 million.
Contracted revenue backlog reached a record $82 million, up 68% YoY, and attach rates rose 400 bps YoY.
summary: Asure reported Q2 FY2025 revenue of $30.1 million, up 7% YoY (10% excluding ERTC), with recurring revenue at $28.6 million (95% of total). Organic growth was only 1%, or 5% excluding a 4% HR Compliance/ERTC headwind. Adjusted EBITDA rose to $5.2 million (17% margin) from $4.1 million (15%), while gross margin slipped to 66% from 67%. Full-year revenue guidance was raised to $138–142 million from $134–138 million, but the low end of the adjusted EBITDA margin range was cut to 22–24% from 23–24%; the raise is largely attributable to the Lathem acquisition (~$7 million in the second half), and core organic guidance was effectively trimmed.

negative_highlights: Total revenues fell 27% year-over-year to $126 million, with online game revenues down 28% YoY
Media platform operating loss was $69 million versus a $72 million loss last year, with no stated breakeven timeline
Q3 guidance implies marketing services revenues down 20-25% YoY and a net loss of $25-35 million
positive_highlights: Online game revenues and bottom line both hit the high end of Q2 guidance
Changyou segment operating profit rose to $51 million from $32 million in the year-ago quarter
Share repurchase program has bought back 6.6 million ADS for approximately $83 million, more than half of the total commitment
summary: Sohu reported Q2 2025 total revenues of $126 million, down 27% year-over-year and 7% quarter-over-quarter, with a GAAP net loss of $20 million versus a $38 million loss in Q2 2024 and net income of $182 million in Q1 2025. Online game revenues of $106 million and bottom-line performance hit the high end of guidance, but marketing services revenues of $16 million fell 21% year-over-year. Q3 guidance calls for online game revenues of $107-117 million (down 8-16% YoY, up 1-10% QoQ), marketing services revenues of $40-50 million (down 20-25% YoY), and a net loss of $25-35 million. Management cited a weak macroeconomic environment and cautious advertiser spending, with no near-term breakeven path for the media platform and buyback now over halfway complete at $83 million.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined 37.4% YoY to $105.6M; guidance for Q3 implies a further sequential decline (midpoint $80M vs $105.6M)
Active earning coaches down 32.7% YoY to 22,800, with continued pressure on client acquisition
Q3 guidance for EPS of $0.00 to -$0.60 indicates potential significant losses and reflects confidence in a near-term recovery
positive_highlights: EPS of $0.22 beat prior year's loss of $0.75 and came in above guidance
Sequential productivity improvement for the second consecutive quarter (Q2 decline of 6.9% improved from 10.9% in Q2 2024)
Balance sheet remains strong with $162.7M cash and no debt
summary: Q2 FY2025 revenue was $105.6M, down 37.4% YoY, with EPS of $0.22 vs a loss of $0.75 in the prior year. Active earning OPTAVIA coaches fell 32.7% YoY to 22,800, and average revenue per coach declined 6.9% YoY to $4,630, though it improved sequentially for the second consecutive quarter. Gross margin contracted 60 bps to 72.6%, but operating loss improved to $1.1M from $7.9M loss a year ago. Guidance for Q3 expects revenue of $70M-$90M and EPS of $0.00 to -$0.60, signaling further deterioration and significant uncertainty from the new Premier+ pricing rollout.

negative_highlights: Full-year revenue guidance narrowed significantly, lowering the midpoint by approximately $500,000.
SG&A expenses increased 11% YoY ($2.2M) primarily due to higher compensation costs for new hires and travel.
Net loss widened slightly from $14.0M in Q2 FY2024 to $14.7M, reflecting the cost of sales force transformation.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 15% YoY driven by expansion into 2 new U.S. territories and growth in Heart Failure units (387 vs 339).
Gross margin held steady at 84%, slightly beating the prior year's level.
Reimbursement environment improving with CMS proposing a higher-paying APC code ($45k) and transition to Category I CPT codes in Jan 2026.
summary: CVRx reported Q2 FY2025 revenue of $13.6 million (up 15% YoY) and a net loss of $14.7 million ($0.57/share), beating the prior year's EPS but missing on top-line growth relative to recent trends due to sales force ramp-up costs. Management narrowed full-year guidance, expecting total revenue between $55M-$57M (down from previous expectations) and operating expenses of $96M-$98M, citing slower productivity gains for new hires than anticipated. Gross margin remained flat at 84%, while SG&A increased significantly due to compensation costs associated with the ongoing sales transformation.

negative_highlights: Written premium growth of 11% is below the expected full-year 13-14%
G&A increased 6% and salaries/benefits up 11% due to technology and headcount costs
Average premium trends are flat due to stable car valuations
positive_highlights: Total revenue increased 18% to $369 million in Q2
Adjusted EBITDA grew 20% to $64 million, net income up 11% to $47 million
Full-year 2025 outlook raised for revenue and profits
summary: Hagerty reported Q2 2025 revenue of $369 million, up 18% year-over-year, with adjusted EBITDA up 20% to $64 million and net income up 11% to $47 million. Written premium grew 11%, commission revenue 11%, earned premium 13%, and membership/marketplace/other revenue jumped 78% to $48 million. The company raised its full-year 2025 outlook, now expecting revenue growth of 13-14%, net income of $112-120 million (up 43-53%), and adjusted EBITDA of $162-172 million (up 30-38%). Management announced a new fronting arrangement with Markel to assume 100% premium and risk starting in 2026, and highlighted strong momentum in marketplace, State Farm ramp, and Enthusiast+ launch.

Reservoir reported Q1 FY2026 revenue of $37.2 million, up 8% year-over-year (5% organic), with Recorded Music +8% to $10.4 million and Music Publishing +4% to $24.9 million. OIBDA rose 12% to $12.8 million and adjusted EBITDA rose 10% to $13.9 million; net loss was about $0.6 million and diluted loss per share was $0.01, same as the prior-year quarter. Management reiterated full-year guidance of $164-169 million revenue and $68-72 million adjusted EBITDA, unchanged from prior guidance. Operating cash flow fell $2.5 million to $6 million on royalty payment timing, and interest expense rose to $6.3 million from $5.1 million on higher debt.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA declined 18% on constant currency basis
North America gross margin pressured by input costs and inefficiencies; 540 bps decline
Europe/APAC combined revenue down 2.7% with flat volumes, EU tariffs and destocking
positive_highlights: Eighth consecutive quarter of volume growth, with 5.2% volume growth overall
Automation revenue increased 34% with robust backlog; full year $40-$45 million expected
Potential multiyear North America deal worth over $100 million could consume Shelton capacity
summary: Q2 FY2025 revenue grew 3.8% on a constant currency basis, with North America up 12.2% and volumes up 14.8%, but adjusted EBITDA declined 18% due to input cost, mix, and inefficiencies. The company is executing $8 million in cost-out actions and expects margin and EBITDA improvement in H2, with automation revenue guided to $40-$45 million. A potential multiyear North America automation deal worth over $100 million was highlighted, but no formal guidance was raised.

negative_highlights: BioPharma revenue remained a headwind, dragging total growth to 16%, though management expects this to be the last quarter of negative impact.
Adjusted EBITDA loss widened to $11.7M from $8.8M in Q2 2024, impacted by higher sales commissions and FX headwinds.
Latin America continued to show softness, partially offsetting broader strength.
positive_highlights: Core revenue (ex-BioPharma) grew 20% YoY, with North America and APAC up 24% and 33% respectively.
Signed 35 new customers in Q2, a record, with average contract values more than doubling YoY for the second consecutive quarter.
Announced the largest contract in company history with AstraZeneca, a multiyear AI and real-world evidence collaboration.
summary: SOPHiA GENETICS reported Q2 FY2025 total revenue of $18.3M, up 16% YoY, with core (ex-BioPharma) revenue growing 20%. Adjusted gross margin expanded 120 bps to 74.4%, and cash burn fell 35% YoY to $8.7M. The company reaffirmed full-year revenue guidance of $72M-$76M and adjusted EBITDA loss of $35M-$39M. New business momentum remained strong with 35 new customers signed in the quarter and a record AstraZeneca partnership announced, though revenue from that deal is expected to be modest in Q4 2025 and more significant in 2026.

negative_highlights: Sample Management revenue decreased 22% year-over-year due to a large consumer genetics customer exit, with no significant expected revenue in the second half of 2025.
International HIV diagnostic orders are slowing considerably as partners work through existing inventory following USAID funding disruptions.
U.S. Diagnostics revenue declined 1% year-over-year amid uncertainty regarding federal budget cuts and staffing reductions at HHS/CDC.
positive_highlights: Core revenue of $30.8 million was above the midpoint of guidance despite headwinds.
Non-GAAP gross margin expanded slightly to 43.2% driven by manufacturing transition benefits and lower scrap rates.
Successfully launched HEMAcollect PROTEIN for blood proteomics research.
summary: OraSure reported Q2 FY2025 core revenue of $30.8 million and total revenue of $31.2 million, which fell in the top half of its guidance range due to a significant decline from one large consumer genetics customer. GAAP gross margin was 42.1% (non-GAAP 43.2%), slightly better than expectations driven by manufacturing improvements and lower scrap rates. Management lowered Q3 revenue guidance to $27M-$30M citing inventory destocking in international markets, a slowdown in the Together Take Me Home program from ~$2M to ~$0.5M expected run rate, and continued disruption from the consumer genetics customer.

negative_highlights: Adjusted pretax income was lower than Q2 FY2024 due to a $4 million unfavorable impact from April interest rate volatility
MSR runoff increased by approximately $8 million year-over-year driven by higher prepayment speeds and reverse asset fair value changes
Reverse servicing channel experienced declining revenue in the quarter primarily due to negative valuation adjustments on reverse buyout loans
positive_highlights: GAAP net income grew significantly, up approximately 2x versus the prior year period
Book value per share increased by $3 and reached $60 per share for the second consecutive quarter of growth
Originations volume delivered strong 35% year-over-year growth compared to the industry's 23%
summary: Onity Group reported Q2 FY2025 GAAP net income of $20 million ($2.40 per share) and adjusted pretax income of $16 million, which was lower than the prior year due to April market volatility impairing margins by over $4 million and higher MSR runoff. Management reaffirmed its full-year 2025 annualized adjusted ROE guidance range of 16% to 18%, maintaining it despite a quarter that missed expectations relative to last year's performance.

negative_highlights: Subscription revenue declined year-over-year by $1.7 million to $9.3 million (though sequential growth was noted)
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 53% year-over-year from $12.4 million to $19 million
Adjusted EBITDA swung positive at $3.1 million, exceeding the high end of guidance
Content licensing revenue surged by over $8 million YoY driven by AI training demand
summary: CuriosityStream reported Q2 FY2025 revenue of $19 million (up 53% YoY), exceeding the high end of guidance with adjusted EBITDA turning positive at $3.1 million from a loss of $1 million last year. Management raised full-year 2025 adjusted free cash flow expectations to an implied range consistent with Q3/Q4 performance, citing strong growth in AI data licensing and new international distribution deals. The company maintained its no-debt balance sheet with $30.7M liquidity.

negative_highlights: Gross margin fell 790 bps to 33.9%, with green coffee inflation (430 bps), trade/pricing (290 bps), and loyalty accrual (160 bps) as key drags.
Adjusted EBITDA dropped to $2.4M from $7.5M in prior year; full-year guidance implies significant back-half weighting.
Full-year revenue and EBITDA guidance maintained but pacing toward lower end; tariff impact and coffee inflation remain headwinds.
positive_highlights: Wholesale segment grew 14% (21% adjusting for one-time items) driven by new distribution and Black Rifle Energy.
Packaged coffee ACV increased 19 points to 46.5%, and RTD coffee held #3 share with 7% sales growth in a category down 4%.
DTC stabilized and returned to modest growth excluding prior-year loyalty reserve benefit; $2.4M benefit distorted comparison.
summary: Q2 2025 net revenue rose 7% YoY to $94.8M, or 14% excluding $3M barter and $2.4M loyalty reserve impacts, with wholesale up 21% on a like-for-like basis. Gross margin contracted 790 bps to 33.9% due to green coffee inflation, trade investment, and loyalty reserve changes. Adjusted EBITDA fell $5.1M YoY to $2.4M. Management maintained full-year revenue guidance of $395-425M and EBITDA guidance of $20-30M, but noted pacing toward the lower end and continued gross margin pressure from tariffs and coffee costs.

negative_highlights: Total revenue declined 36% year-over-year to $105 million
Subscribers fell 40% year-over-year to 2.6 million due to lower traffic from Google AI overviews
Q3 revenue guidance of $75–77 million implies a steep sequential decline from Q2, and free cash flow was negative $12 million
positive_highlights: Busuu B2B revenue grew 39% year-over-year with retention improving 22 percentage points
Non-GAAP operating expenses reduced 33% year-over-year to $64 million, with an additional $10 million opex and $7 million CapEx savings identified for 2026
Skills enrollments rose 16% quarter-over-quarter and monthly active users increased 11% quarter-over-quarter
summary: Chegg reported Q2 FY2025 revenue of $105 million, down 36% year-over-year, with 2.6 million subscribers (down 40%) and adjusted EBITDA of $23 million (22% margin). The company exceeded its own guidance on revenue and adjusted EBITDA, and non-GAAP operating expenses fell 33% year-over-year to $64 million. However, Q3 guidance calls for revenue of $75–77 million, implying a further sequential decline, and free cash flow was negative $12 million. Management highlighted growth in Busuu (15% revenue increase) and Skills enrollments (up 16% quarter-over-quarter) but acknowledged ongoing traffic headwinds from Google AI overviews.

negative_highlights: Full-year revenue growth guidance cut to 6-8% from previous 8-10%.
GE Healthcare relationship being restructured as it has not met margin expectations; this could reduce revenue.
ChemoMouthpiece revenue removed from 2025 forecast pending CPT coding change; no clarity until end of year.
positive_highlights: Gross margin expanded 574 bps to 55.2% in Q2, driven by mix shift to higher-margin oncology and rental revenue.
Adjusted EBITDA rose 32% YoY to $8 million with margin up 427 bps to 22.3%; trailing-12-month adjusted EBITDA margin hit 21.2%.
Operating cash flow doubled to $7 million in Q2; net debt reduced by $2.3 million despite buybacks and Apollo acquisition.
summary: InfuSystem reported Q2 FY2025 net revenue of $36 million, up 6.8% YoY, with gross margin expanding 574 bps to 55.2% and adjusted EBITDA up 32% to $8 million (22.3% margin). Net income increased 262% and operating cash flow more than doubled, with $3.5 million returned via buybacks. Management lowered full-year revenue growth guidance to 6-8% from 8-10%, citing delays in Wound Care volumes, ChemoMouthpiece reimbursement uncertainty, and GE Healthcare restructuring, but raised adjusted EBITDA margin guidance to 20% or higher.

DHC reported Q2 FY2025 revenue of $382.7 million, up 3% YoY, with FFO up 172% to $18.6 million ($0.08/share) and adjusted EBITDAre of $73.6 million, up 7%; management said results met analyst expectations on both top and bottom line. SHOP drove the quarter with same-property NOI up 18.5% YoY to $37.4 million, consolidated occupancy up 160 bps to 80.6%, and average monthly rate up 5.4%. Guidance was raised: 2025 SHOP NOI midpoint increased $10 million to $132-142 million, while 2025 CapEx guidance was trimmed $10 million to $140-160 million. The key balance-sheet change was refinancing activity that redeemed the 2025 notes and cut annual cash interest by almost $15 million, leaving $641 million of January 2026 zero-coupon notes still to address.

negative_highlights: Distributable earnings ex-loss of $0.09/share below the $0.15 dividend, with net interest income drag of ~$0.17 from nonaccruals
GAAP net loss of $11M and a $33M realized loss on a $51M life sciences office loan, in excess of prior CECL reserve
New $81M office loan (Arizona) downgraded to risk-rated 4, with maturity in October and extension discussions ongoing
positive_highlights: Reduced office loans 10% QoQ and 30% YoY to $524M, exiting all life-science-collateralized loans
Closed four new senior self-storage loans totaling $43M post-quarter, first investment commitments of the year
Cut unfunded commitments 50% QoQ and 58% YoY to $36.5M, and net debt-to-equity steady at 1.2x
summary: Q2 2025 GAAP net loss of $11M or -$0.20 per share; distributable earnings loss of $28M or -$0.51 per share, including a $33M realized loss on an office life sciences loan. Excluding that loss, DE was $5M or $0.09 per share, below the $0.15 dividend. Office loans fell 10% QoQ and 30% YoY to $524M; total CECL reserve declined to $119M. Post-quarter, the company closed four senior self-storage loans totaling $43M, its first new investments of 2025, and expects origination activity to build through H2 and over the next 12 months to hold the portfolio at or above current size.

negative_highlights: Full-year revenue guidance cut to $650-670 million from $660-690 million and adjusted EBITDA cut to $21-25 million from $22-27 million
Adjusted EBITDA margin contracted 120 bps to 3.0% and the company swung to an adjusted net loss of $0.09 per share from $0.05 income a year ago

reduce exposure note Systems revenue fell 24% to $43.9 million with adjusted operating income down $3.7 million, and management flagged more OEM downtime June through August than originally anticipated
positive_highlights: Free cash flow of $17.3 million in the quarter versus $0.8 million a year ago, bringing year-to-date to $28.5 million and supporting a raised full-year outlook of at least $30 million
Adjusted gross margin of 12%, up 120 bps sequentially and 70 bps year over year, on operational efficiency initiatives
Global Electrical segment adjusted operating income rose $0.4 million on flat revenue, driven by lower salary expense at new low-cost facilities; net leverage improved to 4.8x from 5.0x
summary: CVG reported Q2 FY2025 revenue of $172 million, down from $193.7 million year over year, with an adjusted EBITDA margin of 3.0% (down 120 bps) and an adjusted net loss of $0.09 per diluted share versus $0.05 income a year ago. Both revenue guidance ($650-670 million, down from $660-690 million) and adjusted EBITDA guidance ($21-25 million, down from $22-27 million) were lowered and tightened, while free cash flow guidance was raised to at least $30 million on $17.3 million of Q2 free cash flow. Trim Systems revenue fell 24% on Class 8 weakness, Global Seating fell 10%, and Global Electrical was flat; net leverage stands at 4.8x against a targeted 2x. Management offset the demand softness with $15-20 million of cost savings and tariff price-recovery negotiations.

negative_highlights: Arcadia sales down 11% YoY on weak high-end residential demand
NobelClad backlog fell to $37 million from $41 million due to tariff-driven lost business
Third-quarter guidance implies sales down $5-13 million sequentially and EBITDA down $1.5-5.5 million
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA of $13.5 million exceeded the $10-13 million guidance range
Total debt reduced 17% sequentially to $59 million
DynaEnergetics adjusted EBITDA margin rose 210 bps sequentially and 190 bps YoY to 13.4%
summary: DMC Global reported Q2 FY2025 consolidated sales of $155.5 million and adjusted EBITDA attributable to DMC of $13.5 million, exceeding the guidance range of $10 million to $13 million. Arcadia sales declined 11% YoY, DynaEnergetics declined 12%, while NobelClad grew 6% but saw backlog fall to $37 million from $41 million. The company cut total debt by 17% to $59 million. Third-quarter guidance is soft at $142-150 million sales and $8-12 million EBITDA due to tariff uncertainty, high interest rates, and weak energy activity.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined 19.5% year over year to $118.6 million as deliveries fell to 939 from 1,159.
Adjusted EBITDA dropped to $10.0 million from $12.1 million on lower deliveries.
Management said total 2025 industry deliveries will come in below the previously expected 40,000-unit average, with softer new-car demand and extended decision cycles tied to tariff uncertainty.
positive_highlights: Gross margin expanded 250 bps to 15% from 12.5% a year ago, driven by favorable product mix and production efficiency.
Operating cash flow of $8.5 million marked a fifth consecutive positive quarter, with $61.4 million cash on hand and no revolver borrowings.
Order intake of 1,226 units gave a 1.3 book-to-bill and grew backlog by roughly 300 units to 3,624.
summary: Q2 FY2025 revenue fell 19.5% to $118.6 million on 939 deliveries versus 1,159 a year ago, but gross margin expanded 250 bps to 15%, adjusted EBITDA was $10.0 million (down from $12.1 million), and adjusted EPS rose to $0.11 from $0.10. Operating cash flow was $8.5 million, a fifth straight positive quarter, with $61.4 million cash and no revolver borrowings; adjusted free cash flow for 1H25 was $20.4 million. Full-year delivery guidance was reaffirmed and SG&A is expected to ease in 2H, but management flagged that total 2025 industry deliveries will fall below the previously expected 40,000-unit average and that extended customer decision cycles, partly tied to tariffs, are pressuring new-car demand. Order intake of 1,226 units (book-to-bill 1.3) lifted backlog to 3,624 units, though dollar backlog stayed flat due to a higher rebuild/conversion mix; the tank car retrofit program remains on track for 2H26 and is expected to add about $6 million of EBITDA over 2026-2027.

negative_highlights: Connected machines revenue decreased 10% due to fewer units sold
Engagement erosion persists, though moderating: 90-day engaged users down 2% versus down 3% a year ago
Subscriber growth may be flat to declining in Q3 due to natural attrition, and Q2 benefited from pull-forward of accessories demand
positive_highlights: Operating income grew 14% and EPS grew 22% YoY
Total gross margin expanded to 59% from 53.5%, with Products gross margin up to 32.4% from 23.3%
Paid subscribers grew 7% YoY to over 3 million, with new user engagement (cuts in first 30 days) improving
summary: Q2 FY2025 revenue grew 2% to $172.1M, with operating income up 14% and EPS up 22%. Platform revenue grew 4% to $80.7M, and Products grew 1% to $91.4M, with connected machines down 10% but accessories and materials up 12% due to tariff-driven pull-forward of shipments. Paid subscribers reached 3+ million, up 7% YoY, while ARPU rose 2% to $53.84. Gross margin expanded significantly, particularly in Products, up to 32.4% from 23.3%. Management cited moderation in engagement erosion but remains cautious on tariff impacts and subscriber seasonality, guiding to potential flat/declining subscriber count in Q3.

negative_highlights: $3 million of adverse prior-year development ($2.3 million in E&S, $0.7 million in Specialty Admitted)
Fronting premiums fell 31% as commercial auto exposure was deliberately reduced, shrinking the Specialty Admitted segment
Average premium per policy declined almost 20% and premium retention fell as much as 20 points as the book shifts from larger to smaller accounts
positive_highlights: E&S combined ratio improved nearly 4 points to 91.7% with $11.7 million of underwriting profit
Casualty E&S premium growth accelerated to 4% from 1% in Q1, with overall casualty rates up 14.5% and excess casualty up 24.2%
Redomicile to Delaware expected to yield a onetime $10-13 million tax benefit and $3-6 million annual savings, moving the tax rate toward 21%
summary: James River reported Q2 2025 adjusted net operating income of $11.7 million, or $0.23 per diluted share, on GAAP net income of $3.2 million ($0.07/share), with a group combined ratio of 98.6% (68.1% loss ratio, 30.5% expense ratio) and a 14% annualized operating return on tangible common equity. E&S gross written premium grew 3% to a record above $300 million, casualty E&S accelerated to 4% growth from 1% in Q1, E&S combined ratio improved nearly 4 points to 91.7%, and casualty rates rose 14.5%. Management guided full-year expense ratio toward roughly 31% and expects a redomicile to Delaware in Q4 to deliver a onetime $10-13 million tax benefit plus $3-6 million annually, moving the effective tax rate from about 30% toward the 21% U.S. statutory rate. Offsets include $3 million of adverse prior-year development, a 31% decline in fronting premiums as commercial auto was cut, and a Specialty Admitted book that is shrinking by design.

negative_highlights: GAAP gross margin declined to 49% from 54% due to amortization and warranty costs
Adjusted gross margin down 220 basis points to 56% driven by higher warranty costs
Operating expenses increased to $21.5 million from $14.7 million due to noncash charges
positive_highlights: Revenue up 14% YoY to $13 million, above internal expectations
Adjusted EBITDA loss improved 45% YoY and 15% QoQ
Record XplorIR units shipped in Q2, with 164 devices placed
summary: 908 Devices reported Q2 2025 revenue of $13 million, up 14% year-over-year, with adjusted EBITDA loss improving 45% year-over-year and 15% sequentially. The company highlighted record XplorIR placements and strong legislative tailwinds, while maintaining its goal of adjusted EBITDA positive by Q4 2025. They launched VipIR, acquired KAF Manufacturing, and completed facility consolidations to reduce costs.

negative_highlights: Infrastructure gross margin compressed year-over-year by approximately 230 basis points to 17.9% due to project timing shifts and inflationary pressure.
Consolidated revenue decreased significantly, with the Infrastructure segment down 23.6% driven by completed large commercial construction projects in Banker Steel and DBMG's fabrication business.
Spectrum segment faced headwinds from network cancellations and ad sales softness despite new launches.
positive_highlights: Infrastructure adjusted backlog increased year-over-year to $1.3 billion, up approximately $300 million from the prior period.
Life Sciences revenue surged 88.2% to $3.2 million driven by R2 growth outside North America and consumable sales.
Company successfully completed early settlement of indebtedness refinancing transactions extending debt maturities.
summary: INNOVATE reported Q2 FY2025 consolidated revenues of $242 million, a decrease of 22.7% year-over-year compared to $313.1 million in the prior period. Net loss attributable to common stockholders was $22 million ($1.67 per share), down from net income of $14.1 million ($1.03 per share) last year, driven primarily by a 23.6% revenue decline and margin compression at the Infrastructure segment. Management highlighted successful debt refinancing extending maturities but noted that first-half results were impacted by project timing issues in infrastructure and network cancellations in spectrum.

negative_highlights: Net sales declined 10.7% year-over-year to $79.2 million on lower power sports, building products and medium/heavy-duty truck demand.
Operating income fell to $5.2 million (6.6% of sales) from $7.5 million (8.4% of sales) a year ago, and diluted EPS fell to $0.47 from $0.73.
Guidance calls for second-half sales to decline 4% to 6% year-over-year, implying continued weakness.
positive_highlights: New business wins of $47 million in the first half, with 99% incremental, already exceeding full-year 2024 wins of $45 million.
Gross margin held at 18.1% and adjusted EBITDA margin was 12%, up 30 basis points from Q1, despite a 10.7% revenue decline.
Free cash flow was $5.2 million for the first half and cash from operations $9.6 million exceeded year-to-date net earnings.
summary: Q2 FY2025 net sales were $79.2 million, down 10.7% year-over-year, with gross margin at 18.1% and adjusted EBITDA margin of 12%. GAAP diluted EPS was $0.47 versus $0.73 a year ago, and adjusted EPS was $0.53; operating income fell to $5.2 million (6.6% of sales) from $7.5 million (8.4%). Management guided second-half sales to decline 4% to 6% year-over-year and said nothing about a rebound in its core truck and power sports markets, though it disclosed $47 million of new business wins in the first half and a $25 million Mexico organic growth investment tied to new Volvo business. CEO Dave Duvall also announced a planned retirement at the end of May 2026 with Eric Palomaki named successor.

positive_highlights: Portfolio-wide 90+ day delinquencies fell 44 bps to 2.35%, with normalization in the 2023 and 2024 securitizations
Weighted average coupon on the residential whole loan portfolio expanded 82 bps QoQ to 8.37%, aided by HELOC purchases averaging nearly 11% coupons
Operating expenses ex-securitization and stock comp fell 15% YoY to $2.9 million and 22% YTD; $931 million of undrawn loan financing capacity remains
summary: Q2 2025 results were described as in line with expectations: net interest income of $9.9 million rose 5% YoY but fell 1% QoQ on interest expense from May's $42.5 million senior unsecured notes issuance, and YTD NII was up 11%. GAAP net income was $767,000 ($0.03 per diluted share) with distributable earnings of $2.6 million ($0.11), while GAAP book value per share fell 3.1% to $10.37 and economic book value fell 3.3% to $12.97. The $0.32 dividend was declared, 90+ day delinquencies improved 44 bps to 2.35%, and management said book value is roughly flat quarter-to-date and expects next quarter to grow net interest margin.

negative_highlights: Second quarter total revenue missed guidance range ($51.8M vs $56M-$61M) driven by softness in May and June across key verticals
National advertising revenue per attendee declined to $0.36 from $0.45 year-over-year despite a 24% increase in attendance
Local and regional advertising revenue fell significantly, down approximately 35% year-over-year due to cautious advertiser sentiment
positive_highlights: Third quarter revenue guidance raised to a range of $62 million to $67 million based on strong early Q3 pacing ahead of last year's levels
Programmatic advertiser volume grew by more than 50% quarter-over-quarter with approximately 70% of advertisers being new to NCM
Self-serve platform revenue increased more than 30% year-over-year signaling strong adoption
summary: NCMI reported Q2 FY2025 total revenue of $51.8 million and adjusted OIBDA of $0.7 million, missing the guidance range of $56M-$61M due to headwinds in government, CPG, and automotive categories driven by tariff uncertainty. Management raised third quarter revenue guidance to a range of $62-67M (up from prior expectations) citing strong early Q3 pacing ahead of last year's levels despite tough box office comparisons. The company reinstated its dividend at $0.03 per share and continued share repurchases, while highlighting growth in programmatic volume (+50% qoq) and self-serve revenue.

negative_highlights: Dividend reduced from $0.21 to $0.15 per share due to FAD coverage dropping to 79%.
Occupancy fell primarily due to the expiration of a lease at Aurora, Illinois and rejection of a master lease at East Orange, New Jersey.
positive_highlights: Successfully retenanted the Beaumont, Texas facility with CHRISTUS Health as of May, ending negative cash flows after nearly two years.
summary: Global Medical REIT reported Q2 FY2025 results with a significant dividend cut from $0.21 to $0.15 per share due to declining cash flow coverage dropping from 110% in Q1 to 79% in Q2. Occupancy declined to 94.5% driven by the expiration of an Aurora, Illinois lease and the rejection of a master lease at East Orange, New Jersey following Prospect Medical's bankruptcy. Management raised full-year CapEx guidance expectations due to leasing activity but emphasized strategic priorities including refinancing debt maturities in late 2025 and potential asset recycling.

negative_highlights: Consumer cannabis revenue fell to $7.9 million from $11.5 million due to strategic shift
Plant propagation adjusted gross margin dropped to 6% from 18% due to nonrecurring quality issue
Q2 free cash flow expected to be impacted by significant cash outflows
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA grew 209% to $10.8 million from $3.5 million
International revenue grew 85% and adjusted gross margin improved 1,000 bps to 52%
Positive free cash flow of $9.2 million; cash rose to $186 million with no cannabis debt
summary: Aurora Cannabis reported strong Q1 FY2026 results with net revenue up 17% to $98 million, global medical cannabis revenue up 37%, and international revenue up 85%. Adjusted gross margin expanded 1,000 basis points to 52%, and adjusted EBITDA more than doubled to $10.8 million. The company achieved positive free cash flow of $9.2 million and ended with $186 million in cash, with no cannabis debt. Management raised no explicit full-year guidance but issued Q2 guidance for 8-12% global medical cannabis growth and continued positive adjusted EBITDA.

negative_highlights: Adjusted revenue fell 2.6% YoY to $754 million and full-year revenue guidance was cut to $3.1-3.2 billion as the company will fall note weakness in of full-year growth
Commercial segment revenue declined 5.9% YoY with margin down 190 bps to 7.4%, driven by continued volume degradation at the largest commercial client
Government segment revenue declined 2.9% YoY on completed/extended implementations, with Q3 revenue guided slightly below Q3 2024
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA margin of 4.9% rose 180 bps YoY and beat guidance, prompting a raised full-year margin midpoint of 5.0-5.5%
New business ACV of $150 million rose 6% YoY and 38% sequentially, with TCV up 21% YoY to $331 million and a $3.3 billion qualified pipeline up 5% YoY
Government segment adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 520 bps YoY to 25.2% on AI and efficiency-driven lower fraud, labor and telecom costs
summary: Adjusted revenue was $754 million, down 2.6% YoY but up sequentially and in line with expectations, while adjusted EBITDA of $37 million (4.9% margin) rose 180 bps YoY and exceeded guidance. Full-year revenue guidance was trimmed to $3.1-3.2 billion (slightly below prior growth expectations), but the full-year adjusted EBITDA margin midpoint was raised to 5.0-5.5% and 2025 exit rates were reaffirmed as a 2026 proxy. Commercial revenue fell 5.9% on continued volume degradation at the largest client (margin down 190 bps), Government revenue fell 2.9% but margin expanded 520 bps, and Transportation grew 7.1%. New business ACV was $150 million, up 6% YoY and 38% sequentially.

negative_highlights: Net IRR of CP VII remained around 8%, with management noting it will not be their best fund
Real estate fundraising environment described as one of the most difficult in recent memory, though the tenth U.S. real estate fund closed 15% larger at $9 billion
positive_highlights: Record FRE of $323 million, up 18% year-over-year, with record first-half FRE margin of 48%
Full-year 2025 FRE growth guidance raised to approximately 10% from 6%, and inflow guidance raised to $50 billion from around $40 billion
Global Credit and AlpInvest delivered record FRE, together accounting for 55% of firm-wide FRE, up from less than 30% two years ago
summary: Carlyle reported record Q2 FY2025 FRE of $323 million (up 18% YoY) and record firm-wide AUM of $465 billion, with first-half FRE of $634 million (up 18%) at a record 48% margin and first-half DE of $2.05 per share. The company raised its full-year 2025 FRE growth outlook to approximately 10% from 6% and increased expected inflows to $50 billion from $40 billion. Global Credit and AlpInvest each delivered record FRE, together contributing 55% of firm-wide FRE versus under 30% two years ago. The quarter was strong on fee-related earnings and AUM, though management acknowledged low net IRRs in some older private equity funds as a remaining issue.

negative_highlights: Credit loss reserves of $1.8 million across Branded Products and Contact Center due to customer bankruptcies, including a solar-industry customer that filed Chapter 11
Contact Center revenue fell 3% and segment EBITDA dropped to $1.6 million from $3.2 million, with SG&A at 48.4% of revenue
Net leverage rose to 2.2x from 1.7x at the start of the year and full-year guidance implies only about 2% growth at the high end
positive_highlights: Branded Products revenue grew 14% with segment EBITDA of $9.0 million, up from $6.7 million a year earlier
Consolidated revenue rose about 9% YoY, the strongest growth since Q3 of last year, with gross margin up 160 bps sequentially to 38.4%
Total EBITDA increased to $6.1 million from $5.6 million and EPS doubled to $0.10 from $0.04
summary: SGC grew consolidated revenue about 9% YoY to a quarter with roughly flat gross margin of 38.4% (up 160 bps sequentially) and EPS of $0.10 versus $0.04 a year ago. Branded Products revenue rose 14% with segment EBITDA of $9.0 million versus $6.7 million, Healthcare Apparel grew 6%, while Contact Center declined 3% and saw EBITDA fall to $1.6 million from $3.2 million after a solar-customer bankruptcy drove a $1.1 million credit loss reserve. Full-year revenue guidance was reiterated unchanged at $550-575 million (about 2% growth at the high end), with management noting tariff-driven price increases phasing in over the second half. The quarter marked a sequential recovery from an operational loss in Q1, aided by cost reductions and roughly $4 million of buybacks at an average $10.26 per share.

negative_highlights: CHMP referral raises questions on tecovirimat efficacy for mpox
International orders expected to remain lumpy
US government RFP timing uncertain, with negotiation expected to take months
positive_highlights: Product revenues of $79M in Q2, fulfilling $70M of outstanding orders
Received $27M in incremental development funding from US government
Pretax operating income of $46M and net income of $35M, with no debt
summary: Q2 2025 product revenue was $79 million (oral TPOXX $53M, IV TPOXX $26M), fulfilling $70M of prior-year orders, with $26M in remaining IV TPOXX orders targeted for 2026 delivery. Pretax operating income was $46 million for the quarter, net income $35 million, and fully diluted EPS $0.49. The U.S. government committed $27 million in incremental development funding under the BARDA 19C contract ($14M manufacturing, $13M pediatric). The CHMP initiated a referral on tecovirimat efficacy for mpox, while management remains confident in the smallpox indication.

negative_highlights: Combined ratio 90.5% in Q2, up nearly 10 points YoY due to FX and higher losses
Management non-renewing a professional indemnity book, cutting gross premiums ~$60M over the next year
positive_highlights: Recorded net income of $34.1M in Q2, up 4% YoY despite higher combined ratio and lower earned premium
Reinsurance segment underwriting income up ~60% in Q2 and ~55% in H1, driving overall profitability
RoAE 20.8% in Q2 and 18.6% in H1; returned $77M to shareholders via dividends and buybacks in H1
summary: IGI reported Q2 2025 net income of $34.1M ($0.77/share), up 4% from $32.8M a year earlier, despite a higher combined ratio (90.5% vs. ~81%) driven by a ~21-point negative FX impact from pound revaluation of non-U.S. dollar reserves. Gross premiums fell 8.7% YoY to ~$190M, with long-tail down ~12%; H1 gross premiums rose ~2% to ~$395M, led by 33% growth in reinsurance. Management announced the non-renewal of a poorly performing professional indemnity book, cutting gross premiums about $60M over the next year, with a net impact of only $6-7M. Guidance was not formally updated, but the company expects continued top-line contraction in certain areas while maintaining profitability focus.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined $5.9 million year-over-year due to a $4.9 million drop in auto/EV sales and declines in other markets.
Semi market orders decreased 24% sequentially, contributing to the overall revenue miss against prior year levels.
Cash and equivalents dropped $2.8 million quarter-over-quarter to $19.2 million.
positive_highlights: Gross margin expanded 110 bps sequentially to 42.6% driven by cost actions and favorable mix.
Orders grew 10% sequentially to $28 million, with strong growth in auto/EV (+40%), life sciences (doubled), and safety/security (+74%).
Defense/aero division secured a large order from a prime contractor for missile test systems.
summary: inTEST reported Q2 FY2025 revenue of $28.1 million, a sequential increase but a year-over-year decline of $5.9 million driven by weakness in the semi and auto/EV markets. Gross margin expanded 110 bps sequentially to 42.6% due to cost reductions and product mix, while adjusted EPS was a gain of $0.03. Management provided Q3 guidance of $28-30 million revenue with similar margins, noting that visibility into the timing of orders remains limited despite an all-time high pipeline.

negative_highlights: Q3 guidance implies revenue decline to $135-145 million from $147.3 million, reflecting full impact of activity and pricing declines.
Coiled Tubing revenue fell 16% and Cementing revenue fell 9% due to Permian weakness.
Liquidity fell to $65.5 million, and additional $13.4 million was drawn on revolver in July.
positive_highlights: Completion Tools revenue grew 9% to $37.0 million, driven by Northeast/Haynesville and international sales.
Wireline revenue grew 11% to $33.0 million, with gains in remedial work and Northeast market share.
International Tools revenue up ~20% in Q2 2025 vs Q2 2024, boosted by MCBV valve and plug sales in Middle East.
summary: Nine Energy Service reported Q2 2025 revenue of $147.3 million, near the upper end of guidance ($138-148M), but adjusted EBITDA fell to $14.1 million amid significant activity and pricing declines, especially in the Permian. Completion Tools and Wireline grew revenue (9% and 11% respectively), while Cementing and Coiled Tubing declined (9% and 16%). Q3 guidance calls for revenue between $135-145 million, implying a sequential decline, reflecting full impact of Q2 headwinds. Management remains optimistic on natural gas and international growth but acknowledges ongoing macro pressures.

negative_highlights: Revenue essentially flat at $19.6 million vs $19.9 million
EV charging revenue fell to $2.7 million from $3.8 million, citing project timing
EV financing uncertainty and tariff concerns noted
positive_highlights: Gross margin reached 30.1%, highest in about six years
Third consecutive quarter of positive adjusted EBITDA
New $6.5 million Boston Public Schools EV charging expansion win
summary: Orion reported Q1 FY2026 revenue of $19.6 million, roughly flat year-over-year, with LED lighting up 1% and maintenance up 21%, offset by a decline in EV charging due to project timing. Gross margin expanded 850 basis points to 30.1%, and net loss narrowed to $1.2 million from $3.8 million, with adjusted EBITDA positive for the third consecutive quarter. CEO stated confidence in achieving FY2026 revenue of about $84 million and positive adjusted EBITDA. Guidance was reiterated, not raised.

negative_highlights: Net revenue was flat year-over-year at $22.1 million and Q3 revenue guidance of $21-22.1 million implies down 1% to up 4%, with GMV growth decelerating sequentially
Q3 adjusted EBITDA margin guidance of a 8-12% loss is wider than Q2's 8% loss
Average order value was flat at ~$2,600 as mix shifted to lower-value orders, and unique sellers fell 21% year-over-year to ~5,900
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA loss of $1.8 million exceeded the high end of guidance, with total operating expenses down 4% year-over-year to $21.6 million
Conversion increased year-over-year for a seventh consecutive quarter, with both new and returning conversion rising
Gross margin held flat at 72% on flat gross profit of $15.9 million, and active buyers rose 5% to ~64,400
summary: 1stdibs reported Q2 FY2025 net revenue of $22.1 million, flat year-over-year, with GMV above the midpoint of guidance and adjusted EBITDA loss of $1.8 million (an 8% margin) that management said exceeded the high end of guidance. Gross margin held at 72%, operating expenses fell 4% to $21.6 million, and conversion grew for a seventh consecutive quarter, though active buyers rose 5% to ~64,400 and listings grew 3% to ~1.9 million. Q3 guidance calls for GMV of $83-89 million (down 2% to up 5%), revenue of $21-22.1 million (down 1% to up 4%), and an adjusted EBITDA margin loss of 8-12%, with a wider loss than Q2's 8%. Key changes versus prior periods: GMV growth decelerated sequentially on softening traffic and moderating AOV, average order value was flat at ~$2,600 while median order value rose 10% on a mix shift toward lower-value orders, and unique sellers fell 21% year-over-year to ~5,900 but were flat sequentially with minimal GMV impact.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to $64 million in Q2, with cash burn nearly doubling sequentially to $57 million.
First flight of prototype now expected 'towards the end of the year' (previously 'next few months'), indicating a slip in timeline.
Engineering prototype does not include recent design changes (e.g., wing optimization), which will only be on conforming prototypes.
positive_highlights: First firm order converted from LOI: Revo contract for 50 aircraft plus TechCare services total potential value of $250 million, with PDPs to start.
Backlog grew to ~2,800 aircraft (~$14 billion) and TechCare contracts with 14 customers could bring up to $1.6 billion in revenue.
Liquidity of $375 million (including cash, standby facilities, and grant) considered sufficient to sustain operations through 2026.
summary: Eve Air Mobility reported Q2 2025 net loss of $64 million, with R&D investment of $55 million and SG&A of $8 million. Cash burn was $57 million in Q2, leading to $83 million consumed in H1, within the full-year guidance of $200-$250 million (likely at low end). The company secured its first firm order (Revo) for 50 aircraft plus services valued at $250 million, and added LOIs for 104 aircraft, bringing backlog to ~2,800 units (~$14 billion). Management reiterated certification and entry-into-service in 2027, with first flight expected end of 2025.

negative_highlights: Revenue fell 16% YoY to $824 million, with North America down 22% and core revenues down 13%.
Adjusted EBITDA margin contracted to 4.7% from 9.5% a year ago, driven by lower volumes and negative price/cost dynamics.
Net leverage increased to 5.7x, far above target, and free cash flow was negligible, with full-year FCF projected as a use of $150 million.
positive_highlights: Reinstated full-year guidance with adjusted EBITDA of $170-200 million, reflecting greater visibility despite a soft environment.
Transformation and cost actions are on track, with $100 million of in-year benefits expected, about half in the second half.
Tariff exposure is limited: ~13% of supplier spend subject to tariffs, direct China sourcing under 1%, and pricing actions aim to recover most costs.
summary: JELD-WEN reported Q2 2025 revenue of $824 million, down 16% YoY, with adjusted EBITDA of $39 million, down from $85 million a year ago, and an adjusted EBITDA margin of 4.7%. The company reinstated full-year guidance, expecting revenue of $3.2-3.4 billion, core revenue down 4-9%, and adjusted EBITDA of $170-200 million, with a midpoint of $185 million, down from prior year's $275 million. Management cited continued volume declines, negative price/cost dynamics, and productivity headwinds, while noting transformation benefits and cost actions are partially offsetting. Net leverage rose to 5.7x, and free cash flow was negligible in the quarter; the company is evaluating strategic options, including a potential sale of European operations, to reduce leverage.

negative_highlights: Lift Truck revenues declined 19% year-over-year, with volumes down across all product lines
Q2 bookings fell to $330 million from $590 million in Q1, driven by tariff-related demand deferrals
Q2 adjusted operating profit down to $5 million, with tariff-driven costs of $10 million
positive_highlights: Operating cash flow improved to ~$30 million in Q2, up from prior year and prior quarter
Unused borrowing capacity increased 3% to nearly $260 million
Bolzoni revenue grew sequentially with improved margins from mix shift
summary: In Q2 FY2025, Hyster-Yale reported Lift Truck revenues down 19% year-over-year, with adjusted operating profit falling sharply to $5 million, impacted by $10 million in tariff-driven costs. Bookings declined to $330 million from $590 million in Q1, and backlog fell from $1.9 billion to $1.7 billion. The company maintained its full-year guidance but emphasized heightened economic uncertainty, tariff volatility, and a cyclical demand trough, while planning to increase production in H2 to meet an expected demand uptick.

negative_highlights: GAAP operating loss widened to $12.4 million from $4.8 million a year ago, driven by a $5 million IP revenue decline and incremental IP amortization
IP licensing revenue fell to $0.3 million from $5.3 million in the prior-year quarter, reflecting episodic deal timing
Deflecto Manufacturing posted a $0.6 million GAAP operating loss; Class 8 truck orders at lowest since 2010 and consumer products customers pausing purchases due to tariff uncertainty
positive_highlights: Benchmark paid down an incremental $3.5 million of debt, bringing 12-month total debt reduction to $24 million
Energy operations generated $15.3 million in revenue versus $14.2 million a year ago, with adjusted EBITDA of $7 million
Printronix is performing ahead of plan following business mix shift to higher-margin consumables
summary: Acacia reported Q2 revenue of $51.2 million, adjusted EBITDA of $1.9 million, and free cash flow of $47.9 million, driven largely by cash collection on a prior IP settlement. The company posted a GAAP diluted EPS loss of $0.03 and an adjusted loss of $0.06, while book value per share was $5.99 ($5.58 excluding noncontrolling interests), essentially flat sequentially. IP revenue fell to $0.3 million from $5.3 million a year ago, and Deflecto's end markets remained pressured by tariff-related demand headwinds in Transportation Safety and Consumer Products. Management highlighted a new $20 million Bitcoin-backed commercial loan commitment with Unchained Capital and Build Asset Management, and noted Benchmark debt paydown of $3.5 million, bringing 12-month reductions to $24 million.

negative_highlights: GAAP net loss of $0.9 million ($0.03 per share) caused by hedge maturity and reduced NIM.
NAV declined approximately $6.2 million (or 2.7%) relative to March 31, ending the quarter at a lower book value.
positive_highlights: Earnings available for distribution (EAD) remained positive at $0.10 per share despite GAAP losses, supporting dividend sustainability.
Servicing costs came in lower than estimates due to deboarding fees from the prior quarter and a drop in loan count following the Mr. Cooper acquisition integration.
summary: Cherry Hill reported a GAAP net loss of $0.9 million ($0.03 per share) for Q2 FY2025, driven by the maturation of a large hedge and lower dollar roll income, resulting in an NAV decline of approximately 2.7%. Book value per common share decreased to $3.34 from $3.58 at quarter-end. Management maintained leverage around 5.3x while raising $9 million via ATM programs.

negative_highlights: Q2 revenue dropped sharply by $3.7M year-over-year primarily due to lower milestones and the discontinuation of a small-molecule ion channel program
Net loss increased from $13.6 million in Q2 FY2024 to $15.9 million in Q2 FY2025 despite operating expense reductions
xPloration revenue is currently minimal, described as 'pretty small numbers', with future recurring revenue estimates withheld
positive_highlights: xPloration Partner Access Program launched successfully with an instrument sold and installed at a global partner within weeks
Active programs increased to 381 in Q2, representing a year-to-date net increase of 18 programs which more than doubled H1 2024 additions
Average royalty rate on antibody programs improved to 3.36% from 3.2% reported in November 2023
summary: OmniAb reported Q2 FY2025 revenue of $3.9 million, a significant decrease from $7.6 million in the prior year period due to lower milestones and service revenue declines offset by new xPloration sales; net loss widened to $15.9 million compared to $13.6 million last year despite cost reductions including headcount cuts to 87 employees. Management reiterated full-year 2025 guidance for revenue between $20-25M and operating expenses of $85-90M, noting that xPloration contributions are currently small but additive.

negative_highlights: Virtual Sports EBITDA declined year-over-year due to sequential timing issues as new products launch later than hoped.
North American iGaming market remains limited with less than 10% population coverage compared to sports betting's 70%, constraining near-term scale.
positive_highlights: Interactive EBITDA surged nearly 50% year-over-year, driven by strong performance across U.K., North America, Greece, and emerging traction in Brazil.
Gaming segment adjusted EBITDA increased 35% YoY due to improved results at William Hill and new cabinet deployments in Canada (Alberta sale) and Illinois.
Company secured a major contract with Jenningsbet, the largest independent bookmaker chain in the U.K., for supply of gaming machines.
summary: Inspired Entertainment reported Q2 FY2025 EBITDA of $28.4 million (up 15% YoY) with overall margins expanding to 35%. The Interactive segment drove growth with adjusted EBITDA up nearly 50% YoY and margin expansion, while the Gaming segment grew 35% YoY led by William Hill improvements; Virtual Sports stabilized sequentially despite a soft year-over-year comparison. Management raised guidance for the second half of the year citing momentum in North America and Brazil.

negative_highlights: Total company revenues were down slightly due to a specific loss of approximately $2 million in card issuing revenue from one large account losing a downstream customer.
Revenue guidance was lowered for the full year to 5%-12% growth, citing delays at two large national accounts including a multi-location building material supplier.
Card issuing and Output Solutions revenues were impacted by specific headwinds: loss of an amusement park client in card issuing and soft ad hoc work/transition pricing in output.
positive_highlights: Gross margins widened significantly, expanding 185 basis points to 25.8%.
ACH revenues grew over 30% for the second consecutive quarter with total payment dollars up 19%. Card processing volume increased 69% in transactions and PayFac revenue rose 17%.
Adjusted EBITDA remained positive at just over $500,000 despite lower top-line revenues.
summary: Total revenues declined slightly due to weakness in card issuing and decreased interest income, though gross margins expanded 185 bps to 25.8% driven by strong ACH growth (up over 30%). Management adjusted full-year revenue guidance down to a range of 5%-12% growth citing prolonged implementation delays at two large national accounts.

negative_highlights: Policy acquisition costs increased $10.3 million (74.8% year-over-year)
General and administrative expenses decreased due to one-time nonrecurring tax credit refunds of $2.9 million
Risk appetite for adding new exposures is limited during the third quarter
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 26% year-over-year
Pretax earnings increased 51% year-over-year
Combined ratio of 60.6%, significantly below the stated target of 65%
summary: American Coastal Insurance Corporation reported Q2 FY2025 results with revenue growing 26% year-over-year and pretax earnings increasing 51%. Net income was $26.4 million while core return on equity reached approximately 42%, driven by a step-down in quota share ceding that increased net premiums earned despite higher acquisition costs. The company achieved a combined ratio of 60.6% against its target and received an upgrade to BBB- with a Positive outlook from Kroll Bond Rating Agency.

negative_highlights: Adjusted net income fell significantly from $4.4 million in the prior year quarter, with preopening costs adding $2.1 million.
Cost of goods sold increased by 97 basis points YoY due to inflation and new restaurant mix.
Customer traffic dropped sharply in April through June following global tariff announcements.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 2.2% YoY driven by new store openings totaling 9 units year-to-date.
Same-store sales showed improvement and stabilization beginning in the last half of July after an earlier decline.
Payroll costs decreased as a percentage of sales (down 163 bps QoQ) due to rolled-out labor efficiencies.
summary: GENK reported Q2 FY2025 revenue of $55 million (a 2.2% YoY increase) and an adjusted net loss before taxes of $1.8 million ($0.05 diluted EPS), down from a profit in the prior year period due to new store preopening costs and macro headwinds including tariffs and immigration policy impacts on traffic. Management maintained its full-year 4-wall margin guidance range of 17% to 18%, citing operational efficiencies like AI tools and automation expected to improve results starting in Q3, despite a sharp downturn in April through June that recovered slightly in July.

negative_highlights: Operating cash flow was weak for the quarter due to over $10 million in delayed collections from two school clients, though 80% collected
Engineering gross margins contracted sequentially and YoY (24.5%) as they remain volatile depending on project mix
positive_highlights: Consolidated gross profit grew 11.4% YoY to $22.3 million, yielding the highest in 13 quarters
Health Care Services revenue increased 21.1% YoY driven by new K-12 contracts and market share gains from competitors
Aerospace group exceeded business plan goals with a sequential gross margin increase of 8%
summary: RCM Technologies reported Q2 FY2025 consolidated gross profit of $22.3 million (up 11.4% YoY) and Adjusted EPS of $0.69 (up 21.1% YoY). The company highlighted strong growth in Health Care Services (+15.4%) and Engineering (+8.8%), with Aerospace exceeding business plan goals by nearly $3 million. Management noted a temporary cash collection delay from two school clients but expects full payment soon, while forecasting low double-digit Adjusted EBITDA growth for the second half of FY2025.

negative_highlights: Total revenue declined 18% YoY due to lower license and PA revenues as customers consolidated programs or shut down operations.
Management lowered full-year core revenue guidance by approximately $5.0 million relative to the prior plan of $35M-$37M.
Gross margin contracted from 86% in Q2 FY24 to 82% in Q2 FY25.
positive_highlights: Instrument revenue grew 22% year-over-year to $2.1 million, indicating recovery in capex spending for lower-priced systems.
Signed two new strategic platform licenses with Anocca AB and Adicet Bio, bringing total SPL agreements to 31 this year.
SeQure Dx integration is on track to meet annual revenue expectations of approximately $2 million.
summary: MaxCyte reported Q2 FY2025 total revenue of $8.5 million (down 18% YoY) and core revenue growth of 8%, driven by a 22% increase in instrument sales but offset by declines in license and PA revenues due to customer program consolidation. Management lowered its full-year 2025 guidance for core business revenue from an expected 8-15% growth range ($35M-$37M) to flat-to-down 10% ($29.5M-$32.5M), citing headwinds including a large customer's manufacturing reorganization and capital equipment purchasing hesitancy.

negative_highlights: Core FFO fell to $0.20 per share from $0.25 and revenue declined to $37.3 million from $40.1 million year over year
Net debt to annualized adjusted EBITDA was 6.93x, and management expects the ratio to rise modestly in the coming year
$110 million credit facility revolver matures May 2026 with no remaining extension options and refinancing still in discussions
positive_highlights: Core FFO guidance raised and narrowed to $0.67-$0.71 per share from $0.61-$0.70
Operating property occupancy rose 310 bps sequentially to 77.4% and lease rate 170 bps to 79.1%
639,000 square feet leased through July 31 with weighted average lease term of 6.4 years, plus $57 million of dispositions under agreement at $106 per square foot
summary: Orion reported Q2 2025 revenue of $37.3 million, down from $40.1 million a year earlier, with core FFO of $11.5 million or $0.20 per share versus $14.2 million or $0.25 per share in Q2 2024, reflecting vacancies, a smaller portfolio and lease timing. Core FFO guidance for 2025 was narrowed and raised to $0.67-$0.71 from $0.61-$0.70, and net debt to adjusted EBITDA guidance was lowered to 7.3x-8.3x from 8.0x-8.8x, partly on one-time items like lease termination income and property tax refunds; G&A guidance of $19.5-$20.5 million was reaffirmed. Occupancy rose 310 bps sequentially to 77.4% with 639,000 square feet leased through July 31, and the company has $57 million of office dispositions under agreement and closed $26.9 million of vacant-property sales in the quarter. Leverage remains elevated at 6.93x net debt to annualized adjusted EBITDA, and the $110 million revolver maturing May 2026 with no remaining extension options is still subject to lender discussions.

negative_highlights: Gross originations declined to $48 million from $166 million quarter-over-quarter
Net investment income fell to $0.46 per share from $0.53 due to fee changes
Net asset value declined from $17.96 to $17.92 per share on valuation losses
positive_highlights: Net investment income of $0.46 per share exceeded the quarterly distribution of $0.45
Nonaccruals improved to 0.2% of fair value, down from 0.4%
Pipeline increasing with deal reviews up over 60% from April to June
summary: NCDL reported Q2 2025 net investment income of $0.46 per share, covering its $0.45 dividend, but down from $0.53 in Q1 due to the expiration of an incentive fee waiver and intentional leverage reduction. Gross originations fell to $48 million from $166 million, reflecting a deliberate slowdown, with portfolio fair value down slightly to $2 billion. Credit quality improved with nonaccruals dropping to 0.2% of fair value, and NAV dipped to $17.92 per share. Management sees positive momentum in the second half with a stronger pipeline and completed rotation to core middle market assets.

negative_highlights: Book value per share decreased to negative $43.14 from negative $40.99.
Corporate unencumbered cash fell to $355 million from $380 million at year-end.
PREPA resolution timing remains uncertain; Oversight Board changes add unpredictability.
positive_highlights: GAAP net loss narrowed to $56 million from $254 million year-over-year.
Transferred $374 million of PREPA claims to custodian to improve marketability.
National statutory capital rose to $914 million from $912 million at year-end.
summary: MBIA reported a narrower GAAP net loss of $56 million in Q2 2025 versus $254 million a year ago, primarily due to lower losses on PREPA exposure. Adjusted net loss was $8 million, improved from $138 million last year. Book value per share declined to negative $43.14 from negative $40.99. Management emphasized persistent PREPA uncertainty and noted a newly transferred $374 million of PREPA claims to a custodian to enhance marketability, while still considering the sale process. Guidance is not applicable, but tone is cautious and forward-looking about PREPA resolution.

negative_highlights: New patient starts declined by approximately 3% quarter-over-quarter and 1% year-over-year.
Total prescriptions decreased slightly, down 2% year-over-year despite a modest sequential increase.
Royalty revenue from international partners is expected to be lower in FY2025 due to fewer shipments to China as the partner works through regulatory transitions.
positive_highlights: Net product revenue increased sequentially by $6.1M to $49.2M driven by higher bottle sales and note price increases.
Full-year net NERLYNX revenue guidance raised to a range of $192 million to $198 million, exceeding prior expectations.
Cash burn improved significantly from approximately $7.8 million in Q1 2025 to about $2.9 million in Q2 2025.
summary: Puma Biotechnology reported Q2 FY2025 net product revenue of $49.2 million (up from $43.1M in Q1) and GAAP EPS of $0.12 per share, driven by a sequential increase in NERLYNX bottle sales to 2,608 units despite new prescription declines of approximately 3% quarter-over-quarter. Management provided full-year net revenue guidance of $192-198 million (raised from prior expectations) and Q3 net income guidance of $2-4 million, while noting that demand growth is currently stronger in the specialty distributor channel than the specialty pharmacy channel.

negative_highlights: Adjusted operating income was only $0.4 million and adjusted EBITDA was $4.6 million or 2% of sales, dragged by $3.4 million of nonoperating FX and $0.5 million of incremental tariff costs
EBITDA guidance was lowered to reflect year-to-date nonoperating FX and ~$1 million of full-year incremental tariff costs, even as revenue guidance was maintained

Electronics adjusted operating margin fell ~190 bps QoQ on unfavorable mix after a record SMART2 quarter, and North American commercial vehicle production is now forecast to decline ~17.5% this year versus a prior expectation of a slight decline
positive_highlights: MirrorEye set a record quarterly sales mark, up 21% QoQ, with two additional North American OEM launches (Daimler Truck, Volvo Trucks) and availability confirmed across every North American OEM

New awards totaled ~$775 million in lifetime revenue, including the ~$535 million MirrorEye extension through 2033 with ~$140 million peak annual revenue, the largest award in company history, plus an ~$85 million Brazil infotainment ECU award

Inventory fell $7.3 million QoQ (over $34 million in 12 months), free cash flow of $7.6 million improved $5.9 million YoY, and total debt was reduced $38.8 million via a $43.8 million cash repatriation
summary: Q2 sales were $228 million with adjusted operating income of only $0.4 million and adjusted EBITDA of $4.6 million (2% of sales), pressured by $3.4 million of nonoperating FX and $0.5 million of incremental tariff costs. Full-year revenue guidance was maintained at $860-890 million, but EBITDA guidance was cut to absorb year-to-date nonoperating FX, while North American commercial vehicle production is now expected to decline ~17.5% versus the prior forecast of a slight decline. MirrorEye set a record sales quarter (+21% QoQ) and the company booked ~$775 million in lifetime awards, including a ~$535 million MirrorEye extension through 2033, the largest in company history. Management also announced a review of strategic alternatives for the Control Devices division focused on a potential sale.

negative_highlights: Gross margin declined 150 bps YoY to 63.5%, with 90 bps from tariffs and 90 bps from a prior-year favorable inventory revaluation.
Management expects a Q3 U.S. distributor inventory reduction that will create a domestic revenue dip before a Q4 rebound.
Full-year gross margin guidance of 61-63% implies second-half margin pressure from lower-ASP international mix and ongoing tariffs.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 21% YoY to a record $10.2 million, with all three growth pillars contributing.
International revenue rose 34% YoY to $2.2 million, with management noting European market share improving to the low 20s from 10-15%.
FY2025 revenue guidance raised to $39.5-$40.5 million from $38.5-$39.5 million, representing 18-20% growth.
summary: KORU reported record Q2 FY2025 revenue of $10.2 million, up 21% YoY, with domestic core up 15%, international up 34%, and Pharma Services up 42%. Gross margin was 63.5%, down 150 bps YoY on tariff impacts and prior-year inventory adjustments. The company raised FY2025 revenue guidance to $39.5-$40.5 million (18-20% growth) from $38.5-$39.5 million, while reiterating 61-63% gross margin and positive operating cash flow for the full year. Q2 cash usage was $600,000, and adjusted EBITDA turned slightly positive versus a prior-year loss.

negative_highlights: Services revenue of $5.4M remained soft, with continued weakness in the managed review business
Operating cash flow for the first half was negative $14.7M, worse than negative $8.0M in the prior-year period
Q3 adjusted EBITDA guidance of negative $5M to negative $3M implies a wider loss than the -$2.7M reported in Q2
positive_highlights: Software revenue of $32.7M grew 12% YoY and exceeded the high end of guidance by roughly $900K
Adjusted EBITDA of negative $2.7M (-7% margin) beat the high end of guidance and improved $2M YoY from -13% margin
Customers spending over $100K reached 323, up 6% YoY, and multi-terabyte Cecilia matters grew 150% in the first half versus year-end 2024
summary: Q2 FY2025 total revenue was $38.1M, up 6% YoY, with software revenue of $32.7M, up 12% YoY and above the high end of guidance; adjusted EBITDA was negative $2.7M (-7% margin), a $2M YoY improvement and a beat of the high end of the range. Full-year FY2025 guidance was raised at the midpoint by $1M for total revenue (to $148-158M), $2.5M for software revenue (to $128-134M), and $1.5M for adjusted EBITDA (to negative $17-13M). Services revenue of $5.4M remained soft in managed review, and operating cash flow for the first half was negative $14.7M versus negative $8.0M a year prior. Management also disclosed that CFO Michael Lafair will step down at year-end, with a search underway.

negative_highlights: M&T revenue declined 14% YoY, the sharpest decline ever
10% workforce reduction announced, with cost savings only starting in Q3
Q3 adjusted EBITDA guided down sequentially due to one-time benefits in Q2
positive_highlights: Subscription and total revenue both above the high end of guidance
Record non-GAAP net profit of $2.5 million and eighth consecutive quarter of adjusted EBITDA profitability
First three AI deals closed, with 100+ qualified AI pipeline opportunities
summary: Kaltura reported Q2 2025 total revenue of $44.5 million, up 1% YoY, and subscription revenue of $42.4 million, up 3% YoY, both above the high end of guidance. Adjusted EBITDA was $4.1 million, record non-GAAP net profit of $2.5 million, and cash flow from operations of $2.7 million, with gross margin up to 70% from 66% YoY. EE&T revenue grew 7% YoY, its highest since Q1 2022, while M&T revenue declined 14% YoY, its sharpest ever. The company announced a restructuring that will cut ~10% of workforce, with expected savings of $2.6 million in 2025 and $8.5 million annualized, but reaffirmed full-year guidance and expects strong Q4 with M&T sequential growth.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA margin down 74 basis points year-over-year
Forward guidance reflects conservative H2 outlook amid economic uncertainty
Safety and Racing division growth tempered by Snell cycle regulatory transition
positive_highlights: Core business revenue grew 3.9% year-over-year, with all divisions positive
Record quarterly free cash flow of $35.7 million, up $11.3 million year-over-year
Tariff mitigation plan working; no meaningful impact to cash flow or margins expected
summary: Holley reported Q2 2025 core revenue growth of 3.9% to $166.7 million, with record quarterly free cash flow of $35.7 million. Gross margin expanded 26 basis points to 41.7%, while adjusted EBITDA margin declined 74 basis points to 21.9%. Management reaffirmed fiscal 2025 guidance, taking a conservative stance on H2 due to macroeconomic uncertainty, though tariff mitigation is on track.

negative_highlights: Net loss of $23.4 million and interest expense of $12.3 million, leaving cash at only $1.6 million
No 45Z or LCFS credit revenue recognized in the quarter; 45Z monetization awaits a DOE GREET model update, and management deferred the EBITDA-impact figure to a later memo
Only 7 of 18 dairy digesters have approved pathways; the 4 pending are projected to contribute no earlier than Q4 2025 and more likely Q1 2026
positive_highlights: Revenue rose $9.3 million sequentially to $52.2 million on resumption of India biodiesel deliveries ($11.9 million shipped)
CARB approved 7 dairy pathways at a blended negative 384 CI score, unlocking ~120% more LCFS credit revenue versus the negative 150 default pathway
California LCFS credit prices rose from about $42 to about $60 following July 1 CARB amendments, with the 2025 cap at $268
summary: Revenue was $52.2 million, up $9.3 million sequentially, driven by $11.9 million of India biodiesel deliveries resuming after a six-month OMC pause. The company still posted a $23.4 million net loss, $12.3 million of quarterly interest expense, and ended with just $1.6 million in cash despite a $4.9 million sequential improvement in operating loss.
