Management highlighted record profitability excluding one-time gains from a produce asset privatization transaction that generated $40 million in cash proceeds.

negative_highlights: Net revenue fell 22% YoY to $10.8 million on a 24% decline in average prices
Adjusted EBITDA fell 23% to $7.7 million and basic EPS dropped to $0.08 from $0.11
Netback from operations fell to $29.66/BOE from $40.40, a 27% contraction
positive_highlights: Production rose 3% YoY to 3,220 BOE/d even with ~540 BOE/d shut in for Lovina completions
Borrowing base increased 30% to $65 million, extending credit flexibility
Lovina wells brought on with a higher-than-expected oil percentage and low gas-oil ratio, and ~130,000 shares repurchased in July
summary: Q2 2025 average production rose 3% YoY to 3,220 BOE/d despite ~540 BOE/d of wells temporarily shut in for Lovina completions, but net revenue fell 22% to $10.8 million on a 24% drop in average prices. Adjusted EBITDA fell 23% to $7.7 million and basic EPS declined to $0.08 from $0.11; netback dropped to $29.66/BOE from $40.40. Management kept full-year production guidance unchanged ('not so far' rethinking it) and reiterated plans to bring 9 new wells online in H2 2025, expecting significant production and cash flow increases; the borrowing base was raised 30% to $65 million and ~130,000 shares were bought back in July.

negative_highlights: Non-GAAP EPS fell to $0.77 from $1.35, and adjusted EBITDA dropped to $15.3 million from $20.1 million
Nightclub same-store sales fell 3.7% and Bombshells same-store sales fell 13.5%, with Bombshells non-GAAP operating margin collapsing to 1.2% from 10.8%
Self-insurance actuarial reserves of $9.4 million year-to-date are unpredictable and hitting both GAAP and adjusted EBITDA, with management unable to estimate a run-rate
positive_highlights: GAAP EPS swung to $0.46 from a $0.56 loss as impairments and other charges fell to $2.3 million from $18.3 million
Free cash flow held about level at $13.3 million and rose sequentially to a 19% of revenue margin from 11% in Q2
Nightclub segment GAAP operating margin expanded to 28.5% from 21.7%, and management noted non-GAAP margin rose sequentially for a second straight quarter
summary: RCI reported Q3 FY2025 revenue of $71.1 million, down from $76.2 million, driven by divestitures of 5 underperforming Bombshells and a 3.7% same-store sales decline in Nightclubs. Non-GAAP EPS fell to $0.77 from $1.35 and adjusted EBITDA fell to $15.3 million from $20.1 million, though GAAP EPS swung to $0.46 from a $0.56 loss on the absence of last year's $18.3 million impairment. Free cash flow was roughly level at $13.3 million and rose sequentially to a 19% margin; management gave no formal guidance, discussing ongoing work to stand up a captive insurance program amid an unpredictable $10-12 million annual self-insurance reserve run-rate.

negative_highlights: Multiplatform Group revenue declined 5.4% YoY and adjusted EBITDA fell 7.6%, missing the prior year's higher base.
Q3 guidance explicitly acknowledges macro volatility, widening the EBITDA range to $180M-$220M compared to a more precise prior expectation of ~$205M.
Free cash flow turned negative at -$13 million in Q2 due to timing differences and higher benefits expenses.
positive_highlights: Digital Audio Group adjusted EBITDA margins expanded 100 bps YoY to 33.2% driven by podcasting revenue growth of 28.5%.
Top 50 total company advertisers grew 9% YoY and top agency groups grew 14%, indicating demand resilience despite macro headwinds.
Company is on track to achieve $150 million in net cost savings for FY2025, with Q2 contributing $40 million.
summary: iHeartMedia reported Q2 FY2025 consolidated revenue of $869 million (sum of segments), up 0.5% YoY and slightly above guidance for low single-digit decline; adjusted EBITDA was $156 million, beating the upper end of its $140M-$160M range by 4%. While Digital Audio Group revenue surged 13.4%, Multiplatform Group revenue declined 5.4% YoY (down 4.8% excluding political), and Q3 guidance was widened to reflect macro uncertainty with expected EBITDA of $180M-$220M.

negative_highlights: GAAP gross margin was 33.2%, down year-over-year due to revenue mix.
Secure Networks revenue contracted, partially offsetting Security Solutions growth.
positive_highlights: Revenue of $36 million grew 26% YoY and exceeded the top end of guidance ($34.5 million).
Adjusted EBITDA of ~$400,000 beat the guidance range of a $0.6–$2.1 million loss.
Free cash flow improved by $16 million YoY to $4.6 million, enabling $4 million of share repurchases.
summary: Telos reported Q2 FY2025 revenue of $36 million, up 26% year-over-year and above the guidance range of $32.5–$34.5 million, with Security Solutions growing 82% and contributing ~90% of revenue. Adjusted EBITDA of ~$400,000 beat the guided loss of $600k–$2.1 million, and free cash flow was $4.6 million vs. a $16 million year-over-year improvement. Q3 guidance implies revenue growth of 85–98% to $44–47 million and adjusted EBITDA of $4–5.7 million, a large sequential step-up; the company repurchased $4 million of shares in the quarter.

negative_highlights: Operating income guidance of $86-$91 million reaffirmed, not raised, alongside the higher sales range
Net tariff cost impact of $1.4 million in the quarter, with a somewhat larger impact expected in the September quarter
Interest expense of $12.8 million and a $2.4 million tax expense with an elevated effective rate due to losses at certain jurisdictions
positive_highlights: Net sales up 10.9% to a Q1 record $188.4 million; gross profit up 16.3% to a record $33.9 million
Full-year sales guidance raised to $800-$820 million, implying 5.6%-8.3% YoY growth
Operating cash flow of $10 million versus a $20.8 million use of cash a year ago; net bank debt cut $7 million to $74.4 million
summary: Net sales rose 10.9% to a first-quarter record $188.4 million and gross profit rose 16.3% to a record $33.9 million, lifting gross margin to 18.0% from 17.2%. Operating income swung to $20.1 million from a $6.5 million loss, and net income was $3.0 million or $0.15 per diluted share versus a $0.92 loss a year ago. Full-year sales guidance was raised to $800-$820 million (5.6%-8.3% growth) from the June range, incorporating tariff pass-throughs, while operating income guidance of $86-$91 million was reaffirmed. Tariff net cost impact fell to $1.4 million from $4.6 million in the March quarter, and net bank debt dropped $7 million to $74.4 million with $10 million of operating cash flow.

negative_highlights: Revenue growth decelerated to 3.3% versus an internal expectation of ~4% due to temporary diabetes supply disruptions requiring modified delivery frequencies.
Diabetes revenue remains below prior year levels and is expected to remain so in the back half despite a planned rebound, driven by structural shifts from DME to pharmacy.
Full-year 2025 adjusted EBITDA guidance was significantly reduced due to discontinued operations classification of P&HS and anticipated stranded costs.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to 14.2% driven by volume growth, improved collection rates, and lower benefit costs.
Sleep category supplies led overall growth with strong performance from Sleep Journey investments.
Ostomy and urology categories showed very strong double-digit percentage-wise growth.
summary: Revenue for continuing operations (Patient Direct) was $682 million in Q2 FY2025, representing a 3.3% increase versus the prior year but missing internal expectations of approximately 4% due to temporary modifications to customer ordering quantities and delivery frequency for diabetes supplies during supplier disruptions. Adjusted EBITDA grew to $96.6 million (14.2% margin) driven by volume growth, improved collections, and lower benefit costs, though this was partially offset by $11 million in stranded costs from the divestiture of Products & Healthcare Services. Management lowered full-year 2025 guidance for adjusted EBITDA to a range of $376-$382 million (down significantly from prior expectations) due to discontinued operations and anticipated increases in stranded costs if the P&HS sale is announced soon.

negative_highlights: Year-over-year net loss widened slightly to $4.8M (vs $5.9M last year) despite expense cuts
Adjusted EBITDA declined quarter-over-quarter from negative $1.1M to negative $1.3M due to lower sales volume
Management explicitly withheld full-year 2025 guidance citing global trade policy and cannabis reform uncertainties
positive_highlights: Net revenue of $41M beat the specific quarterly guidance of $40M
Gross margin expanded sequentially to 28.3% from 26.9%
Proprietary brand sales increased significantly, reaching nearly 32% of total revenue
summary: GrowGeneration reported Q2 FY2025 net revenue of $41 million, beating its guidance of $40 million but missing the prior year's level due to a smaller retail footprint and soft B2C demand. Gross margins expanded sequentially to 28.3% driven by higher proprietary brand sales (up to ~32%), while operating expenses decreased significantly via store closures and cost discipline. Management raised Q3 revenue guidance slightly above $41 million but declined to provide full-year guidance citing tariff uncertainty, regulatory risks regarding cannabis rescheduling, and potential consumer demand variability.

negative_highlights: Q3 guidance includes a 4-point political headwind
Three major advertisers have not resumed spending; Q3 guide excludes them
Contribution ex-TAC growth (16%) lagged revenue growth (18%), partly due to deliberate pass-through of AI savings
positive_highlights: Revenue increased 18% year-over-year
Adjusted EBITDA up 18% to $11.3 million, surpassing guidance midpoint
AI Bidding contribution ex-TAC doubled year-over-year
summary: Viant reported Q2 2025 revenue up 18% YoY and contribution ex-TAC up 16% YoY, with adjusted EBITDA up 18% to $11.3 million, surpassing the midpoint of guidance. CTV drove growth, with Household ID spend up 15% YoY, and AI Bidding now automates 85% of ad spend. Q3 guidance implies a slowdown due to a 4-point political headwind and excludes any resumption of delayed advertiser spending, while a $250 million gross spend pipeline is expected to contribute to 2026 budgets.

negative_highlights: GAAP net loss of $30 million for Q2
Operating expenses up to $83 million from $64 million due to onetime fees
International real estate business was a drag, running about $2 million negative adjusted EBITDA per quarter
positive_highlights: Consolidated revenue up 7% YoY; core segment revenue up 8% and 99% recurring
Core segment like-for-like EBITDA margin improved from 20% to 26%
New client wins and expanded mandates totaling over $900 million projected billable assets in H1
summary: AlTi reported Q2 2025 consolidated revenue of $53 million, up 7% year-over-year, with core Wealth Management and Capital Solutions revenue up 8% to $52 million. Adjusted EBITDA was $4 million consolidated and $14 million in the core segment, with like-for-like core EBITDA margin improving from 20% to 26% excluding a Q1 incentive fee. Management highlighted timing mismatches, including onetime ZBB fees of $7 million and only partial Kontora contribution, with $20 million in annual savings expected from ZBB starting in the second half. The company completed the Kontora acquisition and exited international real estate, aiming to simplify and improve margins.

negative_highlights: No specific financial beat or guidance raise reported; cash burn remains high with $340M expected at year-end.
Management explicitly stated they are still in the process of converting estimates into firm numbers for SN1, requiring another 60-90 days to finalize costs.
Large industrial gas turbines remain sold out through 2030/2031, creating potential supply constraints for the integrated product strategy.
positive_highlights: Project Permian SN1 LCOE meaningfully improved from over $150/MWh to under $100/MWh driven by value engineering and tax incentives (OBBA/45Q parity).
NET Power completed key infrastructure repairs at LaPorte, accelerated testing cadence with Baker Hughes, and validated operational models for Phase 1.
Integrated configuration allows immediate deployment of reliable gas turbine power to meet near-term data center needs while establishing a credible pathway to decarbonization.
summary: NET Power reported Q2 FY2025 results with no specific revenue or EPS figures disclosed in the transcript; management highlighted significant progress on Project Permian SN1 value engineering and a revised LCOE trajectory below $100/MWh via an integrated gas turbine configuration. The company maintains approximately $340 million in cash, guiding to end-of-year levels consistent with prior expectations while pausing long-lead procurement for the core cycle pending offtake commitments.

negative_highlights: Production slower than Q1 due to deliberate activity reduction and completion timing
Second quarter CapEx down 30% sequentially due to dropping a rig in May
Uncertainty around adding second rig in September; retains flexibility to delay
positive_highlights: Generated over $155 million of EBITDAX in Q2 with margins of $33.58 per BOE
Refinanced term loan and RBL, extending maturities to September 2028 and boosting liquidity
Simul-frac on first pad saved ~$400,000 per well, ~10% completion cost reduction
summary: HighPeak Energy reported a solid Q2 2025 with EBITDAX over $155 million and strong margins of $33.58 per BOE, despite lower commodity prices. Production was slightly below Q1 due to planned activity reductions and completion timing, but management reaffirmed full-year 2025 production guidance. The company reduced CapEx by 30% sequentially, dropped to one rig in mid-May, and plans to add a second rig in September, though it retains flexibility to delay. They completed a debt refinancing extending maturities to 2028 and added hedges covering over 50% of H2 volumes at a weighted average floor above $62.

negative_highlights: AUM was flat at BRL 304 billion as BRL appreciation drove roughly BRL 12 billion of negative FX, offsetting BRL 8 billion of appreciation and BRL 3.5 billion of capital formation
FRE margin declined in the quarter; management now targets the low 30s only by Q2/Q3 2026
The earlier double-digit FX-adjusted AUM growth target for 2025 is now uncertain after a weak Q1, per Bruno's remarks
positive_highlights: Adjusted distributable earnings rose 30% YoY to BRL 76 million, with EPS up 9% to BRL 1.20
Fee-related revenue grew 85% YoY to BRL 233 million; FRE ex-catch-up grew 25% YoY
Credit segment post over BRL 2 billion of capital formation and appreciation, reaching over 10% of total AUM; IDE closed near BRL 2 billion
summary: Vinci Compass reported Q2 2025 FRE of BRL 65.2 million (BRL 1.03/share) and adjusted distributable earnings of BRL 75.8 million (BRL 1.20/share), up 30% YoY nominally but only 9% per share. FRE grew 25% YoY ex-catch-up and fee-related revenue rose 85% YoY to BRL 233 million, but AUM was flat at BRL 304 billion as a 5% BRL appreciation drove roughly BRL 12 billion of negative FX, and the FRE margin declined. Management guided to FRE margin expansion to the low 30s by Q2/Q3 2026 and flagged a gradual decline in financial income; the earlier double-digit FX-adjusted AUM growth target for 2025 is now doubtful after a weak Q1.

negative_highlights: Gross margin fell to 53% from 67% due to revenue mix
Marketplace revenue soft at $0.3 million due to halted marketing spend
Credit business revenue declined year-over-year
positive_highlights: Revenue up 18% YoY, with fintech up 28% excluding one-time vendor true-up
First-half net loss improved 46% to $12.8 million
Realized $9M of $11M annualized cost savings in H1
summary: Q2 FY2025 net revenue was $7.1 million, up 18% YoY, with Fintech revenue at $3.4 million (up 15.6%, but would have been $3.8 million or 28% without a $0.4 million vendor true-up), Brands/EveryLife at $3.3 million (up 45.5%), and Marketplace soft at $0.3 million. Gross margin declined to 53% from 67% due to mix. GAAP operating loss improved to $8.1 million from $14 million, and net loss per share improved to -$0.18 from -$0.36. Management announced plans to monetize EveryLife and Marketplace to focus entirely on fintech, expecting completion by Q4 2025. First-half OpEx declined 13% and net loss improved 46%, with $9 million of the expected $11 million annualized savings realized in H1.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA came in slightly below expectations primarily due to initial underperformance of some wells and lower realized commodity prices.
Customers have continued to hold deferred development timing despite crude price rebounds, pushing year-end outlook toward the low end of guidance.
positive_highlights: Executed a new 10-year extension of certain gathering agreements with a key customer in the Williston, increasing weighted average contract life from 4 to 8 years.
summary: Summit Midstream reported Q2 FY2025 adjusted EBITDA of $61 million and capital expenditures of $26.4 million. Management expects to end the year at the low end of its original guidance range due to lower realized commodity prices, timing delays in well completions, and deferred development by customers despite price rebounds. The company highlighted a new 10-year gathering agreement extension increasing weighted average contract life from 4 to 8 years and signed a precedent agreement for 100 million cubic feet per day of firm capacity on Double E.

negative_highlights: Hardware revenue declined 20% year over year, or $2.7 million
Licensing/royalty revenue of roughly $5 million is expected to shrink; management said it is 'not as confident' about Q4 strength after possibly one more good quarter
Gross margin guided down 4-5 points in Q3 and Q4 as royalty revenue declines, with cost-cutting/vertical integration adding back only 1-2 points
positive_highlights: Full-year 2025 revenue guidance raised to $131-$135 million (11-15% growth) from $127-$131 million (8-11% growth)
Gross margin expanded to 68.6% from 62.1% year over year on favorable mix and scale; GAAP net income turned positive at $3.5 million from a $3.9 million loss
Agreement to note noncore Coflex/OUS assets to Companion Spine for approximately $19.2 million, with proceeds split 50-50 between debt paydown and working capital
summary: Xtant reported Q2 2025 revenue of $35.4 million, up 18.0% year over year, driven by biologics growth of over 20% and approximately $5 million in licensing/royalty revenue; hardware revenue fell 20% ($2.7 million decline). GAAP net income was $3.5 million ($0.02 diluted) versus a $3.9 million net loss a year ago, and adjusted EBITDA was $6.9 million versus a $0.6 million loss. Gross margin expanded to 68.6% from 62.1%. The company raised full-year 2025 revenue guidance to $131-$135 million (11-15% growth) from $127-$131 million (8-11%), but management guided Q3/Q4 gross margins down 4-5 points and flagged that licensing revenue strength is expected to moderate after another good quarter, with roughly $5 million of royalties anticipated in H2.

negative_highlights: Retail segment revenue declined 20% year-over-year and down 2% quarter-over-quarter due to consumer confidence issues.
A large social media client is currently unable to process nearly all documents due to a code change on their end, delaying volume ramp-up.
Operating expenses increased $455,000 (10%) year-over-year as the company reduced capitalized R&D spend from Q2 2024 levels.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 10% YoY to $5.1 million, driven by strong pricing power (up 36%) and expansion of multi-year contracts with major bank clients.
Banking vertical revenue increased significantly year-over-year (+85%), offsetting declines in other sectors.
Successfully migrated approximately 95% of IT infrastructure to AWS, expecting annual savings exceeding $300,000.
summary: Intellicheck reported Q2 FY2025 revenue of $5.1 million, representing a 10% year-over-year increase and beating the prior period's $4.7 million. Adjusted EBITDA improved by $145,000 to $75,000 for the quarter compared to the same period last year. Management highlighted significant wins with major bank clients but noted a 20% decline in retail revenue and ongoing technical integration issues with a large social media client.

negative_highlights: Total net revenue fell 11.1% YoY on a same-station basis, driven by a 24.7% decline in local agency revenue and 12.1% decline in national agency revenue.
Q3 revenue pacing down high single digits (excluding political) with continued agency weakness (national -20%, local -15% pacing).
Agency business now ~45% of revenue, and management attributes structural declines to AI-driven planning systems deprioritizing traditional radio—a sustained headwind.
positive_highlights: Digital revenue grew 8.1% on a same-station basis and now represents 25% of total revenue; digital segment operating margin expanded 900 bps QoQ to 26.8%.
Executed ~$30 million in annualized cost reductions over the past 12 months, with $10 million incremental in H1 2025.
Announced $26 million in asset sales (Tampa and Fort Myers clusters) to reduce debt, plus $1.5 million stub note repurchase in Q2.
summary: Q2 net revenue declined 11.1% YoY on a same-station basis, with digital revenue up 8.1% same-station (now 25% of total revenue) but agency revenue down sharply (national -12.1%, local -24.7%). Adjusted EBITDA was $4.7 million, and station operating income margin was 15.6%. Management cut ~$10 million in annualized costs in H1, bringing total reductions to ~$30 million over 12 months, and announced $26 million in asset sales to reduce debt. Q3 revenue is pacing down high single digits (excluding political), with agency softness continuing (national -20%, local -15%) while local direct (+3%) and digital (+18%) grow.

negative_highlights: Reported revenue declined 3% to $428.2 million due to divestiture, FX, and interest impacts
GAAP net loss of $50 million driven by a non-cash $31 million valuation allowance on UK deferred tax assets
Revenue attrition remained elevated at 12%, slightly above the company's target
positive_highlights: Organic revenue growth of 5%, exceeding expectations for the reported quarter
Adjusted EBITDA grew 12% excluding divestiture impacts with margin expansion of 80 bps sequentially
Enterprise bookings up >20% YoY and new product initiatives (PagoEfectivo) showing strong initial adoption
summary: Paysafe reported Q2 FY2025 revenue of $428.2 million, a decline of 3% YoY due to divestiture impacts and FX, though organic growth was in-line at 5%. Adjusted EBITDA grew 12% excluding the divested business with margin expansion driven by cost discipline, while GAAP net income missed significantly due to non-cash valuation allowances. Management reaffirmed full-year guidance citing strong enterprise pipeline and expected acceleration in H2.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA declined to $2.1 million from $3.6 million
Gearing segment reported an adjusted EBITDA loss of $0.1 million
Guidance suspended due to pending asset sale
positive_highlights: Q2 orders of $21 million, up 14% year-over-year
Industrial Solutions record orders and backlog; third straight quarter of records
Gearing orders up 45% and $6 million follow-on order received in July
summary: Q2 2025 revenue rose 8% year-over-year to $39.2 million, but adjusted EBITDA fell to $2.1 million from $3.6 million, with margin down to 5.3% due to capacity inefficiencies. Orders grew 14% to $21 million, with Industrial Solutions setting a record for orders and backlog. The company suspended full-year guidance due to the pending sale of Manitowoc, expecting $13 million cash and $8 million annual cost savings. Gearing continued to rebound with a new $6 million order in July.

negative_highlights: Gross profit margin decreased to 7.7% from 8.5% due to competitive pricing pressure and higher commission splits.
Ancillary revenue declined 10.5% year-over-year, primarily due to the sale of the insurance business in May 2024.
Third-party revenue fell 25% to $600,000 as clients reduced expenses to protect margins.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 36% year-over-year to $121.4 million driven by a 39.5% rise in brokerage revenue.
Company returned to adjusted EBITDA profitability with $29,000 reported for the quarter.
Verus Title revenue surged 90% year-over-year to $1.5 million due to increased order volumes.
summary: Fathom Holdings reported Q2 FY2025 revenue of $121.4 million, a 36% year-over-year increase driven by the acquisition of My Home Group and organic growth, though ancillary revenue declined 10.5%. The company returned to adjusted EBITDA profitability with a non-GAAP measure of $29,000, but GAAP net loss narrowed to $3.6 million ($0.13/share) from the prior year's $1.3 million loss. Management noted gross profit margin compression to 7.7% due to competitive pricing and higher commission splits, while adjusted EBITDA for ancillary businesses (mortgage and title) declined despite revenue growth in the title segment.

negative_highlights: Revenue was flat quarter-over-quarter at $1.2 million despite macroeconomic headwinds and market tailwinds.
Operating loss increased due to substantial one-time costs related to the Google partnership expansion.
EPS remains negative at -$0.16, indicating a continued path away from profitability.
positive_highlights: Subscription revenue mix improved significantly to 96% of total revenue compared to 87% last year.
Gross margin remained resilient at 86% despite heavy investment in AI infrastructure and partnerships.
Secured multi-year renewals with two large Fortune 1000 clients, including a leading Fortune 50 client expanding globally.
summary: Q2 FY2025 revenue held steady at $1.2 million while gross margin contracted slightly to 86% from the prior year's 88%. The company reported an EPS of negative $0.16, representing a sequential improvement but remaining in loss territory due to significant R&D investments and Google partnership costs.

negative_highlights: Net sales declined 28.4% year-over-year to $39.2 million, driven by industry oversupply and weak durable demand.
Adjusted gross margin contracted 520 bps to 19.2%, with proprietary brand mix softening in Q2.
Restructuring plan involves rationalizing over one-third of SKUs, reflecting sustained industry headwinds and tariff uncertainty.
positive_highlights: Delivered 12th consecutive quarter of adjusted SG&A savings, with a 16% year-over-year reduction to $9.8 million.
Generated positive free cash flow of $1.4 million, with working capital benefits, and repaid $4.5 million on term loan.
International sales grew year-over-year, and several proprietary consumable brands showed solid relative performance.
summary: Q2 net sales fell 28.4% to $39.2 million, with adjusted gross profit at $7.5 million (19.2% of sales), down from 24.4% a year ago. Adjusted EBITDA was a loss of $2.3 million, though it improved sequentially. The company initiated a restructuring plan to cut over one-third of SKUs, expecting annual savings of $3 million-plus, and reiterated positive free cash flow for the last nine months of 2025. Guidance was not raised; full-year adjusted gross margin improvement is still expected.

negative_highlights: Net loss included one-time charges totaling approximately $4 million for office sublease impairment, licensing agent commission settlements, and litigation expenses.
Management declined to provide specific guidance or medium-term growth expectations for Licensing revenue due to the step-function nature of deal signings and brand protection priorities.
positive_highlights: Revenue climbed 14% year-over-year driven by a surge in Licensing revenue (up 105%) and strong growth in the Honey Birdette retail business at full price.
Adjusted EBITDA swung positive to $3.5 million, representing a $6.4 million improvement compared to last year's loss of $2.9 million.
Paid voting contest registrations exceeded expectations with over 50% sign-ups in the first few days without marketing activation.
summary: Playboy reported Q2 FY2025 revenue of $13 million (up 14% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $3.5 million ($6.4M positive swing), though net loss widened to include one-time charges for office sublease impairment, licensing agent commissions settlement, and litigation expenses totaling over $3 million. Management raised the outlook by citing a strong financial position with >$30M cash on hand, significant new multi-year licensing deals exceeding 7 figures annually, and successful execution of paid voting contests that exceeded initial expectations.

negative_highlights: Gross margin fell 440 basis points YoY to 83.6% on higher financial-assistance discounting and expired RED inventory
Prior authorization approval rate remains approximately 9%, with about 70% of patients receiving 'no authorization required' and unable to access treatment
Net loss of $1.7 million and operating cash burn of $3.1 million in the first half; cash of $6 million funds operations only into the first half of 2026
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 46% YoY to $894,000, the fourth straight quarter of double-digit growth, with unit sales up 58%
FDA indication expansion to functional dyspepsia with nausea nearly doubles the addressable market and leverages the same CPT code, call point, and sales force
Category I CPT code effective January 1, 2026 carries 1.46 work RVUs and Medicare Site 11 reimbursement above device cost
summary: NeurAxis reported Q2 2025 revenue of $894,000, up 46% year-over-year, marking the fourth consecutive quarter of double-digit growth, while unit sales rose 58%. Gross margin contracted 440 basis points to 83.6% due to higher financial-assistance discounting and expired RED inventory, and the company posted a net loss of $1.7 million, improved 42% from the prior-year quarter. Management cited three milestones: FDA label expansion to functional dyspepsia (nearly doubling the market), publication of NASPGHAN academic society guidelines, and assignment of a Category I CPT code effective January 1, 2026 with 1.46 work RVUs. The company reaffirmed expectations for continued revenue growth in the second half and a path to cash flow breakeven, supported by $6 million in cash.

negative_highlights: Net loss of $41.0 million in the quarter with R&D up to $37.1 million on manufacturing and clinical costs
Primary efficacy readout remains more than a year away in late 2026, and detailed biomarker data will lag top-line results
No revenue, no earnings and no formal guidance; value depends entirely on unread Phase II data
positive_highlights: Cash and marketable securities of $166.2 million with runway stated into early 2027
JCR collaboration structured capital-efficiently: $9.25 million option payment and up to $555 million in milestones plus single-digit royalties
Final enrollment of 542 patients in the Phase II Altitude AD study complete, with top-line results on track for late 2026
summary: Pre-revenue clinical-stage quarter: R&D expenses were $37.1 million and G&A $4.6 million, producing a $41.7 million operating loss and $41.0 million net loss, with $166.2 million in cash and securities expected to fund operations into early 2027. The Phase II Altitude AD study is fully enrolled at 542 patients with top-line efficacy and safety results still expected in late 2026, and a July option/license deal with JCR covers up to $9.25 million in option payments plus up to $555 million in milestones and single-digit royalties, with a development decision on up to two candidates in early 2026. No revenue or EPS guidance exists; the quarter was operationally in line with prior messaging and the timeline was unchanged.

negative_highlights: NAUTILUS missed primary effectiveness endpoint in earlier time-to-event analysis
Operating expenses grew 13%, though below sales growth
Executive transition incurred onetime nonrecurring items
positive_highlights: Record Q2 revenue of $23.5M, up 22% YoY
Raised full-year revenue and gross margin guidance
NAUTILUS data showing >80% median GTC seizure reduction at 18-24 months and 45.2% seizure-free at 12 months
summary: NeuroPace reported record Q2 2025 revenue of $23.5 million, up 22% year-over-year, with total gross margin above 77% and RNS gross margin above 80%. The company raised its full-year revenue guidance to $94-$98 million and gross margin to 75%-76%, citing strong RNS System sales and Project CARE expansion. Management highlighted compelling NAUTILUS data for IGE, with median GTC seizure reduction signaling better than 80% at 18 and 24 months and 45.2% seizure-free at 12 months, and reaffirmed PMA supplement submission in H2 2025. They also completed a refinancing and noted positive CMS IPPS outcome preserving current DRG reimbursement.

negative_highlights: GAAP net loss widened to $56.6 million ($0.50/share) from $36.5 million ($0.38/share) due to restructuring costs and higher R&D.
Operating expenses increased 8% YoY on a non-GAAP basis driven by LOTIS-5/7 trial investments.
Roche received a Complete Response Letter (CRL) for STARGLO, introducing competitive uncertainty in the second-line DLBCL landscape.
positive_highlights: Net product revenues grew slightly YoY to $18.1 million in Q2 and $35.5 million in H1.
LOTIS-7 data showed a 93.3% overall response rate and 86.7% complete response rate with 25 of 26 CRs durable at cutoff.
Cash runway extended into 2028 following a $100 million private placement.
summary: ADC Therapeutics reported Q2 FY2025 net product revenues of $18.1 million, a slight increase from $17 million in the prior year, with first-half revenue reaching $35.5 million versus $34.9 million. The company incurred $13.1 million in one-time restructuring and impairment costs related to closing its U.K. facility and cutting 30% of the workforce. Management expressed confidence in upcoming clinical catalysts, including LOTIS-7 data expected later in 2025 and potential second-line approval for ZYNLONTA plus rituximab by mid-2027.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to $30.5 million ($0.13/share) from $5.8 million ($0.03/share), including a $14.8 million noncash VAC impairment
Operating expenses jumped to $22.5 million from $7.3 million year over year
No timing or data access for the Roche/Genentech Phase IIa OpRegen trial; management explicitly declined to comment on enrollment
positive_highlights: Revenue rose to $2.8 million from $1.4 million in Q2 2024 on higher Roche collaboration revenue recognition
Cash of $42.3 million expected to fund operations into Q1 2027, with a potential $37 million warrant-related inflow if Roche advances OpRegen
First OPC1 administration to a chronic spinal cord injury patient succeeded with a novel delivery device, with a second site process initiated
summary: Lineage reported Q2 2025 total revenue of $2.8 million, up from $1.4 million a year earlier, driven by Roche deferred-revenue recognition. Operating expenses rose to $22.5 million from $7.3 million, largely due to a $14.8 million noncash impairment of the VAC platform intangible and warrant liability remeasurement, producing a net loss of $30.5 million ($0.13/share) versus $5.8 million ($0.03/share) in Q2 2024. Cash stood at $42.3 million, with runway into Q1 2027, and a potential $37 million from warrant exercise tied to Roche advancing OpRegen. Management gave no formal financial guidance but highlighted the first OPC1 chronic spinal cord injury patient dosed via a new delivery device and planned site expansion and CIRM grant application.

negative_highlights: Consolidated Hospitality revenue declined 15% versus pro forma Q2 2024 due to reduced hours and select venue closures at the Tin Building and weakness at stand-alone restaurants
Nike exercised early termination of its Pier 17 office lease, moving expiration from Q1 2030 to Q1 2027
Absence of the Savannah Bananas event at Las Vegas Ballpark created a year-over-year headwind in Q2
positive_highlights: Entertainment segment revenue rose 16% year-over-year, helped by 11 additional concerts, and Entertainment operating EBITDA increased 122%
Total company operating EBITDA increased 95% year-over-year on a pro forma basis; G&A fell 55% year-over-year to $8.3 million
Net loss attributable to common stockholders improved $20.2 million (58%) year-over-year; net cash position of $125 million with negative net debt to gross assets of 3%
summary: Seaport Entertainment Group reported Q2 FY2025 total consolidated revenue of $39.8 million, up 1% year-over-year on a pro forma basis. Entertainment revenue rose 16% and segment operating EBITDA increased 122%, while consolidated Hospitality revenue fell 15% (total hospitality including unconsolidated ventures down 4%, same-store up 1%). The company reported a net loss attributable to common stockholders of $14.8 million, or $1.16 per share, and adjusted net loss of $0.58 per share, with no formal revenue or EPS guidance provided; management said it targets operational breakeven sometime in 2026. Key changes versus the prior period included finalizing the collapse of the Tin Building JV into full ownership with new license agreements with Jean-Georges, and the announcement that Nike exercised an early termination right on office space at Pier 17, moving lease expiration from Q1 2030 to Q1 2027 in exchange for a $4 million termination payment.

negative_highlights: AbbVie partnership remains delayed, with management now expecting it to be a 2026 event.
Cash position remains thin at $0.73 million as of June 30, 2025, relying on recent capital raises.
Tariffs have had a mild negative margin impact on some imported products, though not severe.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 100% YoY to $2.88 million, with contract manufacturing up 103% and consumer products up 95%.
Gross margin expanded to 43.6% from 20.3% in Q2 2024.
Expanded STADA partnership includes $1.0 million non-dilutive funding and multiple product launches expected in Q4 2025 and H1 2026.
summary: Revenue was approximately $2.9 million, up 100% year-over-year (vs. $1.44 million in Q2 2024), with gross margin of 43.6%, more than double the 20.3% from Q2 2024. Adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed to $0.42 million from $0.79 million a year ago. Management reiterated 2025 guidance of $13 million in revenue and positive EBITDA, citing new contract manufacturing wins (iRhythm), STADA expansion, and expected seasonally strong H2. Cash stood at $0.73 million at quarter-end, but subsequent funding includes $1.0 million from STADA and $1.05 million from a registered direct offering.

negative_highlights: Gross margin declined to 84% from 88% due to lower manufacturing efficiency on newly launched products.
Operating loss widened slightly to $7.3 million compared to $8.2 million in the prior year quarter.
Nelitolimod program expenses remain elevated with approximately $500,000 in nonrecurring closeout costs incurred.
positive_highlights: Net sales grew 52% year-over-year to $11.2 million, exceeding sequential expectations with a 22% gain.
TriNav FLX launch is exceeding internal projections and addressing tortuous vascular anatomy needs.
New CPT code coverage for mapping procedures has accelerated adoption since April.
summary: TriSalus Life Sciences reported Q2 FY2025 net sales of $11.2 million, representing a 52% year-over-year increase and a 22% sequential gain. The company reiterated its full-year guidance for 50% revenue growth despite gross margin compression to 84% driven by new product ramp-up inefficiencies. Management highlighted the successful launch of the TriNav FLX system and the commercial impact of new CPT code coverage for mapping procedures.

negative_highlights: Net loss remained substantial at $7.7 million ($1.53 per share), and cash and equivalents stood at only $6.5 million as of June 30, 2025.
Management acknowledged the current quarter is not yet underwritten and that reaching the low end of guidance requires continued sequential growth without new contracts.
International revenue reflects only training and demonstration device sales to partners, with hospital tenders expected no earlier than late fiscal 2026.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 157% year-over-year to $1.8 million and 50% sequentially from the March 2025 quarter.
Gross profit improved to $0.2 million from a $0.3 million loss in the prior-year quarter.
Operating expenses were cut 40% year-over-year to approximately $7.5 million, and net cash burn fell over 60% to $4.7 million.
summary: Beyond Air reported Q1 FY2026 revenue of $1.8 million, up 157% year-over-year from $0.7 million and up 50% sequentially, with gross profit swinging to $0.2 million from a $0.3 million loss a year ago. Net loss narrowed to $7.7 million ($1.53 per share) from $12.2 million, operating expenses fell 40% year-over-year to about $7.5 million, and net cash burn dropped over 60% to $4.7 million. Management reaffirmed FY2026 revenue guidance of $12-16 million, citing international expansion into over 30 countries, a new Premier GPO agreement, and planned LungFit PH II launch in calendar 2026.

negative_highlights: Gross margin contracted significantly by 240 bps (from 30.5% to 28.1%) due to the ongoing tariff environment.
Revenue declined in the U.S. market (-0.4%), and Shower Systems revenue fell -11.2%, offsetting gains elsewhere.
Operating loss widened from a $0.5M gain to a $0.8M loss as lower margins were compounded by increased operating expenses related to growth initiatives.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 5.5% year-over-year to $31 million driven by growth in Sanitaryware (up 4.3%), Bath Furniture (up 2.7%), and Covered Bridge cabinetry (up 67.7%).
Order pipeline is recovering following the initial tariff-induced pause, with management expressing confidence that momentum has returned.
Strategic investments in new programs and global sourcing diversification are progressing to fuel future organic growth.
summary: FGI reported Q2 FY2025 revenue of $31 million (up 5.5% YoY) and gross profit of $8.7 million, but GAAP operating loss widened to $0.8 million from a prior year gain due to margin compression and growth investments. Gross margins declined 240 bps to 28.1%, primarily driven by tariff impacts that caused an industry-wide pause in orders during the quarter. Management maintained full-year guidance of revenue between $135M-$145M, citing a recovering order pipeline despite ongoing uncertainty.

negative_highlights: 2025 services revenue trajectory now softer than the previously stated 9x growth target due to Aquanaut equipment delays and component lead times
Cash fell to $2.7 million from $10.1 million at year-end, requiring additional ATM issuance and a $3 million debt draw
Operating expenses of $8.4 million and adjusted net loss of $7.4 million widened from $6.6 million in Q1 2025 and $6.5 million in Q2 2024
positive_highlights: Revenue of $2.1 million rose $1.6 million year-over-year and $1.9 million sequentially, with service revenue over $2 million (more than 4x the prior-year period)
Customer base expanded to 9 clients on MSA relationships, reducing revenue concentration across offshore wind, oil and gas and government markets

Pending multi-month contract with a supermajor oil company running through Q1 2026 expected to provide off-season revenue and reduce seasonality; Q3 guided to sequential revenue growth with a third asset deployed
summary: Nauticus Robotics reported Q2 FY2025 revenue of $2.1 million, up $1.6 million year-over-year and $1.9 million sequentially, driven by the SeaTrepid acquisition and the Gulf season, with 9 clients served. Operating expenses rose to $8.4 million and net loss was $7.4 million, while cash fell to $2.7 million from $10.1 million at the prior quarter-end. Management said the original 9x services revenue growth target for 2025 is now 'softer than anticipated' due to Aquanaut equipment delays, but expects sequential Q3 growth and a pending multi-month supermajor contract to add Q4/Q1 off-season revenue; Q2 had only two assets in the field.

negative_highlights: Gross margin fell to 53% from 67% YoY due to revenue mix
Marketplace revenue was only $0.3M after marketing spend was halted ahead of the Made in America launch
Credit business revenue declined YoY and merchant onboarding for bundled checkout is taking longer than anticipated
positive_highlights: Fintech revenue would have grown 28% YoY to $3.8M excluding a one-time $0.4M vendor true-up
PSQ Payments revenue rose over 80% from Q1 2025 to $1.0M
GAAP operating loss narrowed to $8.1M from $14M, with net loss per share improving 50% to $0.18 from $0.36
summary: PublicSquare reported Q2 2025 net revenue of $7.1M, up 18% YoY, with Financial Technology revenue of $3.4M (+15.6%, or +28% excluding a $0.4M one-time vendor true-up) and Brands revenue of $3.3M (+45.5%), while Marketplace contributed just $0.3M as marketing spend was halted. Gross margin fell to 53% from 67% on revenue mix, but the GAAP operating loss narrowed to $8.1M from $14M and net loss per share improved 50% to $0.18 from $0.36. Management announced it will monetize EveryLife (sale) and Marketplace (sale or repurposing) to focus entirely on fintech, expecting completion by end of Q4 2025, and reiterated that payment-customer onboarding, though slower than anticipated, should drive material revenue in H2 2025. No formal forward revenue or EPS guidance figures were provided beyond qualitative commentary and cost-savings progress of $9M of the $11M annualized target in H1 2025.

negative_highlights: Bookings fell note weakness in of internal targets primarily because a significant $2.4M-$2.5M CrimeTracer transaction and a PlateRanger deal were pushed into Q3.
Revenue recognition was suspended in Puerto Rico due to bureaucratic delays requiring an RFP process instead of a standard contract extension.
GAAP gross margin contracted from 60% YoY to 53%.
positive_highlights: Revenue decline was only 4% YoY despite losing $2.8M in Chicago revenue, indicating strong growth elsewhere including ~$3.5M NYPD catch-up and new ShotSpotter deployments (New Orleans, Methuen, Victorville).
Pipeline visibility remains healthy at over $37 million for the remainder of 2025.
Customer attrition is outperforming expectations due to retention initiatives.
summary: SoundThinking reported Q2 FY2025 revenue of $25.9 million (a 4% YoY decline) and GAAP net loss of $3.1 million ($0.25/share), driven by a Chicago contract non-renewal headwind partially offset by new NYPD catch-up revenue. Management reaffirmed full-year 2025 guidance for revenue between $111M-$113M and adjusted EBITDA margins of 20%-22%, explicitly stating that the outlook does not include any contribution from a potential Chicago win which is expected in 2026.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined 1.6% year-over-year to $120 million from $122 million on a combined basis.
Net loss of $399 million, including a $382 million noncash impairment.
Adjusted EBITDA fell to $17 million from $19 million a year ago, and APAC revenue and bookings are declining year-over-year.
positive_highlights: Sequential revenue growth of 15.5% from Q1 to Q2, about 5 percentage points ahead of prior-year combined company comparison.
Reaffirmed full-year guidance of broadly flat revenue and adjusted EBITDA of $85 million or more.
Reorganization expected to cut roughly 10% of the global workforce, positioning the company ahead of original year-one cost savings and on track for $45 million of synergies by year three.
summary: Q2 revenue was $120 million, down 1.6% year-over-year on a combined basis but up about 15.5% sequentially from Q1. The quarter included a $399 million net loss driven by a $382 million noncash impairment, with adjusted EBITDA of $17 million versus $19 million a year ago. Management reaffirmed full-year guidance for broadly flat revenue and adjusted EBITDA of $85 million or more, and announced a reorganization cutting about 10% of the global workforce while stating it expects to exceed original year-one cost synergies. The sequential improvement from Q3 to Q4 is guided to continue, a departure from the typical Q2 to Q3 seasonal decline.

negative_highlights: Management explicitly stated they are 'cautious' regarding how the new biomarker approach will translate into enrollment trends due to competition.
The company halted its previously announced evorpacept colon cancer program, indicating a strategic pivot away from that indication.
positive_highlights: New data from ASPEN-06 confirms CD47-high expression as a predictive biomarker, showing an ORR of 65% versus 26% in the control arm for HER2-positive gastric cancer patients.
Cash runway guidance was extended to Q1 FY2027 following capital prioritization and closure of legacy trials (ASPEN-03 through ASPEN-07).
The Phase II breast cancer study design has been amended to pursue a CD47 biomarker-driven strategy, with interim data expected in Q3 2026.
summary: The company reported strong clinical progress in Q2 FY2025, presenting new data from the ASPEN-06 trial identifying CD47 expression as a predictive biomarker for evorpacept efficacy (ORR of 65% vs 26% control). Management announced that ALX2004 is on track to dose its first patient later in Q3 and completed the Sanofi partnership study phase. Financially, management revised guidance extending cash runway into Q1 FY2027 by halting legacy trials like ASPEN-03/04/06/07.

negative_highlights: Full-year revenue guidance remained unchanged despite strong Q2 results, implying a significant step-up is required in H2.
One next-generation system deal slipped from closing on July 1, meaning Q2 revenue was capped below the potential of $3M+.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 26% sequentially to $2.7M with the sale of 8 units, including the first next-generation Swoop system sold before quarter end.
Gross margins expanded 800 bps sequentially to 49.3%, driven by higher ASP and volume.
Net cash burn excluding financing dropped 19% sequentially to $8.1M as the company transitions to a commercial growth stage.
summary: Hyperfine reported Q2 FY2025 revenue of $2.7 million, up 26% sequentially, driven by the sale of 8 units including the first next-generation Swoop system. Gross margins expanded 800 bps to 49.3%, while net cash burn excluding financing decreased 19% sequentially to $8.1 million. Management maintained full-year 2025 revenue guidance of 10%-20% growth over 2024 and reiterated a gross margin target of 47%-50%.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined significantly from approximately $4.9M due to discontinuation of consulting services and equity-based fees dropping from ~$108k to ~$72k
Recorded a substantial impairment expense of approximately $19.9 million on investments deemed other than temporary
positive_highlights: Secured a broker-dealer license for subsidiary Netcapital Securities to participate in larger Reg A capital raisings
Portfolio company MAGFAST raised over $10 million through multiple offerings on the funding platform
summary: Netcapital reported full year fiscal 2025 revenues of $869,460 and a net loss of approximately $28.3 million compared to prior years' figures of roughly $4.9M revenue and $4.9M loss respectively. The company incurred an impairment expense of approximately $19.9 million due to investment write-downs and discontinued its equity-based consulting services, resulting in an operating loss of $8.3 million versus a previous year's loss of $3.4 million. Management highlighted the acquisition of a broker-dealer license for Reg A participation but offered no specific financial guidance or turnaround metrics.

negative_highlights: Operating expenses increased moderately due to payroll setup costs for three new campuses that generated only $200k in revenue during the quarter.
Management declined to provide precise monthly guidance on ground lease signings or specific variance percentages against forecasts, citing schedule variability.
positive_highlights: Consolidated revenue growth accelerated significantly with an 82% increase year-over-year reaching $6.6 million.
Cash flow from operations turned positive at $2.2 million for the Obligated Group subsidiary.
Pre-leasing pilots at Dulles and Bradley achieved signed leases above target revenues, validating a new leasing strategy.
summary: Consolidated revenues increased 82% year-over-year to $6.6 million in Q2 FY2025, driven by the acquisition of Camarillo and higher volumes at existing campuses. The company reaffirmed guidance for cash flow breakeven on a consolidated basis by the end of the year as three new campuses ramp up leasing. Management highlighted that actual revenues are expected to exceed original CBRE projections due to stronger-than-anticipated rents, fuel margins, and occupancy optimization.

negative_highlights: Revenue fell 38% to $8.4 million and net loss widened to $18.3 million ($2.39 per diluted share) from $2 million ($0.27) a year ago
Operating expenses jumped to $36.4 million from $17.9 million, including $40.7 million of accelerated depreciation on citrus trees
The incremental $25 million land sale is not assured; management said timing is 'hazy' and it could slip into fiscal 2026
positive_highlights: Year-to-date land sales of $23.5 million from ~2,794 acres exceeded the original $20 million fiscal 2025 guidance, with potential for another $25 million before year-end
Received $16 million in crop insurance proceeds, lifting cash to $42.1 million from $3.2 million at fiscal year-end 2024 and cutting net debt to $43.2 million
Land management and other operations revenue rose 57% for the quarter and 68% year-to-date on higher rock and sand royalty income and sod sales
summary: Q3 FY2025 revenue fell 38% to $8.4 million from $13.6 million as citrus harvest volume dropped to 2.1 million pound solids from 4.3 million due to Hurricane Milton, and the company reported a net loss of $18.3 million ($2.39 per diluted share) driven largely by $40.7 million of accelerated depreciation on citrus trees. Adjusted EBITDA was $19.3 million versus $1.3 million a year ago, boosted by $16 million of crop insurance proceeds, and cash stood at $42.1 million with net debt down to $43.2 million. Management reaffirmed roughly $20 million of fiscal 2025 adjusted EBITDA, said year-to-date land sales of $23.5 million already exceed the original $20 million guidance, and flagged potential for another $25 million before year-end, though timing of that transaction is uncertain. The quarter reflects the final major citrus harvest as Alico pivots to a land company, with the Corkscrew Grove stewardship district legislation approved and entitlement decisions anticipated in 2026.

negative_highlights: Total Q3 delivered volumes rose 6% but residential and commercial volumes were slightly down year-over-year
Guidance for a modest net loss in Q4 as rate-case revenue timing and seasonal volumes weigh on the quarter
Franklin County expansion capital pushed into fiscal 2026 as the project develops slower than anticipated
positive_highlights: Nine-month net income up 16% to $13.5 million, or $1.31/share versus $1.15
Installed 3.9 new main miles YTD, already 50% above all of fiscal 2024, with 541 new services connected
summary: RGC reported Q3 net income of $538,000 ($0.05/share) versus $157,000 ($0.02) a year ago, with lower operating income offset by higher MVP earnings and lower interest expense. Nine-month net income rose 16% to $13.5 million ($1.31/share) versus $1.15, aided by higher base rates. Full-year EPS guidance was maintained at $1.22-$1.27, but management guided to a modest Q4 net loss given rate timing and seasonal volume, and pushed Franklin County expansion capital into fiscal 2026. Midstream debt was refinanced into a 7-year note at SOFR+1.55%.

negative_highlights: Revenue guidance for 2025 maintained at $64-68 million, implying significant back-half weighted performance
Management notes continued lumpiness in Pharma Biocatalysis revenue due to unpredictable order timing
Gross margin improvement to 72% is not expected to be sustained at that magnitude for the full year
positive_highlights: Revenue in Q2 2025 was $15.3 million, nearly double the $8 million reported in Q2 2024
Operating loss halved year-over-year, with net loss improving to $13.3 million from $23.8 million
Customer engagements for ECO Synthesis exceed 30, with growing interest approaching 40
summary: Codexis reported Q2 2025 revenue of $15.3 million, up from $8 million in Q2 2024, with product gross margin expanding to 72% from 45%. Net loss narrowed to $13.3 million from $23.8 million year-over-year. Management reiterated full-year 2025 revenue guidance of $64-68 million, with growth expected in the second half from ligase and ECO Synthesis. They reported over 30 (approaching 40) customer engagements for ECO Synthesis and are exploring options to expand capacity, including a potential Codexis-owned GMP facility to capture more value from early-phase projects.

negative_highlights: Net revenue fell 30.5% year over year to $19.5 million from $28 million
Gross margin contracted to 54.3% from 60.4%, with Q2 advertising overspend of $0.9 million and a $0.7 million inventory obsolescence charge
Cash declined to $10.5 million from $18 million at December 31, 2024, inventory rose to $18.5 million from $13.7 million, and the share repurchase plan remains suspended
positive_highlights: Fixed-cost reduction plan has identified $5.5 million of the $5-6 million annualized savings target, including $3.8 million from May headcount cuts
H2 2025 adjusted EBITDA guidance of breakeven to a $1 million loss versus the $4.7 million H1 loss, on slightly higher H2 revenue of $36-38 million
Dehumidifier sourcing shifted from 100% China in 2024 to about 65% in 2025 via Indonesia, avoiding peak Chinese tariff rates
summary: Aterian reported Q2 2025 net revenue of $19.5 million, down 30.5% year over year from $28 million, and an adjusted EBITDA loss of $2.2 million versus a $0.2 million gain in the prior year quarter, driven by tariff-related price increases, lower sales velocity, higher marketing spend and a $0.7 million inventory obsolescence charge. Gross margin fell to 54.3% from 60.4%, the operating loss widened to $4.5 million from $3.2 million, and cash declined to $10.5 million from $18 million at year-end 2024. Management guided H2 2025 net revenue of $36-38 million versus $34.8 million in H1 and adjusted EBITDA of breakeven to a $1 million loss versus a $4.7 million H1 loss, expecting full-year exit from the worst tariff impacts without raising equity in 2025. Identified fixed-cost savings of $5.5 million against a $5-6 million target, resourcing of about 35% of dehumidifiers out of China to Indonesia, and a U.S.-sourced consumables pivot including the Squatty Potty flushable wipes launch are cited as the key stabilizers.

negative_highlights: Gross margin declined to 73% from 77% due to hardware mix
Operating loss of $5 million in Q2 2025
SG&A reduction partially offset by higher R&D costs
positive_highlights: Revenue up 49% year-over-year to $1.7 million
Secured major IAM deployment with National Bank of Mozambique
Closed $600,000 follow-on orders from defense ministry, total project over EUR 3 million
summary: Q2 FY2025 revenue increased 49% year-over-year to $1.7 million, with hardware revenue up $458,000, but gross margin declined to 73% from 77% due to product mix. SG&A was reduced 13.5% year-over-year, partially offset by higher R&D, and the company reduced its note payable from $1.5 million to $447,000. Management highlighted new defense contracts, including a first phase deployment for an international defense agency, a 3-year PortalGuard deployment with a Middle East police force, and $600,000 of follow-on orders. Despite a $5 million operating loss in Q2, management expects expense run rate to normalize and sees strong growth opportunities in defense and EMEA in the back half of 2025.

negative_highlights: Product revenue declined 11% year-over-year to $71 million due to tariff impacts in China and Middle East unrest.
China product revenue fell 14% sequentially following the imposition of tariffs, with demand described as 'cautiously guiding'.
U.S. orders remain soft as the replacement market has not yet recovered meaningfully.
positive_highlights: Service revenue grew 4% year-over-year to $57 million, driven by installed base expansion and contract capture.
Gross margin expanded 200 basis points year-over-year to 30.6%, aided by service mix and pricing initiatives.
Company successfully refinanced debt with TCW, extending maturity by 5 years and securing $190 million in new financing.
summary: Total revenue for Q4 FY2025 was $128 million, down 5% year-over-year due to declines in China (-14%) and EIMEA (-34%), while service revenue grew 4% to $57 million. Management provided FY2026 guidance of $471-$485 million in revenue and $31-$35 million in adjusted EBITDA, noting that the outlook assumes continued geopolitical volatility and tariff impacts.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined to $4.5 million from $5.4 million a year ago, with PeriShip revenue down approximately 14%
Gross margin contracted to 35% from 39%, with gross profit falling $0.5 million to $1.6 million
New second freight carrier is not expected to meaningfully contribute until 2026, with integration taking a couple of months and peak-season shipper inertia delaying changes
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA improved to $0.3 million in Q2 2025 from $0.2 million in Q2 2024
Operating expenses reduced approximately 27% versus Q2 2024, to $1.9 million from $2.6 million
Cash balance rose to $6.1 million as of June 30, 2025 from $2.8 million at December 31, 2024, with $0.7 million generated from operations in the quarter
summary: VerifyMe reported Q2 2025 revenue of $4.5 million, down from $5.4 million a year ago, with PeriShip revenue down approximately 14% on previously disclosed 2024 customer losses. Gross margin compressed to 35% from 39%, but operating expenses fell 27% to $1.9 million, net loss narrowed to $0.29 million (-$0.02 per diluted share) from $0.35 million (-$0.03), and adjusted EBITDA improved to $0.3 million from $0.2 million. Cash rose to $6.1 million from $2.8 million at year-end 2024, and the company expects continued positive operating cash flow in the second half of 2025. Management guided for gross margin to increase versus Q3 and Q4 2024, highlighted a new second freight carrier relationship that will take a couple of months to integrate, and said meaningful organic revenue growth is expected in 2026 rather than immediately.

negative_highlights: Gross margin contracted to 15.5% from 16.9% YoY due to front-loaded lease depreciation costs associated with rapid growth.
Write-off rate increased by 50 basis points year-over-year to 9.8%, though management noted this remained within the targeted 8-10% range.
positive_highlights: Gross originations grew 30.4% year-over-year to $72.1 million, beating the top end of the 25-30% outlook range.
Revenue increased 22.1% YoY to $71.9 million, surpassing the 17-20% guidance band for the ninth consecutive quarter of growth.
Adjusted EBITDA turned positive at approximately $300,000 in Q2, exceeding the breakeven expectation and marking a significant step toward profitability.
summary: Katapult reported Q2 FY2025 gross originations of $72.1 million (30.4% YoY growth) and revenue of $71.9 million (22.1% YoY), both exceeding their respective guidance ranges. The company delivered positive adjusted EBITDA of approximately $300,000 against a breakeven outlook while raising its 2025 gross originations forecast to 20-25%. Management highlighted strong top-of-funnel activity with applications up over 91% YoY and reiterated full-year revenue growth guidance of at least 20%.

negative_highlights: Overall net operating income decreased to $9.8 million from $11.8 million in the prior quarter.
Core FFO was negative $7.2 million compared to a loss of $2.1 million in the prior year, with per share core FFO at -$9.53 versus -$21.93 last year.
Office NOI declined by $1.6 million from the prior quarter largely due to real estate tax benefits and lower occupancy at Oakland assets.
positive_highlights: Leasing activity increased significantly with approximately 140,000 square feet executed through July, representing an over 55% increase from the prior year period.
Successfully secured property level financing on 7 assets to fully retire the recourse credit facility and support growth initiatives.
Multifamily occupancy at 701 South Hudson improved to approximately 68% from 41% in the prior quarter.
summary: CMCT reported a miss on revenue and NOI for Q2 FY2025, with overall net operating income decreasing to $9.8 million from $11.8 million in the prior quarter and core FFO turning negative at -$7.2 million. Management highlighted significant progress on balance sheet liquidity, including retiring the recourse credit facility and extending debt maturities, but noted that leasing activity gains are not yet captured in current NOI due to timing of tenant reimbursements. The outlook remains cautious regarding specific assets like Oakland while expressing confidence in long-term opportunities for 2026.

negative_highlights: Cash and cash equivalents fell to $1.39 million from $5.08 million at March 31, 2025.
Operating loss remained significant at $3.62 million despite revenue growth.
Tariff-related cost inflation of 5-10% is pressuring domestic material costs.
positive_highlights: Net sales rose 114% YoY to a record $4.1 million, with June alone at $1.6 million.
Gross profit increased 173% sequentially to $1.08 million, and gross margin expanded 800 bps to 26.4%.
Dealer network added 450+ new accounts year-to-date, up from 94 at the end of last year, supporting over $21.5 million in repeatable annual revenue at full activation.
summary: Worksport reported record Q2 2025 net sales of $4.1 million, up 114% year-over-year and 83% sequentially, with gross margin expanding 800 basis points to 26.4%. Net loss narrowed to $3.73 million from $4.46 million in Q1. Management reaffirmed its full-year 2025 revenue target of at least $20 million and continues to expect gross margin to reach 30% by year-end, with operational cash flow breakeven targeted for late Q4 2025 or early Q1 2026. The company added two national distributors with access to roughly 450 dealer accounts, while cash declined to $1.39 million from $5.08 million in Q1.

negative_highlights: Gross margin contracted to 21% from 25% YoY due to product mix and tariff costs
note, general, and administrative expenses remained high at $2M (66% of sales)
Company holds significant prepaid inventory ($5M+) waiting for potential tariff exclusions
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 134% YoY to $3M driven by RV market recovery and accessory sales
Net loss narrowed significantly to $1.4M (down from $2.2M) due to higher volume
HESS vertical launched with UL certification progress for tax credit eligibility
summary: XPON reported Q2 FY2025 revenue of $3 million (up 134% YoY) but a gross margin contraction to 21%, driven by lower-margin accessory sales and tariff impacts on the RV market. The company posted a net loss of $1.4 million, representing an improvement over the prior year's loss due to higher volume rather than operational profitability. Management expressed confidence in future growth from new HESS products but noted ongoing uncertainty regarding tariffs.

negative_highlights: Q2 revenue of $20.1 million missed expectations due to shipment timing dynamics, resulting in a gross margin contraction from 27% YoY.
Operating loss widened significantly to -$8.7 million compared to -$3.9 million in the prior year quarter.
Production disruptions occurred for two or three weeks in June due to regional conflict and tariff announcements.
positive_highlights: Record backlog of purchase orders totaling roughly $86 million expected for delivery in FY2025, with a specific spike to $43 million near-term.
Full-year revenue guidance reaffirmed at $130M-$140M despite Q2 timing misses.
Adjusted EBITDA is projected to be positive for the full year 2025 as top line ramps above the ~$31M break-even point.
summary: Gauzy reported Q2 FY2025 revenue of $20.1 million and a gross margin contraction to 21.4% due to timing shifts in shipments from the second half into this quarter. Management reaffirmed full-year guidance for revenue between $130M-$140M, citing a record backlog of $43M (approx $86M total expected delivery) and expects adjusted EBITDA to be positive by year-end driven by H2 ramp-up above the ~$31M break-even threshold. The company raised approximately $15 million in debt financing during the quarter.

negative_highlights: Gross margin only 16% in Q2, with fluctuation expected
Cash burn still $7.3 million in quarter; annualized burn remains
ATM program of $75 million launched, indicating financing need
positive_highlights: Q2 revenue up 46% YoY; first-half revenue exceeded all of 2024
Raised NRE booking guidance to $30-60 million from $20-50 million
Signed SOW with top-5 OEM; shipping units, targeting 2027 SOP
summary: Q2 FY2025 revenue was $9.7 million, up 46% year-over-year, with first-half revenue of $27.1 million exceeding all of FY2024. Cash burn fell to $7.3 million from $20.7 million in Q1, and the company raised its NRE booking guidance to $30-60 million from $20-50 million. Management launched the InnovizSMART non-automotive product and signed a development agreement with a top-5 OEM for a 2027 L3 program, while maintaining full-year revenue guidance of $50-60 million. The company is ramping production at Fabrinet and expects 10x unit shipments in Q3 versus Q2.

Afya reported Q2 2025 revenue of BRL 919 million, up 14% YoY, with adjusted EBITDA of BRL 401 million and a 43.6% margin (up 110 bps). First-half revenue rose 15% to BRL 1,856 million and adjusted EBITDA grew 20% to BRL 893 million at a record 48.1% margin, up 220 bps, while first-half basic EPS rose 17% to BRL 4.69. Management reaffirmed full-year 2025 guidance and announced a new buyback of up to 4 million Class A shares, though continuing education residency students fell 29% YoY and medical net ticket grew 3.2%, slightly below inflation.

negative_highlights: Consolidated net loss only improved 43% due to continued THP investment
THP strategic alternatives process initiated, limiting ability to communicate
Additional EUR 2 million OsStic milestone payments remain uncertain in timing
positive_highlights: Surgical net revenue up 28% YoY to $25.8 million
Segment adjusted EBITDA up 239% YoY to $4.7 million
THP pilot program initiated and CarePICS acquisition completed
summary: Sanara MedTech's Surgical segment grew net revenue 28% YoY to $25.8 million, with soft tissue up 28% and bone fusion up 25%. The segment achieved about $500,000 net income, a $2.7 million improvement, and adjusted EBITDA rose 239% to $4.7 million. Management initiated a formal strategic alternatives process for THP and guided second-half THP cash investment down to $5.5-$6.5 million. The company remains on track for OsStic launch in Q1 2027 after BMI completed two milestones.

negative_highlights: Adjusted gross margin rate declined approximately 200 basis points to 34% YoY due to Motif integration costs and external white-label brand impacts.
Temporary disruptions in on-time-in-full (OTIF) service levels for Motif brands caused a 30 bps decline in overall market share versus Q2, though normalized by mid-June.
Net loss of $6.3 million due to non-cash fair value changes in derivative liabilities associated with BAT top-up rights and preferred shares.
positive_highlights: Record quarterly revenue of $110.2 million gross sales and $70.8 million net revenue, representing significant year-over-year growth.
International business scaled significantly with $7.4 million in revenue (up 208% YoY) driven by exports to Germany, Australia, and the U.K.
Operational efficiency realized synergies of $4.2 million ($15M annualized target on track), including capacity additions yielding an extra 14,000 kg annually.
summary: Organigram reported record Q3 FY2025 results with gross sales of $110.2 million (up 73% YoY) and net revenue of $70.8 million (up 72% YoY), driven by acquisitions and international expansion, though adjusted gross margin rate decreased to 34%. Management maintained guidance for full-year margins around 35%, citing temporary drag from Motif integration costs that are expected to normalize in Q4 as synergies flow through.

negative_highlights: No Israel Innovation Authority grant received in Q2, versus $180,000 in prior year
FX headwinds from shekel strength noted, not hedged
Guidance kept at 15-18% growth, implying deceleration from Q2's 19.3%
positive_highlights: Revenue up 19.3% YoY to a record $17.7 million
Non-GAAP operating margin expanded to nearly 20% of revenue
Cash at record $101.6 million, debt-free
summary: RADCOM reported record Q2 2025 revenue of $17.7 million, up 19.3% year-over-year, with non-GAAP operating income of $3.4 million (19.5% of revenue) and non-GAAP net income of $4.2 million ($0.25 per diluted share). Cash reached a record $101.6 million, with positive operating cash flow of $2.6 million. The company maintained full-year revenue guidance of 15-18% growth and noted progress on NVIDIA and ServiceNow partnerships, with some customers moving to lab deployments.

negative_highlights: Guest value perception declined unexpectedly after March menu launch
Company comp traffic down 2.5% in Q2; July started at -0.9%
Full-year guidance lowered; no longer free cash flow positive in 2025
positive_highlights: Same-store sales improved to +5% average in the last 2 weeks
Owned digital traffic up 2% YoY and rewards check-ins up 4% in Q2
Portfolio closures are removing negative-cash-flow restaurants and boosting nearby sales
summary: Noodles & Company reported Q2 FY2025 total revenue of $126.4 million, down 0.7% YoY, with system-wide comp sales up 1.5% but traffic down 2.5%. Adjusted EBITDA fell to $6 million from $9.2 million, and restaurant contribution margin contracted to 12.8% from 15.5%, pressured by $1.7 million in menu-rollout costs. Management cut full-year guidance to revenue of $487-$495 million and comp sales growth of 2.5%-4%, and no longer expects positive free cash flow in 2025. Recent weekly sales trends improved to +5% following the Duos value launch, but overall results missed internal expectations.

negative_highlights: Net loss increased year-over-year primarily due to higher net interest expenses and debt repayment costs
Cash balance decreased significantly to $31.9 million compared to $41.7 million at December 31, 2024
positive_highlights: VERSATILE-002 median overall survival remains steady at 30 months with no new safety signals
Enrollment in VERSATILE-003 Phase III trial is complete and the company is right on schedule for patient accrual
Colorectal cancer cohort of PDS01ADC met criteria to expand from Stage 1 to Stage 2 following positive results
summary: PDS Biotech reported a net loss of $9.4 million ($0.21 per share) for Q2 FY2025, an increase from the prior year's loss due to higher interest expenses and debt repayment costs offset by lower personnel spending. While clinical programs advanced with positive data presented at ASCO 2025 and enrollment in the VERSATILE-003 Phase III trial proceeding on schedule, management noted a cash balance of $31.9 million down from year-end levels.

negative_highlights: Total investment income fell to $23.5 million from $27.5 million in the prior quarter
NAV per share declined to $12.99 from $13.55
Four portfolio companies remain on nonaccrual status and tariffs are pressuring portfolio company margins
positive_highlights: Invested approximately $130 million across 3 new portfolio companies to date in fiscal 2026, versus $221 million for all of fiscal 2025
Adjusted net investment income of $0.24 per share covered the $0.08 monthly distribution
No PIK income and 13.5% floors on the three most recent new deals provide rate-cut cushion
summary: Gladstone Investment reported Q1 FY2026 total investment income of $23.5 million, down from $27.5 million in the prior quarter, which had included $4.2 million of non-recurring success fees and dividend income. Adjusted net investment income fell to $8.9 million, or $0.24 per share, from $9.4 million, or $0.26 per share, and NAV decreased to $12.99 per share from $13.55, largely due to a $0.78 per share distribution. Management highlighted a healthy pace of new buyout activity, investing roughly $130 million across three new portfolio companies versus $221 million for all of FY2025, while noting tariff-driven margin pressure and caution on consumer-facing holdings. The monthly distribution was maintained at $0.08 per share, and an elevated spillover of $1.50 per share remains sufficient to cover distributions.

negative_highlights: Company is pre-revenue with approximately $3.8 million in cash and explicitly will need to raise more money, with timing unresolved
India oncology trial abandoned after CDSCO approval due to projected first-patient treatment slipping to early 2026, with cost savings of only $500,000 to $1 million
Second enrolled patient died from cancer progression and provided only 1 week of follow-up data
positive_highlights: Operating expenses fell 32% to approximately $1.8 million from $2.6 million a year earlier, cutting the operating loss by roughly $800,000
All 3 cohort-1 patients completed 4-hour Hemopurifier treatments with no dose-limiting toxicities or device-related serious adverse events, and the DSMB recommended advancing to cohort 2
Preclinical study showed 98.5% removal of platelet-derived extracellular vesicles in simulated 4-hour treatment
summary: Aethlon reported a fiscal Q1 2026 operating loss of approximately $1.8 million, down 32% from $2.6 million a year earlier, with operating expenses also at roughly $1.8 million versus $2.6 million as payroll, legal, and consulting costs fell; cash stood at about $3.8 million as of June 30, 2025. The company completed Hemopurifier treatments for all three patients in cohort 1 of its Australian oncology trial with no dose-limiting toxicities or device-related serious adverse events, and the DSMB context advancing to cohort 2. Aethlon decided not to proceed with its approved India trial because first patient treatment would likely slip to early 2026, expecting to conserve $500,000 to $1 million and avoid a 1-2 year delay; no revenue or guidance figures were disclosed.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to $7.7 million from $5.1 million, and H1 cash used in operations rose to $14.7 million from $11.2 million
R&D expense rose to $5.8 million from $3.9 million and G&A to $2.2 million from $1.7 million year over year
ReMEDy2 interim analysis of the first 200 patients is not expected until Q2 2026, leaving the stroke program without a near-term catalyst
positive_highlights: July private placement of about $30 million lifts pro forma cash to roughly $60 million, extending runway into the second half of 2027
Positive Part 1a preeclampsia interim results showed statistically significant blood pressure reductions, no placental transfer, and a significant reduction in uterine artery pulsatility index
ReMEDy2 stroke enrollment is tracking above the 25% milestone with about 40 sites, and the first DSMB safety review after 50 participants was positive
summary: DiaMedica reported Q2 2025 R&D expenses of $5.8 million (up from $3.9 million) and G&A of $2.2 million (up from $1.7 million), with a net loss of $7.7 million versus $5.1 million a year prior.
