Cash and short-term investments were $30 million at June 30, 2025, down from $44.1 million at year-end 2024, but pro forma for the roughly $30 million July private placement the company cites about $60 million and runway into the second half of 2027. The quarter's substance was clinical: positive interim Part 1a preeclampsia results drove an added Cohort 10 and planned concurrent Part 1b/2/3 cohorts, while the ReMEDy2 stroke interim analysis of the first 200 patients remains guided to Q2 2026 with enrollment past the 25% milestone. No revenue, EPS, or formal financial guidance was reported, as is typical for a clinical-stage company.

negative_highlights: GAAP gross margin declined to 8.8% from 20.6% sequentially due to mix and tariffs
Non-GAAP gross margin fell to 1.4% from 15% sequentially
Revised FY25 non-GAAP operating loss guidance to $24.4-$26.9M on tariffs and mix
positive_highlights: Record Q2 revenue of $18.4M and 135 units delivered
Lowest operating loss since going public at $7.1M
Positive free cash flow of $4.6M, highest in company history
summary: Xos reported record Q2 2025 revenue of $18.4 million on 135 units, up from $5.9 million on 29 units in Q1, and highest quarterly deliveries in history. GAAP gross margin declined to 8.8% from 20.6% last quarter due to product mix and tariffs, but operating loss hit a record low of $7.1 million and free cash flow was positive at $4.6 million. Management reaffirmed FY2025 revenue guidance of $50.2-$65.8 million and unit deliveries of 320-420, but revised non-GAAP operating loss guidance to $24.4-$26.9 million due to mix and tariffs. The convertible note repayment was amended to extend through 2028, and the company highlighted growth in powertrain orders from Blue Bird and increased interest in the MDXT.

negative_highlights: Net sales declined 20% to $9.5 million from $11.9 million, with management citing lost placements and facings at key national retailers
Gross margin fell to 8% from 32%, including $1.6 million of inventory write-offs; even excluding write-offs, 25% was below prior year on higher trade spend
Net loss widened to $6.0 million from $3.2 million and operating cash use rose to $5.0 million from $0.9 million; cash fell to $2.7 million from $10.4 million at year-end
positive_highlights: Functional soda launch amassed over 9,000 points of distribution since April, including Kroger, Giant Carlisle, Hannaford and Duane Reade
Costco approval for Winter Ginger Ale Variety Pack expected to drive 7-figure product sales in second half of 2025
Safeway secured over 25,000 cases of pre-committed secondary displays across more than 500 stores for Q3/early Q4
summary: Net sales fell to $9.5 million from $11.9 million a year ago, driven by lost retail placements and lower volumes with national customers. Gross margin collapsed to 8% from 32%, including $1.6 million of inventory write-offs; excluding write-offs, gross margin was 25%, still below the prior year due to higher trade spend. Net loss widened to $6.0 million (negative $0.13 per share) from $3.2 million (negative $0.77 per share), and modified EBITDA swung to negative $2.9 million from $45,000. Management gave no quantitative guidance, describing a multi-quarter effort to rebuild lost placements and only general expectations of margin recovery to the '30s' and lower delivery costs.

negative_highlights: Hardware revenue was $25 million, only slightly higher than the prior-year quarter.
Organic revenue growth of 20% lagged total revenue growth of 22%, which included a $1.1 million FX benefit.
M&A inorganic revenue contribution fell note weakness in of the prior $25 million expectation, as management stated it will not reach that target.
positive_highlights: Gross margin expanded 400 bps to 48.3% from 44.3%, with hardware margin up to 35.4% from 28.7%.
Total transaction value rose over 34% YoY to nearly $1.6 billion, driving processing revenue up 35% to $43 million.
Adjusted EBITDA increased to nearly $13 million (13% of revenue) from ~$8.5 million, a $4.5 million improvement.
summary: Nayax reported Q2 FY2025 revenue of $96 million, up 22% YoY, with recurring revenue up 32% to $71 million (74% of total) and adjusted EBITDA of nearly $13 million (13% of revenue). Gross margin expanded to 48.3% from 44.3%, driven by higher recurring and hardware margins, while net income was $12 million (including a $5.6 million one-time gain). Full-year 2025 revenue guidance was reaffirmed at $410–$425 million (30–35% growth, at least 25% organic) and adjusted EBITDA at $65–$70 million. The company highlighted new EV partnerships (Autel for 100,000 UNO Minis, Lynkwell) and expects stronger enterprise-driven performance in H2.

negative_highlights: Total revenue declined 5.5% year-over-year to $283.7 million, with comparable traffic down 5.5% and decelerating through the quarter.
Full-year revenue guidance lowered to ~$1.2 billion from $1.21–1.23 billion due to expected same-store sales declines of 3–4% in H2.
Commodity costs, particularly ground beef and poultry, are expected to create a $2–3 million headwind in the back half of 2025.
positive_highlights: Restaurant-level operating margin expanded 270 bps to 14.5% of restaurant revenue, driven by 300 bps of labor efficiency gains.
Adjusted EBITDA increased $8.8 million year-over-year to $22.4 million in Q2.
Debt reduced by ~$20 million in H1 2025, bringing net leverage to ~2.0x trailing EBITDA, ahead of refinancing discussions.
summary: Red Robin's Q2 2025 revenues fell 5.5% year-over-year to $283.7 million, with comparable restaurant sales down 3.2% (price up 4.4%, traffic down 5.5%). Adjusted EBITDA rose sharply to $22.4 million from $13.6 million a year ago, driven by labor efficiency and lower watching expenses, expanding restaurant-level operating margins by 270 basis points. For 2025, management trimmed revenue guidance to ~$1.2 billion from $1.21–1.23 billion, reflecting expectations of continued comparable sales declines of 3–4%, while maintaining adjusted EBITDA guidance of $60–65 million. The company launched the Big Yummm value deal in July and is investing in marketing and restaurant refreshes, but faces higher commodity costs in H2.

AFCG reported Q2 2025 distributable earnings of $3.4 million, or $0.15 per basic share, matching its $0.15 quarterly dividend, alongside a GAAP net loss of $13.2 million ($0.60 per share) driven by a CECL provision that lifted the reserve to $44 million, or 14.6% of loans at carrying value. Net interest income was $6.2 million on $359.6 million of principal across 15 loans, with book value per share of $8.18. The loan to Private Company P (~$16 million principal) was moved to nonaccrual effective June 1, 2025 after a missed July 1 interest payment, and litigation continues with Justice Grown entities. Management announced a proposed conversion from REIT to BDC status (targeted Q1 2026, subject to shareholder vote) plus an expanded mandate into non-cannabis direct lending, while noting the pipeline has declined for several consecutive quarters and it does not plan to issue equity at current trading levels.

negative_highlights: Realized pricing fell meaningfully QoQ for both gas and oil, cutting cash flows roughly 30% quarter-over-quarter
Impairment taken on the Garrington, Alberta JV from D&C cost overruns and early well performance below expectations
~30% of priority PRB inventory sits under a Converse County drilling permit moratorium, and the deal requires a Q4 shareholder vote with ~21-28% dilution
positive_highlights: Acquisition adds ~2,200 net boe/d at 56% oil with a forecasted base decline of ~15% across 168 early-life wellbores
Proved reserves increase over 150% and priority inventory over 600%, with ~75% of the PRB position held by production
Pro forma leverage of approximately 1x with the existing per-share dividend maintained
summary: Q2 production was roughly flat, but realized pricing fell meaningfully quarter-over-quarter for both gas and oil, driving cash flows down roughly 30% QoQ. The quarter was dominated by the announced Peak Companies acquisition in the Powder River Basin: 6 million shares plus ~$49 million of assumed debt (~21% dilution, up to 28% with contingent shares), adding ~2,200 net boe/d (56% oil) and lifting proved reserves over 150% and priority inventory over 600%. Pro forma leverage is ~1x with the revolver ~50% drawn, and the per-share dividend is maintained. A separate impairment was taken on the Garrington, Alberta JV due to drilling/completion cost overruns and early well performance below expectations; Marcellus drilling is expected to restart in 2026.

negative_highlights: Deal activity constrained due to tariff and regulatory uncertainty
NAV per share declined 0.7% sequentially to $19.55
Watch list 14% of portfolio, gap to nonaccruals narrows versus peers
positive_highlights: NII exceeded dividend with 110% base dividend coverage
NAV per share outperformed average public BDC since IPO
Portfolio yield stable at 10.4% and interest coverage improved to 2.1x
summary: CCAP reported Q2 2025 NII of $0.46 per share, or $0.48 excluding $0.02 of one-time accelerated amortization, up from $0.45 in Q1. NAV per share declined 0.4% to $19.55, largely due to a special dividend, with stable portfolio yield at 10.4% and debt-to-equity at 1.23x. Deal activity was constrained, gross deployment was $58 million with net realizations of $35 million, and the company announced a $20 million stock repurchase program. Management noted watch list at 14% of portfolio at fair value, nonaccruals at 2.4%, and no Q3 supplemental dividend.

negative_highlights: Working capital deficit of approximately $12.6 million at the end of Q2.
R&D expenses decreased due to contra-expenses (nondilutive funding) rather than operational efficiency alone.
Technical difficulties prevented a live Q&A session with analysts.
positive_highlights: Received $17.6 million in net proceeds from stock sales and grants after quarter end, significantly strengthening liquidity.
summary: Daré Bioscience reported a working capital deficit of approximately $12.6 million at quarter end but received an additional $17.6 million in net proceeds from stock sales and grants after the period close to strengthen its balance sheet. G&A expenses decreased slightly year-over-year, while R&D expenses dropped 71% due to nondilutive funding awards offset by new development costs for HPV and LARC programs. Management reiterated a Q4 2025 launch timeline for DARE to PLAY Sildenafil cream via a 503B facility but noted technical difficulties prevented the standard Q&A session.

negative_highlights: Revenue flat year-over-year and below expectations
Net loss more than doubled to $15.7 million
Operating expenses jumped to $15.4 million from $9.3 million
positive_highlights: Gross margin expanded to 73% from 64% year-over-year
Full-year guidance reaffirmed at 70-75% revenue growth
CAPTAIN trial fully enrolled with 212 patients; TULSA-AI BPH software on track for Q4 launch
summary: Profound Medical reported Q2 2025 revenue of $2.2 million, flat year-over-year, with a net loss widening to $15.7 million ($0.52/share) from $6.9 million ($0.28/share) in Q2 2024. Total orders were over $3 million, and gross margin improved to 73% from 64%. Management acknowledged revenue was below expectations due to delays in capital sales but reiterated full-year 2025 revenue growth guidance of 70-75% over 2024. Key milestones include full enrollment of the CAPTAIN trial (212 patients) and pilot launch of TULSA-AI BPH software with 60-90 minute procedure times.

negative_highlights: Net income fell to $1.6 million ($0.06 per diluted share) from $1.7 million ($0.07) in Q2 2024
Operating expenses rose 8.5% to $11.6 million, outpacing 5.4% revenue growth, including a $321,000 rise in D&A and $223,000 in personnel costs
Phoenix-area single-family permits fell 14% YoY and Maricopa permits fell 24% in Q2 2025, signaling slowing connection growth
positive_highlights: Revenue increased 5.4% YoY to $14.2 million, driven by 3.8% connection growth, higher consumption and higher rates
Closed Tucson acquisition of 7 public water systems adding ~2,200 connections and ~$7.7 million rate base at 1.05x rate base, with ~$1.5 million expected annual revenue
Adjusted EBITDA rose 2.1% to $6.9 million; ~$6.5 million annual rate increase proposed in pending Santa Cruz/Palo Verde rate case
summary: Q2 2025 revenue rose 5.4% YoY to $14.2 million, but operating expenses grew faster at 8.5% to $11.6 million, and net income fell to $1.6 million ($0.06 per diluted share) from $1.7 million ($0.07) a year earlier. Adjusted EBITDA edged up 2.1% to $6.9 million. Total active connections grew 3.8% to 65,639, while Q2 Phoenix-area single-family permits fell 14% YoY and Maricopa permits fell 24%. Management pointed to a pending ~$6.5 million annual rate increase under ACC review with an expected mid-2026 outcome, and closed the Tucson acquisition of 7 systems (~2,200 connections, ~$7.7 million rate base) subsequent to the quarter.

negative_highlights: No formal guidance provided; management declined to give quarterly revenue guidance
R&D expenses of $1.4 million and SG&A of $1.5 million with net loss implied given revenue of $422,000
Enrollment completion depends on adding 19 more patients, with timeline slipping to late 2025 or early 2026
positive_highlights: Reported Q2 revenue of $422,000 from RenovoCath commercial sales, all from non-trial customers
DMC recommended continuing the Phase III TIGR PACT trial after second interim analysis
Gross margins on the catheter business are 64% and expected to move toward 70-90% as scale increases
summary: RenovoRx reported Q2 2025 revenue of approximately $422,000 from commercial sales of the RenovoCath device. R&D expenses decreased $100,000 year over year to $1.4 million, and SG&A was flat at $1.5 million. The company ended the quarter with $12.3 million in cash and cash equivalents. The independent Data Monitoring Committee context continuing the Phase III TIGR PACT trial following a second interim analysis, with enrollment completion anticipated in late 2025 or early 2026.

negative_highlights: Gross loss widened from a prior period of $0.3 million to $0.8 million due to inventory obsolescence reserves and unapplied manufacturing overhead.
Engineering services revenue declined, falling from $0.5 million in the prior year's period to $0.3 million this quarter.
R&D expenses increased 9% to $2.6 million primarily due to higher external development costs on new products.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 19% year-over-year to $1.3 million driven by increased sales of M400 smart glasses.
Net loss narrowed significantly from a prior period net loss of $40.6 million to $7.7 million due to lower operating expenses and financing proceeds.
Successfully met all manufacturing yield gates for the second Quanta tranche, securing an additional $5 million in equity funding.
summary: Vuzix reported Q2 FY2025 revenue of $1.3 million (up 19% YoY) and a net loss narrowing to $7.7 million from $40.6 million in the prior year period, driven by reduced operating expenses but offset by inventory obsolescence reserves. The company received $5 million in Series B funding from Quanta Computer contingent on meeting manufacturing yield gates, which were successfully exceeded. Management provided a cautious outlook for 2026 regarding OEM ramps with partners like Quanta and highlighted the upcoming Q4 production rollout of the LX1 enterprise smart glasses.

negative_highlights: EBITDA margin fell to 21.6%, well below the typical 28% run rate, due to three one-off items; adjusted EPS was only $0.02.
Oil sands business experienced an abrupt work stoppage in April, causing inefficiencies and lowering second-half margin expectations.
Free cash flow was neutral in the quarter, with net debt rising $29 million to $897 million; sustaining capital spend was elevated due to component issues in Canada.
positive_highlights: Revenue increased 12% YoY to $371 million, with Australia up 7% QoQ and 14% YoY to $168 million, and MacKellar Group set a monthly revenue record in June ($60 million).
Won the largest contract in company history (Queensland coal mine, ~$2 billion) after quarter close, driving record backlog and 100% renewal rate in Australia.
Direct G&A expenses were 3.6% of revenue, below the 4% target.
summary: Q2 2025 revenue rose 12% YoY to $371 million, but EBITDA fell to $80 million (21.6% margin) due to three one-off items: higher subcontractor maintenance costs in Australia, an abrupt oil sands work stoppage, and a Fargo project margin adjustment. Excluding these, EBITDA would have exceeded $100 million with ~27-28% margins. Adjusted EPS was just $0.02. Management reaffirmed second-half revenue and free cash flow expectations but lowered oil sands margin expectations, and expects a strong back half with normalized margins in 2026.

negative_highlights: Total Q3 net loss of $1.5 million on $1.7 million product revenue indicates the business remains unprofitable
FY2026 guidance omitted; management declined to provide an outlook
Trigeminal nerve ablation revenue not included in the operational plan and dependent on pending FDA 510(k) clearance
positive_highlights: Product gross margin raised to 50–53% guidance from 47–51%, versus 31% in FY2024
Product revenue grew 105% YoY to $1.7 million, with nine-month product revenue up 100% to $6.4 million
Net loss improved to $1.5 million ($0.03/share) from $2.8 million ($0.10/share), with $8 million cash, no debt, and funding through at least fiscal 2026
summary: Product revenue rose 105% YoY to $1.7 million in Q3 FY2025, with product gross margin expanding to 53.9% from 34.1% a year earlier. Nine-month product revenue rose 100% to $6.4 million, with net loss improving to $1.5 million ($0.03/share) from $2.8 million ($0.10/share); the company ended the quarter with $8 million in cash, no debt, and a $8.2 million April raise. FY2025 product revenue guidance was reiterated at $8–10 million (+132–190% YoY), while product gross margin guidance was raised to 50–53% from 47–51%. No FY2026 forecast was provided; management is not factoring near-term trigeminal nerve ablation revenue into its operational plan.

negative_highlights: Cash, cash equivalents, and note weakness in-term investments declined from $21.3 million to $13.1 million.
Phase II bird flu study initiation was deferred due to low likelihood of recruiting subjects with H5N1 infections in the U.S.
Company reprioritized programs to focus on note weakness in- and medium-term shareholder value rather than full commercialization timelines.
positive_highlights: Revenue increased significantly to $2.7M from $57k in the prior year period.
Net loss narrowed substantially to $0.9M from a $123.1M loss in Q2 2024 due to the removal of a noncash charge.
Rigosertib demonstrated an 80% overall response rate in a rare disease study.
summary: Traws Pharma reported Q2 FY2025 revenue of $2.7 million, driven by the recognition of deferred revenue from a licensing agreement termination, compared to $57,000 in the prior year period. The company posted a net loss of $0.9 million ($0.11 per share), a significant improvement over the $123.1 million loss in Q2 2024 which included a noncash charge. Management reprioritized clinical plans to accelerate ratutrelvir for COVID while deferring bird flu studies due to low immediate recruitment likelihood, and cash reserves decreased to $13.1 million.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined 27% on a year-over-year basis due to macro headwinds and tariff uncertainty
Mobile gaming revenue was negligible in the first half of 2025, with only non-immersive platform revenue contributing approximately 15%
Q4 adjusted EBITDA positivity remains an expectation rather than a confirmed result
positive_highlights: Gross margin expanded from 40% in the prior year quarter to 44%
Pro forma operating expense decreased by 23% compared to the prior year quarter
East Coast sales revenue increased by 150% through June 30 compared to the first half of 2024
summary: Super League reported Q2 FY2025 revenue growth of 10% sequentially but a decline of 27% year-over-year due to macro headwinds and tariff uncertainty. Gross margin expanded significantly from 40% in the prior year quarter to 44%, supported by cost reductions that lowered pro forma operating expenses by 23%. Management raised guidance for mobile revenue mix targets while noting Q2 was a transition period with restructuring work behind them.

negative_highlights: Full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance was lowered from a midpoint of -$15 million loss to a range of -$69 million to -$39 million loss.
Membership declined by 9% year-over-year due to the intentional rationalization of underperforming payer and provider partnerships.
A single major national payer caused late data delays and quality measure adjustments that negatively impacted Q2 results.
positive_highlights: Normalized medical cost trends remained materially flat YoY despite unit cost increases of 6% to 7%, demonstrating effective operational execution.
Per member funding improved by 10% on a normalized basis, driven by better burden-of-illness documentation and contract renegotiations.
Operating expenses decreased $3 million (13%) compared to the prior year quarter due to strategic workforce rationalization.
summary: P3 Health Partners reported Q2 FY2025 revenue of $356 million (down 6% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA loss of $17 million ($8 million normalized), missing expectations due to a net $9 million in prior period adjustments. Management revised full-year 2025 guidance for an adjusted EBITDA loss range of $39 million to $69 million, citing headwinds from the single underperforming payer and noncore assets while noting that core business fundamentals are stabilizing.

negative_highlights: Net revenue declined sequentially from $6 million to $4 million as the company cycles out of lower-margin CMO business.
Profitability timeline pushed back to first half of 2026 due to delays in state registrations and distribution adoption.
Gross margin remained at a loss of $0.6 million, consistent with Q1.
positive_highlights: Company has begun shipping Pinnacle VLN products with initial stocking orders exceeding 3,000 cartons in August.
Debt reduced by approximately $1 million during the quarter.
Management expressed high confidence regarding the renewal of the MRTP given compliance with the new FDA low nicotine mandate.
summary: Net revenue was $4 million in Q2 FY2025, a sequential decrease from $6 million in Q1, driven by the company's strategic shift away from low-margin CMO volume toward high-margin branded VLN products which are still ramping up. The company reiterated that it expects to achieve profitability in the first half of 2026 due to latent barriers and delays in state registrations for new products. Operating expenses increased to $2.3 million, and the net loss from continuing operations was approximately $3.3 million.

negative_highlights: Total revenue fell 23% YoY to $8 million and subscription revenue dropped 28% to $4.6 million.
Ending ARR fell to $15.9 million from $23.9 million, reflecting $5.8 million and $3.5 million lapsed contracts.
Contract renegotiation with a large retailer may cut up to $3 million in annual revenue, and internal 2025 gift card revenue estimates were lowered.
positive_highlights: Non-GAAP operating expenses fell 37% YoY to $8.9 million from $14 million, and operating expenses dropped 22% to $13.1 million.
Free cash flow usage improved to $5 million from $6.9 million in Q2 last year, or $3.8 million excluding severance and legal costs.
Signed a multiyear European packaging deal expected to generate near 7 figures of ARR starting next year, plus upsell deals with 3 existing Digimarc Validate customers.
summary: Total revenue fell 23% YoY to $8.0 million from $10.4 million, with subscription revenue down 28% and ending ARR dropping to $15.9 million from $23.9 million, though ARR was in line with the original 2025 internal budget. Management lowered its internal 2025 gift card revenue estimate and disclosed ongoing renegotiations with a large retailer that will likely cut up to $3 million in annual revenue. Operating expenses fell 22% to $13.1 million and non-GAAP operating expenses dropped 37% to $8.9 million, with free cash flow usage improving to $5 million from $6.9 million a year ago. Despite the revenue risks, management still expects positive free cash flow by Q4 2025, citing $22 million in annualized cost savings.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to $13.3 million ($1.23/share) from $6.3 million, including $6.6 million of noncash warrant revaluation expense
H1 revenue fell to $9.7 million from $10 million on lower BARDA-funded development revenue
Cash fell to $32.9 million from $43.6 million at year-end 2024, with $11.9 million used to fund operations in H1
positive_highlights: Gross margin expanded to 23.5% from 8.8% on favorable revenue mix
NexoBrid U.S. revenue grew 52% year-over-year per partner Vericel, with hospital orders and ordering centers both up
Awarded an additional $3.6 million in non-dilutive DoD funding, bringing total program funding to $18.2 million
summary: Q2 2025 revenue was $5.7 million, up from $5.1 million in Q2 2024 (and 43% sequentially), while gross margin expanded to 23.5% from 8.8%. Net loss widened to $13.3 million ($1.23/share) from $6.3 million, driven by $6.6 million of noncash warrant revaluation and higher R&D ($3.5 million vs $1.9 million) for the EscharEx VALUE Phase III. H1 revenue slipped to $9.7 million from $10 million due to lower BARDA-funded revenue, and the full-year $24 million revenue guidance was reiterated, with NexoBrid at effectively zero inventory and H2 revenue ramp expected from development services. NexoBrid via Vericel grew 52% YoY in the U.S.; the manufacturing facility commissioning is on track for year-end, with EMA approval expected H1 2026 and FDA H2 2026.

negative_highlights: Sales decreased by $4.7 million in Brazil and $1.2 million with Pfizer due to timing differences.
R&D expenses increased significantly by 100% (or $3 million) year-over-year as the company prepares for a Phase II trial of PRX-115 starting later this year.
Management explicitly warned that current bulk orders from Chiesi are not indicative of end-user demand and may show quarters with no orders due to inventory destocking in early launch phases.
positive_highlights: Revenues from note goods increased 16% year-over-year to $15.4 million, driven primarily by an $8 million increase in sales to Chiesi for Elfabrio.
Cost of goods sold decreased significantly by 38% (or $3.6 million) compared to the prior year period due to lower Pfizer and Brazil volumes.
Net income swung from a loss of approximately $2.2 million in Q2 FY2024 to a profit of approximately $164,000 in Q2 FY2025.
summary: Protalix reported Q2 FY2025 revenues of $15.4 million from watching goods and $0.2 million from license/R&D services, representing a 16% year-over-year increase driven by sales to Chiesi but partially offset by timing-related decreases in Brazil and Pfizer sales. Net income turned positive at approximately $164,000 compared to a loss of $2.2 million last year due to lower cost of goods sold ($5.9M vs $9.5M) and reduced SG&A expenses. Management provided no updated financial guidance for the full year or next quarter; instead, they reiterated long-term royalty expectations exceeding $100 million by 2030 while noting that current bulk orders do not reflect end-user demand due to early-phase inventory destocking.

negative_highlights: Total revenue declined 21% year over year to $1.7 million
Gross margin dropped to 55.5% from 67.2% due to under-absorption
Operating loss widened to $2.9 million from $2.3 million
positive_highlights: Pediatric revenues increased 23% year over year
Back order resolved in first week of July; building finished goods inventory
Reimbursement increase to $1,639 per day supports outpatient heart failure growth
summary: Second-quarter revenue was $1.7 million, down 21% year over year, due to a temporary sterilization vendor back order that has since been resolved. Pediatrics grew 23%, while heart failure and critical care declined 53% and 35%. Gross margin fell to 55.5% from 67.2%, and operating loss widened to $2.9 million. The company terminated REVERSE-HF to reallocate funds and plans a manufacturing transition, while noting progress in outpatient heart failure with improved reimbursement.

negative_highlights: Cash balance $2.3 million, down from $3.3 million at end of 2024
Revenue remains lumpy; no 2025 revenue guidance
Operating expenses still high relative to revenue
positive_highlights: Revenue up 15% in first half year-over-year
First human product revenue recorded (Nu.Q NETs)
Cash used in operations down 30% in first half
summary: VolitionRx reported Q2 2025 revenue of over $400,000, with first-half revenue up 15% year-over-year, including first human product sales (Nu.Q NETs). Operating expenses down 9% in the quarter, and net cash used in operating activities down 30% in the first half. Cash at end of quarter was $2.3 million, with additional $1.2 million from a registered direct offering after quarter end. Management reiterated goal of cash neutrality for the year, dependent on licensing deals, and highlighted progress in over 10 licensing discussions and upcoming interim lung cancer data at ESMO. The tone is optimistic about future milestones but cautious on revenue guidance, noting lumpiness.

negative_highlights: Net earnings before tax fell 14.2% to $1,790,000 from $2,090,000
Cemetery revenue declined 10% to $4,330,000 and cemetery earnings fell to $822,000 from $1,430,000
Interment volumes fell 16.4% (down 65 interments) and the cemetery sales team saw 60% turnover since January
positive_highlights: Funeral home revenue rose 1.2% to $3,260,000, driven by a 3.3% increase in funeral sales average
Cremation families choosing to have a service rose 6.1%
Mortgage margins were increased in Q2 going into Q3, which management expects to lift Q3 revenue on a comparative basis
summary: Security National Financial reported Q2 2025 revenue of $8.14 million, down 1.7% YoY, and net earnings before tax of $1.79 million, down 14.2% from $2.09 million. Funeral home revenue rose 1.2% to $3.26 million on a 3.3% higher sales average, but cemetery revenue fell 10% to $4.33 million and cemetery earnings dropped to $822 thousand from $1.43 million, with interment volumes down 16.4%. No formal guidance was issued; management cited sales-team turnover (60% since January, half of team hired in last six months), cremation mix at 52.8%, and mortgage-side margin and expense actions as the forward focus.

negative_highlights: Net revenue fell to RMB 8.28 million from RMB 24.74 million year over year
Gross result swung to a gross loss of RMB 10.71 million from a gross profit of RMB 30,000
Cash and cash equivalents dropped to RMB 3.06 million from RMB 32.43 million at December 31, 2024
positive_highlights: Net loss narrowed to RMB 11.78 million from RMB 59.15 million a year earlier
Total operating expenses decreased 53.5% to RMB 27.33 million
Company held over 128,000 BNB as of the earnings call date
summary: Nano Labs reported H1 2025 net revenue of RMB 8.28 million (USD 1.16 million), down sharply from RMB 24.74 million a year earlier, on lower Apollo V series sales volume. Gross profit swung to a gross loss of RMB 10.71 million from a small RMB 30,000 profit, driven by inventory write-downs and decreased revenue; total operating expenses fell 53.5% to RMB 27.33 million and net loss narrowed to RMB 11.78 million from RMB 59.15 million, with basic and diluted loss per share of RMB 0.43 versus RMB 8.46. Cash and cash equivalents fell to RMB 3.06 million as of June 30, 2025 from RMB 32.43 million at December 31, 2024. Management gave no formal forward guidance and instead described a strategic shift toward watching BNB reserves (over 128,000 BNB held) and exploring stablecoin and Web3 investments, with 2025 financing plans tied to expanding that reserve.

negative_highlights: Total revenue of $6.7 million fell 13% YoY, or 5% adjusted for discontinued services
Net installed base declined by 1 system to 378 after 7 installs and 8 returns
Q3 revenue guidance of $6.7–$7.2 million implies roughly flat to modest sequential change after a down YoY quarter
positive_highlights: Non-GAAP gross margin expanded to 52% from 35% a year ago
Flowcells sold grew 17% YoY to 7,233, with existing-customer flowcells up 14%
Consumables and software revenue grew 16% YoY and rose to 73% of product mix from 55%
summary: Bionano reported Q2 FY2025 total revenue of $6.7 million, down 13% YoY (or down 5% excluding $700k of prior-year discontinued services), with non-GAAP gross margin expanding to 52% from 35% and non-GAAP operating expenses cut 53% YoY to $8.8 million. Flowcells sold rose 17% YoY to 7,233 and consumables/software grew 16% YoY, while net instrument installations declined by 1 to 378 systems. Management reiterated full-year revenue guidance of $26–$30 million but raised the new OGM installation outlook to 20–25 from 15–20, and guided Q3 revenue to $6.7–$7.2 million, roughly flat sequentially. The quarter showed sharp margin and cost improvement offset by continued revenue decline and net system attrition.

negative_highlights: Q2 net income included a $39.6M unrealized fair value gain on Bitcoin holdings, meaning a large portion of profit was non-operating and tied to BTC price
No formal financial guidance was provided; management offered only qualitative confidence about the second half of 2025
The call was conducted without a Q&A session; questions were directed to email, limiting direct accountability to investors
positive_highlights: Revenue rose 47.9% QoQ to $115.4M from $78M, with cloud mining revenue up 75.6% QoQ to $94.3M
Net income of $47.1M versus $1.3M a year ago and adjusted EBITDA of $60.7M versus $8.3M, driven partly by a $39.6M unrealized fair value gain
Managed mining capacity reached a record 36.2 EH/s (up 46.6% YoY) and hosting capacity 728 MW (up from 522 MW), with July figures further increasing to 38.6 EH/s and 752 MW
summary: Q2 FY2025 total revenue was $115.4M, up 47.9% QoQ from $78M, with cloud mining revenue of $94.3M (+75.6% QoQ, +22.3% YoY) and net income of $47.1M versus $1.3M a year ago, a rebound from Q1 losses. Adjusted EBITDA reached $60.7M vs $8.3M in Q2 2024, and basic/diluted EPS was $0.29/$0.28, though net income included a $39.6M unrealized fair value gain on Bitcoin. Managed mining capacity hit a record 36.2 EH/s (46.6% YoY) and hosting capacity 728 MW (vs 522 MW), with July figures rising to 38.6 EH/s, 752 MW and 629,000+ registered users. No formal numeric guidance was provided; management expressed confidence in continued growth and BTC price appreciation in 2H25.

negative_highlights: Total operating loss widened to EUR 19.9 million from EUR 13.3 million in Q2 2024 on U.S. commercial investment
Cash, cash equivalents and financial assets fell to EUR 43 million at June 30 from EUR 63 million at March 31; EUR 27.5 million term debt drawdown subject to milestones
No quantitative revenue guidance or year-end launch targets provided; VAC decisions can take up to 9 months, with broader payor coverage decisions framed as a 2026 item
positive_highlights: Q2 2025 revenue rose 73.8% YoY to EUR 1.3 million from EUR 800,000, with gross margin essentially flat at 63.4%
FDA PMA approval for Genio; label carries no contraindication for complete concentric collapse (CCC) and includes positional OSA data
Over 100 U.S. physicians trained and several VAC and pre-authorization approvals received in the first week of commercialization
summary: Nyxoah reported Q2 2025 revenue of EUR 1.3 million, up 73.8% YoY from EUR 800,000, with gross margin essentially flat at 63.4% and an operating loss of EUR 19.9 million versus EUR 13.3 million a year ago, driven by U.S. commercial build-out. The quarter's central event was FDA PMA approval of the Genio system, with U.S. commercialization underway, over 100 physicians trained, and early VAC and pre-authorization approvals. Cash stood at EUR 43 million at June 30 versus EUR 63 million at March 31, with EUR 27.5 million available under a term debt facility tied to milestones. Management did not provide quantitative revenue guidance or year-end launch metrics, and SG&A is expected to roughly double in 2026; an Inspire Medical patent lawsuit is being defended.

negative_highlights: Foreign exchange headwinds prevented adjusted EBITDA from exceeding expectations, holding it back to the bottom of guidance.
Full-year revenue guidance was narrowed due to concerns about longer sales cycles impacting solutions revenue growth in H2.
Tariff volatility and elevated China-U.S. tariffs caused a dip in platform transactions on specific lanes during Q2.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 31% year-over-year driven by a 36% increase in Solutions revenue and robust Platform growth exceeding 20% for the fourth consecutive quarter.
Adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed significantly to negative $2.5 million from negative $3.1 million, demonstrating disciplined cost controls despite currency fluctuations.
Secured a major milestone integration with one of the world's largest ocean container carriers, enabling comprehensive contract and spot booking connections.
summary: Freightos reported Q2 FY2025 revenue of $7.4 million (up 31% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA loss narrowing to negative $2.5 million from a prior period loss of negative $3.1 million, beating guidance on transactions, gross booking value, and revenue while staying within EBITDA expectations despite FX headwinds. Management raised full-year Gross Booking Value (GBV) guidance in line with the strength delivered in H1 but narrowed full-year revenue guidance to reflect cautiousness regarding longer sales cycles for solutions. The company reaffirmed its path to breakeven adjusted EBITDA by Q4 2026.

positive_highlights: Net revenues grew 10% sequentially and 33% year-over-year to reach a record quarterly high of $9.7 million.
summary: Fennec reported Q2 FY2025 net revenues of $9.7 million, representing a 33% year-over-year increase and a 10% sequential gain driven by the addition of 14 new accounts and expansion within existing ones. Management highlighted significant commercial momentum with three consecutive quarters of growth but declined to provide specific Q3 guidance or active prescriber counts due to competitive sensitivities. Full-year cash operating expenses are expected to remain consistent at roughly $33-34 million, similar to FY2024.

negative_highlights: Total revenue declined 6% YoY to $3.8 million, primarily due to a $1.7 million drop in VIP enrollment revenue.
Operating loss widened to $4.9 million in Q2, reflecting significant SCN integration costs and lower revenue.
Cash and equivalents stood at $4.4 million with total liabilities of $21.5 million, and the company raised expensive debt/equity financing.
positive_highlights: Sleep testing revenue from SCN generated an immediate $500k uplift in just 20 days post-closing.
Revenue grew 27% sequentially from Q1 to Q2, with management noting a clear growth trajectory.
Management expects each fully operational SO team to generate over $500k in monthly net collections with contribution margins above 50%.
summary: Q2 FY2025 revenue was $3.8 million, down 6% YoY from $4.1 million, with a 27% sequential increase from Q1. Appliance sales fell 5% to $1.9 million, but guide sales offset $500k of a $600k appliance discount impact; sleep testing revenue rose $500k from the Sleep Center of Nevada (SCN) acquisition. Operating loss widened to $4.9 million in Q2, reflecting ~$1.8 million in SCN acquisition and integration costs, with $700k-$800k of non-recurring expenses. Management guided to cash flow positivity in Q4 2025, citing strong patient demand and plans to deploy additional Sleep Optimization teams.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined 57% year-over-year due to the divestiture of the Lori Goldstein brand.
Net loss widened significantly to $4 million in Q2 compared to a net income of $0.2 million in the prior year quarter.
Management expressed caution regarding Q3 and Q4 outlook citing tariff impacts on key licensees including G-III for the Halston brand.
positive_highlights: Retained brands showed year-over-year EBITDA improvement after adjusting for the Lori Goldstein divestiture impact.
New creator influencer brands (Cesar Millan, Gemma Stafford, Jenny Martinez) were launched earlier than expected to accelerate revenue in Q3 and Q4.
Company raised approximately $2.6 million via a combined public equity offering and private placement to strengthen liquidity for new brand launches.
summary: Xcel Brands reported Q2 FY2025 revenue of $1.3 million, a significant decline from $3 million in the prior year quarter, and a net loss of approximately $4 million or -$1.66 per share compared to a net income of $0.2 million in the prior period. The revenue miss was primarily driven by the sale of the Lori Goldstein brand at the end of Q2 2024, which contributed roughly $1.5 million to last year's revenue. Management noted that while retained brands improved year-over-year on an adjusted basis excluding the divestiture, they are approaching Q3 and Q4 with caution due to tariff impacts on licensees like G-III for the Halston brand.

negative_highlights: Loss from operations increased by $800,000 to $8 million compared to Q2 2024.
Net loss attributable to common shareholders increased by approximately $900,000 to $10.4 million.
The global Phase III on-target trial for cancer therapy-related diarrhea did not meet its primary endpoint for all tumor types.
positive_highlights: Combined net revenue of approximately $3 million increased 10% versus Q2 2024 ($2.7 million).
Crofelemer reduced TPN requirements by up to 27% in MVID patients and 12.5% in SBS patients.
Mytesi prescription volume in Q2 2025 was equal to the volume in Q2 2024.
summary: Jaguar Health reported Q2 FY2025 combined net revenue of approximately $3 million, representing a 10% increase year-over-year but missing the implied growth trajectory from Q1's $2.2 million. Operating loss widened to $8 million (up from $7.2 million in Q2 2024) and net loss increased to $10.4 million. Management highlighted significant clinical catalysts, including proof-of-concept data for MVID and breast cancer diarrhea indications, but provided no specific financial guidance or raised expectations.

negative_highlights: Management stated it expects Q3 2025 to slow down significantly versus Q2
Global real estate revenue declined 7% to $4.7 million due to asset monetization, though operating income rose 56% to $1.5 million
Net loss remained at $2.7 million and cash used in operating activities was $6.2 million for the six months, indicating continuing liquidity pressure
positive_highlights: Global revenue rose 29% YoY to $60.4 million and global operating income swung to positive $2.9 million from a $7.7 million loss, the best Q2 operating income since 2019
Global cinema operating income increased 218% to $5.5 million, with U.S. cinema operating income up 152% to $2.3 million
Debt reduction continued with over $102.5 million repaid since June 2020, and the Cannon Park sale for AUD 32 million generated a $1.8 million gain while paying off the AUD 20 million NAB facility
summary: Reading International reported Q2 2025 total revenue of $60.4 million, up 29% YoY, with operating income of $2.9 million versus a $7.7 million loss in Q2 2024, and adjusted EBITDA of $6.3 million versus negative $3.6 million. The quarter was driven by a strong film slate and included a $1.8 million gain on the Cannon Park property sale; net loss narrowed to $2.7 million ($0.12 per share) from $12.8 million ($0.57 per share). Management did not provide quantitative guidance but said it expects Q3 to slow significantly before a strong Q4, and highlighted debt reduction of over $102.5 million since June 2020.

negative_highlights: The company still posted an adjusted EBITDA loss of $5.2 million for the quarter.
Accounts payable was elevated and described as a strategic lever during fleet expansion, a liquidity concern.
A $250 million S-3 shelf and ATM facility were filed, signaling ongoing capital needs.
positive_highlights: Revenue rose nearly 16% year-over-year to $91.3 million despite operating 10 fewer aircraft.
Gross margin expanded to nearly 15%, roughly double last year and up 200 bps sequentially.
Adjusted EBITDA loss improved 67% to $5.2 million, an $11 million positive swing versus Q2 2024.
summary: flyExclusive reported Q2 FY2025 revenue of $91.3 million, up nearly 16% year-over-year and 4% sequentially, with flight hours up 12% to 18,605 on 10 fewer aircraft. Gross margin nearly doubled year-over-year to about 15%, and the adjusted EBITDA loss of $5.2 million improved roughly $11 million versus last year. Management expects positive adjusted EBITDA by the end of 2025 and a strong back half, though no explicit numeric guidance was given and the bottom line remained a loss.

negative_highlights: Asia segment net sales declined by 28% year-over-year with gross margin contraction of 340 basis points due to macro pressures.
Americas segment faced a significant negative impact on revenues since late April as customers paused ordering patterns waiting for tariff clarity.
positive_highlights: Sale of Madison facility generated over $43.3 million in debt principal reduction and is expected to generate over $20 million in annual operating cost savings once transitioned.
summary: Consolidated net sales for Q4 FY2025 were $138.5 million, down 12% year-over-year due to trade uncertainty and tariff impacts in the Americas and Asia segments. Gross profit declined further as it was unfavorably impacted by softer volumes, transition costs of approximately $10.6 million from facility consolidation, and margin headwinds in Brazil and China. Management expects sequential improvement in Q1 FY2026 driven by cost savings and demand normalization.

negative_highlights: Fourth quarter Senior approved MA policies fell 20% year-over-year due to lower agent headcount and SEP changes.
Fiscal 2026 anticipates flat Medicare Advantage volumes and a reversion to more historical agent productivity, which is a dampening factor.
Guidance for Q1 fiscal 2026 includes an adjusted EBITDA loss of $25-$30 million.
positive_highlights: Healthcare Services revenue grew ~55% to $743 million, with segment EBITDA improving to $25 million and Q4 margin of 5.5%.
Senior segment delivered EBITDA margins ~200 bps higher year-over-year despite 8% lower revenue and 26% smaller agent workforce.
Fiscal 2026 guidance includes positive operating cash flow and Healthcare Services EBITDA exceeding $50 million.
summary: SelectQuote reported fiscal 2025 revenue of $1.53 billion, up 15.5%, and adjusted EBITDA of $126 million, up 8%. Healthcare Services revenue grew ~55% to $743 million, with segment EBITDA of $25 million; Senior segment revenue was $600 million with adjusted EBITDA of $162 million. For fiscal 2026, the company guides revenue of $1.65-$1.75 billion (11% growth at midpoint) and adjusted EBITDA of $120-$150 million, while expecting SelectRx EBITDA to exceed $50 million and positive operating cash flow.

negative_highlights: Total revenue of $2.7M still includes $1.5M from the now-divested Singing Machine business that was pressured by tariffs and inflation
The 35% gross margin was driven by one-time inventory-reserve and co-op adjustments; SemiCab's underlying margin is guided to 5%-10% with gross profit near breakeven near term
Management said additional equity financing is expected over the coming quarters to fund SemiCab working capital
positive_highlights: SemiCab revenue run rate grew about 300% to roughly $7M annualized, with fleet expanded from 140 to 450 trucks
Net loss narrowed to $809K from $6.2M and G&A fell to $1.5M from $2.1M year over year
Singing Machine sale for $4.5M reduced liabilities by roughly $4M and lowers ongoing cash burn
summary: Q2 FY2025 revenue rose to $2.7M from $2.4M, split $1.5M Singing Machine and $1.2M SemiCab, with gross margin at 35% versus 13% aided by one-time inventory-reserve and co-op adjustments. Net loss narrowed to $809K from $6.2M, largely on a prior-year $3.9M lease impairment and lower G&A. Management guided SemiCab Q3 revenue to $2M-$2.5M and projected SemiCab's run rate to rise from roughly $7M to $15M-$20M over 12 months, while flagging future gross margin of only 5%-10% and an expectation of continued equity raises for working capital. Singing Machine was sold August 1 for $4.5M total consideration, reducing liabilities by roughly $4M, with it reported as discontinued operations going forward.

negative_highlights: Gross profit fell 58% YoY to USD 70 million and gross margin contracted to 11%
Software license revenue declined 85% YoY to USD 1.2 million
Service revenue dropped 34% YoY to USD 23 million
positive_highlights: Operating expenses reduced 20% YoY to USD 57.2 million
Shipments of Antora-series solutions rose 112% YoY to 135,000 units
Full year volume guidance of 2.5-2.6 million units implies about 30% YoY growth
summary: Q2 FY2025 revenue was USD 156 million, with sales of goods up only 1% YoY to USD 131 million, software license revenue down 85% to USD 1.2 million, and service revenue down 34% to USD 23 million. Gross profit fell 58% YoY to USD 70 million with gross margin of 11%, down roughly 12 points from the prior year, driven by strategic price cuts and a less favorable software mix; adjusted EBITDA loss was USD 30 million versus a USD 29 million loss a year ago. Management guided to full year revenue growth of close to 20% and adjusted EBITDA breakeven in each remaining quarter, and projected H2 volumes of 1.4-1.5 million units (full year 2.5-2.6 million, up about 30%), while noting pricing pressure and macro uncertainty persist. Operating expenses fell 20% YoY to USD 57.2 million, and ECARX holds USD 99 million in cash.

MainStreet Bancshares reported Q2 FY2025 EPS of $0.53, ROA of 0.86%, return on average tangible common equity of 8.84%, and net interest margin of 3.75%. The quarter included $1.5 million in nonrecurring revenue and $1.8 million in nonrecurring expenses, which together reduced EPS by $0.03 from an adjusted $0.56 and ROA from 0.91%. Total funding costs fell 20 bps to 3.29% and noninterest-bearing and low-cost deposits grew $6 million, while noncore deposits were reduced 19%. Management reiterated low single-digit loan growth guidance, expects the margin to hold steady or improve with $152 million in CDs repricing in the second half, and noted it is just over $3 million in buyback capacity with no shares repurchased in the quarter outside the Russell reconstitution.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA down from $34 million to $26.3 million year-over-year
Capital markets income down from $14.6 million to $11.3 million YoY
XBT product net outflows continue, though slowing
positive_highlights: Fee-paying AUM up 26% QoQ to $6.6 billion
CoinShares Physical highest fees on record at $6.8 million
Treasury unrealized gains of $7.8 million
summary: Q2 2025 asset management fees were $30 million, up from $28.3 million in Q2 2024, with adjusted EBITDA of $26.3 million and profit after tax of $32.4 million. Fee-paying AUM rose 26% quarter-over-quarter to $6.6 billion, driven by strong price recovery and $170 million inflows into CoinShares Physical, which offset XBT outflows. The company highlighted positive momentum into H2, including new all-time highs in July and progress on U.S. expansion and product pipeline.

negative_highlights: Gross margin fell about 210 bps YoY to 68.4% on higher markdown mix and full-price promotional rates, plus roughly 50 bps of tariff pressure
Adjusted EBITDA declined to $25.6 million from $30.2 million and adjusted diluted EPS fell to $0.81 from $1.05

Q3 guidance embeds about $5 million of incremental quarterly tariff cost (annualizing near $20 million) versus the prior 10% all-country/30% China assumption, with gross margin expected down more than Q2
positive_highlights: Sales trends improved each month of Q2 and total sales fell only 0.8% YoY to about $154 million despite a soft start to the quarter
Generated $17 million of free cash flow in the quarter, ending with $46 million of cash, and inventory units were flat YoY excluding tariffs after clearing excess markdown goods
Launched ship-from-store across the entire fleet in July, ahead of plan, enabling fulfillment of previously unfulfillable demand
summary: Q2 FY2025 total sales were about $154 million, down 0.8% YoY, with comps down 1% and adjusted EBITDA of $25.6 million versus $30.2 million last year. Gross margin contracted roughly 210 bps to 68.4% on higher markdown mix and about 50 bps of tariff pressure, and adjusted diluted EPS fell to $0.81 from $1.05. Q3 guidance calls for adjusted EBITDA of $18-22 million on roughly flat to low-single-digit lower sales and low-to-mid-single-digit negative comps, with gross margin down more than Q2 due to an assumed ~$5 million quarterly incremental tariff impact (annualizing near $20 million), up sharply from the prior 10% all-country/30% China assumption. Management described sequential monthly improvement, clean inventory exiting the quarter, $17 million of quarterly free cash flow, and strategic investments in assortment, marketing, and new stores, while tariff-driven cost pressure and pricing receptivity remain the key swing factors.

negative_highlights: Total net sales declined 7.1% to $151.3 million and comparable net sales fell 4.5%
Fiscal August e-commerce net sales fell 12.1% due to a vendor distribution decision that removed $1.8 million in net sales
Q3 guidance projects a net loss of $6.9–10.5 million and comparable sales of -2% to +2%, implying possible sequential deterioration from August
positive_highlights: EPS of $0.10 beat the guidance range and marked the first profitable quarter since 2022
Gross margin improved 180 bps to 32.5% and product margin rose 210 bps on higher initial markups and lower markdowns
Total inventory fell 14.5% YoY and fiscal August comps turned positive at +0.9%, a third straight quarter of sequential improvement
summary: Tilly's reported Q2 FY2025 total net sales of $151.3 million, down 7.1% YoY, with comparable net sales down 4.5% (within guidance) and EPS of $0.10, which beat the prior outlook and was the first profitable quarter since 2022. Gross margin expanded 180 bps to 32.5% on 210 bps of product margin improvement and a 14.5% inventory reduction, while SG&A fell $4.4 million YoY. For Q3, guidance implies net sales of $134–140 million, comparable sales of -2% to +2%, and a net loss of $10.5–6.9 million (EPS loss $0.35–$0.23), an improvement over last year's $0.43 loss. Fiscal August comps turned positive at +0.9%, but management noted a $1.8 million e-commerce sales hit from a vendor's distribution decision and expects a typical post-back-to-school slowdown, positioning the low end near the year-to-date -5% pace.

negative_highlights: Q2 adjusted gross margin fell to -5.7%, down 16 points QoQ, on tariffs, competitive pricing and a negative inventory NRV adjustment
$739 million impairment on Polestar 3 assets booked in Q2, driving a GAAP gross margin of -49% for H1
Financial guidance withdrawn entirely; only the 30-35% retail CAGR target was reiterated
positive_highlights: H1 revenue grew 56% YoY to $1.4 billion, with retail sales up 51% to over 30,000 cars, ahead of the 30-35% growth target
Adjusted gross margin turned positive at 1.4% in H1 from -2.6% a year ago, and adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed 30% to $302 million
Carbon credit sales reached $90 million in H1 versus almost none a year earlier, with the $100 million FY target reiterated as reasonably de-risked
summary: Polestar reported H1 2025 revenue up 56% to $1.4 billion and retail sales up 51% to over 30,000 cars, though Q2 adjusted gross margin fell to negative 5.7% from positive 10.3% in Q1. H1 gap GAAP gross margin was negative 49% on a $739 million Polestar 3 impairment tied to new U.S. tariffs and pricing pressure, while adjusted gross margin was +1.4% versus -2.6% a year ago. Management suspended all financial guidance, reiterating only a 30%-35% retail sales CAGR target through 2027, and disclosed $719 million cash at June-end and a $140 million monthly H1 cash burn while raising $200 million in new equity and roughly $2.1 billion in renewed/secured facilities.

negative_highlights: Q4 revenue declined 6.7% and gross margin contracted 290 bps to 35.5%
Adjusted EBITDA swung to a $24.2M Q4 loss from an $8.8M loss a year earlier; FY adjusted EBITDA fell to $29.2M from $93.1M
Net debt rose to $114M from $31M a year ago, and management cited ineffective retention, inefficient marketing, and expenses not coming down with revenue
positive_highlights: Cost reduction plan targeting ~$40M in annualized savings, of which $17M has already been implemented
Tariff headwind now estimated at $15M versus $55M when quantified in May, and most commodities other than cocoa are reverting toward their mean
Customer base of 9.5M with 74% of revenue from existing customers; multi-branded customers are 13% of customers but 29% of revenue
summary: Consolidated Q4 revenue fell 6.7% (Consumer Floral -8.8%, Gourmet Foods -3.6%, BloomNet -0.6%) on a 5.6% transaction decline and 1.6% lower AOV; full-year revenue fell 8%. Q4 gross margin contracted 290 bps to 35.5% on a highly promotional environment and sales deleverage, and adjusted EBITDA swung to a $24.2M loss from $8.8M, with FY adjusted EBITDA of $29.2M versus $93.1M. Management gave no formal FY2026 guidance, framing the year as a transitional 'foundation setting' period, though it noted the cost plan targeting ~$40M in annualized savings and that tariff exposure is now ~$15M versus $55M at the prior call. Net debt rose to $114M from $31M a year ago.

negative_highlights: Comparable sales declined 6.9% and net sales fell 7.7% year over year to $262.8 million
Gross margin contracted 310 basis points to 35.6%, and adjusted EBITDA margin fell 400 basis points to 8.2%
Full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance was updated to $80-$90 million, incorporating up to $10 million in incremental tariff headwinds and $5 million in added marketing spend
positive_highlights: Sub-brands reached 10% of the business this year and are expected to grow to 25-30% of assortment next year, delivering hundreds of basis points higher product margins
SG&A leveraged 20 basis points to 26.8% and was favorable by $6.3 million year over year, driven by store optimization and project prioritization
Customer retention from 2025 store closures is outperforming fiscal 2024 and remains in line with the 60% target
summary: Torrid reported Q2 FY2025 net sales of $262.8 million, down from $284.6 million a year ago, with comparable sales declining 6.9%. Gross margin contracted to 35.6% from 38.7%, adjusted EBITDA fell to $21.5 million (8.2% margin) from $34.6 million (12.2%), and net income was $1.6 million or $0.02 per share versus $8.3 million or $0.08. Management updated full-year net sales guidance to $1.015-$1.030 billion and adjusted EBITDA to $80-$90 million, citing up to $10 million in incremental tariff headwinds and a $5 million increase in marketing spend. The quarter was in line with internal expectations but reflects softer holiday peaks and a more promotional environment than previously anticipated.

negative_highlights: Q1 net sales fell 28.7% year-over-year to $29.7 million
Non-GAAP EPS swung to a loss of $0.26 from $0.06 profit, and adjusted EBITDA swung to a $3.1 million loss from $2 million income
International net sales declined 58.2% and e-commerce declined 35.2% on a large retailer's purchasing changes
positive_highlights: Gross margin expanded 130 basis points to 46.7% despite tariff pressure
Excluding the ~$10 million order pull-forward, Q1 sales would have declined only about 5%, and the traditional channel would have grown about 15%
Debt-free balance sheet with $17.8 million cash and total available capital up to $108 million; $2.5 million of stock repurchased
summary: Q1 FY2026 net sales fell 28.7% year-over-year to $29.7 million, driven by roughly $10 million of retailer orders pulled forward into Q4 FY2025 plus a 35.2% decline in e-commerce; excluding the pull-forward, sales were down about 5% and the traditional channel would have grown roughly 15%. GAAP EPS was a loss of $0.54 versus a $0.18 loss a year earlier, and adjusted EBITDA swung to a loss of $3.1 million from $2 million of income, though gross margin expanded 130 basis points to 46.7%. Management guided Q2 net sales down roughly 15% year-over-year, citing continued measured retailer ordering and tariff uncertainty, and again said it is premature to resume full-year guidance; the company ended the quarter debt-free with $17.8 million in cash and repurchased $2.5 million of stock.

negative_highlights: Net sales declined 7% year over year to $131.7 million, with direct channel sales down 18% excluding wholesale, primarily due to a decline in web traffic
Men's sales declined 8% and women's sales declined 11.3% as promotional depth was reset
Clearance inventory rose to 22% of total from 11% last year due to slower-than-expected spring/summer note-through, though reduced to 16% by September
positive_highlights: Gross margin expanded 240 basis points year over year to 54.7%, driven by an 8% increase in average unit retail and a greater proportion of full-price sales
Adjusted EBITDA increased $1.5 million to $12 million (9.1% of sales), and adjusted EPS improved by $0.05 to $0.03
Inventory decreased 12% year over year to $148.1 million, with store in-stock levels up 200 basis points and net liquidity of $73.3 million
summary: Duluth Trading reported Q2 FY2025 net sales of $131.7 million, down 7% year over year (down 9.8% excluding a wholesale shipment shift), with gross margin expanding 240 basis points to 54.7% and adjusted EPS of $0.03 versus a $0.05 improvement year over year. Adjusted EBITDA rose $1.5 million to $12 million, and inventory fell 12% to $148.1 million, while direct channel sales declined 18% and retail store sales grew 5.3%. Management maintained full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance of $20 million to $25 million, citing a roughly $15 million tariff impact expected primarily in the second half, offset by over $10 million in cost reductions and targeted price increases of 8% in AUR. The key change versus the prior period is the deliberate top-line contraction from the promotional reset, with clearance inventory at 22% versus 11% last year due to slow spring/summer watch-through.

negative_highlights: FY2025 total revenue fell 5% to $88.4M due to prior messaging churn; adjusted EBITDA margin declined to 10% from 12%
FY2025 operating cash flow fell to $5.3M (6% margin) from $12.5M (13% margin)
Messaging product sunset will remove ~$4.7M ARR during FY2026, a headwind to reported growth
positive_highlights: Q4 revenue $23.2M rose 3% YoY, the first YoY increase in eight quarters, with Q4 non-GAAP EPS $0.09 vs $0.08
Knowledge SaaS ARR grew 25% YoY and net retention for knowledge customers improved to 115% from 98%
Board authorized a $20M increase to the buyback, bringing total authorization to $60M; $3.8M repurchased in Q4 at avg $5.97
summary: eGain reported Q4 FY2025 total revenue of $23.2 million, up 3% year over year and 11% sequentially, marking its first YoY revenue increase in eight quarters, with non-GAAP EPS of $0.09 versus $0.08 a year ago. Q4 non-GAAP gross margin was 73% (SaaS gross margin 80%), and adjusted EBITDA margin rose to 19% from 11%. FY2025 revenue fell 5% to $88.4 million primarily due to messaging churn, while knowledge ARR grew 25% YoY to about 60% of total ARR. Management guided FY2026 total revenue to $90.5–$92 million, representing a return to growth, with 20%+ knowledge ARR growth offset by the sunset of the messaging product (approximately $4.7 million of ARR).

negative_highlights: Gross margin worsened sequentially to negative 41% from negative 35% in Q1, driven by higher warranty provision rates; adjusted gross margin declined to negative 20.9% from negative 19.3%
Net loss widened to $812 million (negative 122% margin) from negative 109% in Q1, and operating cash outflow was $463 million
Guidance for operating outflows of $400-600 million per quarter into 2026-2027, with cash burn at 101% of revenue
positive_highlights: EV deliveries rose 172% YoY to 35,837 units and e-scooter deliveries rose 432% YoY to 69,580 units
Revenue grew 92% YoY to $663 million and the company reaffirmed its 2025 target of at least doubling 2024 deliveries
R&D fell 12% YoY to $93 million and SG&A fell 11% YoY to $136 million, with SG&A at 20% of revenue versus 44% a year ago
summary: VinFast reported Q2 FY2025 revenue of $663 million, up 92% YoY but only 2% QoQ, with EV deliveries of 35,837 units (+172% YoY). Reported gross margin was negative 41% versus negative 35% in Q1 and negative 63% a year ago, worsening sequentially on higher warranty provisions; adjusted gross margin was negative 20.9% versus negative 19.3% in Q1. Net loss widened to $812 million (negative 122% margin) from negative 109% in Q1, and adjusted EBITDA was negative $419 million (negative 63% margin). Management reaffirmed the 2025 delivery target of at least 200,000 units and expects operating outflows of $400-600 million per quarter near term, supported by a $4.2 billion liquidity figure that includes $1.6 billion of expected Novatech spin-off proceeds.

negative_highlights: Revenue fell $22.8 million year-over-year to $36.3 million on lower market rates
Daily fleet TCE declined to about $20,700 from $35,200 in Q2 2024
Newly acquired dry bulk vessels were delivered late in Q2 and contributed little to profitability
positive_highlights: Net income rose 13% quarter-over-quarter to $12.8 million, with EPS of $0.36
Fleet expanded by seven dry bulk ships (about 56%), reaching 19 vessels and $350 million book value
Debt-free balance sheet with $212 million in cash and $42 million operating cash flow in H1 2025
summary: Imperial Petroleum reported Q2 2025 revenue of $36.3 million, down $22.8 million year-over-year, with net income of $12.8 million ($0.36 EPS) and EBITDA of $17.1 million. Profitability improved 13% versus Q1 2025 on higher tanker time charter coverage, but daily fleet TCE fell to about $20,700 from $35,200 in Q2 2024. The fleet expanded by seven dry bulk vessels (about 56%) in the quarter, with most delivered late in the period, limiting their contribution. No formal guidance was provided; management expressed cautious optimism for Q3 2025 based on current favorable rates and a debt-free balance sheet with $212 million in cash.

negative_highlights: Net loss of RMB 2.1 billion due to one-off divestiture loss and noncash hedge accounting adjustment.
Cash cost per BTC of $83,091 and all-in cost of $98,636; industry-wide cost pressure expected in Q3.
Effective operational hash rate in August was ~44 EH/s, below the 50 EH/s capacity.
positive_highlights: Scaled to 50 EH/s, ~6% of global hashrate; July production rose 44% to 650.5 BTC.
Adjusted EBITDA of RMB 710.1 million, vs. RMB 5.4 million a year earlier.
Cash and cash equivalents of RMB 843.8 million ($118 million) and BTC holdings exceeding 5,000 BTC.
summary: Cango reported Q2 2025 revenues of RMB 1 billion, with Bitcoin mining contributing RMB 989.4 million from 1,404.4 BTC mined. The company reported a net loss of RMB 2.1 billion due to one-off divestiture and noncash hedge adjustment, but adjusted EBITDA was RMB 710.1 million. Management affirmed scale of 50 EH/s and plans to optimize efficiency via site upgrades and selective M&A, while noting industry-wide cost pressure from rising network hash rate. The company will change reporting currency to USD starting Q3 2025.

negative_highlights: Total net revenue fell to $47.5 million from $63.3 million, and agribusiness revenue declined to $45.9 million from $61.8 million year over year.
Adjusted EBITDA dropped to $3 million from $13.8 million, and the company posted an adjusted diluted loss of $0.02 versus $0.42 income a year earlier.

Avocado revenue fell to $8.5 million on 5.7 million pounds at $1.50/lb versus $13.9 million on 8.9 million pounds at $1.57/lb, and management said FY2026 avocado volume is unlikely to exceed this year.
positive_highlights: Lemon pricing rebounded into August at roughly $23 per carton versus a Q3 average of $17.02, with Spain and Turkey expected to be note weakness in 20–30% next year.
Sunkist citrus sales and marketing partnership on track for about $5 million in annual cost savings and EBITDA improvement starting FY2026.
Real estate pipeline expected to deliver approximately $155 million in distributions over the next five fiscal years, plus the newly announced 221-acre Limco Del Mar development option.
summary: Q3 FY2025 total net revenue fell to $47.5 million from $63.3 million a year earlier, with agribusiness revenue down to $45.9 million from $61.8 million, driven by lemon pricing pressure in the first two months and lower fresh utilization. The company swung to a net loss per diluted share of $0.06 from EPS of $0.35, adjusted diluted EPS of -$0.02 from $0.42, and adjusted EBITDA of $3 million from $13.8 million. Management held FY2025 volume guidance (4.5–5 million lemon cartons, ~7 million pounds of avocados) and pointed to FY2026 normalization, an expected $5 million annual EBITDA benefit from the Sunkist partnership, ~$155 million of real estate distributions over five fiscal years, and 700 nonbearing avocado acres maturing over 2–4 years. Lemon prices improved in August to around $23 per carton and Spain/Turkey supply shortages of 20–30% are expected to support FY2026 pricing.

negative_highlights: Reported Q4 EPS was a $0.40 loss and adjusted EBITDA was negative $4.8M, with the four charges cutting EPS by $0.53 and adjusted EBITDA by $11.5M
Revenue of $216.4M came in just below the implied Q4 guidance range, depressed by the $6.4M legacy contract recovery reduction
Storage and Terminal Solutions gross margin swung to negative 1.1% from positive 3.1% on labor productivity issues and the legacy charge
positive_highlights: Backlog held near a record $1.4 billion, with 85% of FY2026 planned revenue already booked and nearly all of it on projects already underway
Under-recovery of construction overhead fell from 620 bps in Q1 to 160 bps in Q4, and SG&A leverage improved from 11.2% to 8.1% of revenue
Utility and Power Infrastructure revenue rose 12% to $73M with gross margin up 490 bps to 9.1%, and segment book-to-bill was 1.7 on $121.9M of awards
summary: Matrix reported Q4 FY2025 revenue of $216.4 million, a GAAP EPS loss of $0.40 and adjusted EBITDA of negative $4.8 million, with four charges (a $6.4M legacy contract recovery cut, $3.8M crude project productivity charge, $1.3M adverse court ruling, $3.4M restructuring) subtracting $0.53 from EPS and $11.5M from adjusted EBITDA. Revenue fell just below the implied Q4 guidance range but came in 31% above the start of the fiscal year, and the quarter's awards totaled $186.3M for a 0.9 book-to-bill, leaving backlog near $1.4 billion. Management guided FY2026 revenue to $875-$925 million, roughly 17% growth at the midpoint, with ~85% of forecast revenue already in backlog, and expects a return to profitability as the year progresses. Versus the prior quarter, the legacy charge and restructuring costs widened the loss even as underlying direct margins stayed double-digit and construction overhead under-recovery narrowed from 620 bps in Q1 to 160 bps in Q4.

negative_highlights: Total revenue declined 1.1% year-over-year
Gross margins contracted (GAAP 34.2% vs 35.3% prior year)
Material weaknesses in controlled environment identified
positive_highlights: Record adjusted EBITDA for third consecutive quarter
Backlog up 11% year-over-year to $323 million
Tariffs minimal impact due to mitigation, moved $1.5 million supply purchases from China
summary: Aviat Networks reported Q4 FY2025 revenue of $115.3 million, down 1.1% year-over-year, with non-GAAP EPS of $0.83 (up 15.3%) and record adjusted EBITDA of $15.1 million, up 26.7%. Backlog rose 11% to $323 million. Fiscal 2026 guidance implies roughly 4% revenue growth at the midpoint, with management citing conservatism due to lumpy project demand; they also disclosed material weaknesses in internal controls.

negative_highlights: Wholesale fell 5.1% as fall shipments were delayed ~3 weeks by tariff-related supply chain recalibration, pushing total sales down 1.3%
Q3 adjusted EBITDA margin guided to 2%-5% versus 9.2% in the prior-year period
Net inventory rose to $76.7 million from $66.3 million, including ~$5.2 million from higher tariff-related carrying value
positive_highlights: Gross margin expanded 300 bps YoY to 50.4%, aided by ~340 bps from lower product costing/higher pricing and ~210 bps from lower discounting
Direct-to-consumer rose 5.5% with both e-commerce and stores contributing; adjusted EBITDA more than doubled to $6.7 million from $2.7 million
summary: Vince reported Q2 FY2025 net sales of $73.2 million, down 1.3% YoY, with DTC up 5.5% offset by a 5.1% wholesale decline due to roughly 3-week fall shipping delays from tariff mitigation. Gross margin expanded 300 bps to 50.4% and adjusted net income was $4.9 million or $0.38 per share, with adjusted EBITDA of $6.7 million versus $2.7 million a year ago, helped by $7.2 million in ERC payments. Q3 guidance calls for net sales roughly flat to up low single digits, operating margin of 1%-4% and adjusted EBITDA margin of 2%-5%, well below the prior-year 9.2% EBITDA margin, reflecting reinvestment and $4-$5 million of incremental tariff costs about half of which management expects to mitigate.

negative_highlights: Q4 net revenue declined to $227.8 million from $236.9 million year-over-year.
Full-year revenue fell to $1.06 billion from $1.1 billion, which management attributed to product mix shift.
Management cited China tariffs on Handmade by Robots manufacturing and price increases on certain collectibles affecting consumer demand.
positive_highlights: Q4 gross margin expanded to 15.8% from 11.4%, with gross profit up 34% to $36 million.
Full-year net income rose 229% to $15.1 million and adjusted EBITDA grew 51% to $36.5 million.
Revolver debt reduced 22% and operating cash flow reached $26.8 million; multiple exclusive partnerships and the Walmart video category adviser role were cited as growth drivers.
summary: Alliance Entertainment reported Q4 FY2025 net revenue of $227.8 million, down from $236.9 million a year earlier, but gross profit rose 34% to $36 million with gross margin expanding to 15.8% from 11.4%. Q4 net income was $5.8 million, or $0.11 per diluted share, versus $0.05 a year ago, and adjusted EBITDA grew nearly fivefold to $12.2 million. For the full year, revenue was $1.06 billion versus $1.1 billion, net income rose 229% to $15.1 million ($0.30 per share) and adjusted EBITDA grew 51% to $36.5 million. Management said the margin gains are structural, called them sustainable into fiscal 2026, and pointed to the Walmart video category adviser role, the Paramount catalog license, Handmade by Robots and an AI initiative, while giving no explicit numeric fiscal 2026 guidance.

negative_highlights: Group reported a net loss for the quarter due to non-cash charges including ZAR 335 million in goodwill impairments and ZAR 101 million loss on MobiKwik disposal.
Enterprise division revenue declined 9% YoY as the company closed down non-core business units during restructuring.
Net debt to adjusted EBITDA increased to 2.9x at year-end, though annualized Q4 leverage is 2.2x.
positive_highlights: Consumer division delivered standout performance with net revenue growing 35% to ZAR 1.7 billion and EBITDA up 83% to ZAR 435 million.
Merchant division achieved 46% revenue growth to ZAR 3 billion, aided by the inclusion of Adumo and a sequential margin expansion from 19% in Q3 to 23% in Q4.
Enterprise division adjusted EBITDA increased 66% to ZAR 24 million following restructuring and full-quarter contribution from Recharger.
summary: Lesaka reported Q4 FY2025 net revenue of ZAR 1.5 billion (up 47% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of ZAR 306 million (up 61% YoY), driven by the Consumer division's 106% growth and full-quarter contributions from Adumo and Recharger acquisitions. The quarter included significant non-cash charges, including ZAR 335 million in goodwill impairments and ZAR 239 million in transaction costs, resulting in a net loss despite strong underlying operating performance. Management confirmed FY2026 guidance excludes the pending Bank Zero acquisition and expects EBITDA growth of approximately 46% YoY.

negative_highlights: Net sales declined to $50.7 million from $56.5 million a year ago despite an extra week in the quarter
Upholstery segment sales fell approximately 20% to $22.6 million from $28.5 million on soft residential demand and a tariff-driven pause in China shipments
Non-GAAP operating loss of $1.9 million and adjusted EBITDA of negative $1.1 million, with Q2 guided only to near breakeven to slightly positive
positive_highlights: Gross margin expanded 530 basis points year over year to 14.3% on gross profit of $7.2 million versus $5.1 million
Bedding segment swung to a 10.5% gross margin ($2.9 million) from negative 1.2% (-$326,000) in the prior-year period
New restructuring and integration actions plus price increases expected to generate at least $6 million in annualized cost and efficiency benefits
summary: Culp reported Q1 FY2026 net sales of $50.7 million (with an extra week) versus $56.5 million a year ago, gross profit of $7.2 million (14.3% margin) versus $5.1 million (9.0%), and a net loss of $231,000 or $0.02 per diluted share versus a $7.3 million loss ($0.58) last year; non-GAAP operating loss narrowed to $1.9 million from $4.1 million and adjusted EBITDA was negative $1.1 million. Upholstery segment sales fell about 20% to $22.6 million while bedding sales were roughly flat at $28.0 million but swung to 10.5% gross margin from negative 1.2%. Management gave only limited guidance, citing macroeconomic and tariff uncertainty, but expects sequential sales growth through fiscal 2026 and Q2 adjusted EBITDA from near breakeven to slightly positive, supported by at least $6 million of new annualized cost/efficiency actions plus $10-11 million from prior restructuring. The key change versus the prior period is the bedding segment returning to double-digit gross margin and the overall swing to a small operating profit, offset by a softer upholstery top line and weak demand.

negative_highlights: Fintech vertical revenue share decreased to 10.6% as exposure declined from 13.7%.
Nearshore region revenue contracted by 3%, shifting business volume to offshore locations.
Adjusted EBITDA margin ticked down slightly in the full year due to increased SG&A expenses related to India expansion and Workday implementation.
positive_highlights: Q4 revenue surged to a record $147.1 million, representing an 18% year-over-year increase.
Full fiscal year adjusted EPS hit a new high of $2.75, up 31% from the prior year.
Free cash flow reached a quarterly record of $23 million in Q4 and $27.3 million for the full year.
summary: IBEX reported record Q4 FY2025 revenue of $147.1 million (up 18% YoY) and full-year revenue of $558.3 million (up 9.8%).
