Adjusted EPS reached a record $2.75 for the year, with adjusted EBITDA hitting $72 million. Management provided FY2026 guidance expecting revenue between $590M-$610M and Q1 FY2026 revenue of $143M-$146M.

negative_highlights: Revenue fell approximately 25% to $70.9 million from $94 million with indirect segment down 52.5%
Comparable sales declined 17.3% on conversion declines across full-line, outlet, and e-commerce channels
Swung to a net loss of $0.02 per diluted share from $0.09 income, with no guidance provided
positive_highlights: Gross margin held roughly flat at 49.9% versus 49.8% last year despite the revenue decline
SG&A expense fell $7.3 million to $36.3 million due to restructuring and lower headcount
New customer acquisition on vb.com rose 23% and Instagram followers gained in six weeks exceeded the prior twelve-month total
summary: Vera Bradley reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $70.9 million, down approximately 25% from $94 million, with a net loss of $0.02 per diluted share versus $0.09 income last year. Direct segment revenue fell 16.2% with comparable sales down 17.3% on conversion declines, and indirect revenue dropped 52.5% on lower key-account orders and liquidation sales. Gross margin was roughly flat at 49.9%, while SG&A fell $7.3 million to 51.2% of revenue on restructuring and lower ad spend. The company did not provide guidance, citing its transformation and a dynamic consumer environment, and disclosed an estimated $11 million annualized tariff impact it aims to offset over time. Management highlighted sequential comp and gross margin improvement, early product wins, and new marketing engagement metrics.

negative_highlights: Gross margin fell to 30.0% from 41.1% in Q2 2024, driven by higher revenue share costs as a percentage of revenue and higher fulfillment costs
Adjusted EBITDA dropped to $3.6 million (4.4% of revenue) from $13.7 million (17.4%) a year ago
Free cash flow worsened to negative $26.5 million from negative $4.5 million, and FY2025 free cash flow guidance is now below negative $40 million on recapitalization costs
positive_highlights: Ending Active Subscribers rose 13.4% YoY to 146,373, accelerating from 0.9% in Q1 2025 and negative 4.9% in Q4 2024
Recapitalization cuts total debt from over $340 million to approximately $120 million and extends maturity to 2029
Subscription prices increased effective August 1, with the 2-Swap plan up 14% to $164/month, and impact so far in line with expectations
summary: Rent the Runway reported Q2 2025 revenue of $80.9 million, up 2.5% YoY and 16.2% QoQ, with Ending Active Subscribers up 13.4% YoY to 146,373. Gross margin contracted sharply to 30.0% from 41.1% a year ago on higher revenue share and fulfillment costs, and adjusted EBITDA fell to $3.6 million (4.4% of revenue) from $13.7 million (17.4%). Free cash flow was negative $26.5 million versus negative $4.5 million a year ago. Q3 guidance is revenue of $82-84 million with adjusted EBITDA margin of -2% to 2%; FY2025 free cash flow is now expected below negative $40 million due to recapitalization costs. The company also announced an August 21 recapitalization reducing total debt from over $340 million to about $120 million with maturity extended to 2029, and raised subscription prices about 14% on its most popular plan effective August 1.

negative_highlights: Organic net sales declined 11% in Q4, with adjusted EPS swinging to a $0.02 loss from $0.13 income a year ago.
Adjusted gross margin fell approximately 290 bps to 20.5%, and adjusted EBITDA halved to $20 million from $40 million.
Free cash flow was an outflow of $9 million versus $31 million generated a year ago, while net debt stood at $650 million and leverage rose to 4.7x.
positive_highlights: International remained a bright spot with market share gains across the total U.K. business and 13.3% adjusted EBITDA margin.
Days payable outstanding improved to 65 days from 37 days in FY2023, progressing toward the 70-plus day goal.
Pricing actions were implemented across most of the portfolio, including successful Q4 pricing in International, augmented by retailer acceptance of August pricing in tea, baby and kids categories.
summary: Hain reported Q4 FY2025 organic net sales down 11% year-over-year, with volume/mix down 11 points and flat pricing; adjusted gross margin fell ~290 bps to 20.5%, adjusted EBITDA dropped to $20 million from $40 million (5.5% margin), and adjusted EPS was a loss of $0.02 versus income of $0.13 a year ago. North America organic sales fell 14% and International fell 6%; free cash flow was an outflow of $9 million, net debt ended at $650 million, and leverage rose to 4.7x. Management provided no numeric FY2026 guidance, citing the ongoing strategic review, but said Q1 net sales and adjusted EBITDA should look similar to Q4 2025, with stronger second-half performance and positive full-year free cash flow. The company raised its restructuring charge estimate to $100–$110 million, is eliminating the North America President role, and is committing to an incremental 12% reduction in people-related SG&A with $60 million-plus in FY2026 productivity.

negative_highlights: Q4 adjusted EBITDA declined 13.1% year over year to $7.890 million.
Q4 adjusted net income fell 21.3% year over year to $5.485 million.
Management expects continued near-term volatility from U.S. trade and tariff negotiations and a muted peak season.
positive_highlights: Full-year adjusted EBITDA grew 24.4% to $38.756 million, up $7.6 million year over year, driven by acquisitions.
Full-year net income attributable to Radiant rose 125% to $17.291 million, or $0.37 per basic share.
Strong balance sheet with approximately $23 million cash and only $20 million drawn on a $200 million credit facility.
summary: Radiant reported Q4 FY2025 revenue of $220.6 million versus $206 million a year ago, with net income of $4.907 million, or $0.10 per diluted share, roughly flat versus $4.781 million last year. However, adjusted EBITDA fell 13.1% to $7.890 million and adjusted net income declined 21.3% to $5.485 million, which management attributed to the absence of prior-period tariff pull-forward activity. Full-year revenue rose to $902.7 million and adjusted EBITDA grew 24.4% to $38.756 million, driven mainly by acquisitions, while the company noted near-term volatility from ongoing tariff negotiations and a muted peak season.

negative_highlights: Total revenue decreased by 4.4% to USD 255.2 million due to declining marine fuel prices.
The company reported a net loss of USD 0.99 million for the period.
Geopolitical tensions and Red Sea disruptions caused route diversions that added volatility, though demand was captured in alternative corridors.
positive_highlights: Sales volume increased by 9.8% year-over-year despite challenging macroeconomic conditions.
Net loss narrowed significantly by 38.8% compared to the prior period.
Biofuel sales surged 154.7% year-over-year with volume growth of 189.5%.
summary: CBL International reported first-half 2025 revenue of USD 255.2 million, a 4.4% decrease year-over-year, while sales volume grew by 9.8%. Management highlighted strength in defense and aerospace, progress on cost-saving initiatives, and continued softness in clean energy and automotive.

Q4 normalized FFO guidance of $0.27-$0.29 per share excludes incentive fees, with management noting a full-year incentive fee of $6.3 million would imply under $2 million recorded and paid in January 2026. Three properties are held for sale for roughly $55 million expected to close in Q4 and early 2026, with a $6.1 million impairment taken on one vacant asset.

EAD was $1.01 per share versus $0.04 in Q2, with the $1.30 increase driven by the sale gain, partly offset by a $0.37 decline from real estate operations (a $2.8 million loss including $2 million of exit and accelerated costs). GAAP book value rose to $29.63 from $27.93, and leverage fell to 2.7x from 3.0x. The loan portfolio fell a net $46.8 million to $1.4 billion, but management expects substantial Q4 closings and positive full-year growth, with a CLO targeted for Q1 2026 and a return to book value near $30 and a dividend once the remaining three properties are sold.

summary: FLWS reported Q1 FY2026 consolidated revenue down 11.1%, with Consumer Floral and Gift down 14.6%, Gourmet Foods and Gift Baskets down 8.6%, and BloomNet roughly flat. Gross margin contracted 240 bps to 35.7%, and adjusted EBITDA loss widened to $32.9 million from a $27.9 million loss a year ago. Management framed the weakness as largely a strategic consequence of shifting marketing toward contribution margin rather than top-line revenue, and said that after adjusting for $3-4 million of wholesale order timing, adjusted EBITDA trend was slightly positive -- the first year-over-year improvement in seven quarters. No formal revenue or EPS guidance was provided, but management newly identified an incremental $50 million in run-rate cost savings to be split roughly half in fiscal 2026 and half in fiscal 2027.

Marine segment faced temporary market softness but recovered by September/October, while onshore performed as expected. Management expects continued growth and free cash flow, with debt reduction and capital returns as priorities.

FRE margins were 48%, above last year's record 46%, and the firm repurchased over $200 million of stock.
