Annualized net charge-offs fell to 1.24% in Q3 from 2.6% in Q2
More than 84% of deposits were FDIC-insured at September 30, 2025
summary: BayFirst reported a Q3 FY2025 net loss of $18.9 million versus a $1.2 million loss in Q2, driven by a $7.3 million restructuring charge and a $5.1 million discount on the SBA 7(a) portfolio being sold to Banesco USA. Net interest margin fell 45 bps to 3.61%, noninterest income was negative $1 million versus $10.8 million in Q2 as gain-on-sale revenue ceased, and the provision for credit losses rose to $10.9 million from $7.3 million. Management guided to a return to profitability with 40 to 70 basis points ROA in 2026 once restructuring completes, and expects the Banesco transaction close to be delayed by the federal government shutdown. The company is exiting SBA 7(a) lending entirely and retaining approximately $167 million of unguaranteed SBA balances to watch down over time.

negative_highlights: Revenue missed guidance range by $3-$13 million, with adjusted EBITDA of only $9.6 million.
Sequential revenue declines across all segments: cementing -6%, wireline -15%, completion tools -16%, coiled tubing -7%.
Borrowing base reductions of $2.2 million per month expected from October through January 2026 due to lower inventory appraised values.
positive_highlights: International revenue grew approximately 19% in the first 9 months of 2025 versus the same period in 2024.
Completed a landmark cementing job in the Haynesville with a latex-based slurry, showcasing operational capability.
Full year CapEx budget unchanged at $15-$25 million, likely at the lower end.
summary: Q3 FY2025 revenue was $132 million, below the guidance range of $135-$145 million, with adjusted EBITDA of $9.6 million. Activity and pricing pressure drove sequential revenue declines across all segments, with completion tools down 16% and wireline down 15% YoY or sequentially. The company guided Q4 revenue to $122-$132 million, implying further sequential decline, and noted borrowing base reductions due to lower inventory values. International revenue grew 19% for the first nine months, a bright spot.

negative_highlights: European and APAC volumes down 2.5%, with lower sales environment hurting cash forecast
Year-end cash balance guidance lowered to $65-$70M
Cushioning sales in North America down year-over-year
positive_highlights: Automation revenue up 56% constant currency, on track for $40-45M full-year
North America revenue up 10.9% with automation up 140%
Walmart and Medline partnerships expected to drive significant future growth
summary: Ranpak reported Q3 2025 net revenue growth of 4.4% constant currency, with North America up 10.9% and automation up 56% constant currency, offset by volume declines in Europe and APAC. The company announced a strategic Walmart partnership with up to $300 million in potential spend over 10 years and a Medline enterprise agreement for up to 14 distribution centers. Full-year automation guidance maintained at $40-$45 million. Adjusted EBITDA grew 3.5% constant currency, gross margin improved to 34.5%, and net leverage was 4.4x LTM. Year-end cash forecast lowered to $65-$70 million, and long-term targets include $800 million revenue in 5 years with automation at 15% and >25% EBITDA margin.

negative_highlights: Production impacted by Ecuador landslide and Moqueta trunk line repairs, leading to lower-end guidance
Net debt approximately $755 million, a market overhang
2025 capital program includes $150M for exploration and facility expansion, limiting near-term FCF
positive_highlights: Production up 30% YoY to 42,685 BOE/d
Record Ecuador production: >5,000 bopd in August, >6,000 bopd in early October
Cohembi waterflood response: north area production up 135% to 6,700 bopd
summary: Gran Tierra's Q3 2025 production averaged 42,685 BOE/d, up 30% YoY, but was temporarily impacted by external events including an Ecuador landslide and Moqueta trunk line repairs, leading to a forecast at the lower end of production guidance. Current production is recovering at 45,200 BOE/d, with an expected exit rate of 47,000-50,000 BOE/d. Operating cash flow was $48 million, up 39% from Q2, and the company secured $150 million prepayment facility and extended Canadian credit facility. Management expects a strong finish and plans a 2026 budget focused on free cash flow and deleveraging.

negative_highlights: Active earning OPTAVIA coaches decreased by 35% year-over-year to approximately 19,500.
Gross profit margin decreased 590 basis points due to loss of leverage on fixed costs and a reformulation reserve.
Loss from operations widened to $4.1 million compared to income of $2.1 million in the prior year period.
positive_highlights: Revenue of $89.4 million was at the high end of the company's guidance range.
EPS of a $0.21 loss per share came in within the guided range of -$0.70 to -$1.25.
The new Premier+ pricing and auto ship program showed an uptick in baseline client retention beyond the first month.
summary: Third quarter revenue of $89.4 million decreased 36.2% year-over-year due to a decline in active earning coaches, while EPS was a loss of $0.21 per share. Gross margin contracted by 590 basis points to 69.5%, driven by lower sales volume leverage and a one-time reformulation reserve. Management provided Q4 guidance for revenue between $65 million and $80 million and expects continued pressure on client acquisition.

negative_highlights: Software license revenue fell 92% YoY to $0.9 million due to lower per-vehicle and IP licensing revenue
Cash and restricted cash stood at only $50 million as of quarter end, though a $150 million convertible note was raised after the period
Q1 2026 expected to be seasonally weaker, with no specific volume or revenue guidance provided for 2026
positive_highlights: Achieved first net profit of $0.9 million and adjusted EBITDA of $8.3 million, versus a $32 million loss a year ago
Gross margin expanded to 22% from 18% YoY and 11% QoQ, with hardware margins at 15%
Second project win with a leading European automaker added $400 million in lifetime revenue, bringing overseas pipeline to over $2.5 billion
summary: ECARX reported Q3 FY2025 revenue of $219.9 million, up 11% YoY and 41% QoQ, with gross margin of 22% (up 4 points YoY and 11% QoQ) and its first net profit of $0.9 million and adjusted EBITDA of $8.3 million. Shipments reached 667,000 units, up 51% YoY, and ASP rose 9% sequentially on the Pikes platform and service revenue growth. Guidance implies Q4 revenue and volume at historical highs, maintaining profitability and double-digit 2025 revenue growth, though Q1 2026 is expected to be seasonally softer. The quarter marks a turnaround to profitability, aided by a second European OEM win adding $400 million in lifetime revenue and total overseas pipeline reaching $2.5 billion.

negative_highlights: Gross margin contracted to 21.7% from 33.9%, and consolidated gross profit fell 21% to $30 million
Adjusted EBITDA fell 40% to $8.2 million and diluted EPS declined to $0.26 from $0.38 as electricity cost per kWh rose 20% and gas cost per therm rose 137%
Full-year Adjusted EBITDA guidance now expected at the low end of the $40M-$50M range, and gas gross margins turned negative on a winter supply mark-to-market
positive_highlights: Revenue rose 24% to a record Q3 $138.3 million, with GRE electricity revenue up 26% on a 21% increase in kWh sold
Electricity RCEs grew 5.4% YoY to approximately 318,000 and total RCEs rose 4.2% to 396,000
Diversegy brokerage grew revenue, gross profit and profitability for a third straight quarter and is expected to contribute $5M-$6M in 2026, double this year
summary: Genie Energy reported record Q3 revenue of $138.3 million, up 24% YoY, but consolidated gross profit fell 21% to $30 million with gross margin contracting from 33.9% to 21.7%. Adjusted EBITDA dropped 40% to $8.2 million and diluted EPS fell to $0.26 from $0.38 as GRE electricity costs per kWh rose 20% and gas costs per therm jumped 137%, turning gas gross margins negative. Management said full-year 2025 Adjusted EBITDA will land at the low end of its $40M-$50M range and cited early Q4 indications that margin conditions are improving into 2026.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened slightly year-over-year despite improved adjusted EBITDA, reflecting continued investment in clinical studies and sales expansion.
Accounts receivable increased by $5.2 million due to timing differences on higher revenue volumes rather than collection issues.
Management noted disappointment regarding the HEDIS measures not being pushed out as hoped.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 20% YoY with gross margins expanding 400 bps to 81% despite supply cost pressures.
Primary care adoption of Nodify testing increased from 4% prior to the pilot to 11% in September, driving a 75% growth in tests ordered from this segment.
Development services revenue surged 97% YoY to $1.9 million with an all-time high contract backlog of $12.9 million.
summary: Biodesix reported Q3 FY2025 revenue of $21.8 million, a 20% year-over-year increase driven by lung diagnostic testing (up 16%) and development services (up 97%). Gross margins expanded to 81%, up 400 basis points from the prior year quarter. Management raised full-year 2025 revenue guidance to $84-$86 million, citing strong momentum entering Q4.

ISG Q3 FY2025 revenue was $62.4M, up 8% organically (excluding ~$3.5M from divested automation unit), with Americas up 11% to $42.2M, Europe up 7% to $16M (first growth in two years), and APAC down 15% to $4.2M. Adjusted EBITDA rose 19% to $8.4M with margin up ~200 bps to 13.5%, adjusted EPS was $0.09 vs $0.05 a year ago, and operating cash flow was $11.1M. Q4 guidance targets revenue of $60.5-61.5M and adjusted EBITDA up 15-20% to $7.5-8.5M; AI-related revenue reached $20M, roughly 4x a year ago. Gross debt-to-EBITDA fell to 1.95x from 2.4x at year-end, with $2.8M of buybacks and $2.4M of dividends paid.

negative_highlights: Revenue fell 7% YoY to $138 million and EPS dropped to $0.18 from $0.33, with net income down to $2.7 million from $5.4 million
Gross margin contracted to 38.3% from 40.4%, with Branded down 140 bps on customer mix and Healthcare down from a 41.8% peak
All three segments declined YoY, including a 9% drop in Contact Centers where a solar customer loss is ~$2 million annualized
positive_highlights: SG&A reduced $3.9-4 million YoY (7%) with declines in all three segments, and Q2 cost actions now fully executed against a $13 million annualized target
Guidance range tightened to $560-570 million from $550-575 million, raising the midpoint to imply slight growth at the high end
EBITDA improved sequentially to $7.5 million from $6.1 million in Q2
summary: SGC reported Q3 revenue of $138 million, down 7% YoY, with EPS of $0.18 versus $0.33 a year ago and net income of $2.7 million versus $5.4 million. Gross margin fell to 38.3% from 40.4%, while SG&A was cut 7% ($3.9-4 million) and EBITDA of $7.5 million rose sequentially from $6.1 million but was well below $11.7 million last year. Guidance was tightened to a $560-570 million revenue range from $550-575 million, lifting the midpoint while keeping the high end roughly at slight YoY growth. All three segments declined YoY (Branded -8%, Healthcare -5%, Contact Centers -9%), with management citing tariffs, customer caution, and a solar customer loss in contact centers, partially offset by a $2.9 million 3 Point acquisition contribution.

negative_highlights: G&A expense outlook raised by $1 million due to stock comp
FDA reversal on NMN could increase competition
Niagen Plus pricing remains high, limiting volume potential
positive_highlights: Revenue up 33% YoY to $34 million, record quarter
Net income grew to $4.6 million from $1.9 million
Gross margin expanded 100 bps to 64.5%
summary: Niagen Biosciences reported record Q3 2025 revenue of $34 million, up 33% year-over-year, with net income of $4.6 million (up from $1.9 million). Gross margin improved to 64.5% from 63.5%, and cash reached $64.3 million with no debt. Management raised full-year revenue growth guidance from 22%-27% to 25%-30%, but also increased the G&A expense outlook due to share-based compensation. New clinic partnerships and the Niagen Plus at-home injection launch are key growth drivers, while the company is awaiting results from a Phase III Parkinson's trial expected in early 2026.

negative_highlights: Transition labor costs ran ~240 bps above portfolio-average comp and cost ~$5.1 million in the quarter, dragging reported SHOP NOI and margins
SHOP NOI fell sequentially, with an additional ~$2.5 million seasonal utility increase contributing to the decline
Net debt-to-adjusted EBITDAre remained elevated at 10x (9.3x ex-transition costs), with leverage reduction dependent on pending asset sales closing
positive_highlights: SHOP occupancy rose 210 bps YoY to 81.5%, the fourth consecutive quarter of occupancy growth, with RevPOR up 5.3% and SHOP revenue up 6.9% YoY
Medical Office and Life Science same-property cash NOI rose 1.6% YoY with margins up 100 bps to 58.9%, and consolidated occupancy up 370 bps sequentially to 86.6%
Completed $1 billion Vertex HQ refinancing (DHC received $28M) and issued $375M secured notes, leaving no debt maturities until 2028 after the 2026 bond payoff
summary: DHC reported Q3 2025 total revenue of $388.7 million, up 4% YoY, with normalized FFO of $9.7 million ($0.04/sh) and adjusted EBITDAre of $62.9 million. SHOP NOI rose 7.8% YoY to $29.6 million but was hit by ~$5.1 million of temporary transition labor costs tied to moving 116 AlerisLife communities to 7 new operators; adjusted SHOP NOI would have been $34.8 million at a 10.4% margin. Full-year SHOP NOI guidance was maintained at $132-142 million and 2025 adjusted EBITDAre guided to $275-285 million, with the January 2026 zero-coupon bond expected to be repaid from asset sale proceeds and the new $375 million 7.25% secured notes. Net debt-to-adjusted EBITDAre was 10x (9.3x ex the transition costs), and 44 properties were sold YTD for $396 million with 38 more under agreement/LOI for $237 million.

negative_highlights: Lost a large high-ASP direct bill account which created an in-quarter ASP headwind of approximately $20.
ASP acceleration for new biomarkers is slower than anticipated due to payer scrutiny and higher denials on the RA33 and PAD4 markers.
Net loss widened to $7 million from $5 million, with adjusted EBITDA loss increasing to $1.9 million from $4 million year-over-year.
positive_highlights: Q3 volume was the highest ever recorded for a third quarter, with CTD test volume up 15% year-over-year and remaining strong into October.
Trailing 12-month ASP grew $37 year-over-year to $441 per test, driven by new biomarker launches and revenue cycle improvements.
Pharma Services business generated $800,000 in Q3 revenue, a significant increase from $100,000 in the same period last year.
summary: Exagen reported Q3 FY2025 revenue of approximately $17.2 million, representing a year-over-year increase of over 25% despite the loss of a large high-ASP direct bill account and slower-than-anticipated ASP ramp for new biomarkers. Gross margin was just over 58%, up 260 bps sequentially but down 175 bps year-over-year due to revenue adjustments in the prior period. Management maintained its full-year guidance range of $65 million to $70 million, noting that achieving cash flow positivity may be pushed to 2026.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA margins declined from 20.1% to 17.0% due to unfavorable mix, tariffs, and increased depreciation.
Prepaid sales decreased 7% in the quarter compared to a very strong prior year level with large orders.
positive_highlights: Net sales grew 11% driven by Arroweye addition ($15M contribution) and strong Card@Once instant issuance business performance.
summary: Third quarter net sales increased 11% to $346 million (implied from context of growth rates and prior year levels), but adjusted EBITDA decreased 7% due to unfavorable sales mix, tariff expenses ($1.6M in Q3 alone with total annualized impact near $5M), and higher production costs including new facility depreciation. Management updated the full-year outlook for net sales to low double-digit growth (down from mid-teens) and adjusted EBITDA guidance to flat-to-low-single-digits, citing continued margin pressure.

negative_highlights: Revenue decreased significantly year-over-year to $2.2 million, primarily driven by lower milestones achieved and the completion of small molecule ion channel programs.
Service revenue declined due to program completions earlier in the year, partially offset only modestly by xPloration consumable sales.
Several anticipated second-half 2025 milestones were pushed into early 2026, necessitating a downward revision to annual guidance.
positive_highlights: Program additions in Q3 equaled the total program adds achieved for all of 2024, indicating strong deal flow momentum.
The xPloration platform is generating strong interest with a growing sales funnel and positive feedback on efficiency from partners.
OmniUltra technology validation work was completed across a broad array of therapeutic targets ahead of its December launch.
summary: OmniAb reported Q3 FY2025 revenue of $2.2 million and a net loss of $16.5 million ($0.14/share), both down from the prior year period due to lower milestones, reduced service revenue following program completions, and an $800k headcount reduction charge. Management updated full-year 2025 guidance downward, expecting revenue between $18M-$22M (downward revision) and operating expenses of $82M-$86M due to delayed milestones pushed into early 2026.

negative_highlights: Net interest income fell 5.1% quarter-over-quarter to $13.7 million
Distributable earnings per basic share declined to $0.50 from $0.52
Unscheduled principal repayments of $62.7 million exceeded gross originations of $39.5 million, pressuring net portfolio growth
positive_highlights: Weighted average loan-to-enterprise value of 43.5%, below typical commercial mortgage REIT levels
Only approximately 14% of the floating rate portfolio exposed to further prime rate declines, with 86% fixed or floored
New $75 million 3-year secured revolver to Verano, described as the largest real estate-backed facility among U.S. cannabis operators
summary: Chicago Atlantic Real Estate Finance reported Q3 FY2025 net interest income of $13.7 million, down 5.1% from $14.4 million in Q2, with distributable earnings per basic share of $0.50 versus $0.52 prior quarter. Gross originations were $39.5 million, offset by $62.7 million in unscheduled principal repayments disclosed last quarter, leaving the loan portfolio at $400 million across 26 borrowers with a 16.5% weighted average yield. Management expects to maintain a 90-100% dividend payout ratio and may pay a Q4 special dividend; no new formal guidance was raised or cut. The key changes were a lower net interest income, a lower origination volume relative to repayments, a heavier reliance on rate floors with only 14% of the portfolio exposed to further declines, and a $75 million revolver to Verano.

negative_highlights: Gross margin contracted 520 bps YoY to 36.9%, with 390 bps from trade investment and 300 bps from green coffee inflation/tariffs.
DTC revenue declined 4% YoY, though adjusted for timing and one-time items it was slightly positive.
Q4 gross margin expected to be closer to 35% due to promotional activity and higher tariff impact from cost inventory.
positive_highlights: Wholesale revenue grew 9% YoY adjusting for nonrecurring items, driven by velocity and distribution gains; grocery ACV up 6 points to 48%, total ACV up 9 points to 54%.
Black Rifle unit sales up over 20% YTD, nearly triple the category growth rate of 13.2% in Nielsen-measured channels.
Adjusted EBITDA rose 19% YoY to 8.4% of sales, with operating expenses down 9% and headcount down 19%.
summary: Q3 FY2025 net revenue increased 3% YoY (5% excluding one-time items) to roughly $102M, with wholesale up 5% (9% ex-items) and DTC down 4%. Gross margin fell 520 bps YoY to 36.9% due to trade investment and coffee inflation/tariffs, but adjusted EBITDA rose 19% to 8.4% of sales. Management reaffirmed FY2025 guidance at the lower end: at least $395M revenue, 35% gross margin, and $20M adjusted EBITDA, guiding Q4 to ~$110M revenue and ~35% gross margin. The company raised $40.25M in equity to pay down debt and expects continued sequential revenue step-up, with the final quarter impacted by prior-year one-time items.

negative_highlights: Gross margin contracted sequentially to ~77% as customers migrated to an upgraded platform, though expected to expand in Q4.
Customer count decreased by approximately 3,000 due to one partner renegotiation and migration attrition.
positive_highlights: Achieved record third quarter results with $2.5 million adjusted EBITDA and a margin of 24%.
Enterprise channel grew approximately 26% year-over-year, contributing 45% of revenue.
Net loss narrowed to $0.04 per share from $0.10 in the prior year period.
summary: AudioEye reported record Q3 FY2025 revenue of $10.2 million (up 15% YoY) and a record adjusted EBITDA margin of 24%. Management raised full-year guidance to the top end ($9M-$9.1M adj EBITDA, $40.3M-$40.4M revenue) while narrowing the range due to customer migration impacts in Q4.

negative_highlights: Full-year guidance unchanged despite strong Q1, citing early in the year and government shutdown
U.S. government shutdown could push out some Q2 revenue, with worst-case impact of 4-5%
Management remains cautious on December quarter, not wanting to 'get over our skis'
positive_highlights: Revenue up 21.4% YoY with non-GAAP EPS of $0.43, a $1.30 improvement over last year
Non-GAAP gross margin expanded to 33.8% from 23.2% year-over-year
Launched Aprisa LTE 5G router, addressing a $2.8 billion market with strong customer interest
summary: Aviat Networks reported Q1 FY2026 revenue of $107.3 million, up 21.4% year-over-year, with non-GAAP EPS of $0.43 and adjusted EBITDA of $9.1 million. North America revenue grew 24.7% and international grew 18.3%, with gross margin expanding to 33.8% non-GAAP from 23.2% a year ago. Management maintained full-year guidance of $440-$460 million revenue and $45-$55 million adjusted EBITDA, while expressing confidence in public safety demand and the new Aprisa LTE 5G router opportunity. They noted a minor impact from the U.S. government shutdown, with some revenue pushouts expected in Q2 but recovering in Q3.

negative_highlights: High leverage and expected material outspend over next 2-3 years
2026 production flat due to growth project timing and May 2026 turnaround
Equity dilution via $300 million rights offering
positive_highlights: Recapitalization plan to fully repay senior notes and be debt-free
Expect to hit top end of 2025 production guidance
Boiler restored ahead of schedule and sulfur removal facilities expected in November 2025
summary: Greenfire announced a transformational recapitalization plan to fully repay senior secured notes via a $300 million equity rights offering backstopped by Waterous Energy Fund and secure an upsized $275 million credit facility, leaving the company debt-free after closing. Production is expected to hit the top end of 2025 guidance of 15,000-16,000 bbl/d, with capital guidance reaffirmed at $130 million. The company approved a $180 million 2026 capital budget with flat production guidance of 15,500-16,500 bpd, due to growth projects not reaching first oil until late Q4 2026 and a planned May 2026 turnaround. The boiler outage was resolved ahead of schedule, but the second boiler is being refurbished, and sulfur removal facilities are expected operational in November 2025.

negative_highlights: Revenue fell 19.9% YoY to $58.4 million, and management said the sales decline was more than expected, with product sales ex-Volvo still down 8.7% on truck demand
Diluted EPS dropped to $0.22 from $0.36 a year ago, and the effective tax rate rose to 29.3% from 18.7%
Full-year sales guidance is now down 10%–12%, with truck demand forecast soft in Q4 and tooling revenue timing shifting out of Q3
positive_highlights: Power sports achieved its first year-over-year growth in 8 quarters, supported by the new UTV skid plate program expected to reach roughly $8 million in annual run-rate revenue
Adjusted EBITDA margin of 11% rose 70 basis points from a year ago, and gross margin held at 17.4% despite the revenue decline
Year-to-date operating cash flow of $14.2 million exceeded net earnings, with total liquidity of $92.4 million and debt-to-EBITDA under 1x
summary: Q3 revenue fell 19.9% YoY to $58.4 million, with over half of the decline tied to the known Volvo transition and the remainder to lower medium/heavy-duty truck demand; management noted the sales decline was more than expected. Diluted EPS was $0.22 versus $0.36 a year ago, adjusted EPS $0.24, gross margin held at 17.4% and adjusted EBITDA was $6.4 million (11% of sales). Full-year sales are now guided down 10%–12%, though Q4 is expected up YoY on significantly higher tooling revenue pushed from Q3, with gross margin maintained in the 17%–19% range. Management emphasized growing new business wins ($46.7 million YTD, $65 million over 20 months), power sports returning to growth after 8 quarters, and a pipeline over $250 million, alongside 2027 revenue targets above $300 million.

negative_highlights: Total revenue fell 4.7% YoY to $281 million on Wholesale Express weakness
Wholesale Express revenue fell $14.1 million to $1 million and gross profit dropped to $0.3 million from $3.5 million
Free cash flow was $10.5 million for the nine months versus $67 million in the prior year period
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA rose $5.5 million, or over 80%, to $12.3 million YoY
Powersports revenue up slightly YoY, the first improvement since Q2 2023, with major units up 3.9% to 15,949
New unit gross margin improved to 12.6% from 11.3% and pre-owned to 16.1% from 14.6%
summary: RideNow reported Q3 FY2025 revenue of $281 million, down 4.7% YoY, with the decline driven solely by the Wholesale Express vehicle transportation business, whose revenue fell $14.1 million to $1 million. Adjusted EBITDA rose to $12.3 million, up $5.5 million or over 80% YoY, and powersports revenue of $280 million was up slightly, marking the first YoY improvement since Q2 2023, with major units up 3.9% to 15,949. New unit gross margin improved to 12.6% from 11.3% and pre-owned to 16.1% from 14.6%; adjusted SG&A fell 4.4% to $61.5 million. Management cited a continued turnaround with momentum carrying into Q4, extended the term loan maturity to September 2027 at a lower rate, and lowered annual cash interest by roughly $3.4 million; no explicit forward guidance figures were provided.

negative_highlights: Pediatric indication submission delayed beyond 2025.
DIXI sales decline expected in Q4 due to wind-down.
Operating expenses increased 21% YoY, partly due to higher note costs.
positive_highlights: Total revenue up 30% YoY to $27.4 million, a record.
First-ever positive adjusted EBITDA achieved in Q3.
Full-year revenue guidance raised to $97-$98 million.
summary: NeuroPace reported record Q3 2025 revenue of $27.4 million, up 30% year-over-year, driven by 31% growth in RNS system sales to $22.6 million. The company achieved its first positive adjusted EBITDA and raised full-year revenue guidance to $97-$98 million and gross margin guidance to 76%-77%. FDA submission for NAUTILUS remains on track for year-end, but pediatric indication timelines extend beyond 2025. DIXI wind-down is progressing with lower Q4 contribution expected.

negative_highlights: Net loss of $47 million reflects high R&D and program development costs typical for a pre-operational company.
Cash consumption in Q3 was $60 million, with full-year burn expected near the low end of guidance ($200M-$250M).
First flight of the engineering prototype is not expected until late 2025 or early 2026.
positive_highlights: Raised $230 million in equity, bringing total liquidity to $534 million including grants and credit lines.
Secured a contract with Embraer to produce landing gear for the E100 aircraft.
Pre-order backlog stands at approximately 2,800 aircraft valued close to $14 billion.
summary: Eve Holding reported a net loss of $47 million in Q3 FY2025, driven by $45 million in program development costs and $6 million in SG&A. The company raised cash through a $230 million equity offering, ending the quarter with $412 million in cash and extending its runway to approximately 2.5 years. Management confirmed they are on track to hit the low end of their full-year 2025 guidance for total cash consumption between $200 million and $250 million.

negative_highlights: Adjusted gross margin was flat at 73.1% despite platform analysis volume growing over 40% year-over-year.
Cash burn increased 36.5% year-over-year to $13.1 million due to higher interest expense and vendor payments.
Latin America revenue growth declined, partially offsetting strong performance in other regions.
positive_highlights: Revenue growth accelerated to 23% year-over-year, the highest rate since Q1 2025.
Full-year 2025 revenue guidance was raised by $3 million to a range of $75-$77 million.
New customer signings reached record levels with 31 new customers in Q3, bringing total 2025 signings to 94.
summary: SOPHiA GENETICS reported Q3 FY2025 revenue of $19.5 million, representing a 23% year-over-year acceleration to its highest growth rate in three quarters. Management raised full-year 2025 revenue guidance to $75-$77 million from the prior range of $72-$76 million, citing strong momentum in new customer signings and expanding applications. Adjusted gross margin remained flat at 73.1% despite a 40% increase in data volume, while adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed to $10.2 million.

negative_highlights: Gross margin fell to 68.8% from 71.2% a year earlier on $1.4 million of inventory reserves/write-offs and $1.3 million higher cost of units sold.
Net loss widened to $17.5 million from $4.8 million a year earlier, driven by an $11.3 million loss on debt extinguishment.
SUSTOL net sales fell about 32% YoY to $1.9 million and commercialization will be wound down over the next 12 months, with only a possible late-2027 reintroduction.
positive_highlights: ZYNRELEF net sales rose 49% YoY to $9.3 million and APONVIE rose 173% YoY to $3.0 million, lifting acute care franchise to $12.3 million from $10.7 million in Q2.
ZYNRELEF average daily units increased 28% YoY (882 to 1,127) and ordering accounts rose from 705 to 833; October preliminary units were ~17-18% above September.

Adjusted EBITDA turned positive at $1.5 million for the quarter versus a $0.4 million loss a year earlier, and $9.5 million year-to-date versus a $0.7 million loss; the financing overhang was resolved.
summary: Heron reported Q3 2025 total net revenues of $38.2 million and year-to-date revenues of $114.3 million, with adjusted EBITDA of $1.5 million for the quarter and $9.5 million year-to-date. Gross margin was 68.8%, down from 71.2% a year earlier on $1.4 million of inventory reserves/write-offs (SUSTOL polymer) and $1.3 million higher cost of units sold; adjusted for the onetime charge, gross margin was roughly 74.5%. Acute care grew sharply (ZYNRELEF $9.3 million, +49% YoY; APONVIE $3.0 million, +173% YoY) while CINVANTI was about $24 million (+6% YoY) and SUSTOL $1.9 million (-32%), with SUSTOL to be wound down over the next 12 months. Management reaffirmed full-year net revenue guidance of $153-163 million and adjusted EBITDA of $9-13 million, unchanged from prior guidance.

negative_highlights: Device Solutions revenue decreased 2.9% primarily due to a large equipment sale in the prior year and lower biomedical services volume.
A contract amendment with a major biomedical services customer will reduce annual revenue by an estimated $6 million to $7 million starting in December.
positive_highlights: Net revenue reached a quarterly record of $36.2 million, up 3.3% from the prior year period.
Gross margin expanded to just over 57%, driven by improved labor efficiency and favorable revenue mix.
Oncology net revenue hit an all-time record, with Wound Care revenue surging 116% due to volume increases and acquisitions.
summary: InfuSystem reported Q3 FY2025 net revenue of $36.2 million, a 3.3% increase year-over-year driven by Patient Services growth and Wound Care expansion, partially offset by lower Device Solutions revenue. Gross margin expanded to just over 57%, while Adjusted EBITDA reached $8.3 million (22.8% of revenue). Management reaffirmed full-year guidance for adjusted EBITDA margins of 20% or greater and revenue growth between 6% to 8%. A significant contract amendment with a large biomedical services customer will reduce annual revenue by an estimated $6-7 million starting in December, but is expected to improve operating profitability.

negative_highlights: Q3 revenue declined to $262.8M from $266.3M year-over-year, with the quarter still posting a $24.7M GAAP net loss
Operating expenses excluding commissions and one-offs rose $2.5M in the quarter on higher personnel and bonus accruals
Management flagged ongoing pressure from elevated mortgage rates and geopolitical uncertainty; Q3 adjusted net income of $156K is essentially break-even
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA turned positive at $2.7M vs $2.3M, and adjusted net income was $156K vs an adjusted loss of $2.7M a year ago
Nine-month operating loss narrowed to $21.5M from $52.6M, with adjusted EBITDA up $15.3M to $2.9M
Post-quarter balance sheet: $85M property management sale closed, convert redeemed, leaving ~$126.5M cash and no debt; Q3 sales of homes over $5M rose 20% to 333
summary: Q3 revenue fell to $262.8M from $266.3M a year ago, and GAAP net loss was $24.7M ($0.29/share) versus $27.2M ($0.33) — improved but still a loss. Adjusted EBITDA rose to $2.7M from $2.3M and adjusted net income was $156K versus an adjusted loss of $2.7M. Nine-month revenue rose 5% to $787.6M and the operating loss narrowed to $21.5M from $52.6M; the October property management sale for $85M and convertible redemption left ~$126.5M cash and no debt. No explicit quarterly guidance was given; management framed 2026 as a growth phase.

negative_highlights: Gross margin contracted to 17% from 18%, and gross profit was flat at $1.2 million despite the sales increase
Modified EBITDA loss widened to $3.9 million from $3.0 million as SG&A rose to $4.2 million from $3.1 million
Cash fell to $4.1 million from $10.4 million at December 31, 2024, with $2.8 million used in operating activities versus $1.1 million generated a year ago
positive_highlights: Net sales increased 4% to $7.0 million, driven by higher volumes of Reed's branded products with recurring national customers
Delivery and handling costs fell 14% to $1.1 million, or $2.50 per case from $2.99, on lower transportation costs
Core distribution grew 4% year-over-year across top accounts including Kroger, Sprouts and Ahold Delhaize
summary: Net sales rose 4% to $7.0 million versus $6.8 million, but gross margin contracted to 17% from 18% and gross profit was flat at $1.2 million; excluding $0.1 million of inventory write-offs margin was 19%. SG&A jumped to $4.2 million from $3.1 million, pushing modified EBITDA loss to $3.9 million from $3.0 million and operating cash flow to a $2.8 million use versus $1.1 million generated a year ago. Cash fell to $4.1 million from $10.4 million at year-end. Management cited higher-than-expected trade spend with two large distributors that it is now redefining and expects gross margin expansion going forward, but gave no quantitative guidance and did not raise any outlook. Balancing modest top-line growth and a 14% cut in delivery/handling costs against margin contraction and a materially wider EBITDA loss, the quarter reads as weak on profitability with an unchanged outlook.

negative_highlights: $51 million adverse reserve charge on 2022-and-prior accident years, driven by other liability occurrence and products/completed operations
$0.01 GAAP net loss per share; E&S gross written premium down 8.9% with Manufacturers & Contractors writings down 30% ($13.5 million)
Excess property rates down 19.6% and premiums down 38.2%; Specialty Admitted net written premium down 94% with retention at 3.7%
positive_highlights: Group combined ratio improved to 94.0% from 135.5% in Q3 2024 and 98.6% in Q2 2025
Expense ratio fell to 28.3%, down more than 3 points YoY, with roughly $8 million of lasting savings and headcount down 50 to 590
Tangible common book value per share up 23.4% YTD to $8.24; annualized operating ROE of 19.3% above the mid-teens target
summary: James River reported Q3 2025 adjusted net operating income of $17.4 million ($0.32/share) but a small GAAP net loss of $376,000 ($0.01/share). The group combined ratio improved to 94% from 135.5% a year ago and 98.6% last quarter, with expense ratio down to 28.3%, and tangible book value per share rose 23.4% year-to-date to $8.24. E&S gross written premium fell 8.9% while net earned premium grew 1%, and a $51 million unfavorable reserve development on 2022-and-prior accident years was ceded to legacy covers. Management expects a redomicile to Delaware on Nov 7 with a one-time $10-13 million tax benefit and $3-6 million of ongoing quarterly expense savings, and reiterated a full-year 31% expense ratio target, with no formal guidance raise.

negative_highlights: Interest expense rose to $6.7 million from $5 million on higher debt and rates
Net debt increased to $393.9 million from $366.7 million at March 31, 2025
Publishing synchronization revenue declined due to license timing
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 12% to $45.4 million, with 7% organic growth, ahead of expectations
Recorded music revenue rose 21% and publishing performance revenue rose 47%
Full-year guidance raised and narrowed on both revenue and adjusted EBITDA
summary: Reservoir reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $45.4 million, up 12% year-over-year (7% organic, 5% from acquisitions), driven by 21% growth in recorded music and 8% in music publishing. Adjusted EBITDA rose 10% to $19.4 million and OIBDA rose 10% to $18.2 million; net income was $2.2 million ($0.03 diluted EPS) versus $152,000 a year ago. Management raised and narrowed full-year revenue guidance to $167–170 million (from $164–169 million) and adjusted EBITDA guidance to $70–72 million (from $68–72 million), implying ~6% and ~8% growth at the midpoint respectively. The quarter exceeded internal expectations, aided by the Miles Davis catalog acquisition and a deal pipeline described as over $1 billion.

negative_highlights: Accessories and materials revenue down 17% year-over-year, with continued competitive pressure
Active users roughly flat sequentially and engagement (90-day engaged users) declined 3% year-over-year
Management expects margin pressure from tariffs starting Q4 and accelerating through 2026
positive_highlights: Operating income grew 114% to $22.7 million; EPS doubled to $0.10
Paid subscribers up 6% year-over-year to just over 3 million; platform revenue up 7%
Machine note-out units up year-over-year in North America and globally, and in October Amazon Prime Day
summary: Cricut reported Q3 2025 revenue of $170.4 million, up 2% year-over-year, with net income of $20.5 million and EPS of $0.10, up from $0.05 last year. Platform revenue grew 7% and paid subscribers increased 6% to just over 3 million, but accessories and materials revenue declined 17% year-over-year. Management flagged tariff uncertainty expecting margin pressure starting in Q4 and accelerating through 2026, while remaining optimistic about marketing investments and new machine launches.

negative_highlights: NII per share declined to $0.43 from $0.46 in Q2 due to lower interest income and two new nonaccruals
Portfolio yield declined to 9.9% from 10.1% due to spread tightening and lower base rates
NAV per share fell to $17.85 from $17.92 due to fair value declines in underperformers
positive_highlights: High-quality portfolio with nonaccruals just 0.4% of fair value and watchlist at ~7% of fair value
Churchill platform reviewed 22% more deals in Q3 vs Q2 and saw record July/August/September activity
No exposure to Tricolor or First Brands; portfolio fundamentals show solid single-digit growth
summary: NCDL reported Q3 2025 NII of $0.43 per share, down from $0.46 in Q2, and total investment income declined slightly to $51.1 million from $53.1 million. NAV per share slipped to $17.85 from $17.92, and gross originations fell to $29 million from $48 million, intentionally due to operating at the high end of leverage range. Portfolio credit quality appears stable with nonaccruals at 0.4% of fair value and top 10 positions at 13.6% of fair value, but management is optimistic about 2026 deal flow and highlights no exposure to Tricolor or First Brands.

negative_highlights: GAAP net income was negatively impacted by turning off the accrual of legacy WMC CRE loans as they work through monetization.
Unrealized losses on commercial investments offset some gains from asset appreciation and spread tightening.
Call rights termination is expected to return capital in 3-4 quarters rather than immediately.
positive_highlights: Book value increased to $10.46 per share despite a one-time dilution of 1.8% from issuing shares for Arc Home acquisition.
Investment portfolio grew by over 20% quarter-over-quarter, reaching $8.8 billion through the securitization of residential mortgage loans and home equity lines of credit.
Agency-eligible investor book is performing better than prime jumbo, while non-QM continues to outperform broader market issuance.
summary: MITT reported Q3 FY2025 results with book value rising to $10.46 per share and EAD increasing to $0.23 from $0.18 in the prior quarter. The company executed significant growth initiatives, including acquiring an additional 21.4% of Arc Home (contributing $0.03 EPS) and rotating capital into residential mortgage loans via four securitizations totaling over $1.7 billion. Management noted that while GAAP net income was impacted by turning off accruals on legacy WMC CRE loans, the core portfolio performance remains strong with agency-eligible investor books outperforming prime jumbo.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined quarter-over-quarter due to volume adjustments in the CMO business and restructuring costs.
Gross profit loss widened to $1.1 million from $0.6 million in Q2 due to lower volume, product mix transition, and inventory write-downs.
Adjusted EBITDA loss increased to $2.9 million from $2.6 million in the prior quarter.
positive_highlights: Company is now debt-free with $4.8 million in cash on hand and a $9.5 million receivable from insurance recovery.
Newly branded VLN and Partner VLN products are shipping to approximately 1,500 stores across 21 states.
Management has successfully transitioned the balance sheet from cleanup mode to growth capital positioning.
summary: Third quarter 2025 net revenue was $4 million, a decrease from $4.1 million in the prior quarter, driven by lower volume and strategic shifts away from low-margin CMO business. Gross profit remained a loss of $1.1 million compared to a $0.6 million loss in Q2, while total operating expenses decreased slightly to $2.2 million. The company reported a net loss of $3.8 million from continuing operations but achieved a basic EPS of $1.55 due to a one-time $9.5 million gain on an insurance settlement.

negative_highlights: G&A up 17% and salaries/benefits up 44% due to incentive comp and professional fees
Marketplace segment only slightly operating profit positive, with episodic private sale revenue
No quantified guidance for upcoming transition to 100% risk assumption under Markel fronting
positive_highlights: Total revenue up 18% to $380 million; adjusted EBITDA up 106% to $50 million
Full-year guidance raised for revenue and profit; net income expected up 58-65%
New partnership signed with Liberty Mutual/Safeco to strengthen omnichannel distribution
summary: Hagerty reported Q3 2025 total revenue of $380 million, up 18% year-over-year, with written premium up 16% and commission revenue up 18%. Adjusted EBITDA grew 106% to $50 million, and net income rose 143% to $46 million. The company raised its full-year 2025 guidance, now expecting revenue growth of 14-15%, net income of $124-129 million, and adjusted EBITDA of $170-176 million. Management highlighted a new partnership with Liberty Mutual/Safeco and strong policy-in-force growth momentum, with October PIF growth being the highest in company history.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined 10% year-over-year with core revenue down 19% in North America due to volume loss and share loss.
Adjusted EBITDA dropped $38 million year-over-year, reflecting unfavorable volume, price/cost pressures, and staffing levels set for unrealized share gains.
Full-year outlook was significantly lowered, with sales guidance reduced from a 4%-9% decline expectation to a 10%-13% decline.
positive_highlights: Liquidity position remains strong with approximately $100 million in cash and $400 million of revolver availability.
Working capital performance remained disciplined, contributing modestly to liquidity despite the softer sales environment.
Transformation initiatives and cost reduction programs provided a partial offset to headwinds, delivering additional savings within SG&A.
summary: JELD-WEN reported Q3 FY2025 revenue of $809 million, a 10% year-over-year decline driven by lower volumes and share loss in North America and Europe. Adjusted EBITDA fell to $44 million, significantly below prior year levels and internal expectations due to softening demand, operational inefficiencies, and persistent price/cost headwinds. Management lowered full-year 2025 guidance for sales ($3.1B-$3.2B) and Adjusted EBITDA ($105M-$120M), citing further deterioration in market conditions and an inability to capture planned market share gains.

negative_highlights: Q4 guidance implies sequential decline in revenue and EBITDA
DynaEnergetics sequential EBITDA down 46% due to tariffs and lower pricing
NobelClad sales down 16% YoY due to tariff-related slowdown
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA up 51% YoY to $8.6 million
Arcadia sales up 7% YoY and EBITDA more than doubled
Net debt down 47% since year-start
summary: DMC's Q3 FY2025 revenue of $151.5 million declined 1% YoY, while adjusted EBITDA attributable to DMC rose 51% to $8.6 million. Arcadia grew 7% YoY and EBITDA more than doubled, but DynaEnergetics and NobelClad faced headwinds from tariffs and weak demand, with NobelClad sales down 16% YoY. The company lowered Q4 guidance to $140-150 million sales and $5-8 million EBITDA, citing continued market challenges. Net debt was reduced to $30.1 million, down 47% since the start of the year, and NobelClad won a record $20 million order (plus $5 million follow-on) that will ship in 2026.

negative_highlights: Revenue missed guidance and declined sequentially as a $2 million shipment slip from life sciences and semi markets delayed Q3 recognition.
Gross margin declined 70 basis points sequentially to 41.9% primarily due to lower volume.
Semi market remains sluggish, particularly in analog mixed signal, with limited near-term order placement despite optimism for later 2026.
positive_highlights: Orders reached $37.6 million, the strongest level since Q2 2022, with a sequential increase of $11.4 million in backlog.
Auto/EV orders doubled sequentially to $14.6 million, accounting for roughly three-quarters of the sequential order growth.
Defense/aerospace orders more than doubled sequentially to $6.4 million driven by next-generation weapon system demand.
summary: Revenue for Q3 was $26.2 million, missing the prior guidance range and declining sequentially due to a $2 million shipment slip related to technical challenges in life sciences and semi markets. Management raised Q4 revenue guidance to $30-32 million, citing that the missed quarter's shipments will largely shift into Q1 2026 rather than Q4. While orders reached a strong level of $37.6 million driven by auto/EV and defense/aerospace, gross margin contracted 70 bps sequentially to 41.9% due to lower volume.

negative_highlights: MBIA Insurance Corp. statutory net loss of $25M due to lower Zohar CDO recoveries
PREPA resolution timing uncertain with litigation over board dismissals and bondholder opposition at ~90%
Consolidated book value per share remains negative at -$43.17
positive_highlights: GAAP net loss narrowed from $56M to $8M YoY, driven by PREPA loss reserve benefit of $54M
Adjusted net income of $51M ($1.03/share) versus breakeven in prior year
National statutory capital increased $82M YTD to $994M
summary: MBIA reported a Q3 2025 GAAP net loss of $8 million, narrower than the $56 million loss a year earlier, largely due to a $54 million net benefit from PREPA loss reserves after watching $374 million of bankruptcy claims. Adjusted net income was $51 million versus breakeven a year ago. National's statutory capital rose to $994 million, while MBIA Insurance Corp. posted a statutory net loss on lower Zohar recoveries. PREPA resolution remains uncertain due to board litigation and bondholder opposition, but management believes reduced exposure improves prospects for a future sale or special dividend.

negative_highlights: Total revenue declined by 6% in constant currency due to a 7% decrease in unit volume and shipping/handling decline of 13%
Adjusted EBITDA margin contracted 245 basis points, driven by marketing investment (140 bps), sales deleverage (130 bps), and incentive plan changes
Free cash flow turned to a use of $184 million in the first nine months compared to a source of $102 million last year
positive_highlights: Social and streaming revenue grew 30% year-over-year
QVC added approximately 255,000 new customers via TikTok Shop and 300,000 through traditional channels in Q3
Average customer spend increased for the first time since Q2 2024
summary: QVC Group reported a challenging Q3 FY2025 with total revenue declining by 6% in constant currency and Adjusted EBITDA decreasing 26%. The company cited declines across all segments (QxH -7%, International -5%, Cornerstone -8%) driven by reduced unit volume, sales deleverage, tariffs, and a depressed housing market. Management noted that while social and streaming revenue is growing at low double digits to moderate the overall decline, they remain focused on cost reduction and evaluating financial alternatives.

negative_highlights: Total revenue declined 0.5% YoY
Net loss increased to $9.2 million from $6.8 million
Food costs up 20 bps due to higher food costs
positive_highlights: October comp sales +8% with traffic +1.5%
Adjusted EBITDA up 33% to $6.5 million
Restaurant contribution margin +40 bps to 13.2%
summary: Noodles & Company reported Q3 FY2025 total revenue of $122.1 million, down 0.5% YoY, with system-wide comp sales up 4.0%. Company comp traffic declined 0.6%, but improved sequentially within the quarter and accelerated to +8% in October with traffic up over 1.5%. Adjusted EBITDA rose 33% to $6.5 million, and restaurant contribution margin expanded 40 bps. The company raised its full-year revenue and comp guidance, and is executing restaurant closures expected to positively impact 2026 margins by over $2 million.

negative_highlights: EV charging revenue roughly flat at $4.8 million and expected to be flat to slightly down for the year
LED lighting revenue declined 2% year-over-year
Net loss continued at $0.6 million despite improvement
positive_highlights: Gross profit up 34% year-over-year, gross margin up 790 bps to 31%
Fourth consecutive quarter of positive adjusted EBITDA, improving to $0.5 million from -$1.4 million
Strong segment margins: EV charging 45.8%, lighting 27.5%, maintenance 23.7%
summary: Q2 FY2026 revenue grew modestly to $19.9 million from $19.4 million, with gross margin expanding to 31% from 23.1%. Adjusted EBITDA turned positive for the fourth consecutive quarter at $0.5 million, and the net loss narrowed to $0.6 million from $3.6 million. The company reiterated its full-year revenue guidance of approximately $84 million and expects to approach or achieve positive adjusted EBITDA for the year. Notable wins included an $11 million government lighting award, up to $7 million in automotive LED lighting, and $8.5 million in EV charging work, plus a 3-year retail maintenance renewal worth $42-$45 million.

negative_highlights: Consolidated net sales declined 8% year-over-year driven by tariff-induced demand volatility in Asia (-19%) and the Americas.
Gross margin collapsed to just 2.5%, down from prior periods, reflecting volume declines that outpaced cost savings.
Ordering patterns remain extremely light through Q2 as customers stockpile inventory ahead of tariffs before normalizing in January.
positive_highlights: Cost restructuring initiatives completed, reducing annualized SG&A to under $45M from ~$49M and manufacturing costs by $5M per quarter for the remainder of FY26.
Productivity improved significantly in Americas facilities with output rising from 85 lbs/man-hour to 107 lbs/man-hour following hiring and training.
Brazil segment remains cash-positive despite pricing pressures, maintaining a healthy balance sheet.
summary: Consolidated net sales for Q1 FY26 were $135.7 million, down 8% year-over-year due to trade-related uncertainty and lower volumes in Asia and the Americas. Gross margin contracted significantly to 2.5%, while management highlighted cost restructuring actions including headcount reductions and SG&A savings of approximately $4-5 million annually. Management expects sequential improvement in adjusted EBITDA starting in Q2 as holiday season inventory levels normalize.

negative_highlights: OEM channel revenue declined 20% YoY to $15.8M due to J&J pricing pressure (Monovisc price down 17% YTD).
Gross margin fell 10 pts YoY to 56%, driven by $3.2M reduction in J&J revenue and lower pricing.
Hyalofast Phase III study failed to meet co-primary endpoints, casting regulatory approval uncertainty.
positive_highlights: Commercial Channel revenue grew 22% YoY to $12M, driven by Integrity and international OA Pain growth.
Integrity procedures grew for the sixth consecutive quarter, on track to more than double in 2025; ~500 procedures in the quarter, nearly 300 surgeon users.
Adjusted EBITDA of $0.9M exceeded breakeven guidance; SG&A down 12% YoY; operating cash flow up to $6.9M from $5M prior year.
summary: Q3 FY2025 revenue was $27.8M, down 6% YoY, in line with expectations; Commercial Channel grew 22% to $12M, while OEM declined 20% to $15.8M on J&J pricing pressure. Adjusted EBITDA was $0.9M, above the breakeven guidance, and operating cash flow was $6.9M. Management maintained full-year guidance of $47-49.5M Commercial and $62-65M OEM revenue, and announced a second $15M share repurchase.

negative_highlights: Energy revenue declined to $14.2 million from $15.8 million YoY on a softer oil price environment, and industrial fell to $6.7 million from $7 million
GAAP operating loss of $6.4 million and adjusted net loss of $1.1 million ($0.01/share); consolidated debt of $94 million across Benchmark and Deflecto

Management flagged weak demand: Class 8 September net orders were the weakest since 2019, office products customers are pausing purchases on tariff uncertainty, and energy acquisitions now require more caution as basin valuations rose
positive_highlights: IP segment generated $7.8 million revenue and $3 million adjusted EBITDA versus $0.5 million revenue a year ago, including $7.4 million in paid-up settlements
Manufacturing revenue rose for a third consecutive quarter to $30.8 million from $29 million, with Deflecto G&A falling to $4.6 million from $5.1 million prior quarter
Total cash, equity securities and loans receivable grew to $332.4 million from $297 million at year-end 2024, with parent-level debt at zero
summary: Acacia reported Q3 revenue of $59.4 million, up 16% sequentially and 155% YoY (the YoY figure driven mainly by Deflecto's first full comparable quarter), with total adjusted EBITDA of $8 million, free cash flow of $7.7 million, and a GAAP loss of $0.03 per share ($0.01 adjusted). Segment detail was uneven: IP revenue jumped to $7.8 million ($3 million adjusted EBITDA) versus $0.5 million a year ago, manufacturing rose to $30.8 million from $29 million sequentially, while energy fell to $14.2 million from $15.8 million on softer oil prices and industrial slipped to $6.7 million from $7 million. Management gave no formal numeric guidance, citing persistent tariff headwinds and a weak Class 8 truck market (weakest September orders since 2019), while offsetting with pricing actions, reshoring, cost cuts, and debt paydown of ~$24 million at Benchmark and ~$13 million at Deflecto since their acquisitions. Book value per share was essentially flat at $5.98 ($5.57 attributable to Acacia).

negative_highlights: Revenue declined 15.2% year-over-year due to soft consumer demand and a major retailer delaying orders.
Gross margin fell significantly from 28% in the prior year period to 21.1% in Q3, driven by temporary tariff costs.
Operating profit dropped sharply from $10.6 million (6.8%) last year to $2.9 million (2.2%), as tariff impacts offset expense leverage.
positive_highlights: Sequential revenue improved by 300 basis points compared with Q2 as retailers resumed typical note patterns after destocking.
The company has fully absorbed the impact from peak tariff rates and moved forward with a more balanced inventory position.
Hamilton Beach Health achieved positive operating profit for the first time, driven by new partnerships (CenterWell, Lumisir) and software launches.
summary: Total revenue was $132.8 million in Q3 FY2025, down 15.2% year-over-year due to lower volumes and a large retailer delaying orders. Gross margin compressed to 21.1%, primarily impacted by one-time incremental tariff costs of $5 million related to temporary 125% rates on Chinese imports; excluding this cost, gross margin would have been 24.8%. Net income was $0.12 per diluted share compared to $0.14 in the prior year period.

negative_highlights: Gross margin contracted 360 bps to 40.7% from 44.3%, which management attributed essentially 100% to incremental tariffs
Diluted EPS fell to $0.69 from $0.84 and operating earnings dropped 21% to $8.1 million
BOGS sales declined 17% and the Forsake brand is being wound down; China tariff rate of 30% is set for reevaluation by November 10 with no clarity on outcome
positive_highlights: Legacy brands combined sales rose 3% on 3% lower unit volume, led by Florsheim up 8%
Balance sheet strength: $78.5 million in cash and marketable securities, no debt on the $40 million revolver
Board declared a special cash dividend of $2.00 per share alongside the regular $0.27 quarterly dividend
summary: Weyco reported Q3 FY2025 net sales of $73.1 million, down 2% YoY, with gross margin contracting to 40.7% from 44.3% as incremental China tariffs (30%) were not fully offset by a 10% July 1 price increase. Operating earnings fell 21% to $8.1 million and diluted EPS dropped to $0.69 from $0.84; wholesale volume fell 7% partly on order cancellations from a large customer that did not timely adopt the new pricing. No formal guidance was given beyond noting the customer issue is resolved and Q4 should not be significantly impacted, while tariffs remain fluid with China rates to be reevaluated by November 10. The Board declared a regular $0.27 dividend plus a special $2.00 per share dividend, supported by $78.5 million in cash and no debt.

negative_highlights: Total gross margin contracted by 182 basis points to 44.7%, primarily due to a shift toward lower-margin B2B sales mix.
Rental revenue declined 4.4% to $13.3 million, impacted by higher mix of lower private payer reimbursement rates and a one-time logistics adjustment.
Direct-to-consumer sales fell 17.9% to $15.8 million as the company intentionally shifts toward a leaner operating model.
positive_highlights: International B2B revenue surged 18.8% year-over-year to $38.4 million, driven by expansion in existing markets and new geographies.
Adjusted EBITDA turned positive at $2.3 million, marking the third consecutive quarter of profitability.
Operating expenses decreased 1.4% year-over-year to $48.4 million due to effective cost management.
summary: Inogen reported Q3 FY2025 revenue of $92.4 million, a 4% increase year-over-year driven by strong international B2B growth (18.8%) and domestic B2B gains (6.6%), while DTC sales declined 17.9%. The company raised its full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance to approximately $2 million from a prior breakeven expectation, citing sustained revenue growth and operational discipline. Management reiterated full-year revenue guidance of $354-$357 million and provided Q4 revenue expectations of $87-$90 million.

negative_highlights: Reported a net loss of $8.2 million (-$0.12 per diluted share) and negative AFFO per share of $0.19
Urban hotels posted comparable RevPAR down 3.9%, with Philadelphia citywide occupancy declines hitting the Notary Hotel
Approximately 87% of debt is effectively floating at a blended average rate of 6.9%, leaving interest cost exposed to SOFR
positive_highlights: Comparable hotel EBITDA rose 15.1% year over year to $21.4 million and portfolio GOP margin expanded 160 bps
Resort segment RevPAR grew 5.5% with resort comparable EBITDA up about 58%; Four Seasons Scottsdale RevPAR up roughly 25% and Ritz-Carlton Lake Tahoe total revenue up about 32%
Full-year 2025 group room revenue pace is up 9.1% versus prior year, with Q4 group room revenue pacing ahead 1.7%
summary: Braemar's Q3 2025 comparable RevPAR rose 1.4% to $257 (fourth straight quarter of growth) and comparable hotel EBITDA rose 15.1% to $21.4 million, though the quarter produced a net loss of $8.2 million (-$0.12 per share) and negative AFFO of $0.19 per share. Resort RevPAR grew 5.5% and resort EBITDA rose roughly 58%; excluding the three hotels under renovation, RevPAR grew 3.4%, while urban RevPAR fell 3.9%. No numerical forward guidance was issued; property-level commentary cited full-year group pace up 9.1% and Q4 group room revenue pace up 1.7%. Q3 is seasonally the weakest quarter, and management declined to discuss the announced sale process, noting only the Mariott Seattle Waterfront sale ($145 million) closed and the Clancy ($115 million) is expected to close this month.

negative_highlights: Consumer cannabis net revenue declined to $6.9 million from $10.4 million
Plant propagation gross margin fell to 10% due to inventory write-offs
Free cash flow was negative $42.3 million, weaker than prior year
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA grew 52% to $15.4 million, exceeding top-line growth by 5x
Consolidated adjusted gross margin expanded 700 bps to 61%
Record international medical cannabis revenue up 22% year-over-year
summary: Aurora Cannabis reported Q2 FY2026 net revenue of $90.4 million, up 11% year-over-year, with record global medical cannabis revenue up 15% and international revenue up 22%. Consolidated adjusted gross margin expanded 700 basis points to 61%, and adjusted EBITDA rose 52% to $15.4 million. The company raised its medical cannabis segment growth guidance to 8%-12% for Q3, while noting a softness in Australia due to a transition to premium products and ongoing regulatory uncertainty in Germany. It ended the quarter with $142 million cash and no cannabis debt.

negative_highlights: Product revenue declined 23% year-over-year to $37 million due to slower performance in EIMEA and China.
Gross margin contracted significantly to 28.3% from 33.9% prior year, impacted by sales mix, tariffs ($1.1M), and obsolescence charges ($0.7M).
Operating loss widened to $11.3 million from a $2.1 million loss in the prior year due to restructuring costs.
positive_highlights: Service revenue grew 7% year-over-year to $57 million, driven by 10% growth in contract revenue.
Gross orders totaled approximately $40 million with a trailing 12-month book-to-bill ratio of 1.2.
Order backlog stands at $396 million, representing over 18 months of product revenue visibility.
summary: Accuray reported Q1 FY2026 net revenue of $94 million, down 7% year-over-year, with product revenue missing expectations due to slower performance in EIMEA and China regions. Adjusted EBITDA was a loss of $4.1 million compared to an income of $3.1 million in the prior year, driven by gross margin contraction and restructuring charges. Management reiterated full-year FY2026 guidance for revenue ($471M-$485M) and adjusted EBITDA ($31M-$35M), noting a shift in product demand recognition to the second half of the year.

negative_highlights: Virtual Sports segment continues to be impacted by taxation that started in January in Brazil.
North American Virtual Sports growth is hindered by operators prioritizing iGaming and sports business over virtuals, causing it to slide down their priority list.
Full year guidance remains expressed as high single-digit absolute EBITDA growth rather than specific revenue or EPS targets due to uncertainty around the upcoming U.K. budget tax changes.
positive_highlights: Interactive segment achieved more than 40% adjusted EBITDA year-over-year growth for the ninth consecutive quarter with October being the single largest revenue month in history.
The sale of the holiday parks business is closing on November 7, expected to significantly reduce capital intensity and improve net leverage.
Board reauthorized a $25 million share buyback plan as part of plans going forward.
summary: Third quarter adjusted EBITDA of $32.3 million and trailing twelve-month adjusted EBITDA of $110 million both beat consensus estimates. Management raised guidance for the full year to high single-digit growth in absolute terms (pre-tax impact) following a strong Q4 outlook, though specific revenue/EPS targets were not explicitly restated as numerical beats against prior period numbers other than implied strength.

negative_highlights: Marketing revenue fell 43% year-over-year as Google's AFD product was effectively sunsetting, removing a key monetization source.
Revenue per session (RPS) declined 16% sequentially due to weakness in advertiser demand and tariff uncertainty impacting CouponFollow.
Company is not providing forward guidance for Q4 or FY2025/2026 citing continued volatility tied to Google marketplace dynamics.
positive_highlights: Product revenue increased 8% year-over-year driven by a 23% increase in sessions across Startpage, MapQuest, and CouponFollow.
Transition to Google's new RSOC product is nearly complete, positioning the marketing business for stability heading into 2026.
New AI-focused products launched including Vanish (Private AI Chat) on Startpage and redesigned apps with CarPlay support on MapQuest.
summary: Q3 revenue was $61.6 million, down 4% year-over-year and 21% sequentially due to the effective deprecation of Google's AdSense for Domains (AFD) product which contributed minimal profit in Q3 but historically generated significant value. While the Product segment grew 8% year-over-year with strong session growth, overall adjusted gross profit declined 4% YoY as marketing volatility offset core execution. Management stated they are not providing guidance for Q4 or FY2026 due to ongoing marketplace dynamics.

negative_highlights: Gross premiums written declined intentionally in Q3 due to stringent underwriting controls targeting average annual loss limits.
Policy acquisition costs rose by $4.5 million (21.5%) driven by increased commissions and decreased ceding commission income.
Pricing headwinds persist with rates down approximately 9-13% since year-end, impacting full-year premium outlook.
positive_highlights: Net income grew 16% year-over-year due to muted catastrophe and attritional losses.
Combined ratio improved to 56.9%, significantly below the stated target of 65%.
Cash and investments increased 28.5% since year-end to $695 million.
summary: American Coastal reported Q3 FY2025 net income of $32.5 million and core income of $30.5 million, representing a year-over-year increase in earnings despite a deliberate slowdown in premiums written to manage catastrophe exposure targets. Revenues grew approximately 14-16% driven by increased net premiums earned from stepping down the gross quota share ceded rate from 20% to 15%, partially offset by higher operating costs and acquisition expenses of $5.6 million. Management reverted to normal operations on October 1, expecting a premium rebound in Q4, but noted that pricing headwinds persist with rates still down roughly 9-13% since year-end.

negative_highlights: Net investment income fell to $4.3 million from $9.1 million in the prior quarter, driven by a $5.1 million increase in capital gains-based incentive fees.
Weighted average yield on debt investments declined to 13.4% from 14.1% during the quarter.
A $29.9 million realized loss was incurred on the J.R. Hobbs restructuring.
positive_highlights: Total investment income rose to $25.3 million from $23.5 million in the prior quarter.
NAV per share increased to $13.53 from $12.99 at prior quarter-end, aided by $1.42 per share of net unrealized appreciation.
Nonaccrual investments reduced from four to three companies, representing 1.7% of the portfolio at fair value after J.R. Hobbs restructuring.
summary: Gladstone Investment (GAINZ notes) reported Q2 FY2026 total investment income of $25.3 million, up from $23.5 million in the prior quarter, but net investment income fell to $4.3 million from $9.1 million due to a $5.1 million capital-gains-based incentive fee and higher interest expense. Adjusted NII was flat at $0.24 per share, covering the $0.08 monthly distribution. NAV rose to $13.53 from $12.99, and the number of nonaccrual companies was reduced from four to three after a J.R. Hobbs restructuring that produced a $29.9 million realized loss but established a new $20 million interest-bearing term loan. Management cited a healthy buyout pipeline and continued monthly distributions, while noting tariff and economic uncertainty and no formal guidance.

negative_highlights: Q4 full-year guide implies a step-back in sequential top-line growth compared to recent quarters, with worldwide midpoint suggesting ~6% sequential increase.
New sales reps are still ramping up; CEO noted they have not yet reached expected productivity levels and require 6-12 months to fully contribute.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 10% YoY to $14.7 million driven by expansion into new territories and accounts.
Gross margin expanded to 87%, supported by higher ASPs (north of $31,000) and manufacturing efficiencies reducing cost per unit.
Full-year guidance raised on both revenue and margins despite narrowing the range due to caution in Q4 sequential growth.
summary: CVRx reported Q3 FY2025 revenue of $14.7 million (up 10% YoY) and gross margin expansion to 87%. Management raised full-year 2025 guidance for total revenue ($55.6M-$56.6M vs prior $55M-$57M), gross margin (85%-86%), and operating expenses, citing improved sales force productivity and reimbursement tailwinds from the new Category I CPT code.

negative_highlights: Operating profit declined by $27 million year-over-year due to lower volumes and tariffs.
Backlog fell to $1.35 billion from $1.65 billion in Q2.
Management expects further backlog degradation and softness in near-term demand.
positive_highlights: Bookings rose to $380 million in Q3, up from $330 million in Q2.
EMEA revenues increased year-over-year on higher truck sales and currency.
Operating cash flow improved by nearly 25% sequentially on better inventory.
summary: In Q3 FY2025, Hyster-Yale's lift truck revenues fell 4% year-over-year to $929 million, with operating profit down $27 million due to lower volumes and $40 million in gross tariff costs, only partially offset by pricing. Bookings rose to $380 million from $330 million in Q2, but backlog dropped sharply to $1.35 billion from $1.65 billion due to shipments outpacing bookings. Management guided for further softness in demand and additional backlog deterioration, with near-term profitability expected to decline before improving in early 2026 as tariff-affected backlog clears.

negative_highlights: Gross premiums written decreased about 5% in Q3 driven by a non-renewal of a roughly $50 million PI account.
Net premiums earned declined 10.4% in Q3 and 8.1% for the first nine months due to lower volume and reinstatement impacts.
positive_highlights: S&P upgraded financial rating to A with a stable outlook, opening doors for new business.
Reinsurance segment underwriting income increased significantly by 35% QoQ and 50% YoY due to focus on higher margin areas.
Prior year development was favorable in Q3, amounting to $10.5 million.
summary: IGIC reported Q3 FY2025 net income of $33.5 million and EPS of $0.75, missing the prior year's $34.5 million due to currency revaluation impacts and reinstatement premiums. Gross premiums written declined approximately 5% in the quarter driven by a non-renewal of a large PI account and lower volume in the long-tail segment, while the combined ratio improved to 76.5% primarily due to positive currency revaluation. Management noted increasing competitive pressures across the market and warned that top-line growth may contract in certain areas as they exercise discipline to protect profitability.

negative_highlights: International Diagnostics business is expected to see revenue in the low-to-mid-$30 million range, representing an approximate 20% decline compared to a record 2024.

U.S. Diagnostics business faces budgetary uncertainty and staffing reductions at federal agencies (HHS, CDC), leading to expectations of only a low single-digit percentage revenue decline for the full year.
Sample Management anticipates a sequential revenue decline in Q4 consistent with typical seasonal ordering patterns.

Core Sample Management revenue grew year-over-year excluding the decline from one large consumer genetics customer.
OTI signed a definitive agreement to acquire BioMedomics for $4 million upfront, adding Sickle SCAN testing capabilities.
summary: OraSure reported Q3 FY2025 revenue of $27.1 million and core revenue of $27.0 million, resulting in a GAAP operating loss of $16.1 million against full-year guidance for the International Diagnostics business to decline approximately 20% due to inventory destocking and funding uncertainty. Management provided Q4 guidance of $25-28 million with gross margins expected in the low 40s, citing seasonality and a shift toward lower-margin international revenue as key headwinds.

negative_highlights: Management explicitly stated execution on the $11.5B pipeline will be limited to asset recycling due to current cost of capital constraints.
CEO noted that achieving full external growth targets requires a 'green light from the market' which is currently absent, limiting deal flow despite an active underwriting process.
Full-year AFFO guidance range ($39.0M-$45.8M) implies minimal sequential improvement over Q3 results compared to analyst expectations of significant lease-up driven jumps.

Credit facility amended to extend revolver maturity to October 2029 and remove a 10 bps SOFR credit spread, lowering effective interest rates.
Portfolio occupancy increased to 95.2% with strong visibility on near-term lease-ups targeting 96% by year-end.
summary: Global Medical REIT reported Q3 FY2025 FFO of $14.5M ($1/share) and Adjusted FFO of $16.2M ($1.12/share), representing a 4% per share growth versus the prior year equivalent, while same-store NOI grew 2.7%. Management provided full-year AFFO guidance in the range of $39.0M to $45.8M (implied EPS roughly consistent with Q3 run rates) and reiterated that external acquisitions will be limited until capital markets improve or asset recycling proceeds are available.

summary: Lifetime Brands reported Q3 FY2025 consolidated sales down 6.5% to $171.9 million, with a net loss of $1.2 million ($0.05 per diluted share) versus net income of $0.3 million ($0.02) a year earlier. Adjusted EPS fell to $0.11 from $0.21, adjusted income from operations dropped to $11.5 million from $13.2 million, and consolidated gross margin contracted to 35.1% from 36.7%. No explicit guidance was issued, though management expects Q4 shipments to two of its three largest customers to rebound as orders shifted out of Q3, with a slightly down holiday season and some tariff mitigation still to flow through pricing.
