Genentech opened 8 GAlette clinical sites in the past six months (15 total) versus only 1 new site in all of 2024
WDI partnership expected to fund up to $12M of ReSonance preclinical costs, plus potential ~$7M non-dilutive CIRM grant and ~$37M warrant capital tied to Roche/Genentech advancement
summary: Q3 FY2025 total revenue was $3.7M versus $3.8M a year ago, operating loss was $3.8M (in line with the prior-year period), and net loss widened to $29.8M or $0.13 per share from $3.0M or $0.02, driven by a $26.6M noncash warrant liability remeasurement. Cash at September 30 was $40.5M with runway extended to Q2 2027, one quarter longer than prior guidance, aided by cash received from the new William Demant Invest collaboration. The quarter carries no product revenue events; OpRegen remains with Roche/Genentech (15 GAlette sites now open, 8 added in six months), the CIRM CLIN2 decision is expected at the December 11 ICOC meeting, and the T1D islet-cell go/no-go is expected next quarter.

negative_highlights: Total revenue declined 1% year-over-year due to a significant drop in Dry Eye segment sales.
Surgical Glaucoma gross margin remained flat at 87%, offset by $0.4 million in tariff-related costs of goods sold.
Dry Eye gross margin contracted significantly from 48% to 38% primarily due to higher overhead cost per unit.
positive_highlights: Surgical Glaucoma revenue grew 6% year-over-year, driven by increased ordering accounts (up 8%) and higher average note prices from OMNI Edge adoption.
Management raised full-year 2025 revenue guidance to $76-78 million after previously guiding for $72-76 million.
New Medicare fee schedules established in two jurisdictions ($1,142 payment rate) enable the company to pioneer a reimbursed market for interventional dry eye procedures.
summary: Sight Sciences reported Q3 FY2025 revenue of $19.9 million (down 1% YoY), driven by a 6% increase in Surgical Glaucoma ($19.7M) and a decline in Dry Eye ($0.2M). Management raised full-year 2025 revenue guidance to $76-78 million from the prior range of $72-76 million, citing strong Q3 execution and new Medicare fee schedules for TearCare. Adjusted operating expenses were lowered by 17% YoY due to restructuring costs ($2.8M) and reduced stock-based compensation.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA declined 1.4% YoY to $5.6 million due to approximately $1.8 million of excess medical costs incurred year-to-date.
Healthcare Q3 gross margin contracted from 31.2% to 30.0%, and non-school revenue fell 11.3% due to lower summer session demand.
Cash flow from operations was disappointing in Q3, driven by administrative collection issues with two large school clients.
positive_highlights: Record 2026 engineering backlog reached just over $70 million, a significant increase from last year's $21 million.
Healthcare September gross profit grew over 20% versus the prior year following a slow summer start.
Energy Services delivered its best quarter in history with gross profit growing 17.3% and backlog expanding rapidly.
summary: RCM reported Q3 FY2025 consolidated gross profit of $19.4 million (up 8.8% YoY) and Adjusted EPS of $0.42 (flat), while Adjusted EBITDA declined slightly to $5.5 million due to approximately $1.8 million in excess medical costs year-to-date. Management noted a slow start in Healthcare from lower summer session revenue but highlighted strong September performance, record 2026 engineering backlog of over $70 million, and robust growth in Energy Services (gross profit up 17.3%). The company reiterated expectations for Q4 to yield the highest quarterly gross profit and EBITDA of fiscal 2025.

negative_highlights: Total revenue declined 2% year-over-year to $115 million, reflecting the broader macroeconomic downturn in hiring.
Revenue per paid employer fell 4% year-over-year despite sequential gains from performance-based segments.
positive_highlights: Performance-based revenue increased 12% quarter-over-quarter, driven by higher enterprise campaign optimization tool adoption (up 19%).
Quarterly paid employers reached 67,000, marking the first year-over-year growth since Q1 '22 and three consecutive quarters of sequential employer growth.
Site visits from generative AI models surged 140% sequentially as a new traffic channel.
summary: ZipRecruiter reported Q3 FY2025 revenue of $115 million, a sequential increase but a year-over-year decline, which exceeded the midpoint of guidance despite a persistently soft labor market and low hiring rates. Management raised full-year adjusted EBITDA margin expectations to mid-single digits (implied 9%) by citing Q4 seasonality and stable macro assumptions, noting that revenue growth has returned for the first time since Q3 '22 at the current quarter's midpoint guidance of $109-$115 million. While performance-based revenue grew sequentially due to enterprise adoption, overall top-line momentum remains constrained by a modest decline in hiring trends.

negative_highlights: GAAP net loss of $0.07 per share and distributable loss of $0.15 per share; distributable earnings prior to realized gains/losses only $0.04 per share
A $170 million 4-rated Colorado multifamily loan moved to non-accrual with a $4.5 million accrued-interest reversal, and management said NII will remain 'lumpy'
Term Loan B amendment requires a $150 million paydown and covenant waivers through March 31, 2026, lowering cash to roughly $230-235 million; no refinancing finalized
positive_highlights: Total resolutions reached $2.3 billion year-to-date, exceeding the ~$2 billion target, including 9 watch-list loans totaling $1.1 billion UPB
Liquidity rose $283 million to $385 million as of November 4, and net debt-to-equity fell to 1.9x from 2.4x at year-end 2024
Outstanding financings reduced $376 million in Q3 and $1.4 billion year-to-date through November 4
summary: CMTG reported a Q3 2025 GAAP net loss of $0.07 per share and a distributable loss of $0.15 per share, with distributable earnings prior to realized gains/losses of $0.04 per share. The held-for-investment loan portfolio fell to $4.3 billion from $5 billion at June 30 on four resolutions, and net debt-to-equity improved to 1.9x from 2.2x. Management gave no explicit earnings guidance and noted NII may stay 'lumpy' near term while watch-list loans are worked out, guiding only qualitatively toward a Term Loan B solution in 'the coming months.' The key change was the $150 million Term Loan B paydown with covenant waivers through March 31, 2026, which cuts liquidity to roughly $230-235 million, alongside a $170 million Colorado multifamily loan moved to non-accrual.

negative_highlights: Full-year UPB growth guidance lowered from '10-plus percent' to a range of 5%-10% due to higher prepayment speeds and runoff.
Rithm subservicing portfolio is being transferred in Q1 2026 as it became uneconomical, contributing losses for the last two quarters.
positive_highlights: Originations volume grew 39% year-over-year and 26% sequentially, exceeding industry growth rates.
Adjusted pretax income of $31 million was the positive for the 12th straight quarter.
Book value per share increased to $62, up 5% versus the prior year.
summary: Onity Group reported Q3 FY2025 adjusted pretax income of $31 million and GAAP EPS of $2.03, driven by record originations volume (up 39% YoY) and strong servicing growth despite higher runoff. Management raised full-year guidance for UPB growth to a range of 5%-10%, narrowing from the prior '10-plus percent' outlook due to mix shifts toward higher-margin commercial subservicing, while expecting to exceed adjusted ROE guidance.

negative_highlights: Expected Q3 tax-credit monetization slipped: only $10M of 45Z and $12M of ITCs are in the sale process, versus ~$40M of 2025 45Z management said it could have sold if the DOE calculation were correct
Interest expense steady at ~$13M and cash just $5.6M at quarter end after $4.1M of capex; the ~$266M debt refinance is now a 1H 2026 event with no close this quarter
LCFS pathway approvals were cited as occurring in Q2, and four additional pathways remain under CARB review; India OMC contracts of $58 million (with ~$18M profit) were not performed by the OMCs
positive_highlights: Revenue rose ~$7M sequentially to $59.2M, with India biofuels contributing $14.5M and ethanol production up at 14.7 million gallons
Seven digester LCFS pathways approved at average -384 CI, lifting LCFS credit revenue 160% for those dairies starting Q3
$83 million of ITCs sold to date with >$70 million cash received; MVR project expected to cut natural gas use 80% and add ~$32 million annual cash flow from mid-2026
summary: Revenue of $59.2 million rose about $7 million sequentially on India biodiesel fulfillment plus stronger ethanol and pricing; operating loss improved on higher volumes and lower SG&A, but interest expense held near $13 million and cash was only $5.6 million at quarter end. Management did not report EPS, gross margin, or updated formal guidance. Expected Q4 45Z/48 credit monetization slipped: $10 million of 45Z and $12 million of ITCs are now 'in the sale process' versus prior expectations of Q3 monetization, and the DOE 45Z calculation remains outstanding. Management still guided to strong Q4 operating cash flow, >500,000 MMBtu RNG capacity exiting 2025, an India IPO in early 2026 at $100-$200 million valuation, and a debt refinance in 1H 2026.

New oral on-demand HAE competition (sebetralstat) launched in July, though management cites continued RUCONEST prescriber and patient growth
Opex guidance of $304-308 million remains unchanged and includes ~$7 million in one-time G&A restructuring costs
positive_highlights: Full-year 2025 revenue guidance raised to $365-375 million from $335-350 million, implying 23-26% growth
Q3 operating profit reached $16.0 million versus $4.1 million a year ago, with gross margin expanding to 93% from 91%
Joenja revenue rose 35% YoY to $15.1 million, with 13 new APDS patients identified in Q3 and 54 pediatric patients already diagnosed
summary: Q3 2025 total revenue rose 30% YoY to $97.3 million, with RUCONEST up 29% to $82 million and Joenja up 35% to $15.1 million; gross margin expanded to 93% from 91%, operating profit grew to $16.0 million from $4.1 million, and operating cash flow was $32 million, lifting cash and marketable securities to $168.9 million. Management raised full-year 2025 revenue guidance to $365-375 million from $335-350 million, implying 23-26% growth, while leaving opex guidance at $304-308 million. The quarter's key changes included the planned withdrawal of RUCONEST from certain ex-U.S. markets, a G&A headcount reduction, and the expected January 31, 2026 PDUFA date for the pediatric Joenja label expansion.

summary: In Q3 FY2025, WeightWatchers reported results after emerging from financial reorganization, with the CEO positioning the company for renewed growth. Management highlighted strategic priorities including a digital rebuild, brand refresh, and expansion of medical offerings, while noting that Q3 2025 is expected to be the trough for clinic end-of-period subscribers. Guidance implies a subscriber step-up from Q4 to Q1, but the CFO cautioned that behavioral acquisition challenges, though improved, remain a headwind for 2026. The transcript omits specific revenue, EPS, and margin figures, so performance scoring is limited to qualitative commentary.

negative_highlights: Commission income decreased to $2.5 million from $3.4 million due to the Fortman divestiture and lower medical commission revenues.
Adjusted EBITDA loss widened to $700,000 compared to a gain of $40,000 in the prior year.
Salaries and wages increased to $3.9 million from $1.7 million primarily due to noncash equity grants.
positive_highlights: Completed the sale of Fortman Insurance Services for an approximate $3 million gain.
Unrestricted cash increased by approximately 590% to $2.6 million compared to the prior fiscal year-end.
summary: Reliance Global Group reported a net loss of $1.2 million for Q3 FY2025 compared to a prior year loss of $0.8 million, driven by the sale of Fortman Insurance Services which reduced commission income to $2.5 million from $3.4 million. The company completed the asset sale for an approximate $3 million gain and used proceeds to reduce long-term debt by 50%, resulting in a significant increase in unrestricted cash ($2.6 million) and equity ($6.8 million). Management declared a special cash dividend of $0.03 per share payable on December 2, 2025.

negative_highlights: Backlog fell to $1.2 billion after removing $197 million from two projects, one rescinded and one rebid.
GAAP net loss of $3.7 million and GAAP EPS loss of $0.13, though improved from a $0.33 loss a year ago.
Process and Industrial Facilities segment revenue declined to $27.9 million from $31.4 million, with gross margin contracting to 5.1% from 6.4%.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 28% YoY to $211.9 million, driven by LNG storage and power delivery projects.
Consolidated gross margin expanded to 6.7% from 4.7%, the highest quarterly gross margin in over two years.
Adjusted EBITDA swung to positive $2.5 million from a $5.9 million loss a year ago, and adjusted EPS was nearly breakeven at a loss of $0.01.
summary: Matrix Service reported Q1 FY2026 revenue of $211.9 million, up 28% YoY, with consolidated gross margin of 6.7% versus 4.7% a year ago. Adjusted EPS was a loss of $0.01 (GAAP loss of $0.13 including $3.3 million restructuring costs), and adjusted EBITDA turned positive at $2.5 million. Management reiterated FY2026 revenue guidance of $875–$925 million, with 90%+ of revenue booked at the midpoint, but backlog was reduced by $197 million from two rescinded/rebid projects, ending at $1.2 billion with book-to-bill of 0.9. The quarter showed strong revenue growth and margin expansion offset by the large backlog adjustment and continued net loss.

negative_highlights: Enterprise ARR growth slowed as the company noted it was 'a little bit further along in bookings' than expected, reflecting softer demand for replatforming.
Q4 revenue guidance range was widened by approximately $5 million compared to prior expectations due to caution around holiday consumer performance.

Operating cash flow reached approximately $11 million, marking the second consecutive quarter of double-digit margins and demonstrating strong operating leverage.

summary: Commerce reported Q3 revenue of $86 million in line with guidance and non-GAAP operating income of $8 million exceeding the high end of its profitability range by nearly $5 million. Management updated full-year 2025 non-GAAP operating income guidance to a midpoint increase from $22 million to $27.2 million, while maintaining revenue guidance unchanged at approximately $341-$346 million despite noting softer demand for replatforming due to AI-driven shifts in merchant focus.

negative_highlights: Mobility revenues declined as the company continues its transition away from legacy products

summary: ATN International reported Q3 FY2025 revenues of $183.2 million (up 3% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $49.9 million (up 9% YoY), driven by operational improvements in the U.S. segment which saw revenue rise 4.6%. Management reaffirmed full-year guidance for revenue at approximately $725 million but refined adjusted EBITDA expectations to be flat to slightly above last year's result of $184 million, citing continued cost containment and minor restructuring costs.

negative_highlights: Rig count reduced to 1, Wells drilled down roughly one-third from Q1/Q2

CEO acknowledged 'debt is high' and market confidence eroded
positive_highlights: Production levels consistent with Q2 despite reduced activity

summary: HighPeak reported Q3 2025 results that tracked internal expectations, with production consistent with Q2 despite reduced activity, CapEx down 30% from Q2, and LOE per BOE held flat. The company ran only 1 rig during the quarter, drilled 6 wells, and turned in line 9 wells, with the second rig repickup delayed until mid-October. CEO Mike Hollis acknowledged high debt, poor governance history, and past 'growth at all costs' mentality, outlining a long-term plan focused on debt reduction, free cash flow, and disciplined capital allocation, with scenarios tied to oil prices. The company also announced a share distribution plan over the next two years and expects 16-18 DUCs to support Q1-Q2 2026 production.

negative_highlights: Q3 total revenue fell 18.7% YoY due to timing of hardware deliveries from large cell phone contract.

Operating expenses increased 24.8% on higher SG&A and R&D.

Monitoring revenue grew $422,000 to a record $1.560 million, gross margin expanded to 78.5% from 71.7%, and net income dropped to $252,000 ($0.10 per diluted share) from $725,000 ($0.29) due to lower revenue and higher expenses. negative_highlights: Q4 guidance of $38.75-40.75M total revenue implies a sequential decline from Q3's $40.9M, and adjusted EBITDA is guided to -$3.5M to -$1.5M versus -$0.3M this quarter
Operating cash flow for the first nine months was -$15.7M versus -$10.8M a year earlier
Adjusted EBITDA breakeven target remains Q4 2026, with no pull-forward despite the near-breakeven quarter

Adjusted EBITDA improved $4.2M YoY to -$0.3M (-1% margin) from -$12% margin, and gross margin expanded to 77% from 74%
Customers using Cecilia AI more than tripled YoY, and one Am Law 50 customer grew Cecilia matters 7x with more than 12x related revenue growth
summary: Q3 total revenue was $40.9M, up 13% YoY, with software revenue of $35.2M, up 17% YoY. Results exceeded the high end of guidance for software revenue, total revenue and adjusted EBITDA, though they included $1.3M of one-time contingent case revenue; excluding it, total revenue grew 9% and software 13%, still above guidance. Adjusted EBITDA improved to -$0.3M (-1% margin) from -$4.2M a year earlier, with gross margin at 77% versus 74%. Q4 guidance is $38.75-40.75M total revenue and adjusted EBITDA of -$3.5M to -$1.5M, with FY25 revenue of $154.4-156.4M; the contingent case was already included in the prior full-year guide.

negative_highlights: Economic book value per share declined 1.9% to $12.72 from $12.97 on markups of sold-bond liabilities from the 2021-4/2021-7 deals
Distributable earnings of $529,000 were far below the $11.4 million GAAP net income and the $0.32 dividend, with the gap driven by $9.3 million of unrealized gains
Total NII grew only 2% QoQ, and competition in the space was acknowledged to have increased
positive_highlights: Net interest income grew 13% YoY and 2% QoQ to $10.2 million; interest income rose 34% YoY to $36.7 million
Operating expenses excluding securitization and stock comp fell 13% YoY (19% YTD) to $2.8 million
90-plus day delinquencies fell 15 bps QoQ to 2.2%; GAAP book value per share rose 2.2% to $10.60
summary: AOMR reported Q3 2025 GAAP net income of $11.4 million, or $0.46 per diluted share, with interest income of $36.7 million (+34% YoY) and net interest income of $10.2 million (+13% YoY, +2% QoQ). Results were described as in line with expectations; GAAP book value per share rose 2.2% to $10.60 while economic book value fell 1.9% to $12.72. Management gave no formal numeric guidance but reiterated an expected NII growth trend from loan purchases and Q4 securitization activity, and kept the $0.32 dividend unchanged. Key actions included calling two legacy securitizations ($19 million released), a new and extended warehouse facility, and the October $274 million AOMT 2025-10 deal that paid down $237 million of warehouse debt.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined 4% year-over-year to $60 million, with Q4 guidance implying a further 4–5% decline
cRPO declined mid-single digits excluding the data partnership, and net dollar retention is expected to decline year-over-year
Upsell and downsell pressure persists in the life sciences space, with no notable improvement expected near-term
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA of $18.9 million (32% margin) was $2 million above the high end of guidance
Enterprise customer count grew by 10 sequentially to 520, the highest since Q3 of last year
Full-year guidance midpoint raised on both revenue and non-GAAP profit, with adjusted EBITDA midpoint up $3 million
summary: Definitive Healthcare reported Q3 FY2025 revenue of $60 million, down 4% year-over-year, at the high end of guidance, with adjusted EBITDA of $18.9 million (32% margin) and non-GAAP EPS of $0.07, both above the high end of guidance. The company raised the midpoint of its full-year revenue and profit guidance, now expecting revenue of $239–240 million and adjusted EBITDA of $68–69 million, but Q4 guidance of $59–60 million implies a continued mid-single-digit decline. cRPO of $165 million grew about 1% year-over-year as reported but declined mid-single digits excluding a data partnership, and net dollar retention is expected to modestly decline for the year, with upcoming December/January renewals representing over 30% of annual renewals. Positives included enterprise customer count rising to 520 and improved renewal rates, while life sciences downsell pressure and macro caution remain headwinds.

The dominant event was the pending Peak/Powder River Basin acquisition, with shareholder vote set for November 12 and contingent consideration of 2.5 million shares now expected at closing after BLM permit reissuance. Preliminary 2026 capital plans include about $20 million on Peak assets, roughly $6 million net for two Permian wells, and $13 million in the Marcellus, though management flagged that some Marcellus capital may slip into 2027. Marcellus volumes were curtailed during the quarter on sub-$2 gas prices but have staged back as November pricing firmed.

negative_highlights: Merchant Solutions same-store sales decelerated, with revenue growth moderating to just 2% due to pullbacks in restaurants, construction, and wholesale trade.
Full-year revenue guidance was lowered from a prior range of $970-$990 million to reflect the weaker Merchant performance.
Merchant Solutions gross margins contracted by 50 basis points year-over-year to 21.9% due to lower residual purchases.

summary: Priority Technology Holdings reported Q3 FY2025 net revenue of $241.4 million (up 6% YoY) and adjusted EPS of $0.28 (up 56% YoY). Management revised full-year revenue guidance downward to a range of $950-$965 million due to slower growth in Merchant Solutions, while raising the low end of gross profit guidance to reflect margin expansion driven by Payables and Treasury segments. The company ended with over 1.7 million customer accounts and generated $29 million in free cash flow.

Legacy Outbrain business faced a $10 million headwind from supply cleanup and continued page view declines on partner sites.

Cross-note revenue showed notable inflection with October bookings growing more than 55% month-over-month.
AI and algorithmic improvements from the merger are expected to drive nonlinear performance improvements in 2026.

Management lowered Q4 guidance for Ex-TAC gross profit ($142m-$152m) and adjusted EBITDA ($26m-$36m) citing increased caution regarding advertiser planning cycles and muted end-of-quarter performance. The company is executing a transformation plan targeting $35 million in annualized incremental EBITDA starting in Q4.

negative_highlights: Average realized RIN price dropped 31.4% to $2.29, significantly impacting revenue and operating profit.

Renewable electricity generation operating income improved to a $0.2 million loss from a $0.6 million loss in the prior year quarter.

Management maintained full-year 2025 production guidance but noted that EPA rulemaking delays and government shutdown impacts could extend finalization of renewable volume obligations into 2026.

negative_highlights: Cash runway does not include Phase III costs; management acknowledges need for capital or partnership.
CENDIFOX final data timing is controlled by investigator, creating uncertainty.
CEO candidly noted the stock has not responded to positive data due to macro headwinds and low float.

Cash runway extended into Q1 2027, excluding Phase III costs.
BOLSTER first-line enrollment completed 6 months ahead of plan, accelerating top-line readout to Q4 2025.
summary: Lisata reported Q3 2025 operating expenses of $4.4 million, down 17.3% year-over-year, R&D expenses down 22.9% to $2 million, and net loss of $4.2 million versus $4.9 million in Q3 2024. Cash stood at approximately $19 million, supporting operations into Q1 2027, with Phase III ASCEND trial costs not included in that runway. Key data readouts (ASCEND final, iLSTA final) are expected in Q1 2026, and the company signed a nonexclusive license with Catalent for ADC payload use and a strategic alliance with GATC Health for AI-driven drug discovery.

negative_highlights: Product gross profit swung to negative $6.8 million, including a $5.5 million VSAT inventory write-down and $1.6 million of price-driven losses

summary: Service revenue rose to $25.4 million, up 10% sequentially and 4% year over year, with subscribing vessels up 11% sequentially to about 9,000 (26% YTD) and record ~1,600 terminal shipments. Product gross profit swung to negative $6.8 million from positive $0.3 million, including a $5.5 million VSAT inventory write-down plus $1.6 million from Starlink and H-Series price cuts, and airtime gross margin fell to 31.9% from 35.8% on GEO pressure. Adjusted EBITDA was $1.4 million, down from $2.7 million in Q2, while cash rose $16.9 million to $72.8 million on $7.8 million in facility sale proceeds. No formal guidance was issued, but management expects product margins to improve modestly in Q4, GEO margin pressure to persist until minimum bandwidth commitments drop by about one-third in January 2026, and the Asia Pacific acquisition to add a net ~500 vessels in Q4.

negative_highlights: No revenue figure was reported or discussed on the call, and no revenue guidance was provided for 2026

Commercial pipeline metrics improved sharply (prospects ~600 vs. ~100, quotes tripled, contracts doubled to 12 YTD), but no revenue figure was disclosed and full-year cash burn guidance was reiterated at the high end of $27-29 million rather than raised. Management framed 2026 as an expected inflection point for revenue growth without providing specific revenue guidance.

summary: Q3 2025 revenue rose 24% YoY to $76.6 million and gross profit climbed 38% to $10 million, but operating profit fell to $6.8 million from $19.7 million (which included $13.6 million of 2024 business-interruption insurance recoveries) and net income dropped to $13.3 million ($1.78/share) from $15.6 million ($2.14). Full-year 2025 operating profit will be below 2024, with Q4 consolidated operating profit guided roughly flat YoY, but management expects meaningful YoY improvements in operating profit and net income in 2026; a Q4 pension termination will trigger a noncash settlement charge. Utility Coal results remain pressured by the Mississippi Lignite contract formula until it begins to rectify in 2026, while debt fell to $80.2 million from $99.5 million at year-end 2024.

Healthcare Services EBITDA impacted by approximately $20 million reimbursement headwind, with majority hitting fiscal Q2, pushing that segment to breakeven.

Senior segment revenue declined 37% to $59 million, with EBITDA loss of $21 million, in line with expectations, and Life revenue grew nearly 20%. Management kept the full-year revenue ($1.65-1.75 billion) and adjusted EBITDA ($120-150 million) outlook unchanged, but now expects Healthcare Services EBITDA to be approximately breakeven in Q2, and they no longer expect to hit the $50 million fiscal 2026 target for that segment. They also expect to exit fiscal 2026 with an annualized Healthcare Services EBITDA run rate of $40-50 million.

Distributable earnings were just a couple of pennies below full dividend coverage.
positive_highlights: Net debt-to-equity ratio decreased to 1.1x from 1.2x quarter-over-quarter.
Outstanding borrowings reduced by 9% QoQ and 40% YoY to $811 million.
CECL reserve declined to $117 million, down approximately $2 million from the prior quarter.
summary: ACRE reported Q3 FY2025 GAAP net income of $5 million ($0.08 EPS) and distributable earnings of $6 million ($0.10 EPS), excluding a $1.6 million realized loss on a loan restructuring. The company reduced its net debt-to-equity ratio to 1.1x and outstanding borrowings to $811 million while collecting $498 million in repayments year-to-date. Management declared a regular Q4 dividend payable January 15, 2026, with an annualized yield of approximately 14%.

100% of contractual rents collected; projected 2025 AFFO of $72.7 million is up 28.2% YoY, and portfolio is 91.5% skilled nursing
summary: Strawberry Fields REIT reported Q3 2025 revenue up $10.2 million YoY on acquisitions and retenanting, with net income of $8.8 million or $0.16 per share versus $6.9 million or $0.14 a year earlier; YTD revenue was $114.9 million, up $28.3 million. 11 revenue-bearing contracts in ECO Synthesis, up from 1 a year ago

They announced a strategic shift toward ECO Synthesis and ligase businesses, reducing headcount and small molecule biocatalysis sales efforts, extending cash runway through 2027. A new CEO transition was announced, with Alison Moore succeeding Stephen Dilly.

summary: Puma Biotechnology reported Q3 FY2025 net product revenue of $51.9 million (up from $49.2M in Q2) and GAAP EPS of $0.18 per share, driven by a quarter-over-quarter increase but down year-over-year due to the absence of China supply revenue compared to last year's peak. summary: Holley reported Q3 FY2025 net sales of $138.4 million with 6.4% core business growth, marking the third consecutive quarter of growth, with broad-based gains across all divisions and channels. Net leverage fell below 4x to 3.9x, the first time since 2022, and the company prepaid $10 million post-quarter, totaling $100 million in prepayments since September 2023. Management reaffirmed its outlook with guidance for continued growth, maintaining gross margins above 40% and adjusted EBITDA margins of 20%.

positive_highlights: Pulp sales volumes rose 26,000 tonnes to 453,000 tonnes in Q3

Mass timber backlog ~$80 million with ~$400 million of project inquiries over the last two quarters; management expects mass timber sales to grow from ~$60 million this year to ~$130 million next year
summary: Mercer reported Q3 FY2025 negative EBITDA of $28 million (including a $20 million noncash inventory impairment), wider than the negative $21 million in Q2, with both pulp (-$13M) and solid wood (-$9M) segments negative; net loss was $81 million or $1.21 per share versus a $1.29 loss last quarter. Pulp prices fell across all markets (China NBSK net price down $44 to $690/tonne; North American NBSK list down $120 to $1,700) and cash consumption rose to $48 million from $35 million. Management said headwinds will persist into Q4, expects only modest NBSK price improvement late in Q4 into Q1 2026, sees Q4 fiber cost increases, and is cutting costs including roughly $100 million 2025 CapEx and meaningfully lower 2026 CapEx (~$75 million starting point), plus working capital and cost-reduction actions. Liquidity stood at $376 million ($98 million cash, $278 million undrawn), with management acknowledging the environment is not ideal for asset divestitures.

negative_highlights: Fintech non-GAAP gross margin declined to 68% from 97% a year ago due to revenue mix and lower-margin payment processing
GAAP operating loss from continuing operations remained $9.7 million
Full year 2026 guidance of $32 million+ excludes new products such as private label credit cards, leaving limited visibility on those call options
positive_highlights: Q3 net revenue of $4.4 million beat the September 2025 guidance by $0.4 million, or 10%
Fintech revenue grew 28% quarter-over-quarter, with payments up 50% and credit up 22%
G&A expenses fell $2.3 million, or 22.3%, year-over-year; net loss improved to $0.26 per share from $0.41
summary: PublicSquare reported Q3 FY2025 net revenue from continuing operations of $4.4 million, up 37% year-over-year and beating its September 2025 guidance by $0.4 million, or 10%. Fintech revenue rose 28% quarter-over-quarter, with payments up 50% and credit up 22%; net loss improved to $0.26 per share from $0.41, and G&A fell 22.3% year-over-year. Management reaffirmed Q4 2025 revenue guidance of approximately $6 million and full year 2026 revenue guidance of at least $32 million, while fintech non-GAAP gross margin declined to 68% from 97% on revenue mix. The company is progressing the sale of its Brands segment, targeting a purchase agreement by the end of Q4 2025, and continues to explore a sale or repurposing of Marketplace IP.

negative_highlights: Total revenue fell 9.8% year-over-year to $8.5 million from $9.4 million, and franchise royalties declined to $8.1 million from $9.0 million.
System-wide sales declined to $133.6 million from $148.6 million year-over-year.
Several MRINetwork franchisees did not renew agreements, pressuring year-over-year comparisons, and permanent placement and executive search continue to lag.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to 55% from 52% last year, and adjusted net income rose to $3.4 million or $0.24 per diluted share from $2.8 million or $0.20.
Core SG&A was flat at $4.6 million and total SG&A fell to $5.1 million from $5.4 million, helped by a workers' comp benefit of just under $100,000 versus a $500,000 net expense last year.
Net debt fell to about $1.1 million, down roughly $1 million from Q2 and about $11 million from 9/30/2024, with about $42.5 million of credit availability.
summary: HireQuest reported Q3 FY2025 total revenue of $8.5 million, down 9.8% year-over-year, with franchise royalties of $8.1 million versus $9.0 million and system-wide sales of $133.6 million versus $148.6 million. Net income was $2.3 million or $0.16 per share versus a prior-year net loss, while adjusted net income rose to $3.4 million or $0.24 per share and adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to 55% from 52%, aided by a workers' comp benefit and expense control. No explicit forward guidance was provided, but management said day labor appears to be 'approaching the bottom' and that MRI active franchisees were nearly flat versus the prior-year period after earlier nonrenewals. Results reflect continued demand softness and revenue contraction, partially offset by profitability and margin gains.

negative_highlights: Gain on sale margin guidance for Q4 is lower at 300-325 bps vs 339 bps in Q3
Origination volume decreased 3% sequentially to $6.5B
Total expenses increased 6% quarter-over-quarter, partly due to non-recurring prior quarter benefits
positive_highlights: Adjusted net loss narrowed from $16M to $3M quarter-over-quarter
Pull-through weighted rate lock volume up 10% sequentially to $7B
Cash increased by $51M to $459M at quarter-end
summary: In Q3 FY2025, loanDepot reported an adjusted net loss of $3 million, improved from a $16 million loss in Q2, with pull-through weighted rate lock volume of $7 billion (up 10% QoQ) and adjusted total revenue of $325 million (up from $292 million QoQ). Gain on sale margin was 339 bps, within guidance. For Q4, guidance calls for lock volume of $6-8 billion, origination volume of $6.5-8.5 billion, and gain on sale margin of 300-325 bps. Management highlighted leadership and technology changes and reiterated a focus on profitable market share growth, while noting capital structure review over the next 12-18 months.

negative_highlights: Clinical Solutions revenue declined 13% YoY due to lower average order sizes and soft demand from biotech customers.
Management expects only modest improvement in the custom biopharma segment (approx. 25% of total revenue) for FY2026 unless funding improves.
Free cash flow remains negative, with an expected outflow of less than $12 million for full year 2025.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 16% YoY driven by Lab Essentials catalog sales, marking five consecutive quarters of growth.
Gross margin expanded significantly year-over-year from 0.9% to 30.7%, excluding prior quarter inventory charges.
The company expects low double-digit growth in the non-biopharma segments (animal health, life science tools) which comprise roughly 75% of revenue.
summary: Teknova reported Q3 FY2025 revenue of $10.5 million (up 9% YoY), driven by a 16% increase in Lab Essentials catalog products but offset by a decline in Clinical Solutions revenue due to soft biotech demand. Gross margin expanded significantly to 30.7% from the prior year's 0.9%, primarily because of $2.8 million in nonrecurring inventory charges last quarter, though sequential margins were pressured by cost fluctuations. Management reiterated full-year 2025 guidance ($39M-$42M) but warned they expect to finish slightly below the midpoint due to persistent weakness in custom biopharma products.

negative_highlights: Same-store sales dropped 9.9% in Q3 due to tariff impacts and customer traffic downturns.
Cost of goods sold increased by 334 basis points YoY, with meat prices at an all-time high.
Management indicated potential pause on new restaurant openings for the remainder of 2026 if sales trends do not recover.
positive_highlights: Revenue increased 2.7% YoY to $50.4M driven by expansion of the footprint from 33 to 57 stores.
Labor efficiency improved significantly, reducing payroll and benefits as a percentage of sales by 196 basis points year-over-year.
Grocery initiative launched at Albertsons, Vons, and Pavilions with potential for $100M+ annual revenue over the next 4-5 years.
summary: Q3 FY2025 revenue grew 2.7% YoY to $50.4 million driven by new store openings, while same-store sales declined 9.9% due to macro pressures and tariffs. The company reported a net loss of $3.9 million ($0.11 EPS) with restaurant-level adjusted EBITDA margins at 15%, down from the prior year's 18.2%. Management raised full-year revenue guidance to $220-$225 million but explicitly warned they may slow growth plans in 2026 if economic conditions do not improve.

negative_highlights: ReNu Phase III trial did not achieve statistical significance for its primary endpoint despite numerical improvement in pain reduction compared to the first study.
Gross margin contracted slightly from 77% last year to 76%, attributed primarily to a shift in product mix.
positive_highlights: Net product revenue of $150.5M exceeded the high end of Q3 guidance ($130M-$145M).
Advanced Wound Care sales increased 31% year-over-year to $141.5 million.
Surgical & Sports Medicine products grew 25% year-over-year, primarily due to PuraPly family growth.
summary: Q3 FY2025 net product revenue was $150.5 million, beating the high end of guidance and representing a 31% year-over-year increase driven by Advanced Wound Care (up 31%) and Surgical & Sports Medicine products (up 25%). Management raised full-year 2025 financial guidance significantly, updating GAAP net income expectations from a range including losses to $8.6 million-$25.4 million, while also raising adjusted EBITDA guidance.

negative_highlights: Net loss from REO activities was $1.6 million in Q3, primarily driven by a $6.3 million valuation write-down on existing inventory.
The CFO clarified that the REO loss is a timing adjustment to fair value rather than a fundamental deterioration in asset quality.
positive_highlights: Record loan production of $739 million, representing a 32% year-over-year increase in the portfolio netting out prepayments.
Pretax earnings surged 66.5% to a new record level, with core diluted EPS reaching $0.69.
Portfolio NIM remained stable at 360 basis points, exceeding the target of 3.5%, while nonperforming loan rates declined to 9.8%.
summary: Velocity Financial reported a record quarter with production of $739 million and net income up 60% year-over-year to core diluted EPS of $0.69. The company achieved pretax earnings up 66.5%, driven by stable portfolio NIM at 360 bps and strong demand, though it recognized a one-time REO valuation loss of $6.3 million due to timing issues rather than a trend deterioration. Management raised the outlook, citing robust capital markets, market share gains, and a new single-counterparty securitization partnership that diversifies funding sources.

negative_highlights: The supplier transition for the Ferrari business reduced reported automotive royalties by roughly six figures year-to-date
An investor noted a five-year growth rate of minus 3% and asked where the promised car sales were
Black SPD and multiple automotive programs remain not yet in production, with timing repeatedly pushed out
positive_highlights: Automotive and total royalties increased year-over-year and sequentially after excluding onetime 2024 events
Ferrari's minimum annual royalties were exceeded in Q3, so all Ferrari royalties become fully recordable in Q4
Debt-free balance sheet with about $1.13 million in cash and $1.4 million in working capital as of September 30, 2025
summary: Management said automotive and total royalties rose year-over-year and sequentially in Q3 2025 only after backing out onetime 2024 events, and that the Ferrari licensing transition reduced reported automotive royalties by roughly six figures this year until the new supplier's minimum royalties were met in Q3. The company remains debt-free with about $1.13 million in cash and $1.4 million in working capital as of September 30, 2025, and said it has no current plans to raise capital. No quantitative revenue, EPS, or margin figures and no formal guidance were disclosed; the architectural retrofit system debuted at GlassBuild 2025 and Black SPD was described as very, very far along but not yet in production. An investor challenged the company over a five-year growth rate of minus 3% and repeated unmet prior timelines for high-production automotive programs.

negative_highlights: Board adjusted the dividend down to $0.10 per share, a reduction from prior levels.
G&A and compensation expenses rose sequentially by approximately 12.5% due to personnel changes and professional fees.
positive_highlights: NAV increased by approximately $1.1 million (0.5%) relative to June 30 before any ATM capital raised.
summary: Cherry Hill reported GAAP net income of $2 million ($0.05 per share) and NAV growth of approximately 0.5% quarter-over-quarter to $3.36 per share. Management adjusted the dividend down to $0.10 per share, citing a need for more sustainable alignment with earnings power despite positive momentum from their Real Genius partnership.

negative_highlights: LOQTORZI revenue growth decelerated significantly in Q3 compared to the prior quarter as inventory levels flattened.
One of four sales regions remained flat due to post-restructure vacancies and lower share of voice, requiring targeted expansion plans.
No specific financial guidance was provided for LOQTORZI or pipeline assets beyond general revenue targets.
positive_highlights: LOQTORZI net revenue grew to $11.2M with a 92% YoY increase driven by demand growth of ~20% in Q3 after inventory normalization.
Balance sheet significantly strengthened with cash and investments at $192 million following the exit from biosimilar business.
SG&A expenses decreased 11% year-over-year to $24.9M due to headcount reductions, supporting a leaner operational model.
summary: Coherus Oncology reported Q3 FY2025 net revenue of $11.2 million for LOQTORZI, representing a 92% year-over-year increase but down from the prior quarter's growth rate due to inventory normalization and one lagging region. Management reiterated full-year SG&A guidance between $90M-$100M while highlighting balance sheet strength with $192M in cash post-divestiture. Forward progress is driven by clinical data readouts expected in H1 2026 for CHS-114 and casdozokitug, though no specific revenue guidance was provided.

negative_highlights: FMS business revenue faced note weakness in-term delays due to federal budgeting uncertainties, though management remains optimistic about future scaling.
Fourth quarter is expected to be lower than Q3 as the company enters its annual maintenance cycle for aircraft.
positive_highlights: Revenue increased 5% YoY to a record $67.9 million, driven by record task orders and utilization up nearly 10% year-over-year.
Adjusted EBITDA grew 4.5% YoY to $49.1 million, exceeding the upper bound of the annual guidance range.
Completed balance sheet transformation including a $49 million sale-leaseback and a new $331.5 million credit facility to fund fleet expansion.
summary: Bridger Aerospace reported record Q3 FY2025 revenue of $67.9 million (up 5% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $49.1 million, surpassing the top end of its annual guidance range. The company completed a balance sheet transformation with a $49 million sale-leaseback and a new $331.5 million debt facility to fund fleet expansion. Management raised full-year revenue guidance to $118-$123 million (exceeding prior guidance) and expects adjusted EBITDA at the high end of its $42-$48 million range.

negative_highlights: Organic net sales declined 6% year-over-year, with Snacks down 17% and Baby and Kids down 10%.
Adjusted gross margin fell 120 bps to 19.5%, adjusted EBITDA declined to $20 million from $22 million, and adjusted net loss widened to $0.08 per share from $0.04.
International adjusted EBITDA fell 38% to $13 million and gross margin fell 530 bps, while net leverage rose to 4.8x.
positive_highlights: North America adjusted EBITDA rose 37% to $17 million with gross margin up 200 bps to 22.7% on productivity and pricing/trade efficiencies.
SG&A fell 8% year-over-year to $66 million and reduced from 18.1% to 17.8% of net sales as overhead reduction actions took effect.
Free cash flow outflow improved to $14 million from $17 million a year ago, and days payable outstanding rose to 57 days from 55 a year ago.
summary: Hain Celestial reported fiscal Q1 2026 net sales of $368 million and adjusted EBITDA of $20 million, described as in line with expectations and comparable to Q4 2025. Organic net sales declined 6% year-over-year, a sequential improvement from the 11% decline in Q4, driven by a 7-point drop in volume/mix partly offset by 1 point of pricing, with adjusted gross margin down 120 bps to 19.5% and adjusted net loss of $(0.08) per share versus $(0.04) a year ago. The company reiterated it is not providing numeric FY2026 guidance beyond positive free cash flow, citing uncertainty around the strategic review, but expects stronger second-half top and bottom line performance driven by pricing, cost actions and marketing investment. Segment trends were mixed as North America adjusted EBITDA rose 37% to $17 million on margin expansion, while International adjusted EBITDA fell 38% and gross margin declined 530 bps.

negative_highlights: Q3 revenue of $33 million came in at the low end of guidance, with full-year revenue guidance lowered to $161-166 million from $165-180 million
Gross margin contracted to 43.2% from 44.4% on mix and tariff headwinds, with FY margin seen in the low 40s
Management said it is exploring options to improve liquidity, which could include raising capital, and ended Q3 with $24 million cash plus $12 million revolver borrowings
positive_highlights: Q3 adjusted EBITDA loss of $15.7 million beat the high end of guidance, aided by SG&A down 30% YoY to $22 million
Inventories down 25% YoY to $43 million and international distributor transitions now complete
New products such as the Wool Cruiser and waterproof collection exceeded expectations, with early Q4 trends improving as more product launches
summary: Q3 net revenue was $33 million, at the low end of guidance, while adjusted EBITDA loss of $15.7 million slightly beat the high end of guidance. Gross margin fell to 43.2% from 44.4% on higher digital/international distributor mix and U.S. duties. Full-year revenue guidance was cut to $161-166 million from $165-180 million, though the EBITDA midpoint was reiterated, and Q4 revenue is guided flat to up 9% with a much smaller EBITDA loss of $10-16 million. Management cited slower rebuilding of core franchises like the original runner and an uncertain macro backdrop, while also flagging the need to enhance liquidity, potentially including raising capital.

negative_highlights: No financial figures reported for Q3 revenue, EPS, or margins
Clinical data is pending presentation at SITC and not yet fully matured across all endpoints
Breast cancer program remains a single-arm Phase II trial with first patient in expected Q4 2025
positive_highlights: evorpacept demonstrated an ORR of 65% vs 26% in control for HER2-positive gastric cancer patients with high CD47 expression
ALX-2004 Phase I trial cleared the first dose cohort and is currently dosing the second cohort at 2 mg/kg without DLTs
evorpacept showed a median duration of response of 3x longer (25.5 months vs 8.4 months) in high CD47 patients compared to control
summary: ALXO reported Q3 FY2025 results driven by significant clinical advances in its evorpacept and ALX-2004 programs rather than financial metrics. The company presented data from the ASPEN-06 trial showing a 65% objective response rate (ORR) for patients with high CD47 expression versus 26% in control, validating CD47 as a predictive biomarker. Management confirmed cash runway into Q1 2027 and stated that both clinical programs are on track to hit key milestones next year.

negative_highlights: FY2025 revenue guidance lowered to $3.05B-$3.1B; Commercial segment revenue fell 4.7% YoY on largest-client volume declines
Government segment revenue fell 6.7% YoY, including a client canceling an implementation to do the work in-house
Adjusted free cash flow was negative $54M and net leverage rose to 3.2x on delayed contract amendments and billing
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 110 bps YoY to 5.2% and rose from 4.9% last quarter
Transportation revenue grew 14.9% YoY to $162M with segment margin up 250 bps to 2.5%
Qualified ACV pipeline of $3.4B, up 9% YoY; repurchased ~4.7M shares at $2.70 average
summary: Adjusted revenue of $767M fell 1.8% YoY (from $781M), though management noted it was within the guided range and slightly up sequentially. Adjusted EBITDA rose to $40M with a 5.2% margin, up 110 bps YoY and in line with guidance. Full-year revenue guidance was lowered to $3.05B-$3.1B (attributed to federal workforce reductions and the government shutdown), while the 5%-5.5% EBITDA margin range was maintained. Adjusted free cash flow was negative $54M and net leverage rose to 3.2x on delayed federal contract amendments and billing timing.

negative_highlights: GAAP net loss widened to $2.3 million for the quarter.
New Expensify revenue contribution is less than 50%, indicating migration from Classic has not yet reached a tipping point.
Free cash flow in Q3 was lower than prior quarters due to seasonal timing of annual payments.
positive_highlights: Non-GAAP net income was positive at $4.3 million and adjusted EBITDA reached $6.5 million.
Expensify Travel bookings grew significantly, up 95% since Q1.
Management successfully migrated nearly all 'Collect' customers to New Expensify.
summary: Expensify reported Q3 FY2025 revenue of $35.1 million and a GAAP net loss of $2.3 million against non-GAAP income of $4.3 million. Management reiterated full-year free cash flow guidance but noted that New Expensify currently represents less than 50% of total revenue, with migration to the new platform still underway despite feature parity nearing completion.

negative_highlights: Telecommunications vertical declined 22.5% YoY as legacy carriers reduced volume, though this is the smallest segment at ~10% of revenue.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 16.5% YoY driven by high-margin offshore regions (+20%) and digital services mix expanding to 82% of total revenue.
Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 90 bps sequentially/annually to 12.9%, fueled by operating leverage as SG&A remained flat while revenue accelerated.
Management raised full-year FY'26 guidance for both top-line and adjusted earnings, signaling strong confidence in the business trajectory.
summary: IBEX reported Q1 FY2026 revenue of $151.2 million (up 16.5% YoY) and adjusted EPS of $0.90 (up 74% YoY). Management raised full-year guidance for both revenue ($605M-$620M vs prior $590M-$610M) and adjusted EBITDA ($78M-$81M vs prior $75M-$79M), citing strong momentum in high-margin offshore regions, digital services (now 82% of revenue mix), and AI deployments. While gross margins dipped slightly due to India ramp-up costs and deferred training revenue recognition on new wins, operating leverage drove adjusted EBITDA margin expansion from 12.0% to 12.9%.

negative_highlights: Local Media division Q3 profit dropped significantly from $161M last year to nearly $53M due to the absence of political advertising.
Q4 guidance for Local Media revenue is down ~30% compared to a prior period that included strong political spend, creating an artificial headwind.
National ad marketplace faces secular challenges including weak Direct Response pricing and volatility in Pharma categories.
positive_highlights: Asset sales for WFTX (Fort Myers) and WRTV (Indianapolis) closed at premium multiples of 9.2x and 8.5x blended EBITDA respectively, totaling $123M cash inflow.
Scripps Sports strategy drove significant growth with WNBA revenue on ION nearly doubling (+90% volume increase in upfronts).
Connected TV (CTV) revenue grew 41% YoY to become a major double-digit growth engine.
summary: SSP reported Q3 FY2025 results that met expectations with Local Media revenue down 27% YoY due to the absence of political advertising and Scripps Networks revenue flat at $201 million despite a 41% jump in CTV. Management provided cautious guidance for Q4, expecting Local Media revenue to decline approximately 30% (driven by lack of politics) while anticipating core network revenue growth of ~10%. The company highlighted successful asset sales totaling $123M and significant debt paydowns improving leverage from 6x in the prior year.

negative_highlights: Q3 2025 product revenue only $0.9 million; net loss per share $0.09
EMA raised questions on TPOXX efficacy in mpox; CHMP decision pending
Government shutdown may delay CDC analysis for PEP program, affecting FDA submission timeline
positive_highlights: Product sales for 9 months outpaced prior year: $86 million vs $54 million
Cash balance strong at $172 million with no debt, more than 4x annual operating expense run rate
Management expects multiple international sales in 2026
summary: SIGA reported Q3 2025 product revenues of only $0.9 million, a quiet quarter after a strong Q2 with $79 million; nine-month product revenues were approximately $86 million versus $54 million in the prior year. The company noted $26 million of outstanding U.S. government orders for IV TPOXX expected for delivery in 2026. Management is actively engaged with the U.S. government on future procurement and remains encouraged despite the government shutdown, and expects multiple international sales in 2026. The EMA's CHMP will meet next week regarding the TPOXX referral, and management expressed confidence in their responses.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA fell to $19.5 million from $31.1 million a year ago as realized RIN price dropped to $2.15 from $3.13
Full-year guidance held only at the low end, with Q4 adjusted EBITDA flagged as likely toward the lower end of the range
Fuel Station Services growth is now expected at the low end of the 30-50% target as a difficult freight backdrop slowed CNG tractor purchases
positive_highlights: RNG production of 1.3 million MMBtu rose about 30% YoY, with October the highest rate in company history after a record September
Atlantic came online on schedule, bringing 12 operating facilities and 9.1 million MMBtu of design capacity; CMS began construction, taking the in-construction portfolio to 2.8 million MMBtu
ITC monetization reached $43 million gross year-to-date against an approximately $50 million full-year target, with $184 million of total liquidity
summary: Revenue was $83 million versus $84 million a year ago, and adjusted EBITDA fell to $19.5 million from $31.1 million, driven by a realized RIN price of $2.15 versus $3.13 and the ISCC pathway expiration, partly offset by RNG production of 1.3 million MMBtu, up about 30% YoY. Full-year guidance was maintained but redirected toward the low end on production, Fuel Station Services EBITDA growth (low end of 30-50%), and Q4 adjusted EBITDA ("likely towards the lower end"). The Atlantic project came online (12 operating facilities, 9.1 million MMBtu), CMS entered construction (2.8 million MMBtu in construction), and 45Z credits begin in Q4 with a full year expected in 2026.

negative_highlights: Equity in earnings of unconsolidated joint ventures fell $1.3 million year-over-year, driven by lower TA/Petro earnings ($1.9 million in the quarter) on reduced Interstate 5 traffic.
No formal financial guidance was provided, and management stated the company is 'not yet where it needs to be.'
Shareholders cited a 52-year-low share price, no return of capital, and a $3.5 million proxy fight cost, with management acknowledging the share price performance is 'unacceptable.'
positive_highlights: Farming revenues increased more than 50% year-over-year and the segment's GAAP operating loss narrowed by 40% as expenses were held flat.
Consolidated operating income rose 37% to $3.4 million and total costs and expenses declined nearly 5% year-over-year.
A 20% workforce reduction is expected to save more than $2 million per year, and the industrial portfolio remains 100% leased.
summary: Tejon Ranch reported Q3 FY2025 net income of $1.7 million ($0.06 per share) versus a $1.8 million loss ($0.07 per share) a year ago, on total revenues of $12 million, up 10% year-over-year, with total costs and expenses down nearly 5%. Farming revenues rose more than 50% and the segment's GAAP operating loss narrowed by 40%, while consolidated operating income improved 37% to $3.4 million and adjusted EBITDA year-to-date was $13.9 million, up 7.3%. Management announced a workforce reduction of 20% that will save more than $2 million annually and said the company is 'not yet where it needs to be,' with no formal numeric guidance provided. The quarter also faced shareholder criticism over the 52-year-low share price, governance, and the lack of capital returns.

negative_highlights: Vessel operating expenses increased approximately 57% year-over-year due to the addition of the SSI fleet and higher loan days.
Total general and administrative expenses rose significantly from $6 million to approximately $9.8 million, driven by consolidation costs and timing of incentive compensation recognition.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA increased approximately $4.9 million year-over-year to $28.9 million, reflecting strong TCE premiums of ~10% over market indices.
Shipping days surged by 22% YoY following the integration of 15 Handysize vessels acquired from SSI at the end of last year.
Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to 17.1%, up from 15.7% in the prior period, supported by a 13% decrease in voyage expenses per day.
summary: Pangaea Logistics Solutions reported Q3 FY2025 adjusted EBITDA of $28.9 million (up ~$4.9M YoY) and GAAP net income of $12.2 million ($0.19/share), driven by a 22% increase in shipping days from SSI integration despite higher vessel operating expenses. Management booked approximately 1,710 Q4 days at an average TCE of $16,537/day and reiterated that broader dry bulk market pricing remains buoyant for the quarter ahead. The company maintained its disciplined capital allocation approach with continued share repurchases ($2M in Q3) and a declared quarterly dividend.

negative_highlights: Mobile revenue declined year-over-year reflecting record carrier promotions from Q4 FY2024 that will normalize in future quarters.
Q4 guidance for total revenue ($45M-$48M) and adjusted EBITDA ($4M-$5M) is lower than the sequential growth rate achieved in Q3, acknowledging seasonality.
positive_highlights: FWA shipment volumes were up more than 50% year-over-year driven by T-Mobile and a new Tier 1 carrier win.
Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded sequentially to 12.5%, the third highest in over a decade, aided by strong FWA mix.
Software services revenue remained consistent at $12 million, providing stable high-margin recurring revenue.
summary: Inseego reported Q3 FY2025 revenue of $45.9 million and adjusted EBITDA of $5.8 million, both beating guidance with a second consecutive quarter of sequential growth in each metric. Management raised full-year expectations by citing strong mobile volume gains from new carrier ramps and FWA expansion into MSOs/MSPs despite Q3 being a record for fixed wireless. The company highlighted the launch of premium FX4200 hardware and Inseego Connect SaaS updates as key drivers, while noting that non-GAAP gross margin is expected to be modestly lower in Q4 due to higher mobile mix.

negative_highlights: Revenue fell to $37.1 million from $39.2 million and core FFO per share declined to $0.19 from $0.21 year-over-year
The guidance raise is attributed primarily to ~$0.05 per share of non-recurring Fresno lease termination income, not recurring earnings
Operating property occupancy declined to 72.8% from 73.7% at December 31, 2024; CapEx and leasing costs jumped to $18.3 million from $6.1 million
positive_highlights: Full-year core FFO guidance raised to $0.74-$0.76 from $0.67-$0.71 per share
Portfolio WALT now 5.8 years versus roughly 3.5 years at spin, with 919,000 square feet leased YTD through November 6
Positive rent spreads of over 2% on renewals and over 4% on total leasing activity; 12 properties sold or under contract for 1.3 million square feet and over $110 million
summary: Orion reported Q3 FY2025 revenue of $37.1 million, down from $39.2 million a year ago, and core FFO of $11.0 million or $0.19 per share versus $12.0 million or $0.21 in Q3 2024; adjusted EBITDA fell to $17.4 million from $19.1 million. Full-year core FFO guidance was raised to $0.74-$0.76 from $0.67-$0.71, but the increase is driven primarily by roughly $0.05 per share of Fresno lease termination income rather than recurring operations, while net debt/EBITDA guidance improved to 6.7x-7.2x from 7.3x-8.3x and G&A tightened to $19.5M-$20M. Portfolio occupancy slipped to 72.8% from 73.7% at year-end 2024 (74.5% adjusting for properties sold or under agreement), though management called 2025 the trough for core FFO and pointed to 919,000 square feet of YTD leasing and a $500,000+ square foot pipeline. CapEx and leasing costs jumped to $18.3 million from $6.1 million on accelerated leasing.

negative_highlights: Cash OpEx increased to $12.4 million due to higher bonus payouts tied to strong performance, though this is a one-time variance.
Management noted that Q3 revenue was lower than the prior quarter's managed services spike as business normalizes.
positive_highlights: Revenue increased 22% year-over-year to $26.1 million, significantly ahead of consensus estimates.
Adjusted EBITDA improved over $2 million sequentially from the prior period to reach $5.1 million.
Gross margin expanded substantially YoY to 67.2%, driven by favorable product and channel partner mix.
summary: OptimizeRx reported Q3 FY2025 revenue of $26.1 million (up 22% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $5.1 million, beating consensus estimates. Management raised full-year guidance to revenue between $105M-$109M and adjusted EBITDA between $16M-$19M, while also providing initial FY2026 outlooks with revenue expected at $118M-$124M. Gross margin expanded 410 bps YoY to 67.2% driven by product mix and channel partner shifts.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined significantly due to a timing issue where leads remained strong but conversion lagged, resulting in Q3 revenue lower than anticipated.
A noncash impairment charge of $4.6 million was recorded related to unused Salesforce technology components for operations and clinical needs.
The closure of the London facility resulted in an additional loss of approximately $2.3 million.
positive_highlights: Same-store sales performance in Q4 is improving compared to year-to-date trends, suggesting stabilization ahead.
Pilot programs for skin tightening are expanding to multiple centers with higher conversion rates observed among GLP-1 patients.
Management has generated over $3 million in annualized cost savings and repaid nearly $18 million of debt year-to-date.
summary: Third quarter revenue declined 17.8% year-over-year to $35 million due to a timing issue and challenging consumer sentiment for considered purchases rather than demand destruction. Management lowered its full-year 2025 revenue guidance from the prior range of $160M-$170M to approximately $153 million, while reiterating EBITDA at the low end of the previous guide ($16M). The company closed an unprofitable London center and recorded a noncash impairment charge related to Salesforce components.

negative_highlights: Total net sales were lower versus $50 million in Q3 FY2024 due to a reduction of 19 retail locations since July.
Management explicitly tempered expectations for gross margins in the fourth quarter, anticipating compression relative to durable activity and tariff impacts (estimated at ~1% of sales).
Revenue growth is expected to slow sequentially in Q4 as durable equipment sales volume increases from $7M to $13M.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA returned positive at $1.3 million compared to a loss of $2.4 million last year, marking an inflection point after restructuring costs were removed.
Gross margins expanded significantly to 27.2% from 21.6%, driven by proprietary brands growing their share of cultivation and gardening revenue to 31.6% (up from 23.8%).
Operating expenses decreased 31.5% year-over-year as the company closed underperforming stores, reducing total locations to 24.
summary: GrowGeneration reported Q3 FY2025 net sales of $47.3 million (up 15% sequentially) and adjusted EBITDA returning to positive $1.3 million after a restructuring-driven loss in the prior year period, exceeding its own guidance of $41 million but missing consensus expectations due to store count reductions from 63 to 24 locations. Gross margins expanded to 27.2%, driven by proprietary brand mix shifting to 31.6% and lower operating expenses, though management explicitly warned of expected margin compression in Q4 due to higher durable sales volume (up to $13M) and tariff impacts.

negative_highlights: Commercial/industrial revenue fell 16% and NOI fell 25%, with 51% of the segment vacant including the fully vacant 258,000 square foot Chelsea building
Multifamily NOI fell 3.2% on higher operating costs, property taxes and uncollectible revenue at Maren; D.C. new supply continues to pressure concessions and trade-outs
GAAP net income fell 51% to $700,000 ($0.03/share) on $1.3 million of Altman acquisition expenses
positive_highlights: Adjusted net income rose 21% to $281,000 above last year's Q3, and adjusted NOI was up 1% excluding the prior-year $1.9 million royalty
Mining and royalty revenue rose 15% to $3.7 million on higher royalties
Altman acquisition adds 1.8 million square feet of industrial pipeline and a 382,000 square foot Florida JV now owned 100%
summary: GAAP net income fell 51% to $700,000 ($0.03/share) due largely to $1.3 million of Altman acquisition costs, while adjusted net income rose 21%; pro rata NOI fell 16% to $9.5 million but adjusted NOI was up 1% excluding last year's $1.9 million nonrecurring mining royalty. Commercial/industrial revenue and NOI fell 16% and 25% with 51% of the segment vacant, and multifamily NOI declined 3.2% on higher operating costs and uncollectible revenue at Maren. Management described 2025 as a foundational, not growth, year and gave no numeric guidance, citing 1.6 million square feet of industrial space to lease over the next 12 months; the Altman Logistics acquisition closed after quarter-end and adds 1.8 million square feet of pipeline.

negative_highlights: Revenue down 5.8% organically to $422.6 million, with Construction equipment sales down $18.7 million YoY
FY2025 adjusted EBITDA guidance reduced to $168-172 million
Material Handling backlog burned down from $125 million at the start of the year to the low $100 millions
positive_highlights: October Construction Equipment sales topped $75 million, nearly 60% of Q3's entire equipment sales
SG&A down roughly $25 million year-to-date on structural cost savings
Free cash flow before rent-to-note of ~$25 million in Q3 and ~$80 million YTD, with FY guide held at $105-110 million
summary: Revenue fell 5.8% organically to $422.6 million with equipment sales the main drag; Construction Equipment equipment sales dropped $18.7 million YoY, partly offset by Product Support growth. Adjusted EBITDA of $41.7 million was slightly below last year on a pro forma basis, and FY2025 adjusted EBITDA guidance was cut to $168-172 million while free cash flow guidance of $105-110 million was held. Management framed Q3 as timing-driven rather than demand-driven, citing October Construction sales above $75 million (nearly 60% of Q3 equipment sales), a Material Handling backlog above $100 million, and roughly $25 million of YTD SG&A savings, but also noted tariff pressure at Ecoverse, soft Midwest/Canada manufacturing, and still-oversupplied equipment markets.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined $8.5 million sequentially due to the divestiture of VoIP Supply LLC.
Gross margin was 72%, lower than the 76% seen in Q4 without VoIP Supply, due to a higher mix of lower-margin product revenue.
Free cash flow of $3.2 million was impacted by a one-time $3.2 million negative change in working capital from transitioning payment processors.
positive_highlights: Revenue beat consensus analyst expectations while tracking to internal plan.
New pipeline creation increased 39% quarter-over-quarter with larger strategic deals accelerating.
Average revenue per customer grew 19% year-over-year driven by bundling and upsell initiatives.
summary: Sangoma reported Q1 FY2026 revenue of $50.8 million, which tracked to plan and beat consensus expectations despite a sequential decline driven by the divestiture of its VoIP Supply hardware resale business. Adjusted EBITDA was $8.3 million (16% margin), with management reaffirming full-year guidance of $200-$210 million revenue and 17-19% adjusted EBITDA margins. Management highlighted strong pipeline creation up 39% QoQ, larger strategic deal closures including a $150,000 MRR win, and a transition to a recurring revenue model representing over 90% of total revenue.

negative_highlights: Multiplatform Group revenue declined 4.6% YoY, missing the prior year's political advertising boost which inflated Q3 FY2024 results.
GAAP operating loss of $116M due to a one-time $29 million FCC license impairment charge and lower broadcast margins (down from 77M income in prior year).
Free cash flow turned negative at -$33M compared to +$73M last quarter, driven by timing differences in political revenue recognition.
positive_highlights: Digital Audio Group revenue grew 13.5% YoY to $342M, significantly beating guidance of high single digits.
Podcasting revenue increased 22.5% YoY with adjusted EBITDA margins expanding from 33.2% to 38.1%.
Management announced an additional $50 million in annual cost savings beginning in 2026.
summary: Consolidated revenue was down 1.1% YoY at the high end of guidance (low single digits), while Digital Audio Group revenue beat expectations with a 13.5% increase driven by podcast growth; however, Multiplatform and Audio & Media Services groups missed due to political advertising headwinds in Q4 prior year comparisons. Adjusted EBITDA was $205M, slightly above the midpoint of guidance but flat YoY, impacted by a one-time FCC license impairment charge that caused GAAP operating loss. Management raised 2026 cost savings expectations and reiterated confidence in digital growth despite macro uncertainty.

negative_highlights: Total company revenue declined 11% year-over-year on a same-station basis, with management describing the results as 'unacceptable'.
National agency revenue ex-political declined approximately 16% year-over-year due to pullback in telecom, cable, insurance, and quick service restaurant advertising.
New business remains under pressure, down approximately 12% year-over-year ex-political.
positive_highlights: Digital revenue grew approximately 28% year-over-year on a same-station basis, now accounting for roughly 25% of total company revenue.
Local direct revenue grew 3.5% year-over-year and now represents nearly 60% of total local business.
Station operating expenses were down 8% year-over-year, totaling approximately $4 million less than the prior period.
summary: Total company revenue declined 11% year-over-year to $51 million on a same-station basis, driven by an 16% drop in national agency revenue and a 17% decline in local agency revenue. While digital revenue grew 28% year-over-year and operating expenses fell 8%, management explicitly stated the results were 'unacceptable' and that the rate of revenue decline underscores a fundamental need for more aggressive execution. Guidance for Q4 ex-political revenue is pacing down in the high single digits, consistent with third-quarter trends.

negative_highlights: FY2026 revenue guidance updated to $8-10 million, likely lowered from prior expectations
Sequential revenue growth was only 3%, essentially flat
positive_highlights: Revenue increased 128% year over year to $1.8 million from $0.8 million
Operating expenses reduced 37% year over year to $7.4 million from $11.7 million
First international commercial placement of LungFit PH and first US hospital capital purchase occurred
summary: Beyond Air reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $1.8 million, up 128% year over year from $0.8 million but essentially flat sequentially (3% growth). The company updated its FY2026 revenue guidance to $8-10 million, a reduction from prior guidance attributed to a CCO transition and lumpy hospital purchasing cycles. Gross margin slipped back to negative $0.3 million due to device upgrade costs and excess inventory provisions, while operating expenses fell 37% year over year to $7.4 million and net loss improved to $7.9 million from $13.4 million. Subsequent to quarter end, the company raised $12 million in debt and established a $20 million equity line with Streeterville Capital, extending its runway into calendar 2027.

negative_highlights: Gross margin contracted to 19.3% from 19.8% a year earlier, with $3.6 million of noncash and $698,000 of one-time cash expenses
Net loss of $2.1 million ($0.11/share), reflecting a $3.6 million tax expense versus $912,000 prior year
One of the largest customers delayed purchases offsetting the $14.8 million core revenue gain, with management also citing consumer repair deferral and government shutdown impact
positive_highlights: Operating income rose 30.8% to $16.4 million from $12.5 million a year earlier
Six-month operating cash flow of $31.9 million versus $2 million in the prior-year period, with net bank debt cut $24.6 million to $56.7 million
Interest expense fell $1.5 million to $12.7 million on lower balances and rates; 287,910 shares repurchased for $3.4 million in H1
summary: MPAA reported Q2 FY2026 net sales up 6.4% to $221.5 million and a record Q2 gross profit of $42.7 million, but gross margin slipped to 19.3% from 19.8% and the company posted a net loss of $2.1 million ($0.11/share) versus a $3.0 million loss a year ago. Sales included a one-time $14.8 million core-returns accrual gain that was offset by a roughly equal temporary purchase deferral from one large customer, which management expects to recover in the second half; fiscal 2026 guidance was confirmed, not raised, and excludes the one-time core revenue. Operating income rose 30.8% to $16.4 million, H1 operating cash flow was $31.9 million versus $2 million a year ago, and net bank debt was reduced $24.6 million to $56.7 million. The key change versus the prior period is the customer purchase timing shift and consumer repair deferral, which management framed as short-lived for nondiscretionary parts.

negative_highlights: Total Q3 revenue fell 42% year-over-year to $78 million, with Google traffic down about 50% cutting subscribers and ad sessions
Q4 total revenue is guided to $70-72 million, implying further sequential decline and continued year-over-year contraction
Free cash flow was negative $0.9 million in Q3, and $15-19 million of severance and transition payments will hit cash flow over Q4 and Q1 2026
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA of $13 million beat guidance by $5 million, a 17% margin, driven by non-GAAP operating expenses cut 46% year-over-year to $49 million
Skilling business (Busuu and Chegg Skills) is expected to grow 14% year-over-year with ~$70 million of 2025 revenue and double-digit growth projected into 2026
Company is on track to reduce non-GAAP expenses from $536 million in 2024 to under $250 million by 2026, with CapEx down 63% year-over-year to $6 million
summary: Chegg reported Q3 FY2025 total revenue of $78 million, down 42% year-over-year, as reduced Google traffic cut subscribers and advertising sessions. Adjusted EBITDA was $13 million (17% margin) and beat the company's own guidance by $5 million, aided by non-GAAP operating expenses falling 46% to $49 million and a restructuring that removed almost 400 roles; free cash flow was negative $0.9 million due to a $7.5 million FTC settlement and $5.5 million in severance. Q4 guidance is total revenue of $70-72 million, gross margin 57-58%, and adjusted EBITDA of $10-11 million. Management is splitting the company into a growing B2B skilling unit (Busuu plus Chegg Skills, expected ~14% year-over-year growth and about $70 million in 2025 revenue) and a cash-generating legacy academic services unit, with no formal full-year 2026 guidance yet.

negative_highlights: Revenue fell 23% YoY to $5.0M from $6.5M
Non-GAAP adjusted EBITDA remained a loss of $3.6M (improved from $4.5M)
Q4 guidance of $5.4M-$5.9M implies only modest sequential recovery, with margin benefits not fully realized until Q1 2026
positive_highlights: Non-GAAP gross margin rose to 19.1% from 3.6% GAAP in Q3 2024, reflecting completed Thailand transition and lower manufacturing overhead
GAAP net loss narrowed to $3.5M ($0.15/share) from $9.3M ($0.40/share) a year ago
New opportunity pipeline grew to 108 (net +18 QoQ) with 18% converted to sales year-to-date, two-thirds at >30% gross margin
summary: Revenue of $5.0M was within the previously guided range but fell from $6.5M in Q3 2024, as expected after exiting lower-margin business. Non-GAAP gross margin improved to 19.1% from 60.3% a year ago, boosted by the completed Singapore-to-Thailand production transition, fully reserved inventory sales, and lower fixed costs, while GAAP net loss narrowed to $3.5M from $9.3M. Q4 guidance is $5.4M-$5.9M (~11% sequential growth), and management expects further margin expansion into Q1 2026 as Singapore shutdown completes by year-end.

negative_highlights: GAAP net loss of $77 million driven by an $80 million non-cash impairment from reduced market capitalization
Full-year revenue guidance remains broadly flat versus prior year, with no raise despite Q3 momentum
CEO noted clients are redirecting resources to AI R&D, temporarily pressuring go-to-market and marketing budgets
