positive_highlights: Revenue returned to positive YoY growth at ~1% ($122M vs $121M), improving from -1.6% in Q2 and -5.8% in Q1
Adjusted EBITDA grew 9% YoY, outpacing ~1% revenue growth and delivering margin expansion
Bookings up YoY with longer-term contracts and larger average deal sizes; management expects a healthier backlog entering 2026
summary: Q3 revenue was $122 million vs $121 million a year ago on a combined basis, roughly 1% YoY growth and a 2% sequential increase, marking a swing from -5.8% YoY in Q1 and -1.6% in Q2 to positive growth. Adjusted EBITDA grew 9% YoY ahead of revenue, but GAAP net loss was $77 million, largely due to an $80 million non-cash impairment tied to lower market capitalization. Full-year 2025 guidance was reaffirmed: broadly flat revenues and adjusted EBITDA above $85 million. Management cited improving bookings, larger average deal sizes, and a healthier expected backlog entering 2026, while noting clients are redirecting budget toward AI R&D and away from go-to-market spend.

negative_highlights: Net income fell 61.7% to $1.293 million ($0.03 per diluted share) from $3.376 million ($0.07)
Adjusted EBITDA declined 28.1% year over year to $6.797 million from $9.452 million
Management cited persistent headwinds in a difficult freight market expected to persist into calendar 2026, and booked a $1.3 million bad debt charge on the First Brands bankruptcy
positive_highlights: Revenue rose to $226.7 million from $203.6 million in the prior-year quarter
Excluding the $1.3 million First Brands bad debt charge, adjusted EBITDA was $8.1 million, above the $7.9 million reported in Q4 2025
Virtually debt-free with net debt of approximately $2 million against a $200 million credit facility, and $3.6 million of buybacks executed in the quarter plus post-quarter period
summary: Radiant reported Q1 FY2026 revenue of $226.7 million, up from $203.6 million a year ago, but net income fell 61.7% to $1.293 million ($0.03 per diluted share) from $3.376 million ($0.07 per share), and adjusted EBITDA declined 28.1% to $6.797 million from $9.452 million. Results included a one-time $1.3 million bad debt charge tied to the First Brands bankruptcy; excluding it, adjusted EBITDA would have been $8.1 million, modestly above Q4 2025's $7.9 million. Management gave no formal numeric guidance, describing continued freight-market headwinds into calendar 2026 mitigated by value-added services, and highlighted the Navegate technology platform, the Weport Mexico acquisition, and $0.8 million of buybacks in the quarter plus $2.8 million more subsequent to quarter-end.

negative_highlights: Q4 cash gross margin guided to approximately 40–41%, down sequentially from 44.8% in Q3.
Federal government shutdown has stalled awards and caused administrative delays, with some deals sliding into 2026.
Secure Networks segment expected to contract by $11 million in 2026.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 116% YoY to $51.4 million, exceeding the $44–$47 million guidance range.
Adjusted EBITDA of $10.1 million beat the $4–$5.7 million guidance range, with a 19.6% margin and 51.5% incremental margin.
Second-half 2025 revenue guidance raised by $5.6 million (6%) and adjusted EBITDA guidance raised by $5.2 million (54%) at the midpoint.
summary: Telos reported Q3 FY2025 revenue of $51.4 million, up 116% year-over-year, beating the guidance range of $44–$47 million, with adjusted EBITDA of $10.1 million versus guidance of $4–$5.7 million. GAAP gross margin was 39.9% and cash gross margin 44.8%, both above guidance and prior-quarter levels. Management raised its second-half 2025 outlook, citing 6% higher revenue and 54% higher adjusted EBITDA at the midpoint, and guided Q4 revenue to $44–$46.3 million (67–76% growth) with adjusted EBITDA of $4–$5.7 million. The quarter also included the launch of Xacta.ai with a first enterprise customer and the TSA PreCheck program reaching 504 enrollment locations.

negative_highlights: Full-year revenue guidance lowered to $500–$530 million due to a higher proportion of lower-ASP conversions
Q4 implied adjusted EBITDA margin steps down to ~8% (vs 10.6% in Q3) on commodity mix and the December maintenance shutdown
Industry orders remain below the ~40,000 normalized level with full-year deliveries under 30,000 railcars
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA hit a facility-record $17 million (10.6% margin, up ~100 bps YoY), the strongest since relocating to Mexico
Revenue up over 42% YoY to $160.5 million on deliveries of 1,304 vs 961
Adjusted net income of $7.8 million ($0.24/diluted share) and $2.2 million adjusted free cash flow, an improvement of $1.2 million YoY
summary: Q3 FY2025 revenue rose 42% YoY to $160.5 million on 1,304 deliveries (vs 961 prior year), with gross margin of 15.1% (up ~80 bps), adjusted EBITDA a facility-record $17 million (10.6% margin, up ~100 bps), and adjusted EPS of $0.24; reported net loss of $7.4 million reflected a $17.6 million non-cash warrant-liability charge. Backlog stood at 2,750 units / ~$222 million with 430 orders received in the quarter. Full-year adjusted EBITDA and unit guidance reaffirmed, but revenue guidance was cut to $500–$530 million to reflect a higher mix of lower-ASP conversions; Q4 margin is guided down versus Q3 (~8%) on commodity mix and the annual December maintenance shutdown.

negative_highlights: Total revenue of $3.2 million was down from $3.8 million in the year-ago quarter due to the memory IC end-of-life
Q4 2025 guidance of $2.8-3.1 million is below the $3.2 million just reported, indicating a sequential decline
Cash balance of only $1.9 million was sustained by $900,000 of warrant inducement proceeds and $700,000 from the at-the-market program, with the strategic review still unresolved
positive_highlights: Total revenue rose more than 45% sequentially to $3.2 million, driven by record millimeter wave revenue of $3.0 million versus $100,000 a year ago
GAAP and non-GAAP gross margin expanded to 56.2% from 48.3% in the prior quarter, at the top of the targeted mid-fifty percent range
A first-time OEM customer placed an initial volume order for millimeter wave modules, and the company has a double-digit number of new customer SKUs in preproduction for the first time
summary: Peraso reported Q3 2025 total net revenue of $3.2 million, up from $2.2 million in the prior quarter but down from $3.8 million a year ago, with millimeter wave product revenue of $3.0 million versus $100,000 in Q3 2024. GAAP and non-GAAP gross margin both reached 56.2%, up from 48.3% sequentially on favorable millimeter wave mix and shipments of previously written-down inventory. Q4 2025 guidance was set at $2.8-3.1 million, which is below the $3.2 million just reported, and includes roughly $375,000 of high-margin memory shipments. Non-GAAP net loss was $1.1 million or $0.15 per share, cash ended at $1.9 million, and the strategic review process remains ongoing with no new update.

negative_highlights: Core Simoa organic revenue declined 36% YoY due to smaller project sizes driven by the weak grant environment.
Spatial revenue fell 9% YoY, with U.S. academic revenue down ~30% and pharma revenue down 23%.
Full-year guidance tightened on gross margins (45%-47%) compared to prior expectations due to accounting reallocations.
positive_highlights: Revenue beat revenue guidance of $38-42M, driven by a partial quarter contribution from Akoya ($17.2M).
Integration synergies realized at $67 million against an $85 million target within three months post-closing.
Sequential improvement in Accelerator and Instrument revenues signaled gradual recovery despite academic weakness.
summary: Q3 FY2025 revenue was $40.2 million (up 12% YoY), driven by a partial quarter of Akoya and integration synergies realized at $67M against an $85M target, though core Simoa organic revenue declined 36%. Management maintained full-year guidance for total revenue between $130-135M but tightened gross margin expectations to 45%-47% due to accounting reallocations from the Akoya integration. The company expects cash flow breakeven in 2026 and ends with approximately $120M in cash.

negative_highlights: New bookings did not show the expected sequential increase in Q3
Revenue guidance lowered due to ~$0.5 million delay from two customer projects
M&T gross retention still lower than usual, though improving
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA of $4.2 million, a record, marking ninth consecutive quarter of profitability
Non-GAAP gross margin improved to 70% from 68% YoY
Closed five AI deals for ContentLab and Genie, with pipeline supporting Q4 pickup
summary: Kaltura reported Q3 2025 revenue of $43.9 million and subscription revenue of $42 million, with record adjusted EBITDA of $4.2 million, the ninth consecutive profitable quarter. Non-GAAP gross margin expanded to 70% from 68% YoY, and non-GAAP net profit was $2 million. The company announced the planned acquisition of Ethof.ai for up to ~$27 million and a share repurchase of 14.4 million shares from Goldman Sachs at a 25% discount. New bookings remained soft in Q3, with a pickup expected in Q4, and two customer projects caused a ~$0.5 million revenue recognition delay into next year.

negative_highlights: Q4 normalized gross profit growth guided to the low end of the prior range (high single digits) due to ongoing margin pressures, and Q4 free cash flow conversion outlook cut to above 50% from 60% on working capital timing.

Gross profit margins compressed approximately 340 bps year over year due to lapping one-off client losses, political media contributions, and a mix shift toward larger clients with volume discounts and higher ACH/check volumes.
Consumer payments gross profit grew only 1% year over year, and management noted continued softness in the automotive/used car subvertical with a stable but not improving consumer backdrop.
positive_highlights: Business payments normalized gross profit increased 12% year over year, with core AP platform growing double digits and supplier network growing approximately 60% to over 540,000 (corrected to 524,000).
Repurchased approximately 3.1 million shares for $15.6 million in August, totaling $38 million and 7.9 million shares year to date, reducing fully diluted shares by approximately 8%.
Retired $73.5 million of 2026 convertible notes at a discount and maintained strong liquidity of $346 million with net leverage around 2.5x.
summary: Repay reported Q3 revenue of $77.7 million and gross profit of $57.8 million, with normalized revenue and gross profit growth of 5% and 1% respectively (excluding 2024 political media). Adjusted EBITDA was $31.2 million (40% margin) and adjusted EPS came in at $0.21. Management guided Q4 normalized gross profit growth to 6-8% (high single digits), explicitly at the low end of the prior outlook due to ongoing margin pressures, and lowered free cash flow conversion guidance to above 50% from 60% due to working capital timing. Gross margins compressed roughly 340 bps year over year on client losses, political media lapping, and a mix shift toward larger volume-discounted clients and ACH/check volumes.

negative_highlights: Quarterly growth included a 600 basis point headwind from a lost advertiser
Political advertising created temporary distortion in reported growth
Majority of $250 million opportunity still undecided
positive_highlights: Revenue increased 7% YoY, above the midpoint of guidance
Adjusted EBITDA of $16 million exceeded the high end of guidance
Flagship multiyear partnership with Molson Coors as advertising platform
summary: Viant reported record Q3 2025 results with revenue up 7% and contribution ex-TAC up 12%, both above the midpoint of guidance. Adjusted EBITDA reached $16 million, up 9% and above the high end of guidance. Excluding political advertising, revenue and contribution ex-TAC grew 19% and 22% respectively. The company highlighted a flagship multiyear partnership with Molson Coors and raised full-year guidance.

negative_highlights: ContraPest revenue decreased approximately 31% year-over-year, though it was flat sequentially.
Adjusted EBITDA loss of $1.2 million remains a negative cash flow event, albeit the best in company history.
International sales were nominal during the quarter due to pending regulatory approvals.
positive_highlights: Record quarterly revenue of $690,000 driven by rapid adoption of the Evolve product line.
Gross margins held steady at 63% despite high growth volume.
Operating expenses decreased 12% sequentially and 4% year-over-year due to cost discipline.
summary: SenesTech reported Q3 FY2025 revenue of $690,000, representing a 43% year-over-year increase and a 10% sequential increase. Gross margins remained strong at 63%, while operating expenses decreased by 4% year-over-year and 12% sequentially. The company achieved its best adjusted EBITDA loss in history at $1.2 million, driven by record revenues from the Evolve product line and a new partnership with Lowe's.

negative_highlights: Total revenue missed expectations with a 3% year-over-year decline, including a 3% drop in guest traffic.
Comparable restaurant sales are expected to decline approximately 3% in the fourth quarter.
Food and beverage costs increased by 25% due to beef inflation, which management expects to persist through Q4.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA beat expectations at $7.6 million, an increase of $3.4 million versus the prior year quarter.
The 'Big Yummm' value promotion is mixing at approximately 8% of total sales and drove a 250 basis point sequential traffic improvement.
Restaurant-level operating profit margin expanded to 9.9%, up 90 basis points year-over-year driven by labor efficiency gains.
summary: Red Robin reported Q3 FY2025 total revenues of $265.1 million, a decline of approximately 3% year-over-year compared to $274.6 million in the prior year quarter. Management raised guidance for full-year 2025 adjusted EBITDA to at least $65 million (from $60-65 million) and restaurant-level operating profit to at least 12.5%, while keeping total revenue guidance unchanged at approximately $1.2 billion. The company noted that traffic trends slowed in recent weeks due to intentional marketing timing shifts and the government shutdown, leading to a specific expectation of a 3% decline in comparable restaurant sales for Q4.

negative_highlights: U.S. Cannabis segment posted a small negative adjusted EBITDA due to regulatory headwinds and unregulated hemp competition.
Netherlands recreational cannabis gross margin declined slightly sequentially, attributed to start-up ramp dynamics rather than structural issues.
Produce sales decreased 10% YoY primarily because of commissions paid following the privatization of a portion of that business.
positive_highlights: Canadian cannabis gross margin expanded sequentially to record levels at 56%, well above the high end of the targeted 30-40% range.
Adjusted EBITDA from Canadian operations reached an all-time quarterly record of $26.6 million, more than tripling YoY performance.
International medical exports surged over 750% YoY to $16.3 million as the company solidified its position in Germany.
summary: Village Farms International reported record Q3 FY2025 results with consolidated net sales increasing 21% YoY to $66.7 million and adjusted EBITDA rising 309% YoY to $20.7 million (41% margin). Canadian cannabis gross margins expanded significantly to 56%, driven by improved pricing, higher yields, and a shift toward high-margin SKUs following portfolio realignment. The company reaffirmed its long-term target range of 30-40% for the sweet spot while noting current performance exceeded expectations due to supply constraints.

negative_highlights: Net product revenues declined year-over-year to $15.8 million from $18 million.
Revenue ramp-up for new indications is not expected until the first half of 2027 following compendia inclusion and approvals.
Indolent lymphoma markets (follicular and marginal zone) are described as highly competitive with many agents in Phase III trials.
positive_highlights: Secured a $60 million private placement led by TCGX, extending the cash runway to at least 2028.
Phase II IIT data for ZENLATA in follicular lymphoma showed an overall response rate of 98.2% and complete response rate of 83.6%.
LOTUS VII trial interim data demonstrated a 93.3% overall response rate and 86.7% complete response rate.
summary: Net product revenues were $15.8 million in Q3 2025, down from $18 million in the prior year quarter due to variability in customer ordering patterns. The company reported a GAAP net loss of $41 million compared to $44 million last year, driven by lower R&D expenses. Management highlighted strong clinical data for ZENLATA in upcoming trials but noted that revenue inflection points are expected in 2027 following regulatory approvals.

negative_highlights: Total revenue declined 4% YoY, with handheld revenue down 5%.
Approximately $4 million of Q4 revenue potentially impacted by government shutdown delays.
Gross margin decreased slightly to 53% due to product mix and unabsorbed precision machining costs.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA loss of $1.8 million was the lowest in company history, down 53% quarter-over-quarter.
Recurring revenue grew 10% YoY, and Explorer shipments set a record with 30% sequential growth.
Cash position strong at $112 million with no debt.
summary: 908 Devices reported Q3 2025 revenue of $14 million, down 4% YoY but up 8% sequentially, with gross margin at 53% on a GAAP basis and 58% on an adjusted basis. Recurring revenue grew 10% YoY to $4.8 million, representing 36% of total revenue. The adjusted EBITDA loss improved to $1.8 million, the lowest in company history, but management flagged an estimated $4 million of Q4 revenue at risk due to the U.S. government shutdown, while reaffirming full-year guidance. Explorer and Viper showed strong traction, with Explorer placements up 30% sequentially and Viper expected to ramp in 2026.

negative_highlights: Core consumer brand business revenue not broken out separately; digital asset revenue dominates
Company acknowledged that staking yield has not been maximized yet, with exact yield not disclosed
Management noted potential for discount to NAV, though not current, and no specific mitigation plan detailed
positive_highlights: Staking revenue of $6.1 million in Q1, with total treasury yield of $7.1 million since inception
SOL holdings increased by 1,322,000 tokens during the quarter, reaching 2.1 million total
Net income of $66.7 million and EPS of $1.21, driven by $78 million unrealized gains
summary: Upexi reported fiscal Q1 2026 revenue of $9.2 million, up $4.9 million year-over-year, driven by $6.1 million in Solana staking revenue. Net income was $66.7 million (EPS $1.21), including $78 million in unrealized gains. The company raised $300 million in equity and convertible note offerings during the quarter, increasing SOL holdings to $2.1 million tokens valued at $327 million. Adjusted SOL per share increased 47% in SOL terms and 82% in USD terms, with management guiding to higher staking yield next quarter.

negative_highlights: Gross margin declined to 83.3% from 85.4% due to higher discounting, mix shift to lower-margin financial assistance program, and expired RED inventory charges
Net loss widened 21% to $2.1 million and operating loss rose 27% to $2.1 million
No specific financial guidance provided; management noted adult IV Stem faces likely 2026 coverage and reimbursement issues
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 22% year over year to $811,000, the fifth consecutive quarter of double-digit growth
Unit deliveries increased approximately 38% year over year
FDA indication expansion to functional abdominal pain/IBS and functional dyspepsia with nausea in adults, plus label expansion to ages 18-21 with up to four devices per patient
summary: NeurAxis reported Q3 FY2025 revenue of $811,000, up 22% year over year, marking the fifth consecutive quarter of double-digit growth, with unit deliveries up approximately 38%. Gross margin declined to 83.3% from 85.4%, operating expenses rose 25% to $2.8 million, and net loss widened 21% to $2.1 million. Management provided positive forward commentary tied to the new category one CPT code effective January 1, 2026, and FDA indication expansion, but offered no specific revenue or EPS guidance and acknowledged that adult IV Stem coverage issues are likely in 2026.

negative_highlights: GAAP net loss remained at $4.4 million, though improved from $8.1 million in the prior year.
Verus Title segment posted an adjusted EBITDA loss of $191,000 despite 28.6% revenue growth due to increased operating expenses.
No share repurchases were made during the first 9 months of 2025 under the authorized program.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 37.7% year-over-year to $115.3 million, nearly doubling analyst expectations of a 20% increase.
Adjusted EBITDA achieved profitability of $6,000 in Q3 2025 compared to a negative $1.4 million in the prior year quarter.
Ancillary business file starts for mortgage and title increased by more than 60% compared to the same period last year.
summary: Fathom Holdings reported Q3 FY2025 revenue of $115.3 million, a 37.7% year-over-year increase driven by the addition of My Home Group and organic growth. Adjusted EBITDA turned positive at $6,000 for the quarter compared to a loss in the prior year period, while GAAP net loss narrowed to $4.4 million. Management raised guidance expectations implicitly by citing accelerating growth in ancillary businesses (mortgage, title) and file starts up 60% YoY, projecting operational cash flow breakeven by Q2 2026.

negative_highlights: Full-year 2025 adjusted EBITDA guidance cut to $17-19 million from $21-25 million, and revenue guidance lowered to $640-650 million from $650-670 million.
reduce exposure note Systems and Components revenue fell 29% to $34.3 million, swinging to an adjusted operating loss of $0.3 million from a $4.1 million profit, as Class 8 builds fell 39%.
Q3 free cash flow was negative $3.4 million versus positive $17.1 million prior year, and net leverage stood at 4.9x, above the 2x target.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 50 bps to 3.0% despite a $19.3 million year-over-year revenue decline, with adjusted gross margin up 50 bps to 12.1%.
Global Electrical Systems revenue grew 6% to $49.5 million with adjusted operating income of $1.4 million, up $1.6 million from the prior year on new program ramps.
Free cash flow guidance of at least $30 million for the full year was maintained, supported by $25 million generated in the first nine months and a 50% planned CapEx reduction.
summary: CVG reported Q3 2025 revenue of $152.5 million, down from $171.8 million a year ago, with a GAAP net loss of $6.8 million ($0.20 per diluted share) versus a $0.9 million loss prior year. Adjusted EBITDA rose to $4.6 million (3.0% margin, up 50 bps) on operational efficiency, but the company lowered full-year 2025 revenue guidance to $640-650 million from $650-670 million and adjusted EBITDA guidance to $17-19 million from $21-25 million. Trim Systems revenue fell 29% on a 39% Class 8 production decline, while Global Electrical Systems grew 6% on new program ramps. Free cash flow guidance of at least $30 million was maintained.

negative_highlights: October SAAR slowed significantly to 15.3 million units compared to Q3 strength.
Management expects modestly lower fourth-quarter revenues than the third quarter due to current market sluggishness.
Pricing environment remains weak with limited spot volume opportunities and OEM contract renewals showing mixed results.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 24.9% YoY driven by market share gains and the Brothers acquisition (up 21%).
Adjusted operating ratio improved 250 bps to 96.3%, demonstrating operational efficiency despite a $1.9M restructuring charge.
Sister hauls increased to 11% of revenue, reducing empty miles through unified systems.
summary: Proficient Auto Logistics reported Q3 FY2025 revenue of $114.3 million (up 24.9% YoY) and adjusted operating ratio improvement to 96.3%. Management raised full-year top-line growth guidance to a range of 10-12%, but warned that fourth-quarter revenues will be modestly lower than Q3 due to softness in October volumes, despite expecting seasonal strength later in the year.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to $32 million due to a combined increase in intangible amortization, interest expense, and legacy litigation costs.
Everspan's net written premium declined significantly year-over-year from $33 million to $18 million following the proactive nonrenewal of auto programs.
Loss ratio deteriorated materially to 84.5% in Q3 FY2025 compared to 74.4% last year, driven by adverse development on runoff commercial auto.
positive_highlights: Insurance distribution segment revenue increased by 80% year-over-year to $43 million driven by strong organic growth.
Adjusted EBITDA for the insurance distribution segment reached a record $6 million, up from $2.1 million in the prior period.
Corporate G&A expenses decreased slightly on an absolute basis ($27.2M vs $26.6M) despite one-time M&A and exit costs.
summary: Octave Specialty Group reported a net loss of $32 million ($0.67 per share) for Q3 FY2025 compared to an $18 million loss in the prior year period. While insurance distribution revenue surged 40% organically, overall results were weighed down by higher intangible amortization and interest expenses following a legacy business exit. Management provided cautious guidance on Everspan's premium outlook for 2026, projecting growth north of $400 million but noting modest sequential increases rather than aggressive expansion.

negative_highlights: Total consolidated revenue grew only 1% YoY pro forma to $45.1 million; hospitality revenue fell 4% pro forma and entertainment revenue fell 5% on seven fewer concerts
Entertainment segment adjusted EBITDA declined 51% YoY; reported consolidated segment adjusted EBITDA fell $7 million pro forma
GAAP net loss of $33.2 million ($2.61/share) included ~$11 million in leadership-transition accruals; management gave no forward guidance and deferred the Tin Building plan to the next call
positive_highlights: Adjusted net loss improved 71% YoY to $7.2 million and adjusted loss per share improved 87% to $0.57
Excluding one-time items, consolidated segment adjusted EBITDA improved 76% ($4 million+) YoY, with hospitality adjusted EBITDA up 40% and landlord up 76% on that basis
Same-store hospitality revenue rose 11% and combined hospitality revenue including Lawn Club grew 5%; rental revenue rose 56% pro forma
summary: Total consolidated revenue was $45.1 million, up 1% YoY on a pro forma basis, with hospitality revenue down 4% pro forma (though up 5% including Lawn Club and same-store hospitality up 11%) and entertainment revenue down 5% on seven fewer rooftop concerts. Consolidated segment adjusted EBITDA fell $7 million YoY pro forma, but improved 76% (over $4 million) excluding non-recurring items like the $4 million 250 Water Street held-for-sale loss, $2 million rooftop structure write-off, and prior-year reimbursement benefit. GAAP net loss was $33.2 million ($2.61/share), including an ~$11 million leadership-transition accrual, while adjusted net loss improved 71% to $7.2 million ($0.57/share). Management gave no formal guidance, deferring Tin Building plans to the next call and flagging Q4 F&B revenue moderation, while pointing to the 250 Water Street sale (now $152 million, closing by December 15) and ~100,000 sq ft of leasing pipeline for future momentum.

negative_highlights: Revenue flat year over year at $2.9 million
Logistical delays pushed new product launches to late September, impacting potential sales by $100,000-$200,000
Full-year guidance of $12-$12.5 million implies a flat-to-down year versus prior-year revenue of ~$12.9 million (if guidance is met at midpoint), and AbbVie relationship is uncertain
positive_highlights: Gross margin expanded to 42.4% from 39.3% year over year
Adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed sequentially for third consecutive quarter to $354,000
Received Health Canada approval for SilverSeal and expanded Stada partnership with new product launches planned
summary: NEXGEL reported Q3 FY2025 revenue of $2.9 million, flat year over year; gross margin improved to 42.4% from 39.3%, and adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed to $354,000 from $500,000 in Q1 and $419,000 in Q2. The company guided full-year 2025 revenue to $12-$12.5 million (implying a strong Q4) and expects to approach adjusted EBITDA breakeven in Q4. Contract manufacturing remained steady, with iRhythm orders anticipated in Q4, but consumer product launches were delayed by logistical issues, and uncertainty surrounds the AbbVie relationship.

negative_highlights: Total 19% revenue growth was largely driven by $5.5 million of licensing revenue, while hardware product revenue declined 6% ($736,000)
Full-year 2025 revenue guidance was reiterated rather than raised, and initial 2026 guidance was deferred to March
positive_highlights: Gross margin expanded to 66.1% from 58.4% year-over-year on favorable mix and greater scale
Adjusted EBITDA was $4.5 million versus a $1 million loss in the prior-year quarter, and net income was $1.3 million versus a $5 million loss
The pending $19.2 million sale of non-core assets to Companion Spine, with $7.5 million already paid, is expected to remove the need for additional external capital
summary: Xtant reported Q3 2025 revenue of $33.3 million, up 19% year-over-year, but the increase was driven by $5.5 million of one-time licensing revenue while core Biologics grew only 4%, below management's long-term expectation. Gross margin expanded to 66.1% from 58.4%, net income was $1.3 million versus a $5 million loss, and adjusted EBITDA was $4.5 million versus a $1 million loss. Management reiterated full-year 2025 revenue guidance of $131-135 million and said the pending $19.2 million sale of non-core Coflex/Cofix and international assets to Companion Spine, expected to close by year-end, should eliminate the need for external capital; 2026 guidance is deferred to March.

negative_highlights: CFO transition announced (Hadar leaving, incoming CFO Hod Cohen)
Gross margin may vary based on revenue mix; expected to sustain at ~77% in Q4 only
R&D grant expected to decline to ~$50k in Q4
positive_highlights: Record revenue of $18.4 million, up 16.2% year-over-year
Record non-GAAP operating income of $3.8 million (20.9% of revenue)
Positive cash flow of $5.1 million and record cash balance of $106.7 million
summary: RADCOM reported record Q3 2025 revenue of $18.4 million, up 16.2% year-over-year, with record non-GAAP operating income of $3.8 million (20.9% margin) and record non-GAAP EPS of $0.29. Cash flow from operations was $5.1 million, ending cash at $106.7 million. Management reiterated full-year 2025 revenue growth guidance of 15-18% and targets double-digit growth for 2026, citing strong pipeline and new partnerships (NVIDIA, ServiceNow, 1Global) expected to contribute initial revenue in 2026.

Prelude Therapeutics reported strategic progress in Q3 FY2025, including an exclusive option agreement with Incyte for its JAK2V617F program, with $60 million upfront (including $25 million stock purchase) and potential $100 million option exercise payment plus milestones up to $775 million. Management highlighted two lead programs on track for IND filings in 2026: a JAK2V617F selective inhibitor (IND Q1 2026, Phase I in H1 2026) and a KAT6A selective degrader (IND mid-2026, Phase I in H2 2026). Preclinical data show differentiation over existing therapies, but no financial results (revenue, EPS) were provided, and clinical data readouts for KAT6 will likely not come until 2027. The tone is confident and forward-looking, emphasizing pipeline progress and business development.

negative_highlights: THP discontinued after failing to find strategic partner
Q4 growth expected to decelerate due to tough comparison and prior saline shortage benefits
Sequential EBITDA margin flat
positive_highlights: Net revenue grew 22% YoY to $26.3 million
Adjusted EBITDA improved by $2.3 million YoY
Distributor network expanded from 300 to 400+ in trailing twelve months
summary: Sanara MedTech reported Q3 FY2025 surgical net revenue of $26.3 million, up 22% year-over-year, driven by soft tissue repair product sales up 24% to $23.4 million. Adjusted EBITDA improved by $2.3 million and operating cash flow was $2.2 million. The company announced discontinuation of Tissue Health Plus (THP) after failing to find a strategic partner, with expected cash costs of $5.5–$6.5 million in H2 2025 and no material cash spend after 2025. Management expects slower growth in Q4 2025 due to a tough comparison and one-time benefits from last year's saline shortage, but remains confident in the surgical business.

negative_highlights: Management tempered full-year FY2025 guidance for gross originations (now 20-23%), revenue (18-20%), and adjusted EBITDA ($8-9M) citing macroeconomic uncertainty.
Write-offs as a percent of revenue increased to 9.9%, up 60 basis points from the prior year quarter, though within target range.
Gross margin contracted slightly to 19.7% compared to 19.8% in Q3 FY2024.
positive_highlights: Gross originations grew 25.3% YoY, marking the 12th consecutive quarter of growth in this metric.
Revenue delivered $74M (up 22.8%), representing the tenth consecutive quarter of year-over-year revenue growth.
Adjusted EBITDA was positive at $4.4 million, exceeding the previously guided range of $3-3.5 million.
summary: Katapult reported Q3 FY2025 gross originations of $64.2 million (up 25.3% YoY) and revenue of $74 million (up 22.8%), both within the company's outlook range, while delivering positive adjusted EBITDA of $4.4 million above its guidance. Management highlighted strong application growth but noted a minor headwind from recent underwriting tightening and comped against robust Q4 2024 results when setting forward expectations. Consequently, management tempered full-year FY2025 outlooks for gross originations (now 20-23%), revenue (18-20%), and adjusted EBITDA ($8-9 million) due to macroeconomic uncertainties.

negative_highlights: Core revenue declined YoY as instrument and license sales were adversely impacted by customers consolidating programs due to the depressed funding environment.
Management expects a drag on growth through the first half of next year from key customers rationalizing their pipelines.
Gross margin contracted in non-GAAP terms (81% vs 85%) reflecting lower volume and product mix shifts toward less expensive instruments.
positive_highlights: Signed four strategic platform licenses (SPLs) this year, bringing the total signed SPL count for FY2025 to 4 and cumulative portfolio to 32.
SeQure DX is fully integrated with growing customer interest in its unique off-target risk assessment assays.
Vertex's CASGEVY program showed strong momentum with cell collections doubling year-over-year, driving royalty revenue.
summary: MaxCyte reported Q3 FY2025 core revenue of $6.4 million and total revenue of $6.8 million, both missing prior year levels due to timing shifts into Q4 and a challenging operating environment affecting key customers. Management reiterated full-year guidance for flat-to-10% decline in core revenue but highlighted significant restructuring actions including a 34% workforce reduction expected to generate $17M-$19M in annualized savings starting in late 2025.

negative_highlights: No explicit revenue or EPS guidance was provided for fiscal 2026; management only framed the 4.8% adjusted EBITDA margin as a 'new baseline'
Handmade by Robots will not materially impact fiscal 2026 results, with meaningful contribution deferred to fiscal 2027–28
Cash balance was just $3.2 million against $66 million of debt, leaving limited liquidity headroom before the new revolver
