Adjusted EBITDA rose 259% to $12.2 million, a 4.8% margin versus 1.5% a year earlier
Net income improved to $4.9 million, or $0.10 per diluted share, from $400,000, or $0.01
summary: Alliance Entertainment reported Q1 FY2026 net revenue of $254 million, up 11% YoY from $229 million, with gross margin expanding 340 bps to 14.6% and adjusted EBITDA rising 259% to $12.2 million (4.8% margin). Net income was $4.9 million, or $0.10 per diluted share, versus $0.01 a year ago. Management called the 4.8% adjusted EBITDA margin a 'new baseline' for fiscal 2026, but did not issue explicit numeric revenue or EPS guidance, and clarified that the Handmade by Robots acquisition will not materially affect fiscal 2026 results, with impact expected in fiscal 2027–28.

negative_highlights: Net loss of $26.5 million in the quarter with no product revenue
G&A of $4.5 million reflects ongoing public-company costs against no offsetting revenue
Timeline for ALTITUDE-AD top-line data remains late 2026, roughly a year away, with EBD candidate selection data not until early 2026
positive_highlights: Cash of $136.1 million expected to fund current clinical and operational activities into early 2027
R&D expense fell to $22 million from the prior year on reduced CRO costs after ALTITUDE-AD enrollment completed in March 2025
First ALTITUDE-AD participants scheduled to dose in the open-label extension as soon as today, with all 542 enrollees eligible for up to 52 weeks of sabirnetug
summary: Acumen reported Q3 2025 R&D expense of $22 million and G&A of $4.5 million, producing a net loss of $26.5 million, with $136.1 million in cash and marketable securities expected to fund operations into early 2027. The company reaffirmed top-line ALTITUDE-AD data in late 2026, with the first participants now entering the open-label extension, and reiterated a nonclinical EBD data package in early 2026 to inform advancement of up to two development candidates under the JCR agreement. No revenue, EPS, or formal financial guidance was disclosed; R&D declined year over year on lower CRO costs after ALTITUDE-AD enrollment completed in March 2025. Management tone was steady, with no changes to prior timelines.

negative_highlights: Subscription, retail, and wholesale combined revenue declined year-over-year despite sequential improvement.
Net loss widened to $3.7 million due to a non-cash stock-based compensation charge of approximately $7 million.
G&A expenses increased significantly by 52% YoY primarily due to the one-time SBC charge and secondary offering costs.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 46% year-over-year to $18.4 million, exceeding prior guidance.
Adjusted free cash flow surged 88% YoY to $4.8 million for the seventh consecutive quarter of positive FCF.
Licensing revenue increased over 40% YoY driven by AI training data demand and new partnerships.
summary: CuriosityStream reported Q3 FY2025 revenue of $18.4 million (up 46% YoY), exceeding guidance with adjusted free cash flow rising to $4.8 million (+88%). Licensing drove the majority of growth at $8.7M, while subscription revenue declined sequentially despite sequential improvement over prior quarters; net loss was $3.7M driven by a one-time stock-based compensation charge of ~$7M and secondary offering expenses. Management raised full-year 2025 guidance to an implied range of $70-72 million based on Q4 expectations, while maintaining no-debt balance sheet with over $29M liquidity.

negative_highlights: Gross margin fell 320 bps YoY to 60.2% on manufacturing costs, lower yields, geographic mix, and ~50 bps of tariffs
Reported domestic revenue declined 5%, with a $1.2M geographic revenue imbalance distorting the quarter
Two previously announced IG pharma collaborations pushed launch dates into 2027, and a rare disease candidate slipped a quarter to Q1 2026
positive_highlights: Revenue rose 27% YoY to a record above $10 million, with core business up 30%
Full-year revenue guidance raised to $40.5M-$41.0M from $39.5M-$40.5M
Positive adjusted EBITDA and $400,000 of cash generated in the quarter, with YTD net loss halved to $2.2M from $4.5M
summary: KORU reported Q3 FY2025 revenue above $10 million for a second straight quarter, up 27% YoY, with core business growth of 30%. Gross margin fell 320 bps to 60.2% on higher manufacturing costs, lower yields, unfavorable geographic mix, and ~50 bps of tariffs, though full-year margin guidance of 61%-63% was reiterated. Full-year revenue guidance was raised to $40.5M-$41.0M (20%-22% growth) from a prior $39.5M-$40.5M range, while positive operating cash flow guidance was reaffirmed. Management flagged a $1.2M geographic revenue shift (US distributor destocking, outsized international stocking orders, and a distributor cross-border sale) that depressed reported domestic revenue 5% against 230% international growth.

negative_highlights: Effective tax rate rose to 9.7% from 5.1% due to OECD Pillar Two provisions, and management expects convergence to 15% from 2026
Residency student count fell 36% to 9,969 and paying medical practice users declined 2% to 195,000
Medical practice monthly active users decreased to 228,000 from 249,000 a year earlier
positive_highlights: Nine-month revenue grew 13% YoY to BRL 2.784 billion and adjusted EBITDA rose 19% to BRL 1.292 billion with margin up 200 bps to 46.4%
Net income increased 20% to BRL 593 million and basic EPS rose 20% to BRL 6.40 for the nine-month period
Operating cash flow reached a record BRL 1.292 billion with 101.5% cash conversion; net debt fell BRL 473 million to BRL 1.342 billion and leverage was 0.8x
summary: Afya reported Q3 2025 revenue of BRL 2.784 billion for the nine-month period, up 13% year-over-year, with adjusted EBITDA rising 19% to BRL 1.292 billion and a 46.4% margin (up 200 bps). Q3 adjusted EBITDA grew 15% to BRL 399 million at a 43% margin (up 160 bps); net income for the nine-month period rose 20% to BRL 593 million and basic EPS grew 20% to BRL 6.40. Management provided no explicit updated full-year guidance but indicated 2026 gross tuition increases of 5.0-5.2% and expects the effective tax rate to converge toward the 15% Pillar Two minimum from 2026. Key changes included approval of 100 new medical seats (total 3,753), a 36% decline in residency students (one-time product bundling effect), and a 2% decline in paying medical practice users.

negative_highlights: Retail segment revenue declined approximately 5% YoY as Intellicheck diversifies away from this vertical which now represents only ~30% of the mix.
A major social media client is still in a build-out phase with delayed image capture capabilities, generating only mid-5-figure revenue and expected to reach low 6-figures in Q4.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 28% YoY to a third-quarter record of $6 million driven by banking growth (approx. 80%) and title insurance expansion (+120%).
Adjusted gross margin expanded to 92.8%, up from 91.5% in the prior year.
Operating expenses remained flat at $5.21 million despite full recognition of R&D costs, demonstrating disciplined cost management.
summary: Intellicheck reported Q3 FY2025 revenue of $6 million, a 28% year-over-year increase driven by banking and lending growth (approx. 80%) which now represents roughly half the business. Adjusted gross margin improved to 92.8%, while operating expenses remained flat at $5.21 million despite no capitalization of software development costs this quarter, resulting in a record adjusted EBITDA of $631,000 and positive net income of $290,000.

negative_highlights: Total revenue declined YoY primarily due to lower realized oil and NGL prices, down 14% and 8%, respectively.
Adjusted EBITDA contracted from $8.1 million last year reflecting the impact of lower commodity prices and higher lease operating costs at TexMex during operator transition.
Delhi production was impacted by downtime related to unscheduled turbine repair and higher summer temperatures, reducing CO2 activity.
positive_highlights: Evolution declared its 49th consecutive quarterly cash dividend of $0.12 per share for fiscal Q2, maintaining a strong financial foundation with ample liquidity.
The company closed an acquisition consisting only of minerals and royalties in the SCOOP/STACK region, expanding exposure to high-quality reserves without future capital commitments.
Natural gas revenues increased 38% over the year-ago quarter driven by higher realized prices despite Henry Hub averaging $3.03.
summary: Total revenue declined modestly to $21.3 million from the prior year period due to lower realized oil and NGL prices partially offset by a 43% increase in natural gas pricing. Net income fell to $0.8 million ($0.02 per share) compared to $2.1 million last year, while Adjusted EBITDA decreased to $7.3 million from $8.1 million due to lower commodity prices and higher lease operating costs at the TexMex asset.

negative_highlights: Automotive gross margin declined sequentially to 43.2% from Q2's 50.5%, attributed to product mix and manufacturing line transition expenses.
Cash balance decreased quarter-over-quarter, ending at $93.5 million compared to $102.7 million in Q2.
positive_highlights: Revenue beat expectations at $17.3 million versus a guided range of $15.1 million to $15.6 million.
GAAP gross margin expanded sequentially and came in above guidance at 63% (vs. Q2's 63%).
Adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed significantly to $4.3M, better than the guided range of a $7.4M-$6.8M loss.
summary: Valens Semiconductor reported Q3 FY2025 revenue of $17.3 million, beating the guidance range of $15.1M-$15.6M and marking a sequential increase from Q2's $17.1M. GAAP gross margin expanded to 63%, exceeding the guided range of 58%-60%. Management raised full-year revenue expectations to $69.4M-$70.1M (midpoint ~$69.75M) and provided Q4 guidance of $18.2M-$18.9M, projecting seven consecutive quarters of growth.

negative_highlights: Management noted they have been slower or slightly delayed in terms of campus delivery compared to original projections four years ago, though this was met with additional equity.
Construction costs remain higher than originally forecasted when the bond deal was issued four years prior.
positive_highlights: Consolidated revenues grew 78% YoY and 11% sequentially, reaching $7.3 million.
Operating expenses decreased moderately as one-time non-recurring startup costs from Q2 did not carry into the quarter.
Company is less than $1 million away from breakeven on a cash flow for operations basis.
summary: Consolidated revenues increased 11% sequentially to $7.3 million in Q3 FY2025, driven by the acquisition of Camarillo Campus and higher activity at existing sites. Operating expenses dropped slightly due to one-time startup costs from prior quarters not recurring, bringing the company within less than $1 million of breakeven on a cash flow basis for operations. Management reaffirmed guidance to reach 23 airports by year-end despite recent project modifications.

negative_highlights: Cash burn was $14M in the quarter, though expected to decline sequentially
No specific margin or profitability metrics disclosed
Guidance reiterated rather than raised for full-year revenue
positive_highlights: Q3 revenue $15.3M; year-to-date $42.4M, up 2.3x vs prior year
Major commercial vehicle OEM selected Innoviz for level 4 autonomous trucks
NRE payment plans raised above $110M for 2025-2027
summary: Innoviz reported Q3 2025 revenue of $15.3 million, with year-to-date revenue of $42.4 million, up 2.3x from the prior year. Management reaffirmed FY2025 revenue guidance of $50-60 million, more than double YoY, and raised NRE booking guidance to $30-60 million, already within range. The company announced a new level 4 autonomous trucking OEM win, ramped production at Fabrinet, and highlighted continued momentum in level 4 programs with VW/MOIA and non-automotive Innoviz Smart deployments. Innoviz Three was unveiled with a 60% smaller form factor and planned behind-windshield integration.

negative_highlights: Prior year net reserve development was unfavorable by approximately $1 million for the first nine months of the year.
Management expects underlying loss ratios to increase slightly (by about one point) over the next 12 months due to inflation and Citizens book impacts.
positive_highlights: Gross premiums written surged 49% YoY to $239 million, driven primarily by voluntary market growth rather than Citizens takeouts.
Underlying loss ratio remained favorable at approximately 17.4% on a gross basis for the year-to-date period, aligning with expectations despite inflationary pressures.
Combined ratio improved substantially from 94% in Q3 '24 to 79% in Q3 '25 due to scale benefits and stronger ceding commissions.
summary: American Integrity Insurance Group reported a strong Q3 FY2025 with gross premiums written increasing 49% to $239 million and net income available to common shareholders reaching $13 million ($0.67 EPS). The combined ratio improved significantly to 79%, driven by favorable non-cat losses (underlying loss ratio of ~17%) and disciplined expense management, though the company noted some immaterial unfavorable reserve development offsetting prior year gains. Management raised guidance for future profitability by confirming a plan to gradually reduce quota share reinsurance usage in 2026 while expanding voluntary growth into middle-aged homes and new states.

negative_highlights: Netbacks fell 23% YoY to $30.84/BOE on lower realized prices
Basic EPS fell to $0.10 from $0.14, with net income down to $3.6 million from $5.1 million on a $1.8 million negative hedge mark-to-market swing
CEO signaled a 2026 program likely targeting flat production given weak prices, and deferred East-side (Forguson) drilling until prices rise
positive_highlights: Production up 40% YoY to 4,254 BOE/d (from 3,032) and up from 3,200 BOE/d in Q2 2025
Revenue up 15% to $15 million and adjusted EBITDA up 9% to $11.1 million despite an 18% price decline
$65 million borrowing base reaffirmed; operating costs excluding one-time production tax true-up fell 1% YoY to $6.57/BOE
summary: Q3 2025 production rose 40% YoY to 4,254 BOE/d and revenue grew 15% to $15.0 million, but realized prices fell 18%, netbacks dropped 23% to $30.84/BOE, and EPS fell to $0.10 from $0.14 (partly a $1.8 million negative hedge mark-to-market swing). Adjusted EBITDA rose 9% to $11.1 million; the $65 million borrowing base was reaffirmed in October, and net debt stood at $42.8 million with $18.5 million of availability. The 4 new wells are being fracture-stimulated and are expected to produce in early December, supporting a record exit rate, but management signaled a 2026 program likely targeting flat to slightly-growing production given weak oil prices, and it deferred further East-side drilling until prices recover.

negative_highlights: Q2 revenue guided to $22.3-22.8 million, a sequential decline driven by sunsetting the messaging platform (~$600,000) and government shutdown-related services delays
Full-year FY2026 revenue guidance of $90.5-92 million implies modest growth; EPS guidance includes a 1% dilution impact from higher share count
Sales and marketing spend declined sequentially and year over year; sales hiring step-up deferred to the second half
positive_highlights: Total gross margin expanded 600 bps to 76% from 70%, with SaaS gross margin up to 81% from 77%
Non-GAAP EPS of $0.17 versus $0.04 a year ago; adjusted EBITDA margin of 21% versus 6%
Total RPO up 23% year over year; operating cash flow of $10.4 million versus $1 million a year ago
summary: eGain reported Q1 FY2026 total revenue of $23.5 million, up 8% year over year and at the high end of guidance, with SaaS revenue up 10% and SaaS ARR for knowledge customers up 23%. Total gross margin expanded 600 basis points to 76%, non-GAAP EPS rose to $0.17 from $0.04, and operating cash flow was $10.4 million (44% margin). For Q2, guidance of $22.3-22.8 million reflects about $600,000 of messaging platform revenue being sunset plus government shutdown-related services delays; full-year FY2026 revenue is guided to $90.5-92 million, a return to growth, with non-GAAP EPS of $0.29-0.34. Management noted sales and marketing spend stepped down in the quarter and plans to increase sales hiring in the second half.

negative_highlights: U.S. revenue growth decelerated to just 1% YoY
Full-year 2025 revenue guidance cut to $89-$90 million
Operating leverage remains elusive with net loss of $14 million
positive_highlights: Gross margin improved to 75% from 74%
International revenue grew 15% YoY
Added 9 new U.S. centers in the quarter
summary: Pulmonx reported Q3 FY2025 revenue of $21.5 million, up 5% YoY (4% constant currency), with U.S. revenue up only 1% and international up 15% (9% constant currency). Gross margin improved to 75% from 74%, but net loss remained at $14 million (EPS -$0.34) and adjusted EBITDA loss was $8.2 million. Management lowered full-year 2025 revenue guidance to $89-$90 million (from a prior range not in the transcript) and acknowledged slowing U.S. growth and lack of operating leverage. Newly returned CEO and CFO are conducting a bottom-up review to realign spending and extend cash runway, but provided no specifics.

negative_highlights: Revenue missed expectations due to delays in three specific large contracts totaling approximately $6.4 million, including an expected Brazil CapEx deployment and a Puerto Rico renewal.
Management admitted they are 'not where we need to be' regarding sales execution despite having healthy demand across existing and new markets.
Gross profit margin contracted from 58% in the prior year period to 54%, primarily attributed to the mix of delayed deals.
positive_highlights: Retention is coming in better than expected this quarter due to intentional customer success engagement, reflected by an NPS score of plus 70 up four points from last year.
SafePoint weapons detection technology gained momentum following California's AB-2,975 mandate with multiple pilot programs underway and a new booking secured at a Florida nonprofit hospital.
Cash generation remained positive with adjusted EBITDA of $3.5 million despite the revenue shortfall.
summary: Third-quarter revenues were $25.1 million, a decrease of approximately 4% year-over-year to $26.3 million in the prior period, driven by delays in three large contracts including an expected CapEx deployment in Brazil and a Puerto Rico renewal. Consequently, full-year 2025 revenue guidance was lowered from a range of $111-113 million to approximately $104 million, with adjusted EBITDA margin guidance reduced from 20%-22% to 14%-15%. Management cited sales execution challenges and delays in converting pipeline as the primary drivers for these misses.

negative_highlights: DBMG gross margin compressed year-over-year by approximately 510 basis points to 13.6%.
Spectrum segment adjusted EBITDA decreased $700,000 due to softness in ad sales and customer terminations.
positive_highlights: Infrastructure adjusted EBITDA increased by $2.6 million ($19.8M total) driven by revenue growth in commercial structural steel fabrication.
summary: Consolidated revenue increased 43.3% to $347.1 million and adjusted EBITDA rose to $19.8 million in Q3 FY2025 compared to the prior year period. The Infrastructure segment drove growth with a 45.4% revenue increase, while Life Sciences grew modestly at 3.3%. However, margins compressed significantly across segments due to macro headwinds and project timing shifts.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA fell to $6M from $12M a year ago
GAAP net loss of $107M due to noncash charges including $35M impairment and $30M tax valuation allowance
International real estate business placed in administration with ongoing wind-down support through 2027
positive_highlights: Revenue up 10% year-over-year to $57M, with 95% recurring management fees
International added over $600M in new assets during the quarter, including a $240M mandate
Zero-based budgeting delivering savings, with $20M in recurring annual savings expected by 2026
summary: AlTi Global reported Q3 2025 revenue of $57M, up 10% year-over-year, with 95% recurring revenue, but adjusted EBITDA fell to $6M from $12M a year ago. The quarter included large noncash charges: a $35M impairment of the arbitrage fund intangible, $16M receivable write-off, $30M tax valuation allowance, and a $20M loss from discontinued operations (international real estate). The CEO cited continued cost-cutting, with $20M in annual gross savings expected by 2026, and strong new asset flows ($1.2B international YTD, $1.1B US through September), but net loss widened to $107M.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA was significantly impacted by $2.5 million in litigation expenses related to China and domestic arbitration.
The company is not currently utilizing its stock buyback authorization as the priority remains deleveraging and extending debt maturity until May 2028.
Honey Birdette growth strategy relies on raising third-party capital rather than using internal cash flow, indicating a need for external investment to accelerate expansion.
positive_highlights: Licensing revenue grew 61% year over year, driven by six new deals signed in the quarter bringing total YTD to 14.
Honey Birdette comparable store sales increased 22% year over year with gross margins expanding 700 bps from 54% to 61% due to reduced promotions and full-price item growth of 15%.
The Great Playmate Search exceeded expectations with approximately 130,000 unique users signing up for a multimillion-dollar annualized business potential.
summary: Playboy reported Q3 FY2025 revenue of $29 million and net income of $500,000, marking the first quarter of positive net income since going public. Adjusted EBITDA was $4.1 million inclusive of $2.5 million in litigation expenses (excluding which it would have been $6.6 million). Management raised guidance for licensing revenue growth and highlighted strong underlying trends after normalizing prior-year one-time items.

negative_highlights: Management explicitly stated there was no material contribution from the ExoDx acquisition in Q3 due to closing at end-of-quarter.
The company decided to forego focus on its germline offering for H1 and likely part of H2, reducing expected revenue by approximately $5 million compared to prior expectations.
Tissue-based volumes faced a sequential slowdown driven by reduced patient flow directed toward biopsies.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA turned positive at $1 million for the quarter, following first profitability in Q2.
Gross margins expanded four percentage points YoY to 65.2% driven by test mix and operational efficiencies.
Operating loss declined significantly from a prior year deficit of $6.1 million to just $2.6 million.
summary: Q3 revenue grew 18% YoY to $27.4 million while adjusted EBITDA turned positive at $1 million following the ExoDx acquisition closing in September. Management maintained full-year guidance of $108-$110 million despite foregoing material contribution from the germline offering, offsetting it with Q4 contributions from Exo and ResolveMDx growth. The company expanded its sales organization to 60 reps across eight regions but noted a sequential slowdown in tissue-based biopsy patient flow.

negative_highlights: Total revenues were adversely impacted primarily by continued weakness in card issuing along with a decline in interest income
Adjusted EBITDA declined incrementally on a sequential basis from $500,000 in the second quarter to $368,000 this quarter
Some government-related programs and SNAP payments were pushed out or put on hold due to federal government shutdown concerns
positive_highlights: Record quarterly overall transaction volume of 16,200,000 representing an 8% increase from a year ago
ACH revenues up strongly for the third consecutive quarter with electronic check transactions growing sequentially in all periods reported
Penless debit offering set all-time records with growth over the same period in 2024 of 96% for transactions processed and 87% for dollars processed
summary: Q3 FY2025 revenues were relatively unchanged year-over-year due to weakness in card issuing and a decline in interest income, though the quarter saw record processing volumes across all channels including an ACH volume up 8% YoY. Adjusted EBITDA was $368,000, down sequentially from Q2 but remaining positive with operating cash flow of $1,400,000 and share repurchases totaling approximately $750,000 year-to-date. Management noted that the current quarter includes one-time non-recurring items in last year's comparison which will normalize going forward.

negative_highlights: Q4 2025 dividend suspended: no distribution anticipated due to an expected approximately $4.0 million taxable loss on the Private Company P settlement
GAAP net loss of $12.5 million ($0.57 per share) versus $3.5 million of distributable earnings ($0.16), with a $51.3 million CECL reserve equal to 18.7% of loans at carrying value
Private Company P loan moved to nonaccrual, settled at $13.3 million against a $15.3 million carrying value; Private Company K dispensary sales not expected to close until 2026
positive_highlights: Shareholders approved both BDC conversion proposals, with over 61% of outstanding shares represented and over 94% of votes cast in favor
Received $43 million of principal repayments since the end of Q2, including Private Company J's $23.2 million payoff at par plus accrued interest
Built an approximately $415 million pipeline including roughly $60 million in cannabis and the balance non-cannabis, with target IRRs described as low double-digit
summary: AFCG reported Q3 2025 net interest income of $6.5 million and distributable earnings of $3.5 million, or $0.16 per basic share, against a GAAP net loss of $12.5 million ($0.57 per share). Book value was $7.49 per share with a $51.3 million CECL reserve (18.7% of loans at carrying value). Management said it does not anticipate a Q4 2025 distribution due to an expected ~$4.0 million taxable loss on the Private Company P settlement, and said the board will reset the go-forward dividend policy alongside the BDC conversion expected in Q1 2026. Shareholders approved the REIT-to-BDC conversion with over 94% of votes cast in favor, and management cited an approximately $415 million pipeline, of which roughly $60 million is cannabis.

negative_highlights: Total revenue decreased year-over-year and sequentially due to the deliberate phase-out of non-core hardware components.
The company remains unprofitable with an EPS loss of $0.13, though this represents a substantial improvement over prior periods.
Management declined to provide specific unit deployment numbers for new kiosk products or exact ARR figures.
positive_highlights: Subscription revenue mix increased significantly from 88% last year to 99% in Q3, enhancing predictability and margins.
Gross margin expanded to 89%, up from 86% the prior quarter, reflecting disciplined cloud cost management.
Operating expenses reduced by $400k (approx. 8%) compared to Q2 despite increased stock-based compensation.
summary: Q3 revenue declined to $1.1M from Q2's $1.2M due to a strategic shift away from hardware sales toward pure software subscriptions (ARR mix rose to 99%). Gross margin improved to 89% driven by cost controls, while operating expenses decreased quarter-over-quarter despite higher stock-based compensation. The company reported an EPS loss of negative $0.13 compared to a larger loss previously.

negative_highlights: No financial results or guidance provided in the call
Phase III readouts not expected until mid-2026 and end of 2026
Ended formal engagement with Evercore, indicating no imminent strategic transaction
positive_highlights: Enrollment for CBEYOND on track to complete next month; top-line results mid-2026
Cash of $329.3 million provides runway through 2027
New dual mechanism of action for bemifovir may explain higher potency vs sofosbuvir
summary: Atea Pharmaceuticals reported no financials for the quarter; instead, the call focused on clinical progress. Enrollment for the Phase III HCV trial CBEYOND is on track to complete next month, with top-line results expected mid-2026; C FORWARD enrollment completes mid-2026 with results by end of 2026. New data highlighted a dual mechanism of action for bemifovir, no drug-drug interactions with PPIs, and positive resistance analysis. The company also announced expansion into hepatitis E with two preclinical candidates and maintained a strong cash position of $329.3 million, sufficient through 2027. The company ended its formal engagement with Evercore to focus on Phase III execution.

negative_highlights: Enrollment remains slow, with management targeting only about one patient per month and noting an Australian summer holiday slowdown.
Cash balance of approximately $5.8 million is modest relative to the ongoing trial and no revenue is being generated.
EV data is based on only three patients with noted heterogeneity in timing and magnitude of changes, and no clinical response can be commented on from this safety/feasibility trial.
positive_highlights: Operating expenses fell 48% to approximately $1.5 million from $2.9 million a year earlier, and operating loss narrowed to $1.5 million from $2.8 million.
All three Cohort 1 participants completed treatment with no dose-limiting toxicities or device-related serious adverse events; the DSMB recommended advancing to Cohort 2.
Decreases in PD-L1-carrying large extracellular vesicles were observed in all three participants, with EV reductions in two of three.
summary: Aethlon reported fiscal Q2 2026 operating expenses of approximately $1.5 million, down 48% from $2.9 million a year earlier, with an operating loss narrowing to $1.5 million from $2.8 million, and ended the quarter with roughly $5.8 million in cash. The company is a pre-revenue medical device firm, so there was no revenue or EPS; the key operational update was that three Cohort 1 patients completed a single 4-hour Hemopurifier treatment with no dose-limiting toxicities or device-related serious adverse events, and the DSMB context advancing to Cohort 2. Management flagged slow enrollment, targeting roughly one patient per month with a summer holiday slowdown in Australia, and described the trial as difficult to watch to patients. No formal financial guidance was provided.

negative_highlights: ReMEDy2 stroke enrollment below the previously used ~0.25 patients/site/month historical rate, pushing the 200-patient interim analysis to H2 2026
Net loss widened to $8.6 million in Q3 from $6.3 million a year earlier; 9-month operating cash use rose to $21.3 million from $15.6 million
Management declined to provide the assumed enrollment rate needed to reach the H2 2026 interim analysis
positive_highlights: Cash, cash equivalents and note weakness in-term investments of $55.3 million, up from $30.0 million at June 30, 2025, after the July private placement; runway stated into H2 2027

Preeclampsia Part 1a interim data showed statistically significant, dose-dependent reductions in systolic and diastolic blood pressure and a statistically significant reduction in uterine artery pulsatility index
Cohort 10 completed and a 12-patient expansion cohort initiated at the expected therapeutic dose; Part 3 fetal growth restriction screening expected to start in coming weeks
summary: DiaMedica reported no revenue and a Q3 net loss of $8.6 million versus $6.3 million a year earlier, with R&D up to $6.4 million from $5.0 million and cash of $55.3 million after a July private placement, funding operations into H2 2027. The main change was in the stroke program: management said ReMEDy2 enrollment is running below its previous 0.25 patients/site/month assumption due to shifting stroke referral patterns and now expects the 200-patient interim futility analysis in H2 2026 rather than earlier. Preeclampsia progress continued, with Cohort 10 completed, a 12-patient expansion cohort dosing, and an FDA pre-IND meeting held. No guidance on enrollment rates was provided.

negative_highlights: Q3 revenues declined to $2.4 million, impacted by corporate restructuring efforts
Revenue from Roblox decreased as a percentage of revenue mix (down from 57% in 2024)
Demand reduction noted for brands building custom destinations on platforms
positive_highlights: Gross margin expanded to 45% from 44% in the prior quarter
Pro forma operating costs decreased by 29% compared to the respective prior year periods
Weighted pipeline increased by 69% over the past six weeks
summary: Q3 FY2025 revenues decreased to $2.4 million compared to the prior year period due to a focus on corporate turnaround and cost reduction initiatives. Gross margin improved sequentially to 45% from Q2's 44%, while pro forma operating costs dropped significantly by 29%. Management raised guidance for future quarters, stating that booked revenue for Q4 is already higher than Q3 and Q1 2026 expectations are approaching Q1 2025 levels.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined 16% year-over-year due to decreased sales of M400 smart glasses
Gross loss widened to $0.4 million compared to a gross loss of only $0.3 million in the prior period
R&D expenses increased approximately 26% primarily due to higher external development costs and depreciation
positive_highlights: Quanta Computer completed a third $5 million tranche of investment totaling $20M after meeting manufacturing milestones
Defense business transitioning into production deliveries for military heads-up displays with revenue contribution beginning in Q4
Cash position strengthened to $22.6 million, up from $17.5 million at the start of the quarter
summary: Vuzix reported Q3 FY2025 revenue of $1.2 million, down 16% year-over-year due to decreased M400 sales and lower engineering services ($0.3M vs $0.4M prior). The company recorded a net loss of $7.4 million compared to $9.2 million in the prior year period, with total operating expenses declining by $1.8 million (20%) driven largely by reduced stock-based compensation. Management indicated that while business momentum is increasing for Q4 based on current orders and new defense production deliveries starting this quarter, they are cautious about providing specific volume ramp timelines due to supply chain issues and tariffs.

negative_highlights: No commercial revenue reported or recognized for Q3 FY2025; company remains pre-revenue.
G&A expenses increased year-over-year from $2.0M to $2.5M due to professional services and commercial readiness costs.
ATM program capacity is currently limited by 'baby shelf' market cap restrictions.
positive_highlights: On track to launch DARE to PLAY Sildenafil Cream via 503B compounding by end of year (December start).
Significant capital raise: $18.7M from stock sales and $7.3M in grants strengthened the balance sheet.
FDA regulatory environment improved for hormone therapy, removing black box warnings that hindered DARE to RECLAIM development.
summary: Daré Bioscience reported Q3 FY2025 financial results showing a significant reduction in R&D expenses to $1.2 million (down from $2.7M) and an increase in G&A to $2.5 million, while raising approximately $18.7 million via stock sales and receiving $7.3 million in grants. The company provided no specific revenue or EPS figures for the quarter but confirmed it is on track to begin commercializing DARE to PLAY Sildenafil Cream through a 503B outsourcing facility starting December 2025, with initial revenue expected in Q4 FY2025.

negative_highlights: Total revenue fell 15% YoY to $142 million and adjusted EBITDA fell to $4 million from $30 million in Q3 2024
Non-core project burn is now expected near 20% of full-year revenue versus the ~10% originally guided, creating an unfavorable mix drag on gross margin
Full-year adjusted EBITDA is now expected toward the lower end of the $5-15 million range, and net loss was $4 million for the quarter
positive_highlights: Backlog grew over $100 million sequentially (15%) to $754 million, with a book-to-burn ratio of 1.7x, the first time above 1.0x in two years
Shimmick core project revenue rose 6% YoY to $107 million and core gross margin rose 61-67% YoY as new projects ramped up
Total liquidity of $48 million and management stated comfort with the capital position
summary: Shimmick reported Q3 FY2025 revenue of $142 million, down 15% YoY, but that decline was entirely due to a one-time $31 million GGB claim settlement in the prior-year quarter; on a like-for-like basis revenue grew 5%. Gross margin was $11 million versus $12 million a year ago, again distorted by the prior-year settlement, and adjusted EBITDA was $4 million versus $30 million in Q3 2024, though the company noted this was its first positive adjusted EBITDA of the year. Management reaffirmed full-year 2025 guidance but said revenue should land in the higher end of the range while adjusted EBITDA lands toward the lower end, citing non-core project burn now expected near 20% of total revenue versus the ~10% originally anticipated. Backlog rose over $100 million sequentially, or 15%, to $754 million, with a book-to-burn ratio of 1.7x, the first time above 1.0x in two years.

negative_highlights: Q3 revenue declined from $3.1 million in prior period due to BARDA contract termination and zero Q3 contract revenue
Net loss widened to $6.3 million versus $5.8 million in the same quarter last year
Cash balance decreased to $5 million at September 30, down from $5.5 million a quarter ago
positive_highlights: EMA provided expedited development path guidance for GEO-MVA against Mpox and Smallpox
Initiated fill/finish of clinical batch vaccine material with availability anticipated early next year
Gedeptin Phase II trial protocol modified to first-line therapy mimicking KEYNOTE-689 historical control
summary: GeoVax reported Q3 FY2025 revenues of $2.5 million versus $3.1 million in the prior year period due to the termination of BARDA Project NextGen contracts and no contract revenue in Q3, resulting in a net loss of $6.3 million compared to $5.8 million previously. Management highlighted positive regulatory progress for GEO-MVA with EMA guidance allowing bypass of Phase I/II trials, but explicitly stated they do not anticipate commercialization or emergency use licensing prior to clinical evaluation.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined to $29.8 million from $33.6 million a year ago, reflecting significant industry-wide traffic volatility from algorithmic changes.
Management said news-related traffic remains off its Q2 peak, and e-commerce content is expected to be stronger in Q4 but off a lower base.
No specific financial guidance was provided; the debt refinance timeline is uncertain as banks want more quarters of profitability.
positive_highlights: Net income rose to $6.9 million from $4.0 million a year ago, with net margin expanding to 23.2% from 11.9%.
Adjusted EBITDA increased to $11.9 million from $11.2 million, and gross margin held above 50%.
Generated $12.1 million cash from operations, fully repaid the revolving credit facility, and reduced total debt by over $10 million year-to-date, ending with $12.5 million cash.
summary: Q3 FY2025 revenue fell to $29.8 million from $33.6 million, while net income rose to $6.9 million and adjusted EBITDA to $11.9 million, with gross margins above 50% and net margin expanding to 23.2% from 11.9%. The company generated $12.1 million in operating cash flow, repaid its revolver, and reduced debt by over $10 million, ending with $12.5 million cash. Management described traffic as stabilizing after algorithmic headwinds, pointed to e-commerce recovery and Q4 sequential growth, but gave no formal financial guidance and said a debt refinance will proceed deliberately.

negative_highlights: Valuation gain of $7.1 million was 12.5% lower than the prior year, primarily due to stabilization in Colombia and impacts from construction investments in Peru.
Rental revenue in Costa Rica decreased 1.5%.
Revenue growth in Mexico is currently limited to roughly $222,000 in rental revenue for the quarter.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 14.3% in Mexico due to the acquisition of two facilities in Puebla anchored by a 5-year dollar-denominated lease with DHL.
SG&A expenses decreased 5% year-over-year, creating meaningful operating leverage as the portfolio expands.
Occupancy rate remained strong at 98% across the operating portfolio with all renewals for the next 12 months completed.
summary: LPA reported Q3 FY2025 revenue of $12.9 million, which was in line with guidance and driven by double-digit growth in Colombia and Peru. Net Operating Income (NOI) increased 8.7% year-over-year to $10.4 million, while SG&A expenses decreased 5%. Management raised full-year visibility for sustained double-digit revenue growth following the completion of lease renewals for the next 12 months.

negative_highlights: No financial beat or guidance raise reported; call focused entirely on clinical milestones rather than quarterly earnings performance.
Management noted that some study sites were terminated due to enrollment fit issues, though this is described as standard course of business.
positive_highlights: Last patient completed the randomized double-blind phase of PALISADE 3, with top-line results expected before the end of the calendar year.
Company has $77.2 million in cash and marketable securities to fund ongoing development.
New board member Paul Edick joined with decades of experience leading FDA approvals.
summary: VistaGen Therapeutics provided a corporate update for the second quarter of fiscal year 2026 (ended Sept 30, 2025), reporting $77.2 million in cash and marketable securities. The company confirmed it is on track to release top-line results from its PALISADE 3 Phase 3 trial for social anxiety disorder by the end of the calendar year. Management also welcomed a new board member and reiterated that current cash reserves cover known aspects of the ongoing US registration-directed program.

negative_highlights: No revenue or earnings reported as the project is still in development prior to Final Investment Decision (FID).
Initial head grade variance observed during early vertical well operations, though resolved by horizontal testing.
Offtake agreements are not yet secured; management targets 70% of production under contract but negotiations remain ongoing.
positive_highlights: Boron officially recognized as a U.S. critical mineral, unlocking federal funding eligibility including USXM loans and DFC investments.
Horizontal well tests validated commercial design consistency with head grades around 7% after initial variance issues were resolved.
Full-scale product testing underway with multiple Tier 1 specialty glass manufacturers following successful shipment to Taiwan.
summary: The company reported no financial results for Q1 FY2026 as it remains in the development phase with a pre-feasibility study confirming project economics of a $725 million NPV and 39.5-year mine life. Management highlighted that boron was officially added to the U.S. Critical Minerals list, validating their strategy and unlocking access to federal funding programs like USXM and DFC loans totaling up to $435 million in potential capital. Operational progress included successful horizontal well testing showing consistent head grades around 7% and full-scale product trials with Tier 1 specialty glass manufacturers.

negative_highlights: Net income fell to $1.7 million ($0.06 per diluted share) from $2.9 million ($0.12), with operating expenses up 21.9% to $12.6 million; adjusted EBITDA down 5% to $7.8 million
ACC staff report on the rate case was 'unexpected' per management, proposing roughly 50% below the company's request; final outcome not expected until mid-2026
Phoenix metro single-family permits fell 29% in Q3 (to 4,724) and Maricopa permits fell 20% (to 164); organic connection growth was 3.3% annualized
positive_highlights: Revenue increased 8.4% to $15.5 million, aided by the Tucson acquisition, organic connection growth and higher rates at GW Farmers and GW Saguaro

Closed Tucson acquisition of 7 water systems (~2,200 connections, ~$7.7 million rate base) at 1.05x rate base, versus the 1.5x-2x peer range cited by management; expected to generate ~$1.5 million annual revenue
Total active service connections rose 6.6% to 68,130; Highway 347 expansion fully funded and Ag-to-Urban water legislation signed, both cited as growth drivers for Maricopa
summary: Q3 2025 revenue rose 8.4% to $15.5 million, but operating expenses jumped 21.9% to $12.6 million, pushing net income down to $1.7 million ($0.06 per diluted share) from $2.9 million ($0.12) a year earlier. Adjusted EBITDA fell 5% to $7.8 million. Management said the ACC staff report on the pending rate case was unexpected and contrary to its proposal, though it still expects a fair outcome in mid-2026 with rates effective around July 1; the case now supports a $4.3 million annual rate increase. Total connections grew 6.6% to 68,130, including the July Tucson acquisition (7 systems, ~2,200 connections, ~$7.7 million rate base at 1.05x), while organic connection growth was 3.3% annualized and Phoenix-area building permits fell 29% in Q3.

negative_highlights: Net revenue declined 27.5% year-over-year to $19 million from $26.2 million
Gross margin contracted to 56.1% from 60.3% a year ago, including a $400,000 product remediation charge
Cash balance fell to $7.6 million from $18 million at December 31, 2024, and inventory rose to $17.2 million from $13.7 million at year-end
positive_highlights: Contribution margin expanded over 700 basis points sequentially to 15.5% from 7.8% in Q2 2025
Adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed by over 80% quarter-over-quarter to approximately $400,000 from $2.2 million
Secured approximately $5.5 million of the targeted $5–6 million in annualized fixed cost savings
summary: Aterian reported Q3 2025 net revenue of $19 million, down 27.5% year-over-year, with gross margin falling to 56.1% and a net loss of $2.3 million; adjusted EBITDA shifted to a $400,000 loss from a $500,000 gain a year earlier. Sequentially, revenue declined just 2% from Q2, while contribution margin improved to 15.5% and the adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed from $2.2 million, reflecting cost reductions and pricing actions. Management reaffirmed its initial guidance for the six months ending December 31, 2025, of $36–38 million revenue and adjusted EBITDA between breakeven and a $1 million loss, unchanged from prior guidance. The company suspended its share repurchase program in May and holds $7.6 million in cash versus $18 million at year-end 2024.

negative_highlights: Stellantis terminated its offtake agreement, one of three supporting debt financing
Debt syndication process paused due to the Stellantis withdrawal
Government shutdown impacting permitting progress and travel at Coosa deposit
positive_highlights: $53 million cash balance provides solid runway
Qualification line successfully delivering large samples (over 1 metric ton) of CSPG
US patent secured for environmentally friendly purification process
summary: Westwater Resources reported Q3 FY2025 results with no specific revenue or EPS figures disclosed in the transcript; management highlighted a significant negative development where Stellantis terminated its offtake agreement, pausing debt syndication. The company raised approximately $55 million since June to maintain liquidity and is optimizing Kellyton Phase 1 capacity alignment while awaiting early 2026 strategy updates.

Net income conversion was muted by a higher tax rate as NOLs are largely exhausted, with management stating the rate will exceed 6% going forward
Management noted the government shutdown, tariffs, inflation and import restrictions are making the food industry more cautious, with some level of impact
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 10% to $6.0 million from $5.4 million while total operating expenses rose only 3% and SG&A 6%
Income from operations rose 28% to $1.9 million and GAAP net income rose 13% to $1.8 million despite the higher tax rate
Balance sheet carries $28.8 million in cash with zero bank debt, plus 8,715 shares repurchased for $150,000 and continued preferred redemption at $750,000 per quarter
summary: ReposiTrak reported Q1 FY2026 revenue up 10% to $6.0 million from $5.4 million, income from operations up 28% to $1.9 million, and GAAP net income up 13% to $1.8 million ($0.09 diluted), with EPS up 13% despite a higher tax rate as NOLs have largely run out. No explicit forward revenue or EPS guidance was given; management reiterated its 10-20% ARR growth and faster profitability growth framework and said the tax rate will be higher than 6% going forward. Cash from operations fell to $1.5 million from $1.9 million on deferred revenue conversion, while total cash rose to $28.8 million with no bank debt. The key change versus prior periods is the announced multiyear development-environment modernization and AI initiative, framed as near cost-neutral via reallocated capex.

negative_highlights: Company explicitly declined to provide specific guidance on capital raising cadence or token acquisition volumes for the remainder of Q4 and early 2026.
Yield generation is described as fluctuating, with management stating they cannot promise sustained yields in the higher double-digit range (11-12%) indefinitely.
Management refused to comment on trading dynamics regarding high note weakness in interest or potential for a note weakness in squeeze.

On-chain allocation has increased to over 15%, providing access to higher yielding opportunities compared to previous levels under 10%.
Management confirmed that management and insider shares are not lent out for note weakness in note.
summary: DeFi Development Corp reported Q3 FY2025 results where the company beat its full-year guidance for average organic yield by generating 11.4% versus a target of approximately 10%. Management maintained forward guidance for roughly 10% average organic yield and reiterated a long-term goal to reach $1 SOL per share by December 2028, though they declined to provide specific cadence or volume guidance for token acquisitions in Q4/early 2026. The company highlighted the successful execution of its Treasury Accelerator program and on-chain expansion while noting that yield rates fluctuate.

negative_highlights: Cash and cash equivalents of only $1.3M as of September 30, 2025, down from $2.6M at June 30, 2025
Revenue is entirely event-driven from a single partner (BI); no other collaboration was announced despite stated business development focus
Obesity programs remain preclinical, with IND-enabling work still ongoing and first-in-human data not expected until the second half of 2026

Net income of $4.7M versus a $7.8M net loss a year ago, with operating expenses down to $4.2M from $7.8M
$18.2M upsized public offering closed, restoring NYSE American compliance and, combined with projected expenses, removing the going concern provision and extending runway beyond December 31, 2026
summary: Palatin reported Q1 FY2026 collaboration license revenue of approximately $8.8 million versus $0 in the prior-year quarter, driven entirely by the Boehringer Ingelheim agreement (a ~$2.3M upfront and a ~$6.5M research milestone, plus cost reimbursements). Total operating expenses fell to $4.2 million from $7.8 million, net cash used in operations decreased to $1.6 million from $7.0 million, and the company swung to net income of $4.7 million from a $7.8 million net loss. Cash was only $1.3 million at September 30, 2025 (excluding the $6.5 million milestone received in October and $16.9 million net offering proceeds), but the November 2025 $18.2 million upsized offering removed the going concern provision, restored NYSE American compliance under ticker PTN, and extended runway beyond December 31, 2026. Management guided to roughly $15 million in near-term BI research milestones within the next 12 months and reiterated PL-7737 IND filing in the first half of calendar 2026 with data in the second half.

negative_highlights: FY2025 revenue and gross profit came in slightly below expectations due to housing headwinds and percent-completion revenue pushing into 2026
FY2026 guidance implies lower EPS than 2025 despite higher revenue, since the nearly 100%-margin oil and gas royalty contribution is unlikely to repeat
Higher cost of revenue from tariffs and inflation, and land development revenue in 2026 expected slightly down depending on housing

Recurring water customer base growing at roughly a 22% CAGR, with ~1,600 commercial connection points out of 60,000 potential
Single-family rental portfolio at ~97% occupancy with ~40 homes under contract delivering ~5 units per month into fiscal 2026
summary: Pure Cycle's fiscal Q4 and full-year 2025 revenue and gross profit came in below management's expectations, driven by housing headwinds and roughly $800,000 of land-development revenue slipping into Q1 2026. Full-year net income and EPS exceeded forecast (prior plan ~$12.5M) on stronger oil and gas royalty income from 6-7 newly completed wells, partly offset by higher cost of revenue from tariffs and inflation. Management guided FY2026 revenue growth to a 26%-30% range with EPS likely down versus 2025 because that year's oil and gas royalty margin will not repeat, and sees land development slightly down depending on housing.

negative_highlights: EBITDA and EBIT declined year-over-year in Q3, though in line with H2 guidance.
Management remains cautious on Canadian fleet rightsizing, with 2026 outlook deferred until mid-December pending oil sands tender outcomes.

Infrastructure opportunities (like Fargo wind-down) are still in early stages, with no contracts inked for subcontracting work, and Canadian critical mineral project timing expected no earlier than 2027.
positive_highlights: Australia revenue grew 26% YoY to $188M, driven by new contracts and expanded production, with September monthly revenue of $65M setting a company record.
Gross margin expanded to 14.6% from 8.9% in Q2, with Australia at 19.6% and oil sands improving to 9.2%, aided by reduced reliance on external maintenance providers.
Bid pipeline increased $2B to a record $12B, including $2B added to backlog, and senior secured leverage improved to 1.3x pro forma for the October notes offering.
summary: NOA reported Q3 FY2025 revenue of $390M, up 6% sequentially, with Australia revenue growing 26% YoY and 12% sequentially to $188M, setting a monthly record of $65M in September. Combined gross margin was 14.6%, up from 8.9% in Q2 (restated), and adjusted EPS was $0.67. EBITDA margin improved to 25.3% from 21.6% in Q2, in line with H2 guidance, while free cash flow was $46M. Management reiterated its H2 2025 outlook and expects to provide 2026 guidance in mid-December after oil sands tenders are resolved.

negative_highlights: Revenue fell to $6.5M from $18.4M in Q2 and $15.8M YoY
GAAP gross margin 15.3% down from 18.1% year ago
Non-GAAP gross margin 9.3% YTD versus 16.6% prior year
positive_highlights: Record 140 vehicles shipped in Q3, including 10 strip chassis

summary: In Q3 2025, Xos reported revenue of $6.5 million, below sequential and year-ago levels, but shipped a record 140 vehicles (130 recognized). GAAP gross margin improved to 15.3% from 8.8% QoQ, and operating loss hit a record low at $7 million. Cash rose to $14.1 million from $8.8 million, aided by ATM proceeds and inventory reductions. Management emphasized expanded powertrain orders from Bluebird, Hub momentum, and amended convertible note terms, while noting tariff and mix pressures on near-term margins.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA declined $2.4 million year-over-year due to manufacturing inefficiencies and lower capacity utilization.
Gearing segment revenue down period-over-period due to lower deliveries and capacity utilization.
PRS softness continues, with customers citing oil prices as a restraint on capital.

Revenue guidance raised to $155–$160 million for fiscal 2025.

Adjusted EBITDA fell by $2.4 million year-over-year to $3.4 million, impacted by manufacturing inefficiencies and lower gearing utilization. The company completed the sale of its Manitowoc industrial fabrication operations, boosting liquidity and reducing debt, and announced a $3 million share repurchase program. Management raised full-year 2025 revenue guidance to $155–$160 million (from $145–$155 million) while maintaining adjusted EBITDA guidance of $9–$10 million, and expects improved capacity utilization and operational leverage heading into 2026.

summary: Bionano reported Q3 2025 total revenue of $7.4 million, up 21% year-over-year (12% on a core basis after adjusting a $0.5 million prior-year discontinued-services write-down), with a record 8,390 flow cells sold (+7% YoY). Non-GAAP gross margin expanded to 46% from 26%, and non-GAAP operating expense fell 40% to $9.7 million. The company reiterated full-year 2025 revenue guidance of $26-30 million and guided Q4 to $7.5-7.9 million, while raising the outlook for new OGM system placements to above the prior 20-25 range. Net installed base rose to 384, and cash ended at $31.8 million after a $10 million equity offering, extending runway into Q3 2026.

Net interest expense increased by $400k quarter-over-quarter due to lower cash deposits.
positive_highlights: Net loss decreased from $10.7 million in Q2 FY24 to $9 million in Q3 FY25 due to lower operating expenses of $8.1 million versus $10.2 million prior year.

VERSATILE-002 trial final data showed median overall survival of 39.3 months and progression-free survival of 10.3 months for patients with CPS >= 1, supporting the drug's efficacy in HPV-positive head and neck cancer.
Company raised $5.8 million from a sale of common stock or prefunded warrants to bolster cash reserves.
summary: PDS Biotechnology reported a net loss of $9 million ($0.19 per share) for Q3 FY2025, representing an improvement from the prior year's loss of $10.7 million due to lower operating expenses and R&D costs. The company completed its VERSATILE-002 trial with robust Phase 2 data showing a median overall survival of 39.3 months for HPV-positive patients but paused enrollment in the pivotal VERSATILE-003 Phase 3 trial while seeking FDA approval to add progression-free survival as a primary endpoint to accelerate readouts.

Hardware sales fell to $1.2 million from $1.3 million due to lower tag volumes and herd shrinkage.
Operating income decreased to $575,000 from $608,000 in the prior year.

Verification revenue for pork, dairy, egg, organic, non-GMO, gluten-free, and Upcycled programs all increased year-over-year.
Customer retention rates remain well above the 90% level.

Net income grew significantly to $1.1 million ($0.22 per share) primarily due to a $946,000 gain on the sale of Progressive Beef and asset gains, rather than core operational expansion. Management expressed caution regarding near-term beef supply recovery due to border closures with Mexico and drought, while noting that cattle prices are beginning to support herd rebuilding.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to $4.9 million and operating loss widened to $4.8 million, compared with $3.9 million and $3.6 million in Q3 2024 and Q2 2025 respectively.
Operating expenses rose to $6.4 million from $4.2 million in Q3 2024 and $4.7 million in Q2 2025, with sales and marketing at $2.4 million driving the increase.

Gross margin expanded to 31.3% from 7.9% in Q3 2024 and 26.4% in Q2 2025, with YTD gross margin at 26.7% versus 10.5% a year ago, driven by fixed cost absorption and product mix.
Total indebtedness was reduced to $2.9 million from $4.8 million at year-end 2024, with $3.3 million of unused line of credit and $3.8 million in cash.
summary: WKSP reported Q3 2025 net sales of $5.0 million, up 61% year over year and 22% sequentially from $4.1 million in Q2. Gross margin expanded to 31.3% from 7.9% in Q3 2024 and 26.4% in Q2 2025, with YTD gross margin at 26.7% versus 10.5% a year ago. However, the company reported a net loss of $4.9 million and an operating loss of $4.8 million, wider than both the $3.9 million loss in Q3 2024 and $3.6 million in Q2 2025, as operating expenses rose to $6.4 million. Management guided to FY2025 revenue of $17-21 million versus 2024 ARR of $8.5 million, and stated a target for operating cash flow positivity in H1 2026, with 35% gross margins expected by year-end and 35-40% targeted for 2026.

The JetAI merger outside date and finalization of the ATM facility were both delayed by the federal government shutdown
Wholesale revenue grew only 4% year to date, versus 15% in Q3, showing uneven growth in that channel
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed to $1.9 million from a $13 million loss in Q3 2024, a nearly 1,500 bps YoY margin improvement

summary: Q3 FY2025 revenue rose 20% YoY to $92.1 million, and the adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed sharply to $1.9 million from a $13 million loss a year earlier, a roughly 1,500 bps improvement. Flight revenue grew 17%, MRO revenue doubled to $3.1 million, retail membership rose 51%, and contracted programs reached about 45% of flight revenue. Management gave no formal numeric guidance but said it expects positive adjusted EBITDA in the near term and to sustain it into 2026, citing a record October and November trending above record levels. The JetAI merger outside date and the ATM facility were both delayed by the federal government shutdown.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to $11 million from $9.2 million in the prior quarter due to warrant liability changes and growth investments.
Management declined to provide specific directional guidance for 2026, focusing only on Q4 2025 targets.
International expansion faces longer procurement timelines compared to US deals, particularly in hospital settings.

Gross margins expanded 450 bps sequentially to a record 53.8% due to higher average note prices.
Cash burn decreased 27% sequentially to $5.9 million excluding financing, extending the cash runway into 2027.
summary: Hyperfine reported Q3 FY2025 revenue of $3.4 million (up 27% sequentially) and gross margins expanding to a record 53.8%. The company raised full-year 2025 guidance to $30-$40 million revenue and increased the gross margin range to 49%-51%, citing strong pipeline growth in hospitals, offices, and international markets.

EPS declined from $0.11 to $0.01 due to higher expenses for the beverage launch and public company costs
Cash used in operating activities increased significantly to $3.21 million over nine months

summary: Synergy CHC reported Q3 FY2025 revenue of $8 million (up 12.4% YoY) and gross margin expansion to 70.9%, but net income fell significantly from $783,600 to $125,300 due to higher operating expenses associated with launching the beverage division and public company costs. Adjusted EBITDA grew by 13.4% YoY despite a slight decline in reported EBITDA driven by one-time other income last year. Management highlighted new distribution wins (EG of America, Wakefern) but noted that G&A will likely increase further as they scale the beverage sales network.

R&D expenses increased to $5.2 million, including a one-time charge of approximately $2.1 million for nelitolimod study closure.

TriNav FLX now accounts for approximately 35% of the product mix, showing rapid adoption.
summary: TriSalus reported Q3 FY2025 revenue of $11.6 million, representing a 57% year-over-year increase and a 3% sequential gain. The company reaffirmed its full-year guidance for 50% revenue growth while noting that gross margins declined slightly to 84% due to manufacturing inefficiencies associated with newly launched products. Management highlighted strong commercial momentum driven by the new CMS reimbursement code C8004 for mapping procedures and the expansion of the TriNav product suite.

negative_highlights: Full-year revenue guidance lowered to a range of 5%-6%, slightly below prior expectations due to slower growth in digital wallets.
Adjusted EBITDA margin expected to drop from Q3 levels to approximately 23% for the full year as low-margin ISO business outpaces direct channels.
New product initiatives, specifically new wallet solutions, are taking longer than planned to deliver and gain momentum.
positive_highlights: Organic revenue growth accelerated to 6% with double-digit contribution from new sales and product initiatives.
E-commerce volume grew over 20%, driven by iGaming which exceeded 50% growth in the quarter.
Digital wallet segment achieved strong consumer engagement, surpassing 500,000 registrations for account and card products.
summary: Paysafe reported Q3 FY2025 revenue of $433.8 million (up 2% YoY) and adjusted EPS growth of 37%, though organic revenue growth was slightly below expectations at 6%. Management updated its full-year guidance to expect lower margins due to a slower rollout of new wallet products, weaker e-commerce in non-core verticals, and continued strength in the low-margin ISO channel. The company returned $20 million via share repurchases and authorized an additional $70 million for buybacks.

summary: Nyxoah reported Q3 2025 revenue of EUR 2.0 million, up 56% YoY from EUR 1.3 million, with gross margin of 60.5% versus 62% a year ago and an operating loss of EUR 24.4 million versus EUR 15 million, driven by U.S. launch investment. Following FDA approval on August 8, the first U.S. commercial implant was completed in September, generating EUR 231,000, with 15 implants across 9 accounts through end of October and 35 of 102 VAC submissions approved. Q4 2025 guidance is EUR 3.4-3.6 million, and the company secured up to $77 million in new capital (a ~$25 million equity private placement plus a convertible bond of up to $52 million) extending cash runway into Q1 2027. Cash fell to EUR 22.5 million at September 30 from EUR 43 million at June 30.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened from $10 million in Q4 FY2024 to $113 million in Q4 FY2025 due to non-cash goodwill impairments of $146 million
Full-year gross profit decreased 2% despite revenue growth, resulting in a full-year operating loss of $130 million for the quarter
Adjusted EPS declined from a loss of $0.36 to less than $0.1 due to significant non-operational charges
positive_highlights: Revenue increased 22% in Q4 to $460 million and full-year sales grew 6% to $1.9 billion
New boat demand normalized with unit volume up significantly compared to the prior year's hurricane-impacted quarter
Exited brands allowed for a cleaner inventory position, described as 'the cleanest we've seen in years'
summary: Fiscal fourth quarter 2025 revenue increased 22% to $460 million and full-year revenue rose 6% to $1.9 billion, driven by higher new boat volumes following prior year hurricane disruptions. However, the company reported a net loss of $113 million in Q4 (vs $10M) due to non-cash goodwill impairments of $146 million and an adjusted EBITDA miss relative to implied expectations given the strong top-line growth. Management provided flat same-store sales guidance for 2026 ($1.83B-$1.93B revenue), explicitly noting that this outlook is offset by a headwind from exited brands.

Two tariff-impacted investments drove $0.15 per share in unrealized losses
Fee income ran at about one-third of historical run rate; no Q4 supplemental dividend
positive_highlights: NII per share stable at $0.46 with 110% dividend coverage for Q3

NAV fell to $19.28 from $19.55, driven by $0.15 per share in unrealized losses from two tariff-affected investments. Portfolio yield held at 10.4%, non-accruals improved to 1.6% from 2.4%, and management maintained the $0.42 dividend while flagging potential NII pressure from lower base rates. Fee income was about one-third of historical run rate, and no Q4 supplemental dividend was declared.

Gross margin contracted significantly from 32.4% to 28.6%
Net loss widened to $0.15 per share compared to $0.10 in the prior year period
positive_highlights: Secured large new orders totaling $2.4 million from top material handling customers
Doubled airline customer base, now supplying eight major North American airlines including a significant ground service equipment order
Completed two capital raises totaling $13.8 million to support working capital and product development
summary: Revenue declined to $13.2 million from $16.1 million in the prior year quarter due to a pause in customer orders caused by tariff uncertainty and macroeconomic concerns. Gross margins contracted to 28.6% from 32.4%, while operating expenses decreased to $5.9 million following workforce reductions, resulting in an expanded net loss of $0.15 per share versus $0.10 last year. Management noted a temporary pause but highlighted multimillion-dollar orders received and expects order trends to strengthen in the second half of the fiscal year.

negative_highlights: Q3 revenue decreased by 1% ($0.1M) compared to Q2, driven entirely by partner inventory timing rather than demand issues
Management explicitly refused to provide any forward guidance or predictability on future revenues due to Chiesi's private status and inventory control
R&D expenses surged 58% in the nine months ended Sept 30 ($13.9M) primarily due to preparations for PRX-115 Phase II
positive_highlights: Net income turned positive at approximately $2.4 million ($3 EPS) compared to net loss or lower earnings previously
Successfully filed IND for PRX-115 Phase II trial in October with plans to initiate patient screening later this year
Cash position of $29.4 million is sufficient to fund operations and the upcoming clinical trial for more than 12 months
summary: Protalix reported Q3 FY2025 revenues of $17.9 million (down 1% YoY) and net income of approximately $2.4 million ($3 EPS), compared to a prior quarter revenue miss driven by partner inventory dynamics rather than patient demand. Management explicitly declined to provide forward guidance on full-year or next-quarter numbers, citing limitations with their private partner Chiesi's inventory management practices which decouple sales from underlying product uptake. While the company maintains sufficient cash for over 12 months and advanced its PRX-115 Phase II trial IND filing in October, the lack of revenue visibility creates a cautious outlook.

AUM reached a record BRL316 billion ($59.4 billion), up 4% quarter over quarter with BRL19 billion in capital formation and appreciation
summary: Vinci Compass reported Q3 FY2025 FRE margin of 32.3%, the highest in 2025 and above the 30% threshold, with net earnings of BRL77.1 million (BRL1.22/share) and adjusted distributable earnings of BRL73.1 million (BRL1.16/share), up 28% YoY nominally but only 7% per share. AUM rose 4% QoQ to BRL316 billion ($59.4 billion) on BRL19 billion of capital formation and appreciation, though largely offset by a BRL6 billion negative FX impact. Management guided that Q4 FRE margin would be slightly below 32.3% but above 30%, and that the VERGI acquisition closing in November should lift margins toward the mid-30s in 2026, keeping the 38% target by 2028 intact. The quarter's strongest driver was global IP&S, including TPD alternative upfront fees that management expects to be smaller in Q4.

negative_highlights: Q3 revenue was only approximately $266,000, with nine-month 2025 revenue of approximately $900,000, showing limited commercial traction so far.
Management will refresh the expiring three-year shelf registration and establish an at-the-market offering, implying potential future dilution.
TIGER PACT enrollment completion and final data were guided to early 2026 and 2027, respectively, leaving the key clinical catalyst still years away.
positive_highlights: RenovoCath approved purchasing centers grew from 5 at the start of 2025 to 14, with 5 centers already using the device and placing repeat orders.
24 centers have formally requested RenovoCath quotes, up from the 14 approved purchasing centers, indicating a broader demand pipeline.
Cash and cash equivalents exceeded $10 million as of September 30, 2025, which management said funds commercial scale-up and TIGER PACT enrollment completion into 2026.
summary: RenovoRx reported Q3 2025 revenue of approximately $266,000 from RenovoCath sales, bringing first-nine-month 2025 revenue to roughly $900,000, with R&D and SG&A each at $1.7 million and over $10 million of cash as of September 30, 2025. The company has expanded from five centers approved to purchase RenovoCath at the start of 2025 to fourteen now approved, with five having used the device and placed repeat orders, plus 24 centers having formally requested quotes. Management reaffirmed Phase III TIGER PACT enrollment completion in early 2026 with final data in 2027, and said cash is sufficient to fund commercial scale-up and the trial into 2026. No formal revenue or EPS guidance was provided, though management said it expects revenue to grow in 2026 and that it will refresh its shelf registration and establish an at-the-market offering.

positive_highlights: Revenue up 87% YoY to $5.3M

Gross margin improved to 74.3% from 63.1% a year ago, while net loss narrowed to $8 million from $9.4 million. The company announced full launch of its TULSA-AI Volume Reduction software at RSNA, increased installed base to 70 sites, and guided to sustained 70% growth. Management expressed confidence in achieving profitable growth, citing a pipeline of 93 new systems in late-stage sales processes.

Management notes a 'horrible' capital-raising market and need to save every penny
Milestone-based warrants not yet triggered; additional financing done via offerings
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 32% YoY to $0.6 million

Signed two partnerships with Werfen and Hologic; Werfen included upfront and ongoing payments
summary: In Q3 FY2025, VolitionRx reported revenue of $0.6 million, up 32% year-over-year, with operating expenses down 10% and net cash used in operating activities down 33%. The company signed two partnerships: a research license and exclusive commercial option with Werfen for APS, and a co-marketing agreement with Hologic for Nu.Q Discover. Management remains cautious, noting revenue lumpiness, no guidance, and a tough capital-raising environment, but expressed confidence in delivering more licensing deals and upcoming clinical milestones.

negative_highlights: Operating cash flow remains negative at approximately $3-4 million run rate, requiring continued fundraising or asset deployment
Life sciences segment continues to contribute losses and liabilities as the company pivots away from its legacy biotech business
Stock-based compensation was a tailwind of -$1.3M in Q3 due to leadership changes rather than operational performance
positive_highlights: Record GAAP net income of $6.6 million compared to a Q3 '24 loss of $7.9 million
Adjusted revenue grew significantly from less than $2,000 in Q3 '24 to over $300k in Q3 '25 due to new DeFi monetization services
Gross HYPE holdings increased to 1.7 million tokens ($77.8M) following a strategic purchase of an additional $20M worth of assets
summary: Hyperion DeFi reported record GAAP net income of $6.6 million and adjusted EBITDA of $8.0 million for Q3 FY2025, driven by a digital asset treasury strategy that generated over $300k in revenue from staking rewards and new HAUS agreements with Credo and Felix. The company raised approximately $41.8 million via PIPE and ATM offerings to purchase an additional 20M worth of HYPE tokens, expanding its gross holdings to roughly 1.7 million tokens valued at $77.8 million as of quarter-end. Management provided initial forward guidance for Q4 adjusted revenue between $475k-$515k (31-43% qoq growth) and aims to achieve operating cash flow positivity in 2026.

negative_highlights: Full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance was lowered from previous expectations to a loss range of minus $95 million to minus $110 million
Q3 results were impacted by an unfavorable midyear settlement adjustment of approximately $24 million total ($21M in Q3 and $3M prior period)
The company remains at a significant EBITDA loss, with normalized year-to-date adjusted EBITDA still showing a loss of approximately $70.1 million
positive_highlights: Normalized adjusted EBITDA loss improved by over $100 million compared to the same quarter last year
Medical margin expanded significantly from a prior period loss of $500,000 to a gain of $4.4 million in Q3 due to settlement adjustments
Operating expenses decreased 33% (or $10.4 million) compared to the prior year quarter
summary: P3 Health reported Q3 FY2025 capitated revenue of $341.6 million and an adjusted EBITDA loss of $45.9 million for the quarter. The company revised its full-year guidance to a range of minus $110 million to minus $95 million, citing unfavorable midyear settlements totaling approximately $21 million in Q3 that were not present in prior period expectations. Management highlighted stable normalized medical cost trends and over $100 million in EBITDA improvement year-over-year due to operational discipline.

negative_highlights: Management explicitly stated no financial results were provided as this is a strategic pivot to capital-intensive projects rather than reporting earnings
First-of-a-kind oxy-combustion project costs are rising, pushing potential Commercial Operation Date (COD) back to 2030 or 2031
Transitioning from a licensing model to building plants requires significant equity and debt financing which is not yet secured
positive_highlights: Identified West Texas Permian site as potentially the lowest cost clean firm power location in North America targeting below $80 LCOE
Established an exclusive partnership with Entropy, operator of the only operational natural gas CCS facility in North America
summary: NET Power Inc. announced a strategic pivot away from its long-term oxy-combustion technology to partner with Entropy for near-term deployment of conventional gas turbines with post-combustion carbon capture (PCC). The company expects to finalize the joint venture and achieve First Investment Decision in 2026, targeting commercial operation by 2028-2029. Management highlighted a potential CapEx range of $375-$425 million for Phase One but noted that no financial results were reported as this is an expansion into capital-intensive project development rather than current operations.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined approximately $595,000 year-over-year
Revenue expected to be flat or down year-over-year for full year
Net loss of $965,000 in Q3 due to lower revenue
positive_highlights: Gross margin remained strong at 77% in Q3 2025
OpEx decreased 8% year-over-year, reflecting cost discipline
Post-quarter $2.9 million net proceeds from warrant exercises strengthen cash position
summary: BIO-key reported Q3 2025 revenue of $1.55 million, down about $595,000 year-over-year primarily due to timing of large orders in Q3 2024. Gross margin remained strong at 77%, and operating expenses decreased 8% year-over-year. Net loss improved to $965,000 from $739,000 in Q3 2024 due to lower expenses. Management expects a strong Q4 and renewed subscription from a large banking customer in early 2026, with proceeds of $2.9 million raised post-quarter from warrant exercises strengthening liquidity.

negative_highlights: Management explicitly stated they would not provide prepared remarks or specific financial figures, making it impossible to verify revenue beats or misses.
The CEO described the quarter as 'grindy' and noted a volatile environment where deals were pulled after initial interest due to market headfakes.
