positive_highlights: CEO expressed optimism about capital markets picking up and a palpable sense that money is still on the sidelines for acquisitions.
summary: Management declined to provide prepared remarks or specific financial results for Q3 FY2025, citing a preference to answer questions directly after the press release was issued post-market close. The CEO expressed optimism regarding future capital markets and acquisition activity but noted that current external growth is limited by high interest rates rather than operational weakness. A one-time fee of $300,000 related to terminating easements on other property income was recognized in the quarter.

negative_highlights: Q3 revenue of $1.9 million came in below original expectations and declined $0.1 million sequentially, with work deferred into 2026
Net loss of $6.6 million against $1.9 million of revenue, with adjusted net loss of $6.7 million
NASDAQ delisting risk: market cap cited around $20 million versus a $35 million requirement, with a shareholder-equity alternative requiring $2.5 million and an early-December hearing
positive_highlights: Successfully operated Aquanaut to 2,300 meters water depth in the Gulf, the company's deepest subsea test to date
First commercial deployment of Nauticus ToolKITT on a third-party ROV, with a stated addressable market of 300-plus vehicles and software gross margins in the 80-plus percent range
Cash increased to $5.5 million at quarter end from $2.7 million in the prior quarter, aided by ATM funding and lender debt-to-equity conversions
summary: Q3 2025 revenue was $1.9 million, down $0.1 million sequentially and slightly below the company's original expectations, with management characterizing the shortfall as a strategic deferral of work into 2026. Net loss was $6.6 million (adjusted net loss $6.7 million) versus $7.4 million adjusted in Q2, while operating expenses of $7.8 million fell $0.6 million sequentially. Cash rose to $5.5 million from $2.7 million on ATM funding, and management cited a $250 million equity line of credit plus lender debt conversions and a $2.5 million shareholder-equity plan to address NASDAQ compliance, with a hearing in early December. Technical milestones included a 2,300-meter Aquanaut dive and first commercial deployment of ToolKITT on a third-party ROV, with 2026 pipeline described as beginning to fill, though 2025 project work has been pushed into 2026.

negative_highlights: Overall NOI declined by approximately $600,000 year-over-year.
Office segment NOI decreased due to lower rental revenues and higher real estate taxes at specific properties.
Hotel NOI dropped significantly to $850,000 from $4.2 million in the prior quarter due to renovation disruption.
positive_highlights: Core FFO improved to negative $10.5 million from negative $11.5 million in the prior year comparable period.
Multifamily NOI increased by approximately $284,000 year-over-year driven by lower real estate taxes.
Office leasing activity accelerated with 159,000 square feet executed in the first nine months of 2025, a 69% increase versus the prior year.
summary: Q3 FY2025 results showed a decline in overall Net Operating Income (NOI) to $7 million from $7.6 million in the prior year, driven by decreases in office and hotel segments. Core FFO was negative $10.5 million, an improvement from the prior year's negative $11.5 million, primarily due to reductions in preferred stock redemption expenses and dividends. Management highlighted progress on refinancing initiatives, the sale of the lending business for approximately $44 million, and steady growth in the multifamily portfolio.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined 7% year-over-year to $5.0 million, primarily due to $0.8 million of discontinued services.
A significant one-time non-cash impairment charge of $3.9 million was recognized in Q3.
Management explicitly stated they are unable to provide guidance for 2026 due to the transitional impact of switching shipping partners.
positive_highlights: Gross margin improved to 41% from 35% year-over-year, driven by better negotiated rates with a primary supplier.
Adjusted EBITDA improved to $0.8 million from $0.2 million in the prior year quarter.
Operating expenses decreased to $1.7 million from $2.5 million due to divestiture and cost-cutting measures.
summary: Third quarter revenue decreased 7% year-over-year to $5.0 million due to discontinued services and a transition from a previous shipping partner, while gross margin expanded to 41%. The company recognized a one-time non-cash impairment charge of $3.9 million related to goodwill and intangible assets in the PeriShip business. Management explicitly stated they cannot provide guidance for 2026 due to the ongoing transition dynamics.

negative_highlights: Q4 guidance implies a 24–30% sequential decline in online game revenue to $130–$123 million.
Q4 net loss attributable to Sohu guided at $25–$35 million on both GAAP and non-GAAP bases.
Marketing services revenue fell 27% YoY to $14 million, with management citing macro pressure and deteriorating auto and IT services ad demand.
positive_highlights: Total revenue rose 19% YoY and 43% QoQ to $180 million, with online games up 27% YoY and 53% QoQ to $162 million.
Returned to profitability with $9 million GAAP and non-GAAP net income, versus a $20 million net loss in Q2 and a $60 million GAAP net loss a year ago.
TLBB Return launch exceeded expectations and repurchases reached 7.6 million ADS for about $97 million, roughly two-thirds of the $150 million program.
summary: Sohu reported Q3 2025 total revenue of $180 million, up 19% year-over-year and 43% sequentially, driven by online games of $162 million (up 27% YoY, 53% QoQ), while marketing services fell 27% YoY to $14 million. GAAP and non-GAAP net income attributable to Sohu was $9 million, versus a $60 million GAAP net loss a year ago and a $20 million net loss in Q2. However, Q4 guidance implies a sharp sequential reversal: online game revenue of $130–$123 million (down 24–30% QoQ) and a projected net loss of $25–$35 million, as the Q3 spike from the TLBB Return launch normalizes and fewer promotional activities are planned.

negative_highlights: Organic revenue growth expectations were not met due to delayed rate cuts.
Tariff uncertainty created a slower sales cadence in the sector.
Non-recurring acquisition-related and non-cash financing costs totaled around $1.5 million, negatively impacting net income.
positive_highlights: Revenue up 19% YoY to $41.2 million driven by Carolina Stone integration.
Adjusted EBITDA increased 46% YoY reflecting acquisition growth and cost discipline.
Gross margin expanded from 21.7% to 24.4% due to sourcing improvements and product mix.
summary: Year-to-date revenue grew 19% year-over-year to $41.2 million driven by the Carolina Stone acquisition, while adjusted EBITDA increased 46%. Management noted that organic growth expectations were not met due to delayed rate cuts and tariff uncertainty, though they remain on track to close a fourth-quarter acquisition by December 15th. The company expects to execute 3-4 acquisitions in 2026 as the macro environment improves.

negative_highlights: Q4 revenue growth expected to be slower than anticipated due to delayed closing on enterprise SaaS deals and a specific nonrecurring project ending.
Adjusted EBITDA improvement was partially offset by significant foreign exchange headwinds from the stronger euro against the U.S. dollar.
Solutions segment delivered 30% growth, which is below management's initial expectation for even stronger revenue expansion.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 24% year-over-year with gross margin expansion from 65% to 69.1% on an IFRS basis.
Strategic partnership announced with Visa and Transcard to enhance payment solutions for freight forwarders.
Commercial validation of the new multimodal WebCargo Rate & Quote ocean product at Nippon Express.
summary: Freightos reported Q3 FY2025 revenue of $7.7 million (up 24% YoY), driven by a 15% increase in Platform and a 30% increase in Solutions segments, with gross margins expanding to 69.1% on an IFRS basis. Management maintained full-year guidance despite acknowledging slower-than-anticipated Q4 solutions revenue due to longer sales cycles for enterprise deals and FX headwinds reducing adjusted EBITDA improvement. The company reaffirmed its plan to reach adjusted EBITDA breakeven in Q4 2026, noting that ocean carrier integrations will not contribute meaningfully until 2028.

negative_highlights: A $3.9 million non-cash goodwill and intangible impairment was recognized on the PeriShip business, driving a $3.4 million net loss ($0.26 per diluted share)
Q3 revenue fell to $5.0 million from $5.4 million, with $0.8 million of discontinued Proactive services cited
Management guided that Q4 2025 and Q1 2026 revenue will decline year over year and declined to provide 2026 guidance until the next earnings call
positive_highlights: Gross margin expanded to 41% in Q3 2025 from 35% a year earlier, a third consecutive quarter of improved gross profit
Adjusted EBITDA improved to $0.8 million from $0.2 million in Q3 2024
Operating expenses fell to $1.7 million from $2.5 million a year ago, including about $500,000 of Trust Codes costs in the prior-year period
summary: Q3 2025 revenue was $5.0 million, down approximately 7% from $5.4 million a year ago, as $0.8 million of discontinued Proactive services offset gains from new and existing Precision Logistics customers. Gross margin improved to 41% from 35% (gross profit $2.1 million), adjusted EBITDA rose to $0.8 million from $0.2 million, and excluding a $3.9 million non-cash PeriShip goodwill/intangibles impairment, operating income was $0.5 million versus a $0.2 million loss. The reported net loss was $3.4 million, or $0.26 per diluted share, versus $2.9 million, or $0.23 per share. Management gave no 2026 guidance and expects Q4 2025 and Q1 2026 revenue to decline year over year due to the transition to a new Proactive shipping partner, while expecting gross margin to hold near current levels and full-year 2025 to remain cash-flow positive.

negative_highlights: Q3 2025 loss from operations of $2.3 million with cash only $2.15 million at September 30
MoUs not yet converted to binding orders; timeline depends on future NRC approvals
No revenue reported in the quarter
positive_highlights: Completed business combination generating $109 million net proceeds, fully funding FOAK activities estimated at $17 million
Signed MoU for up to 100 Solo units representing $1.9 billion in potential revenue
NRC licensing fees reduced by 50% and accelerated dual-track licensing process in place
summary: Terra Innovatum reported its first earnings as a public company post business combination, with Q3 2025 loss from operations of $2.3 million and cash of $2.15 million at September 30. Management emphasized strong regulatory tailwinds, NRC licensing progress with FOAK approval expected in 2027 and commercial approval in 2028, and noted an MoU for up to 100 units worth $1.9 billion in potential revenue. They are fully funded with $109 million net proceeds to advance licensing and construction, and maintain confidence in converting pipeline to binding orders within 12 months.

negative_highlights: Voyage revenues fell 26% to $24.2 million due to 74 nonrevenue drydocking days
TCE rates dropped 40% compared to the same period in 2024
Cash balance decreased 48% to $6.6 million due to vessel purchase settlement
positive_highlights: Net income increased 281% to $5.26 million for 9M 2025 from a net loss in 2024
EBITDA rose 245% to $10 million for 9M 2025
Fleet is fully delevered; all CapEx obligations repaid without bank debt
summary: For the first 9 months of 2025, C3is reported net income of $5.26 million (up 281% YoY) and EBITDA of $10 million (up 245%), though voyage revenues fell 26% to $24.2 million due to 74 days of drydocking on its Aframax tanker, which also drove a 40% drop in TCE rates. The company settled the final $14.6 million balance on the Eco Spitfire in April 2025, leaving the fleet fully unencumbered with no bank debt. Management noted market uncertainty from geopolitics and tariffs but highlighted fleet quality and strategic relationships with repeat charters.

negative_highlights: Net loss of $352.8 million was significantly wider than the prior year's loss of $3.7 million.
Unrealized loss on digital assets totaled $30.5 million, and non-cash charges related to warrants and financing costs exceeded $700 million combined.
Operating expenses surged to $36 million in 2025 compared to $3.9 million in 2024.
positive_highlights: Revenue increased from the prior year period due to the activation of staking rewards ($342,000).
The company successfully raised over $500 million via a PIPE transaction in September to fund its digital asset treasury strategy.
Staking yield averaged 7.3% APY in October, outperforming the top 10 largest validators by approximately 36 basis points.
summary: Third-quarter revenue was $697,000, driven by $342,000 in first-time staking rewards, but the company reported a net loss of $352.8 million (or $32.89 per share) due to significant unrealized losses on digital assets ($30.5 million), derivative liabilities ($545.7 million), and financing costs ($194.7 million). The quarter was the first full period of operations following a $500+ million PIPE transaction closed in September, resulting in a substantial increase in operating expenses to $36 million compared to $3.9 million in the prior year. Management noted that the digital asset treasury market has cooled and is entering an execution phase, while highlighting progress on their legacy neurotechnology platform.

negative_highlights: GAAP revenues were negative $2.8 million in the quarter versus positive $8.6 million in the prior-year period
Ben Liquidity interest income declined 3.8% sequentially to $8.5 million, and six-month interest income fell 24.1% year over year
Ben Custody six-month revenues fell 32.5% year over year, with NAV of alternative assets held in custody down to $271.4 million from $338.2 million at March 31, 2025
positive_highlights: Q2 operating expenses excluding noncash goodwill impairment and loss contingency accrual fell to $13.4 million from $22.0 million a year earlier
Third-party debt was reduced to under $4 million from $27 million in January
GWG-related settlement received preliminary court approval with no out-of-pocket payments by the company
summary: Beneficient reported Q2 FY2026 GAAP revenues of negative $2.8 million versus positive $8.6 million in the prior-year period, with GAAP net loss attributable to common shareholders of $3.6 million. Ben Liquidity interest income fell 3.8% sequentially to $8.5 million on higher nonaccrual loans, and Ben Custody revenue declined to $3.1 million from $4.2 million, with six-month custody revenue down 32.5%. Q2 opex excluding noncash items fell to $13.4 million from $22.0 million, and the company reduced third-party debt to under $4 million from $27 million in January, while total debt remained $104.0 million including Heppner-related HCLP notes. No forward financial guidance was provided; management cited stabilization efforts, NASDAQ compliance progress, and a planned December 1 reverse-split vote.

negative_highlights: Full-year 2025 revenue guidance was lowered to $400–405 million (27–29% growth) from the original 30–35% target due to delayed M&A transactions
Inorganic contribution guidance was cut to $60–65 million, reflecting dropped and delayed acquisitions, including one abandoned during due diligence
Organic revenue growth of 25% in Q3 remained below the 30–35% full-year target and free cash flow was only $3.9 million on the timing of processing cash settlements
positive_highlights: Gross margin expanded to 49.3% from 45.7% YoY, driven by processing margin rising to 39.6% from 33% on acquirer consolidation and contract renegotiations
Adjusted EBITDA grew to $18.2 million (17.5% of revenue), an improvement of more than $7.2 million YoY, and operating profit improved by $6.4 million to $7.8 million
Total transaction value rose 35% to $1.8 billion and average transaction value increased from $2.15 to $2.40, aided by mix into EV charging, amusement, and car wash verticals
summary: Nayax reported Q3 FY2025 revenue of $104.3 million, up 26% YoY, with organic growth of 25% accelerating sequentially; recurring revenue grew 29% to $77 million (74% of total) and processing revenue rose 33% to $48 million. Gross margin expanded to 49.3% from 45.7%, adjusted EBITDA rose to $18.2 million (17.5% of revenue), operating profit was $7.8 million, and net income was $3.5 million. Full-year 2025 revenue guidance was lowered to a $400–405 million constant-currency range (27–29% growth) from the prior 30–35% target including inorganic, because of delays in M&A transactions; organic growth guidance of at least 25% was reiterated. The 2028 targets (approximately 35% annual revenue growth, 50% gross margin, 30% adjusted EBITDA margin) were left unchanged.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to $5.4 million as upfront integration costs and hiring expenses outpaced revenue recognition.
Gross margin contracted slightly to 58% from 60% due to higher cost of sales associated with SCN investments.
Revenue growth is currently constrained by the time required to license, credential, and deploy new dental providers (3-6 month ramp).
positive_highlights: Revenue surged 76% YoY to $6.8M driven by successful integration of SCN and new SAMC treatment centers.
Management confirmed excess patient demand is booking out into February 2026, indicating capacity constraints rather than lack of interest.
New affiliation model with MISleep LLC in Michigan is expected to be operational by early December.
summary: Vivos reported Q3 FY2025 revenue of $6.8 million, a 76% year-over-year increase driven by the acquisition of Sleep Center of Nevada (SCN) and new treatment centers, while legacy VIP enrollment revenue decreased by $800,000. Gross margin declined slightly to 58% due to significant upfront investments in SCN integration, staffing, and facility expansion that incurred costs before full revenue realization. Management views this as an inflection point with a clear path to cash flow breakeven as provider teams ramp up over the next 3-6 months.

negative_highlights: Net licensing revenues declined 27% year-over-year to $1.1M, missing the implicit expectation of growth or stability.
The Halston business underperformed expectations, contributing to the revenue miss and requiring merchandising adjustments.
Interest and finance expense surged to $500K in the quarter compared to $100K last year due to higher rates and debt balances.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed significantly to $653K, a 38% year-over-year improvement compared to Q3 2024.
Direct operating costs decreased by 23% in the quarter and 36% year-to-date due to business transformation and cost reduction actions.
Management confirmed that operational disruptions regarding HSN's studio move and vendor tariff issues have been resolved.
summary: Xcel Brands reported Q3 FY2025 net licensing revenues of $1.1M, down from $1.5M in the prior year quarter, driven by cautious consumer spending and lower-than-expected performance in the Halston license. The company posted an adjusted EBITDA loss of $653K, representing a 38% improvement over Q3 2024 but remaining below the full-year guidance range of $1M-$2.5M which was weighted to the second half. Management noted that results were impacted by the Halston business softness and temporary disruptions from HSN's studio move and tariff-related vendor issues, though they stated these operational issues have been resolved.

negative_highlights: Gross loss widened to $351,000 from $32,000 a year ago, with gross margin at negative 20%
New SemiCab Apex SaaS platform targets 90%–95% gross margins, but the current managed-services model remains gross-margin negative due to underutilized truck contracts
Management guided net loss to remain at similar levels over the next 12 months as investment in SemiCab growth offsets cost reductions
positive_highlights: Revenue increased roughly 1,300% year-over-year to $1.7 million, driven by the May 2, 2025 SMCB/SemiCab India acquisition
Four new Fortune 500 clients added in India and five pilot programs converted to multimillion-dollar contract expansions, tracking toward ~$10 million annual contractual run rate
Operating expenses fell to $1.2 million from $1.8 million on cost-reduction measures, and net loss narrowed to $1.8 million from $2.1 million
summary: Algorhythm's Q3 FY2025 revenue rose to $1.7 million from $100,000 a year ago, driven entirely by the SMCB/SemiCab India acquisition, but the company reported a gross loss of $351,000 (negative 20% gross margin) and a net loss of $1.8 million versus a $2.1 million loss last year. Management guides Q4 revenue to about $2 million and expects the annualized revenue run rate to reach $15–$20 million by the end of next year, helped by the new high-margin SemiCab Apex SaaS platform. The quarter was the first reflecting only continuing operations after the August 1 sale of the legacy Singing Machine business; operating expenses fell to $1.2 million from $1.8 million on cost cuts, but management expects G&A and net losses to remain at similar levels over the next 12 months.

negative_highlights: Total revenue fell 13% YoY to $52.2 million on weaker 2025 film slate
Global cinema revenue declined 14% to $48.6 million and cinema operating income fell 21% to $1.8 million
New Zealand cinema revenue fell 23% and operating income collapsed 96% to just $10,000
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA increased 26% YoY to $3.6 million, the fifth consecutive quarter of positive EBITDA
Debt reduced to $172.6 million from $202.7 million at Dec 31, 2024, cutting 9-month interest expense by $2.6 million (17%)
Q3 net loss improved 41% to $4.2 million, the best third-quarter result since Q3 2019
summary: Q3 2025 consolidated revenue fell 13% YoY to $52.2 million, driven by a weaker Hollywood slate versus the prior-year quarter, FX headwinds, and the San Diego cinema closure. Cinema revenue dropped 14% to $48.6 million with cinema operating income down 21% to $1.8 million, though adjusted EBITDA rose 26% to $3.6 million and the net loss improved 41% to $4.2 million (best Q3 since 2019); basic loss per share was $0.18 versus $0.31. Debt was reduced to $172.6 million from $202.7 million at year-end 2024, and management pointed to a strong holiday/2026 slate and roughly $850,000 in global presales for Wicked: For Good while noting no formal forward guidance was provided.

negative_highlights: Operating loss widened to $6.5M from $5.1M and adjusted EBITDA loss widened to $5.4M from $3.7M YoY
R&D rose to $3.5M from $2.5M and SG&A to $4.0M from $3.2M, with 9-month operating loss up to $17.5M from $13.3M
Several EU VALUE trial sites required regulatory adjustments and management said it cannot yet assess whether this will impact the overall study timeline
positive_highlights: Revenue rose 23% YoY to $5.4M from $4.4M, driven by development services including additional DoD contracts
Updated independent U.S. market access assessment raised estimated EscharEx peak sales to about $831M from $725M based on higher modeled pricing
NexoBrid manufacturing expansion completed, taking production capacity to 6x prior levels, with full operational capacity expected by year-end 2025
summary: Q3 2025 revenue was $5.4M, up 23% YoY from $4.4M, driven by higher development services revenue including added DoD contracts, while gross margin improved to 16.5% from 15.5%. Operating loss widened to $6.5M from $5.1M and adjusted EBITDA loss widened to $5.4M from $3.7M on higher R&D ($3.5M) and SG&A ($4.0M). The company gave no formal revenue guidance; it said EU site adjustments in the VALUE Phase III VLU trial may affect timing but an update will come only as visibility improves, and the BARDA RFP is not yet awarded with Q4 timing uncertain after the government shutdown. An updated market assessment lifted estimated EscharEx U.S. peak sales to about $831M from $725M on higher modeled pricing, and NexoBrid manufacturing capacity is now 6x larger with full operational capacity expected by year-end.

negative_highlights: Net loss recorded on European CLO equity subsector
CLO equity returns muted due to prepayments and distressed exchanges
Credit issues like First Brands caused note pressure on closed-end fund stocks
positive_highlights: Achieved full dividend coverage from net investment income in September
CLO portfolio increased by 20% sequentially to $380 million
Active trading activity rose to 92 distinct trades, up from 79 in Q2
summary: Ellington Credit Company reported GAAP net income of $0.11 per share and net investment income of $0.23 per share for Q3, achieving full dividend coverage from net investment income in September. The CLO portfolio grew sequentially by 20% to $380 million at quarter-end, with active trading activity increasing to 92 distinct trades. Management noted a shift toward mezzanine debt and secondary market acquisitions while maintaining robust credit hedging.

negative_highlights: Time charter revenues dropped by approximately 9% year-over-year to $51.9 million following the sale of three vessels.
Adjusted EBITDA decreased to $20.3 million from $23.7 million, consistent with a smaller fleet size.
positive_highlights: Net income nearly doubled to $7.2 million from $3.7 million due to lower expenses and a €10.6 million gain on Genco investment valuation.
summary: Time charter revenues declined to $51.9 million in Q3 FY2025 from $57.5 million a year ago due to the sale of two vessels and one vessel sold earlier that year. Adjusted EBITDA fell to $20.3 million compared to $23.7 million last quarter, while net income nearly doubled to $7.2 million driven by non-operating gains from an investment in Genco rather than operational performance. Management noted a 1% decrease in time charter equivalent rates and warned that projected revenues for the remainder of 2025 may not recover breakeven levels.

negative_highlights: GAAP gross margin fell to negative 56.2% from negative 41.1% in Q2 and negative 24.0% a year earlier, with $176 million of COGS recognized ahead of revenue
Net loss of $953 million (negative 132.7% margin) and adjusted EBITDA of negative $576 million; SG&A rose 27% QoQ including a $49 million impairment
US/Europe presence being pulled back: D2C showrooms closed, no new US dealerships planned until the market stabilizes, North Carolina SOP pushed to 2028
positive_highlights: Revenue rose 47% YoY and 9% QoQ to $719 million; 9M EV deliveries reached 110,362, up 149% YoY
Adjusted gross margin improved to negative 17.1% from negative 20.8% in Q2 and negative 27.3% a year ago, excluding the revenue-timing and NRV items
E-scooter deliveries hit 120,052, up 535% YoY and 73% QoQ, with 2-wheeler target of 1.5 million units in Vietnam for 2026; Green series backlog described as strong
summary: VinFast reported Q3 FY2025 revenue of $719 million, up 47% YoY and 9% QoQ, on 38,195 EV deliveries (+74% YoY, +7% QoQ) plus 120,052 e-scooters (+535% YoY). GAAP gross margin deteriorated sharply to negative 56.2% from negative 24.0% a year ago and negative 41.1% in Q2, driven by $176 million of COGS recognized ahead of revenue, higher US/Europe warranty costs, and a $49 million battery-project/DC showroom impairment; adjusted gross margin improved to negative 17.1% from negative 20.8% in Q2. Net loss was $953 million (negative 132.7% margin) and adjusted EBITDA negative $576 million, with liquidity of $3.7 billion giving roughly 18 months of runway. Full-year 2025 volume guidance to at least double deliveries was reiterated, but no 2026 guidance was given and the company said it will not open more US dealerships until the market stabilizes.

negative_highlights: Management maintains a cautious stance despite easing uncertainty, citing potential earnings decline in customer business if US interest rates trend lower due to rising unemployment.
Cross-share holdings ratio remains high at 30.7%, with a target to reduce it below 20% by March 2028.
positive_highlights: Full-year profit outlook raised to JPY 1.13 trillion from a prior plan of JPY 940 billion.
Americas CIB gross profit increased 10% year-over-year to $5.2 billion following the Greenhill acquisition.
Retail segment gross profit grew 8% with new account openings up 6%.
summary: Mizuho reported a full-year profit outlook of JPY 1.13 trillion for FY2026, representing an upward revision from the prior guidance of JPY 940 billion in Q1 and JPY 1.05 trillion (implied) after the Q1 revision. The company announced an additional share buyback of JPY 200 billion, bringing total annual buybacks to JPY 300 billion alongside a dividend increase. Gross profit grew significantly across segments, with Americas CIB up 10% YoY and retail gross profit up 8%, driven by strong corporate actions and the Greenhill acquisition.

negative_highlights: Full-year net loss of $147.3 million, driven by $162.7 million accelerated depreciation and $25 million in asset impairments
Q4 revenue fell to $802,000 from $935,000 as citrus operations wound down
No fiscal 2026 land-sales guidance provided, and development revenue hinges on a 2026 Collier County decision
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA of $22.5 million exceeded the $20 million guidance target
Land sales of $23.8 million from 96 acres surpassed the $20 million guidance
Net debt cut to $47.4 million from $89 million while cash rose to $38.1 million from $3.2 million
summary: Alico reported Q4 revenue of $802,000 versus $935,000 a year ago and a net loss of $8.5 million ($1.11/share) versus an $18.1 million loss prior year, reflecting the completed exit from citrus production. Full-year adjusted EBITDA of $22.5 million exceeded the $20 million target and land sales of $23.8 million from 96 acres topped the $20 million guidance. Cash rose to $38.1 million from $3.2 million and net debt fell to $47.4 million from $89 million. Management gave no fiscal 2026 land-sales guidance but cited a $650-750 million NPV estimate on ~49,000 acres against a ~$240 million market cap and detailed the Corkscrew Grove entitlement timeline (Collier County decision in 2026, construction as early as 2028).

negative_highlights: No explicit revenue, EPS, or margin figures versus prior guidance or consensus were stated; FY2026 outlook is limited to mid-single-digit adjusted EBITDA growth
Debt was reduced only about $3.5M in the fiscal year excluding cyber-incident-related interest and rent waivers, with total debt reduction of $121M since 2020
CFO Tim Millage is departing in March 2026 and a successor has not yet been named, with details deferred to the next call
positive_highlights: Digital revenue reached $298M, or 53% of total revenue, up from 21% of revenue in 2020 when the three-pillar strategy launched
Digital-only subscription revenue grew 16% same-store to $94M on 633,000 digital-only subscribers; Amplify agency surpassed $100M at $103M, up 5% same-store
Cash costs decreased 5% to $524M, supported by ~$40M of annualized cost reductions in Q2 plus $10M entering FY2026, and the fully funded pension plan was terminated
summary: Lee reported FY2025 total revenue of $562M, 53% of which was digital ($298M), with digital-only subscription revenue of $94M up 16% same-store on 633,000 digital-only subscribers and Amplify digital agency surpassing $100M ($103M) up 5% same-store. Adjusted EBITDA grew for a second consecutive quarter when adjusted for the prior year's extra week, and cash costs fell 5% to $524M after roughly $40M of annualized reductions plus $10M entering FY2026. For FY2026 management guided to mid-single-digit adjusted EBITDA growth, alongside a planned $50M common stock rights offering that would cut the Berkshire debt rate from 9% to 5% for five years (~$18M annual interest savings). No explicit revenue or EPS figures versus guidance or consensus were stated, and CFO Tim Millage is departing in March 2026.

negative_highlights: All-in cost to mine Bitcoin was $99,383 per coin, which exceeds the current Bitcoin price, raising margin concerns.
Operational hashrate of 46.09 EH/s remains below the deployed 50 EH/s, with uptime around 90% due to external factors.
Management acknowledged heightened Bitcoin price volatility and market uncertainty, without providing specific downside mitigation plans beyond flexibility.
positive_highlights: Revenue rose 60.6% sequentially to $224.6 million, driven by Bitcoin mining revenue up 50.9% sequentially.
Net income swung to $37.3 million from a $9.5 million loss in the prior-year quarter.
Average operating hashrate improved from 40.91 EH/s in July to 46.09 EH/s in October, with efficiency above 90%.
summary: Cango reported Q3 2025 revenue of $224.6 million, up 60.6% sequentially, with Bitcoin mining revenue of $220.9 million and 1,930.8 Bitcoins mined. Net income was $37.3 million versus a loss last year, and adjusted EBITDA was $80.1 million. Management maintained its mine-and-hold strategy and highlighted operational uptime stabilization at about 90%, despite Bitcoin price volatility. The company is proceeding with small-scale pilots in clean energy and AI compute, with commissioning expected in 1-2 years.

negative_highlights: Total net sales fell 2.7% to $139.6 million despite positive comps
E-commerce net sales declined 9% on a 51% reduction in clearance sales
Q4 pretax loss and net loss guided to $5.6 million to $3.5 million, or a loss of $0.19 to $0.12 per share
positive_highlights: Comparable net sales turned positive for the first time since 2021, up 2%, with store comps up 5.3%
Gross margin expanded 460 bps to 30.5% on 390 bps of product margin improvement
Q4 guidance implies 4% to 8% comp growth after Q3's 2% gain
summary: TLYS reported Q3 FY2025 net sales of $139.6 million, down 2.7% YoY, but comparable net sales rose 2%, the first positive quarterly comp since 2021. Gross margin expanded 460 bps to 30.5%, SG&A fell $6.7 million to $44.5 million, and net loss narrowed to $1.4 million ($0.05 per share) from $12.9 million ($0.43 per share) a year earlier. Q4 guidance calls for total net sales of $106 million to $151 million, a 4% to 8% comparable sales increase, and product margin improvement of 300 to 350 bps. Quarter-to-date comps through December 2 are up 6.7%, with store comps up 9.3% over Thanksgiving through the prior day.

negative_highlights: Q4 swung to a net loss of $204,000 or $0.02 per share from net income of $141,000 or $0.01 a year earlier on higher expenses
~$0.06 per share of housing authority donation gains in FY2025 will not recur in FY2026
FY2026 guidance uses a wider-than-normal range and management said the year is already more challenging than 2025
positive_highlights: FY2025 net income rose 15% to $13.3 million or $1.29 per share from $11.8 million or $1.16
Record annual gas deliveries with volumes up 14% and heating degree days up 18% year over year
Dividend raised $0.04 per share annualized to $0.87, nearly a 5% increase
summary: RGC reported a Q4 net loss of $204,000 or $0.02 per share versus net income of $141,000 or $0.01 a year earlier, with higher expenses and seasonally weak results; both periods included ~$0.06/share of housing authority donation gains that will not recur. Full-year FY2025 net income was $13.3 million or $1.29 per share, up 15% from $11.8 million or $1.16, on record gas deliveries with heating degree days up 18% and volumes up 14%. For FY2026 management guided a wider-than-normal EPS range, citing non-recurrence of the housing authority gains, a deliberate lower volume plan, inflation, and pending rate relief from a December 2 filing seeking ~$4.3 million in annual revenue effective January 1, 2026 subject to refund. The board raised the annual dividend by $0.04 to $0.87 per share, nearly 5%.

negative_highlights: Comparable sales declined 8.3%, with the footwear pause contributing ~400 bps
Adjusted EBITDA fell to $9.8 million (4.2% margin) from $19.6 million (7.4% margin), missing internal expectations
Gross margin contracted 120 bps to 34.9% due to higher promotions and sales deleverage
positive_highlights: Denim delivered mid-single-digit growth on top of last year's double-digit performance
Sub-brands on track to deliver approximately $80 million in sales this year
SG&A reduced 11.5% year-over-year to $66.3 million, leveraging 30 bps to 28.2% of sales
summary: Torrid reported Q3 FY2025 net sales of $235.2 million, down from $263.8 million, with comparable sales falling 8.3% and adjusted EBITDA of $9.8 million (4.2% margin) versus $19.6 million (7.4% margin) last year. The company slightly lowered its full-year guidance to net sales of $995–$1.002 billion and adjusted EBITDA of $59–$62 million, citing deeper promotions and assortment missteps. Management detailed corrective actions—approximately $12.5 million in lost sales from a footwear pause, a planned return to ~$40 million footwear sales in 2026, and chase orders for tops arriving in January—while noting a 6.8% inventory reduction and 11.5% SG&A decline. No explicit EPS guidance was provided beyond the GAAP loss of $0.06 per share.

negative_highlights: Gross margin contracted 80 bps to 49.2%, driven by 260 bps of higher tariffs and 100 bps of increased freight costs.
Q4 adjusted EBITDA margin is guided to 2-4% versus 6.7% in the prior-year period, reflecting $4-5 million of incremental tariff costs.
Net income fell to $2.7 million ($0.21 per share) from $4.3 million ($0.34 per share), primarily due to a $2 million income tax expense versus zero in the prior year.
positive_highlights: Q3 net sales rose 6.2% to $85.1 million, with growth across all channels and both women's and men's assortments.
Strategic price increases of approximately 6% were accepted with units nearly flat, and women's (highest tariff impact) saw larger increases with units holding strong.
summary: Vince Holding reported Q3 FY2025 net sales of $85.1 million, up 6.2% year-over-year, with wholesale up 6.7% and DTC up 5.5%, exceeding company expectations for both top and bottom line. Gross margin fell 80 basis points to 49.2% due to 260 bps of tariff costs and 100 bps of higher freight, partially offset by pricing, lower product costs, and reduced discounting. Q4 guidance implies net sales growth of ~3-7% and adjusted EBITDA margin of 2-4% vs. 6.7% prior year, reflecting $4-5 million of incremental tariff costs. Full-year net sales growth is guided to 2-3% with adjusted EBITDA margin of 4-5% vs. 4.8% last year.

negative_highlights: Gross margin fell to 45.6% from 48.0%, and would have been ~150 bps higher without clearing slow-moving inventory; guided to 42%-43% for Q3 and FY2026
E-commerce net sales declined 15.9%, driven largely by lower sales to the largest online-only partner
Full-year net sales guided down roughly 13%-14% and non-GAAP EPS fell to $0.29 from $0.37; inventory up $12.4 million year over year due to $14 million of capitalized tariffs
positive_highlights: Total POS up 4% year over year, the second consecutive quarter of favorable POS, with November outdoor lifestyle POS up approximately 13%
New products drove over 31% of net sales, and Caldwell expanded distribution into thousands of stores at a major mass-market retailer
Debt-free balance sheet with $93 million total available capital; Board approved a new $10 million repurchase program and $662,000 of stock was bought back in Q2
summary: Q2 FY2026 net sales fell 5% to $57.2 million from $60.2 million, with traditional channel up 2.3% and e-commerce down 15.9%; gross margin compressed to 45.6% from 48.0%, non-GAAP EPS declined to $0.29 from $0.37, and adjusted EBITDA fell to $6.5 million (11.3% of sales). Management guided FY2026 net sales down roughly 13% to 14% (or about 5% excluding the $10M of orders accelerated into FY2025), Q3 sales down ~8%, gross margin of 42% to 43% for Q3 and the full year, and adjusted EBITDA of 4% to 4.5% of net sales. The quarter beat internal expectations on total POS up 4% and November outdoor lifestyle POS up 13%, but tariff amortization beginning in December and soft e-commerce ordering pressure the back-half outlook.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA declined to $24.3 million from $26.8 million, and adjusted diluted EPS fell to $0.76 from $0.89 year over year.

Q4 guidance implies a sharp slowdown, with sales down about 5% to 7% and adjusted EBITDA of only $3 million to $5 million versus $26.8 million in Q3, due to heavy promotions and about $5 million of net tariffs hitting Q4 cost of goods sold.
Management said the customer is increasingly price sensitive, the competitive market became very promotional very early, and holiday assortments did not resonate as planned.
positive_highlights: Direct channel sales rose 2% year over year while store sales fell 2.6%, with positive traffic in direct and higher average unit retails in both channels.
Company repurchased 115,612 shares for about $2 million in Q3, bringing year-to-date repurchases to roughly 371,000 shares for $6.5 million, and paid a $0.08 quarterly dividend.
Newness tests in jackets, bottoms, cashmere, sleep, and travel sets saw full-price success, and the New York localized merchandising test produced encouraging early results.
summary: Q3 total sales were about $151 million, down 0.5% year over year, with comparable sales down 0.9%; adjusted net income per diluted share fell to $0.76 from $0.89, and adjusted EBITDA declined to $24.3 million from $26.8 million. Gross margin was 70.9%, down 50 basis points, and included roughly $2.5 million of net tariff pressure, while inventory ended up 8.4% including tariffs. Management guided Q4 sales down approximately 5% to 7% with comparable sales down 6.5% to 8.5% and adjusted EBITDA of $3 million to $5 million, citing an early and deep promotional environment, increased consumer price sensitivity, and holiday assortments that did not resonate. Full-year sales are expected down about 3% and comparable sales down about 4%, with adjusted EBITDA of $80 million to $82 million.

negative_highlights: Company remains unhedged on gold prices for FY2026 despite high current levels
Major mill expansion (SAG/Ball mills) is not expected until the first half of FY2027, limiting immediate throughput growth beyond PEA estimates
positive_highlights: Record Q4 results driven by high-grade ore access following the Stage 1 stripping campaign
Recovery rates improved significantly from the high 60s in Q3 to the low 80s due to oxidation technology and process optimization
Balance sheet recapitalized with positive working capital, repayment of all borrowings, and a cash position increase of $1.2 million
summary: TRX reported record Q4 FY2025 results with production of over 6,400 ounces and sales of almost 7,000 ounces driven by a successful stripping campaign accessing high-grade ore blocks. The company achieved full-year revenue of nearly $60 million on approximately 19,000 ounces produced in 2025, benefiting from record gold prices averaging over $3,000/oz and improved recovery rates rising to the low 80s. Management provided a production guidance range for FY2026 between 25,000 and 30,000 ounces with cash costs expected at $1,400-$1,600/ounce.

negative_highlights: Consolidated net sales declined from $55.7 million to $53.2 million year-over-year
Upholstery segment sales fell approximately 12% year-over-year to $22.4 million and gross margin contracted to 16.1% from 16.9%
Tariff increases on Turkey and Haiti created cost pressure with an approximately 60-day lag before mitigation, and the company continues to report net losses
positive_highlights: Bedding segment sales rose over 2% year-over-year to $30.8 million and segment gross margin improved 200 bps to 10.1%
Adjusted operating loss narrowed to $2 million from $2.6 million a year ago, with adjusted EBITDA improving to negative $1 million
Free cash flow improved to roughly breakeven ($10,000) from negative $3.4 million in the prior-year period
summary: Culp reported Q2 FY2026 consolidated net sales of $53.2 million, up sequentially from $50.7 million (which included an extra week) but down from $55.7 million a year ago. Gross margin was 10.9% (12.6% adjusted, up from 12.1% adjusted), operating loss narrowed to $3.5 million from $5.4 million, and adjusted EBITDA was negative $1 million versus negative $1.1 million prior year. Bedding sales rose over 2% year-over-year and gross margin improved 200 bps, while upholstery sales fell approximately 12% and segment gross margin contracted to 16.1% from 16.9%. Management issued only limited guidance, expecting steady Q3 sales, continued operating loss improvement, and near breakeven to positive adjusted EBITDA, with tariff surcharges and cost actions phased in through late Q3 and Q4.

negative_highlights: Total revenue declined 11.7% year over year to $62.3 million, with indirect segment revenue down 30.2% to $12.6 million
Non-GAAP net loss widened to $8.3 million ($0.30 per diluted share) from $3.7 million ($0.13 per diluted share) in the prior-year quarter
Gross margin contracted to 41.7% from 54.5% year over year, driven by a $5.9 million inventory write-down and $4 million media credit write-off
positive_highlights: Gross margin, excluding the $5.9 million inventory write-down, expanded sequentially to 51.2%, a third consecutive quarter of improvement
Direct segment comparable sales improved sequentially for the third consecutive quarter, with positive brand channel comps over the past five months
Inventory decreased 24.3% year over year to $82.9 million and declined 9.3% from Q2 FY2026
summary: Vera Bradley reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $62.3 million, down 11.7% year over year, with a non-GAAP net loss of $8.3 million or $0.30 per diluted share, a deterioration from prior-year net loss of $3.7 million or $0.13 per share. Gross margin fell to 41.7% from 54.5% due to a $5.9 million inventory write-down and $4 million media credit write-off; excluding the write-down, gross margin was 51.2%, a third consecutive quarter of improvement. Direct segment revenue declined 5.3% with comparable sales down 5.8%, though this marked a third quarter of sequential improvement, while indirect revenue fell 30.2% on lower specialty and key account orders. Management provided no updated numerical guidance but expressed confidence in Project Sunshine initiatives and product-led momentum in brand channels.

negative_highlights: Gross margin contracted to 29.6% from 34.7% a year ago on higher revenue-share costs from greater share-by-RTR inventory levels
Adjusted EBITDA fell to $4.3 million (4.9% of revenue) from $9.3 million (12.3%) a year ago
Free cash flow worsened to -$13.6 million from -$3.4 million, with full-year free cash flow still expected below negative $40 million
positive_highlights: Revenue growth accelerated to 15.4% year over year from 2.5% in Q2 and -7.2% in Q1, with total revenue of $87.6 million
Ending active subscribers rose 12.4% to 148,916 and average active subscribers rose 12.9%, with retention improving despite the August price increase
Debt cut from approximately $319 million to approximately $120 million with maturity extended to 2029
summary: Revenue of $87.6 million rose 15.4% year over year, a sharp acceleration from +2.5% in Q2 and -7.2% in Q1, driven by 12.4% ending active subscriber growth to 148,916 and an August 1 price increase. Gross margin fell to 29.6% from 34.7% a year ago and 30.0% in Q2 on higher revenue-share costs, adjusted EBITDA dropped to $4.3 million (4.9% of revenue) from $9.3 million (12.3%), and free cash flow worsened to -$13.6 million from -$3.4 million. Q4 revenue is guided to $85-87 million (11-14% growth) with adjusted EBITDA margin of 11-13%, while full-year revenue of $323.1-325.1 million and 4.9-5.5% adjusted EBITDA margin are unchanged; FY free cash flow remains expected below negative $40 million. The company closed its recapitalization, cutting total debt from roughly $319 million to about $120 million and extending maturity to 2029.

negative_highlights: Full-year sales were flat versus prior year
Tax expense of $25 million driven by $25.9 million deferred tax asset reserve
Management says it's too early to tell if market has turned
positive_highlights: Gross margin improved to 35.1%, up 1.2 points from prior year
New fishing products drove double-digit second-half growth
Operating loss improved to $16.2 million from prior year
summary: Johnson Outdoors reported full-year fiscal 2025 sales flat year-over-year, with an improved operating loss of $16.2 million versus the prior year. Gross margin improved 1.2 points to 35.1%, and operating expenses decreased 8%. Management highlighted strong demand for new fishing products driving double-digit second-half growth, but remained cautious on market recovery and faces headwinds from tariffs and a $25.9 million deferred tax asset reserve.

negative_highlights: Revenue fell to $400,000 from $2.4 million in the prior-year period
Gross profit swung to a $1.4 million loss from $800,000 positive a year ago
Net loss widened to $10.8 million from $3.9 million, with net cash used in operations of ~$13 million versus $10.9 million
positive_highlights: Backlog rose to approximately $15 million, up $11.2 million from the prior-year period
Pipeline expanded to $137.5 million, up $53.2 million year over year
Delivered eight WAMVs in the quarter and began pre-building buoy assets for anticipated orders
summary: Q2 FY2026 revenue was $400,000 versus $2.4 million a year ago, with the shortfall attributed to the government shutdown delaying deliverables; six-month revenue fell to $1.6 million from $3.7 million. Gross profit swung to a $1.4 million loss from $800,000 positive, net loss widened to $10.8 million from $3.9 million, and opex rose to $8.8 million from $4.7 million on higher stock-based comp. Backlog reached ~$15 million (up $11.2 million YoY) and pipeline $137.5 million (up $53.2 million YoY), with management citing accelerated government engagement post-shutdown and pre-building buoys for anticipated orders, but no formal revenue or EPS guidance was issued.

negative_highlights: Revenues dropped significantly to ~$51k due to the exit of the consorting for equity model.
No revenue has been generated yet from the newly licensed broker-dealer or Reg A offerings despite a year having passed since licensing.
Management acknowledged that note weakness in-term revenues will struggle during the strategic pivot.
positive_highlights: Operating loss narrowed to $2.1 million from a prior year operating loss of approximately $2.2 million, driven by reduced losses per share falling from $2.34 to $0.44.
summary: Netcapital reported Q2 FY2026 revenues of approximately $51,000 and an operating loss of $2.1 million, representing a significant decline from the prior year period due to decreased portal fees following a strategic pivot away from its consorting for equity model. Management provided no specific financial guidance but emphasized that revenue will struggle in the short term during this transition while focusing on building volume through their newly licensed broker-dealer and tokenized asset strategies.

negative_highlights: Q4 net loss widened significantly to $38 million due to higher noncash mark-to-market adjustments on derivative liabilities.
Free cash flow was negative $0.7 million, missing the previously estimated positive guidance for Q4 primarily due to higher working capital investments.
positive_highlights: Record quarterly gross and net revenue delivered alongside highest adjusted gross margin (38%) since end of 2019.
#1 market share position achieved in Canada with strong performance across Ontario, Quebec, BC, and Alberta.
International sales grew 31% sequentially to $9.7 million in Q4, supported by new partnerships in Germany and US hemp-derived THC beverages.
summary: Organigram reported record Q4 FY2025 net revenue of $80.1 million (up 79% YoY) and adjusted gross margin expanding to 38%. The company achieved its highest adjusted EBITDA since late 2019 at $9.8 million, driven by the Motif acquisition integration and international sales growth which reached a record $9.7 million in Q4 alone.

negative_highlights: Net sales fell 9.6% year over year to $114.9 million, with direct channel sales down 16% on lower web traffic
Full-year sales guidance was lowered to $555–565 million from an initial $570–595 million
Total customer counts declined versus last year as promotional depth was pulled back
positive_highlights: Gross margin expanded 150 basis points year over year to 53.8% despite tariffs and higher clearance carry-in, driven by shallower promotions and price increases
Inventory was reduced 17% year over year to $192.2 million, with clearance down to 8% of mix from 22% at the end of July
Adjusted EBITDA improved $5.5 million year over year to negative $0.7 million, and cost savings are now expected to exceed $12 million versus the prior $10 million target
summary: Duluth Trading reported Q3 FY2025 net sales of $114.9 million, down 9.6% year over year, with gross margin expanding 150 basis points to 53.8% and adjusted EPS loss of $0.23, a $0.21 improvement versus last year. Adjusted EBITDA was negative $0.7 million, a $5.5 million year-over-year improvement, and inventory fell 17% to $192.2 million. The company lowered its full-year sales outlook to $555–565 million from an initial $570–595 million but raised the low end of its adjusted EBITDA guidance to $23–25 million from $20–25 million, while targeting over $12 million in cost savings and a $12 million tariff impact. Management stressed a promotional reset, price increases, and improved operations, and reported that it exited the credit facility with roughly $125 million in liquidity post-peak.

negative_highlights: No fiscal 2026 financial guidance was provided, as management awaits a final forecast from Zimmer Biomet
NASDAQ granted a 180-day extension to May 4, 2026, to regain compliance with the minimum bid price rule
Q4 total operating expenses fell only 2% YoY to $2.9 million, with R&D flat at $1.1 million
positive_highlights: Q4 product revenue rose 907% YoY to $2.7 million, and full-year product revenue grew 163% to $9.1 million
Product gross margin expanded to 55.8% in Q4 and 56.5% for the full year, up from 31.3% in FY2024
Full-year net loss narrowed 71% to $3.6 million, with cash of $6.6 million versus $1.5 million a year earlier and no debt outstanding
summary: NeuroOne reported record Q4 FY2025 product revenue of $2.7 million, up 907% year-over-year, with product gross margin of 55.8% versus 51.8% a year earlier. Full-year product revenue rose 163% to $9.1 million, product gross margin improved to 56.5% from 31.3%, and net loss narrowed 71% to $3.6 million; total operating expenses decreased 2% in Q4 and 5% for the year, and cash rose to $6.6 million from $1.5 million. No fiscal 2026 guidance was issued, with management saying it will provide guidance once it receives a final forecast from distribution partner Zimmer Biomet. The company disclosed a NASDAQ minimum bid price extension to May 4, 2026, and said future growth assumptions exclude trigeminal neuralgia ablation revenue, pain management strategic agreements, and drug delivery partnerships.

negative_highlights: Q4 FY2025 net loss per diluted share widened to 49 cents from 11 cents a year earlier, with adjusted EBITDA swinging to a $7.0 million loss from $1.2 million income
FY2025 adjusted EBITDA was a loss of $6.5 million, compared with positive $26.7 million in FY2024, and total net revenue fell to $159.7 million from $191.5 million
positive_highlights: Fresh packed lemon sales rose to $19.2 million with 821,000 cartons at $23.33 average price, versus 470,000 cartons at $17.95 in Q4 FY2024
Expected ~$10 million in FY2026 cost savings from the Sunkist transition and operational restructuring, including reducing the sales and marketing cost from $1.50 to $0.60 per carton
Completed $15 million sale of Chilean assets in November and identified ~$40 million more in planned divestitures (Windfall Farms and Argentina assets) targeted by end of FY2026
summary: Limoneira reported Q4 FY2025 net revenue of $42.8 million, down from $43.9 million a year earlier, with an operating loss of $11.1 million and a net loss per diluted share of 49 cents, including $6.7 million in strategic transformation costs. FY2025 net revenue fell to $159.7 million from $191.5 million, and adjusted EBITDA swung to a $6.5 million loss from $26.7 million income, as avocado revenue collapsed to $0.3 million from $8.9 million due to the crop's alternate-bearing year. The company did not provide EPS or revenue guidance for FY2026, instead guiding fresh lemon volumes of 4-4.5 million cartons and avocado volumes of 5-6 million pounds, plus roughly $10 million in expected cost savings from the Sunkist transition and operational restructuring. Management framed the results as a transition year, pointing to future drivers including 700 nonbearing avocado acres, a planned organic recycling joint venture, and $155 million in expected real estate distributions over five years.

negative_highlights: Water utility segment softer than normal due to timing of building permits/tap fees and a gap in oil and gas water deliveries
Only about 3% of water portfolio used in the quarter (~150 of ~2,800 acre-feet annual production capacity)
FY2027 framed as 'not a real breakout year,' with commercial scale and the interchange pushed to 2027-2028
positive_highlights: Revenue of about $9 million and gross profit of about $6.2 million, described as a record Q1, with net income and EPS up significantly year over year
Company has booked about one-third of FY2026 revenue guidance and roughly 37% of EPS guidance in Q1, ahead of schedule on unchanged $26-30 million revenue and $0.43-0.52 EPS guidance
Phase 2D roads about 80% complete and 5-6 months ahead of schedule, with builder count expanded from 4 to 7 national homebuilders
summary: Pure Cycle reported Q1 FY2026 revenue of just over $9 million and gross profit of about $6.2 million, a record Q1, with net income and EPS up significantly on Phase 2D land development progress. Management said it has achieved roughly one-third of its full-year revenue forecast and about 37% of EPS guidance, putting it ahead of schedule on unchanged FY2026 guidance of $26-30 million revenue and $0.43-0.52 EPS. The water utility segment was softer than normal on building-permit timing and a pause in oil and gas water deliveries, which management expects to pick up as fracking restarts this month. Phase 2D roads are about 80% complete and 5-6 months ahead of schedule, and the builder portfolio has expanded to seven national homebuilders.

negative_highlights: Total revenue declined year-over-year by approximately $400,000 (from $7.9M to $7.5M) due to intentional exit of low-margin wholesale and special streams.
note weakness in-term operational inefficiencies related to higher material costs and freight costs partially offset gross profit gains.
Revenue growth from new stores is not expected until next year, with a lag time of roughly three years for new locations to reach maturity.
positive_highlights: Gross profit dollars increased substantially from $700,000 to $1.4 million due to pricing actions and improved product mix.
Net loss narrowed significantly to negative $200,000 (or -2 cents per share) compared to a net loss of $800,000 in the prior year quarter.
Gross manufacturing margin expanded materially to 21.4% from 10% last year and improved from a negative 0.6% in the previous quarter.
summary: Total revenue declined year-over-year to $7.5 million as the company executed a margin-first strategy by exiting low-margin streams and implementing price adjustments. Despite the top-line miss driven by these deliberate actions, gross profit improved significantly from $0.7M to $1.4M with margins expanding to 21.4%, while net loss narrowed to negative $200k or -2 cents per share compared to a prior year loss of $800k. Management highlighted progress in franchise development with 34 new area agreements and two stores under construction, noting that significant revenue growth from these initiatives is expected next year rather than immediately.

negative_highlights: Total liquidity available was $7.7 million, which management explicitly stated will continue to decrease in the coming quarters.
The company is focused on raising remaining financing required for equity contribution and operating expenses until facility start-up.
positive_highlights: Secured an anchor supply contract with Nike for a fixed amount of twist at a fixed price on an annual basis.
summary: Loop Industries reported Q3 FY2026 with cash operating expenses of $2.2 million (a year-over-year decrease of $1.1 million) and total liquidity available at quarter-end of $7.7 million. Management highlighted progress on the India facility, which is on budget and schedule for completion in late 2027, secured a fixed-price supply contract with Nike as an anchor customer, and finalized site selection discussions for a European plant with Reed Societe Generale Group expected to begin generating engineering revenue by early 2026. The company stated that cash operating expenses will continue to decrease as more costs are transferred to the joint ventures in India and Europe.

negative_highlights: Net Interest Margin compressed slightly as loans reached their floors and depositors insisted on higher rates despite rate cuts.
Oil and gas revenue is expected to gradually decline over the next three or four years from a GAAP perspective, potentially negatively impacting net income.
positive_highlights: Outstanding loan growth achieved without sacrificing underwriting discipline, resulting in asset quality better than ever before.
summary: Management expressed delight with Q4 FY2025 results driven by strong loan growth and fee income without sacrificing underwriting standards. However, Net Interest Margin (NIM) experienced slight compression as loans reached rate floors while deposit costs remained elevated due to customer awareness of interest rates. Management indicated that oil and gas revenue will continue a gradual decline over the next 3-4 years from a GAAP perspective.

negative_highlights: Negotiations for new government framework agreements are described as 'slow' compared to US/Canada standards, though progress is being made.
Expansion of the processing plant (SAG mill) faces lead times estimated at 7-9 months before full benefits materialize in FY2027.
positive_highlights: Record quarterly production of just under 6,600 ounces driven by higher grade ore blocks (approx 2.1-2.5 g/t) and improved mill recovery (~75%).
Positive working capital balance reached $15 million with a ratio of 1.7x following the completion of the strip campaign.
Plant utilization increased to 90% due to preventative maintenance, spares management, and process improvements.
summary: TRX reported record Q1 FY2026 results with production of just under 6,600 ounces and revenue exceeding $25 million against a full-year guidance range of 25,000 to 30,000 ounces. The company achieved an all-in cash cost around $1,500/oz at realized gold prices near record highs above $4,600/oz, resulting in adjusted EBITDA over $13 million and a positive working capital ratio of 1.7x. Management confirmed they remain on track for full-year guidance while executing plant upgrades that are expected to further increase throughput and recovery rates.

negative_highlights: Net interest margin dropped 3 basis points linked quarter on loan growth and seasonal municipal deposit outflows
Unadjusted pre-provision net revenue fell 2% linked quarter, with expenses up 5% linked quarter on lower loan expense deferrals, stock vesting, and elevated incentive accruals
Quarter included about $520,000 in merger charges, and no explicit 2026 financial guidance was provided
positive_highlights: Net interest spread expanded 62 basis points, lifting net interest income 62% versus 2024
Net income and EPS more than doubled on an adjusted basis, with improved returns on average assets and tangible equity
Presence Bank acquisition closed January 5, growing the asset base by 20% and adding four branches in Southeast and South Central Pennsylvania
summary: Q4 2025 net interest income rose $5 million linked quarter and 62% for the year as net interest spread expanded 62 basis points, but the net interest margin fell 3 basis points linked quarter and unadjusted pre-provision net revenue declined 2% linked quarter on higher expenses. Quarterly expenses were up 1.5% year over year and 5% linked quarter, and the quarter included about $520,000 in merger charges. No numeric 2026 guidance was given; management highlighted the Presence Bank acquisition that closed January 5, adding roughly 20% to assets and four branches. No analyst questions were asked on the call.

negative_highlights: GAAP diluted EPS of $0.07 was hit by a $5.6 million after-tax securities sale loss ($0.31/share) and a $0.06/share prior-period state tax charge
Deposits declined in the final weeks of the year, including a client move of over $100 million and a $50 million correspondent banking swing
Nonperforming loans rose 8 bps to 0.14% and classified loans increased to $6.4 million, both tied to two residential real estate loans
positive_highlights: NIM expanded 13 bps QoQ and 11 bps YoY to 3.27%, supported by a 27 bp decline in interest-bearing deposit rates to 3.02%
Board approved a 25% increase in the quarterly dividend to $0.125 per share
Loan production reached $196 million in Q4, the strongest quarter of the year, with December a record monthly closing high
summary: Q4 2025 GAAP diluted EPS was $0.07, depressed by a $5.6 million after-tax securities restructuring loss ($0.31/share) and a $0.06/share prior-period state tax charge; operational EPS was $0.44, flat sequentially. NIM expanded 13 bps QoQ to 3.27%, loans grew 11% YoY and 6% annualized QoQ, deposits were stable (down $3.9 million QoQ, up $314.6 million YoY), and the Board raised the quarterly dividend 25% to $0.125. Management guided NIM flat to slightly up in Q1 2026 with high-single-digit to low-double-digit loan growth, a 26.4% tax rate, expenses baselined near $13.2 million, and noninterest income of $3.5-$3.8 million. The quarter featured a deliberate balance-sheet repositioning, a large year-end deposit outflow, and no formal EPS or revenue guidance versus consensus.

negative_highlights: Credit card transactions fell to $99 million in Q4 from $330 million in Q3
Application process failure and ACH fraud issues forced shutdown and reduced transactions
DraftKings and FanDuel have stopped credit card loads in some states
positive_highlights: No fraud has penetrated the app process in the last 60 days
BoltBetz licensing approvals and bank holding funds recognized by Gaming
Expect credit card volume to recover quickly once marketing resumes
summary: GBank reported Q4 2025 with credit card transaction volume declining to approximately $99 million from about $330 million in Q3, due to a deliberate pause in marketing and tighter fraud controls after an application process failure and ACH fraud concerns. Management emphasized investments in KYC, fraud prevention, and moving ACH in-house to rebuild a scalable foundation. They expect credit card volumes to recover quickly once marketing resumes, and anticipate a similar net interest margin for the coming year assuming a couple of rate cuts. SBA originations are expected to grow, with about 64% of originations sold, and noninterest expenses will rise with transaction volumes.

negative_highlights: Fourth-quarter net income was suppressed by a $4 million pretax loss from note $64 million of securities available for sale.
Loan outstandings decreased slightly in the quarter due to asset sales and refinancing activity, with over $50 million in payoffs related to medical office buildings.
Outlook on deposit growth is described as uncertain due to anticipated outflows from public funds into 2026.
positive_highlights: Net income for full-year 2025 increased 35% year-over-year to $32.6 million compared to $24.1 million in 2024.
Core deposit balances excluding brokered funds grew by approximately $212 million during the fourth quarter, driven by increases across retail and commercial sectors.
Net interest margin improved sequentially by 11 basis points as the cost of deposits declined 64 basis points compared to last year.
summary: West Bancorporation reported Q4 FY2025 net income of $7.4 million compared to $9.3 million in the prior quarter and $7.1 million a year ago, resulting in an earnings miss driven by a realized pretax loss of $4 million from watching $64 million of securities available for sale; without this transaction, fourth-quarter net income would have exceeded $10 million. Net interest margin expanded 11 basis points sequentially to approximately 2.5% at year-end due to deposit cost declines and loan repricing opportunities in the fixed-rate portfolio. Management noted uncertainty regarding future deposit growth as public fund inflows from bond offerings are expected to reverse into 2026.

negative_highlights: Guiding to higher provision for 2026 due to SBA and franchise credit problems
SBA gain on sale expected to drop to $19-20 million from $29.4 million in 2025
Credit issues in SBA portfolio may persist with more pain expected from late 2024/early 2025 originations
positive_highlights: Adjusted revenue up 21% year-over-year and adjusted pre-provision net revenue up 66%
Net interest margin expanded to 2.30% FTE, up 55 basis points year-over-year
BaaS deposits grew to $1.3 billion for 2025, more than tripling prior year
summary: First Internet Bancorp reported Q4 2025 net income of $5.3 million or $0.60 per share (adjusted $0.64), with adjusted revenue up 21% year-over-year. Net interest margin expanded to 2.30% FTE, and full-year NII grew 30%. However, credit issues in SBA and franchise finance portfolios persist, with management guiding to a higher provision for 2026 and expecting credit to stabilize in the second half. Guidance for 2026 includes SBA production of ~$500 million and gain on sale revenue of $19-20 million (down from $29.4 million in 2025), while NIM is projected to rise to 2.75-2.80% by year-end. Loan growth expected 5-17% and deposit growth 8-10% for 2026.

negative_highlights: Gross loans decreased $6.3 million QoQ to $1.1 billion as commercial and residential real estate declines offset CRE and agriculture growth
Noninterest expense rose $1.0 million QoQ to $12.3 million, including a $356,000 impairment on repossessed assets and $511,000 higher compensation
Net charge-offs of $341,000 rose versus $219,000 in Q4 2024
positive_highlights: Net interest margin expanded 20 bps QoQ to 4.03% and 52 bps YoY, with total cost of deposits at 1.50%
Full-year EPS of $3.07 rose 43% over 2024, and the efficiency ratio improved to 62.7% from 69.1%
Tangible book value per share rose $4.09, or 24%, to $20.79 versus year-end 2024, and nonperforming loans fell 24% ($3.1 million) from year-end 2024
summary: Landmark Bancorp reported Q4 2025 net income of $4.7 million, or $0.77 diluted EPS, up from $3.3 million in Q4 2024, driven by net interest income of $14.8 million (up $695,000 QoQ and $2.4 million YoY). NIM expanded 20 bps QoQ to 4.03% and 52 bps YoY, with total cost of deposits at 1.50%. Full-year EPS of $3.07 rose 43% on 17% revenue growth, the efficiency ratio improved to 62.7% from 69.1%, and tangible book value per share reached $20.79, up 24% year-over-year. No explicit forward guidance was provided; the board declared a $0.21 per share dividend, the 98th consecutive quarterly payout. Gross loans slipped $6.3 million QoQ to $1.1 billion, and noninterest expense rose $1.0 million to $12.3 million, including a $356,000 impairment on repossessed assets.

negative_highlights: Net charge-offs rose to $6.7 million from $3.1 million and provision for loan losses to $17.7 million from $12.8 million, cutting Q4 net income by $1.1 million after tax (~$0.08/share)
Efficiency ratio deteriorated to 50.5% from 47.6% as noninterest expense rose to $23.7 million from $17.4 million
NPL balance reached $43.7 million with guidance of up to $10 million more watch-list migration in Q1 2026; SBA 7(a) originations fell sequentially on SBA staffing cuts and the shutdown
positive_highlights: Q4 originations of $1.6 billion exceeded the $1.4 billion initial guide, bringing FY2025 originations to $6.1 billion, up 22% YoY
Credit-enhanced balances reached $118 million, above both the $115 million prior outlook and the $50-100 million initial guidance
Net interest income rose to $24.6 million from $18.6 million sequentially and noninterest income to $22.3 million from $18 million, lifting NIM to 11.42% from 9.01%
summary: FinWise reported Q4 net income of $3.9 million and diluted EPS of $0.27, with net interest income of $24.6 million (up from $18.6 million) and total noninterest income of $22.3 million (up from $18 million), driven largely by the credit-enhanced portfolio growing $76.5 million. Full-year 2025 net income rose 26% and originations of $6.1 billion grew 22% YoY, with Q4 originations of $1.6 billion exceeding the $1.4 billion guide. However, net charge-offs jumped to $6.7 million from $3.1 million and provision rose to $17.7 million from $12.8 million, partly from tightened servicing standards that management frames as a roughly $1.1 million after-tax ($0.08/share) one-time item; the efficiency ratio worsened to 50.5% from 47.6%. Guidance points to a ~$1.4 billion quarterly origination baseline plus 5% growth for 2026, $8-10 million/month credit-enhanced balance growth, ~$3.5 million quarterly core net charge-offs, and up to $10 million in NPL migration in Q1 2026.

negative_highlights: New boat sales declined 6% compared to the prior year period due to lower unit volumes.
Management lowered industry expectations from a recovery narrative to flat-to-low-single-digit growth for FY26.
Same-store sales are expected to be impacted by brand rationalization headwinds, resulting in flat overall same-store sales.
positive_highlights: Gross profit margin expanded to 23.5%, an improvement of 110 basis points compared to the prior year quarter.
Pre-owned boat sales were up 24% YoY driven by increased unit volume and average unit price as inventory availability normalized.
Service, parts, and other revenue grew by 10% YoY demonstrating strength in distribution operations.
summary: Fiscal Q1 FY26 revenue was $381 million (up 1% YoY) with gross margins expanding to 23.5%, driven by pre-owned sales growth and portfolio optimization despite a new boat volume decline of 6%. Management maintained full-year guidance ranges for total sales ($1.83B-$1.93B), adjusted EBITDA, and EPS while issuing a softer industry outlook expecting flat-to-low-single-digit year-over-year performance.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined 9.5%, with Consumer Floral and Gift down 22.7% and order volume down about 16%
Gross margin contracted 120 bps to 42.1% on deleveraging and higher tariff, commodity, and shipping costs
Adjusted EBITDA fell to $98.1 million from $116.3 million, and FY2026 revenue is guided to decline low double digits
positive_highlights: Achieved approximately $15 million in annualized run-rate cost savings in FY2026 toward the ~$50 million target across FY2026-FY2027
Operating expenses declined $23.4 million to $221.1 million, and $25.9 million excluding non-comparable items, on lower marketing and labor costs
AOV rose 5.2% and B2B/wholesale growth partially offset the e-commerce decline; revolver borrowings were fully repaid and net cash position was $42.3 million
summary: Consolidated revenue fell 9.5% in Q2 FY2026, with Consumer Floral and Gift down 22.7% and BloomNet down 3.8%; revenue came in below the prior view on reduced marketing spend and lower direct traffic from search engine results page changes. Gross margin contracted 120 bps to 42.1% on deleveraging plus higher tariff, commodity, and shipping costs, and adjusted EBITDA fell to $98.1 million from $116.3 million. Management guided FY2026 revenue to decline low double digits and adjusted EBITDA to decline slightly, with a normalized slight increase excluding ~$12 million of incentive compensation and consultant costs. Roughly $15 million of the targeted ~$50 million run-rate cost savings has been achieved, and the company is moving to a function-based operating structure with workforce reductions.

negative_highlights: Net loss of $2.5 million for Q4 2025, following an $18.9 million loss in Q3
Annualized net charge-off ratio rose to 1.95% from 1.24% in Q3, with additional SBA 7(a) charge-offs expected in 2026
Loans held for investment declined 9.6% over the past year to $963.9 million, and tangible book value per share fell to $17.22 from $17.90 sequentially
positive_highlights: Deposits grew $12.5 million (1.1%) sequentially to $1.18 billion, with 85% of deposits insured
Net interest margin was stable at 3.58%, and net interest income rose $500,000 year-over-year
Non-interest expense fell to $11.9 million in Q4 from $25.2 million in Q3 (which included a $7.3 million restructuring charge)
summary: BayFirst reported a Q4 2025 net loss of $2.5 million, an improvement from the $18.9 million loss in Q3 but a full-year loss nonetheless. Provision expense of $2.0 million drove elevated net charge-offs of $4.6 million, with $1.0 million from unguaranteed SBA 7(a) loans, and the annualized charge-off ratio rose to 1.95% from 1.24% in Q3. Deposits grew $12.5 million sequentially to $1.18 billion and NIM held at 3.58%, but loans held for investment fell 9.6% year-over-year to $963.9 million as the SBA exit and balance sheet deleveraging played out. Management guided that additional SBA charge-offs are likely in 2026, though they expect a lessening impact; tangible book value slipped to $17.22 from $17.90.

negative_highlights: Full-year revenue guidance was lowered from $240 million to over $210 million due to game release delays.
Net loss widened substantially to a $5.6 million deficit compared to an $0.8 million profit in the prior year period.
EBITDA swung to a loss of $2.7 million from a gain, reflecting significant acquisition and integration expenses.
positive_highlights: Group revenues nearly doubled year-on-year to $98.7 million driven by the consolidation of Ban Leong Technologies.
Gross profit rose significantly by 54.5% to $10.8 million despite margin compression from hardware integration.
Secured an additional $13 million in strategic investments (total) from ADATA Technology, validating the publishing subsidiary's position.
summary: GCL reported first half FY2026 revenues of $98.7 million (nearly doubling YoY) and gross profit rising to $10.8 million due to the Ban Leong acquisition, though net loss widened to $5.6 million from a prior year profit driven by integration costs. Management revised full-year guidance downward for both revenue ($240m -> >$210m) and gross profit ($30m -> >$21m), citing delays in two game titles required for quality refinements.

negative_highlights: Q4 core expenses rose to $28M from $22M in Q3 due to compensation accruals
Digital deposits declined less than 10% despite rate cuts
Specific provisions of $1M for impaired loans at year-end
positive_highlights: Net interest margin expanded to 3.28% from 2.90% year-over-year
