Checking accounts grew 23%, noninterest-bearing deposits up to 16.3%
December core bank closed $75M commercial loans with $90M related deposits
summary: Primis Financial reported Q4 2025 earnings of $29.5 million or $1.20 per share, including a gain from a sale-leaseback transaction, with a nearly 3% ROA. Core run-rate earnings were about $8 million for 2025, an 80 basis point ROA, with margin expanding to 3.28% from 2.90% a year ago. The company grew checking accounts 23%, grew noninterest-bearing deposits to 16.3% of total deposits, and expects further margin expansion in 2026, targeting a 1% ROA. Management guided to core quarterly expenses of $23-24 million for 2026 and expressed confidence in achieving sustainable 1% ROA.

negative_highlights: Total revenues fell 90% year over year to CNY 91.3 million
Net loss attributable to Origin was CNY 53.3 million
Decline driven by non-proprietary seed sales drop and increased competition for legacy products
positive_highlights: Cash and cash equivalents increased 89% to CNY 15.9 million
Headcount recovered from 68 to 97 professionals
New sales force established in Northeast and East China provinces
summary: Origin Agritech reported fiscal year 2025 revenue of CNY 91.3 million ($12.9 million), a 90% decline from the prior year, with a net loss of CNY 53.3 million ($7.5 million) versus a year that included a one-time gain from a subsidiary disposal. The company raised $5.38 million via share sales, boosting cash by 89% to CNY 15.9 million, and invested in facility upgrades and headcount recovery (from 68 to 97 employees). Management framed 2025 as a 'transformative' recovery year and reaffirmed a three-stage strategic plan, with stage one (recovery) expected through 2026, but provided no specific forward revenue or earnings guidance.

negative_highlights: Total revenue grew only 3% year-over-year (5% ex-sunset messaging), with SaaS growth of 5% (8% ex-messaging) still modest
PS revenue was sequentially lower and produced a negative PS gross margin, attributed to late-quarter bookings and the government shutdown
Q3 revenue guidance of $22.2-22.7 million implies a sequential decline from $23 million, partly due to an approximate $400,000 fewer-days impact
positive_highlights: Total revenue of $23 million exceeded guidance and consensus; non-GAAP EPS of $0.11 more than doubled from $0.05 a year ago
Total gross margin expanded 300 bps year-over-year to 74%, and adjusted EBITDA margin rose to 14% from 7%
Operating cash flow of $10.1 million (44% margin) versus $6.4 million a year ago; cash balance grew to $83.1 million with no debt
summary: eGain reported Q2 FY2026 total revenue of $23 million, up 3% year-over-year and ahead of both guidance and street consensus, with SaaS revenue up 5% and representing 95% of the total. Non-GAAP EPS came in at $0.11 versus $0.05 a year ago, total gross margin expanded 300 basis points to 74%, and operating cash flow was $10.1 million (44% margin) compared with $6.4 million a year ago. Full-year FY2026 revenue guidance was reaffirmed at $90.5-92.0 million (a return to growth), while Q3 revenue guidance of $22.2-22.7 million implies a sequential decline due largely to fewer days and the PS segment softness. AI Knowledge ARR grew 27% year-over-year and now represents 64% of total SaaS ARR, while overall SaaS ARR rose 7% (11% ex-sunset messaging products).

negative_highlights: Q2 revenues of $111.5 million down from $118.2 million year ago
Gross margin declined to 32.9% non-GAAP from 35.3% in prior year quarter
Full-year guidance unchanged; BEAD and new product contributions not yet material
positive_highlights: Highest second quarter bookings in the last ten years
Six-month revenues up 5.9% vs prior year; adjusted EBITDA up $13.2 million year-to-date
Initial purchase orders for PISA LTE 5G router and MDU solution with a US tier one provider
summary: Aviat Networks reported Q2 FY2026 total revenues of $111.5 million, down from $118.2 million a year ago, but six-month revenues were $218.8 million, up 5.9% year over year. Adjusted EBITDA was $11.3 million (10.1% of revenues), non-GAAP EPS was $0.54, and operating cash flow was $23.9 million. Gross margins contracted year over year due to mix, but improved sequentially for the first half. Management kept full-year FY2026 guidance unchanged, noted highest Q2 bookings in ten years, and highlighted initial orders for its PISA cellular router and MDU solution, while keeping BEAD out of guidance.

negative_highlights: Net sales declined 12.5% year-over-year driven by lower demand in Asia and pricing pressure in Brazil
Asia segment net sales fell 27% due to volume declines and tariff uncertainty
Revenue remains below the new breakeven point of approximately $575 million
positive_highlights: Consolidated gross margin expanded from 0.4% to 3%
SG&A expenses improved by 25% YoY following restructuring
Year-to-date free cash flow reached $13.3 million
summary: Unifi reported Q2 FY26 net sales of $314 million (down 12.5% YoY) and consolidated gross margins expanding to 3%, driven by cost-saving initiatives that improved SG&A by 25%. While adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed significantly, revenue remains below the new breakeven threshold due to demand softness in Asia (-27%) and pricing pressure in Brazil.

negative_highlights: Consumer cannabis revenue fell 48% year-over-year to $5.2 million
Plant propagation gross margin dropped to 16% from 40% due to costs and write-offs
Adjusted EBITDA declined to $18.5 million from $19.4 million year-over-year
positive_highlights: Global medical cannabis revenue grew 12% to a record, with international up 17%
Adjusted gross margin expanded 100bps to 62%, with medical at 69%
Generated positive free cash flow of $15.5 million and ended with $154 million cash
summary: Aurora Cannabis reported fiscal Q3 2026 net revenue of $94.2 million, up 7% year-over-year, with global medical cannabis revenue up 12% to a record, including 17% international growth. Adjusted gross margin expanded 100bps to 62%, adjusted EBITDA was $18.5 million, adjusted net income $7.2 million, and free cash flow $15.5 million, ending with $154 million cash and no cannabis debt. Management announced exits from select Canadian consumer cannabis markets and divestiture of Bevo plant propagation, expecting improved margins and EBITDA thereafter, while also filing a $100 million ATM for strategic purposes. Guidance for fiscal 2026 global medical cannabis revenue was reiterated at $269-$281 million, implying 10-15% growth.

negative_highlights: Net revenue missed expectations and declined 12% year-over-year to $102.2 million.
Product gross margin contracted significantly to 19.7% from 43.5% in the prior year, primarily due to China mix and tariffs.
Management cut full-year revenue guidance by approximately $31 million and adjusted EBITDA guidance by roughly $8-9 million.
positive_highlights: Service revenue grew 4% year-over-year to $57.2 million, demonstrating resilience against macro headwinds.
Product gross orders were approximately $66 million with a book-to-bill ratio of 1.5.
Operating expenses declined almost 21% quarter-over-quarter excluding one-time restructuring costs.
summary: Net revenue for Q2 FY2026 was $102.2 million, down 12% year-over-year, driven by a 26% decline in product revenue due to tariffs and geopolitical tensions in China, while service revenue grew 4%. Management reset full-year fiscal 2026 guidance to $440-$450 million in revenue (down from $471-$485 million) and $22-$25 million adjusted EBITDA (down from $31-$35 million), citing continued volatility in China and tariff impacts. The company recognized $6.1 million in one-time restructuring charges related to a 15% workforce reduction.

negative_highlights: Adjusted NII declined to $0.21 per share from $0.24 per share in the prior quarter, and GAAP net investment loss was $6.5 million versus net investment income of $4.3 million in the prior quarter
Net expenses rose to $31.6 million from $21 million, primarily due to a $9.9 million increase in capital gains-based incentive fee accrual
Total investment income fell slightly to $25.1 million from $25.3 million, with dividend and success fee income down $400,000 quarter over quarter
positive_highlights: NAV increased to $14.95 per share from $13.53 per share, driven by $1.77 per share of net unrealized appreciation and $0.09 per share of net realized gains
Portfolio company valuations increased $7.2 million in aggregate, with the three largest contributors (Shilling, Old World, SFEG) appreciating on EBITDA growth rather than multiple expansion
The company redeemed $74.8 million of 8% notes using $60 million of 6.875% notes, reducing the interest burden on that debt by approximately 110 basis points
summary: GAIN reported Q3 FY2026 total investment income of $25.1 million, down slightly from $25.3 million in the prior quarter, and adjusted NII of $0.21 per share versus $0.24 per share in the prior quarter. A $9.9 million increase in the accrual of capital gains-based incentive fees drove net expenses to $31.6 million and produced a GAAP net investment loss of $6.5 million, though NAV rose to $14.95 per share from $13.53 on $1.77 per share of unrealized appreciation. The company maintained its $0.08 monthly distribution, redeemed $74.8 million of 8% notes with $60 million of 6.875% notes, and reported three non-accrual companies at 3.8% of cost and 1.5% of fair value.

negative_highlights: Net income fell to roughly $2.2 million from $5.3 million and EPS dropped to $0.03 from $0.08 on a swap fair-value loss and $6.6 million interest expense
Total net debt rose to $431.7 million from $366.7 million at March 31, 2025 to fund catalog acquisitions
Recorded Music Synchronization revenue declined on license timing, and the CEO flagged CRB rate uncertainty as a potential headwind
positive_highlights: Full-year revenue guidance raised to $170-173 million from $167-170 million, implying 8% growth at the midpoint
Adjusted EBITDA guidance raised to $71.5-73.5 million from $70-72 million, and Q3 adjusted EBITDA grew 11% to $19.2 million
Music Publishing revenue grew 12% to $30.1 million and operating margins expanded as revenue growth outpaced an 8% cost increase
summary: Revenue was $45.6 million, up 8% reported and 5% organically, with Music Publishing +12% to $30.1 million and Recorded Music +8% to $12.9 million. OIBDA rose 11% to $18.1 million and adjusted EBITDA rose 11% to $19.2 million, while net income fell to roughly $2.2 million and EPS dropped to $0.03 from $0.08 on a swap fair-value loss and higher interest expense. Full-year revenue guidance was raised to $170-173 million from $167-170 million and adjusted EBITDA to $71.5-73.5 million from $70-72 million. Net debt rose to $431.7 million from $366.7 million at March 31, 2025 to fund M&A.

negative_highlights: Revenue excluding VoIP Supply was 2% lower year-over-year on a like-for-like basis due to the divestiture.
Management explicitly stated they are tightening guidance for fiscal '26 despite strong bookings momentum.
G&A and sales/marketing spend increased by approximately $2 million to accelerate pipeline development.
positive_highlights: MRR bookings surged 67% sequentially and 60% year-over-year driven by large strategic mid-market deals.
Blended churn improved to just under 1%, reflecting stability in the recurring revenue base.
Starting backlog for Q3 increased approximately 125% compared to the start of Q2, providing strong visibility.
summary: Sangoma reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $51.5 million, representing a 1.2% sequential increase and 1% growth in service revenue. Adjusted EBITDA was $8.3 million with 16% margins, while free cash flow improved to $8 million. Management tightened fiscal '26 guidance to expect revenue between $205 million and $208 million, citing the divestiture of VoIP Supply and a focus on organic growth.

negative_highlights: A $3.6 million charge on a specialty tank project reduced gross profit and drove a Q2 net loss of $0.9 million (EPS -$0.03).
Q2 book-to-bill was 0.8 on $177 million of awards, and management said large 'chunk' projects will likely push award timing into fiscal 2027, so backlog is unlikely to exit FY2026 above 1.0.
Storage and Terminal Solutions segment gross margin fell to 4.8% from 7.6% YoY, and SG&A guidance remains near a $16.5 million quarterly run rate ahead of returning to profitability.
positive_highlights: Revenue rose 12% YoY to $210.5 million, with growth in all three segments and Utility & Power Infrastructure up 23% to $75.4 million.
Utility & Power Infrastructure gross margin expanded to 9.6% from 5.6% on strong project execution and better overhead recovery; adjusted EBITDA improved $4.6 million YoY to positive $2.4 million.
Opportunity pipeline grew to $7.3 billion (up roughly $600 million sequentially) on LNG, NGL, mining and minerals, and electrical activity, with cash of $224 million and no debt.
summary: Matrix Service reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $210.5 million, up 12% YoY, with growth in all three segments, but a $3.6 million ($0.13/share) commissioning charge on a substantially complete specialty tank project drove a net loss of $0.9 million and EPS of -$0.03, versus -$0.20 a year ago; adjusted EBITDA was a positive $2.4 million. Management reiterated full-year revenue guidance of $875–$925 million and said it will achieve profitability in the second half of the fiscal year. Awards of $177 million produced a 0.8 book-to-bill in the quarter, and the opportunity pipeline expanded to $7.3 billion, though management attributed slower awards to trade-policy, permitting, and government-shutdown uncertainty and said large awards are likely to slip into fiscal 2027. The company also announced a CEO transition, with Sean Payne becoming CEO effective June 30, 2026.

negative_highlights: Total revenue fell to $1.9M from $16.9M as the citrus exit removed most of the top line
Citrus segment still showed a $6.5M gross loss on $900,000 of revenue
Net cash used in operating activities was $5.5M in the quarter
positive_highlights: EBITDA swung to positive $2.4M from negative $6.7M a year ago, a $9.1M improvement
Net loss narrowed to $3.5M ($0.45/share) from $9.2M ($1.20/share)
Land sales totaled $34.5M fiscal year-to-date through January, including the $26.8M/~2,950-acre grove sale after quarter end
summary: Alico reported Q1 FY2026 total revenue of $1.9M versus $16.9M a year ago, reflecting the exit from citrus; the net loss narrowed to $3.5M ($0.45/share) from $9.2M ($1.20/share) and EBITDA turned positive at $2.4M versus negative $6.7M. Land sales generated $7.7M in the quarter with a ~$4.9M gain, and a further ~2,950-acre grove sold for $26.8M in January, bringing fiscal year-to-date land sales to $34.5M. Management introduced FY2026 guidance of approximately $14M adjusted EBITDA and roughly $50M ending cash, with net debt falling to about $35M. Farmable land is now ~97% leased (~32,500 acres), though management declined to quantify the expected revenue contribution.

negative_highlights: Merchant division net revenue pulled back 2% due to refocusing distribution on high-potential clients and ongoing pricing pressure.
Merchant ARPU declined 10% year-on-year driven by lower airtime volumes and margin compression in the ADP product.
positive_highlights: Consumer division achieved a record quarter with net revenue rising 38% year-on-year to ZAR 567 million.
Enterprise division delivered ZAR 217 million in net revenue, representing a 67% year-on-year improvement.
Group adjusted EBITDA grew 47% year-on-year, landing slightly above the midpoint of guidance.
summary: Lesaka reported Q2 FY2026 net revenue of ZAR 1.6 billion (up 16% YoY) and group adjusted EBITDA of ZAR 304 million (up 47% YoY), meeting guidance. The Consumer division delivered a standout quarter with revenue rising 38% YoY, while the Merchant segment pulled back 2% due to strategic refocusing and pricing pressure. Management reaffirmed full-year guidance for net revenue between ZAR 6.4 billion and ZAR 6.9 billion.

negative_highlights: LED lighting segment revenue declined to $12.1M from $13.2M
Maintenance segment gross margin declined to 25.5% from 26.4%
Year-to-date operating cash flow down to $0.4M from $1.3M prior year
positive_highlights: Revenue up 7.7% to $21.1 million, above prior expectation of about $21 million
Raised FY26 guidance to $84-86M revenue at positive adjusted EBITDA, up from $84M at or near
EV charging revenue nearly doubled to $4.7M with gross margin up 670 bps to 36.7%
summary: Orion Energy Systems reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $21.1 million, up from $19.6 million a year ago, with positive adjusted EBITDA of $761,000, its fifth consecutive quarter. The company raised its FY2026 revenue guidance to $84-86 million with positive adjusted EBITDA, and initiated FY2027 guidance of $95-97 million revenue at positive adjusted EBITDA. Segment highlights included EV charging revenue nearly doubling to $4.7 million and strong gross margin expansion, while LED lighting revenue declined. Management cited a new $14-15 million exterior lighting project and continued cost discipline as key drivers.

negative_highlights: GAAP earnings were impacted by a nonrecurring charge of $300 million related to the Marshall Wildfire settlement, leaving only three individual plaintiffs remaining.
O&M expenses increased $190 million due to accelerated wildfire mitigation costs in Colorado and excess liability insurance premiums.
positive_highlights: Ongoing earnings of $3.80 per share marked the twenty-first consecutive year of meeting or exceeding initial ongoing earnings guidance.
Data center contracted capacity doubled from three gigawatts to over two gigawatts recently signed, with a target of six gigawatts by 2027.
Received approval for an additional $1.5 billion in new ultra-high voltage transmission lines in SPP.
summary: Xcel Energy reported full-year 2025 ongoing earnings of $3.80 per share, beating the prior year's $3.50 and meeting initial guidance for the twenty-first consecutive year. Management reaffirmed its 2026 EPS guidance range of $4.04 to $4.16 despite a nonrecurring wildfire settlement charge impacting GAAP results. The company highlighted significant progress on data center contracts, now totaling over two gigawatts with an expectation to reach six gigawatts by 2027.

negative_highlights: FY2026 guidance reduced by ~$40M due to two $20M headwinds: PBM reimbursement change and a carrier's marketing budget cut.
The carrier's action cuts marketing budgets across all distribution channels, signaling potential industry-wide shift.
Healthcare services membership expected to be flat to modestly down by end of FY2026, indicating prioritization of profits over growth.
positive_highlights: Senior EBITDA margin reached 39%, near record, for the fourth consecutive AEP above 30%.
Healthcare services revenue grew 26% YoY to $231M, with members up 17% to 113,000.
New $415M credit facility extends maturities to 2031, improving liquidity and reducing interest rate by up to 100 bps.
summary: Q2 FY2026 revenue grew 12% YoY to $537M, with senior revenue up 2% to $262M and healthcare services revenue up 26% to $231M. Senior adjusted EBITDA margin was 39%, near record, but consolidated EBITDA was impacted by a $20M PBM reimbursement headwind. Management lowered FY2026 consolidated revenue guidance to $1.61-1.71B and adjusted EBITDA to $90-100M, reflecting an additional ~$20M impact from a national carrier cutting marketing budgets across distribution channels. Despite the guide down, management reaffirmed long-term targets of 20%+ senior EBITDA margin and $40-50M annualized healthcare services EBITDA exit rate, and raised FY2026 operating cash flow guidance to $25-35M.

negative_highlights: Tax expense of about $2 million from US valuation allowance
Operating expenses increased $2.1 million
Warranty expense decrease was less than a point of operating expense
positive_highlights: Revenue growth was double-digit, led by unit volumes
Gross margin improved 6.7 points to 36.6%
Pre-tax loss improved by $17.6 million year-over-year
summary: Q1 FY2026 pre-tax loss narrowed to $1.3 million from $18.9 million a year ago, with gross margin up 6.7 points to 36.6% on higher volumes, pricing, and cost savings. Revenue grew double-digit, driven by unit volumes and new products, with solid demand across Fishing, Jetboil, Old Town, and Scubapro's Hydros Pro 2. The company remains debt-free, reduced inventory by $17.7 million to $103.9 million, and continues its dividend, but tax rate will remain volatile due to US valuation allowance.

negative_highlights: Q4 fee revenues grew just 2% year over year to $670 million, a sharp deceleration from full-year 10% growth
Q4 global credit FRE increased only 4% year over year to $102 million, versus 21% full-year growth
Management declined to provide 2026 guidance on margins, management fee growth, Fund IX fundraising and realizations, deferring detail to the February 26 shareholder update
positive_highlights: Full-year fee-related earnings rose 12% to a record $1.24 billion and FRE margin expanded to a record 47% from 46%
2025 inflows totaled $54 billion, up 32% year over year and well above the original $40 billion guidance
Realized proceeds reached $34 billion, up almost 20% year over year, with over $18 billion of GPE proceeds, aiding exit momentum
summary: Carlyle reported full-year 2025 record fee-related earnings of $1.24 billion, up 12% organically, and a record 47% FRE margin, with $54 billion of inflows exceeding its original $40 billion target. Q4 distributable earnings were $436 million, or $1.01 per share, on quarterly FRE of $290 million and fee revenues of $670 million, up 2% year over year. Full-year DE reached $1.7 billion, or $4.20 per share, up 11% and the highest since 2022, with a record $225 million of transaction fees. Management deferred multi-year financial targets and much forward guidance to a February 26 shareholder update, while noting a constructive but volatile macro backdrop and 6% of AUM in software exposure.

negative_highlights: Telecommunications vertical declined 23.1% as legacy carrier volumes decreased, dropping below 10% of total revenue for the first time since pre-IPO
Gross margins were pressured by deferred training revenue recognition in high-growth programs and ongoing investment costs in India expansion
positive_highlights: Record quarterly adjusted EBITDA of $20.7 million representing 12.6% of revenue
HealthTech vertical grew rapidly by 35.1%, on track to reach $100M in annualized run-rate by year-end
Adjusted EPS increased 46% YoY driven by strong operating performance and share repurchases
summary: IBEX reported record Q2 FY26 revenue of $164.2 million (up 17% YoY) and adjusted EPS growth of 46%, driven by strong performance in HealthTech (+35%) and digital acquisition services. Management raised full-year guidance for both Revenue ($605M-$620M to $620M-$630M) and Adjusted EBITDA ($78M-$81M to $80M-$82M). While gross margins faced temporary headwinds from deferred training revenue recognition in high-growth programs, operating leverage improved SG&A as a percentage of revenue.

negative_highlights: Q4 revenue missed internal guidance due to a lack of seasonal push in November and December following the March/April peak.
Adjusted operating ratio was unfavorably impacted by elevated insurance claims expense from a major claim under new retention levels ($500k reserve).
Management expects Q1 FY2026 revenue to be lower sequentially than Q4 2025 due to extended plant shutdowns and weather interference.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 11% YoY to $105.4M despite a challenging core market environment and lack of typical year-end seasonality.
Adjusted EBITDA increased 32% YoY to $9.2M, reflecting the benefit from acquisitions (Brothers) and new business wins offsetting volume weakness.
Net debt-to-EBITDA improved significantly to 1.5x at quarter end, enhancing balance sheet flexibility.
summary: Proficient Auto Logistics reported Q4 FY2025 revenue of $105.4 million (up 11% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $9.2 million (up 32% YoY), though the quarter missed internal expectations due to weaker-than-anticipated November/December seasonality, a major insurance claim reserve of $500k, and reduced operating leverage from core market volume declines. Management lowered its Q1 FY2026 revenue outlook citing severe winter weather disruptions and forecasted lower SAAR than 2025 actuals, while maintaining guidance for modest sequential OR improvement driven by cost savings initiatives rather than general market recovery.

negative_highlights: NYSE delisting notice received, with a potential reverse stock split being considered to regain compliance
Q4 free cash flow was negative $15M, and 2026 carries $18M of severance cash costs (~80% in Q1)
Total revenue guided to $60-62M in Q1 2026 versus $73M in Q4, reflecting ongoing attrition in the academic business
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA of $13M exceeded the high end of guidance by $2M at an 18% margin
Chegg Skilling revenue of $18M grew double digits and is guided to double-digit growth for 2026
Non-GAAP operating expenses fell 47% YoY to $44.8M with CapEx down 51% to $6M
summary: Chegg reported Q4 FY2025 total revenue of $73M, split between $18M in Chegg Skilling (up double digits, said to be tracking for double-digit 2026 growth) and $55M in the declining academic-services business. Adjusted EBITDA was $13M (18% margin), beating the high end of guidance by $2M, with non-GAAP opex down 47% YoY to $44.8M, but free cash flow was negative $15M driven by $12M of severance. Q1 2026 total revenue guidance is $60-62M with adjusted EBITDA of $11-12M, and management targets 2026 non-GAAP expenses under $250M and zero debt by year-end; the company also disclosed an NYSE delisting notice and the possibility of a reverse stock split.

negative_highlights: Organic net sales declined 7% YoY with the decline driven by a 9-point volume/mix contraction
Adjusted gross margin fell ~340 bps YoY to 19.5% and adjusted EBITDA fell to $24 million from $38 million
Adjusted EPS swung to a $0.03 loss from $0.08 income a year ago, and no numeric FY2026 guidance was provided
positive_highlights: Free cash flow rose 22% YoY to $30 million, with net debt reduced by $32 million to $637 million
SG&A fell 13% YoY to $61 million, or 15.9% of net sales versus 17.0% a year ago
North America tea, yogurt, and Earth's Best finger foods/cereal grew, with Greek Gods dollar and unit sales up high teens
summary: Hain reported Q2 FY2026 organic net sales down 7% YoY (9-point volume/mix decline, 2-point price increase), adjusted gross margin of 19.5% (down ~340 bps), adjusted EBITDA of $24 million versus $38 million a year ago, and an adjusted net loss of $0.03 per diluted share versus $0.08 income. North America organic sales fell 10% and international fell 3%; free cash flow was $30 million (up 22%) and net debt was reduced by $32 million to $637 million. Management provided no numeric FY2026 guidance, citing the strategic review, but continues to expect stronger H2 versus H1 and positive full-year free cash flow; the company agreed to watch its North American snacks business for $115 million in cash, which would reduce pro forma leverage from 4.9x to roughly 4x.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined to $232.1 million from $264.5 million a year ago, and reported net income fell 18% to $5.35 million
Reported adjusted EBITDA of $11.774 million was essentially flat (-2%) versus $12.16 million in the prior-year period
Ocean imports remain relatively soft, and the upcoming March quarter is described as historically the seasonally slowest
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA of $11.8 million would represent 93.4% growth over a normalized prior-year $6.1 million excluding the $5.9 million Milton project
Adjusted gross margin expanded 340 bps to 27.3% from 23.9% as lower-margin Milton revenue rolled off
Virtually debt-free with no net debt and $2.7 million of stock repurchased in the quarter
summary: Radiant reported Q2 FY2026 net income of $5.35 million ($0.11 per diluted share) on $232.1 million of revenue, down from $6.47 million and $264.5 million a year ago. Adjusted EBITDA was $11.774 million, essentially flat versus $12.16 million, but excluding the prior-year $5.9 million Milton project cargo adjusted EBITDA would have risen 93.4% to $11.8 million from a normalized $6.1 million. Adjusted gross margin expanded 340 bps to 27.3% as the lower-margin Milton work rolled off, and the company remains net debt-free, watching back $2.7 million of stock. Management gave no formal guidance and declined to quantify Navigate revenue, but noted improving demand and tightening capacity while flagging ocean imports as still soft.

negative_highlights: FY26 sales guidance cut to $750-760M, with up to ~$50M of impact from the large customer's store closures and distribution center consolidation
Gross margin contracted to 19.6% from 24.1% a year earlier on lower volume and capacity absorption
Outlook assumes a 15% reduction tied to the customer's roughly 15% store closure, with full recovery not expected in Q4
positive_highlights: Net bank debt fell $10.9M to $70.5M over nine months, after $8.4M of share repurchases, with net bank debt/EBITDA at roughly 0.84x
Gross margin improved sequentially to 19.6% from 18.0% in Q1 and 19.3% in Q2, with Q4 guided higher again
Total cash and availability of approximately $146M as of December 31, 2025
summary: Sales came in below expectations and fiscal 2026 sales guidance was cut to $750-760M, with operating income now guided to $72-79M, after one large customer reduced purchases by up to roughly $50M and did not recover as management expected. Gross margin fell to 19.6% from 24.1% a year earlier on lower volume, capacity absorption and mix, though it improved sequentially from 19.3% in Q2. Management said orders from that customer are rebounding and guided Q4 gross margin up sequentially, while noting strong liquidity of about $146M, nine-month operating cash flow of $23.7M, net bank debt down $10.9M to $70.5M and $8.4M of buybacks, with strategic alternatives being explored for the noncore EV emulator business.

negative_highlights: Marketing services revenues fell 10% year-over-year in Q4 to $17 million, and FY2025 marketing services revenue of $60 million was down 18% versus 2024.
Q1 2026 marketing services guidance of $10-11 million implies a 20-27% annual decline and a 35-41% sequential decline.
Social media platform posted a Q4 operating loss of $72 million (versus a $69 million loss a year earlier) and a full-year 2025 operating loss of $283 million.
positive_highlights: Online game revenues rose 10% year-over-year to $120 million in Q4 2025, with Changyou full-year 2025 operating profit improving to $238 million from $196 million in 2024.
Marketing services revenues of $17 million rose 25% quarter-over-quarter, helping full-year 2025 revenue exceed previous guidance.
Share repurchase program bought 8,100,000 ADS for approximately $150 million as of February 5, 2026.
summary: Q4 2025 total revenue was $142 million, up 6% year-over-year but down 21% quarter-over-quarter, with marketing services at $17 million (down 10% YoY, up 25% QoQ) and online games at $120 million (up 10% YoY, down 26% QoQ). Both GAAP and non-GAAP net income were heavily distorted by a ~$285 million Changyou withholding income tax reversal, producing GAAP net income of $123 million; excluding that reversal, full-year 2025 was a $51 million loss. Q1 2026 guidance calls for marketing services of $10-11 million, implying a 20-27% annual decline and a 35-41% sequential decline, online games of $123-130 million, and a GAAP and non-GAAP net loss of $10-20 million. Management attributed the soft Q1 ad outlook to the late Chinese New Year timing and a still-uncertain macro environment, and said the Q4 revenue beat was due to better execution rather than a one-off event.

negative_highlights: Sequential revenue decline of 21% due to seasonality, BC labor strike impact, and lower international sales volumes.
International flower out-of-spec issues resulted in an unanticipated sequential volume decline impacting approximately $3.5 million in Q1 revenue.
U.S. market penetration remains slower than anticipated with less than 1% of total revenues due to regulatory uncertainty.
positive_highlights: Net revenue increased 49% YoY to $65.3M, supported by Canadian growth and Motif integration.
Adjusted gross margin remained stable sequentially at 38%, demonstrating operational efficiency gains despite competitive pressures.
BC market share recovery is complete with inventory restock finished after the union strike ended.
summary: In Q1 FY2026, Organigram reported net revenue of $65.3 million (up 49% YoY) and adjusted gross profit of $23.9 million with a stable sequential margin of 38%. Adjusted EBITDA was $5.3 million, up significantly from the prior year period despite seasonal resets and operational headwinds including an unanticipated international sales decline driven by out-of-spec flower issues costing approximately $3.5 million in revenue.

negative_highlights: Net loss of $178.9 million in Q2 FY2026, or $2.94 per share, driven by $164.5 million of unrealized losses on Solana, which fell 40% during the quarter and another 31% after quarter-end.
Direct treasury expenses for the six months were $6.0 million, including fees and interest, without associated revenue.

The stock price and treasury company multiples compressed, with over 200 treasury companies trading at discounts to net asset value; management acknowledged the downturn has not been stemmed despite accretive raises.
positive_highlights: Total revenue of $8.1 million in Q2 FY2026, up over 100% from $4 million in the prior-year quarter, with six-month revenue of $17.3 million versus $8 million.
Treasury tokens increased by 106,000 Solana tokens during the quarter; 85% of tokens are staked.
Raised $19 million in equity and $7 million subsequent to quarter end, plus a $36 million in-kind convertible note, all at or above NAV, and announced a $50 million share repurchase program.
summary: Upexi reported Q2 FY2026 total revenue of $8.1 million, up over 100% YoY from $4 million, but net loss widened to $178.9 million (or $2.94 per share) primarily due to $164.5 million of non-cash unrealized losses on digital assets. The company held 2,170,000 Solana tokens at quarter-end (85% staked) and added 106,000 tokens during the quarter. Management raised $19 million in equity and a $36 million in-kind convertible note subsequent to quarter end, and announced a $50 million share repurchase program, but Solana's 40% price decline and continued treasury multiple compression pressured results. Revenue grew with the addition of the digital treasury, but earnings were deeply negative on fair value adjustments.

negative_highlights: Included $2 million of business interruption insurance proceeds; excluding them, adjusted EBITDA growth was 35% rather than the headline 61%
Digital-only subscription revenue grew only 5% YoY, slower than the 14% twelve-month growth cited by the CEO
Full-year outlook reaffirmed at only mid-single-digit adjusted EBITDA growth despite the strong Q1
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA grew 61% YoY to $12 million, with margin up to 9.4% from 5.3%
Interest rate on $455 million of debt cut to 5% from 9%, expected to save about $18 million annually, up to $90 million over five years
$50 million equity private placement closed at $3.25 per share, strengthening the balance sheet; total cash costs fell $17 million YoY
summary: Q1 FY2026 adjusted EBITDA rose 61% YoY to $12 million, with margin expanding to 9.4% from 5.3%, aided by $2 million of cyber insurance proceeds (35% growth ex-proceeds). Total digital revenue exceeded $70 million, or 54% of total revenue, with digital-only subscription revenue up 5% to $23 million on 609,000 digital-only subscribers. The company reaffirmed FY2026 guidance of mid-single-digit adjusted EBITDA growth. The quarter's key event was the close of a $50 million common stock private placement at $3.25 per share and an amended credit agreement cutting the debt interest rate to 5% from 9%, expected to save roughly $18 million annually on $455 million of debt.

negative_highlights: 2025 was a challenging year; Q4 results do not reflect full potential
International retail, particularly EMEA, was softer than expected
Margins to be under pressure in the near term as production runs below wholesale
positive_highlights: North American dealer inventory declined 16% and globally down 17%, exceeding the 10% target
North American retail sales growth accelerated into December
Expects at least $150 million of annual run-rate savings impacting 2027 and beyond
summary: Q4 2025 was a challenging year with intentional wholesale reductions to address elevated dealer inventory, particularly touring in North America. Dealer inventory globally down 17% versus year-end 2024, exceeding the 10% target. Retail sales in North America were up year-over-year with December accelerating, but international retail especially EMEA was softer. Management sees 2026 as a transition year, expects margins under pressure, and announced at least $150 million of annual run-rate savings impacting 2027 and beyond. They are evaluating buyback timing and plan to share strategic details in May.

negative_highlights: Reported a distributable earnings loss of $7 million ($0.12 per diluted share) for the quarter.
CECL reserve increased by $10 million to $127 million, with 92% allocated to risk-rated four and five loans.
One multifamily loan was downgraded from risk-rated four to five due to potential loss severity on a property sale.
positive_highlights: Office loan exposure reduced by 30% year-over-year to $447 million, down from 38% portfolio weight at year-end 2024.
Closed eight new loan commitments totaling $393 million in Q4, with over 50% collateralized by residential and industrial properties.
Board declared a regular cash dividend of $0.15 per common share for 2026.
summary: ACRE reported a GAAP net loss of $1 million ($0.02 per diluted share) and a distributable earnings loss of $7 million ($0.12 per diluted share) for the fourth quarter of FY2025, driven by loan basis reductions on nonaccrual interest collections. The company reduced its office loan portfolio by 30% year-over-year to $447 million and closed eight new commitments totaling $393 million in Q4, bringing the total portfolio to $1.6 billion. Management maintained a net debt-to-equity ratio of 1.6x and declared a regular cash dividend of $0.15 per share for 2026.

negative_highlights: Reinsurance Q4 net premiums written fell approximately 5.2% YoY, and January 1 property cat and note weakness in-tail excess of loss rates declined 10-20%.
Insurance Q4 net premiums written declined 4% YoY, with the acquisition expense ratio up 150 bps due to the roll-off of a 2024 benefit.
Management noted reinsurance margins are under pressure from both lower pricing and higher ceding commissions.
positive_highlights: Q4 after-tax operating income rose 26% YoY to $1.1 billion, with full-year operating income a record $3.7 billion.
Consolidated combined ratio was 80.6%, and the ex-cat accident year combined ratio improved 100 bps sequentially to 79.5%.
The company repurchased $798 million of shares in Q4 and $1.9 billion for the year, with an additional $349 million bought back so far in 2026.
summary: Arch Capital reported Q4 FY2025 after-tax operating income of $1.1 billion, up 26% YoY, or $2.98 per share, with book value per share up 4.5% in the quarter. The consolidated combined ratio was 80.6% and the ex-cat accident year combined ratio improved 100 bps from last quarter to 79.5%. Full-year after-tax operating income was a record $3.7 billion, or $9.84 per share, and the company repurchased $798 million of stock in Q4 and $1.9 billion for the year. Management cited increasing competition and rate pressure in reinsurance, with January 1 property cat rates down 10-20% and margins under pressure, but expects 2026 corporate expenses of $80-90 million and a reinsurance expense ratio of 3.9-4.5% aided by Bermuda tax credits.

negative_highlights: Net income fell to $4.8 million ($0.47 per share) from $5.3 million ($0.51 per share) a year ago
Management said fiscal Q2 will be weaker after losing roughly two weeks of construction, about 17% of working days in the quarter
A top-five industrial customer announced a plant closure expected later in calendar 2026, and a $15 million note now sits in current liabilities pending refinancing
positive_highlights: Residential gas volumes rose 8% and heating degree days were up 11% year over year
SAVE program service renewals increased 80% to 117 services in the quarter
Interim rate case rates effective January 1, 2026, seeking approximately $4.3 million in incremental annual revenue
summary: RGC Resources reported Q1 FY2026 net income of $4.8 million, or $0.47 per share, down from $5.3 million, or $0.51 per share, a year ago, as higher personnel, IT, property tax, and depreciation costs more than offset slightly higher gas margins and lower interest expense. Total delivered volumes were flat, with residential volumes up 8% and an 11% increase in heating degree days offset by lower usage from a large industrial customer. Management reiterated its FY2026 EPS forecast of $1.27-$1.35 and $22 million capital plan, unchanged from December, but flagged a weaker fiscal Q2 due to weather-related construction delays. The company noted an estimated $8 million-$10 million gas cost undercollection from Winter Storm Fern and said a top-five industrial customer announced a plant closure expected later in calendar 2026.

negative_highlights: Delhi field experienced equipment-related downtime related to CO2 compressor issues that limited injection volumes for much of the period.
Production growth was partially offset by lower oil and NGL pricing compared to natural gas gains.
Barnett Shale production costs saw a sequential decline driven largely by an Advel billing adjustment rather than structural cost changes.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA increased 41% YoY despite only a 2% revenue increase, demonstrating strong operating leverage.
Lease operating expenses improved significantly to $16.96/BOE from $20.05/BOE in the prior year quarter due to cost discipline and cessation of CO2 purchases at Delhi.
Mineral and royalty acquisitions are driving incremental high-margin production without requiring development capital.
summary: Evolution Petroleum reported Q2 FY2026 revenues of $20.7 million (up 2% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA increasing 41% to $8 million driven by higher natural gas prices and lower lease operating costs. The company declared a quarterly cash dividend of $0.12 per share, bringing total dividends paid in the quarter to $4.2 million. Management raised CapEx guidance for the remainder of the fiscal year slightly above prior estimates due to activity on SCOOPSTACK minerals.

GCI Liberty reported Q4 revenue of $262 million, flat year over year, with adjusted OIBDA up 7% to $90 million on lower SG&A. Full-year revenue rose 3% to slightly over $1 billion and adjusted OIBDA reached a record $403 million, up 12%, with free cash flow of $146 million up over 70%. Management guided 2026 as a 'stable' year and declined to guide margins, while flagging 2026 CapEx of approximately $290 million as the peak year, driving proportionately lower year-over-year free cash flow. summary: Inogen reported Q4 FY2025 revenue of $81.7 million (down 2% YoY) and full-year revenue of $348.7 million (up 4% YoY), driven by strong international growth but offset by a shift in large customer orders into 2026 and lower U.S. sales. Management provided full-year 2026 revenue guidance of approximately 6% growth ($366M-$373M), noting that Q1 is expected to be in-line with Q1 2025 due to the timing shift of orders.

The company highlighted gross margin expansion to just over 56%, driven by improved labor efficiency and pricing, while noting ongoing ERP upgrade costs will taper after Q1.

Reinsurance segment underwriting income was up nearly 30% for the full year.
summary: IGIC reported a Q4 FY2025 net income of $32.3 million ($0.76/share) and full-year net income of $127.2 million ($2.89/share), both missing the prior year's EPS of $0.65 and $2.98 respectively. summary: Ashford reported a Q4 net loss attributable to common stockholders of $131.1 million, or $23.83 per diluted share, and negative AFFO of $2.21 per share; full-year net loss was $82.5 million with AFFO of -$4.84. Comparable RevPAR rose 3% and hotel EBITDA grew 6.2%, with gross operating margin up ~141 bps and December hotel EBITDA up 12%. Liquidity includes $112.9 million of cash, $2.6 billion of loans at a 7.9% blended rate (77% effectively floating), and $438.7 million of post-quarter mortgage debt was refinanced via a $580 million loan; no common dividend is expected in 2025. Management gave no explicit 2025 RevPAR, EBITDA, or AFFO guidance, citing ~$95-115 million of 2025 capex and continued GrowAHT rollout with a $50 million target.

negative_highlights: Q4 time charter revenues decreased to $52.1 million from $57.1 million due to the sale of two vessels reducing ownership days.
Time charter equivalent rate averaged USD 15,397 per day in Q4, a decrease compared to last year's average of USD 15,589.
Vessel operating expenses increased by 6% on a total basis and daily OPEX rose 11%, driven by higher crew costs.
positive_highlights: Fleet utilization reached an impressive 99.7% for the year ended December 31, 2025.
Q4 Capesize earnings averaged USD 28,892 per day with a brief peak of USD 45,000 in December.
The company declared a quarterly cash dividend and repurchased $23 million worth of common shares.
summary: Diana Shipping reported Q4 FY2025 time charter revenues of $52.1 million and adjusted EBITDA of $19.3 million, both lower than the prior year quarter due to a smaller fleet size (average 36 vessels vs 38) and timing of renewals under its medium-term strategy. The company declared a quarterly cash dividend of $0.01 per share totaling approximately USD 1.16 million while maintaining strong liquidity with $122.3 million in cash reserves as of quarter-end.

negative_highlights: Reported revenue was $1 million lower than the pre-release approximation due to complex closing processes following acquisition integration.
Operating loss increased by 43% year-over-year (from $4.6M) primarily driven by headcount increases and ExoDx-related expenses.
Tissue-based ASPs declined quarter-over-quarter, attributed to a mix shift between GPS ($3,850) and Confirm ($2,000).
positive_highlights: Liquid-based test volumes surged 128% year-over-year driven by the newly acquired ExoDx business and SelectMDx conversions.
Gross margins expanded slightly to 63.2%, reflecting economies of scale despite mix shifts.
Management successfully transitioned all SelectMDx customers to ExoDx ahead of schedule, accelerating operating efficiencies.
summary: MDxHealth reported Q4 FY2025 revenue of $107.9 million (down from a prior pre-release estimate) and full-year growth driven by liquid-based tests (+128% unit volume), though tissue volumes declined (-5%). The company amended its Exact Sciences earnout to lower upcoming payments, providing flexibility despite an operating loss widening to $5.3 million due to ExoDx integration costs.

negative_highlights: 2026 same-practice revenue growth guidance of 3.5%-5.0% is below the 5.8% reported for full-year 2025
EPS declined year-over-year, driven by $8.8 million of non-cash share-based compensation and a larger share count; shares could reach about 6.6 million by end-2028 if pre-IPO shares fully vest
New public-company costs are expected at $400,000-$500,000 per quarter, and 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance of 8.3%-8.9% of revenue implies margin pressure versus prior-year levels
positive_highlights: Q4 revenue grew 7.5% year-over-year to $61.2 million, with multi-specialty revenue up 11.3% to $16.5 million
Full-year operating cash flow was $17.6 million and the company had $25.2 million of cash plus an undrawn $15 million credit line at year-end
Entered a third state (Arizona) with acquisitions in Phoenix and Tucson and closed three practices plus one de novo in 2025
summary: Q4 revenue was $61.2 million, up 7.5% year-over-year, with general practice revenue up 6.2% to $44.7 million and multi-specialty revenue up 11.3% to $16.5 million; full-year revenue totaled $244.5 million, up 6.4%, and same-practice revenue grew 5.8% for the year. 2026 guidance calls for revenue of $254-$258 million, same-practice growth of 3.5%-5.0%, and adjusted EBITDA of $21-$23 million (8.3%-8.9% of revenue), a same-practice deceleration from 2025. The quarter included $8.8 million of non-cash share-based compensation tied to the IPO, which management flagged as a driver of the year-over-year EPS decline together with higher share count; the company ended the year with $25.2 million of cash after $18.4 million of IPO net proceeds, $10.1 million of long-term debt, and a newly amended undrawn $15 million credit line.

negative_highlights: Wavelo adjusted EBITDA margin expected down year-over-year in 2026
Conservatively forecasting possible reduction in Wavelo fees from Ting process
Capital allocation conservative, no commitment to buybacks
positive_highlights: Ting process ongoing and not delayed despite external volatility
Liquidity remains sound with $20.9 million unrestricted cash excluding Ting
Syndicated debt paydown ongoing, increasing borrowing capacity
summary: Tucows reported Q4 2025 results and addressed investor questions. Management provided no update on the Ting asset sale timeline, stating it is ongoing and not delayed despite market volatility. They conservatively guided 2026 Wavelo adjusted EBITDA margin down year-over-year, citing potential loss of Ting customers and fully annualized investments. The company noted liquidity of $20.9 million excluding Ting and emphasized deleveraging and conservative capital allocation, with a stock buyback program providing flexibility but no commitment to repurchase.

negative_highlights: Management lowered full-year 2026 revenue outlook to a decline of 25% to 38% year-over-year due to clinician confusion and market freeze following CMS comments on December 30.
First quarter 2026 is expected to see approximately 50% year-over-year revenue declines driven by the aforementioned utilization issues.
Surgical & Sports Medicine segment sales declined 2% year-over-year, though this was within guidance assumptions.
positive_highlights: Advanced Wound Care revenue surged 83% year-over-year to $217.2 million, driven by strong execution and favorable product mix rather than inventory pull-forward.
Total Q4 net income jumped from $5.1 million in the prior year period to $31.5 million for common shareholders (GAAP) or $52.9 million adjusted.
The company delivered record sales results that exceeded the high end of its previously issued guidance range.
summary: Organogenesis reported Q4 FY2025 net product revenue of $225.1 million (up 78% YoY), significantly beating the high end of guidance and exceeding expectations by approximately $50 million due to an 83% surge in Advanced Wound Care sales, while Surgical & Sports Medicine declined 2%. Despite strong Q4 execution, management lowered full-year 2026 revenue guidance to a decline range of 25%-38% YoY citing clinician confusion from recent CMS comments and the $127 price reduction. Management expects first-half declines followed by substantial market share gains in the second half as competitive dynamics improve.

negative_highlights: Q4 comparable sales declined 3.3% excluding deferred loyalty revenue due to a 3.6% drop in traffic.
Restaurant-level operating margin contracted by 10 basis points to 11.4% compared to the prior year quarter.
Beef inflation is expected to remain high in 2026, with commodity costs projected to be up roughly 4%.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA of $11.8 million in Q4 was ahead of expectations discussed on the last earnings call.
Full-year 2025 adjusted EBITDA grew 53% year-over-year to $69.7 million, driven by labor efficiency and cost savings.
December traffic outpaced the Black Box casual dining index for the first time since Q3 2024.
summary: Red Robin reported Q4 FY2025 revenues of $269 million, a decrease of $16.2 million year-over-year driven by a 3.6% decline in traffic and restaurant closures. While adjusted EBITDA of $11.8 million beat expectations, the company provided full-year 2026 guidance for comparable sales growth of 0.5% to 1.5%, reflecting a cautious outlook due to weather impacts and commodity inflation.

negative_highlights: NAV per share declined to $19.10 from $19.28
Weighted average yield on income-producing securities fell 40 bps to 10%
Nonaccruals increased with two new additions in Q4
positive_highlights: NII covered the base dividend by 107% in Q4
Spillover income of $1.16 per share, nearly 3x the dividend
Pro forma nonaccruals improved after January restructurings
summary: CCAP's Q4 2025 NII was $0.45 per share, down from $0.46 sequentially, and over-earned the $0.42 dividend by 107%. NAV per share fell to $19.10 from $19.28, driven by unrealized losses and higher nonaccruals (two new nonaccruals, with pro forma nonaccruals improving after January restructurings and a sale). Gross deployment was $71 million, but net realizations were about $7 million negative due to $78 million in exits. Management flagged earnings headwinds from lower base rates and is reviewing dividend policy and capital options, with an update expected in May. The supplemental dividend is not paid for Q4 due to the NAV-based measurement test, but the policy remains in place.

negative_highlights: Q4 revenue includes $1.0 million in collections from claims older than one year, excluding which core organic growth was lower
First quarter is expected to show a step-down in volume and ASP consistent with historic seasonality
Recent weather events caused disruptions that were considered in the guidance range
positive_highlights: Achieved adjusted EBITDA positivity of $530k in Q4 FY2025
Gross margins expanded to 83% driven by volume growth and improved reimbursement collections
Primary care channel volumes grew 67% YoY, accounting for 12% of total Nodify tests
summary: Biodesix reported Q4 FY2025 revenue of $28.8 million (up 41% YoY) and achieved adjusted EBITDA positivity of $530k for the first time in company history, driven by a core organic lung diagnostic growth of 40%. Gross margins expanded to 83%, while management provided FY2026 revenue guidance of $106M-$112M (midpoint representing ~23% annual growth). The quarter was impacted by Q1 seasonality and weather events, which were explicitly factored into the forward outlook.

negative_highlights: Management initiated a lower free cash flow guidance for FY2026 ($6M-$9M) citing conservative outlooks and planned increases in sales/marketing/AI investment.
Q1 paid members decreased to 626,000 from the Q4 level of 650,000 due to expected seasonality.
positive_highlights: New Expensify achieved full feature parity with Classic for customers representing 90% of revenue.
Expensify travel bookings in Q4 were up 434% compared to the prior year period.
Interchange fees increased 24% year-over-year, totaling $5.5 million in Q4.
summary: Expensify reported Q4 FY2025 revenue of $35.2 million and full-year revenue of $142.1 million with an average paid member count of 650,000 for both periods. The company generated $19.9 million in free cash flow for the year but initiated a lower fiscal year '2026 guidance range of $6 million to $9 million due to conservative investment plans and increased spending on sales, marketing, and AI.

negative_highlights: Q4 revenue declined 3% quarter-over-quarter due to seasonal hiring slowdowns.
Job openings dropped 10% year-over-year, with job seeker traffic from LLMs still a small portion of the overall mix.
SMB demand remained soft in Q4 despite enterprise strength.
positive_highlights: Achieved first year-over-year revenue growth since Q3 2022 with $111.7M reported.
Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded sequentially and YoY, reaching 15% from a lower base of paid employers (up 2%).
Enterprise performance marketing revenue grew 9% year-over-year in Q4.
summary: ZipRecruiter reported Q4 FY2025 revenue of $111.7 million (up 1% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA margins expanding to 15%. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance, projecting flat revenue growth against a lower base due to soft holiday seasonality in SMB demand.

negative_highlights: Total investment income declined to $50 million from $51.1 million due to lower base rates
NAV per share decreased to $17.72 from $17.85
Q1 2026 dividend reduced to $0.40 per share from $0.45
positive_highlights: NII per share increased sequentially to $0.44 from $0.43
Non-accruals remain low at 0.5% of fair value
Refinanced secured credit facility, reducing borrowing costs by 17 bps
summary: NCDL reported Q4 FY2025 NII of $0.44 per share, slightly above Q3's $0.43, with total investment income declining slightly to $50 million from $51.1 million due to lower base rates. Non-accruals remained low at 0.5% of fair value, and NAV per share dipped to $17.72 from $17.85. Management declared a Q1 2026 dividend of $0.40 per share (regular $0.36 plus $0.04 supplemental), down from the prior quarter's $0.45, and authorized a $50 million share repurchase program. They enter 2026 with a strong pipeline and stabilized spreads, but acknowledge earnings pressure from rate cuts and competitive spreads.

negative_highlights: Guidance explicitly excludes speculative acquisition or disposition activity due to current cost of capital constraints.
Ongoing negative NOI impact from the East Orange asset affected by Steward bankruptcy proceedings.
Management noted potential earnings dilution during the transition period as they delever and note legacy assets.
positive_highlights: Same-store cash NOI increased 5.4% on a year-over-year basis with sequential performance at 2.9%.
Net debt to adjusted EBITDA REIT decreased to 6.2x, driven by preferred equity issuance and asset sales.
Company successfully sold an early vintage medical office for $10 million proceeds used for stock repurchase.
summary: Chiron Real Estate reported Q4 FY2025 with Core FFO of $1.16 per share and unit (transitioning from AFFO) and NAREIT-defined FFO of $0.97. Management provided initial 2026 core FFO guidance ranging between $4.30 to $4.45, explicitly excluding speculative acquisition or disposition activity but including anticipated headwinds related to balance sheet fortification efforts in the back half of last year.

negative_highlights: FY2026 revenue guided to $220-226 million, a 6-9% decline year-over-year, with Q1 2026 revenue guided down 5-9%
FY2026 adjusted EBITDA margin guided to 24-26%, down from 29% in 2025, with management citing negative operating leverage
Total remaining performance obligations declined 18% year-over-year and current RPO declined 12% year-over-year; net dollar retention declined due to reduced upsell and cross-note
positive_highlights: Q4 revenue of $61.5 million and adjusted EBITDA of $18 million both exceeded the high end of guidance
Adjusted gross margin expanded ~100 bps to 82% and adjusted EBITDA margin expanded ~120 bps year-over-year to 29%
Gross dollar retention improved approximately 2 points year-over-year, with enterprise/life sciences leading the improvement; diversified and provider segments returned to growth in Q4
summary: Q4 2025 revenue of $61.5 million came in above the high end of guidance but was down 1% year-over-year, with subscription revenue declining 3% (down 7% excluding data partnerships) and adjusted EBITDA of $18 million at a 29% margin, $1.1 million above the high end. Full-year 2025 revenue of $241.5 million declined 4%. Management guided FY2026 revenue to $220-226 million, a 6-9% decline, with EBITDA margin compressing to 24-26% from 29%. The key change versus prior periods is the 2026 revenue and margin outlook, both well below 2025 levels, reflecting ongoing top-line pressure and a modestly improved but still challenged renewal and upsell environment.

negative_highlights: Semi business orders remained soft, representing only 25% of total orders compared to 40% in 2024.
Full-year 2025 net loss was $2.5 million with adjusted EPS of $0.06, down from $0.51 adjusted EPS prior year.
Management explicitly stated guidance does not contemplate a meaningful rebound in semi sales for 2026.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 25% sequentially to $32.8M, exceeding the guidance range.
Gross margin expanded 350 bps sequentially to 45.4% driven by new product mix and cost discipline.
Non-semi revenues grew at a 20% CAGR over the past five years, reducing cyclicality exposure.
summary: Fourth quarter revenue increased 25% sequentially to $32.8 million, driven by strength in industrial, defense, aerospace, and life sciences, though semi orders remained soft. Gross margins expanded 350 bps sequentially to 45.4%, aided by new product mix and cost actions. Management provided full-year 2026 guidance of $125-$130 million revenue (approx. 12% growth) with gross margins around 45%, explicitly noting the absence of a meaningful semi rebound in the forecast.

negative_highlights: Q4 net loss attributable to common stockholders of $46.0 million (-$0.67/diluted share) and AFFO per diluted share of negative $0.02
Comparable Q4 RevPAR was flat at $340, with renovation disruptions at three hotels and below-normal snowfall/delayed mountain openings at Park Hyatt Beaver Creek and Ritz-Carlton Lake Tahoe
Board has not declared a 2026 common dividend policy and preferred dividend declaration timing was changed amid the ongoing company sale process
positive_highlights: Resort portfolio comparable RevPAR rose 4.1% and comparable hotel EBITDA rose 6%, with Ritz-Carlton Sarasota RevPAR up 25.5% and hotel EBITDA up 48%
Excluding renovation-affected hotels, Q4 comparable RevPAR grew 2.6% and comparable hotel EBITDA grew 6.4%
Sold the Clancy San Francisco for $115 million, paid down ~$65 million of debt, and redeemed $149 million (~32%) of non-traded preferred stock
summary: Braemar reported flat comparable Q4 RevPAR of $340 and 1.8% comparable total revenue growth, with net loss attributable to common stockholders of $46.0 million (-$0.67/diluted share) and AFFO per share of negative $0.02; full-year AFFO per share was $0.28 and Adjusted EBITDAre was $147.0 million. Resorts outperformed (RevPAR +4.1%, hotel EBITDA +6%), but three hotels under renovation (Cameo Beverly Hills, Park Hyatt Beaver Creek, Hotel Yountville) plus weak mountain snowfall dragged portfolio results, though ex-renovation RevPAR rose 2.6%. No 2026 common dividend policy was declared and preferred dividend declaration timing was changed amid an ongoing company sale process (Baird engaged), with the Clancy sold for $115 million and $149 million of non-traded preferred redeemed. Guidance was limited to 2026 capex of $25-35 million versus $78 million in 2025; no forward RevPAR or EBITDA guidance was provided.

negative_highlights: GMV of $90.2M fell 5% and came in at the low end of the guidance range, with order volumes down 9%
Active buyers fell 5% to ~60,700 and unique sellers fell 4% to ~5,700 following Q4 pricing adjustments
Q1 GMV guidance of down 9% to down 3% YoY implies continued contraction, and a return to GMV growth is not expected until Q4 2026
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA of $1.3M (6% margin) beat the high end of guidance, a ~1,300 bps margin expansion from a $1.6M loss a year ago and the first positive adjusted EBITDA quarter as a public company
Take rate rose ~140 bps YoY on October pricing increases and sponsored listings growth, lifting revenue 1% to $23.0M even as GMV fell 5%
Sales and marketing fell 44% to $5.9M (26% of revenue vs 46% a year ago), and total operating expenses dropped 18%, with ~80% of traffic now organic (up 8 pts)
summary: Q4 GMV of $90.2M fell 5% YoY and landed at the low end of guidance, while net revenue rose 1% to $23.0M and adjusted EBITDA of $1.3M (6% margin, up ~1,300 bps) came in above the high end and marked the first profitable adjusted EBITDA quarter as a public company. Q1 guidance calls for GMV of $86.5-91.5M (down 9% to down 3%), revenue of $22.1-23.1M (down 2% to up 2%), and adjusted EBITDA margin of breakeven to 4%. No full-year guidance was given, but management expects a third consecutive year of revenue growth, gross margins of 72-74% (up from 71-73%), take rates of 25-26%, positive full-year adjusted EBITDA and free cash flow, and a return to YoY GMV growth by Q4 2026. Order volumes fell 9% and active buyers fell 5% to ~60,700, while take rate rose ~140 bps and conversion grew for a ninth consecutive quarter.

negative_highlights: Net sales declined 2.2% on softer demand in basketball, outdoor games, and e-commerce channels
SG&A increased 6.8% to $11.6 million, including $0.5 million of nonrecurring executive transition costs
No explicit 2026 revenue or EPS guidance provided; management expects consumer conditions to remain mixed
positive_highlights: Gross margin expanded 280 bps to 27.7% from 24.9% despite a 2.2% sales decline
Operating cash flow rose to $14.9 million from $12.3 million, aided by a 10% ($7.6 million) inventory reduction
EBITDA increased to $6.5 million from $5.9 million and net leverage is 0.3x with $11.9 million cash
summary: Escalade reported Q4 FY2025 net sales of $62.6 million, down 2.2% year-over-year, with net income of $3.7 million or $0.27 per diluted share. Gross margin expanded 280 bps to 27.7% on facility consolidation, lower storage/handling costs, and the accretive Gold Tip acquisition, while SG&A rose 6.8% to $11.6 million on $0.5 million of nonrecurring executive transition expense. EBITDA rose to $6.5 million from $5.9 million, operating cash flow increased to $14.9 million from $12.3 million, inventory fell 10%, and net leverage stood at 0.3x. Management gave no explicit 2026 revenue or EPS guidance, citing a mixed consumer environment, and flagged a potential $4-5 million tariff refund if the Supreme Court decision triggers refunds.

negative_highlights: Consolidated GAAP net loss of $177 million for 2025, with book value per share declining to negative $44.27
No substantive progress on PREPA due to unresolved Oversight Board legal issues
MBIA Insurance Corp. statutory capital declined to $79 million from $88 million
positive_highlights: Full-year adjusted net income of $23 million vs. adjusted net loss of $184 million in 2024
PREPA-related loss and LAE benefit in 2025 from sale of custodial receipts at favorable prices
National's statutory capital increased to $937 million, up $25 million from year-end 2024
summary: MBIA reported a consolidated GAAP net loss of $177 million for full year 2025, improved from a $447 million loss in 2024, driven by lower PREPA losses and VIE-related expenses. Adjusted net income was $23 million for 2025 versus a $184 million loss in 2024. Book value per share fell to negative $44.27. National's statutory capital rose to $937 million, but PREPA resolution remains stalled due to Oversight Board legal issues, though management expressed optimism for progress this year.

negative_highlights: Company remains in a cash-burn phase with no revenue reported.
Phase 2 ASPEN-9 primary endpoint changed to response rate by high CD47 expression, requiring larger sample size and pushing top-line data readout to mid-2027.
positive_highlights: GAAP net loss decreased YoY from $29.2M to $22.8M due to lower stock compensation and personnel costs.
Completed financing raised net proceeds of ~$140.4M, extending cash runway through 2028.
Phase 2 ASPEN-9 breast cancer trial upsized from 80 to 120 patients to ensure robust biomarker data for CD47 overexpressors.
summary: ALX Oncology Holdings Inc. reported a GAAP net loss of $22.8M for Q4 FY2025 (or $0.42/share), representing an improvement from the prior quarter's $29.2M loss ($0.55/share) driven by lower stock compensation and personnel costs following pipeline prioritization. The company successfully closed a financing round raising net proceeds of approximately $140.4M, strengthening its balance sheet to fund operations through 2028. Management confirmed that clinical timelines for both lead programs remain on track with the goal of advancing them to pivotal studies by year-end next.

negative_highlights: Multiplatform Group GAAP adjusted EBITDA fell 14.2% YoY due to the absence of ~$80M political revenue compared to prior year.
Digital Audio Group Q4 margins contracted slightly from 35.1% in the prior year quarter to 34.1%, driven by variable content costs.
Q1 EBITDA expected to decline despite cost savings, attributed to prepaid marketing expenses deployed early and small base effects.
positive_highlights: Digital Audio Group revenue surged 14.1% YoY driven by podcasting (up 24.5%) exceeding mid-teens guidance.
Consolidated adjusted EBITDA hit $220 million, landing at the midpoint of the provided range despite a non-political year.
Full-year and Q1 revenue guidance raised to high single digits following an in-line quarter.
summary: iHeartMedia reported Q4 FY2025 consolidated revenue of $1.1 billion (up 0.8% YoY), beating guidance for low single-digit decline and hitting adjusted EBITDA at the midpoint of its range ($220M vs $200-240M). The Digital Audio Group significantly outperformed with revenue up 14.1%, while the Multiplatform Group missed on a GAAP basis due to political advertising comparisons, though excluding politics it grew 2.3%. Management raised full-year EBITDA guidance to approximately $800 million and provided specific Q1 expectations of high single-digit revenue growth.

negative_highlights: Reported Q4 gross margin contracted slightly to 67.7% from 68.2%.
Adjusted EBITDA loss widened to $9.9M in Q4 compared to $9.1M prior year, impacted by $1.8M Guardant litigation costs and FX headwinds.
Cash burn increased to $12.3M in Q4 due to foreign exchange impacts from the strengthening Swiss franc.
positive_highlights: Q4 revenue grew 22% YoY to $21.7M, with clinical revenue excluding biopharma up 31%.
Signed a record 124 new customers in 2025, including two of the largest US health systems serving ~60,000 patients annually.
Adjusted gross margin expanded 140 bps to 74.2% due to compute optimizations and scrap cost reductions.
summary: SOPHiA GENETICS reported Q4 FY2025 revenue of $21.7 million, representing a 22% year-over-year increase driven by strong clinical growth and new customer signings. Full year 2025 revenue reached $77.3 million (up 19%), with adjusted gross margin expanding to 74.2%. Management provided full year 2026 guidance for reported revenue between $92 million and $94 million, implying approximately 20-22% growth.

negative_highlights: MX908 product and service revenue was relatively flat in Q4.
International revenue mix was 27% in 2025, a modest increase from 25% in 2024.
Management noted possible timing delays from Middle East conflict but no material impact expected.
positive_highlights: Q4 revenue up 21% YoY to $17.4M with positive adjusted EBITDA of $0.7M.
Explorer device grew over 40% YoY, with 150+ units shipped in its first full year.
Viper shipped >40 units in Q4, generating over $3M in revenue (initial demand).
summary: 908 Devices (MASS) reported Q4 2025 revenue of $17.4M, up 21% YoY, with positive adjusted EBITDA of $0.7M versus a loss of $4.0M a year ago. Full-year revenue from continuing operations reached $56.2M, up 18% YoY, and recurring revenue grew 22%, representing 35% of total revenue. The company cited strong Explorer demand (up 40% YoY), early Viper traction (>40 units, $3M revenue in Q4), and 600 bps gross margin improvement. Guidance for 2026 was not explicitly stated in the transcript, but management expressed confidence in sustaining growth and improving profitability with targeted investments.

negative_highlights: Q4 revenue down 3% YoY to $203.6 million
Accessories and materials sales down 13% in Q4 and 9% for the year
Management disappointed in lack of total company sales growth for Q4 and 2025
positive_highlights: Paid subscribers up over 4% YoY to 3.09 million in Q4
Full-year net income increased 22% to $76.7 million
International sales up 9% in Q4 and 8% for the year
summary: In Q4 2025, Cricut reported revenue of $203.6 million, down 3% YoY, and full-year revenue of $708.8 million, down less than 1%. Net income for the quarter was $7.8 million and $76.7 million for the year, up 22% from 2024. Paid subscribers grew over 4% YoY to 3.09 million, but accessories and materials sales fell 13% in Q4. Management expressed disappointment in flat revenue and guided for flat to slightly down revenue in 2026, while launching two new next-generation machines bundled with materials and a new DTF service.

negative_highlights: Q4 revenue fell 11.2% to $308.5 million with a GAAP net loss of $7.2 million and diluted loss per share of $0.15 versus $0.11 income prior year
Platform Solutions revenue dropped 56.5% to $25.1 million as carriers internalized claims and weather revenue fell roughly 33%

Management guided to a subdued Q1 2026 and flagged that Winter Storm Fern and Gianna are not producing significant claims activity; Q4 also carried $14 million of pre-tax restructuring and other costs
positive_highlights: Broadspire delivered record full-year revenue and operating earnings, with Q4 revenue up 3.9% to $101.5 million and operating earnings up 30.2% to $13.2 million at 94% client retention
Operating cash flow rose to $101.8 million from $51.6 million in 2024, with free cash flow of $63.3 million versus $10 million
Consolidated full-year operating earnings grew just over 10% to $82.3 million, margin expanded to 6.5%, and leverage was 1.39x EBITDA with net debt of $125 million
summary: Q4 2025 revenue fell 11.2% to $308.5 million and GAAP diluted EPS swung to a loss of $0.15 from earnings of $0.11 (CRDA), with non-GAAP EPS down to $0.15 from $0.19 and non-GAAP operating margin narrowing to 5.1% from 5.4%. The decline was weather-driven: Platform Solutions revenue fell 56.5% and North America Loss Adjusting fell 11.8% against a Q4 2024 that included over $30 million from hurricanes Helene and Milton, roughly a 33% drop in weather-related revenue; Broadspire grew revenue 3.9% and operating earnings 30.2%. Full-year revenue was flat at $1.27 billion with operating earnings up just over 10% to $82.3 million, margin of 6.5%, non-GAAP EPS of $0.91 and operating cash flow of $102 million. Management guided to a subdued first quarter of 2026, citing no repeat of Helene/Milton carryover, carrier insourcing, and Broadspire moderation from advance hires, and announced a new three-segment structure effective January 1, 2026.

negative_highlights: SMB business declined 3% in the quarter and grew only modestly at +1% for the full year due to a mix shift toward lower-margin ISO channels
Adjusted EBITDA margin contracted by 130 basis points, with gross margins pressured by interest revenue declines of $13 million annually
Net leverage ratio increased to 5.5x from 4.7x primarily due to FX fluctuations and the business disposal
positive_highlights: Digital Wallet segment revenue grew organically by 13% to $220.2 million, driven by a >200% increase in Latin America
E-commerce processing volumes reached record levels during the U.S. football season with +24% Q4 growth
New product vitality index hit $270 million (16% of total revenue), up from 2% three years ago
summary: Paysafe reported Q4 FY2025 revenue of $438.4 million (organic growth +6%) and full-year organic revenue growth of 5%, though adjusted EBITDA declined 1% to $102.1 million in the quarter due to higher marketing investment, OpEx timing items, and a business disposal headwind. Management reiterated FY2026 guidance for revenue between $1.79 billion and $1.83 billion (5-8% growth) with adjusted EBITDA of $449-$464 million, maintaining the full-year margin outlook despite Q4 mix-driven compression. The company highlighted strong e-commerce volumes (+24%) and digital wallet growth in Latin America while noting softer SMB performance.
