In February 2026 the company completed an oversubscribed $1.1 million private placement at $1 per share with 5-year warrants, despite having guided in Q3 to sufficient working capital for more than five years. Key licensee Gauzy's French subsidiaries entered a court-supervised rehabilitation in mid-November 2025, prompting headcount cuts and a liquidity reallocation, though management said SPD film production in Germany and emulsion production in Israel continue. Management reported an expanded automotive pipeline (four high-volume quotations, a new European OEM, specialty programs), completed transition of the Ferrari business to Isoclima, and launch of an architectural retrofit product, but gave no revenue or earnings guidance for 2026.

negative_highlights: Hardware revenue declined 8% due to contract timing and deferred amortization.
Residential generator market slowed due to high interest rates and fewer outages.
AIO partnership not expected to contribute revenue until second half of 2026.
positive_highlights: Revenue rose 4.5% to $11.478 million, a record year.
Monitoring revenue grew 22% with 95% gross margin.
Cash flow from operations more than doubled to $2.09 million, up 131%.
summary: Acorn Energy reported record 2025 revenue of $11.478 million, up 4.5% YoY, with monitoring revenue growing 22% and gross margin improving to 76.8% from 72.8%. Operating cash flow more than doubled to $2.09 million, and the company remains debt-free with $4.45 million in cash. Management reaffirmed a 20% average annual revenue growth target over 3-5 years, though hardware revenue declined due to a large customer contract timing and a decrease in deferred revenue amortization. The new AIO partnership is expected to contribute revenue in the second half of 2026, but no numbers were given.

negative_highlights: Nelitolimod clinical update delayed to second half of 2026 due to consolidation of Phase I data, though not driven by safety concerns.
Sales and marketing expenses increased to $8 million in Q4 due to higher performance-based compensation.
positive_highlights: Q4 revenue grew 60% YoY to $13.2M and full-year revenue grew 53% to $45.2M.
Gross margin expanded from 85% in the prior year period to 87% in Q4.
Company raised $46 million via a public offering that was more than 2x oversubscribed.
summary: TriSalus Life Sciences reported Q4 FY2025 revenue of $13.2 million, a 60% year-over-year increase, and full-year revenue of $45.2 million, up 53%. The company reaffirmed its 2026 revenue guidance of $60 million to $62 million, noting that growth will be weighted towards the second half due to commercial expansion timing. Gross margin expanded to 87% in Q4 driven by manufacturing efficiencies on new products.

negative_highlights: GAAP EPS declined to -$0.32 in Q4 compared to $0.14, driven by higher other expenses including a minority equity investment mark-to-market charge.
Domestic segment revenue contracted slightly (-2%) for the full year as management pivots away from legacy subsidized consumer offerings in Southwest markets.
FY2026 outlook incorporates headwinds of approximately $5M related to high-cost funding support ending in U.S. Virgin Islands and potential additional reductions upon tower sale closing.
positive_highlights: Q4 revenue grew 2% YoY to $184.2M driven by International segment growth (+3%) and Domestic carrier services expansion.
Adjusted EBITDA expanded 8% sequentially or 8% YoY to $50.0M, reflecting successful cost management efforts in the U.S. market.
Full-year net loss narrowed significantly from a prior year loss of $26.4M to $14.9M due to improved operating performance and absence of specific tax benefits seen previously.
summary: ATN International reported Q4 FY2025 revenue of $184.2 million (up 2% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $50.0 million (up 8%), while full-year revenues remained essentially flat at $728 million against a prior loss narrowing to a net loss of $14.9 million for the year. Management provided a modestly raised FY2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance range of $190-200 million (excluding tower sale impacts) and confirmed maintenance of the quarterly dividend at $0.275 per share with no buybacks in Q4.

Q4 revenue fell to $1.9M from $5.8M a year ago and full-year 2025 revenue came in at $17.0M versus $20.2M in 2024, well below the roughly $24M previously expected; management attributed the shortfall mainly to the U.S. government shutdown delaying BARDA-linked development services revenue and new contracts, with a smaller contribution from lower Vericel product sales. Q4 gross margin was 14.9% (vs 15.5%), operating loss widened to $7.8M from $6.1M, net loss was $7.2M or $0.56 per share, and adjusted EBITDA loss widened to $6.5M from $4.9M; full-year adjusted EBITDA loss was $20.3M versus $14.8M. The company reaffirmed prior 2026 revenue guidance of $24-26M, 2027 of $32-35M and 2028 of $50-55M, assuming BARDA and Department of War support, 2026 regulatory clearance of the expanded sixfold-capacity facility, and BARDA-linked revenue only starting in Q2 2026. Cash and deposits stood at $53.6M at year-end after a $30.0M registered direct offering and $3.5M in warrant proceeds, with $21.4M used in operating activities during 2025.

negative_highlights: Q4 revenue declined year-over-year by $2.4 million ($8.4M vs $10.8M) due to lower license and milestone payments.
Full-year FY2025 revenue of $18.7M is significantly below the prior year's $26.4M, indicating a material contraction in core business performance.
Company recorded a noncash impairment charge of $3.9 million related to legacy small molecule ion channel assets.
positive_highlights: OmniUltra launch received strong initial reception with early programs already progressing; interest is high among existing partners for new discovery work.
xPloration platform generated approximately $800,000 in Q4 revenue from instrument sales and services, adding a scalable service stream to the business model.
Pipeline advancement remains robust with 25 total program progression events in FY2025, including one OmnidAb-derived program entering human clinical trials.
summary: OmniAb reported Q4 FY2025 revenue of $8.4 million (down from $10.8M in the prior year) and a net loss of $14.2 million ($0.11/share), driven by declines in license and milestone revenue partially offset by new xPloration service revenue. For full-year 2025, total revenue was $18.7 million versus guidance expectations (implied miss relative to prior year levels) with operating expenses decreasing to $87.6M due to workforce reductions but including a noncash impairment charge of $3.9M. Management provided FY2026 revenue guidance in the range of $25-30 million, which represents a significant contraction from 2024 full-year levels and reflects current partner pipeline visibility.

negative_highlights: Management explicitly lowered FY2026 revenue guidance to $109-114M, citing a one-time ~$9M managed service contribution in H1 2025 that is not expected to repeat.
Year-to-date contracted revenue numbers are running roughly 15% to 20% below last year's levels due to shorter contract durations and client conservatism regarding MFN pricing negotiations.

Q4 net income of $5M was partially driven by a one-time favorable mix; management does not anticipate gross margins remaining at the record Q4 level in FY26, expecting them to settle in the mid-60% range.
positive_highlights: Q4 revenue of $32.2M beat consensus estimates; full year FY25 adjusted EBITDA margins exceeded 20% with nearly $19M in free cash flow generated.
Gross margin expanded significantly to 74.8% in Q4, driven by a favorable solution and channel partner mix including high-margin specialty messaging.
summary: OptimizeRx reported Q4 FY2025 revenue of $32.2 million and adjusted EBITDA of $12 million, beating consensus estimates but noting softness in year-to-date contracted revenue due to a market shift away from managed services (which contributed ~$9M in H1 2025) and conservative client spending on MFN pricing adjustments. Management updated its FY2026 guidance downward for revenue ($109-114 million range, down from prior expectations of higher growth driven by the one-time managed service spike) while maintaining or slightly raising adjusted EBITDA guidance ($21-25 million). The company highlighted a gross margin expansion to 74.8% in Q4 (driven by favorable mix), net income turning positive at $0.26/share, and authorized a new $10 million share repurchase program.

negative_highlights: Full-year net loss widened to $63.5 million from $18.6 million, driven by a $37.9 million noncash warrant-liability charge and a $14.8 million impairment of the VAC intangible
Full-year operating expenses rose to $51.2 million from $31.0 million, and Q4 R&D increased $4.8 million to $8.2 million

No OpRegen data timing or regulatory detail was provided; management said Roche/Genentech regulatory strategy is not visible to Lineage, and OPC1 enrollment required a protocol amendment to broaden the patient criteria
positive_highlights: Q4 revenue rose to $6.6 million from roughly $2.9 million a year earlier, and Q4 swung to $0.9 million of net income ($0.04 per share)
Cash runway extended into Q2 2028 from prior guidance, helped by $21 million from a November ATM block trade, $5.4 million of March warrant exercises and the first $5 million Roche milestone
The islet cell initiative passed its first internal go/no-go milestone, with reproducible 0.5-liter scale achieved; Genentech opened 9 new OpRegen clinical sites in 2025 to reach 17 total locations
summary: Q4 revenue was $6.6 million versus $2.9 million in the prior-year quarter, driven by Roche milestone revenue and the new WDI research collaboration, with a net income of $0.9 million or $0.04 per share versus a $3.3 million net loss in Q4 2024. Full-year net loss widened to $63.5 million from $18.6 million, mostly on a $37.9 million noncash warrant-liability remeasurement and a $14.8 million intangible impairment. Cash of $55.8 million plus $5.4 million of March warrant proceeds extends the runway into Q2 2028, above prior guidance, though $32 million of remaining warrants at $0.91 are excluded. The company met its internal go/no-go milestone at 0.5-liter scale for its islet cell initiative and gave no updated guidance on the OpRegen trial timing or data.

negative_highlights: Prepaid revenue declined 27% year-over-year due to an exceptionally high prior period and accounting changes
Full-year net income decreased 23% primarily driven by $6M in acquisition integration costs and a higher tax rate of ~31%
Tariff expenses totaled approximately $4.0 million impacting profitability
positive_highlights: Fourth quarter revenue hit a record of $153M representing a 22% year-over-year increase
Adjusted EBITDA surged 34% to $29.4 million with gross margin expansion of 170 bps
Integrated PayTech segment grew nearly 20%, now contributing over 20% of total profitability
summary: CPI Card Group reported record fourth quarter revenue of $153 million, a 22% increase driven by the ArrowEye acquisition and organic growth in debit/credit segments. Adjusted EBITDA grew 34% to $29.4 million with margins expanding 170 bps despite tariff expenses and integration costs. Management raised full-year revenue guidance expectations citing strong execution, though they noted a slow start for prepaid business.

negative_highlights: Full-year Adjusted EBITDA remained a $7 million loss despite the Q4 inflection
Q1 2026 expected to remain loss-making, with the guided ~50% reduction still implying roughly a $6 million Adjusted EBITDA loss
No formal guidance and commentary framed as 'not formal guidance… simply transparency', limiting forward visibility; the Jet.AI merger outside date was extended
positive_highlights: Q4 Adjusted EBITDA turned positive at $6.6 million (6.0% margin), the first positive quarter since going public, improving over $13 million versus Q4 2024
Full-year gross profit up 53% and gross margin expanded to 18% in Q4 (15% FY), with margins improving sequentially each quarter
summary: flyExclusive reported Q4 FY2025 revenue of $104.3 million, up 14% year-over-year, and its first positive Adjusted EBITDA as a public company at $6.6 million (6.0% margin), an improvement of over $13 million versus Q4 2024. Full-year revenue rose 15% to $375.9 million, full-year Adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed to $7 million (an improvement of over $49 million, margin up 1,531 bps), and gross margin reached 18% in Q4. Management gave no formal guidance but said Q1 2026 will soundly exceed Q1 2025 (which had Adjusted EBITDA of -$12.5 million and management Adjusted EBITDA of -$6.4 million) with an expected ~50% reduction in that loss, that every 2026 quarter will meaningfully outperform the corresponding 2025 quarter, and that flight hours will grow more than 15% with ~20 aircraft additions. Key changes include a 14% smaller fleet flying 13% more hours, long-term debt reduced ~$84 million (36%), and pending closings of the Jet.AI merger and second Volato tranche.

negative_highlights: GAAP net loss of $0.56 per share driven by significant mark-to-market losses on CLO equity.
Net asset value (NAV) total return for the quarter was negative 9.1%.
Credit hedges acted as a drag on results, with management estimating an annualized cost of 1% to 2% of fund NAV.
positive_highlights: Fund limited losses to approximately 9% of NAV, outperforming the overall peer set which saw median returns of negative 9%.
CLO mezzanine debt tranches proved resilient and opportunistic trading contributed positively to results.
Credit hedges were increased significantly to roughly $175 million (approx. 90% of NAV) to provide protection against tail risks.
summary: Ellington Credit Company reported a GAAP net loss of $0.56 per share for Q4 FY2025, driven by significant mark-to-market losses on CLO equity tranches in a challenging market environment where the median peer return was negative 9%. The fund limited its own losses to approximately 9% of NAV through active trading and credit hedges, outperforming peers but failing to meet implied expectations for a closed-end fund. Management noted that while some mark-to-market declines reflect reversible spread widening rather than fundamental impairment, the quarter remains a miss relative to the defensive positioning expected in a distressed market.

negative_highlights: Reported Q4 net loss of $3.8M, or $0.52 per share, versus net income of $7.6M, or $1.02 per share, in 2024, driven by a $7.8M noncash pension settlement charge and a tax true-up

Minerals and Royalties operating profit expected to decrease year over year in 2026, particularly in the second half, and Utility Coal's 2026 improvement is partly offset by lower unconsolidated mining earnings at Sabine as reclamation winds down

Mississippi Lignite customer power plant entered a maintenance outage in mid-February affecting Q1 demand, and a $1.1M loss contingency tied to the December safety incident hit Contract Mining operating profit
positive_highlights: Consolidated Q4 operating profit rose 95% to $7.6M from $3.9M, with all three reportable segments improving year over year
Adjusted EBITDA up 59% to $14.3M from $9.0M, and full-year 2025 cash from operations of $50.9M versus $22.3M in 2024
Utility Coal Mining segment operating profit rose to $7.2M from $2.0M, with the segment reporting gross profit after several quarters of losses
summary: Q4 revenue rose 5% to $66.8M with gross profit up 42% to $12.0M, operating profit up 95% to $7.6M, and adjusted EBITDA up 59% to $14.3M, with all three segments improving; however, a $7.8M noncash pension settlement charge ($6.0M after tax) drove a net loss of $3.8M, or $0.52 per share, versus net income of $7.6M, or $1.02 per share, a year ago. Management expects meaningful year-over-year improvements in consolidated operating profit, net income, and EBITDA in 2026, with Utility Coal Mining operating profit up (offset by lower unconsolidated mining earnings at Sabine), Contract Mining up significantly, and Minerals and Royalties down, particularly in the second half. The Utility Coal segment returned to gross profit after multiple loss quarters on stronger Mississippi Lignite efficiency, though a mid-February customer plant outage affects Q1 demand; the pension plan was fully settled in the quarter. 2025 cash from operations was $50.9M versus $22.3M in 2024, with total liquidity of $124.2M.

negative_highlights: Asia Pacific revenue fell to $3.9M, down $1.1M YoY, with recovery dependent on public sector spending later in the year.
GAAP net income declined to $2.6M ($0.05/share) from $3.0M ($0.06/share) in the prior-year quarter.
Management cited US deals moving from Q1 into Q2 and a tough Q1 compare, with a choppy pace expected for one to two quarters.
positive_highlights: Q4 revenue of $61.2M at the top end of guidance, up 6% YoY, with Europe up 28% to $19.1M.
Adjusted EBITDA up 24% to $8.1M, margin up 189 bps to 13.2%; full-year adjusted EBITDA over $32M, up 28%.
AI-related services reached nearly 35% of Q4 revenue and ~30% for the full year, up 3x from 2024; Tango TCV exceeded $25B vs $7B prior year.
summary: ISG reported Q4 revenue of $61.2 million, up 6% YoY and at the top end of guidance, with Europe up 28% to $19.1 million and recurring revenue up 13%. Adjusted EBITDA rose 24% to $8.1 million, expanding margin by 189 bps to 13.2%, and full-year adjusted EBITDA grew 28% to over $32 million with a 13.2% margin (up 300 bps). Q1 guidance calls for revenue of $60.5-$61.5 million and adjusted EBITDA of $7.5-$8.5 million, representing continued YoY growth, though management flagged a tough Q1 compare, some US deals pushing into Q2, and a cautious macro backdrop.

negative_highlights: Voyage costs and running costs increased significantly due to fleet growth, with running costs up $4.6 million YoY, pressuring margins.

The U.S.-Iran conflict has disrupted trade through the Strait of Hormuz, with vessel arrivals down 80%, creating uncertainty over future tanker demand and potential oil price-driven demand destruction.
No explicit forward financial guidance was provided, leaving visibility limited beyond fleet delivery schedules.
positive_highlights: Q4 revenues rose 95% year-over-year to $51.1 million, driven by fleet expansion and higher Suezmax rates ($92,000/day vs $55,000/day in Q3).
Operating cash flow for 2025 was $81 million, supporting a debt-free balance sheet with cash and time deposits of $179 million at year-end (close to $198 million today).
Fleet operational utilization hit 91.8% in Q4, the best quarterly performance of 2025, with commercial off-hire days reduced 24.3% sequentially.
summary: Imperial Petroleum reported Q4 2025 revenues of $51.1 million, up 95% year-over-year, with net income of $15 million and operating income of $13.7 million (up 174% YoY). Full-year 2025 net income reached $50 million, EBITDA $71 million, and operating cash flow $81 million. Fleet expansion continued with six vessels to be delivered in 2026, bringing the total to 26 ships, funded without bank debt, and a $10 million share repurchase program was initiated. Management highlighted geopolitical tensions (U.S.-Iran conflict) that have already spiked tanker rates but could also disrupt trade and cause demand destruction.

negative_highlights: Full-year revenue fell to $147.6M from $164.9M and core FFO dropped to $0.78 from $1.01 per share
Implied 2026 core FFO guidance of $0.69-$0.76 is roughly flat versus the $0.69 2025 figure excluding $0.09 of termination income
Arch Street JV investment written down to zero and member loan reserved, with partner unable to fund a ~$16M principal prepayment
positive_highlights: Leased rate improved 600 bps YoY to over 80% and occupancy rose 500 bps to 78.7% at year end
Completed debt maturities addressed: new $215M revolver to Feb 2029 (margin cut 50 bps to SOFR+2.75%) and CMBS extended to Aug 2030
2026 scheduled expirations of only $11.4M annualized base rent versus $16.2M in 2025 and $39.4M in 2024
summary: Q4 revenue fell to $35.2M from $38.4M YoY, though core FFO rose to $0.19/share from $0.18; full-year revenue dropped to $147.6M from $164.9M and core FFO fell to $0.78 from $1.01, with 2025 including ~$0.09 of lease termination income. 2026 core FFO guidance is $0.69-$0.76, roughly flat to up versus the $0.69 2025 figure excluding termination income, with net debt/EBITDA guided to 6.5x-7.3x. The company cut its investment in the Arch Street JV to zero and recorded a member loan loss reserve after the partner could not fund a ~$16M prepayment, offset by leasing momentum (900K sq ft in 2025, 1M+ sq ft pipeline), a $600 bps YoY leased-rate gain to over 80%, and completed debt extensions to 2029-2030.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to $8.2 million in Q4 2025 from $4.9 million a year ago
Gross margin declined to 67% from 71% due to product mix and introductory international pricing
Operating expenses remained elevated at $11.4 million vs $11.3 million prior year
positive_highlights: Q4 revenue up 43% YoY to $6 million
Commercial inflection point with pipeline of 110 new systems in final sales stages
TULSA reimbursement confirmed for 2026 with Category 1 CPT codes and private payer coverage expected in H2 2026
summary: Profound Medical reported Q4 2025 revenue of $6 million, up 43% year-over-year, with gross margin at 67% versus 71% in Q4 2024 due to product mix and introductory international pricing. The net loss widened to $8.2 million from $4.9 million, with cash at $59.7 million. Management highlighted a growing sales pipeline (110 systems in final sales stages), continued reimbursement momentum with CPT Category 1 codes confirmed for 2026, and early international distribution success in Saudi Arabia and Australia. They reiterated a path to profitable growth, targeting ~$85 million annual revenue with 200 sites and 50 procedures per site, and expect high double-digit to low triple-digit revenue growth in 2026. Upcoming CAPTAIN trial data presentations are key catalysts.

negative_highlights: Q4 2025 revenue declined YoY to $8.5 million, though management attributed this to timing differences in Super Scooper deployments.
Q4 2025 reported a net loss of $15.1 million and negative adjusted EBITDA of $9.5 million due to one-time debt extinguishment losses and warrant fair value adjustments.
positive_highlights: Full year 2025 revenue increased 25% YoY to $122.8 million.
Adjusted EBITDA grew to $45.3 million for the full year 2025.
Management raised 2026 revenue guidance range to $135-$145 million and adjusted EBITDA to $55-$60 million.
summary: Full year 2025 revenue grew 25% to $122.8 million, driven by a 23% increase in core operations excluding Spanish Super Scooper return-to-service work. The company reported positive net income of $4.1 million and adjusted EBITDA of $45.3 million for the year. For 2026, management raised guidance to $135-$145 million in revenue and $55-$60 million in adjusted EBITDA, citing fleet expansion and improved utilization.

negative_highlights: Core FFO remained negative at $5.9 million, compared to a loss of $7.1 million for total FFO.
Multifamily segment NOI decreased by $1.7 million due to lower appraisals at two joint ventures and a $3.5 million impairment charge on an Oakland site.
Office NOI in Los Angeles declined due to decreased occupancy, and the Oakland office asset continues to face soft demand.
positive_highlights: Completed sale of lending division generating $31.2 million in net cash proceeds.
Office lease occupancy reached 88.5% at year-end 2025, a 680 basis point improvement over the prior year.
Multifamily occupancy increased to 88.5% in Los Angeles and 88.4% in Oakland.
summary: CMCT reported Q4 FY2025 Core FFO of negative $5.9 million and overall NOI of $10.9 million, an increase from the prior year but offset by a multifamily segment loss of $870,000 and a $3.5 million impairment charge on an Oakland development site. Management highlighted balance sheet improvements including the sale of the lending division for net cash proceeds of $31.2 million and the retirement of preferred stock to improve annual FFO by approximately $16 million. Forward guidance remains cautious due to soft demand at the Oakland office asset, though occupancy improved significantly across other segments.

negative_highlights: Q4 revenue delta versus demand growth was negatively impacted by wholesaler inventory declines
R&D expenses increased quarter-over-quarter in Q4 as the company invested heavily in pipeline development
No specific guidance provided for full-year 2026, with management stating it will be released on August earnings call
positive_highlights: LOQTORZI full-year sales doubled in 2025, reaching $40.8M versus $19.1M prior year
Q4 net revenue grew sequentially by 11% to $12.4M with strong demand growth of 15.5%
Debt principal reduced from peak of $480 million down to just $38.8 million at year-end
summary: Coherus Oncology reported Q4 FY2025 net revenue of $12.4 million (up 11% sequentially) and full-year 2025 LOQTORZI sales doubling to $40.8M from $19.1M in 2024, driven by new patient starts and guideline adoption. The company successfully reduced debt by over 90% to $38.8 million and cut headcount while maintaining a strategic focus on advancing its oncology pipeline with data readouts expected mid-2026.

negative_highlights: Q4 GAAP results included a $138.9 million non-cash goodwill impairment tied to the consumer payments segment
Consumer payments growth was modest at 8% revenue and 6% gross profit YoY
Q1 2026 growth guided below the full-year rate as client implementations slipped and prior churn annualizes, with reacceleration dependent on the second half
positive_highlights: Business payments normalized revenue rose ~41% and gross profit ~73% YoY in Q4
Supplier network grew over 65% YoY to 602,000 suppliers, adding more than 240,000 during 2025
Adjusted EBITDA margin held at roughly 41% with 43% free cash flow conversion in Q4
summary: REPAY reported Q4 revenue of $78.6 million and gross profit of $58.3 million, with normalized revenue and gross profit growth of 10% and 9% respectively (excluding 2024 political media). Adjusted EBITDA was $32.4 million at roughly 41% margin and adjusted net income was $16.8 million or $0.19 per share, while GAAP results were hit by a $138.9 million non-cash goodwill impairment in consumer payments. FY2026 guidance calls for revenue of $340-346 million (10-12% reported, ~7-9% normalized) and adjusted EBITDA of $136.5-141.5 million at ~40% margins, but Q1 growth is expected below the full-year rate due to pushed-out implementations and prior-year churn, with a second-half reacceleration assumed. Free cash flow of $13.8 million came in slightly below expectations on working capital timing, and $147 million of 0% converts were repaid at maturity in January, leaving pro forma net leverage near 2.5x.

negative_highlights: Reported net loss remained at $56 million due to significant non-cash items including $42.9 million in impairment and restructuring provisions.
Cash used in operations was still $10.6 million, though improved from $46.3 million the prior year.
The company is still navigating legal proceedings, including an arbitration case with LGI seeking to recover shares and funds.
positive_highlights: Pro forma revenue grew 80% YoY to $13.6M driven by a 1,053% increase in average revenue per paying student.
The company achieved operational profitability across all three business units (School, Academy, Resorts) for the first time in Q4 2025.
Genius Resorts generated $2.2 million in revenue in just five months of operations under the group.
summary: Genius Group reported pro forma revenue of $13.6 million for FY2025, representing an 80% year-over-year increase driven by a shift to a high-value premium model where average revenue per paying student grew 1,053% to $1,856. The company achieved operational profitability in Q4 2025 for the first time as a group and is guiding for FY2026 revenue between $20 million and $22 million (48% growth) with positive EBITDA of $1.5 million to $2 million. Management highlighted the successful integration of three business units, including Genius Resorts which generated $2.2 million in five months, and the commencement of construction for the first Genius City.

negative_highlights: Total revenue declined 4.7% to $256.9 million from $269.6 million
Free cash flow fell to $10.3 million for the year from $97.4 million, and operating cash flow to $15.9 million from $99.4 million
New powersports major unit sales fell 2.9% to 9,924 units and full-year powersports units dropped to 61,894 from 64,988
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA rose 341% to $9.7 million from $2.2 million in Q4 last year
Same-store revenue grew 6.3% and same-store gross profit rose 13.8% to $66.8 million
New unit gross margin improved to 13.2% from 10.8% and pre-owned to 14.4% from 12.3%
summary: RideNow reported Q4 2025 total revenue of $256.9 million versus $269.6 million a year earlier, with the decline driven by the wind-down of Wholesale Express, and revenue ex-Wholesale Express flat year-over-year. Adjusted EBITDA rose 341% to $9.7 million from $2.2 million, and same-store gross profit increased 13.8% to $66.8 million on a 6.3% same-store revenue gain, the second consecutive quarter of same-store revenue and unit growth. Full year 2025 revenue was $1.08 billion with adjusted EBITDA up 40.4% to $46.2 million. Management gave no explicit quantitative guidance, but expects Q1 momentum to continue and sees potential term loan refinancing in the near future; free cash flow fell to $10.3 million from $97.4 million a year earlier.

negative_highlights: FY2025 free cash flow of ~$12 million was only 20% of adjusted EBITDA, below guidance, due to working capital and inventory build
Q4 take rate was relatively lower than the prior ~18 months, with geography/vertical mix pressuring it
2026 revenue guidance includes the Lynkwell acquisition and excludes further M&A, a change from prior practice of including acquisitions
positive_highlights: FY2025 gross margin expanded to 48.2% from 45.1%, with processing margin up to ~38% from ~34%
First-ever net income of $35.5 million versus a loss a year ago; adjusted EBITDA margin 15.3%
Q4 revenue grew 34% to $119.5 million with ~30% organic growth, and installed base reached ~1.46 million devices
summary: Nayax reported FY2025 revenue of $400 million, up 28% year-over-year (24% organic), with Q4 revenue of $119.5 million up 34% and ~30% organic. FY2025 was the first-ever net income at $35.5 million (including a $10.3 million one-time gain), adjusted EBITDA of $61.1 million (15.3% margin), and gross margin expanded to 48.2% from 45.1%; recurring revenue was 72% of total. 2026 guidance is $510-520 million revenue (22-25% organic, including Lynkwell, excluding further M&A) and ~17% adjusted EBITDA margin ($85-90 million). Free cash flow was only ~$12 million (20% of adjusted EBITDA), below guidance due to working capital, with 2026 conversion guided to improve to ~40% of adjusted EBITDA.

negative_highlights: Q4 vessel growth slowed to 1% sequentially due to termination of two Southeast Asian low-ARPU fishing fleets, though growth was 8% excluding those fleets.
Full-year service revenue grew only 2% to $98.4 million, held back by $7.7 million of non-recurring U.S. Coast Guard revenue.
A new Starlink terminal access charge is expected to slightly pressure margins in the Starlink portion of the business.
positive_highlights: Q4 service revenue grew 27% year over year to $28.3 million, with adjusted EBITDA of $3.1 million versus $1.4 million in Q3.
Subscribing vessels rose 28% to more than 9,000, with the second Starlink data pool representing a 300% increase and a $45 million 18-month commitment.
Board increased the share repurchase program from $10 million to $15 million, and the company ended with $69.9 million in cash and no debt.
summary: KVH reported Q4 2025 service revenue of $28.3 million, up 27% year over year, with service gross margin flat at 34%, and delivered its strongest quarterly adjusted EBITDA of the year at $3.1 million. Full-year service revenue grew 2% to $98.4 million, or 11% excluding $7.7 million of non-recurring U.S. Coast Guard revenue, while subscribing vessels rose 28% to over 9,000. Management guided 2026 revenue to $130-145 million and adjusted EBITDA to $11-16 million, without a prior 2026 outlook to compare against. The board raised the share repurchase authorization from $10 million to $15 million, and management noted Q4 vessel growth slowed due to termination of two low-ARPU Southeast Asian fishing fleets.

negative_highlights: Virtual Sports revenue growth missed expectations due to seasonality and lag pre-World Cup, though margins expanded significantly.
Softening observed in the Brazil market during Q1 following strong Q4 performance.
UK tax changes will reduce customer GGR; while management claims margin impact is neutral on a per-revenue basis, total revenue from UK customers may decline.
positive_highlights: Interactive segment revenue grew 53% YoY with EBITDA growing 60%, marking the single highest day and weekend GGR in recent history.
Full-year company-wide EBITDA margin reached a record 42% for Q4, validating the transformation thesis to move into mid-40s margins by 2026.
Successful launch of NFL licensed Virtual Sports with BetMGM in New Jersey and Ontario serves as a proof point for North American expansion.
summary: Inspired Entertainment reported Q4 FY2025 results with revenue and EBITDA up significantly in the interactive segment (up 53% and 60%, respectively), driving a record full-year company-wide EBITDA margin of 37%. Management raised its 2026 EBITDA guidance to $112 million-$118 million, citing strong momentum from digital mix shifts and successful North American launches. The company is de-levering toward a target net leverage of 2.5-3x by year-end 2026.

negative_highlights: Adjusted net loss widened to $21M from $3M in prior quarter.
Gain on sale margin declined to 324 bps from 339 bps, with Q1 guidance of 270-300 bps.
Cash decreased by $122M from prior quarter to $337M.
positive_highlights: Origination volume of $8.0B was highest since 2022, up 23% from prior quarter.
Recapture rate reached 71% from in-house servicing platform.
Adjusted revenue up 10% YoY with expense growth under 1% for full year.
summary: loanDepot reported Q4 2025 adjusted net loss of $21 million, worse than the $3 million loss in Q3, due to lower gain on sale margin, higher MSR amortization, and higher expenses. Pull-through weighted lock volume rose 4% to $7.3 billion, and origination volume hit $8.0 billion, the highest since 2022 and up 23% sequentially. Gain on sale margin was 324 basis points at the high end of guidance but down from 339 bps. Q1 2026 guidance calls for lock volume of $7.75-8.75 billion and margin of 270-300 bps. Management emphasized market share gains, a 71% recapture rate, and investments in AI and technology to drive operating leverage.

negative_highlights: Full-year revenue declined 5% to $8.3 million
Ended the year with only $1.2 million in cash despite $7 million raised
Critical care revenue declined 19% for the full year and 24% in the fourth quarter
positive_highlights: Gross margin expanded to 68.2% in Q4, up 9.9 percentage points year-over-year
U.S. console sales increased 208% with eight units sold versus three in prior-year
Heart failure and pediatrics grew 814% year-over-year
summary: Nuwellis reported Q4 2025 revenue of $2.4 million, up 4% year-over-year and 9% sequentially, with gross margin expanding to 68.2% from 58.4%. Full-year revenue declined 5% to $8.3 million, with heart failure and pediatrics growing 814% each, offset by a 19% decline in critical care. The company ended the year with $1.2 million cash and no debt, but raised $7 million and reduced guidance on cash burn. Management is focused on operational restructuring, exiting EU markets, terminating a clinical trial, and integrating a new acquisition to drive future growth.

negative_highlights: Full-year 2025 revenue declined 9.5% and Q4 gross margin fell to 15.2% from 17.4% for the year, with hourly severance and tooling mix a ~230 bps drag
Full-year free cash flow was just $1.9 million on $19.2 million operating cash flow, down from $35 million of operating cash flow in fiscal 2024
FY2026 sales guidance is only flat to up 5%, with truck at 44% of product sales and recovery pushed to the second half of 2026
positive_highlights: Q4 revenue of $74.7 million grew 19.5% year over year and 27.8% sequentially, with adjusted EBITDA margin up 100 bps to 10.2%
Q4 operating income rose to $3.6 million (4.8% of sales) from $0.9 million (1.4%) a year earlier, and SG&A fell to 10.4% of sales from 14.4%
$63 million in 2025 business wins, 65% in new markets, with a $220 million pipeline and a target of $50 million more awards in 2026
summary: Q4 revenue of $74.7 million rose 19.5% year over year and 27.8% sequentially, helped by more than $19 million of tooling revenue offsetting continued truck softness. Gross margin fell to 15.2% (about 230 bps unfavorable from hourly severance and tooling mix), but SG&A dropped to 10.4% of sales and operating income rose to $3.6 million (4.8%) from $0.9 million, with adjusted EBITDA margin up 100 bps to 10.2%. Full-year 2025 revenue fell 9.5% on truck weakness while gross margin held at 17.4% and operating cash flow was $19.2 million. FY2026 guidance is flat to up roughly 5% in sales with 17%-19% gross margin, and management expects truck recovery in the second half of 2026 with $63 million in new 2025 wins ramping in late 2026 and 2027.

negative_highlights: Full-year net loss widened to $142.6M ($1.12/share) from $157.8M in the prior year, though GAAP loss per share narrowed.
Q4 revenue growth was attributed to variability in customer ordering patterns rather than sustained volume expansion.
No annual net revenue guidance provided; management expects sales to remain broadly in line with recent years until new indications launch.
positive_highlights: Net product revenues grew 36% YoY to $22.3M in Q4 driven by customer ordering patterns and new account activation.
Total adjusted operating expenses decreased 15% sequentially and 6% YoY, with R&D down approximately $10M from the prior quarter.
Cash balance strengthened to $261.3M at quarter-end, providing a runway into 2028 following $100M and $60M PIPE financings.
summary: ADC Therapeutics reported Q4 FY2025 net product revenues of $22.3 million, up from $16.4 million in the prior year quarter, with full-year sales of $73.6 million remaining roughly stable versus expectations. The company reduced total adjusted operating expenses by 15% sequentially and 6% year-over-year to $39.4 million for the quarter, driven by lower R&D spend. Management expressed confidence in upcoming clinical readouts for LOTIS-5 (Q2 2026) and LOTIS-7, projecting a potential peak annual U.S. revenue opportunity of $600 million to $1 billion assuming regulatory approvals.

negative_highlights: No specific revenue or earnings figures were reported; management focused entirely on forward-looking project milestones rather than current financial performance.
The company explicitly stated that oxy-combustion work streams have been suspended pending a viability evaluation, representing a significant strategic pivot away from prior technology focus.
positive_highlights: Net Power increased Project Permian Phase I net electrical output capacity from approximately 60 MW to roughly 80 MW via design restructuring.
The company secured two modular gas turbine packages with delivery targeted for early 2028, de-risking the power island supply chain.
Management confirmed site control is in place with an executed ground lease and progressing grid interconnection discussions.
summary: Net Power Inc reported Q4 FY2025 results with no specific revenue or EPS figures disclosed in the transcript; management highlighted a strategic pivot from oxy-combustion to a combined cycle gas turbine plus post-combustion carbon capture (GT+PCC) solution for Project Permian. The company raised its net electrical output target for Phase I from 60 MW to approximately 80 MW and confirmed an FID target in the second half of 2026 with commercial operations targeted for early 2029, though no specific financial guidance was updated or issued during this call.

negative_highlights: Q4 revenue fell to $125.6M from $137.7M a year ago on a lower-ASP conversion mix, with gross margin down 190 bps to 13.4% and adjusted EBITDA down to $10.4M from $13.9M
Q4 adjusted EPS declined to $0.16 from $0.21, and the quarter included a $16.6M GAAP net loss on $19.9M of noncash share-appreciation adjustments
Backlog of 1,926 railcars / $137.5M covers a smaller portion of the 4,250-unit 2026 delivery midpoint, and 2026 guidance implies deliveries up only ~3% with a second-half-weighted cadence

summary: FreightCar America reported Q4 revenue of $125.6M (down from $137.7M a year ago) on 1,172 deliveries, with gross margin of 13.4% versus 15.3%, adjusted EBITDA of $10.4M versus $13.9M, and adjusted EPS of $0.16 versus $0.21. FY2025 revenue was $501M on 4,125 units, with gross margin up 260 bps, adjusted EBITDA of $44.8M and free cash flow of $31.4M (up 44.8%), ending with $64.3M cash. Guidance for 2026 is revenue of $500-550M, deliveries of 4,000-4,500 and adjusted EBITDA of $41-50M, with a stronger second-half cadence; the company noted industry deliveries fell to ~31,000 units from 42,000 while it gained ~300 bps of share. The key negative change was Q4 margin and EBITDA contraction on a heavier conversion/retrofit mix, partly offset by productivity gains and the Cardium aftermarket acquisition.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to $7.8 million for Q4 due to increased operating expenses, legal costs related to litigation, and IPO transition fees.
SG&A expenses surged from $9.1M in the prior year quarter to $16.3M, driven by headcount expansion and public company overhead.
Gross margin contracted slightly sequentially (76.5% full-year vs 77.0% prior year) as ASPs faced slight pressure.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 65% year-over-year driven by accelerated adoption among new surgeons (134 core/contender surgeons, up 61%).
Gross margin held steady at 76.7%, demonstrating pricing power and cost discipline despite rapid growth.
New product launches including the InSet I-135RFX Humeral Stem and N-22 Humeral Head are in limited market release with positive early feedback.
summary: Shoulder Innovations reported Q4 FY2025 revenue of $14.4 million (up 65% YoY) and full-year revenue of $47.3 million (up 50%). Gross margins remained strong at 76.7% for the quarter, though SG&A expenses increased significantly due to IPO-related costs and headcount expansion in the commercial organization. Management initiated FY2026 guidance of $62-$65 million revenue.

negative_highlights: Full-year gross margin contracted to just over 58% from 60% in 2024 due to ASP pressure and incremental costs from seven new biomarkers.
Adjusted EBITDA loss widened slightly to $9.8 million as the company increased operating expenses by 13% to fund commercial expansion and R&D.
ASP for new biomarkers (T-cell and RA33) faced headwinds, requiring revenue cycle management efforts to recover from an accrual of mid-$70s toward a target of roughly $80.

Volume growth accelerated significantly in the second half of the year, bucking typical seasonality to reach Q4's highest volume ever at 137,000 tests.
Pharma Services business scaled rapidly from roughly $100,000 in 2024 to $1.7 million in revenue in 2025 with over $4 million in backlog.
summary: Exagen reported full-year 2025 revenue of $66.6 million, a near 20% increase driven by over 11% volume growth and a 7% rise in trailing twelve-month ASP to approximately $441. The company provided full-year 2026 guidance of $70-$73 million, maintaining the prior revenue range while adjusting the breakeven Adjusted EBITDA threshold upward to roughly $80 million due to strategic investments in commercial expansion and R&D.

negative_highlights: Commission income declined year-over-year from $14.1 million to $12.4 million due to portfolio realignment.
Adjusted EBITDA remained a loss of $1.6 million, up from a loss of $0.3 million in the prior year.
Salaries and wages increased significantly to $10.3 million, driven largely by non-cash share-based compensation.

Stockholders' equity increased $3.4 million (114%) to $6.4 million.
Commission income generated more than $12 million from the remaining insurance and insurtech platform.
summary: Reliance Global Group reported a net loss of $9.1 million for the year ended December 31, 2025, compared to a loss of $9.1 million in 2024 (text states 'Net loss improved by $2 million-$7 million' but cites $9.1M for both years, implying stability or slight improvement masked by divestitures). Commission income decreased to $12.4 million from $14.1 million due to the strategic sale of subsidiaries including Fortman Insurance Services, Employee Benefits Solutions, and U.S. Benefits Alliance. The company strengthened its balance sheet with unrestricted cash increasing 250% to $1.3 million and stockholders' equity rising 114% to $6.4 million.

negative_highlights: Management lowered Payables organic growth expectations for FY2026 to an 8%-10% range citing headwinds from lower interest rates and card network changes.

Treasury Solutions gross margins contracted approximately 170 basis points YoY as high-margin CFTPay growth was offset by the addition of lower-margin Passport and Priority Tech Ventures revenue.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EPS increased $0.52 or 102% year-over-year to $1.03 driven by significant operating leverage in Payables (EBITDA up 61%) and Treasury Solutions.
Q4 revenue grew 9% YoY with adjusted gross profit margins expanding 360 basis points to 40.6%, reflecting the accretive impact of acquisitions.
The company successfully remediated a material weakness in internal controls over financial reporting as of December 31, 2025.
summary: Priority Technology Holdings reported Q4 FY2025 revenue of $247.1 million (up 9% YoY) and adjusted EPS of $1.03 (up 102% YoY). Management provided full-year 2026 guidance for top-line growth in the range of 6%-9%, with a specific note that Payables organic growth expectations were lowered to an 8%-10% range due to market headwinds including lower interest rates. While Q4 results showed strong margin expansion and EBITDA beats, management explicitly moderated forward outlooks for key segments.

positive_highlights: Secured $27 million in U.S. government development funding during 2025

summary: SIGA reported full-year 2025 product revenues of approximately $88 million, with $53 million from oral TPOXX and $26 million from IV TPOXX under the BARDA 19C contract, plus $6 million international sales. Pretax operating income was about $24 million, net income about $23 million, and diluted EPS $0.32. The company ended 2025 with $155 million cash and no debt, and has $26 million of outstanding U.S. government orders expected to deliver in 2026. Management remains engaged with the U.S. government but gave no timing on a new procurement contract, while the EMA CHMP is expected to issue a context in March, with management expecting the smallpox indication maintained and the mpox indication withdrawn.

negative_highlights: The company remains unprofitable on a full-year basis and guided Q1 FY2026 to a net loss of $8–$10.1 million.
Full-year comps were only +0.3%, as the strong Q4 followed weakness in the first half of fiscal 2025.
Sales per square foot ended FY2025 at roughly $260, still well below historical levels, and management noted macro pressure could make double-digit comps harder to sustain.
positive_highlights: Gross margin expanded 720 basis points to 33.2% of net sales, driven by a 470 basis point product margin improvement from higher initial markups and lower markdowns.
Comparable net sales accelerated through Q4 to +10.1% and February FY2026 comps reached +20.1%, with March trending even stronger.
SG&A fell $3.5 million YoY to $48.9 million (31.5% of net sales), and the company ended FY2025 with $87.8 million in total liquidity, no debt, and inventories 10.8% lower.
summary: Tilly's reported Q4 FY2025 total net sales of $155.1 million, up 5.3% YoY, with comparable net sales up 10.1% and gross margin expanding 720 basis points to 33.2%. Net income improved to $2.9 million or $0.10 per diluted share, versus a net loss of $13.7 million or $0.45 per share a year ago, marking the company's first profitable fourth quarter since fiscal 2021. Management provided Q1 FY2026 guidance for total net sales of $119–$125 million (comps +16% to +22%), product margin improvement of 310–330 basis points, SG&A of $44–$45 million, and a net loss of $8–$10.1 million or $0.27–$0.34 per share. February comps rose 20.1% and March is off to an even stronger start; the company expects further top- and bottom-line improvement in each quarter of FY2026 but did not provide annual guidance, noting it would take roughly an 8–9% annualized comp to return to full-year profitability.

negative_highlights: Q1 FY2026 guidance implies a net loss of $8M-$10.1M and a loss per share of $0.27-$0.34, with no annual guidance provided
SG&A remains elevated at 31.5% of net sales and the company is not yet profitable on an annualized basis, needing ~8-9% comps to reach full-year profitability
Total capital expenditures and new store openings (4-6) remain modest, and underlying macro pressure on discretionary spending could challenge sustaining double-digit comps
positive_highlights: Q4 comps accelerated to +10.1%, with monthly comps rising from +1% in August to +12.4% in January and +20.1% in February

summary: Tilly's reported Q4 FY2025 total net sales of $155.1M, up 5.3% YoY with comparable net sales up 10.1%, and swung to net income of $2.9M ($0.10 per diluted share) from a net loss of $13.7M ($0.45 per share) last year, the first profitable Q4 since fiscal 2021. Gross margin expanded 720 bps to 33.2% and operating income was $2.6M (1.7% of net sales) versus an operating loss of $14.1M last year. Q1 FY2026 guidance calls for total net sales of $119M to $125M (comps up 16% to 22%), product margin improvement of 310-330 bps, but a net loss of $8M to $10.1M; the company did not provide annual guidance, noting ~8-9% annualized comp would be needed to be profitable for the full year. Momentum continued with a 20.1% comp in February and a stronger start to March, while the company plans to open 4-6 new stores in FY2026 after 21 closures in FY2025.

negative_highlights: Net loss from loan charge-offs and REO activities was $3.7M in FY2025, attributed to a couple of large legacy loan write-downs.

The company issued its first rated unsecured debt offering of $500M to reduce reliance on note weakness in-term warehouse lines.
summary: Velocity Financial reported a strong Q4 FY2025 with core net income of $36.3M ($0.93/share) and loan production of $634M, up 12.5% YoY. The company achieved record levels in originations ($2.7B for the year), portfolio growth (28%), and pretax ROE (26%). A transformative NPL sale in Q4 contributed significantly to earnings while freeing working capital. Management raised the full-year outlook, citing healthy markets, stable credit, and robust securitization demand.

New $150M Capital One warehouse line and $900M prime forward-flow commitment ($50M/month from a large credit union); Generation 9 AI credit model raised approvals 11% and fundings about 8.4%
summary: Q4 revenue rose to $109.44M from $105.3M, pretax earnings were $7.2M versus $7.4M, net income $5.0M versus $5.1M, and diluted EPS was flat at $0.21; full-year revenue grew 10% to $434M with EPS of $0.80 versus $0.79. Full-year pretax income of $28M was essentially flat versus $27.4M, but ex-fair-value-marks pretax income rose to $21.5M from $6.4M as 2025 carried no Q4 marks versus $5M a year earlier. Full-year originations of $1.638B were slightly below 2024's $1.682B with portfolio growth of 8.24%, and management gave no formal numeric guidance, describing 2026 qualitatively as looking 'very, very good' on planned portfolio growth, margin improvement, and runoff of the underperforming 2022-2023 vintages to de minimis by year-end. Credit was stable—total delinquency 14.77% versus 14.85% and net charge-offs 7.76% versus 7.62%—while recoveries of 28-30% remained well below the low-40s target.

positive_highlights: Non-GAAP net income per diluted share of $0.05 versus a $0.22 loss in Q4 last year; first positive non-GAAP net income and free cash flow in over twelve years

summary: Q4 revenue was $8.9M, up 3% YoY from $8.7M, with subscription revenue up 6% to $5.3M including $1.4M of IP license fees from two new agreements. Management guided to a Q1 free cash flow loss of $1-2M and expects significant ARR growth in 2026 led by secure gift cards, with no formal revenue guidance and no Q&A due to a technical failure.

summary: CuriosityStream reported Q4 FY2025 revenue of $19.2M (up 36% YoY) and full-year revenue of $71.7M (up 40%), with adjusted free cash flow reaching $4.3M in the quarter ($13.9M for the year).
