Debt reduction: ~$23 million paid down at Benchmark since April 2024 and ~$16 million at Deflecto since October 2024, with parent-level debt at zero
summary: Acacia reported Q4 revenue of $50.1 million, up 3% YoY, with total company adjusted EBITDA of $17.4 million and operated segment adjusted EBITDA (including IP) of $22.4 million; full-year revenue was a record $285.2 million (up 133% YoY) with adjusted EBITDA of $77.9 million, aided by a partial year of Deflecto and $78.4 million of IP licensing revenue. GAAP net income was $3.4 million ($0.04/share) versus a $13.4 million loss a year ago, boosted by a one-time IP settlement against costs incurred in prior periods. No formal forward guidance was given, but management cited green shoots in Class 8 truck orders (December-February up 23%, 25%, 156%) and an expected tariff relief benefit in 2026, while Deflecto remained under cyclical and tariff pressure and a buyback stays constrained by tax-related limits into next year.

negative_highlights: Q4 2025 included a one-time restructuring charge.
ECO business currently services-based with limited gross margin contribution.
Guidance includes a speculative portion per CFO comments.
positive_highlights: Full-year revenue up 19% YoY to $70.4 million; gross margin expanded to 64%.
Signed three CDMO agreements and first commercial contract for ECOsynthesis siRNA.
Raised 2026 revenue guidance to $72-76 million.
summary: Codexis reported full-year 2025 revenue of $70.4 million, up from $59.3 million in 2024, with product gross margin expanding to 64% from 56%. The company signed three CDMO agreements with Bachem, Nitto Avecia, and Axolabs, and announced its first contract for fully enzymatic siRNA supply (low 7-figure) with an emerging biotech. Management provided 2026 revenue guidance of $72-76 million and expects current cash to fund operations through 2027. A one-time restructuring charge was taken in Q4, and the company expects to sign another licensing-type deal in 2026.

negative_highlights: Q4 revenue declined 5.2% to $154.8M and adjusted net loss widened to $0.18 per share from $0.15
reduce exposure note Systems revenue fell 22.5% YoY and swung to a $1.4M adjusted operating loss from $0.9M profit
Full-year adjusted EBITDA fell to $17.8M from $23.2M with margin down 50 bps to 2.7%
positive_highlights: Adjusted gross margin of 10.3% rose 190 bps YoY despite the demand downturn
Global Electrical Systems revenue grew 12.7% YoY to $49.7M with adjusted operating income up $3.9M YoY
Full-year free cash flow of ~$33.4M exceeded guidance and reduced net debt by $35.8M, lowering leverage to 4.1x from 4.7x
summary: Q4 revenue fell 5.2% YoY to $154.8M while adjusted EBITDA rose to $2.3M (1.5% margin, up 90 bps) from $0.9M; full-year revenue dropped to $649M from $723.4M and adjusted EBITDA fell to $17.8M (2.7% margin, down 50 bps). The quarter produced an adjusted net loss of $0.18 per share versus $0.15 a year ago, and Trim Systems revenue fell 22.5% with a $1.4M operating loss. Full-year free cash flow of about $33.4M beat guidance and cut net debt by $35.8M to bring leverage to 4.1x from 4.7x. 2026 guidance calls for revenue of $660-700M (up ~5% at midpoint) and adjusted EBITDA of $24-30M (up ~50% at midpoint), with Electrical Systems expected to grow more than 10% on the Zoox ramp in 2H26.

negative_highlights: Vessel operating expenses surged 94% year-over-year due to the integration of the SSI fleet and transfer costs.
Charter-in cost per day increased 39% YoY to $19,100 as market rates rose for new vessels.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA grew 22% year-over-year to $28.7 million, supported by a 26% increase in shipping days.
TCE rates averaged 19% above prevailing market indices for Panamax, Supramax, and Handysize vessels.
Management expects approximately $3 million of incremental EBITDA from new terminal operations (Lake Charles, Tampa) coming online throughout 2026.
summary: Pangaea Logistics Solutions reported Q4 FY2025 Adjusted EBITDA of $28.7 million (up 22% YoY) and GAAP net income of $11.9 million ($0.19/share), driven by a 26% increase in shipping days to 3,000+ total days despite higher charter-in costs due to market rate increases. Management raised full-year EBITDA guidance expectations for the integrated logistics platform (anticipating ~$3M incremental from new terminals) and reaffirmed priorities of fleet renewal and shareholder returns via dividends ($16.3M paid in 2025) and buybacks (~600k shares).

negative_highlights: Total net revenues fell to $18.2 million from $34.3 million, and fresh packed lemon volume dropped to about 681,000 cartons from about 1,147,000 cartons a year earlier
Adjusted EPS swung to a $0.48 loss from a $0.14 loss, and adjusted EBITDA worsened to a $7.7 million loss from a $2.3 million loss
positive_highlights: Total costs and expenses fell 27% year over year to $28.8 million from $39.7 million, largely from eliminating citrus sales and marketing costs after the Sunkist transition
Fresh utilization improved in Q1, with a higher percentage of standard-grade fruit sold fresh rather than juiced
Roughly $10 million in annualized SG&A savings expected for FY2026, and full-year lemon and avocado volume guidance was reiterated
summary: Q1 FY2026 total net revenues were $18.2 million versus $34.3 million a year earlier, with agribusiness revenue of $16.8 million versus $32.9 million, driven by the shift in sales cadence under the Sunkist partnership plus exits from the brokerage and farm management businesses. The quarter swung to a net loss of $9.6 million ($0.53 per diluted share GAAP, $0.48 adjusted) from a $3.2 million loss ($0.18 diluted) a year earlier, and adjusted EBITDA deteriorated to a $7.7 million loss from a $2.3 million loss, absorbing $2.5 million of specific items (packing house repairs, Chilean shutdown costs, FX on Chilean receivables). Full-year FY2026 volume guidance was reiterated at 4.0-4.5 million fresh lemon cartons and 5.0-6.0 million pounds of avocados, with roughly $10 million of annualized SG&A savings expected and management flagging Q2 improvement and the strongest results in Q3/Q4. Long-term debt rose to $89.9 million from $72.5 million at fiscal year-end, with net debt of $88.0 million against $1.3 million of cash.

negative_highlights: Q4 underperformed prior expectations, with Control Devices note weakness in ~$2M, incremental tariffs of $1.2M, and incremental quality/warranty costs of ~$3.3M
2026 midpoint EBITDA guidance of $22.5M is below 2025's $28.6M, with Q1 expected at roughly breakeven and a $6.7M incentive compensation and wage headwind
SmartTube Tachograph sales are expected to decline ~$12M in 2026, and customer price reductions are expected to offset FX tailwinds and tariff recoveries
positive_highlights: MirrorEye sales reached $111M in 2025, up $45M or ~69%, and are guided to at least $160M (~45% growth) in 2026
Stoneridge Brazil sales grew ~30% ($15M) with record OEM sales of $26.7M, roughly double prior year, and adjusted operating income up $4.6M (660 bps)
Full-year free cash flow of ~$19M driven by an $18.7M inventory reduction, with material costs down 80 bps and quality costs down $6.6M
summary: Q4 results underperformed prior expectations: Control Devices, since divested, missed by ~$2M on FX and tariffs, tariffs added an incremental $1.2M versus expectations, and quality-related costs were $3.3M above plan on legacy warranty settlements. Full-year 2025 adjusted EBITDA was $28.6M (3.3% of sales), down 60 bps versus the prior year, as weighted average end markets fell ~7% versus initial expectations of roughly flat. 2026 guidance assumes flat OEM end markets with revenue growth of ~4.2% to ~$637M, driven by MirrorEye growing ~45% to at least $160M, partly offset by a ~$12M SmartTube decline; midpoint EBITDA guidance of $22.5M implies a step down from 2025, with Q1 roughly breakeven. Management cited $5M of structural cost savings, improving second-half order signals, and a 2027 revenue target of at least $715M and EBITDA of at least $44M.

negative_highlights: Q1 2026 US RUCONEST revenue growth expected to decline 7-9% YoY from inventory drawdowns, with only mid-single-digit full-year RUCONEST growth assumed
FDA issued a complete response letter in January 2026 for the Joenja pediatric APDS label expansion, and US pediatric revenues are excluded from 2026 guidance
Q4 2025 US RUCONEST volume growth was only 2% as new HAE therapies began causing patient trialing
positive_highlights: Full-year 2025 total revenues grew 27% to EUR 376.1 million, with Joenja growing 53% in Q4 to EUR 19.8 million
Adjusted operating profit swung to EUR 36.4 million in 2025 from a EUR 8.6 million loss in 2024, with operating cash flow of EUR 54.7 million
US identified APDS patients increased by 40 in 2025, more than double the 18-patient increase in 2024
summary: Pharming reported Q4 2025 total revenues of EUR 106.5 million, up 15% YoY, with full-year revenues up 27% to EUR 376.1 million; RUCONEST grew 9% in Q4 and 26% for the year, while Joenja grew 53% in Q4 to EUR 19.8 million and 29% for the year. FY2025 adjusted operating profit was EUR 36.4 million versus a EUR 8.6 million loss in 2024, operating cash flow reached EUR 54.7 million, and cash rose to EUR 181.1 million despite the EUR 68 million Abliva acquisition. Management reaffirmed 2026 revenue guidance of EUR 405-425 million (8-13% growth) but flagged Q1 2026 US RUCONEST revenue growth of negative 7-9% from inventory drawdowns, and 2026 guidance excludes any US pediatric Joenja revenues pending an FDA Type A meeting after a January complete response letter.

negative_highlights: Q4 adjusted EPS was a loss of CAD 0.14 due to a $13 million life-to-date cost adjustment on Fargo and wet weather in Australia.
Fargo project required a third retroactive cost adjustment, increasing total costs by ~$50 million gross; only ~85% complete.
EBITDA margin was 23%, down approximately 7% from the run-rate of around 30% due to the same factors.
positive_highlights: Australia Q4 revenue was a record AUD 176 million despite wet weather; full-year Australian revenue up 17%.
Free cash flow of CAD 57 million in Q4, and CAD 103 million in H2 2025, supports 2026 guidance.
Backlog is approximately CAD 3.9 billion, with CAD 1.2 billion secured for 2026; bid pipeline of CAD 12.6 billion, including CAD 4.6 billion in active tenders.
summary: Q4 2025 revenue was CAD 344 million, with adjusted EPS a loss of CAD 0.14, impacted by a $13 million life-to-date cost adjustment on the Fargo project and wet weather in Australia. Excluding these items, gross margin was ~15%, with Q4 EBITDA of CAD 78 million. Full-year 2025 combined revenue was CAD 1.5 billion, up 10% year-over-year. Guidance for 2026 is unchanged: combined revenue of CAD 1.6 billion, adjusted EBITDA of CAD 400 million, and free cash flow of CAD 120 million, excluding any material new wins. The IMC acquisition is delayed to Q2 2026 due to regulatory review but is expected to close with retroactive earnings to January 1.

negative_highlights: Gross margin contracted 30 bps YoY in Q4 and full-year margin fell to 62.3% on higher material, packaging, and tariff costs
PST business declined 30% YoY in Q4 on milestone timing, and guidance assumes PST stays at historical levels
Guidance flags geopolitical risk from Middle East events and first-half 2026 lapping a prefill inventory build in a key EU market
positive_highlights: Q4 revenue of $10.9M grew 23% YoY, marking a third straight quarter above 20% growth
International Core grew 71% in Q4, lifting European SCIg share from ~10% in 2024 to 20% in 2025
Full-year adjusted EBITDA of $0.6M, a 124% improvement, with positive cash flow from operations for the year
summary: KORU reported Q4 2025 revenue of $10.9M, up 23% YoY, its third consecutive quarter above 20% growth, with full-year revenue of $41.1M (+22%). Domestic Core grew 18% and International Core 71% in Q4, while PST fell 30% on milestone timing; gross margin slipped 30 bps YoY and full-year adjusted EBITDA turned positive at $0.6M (+124%). Management initiated 2026 guidance of $47.5-50M (15-22% growth), 61-63% gross margin, and positive adjusted EBITDA and cash flow, with a noted H2 revenue ramp and some geopolitical risk baked in. CEO Linda Tharby announced her retirement effective June 30, with CCO Adam Kalbermatten named successor.

negative_highlights: Q4 adjusted EBITDA margin contracted 50 bps YoY to 42.6%, with FY2026 guidance implying about 190 bps of further margin decline to roughly 43.5%
Medical practice solutions monthly active users fell to 220,000 from 238,000 YoY, and paying users were flat at 196,000, with segment revenue growing only 6%
Residency Journey student base remains 21% below 2024 levels, and Q4 revenue growth of 8% was below the full-year 12% pace
positive_highlights: FY2025 revenue grew 12% YoY to BRL 3.697 billion and adjusted EBITDA rose over 50% YoY to BRL 1.680 billion, meeting/exceeding guidance for a seventh consecutive year
FY2025 adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 130 bps to 45.4% and net income rose 18% to BRL 768.4 million, with EPS up 19% to BRL 8.32
Undergrad gross margin hit a record 63.9% and continuing education gross margin expanded 363 bps, while B2B revenue in that segment grew 48%
summary: Afya reported FY2025 revenue of BRL 3.697 billion, up 12% YoY, adjusted EBITDA of BRL 1.680 billion (margin 45.4%, +130 bps), and net income of BRL 768.4 million (+18%) with EPS of BRL 8.32 (+19%), meeting the guidance midpoint. Q4 revenue rose 8% to BRL 913 million, but Q4 adjusted EBITDA margin fell 50 bps to 42.6% as investments began. FY2026 guidance of BRL 3.950-4.100 billion revenue and BRL 1.700-1.800 billion adjusted EBITDA implies a margin around 43.5%, roughly 190 bps below 2025, driven by ramp-up spending in continuing education and medical practice solutions plus segment mix; the company declared a BRL 307.4 million dividend (BRL 3.45/share, 40% of net income).

negative_highlights: Q4 revenue was negatively impacted by a labor strike in British Columbia, estimated to reduce sales by approximately $2.5 million.
International export shipments from Germany were delayed into Q1 due to regulatory uncertainty and inventory adjustments at customer sites.
Legacy produce operations saw a 21% decline in sales compared to the prior year quarter.
positive_highlights: Consolidated net sales increased 9% YoY to $49.6 million, driven by a 384% increase in international medicinal exports from Canada.
Canadian cannabis gross margin expanded significantly to 43%, up from the prior year's negative impact of impairment charges.
Company achieved record levels for profitability ($21M net income full-year), cash flow ($58M), and adjusted EBITDA ($50M) in FY2025.
summary: Village Farms reported Q4 FY2025 consolidated net sales of $49.6 million (up 9% YoY) and record profitability with net income from continuing operations of $2.3 million ($0.02/share). The quarter was impacted by a labor strike in British Columbia reducing revenue by approximately $2.5 million, but gross margins expanded to 43%, driven by higher-margin international exports which grew nearly fourfold year-over-year. Management raised full-year guidance expectations for the cannabis business following record performance and confirmed capacity expansion projects remain on track.

negative_highlights: Total Q4 revenue declined 4% year-over-year to $100 million, driven by a $24 million drop in noncore project revenue
2026 guidance anticipates a slower start due to heavy rainfall in California and cold weather in Texas, plus slower ramp-up on new contracts
Q4 net loss of $3 million, though improved by $37 million from the prior-year loss
positive_highlights: Consolidated gross margin improved to 10% in Q4 from negative 20% in Q4 2024, a $31 million swing
Full-year adjusted EBITDA of $5 million, a $66 million improvement from negative $61 million in 2024
Backlog of $793 million with book-to-burn of 1.4x in Q4, plus $128 million in new 2026 awards and $234 million pending
summary: Shimmick reported Q4 FY2025 total revenue of $100 million, down from $104 million, but Shimmick project revenue rose 4% to $84 million and consolidated gross margin swung to 10% from negative 20% a year ago. Full-year revenue was $493 million, up 3%, with adjusted EBITDA of $5 million versus negative $61 million in 2024. The company issued 2026 guidance of 12-22% revenue growth (to $550-600 million) and adjusted EBITDA of $15-30 million (200-500% growth), while noting weather-related delays in California and Texas. Management highlighted $793 million in backlog, $128 million in new 2026 awards, and $234 million in pending awards.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to $6.4 million from $6.2 million in 2024, including approximately $131,000 in one-time legal expenses.
Inventory grew 25% year-over-year, reflecting preparation for anticipated surge demand rather than slower turnover.
CEO transition underway with a formal search process initiated to identify the next leader.
positive_highlights: Full-year revenue increased 20% to approximately $2.2 million compared with $1.86 million in 2024.
Gross margin improved significantly to 62.5% from 54.1% in 2024, driven by improved product mix and e-commerce channels.
Legal dispute with Leafotech has been resolved satisfactorily, dismissing all litigation.
summary: SenesTech reported full-year 2025 revenue of approximately $2.2 million, representing a 20% increase year-over-year, with gross margin expanding to 62.5%. The company ended the year with $8.6 million in cash and short-term investments. Management noted that excluding a one-time transition effect related to directly managing Amazon sales, full-year revenue growth would have been closer to 30%, indicating strong underlying performance.

negative_highlights: Average realized RIN price decreased approximately 29% year-over-year from $3.28 to $2.33.
Operating profit declined significantly by $15.2 million compared to the prior year.
Recorded impairment losses of $3.2 million for the Blue Granite development project where the local utility ceased accepting RNG.
positive_highlights: RNG production grew 31.8% at the Pico facility due to increased feedstock inlet averages of approximately 458,000 gallons per day.
Commissioning of the second RNG processing facility at the Apex landfill contributed an additional 7.8% to total RNG production.
Successfully completed a $200 million senior credit facility with HASI in March 2026 to restructure debt and fund development.
summary: Full year 2025 revenue was $176.4 million, flat compared to the prior year, driven by a 29% decline in average realized RIN prices ($2.33 vs $3.28) and lower renewable electricity production. Adjusted EBITDA decreased 16.5% to $35.6 million due to higher operating expenses and impairment losses of $3.2 million related to the Blue Granite project. Management provided 2026 revenue guidance for RNG between $175 million and $190 million, citing potential RIN price volatility as a key variable.

negative_highlights: Two Arizona loans to the same sponsor were classified as new nonaccruals during the quarter
Liquidity of roughly $50 million is described as insufficient relative to the $616 million pipeline, constraining capital deployment
$37.3 million of early prepayments after quarter-end included full repayment of loan number one and loan number 27, with timing of future repayments acknowledged as difficult to forecast
positive_highlights: Pipeline expanded to $616 million from $415 million in the prior quarter, with the company targeting net portfolio growth in 2026
Only 9% of the portfolio is exposed to further prime rate declines, with a hypothetical 100 bps cut estimated to reduce net investment income by just $14,000
summary: Net interest income rose 4% QoQ to $14.2 million, aided by a $1.7 million collection of past-due interest on loan number nine, which was offset by two 25 bps prime rate cuts in Q4. Distributable earnings were $0.44 per basic share for the quarter and $1.92 for the year, while book value stood at $14.60 and leverage ticked down to 32% from 33%. Management said it is targeting net portfolio growth for 2026, with the pipeline rising to $616 million from $415 million last quarter, but flagged roughly $50 million of liquidity against that pipeline and uncertainty over prepayments; two Arizona loans tied to the same sponsor were placed on nonaccrual. The dividend payout ratio guidance of 90% to 100% of basic distributable earnings for 2026 was maintained.

negative_highlights: Revenue fell to $6.2 million from $6.7 million a year ago, and full-year FY2025 revenue declined $5.1 million to $21.5 million
IFCO gross margin will be below the company's 30% target margin
Management expects 2026 cash usage of $14-$16 million and near-term gross margin variability during program ramps
positive_highlights: Non-GAAP gross margin expanded to 25.6% from negative 5.2% in Q4 2024, with GAAP gross margin at 18.1% versus negative 14.9%
Q4 revenue of $6.2 million exceeded the previously announced guidance range
Signed a multiyear exclusive IFCO BLE smart label agreement, with capacity scaling toward 100 million units per year and IFCO committing CapEx and volumes
summary: Identiv reported Q4 FY2025 revenue of $6.2 million, above its guidance range but down from $6.7 million a year earlier on the intentional exit of lower-margin business. Non-GAAP gross margin expanded to 25.6% from negative 5.2% a year ago after completing the Singapore shutdown and consolidating production in Thailand, while GAAP net loss narrowed to $3.7 million ($0.16/share) and non-GAAP adjusted EBITDA loss improved to $2.5 million from $4.5 million. Q1 2026 revenue is guided to $6.7-$7.2 million, up 26%-35% YoY, though management flagged near-term gross margin variability from ramping IFCO and a new customer, plus expected 2026 cash usage of $14-$16 million. The quarter's key change was the newly signed multiyear exclusive IFCO BLE smart label agreement with capacity scaling toward 100 million units per year.

negative_highlights: Suspended dividend to save $20-25 million annually, reflecting market not crediting the payout
Northeast Flat Top area has six wells with anomalous water inflows; no new drilling there in 2026
High cost of capital (10%+ interest) on term loan, with debt reduction as a priority
positive_highlights: Quarter-to-date 2026 production averaging over 46,000 BOE/d, roughly 10% above the midpoint of guidance
Capital budget ~50% lower than 2025, with estimated 65% increase in production per dollar invested
More than 2,600 total drilling locations across stacked formations, with over 100 rig-years of inventory
summary: HighPeak Energy's Q4 2025 earnings release focuses on a conservative 2026 plan prioritizing balance sheet strength and free cash flow over production growth. The company has suspended its dividend (saving $20-25 million annually) and reduced its 2026 capital budget by nearly 50% year-over-year, with early 2026 production of over 46,000 BOE/d running about 10% above the midpoint of guidance. Management has expanded hedging and plans to pay down debt aggressively, especially with stronger oil prices, but also highlights six wells with anomalous water inflows in the Northeast Flat Top area, leading to no new drilling there in 2026.

negative_highlights: Net sales declined 3.3% YoY to $56.6M and GAAP EPS swung to a $0.32 loss from $0.01, with non-GAAP EPS falling to $0.12 from $0.21
Gross margin contracted 370 bps to 41%, including $1.7M of IEEPA tariffs and a $1.2M aiming solutions inventory reserve
Shooting sports net sales fell 15% on aiming solutions softness; UST brand is being divested with a $3.4M non-cash impairment
positive_highlights: Outdoor lifestyle net sales grew 5.4% YoY to $35.3M, led by BOG and MEAT! Your Maker, with POS up 5% for a third straight favorable quarter
New products represented over 26% of quarterly net sales; Caldwell grew on the Claycopter platform, and ScoreTracker Live is set for April rollout
Debt-free with $10.4M cash, $9.9M Q3 operating cash inflow, and inventory reduced $13.8M sequentially to $110.2M
summary: Q3 FY2026 net sales were $56.6M, down 3.3% YoY but above expectations, with outdoor lifestyle up 5.4% to $35.3M and shooting sports down 15% on aiming solutions weakness. GAAP EPS was a loss of $0.32 (including a $3.4M UST impairment and $1.2M inventory reserve) versus $0.01 last year, while non-GAAP EPS fell to $0.12 from $0.21. Gross margin contracted 370 bps to 41% on new IEEPA tariffs and the reserve, and adjusted EBITDA fell to $3.3M from $4.7M. Management reiterated full-year net sales guidance of $191-193M, gross margin of 42-43%, and adjusted EBITDA of 4-4.5% of net sales, while lowering CapEx by $500K.

negative_highlights: Net sales declined to $48.0 million from $52.3 million, with Bedding down ~5% and Upholstery down ~12%
Gross margin contracted to 11.1% from 12.1%, and adjusted EBITDA worsened to -$2.2 million from -$457,000 a year ago
Adjusted loss from operations widened to $3.1 million from $1.6 million in the prior-year period
positive_highlights: Net loss improved sequentially about 20% from Q2 and roughly 17% versus the prior-year $4.1 million loss
Completed all restructuring and integration initiatives in Q3, generating over $20 million in annualized cost savings
Free cash flow improved to -$1 million from -$10.1 million in the prior-year period, with total liquidity of $27.7 million
summary: Culp reported Q3 FY2026 net sales of $48.0 million, down from $52.3 million a year ago, with a net loss of $3.4 million or $0.27 per diluted share versus a $4.1 million loss ($0.33) in the prior-year period. Gross margin fell to 11.1% from 12.1%, and adjusted EBITDA was -$2.2 million versus -$457,000, pressured by excess-inventory markdowns tied to restructuring and unfavorable China FX. Management gave only limited Q4 guidance, expecting sequential consolidated sales growth led by Bedding, cost benefits from completed restructuring (over $20 million in annualized savings), and cost-neutral tariff pricing, but withheld more specific operating guidance pending potential IEEPA tariff refunds of $6-7 million. Third quarter was the capstone of the integration and restructuring initiatives, with Q4 the first quarter of fully enacted savings.

negative_highlights: R&D expenses rose 31% YoY to $12.6M driven by external development costs for the LX1 product that did not begin shipping until early 2026
Management explicitly stated it is 'impossible' to predict exact FY2026 revenue ranges or specific order volumes due to a bumpy business environment
Significant portion of R&D spend allocated to new products (LX1) and waveguide optimization that are not yet generating commercial sales
positive_highlights: Q4 revenue increased 76% YoY to $2.2 million driven by M400 unit sales and engineering services
Full-year gross loss improved significantly from a $5.6M loss in 2024 to a $1.1M loss, primarily due to lower inventory obsolescence reserves
Net cash position strengthened to $21.2 million at year-end with no debt outstanding
summary: Vuzix reported Q4 FY2025 revenue of $2.2 million (up from $1.3M in prior year) and full-year revenue of $6.3 million (up 9% YoY), driven by higher unit sales of the M400 platform and engineering services, though gross loss narrowed to a net loss attributable to common shareholders of $8.7 million for Q4 ($0.12/share). Management provided no specific numerical guidance or earnings estimates for FY2026, instead offering qualitative 'spitball' commentary on OEM growth surpassing branded enterprise revenue later in the year and citing new contracts with Amazon and Collins Aerospace without quantified production timelines.

negative_highlights: Consolidated sales declined 5.2% to $204.1 million, with the U.S. segment down 5.5% and International down 2.3%.
Full-year 2026 guidance was not provided; management will wait until Q1 results in mid-May.
International segment gross margin fell to 30.8% from 38.6% due to higher customer support spending.
positive_highlights: Adjusted net income rose to $23 million ($1.05 per diluted share) from $12 million ($0.55) in the prior year.
Adjusted income from operations for Q4 2025 was $26.4 million, up over 30% from $20.2 million in Q4 2024.
Gross margin expanded to 38.6% from 37.7%, driven by lower ocean freight rates, favorable product mix, and FIFO inventory timing.
summary: Q4 FY2025 revenue was $204.1 million, down 5.2% YoY, with U.S. segment sales down 5.5% to $185.3 million and International down 2.3% to $18.8 million. Adjusted net income rose to $23 million ($1.05 per diluted share) from $12 million ($0.55) in the prior year, and adjusted income from operations increased over 30% to $26.4 million. Gross margin expanded to 38.6% from 37.7%, and SG&A fell 12% to $38 million. Full-year 2026 guidance will be provided with Q1 results in mid-May, with management prioritizing a return to sustainable top-line growth.

negative_highlights: Full-year revenue plus tax credits declined to $208 million from $268 million in 2024
Full-year operating loss of $37.2 million and net loss of $77 million remain large in absolute terms
45Z economics and the exact 2026 revenue picture remain unquantified pending the DOE GREET model spreadsheet, which management said is out of its control
positive_highlights: Quarterly gross profit swung to $7.7 million from a $2 million gross loss in the prior-year period
Biogas segment generated $12.2 million of net income in 2025 with Q4 RNG production up 61% year over year
MVR system at Keyes (roughly $40 million, more than half spent) expected to cut natural gas use 80% and add about $32 million in annual plant cash flow by Q4 2026
summary: Q4 revenue plus tax credits totaled $53.7 million versus $47 million a year ago, with quarterly gross profit of $7.7 million turning from a $2 million gross loss, and operating loss narrowing to $2.5 million from $13.5 million. Full-year 2025 revenue plus tax credits fell to $208 million from $268 million in 2024, though operating loss improved to $37.2 million and net loss to $77 million from $87.5 million. Management gave no formal 2026 guidance but said cash flow should be significantly above 2025, citing $12.2 million of 2025 biogas segment net income, 61% Q4 RNG production growth, MVR completion targeted for Q3 2026 worth roughly $32 million annual cash flow, and only $5 million of 45Z monetized to date. Key swing factors cited were LCFS credit prices rising from $40 to $70 and the pending DOE GREET model needed to calculate 45Z revenue.

negative_highlights: Rockies and Southwest segments saw revenues decline roughly 9-10% sequentially due to severe weather, seasonality, and customer budget exhaustion.
Q4 revenue per rig was approximately $297,000 but Q1 guidance forecasts a decrease of about 3% despite the company maintaining its asset base.
Corporate adjusted EBITDA loss remains elevated at approximately $6.3 million in Q4 compared to historical levels.
positive_highlights: Northeast/Mid-Con segment delivered adjusted EBITDA margin expansion to 25.3% driven by robust gas-directed work and rig count increases of approximately 6%.
Adjusted EBITDA reached a quarterly high of $23 million, representing the strongest profitability for the year.
Dry gas revenue in Northeast/Mid-Con increased 5.3% quarter over quarter as the portfolio continues to align with higher-margin opportunities.
summary: Fourth quarter revenue of approximately $157 million was in line with guidance but decreased due to seasonality and budget exhaustion. Adjusted EBITDA reached a quarterly high of roughly $23 million (margin ~14%), driven by strong performance in the Northeast/Mid-Con segment where dry gas revenue grew 5.3% sequentially, while Rockies and Southwest segments declined on weather and activity softness. Management provided Q1 guidance for revenues between $145M-$150M (down ~3%) but expects a gradual market recovery starting in H2 2026.

negative_highlights: Total Q4 revenue declined 1.7% year over year to $84.9 million, with Direct segment revenue down 2.6%
FY2027 sales guidance of $255 million to $270 million implies a decline from the FY2026 level

Operating loss improvement of 40% or better versus FY2026 still leaves the company unprofitable on a full-year basis, and management expects Project Restoration inventory overhang to persist for 6 to 12 months
positive_highlights: Returned to profitability with net income of $2.5 million, or $0.09 per diluted share, a $0.28 year-over-year improvement from a $0.19 loss
Gross margin expanded approximately 100 basis points to 47.8%, aided by lower promotional activity and freight cost savings
Fiscal 2026 net cash flow improved to negative $11.9 million from negative $46.9 million in FY2025, and the ABL facility was paid off with no borrowings at year-end
summary: Vera Bradley reported Q4 FY2026 revenue of $84.9 million, down 1.7% year over year, with Direct segment revenue down 2.6% to $74.5 million and Indirect up 4.9% to $10.4 million. The company returned to profitability with net income of $2.5 million, or $0.09 per diluted share, versus a $5.4 million loss a year ago, helped by roughly 100 basis points of gross margin expansion to 47.8% and a $10.6 million reduction in SG&A. FY2027 guidance calls for sales of $255 million to $270 million and an operating loss improvement of 40% or better versus an adjusted operating loss of $21.7 million in FY2026. Management framed FY2027 as a year of stabilization, citing a planned halt to the annual outlook sale in Q1 and continued Project Restoration inventory clearance as headwinds.

negative_highlights: Revenue base remains small at $0.9 million for the quarter; profitability path not quantified.
InstaMortgage closing remains subject to state-by-state regulatory approvals, with timing uncertain.
Company still early stage with no explicit guidance for 2026 beyond 'predictable growth'.
positive_highlights: Full-year revenue grew 376% to $4.5 million; Q4 revenue grew 70% YoY to $0.9 million.
Cash and cash equivalents ended at $7.8 million, up 149% YoY, and parent-level debt was eliminated.
Prevu acquisition added 13 states and D.C., expanding realty footprint; InstaMortgage deal expected to add lending capabilities.
summary: Q4 FY2025 revenue was $0.9 million, up 70% YoY; full-year revenue rose 376% to $4.5 million. Full-year gross profit was $2.5 million, and cash ended at $7.8 million, up 149% YoY. Management highlighted the Prevu acquisition and the planned InstaMortgage deal (closing expected late Q1 or early Q2) as key drivers for continued platform integration. No formal guidance was provided; tone was upbeat but qualitative.

negative_highlights: Q4 adjusted EBITDA loss widened to $10.6M from a $6.6M loss a year ago
Q4 adjusted net loss of $14.2M (-$0.17/share) versus adjusted net income of $1.3M (+$0.01) in Q4 2024
January-February 2026 total brokerage cash receipts down 12.4% and existing-home-sale receipts down 11% versus the prior year
positive_highlights: Full-year adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed to $14M from $24.1M in 2024
Development marketing pipeline totals $25.3B gross transaction value, with $7.5B expected to come to market through December 2026; division revenue rose to $80.4M from $67.8M
summary: Q4 revenue was $245.4M versus $243.3M a year ago, but excluding the disposed property management business revenue rose 3.8% to $243.3M. GAAP net income of $68.6M ($0.68/share) was driven by an $81.7M gain on the property management sale; adjusted EBITDA was a loss of $10.6M versus a $6.6M loss in Q4 2024, and adjusted net loss was $14.2M (-$0.17/share) versus $1.3M income (+$0.01) a year ago. No formal guidance was issued, but management disclosed that January-February 2026 existing-home-sale cash receipts were 11% below the prior year and total brokerage cash receipts were 12.4% lower. Full-year revenue was $1.033B, up 3.8%, with adjusted EBITDA loss narrowing to $14M from $24.1M; the balance sheet holds $115.5M cash and no long-term debt after redeeming the convertible notes.

negative_highlights: Q4 cash cost to mine Bitcoin reached $84,552 per coin, exceeding the average Bitcoin price during the period, causing operational losses.
Net loss from continuing operations for Q4 was $285 million, driven by $171.4 million fair value loss on Bitcoin collateral receivables and $81.4 million impairment on mining machines.
Hash rate will contract in the near term as inefficient machines are phased out, and no specific 2026 hash rate targets were provided.
positive_highlights: Full-year adjusted EBITDA was positive at $24.5 million, despite the net loss.
Revenue grew strongly to $688.1 million for 2025, up from the prior year's small base.
Company raised $75.5 million in new equity financing ($10.5 million injection and $65 million agreements) to strengthen the balance sheet.
summary: Cango's Q4 2025 revenue was $179.5 million with a net loss from continuing operations of $285 million, reflecting heavy impairment and fair value losses. Full-year 2025 revenue reached $688.1 million with a net loss of $622 million, including $96.5 million fair value loss on Bitcoin holdings and $81 million impairment on mining machines. The company sold 4,451 Bitcoin in February 2026 to repay debt and is shifting focus to an AI compute subsidiary, EcoHash, with a pilot in Georgia expected to generate revenue this year. Management guided that hash rate will temporarily decline as they phase out inefficient machines, while emphasizing balance sheet strength and capital discipline.

negative_highlights: Q4 revenue fell to $2.9M from $3.2M in Q3 and $3.7M a year ago; Q4 GAAP gross margin fell to 52.2% from 56.2% in Q3
Q1 2026 revenue guided to approximately $1.2M, with a customs-delayed order of more than $500K pushed from Q1 into Q2
Management cited lower visibility from irregular FWA order patterns and new customers without established order patterns; cash of $2.9M, up only via $2.1M of ATM proceeds
positive_highlights: Full-year millimeter wave revenue grew to $9.1M from $1.3M in 2024, roughly six-fold
Full-year GAAP gross margin expanded to 58.0% from 51.7%, and GAAP operating expenses fell to $11.8M from $20.0M
Full-year GAAP net loss narrowed to $4.8M ($0.67/share) from $10.7M ($3.57/share) in 2024
summary: Q4 revenue was $2.9M, down from $3.2M in Q3 and $3.7M in the year-ago quarter, while full-year 2025 revenue fell to $12.2M from $14.6M as memory IC end-of-life offset millimeter wave growth. Q4 GAAP gross margin contracted to 52.2% from 56.2% in Q3, though full-year GAAP gross margin expanded to 58.0% from 51.7%. Q1 2026 guidance was set at approximately $1.2M, reflecting a customs-delayed order worth more than $500K that slipped from Q1 to Q2 plus lower demand visibility from irregular FWA order patterns. The offset is that full-year millimeter wave revenue grew to $9.1M from $1.3M in 2024, and management expects continued year-over-year millimeter wave growth in 2026.

negative_highlights: 2026 guidance tempered by M&T's double-digit revenue decline due to prior bookings lag
PathFactory acquisition adds investment costs and integration uncertainty for 2026
FX headwinds from Israeli shekel continue to pressure expectations
positive_highlights: Record adjusted EBITDA of $6.3M, tenth consecutive quarter of profitability
Full-year 2025 adjusted EBITDA grew 150% YoY, above original guidance
PathFactory acquisition adds AI-driven content journey orchestration, with run rate in teens of millions
summary: Kaltura reported Q4 2025 total revenue of $45.5 million and subscription revenue of $42.7 million, with record adjusted EBITDA of $6.3 million, marking the tenth consecutive quarter of profitability. Full-year 2025 adjusted EBITDA was $18.6 million, up 150% year-over-year and above original guidance. The company announced the planned acquisition of PathFactory for about $22 million, expanding its agentic digital experience platform, and guided 2026 with caution, citing headwinds from M&T revenue decline and PathFactory's contribution timing. New product launches include agentic avatars and an Avatar SDK, with revenue expected in the second half of 2026.

negative_highlights: Q4 gross margin remained deeply negative at -40%, with net loss of $1.4 billion (a -89% net margin)
Q4 included roughly a $236 million impairment on the North Carolina factory tied to revised project timing
Related-party deliveries were ~27% of FY2025 volume and ~33% in Q4, and international markets were only 11% of FY deliveries
positive_highlights: Q4 revenue of $1.6 billion rose 139% YoY and 118% QoQ; FY revenue of $3.6 billion was up 105%
FY2025 EV deliveries of 196,919 exceeded the at-least-double guidance, and 2026 guidance targets at least 300,000 EVs
Gross margin improved to -40% in Q4 from -79% a year earlier, and full-year gross margin improved to -43% from -57%
summary: VinFast reported Q4 FY2025 revenue of $1.6 billion, up 139% YoY and 118% QoQ, with full-year revenue of $3.6 billion (+105%). Q4 gross margin was -40%, improving from -79% a year earlier but still deeply negative, while net loss was $1.4 billion (a -89% net margin) and adjusted EBITDA was -$1.0 billion; results included a ~$236 million North Carolina factory impairment and delayed revenue recognition, which management excluded for underlying margins. FY2025 EV deliveries reached 196,919, exceeding the at-least-double guidance, and the 2026 outlook targets at least 300,000 EVs and at least 2.5x two-wheeler volume. Delivery mix skews to Vietnam and related parties (27% of FY deliveries, ~33% in Q4), with international at 18% of Q4 volume.

negative_highlights: Non-GAAP net loss widened to $6.8 million ($0.15 per share) from $5.4 million ($0.17 per share) in the prior quarter
Q4 cash burn rose to $7.5 million from $6.4 million a year earlier, and full-year 2026 burn is guided at $30-35 million
Management said meaningful revenue from the $30 million transportation OEM program is not expected until 2027, with only modest 2026 contribution
positive_highlights: Ended year with $86.5 million in cash and marketable securities, providing runway well into 2028
Active customer count grew from 12 to 16 with active engagements up over 40% and quotes up more than 30% quarter over quarter
Fully repaid 2025 convertible note and eliminated legacy warrants, leaving the company virtually debt free
summary: AEye reported Q4 2025 GAAP net loss of $7.3 million, or $0.17 per share, versus a $9.3 million loss ($0.30) in Q4 2024, though non-GAAP net loss widened to $6.8 million from $5.4 million in the prior quarter. Cash burn rose to $7.5 million excluding financing proceeds, driven by engineering costs, insurance and long-lead components, and full-year 2026 burn is guided to $30-35 million. The company ended 2025 with $86.5 million in cash, fully repaid its convertible note, grew active customers from 12 to 16, and said it expects revenue contribution from its $30 million transportation OEM win to be modest in 2026 with meaningful revenue in 2027. No specific revenue or EPS guidance was given; tone was positive on pipeline and product launches including Apollo, Optus and Stratos.

negative_highlights: Q4 revenue fell to $28.2 million from $36.2 million a year ago, pressured by UX testing and traffic volatility
Q4 net income declined to $5.3 million (18.8% of revenue) from $6.9 million (19.1%)
No formal 2026 guidance provided; share repurchase program announced in July remains unused pending a debt refinance with no stated timeline
positive_highlights: Full-year adjusted EBITDA rose to $51.5 million (38.2% of revenue) from $27.0 million (21.4%) in 2024
Non-advertising revenue increased more than $21 million, cutting advertising share of total revenue to 64% from 74%
Debt reduced by $23.5 million in 2025 with cash up nearly $6 million to $10.3 million
summary: Q4 2025 revenue fell to $28.2 million from $36.2 million a year earlier, driven by user-experience testing that impacted ads and ongoing search-algorithm traffic volatility. Q4 net income was $5.3 million (18.8% of revenue) versus $6.9 million (19.1%), while Q4 adjusted EBITDA of $10.1 million held a 35.8% margin, roughly flat year over year. Full-year 2025 revenue rose to $134.8 million from $125.9 million, with adjusted EBITDA of $51.5 million (38.2% of revenue) versus $27.0 million (21.4%) in 2024, aided by non-advertising revenue up over $21 million and debt repayment of $23.5 million. Management gave no formal 2026 guidance, said Q1 traffic represents a 'base' level for planning, expects a similar 2026 margin profile as 2025, and targets advertising below 50% of revenue while continuing one-to-two tuck-in media acquisitions per quarter.

negative_highlights: Q4 GAAP results included a $14.9 million noncash goodwill impairment in the Secure Networks segment and a $1.5 million restructuring charge, totaling $16.4 million.
Cash gross margin is guided to decline to 37-39.5% in 2026 from 41.9% in Q4 2025, driven by lower-margin IT GEMS third-party hardware/software mix and prepaid expense recognition.
Pipeline awards have shifted to the right due to government shutdown, funding constraints, and increased government review, with only about 20% of pipeline value expected in the first half of 2026.
positive_highlights: Q4 revenue of $46.8 million exceeded guidance and grew 77% year over year, driven by Telos ID and large program ramps.
Adjusted EBITDA of $7.3 million significantly beat the high end of the $4.0-5.7 million guidance range, with 15.6% margin.
2026 guidance for revenue growth of 14-21% and adjusted EBITDA margin expansion to 11-14%, supported by existing programs and recent new business.
summary: Telos reported Q4 FY2025 revenue of $46.8 million, up 77% year over year and above the guidance range of $44-46.3 million, with GAAP gross margin of 35% (36% excluding a $0.5 million charge; cash gross margin 41.9%) and adjusted EBITDA of $7.3 million versus guidance of $4.0-5.7 million. Full-year 2025 revenue rose 52% to $164.8 million and adjusted EBITDA was $18.1 million, a $27.8 million improvement. The company initiated 2026 guidance for revenue of $187-200 million (14-21% growth), adjusted EBITDA of $20.6-28.0 million, and cash gross margin of 37-39.5%, with cash gross margin expected to decline year over year before rising again. Shares repurchased in 2025 totaled $13.6 million (about 4.3% of shares) at an average price of $4.38, and the board increased the repurchase authorization from $50 million to $75 million.

negative_highlights: Operating expenses decreased but were burdened by ~$3.3 million in transaction and brand marketing costs
Website relaunch is expected later this year rather than immediately monetizing the new digital hub
Honey Birdette growth relies on a recent price increase of 10% which may face macro headwinds
positive_highlights: Honey Birdette sales grew 9% year over year, driven by full-price note up 21% and retail growth of 17% like-for-like
Licensing revenue reached $46 million in FY2025 with a 90% gross margin and nearly half guaranteed via contract
Adjusted EBITDA turned positive for the fourth consecutive quarter at $7.1M, excluding litigation expenses it would have been $8.0M
summary: Playboy reported Q4 FY2025 revenue of $34.9 million (up from $33.5M in prior year) and net income of $3.6 million ($0.03/share), marking a significant turnaround from the previous year's loss. The company achieved its fourth consecutive quarter of positive Adjusted EBITDA at $7.1 million, driven by strong performance across licensing (over 90% guaranteed revenue) and Honey Birdette retail growth. Management highlighted successful deleveraging with debt reduced to ~$160M following a UTG China deal expected to close soon.

Q4 revenue was $99.8 million and adjusted EBITDA $34.2 million, up from $80.0 million and $22.6 million a year earlier on higher production and 45Z recognition; full-year adjusted EBITDA of $90.2 million was flat versus 2024 and only landed inside guidance despite 28% RNG production growth to 4.9 million MMBtu, as realized RIN prices fell to $2.45 from $3.13. Fuel Station Services EBITDA rose 22% to $46.7 million but came in below guidance on deferred fleet investment. 2026 guidance is $95-110 million adjusted EBITDA (about 14% growth at the midpoint) and 5.4-5.8 million MMBtu of production, with most growth assumed from existing assets and a weak Q1 flagged. Management described 2026 as a transitional year for the downstream segment, with real growth pushed to 2027.

negative_highlights: Q4 swung to a $0.1 million net loss with adjusted EBITDA margin of just 8.9% of revenue
Compensation ratio rose to 67% of revenue from 62% in 2024, with management expecting it elevated 'for the foreseeable future' due to continued hiring
Full-year revenue grew only 1.3% versus a 9.4% expense increase, and discretionary AUM declined 1.2% in Q4
positive_highlights: Full-year organic new client flows of $688.3 million, described as one of the stronger levels of recent years
Discretionary AUM up 3% for the year to $24 billion, aided by markets and organic flows
Roughly $50.4 million of shares repurchased, nearly completing the announced $25 million program
summary: Silvercrest reported Q4 revenue of $32 million and a net loss of $0.1 million (GAAP -$0.01/share), with adjusted EPS of $0.19 basic and adjusted EBITDA of $2.9 million, just 8.9% of revenue. Full-year revenue rose only 1.3% to ~$125 million while expenses grew 9.4%, lifting the compensation ratio to 67% of revenue from 62% in 2024. Discretionary AUM fell 1.2% in Q4 to $24 billion despite $124.5 million of organic new accounts. Management guided that the elevated compensation ratio will persist 'for the foreseeable future,' with further hiring in Atlanta, Singapore, and Dublin ahead of revenue. It completed ~$50.4 million of buybacks under a $25 million program but flagged share count will tick up from new equity awards near term.

negative_highlights: Fintech non-GAAP gross margin fell from 96% to 69% due to mix shift
Operating loss of $32 million for 2025, though improved by $9.7 million
Cash and restricted cash only $16.1 million with $6.2 million drawn on credit line
positive_highlights: 2025 net revenue of $18.2 million exceeded guidance of $16.5 million, up 81% YoY
Q4 fintech revenue up 109% YoY and 100%+ QoQ
G&A expenses reduced by $9.9 million (26%) YoY
summary: PSQH reported 2025 net revenue from continuing operations of $18.2 million, an 81% increase year-over-year and above guidance of $16.5 million. Q4 fintech revenue grew 109% to $7.3 million, with credit revenue up 47% to $4.8 million. The company reduced operating loss by $9.7 million versus prior year, cut headcount by over 40%, and expects annualized cash savings of about $8 million. Management is focused on fintech-only strategy, with divestitures of brand and marketplace underway.

negative_highlights: Mortgage origination volume fell 13% sequentially to $540 million and market share dropped to 9 bps from 11 bps in Q3
Cemetery revenue fell 11.3% to $3.86 million in Q4 on lower pre-need land sales, and full-year cemetery revenue declined 6.2% to $15.22 million
Consolidated revenue growth of only 3% was muted by ~$6 million in added costs (personnel +$2 million, other +$3 million), and core Life premium was flat at ~$120 million
positive_highlights: Full-year net earnings rose $3 million or 10%, with management calling 2025 the best net profit year ever excluding 2020-2021
Mortgage Q4 pre-tax loss narrowed 74% to $1.161 million from $4.4 million on a 6% origination volume decline
Life segment net investment income grew ~12% to ~$76 million, lifting segment pre-tax net income ~8% to $37.4 million; stockholders' equity rose 7.5% to $410 million
summary: Security National reported its best net profit year excluding pandemic years 2020-2021, with full-year net earnings up $3 million or 10% and revenue up 3%, driven mainly by investment returns; Q4 net income rose nearly 200% over the prior year's Q4. The Life segment posted $37.4 million in pre-tax net income (up ~8%) on ~$208 million revenue (up ~5%), with net investment income up ~12% to ~$76 million, while core premium was roughly flat at ~$120 million. Mortgage cut its Q4 pre-tax loss to $1.161 million from $4.4 million despite a 6% YoY and 13% QoQ drop in originations to $540 million, and market share slipped to 9 bps from 11 bps. Cemetery and Mortuary Q4 pre-tax rose to $1.74 million on 9.7% revenue growth, though full-year pre-tax was roughly flat at $8.82 million. No formal forward guidance was provided; management offered qualitative confidence and noted macro sensitivity in real estate-related investments.

negative_highlights: Rockies segment adjusted EBITDA decreased by $1.2M due to natural production declines and no new well connections in Q4
Piceance segment expected decline in volume throughputs with MVC shortfall payments rolling off from $17M in 2025 to ~$13M in 2026
positive_highlights: Full-year FY2025 adjusted EBITDA beat of approximately $46M driven by Permian segment growth
Double E Pipeline mainline capacity now generally fully subscribed with over 1.6 Bcf/day in firm take-or-pay contracts
New term loan refinancing enabled an $85 million distribution to repay preferred dividends and reduce debt
summary: Summit Midstream Corp reported Q4 FY2025 adjusted EBITDA of $58.6 million and full-year 2025 adjusted EBITDA of $243 million against a prior year total of approximately $197 million, representing a significant beat driven by Permian volume growth. Management raised the 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance range to $225-$265 million and increased capital expenditure guidance to $85-$105 million following the execution of new long-term take-or-pay agreements on Double E Pipeline that fully subscribed existing capacity. The company also refinanced its Permian joint venture, enabling an $85 million distribution back to Summit Midstream Corp., which will be used to repay accrued preferred dividends and reduce ABL borrowings.

negative_highlights: Cash consumption is expected to increase significantly in 2026, rising from ~$200 million last year to between $225-$275 million.
Backlog contraction occurred as some customers withdrew non-binding letters of intent (LOIs) due to changing strategies or bankruptcy.
Certification timeline faces delays and rework regarding means of compliance with new FAA regulations, impacting the path to type certificate issuance.
positive_highlights: Completed first flight of engineering prototype on December 19, validating integration of fifth-generation fly-by-wire and fixed pitch lifter rotors.
Secured firm orders with AirX for two aircraft plus an option for 48 more, alongside a backlog of ~2,700 aircraft valued at $13.5 billion.
Total liquidity reached $641 million after securing a new syndicated loan and refinancing existing debt.
summary: Eve Holding reported a net loss of $64 million for Q4 2025 and $224 million for the full year, driven by $59 million in R&D expenses and $8 million in SG&A. The company ended the quarter with $393 million in cash and total liquidity of $541 million, which is sufficient to cover expected capital needs well into 2028. Management raised guidance for 2026 cash consumption to a range of $225-$275 million from the prior year's low end of $200 million due to intensified development activities and supplier payments.

negative_highlights: Canadian same-store sales only marginally positive, with industry sales down 1% year-over-year for the three months ended December 2025
Remexian gross margins pressured at ~20% due to 7-8 tons of biomass stalled in Portugal
Potential headwinds from new German medical cannabis access law, though expected to be more benign than feared
positive_highlights: Revenue up 25% year-over-year to a record CAD 178.3 million, fastest growth in 10 quarters
Adjusted EBITDA grew 62% year-over-year to CAD 11.5 million
Free cash flow swung to CAD 2.9 million from -CAD 1.9 million in Q1 last year
summary: High Tide reported Q1 FY2026 revenue of CAD 178.3 million, up 25% year-over-year (fastest in 10 quarters) and 9% sequentially, with adjusted EBITDA of CAD 11.5 million, up 62% year-over-year. The brick-and-mortar segment posted its fifth consecutive quarter of sequential gross margin expansion to 28%, and consolidated free cash flow swung to CAD 2.9 million from negative CAD 1.9 million a year ago. However, Canadian same-store sales were only marginally positive amid an industry slowdown and severe January weather, and German medical cannabis gross margins remained at ~20% due to Portugal supply delays. Management reiterated its 20-30 store growth target in Canada and expressed confidence in achieving 20-25% German gross margins once Canadian biomass arrives, while noting potential headwinds from new German medical cannabis regulations.

negative_highlights: Card Issuing revenues declined in Q4 due to an indirect acquisition of a reseller's amusement park card program
SG&A expenses increased 10% for the year, though management expects headcount savings and flat SG&A in 2026
positive_highlights: Record quarterly and annual revenues with total dollars processed up 19% year-over-year
ACH segment led growth with over 30% revenue increase driven by pinless debit volume surging more than 80%
Output Solutions achieved strong momentum with pieces mailed up 11% in the fourth quarter
summary: USIO reported a solid Q4 FY2025 with record revenue growth accelerating to 8% sequentially and year-over-year for the full year. The company delivered positive adjusted EBITDA for three consecutive years while executing on its strategy of increasing wallet share across ACH, Card, and Output Solutions segments. Management reaffirmed guidance for 10%-12% revenue growth in fiscal 2026.

negative_highlights: Q4 service revenue was lower than expected due to accounting adjustments related to technology upgrades and foreclosures.
Large IDN deals introduce potential quarterly lumpiness due to budget cycles, creating variability in revenue recognition timing.
positive_highlights: Q4 revenue surged 128% YoY to $5.3M with 16 units sold versus 9 in the prior year.
Gross margin expanded 1,530 bps sequentially to 50.9%, marking the second consecutive quarter above 50%.
Net cash burn declined 30% YoY to $5.7M as the company transitions to a commercial growth stage.
summary: Hyperfine reported Q4 FY2025 revenue of $5.3 million, a 128% year-over-year increase driven by the sale of 16 next-generation Swoop units. Gross margin expanded significantly to 50.9%, and net cash burn decreased by 30% to $5.7 million. For FY2026, management raised revenue guidance to a range of $20-22 million (midpoint 55% growth) and lowered full-year cash burn expectations to $26-28 million.

negative_highlights: Full year 2025 revenues decreased compared to the prior period
Net loss of $6.6 million reflecting increased investment in clinical pipeline and R&D expenses rising 51% YoY
R&D spending on PRX-115 is expected to continue increasing
positive_highlights: $25 million regulatory milestone payment earned from Chiesi
Projected full year 2026 revenue growth of more than 50% driven by high-margin Chiesi sales ($33M-$35M)
PRX-115 Phase II RELEASE study has enrolled first patients with top-line results expected in H2 2027
summary: For full year 2025, Protalix reported revenues of $51.8 million (a modest decrease from the prior year) and a net loss of $6.6 million compared to income in 2024, driven by increased R&D spending on PRX-115. The company received a $25 million regulatory milestone payment for an EU dosing regimen approval, projecting total cash balances near $50 million by early April 2026.

negative_highlights: Revenue fell to $0.5 million for the quarter from $0.8 million a year ago, and to $2.1 million for nine months from $4.5 million
Gross profit swung to a $0.8 million loss from $0.2 million profit, with gross margin hit by one-time losses on strategic contracts
Net loss widened to $11.4 million from $6.7 million, and nine-month operating cash use rose to $19.9 million from $14.6 million
positive_highlights: Backlog reached a record $19.9 million, up $12.4 million or 165% year-over-year
Pipeline expanded to $163.9 million, up $74.7 million or 84% year-over-year, with a large portion tied to defense and security programs
The $6.5 million DHS award plus Anduril integration positions PowerBuoy systems in a next-generation defense sensing network, with first systems being readied for shipment
summary: Q3 FY2026 revenue fell to $0.5 million from $0.8 million a year ago, and the nine-month figure dropped to $2.1 million from $4.5 million, which management attributed to the October-November 2025 federal government shutdown shifting deliverables into later quarters. Gross profit swung to a $0.8 million loss due to one-time losses on certain strategic contracts, and the net loss widened to $11.4 million from $6.7 million, with operating cash use of $19.9 million over nine months versus $14.6 million prior. Backlog reached a record $19.9 million (up 165% YoY) and pipeline $163.9 million (up 84% YoY), with cash of $7.2 million versus $6.9 million at fiscal year start. No formal revenue or EPS guidance was provided; management said some delayed work should convert later in the fiscal year and expects gross margin improvement as deployments scale.

negative_highlights: Q4 comparable sales declined 10%, with a 460 bps hit from the footwear pause, and net sales fell to $236.2 million from $275.6 million
Gross margin contracted 360 bps to 30.0% from 33.6% on promotional activity, product mix, and deleverage; adjusted EBITDA margin fell to 2.2% from 6.1%

FY2026 net sales guidance of $940-960 million is below FY2025's $1.0 billion, and $40 million of cost savings only bridges to a $70 million EBITDA midpoint, with offsets from lower gross margin dollars and a reset incentive comp program
positive_highlights: Full-year FY2025 net sales of $1.0 billion hit the top end of guidance and adjusted EBITDA of $63.6 million exceeded the high end of the outlook
SG&A fell $11.4 million to $62.4 million and leveraged 40 bps to 26.4% of net sales despite the sales decline
Sub-brands generated over $70 million in 2025 and are projected to grow roughly 60% to about $110 million in 2026, with higher product margins than core assortment
summary: Torrid reported Q4 FY2025 net sales of $236.2 million versus $275.6 million a year ago, a 10% comparable sales decline that included a 460 basis point negative impact from the footwear pause. Gross margin contracted to 30.0% from 33.6%, adjusted EBITDA fell to $5.2 million (2.2% margin) from $16.7 million (6.1%), and the net loss widened to $8.1 million ($0.08 per share) from $3.0 million ($0.03). Full-year net sales of $1.0 billion were at the top end of guidance and adjusted EBITDA of $63.6 million exceeded the high end, while FY2026 guidance was set at net sales of $940-960 million (below FY2025) with adjusted EBITDA of $65-75 million and up to 140 bps of margin expansion. Management framed 2026 as a pivot from a two-year restructuring of stores, product, and pricing toward customer-file growth, supported by $40 million of incremental store-closure cost savings.

summary: Torrid reported Q4 FY2025 net sales of $236.2 million versus $275.6 million a year ago, with comparable sales down 10% (including a 460 bps hit from the footwear pause) and a net loss of $8.1 million, or $0.08 per share, versus a $3.0 million loss last year. No formal 2026 capex or production guidance was issued; management said it will start drilling in coming months, targeting roughly three wells (~$7 million each) with potential to add more at higher prices, and plans to pay down the $46 million net debt in H1. BitFuFu reported full-year 2025 revenue of $475.8 million versus $463.3 million in 2024, but swung to a net loss of $57.4 million from net income of $54 million, driven by non-cash mining equipment impairments, unrealized Bitcoin fair value losses, and a lower realized gain on digital asset sales. Cloud mining revenue grew 29.3% to a record $350.6 million (74% of total) while self-mining revenue collapsed to $63.1 million from $157.5 million on weaker hash price and higher network difficulty. summary: MaxCyte reported full-year FY2025 revenue of $33 million (down 15% YoY) and Q4 revenue of $7.3 million (down 16% YoY), driven by a largest customer's inventory drawdown, program rationalization across SPL partners including six discontinued programs, and reduced leases from manufacturing site reorganization. Management provided FY2026 guidance for total revenue between $30M-$32M ($25M-$27M core + ~$5M SPL), explicitly incorporating a near-term headwind of approximately $4 million in core revenue relative to 2025 levels before expecting stabilization and growth. The company highlighted the launch of ExPERT DTX, integration progress with SecurDx, reduced annual cash burn by over $16 million via restructuring, and receipt of seven-figure milestone payments.

Fourth quarter total revenue only up 0.8% due to store closures
Company closed 33 restaurants in 2025 and expects 30-35 more in 2026

summary: Noodles & Company reported Q4 2025 total revenue of $122.8 million, up 0.8% YoY, with system-wide comp sales up 6.6%. Restaurant contribution margin expanded to 14.1% from 11.2%, and adjusted EBITDA rose over 88% to $7.6 million. The company guided 2026 to comp sales of 6-9% and adjusted EBITDA of $30-35 million, more than double prior year, with early Q1 2026 comp trends over 9%. Management attributes momentum to portfolio optimization, menu innovation, and operational improvements.

Adjusted Funds From Operations (AFFO) declined to $4 million ($0.32 per share), driven by lower cash rents partially offset by reduced interest expense and dividends. Management indicated that asset recycling activity will pick up in earnest during 2026, though the current M&A environment remains volatile with rates gyrating.

17th consecutive quarterly dividend declared plus renewed buyback for up to 10% of shares outstanding
summary: Epsilon reported FY2025 adjusted EBITDA growth of 75% and production growth of 54% year over year, with Proved Developed Producing reserves up 69% and total proved reserves up 86% following the PEEP/Powder River Basin acquisition closed in November 2025. Q4 operating results were not separately itemized in the transcript, and no formal 2026 production or cash flow guidance was given; management instead detailed 2026 capital plans, including roughly $6M for two Niobrara DUC completions, ~$22M for three Parkman wells starting in Q3, ~$4M in the Barnett, and ~$4M in the Marcellus. The company recorded $6.9M of Peak transaction costs plus impairments in Canada and New Mexico driven by a sub-$60 WTI year-end strip, and described Canada as non-competitive for capital with no 2026 activity planned. The Board declared a 17th consecutive quarterly dividend and renewed a buyback of up to 10% of shares outstanding, with debt paid down $5M in Q1 and liquidity actions underway (Marcellus ORRI sale, $3M Colorado office building under contract).

negative_highlights: Company remains pre-revenue with no commercial production of battery-grade lithium carbonate yet started.
Management explicitly declined to provide forward-looking guidance or estimates for the period.
Cash burn continues with net cash used in operating activities totaling $8.3 million.
positive_highlights: Net loss narrowed to $15.7 million from $23.8 million in the prior year due to lower financing charges and reduced general and administrative expenses.
Secured an air quality construction permit from ODEQ, allowing the project to proceed with construction and commissioning.
Completed FEL-3 engineering study and independent review by Black & Veatch validating low technical and design risk.
summary: Stardust Power reported a net loss of $15.7 million for the year ended December 31, 2025, an improvement from the prior year's $23.8 million loss driven by lower financing charges and reduced G&A expenses. The company remains pre-revenue with no commercial production yet started, holding $3.5 million in cash as of year-end. Management explicitly stated that no forward-looking guidance or estimates would be provided during the call.

negative_highlights: Net sales fell 23% to $7.5 million from $9.7 million on lower volumes with recurring national customers and higher promotional allowances

summary: Reed's Q4 FY2025 net sales fell to $7.5 million from $9.7 million a year ago on lower volumes with recurring national customers and higher promotional allowances. Gross margin contracted to 20% from 30% on inventory write-offs and higher COGS, though SG&A fell 19% to $4.0 million and delivery/handling dropped 35%, narrowing net loss to $3.8 million (-$0.44/share) from $4.1 million (-$1.33). EBITDA worsened to negative $3.6 million from negative $3.1 million, and the company provided no explicit numerical guidance, only directional talk of margin expansion and 2026 growth. CEO Cyril Wallace stepped down, with COO Neal Cohane named Interim CEO and a permanent search underway; the company also completed a $10 million offering and NYSE American uplisting. Management said it has 'work to do' on placements and declined to give specifics on the path to profitability.

Cash of $10.1 million at year-end is modest relative to the $9.4 million quarterly opex run rate

Closed a $14 million private placement with new and existing investors
summary: CapsoVision reported Q4 2025 total revenue of $3.9 million, up 13% year-over-year, with gross profit of $2 million and gross margin at 50%, consistent with expectations. Q4 patient volume rose 12% to approximately 9,400 and new accounts grew 16%, while hospital system customers increased 87%. Full-year revenue grew approximately 15%, and the company ended with $10.1 million in cash before raising $14 million in a private placement priced at $4.88 per share. Management guided to a CapsoCam Colon Gen 2 510(k) submission in Q3 2026 with potential clearance in Q1 2027 and launch in the first half of 2027, while operating expenses rose $3.1 million to $9.4 million.

Core operating expenses (ex-SBC) declined 30% quarter-over-quarter, dropping from $4.3M to $3.0M.
Announced a non-binding letter of intent to monetize the Optejet user-filled device in Q1 2026.
summary: Hyperion DeFi reported Q4 FY2025 adjusted gross profit of $821,000, an 87% quarter-over-quarter increase driven by ramping DeFi strategies like staking and validator commissions. However, the company recorded a GAAP net loss of $39.8 million due to significant treasury losses of $36.8 million as HYPE prices declined from ~$45 in Q3 to ~$25 at quarter-end. Management highlighted strong operational execution with core costs declining 30% and announced an LOI to monetize the Optejet life sciences asset, but provided no specific financial guidance for future quarters.

Management guided FY2026 revenue to $35-42M (~2.2x) at ~35% gross margin and targets operating cash flow positivity and a $9M quarterly revenue run-rate, but new SOLIS/CORE products only launched in December and are not yet contributing meaningfully. The quarter missed prior-period sales momentum while the full-year and forward guide are aggressive relative to the starting point.

R2 segment achieved record full-year revenue of $12.5 million with a 123% surge in international demand
summary: INNOVATE reported Q4 FY2025 consolidated revenues of $382.7 million (up 61.7% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $24.5 million, driven primarily by a massive increase in the Infrastructure segment which grew revenue to $373.9 million. However, this growth was partially offset by significant declines in Life Sciences (-24.4%) and Spectrum segments due to inventory constraints at R2 and soft advertising environments respectively. Management noted gross margin compression of 350 bps year-over-year in the Infrastructure segment despite backlog expansion.

R&D rose to $104.9 million and G&A fell to $18.9 million, producing a $121.3 million operating and net loss, with $116.9 million in cash and securities funding operations into early 2027 before a March 2026 private placement grossed $35.75 million. No revenue, EPS, or formal guidance was provided; management reiterated the ALTITUDE-AD data timing and targeted a mid-2027 IND for the JCR-partnered EBD program, citing 14- to 40-fold higher brain levels in nonhuman primates versus native antibody.

The company reported a gross loss of $0.8 million and an operating loss of $2.8 million for the quarter, though these losses improved sequentially from the third quarter following cost reduction initiatives. Management noted that revenue is expected to remain flat in Q1 2026 before growing as distribution expands.

summary: For Q4 FY2025 and the full year ended Dec 31, PIII reported total revenue of $384.8 million (Q4) and $1.46 billion (FY), representing a decline from prior periods due to membership mix changes despite higher per-member-per-month rates ($1,060 in Q4). Adjusted EBITDA losses narrowed year-over-year on a normalized basis (-$149.1M vs -$193.0M) but remained negative at -$76.1 million for the quarter and -$161.3 million for the full year. Management provided 2026 guidance of Adjusted EBITDA between -$20 million and $40 million (midpoint $10 million), citing structural improvements, contract renegotiations, and a new partnership adding 29,000 lives under management.

Large fleet agreements may compress near-term margins

summary: Xos reported Q4 2025 revenue of $5.2 million on 34 units delivered, with the balance of a 200+ unit UPS program recognized in future periods. Full-year 2025 revenue was $46 million on 328 units, up from prior years, with GAAP gross margin of 5.9%, operating loss narrowed 28% to $33.1 million, and positive free cash flow of $5.4 million versus negative $49.1 million in 2024. The company ended the year with $14 million in cash, down $26.9 million to $6 million in accounts receivable, and renegotiated its convertible note with Aldermay to quarterly installments through 2028. Management guided to expanding operations in 2026 with an upgraded hub product in three configurations, a growing powertrain business with Blue Bird, and continued focus on working capital and inventory turns, while being selective on ATM usage.

summary: Daré Bioscience reported full-year FY2025 revenue of $1.3 million and GAAP net loss of $(48) million with no EPS data provided due to lack of income statement details in the transcript text. The company disclosed a cash balance of approximately $24.7 million at year-end, supported by non-dilutive grants totaling roughly $19.5 million received during 2025. Management indicated that product revenue from DARE to PLAY and Flora Sync LF5 is expected to begin in Q2 2026 following the completion of state licensing for dispensing.

summary: FY2025 revenue fell 15% to $174 million, attributed to 2024 restructuring and the April 2025 fee-structure change, while net income rose 9% to $51 million and EPS rose 4% to $0.50 largely because prior-year listing and revaluation costs did not recur; EBITDA was $70 million at a 40.4% margin. No numerical FY2026 guidance was provided; management declined to size the SBC Wellness revenue contribution and gave no investment or M&A amounts, citing dependence on opportunity. Key changes were the OrangeTwist minority investment and BLEZ Thailand partnership, plus a buyback program authorized in December that had not been used as of the call.

negative_highlights: GAAP net loss for FY2025 was $8.5 million due to one-time non-cash debt fair value mark-to-market and extinguishment charges.

Q1 2026 revenue outlook remains lagged due to the demands of restructuring work completed in late 2025.

Gross margins expanded to 40% for FY2025 from 38%, driven by disciplined program structuring.
Pro forma cash basis EBITDA improved 31% YoY, including a 56% improvement in Q4 alone.

Management highlighted improved gross margins of 40% for FY2025 (up from 38%) and reduced pro forma cash basis OpEx by 29%, but explicitly stated that full financial benefits are not yet reflected due to ongoing restructuring lag effects expected through Q1-Q2 2026. The company announced a definitive agreement to acquire the Misfits Ads Division, which is pending stockholder approval.

negative_highlights: Q4 revenue declined 1.2% year-over-year as brokerage revenue fell 3.2% due to elevated mortgage rates and affordability constraints.
December cancellation rates hit 16.3%, the highest level recorded since tracking began in 2017, indicating significant market volatility.
The company ended Q4 with a GAAP net loss of $6.7 million ($0.21/share), an increase from the prior year's loss, driven by lower tax benefits and a business sale loss.

Gross profit margin expanded to 8.1% from 7.2% due to a favorable revenue mix and higher-margin ancillary services.
New structural pricing changes, including the Edge plan and $250 transaction fee, are projected to increase gross profit per transaction by over 100% on pre-cap deals.
summary: Fathom Realty reported Q4 FY2025 revenue of $90.6 million, a 1.2% year-over-year decrease driven by a 3.2% drop in brokerage revenue due to softer market conditions and higher cancellation rates (approx. 16.3% in December). While ancillary businesses grew 54.2%, the company posted a GAAP net loss of $6.7 million ($0.21/share) and an Adjusted EBITDA loss of $2.6 million, representing a modest improvement over the prior quarter but failing to meet expectations for a full recovery. Management highlighted structural pricing changes and margin expansion initiatives as key drivers for 2026 rather than relying on immediate market volume recovery.
