KOASTAL-2 and KOASTAL-3 fully enrolled with more than 400 patients each; joint top-line data expected in Q2 2026
Cash of $182.5M at year-end 2025 expected to fund operations into Q3 2027; NMRA-215 spend reduced by delaying clinic entry to Q1 2027
summary: Neumora's Q4 call was a pipeline update rather than a commercial quarter: it ended 2025 with $182.5M in cash and guided that runway extends into Q3 2027, with 2025 net loss described as comparable to 2024. Positives included positive NMRA-511 Phase Ib data (Cohen's d 0.32-0.34 on CMAI in the NPI-AA>=4 population) and full enrollment of KOASTAL-2 and KOASTAL-3 (>400 patients each, data expected Q2 2026). However, unexpected adverse findings in a 13-week rat tox study pushed the NMRA-215 clinic entry to Q1 2027 (from prior timing), triggering a for-cause audit and CRO change, while the M4 franchise lead shifted to NMRA-898 and NMRA-861 development was paused.

negative_highlights: Q4 2025 revenue of $238,000 tracked closely to Q3, marking two consecutive sequentially down quarters at an absolute level below $500,000.
No specific quarterly revenue guidance was provided; management explicitly declined to provide Q1 guidance and cited likely continued lumpiness.
Q4 R&D expense of $1.5 million and SG&A of $2.2 million against $238,000 of quarterly revenue, with SG&A expected to rise as sales/marketing headcount is added.
positive_highlights: Full year 2026 revenue guidance of $3-4 million versus $1.1 million in 2025, with Q1 2026 described as potentially the strongest quarter yet and potential for multiple expansion over Q4's $238,000.

Active commercial sites grew from about 6 in Q3 2025 to 9 exiting Q4 to 12 as of February 27, 2026, with a target of ~36 by year-end and a pipeline of 33 centers (12 active plus 21 evaluating/completed evaluation/preparing activation), a tripling of the near-term pipeline versus Q1 2025.
Completed a ~$10 million oversubscribed private placement on March 23, 2026 led by new and existing institutional investors, adding to ~$7 million in cash at year-end.
summary: RenovoRx reported Q4 2025 revenue of $238,000, roughly flat versus Q3, bringing full year 2025 revenue to $1.1 million in its first full year of RenovoCath commercialization; Q4 gross margin was 88% and year-end cash was ~$7 million. Management issued full year 2026 revenue guidance of $3-4 million, implying roughly a tripling of revenue, tied to a plan to grow active commercial sites from 12 (as of February 27, 2026) to about 36 by year-end, and said Q1 2026 should be the strongest revenue quarter yet with potential for multiple expansion over Q4. The company also announced a new CEO/Executive Chairman structure, a new CFO, and a ~$10 million oversubscribed private placement closed March 23, 2026. The Phase III TIGeR-PaC trial has randomized 104 of the required 114 patients with 72 of 86 required events observed, and enrollment completion is expected around mid-2026 with final data in 2027.

GAAP diluted EPS was $0.11 vs $0.16, though adjusted net income was flat at $2.7M/$0.19 per share and full-year adjusted EPS held at $0.71. Management described the market as finding a bottom after three years of decline but explicitly guided to no boom in 2026, and divested majority ownership of MRI's permanent placement business effective January 1.

summary: Nano Labs reported H2 2025 net revenue of RMB 80.7 million ($2.7 million), up 18.1% year over year, driven by higher iPollo V series sales volumes. Management gave no quantitative forward guidance, instead outlining continued BNB accumulation, an up-to-$25 million buyback announced in October 2025, and the March 2026 launch of the iPollo ClawPC A1 Mini for AI agents.

positive_highlights: Wholesale fuel contribution grew 8% to $24.0M driven by a volume increase of ~4% and margin expansion from dealerization conversions totaling over 650 sites year-to-date.
Fleet fueling margins remained strong at 45.6 cents per gallon in Q4, benefiting from high diesel prices on cost-plus contracts where the company captures prompt pay discounts.
summary: ARKO Petroleum reported Q4 FY2025 net income of $8.1 million and Adjusted EBITDA of $36.9 million, representing a decline in full-year fuel contribution for the GPMP segment due to lower gallons sold at its related-party retail sites despite margin stability from dealerization conversions. Management provided 2026 guidance expecting approximately $156 million in Adjusted EBITDA and noted that recent Middle East volatility has increased costs by roughly $1/gallon, though they expect prompt pay discounts will offset some of this impact.

negative_highlights: Market cap at discount to treasury valuation
Crypto sector out of favor, impacting digital treasury companies
Earlier stage biotech funding scarce
positive_highlights: Net income of $1.23 billion and EPS of $25.48 for 2025
FDA clearance for Phase IIb knee osteoarthritis trial
Extended RAIN token option to Dec 31, 2027 at same price
summary: For full-year 2025, Enlivex reported net income of $1.23 billion and diluted EPS of $25.48, driven by appreciation in treasury assets tied to the Rain Protocol prediction markets token. The company entered a $21 million convertible debt financing, extended its Rain token option to 2027, and approved a $20 million buyback. Clinically, FDA cleared a Phase IIb trial in knee osteoarthritis, with top-line data expected in 2027.

negative_highlights: Loss from operations was $201.1 million, compared to a loss of only $3.1 million in the prior year period.
Significant non-cash charges included $178.3 million in unrealized losses on digital intangible assets and $12.1 million in realized losses on digital intangible assets.
The Anchorage Digital collaboration has not yet taken off, with management stating they are still working out the kinks.
positive_highlights: Net income of $325.6 million driven by a $526.3 million gain on warrant fair value changes.
Staking yield outperformed system-wide average with an internal calculation of 6.8% versus 6.2% benchmark.
SOL per share increased by 14% over the six months since launching the digital asset treasury strategy.
summary: Solana Company reported Q4 FY2025 revenue of $5.2 million and net income of $325.6 million, driven by a $526.3 million non-operating gain from warrant fair value changes rather than core operations. The company incurred a loss from operations of $201.1 million due to significant unrealized losses on digital assets ($178.3 million) and intangible assets ($12.1 million). Management noted that the Anchorage Digital borrowing partnership is still in early stages with 'kinks' being worked out, and while staking yields remain strong at 6.8%, the quarter reflects a volatile asset environment.

negative_highlights: Total revenue fell sharply by 36% from the prior year's $7.2 million due to deliberate exit of lower-quality contracts and customer churn.
Operating expenses increased despite a significant cut in sales and marketing, driven largely by a non-cash goodwill impairment charge of $2.1 million.
Management explicitly stated they are not providing specific financial guidance for the upcoming fiscal year.
positive_highlights: Gross margin expanded five points year-over-year to 87% due to reduced cost of revenues and platform efficiency gains.
Subscription revenue quality improved significantly, now representing 98% of total revenue compared to 87% a year ago.
Cash balance strengthened to $11.1 million as of December 31, providing sufficient runway for six quarters.
summary: Total revenue declined 36% year-over-year to $4.6 million due to the exit of non-core contracts and churn during a strategic platform transition from SaaS to AI-native agentic solutions. Gross margin expanded structurally by five points to 87%, driven by disciplined cloud cost management, while operating expenses increased primarily due to a one-time goodwill impairment charge of $2.1 million. Management provided no specific financial guidance for FY2026 but expressed confidence in achieving double-digit growth once the transition is complete.

negative_highlights: Same-store sales dropped by 11.6% in Q4 due to customer retreat caused by immigration enforcement and reduced discretionary spending.
Cost of goods sold increased significantly, rising 285 basis points to 36.9% in the quarter.
Full-year adjusted EBITDA declined from $13.3 million in FY2024 to just $0.7 million in FY2025.
positive_highlights: CPG business expanded rapidly to over 800 locations in early 2026, projected to reach $100M annual run rate within three years.
Costco gift card sales reached approximately $29 million in FY2025, a 150% increase year-over-year.
CPG business achieved an initial 100% note-in rate from supermarket buyers with no turndowns reported.
summary: Q4 FY2025 revenue decreased to $49.7 million (down from $54.6M in Q4 2024) driven by an 11.6% same-store sales decline due to immigration enforcement and fuel price pressures, resulting in a net loss of $12.5 million ($0.36 diluted EPS). Management lowered full-year guidance for FY2026 to a range of $215-$225 million (down from prior expectations) while initiating a joint venture with Chubby Cattle International and accelerating its consumer packaged goods division.

negative_highlights: Full-year total revenue fell to $17.0 million from $17.8 million in FY2024
No formal forward revenue or earnings guidance was provided; CFO's financial update emphasized balance-sheet metrics over income-statement results
Notes Theater in Colorado Springs closed in July 2025 and Colorado Springs saw softer venue rentals
positive_highlights: Luxe FireSuite and Aikman Club sales reached $126 million in FY2025, up 62% from $77 million in FY2024
Total assets grew 108% to $370 million and property and equipment rose 123% to $305 million year-over-year
Ford Amphitheatre revenue grew 94% year-over-year on a full April-October season versus a partial 2024 season; 2026 offers and pending offers nearly double last year
summary: Venu reported full-year 2025 total revenue of $17.0 million versus $17.8 million in FY2024, a slight decline, while total assets grew 108% to $370 million and property and equipment rose 123% to $305 million. Luxe FireSuite/Aikman Club sales reached $126 million, up 62% from $77 million, with the mid-2025 triple-net leaseback model at about 25% of fire suite sales. No formal revenue or EPS guidance was issued; management pointed to FY2026 growth in show count and average ticket price at Ford Amphitheatre and targeted Tulsa (fall 2026) and McKinney (Q1 2027) openings. The company closed an $86 million raise and cited a $1.24 billion as-completed third-party appraisal versus balance-sheet assets held largely at basis.

negative_highlights: GAAP net loss of $155 million for the year.
CEO transition and ongoing strategic review add uncertainty.
Operating leverage not yet visible due to onetime costs.
positive_highlights: Total revenues up 29% year-over-year to $255 million.
Management fees grew 9% to nearly $200 million; Q4 management fees up 14% YoY.
Adjusted EBITDA rose 45% to $35 million for the year.
summary: AlTi reported full-year 2025 total revenues of $255 million, up 29% year-over-year, with management fees near $200 million, up 9%. Adjusted EBITDA rose 45% to $35 million, but the company posted a GAAP net loss of $155 million, including a $35 million impairment in Q3. AUM reached $50 billion, up 10% year-over-year, aided by the Kontora acquisition. CEO Michael Tiedemann is stepping down, with Nancy Curtin as Interim CEO; a special committee continues evaluating strategic alternatives, and Allianz has filed a 13D. Management expects 2026 to show clearer operating leverage from zero-based budgeting and simplified operations.

negative_highlights: Q4 adjusted net income per diluted share was a loss of $0.02 versus $0.32 earnings per share a year earlier, with adjusted EBITDA falling to $7.2 million from $14.5 million.
Q4 gross margin declined 320 bps to 63.1% on about $4.5 million of net tariff costs and deeper discounting; Q1 FY2026 gross margin is guided down about 400 bps.
FY2026 adjusted EBITDA is guided to $70-75 million versus $84.3 million in FY2025, and Q1 sales are expected down 5-7% with comps down 7-9% amid a softer start to the year.
positive_highlights: Direct sales rose 2.6% year over year in Q4, aided by markdown sales and ship-from-store capabilities.
FY2025 free cash flow was $23.2 million, with $41 million of cash at year-end and a $75 million term loan refinanced to save about $2 million in annual interest expense.
The board approved a 12.5% increase in the quarterly dividend to $0.09, and FY2025 included $10.4 million of share repurchases and $5 million of dividends.
summary: J.Jill reported Q4 FY2025 total sales of $138.4 million, down 3.1% year over year, with total company comps down 4.8%, gross margin down 320 bps to 63.1%, and an adjusted net loss of $0.02 per diluted share compared to $0.32 earnings per share a year earlier. FY2026 guidance calls for sales down 2% to flat, comps down 1% to 3%, adjusted EBITDA of $70-75 million versus $84.3 million delivered in FY2025, and full-year gross margin down about 50 bps, with Q1 sales guided down 5-7% and Q1 gross margin down roughly 400 bps. The main change is an explicitly investment-heavy transition year, with roughly $15 million of net tariff costs in 2026 versus $7.5 million in 2025 and new assortments not fully in place until Q2. Management noted a soft start to Q1 and plans a $0.01 quarterly dividend increase to $0.09, plus continued share repurchases under the remaining $14.1 million authorization.

negative_highlights: FY2026 revenue guidance of $95M–$99M is far below FY2025's $133.9M, reflecting divestiture and license revenue loss
Q1 2026 biologics expected down low double digits YoY due to lost amnio product
Hardware expected to decline at a high-teens rate through 2026
positive_highlights: Q4 gross margin expanded 410 bps to 54.9% from 50.8% on favorable mix and scale
Full year adjusted EBITDA swung to $16.3M from a $1.9M loss in 2024
Doubled regional sales reps and launched nanOss Strata and CollagenX in Q4
summary: Q4 FY2025 revenue was $32.4M, up 3% YoY, with adjusted EBITDA of $1.9M and net income of $57,000 ($0.00/share), versus a $3.2M net loss in Q4 2024; gross margin expanded to 54.9% from 50.8%. Full year revenue was $133.9M, up 14% YoY and near the upper end of prior guidance of $131M–$135M, with adjusted EBITDA of $16.3M versus a $1.9M loss, and the company generated positive free cash flow. However, FY2026 revenue guidance is $95M–$99M, reflecting the Companion Spine divestiture and the loss of Q-Code/amniotic license revenue, and management guided Q1 2026 biologics down low double digits and hardware down mid-teens. The sharp step-down in 2026 top line, along with expected continued hardware declines, tempers the otherwise improved profitability trends.

negative_highlights: Company said rabbits may not be a suitable model for the FDA-requested reproductive tox study, and declined to give a timeline for an alternative species or FDA alignment
Part 1a expansion cohort enrollment slowed due to site staffing challenges, pushing completion to H1 2026
Net cash used in operations rose to $29.1 million from $22.1 million, and R&D increased $5.5 million to $24.6 million year over year
positive_highlights: ReMEDy2 interim analysis on track for H2 2026, with almost 70% of the 200-patient interim enrollment completed and close to 61 active sites
Cash and note weakness in-term investments rose to $59.9 million from $44.1 million at year-end 2024, with funding now guided through end-2027
Health Canada regulatory clearance received to initiate a global phase II trial of DM199 in early-onset preeclampsia
summary: DiaMedica reported full-year 2025 financials: cash and short-term investments of $59.9 million versus $44.1 million at year-end 2024, working capital of $55.5 million, R&D of $24.6 million (up from $19.1 million), G&A of $9.8 million (up from $7.6 million), and net cash used in operations of $29.1 million (up from $22.1 million). No product revenue or EPS figures exist as this is a clinical-stage company; management said cash funds operations and planned studies through end-2027. The stroke program reiterated guidance to complete the ReMEDy2 interim analysis in H2 2026 with ~70% of the 200-patient interim enrollment complete and ~61 active sites, and the preeclampsia program added a Health Canada clearance for a global phase II early-onset trial. The chief negative was confirmation that rabbits are likely an unsuitable species for the FDA-requested reproductive tox study, with no timeline for resolving the alternative-model path.

negative_highlights: Full-year Adjusted EBITDA of ~$220M (pro forma) missed management's specific guidance range by approximately $20 million.
Q1 production is expected to decline to the low-23,000 BOE/d range due to planned shut-ins for reoccupying pads and offset frac activities.
Recent well performance showed declining initial rates in newer locations (Simpson ~500 BOE/d) compared to earlier performers like Opal Coal Bank (~725 BOE/d).
positive_highlights: Production of ~18,500 BOE/d (excluding Bayswater) met original full-year guidance range when adjusted to pro forma levels (~24,000 BOE/d).
Capital expenditures totaled $183.4 million, coming in significantly below the prior stated CapEx guidance.
Company achieved a 0.0 safety record for FY2025 with no incidents.
summary: Prairie Operating Company reported full-year FY2025 revenue of $242 million (excluding Bayswater) and Adjusted EBITDA of $156 million, both modestly missing pro forma guidance due to the exclusion of Q1 Bayswater volumes. While production exited at 28,000 BOE/d in line with original targets, management lowered full-year 2026 capital expenditure guidance by approximately $90 million below the prior midpoint and provided a conservative free cash flow outlook for FY2026.

negative_highlights: Q4 system sales outside the U.S. dropped significantly, with only one sale compared to ten in Q4 FY2024
Gross margin contracted from 48% in FY2024 to 46% in FY2025 due to inflation and tariffs
International business expansion halted for nine months due to acquisition uncertainty
positive_highlights: Full-year procedure volume grew 22%, surpassing 206,000 globally
Recurring revenue increased 15% in FY2025 to $46.3 million annualized run rate
Company retained a $10 million transaction deposit and secured payment deferrals on remaining liabilities
summary: Q4 FY2025 revenue declined 4% year-over-year to $16 million due to lower system sales outside the U.S., while full-year recurring revenue grew 15%. The company terminated its acquisition by Alcon, retaining a $10 million escrow deposit and writing off approximately $9.3 million in unpaid merger-related costs. Management expects operating expenses for FY2026 to be roughly flat or up only ~10% from the normalized base after removing M&A transaction impacts.

negative_highlights: FY2025 revenue fell 12% to $6.1M
Gross margin declined to 77.5% from 81.4%
Net loss widened to $4.6M from $4.3M
positive_highlights: Q1 2026 revenue guided to $2.2M, up 37% YoY with better bottom-line improvement
Foreign bank renewed at over $1M for 2026, a ~30% increase
Cash up $2M+ to $2.7M and book value doubled to $7.6M
summary: BIO-key reported FY2025 revenue of $6.1 million, down 12% YoY, with hardware revenue more than doubling to $1.3 million and services up 6%. Net loss widened to $4.6 million but per-share improved to $0.69. Management guides Q1 2026 revenue to about $2.2 million, up 37% YoY, and expects to approach breakeven in early 2026. Key drivers include an expanded $1M+ renewal from a foreign bank, EMEA transition to branded solutions, and new product launches like EcoID III and PortalGuard 7.0.

negative_highlights: Cash and cash equivalents only $1.1 million at year-end
Revenue remains lumpy and company does not provide 2026 guidance
Operating expenses reduction driven partly by severance and fundamental shift away from R&D
positive_highlights: Q4 revenue up 133% YoY; full-year revenue up 40% to $1.7 million
First order for Nu.Q Cancer clinical certification; Nu.Q NETs inclusion in French government-backed $7.3 million DETECSEPS sepsis program
Two licensing agreements signed (Werfen and Hologic); $5 million feline milestone expected this year
summary: For full fiscal year 2025, VolitionRX reported $1.7 million in revenue, up 40% year-over-year, with Q4 revenue growing 133% year-over-year. Operating expenses decreased 17% to $4.8 million lower than 2024, and net cash used in operating activities fell 24% to $19.7 million. Cash at year-end was $1.1 million, but subsequent to year-end the company raised $5.4 million via ATM and $1.9 million via convertible note, plus received $2.3 million in non-dilutive funding. Management expects to collect a $5 million milestone payment from the feline cancer study and plans to cut cash operating expenses by another 25-30% during 2026. First commercial orders for Nu.Q Cancer and Nu.Q NETs were received, and licensing discussions with about 10 companies are ongoing.

negative_highlights: Full-year 2025 net loss of $10.4M including $7.5M of non-recurring merger costs and $8.1M of deferred income tax expense
Full-year LOE per BOE rose to $11.62 from $10.36, attributed to higher-cost acquired assets, with the benefit of optimization only expected later in 2026

Debt draw rose to $98M by Feb 5, 2026 from $87M at year-end, leaving about $25M of liquidity, and management guided Q1 2026 as the peak production quarter with volumes set to settle toward 6,400-6,500 BOE/d
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA of $15.4M in Q4 grew 203% YoY despite a 16% decline in realized crude oil prices
Identified $10M-$13M of optimization projects expected to cut LOE by up to $1M per month, or $10M-$12M annually, most of the work targeted for completion by Q3-Q4 2026
Proved reserves nearly doubled to 32.1M BOE (about $27/share post-split) and 31 of 32 wells in progress at closing are online and producing, with the majority outperforming type curves
summary: PEDEVCO's first report as a combined company (Juniper merger closed Oct 31, 2025) showed Q4 revenue of $23.1M, Adjusted EBITDA of $15.4M and production of 483,159 BOE (about 5,300 BOE/d), with Adjusted EBITDA up 203% YoY despite a 16% decline in realized crude prices. Full-year net loss was $10.4M, driven by $7.5M of non-recurring merger costs, $8.1M of deferred tax expense and $2.8M of accelerated share-based compensation. Guidance: FY2026 Adjusted EBITDA of $60M-$70M at $65/bbl oil and $3.50/Mcf gas, with capex of $16M-$20M (roughly $10M-$13M of LOE optimization) and a target leverage of about 1.2-1.3x; no prior guidance was disclosed in the text, so the guidance is the initial combined-company outlook. Management guided Q1 2026 as the peak production quarter, with volumes settling toward roughly 6,400-6,500 BOE/d on decline, and pointed to LOE savings of $10M-$12M annually as the main forward driver.

negative_highlights: Q4 net revenue fell 41% year-over-year due to a $2.9 million reversal of terminated international license agreement
Weight loss business (Flat Tummy) continues to decline as the industry shifts toward GLP-1 products
Full-year income from operations dropped significantly, with normalized results still impacted by increased professional fees for corporate development
positive_highlights: Normalized gross margin excluding one-time charges expanded to 68.8% in Q4 compared to prior year
Beverage division generated over $2.5 million run-rate revenue for 2026 following successful Mexico subsidiary launch and Costco shipments
Cash position strengthened significantly with cash and equivalents rising from $687k at end of 2024 to $2.6M in Q4 2025
summary: Synergy CHC Corp reported a Q4 FY2025 net revenue of $6.07 million and a full-year revenue of $30.38 million, both representing significant year-over-year declines driven by the termination of an international license agreement ($2.9M reversal) and GLP-1 headwinds in weight loss products. Management highlighted that excluding one-time charges (bad debt write-offs, inventory obsolescence), normalized gross margins would have expanded to 68.8% for Q4 and $3 million income from operations was expected for the full year without these items. The company maintains a cautious outlook citing macro volatility in international markets while focusing on executing beverage growth initiatives in Mexico and restoring TV advertising.

negative_highlights: Q4 revenue missed significantly due to a challenging consumer spending environment causing lower case volume.
Full-year adjusted EBITDA margin contracted from 12% in FY2024 to 10%, reflecting the impact of prior year growth and current headwinds.
Cash flow from operations declined sharply to $3.1 million compared to $11.4 million in fiscal 2024.
positive_highlights: Same-store sales turned positive in February after being down 22% at the start of FY2025, indicating stabilization.
Gross margin expanded by roughly 2 percentage points to approximately 59%, driven by an $18.3 million decline in cost of services and a reduction in SG&A expenses of ~$5 million.
Company strengthened its balance sheet with cash at $8.4 million, gross debt reduced to $56 million via ATM proceeds and term loan paydowns.
summary: AirSculpt reported Q4 FY2025 revenue of $33.4 million, a decline of approximately 15% year-over-year driven by lower case volume and same-store sales down 16%. Adjusted EBITDA was $2.5 million with an expansion to roughly 7.4%, while full-year adjusted EBITDA margin contracted from 12% in FY2024 to 10% due to the revenue miss. Management provided a cautious outlook for fiscal 2026, guiding revenue between $151 million and $157 million (midpoint implying ~3% comparable growth) with adjusted EBITDA expected between $15 million and $17 million.

negative_highlights: Gross loss of $1.3 million versus $194,000 prior year; managed-services margins remain negative
Net loss from continuing operations of $15.2 million, and management expects G&A to increase over the next 12 months
The $4.4 million of revenue is essentially all from an eight-month acquisition; the legacy U.S. SemiCab business generated $300,000 and no Apex SaaS revenue exists yet, with no signing timeline given
positive_highlights: Annualized revenue run rate reached nearly $10 million in December 2025, with guidance for $15-20 million by end-2026
Secured four new Fortune 500 clients in India and converted five pilots into multi-million dollar contract expansions
Cash rose to $10.9 million as of March 25, 2026 from $6.1 million at year-end, and liabilities were cut almost 50%
summary: FY2025 continuing-operations revenue rose 1,370% to $4.4 million, but that is almost entirely the eight-month consolidation of acquired SMCB (SemiCab India), which contributed $4.4 million while legacy U.S. SemiCab generated $300,000 in 2024. Gross loss widened to $1.3 million from $194,000 as truck contracts are signed ahead of route utilization, and net loss from continuing operations was $15.2 million versus $18.9 million. Management guided the annualized revenue run rate from nearly $10 million at December 2025 to $15-20 million by end-2026 and expects gross loss as a percent of revenue to shrink, with cash of $10.9 million as of March 25, 2026. No SaaS revenue has been recognized yet; management repeatedly declined to give a timeline for Apex contract signings.

negative_highlights: Net loss expanded to $16.6 million ($4.11 EPS) from a prior year loss of $1.9 million.
Operating expenses surged to $16.8 million due to a $7.8 million non-cash unrealized loss and a $5.6 million IP impairment.
Management explicitly stated they would not provide specific numbers regarding the M&A pipeline search.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew materially to $1.1M from $27k due to successful implementation of the Avalanche treasury strategy.
Company generated approximately $2.5M in AVAX staking rewards since November, representing an annualized yield of 5.5%.
Cash and cash equivalents reached $22.1 million, providing approximately 3 years of operating runway without external capital.
summary: Total revenue increased materially to $1.1 million in Q4 FY2025 compared to $27,000 in the prior year quarter, driven by new staking rewards and Bitcoin mining. However, net loss widened significantly to $16.6 million ($4.11 EPS) due to a $7.8 million non-cash unrealized loss on digital assets and a $5.6 million IP impairment. Management provided forward guidance for 2026 expecting positive EBITDA under current market conditions, supported by a new $40 million share repurchase program.

negative_highlights: Gold production at How Mine fell to approximately 25,000 oz from 36,743 oz in the prior year due to transition between ore bodies.
Cash cost per ounce rose by $1,653 to approximately $3,800/oz due to lower volumes against a fixed cost base.
The company decided to let licenses for 13 exploration assets in the DRC lapse to focus capital on core operations.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA grew 18% to $29 million despite a significant drop in production volumes due to mine transition.
All-in sustaining costs were maintained below the prior year range, reflecting disciplined cost management and optimized power costs.
Red Wing dewatering is progressing as expected with water levels reduced to 7.8m after pumping 145,000 cubic meters.
summary: Namib Minerals reported full year 2025 revenue of $82.6 million and adjusted EBITDA of $29 million, driven by a 44% increase in gold prices to an average realized price of $3,156/oz despite production declining to approximately 25,000 oz at How Mine. Management delivered on full year production guidance and exceeded cost targets, with all-in sustaining costs remaining below the prior year range. The company provided 2026 guidance for production between 28,000-31,500 oz and adjusted EBITDA of $50-62 million based on a gold price assumption of $4,500/oz.

negative_highlights: Q4 2025 consolidated revenue decreased 8.3 million to 50.3 million, with global cinema revenue down 14% and operating income down 76%.
Q4 2025 adjusted EBITDA fell 25% to 5.1 million, and net loss per share widened to $0.11 from $0.10.
New Zealand cinema revenue declined 36% in Q4 and 14% for the full year, with full-year operating income turning to a loss of $479,000.
positive_highlights: Full-year adjusted EBITDA increased 744% to $17.8 million, and global cinema operating income improved 230% to $3.6 million.
Global debt reduced from $202.7 million to $185.1 million (almost 10%), with interest expense down $3.2 million or 15% year-over-year.
2026 global cinema trading is ahead by over 11% year-to-date, and F&B spend per person set all-time records in 2025.
summary: Q4 2025 consolidated revenue fell 8.3 million to 50.3 million versus Q4 2024, with a net loss of 2.6 million and adjusted EBITDA down 25% to 5.1 million; full-year revenue declined 4% to 203 million. Management explicitly called the quarter 'somewhat disappointing,' citing a weaker film slate and FX headwinds, though full-year adjusted EBITDA rose 744% to 17.8 million and debt was reduced by almost 10%. Guidance was not provided, but management noted 2026 global cinema trading is up over 11% year-to-date and expressed confidence in a stronger 2026 box office.

negative_highlights: note-side revenue fell to $0.2 million in Q4 from $2.7 million a year earlier, driven by lower impression inventory
Gross margin contracted to 27% from 32%, and Q4 net loss widened to $12.6 million from $6.6 million
Cash fell to $0.7 million from $1.4 million, and the company received a NASDAQ listing deficiency notice on stockholders' equity
positive_highlights: note-side revenue grew 28% to $8.2 million in Q4 and 10% for the full year
$1.7 million of Q4 revenue came from customers in new verticals, with about $7 million from new customers for the year
Full-year operating expenses fell 18% to $25.2 million, a $5.4 million reduction
summary: Direct Digital reported Q4 2025 revenue of $8.4 million, down from $9.1 million a year ago, as watch-side revenue grew 28% to $8.2 million but watch-side revenue collapsed to $0.2 million from $2.7 million. Gross margin fell to 27% from 32%, net loss widened to $12.6 million from $6.6 million (including $7.4 million of non-operational financing costs), and adjusted EBITDA loss was $3.6 million versus a $3.4 million loss last year. Management guided to break-even or better quarterly performance in H2 2026, ~10% annual watch-side growth, and roughly $500,000 per quarter of cost savings beginning in Q2. The company also disclosed a NASDAQ listing deficiency notice regarding stockholders' equity and said it is evaluating steps to regain compliance.

negative_highlights: Full-year revenue declined significantly due to the divestiture of the Lori Goldstein brand and a supplier transition gap.
Results were explicitly described as 'less than our expectations' driven by the Halston business not materializing.
Management remains cautious regarding the near term due to lingering inflation, trade tariffs, and geopolitical instability.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA loss improved by 24% year-over-year to $600,000.
Social media following grew from 5 million to 46 million with new influencer-led brands.
Halston delivered a strong second half of 2025 despite missing full-year targets.
summary: Xcel Brands reported Q4 FY2025 revenue of $1.17 million, a decline from the prior year quarter primarily due to a supplier transition gap in its HSN business. Full-year 2025 revenue fell to $4.94 million from $8.26 million following the divestiture of the Lori Goldstein brand. While adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed to $600,000 (from $792,000), management explicitly stated results were less than expectations due to a failed Halston deal and supply transition issues.

negative_highlights: Full year net revenue declined 14% to $206 million due to Agency weakness and lack of Political spend.
National revenue declined approximately 34% for the full year, with a 50% drop in Q4.
New business declined 14% for the full year and 18% in Q4.
positive_highlights: Digital revenue increased 21% on a same-station basis to approximately $49.5 million.
Digital operating margins expanded significantly to over 29% in Q4 2025 from 17.4% in Q4 2024.
Total debt is expected to be reduced from approximately $220 million to $110 million upon completion of the debt exchange by end of April.
summary: Full year net revenue declined to approximately $206 million from $240 million in 2024, driven by a $13.6 million absence of Political advertising and structural declines in Agency channels. Adjusted EBITDA fell to $10.5 million from $25.8 million, though Digital revenue grew 21% on a same-station basis to $49.5 million. Management raised Q1 2026 guidance expectations for stabilization, projecting same-station revenue down only in the mid-single digits compared to prior year.

negative_highlights: Single-family rental expansion was scaled back from ~90 to ~60 units, with the company citing corporate-ownership pressure and an unresolved return test (~8-10% unlevered)
Margins moderated as lot-delivery investment ran ahead of contract milestones, and lot development pace is guided to normalize lower for the rest of the year
Industrial water demand is variable with no meaningful take-or-pay, so oil and gas revenue is heavily tied to commodity prices
positive_highlights: Q2 net income of roughly $1 million and EPS of about $0.05, up ~36% YoY, marking a 27th consecutive profitable quarter
Half-year revenue of ~$14.3M and profit of ~$9M put the company at about 50% of full-year guidance despite winter normally being the weakest seasonal quarter
Industrial water sales are expected to exceed prior guidance, with a dedicated rig working ~200 permits that should take ~3 years to drill
summary: Pure Cycle reported H1 FY2026 revenue of roughly $5.1 million and gross profit of about $2.8 million, with Q2 net income a little over $1 million (~$0.05 EPS), up about 36% YoY, and a 27th consecutive profitable quarter. Management said it is tracking at about 50% of full-year guidance (~$14.3M revenue vs a $26-30M range, ~$9M profit vs a ~$19M range), reaffirmed FY26 revenue of $26-30M and EPS of $0.43-0.52, and deferred FY27 guidance to Q3. Land lot deliveries were pulled forward on a mild winter (Phase II-C ~95% and II-D ~80% complete), while the single-family rental build-out was cut from ~90 to ~60 units and industrial water sales were cited as likely to exceed plan on higher oil prices.

negative_highlights: Mytesi prescription volume decreased by 12.2% in Q4 2025 compared to the same period last year.
Net loss attributable to common shareholders increased to $53.6 million for the year ended December 31, 2025, up from $38.5 million in 2024.
Loss on extinguishment of debt increased to a $1.8 million loss due to modifications in a royalty interest agreement.
positive_highlights: Received $16 million upfront payment plus additional payments from the Future Pak license agreement, providing non-dilutive capital for the rare disease pipeline.
Crofelemer demonstrated reduction of parenteral support by 12.5% to 37% in pediatric intestinal failure patients in recent proof-of-concept studies.
Targeted New Drug Application filing for Microvillus Inclusion Disease (MVID) is set for the first half of 2027.
summary: Jaguar Health reported Q4 FY2025 net revenue of approximately $3.2 million, representing a 5% increase from Q3 but an 8% decrease year-over-year due to a 12.2% decline in Mytesi prescription volume. The company recognized significant non-dilutive cash inflows from a new U.S. out-license agreement with Future Pak, receiving $16 million upfront and additional payments, which funds its rare disease intestinal failure pipeline targeting MVID and short bowel syndrome. Management maintains a cautious outlook on the HIV market while emphasizing that the strategic pivot to rare diseases is fully aligned with their 2026 business development strategy.

negative_highlights: Commercial/Industrial NOI fell 11.8% in Q4 and 13.6% for the year; occupancy dropped to 47.5% (69.9% ex-Chelsea) from 95.6%
2026 NOI guidance of $37.1-$37.7 million is roughly flat to below 2025's ~$37.9 million, with G&A rising to $15-16 million and G&A/NOI elevated in the low 40% range
Multifamily Q4 was below expectations: NOI down 2.6%, Maren occupancy ~89%, ~88% economic occupancy, D.C. supply and delinquency pressure
positive_highlights: Mining & Royalties NOI rose 11.5% in Q4 and 1.5% for the year, providing durable high-margin cash flow
~$3.3 million of incremental annual NOI available from ~423,000 sq ft of vacant industrial space (~52% of the segment)
$144 million year-end liquidity, net debt to enterprise value ~21%, weighted average interest rate ~5.24%
summary: Full-year 2025 NOI was ~$37.9 million and FFO ~$22.1 million ($1.16/share), with ~$144 million liquidity, which management called generally in line with expectations. Segment trends diverged: Commercial/Industrial NOI fell 13.6% for the year with occupancy down to 47.5% (69.9% excluding Chelsea) from 95.6%, Multifamily NOI dipped 0.4%, while Mining & Royalties NOI rose 1.5%. 2026 guidance is an 'investment year': NOI of ~$37.1-$37.7 million (roughly flat to down) with G&A rising to $15-16 million and G&A/NOI elevated in the low 40% range before normalizing, while the ~$33.5 million Altman Industrial acquisition added ~1.6 million sq ft of pipeline. Management framed slowing industrial leasing as timing rather than demand weakness and highlighted ~$3.3 million of incremental NOI from lease-up and a $441 million development pipeline.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined by 14.4% YoY as customers accelerated purchases ahead of anticipated trade policy shifts in Q4 2024

Net loss attributable to shareholders widened to $2.6 million from a net loss of $0.4 million, driven primarily by valuation allowance on deferred tax assets and non-recurring IPO-related compensation
positive_highlights: Gross margin expanded by 210 basis points to 26.7% driven by better relative performance of higher-margin businesses
Operating loss improved significantly from $1.3 million in the prior year period to a GAAP operating loss of only $0.7 million due to optimized warehouse operations and lower R&D costs
summary: Fourth quarter revenue decreased by 14.4% to $30.5 million compared to the prior year due to order pull-forward effects and tariff headwinds impacting volumes in sanitaryware and shower systems businesses. Gross margin expanded 210 basis points to 26.7%, while GAAP operating loss narrowed from a loss of $1.3 million to $0.7 million, though net loss widened to $2.6 million due to non-recurring items including valuation allowances on deferred tax assets and IPO-related compensation.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA margin fell to 20% from 22.8% YoY, helped by a 2.1% incentive comp reversal
FY2025 free cash flow worsened to -$46 million from -$7.2 million due to inventory investment
Guidance implies FY2026 adjusted EBITDA margin of 4-7% versus 7.5% in FY2025, and Q1 2026 adjusted EBITDA -5% to -7% versus -1.9% a year ago
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 20% YoY to $91.7 million, with subscription and reserve rental revenue up 20.4%
Gross margin expanded to 38.6% from 37.7% YoY, and up sharply from 29.6% in Q3
Ending active subscribers rose 20.1% YoY to 143,796, and Q4 free cash flow was positive $0.5 million
summary: Q4 FY2025 revenue was $91.7 million, up 20% YoY but up only 4.7% sequentially, with ending active subscribers at 143,796 up 20.1% YoY though down 3.4% from Q3. Gross margin expanded to 38.6% from 37.7% a year ago, but adjusted EBITDA fell to $18.3 million (20% of revenue) versus $17.4 million (22.8% of revenue) in Q4 FY2024, aided by a 2.1% incentive comp reversal. FY2025 free cash flow deteriorated to -$46 million from -$7.2 million as inventory investment front-loaded. Guidance calls for Q1 2026 revenue of $85-87 million (22-25% growth) but adjusted EBITDA margin of -5% to -7% (versus -1.9% a year ago), and FY2026 double-digit revenue growth with adjusted EBITDA margin of 4-7% (versus 7.5% in FY2025) on significantly higher revenue share expenses.

negative_highlights: Loan growth expectations have slightly slowed down from robust levels seen previously due to sizable early payoffs.
Energy portfolio is at a 10-year low (over 8% of the portfolio) with limited dynamic change expected despite energy price spikes.
positive_highlights: Management stated goals for the year remain intact despite a slight slowdown in loan growth compared to Q3/Q4 of last year.
summary: Bank7 Corp reported Q1 FY2026 results where management expressed satisfaction with performance despite market expectations of rate cuts being replaced by potential increases due to Middle Eastern conflict and commodity prices. The company maintained its goal for moderate single-digit loan growth, noting a slight slowdown from the robust pace seen in late last year but expecting similar bookings this year. Net Interest Margin (NIM) is modeled between 440-445 basis points excluding fees, with fee income expected to revert to normalized levels of 28-35 bps.

negative_highlights: Gross margin contracted 100 bps to 49.1% due to ~300 bps tariff impact, 160 bps promotional events, and 125 bps freight costs.
Q4 adjusted EBITDA fell to $4.5 million from $5.4 million in the prior-year quarter.
A $6 million bad debt expense related to the Saks Global reorganization hurt GAAP profitability, contributing to a net loss of $3.6 million.
positive_highlights: Direct-to-consumer sales increased 10.4%, driving total net sales up 4.7% to $83.7 million.
Adjusted net income more than tripled to $2.4 million ($0.18 per share) from $0.8 million ($0.06 per share) last year.
Full-year FY2026 guidance implies net sales growth of 3%-6% and adjusted EBITDA of 5%-5.5% of sales, continuing momentum on top of FY2025 adjusted EBITDA of $15.1 million.
summary: Vince Holding reported Q4 FY2025 net sales up 4.7% to $83.7 million, with DTC up 10.4% and wholesale down 1.2% due to paused Saks Global shipments. Adjusted net income rose to $2.4 million ($0.18 per share) from $0.8 million ($0.06), though adjusted EBITDA declined to $4.5 million from $5.4 million. Gross margin contracted 100 bps to 49.1% on tariffs, promotions, and freight, partly offset by pricing. Management guided Q1 FY2026 sales growth of 8.5%-10.5% and full-year growth of 3%-6%, with adjusted operating income at 3.5%-4% and adjusted EBITDA at 5%-5.5% of sales.

negative_highlights: Dividends will not be paid this year to fund expansion CapEx plans.
Open pit life reduced by 100-130 meters, deferring underground mining of the Main Zone by at least five years.
Full-year CapEx is expected towards the upper end of guidance ($20 million).
positive_highlights: Gold production hit a quarterly record of just under 7,500 ounces.
Revenue exceeded $34 million with gross profit margins at 62%.
Adjusted EBITDA reached over $20 million in the quarter.
summary: TRX Gold reported a record quarter with gold production of just under 7,500 ounces and revenue exceeding $34 million driven by an average realized price of $4,655/oz. Adjusted EBITDA reached over $20 million for the quarter, while full-year guidance remains on track to produce between 25,000 and 30,000 ounces with cash costs guided at $1,400-$1,600/oz. Management confirmed that dividends will not be paid this year due to capital expenditure plans for plant expansion.

negative_highlights: Legacy VIP appliance revenue fell 18% to $6.5 million due to strategic pivot and increased discounts.
Net loss widened to $21.2 million, reflecting high upfront costs of the new business model.
Q4 revenue declined from Q3 levels due to unexpected provider attrition and lost doctor days.
positive_highlights: Full year revenue grew 16% despite the strategic pivot away from legacy VIP dentists.
Gross margin held steady at 60% despite significant cost increases from integration.
SCN operations are fully booked through April 2026 with in-network status secured for major payers.
summary: Full year 2025 revenue increased by $2.4 million (16%) driven by a $4.8 million rise in sleep testing services and $2.2 million in treatment revenue from the Sleep Center of Nevada acquisition, partially offset by a $1.4 million decline in legacy VIP appliance sales. Gross margin remained constant at 60%, while operating expenses surged to $30.4 million due to integration costs, resulting in a net loss of $21.2 million. Management noted Q4 revenue was lower than Q3 due to unexpected provider attrition and staffing challenges, though they expect significant improvement in Q1 and Q2 as new providers ramp up.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to $2.7 million in Q4 from $1.3 million in the prior year due to increased hiring and operating expenses.
Revenue remains extremely low at $15,000 for the quarter, with over 90% derived from a single customer (Hancock Health).
Management explicitly stated they are not pursuing permanent deployments yet to avoid obsolete inventory as they iterate on AP3/AP4/AP5 platforms.
positive_highlights: Executed a $10 million draw from the credit facility in January 2026, strengthening the balance sheet and extending runway.
Secured 10th patent issued March 31st, 2026, enabling shared use of secure delivery endpoints across multiple users.
Live deployment at Hancock Health demonstrated reliable operation within active care conditions, reducing staff walking time.
summary: Arrive AI reported Q4 FY2025 revenue of $15,000 (all recurring subscription) and a net loss of $2.7 million, driven by higher operating expenses from hiring. The company disclosed an accounting error regarding convertible notes that will result in restated prior quarters but explicitly stated no cash impact or change to current Q4 revenue figures. Management emphasized a strategy of short-term deployments for learning rather than permanent sales, noting the AP5 platform is expected to be deployment-ready later this year.

negative_highlights: Guidance of about $160 million was not broken down by segment, and management declined to disaggregate Drone Nerds from the rest of the business
The VTOL/TriFan program was paused and reclassified into the ADS division, with no spend going against it
Revenue remains concentrated in distribution of foreign-made drones and is exposed to the DJI/Autel FCC ban, which management described as disruptive with mixed customer adoption
positive_highlights: FY2025 pro forma revenue of over $121 million with positive cash flow and gross margins above 20%, anchored by the Drone Nerds distribution platform
Management guided calendar 2025 revenue to roughly $160 million versus the $121 million base, implying meaningful growth
Company is bidding on up to approximately $150 million of contract value with $1.5 billion of stated production value across Navy, Marines, Air Force, and SOCOM programs
summary: XTI reported FY2025 pro forma revenue of over $121 million with roughly $41 million in Q4, at over 20% gross margin and positive cash flow, heavily weighted to the Drone Nerds distribution business. Management guided to approximately $160 million for calendar 2025, though it declined to break the figure down by segment and noted it does not separately discuss Q4 results. The call was largely narrative: the VTOL/TriFan program is paused with no spend, the company exited a division, and it is bidding on up to roughly $150 million of government contract value with $1.5 billion in claimed production value, none of it won. No EPS, net income, or prior-period comparison figures were stated, and a DJI FCC transition was described as disruptive but not traumatic.

negative_highlights: FDA placed the IND for Tivoxavir on clinical hold due to concerns with the toxicology data package.
Cash equivalents and note weakness in-term investments decreased to approximately $3.8 million from $21.3 million year-over-year.
Management cannot confirm if the MHRA will approve the U.K. challenge study as submitted without potential delays.
positive_highlights: Revenue increased significantly to $2.8 million from $226,000 in the prior year.
Net income turned positive at $9.2 million compared to a $166.5 million loss last year.
Acquired-in-process research and development expense was zero for 2025 versus $117.5 million in 2024.
summary: Traws Pharma reported full-year 2025 revenue of $2.8 million, a significant increase from $226,000 in 2024 driven by deferred revenue recognition following the termination of a legacy oncology licensing agreement. The company achieved a net income of $9.2 million ($0.83 per share) compared to a net loss of $166.5 million in the prior year, primarily due to the absence of acquired-in-process research and development expenses. While management secured a $60 million private financing to fund clinical trials, the FDA placed the company's Investigational New Drug application for Tivoxavir on clinical hold due to toxicology data concerns, with a goal to resolve this by late 2026.

negative_highlights: Q4 GAAP gross margin remained deeply negative at -38% on $340 million of impairment charges, and full-year GAAP gross margin was -35% on $1.1 billion of impairments
U.S. retail sales fell to 7% of total volume from 14% in 2024 amid expired EV tax credits and adverse regulation, and average cash burn remained elevated at ~$120 million per year
Management flagged ongoing pricing pressure and higher tariffs/duties as persistent headwinds, with 2026 retail growth guidance of only low double digits (below 2025's 34%)
positive_highlights: Q4 revenue rose 54% YoY to $887 million and full-year revenue surpassed $3 billion, up 50% YoY on record retail sales of 60,100 units (+34%)
Adjusted gross margin improved to +2% in Q4 from -39% a year ago, with full-year adjusted gross margin near breakeven at -0.7% versus -12.5% in 2024
Secured $1.2 billion in new equity from June 2025 to March 2026 and $639 million of shareholder loans converting to equity, ending the year with ~$1.2 billion cash and covenant compliance
summary: Polestar reported Q4 FY2025 retail sales of over 15,600 cars, up 27% year-over-year, and revenue of $887 million, up 54%, but gross margin remained negative at -38% due to $340 million in impairment charges; adjusted gross margin turned positive at +2% versus -39% in the prior-year quarter. Full-year revenue surpassed $3 billion (+50% YoY) with record retail sales of 60,100 units (+34%), yet GAAP gross margin was -35% on $1.1 billion in impairments, while adjusted gross margin improved to near breakeven at -0.7%. Q4 net loss was $799 million (improved 32% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed to -$223 million from -$470 million; full-year adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed 27% to -$783 million. Guidance for 2026 reiterates low double-digit retail sales growth with progress through the year, supported by $1.2 billion in new equity raised since June 2025 and ~$639 million of shareholder loans converting to equity.

MainStreet Bancshares reported Q1 FY2026 EPS of $0.48, net interest income up 5% after credit provision, and net interest margin of 3.47% (core NIM 3.54%), with ROAA of 0.76% and return on tangible common equity of 7.58%; results included a non-recurring $685,000 loss on an OREO disposition. Net charge-offs were low at $259,000, classified loans were 3.09% of gross loans and non-accruals 2.88%, and the company repurchased over 482,000 shares across the last two quarters for $0.30 per share accretion. Guidance was limited to loan growth expectations of 3%-5% for 2026 and an efficiency ratio target of roughly 53%-55%, with management noting the pace of deposit cost improvement should slow from prior quarters. The key change versus prior periods was continued deposit repricing that lowered funding costs 64 basis points over five quarters, though a competitive deposit market and reversal of interest on a few non-accrual loans tempered the margin benefit.

negative_highlights: Operating income and net income declined year-over-year in the second half due to increased expenses for building the Bitcoin treasury platform.
Online sales declined in the second half reflecting a deliberate reduction in marketing spend and strategic shift away from lower-margin promotional channels.
positive_highlights: Record full-year revenue of $39.2 million with positive adjusted EBITDA.
Gross margin expanded 303 bps to 31.4% driven by supply chain optimization and favorable costs.
Second-half revenue grew 17% year-over-year to $23.6 million reflecting strong demand in core Asia markets.
summary: DDC reported full year 2025 record revenue of $39.2 million and positive adjusted EBITDA, with second-half revenue growing 17% year-over-year to $23.6 million. Gross margins improved 303 basis points to 31.4% for the full year, supported by supply chain optimization and favorable raw material costs. The company significantly expanded its Bitcoin treasury holdings, doubling from 1,181 BTC at year-end to 2,383 BTC as of today.

negative_highlights: Loan portfolio remained flat at $3 billion as customers refinance into secondary markets rather than growing the bank's book
Deposit balances declined slightly from year-end levels due to normal cash flow fluctuations and seasonality
New loan activity is described as 'mild' with new construction projects still ramping up slowly
positive_highlights: Net income increased $2.8 million (35%) YoY to $10.6 million
Net interest margin expanded 12 bps QoQ, with deposit costs declining 40 bps YoY
Credit quality remains pristine with no loans past due >30 days and watch list down 20% year-over-year
summary: West Bancorporation reported Q1 FY2026 net income of $10.6 million, a 35% increase from the prior year quarter driven by a 17% rise in net interest income and margin expansion of 12 basis points to previous quarters. Loan balances remained flat at $3 billion due to secondary market refinancing payoffs, while deposits saw normal seasonal fluctuations with about 75% remaining on a specific municipal bond deposit tranche from the prior year. Management maintained guidance for continued earnings improvement assuming steady Fed rates and expressed confidence in future loan growth as construction projects ramp up.

negative_highlights: Net income fell 40% to $0.985 million and EPS dropped to $0.24 from $0.41
Core/legacy gross margin declined roughly 200 basis points, and SG&A rose to 36% of sales from 34%
Net debt increased to $38.6 million from $27.2 million, and the company bought about $10 million of incremental inventory to hedge Iran-war supply risk
positive_highlights: Net sales rose 14% to $52.3 million, with Europe up 19% in local currency and Canada up 11% (16% overall), and U.S. up 12%
Gross margin expanded to 39.7% from 39.0% on higher-margin My Medic direct-to-consumer mix; Spill Magic sales grew over 30% in the quarter
Roughly $14.2 million of free cash flow generated in the trailing twelve months and dividends of about $2.4 million paid
summary: Acme United reported Q1 FY2026 net sales up 14% to $52.3 million, but net income fell to $0.985 million ($0.24 per diluted share) from $1.6 million ($0.41) a year ago, a 40% decline driven by peak-cost tariffs flowing through inventory and roughly $300,000 of non-recurring Med-Nap quality-assurance expense. Gross margin was 39.7% versus 39.0%, but the CFO said core/legacy gross margin fell about 200 basis points due to tariffs and roughly 8 points of the sales gain came from the newly acquired, breakeven My Medic. Management said the tariff drag should lessen over the next three quarters, the Med-Nap QA cost will not repeat, and cited strong order trends at Spill Magic (up over 30%), record European first aid, and easy Westcott comparisons for the rest of the year; no formal full-year guidance was given, and net debt rose to $38.6 million from $27.2 million.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EPS fell $6.41 sequentially to $44.86 and NIM compressed 11 bps to 3.09% as the late-2025 Fed cut pressured earning asset yields.
Non-accrual loans rose to 96 bps from isolated credits, and management flagged elevated losses in commercial general office and SVB commercial books in the medium term.

The CET1 target was cut 50 bps to 10%-10.5% and buybacks are expected to moderate toward the lower end of $600-900 million per quarter, while net interest income guidance was tightened on persistent DDA pressure and deposit competition.
positive_highlights: Period-end deposits grew $9.3 billion, or 5.7% sequentially, with SVB tech/healthcare and Global Fund Banking up $5.6 billion.
Adjusted non-interest expense came in $38 million lower sequentially, outperforming prior guidance, and the full-year expense range was reduced to $5.34-5.43 billion.

Net charge-offs fell 9 bps sequentially to 30 bps, beating guidance, and the full-year net charge-off outlook was lowered to 30-40 bps; full-year adjusted non-interest income guidance was raised to $2.12-2.22 billion.
summary: First Citizens reported Q1 FY2026 adjusted EPS of $44.86, down $6.41 sequentially, on net income of $560 million, with NIM compressing 11 bps to 3.09% and net interest income down $101 million, both largely in line with prior guidance. Period-end deposits grew 5.7% sequentially to $9.3 billion and period-end loans rose 0.5%, while adjusted non-interest expense beat guidance by $38 million; credit was favorable with net charge-offs of 30 bps. Full-year loan and deposit guidance was reaffirmed, adjusted non-interest income guidance was raised to $2.12-2.22 billion, expenses were reduced to $5.34-5.43 billion (plus a $20-30 million brand-strategy add), and the net interest income range was marginally tightened to $6.5-6.8 billion. Management also lowered its CET1 target by 50 bps to 10%-10.5% and signaled a slower buyback pace as it approaches that range.

negative_highlights: Total revenue up only 0.3% YoY, below 4-8% guidance pace
Jafra Mexico revenue moderated due to productivity focus, associate base declined
Q1 had one fewer week, impacting reported growth; Betterware comparable growth 3.3%
positive_highlights: EBITDA grew 14% YoY, margin expanded 211 bps to 17.4%
Jafra US net revenue up 8.6% in USD, associate base up 3.4%
Tupperware transaction expected Q2 approval, immediately accretive ~40% to EPS
summary: BeFra reported flat revenue growth of 0.3% YoY, below the high end of its 4-8% full-year guidance, but delivered a 14% EBITDA increase with margin expanding 211 bps to 17.4% (18.4% ex-Tupperware expenses). Management highlighted improving associate trends at Betterware, strong Jafra US growth of 8.6% in USD, and the expected Q2 approval of the accretive Tupperware acquisition, which will add ~40% to EPS. They maintained full-year revenue growth guidance of 4-8%, with an expected inflection in Jafra Mexico starting in Q2.

negative_highlights: Operating profit declined to $3.4 million from $3.8 million
Advertising revenue slowed late Q1 due to geopolitical issues
EPS reduced by $0.13 due to member acquisition costs
positive_highlights: Revenue increased 5% year-over-year, with growth across all segments
Club member growth up 112% year-over-year
Expect membership fees to account for over 20% of revenue this year
summary: Q1 2026 revenue rose 5% YoY to $24.3 million, but operating profit fell to $3.4 million (14% of revenue) from $3.8 million, partly due to higher marketing spend on club member acquisition. The company guided for continued revenue growth and expects margins to recover as renewals grow, but noted a slowdown in advertising revenue late in Q1 due to the war and geopolitical uncertainty. Membership fees are expected to exceed 20% of revenue this year.

negative_highlights: GAAP EPS declined to $0.30 from $0.92 YoY due to prior-year gain on deconsolidation
Mortgage revenue impacted by market volatility late in Q1, masking an otherwise blowout quarter
positive_highlights: Operating EPS up 126% YoY to $0.33, ROA doubled to 84 bps
Net interest margin expanded to 3.43% from 3.15% YoY, with expectations for further expansion
Revenue up ~34% YoY with only 4% OpEx growth, showing strong operating leverage
summary: Primis Financial reported Q1 FY2026 operating EPS of $0.33, up 126% from $0.14 in the year-ago quarter, with ROA improving to 84 bps from 40 bps. NIM expanded to 3.43% from 3.15%, and loans grew 11.7% YoY to $3.4B, with mortgage warehouse near $460M. Management highlighted strong operating leverage (revenue up 34%, OpEx up only 4%) and raised its mortgage production outlook to ~$1.8B for 2026, while guiding to further margin expansion and an aspirational 1% ROA by year-end.

negative_highlights: Net interest income was constrained by $114 million of late-quarter closings and elevated early payoff activity
Loan payoffs, including a loan yielding roughly 4.85%, create a drag on near-term yield, though management expects offsetting production yields near 6.2%
Non-performing loans increased 6 bps to 0.16% of the portfolio, driven by two past-due residential real estate loans
positive_highlights: Adjusted EPS of $0.47 with operating ROAA of 1.25% and operating ROAE of 15.92%
Loan growth of 10.1% YoY with $188 million in Q1 gross production, 60% closing in March and April activity remaining strong
Deposit costs fell 8 bps QoQ to 2.20%, helping stabilize margin at 3.27%
summary: USCB reported Q1 2026 GAAP net income of $9.4 million, or $0.51 per diluted share, with adjusted EPS of $0.47 that included a $619,000 tax benefit. Loans rose 10.1% YoY, deposits grew 8% YoY to $2.5 billion, and net interest margin held at 3.27% even as the reported margin was constrained by late-quarter closings and early payoffs. Management said the loan pipeline is among the strongest seen, guiding to flat-to-slightly-higher margin, and announced plans to open two to four branches in Broward and Palm Beach over three years.

negative_highlights: Adjusted net loss widened $5 million to $31.1 million versus $26.1 million in 2024, and operating expenses rose 15% to $29 million
No numerical 2026 revenue or earnings guidance was provided; Q4/full-year revenue was described by the CEO as a 'shortfall' tied to pulling the Aquanaut from the field
Six customers accounted for the majority of revenue, and management said the UAE/Master Investment Group engagement has been delayed by Middle East conflict with travel and ramp-up timing unknown
positive_highlights: Revenue grew roughly 190% to $5.3 million in FY2025 from $1.8 million in 2024, aided by the SeaTrepid acquisition
Net loss fell $94.1 million year-over-year to $40.8 million and shareholder equity turned positive at $7.7 million from a $20.4 million deficit
Cost of revenue as a percentage of revenue improved by approximately 300 percentage points, and G&A trended back toward pre-acquisition levels in the second half
summary: Nauticus Robotics reported FY2025 revenue of $5.3 million, up $3.5 million (roughly 190%) from $1.8 million in 2024, driven largely by the SeaTrepid acquisition. Net loss was $40.8 million versus $102.6 million-plus in 2024 (which included a $127.6 million debt extinguishment loss), while adjusted net loss widened $5 million to $31.1 million; cash rose to $7.6 million and shareholder equity turned positive at $7.7 million. Management gave no numerical 2026 guidance, saying revenue was suboptimal because the Aquanaut was pulled from the field on a technical issue that also disrupted ROV scheduling, with both Aquanauts ready to return to the Gulf in May. CEO John Gibson said the next call would be 'all about revenue,' targeting Q2 for visibility, while noting a delay in the UAE program tied to Middle East conflict.

negative_highlights: About $5M in merger charges pressured GAAP results in the quarter
Non-performing assets rose to roughly $11M, concentrated in commercial credits, not from the Presence acquisition
Quarterly expenses rose as a percentage of average assets, driven by technology investment, with opex guided no lower than $15.8M per quarter
positive_highlights: Net interest income hit a record $24.6M, up 38% YoY, with NIM expanding 38 bps to 3.68%
Post-acquisition organic growth since January 5: loans +$46M (8.4% annualized) and deposits +$70M (11.6% annualized)
Adjusted PPNR up about 11% linked-quarter; management now expects tangible book value payback ahead of original projections
summary: Record net interest income of $24.6M rose 38% YoY, with NIM up 38 bps YoY to 3.68% (8 bps linked-quarter); adjusted net income and EPS rose 35% and 14% respectively, though GAAP results included about $5M in merger charges. Since the January 5 Presence Bank close, loans grew roughly $46M (8.4% annualized) and deposits about $70M (11.6% annualized), and management now expects tangible book value payback ahead of original projections. Guidance: margin should expand another 3-5 bps over the next couple of quarters (less than Q1's 8 bps), opex around $15.8-16M per quarter is a reasonable run rate, and purchase accounting accretion is scheduled at about $2.2M for 2026 and $2M for 2027. Non-performing assets rose to roughly $11M, driven by commercial credits rather than the acquisition.

negative_highlights: Brass alloy ingot revenue fell to $994,000 from $4.3 million, with management not assuming a near-term recovery
Operating cash flow swung to a $9.0 million outflow from $2.0 million inflow, driven by a $9.7 million receivables build
Cash and cash equivalents declined to $957,000 from $1.85 million at the prior year-end
positive_highlights: Revenue rose 23% to a record $65.8 million and net income grew 82% to $11.8 million
Gross margin expanded 417 bps to 23.94%, helped by lower copper and aluminum raw material purchase prices
Copper alloy ingot revenue grew to $45.1 million with sales volume up 37% year-over-year
summary: One and One Green Technologies reported FY2025 revenue of $65.8 million, up 23% from $53.5 million, with copper alloy ingot revenue rising to $45.1 million (+37% on a volume basis) and aluminum alloy to $19.8 million, partly offset by brass alloy falling to $994,000 from $4.3 million. Gross margin expanded 417 bps to 23.94%, net income rose 82% to $11.8 million, and EPS was $0.2254 versus $0.1246. Operating cash flow swung to a $9.0 million outflow on $9.7 million higher receivables and other working capital build, while the October IPO raised roughly $11.5 million gross and the balance sheet remains debt-free. No formal numeric guidance was given; management outlined 2026 priorities in geographic expansion and a lithium battery recycling facility within three years, and explicitly said it is not modeling a brass recovery.

negative_highlights: Full-year 2025 revenue was GBP 423,000, a decrease from the prior year due to lower note weakness in-term commercial activity.
Reported operating loss of GBP 62.5 million and net loss of GBP 62.7 million, including approximately GBP 53.7 million in non-cash share-based compensation charges.
No forward financial guidance was provided; management indicated continued investment in U.S. expansion without specifying revenue or profitability targets.
positive_highlights: GBP 2 million of proceeds received since year-end from exercises under the performance incentive grant program, providing working capital support.
U.K. pilot processed over GBP 100 million in GMV through an invitation-only platform, validating the ShareBack acquisition model.
Company has begun active U.S. platform testing since November 2025 and is onboarding retail partners.
summary: WeShop reported full-year 2025 revenue of GBP 423,000, down year over year, which management attributed to reduced short-term commercial activity in the U.K. during its Nasdaq listing process. The company reported an operating loss of GBP 62.5 million and a net loss of GBP 62.7 million, heavily driven by non-cash share-based compensation of approximately GBP 35.9 million and GBP 17.8 million in G&A option awards. No formal forward guidance was provided, though management highlighted GBP 2 million in post-year-end proceeds from performance incentive grant exercises and ongoing U.S. platform testing. Management's commentary focused on long-term U.S. expansion and community-based ownership rather than near-term financial metrics, and CEO John Garner defended the company against negative Trustpilot reviews during Q&A.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA margin declined YoY due to higher operating expenses from executive team expansion, one-time corporate costs, and annual merit increases.
Q2 2026 EBITDA margin expected to be flat sequentially due to Phase I implementation costs for the landmark deal.
A $9.4 million charge will be recorded in Q2 related to accelerated vesting of executive restricted equity, including $2.8 million in cash bonus payments.
positive_highlights: TRCV increased 13% YoY to $152.1 million, an all-time high and the largest single-quarter increase in at least seven years.
Booking a landmark multi-year customer win (largest in company history) across multiple products, with phased implementation expected to be accretive to margins after Phase II go-live.
Gross retention rate reached its highest level in over seven years, and pipeline is up 41% YoY.
summary: Q1 FY2026 revenue was $34.8 million, up 4% YoY, the first positive revenue growth since 2023. Total Recurring Contract Value (TRCV) rose 13% YoY to $152.1 million, and new sales bookings grew over 200% YoY, driven by the largest deal in company history. Adjusted EBITDA was $9.4 million (27% margin), up 230 bps sequentially, and adjusted EPS was $0.21, up $0.05 sequentially. Management expects Q2 EBITDA margin to remain flat sequentially due to implementation costs for the landmark deal, with margin expansion resuming in Q3, and reiterated a path to low-30s EBITDA margin in the midterm.

negative_highlights: Gross margin down 470 basis points to 36.5% due to higher tariffs
Adjusted EPS fell to $0.24 from $0.73 in the prior year
Georgia Boot saw slight single-digit decline, though timing-driven
positive_highlights: Q1 sales up 9.1% year-over-year to $124.4 million, in line with expectations
Retail sales increased 16.5% to $42.7 million
Best booking season ever noted across new spring and fall 2026 products
summary: Rocky Brands reported Q1 FY2026 sales of $124.4 million, up 9.1% year-over-year, in line with expectations. Gross margin fell 470 basis points to 36.5% due to over $7 million in higher tariffs, and adjusted EPS dropped to $0.24 from $0.73. The company reiterated full-year guidance of ~6% revenue growth, with tariffs expected to be a ~$10 million headwind split roughly 70/30 between Q1 and Q2. Management cited strong full-price watching, D2C growth, and improving wholesale trends, but noted tariff uncertainty ahead.

negative_highlights: Book value per share decreased to $9.97 from a prior level of $10.48, reflecting significant unrealized losses.
The company reported a GAAP net loss of approximately $8.7 million or $0.27 per share entirely driven by the investment portfolio's performance in March.
Commercial loan resolution is taking longer than anticipated, with some hotel assets expected to wrap up as late as 2027.
positive_highlights: EAD of $0.26 exceeded the newly increased dividend of $0.24 per share, demonstrating earnings resilience despite market volatility.
Arc Home delivered a meaningful contribution to EAD of approximately $0.04 per share driven by strong non-agency originations and improved gain on sale margins.
Serious delinquencies in the non-agency portfolio remain low at 1.3%, with home equity portfolios even lower at 0.4%.
summary: Book value per share declined 4.9% to $9.97 due to net unrealized losses of approximately $8.7 million driven by March macroeconomic volatility and widening spreads. Despite the GAAP miss on book value, Earnings Available for Distribution (EAD) increased to $0.26 per share, fully covering the raised quarterly dividend of $0.24. Management noted that at least 50% of the unrealized decline had already recovered by April.

negative_highlights: Net sales declined 4.3% ex-divestiture, driven by lower print and agency volumes
Agency solution sales pulled back and project work shifting to AOR engagements
USPS rate increase expected up to 10% for Co-mail clients; European divestiture note payment past due
positive_highlights: Adjusted diluted EPS up 25% year-over-year
Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded from 7.2% to 7.7%
Returned $7 million to shareholders including dividend increase of 33%
summary: Quad reported Q1 2026 net sales of $581 million, down 4.3% excluding the European divestiture, with adjusted EBITDA of $45 million versus $46 million a year ago and adjusted diluted EPS up 25% to $0.25. Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to 7.7% from 7.2% due to cost actions and productivity. Management maintained full-year guidance despite postage increases and a temporary ink surcharge, while noting free cash flow was negative $107 million in the quarter, and a $6 million payment from the European divestiture was past due.

negative_highlights: Fraud charge-off of $0.22 per share hit earnings
Net interest margin compressed due to rate cuts and high deposit costs
At-risk non-performing loans increased to $13.2M
positive_highlights: Loan originations up 56% YoY, 65% QoQ
SBA gain on sale margin 4.79% exceeded budget of 4%
April SBA sales already at $39.5M with $2M gain
summary: GBank reported Q1 FY2026 results impacted by a $0.22 per share charge-off related to third-party credit card fraud, which management attributes to bot attacks on a canceled retail card program. Despite this, loan originations surged 56% YoY to $208 million, surpassing $1 billion in on-balance-sheet loans, and SBA gain on sale margins reached 4.79% versus a 4% budget. Net interest margin compressed due to rate cuts and high deposit costs, but management expects improvement in Q2. The company continues to develop its gaming fintech platforms, including Bold Bets V2 and a new Bankroll joint venture.

negative_highlights: Overall ex-cat accident year combined ratio worsened 130 bps to 82.3%, reflecting a more competitive environment
Reinsurance net premiums written declined 6% year over year, driven by rate reductions and higher retentions
Insurance net premiums written fell 1.4% as competitive pressures and nonrenewals of MCE-acquired program business weighed on volume
positive_highlights: Reinsurance underwriting income of $441 million and a 76% combined ratio, marking the fourth straight quarter of sub-80% combined ratios
Mortgage segment underwriting income of $221 million, with new insurance written boosted by a $2.2 billion large non-GSE transaction
Book value per share grew 1.7% while repurchasing $783 million of shares, and $311 million more was repurchased early in Q2
summary: Arch reported Q1 2026 after-tax operating income of $901 million, or $2.50 per share, with a 15.4% annualized operating ROE and 17.8% annualized net income ROE. The ex-cat accident year combined ratio rose 130 bps to 82.3%, reinsurance net premiums written fell 6% and insurance net premiums written declined 1.4% amid a more competitive market, while mortgage delivered $221 million of underwriting income and the portfolio generated $408 million of net investment income. Management flagged rate pressure in short-tail property and property cat, with U.S. casualty roughly at rate adequacy and international short-tail seeing low single-digit rate decreases, and said risk-adjusted returns remain attractive at high-teens levels.

negative_highlights: Cost of sales for tangible products rose significantly due to high upfront machine purchase costs in FY2025
Expansion into Southeast Asia faces challenges regarding language and culture barriers requiring local dealer partnerships
positive_highlights: Record high revenue of $19.1 million marking a 49% year-over-year increase
Gross profit increased by 45% to $4.3 million driven by SaaS channel fixed costs and kiosk demand
EBITDA margin expanded to 17.8% from the prior period
summary: Sagtec reported record revenue of $19.1 million in FY2025, representing a 49% year-over-year increase driven by service and product sales growth. Gross profit rose to $4.3 million (a 45% YoY increase) with EBITDA reaching $3.4 million on an expanded margin of 17.8%. Management discontinued the rental business model in favor of machine sales and SaaS, positioning for continued expansion into Southeast Asia markets like Indonesia.

negative_highlights: OEM revenue benefited from order timing that may affect Q2 reported revenue
R&D expenses increased 11% YoY due to pipeline investment
ORTHOVISC demand was lower than expected, offset by MONOVISC strength
positive_highlights: Commercial channel revenue grew 12% YoY, with Integrity U.S. procedures up 35% and over 3,000 cases
GAAP gross margin expanded 800 bps to 64% from 56%
Adjusted EBITDA increased by more than $4 million YoY to $4.3 million
summary: In Q1 FY2026, Anika reported total revenue of $29.6 million, up 13% year-over-year, with commercial channel revenue up 12% to $12.6 million and OEM revenue up 14% to $17 million. GAAP gross margin expanded to 64% from 56%, and adjusted EBITDA was $4.3 million, up more than $4 million year-over-year. The company maintained its full-year 2026 guidance for revenue of $114 million to $122.5 million and adjusted EBITDA margin of 5% to 10% of revenue, while completing its $15 million 10b5-1 share repurchase program.
