negative_highlights: New lease change was lighter than expected at -1.1% for the quarter, offsetting strong retention.
Boston started the year challenging due to weather impacts in Cambridge around life science funding.
Seattle is trending below expectations as it works to absorb new deliveries from 2025.
positive_highlights: San Francisco and New York exceeded high expectations with strength from AI-driven demand and limited new supply.
summary: Equity Residential reported Q1 FY26 results that met expectations with same-store revenue in line and blended rate growth of 1.5%, though new lease change was lighter than anticipated at -1.1%. Management maintained full-year guidance for blends despite a slower start in Boston, Seattle, D.C., and L.A., while highlighting strong performance in San Francisco and New York driven by low supply deliveries.

negative_highlights: Adjusted sales down 7.3% YoY to $83.9 million
Elektron sales declined 14.8% due to lower volumes and timing
Cash from operations was an outflow of $4.1 million in the quarter
positive_highlights: Adjusted EPS up 17% YoY to $0.27, ahead of expectations
Adjusted EBITDA margin improved 220 bps to 14.7% despite lower sales
Full-year 2026 adjusted EPS guidance raised to a midpoint of $1.17
summary: Luxfer reported Q1 2026 adjusted EPS of $0.27, up 17% YoY, with adjusted EBITDA up 8.8% to $12.3 million and EBITDA margin up 220 basis points to 14.7%, despite sales down 7.3% to $83.9 million. The company raised full-year 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to a midpoint of $1.17, from a range of $1.12-$1.22, citing improved visibility and a strong start to the year. Management also outlined a credible path to robust double-digit earnings growth in 2027, driven by SCBA replacement, aerospace and defense strength, and operational initiatives.

negative_highlights: Total revenue declined 9% year-over-year, with U.S. down 7% and international down 12% (down 21% constant currency).
International revenue decline fully attributed to the absence of China distributor sales; Chinese registration renewal expected only in second half 2026.
Revenue guidance implies no meaningful China contribution in the back half, and return to growth is back-half loaded.
positive_highlights: Gross margin improved to 78% from 73% year-over-year, driven by lower distributor mix.
Excluding China, international revenue grew 22% year-over-year, up 9% constant currency.
Adjusted EBITDA loss (excluding restructuring) improved 18% year-over-year to $7 million.
summary: Pulmonx reported Q1 2026 revenue of $20.6 million, down 9% year-over-year and down 12% in constant currency, with U.S. revenue down 7% and international down 12% (or down 21% constant currency) due to the absence of China sales. The company reiterated full-year 2026 revenue guidance of $90-$92 million and expects a return to growth in the back half of the year. Gross margin improved to 78% from 73% a year ago, and adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed to $7 million excluding restructuring charges, with a reduced cash burn outlook of about $23 million for the year. Management highlighted progress in restocking the U.S. sales team and advancing AeriSeal CONVERT II enrollment, while still navigating the Chinese registration renewal and ongoing execution challenges.

negative_highlights: Non-performing assets increased slightly, with $12.2 million related to a single credit
Average loan growth occurred late in the quarter, so full benefit to net interest income was not realized in Q1
Tangible book value per share decreased sequentially due to higher unrealized losses and share count
positive_highlights: Net income up 45% year-over-year to $5.2 million, with diluted EPS of $0.39, up 44%
Net interest margin expanded 8 basis points to 3.71%, with loans up 10% annualized
Payment card and service charge income up 13.5% sequentially; subsequent $10 million pre-tax fintech investment gain
summary: MVB reported Q1 FY2026 net income of $5.2 million, up 45% year-over-year, with diluted EPS of $0.39, up 44%. Revenue grew 8.8% year-over-year, with net interest income up 7% and non-interest income up 17%, while non-interest expense decreased 2%. Loan growth was 10% annualized from the prior quarter, with deposits up $60 million point-to-point despite $90 million of CD runoff. Management expressed confidence in continued growth, with a pre-tax gain of approximately $10 million on a fintech investment subsequent to quarter end, and expects annual savings of $1.8 million from the repayment of $40 million in subordinated debt.

negative_highlights: Distributable earnings of $0.24 per share include $0.08 of dilution from the December rights offering and do not cover the $0.28 dividend
Recent market volatility tied to the Iran conflict and higher rates has moderated acquisition and sales activity, with borrowers pausing decisions
Three pending loans totaling $78 million are expected at ~180 bps NIM, below the 195 bps Q1 level, reflecting multifamily spread compression
positive_highlights: Total loan commitments hit a record ~$776 million after $67.5 million of Q1 originations across medical office, retail and hospitality
2026 originations executed at ~195 bps net interest margin, the highest level in four years
Credit quality strong: weighted average risk rating of 2.8, CECL reserve at 130 bps flat, no 5-rated or collateral-dependent loans and all loans current
summary: Seven Hills reported Q1 FY2026 distributable earnings of $5.3 million, or $0.24 per share, at the high end of guidance but including $0.08 of dilution from the December rights offering. Total loan commitments reached a record ~$776 million after $67.5 million of new originations at a net interest margin of ~195 bps, the highest in four years, with no realized losses and all loans current. Q2 distributable earnings guidance is $0.23-$0.25 per share, and management expects DE to return to the $0.28 quarterly dividend level by year-end; near-term transaction activity is seen as uneven given rate and geopolitical volatility. Originations carry a dividend not yet covered by earnings, and the pipeline's three pending loans at ~180 bps NIM are inside the Q1 level.

negative_highlights: GAAP net income dropped to $2.0 million ($0.09/share) from $5.2 million ($0.25/share) a year earlier
License and hardware revenue fell to $1.5 million from $3.0 million due to lower Software Operations bookings
Guidance was reiterated, not raised, and management said it needs more visibility before committing to upside from rebounding bookings or cost cuts
positive_highlights: Managed Professional Services revenue grew nearly 57% year over year to $2.1 million
Software Operations bookings for Q2 already exceed the entirety of Q1 2026 bookings
Workforce reduction of ~10% expected to cut annualized headcount-related expense by over $6 million, supporting EBITDA
summary: Q1 FY2026 GAAP net income fell to $2.0 million ($0.09/diluted share) from $5.2 million ($0.25) a year earlier, driven by lower Software Operations bookings and license revenue ($1.5 million vs $3.0 million), partially offset by ~57% growth in Managed Services revenue ($2.1 million) and ARPU up $0.05. Adjusted EBITDA was $5.3 million and adjusted operating expenses were $29.5 million, essentially flat versus $29.4 million. Management reiterated 2026 guidance of $136-143 million revenue and $27.5-32.5 million Adjusted EBITDA rather than raising it, citing a need for more visibility, while noting Q2 software bookings already exceed all of Q1. A ~10% workforce reduction was announced, expected to cut over $6 million in annualized headcount expense and incur $1.6-2.0 million of restructuring charges in Q2-Q3.

negative_highlights: Weather-related losses of $17.2 million were double the prior year quarter
Commercial lines segment posted an underwriting loss with a statutory combined ratio of 104.6%
Personal lines net premiums written declined 13.1% due to rate and exposure slowdowns
positive_highlights: Core loss ratio improved to 53.4% excluding specific loss components
Net investment income increased 19% year-over-year to $14.3 million
Personal lines real retention rate was healthy at 88.7%
summary: Net premiums earned decreased 4.9% to $221.4 million and net income fell to $11.5 million from $25.2 million in the prior year quarter, driven by weather-related losses of $17.2 million and large fire losses. Management explicitly stated that first quarter results did not meet expectations due to these unusual loss events, though core underlying performance remained solid.

negative_highlights: North American sales down 16% to $78M
Adjusted EBITDA swung to a loss of $371K from a gain of $354K
U.S. accounts remain cautious and tentative about the year
positive_highlights: International sales up 38% to $29M in Q1
Gross margin held at 33.4%
Board approved $0.25 per share dividend, cash up to $64M
summary: Q1 FY2026 revenue was $170M, down 6% YoY, with North America down 16% and international up 38%. Adjusted EBITDA was a loss of $371K vs. a gain of $354K a year ago, reflecting margin pressure and tariffs. Management notes cautious U.S. retailers and expects to stay on track for full-year goals, while investing in new anime platform and 2027 launches.

negative_highlights: Revenue fell to $25.0 million from $27.1 million in Q4 2025, and GAAP EPS declined to $0.09 from $0.21
Net outflows of $50 million in AUM and $50 million in assets under advisement
U.S. value equity strategies remain under pressure, with traditional strategies still seeing outflows
positive_highlights: AUM grew to $18.3 billion from $17.4 billion at year-end, driven by $0.8 billion of market appreciation
Westwood Energy Secondaries Fund II closed with over $300 million in commitments, more than double the $150 million target
ETF suite surpassed $315 million in combined AUM, with MDST crossing $200 million in under two years and gaining its first major wirehouse approval
summary: Westwood reported Q1 2026 revenue of $25.0 million, down from $27.1 million in Q4 2025 but up from $23.3 million a year earlier; GAAP net income was $0.8 million ($0.09/share) versus $1.9 million ($0.21) in Q4, and non-GAAP economic earnings were $2.8 million ($0.31/share) versus $3.3 million ($0.36). Firm-wide AUM rose to $18.3 billion from $17.4 billion at year-end on $0.8 billion of market appreciation, despite $50 million of net outflows. Growth came from private energy secondaries (Fund II closed above $300 million versus a $150 million target) and ETFs (over $315 million combined), while U.S. value equity remained under pressure, and the board declared a $0.15 dividend. No formal forward guidance was given, though management cited a pipeline above $1 billion and expected a next institutional MIS client in coming months.

negative_highlights: Net income fell to $0.42 per diluted share from $0.70 a year earlier on mark-to-market declines in preferred stock and warrants
Book value per share decreased 0.3% from Q4 2025 to $18.96 on unrealized losses on preferred stock and warrants
Q2 CAD guidance midpoint of $0.54 is below Q1's $0.58, even as the new TRS facility was described as already driving modest CAD increases
positive_highlights: Cash available for distribution rose to $0.58 per diluted share from $0.45 a year earlier, 1.16x covering the $0.50 dividend
Re-REMIC of FREMF 2017-K62 B-Piece generated $0.46 per share of book value appreciation and ~$0.34 per share of expected annual CAD accretion, reducing repo financing by $75 million
$242 million TRS refinancing replaced $180 million of 5.75% notes maturing May 1 with a three-year term, adding ~$45 million of capacity without diluting common shareholders
summary: NREF reported Q1 2026 net income of $0.42 per diluted share (down from $0.70 in Q1 2025) on mark-to-market declines and CMBS VIE changes, while earnings available for distribution rose to $0.43 from $0.41 and cash available for distribution rose to $0.58 from $0.45. Q2 guidance was set at EAD of $0.43 per share (range $0.38-$0.48) and CAD of $0.54 per share (range $0.49-$0.59). The quarter's key developments were a $242 million TRS refinancing replacing $180 million of 5.75% notes maturing May 1, and a re-REMIC of the FREMF 2017-K62 B-Piece generating $0.46 per share of book value appreciation and roughly $0.34 per share of expected annual CAD accretion. Book value slipped 0.3% to $18.96, and the $0.50 dividend was 1.16x covered by CAD.

negative_highlights: Gross margin fell to 59.0% from 61.0% a year ago, pressured by pulled-forward investments and front-loaded costs on non-subscription engagements
Adjusted EBITDA declined to $8.9 million (8.4% of revenue) from $15.7 million (15.1%), and non-GAAP EPS fell to $0.04 from $0.10
Sales and marketing expense rose to 36.6% of revenue from 32.9%, and full-year guidance was reiterated rather than raised despite the Q1 revenue beat
positive_highlights: Billings increased 19.9% year-over-year to $95.3 million, with a 22.9% increase excluding PeopleSoft support
RPO grew 16.4% to $643.6 million (up 18.2% excluding PeopleSoft), and 11 deals over $1 million TCV totaling $33 million closed versus 5 deals totaling $5.6 million a year ago
Debt balance reduced to $58.4 million after $10 million of voluntary prepayments, lifting net cash to $73.8 million
summary: Q1 FY2026 revenue was $105.5 million, up 1.2% year-over-year (up 5.2% excluding PeopleSoft), with GAAP diluted EPS of $0.01 versus $0.04 a year ago and non-GAAP EPS of $0.04 versus $0.10. Billings rose 19.9% to $95.3 million and RPO rose 16.4% to $643.6 million, while gross margin contracted to 59.0% from 61.0% and adjusted EBITDA fell to $8.9 million (8.4% of revenue) from $15.7 million (15.1%). Management guided Q2 revenue to $106-108 million and reiterated full-year 2026 revenue growth of 4-6% and adjusted EBITDA margins of 12.5-15.5%, declining to raise the annual outlook despite the Q1 revenue beat.

negative_highlights: Q1 consolidated sales down 15% YoY; adjusted EBITDA down to $3.9 million from $14.4 million
Aluminum costs up 64% YoY, pressuring Arcadia margins
DynaEnergetics sales down 9% YoY; Middle East shipments delayed
positive_highlights: NobelClad backlog up 12% sequentially to $70.3 million, highest in more than 15 years
Q2 guidance implies sequential revenue and EBITDA growth across all three businesses
Architectural Billings Index for Western U.S. rose above 50 for first time since December 2024
summary: Q1 FY2026 revenue fell 15% YoY to $135.6 million, with adjusted EBITDA down to $3.9 million from $14.4 million, reflecting macro challenges, aluminum cost inflation, and Middle East conflict disruptions. Q2 guidance of $148-$158 million sales and $6-$8 million EBITDA implies sequential improvement, but management cautions on persistent headwinds and uncertain macro environment. Order backlog at NobelClad rose 12% sequentially to $70.3 million, a 15-year high, and management cites early positive indicators in end markets, though improvement is expected only in the longer term.

negative_highlights: CEO noted that attritional loss ratios have been increasing year-over-year, primarily driven by mix shifts rather than underlying liability changes.
Management acknowledged competitive pressure intensifying in parts of the E&S market and admitted to walking away from large non-CAT accounts where rates were not right.
positive_highlights: Adjusted net income surged to $25.6M from $8.5M YoY, driven by top-line growth and improved margins.
Combined ratio tightened significantly to 87.4% (from 90.9%) due to a loss ratio drop of 1 point to 58.8% and expense ratio improvement of 2.5 points.
Gross written premiums grew broadly with casualty up 27%, property up 13%, and net earned premiums rising 34%.
summary: Ategrity reported record Q1 FY26 results with gross written premiums growing 23% YoY to $478M and adjusted net income surging from $8.5M to $25.6M, driven by a combined ratio improvement to 87.4%. Management raised the full-year guidance range for direct premium growth (now expecting ~19-20%) while maintaining its Q2 outlook of approximately 20% above market and an underwriting margin in the high 80s.

negative_highlights: Net income fell to $5M ($0.20/share) from $12M ($0.50/share) a year ago, driven by $9.1M lower equity gains
Operating costs rose to $22.4M from $20.8M on higher employee and servicing expense, with more hiring planned
Provision of $22.5M was up slightly YoY, and management said rec charge-offs remain above historical levels
positive_highlights: Record total loans of $2.62B, up 5% YoY, with $377M of quarterly originations
Rec originations grew 64% to $142.5M and home improvement originations grew 32% to $64.4M
Q2 dividend raised 16.7% to $0.14 per share, and rec 90+ day delinquencies at just 0.57%
summary: Net interest income rose 5% to $54.1M with NIM at 8% (up 6 bps YoY), and loans reached a record $2.62B, up 5%, on $377M of originations, including a 64% jump in rec originations to $142.5M. However, net income fell to $5M or $0.20 per diluted share from $12M or $0.50, largely because the prior-year quarter included $9.1M of higher equity gains; provision was $22.5M versus $27.7M in Q4 and $22M a year ago. The board raised the Q2 dividend 16.7% to $0.14 per share and the company closed a $75M notes offering, with management citing ~10% expected loan growth versus 3% in 2025. No formal EPS or revenue guidance was given.

negative_highlights: SaaS Adjusted EBITDA came in below guidance due to gross margin compression from strategic customer upgrades.
Marketing Services billings declined 33% YoY as legacy digital products are migrated to SaaS.
Full-year SaaS revenue growth is expected to be flat to slightly down before returning to top-line growth in 2027.
positive_highlights: SaaS revenue of $117M beat expectations with a 5% YoY increase.
Marketing Center grew approximately 30% year-over-year, validating the Market, note, and Grow strategy.
Quality customers now represent 70% of SaaS revenue, up from 62% a year ago.
summary: Thryv reported Q1 FY2026 SaaS revenue of $117 million (up 5% YoY) and Marketing Services revenue of $50.9 million, both beating guidance. Adjusted EBITDA beat for the quarter despite a deliberate near-term gross margin compression from upgrading legacy customers to the higher-margin SaaS platform. Management raised full-year SaaS revenue guidance to $463-471 million while maintaining other full-year targets.

negative_highlights: PPS volumes only grew 0.8% due to challenging distribution channel comparison
Adjusted EBITDA flat in constant currency for the quarter
Net leverage high at 4.7 times, with goal of 2.5-3 turns in 24 months
positive_highlights: Automation revenue increased 111% year-over-year, excluding FX
Gross margin improved 210 bps to 43.1% ex-warrants and depreciation
Revenue growth of 4.5% constant currency, with currency tailwinds adding 6.5 points
summary: Ranpak's Q1 2026 revenue grew 4.5% constant currency (5.4% ex-warrants), with automation up 111% and PPS volumes up 0.8%. Adjusted EBITDA was flat constant currency, up 5% ex-warrants, and up 9.2% reported. Management expects 200 bps gross margin improvement for the year and automation revenue near $60 million, with a path to $100 million. They are implementing a temporary surcharge in Europe to offset paper price increases while remaining confident in the growth strategy.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined 9% due to event timing shifts (approx. half the decline) and lower new boat unit volumes.
Net loss widened significantly from a prior year net loss of $375,000 to $13 million.
Industry retail demand remains pressured with SSI data indicating double-digit declines in competitive categories.
positive_highlights: Gross margin expanded 110 basis points to 23.9% driven by portfolio optimization and favorable mix.
Pre-owned revenue increased 5% supported by improved availability in a disciplined pricing environment.
Net debt-to-EBITDA ratio improved sequentially and year-over-year to 4.1x following $57M of debt repayment.

Gross margin expanded 110 basis points to 23.9%, but SG&A expenses rose as a percentage of sales due to the revenue drop. Management maintained full-year guidance for adjusted EBITDA ($60M-$80M) and EPS ($0.20-$0.70), citing industry headwinds, potential macro noise (e.g., fuel prices), and uncertainty about consumer confidence.

The $1.6 billion new JV debt carries a 24-month lockout period limiting disposition flexibility in that pool
Net debt leverage remains elevated at 11.6x and net debt to total assets at 68.8%
positive_highlights: Normalized FFO of $0.33 per share exceeded the high end of guidance by $0.02 and grew 63% year-over-year
Leased 862,000 sq ft at a 26.3% weighted average rent roll-up, the sixth consecutive quarter of double-digit rent growth
$1.6 billion JV refinancing at 5.71% fixed rate makes all consolidated debt fixed-rate and non-amortizing, unlocking nearly $20 million in annual cash flow
summary: ILPT reported Q1 2026 Normalized FFO of $22 million, or $0.33 per share, exceeding the high end of guidance by $0.02, with a $1.1 million boost from one-time items ($650K percentage rent, $450K remediation fee). Normalized FFO grew 16% sequentially and 63% year-over-year, while Same Property Cash Basis NOI rose over 4% YoY to $87.4 million and Adjusted EBITDAre was $87 million. The company introduced full-year 2026 guidance of Normalized FFO $1.27-$1.34 per share and Adjusted EBITDAre $344-$349 million, and priced $1.6 billion of 5.71% fixed-rate JV debt that eliminates floating-rate exposure and unlocks nearly $20 million in annual cash flow. Leasing totaled 862,000 sq ft at a 26.3% rent roll-up, and management expects to fully lease the 535,000 sq ft Indianapolis vacancy in June.

negative_highlights: Income before tax of $2.4 million was heavily driven by non-operating fair value gains of $8.7 million rather than core mining cash flow.
Company is currently in a transition period focused on strategic partnership negotiations and project finance, delaying FID.
Royalty rates in Indonesia increased by 50% to 15%, adding to operating cost pressures.
positive_highlights: Cash outflows from operations improved significantly to $1.2 million compared to $3.3 million in the prior year period.
Nickel spot prices reached a two-year high, up 37% from late 2025 lows, creating significant upside risk for the project NPV.
Completed ISO-compliant life cycle analysis with results demonstrating low emission impact compared to Indonesian peers.
summary: Lifezone Metals reported Q1 FY2026 cash outflows from operations of $1.2 million (down from $3.3m prior year) and ended the quarter with $15.27 million in cash plus $18.3 million remaining on its Taurus bridge loan. Management highlighted a significant fair value gain of $8.7 million driven by share price recovery, resulting in income before tax of $2.4 million. The company raised an additional $23.3 million in equity last week and completed the second drawdown of its Taurus facility.

negative_highlights: GAAP net loss of $1.0 million, or $0.16 per share, versus the prior quarter's EAD loss position; net interest income declined $1.4 million sequentially.
Net real estate operations swung to a $1.2 million net loss, a $1.3 million decline from the prior quarter.
Internalization economics are largely undisclosed: no pro forma book value provided and no explicit dividend timing beyond 'as we earn them.'
positive_highlights: Loan portfolio grew to $2.2 billion across 60 investments, up a net $374.4 million in the quarter on $495.6 million of new commitments.
Realized a $3.3 million GAAP and EAD gain on the Philadelphia land sale, plus a $1 million CECL reserve release ($0.15/share).
Weighted average risk rating improved to 2.5 from 2.7, and loans rated 4 or 5 fell to 14% of the portfolio from 17% at December 31.
summary: GAAP net loss allocable to common was $1.0 million, or $0.16 per share, with net interest income of $9.3 million, down $1.4 million sequentially on the FL4 securitization ramp-up and lower payoff fees. EAD was $0.02 per share versus an EAD loss of $0.48 in Q4, and GAAP book value was $29.98 per share versus $30.01 at year-end. The quarter included a $3.3 million gain on a Philadelphia land sale and a $1 million CECL reserve release. Leverage rose to 3.4x from 2.8x after closing the $1 billion 2026-FL4 securitization, with the full run-rate benefit expected in Q2. Management announced a proposed internalization of ACRES management at book value, subject to a June 22 shareholder vote, with no pro forma book value disclosed.

negative_highlights: 30-89 day delinquent loans more than doubled to $7.4 million (0.68% of gross loans) from $4.3 million (0.38%) at year-end
Non-performing loans rose to 0.94% of gross loans, including a $1.3 million commercial relationship moved to non-accrual after ceasing operations
Deposits fell $66.2 million in the quarter and a $433,000 fraud loss tied to a non-executive officer was recorded
positive_highlights: Net interest margin expanded 21 bps QoQ to 4.24% and 48 bps YoY, driven by higher investment yields (3.39% to 3.55%) and lower deposit costs (down 16 bps to 1.90%)
EPS of $0.83 rose 6.7% QoQ and 7.2% YoY, with return on assets up 12 bps QoQ to 1.29%
Commercial real estate grew $13.6 million and mortgage originations rose 9% YoY, lifting gain-on-sale income
summary: Landmark posted record total revenue of $18.8 million, EPS of $0.83 (up 6.7% QoQ and 7.2% YoY), and net income of $5.1 million versus $4.7 million a year ago. Net interest margin expanded 21 bps QoQ to 4.24% (up 48 bps YoY) on lower deposit and borrowing costs, while loans declined $13.5 million to $1.1 billion and deposits fell $66.2 million largely from seasonal public-fund outflows. Credit metrics ticked up: non-performing loans rose to 0.94% of gross loans from 0.90%, 30-89 day delinquencies jumped to 0.68% from 0.38%, and a $433,000 fraud loss was recorded. No explicit forward guidance was given; the board declared a $0.21 dividend, the 99th consecutive quarterly payout.

negative_highlights: Net charge-offs were $9.4 million versus $6.7 million in the prior quarter; management expects approximately $45 million per quarter in non-credit-enhanced net charge-offs through the rest of 2026.
Credit-enhanced balances grew only $1 million in the quarter versus the guided $8-10 million per month pace, and NPL balances rose $6.1 million sequentially to $49.8 million.
Non-interest income fell to $14.6 million from $22.3 million, and the efficiency ratio rose to 66.3% from 50.5%, with the 60% target now requiring about $2 million more revenue.
positive_highlights: Q1 loan originations totaled $1.7 billion, up 38% year-over-year and above the $1.4 billion guidance baseline, driven by student lending seasonality.
Interchange income rose to $703,000 from $310,000 last quarter on early credit card portfolio contributions.
Tangible book value per share grew to $14.34, with a bank leverage ratio of 16.8%, nearly double the well-capitalized minimum.
summary: FinWise reported Q1 FY2026 net income of $2.7 million and diluted EPS of $0.20, with net charge-offs rising to $9.4 million from $6.7 million in the prior quarter, driven by $2.2 million in legacy SBA 7(a) losses. Net interest income rose to $28.1 million from $24.6 million, but reported NIM of 12.9% was inflated by a change in excess-spread estimate; excluding credit-enhanced program effects, NIM fell to 7.15% from 7.85%. Non-interest income dropped to $14.6 million from $22.3 million, and the efficiency ratio rose to 66.3% from 50.5%. Management guided to roughly $45 million in quarterly non-credit-enhanced net charge-offs for the remainder of the year and flagged up to $10 million of watch-list loans potentially migrating to non-performing in Q2, while reaffirming $1.4 billion baseline quarterly originations and $8-10 million per month of credit-enhanced balance growth skewed to the second half.

negative_highlights: Net sales grew only "slightly" YoY, with growth reliant on the Gold Tip acquisition; organic demand was soft in outdoor and indoor games.
Mass merchant channel saw a dip as prior-year sales did not repeat; specialty growth was attributed to the Gold Tip acquisition.
Management flagged inflationary pressure from high energy costs and expected consumer demand to remain uneven in coming quarters.
positive_highlights: Gross margin expanded ~400 bps YoY to 30.7% from 26.7% on facility consolidation, cost rationalization, and favorable mix.
EBITDA increased $2.2 million to $7.1 million; operating cash flow rose to $6.1 million from $3.8 million.
Inventory declined $3.4 million YoY despite two H2 2025 acquisitions; net leverage was 0.1x with $13.1 million cash.
summary: Escalade reported Q1 FY2026 net sales of $55.8 million, "slightly" up YoY, net income of $4.4 million ($0.32 diluted EPS), and gross margin of 30.7%, up ~400 basis points from 26.7%. EBITDA rose to $7.1 million from $4.9 million, operating cash flow rose to $6.1 million from $3.8 million, and inventory fell $3.4 million YoY despite two acquisitions. Management guided only qualitatively—expecting gross margins above prior year and higher 2026 capex—while noting a still "uneven" consumer backdrop and softer demand in outdoor and indoor games, partially offset by billiards, safety, and the Gold Tip acquisition. No formal revenue or EPS guidance was provided.

positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA up 69% YoY to $12.3M; adjusted EBITDA margin expanded ~800 bps to 29%

Multiproduct attach grew 15% YoY; Asure Central adoption near majority of ~30,000 direct clients by end of Q2 and new bookings up 13%
summary: Q1 FY2026 revenue was $42.8M, up 23% YoY with organic growth accelerating to 7% from 3% in Q1 2025. Adjusted EBITDA rose 69% to $12.3M and margin expanded ~800 bps to 29%. Full-year 2026 guidance calls for $159M-$163M revenue and 23%-25% adjusted EBITDA margin, with Q2 guided to $36M-$38M and $6M-$8M EBITDA; management framed the outlook as conservative given 'global uncertainty' while reiterating a path to double-digit organic growth. Recurring revenue was $37.8M, 88% of total, and contracted backlog stood at ~$85.6M with ~38% expected to convert over the next 12 months.

summary: First Internet Bancorp reported Q1 2026 net income of $2.5 million ($0.29 per share), with total revenue of $43.1 million, up 21% YoY. Net interest income rose 26% YoY, and fully taxable equivalent net interest margin expanded 54 basis points YoY to 2.45%. Pre-provision net revenue grew 51% YoY to $18.1 million. Credit trends improved, with SBA delinquencies down 118 bps QoQ. Management reaffirmed full-year fee income guidance of $33-35 million and expects profitability to improve, targeting a return to 1% ROA by end of 2027.

summary: BayFirst reported a Q1 FY2026 net loss of $5.7 million, widening from the $2.5 million loss in Q4 2025, with loans held for investment down 3% to $930.4 million and deposits down 8% to $1.09 billion. Net interest margin fell 16 bps to 3.42% and net interest income dropped $1.7 million to $9.4 million, while provision for credit losses was $3.1 million and annualized net charge-offs ran at 1.98% of average loans. The company announced an $80 million PIPE capital raise, a rights offering for existing shareholders, a new CEO, and a planned resumption of preferred dividends, improving pro forma Tier 1 leverage to 10.02%.

Adjusted EBITDA was $34.4M at roughly 43% margin and Adjusted EPS was $0.22; free cash flow was $5.4M (16% conversion) after a $15M TRA payment and $22.5M strategic partner purchase. FY2026 guidance is $340-346M revenue (10-12% reported, 7-9% normalized) and $141-146M Adjusted EBITDA (~42% margin), with the EBITDA outlook raised on a strategic distribution partner deal worth about $4.5M while revenue guidance is reiterated. The quarter's main event is the pending KUBRA acquisition (expected to close in Q2, roughly doubling revenue); the board unanimously rejected a Forager Capital proposal as undervaluing the company.

Record high percentage of new clients coming from referrals in March.
summary: First quarter 2026 revenue was $76.0 million, a decrease of 34.3% year-over-year, while EPS loss narrowed to $0.19 per share from $0.07 in the prior year period. Management reported its first sequential quarterly revenue growth in three years and a second consecutive quarter of year-over-year coach productivity gains (up 19% YoY). The company reaffirmed full-year 2026 guidance of $270-$300 million revenue and expects to return to profitability starting in the fourth quarter of 2026.

SGC reported Q1 FY2026 revenue up 3% to $141 million, with Branded Products and Healthcare Apparel each up 5% and Contact Centers down 8% on prior-year client attrition. Gross margin expanded 30 bps to 37.1%, SG&A fell to 35.8% of sales, EBITDA rose to $4.8 million from $3.5 million, and diluted EPS was $0.06 versus a $0.05 loss last year. Management maintained full-year guidance of $572-$585 million in net sales and $0.54-$0.66 in diluted EPS, still back-half weighted, and noted EPS came in slightly above expectations partly on timing. Healthcare gross margin fell 160 bps on lower-margin customer growth and Contact Centers margin declined 140 bps on higher labor costs.

summary: Biodesix reported Q1 FY2026 revenue of $25.6 million, a 42% year-over-year increase driven by 37% growth in diagnostic testing and near-doubling development services revenue. The company raised its full-year 2026 revenue guidance range from the prior $105M-$111M (implied) to a new midpoint of $109 million, citing strong Q1 performance and continued commercial expansion.

FY2026 guidance lowered for both revenue and adjusted EBITDA
positive_highlights: Maintained trailing 12-month book-to-bill ratio greater than 1.0

summary: Aviat Networks reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $100.0 million, down from $112.6 million a year ago, with non-GAAP EPS of $0.06 and adjusted EBITDA of $4.4 million. Results were hurt by roughly $9 million in Middle East conflict-related project pushouts and demand shifts. The company lowered full-year revenue guidance to $428-$440 million and adjusted EBITDA to $35-$40 million, but expects Q4 revenue normalization and flagged growth drivers like MDU, utilities, and BEAD for potential FY2027 contribution.

Company has entered a quiet period and will not engage with investors until LOTIS-5 data is disclosed.

Non-GAAP operating expenses decreased by 13% to $42.9 million driven by lower R&D.
Company maintains a healthy cash balance of $231 million providing runway into 2028.
summary: First quarter 2026 net product revenues were $20.0 million, representing a 15% year-over-year increase from $17.4 million in Q1 2025, driven by normal quarter-to-quarter variability rather than a confirmed trend change. On a non-GAAP basis, total adjusted operating expenses decreased by 13% to $42.9 million due to lower R&D spending and a reallocation of personnel costs to cost of goods sold. The company maintains a cash balance of $231 million with an expected runway into 2028 while entering a quiet period ahead of the anticipated top-line readout for the LOTIS-5 trial in June.

negative_highlights: Reaffirmed FY2026 guidance despite strong quarter, citing potentially elevated carrier approval rates that may pull forward policy volume from Q4.
SelectRx revenue impacted by IRA implementation (max fair prices on 10 drugs) and carrier-specific reimbursement actions, though EBITDA impact was low single-digit millions.
Term life insurance remains competitive with consumers shifting media consumption habits, partially offsetting final expense strength.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA grew 18% YoY to $45 million, with consolidated EBITDA margin of 7% excluding the $14 million adjustment.
Senior segment achieved 26% EBITDA margin excluding the adjustment, marking four consecutive years of 25%+ margins during AEP and OEP.
SelectRx membership grew 11% to nearly 117,000 members, with 64% increase in prescriptions shipped versus two years ago.
summary: SelectQuote reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $431 million, up 6% YoY, and adjusted EBITDA of $45 million, up 18% YoY, aided by a $14 million positive change in estimate on commissions receivable. Senior revenue grew 8% to $183 million, healthcare services revenue grew 5% to $199 million, and life insurance revenue grew 4% to $48 million. Management reaffirmed FY2026 guidance of $1.61-$1.71 billion revenue and $90-$100 million adjusted EBITDA, citing elevated MA approval rates that may be timing-related and could impact Q4.

negative_highlights: Total company sales declined less than 2% year-over-year
Paid subscribers dropped 13,000 sequentially from Q4 2025
Gross margin pressured by tariffs, end-of-life impairments, and lower excess inventory monetization
positive_highlights: Platform revenue increased nearly 6% to almost $84.8 million

summary: Cricut's Q1 FY2026 revenue declined less than 2% year-over-year, with platform revenue up nearly 6% to almost $84.8 million and paid subscribers up over 3% to almost 3.08 million, though sequentially down 13,000. The company launched new machines (Joy 2, Explore 5) and its first service (DTF), with encouraging early adoption and active users up 1%. Gross margin faced headwinds from end-of-life inventory impairments, tariff costs (now ~10% average impact), and lower monetization of excess inventory, while international revenue grew 16% (10 points from FX). Management expects a challenging environment but remains focused on innovation, bundle strategy, and cost discipline.

Second quarter revenue expected to grow at least 10% YoY, lower than Q1's 21%, due to shipment timing and tougher comparisons.
Elevated commodity costs and $1.4 million fuel cost risk noted as near-term margin headwinds.
positive_highlights: Net revenue up 21% YoY with wholesale up 31.5% and DTC up 7%.
Adjusted EBITDA increased from under $1 million to over $7 million, with 570 bps margin expansion.
Bagged coffee dollar share up 55 bps to 3.3% and pods up 45 bps to 2.2%; unit growth 2.5x the category.
summary: In Q1 FY2026, BRCC revenue grew 21% YoY to approximately $430 million annualized, with wholesale up 31.5% and DTC up 7%. Adjusted EBITDA surged from under $1 million to over $7 million, an eightfold increase with 570 bps margin expansion. Management raised FY2026 revenue guidance to at least 8% growth (~$430M) and adjusted EBITDA to at least 35% growth (~$29M), citing distribution gains, pricing, and cost discipline. However, gross margin fell 305 bps to 33% due to non-recurring items and elevated coffee costs.

negative_highlights: Orders declined 15% sequentially from Q4 levels.
Semi orders specifically declined as customers prioritized fulfillment of prior quarter's orders.
Front-end semi business remains slower with no significant uptick in new equipment orders yet.

Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to 9.3%, outperforming the guidance range of approximately 45%.
Backlog increased 36% year-over-year to $51.8 million, providing strong revenue visibility.
summary: InTest reported Q1 FY2026 revenue of $33.9 million, a 27% year-over-year increase driven by gains in defense, aerospace, life sciences, and auto EV. Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to 9.3%, exceeding guidance, while backlog grew 36% year-over-year to $51.8 million. Management raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to a range of $130-$135 million, citing improved market conditions and diversified demand.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined 33% year-over-year to $64.3 million on lower railcar deliveries (577 vs. 710 units).
Adjusted EBITDA fell to $3.2 million from $6.4 million, and adjusted EPS swung to a loss of $0.04 from income of $0.05.
SG&A as a percentage of revenue rose to 17.7% from 10.9% due to lower revenue.

summary: Q1 FY2026 revenue fell to $64.3 million from $96.3 million a year ago on 577 railcar deliveries versus 710, while gross margin expanded 190 bps to 16.8%. Adjusted net loss was $0.5 million, or $0.04 per share, versus adjusted net income of $1.6 million, or $0.05 per share, and adjusted EBITDA declined to $3.2 million from $6.4 million. Management reaffirmed full-year 2026 guidance of 4,000-4,500 deliveries with performance weighted to the second half, supported by $156 million backlog, an 86% increase in aftermarket sales, and the tank car retrofit program starting in Q3. The key change versus prior periods is the shift toward conversion and aftermarket mix, which lifted margins despite lower volumes.

negative_highlights: Net income declined sharply by 57% YoY due to one-time integration costs of $3M.
Prepaid Solutions segment revenue fell 17%, dragging overall gross margins down from 33.2% to 30.0%.
Q2 Adjusted EBITDA is expected to be slightly lower than the prior year period due to timing of investment spending.
positive_highlights: Revenue increased 20% YoY to $147M, led by a 35% surge in secure card solutions including Arroweye.
Free cash flow jumped significantly from $0.3 million last year to $10.1 million this quarter.
Contactless metal and closed-loop prepaid segments showed strong growth.
summary: CPI Card Group reported Q1 FY2026 revenue of $147 million, a 20% increase year-over-year driven by secure card solutions and Arroweye, while the prepaid segment declined 17%. Adjusted EBITDA grew 9%, but net income fell 57% due to $3 million in pre-tax integration costs. Management affirmed full-year guidance for high single-digit revenue growth despite Q2 expectations being slightly lower than prior year.

negative_highlights: GAAP net loss of $7.4 million, or $0.30 per share, versus $0.87 per share of net income in Q1 2025, driven by $13.1 million of unrealized portfolio losses.
Book value declined: GAAP BVPS fell 4% to $10.31 and economic BVPS fell 3.3% to $12.28 versus year-end 2025.
Current securitization ROEs have compressed to the low- to high-12% range from the prior 15-20% target, and 90+ day delinquency rose ~50 bps from Q4 2025 to ~2.7%.

Interest income rose 24% YoY to $40.7 million, supported by $246.2 million of Q1 loan purchases at a 7.3% weighted average coupon and 67% weighted average CLTV.

summary: Angel Oak Mortgage REIT reported a Q1 2026 GAAP net loss of $7.4 million ($0.30 per diluted share) versus prior-year net income of $20.5 million, driven by $13.1 million of unrealized losses on the securitized and residential loan portfolios plus a ~1 point decline in whole loan pricing. This was partly offset by distributable earnings of $4.6 million (up from $4.1 million), interest income of $40.7 million (up 24% YoY), and net interest income of $12.1 million (up 20% YoY). GAAP book value per share fell 4% to $10.31 and economic book value fell 3.3% to $12.28 quarter-over-quarter, though management noted book value has increased slightly since quarter-end. The $0.32 dividend was maintained; management expects continued quarterly securitizations (4/year), but current ROEs on new deals are lower (low- to high-12s vs. 15-20% target) and any call of legacy 2021-22 securitizations hinges on rate volatility subsiding.

HDMC gross margin down 380 basis points to 25.3% due to tariffs and pricing
HDMC operating income down to $19M from $116M year-over-year
positive_highlights: North America retail sales up 14% with U.S. up 16% and market share up 2 points to 38%

summary: Q1 2026 revenue down 12% and EPS down to $0.22 from $1.07, driven by HDFS transition and HDMC tariff costs of $45M. Global retail sales up 8% with North America up 14%, but international down 4%. Management lowered full-year tariff guidance to $75M-$90M, raised 2027 cost savings target to $150M+, and expects improved shipment cadence in Q2 and Q4.

Adjusted EBITDA declined to $6 million from $22 million in the prior year period as inflationary pressures on freight and materials outweighed productivity gains. Management raised full-year revenue guidance slightly while holding Adjusted EBITDA expectations unchanged, citing improved service levels but acknowledging persistent macro softness.

negative_highlights: Net premium earned decreased year-over-year due to average account rate decreases in a softening market
Other income declined by $900,000 driven by non-recurring items present in the prior year
Management cautioned that using Q1 results alone is premature for revising full-year guidance given H2 volatility
positive_highlights: Net income of $19.3 million with a combined ratio of 66% in line with targets
Account retention remained within the target low-to-mid-80s range after bouncing back from January walkaways
Core catastrophe reinsurance program renewal secured risk-adjusted cost decreases and increased exhaustion point to over $1.6 billion
summary: American Coastal Insurance Corporation reported Q1 FY2026 net income of $19.3 million and a combined ratio of 66%, which was an increase from the prior year but in line with management's target range. Revenue guidance for the full year remains unchanged, though management noted that H2 results will be critical to meeting these estimates given softening market conditions on the front end. The company highlighted strong retention within its targeted range and successful reinsurance renewals despite losing some premium rates.

$6.7 million of reinsurance reinstatement premiums from a 2022 E&S claim added roughly five points to the 104.6% group combined ratio

summary: James River reported a Q1 2026 net loss to common shareholders of $10.9 million versus net income of $7.6 million a year ago, with operating earnings of $5.8 million or $0.12 per diluted share versus $0.19. Results were hit by $6.7 million of reinsurance reinstatement premiums tied largely to a single 2022 E&S claim, adding about five points to the group combined ratio of 104.6%; absent that impact operating EPS would have been $0.22 and the combined ratio 99.7%. E&S combined ratio was 96.5% (91.8% adjusted, in line with the prior quarter), casualty rates were positive at 7.7%, G&A fell 11%, and investment income rose 6.6% to $21.3 million. Management flagged increasing competition in primary general casualty and some business moving back to the admitted market, and gave no explicit forward guidance figures.

negative_highlights: Non-GAAP EPS fell to $0.16 from $0.21 and GAAP EPS to $0.10 from $0.13; consolidated operating earnings dropped 23.2%
U.S. Property and Casualty revenue fell 11.3% and segment operating earnings dropped 22.1% with margin down 150 bps
Broadspire revenue grew only 1% with margin down 120 bps and retention at 86%, plus unallocated corporate costs rose to $8.8 million from $6.1 million

Leverage ratio of 1.62x EBITDA with $24 million of new and enhanced business won in the quarter
summary: Crawford reported Q1 2026 revenues of $309.5 million, down 1% year-over-year, with non-GAAP diluted EPS of $0.16 versus $0.21 a year earlier and GAAP EPS of $0.10 versus $0.13. Consolidated operating earnings fell 23.2% and non-GAAP operating margin contracted to 4.4% from 5.7%, driven by an 11.3% revenue decline in U.S. Property and Casualty and higher unallocated corporate costs of $8.8 million versus $6.1 million. Broadspire grew revenue just 1% to $104.8 million on a slow ramp of new client wins and an 86% retention rate from one client loss, while International revenue rose 4.5% (+4.5%, but -1.7% constant currency) with operating earnings up 80%. No formal forward guidance was provided; management framed the softness as weather-driven and noted severe convective storms in March and April benefiting the business, while acknowledging softening insurance rates. Operating cash flow improved $17.2 million year-over-year to $3.3 million.

negative_highlights: Adjusted pre-tax loss of $6 million, down from prior year income levels due to higher MSR runoff and servicing impacts.

Subservicing additions surged up 94% versus the prior year, with total servicing UPB growing 11% YoY to $338 billion.
Management identified specific incremental adjusted pre-tax income improvement opportunities totaling approximately $27 million for future quarters.
summary: Onity Group reported Q1 FY2026 adjusted revenue growth of double-digits (specifically +26% YoY) but recorded an adjusted pre-tax loss of $6 million compared to prior year income levels. Management revised its full-year 2026 adjusted ROE guidance downward from a previous range, widening it to 10%-15%. The quarter was impacted by elevated FHA delinquencies due to rule changes and higher-than-expected refinancing activity that strained staffing capacity.

negative_highlights: Adjusted net loss widened to $34 million from $21 million in prior quarter

summary: loanDepot reported Q1 FY2026 adjusted net loss of $34 million, wider than the prior quarter's $21 million loss, with adjusted total revenue down to $299 million from $316 million. Pull-through weighted rate lock volume rose 14% to $8.3 billion, within guidance, and closed loan volume of $7.7 billion hit the high end of guidance. Gain on sale margin fell to 271 bps from 324 bps due to rate volatility and product mix. Management guided Q2 lock volume lower to $5.75-$7.75 billion but origination volume higher to $7.25-$9.25 billion, and margin up to 330-360 bps, driven by the new 5x5 HELOC product and Figure partnership. They also highlighted market share gains, a 73% recapture rate, and are actively working on debt maturities.

negative_highlights: Revenue fell note weakness in of expectations due to broader market reality and customer caution carried into the new year.
Adjusted EBITDA loss widened slightly compared to Q1 prior year, though improved significantly from Q4 FY2026.
Cash balance decreased by $300k during the quarter.

Operating expenses decreased by $200k year-over-year (8%) despite slower business activity.
Inventory levels were reduced to $3.9 million from $4.2 million at year-end.
summary: Socket Mobile reported Q1 FY2026 revenue of $3.7 million, a 7% year-over-year decline to $4.0 million in the prior quarter and down from $4.0 million last year. Gross margins expanded to 51.3%, while operating expenses decreased by 8% year-over-year despite slower business activity. The company lowered inventory levels but acknowledged that top-line results fell short of expectations due to continued customer caution.

negative_highlights: SHOP same-property occupancy was flat sequentially at 82.4%, with management citing seasonality and operator transitions.
Q1 G&A included $6.6 million of incentive management fees tied to stock performance; excluding it, G&A would have been $7.4 million.

positive_highlights: Same-property SHOP NOI grew 13.5% YoY to $44.3 million, or 22% excluding Q1 2025 insurance proceeds.

Net debt to annualized Adjusted EBITDAre improved to 7.8x from 8.8x a year ago, and Moody's upgraded the corporate family rating to B3 from Caa1 with a positive outlook.
summary: DHC reported Q1 FY2026 Normalized FFO of $33.1 million ($0.14/share) and Adjusted EBITDAre of $74 million, both ahead of analyst consensus. Consolidated NOI rose 4.7% YoY to $75.9 million, with same-property SHOP NOI up 13.5% to $44.3 million on 110 bps occupancy growth and 5.9% average monthly rate growth; same-property SHOP margin expanded 160 bps to 14.9%. Management reaffirmed FY2026 guidance ranges (SHOP NOI $175-185 million, Adjusted EBITDAre $290-305 million, Normalized FFO $0.52-0.58/share) and noted SHOP NOI is tracking ahead of initial expectations, while SHOP occupancy was flat sequentially at 82.4%.

negative_highlights: Sequential revenue decline of 16.1% due to seasonality and pull-in effects
Bad debt expense of $1 million from a European distributor bankruptcy
Americas revenue down 43% sequentially due to tax credit expiration pull-forward
positive_highlights: Revenue up 33.7% YoY to $25.2 million, ahead of typical seasonality

summary: Tigo delivered a strong start to fiscal Q1 2026 with revenue of $25.2 million, up 33.7% year-over-year, although down 16.1% sequentially. Gross margin improved to 42.8% from 38.1%, largely due to no warranty charges. GAAP net loss narrowed to $1.8 million from $7 million, and adjusted EBITDA loss reduced to $0.5 million from $2 million. Management provided Q2 guidance of $30-32 million revenue and $1-3 million adjusted EBITDA, and reaffirmed full-year revenue of $130-135 million, while noting several growth catalysts including the EG4 partnership, new battery products, and emerging utility-scale pipeline.

negative_highlights: Credit costs increased by over $1 million due to aggressive usage of 60-month financing options.
Inventories rose $10.7 million to $106.9 million, though management expects a drop below $100M in Q2.
Two stores closed in Texas (San Angelo and College Station) due to demographic shifts and weak housing growth.

Management raised full-year guidance for gross margins and fixed SG&A expenses despite macro headwinds.
summary: Haverty Furniture reported Q1 FY2026 net sales of $189.1 million, a 4.1% increase year-over-year, with gross margins expanding to 61.5%. The company raised its full-year 2026 guidance for gross margins (now 60.5%-61%) and fixed SG&A expenses ($307M-$309M) despite headwinds from tariffs, fuel costs, and higher credit card fees. Management expressed optimism for the remainder of the year driven by resilient consumer demand, new store openings, and a refreshed product assortment.

negative_highlights: Latin America revenue remains soft following leadership changes in Brazil to address performance issues.
Foreign exchange headwinds from the strengthening Swiss Franc negatively impacted reported operating expenses and results.
Cash burn increased year-over-year to $19.5 million due to higher bonus payouts, new lab build-out costs, and ongoing litigation defense against Guardant Health.

U.S. volumes expanded at a healthy 28% year-over-year, with major partnerships including Mount Sinai driving decentralized testing adoption.
summary: SOPHiA GENETICS reported Q1 FY2026 revenue of $21.7 million, representing a 22% year-over-year increase driven by volume growth and U.S./EMEA expansion. The company reaffirmed its full-year 2026 revenue guidance of $92-$94 million despite noting that Latin America remains soft due to local headwinds. Adjusted gross margin was 75.4%, while adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed slightly to a range consistent with prior expectations.

negative_highlights: Net loss of $69 million for the quarter.
Cash consumption of $69 million in Q1 (including a $11M deferred payment), though excluding this it was $57M and in line with guidance.
No revenue reported as the company remains in the engineering prototype phase.

Engineering prototype validated 130 performance points including autoland and maneuvers in all four axes.
New 5-year, $150 million loan secured to support operations through 2028.
summary: Eve Holding reported a net loss of $69 million for Q1 FY2026, driven by $59 million in R&D and $7 million in SG&A expenses. The company ended the quarter with record cash liquidity of $578 million, supported by a new $150 million loan and an Embraer synergy initiative targeting $100-$150 million in cost reductions over three years. Management confirmed the engineering prototype has completed 59 flights and validated 130 performance points, with a target of 300 total flights for the year to support certification plans likely in 2028.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined 8.6% due to weaker discretionary spending and elevated fuel costs impacting price-sensitive U.S. consumer shoppers.
Operating profit margin is expected to decline low teens percentage-wise in FY26 driven by incremental $6 million advertising spend and accelerated depreciation of the legacy ERP system.
Net cash provided by operating activities decreased from $6.6M to $3.3M due to higher net working capital requirements.

Operating profit more than doubled to $5 million from the prior year period despite lower revenue volumes.
Hamilton Beach Health achieved a third consecutive quarter of profitable growth with sales on track for 50% increase in FY26.
summary: First quarter revenue declined 8.6% year-over-year to $122 million due to softer U.S. consumer volumes and elevated fuel costs, though gross margin expanded significantly by 510 bps driven by pricing and tariff timing benefits. Operating profit more than doubled to $5 million despite the sales miss, but management reiterated previously issued guidance expecting revenue growth in the mid-single-digits for FY26 while acknowledging a projected decline in operating profit percentage due to increased advertising spend and accelerated depreciation.

summary: KORU reported Q1 2026 revenue of $11.8 million, up 22% year-over-year, with domestic core +12% and international core +35%; PST revenue grew 166% on clinical trial orders. Gross margin was 61.5% versus 62.8% a year ago, a 130 bps decline driven by production-run timing and 87 bps of tariff costs. Adjusted EBITDA was -$10,000, essentially break-even and a 95% improvement, with cash usage of just $100,000. Full-year 2026 guidance was reiterated at $47.5M-$50M revenue (15%-22% growth), 61%-63% gross margin, and positive adjusted EBITDA and cash flow, despite the Q1 beat.

Management provided Q2 revenue guidance of $27-$30 million with operating expenses expected in the high $20s.

Management expressed positive momentum driven by state and local demand and the DHS funding bill, while maintaining prior guidance.

summary: Q1 FY2026 total revenue was $41.9M, up 14% YoY and above the high end of guidance, with software revenue of $34.7M (+12%) and services of $7.2M (+25%). Adjusted EBITDA was -$3.5M (margin -8%), improving 600 bps YoY and above the high end of guidance, while gross margin held at 75%. Management raised FY2026 total revenue guidance to $169.25M-$178.75M and software to $146M-$152.5M, with adjusted EBITDA of -$8M to -$4M, and reiterated a target of adjusted EBITDA profitability in Q4. The key change was a better-than-expected DISCO Platform launch driving larger, multi-year enterprise agreements, though software revenue has been roughly flat over recent quarters.

summary: Lifecore reported Q1 FY2026 revenue of $23.2 million, a 34% decrease year-over-year compared to $35.2 million in the prior period, driven by headwinds including customer supply chain initiatives and an agreement termination. The company recorded a net loss of $15 million and adjusted EBITDA of $1 million, missing expectations due to the revenue decline. Management reaffirmed full-year 2026 guidance for revenue ($120M-$125M) and adjusted EBITDA ($20.5M-$25M), noting that roughly 80% of the identified headwinds will impact the first half of the year.

summary: Q1 FY2026 revenue was $171.5M vs $169.8M a year ago, with adjusted gross margin up 140 bps YoY and 250 bps sequentially to 12.2%. Adjusted EBITDA fell to $4.8M (2.8% margin) from $5.8M (3.4%) on higher SG&A and interest, and adjusted EPS was a loss of $0.10 versus a loss of $0.08 prior year, while GAAP net income of $0.9M was lifted by a $14M gain on the Vonore sale-leaseback. Full-year guidance for net sales of $660M-$700M and adjusted EBITDA of $24M-$30M was reaffirmed, with management noting results could land toward the high end if ACT's 9% Class 8 build forecast plays out. Net leverage fell to 3.8x from 4.1x after a $12.8M debt reduction, and management stayed cautious on supply-chain and trade constraints despite early end-market recovery signs.

UK market starting slow for Hiya

summary: In Q1 FY2026, USANA reported core nutritional net sales of $204 million, up 7% sequentially, with sequential active customer growth led by China. Hiya generated $32 million in sales with 186,000 subscribers, while Rise Wellness delivered $14 million in sales, up over 8x year-over-year and 143% sequentially, driven by the Costco launch. The company reaffirmed full-year guidance of $925 million-$1 billion in consolidated net sales and expects omnichannel to exceed 20% of total sales, up from 16% in 2025. Management noted Hiya's elevated customer acquisition costs due to Meta advertising disruptions but expects stronger second-half performance.

A significant one-time $19 million write-off related to the termination of an Akoya Biosciences development agreement impacted operating expenses.

summary: Q1 FY2026 revenue was $36.4 million (up 20% YoY but down 21% organic), with instrumentation sales softer than expected due to timing issues and a one-time $19M write-off reducing non-GAAP operating expenses by roughly $2.3M sequentially. Management maintained full-year 2026 revenue guidance of $169-$174 million despite the miss, citing commercial investments that will drive growth in H2 without assuming material market improvement.

note and marketing expense rose to 30.7% of net sales, up from 26.6%

summary: Niagen delivered Q1 FY2026 revenue of $31.5 million, up 5% year-over-year excluding divested reference standard business, with e-commerce up 14% and Tru Niagen revenue up 4%. New products like Niagen Plus injection kit and NanoCloud skincare show strong early demand, though NMN competition is pressuring sales and marketing costs.

summary: Q1 FY2026 net sales were $68 million, flat YoY, with gross margin down 50 bps to 44.2%, but operating earnings rose 7% to $7.5 million and diluted EPS rose to $0.64 from $0.57 on a 10% net earnings increase. North American wholesale sales fell 1% to $53.6 million (Florsheim +5%, Nunn Bush flat, Stacy Adams -9%, Bogs -11%), retail rose 2% to $8.8 million, and Florsheim Australia rose 10% (flat in local currency). Management gave no formal margin or earnings guidance, citing tariff uncertainty, though it disclosed a $10 million annualized tariff burden at the current 10% rate versus the prior IEEPA regime, with a phased $18.6 million refund claim submitted. The quarterly dividend was raised 4% to $0.28 per share.

negative_highlights: GAAP revenue down 5% due to new Markel fronting arrangement
GAAP net loss of $13 million from deferred ceding commission amortization
Marketplace revenue down 12% due to one-time prior-year sale
positive_highlights: Written premiums up 18%, ahead of full-year expectations

Record 112,000 policies added in the quarter
summary: Hagerty reported Q1 2026 written premiums of $289 million, up 18% year-over-year and ahead of full-year guidance of 15%-16%. Earned premium jumped 42% to $240 million, and adjusted EBITDA rose 77% to $85 million. The GAAP revenue decline of 5% and net loss of $13 million are due to the new Markel fronting arrangement and amortization of deferred ceding commissions, which wind down by year-end. The company highlighted record policy additions of 112,000, a 77% jump in adjusted EBITDA, and strong auction results at Amelia, including $111 million in sales.

negative_highlights: Interventional glaucoma growth was partially offset by lower utilization per account despite increases in volume and price.
$5.4 million one-time fee earned upon a successful final judgment in Alcon litigation case inflated operating expenses, masking underlying cost discipline.

Interventional dry eye revenue nearly doubled from Q4 ($0.4M) to $1.4M, validating the reimbursed business model.
SmartLids utilization per active account increased significantly from 9 to approximately 16 in the first quarter.
summary: Sight Sciences reported Q1 FY26 revenue of $19.7 million (up 13% YoY), driven by a return to double-digit growth in interventional glaucoma ($18.3M) and strong sequential expansion in the newly launched dry eye segment ($1.4M). Management raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $83-$89 million while maintaining adjusted operating expense guidance of $93-$96 million, citing disciplined execution and early validation of their procedural business models.

negative_highlights: Gross written premiums declined 4.5% YoY reflecting active cycle management in response to tough market conditions and competitive pressures.
The company incurred approximately $10.5 million net loss from a specific energy incident related to the Middle East conflict, with further development expected in Q2.
Competitive pressure has increased to 'quite irrational' levels in some pockets of the property book.
positive_highlights: Underwriting income increased by 35.1% YoY despite a decline in gross written premiums due to strategic cycle management.
Political violence lines are seeing rate increases amounting to thousands of percentage points as capacity shrinks.
summary: IGIC reported Q1 FY2026 gross written premiums of $197.2 million (a 4.5% decline YoY) and underwriting income of $37.7 million (up 35.1%), though the combined ratio was impacted by approximately $15 million in Middle East conflict losses. Management noted that while core operating income rose to $0.56 per share, competitive pressures have intensified significantly across property and energy lines, leading to cycle management actions including non-renewals of reinsurance programs.

negative_highlights: Academic Services revenue declined (traffic headwinds continue) to $45.7 million
Q2 total revenue guidance of $49–50 million implies a sequential decline from $63.3 million in Q1
Free cash flow of $3.1 million was dampened by $12.9 million in severance payments
positive_highlights: Chegg Skilling revenue grew 9% YoY to $17.6 million, with double-digit full-year growth expected

Non-GAAP operating expenses fell 55% YoY ($36.4 million reduction) and CapEx dropped 88% YoY to $1 million
summary: Chegg reported Q1 2026 revenue of $63.3 million, with Chegg Skilling at $17.6 million (9% YoY growth) and Academic Services at $45.7 million. Adjusted EBITDA was $15.5 million (24% margin), net income turned positive for the first time in two years, and free cash flow was $3.1 million, though it included $12.9 million in severance payments. Q2 guidance was given for total revenue of $49–50 million, adjusted EBITDA of $5–6 million, and gross margin of 51–52%; full-year 2026 targets include double-digit Skilling growth, a 60% CapEx reduction, and full convertible debt repayment by September.

negative_highlights: closing 20 company-owned restaurants in Q1 with 30-35 planned for 2026
total revenue flat at $123.8 million due to restaurant closures
net loss of $3.4 million, though narrowed from prior year
positive_highlights: system-wide comp sales growth of over 9% in Q1 and April
adjusted EBITDA more than tripled to $7.7 million
restaurant contribution margin up 460 basis points to 14.9%
summary: Noodles & Company reported Q1 FY2026 system-wide comp sales growth of 9.1% (company 9.4%, franchise 8%), with adjusted EBITDA more than tripling to $7.7 million from $2.4 million year-over-year. Restaurant contribution margin improved 460 basis points to 14.9%, and net loss narrowed to $3.4 million from $9.1 million. The company raised full-year 2026 guidance, including comp sales growth of 7%-10%, restaurant contribution margin of 15.5%-17%, and adjusted EBITDA of $32.5-$37.5 million. April comp sales continued above 9%, and new guest active purchases increased 36% year-over-year.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined 7% year-over-year due to indefinite shipment delays in Middle East, North Africa, and Pakistan regions.
Gross margins contracted significantly to 24.1% from 27.9% prior year, with service margins dropping 600 bps due to higher parts consumption and tariffs.
Company withdrew all financial guidance citing significant unpredictability in the geopolitical environment.
positive_highlights: Transformation plan is ahead of schedule with approximately $10 million of annualized cost improvements already realized versus a $12 million target for fiscal 2026.
Service contract capture rate remains at nearly 90% across the active installed base.
CEO appointed Paul Miele as Chief Commercial Officer to strengthen commercial leadership and top-line growth.
summary: Total revenue was $104.8 million, down 7% year-over-year and down 10% on a constant currency basis, driven by geopolitical disruptions in the Middle East and headwinds in China. The company withdrew its financial guidance due to significant unpredictability regarding product shipments and service revenue in affected regions. While transformation initiatives have achieved approximately $10 million of annualized cost improvements ahead of the original $12 million target for fiscal 2026, gross margins contracted to 24.1% from 27.9% in the prior year.

negative_highlights: Q1 origination volumes were slightly lower than Q4 2025 ($639M vs $635M), though management attributes this to seasonality.
Net Interest Margin remained flat at 3.56% compared to Q4, despite portfolio yield expansion.
positive_highlights: Core net income increased 30% over the prior year's quarter.
Portfolio grew 25.6% year-over-year to $6.8 billion in UPB.
Successfully issued first-ever $500 million unsecured corporate debt, reducing reliance on warehouse lines.
summary: Velocity Financial reported Q1 FY2026 results that were in line with expectations, delivering core net income up 30% year-over-year and portfolio growth of 25.6%. The company maintained a healthy Net Interest Margin (NIM) of 3.56% while expanding its loan portfolio to $6.8 billion through disciplined originations at tight credit levels. Management confirmed the trajectory laid out at the start of the year remains intact, with no specific guidance raise or cut mentioned beyond maintaining current targets.

negative_highlights: Net sales declined 3.7% to $147.3 million, impacted by weather and elevated distributor inventories
American Performance division declined 9.7% due to weather and inventory dynamics at key partners
Free cash flow still negative at -$6.3 million for the quarter
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA flat year-over-year at $27.3 million despite lower revenue, with 71bps margin expansion
Safety & Racing grew 10.2%, Truck & Off-Road up 3.8%, and Euro & Import up 1%
April trends showing mid-single digit growth with channel inventory normalizing
summary: Holley's Q1 FY2026 net sales were $147.3 million, down 3.7% year-over-year, with adjusted EBITDA flat at $27.3 million, expanding 71 basis points to 18.5% of sales. Free cash flow was negative $6.3 million, improving $4.5 million year-over-year. Management attributed the weakness to weather and distributor inventory normalization, but noted improving trends from week 8, with April growth in the mid-single digits. Full-year guidance for the core business was reaffirmed, with portfolio rebalancing expected to yield over $15 million in cash proceeds and 75-150 basis points of EBITDA margin expansion.

negative_highlights: $800,000 severance expense incurred due to client volume shift from nearshore to offshore regions
Telecommunications vertical declined 23.1% YoY as legacy carriers reduced volumes
Adjusted EBITDA margin contracted by 40 basis points primarily due to the temporary impact of work shifting and deferred training revenue
positive_highlights: Record revenue of $164.4 million representing double-digit organic growth for the fifth consecutive quarter
Health tech vertical grew nearly 54% YoY to become a standout performer exceeding expectations
Raised full-year guidance on both revenue and adjusted EBITDA following announcement of strategic partnership with Sierra
summary: IBEX reported record Q3 FY2026 revenue of $164.4 million (up 17% YoY) and adjusted EPS of $0.91 (up 11%), driven by double-digit growth across all verticals including a standout 54% increase in health tech. Management raised full-year guidance for both revenue ($638M-$642M vs prior $620M-$630M) and adjusted EBITDA ($82M-$84M vs prior $80M-$82M), citing a new strategic partnership with Sierra to integrate AI technology. The company highlighted 100% client retention, strong organic growth in top clients, and the successful transformation of its lower-margin US business.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA declined to $2.8 million from $3.1 million in Q4 2025
Cash fell ~$10.8 million to $59.2 million, driven by a $16 million Starlink data installment payment
Management declined to call the record shipment rate sustainable, citing seasonality and 60-90 day lag to activation
