Subscribing vessels up 7% QoQ and 30% YoY to over 9,600
LEO services now over 45% of airtime revenue, up from less than 30% a year ago
summary: KVH reported Q1 2026 revenue of $32.3 million, up sequentially from Q4 2025, driven by record connectivity terminal shipments of roughly 3,100 units, a 70% increase over the prior high (~1,800-1,850) set in Q3 2025. Service gross profit was $9.8 million at a 35% margin, up from 34% in Q4, and subscribed vessels rose 7% QoQ and 30% YoY to over 9,600. Adjusted EBITDA fell to $2.8 million from $3.1 million in Q4, and cash declined about $10.8 million to $59.2 million on a $16 million Starlink data installment payment; LEO reached over 45% of airtime revenue from under 30% a year ago. No explicit forward guidance figures were given, though management said India and Latin America and managed IT costs are already embedded in guidance, and it declined to say the record shipment rate is sustainable.

negative_highlights: Consolidated net sales declined 11% year-over-year, with Americas volume down 16% due to geopolitical and tariff headwinds.
Asia segment revenue fell primarily due to lower volumes associated with trade uncertainties and pricing dynamics in the region.
Central America business faces continued demand challenges as customers navigate complex sourcing decisions regarding tariffs.
positive_highlights: Consolidated gross profit turned positive to $9.1 million from a loss of $0.4 million year-over-year due to cost base reduction and efficiency gains.
Q3 free cash flow generation beat expectations at $7.2 million, reversing anticipated burn with year-to-date FCF reaching $20.5 million.
Americas segment generated positive gross profit for the first time in some period despite a 16% sales decline.
summary: Consolidated net sales were in line with expectations at $X million (implied by context of 'in-line'), down 11% year-over-year but up 7% sequentially, while consolidated gross profit improved to a positive $9.1 million from a loss in the prior period due to cost reductions and portfolio optimization. Management highlighted that Q3 free cash flow generation beat expectations at $7.2 million against anticipated burn, driven by operational efficiencies following plant closures. For Q4 guidance, management expects moderate working capital increases but anticipates revenue improvement specifically in Brazil and Asia segments as supply chain dynamics normalize.

negative_highlights: Management explicitly stated they are not ready to increase guidance despite the strong start, maintaining a conservative stance.
Lab Essentials revenue growth was only single-digit (3%) due to decreased customer count offsetting higher average revenue per customer.
Net loss widened slightly from $4.6M in Q1 2025 to $4.7M in Q1 2026, with operating expenses rising despite lower stock-based compensation.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 13% YoY to reach over $11M in Q1, marking the first such quarterly result in nearly three years.
Clinical Solutions revenue surged 85% YoY due to broad-based growth across multiple customers rather than a single lumpy order.
Gross margin expanded from 30.7% to 34.2%, driven by higher volume and operational efficiencies like digital migration of batch records.
summary: Teknova reported Q1 FY2026 revenue of $10.5 million (sum of Lab Essentials and Clinical Solutions), representing a 13% year-over-year increase driven by an 85% surge in Clinical Solutions, while gross margin expanded to 34.2%. Management reiterated full-year 2026 total revenue guidance of $42-$44 million without raising the range despite the strong quarter, citing a need for more durability before adjusting expectations.

negative_highlights: Adjusted operating loss of $26 million in Q1
Tariff costs of approximately $30 million in Q1; expect higher in Q2
Revenue declined due to shift to lighter-duty, lower-priced trucks
positive_highlights: Bookings improved 7% sequentially from Q4 2025
Backlog increased modestly and new products are gaining traction
Dealer inventories back to normal; RFQs and customer engagement rising
summary: Q1 2026 revenue declined to $795 million with an adjusted operating loss of $26 million, including approximately $30 million in gross tariff costs. Tariffs and a shift toward lighter-duty, lower-priced trucks drove the loss, though bookings improved 7% sequentially and operating cash flow improved slightly. Management expects Q2 to be the low point and a modest full-year operating profit with second-half improvement, while tariffs are expected to rise in Q2 before mitigation actions take effect. Potential refunds of $40 million and $15-20 million in supplier reimbursements are not included in guidance.

negative_highlights: Annualized net charge-offs rose to 8.57% of the average portfolio from 7.54% in Q1 2025
Prior-year quarter included a $3.5 million fair value mark that was absent in Q1 2026, tempering reported revenue growth
No formal numeric guidance was provided; forward commentary relied on qualitative statements about Q2
positive_highlights: Diluted EPS of $0.24, up 22% YoY from $0.19, with net income up 18% to $5.5 million
Originations of $533 million rose 18% YoY, with March alone contributing $250 million
Core operating expenses fell 2% to $44.2 million even as the portfolio grew, lowering the expense ratio to 4.6% from 5.1%
summary: Consumer Portfolio Services reported Q1 FY2026 revenue of $112.3 million, up 5% YoY, with diluted EPS of $0.24 versus $0.19, an 18% increase in net income to $5.5 million. Originations jumped 18% to $533 million (47% above a mis-stated prior-year figure), and the managed portfolio grew 9% to $3.94 billion. Core operating expenses fell 2% to $44.2 million, pushing the expense ratio down to 4.6% from 5.1%. Management gave no formal numeric guidance but described Q2 as looking 'very interesting' and reaffirmed a growth streak, while noting higher annualized net charge-offs of 8.57% versus 7.54%.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined 4% year-over-year to $62.8 million
Minerals and Royalties guided to a year-over-year decrease in operating profit and segment adjusted EBITDA for 2026 on natural gas production declines
Outstanding debt rose to $126.4 million from $100.9 million at December 31, 2025, with greater cash use expected in 2026
positive_highlights: Operating profit rose 43% year-over-year to $11 million and 45% sequentially
Net income increased 80% to $8.8 million, or $1.17 per share, from $0.66 per share
Adjusted EBITDA grew 28% year-over-year to $16.4 million, with utility coal segment operating profit up to $7.4 million from $3.8 million
summary: NACCO reported Q1 2026 revenue of $62.8 million, down 4% year-over-year, but gross profit rose 48% to $14.3 million and operating profit climbed to $11 million from $7.7 million. Net income was $8.8 million or $1.17 per share, up 80% from $4.9 million or $0.66 per share, and adjusted EBITDA grew 28% to $16.4 million. Utility coal and contract mining drove the improvement, aided by a $900,000 depreciation method change and prior-year comparison against a $3 million inventory impairment; management expects meaningful full-year growth in operating profit, net income, and adjusted EBITDA, though Minerals and Royalties is guided to a year-over-year decline and growth is expected to moderate in the second half. Debt rose to $126.4 million from $100.9 million at year-end, with total liquidity of $102.7 million.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined year-over-year primarily due to non-recurring return-to-service revenue of $1.7 million in Q1 compared to $5.9 million in the prior period.
Net loss increased significantly from $0.41 per share to $0.69 per diluted share, with adjusted EBITDA deteriorating from negative $5.1 million to negative $14.5 million.
Cash and cash equivalents decreased to $9 million at quarter-end due to strategic investments in aircraft production slots and fleet modernization.
positive_highlights: Hours flown on sensor planes nearly doubled in Q1 versus last year, indicating rapid adoption of technology-enhanced capabilities.
Management qualified two new Super Scooper captains and two initial attack captains to expand operational capacity for the peak season.
The company secured an exclusive use multi-year contract with Alaska involving two aircraft dedicated to that region.
summary: First quarter revenue of $8.5 million missed expectations due to non-recurring return-to-service work on Spanish Scoopers in the prior year and early deployment activity last January related to the Palisades Fire. Net loss widened to $31.3 million compared to a net loss of $15.5 million in Q1 2025, driven by increased SG&A expenses and interest costs. Management reiterated full-year 2026 guidance for revenue between $135-$145 million and adjusted EBITDA between $55-$60 million.

negative_highlights: Total revenue fell 4% YoY to $256 million and Adjusted OIBDA fell 18% YoY to $93 million

TTM free cash flow fell ~13% to $99 million, and management expects proportionately lower FCF YoY as 2026 CapEx peaks at ~$290 million
positive_highlights: Consumer gross margin rose to 72.2% on lower video programming costs after exiting video

Management said the pace of broadband losses is decreasing, indicating a stabilizing base, with 15,500 data subs after a 700 loss
summary: GCI's Q1 revenue fell 4% YoY to $256 million and Adjusted OIBDA dropped 18% to $93 million, with roughly $13 million of the decline tied to non-recurring comparability items including a $4 million 2025 rate-appeal benefit and a $2 million Quintillion fiber-break benefit. Consumer revenue declined 5% (video shutdown plus data subscriber losses) and business revenue fell 3%, though business revenue would have been flat ex the prior-year out-of-period recovery. Management gave no formal revenue/EBITDA guidance, but reiterated 2026 as peak CapEx year (~$290 million) and flagged proportionately lower free cash flow YoY after TTM FCF of $99 million, down 13%. Strategic changes dominated: a $310 million cash deal for Quintillion, a ~$107 million purchase of a 6% Liberty Latin America equity stake, and a planned rename to Liberty Capital Corporation.

negative_highlights: FY2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance was reduced by $5 million on each end to $167.5-$182.5 million.
Revenue declined 3% year-over-year to $410.5 million, with adjusted EBITDA of $28.1 million coming in below internal expectations.
Self-insured health plan expense was about $3 million higher year-over-year, and harsh winter weather delayed the construction season and constrained field service, parts, and rental utilization.
positive_highlights: Gross margins increased 240 basis points sequentially, which management sees as a signal of improving pricing and supply-demand dynamics.
Material Handling bookings increased over 20% in the quarter, with March the strongest single booking month since June 2023.
Operating cash flow was $20.8 million, an improvement of $38.3 million versus Q1 2025, and net leverage stayed flat versus year-end.
summary: Alta Equipment reported Q1 FY2026 revenue of $410.5 million, down 3% year-over-year, with adjusted EBITDA of $28.1 million, which management said was below internal expectations. The company lowered its FY2026 EBITDA guidance by $5 million on each end to $167.5-$182.5 million, while expecting $100-$110 million of free cash flow. Positively, gross margins rose 240 bps sequentially, operating cash flow improved by $38.3 million year-over-year to $20.8 million, March EBITDA was 3x January, and Material Handling bookings increased over 20% with March the strongest booking month since June 2023. Management attributed the shortfall to weather, Q4 tax-related pull-forward, and higher healthcare costs, but expects recovery through the balance of the year.

negative_highlights: GAAP net loss attributable to Acacia was $15.7 million (-$0.16/share) versus $24.3 million net income a year ago, including a $9.7 million unrealized hedge mark-to-market loss and a $1.6 million equity portfolio unrealized loss
IP segment revenue fell to $0.7 million from $70 million a year ago (lapping the Atlas settlement), producing negative $3.5 million adjusted EBITDA

Deflecto's Portland-to-Dover consolidation is expected to yield ~$2 million in annualized cost savings beginning in H2 2026, with Deflecto revenue up 4.6% and adjusted EBITDA up 1.3% sequentially
summary: Q1 2026 total revenue was $54.2 million with operated segment adjusted EBITDA of $6.8 million, or $10.3 million ex-IP, and total company adjusted EBITDA of $1.6 million. GAAP net loss attributable to Acacia was $15.7 million (-$0.16/share) versus prior-year net income of $24.3 million ($0.25), driven by a $9.7 million unrealized hedge mark-to-market loss and the lapping of a Q1 2025 Atlas IP settlement ($0.7 million IP revenue this quarter versus $70 million a year ago); adjusted diluted EPS loss was $0.07. Benchmark posted record revenue of $18.7 million with $7.7 million adjusted EBITDA and completed its first Cherokee well on budget ($11.5 million, >2.5x MOIC), while Deflecto revenue fell to $27.7 million from $28.5 million on Canadian housing weakness and building products declined 13.1% year-over-year. No formal guidance was issued; management did not commit to a well count and deferred buyback specifics to other capital allocation priorities.

One new non-accrual with $7.2M cost and $5M fair value

summary: NCDL reported Q1 2026 NII of $0.41 per share, or $0.43 ex one-time refinancing expenses, down from $0.44 in Q4 2025. Total investment income declined to $46.3M from $50M on lower base rates. NAV fell to $17.50 from $17.72 due to spread widening and a new non-accrual. Management notes wider spreads (now ~5-5.5% vs 4.5-4.75%) and expects continued deal activity, with pipeline momentum in recent weeks.

negative_highlights: Still reporting net loss of CAD 7 million
Only 80 TULSA-PRO install base at quarter end, still note weakness in of 120 target
Cash burn continues, though expected to decline
positive_highlights: Revenue up 104% YoY to CAD 5.3 million
Gross margin 72%, above prior year's 71%
CAPTAIN trial showed statistically superior quality of life outcomes
summary: Profound Medical reported Q1 FY2026 revenue of CAD 5.3 million, up 104% year-over-year, with gross margin at 72%. Net loss narrowed to CAD 7 million from CAD 10.7 million a year ago. The company maintained full-year 2026 revenue guidance of approximately CAD 25 million (56% growth) and gross margin of 70% or better, and reiterated its path to profitability. Key highlights include positive CAPTAIN trial data showing superior quality of life outcomes for TULSA versus radical prostatectomy, a new TULSA Index for same-store sales transparency, and an FDA clearance anticipated for the Siemens Free Series interventional MR by year-end.

negative_highlights: Merchant net revenue declined 4% to ZAR 751 million due to the exit of non-core ATM business and Switch Pay.
Merchant ARPU fell 7% YoY as the portfolio mix shifted towards lower-ARPU community merchants.
Total impairment charges of approximately ZAR 33 million were recognized for legacy assets, including a ZAR 26 million lease premises charge.

Consumer division delivered record performance with net revenue up 41% to ZAR 627 million and segment adjusted EBITDA surging 81%.
Operating margin expanded significantly from 17.2% a year ago to 21.4% this quarter.
summary: Lesaka reported Q3 FY2026 net revenue of ZAR 1.58 billion (up 16% YoY), driven by a record Consumer division (ZAR 627m) and Enterprise growth, though Merchant revenue declined 4% due to non-core exits and integration focus. Group adjusted EBITDA hit an all-time quarterly high of ZAR 337 million (up 45% YoY), with operating margins expanding from 17.2% to 21.4%. Management tightened full-year FY2026 revenue guidance to ZAR 6.2-6.5 billion but raised adjusted EPS guidance to ZAR 5.50-6.00 per share.

negative_highlights: Extended Warranty adjusted EBITDA fell to $0.4 million from $0.9 million year-over-year
Extended Warranty G&A growth outpaced revenue on sales/marketing and an ERP conversion, pressuring segment profitability
Total net debt rose to $63.9 million from $62.4 million at December 31, 2025
positive_highlights: KSX revenue grew 80.7% to $21.1 million and segment adjusted EBITDA rose 82% to a record $3.5 million
Consolidated adjusted EBITDA increased to $2.4 million from $1.4 million, and net loss narrowed to $2.2 million from $3.1 million
SPI annual recurring revenue rose over 45% with gross revenue retention of 97% and net revenue retention above 100%
summary: Kingsway reported Q1 FY2026 consolidated revenue up 37.4% to $39.0 million, with KSX revenue up 80.7% to $21.1 million and Extended Warranty revenue up 7.2% to $17.9 million. Consolidated adjusted EBITDA rose to $2.4 million from $1.4 million, while net loss narrowed to $2.2 million from $3.1 million. KSX adjusted EBITDA hit a record $3.5 million (+82%), but Extended Warranty adjusted EBITDA fell to $0.4 million from $0.9 million. Management reiterated expectations for double-digit organic growth at both segments in 2026 and confirmed its 3-5 acquisition target, with one tuck-in (Ledgers by Ravix) already completed.

negative_highlights: GAAP net loss of $9.6 million ($0.17 per share) due to realized losses on asset resolutions.
CECL reserves increased by approximately $11 million, primarily driven by higher provisions for two large legacy loans (Chicago office and Brooklyn condo).
Resolution timelines for the Chicago risk-rated 5 loan remain uncertain as they depend on external market conditions outside management's control.
positive_highlights: Portfolio grew by $110 million quarter-over-quarter to reach $1.7 billion with no negative credit migrations in the risk-rated 1-3 portfolio.
Liquidity strengthened significantly as available capital reached $163 million, supported by a $94 million repayment collection and an additional $300 million increase in borrowing capacity.
Management successfully exited or reclassified legacy assets including a Chicago office loan (risk-rated 5) and North Carolina REO to reduce risk exposure.
summary: ACRE reported a GAAP net loss of $9.6 million ($0.17 per share) for Q1 FY2026, driven by a realized loss of $3.3 million on the exit of a risk-rated 5 Pennsylvania multifamily loan and an increase in CECL reserves to $138 million. Distributable earnings were approximately $3.2 million ($0.06 per share), excluding the specific resolution losses but including cash interest collected from nonaccrual loans. Management highlighted portfolio growth with new commitments totaling $294 million, a 22% year-over-year increase in loan balance to $1.7 billion, and improved liquidity via increased borrowing capacity.

negative_highlights: Net loss increased to $6.5 million due to non-cash warrant liability
Firearms market remains soft per NICS data
Lease revenue expected to moderate as originations shift
positive_highlights: Revenue up 167% year-over-year to $8.2 million
Payments GMV up 417% to $186.2 million
Operating loss improved 34% year-over-year
summary: PSQ Holdings reported Q1 FY2026 revenue of $8.2 million, up 167% year-over-year, with operating expenses down 18% and operating loss improved 34% to $6.1 million. Payments GMV surged 417% to $186.2 million, while credit GMV grew 32% to $15.1 million against a soft firearms market. Headcount was cut 31% to 47, boosting revenue per employee 287% to $173,583, and management reiterated expectations of $8 million in annualized cash savings from restructuring. The company ended the quarter with $10.1 million unrestricted cash and expects existing cash plus brand sale proceeds to fund operations for at least 12 months.

negative_highlights: Full-year revenue guidance midpoint was cut 2.2% to $880 million from $900 million due to timing delays, with roughly $20-25 million of Q3 revenue deferred.
Process and Industrial Facilities revenue fell to $35.1 million from $45.4 million, and segment gross margin dropped to 2.5% from 8.3%.
Backlog has drifted lower for four consecutive quarters and quarterly awards came in below expectations; CFO is departing in September and no COO will be backfilled.
positive_highlights: Gross margin expanded to 8.3% from 6.4% a year ago, with Storage & Terminal Solutions margin up to 7% from 3.9% and Utility & Power margin up to 13.6% from 9.4%.
Adjusted EPS of $0.13 signaled a return to profitability versus a $0.12 adjusted loss per share last year; adjusted EBITDA improved to $4.9 million from breakeven.
Cash rose $34 million in the quarter to $258 million, with total liquidity of $297 million, aided by resolution of two legacy legal disputes expected to add nearly $20 million in cash.
summary: MTRX returned to profitability in Q3 FY26 with adjusted EPS of $0.13 versus a $0.12 loss per share a year ago, on revenue of $206.7 million versus $200.2 million, up 3.2% YoY. Gross margin expanded to 8.3% from 6.4%, driven by Storage and Terminal Solutions revenue growth of 16% to a six-year-high $111.6 million and Utility and Power gross margin of 13.6%, partly offset by Process and Industrial gross margin collapsing to 2.5% from 8.3%. However, full-year revenue guidance midpoint was reduced 2.2% to $880 million from $900 million due to weather-related and client-caused delays that deferred $20-25 million of Q3 revenue, and quarterly awards came in below expectations. Management said Q4 revenue should turn upward and profitability should continue, while bookings and backlog growth are now expected to reaccelerate in fiscal 2027.

positive_highlights: Retail sales grew 7% year-on-year to over 13,100 cars, a record first quarter for Polestar
Polestar 4 made up 67% of volume versus 49% a year earlier, supporting profitability mix
Cash position of approximately $676 million with covenant compliance at quarter-end
summary: Polestar reported Q1 FY2026 retail sales of over 13,100 cars, up 7% year-on-year, with revenue broadly flat at $633 million. Gross margin was -3.2% and adjusted gross margin -3.3%, while net loss widened to $383 million from $166 million a year earlier and adjusted EBITDA loss widened to $235 million from $96 million. Management cited pricing pressure, EU and U.S. tariffs, lower carbon credit sales, and negative FX as drivers, and reaffirmed its February volume guidance of low double-digit growth without providing new numerical guidance on margins or cash flow. The company ended the quarter with approximately $676 million in cash and remains in compliance with covenants, with two planned debt-to-equity conversions from Geely Sweden and Volvo Cars expected later this year.

negative_highlights: Updated IHS weighted-average OEM end market growth forecast cut to 1.8% from 7.1% at the Q4 call
Full-year revenue guidance range lowered by $20 million to $645-670 million (attributed to contract manufacturing revenue recognition)

Net debt reduction of ~$42 million came from Control Devices sale proceeds rather than operations; credit facility matures July 1, 2027 with refinancing only initiated in April and targeted for completion by November
positive_highlights: MirrorEye sales set a quarterly record of $33 million, up 11% QoQ and 32% YoY
Adjusted gross margin expanded 400 bps QoQ and adjusted operating margin 180 bps QoQ; adjusted EBITDA of $2 million beat prior expectation of approximately break-even
Two new program awards totaling ~$135 million lifetime revenue, including a fourth North American Class 8 OEM MirrorEye program and a ~$65 million off-highway controls award
summary: SRI reported Q1 FY2026 sales of $160.8 million, up 9.2% QoQ and relatively consistent with prior expectations, with revenue outpacing a weighted-average OEM end market that declined 9.1% QoQ; MirrorEye set a record at $33 million (+11% QoQ, +32% YoY) and Brazil OEM sales grew 54%. Adjusted gross margin expanded 400 bps QoQ and adjusted operating margin 180 bps QoQ, driving adjusted EBITDA of $2 million versus prior expectations of approximately break-even. Full-year 2026 revenue guidance was adjusted by $20 million to $645-670 million and adjusted operating margin to approximately breakeven to 0.5% purely for contract manufacturing revenue recognition tied to the Control Devices sale; adjusted EBITDA guidance of $20-25 million and base guidance were reaffirmed. Updated IHS forecasts now show the weighted-average OEM end market growing just 1.8% for the year versus 7.1% previously, though management said this is now in line with its initial guidance expectations.

negative_highlights: Total revenue declined 28.1% due to 55.7% drop in hardware revenue
Consolidated net loss of $77,000 versus net income of $464,000 in prior year
No revenue expected from Infrastructure Solutions segment in first half of 2026
positive_highlights: Monitoring revenue grew 11.7% year-over-year to $1.417 million
Gross margin improved to 80.2% from 75.1%
OmniMetrix delivered operating income of $395,000
summary: Q1 2026 revenue fell 28.1% to $2.227M due to a 55.7% decline in hardware revenue from the cell phone provider contract, while monitoring revenue grew 11.7% to $1.417M. Gross margin improved 510 bps to 80.2%, and OmniMetrix remained profitable with operating income of $395k, but consolidated net loss was $77k including higher stock comp. Management expects incremental hardware revenue of $350k-$500k from the customer in 2026 and reiterated 20% average annual revenue growth target. AIO partnership is pre-revenue with two demo sites live.

negative_highlights: Minimal product deliveries in Q1 leading to operating loss of ~$5 million
Pace of progress toward new U.S. government contract slower than prior processes
CHMP recommended withdrawal of TPOXX's mpox indication in Europe
positive_highlights: Declared and paid a special cash dividend of $0.60 per share, fifth consecutive annual special dividend
Expected Q2 delivery of approximately $13 million oral TPOXX to international customer
Entered exclusive license and distribution agreement with Hikma MENA for TPOXX in MENA region
summary: SIGA reported minimal Q1 2026 product deliveries, with product revenues of roughly $3 million (including IV TPOXX to SNS and reimbursement revenues) and R&D revenues of about $3 million. The company posted a pre-tax operating loss of about $5 million and a net loss of $0.05 per share. Management expects Q2 product revenues of approximately $13 million from an international oral TPOXX order and additional IV TPOXX deliveries. U.S. contract progress is slower than prior processes, but the company cites $27 million in 2025 funding and a new MENA distribution agreement with Hikma as positive signals, while also noting a pending CHMP context to withdraw the mpox indication.

negative_highlights: Three loans remain on non-accrual, and the Justice Grown loan entered maturity default on May 1, 2026, with management saying it is too early to predict outcomes
Management declined to give fundings guidance for the rest of the year, making deployment timing hard to model
Expected lower middle market yields are guided down into the low double-digit range, below the prior mid-to-high teens cannabis yields
positive_highlights: NAV per share increased $0.44 to $7.90, driven by $0.21 of NII and approximately $0.28 of unrealized appreciation on investments
Closed two non-cannabis lower middle market loans totaling about $90 million, plus $5 million subsequent to quarter end, in first quarter as a BDC
Received $6.2 million of paydowns on Debbie Holt's in Q1, bringing total since receivership to $20.8 million, and expanded the revolver to $80 million with a new $30 million commitment
summary: AFC reported Q1 2026 total investment income of $9.8 million and net investment income of $4.8 million, or $0.21 per basic weighted average share, and declared a $0.05 quarterly distribution. NAV per share rose $0.44 to $7.90, driven by $0.21 of NII and roughly $0.28 of unrealized appreciation. Management gave no formal guidance on fundings for the rest of the year, citing difficulty predicting deployment in the new lower middle market strategy, though the pipeline stands at over $1.5 billion of deals. The company closed two non-cannabis loans totaling about $90 million in its first quarter as a BDC, while three loans remain on non-accrual and the Justice Grown loan entered maturity default on May 1, 2026.

negative_highlights: Q2 revenue guidance ($84.5M-$85.5M) represents a sequential decline compared to Q1, attributed to timing of BigCommerce Payments launch.
Full-year non-GAAP operating margin guidance capped at 14% with combined Rule of 40 growth plus margins between 11%-22%.
positive_highlights: Achieved first-ever GAAP net income of $3.7 million driven by operational discipline and margin expansion.
Non-GAAP operating income beat the high end of guidance at $12.4 million, reflecting leverage in the cost structure.
GMV growth accelerated to 14% YoY from 12% for full year FY25.
summary: Commerce.com reported Q1 FY2026 revenue of $86.8 million (up 5% YoY) and non-GAAP operating income of $12.4 million, both beating the high end of guidance ($82.5M-$83.5M rev; $9.3M-$10.3M op inc). The company achieved its first quarter of GAAP profitability with net income of $3.7 million and delivered GMV growth acceleration to 14% YoY. Management reaffirmed full-year FY26 revenue guidance between $347.5M and $369.5M, noting that the sequential step-down in Q2 is due primarily to timing differences related to an earlier-than-expected launch of BigCommerce Payments.

negative_highlights: Farming segment revenue fell to about $900,000 from $1.6 million on lower carryover crop available for sale
Commercial and industrial real estate revenue was flat at $2.8 million year over year, with diesel fuel margin pressure noted at the TA Petro JV
Shareholders pressed on continued spending for Mountain Village and Centennial, which generate no income, and management gave no timeline or commitment beyond considering alternatives
positive_highlights: Operating costs fell 14% including a $2.4 million reduction in corporate costs, driving net income up $1.6 million and adjusted EBITDA up $3.1 million
Mineral resources revenue rose 36% to $3.5 million with segment operating profit more than doubling to $1 million on opportunistic water sales
TRCC industrial portfolio 2.8 million sq ft is 100% leased, commercial/retail 95% leased, and a new 510,000 sq ft Class A facility broke ground
summary: Q1 FY2026 revenue and other income rose 13% to $10.8 million from $9.6 million, with operating costs down 14% (including a $2.4 million cut in corporate costs), net income up $1.6 million, and adjusted EBITDA up $3.1 million; trailing 12-month adjusted EBITDA was $27.2 million. Mineral resources revenue rose 36% to $3.5 million on opportunistic water sales, commercial/industrial real estate was flat at $2.8 million, and farming revenue fell to about $900,000 from $1.6 million on lower carryover crop. Total liquidity was roughly $86 million. No formal forward guidance was given; management reiterated priorities of Terra Vista lease-up, TRCC momentum, and seeking external capital for master-planned community development, while facing shareholder criticism on capital allocation and a commitment to take an 'objective look' at the farming business.

negative_highlights: RNG commodity revenue decreased 49.3% YoY due to the expiration of fixed price pathway contracts.
Renewable electricity generation operating loss widened to $2.2 million from $1 million in the prior year.
Full-year renewable electricity revenue guidance was lowered due to a one-month delay in project commissioning.
positive_highlights: Total revenues increased 9% YoY to $46.4 million, driven by a 25.5% increase in RINs sold (12.4 million units).
Adjusted EBITDA grew 22.8% YoY to $10.8 million.
Successfully commissioned the Montauk Ag Renewables project in Turkey and North Carolina, with production expected to commence in May 2026.
summary: Total revenues of $46.4 million in Q1 2026 represented a 9% increase year-over-year, driven by higher RIN sales volume and environmental attribute revenue, while RNG commodity revenue fell 49.3%. The company reaffirmed full-year 2026 production guidance but updated revenue ranges downward due to a one-month delay in the commissioning of the Montauk Ag Renewables project in North Carolina.

negative_highlights: Total revenue declined 2% year-over-year and 4% quarter-over-quarter due to a subdued hiring environment with quits rates at lowest levels since 2015.
Revenue per paid employer fell 2% YoY ($1,698) as the number of quarterly paid employers remained flat despite seasonal sequential growth.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA came in at $9.7 million, exceeding the high end of guidance and expanding margin from 5% YoY to 9% sequentially driven by efficient marketing spend.
New AI search engine drove a 37% increase in application volume for exposed job seekers within Q1.
Enterprise segment revenue grew 5% year-over-year, doubling its share of total revenue compared to pre-COVID levels.
summary: ZipRecruiter reported Q1 FY2026 revenue of $107.5 million (a decline) and Adjusted EBITDA of $9.7 million, beating the high end of guidance despite a soft hiring backdrop with job openings down 3% YoY. Management raised full-year outlook expectations to flat top-line growth in 2026 compared to declines previously expected, citing operational efficiency gains that pushed Q1 margins above the upper range of their forecast.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA remained negative at $1.3 million and net loss was still $21.7 million
Liquidity is thin at $4.8 million in cash against $6.5 million of quarterly capital spending
$4 million of 45Z production tax credits were needed to reach the reported gross profit, and the updated 45Z GREET model remains unpublished, delaying project financing
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 27% to $54.6 million with growth in all three reportable segments
Gross profit swung positive to $2.8 million from a $5.1 million gross loss a year ago, an ~$8 million improvement
Dairy RNG volumes rose 55% to 110,000 MMBtu and seven new LCFS pathways at an average CI of -380 were approved
summary: Q1 FY2026 revenue rose 27% to $54.6 million from $42.9 million, with gross profit turning positive at $2.8 million versus a $5.1 million gross loss a year ago, and operating loss narrowing roughly 60% to $6.3 million. Net loss improved to $21.7 million from $24.5 million, but adjusted EBITDA was still negative $1.3 million and cash was only $4.8 million. $4 million of 45Z credits propped up the operating result, and no formal revenue, EPS or EBITDA guidance was provided; forward commentary centered on DOE's 45Z GREET update, MVR commissioning at Keyes, LCFS prices and an India IPO. Dairy RNG volumes rose 55% to 110,000 MMBtu and biodiesel revenue rebounded to $10.5 million in India.

negative_highlights: Consolidated commission income decreased year-over-year due to the divestiture of certain non-core operations in 2025
EBITDA turned negative at -$0.4 million compared with positive EBITDA of $0.1 million in the prior period
positive_highlights: Retained insurance businesses achieved 11% organic revenue growth despite portfolio realignment
Balance sheet strengthened with unrestricted cash increasing to $2.3 million and stockholders' equity rising to $7.4 million
summary: Commission income declined to $3.8 million from $4.2 million in the prior year period due to a divestiture of non-core operations, though retained businesses showed 11% organic growth. Net loss narrowed slightly to $1.4 million compared with $1.7 million previously, driven by lower operating expenses and reduced interest costs. Management highlighted balance sheet improvements but provided no specific financial guidance for the next quarter.

negative_highlights: Total revenue declined sequentially from $59.9 million in Q4 2025 due to a $7.9 million inventory drawdown and lower demand.
Royalty revenue fell significantly to $2.8 million compared to $15.6 million in the prior quarter, driven by lack of large China shipments.
Demand decreased approximately 6% quarter-over-quarter despite year-over-year growth.
positive_highlights: Full-year guidance raised for both net NERLYNX product revenue (to $202-$206 million) and net income (to $16-$19 million).
New prescriptions increased approximately 25% quarter-over-quarter, indicating underlying demand growth.
Company is now debt-free after making its final payment to Athyrium.
summary: Puma Biotechnology reported Q1 FY2026 revenue of $44.8 million ($42M product net), which declined from the prior quarter due to a $7.9 million inventory drawdown and lower demand, though new prescriptions rose 25% year-over-year. Management raised full-year guidance for net NERLYNX product revenue (now $202-206M vs previous $194-198M) and net income ($16-19M), but the quarter itself was a miss on sequential growth driven by inventory normalization.

negative_highlights: One new mobile hotspot model launch delayed into late June due to engineering issues persisting into Q2, impacting quarterly outlook.
FWA revenue declined sequentially as a specific large customer overhauled its executive team and changed go-to-market approach.
Q2 adjusted EBITDA expected to be lower sequentially due to increased investment in sales, marketing, and R&D before second-half profitability improves.
positive_highlights: Q1 results delivered within the guided range with healthy gross margins at 48.9%.
Announced a transformational acquisition of Nokia's FWA business valued at $20 million, which more than doubles revenue size and provides immediate global scale.
Secured commitments for next-generation FWA platforms from existing large customers despite near-term disruption.
summary: Q1 FY2026 revenue grew 8% year-over-year to $34.3 million with adjusted EBITDA of $1.8 million at the higher end of guidance. Management noted a sequential decline in FWA revenue due to customer executive changes and persistent delays on one mobile hotspot model impacting Q2 outlook, though they remain positive on full-year targets including an acquisition that will double company scale.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined 6% year-over-year
Paid active member count decreased 4% year-over-year
New Expensify performance is not yet fast enough for larger customers seeking migration
positive_highlights: Interchange revenue increased 10% year-over-year to $5.5 million
Free cash flow generated was $2.5 million (excluding a one-time legal payment)
April paid active members rose to 641,000 from the Q1 average of 632,000
summary: Expensify reported Q1 FY2026 revenue of $34 million, down 6% year-over-year, with paid active members declining to an average of 632,000 (down 4%). Management reiterated full-year free cash flow guidance at $6-$9 million and noted a one-time legal payment reduced the quarter's reported FCF from roughly $5 million. While April saw member count improvement to 641,000 and interchange revenue grew 10% YoY, management emphasized performance issues in New Expensify are delaying migration of larger customers.

negative_highlights: Virtual Sports growth remains flat as headwinds in Brazil offset gains from other regions
U.K. Interactive revenue faced a tax rate increase from 21% to 40%, though still grew >10%
BetMGM integration results in New Jersey described as 'mixed bag' and below initial hopes
positive_highlights: Continuing revenue grew 15% YoY to $57 million driven by a 38% surge in Interactive segment
Adjusted EBITDA expanded 29% with margin improvement of 1,100 bps after restructuring adjustments
Generated approximately $60 million in free cash flow used for debt paydown and share buybacks
summary: Continuing revenue grew by 15% year-over-year to $57 million in Q1 FY26, driven primarily by a 38% increase in the Interactive segment and strong retail performance despite U.K. tax rate hikes offsetting growth. Adjusted EBITDA rose 29%, expanding margins by 1,100 basis points after adjusting for one-time restructuring impacts from divesting holiday parks and restructing pubs. Management raised adjusted EBITDA margin guidance while maintaining revenue expectations, citing steady sequential trends post-seasonality removal.

negative_highlights: Management withdrew full-year earnings guidance citing a focus on portfolio transition rather than performance issues
Monthly distribution reduced to $0.16 per share starting July, lowering annual run rate to $1.92
positive_highlights: Same-store cash NOI increased 3.2% year-over-year
Net debt to adjusted EBITDA decreased by 0.4 times from the prior quarter
Secured $100 million strategic investment and board seat with Maewyn Capital Partners
summary: Chiron Real Estate reported Q1 FY2026 with Net redefined FFO of $0.97 per share and Core FFO of $1.11 per share, while Same-store cash NOI increased 3.2% year-over-year. Management withdrew its full-year earnings guidance to better focus on the strategic transition toward senior housing rather than due to negative performance events. The company reduced its monthly distribution run rate to $0.16 per share starting in July to retain capital for growth investments.

negative_highlights: Total revenue declined 10% YoY
Behavioral subscribers declined 25% YoY
Adjusted EBITDA loss of $1.8 million in Q1
positive_highlights: Clinical subscription revenue grew 32% YoY and clinical subscribers grew 46% YoY
Core+ subscribers grew 6% YoY, first growth in years
Adjusted gross margin near record at 73.6%
summary: In Q1 2026, WeightWatchers reported revenue of $168 million, down 10% year-over-year, with clinical subscription revenue up 32% and behavioral subscription revenue down 17%. End-of-period clinical subscribers grew 46% year-over-year and 51% sequentially to 197,000, while total behavioral subscribers fell 25% to 2.5 million, though Core+ grew 6% to 537,000. Adjusted EBITDA was a loss of $1.8 million, but the company reaffirmed full-year 2026 guidance of $620-$635 million revenue and $105-$115 million adjusted EBITDA, and expects cash generation. Management highlighted the strategic investment in Med+ marketing during the Wegovy pill launch, which drove a 10-point increase in GLP-1 awareness, and expects clinical subscriber growth to continue but at a slower sequential pace.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined 11.6% overall, with Consumer Floral & Gifts down 18.7% and BloomNet down 5.9%
Non-cash goodwill and trade name impairment recorded on Consumer Floral & Gifts and the Personalization Mall trade name

Q4 profitability expected to be pressured by reinvestment in marketing and martech, with management saying the savings will not flow dollar-for-dollar to EBITDA and net debt rising to $94.3M from $75.3M
positive_highlights: Achieved full $50M annualized run-rate cost savings in under a year versus a two-year target, with a new $15M-$20M incremental target (total ~$65M-$70M)
Adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed to $31.2M from $34.9M a year ago despite lower revenue
Gross margin improved 10 bps to 33.2% on cost reductions and pricing discipline, and core headcount cut ~20% since January 2025
summary: Consolidated revenue fell 11.6% with Consumer Floral & Gifts down 18.7%, Gourmet Foods & Gift Baskets essentially flat (+~5% Easter timing lift), and BloomNet down 5.9%. Adjusted EBITDA loss was $31.2M versus a $34.9M loss a year ago, gross margin improved 10 bps to 33.2% excluding prior-year system issues, and a non-cash goodwill/trade name impairment was recorded. FY2026 guidance calls for revenue down ~10%-12% and adjusted EBITDA of approximately break-even ±$2M, including ~$22M of incentive comp and consultant costs. The company hit its full $50M cost-savings target ahead of plan and added a new $15M-$20M incremental target, but flagged Q4 margin pressure as it shifts toward targeted marketing and martech investment.

negative_highlights: Operating loss widened slightly to $3 million from $2.8 million.
Adjusted EBITDA deteriorated to negative $2.6 million from negative $2.4 million.
Management explicitly stated overall performance remains below targets.
positive_highlights: Sequential revenue growth of 16.1% driven by VLN product rollout.
Gross loss narrowed from $0.8 million in Q4 to $0.6 million in Q1.
Secured distribution with the number three purveyor and expanded into Illinois.
summary: Q1 FY2026 net revenue was $4.1 million, representing a 16.1% sequential increase from Q4 2025's $3.5 million. However, the company reported a gross loss of $0.6 million and an operating loss of $3 million, with no specific guidance raised or lowered in the text provided. Management expressed cautious optimism about the back half of the year while acknowledging that top-line and profitability performance remain below targets.

negative_highlights: Total revenue of $55.9M declined 6% year-over-year, driven by continued life sciences weakness, and Q2 guidance implies a steeper 8%-9% decline.
Deferred revenue fell 12% year-over-year to $99M, total remaining performance obligations declined 18%, and current RPO declined 12%, partly due to a shift toward single-year deals.
A $197M goodwill impairment charge was recorded in Q1 due to the stock price decline, despite being non-cash.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA of $15.3M exceeded the high end of guidance by $2.3M, with margin expanding 260 basis points year-over-year to 27%.
Full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance midpoint raised by $1.5M to $55M-$59M, reflecting the strong start and expense discipline.
Net dollar retention improved year-over-year on a trailing-12-month basis, and renewal rates improved both year-over-year and quarter-over-quarter.
summary: Definitive Healthcare reported Q1 FY2026 revenue of $55.9 million, down 6% year-over-year, with adjusted EBITDA of $15.3 million (27% margin) and non-GAAP EPS of $0.06, both at or above the high end of guidance. Full-year revenue guidance remains $220M-$226M (a 6%-9% decline), but full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance was raised by $1.5M at the midpoint to $55M-$59M. Diversified and provider segments returned to modest growth, while life sciences continued to decline; net dollar retention improved year-over-year, and cash flow remained strong. However, Q2 revenue guidance implies a steeper 8%-9% decline, and deferred revenue, total RPO, and current RPO all declined double digits year-over-year.

negative_highlights: New program starts in the quarter were softer than expected, though management characterized this as standard fluctuations rather than a trend.
A one-time non-cash write-off of $2.9M related to legacy small molecule ion channel and tangible assets impacted GAAP operating expenses.
positive_highlights: Total revenue increased significantly year-over-year from $4.2M to $14.4M driven by higher milestones.
Operating expenses decreased slightly to $22.3M, excluding a one-time non-cash write-off of $2.9M related to legacy assets.
Management raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance from prior expectations due to strong Q1 performance and an unanticipated milestone.
summary: OmniAb reported Q1 FY26 revenue of $14.4 million (up from $4.2M in Q1 FY25) driven by milestone payments and service revenue growth, while operating expenses decreased to $22.3 million excluding a one-time non-cash write-off of $2.9 million. Management raised full-year 2026 total revenue guidance to a range of $28-$33 million due to the strong Q1 performance and an unexpected milestone achievement by a partner, while keeping cash operating expense guidance unchanged at $50-$55 million.

negative_highlights: Consolidated revenue dropped sharply by $10.1 million year-over-year due to a largest material handling customer implementing a capital freeze.
Gross margin contracted significantly from 32% in the prior year period to 27.3% driven by lower volumes and higher unabsorbed labor/overhead.
Net loss widened to $3.2 million ($0.15/share) compared to a net loss of $1.9 million ($0.12/share) in Q3 FY2025.
positive_highlights: Operating expenses declined significantly to $4.8 million from $6.9 million prior year due to efficiency actions and headcount reduction.
Flux Power won the Innovation in Sustainability Award at MODEX for its holistic energy lifecycle management solution.
Management expects sequential revenue growth of approximately 20% in Q4 following a return to normal order activity.
summary: Third quarter revenue fell to $6.6 million from $16.7 million a year ago due to a major customer's capital freeze and geopolitical headwinds. Gross margin contracted to 27.3% from 32%, while operating expenses decreased by 30% YoY following cost-cutting measures including headcount reductions. Management provided no specific financial guidance but indicated an expectation of approximately 20% sequential revenue growth in the fourth quarter.

negative_highlights: Reported a GAAP net loss of $0.39 per share and a distributable loss of $0.52 per share in the quarter
Non-accruals totaled $1.55 billion across 11 loans, roughly 44% of the portfolio

CECL reserve rose to 11.4% of UPB from 10.9% at year-end, and a $155 million Phoenix multi-family loan was moved to non-accrual and a $127 million Texas loan was downgraded to 4 ahead of a June 2026 maturity
positive_highlights: Completed ~$600 million of loan resolutions across five loans, four of which were watchlist, cutting the held-for-investment portfolio to $3.2 billion from $3.7 billion
Net debt-to-equity fell to 1.7x from 1.9x at December 31 and 2.4x a year earlier, with $132 million of liquidity at quarter end
Retired the term loan B maturing August 2026 with a new $500 million 4-year senior secured term loan from HPS at SOFR plus 675 bps
summary: CMTG reported a GAAP net loss of $0.39 per share and a distributable loss of $0.52 per share ($0.05 distributable loss prior to realized losses) for Q1 2026. The company completed roughly $600 million of loan resolutions across five investments, four on the watchlist, reducing the held-for-investment portfolio to $3.2 billion from $3.7 billion, and cut net debt-to-equity to 1.7x from 1.9x at year-end and 2.4x a year ago, with $132 million of liquidity at quarter end. No formal guidance was given; management reiterated priorities of turning over the portfolio, resolving watchlist loans, repositioning REO, and deleveraging, with capital allocation decisions expected later in the year. Non-accruals totaled $1.55 billion on 11 loans, about 44% of the portfolio, and the CECL reserve rose to 11.4% of UPB from 10.9% despite total reserves declining to $399 million from $443 million.

negative_highlights: Revenue missed prior guidance expectations, which had called for a total revenue decline of approximately 50% YoY.
Gross margin contracted significantly from 73% last year to 29%, impacted by inventory write-downs and regulatory changes.
Operating loss widened substantially to $68.9 million compared to an operating loss of $26.7 million in the prior period.
positive_highlights: Company enhanced market share position as unit volume outperformed industry declines despite significant headwinds.
Completed BLA submission for ReNu program, advancing the pipeline with a new regenerative therapy for knee osteoarthritis.
PuraPly AM trial achieved primary endpoint demonstrating statistically significant wound closure at 12 weeks (p < 0.0477).
summary: Net revenue declined 58% year-over-year to $36.3 million in Q1 FY2026, driven by a 63% drop in advanced wound care sales due to market disruption and CMS commentary on product wastage. Management updated its full-year 2026 guidance downward from a prior decline range of 25%-38% YoY to an expected revenue decline of 45%-52%, citing a more prolonged recovery timeline than previously anticipated.

negative_highlights: Gas netbacks remain weak due to Waha-Henry Hub dislocation
Wrote off 18 wells in the red box area, will not drill there
Back half production likely flat, relying on base optimization
positive_highlights: Production averaged ~46,000 BOE/d, ~7.5% above guidance midpoint
LOE per BOE came in 17%+ below guide and ~22% below Q4
Generated $21M+ FCF excluding working capital, up from -$42M last quarter
summary: HighPeak Energy reported strong Q1 FY2026 results, with production averaging 46,000 BOE/d, about 7.5% above guidance midpoint, and oil production up 10% quarter-over-quarter. LOE per BOE came in more than 17% below guidance and roughly 22% below Q4 levels, while capital spending was about 29% of the full-year budget. The company generated over $21 million of free cash flow excluding working capital changes, and it maintains its maintenance-mode strategy with 2026 capital at roughly $270 million midpoint, expecting flat production for the year. Management expressed confidence in continued efficiency gains and upside to spot pricing given 40% exposure to spot oil.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA margin contracted 200 basis points YoY to 50.5% due to higher costs in Continuing Education and Medical Practice Solutions.
Medical Practice Solutions active payers declined 1% YoY to 201,000 and monthly active users fell 10% YoY to 221,000.
Residency journey students decreased 20% YoY to 9,744, reflecting weakness in that product line.
positive_highlights: Revenue increased 8% YoY to BRL 1.013 billion, driven by higher medical tickets and non-medical undergraduate growth.
Continuing Education revenue grew 11% YoY to BRL 79 million, with B2B revenue up 13% to a record BRL 74 million.
Operating cash flow conversion was 92.5%, supporting a net debt reduction of BRL 280 million and a leverage ratio of 0.7x.
summary: Afya reported Q1 2026 revenue of BRL 1.013 billion, up 8% YoY, with adjusted EBITDA of BRL 511 million, up 4% YoY but at a 50.5% margin, down 200 basis points YoY. Net income rose 2% to BRL 262 million and EPS reached BRL 2.88, up 3% YoY, while free cash flow grew 3% to BRL 376 million. The company cited a healthy first-half intake cycle with a 4.6% price increase, but MPS active payers declined 1% and monthly active users fell 10%, alongside a 20% drop in residency students. Management did not change full-year guidance and stated that Enamed-related investment and tax impacts are already embedded in the outlook.

negative_highlights: GAAP net loss of $0.05 per share with comprehensive loss reaching $0.12 per share due to mark-to-market adjustments
Book value declined 6.1% quarter-over-quarter driven by March volatility and widening spreads
Economic return was negative at -3.2%, offsetting January gains from spread tightening
positive_highlights: Strategic partnership investment with Real Genius continues to progress in line with expectations
MSR portfolio valuation improved, demonstrating resilience despite the challenging environment
RMBS net interest spread expanded to 2.9% driven by reduced repo costs and dollar roll income
summary: Cherry Hill reported a GAAP net loss of $0.05 per diluted share and an economic return of -3.2% for Q1 FY26 due to geopolitical volatility widening mortgage spreads in March. Book value declined by 6.1% (down $7.9M) from year-end, though it recovered nearly 2% post-quarter end as April spread softening began. Management maintains a solid liquidity profile with $47 million cash and expects continued market turbulence until Middle East stability is achieved.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined 7% year-over-year to EUR 266 million.
Adjusted free cash flow showed a use of cash of $41 million, driven by semi-annual bond interest payment and severance costs.
Q1 revenue decline was exacerbated by quality-related cleanups in the direct response business from the prior year.
positive_highlights: Ex-TAC gross profit increased 5% year-over-year to EUR 108 million despite revenue decline.
CTV revenue grew over 50% year-over-year, driven by strong momentum in EMEA and APAC.
Management exceeded Q1 guidance for Ex-TAC gross profit and achieved Adjusted EBITDA guidance.
summary: Q1 revenue declined 7% year-over-year to approximately EUR 266 million, while Ex-TAC gross profit grew 5% YoY to EUR 108 million due to a favorable revenue mix shift. Management exceeded Q1 guidance for Ex-TAC gross profit and met Adjusted EBITDA guidance of $1 million, but noted that the quarter was an anomaly driven by working capital timing and a one-time bond interest payment of $31 million. Forward guidance for Q2 2026 expects Ex-TAC gross profit between $121 million and $131 million and Adjusted EBITDA between $14 million and $22 million.

negative_highlights: Q1 2026 reported revenues declined versus Q1 2025, due to revenue recognition timing and the non-recurrence of Q1 2025 upfront ASC 606 revenue from a new license agreement
French rehabilitation proceedings involving Gauzy's subsidiaries slowed payments and revenue recognition, temporarily affecting Research Frontiers' liquidity
Court hearing outcomes include potential liquidation of the French subsidiaries, and two licensees liquidated in the past 12 months
positive_highlights: Cash and cash equivalents increased to approximately $1.28 million at March 31, 2026 from approximately $664,000 at year-end 2025, with the company remaining debt-free
Operating expenses and R&D expenses both declined versus the same period last year
Sequential royalty increases from the automotive and aircraft markets from Q4 2025 to Q1 2026, and a meaningful payment received from Vision Systems authorized by the French monitor
summary: Q1 2026 revenues fell versus the prior-year quarter, pressured by the timing of revenue recognition under license agreements and the non-recurrence of upfront ASC 606 revenue from a new license agreement signed in Q1 2025; royalties from automotive and aircraft markets rose sequentially from Q4 2025. Management cited temporary operational and liquidity impacts from the French rehabilitation proceedings of licensee Gauzy's subsidiaries, which slowed payments and revenue recognition, and said a court hearing on May 12, 2026 will determine the next steps, with approval of Gauzy's continuation plan viewed as the most likely outcome. Cash and cash equivalents rose to roughly $1.28 million as of March 31, 2026 from about $664,000 at year-end 2025 after a financing with long-term accredited investors, and the company remains debt-free with lower operating and R&D expenses year over year. No formal forward guidance was provided, and the company declined a live Q&A due to the pending French court proceedings.

negative_highlights: Cash decreased to $65.1 million from $78.2 million at end of 2025
Revenue guidance unchanged at $72-$76 million with second-half weighting
No new major partnership or licensing deal closed in the quarter
positive_highlights: Total revenues of $15.2 million in Q1 2026, up from $7.5 million in Q1 2025
Product gross margin expanded to 71% from 55%
Net loss reduced to $8.7 million from $20.7 million
summary: Codexis reported Q1 2026 total revenues of $15.2 million, up from $7.5 million in Q1 2025, driven primarily by the fully recognized Merck Technology Transfer Agreement. Product gross margin improved to 71% from 55%, and net loss narrowed to $8.7 million from $20.7 million. The company reiterated its 2026 revenue guidance of $72-$76 million, with revenue expected to be weighted to the second half. Management highlighted progress in its ECO Synthesis platform, including new stereochemistry control, over 50 opportunities in the sales pipeline, and ongoing CDMO partnerships, with a goal to sign a licensing deal with a major pharma company in the back half of 2026.

negative_highlights: Total Q1 revenue fell 8% year-on-year to EUR 72.4 million, with RUCONEST down 15%
RUCONEST faces an 8% inventory drawdown, a 3% ex-U.S. exit effect, and early competitive impact from new HAE therapies
Further RUCONEST pressure is expected in Q2, with growth only assumed in the second half of the year
positive_highlights: Joenja revenue grew 34% year-on-year to $14.1 million, with U.S. paid patients up 25% to 127 and seven net new starts in the quarter
Q1 operating cash flow was positive at EUR 2 million and total operating expenses fell 9% year-on-year
Joenja pediatric sNDA for 40mg/50mg was resubmitted in April with a six-month FDA review expected, and launches in Germany and Japan are planned for later this year
summary: Q1 2026 revenue was EUR 72.4 million, down 8% year-on-year, as RUCONEST fell 15% on an 8% U.S. inventory drawdown, a 3% ex-U.S. exit impact, and competition, while Joenja grew 34% to $14.1 million with U.S. paid patients up 25% year-on-year to 127. Full-year 2026 revenue guidance was reaffirmed at $405-425 million (8-13% growth) and opex at $330-335 million; U.S. pediatric APDS revenue is now included for later this year, which was previously excluded. Operating expenses fell 9% year-on-year and Q1 operating cash flow was positive at EUR 2 million despite softness in the quarter.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined 4.7% year-over-year, with medium/heavy-duty trucks falling to 34% of product sales from 44% in fiscal 2025
Operating income fell to $764,000 from $2.8 million, and net income was only $605,000 or $0.07 per diluted share
Operating cash flow was a $9.2 million use and free cash flow was negative $13 million, with $25-$30 million of full-year capex planned
positive_highlights: Gross margin of 20.4%, up 120 bps year-over-year and 520 bps sequentially, the best gross margin quarter in over a decade
$17 million of new business wins in Q1, including a $9 million-per-year battery energy storage award with a three-year minimum commitment
Powersports revenue grew 45.7% year-over-year, the third consecutive quarter of year-over-year growth in that market
summary: Q1 FY2026 revenue fell 4.7% year-over-year to roughly $58.7 million on truck cycle dynamics, with GAAP EPS of $0.07 versus $2.8 million operating income in the prior-year period, though GAAP operating income was only $764,000 after $2.1 million of Mexico expansion costs and $924,000 of succession costs. Gross margin of 20.4% (up 120 bps year-over-year) was the best in over a decade, and adjusted EBITDA was $7.3 million or 12.5% of sales versus $7.2 million or 11.7%. Full-year guidance was reaffirmed: sales flat to up ~5%, gross margin 17%-19%, capex $25-$30 million, with truck recovery expected in the second half of 2026. The company added $17 million of new business wins in the quarter, including a $9 million-per-year, three-year minimum battery energy storage project, while powersports grew 45.7% year-over-year, partly from pulled-forward demand.

negative_highlights: Net interest income fell 8% quarter over quarter to $13.1 million, with weighted average yield to maturity down to 15.8% from 16.3%.

CECL reserve rose approximately $3.8 million to $8.7 million, or 2.1% of principal, driven by LTV increases on Loans No. 4, 34, and 36, with Loan No. 36 downgraded from risk rating 3 to 4 and portfolio loans rated 4+ rising to 10.7% from 4.8%.
Total leverage rose to 38% of book equity from 32%, and weighted average revolver borrowings increased to $48 million from $33.6 million.
positive_highlights: Loan No. 9 returned to accrual status after three consecutive months of timely payment, cutting non-accrual loans to 4.8% of the portfolio from 11.1% at December 31, 2025.
Pipeline of cannabis opportunities stands at $482 million, of which approximately $133 million is backed by real estate collateral.
Floating-rate loan structure with prime-rate floors leaves only about 4% of loan principal exposed to further rate declines, and the portfolio retains 1.2x weighted average real estate coverage.
summary: REFI reported Q1 FY2026 net interest income of $13.1 million, down $1.2 million or 8% from $14.2 million in Q4 2025, primarily due to the prior quarter's $1.7 million catch-up of accrued interest on Loan No. 9. Distributable earnings were $0.47 basic and $0.46 fully diluted, with book value per common share of $14.39 and a $0.47 Q4 dividend declared in April. Credit was the main negative: CECL reserves rose about $3.8 million to 2.1% of principal, driven by LTV increases on Loans No. 4, 34, and 36, and the portfolio's weighted average yield fell to 15.8% from 16.3%, offset partly by Loan No. 9 returning to accrual status (non-accruals cut to 4.8% from 11.1%). Management offered no formal numeric guidance beyond maintaining a 90-100% dividend payout ratio for the 2026 tax year, and cited the April 23 DEA Schedule III medical rescheduling as a prospective positive while explicitly staying in a 'wait-and-see' mode.

negative_highlights: Net cash used in operations widened to $9.1 million from $7.1 million a year ago as R&D climbed to $8.0 million from $5.7 million
Cash and investments fell to $51.3 million from $59.9 million at December 31, 2025
U.S. IND remains blocked: an adverse rabbit immune response prevented the FDA-requested pre/postnatal study, and the company is awaiting FDA feedback on a proposed rat study
positive_highlights: ReMEDy2 enrollment surpassed 70% of the target for interim analysis, with ~70 sites activated including six new European countries
Reaffirmed intention to complete the stroke interim analysis by end-2026 and to complete full enrollment in Q1 2027
Health Canada approved the early-onset preeclampsia Phase II, with Canada sites selected and enrollment targeted by year-end
summary: Clinical-stage biotech with no product revenue; Q1 2026 net cash used in operations was $9.1 million versus $7.1 million a year ago, R&D rose to $8.0 million from $5.7 million, and G&A held at $2.5 million. Cash, equivalents and short-term investments were $51.3 million at March 31, 2026, down from $59.9 million at year-end, with working capital of $46.6 million and runway stated through 2027. R&D expense is guided to increase modestly, with the CFO citing no more than roughly 10% per quarter. Preeclampsia Part 1a extension data are expected this quarter, Part 1b/Part 2 cohorts should begin this summer, Health Canada approved the Phase II, and the ReMEDy2 stroke trial surpassed 70% enrollment with interim analysis reaffirmed by end-2026, though the U.S. IND remains pending an FDA response after a rabbit model immune-response issue.

negative_highlights: Digital-only subscribers of 591,000 were down YoY, with management citing lost starts during last year's cyber event and processing limitations
Digital advertising revenue declined modestly YoY, partly from an intentional exit of lower-margin advertisers and products
No debt principal was paid in Q2; the $1 million payment came after quarter-end, and full-year EBITDA guidance was reaffirmed rather than raised
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA rose 95% YoY to $15 million with margin expanding 670 bps; excluding $4 million of cyber insurance proceeds, growth was still 45%
Cash costs declined $37 million (14%) in the first half, including roughly $23 million of SG&A reduction and $13 million of legacy print cost savings
Interest expense fell $2.4 million YoY after the rate cut from 9% to 5%, with about $18 million in expected annual interest savings
summary: Q2 FY2026 adjusted EBITDA nearly doubled to $15 million with margin up 670 bps, aided by $4 million in cyber-event business interruption insurance proceeds; excluding those, adjusted EBITDA grew 45% YoY. Cash costs fell 15% ($19 million) and digital revenue reached 56% of total revenue, up 270 bps, but digital-only subscribers of 591,000 were pressured by lapping the prior-year cyber event and management called the quarter a 'clean baseline.' Digital advertising declined modestly YoY while showing a second consecutive quarter of sequential improvement and a two-point same-store improvement. Full-year guidance for mid-single-digit adjusted EBITDA growth was reaffirmed, not raised, with the operating beat substantially driven by cost cuts and insurance recoveries rather than revenue growth.

negative_highlights: Full-year Adjusted EBITDA guidance remains unchanged despite strong quarter, implying the tower sale proceeds will not be used for growth investments this year.
Net cash from operating activities decreased by approximately $6 million compared to the prior year due to higher working capital requirements related to government program payments timing.
positive_highlights: Total revenue grew nearly 2% year-over-year to $182 million driven by business and carrier services growth.
Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded significantly, improving 200 basis points to 26.7% from the prior year period.
Net loss narrowed substantially to a $3 million loss ($0.29/share) compared to a $9 million loss in Q1 last year.
summary: ATN reported Q1 FY2026 revenue of $182 million (up ~2% YoY) and Adjusted EBITDA of $49 million (up 10%), with a net loss narrowing to $3 million. Management reiterated the full-year 2026 Adjusted EBITDA guidance range of $190-$200 million, noting that this excludes approximately $6-8 million in expected reductions following an anticipated tower sale closing in Q2.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA down 15% to $11.7 million
Net loss widened to $18.1 million from $15.1 million
Wavelo gross profit and EBITDA declined due to sales and marketing investment
positive_highlights: Consolidated revenue up 2% to $96.7 million, gross profit up 2.5%
Ting revenue up 19%, adjusted EBITDA loss improved 50% year-over-year
Return to positive operating cash flow of $3.5 million
summary: Tucows reported Q1 FY2026 consolidated revenue of $96.7 million, up 2% year-over-year, with gross profit up 2.5%. Adjusted EBITDA fell 15% to $11.7 million, and GAAP net loss widened to $18.1 million. Domains revenue declined 2% but gross profit and adjusted EBITDA grew; Ting revenue surged 19% with adjusted EBITDA loss cut by 50%; Wavelo revenue was flat but EBITDA declined due to go-to-market investments. The company returned to positive operating cash flow of $3.5 million and remains in covenant compliance. Guidance was not provided, but the Radix migration is expected to benefit Q2, and legacy mobile headwinds persist.

negative_highlights: GAAP net loss was $70.8 million, including a $45 million non-cash goodwill impairment.
Intelligence and Advisory segment revenue declined ~4% year-over-year due to lower go-to-market strategic consulting.
Multi-year contract environment remains weak, with customers shortening commitments through 2025 and no pickup in 2026; churn is higher at the lower end of the SME segment.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA rose 27% year-over-year to $7.4 million, with margin expanding to 6.9% from 5.6%.
Brand to Demand segment, ~70% of revenue, grew ~5% year-over-year, led by Unified Demand offering.
Active membership in priority personas (CIO, CISO) grew high single digits, and Omdia KPIs (users, engagement, NPS) were up double digits.
summary: Informa TechTarget reported Q1 FY2026 revenue of $106 million, up 2% year-over-year, with adjusted EBITDA of $7.4 million, up 27% year-over-year, and adjusted EBITDA margin of 6.9% versus 5.6% in the prior year. GAAP net loss was $70.8 million, including a $45 million non-cash goodwill impairment. The company maintained its full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance of $95 million-$100 million, with no change to prior guidance. Segment performance was mixed: Brand to Demand revenue grew ~5% while Intelligence and Advisory revenue declined ~4%.

negative_highlights: GAAP swung to a $0.57 loss per share from $1.01 earnings, with $10.1M of net charges this quarter versus $3.2M of net gains a year ago
Nightclubs segment operating margin contracted to 30% from 33.8%, and Bombshells swung to a $139K operating loss from $1.9M income on revenue down $1.2M
Free cash flow fell to $6.7M from $12.1M and operating cash flow to $7.8M from $13.3M; debt rose $20.6M and weighted average interest rate climbed to 7.16% from 6.65%
positive_highlights: Higher-margin club service revenues rose 6.7% year-over-year despite consumer uncertainty
Bought back more than one million shares year to date, reducing shares outstanding 14.6% since the plan began, and added $20M to the repurchase authorization
Nightclubs revenue rose $0.6M to $62.3M on $4.9M from five new/reopened clubs, and corporate expenses fell to $7.4M (10.4% of revenue) from $8.8M (12.3%)
summary: Q1 FY2026 revenue was $70.8M vs $71.5M a year ago, with GAAP loss per share of $0.57 vs $1.01 in earnings, driven largely by $10.1M of net charges (including a $9.9M non-operating charge and $1.2M impairments) against $3.2M of year-ago net gains. Non-GAAP EPS was $0.74 vs $0.80, adjusted EBITDA was flat at $15.7M, and free cash flow fell to $6.7M from $12.1M on year-end legal, delayed-filing, and insurance payments. Nightclubs revenue rose $0.6M to $62.3M but segment operating margin fell to 30% from 33.8%, while Bombshells revenue fell $1.2M to $8.4M and swung to a $139K operating loss. Management reaffirmed its five-year plan (approx. 40% of FCF to acquisitions, 60% to buybacks/debt/dividends, 10-15% FCF-per-share growth) and cited sequential same-store sales improvement into Q2, plus $31.7M of small clubs and real estate being marketed for sale.

negative_highlights: GAAP net loss widened to $4.8 million (-$0.22/share) from -$4.2 million, with an operating loss of $2.2 million versus prior-year income of $1.1 million
SG&A rose 16.8% to $36.8 million, and unit sales declined in the single-digit percentage range
E-commerce declined early in the quarter on Amazon negotiations and reduced ad spend; the cutlery category saw a year-over-year decline
positive_highlights: Adjusted net income swung to $0.04/share from an adjusted loss of $0.25 in the prior year
Gross margin expanded to 37.7% from 36.1%, with U.S. segment margin at 37.9% versus 36.2%
Generated $30 million of free cash flow, reducing net debt to $170 million and improving the adjusted EBITDA/net debt ratio to 3.2x
summary: Q1 FY2026 net sales rose 2.4% to $143.5 million, with the U.S. up 1.7% and international up 10.6% (2.5% ex-FX). GAAP net loss widened to $4.8 million (-$0.22/share) from -$4.2 million, but adjusted net income was $0.04/share versus a $0.25 loss a year earlier, and gross margin expanded to 37.7% from 36.1%. Management introduced full-year 2026 guidance of $650-700 million in net sales, $53.5-56 million adjusted EBITDA and $16-17.5 million adjusted net income, citing the full-year benefit of 2025 pricing, a reset cost base and Hagerstown transition costs. Positives include the adjusted earnings swing, gross-margin expansion and $30 million of free cash flow cutting net debt to $170 million (3.2x); offsets include a wider GAAP loss, a 16.8% SG&A increase, a unit decline and a cited $41.7 million potential tariff refund excluded from guidance.

negative_highlights: Q1 results came in below internal expectations, driven by longer producer turnaround and lower Shenandoah rates
Shenandoah 2026 segment margin revised down by $12-15 million versus original guidance
Increasing noneconomic Chinese flake NaHS competition in South American markets
positive_highlights: Full-year 2026 Adjusted EBITDA reaffirmed at or near midpoint, growth of 15-20% over ~$500-510M baseline
Financing cost reduced by ~$12 million annually with balance sheet actions completed during the quarter
Multiple new wells and tiebacks (Monument, Shenandoah South, Tiberius) expected to flow through Genesis infrastructure with no capital
summary: Q1 2026 results came in slightly below internal expectations due to longer-than-expected producer turnarounds and lower-than-anticipated Shenandoah volumes, but other segments met expectations. Management revised Shenandoah 2026 segment margin down by $12-15 million but reaffirmed full-year Adjusted EBITDA at or near the midpoint of prior guidance (~$500-510M baseline, 15-20% growth). Balance sheet actions—new 6.75% notes, redemption of 7.75% notes, upsized revolver, $135M preferred buyback—reduce annual financing costs by ~$12 million. Long-term outlook remains positive with multiple development projects and no required capital.

negative_highlights: Total revenue fell 21% and hospitality revenue fell 34%; ex-closures and Gitano, hospitality revenue was still down 22% on extended below-freezing weather and two major snowstorms
GAAP net loss widened 38% to $44.1 million and net loss per share rose to $3.47 from $2.51, driven by ~$14 million of Tin Building write-off depreciation and restructuring costs

Landlord rental revenue fell 27% (iPic $800K non-cash adjustment, ESPN lease expiration) and the ~$1 million loss from Lawn Club and Jean-Georges ventures reflected weather and a 10-day waterline closure
positive_highlights: Operating EBITDA improved $3.1 million or 21% YoY to a loss of $11.8 million, with hospitality operating EBITDA up $2.9 million or 36% on the Tin Building and Malibu Farm closures
Non-GAAP adjusted net loss improved 21% ($4.9 million) YoY to $17.9 million, and G&A excluding restructuring fell $3.1 million or 31% YoY
Balance sheet strengthened with total cash up $57.3 million to $144.7 million and a $105.6 million net cash position after the 250 Water Street sale; Las Vegas revenue grew 8%
summary: Seaport Entertainment reported Q1 2026 total operating EBITDA improved 21% YoY to a loss of $11.8 million, but revenue fell 21% YoY, with hospitality revenue down 34% ($2.6 million) on the Tin Building and Malibu Farm closures, and excluding those plus Gitano, hospitality revenue declined 22% on severe weather. GAAP net loss widened 38% to $44.1 million ($3.47/share from $2.51), driven by ~$14 million of Tin Building write-off depreciation, restructuring, and weather-hit New York venues, while non-GAAP adjusted net loss improved 21% to $17.9 million (-$1.41/share). Landlord operating EBITDA was flat with rental revenue down 27% (up 4% ex-$800K iPic non-cash adjustment), Las Vegas revenue grew 8% but entertainment EBITDA only rose 3%, and the company gave no formal guidance, reiterating the $70-$90 million remaining capex through 2028 and noting a $105.6 million net cash position after the 250 Water Street sale. Management framed the quarter as a turning point behind leasing momentum (Balloon Museum, Meow Wolf, Public Service, Sadie's) and cost reductions, but the reported numbers show continued revenue erosion and a wider net loss.

negative_highlights: U.S. sales declined 5% year-over-year due to structural conversion of patients from rental tanks to POCs affecting DTC and rental channels.
Adjusted net loss increased to $4 million from $2.9 million in the prior year period due to timing of incremental R&D and advertising spend.
Rental patient counts declined at a steeper rate than recent trends, creating continued pressure on that channel.
positive_highlights: International revenue grew 18% year-over-year to $37.7 million, offsetting U.S. declines.
Adjusted gross margin expanded 30 basis points to 44.7% driven by cost improvements.
New Aurora CPAP mask launch in the U.S. is meeting and exceeding early expectations with high reorder rates.
summary: Inogen reported Q1 FY2026 revenue of $85.1 million, representing a 3.4% year-over-year increase driven by strong international growth (18%) and unit volume expansion (14%), which exceeded expectations despite a 5% decline in U.S. sales due to channel mix shifts. The company reaffirmed its full-year 2026 revenue guidance of $366 million-$373 million, citing continued core business strength and scaling new products like Aurora and Voxi 5. Adjusted gross margin expanded 30 basis points to 44.7%, while adjusted net loss widened slightly to $4 million due to accelerated R&D and commercial investments.
