negative_highlights: Revenue decreased 1.6% YoY and Adjusted EBITDA dropped significantly due to a $10 million unplanned cost headwind from March.
Underlying market demand is down, tracking with SAAR which fell approximately 5% versus Q1 FY25.
Supply constraints are driven by financial pressure on smaller carriers exiting the market and driver attrition.
positive_highlights: Company delivered a market share gain despite being down less than the industry average in terms of units delivered.
Spot participation increased by a couple percentage points with rate premiums better than recent quarters during March volume recovery.
Management expects Q2 revenue to reflect meaningful sequential increases as fuel surcharge index adjustments normalize.
summary: Total operating revenue for Q1 FY26 was $937 million (decreased 1.6% YoY), while Adjusted EBITDA fell to $45 million from $78 million in the prior year quarter due to a material unplanned cost headwind of approximately $10 million caused by higher fuel costs and timing lags on surcharge recoveries. Management expressed clear disappointment with the results, citing extended plant shutdowns, weak SAAR (down ~5%), severe winter weather, and supply constraints as primary drivers that muted underlying efficiency improvements.

negative_highlights: Reported net loss widened to $6.9 million due to a $2.1 million litigation settlement and associated legal fees
New MGA investments reduced EBITDA by approximately $1.1 million in the quarter compared to $0.6 million prior year
Property lines are softening with rate declines observed, particularly in large/middle market accounts
positive_highlights: Insurance distribution segment revenue grew 92% YoY driven by organic growth of 42% and ArmadaCare acquisition
Adjusted EBITDA increased nearly four-fold to $25.3 million with margins expanding to record highs of 32.3%
Corporate nominal expenses declined significantly from $15 million last year to just over $12 million
summary: Octave Specialty Group reported Q1 FY2026 results with total revenue growing 92% to $78.5 million for the insurance distribution segment, driven by a 42% organic increase and the October 2025 acquisition of ArmadaCare. Adjusted EBITDA surged nearly four-fold to $25.3 million as margins expanded to record highs of 32.3%, though reported net loss was $6.9 million due to litigation settlements at Everspan. Management noted Q1 execution exceeded initial expectations but stated guidance for the full year remains unchanged.

negative_highlights: GAAP revenue declined by approximately $1 million due to a restructuring of the GE HealthCare contract that reduced quarterly rental revenues.
Device Solutions segment net revenue decreased by $2.3M (down 17%), with nearly 70% attributable to the GE HealthCare transition and lower equipment sales/rentals from customer buyouts.
Operating cash flow dropped significantly year-over-year, generating only $970k compared to prior year levels due to higher working capital increases.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded modestly from 18.2% to 18.9% despite lower net revenue due to favorable trade-offs between GE HealthCare restructuring and field service projects.
Wound care segment grew nearly 112% year-over-year, driven by a new compression device supplier adding adjustable wraps for patients with limited mobility.
Successfully cleared the go-live hurdle for the new enterprise resource planning (ERP) system on March 1st, integrating data and workflows across business lines.
summary: InfuSystem reported Q1 FY26 revenue of $33.7 million, a GAAP decline of ~$1M driven by the restructuring of its GE HealthCare biomedical services contract which reduced revenue by $1.6M; however, pro forma revenue grew 1.7% and adjusted EBITDA was approximately $6.4M (GAAP) or $6.3M per CFO figures), in line with prior year despite lower top-line growth. Management raised full-year guidance to a range of 6%-8% annualized pro forma revenue growth, citing the successful go-live of their new ERP system and expansion in wound care compression devices as key drivers for future performance.

negative_highlights: A top-five volume customer idled operations in March, expected to be a headwind into the second half of 2026.
LNG peak shaving facility damaged; not expected to be available for the coming winter season, with costs and repair/replacement investment not yet estimable.
Total delivered gas volumes fell 5% in Q2 and 3% in the first half versus prior-year periods.
positive_highlights: Q2 net income rose 14% to $8.7 million, or $0.84 per diluted share, from $7.4 million, or $0.74, a year ago.
FY2026 EPS guidance range narrowed and raised to $1.31-$1.37.
First-half EPS increased 5.3% to $1.31 from $1.26.
summary: RGC Resources reported Q2 FY2026 net income of $8.7 million, or $0.84 per diluted share, up 14% from $0.74 a year ago, driven by new Roanoke Gas rates effective January 1, higher earnings from affiliate MVP, and lower interest expense. First-half EPS was $1.31 versus $1.26, a 5.3% increase. Management narrowed and raised its FY2026 EPS guidance range to $1.31-$1.37. However, a top-five volume customer idled operations in March, creating a second-half headwind, and damage to the LNG peak shaving facility means it will be unavailable for the coming winter season, with costs and repair investment not yet estimable.

negative_highlights: Breached the leverage ratio covenant on the German revolver and received a waiver covering Q1 plus two subsequent quarters; compliance not expected until Q4.
Liquidity fell $201 million to about $229 million, including a EUR 70 million temporary reduction in German facility availability, and the quarter carried a $22 million non-cash inventory impairment.
$52 million net loss ($0.78/share) and a $6 million negative EBITDA in solid wood, with pulp realizations down to $696/ton from $702/ton and fiber costs up roughly 10% quarter-over-quarter.
positive_highlights: Operating EBITDA rose $28 million quarter-over-quarter to about $8 million, helped by the absence of planned maintenance (versus 21 days at Stendal in Q4) and $11 million of One Goal 100 savings in Q1.
Mass timber revenues rose over 60% and production over 20% quarter-over-quarter, with a $171 million backlog (~60% hyperscaler data center projects) supporting production through 2027.

Liquidity actions: obtained covenant waiver with over 80% bondholder consent for a consent solicitation, and U.S. lumber tariff exposure is only 10% versus an average ~35% combined tariff/duty rate for Canadian exports.
summary: Mercer reported Q1 FY2026 operating EBITDA of about $8 million, up $28 million from Q4, but the quarter included a $22 million non-cash inventory impairment and a consolidated net loss of $52 million, or $0.78 per share. The company breached the leverage ratio covenant on its German revolving credit facility and obtained a lender waiver covering Q1 plus the next two quarters, with compliance expected by Q4; aggregate liquidity fell $201 million to roughly $229 million. Pulp sales realizations slipped to $696/ton from $702/ton while fiber costs rose about 10% versus Q4, and the solid wood segment posted negative EBITDA of about $6 million. Management guided to modest NBSK price improvement in Q2, stabilizing fiber costs, $60-$80 million of 2026 CapEx, and $5-$10/ton higher freight plus roughly $5/ton higher chemical costs in Q2.

negative_highlights: No financial guidance provided; revenue and EPS figures were not disclosed in this clinical update call, limiting quantitative performance assessment to program progress only.
Regulatory path remains uncertain with management stating a Phase III trial is the base case assumption rather than accelerated approval based on single-arm data.
positive_highlights: New clinical data showed all patients who were centrally confirmed HER2-positive and CD47 high achieved a response (100% ORR) including one complete response, compared to lower rates in low expression cohorts.
Median duration of response was observed at 20 months for responders with high CD47 expression versus shorter durations in the overall population or low expressers.
Strong financing from February anchored by very strong investors further strengthens the balance sheet enabling execution through data milestones.
summary: ALX Oncology reported Q1 FY2026 results driven by positive clinical data readouts for evorpacept in HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer presented at ESMO Breast Cancer 2026 and progress on the ALX2004 EGFR-targeted ADC program. The company highlighted a strong balance sheet following February financing, new leadership hires including Jeff Knight as CDO/COO, and continued execution with both programs remaining on track for key milestones in late 2027.

negative_highlights: No acquisitions closed in Q1, with management acknowledging a 'slow start' to the year
Lost two larger deals to competitors Welltower and CareTrust, with the CareTrust loss involving a last-minute broker deal at an 8.5% cap rate
Net debt to net asset ratio at 49.0% with $255 million maturing through the remainder of 2026, requiring refinancing
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 7.1% YoY to $40 million and net income rose to $9.4 million ($0.17/share) from $6.9 million ($0.13/share)
100% of contractual rents collected with tenant rent coverage of 2.1x
Dividend increased to $0.17/share from $0.16, maintaining a low 47.3% AFFO payout ratio
summary: Strawberry Fields REIT reported Q1 2026 revenue of $40 million, up 7.1% YoY, with net income of $9.4 million ($0.17/share) versus $6.9 million ($0.13/share) in Q1 2025. Management projected 2026 AFFO of $75.4 million (11.4% growth) and adjusted EBITDA of $128.1 million (13.5% growth), though no prior guidance was provided for comparison. The quarter saw no acquisitions, but the company signed a term sheet for a $300 million credit facility (SOFR+2.75) and an $8.6 million hospital campus acquisition subsequent to quarter end; the dividend was raised to $0.17 from $0.16. Management reiterated its $100-$150 million acquisition target for the year, expecting closings to be back-loaded into Q3/Q4.

negative_highlights: Segment NOI declined $1.9 million year-over-year, with office NOI down $602,000 and hotel NOI down $700,000.
FFO of -$28.8 million was significantly worse than the prior year's -$5.4 million due to preferred stock redemptions and loss on early extinguishment of debt ($705,000).
Hotel segment faced temporary NOI headwinds from renovation disruptions and mechanical system issues removing rooms in March.
positive_highlights: Multifamily NOI increased 64% year-over-year excluding joint ventures, supported by occupancy gains to 89.6% and rent growth of 7.6% in San Francisco.
Sold lending division (First Western) for net cash proceeds of approximately $31 million after expenses.
summary: CMCT reported a segment NOI miss of $1.9 million year-over-year, driven by declines in office and hotel segments, while multifamily NOI increased 64% excluding joint ventures. FFO was -$28.8 million due to the redemption of $243 million in preferred stock and associated costs, though the company completed a strategic transformation including the sale of its lending division for $44.9 million. Management expressed cautious optimism regarding multifamily recovery in the Bay Area but noted ongoing challenges with debt maturities and temporary operational disruptions.

negative_highlights: Americas revenue fell 2.9% to $39.8 million and Asia Pacific fell 14.7% to $4.1 million
Q2 revenue guidance of $62.5–63.5 million is only modestly above the prior-year $61.6 million, which management attributed to macro conservatism
Net cash used in operations of $0.7 million in the quarter and cash declined to $22.7 million from $28.7 million at year-end
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA up 11.8% to $8.3 million, sixth consecutive quarter of double-digit growth, with margin up 111 bps to 13.5%
Europe revenue grew 25.3% to $17.3 million and recurring revenue rose 9% to roughly 47% of the total
AI-related revenue reached $21 million (about a third of firm total) versus $12 million a year ago, and ISG signed its largest-ever deal, valued up to $17 million over up to eight years
summary: ISG reported Q1 revenue of $61.2 million, up 3% YoY and at the top end of guidance, with adjusted EBITDA up 11.8% to $8.3 million and margin expanding 111 bps to 13.5%. Europe grew 25.3% and recurring revenue rose 9% (about 47% of revenue), while Americas fell 2.9% and Asia Pacific fell 14.7%. Management guided Q2 to $62.5–63.5 million revenue and $8–9 million adjusted EBITDA, implying continued YoY growth and margin expansion, and cited AI-related revenue of $21 million (about a third of the total) plus a landmark up-to-$17 million, ~8-year governance contract. Guidance commentary framed the outlook as conservative amid an uncertain macro environment.

negative_highlights: Adjusted net loss unchanged at $8 million with book value declining to -$44.82 per share
No substantive progress on PREPA resolution; legal litigation remains unresolved
Management reported no update on strategic process
positive_highlights: GAAP net loss improved to $40 million from $62 million in Q1 2025
National's leverage ratio improved to 23-to-1 from 24-to-1 at year-end
National statutory net income rose to $11 million from $4 million year-over-year
summary: In Q1 FY2026, MBIA reported a consolidated GAAP net loss of $40 million (-$0.80 per share), an improvement from the $62 million loss (-$1.28 per share) in Q1 2025. Adjusted net loss was $8 million (-$0.16 per share), unchanged year-over-year. National's insured portfolio declined to $21.5 billion, with gross par to statutory capital improving from 24 to 23 to 1. Book value per share fell to -$44.82. No substantive progress on PREPA resolution, with litigation over the Oversight Board stalling negotiations. Management noted no updates on strategic alternatives and limited near-term debt buyback opportunities.

1stDibs reported Q1 FY2026 GMV of $89.7M (down 5%) and revenue of $22.4M (down 1%), both in line with expectations, with adjusted EBITDA of $0.6M (about 2.5% margin) above the midpoint of guidance and gross margin of roughly 74%, up 2 points and at the high end of the 72%-74% range. Full-year 2026 framework is unchanged: third consecutive year of revenue growth, return to GMV growth by Q4, positive adjusted EBITDA, and positive free cash flow. Q2 guidance calls for GMV of $86M-$91M (down 4% to up 1%), revenue of $21.6M-$22.6M (down 2% to up 2%), and adjusted EBITDA margin of -2% to +2%. Active buyers fell 10% to about 58,300 and order volume dropped 12% as a deliberate near-50% cut to performance marketing in Q4 2025 weighed on traffic, partially offset by a tenth consecutive quarter of conversion growth and AOV up 7% to about $2,750.

negative_highlights: Net loss of $119 million driven by non-cash charges and non-recurring items
Production down 2% YoY due to waterflood timing and Simonette disposition
Hedging losses forecast of $70-72 million partially offset higher oil prices
positive_highlights: CapEx came in under plan at $45 million
Completed bond exchange and asset disposition, strengthening balance sheet
New strategic partnerships including Azerbaijan and Ecopetrol Tisquirama block
summary: Gran Tierra reported Q1 2026 results with net loss of $119 million, primarily due to non-cash charges and non-recurring items, while adjusted EBITDA was $74 million and funds from operations were $43 million. Production averaged 45,500 BOE/d, down 2% YoY. CapEx was $45 million, below plan, and the company exited with $125 million cash and net debt of $481 million. Management revised 2026 guidance: production 40,000-45,000 BOE/d, EBITDA $345-395 million, free cash flow $95-115 million, capex $130-170 million, reflecting new partnerships and hedging losses.

negative_highlights: System capital sales declined significantly by roughly $1.8 million due to lower placement activity following the merger termination.
Adjusted EBITDA turned negative at -$311,000 compared to positive cash flow in Q1 FY2025.
Gross margin contracted from 50% to approximately 48%, reflecting higher production costs and tariffs that management chose not to pass on.
positive_highlights: Recurring revenue grew by $1.1 million (9%) driven by continued growth in global procedure volumes despite lower placements.
The ALLY installed base reached approximately 205 systems with another 11 on backlog, demonstrating strong adoption of the next-generation platform.
Procedure volume increased to approximately 54,000 procedures from about 52 last year and 39,000 in Q1 2024.
summary: Total revenue was $13.4 million in Q1 FY2026, down approximately 5% year-over-year to $14.2 million due primarily to lower system capital sales of roughly $1.8 million compared to the prior period. Recurring revenue remained a bright spot at $12.6 million (94% of total), up 9%, while adjusted EBITDA was negative $311,000 versus positive $165,000 last year due to lower placements and lack of OUS activity during the quarter. Management provided no forward guidance for revenue or earnings as they focus on rebuilding momentum post-merger termination.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA margin contracted to roughly 8.4% from the prior year's 9.5% due to deliberate increases in marketing spend.
Customer acquisition costs rose significantly to $3,400 per case compared to $3,130 in the prior quarter.
positive_highlights: Revenue stabilized with positive same-store sales growth of 1% excluding London, marking a key turning point after two years of decline.
Gross margin expanded to roughly 60%, driven by higher case volume and cost discipline despite increased SG&A investments.
Balance sheet strengthened significantly with cash at $16.7 million and leverage reduced below 2.5x.
summary: AirSculpt reported Q1 FY2026 revenue of $39.4 million, which was flat year-over-year but up 1% on a same-store basis excluding London. Adjusted EBITDA decreased to roughly 8.4% of revenue from 9.5% in the prior year due to increased marketing investments and higher customer acquisition costs ($3,400 vs $3,130). Management reaffirmed full-year 2026 guidance for revenue between $151 million-$157 million but explicitly stated no new center openings (de novos) are contemplated in the current year.

negative_highlights: Scripps Networks revenue down 10% in Q2 guidance citing macroeconomic pressure on direct response
Nielsen methodology change negatively impacted audience delivery for over-the-air networks, reducing impressions
GAAP EPS loss of $0.20 includes a $30 million gain from asset sales and preferred dividend impact
positive_highlights: Local media core advertising grew industry-leading 7% YoY driven by NHL partnerships and political spending
Scripps Sports Network launched successfully on major streaming platforms (Roku, LG, Samsung)
Net leverage improved to 3.9x ahead of schedule due to asset sales and transformation cost recognition
summary: Local media revenue grew 5.8% YoY to $331 million driven by sports and political advertising, while Scripps Networks revenue declined 9.5% YoY to $174 million due to macro softness and Nielsen methodology impacts. The company reported a GAAP loss of $0.20 per share but raised its EBITDA improvement plan run rate to $75 million annually by Q3/Q4, with full-year net distribution revenue guidance revised slightly upward despite the Comcast impasse.

negative_highlights: Operating expenses rose $11.2 million due to volume and variable comp
Management notes dynamic component costs as a potential headwind
Consumer confidence is down and consumer remains cautious
positive_highlights: Second-quarter revenue grew 15.5% with all segments contributing
Gross margin improved 3.8 points to 38.8% on cost savings and absorption
Fishing demand strong with XPLORE, MEGA Live 2, and Minn Kota line
summary: Johnson Outdoors reported 15.5% revenue growth in the fiscal Q2, with all segments contributing and operating income much improved. Gross margin expanded 3.8 points to 38.8%, driven by volume absorption and cost savings. Year-to-date sales are up 21.5%, and management remains optimistic but cautious about the upcoming season. No formal guidance was provided.

Orion reported Q1 FY2026 revenue of $36.3 million versus $38.0 million a year ago, with net loss of $0.24 per share (worse than $0.17 prior) but Core FFO of $0.21 per share versus $0.19, aided by a one-time $1.9 million East Syracuse lease termination payment. Full-year 2026 Core FFO guidance of $0.69-$0.76 was affirmed, not raised, and CFO Gavin Brandon said no meaningful lease termination income is expected for the remainder of the year. Occupancy rose to 83.1% from 73.7% a year ago on 355,000 sq ft of Q1 leasing, a 172,000 sq ft 12-year Irving, Texas full-building lease, and continued non-core dispositions, but revenue fell, the GAAP loss widened, and CapEx jumped to $18.7 million from $8.3 million. Management gave no specifics on the ongoing strategic options review, and a joint venture investment has been written down to zero with a full loan-loss reserve.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA of $93 million missed previously provided guidance of ~$100 million due to higher-than-anticipated non-cash marketing expenses and lower March advertising revenues.
Multiplatform Group revenue grew only +4.3% YoY, falling slightly below the midpoint of management's mid-single digit guidance range.
Free cash flow was negative $114 million in Q1 compared to -$81 million last year, driven by a ~$40 million increase in interest expense following debt refinancing.
positive_highlights: Consolidated revenue grew 9.6% YoY and Digital Audio Group outperformed guidance with +18% growth driven by a 26.9% increase in podcasting revenues to $147 million.
Management announced a new cost reduction initiative targeting an additional $50 million of annualized savings beginning in H2 FY2026, on top of previously announced measures.
Tax code changes are expected to effectively eliminate cash taxes for the next few years, preserving approximately $150-$200 million in free cash flow over 2026-2028.
summary: Consolidated revenue of $884 million beat consensus expectations and came in line with guidance at +9.6% YoY, while Adjusted EBITDA of $93 million missed the prior guidance range by approximately $7 million due to timing differences in non-cash marketing expenses and March softness linked to macro uncertainty. Management reaffirmed full-year 2026 Adjusted EBITDA guidance at $800 million despite Q1 misses, citing a new cost reduction initiative expected to generate an additional $50 million of annualized savings starting in the second half of the year.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined to $20.4 million from $31.8 million in Q1 2025.
Adjusted EBITDA fell to $1.7 million from $9.7 million, and the company swung to a $2.7 million net loss from $4 million of net income a year ago.
Over $1 million of severance and professional fee costs were incurred in Q1, and no specific revenue or EPS guidance was provided for the remainder of 2026.
positive_highlights: Cash balance increased approximately $1 million to $11.2 million as of March 31, 2026, from $10.3 million at December 31, 2025.
Licensed badging business grew 72% year over year and Men's Journal Spirit shop average weekly sales rose 165% in Q1 versus Q4 2025.
ShopHQ orders rose 14% in Q1 over Q4 2025, adding 40 partners and 44 brands, with a TikTok Shop launch planned for Q2.
summary: Q1 2026 revenue fell to $20.4 million from $31.8 million a year ago, with a net loss of $2.7 million versus $4 million of net income in Q1 2025 and adjusted EBITDA of $1.7 million versus $9.7 million. Management attributed the decline to referral traffic changes and deliberate monetization/audience testing estimated to have cost millions in revenue, and said monetization returned to parity in late March. Cash rose about $1 million to $11.2 million, licensing badging grew 72% year over year and ShopHQ orders rose 14% sequentially, while no explicit full-year revenue or EPS guidance was given beyond an expectation of sequential yield improvement and stronger remaining quarters.

negative_highlights: Cash flow from operations was negative $16.8 million due to a one-time payment of CAD 16.4M ($12.1M) for Canadian corporate income taxes.
Netherlands phase II facility in Groningen faces a delay, with full operations expected only after regulatory approval anticipated by May rather than late March.
positive_highlights: International export sales increased 171% year-over-year and 60% sequentially, reaching a record $15 million net of slipped orders.
Consolidated adjusted EBITDA grew 118%, significantly outpacing revenue growth to achieve an expanded margin profile.
Company achieved its first harvest from the Delta 2 expansion in Canada with initial sales expected by late Q2.
summary: Village Farms reported Q1 FY26 net sales of $50.2 million, a 27% year-over-year increase driven by international exports up 171%. Adjusted EBITDA surged to $9.9 million (up 118%), resulting in positive net income for the fourth consecutive quarter despite negative cash flow from operations due to Canadian tax payments of CAD 16.4 million ($12.1M). Management raised no specific full-year guidance but reiterated a clear line of sight to profitable growth as new capacity ramps up.

negative_highlights: Gross margin fell to 69% from the typical low-to-mid 70% range on secondary CINVANTI supplier costs
Adjusted EBITDA was -$727,000 for the quarter
Surgical volumes declined roughly high single digits sequentially, exceeding prior-year seasonal softness
positive_highlights: March net revenues returned to over $15 million after a difficult January and February
APONVIE demand units grew 68% YoY with 371 ordering accounts in March, an all-time high
Ignite 2.0 expanded targeted accounts 38% to 3,109 for full-year 2026, versus 2,261 in Ignite 1.0
summary: Q1 2026 net revenue came in at $34.7 million with gross margin of 69%, below the typical low-to-mid 70% range, and adjusted EBITDA of -$727,000; management said results were modestly below plan. Full-year 2026 guidance was reaffirmed at $173-183 million in net product sales and $10-20 million in adjusted EBITDA, with no raise. Acute care products grew year-over-year (ZYNRELEF demand +22%, APONVIE +68%) and March net sales rebounded above $15 million, but weather-driven surgical volume declines of roughly high single digits and temporary secondary-supplier margin pressure weighed on the quarter.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA margin was only ~0.2%, and SG&A of $22.7 million was 24% of revenue, leaving the company just barely profitable on an adjusted basis

Fuel costs moved significantly higher; pass-through is limited to contracted programs, while wholesale absorbs fuel as a more direct cost input
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA swung to positive ~$0.2 million from a $6.4 million loss, a $6.6 million YoY improvement
Gross margin expanded ~700 bps to 20% and contribution margin rose ~360 bps to 50.5%
Dispatch availability improved ~760 bps YoY, worth roughly $2.5 million of annual contribution per point; utilization rose 15% to 75 hours per aircraft per month
summary: flyExclusive reported Q1 FY2026 revenue of ~$96.3 million, up ~9% YoY, with gross margin expanding ~700 bps to 20% and contribution margin up ~360 bps to 50.5%. Adjusted EBITDA turned positive at ~$0.2 million versus a $6.4 million loss in Q1 2025, a $6.6 million YoY improvement, and long-term debt was cut by ~$10 million. Management gave no formal full-year guidance but stated every 2026 quarter should outperform the corresponding 2025 quarter on revenue, adjusted EBITDA, and flight hours, and guided Q2 to ~15% sequential top-line growth. Operating losses from legacy non-performing aircraft fell from over $3 million per month to under $250,000.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA fell 17.5% YoY to $7.751 million from $9.398 million
Adjusted net income declined 22.4% YoY to $5.337 million from $6.881 million
Nine-month adjusted net income down 29.8% to $17.881 million and adjusted EBITDA down 14.7%, with international ocean volumes weak and no quantitative guidance provided
positive_highlights: GAAP net income rose 83.8% YoY to $4.671 million, or $0.10 per diluted share versus $0.05
Domestic truckload and intermodal renewal rates running high single-digits with spot rates, tender rejections and cycle indicators moving higher
Net-debt-free balance sheet relative to the $200 million credit facility, supporting tuck-in acquisitions (including recent NVOCC purchases) and buybacks
summary: Radiant reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $214.1 million, essentially flat versus $214.0 million a year earlier, while GAAP net income rose 83.8% to $4.671 million ($0.10 per diluted share) from $2.541 million ($0.05). However, adjusted net income fell 22.4% to $5.337 million and adjusted EBITDA declined 17.5% to $7.751 million from $9.398 million, with nine-month adjusted EBITDA down 14.7% to $26.322 million. Management gave no quantitative guidance, citing a seasonally slow quarter, tariff/trade and Middle East shipping disruptions hitting international volumes, and early signs of a supply-driven domestic truckload/intermodal recovery expected to benefit future quarters.

Q1 FY2026 revenue fell to $73.3M from $85.4M a year earlier and adjusted EBITDA dropped to $16.7M from $20.1M, a $3.4M decline driven by realized RIN prices falling $0.30 to $2.41 (~$4M EBITDA impact), partly offset by RNG production up 9% to 1.2 million MMBtu. Fuel Station Services EBITDA fell to $9.2M from $10.9M on lower construction revenue and maintenance timing. Management reiterated full-year 2026 guidance, citing weather-driven OpEx pressure in a seasonally soft Q1 and easier comps ahead, with firming D3 RINs above $2.50 and construction of Cottonwood, Burlington, and CMS projects progressing for late 2026/early 2027. Liquidity was ~$233M after $288M of financing transactions, including a $180M preferred facility and $100M 45Z tax credit monetization.

negative_highlights: Merchant Solutions gross margins contracted due to higher-than-normal credit losses and a mix shift from acquisitions.
Payables segment margin declined 210 bps YoY primarily due to revenue mix shifts toward lower-margin buyer-funded revenues.
Operating expenses increased 27.4% in Merchant Solutions driven by cloud/software costs, non-recurring legal fees, and acquisition-related headcount.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 11% YoY to $249.6M driven by 35.6% growth in the high-margin Payables segment.
Adjusted gross profit margin expanded 70 bps to 39.6%, with recurring revenue margins reaching over 63%. Adjusted EBITDA grew 13% YoY to $58.1M.
Total customer accounts increased by 50,000 to reach 1.8 million on the commerce platform.
summary: Priority Technology Holdings reported Q1 FY2026 revenue of $249.6 million (up 11% YoY) and adjusted EPS growth of 27%. Management maintained its full-year guidance for revenue between $1.01 billion-$1.04 billion and adjusted EBITDA between $230 million-$245 million, citing strong organic momentum in Payables (+35.6%) and Treasury Solutions segments.

negative_highlights: Total revenue declined 3.7% YoY to $723 million, with Commercial revenue down 10.2%
Transportation Adjusted EBITDA was negative $4 million on post-implementation expense at one contract
Adjusted free cash flow was negative $15 million in the quarter

Qualified ACV pipeline of $3.5 billion, up 10% YoY, with Government pipeline up 27%
summary: Revenue fell 3.7% YoY to $723 million, with Commercial down 10.2% to $361 million on volume declines at one large client (about 36% of the drop) and lost business, partly offset by Government up 4.6% to $226 million and Transportation up 2.3% to $136 million. Adjusted EBITDA rose to $49 million with margin up 190 bps to 6.8%, though discrete items added about 64 bps, and adjusted free cash flow was negative $15 million versus a $50 million operating cash flow improvement YoY. 2026 guidance is $2.8-2.9 billion revenue and $160-190 million adjusted EBITDA, with 2027 revenue flat to positive and EBITDA of $190-220 million. New business ACV was $114 million, up 5% YoY and a sixth straight quarter of growth, and management targets over $200 million from 2026 divestitures plus $100 million of cost cuts over 18 months.

negative_highlights: Adjusted distributable earnings flat YoY at BRL 62.2 million as realized financial income fell 35% and PRE dropped to BRL 2 million
Advisory fees fell 35% YoY to BRL 16 million, with management citing a slow second-quarter pipeline and high Selic and election uncertainty
Normalized effective tax rate guided up to ~21-22% from a prior 17-18% due to Verde's real tax regime
positive_highlights: Record quarterly FRE of BRL 96.3 million, up 47% YoY and 42% on a per-share basis
FRE margin expanded to 35.4%, driven by Verde's full-quarter contribution and operating leverage
AUM reached BRL 347 billion, up 22% YoY ex-FX and 2% QoQ, with BRL 7 billion of capital formation in the quarter
summary: Vinci Compass reported record Fee Related Earnings of BRL 96.3 million (BRL 1.47/share), up 47% YoY, on fee-related revenues of BRL 272 million (+17% YoY) with management fees of BRL 245 million (+25% YoY). FRE margin expanded to 35.4%, helped by a full quarter of Verde consolidation and operating leverage, though management flagged first-quarter seasonal cost benefits. Adjusted distributable earnings of BRL 62.2 million (BRL 0.95/share) were flat YoY as lower realized financial income, PRE of BRL 2 million, and IRE of BRL 4 million offset the FRE record. AUM reached BRL 347 billion (22% YoY ex-FX growth) and a ~BRL 100 million after-tax Galeão indemnification is expected to benefit distributable earnings in Q3/Q4 2026; a quarterly dividend of $0.17 per share was declared.

negative_highlights: Full-year revenue and adjusted EBITDA guidance was reaffirmed rather than raised despite the large Q1 beat
Xacta software contribution was approximately flat year-over-year
Q2 guidance implies a sharp sequential deceleration with revenue of $44-46 million and adjusted EBITDA margin of 11.4-13%
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 56% year-over-year to $47.7 million, exceeding the $44-45 million guidance range
Adjusted EBITDA of $7.9 million (16.5% margin) beat the $4.5-5 million guidance and rose from 1.2% margin a year earlier
Free cash flow of $6.4 million (13.4% margin) marked the fifth consecutive quarter above 12%
summary: Telos reported Q1 FY2026 revenue of $47.7 million, up 56% year-over-year and above its $44-45 million guidance range. Adjusted EBITDA reached $7.9 million (16.5% margin) versus guidance of $4.5-5 million, while free cash flow was $6.4 million (13.4% margin), the fifth consecutive quarter above 12%. Q2 guidance implies revenue of $44-46 million (22-28% growth) and adjusted EBITDA of $5-6 million, but the full-year revenue and adjusted EBITDA outlook was reaffirmed despite the Q1 beat, with only the low end of the full-year cash gross margin assumption raised. The company repurchased $2.2 million of stock in Q1 and intends to accelerate buybacks in Q2.

negative_highlights: Q1 net sales declined quarter-over-quarter from $12.4M due to severe weather causing patients to miss treatment cycles
Full-year 2026 revenue guidance is deferred until the August earnings call rather than being provided today
Existing patient growth was negatively impacted by winter storms affecting roughly two-thirds of the country
positive_highlights: LOQTORZI new patient starts reached an all-time high driven by broader prescribing and deeper use
R&D expenses decreased year-over-year from $24.4M to $21.5M due to headcount savings
Tagmokitug clinical programs are tracking to plan with accrual progressing well in HCC, Head & Neck, and GI cohorts
summary: Coherus Oncology reported Q1 FY2026 net sales of $11.8 million for LOQTORZI, a decline from the prior quarter due to severe weather impacting existing patient cycles and seasonal trends, though new starts reached an all-time high. Management reiterated revenue guidance targets but noted that full-year 2026 guidance will be provided in August rather than today. The company raised $54 million via a follow-on equity offering to fund clinical trials.

negative_highlights: Total net revenue fell to $1.0 million from $2.9 million sequentially and $3.9 million YoY; mmWave revenue dropped to $0.6 million from $2.4 million
Q2 guidance of approximately $1.2 million implies continued depressed revenue, with visibility described as below desired levels
GAAP net loss widened to $2.5 million and adjusted EBITDA fell to -$2.3 million from -$1.1 million, while cash declined to $2.7 million with the strategic review still unresolved
positive_highlights: Gross margin expanded to 61.5% from 52.2% in the prior quarter on a higher NRE revenue mix
New design wins disclosed: MikroTik's 60 GHz nRAY product launch and InTACT as a defense contractor customer, with initial limited production modules shipped mid-April
Non-GAAP opex held near $3 million per quarter on prior cost reductions
summary: Peraso reported Q1 FY2026 total net revenue of $1.0 million versus $2.9 million in the prior quarter and $3.9 million a year ago, with mmWave product revenue of $0.6 million, down from $2.4 million sequentially and $1.5 million YoY. GAAP net loss widened to $2.5 million (-$0.22 per share) from $1.2 million in Q4 and non-GAAP adjusted EBITDA deteriorated to -$2.3 million from -$1.1 million. Gross margin rose sequentially to 61.5% from 52.2% on higher NRE mix but CFO guided Q2 margins back into the 50s. Q2 revenue guidance is approximately $1.2 million, citing lumpy orders and customer memory-chip shortages, while the strategic review remains ongoing with no update.

negative_highlights: Total revenue down 5% YoY and subscription revenue down 4% YoY
Media & Telecom segment revenue down 17% YoY
GAAP net loss widened to $3.8M from $1.1M YoY
positive_highlights: Revenue and adjusted EBITDA exceeded high end of guidance
Adjusted EBITDA up 37% YoY and positive first-quarter operating cash flow achieved
Gross retention improved to highest level in last 5 quarters
summary: Kaltura reported Q1 FY2026 revenue of $44.6M, down 5% YoY but above the high end of guidance ($42.6M-$43.4M), with subscription revenue of $43.2M, down 4% YoY, also beating guidance. Adjusted EBITDA was $5.7M, up 37% YoY and well above guidance, while the company achieved its first positive operating cash flow in a first quarter. Management raised full-year guidance and noted improving gross retention, but revenue declines persist due to legacy Media & Telecom churn and a large EE&T customer's shift in event timing. They expect new product contributions to begin in H2 2026 and more meaningful impact in 2027.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined 6.8% due to the exit from a large commercial payer, though organic growth would have been ~1%
Home respiratory category fell about 4% excluding payer impact
Diabetes revenue was flat as insulin pump growth did not offset drops in CGMs
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA of $58 million met management expectations
Sleep Journey program delivering anticipated results with strong YoY growth in sleep supplies excluding payer impact
Completed balance sheet optimization transaction to extend debt maturities and reduce near-term pressure
summary: Accendra Health reported Q1 FY2026 revenue decline of 6.8% YoY and adjusted EBITDA of $58 million in line with expectations, driven by the exit from a large commercial payer which reduced growth to approximately -7%. Management affirmed its full-year outlook for both revenue and adjusted EBITDA despite higher interest expenses expected post-financing restructuring.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined to $6.7 million from $8.2 million a year ago on a $2 million drop in DSP customer spending
Net loss was $5.6 million and cash and cash equivalents stood at only $800,000
No forward financial guidance was provided for revenue, margins, or adjusted EBITDA despite the June 2026 quarterly call
positive_highlights: Gross margin expanded 500 basis points to 34% from 29% a year ago
Operating expenses decreased 13% to $5.5 million from $6.3 million, and adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed to $2.6 million from $3.0 million
Non-DSP customer spending rose 8% ($500,000) year over year, and the Ignition+ platform launched in March saw initial mid-market enterprise interest
summary: Direct Digital Holdings reported Q1 2026 revenue of $6.7 million, down from $8.2 million a year ago, as demand-side platform customer spending fell $2 million, partly offset by an 8% ($500,000) increase in other customer spending. Gross margin improved to 34% from 29%, operating expenses fell 13% to $5.5 million, and adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed to $2.6 million from $3.0 million, though net loss was $5.6 million versus $5.9 million. Management said results were in line with internal expectations and exceeded analyst estimates, but provided no forward financial guidance and instead emphasized the March launch of Ignition+ and potential strategic partnerships or acquisitions. The company ended the quarter with $800,000 in cash and no explicit revenue or EBITDA outlook.

negative_highlights: Organic net sales declined 6% year-over-year, with volume/mix down 11 points, and adjusted EPS swung to a loss of $0.01 from $0.07 income a year ago.

positive_highlights: Free cash flow was $35 million versus an outflow of $2 million a year ago, driven by inventory reduction, improved receivables, and insurance proceeds.
Net debt was reduced by $145 million since the start of the fiscal year to $505 million, aided by the North America Snacks divestiture.
North America adjusted EBITDA margin excluding snacks was 16.4% in the quarter, versus the reported 10%, demonstrating a stronger go-forward margin profile.
summary: Hain reported Q3 FY2026 organic net sales down 6% year-over-year, with adjusted gross margin of 21% (down ~90 bps YoY but up ~150 bps sequentially) and adjusted EBITDA of $26 million versus $34 million a year ago. Adjusted EPS was a loss of $0.01 versus $0.07 income last year. North America organic sales fell 3% while international fell 8%, and the company cited volume softness and private label competition. Management did not provide numeric FY2026 guidance, reiterated positive free cash flow for the year, and said it is actively addressing the December debt maturity, expecting to refinance, extend, or repay prior to maturity.

Strategic review costs may continue into Q3

Management emphasizes cost discipline and organic growth, with expected cost benefits in H2 2026, while strategic review costs may persist into Q3.

Management reaffirmed full-year 2026 revenue guidance of $70-$73M despite Q1 volume being impacted by winter storms.

Paid voting contests are on track to exceed 30,000 contestants in the new model search collaboration with Honey Birdette.

Adjusted EBITDA reached approximately $5 million (up 111%), marking the fifth consecutive quarter of positive adjusted earnings and an improvement over the prior year's net loss of $9 million due to a one-time transaction expense reduction. Management closed the UTG China deal, paid down $15M in debt, and announced plans for five new Honey Birdette stores while launching major media initiatives like the Karol G magazine cover.

GPMP segment gallons decreased as retail sites converted to wholesale dealer locations reduced related-party sales volume.
New fleet cardlock locations are expected to contribute primarily in 2027 rather than the current year.

Wholesale fuel contribution increased 14.2% due to dealerization conversions (totaling 450 sites since mid-2024) and prompt pay discounts.
Net leverage reduced to 2.1x with liquidity of $731 million following the IPO capital raise.
summary: ARKO Petroleum reported Q1 FY2026 adjusted EBITDA of $36.4 million (up 18% YoY) and discretionary cash flow of approximately $25 million. The company maintained its full-year guidance for adjusted EBITDA at ~$156M, citing strong execution despite fuel cost volatility. Management highlighted a net leverage ratio of 2.1x following an IPO debt reduction.

BENEFIT-HF trial ramp is expected to take multiple quarters, with full enrollment potentially taking 4-6 years.

Gross margin expanded significantly to 87%, driven by ASP increases and manufacturing efficiencies.
Transition to Category I CPT codes is underway with a Q1 approval rate of 46% vs 31% in 2024.
summary: CVRX reported Q1 FY2026 revenue of $14.8 million (up 20% YoY) and gross margin expansion to 87%, driven by US growth exceeding the high end of prior guidance. Management reiterated full-year 2026 total revenue guidance between $63M-$67M without raising it, citing a desire not to get ahead of themselves early in the year despite Q1 re-acceleration. The company noted March softness in Medicare Advantage approval rates due to new regulatory automation but expects normalization and maintained that current trends support hitting existing targets.

Political advertising contribution in Q2 is expected to be light
Potential for digital ad volatility is acknowledged, though not currently observed

Adjusted EBITDA rose 81% YoY to $9.8 million, exceeding guidance. CTV spend grew over 40% YoY for the third consecutive year, now over 50% of total ad spend. Management expects accelerating top-line performance through the year, citing strong demand, new flagship customers, the 2026 World Cup, political advertising in H2, and the recent acquisition of TVision for attention-based measurement.

Year-end cash guidance cut to ~$40 million and net debt guidance raised to ~$45 million from prior levels due to the $10 million buyback

Land management and other operations revenue up 113% in the quarter and 97% for six months, with 97% of ~32,500 farmable acres now revenue-generating

Net income was $11.4 million ($1.49 per diluted share) versus a $111.4 million net loss, driven by a $26.9 million January land sale that generated a ~$19.8 million gain, and adjusted EBITDA was $16.9 million versus $12.7 million. Full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance was maintained at approximately $14 million, but year-end cash guidance was lowered to roughly $40 million and net debt raised to approximately $45 million to reflect $10 million of buybacks through April. Non-citrus land management revenue rose 113% in the quarter while Collier County unanimously approved the 1,446-acre Corkscrew Grove East Village entitlement, with state approval targeted for 2027 and federal by end-2028.

summary: Q1 FY2026 revenue was $1.6 million, up 80% YoY from $896,000 and the strongest quarter in company history, with gross margin expanding 200 bps to 86.4% and ASP up 33% to $1,017 on a payer mix shift toward reimbursed procedures. Net loss narrowed 23% to $1.8 million and free cash outflow improved to $1.2 million from $1.6 million, with cash of $7.1 million rising to approximately $8 million after an incremental $2.1 million raise. Management gave no formal revenue guidance but said it expects quarterly burn of $1 million or less for the rest of the year and roughly $15 million in revenue for cash flow break-even, while cautioning that payer coverage expansion will unfold gradually and that Q2 will include a one-time stock compensation charge exceeding $4 million.

Title insurance activity slowed by rising mortgage rates and geopolitical uncertainty
CEO explicitly stated no formal guidance will be provided for the full year or Q2

Banking and lending vertical grew strongly with over 50% of quarterly revenue
summary: Intellicheck reported Q1 FY2026 revenue of $5.5 million (up 13% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $935,000 against a prior year loss of $17k, marking the fourth consecutive quarter of positive adjusted EBITDA. Gross margin expanded to 91% GAAP and 93.4% adjusted, driven by operating leverage despite macro headwinds in retail and title insurance verticals due to geopolitical conflict and high interest rates. Management declined to provide formal guidance but noted potential acceleration in the back half of the year.

negative_highlights: No revenue or earnings reported as operations are suspended pending the commercial offtake agreement for Project Permian Phase I.

positive_highlights: Company ended Q1 with approximately $319 million in cash and no debt, providing sufficient dry powder to fund development milestones.

Management highlighted $319 million in cash on hand, low G&A burn ($8-9M/quarter), and progress on securing long-lead equipment while emphasizing that capital release is contingent on the outcome of the active strategic advisor-led offtake process. The company reiterated a target Total Investment Cost (TIC) range of $475-$575 million for the first project.

summary: Lineage reported Q1 2026 total revenue of approximately $1.7 million versus $1.5 million a year earlier, with operating expenses rising to $9.3 million and a net loss of $4.8 million ($0.02 basic, $0.03 diluted). Cash stood at $53.4 million, expected to fund operations into Q2 2028, plus up to roughly $32 million from warrant exercises and $615 million in potential Roche/Genentech milestones. No revenue or EPS guidance was provided, and OpRegen timing remains undetermined pending partner Genentech's decision on a multi-center controlled trial. The most notable change was pipeline expansion: launch of the wholly owned COR1 corneal endothelial program and progress on the ILT1/AlloSCOPE 5D islet scale-up initiative.

summary: Upexi reported Q3 FY2026 total revenue of $4.6 million, up from $3.2 million in the prior year quarter, but posted a net loss of approximately $109 million ($1.67 per share), driven largely by a $92.3 million unrealized loss on digital assets as Solana fell 33% during the quarter. The company increased its Solana token holdings by 189,000 tokens (9% sequentially) and reduced short-term debt by $7.6 million. Management expects ongoing cash expenses to fall below staking revenue by July 1, 2026, and reiterated confidence in Solana's long-term fundamentals despite near-term price weakness.

negative_highlights: Operating loss of $21.1 million and net loss of $20.7 million in the quarter, with no revenue and no commercial product
No new efficacy or safety data this quarter; the sole near-term catalyst (ALTITUDE-ad) is still blinded and roughly two quarters away
Management flagged external skepticism on the anti-amyloid class (Cochrane report, slower-than-expected uptake of approved antibodies) without providing data to rebut it
positive_highlights: Cash and marketable securities of $128.4 million after a $35.75 million gross private placement, expected to fund operations into early 2027
Q1 R&D fell to $16.5 million and G&A to $4.7 million, both down year-over-year on lower manufacturing, CRO, legal and insurance costs
ALTITUDE-ad top-line readout remains on track for late 2026, with high conversion into the 12-month open-label extension and a planned Q2 2026 option exercise on two JCR EBD compounds
summary: A clinical-stage biotech with no product revenue; Q1 FY2026 R&D was $16.5 million, G&A $4.7 million, operating loss $21.1 million and net loss $20.7 million, with $128.4 million in cash and securities after a $35.75 million gross private placement, funding operations into early 2027. The sole value driver, the phase II ALTITUDE-ad readout, remains on track for late 2026, with high open-label extension conversion and a planned Q2 2026 option exercise on two JCR EBD compounds and an IND targeted mid-2027. Management addressed skepticism on the anti-amyloid class (Cochrane report, slow commercial uptake) by pointing to the oligomer-targeted, IgG2 differentiation thesis, but offered no new efficacy data. Versus the prior quarter, the key change was the $35.75 million private placement extending the cash runway and imminent EBD candidate selection.

positive_highlights: 19% revenue growth, above expectations, despite weather shutdown
