positive_highlights: Non-GAAP net loss narrowed 81% to $1.6M from $8.5M, and non-GAAP net loss per diluted share fell to $0.07 from $0.40
Subscription gross margin expanded 400 bps to 90%, with platform costs down $300K year-over-year
Rollout discussions expanded to 15 North American retailers, including 8 of the 20 largest, from 8 and 4 two months ago
summary: Q1 FY2026 revenue fell to $7.6M from $9.4M a year ago, with subscription revenue down $900K to $4.4M and service revenue down $800K to $3.2M. Ending ARR was $15M versus $20M a year ago, as the previously disclosed loss of two contracts removed $6.8M of ARR; excluding those, ARR grew $1.8M YoY and 9% sequentially. Non-GAAP net loss improved 81% to $1.6M ($0.07 per diluted share versus $0.40) on operating expense cuts, and subscription gross margin rose 400 bps to 90%. Management still expects significant ARR growth in 2026 but said gift cards will no longer be the largest contributor due to a scanner-vendor firmware delay that pushed one retailer's full ~600-store rollout to January 2027.

negative_highlights: Phase III data readouts still pending; no efficacy results disclosed yet
AT-587 is still in preclinical phase with first-in-human study not yet initiated
Commercial launch dependent on regulatory approval and Phase III success
positive_highlights: Cash position of $256 million extends runway through 2027
C-BEYOND fully enrolled and C-FORWARD 95% enrolled ahead of mid-year completion
Payer research shows favorable outlook for formulary inclusion across segments
summary: Atea Pharmaceuticals reported Q1 FY2026 with cash and marketable securities of $256 million, sufficient to fund operations through 2027. The company is advancing its global Phase III hepatitis C program, with C-BEYOND fully enrolled and top-line data expected mid-year, and C-FORWARD 95% enrolled with completion and top-line data expected around year-end. Additional progress includes preparation for first-in-human studies of AT-587 for hepatitis E and commercial launch readiness activities.

negative_highlights: Q1 revenue growth of only 2% was muted by note weakness in-term channel disruption from the transition to direct Amazon management.
Operating expenses included approximately $443,000 in one-time costs related to organizational transition and legal matters.
positive_highlights: Direct-to-consumer revenue increased 42% to a record $194,000 despite Amazon transition disruption.
Gross margin improved to a company record of 68.6%, up from 64.5% in the prior year period.
Subscription revenue grew 44% to $56,000 with subscriber counts increasing more than 50%.
summary: SenesTech reported Q1 FY2026 revenue of $493,000, a 2% increase year-over-year to $485,000, driven by strong growth in direct-to-consumer and B2B channels. Gross margin expanded to a record 68.6% from 64.5%, reflecting improved production efficiency and reduced reliance on discounts. Management highlighted record subscription revenue of $56,000 (up 44%) and noted that April post-transition e-commerce sales surged 163% year-over-year.

negative_highlights: The company remains in a net loss position with Q1 net loss of $8.6 million.
IDN sales cycles are described as longer and more involved than single-site hospital processes.
positive_highlights: Revenue surged 83% YoY to $3.9M, marking the second-highest quarter ever.
Gross margin expanded approximately 940 bps to 50.7%, exceeding 50% for the third consecutive quarter.
Net cash burn improved by 13% to $8.8M, with a strong balance sheet of $40.8M in cash.
summary: Hyperfine reported Q1 FY2026 revenue of $3.9 million, an 83% year-over-year increase driven by the sale of 10 units of its next-generation Swoop system. Gross margin expanded significantly to 50.7%, and net cash burn decreased to $8.8 million from $10.1 million in the prior year quarter. Management reiterated full-year 2026 guidance for revenue between $20 million-$22 million and gross margins of 50%-55%.

negative_highlights: Compensation and benefits rose to 67.2% of revenue from 60.2% a year ago, and total expenses increased 13.5% ($3.6 million) against flat revenue
Discretionary AUM fell 3.7% sequentially to $23.1 billion on net institutional outflows tied to performance concerns and fully funded pension plans
Cash fell to $11.6 million from $44.1 million at year-end with $10 million of borrowings, and management signaled a likely pause in buybacks
positive_highlights: Organic new client flows were $81 million in Q1, primarily from high net worth investors
Year-over-year discretionary AUM grew nearly 2%, from $22.7 billion to $23.1 billion, and total AUM rose 1.1% to $35.7 billion
Completed the previously announced $25 million repurchase plan with $1.9 million bought in Q1, alongside a maintained $0.21 quarterly dividend
summary: Revenue was essentially flat year-over-year at $31.4 million while expenses rose 13.5% to $3.6 million higher, driven by a compensation ratio that jumped to 67.2% from 60.2% a year ago. Reported net income was $0.5 million ($0.03 per Class A share) and adjusted EBITDA fell to $3.7 million or 11.8% of revenue, with adjusted diluted EPS of $0.12. Discretionary AUM declined 3.7% to $23.1 billion on net institutional outflows, partially offset by $81 million of organic new client flows and 1.1% year-over-year total AUM growth to $35.7 billion. Management gave no quantitative guidance, said the elevated compensation ratio will persist as investment matures, described a pipeline 'in the billions' but declined to forecast timing, and signaled a likely 'slight pause' in capital returns after completing the $25 million buyback plan.

negative_highlights: Operating expenses increased to $6M from $4.1M
Cash and restricted cash only $2.2M
Net loss of approximately $4.3M
positive_highlights: Revenue increased 26% year-over-year
Gross margin improved to 70.1%, up 14%
Pediatrics now represents approximately 50% of total U.S. revenue
summary: Q1 FY2026 revenue was $2.4M, up 26% YoY, with gross margin improving to 70.1% from 56.1% (14% increase). Operating expenses rose to ~$6M from $4.1M due to higher sales headcount, and net loss was ~$4.3M. Cash and restricted cash stood at $2.2M with no debt. The company completed the acquisition of Rendiatech, plans a cash burn reduction of ~50% by Q4 2026, and will launch a new product in 2027.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened significantly to $18.9 million from $5.2 million in the prior year quarter due to increased R&D and G&A expenses.
No specific financial guidance (revenue or EPS) was provided for the full year, as the company is pre-revenue.
positive_highlights: FDA confirmed C-peptide as a potential surrogate endpoint for accelerated approval, de-risking the regulatory path.
Part A of the SAFEGUARD trial completed enrollment with 12 adult patients; Part B is actively enrolling 147 pediatric and adolescent patients.
Multi-year manufacturing agreement executed with Emergent BioSolutions to support commercial launch.
summary: SAB BIO reported a net loss of $18.9 million for Q1 FY2026, an increase from $5.2 million in the prior year quarter, driven by R&D expenses of $13.4 million and G&A of $6.6 million. The company ended the quarter with $217.6 million in cash, providing a runway through 2028. Key operational highlights included the completion of enrollment for Part A of the SAFEGUARD trial and FDA written confirmation that C-peptide may serve as a surrogate endpoint for accelerated approval.

negative_highlights: Product gross margin contracted 180 bps to 53.8% in Q2 and 390 bps to 54.0% for the first half
Cash and cash equivalents fell to $2.8 million from $6.6 million at September 30, 2025, with working capital down to $5.7 million from $7.9 million
First-half net loss widened to $3.5 million versus $0.5 million a year ago, reflecting the absence of the $3 million Zimmer Biomet license revenue recognized in Q1 FY2025
positive_highlights: Q2 product revenue rose 72% YoY to $2.4 million from $1.4 million, driven by higher OneRF sales
16 Trigeminal Nerve ablation cases completed to date with all patients reportedly pain-free
Stage 2 ISO 13485 audit completed for the Minnesota facility, targeting certification in the latter part of 2026 to enable international distribution
summary: NeuroOne reported Q2 FY2026 product revenue of $2.4 million, up 72% year over year though the year-ago quarter also carried a $3 million license revenue item that is absent this year, making first-half product revenue $5.3 million (+13% YoY) and net loss $3.5 million for the six months versus a $0.5 million loss in the prior-year period. Product gross margin contracted 180 bps to 53.8% in the quarter and 390 bps to 54.0% for the first half, while operating expenses were flat and cash fell to $2.8 million from $6.6 million at September 30, 2025. Management reaffirmed the full-year product revenue guidance of approximately $10.5 million, which excludes contributions from drug delivery and facial pain, and flagged international distribution as a later-2026 catalyst pending ISO 13485 certification. The quarter also included a CFO transition (Chris Volker replacing Ron McClurg effective July 1, 2026) and a 1-for-6 reverse split to regain Nasdaq compliance.

negative_highlights: Adjusted revenue fell 18% YoY due to a 29% decline in marketplace trading volume
Net loss of JPY 1.2 billion ($7.6 million) caused by severance expenses, professional fees, and software impairment costs
Customer assets decreased primarily due to the decline in market prices for crypto holdings
positive_highlights: Total revenue grew 4% YoY to JPY 119.7 billion driven by institutional demand
Verified accounts increased 10% to 2.5 million despite market headwinds
Strategic partnerships announced with KDDI (telecom giant) and Scotiabank subsidiary Dynamic Funds
summary: Total revenue increased 4% to JPY 119.7 billion ($752 million) in Q4 FY2026, driven by institutional and counterparty transactions, while adjusted revenue decreased 18% due to lower marketplace trading volume. The company reported a net loss of JPY 1.2 billion ($7.6 million), down from the prior year's profit but better than fiscal 2025 losses, with significant SG&A increases including severance and impairment costs offsetting some revenue gains.

negative_highlights: Gross margin fell to 57% in Q1 2026 from 62% in Q1 2025 due to production yield issues
Operating expenses increased to EUR 24.2M from EUR 21.4M a year ago, driven by U.S. commercial investment
positive_highlights: U.S. net revenue rose 25% sequentially to EUR 4.3M in Q1 2026
Worldwide net revenue grew 13% sequentially, avoiding typical Q4-to-Q1 decline
91 active accounts achieved out of 125 targeted, with 241 patients pending prior authorization
summary: Q1 2026 net revenue was EUR 6.4M (EUR 6.7M gross before EUR 0.3M patch deferrals), up 13% sequentially; U.S. net revenue was EUR 4.3M, up 25% sequentially. Gross margin fell to 57% from 62% a year ago on production yield issues, while operating expenses rose to EUR 24.2M from EUR 21.4M. Management guided Q2 U.S. revenue to grow 25%-30% sequentially and full-year 2026 worldwide net revenue to EUR 36M-EUR 40M, with gross margin of 60%-62% and total operating expenses of EUR 97M-EUR 99M. The quarter had no year-ago prior guidance comparison, but U.S. launch KPIs expanded: 91 active accounts of 125 targeted and 241 patients pending prior authorization.

negative_highlights: Hardware gross margin fell to 33.1% from 39.5% due to promotions on new PIN-on-glass devices in Europe
Free cash flow was negative $6 million in the quarter, versus positive operating cash flow of $3.6 million
Operating profit was $4 million, but financial expenses rose $2.9 million from new bond interest, leaving net income at just $1.3 million
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 32% to approximately $107 million, with 26% organic growth
Processing margin expanded to nearly 40% from 36% a year earlier, aided by acquirer contract renegotiations and smart routing
Adjusted EBITDA rose 43% to $14 million, expanding margin to 13% from 12%
summary: Nayax reported Q1 FY2026 revenue of approximately $107 million, up 32% year-over-year (26% organic), with adjusted EBITDA of $14 million at a 13% margin versus 12% a year earlier. Recurring revenue grew 27% and represented about 74% of total revenue, while hardware revenue rose 46% to roughly $28 million and the installed base surpassed 1.5 million devices. The company reaffirmed full-year 2026 guidance of $510-$520 million in revenue (22%-25% organic growth) and $85-$90 million adjusted EBITDA, with free cash flow conversion of about 40% of adjusted EBITDA. Gross margin was flat year-over-year at 49%, and free cash flow for the quarter was negative $6 million due to infrastructure investment and processing settlement timing.

negative_highlights: MidCon segment underperformed due to lower volumes from two Arkoma pads drilled on the outer edges of dedicated acreage.
Permian segment Adjusted EBITDA was flat relative to Q4, driven by a 7.3% decline in volume throughput including temporary shut-ins.
positive_highlights: Rockies segment generated $26.4 million in Adjusted EBITDA driven by higher crude oil pricing and improved NGL prices starting in March.
summary: Summit Midstream reported Q1 FY2026 Adjusted EBITDA of $54.2 million and Distributable Cash Flow of $26.9 million, which management described as generally in line with expectations despite lower volumes and realized residue gas prices in the Arkoma segment. The company reiterated its full-year 2026 guidance range of $225-$265 million Adjusted EBITDA but noted that current activity levels suggest results will trend toward the midpoint rather than exceeding it, reflecting a cautious outlook on near-term growth acceleration.

negative_highlights: Total advertising revenue was $31.9 million, approximately in line with the prior year rather than showing growth.
National advertising revenue declined by approximately 2% on a pro forma comparable basis due to deal concentration and Winter Olympics impact.
Q2 adjusted OIBDA guidance range lowered significantly from last quarter's expectation of $4-9M to $1-5M.
positive_highlights: Domestic box office attendance reached 83 million, up 15% versus the prior year period.
Platinum inventory demand remained strong with revenue per attendee up over 54% on a calendar-adjusted basis.
Second quarter booked local revenue is already ahead of last year's second quarter.
summary: NCMI reported Q1 FY2026 revenue of $34 million and adjusted OIBDA of negative $10.5 million, both within the previously provided guidance ranges but missing on a comparable basis due to Winter Olympics competition and a fiscal calendar shift. Management noted that while domestic box office attendance grew 15% year-over-year (83 million), national advertising revenue was flat versus the prior year despite strong Platinum inventory performance. The company raised its Q2 FY2026 guidance for adjusted OIBDA from $4-9 million to a range of $1-5 million, citing expected lower attendance levels compared to last year's robust September.

negative_highlights: FDA paused 180-day review clock for follow-up questions on NAUTILUS PMA supplement
GAAP net loss increased to $6.7 million from $6.6 million year-over-year
First-half growth moderation as expected, and IGE still not in guidance
positive_highlights: Revenue growth 20% year-over-year excluding DIXI, above prior commentary
Raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $99-$101 million from $98-$100 million
All-time highs in active prescribers, accounts, and patient pipeline during the quarter
summary: NeuroPace reported Q1 2026 revenue of $22.1 million, excluding DIXI Medical $22.0 million, up 20.1% year-over-year with RNS System revenue of $21.7 million. Non-GAAP operating loss narrowed to $3.3 million from $4.1 million, and adjusted EBITDA loss improved similarly. Management raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $99-$101 million from $98-$100 million, citing improved visibility into service and core RNS revenue; guidance still excludes any IGE contribution. FDA mid-cycle review for NAUTILUS PMA supplement completed with a pause for follow-up questions, but management expects a mid-year determination and is confident in the data.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to $8.4 million (from $4.7M prior year) and adjusted EBITDA loss increased to $7.0 million due to higher SG&A ($18.2M vs $10.5M).
Cash burn occurred in Q1 as the company proactively increased inventory and asset purchases for accelerated growth.
Q3 2026 is expected to be lighter sequentially than Q4, introducing typical seasonal volatility.
positive_highlights: Net revenue surged 65% year-over-year driven by rapid adoption among roughly 1,800 high-volume shoulder specialists.
Gross margin expanded 80 basis points sequentially to 77.7%, supported by improved ASPs and cost reduction programs.
The i135RFX product transitioned from limited user release to full commercial launch following FDA clearance for complex fractures.
summary: Shoulder Innovations reported Q1 FY2026 net revenue of $16.7 million, a 65% year-over-year increase and 16% sequential gain, with gross margin expanding to 77.7%. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance to $65-$68 million (37%-44% growth) from the prior range of $62-$65 million due to strong commercial execution and new product launches.

negative_highlights: Oral small molecule PL7737 deprioritized after management judged it would not meet best-in-class selectivity/dosing goals, pushing the next-generation oral IND to first half of calendar 2027
Total operating expenses rose to $5.5 million from $4.8 million on higher compensation and professional fees
Cash of $10.2 million and a $1.4 million quarterly net loss leave a limited runway funded only through June 30, 2027
positive_highlights: Revenue of $3.9 million versus none in the prior-year quarter, driven by the Altanispac Labs sub-license, cut net loss to $1.4 million from $4.8 million
Once-weekly MC4R peptide program on track for a Q4 calendar 2026 IND submission, with IND-enabling studies already underway
Non-dilutive capital raised: EUR 7.5 million (~$8.8 million) from Boehringer Ingelheim and $3.8 million Altanispac upfront
summary: Palatin reported Q3 FY2026 collaboration and license revenue of $3.9 million versus no revenue in the prior-year period, driven by recognition of the Altanispac Labs sub-license upfront consideration, narrowing the net loss to $1.4 million ($0.37 per share) from $4.8 million ($9.13 per share). Operating expenses rose to $5.5 million from $4.8 million, and cash and equivalents stood at $10.2 million with roughly $2.2 million in expected receivables, funding operations into June 2027. The once-weekly MC4R peptide remains on track for a Q4 calendar 2026 IND submission, while the oral small molecule candidate PL7737 was effectively deprioritized in favor of next-generation compounds now targeted for a first-half calendar 2027 IND, about a year later than before.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined sequentially by roughly 7.8% compared to Q4 FY2025 ($1.02M).
Gross margin contracted from 87% in the prior quarter to 83% due to incremental infrastructure investments.
Management explicitly stated they do not provide guidance for revenue or bookings.
positive_highlights: Bookings reached $1.4M, representing a 12.5% year-over-year increase compared to Q1 FY2025.
Subscription revenue mix improved to 98%, up from 96% in the prior quarter.
Closed three strategic multi-year enterprise deals with approximately $5 million total contract value.
summary: CXAI reported Q1 FY2026 revenue of $950K, a slight decline from the prior quarter's $1.02M due to timing differences in enterprise contract recognition and new deal closures. While GAAP EPS improved slightly to negative $0.08 (from -$0.13), gross margin compressed to 83% as management invested in infrastructure for agentic AI rollout and Google Cloud partnerships. Management explicitly declined to provide forward guidance on revenue or bookings, citing a focus on execution over specific targets.

negative_highlights: Gross margins were lower than the prior-year quarter due to decreased interest income and revenue mix shifts.
Overhead expenses increased slightly compared to the prior year despite sequential declines.
RTP growth is partially cannibalizing PINless Debit volume, though RTP offers superior margin profiles.
positive_highlights: Record quarterly revenues across all business units with Card hitting an all-time high at $9.7 million (+23%).
Output Solutions revenue accelerated sequentially to +19%, driven by a new printer installation and digital mix shift.
Real-Time Payments (RTP) volume surged from 2,000 transactions in January to over 200,000 in April.
summary: Usio reported a record Q1 FY2026 with revenue up 16% YoY to $34 million (implied from growth rates and prior context) driven by strong performance across Card (+23%), ACH/Complementary Services (+25%), and Output Solutions (+19%). The company achieved positive GAAP net income, adjusted EBITDA, and operating cash flow. Management reiterated full-year 2026 guidance of 10%-12% revenue growth.

negative_highlights: Net sales fell 29% to $7.1 million from $10.0 million and gross margin contracted to 10% from 34%
Net loss widened to $6.5 million (-$0.55 per share) from $2.0 million (-$0.27) as SG&A rose to $5.8 million from $3.5 million
Cash used in operations was $5.8 million and cash fell to $4.6 million from $10.4 million at December 31, 2025 against $9.2 million of debt
positive_highlights: Delivery and handling costs fell 31% to $1.1 million and dropped to $2.57 per case from $3.17 per case
Company exited a third-party Amazon fulfillment arrangement that had been generating approximately $1 million of annual losses

Reversed planned discontinuations of Reed's and Virgil's heritage glass bottles and Virgil's Zero Sugar cans, and expanded field coverage from roughly 12 internal sales reps to more than 80 broker professionals
summary: Reed's reported Q1 FY2026 net sales of $7.1 million versus $10.0 million a year ago, with gross margin collapsing to 10% from 34% and gross profit of $0.7 million versus $3.4 million. The net loss widened to $6.5 million (-$0.55 per share) from $2.0 million (-$0.27), EBITDA was -$6.2 million versus -$1.7 million, and SG&A rose to $5.8 million from $3.5 million. Management attributed the shortfall to inventory liquidation and write-offs, misaligned SG&A, missed category review windows, and sales execution issues, and gave no quantified guidance beyond an expectation of sequential improvement in net sales, gross margin, and net loss through Q2 and 2026. Cash fell to $4.6 million from $10.4 million at December 31, 2025 against $9.2 million of debt.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to $4.7 million from $2.7 million due to higher stock-based comp and development costs
SK On terminated its procurement agreement, requiring new contracts with other customers
Capital raise of only $1.2M via ATM against a ~$50M liquidity need highlights financing pressure
positive_highlights: Received FAST-41 federal permitting designation for Coosa, improving coordination across agencies
Qualification line at Kellyton produced over 1 metric ton of CSPG samples with positive customer feedback
Company maintains a multi-year first-mover advantage as the most advanced domestic developer
summary: Westwater Resources reported a net loss of $4.7 million ($0.04/share) in Q1 FY26 compared to a $2.7 million loss last year, driven by increased permitting and development costs at Coosa and Kellyton. The company advanced FAST-41 designation for the Coosa permit but lost an agreement with SK On due to evolving market conditions. Management maintains Phase 1 capital guidance of approximately $245 million and expects initial production within roughly 12 months once financing is secured.

negative_highlights: Realized prices were negatively impacted by winter differentials at Jonah and Barnett which were the worst since ownership began.
Unrealized hedge losses totaled $7.6 million due to a spike in crude oil prices, contributing significantly to the reported net loss of $8.9 million.
Production was heavily impacted by January ice storms causing power outages and equipment damage across assets like Tex Mex and Delhi.
positive_highlights: Production held flat year-over-year at 6,700 BOE per day despite significant weather-related downtime and operational disruptions across the portfolio.
Lease operating expenses improved to $13 million ($21.49/BOE) from $22.32/BOE in the prior quarter driven by reduced ad valorem taxes at Barnett Shale and cessation of CO₂ purchases at Delhi.
The board declared its 51st consecutive quarterly dividend of $0.12 per share, reinforcing confidence in underlying cash generation durability.
summary: Fiscal Q3 FY26 revenue declined 11% year-over-year to $20.2 million due to regional natural gas pricing dislocations and a one-time prior period transportation adjustment of $1.2 million at Delhi, resulting in an Adjusted Net Loss of $2.9 million versus adjusted income the prior year. Management attributes reported weakness largely to temporary headwinds including weather-related production disruptions exceeding 300 net BOE per day across multiple fields and unrealized hedge losses of $7.6 million driven by elevated crude prices, rather than structural issues with assets or costs.

negative_highlights: Product revenue from note goods declined YoY to $7.4 million due to lower purchases by Pfizer and Fiocruz driven by timing and inventory dynamics
R&D expenses increased significantly to $5.4 million as the company prepares for initiation of PRX-115 phase II RELEASE study
positive_highlights: $25 million milestone received from Chiesi following EC approval of every-four-week regimen
Net income turned positive to $18.2 million ($0.23/share) compared to a net loss in the prior year period
Strong balance sheet with $51 million cash and no outstanding debt or warrants
summary: Total revenue was $33.8 million in Q1 FY26, driven by a $25 million milestone from Chiesi following European Commission approval of the every-four-week dosing regimen for Elfabrio; excluding this one-time payment and milestones, product revenues were $7.4 million versus $10 million last year due to lower Pfizer/Fiocruz purchases. The company reaffirmed its full-year 2026 guidance range of approximately $78-$83 million total revenue (inclusive of the milestone) with Elfabrio non-milestone sales expected at $33-$35 million and Elelyso revenues at $20-$23 million, while cash on hand stands at $51 million.

negative_highlights: Total revenue fell to $20.9 million from $32.9 million a year ago, and was down versus $23.9 million on a pro forma basis
Gross margin contracted to 57.3% from 61.5%, with Q-code license revenue terminating at the end of 2025
Net loss of $3.1 million ($0.02/share) and adjusted EBITDA loss of $1.6 million versus positive $3 million a year ago
positive_highlights: Full-year 2026 revenue guidance raised to $101-$105 million, citing the Dilon HEMOBLAST agreement and new product launches
Total indebtedness reduced by $13.3 million in Q1 to $12.2 million, lifting revolver availability from $3.8 million to $11.8 million
Commercial launch of Trivium Shaped and new HEMOBLAST Bellows agreement give entry into an estimated $2 billion global hemostatic market
summary: Xtant reported Q1 2026 revenue of $20.9 million, down from $32.9 million a year ago and $23.9 million on a pro forma basis, with the decline driven primarily by amnio/wound-care headwinds. Gross margin fell to 57.3% from 61.5% due to the termination of Q-code license revenue at the end of 2025, and the company posted a net loss of $3.1 million ($0.02/share) versus roughly break-even a year ago; adjusted EBITDA was a $1.6 million loss versus positive $3 million. Management raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $101-$105 million, citing the Dilon HEMOBLAST distribution agreement and new product launches, while noting the Dilon sales force adds at least $2.5 million in quarterly sales and marketing expense. The quarter reflects a divestiture-altered base plus a pro forma revenue decline against a raised full-year outlook.

negative_highlights: Absolute Q1 revenue of only $101,000, up just slightly from Q4 2025
GAAP net loss widened to $8.3 million ($0.18/share) from $7.3 million ($0.17/share) in Q4 2025
Q1 cash burn rose to $9.2 million from $7.5 million in Q4 2025 and cash plus marketable securities declined to $77.2 million from $86.5 million
positive_highlights: Revenue-generating customer count rose from 16 to 21, with issued quotes and active engagements up nearly 40% quarter-over-quarter
Q1 revenue up almost 60% YoY to $101,000 from $64,000 in Q1 2025
2026 full-year cash burn target reaffirmed at $30-35 million, with cash plus marketable securities of ~$77.2 million and runway stated into 2028
summary: Q1 2026 revenue was $101,000, up almost 60% YoY from $64,000 and up slightly versus Q4 2025, while GAAP operating expenses rose to $8.9 million from $8.3 million and GAAP net loss widened to $8.3 million ($0.18/share) from $7.3 million ($0.17/share) in Q4 2025. Non-GAAP net loss was $6.7 million ($0.15/share), essentially flat sequentially, Q1 cash burn was $9.2 million versus $7.5 million in Q4 2025, and cash plus marketable securities fell to $77.2 million from $86.5 million. Management reaffirmed its 2026 full-year cash burn target of $30-35 million and said it still expects a revenue inflection, with more units in the Q2 pipeline continuing into Q3 and Q4. The key change was a growing commercial pipeline—revenue-generating customers up from 16 to 21 and issued quotes and active engagements up nearly 40% QoQ—against still-tiny absolute revenue.

negative_highlights: Cash and cash equivalents fell to $566,000 from approximately $5.9 million at December 31, 2025, with net cash used in operations of about $8.2 million
Operating expenses rose 41% to $6.6 million, driven by a 148% increase in sales and marketing to $2.1 million and a 24% rise in G&A to $4.3 million, producing a $5.8 million net loss

Gross margin declined sequentially to about 26% from about 30% in Q4 2025 on a mix shift toward lower-margin B2B, and management acknowledges last year's guidance was missed ($20 million targeted versus $16.1 million actual)
positive_highlights: Revenue grew approximately 47.9% year-over-year to $3.3 million and gross profit more than doubled (+115.5%) to about $0.9 million
Gross margin expanded to approximately 26% from about 18% in Q1 2025, with B2C margin improving sequentially from roughly 30% to 34%

Commercial milestones: SOLIS and COR began shipping in January, COR secured UL and CSA certifications in April, NEXUS launched in April, and Tri-State Enterprises placed initial purchase orders and reorders
summary: Q1 2026 net sales rose 47.9% year-over-year to $3.3 million, with gross profit up 115.5% to about $0.9 million and gross margin at approximately 26% versus 18% a year ago but down sequentially from roughly 30% in Q4 2025 on B2B mix. However, operating expenses jumped 41% to $6.6 million (sales and marketing up 148% to $2.1 million), net loss was about $5.8 million, operating cash use was approximately $8.2 million, and cash fell to $566,000 from $5.9 million at year-end. Management reaffirmed its 2025-issued 2026 revenue guidance of $35 million-$42 million, announced a shift from quarterly to annual guidance, and said it targets operational cash flow positivity in fiscal 2026, while the company continues to carry a going concern disclosure and raised about $2.2 million via its ATM, issuing 1.46 million shares in Q1. New products SOLIS/COR shipped from January and NEXUS launched commercially in April, with COR receiving UL/CSA certification and Tri-State Enterprises signed as a distributor placing initial orders and reorders.

negative_highlights: Gas transportation auction results were less than requested (received ~400k m3 vs asked for 1.6 million), creating winter supply constraints.
Spot market dispatch prices are volatile, currently around $40/MWh depending on fuel efficiency and equipment type.
Vaca Muerta acquisition requires a de-risking phase with no fixed timeline for drilling pilots or specific CapEx estimates yet.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA reached $120.0 million, a 41.6% quarter-on-quarter increase driven by new generation assets and market normalization.
Secured a landmark concession renewal for Piedra del Aguila hydro asset extending to January 2056 under Resolution 400/2025.
Achieved number one market share in MAT-P contracted capacity segments, with 44% of revenues generated from contracted sales.
summary: Central Puerto reported Q1 FY2026 Adjusted EBITDA of $120 million (up 41.6% qoq) and revenues of $248.6 million (up 43.8% qoq), driven by the full contribution of new assets like Brigadier Lopez combined cycle, solar farms, and Piedra del Aguila following a concession renewal to 2056. Management highlighted strong commercial execution with number one market share in MAT-P contracted capacity segments under Resolution 400/2025. The quarter was capital intensive due to the $301 million CapEx including the transfer of Piedra del Aguila shares and the acquisition of Patagonia Energy S.A.

negative_highlights: Revenue down 6.7% YoY driven by pressure in legacy local and national agency streams
Adjusted EBITDA missed significantly with a loss of approximately -$375k versus $1.1M prior year
Q2 revenue guidance lowered to 'mid to high single digits' decline due to macroeconomic strain on consumers
positive_highlights: Digital revenue increased 18% on a same-station basis to approximately $10.7 million
Owned and operated digital grew 26% year-over-year while lower margin third-party programmatic declined
Completed second lien restructuring exchanging $184M of notes for $98M PIK notes, reducing near-term interest burden
summary: Q1 FY2026 revenue was $41.3 million, down 6.7% year-over-year (or 13% per segment breakdown), with adjusted EBITDA of approximately -$375,000 compared to a prior period profit of $1.1 million. Management raised guidance for Q2 FY2026 revenue decline expectations from mid-single digits to 'mid to high single digits' on a same-station basis due to macro pressure and internal timing dynamics. The company executed significant balance sheet actions including an asset sale, second lien restructuring reducing debt by $86M net, first lien repurchases, and new ABL facility establishment.

negative_highlights: Total revenue grew only 4% year-over-year to $6.7 million, the lightest quarter management expects for the year
Software revenue fell 40% year-over-year to $1.2 million due to a large prior-year sale expected to cover 2025 and 2026 needs
Management said it does not expect to reach cash flow break even by end of 2026 and provided no guidance it can achieve break even by Q4 2027
positive_highlights: Consumable revenue rose 20% year-over-year to $3.9 million, with flow cells sold up 17% to a record Q1 volume of 8,178 units
Adjusted gross margin expanded to 49% from 46% a year earlier, continuing a multi-year climb from the high-20% profile in 2023
2026 clinical lab fee schedule raised OGM hematologic malignancy CPT payment 47% to $1,853.22, and a new constitutional disorder CPT code took effect January 1, 2026
summary: Bionano reported Q1 2026 revenue of $6.7 million, up 4% year-over-year and at the high end of its $6.5-$6.7 million guidance, with adjusted gross margin of 49% versus 46% a year earlier. Consumables rose 20% to $3.9 million and other revenue rose 36% to $1.6 million, but software revenue fell 40% to $1.2 million on a large prior-year sale. The company reaffirmed full-year 2026 revenue guidance of $30-$33 million (5%-16% growth), initiated Q2 guidance of $7.5-$7.8 million (12%-16% growth), and said it does not expect cash flow break even by end of 2026, with runway into 2027 and convertible debt to be retired this month. The quarter included a leadership transition with Al Luderer stepping in as Interim CEO.

negative_highlights: Net loss before tax hit $13.3 million, primarily driven by non-cash fair value adjustments on derivative instruments unrelated to operations.
Graphite-related expenditures totaled approximately $2.3 million in Q1 as the company transitions from development to commercial execution.
Germanium recovery initiative with Teck Metals is still a cooperation agreement requiring feedstock threshold work, with no cash payments or offtake revenue expected within 12 months.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 22% year-over-year to $19.6 million supported by consistent zinc sales volumes.
Zinc production of 14.2M payable pounds was delivered in line with the mine plan and cost guidance.
Commenced first end-to-end domestic natural flake graphite concentrate shipments from the U.S. demonstration facility.
summary: Titan Mining reported Q1 FY2026 revenue of $19.6 million (up 22% YoY) and a net loss before tax of $13.3 million driven by non-cash fair value adjustments on derivatives rather than operational performance. The company delivered zinc production in line with guidance, maintained cost discipline within the $0.98/lb C1 cash cost range, but incurred approximately $2.3 million in graphite-related expenditures and a net loss that masks underlying robust operating capacity.

negative_highlights: Net income dropped significantly due to elevated Citizens takeout activity in Q1 FY25 moderating, resulting in a lower comparable quarter.
Expense ratio increased structurally from 12% to 37.6% YoY as the company retained more premium and associated expenses while reducing quota share ceding commissions.
Combined ratio widened materially due to higher loss ratios (37.3%) and expense levels compared to the prior year period which benefited from non-recurring Citizens dynamics.
positive_highlights: Voluntary customer growth of approximately 9 million homes driven by double-digit policy increases across nearly every channel (agents +9%, alliances +40%).
New business production in Tri-County HO-3 policies surged to a quarter of voluntary Florida new gross written premium, up from low single digits last year.
Reinsurance market conditions improved with strong engagement and anticipated meaningful reduction in risk-adjusted pricing at the June 1 renewal.
summary: American Integrity Insurance Group reported Q1 FY2026 net income of $19.9 million ($1.02 diluted EPS) and gross premiums written of $220 million (up 3.7% YoY), though these results are structurally lower than the prior year due to a lack of Citizens takeout activity which benefited Q1 FY25. Management highlighted strong voluntary growth in Tri-County and middle-aged homes, with policies in force growing 14% YoY, but noted that expense ratios increased significantly as they retained more premium via reduced quota share ceding.

negative_highlights: Company remains pre-revenue with no commercial sales reported.
Cash balance of $21.7 million must fund ongoing clinical trials and manufacturing validation without income offsetting burn.
No specific guidance provided for future cash runway or revenue timing.
positive_highlights: Net loss narrowed to $7.3M from $8.5M due to lower clinical and manufacturing costs ($3.5M R&D vs $5.8M prior year).
VERSATILE-003 trial amendment reduces patient count by ~100 (from 350 to 250) and shortens duration, lowering external costs.
PDS01ADC stage I data published in JCO Oncology Advances showing encouraging results for metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer.
summary: PDS Biotechnology reported a net loss of $7.3 million ($0.13 per share) for Q1 FY26, an improvement from the prior year's $8.5 million loss driven by lower R&D and G&A expenses totaling $6.5 million versus $9.1 million previously. Management highlighted significant clinical progress including a trial amendment to reduce patient count from 350 to 250 and costs for PDS0101, alongside positive data publication for PDS01ADC in colorectal cancer; however, the company has no commercial revenue as it remains pre-revenue with cash of $21.7 million.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined sequentially in every product service line except tech services, primarily due to Winter Storm Fern causing a revenue loss of over $5 million.
Rockies segment posted an operating loss of about $3.8 million and Southwest region reported an operating loss of $3.4 million driven by reduced oil-directed activity.
positive_highlights: Northeast Mid-Con segment revenue increased 28% year-over-year to $52.5 million with Adjusted EBITDA quadrupling compared to the prior year period.
Dry gas revenue in the Northeast region was up approximately 45% year-over-year driven by sustained activity in Haynesville and Marcellus Utica basins.
summary: First quarter revenue was $145 million, down approximately 6% year-over-year and at the lower end of guidance due to Winter Storm Fern delays pushing over $5 million into Q2 and customer budget resets. Adjusted EBITDA margin compressed to about 8%, reflecting typical seasonality and weather-related white space in the Rockies segment which saw a revenue decline of roughly 19%. Management maintains full-year CapEx at approximately $40 million but notes it is tracking below that framework, while forecasting sequential Q2 revenue improvement driven by seasonal rebounds.

negative_highlights: Commercial/industrial occupancy dropped to ~47.5% from ~85% a year ago, cutting segment NOI to ~$758K from $1.139M
Multifamily NOI of ~$4.1M came in below expectations on lower D.C. economic occupancy (high 80% range) and higher operating costs
CEO stated Q1 results are 'worse than 2025' and full-year FFO is expected to remain pressured near term
positive_highlights: Mining and Royalties NOI rose $498K, or 15% YoY, to ~$3.8M, the second consecutive quarter of double-digit growth
Signed leases/LOIs totaling ~53,000 sq ft representing ~$1M of future annualized NOI, with management calling activity 'completely flipped' versus 2025
~$130M of liquidity with conservative asset-level leverage; Altman acquisition added ~1.6M sq ft to a ~$441M pipeline targeting ~$30M stabilized incremental NOI
summary: FRPH reported Q1 2026 NOI of ~$8.9M and FFO of $3.6M ($0.19/share), with full-year 2026 NOI guided to remain roughly stable at ~$37M and FFO expected to stay pressured by lease-up timing, elevated platform costs, and higher interest expense. Commercial/industrial occupancy fell to ~47.5% from ~85% a year ago, driving segment NOI down to ~$758K from $1.139M. Mining royalties grew 15% YoY to ~$3.8M NOI, while multifamily NOI of ~$4.1M came in below expectations on D.C. occupancy and cost pressure. Management framed the weakness as timing, citing 53,000 sq ft of leases/LOIs worth ~$1M annualized NOI and describing leasing activity as having 'completely flipped' versus last year.

negative_highlights: Full-year revenue guidance was lowered to CAD 204-205 million due to geopolitical disruptions and pricing pressure in software markets.
Revenue from outside the U.S. declined approximately CAD 300,000 quarter-over-quarter due to international trade-related pressures.
Large integrated deployments are causing lumpiness in revenue recognition, with some deals only partially implemented (e.g., ~15% of a 150K MRR deal) by quarter-end.
positive_highlights: Data networking and voice networking segments grew approximately 9% and 17% year-over-year, respectively, driven by AI-enabled infrastructure demand.
Churn improved to approximately 0.79%, down from a historical level of 1%, reflecting significant improvements in customer satisfaction.
The company generated CAD 6 million in net cash from operating activities with an 80% conversion rate from adjusted EBITDA.
summary: Sangoma reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of CAD 51 million and adjusted EBITDA of CAD 7.5 million, resulting in a flat-to-miss performance relative to the company's own prior guidance due to timing delays on large integrated deployments and international headwinds. Management lowered full-year fiscal 2026 revenue guidance to CAD 204-205 million and adjusted EBITDA margin guidance to 15%-16%, citing geopolitical disruptions, supply chain costs, and pricing pressure in commoditized software segments. While the company highlighted strong growth in its infrastructure portfolio (data networking +19% YoY, voice networking +9% YoY) and improved operational metrics like churn (0.79%), the consolidated results were weighed down by slower recognition of revenue from multi-year bundled deals.

negative_highlights: Cross-Industry Business (CIB) revenue declined sequentially as demand was pulled into Q4
Management explicitly stated CIB growth will not occur until the second half of the year
Automotive segment margin contracted to 46.2% from 48.4% in prior-year quarter
positive_highlights: Revenues exceeded top-end guidance at $16.9 million
GAAP gross margin expanded to 62.2%, significantly above the guided range of 57%-59%
Adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed to $5.5M, better than anticipated
summary: Valens reported Q1 FY26 revenues of $16.9 million, exceeding the top end of guidance ($16.3M-$16.7M), with GAAP gross margin expanding to 62.2% versus a guided range of 57%-59%. Adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed to $5.5 million compared to an anticipated loss between $4.4M and $7.9M, though the company noted Q1 revenue was lower than Q4 due to seasonality and demand digestion in its Cross-Industry Business (CIB). Management provided unchanged full-year guidance of $75M-$77M but issued a specific warning that CIB growth will accelerate only starting in H2 2026, implying the first half remains soft.

negative_highlights: Net income decreased 2.3% YoY due to a one-time equity tax impact and higher funding costs
NIM on loans contracted significantly as the central bank raised rates by 200 bps in Q1, with further hikes expected later in the year
Full-year ROE guidance lowered after adjusting for the equity tax and building in a tougher interest rate environment
positive_highlights: Completed sale of MFG for $464 million to strengthen capital position
Banco de Bogotá acquired Itaú's personal banking business, hold COP 3.2 trillion in mortgage lending and positioning it third in the housing market
Aval Fiduciaria ROE reached 33% with net income of COP 22 billion
summary: Grupo Aval reported Q1 FY26 net income of COP 336 billion, a decrease of 2.3% YoY due to the impact of an equity tax and higher funding costs from central bank rate hikes. Gross loans grew 6% YoY while deposits increased 11.7%, but NIM compressed as liability repricing outpaced asset growth in this quarter. Management lowered full-year ROE guidance by roughly 20 basis points after stripping the one-time equity tax impact, citing a tougher interest rate environment and electoral uncertainty.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA margin declined by 130 basis points due to increased marketing and IT investments ($6M) and higher credit loss expense.
Merchant segment adjusted EBITDA decreased year-over-year, reflecting a decline in underlying gross margins driven by business mix shifts toward lower-margin ISO channels.
SMB revenue growth was modest at 2%, with management noting limited expectations for significant contribution from this segment through the remainder of the year.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 10% year-over-year with organic growth of 8%, offsetting the prior period's business disposal impact.
Adjusted EPS increased 21% due to a reduced share count and strong top-line performance in iGaming (up 20%).
Unlevered free cash flow rose 17% year-over-year to $67 million, with net leverage improving from 5.5x to 5.2x.
summary: Paysafe reported Q1 FY2026 revenue of $442.7 million (up 10% YoY) and adjusted EPS growth of 21%, driven by strong iGaming performance during the NFL playoffs and a one-time licensing data deal contributing $7M. Management reaffirmed full-year guidance for revenue, EBITDA, and EPS despite Q1 margins being pressured by higher marketing/IT investments ($6M increase) and credit losses ($10M). The company generated $67 million in unlevered free cash flow (up 17% YoY) while reducing net leverage to 5.2x.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to $26.1 million in Q1 FY2026 compared to a net loss of $20.8 million in the prior year quarter
Commercial expenses increased significantly to $15.8 million from $10.4 million due to launch-related personnel and operational costs
Only 300 prescriptions were captured through late April, representing an early-stage partial quarter with limited revenue generation
positive_highlights: CARDEMYST launched within two months of FDA approval as an aggressive goal was successfully met
Express Scripts secured national preferred formulary coverage early in the launch quarter, covering approximately one-quarter of commercially insured lives with quality access
Over 400 unique prescribers wrote prescriptions for CARDEMYST by late April, indicating broad initial adoption
summary: Milestone Pharma reported its first partial quarter of commercial sales for CARDEMYST in Q1 FY2026 with $0.2 million in product revenue and a net loss of approximately $26.1 million ($0.20 per share). The company successfully launched the drug within two months of FDA approval, capturing roughly 300 prescriptions by late April after securing an early formulary win with Express Scripts covering about one-quarter of commercially insured patients. Management noted that while launch execution is on track and prescriber reception is positive, financial results reflect a pre-revenue phase driven largely by commercial expenses.

negative_highlights: GAAP net income of $9.9 million ($0.41/share) came in below adjusted net income, reflecting $2.5 million of adjustments
Strait of Hormuz closure cut Persian Gulf export volumes by approximately 50%, a drag on Supramax flows
No explicit forward guidance was given, and no analyst questions were taken, limiting visibility on outlook
positive_highlights: Adjusted net income of $12.4 million ($0.51/share) with total cash exceeding debt by approximately $127 million, a net cash position
Sale of a 2011-built Capesize generated capital gains of approximately $7 million
Transfer of legacy trading portfolio to Cargill substantially complete, derisking the balance sheet with only one vessel left to novate
summary: Costamare Bulkers reported Q1 2026 net income of $9.9 million ($0.41/share) and adjusted net income of $12.4 million ($0.51/share). The company ended the quarter with total cash above debt by roughly $127 million ($270 million cash vs $640 million debt), and it sold a 2011-built Capesize for about $7 million in gains while acquiring a 2018-built Ultramax and taking delivery of a chartered-in newbuilding Kamsarmax. The Cargill credit-book transfer is substantially complete with one vessel remaining to be novated, and management expects legacy trades to be cleared by year-end. No financial guidance was provided, and the call ended with no analyst questions. No prior-period comparison or consensus figures were stated in the text.

negative_highlights: Q2 guidance of $5.4-$6.0 million is below Q1 revenue, reflecting pull-forward of a full-year customer order into Q1
Consumer-facing demand softening, representing roughly 25% of the customer base, with some orders being pushed out
Supplier price increases and IFCO ramp costs expected to offset margin gains in the second half; full-year cash usage guided to $14-$16 million
positive_highlights: Revenue of $7.4 million exceeded prior guidance and grew from $5.3 million in Q1 2025
Non-GAAP gross margin expanded to 23.8% from 10.8% a year ago on the completed Thailand manufacturing transition
Two of the top three customers extended supply agreements in Q1
summary: Q1 FY2026 revenue of $7.4 million exceeded the previously announced guidance range and rose from $5.3 million in Q1 2025, but the beat was driven by one large customer ordering its full 2026 volume in Q1. GAAP gross margin was 17.4% and non-GAAP 23.8%, up from 2.5% and 10.8% a year ago on the Singapore-to-Thailand production transition, though margins declined sequentially on product mix and new-customer costs. Q2 guidance of $5.4-$6.0 million reflects the pull-forward of that volume into Q1 plus softening demand among consumer-facing customers, and GAAP net loss was $3.4 million ($0.15/share) with non-GAAP adjusted EBITDA loss of $2.7 million. Management reiterated expected full-year margin improvement while flagging supplier price increases, IFCO scale-up costs in H2, and 2026 cash usage of $14-$16 million.

negative_highlights: Top-line revenue declined 3.6%, with decreases in insurance premiums, mortgage fee income, and net investment income
Mortgage lost money in the quarter and cited a 50 bps (~$200 million volume) investor pricing shortfall in March and a 6% origination decline
Life insurance segment revenue fell ~3% to $48.9 million and net earnings ~5% to $5.9 million, with $37 million added land carrying near-term opportunity cost
positive_highlights: Net earnings rose 9.2% (nearly $600,000) to about $7 million while revenue fell 3.6%, as total expenses dropped 5.6%
Mortgage pre-tax loss narrowed 65% to $698,000 from $1.995 million, with average loans per loan officer per month up 23% and refinance volume at 24% (from 19%)
Cemetery/mortuary operating pre-tax earnings rose 15.7% to $1.523 million on 35.1% growth in pre-need land sales
summary: Consolidated revenue fell 3.6% to about $90 million, but net earnings rose 9.2% (~$7 million) on a 5.6% expense reduction, with growth in every segment below the top line. The mortgage segment lost $698,000 (65% better than the prior-year $1.995 million loss) on a 6% origination decline and a 50 bps (~$200 million volume) hit from a surprise March investor pricing decline; life revenues fell ~3% to $48.9 million with net earnings down ~5% to $5.9 million; cemetery/mortuary revenue rose 4.4% while pre-tax earnings fell 4% on investment losses. Management provided no numeric guidance, characterizing Q1 as a modest step back tied to sales-force reorganization, land investments, and lower builder profit share.

negative_highlights: Pro forma gross margin contracted to 62.9% from 68%, primarily due to a shift toward tissue testing mix
Tissue volumes declined sequentially, attributed to integration distraction and conservative accounting for the Resolve exit
Company is facing potential liability of up to $10.4 million in Medicare recoupments related to historical claims
positive_highlights: Pro forma revenue increased by 11% year-over-year on a comparable basis excluding the discontinued Resolve business
Management completed strategic mapping and cross-training of sales force for core prostate cancer menu (Confirm, GPS, ExoDx)
Company maintains strong cash position with $43.2 million in cash and equivalents as of March 31
summary: MDxHealth reported Q1 FY26 revenue of $27.4 million and a pro forma operating loss of $7.9 million after exiting the Resolve UTI business due to reimbursement uncertainty from Novitas. Management updated full-year 2026 guidance for its core prostate cancer operations to $110-$115 million, reflecting an expected sequential decline in tissue volumes during integration while maintaining confidence in future acceleration.

negative_highlights: Management explicitly refused to provide formal guidance for full-year revenues or EBITDA, citing early-stage variability and a lack of visibility into future project completions.
Operating expenses increased significantly in tandem with new campus openings, including non-cash accruals related to ground leases signed at the end of 2025 that are not yet operational.
Denver APA phase I is only 44% leased six months post-opening and described as lagging compared to other campuses.
positive_highlights: Revenues surged 56% sequentially and 76% year-over-year driven by new campus openings including Opa-locka phase II which opened mid-quarter at 68% pre-leasing occupancy.
Assets under construction increased $75 million to over $352 million, indicating accelerating investment pace.
Re-lease escalation rates averaged 23%, up from the prior quarter's 22%, demonstrating strong pricing power independent of CPI.
summary: Q1 FY26 revenues increased 76% year-over-year to an annualized run rate of $35 million, driven by new campus openings and occupancy gains at Opa-locka phase II (opened mid-quarter) and Denver. However, management explicitly declined to provide full-year guidance for the Obligated Group due to early-stage variability in project cadence, noting that significant cash flow generation is expected only from 2027 onwards.

negative_highlights: Q1 adjusted EBITDA of $3 million was negatively impacted by a $5.5 million inventory write-down and severe weather; completion tool revenue fell 10% quarter-over-quarter.
Cash flow from operations was negative $12.4 million in Q1, and liquidity as of March 31 was $46.9 million.
Recent natural gas prices have fallen below $3, down from $4.70 average in Q1, which could dampen the gas-driven activity uptick.
positive_highlights: Q2 guidance implies mid-single-digit revenue growth (to $141 million midpoint) and a sharp EBITDA step-up from $3 million to $12.5 million midpoint.
Completion tools team surpassed 500,000 Scorpion plugs sold, with updated versions and new tools expected in the summer.
International tools revenue grew ~14% sequentially in 2025, driven by UAE, Argentina, and Saudi Arabia; new Haynesville wireline facility opened.
summary: Nine Energy Service reported Q1 2026 revenue of $130 million and adjusted EBITDA of $3 million, which included a $5.5 million non-cash inventory write-down; the quarter was disrupted by severe weather and bankruptcy-related noise. Each segment showed modest declines or flat results: wireline revenue fell 5%, completion tools fell 10%, while cementing and coiled tubing were slightly up. The company guided Q2 revenue to $136 million-$146 million and adjusted EBITDA to $10 million-$15 million, reflecting normalization and less weather impact. Management remains confident in the better run rate, with new product launches and international growth expected to support the back half of the year.

negative_highlights: Marketing revenue declined 5% year-over-year due to negative SEO trends and regulatory impacts in the U.K. and Finland.
Full-year guidance was lowered by approximately EUR 8 million for revenue and EUR 7 million for EBITDA relative to prior expectations.
Adjusted free cash flow dropped significantly to EUR 3.9 million from EUR 10.3 million due to lower earnings and higher capital expenditures.
positive_highlights: Sports data services revenue grew 13% year-over-year driven by enterprise adoption and AI integrations (Claude/Perplexity).
Non-SEO marketing revenue exceeded SEO revenue for the second consecutive quarter, indicating successful diversification strategy.
OpticOdds business saw strong growth with new deal increases of 94% compared to Q1 2025.
summary: First quarter revenue of EUR 40.4 million was flat year-over-year and in line with expectations, while adjusted EBITDA declined to EUR 9 million from EUR 15.9m due to a mix shift where lower-margin non-SEO channels grew faster than SEO traffic. Management lowered full-year guidance for both revenue (to EUR 165-170M) and adjusted EBITDA (EUR 45-50M), citing regulatory headwinds in the U.K./Finland, a slower-than-expected shift away from high-margin SEO search results, and increased costs associated with diversifying traffic sources. The company announced a strategic restructuring to reduce headcount by approximately 25% starting Q3, targeting EUR 13 million in annualized cost savings.

negative_highlights: GAAP net loss of $25.6M driven by a $31.3M net loss on derivatives, including $27.9M non-cash mark-to-market as oil prices rose above hedge strikes
Q1 was flagged as a high watermark; production is expected to decline over the next quarter or two as wells follow natural decline curves
Net cash from operating activities of $10.5M was reduced by a $10.7M working capital use of cash, with $98M drawn on the revolver and only ~$22M availability
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA of $21.5M rose 404% from $4.3M in Q1 2025, and the 31 DJ Basin wells mostly performed ahead of their type curves
Working capital deficit improved $27.1M from $34.1M at year end to $7M at March 31
Full-year guidance reiterated at 6,500-7,000 BOE/d and $60-70M Adjusted EBITDA on $16-20M net capex
summary: PEDEVCO reported Q1 revenue of $40.2M (up 360% YoY, mostly volume from the Juniper merger), Adjusted EBITDA of $21.5M, and a GAAP net loss of $25.6M driven by a $31.3M derivative loss ($27.9M non-cash mark-to-market). Production averaged 8,091 BOE/d, which management said exceeded internal expectations and represented a high watermark for the year as the 31 DJ Basin wells reached peak production in Q1. Full-year guidance was reiterated at 6,500-7,000 BOE/d and $60-70M Adjusted EBITDA on $16-20M net capex, with production expected to decline over the middle quarters before second-half development supports volumes into 2027. The working capital deficit improved $27.1M to $7M and net debt stood at approximately $87M.

negative_highlights: Total revenue declined 12% year-over-year due to lower M400 sales volume.
Overall gross loss widened from $0.3 million in the prior period to $0.4 million as fixed manufacturing costs were less absorbed by lower total sales.
positive_highlights: Engineering services revenues increased 36% year-over-year to $0.35 million.
summary: Vuzix reported Q1 FY2026 revenue of $1.4 million, a decrease of 12% year-over-year compared to $1.6 million in the prior period, driven primarily by lower M400 product sales. The company posted an overall gross loss of $0.4 million and a net loss attributable to common shareholders of $7.1 million ($0.09 per share). Management reiterated that current cash resources provide sufficient runway into 2027 while noting the business is accelerating on OEM programs.

negative_highlights: Net loss of $0.4 million (-$0.01 per diluted share) versus $0.6 million net income ($0.02) in Q1 2025
Operating expenses rose 15.1% to $12.9 million, including a $0.9 million increase in depreciation, amortization and accretion
GW Palo Verde rate review was withdrawn, deferring the new filing to 2027 with rates estimated to be implemented in 2028; adjusted EBITDA was flat at $5.6 million
positive_highlights: Revenue increased 6.7% YoY to $13.3 million, driven by the seven Tucson water systems acquisition, organic growth and higher GW Farmers rates
Rate settlement contemplates a ~$2.3 million water revenue increase for GW Santa Cruz, with an estimated effective date of November 1, 2026
Total active service connections rose 5.7% to 68,885, with 2.6% year-over-year organic connection growth
summary: Q1 FY2026 revenue rose 6.7% YoY to $13.3 million on the Tucson system acquisition, organic connection growth and higher GW Farmers rates, but operating expenses jumped 15.1% to $12.9 million, swinging results to a net loss of $0.4 million (-$0.01 per diluted share) from $0.6 million net income ($0.02) a year earlier. Adjusted EBITDA was flat at $5.6 million. A settlement in pending rate reviews contemplates a ~$2.3 million water revenue increase for GW Santa Cruz and a ~$0.4 million wastewater decrease for GW Palo Verde, effective November 1, 2026, with the Palo Verde review withdrawn and a new filing pushed to 2027 for 2028 rates. Total active connections grew 5.7% to 68,885, though Phoenix MSA single-family permits fell 18.8% YoY in Q1.

negative_highlights: Total at-risk membership declined from approximately 118,000 in Q1 2025 to 106,000 in Q1 FY2026 due to deliberate portfolio exits.
Underlying adjusted EBITDA excluding prior-year items was only $8 million for the quarter.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA swung from a loss of $22 million in Q1 2025 to $26 million in Q1 FY2026, exceeding internal expectations.
MA funding rates improved approximately 15% year-over-year due to contract restructuring and rate progression.
Medical cost trend remained flat compared to the full year 2025 baseline despite industry guidance of 7% or higher.
summary: Q1 FY2026 revenue was $386 million (up from $373M in Q1 2025) with adjusted EBITDA of $26 million compared to a loss of $22 million last year. Management raised the full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA outlook range to $20-$60 million, citing structural contract improvements and favorable prior-year development ($17M). The company reduced its at-risk membership base by exiting non-economic arrangements while maintaining flat medical cost trends.

negative_highlights: OpEx increased by approximately $6 million year-over-year due to SG&A expansion supporting PEDMARK growth.
German milestone payment from partner Norgine is not anticipated for this quarter or near term despite launch efforts in multiple markets.
Cash position decreased slightly during the quarter, with Q2 cash expected to be lower than Q1 before recovering in H2 2026.
positive_highlights: Net product sales surged 73% year-over-year to $15.1M driven by record new patient enrollments in March and April.
Fennec HEARS full-service hub accounted for over 50% of total Q1 demand, with conversion rates hitting the 80% benchmark for the first time.
Commercial footprint expanded significantly via Project Ignite to reach a target base increasing from ~1,300 to over 5,000 healthcare professionals.
summary: Fennec Pharmaceuticals reported Q1 FY2026 net product sales of $15.1 million, a 73% year-over-year increase from $8.8 million in the prior period and representing six consecutive quarters of growth since new leadership took over. Management highlighted record patient enrollments in March and April as their highest demand month ever, with Fennec HEARS driving approximately 50% of total Q1 demand by itself. While OpEx increased to roughly $14 million due to expanded marketing and headcount for Project Ignite, the company maintains a predominantly fixed cost base and expects meaningful operating income growth in subsequent quarters.

negative_highlights: Quarterly gross margin contracted to 12.8% from 13.6% a year ago on unfavorable category and product mix
Adjusted EBITDA grew only 4% year-over-year ($5.1M vs $4.9M), well below the 21% revenue growth rate
No explicit forward financial guidance was issued; Alliance Authentic and Endstate Authentic are described as in 'extreme startup phase' with revenue expected only in fiscal 2027
positive_highlights: Net revenue rose 21% year-over-year to $258 million with net income up 25% to $2.3 million
Year-to-date adjusted EBITDA increased 47% to $35.7 million and gross margin expanded 170 bps to 13.3%
Collectibles revenue grew 48% year-over-year, CD revenue surged 90% to $39 million, and vinyl increased 15% to $99 million
summary: Alliance Entertainment reported Q3 FY2026 net revenue of $258 million, up 21% year-over-year from $213 million, with net income up 25% to $2.3 million ($0.05 diluted EPS) and adjusted EBITDA of $5.1 million versus $4.9 million a year ago. Gross margin contracted to 12.8% from 13.6% on category and product mix, though year-to-date gross margin expanded 170 bps to 13.3% with 9-month net income up 78% to $16.6 million and adjusted EBITDA up 47% to $35.7 million. Category growth was broad-based: collectibles +48%, CD revenue +90% to $39 million, vinyl +15% to $99 million, and physical movie revenue +5% to $61 million. No explicit financial guidance was provided; management said they 'remain confident in the trajectory,' highlighted the fiscal 2027 ramp of Alliance Authentic and Endstate Authentic, and flagged Grand Theft Auto VI and its vinyl soundtrack as Q4 drivers.

negative_highlights: Gross margin contracted to 48% from 54% in Q1 2025, attributed to tariffs hitting cost of goods sold
Capsule shipments fell 3% YoY to 6,229, with shipments pushed into April
Operating expenses rose $1.5 million YoY to $8.4 million on pipeline and clinical trial investment, with continued spend expected through Q3
positive_highlights: Total revenue $2.8 million held flat YoY despite capsule shipments declining 3%, helped by a favorable mix-driven ASP increase (no price increase taken)
Secured key renewals with large GI networks including Indiana University Health, Providence Health & Services, and Gastro Health
Cash position strengthened to $17.9 million after closing a $14 million private placement in March with new and existing investors
summary: CapsoVision reported Q1 FY2026 revenue of $2.8 million, flat versus the prior year, with capsule shipments of 6,229 down 3% YoY (prior year 6,447) due to order timing shifting into Q2. Gross margin fell to 48% from 54% on tariff pressure, and operating expenses rose $1.5 million to $8.4 million on Canon sensor development and Colon Gen Two trial costs, ending with $17.9 million in cash after a $14 million March private placement. Management guided Q2 revenue above Q1 and H2 above H1, tied to the anticipated AI Highlights launch (510(k) clearance still expected around mid-year) and Colon Gen Two submission in Q3 2026, while noting R&D spending will be similar to 2025. No formal guidance figures were quantified, and the quarter showed stable rather than improving reported financials.

negative_highlights: Total operating expenses surged from $1.4 million in Q1 2025 to $5.6 million in Q1 2026
Cash and cash equivalents declined significantly from $12.6 million at year-end to $7.2 million by March 31, 2026
No current revenue generated; all income comes from discontinued operations or non-dilutive government contracts
positive_highlights: Secured first FDA precedent gastrointestinal study protocol from NIAID to fully fund BLA enabling programs
Completed 200-fold manufacturing scale-up at Velocity Bioworks within budget and specifications
Net loss per share improved to $2.23 despite higher absolute losses due to increased weighted average shares
summary: Valion Bio reported a net loss of $6.2 million for Q1 FY2026 compared to a prior year loss of $1.5 million, driven by the integration of Velocity Bioworks which added approximately $3.8 million in SG&A and $1.9 million in R&D expenses. The company did not provide specific revenue guidance or financial targets due to its transition from Tivic Health Systems and lack of current commercial sales for entolimod. Management highlighted significant non-dilutive federal funding milestones, including a new NIAID agreement and Department of War engagement, but noted that third-party CDMO revenue remains in the early pipeline development stage.

negative_highlights: Life Sciences revenue fell 48.4% YoY due to decreases in Glacial FX and Rx unit sales in North America
Spectrum segment faced headwinds from advertising demand softness, network cancellations, and a $900k revenue decline
Company stated it is working with lenders on strategic alternatives as it focuses on fixing its capital structure
positive_highlights: Consolidated revenue increased 33% YoY to $364.8 million
Infrastructure segment adjusted EBITDA rose significantly, with gross margin compression of only ~140 bps despite higher activity
DBM Global backlog remained stable at $1.8 billion while increasing revenue compared to the prior year quarter
summary: Innovate reported Q1 FY2026 consolidated revenue of $364.8 million (up 33% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $19.7 million (up from $7.2m), driven by a strong Infrastructure segment but offset by significant declines in Life Sciences (-48.4%) and Spectrum segments. While the company raised guidance for its core DBM Global infrastructure business, it explicitly stated that near-term performance at other units remains challenged due to demand softness and network cancellations.

negative_highlights: An EMEA on-premise customer terminated its agreement, reducing total SaaS ARR by ~$1.6M (of which ~$900K was AI Knowledge)
Total company SaaS ARR grew only 7% YoY (11% ex-messaging) and Q4 revenue is guided to $21.5M-$22M, below Q3's $22.5M
Longer sales cycles for larger AI Knowledge opportunities are delaying deal conversions and weighing on the FY2026 revenue outlook
positive_highlights: Knowledge customer SaaS ARR grew 26% YoY and LTM dollar-based net retention for Knowledge customers rose to 116% from 97% a year ago
Total gross margin expanded 500 bps to 74% and non-GAAP net income grew to $3.2M from $765K, with adjusted EBITDA margin of 14%
Year-to-date operating cash flow of $18.7M (27% margin) and cash of $80.5M, up from $62.9M at June 30, 2025
summary: eGain Q3 FY2026 total revenue was $22.5M, up 7% YoY, with SaaS revenue also up 7% and representing 93% of total; excluding sunsetting non-core messaging products, revenue and SaaS would have been up 13% and 14%. Non-GAAP net income rose to $3.2M ($0.11 dilutive) from $765K, total gross margin expanded 500 bps to 74%, and LTM dollar-based SaaS net retention for Knowledge customers jumped to 116% from 97%. However, an EMEA on-premise customer terminated rather than migrate to cloud, cutting total SaaS ARR by ~$1.6M (~$900K from AI Knowledge), and FY2026 revenue guidance of $90.5M-$91M reflected longer sales cycles that are delaying deal conversions. Knowledge SaaS ARR grew 26% YoY while all-customer SaaS ARR rose just 7% (11% ex-messaging), with Q4 revenue guided to $21.5M-$22M.

negative_highlights: Consolidated revenue fell to $88 million from $122 million a year ago after the Chickamauga Lock Replacement Project termination
Shimmick core project revenue declined to $88 million from $93 million on project completions and slower burn on new work
Full-year revenue guidance was reaffirmed but the CEO said results may trend toward the lower end of the range
positive_highlights: Total gross margin improved to 12% from 4% a year ago, with Shimmick project gross margin up 89% to 11%
Backlog rose to $944 million, the highest in more than two years, on $289 million of new awards and a record 2.6 book-to-bill

summary: Shimmick reported Q1 FY2026 consolidated revenue of $88 million, down from $122 million a year ago, as non-core revenue collapsed to $200,000 from $29 million due to the Army Corps' termination of the Chickamauga Lock project; Shimmick core revenue slipped to $88 million from $93 million. Gross margin expanded sharply to 12% consolidated from 4%, with Shimmick project gross margin at 11% versus 6%, and adjusted EBITDA turned positive at $3 million from negative $3 million. New awards of $289 million drove a record 2.6 book-to-bill and total backlog to $944 million, the highest in over two years, with non-core backlog now under 5% of the total. Management reaffirmed full-year 2026 guidance for 12%-22% revenue growth and 200%-500% adjusted EBITDA growth, despite the Chickamauga termination, though the CEO noted revenue may trend toward the lower end of the range.

negative_highlights: Net income dropped to $4 million ($0.11 per share) from $5.8 million ($0.16) on a $2.9 million non-cash mark-to-market loss on commodity contracts
Operating expense rose 13% to $8 per BOE from $7.07 per BOE, driven by non-operated workover costs and higher water hauling
Management declined to provide updated guidance or production run-rates, deferring capital allocation decisions to the new board
positive_highlights: Record quarterly net revenue of $19.6 million, up 20% from $16.4 million in the prior quarter
Production rose 15% to 4,685 BOE per day and adjusted EBITDA hit a record $14.8 million, up 16% sequentially
Credit facility borrowing capacity was increased from $65 million to $75 million while net debt fell to $45 million
summary: Kolibri reported record quarterly net revenue of $19.6 million, up 20% sequentially, and record adjusted EBITDA of $14.8 million, up 16%, on production of 4,685 BOE per day versus 4,077 BOE per day in Q4 2025. Net income fell to $4 million ($0.11 per basic share) from $5.8 million ($0.16) a year earlier due to a $2.9 million non-cash mark-to-market loss on commodity contracts; operating expense rose 13% to $8 per BOE on workover and water-handling costs. The credit facility borrowing capacity was redetermined up to $65-75 million, net debt was $45 million, and $8 million of paydowns are planned. Management gave no formal updated guidance, saying capital allocation options (more drilling, debt paydown, buybacks) will be presented to the new board in coming weeks, while the three-well program is drilling with wells expected online in Q3.

negative_highlights: No explicit Q1 revenue, EPS, or margin figures were disclosed on the call, leaving the quarter's actual results unquantified
Company remains EBITDA- and cash-flow-negative, with positive operating cash flow only expected to begin in Q3 2026

positive_highlights: EBITDA loss narrowed to -$5 million in Q1 2026 from -$10 million in Q4 2025
Full-year 2026 guidance reiterated at approximately $160 million or greater revenue, with 19%-21% gross margin and 9%-10% EBITDA margin
Management expects better than the 19%-21% guided gross margin in future years as NDAA/Blue UAS and services mix expands
summary: First quarter FY2026 was the first full quarter including Drone Nerds operations; the call disclosed no explicit Q1 revenue or EPS figures, only that Q1 is the seasonal low point and Q4 the high point. Management reiterated FY2026 guidance of approximately $160 million or greater revenue, 19%-21% gross margin, and 9%-10% EBITDA margin, and continues to expect positive operating cash flow starting in Q3. Adjusted EBITDA burn narrowed from -$10 million in Q4 2025 to -$5 million in Q1 2026, with $15.2 million unrestricted cash plus roughly $8 million of remaining borrowing base under a $20 million JPMorgan ABL (about $4.8 million drawn). The company guided to year-end cash of roughly $15 million-$17 million and second-half positive cash flow of $2 million-$3 million.

negative_highlights: GAAP net loss of $0.4 million, or $0.09 per share, versus net income of $1.6 million, or $0.88 per share, in Q1 2025

Q2 revenue growth is expected to be lower than Q1, driven by timing of hiring and acquisition integration

summary: Park Dental Partners reported Q1 FY2026 revenue of $62.7 million, up 6.2% year-over-year, with same-practice revenue growth of 4.1%, general practice revenue of $46.1 million (+6.4%) and multi-specialty revenue of $16.6 million (+5.7%). GAAP net loss was $0.4 million or $0.09 per share versus net income of $1.6 million or $0.88 per share in Q1 2025, while non-GAAP adjusted EBITDA was $4.7 million (7.6% of revenue) and adjusted EPS was $0.44. Management maintained its full-year 2026 outlook and noted Q2 revenue growth will be lower than Q1, with Q3 and Q4 at or above Q1's rate. The main change versus prior periods is the earnings drag from IPO-related share-based compensation and new public company costs, which offset revenue growth and operating leverage.

negative_highlights: Revenue growth impacted by lower average note price from powertrain mix
Operating expenses increased sequentially from $7.1M to $9.0M
Management cautions margins will not hold at this level every quarter
positive_highlights: Revenue nearly doubled YoY to $11.2 million
Record GAAP gross margin of 38.6%
