summary: XOS reported Q1 2026 revenue of $11.2 million, nearly double the prior year's $5.9 million, with 95 units delivered versus 29 a year ago. GAAP gross margin hit a record 38.6%, up from 20.6% in Q1 2025 and a loss in Q4 2025, driven by a favorable mix of higher-margin hub and powertrain sales. Management highlighted strong demand for the Hub, including a new deployment with MacAllister Caterpillar for a hyperscaler data center project, and expects full-year 2026 margins to be meaningfully better than 2025. They also noted continued cost discipline and a pipeline expansion into public sector and defense applications.

negative_highlights: Subscription revenue was flat sequentially, equivalent only to the prior quarter

Q1 sequential decline in total revenue is attributed to strategic trade-offs prioritizing durable licensing relationships over maximizing upfront recognition

Gross margin expanded from 53% in Q4 2025 to 56% in Q1 FY2026
summary: CuriosityStream reported Q1 FY2026 revenue of $15.2 million (slight YoY increase) and adjusted EBITDA of $0.9 million, marking the fifth consecutive quarter of positive results but missing prior expectations due to deliberate strategic choices favoring long-term licensing structures over immediate quarterly recognition. Management provided forward guidance for H1 2026 revenue between $35M-$41M (up from implied Q1 levels) and full-year FY2026 revenue between $75M-$80M, alongside adjusted EBITDA of $16M-$20M. The company raised its quarterly dividend to $0.085 per share while executing a small buyback.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened year-over-year primarily driven by changes in fair value of warrant liabilities and expenses related to Q4 debt financing.
Company explicitly stated it will not provide forward-looking guidance or estimates during this call, indicating a lack of specific financial targets.
positive_highlights: Secured a minor source air quality construction permit, enabling the start of construction once financing is complete.
summary: Stardust Power reported a net loss of $5.2 million for Q1 FY2026 compared to $3.8 million in the prior year, with operating cash usage improving to $2.1 million due to disciplined cost controls and non-operating items. The company remains pre-revenue as it advances development milestones at its Muskogee refinery but explicitly declined to provide forward-looking guidance or estimates during this call.

RideNow reported Q1 FY2026 revenue of $260.4 million, up 6.4% YoY (8.9% excluding the wound-down Wholesale Express), with adjusted EBITDA of $9.3 million up 32.9% from $7.0 million and a fourth consecutive quarter of YoY improvement. Same-store revenue rose 13.1%, units 16.3%, and gross profit 12.2%, while adjusted SG&A fell 130 bps to 84.3% of gross profit. Management cited continued YoY comp growth into April though below March's pace due to higher gas prices, guided to more adjusted EBITDA and increased free cash flow in 2026, and noted refinancing progress without specifics. Cash used in operations was $27.6 million versus $6.9 million a year ago, driven by inventory purchases ahead of the watching season.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened significantly to $46.4 million ($0.48 per diluted share) compared to a net loss of $145,000 in the prior year.

Company secured a Nasdaq listing extension until July 6th to regain compliance with minimum stock price requirements.

However, total operating expenses spiked to $47.1 million due to $43.3 million in non-cash unrealized losses on digital assets and other charges, resulting in a net loss of $46.4 million ($0.48/share). Management provided no financial guidance but highlighted progress on a 10-MW AI infrastructure project in Alberta with deployment readiness targeted for Q1 2027.

Management said customer counts and average revenue per visit both rose YoY, with average ticket beginning to recover alongside easing competition.
summary: Q1 FY2026 total revenue was $43 million, down 9% YoY, driven mainly by last April's fee-structure revisions that cut franchising revenue by $6.2 million and management services by $2.4 million ($8.7 million total). Net income fell YoY, partly on an $8.7 million one-time life insurance surrender gain in the prior-year quarter. Management said underlying revenue grew 11% and underlying EBITDA grew 17% excluding those revisions and a $1.3 million AHH consolidation-period difference, and stated the fee-structure impact is now over with revenue up 9% QoQ. No explicit forward guidance figures were given; management said margins should be stable and improve over time and that EBITDA margin is on an upward trajectory.

negative_highlights: Company explicitly stated it does not have a full year of cash runway without anticipated revenue inflows.

DARE to PLAY received enthusiastic reception at ACOG, with providers writing prescriptions on the spot.
summary: Daré Bioscience reported Q1 FY2026 results with no product revenue recorded as the company remains in a pre-commercial phase for its key assets like DARE to PLAY and Flora Sync LF5 (launching June). Management highlighted positive interim data from the Ovaprene Phase III trial, including two consecutive DSMB reviews and improved tolerability metrics. The company ended the quarter with $18.5 million in cash but explicitly stated it does not have 12 months of capital runway without anticipated revenue inflows.

Net cash used in operating activities was $4.2 million, though excluding stablecoin acquisition it would have been lower.
positive_highlights: Adjusted gross profit grew sequentially from $821,000 in Q4 to $960,000 in Q1 despite a 33% decline in HYPE token price.
Yield enhancement strategies saw over 150% quarter-over-quarter growth driven by volatility and Rysk Premium partnerships.
DeFi monetization grew by 140%, fueled by HIP-3 market volume, Felix Exchange activity, and Silhouette spot testing.
summary: Hyperion DeFi reported Q1 FY2026 adjusted gross profit of $960,000, representing a sequential increase from $821,000 in Q4 and an annualized run rate that supports raised full-year guidance. Management increased its 2026 adjusted gross profit guidance by approximately 20% to the range of $5 million-$7 million, driven by substantial growth across staking yield ($313k), validator commissions ($40k), yield enhancement ($211k), DeFi monetization ($245k), and ecosystem rewards ($150k). The company also highlighted a record Q1 net income of $8.8 million compared to a loss in the prior quarter, with cash flow breakeven anticipated by year-end.

negative_highlights: Reported quarterly earnings materially reduced by unrealized hedge losses, a P&L mismatch versus realized pricing.
Q1 unit OpEx elevated to the high-10s/low-20s per BOE in the Powder River Basin due to PDP-only production and fixed-cost drag, with improvement not expected until Q4.
Parkman three-well peak rate guidance was clarified down from 1,600 BOE/d to 1,060 BOE/d, reflecting an assumed 20-33% working-interest note-down.

Debt paid down $10M to $40.5M since the November Peak acquisition close.
Non-core asset sales: PA overriding royalty package for $3.9M at ~6x next-12-month cash flow, and an office building under contract for $3M.
summary: Epsilon reported Q1 FY2026 adjusted EPS of $0.29, with GAAP results materially hurt by non-cash unrealized hedge losses tied to the sharp oil price move; no explicit revenue or production figures were given on the call. Management reiterated that full-year plans are on track for oil-weighted production growth, with the first 3-plus mile Barnett well (226 BOE/d net) online in Q2, two Niobrara DUCs completing in June, and a three-well Parkman program spudding in August. Debt was reduced $10M to $40.5M, and non-core asset sales (a $3.9M PA royalty package, a $3M office building) are funding the elevated CapEx cadence planned over the next three quarters. This is an in-line execution update with no changes to prior guidance.

negative_highlights: Full year 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance lowered to $32.5-$40 million from $40-$50 million
Consolidated gross margin fell 640 bps to 21% as power and gas costs rose 28% and 55% per unit
Diluted EPS fell to $0.11 from $0.40; GRE adjusted EBITDA dropped to $7.0 million from $17.1 million and GREW loss widened to $2.3 million
positive_highlights: Record quarterly revenue of $142 million, up 4% YoY, with GREW revenue up 74% to $7.5 million
Net customer growth of 25,000 RCEs and 18,000 meters in the quarter, with 84,000 new retail customers acquired
Strong balance sheet: $199.8 million in cash, equivalents, restricted cash and marketable securities against $6.8 million total debt
summary: Genie Energy reported Q1 FY2026 revenue up 4% to $142 million, but consolidated gross profit fell 20% to $29.8 million with margin down 640 bps to 21%, and diluted EPS dropped to $0.11 from $0.40 a year ago. Adjusted EBITDA was $2.8 million versus expectations, and management cut full year 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance to $32.5-$40 million from the prior $40-$50 million range. The shortfall stemmed from extreme winter weather compressing retail power and gas margins in the first two months, higher customer acquisition spend of roughly $3 million, and a further solar panel inventory write-down at GREW. Management said March margins normalized and expects improvement through the rest of 2026, with 354,000 RCEs after a net increase of 25,000 and cash and securities of $199.8 million.

negative_highlights: Same-store sales declined approximately 8.8% due to fuel price impacts and reduced discretionary spending
Cost of goods sold as a percentage of restaurant sales increased significantly to 38%, up from 33.6%
Company suspended construction on six additional stores and slowed new openings to only 5-7 for the full year
positive_highlights: Same-store sales decline improved sequentially to -8.8% from Q4's -11.7%
Cost of goods sold margin expanded via a $1 price increase, though COGS % rose to 38%
Retail CPG division secured commitments for an estimated run rate exceeding 2,000 supermarket locations by end-2026
summary: In Q1 FY26, the company reported a net loss of $7.5 million ($0.22 diluted EPS) and an adjusted net loss of $4.5 million ($0.14 diluted EPS), driven by same-store sales declines of approximately 8.8% due to macroeconomic pressures like high fuel prices in California. Management guided for full-year revenues between $215-$225 million, a significant slowdown from prior growth plans, and restaurant-level adjusted EBITDA margins targeting 15%-15.5% in the second half of the year following initiatives including menu streamlining and new retail partnerships.

Gross margin approximately -22% due to revenue mix and lower fixed cost absorption.

summary: Innoviz reported Q1 2026 revenues of $7.1 million, with some NRE milestones delayed to later quarters but POs in place. The company reaffirmed its full-year guidance of $67-$73 million, expecting 27% YoY revenue growth. Record unit shipments and entry into defense/homeland security were highlighted, with new partnerships including Kela and a large holding group. Gross margin was -22% due to revenue mix and low absorption, but fixed cost absorption is expected to improve with volume ramp.

negative_highlights: NII down from $0.45 to $0.38 per share due to non-accruals and lower base rates.
NAV fell from $19.10 to $18.27 per share, driven by market and credit-specific markdowns.
Non-accruals increased to 5.7% of cost (from 4.1%) with 5 new health-care non-accruals.

Attractive new investment spreads: new platforms at ~500 basis points with 93% lead/agent.
summary: Q1 FY2026 was a challenging quarter for CCAP: NII fell to $0.38 per share (down from $0.45), NAV decreased to $18.27 from $19.10, and non-accruals rose to 5.7% of cost. Management reduced base and incentive fees, reset the regular dividend to $0.34 per share, and approved special dividends to manage spillover. Deployment remained modest at $115 million with net deployment of $22 million.

Management noted that unrealized gains from partnerships may not be visible in SPS growth during bear markets or flat markets.

Management states confidence in sustaining operations for well over two years at current prices with staking revenue, even if SOL drops 50%.
summary: Management provided no reported financial results for Q1 FY2026 in the transcript; instead of reporting revenue or EPS beats/misses, they focused on strategic updates regarding their Solana treasury and partnerships.

Persistent headwinds from tariffs and a smaller herd size impacted the beef side of the business.

RaiseWell program secured Whole Foods Market as the first major retailer to adopt the program.

The company returned to profitability despite headwinds from tariffs and a smaller herd size, with the new RaiseWell program securing Whole Foods Market as a first major retailer. Management plans to continue its stock repurchase program, having bought back 24,469 shares in the quarter.

GAAP net income rose only 1% as tax expense increased roughly 200% (~$300,000) with NOL carryforwards no longer offsetting taxable income
No explicit forward revenue or EPS guidance was provided; SPARGroup and Touchless Traceability revenue is not expected to show for six to nine months
positive_highlights: Operating expenses decreased 12% to $3.6 million and income from operations rose 24% to roughly $2.3 million
YTD revenue grew 5% to $17.7 million and YTD diluted EPS rose 9% to $0.28

summary: ReposiTrak reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $5.9 million, essentially flat year-over-year versus $5.9 million, which management attributed to non-recurrence of elevated traceability onboarding in the prior-year March quarter ahead of the original FDA deadline (prior year grew ~16%). Operating expenses fell 12% to $3.6 million, lifting income from operations 24% to approximately $2.3 million; GAAP net income rose 1% to about $2 million and diluted EPS was $0.10, with tax expense up roughly $300,000 (~200%) as NOL benefits no longer offset taxable income. YTD revenue rose 5% to $17.7 million and YTD diluted EPS rose 9% to $0.28; the company ended with $26.4 million cash and zero bank debt. summary: Mizuho reported FY2025 (period labeled Q4 FY2026) profit attributable to owners of parent of JPY 1,248.6 billion with a 60% total payout ratio, against a normalized basis of roughly JPY 1,150 billion. Guidance explicitly excludes any impact from the Middle East conflict and is described as "full tilt," with management flagging that prolonged conflict could materially hurt corporate sentiment. A JPY 100 billion buyback was launched, initially sized modestly due to Middle East uncertainty, with the 50%+ total payout policy unchanged and cross-shareholding reduction at 45% progress (JPY 152.4 billion).

summary: In Q1 FY2026, GAAP revenue was $29 million, up 33% year-over-year but down 3% sequentially (up 2% normalizing for tax accrual release). Adjusted EBITDA loss was $13 million, worse than Q4's $10 million loss but improved from $17 million loss a year ago; excluding litigation expenses, loss narrowed to $7 million, a 15% sequential improvement. Paying MAU declined 9% sequentially to 128,000 due to reduced UA spend, but ARPPU increased 7% and GMV grew. The jury awarded $420 million in damages against Papaya, with potential total award up to $1.2 billion, but collectability and timing remain uncertain. Guidance was not provided, and management's outlook is mixed: they expect PMAU to be flat to up with better unit economics, while RZR remains profitable for a third consecutive quarter.

summary: Imperial Petroleum reported Q1 FY2026 revenue of $61.7 million, up 92% YoY and 21% QoQ, with net income of $28 million (EPS $0.60) and operating income of $26.5 million, marking its second-best quarterly result. The surge was driven by the Strait of Hormuz closure, which lifted tanker rates to approximately $56,000/day for product tankers and over $260,000/day for suezmaxes, alongside fleet expansion. Management gave no formal guidance, noting continued tanker rate normalization in April after a ceasefire before picking up again after April 20. The company remains debt-free with $213 million in cash and an active buyback program (855,769 shares repurchased for $3.8 million), but flagged uncertainty from the longer-than-expected conflict and potential impacts of a Hormuz reopening or Russian sanctions lifting.

Avocado volume guidance was raised to 5.5-6.5M pounds and roughly 500,000 pounds of harvest was deliberately pushed from Q2 into Q3, where pricing is running around $1.30-$1.40 per pound.

Management reiterated the targeted $10M in annual SG&A savings and expects positive Adjusted EBITDA in both Q3 and Q4, alongside a $16M Paso Robles vineyard partial-sale agreement ($10M cash at closing) and a $155M multi-year real estate proceeds pipeline.
summary: Q2 FY2026 total net revenues fell to $23.9M from $35.1M a year ago, with fresh lemon carton sales of $17.1M on 1,028,000 cartons at $16.63 (up from $14.52) under the new Sunkist cadence. GAAP net loss widened to $21.4M or $1.20 per diluted share, driven largely by $23.8M of mostly non-cash charges ($9.3M Windfall Farms impairment, $7.8M asset disposal loss, $5.1M FX losses, $1.6M foreign receivable allowance); adjusted EPS loss was $0.29 and Adjusted EBITDA was a loss of $1.7M versus a $0.2M loss a year ago. Management reiterated FY2026 fresh lemon volumes of 4-4.5M cartons, raised avocado volumes to 5.5-6.5M pounds, and said it expects positive Adjusted EBITDA in both Q3 and Q4 on higher lemon and avocado volumes plus $10M in SG&A savings.

negative_highlights: Total sales fell 6% to about $144 million and comparable sales declined 8.7%
Gross margin contracted 350 bps to 68.3% on $4.7 million of net tariff costs and higher markdown mix
Adjusted EBITDA fell to $16.7 million from $27.3 million and adjusted EPS dropped to $0.45 from $0.88
positive_highlights: New-to-brand customer acquisition grew slightly YoY, skewed younger and spent at a higher average order value
Jackets, outerwear and accessories posted strong growth, and color deliveries sold at full price
Full-year guidance was reaffirmed for sales, comps, gross margin, adjusted EBITDA of $70-$75 million and free cash flow of about $20 million
summary: Q1 FY2026 total sales were about $144 million, down 6% YoY, with comparable sales down 8.7% and adjusted EPS of $0.45 versus $0.88 a year ago. Gross margin contracted 350 bps to 68.3% on $4.7 million of net tariff costs and a higher markdown mix, and adjusted EBITDA fell to $16.7 million from $27.3 million. Management reaffirmed full-year sales, comp, gross margin, EBITDA and free cash flow guidance but reduced planned net new store openings to 1-5 from about 5 and cut CapEx to $20-$25 million from about $25 million, while guiding Q2 sales down 1-3% and comps down 2-4%. The quarter met internal expectations but showed steep YoY declines, offset by early new-customer growth, strong color/jacket/accessory watching and encouraging early Q2 reads.

negative_highlights: At approximately $5 million in cash and cash equivalents at March 31, 2026, the company remains pre-revenue with no product sales.
Subsequent to year-end the company raised only approximately $1.85 million in net proceeds via its at-the-market program, a modest amount relative to its ongoing clinical and research spending.

Enrollment in cohort 3 has begun but the company noted screen failures among prospective participants, and no clinical efficacy has been established — the trial's primary endpoint is safety, with the study explicitly too small for clinical efficacy.
positive_highlights: Operating expenses declined 21.9% year-over-year to approximately $7.3 million, reflecting a $1.1 million payroll reduction, $500,000 lower G&A, and $400,000 lower professional fees.
Net loss narrowed to $7.2 million for fiscal 2026 from $13.4 million in fiscal 2025, and the operating loss decreased to approximately $7.3 million from $9.3 million.

Cohort 2 of the Australian oncology trial completed with no safety concerns and DSMB recommended advancing to cohort 3 with no protocol modifications; the first cohort 3 participant was enrolled and treated without device deficiencies.
summary: Aethlon Medical reported fiscal 2026 operating expenses declining 21.9% year-over-year to approximately $7.3 million, with net loss narrowing to $7.2 million from $13.4 million in the prior fiscal year, and cash of approximately $5 million at March 31, 2026. Subsequent to year-end, the company raised approximately $1.85 million in net proceeds through its at-the-market program. Clinically, cohort 2 of the Australian oncology trial was completed with no safety concerns and DSMB context advancing to the final cohort, in which the first participant has been enrolled and treated. No revenue guidance, per-share earnings, or explicit financial outlook was provided.

negative_highlights: Full-year revenue guidance of $255-$270 million was maintained, not raised, despite the strong Q1
Indirect segment growth of 26.6% was driven by collaborations, and would have been roughly flat excluding that benefit
Management cited consumer headwinds from higher inflation and fuel prices, and expects quarter-to-quarter improvement to be uneven
positive_highlights: Revenue returned to positive growth at $55.7 million, up 7.8% year-over-year, the first overall revenue growth since Q4 FY2022
Non-GAAP gross margin expanded 430 basis points to 51.8%, and operating loss improved 76% to negative $3.3 million
Full-year outlook for non-GAAP operating loss improvement raised to at least 50% from 40%
summary: Vera Bradley reported Q1 FY2027 revenue of $55.7 million, up 7.8% year-over-year, the first quarter of overall revenue growth since Q4 FY2022, with direct segment up 4.1% and indirect up 26.6%. Non-GAAP gross margin expanded 430 basis points to 51.8%, SG&A fell $5.6 million, and the operating loss improved 76% to negative $3.3 million, while inventory dropped 26% to $73 million. Full-year revenue guidance was maintained at $255-$270 million, but the operating loss improvement outlook was raised to at least 50% from 40%. Management flagged uneven quarterly improvement ahead and cited inflation and fuel-price headwinds.

negative_highlights: Q4 adjusted net income fell to CAD 5.6M from CAD 16.3M, due to higher SG&A and lower FX/interest
Canadian federal reimbursement change effective April 2026 expected to hit FY2027 revenue and margins
Consumer cannabis revenue dropped to CAD 3.6M from CAD 8.2M as segment wound down
positive_highlights: Q4 net revenue +10% YoY; global medical +14%, international +19%
Full-year adjusted EBITDA +32% to CAD 54 million; net revenue exceeded guidance
Acquired EU GMP Safari Flower Company to expand capacity; strong cash position
summary: Aurora reported Q4 FY2026 net revenue of CAD 84.8 million, up 10% year-over-year, with global medical cannabis revenue up 14% and international revenue up 19%. Adjusted gross margin was 60% (medical at 66%), adjusted EBITDA came in at CAD 9.2 million, and adjusted net income was CAD 5.6 million, down from CAD 16.3 million a year ago due to higher SG&A and lower interest/foreign exchange gains. Full-year net revenue rose 11% to CAD 321 million, above the guided range by CAD 8 million; adjusted EBITDA grew 32% to CAD 54 million; cash stood at CAD 165 million with no debt. Management exited certain lower-margin Canadian consumer markets, divested Bevo, and acquired Safari Flower Company; FY2027 guidance reflects a regulatory change in Canada that will impact top line and margins, but tone remains confident on international growth.

negative_highlights: Total revenue declined 2% year-over-year primarily due to variability in overage-related revenue recognition.
Billings decreased year-over-year from $63.9 million to $60.4 million due to timing dynamics.
Existing debt facility carries a current classification on the balance sheet due to non-compliance with minimum ARR covenant.
positive_highlights: Gross retention increased 240 bps year-over-year to 86.7%.
Net retention rose 150 bps year-over-year to 95.5%.
Adjusted free cash flow was close to break even with positive operating cash flow of $5.2 million.
summary: Domo reported Q1 FY2027 revenue of $79.4 million, a 2% year-over-year decline driven by overage variability and timing dynamics in billings. While underlying metrics like gross retention (86.7%) and net retention (95.5%) improved significantly, the company disclosed it will not provide financial guidance due to an advanced stage of strategic transaction negotiations. The CFO explicitly stated that existing debt is classified as current due to a missed ARR covenant, though a forbearance agreement has been secured.

negative_highlights: Q1 loss from operations was $2.6 million and adjusted EBITDA was negative $1.1 million
Net inventory rose to $70.8 million from $62.3 million, including ~$4.5 million higher carrying value due to tariffs
Guidance assumes no tariff refunds and reflects higher input costs and lower reciprocal tariff rates, with management citing ongoing macro volatility
positive_highlights: Net sales rose 10.5% to $64 million, with DTC up 15.6% and wholesale up 5.9%
Full-year FY2026 outlook raised to net sales growth of approximately 7%-8%, with adjusted operating margin of 4%-4.5% and adjusted EBITDA margin of 5.5%-6%
Gross margin expanded 30 bps to 50.6%, driven by ~130 bps from higher pricing and ~100 bps from lower discounting, partly offset by tariffs
summary: Vince reported Q1 FY2026 net sales up 10.5% to $64 million, with DTC up 15.6% and wholesale up 5.9%, and gross margin improving 30 bps to 50.6%. Loss from operations narrowed to $2.6 million from $4.4 million, and net loss per share improved to $0.16 from $0.37, while adjusted EBITDA improved $1.9 million to negative $1.1 million. Management raised its full-year FY2026 outlook to net sales growth of approximately 7%-8%, with adjusted operating margin of 4%-4.5% and adjusted EBITDA margin of 5.5%-6%, and guided Q2 sales up 10%-12%. Q2-to-date sales trends are running above low double digits, though guidance excludes any tariff refunds and incorporates higher input costs and lower reciprocal tariff rates.

negative_highlights: Same-store sales declined 1.2%
Free cash flow fell to CAD 1.5 million due to CAD 4.3 million working capital investment
Management cautioned that German business may be lumpy and Q2 may not be a representative run rate
positive_highlights: Revenue up 30% YoY to a record CAD 179.3 million
Adjusted EBITDA up 73% YoY to a record CAD 13.9 million
German segment gross margin doubled to 27% from 12% in Q1, driving positive segment EBITDA of CAD 3.2 million
summary: High Tide reported record Q2 FY2026 results with revenue of CAD 179.3 million (up 30% YoY, fastest growth in 11 quarters), record gross profit of CAD 48.4 million (up 36% YoY), record adjusted EBITDA of CAD 13.9 million (up 73% YoY), and net income of CAD 0.01 per share. Consolidated gross margin reached 27%, an eight-quarter high, driven by the German medical cannabis segment (Remexian) which saw margins more than double to 27% from 12% in Q1. The company reiterated its target to add 20-30 stores in Canada and announced a CAD 40 million credit facility with Bank of Montreal; however, same-store sales declined 1.2%, which management attributed to core customer trade-down and economic pressures, though trends are stabilizing in Q3. Free cash flow was CAD 1.5 million due to a CAD 4.3 million working capital build.

negative_highlights: FY2026 net sales declined 14.3% to $190.5M and Q4 net sales fell 24%, with adjusted Q4 down 9.2% driven almost entirely by aiming solutions weakness
Non-GAAP EPS fell to $0.28 from $0.76 and adjusted EBITDA dropped to $10.2M from $17.7M
Shooting sports net sales declined 15.9% and e-commerce net sales fell 15.6% amid the largest e-com retailer's inventory reset; Q1 FY2027 adjusted EBITDA expected to be slightly negative
positive_highlights: POS grew ~4% in FY2026, the fourth consecutive quarter of positive year-over-year POS growth, with outdoor lifestyle POS up 7%
FY2027 net sales guidance of $200M-$210M implies 7.5% growth at the midpoint, with adjusted EBITDA guided to 6.5%-7.5% of net sales, over 40% higher at the midpoint than FY2026
Filed a $15.2M IEPA tariff refund claim and ended FY2026 with $21.4M cash, zero debt, and over $110M total available capital
summary: FY2026 net sales fell 14.3% to $190.5M and Q4 net sales dropped 24%, with management attributing the declines largely to ~$10M of retailer orders accelerated into the final two weeks of FY2025; adjusted for that, full-year sales declined 5.4% and Q4 fell 9.2%. GAAP EPS was a loss of $0.73 versus a $0.01 loss, non-GAAP EPS was $0.28 versus $0.76, adjusted EBITDA fell to $10.2M from $17.7M, and gross margin rose 10 bps to 44.7%. Management guided FY2027 net sales to $200M-$210M (midpoint +7.5%) with adjusted EBITDA at 6.5%-7.5% of net sales, above 40% growth at the midpoint, and cited Q1 FY2027 sales ~20% above Q1 FY2026. The company filed a $15.2M IEPA tariff refund claim, ended the year with $21.4M cash and no debt, and repurchased ~551,000 shares at an average of $9.24.

negative_highlights: Calendar 2026 revenue guidance of $8 million implies only ~15% growth versus the 107% reported in FY2026

Gen 2 LungFit remains under FDA review with no approval; the 2027 guidance of $16-$18 million is explicitly contingent on Gen 2 approval and launch, and a one-for-20 reverse split was implemented to address Nasdaq listing compliance
positive_highlights: FY2026 revenue grew 107% YoY to $7.7 million from $3.7 million
Gross profit turned positive at $300,000, a $2 million swing from a $1.7 million loss
Customer renewal rate approximately 90%, with three major GPO agreements including a new national agreement covering almost 2,000 hospitals
summary: Beyond Air reported FY2026 revenue of $7.7 million, up 107% from $3.7 million, with a ~90% customer renewal rate, and swung gross profit to a positive $300,000 from a $1.7 million loss. Operating expenses fell sharply (R&D -39% to $10.2 million; SG&A -27% to $19.1 million), but net loss was still $33.2 million (-$4.01/share) with cash burn of $19.1 million and $17.3 million in cash/marketable securities against $21.6 million long-term debt. The company gave first-time calendar 2026 revenue guidance of $8 million (~15% growth, no Gen 2 revenue assumed) and calendar 2027 guidance of $16-$18 million, contingent on FDA approval and commercial launch of Gen 2 in 2027, and disclosed a one-for-20 reverse split to address Nasdaq minimum bid compliance by July 31, 2026.

negative_highlights: Net loss of $2.2 million (-$0.18 per share) in Q4, with full-year net loss of $10.2 million (-$0.81 per share).
Gross profit fell year-over-year to $6.8 million (13.2% of sales) from $7.7 million (15.7% of sales), partly due to a $1.7 million prior-year inventory policy benefit.
Adjusted EBITDA remained negative at -$0.6 million for the quarter and -$4.7 million for the full year.
positive_highlights: Bedding segment sales rose 12.5% year-over-year to $30.5 million, with gross profit up 38% sequentially.
Total inventory was reduced to $47.5 million from $52.2 million at Q3-end, a $4.7 million sequential decline.
The company received approximately $7 million in IEEPA tariff refunds in Q1 FY2027, expected to reduce net debt to as low as ~$5 million.
summary: Culp reported Q4 FY2026 net sales of $51.6 million, up 7.6% sequentially and roughly 6% year-over-year, with a net loss of $2.2 million (-$0.18 per diluted share) and an operating loss of $1.6 million. The company remained unprofitable on a full-year basis (net loss $10.2 million, or -$0.81 per share) despite improvement over the prior year's -$1.53 per share loss, and adjusted EBITDA stayed negative at -$0.6 million for the quarter. Management guided only limited forward outlook: Q1 FY2027 consolidated sales to moderately improve sequentially and year-over-year, with breakeven-to-positive adjusted EBITDA, and cited over $20 million of annualized restructuring savings. Key positives include bedding sales up 12.5% year-over-year, a $5 million inventory reduction, and a pending ~$7 million IEEPA tariff refund received in Q1 FY2027 to cut debt; the broader backdrop remains soft with upholstery sales down 2.5% and full-year revenue off 4.6%.

negative_highlights: Single-family rental segment scaled back from ~100 homes to the high-60s/low-70s units, roughly a 30% cut
Management said the housing market is not as strong as 2024 and cited a consumer confidence issue among buyers
Industrial water sales strong but below the record 2024 level
positive_highlights: Revenue of $8.2 million with $4.3 million gross profit, a 52% gross margin
Lot deliveries up almost 70% year-over-year in Q3, aided by a mild winter
Company is slightly ahead of full-year guidance of $20-32 million revenue and ~$0.50 EPS, with potential to exceed
summary: Pure Cycle reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $8.2 million and gross profit of $4.3 million, a 52% gross margin, driven by percent-complete recognition on Phase 2 lot deliveries that were pulled forward by a mild winter. Management said it is slightly ahead of its full-year guidance of $20-32 million in gross revenue and roughly $0.50 EPS, and could finish at or a bit above forecast. Lot deliveries were up almost 70% year-over-year and industrial water sales were better than expected versus last year, though management noted the housing market is not as strong as 2024 and scaled back the single-family rental build-out from about 100 to the high-60s/low-70s units. Liquidity was refreshed after the Phase 2D acceleration, with buybacks expected to increase as bond reimbursements come back over the next two years.

negative_highlights: No revenue or earnings reported; financial performance is entirely forward-looking and dependent on future milestones.
Customer contracts are primarily LOIs rather than firm offtake agreements, as customers prefer spot note models.
positive_highlights: Received additional term sheets from new lenders for the India joint venture debt financing process.
summary: Loop Industries provided a corporate update for Q1 FY2027 with no reported financial results or GAAP/Adjusted EPS figures in the transcript. Management highlighted progress on project financing and customer LOIs but noted that revenue generation is contingent upon future engineering contracts starting in September, which are not yet realized. The company maintains approximately CAD 3.6 million in liquidity as of May 31st to fund back office expenses.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened significantly from $6.8M to $38.6M due to one-time charges including digital asset fair value losses, legacy biotech impairment (Compedica), and legal costs associated with the strategic pivot.
Balance sheet showed substantial doubt at period end with only ~$700k cash on hand against ~$13M current liabilities before subsequent financing events improved liquidity to $10.3M by July 2026.
Fiscal year results reflect a company in transition rather than an operating business, as the primary revenue drivers (anchor compute contract and GAMEE) were signed/acquired after March 31st.
positive_highlights: Signed first enterprise offtake agreement: two-year contract with $32.2 million total value ($16.1M annual) and an upfront payment of $7.5 million received, bringing the company to full live status on ALPHA-01 cluster.
Acquired GAMEE for a 60% controlling interest adding 120 million registered users to the ecosystem with revenue growth continuing into the new fiscal year.
Secured qualified pipeline exceeding $200 million in annualized opportunities across AI research labs and sovereign entities, indicating strong demand despite early stage.
summary: Alpha Compute Corp reported a net loss of approximately $38.6 million for fiscal year ended March 31, 2026, driven by transition costs and legacy impairments rather than the new AI compute business which generated negligible revenue in this period due to timing differences with its first enterprise contract signed after year-end. Management clarified that reported results do not yet reflect the full scale of operations as significant contracted revenue from the anchor customer ($16.1M annual) and GAMEE acquisition sit entirely within the current fiscal year starting April 1st, leading to a going concern disclosure at period end despite subsequent cash improvements.

negative_highlights: Stock price decline noted by management despite strong fundamentals, attributed to market dynamics rather than operational issues
Processing costs per ton increased over $25 due to reagent usage for recovery optimization before normalization is expected in future quarters
No dividend or buyback declared; capital remains reinvested into expansion projects
positive_highlights: Record quarterly production exceeding 7,400 ounces driven by metallurgical upgrades and higher gold prices
Adjusted EBITDA hit a record $21 million with gross margins near 60%
Full-year guidance of 25k-30k oz already achieved as of Q3 end
summary: TRX Gold reported a record Q3 with revenue of $33 million and adjusted EBITDA of nearly $21 million, driven by gold production exceeding 7,400 ounces (up ~60% YoY) at an average realized price over $4,700/oz. Management confirmed the company has already achieved its full-year guidance range of 25,000-30,000 ounces and expects to produce towards the top end in Q4 following record throughput of 1,690 tons/day. The quarter featured significant operational improvements including recovery rates nearing 85% and normalized mining costs.

negative_highlights: Significant loan paydowns anticipated in back half requiring offsetting growth
One-time IT expenses incurred for material weakness remediation and M&A activity
Deposit costs static at ~2.3% limiting immediate margin expansion potential
positive_highlights: $3.7 million net gain recognized from oil and gas asset sale
Loan pipeline robust for Q3, expected to produce double the volume of Q2
Asset quality described as never better with strong liquidity position
summary: Management expressed strong satisfaction with Q2 FY26 results, highlighting a $3.7 million net gain from the sale of oil and gas assets which offset prior losses. The bank reported robust loan pipeline activity in Q3 expected to double Q2 fundings despite significant paydowns later in the year. Core NIM guidance for H1 is set at 4.53%-4.45%, with deposit costs stabilizing around 2.28%-2.3%.

negative_highlights: Classified non-accruals of $61.3 million plus $54.4 million in classified performing loans, with the two largest non-performers stuck in the court system.
Management said it expects 'a little bit of loss' resolving the current book and that dialing in some charge-offs 'wouldn't be wrong,' with size unknown.
Deposit pricing pressure expected to increase slightly, with funding costs likely to remain above the peer group.
positive_highlights: Net interest income grew over 4% in the quarter with NIM expanding to 3.53%, the third straight quarter of net interest income expansion.
Loan growth of over 4% in Q2 alone and 5% year-to-date, with owner-occupied real estate up $97 million over the last year.
Book value per share grew 9% year-over-year, supplemented by 207,000 shares repurchased at an average price of $24.09.
summary: MNSB reported Q2 FY2026 EPS of $0.58, net interest income growth over 4% in the quarter, NIM of 3.53%, ROAA of 0.85% and return on tangible common equity of 8.88%. Management guided to single-digit NIM movement and roughly flat margin for the remainder of the year with slightly higher funding cost pressure, while targeting 5%-7% loan growth and operating costs held at current levels through 2026. Credit is the key change versus prior periods: $54.4M in classified performing loans and $61.3M in classified non-accruals, with management acknowledging some loss is likely as the two largest non-performers move through the court system. Buybacks remain active with about $5 million left in the program but are throttled by CRE concentration.

negative_highlights: Six-week titanium production pause following two safety incidents in May, deferring roughly AUD 1.3 million of orders into Q1 FY2027; TOSHA investigation ongoing with a three-to-six month timeframe and no update
Explicit forward guidance withdrawn due to SEC Rule 135 restrictions on the confidential S-1, limiting visibility into FY2027 revenue and EBITDA breakeven
Cash fell from AUD 38.3 million to AUD 25.2 million in Q4 (pro forma AUD 29.9 million), with AUD 6.5 million used in operations, AUD 8.5 million capex, and AUD 4.4 million inventory purchases
positive_highlights: Record Q4 revenue of AUD 7.8 million, up 417% YoY, with FY2026 revenue of AUD 18.1 million landing inside the AUD 18-20 million guidance range
Contracted backlog of AUD 23.1 million (about 128% of FY2026 revenue), including AUD 8.5 million secured since 30 June and AUD 12.9 million scheduled for completion by 31 December 2026
AUD 6.5 million U.S. Department of War refractory alloy contract plus first BPMI low-rate initial production award, and EXIM credit commitment raised from $22.8 million to $26.1 million
summary: Amaero reported FY2026 revenue of AUD 18.1 million, up 376% YoY and within the AUD 18-20 million guidance range, with record Q4 revenue of AUD 7.8 million (+417% YoY) despite roughly AUD 1.3 million of titanium orders deferred by a six-week production pause. Contracted backlog stands at AUD 23.1 million, about 128% of FY2026 revenue, including AUD 8.5 million secured since 30 June, and a new AUD 6.5 million U.S. Department of War refractory alloy contract was announced. The approximately AUD 80 million three-year capital program is complete on budget, with 680 metric tons of annual powder capacity scaling to 920 metric tons in 2027. Explicit forward financial guidance was withheld under SEC Rule 135 following the confidential Form S-1 submission.

negative_highlights: A $22 million customer loan filed Chapter 11, producing a $700k net charge-off plus $75k in related legal bills and lifting NPAs to ~$22.5 million
Pipeline yields fell to the mid-to-high 6% range from ~7% cited last quarter, and loan growth missed internal expectations due to higher-than-expected payoffs
Management flagged rising deposit competition, with June spot deposit costs ~2 bps above the quarterly average and the CD roll-down benefit unlikely to repeat
positive_highlights: Net interest margin expanded 47 bps YoY and 22 bps QoQ to 3.9%, driven largely by managed-down money market and CD costs
Pre-provision net revenue of $13.6 million rose 55% YoY and more than doubled sequentially from Q1 2026
Tangible book value per share of $22.96 exceeded the $22.90 pre-acquisition level, recouping Presence Bank dilution two years ahead of estimate
summary: Norwood reported record Q2 FY2026 net income of $9.3 million, or $0.86 per diluted share, versus $6.2 million and $0.67 a year ago; net interest margin expanded 47 bps YoY and 22 bps QoQ to 3.9%, with ~$241k (~3-4 bps) of non-recurring interest income. Pre-provision net revenue reached $13.6 million, up 55% YoY, and tangible book value per share rose to $22.96, above the $22.90 pre-acquisition level, recouping the Presence Bank dilution two years early. A single $22 million customer loan filed Chapter 11 in June, driving a $700k net charge-off and a higher provision, with non-performing assets of roughly $22.5 million, about flat to Q1. Management gave no formal quarterly guidance, but noted pipeline yields have slipped to the mid-to-high 6% range versus ~7% previously and that the Q2 deposit-cost benefit is unlikely to repeat as CD specials roll off.

negative_highlights: Deposit competition described as fierce, with Direct Bank marginal cost north of 4% blunting asset sensitivity; NIM expected flat in Q3 and Q4
Buyback pace moderating sharply to ~$600 million in Q3 and ~$300 million in Q4 as CET1 nears its 10-10.5% target
Commercial Bank deposits fell $1.5 billion sequentially on anticipated early-quarter corporate outflows; Global Fund Banking growth expected to moderate
positive_highlights: Adjusted EPS of $57.09 with adjusted net income up over 20% sequentially, exceeding guidance and consensus
Full-year non-interest income guidance raised to $2.14B-$2.22B, with Q2 non-interest income up $66 million sequentially
Full-year expense guidance improved to $5.34B-$5.41B and Q2 expenses landed at the favorable end of guidance
summary: First Citizens reported Q2 FY2026 adjusted net income of $691 million and adjusted EPS of $57.09, with both adjusted ROE (12.94%) and ROA (1.18%) rising more than 20% sequentially on revenue that exceeded guidance and consensus. Net interest income rose $35 million with headline NIM up 1 bp and core NIM flat, while non-interest income rose $66 million sequentially (including $50 million of asset monetization/revaluation) versus guidance. Full-year non-interest income guidance was raised to $2.14B-$2.22B and full-year expense guidance improved to $5.34B-$5.41B, while NII was kept at midpoint ($6.6B-$6.75B) and credit guidance tightened (NCOs to 30-35 bps). Share repurchases were $600 million in the quarter, with buyback pace moderating to ~$600 million in Q3 and ~$300 million in Q4 as CET1 (10.77%) approaches the 10-10.5% target.

negative_highlights: First industry-scale facility is a few months later than originally planned
Non-cash, non-strategic impairment recorded in the quarter
Silver yield is not yet proven; pilot validation is pending
positive_highlights: Ended quarter with $31.4 million cash and no debt
Mining asset sale expected to bring $20 million in August and eliminate $1.4 million annual costs
Solar panel recycling revenue in June and July about double May's rate
summary: Comstock ended Q2 2026 with approximately $31.4 million cash, no debt, and total working capital of $39.9 million. The company expects an additional $20 million in August from the sale of legacy mining assets to Mackay Precious Metals, which will also eliminate reclamation liabilities and $1.4 million in annual costs. Metals recycling revenue ramped in June and July, with solar panel recycling revenue of $2.6 million for the first half, and the first industry-scale facility is set to begin continuous operations in August, initially at 25% capacity. Management guided to at least 25% capacity for four months and highlighted a 1-ton-per-day metal recovery pilot targeted by year-end to validate silver extraction.

negative_highlights: Organic EBITDA decreased due to deliberate gross margin investment in JAFRA Mexico
Non-recurring expenses related to Tupperware transaction hit net income
Tupperware Brazil still declined 7% YoY in June
positive_highlights: Organic revenue growth accelerated to 4.1% Q2 FY26 from 0.3% in Q1 FY26
Tupperware direct note revenue grew nearly 30% YoY in first month
Raised quarterly dividend to MXN 250 million, 26th consecutive quarter
summary: In Q2 FY2026, Betterware reported organic revenue growth of 4.1% YoY, accelerating from 0.3% in the prior quarter, with total revenue up 16.8% including the first month of Tupperware. Organic EBITDA decreased due to deliberate gross margin investment in JAFRA Mexico and non-recurring acquisition expenses, but normalized EBITDA margin was approximately 19.3%. The company raised its quarterly dividend to MXN 250 million and highlighted accretive Tupperware results, with pro forma EPS 36% higher. Guidance was not provided, but management expressed confidence in continued growth across all brands.

negative_highlights: First-half net income fell 6% to $6.0 million and EPS fell 7% to $1.46, driven by higher Q1 tariff costs
U.S. gross margin declined approximately 100 bps excluding MyMedic due to capitalized high-tariff inventory now being sold
SG&A rose to 32% of sales from 29% and first-half SG&A to 34% from 31%, due to MyMedic advertising costs; net debt increased to $27.3 million from $22.8 million
positive_highlights: Net sales rose 16% to $62.7 million, with 8% growth excluding the MyMedic acquisition
Gross margin expanded 160 bps to 42.6% from 41.0%, a record level per the analyst, driven by higher-margin MyMedic DTC mix
Europe sales grew 19% in local currency with a record quarter in both sales and earnings; Spill Magic year-to-date sales up about 30%
summary: Acme United reported Q2 FY2026 net sales of $62.7 million, up 16% from $54 million, with 8% organic growth excluding the January 2026 MyMedic acquisition. Diluted EPS rose 5% to $1.22 and net income rose 6% to $5.1 million, while gross margin expanded to 42.6% from 41.0% on MyMedic mix despite roughly 100 bps of tariff drag in the U.S. First-half net income fell 6% to $6.0 million ($1.46 per share) due to Q1 tariff costs, but management expects the impact to lessen over the next two quarters as lower-tariff inventory replaces higher-cost stock. No explicit numerical guidance was given; management pointed to continued first aid growth, resumed Westcott promotions, improving MyMedic profitability, and gross margin recovery.

negative_highlights: Deposit gathering faces fierce competition with pressure on transactional accounts and money market funds.
Commercial real estate development loans declined as borrowers became cautious due to high perceived interest rates for new projects.
Significant loan payoffs of over $200 million occurred in the first half, offsetting organic growth.
positive_highlights: Net income surged 39% year-over-year to $11.1 million driven by net interest margin expansion of 42 bps vs prior year.
Credit quality remains pristine with zero non-accruals, no OREO, and a watch list declining 50% from Q1.
Board approved an increased quarterly dividend to $0.26 per share, the highest level in company history.
summary: West Bancorporation reported a strong Q2 FY2026 with net income of $11.1 million, representing a 39% year-over-year increase and a 47% quarter-over-quarter beat against the prior period's $8 million (implied by YoY math). Net interest margin expanded 10 basis points to an implied level driven by asset repricing, while deposit costs declined slightly despite fierce competition. Management raised the quarterly dividend to $0.26 per share and maintained a pristine credit profile with zero loans past due.

negative_highlights: Outdoor seasonal business down 12% in Q2 and 17% year-to-date, described as a structural headwind.
Gross margin at 32.3% was slightly lower than 32.8% a year ago.
No new toy introductions in the second half to support holiday theatrical releases.
positive_highlights: Net sales up 17% YoY to $139.2 million in Q2.
Adjusted EBITDA up to $5.4 million, with 12-month trailing Adjusted EBITDA at $37.8 million.
Tariff refunds of $6.8 million recognized as non-operating income.
summary: Q2 net sales were $139.2 million, up 17% YoY, with Adjusted EBITDA up to $5.4 million from $2.3 million. Adjusted EPS was $0.25 versus $0.03 last year. Management noted an operating loss of $142,000, improved from a $2.8 million loss, and reiterated a front-loaded year with no new toy introductions in the second half. Tariff refunds of $6.8 million were recognized as non-operating income, but excluded from non-GAAP metrics.

negative_highlights: Specific reserve build of $5.3 million on largest office CRE credit
Core net charge-offs rose to 53 bps from 6 bps last quarter
Core OpEx burden expected to remain elevated in Q3 before normalizing
positive_highlights: Core revenue exceeded $50 million for the first time, up 40% YoY
Net interest margin expanded to 3.45% from 2.86% a year ago
Non-performers declined 36% quarter-over-quarter
summary: FRST reported Q2 FY2026 net earnings of $9.4 million or $0.38 per share, up from $2.4 million a year ago, with revenue exceeding $50 million for the first time. Net interest margin expanded to 3.45%, up from 2.86% a year ago, and non-performers declined 36%. Management highlighted $6.1 million in expected earnings improvements from core consolidation and expressed confidence in continued operating leverage.

negative_highlights: Non-interest income fell to $3.6 million (12.7% of revenue) as swap fees normalized to $572,000 from $1.6 million in Q1
End-of-period deposits were modestly lower QoQ after exiting brokered CDs, and management flagged possible upward pressure on deposit costs
New loan production is expected to moderate to $175-190 million from a record $272 million, with the lower-yielding Correspondent Banking segment (5.22% yield) a growing share of closings
positive_highlights: EPS rose 22.5% YoY to $0.49 and net interest margin expanded 22 bps QoQ to 3.49%
Efficiency ratio improved to 49.97%, below 50% for the first time and down from 52.34% in Q1
Credit quality pristine: NPLs at 0.09% of loans, net charge-offs 0.05%, classified loans down 20 bps to 30 bps
summary: USCB reported Q2 FY2026 net income of $9.1 million, or $0.49 per diluted share, up 22.5% YoY, with total assets surpassing $3 billion (up 11% YoY), loans of $2.3 billion (up 9.9% YoY), and deposits of $2.5 billion (up 5% YoY). Net interest margin expanded 22 bps to 3.49% from 3.27%, the efficiency ratio improved to 49.97% from 52.34%, and credit remained pristine with NPLs at 0.09% of loans. Management reiterated high single digit to low double digit net loan growth guidance for the back half of 2026 and guided to a 340-350 bps NIM range, with the Q2 provision of $1.3 million partly tied to record $272 million in new loan production weighted to late in the quarter. Average loans grew 15% annualized and average non-interest-bearing DDA rose 32.5% annualized, though end-of-period deposits were modestly lower as the bank deliberately exited brokered CDs in favor of lower-cost FHLB advances.

negative_highlights: Franchise same-store sales spread to company comps grew to ~600 bps; management cites variability
Portfolio optimization includes 30-35 company-owned restaurant closures in 2026
Debt reduction target of only ~$10 million for 2026, though progress noted
positive_highlights: Restaurant-level margin expanded by >400 bps YoY to over 17%, highest in 5 years
Adjusted EBITDA up ~80% in Q2, more than doubled in H1
Full-year 2026 guidance raised for revenue, margins, and adjusted EBITDA
summary: Noodles & Company reported its strongest second quarter as a public company, with restaurant-level margins expanding by over 400 basis points to over 17%, the highest in five years. Adjusted EBITDA grew about 80% in Q2 and more than doubled in the first half. Comparable sales have been positive and increasingly positive for 18 months, with Q2 company-owned comps far exceeding the Black Box index and Q3 quarter-to-date company-owned comps up approximately 10%. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance for revenue, margins, and adjusted EBITDA, and expects year-end debt at or below 3x EBITDA.

negative_highlights: Non-interest income decreased by $0.3 million quarter-over-quarter due to lower mortgage gains.
Non-interest expense guided higher to $20-$21 million per quarter going forward.
Management noted price competition on loans and disciplined pricing may temper loan growth.
positive_highlights: Net income grew 119% year-over-year to $6.7 million, with EPS of $0.57 up 129% from prior year.
Net interest margin expanded 9 bps to 2.9% and gross revenue increased 16% YoY.
No loan charge-offs for the second consecutive quarter; classified and criticized loans slightly down.
summary: First Western Financial reported Q2 2026 net income of $6.7 million and diluted EPS of $0.57, up 119% year-over-year. Net interest margin expanded 9 bps to 2.9%, and loans grew for the fifth consecutive quarter with total deposits up 12.6% YoY. Management raised guidance for quarterly non-interest expense to $20-$21 million and expects improved balance sheet growth and NIM expansion in the second half.

negative_highlights: NPLs increased due to KRW 130 billion in exposures related to the Chung Hong group workout.
SG&A expenses rose QoQ by KRW 42.8B (up 15%) primarily due to one-off voluntary retirement costs, though recurring SG&A declined.
positive_highlights: Net income surged 66% QoQ to KRW 1 trillion, regaining the quarterly level of over KRW 1T.
Non-interest income hit a record high of KRW 628.9 billion in Q2, up 20% YoY driven by capital market performance and fee businesses exceeding KRW 700B quarterly for the first time.
CET1 ratio strengthened to 13.71%, providing ample buffer above the 13% threshold required for aggressive buybacks.
summary: Woori Financial Group reported Q2 FY26 net income of KRW 1 trillion and 4.6 billion (up 66% QoQ), driven by record non-interest income of KRW 628.9 billion which increased 20% YoY. The group maintained a stable NIM at 1.51% despite rising market rates, supported by ALM optimization and core deposit expansion. Management raised the full-year share buyback target to KRW 350 billion (the largest in history) and approved an additional KRW 221 per share dividend.

negative_highlights: Broadscale application delayed, no 2027 GA at target specs
R&D resources shifted from Broadscale, slowing its development
Nine out of ten sales conversations hit sample-type limitation (tau brain-only)
positive_highlights: First revenue recognized from Baylor College and Michael J. Fox Foundation
AKT1, EGFR, and p53 oncology assays met reproducibility criteria, repeatable methodology
Proteoform assay development now capacity-limited, with expected scale to ~20 assays by mid-2028
summary: Nautilus reported its first revenue in Q2 FY2026 from Baylor College and Michael J. Fox Foundation, driven by proteoform assays. However, Broadscale application GA is delayed beyond 2027 due to insufficient assay improvements, and R&D resources are being reallocated to proteoform applications. The company expects tau and AKT1 general availability in mid-2027, with further oncology assays and ~20 proteoform assays by mid-2028.

negative_highlights: Reported operating loss of $2.8 million versus prior year profit
Revenue declined 3% year-over-year due to international conflicts
Cash balance fell to $7.6 million, partly from share repurchases and lower merchant payables
positive_highlights: Management expects 2027 EPS incremental benefit of $1.20 from membership investments
Membership fee revenue grew to $5 million and is expected to exceed 20% of revenue
Advertising revenue improved in June and July, indicating demand recovery
summary: Q2 FY2026 revenue declined 3% year-over-year to $23.2 million, with a reported operating loss of $2.8 million versus a $2.1 million profit a year earlier. Management accelerated membership spending, driving marketing costs to $4.6 million, which they expect to produce higher revenue and margins in future periods. They estimate 2027 EPS of $1.20, but clarify this is incremental benefit, not a projection. Q3 revenue growth is expected as demand improves, though international conflicts remain a temporary drag.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA margin was 27%, three points lower YoY, driven by higher operating expenses.
Accounting change created a two-point revenue headwind, affecting reported growth.
Average deal size in the pipeline is down, reflecting current market uncertainty.
positive_highlights: TRCV grew 11% YoY to $151.9 million, with Experience TRCV up mid-teens.
The Governance Institute achieved its strongest bookings in seven years and TRCV growth of nearly 10%.
Pipeline up 60% year-over-year, with sales meetings up 35%.
summary: NRC Health reported Q2 FY2026 revenue up approximately 4% YoY and 2% sequentially, with a two-point headwind from an accounting change in reputation management SKUs. TRCV grew 11% YoY to $151.9 million, with Experience TRCV up mid-teens and Governance Institute TRCV up nearly 10%. Adjusted EBITDA margin was 27%, flat with Q1, and adjusted EPS was $0.31. Management expects Q3 revenue to increase sequentially with EBITDA margin similar to H1, and Q4 margin upside.

negative_highlights: Provision expense increased to $4.7M, including $3.3M of specific reserves on legacy SBA and other isolated loans.
Pre-tax gain of $10M on fintech investment inflated reported earnings; core fee income ex-gain was up only 7%, and Q3 fee income is typically seasonally softer.
Expenses rose $2M in Q2, partly due to annual salary adjustments and incentive accruals; management expects costs to be flat or slightly lower going forward.
positive_highlights: Net interest margin expanded 43 bps sequentially (14 bps core) to 4.16% (3.87% core), driven by loan growth and funding mix.
Deposits grew 7.4% with 5.7% growth in non-interest-bearing deposits, lowering cost of funds.
Fintech momentum: 5 new partners launched in H1 (matching all of 2025), with 15 more expected in H2; new fee revenue of $2M year-to-date, with 60% coming in Q2.
summary: MVB Financial reported Q2 FY2026 net income of $12.3M ($0.93 per diluted share), up significantly from both Q1 and Q2 of last year. Core NIM expanded 14 bps to 3.87%, and net interest income rose 13% sequentially to $32.3M, though it included $2.3M of non-recurring income. Loan growth continued at 12% annualized for the fifth consecutive quarter, and deposits grew 7.4%. Management expects continued but slower NIM expansion and similar loan growth in the second half, while fintech launches are accelerating with five new partners in H1 and potentially 20 for the full year.

negative_highlights: Gross margin excluding tariff refund down 430 bps in wholesale due to sourcing and freight headwinds
Inventory down 7.1% but with $3 million expected headwind from expedited sourcing
Customer bankruptcy drove $1.1 million accounts receivable write-off
positive_highlights: Sales up 12% to $118.4M, highest since 2022
XTRATUF became the largest brand, expected to surpass $100M for the year
B2B Lehigh continued strong growth with substantial new account additions
summary: Rocky Brands reported Q2 FY2026 net sales of $118.4 million, up 12% year-over-year, with wholesale up 7.9%, retail up 21.8%, and contract manufacturing up 17.2%. GAAP EPS was $1.83, up from $0.48, partly due to a $15 million net IEEPA tariff refund benefit. Full-year guidance was raised modestly, reflecting strong demand and pre-book orders, but management remains cautious on tariff and consumer uncertainty. XTRATUF is expected to exceed $100 million in sales for the year, up 30% over last year.

negative_highlights: OEM revenue guidance implies sequential step-down in H2 due to $1-2 million order timing favorability and tough Q4 2025 comparison
Excluding Hyalofast from 2027 guidance reduces expected revenue by $3 million, reflecting continued regulatory uncertainty
Free cash flow conversion lagged in H1 due to higher AR and inventory investment, expected to improve in H2
positive_highlights: Gross margin expanded 1,400 bps in first half to 65%, driven by manufacturing productivity and mix
International revenue reached a record $12.6 million, up 22% YoY, with Cingal up 32% and Monovisc up 24%
Raised full-year adjusted EBITDA margin guidance to 13%-17% from 5%-10%, reflecting strong operating leverage
summary: Anika reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $32.6 million, up 16% YoY, with commercial channel revenue up 17% to $13.9 million and OEM up 14%. Gross margin expanded to 65% from 51%, and adjusted EBITDA rose to $7.1 million (22% margin), the strongest quarterly profitability since 2020. The company raised full-year 2026 guidance: total revenue growth to 5%-10% (from 1%-9%), OEM growth to 0%-5% (from down 5% to flat), and adjusted EBITDA margin to 13%-17% (from 5%-10%). The company also adopted a new revenue guidance practice for 2027 excluding unapproved Hyalofast sales, implying a reduction of $3 million in U.S. revenue expectations.

negative_highlights: Loans decreased by $117 million linked-quarter due to residential paydowns and integration focus.
Net interest margin declined quarter-over-quarter, though management attributes this primarily to a one-time Q1 loan income anomaly rather than structural weakness.
Management expressed caution regarding aggressive competitor pricing on large loans (e.g., 5.5% fixed rates) which may limit organic growth opportunities.
positive_highlights: Net income increased 20% YoY to $162 million driven by Stellar integration and margin expansion.
Stellar Bancorp delivered strong adjusted pre-tax core income of $42.1 million in the quarter.
Non-interest expense normalized significantly with an efficiency ratio improving to 46% from Q1's 59.2%.
summary: Prosperity Bancshares reported Q2 FY2026 net income of $162 million and diluted EPS of $1.62, excluding one-time merger gains from Stellar Bancorp which contributed approximately $33 million in adjusted net income. Net interest margin expanded to 3.47% YoY but declined slightly quarter-over-quarter due to a prior period anomaly; management maintains guidance for NIMs between 3.70%-3.85%. Loan growth was flat linked-quarter as paydowns offset new originations, while deposit costs remained stable.

negative_highlights: Negative commentary on macro: ABI down 41 months, 'longest downturn'
DynaEnergetics margin down from 13.4% to 8.4% on pricing/mix, only benefiting from tariff refund
NobelClad sales decreased 17% YoY on weak oil and gas
positive_highlights: Consolidated sales at high end of guidance and adjusted EBITDA above high end
Arcadia sales up 9% YoY and 19% sequentially, EBITDA best in over a year
Q3 guidance implies sequential improvement across all segments
summary: Q2 FY2026 revenue of $157 million hit the high end of guidance, and adjusted EBITDA of $10.7 million beat the high end, driven by Arcadia's 9% YoY and 19% sequential sales growth and margin expansion to 13.6%. DynaEnergetics was flat YoY but improved sequentially with a $1.5 million tariff refund; NobelClad sales fell 17% YoY but rose 15% sequentially. Q3 guidance is $158-168 million sales and $10-13 million EBITDA, with no tariff refunds assumed. Management emphasized continued end-market headwinds and discussed the upcoming put/call option on the remaining 40% Arcadia stake.

negative_highlights: Distilling Solutions sales down 42% with brown goods down 59%
Ingredient Solutions gross margin only 10.1% due to waste starch costs
RNDC bankruptcy created financial impact and ongoing distributor transitions
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA and EPS ahead of expectations
Branded Spirits ex other products up 3%, premium plus up 5% vs industry declines
Penelope up 13%, Yellowstone up 54%, Everclear up 13%
summary: Q2 FY2026 sales fell to $124.4M with adjusted EBITDA of $27.6M and adjusted EPS of $0.72, both above expectations though down YoY. Branded Spirits sales ex other products rose 3% with premium plus up 5%; Ingredient Solutions grew 2%, while Distilling Solutions sales dropped 42% due to oversupply. Management guided to higher putaway in H2, raised digital A&P to 15%, and rationalized 52 brands representing 47% of SKUs.

negative_highlights: Cost pressures persist, notably in ink due to Middle East supply chain issues
USPS postage increase up to 10% for mailing clients effective July 12
Global shipping and logistics costs elevated due to Strait of Hormuz security concerns
positive_highlights: Net sales increased compared to the second quarter of 2025
Strong free cash flow generated in the second quarter
Packaging business expected to grow in 2026; new Salt Lake City facility to open in Q4
summary: Quad's Q2 FY2026 results were in line with expectations and full-year guidance is reaffirmed. Net sales increased versus prior year, and strong free cash flow supported returning $13 million to shareholders. The company is expanding its packaging business with a new Salt Lake City facility and growing its in-store retail media network with new retailer wins and expansions. Management continues to manage cost pressures from ink and postage, while pursuing long-term growth initiatives.

negative_highlights: Fiscal 2026 revenue fell to $4.1 million from $5.9 million in the prior year
Gross loss of $8.1 million versus gross profit of $1.7 million a year earlier, reflecting project mix and low-margin strategic contracts
Net loss widened to $43.7 million from $21.5 million, and net cash used in operating activities rose to approximately $22.7 million from $18.6 million
positive_highlights: Record backlog of $19.8 million, up 58% from $12.5 million at the prior fiscal year-end
Largest deployment and recurring revenue contract in company history secured; approximately $6.5 million of pipeline tied to the U.S. Coast Guard project with a 15-month period of performance
Sales pipeline grew to $142.3 million from $137.5 million a year ago; combined cash, equivalents, and note weakness in-term investments increased to $8.7 million from $6.7 million
summary: Ocean Power Technologies reported fiscal 2026 revenue of $4.1 million, down from $5.9 million a year ago, and swung from gross profit of $1.7 million to a gross loss of $8.1 million due to project mix and strategic contracts accepted at lower margins. Net loss widened to $43.7 million from $21.5 million, with operating expenses of $31.7 million versus $23.3 million including $9.5 million of non-cash stock-based compensation. Offsetting the results, backlog rose 58% to a record $19.8 million, the sales pipeline was $142.3 million versus $137.5 million, and the company closed with $8.7 million in cash and short-term investments, down from $22.7 million of operating cash burn during the year. Management framed fiscal 2027 as a year of execution on backlog and recurring revenue, and noted a reverse stock split request to preserve the NYSE American listing.

negative_highlights: DE of $0.23 per share landed at the low end of guidance, down $0.01 from Q1, as $75 million of production was offset by $85 million of repayments
CECL reserve rose 60 bps to 190 bps of commitments, with a $4.9 million increase from two office loans maturing in 2026
Dividend of $0.28 per share remains uncovered for a second consecutive quarter, with coverage only expected by year-end
positive_highlights: Originations year-to-date executed at 1.86% net interest margin, the highest level in four years
Portfolio grew roughly $65 million year-to-date to about $790 million, with seven term sheets outstanding totaling approximately $300 million
Legacy office exposure fell from 24% at year-end to 19%, with the $44 million Dallas office loan expected to be paid off at maturity
summary: Seven Hills reported Q2 FY2026 distributable earnings of $5.1 million, or $0.23 per share, at the low end of guidance and down $0.01 from Q1, driven by loan closings slipping later in the quarter. Q3 DE guidance was set at $0.23-$0.25, and management reiterated the full-year portfolio target of $950-$960 million and expectations to cover the $0.28 quarterly dividend by year-end. The CECL reserve rose 60 bps to 190 bps of total commitments, with a $4.9 million increase tied to two office loans maturing in 2026, though all loans remain current with no realized losses and a 2.9 weighted average risk rating.

negative_highlights: EPS of $0.15 was below management expectations, with core provision of $6 million and net charge-offs of $5.2 million above the $4-5 million guided range
Prior guidance of ~$217 million in credit-enhanced balances by year-end 2026 was withdrawn
SBA net charge-offs rose to $2.9 million from $2.2 million, with management flagging elevated charge-offs over the next few quarters
positive_highlights: Originations of $1.6 billion beat the $1.4 billion guidance and were up roughly 8% year-over-year
Net interest margin expanded to 13.69% from 12.90% sequentially, and net interest income rose to $28.7 million from $28.1 million
Non-performing loans fell to ~$38 million from nearly $50 million, with ~$19 million federally guaranteed
summary: FinWise reported Q2 FY2026 net income of $2.1 million and EPS of $0.15, which management said was short of expectations, driven by a $6 million core provision and $5.2 million in non-credit-enhanced net charge-offs, slightly above the $4-5 million guided range. Net interest income rose to $28.7 million from $28.1 million and NIM expanded to 13.69% from 12.90%, while originations of $1.6 billion beat the $1.4 billion guide. Prior credit-enhanced balance guidance of ~$217 million by year-end 2026 was withdrawn due to the Tallied restructuring, though management said net charge-offs may see at $4-5 million and Q1 2026 is a reasonable proxy for Q3 and Q4 earnings.

negative_highlights: Revenue guidance midpoint lowered to $136M from prior, with management citing a 'more cautious approach'
GAAP net income fell to $4.1M ($0.20) from $4.6M ($0.22) a year ago
Deals taking longer to close and customers favoring shorter terms with termination-for-convenience clauses, compressing near-term revenue
positive_highlights: Adjusted EPS rose to $0.25 from $0.19 a year ago after excluding $1.5M severance/restructuring and a prior-year $700K gain
Software license revenue jumped to $3.6M from $2.4M, and managed professional services revenue rose 53% to $2.3M
Adjusted operating expense fell nearly 8% to $27.1M, with G&A down nearly 14% and note/marketing down nearly 10%
summary: Spok reported Q2 FY2026 GAAP net income of $4.1M ($0.20/diluted share), down from $4.6M ($0.22) a year ago, though adjusting for a $1.5M severance/restructuring charge and a prior-year $700K domain-sale gain, adjusted EPS rose to $0.25 from $0.19. Adjusted operating expense fell nearly 8% to $27.1M, software revenue grew over 3% with license revenue of $3.6M vs $2.4M, managed professional services rose 53%, and adjusted EBITDA hit a record; cash was $16.6M at quarter-end. Guidance was slightly lowered at the midpoint: total revenue now $132.5M-$139.5M (midpoint $136M) with wireless $67M-$70M and software $65.5M-$69.5M, while adjusted EBITDA midpoint held at $30M ($28M-$32M). Management cited longer deal cycles and customers favoring shorter terms amid tight hospital budgets; a separate spectrum license sale to Sensus USA for $8M closed July 20 with roughly $7M net cash expected in Q3.

negative_highlights: Total revenue down 5% YoY, with U.S. down 4%
International revenue down 6% due to China suspension
Second consecutive quarter of revenue decline; expects typical Q3 seasonality
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA loss improved nearly 40% to $5.1 million from $8.4 million
Gross margin expanded to 78% from 72% YoY
China registration renewed, shipments expected to resume by early 2027
summary: Pulmonx reported Q2 2026 revenue of $22.8 million, down 5% YoY and 6% constant currency, in line with expectations. U.S. revenue declined 4% YoY but rose 7% sequentially, with 12 new treating centers; international ex-China grew 9% constant currency. Adjusted EBITDA loss improved nearly 40% to $5.1 million, and net loss narrowed to $10.1 million. Full-year revenue guidance was reiterated at $90-$92 million, while operating expense guidance was reduced to $109-$111 million.

negative_highlights: Insurance segment underwriting income was only $27 million due to $201 million of net catastrophe losses, primarily Iran conflict
Reinsurance net premiums written fell 10.4% YoY and insurance net premiums written fell 5.1% YoY amid a softening market
Property CAT rates declined in the mid-teens at mid-year renewals, pressuring reinsurance top-line and margins
positive_highlights: Reinsurance underwriting income of $410 million with a 79.9% ex-CAT accident year combined ratio
Share repurchases of $1.2 billion in the quarter and $1.95 billion in H1, roughly 94% of H1 net income
Mortgage segment delivered $220 million of underwriting income with USMI delinquency flat at 2.1%
summary: Arch reported Q2 2026 after-tax operating income of $893 million, or $2.56 per share, with an ex-CAT accident year combined ratio of 82.5% (up 160 bps YoY) and book value per share up 2.8% in the quarter. The reinsurance segment posted $410 million of underwriting income despite net premiums written falling 10.4% YoY, while insurance underwriting income was only $27 million due to Iran-conflict catastrophe losses and net premiums written declined 5.1%; mortgage delivered $220 million of underwriting income with a flat 2.1% USMI delinquency rate. Management described an increasingly competitive, early-stage softening market with property CAT rates down mid-teens, continued discipline in casualty, and no formal guidance change; the company repurchased 12.4 million shares for $1.2 billion, about 94% of H1 net income.

negative_highlights: Net interest margin declined to 3.78% due to funding costs and loan yield compression
Provision expense increased by $2.8 million sequentially, driven by higher non-performing assets
Credit card transactions declined to $84.2 million following operator restrictions on card usage
positive_highlights: SBA originations reached $131.4 million with retained yields of 8.01%
Gain on sale income rose to $9.3 million from $5.1 million in the prior-year period
New BVNKROLL partnership with AXES expected to drive scalability
summary: In Q2 FY2026, GBank reported strong SBA loan production of $131.4 million, with $61.3 million retained at an average yield of 8.01%, and gain on sale income rose from $5.1 million to $9.3 million for the first six months. However, net interest margin fell to 3.78%, and provision expense increased $2.8 million due to elevated non-performing assets, including SBA hotel loans and retail credit card delinquencies. Management provided no formal guidance but noted near-term allowance levels may remain elevated while fundamental credit quality is better than reported due to SBA guarantees. The company also highlighted new gaming fintech initiatives, including a BVNKROLL partnership with AXES and a Visa Prepaid Card planned for Q4 launch.

negative_highlights: GMV lines down modestly sequentially in Q2 vs Q1
Cash flow positivity not expected until mid-2027
Revenue growth expected to soften from triple-digit rates
positive_highlights: Revenue up 108% YoY and 136% for the first half
Non-GAAP operating income turned positive to +$400,000 from -$2.7M loss
Operating cash burn cut 52% YoY
summary: PSQH reported Q2 FY2026 revenue up 108% YoY, with non-GAAP operating income turning positive at +$400,000 versus a -$2.7M loss a year ago. The company divested EveryLife for $5.5M in cash and is affirming full-year 2026 revenue of about $32M with positive non-GAAP operating income, targeting operating cash flow positivity in 2027. Payments volume grew 153% YoY, while credit GMV grew 32% YoY. Management emphasized disciplined cost cuts and a focus on core fintech operations.

negative_highlights: Loss ratio increased 0.5 percentage point due to mix shift toward higher loss-ratio brokerage channel
Net written premiums growth (30.8%) lagged gross premium growth, reflecting lower retention in the quarter
positive_highlights: Gross written premiums grew 23.4% YoY to record levels
Combined ratio improved 3 points YoY to 85.9%
Operating expense ratio declined 2.9 points YoY to 9.5%
summary: Ategrity reported record Q2 FY26 results with gross written premiums growing 23.4% YoY and underwriting income rising 66.9%. The combined ratio improved to 85.9%, driven by an operating expense ratio decline to 9.5% despite a slight loss ratio increase of 0.5 pp due to mix shifts toward the brokerage channel. Management raised Q3 guidance for gross written premium growth (expecting >20 pts above market) and combined ratio improvement, citing strong momentum in property and casualty.
