negative_highlights: Loss before tax of $7 million includes significant interest expense payments, including one-off charges exceeding $3 million on convertible notes.
Fair value gains on warrants and deferred consideration were recorded due to a reduction in share price.
Framework Agreement signing is contingent on finalizing the joint financial model linked to the strategic investment consortium.
positive_highlights: Cash balance strengthened to $37.3 million from $21.1 million at end of December 2025.
Operating cash flows significantly improved year-over-year due to external client work by Simulus Group and streamlined corporate overhead.
Strategic funding process advanced with a preferred partner selected and discussions in the final phase.
summary: Lifezone Metals reported a loss before tax of $7 million for H1 2026, translating to an approximate loss of $0.08 per share, driven by high interest charges and one-off expenses related to convertible notes. The company strengthened its balance sheet with cash ending at $37.3 million following a $23.3 million equity raise and partial drawdown of a bridge facility. Management provided no financial guidance for the full year but confirmed that strategic funding discussions are in the final phase, with an announcement expected in the near term.

negative_highlights: Organic growth decelerated to 5% in Q2 from 7% in Q1, and implied FY midpoint implies ~7% versus the stated double-digit organic target
Net loss of $4.4M on a GAAP basis and $68.9M total debt against $19.7M cash
Back-half non-recurring revenue guided to ~$5-6M versus ~$10M last year, muting total growth; no M&A or large tax deals included in guidance
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA up 48% YoY to $7.7M, with margin expanding 400 bps to 21%
Revenue grew 23% YoY to $37.1M and recurring revenue rose 19% to $34M (91% of total)
Vensure milestone: 2 million supported employees now live on the enterprise payroll tax platform; core HCM payroll bookings up 14% YoY
summary: ASUR reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $37.1M, up 23% YoY, with organic growth of 5% (down from 7% in Q1 on seasonality). Adjusted EBITDA rose 48% to $7.7M and adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 400 bps to 21%; GAAP gross margin was 68% vs 66%, while net loss narrowed to $4.4M from $6.1M. Full-year 2026 revenue guidance is $159M-$163M at 24%-25% adjusted EBITDA margins, with Q3 revenue of $38M-$40M and adjusted EBITDA of $8M-$10M; management noted the back half faces a roughly $4-5M non-recurring revenue headwind versus last year's ~$10M. Tone was confident, citing a 2M-employee Vensure go-live, majority of ~30,000 direct clients on Asure Central, and a 14% rise in core HCM payroll bookings.

negative_highlights: The $13.2 million EBITDA and operating income include approximately $9.9 million of non-recurring tariff recoveries, so underlying operating results are materially lower than headline profitability
Total cash flow from operations fell to $8.7 million from $13.3 million YoY on increased working capital use
SG&A rose $2.2 million YoY to $12.5 million from acquired businesses and higher variable compensation, and management flagged freight, commodity and tariff cost pressure plus macro headwinds
positive_highlights: Net sales grew 6% YoY to $57.7 million on new archery products, the Gold Tip acquisition, and strength in safety, table tennis and basketball
Gross margin expanded 146 bps to 26.2% from 24.7% on better absorption, operating leverage and favorable mix including the accretive Gold Tip acquisition
summary: Escalade reported Q2 FY2026 net sales of $57.7 million, up 6% YoY, with net income of $9.4 million or $0.68 per diluted share and gross margin expanding 146 bps to 26.2% from 24.7%. EBITDA rose $9.3 million to $13.2 million, but roughly $9.9 million of that came from non-recurring recovery of tariffs paid in prior quarters, which also flowed into operating income. No formal guidance was given; management said it expects inventory to decline further in the second half and does not plan near-term price increases, using the tariff refund to offset freight and commodity costs and fund incremental Q3/Q4 promotions. Operating cash flow fell to $8.7 million from $13.3 million on higher working capital use, while debt was reduced $1.8 million and cash rose to $16.4 million, moving to a net cash position.

CMTG reported a Q2 2026 GAAP net loss of $1.81 per share and a distributable loss of $0.63 per share ($0.07 prior to realized gains/losses), driven by $183 million of incremental specific CECL provisions ($1.26 per share) on office and Sun Belt multifamily loans plus a $30 million loss on two REO assets moved to held-for-sale. Book value fell to $8.58 per share and net debt-to-equity rose to 2.0x from 1.7x, though pro forma leverage is 1.7x after July resolutions and liquidity rose to $168 million from $116 million. Management said it 'largely turned the corner' and expects to be able to make capital allocation decisions in coming quarters, with new originations possible in late 2026 or early 2027, but declined to indicate where book value might trough. Watchlist loans declined to $1.1 billion from $1.7 billion at year-end 2025 and $2.7 billion at year-end 2024, with $1 billion of loan resolutions year to date.

negative_highlights: Commission income fell significantly due to the divestiture of non-core operations and portfolio realignment.
positive_highlights: Operating expenses decreased approximately 28% year-over-year to improve cost structure.
summary: Commission income declined to $2.1 million from $3.1 million in the prior year quarter due to portfolio realignment and divestitures of non-core operations. Net loss improved to $2 million compared with a net loss of $2.7 million, driven by reduced operating expenses (down 28% YoY) and lower share-based compensation. Management provided no specific financial guidance for future quarters.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA declined to $10.5 million (9.5% of revenue) from $14 million (13.4%) a year ago
Billings fell 8.8% YoY to $100.9 million, with the company citing renewal timing differences
Non-GAAP EPS dropped to $0.06 from $0.08, and sales & marketing expense rose to 37.6% of revenue from 35.5% a year ago
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 6.7% YoY to $111.1 million, with adjusted revenue excluding PeopleSoft up 10%
Gross margin expanded to 60.9% (up 190 bps sequentially) and ARR ex-PeopleSoft rose 8.1% YoY to $401.1 million
Closed 14 new client transactions over $1M TCV totaling $30M and added 58 new logos in Q2
summary: Rimini Street reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $111.1 million, up 6.7% YoY (10% excluding PeopleSoft), with GAAP EPS of $0.03 and non-GAAP EPS of $0.06 vs $0.08 a year ago. Gross margin expanded to 60.9% (up 190 bps sequentially), but adjusted EBITDA fell to $10.5 million (9.5% of revenue) from $14 million (13.4%) a year ago, and billings declined 8.8% YoY. The company reiterated FY2026 guidance of 4–6% revenue growth and 12.5–15.5% adjusted EBITDA margins (Rule of 20) and guided Q3 revenue to $110–112 million. The quarter showed continued new logo additions and ARR growth, but profitability metrics weakened versus the prior-year period, which included a one-time Oracle settlement gain.

negative_highlights: Full-year revenue guidance cut by $30 million to $375-395 million, only ~0-5% growth versus 2025
RUCONEST revenue fell 10% year-over-year to $72.3 million and total revenue declined 3% to $90.2 million
Operating cash flow was an outflow of $9.7 million and cash fell $12.3 million sequentially to $159.5 million
positive_highlights: Joenja revenue grew 40% year-over-year to $17.9 million, with international revenue up 150% to $2.5 million
RUCONEST active patient base held at 93% of prior-year levels and new enrollments rose to 84 from ~50 in Q1
$15 million reduction in full-year opex guidance to $315-320 million, with adjusted H1 opex up just 1% despite $13 million higher R&D
summary: Q2 FY2026 total revenue was $90.2 million, down 3% year-over-year, with RUCONEST declining 10% to $72.3 million and Joenja growing 40% to $17.9 million. Full-year revenue guidance was cut by $30 million to $375-395 million (roughly 0-5% growth versus 2025), while full-year opex guidance was reduced by $15 million to $315-320 million. Q2 operating profit and adjusted operating profit were both positive, but adjusted operating profit fell $5 million year-over-year and operating cash flow was an outflow of $9.7 million, leaving cash and marketable securities at $159.5 million. Management emphasized RUCONEST patient-base resilience at 93% of prior-year levels and a return to growth in H2 2026, alongside upcoming Joenja catalysts including an October 24 pediatric PDUFA date, a Japan launch, and Q4 phase II CVID/PID data.

negative_highlights: Net premiums earned decreased 4% to $222.6 million driven by lower rate increases and retention levels
Expense ratio increased to 35.8%, breaking the recent trajectory of decreasing expenses due to legacy system costs and incentives
Commercial lines growth slowed with a real exposure increase excluding workers' comp dropping to 7.8%
positive_highlights: Net premiums written decreased only 3.2% compared to prior year
Commercial lines new business premium growth goals were achieved for H1 2026 despite competitive pressures
Personal auto loss ratio deterioration was offset by favorable weather impacts and reserve development
summary: Net premiums earned decreased 4% to $222.6 million and net income was up 32% year-over-year due to investment gains despite a higher expense ratio of 35.8%. Management noted that the combined ratio improved primarily from lower weather losses, but acknowledged softening market conditions impacting rate achievement and retention.

negative_highlights: GAAP net loss of $12.5 million, or $1.87 per share, and EAD loss of $0.74 per share versus a $0.02 gain in Q1
GAAP book value per share fell to $26.76 from $29.98 at March 31
Loan portfolio declined $74.9 million net as $92.7 million of payoffs dwarfed $17.8 million of fundings, and CECL reserves rose $1.7 million
positive_highlights: Net interest income rose $1.3 million to $10.5 million, helped by a full quarter of the new CRE securitization
Approximately 99% of votes cast favored the internalization share issuance, with employees to own 40-plus percent of common stock pro forma
Management reiterated its $500 million net growth target for 2026 and called the pipeline 'stronger than ever'
summary: ACR reported a Q2 GAAP net loss of $12.5 million, or $1.87 per share, driven largely by $5.1 million of internalization transaction costs and $4.0 million of accelerated vesting comp; EAD was a loss of $0.74 per share versus a gain of $0.02 in Q1, though EAD would have been $0.14 excluding $5.5 million of deal costs and $984K of accelerated deferred debt costs. Net interest income rose $1.3 million to $10.5 million on a full quarter of the new CRE securitization, but CECL reserves increased $1.7 million and book value fell to $26.76 from $29.98. The loan portfolio shrank $74.9 million net on $92.7 million of payoffs against $17.8 million of fundings, and management reiterated its target of $500 million of net 2026 growth while flagging additional (but lower) transaction costs in Q3. Weighted average risk rating ticked up to 2.6 from 2.5 and REO hotel sales remain stalled on labor union issues.

negative_highlights: Net income fell to $7.4M ($0.31/diluted share) from $11.1M ($0.46) a year ago
Net interest margin compressed 15 bps YoY and 6 bps QoQ to 7.94% as average cost of borrowings rose to 4.32% from 4.20%
Operating costs rose to $25M from $21.5M a year ago; recreation charge-offs stayed elevated at 3.14%
positive_highlights: Home improvement originations hit a record $128.6M, up over twofold YoY, with active contractors up to 800 from 700
Recreation originations of $228.5M were a quarterly record, up 60% YoY, with growth continuing through July
Dividend raised 16.7% QoQ to $0.14 per share and ~780,000 shares repurchased below book and tangible book value
summary: Record originations (home improvement $128.6M, up over twofold YoY; recreation $228.5M, up 60%) drove loan growth to $2.79B, up 12% YoY and 7% QoQ, and record net interest income of $57.2M, up 7% YoY, with NIM at 7.94% (down 15 bps YoY). But net income fell to $7.4M, or $0.31 per diluted share, from $11.1M or $0.46 a year ago, held back by ~$6.5M of day-one provisioning (~$0.18/share) on growth and a $5.9M swing in equity-investment gains. Provision was $22.3M versus $21.6M a year ago; recreation net charge-offs were 3.14% versus 3.11%, home improvement improved to 1.37% from 1.87%. Management reiterated mid-teens full-year loan growth, raised the quarterly dividend 16.7% to $0.14, and repurchased ~780,000 shares.

negative_highlights: Net charge-offs in franchise finance remained elevated at $11.6 million
Linked quarter revenue declined due to lower gain on sale revenue
Average loan balances down 1% sequentially due to paydowns
positive_highlights: Non-performing loans declined sequentially to 1.58% from 1.63%
Total delinquencies fell 26% from Q1 to $29.1 million
Fintech fee revenue up 222% trailing twelve months
summary: First Internet Bancorp reported Q2 2026 net income of $2.4 million or $0.27 per diluted share, with total revenue up 23% year-over-year to $41.1 million and pre-provision net revenue up 28% to $15 million. Provision for credit losses declined sequentially to $13.4 million from $16.3 million, while total delinquencies fell 26% from Q1 to $29.1 million (78 bps of performing loans). Management highlighted a credit inflection point, with SBA charge-offs down nearly 50% sequentially and expectations for continued credit improvement and stronger H2 origination volumes.

negative_highlights: Same-property NOI of $88.6 million grew only 2% YoY, held back by a one-time bad debt reserve on a Hawaii tenant; 2Q normalized FFO of $0.31 landed at the low end of prior quarterly guidance
Net debt to total assets rose to 69.2% and net debt leverage remains 11.5x, which management characterized as elevated
CAD payout ratio rose to 50% from 29% on elevated leasing commissions, and the Hawaii ground lease carries a three-year free-rent period before cash rent begins
positive_highlights: Record 5.4 million sq ft leased at 35% GAAP / 14% cash spreads, seventh consecutive quarter of double-digit rent growth and fifth straight quarter of accelerating mark-to-market
Occupancy rose 450 bps to 99%, 590 bps above the national industrial average, after resolving the Indianapolis FedEx lease and the 2.2 million sq ft Hawaii ground lease
Full-year 2026 normalized FFO guidance raised $0.05 at the midpoint to $1.31-$1.39; adjusted EBITDAre guidance raised $4 million to $348-$353 million; dividend doubled to $0.10 per share
summary: ILPT reported Q2 2026 normalized FFO of $20.8 million, or $0.31 per share, up 51% YoY and in line with guidance; same-property Cash Basis NOI rose 2% (3.8% excluding a Hawaii bad debt reserve) and adjusted EBITDAre rose 3% to $87.4 million. The company completed a record 5.4 million sq ft of leasing at 35% GAAP and 14% cash spreads, drove consolidated occupancy up 450 bps to 99% by resolving its two large vacancies (FedEx Indianapolis lease; Hawaii ground lease), and refinanced $1.6 billion of floating-rate JV debt into fixed rate at 5.71%, leaving all consolidated debt fixed with no maturities until 2029. Full-year 2026 normalized FFO guidance was raised $0.05 at the midpoint to $1.31-$1.39 per share and adjusted EBITDAre guidance raised $4 million at the midpoint to $348-$353 million; the quarterly dividend was doubled to $0.10 per share.

negative_highlights: Daily operating expenses increased to $6,396 from $5,944 due to higher crew-related costs and maintenance
Fleet size decreased slightly to an average of 36 vessels compared to 37 in the prior year quarter following a vessel sale
positive_highlights: Time charter revenue increased to $57.3M from $54.7M in Q2 2025
Fleet time charter equivalent rate rose 7% year-over-year to $16,581 per day
Secured $94.7 million of contracted revenues for the remainder of 2026 at an average daily rate of approximately $18,337
summary: Diana Shipping reported a strong Q2 FY2026 with time charter revenues increasing to $57.3 million from $54.7 million in the prior year period and net income rising to $19.3 million compared to $3.1 million previously, driven by higher rates of $18,350 for a new Ultramax charter and an overall fleet time charter equivalent rate increase of 7% to $16,581 per day. The company maintained near-full utilization at 99.6%, secured approximately $94.7 million in contracted revenues for the remainder of 2026 representing 88% of ownership days, and declared a quarterly cash dividend of $0.01 per share.

negative_highlights: Non-performing loans rose $2.7 million to $13.1 million, or 1.18% of gross loans, from 0.94% in Q1, driven by two relationships moving to non-accrual
Net interest income grew only $57,000 sequentially and NIM contracted 2 bps to 4.22%; average loans declined $3.2 million and tax-equivalent loan yield fell to 6.31% partly on the nonaccrual increase

Non-interest expense rose $63,000 to $12.0 million, including $487,000 of professional fees tied to forensic accounting and one-time legal costs from previously disclosed fraudulent activity by a non-executive officer
positive_highlights: Record revenue of $19.2 million, with non-interest income up $331,000 QoQ to $4.1 million on a $356,000 increase in gain on sale of loans
Core deposits grew $11.0 million (3.4% annualized) including a $12.8 million rise in non-interest-bearing deposits; total cost of deposits improved to 1.3%
Tangible book value per share rose to $21.76 (16.8% annualized linked-quarter growth) and the board declared a $0.21 dividend, the 100th consecutive quarterly cash dividend
summary: Landmark reported Q2 FY2026 record revenue of $19.2 million, net income of $5.4 million (up from $5.1 million in Q1), EPS of $0.88, ROAA of 1.35% and ROAE of 13.23%. Net interest income of $15.1 million rose just $57,000 sequentially, NIM slipped 2 bps to 4.22% on a tax-equivalent basis, and gross loans grew $4.4 million to about $1.1 billion while average loans fell $3.2 million. Non-performing loans jumped $2.7 million to $13.1 million (1.18% of gross loans) on two borrower relationships migrated to non-accrual, and net charge-offs rose to 0.17% of average loans from 0.13%. Management gave no formal numeric guidance, calling the H2 growth outlook 'cautiously optimistic' and guiding to holding the margin near the 420 area, while noting $28.7 million of the deposit decline came from brokered deposits and core deposits grew $11.0 million.

negative_highlights: Customer caution and conservative spending due to elevated oil and gas prices
EMEA margin pressure due to timing lag between surcharge implementation and input cost increases
North America PPS volume was a slight detractor due to tough comparison
positive_highlights: Automation revenue increased 139% year-over-year on a constant currency basis
Consolidated net revenue up 12.2% constant currency, with North America up 8.5% and Europe/APAC up 15.4%
Gross margin improved 150 basis points versus prior year
summary: Ranpak reported Q2 FY2026 consolidated net revenue up 12.2% constant currency (14% reported), with automation revenue surging 139% year-over-year constant currency. Adjusted EBITDA rose 13.9% constant currency to $19.1 million, with gross margin up 150 bps year-over-year. Management reiterated full-year automation revenue target of ~$60 million and automation adjusted EBITDA breakeven by year-end, while noting macro uncertainty and a temporary European surcharge to offset input costs.

negative_highlights: July completion factor of 91% below winter storm lows
Weather disruption impacting Q3 start
Integration costs and duplicative overheads persist until early 2028
positive_highlights: Adjusted EPS of $0.89 and revenue up 8% sequentially on 7% higher block hours
Full-year guidance raised on block hours, revenue, and adjusted EBITDAR
Integration ahead of schedule with FAA approval on first revision cycle
summary: Republic Airways reported Q2 2026 adjusted net income of $41 million ($0.89 per diluted share) on revenue of approximately $571 million, up 8% sequentially as block hour production rose 7%. The company raised full-year guidance: block hours to ~880,000 (from at least 865,000), revenue to >$2.1 billion (from >$2 billion), and adjusted EBITDAR to $395-$405 million (from >$380 million). July weather has hurt completion factor to 91%, but management remains confident, citing strong partner demand and ahead-of-schedule Mesa integration. Integration benefits are expected to materialize in late 2027 into 2028.

negative_highlights: Revenue fell note weakness in of expectations at $3.0 million versus prior year's $3.9 million
Gross margin declined significantly from 49.9% to 46.4%
Operating loss widened to $1.2 million compared to $687,000 in the same quarter last year
positive_highlights: Still a preferred supplier to Shopify despite overall retail decline
No going concern issue raised by auditors
Industrial scanning business grew to ~10% of Q2 revenue with direct enterprise sales gaining traction
summary: Socket Mobile reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $3.0 million, a decline from the prior year's $3.9 million and missing expectations due to challenges in its retail scanning business. Gross margin contracted to 46.4% from 49.9%, driven by underutilized manufacturing capacity, resulting in an operating loss of $1.2 million compared to a smaller loss previously. Management confirmed continued cost-cutting measures including headcount reductions and highlighted the growing industrial segment which contributed approximately 10% of revenue.

negative_highlights: Revenue decreased 4% due to lower unit volumes and a difficult prior-year comparison for pre-owned revenue which was up 18%
Service parts and other revenue declined 13%, primarily reflecting the impact of the Ocean Bio-Chem sale
Full-year guidance narrowed with expectations that same-store sales will be down low to mid-single digits
positive_highlights: Gross margin expanded 70 basis points to 24% driven by favorable product mix and exiting brands with lower margins in prior year
Adjusted net leverage improved significantly from 5.8x trailing EBITDA at the end of last year to 3.7x, achieving the target under four times ahead of schedule
Same-store sales declined only 2%, outperforming an industry that is down high single digits
summary: Revenue declined 4% year-over-year to $531 million while gross margin expanded 70 basis points to 24%. Management updated and narrowed full-year guidance for revenue ($1.75B-$1.8B) and adjusted EBITDA, citing a challenging retail environment where the industry is expected to be down high single digits.

negative_highlights: Credit and occupancy loss guidance assumes 25 basis points, though year-to-date actuals at 10 basis points
Rising interest rates and macro uncertainty noted as risks
positive_highlights: Record quarterly investment volume of over $500 million
AFFO per share up 7.4% year-over-year and guidance raised
Occupancy at record 99.8%, recapture rate 105%
summary: Agree Realty reported record Q2 2026 investment volume of over $500 million across its three platforms, with acquisitions of $451 million at a 7% cap rate and 73% investment-grade tenants. Core FFO per share rose 7.5% to $1.13 and AFFO per share rose 7.4% to $1.14. Full-year AFFO guidance was raised to $4.57-$4.59 and investment volume guidance to $1.6-$1.8 billion. Occupancy set a record at 99.8%, and the company executed 1.6 million square feet of leases in the first half at a 105% recapture rate.

negative_highlights: Temporary loss of ~10% of upstream production due to Middle East conflict
Global diesel and chemical supply constrained; Strait closure removing ~3M bpd refining capacity
Cash opex held flat year-over-year only by offsetting inflation with cost savings
positive_highlights: Earnings of $14.5B and cash flow from operations of $23.6B despite 10% upstream production loss
Guyana production ~900k bpd and Errea Wittu FPSO on schedule; capital recovery accelerated two years
Chemical margins up ~180% QoQ; specialty products record earnings; cumulative cost savings $16.3B
summary: ExxonMobil reported exceptional Q2 results despite losing ~10% of upstream production due to Middle East conflict, with industry-leading earnings of $14.5B and cash flow from operations of $23.6B. Upstream production outside the Middle East hit a two-decade high, chemicals margins surged ~180% QoQ, and specialty products posted record earnings. Guyana's Errea Wittu FPSO on track, and the company achieved $16.3B cumulative structural cost savings since 2019. Guidance implies continued momentum with free cash flow expected to double by 2030 versus 2025.

negative_highlights: Management declined to comment on individual shareholder note, which has pressured the stock
Utility corridor developments are capital-intensive, though planned in advance
No significant impact from AI-related cost increases, but noted only slight revenue reduction from non-strategic asset sales
positive_highlights: Total revenue up 23% and net income up 37% YoY, both second-quarter records
Gross margins expanded across all segments (residential 45% to 48%, hospitality 39% to 42%, commercial 57% to 65%)
Repurchased $32.7 million of stock, reducing share count to lowest in ~30 years
summary: The St. Joe Company reported Q2 2026 total revenue of $158.9 million, up 23% YoY, and net income of $40.5 million, up 37% YoY, both record highs for the quarter. Gross margins expanded across all segments: residential to 48%, hospitality to 42%, and commercial to 65%. The company allocated $32.7 million to buybacks, $24 million to capex, and repaid $10.9 million in debt, with share count at a 30-year low. Management emphasized long-term capital allocation, continued demand from in-migration, and no near-term constraints from power development.

negative_highlights: Non-performing assets up nominally to ~$1.07 billion due to rate delays
Realized losses expected to rise to $20-30 million per quarter
Distributable earnings guided at $0.15-0.17 per share for next few quarters
positive_highlights: Year-to-date agency volume up 30% year over year
$135 million additional liquidity from CLO unwind with reduced pricing and enhanced leverage
Cost-cutting measures expected to save ~$10 million annually
summary: Arbor Realty Trust reported Q2 2026 distributable earnings of $0.15 per share, in line with guidance, but noted $0.02 per share of one-time financing drag and higher specific reserves. Non-performing assets remained around $1.07 billion, with $90 million resolved in July and $105 million contracted for August. The company closed a $375 million convertible offering, used $114 million to watch back stock at 50% of book value, and cut annual expenses by ~$10 million. Agency origination volume was $1.1 billion in Q2, up 30% year-to-date, but management expects a slower resolution timeline for legacy assets due to elevated rates.

negative_highlights: Slower M&A environment tempered deployment but improved sequentially
Gross-to-net trends remain pressured due to high incumbent deployment (75%)
Non-traded BDC redemptions from non-U.S. investors remain elevated
positive_highlights: Record quarterly fundraising of $36B, highest in history
FRE and realized income up 20% and 30%+ respectively
Dividend increased over 20% year-over-year
summary: Ares delivered a record fundraising quarter with $36B raised, driving AUM and fee-paying AUM up 17% YoY to $671B and $410B respectively. FRE grew 20% and realized income grew over 30%, both at or above long-term growth targets. The company raised its dividend by over 20%, and management remains on track for another record fundraising year with a record pipeline and strong deployment outlook for H2.

negative_highlights: Crop Protection pricing declined low-single-digits in Latin America due to competitive dynamics and patent expirations.
Second-half EBITDA is expected to be flat versus last year due to tariffs, dis-synergies, and geopolitical uncertainty.
Brazil corn area is forecasted to remain flat, limiting volume growth potential for the seed business.
positive_highlights: First-half net sales increased 4% to $11.3 billion driven by organic growth across all regions.
Operating EBITDA grew 10% to $3.7 billion, with margin expanding nearly 200 basis points to 32.8%.
Licensing business is performing several years ahead of the original plan.
summary: Corteva reported Q2 FY2026 net sales of $6.4 billion and Operating EBITDA of $2.3 billion for the quarter, with first-half net sales increasing 4% to $11.3 billion and Operating EBITDA rising 10% to $3.7 billion. Management raised full-year guidance for Operating EBITDA to $4.1-$4.3 billion (9% growth at midpoint) and Operating EPS to $3.60-$3.80 per share (11% growth at midpoint). The company remains on track to complete its separation into Vylor and New Corteva by October 1st.

negative_highlights: Ending loans declined due to one-time billing cycle change
NIM is expected to compress as mix shifts to fintech lending
Cash App contribution appears pushed to late Q4/early 2027
positive_highlights: EPS growth of 14.2% year-over-year and raising full-year guidance
Fintech GDV growth of 22.5% year-over-year, above trend
REBL criticized loans down another 22% to lowest level since mid-2023
summary: The Bancorp reported Q2 2026 EPS of $1.45, up 14.2% year-over-year, with ROE at 34.7%. Fintech GDV grew 22.5% YoY and fintech revenue grew 21%. The company raised its full-year 2026 EPS guidance to $5.95-$6.05 and reiterated 2027 guidance of $8.10-$8.30. Management expects Cash App to contribute more materially in late Q4/early 2027 and announced two new sponsored lending programs expected within six months.

negative_highlights: International comparable sales down approximately 9%
Technology peripherals industry demand weak
Inflationary costs expected to pressure second-half margins
positive_highlights: Second quarter sales and adjusted EPS exceeded our outlook
Americas margin improved 380 basis points to 21.2%
Full-year outlook raised for sales and adjusted EPS
summary: ACCO Brands reported Q2 2026 sales and adjusted EPS above outlook, with consolidated sales up 5% and adjusted operating margin up 20 basis points to 33.1% gross margin. Americas comparable sales grew 2% with strong back-to-school and Mexico performance, while international comps fell 9% due to soft EMEA/Australia and a distribution upgrade disruption. The company raised full-year 2026 guidance for reported sales (up 2%-5%) and adjusted EPS ($0.87-$0.91) but maintained a prudent stance on the second half, citing geopolitical uncertainty and higher inflation. EPOS acquisition remains on track with $80M full-year sales and $15M synergies expected, and technology peripherals face short-term demand weakness.

negative_highlights: Fluid Power segment adjusted EBITDA margin declined 120 bps due to realignment costs and investments

summary: Stoke Therapeutics reported significant progress in its phase III EMPEROR study for zorevunersen in Dravet syndrome, with enrollment completed at 162 patients in just 10 months and no treatment discontinuations. The company is on track for a phase III readout in Q3 2027 and plans a rolling NDA submission starting Q1 2027. Long-term OLE data show durable seizure control and statistically significant improvements in cognition and behavior through four years, with a strong safety profile. The company has a pro forma cash position of approximately $420 million, providing runway to a potential U.S. launch by early 2028. Additionally, STK-002 for ADOA has completed dosing of the first cohort and is advancing to higher doses, with early results expected in the first half of 2027.

Expect to be below midpoint of 2026 guidance
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA up 34% YoY to $1.2B
Announced 1.2 GW BYOP project with $500M EBITDA potential
2026 guidance reaffirmed
summary: Q2 2026 adjusted EBITDA was $1.2B, up 34% YoY, driven by the acquired LS Power portfolio, higher PJM capacity values, and Smart Home growth, but adjusted EPS fell to $1.49 from $1.73 due to higher interest and D&A. The company reaffirmed 2026 guidance but expects to be below the midpoint due to weak ERCOT prices. Management announced a 1.2 GW BYOP project with a hyperscaler, targeting late 2029 COD, with $500M annual EBITDA and $375M FCF at full operation, and plans to maintain $1B annual buybacks.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA flat YoY as reported due to fuel cost, weather, and project timing
Diesel costs increased by $10 million YoY with only $4 million recouped via fuel surcharges
Contracting services margins declined due to type and timing of work, impacting EBITDA by $8 million
positive_highlights: Revenue up 13% YoY, with record backlog converted
Aggregate pricing up 8% on a product mix adjusted basis
Gross profit up double digits for aggregates, ready-mix, and asphalt
summary: Knife River reported Q2 2026 revenue growth of 13% year-over-year, with aggregates volumes up 14%, ready-mix up 15%, and asphalt up 24%, but adjusted EBITDA was flat as-reported due to fuel costs, weather delays, and project timing. Management raised full-year revenue guidance to $3.4-$3.6 billion and reaffirmed adjusted EBITDA guidance of $520-$560 million. They expect volumes up high single digits for aggregates and asphalt, mid-teens for ready-mix, and anticipate improved contracting services margins in H2.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA down from $36.2 million in Q2 2025 due to non-repeating Neptune project
Middle East conflict causing delayed fluid shipments and unpredictability
Completion Fluids EBITDA margin at 26.4%, below historical highs, partly due to higher third-party bromine costs
positive_highlights: Revenue increased 19% sequentially to $185.7 million; international and global offshore revenues hit 10-year highs
Adjusted EBITDA margin in Water & Flowback expanded to 14.8% from 9.9% year-over-year, up 68%
Completed equity offering raising ~$108 million to fund Arkansas bromine project; net leverage improved to 0.4x
summary: TETRA reported Q2 2026 revenue of $185.7 million, up 19% sequentially and 7% year-over-year, with adjusted EBITDA of $31.9 million (up 24% sequentially). International and global offshore revenues reached 10-year highs, and the company advanced strategic projects including the Arkansas bromine facility FID and new TETRA Neptune Z-Lite product. Management expects base business to perform in line with market expectations, with potential upside from Neptune jobs and continued growth drivers.

negative_highlights: Cybersecurity revenue declined 7.5% to $40.9 million
Adjusted EBITDA margin decreased to 27.9% from 29.5% YoY
GAAP EPS declined to $0.18 from $0.21 YoY
positive_highlights: Raised FY2026 revenue and EBITDA guidance
Subscription revenue grew 11% to $47 million, 77% of total revenue
Digital agreements revenue grew 25.2% to $19.5 million
summary: OneSpan reported Q2 FY2026 total revenue of $60.5 million, up 1% YoY, with subscription revenue up 11% to $47 million and adjusted EBITDA margin of 28%. ARR grew 7% to $190 million, with NRR at 103%. The company raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $248-$252 million from $244-$249 million and adjusted EBITDA guidance to $67-$71 million from $64-$68 million, citing higher e-signature overages and increased hardware bookings. Management also highlighted the launch of DigipassONE platform as a strategic milestone.

negative_highlights: Legacy MasterBrand adjusted EBITDA margin was 8.4%, down due to volume, mix, and inflation
Market decline mid to high single digits with no improvement expected in 2026
American Woodmark's H2 EBITDA margin roughly on par with Q2 partial period, described as 'not what we expected'
positive_highlights: Free cash flow was $129 million versus $67 million last year, reflecting improved working capital
Executed approximately $30 million of annualized cost synergies and raised synergy target to over $100 million
Initiated two plant closures and expect $15 million synergies in second half 2026
summary: MasterBrand reported Q2 2026 net sales of $815 million, including $126 million from American Woodmark post-close, with legacy sales of $690 million in line with guidance. Adjusted EBITDA was $63 million (7.7% margin), with legacy margin at 8.4% down year-over-year on volume declines and inflation. The company introduced second-half guidance for the combined company, expecting $15 million in synergies in H2 and raising the long-term synergy target to over $100 million annually by year three. Management maintained a cautious market outlook, expecting continued softness and no demand recovery until 2027, while noting ongoing inflation and tariff pressures.

negative_highlights: Net income fell to $0.01 per share from $0.05 a year ago
Ingredient business expected to be lower for full year due to competitive landscape
Amazon growth was hit by a temporary platform issue in early June
positive_highlights: China cross-border revenue through May 2026 exceeded full-year 2025 total
Tru Niagen website sales up 23% YoY
Two global skincare companies evaluating Niagen for incorporation
summary: In Q2 FY2026, Niagen Bioscience reported revenue of $29.8 million, with Tru Niagen at $24.2 million (up 6% YoY) and e-commerce at $20.5 million (up 14% YoY). Net income was $1 million, or $0.01 per diluted share, down from $0.05 a year ago, while gross margin was stable at 64.8%. Management highlighted strong China cross-border growth, a skincare product launch, expansion of Niagen Plus, and the launch of NAD Pharmaceuticals. Full-year e-commerce growth is expected at 10%-15%, but ingredients business is expected to be lower due to competition.

negative_highlights: Revenue remains minimal at $158,000
Net loss widened year-over-year to $6.3 million
Cost increases from suppliers may push 2026 OpEx to high end of range
positive_highlights: Passed a significant GAA milestone with one of two active customers
GaN-on-Silicon RF data shows ~1,000x better linearity than reference
New NAND value proposition more than doubles TAM if adopted
summary: Atomera reported Q2 2026 revenue of $158,000, GAAP net loss of $6.3 million ($0.17 per share), and non-GAAP loss of $5 million. The company highlighted a significant Gate-All-Around milestone with one customer, a new 4F² DRAM value proposition, NAND interest, and strong GaN-on-Silicon RF results that attracted new customers. However, costs are rising, and the company now expects 2026 non-GAAP operating expenses near the high end of its $18.5 million ±$250,000 range.

negative_highlights: Belt divestiture expected to slow sales in Q3 as it ramps down
Power and electrification sector saw sizable decline in solar sales
Material and logistics costs modestly higher than last year
positive_highlights: Adjusted EPS up nearly 30% YoY to $1.83
Full-year adjusted EPS guidance raised to $6.05-$6.35, implying 16% growth
Industrial Motion segment margins up 500 bps to 23.3% on record sales
summary: Timken reported Q2 FY2026 total sales of $1.26 billion, up 7.5% year-over-year with organic growth of 4.4%, and adjusted EPS of $1.83, up almost 30% year-over-year. Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to 19.6% from 17.7%, with incremental margins over 40%. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance: total sales growth now 5%-6% and adjusted EPS of $6.05-$6.35, up $0.20 at midpoint. Industrial Motion hit a record quarter with sales up 14.6% and margins up 500 basis points to 23.3%.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA fell to $132M from $136.4M, and West Coast contract missed by $15M.
Full-year guidance reset downward due to $40M West Coast impact and $30M supplier price increase.
Free cash flow negative at -$20.9M in the quarter with elevated capex.
positive_highlights: Revenue up 12.7% YoY, organic growth 15.9%, with record volumes.
New Humana OneHome agreement expands capitated reach to 33 states plus D.C.
myAPP users up 56% since end of 2025 and new AI mask fitting tool shows strong conversion.
summary: AdaptHealth delivered strong top-line growth in Q2 FY2026, with continuing ops revenue up 12.7% YoY to $740.3M and organic growth of 15.9%, driven largely by the new West Coast capitated contract. However, Adjusted EBITDA fell to $132M from $136.4M, and management cited two major profit headwinds: a $40M expected impact from West Coast contract cost overruns and a $30M second-half hit from a manufacturer's contract termination and price increase. The company reset full-year guidance downward, announced a workforce restructuring for $19M in annualized savings, and is divesting its Diabetes Health business to sharpen focus. Free cash flow was negative at -$20.9M due to heavy capex, and a $144.2M non-cash goodwill impairment was recorded.

negative_highlights: Total revenue declined 9% year-over-year, with product revenue down 22%.
Accessories and materials business remains challenged by competitive pressures and promotional pricing.
Gross margin benefited from one-time items; excluding them, gross margin was roughly flat at 58.9%.
positive_highlights: Platform revenue grew just over 5% to $85 million, with ARPU up 5% to $56.37.
Paid subscribers increased by 93,000 year-over-year to just over 3.1 million.
Connected machine note-out units grew double-digit, driven by Joy 2 and Explore 5 bundles.
summary: Cricut reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $156.3 million, down 9% year-over-year, with platform revenue up 5% to $85 million and product revenue down 22% to $71.3 million. Net income was $39.1 million, benefiting from one-time items including $17.9 million in IEEPA tariff refunds and a $6.4 million legal settlement. Exclusive of these items, gross margin was approximately 58.9% and operating margin was 14.7%. Paid subscribers grew 3% year-over-year to just over 3.1 million, and management noted strong machine watch-out growth but continued challenges in accessories and materials, with expectations for improvement in the second half.

negative_highlights: Macro backdrop remains challenging with negative U.K. visa trends and higher Australia visa fees
Regulations in U.S. and U.K. have become more stringent
Large healthcare deals can create tough comps
positive_highlights: Signed over 200 new clients across 45 countries for second consecutive quarter
Education revenue outside big four grew over 30% YoY
SFS deals in U.S. had ARR double year-ago signings
summary: Flywire reported strong second quarter FY2026 results with robust revenue and EBITDA growth, signing over 200 new clients across 45 countries for the second consecutive quarter. Management emphasized strategic vendor consolidation, geographic diversification, and software-led monetization as structural growth drivers, with education revenue outside the big four growing over 30% year-over-year. The company reiterated long-term targets of $1 billion annual organic revenue and 30% adjusted EBITDA margin, while acknowledging a challenging macro environment with negative U.K. visa trends and stricter regulations. AI-driven automation is already resolving ~45% of customer inquiries automatically, with a target of over 50% by year-end.

negative_highlights: Q2 gas prices at Waha were negative, though July has seen positive prices.
Global inventory refill needs are uncertain, subject to geopolitical volatility.
Still evaluating EOR dispersion; some wells saw zero uplift.
positive_highlights: Production up ~4% from start of year, responding quickly to price signals.
Reduced net debt by $1.6 billion, adding $5.60 per share of equity value.
EOR wells averaging 100-150 bbl/d uplift, with clear economic benefit on some wells.
summary: In Q2 2026, Diamondback Energy increased production by ~4% from year-start, responding to price signals with a 3-4% hike in March. Management cited low global inventories and expects continued low single-digit organic growth in 2027 while maintaining capital efficiency. They reduced net debt by $1.6 billion, translating to $5.60 per share of value, and allocated modestly to buybacks. Gas outperformance and EOR results were highlighted, with initial EOR wells showing 100-150 bbl/d uplift on average, though dispersion is wide.

negative_highlights: Vehicle Control sales down 1.6% due to secular decline in wire set category
Vehicle Control adjusted EBITDA margin down to 8.6% on elevated distribution costs
Guidance unchanged, implying slower H2 as comps get harder
positive_highlights: Adjusted sales up nearly 7% in Q2, year-to-date up nearly 8%
Record-setting $63.5 million adjusted EBITDA in the quarter
Engineered Solutions up nearly 17% and Temperature Control up nearly 16%
summary: SMP reported strong Q2 FY2026 with adjusted sales up 6.7%, record adjusted EBITDA of $63.5 million (12.1% of sales), and non-GAAP EPS up 8.6% to $1.40. Vehicle Control sales fell 1.6% due to wire set decline, but Temperature Control surged 15.7%, Engineered Solutions up 16.8%, and Nissens up 4.8%. Full-year guidance is unchanged: low-to-mid single-digit sales growth and 11%-12% EBITDA margin. Management remains bullish, citing strong performance despite tariff and Middle East uncertainties.

negative_highlights: Cost of deposits declined only 3 basis points in the quarter
Intense price competition on loan yields and yield-seeking deposits
positive_highlights: Adjusted net income increased by $15.4 million, or 16% year-over-year
Net interest margin expanded 13 basis points to 4.43%
Board refreshed buyback authorization to $100 million
summary: Central Bancompany reported Q2 FY2026 net income of $113.8 million, or $0.47 per share, with adjusted net income up 16% year-over-year. Net interest margin expanded 13 basis points to 4.43%, and asset quality remained consistent with net charge-offs at 10 basis points. Management noted broad-based loan growth (6.5% annualized ex-consumer), robust pipelines, and a refreshed $100 million buyback authorization, while seeing value in the stock despite trading at a discount to peers. They expect deposit costs to be stable and loan yields to grind higher with back-book repricing, but highlighted intense price competition and a shift to lower-yielding mortgage loans.

negative_highlights: China remains a drag on Diagnostics, with DRG headwinds causing low-single-digit declines
Adjusted EPS growth of only 3% due to FX and acquisition dilution
Flow research in China still declining mid-single digits in Q2
positive_highlights: Organic revenue grew 9% constant currency, exceeding guidance by ~100 bps
Acquired businesses accelerated to 4% reported growth from 1% in Q1
Full-year guidance raised, with second-half momentum expected to be stronger
summary: Waters delivered Q2 FY2026 organic revenue of $828 million, up 9% constant currency, exceeding guidance by ~100 bps, with total revenue of $1.645 billion including $817 million from acquired BD businesses that grew 4% as reported, a 400 bps acceleration from Q1. Adjusted EPS grew 3% to $3.05, hitting the high end of guidance despite FX headwinds. Management raised full-year guidance and highlighted a 10% constant currency organic growth in the first half, with double-digit growth in pharma and academic/government, and strong momentum in acquired businesses with accelerating growth. They also noted 90 basis points of price realization in acquired businesses and a $200 million cost synergy run-rate by Q4.

negative_highlights: Guidance assumes no meaningful revenue from ENHANCE Part B or DENOVO, with contributions delayed to late Q4/2027
CFO noted Q2 service gross margin will not be sustained in Q3 due to seasonal volume softness
Stock volatility and investor concerns over growth investments versus near-term operating leverage acknowledged
positive_highlights: Record quarterly revenue of ~$190M, up 21% YoY and 9% sequentially
Service revenue grew 29% YoY and logistics 39% YoY, demonstrating platform strength
Raised low end of FY2026 revenue guidance to $737M-$757M
summary: TransMedics reported record Q2 FY2026 revenue of ~$190M, up 21% YoY and 9% sequentially, with service revenue up 29% YoY and logistics up 39% YoY. Adjusted operating margin was 14% and cash stood at ~$473M. The company raised the low end of full-year revenue guidance to $737M-$757M (22-25% growth), while reaffirming a growth-focused investment strategy across heart/lung, kidney, international expansion, and Gen 3.0 platform. Guidance excludes contributions from ENHANCE Part B, DENOVO, and PAD Aviation investment.

negative_highlights: General Education revenue down 2% and enrollments down 2.5%
Gross margin down 140 basis points to 37.8%
Applications tracking slightly behind last year
positive_highlights: Revenue growth of 4.7% and adjusted EBITDA up 8.2%
Career Learning revenue up 19% with enrollment up 14%
Re-registration activity tracking slightly ahead of last year
summary: Stride reported FY2026 revenue of $2.518B (+4.7% YoY), adjusted operating income of $498.4M (+7%), adjusted EBITDA of $617.6M (+8.2%), and adjusted EPS of $8.33. Career Learning revenue grew 19% to $1.04B, while General Education revenue fell 2% to $1.42B. The company noted a CFO leadership transition, a non-renewal by Roscoe ISD, and guided to flat/up revenue per enrollment for FY2027, with formal guidance deferred to Q1 results. Management expects count-date enrollment growth to be modest due to tougher comparisons.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to $115.2 million from $2.9 million, largely due to non-cash warrant charge
Operating expenses increased 157% year-over-year to $7.2 million
G&A expenses surged 236% due to public company transition
positive_highlights: Cash increased to $113.3 million, a net increase of $16.7 million from March quarter
Beryllium object-oriented quantum programming language now available in early access
Ember-1 superconducting testbed opened to first users, enabling real-time execution
summary: Horizon Quantum reported Q2 2026 net loss of $115.2 million, driven mainly by a $108.3 million non-cash warrant derivative remeasurement charge. Operating expenses rose to $7.2 million from $2.8 million a year ago, reflecting increased R&D and public company costs. Cash reached $113.3 million, boosted by $27.5 million in warrant exercise proceeds. Key progress includes Beryllium early access, Ember-1 testbed opening to users, and a new internal applications team, while management notes a large non-cash loss that does not affect runway.

negative_highlights: U.S. same-market treatment growth declined 0.9% due to referral execution gap
Expect 2026 U.S. same-market treatment growth around Q2 level due to compounding lower first-half referrals
Regulatory pressure in China and Middle East logistics costs remain headwinds
positive_highlights: Operating income growth accelerated to 23% in line with planned phasing
Value-Based Care turned to EUR 18 million operating income from a EUR 9 million loss
Completed EUR 1 billion buyback and launched second EUR 1 billion program
summary: FMS reported Q2 FY2026 with solid 5% organic revenue growth and 23% operating income growth at constant currency, plus 180 bps margin expansion. However, U.S. same-market treatment growth declined 0.9%, and management lowered expectations for 2026 U.S. same-market treatment growth to around Q2 levels due to referral execution gaps. The company confirmed full-year guidance, completed a EUR 1 billion buyback and launched a second, while absorbing external cost headwinds and regulatory pressures in China.

negative_highlights: Interest and other income fell to $5.8M from $10.0M sequentially
Recorded $102.4M provision for loan losses (excluded from normalized results)
Senior housing triple-net occupancy and coverage dipped due to one asset transition
positive_highlights: Same-store SHOP cash NOI grew 13.7% YoY, with margin expansion of 130 bps sequentially
Closed and awarded investments total ~$700 million year-to-date; pipeline robust
Leverage improved to 4.61x from 5.04x sequentially
summary: Sabra reported Q2 2026 normalized FFO per share of $0.38 and normalized AFFO per share of $0.40, up 3% and 5% year-over-year, respectively, in line with the prior quarter. Total cash NOI rose to $144.3 million from $138.7 million sequentially, driven by managed senior housing growth and rent resets. Same-store managed senior housing revenue grew 8.6% YoY with cash NOI up 13.7%, and portfolio occupancy increased to 88.2%. The company raised and reaffirmed 2026 FFO and AFFO per share guidance, projecting roughly 7% and 8% growth at midpoint, and net debt to adjusted EBITDA fell to 4.61x from 5.04x. Investment activity was robust with about $599 million closed year-to-date and an additional $100 million awarded, plus $330 million in pipeline, with deals yielding about 7.5% initially.

negative_highlights: Heightened inflation now projected upwards of $150 million for the year
Adjusted cash flow guidance lowered to $600-$700 million due to inflation and inventory timing
Household and foodservice segments declined as consumers delayed discretionary purchases
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA landed at the top of guidance with sequential margin expansion to 11.3%
Adjusted cash flow improved $55 million year-over-year to $138 million
Cost savings reached roughly $85 million and capex guidance reduced to below $450 million
summary: Graphic Packaging reported Q2 FY2026 net sales of $2.2 billion, adjusted EBITDA of $247 million at the top of guidance, adjusted EPS of $0.14, and adjusted cash flow of $138 million, up $55 million year-over-year. Margins expanded sequentially to 11.3%, with volumes steady despite higher gas prices. The company raised its 2026 inflation estimate to $150 million, achieved $85 million in cost savings, and reduced capital expenditure guidance to below $450 million, but lowered adjusted cash flow guidance to $600-$700 million due to inflation and inventory timing. Management announced price increases and progress on footprint optimization, but noted softness in household and foodservice segments.

negative_highlights: Wheat harvest smaller due to dry conditions in Western Corn Belt
Weather market with above-normal temperatures and reduced rainfall
Asset footprint experienced limited space income due to volatility
positive_highlights: Record earnings in Renewables with adjusted pre-tax income of $88M vs $10M year-over-year
Adjusted EPS of $2.15 and adjusted EBITDA of $140M, among best historical quarters
Reaffirmed $7 per share EPS target by 2028, with ability to exceed $6 trailing twelve months
summary: Record Renewables earnings drove a strong Q2 2026, with adjusted EPS of $2.15 and adjusted EBITDA of $140M, up from $0.24 and $65M in the prior year. Renewables pre-tax income surged to $88M from $10M, aided by $24M in 45Z credits, while Agribusiness pre-tax income improved to $20M. Management reaffirmed the $7 per share EPS target by 2028, citing strong execution and favorable market conditions.

negative_highlights: Q2 revenue came in slightly below the low end of guidance.
Global S&BT and Oracle segments declined sequentially by 2% and 1%, respectively.
IBM deferred joint go-to-market activities.
positive_highlights: Sequential gross margin improved to 44.1% from 42.3%.
Closed significant proposals totaling over $30 million.
Q3 EPS guidance of $0.37-$0.39 implies sequential earnings growth.
summary: Q2 2026 revenue before reimbursements was $68.3 million, slightly below guidance, and adjusted EPS of $0.34 was at the midpoint. Management highlighted an inflection point with over $30 million in significant new platform-led deals closed, expected to drive Q3 EPS of $0.37-$0.39 and a strong Q4 and 2027. Gross margin improved to 44.1% from 42.3% sequentially, and cash flow from operations was $15.2 million.

negative_highlights: Five convention hotels saw RevPAR decline 5% in the quarter
Hilton Garden Inn Portsmouth RevPAR down 8% due to leisure softness from Canada, wildfire impact, and new supply
Management assumes low single-digit RevPAR growth for second half citing Middle East conflict and limited visibility
positive_highlights: RevPAR grew 3% in Q2 and 10% in July, with June and July RevPAR at all-time highs for those months
Guidance increased approximately 20% since start of year; second quarter beat expectations across RevPAR, margins, EBITDA, and FFO
Silicon Valley July RevPAR up 26%, with Sunnyvale hotels up 41%
summary: Chatham Lodging Trust reported a strong Q2 2026, with RevPAR up 3%, pro forma GOP margins up 170 basis points, and hotel EBITDA margins up 220 basis points, beating internal expectations. The company increased its annual guidance by approximately 20% since the start of the year, citing strong business travel, robust performance from the recently acquired six-hotel portfolio (RevPAR up 9% in Q2 and 13% in July), and accelerating Silicon Valley demand (July RevPAR up 26%). Management remains optimistic about the lodging upcycle but exercises conservatism in second-half guidance due to Middle East conflict and limited visibility.

negative_highlights: GAAP net loss of $29 million due to $84 million negative fair value adjustments
Gain on sale margins experienced volatility from interest rate movements
Tangible equity value per share declined slightly due to GAAP loss
positive_highlights: Adjusted EPS of $0.84, a 53% improvement over Q2 2025
Funded volume up 21% YoY to $730 million, reinforcing guidance
Cash generated $58 million from originations and capital markets activities
summary: Finance of America reported Q2 2026 adjusted net income of $19 million ($0.84 per share), up 53% year-over-year, despite a GAAP net loss of $29 million driven by non-cash fair value adjustments. Funded reverse mortgages totaled $730 million, up 21% year-over-year, and submissions exceeded $1 billion, up 19% year-over-year. The company reaffirmed full-year guidance of $2.8-3.1 billion in funded volume and $4.50-$5.00 adjusted EPS, and highlighted strong cash generation of $58 million in the quarter, used to fund the Onity MSR acquisition and debt payments. Management expressed confidence in achieving guidance and continued investment in growth.

negative_highlights: Anchor lease occupancy fell 40 bps due to Painted Tree vacancy
Expected temporary occupancy impact of 50 bps in Q2
Net leverage rose to 5.3x from 4.5x at year-end
positive_highlights: Same Property NOI growth accelerated to 4.1% in Q2
Year-to-date Nareit FFO per share increased 11.1%
Raised full-year Nareit FFO guidance to $2.01-$2.07 per share
summary: InvenTrust reported Q2 FY2026 Same Property NOI growth of 4.1%, with year-to-date Nareit FFO up 11.1% and Core FFO up 9.1%. Leasing activity remained strong with 76 leases, 88% retention, and 8.5% blended lease spreads. The company acquired six properties for $290 million, expanding into emerging Sun Belt markets, and reaffirmed full-year Same Property NOI and Core FFO guidance while raising Nareit FFO guidance to $2.01-$2.07. Management remains confident in the portfolio and external growth pipeline.

negative_highlights: Revenue slipped to $321.4 million year-over-year; U.S. P&C revenue fell 10.2% on softer networks business and below-historical claims frequency
International operating margin near 8% was boosted by weather carryover in Australia and Asia that management expects to moderate in Q3 and especially Q4
Q2 included a $2.3 million software impairment and a $1.3 million net loss on the legal services disposal, with an additional ~$1.3 million expense expected on U.K. entity shutdown
positive_highlights: Non-GAAP EPS rose to $0.38 from $0.22; GAAP diluted EPS increased to $0.27/$0.28 from $0.16
Consolidated operating earnings up 34% year-over-year; adjusted EBITDA $37.6 million (11.7% of revenues) versus $31.4 million (9.7%)
Board raised quarterly dividend to $0.08 per share from $0.075; leverage ratio 1.45x EBITDA at low end of target range
summary: Crawford reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $321.4 million, down slightly year-over-year, while non-GAAP EPS rose to $0.38 from $0.22 and consolidated operating earnings grew 34%. Non-GAAP operating margin expanded to 9.2% from 6.8% and adjusted EBITDA margin rose to 11.7% from 9.7%, helped by International weather-related claims and Broadspire growth. Segment results were uneven: U.S. P&C revenue fell 10.2% and International's 4.2% growth was largely FX and episodic weather carryover that management said would moderate in Q3 and Q4. The board raised the quarterly dividend to $0.08 from $0.075, but no formal revenue or EPS guidance was provided.

negative_highlights: Removed previous commitment to return at least 75% of cash available for distribution
Management noted market not rewarding Viper's growth or valuation versus peers
Volatility in commodity prices cited as not helpful for M&A
positive_highlights: Q3 production guidance implies ~4.5% sequential growth and ~15% annualized per-share oil growth
Base dividend increased 32% to $2 per share annually, implying ~4.5% yield
Board approved strategic shift to high base dividend with buyback optionality
summary: In Q2 2026, Viper Energy turned 691 gross horizontal wells to production with an average 3% net revenue interest, and initiated Q3 production guidance implying ~4.5% sequential growth and ~15% annualized per-share oil growth. The company announced a 32% increase in its base dividend to $2 per share annually (~4.5% yield), while removing the previous 75% quarterly payout commitment to fund buybacks, M&A, or debt reduction. Management expressed confidence in the new capital allocation framework, citing a protected dividend to $30 oil and a robust A&D market.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA margin declined to 39.8% from 40.3% due to a higher mix of Latin America revenue
Recorded impairment charges related to exiting a JV in Latin America
Tax rate increased due to a larger share of income from higher-tax jurisdictions
positive_highlights: Revenue up 20% YoY to $275 million, above the high end of guidance
Latin America segment revenue up 52% reported (42% constant currency) with new client wins
Repurchased 2 million shares for $47 million and board replenished authorization
summary: EVERTEC reported Q2 2026 revenue of $275 million, up 20% year-over-year (16% on a constant currency basis), with adjusted EBITDA of $109 million (up 18%) and adjusted EPS of $1.05 (up 18%). The quarter included significant strategic wins, including a multi-year agreement with Transbank in Chile and a contract with Clip in Mexico, and the acquisitions of Dimensa and BBChain closed in the quarter. Management confirmed existing guidance and noted synergies from acquisitions are expected to be more meaningful in 2027.

negative_highlights: Other segment (upstream) down $14 million due to divestiture
Management remains cautious on hurricane season and weak summer gas prices
Sequent business sees seasonally lower Q2 opportunities
positive_highlights: Q2 EBITDA up 6% over 2025; year-to-date up 10%
Full-year 2026 EBITDA guidance raised by $200 million at midpoint to $8.3-$8.5 billion
summary: Williams reported Q2 2026 EBITDA of $1.92 billion, up 6% year-over-year, and increased full-year 2026 EBITDA guidance to $8.3-$8.5 billion, reflecting a $200 million midpoint raise. The company announced two major strategic moves: a Power Innovation financing JV with Blackstone providing $5.34 billion of committed capital, and the $5.5 billion acquisition of Momentum Midstream. Combined company on track for FY2026 EPS at least $6 per share

The company closed the Sun Country acquisition, is on track for full-year 2026 EPS of at least $6 per share, and expects Q3 unit revenue growth in line with Q2. Despite Sun Country pilot attrition and elevated fuel costs, management expects Q3 operating profit and full-year margin expansion.

negative_highlights: Adjusted gross margin down 740 bps to 27.7% due to cost inflation and inventory charge.
Full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance lowered to $275-$295 million.
Price increase expected to drive elasticity slightly greater than one.

summary: BellRing Brands reported Q3 net sales growth of 4%, with Premier Protein RTD shake volume up 3% and Dymatize sales up 27%, both beating expectations. However, adjusted gross margin fell to 27.7% from 35.1% due to protein and freight cost inflation, tariffs, and a $28 million inventory-related charge. Management raised full-year net sales guidance to 1-3% growth but lowered adjusted EBITDA guidance to $275-$295 million, and announced a double-digit price increase on Premier Shakes for fiscal Q1 2027, expecting elasticities slightly greater than one. A new CEO, Mike Axelrod, joined and acknowledged execution issues while outlining actions to improve profitability in fiscal 2027.

negative_highlights: Semi gross margins down slightly due to product mix and investments

summary: Qnity reported strong Q2 FY2026 results with organic sales up 22% YoY, adjusted EBITDA up 24%, and adjusted EPS up 53% to $1.19, exceeding expectations. Both segments delivered double-digit organic growth, with ICS up 28% and Semi up 17%. Management raised guidance for the full year, citing broad-based demand from AI-driven applications and advanced packaging. The company repriced debt to enhance free cash flow and continues to invest in capacity and innovation.

summary: BXDC completed its IPO in May 2026, raising $2 billion, the largest blind pool REIT IPO in history. Q2 GAAP net income was $0.14 per share, FFO $0.07, and AFFO $0.08, with no real estate operations yet; results reflect only post-IPO period interest income of $9.3 million and minimal expenses. Management is confident in deploying capital at attractive yields, citing a robust pipeline, strong market fundamentals (1% vacancy), and supportive comparable transactions at low-to-mid six cap rates.

Phase III SELVA met primary and all secondary endpoints with 95% of patients improving at week 24.
Cash position ~$250 million, well-capitalized through launch; sales force increased to ~40 reps.
summary: Palvella reported Q2 2026 milestones including a successful pre-NDA meeting with FDA for QTORIN rapamycin in microcystic lymphatic malformations, rolling review granted, and first NDA module submitted. The company is on track to complete NDA submission in 2H 2026 with potential approval in 1H 2027. Management increased planned launch sales force to ~40 reps and strengthened balance sheet with $250 million cash, guided pricing range of $100k-$200k per patient per year for mLM. Pipeline expansions include potential approvals in cutaneous venous malformations (2029) and clinically significant angiokeratomas (2031), with a fourth indication to be announced later this year.

The company raised its full-year sales outlook to 14%-16% growth and expects non-GAAP EPS of $20.75-$21.25, while navigating a memory cost headwind of approximately $120M. Q3 guidance calls for adjusted EBITDA margin near 22% and non-GAAP EPS of $4.70-$4.90.

Gross margin fell to 39.3% from 44.7%, and adjusted EBITDA was nearly breakeven at $52,000. The company revised full-year revenue guidance down to $100–$110 million from prior expectations, citing the EG4 optimized inverter launch pushout to Q4, slower GO Battery ramp, and gradual European recovery. Management expressed confidence in policy tailwinds from FCC and EU restrictions but remained cautious on near-term demand.

Management raised full-year revenue and EPS guidance, citing strong performance and momentum, while noting headwinds from FX and planned incremental investments in the second half.

The engineering prototype achieved partial transition flight milestones, logging two hours and 46 minutes across 66 flights while validating over 150 test points. Management raised the full-transition timeline to late Q4 FY26 (from earlier expectations) due to a deliberate focus on quality testing rather than rushing.

Adjusted EBITDA came in within guidance, but product commerce gross margin contracted 210 bps YoY due to supply chain headwinds, promotional activity, and a $410 million regulatory fine. Membership recovered above pre-incident levels, and underlying customer spend (excluding non-returned cohort) grew 16% YoY, but management guided Q3 to 8-9% growth, citing calendar effects and the missing cohort. Management expects margin recovery for product commerce by mid-2027.

The company reaffirmed its 2026 EPS guidance of $6.55-$6.80 and its 5%-7% growth through 2030, expressing confidence in top-half results from 2028. Management highlighted a favorable North Carolina rate settlement, 7.8 GW of data center ESAs, and $5B-$10B of potential capital-plan upside.

Management highlighted accelerating new lease spreads, a successful Wi-Fi initiative contributing $400,000 in Q2 revenue, and a commitment to value-add renovations as key drivers for 2027 momentum.

summary: Arvinas reported Q2 2026 with cash of $567.9 million, down from $685.4 million at end of 2025. The FDA approved VEPPANU (first PROTAC degrader) and it was out-licensed to Rigel Pharmaceuticals. The KRAS G12D program ARV-806 is deprioritized for partnering. Clinical milestones: ARV-393 phase I data expected by end of 2026, ARV-027 healthy volunteer data in H1 2027, ARV-102 trials now expected to begin in 2027. Financials include a one-time revenue recognition from Pfizer collaboration and a $52.7 million liability for VEPPANU closeout.

Management highlighted continued diversification from Block, with non-Block TPV growing over 2x faster, and raised expectations for the remainder of 2026 based on strong execution and product momentum.

Tinder DAU improved to -4% year-over-year, with MAU still declining 7% but improving sequentially, and payers expected to return to growth by Q4 next year. Hinge MAU grew 13% globally with 22% revenue growth, while E&E faces headwinds from Azar's App Store removal. Management raised the outlook for Adjusted EBITDA to at or above the high end and is confident in a Tinder turnaround, with MAU expected flat by Q4 next year and 2027 Tinder revenue up year-over-year.

Management raised full-year EBITDA, adjusted EPS, and free cash flow guidance, and expects CV growth to continue accelerating. The company is optimistic about AI-driven demand and its Business and Technology Insights transformation.

Adjusted EBITDA rose 13% to $15.7 million and OIBDA rose 7% to $13.7 million, while net loss narrowed to about $508,000 and diluted EPS was break-even versus a $0.01 loss a year ago. Full-year guidance was reiterated at $186-191 million revenue (about 7% growth at the midpoint) and $75-79 million adjusted EBITDA (about 5% growth). Cash used in operating activities was $1.4 million, a $7.4 million improvement, and net debt rose to $448.5 million from $429.8 million at March 31, 2026.

summary: Addus HomeCare reported Q2 2026 revenue of $377.4 million, up 8% YoY, and adjusted EPS of $1.73, up 16.1%. Adjusted EBITDA rose 11.9% to $49.2 million, with margin expanding to 13%. Personal care same-store revenue grew 6.8%, driven by 2.2% same-store hour growth; hospice same-store revenue rose 11.1%, while home health same-store revenue declined 2.8% but improved sequentially. Management raised expectations for personal care organic growth to 6-6.5% for 2026 and remains optimistic about eliminating the 80/20 rule and M&A pipeline.

However, operational performance fell short and cost reductions have not yet flowed to the bottom line; management guided to $18 billion in structural costs by end of 2026, from $22 billion in 2025. BPX production grew to 545,000 boe/d, with a new basin production record. Management emphasized 'Fit to Grow' strategy, portfolio simplification, and balance sheet strengthening, but acknowledged past impairments and slower cost progress.

Excluding that benefit, comparable EPS was $1.90. Light Duty sales were flat YoY on tough comps, Heavy Duty grew ~7%, Specialty Vehicle declined 1%. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance to 3%-5% net sales growth and adjusted EPS of $8.50-$8.80, reflecting lower tariff environment and pricing actions. Heavy Duty margin improved 150 bps ex-refund, but freight market remains challenged.

Revenue grew 9% to $312 million, with gross margin steady at 30.6% and EPS rising to $1.42 from $1.32. The company is aggressively expanding capacity, planning a new facility and expects strong performance into FY2027.

Plans for leadership transition and increased MGM ownership were reiterated.

Gross margin was 56.6%, including a 160 basis point benefit from tariff refunds; adjusted EBITDA rose to $27 million from $23 million, with EPS of $0.26 versus $0.14 in the prior year. Management expects double-digit revenue growth for the full year and noted July sales up 18% year-over-year.

International/offshore revenue rose 11% sequentially, while NAM land fell 4% sequentially due to Canada seasonality. The company closed the TCO Group acquisition for $95 million and guided Q3 revenue to $260-270 million and adjusted EBITDA to $51-57 million, implying sequential growth. Management cited strong subsea momentum, Mexico activity, Saudi market share gains, and expects U.S. land growth in the back half.

summary: Q2 revenue was a record $201 million, up 18% sequentially and 62% year-over-year, with non-GAAP EPS of $0.53, up over 120% year-over-year and above the high end of guidance, driven by strength across all end markets, especially compute and communications. Q3 guidance calls for FPGA revenue of $210-230 million and combined revenue of $245-265 million, including two months of AMI, with non-GAAP EPS of $0.54-0.58, which implies roughly 100% year-over-year EPS growth. The acquisition of AMI closed in late July and is expected to be accretive to EPS starting in Q4, with AMI expected to exit 2026 at a revenue run rate of more than $200 million and grow 25% in 2027. New product revenue is expected to exceed 25% of total revenue this year, and the company described a 'rule of 105' based on 62% growth and over 40% EBITDA margin.

The order book is up over 50% year-over-year, with record aerospace and defense shipments and a near doubling of industrial backlog. Management guided to slightly higher Q3 adjusted EBITDA sequentially and year-over-year, with price increases announced effective August, fully realized in 2027.

summary: DuPont reported Q2 FY2026 organic sales growth of 4%, operating EBITDA margin up 80 basis points to 24.6%, adjusted EPS up 21% to $1.88, and free cash flow conversion of 127% for the quarter. Management also announced a Q3 $250M share repurchase and expects full-year free cash flow conversion ahead of the 90% target. Bookings showed strength in biopharma (up >20% organic) and deep tech (semiconductor and energy research both up >50% organic), though U.S. academic order weakness persists and some revenue is pushed to Q4 and 2027 due to long lead times.
