negative_highlights: Northwest Natural Gas EPS declined to $0.09 in the quarter compared to $0.12 in the prior year period
Water utility financial results were modestly below plan due to higher O&M expenses supporting platform integration and centralization efforts
SiEnergy earnings of $0.05 per share represented a decrease from $0.03 in Q2 2025, though this was partially offset by the full quarter contribution from the Pines acquisition
positive_highlights: SiEnergy achieved organic customer growth exceeding 15% in the second quarter
Northwest Natural received a Washington regulatory order granting over 80% of requested revenue requirement increase with new rates effective August 1st, 2026
MX3 storage expansion project secured unanimous approval from Columbia County Board of Commissioners for its conditional use permit
summary: Northwest Natural reported Q2 FY26 EPS of $0.01 for the consolidated company and segment-specific results including Northwest Natural Gas at $0.09 (vs prior year $0.12) and SiEnergy at $0.05 (vs prior year $0.03). Management reaffirmed full-year 2026 guidance in the range of $2.95-$3.15 per share, stating they now expect to finish in the top half of that range driven by strong first-half performance and regulatory settlements. The quarter was impacted seasonally for gas utilities (winter heating months) while water utility results were modestly below plan due to integration costs.

negative_highlights: Management explicitly stated they remain 'measured' on expectations due to soft housing conditions expected to persist through Q3 and beyond.
Structural gross margins are projected to decline from current levels (8.5%-9.5% guidance) as elevated pricing normalizes in the back half of 2026.
SG&A expenses rose $12M YoY due to Disdero acquisition, fuel costs (+50%), and freight rates.
positive_highlights: Net sales increased >4% YoY driven by Disdero acquisition ($25M contribution) and volume growth in multi-family channels (up 11%).
Specialty gross margin expanded to 20.0%, excluding a $7.2 million duty-related benefit.
Announced new partnership with Trex for distribution rights in 11 markets, validating the channel strategy.
summary: BlueLinx reported Q2 FY2026 net sales of $814 million (up >4% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $35.6 million ($9.1M adj net income), beating expectations despite a challenging housing market. Management noted that structural gross margins were elevated at 10.9% due to pricing but expects them to normalize in the back half, while specialty volumes are projected to be flat sequentially. The company announced new distribution rights for Trex and Georgia-Pacific, with full impact expected starting in Q3/Q4.

negative_highlights: GAAP net loss widened significantly from $15.7 million in Q2 FY2025 to approximately $23.8 million in Q2 FY2026.
Average Revenue Per Member (ARPM) declined by $0.06 quarter-over-quarter due to the heavy weighting of discounted annual memberships and theatrical revenue mix shifts.
Gross margin contracted from 69% in Q2 FY2025 to 54% in Q2 FY2026, primarily driven by a shift away from high-margin distribution/theatrical titles toward lower-margin core Guild subscriptions.
positive_highlights: Guild membership grew by nearly 400,000 in Q2 (approx +17% sequentially), significantly outpacing the prior year's pace of 230,000 additions.
Sales and marketing expense decreased to $61.1 million from $81.7 million in comparable periods last year as a percentage of revenue improved substantially due to scale.
Deferred revenue increased by $16 million quarter-over-quarter to $83 million following the successful launch of annual memberships.
summary: Angel reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $111 million (up 28% YoY) and Guild membership growth to 2.85 million members, driven by the 'America 250' campaign which boosted annual sign-ups but lowered Average Revenue Per Member (ARPM). While operating leverage improved with sales/marketing spend dropping as a percentage of revenue, GAAP net loss widened to $23.8 million and adjusted EBITDA loss was approximately $7.7 million for the first half of 2026. Management reaffirmed its commitment to limit full-year adjusted EBITDA losses to no more than $25 million.

negative_highlights: Headline margin and EPS gains were substantially driven by one-time IEEPA refunds; operating margin ex-refunds would be far below reported levels
Nunn Bush sales fell 3% amid pressure from private label and lower-priced licensed brands; Florsheim Australia local-currency sales declined 1%
Management flagged near-term gross margin uncertainty from the July 24 tariff increase to 12.5% and gave no quantitative guidance; inventories planned to rise to ~$70 million by Q4 from $49.1 million
positive_highlights: Wholesale net sales rose 7% to $58.8 million with growth in three of four brands (Florsheim +12%, BOGS +10%, Stacy Adams +4%)
Recognized $15.3 million of tariff refunds as a cost-of-sales reduction, plus $700K interest income, driving gross margin to 70.4% and operating earnings to $17 million
Balance sheet is strong with $98.1 million in cash and marketable securities and no debt drawn; $17.5 million of additional refund proceeds received in early July
summary: Net sales rose 7% to $62.2 million and diluted EPS jumped to $1.39 from $0.24, but the bulk of the gain came from $15.3 million of recognized IEEPA tariff refunds booked as a reduction to cost of sales, lifting gross margin to 70.4% from 43.3% and operating earnings to $17 million. Underlying demand was modest: wholesale up 7% (Florsheim +12%, Stacy Adams +4%, BOGS +10%, Nunn Bush -3%), retail +4%, and Florsheim Australia down 1% in local currency. Management gave no quantitative guidance, cited an unpredictable tariff environment (China/DR/Vietnam incremental tariff raised to 12.5% on July 24), and said inventories will build to roughly $70 million by year-end from $49.1 million at June 30. Excluding the one-time refunds, margins and EPS were materially lower than the headline.

negative_highlights: Organic e.l.f. brand (excluding Rhode) was largely in line with the previously outlined high single-digit decline.
Unit volumes were down approximately three percentage points, though pricing and mix added roughly 39 percentage points to growth.
Marketing spend for Q1 was below expectations due to timing of investment.
positive_highlights: Net sales grew 36% year-over-year, marking the company's 30th consecutive quarter of growth.
Rhode contributed approximately $160 million in net sales driven by record-breaking summer innovation launches.
Management raised full fiscal 2027 guidance for organic net sales to 6%-7%, up from a prior outlook of 4%-5%.
summary: e.l.f. Beauty reported Q1 FY2027 net sales growth of 36% year-over-year and adjusted EPS of $1.75 per diluted share, significantly beating expectations driven by Rhode's record performance and a one-time tariff refund benefit. Management raised its full fiscal 2027 guidance for net sales growth to an 18%-20% range from the prior 12%-14%, along with corresponding increases in adjusted EBITDA and EPS outlooks.

negative_highlights: GAAP operating loss remains at $43.3 million despite significant improvement over the prior year period.
Full-year guidance does not yet include revenue contribution from the pending LivePerson acquisition, which is expected to close in H2 FY2026.
positive_highlights: Revenue reached an all-time high of $61.9M, up 45% YoY and 40% QoQ.
Adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed by 33% year-over-year to a loss of $9.6 million due to disciplined cost management and synergies from acquisitions.
OASYS platform is driving rapid conversion, including an eight-figure commitment signed in less than 90 days.
summary: SoundHound reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $61.9 million, a 45% year-over-year increase and its largest all-time quarter driven by the OASYS platform launch. Adjusted EBITDA improved significantly with a loss narrowing to $9.6 million (a 33% improvement), while GAAP gross margin expanded six percentage points sequentially to 58%. Management raised full-year revenue guidance expectations based on this strong first-half performance.

positive_highlights: Total revenue of $233 million exceeded expectations and the high end of the prior quarter's guidance range.
summary: Oportun reported Q2 FY2026 total revenue of $233 million and adjusted EBITDA of $49 million, both exceeding the high end of prior guidance ranges. The company delivered its seventh consecutive quarter of GAAP profitability with EPS growing year-over-year while improving credit performance to a 12% annualized net charge-off rate. Management raised full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance by approximately $10 million at the midpoint and lowered the projected annualized net charge-off rate, citing balance sheet optimization and disciplined growth.

positive_highlights: Signed a key joint development agreement with a leading provider for optical connectivity integration targeting millions of units annually starting in 2027.
summary: Aeva reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $6.1 million and non-GAAP operating loss of $26 million, with liquidity strengthened to over $300 million following an equity raise. Management highlighted a major joint development agreement for optical connectivity targeting initial volumes in H2 2027 and ramping in 2028, alongside progress on automotive programs like Bendix and Daimler Truck. The company emphasized financial discipline while expanding into new markets without significant reconfiguration of core technology.

negative_highlights: Core Gas Utility segment reported an adjusted loss of $3 million, up from a $10 million loss in the prior year due to higher bad debt expense and O&M costs.
Missed revenue recovery expectations as lower usage net of weather mitigation in Missouri partially offset gains in Alabama.
Regulatory settlements in Missouri regarding accounting authority did not immediately resolve lost margin issues, requiring future rate cases for durable solutions.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EPS improved by $0.03 per share compared to the prior year quarter due to non-recurring preferred dividend expense in FY25 and a gain on sale of divested businesses totaling $254.6 million after-tax.
Completed divestitures of Spire Marketing and Spire Storage, simplifying the business model into a fully regulated utility profile with enhanced earnings visibility.
summary: Spire reported an adjusted loss of $15 million ($0.26 per share) for Q3 FY2026, a slight improvement from the prior year's loss but still below expectations given recent divestitures and transition costs. Management reaffirmed fiscal 2026 guidance of $3.90-$4.10 EPS (excluding discontinued operations) and maintained long-term growth targets despite ongoing regulatory settlements in Missouri and Alabama. The company highlighted a gain on sale of $254.6 million from divested businesses which significantly impacted the bottom line, while noting that core utility earnings remain under pressure.

negative_highlights: Hardware revenue declined by 10% YoY to $14 million, reflecting changes in product mix and lower unit prices.
Total bookings were weighted towards IoT solutions which had a lower ARPU compared to other segments.
Professional services gross margin was volatile at 21%, recovering from -44% the prior year due to specific project mixes.
positive_highlights: Core revenue accelerated to a double-digit growth rate of 14% YoY, marking the highest quarterly growth in over two years.
Gross margins expanded by 760 bps to 41%, reflecting structural cost reductions and higher SaaS mix.
The company achieved positive adjusted EBITDA for the third consecutive quarter with $93 million in cash on hand.
summary: SmartRent reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $40 million (up 4% YoY) and core revenue of $38 million (up 14%), driven by a 13% increase in SaaS revenues to $16 million. Gross margins expanded significantly by 760 basis points to 41%, while the company achieved its third consecutive quarter of positive adjusted EBITDA at $700,000 and deployed share buybacks totaling approximately $3 million.

negative_highlights: EV charging gross margin contracted to 26.9% from 33.8%
Maintenance revenue nearly flat at $4.1M vs $4.0M
Data center revenue upside expected only in next fiscal year
positive_highlights: Revenue up 32% YoY to $25.7M

summary: Orion Energy Systems reported Q1 FY2027 revenue of $25.7 million, up 32% year-over-year, with net income of $2 million versus a loss of $1.2 million in the prior year. The company reiterated its fiscal 2027 guidance of $95-$97 million revenue and positive adjusted EBITDA, and highlighted strength in automotive, retail, public sector, and EV charging, plus initial data center entry.

negative_highlights: Hawaii conventional throughput is expected between 59,000 and 65,000 barrels per day in Q3 due to the refinery turnaround.

positive_highlights: Adjusted net income reached $499 million, or $10.10 per share, reflecting exceptional operational execution in volatile markets.
Hawaii crude differential guidance was raised to between $11.50 and $13.50 per barrel for the third quarter following the turnaround completion.
Total liquidity strengthened to approximately $1.4 billion after reducing term debt by over 20% via a new senior unsecured notes issuance.
summary: Par Pacific reported strong Q2 FY2026 results with adjusted net income of $499 million ($10.10 per share) and adjusted EBITDA of $571 million, driven by a combined refining index averaging approximately $33 per barrel. Management raised full-year guidance for Hawaii crude differentials to between $11.50 and $13.50 per barrel following the completion of the refinery turnaround in July. The company strengthened its balance sheet with total liquidity of approximately $1.4 billion after reducing term debt by over 20% via a new senior unsecured notes issuance.

positive_highlights: Set company records for highest second quarter total revenue and lowest gross debt balance

summary: Cushman & Wakefield reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $2.8 billion (up 11% YoY) and adjusted EPS of $0.35 (up 17%), setting records for total revenue and leasing/services volume while achieving the lowest gross debt balance in company history. Management raised its full-year 2026 guidance, projecting mid-to-high single-digit revenue growth and increasing the annualized adjusted EPS target to a range of 18%-23%. The strong performance was driven by double-digit growth across all geographies (Americas, APAC, EMEA) with leasing up 27% globally and services expanding 7%, despite a softness in capital markets.

Company successfully reduced channel inventory weeks on hand from above nine at the start of the year down to a healthy range of 7.3 weeks.

Credit trends improved with total delinquency down to 12.16% from 13.14% and net charge-offs down to 7.28% from 7.45%; no explicit numeric guidance was issued, though management said the trajectory 'paints a pretty good picture for the rest of 2026.'

Management raised full-year outlooks for Q3 with a midpoint representing a 4.5% sequential increase, while reaffirming the path toward exiting at 24% quarterly gross margin.

Kumamoto earthquake caused production suspensions at several plants through at least August 19th
Full-year unit sales guidance left unchanged despite Q1 shortfall in China
positive_highlights: Record Q1 operating profit of JPY 530.7 billion, up JPY 286.5 billion YoY

Full-year operating profit guidance raised by JPY 150 billion to JPY 650 billion
summary: Honda reported record Q1 FY2027 operating profit of JPY 530.7 billion, up JPY 286.5 billion YoY, with net profit attributable to owners of JPY 450.9 billion, up JPY 254.2 billion. Motorcycle segment posted record operating profit of JPY 233.9 billion (margin 11.6%), while automobile operating profit was JPY 192.1 billion (margin 5.0%). The company raised full-year operating profit guidance to JPY 650 billion from JPY 500 billion and adjusted operating profit to JPY 1.17 trillion from JPY 1.0 trillion, while keeping unit sales and dividend guidance unchanged. Key concerns include a 50% YoY decline in China retail sales and production suspensions following the July 28 Kumamoto earthquake.

negative_highlights: Pharma R&D services revenue was $11.4 million, reflecting timing of deliverables and a strategic shift away from one-time smaller deals.
Operating expenses increased by approximately $21 million year-over-year due to commercial expansion and product pipeline investments.
positive_highlights: Total revenue increased 45% year-over-year to $263.7 million driven by volume growth and ASP increases.
GAAP gross margins expanded significantly from 63% last year to 68% in the current quarter.
Caris Detect launched with strong interest, while Caris Assure blood cases grew 50% year-over-year.
summary: Caris Life Sciences reported Q2 FY2026 total revenue of $263.7 million, a 45% year-over-year increase driven by molecular profiling services growth of 55%. GAAP gross margins expanded to 68%, and the company achieved its fifth consecutive quarter of positive Adjusted EBITDA ($55.7M) and free cash flow ($6.4M). Management raised full-year revenue guidance to $1.03-$1.04 billion from a prior range of $1.0-$1.02 billion, citing strong H1 performance.

negative_highlights: CMS has filed notice of intent to appeal the District Court's decision regarding the four and a half star rating, creating litigation uncertainty for future payments.
Outpatient cost trends remain elevated compared to prior years despite moderating in Q2
Second-half outlook anticipates seasonal EBITDA loss in Q4 due to AEP-related investments
positive_highlights: GAAP net income increased by $67 million year-over-year in the first half of 2026
Operating leverage expanded by more than 200 basis points, with SG&A improving approximately 220 bps YoY
Cohort progression is delivering stronger economics as members move from year one to two
summary: Clover Health reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $1.5 billion (up >$550M YoY) and GAAP net income of $28 million for the quarter ($55M H1), beating expectations with membership growth of 48% in Medicare Advantage. Management increased full-year guidance across all metrics, including total revenue to $2.92B-$3B and adjusted EBITDA to $70M-$85M, citing favorable cost trends and cohort maturation under Clover Assistant as key drivers.

negative_highlights: Revenue growth was muted at only +2% sequentially as stronger bookings have not yet fully translated into shipments.
Tariff-related headwinds persisted, including $10 million in higher gross tariff expenses offsetting a $35 million refund.
Production rates are expected to lag booking growth through the second half of 2026 due to sourcing transitions and hiring needs.

Operating cash flow turned positive ($17 million) and improved by approximately $50 million from Q1.
Bolzoni returned to profitability due to favorable product mix and lower freight costs.

Consolidated operating loss narrowed to $18 million from a prior period, driven by lift truck improvements and tariff refunds offsetting higher material costs and tariffs; however, profitability remains under pressure with shipments lagging bookings due to production ramp-up constraints.

negative_highlights: Second quarter adjusted EPS missed expectations at $0.16 versus $0.22 year-over-year, reflecting higher O&M costs from severe weather events.
Management is still evaluating a recent Indiana TDSIC order regarding gas modernization investments which may impact recovery mechanisms and requires demonstrating specific project benefits.
positive_highlights: Management confirmed the data center strategy remains on track with Amazon and Alphabet agreements approved, expected to provide approximately $1.4 billion in bill reductions for existing customers over contract terms.
Demand from large load customers is robust with 3 GW of active strategic negotiations and line of sight to an additional 2 GW of potential customers beyond the current pipeline.
summary: NiSource reported Q2 FY2026 consolidated adjusted EPS of $0.16 compared to $0.22 in the prior year period, driven by increased revenue from new rates offset by higher O&M expenses due to storm activity and union negotiations. Management reaffirmed full-year guidance for 2026 at a range of $2.02-$2.07 per share despite an Indiana regulatory order regarding gas modernization investments that requires better demonstration of project benefits before recovery.

negative_highlights: Net debt leverage ratio increased to two times due to $100 million Calabrian financing, up from 1.2x
Management remains cautious about potential demand destruction in industrial applications if sulfur prices moderate
Capital expenditures expected to rise to $85-$95 million for Gulf Coast expansion and integration

summary: Ecovyst reported Q2 FY2026 sales of $250 million and Adjusted EBITDA of $53 million, which beat consensus expectations by solidly meeting the upper end of its guidance range ($48-$59m). Management raised full-year 2026 Adjusted EBITDA guidance to a range of $195-$207 million following the closing of the Calabrian acquisition and favorable first-half results. The company ended with net debt leverage at two times, funded by new term loan proceeds for the acquisition.

The company expects a timing benefit regarding inventory levels that will partially reverse working capital improvements in H2.
positive_highlights: Underlying adjusted gross margins hit an all-time high of 43.8%, driven by favorable mix and supply chain savings.
Flushable wipes grew more than 200% YoY, making Honest the fastest-growing branded player in that segment.
Household penetration improved to 8.1%, with nearly two-thirds of growth coming from no-kid households.
summary: The Honest Company reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $83.3 million (down 10.9% YoY due to strategic exits and diaper declines) but achieved organic growth of 6.7%. Underlying adjusted gross margins expanded to 43.8%, marking an all-time high, while the company raised its full-year outlook for both revenue ($319M-$325M) and Adjusted EBITDA ($23M-$25M). Management highlighted strong momentum in Wipes (consumption up 26%) and Personal Care (+19%), which now comprise over 70% of consumption, offsetting structural headwinds in the diaper category.

negative_highlights: Silicon metal average note price declined 6% sequentially to $2,592 per ton due to low-price imports.
Company explicitly stated it will not resume the share buyback program at this time despite positive cash flow generation.
European ferrosilicon index prices fell 6%, with safeguards noted as ineffective against substitution of silicon metal.

Free cash flow turned positive at $20 million after improving from -$16 million in the prior quarter.
Manganese-based alloys adjusted EBITDA margins expanded significantly to 12%, up from 9% in Q1.
summary: Ferroglobe reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $379 million (up 9% sequentially) and adjusted EBITDA of $13 million (up $10m), driven by a 7% volume increase in silicon metal. Free cash flow improved to +$20 million, supported by a $28 million working capital release, though the company explicitly declined to resume share buybacks due to market conditions. Management expressed cautious optimism about demand stabilization but highlighted persistent pricing pressure from Chinese and Angolan imports.

negative_highlights: GAAP net loss widened to a $2 million loss (-3% margin) due to stock-based compensation costs.
Branded performance marketing spend saw a 9% pullback in the quarter, though management notes this is not expected to be a significant driver of growth for the rest of the year.
positive_highlights: Revenue exceeded the high end of guidance at $75M, driven by a self-serve channel growing 32% YoY to comprise roughly 67% of total revenue.
Adjusted EBITDA reached $10 million (13% margin), representing a $12 million improvement over last year and beating the prior guide range significantly.
Platform WAU grew sequentially for the second consecutive quarter, reaching an all-time high of 22.9M users.
summary: Nextdoor reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $75 million (up 15% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $10 million, beating the high end of its prior guidance range ($71M-$73M). Management raised full-year outlooks for both revenue growth to low teens and adjusted EBITDA margin to approximately 10%. Platform WAU reached an all-time high of 22.9 million with two consecutive quarters of sequential growth.

negative_highlights: Total gross profit decreased by 6.4% (from $39.8M to $37.3M) driven primarily by the lower margin profile of Pioneer Power.
ODR organic revenue declined 3.4%, and GCR margins contracted significantly due to project timing issues rather than execution failures.
positive_highlights: Total bookings reached $616 million over the past three consecutive quarters, demonstrating underlying demand health despite near-term margin pressure.
The company completed its acquisition of CYMCOR for $30 million to expand geographic reach in data centers and enhance program management capabilities.
summary: Limbach Holdings reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $173.5 million and adjusted EPS of $0.64, both missing expectations due to project timing and softness in healthcare/institutional markets which pressured gross margins down to 21.5%. Management lowered its Adjusted EBITDA guidance range for the full year while raising the revenue outlook to reflect acquisition contributions and execution adjustments.
