Customers spending over $100,000 grew to 354 (15% YoY, 77% of LTM revenue) and generative/agentic AI revenue more than tripled year-over-year, though the newly announced Unified Litigation Solution carries no near-term revenue and was explicitly excluded from 2026 models.

negative_highlights: Production fell 9% sequentially and 12% year-over-year due to Canadian dispositions and unplanned lift failures
Oil sales volume decreased despite higher prices, with lower Colombia differentials offsetting price gains
Announced definitive agreement to note all oil businesses in Colombia and Ecuador
positive_highlights: Net income of $25 million compared to a net loss of $13 million in Q2 2025
Adjusted EBITDA increased to $85 million from $74 million in the prior quarter
Completed $123 million capital carry commitment on Sur Oriente block improving future economics
summary: Gran Tierra Energy reported Q2 FY2026 net income of $25 million and adjusted EBITDA of $85 million, driven by stronger commodity prices (M-1 benchmark at $101.89/bbl) and lower operating costs ($52m). However, production declined 9% sequentially due to Canadian asset dispositions and operational issues in Ecuador, while the company announced a definitive agreement to watch its Colombia and Ecuador businesses.

negative_highlights: Government services segment Adjusted operating income decreased $2.3 million due to elevated transition costs, overtime ($3.3M), fuel price pass-through delays ($1.5M impact), and supply chain penalties.
Supply chain challenges regarding Leonardo AW189 deliveries delayed aircraft modifications, adversely impacting 2026 adjusted operating income by approximately $8 million.
OES revenue guidance range was tightened despite higher Q2 performance due to increased certainty around future revenues.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA increased $20.5 million sequentially driven by higher revenues across segments and lower repairs/maintenance costs.
Berry Aviation acquisition closed successfully with a presence now on six continents, expected to be immediately accretive to earnings and free cash flow.
OES business performance improved due to higher rates in Europe/Americas and consistent activity in Africa.
summary: Bristow Group reported Q2 FY2026 results with revenues of $23.1 million higher than the prior quarter and Adjusted EBITDA up by $20.5 million compared to Q1. Management affirmed full-year 2026 guidance for total revenue ($1.6 billion-$1.7 billion) but tightened OES revenue guidance while updating government services segment guidance due to transition costs and supply chain delays impacting profitability. The company closed the acquisition of Berry Aviation, which is expected to be accretive, and continues pursuing the sale of its Norway Offshore Energy Services business.

negative_highlights: Revenue missed expectations primarily due to Google's policy change deprecating Explore More (impacting over $20 million of ex-TAC in H2) and removal of low-quality publishers.
Average revenue per scaled advertiser remained relatively flat despite a 2% growth in the number of scaled advertisers YoY.
Foreign exchange represented roughly a $7.5 million headwind to adjusted EBITDA, with FX expected to remain a drag for the remainder of 2026.
positive_highlights: xTAC gross profit increased 12% year-over-year to $192.4 million driven by higher ad rates and mix shifts towards premium publishers.
Adjusted EBITDA of $55.5 million came in above the high end of guidance with a margin of 29%.
Strategic win secured with Fox News, expanding partnership across the Fox ecosystem including local news, sports, and weather.
summary: Taboola reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $476.8 million (up 2% YoY), which missed the high end of its guidance due to a Google policy change deprecating Explore More and an aggressive cleanup of low-quality international publishers. Despite these headwinds, xTAC gross profit grew 12% YoY to $192.4 million driven by higher ad rates and mix shifts, while adjusted EBITDA came in at the high end of guidance ($55.5m). Management raised full-year ex-TAC guidance to a midpoint range reflecting these impacts but noted that revenue would have exceeded expectations absent the specific headwinds.

negative_highlights: Blended acquisition cap rate was lower than the prior quarter, though management attributed this to design choices within their Core Plus Fund.
New client rent recapture rates were materially below portfolio averages due to a small number of new tenant deals involving strategic haircuts.
positive_highlights: AFFO per share grew 3.8% to $1.09 in Q2 with YTD growth accelerating to 5.2%.
Full-year investment volume guidance raised from $9.5 billion to $10 billion due to robust pipeline strength.
Global investments totaled approximately $2.6 billion at a weighted average cash yield of 7.3%, including new data center JV activity.
summary: Realty Income reported strong Q2 FY26 results with AFFO per share growing 3.8% to $1.09 and YTD growth accelerating to 5.2%. Management raised full-year guidance for both AFFO (midpoint up $0.02) and investment volume ($10B vs prior $9.5B), citing a robust pipeline, disciplined capital allocation, and successful execution of new funding channels including the Cloud Capital data center JV.

negative_highlights: Reported interactive margin was depressed by the doubling of U.K. tax rates from ~21% to 40%
Sequential revenue growth in interactive decelerated due to the full impact of new taxes
First-half free cash flow conversion is lower than pro forma estimates due to a $7 million restructuring outflow
positive_highlights: Interactive revenue grew 15% and EBITDA grew 13% year-over-year despite the tax hike
U.K. gross gaming revenue increased 40% year-over-year, demonstrating strong underlying demand
Retail solutions achieved adjusted EBITDA margins above 50%, a first for the segment
summary: Second quarter revenue and EBITDA of $61 million and $27 million were in line with expectations but impacted by a near doubling of the U.K. Remote Gaming Duty which negated underlying gross gaming growth. Management raised full-year free cash flow conversion guidance to over 25% from prior guidance, citing pro forma adjustments for one-time working capital outflows rather than operational improvement.

negative_highlights: Revenue and Adjusted EBITDA fell note weakness in of the midpoint of guidance ranges due to lighter model improvement pace in Q2.
Higher compute costs associated with training existing models and new development reduced sequential flow-through to Adjusted EBITDA to 70%.
positive_highlights: Consumer vertical advertiser spend set another record, finishing 28% above Q4 2025 levels despite being a seasonally slow period.
MAX publisher earnings grew double digits quarter-over-quarter with consistent share of waterfalls.
SEC inquiry concluded with no recommended action.
summary: AppLovin reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $1.92 billion (up 53% YoY) and Adjusted EBITDA of $1.61 billion (up 58% YoY), both falling slightly below the midpoint of guidance ranges due to lighter-than-normal model improvement timing rather than demand weakness or competitive issues. Management noted that Q3 is off to a strong start with new model improvements now live, leading them to raise their full-year outlook and guide for Q3 revenue between $2.055 billion and $2.085 billion (46%-48% YoY growth). The company repurchased approximately 1.14 million shares ($551 million) during the quarter while maintaining a net leverage of roughly 0.1x.

negative_highlights: Total revenue declined 16% year-over-year due to a $19 million drop in eXtend and AV ancillary revenues.
Daily throughput per stall was 2% lower year-over-year, softer than expected as the network enters 2026.
Adjusted EBITDA loss of $10.6M widened compared to prior periods due to non-charging headwinds.
positive_highlights: Core charging business delivered its 18th consecutive quarter of double-digit year-over-year revenue growth (up 19%).
EVgo announced a strategic agreement to deploy EVgo-branded Superchargers with Tesla, effectively doubling the addressable market.
Mature 350 kW stalls are already operating at mid-2028 levels of daily throughput per stall.
summary: EVgo reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $83 million, a 16% year-over-year decrease driven entirely by lower non-charging business (eXtend and AV), while core charging network revenue grew 19%. Adjusted EBITDA was a loss of $10.6 million in the quarter, aligning with prior guidance but missing market expectations for profitability given the top-line miss.

negative_highlights: Adjusted combined ratio increased to 76.7% from 73.1% YoY, primarily driven by higher attritional losses in the rapidly growing crop book.
Commercial earthquake rates declined more than 20%, and large commercial new business pricing faced pressure below technical levels.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EPS grew 34% driven by opportunistic buybacks and strong underwriting performance across a diversified portfolio.
Crop gross written premium surged 96% YoY, with full-year outlook raised to over $400 million from an initial expectation of ~$280-$350 million (implied).
Company initiated a quarterly dividend of $0.45 per share and repurchased approximately 369k shares at attractive prices.
summary: Palomar Holdings reported a strong Q2 FY2026 with adjusted net income of $63.8 million (up 31% YoY) and gross written premium increasing 27%. Management raised full-year adjusted net income guidance to the range of $270-$280 million, citing record crop growth exceeding initial expectations despite higher attritional losses in that segment.

GMV of $96M rose 7% and revenue of $23.3M rose 5%, both above the high end of guidance, with adjusted EBITDA margin of ~6% versus over 13 points of prior-year expansion; gross margin was 73.9%, up 210 bps. The company upgraded its full-year framework to expect GMV growth for 2026 and reaffirmed a Q4 GMV growth milestone, though Q3 guidance of $89-94M GMV is flat to up 6% and adjusted EBITDA margin of -1% to +2%. Full-year revenue take rates were lowered to ~24-25% from 25-26% on mix shift to higher-value orders, and positive free cash flow for 2026 is now unlikely due to a $5.9M payment-processor cash reclassification, which management says has no economic impact. Active buyers fell 10% to ~57,700 on deliberate sales-and-marketing cuts, and adjusted EBITDA margin is guided sequentially lower in the seasonally soft Q3.

negative_highlights: Total net product revenue decreased by approximately 34% year-over-year, primarily due to lower demand for ELEVIDYS.
Management explicitly expects total net product revenue in the second half of 2026 to be modestly lower than the first half as new patient cohorts progress through the treatment journey.
Q3 ELEVIDYS revenue is expected to trend lower than Q2 due to variability inherent in one-time gene therapy sales cycles.
positive_highlights: Company delivered GAAP and non-GAAP operating profitability for the quarter with combined R&D and SG&A expenses decreasing significantly year-over-year on a non-GAAP basis.
Cash and investments increased by approximately $197 million during the quarter, strengthening liquidity to fund pipeline initiatives independently.
PMO franchise remains stable with adherence rates exceeding 90% despite competitive pressures expected later in 2027.
summary: Sarepta reported Q2 FY26 net product revenue of $329 million and total revenues of $401 million, representing a significant year-over-year decline driven by lower demand for ELEVIDYS which performed in line with expectations. Management narrowed its full-year 2026 guidance to the range of $1.2 billion-$1.3 billion (lower than prior) while raising collaboration revenue guidance due to higher contract manufacturing from Roche, and tightened operating expense guidance to reflect disciplined cost management.

negative_highlights: Gross written premium declined 2% year-over-year to $340 million in a challenging direct market environment.
Management expects PIF growth to be relatively flat on a year-over-year basis by end of 2026 if the competitive environment persists.
Average premiums came down somewhat nationally, with management indicating rates are currently overpriced by approximately 3%.
positive_highlights: Net income increased 15% year-over-year to $25 million, generating a 31% annualized return on equity.
Policies in force grew 6% year-over-year to 484,000 despite sequential runoff and competitive pressure.
Partnership and independent agent channels represented approximately 51% of new writings during the quarter.
summary: Root reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $389 million (up 2% YoY) and net income of $25 million (up 15% YoY), though gross written premium declined 2%. Management guided for relatively flat year-over-year Policies in Force growth by the end of 2026 due to a competitive direct market environment, while noting that PIF is currently flat with Q2 levels. The net combined ratio improved to 92%, driven by an expense ratio decline partly attributable to lower performance-based equity compensation.

negative_highlights: Software gross margin contracted from 76% to 71%, reflecting revenue recognition timing on accelerated transition to hosted licensing.
Contribution ACV declined year-over-year due to the completion of initial Gates Foundation funding for Predictive Toxicology.
positive_highlights: ACV grew 27% year-over-year driven by broad-based demand and new product launches including Predictive Toxicology.
Hosted revenue percentage accelerated significantly, rising to 47% of software total in Q2 compared to 31% last year.
Net income turned positive at $6 million following a net loss of $43 million in the prior-year quarter.
summary: Second quarter revenue was $58.9 million with ACV growth of 27% year-over-year to $29.6 million, driven by new products like Predictive Toxicology and the launch of Bunsen. Management raised full-year drug discovery guidance from a prior range of $55M-$65M to $65M-$75M due to a specific $10M milestone payment received from Ajax Therapeutics.

negative_highlights: Issued 11.8 million partnership units for Stellus acquisition, increasing diluted shares outstanding to ~130 million
Leverage ratio elevated pro forma to approximately 2.8x EBITDA following the June acquisition
positive_highlights: Fee-related earnings increased 10% year-over-year to $39 million
Core fee rate expanded three basis points sequentially to 100 bps in Q2
AUM surpassed the milestone of $50 billion at period end
summary: Ridgepost Capital reported Q2 FY2026 results with fee-related earnings of $39 million (up 10% YoY) and adjusted EPS of $0.24 per share (vs $0.23 in prior year). Fee revenue grew 11% to $81 million, driven by a core fee rate increase to 100 bps and strong AUM growth where fee-paying AUM rose 19% YoY to nearly $35 billion. Management reiterated full-year FRE margin guidance for the mid-40s despite Stellus integration costs.

negative_highlights: Softness among smaller U.S. spine distributors (representing ~20% of revenue) continues with performance below expectations.
Non-GAAP adjusted gross margin was 71.7%, reflecting an unfavorable geography mix during the quarter.
European MDR strategy creates a discrete timing headwind, expected to reduce net sales by approximately $22 million in 2027.
positive_highlights: Global limb reconstruction net sales grew 11% on a constant currency basis led by TrueLok Elevate and Fitbone adoption.
Biologics business moved from double-digit declines to approximately flat year-over-year growth for the second consecutive quarter, indicating stabilization.
CMS restored Medicare reimbursement for bone growth stimulators retroactive to May 18th, removing a meaningful headwind for Therapeutic Solutions.
summary: Orthofix reported Q2 FY2026 net sales growth of approximately 5% on a pro forma constant currency basis and raised its full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance to $95-$98 million from the prior May outlook. The beat was driven by double-digit growth in global limb reconstruction, stabilization in biologics following declines, and the restoration of Medicare reimbursement for bone growth stimulators which removed a headwind. However, management explicitly noted that profitability trends were impacted by unfavorable geographic mix, credit losses in international markets, and ongoing softness among smaller U.S. spine distributors where performance remains below expectations.

negative_highlights: Beef inflation accelerated throughout the quarter, peaking in June at record-high levels that exceeded original expectations.
Restaurant-level margins declined 90 basis points year-over-year to 23% due to higher food costs and operating expenses.
Management announced a strategic shift away from quarterly guidance citing volatility, leaving investors without near-term visibility on EBITDA targets.
positive_highlights: Same-store sales growth extended to a streak of 22 consecutive quarters with positive comp sales excluding World Cup impact.
Digital ecosystem delivered strong traffic, with comparable app channel sales growing nearly 30% year-over-year.
Company opened 16 new company-operated Shacks in the quarter, exceeding last year's pace and staying on track for a total of 60-65 openings.
summary: Shake Shack reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $417.6 million (up 17.2% YoY) and same-store sales growth of 3.5%, driven by new openings and digital channel strength despite a challenging cost environment. Management delivered results within the revised guidance range but explicitly moved away from providing quarterly outlooks, retaining only full-year annual guidance which remains at the low end due to elevated beef inflation persisting into the second half. While CEO Rob Lynch expressed confidence in long-term resilience and traffic momentum, CFO Michelle Hook noted that restaurant-level margins declined 90 bps YoY as record-high beef costs outweighed operational efficiencies.

negative_highlights: Q4 exabyte growth of 22% was below the prior quarter's pace, though management attributes this to product mix variations rather than a demand slowdown.
Sequential incremental gross margin guidance for Q1 FY27 is lower (80-81%) compared to Q4 actuals (84-85%), reflecting expected quarterly fluctuations.
positive_highlights: Revenue beat high end of guidance driven by a 44% YoY increase in exabyte shipments to 231 EB.
Gross margin expanded significantly year-over-year to 54.4%, aided by favorable pricing and mix shift to higher capacity drives.
Management confirmed strong LTA visibility extending through calendar years 2029-2031 with customers.
summary: Western Digital reported Q4 FY26 revenue of $3.75 billion (up 44% YoY) and EPS of $3.56 (up 109% YoY), beating the high end of guidance with gross margins expanding to 54.4%. Management raised visibility on AI-driven demand, citing strong LTA extensions through 2031, while guiding Q1 FY27 revenue at midpoint growth and EPS between $3.85-$4.15.

negative_highlights: EBIT margin compressed year-over-year by 550 basis points due to deliberate strategic investments over note weakness in-term profitability.
Acquiring margins in Mexico faced compression from device restocking losses and memory chip cost inflation.
positive_highlights: Net revenue surpassed $10 billion for the first time with a robust 50% year-over-year growth rate.
Credit portfolio reached $16.4 billion growing 75% YoY, supported by NPLs at historical lows (7.0% total) and normalized provisions in Brazil.
Brazil commerce conversion improved significantly (+1.1 percentage points YoY) following the free shipping threshold change.
summary: MercadoLibre reported Q2 FY2026 net revenue surpassing $10 billion for the first time with a year-over-year growth of 50%, while income from operations was $683 million representing an EBIT margin of 6.7%. Sequentially, margins were broadly stable but down 550 basis points year-on-year due to strategic investments in Brazil commerce (lower take rates), device restocking costs in Mexico, and energy cost absorption. Management emphasized strong cash generation ($214M adjusted free cash flow) despite high capital expenditures of $441 million.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA margin remained flat at 6.4% compared to the prior year quarter.
Revenue growth was impacted by timing differences in new contract startups and exits.
No specific quantitative guidance provided for AI/automation (GXO IQ) impact on margins or site count beyond qualitative targets.
positive_highlights: Strongest commercial quarter in three years with new business wins up more than 30% YoY to $410 million, driven by strategic verticals like data centers and aerospace/defense.
Record level of incremental revenue secured for the full year at over $1 billion ($353 million specifically for 2027).
Balance sheet strengthened with net leverage down to 2.6x from 3x, positive free cash flow generation, and resumption of share buybacks.
summary: GXO reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $3.4 billion (up 4% YoY) and adjusted EPS of $0.59, with an EBITDA margin of 6.4% consistent with the prior year quarter. Management reiterated full-year guidance for organic growth at 4%-5%, adjusted EBITDA between $945 million-$965 million, and diluted EPS between $2.95-$3.15, citing strong commercial momentum in strategic verticals like data centers and aerospace/defense. The company highlighted a record of over $1 billion in incremental revenue secured for 2026 and resumed share repurchases.

negative_highlights: RVO costs remain elevated due to the absence of Small Refinery Exemptions for qualifying refineries in 2025.
Wholesale marketing contribution was partially offset by a $3 million reduction in asphalt results amid price volatility.
Refining margins face headwinds as crude differentials and backwardation curves have flattened compared to Q2 levels.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EPS beat expectations at $5.48 per share driven by stronger refining margins and higher throughput following the Big Spring turnaround completion.
Logistics segment delivered record quarterly adjusted EBITDA of approximately $144 million across all Permian Basin offerings.
Delek Logistics (DKL) reached 80% third-party income on a pro forma basis, reinforcing economic separation strategy.
summary: Delek US reported Q2 FY2026 net income of $170 million ($2.71/share) and adjusted EPS of $5.48 per share. The company reaffirmed its full-year 2026 EBITDA guidance range of $520-$560 million, citing strong execution despite Middle East volatility. Management highlighted a successful turnaround at Big Spring refinery with improved reliability and yields.

negative_highlights: Total revenue was below expectations, with the first half described as one of the most consequential periods that did not meet investor hopes for faster acceleration.
Nebulized TYVASO sales remained pressured by increasing competitive dynamics within the inhaled prostacyclin category.
Management explicitly declined to reaffirm or update 2026 revenue growth expectations, noting that while a path exists, it has 'certainly narrowed'.
positive_highlights: Total revenue of $453 million from the core TYVASO franchise, driven by record levels of starts, referrals, total patients, and commercial patients exiting the quarter.
Significant expansion of the sales force to roughly double its size, with representatives deployed in early July to increase engagement frequency across PAH and PH-ILD indications.
Submission of two major new drug applications (sNDA for nebulized TYVASO in IPF and NDA for ralinepag in PAH) representing potential multi-billion dollar growth catalysts.
summary: United Therapeutics reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of approximately $783 million, which was essentially flat with the prior quarter and below management's expectations due to competitive dynamics in the nebulized TYVASO category. Management explicitly stated they are not reaffirming or updating any prior 2026 growth guidance despite expecting a stronger second half driven by sales force expansion and record patient metrics. The company highlighted significant clinical progress with sNDA filings for ralinepag (PAH) and nebulized TYVASO (IPF), targeting potential approvals in 2027.

negative_highlights: SG&A expenses increased by 19% year-over-year to $82.1 million, primarily driven by personnel costs from sales force expansion.
R&D expenses were relatively flat at $20.4 million despite ongoing clinical investments in new indications like vitiligo and hidradenitis suppurativa.
positive_highlights: Net product revenues reached $129.9 million with a robust 59% year-over-year growth rate.
Raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to the range of $525-$540 million, reflecting strong momentum in H1.
Received FDA approval for ZORYVE cream 0.3% for plaque psoriasis in children down to age two.
summary: Arcutis Biotherapeutics reported Q2 FY26 net product revenues of $129.9 million, a 59% year-over-year increase and a 23% quarter-over-quarter rise driven by strong demand for ZORYVE in plaque psoriasis, atopic dermatitis, and seborrheic dermatitis. The company raised its full-year 2026 revenue guidance from $480-$495 million to $525-$540 million following the launch of new commercial initiatives including a virtual health platform and expanded sales forces in primary care/pediatrics. Management highlighted FDA approval for ZORYVE cream 0.3% in children as young as two years old, marking significant expansion into pediatric indications.

negative_highlights: Consolidated revenue growth was minimal at only 0.5% year-over-year.

Significant capital commitment required for SK Hyper (KRW 750 billion) with further investment needed to reach the 15 GW target, raising concerns about direct financial burden despite plans for external financing.
positive_highlights: AIDC revenue surged 92.5% year-over-year driven by the Pangyo Data Center and new Seoul construction.
Operating income expanded significantly due to base effects from prior cybersecurity incident expenses, masking underlying operational strength.
Management confirmed stable shareholder returns with a Q2 dividend of KRW 830 per share.
summary: Consolidated revenue was KRW 4,359 billion (up 0.5% YoY) and operating income reached KRW 566 billion (up 67.3% YoY), driven by the data center business which grew 92.5%. Management established a new subsidiary, SK Hyper, with an initial capital commitment of KRW 750 billion to expand AI infrastructure capacity toward a target of 15 GW.

negative_highlights: HETLIOZ net product sales plummeted 65% year-over-year to $5.6 million due to generic competition and destocking at specialty pharmacies.
NEREUS revenue was constrained to only $1 million in Q2 despite a wholesaler stocking of $15.2 million, reflecting significant uncertainty regarding patient demand and potential returns.
Operating expenses increased 23% year-over-year to $114.3 million due to commercialization spending for new launches and R&D ramp-up.
positive_highlights: Fanapt net product sales increased 23% year-over-year to $36 million, driven by a 31% increase in total prescriptions (TRx) and new-to-brand starts up 32%. Weekly TRx reached an 11-year high of over 2,700.
BYSANTI received FDA approval for bipolar I disorder and schizophrenia with launch expected in the second half of 2026. The company now has six approved products by end-of-2026.
summary: Vanda Pharmaceuticals reported Q2 FY2026 total revenues of $50.5 million, a decrease of approximately 4% year-over-year and 2% sequentially compared to the prior quarter. The decline was primarily driven by a significant drop in HETLIOZ revenue due to generic competition and shipment timing issues, partially offset by growth from Fanapt bipolar I disorder launch ($36M) and PONVORY ($7.9M). Net loss widened to $62.5 million compared to Q2 2025.

negative_highlights: Water Services revenues grew only approximately 4% sequentially, outpacing a guided decline but remaining below the top-line momentum of other segments.
Management noted that full-year free cash flow potential remains limited in 2026 due to ongoing capital investment needs for infrastructure build-out.
positive_highlights: Consolidated adjusted EBITDA of $93 million significantly beat the high end of prior guidance range ($77M-$80M).
Water Infrastructure segment delivered record quarterly revenue of $102 million with gross margins expanding to 58% before D&A.
Chemical Technologies segment achieved record-setting revenue of $96 million and sequential gross profit growth of 35%.
summary: Select Water Solutions reported Q2 FY2026 consolidated revenue of $396 million and adjusted EBITDA of $93 million, significantly beating the high end of guidance ($77M-$80M). The company delivered record revenues in its Water Infrastructure segment ($102M) and Chemical Technologies segment ($96M), while outperforming expectations in Water Services. Management raised full-year growth guidance for the Water Infrastructure segment to 25%-30% YoY, citing strong execution across all three operating segments.

negative_highlights: Q3 revenue guidance ($373M-$375M) represents a sequential deceleration compared to Q2's growth trajectory.
Gross margin is expected to vary quarter-to-quarter in the near term due to inference costs for beta products not yet monetized.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 48% YoY to $370M, marking the third consecutive quarter of accelerated growth.
Non-GAAP gross profit dollars grew 40% YoY as AI credit monetization contributed for the first full quarter.
Net dollar retention rate remained strong at 136%, with two-thirds of large customers adding full seats at renewal.
summary: Figma reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $370 million (up 48% YoY) and Non-GAAP gross profit growth accelerating to 40%, marking its first full quarter of AI credit monetization. Management raised the Full Year non-GAAP operating income guidance by approximately $40 million, citing strength in AI consumption and new product launches like Figma Agent and Code Layers. The company ended with $1.7 billion in cash equivalents.

negative_highlights: Potash segment sales declined year-over-year by roughly 10% due to lower volumes, offsetting higher prices.
Management noted a slight softness in Trio demand during late May and early June before the fall application season begins.
Net income from continuing operations was $2.4 million or $0.18 per diluted share, which includes a non-operational $5 million accrual related to water repayment obligations.
positive_highlights: Gross margin increased 35% year-over-year to $16.6 million due to stronger Trio margins and better potash production performance.
Trio delivered its lowest cost of goods sold per ton since Q4 2019, with sales increasing 7.5% despite flat volumes as average net realized note price rose 6%.
Full-year capital expenditure guidance was reduced to approximately $40 million reflecting disciplined management of the AMAX and Primary Pond 8 projects.
summary: Second quarter sales from continuing operations were flat at $66.7 million compared to the prior year, while gross margin expanded significantly by 35% to $16.6 million driven by Trio pricing and operational efficiency gains. Management raised full-year production guidance for both potash (to 290k-300k tons) and Trio (to 295k-305k tons), supported by improved recoveries, throughput increases of over 7% in Trio, and a cleaner portfolio following the $68.9 million South Ranch asset sale.

negative_highlights: FY2026 NOI guidance cut to ~$36.2M from an original ~$37.1M, citing ~$800K delayed industrial lease-up and ~$1M D.C. multifamily headwinds
Maryland same-store industrial occupancy fell to 70.6% from 92% in Q1 2025, with Chelsea still functionally vacant and no leases signed at Lakeland
D.C. multifamily: ~8% of tenants not paying, evictions taking 12-18 months, and trade-out rents ~10% below prior tenants; management said delinquency is not changing anytime soon
positive_highlights: Mining NOI rose approximately 12% year-over-year to about $4.1M and beat plan by roughly $850K
Balance sheet: debt service coverage of ~2.82x, net debt ~19% of fair market value, and ~$130M liquidity including ~$101M cash
Industrial pipeline to grow from ~800,000 sq ft at end-2025 to ~2.1M sq ft, with ~97,500 sq ft in active lease negotiations and a ~25,000 sq ft Davie lease close to signing at a strong rate
summary: FRP reported roughly $9.4M of pro forma NOI, $4.1M FFO ($0.21/share), and about $130M of liquidity ($101M cash) for Q2 FY2026, with results down modestly year-over-year. Full-year NOI guidance was cut to approximately $36.2M from an original plan of $37.1M, driven by $800K of delayed industrial lease-up and $1M of Washington D.C. multifamily headwinds, partly offset by $850K of stronger mining performance (mining NOI up ~12% YoY). Maryland same-store industrial occupancy fell to 70.6% from 92% in Q1 2025, and D.C. multifamily delinquency (~8% of tenants not paying) and trade-outs ~10% below prior rents remain unresolved. Management cited increased leasing activity but acknowledged it had not yet converted into signed leases, calling the outlook a 'more cautious optimism.'

negative_highlights: Q4 EBITDA expected to be lower than Q3 due to holiday seasonality and higher tax rates (expected ~27% vs 17%).
Operating expenses excluding one-time benefit grew 16.3%, though still well below revenue growth.
positive_highlights: Revenue of $28.3M beat the high end of guidance ($26.2-$26.7M).
Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded significantly from 23.7% to 34%. Adjusted operating income converted roughly half of incremental revenue.
Plasma business recovered with monthly revenue per center reaching $7,699, the strongest reading since Q3 FY25.
summary: Paysign reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $28.3 million (up 48% YoY) and GAAP net income of $6.8 million ($0.11/share), significantly beating the high end of guidance for both metrics. Management raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to a range of $114-$117 million, citing strength in Patient Affordability (up 89% YoY) and recovery in Plasma. Gross margin expanded 170 bps to 63.3%, driven by higher pharma mix.

negative_highlights: Adjusted free cash flow guidance lowered to $140M-$160M from prior range of $160M-$180M due to higher CapEx.
Capital spending increased significantly to an expected $135 million for the full year, up from a previously guided $120 million.
U.S. Cardiopulmonary growth was softer than international regions; Epilepsy faces a tougher sequential comparison as it lapses prior-year field safety notice impacts.
positive_highlights: Record quarterly revenue of $391 million with double-digit growth in both Cardiopulmonary (+10%) and Epilepsy segments.
Adjusted gross margin expanded 200 bps to 71%, aided by a one-time $6M tariff refund benefit (approx. 150 bps).
summary: LivaNova reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $391 million (up 9.8% constant currency) and adjusted EPS of $1.26 versus $1.05 prior year, driven by double-digit growth in Cardiopulmonary ($222M, +10%) and Epilepsy (+10%). Management raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to 8%-9% (from 7%-8%), adjusted EPS to $4.30-$4.40 (up from implied ~$4.05), but lowered free cash flow guidance to $140M-$160M due to increased capital spending on capacity expansion and IT infrastructure.

negative_highlights: Non-traded BDC space faces relative softness, though offset by significant inflows into other private wealth products like infrastructure
Q4 earnings growth may be lower sequentially as the company lapses a very strong prior year quarter in Q3
positive_highlights: Record quarterly fundraising of $77 billion led by the Just Group mandate which increased insurance capital managed by more than one-third
Fee-related earnings grew 20% year-over-year to $808 million driven by strong inflows into flagship strategies and Oaktree integration benefits
AI infrastructure strategy expanded partnership with Bloom Energy fivefold from $5 billion to $25 billion in nine months
summary: Brookfield Asset Management reported record Q2 FY2026 results with fee-related earnings of $808 million (up 20% YoY) and distributable earnings of $707 million (up 15%). The company raised a record $77 billion in the quarter, bringing year-to-date fundraising to $98 billion. Management reaffirmed expectations for a record full-year 2026 driven by strong demand across infrastructure, private equity, credit, and insurance mandates.

negative_highlights: Q2 EBITDA leverage was muted as a one-time increase in incentive compensation accruals reduced the flow-through from sales to earnings.
Management explicitly stated Q3 growth will moderate, particularly for Scent (mid-single digits) and Fragrance Ingredients due to normalizing comparables after strong H1.
$100 million of stranded costs remain post-divestiture, temporarily pressuring business unit margins until remediation is complete.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew across all three core segments (Taste +4%, Health & Biosciences +5%, Scent +8%) driven by volume and new wins.
Free cash flow generation remained robust at $378 million for H1, up $284 million YoY due to working capital improvements.
Scent segment delivered double-digit growth in Fragrance Ingredients (north of 20%), offsetting softer Fine Fragrances.
summary: IFF reported Q2 continuing operations revenue of just under $2 billion (up ~6% YoY) and Adjusted EBITDA of $408 million (up 6%), driven by volume growth across Taste, Scent, and Health & Biosciences. Management raised full-year sales guidance to a range of $7.4-$7.6B (+2%-4%) and EBITDA to $1.53-$1.6B (+4%-8%), citing strong H1 performance but explicitly warning that Q2 outperformance was not fully leveraged due to higher incentive accruals, with expectations for growth moderation in the second half of 2026.

negative_highlights: Gross margin contracted from 31% in Q2 FY2025 to 26%, driven by a 232 bps reduction due to lower HFC prices and higher freight costs.
Net income dropped sharply year-over-year, falling from $10.2 million to $4.9 million ($0.23 vs $0.12 per diluted share).
The Illinois facility was out of service for approximately three weeks due to tornado damage in June.
positive_highlights: Sales volume grew strongly by 12% despite challenging market conditions and soft pricing dynamics.
The company successfully secured a bridge contract for the DLA, resolving uncertainty after seven months of review following a competitor challenge.
Recovery volumes continued to grow as customers maintained commitment to refrigerant lifecycle management.
summary: Hudson Technologies reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $78.3 million (up 8% YoY) driven by a strong 12% volume increase, partially offset by a 6% decline in average refrigerant sales prices and higher operating expenses including freight costs related to the Middle East conflict. Net income fell significantly from $10.2 million last year to $4.9 million due to soft HFC market pricing, inflationary pressures on fuel/freight, ERP optimization costs, and legal fees associated with DLA contract re-awards. Management revised its full-year 2026 gross margin target down from mid-20% to low-to-mid-20%, citing continued trough in refrigerant prices.

negative_highlights: GAAP operating profit declined $200k sequentially, with FX reducing profits by approximately $900k compared to Q1.
Revenue was negatively impacted by a temporary delay of approximately $3 million in shipments at the KELK business due to ERP implementation challenges.
Measurement Systems revenue decreased 3% sequentially and orders fell 22%, reflecting softness in AMS, transportation, and steel markets.
positive_highlights: Sensors segment delivered a book-to-bill ratio of 1.44, driven by robust demand from semiconductor equipment makers and data center infrastructure.
Received an official vendor nomination letter for the initial humanoid robotics customer, positioning VPG to support production ramping in H2 2026.
Gross margin expanded 300 bps sequentially in Weighing Solutions to 37.3% due to cost reductions and favorable product mix.
summary: VPG reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $83.9 million (up 12% YoY) and adjusted EPS of $0.04, though GAAP resulted in a loss due to FX headwinds and restructuring costs. Management noted that sequential growth was impacted by temporary shipment delays at the KELK business related to an ERP implementation, which are expected to be resolved by Q4 2026. While order momentum remains strong with record bookings in Sensors ($48.1M), revenue guidance for H2 is not explicitly raised despite positive commentary on AI and humanoid robotics milestones.

negative_highlights: GAAP EPS of $0.59 missed the guidance range due to an acceleration of restructuring charges totaling roughly $0.91 per share.
Reported free cash flow was impacted by a one-time restructuring payment, though underlying FCF before this charge remained strong at $720 million for the year.
Backlog decreased sequentially by approximately $20 million despite growing 2.7% year-over-year.
positive_highlights: Managed services delivered record quarterly revenue of $791 million, up 2.5% year-over-year.
Non-GAAP operating margin expanded by 20 basis points sequentially and 10 bps year-over-year to 21.6%.
Signed a major multi-year flagship engagement with Liberty Latin America for end-to-end IT transformation.
summary: Q3 revenue of $1.175 billion and non-GAAP EPS of $1.84 were consistent with the midpoint of guidance, while GAAP EPS missed due to a restructuring charge. Management reiterated full-year FY2026 guidance for constant currency growth at 3% (midpoint) but tightened the reported revenue range slightly compared to prior outlooks.

negative_highlights: Full-year guidance lowered for both total revenue ($945M-$965M) and adjusted EBITDA margin (38%) following the execution of new contracts with less favorable terms.
A non-cash goodwill and intangible asset impairment charge of $104 million reduced GAAP net loss to a normalized effective tax rate context, resulting in a diluted EPS loss of $0.32 per share.
Commercial Services revenue growth is expected to decelerate into negative high single-digits for the full year due to volume modulation options and pricing adjustments.
positive_highlights: Government Solutions revenue grew 17% driven by New York City camera installations, which exceeded updated contract pricing changes to generate 36% service revenue growth in the quarter.
Commercial Services profit margins expanded 100 basis points due to operating leverage and improved cash collections.
summary: Verra Mobility reported Q2 FY26 revenue growth driven by a 17% increase in Government Solutions and a return to Commercial Services growth of 6%, though total product revenue was $17 million. The company recorded an adjusted EPS beat at $0.38 but faced significant headwinds from new, less favorable pricing terms on renewals with Avis Budget Group and Hertz, as well as a non-cash impairment charge of $104 million related to T2 Systems. Consequently, management lowered its full-year 2026 guidance for revenue ($945M-$965M) and adjusted EBITDA margins (38%), citing the revised commercial terms.

negative_highlights: Q2 consumption declined by approximately 2.5%, reversing Q1 gains
Market share lost an additional 30 basis points in the first half compared to historical levels
Industry remains soft when normalized for cost and tariff-related inflation
positive_highlights: Heinz condiments in the U.S. grew 3% year-to-date with prospects to continue improving
Emerging markets delivered a terrific quarter with Heinz up 12%
Global away from home business returned to growth
summary: Management reported a Q2 consumption decline of approximately 2.5% and noted that the second half guidance implies weaker sales growth in H2 compared to H1 at the midpoint due to shipment phasing from snowstorms (0.8 pts) and Easter benefits (0.7 pts). While management expressed confidence in improving momentum, share trends remained flat or slightly negative relative to Q1 exit rates despite investments ramping up. The company announced an incremental $100 million investment for marketing but explicitly stated no wraparound of these costs into 2027.

negative_highlights: GAAP revenue down 6% in first half due to Markel Fronting Arrangement accounting
Marketplace private sales declined due to prior year large single-owner collection sale
Hagerty Re combined ratio at 90% in Q2 due to inflationary pressures
positive_highlights: Written premium grew 19% in Q2 and first half, accelerating from 14% last year
Record 279,000 new members added in first half
Adjusted EBITDA up 32% to $160 million in first half
summary: Hagerty reported a record first half of 2026 with written premium growth of 19%, ahead of prior guidance, and adjusted EBITDA up 32% to $160 million. The company added a record 279,000 new members, crossing 3 million vehicles insured, driven by State Farm conversions. Full-year guidance was raised: written premium growth now 16%-17%, adjusted EBITDA $270-$280 million, and GAAP net income $18-$30 million. The acquisition of Bennetts, the second largest U.K. specialty motorcycle insurer, was announced post-quarter.

negative_highlights: Full-year revenue guidance was lowered due to an extended Middle East conflict impact on the travel portfolio, now expected to persist through Q4 rather than normalizing.
Other revenue (non-core portfolios) is declining as Global Payments winds down relationships that do not align with its go-forward strategy.
SMB growth in the U.K. market remains soft due to macroeconomic struggles and lower GDP levels.
positive_highlights: Adjusted operating margins expanded 70 basis points to a normalized level driven by Worldpay integration synergies and cost discipline.
Genius bookings grew over 25% sequentially in the second quarter, with new customer yields increasing 75% year-over-year demonstrating strong product demand.
Enterprise segment delivered low double-digit volume growth despite a significant headwind from reduced travel activity.
summary: Global Payments reported Q2 FY26 adjusted net revenue of $3.16 billion (4% normalized growth) and adjusted EPS of $3.46 (+12%), beating expectations despite a ~100 bps headwind from the Middle East conflict on travel volumes. Management updated its full-year 2026 guidance to constant currency adjusted net revenue growth of approximately 4-5%, citing that the negative impact of the geopolitical situation will persist through year-end rather than normalizing as previously assumed. The company returned $550 million in shares during the quarter and remains on track for over $2 billion total capital return, while projecting full-year margin expansion of roughly 150 bps.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined sharply by 48% quarter-over-quarter and 49% for the first half of the year.
Adjusted EBITDA deteriorated from -$25 million in Q1 to -$36 million in Q2, driven largely by increased lease carrying costs.
positive_highlights: Cash burn decreased to $45 million in Q2 from $38 million last year, with H1 total burn down 3% YoY due to completed restructuring.
summary: Q2 FY2026 revenue was $20 million, down 48% year-over-year to $137 million in Q2 2025, with H1 2026 revenue of $40 million excluding a one-time non-cash item. Net loss from continuing operations widened slightly to $57 million compared to $53 million last quarter, while adjusted EBITDA remained negative at -$36 million versus -$25 million in the prior year period. Management reaffirmed full-year 2026 cash burn guidance of $125-$150 million despite restructuring efforts that reduced quarterly burn.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to $25.7 million from a prior period net loss of $38 million (pro forma basis), driven by integration expenses.
Adjusted EBITDA ($19.1M) was significantly lower than the pro forma Adjusted EBITDA of $31 million in the comparable prior year quarter.
Management noted that full synergy realization on vendor contracts is still early, with larger multi-year deals yet to be executed.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA increased to $19.1 million, reflecting progress in integration despite lower pro forma comparables.
Subscriber base grew sequentially by 25,000 following World Cup engagement and new content availability (NBC/Telemundo).
Advertising CPMs showed healthy increases year-over-year for news, sports, and entertainment categories.
summary: FuboTV reported Q3 FY26 revenue of $1.474 billion (up YoY) and ended the quarter with 5.75 million North American subscribers (+2% YoY). The company delivered Adjusted EBITDA of $19.1 million, a decline from pro forma prior year levels due to integration costs in this second full quarter post-merger. Management raised fiscal 2026 guidance for Adjusted EBITDA by approximately $10M (to the upper end of the range) and maintained positive free cash flow expectations for FY27/FY28.

negative_highlights: Net investment income declined 13.8% year-over-year driven by lower base rates
Portfolio fair value decreased approximately $45 million (or ~3.6%) quarter over quarter due to market pricing moves in the broadly syndicated loan sector
Realized losses of roughly $109.8 million during the period, with YTD realized net losses totaling around $14 million
positive_highlights: Expanded share repurchase program significantly due to attractive valuations and lack of M&A opportunities
Successfully reset BDC CLO, lowering weighted average cost of debt from SOFR +1.72% to SOFR +1.39%
Non-accrual rate remained resilient at 0.29% despite macro uncertainty
summary: Palmer Square Capital BDC reported Q2 FY26 net investment income of $12 million ($0.39/share), missing the prior year's $13.8 million due to lower base rates and a portfolio fair value decline from $1.15 billion in Q1 to $1.11 billion, reflecting unrealized losses. Management raised share repurchases by approximately 4x (to ~$30M) as deal activity remained subdued while maintaining the dividend at current levels.

negative_highlights: IntelliQuick CT/NG test submission withdrawn following FDA feedback, delaying expected launch
Operating cash flow remained negative at -$9.9 million in Q2
G&A expenses increased year-over-year due to non-recurring legal and professional service costs related to activism
positive_highlights: Total revenue of $30.6 million exceeded guidance range
GAAP gross margin expanded sequentially by 120 bps to 43.5%
FDA clearance received for Colli-Pee Dx urine collection kit with NucleoPrecision Technology
summary: Total revenue was $30.6 million in Q2 FY2026, exceeding the company's guidance range and growing sequentially by 9.7%. GAAP gross margins expanded 120 basis points to 43.5%, driven by operational efficiencies and lower scrap costs. Management raised concerns regarding a delay for the IntelliQuick CT/NG test due to FDA feedback but maintained its full-year revenue growth outlook.

negative_highlights: U.S. food service revenues fell sharply by 27.6% due to distribution losses among smaller operators.
Gross margin was negatively impacted by higher materials costs and manufacturing expenses including depreciation drag from China cessation.
Management explicitly stated they are providing only limited net revenue guidance given ongoing uncertainty.
positive_highlights: Net revenues came in at roughly $4 million above the high end of the prior quarter's guidance range ($60M-$65M).
Sequential revenue decline slowed significantly from -19.7% to -8.2%, indicating stabilization.
International retail channel grew 16.5% year-over-year, driven by double-digit growth in Europe and Canada.
summary: Net revenues decreased 8.2% year-over-year to $68.8 million in Q2 FY2026, driven by a 9.5% decline in volume partially offset by a 1.4% increase in net revenue per pound. Gross margin was 8.5%, reflecting the drag of China cessation costs and lower overhead absorption due to reduced volumes. Management provided limited guidance for Q3, expecting revenues between $60 million and $65 million.

negative_highlights: Global Print organic revenues declined 3% on an organic basis
Tax, Audit & Accounting transactional growth fell note weakness in of expectations due to go-to-market execution challenges and product update timing shifts
Q3 adjusted EBITDA margin guidance lowered slightly from Q2 levels due to $19 million in severance expense
positive_highlights: Big 3 organic revenue growth accelerated sequentially from 9% to 10%
Legal professionals segment grew organically at a record pace, excluding government which remained strong at 11%
Adjusted EBITDA increased 29% YoY in free cash flow terms and margins expanded year-over-year
summary: Thomson Reuters reported Q2 FY26 organic revenue growth of 8%, with Big 3 segments accelerating to 10% and Legal professionals reaching double-digit growth driven by CoCounsel Legal momentum. Adjusted EBITDA rose 10% YoY to $745 million, while the company announced a definitive agreement to watch a majority stake in Global Print for approximately $500 million cash proceeds. Management raised full-year revenue guidance to the high end of its prior range and reaffirmed an adjusted margin outlook of approximately 40%, noting Q3 will include roughly $19 million in severance expense.

negative_highlights: Prudential of Japan (POJ) voluntary sales suspension continues to impact international results despite resilient third-party channel performance
Management explicitly declined to provide new forward guidance or revenue targets for two quarters due to execution complexity and POJ resumption timeline
PRT institutional retirement sales remained muted in the quarter with a notable absence of jumbo transactions
positive_highlights: Adjusted operating income of $1.4 billion was 14% higher year-over-year
PGIM private capital deployment grew nearly 60% sequentially, driven by asset-backed finance and investment-grade credit
Group Insurance delivered record quarterly earnings with strong sales in the middle market
summary: Prudential reported Q2 FY2026 adjusted operating income of $1.4 billion ($4.08 per share), representing a 14% year-over-year increase driven by business growth in PGIM and international segments, though the quarter was impacted by voluntary sales suspensions at Prudential of Japan (POJ). Management outlined a refreshed strategy to narrow its geographic footprint, exit emerging markets with over $3 billion in capital rotation, and target approximately $750 million in pre-tax run-rate efficiency benefits by year-end 2028. While the company beat earnings expectations due to fundamental growth and one-time items, it explicitly declined to provide new forward guidance for two quarters while waiting for POJ sales resumption.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA declined 45% due to a deliberate increase in U.S. promotional spend, investments in prediction markets, World Cup marketing, and one-off historical tax costs of $95 million.
Full-year revenue guidance was reduced by $395 million (to midpoint $17.91 billion) primarily due to the confirmed NFL season delay impacting H2 forecasts.
U.S. sportsbook trends were 6% lower year-over-year, reflecting a six percentage point negative impact from unfavorable customer-friendly sports results in June.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 3% year-over-year reflecting M&A benefits and strong engagement during the FIFA World Cup in both U.S. and international markets.
U.S. sportsbook active users increased by 25% year-over-year during NBA Finals, with record weeks seen in MLB leading into the NFL season.
International revenue grew 10%, driven by exceptional growth in Italy (including SNAI acquisition) and SEA iGaming up 34%.
summary: Flutter reported Q2 FY26 revenue growth of 3% and adjusted EBITDA declining by 45%, driven primarily by a net loss of $296 million due to significant investments in U.S. generosity (promos) and one-off historical tax costs of $95 million. Management updated full-year guidance downward, reducing group revenue midpoint to $17.91 billion and adjusted EBITDA to $2.655 billion following a confirmed NFL season delay impacting the second half outlook.

positive_highlights: Net revenue grew 17% year-over-year and 11% quarter-over-quarter to $57.5 million.
summary: Geron reported Q2 FY26 net revenue of $57.5 million, representing a 17% year-over-year increase and an 11% quarter-over-quarter gain. The company delivered H1 2026 net revenue growth of approximately 24%, exceeding the prior period's trajectory while maintaining financial discipline with total operating expenses down 4%. Management reaffirmed full-year RYTELO guidance at $220 million-$240 million, expecting to finish in the mid-to-high end of that range.

negative_highlights: R&D expenses increased 22% quarter-over-quarter to $109.1 million (excluding stock-based comp) reflecting continued investment in the advancing clinical portfolio
Acknowledged increase in placebo rates observed in recent AD studies, requiring study power adjustments
positive_highlights: Completed enrollment in Phase II-B AD trial approximately six months ahead of schedule
$45 million option exercise fee from Gilead Sciences and $20 million milestone payment from Sanofi recognized in Q2 revenue
KT-621 expected to report top-line data by year-end 2026, initiating Phase III around mid-2027
summary: Kymera Therapeutics reported Q2 FY2026 collaboration revenue of $65 million, driven by a $45M Gilead option exercise and a $20M Sanofi milestone for KT-485. The company completed enrollment in the Phase II-B AD trial six months ahead of schedule with top-line data expected year-end 2026, while maintaining financial strength with approximately $1.5 billion in cash runway extending into 2029.

negative_highlights: Net new customer additions of 7,000 missed the prior guidance range of 9-10k due to weaker conversion rates and buyer hesitancy.
Management lowered full-year guidance for constant currency growth (to ~16%) citing persistent headwinds from pricing changes and demand environment shifts.
positive_highlights: Operating margin expanded three points year-over-year to 20% despite AI investment costs.
Deals over $120k ARR grew 38% year-over-year, reflecting strong up-market demand.
AI adoption is accelerating with Data Agent activations up 80% quarter-over-quarter.
summary: Q2 revenue grew 17% in constant currency and operating margin expanded to 20%, but net new customer additions of 7,000 missed the prior guidance range of 9-10k due to deliberate pricing changes and increased budget sensitivity. Management raised Q3 full-year guidance for as-reported revenue (up ~14%) and non-GAAP EPS ($3.25-$3.27) while explicitly stating that headwinds from product trials, lower entry prices, and customer optimization will persist through the second half of 2026.

negative_highlights: Gross profit margin for Electronic Components was down 14 basis points year-over-year to 10.4%, though up sequentially, due to mix shifts and pricing dynamics.
Inventory days increased slightly to 71 from 69 in the prior quarter as working capital grew $559 million primarily driven by a $1.2B increase in accounts receivable.
positive_highlights: Record Q4 sales of $8.3B representing a 48% year-over-year increase with all three regions growing double digits sequentially and YoY.
Adjusted operating margin expanded to 3.8%, the fourth consecutive quarter of expansion, driven by volume growth and pricing power in memory components.
Q1 FY27 guidance raised significantly on sales ($9B-$9.3B) and EPS ($2.80-$2.90), implying a sequential increase of approximately 10% at the midpoint.
summary: Avnet reported record Q4 FY26 sales of $8.3 billion (up 48% YoY) and adjusted EPS of $2.28, significantly beating the high end of guidance. The company achieved a record operating margin of 3.8%, driven by broad-based volume growth across all regions and pricing increases in memory components which accounted for roughly one-third of gross profit dollar growth. Management raised Q1 FY27 sales guidance to $9 billion-$9.3 billion (implying ~10% sequential growth) and EPS guidance to $2.80-$2.90, citing strong backlog visibility extending into 2027.

negative_highlights: Net unrealized gains on investments decreased NAV by $0.04 per share due to widening credit spreads in the equity market multiples.
Management explicitly stated they do not have specific guidance for the Structured Credit Partners JV dividend contribution beyond medium-run targets.
positive_highlights: Repayment activity increased by approximately 70% compared to Q1, driven by refinancings and M&A payoffs including TS Imagine which delivered an unlevered IRR of 15%.
Weighted average spread on new first lien investments reached 690 bps, significantly outperforming BDC peers at 527 bps due to disciplined underwriting processes.
Portfolio credit quality remains stable with no additions to non-accrual status and improving interest coverage ratios across core borrowers.
summary: Sixth Street Specialty Lending reported Q2 net investment income of $0.43 per share and NAV stable at $16.24, driven by a sequential increase in repayment activity that generated $55 million in payoffs and $0.08 per share in fees. Management noted direct lending volumes declined sequentially due to market volatility but highlighted improving M&A pipeline momentum for the second half of 2026. While earnings beat expectations relative to the base dividend, guidance remains tied to portfolio turnover rather than a specific raised target.

negative_highlights: Second quarter Waha pricing was described as tough, though management noted strong positioning for the balance of the year
Stock underperformed relative to new large-cap peer group due to market uncertainty regarding asset sales and portfolio direction
positive_highlights: Oil production beat the midpoint of guidance by 2% at 503,000 barrels per day
Total capital spending came in $68 million below the guide's midpoint ($1.3 billion vs ~$1.34B)
$1.7 billion adjusted free cash flow generated with a reinvestment rate of 43%
summary: Devon Energy reported Q2 FY2026 results reflecting legacy operations plus Coterra from May 7th, beating guidance on oil production (503k bpd vs midpoint) and total volumes while spending $1.3B in capital below the guide's midpoint. The company delivered $1.7 billion of adjusted free cash flow and raised its quarterly dividend by 33% to $0.32/share alongside a resumption of share buybacks post-merger. Management tightened full-year production guidance ranges for oil (495k-505k bpd) and total volumes (~1.4M boe/d), citing strong first-half execution.

negative_highlights: SaaS ARR growth decelerated from the prior year's spike (which included large wins like John Deere) as comparables normalize.
Management noted a transition period where declining traditional service contracts offset subscription revenue growth, potentially capping near-term top-line acceleration.
positive_highlights: Revenue of $339 million beat consensus estimates by exceeding the high end of guidance range.
Gross margins expanded to 62.7%, driven by timely pricing actions and a 40-basis-point improvement in product margins.
Supply chain secured into fiscal 2028, allowing Extreme to meet demand while competitors face lead time constraints.
summary: Extreme Networks reported Q4 FY26 revenue of $339 million (up 10% YoY) and EPS of $0.32 (up 28% YoY), both exceeding consensus estimates. Gross margins expanded to 62.7%, driven by pricing actions and supply chain improvements, while operating margin rose to 15.7%. Management raised full-year FY27 guidance for revenue ($1.38B-$1.40B) and EPS ($1.28-$1.33), citing strong demand, a secured supply chain through fiscal 2028, and continued upmarket migration.

negative_highlights: Surgical Solutions revenue declined 5% YoY due to timing shifts of Ultrasonics capital placements and international orders.
Restorative Therapies revenue fell 2% driven by changes in Medicare patient mix and a challenging prior-year comparison.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 20 bps to 23% despite increased investments in growth drivers.
Pain Treatments business delivered double-digit revenue growth, led by strong volume gains for DUROLANE.
Cash from operations totaled $20 million with a trajectory expected to approximately double in the second half.
summary: Bioventus reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $153 million (up 4% YoY) and adjusted EPS of $0.22 per share. Management reaffirmed full-year guidance for revenue between $600-$610 million, adjusted EPS between $0.75-$0.79, and cash from operations between $84-$89 million. The company reduced net leverage to below 2x by repaying an additional $24 million of debt.

negative_highlights: Non-GAAP operating income guidance lowered to a range of $212-$218 million due to Agency acquisition costs.
Full-year non-GAAP operating margin expected at approximately 14%, down from prior outlooks.
Q3 and Q4 gross margins projected to decline slightly as text messaging growth outpaces total revenue.
positive_highlights: Revenue beat expectations with Q2 growth accelerating to 26% year-over-year.
Full-year revenue guidance raised by $12 million at the midpoint despite margin headwinds.
Enterprise momentum strong, growing larger customer base (>$50K ARR) by 36% YoY.
summary: Klaviyo reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $370.6 million, up 26% year-over-year and beating guidance, driven by strong growth in text messaging (WhatsApp) and enterprise deals including an eight-figure contract with Warner Music Group. Management raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to a range of $1.526-$1.534 billion but lowered non-GAAP operating income guidance due to acquisition costs for the Agency team, resulting in a neutral-to-positive impact on annual margins.

negative_highlights: Full-year revenue guidance was lowered by $30-$40 million due to compute cost inflation and lower instrument ASPs.
Non-GAAP gross margin declined 200 bps YoY, with cash burn breakeven pushed back one year from late 2027 to 2028.
Americas revenue declined on academic/government funding constraints, while Asia Pacific consumables fell 45% as customers worked through inventory.
positive_highlights: Consumables revenue grew 6% YoY to $20.1 million driven by expanding Revio installed base and clinical customer utilization.
Revio instrument sales rebounded with 20 units sold (up from 15), including multi-system orders for population-scale projects.
Clinical shipments surged 67% year-over-year as customers transition to routine production sequencing.
summary: PacBio reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $39 million (flat YoY) and non-GAAP gross margin contraction to 36% from 38%, driven by compute cost inflation, Vega manufacturing transition costs, and lower instrument ASPs. Management lowered full-year 2026 revenue guidance to a range of $155-$165 million and extended cash flow breakeven expectations to the end of 2028 due to persistent headwinds in memory/compute costs and slower-than-anticipated SPRQ-Nx adoption.

negative_highlights: Jet fuel prices surged by more than 80% year-over-year, causing a 93% increase in total fuel costs and creating significant cost pressure.
Consolidated load factors declined modestly from 83.5% to 81.8%, reflecting some demand softness linked to the FIFA World Cup impact on travel patterns.
Domestic Spanish-speaking countries capacity guidance was cut slightly compared to prior expectations due to a weak domestic Chile environment.
positive_highlights: Total revenues increased almost 28% year-over-year to nearly $4.2 billion driven by passenger and cargo revenue growth.
Adjusted operating margin reached 5.4%, successfully mitigating the impact of a >$700 million fuel cost headwind through fare adjustments and capacity management.
Premium revenues now represent 29% of total passenger revenues, demonstrating strong demand resilience in the premium segment.
summary: LATAM delivered a solid beat with total revenues increasing nearly 28% year-over-year to $4.2 billion and adjusted operating margins expanding to 5.4%, despite jet fuel costs rising over 93%. Management reinstated full-year guidance, raising the EBITDA midpoint by $250 million based on more constructive assumptions for H2 fuel prices while maintaining capacity growth of 9%-10%.

negative_highlights: Attraction ticket revenue grew only 3% YoY due to poor weather conditions in Canada compared to the prior year's ideal weather.
Adjusted EBITDA margin contracted approximately 90 basis points YoY as lower-margin lodging growth offset high-margin attraction drag from weather.
Full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance was reduced by roughly $2 million relative to prior expectations due to unfavorable exchange rate assumptions.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 14% YoY to record $133.5 million, driven by Tabacón's exceptional first-year performance under Pursuit ownership.
Lodging RevPAR increased 9% on a same-store basis with strong demand in the U.S., partially offsetting Canadian weather headwinds.
Completed acquisition of Eagle Wing Tours at roughly 6.5x adjusted EBITDA and sale of Flyover to strengthen balance sheet liquidity.
summary: Pursuit reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $133.5 million (up 14% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $32.7 million (up ~$3M YoY), driven by strong Tabacón performance offsetting weather impacts on attractions. Management raised full-year guidance for both revenue and adjusted EBITDA to incorporate the Eagle Wing Tours acquisition, Flyover sale proceeds, and FX headwinds while maintaining a 14% midpoint growth target. The company completed two strategic transactions: acquiring Eagle Wing Tours in Victoria and watching its non-core Flyover business.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA was flat despite revenue beat due to $32 million of temporary operating costs related to Middle East conflict and customer-driven disruptions.
EMEA sales remained below market levels with lower volumes and profitability pressured by ongoing market softness in the region.
Asia adjusted EBITDA declined 6% YoY reflecting expected margin compression from shifting mix toward local OEMs (approx. 70%) and softer ICE demand.
positive_highlights: Consolidated sales increased 5% YoY driven by favorable volume, pricing, and FX across Americas and Asia regions.
Americas region outperformed the market supported by strong volumes, recent program launches (Ram Dakota, Honda Pilot), and GM Supplier of the Year recognition for fifth consecutive year.
Asia business remains accretive with 33% YoY sales growth in China driven by NIO, Leapmotor, and Nissan ramp-ups.
summary: Adient reported Q3 FY2026 consolidated revenue of $3.9 billion (up 5% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $225 million (flat YoY), missing internal expectations due to external headwinds including Middle East conflict costs ($32M absorbed). Management raised full-year fiscal 2026 revenue guidance to approximately $15B while maintaining the adjusted EBITDA outlook at ~$885M. The company returned $30 million in share repurchases and maintains a strong balance sheet with $1.8 billion liquidity.

negative_highlights: Pediatric launch delayed due to manufacturing issues, though early demand signals are positive
