Management raised full-year operating expense guidance to $260-$270 million due to accelerated commercial investment while maintaining confidence in reaching profitability with existing capital resources, though no specific ZUSDURI revenue guidance was issued for the remainder of 2026.

negative_highlights: Smart mobile device revenue declined 6% YoY due to reduced handset forecasts driven by memory pricing shortages.
Automotive revenue decreased 13% sequentially and 10% YoY, primarily attributed to customer-led shipment timing shifts rather than demand weakness.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 9% sequentially and 6% year-over-year, exceeding the high-end of guidance ranges for both metrics.
Gross margin expanded nearly 500 bps YoY to approximately 30%, driven by a richer mix in data center technologies like silicon photonics and SiGe.
Silicon photonics revenue is expected to more than double in 2026 compared with the prior year, supported by new design wins and capacity ramping.
summary: GlobalFoundries reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $1.786 billion (up 6% YoY) and gross margin expansion of nearly 500 bps to ~30%, driven by a mix shift toward high-growth data center applications like silicon photonics which grew 62% YoY. Management raised full-year guidance for the communications infrastructure and data center end-market from high-30s growth to an expected range of 50%-60%. The company also announced its first-ever quarterly cash dividend of $0.12 per share.

negative_highlights: Gross margin on subscription business contracted slightly from 71.1% in the prior year period to 70.2%, reflecting higher veterinary invoice costs.
Average monthly revenue per pet grew only modestly by 9% YoY despite overall volume growth, indicating pricing pressure or mix shifts.
positive_highlights: Subscription adjusted operating margin expanded to 15% from 13.8% in the prior year period.
Net subscription pet growth accelerated significantly with approximately 68,100 new pets acquired via capital deployment compared to historical averages.
Lifetime value of an enrolled pet increased by 25% during the quarter due to disciplined pricing and product enhancements.
summary: Trupanion reported Q2 FY2026 subscription revenue of $276.7 million (up 14% YoY) and total adjusted operating income of $43.3 million (up 24% YoY), beating expectations with a net pet growth of approximately 18,800 pets in the quarter. Management raised full-year guidance for subscription revenue to between $1.124 billion-$1.133 billion and adjusted operating income to between $176 million-$184 million, citing improved unit economics from new product offerings like expanded deductibles and co-insurance options.

negative_highlights: Semiconductor Fabrication Solutions segment revenue declined ~13% YoY due to structural decline in silicon carbide demand with no expected recovery
R&D expenses more than doubled from prior year, though flat vs Q2, indicating potential future cost pressure as new platforms are built out
positive_highlights: Revenue beat top-end of guidance driven by AI-related demand up ~120% YoY in Thermal Processing Solutions segment
Gross margins expanded nearly 400 bps to 50%, supported by operating leverage and parts/services growth (+30%)
Book-to-bill ratio approached 1.4 for the third consecutive quarter with backlog building into FY27
summary: Amtech Systems reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $22.4 million (up 14% YoY) and GAAP EPS of $0.10, beating guidance with gross margins expanding to 50%. Management raised the Q4 revenue outlook range slightly while maintaining Adjusted EBITDA margin expectations in the low-to-mid teens despite a shift from CEO Bob Daigle to Guy Shechter.

negative_highlights: Agentic traffic remains low despite testing, as consumers prioritize end-to-end experience over specific AI sourcing methods.
Take rate expected to flatten or decline slightly in Q3 and lower again in Q4 due to seasonal increases in Dasher costs.
International markets are described as 'minimum viable scale' businesses where market position does not always correlate directly with economic profile.
positive_highlights: Accelerating restaurant growth driven by increased DashPass adoption and improved selection/quality in mature cohorts.
Record paid subscriber growth internationally, with Deliveroo showing the highest year-over-year volume growth seen in recent years.
New verticals (grocery) business is on track to be gross profit positive in the second half of the fiscal year.
summary: DoorDash reported strong underlying growth in Q2 FY26 with accelerating restaurant orders and record paid subscriber additions for DashPass across both domestic and international markets. Management highlighted significant improvements in unit economics driven by higher basket sizes from new verticals (grocery/retail) and improved retention, while noting that the quarter was impacted seasonally lower Dasher costs compared to Q1. The company reaffirmed its strategy of reinvesting efficiency gains into product development like autonomous delivery ('Dot') and AI tools rather than managing for specific take-rate targets.

negative_highlights: R&D expenses increased significantly year-over-year due to a $48 million milestone payment to Sanofi and qualification manufacturing costs.
SG&A expense rose primarily due to one-time advisory and legal fees associated with closing the Astellas agreement in Q2.
positive_highlights: Completed enrollment in ECLIPSE 2 switch cohort, providing unique data on patients transitioning from bulevirtide with no comparable competitor expected at launch.
SOLSTICE trial week-96 results showed 88% target not detected (TND) and 53% ALT normalization rates for the combination regimen versus monotherapy alone.
Received $240 million upfront payment from Astellas, strengthening cash position to approximately $1.01 billion in equivalents.
summary: Vir Biotechnology reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $238.9 million driven by a $240 million upfront payment from Astellas for the VIR-5500 collaboration and recognized net income of $80.1 million compared to a loss last year, while R&D expenses rose 40% YoY due to milestone payments and manufacturing costs. Management completed enrollment in ECLIPSE 2 (switch cohort) with top-line data expected from ECLIPSE 1 later this year, citing robust week-96 SOLSTICE trial results showing 88% target not detected rates. The company maintains a cash runway into the second half of 2028 following significant capital raises.

negative_highlights: High-volatile (high vol) metallurgical coal market remains weak due to oversupply, forcing the company to idle one of three Stonecoal sections at Elk Creek.
Diesel fuel costs increased quarterly by roughly 33% in Q2 and averaged $4.64/gallon, adding approximately $3/ton to produced coal costs compared to start-of-year levels.
Brook Mine project timeline pushed out with initial production now estimated for late 2027 or later due to supply chain constraints on large power transformers.
positive_highlights: Operational safety improved significantly with a 54% reduction in total reportable incident rate year-to-date compared to Q2 FY2025.
Company repurchased more than $66 million of Class A shares, representing over 8% of outstanding equity, utilizing record liquidity levels above $400 million.
Low-vol coal production portfolio is expanding with new underground sections at Maben and Berwind expected to add roughly 1.5 million tons annually by late 2027.
summary: Ramaco Resources reported Q2 FY2026 results where the company maintained full-year cost per ton guidance despite a $3/ton increase in coal costs driven by higher diesel prices averaging $4.64/gallon. Management highlighted that operational safety improved with a 58% reduction in incidents compared to the prior year and noted record liquidity of over $400 million following share buybacks exceeding 8%. Forward guidance remains intact for low-vol production growth, though high-vol output is expected to decline as the company idles sections at Elk Creek.

negative_highlights: Oil prices remain volatile with supply disruptions from the Iran conflict weighing on global inventories, though management views this as temporary rationing.
UAE operations in Bahrain have been intermittent due to ongoing regional conflicts, limiting immediate volume contribution there.
Delaware Basin oil growth is expected to decrease slightly year-over-year compared to other basins like Utica.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EPS reached record levels at $5.7, significantly beating expectations given the macro environment.
Total company volumes came in higher than guidance midpoint due to strong UAE initial production and domestic execution.
Capital expenditures were below guidance driven by operational timing shifts rather than a lack of opportunity.
summary: EOG delivered exceptional Q2 FY26 results with record adjusted EPS of $5.7 and free cash flow of $2.8 billion driven by robust oil prices and lower-than-expected LOE expenses. Total company volumes exceeded guidance, while capital expenditures came in below the midpoint due to operational timing shifts in Gulf States. Management reiterated its 2026 plan for low single-digit oil growth (5% total production) with unchanged full-year capex of $6.5 billion and a commitment to return at least 70% of annual free cash flow.

negative_highlights: Medical-Surgical Solutions segment saw a 20% decrease in operating profit due to product mix and one-time administrative expenses.
Free cash flow was negative $372 million for the quarter, though management noted this is typical Q1 timing driven by working capital.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EPS increased 20% YoY to $9.93 driven by strong operational performance and share repurchases.
North American Pharmaceutical revenue grew 5% with GLP-1 revenues reaching $15 billion, up approximately 24% YoY.
Oncology & Multispecialty segment delivered double-digit growth in both revenue (up 33%) and operating profit (up 41%).
summary: McKesson reported Q1 FY2027 revenue of $105 billion (up 8% YoY) and adjusted EPS of $9.93 (up 20%), both exceeding expectations with three segments delivering double-digit operating profit growth. Management raised full-year fiscal 2027 adjusted EPS guidance to a range of $44.20-$45 from the prior range of $43.80-$44.60, citing strong momentum and disciplined execution across North American Pharmaceutical ($105B revenue) and Oncology & Multispecialty (up 33%). The company also announced a new regional distribution center in Moore, Oklahoma to increase throughput by 75%.

negative_highlights: CTV revenue mix shifted due to a managed service business that declined significantly, contributing to the delta between total CTV growth (11%) and Contribution ex-TAC growth (17%).
Management noted conservatism in full-year estimates for H2 regarding potential macro risks including inflation and geopolitical challenges.
DV+ guidance decelerates slightly with a projected range of -1% to 1% growth, though still above the prior year level.
positive_highlights: CTV Contribution ex-TAC grew 36% year-over-year to $97 million, driven by mid-to-high double-digit growth in top accounts and international expansion.
DV+ returned to positive growth with a 2% increase year-over-year after prior declines.
Management raised full-year guidance for Contribution ex-TAC growth from at least 11% to between 13%-14%, and Adjusted EBITDA margin to at least 37%.
summary: Magnite reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $193 million (up 11% YoY) and Contribution ex-TAC of $190 million (up 17%), significantly beating consensus estimates. Management raised full-year guidance for both Contribution ex-TAC growth to the high teens/low double digits range and Adjusted EBITDA margin expansion, citing broad-based strength in CTV (+36% YoY) and a return to DV+ growth (+2%). The company highlighted structural tailwinds including programmatic adoption acceleration, international expansion, and early validation of its AI orchestration platform.

negative_highlights: FDA recommended conducting an additional Phase III study for volixibat in PSC, delaying planned NDA submission to H1 FY2027
New FDA review team was not fully familiar with the VISTAS data history and program background during pre-NDA discussion
positive_highlights: Net product sales reached $176 million in Q2 FY2026 compared to $128 million last year
FDA granted breakthrough therapy designation for volixibat in PSC based on VISTAS study results
Zilurgisertib NDA is proceeding as expected towards the September 2026 PDUFA date with launch preparation underway
summary: Mirum Pharmaceuticals reported Q2 FY2026 net product sales of $176 million (up from $128m prior year), raising full-year guidance to $680-$700 million. While commercial execution remains strong with durable growth in LIVMARLI and bile acid medicines, the company faces a regulatory delay for volixibat PSC NDA submission due to FDA requests for further data supplementation, pushing the filing target to the first half of 2027.

negative_highlights: EMEA revenue declined approximately 8% YoY due to regional geopolitical dynamics and budgetary pressures.
GAAP net loss widened to $12.2 million from a prior year gain of $5.6 million, driven by foreign exchange losses and litigation expenses.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 6% YoY with double-digit growth in U.S. (18%) and China segments.
Recurring revenue base expanded to represent 35% of LTM revenue, up from 32%.
New product launches including the Borealis full spectral-flow cytometer received strong early access feedback.
summary: Cytek Biosciences reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $48.1 million (up 6% YoY), driven by strong growth in the U.S. and China but offset by softness in EMEA. The company raised its full-year 2026 revenue guidance range to $207-$212 million, increasing the midpoint by $1 million while maintaining a breakeven adjusted EBITDA outlook for the year.

negative_highlights: Same-store throughput pallets declined 1.8% year-over-year due to trade-related port volume pressure with container volumes down 14%.
A $7 million legal settlement related to an employment matter impacted the Global Integrated Solutions segment NOI, lowering full-year outlook for that segment.
The Big Bear fire is expected to drag on Q3 and Q4 adjusted EBITDA by approximately $15 million due to lost revenue during recovery.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA of $320M and AFFO per share of $0.76 beat both internal expectations and consensus estimates.
Same-store physical occupancy increased 90 basis points year-over-year to approximately 80%, marking the first YoY gain since going public.
Non-same store NOI contribution came in better than expected, driven by strong demand for high-quality modern assets.
summary: Lineage reported Q2 FY26 adjusted EBITDA of $320 million and AFFO of $198 million ($0.76/share), both beating internal expectations and consensus estimates despite a legal settlement impact in the Integrated Solutions segment. Management raised full-year same-store NOI guidance to -3% to 0% (from -4% to -1%) and increased AFFO per share guidance to $2.80-$3.05, while maintaining EBITDA midpoint unchanged due to Big Bear fire headwinds estimated at approximately $15 million in Q3/Q4 impact.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to $110.2 million due to sales force expansion costs and lower ASPs
Adjusted EBITDA remained negative at -$90.3 million, reflecting the pull-forward of R&D expenses for ASCO presentation
positive_highlights: Sold over 61,000 Galleri tests in Q2, a 35% increase year-over-year
Total screening revenue reached $42.6 million, up 24% from the prior period
Completed strategic collaboration with Samsung C&T Corporation for commercialization in South Korea
summary: GRAIL reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $44.7 million, a 26% year-over-year increase driven by screening volumes exceeding 61,000 tests (up 35%). The company completed an $110 million financing with Samsung and expanded its field sales force to prepare for anticipated FDA approval in early 2027.

negative_highlights: Revenue from the largest client declined approximately 22% year-over-year, with management warning of continued headwinds through H2 2026 due to their automation and cost optimization efforts.
Trust & Safety revenue fell 12.3%, driven by declining demand at social media clients as they invest in automating content moderation workloads.
Cost of service increased to 65.3% from 61.4% year-over-year due to personnel inflation and a shift toward lower-margin U.S.-based delivery.
positive_highlights: Revenue beat guidance by $10.9 million driven by outperformance from clients other than the largest account, excluding which growth accelerated to approximately 15% year-over-year.
AI Services grew 26% year-over-year for a seventh consecutive quarter, with new signings in autonomous vehicle and robotics verticals offsetting declines at social media clients.
Management raised full-year revenue guidance range by $10 million and increased free cash flow outlook to between $110-$120 million.
summary: TaskUs reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $308.9 million, beating the top end of guidance by $10.9 million (3.6%), with adjusted EBITDA margins expanding to 18.7% versus a guided range that implied lower performance due to anticipated headwinds from its largest client. Management raised full-year revenue guidance to $1.22-$1.24 billion and increased the free cash flow outlook, citing strong growth in AI Services (up 26%) and Digital Customer Experience despite an approximate 22% decline at their top client which now represents only 20% of total revenue.

negative_highlights: Free cash flow turned negative at $6.6 million due to working capital investments and lower operating profitability.
Adjusted EBITDA margin contracted from the prior year period, impacted significantly by approximately $2.1 million in project launch costs.
Full-year free cash flow guidance was lowered despite a net sales raise.
positive_highlights: Top-line performance exceeded expectations with a 23.2% year-over-year increase driven by data center momentum.
summary: Second quarter net sales increased 23.2% year-over-year to $163 million, driven by strong data center growth and commercial vehicle recovery, though organic sales grew only 9.2%. Manufacturing margin expanded slightly to 10.9%, partially offset by approximately $2.1 million in project launch costs for new programs. Management raised full-year net sales guidance but lowered free cash flow expectations due to anticipated continued outsourcing and launch-related expenses.

negative_highlights: Net investment income per share decreased quarter-over-quarter primarily due to lower dividend income and timing of prepayment fees.
Effective yield dropped 80 basis points compared to prior periods, attributed to product mix shifts (strong sponsor finance vs. life sciences) rather than fee compression.
Significant payoffs occurred early in the quarter before redeployment could occur, creating a near-term drag on interest income.
positive_highlights: NAV grew 9% quarter-over-quarter to a record $1.3 billion, driven by accretive ATM issuances at an average 24% premium to NAV.
Record originations of $619 million in fundings and $709 million in commitments were achieved across five lending verticals.
Managed funds platform contributed $0.03 per share to NII, with the SBIC fund closing over $75 million in equity commitments.
summary: Trinity Capital reported Q2 FY26 results with record NAV of $1.3 billion (up 37% YoY) and total investment income of $87 million (a 25% increase), though net investment income per share was slightly lower at $0.51 due to timing mismatches in prepayment fees and a non-recurring dividend from Q1. The company highlighted record originations of $619 million, which were back-end weighted for the quarter, resulting in full benefits expected in Q3. Management raised guidance by reiterating confidence in earnings trajectory while noting that effective yields dropped 80 bps due to product mix and timing rather than fee impacts.

negative_highlights: Management explicitly moderated H2 guidance expectations due to the 'transactional nature' of domestic chemistry business following an anomalously high June quarter.
Guidance for Q4 excludes any financial impact from the new Puerto Rico contract, which is not expected to contribute revenue until early 2027.
positive_highlights: Data analytics revenue shattered records, achieving its highest quarterly total in company history with service revenues exceeding prior year totals by over double (223% YoY).
International chemistry revenue reached $10.6 million, representing a massive expansion from the prior year and 93% of full-year 2025 international targets.
Company secured a major new contract award with PREPA for a 400 MW project in Puerto Rico, adding approximately $400 million to the revenue backlog.
summary: Flotek reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of approximately $100 million (up ~$41M YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $16.8 million (up 109% YoY), driven by a record data analytics quarter and strong international chemistry sales in June. Management updated full-year guidance to midpoints implying significant growth versus 2025 actuals, citing the normalization of transactional domestic chemistry revenue after an exceptionally high Q2 as the primary factor for H2 moderation relative to the explosive Q1/Q2 pace. The company highlighted a new $400 million backlog from Puerto Rico and expects data analytics segment gross profit contribution to reach 51%.

negative_highlights: Net loss of $4.4 million, though improved from the prior period.
$5.4M cash outflow for a litigation success fee against Alcon partially offset by tariff refunds.
positive_highlights: Interventional dry eye achieved record quarterly revenue of $2.7 million with nearly doubling from Q1.
Gross margin expanded significantly year-over-year to 91% (excluding one-time tariff refunds).
Management raised full-year guidance while simultaneously reducing adjusted operating expense outlook.
summary: Sight Sciences reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $23.4 million (up 20% YoY), driven by record interventional dry eye revenue ($2.7M) and strong glaucoma growth ($20.7M). Management raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $88-92M while lowering adjusted operating expense guidance to $92-94M, citing improved cash usage and operational discipline.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA loss remains at $1.4 million, indicating the company has not yet achieved profitability.
Total operating expenses increased to $2.4 million due to $270,000 in severance costs and continued investment in growth initiatives.
Management explicitly declined to provide forward guidance on revenue acceleration or timelines to profitability.
positive_highlights: Revenue reached a company record of $770,000 with sequential growth of 56%.
Gross margins improved to a record 73.6%, expanding 510 basis points sequentially.
E-commerce revenue hit a record $511,000, up 186% sequentially, driven by in-house Amazon management.
summary: SenesTech reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $770,000, a 23% year-over-year increase and a record 56% sequential rise driven by in-house management of Amazon channels. Gross margins expanded to a company record of 73.6%, while Adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed sequentially to $1.4 million despite increased operating expenses including $270,000 in severance costs. Management highlighted record e-commerce performance and accelerating subscription revenue as evidence that their strategic transformation is executing faster than planned.

negative_highlights: Consolidated sales growth was partially offset by Middle East and Africa decline (-24%) due to ongoing war impacts.
European-based operations saw organic declines in both Q2 (5%) and H1, weighed down by softer demand in Western Europe.
Operating profit declined 16% year-over-year as SG&A expenses rose despite sales growth.
positive_highlights: Coach grew 10% H1 and Jimmy Choo surged 23% in Q2; Ferragamo sales jumped 41% in Q2 following new launches.
Gross margin expanded 90 bps to 61.6% in the U.S.-based operations, driven by favorable mix and tariff refunds.
Operating cash flow reached $46 million H1 (up from $5M prior year), with a strong balance sheet of $211M cash equivalents.
summary: Inter Parfums reported Q2 FY2026 consolidated sales growth of 2% (organic +4%) and diluted EPS of $1.35 for the quarter ($74M net income H1 vs $74M prior year), beating consensus estimates but missing internal guidance due to Middle East headwinds and FX tailwind normalization. Management maintained full-year sales guidance at approximately $1.48 billion while acknowledging a 2026 second-half decline relative to the prior year, driven by expected foreign exchange impacts in Europe.

negative_highlights: Distributable earnings (DE) declined due to a one-time realized credit loss of $24.5 million on resolved delinquent assets.
Economic book value decreased by approximately 2% subsequent to quarter end driven by higher market interest rates and wider spreads.
Management expects elevated realized credit losses in the third quarter before moderating later in the year.
positive_highlights: Resolved approximately $200 million of previously delinquent loans, reducing the 60+ day delinquency rate from 7.8% to 7.0%.
Lima One origination volume surged nearly 45% quarter-over-quarter to $316 million as technology and sales force improvements pay off.
Investment portfolio grew to approximately $13 billion, up roughly 20% year-over-year with growth concentrated in Agency MBS.
summary: MFA Financial reported Q2 FY2026 GAAP net income of $46.8 million ($0.35 EPS) and economic book value effectively unchanged at $13.20 per share. Distributable earnings declined to $12.2 million due to a one-time charge from resolving approximately $200 million in delinquent assets, though excluding this credit loss the metric improved 14% sequentially. Management raised guidance for G&A expenses to normalize around $26-$27M and expects realized credit losses to remain elevated in Q3 before moderating.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA fell to CAD 3.4 million from CAD 10.8 million year-over-year
Adjusted net income declined to CAD 3.8 million from CAD 6.6 million
Free cash flow swung to an outflow of CAD 5.8 million, from an inflow of CAD 6.8 million a year ago
positive_highlights: International medical cannabis net revenue rose 17% to CAD 43 million, driven by strong performance in Germany
Adjusted gross margin was 58%, at the high end of the expected annual range
Safari Flower Company acquisition was accretive to adjusted EBITDA in Q1 and received EU-GMP certification
summary: Aurora Cannabis reported Q1 FY2027 net revenue of CAD 67.6 million, with international medical cannabis revenue up 17% to CAD 43 million, offset by the expected Canadian medical reimbursement rate cut and the planned exit from its Canadian consumer business. Adjusted gross margin held at 58% (high end of guidance), but adjusted EBITDA fell to CAD 3.4 million from CAD 10.8 million a year earlier; free cash flow was an outflow of CAD 5.8 million. Management reaffirmed fiscal 2027 guidance, calling it a transitionary year, and expects Q2 revenue and adjusted EBITDA to be sequentially higher.

negative_highlights: Hormuz transits remain fragile with reduced volumes since June due to renewed escalation
Suezmax TD20 rates faced temporary pressure around $70k/day due to ballast exposure and CPC terminal security concerns, though management expects a bottom soon
positive_highlights: Adjusted EPS of $5.91 represents a record quarter in company history
Fleet-wide TCE reached approximately $181,000 per day with spot VLCC earnings at ~$214k/day and Suezmax at ~$175k/day
Completed delivery of all four acquired vessels (Nissos Tigani and Nissos Vous included), bringing the total fleet to 18 modern eco scrubber-fitted ships
summary: OET reported a record Q2 FY2026 with Adjusted EPS of $5.91 and Adjusted Net Profit of $231 million on fleet-wide TCE revenue of approximately $181,000 per day. The company declared its highest quarterly dividend ever at $5.25 per share (approx 90% payout) following the full delivery of its 18-vessel fleet in Q2/Q3 transition. Management raised guidance for spot VLCC rates to ~$207k/day and Suezmax to ~$133k/day, citing strong market conditions despite geopolitical volatility.

negative_highlights: Operating costs increased 9% excluding FX, stock comp, amortization, and a $100 million settlement charge related to the FTC matter.
Corporate Payments organic growth faced an 180 basis point drag from float revenue compression due to lower interest rates year-over-year.
positive_highlights: Revenue beat of approximately $45 million, with about $15 million attributed to underlying performance excluding a $30 million macro benefit.
Cash EPS reached an all-time record high of $7.00, representing a 36% year-over-year increase and significant accretion from Alpha ($0.29) and Avid ($0.10).
Corporate Payments segment delivered robust organic growth of 16%, driven by strong sales (40%) in cross-border and payables.
summary: Corpay reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $1.34 billion (up 21% YoY) and Cash EPS of $7.00 (up 36%), beating expectations by approximately $45 million in revenue and setting an all-time earnings record. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance to a midpoint of $5,310 million for revenue ($17% growth) and $27.35 per share for Cash EPS (up ~$6 from the prior year), driven by strong underlying fundamentals in Corporate Payments (+16%) and Vehicle Payments (+8%), alongside favorable macro conditions.

negative_highlights: Renewable fuel export volumes declined compared to last year due to Middle East geopolitical disruption affecting freight costs and vessel availability
Realized gains from derivatives offset a narrowing premium on high-quality alcohol sales, limiting net revenue impact but not fully reversing the volume decline in exports
positive_highlights: Crush margins improved significantly to $0.33 per gallon, up from $0.11 per gallon last year
Gross profit increased by $19 million YoY due to sales mix changes and stronger industry crush margins
Company paid down an additional $8.5 million in term debt principal during the quarter
summary: Alto Ingredients reported Q2 FY2026 net sales of $246 million (up $27M YoY) and EPS of $0.15 per share, reversing a prior year loss to generate positive adjusted EBITDA of $23.7 million driven by crush margins expanding significantly from $0.11/gallon in Q2 2025 to $0.33/gallon this quarter.

negative_highlights: GAAP net loss widened significantly to $939.9M from Q1's $427.6M primarily due to a non-cash fair value adjustment of $755.7 million on Google warrants.
Non-GAAP Adjusted EBITDA declined to -$18.3 million as pre-revenue operating costs and development spend outpaced revenue recognition from partial CB-3 contribution.
Cost of revenue increased sharply due to lower demand response proceeds ($2.8M vs $14.1M in Q1) and higher site-level expenses including security, labor, and demolition.
positive_highlights: Completed CB-3 delivery, bringing total operating critical IT capacity to 102 MW and activating $600 million in Google credit support.
Entered an agreement to note Abernathy Joint Venture interest for approximately $530 million, recycling capital into larger-scale opportunities.
summary: TeraWulf reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $44.8 million and a GAAP net loss attributable to the company of $939.9 million, driven by non-cash fair value adjustments on Google warrants ($755.7M) and pre-revenue operating costs at new sites. Management reaffirmed its target of contracting 250-500 MW annually but noted that Q2 Adjusted EBITDA was -$18.3 million due to significant development spend ahead of capacity delivery. While major milestones like the Anthropic lease ($19B contracted) and Abernathy sale were announced, guidance remains unchanged as execution focuses on converting construction into revenue.

negative_highlights: Consolidated GAAP results showed a net loss of $453 million due to non-economic impacts from the hedge portfolio.
Alternative investment returns were pressured by lagged Q1 market declines, resulting in an annualized return of slightly over 1% for the quarter.
Cumulative EPS growth through H1 was approximately 10%, falling note weakness in of the initial 12%-15% target range.
positive_highlights: Non-GAAP EPS of $1.70 represented a 24% YoY increase, exceeding the >15% full-year guidance range.
Record assets under management reached $1.2 trillion, up 10% year-over-year driven by positive net flows and equity market uplift.
Retirement business delivered strong organic growth with RILA sales up 10% YoY to generate $1.7 billion in net inflows.
summary: Equitable Holdings reported Q2 FY26 non-GAAP operating earnings of $1.70 per share (up 24% YoY), driven by record assets under management and positive net flows across Retirement ($1.7B inflows) and Wealth Management ($2B advisory inflows). The company reaffirmed its full-year EPS growth guidance for the merger era while noting that cumulative H1 EPS growth of ~10% is slightly below the 12%-15% target, with expectations to hit the low end by year-end. Management highlighted a neutral-to-slightly-positive impact from watching the employee benefits business and expects returns on alternative investments to improve in H2.

negative_highlights: Core advertising revenue declined 3% YoY due to political crowd-out effects and caution from cost-pressured advertiser categories like services and medical.
Tennis segment Adjusted EBITDA fell to $8 million (from $13M) primarily reflecting higher programming costs for rights monetization.
positive_highlights: Political advertising revenue reached a record pace, up 9% YoY with Q2 results of $59M significantly ahead of prior periods.
Full-year Adjusted EBITDA guidance was raised by $25 million at the midpoint to between $730 million and $760 million despite core ad resets.
Deleveraging progress accelerated with approximately $320 million in debt repaid or retired during the quarter.
summary: Sinclair reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $840 million (up 7% YoY) and Adjusted EBITDA of $149 million (up 45%), driven by strong political advertising ($59M, up 9%) and distribution growth. Management raised full-year guidance for political advertising to at least $375 million and increased total company Adjusted EBITDA guidance midpoint despite resetting core advertising revenue expectations due to crowding out from the robust political cycle.

negative_highlights: Gross margin declined sequentially to 20.1% (down 70 bps), with non-netted down revenue streams growing faster than netted ones.
Adjusted free cash flow conversion was low at ~45-46% for the first half, below the target of 80%-90%, due to inventory buildup and working capital investments.
positive_highlights: Net sales of $6.6 billion up 10% YoY with new all-time quarterly records set across top-line, gross profit ($1.3B), and non-GAAP EPS ($2.91).
Government segment net sales increased approximately 14%, driven by improving federal demand.
International operations delivered exceptional growth of approximately 23% YoY.
summary: CDW reported Q2 FY26 net sales of $6.6 billion (up 10% YoY) and non-GAAP EPS of $2.91 (up 12%), setting new all-time quarterly records for top-line, gross profit, and earnings per share despite a sequential decline in gross margin to 20.1%. Management raised its full-year outlook, projecting mid-single-digit growth in gross profit and high-end single-digit non-GAAP EPS expansion driven by strong AI infrastructure demand and operating leverage from the 'Geared for Growth' initiative.

negative_highlights: Same-property cash NOI decreased by 1.2% for the quarter.
Office occupancy guidance lowered to a range of 75%-77% solely due to including Studio Plaza, which is leased well over 50% but below portfolio average.
Higher market interest rates are anticipated to offset operating income improvements.
positive_highlights: Signed 960,000 sq ft of office leases with new and renewal deals; straight-line lease values increased by 3% over expiring space.
Acquired a well-leased block of prime Beverly Hills medical office properties (The Bedford Collection) for $260 million via joint venture.
Refinanced over $800 million in debt, fixing interest rates at approximately 6.15%-6.18%.
summary: Revenue increased from $252 million to approximately $257 million in Q2 FY26, driven by leasing activity and a new medical office acquisition, though same-property cash NOI decreased 1.2%. Management lowered full-year occupancy guidance for the office portfolio to 75%-77% due to including Studio Plaza (leased >50%) which drags down average metrics despite operational progress. Net income expectations remain negative ($-$0.20 to $-$0.16) as higher interest rates offset operating improvements.

negative_highlights: REA India business was sold last month and will not be treated as a discontinued operation due to lack of materiality.
Dow Jones Energy revenues grew only modestly (4%) impacted by the conflict in the Middle East affecting some clients.
News Media segment EBITDA declined $4 million YoY reflecting disciplined reinvestment for the launch of the California Post.
positive_highlights: Total segment EBITDA surged 31% YoY to $423 million, marking the highest quarterly profit on record even including prior-year Foxtel contributions.
Digital Real Estate Services (Realtor.com and REA) delivered exceptional growth with revenues up 19% reported and EBITDA expanding 46%, driven by strong Australian residential listings.
Dow Jones B2B capabilities now account for over 50% of segment profitability, supported by an 11% increase in Risk & Compliance revenue.
summary: News Corp reported record Q4 FY26 results with revenue of $2.3 billion (up 11% YoY) and total segment EBITDA soaring to $423 million (up 31%). Adjusted EPS was $0.35 compared to $0.19 in the prior year, while full-year margins expanded from 16.7% to 18%. Management raised guidance for fiscal 2027 by citing strong starts at Dow Jones and Digital Real Estate Services despite macro headwinds.

negative_highlights: Total revenue down 14% YoY to $162.3M from $189.2M
Behavioral subscribers down 24.6% YoY to 2.3 million
Full-year guidance reaffirmed, with expected moderate clinical subscriber declines ahead
positive_highlights: Core+ subscribers up 13.9% YoY, third consecutive sequential growth quarter
Clinical subscribers up 55.7% YoY and clinical revenue up 30.4%
Adjusted EBITDA of $39.8M, positive operating cash flow of $24.3M
summary: Weight Watchers Q2 FY2026 revenue fell to $162.3M from $189.2M a year ago, with behavioral subscribers down 24.6% YoY but clinical subscribers up 55.7% YoY. Adjusted EBITDA was $39.8M (24.5% margin), a turnaround from Q1's $1.8M loss, and the company reaffirmed full-year revenue and adjusted EBITDA guidance. Core+ subscriber growth reached a third consecutive sequential quarter, and management highlighted clinical revenue mix rising to 24.6% of total revenue.

negative_highlights: Wine operating segment EBITDA contracted by 61.9%, driven by a 26.9% drop in gross profit due to higher cost of wine and volume declines.
International Business volumes fell 7.4% (Argentina) and 13.7% (Bolivia), with Argentina beer industry facing high single-digit compression.
Distribution expenses rose 3.3%, partially offset by efficiencies, but distribution costs remain a pressure point due to higher oil prices.
positive_highlights: Consolidated EBITDA grew 59.4% despite volume declines, primarily supported by price actions across all segments.

Chile operating segment expanded top line by 1.5% with a 264 bps expansion in EBITDA margin to 30.8% (implied from context of growth and prior margins) or simply noted as expanding significantly; specifically, non-alcoholic categories grew mid-single digits.
CCU acquired the remaining 51% stake in Aguas CCU-Nestlé for full consolidation.
summary: CCU reported Q2 FY2026 consolidated net sales growth of 4.8% driven by a 6.4% increase in average prices despite a 1.5% volume decline. Consolidated EBITDA expanded significantly by 59.4%, with the Chile segment expanding EBITDA 26.2% and International Business reducing its loss, while the Wine segment contracted sharply due to unfavorable global trends and higher costs. Management noted that Argentina volumes remain under pressure but expect a recovery in H2 driven by seasonal adjustments and macro stabilization.

negative_highlights: TSS Net Sales declined sequentially due to lower aftermarket volumes from elevated inventory levels following the AIM Act transition.
Full-year guidance was lowered on revenue expectations as destocking of Opteon blends is expected to weigh on TSS through Q3 and into early next year.
APM Adjusted EBITDA declined year-over-year reflecting volume impacts from the SPS Capstone line closure completed in late 2025.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA exceeded expectations driven by stronger operational performance and improved product mix.
TT business delivered net sales increases via global pricing strength, including a new price increase effective June 1 supporting ~5% YTD growth.
APM Performance Solutions portfolio grew net sales 8% year-over-year with strong order book momentum in data center and semiconductor markets.
summary: Net sales were slightly below expectations due to softer residential stationary AC demand in the TSS business and lower volumes from a planned line closure in APM, while Adjusted EBITDA exceeded expectations supported by pricing strength in TT and improved mix. Management lowered full-year net sales guidance to a range of 1% to 5% growth (downward revision) citing destocking trends in the aftermarket that are expected to persist through Q3 before normalizing later in the year.

negative_highlights: Q3 revenue outlook is down sequentially by approximately $15M in Europe primarily due to seasonality, excluding any U.S. pickup.
U.S. residential demand remains soft as customers navigate a slower tax equity funding environment and uncertainty around FEOC definitions.
Non-GAAP gross margin guidance for Q3 (22%-26%) is lower than the current quarter's 28.6% due to scale differences in fixed costs.
positive_highlights: Non-GAAP operating income turned positive ($10.2M), marking a return to profitability after nearly three years of losses.
Revenue beat non-GAAP guidance range, finishing at $345.5 million versus the midpoint expectation.
U.S. C&I market share increased to over 50% due to compliance with FCC Covered List and domestic manufacturing.
summary: SolarEdge reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $346 million (up 19.6% YoY) and achieved non-GAAP operating profitability for the first time in nearly three years with a margin expansion to 28.6%. Management raised guidance expectations, noting that actual results exceeded the midpoint of their range due to IEEPA tariff refunds which are not expected to recur. For Q3 FY26, revenue is guided at $310-$340 million (down sequentially) driven by European seasonality and continued softness in the U.S. residential market.

negative_highlights: Cash re-leasing spreads in outpatient decelerated slightly from the prior quarter
Lab occupancy remains below breakeven at 78.5% despite sequential improvement, with inflection timing uncertain
Boston market faces significant supply overhang compared to other core markets
positive_highlights: FFO adjusted beat expectations at $0.46 per share
Same-store NOI guidance raised by 75 bps driven by lab (80 bps) and senior housing (260 bps)
Outpatient cash re-leasing spreads reached +5%, significantly above pre-merger averages
summary: Healthpeak reported FFOs adjusted of $0.46 per share for Q2 FY2026 and raised its full-year guidance range by $0.02 to $1.73-$1.77 driven by a 75 bps increase in same-store NOI at the midpoint, including significant gains in lab (80 bps sequential) and senior housing (260 bps). The company highlighted strong outpatient leasing with +5% cash re-leasing spreads despite modest TIs, while total occupancy improved sequentially across all segments. Management emphasized a strengthened balance sheet with leverage below 4.7x net debt to EBITDA and active capital recycling initiatives.

negative_highlights: Quarterly dividend was rightsized down significantly from $0.48 to $0.33 per share, reducing annual payout.
AFFO growth is currently flat compared to the first quarter of 2026 despite strategic initiatives.
Portfolio faces significant lease expirations in 2025 and 2026 (north of 10% turnover) which have moderated leasing momentum.
positive_highlights: Leasing activity remains strong with over 100,000 sq ft in new leases signed YTD, surpassing total volume for all of 2025.
Strategic capital recycling generated $38.5 million in net proceeds from seven property sales to date.
Targeted redevelopment projects offer compelling risk-adjusted returns with a 9%-12% yield on cost.
summary: Community Healthcare Trust reported steady AFFO per share of $0.56 and FFO per share of $0.48 for Q2 FY2026, matching the prior quarter but missing implied growth expectations due to a significant dividend reduction from $0.48 to $0.33 per share. Management outlined a strategic plan involving capital recycling via property sales ($70M in assets marketed) and rightsized dividends to fund an acquisition pipeline of $85-$90 million for 2026, targeting 92% occupancy by the end of 2027.

negative_highlights: Q3 enterprise revenue is expected to be slightly below last year due to roofing distributor pull-forward and seasonal storm demand normalization.
Doors sales declined 7% YoY in Q2 primarily driven by strategic business exits including the distribution divestiture.
Roofing EBITDA margin guidance for Q3 drops significantly (approx. 400 bps) due to volume deleverage and negative price cost from inflation.
positive_highlights: Insulation business delivered resilient results with sales up 4% YoY driven by higher volumes in Europe and non-residential segments.
Doors business achieved an EBITDA margin of 11%, ahead of guidance, aided by tariff refunds.
Roofing components outperformed the broader market on volume despite a low-margin contract exit.
summary: Owens Corning reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $2.8 billion (relatively flat YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $660 million ($3.93 EPS), with margins supported by a one-time $25M tariff refund partially offsetting cost inflation from the Iran conflict. Management provided cautious Q3 guidance expecting enterprise revenue to decline slightly due to roofing volume pull-forward, while insulation is expected to grow mid-single digits and doors will be down primarily due to prior divestitures.

negative_highlights: CELESTIMO 301 study did not reach statistical superiority in uMRD analysis versus VO regimen, though PFS remains on track
Operating expenses increased to CNY 1.2 billion reflecting continued investment in clinical programs and commercial growth
positive_highlights: Total revenue of $1.7 billion representing a 30% year-over-year increase
BRUKINSA U.S. sales reached $893 million with sustained new patient starts at highest levels since launch
FDA approval achieved for Beqalzi as the first and only BCL-2 inhibitor in mantle cell lymphoma
summary: BeOne Medicines reported Q2 FY26 total revenue of $1.7 billion (30% YoY growth) and GAAP EPS of $2.05 (144% YoY). Management raised full-year 2026 guidance for revenue by CNY 300 million to a range of CNY 6.6-6.8 billion, driven primarily by strong BRUKINSA performance in the U.S., which grew sales by $893 million (31% YoY). The company also highlighted significant pipeline progress including FDA approval for Beqalzi and positive data from the MANGROVE study.

negative_highlights: Door volume declined slightly due to soft residential market conditions
Gross margin contracted from 48.7% prior year quarter to 47%
Commercial new construction remains low relative to prior years
positive_highlights: Revenue grew organically by 7% with price/mix contributing +6%

Closed Australasia joint venture generating $181 million in cash and a note receivable

Management recorded a non-cash impairment charge of approximately $191 million related to NARCAN asset group valuation.
Q3 outlook anticipates a step-down in total revenue between $110M-$130M following accelerated first-half MCM deliveries.

Company ended Q2 with $140 million in cash and secured a new term loan refinancing extending maturities to 2031.
summary: Emergent BioSolutions reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $234 million and adjusted EBITDA of $97 million (41% margin), significantly beating the high end of prior guidance due to accelerated Medical Countermeasure deliveries. The company also announced restructuring actions targeting approximately $40 million in annualized savings, including a workforce reduction of 90 positions.

summary: Criteo reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $428 million and Adjusted EBITDA of $73 million, missing internal expectations due to soft spending from several large enterprise clients in Performance Media. Despite top-line headwinds and a conservative near-term view, the company generated positive operating cash flow of $20 million and deployed $30 million in share buybacks.

negative_highlights: Total reported revenue decreased 4.2% year-over-year due to the inclusion of Celero transaction-related expenses

summary: ThredUp reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $90.8 million (up 16.9% YoY) and gross margin expansion to 79.9%, driven by strong new buyer growth despite a challenging macro environment requiring incremental promotions on price-sensitive shoppers. Management updated full-year guidance downward, citing an estimated $3-7 million headwind in the second half due to elevated promotional activity needed for budget customers and higher gas prices affecting demand. The company maintains its strategic focus on shifting mix toward premium buyers via Meta/Pinterest channels while managing older inventory through targeted discounts.

negative_highlights: Total revenue decreased 21% to $523 million reflecting hardware transition and lower than anticipated restaurant installations

Non-GAAP operating margin expanded to 32.9% (up 330 bps), with organic expansion of 140-150 basis points excluding one-time tariff refunds.
Record Q2 ending backlog reached $15.6 billion, up 11% YoY and driven by record orders in MCN, video, and command center.
summary: MSI reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $1.3 billion (up 13% YoY) and Non-GAAP EPS of $4.41 (up 24%), beating consensus by approximately $130 million driven by strong LMR demand and Silvus growth. Management raised full-year guidance for both sales ($12.975B vs prior $12.8B) and non-GAAP EPS ($17.62-$17.72 vs prior), citing record backlog of $15.6 billion and double-digit order growth across all segments. The quarter featured operating margin expansion to 32.9% (Non-GAAP) excluding a one-time IEEPA refund benefit, with forward-looking expectations for comparable gross margins despite higher memory costs.

negative_highlights: Q2 revenue decreased by $2.3 million (6.2%) year-over-year to $34.2 million.

summary: Lifecore Biomedical reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $34.2 million, a decrease of 6.2% year-over-year, and adjusted EBITDA of $8.6 million, down from $9.1 million in the prior period. While management expressed confidence in their growth strategy and new business wins, the quarter was impacted by lower development revenue, unfavorable manufacturing costs, and timing differences.

Board raised quarterly cash dividend by 10% to $0.33 per share.

Consolidated OIBDA rose 29% to $160 million while AFFO increased 45% to $121 million. Management raised full-year guidance for reported AFFO growth to the low-20s percent range relative to last year.

Leverage remains elevated at 4.2x covenant EBITDA with $755 million adjusted net debt.

CEO Dan Krawczyk confirmed the strategic review remains active with no delay or narrowing of scope.

High Purity Cellulose margins expanded significantly, but Paperboard & High-Yield Pulp continued to report an adjusted EBITDA loss of -$10 million due to lower pricing and maintenance downtime. Management reiterated full-year free cash flow expectations remain aligned with prior guidance despite elevated leverage.

Full-year operating expense guidance was lowered despite robust volume growth.

Bloomberg Financial Futures launched with market depth and volumes 'in line with expectations' ahead of retail onboarding.

Management lowered full-year operating expense guidance due to shifts between cash compensation and stock-based comp, while maintaining capital expenditure expectations around $40-45 million. The quarter highlighted the successful launch of Bloomberg Financial Futures products with liquidity metrics meeting expectations.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined 3% year-over-year due to customers purchasing IBM hardware/software directly and lengthening sales cycles.
Adjusted pre-tax income turned into a $37 million loss, primarily impacted by $152 million in workforce rebalancing charges.

New scope and new logos accounted for approximately 30% of large deal value over the last 12 months, up from 15% in fiscal 2025.
summary: Kyndryl reported Q1 FY2027 revenue of $3.6 billion, down 3% year-over-year on both a reported and constant currency basis, driven by headwinds from customers procuring hardware/software directly from IBM and lower signings in focus accounts. Adjusted pre-tax loss was $37 million due to $152 million in workforce rebalancing charges, while adjusted EBITDA remained at $512 million. Management maintained a flat-to-down 2% constant currency revenue outlook for the full year despite strong growth in Kyndryl Consult (up 14%) and hyperscaler-related streams.

negative_highlights: Free operating cash flow turned negative at -$79 million due to working capital build for tungsten prices
Share repurchase program paused as management prioritizes liquidity needs over buybacks

The company provided FY2027 guidance for sales between $3.33B-$3.45B and adjusted EPS in the range of $4.15-$5.15, which is essentially flat year-over-year compared to FY2026's midpoint.

negative_highlights: G&A expenses increased slightly due to a one-time expense related to line of credit expansion and interest on funds held.

New product launches (Asset Management, Career & Succession Planning) are gaining traction with early adopters despite being recent releases.
summary: Paycom reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $531 million (up 10% YoY) and GAAP net income of $107 million ($2.34/share), beating expectations with broad-based demand across all buckets. Management raised full-year guidance, projecting total revenues between $2.197 billion and $2.212 billion (7-8% growth) and record adjusted EBITDA margins of 46%. The company returned significant capital to shareholders via buybacks ($346 million in Q2 alone) and dividends.

positive_highlights: CABOMETYX U.S. Q2 net product revenue grew approximately 10% year-over-year to $573 million

positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA delivered $374 million for Q2 FY26

summary: Talen Energy reported Q2 FY26 adjusted EBITDA of $374 million and adjusted free cash flow (FCF) of $212 million, driven by the integration of recent acquisitions including Freedom, Guernsey, Waterford, Darby, and Lawrenceburg. Management noted potential inflationary cost pressures in H2 that could add a few dollars per ton.

Free cash flow generation reached $103 million in Q2 and turned positive for H1 at $11 million.
Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded significantly to 31%, up from 18% in the prior year quarter.
summary: Warrior Met Coal reported Q2 FY2026 net income of $87 million ($1.65 EPS) and adjusted EBITDA of $157 million, driven by record sales volumes of 3.7 million short tons (a 65% YoY increase). The quarter marked a key inflection point with free cash flow generation exceeding expectations at $103 million for the period. Management raised full-year volume guidance by 0.5 million tons to reflect strong adoption and contracting success from their new Blue Creek mine.

U.S. PHESGO 510(k) withdrawn, pushing U.S. oncology entry later than the previously expected second half of 2026 and cutting the PHESGO infusion opportunity from ~1.1-1.2 million to ~600,000 annually
