Delivered first positive net income since 2019 and positive adjusted EBITDA of $900,000 in the first half, with cash usage down 62% YoY
summary: KORU reported record Q2 FY2026 revenue of $12.0 million, up 18% YoY, with international core up 59% to $3.5 million and domestic core up 12% to $8 million; PST fell 35% to $600,000. Gross margin rose 160 bps to 65.1% and the company posted positive net income for the first time since 2019, with positive adjusted EBITDA of $900,000 in the first half. Guidance was narrowed to $47.5-48.5 million from a prior, more back-half-weighted outlook, as non-tender international PFS markets ramp slower and the opportunity shifts into 2027; gross margin guidance was raised to 62%-64% from 61%-63%. The company also withdrew its U.S. PHESGO 510(k) to pivot to other oncology molecules and acquired a connected monitoring technology asset, both of which push U.S. oncology entry later.

negative_highlights: Medicare Advantage membership declined year-over-year by roughly 14% (from 498k in Q2 FY2025) as management executes a disciplined, profitability-focused contracting strategy.
Second quarter medical costs remained elevated at the low 7% range due to limited paid claims data visibility for that specific period.
positive_highlights: Medical margin of $197 million exceeded guidance midpoint by approximately $74 million compared to -$53 million a year ago.
Adjusted EBITDA reached $70 million, beating the second quarter guidance midpoint by roughly $50 million after turning from an annual loss in 2025.
Full-year 2026 revenue guidance raised to approximately $5.8 billion at the new midpoint due to strong Q2 performance and improved cost trends.
summary: Agilon Health exceeded second quarter guidance for medical margin and adjusted EBITDA, driven by a $22 million favorable prior year development item and improved risk adjustment estimates of approximately 3% net of V28 impact versus an earlier estimate of 1.5%. Management raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to approximately $5.8 billion (midpoint) from the previous range, citing better-than-expected performance in diagnosis, assessment, and treatment alongside favorable medical expense development for both 2025 and Q1 2026.

negative_highlights: Rest of World referral revenue declined 11% year-over-year, impacted by approximately 7% foreign exchange headwinds and geopolitical pressures in the Middle East.
Operational expenses increased EUR 26.9 million year-over-year due to higher investments in brand and performance marketing channels.
positive_highlights: Achieved positive adjusted EBITDA of EUR 1.1 million in Q2, marking the first profitable quarter since 2023 despite FX headwinds.
Product conversion rate increased by 64% compared to Q2 2023 due to enhanced user experience and AI features.
Referral revenue from CRM channels more than doubled year-over-year as member strategy matures.
summary: Trivago reported Q2 FY26 total revenue of EUR 168.4 million, representing a 21% year-over-year increase and its sixth consecutive quarter of double-digit growth. The company achieved positive adjusted EBITDA of EUR 1.1 million in the second half of 2025 for the first time since Q3 2023, driven by improved unit economics and conversion rates up 64% since Q2 2023. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance to mid-teens percentage revenue growth and adjusted EBITDA around EUR 30 million.

negative_highlights: GAAP net loss of $19 million compared to GAAP income of $700,000 in the prior year quarter.
Adult Afrezza revenue showed softness driven by a disproportionate decrease from top 10 prescribers, though underlying growth remains positive when excluding them.
SG&A expenses surged to $58.3 million (up nearly double) and R&D rose to $18 million due to launch preparations for ReadyFlow and pediatric expansion.
positive_highlights: FUROSCIX ReadyFlow received FDA approval with a CVR payout of approximately $45 million expected in Q3 following the PIPE financing that raised cash to $161 million at quarter end.
Pediatric Afrezza launch is gaining early momentum, with one-third of top 100 pediatric insulin writers already prescribing and refills observed by month two.
Nintedanib DPI Phase I-B study demonstrated a clean safety profile in IPF patients with zero serious adverse events or discontinuations due to cough.
summary: MannKind reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $109.4 million (up 43% YoY) and a GAAP net loss of $19 million versus prior year income due to significant investments in the FUROSCIX ReadyFlow launch, pediatric Afrezza expansion, and MNKD-201 development. While all three major catalysts were delivered—pediatric approval for Afrezza, FDA approval for FUROSCIX ReadyFlow, and positive Phase I-B data for nintedanib DPI—the company explicitly stated that 2026 is a 'deliberate investment year' with costs rising significantly in SG&A ($58.3M vs $31.6M prior) and R&D ($18M). Management noted softness in adult Afrezza sales driven by top prescribers, though pediatric uptake remains strong.

negative_highlights: Storage and transportation adjusted EBITDA declined to $16 million from $17 million due to a January related party transaction.
Wholesale marketing segment saw lower results of $13 million compared to $23 million last year, attributed to the amend and extend agreement.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA reached a record $144 million, up from $127 million in Q2 FY25.
Delaware crude gathering achieved record volumes of over 157,000 barrels per day versus 129k in Q1.
Wholesale marketing and terminaling EBITDA was bolstered by stronger realized margins in the Permian Basin.
summary: DKL reported adjusted EBITDA of $144 million for Q2 FY26, a record beat against the prior year's $127 million and in-line with expectations given strong third-party business growth. Management reaffirmed full-year 2026 guidance of $520-$560 million despite delivering results that suggest potential upside to the range. The company raised its quarterly distribution to $1.135 per unit, marking the 54th consecutive increase.

negative_highlights: Specialty Contractors segment remains at a low positive operating margin of 2.2% despite sequential improvement, though still below historical norms.
Management notes they are not setting new cash flow records in the second half and expect outcomes closer to last year's levels rather than exceeding them.
positive_highlights: Record Q2 revenue of $1.6 billion representing a 19% year-over-year increase driven by ramp-up on nine mega projects.
Adjusted EPS beat expectations at $1.74, reflecting a 54% surge in operating income to record levels of $118 million.
Civil segment margin expanded sequentially to 15.3%, exceeding the high end of management's anticipated full-year range for that segment.
summary: TPC reported record Q2 FY26 revenue of $1.6 billion (up 19% YoY) and adjusted EPS of $1.74 (up 23%), driven by strong execution on mega projects in Civil, Building, and Specialty segments. Management raised its full-year 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to a range of $5.15-$5.45 from the prior $4.90-$5.30, citing record first-half operating cash flow of $334 million and improved segment margins across all lines of business.

negative_highlights: Revised full-year 2026 CAFD guidance range down to $430-$475 million from prior of $470-$510 million due to low wind resource.
Solar and battery fleet results were impacted by lower realized revenues.
summary: Clearway Energy reported Q2 FY26 adjusted EBITDA of $409 million and CAFD of $167 million, with year-to-date CAFD at $237 million. Management revised the full-year 2026 CAFD guidance range down to $430-$475 million from a prior range of $470-$510 million due to lower-than-typical wind resources in H1 driven by ENSO patterns. While reaffirming long-term targets, management noted that the underlying earning power remains intact despite transitory weather impacts.

negative_highlights: Subscription streaming growth decelerated slightly quarter-over-quarter due to tough comparable periods, though management expects normalization in Q4.
Ad-supported streaming revenue was elevated at 10% specifically because of non-recurring FIFA World Cup ad spending spikes.
positive_highlights: Recorded music subscription streaming revenue grew 12% on an adjusted basis, led by pricing increases and subscriber growth.
Total company Adjusted OIBDA margin expanded 130 bps year-over-year as cost savings initiatives delivered $200 million in annualized run-rate savings.
Physical revenue surged 17%, driven by Madonna's 'Confessions on a Dance Floor' debut and catalog strength.
summary: Warner Music Group reported Q3 FY26 results with total revenue up 9% (11% adjusted) and Adjusted OIBDA growing 18%, driven by a robust 12% increase in recorded music subscription streaming. Margins expanded significantly, with Recorded Music margin improving 150 bps to 25.3% and Total Company margins expanding 130 bps on an adjusted basis. Management reiterated high single-digit revenue growth targets for the full year while noting a slight QoQ deceleration in subscription streaming due to tough comps.

negative_highlights: Gross margin declined to 31.8% from 35.3% YoY, reduced by approximately 1.8 percentage points due to one-time items.
Full-year guidance lowered for fiscal 2026 as industry demand constraints force a reduction in expected net sales range of $151 million-$155 million.
positive_highlights: Secured an initial purchase order totaling approximately $22 million for a hyperscale data center project with shipments expected in early FY27.
summary: Third quarter net sales were $43.9 million (up 13% YoY), but gross margin contracted to 31.8% due to one-time items and higher costs. Management lowered full-year guidance for fiscal 2026, citing industry demand constraints from the BEAD program delays and a lack of fiber availability.

negative_highlights: Google monetization dropped more than 30% in June, causing a significant drop in net revenue per day for the partner network business.
Products revenue per session was down 2%, primarily due to Startpage facing industry-wide Google syndication issues where fewer ads are shown and paid less.
Management explicitly declined to provide forward guidance citing volatility that prevents reliable forecasting.
positive_highlights: Total sessions increased 5% sequentially, driven by a rebound in CouponFollow organic traffic (+11%) and strong mobile growth for Startpage (+63% YoY).
Debt exchange finalized successfully reduced total outstanding debt to $150 million from over $302 million.
CouponFollow is now the number two coupon site by organic traffic behind only Reddit.
summary: Q2 revenue was $30.2 million, representing a 61% year-over-year decrease and a 19% sequential decline driven by significant monetization volatility from Google in the partner network business. Adjusted EBITDA fell to $1.9 million (down 83% YoY) as management explicitly stated they are not providing Q3 or full-year guidance due to continued uncertainty with Google's RSOC market and antitrust litigation risks.

negative_highlights: Q3 bookings guidance implies growth of roughly 24-26%, which is lower than the Q2 actuals and significantly below the ~30%+ rates seen in prior quarters.
Management noted that Q3 free cash flow will be negatively impacted by a $315 million settlement with credit card partners, though this was expected.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded approximately 900 basis points year-over-year to a record high of 36.4%.
Free cash flow reached $189 million in Q2, representing a 60% increase compared to the prior year period.
Active CLEAR+ member base grew by 15.2% sequentially to reach approximately 8.3 million members.
summary: CLEAR reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $277.8 million (up 26.6% YoY) and total bookings of $295.9 million (up 32.8%), with adjusted EBITDA margins expanding to 36.4%, surpassing the IPO target of 35%. Management raised full-year free cash flow guidance from at least $465M to at least $480M and provided Q3 revenue guidance between $284M-$287M, citing strong customer acquisition and retention trends.

negative_highlights: Net sales declined 8% year-over-year primarily due to the full impact of exiting the lower-margin pet distribution business.

Pet segment net sales fell 19%, with Dog and Cat revenues down more than normal top-line growth due to promotional timing differences and a one-time supply disruption from a facility fire in South America.
positive_highlights: Organic net sales rose 2% to $862 million reflecting broad gains across the portfolio excluding pet distribution.
Garden segment delivered record performance with non-GAAP operating income up 7% and margin expanding 70 bps to 18.9% despite challenging weather conditions.
Cash provided by operations reached a record $327 million, driven by inventory unwinds from the pet distribution exit.
summary: Net sales declined 8% to $882 million due to the exit of the pet distribution business, while organic net sales rose 2% to $862 million driven by growth in both garden and pet segments. Operating margins expanded 90 basis points to 15.4%, supported by a favorable product mix and productivity improvements that offset higher freight costs. Management raised fiscal 2026 non-GAAP diluted EPS guidance from $2.70 or better to $2.85 or better, citing strong momentum entering the fourth quarter.

negative_highlights: Full-year 2026 revenue guidance of EUR 36-40 million was left unchanged, implying a H2 range of EUR 22-26 million
Total operating expense guidance was raised by EUR 1 million to EUR 99-102 million
U.S. GAAP operating loss was EUR 20.6 million, roughly flat versus EUR 19.9 million in Q2 2025
positive_highlights: Worldwide net revenue grew 21% sequentially to EUR 7.7 million, with U.S. revenue up 22% sequentially to EUR 5.2 million and international up 19%
Gross margin expanded to 60% in Q2 from 57% in Q1
U.S. active high-volume AGNS accounts doubled to 180, with 262 surgeons trained and 427 patients under prior authorization entering Q3, a 77% sequential increase
summary: Nyxoah reported Q2 2026 worldwide net revenue of EUR 7.7 million, up 21% sequentially from Q1 and versus EUR 1.3 million in Q2 2025, with U.S. net revenue of EUR 5.2 million (up 22% sequentially) and international net revenue of EUR 2.5 million (up 19% sequentially). Gross margin rose to 60% from 57% in Q1, and the company secured $110 million in financing, ending the quarter with EUR 97.8 million in cash and equivalents plus financial assets. Full-year 2026 revenue guidance was left unchanged at EUR 36-40 million, gross margin guidance unchanged at 60-62%, while total operating expense guidance rose by EUR 1 million to EUR 99-102 million due to a one-time share-based compensation charge; non-GAAP cash opex guidance was unchanged at EUR 88-90 million. U.S. active accounts doubled to 180, surgeons trained reached 262, and patients under prior authorization entering Q3 rose 77% to 427.

negative_highlights: Top 10 customer concentration increased slightly to 37%, with these accounts driving the majority of quarterly growth.
Non-AI traffic growth decelerated by approximately six points year-over-year compared to Q1, though still positive at low-20s.
positive_highlights: Revenue beat high-end guidance driven by a record $183M total, with security growing 43% YoY to nearly $200M annual run rate.
Gross margin hit an all-time high of 65.8%, up 680 bps from the prior year quarter due to revenue mix and cost discipline.
Trailing twelve-month net retention expanded for a fifth consecutive quarter, reaching 117% as customers standardize their stack on Fastly.
summary: Fastly reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $183 million (up 23% YoY), exceeding the high end of guidance with gross margins expanding to a record 65.8%. Operating income reached $27 million, surpassing the upper bound of its range, while trailing twelve-month net retention rose to 117%. Management raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance by approximately 4% and increased non-GAAP operating profit expectations.

negative_highlights: Automated Stores remain below prior year levels due to slower bookings from macro-driven budget constraints and quality remediation costs of approximately $1 million in the quarter.
Adjusted EBITDA margins declined slightly year-over-year by 60 basis points, partially offsetting top-line growth benefits.
Management explicitly stated that recovery across portions of the portfolio remains uneven with research spending still below prior year levels.
positive_highlights: Organic revenue grew 9% year-over-year, exceeding management's prior expectations and consensus estimates.
Recurring revenue businesses (biorepositories and C&I) delivered strong results with over half of total revenue now recurring in nature.
Multiomics North America showed modest sequential improvement supported by new commercial leadership filling a key gap.
summary: Third quarter revenue of $161 million beat expectations with organic growth of 9%, driven by strong performance in biorepositories and C&I segments which now represent over half of total revenue as a recurring stream. Adjusted EBITDA margins were approximately 11.4% but declined slightly year-over-year due to quality remediation costs, lower volumes in Automated Stores, and ongoing investments in commercial capabilities. Management raised the full-year FY2026 organic revenue outlook from down -2% to flat/up +1%, while maintaining a cautious view on Q4 given challenging comparisons.

negative_highlights: Net loss attributable to IEP was $355 million, a significant deterioration from the prior year quarter's net loss of $165 million.
Investment funds posted a negative return of 7.7% for the quarter (excluding refining hedges), contributing heavily to NAV decline.
positive_highlights: Energy segment Adjusted EBITDA increased by $62 million year-over-year due to strong refining operations with crude utilization over 98% and robust fertilizer demand.
summary: IEP reported a Q2 net loss of $355 million ($0.52 per unit) and an Adjusted EBITDA loss of $134 million compared to prior year gains, driven by significant declines in investment funds performance (-7.7% excluding hedges). While the Energy segment saw strong refining utilization (over 98%) and fertilizer demand, other segments like Pharma faced headwinds from generic competition and supply chain disruptions. Management confirmed a definitive agreement to watch Pep Boys for $700 million expected to close in Q3.

negative_highlights: Production was materially impacted by record rain and snow melt (highest precipitation in over 30 years), leaving an estimated value on the table of roughly 60,000 barrels per day.
Refining throughput fell note weakness in of previous records due to weather constraints, though network utilization remained high at 92% against new higher capacity.
Upstream production averaged only 761,000 bpd in the quarter compared to July's preliminary rate of 870,000 bpd which was expected to be a record.
positive_highlights: Adjusted Funds From Operations reached an all-time quarterly record of CAD 5.3 billion, nearly double the level from Q2 2022 despite lower commodity prices.
Downstream AFFO hit a new record of CAD 2.3 billion with margin capture at 89% (excluding RVO variance) and upgrader utilization reaching 94%, a company-wide high.
Firebag turnaround completed in 44 days for CAD 118 million, achieving a 25,000 bpd improvement versus plan compared to the prior similar event.
summary: Suncor reported Q2 FY2026 production of 761,000 barrels per day and refining throughput of 471,000 bpd, both significantly below historical records due to unprecedented weather conditions causing an estimated impact of 50,000-60,000 bpd. Despite the volume miss from rain and snow melt, management highlighted record downstream AFFO of CAD 2.3 billion (nearly double Q2 2022 levels) driven by strong margin capture in a lower price environment. The company increased its monthly share buyback to CAD 500 million starting this week while maintaining flexibility on dividend growth.

negative_highlights: Q3 guidance lowered due to accelerated closure of Lanaken plant pulling forward inventory absorption.
Equity earnings expected to be $10 million lower this year due to Ibn Sina disruptions hitting in Q3.
Raw material cost inflation is flowing through margins starting in the third quarter, compressing results.
positive_highlights: Celanese ended Q2 with higher benefit from supply chain opportunities and EM pre-note than originally guided for.
summary: Celanese reported Q2 FY26 results where management noted they ended up getting slightly more benefit than originally guided for the quarter due to supply chain dynamics and EM pre-watching. However, guidance was lowered for Q3 driven by accelerated plant closures in Lanaken and Ibn Sina causing inventory absorption hits, with equity earnings expected to be $10 million lower than anticipated this year. Management maintains a full-year free cash flow guide of $700-$800M but warns that raw material cost inflation will compress margins in the third quarter.

negative_highlights: Surgeries and admissions declined 5% and 2% respectively in April-May, with full quarter declines of 2.9% and 1%.
Net patient service revenue per adjusted admission decreased 3.9% due to lower acuity mix.
Exchange admissions dropped 8% YoY as patients lost subsidies.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA of $115 million maintained full-year guidance despite volume softness in April-May.
Operating cash flow surged to $197 million, up from $117 million a year ago.
SW&B growth slowed significantly to 0.7% YoY as contract labor spend was reduced by 42%.
summary: Ardent Health reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $1.62 billion and adjusted EBITDA of $115 million, maintaining its full-year guidance despite a volume headwind driven by April-May softness that improved in June/July but is expected to persist through the second half. Management reaffirmed 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance of $485M-$535M and revenue bias towards the lower end ($6.4B-$6.7B) while increasing the IMPACT savings target to over $70 million via structural changes and payer contract improvements.

negative_highlights: Second quarter O&M expenses increased approximately 6.6% year-over-year due to elevated line-locating tickets and fuel costs.
Warm winter weather resulted in lower storage consumption, though this created capacity release opportunities rather than a direct revenue miss.
positive_highlights: Adjusted net income increased by 52% year-over-year to $52.1 million ($0.82 per share).
Texas House Bill 4384 contributed approximately $16 million in new revenue and is expected to contribute ~$0.42 to full-year adjusted EPS.
Large load projects are advancing, with one data center project placed under contract this quarter representing roughly $15 million of incremental annual revenue.
summary: Adjusted EPS of $0.82 beat the prior year's $0.54 by 52%, driven by new rates and Texas House Bill 4384 benefits which contributed approximately $16 million in revenue. Management raised full-year adjusted earnings expectations to the upper half of their range ($310M-$314M, or $4.89-$4.95 EPS) citing strong first-half performance and continued large load growth opportunities.

negative_highlights: Revenue per lead was up only +1%, indicating that higher job costs are suppressing volume as homeowners do fewer jobs.
Unbranded SEO channel is down close to 5% of total service request volume with no assumed recovery in the near term.
Goodwill impairment charge of $235 million reflects sustained declines in market capitalization since year-end.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA grew faster than revenue sequentially from Q1 to Q2 due to improved marketing ROI and reallocation of $6 million in inefficient TV spend.
Win rates have increased roughly 20% compared to a year ago, improving pro retention prospects.
Pro capacity utilization is stabilizing after declines, moving from down -13% in Q1 to flat year-over-year by July.
summary: Angi reported Q2 FY2026 revenue down 11% year-over-year and service requests down -6%, driven by a shift away from network channels (down 34%) and lower quality marketing sources. The company recorded a $235 million non-cash goodwill impairment charge on its U.S. reporting unit due to sustained declines in market capitalization, though international operations remained healthy with substantial headroom. Management stated they are not reinstating guidance at this time but expect modest sequential improvements as the year progresses.

negative_highlights: GAAP net income attributable to Acacia was just $47,000, or $0.00 per diluted share, despite $114.6 million of revenue
Full impairment of the MalinJ1/Viamet investment tied to Mycovia's liquidity issues; book value fell to $557 million ($5.71/share) from $567.2 million ($5.87/share)

The quarter's headline revenue is heavily one-time: roughly $60.6 million of episodic licensing revenue, with a portion shared with contingency counsel at an elevated rate given TP-Link ran nearly through the courts
positive_highlights: Benchmark delivered record revenue of $20.5 million with $9.8 million adjusted EBITDA and $6.5 million free cash flow, the first full quarter including the Cherokee well
Balance sheet of $334.6 million in cash, securities and loans receivable, up about $4.7 million in the quarter, with no parent company debt
$59.5 million of the $90.4 million gross debt is non-recourse at Benchmark and $30.9 million non-recourse at Deflecto
summary: Acacia reported total revenue of $114.6 million versus $51.2 million in the prior year period, though the increase was driven by roughly $60.6 million of episodic Wi-Fi 6 licensing revenue tied to the TP-Link settlement (cash received in Q3, booked as AR at quarter end). Total company adjusted EBITDA was $17.3 million against operating segment EBITDA of $22.8 million; GAAP net income was only $47,000 ($0.00/share) versus adjusted net income of $12.8 million ($0.13/share), with a $3.7 million non-recurring legacy litigation expense not adjusted out. Benchmark posted record revenue of $20.5 million, $9.8 million EBITDA and $6.5 million free cash flow, while Deflecto ($27.1 million revenue, $1.1 million EBITDA) and Printronix ($6 million revenue, $1 million EBITDA) remained modest, and the company took a full write-down of the MalinJ1/Viamet investment plus a decline in book value to $5.71/share from $5.87. No formal forward guidance was given; management reiterated an unchanged capital-allocation strategy and described a strengthening acquisition pipeline.

negative_highlights: Phosphate production curtailed across U.S. and Brazil, with Louisiana facility entirely offline and Bartow running at ~40% capacity due to sulfur constraints.
Q3 idle expenses expected to double from Q2's $60M (approx. $90-100M total) as facilities remain in stasis while preserving asset health.
North American phosphate application forecasted down 20% vs normal, with Latin America facing similar declines driven by affordability and availability issues.
positive_highlights: Successfully completed Esterhazy annual turnaround and expects lower unit costs in potash segment due to Hydrofloat Project volumes.
SG&A costs reduced by 20% year-over-year despite inflation through aggressive spending discipline.
summary: Mosaic reported Q2 FY26 results driven by significant phosphate production curtailments in the U.S. and Brazil due to high sulfur costs, resulting in lower volumes but preserved margins via cost discipline ($1B term loan taken). Management provided specific guidance for raw material costs (sulfur $705/ton) and sales prices for Q3, acknowledging that idle expenses will double in Q3 compared to the prior quarter. The company expects a working capital release of $300M-$500M later in the year as Brazil collections normalize.

negative_highlights: GAAP EPS of $0.14 was significantly lower than the prior year's $1.24 due to a $6.4 million non-cash warrant charge.
European regulatory re-examination for arimoclomol faces uncertainty with an expected CHMP opinion in Q4 following a negative initial review.
Reimbursements beyond France remain highly variable and unpredictable.
positive_highlights: Net revenue grew 53% year-over-year to $39.7 million, with U.S. MIPLYFFA sales increasing 40% YoY.
Channel inventory returned to target levels after falling below range in Q1.
Total cash equivalents and investments reached $260.2 million.
summary: Zevra reported Q2 FY26 net revenue of $39.7 million (up 53% YoY), driven by U.S. MIPLYFFA sales of $30.2 million and global reimbursements, while GAAP EPS was $0.14 due to a non-cash warrant charge reducing adjusted earnings from an expected beat. Management maintained full-year guidance despite acknowledging unpredictable reimbursement patterns outside France and the ongoing European regulatory re-examination process for arimoclomol.

negative_highlights: North America organic growth decelerated to approximately 2% in the quarter due largely to timing of customer deployments shifting into H2.
Latin America performance was impacted by depressed consumption and austerity measures specifically affecting Argentina, though described as an anomaly rather than a structural issue.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA grew 11% YoY to $257 million with margin expansion of 70 bps driven by productivity initiatives and favorable mix.
AMS/DRS segment achieved a record organic growth rate of 14%, marking the 14th consecutive quarter of mid-teens or better performance in that line of business.
Acquisition regulatory progress accelerated with early termination granted by U.S. antitrust regulators, moving estimated closing to early Q1 FY2027.
summary: BCO reported Q2 FY2026 revenue growth of 4% on a constant currency basis (total increase of 7%), with Adjusted EBITDA rising 11% to $257 million and margins expanding 70 bps to record levels. Management raised full-year profit expectations after delivering second-quarter results above the midpoint of prior guidance, while maintaining unchanged revenue frameworks for organic growth in mid-single digits and AMS/DRS expansion.

negative_highlights: Management revised full-year growth expectations for commissions, fees, and insurance results down from a range of 5%-9% to 2%-5% due to observed moderation in economic activity.
Current accounts for individuals declined both quarter-over-quarter and year-over-year as part of an ongoing transformation strategy to reduce friction and increase customer lifetime value.
NII with clients growth was described as stable rather than accelerating, reflecting a cautious outlook on fee income sustainability.
positive_highlights: Recurring net income grew 7.8% year-over-year to BRL 12.4 billion with ROE reaching 24.3% on a consolidated basis.
Loan portfolio expanded by nearly 10% YoY, driven by strong growth in private payroll loans (up 90.1%) and mortgage lending surpassing credit cards at BRL 152 billion.
Cost discipline remained intact with non-interest expenses growing only 3.1% year-over-year while efficiency ratios improved to 37.4% consolidated.
summary: The bank delivered a solid quarter with recurring net income of BRL 12.4 billion (up 7.8% YoY) and loan portfolio growth of nearly 10% year-over-year to reach BRL 1.522 trillion, supported by disciplined cost control that kept non-interest expenses up only 3.1% YoY. Management maintained guidance ranges for most lines but revised the expected growth range for commissions, fees, and insurance results down from 5%-9% to 2%-5%, citing moderation in economic activity levels as a key change versus prior expectations.

negative_highlights: Variable investment income significantly underperformed, causing overall EPS to miss year-over-year expectations by roughly one-third due to PE fund mark-to-market losses.
Underwriting margins decreased 1% year-over-year as the business transitioned from spread-based products toward capital-light fee structures in Group Retirement and Life segments.
Management expects variable investment income returns to remain below target for the remainder of the year, citing geopolitical uncertainty and AI valuation headwinds.
positive_highlights: Run rate earnings per share increased 16% year-over-year to $1.35 when excluding variable investment income impacts.
Fee income grew 17% year-over-year driven by asset growth, while spread income rose 4% due to successful asset repositioning into higher yields.
Life insurance sales reached a run rate above the top end of guidance with favorable mortality results supporting underwriting margins.
summary: Corebridge Financial reported Q2 FY2026 results that were in-line with full-year guidance, delivering Adjusted Pre-Tax Operating Income of $664 million and EPS of $1.12 despite a miss on variable investment income which dragged overall earnings down by approximately 35% year-over-year. Management reiterated its base spread income estimate for the remainder of the year at roughly $2.55 billion, acknowledging continued single-digit compression from book roll-off while noting sequential improvements in sales and fee income across segments.

negative_highlights: Communication market revenue declined 7% sequentially as smartphone demand remains soft in China.
Consumer segment growth slowed to near-flat sequential performance due to memory shortages and slower end-market demand.
positive_highlights: Revenue increased $79.3 million year-over-year driven by record global POS levels.
Gross margin expanded 160 basis points to 33.1% due to cost initiatives and capacity utilization improvements.
Non-GAAP earnings per share more than doubled sequentially, reaching $0.70 from $0.42 in the prior quarter.
summary: Diodes reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $445.5 million (up 22% YoY and 10% sequentially) with GAAP gross margin expanding to 33.1%. The company significantly beat consensus expectations, exceeding its own guidance midpoint for the quarter while maintaining strong demand across automotive, industrial, AI server, and computing segments.

negative_highlights: Excluding the one-time refund benefits, underlying gross margins were flat at 26.1%, offsetting prior period tariff impacts.
Operating profit guidance was lowered from a low teens percentage decline to high single digits due to incremental $6 million in advertising spend and accelerated depreciation.
Management indicated that upside from inventory note-through will be largely offset in the second half of the year by higher commodity costs and freight rates.
positive_highlights: Net sales increased low double digits (11.6%) driven by recovery of U.S. consumer volumes lost to retailer inventory pauses last year.
Gross margin expanded significantly due to a $36.5 million tariff refund and note-through of pre-tariff priced inventory, reaching 54.3% vs 27.5% prior period.
Hamilton Beach Health achieved four consecutive quarters of profitable growth with sales projected to increase by 50% this year.
summary: Hamilton Beach Brands reported Q2 FY2026 net sales of $142.6 million (up 11.6% YoY) and diluted EPS of $2.49, driven by a one-time IEEPA tariff refund of $36.5 million that inflated gross margin to 54.3%. Excluding the refund, underlying operating performance was in-line with expectations as management reinvests proceeds into marketing rather than accelerating buybacks or dividends significantly.

negative_highlights: Occupancy moderated slightly from Q1 due to the proactive recapture of Saks OFF 5th spaces, creating temporary vacancy drag
Recurring CapEx guidance remains unchanged despite elevated TI spend in Q2 related to new openings and re-tenanting
positive_highlights: Core FFO increased 10.3% year-over-year to $0.64 per share

Adjusted operating profit rose 8% to $99 million with an expanded margin of 9.3%, driven by self-help cost initiatives that added roughly 160 bps YoY despite higher input costs like aluminum (+80%) and steel (+20%). Management lowered full-year wholesale shipment guidance from a prior range of 315,000-330,000 to 280,000-300,000 units while maintaining the original adjusted operating profit margin outlook.

negative_highlights: Cash App actives grew only 3% year-over-year in June, reflecting low single-digit expectations for the remainder of 2026.
Consumer lending origination volume normalization is expected to moderate growth rates as Borrow cohorts mature and lapping high-growth periods occurs.
positive_highlights: Gross profit grew 25% year-over-year, driven by strong performance across Square and Cash App ecosystems.
Adjusted diluted EPS increased 65% year-over-year to an all-time high adjusted operating income margin of 27%.
Square U.S. GPV growth accelerated to the strongest rate since Q2 2023, with international growth up 25% on a constant currency basis.
summary: Block reported a strong Q2 FY26 with gross profit growing 25% YoY and adjusted diluted EPS rising 65%, significantly outperforming prior guidance. Management raised full-year guidance for gross profit to $12.5B, adjusted operating income margin to 28%, and adjusted diluted EPS growth of 70%. The company highlighted record profitability in the quarter while accelerating U.S. GPV growth rates not seen since Q2 2023.

negative_highlights: Wireless products continue to face anemic and stable customer demand despite the company's optimism regarding longer-term prospects.
Q1 FY27 guidance includes a net benefit from tariff refunds but is offset by elevated variable costs due to adding one week to the quarter.
positive_highlights: Revenue beat high end of guidance by ~$6 million driven by a massive 52.5% YoY increase and strong sequential growth.
Operating margin expanded significantly to 24%, well above the guided range, aided by favorable product mix in data center lab production.
Data center ecosystem revenue now accounts for approximately 50% of NSE segment total, with Spirent acquisition contributing $145M full-year.
summary: Viavi Solutions reported Q4 FY26 net revenue of $443.1 million (up 52.5% YoY), exceeding the high end of guidance ($427M-$437M). Operating margin expanded to 24%, surpassing the upper bound of its range, driven by a strong data center ecosystem and aerospace/defense demand. Full year revenue reached $1.518 billion (up 40% YoY) with full-year operating margins at 20.6%. Management raised Q1 FY27 guidance to $450M-$460M, citing continued strength in data center optical products.

negative_highlights: Adjusted gross margin contracted to 71.1%, down 120 bps year-over-year due to increased manufacturing costs and mix.
International knee business declined 1.5% in the quarter, heavily impacted by China and core emerging markets.
Pricing pressure remained a headwind of 80 basis points within management's guidance range.
positive_highlights: U.S. hip growth accelerated to 5.9% driven by the Z1 Triple Taper Stem penetration exceeding 40%.
Surgical Technology (S.E.T.) grew 3.4%, a significant acceleration from Q1, led by mid-teens Paragon 28 sales and double-digit CMFT growth.
Technology segment surged with bone cement growing over 50% driven by the ROSA platform.
summary: Zimmer Biomet reported Q2 FY26 net sales of $2.177 billion (4% organic growth) and adjusted EPS of $2.07, beating expectations as the Salesforce transformation accelerated U.S. hip growth to 5.9%. Management raised full-year revenue guidance to 2.25%-3.25% from 1%-3% and increased adjusted EPS guidance to $8.47-$8.59 from $8.40-$8.55, citing strong execution in hips, S.E.T., and robotics despite a pricing headwind of 80 bps.

negative_highlights: International organic FX neutral GMV growth decelerated slightly to 4% in Q2, though this was supported by a 160 bps foreign exchange tailwind.
Management noted that lapping dynamics for certain high-growth categories like Pokémon and bullion will create some near-term pressure on overall growth rates starting in the second half of the year.
positive_highlights: GMV grew 14% YoY to $22.4 billion with Focused Categories growing at a robust 26%, now representing over 70% of total GMV.
Non-GAAP operating income expanded 16% year-over-year to $893 million, demonstrating strong flow-through from top-line growth despite strategic investments.
eBay Live achieved record performance with GMV growing roughly 8x YoY and the platform expanding beyond its invite-only model to self-service onboarding.
summary: eBay reported Q2 FY26 results with GMV growing 14% YoY to $22.4 billion and revenue rising 14% to $3.13 billion, exceeding consensus expectations across all key metrics. Non-GAAP operating income grew 16% year-over-year to $893 million while non-GAAP EPS increased 17% to $1.60. Management raised its full-year GMV guidance range and reiterated strong confidence in the durability of growth driven by strategic priorities like C2C, focused categories, and the newly acquired Depop.

negative_highlights: Effective tax rate increases slightly impacted net income despite underlying business strength.
positive_highlights: Claims volume grew 8% YoY for Patient Management, marking the largest annual quarter-over-quarter increase since December 2024.
New customer sales improved over 60% year-over-year with nearly half of that growth occurring in June alone.
Free cash flow increased to $43.1 million compared to the prior year period.
summary: CorVel reported Q1 FY2026 revenue of $260 million (up 11% YoY) and EPS of $0.63 (up 22% YoY), driven by an 8% increase in claims volume for Patient Management and strong growth across Network Solutions segments including CERIS. The company highlighted a disciplined capital allocation strategy with the repurchase of approximately 377,098 shares ($21.8 million) funded by $43.1 million in free cash flow.

negative_highlights: Free cash flow was impacted by timing of payments related to project starts and activity.
Backlog decreased slightly quarter-over-quarter from $23.7B (implied) to $22.5B due to revenue recognition offsetting additions.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA of $95M more than doubled year-over-year compared to $45M in Q3 FY25.
Gross margin expanded sequentially and year-over-year due to strong project execution, cost discipline, benefits from scale, and revenue mix.
SymMicro prototype installation at Walmart began with a second site following shortly after.
summary: Symbotic reported Q3 FY26 revenue of $721 million (up 22% YoY) and GAAP net income of $55 million, driven by expanding margins where gross margin reached approximately 40.8%. Adjusted EBITDA was $95 million, exceeding the forecast range due to operational efficiencies and a strong mix from software services revenue which grew 57% YoY.

negative_highlights: Adjusted operating costs grew 10% in the quarter, exceeding the guidance range of 8%-9%, primarily due to incremental variable compensation.
Digital subscription revenue growth outlook for Q3 (12%-15%) is noted as slightly below recent operational performance levels.
positive_highlights: Digital subscription revenues surged 16.4% YoY with net new digital subscribers adding 280,000 in Q2.
Total advertising revenue beat expectations by growing 11.3%, driven primarily by higher Wirecutter affiliate referral revenues and strong marketer demand.
summary: Consolidated revenues grew 11% YoY to approximately $2 billion (implied), driven by digital subscription revenue growth of 16.4% and total advertising revenue increases exceeding expectations at +11.3%. Adjusted operating profit expanded 16%, while adjusted diluted EPS rose 19% to $0.69, though costs grew slightly above the guided range due to variable compensation tied to outperformance.

negative_highlights: High-Value Sender volume growth was softer in June due to fluctuations in the Indian rupee relative to primary send currencies.
Q2 results lapped a particularly strong holiday season (Ramadan/Easter) which drove outsized prior-year growth, potentially complicating Q3 comparisons.
positive_highlights: Revenue beat high-end guidance by $11M, driven by 27% send volume growth to $23.5B and High-Value Sender volume more than doubling in the U.S.-Mexico corridor.
Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded significantly year-over-year due to AI-driven productivity gains (holding headcount below plan) and lower transaction losses of $24.5M.
Growth accelerators gained traction with record new customer additions, over 10 million quarterly active users reached for the first time, and revenue from receivers generated positive contribution.
summary: Remitly reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $495 million (up 20% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $115 million (margin expanded to 23%), both beating the high end of guidance. Management raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance by approximately $80-90M, citing strong core momentum and scaling growth accelerators like High-Value Senders and Business segments. The company achieved a milestone with over 10 million quarterly active users and generated record free cash flow of $130 million.

negative_highlights: Total revenue declined $13.4 million year-over-year primarily due to generic competition impacting AURYXIA sales.
The company swung from net income of $0.2M in Q2 FY2025 to a net loss of $8.9M in Q2 FY2026.
Management explicitly stated that 2027 revenues are expected to decrease compared to 2026 due to planned price cuts.
positive_highlights: Vafseo net product revenue increased $8.0 million quarter-over-quarter (34% growth) and year-over-year (60%).
The VOICE trial interim analysis met stopping criteria with a P value of 0.0016, demonstrating superiority over ESAs.
Patient adherence on first refill is strong at approximately 89%, indicating good initial compliance.
summary: Total revenues decreased to $49.1 million in Q2 FY2026 from $62.5 million a year ago due to lower AURYXIA sales ($25.5M vs $47.2M) partially offset by strong Vafseo growth ($21.3M, up 60% YoY). The company reported its first quarter with over 10,000 patients on therapy and a net loss of $8.9 million driven by lower revenues and higher expenses including commercial reorganization costs. Management expressed confidence in the VOICE trial results but cautioned that Vafseo unit sales volumes will increase while total revenue is expected to decrease in 2027 due to planned price reductions after the TDAPA period ends.

negative_highlights: Net investment loss of $23.8 million, primarily due to a -5.4% return in the Solasglas portfolio
Underwriting result included a combined ratio of 100.1%, with cat and large losses accounting for 17.1 percentage points
Middle East conflict reserves increased by $20 million plus an additional $6.5 million provision for Qatar refinery explosion
positive_highlights: Innovation segment generated $2.6 million underwriting profit and achieved a combined ratio of 89.7%, down from 107% last year
Attritional loss ratio improved by 4.3 percentage points to 51.7%
Company repurchased shares totaling $18.1 million during the quarter ($14.2M + $3.9M)
summary: Greenlight Re reported a net loss of $29.6 million ($0.89 EPS) for Q2 FY2026 driven by investment losses from the Solasglas portfolio and underwriting provisions totaling $26.5 million related to Middle East conflict and Qatar refinery events. While the innovation segment delivered strong results with an 89.7% combined ratio, overall net written premiums declined 11% as management reduced exposure in response to softening market conditions.

negative_highlights: Gross margin contracted by approximately four points sequentially (to 71%) due to Statsig hosting environment optimization needs and higher AI inference adoption.
Operating loss widened slightly to $1.5M as the company invests in scaling new products like Wave and optimizing cloud structures.
positive_highlights: Raised full-year non-GAAP operating income guidance range significantly above prior expectations based on Q2 performance.
Organic ARR growth of $19M combined with Statsig contribution drove total ARR up to $410M, a record level for the company.
Free cash flow hit an all-time quarterly high of $23.7 million despite increased inference spend and integration costs.
summary: Amplitude reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $101 million (up 21% YoY) and Total ARR of $410 million (up 22% YoY), driven by organic growth of $19M and inorganic Statsig acquisition. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance for non-GAAP operating income to between $6.3M-$9.3M, citing strong pipeline conversion from new pricing/packaging and AI adoption. While gross margins dipped slightly due to inference costs and integration expenses, the company returned a record $23.7 million in free cash flow.

negative_highlights: GAAP net loss of $5.1 million, though adjusted non-GAAP metrics show improvement with negative EBITDA narrowing.
Working capital increased due to deliberate inventory buildup ($3.3M) and receivables growth ($40.7M) for H2 ramp.
positive_highlights: Revenue beat expectations with sequential growth for the sixth consecutive quarter driven by strong drone adoption.
Gross margin expanded significantly to 27% (up from 9% YoY) as favorable mix and cost efficiencies took hold.
Raised full-year revenue guidance to $140M+ and gross margin target to 28%, reflecting high demand visibility.
summary: Amprius reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $34 million (up 19% sequentially and 2.3x YoY) with a gross margin expansion to 27%. The company raised its full-year 2026 revenue guidance from >$130M to at least $140M, along with raising the gross margin target to at least 28%, while reiterating adjusted EBITDA of more than $4 million. Management highlighted robust demand in defense drones and commercial UAVs, including a new $24M order from a European customer.

negative_highlights: Revenue growth was offset by a significant $2.4 billion headwind due to manufacturer list price reductions in the U.S. Healthcare Solutions segment.
The company lost an oncology customer (Florida Cancer) which impacted revenue, though this impact is now fully lapped for Q4 guidance.
positive_highlights: Adjusted operating income grew 17% to $1.2 billion, driven by double-digit organic growth in the core business excluding OneOncology contributions.
GLP-1 sales increased significantly year-over-year with a headwind of only $2.4 billion from manufacturer list price reductions.
OneOncology and RCA platforms performed ahead of expectations following weather-related disruptions seen previously.
summary: Cencora reported Q3 FY26 adjusted operating income growth of 17% and EPS growth of 12%, driven by strong execution in the U.S. Healthcare Solutions segment including OneOncology performance and GLP-1 sales up $2.3 billion YoY, partially offset by a manufacturer list price headwind of $2.4 billion. Management raised full-year FY26 adjusted EPS guidance to $17.75-$17.95 from the prior range of $17.70-$17.90 while keeping revenue guidance unchanged and raising operating income growth expectations for both consolidated and U.S. segments.

negative_highlights: BIVIGAM revenue remains substantially down compared to the prior year as competitive pressures persist in the standard immunoglobulin market.
Management explicitly stated they are not guiding for BIVIGAM recovery, anticipating it will remain roughly 40%-50% below 2025 levels through the balance of the year.
positive_highlights: ASCENIV revenue grew 24% year-over-year to $102.9 million as demand accelerated with June delivering the strongest sequential utilization growth since H1 2024.
Gross margin expanded significantly to 69%, up from 55% in the prior year period, reflecting ASCENIV mix expansion and yield-enhanced manufacturing benefits.
Real-world evidence base strengthened with new data showing reduced hospitalizations and antibiotic use for medically complex patients.
summary: ADMA reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $124.4 million (up 2% YoY) and gross margin expansion to 69%, driven by a 24% increase in ASCENIV sales while BIVIGAM stabilized sequentially. Management reiterated full-year guidance for total revenue between $530M-$560M, adjusted EBITDA of $265M-$300M, and adjusted net income of $170M-$200M despite ongoing competitive pressures in the standard immunoglobulin market.

negative_highlights: Reported adjusted EBITDA was impacted by a non-routine self-insurance adjustment of $16M related to adverse development on prior year claims.
Elevated fuel costs created an estimated $4 million headwind in the quarter, with management noting these pressures are expected to persist through Q4 2026.
Ancillary revenue growth was modest at approximately 2% as the company balanced pricing against customer acceptance.
positive_highlights: Land maintenance grew 2.3% YoY for a second consecutive quarter with contract book growth accelerating to 4% from Q2.
Customer retention improved by approximately 250 basis points and frontline turnover decreased about seven percentage points versus the prior year.
Operational efficiency initiatives reduced fuel consumption by 10%, mitigating roughly $2 million of headwinds despite higher prices.
summary: BrightView reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $718 million (up 1.3% YoY), driven by a second consecutive quarter of land maintenance growth (+2.3%) but offset by snow declines and headwinds from elevated fuel costs ($4M impact) plus a non-routine self-insurance adjustment ($16M). Management reaffirmed its previously raised FY2026 guidance for total revenue ($2.75B-$2.78B) while revising adjusted EBITDA and free cash flow targets downward to reflect the specific quarter's fuel and insurance impacts, excluding which they remain on track for record levels.

negative_highlights: Wastewater results described as 'pretty soft'.
Formal delays communicated on mega projects due to financing challenges and geopolitical risk premiums.
Contracting activity in the Middle East has resumed but delivery timelines remain pushed out, limiting immediate revenue impact.
positive_highlights: Pipeline characterized as 'uniquely strong' with forward visibility extending five years despite timing uncertainties.
summary: Management provided no specific revenue or EPS figures for Q2 FY2026 in the transcript, noting only that wastewater results were 'pretty soft' while OEM and aftermarket businesses remained resilient despite geopolitical headwinds. The company reiterated its full-year CapEx guidance of $3 million-$6 million but declined to provide updated financial guidance due to ongoing delays caused by financing challenges and geopolitical risks in key markets.

negative_highlights: Management noted a foreign exchange headwind of approximately $4 million on revenue due to U.S. dollar strength.
Q1 net new ARR growth was exceptionally high at 66% organically, which management cautioned is not sustainable quarter-over-quarter.
positive_highlights: Total ARR grew 17% YoY with record new logo growth exceeding 160% driven by large enterprise lands averaging nearly $285k.
Non-GAAP operating margin expanded to 29%, beating the high end of guidance by 100 bps due to revenue upside and expense timing.
Log management consumption doubled since crossing the $100M milestone, now reaching nearly $200 million in annualized run rate.
summary: Dynatrace reported Q1 FY2027 revenue of $555 million and subscription revenue of $530 million, both exceeding the high end of guidance by approximately 1% (100 bps). Total ARR grew 17% YoY to $2.14 billion with record new logo growth over 160%, while non-GAAP operating margin expanded to 29%. Management raised full-year revenue and EPS guidance, citing strong momentum in logs consumption ($200M) and AI observability adoption.

negative_highlights: HomeXpress earnings grew only modestly quarter-over-quarter due primarily to margin compression from increased competition.
GAAP net loss of approximately $4 million, with book value per share declining 3.2% to $17.75 driven by mark-to-market volatility on securitized loans.
Third-party advisory fee revenue experienced some dilution amid reduced transaction activity.
positive_highlights: HomeXpress loan production grew by 30% compared to the second quarter of 2025, reaching record monthly volume in June.
Net origination margin for HomeXpress expanded to 124 basis points despite competitive pressure.
Company redeployed nearly $700 million from portfolio management activities into liquid agency MBS and new credit opportunities.
summary: Chimera Investment Corporation reported a GAAP net loss of $4 million for Q2 FY26, driven by an investment portfolio segment loss of $13 million offset by residential origination income of $9 million and EAD per share of $0.46. Management noted that HomeXpress loan production grew 30% year-over-year to $1.1 billion but earnings growth was modest due to margin compression from increased competition, with net origination margins expanding only 10 bps despite tighter pricing. The company pivoted strategy toward acquiring and securitizing third-party loans while maintaining a strong liquidity position of $656 million.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA loss increased significantly from CAD 13.9 million in Q1 to CAD 21.3 million due to higher R&D spend.
Grant revenue was lower than expected, contributing directly to the widening operating losses.
Management declined to provide explicit OpEx/CapEx guidance for H2 and stated they are not providing specific financial forecasts.
positive_highlights: Achieved ultra-low-loss photonic chip packaging milestone with an average edge coupling loss of just 0.085 dB per facet.
Increased fabrication runs on thin-film lithium niobate platforms by roughly 75% and silicon nitride by roughly 50%. Albany workforce has grown more than fivefold since 2023.
PennyLane foundational white paper surpassed 2,000 citations; active user base continues to increase across universities and corporate entities.
summary: Xanadu reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of CAD 1.5 million (down from CAD 2.8M in Q1 and up slightly from the prior year quarter), with R&D expenses rising to CAD 19.7 million and Adjusted EBITDA loss widening to CAD 21.3 million compared to a CAD 13.9 million loss in Q1, driven by increased headcount and lower grant revenue.

negative_highlights: Product delays created a revenue gap that will not be fully recovered in 2026 due to accelerated new product introduction pace
Recovery of largest FWA customer taking longer than expected, factored into lower second-half revenue expectations
MSO opportunity removed from full-year outlook as conversion is slower than anticipated
positive_highlights: Q2 revenue delivered at the high end of guidance range driven by strong mobile portfolio launches across three tier-one carriers
Newest tier-one carrier relationship performing well in both mobile and FWA segments, validating strategy to broaden customer base
Inseego Subscribe achieved CMMC Level 2 certification, strengthening platform ability for U.S. federal government programs
summary: Q2 revenue was $44 million (high end of guidance) with sequential growth driven by late-quarter orders from a new tier-one carrier to front-load memory costs before anticipated price increases in H2; however, gross margin compressed to 34% due to higher-cost component allocation on that specific deal. Management updated the full-year 2026 revenue outlook down to approximately $155 million citing product delays and slower recovery from a large FWA customer, while removing MSO revenue from forecasts as conversion takes longer than expected.

negative_highlights: $37.5 million milestones were not achieved in Q2 due to buyer-reported results, though they remain eligible for future quarters
Cash equivalents and investments decreased from $167M at Q1 end to $105.3M at Q2 end
positive_highlights: LOQTORZI net sales grew 15% q-o-q to $13.6M with highest new patient starts since launch
R&D expenses decreased YoY from $26.3M to $21.4M driven by reduced head count and trial costs
SG&A expense declined YoY from $26.0M to $21.0M following the exit of the biosimilar business
summary: Coherus Oncology reported Q2 FY26 net sales of $13.6 million for LOQTORZI, representing a 15% quarter-over-quarter growth and the highest number of new patient starts since launch following a seasonal slowdown. The company exited with renewed momentum in its commercial business while clinical programs advanced to initial data readouts expected later this year or Q4. Financially, R&D expenses decreased to $21.4 million and SG&A fell to $21.0 million due to post-divestiture savings.

negative_highlights: $244 million non-cash goodwill impairment charge related to Omni Logistics customer uncertainty
Operating loss of $201 million due to the one-time impairment, excluding which income was only $43M
Revenue per hundred weight decreased as a strategic trade-off for increased load factors and higher tonnage
positive_highlights: Operating revenue hit a record high of $673 million, up from $619 million last year
Expedited Freight segment achieved best EBITDA ($43M) and margin (13.6%) since early 2024
Intermodal segment reported its best EBITDA in five quarters with a 16.7% margin
summary: Forward Air reported Q2 FY26 operating revenue of $673 million and consolidated EBITDA of $93 million, both record highs for the company since the transaction two years ago. However, a non-cash goodwill impairment charge of $244 million in the Omni Logistics segment resulted in an operating loss of $201 million for the quarter. Management highlighted strong market fundamentals including higher diesel prices and capacity tightening but noted that macro uncertainties remain.

negative_highlights: GAAP net income and EPS declined slightly due to a higher effective tax rate rather than business softening.
Total loan production in dollars was $672.6 million, down from $725 million a year ago due to lower average loan size.
Net gain on non-performing loan resolution decreased to $2.5 million compared to $2.8 million in the prior year.
positive_highlights: Core net income grew to $27.9 million while GAAP pre-tax income increased 3.9% YoY to $35.2 million.
Non-performing loan rate fell to 9.6% of held for investment loans, down from 10.3% a year ago.
Unit production rose 3.3% with weighted average coupon on new originations holding steady at approximately 10%.
summary: Velocity Financial reported Q2 FY2026 core net income of $27.9 million and pre-tax income up 3.9% year-over-year to $35.2 million, though GAAP net income decreased slightly due to a higher effective tax rate. The company grew its total loan portfolio to $7 billion in UPB (up 19% YoY) with unit production increasing 3.3% despite a slight decline in dollar volume driven by lower average loan sizes. Management expressed confidence in the pipeline and expects origination volumes to increase for the rest of the year, though they declined to provide formal forward guidance.

negative_highlights: Average note price (ASP) ticked lower sequentially due to channel mix shifts toward community/independent orders and a shift by consumers to base-level models.
Adjusted gross margin is expected to be in the low-to-mid-20s range for Q2, reflecting ongoing elevated input cost inflation that pricing actions have not yet fully offset.
Canadian home sales declined volume-wise (185 units vs 250 prior year) due to weather-related disruptions.
positive_highlights: Net sales increased 1.3% year-over-year to $710.2 million, slightly ahead of expectations due to stronger anticipated demand.
Manufacturing backlog grew significantly to $421.8 million from $302 million in the prior period, indicating robust order flow despite industry-wide declines.
The company successfully closed the Homes Direct acquisition on August 1st and integrated its team into Champion.
summary: Champion Homes reported Q1 FY2027 net sales of $710.2 million (up 1.3% YoY) and adjusted EPS of $0.88 per share, slightly ahead of expectations with results aligning to guidance. The company raised its backlog by approximately 34% sequentially to $421.8 million while maintaining utilization at 62%. Management provided Q2 revenue guidance in the mid-single digits excluding Homes Direct and expects adjusted gross margins between 25%-26%, citing elevated input costs as a primary headwind.

negative_highlights: International organic sales declined 1.4% due to Middle East conflict, lower private label sales from supply disruptions, and a weak sun season start.
Adjusted gross margin declined 30 basis points YoY as higher inflation on commodities offset productivity savings of ~200 bps.
Private label wet shave availability constraints pressured overall branded share in the U.S. by 40 basis points.
positive_highlights: Organic net sales returned to growth of 1.1% in the quarter, driven by North America (+3%) and branded wet shave recovery.
Cremo delivered seven consecutive quarters of approximately 20% or more growth; Hawaiian Tropic grew 110 basis points on the year to become #4 brand.
Branded unit market share held steady or increased in 39 of the past 43 weeks in the U.S.
summary: Edgewell reported Q3 FY26 organic net sales growth of 1.1% and adjusted EPS of $0.72 (flat YoY), beating expectations despite a decline in international sales due to supply disruptions and Middle East conflict impacts. Management maintained full-year guidance ranges for Adjusted EPS ($1.80-$2) and EBITDA ($250m-$260m) while narrowing the outlook, citing Q4 as an inflection point with expected margin expansion from productivity savings and favorable FX. The company reaffirmed its commitment to planned A&P investment levels despite a challenging cost environment.

negative_highlights: Renewables gross margins were slightly negative due to project cost overruns on six specific projects that are expected to be completed by year-end.
Communications segment revenue and margin declined as customers transitioned from fiber-to-the-home programs to BEAD-funded maintenance work.
Cash used in operations was $8.7 million, a significant decrease compared to the prior year's cash provided of around $78 million.
positive_highlights: Record backlog reached just under $13.9 billion at quarter-end, an increase of approximately $2.2 billion sequentially driven by strong energy segment bookings for natural gas generation and electrical construction services from PayneCrest.
PaynCrest acquisition is exceeding expectations with the business adding $250 million in new awards during its first two months under Primoris ownership.
Natural gas power generation delivered double-digit revenue growth, accounting for approximately $1.4 billion of sequential backlog increase.
summary: Primoris reported Q2 FY26 revenue of approximately $1.7 billion, a decrease of about $200 million (or 10.7%) year-over-year driven by lower activity in the energy segment's renewables business and communications. Gross profit declined to $82.4 million with gross margins contracting significantly from 12.3% in the prior year to 4.9%, primarily due to cost overruns on six specific renewable projects and a shift toward maintenance work in utilities. Management maintained full-year guidance for adjusted EPS of $2.05-$2.60, stating that Q2 results represent the low point before sequential improvement is expected through H2.

negative_highlights: Full-year free cash flow conversion expected to normalize with lower margins (8.5%) for the second half due to higher levels of growth investments
Pending integration costs associated with recent acquisitions of SE&M and Epsilon Industries will impact near-term liquidity
positive_highlights: Record Q2 revenues of $1.23 billion representing a 34% year-over-year increase
EBITDA margin expanded to 10.4%, up 130 basis points from the prior year period
Backlog grew significantly to $4.55 billion, driven by organic growth in E&M and contributions from SE&M acquisition
summary: Everus reported record Q2 FY26 revenues of $1.23 billion (up 34% YoY) and EBITDA of $128.6 million with a margin expansion to 10.4%. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance, forecasting revenue between $4.5B-$4.7B and EBITDA between $410M-$425M based on strong first-half execution.

negative_highlights: Adjusted net investment income decreased due to lower leverage, lighter non-recurring income, and partial incentive fee payment
Approximately $50 million in realized credit losses recognized during the quarter from longstanding positions like Dominion
Proceeds from exits declined to $263 million compared to $334 million last quarter
positive_highlights: Non-accruals declined to 1.8% of total debt portfolio, down from 3.2% one year ago
Thrasio repayment converted a non-accrual position into cash proceeds and an income-producing loan expected to be repaid in the near term
NAV per share remained stable at $15.70 despite realized losses
summary: Adjusted net investment income declined to $32.2 million ($0.37 per share) from the prior quarter's $33.7 million due to lower leverage and a partial incentive fee payment of $2.4 million, while adjusted total investment income fell slightly to $69.2 million. The company reduced non-accruals by exiting five positions including Thrasio repayments but recognized approximately $50 million in realized losses during the quarter. Management maintains net leverage at 1.02x and emphasizes a defensive posture with ample liquidity of nearly $700 million amidst market volatility.

negative_highlights: Gross margin contracted by 210 basis points to 43.8% due to a higher mix of capital equipment and the amortization impact from the Kadant Profil acquisition.
Capital project bookings remain soft with extended approval cycles, though management notes projects are being deferred rather than lost.
Leverage ratio increased sequentially to 1.72 as net debt rose $129 million due to funding for recent acquisitions.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EPS of $3.42 exceeded prior high-end guidance by $0.44, driven by record aftermarket revenue ($214M) and strong acquisition performance.
Organic capital revenue grew 23%, with the Industrial Processing segment delivering a record adjusted EBITDA margin of 26.1%.
Management raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $1.19B-$1.21B following an outperforming quarter.
summary: Kadant reported record Q2 FY26 revenue of $313 million (up 8% organic) and adjusted EPS of $3.42, which exceeded the high end of prior guidance by $0.44 due to strong acquisitions and lower expenses than forecasted. Management raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance from a range of $1.178B-$1.203B to $1.19B-$1.21B, while keeping adjusted EPS guidance unchanged at $12.43-$12.68 despite the beat. The company remains cautious regarding capital project timing due to geopolitical uncertainty and customer approval cycles.

negative_highlights: Bunker prices increased approximately 36% quarter-over-quarter due to Middle East disruptions and inconsistent fuel availability
Panama Canal auction fees remained elevated, impacting realized rates despite high freight postings
Peace prospects remain fragile with ceasefire breakdowns in early July reaffirming market uncertainty
positive_highlights: Record-high TCE revenue of $75,926 per available day reported for the quarter
Helios Pool earned $82,445 in TCE per day reflecting favorable market conditions
U.S. exports reached a record 20.8 million tons with Panama congestion amplifying ton-mile demand
summary: Dorian LPG reported Q1 FY2026 (ended June 30) results driven by a de facto closure of the Strait of Hormuz which disrupted Middle East volumes and drove fleet to U.S. Gulf, resulting in record-high freight rates but also significantly elevated bunker costs (+36% qoq). The company declared an irregular $1 per share dividend ($42.8M total) as its 20th payment while maintaining a conservative approach to new building orders despite strong cash balances nearing $600 million.

negative_highlights: Adjusted SG&A increased as a percentage of net sales due to higher variable compensation and logistics costs (6.9%).
Household penetration growth is expected to slow or stabilize sequentially in the second half of the year.
Q3 YoY comps will be tougher by more than two points due to prior-year expansion at a large club customer.
positive_highlights: Delivered strongest growth rate in over a year with volume contributing 15.7% YoY growth despite challenging macro backdrop.
Adjusted gross margin expanded significantly by 170 bps to 48.6%, driven by operational leverage and lower input costs.
Raised full-year sales guidance range from 8%-11% to 10%-12% based on strong first-half performance.
summary: Freshpet reported Q2 FY26 net sales of $305.6 million (up 15.5% YoY) and adjusted gross margin expanding to 48.6%. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance for net sales growth to 10%-12% from the prior range of 8%-11%, while also raising Adjusted EBITDA guidance to $210-$220 million.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA missed internal targets by approximately $2.8 million, primarily driven by the conscious decision to lower introductory pricing for branded GLP-1s.
Revenue declined sequentially by roughly 6% due to planned step-down in marketing investments and increased cost-per-acquisition (CPA) levels throughout much of the quarter.
The company admitted it underestimated the near-term profitability pressure caused by its strategic transition away from a purely paid-media growth model.
positive_highlights: Gross margin expanded sequentially by approximately 60 basis points (bps) to 89% driven by lower shipping costs and improved provider efficiency.
Weight management customer acquisition costs moderated significantly, dropping to approximately 50% of their peak levels since mid-June.
Women's health patient base grew 134% quarter-over-quarter with new daily acquisitions ranging from 50-100 patients.
summary: LifeMD reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $47.3 million within guidance but missed its own adjusted EBITDA target with a loss of approximately $3.5 million due to elevated customer acquisition costs and the introduction of a new $39 introductory offer for branded GLP-1 therapies. Management revised full-year 2026 outlooks, lowering revenue expectations to $205.5M-$212.5M and adjusted EBITDA guidance to negative $6 million through breakeven, citing the near-term pressure from strategic restructuring investments in pharmacy, insurance partnerships, and new product launches.

negative_highlights: U.S. price declined by 3% (9% excluding rebate adjustments) driven by ZEPBOUND and MOUNJARO
Marketing, note, and administrative expenses increased 25% due to promotional investments for launches
Foundayo U.S. launch curve described as slower than anticipated in early phases
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 48% YoY driven by ZEPBOUND and MOUNJARO with key products up nearly $6.8 billion
Non-GAAP EPS of $8.38 beat prior year, reflecting a strong underlying performance across all therapeutic areas
Foundayo U.S. launch showing inflection point in late July with volume doubling from the previous month and 1-in-4 new starts on Foundayo
summary: Q2 FY2026 revenue grew 48% YoY to $37 billion (implied from growth rate and context), with key products increasing by almost $6.8 billion driven by ZEPBOUND and MOUNJARO. Management raised full-year guidance, updating the non-GAAP EPS range midpoint up by $2.78 per share before IPR&D charges and expanding revenue expectations to between $85B-$87B. The quarter featured robust international growth (Europe +55%, China +93%) alongside strong U.S. volume expansion for incretins, despite a noted 3% price decline in the U.S.

negative_highlights: Q3 consolidated revenue growth was muted at only +$119M YoY due to Micro Bird consolidation and a 7% unit volume decline driven by finished goods inventory
Reported gross margin compressed to 20.0%, down 160 bps from prior year, primarily due to the full-year consolidation of Micro Bird revenue versus partial EBITDA contribution
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA hit a record $71 million, up $13M YoY and beating guidance on all metrics
Raised full-year Adjusted EBITDA guidance to $245-$250 million following the strong Q3 beat
Announced expanded collaboration with Ford for Class 5/6 chassis market starting in fiscal 2028, expanding total addressable market by over $1.4 billion
summary: Blue Bird reported Q3 FY26 revenue of $517 million and Adjusted EBITDA of a record $71 million, beating guidance on all metrics for the 15th consecutive quarter despite unit volume being down 7% due to finished goods inventory. Management raised full-year fiscal 2026 Adjusted EBITDA guidance to a range of $245-$250 million (midpoint ~$247M) and maintained revenue guidance at the same midpoint, citing strong Q3 execution as justification for the raise. The quarter included consolidation effects from Micro Bird acquisition which compressed reported margins but improved underlying profitability.

negative_highlights: Fourth quarter UTI high school starts are tracking below initial outlook due to an execution issue where field staffing levels were insufficient to convert all prospective leads.
The portfolio mix shifted faster than anticipated toward skilled trades programs, which have shorter durations and drive less revenue per student compared to automotive/diesel offerings.
Full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance was lowered from a prior expectation of north of $155M to an expected range between $100-$103M.
positive_highlights: New campus launches outperformed expectations, with Atlanta tracking 30% ahead of plan and San Antonio at roughly 40% above launch model projections.
Total new student starts increased 10.9% YoY to 6,342 driven by strength in skilled trades offerings across both divisions.
Average full-time active students grew 5.8% YoY to 25,131 reflecting continued enrollment growth.
summary: UTI reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $219 million (7% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $18 million after excluding $9M in strategic growth investments. Management lowered full-year fiscal 2026 guidance, projecting consolidated revenue between $893-$900 million due to softer-than-expected Q4 high school starts in the UTI division's auto/diesel channel and a faster-than-planned shift toward lower-revenue skilled trades programs.

negative_highlights: Pre-tax profits declined 47% quarter-over-quarter to BRL 115 million due to high upfront costs and provisioning for new loan vintages.
Net Interest Margin (NIM) compressed by 50 basis points on a quarterly basis, with the annualized NIM flattish at 11.9%.
Operating efficiency ratio increased only slightly to 48.9%, reflecting variable expenses tied to rapid client acquisition ahead of revenue compounding.
positive_highlights: Private payroll portfolio grew nearly 50% quarter-over-quarter, with secured personal loan originations increasing more than 80%.
Fee revenues reached BRL 135 million and increased over 35% sequentially, driven by an 80% increase in brokerage fees.
Agi+ subscription platform launched successfully with over 250,000 subscribers in just 45 days.
summary: Agi reported Q2 FY26 revenue of BRL 3.2 billion (up 26% YoY) and recurring net income of BRL 200 million (down 47% quarter-over-quarter). While credit origination surged with the private payroll portfolio growing nearly 50% sequentially, pre-tax profits were pressured by upfront costs associated with rapid growth in untested products. Management describes this as a recovery inflection point but explicitly characterizes the profit decline and margin compression as transitory due to high provisioning needs for new vintages.

negative_highlights: Same-restaurant sales declined 1.2% due to a combination of traffic headwinds and promotional lapses.
