negative_highlights: Drydock costs expected to increase in Q3 and Q4 2026
Supply growth of 3.3% over last 12 months
No explicit full-year guidance provided
positive_highlights: Adjusted EPS of $1.21 and EBITDA of $184.2 million
Cash balance increased to $532 million despite shareholder returns
Mark-to-market gain of ~$56 million on Kamsarmax newbuildings
summary: Star Bulk reported Q2 FY2026 adjusted EPS of $1.21 and adjusted EBITDA of $184.2 million, with a daily cash margin of $17,944. The company declared a $0.09 per share dividend and continues to return 100% of operating cash flow. Management highlighted strong cash generation, low leverage (net debt at 50% of demolition value), and ongoing fleet rejuvenation with new Kamsarmax deliveries, while noting expectations for Simandou volumes to ramp from 15-20 million tons in 2026 to 120 million by 2029.

negative_highlights: Q2 net income was impacted by a one-time inventory step-up amortization of $2 million and contingent consideration expense of $5.9 million.
FX headwinds reduced bottom-line earnings by approximately $6.6 million in the quarter.
Management noted that Q3 revenue is expected to be lower than Q2 as mix reverts from high-margin Zircaloy robotic arms, with European margins potentially softening.
positive_highlights: Net sales grew 32% year-over-year to $207.1 million, significantly exceeding typical expectations given recent M&A integration headwinds.
Adjusted EBITDA surged 56% YoY with gross margins expanding 120 bps to 42.6%, aided by favorable mix and volume leverage in the Zircaloy segment.
Backlog increased $13 million sequentially, driven particularly by Environmental Operations Division (EOD) demand for sensors and robots.
summary: Cadre reported Q2 FY26 net sales of $207.1 million (up 32% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA growth of 56%, driven by strong performance in armor, duty gear, nuclear, and distribution segments including recent acquisitions Alien Gear and TYR Tactical. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance to revenue between $749M-$769M (midpoint ~$759M) and adjusted EBITDA of $139M-$144M (implied margin 18.6%), citing a record backlog increase of $13 million sequentially. The company expects Q3 revenue around $190M with margins normalizing, while maintaining an organic growth outlook in the high single digits to low double digits for nuclear and mid-single digits for distribution.

negative_highlights: Q3 revenue growth guidance of 25.5%-26% implies deceleration from Q2's 27%
Q3 adjusted EBITDA guidance remains negative, reflecting seasonal patterns and investment
Gross margin expected to revert lower in Q3 as non-subscription revenue normalizes
positive_highlights: Revenue up 27% YoY to $136 million, above the high end of guidance
Pipeline doubled YoY for the second consecutive quarter, surpassing $700 million in growth ACV
Adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed to -$3.4 million, a record low margin of -2.5%
summary: Via reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $136 million, up 27% year-over-year, with 847 customers (up 23% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA loss narrowing to -$3.4 million from -$8.1 million in the prior year. Management raised full-year revenue guidance to $550-$553 million (26.6%-27.3% growth) while maintaining adjusted EBITDA guidance, and noted pipeline doubled for the second consecutive quarter. Gross margin expanded to 41% due to favorable mix, and adjusted net loss per share improved to -$0.01. Growth is driven by strong U.S. performance (up 35% YoY), network deals, and new AI Labs initiatives.

negative_highlights: Cable segment EBITDA declined 3% in Q4 due to higher sports rights costs
Free cash flow impacted by World Cup working capital timing, with collections expected in fiscal 2027
positive_highlights: Record full-year revenue of over $17 billion and EBITDA of $3.9 billion
Q4 advertising revenue up 78%, with Tubi revenue growth accelerating to 35%
Management calls fiscal 2027 off to an excellent start with strong political and upfront momentum
summary: Fox delivered record fiscal 2026 results with revenue up 5% to over $17 billion and EBITDA up 8% to a record $3.9 billion. Q4 revenue grew 28% to $4.2 billion and EBITDA grew 27% to $1.2 billion, driven by a 78% advertising revenue increase from the FIFA World Cup and Tubi's 35% revenue growth. Management raised the semi-annual dividend to $0.29 and expects continued momentum in fiscal 2027 with World Cup knockout stages and midterm elections. The pending Roku acquisition is on track for closing in first half calendar 2027.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened significantly to $159 million from $42.7 million year-over-year, primarily due to an $86.2 million non-cash warrant fair value adjustment.
R&D expenses increased substantially to $48.7 million (from $29.8M) and G&A rose to $26.4 million (from $11.1M), reflecting heavy investment in clinical trials and commercial build-out.
positive_highlights: Phase III study EMERGE met all primary endpoints, demonstrating an 8.1 point placebo-adjusted improvement on MADRS at week six and the largest treatment effect ever reported in a Phase III MDD study.
summary: Definium Therapeutics reported Q2 FY2026 results with R&D expenses of $48.7 million and G&A expenses of $26.4 million, driven by clinical program expansion and commercial readiness investments for DT120 ODT. The company recorded a net loss of $159 million in the quarter compared to $42.7 million last year, largely due to an $86.2 million non-cash expense from warrant fair value adjustments as share prices rose. Management highlighted positive Phase III EMERGE data for MDD and upcoming VOYAGE results for GAD while noting a strengthened balance sheet with approximately $1.1 billion in cash sufficient through 2030.

negative_highlights: Management noted potential operational inefficiencies and higher auction fees for Panama Canal transits due to a high probability of El Niño weather events.
Other operating expenses included financial advisory costs related to inadequate tender offers from Diana Shipping, totaling $13.1 million.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA of nearly $57 million exceeded expectations as dry bulk market fundamentals strengthened.
Q2 dividend increased by over 400% year-over-year, marking a record level since the strategy's inception in 2021.
Fleet acquisitions have generated an IRR exceeding 30%, with new vessels contributing approximately $0.15 per share to Q2 dividends.
summary: Genco Shipping reported Q2 FY2026 adjusted EBITDA of $56.7 million and declared a dividend of $0.80 per share, which was more than double the prior quarter's payout. The company generated strong cash flow driven by a time charter equivalent rate (TCE) averaging over $24,200 per day, its highest quarterly level since 2022. Management projects Q3 and Q4 dividends to exceed $1 per share each based on current fixtures and the forward freight curve.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA guidance moved to lower end of previous range
Rest of world EBITDA declined slightly due to inflation outpacing pricing
Macroeconomic uncertainty and demand softness in Europe
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA up 9% to $99 million, strongest quarter as Magnera
Americas adjusted EBITDA up 16% to $71 million
Free cash flow guidance reaffirmed at $90-$110 million
summary: Magnera reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $857 million with adjusted EBITDA of $99 million, a 9% increase and 70 basis point margin improvement year-over-year. The company reaffirmed free cash flow guidance of $90-$110 million but moved adjusted EBITDA to the lower end of prior guidance due to persistent inflation and macroeconomic uncertainty. Americas EBITDA rose 16% to $71 million, while Rest of World declined slightly. New product Universa launched and Project CORE synergies are at full run rate.

negative_highlights: Non-GAAP EPS fell to $0.17 from $0.30 YoY due to one-time items
Gross margin at 26.3%, impacted by ~160 bps from Comtrafo purchase accounting and unfavorable mix
Q2 revenue guidance of >$85M implies sequential decline due to accelerated deliveries into Q1
positive_highlights: Q1 revenue of $94.1M, up 30% YoY, surpassing expectations
Orders over $130M, including record $25M utility mining order; backlog above $300M
Generated $16M operating cash flow; cash at $153.1M
summary: AMSC reported Q1 FY2026 revenue of $94.1 million, up 30% year-over-year, with Grid up 27% and Wind up 45%. GAAP net income was $9.5 million ($0.21 per share), while non-GAAP net income was $7.6 million ($0.17 per share), down from $0.30 a year ago due to purchase accounting and tax timing. Orders reached over $130 million, including a record $25 million mining utility order, and 12-month backlog exceeded $300 million. Q2 guidance calls for revenue above $85 million and non-GAAP EPS above $0.17, with fiscal 2026 expected to be better than fiscal 2025.

negative_highlights: Natural gas Waha prices averaged negative $3.14/Mcf, forcing curtailments
Inflationary pressures from rising diesel costs partially offset by efficiency gains
Management expressed uncertainty about hitting $675M CapEx target if oil prices stay high, affecting fuel costs
positive_highlights: Record FCF of $751M, up ~50% QoQ, and record FCF/share of $0.88
Full-year oil production guidance raised to 199 MBbl/d, 10% above 2025, with CapEx down ~1%
Year-to-date added ~55,000 net acres for ~$1.05B at attractive valuations
summary: Permian Resources reported record Q2 free cash flow of $751 million, up nearly 50% quarter-over-quarter, and record FCF per share of $0.88. Oil production increased 3% sequentially to about 198,000 bbl/day, helped by a 50% increase in workover rigs and higher working interest (82% vs original 75% expectations). Full-year oil production guidance was raised to 199,000 bbl/day (10% above 2025), while CapEx midpoint is $1.95 billion, about 1% lower than last year. Management highlighted aggressive year-to-date acquisitions of about 55,000 net acres for ~$1.05 billion, with leverage at 0.5x.

negative_highlights: CRS segment-adjusted EBITDA margin declined 270 bps to 26.3%
Military and helicopter revenue declined 3% due to input delays
Free cash flow guidance maintained despite strong Q2 due to supply chain fluidity
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 100 bps to a record 14.4%
LEAP and CFM56 DFW programs reached profitability in the quarter
Raising full-year 2026 guidance for revenue, adjusted EBITDA, and adjusted EPS
summary: StandardAero's Q2 2026 showed revenue up 4.6% to $1.6B, adjusted EBITDA up 12.3% to $230M with record 14.4% margin, and adjusted EPS up 24% to $0.40. Both LEAP and CFM56 DFW programs reached profitability, and the company raised full-year guidance for revenue, adjusted EBITDA, and adjusted EPS. CRS segment margin declined 270bps on timing issues but is expected to recover in H2. A new $180M license expansion is expected to add ~$25M annual EBITDA over the next few years.

negative_highlights: Salt Adjusted EBITDA down 15% due to higher production costs and lower highway volumes
Production costs at Goderich higher than planned, with no efficiency gains yet
Tariff exposure on Canadian salt a fluid risk despite mitigation efforts
positive_highlights: Plant Nutrition Adjusted EBITDA up 32% to $15 million, full-year guidance raised to $49-$57 million
Highway de-icing pricing up 8%, C&I pricing up 6%, with substantial double-digit bid season price gains
summary: Compass Minerals reported Q3 FY2026 total Adjusted EBITDA of $39.9 million, slightly down from $41 million a year ago, with a net loss of $5.7 million improved from a $17 million loss. Salt revenue rose 5% to $173.9 million on 9% pricing gains, but salt Adjusted EBITDA fell 15% due to higher costs and lower volumes. Plant Nutrition Adjusted EBITDA jumped 32% to $15 million, prompting a full-year segment guidance raise to $49-$57 million. Management raised consolidated EBITDA guidance midpoint to $230 million (range $218-$242 million) but narrowed salt guidance, citing cost pressures and operational delays; bid season pricing is strong with double-digit increases, but tariffs remain a risk.

negative_highlights: Husky adjusted net sales fell ~9% YoY to $339.6 million due to macro uncertainty, elevated resin prices, shipping disruptions from the Middle East conflict, and tariff impacts.
Pro forma adjusted EBITDA margins contracted by approximately 230 bps on a consolidated basis as Husky's weakness offset CompoSecure's strength.
Management explicitly stated that full-year guidance does not assume material improvements in macro conditions or resin prices beyond marginal stabilization.
positive_highlights: CompoSecure delivered record sales of $133.6 million, up ~12% YoY, with adjusted EBITDA margins expanding 70 bps to 41.3% driven by ROS deployment and new program wins like Samsung and American Express.
Husky expanded margin sequentially by approximately 590 basis points through better labor/fixed cost absorption despite lower volume.
Pipeline growth at Husky accelerated with double-digit increases in systems and aftermarket tooling, indicating demand is being deferred rather than canceled.
summary: GPGI reported Q2 FY26 pro forma adjusted net sales of $473.2 million (down ~4% YoY) and pro forma adjusted EBITDA of $113.9 million (down ~13% YoY), driven by a strong beat at CompoSecure but significant weakness at Husky due to macro headwinds, volatile resin prices, shipping disruptions, and tariffs. Management reiterated full-year guidance for revenue ($1.95B-$2.1B) and adjusted EBITDA margins (27%-29%), noting that the maintained ranges do not assume material further improvement in market conditions despite some stabilization.

negative_highlights: Q4 net churn rose 37 bps YoY to 2.2%, with 17 bps from one-time factors
Q4 free cash flow fell 21% YoY to $89M due to working capital timing
FY2027 churn expected roughly flat YoY
positive_highlights: Revenue of $608M beat the high end of implied guidance by $6M
Adjusted EBITDA ex-items of $166M was $12M above the high end of guidance
Exceeded $100M cost savings goal; first full year of positive net income and operating income
summary: Peloton delivered Q4 FY2026 revenue of $608M, slightly above guidance, with gross margin up 260bps to 56.7%. Adjusted EBITDA was $142M (or $166M excluding one-time legal contingencies), above guidance, and FY2026 marked the first full year of positive net income ($63M) and operating income ($161M). Management projects record gross margin, EBITDA, and net income in FY2027, while expecting churn to be roughly flat year-over-year. The company is also executing a balance-sheet refinancing and plans new consumer product launches in fall 2027.

negative_highlights: Adjusted OIBDA decreased year-over-year by approximately 10% to $96 million, primarily due to the video business shutdown and higher distribution costs.
Consumer revenue declined 2%, with organic broadband subscriber count dropping by 500 lines before acquisition offset.
Business gross margin contracted to 75.5% as a result of roughly $12 million in increased distribution costs related to Quintillion network restoration.
positive_highlights: Consumer gross margin expanded to 71.8% driven by declines in video programming costs following business exit.
Wireless subscriber base grew by 2,100 lines during the quarter despite organic broadband churn.
GCI net leverage stands at 2.1x with $447 million of undrawn capacity on its credit facility.
summary: Liberty Capital reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $261 million (flat YoY) and Adjusted OIBDA of $96 million (down 11% YoY). The quarter was impacted by the shutdown of the video business, a small organic decline in consumer broadband subscribers offset by an acquisition, and increased distribution costs from restoring service on the Quintillion network. Management announced plans to initiate a quarterly dividend starting December with an initial aggregate amount of $60 million per year.

negative_highlights: GAAP net income dropped sharply to $0.07 per share due to a one-time charge of approximately $0.34 per share.
Gross originations declined significantly from Q1 levels as the company managed leverage and waited for deal closings in July.
Non-accruals increased slightly, representing 2.7% of cost basis or 1.5% of fair value at quarter end.
positive_highlights: Net investment income fully covered the declared third quarter distribution of $0.38 per share ($0.36 regular + $0.02 supplemental).
Weighted average internal risk rating remained stable at 4.3, consistent with the prior quarter.
Interest coverage ratio improved to 2.5x from 2.3x in Q1 despite adding four new non-accrual names.
summary: NCDL reported Q2 FY26 net investment income of $0.41 per share and GAAP EPS of $0.07, which was significantly below the prior quarter's $0.18 due to realized/unrealized losses totaling $0.34 per share driven by amendments on two underperforming investments. Net asset value declined 1.8% quarter-over-quarter from $17.50 to $17.19, while gross originations fell materially to approximately $12 million compared to $83 million in Q1 due to leverage management and deal timing. Management maintained a defensive posture with non-accruals rising slightly to 1.5% of fair value but emphasized strong credit metrics including an interest coverage ratio of 2.5x.

negative_highlights: Total consolidated revenue declined 1.2% YoY due to a 9.4% drop in the Consumer segment.
Q3 guidance anticipates combined gross margin headwinds of approximately 200 bps driven by elevated memory costs and supply constraints.
APAC Enterprise growth was down 16% YoY as management addresses ongoing go-to-market transformation challenges.
positive_highlights: Enterprise revenue grew 7.7% YoY to $89M driven by double-digit growth in Pro AV Managed Switches.
Non-GAAP gross margin hit an all-time high of 54.1%, up 660 bps YoY, with contribution margin at its highest level since Q1 2019 (25.9%).
Consumer ARR grew 15% YoY to $41.6M and direct-to-consumer channel revenue increased over 20%.
summary: NETGEAR reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $168.6 million (down 1.2% YoY) and non-GAAP EPS of $0.16, beating the high end of guidance due to strong Enterprise growth offsetting Consumer declines. Management raised full-year outlooks for both revenue and operating margin based on this performance but issued a cautious Q3 guide expecting combined gross margins to face approximately 200 bps headwinds from memory costs, with non-GAAP operating margins projected between -3% and 0%. The company repurchased $12.9 million in shares during the quarter.

negative_highlights: Gross margin declined 150 basis points due to revenue mix shift toward equipment-heavy commercial projects
Management conservatively guided, noting Q2 included some revenue acceleration that will impact second-half performance
Interest expense was lower, but operating cash flow not fully detailed in this excerpt
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA up 51% to a record $33 million, with a record 28.2% margin on net revenue
Contract revenue up 33% to $231 million; organic net revenue growth was 18% year-over-year
Full-year financial targets raised; strong contract wins including $110 million LADWP solar streetlight expansion
summary: Willdan reported a strong Q2 FY2026 with contract revenue up 33% year-over-year to $231 million, net revenue up 23% to $117 million, and record adjusted EBITDA of $33 million, a 51% increase. Adjusted EPS rose 38% to $2.07, and GAAP EPS increased 53% to $1.58. Management raised full-year financial targets, citing robust demand, especially from commercial data center projects, and margin expansion driven by mix and AI-enabled productivity. They guided to a 25% adjusted EBITDA margin for 2026, up from 21.8% in 2025, though noted Q2's 28.2% margin was aided by revenue acceleration and may not persist.

negative_highlights: Core Celsius brand net sales declined approximately 12% YoY due to SKU rationalization and shipment timing gaps.
Q3 outlook for Celsius is expected to be similar to Q2 before exiting the year into growth, indicating continued pressure.
Alani Nu faces a tougher comp in Q4 compared to Q3 as it rolls over inventory builds from last year.
positive_highlights: Alani Nu net sales grew approximately 21% YoY with retail and track channel growth of ~56%.
Gross margins remained consistent at ~48%, offsetting commodity inflation through integration efficiencies.
Completed Rockstar Energy integration on the nine-month timeline, stabilizing that portfolio segment.
summary: Celsius Holdings reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $818 million (up ~11% YoY), driven by Alani Nu's strong growth but offset by a decline in the core Celsius brand due to SKU rationalization and shipment timing. Gross margins remained flat at approximately 48%, while SG&A was held steady despite lower volume, resulting in adjusted EBITDA of $184 million (down from prior year). Management reaffirmed that Q3 results will mirror Q2 for the Celsius brand before a recovery is expected to begin in late 2026/early 2027.

negative_highlights: One-time non-cash charge of ~$31 million related to convertible note remeasurement
SG&A guidance increased by an additional $5 million to ~$50 million increase for the year
Gvoke's weak start to the year, though it rebounded sequentially
positive_highlights: Total revenue $92.1 million, up 29% YoY; net product revenue up 34%
RECORLEV up 81% YoY to $56.8 million with records in referrals, new starts, and prescribers
Full retirement of convertible notes eliminates ~$3 million annual interest and simplifies capital structure
summary: Xeris reported record Q2 2026 total revenue of $92.1 million, up 29% year-over-year, and net product revenue of $91 million, up 34%. RECORLEV grew 81% to $56.8 million, Gvoke rebounded sequentially to $22.5 million, and KEVEYIS delivered $11.7 million. Adjusted EBITDA rose over 50% to $19.3 million. The company raised the bottom end of full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $385-390 million, reflecting 33% growth at the midpoint. It also fully retired its convertible notes with a one-time non-cash charge of $31 million, and advanced its XP-8121 pipeline toward a planned phase III start by year-end.

negative_highlights: Phase III readout timing for petosemtamab colorectal cancer trials delayed to Q1 FY27 from earlier expectations.
Interim analysis for EPKINLY frontline DLBCL study expected in Q4, later than analyst models anticipated.
positive_highlights: EPKINLY sales grew 48% YoY to DKK 312 million with accelerated growth and new site activations in the US community setting.
Positive top-line results from Phase III EPCORE DLBCL-2 trial showing statistically significant improvement in progression-free survival for EPKINLY plus lenalidomide/rituximab.
European approval of EPKINLY plus R-squared for second-line follicular lymphoma, making it the first and only bispecific-based therapy approved in Europe for this indication.
summary: Genmab reported strong first-half FY26 results with total revenue growing 25% YoY to DKK 396 million for its proprietary portfolio (EPKINLY and TIVDAK), driven by a 48% increase in EPKINLY sales. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance, now expecting revenue of DKK 4.3-4.5 billion (+19% YoY) and operating profit of DKK 1.1-1.4 billion, reflecting the strength of their late-stage pipeline progress including positive Phase III interim data for EPKINLY in DLBCL.

negative_highlights: Life Sciences revenue fell 31.3% YoY due to liquidity constraints impacting R2 unit sales
Spectrum segment revenue decreased by $54 million (from implied prior period) and Adjusted EBITDA dropped ~$600k-$400k due to network terminations
Cash position declined from $108.2M at year-end 2025 to $87.8M as of June 30, 2026
positive_highlights: Infrastructure achieved a record quarter with Adjusted EBITDA of $48.7M and gross margin expansion of ~60 bps YoY
Broadcasting completed refinancing to retire debt, repurchase equity interests, and fund transaction costs ahead of CONX acquisition
DBMG adjusted backlog increased to $2.7 billion with strong demand visibility into 2027-2028
summary: INNOVATE reported Q2 FY2026 consolidated revenue of $421.6 million (up 74.2% YoY) and Adjusted EBITDA of $46.3 million (up from $15.7m), driven primarily by a record Infrastructure segment ($414M). However, Life Sciences revenue declined 31.3% to $2.2 million due to liquidity constraints at R2, while the Spectrum segment saw slight declines following network terminations.

negative_highlights: Sales down 21% year-over-year to $152.5 million
Oil and gas end market remains soft with no sign of significant improvement
Capacity ramp-up costs at Wisconsin are expected to persist, pressuring gross margin
positive_highlights: Q2 sales of $152.5 million up 18.6% sequentially, exceeding prior expectation of roughly flat revenue
Gross margin improved 420 basis points sequentially to 27.1% from 22.9%
Operating cash flow of $56.6 million enabled debt reduction of ~$30.8 million
summary: In Q2 FY2026, Power Solutions International reported net sales of $152.5 million, up 18.6% sequentially from Q1, exceeding expectations, but down 21% year-over-year due to softer oil and gas demand and shipment timing. Gross margin improved sequentially by 420 basis points to 27.1%, driven by operational improvements at Wisconsin, though year-over-year it declined from 28.2%. Operating cash flow was strong at $56.6 million, enabling $30.8 million debt reduction. Management expects H2 2026 sales to exceed H1, roughly in line with H2 2025, but provided no formal guidance due to order timing variability and continued oil and gas softness.

negative_highlights: Two Florida managed-only contracts valued at $100 million combined annual revenue were delayed until July 1, 2027 due to unresolved budgetary issues.
No revenues were recognized from the new skip tracing contract in Q2 due to a lapse in ICE appropriations funding during the government shutdown.
positive_highlights: Revenue increased 15% YoY and net income surged 63% YoY driven by new contracts entered in 2025 totaling up to $520 million annually.
ISAP V contract revenue remained resilient despite reduced pricing due to a technology shift toward higher-priced ankle monitors, with participant counts rising from ~17k to ~54k on GPS devices.
Management raised full-year net income guidance range and adjusted EBITDA guidance following strong first-half performance.
summary: GEO reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $732 million (up 15% YoY) and net income of $47.5 million (up 63% YoY), driven by new ICE contracts and a technology mix shift in the ISAP program. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance for GAAP net income to $168-$175 million on revenues of $2.95-$3.05 billion, excluding earnings from two Florida facilities delayed until July 1, 2027 due to budgetary issues.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA declined to $18 million from $27 million year-over-year
Adjusted net loss widened to $17.7 million from $10.8 million
Operating and G&A expenses up 3.8% due to higher payroll and fuel costs
positive_highlights: May and June volumes exceeded prior year levels due to counter-seasonal customer growth
RNG credit prices up: California LCFS +31% YoY, D3 RIN +8% YoY
New RNG facilities to add ~300,000 MMBtus annually, reaching full operational platform
summary: Suburban Propane reported an adjusted net loss of $17.7 million ($0.27 per unit) for Q3 FY2026, wider than the prior year's loss of $10.8 million ($0.17). Adjusted EBITDA fell to $18 million from $27 million. Retail propane volumes declined 1.8% to 70.6 million gallons, mainly due to warm April weather, partially offset by customer base growth. The company highlighted RNG project progress, with new facilities expected to boost annual injection to 750,000-800,000 MMBtus for FY2027, and noted improving environmental credit prices.

negative_highlights: Wheels volume declined 8% YoY (though up sequentially), with aluminum pass-through diluting margins by ~360 bps
Engineered Structures revenue fell 13% due to the divestiture of the Savannah Disc facility
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 24% YoY with organic growth of 21%, excluding M&A impacts
EBITDA margin expanded 340 bps to 32.1%; EBITDA outpaced revenue by 59%
Free cash flow in Q2 was $479 million, enabling a dividend increase and share repurchases
summary: Howmet reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $3.4 billion (up 24% YoY) and adjusted EPS of $1.33 (up 46%), both beating the high end of guidance with EBITDA margin expanding to 32.1%. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance for revenue, EBITDA, and EPS across the board while maintaining a strong balance sheet following an $840 million free cash flow generation in H1.

negative_highlights: Gross-to-Net (GTN) for BRINSUPRI came in at the lower end of the previous guidance range due to better-than-expected contracting dynamics.
Combined R&D and SG&A expenses increased by 38% year-over-year as investments scale up.
positive_highlights: BRINSUPRI revenue reached $309.2M in Q2 with new patient starts accelerating to approximately 7,000 per quarter (vs prior expectation of 6,300).
Management raised peak sales estimates for BRINSUPRI from >$5B to >$7B and TPIP from >$2B to >$6B.
TPIP open-label extension data showed patients catching up on efficacy metrics after switching from placebo, with 80% achieving functional Class 1 or 2.
summary: Insmed reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $425.5 million ($309.2M from BRINSUPRI and $116.3M from ARIKAYCE), representing strong sequential growth driven by organic new patient starts exceeding expectations for the blockbuster launch. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance for BRINSUPRI to a range of $1.25 billion-$1.4 billion (from >$1B) and increased peak sales estimates significantly, projecting combined lead asset peaks over $14 billion versus previous projections of ~$8 billion.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined sequentially from Q1 primarily due to lower natural gas prices and reduced trading volatility consistent with normal seasonal patterns.
RNG upstream business saw results close to breakeven EBITDA in the quarter, requiring continued ramp-up for profitability.
Uncertainty surrounding final 2027 emission standards led to a large pre-note of legacy diesel trucks by fleets.
positive_highlights: RNG fuel volumes increased 3% YoY to 63.2 million gallons, with upstream dairy projects producing 2.1 million gallons in Q2.
Fuel and customer mix variations modestly reduced margins during the quarter, which is normal seasonal behavior factored into outlooks.
Completed two additional stations including a critical node in British Columbia to complete the Western Canadian natural gas fueling network.
summary: Clean Energy reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $106 million and adjusted EBITDA of $16 million, which management described as in-line with expectations but missing the upper end of its annual guidance range. The company maintained full-year financial outlooks assuming improved performance in H2 2026, though it noted that RNG upstream results were close to breakeven despite sequential improvement over Q1. Management highlighted uncertainty regarding the timing and value of the Section 45Z production tax credit rules expected later this year.

negative_highlights: Net income fell to $0.29 per diluted share from $0.54 in Q2 2025
Book value per diluted share declined 1.9% sequentially to $18.60 on an unrealized loss in the stock loan portfolio
Q3 EAD guidance midpoint of $0.43 is below the $0.46 just reported and below the $0.50 dividend, extending the multi-quarter gap between EAD and the distribution
positive_highlights: Cash available for distribution rose to $0.58 per diluted share from $0.46 a year earlier, covering the $0.50 dividend 1.16x
Earnings available for distribution of $0.46 per diluted share exceeded the April guidance, per management
Blended residential lease trade-outs improved from negative 1.7% in April to positive 30 bps in July, the first positive print since early 2025
summary: NREF reported Q2 2026 net income of $0.29 per diluted share versus $0.54 a year earlier, while earnings available for distribution rose to $0.46 from $0.43 and cash available for distribution rose to $0.58 from $0.46; the $0.50 dividend was 1.16x covered by CAD. Q3 guidance was set at EAD of $0.43 per share (range $0.38-$0.48) and CAD of $0.55 per share (range $0.50-$0.60), and management stated earnings came in ahead of the April guidance. The key balance-sheet change was a new $375 million drawable term loan facility with Mizuho that repaid the $180 million 5.75% senior unsecured notes at their May 1 maturity, with a total return swap reducing net interest cost to SOFR plus 245; book value per share fell 1.9% sequentially to $18.60 on a small unrealized stock loan loss. Portfolio remained $1.1 billion across 85 investments, 39.4% life sciences and 37.6% multifamily, with 63.4% loan-to-value and 1.39x weighted average DSCR.

negative_highlights: Midstream constraints in April-May reduced oil production by ~2,000 bbl/d
Q2 free cash flow fell to $6 million due to 153% CapEx increase
Turn-in-lines missed guidance due to third-party infrastructure delays
positive_highlights: Raised full-year oil production guidance to ~30% year-over-year growth
Drilling costs per lateral foot down 7.5% in Texas and 32% in New Mexico
Silverback production approximately double note-side case projection
summary: Riley Exploration Permian reported Q2 FY2026 with oil production near the high end of guidance, 5% sequential growth, and a June exit rate of 24.4 thousand barrels per day. The company raised full-year oil production guidance to ~30% year-over-year growth, with Q3 expected to be up >20% sequentially. Midstream constraints in April-May reduced oil production by ~2,000 barrels per day, but new Targa pipeline is expected in early Q4 2026. Full-year CapEx guidance was increased by 12% at the midpoint, and free cash flow declined to $6 million in Q2 due to higher capital spend.

negative_highlights: Adjusted operating margin was impacted by a 60-basis point headwind from Argentina anticipation and lower hardware sales compared to the prior year.
Financial Solutions organic revenue declined 10%, driven primarily by higher non-recurring revenue in the comparable period last year rather than volume deterioration.
Full-year guidance for adjusted operating margin was lowered due to incremental technology infrastructure investments exceeding $100 million and slower execution of growth initiatives.
positive_highlights: Free cash flow generation exceeded $1 billion for the quarter with an FCF conversion rate of 112%.
Clover GPV grew at 9% in the quarter, while Clover revenues increased by 13% adjusted for anticipation and non-recurring revenue.
Recurring revenue represented approximately 84-85% of total adjusted revenue with underlying growth remaining stable.
summary: Fiserv reported Q2 FY26 adjusted revenue of $4.96 billion, a decrease of 4% YoY and 5% organically, with EPS of $1.84. Management updated full-year guidance to organic revenue growth of -1% to flat (down from prior expectations) due to Argentina macro headwinds, slower client ramps, hardware attrition, and divestitures. Adjusted operating margin was lowered to a range of 31%-31.5%, reflecting incremental technology investments and the aforementioned impacts.

negative_highlights: Revenue flat at $56.4M, below prior-year $56.8M
Net loss widened to $7.3M from $2.9M
Channel inventory remained below historical norms through much of Q2
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA improved to $1.3M from -$3.0M
Gross margin up 660 bps to 38.8% (with tariff refunds)
Early Q3 weekly year-over-year note-through growth since GTA VI pre-orders
summary: Turtle Beach reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $56.4 million, essentially flat year-over-year, with gross margin expanding to 38.8% including tariff refunds (excluding one-time items, about 31.2%). Adjusted EBITDA improved to $1.3 million from -$3.0 million, but net loss widened to $7.3 million due to increased marketing and higher interest. Management reaffirmed full-year guidance of $335-$355 million revenue and $44-$48 million adjusted EBITDA, citing strong second-half catalysts like GTA VI and Call of Duty. They highlighted early Q3 weekly year-over-year watch-through growth and repurchased $25 million of stock in the quarter.

negative_highlights: Total loan growth slowed to +2.3% YoY, significantly below the prior ~7% guidance and industry average.
Management explicitly revised full-year nominal loan growth forecast down from around 7% to around 6% due to subdued GDP activity in H1.
Cost of risk increased quarter-over-quarter as management established an additional CLP 50 billion in provisions reflecting a cautious stance on macro uncertainty.
positive_highlights: Operating revenues surged 20.9% year-over-year to CLP 922 billion supported by a 5.8% net interest margin expansion from higher inflation.
Fee income grew 10.7% YoY, with transactional services rising 20.4%, driven by increased card activity and new acquiring partnerships (Banchile Pagos).
The bank maintained its leading market share in local currency demand deposits at 19.7% among private banks.
summary: Banco de Chile reported Q2 FY26 operating revenues of CLP 922 billion (up 20.9% YoY) and net income of CLP 391 billion driven by higher inflation and fee growth, though loan growth was muted at +2.3% due to a one-time accounting migration effect masking underlying pro forma growth of +2.9%. Management revised its full-year nominal loan growth guidance down from ~7% to ~6% citing weaker-than-expected macroeconomic performance in the first half, while maintaining NIM expectations around 4.6% and raising cost-of-risk provisions by CLP 50 billion.

negative_highlights: No change in cash runway guidance; no updates on enrollment percentages
FDA meeting for non-IPF ILD program still not granted; timeline subject to approval
RCC market strategy remains narrow until phase II dose data available
positive_highlights: Cash runway extends into 2030, fully funding development programs
Competitive failure in RCC leaves Trevi essentially alone in all three cough indications
ATS presentations and JAMA highlight reinforce drug's efficacy profile
summary: Trevi's Q2 2026 call highlights continued pipeline execution: OCEAN-1 phase III and LAKE-2b phase IIb trials initiated, with OCEAN-2 expected in Q3. Cash of ~$319M extends runway into 2030, funding IPF and non-IPF ILD programs. The highly anticipated FDA meeting for non-IPF ILD is a near-term catalyst, and the competitive RCC program termination is viewed positively, reinforcing Trevi's potential first-in-class position. Guidance unchanged.

negative_highlights: Consolidated revenue declined 4.6% to $100.4 million; kilowatt hours sold fell 17% and therms sold fell 23% as the customer base contracted
Meter counts fell to 345,000 RCEs and 363,000 meters from 413,000 and 419,000 a year earlier, and gross new customers slipped to 65,000 from 70,000
SG&A rose 28% to $27.2 million on a shift toward higher-cost acquisition channels, and the $11.4 million net income was helped by an unspecified 'other income' line management said is hard to predict
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA rose $4.5 million to $7.5 million and net income attributable to common stockholders reached $11.4 million, or $0.42 per diluted share, versus $0.09 a year earlier
GREW swung to positive Adjusted EBITDA of $300,000 from a $97,000 loss, with gross profit up 55% to $3.3 million on Diversegy and Genie Solar contributions
summary: Consolidated revenue fell 4.6% YoY to $100.4 million as GRE revenue dropped 4.9% to $94.1 million on the expiration of low-margin aggregation deals, with RCEs down to 345,000 from 413,000. Profitability sharply improved: gross profit rose 43.4% to $33.7 million (33.5% margin), Adjusted EBITDA rose $4.5 million to $7.5 million, and net income was $11.4 million or $0.42 per diluted share versus $0.09 a year earlier. GREW turned EBITDA-positive at $300,000 on flat $6.3 million revenue. Management reaffirmed its prior full-year guidance without a specific raise, and returning cash continued with a $2 million dividend and $659,000 of buybacks.

negative_highlights: Revenue of $475.5 million remained modestly below prior-year levels
Adjusted EBITDA guidance upper end cut by $5 million to $172.5 million
Rental fleet utilization at ~35% versus a high-30s to ~40% target, with further construction fleet paring planned
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA rose $20.5 million sequentially to $48.6 million with EBITDA margin expanding 340 bps from Q1 to 10.2%
Material handling adjusted EBITDA up ~13% YoY to $19 million on lower revenue; company-wide equipment gross margin improved to 15.3%
Ecoverse revenue grew to $22.8 million from $20.9 million with adjusted EBITDA up to $2.8 million from $1.1 million as tariff pressure subsided
summary: Alta reported Q2 2026 revenue of $475.5 million (modestly below prior year) and adjusted EBITDA of $48.6 million, with gross margin up ~70 bps YoY to 26.1% and EBITDA margin at 10.2%. Sequentially, revenue rose ~$65 million and adjusted EBITDA rose ~$20.5 million from $28.1 million in Q1, with equipment gross margins improving to 15.3%. Guidance narrowed from $167.5M-$177.5M to a $5M lower top end while the low end is reaffirmed, and free cash flow before rent to watch guidance of $100M-$110M was maintained. Management cited timing of material handling deliveries rather than demand change for the trim, with backlog at ~$143 million, the highest since 2023.

negative_highlights: Transportation demand remains soft reflecting lower vehicle production rates, with no expectation of improvement in Q3 or the second half.
Healthcare business is experiencing a rebalancing of inventory levels by customers which weighed on first-half results despite intact underlying trends.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EPS beat by $0.09 driven by better-than-expected volume growth (+1% vs projected negative) and pricing execution (3/4 of organic growth).
Asia segment delivered double-digit organic sales growth, with the region growing sequentially +20%. Both business segments showed strong momentum in Asia.
Adjusted EBITDA margins hit a record 18.3%, expanding 110 bps year-over-year due to operating leverage and productivity initiatives.
summary: Avient reported Q2 FY26 adjusted EPS of $0.96, beating expectations by $0.09 driven by volume growth and pricing actions that pushed organic sales up 4.3%. Adjusted EBITDA margins expanded to a record 18.3%, an increase of 110 bps year-over-year. Management raised full-year guidance for adjusted EBITDA, EPS, and free cash flow while updating capital expenditure expectations downward.

negative_highlights: Middle East conflict still causing some disruption and slower rig reactivations in Saudi
International guidance reflects near-term conflict-related activity changes
Visibility limited due to volatile commodity prices
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA of $236 million, above guidance midpoint
Direct margin per day up over $1,000 sequentially to $18,700
Raised Q4 and full-year guidance for North America Solutions
summary: HP delivered strong Q3 FY2026 results with adjusted EBITDA of $236 million, beating guidance midpoint, and direct margins exceeding ranges across all segments, including North America Solutions at the high end with $241 million. Management raised Q4 and full-year guidance for North America Solutions and remains committed to $45 million+ quarterly direct margins in International Solutions, with strong growth in Argentina. Geothermal and international activities expanded, including three new rig agreements and a four-year offshore contract renewal, while the Middle East conflict still creates some disruption. The company highlighted ongoing tightness in super-spec supply and expects a multi-year upstream growth cycle leading into 2027.

negative_highlights: Q3 revenue guidance of $43-44 million implies a sequential decline from Q2's $51.8 million
Q3 adjusted EBITDA guidance of only $1-2 million is well below Q2's $9.1 million, reflecting a seasonally lower revenue quarter
Severance payments of about $14-15 million weighed on first-half cash flow, and the company stopped providing separate academic services and Chegg Skills revenue guidance
positive_highlights: Q2 revenue of $51.8 million exceeded internal expectations, with adjusted EBITDA of $9.1 million (17% margin)
Non-GAAP operating expenses fell to $32.3 million, nearly half of Q2 last year's level
First-half free cash flow of $9.5 million was generated despite $14.4 million in severance payments, and the company expects to fully repay convertible debt in Q3
summary: Q2 FY2026 revenue was $51.8 million, above the company's expectations, with non-GAAP operating expenses of $32.3 million (roughly half of last year's Q2), adjusted EBITDA of $9.1 million (17% margin), and free cash flow of $6.4 million. Q3 guidance calls for total revenue of $43-44 million, gross margin of 48-49%, and adjusted EBITDA of $1-2 million, a step down from Q2 with Q3 described as a seasonally slower quarter; no prior guidance is stated for comparison. Management said severance payments of roughly $14-15 million are almost entirely behind them and expects free cash flow positive in the back half of 2026. The call's dominant theme was a strategic pivot toward employability, with a soft launch of a new Chegg job-search and coaching product in Q3 and expansion throughout 2027.

negative_highlights: G&A expense up ~$3 million YoY
DD&A expense increased to $962 per GEO from $487
Antamina NPI volatility noted as source of uncertainty in copper guidance
positive_highlights: Record operating cash flow of $335 million, up 119%
Adjusted EBITDA margin remained high at 83%
Deal pipeline described as 'as busy as ever'
summary: Revenue surged 115% YoY to $451 million with record operating cash flow of $335 million, up 119%. Adjusted EPS rose 41% to $2.56. Guidance for gold and silver is tracking well; copper and other metals trending around or above top end. Management noted strong portfolio diversification and progress simplifying Sandstorm assets.

negative_highlights: Direct response and SME business Ex-TAC gross profit declined 30% year-over-year to $34 million.
Premium publisher page views declined by 15%-25% due to AI search shifts and platform policy updates.
Adjusted EBITDA missed guidance due to discretionary expense spikes in T&E, marketing, and cloud migration costs.
positive_highlights: CTV revenue grew 67% year-over-year to approximately $40 million, accounting for 13% of Q2 revenue.
Enterprise advertiser spend stabilized and turned positive year-over-year in May and June.
Teads EngageOS launched to unify content and ad inventory, aiming to improve yield on end-of-article placements.
summary: Revenue declined 17% year-over-year to approximately $285 million, while Ex-TAC gross profit fell 14% to $123 million. Adjusted EBITDA of $7 million missed the expected range due to timing and cutoff expenses, FX headwinds, and elevated bad debts. Management suspended full-year 2026 guidance citing volatility in the direct response business but expects a return to growth in the enterprise segment by H2.

negative_highlights: RNG commodity revenue fell 63.7% due to the expiration of fixed-price contracts.
Average natural gas commodity pricing was 15.7% lower than the prior year quarter.
Production at Galveston and Atascocita facilities decreased due to host wellfield operational changes and maintenance timing.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA surged 144.5% to $12.3 million compared to $5.0 million in the prior year quarter.
RIN sales volume increased 29.1% to 14.3 million units, with average pricing up 1.2% to $2.45.
Operating loss decreased by 96.8% to just $75,000 as RNG operating income rose to $9.6 million.
summary: Total revenues increased 19.7% to $54.0 million in Q2 FY2026, driven by a 29.1% rise in RIN sales revenue ($8.4M) which offset a 63.7% decline in RNG commodity revenue due to expired fixed-price contracts. Operating loss narrowed significantly to $75,000 from a $2.4 million loss in the prior year period as RNG operating income grew 4.5%. Management reaffirmed full-year 2026 guidance for RNG production (5.8-6.0 million MMBtu) and revenue ($175-190 million), explicitly including GreenWave Energy Partners distributed RIN revenues.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to $52.6M GAAP (vs $39.7M) and $16M non-GAAP (vs $13.3M)
Operating expenses increased to $30.3M from $20.4M year-over-year
Prospective government funding is not yet a definitive agreement and subject to approvals
positive_highlights: Revenue grew over 180% year-over-year to $5.1M, driven by Novera QPU sales
Gross margin expanded to 43% from 31% year-over-year
Signed LOI for up to $100M in CHIPS Act funding and expanded HPE/PSC collaboration
summary: Rigetti reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $5.1M, up from $1.8M a year earlier, driven by on-premises Novera QPU sales. Gross margin improved to 43% from 31%, while GAAP net loss widened to $52.6M due to non-cash warrant and earn-out fair value adjustments; non-GAAP net loss was $16M or $0.05 per diluted share. The company highlighted technical progress, a $100M CHIPS Act letter of intent, and expanded HPE/Pittsburgh Supercomputing Center collaboration, with guidance expectations for the remainder of the year referenced but not fully quantified in the transcript excerpt.

negative_highlights: Community operating expenses increased 10% in the quarter due to higher payroll, taxes, insurance, and water/sewer costs.
Total occupancy remains at 89%, which may limit near-term rental growth.
Full-year guidance was maintained, not raised, despite strong quarterly results.
positive_highlights: Normalized FFO per share of $0.25, up 9% YoY and in line with prior year's trend.
Same-property NOI grew 9% with site rent increases of 5% and occupancy up 437 units YoY.
Home sales revenue increased 10% to a record $11.5 million for the quarter.
summary: UMH reported Q2 2026 Normalized FFO per share of $0.25, up 9% year-over-year, and net income per diluted share of $0.05, up 67% year-over-year. Same-property NOI grew 9% driven by site rent increases of 5% and higher occupancy. The company maintained its full-year Normalized FFO guidance of $0.98-$1.04 per share. Management expressed strong conviction in growth prospects from factory-built housing policy and their development pipeline.

negative_highlights: Total investment spread narrowed to 97 basis points in Q2, missing the guidance range of 100-120 bps primarily due to weaker private equity returns within Variable Investment Income (VII).

Corporate & Other reported an adjusted loss of $160 million compared to a prior year loss of $142 million, reflecting foregone earnings from strategic reinsurance transactions and market-related employee costs.
Management noted that mortality favorability is expected to normalize over the next few years as claims severity trends shift back toward pre-COVID levels.
positive_highlights: Group Benefits adjusted earnings surged 25% year-over-year driven by a mortality ratio of 79%, significantly better than the target range and reflecting continued favorable trends among working-age populations.
Asia segment delivered robust growth with sales up 17% on a constant currency basis, fueled by strong momentum in Korea and double-digit A&H growth following new product launches.
Latin America achieved record quarterly adjusted earnings of $268 million (up 15%), supported by broad-based volume growth across Brazil, Mexico, and Chile.
summary: MetLife reported adjusted earnings of $1.6 billion ($2.43 per share), representing a 15% year-over-year increase and an EPS beat driven by strong volume growth across all segments and favorable underwriting margins in Group Benefits. The company maintained its full-year expense ratio target at 12.1%, though variable investment income was slightly below the implied run rate due to weaker private equity returns, which management expects to normalize in Q3. Management reiterated confidence in their 'New Frontier' strategy with no changes to guidance or capital deployment priorities.

negative_highlights: ironSource sunset had only $3 million positive impact on Vector growth
Create revenue growth slowed to 7-10% expected in Q3
Stock comp still 14% of revenues, though down 25% YoY
positive_highlights: Q2 strategic revenue up 63% YoY with Vector up 23% QoQ
Adjusted EBITDA grew 77% YoY, margins expanded 800 bps to 29%
Q3 revenue guidance implies 44-47% YoY growth, a material acceleration
summary: Unity reported a record Q2 with strategic revenue up 63% year-over-year to $329 million, driven by Vector's 23% quarter-over-quarter growth. Adjusted EBITDA grew 77% to $160 million with margins at 29%, and free cash flow hit $202 million. The company raised Q3 guidance to 44-47% strategic revenue growth and pulled forward GAAP net income profitability to Q3. Key strategic moves include closing the Supersonic sale, sunsetting the ironSource ad network, and investing in AppsFlyer.

negative_highlights: Medical Solutions segment gross margins contracted sequentially by 230 bps in Q2 due to a higher mix of lower-margin precision medicine products and temporary operational transformation costs.

Precision Medicine business sales declined year-over-year (5% growth mentioned but context implies recovery from prior decline or specific headwinds, though text says 'sales grew by 5%', I will correct based on strict reading: Text actually says 'sales grew by 5%' for Precision Medicine. However, the Life Sciences exposure is expected to be less than 10% and not return to sustained growth in 2026.
Tariff-related costs (Section 232/301) remain a net negative headwind that customers bear partially.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EPS grew 17% to $0.89, driven by a specific $0.06 beat from the Riverpoint transaction in Q3 guidance plus organic base improvement.
Gross margin expanded 100 bps year-over-year to 47%, with full-year outlook raised to approximately 48% due to site closures and acquisition accretion.
Riverpoint Medical closed successfully, doubling recurring medical consumable business exposure to roughly $300 million annualized.
summary: Novanta reported Q2 FY26 revenue growth of 10% (reported) and 9% organic, with adjusted EPS growing 17% to $0.89 on a 47% gross margin that expanded 100 bps year-over-year. The company closed its largest acquisition in history, Riverpoint Medical, which immediately raised the full-year 2026 revenue guidance range to approximately $1,130-$1,140 million (representing >15% reported growth) and adjusted EBITDA guidance to $273-$278 million. Management highlighted strong momentum in new product revenue (>50% QoQ), backlog increases of 11%, and record year-to-date operating cash flow exceeding full-year 2025 levels.

negative_highlights: Primary deal activity stayed subdued during the quarter.
Software exposure remains high at approximately 70% of the portfolio.
Adjusted NII of $0.30 per share is below the base dividend of $0.35 per share.
positive_highlights: Non-accruals remain among the lowest in the industry at 10 basis points at fair value.
Adjusted NII increased, supported by continued deployment and growth in net leverage.
All existing bank partners renewed revolver commitments and added a new lending relationship.
summary: OTF reported Q2 2026 adjusted NII of $0.30 per share, stable NAV of $16.48, and non-accruals at 10 basis points, among the lowest in the industry. Net leverage rose to 0.93x, near the low end of the target range, and the company completed $500 million unsecured bond, $150 million secured facility, and extended its revolver. Management expects to cover the base dividend by mid-next year and continues repurchasing shares, with $195 million still available. The investment environment has improved with wider spreads, and management remains confident in portfolio quality despite slower technology deal activity.

negative_highlights: Q2 demand softened in the second half as global nitrogen channels drew inventories down to very low levels, leading to a buyer's holiday.

Yazoo City complex operations delayed until H1 FY2027 following $53 million in total impairments ($25M Q4 prior + $28M current) and business interruption insurance recoveries of approximately $75 million.
positive_highlights: Operated available ammonia capacity at nearly 98% utilization in H1 despite global disruptions, enabling strong delivery performance to domestic customers.
Low-carbon sales program earned an average premium of more than $20 per ton on approximately 10% of first-half ammonia volumes.
summary: CF Industries reported Q2 FY2026 net earnings of $727 million ($4.73 diluted EPS) and adjusted EBITDA of $1.2 billion for the quarter, with H1 adjusted EBITDA reaching $2.2 billion. Management raised mid-cycle baseline expectations to approximately $2.9 billion in EBITDA and $1.7 billion in free cash flow by 2026, citing structural tightening from rising global capital costs rather than solely geopolitical factors. The company increased its quarterly dividend by 20% to $0.60 per share while maintaining a robust buyback program.

negative_highlights: Tim Hortons Canadian comps flat at +0.1%
Popeyes same-store sales declined 5.2% and company cites soft sales
Beef costs remain at all-time high, delaying franchisee profitability
positive_highlights: Burger King US same-store sales up 8.5%, beating industry by over 9 points
International delivered 5.5% comps and 5.1% net restaurant growth
Company delivered 12.9% Adjusted EPS growth and returned $435 million to shareholders
summary: In Q2 2026, RBI reported 3.8% same-store sales growth, 6.7% organic Adjusted Operating Income growth, and 12.9% Adjusted EPS growth, with Burger King US delivering an exceptional 8.6% same-store sales, beating the industry by over nine points. Tim Hortons was flat, Popeyes declined 5.2%, but International grew 5.5%, and Firehouse grew 0.4%. The company reiterated its 2026 algorithm and expects improving momentum, with Popeyes returning to positive comps in H2 and Burger King's elevation driving sustained outperformance, though beef costs remain a near-term headwind.

negative_highlights: Phoenix RevPAR decreased 5%, driven by declines in both occupancy and rate linked to semiconductor business pullback.
Fixed expenses declined due to favorable insurance renewal but utilities grew 9% year-over-year, creating a headwind against variable cost discipline.
positive_highlights: Comparable hotels RevPAR grew 5.3%, driven by weekday occupancy outpacing weekend improvement (+130 vs +240 basis points respectively).
Adjusted hotel EBITDA margin expanded 120 bps to 38.1% due to disciplined expense management and flow-through of revenue growth.
Group segment grew to 18% of occupancy mix, providing a strong base at attractive rates.
summary: Apple Hospitality REIT reported Q2 FY26 comparable RevPAR growth of 5.3% (ADR +3.5%, occupancy +130 bps) and adjusted hotel EBITDA margin expansion of 120 basis points to 38.1%. Management raised full-year guidance for RevPAR by 225 bps to a midpoint of 3.25% and increased the comparable hotels adjusted hotel EBITDA margin outlook by 75 bps, citing broad-based demand strength beyond World Cup markets.

negative_highlights: Full-year revenue outlook lowered due to Vitalware divestiture removal
Adjusted gross margin expected below 50% for full year as lower-margin services mix increases
Significant near-term cost pressure from platform migrations and data loading
positive_highlights: Revenue exceeded high end of guidance at $70.5M
Adjusted EBITDA hit midpoint/high-end range at $9.9M
Company fully retired ~$160M debt and is now debt-free
summary: Health Catalyst reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $70.5 million and adjusted EBITDA of $9.9 million, both exceeding the high end of guidance driven by a strong quarter before closing its Vitalware divestiture on July 31st. Management updated full-year 2026 guidance to reflect the removal of Vitalware's contribution, projecting total revenue between $246-$249 million and adjusted EBITDA between $18-$18.5 million for the remainder of the year. The company is now debt-free following the repayment of approximately $160 million in credit facility debt using proceeds from the divestiture.

negative_highlights: Second-half outlook expects net sales to decline low single digits and adjusted EBITDA to drop due to the timing shift of club launches into Q2.
Softness persists in wearables, specifically footwear and apparel markets in Japan and Korea.
First half gross margin excluding tariff refunds was down 50 bps YoY due to incremental tariffs on synthetic rubber and tungsten.
positive_highlights: Titleist golf clubs grew 14% YoY in the quarter and 24% for the half, led by a successful early launch of GTS metals that moved from Q3 into Q2.
Golf balls revenue increased 6% despite challenging comps against last year's Pro V1 launch volumes.
FootJoy operating margin improved significantly with underlying fundamentals strengthening via premium product mix shifts.
summary: Acushnet reported Q2 FY26 net sales of $820 million (up 14% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $209 million (a 46% increase), driven by strong Titleist equipment growth including a new GTS line. The company raised its full-year guidance to expect sales between $2.65 billion and $2.675 billion, citing the one-time benefit from IEEPA tariff refunds which boosted Q2 EBITDA but will not recur in H2. Management noted that while first-half results exceeded expectations due to accelerated club launches, second-half comps are expected to be challenging as those volumes shift into Q4.

negative_highlights: Q2 production was weaker than Q1 due to infrastructure investments at MSG, resulting in lower grades from surface stockpiles.
Borborema production decreased sequentially as the mine sequence shifted to higher-grade zones for later quarters (Q3/Q4).
Recurring cash flow of $80 million excluded realized losses on gold hedges ($37M paid out) and mark-to-market gains.
positive_highlights: Record high net income of $218 million driven by mark-to-market gains on gold hedges (+$126M).
MSG turnaround progressing ahead of schedule with reserves doubling to ~753k ounces and underground development performance up 89%.
Strong capital allocation returning cash via dividends ($0.72/share) and a new $200 million share buyback program.
summary: Aura Minerals reported Q2 FY26 net revenues of $336 million and adjusted EBITDA of approximately $197-$200 million, driven by lower production (totaling ~313k ounces for the trailing twelve months) due to infrastructure work at MSG. Management maintained full-year guidance of 340k-390k ounces despite Q2 weakness caused by mine sequencing and turnaround activities. The company returned $68 million via dividends ($0.72/share) and a new share buyback program, while investing in growth CapEx.

negative_highlights: Hai Su Vang 4X was a dry hole due to low reservoir quality, reducing resource estimates for the field
Capital program increased significantly with $190M allocated to Bubale appraisal and $70M accelerated Eagle Ford spend
Future capital spending in Vietnam remains uncertain pending results of Lac Da Vang North 1X
positive_highlights: Production averaged 169,000 boe/d, beating the midpoint of guidance
$110 million free cash flow generated in Q2 with leverage below 1x and $2.5 billion liquidity ending quarter
Bubale discovery encountered oil in both Turonian and Cenomanian reservoirs
summary: Second quarter production averaged 169,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day, beating the midpoint of guidance and generating $110 million in free cash flow while maintaining leverage below 1x. Management raised the full-year capital expenditure estimate from a prior range to a new midpoint of $1.55 billion, driven by incremental spending on the Bubale discovery appraisal ($90M) and an acceleration of Eagle Ford activity ($70M). However, this comes after disappointing results in Vietnam where Hai Su Vang 4X was a dry hole due to low reservoir quality rather than lack of oil-water contact.

negative_highlights: Closed block segment reported an adjusted operating loss of $110 million driven by a pre-tax liability remeasurement loss of $127 million.
A to E losses in the first half of 2026 have trended above the level implied by full-year expectations, potentially leading to higher total A to E losses for the year.
CareScout Services match volumes are currently pacing below the trajectory required to reach the full-year target of approximately 7,500 matches.
positive_highlights: Enact delivered strong performance with adjusted operating income of $143 million, up versus the prior quarter due to seasonally lower losses and higher net investment income.
Share repurchase guidance for full year 2026 was raised to a range of $225-$250 million.
Enact's PMIER sufficiency ratio remains strong at 161%, providing approximately $1.9 billion above requirements.
summary: Genworth reported Q2 FY26 net income of $47 million ($0.12/share) and adjusted operating income excluding the closed block of $112 million ($0.29/share). The quarter was impacted by a pre-tax liability remeasurement loss in the closed block segment of $127 million, driven by A to E variances that trended above full-year expectations. Management raised share repurchase guidance for 2026 to between $225 million and $250 million while maintaining Enact capital return estimates.

negative_highlights: New store contribution to volume growth decelerated from previous quarters as large accounts rotated into same-store sales dynamics.
No tariff refund benefit was realized in this quarter, which impacted the reported adjusted EBITDA margin compared to prior periods where such benefits may have been expected.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 20.1% YoY, marking a seventh consecutive quarter of growth above 20%.
Adjusted operating expenses remained flat at $145 million despite strong revenue growth, demonstrating significant operating leverage.
Free cash flow reached a record positive $37.5 million for the quarter.
summary: iRhythm reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $224.2 million (up 20.1% YoY) and adjusted EPS of $0.58, driven by volume growth with new stores contributing ~45%. The company announced an agreement to acquire VitalConnect for complementary MCT capabilities and raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $880-$890 million (up from prior expectations). Management also raised the adjusted EBITDA margin outlook for FY26 to 13%-14%.

negative_highlights: Collaboration revenue fell significantly year-over-year from $14.2 million to $7.7 million due to lower Regeneron payments.
Net loss widened slightly to $106.6 million compared to $101.3 million in the prior quarter, driven by higher G&A expenses related to commercial infrastructure build-out and legal costs.
Nex-z Phase III trials faced a clinical hold earlier this year due to Grade 4 liver transaminase elevations observed in less than 1% of patients.
positive_highlights: Lonvo-z achieved statistical significance for primary endpoints in the HALO trial with an 87% reduction in mean monthly attacks versus placebo and a 6-month BLA submission underway.
Nex-z resumed enrollment and dosing in both Phase III trials after resolving clinical holds, with screening rates rapidly increasing globally.
Genomic analysis identified HLA allele C0501 as the driver for Grade 3+ transaminase elevations, allowing patient stratification to mitigate risk.
summary: Intellia Therapeutics reported Q2 FY2026 collaboration revenue of $7.7 million versus $14.2 million in the prior year quarter due to reduced Regeneron payments, while R&D expenses decreased to $82.6 million and G&A increased to $37.8 million driven by commercial build-out costs. The company completed a recent equity financing yielding approximately $195 million in net proceeds, bringing cash, equivalents, and marketable securities to $628.4 million as of June 30th, which management believes is sufficient through at least 2028 excluding product revenues.

negative_highlights: Net revenue declined 13% YoY due to planned refranchising of Western U.S. and Japan operations.
International organic revenue decreased 5.1%, driven by declines in the UK and Australia markets.
Adjusted EBITDA for international segment fell 22% primarily due to margin compression from the Japan refranchising deal.
positive_highlights: System-wide sales grew 2.6% excluding McDonald's impact, driven by U.S. digital channel growth of 8% YoY.
U.S. organic revenue increased 0.1%, with underlying growth accelerating to 4.4% when excluding the exited partnership.
Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded significantly in the U.S., offsetting international declines and refranchising impacts.
summary: Krispy Kreme reported Q2 FY26 net revenue of $331 million (down 13% YoY) and system-wide sales growth of 2.6%, excluding the impact of the ended McDonald's USA partnership. Adjusted EBITDA was $28.8 million, up 43% due to productivity initiatives and cost controls, while margins improved significantly in the U.S. segment but declined internationally due to refranchising impacts. Management maintained full-year guidance for revenue ($1.25B-$1.35B) and system-wide sales growth (2%-4%), citing strong underlying demand despite headwinds from international declines.

negative_highlights: AST services growth was light with inventory destocking expected to persist into Q2
Healthcare capital equipment revenue only grew 1% due to shipment timing
Life Sciences EBIT margin decreased 140 bps due to productivity and inflation
positive_highlights: EPS up 11% to $2.59, driven by higher margins despite higher tax expense
Healthcare services grew 10% and consumables grew 9% with strong endoscopy demand
Backlog in healthcare capital equipment increased to $444 million despite flat revenue growth
summary: Q1 FY2027 results showed as-reported revenue growth of 7% and constant currency organic growth of 6%, with EPS of $2.59, up 11% YoY. Gross margin expanded 70 bps to 46%, and EBIT margin rose 100 bps to 23.8%. The company maintained its FY2027 revenue and EPS guidance, and announced a $600 million investment in a new Formulated Chemistry Center of Excellence, increasing CapEx guidance to ~$450 million, while keeping free cash flow at $800 million. Healthcare services grew 10% and consumables 9%, but AST services volume was soft due to inventory destocking, with expectations of acceleration in the second half.

negative_highlights: Revenue growth minimal, only 1% sequentially
GAAP net loss of $240M, though improved from $378M
Gross margin declined to 38% from 40% due to higher power costs
positive_highlights: Signed 20-year triple net lease with high investment-grade tenant, $6.6B contracted revenue
Normalized adjusted EBITDA positive $20M, excluding $133M mark-to-market loss
summary: Q3 FY2026 revenue was $138M, up 1% sequentially; GAAP net loss narrowed to $240M from $378M, driven by a smaller Bitcoin mark-to-market loss. Adjusted EBITDA was negative $113M including that non-cash item, but positive $20M when normalized. The major event was a 20-year triple net lease at Sandersville for $6.6B in contracted revenue (up to $11.6B with extensions), with the Texas portfolio under exclusivity for 885MW. Management reaffirmed no equity raise for Sandersville and expects project financing at >90% loan-to-cost.

negative_highlights: Bookings slightly below expectation due to sales team transition in May-July
Revenue outlook reflects the bookings impact from transition
SDR motion caused AEs' calendars to be too full with lower-value opportunities
positive_highlights: Revenue up 15.5% to $67.5M, payments growing at roughly double that rate
Record new location adds in Q2, strongest dental quarter in eight quarters
Operating margin expanded to ~5%, sales & marketing cost down 240 bps sequentially
summary: Weave reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $67.5 million, up 15.5% year over year, with payments revenue growing roughly double that rate. The company added record gross and net new locations, especially in dental, and expanded adjusted operating margin to nearly 5%, up from roughly breakeven a year ago. However, management noted a go-to-market transition led to bookings slightly below expectations, reflected in the revenue outlook. CEO expressed strong optimism about demand and AI-driven monetization opportunities.

negative_highlights: Sales down 4% YoY and sequentially due to Hormuz closure postponing Middle East shipments
EBITDA down 12% sequentially to $649 million on lower fixed-cost absorption and higher costs
Guidance excludes $130 million of backlog for Iraq, Kuwait, and Qatar
positive_highlights: Bay City mill producing at record levels, adding work shifts
Backlog of offshore projects increased, expecting sales benefit from Q4 into 2027
Board doubled interim dividend to ~$600 million
summary: Tenaris reported Q2 sales of $3 billion, down 4% YoY and sequentially, with EBITDA down 12% sequentially to $649 million and net income down 13% to $492 million, primarily due to Strait of Hormuz disruption and higher costs. Management kept H2 2026 revenue and EBITDA guidance in line with H1, with Q4 expected to improve on volume and pricing as offshore backlog and North American activity ramp. The board doubled the interim dividend to ~$600 million, signaling sustained capital returns. Full-year outlook is underpinned by higher prices and cost recovery, but the reopening of Hormuz is removed from the base case.

negative_highlights: Usage reduction from one of the largest customers was fully incorporated into Q3 guidance, creating a headwind that management chose to de-risk rather than exclude.
Gross margin contracted slightly quarter-over-quarter from 80.2% to 79.6%, though still within historical expectations.
positive_highlights: Revenue growth accelerated across the broadest base in years, with non-AI customers growing high-20s% year-over-year versus mid-20s last quarter.
New logo annualized bookings more than doubled year-over-year, driven by strong enterprise adoption and faster ramp times for new logos.
AI-native customer cohort diversified significantly to include hyperscalers running in-house AI labs.
summary: Datadog reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $1.12 billion, representing a 36% year-over-year increase and beating the high end of guidance. The company ended with approximately 4,720 customers having an ARR over $100k (up from ~3,850 last year) and generated free cash flow of $279 million. Management raised full fiscal year 2026 revenue guidance to a range of $4.45-$4.47 billion (+30% YoY), while maintaining Q3 guidance despite incorporating usage reductions from one large customer.

negative_highlights: Normalized adjusted EBITDA declined 8.9% year-over-year to $55 million due to higher fuel/shipping costs and strategic investments
Gross margin compressed 70 bps on a normalized basis (excluding tariff refunds) driven by elevated logistics expenses
Full-year outlook assumes no meaningful improvement in housing turnover or consumer confidence despite strong Q2
positive_highlights: Record quarterly net revenue of $385 million representing a 7.4% year-over-year increase
Comparable written sales accelerated to +12.5%, exceeding the high end of guidance
Successful recovery of ~$38M in IEEPA tariffs, with full cash refund received by quarter-end
summary: Arhaus reported record Q2 net revenue of $385 million (up 7.4% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $70 million, both beating the high end of prior guidance due to a one-time IEEPA tariff refund benefit of approximately $24 million recognized in gross profit. Excluding this discrete item, core performance showed revenue growth but margin compression driven by elevated fuel/shipping costs ($16M impact) and strategic investments (IT/POS), resulting in adjusted EBITDA down 8.9% YoY on a normalized basis. Management maintained full-year net revenue guidance of $1.43B-$1.47B while updating profitability expectations to reflect the tariff windfall, with Q3 outlook citing ongoing macro uncertainty and cost headwinds.

negative_highlights: Studio film results were weaker than expected
International linear advertising softer in Q2
NBA exit a negative driver on ad revenues
positive_highlights: Streaming revenue exceeded $3 billion for the first time
Streaming adjusted EBITDA up over 60% year-over-year
HBO Max retention on track for best year ever
summary: Warner Bros. Discovery reported record streaming revenues of over $3 billion in Q2 2026, with subscriber-related revenue growth accelerating 200 basis points sequentially to 10% ex-FX. Streaming adjusted EBITDA rose more than 60% year-over-year to $512 million, a nearly 17% margin. The studio segment faced a tough film quarter due to weak releases and a difficult comparison, but management reiterated the long-term $3 billion EBITDA target. Management noted international linear advertising was weaker in Q2, and the company remains confident in its pending sale to Paramount Skydance.

negative_highlights: Revenue dropped sharply to $1.4M from $18.7M in Q2 FY25 due to the conclusion of BMS and Astellas collaborations.
Operating expenses increased by $5.3 million (from $19.9M) primarily due to manufacturing activities for Varseta-M and higher consulting spend.
No financial guidance provided or raised; management noted a cash runway extending only to H2 2028.
positive_highlights: Enrollment completed across all Varseta-M dose optimization cohorts (8.6 and 10 mg/kg) for late-line CRC, targeting an end-of-year data readout.
Initiation of Phase I/II combination study with bevacizumab in Q4 to evaluate replacing irinotecan in second-line CRC patients.
Expansion into four additional EpCAM-positive GI cancers (gastric, GEJ, pancreatic, biliary) starting with ~20 patients per tumor type.
summary: CytomX reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $1.4 million and EPS loss (implied by lack of GAAP/Adj distinction in text but clear cash burn), representing a significant decline from the prior year due to collaboration expirations with BMS and Astellas, while operating expenses rose 27% YoY to $25.2M driven by Varseta-M manufacturing costs. Management provided no financial guidance updates or earnings estimates for Q3/Q4 FY26; instead, they focused entirely on clinical progress including the enrollment of 113 patients in the Phase I monotherapy study and a new collaboration expansion with Regeneron.

negative_highlights: Net loss per share widened to $0.07 from $0.05 in the prior year quarter
Total operating expenses increased by approximately 18% YoY to $17.9 million
No revenue reported as company remains pre-commercialization
positive_highlights: FDA cleared Phase III trial for OCU410 in geographic atrophy and granted RMAT designation
Completed enrollment of the liMeliGhT Phase III trial for retinitis pigmentosa with top-line data expected Q2 2027
Extended cash runway into late 2028 following $130 million convertible note financing
summary: Ocugen reported a net loss of $0.07 per share for Q2 FY26 compared to a $0.05 loss in the prior year quarter, with total operating expenses rising from $15.2 million to $17.9 million driven by increased R&D spend as Phase III trials initiate. Management highlighted significant clinical milestones including FDA clearance for OCU410 dosing and RMAT designation, but explicitly stated that top-line data is not expected until Q2 2027 or H1 2027 depending on the program. The company extended its cash runway to late 2028 following a $130 million convertible note financing.
