negative_highlights: Defense revenues were partially offset by temporary weakness in radar, space, naval, and fixed-wing segments due to timing of orders.
Commercial aerospace business still faces destocking headwinds expected to persist through the end of 2026 before a glide path resumes growth into 2027.
positive_highlights: Revenue hit a new quarterly record of $224 million with five consecutive quarters over $200M and the company's 21st consecutive quarter of year-over-year revenue growth.
Defense missile business surged 68% in Q2, driven by strong performance on PAC-3, SM-6, AMRAAM, Tomahawk, and THAAD programs under new framework agreements.
Commercial aerospace grew 16%, supported by higher OEM production rates for single-aisle platforms (737 MAX) and a significant aftermarket retrofit order.
summary: Ducommun reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $224.5 million, a 12% year-over-year increase driven by strong commercial aerospace growth (16%) and defense missile business expansion (68%). Gross margin expanded to 28%, while adjusted operating income reached an 11.9% margin on the quarter. Management reiterated full-year guidance for mid-to-high single-digit revenue growth, noting that a pull-forward of production in Q2 will result in lower sequential growth rates expected in H2.

negative_highlights: Emerging markets net sales declined 2% year-over-year due to ARV supply constraints
Manufacturing disruptions at Nashik facility following Q1 fire
Europe brands declined slightly year-over-year due to competition on Dymista
positive_highlights: Total revenues of $3.8 billion, up 3.5% operationally, exceeded expectations
Greater China net sales increased 16% year-over-year, ahead of expectations
Raised midpoint of 2026 financial guidance across all key metrics
summary: Viatris delivered Q2 2026 revenue of $3.8 billion, up 3.5% operationally year-over-year, with adjusted EBITDA of $1.2 billion and adjusted EPS of $0.69, exceeding expectations. The company raised its full-year guidance across all key financial metrics. Growth was led by Greater China (up 16% year-over-year) and strong complex generics in North America, while emerging markets declined 2% due to supply constraints. Management also highlighted strategic progress including FDA approval for Gwyn Lo, the planned sale of Tyrvaya, and continued capital returns of $550 million to shareholders.

negative_highlights: Q3 energy prices are expected to be lower than last year despite having fewer resources due to the dry season.
El Niño scenario brings pressure on note weakness in-term prices in July, August, and September with recovery only expected starting October.
Financial results were partially offset by worsening interest rates (SELIC at 14%) and slightly higher leverage.
positive_highlights: EBITDA reached BRL 6.7 billion, representing a 21.5% year-over-year increase driven by generation segment contribution.
Generation unit margin improved from BRL 80 to BRL 100 quarter-on-quarter due to favorable price mix in the Northeast and Southeast sub-markets.
Company successfully migrated to Novo Mercado (highest governance level) at B3 and received Pro-Ethics seal for 2025-2026.
summary: AXIA Energia reported Q2 FY2026 EBITDA of BRL 6.7 billion (up 21.5% YoY), driven by improved generation margins and stable transmission results. Management raised full-year investment targets to approximately BRL 5-5.5 billion, citing the need for asset resilience against climate risks like El Niño. While capital allocation remains robust with a declared shareholder return program of BRL 7.7 billion (including new PNC redemptions), management issued cautious guidance on Q3 energy prices and availability due to seasonal dry season pressures.

negative_highlights: Illinois ZEC revenue recognition was $85 million in Q2 compared to $200 million last year due to timing differences.
Nuclear capacity factor reduced by 1.8% quarter-over-quarter primarily due to additional planned refueling outage days.
positive_highlights: Raised full-year operational earnings guidance range to $11.50-$12.50 EPS (midpoint up $0.50).
Nuclear fleet achieved a capacity factor above 99% during the Mid-Atlantic heat wave ahead of July.
summary: Constellation Energy reported Q2 FY26 GAAP EPS of $1.42 and adjusted operating earnings per share (EPS) of $2.55, beating expectations driven by Calpine accretion and higher PJM capacity prices despite a lower-than-expected Illinois ZEC revenue recognition ($85 million vs $200 million prior year). Management raised full-year 2026 adjusted operating EPS guidance to an expanded range of $11.50-$12.50 per share, increasing the midpoint by $0.50 from the previous outlook.

negative_highlights: Total revenue declined 5.8% year-over-year, with video and news/advertising driving approximately 75% of the decline.
Broadband net subscriber losses remained elevated at 40,000 in a highly competitive environment.
Residential ARPU declined 1.1% year-over-year due to product mix shifts away from lower-margin video.
positive_highlights: Gross margin reached an all-time high of 71%, expanding 180 bps year-over-year despite lower revenues.
Mobile net additions accelerated significantly with 50,000 lines added (up ~33% YoY), marking the best quarter to date.
Convergence ARPU grew 2.4% year-over-year to $79.80 driven by multi-product relationships.
summary: Optimum reported Q2 FY26 revenue of approximately $2 billion (down 5.8% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $786 million (down 2.2% YoY). Broadband net losses were 40,000 while mobile added 50,000 lines; gross margin expanded to an all-time high of 71%. Management reiterated a full-year revenue decline expectation and noted that ARPU is expected to face tougher comparisons in the second half.

negative_highlights: Rubber segment adjusted EBITDA fell 61% year-over-year primarily due to lower annual pricing agreements and unfavorable customer mix.
Tire production rates in key regions remain below historical norms, limiting near-term volume recovery potential for the Rubber business.
Management noted limited order visibility into the second half of the year despite reaffirming guidance.
positive_highlights: Specialty segment delivered its best quarterly performance since early 2022 with adjusted EBITDA increasing 96% year-over-year driven by volume growth and pricing actions.
Working capital initiatives generated a $4 million cash source in the quarter, offsetting roughly $60 million of headwind from higher oil-derived feedstock costs.
Management reaffirmed full-year guidance while lifting free cash flow expectations to slightly positive levels at the midpoint.
summary: Orion reported Q2 FY26 adjusted EBITDA of $58 million (up 26% sequentially) and generated positive free cash flow of $2 million despite a year-over-year decline in the Rubber segment driven by lower contractual pricing. Management reaffirmed full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance of $170-$210 million while lifting the midpoint for annualized free cash flow to $5 million, citing working capital improvements and favorable trade flows.

negative_highlights: Large display driver IC sales declined 21.0% sequentially as panel makers pulled forward inventory purchases in prior quarters.
Supply constraints from AI demand are rippling across the semiconductor supply chain, causing higher manufacturing costs and extended lead times for mature process nodes.
Q3 guidance anticipates a sequential decline in large display driver IC sales due to continued customer inventory pull-forward.
positive_highlights: Automotive driver IC sales increased double-digits sequentially due to broad-based customer replenishment following the Lunar New Year slowdown.
Gross margin expanded significantly to 33.1% from 30.4% in Q1, exceeding guidance of around 32%.
Himax is well-positioned for automotive growth with LTDI and TCON solutions becoming standard platforms for ultra-large displays.
summary: Himax reported Q2 FY2026 revenues of $227.4 million (up 14.2% sequentially and 5.9% YoY) with gross margins expanding to 33.1%, both significantly exceeding the company's guidance range. Diluted EPS was $0.114, beating the upper end of the guided range ($0.086-$0.103), driven by strong automotive IC sales and a favorable product mix despite supply constraints in non-AI applications.

negative_highlights: Hardware delivery and data center readiness remain primary execution risks to revenue ramp
Contracted capacity only 120 MW of 212 MW, leaving 92 MW yet to be sold
positive_highlights: Secured capacity increased to 212 MW, up 80 MW from prior guidance, and capacities quadrupled year-to-date
Executed $8.8 billion of total contract value year-to-date, including $4.9 billion NVIDIA partnership
Raised approximately $2.2 billion of capital since December 2025 with a $1.6 billion oversubscribed financing
summary: In Q2 FY2026, SharonAI reported a major expansion in secured AI factory capacity to 212 MW from 132 MW prior, and contracted capacity grew to 120 MW with total contract value reaching approximately $8.8 billion year-to-date. Key wins include a six-year $4.9 billion NVIDIA partnership, a $1.32 billion take-or-pay with a global AI lab, and a $373 million agreement at a record price over $4 per GPU hour. The company raised about $2.2 billion in capital since December 2025, including a $1.6 billion oversubscribed round. Management expressed confidence in demand outpacing supply and guides for material revenue ramp from Q3 through 2027.

negative_highlights: Patient Services gross profit declined 57% YoY due to increased clinical labor costs and conservative fee-for-service approach.
Medical Loss Ratio (MLR) for capitated members rose to 85.5% from 71%, reflecting the ramp-up of new delegated lives.
One major Florida contract launch was delayed by two months, pushing effective date from Q3 to Q4.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 34.6% YoY driven by Specialty Pharmacy growth of 57.6% and new capitated contracts in Nevada, Oregon, and California exclusivity.
Adjusted EBITDA turned positive at $0.2 million, marking the second profitable quarter as a public company within guidance range.
Strategic refinancing replaced an expiring convertible note with a 5-year term loan ($75M), improving liquidity without dilution.
summary: Starling Oncology reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $161 million (up 34.6% YoY) and achieved positive adjusted EBITDA of $0.2 million, beating the prior loss guidance range. Management raised full-year 2026 revenue and gross profit ranges while narrowing the adjusted EBITDA outlook to reflect a delayed contract launch in Q3. The company successfully completed a strategic refinancing extending debt maturities to 2031 without equity dilution.

negative_highlights: Net loss included roughly $33 million in pre-tax costs related to reverse asset sales and legacy subservicing transfers.
Servicing adjusted pre-tax income decreased over 60% year-over-year due to an almost 80% increase in MSR runoff driven by lower interest rates.
Unfavorable fair value adjustments on the reverse mortgage book totaled approximately $12 million, creating significant volatility.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 24% year-over-year with record origination volume and servicing additions exceeding first-half expectations.
Originations pre-tax income increased over three times versus last year, while margins improved to 26 basis points from the prior quarter.
Servicing UPB ended the quarter up 10% year-over-year against an industry growth of only 3%, driven by organic expansion.
summary: Onity reported Q2 FY26 revenue growth of 24% year-over-year driven by record origination volume and servicing additions exceeding guidance. However, the quarter included a net loss due to roughly $33 million in pre-tax transaction costs related to asset sales/transfers and approximately $24 million in unfavorable fair value adjustments on reverse MSRs. Management lowered its full-year 2026 adjusted ROE outlook to the low end of the previously guided range (10%-15%) citing persistent market volatility.

negative_highlights: Progress toward new U.S. contract slower than in the past
Q1 had minimal product revenues, reflecting variability
Meridian promotion agreement expired and was not renewed
positive_highlights: Q2 product revenues of $38M, with $24M IV TPOXX delivered to SNS and $13M international orders
Net income of $12M, EPS of $0.17
Targeting new international contract and order delivery by March of next year
summary: In Q2 FY2026, SIGA reported product-related revenues of $38 million, including $24 million of IV TPOXX delivered to the U.S. Strategic National Stockpile and $13 million of oral TPOXX to international customers. Net income was $12 million, with fully diluted EPS of $0.17. The U.S. contract process is slower than expected, but management remains confident in TPOXX's role, and they are targeting a new international contract with delivery by March 2027.

negative_highlights: Management explicitly stated they will not add incremental fleets speculatively despite tight market conditions.
Pricing pressure persists specifically in the sand and proppant markets within West Texas.
Free cash flow remains negative due to capital expenditures of $32 million.
positive_highlights: Revenues increased sequentially by $48 million driven by stimulation services ($430M) and Flotek ($102M).
Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to 14% from 12% in the prior quarter.
Free cash flow improved significantly to a negative $8 million, up from negative $25 million in Q1.
summary: ProFrac reported Q2 FY2026 revenues of $498 million (up from $450M in Q1) and adjusted EBITDA of $69 million with a margin expansion to 14%. Management raised the full-year capital expenditure guidance range slightly higher than previously stated, citing an acceleration of engine upgrade programs. The company reiterated its disciplined approach to not adding incremental fleets speculatively while noting that pricing benefits are layering in for Q3 and Q4.

negative_highlights: Cyber Safety segment growth remained mid-single digits
Operating profit growth of 9% lagged revenue growth
Agentic AI revenue expected to be modest in FY2027
positive_highlights: Bookings and revenue both up 11% year-over-year, above guidance
Trust-Based Solutions bookings grew 25%
Engine passed half a billion dollars in annual revenue run rate
summary: Gen delivered Q1 FY2027 with bookings and revenue both up 11% year-over-year, above the high end of guidance, and non-GAAP EPS grew 19%. The company raised full-year FY2027 guidance to 9%-11% revenue growth and 14%-18% EPS growth. Cyber Safety grew mid-single digits, while Trust-Based Solutions grew 25%, with Engine crossing a $500 million annual revenue run rate. Management highlighted record paid customers of over 80 million and continued margin stability at 50%.

negative_highlights: R&D expenses are expected to increase in H2 due to the ramp-up of the STARS-2 trial.
SG&A expense is anticipated to see a modest increase during the remainder of the year.
positive_highlights: LINZESS delivered a second consecutive quarter of strong performance with U.S. sales up 14% YoY to $282.3 million driven by mid-single-digit demand growth and improved net price.
Full-year LINZESS guidance raised significantly, projecting annualized sales between $1.15 billion and $1.20 billion representing a greater than 30% increase year-over-year.
FDA approval of LINZESS for functional constipation in pediatric patients two years and older established it as the only prescription therapy approved for this age group.
summary: Ironwood reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $113 million with LINZESS U.S. net sales reaching $282.3 million (up 14% YoY). Management raised full-year guidance for LINZESS to a range of $1.15 billion-$1.20 billion and adjusted EBITDA to greater than $310 million, citing mid-single-digit demand growth and improved net price. The company repaid its convertible notes at maturity with cash on hand.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EPS midpoint reduced by roughly $0.12 due to financing costs, price/cost neutrality drag of ~$15M, and Eddyfi integration dilution
Gross margins declined 90 bps YoY driven by transitory logistics cost spikes in the Middle East (up triple) and commodity inflation
Middle East volumes down double digits due to geopolitical conflict, though management views this as temporary
positive_highlights: Total core sales reached record levels with double-digit organic growth in equipment segments
Eddyfi acquisition closed ahead of schedule, contributing approximately $35 million to full-year EBITDA guidance increase
Americas segment delivered strong performance with North America showing particularly robust demand for automation and gas control
summary: ESAB reported Q2 FY26 total sales of $766 million (up 13% YoY) and Adjusted EBITDA of $150 million (up 8%), driven by record core sales and the integration of Eddyfi. Management raised its full-year 2026 outlook for both Total Core Sales ($3B-$3.1B) and Adjusted EBITDA ($615M-$625M), incorporating seven months of Eddyfi results while acknowledging $15 million in transitory price/cost headwinds from logistics and commodities. The company noted a 90-basis-point margin decline due to these costs, though it expects sequential pricing improvement and volume growth in the second half.

Liberty Capital (formerly GCI Liberty) reported Q2 revenue of $261 million, flat year-over-year, with adjusted OIBDA of $96 million down 11% YoY and trailing-12-month free cash flow of $59 million, a YoY decline on higher CapEx, lower OIBDA and working capital swings. Management kept full-year GCI OIBDA guidance at approximately stable with performance weighted to Q4, maintained 2026 CapEx of about $290 million as the peak year, and expects capital intensity to decline in 2027 and 2028. The company introduced a new capital allocation policy: a $60 million annual dividend (~$15 million quarterly) starting in Q4, targeting ~3x long-term net leverage at GCI, with the Quintillion acquisition still expected to close this year (HSR expired, FCC pending) and roughly $20 million of run-rate synergies over 24 months. Consumer revenue fell 2% on the video shutdown, business revenue rose 1% while business gross margin fell to 75.5% on a $9 million distribution cost increase, and consumer broadband declined organically by 500 subs, more than offset by a 5,400-subscriber acquisition.

negative_highlights: GAAP net loss of $77 million due to one-time transaction costs, financing fees ($41M), and non-cash intangible asset amortization from the Legend acquisition.
Cash balance at quarter-end was $155 million, below the prior range guidance but attributed to seasonal lows and significant debt financing costs associated with closing the deal.
positive_highlights: Revenue beat guidance by $10M ($196M vs implied ~$185-190M) driven by a massive 193% growth in the media segment (including Legend).
Adjusted EBITDA of $53 million exceeded the guided range, resulting in an operating margin roughly 270 bps above guidance.
Legend acquisition synergies are realizing faster than expected with cross-note underway and prediction market deals signed immediately post-close.
summary: Genius Sports reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $196 million (up 65% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $53 million, beating guidance on all metrics including a significant margin expansion to roughly 27%. Management raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $1.005-$1.025 billion and adjusted EBITDA to $285-$295 million (approx. 29% margin), citing strong organic growth, Legend integration synergies ahead of schedule, and new prediction market partnerships with Kalshi and Polymarket.

negative_highlights: Product revenue fell 66% YoY and service repair activities were slower than planned due to geopolitical uncertainty in the Middle East.
Total orders declined sequentially by 6%, reflecting timing delays rather than demand destruction.
$10 million of discrete revenue headwind recognized specifically from installation/commissioning delays.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA margins expanded year-over-year to 20% driven by disciplined cost execution and favorable mix.
Spares revenue increased 70% YoY as customers prepare for upcoming contracts.
summary: HMH reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $171 million (flat sequentially) and adjusted EBITDA of $34 million with margins expanding to 20% YoY despite a discrete $10M headwind from Middle East delays. Management maintained full-year guidance for adjusted EBITDA between $157-$177 million, citing strong digital technology order intake offsetting slower repair activity and geopolitical timing shifts.

negative_highlights: Q3 production guidance assumes a ramp-up from Ras Laffan, which was largely shut-in due to conflict impacts.
Willow project remains on track for early 2029 first oil but peak CapEx has not yet been passed.
positive_highlights: Production beat high-end guidance driven by record Permian output exceeding 900k bbls/day and strong Lower 48 performance.
$5 billion disposition target achieved ahead of schedule with $1.7 billion in non-core asset sales completed in July.
LNG portfolio expanded to 12 million tons per annum via new agreements in Indonesia and the U.S. Gulf Coast.
summary: ConocoPhillips reported Q2 FY26 production of 2.248 million boe/d and adjusted EPS of $3.24, both exceeding the high end of guidance. The company generated $7.2 billion in cash flow from operations and delivered $4.2 billion in free cash flow after $3 billion CapEx. Full-year distribution targets remain unchanged at 45% of CFO, with production guidance for Q3 raised to a range of 2.29-2.32 million boe/d.

negative_highlights: Gross margin dropped to 37.3% from 44.7% YoY, with adjusted EBITDA margin down to 17.5% from 31.2%
Section 232 tariff expenses added ~$17M in the quarter; net leverage low but cash flow pressured
Q3 revenue expected to step down sequentially due to pull-forward of $15-20M residential orders
positive_highlights: Record revenue of $295.3M, up 15.6% YoY with double-digit growth in both segments
Backlog grew 15.6% to record $1.4B; book-to-bill 1.1 for 23 consecutive quarters
Strong demand commentary: quoting activity 'crazy high' across the U.S., and New York coming back strong
summary: Tecnoglass reported record Q2 2026 revenue of $295.3 million, up 15.6% YoY, with record backlog of $1.4 billion and adjusted EBITDA of $51.7 million (17.5% margin). Margins fell sharply due to higher aluminum costs (+77% YoY), peso appreciation, and Section 232 tariffs ($17M expense). Management narrowed FY2026 revenue guidance to $1.08-1.12B and adjusted EBITDA to $220-230M, expecting Q3 EBITDA roughly flat sequentially. Demand remains strong, pricing actions are flowing through starting Q3, and automation is on track, but margin headwinds persist.

negative_highlights: R&D expenses increased to $27.7 million from $17.5 million prior year due to Hypercon investment.
note, general, and administrative (SG&A) expenses rose to $57 million compared to $41.6 million in the prior period.
positive_highlights: Total revenue grew 48% year-over-year to $481 million, exceeding consensus estimates.
Royalty revenues surged 50% YoY to CHF $307.7 million due to strong performance from DARZALEX SC and VYVGART Hytrulo.
Signed five new collaboration agreements in the quarter (four announced Q2, one in July), including firsts for ADCs and nucleic acids.
summary: Halozyme reported a record second quarter with total revenue of $481 million (up 48% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of CHF 329 million, driven by robust royalty growth of 50%. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance for total revenue to the range of $1.835 billion-$1.91 billion and increased projected royalties significantly above prior expectations.

negative_highlights: Product segment gross margin contracted to 9.7% from the prior year due to increased European construction costs
Net income decreased slightly on a GAAP basis (EPS $0.43 vs $0.46) reflecting a one-time $6.6 million write-off of a storage project not pursued
positive_highlights: Revenue increased 10.6% to $258.8 million with gross profit up 20.8% to $68.7 million
Energy storage revenue surged 195.1% year-over-year to $42.8 million due to new capacity and high asset availability in PJM
Full-year guidance raised significantly for both total revenues ($1.15B-$1.2B) and adjusted EBITDA ($630M-$650M)
summary: Second quarter revenue increased 10.6% to $258.8 million driven by strong energy storage performance and electricity segment growth, while gross profit expanded 20.8%. Management raised full-year guidance for both total revenues (now expecting $1.15B-$1.2B) and adjusted EBITDA ($630M-$650M), citing accelerating momentum across all three business segments.

negative_highlights: Q2 growth was capped below expectations due to a customer's inability to source sufficient switches caused by memory shortages, leading to an estimated $20-$25M revenue reduction in Q3 for the 100G segment.
Production capacity remains significantly constrained through mid-2027; current output is bounded almost entirely by production limits and key component availability (specifically DSPs/TIAs).
Q4 guidance implies a slower ramp than anticipated due to material constraints, with management expecting only $50M-$80M of 1.6T revenue in Q4 despite high demand.
positive_highlights: Returned to non-GAAP profitability with income per share of $0.06, beating the expected range of a loss of $0.03 to earnings of $0.03.
800G revenue increased more than tenfold year-over-year and doubled sequentially; 1.6T volume orders received from major hyperscale customers are beginning shipment in Q2/Q3.
CATV business delivered record revenue of $84.6 million (including the specific figure mentioned for total CATV), up 43.8% YoY, driven by Mediacom selection and amplifier shipments.
summary: Applied Optoelectronics reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $191.9 million (up 86% YoY), which was in line with guidance but missed the upper end due to a specific customer shortage affecting 100G products that reduced expected growth by an estimated $20-$25M for Q3. The company returned to non-GAAP profitability with income of $0.06 per share, beating expectations and marking its fifth consecutive quarter of record revenue. Management reiterated full-year guidance around $1.1B but noted near-term capacity constraints on 800G/1.6T products remain the primary limiter despite robust demand.

negative_highlights: Order book remains low at 14.4% of existing fleet compared to historical highs like 66% in 2008.
Global trade volume growth projected to slow from 5% in 2025 to 3.5% in 2026 due to tariff impacts and unwinding front-loading effects.
positive_highlights: Net income swung from a loss of $3.1M in Q2 FY25 to $6.6M in Q2 FY26, driven by rates more than doubling year-over-year.
Operational utilization remained at 100% with no idle periods for the quarter.
Refinanced MV Ekaterini loan facility increased balance by approximately $8 million, boosting liquidity.
summary: EuroDry reported Q2 FY26 net revenues of $17.7 million and adjusted EPS of $2.44, representing a significant recovery from the prior year's loss driven by time charter rates more than doubling to an average of $20,398 per day. Management highlighted strong liquidity with cash assets at $37.5 million and announced a refinancing agreement for MV Ekaterini that increased its loan facility balance by nearly $8 million. The company reiterated disciplined capital allocation through newbuild orders while maintaining operational flexibility on index-linked charters.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA margin is expected to be slightly down compared to Q3 2025 due to the timing of investments in sales and marketing.
Implied take rate for full year 2026 is projected to remain relatively flat versus 2025, impacted by new business incentives.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 17% year-over-year to $3.6 billion, exceeding the high end of management's outlook.
Growth among first-time bookers accelerated to 11%, marking the highest growth seen in four years.
Customer support costs per booking declined approximately 16% year-over-year driven by AI assistant adoption.
summary: Airbnb reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $3.6 billion (up 17% YoY) and gross booking value growth of 16%, exceeding the high end of its outlook across every key metric including nights booked, ADR, and first-time bookers. Management raised full-year guidance for both top-line growth to at least mid-teens and adjusted EBITDA margin to a minimum of 35.5%. The company highlighted accelerated momentum in core markets like the U.S., France, UK, and Australia alongside strong expansion market performance.

negative_highlights: Organic volume down 1.6% on total revenue, impacted by prior-year landfill event volumes
Residential volume declined 4.3% due to known contract losses
Large container volumes declined 2.2% due to soft construction activity
positive_highlights: Raised full-year 2026 guidance across all metrics
Core price on related revenue of 6.4% exceeded cost inflation
Underlying business margin expanded 90 basis points
summary: Republic Services reported Q2 FY2026 revenue growth of 4.6% and adjusted EBITDA growth of 4.5%, with adjusted EPS of $1.85. The company maintained adjusted EBITDA margin at 32.1% despite headwinds from prior-year landfill event volumes. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance across revenue, adjusted EBITDA, EPS, and free cash flow, citing higher fuel recovery fee revenue, increased recycling commodity prices, and acquisitions. Volume declined 1.6% on total revenue due to tough comps, but underlying pricing exceeded cost inflation and management expects sequential volume improvement.

negative_highlights: Operating income included a one-time gain from the U.S. tower portfolio sale, masking underlying organic operating performance.
International revenue growth was dampened by an expected loss of government support in the U.S. Virgin Islands which expired at end of 2025.
Capital expenditures decreased $3.8 million year-over-year due to variable timing of reimbursable spending under government programs.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded by approximately 170 basis points year-over-year to reflect operating discipline.
Net leverage ratio improved significantly from 2.36 times at end of 2025 to 0.91 times following the $268 million tower sale proceeds.
Board authorized an expansion of share repurchase authorization to $30 million and increased quarterly cash dividend by 5.5%.
summary: ATN International reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $184.5 million (up 2% YoY) and Adjusted EBITDA growth of nearly 9%, driven by a one-time gain from the U.S. tower portfolio sale which improved operating income to $240 million. Management reaffirmed its full-year 2026 Adjusted EBITDA guidance range of $183-$193 million, maintaining expectations despite excluding recurring impacts like lost rents and expired subsidies in specific regions.

negative_highlights: note, general, and administrative expenses increased significantly by $6.3 million (from $15.6M to $21.9M) driven primarily by a one-time legal charge.
Research and development spending decreased slightly due to reduced AMX0035 activity for progressive supranuclear palsy, offset by higher avexitide spend.
positive_highlights: Ended Q2 with $250.8 million cash and marketable securities, securing runway into 2028 for milestones including LUCIDITY readout and potential launch.
LUCIDITY trial last patient visit completed; database expected to lock in late August or early September following a successful double-blind period.
CMS/CDC published new ICD-10 code specific to PBH effective October 2026, enhancing recognition of the condition for diagnosis and epidemiology.
summary: Amylyx reported Q2 FY2026 operating expenses of $45.7 million (up 7% YoY) and ended the quarter with $250.8 million in cash, providing a runway into 2028 to fund operations through the anticipated LUCIDITY top-line readout in late August or early September. Management reiterated its strategic priorities of advancing NDA readiness for avexitide and strengthening commercial launch preparations targeting a potential 2027 launch if approved by the FDA. The company remains blinded to the pivotal Phase III data but expressed strong confidence in execution as they await results from the study evaluating their first-in-class GLP-1 receptor antagonist.

negative_highlights: Outpatient utilization elevated through first six months
Expect increasing membership churn in back half due to CMS program integrity
Market morbidity data only four months, not fully credited in guidance
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 70% year-over-year to $4.9 billion
Earnings from operations increased $619 million year-over-year to $389 million
Full-year earnings from operations guidance raised by $250 million
summary: Oscar Health reported Q2 2026 revenue of $4.9 billion, up 70% year-over-year, with MLR improving to 79.2% and SG&A expense ratio at a record low of 14.2%. Earnings from operations surged to $389 million, and net income was $362 million, both up sharply year-over-year. The company raised full-year 2026 earnings from operations guidance to $500-700 million, up $250 million, and improved MLR guidance to 81.5%-82.5%. Management highlighted favorable risk adjustment and utilization trends but remained cautious on CMS program integrity-driven member churn in the second half.

negative_highlights: Revenue down 7.8% YoY, at low end of guidance
Delivery Systems revenue down 18.4% with 770 systems placed vs 957
Lowered full-year revenue outlook to $280-290 million
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA of $17 million, up from $13.9 million YoY and above guidance
Adjusted gross margin expanded 590 basis points to 71.8%
SkinStylus revenue grew nearly 50% YoY in Q2
summary: Q2 revenue of $72.1 million fell 7.8% YoY and came in at the low end of guidance, with equipment sales down 18.4% and consumables down 3.5%. Adjusted EBITDA of $17 million beat guidance of $11-13 million, driven by gross margin expansion and cost discipline. Management lowered the full-year revenue outlook to $280-290 million while raising adjusted EBITDA guidance to $39-46 million. They introduced a new device rental program, received FDA clearance for SkinStylus periorbital wrinkles, and plan to repay the October 2026 convertible maturity with cash.

negative_highlights: Core earnings declined 10% year-over-year in Canada due to unfavorable claims and expense experience within group insurance.
Corporate segment loss widened by approximately CAD 45 million compared to the prior year, driven by P&C retro business cycle softening and increased central AI spending.
Retail outflows persisted in Global WAM despite improved sequential trends.
positive_highlights: Asia core earnings grew 21% year-over-year to record levels driven by double-digit sales growth in Hong Kong, Singapore, and Japan.
Global WAM generated net inflows of CAD 4 billion supported by record gross flows and strength in institutional business (CQS/Comvest).
summary: Manulife reported Q2 FY26 results with APE sales growing 21% year-over-year and core EPS increasing 16%. Core ROE rose to 16.3%, driven by strong performance in Asia (core earnings +21%) and Global WAM, partially offset by unfavorable claims experience in Canada's group insurance segment. The company announced a new long-term care reinsurance transaction transferring biometric risk on CAD 3.2 billion of reserves while retaining asset management.

negative_highlights: Logistics revenue down 10% sequentially on lower last-mile transportation activity
Grid interconnection delays persist (e.g., 7-8 year wait for one energy customer)
Guidance excludes potential ancillary services, which are hard to predict
positive_highlights: Record quarter with revenue up 12% sequentially and adjusted EBITDA up 30% sequentially
Raised Q3 guidance and introduced Q4 guidance with strong ramp expectations
Expanded contracts with three investment-grade technology companies, including new scope and longer terms
summary: Solaris reported record Q2 2026 with revenue of ~$219M, up 12% sequentially, and adjusted EBITDA of ~$108M, up 30% sequentially, with adjusted pro forma EPS of $0.39. The company raised Q3 adjusted EBITDA guidance to $90M-$105M and introduced Q4 guidance of $100M-$120M, reflecting GESA acquisition and new contract ramps. Management highlighted multiple contract expansions with three investment-grade tech customers, a new nuclear SMR investment, and strong demand with multiple gigawatts in active negotiations.

negative_highlights: Net revenue declined 10.1% to $166 million, with adjusted EBITDA loss of $26.6 million
Full-year supply management costs raised to mid-$30 million from initial $32 million estimate
Share repurchase program terminated; new term loan and ABL facility replace revolving credit line
positive_highlights: Retail dollar share of shell egg category gained more than 200 basis points year-over-year in Q2
TDPs averaged 148.7 year-to-date, on track for 170-175 in Q4
Reduced annualized SG&A run rate by approximately $6-7 million
summary: Vital Farms reported Q2 FY2026 net revenue of $166 million, down 10.1% year-over-year, with an adjusted EBITDA loss of $26.6 million, reflecting $28.1 million in supply management and discrete costs including excess breaker sales and butter wind-down. Management reaffirmed full-year revenue guidance of $775-$800 million and adjusted EBITDA of $0-$10 million, and expects Q3 sequential revenue improvement with Q4 gross margin exiting around 30%. They noted progress on narrowing price gaps and distribution gains, but raised full-year supply management costs to mid-$30 million and took on new debt while terminating share repurchases.

negative_highlights: CEO explicitly stated results were 'clearly disappointing' due to a combination of external factors and internal structural issues.
Production transfer of Natuzzi Editions from the U.S. market (China) to Italy negatively affected the margin profile for this line.
Management described their industrial footprint in Italy as currently oversized compared to present sales volume, necessitating significant cost reduction.
positive_highlights: Retail expansion continued at a healthy pace with the opening of 26 new stores during H1 FY2026 following 49 openings in 2025.
The launch of Natuzzi Studio exceeded expectations, generating strong interest from dealers for this new urban design hub format.
summary: The company reported disappointing Q1 FY2026 results driven by geopolitical instability, U.S. tariffs, weak housing markets, and a specific margin hit from transferring Natuzzi Editions production to Italy. Management announced an immediate restructuring plan initiated in July to reduce fixed costs, including relocating some production to Romania, consolidating Italian plants from five to two, and offering voluntary exit programs for 120 employees with cash flow impacts expected in 2027.

negative_highlights: Full-year revenue guidance cut from $26 million to $9-$10 million
Delivery revenue declined meaningfully in Q2 versus Q1
Uber partnership likely not renewed in early 2027
positive_highlights: Total revenue up 9% sequentially and over 400% YoY to $3.2 million
Delivery volume via DoorDash grew nearly 50% in a single quarter
Recurring revenue was over 50% of total revenue; cash liquidity over $240 million
summary: Serve Robotics reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $3.2 million, up 9% sequentially and over 400% YoY, but below expectations due to a decline in Uber delivery volume. The company materially lowered full-year revenue guidance from $26 million to $9-$10 million, citing the removal of assumed second-half growth from Uber. Management says the Uber agreement may not be renewed in early 2027 and is reallocating resources to diversified channels, including DoorDash (up ~50% sequentially), advertising (~50% of robot delivery revenue), and hospital robotics. Gross margin was -271% with a gross loss of ~$8.8 million, but fleet gross margin improved sequentially.

negative_highlights: G&A of $56 million exceeded guidance due to $11 million of acquisition costs
Fuel costs remain 20%-40% above pre-war levels
Awaiting regulatory clearance in Brazil and the U.S. for the Valaris deal
positive_highlights: Revenue of $966 million was at the upper end of guidance
Adjusted EBITDA margin of 32%, with fleet uptime at 98%
Backlog strengthened by ~$300 million, plus $1 billion pending Equinor award
summary: Transocean beat its Q2 FY2026 guidance on revenue and cost, with revenue of $966 million at the upper end of the range and adjusted EBITDA margin of 32%. Fleet uptime hit 98%, and backlog grew by about $300 million excluding a pending $1 billion Equinor award. The company raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance, expects to close the Valaris acquisition in Q4, and plans to call $200 million of 8% notes, reducing gross debt to below $4.8 billion.

negative_highlights: Gross margin declined to 8.3% from 8.9% due to higher capped-agent mix
Reported operating loss of $7 million vs. operating income of $1.7 million in prior year, due to $11.6 million acquisition costs
Guidance expects Q3 revenue and adjusted EBITDA to decline sequentially from Q2
positive_highlights: Revenue up 30% YoY to $700.6 million, with 27% increase in closed transactions to a record 62,380
Adjusted EBITDA up 38% YoY to $27.6 million, with margin expansion to 3.9%
Record cash of $86.6 million, up from $49.9 million at start of year
summary: The Real Brokerage reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $700.6 million, up 30% year-over-year, and adjusted EBITDA of $27.6 million, up 38% year-over-year. Despite a challenging housing market, closed transactions rose 27% to a record 62,380. The company reaffirmed its pending RE/MAX transaction, expecting to complete it in H2 2026 and targeting $30 million in cost synergies within three years. Guidance indicates Q3 sequential declines due to seasonality, with combined company guidance planned for the Q3 call.

negative_highlights: R&D expenses increased to $41.3 million due to expanded clinical programs
No full visibility into prescription data, limiting precise adoption metrics
positive_highlights: Net product revenues of $25.1 million with significant quarter-over-quarter growth in adoption
Pro forma cash balance of $201.4 million, extending runway into second half of 2027
VS-7375 phase II studies initiated and first patients dosed in all three trials
summary: Verastem reported Q2 2026 net product revenues of $25.1 million, showing a meaningful rebound and quarter-over-quarter growth in CO-PACK adoption, with management confident in reaching self-sustainability for the LGSOC franchise by end of 2026. The company secured up to $75 million in non-dilutive royalty financing and a $15 million COPIKTRA milestone, extending cash runway into the second half of 2027. VS-7375 development progressed with completion of enrollment in dose expansion cohorts and initiation of three phase II registration-directed studies, with a data update expected in October. Non-GAAP adjusted net loss improved to $30.6 million versus $41.3 million in the prior year.

negative_highlights: Aurora adjusted EBITDA down 43% year-over-year, with full-year guidance lowered to $200-225 million
Memory chip cost impact increased to approximately $40 million, with limited visibility
positive_highlights: Aurora backlog remains strong at $470 million, with $200 million of orders received in July
DOCSIS 4.0 products now represent about 70% of Aurora revenue, with FDX deployment with Comcast going well
Completed RUCKUS sale for $1.846 billion, enabling a $5 per share special distribution and an unlevered balance sheet
summary: Vistance Networks' Q2 FY2026 results showed net sales of $320 million, down 1% year-over-year, with adjusted EBITDA of $36 million, down 32%, and adjusted EPS of $0.12, down 8%. The Aurora segment saw revenue of $319 million (down 1%) and EBITDA of $46 million (down 43%), which was in line with expectations but impacted by memory chip issues and stranded costs. Full-year Aurora EBITDA guidance was lowered to $200-225 million, and the company announced a $5 per share special distribution from the RUCKUS sale proceeds of $1.846 billion. Management highlighted a strong DOCSIS 4.0 position and order strength with $200 million received in July, but cited customer upgrade delays and limited visibility on memory chip costs.

negative_highlights: Profitability was heavily aided by the one-time Dedeaux land sale; excluding it, recurring operations were only modestly profitable, and a shareholder challenged that the company would still be losing money without the sale.
Farm and ranch operations still do not earn an adequate return by management's own admission, with the farm profitable only before fixed water obligations.
Centennial's timeline beyond this year's county hearings is unquantifiable, with renewal of litigation flagged as an uncertain impediment; no construction start date given.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA grew approximately 47% YoY and TTM adjusted EBITDA reached $29.8 million, up 21% from a year ago.
Net income of $2.6 million ($0.10/share) versus a $1.7 million loss a year ago; management noted profitability held even excluding the $2 million Dedeaux land-sale profit.

Expenses excluding cost and sales on land and water declined nearly 18% year-to-date, with segment expenses outside corporate and Terra Vista down roughly 8%; balance sheet at ~$79 million liquidity and 16.3% debt-to-capital.
summary: Tejon Ranch reported Q2 FY2026 net income of $2.6 million ($0.10 per share) versus a $1.7 million loss a year ago, a $4.3 million swing, with revenue up across all segments and adjusted EBITDA up roughly 47% YoY. The Dedeaux Properties 1B land sale contributed $6.9 million of revenue and $2 million of recognized profit, with $3 million deferred against the retained JV interest. TTM adjusted EBITDA was $29.8 million, up 21%, and the company ended with ~$79 million of liquidity and a 16.3% debt-to-capital ratio. No quantitative forward guidance was given; management flagged continued work on Centennial entitlements and potential renewed litigation, and acknowledged the farm/ranch businesses have not earned an adequate return amid pointed shareholder criticism over stock price and capital allocation.

negative_highlights: Distribution expenses rose significantly to $118.8 million (4.7% of sales) due to higher freight and fuel costs.
note expenses increased substantially to $269.2 million (10.6% of net sales), reflecting heavy investments in marketing, sponsorships like the UFC fight at the White House, and digital campaigns.
Aluminum can costs are expected to see a continued modest sequential increase through the end of 2026 due to Midwest premiums.
positive_highlights: Net sales crossed the $2.5 billion threshold for the first time in company history with a 20.2% YoY increase.
Monster Energy drinks segment grew 21.6% to $2.36 billion, while international net sales surged 34.6%. The Ultra brand family grew 19% and Juice Monster increased 26% in the U.S.
Gross profit margin expanded 20 bps to 55.9%, driven by pricing actions that partially offset aluminum cost increases.
summary: Monster Beverage reported Q2 FY26 net sales of $2.54 billion, a 20.2% increase year-over-year driven by double-digit growth across all regions and the Monster Energy drinks segment rising 21.6%. Gross margin expanded slightly to 55.9%, supported by pricing actions that offset higher aluminum costs and freight expenses. Management raised July sales estimates on an FX-adjusted basis excluding alcohol, citing strong international performance.

negative_highlights: Full-year LOE expense raised to $10.30 per BOE due to production enhancement initiatives and higher workover costs
Net premium on Bakken crude expected to fade over the course of the year as differentials normalize below WTI
positive_highlights: Adjusted free cash flow of $414 million exceeded expectations
Oil production came in at the high end of guidance driven by four-mile program execution (26 wells executed)
Balance sheet grew to $612 million with normalized leverage declining below one-half turn
summary: Chord Energy reported Q2 FY26 results with oil production at the high end of guidance and adjusted free cash flow of $414 million exceeding expectations. Management raised full-year volume guidance by 2,000 bpd due to investments in low-cost base production initiatives while maintaining capital spending outlooks essentially unchanged despite dropping a frac crew later in the year.

negative_highlights: Pressure restrictions from Milepost 171 incident to be lifted through 2026 into 2027
Growth capital outlook increased for development activities
Permit durability remains a key requirement, not yet finalized
positive_highlights: Record throughput on U.S. Gulf Coast segment; strong demand for connectivity
Increased full-year normalized EBITDA guidance to CAD 1.04 billion
Open season secured 465,000 bpd of 20-year customer commitments
summary: South Bow reported strong Q2 2026 results, with record throughput on the U.S. Gulf Coast segment and raised full-year normalized EBITDA guidance to CAD 1.04 billion (within a 2% range) and distributable cash flow guidance to CAD 665 million (within 2%). Leverage improved to 4.4x net debt to EBITDA, and the board approved a CAD 0.50 quarterly dividend. Management highlighted the successful open season securing 465,000 bpd of 20-year commitments, advancing Prairie Connector and Liberty Bridge projects toward a mid-2027 FID, and noted pressure restrictions on Keystone are expected to be lifted in phases through 2026 and 2027.

negative_highlights: GAAP gross margin contracted slightly to 7.3% from 7.5%, driven by scaled payments to publishers for Carrot Ads.
Q2 GAAP net income declined 4% YoY primarily due to a timing shift in stock-based compensation vesting dates, not operational weakness.
positive_highlights: GTV grew 14% YoY with orders up 9%, outpacing order growth via deepening customer engagement and AOV increase of 4% to $115.
Advertising and other revenue accelerated to +16% YoY, significantly outperforming GTV growth at a rate of 2.9% investment.
Operating cash flow surged 143% YoY to $493 million, supported by strong collections and efficiency gains.
summary: Instacart reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $1.04 billion (up 14% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $313 million (up 19% YoY), driven by GTV growth of 14%. Management raised the midpoint for both GTV ($10.425B, +14%) and adjusted EBITDA ($330M, +19%) guidance for Q3 FY26 while widening the ranges to reflect increased scale.

negative_highlights: Total revenue growth only 0.9% constant currency; customer support revenue down 4.6% YoY
ARR up only 0.2% YoY
FY2027 guidance (core revenue +2%-3%) implies modest growth, with no acceleration expected

Core cloud revenue up 8.9% constant currency, with 64 cloud deals >$1M, up 49% YoY
Non-GAAP diluted EPS up 26.8% and gross margin up 220 basis points
summary: OpenText reported Q4 FY2026 total revenue of $1.35 billion, up 2.9% YoY (0.9% constant currency), with core portfolio revenue up 5.3% (3.1% cc) and cloud revenue up 6.0% (4.3% cc). Core cloud revenue grew 8.9% cc, and enterprise cloud bookings rose 24.1% YoY, above the 16%-20% target. Adjusted EBITDA margin was 37.1%, non-GAAP EPS was $1.23 (up 26.8%), and operating cash flow was $186 million (up 17.5%). Management guided FY2027 core revenue growth of 2%-3% and cloud revenue growth of 8%-10%, calling FY2027 a 'foundation year' with investments in sales capacity and ecosystem partnerships.

negative_highlights: GAAP net loss widened to $10.0 million ($0.22/share) from $8.3 million ($0.18) in Q1
GAAP operating expenses rose to $10.6 million from $8.9 million, with non-GAAP opex at $8.2 million vs $7.4 million
Cash and securities declined to $71.5 million from $77.2 million, and H2 cash use is expected to run above H1
positive_highlights: Revenue rose to $202,000, ~9x YoY and ~100% QoQ, the fourth consecutive quarter of growth
First-half revenue of $303,000 already exceeds full-year 2025 revenue of $233,000
New $30,000 contract development revenue line (customer-funded aerospace/defense engineering) launched this quarter
summary: AEYE reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $202,000, ~9x the $22,000 in Q2 2025 and roughly double Q1's $101,000, with first-half revenue of $303,000 already exceeding full-year 2025 revenue of $233,000. GAAP net loss was $10.0 million ($0.22/share) versus $8.3 million ($0.18) in Q1, as operating expenses rose to $10.6 million on stock-based comp and pre-ramp engineering costs; cash fell to $71.5 million from $77.2 million. The company reaffirmed its 2026 full-year cash use outlook of $30-35 million but did not provide revenue guidance, instead pointing to continued quarter-over-quarter growth, a 25-customer program base, and an expected production ramp in the second half. New proof points included selection as preferred lidar vendor for sports analytics provider Alive3D, a third consecutive paid defense order, and $30,000 in contract development revenue, a new revenue line.

negative_highlights: NAV declined sequentially from $11.02 to $10.94 driven primarily by net unrealized depreciation on select investments.
Net realized losses were recorded during the quarter, associated with restructuring activity and legacy portfolio investments.
Management noted heightened investor scrutiny around redemption activity in non-traded perpetual BDCs and AI-related disruption concerns.

Termination of legacy Sierra Credit Support Agreement freed approximately $67 million for redeployment into new assets.
Credit quality improved quarter-over-quarter with non-accruals not covered by CSA at only 0.2%.
summary: Barings BDC reported Q2 FY2026 net investment income of $0.28 per share and NAV of $10.94, which declined sequentially from the prior quarter due to unrealized depreciation on select investments despite earnings exceeding the dividend. The company successfully terminated a legacy credit support agreement freeing approximately $67 million for redeployment while maintaining leverage at 1.18x within its target range. Management noted that private credit behavior is becoming more rational with reduced capital chasing, though they remain selective and cautious regarding sectors like software due to AI-related market noise.

Full-year FX-neutral subscription revenue guidance reduced to low single-digit growth
Remainder of subscription revenue (ex-growth drivers) declined modestly FX neutral due to weak consumption and mix

CX Platform saw average sales cycles decline more than 50% and implementation time cut from 30 days to one week
summary: VTEX reported Q2 2026 subscription revenue of $63.8 million, up 11% in USD and 1.3% FX neutral, coming in just above the bottom of guidance. GMV grew 18% in USD and 7% FX neutral. Profitability was strong with non-GAAP operating income up 62% and free cash flow up 79%. Management lowered full-year FX-neutral subscription revenue guidance to low single-digit growth, citing macro headwinds in Brazil and Argentina and a mix shift to larger accounts.

Personal Auto profitability is constrained by high concentration in California requiring double-digit rate increases and slowing new business growth.

Life business generated $18 million of net operating income supported by growth in earned premiums and favorable mortality experience.
summary: Kemper reported a net loss of $464.8 million ($7.90 per share) driven by a non-cash goodwill impairment of $460 million and an allowance for credit losses on surplus notes; adjusted consolidated net operating income was $26.3 million, reflecting sequential improvement in underlying P&C underwriting performance but being offset by prior year reserve development in Commercial Auto ($17.7M). Management emphasized that restoring profitability is the top priority over growth, citing a need to tighten underwriting and take additional rate actions despite strong underlying combined ratios.

Adjusted EBITDA for Q3 expected in a wide range of $1M-$7M, down significantly from the prior quarter's $13.8M

Awarded Joint Laser Weapon System contract with a ceiling exceeding $600 million
Defense segment grew 72% year-over-year driven by HELSI-2 and munitions programs
summary: nLIGHT reported record Q2 FY26 revenue of $83 million (up 34% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $11 million, beating expectations with strong growth in defense products (+72% YoY). Management raised the ceiling on a new Joint Laser Weapon System contract to over $600 million while maintaining progress on HELSI-2. However, Q3 revenue guidance was lowered due to supply chain constraints affecting commercial optics from Chinese suppliers.

Management remains cautious regarding software exposure (18% of portfolio) citing rapid market changes, despite it being their best-performing sector.

positive_highlights: Q4 revenue grew 43% YoY; adjusted EBITDA up 87% YoY with 270 bps margin expansion

The home services vertical, boosted by HomeBuddy, grew 88% YoY, while financial services grew 24% with auto insurance up 37%.

negative_highlights: NII net provisions were flat at 3.5%, reflecting higher cost of risk from government lines (FGI/FGO) and legacy cohorts.
Fee and commission income growth slowed to just 1.7% year-over-year compared to double-digit revenue growth in other segments.
positive_highlights: Net income grew 16.2% year-over-year to BRL 7.1 billion with ROAE of 16.2%, exceeding market expectations.

Insurance group operating result grew 8.3% year-over-year to reach a net income of BRL 2.9 billion.
summary: BBDO reported Q2 FY2026 net income of BRL 7.1 billion (up 16.2% YoY) and total revenue of BRL 37.6 billion (up 10.3% YoY), driven by loan portfolio growth of 11.6%. The bank raised its full-year guidance for the insurance group to a range of 6%-8%, citing strong H1 performance, while noting that NII net provisions are expected to be slightly below the midpoint due to higher baselines in government lines.

negative_highlights: International volumes were lower due to Middle East disruptions
Sulfur sales could see delays or disruption due to Middle East freight volatility
Waha to Gulf Coast spread normalization may reduce midstream gas marketing income

Midstream and marketing adjusted earnings of ~$960 million, a new quarterly record
summary: Occidental reported Q2 2026 adjusted EPS of $2.40, with production of 1.43 million BOE/d, exceeding the midpoint of guidance by 23,000 BOE/d. Free cash flow was approximately $3 billion, the highest since Q3 2022, and midstream and marketing set a new record with adjusted earnings of about $960 million. The company reduced principal debt to $11.8 billion, raised the dividend by 8%, and reaffirmed a plan to add over $4 billion of annual sustainable cash flow by 2030, with approximately 85% achievable at lower prices. Guidance reflects expectations for normalized Waha/Gulf Coast spreads partially offset by upstream price improvements, while Middle East disruptions could impact sulfur sales and freight costs.

negative_highlights: Q3 LOE expected to rise to $73-$81M from $72M

Surety lawsuit outcomes uncertain; potential damages not assured

summary: Stoneridge reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $181 million, up over 15% YoY but only ~8% on a core basis after excluding ~$4 million FX and $7 million of Mexico Manufacturing Agreement revenue tied to the Control Devices sale; MirrorEye hit a record $37 million (+39% YoY) and Brazil reached a record $20.5 million (+38%). Full-year 2026 guidance was reaffirmed at $645-670 million revenue and $20-25 million Adjusted EBITDA, with Q3 and Q4 revenue expected modestly below Q2 on normal seasonality while EBITDA should improve sequentially. The key change versus the prior quarter is incrementally positive demand commentary—IHS now forecasts 5.5% OEM end-market growth in 2026 versus 1.8% at the May call—though management balanced this against macro and geopolitical uncertainty.

Unexpected Wren Kitchens bankruptcy impacted occupancy, though settlement income was received.

New lease cash spreads year-to-date nearly 30% and expected to exceed 20% for the year.

The company raised its full-year FFO guidance by $0.02 to $1.50-$1.54 per share and increased the low end of same-property NOI guidance to 3.25%. Leasing activity remains robust with new lease cash spreads of 13% in the quarter and nearly 30% year-to-date, though shop occupancy dipped to 91.7% due to strategic recaptures and the Wren Kitchens bankruptcy. Capital recycling continued with acquisitions in Virginia and Massachusetts funded by asset sales, and management expressed confidence in continued rent growth driven by limited supply and strong demand.

summary: ISG reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $65.5 million, up 6.4% YoY (7% ex-FX per regional detail), and adjusted EBITDA of $9.4 million, up 12.9%, with margin expanding 80 bps to 14.3%; operating income rose 25.6% to $5.9 million for an 8.9% margin. Both revenue and EBITDA were above management's expectations and were the best since 2023, with AI-related revenue up 64% to $26 million (37% of first-half revenue) and record recurring revenue of $30 million. Q3 guidance was set at $63.5–64.5 million revenue and $8.5–9.5 million adjusted EBITDA, lower sequentially on European summer seasonality. The board authorized a new $30 million buyback, the largest in company history, and gross debt/EBITDA fell to 1.7x from 1.9x at year-end.

negative_highlights: Sustaining capital at Gibraltar elevated at CAD 48 million in H1 2026
Gibraltar cathode production lower due to SX/EW electrical issues
Florence C1 cost of $4.72/lb not indicative of future; fixed costs high during ramp-up
positive_highlights: Revenue of CAD 331 million was the highest ever for Trekor
Adjusted EBITDA of CAD 125 million and operating cash flow of CAD 183 million

Florence produced over 5 million lbs of cathode in its first full production quarter, while Gibraltar produced 30 million lbs; the company maintained annual guidance. Management expressed confidence in ramp-up progress and highlighted strong copper prices and a contracted negative TC of -CAD 140/t for 2027, while noting cost pressures and higher sustaining capital.

summary: RXO reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $1.8 billion, adjusted EBITDA of $40 million (above the high end of guidance), and adjusted EPS of $0.06. Brokerage volume grew 2% YoY, with truckload spot mix up 900 bps sequentially to 42% and truckload gross profit per load up 11% sequentially, the largest gain in four years. Last mile stops grew 3%, and managed transportation won ~$100 million in freight under management. Management guided to continued brokerage volume and gross profit per load growth in Q3, but expects weakening in last mile. Free cash flow was -$42 million due to working capital, expected to convert strongly in Q3.

negative_highlights: Quarter described as 'quiet' with no major business updates
Launch pace for brepocitinib expected to be 'slow and steady'
Continued litigation uncertainty with Pfizer and BioNTech
positive_highlights: Phase III cutaneous sarcoidosis study enrollment initiated ahead of schedule
Received $950M upfront payment from Moderna settlement, with $770M to Genevant
Cash position strong at ~$4B before receiving settlement funds
summary: Roivant reported a quiet Q1 FY2027 with $200M R&D expense, ~$100M non-GAAP G&A, and cash just under $4B before receiving $772M from Moderna's settlement. The company initiated Phase III for cutaneous sarcoidosis ahead of schedule, with top-line data expected in 2028. Management reiterated readiness for brepocitinib launch in dermatomyositis by end of September and expects a busy second half with multiple readouts. They continue share repurchases, having bought back ~$200M in the quarter at average high-$20s per share.

negative_highlights: $176 million one-time non-cash impairment charge recognized for capitalized development expenses on discontinued ATJ-60 project in South Dakota.
GAAP net loss of $177 million ($0.75/share) due to the significant impairment and severance charges.
Gross margin contracted slightly from 44% YoY despite revenue growth.

Revenue grew 7% YoY despite planned maintenance downtime at the North Dakota facility.
Canada Clean Fuel Regulation (CFR) pathway approved retroactively, unlocking access to a >1 billion gallon compliance market starting Q3.
summary: Gevo reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $47 million (up 7% YoY) and gross profit of $20 million on a margin of 43%. Management raised its full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance from the prior estimate of ~$30 million to more than $60 million.

negative_highlights: Full-year EBITDA margin guidance implies a slight step-down to ~29.7%, driven by normalizing contract mix from cost-plus acquisitions rather than operational weakness.

positive_highlights: Revenue beat consensus with sequential growth of 20.4% and year-over-year organic growth of 24.4%.
Backlog reached a record $1.3 billion, up 65% from the prior fiscal year end.
Bookings in Q2 totaled nearly $500 million across all end markets.
summary: Karman Space & Defense reported record Q2 FY26 results with revenue of $182 million (up 58% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $55 million (up 55% YoY). The company raised its full-year 2026 guidance to a range of $730-$745 million in revenue, citing strong visibility from a record backlog. Management reaffirmed expectations for 25% or higher organic growth and highlighted the conversion of contingent supply agreements into firm contracts.

negative_highlights: The software practice within investment banking continued to face headwinds due to AI-related disruption concerns in that specific sector.
positive_highlights: Record second quarter revenue of $226 million representing a 51% year-over-year increase and 43% sequential growth.
Investment banking revenues surged 56% to $178 million, driven by double-digit growth across M&A, capital advisory, Private Funds Advisory, portfolio valuations, and transaction opinions.
Non-compensation expense grew only high single digits for the full year despite significant revenue expansion, demonstrating strong operating leverage.

Adjusted operating margin was 20%, with investment banking revenues up 56% and valuation/opinions revenues up 35%. Management raised the full-year guidance for non-compensation expense to high single-digit growth, citing strong leverage from top-line expansion.

Higher sales force costs are expected to continue for the next couple of quarters, creating a headwind.
Healthcare case volumes eased from Q1 in both one- and two-year stack basis.

Independent restaurant case growth of 5.1% was the strongest since Q4 2023, with 21st consecutive quarter of share gains.
Pronto sales outlook raised to $1.3 billion for 2026 and $1.7 billion for 2027, up from prior estimates.
summary: US Foods delivered record adjusted EBITDA of $604 million, up 10%, with adjusted EBITDA margin expanding 29 basis points to a record 5.7%. Adjusted EPS grew 21%. Independent restaurant case growth reached 5.1%, the strongest since Q4 2023, with 21st consecutive quarter of share gains. The company raised Pronto sales guidance to $1.3 billion for 2026 and $1.7 billion for 2027, up from prior estimates. Management remains confident in achieving over $300 million in cost savings by 2027, with $50 million already realized in H1 2026.

Softer new residential construction activity expected in Q4

WMS adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 650 bps to a record 28.1%

WMS led growth with sales up 10.3% and EBITDA margin up 650 bps to 28.1%, and specialty valves are seeing traction in industrial water/data centers.

negative_highlights: Automotive revenue declined in high single digits due to weakness in Europe, though nearly flat YTD
Europe region saw a decline of 15% YoY (low single digits excluding procurement entity changes)
Memory price headwinds expected to impact gross margins by approximately 75 basis points in Q3
positive_highlights: Record quarterly revenue reached a new high for the company
Adjusted EPS grew 80% year-over-year to $0.45 driven by operating leverage
Semiconductor segment delivered exceptional double-digit growth across all geographies
summary: Cognex reported record Q2 revenue of $314 million (up 17% YoY) and adjusted EPS growth of 80%, driven by strong performance in semiconductor, electronics, and logistics segments. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance for nearly all end markets to double-digit or high single-digit growth ranges, citing favorable demand environments and successful execution of cost reduction initiatives which delivered approximately $35 million in annualized net reductions. The company highlighted record quarterly revenue, margin expansion with adjusted EBITDA margins reaching 32.2%, and robust free cash flow conversion.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EPS growth in Q4 was only 6.1% due to a lower tax provision in the prior year.
FY2026 EPS was negatively impacted by $120M in additional interest and tax expense.
Revenue guidance includes $500M acquired growth, implying organic growth lower than total.
positive_highlights: Record performance with revenue growth of 17.6% in Q4 and 10.9% for FY2026, exceeding expectations.
EBITDA margin expansion of 110 bps to 12.3% and free cash flow per share up 68%.
Raised fiscal 2027 guidance with revenue growth over 11%, EBITDA margin in high 12% range, and at least $900M free cash flow.
summary: CACI reported Q4 and FY2026 with record revenue, EBITDA margin, and free cash flow. Q4 revenue was $2.7B (+17.6% YoY, 11.6% organic), EBITDA margin 13% (up 150 bps), adjusted EPS $8.91 (+6.1%), and free cash flow $233M. Full-year revenue grew 10.9%, EBITDA margin 12.3%, free cash flow $735M (up 68% per share), and contract awards exceeded $10B. Fiscal 2027 guidance calls for revenue growth of 11.3%-13.4%, high-12% EBITDA margin, adjusted EPS of $32.96-$33.86, and free cash flow of at least $900M. Executives highlighted strength in electronic warfare, space, and counter-UAS, with the $500M Domestic Shield award and a classified counterspace win. Leverage reduced to 3.7x and expected to reach low-3s by June 2027.

negative_highlights: Supply Chain Services sales were flat (+0.6%) due to decreased activity with certain existing customers.
SG&A expenses increased by $15.7 million YoY, though operating leverage helped offset this in the margin calculation.
Management declined to provide specific Q3 guidance or confirm if 12% margins are sustainable beyond mix effects.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to 12.2%, a new high watermark up from 11.5% last year.
Innovative Pumping Solutions sales surged 52.6% YoY driven by water and wastewater activity, reaching $142.7 million.
Free cash flow turned positive at $29.8 million for the quarter after negative FCF in H1 FY2025.
summary: DXP reported Q2 FY2026 sales of $576.5 million (up 15.6% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA margins expanding to a new high watermark of 12.2%. The company generated strong free cash flow of $29.8 million for the quarter, reversing prior year negative trends through reduced CapEx and improved profitability.

negative_highlights: NAV declined 10.4% due to the portfolio sale at a 5% discount plus transaction costs
Quarterly NAV fell 2.1% due to markdowns at Pluralsight, PVHC, and Zilliant
Net investment income per share of $0.22 was modest relative to dividend of $0.17

Management announced a major portfolio sale to a continuation vehicle at a 5% discount, reducing NAV by 10.4% but cutting net leverage to ~0.4x, and initiated a strategic review with KBW. Repayment activity was strong, and the Domo sale is expected to repay $69 million in Q4.

negative_highlights: NUCYNTA franchise net revenue was lower than expected, down 24% year-over-year due to pricing for authorized generic products.
Total product revenue guidance lowered from prior expectations of approximately $850-$925 million (implied) to a new range of $825-$855 million.
positive_highlights: JORNAY prescriptions grew by 13.1% year-over-year with prescribers reaching an all-time high of over 30,000 healthcare providers.
AZSTARYS acquisition integration is complete and revenues beat consensus expectations for a partial quarter at $12.9 million.
BELBUCA revenue increased 10% year-over-year to $57.7 million.
summary: Collegium reported Q2 FY26 net product revenues of $199.9 million (up 6% YoY), driven by a 41% increase in JORNAY revenue to $46.1M and initial AZSTARYS sales, partially offset by lower NUCYNTA franchise revenue due to authorized generic pricing dynamics. Management raised full-year guidance for the ADHD portfolio while lowering total product revenue expectations from prior levels of approximately $850-925 million (implied) to a new range of $825-$855 million, citing specifically lower pain portfolio net revenue.

negative_highlights: Heavy capital spending does not commence until February/March 2027, meaning Q3 FY26 cash flow will remain driven by exploration rather than production.
Resource statement for Patterson Corridor East is delayed pending further drilling results to define the high-grade subdomains and overall footprint.
positive_highlights: Completed all planned key construction milestones on schedule and within budget, validating conservative cost estimates despite industry inflation pressures.

Executed a new term sheet to note an additional 1.3 million pounds of uranium at spot price exposure, bringing total contracted volume under negotiation for up to 20 million pounds with global utilities.
Confirmed strong market demand with the five-year forward uranium price sitting at $105/lb and spot prices stabilizing around a new floor of $85.
summary: NexGen Energy provided a construction update for Q2 FY2026 rather than financial earnings results, reporting that all planned key milestones were completed to scope and budget within the CAD 2.2 billion project guidance established in August 2024. The company executed a term sheet to watch an additional 1.3 million pounds of uranium at spot price exposure during the quarter while maintaining strong liquidity with over CAD 970 million available for construction financing options including prepayments.

negative_highlights: Reported diluted EPS only $0.09 due to $23 million in charges from fraudulent loan repurchases
Net income down 10% in capital markets segment due to mix shift to brokered lending
Additional $12-16 million expected in Q3 for Fannie Mae review completion
positive_highlights: Transaction volumes up 3% YoY to $14.4 billion, debt financing up 8% to $12.5 billion
Adjusted core EPS increased 3% to $1.19, excluding repurchase-related charges
GSE market share up 350 basis points to nearly 15% year to date
summary: Walker & Dunlop's Q2 FY2026 core business grew modestly with transaction volumes up 3% to $14.4 billion and adjusted core EPS up 3% to $1.19, but reported diluted EPS was $0.09 due to $23 million in charges related to fraudulent loan repurchases. Management confirmed Freddie Mac's investigation is complete and expects $12-16 million additional charges in Q3 for Fannie Mae, with no further repurchases expected. Guidance for the year was not formally revised but management expressed confidence in core earnings excluding these charges, with GSE market share up to 15% and $114 billion in remaining GSE capacity.

negative_highlights: Natural gas prices fell significantly due to widening regional differentials
Adjusted G&A increased to $2.7M, though low among peers
Uncertainty around new Cherokee test well and potential stacked pay opportunity
positive_highlights: Revenue up 48% YoY and adjusted EBITDA up 49% YoY

Continued shareholder returns with $5.05 per share in dividends since 2023
summary: SandRidge reported record Q2 FY2026 results with revenue up 48% YoY to $51M, adjusted EBITDA up 49% to $34M, and net income of $27M ($0.72/share). Production grew 11% YoY (22% oil growth), driven by higher oil prices and the Cherokee drilling program. The company announced a bolt-on acquisition in the Cherokee Play, continues to pay dividends, and maintains a strong balance sheet with no debt. Guidance for 2026 remains intact with $76-97M capex and 10 wells planned.

negative_highlights: Management expects modest compression in Title margins for H2 due to front-loaded recruiting expenses and tuck-in acquisitions.
Residential purchase volumes remain at historically low levels (~4M annual pace) driven by elevated mortgage rates, limiting near-term growth potential.
positive_highlights: Adjusted net earnings beat prior year by $52M, with Title segment earnings up 33% YoY to $448 million.
Commercial revenue reached a record pace for H1 at $778 million (up 24%), driven by strong order volumes across industrial and multifamily sectors.
Title adjusted pre-tax margin expanded significantly to an industry-leading 17.8% from 15.5% in the prior year.
summary: FNF reported Q2 FY26 adjusted net earnings of $370 million ($1.39/share), beating the prior year's $318 million driven by a 33% increase in Title segment pre-tax earnings to $448 million and strong commercial revenue growth up 24%. The company returned approximately $195 million to shareholders via dividends and buybacks while maintaining an adjusted pre-tax title margin of 17.8%, though management noted modest compression is expected in the second half due to recruiting costs.

negative_highlights: Europe delivered only mid-single-digit growth, with traffic pressured by macro and tourism slowdown
Full-year outlook remains prudent on Europe due to macroeconomic uncertainty
Tariff and higher labor/material costs partially offset margin expansion
positive_highlights: Revenue increased 13%, ahead of mid to high single-digit outlook
Gross margin expanded 130 basis points to 73.6%
Full-year outlook raised after Q1 over-delivery
summary: Q1 FY2027 revenue grew 13% in constant currency, exceeding the mid-to-high single-digit outlook, with Asia up 25%, North America up 13%, and Europe up 5%. Adjusted gross margin expanded 130 basis points to 73.6%, and AUR increased 15%. The company raised its full-year outlook while maintaining caution on Europe due to macro uncertainty. New customer acquisition was 1.5 million in DTC, and core product sales grew mid-teens.

negative_highlights: Red Sea hostilities forced ships to reroute via the Suez Canal and exit high-risk zones, reducing fleet efficiency
Spot supply remains tightly constrained following major consolidation by a private aggregator earlier in the year
Second-hand asset values are currently at premium levels making it challenging for DHT to acquire additional tonnage
positive_highlights: Q2 revenue reached $255 million on TCE basis with adjusted EBITDA of $231 million
