Fleet secured two additional one-year time charter contracts at an average rate of $109,000 per day for older vessels
summary: DHT Holdings reported Q2 FY2026 revenues of $255 million and adjusted EBITDA of $231 million, marking the company's strongest quarter in history with net income reaching a record $198.3 million ($1.23 per share). Management raised full-year guidance expectations by citing strong market conditions driven by geopolitical disruptions that expanded ton-mile demand while maintaining conservative leverage and robust liquidity. The board approved a quarterly cash dividend of $1.22 per share, continuing its streak of 66 consecutive payouts.

negative_highlights: Management confirmed that full-year earnings guidance is being reevaluated and will likely be lower due to reduced gain-on-sale revenue.
Net Interest Margin (NIM) contracted significantly at the holding company level as operations moved into the bank, where interest income replaces securitization gains.

Tangible book value per share has grown 75.3% over the last 12 quarters since converting to a financial holding company structure.
summary: NewtekOne reported Q2 FY2026 results where net interest income grew significantly to $25 million from the prior year period due to a shift of operations into Newtek Bank and increased SBA loan holdings. However, management explicitly stated that guidance for full-year earnings is being reevaluated as they transition away from gain-on-sale revenue toward stable net interest income. Consequently, forward-looking EPS targets previously cited ($0.79-$0.89) are no longer supported in the current quarter's outlook.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to $18 million from $8 million year-over-year due to higher clinical trial costs and personnel expenses
R&D expenses increased significantly to $16 million compared to $7.9 million in the prior period
No financial guidance provided for revenue or cash burn rate

Atopic dermatitis Phase I data showed strong efficacy, with 75% of patients achieving EASI-75 in Cohort 4 versus 20% placebo
No significant safety issues or disease rebound observed after treatment cessation
summary: Corvus Pharmaceuticals reported a net loss of $18 million for Q2 FY2026 compared to an $8 million loss in the prior year period, driven by increased R&D expenses and stock compensation. The company maintains cash reserves sufficient to fund operations into Q2 2028 following a recent capital raise. Management provided clinical updates on soquelitinib but did not offer any financial guidance or revenue projections.

negative_highlights: Total revenue missed expectations due to a decline in equipment sales and legacy ATG service pressure
Full-year guidance was lowered on both top-line EBITDA and free cash flow metrics
Galileo FDX STC approvals for mid-to-large airframes are coming online slower than anticipated
positive_highlights: Military and government service revenue surged +40% YoY driven by geopolitical demand

5G unit shipments accelerated significantly to 138 units in the quarter
summary: Gogo reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $222.8 million (down 1% YoY) and a net loss of -$2 million compared to prior year profit, driven by lower equipment sales ($31.5M vs expectations). Digital-only subscription revenue grew for the second consecutive quarter and digital other revenue also grew, but content licensing was lumpy and search-driven traffic declined. Management reaffirmed full-year guidance, expecting improved revenue trends, EBITDA and margin expansion, and fourth consecutive year of free cash flow growth, with a goal of becoming majority digital in the back half of 2026.

Restructuring charges of $151 million impacted the quarter's net income and GAAP profitability.

summary: Cloudflare reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $696.1 million, a 36% year-over-year increase driven by record large customer additions and accelerating growth in the Workers developer platform. Operating income rose to $96.1 million (non-GAAP margin 13.8%) with gross margins expanding sequentially for the first time in eight quarters to 73.1%. Management raised full-year revenue guidance expectations, citing strong momentum across all product lines and customer cohorts.

G&P results slightly offset by commodity price sensitivity

The company continues its deleveraging strategy with net debt leverage reduced to 0.8x and expects stronger production in the second half.

negative_highlights: U.S.-based revenue remained flat or slightly down, primarily attributed to the company assuming last year's run rate for EOCL contracts.

Management reaffirmed full-year guidance for revenue between $130M-$150M and adjusted EBITDA between $12M-$24M, citing strong momentum from Gen-3 scaling.

Operating expense ratio decreased to 47 basis points at quarter-end, continuing a multi-year trend of scale benefits.

Management highlighted strong core retail sales momentum but noted that alternative investment returns were below the long-term target, with Q2 annualized returns at approximately 5.9%. The company executed significant capital return activities including share repurchases of 4.5 million shares and dividends paid from self-funded capital.

FDA granted Fast Track designation for lifileucel in undifferentiated pleomorphic sarcoma and dedifferentiated liposarcoma.
summary: Iovance reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $99.3 million (up 66% YoY), driven by record Amtagvi sales of approximately $91 million which exceeded the guidance range of $79M-$81M. Gross margin expanded to an all-time high of 56%, up from 41% in Q1, while R&D expenses decreased for a fourth consecutive quarter. Management declined to provide specific full-year revenue guidance but confirmed they are reviewing their previously issued range and expect to announce updated figures during the third quarter.

Oncology progress remains preclinical or early-stage with no specific licensing timelines provided, relying on partner experimentation.

Combined GAAP R&D/SG&A expense guidance improved by $10 million, with a target of achieving non-GAAP P&L profitability as early as 2028.
Sanofi partnership confirmed intent to be among first movers in combination vaccine market; Phase III study initiation could trigger a $125M milestone payment.
summary: Novavax reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $57 million (down from $239M prior year due to a one-time milestone in the comparison period) and an adjusted net loss driven by R&D expenses. Management raised its full-year 2026 guidance for non-GAAP total revenues ($235-$275M midpoint increase of $5M) and combined GAAP R&D/SG&A expenses (midpoint reduction to $390M). The company reiterated a three-year expense framework targeting profitability by 2028, citing cost reductions and strong partner momentum as key drivers.

negative_highlights: Revenue dropped sharply from $28.9M in Q2 FY25 due to absence of licensing revenue this quarter

ZYNQUISTA NDA resubmission delayed slightly, now anticipated for Q4 2026
positive_highlights: SONATA-HCM trial completed enrollment and was significantly over-enrolled

The company recorded a net loss of $31.8 million ($0.07/share) driven by R&D expenses rising to $17.4 million primarily due to the SONATA-HCM trial and an early debt extinguishment charge of $4.3 million. summary: Encompass Health reported Q2 FY2026 revenue growth of 9.6% and adjusted EBITDA increase of 9.2%, driven by discharge volume growth and higher net revenue per discharge due to increased patient acuity. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance for both operating revenue ($6.41B-$6.49B) and adjusted EPS ($6.02-$6.25), citing strong capacity additions, favorable ePOB trends, and a successful admit-and-appeal strategy with an 89% success rate on Medicare Advantage denials.

negative_highlights: R&D expenses increased slightly due to timing differences and lower external spending on small molecule programs (offset by launch investments)
note, general, and administrative expenses rose $4M YoY primarily reflecting commercial launch support costs

positive_highlights: $3.6M net product revenue in first full commercial quarter

>50% of covered lives secured for AVLAYAH with high physician awareness
summary: Denali Therapeutics reported Q2 FY26 net product revenue of $3.6 million from its first full commercial quarter for AVLAYAH in Hunter syndrome. Management raised guidance for the following quarter (Q3) to a range of $10-$12 million, citing strong physician engagement and payer access exceeding 50% coverage. Operating expenses were flat compared to the prior year period despite launch investments.

negative_highlights: Total revenue declined significantly year-over-year from $107.4 million due to no flight equipment sales.
Overall gross margin contracted sharply to 22.9% compared to 32.9% last year, exacerbated by startup costs at new facilities.
MRO facility utilization remains low (Goodyear under 20%, Millington ramping up), delaying the realization of operating leverage.

Tech Ops revenue increased nearly 9% to $33.8 million due to the ramp-up of CRJ multi-line maintenance at Millington.
Secured a $35 million sale contract for a 737 aircraft to the U.S. Marshals Service, expected to close in Q4.

Management maintains that these results reflect timing rather than trajectory, with guidance for the second half remaining unchanged but dependent on ramping up MRO capacity at Goodyear and Millington. The company expects meaningful improvement as stored Spirit aircraft are returned to service and new lease deliveries occur.

Website units (Dealer Inspire) continued to decline compared to the prior year as management shifts focus from volume expansion to product innovation.
Lower uptake of add-on dealer media products remained a near-term headwind partially offsetting core marketplace gains.

Marketplace revenue grew over 7% year-over-year, driven by dealer count growth and new Premium Plus package adoption.
Dealer Verified Listings launched successfully in June as an integrated trust signal connecting AccuTrade assets with consumer marketplace listings.
summary: Cars.com reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $179.9 million (up 1% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA margin expansion to 29.4%, beating the high end of guidance for a second consecutive quarter. Management reaffirmed full-year 2026 guidance with flat-to-2% revenue growth and margins between 29%-30%. While OEM/national revenue declined, strong marketplace performance (up 7%) and cost discipline drove profitability.

U.S. distribution expense rose to 11.9% of goods shipped from 11% on Hagerstown labor inefficiencies, with $2.2 million of non-recurring startup costs and ongoing Q3 disruption risk

positive_highlights: Recognized $40.1 million of IEEPA tariff refunds through COGS, with ~$36.4 million received in cash to date

International sales up 6.8% (5.3% local currency) to $13.4 million, segment gross margin up to 42.5% from 32.5%, and on track for pro forma breakeven in 2026
summary: Lifetime Brands reported Q2 FY2026 net sales up 7.4% to $141.6 million, with EPS of $0.87 GAAP and $1.18 adjusted versus a $0.12 adjusted loss a year ago; results were heavily distorted by a $40.1 million IEEPA tariff refund booked through cost of goods sold, lifting gross margin to 65.9% from 38.6%. Full-year net sales guidance was maintained at $650-$700 million while adjusted EBITDA guidance was raised to $90.5-$93 million (largely reflecting the refund offset by reinvestment), and management described the organic outlook as unchanged and the quarter as in line with expectations. Underlying demand remains soft, with core consumer durable categories down 2-3% on dollars and 7.5-10% on units per Circana, plus shipment timing delays and Hagerstown distribution center ramp-up disruption carried into Q3. Since Q1 the company repaid $40 million of term debt and has $151 million of liquidity, with a debt refinance in final stages.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA margin decreased approximately 90 basis points to 21% due to increased R&D investments and Endospan integration costs.
Free cash flow turned negative at -$12 million compared to +$11.7M in the prior year, impacted by $10.2M transaction bonuses for Endospan acquisition.

positive_highlights: Stent graft revenue accelerated to +12% YoY against a much tougher comparison, up from Q1's +10% growth.

summary: Artivion reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $125.8 million (up 9% constant currency) and adjusted EBITDA growth of approximately 7%, driven by stent graft acceleration (+12%) and On-X gains (+18%). Management reiterated full-year 2026 guidance for adjusted revenue between $480M-$496M and adjusted EBITDA between $92M-$99M, declining from prior expectations despite the strong quarter. The company cited a prudent decision to maintain conservatism in guidance due to timing shifts in preservation services (Q3) and ongoing integration costs associated with the Endospan acquisition.

negative_highlights: SCO pricing outlook is described as dependent on diesel draw and volatile forward curves, with management noting difficulty in predicting end-of-year levels.
positive_highlights: Adjusted net earnings hit all-time high of CAD $4.6 billion with adjusted funds flow reaching record levels at CAD $6.9 billion.
Total corporate production set a new company record averaging approximately 1,677,000 BOEs per day in Q2 FY26.
Oil sands mining and upgrading achieved the highest quarterly net back ever recorded at approximately CAD $78 per barrel.
summary: Canadian Natural reported record Q2 FY26 results with adjusted net earnings of CAD $4.6 billion (CAD $2.20/share) and funds flow of CAD $6.9 billion, driven by a historic production run rate averaging approximately 1.677 million BOEs per day. Management raised its full-year annual production guidance range to between 1.637 million and 1.682 million BOE/d (a 20k increase at the midpoint) while maintaining an unchanged capital program of CAD $6 billion before acquisitions. The company returned approximately CAD $4 billion in cash, including a quarterly dividend of CAD $0.525 per share.

negative_highlights: $298.8 million non-cash impairment charge recorded in the second quarter related to Lancaster and Plainville facilities classified as held for sale

Power costs remain a headwind year-over-year requiring pass-through adjustments
positive_highlights: AFFO per share of $0.35 came ahead of expectations for the fourth consecutive quarter

Economic occupancy grew year-over-year while churn remained low at 2.1%
summary: Americold Realty Trust reported Q2 FY26 AFFO per share of $0.35, beating analyst consensus for the fourth consecutive quarter and exceeding original expectations despite a non-cash impairment charge related to portfolio realignment. Management raised full-year AFFO guidance by $0.04 at the midpoint (to $1.26-$1.32) driven by physical occupancy gains of over 200 bps sequentially, pricing increases in storage and handling, and cost savings that offset wage inflation. The company is executing a strategic joint venture with EQT to delever its balance sheet while maintaining disciplined execution across five key priorities.

negative_highlights: Full-year royalty revenue guidance lowered to a range of $19-22M from the prior expectation of $20-23M due to potential generic market share thresholds in China
Commercial new patient starts declined 6% quarter-over-quarter despite overall demand growth
positive_highlights: Net product revenue increased quarter-over-quarter by $11.6M driven by higher demand and inventory decrease of approximately $1.3 million
Full-year 2026 net income guidance raised to a range of $17-20 million, exceeding the prior expectation of $16-19 million
Company is now debt-free after making its final quarterly principal loan payment of $11.1 million
summary: Puma Biotechnology reported Q2 FY2026 net product revenue of $53.6 million (up from $42M in Q1) and GAAP EPS of $0.16 per share, turning a loss to profit driven by demand growth and inventory drawdowns. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance for net NERLYNX revenue ($205-209M vs prior $202-206M) and net income ($17-20M vs prior $16-19M), while slightly lowering royalty expectations due to potential generic competition in China. The company is now debt-free following a loan payoff, with R&D expenses increasing significantly as Phase II trials for alisertib progress.

Move-in rates per square foot were down 4.4% on average

positive_highlights: FFO as adjusted per share up 17.6% year-over-year, beating expectations

The company raised its full-year same-store revenue and NOI guidance and FFO guidance to $1.98-$2.04 per share, citing better-than-expected momentum. They also introduced the Deca Initiative, aiming for a $10 billion capitalization level, and increased capital deployment guidance to $55-$75 million. Management expressed confidence in the acquisition pipeline and recovery from L.A. fire restrictions.

negative_highlights: Management expects total market volume to be down approximately 11% year-over-year in Q4 due to a higher-for-longer rate environment.
An uptick in churn notices was observed, with customers moving toward lower-cost or free point solutions.

Autopilot is commercially available with over 45,000 loans processed and early data showing a 10%-15% improvement in pull-through rates.
Share repurchases continued during Q2 (11 million shares) leaving $13.2 million remaining under the authorization.
summary: Blend reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $33.8 million (up 7% YoY) and non-GAAP operating income of $14.5 million ($7M above the high end of guidance). While profitability beat expectations, management issued a cautious outlook for H2 due to higher mortgage rates suppressing refinance volumes and an uptick in churn notices from customers seeking lower-cost solutions.

$8.5M one-time settlement payment recognized in Q2

Management raised full-year 2026 guidance to revenue of $1.43-$1.45 billion and adjusted EBITDA of $129-$131 million, citing strong underlying organic growth and successful mitigation of margin impacts from the Inflation Reduction Act.

summary: Privia Health reported strong Q2 results: practice collections grew 12.4% to $970 million, adjusted EBITDA increased 29% to $37.4 million with margin expanding 310 bps to 28.3% of care margin. Implemented providers grew 10.1% and attributed lives grew 19.2%. The company raised its 2026 guidance across most metrics, citing strong first-half performance. Management remains confident in long-term growth and margin expansion, despite minor CMS cash timing delays.

summary: Dropbox reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $631.5 million (up 0.9% YoY) and non-GAAP operating margin of 38.7%, beating guidance of 38.5%. The company added 96,000 paying users in the quarter, exceeding expectations, while gross margins contracted by roughly 60 bps due to AI compute costs. Management raised full-year FY26 revenue and non-GAAP operating margin guidance following strong Q2 execution.

Senior living margins face lumpiness in Q3/Q4 from new acquisitions
Hospice faces administrative costs from new program integrity measures

summary: Q2 2026 showed strong results with revenue up 35.8% to $298M and adjusted EBITDA up 48.2% to $24.3M, driven by acquisitions and operational excellence. Adjusted EPS rose 33.3% to $0.36. Management raised full-year guidance, citing momentum and better-than-expected acquisition transitions. Home health and hospice segments delivered strong same-store growth, while senior living showed stable improvements.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened significantly to $22.5 million compared to $10.1 million in the prior year quarter due to increased clinical trial costs.
R&D expenses more than doubled to $16.2 million, reflecting the heavy investment required for registrational trial advancement.
positive_highlights: Enrollment in SAFEGUARD accelerated with over 60 active clinical sites and increased screening/randomization rates.
Breakthrough T1D awarded a grant to support the new PRISE-hATG Phase III study, validating the approach for patients beyond 100 days from diagnosis.
Company confirmed sufficient drug supply exists to support both SAFEGUARD and PRISE trials.
summary: SAB Bio reported Q2 FY2026 net loss of $22.5 million, driven by R&D expenses of $16.2 million and G&A of $7.2 million as the company advances its lead candidate SAB-142 through the registrational SAFEGUARD study. Management confirmed enrollment in SAFEGUARD is on track to complete in Q4 2026 with top-line data expected in H2 2027, and announced a new Phase III study (PRISE-hATG) funded by Breakthrough T1D for patients up to two years from diagnosis. The company ended the quarter with $208 million in cash equivalents providing operational runway through 2028.

Strong rate increases and customer growth drove operating income, but APT spreads narrowed sharply in late June/July as new takeaway capacity came online sooner than expected, leading management to guide toward the lower end of the $0.08-$0.12 second-half APT range. O&M guidance was raised to $875-$885 million, and capital spending remains on track at ~$4.2 billion.

Gross profit rose 9% year-over-year to $2.7 million with margins expanding to 40.6%, while operating income grew 21% to $665,000 despite a non-cash fair market value loss on digital assets reducing net income. Management expressed confidence in the diverse solutions portfolio and renewed focus on M&A, noting that beef represents roughly 50% of revenue.

summary: Sweetgreen reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $192.7 million, up ~4% YoY, but comparable restaurant sales declined 6.2%, with adjusted EBITDA near breakeven at a loss of $0.2 million. Management noted sequential monthly improvement in transactions, with flat transaction comps in June, but flagged the impact of a Cyclospora outbreak and a jalapeno recall on outlook. Guidance for Q3 was lowered, reflecting recovery assumptions, and the company emphasized disciplined investment and menu innovation like wraps, which lifted transactions but created a check drag.

negative_highlights: Colombia subscriber figures include normalization effect from reporting harmonization
Chile remains highly competitive with aggressive pricing and elevated churn
Q2 EFCF benefited from timing; management cautioned on H2 forecasting

summary: Millicom delivered record Q2 FY2026 results: service revenue of $2 billion, up 5% organically YoY (strongest since 2021) and 60.1% reported; adjusted EBITDA of $1 billion (first time surpassing that milestone) with organic growth of 9.1% YoY; record equity free cash flow of $327 million, up 50%+ YoY. Management raised FY2026 equity free cash flow guidance from at least $900 million to around $1.1 billion and improved the year-end leverage target to below 2.5x. The board approved an additional interim dividend of $1.50 per share payable in two installments.

negative_highlights: Company remains unprofitable with a non-GAAP operating loss of $8.9 million.

Radar solution gaining traction with Volvo and new wins announced for leading Tier 1s.

Non-GAAP operating loss narrowed to $8.9 million from a prior period loss of $14.5 million as core business grew over 5%. Management raised Q3 FY2026 revenue guidance to a range of $67-$73 million, with expectations for continued expense improvement.

negative_highlights: SPD film and emulsion production slowed significantly and at some point essentially stopped, which management said is reflected in lower royalties this quarter
Accounts receivable reserves and going concern language were taken on amounts owed by Gauzy and Vision Systems due to uncertain timing of collection
Nasdaq listing compliance has not yet been regained, and management said it is actively monitoring the situation
positive_highlights: New license agreement signed with KLIM, a division of Polaris, for SPD motorcycle helmet visors and goggles, during the Gauzy restructuring period
Two new major aircraft programs won with a large unnamed OEM, which management said is a $25 million revenue opportunity for Research Frontiers
Gauzy received court approval on July 18 for a debt restructuring plan and secured a $7 million financing, with money reportedly starting to flow toward restarting German production
summary: Research Frontiers reported Q2 FY2026 with no revenue or EPS figures disclosed in the transcript, but management explicitly attributed lower royalties this quarter to the near-halt in SPD film/emulsion production at principal licensee Gauzy, which is in court-supervised restructuring in France and Israel. Management described four contingency supply plans (Plan A being Gauzy's likely emergence and full production restart) and said Gauzy's $7 million financing has begun flowing toward restarting German operations. No formal guidance was issued, though management said it believes volumes can recover by year-end; accounting reserves on Gauzy/Vision Systems receivables and ongoing Nasdaq listing non-compliance remain unresolved. The key change versus the prior period is that production has started to restart and the restructuring is described as substantially closer to conclusion, but no hard financial results were provided.

Third-quarter results are expected to reflect normal seasonal weakness in both U.S. and international markets.
Reconstruction approval is not anticipated until late 2027 or beyond, limiting near-term TAM expansion from that segment.

Minimally invasive procedures generated $12.1 million in the quarter, exceeding original expectations and contributing 18% of total revenue.
summary: Establishment Labs reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $67.5 million (up 31.7% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $3.7 million, a significant turnaround from the prior year's loss. Management raised full-year revenue guidance to $269-$271 million from the previous range of $266.5-$268.5 million driven by strong U.S. growth (up 140% YoY) and expansion in minimally invasive procedures. The company expects to transition to free cash flow positive during H2 2026.

summary: Nexstar reported record Q2 2026 revenue of $1.99 billion, up 62.2% YoY (including TEGNA), with adjusted EBITDA of $633 million and free cash flow of $238 million, more than doubling YoY. Advertising revenue grew 81.5% to $862 million, driven by TEGNA and political, while combined non-political advertising fell 5.8%. The company reaffirmed legacy distribution guidance, raised no forward revenue targets, and remains focused on debt repayment, having repaid $409 million in the quarter.

Subscription revenue grew 39% YoY to $28.5 million following the May launch of GoodRx Companion.
Management raised full-year guidance for both top-line revenue and adjusted EBITDA, signaling confidence in execution.
summary: GoodRx reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $200.4 million and adjusted EBITDA of $63.7 million (margin 31.8%), driven by Pharma Direct growth of 76% YoY and subscription revenue up 39%. Management raised full-year guidance for both revenue ($790M-$805M) and adjusted EBITDA ($240M-$250M), projecting a return to year-over-year revenue growth earlier than anticipated. The quarter highlighted the strategic shift toward high-value subscriptions (GoodRx Companion launch) while prescription transaction revenue moderated as planned.

positive_highlights: Net income attributable to shareholders rose 57% to $6.4M and GAAP EPS rose 80% YoY

summary: RCI reported Q3 FY2026 total revenue of $73.9M, up 4% YoY, with GAAP EPS up 80% and non-GAAP EPS of $0.90, up 17%; net income attributable to shareholders rose 57% to $6.4M and adjusted EBITDA rose 10% YoY (and 9% sequentially) to $16.9M. Nightclub revenue was a record $63M (+1%), while Bombshells revenue rose 25.4% to $10.8M with segment operating margin up to 7.0% from 0.8%. Operating and free cash flow were each $2.5M lower YoY on payable timing, though up 14% and 26% sequentially, and the company paid down $8.6M of debt and bought back $1M of shares. Management said share buybacks are paused until roughly October to bring leverage down, with total debt reduction of about $25M targeted over three months; no formal financial guidance was given.

negative_highlights: Adjusted free cash flow for Q2 was burdened by approximately $10 million in transaction costs.

Production contribution from the new operated drilling program is not expected until 2027.

Company raised full-year Adjusted EBITDA guidance range from prior levels to $960 million-$1 billion.

Management updated full-year 2026 guidance, raising the Adjusted EBITDA range to $960-$1 billion and increasing expected annualized free cash flow to approximately $440 million. The company announced a new operated development program targeting offsetting production decline rather than pure volume growth.

Management highlighted a reserve increase driven by successful integration of Cardinal and new BLM leases.

Latin America and SMG contributed significant growth, and management raised no formal guidance but expressed confidence in continued momentum. Scrap margins normalized sequentially as expected, and the company completed full ownership of SMG.

summary: Crane NXT reported Q2 FY26 sales of $493 million (up 22% YoY) and adjusted EPS of $1.10 (up 13% YoY), driven by strong performance in SAT (+17%) and DTT (+26%). Management raised full-year adjusted EPS guidance to a range of $4.22-$4.42, citing improved non-operating expenses and stronger-than-expected first-half momentum.

negative_highlights: F1 Adjusted OIBDA declined 30% year-to-date due to lower race count (22 vs prior year)
MotoGP revenue growth partially offset by a reduction in contractual media rights

Las Vegas Grand Prix ticket sales trending well ahead of last year's levels

MotoGP showed growth with increased sponsorship revenue, though results are presented on a pro forma basis following its July acquisition. Management noted that F1's decline is temporary due to rescheduled races and expects leverage improvement over time.

negative_highlights: Operating expenses increased significantly due to higher depreciation from a larger portfolio and payment of incentive fees.

Equity issuance via ATM was suspended for the six months ended June 30, 2026 due to unattractive stock prices.
positive_highlights: Acquired Newport News property leased to Huntington Ingalls for $22.75 million, doubling straight-line rent compared to the sold North Carolina asset without issuing new shares.
summary: Gladstone Commercial reported Q2 FY26 FFO and Core FFO of $0.38 per share compared to $0.33 in the prior year period, driven by a portfolio acquisition that doubled straight-line rent from an asset sale rather than organic growth or same-store expansion. Operating revenues increased due to higher rental rates and recovery revenue, but expenses rose significantly due to depreciation on a larger portfolio and incentive fees. Management highlighted strong industrial occupancy (98.7%) and market improvements while explicitly stating they are not looking to grow their office portfolio and face challenges in the current equity capital markets.

negative_highlights: Other packaging and specialty device revenue declined sequentially as expected due to material input costs, though a rebound is anticipated next quarter
Silicon photonics orders are nascent with roughly two-thirds of the $50 million in orders scheduled for delivery in 2027

Management raised H2 2026 revenue growth expectations to >25% from a prior expectation of 15%, citing record backlog surpassing $1.1 billion driven by strong demand in advanced packaging and nodes.

Management raised full-year revenue guidance range from $785-$805M to $805-$820M based on strong first-half performance and pipeline replenishment.
International operations grew 32.9% YoY, driven organically in Life Sciences and Antitrust & Competition Economics practices.

Management raised full-year 2026 annual revenue guidance to a range of $805-$820 million from the prior $785-$805 million while reaffirming profit margin targets, citing strong performance across eight practices including double-digit growth in Energy and Life Sciences.

negative_highlights: A severe tornado damaged the primary third-party paper distribution center in Menasha, Wisconsin, causing an estimated $20-25 million sales impact to Q3.
FAM segment net sales were down 1% on a reported basis due to lower volume mix and the exit of the Wilson facility.
Q3 price-to-cost performance is expected to be less favorable than Q2 as raw material cost recognition catches up.

SAS segment produced record-adjusted EBITDA and margins with tapes and labels expanding almost 10%.
New aerospace and defense commitment from a global space exploration leader is ramping up as planned.
summary: Mativ reported Q2 FY2026 net sales of $532 million (up nearly 2% organically) and adjusted EBITDA of $75 million, marking a quarterly record with margins expanding to 14.1%. Management raised the full-year inflation impact estimate for Middle East conflict costs but maintained that Q3 volume growth is expected excluding tornado impacts which are estimated at $20-25M in sales loss.

Utilization rates driving longer lead times for internally manufactured products

All end markets grew sequentially, led by data center (up ~40%) to $137.6 million, with I&D and telecom also up. Book-to-bill was a record 1.6:1, and gross margin expanded 120 bps to 59.7%. The company expects continued growth with data center and defense strength, launching CW laser production potentially in late calendar 2027.

negative_highlights: International growth was negatively impacted by the Middle East conflict (approx. 40 bps headwind to total Enovis).
Q3 is expected to be seasonally softer than in prior years due to Western Europe market conditions and ongoing conflicts.
Inflationary pressure from raw materials, freight, and distribution costs added $2 million of unplanned impact in Q2.

U.S. Recon grew organically at 8% driven by hips/knees (Nebula/ARG) despite a tough comparison from the ARG launch last year.
Free cash flow turned positive for H1 with Q2 generation of $31 million, improving significantly versus the prior year.
summary: Enovis reported Q2 FY26 sales of $583 million (up 3% YoY) and adjusted EPS of $0.90 (14% underlying growth), with organic revenue up 5%. The company reaffirmed its full-year 2026 guidance, noting that the quarter was in line with expectations despite a divestiture headwind and Middle East conflict impacts. Management expressed confidence in second-half acceleration driven by new product launches like ARVIS but warned of seasonally softer conditions in Q3.

negative_highlights: Recall volume surged 300% year-over-year in Q2, impacting an average of 15,000 vehicles monthly and reducing gain on sale proceeds.
Liquidity guidance for FY26 was lowered to $1.0B-$1.4 billion after removing ATM program proceeds from the forecast.
Net DPU increased slightly due to note older vehicle models in a softening wholesale market.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 10% year-over-year driven by strong pricing (RPD up 9%) and fleet utilization gains of 80 bps despite recalls.
Adjusted Corporate EBITDA improved $63 million YoY, exceeding the top end of previous guidance at $81 million.
Company achieved a record second-quarter RPD per day excluding COVID-2022 levels.
summary: Hertz reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $2.4 billion (up 10% YoY) and Adjusted Corporate EBITDA of $81 million ($63M improvement), beating consensus despite a headwind from elevated recalls impacting ~$55M in EBITDA. Management raised full-year RPU expectations to trend above the North Star target, citing strong commercial momentum and pricing power that drove 200 consecutive days of positive YoY RPD growth. While liquidity guidance was lowered slightly by removing ATM proceeds from forecasts, management reaffirmed a path to profitability in 2027.

Energy Industrial revenue declined 6% QoQ and is expected to remain subdued in H1 driven by logistics constraints and inventory challenges

positive_highlights: Q2 revenue grew 32% quarter-over-quarter driven by Thermal Barrier segment growth of 81% QoQ
European OEM outlook raised to $20 million-$30 million for 2026, up from prior guidance of $10 million-$15 million

summary: Aspen Aerogels reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $49.8 million (up 32% quarter-over-quarter) and adjusted EBITDA of negative $6.6 million, following a GAAP net loss of negative $23.3 million driven by an $8.9 million insurance receivable offsetting property damage from the East Providence incident. Management raised the dividend to $0.29 per share and expects continued momentum into fiscal 2027 with World Cup and midterm advertising tailwinds.

negative_highlights: The company completed its current share buyback authorization, leaving no active program for further capital return in the near term unless a new one is approved.
Average premium per policy remained flat despite revenue growth, indicating pricing pressure or volume-driven expansion rather than rate hikes.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew by 11% driven by premium growth while average premium per policy remained flat.
Pre-tax income was $18 higher than the same quarter last year despite challenging market conditions and rate softening.
Retention rates consistently remain above 90%, demonstrating strong customer stickiness.
summary: HCI Group reported Q2 FY2026 results with revenue growing by 11% and diluted EPS of $5.60 (up from $5.18 YoY), driven by a 6% increase in gross premiums earned despite flat average premium per policy. Pre-tax income exceeded $110 million, representing an 18% year-over-year increase compared to the record prior period. Management highlighted strong retention rates above 90%, successful pivots of CORE into residential markets generating ~$6M/month new business, and a completed share buyback program utilizing over half of its authorization.

negative_highlights: North America tours increased only 3% in Q2, up 1% year-to-date
Company remains at 4x net debt to EBITDA, expecting upper threes by year-end
Average owner down payment including equity unchanged at mid-to-high twenties
positive_highlights: Contract sales increased 22% over prior year, exceeding high end of guidance
Adjusted EBITDA grew to $215 million, $20 million above guidance midpoint
Raised full-year EBITDA guidance by $50 million to $805-$830 million
summary: Marriott Vacations Worldwide reported Q2 2026 contract sales up 22% year-over-year, with VPG up 23% to $4,477, and adjusted EBITDA of $215 million, exceeding the high end of guidance. Adjusted free cash flow for the first half was $201 million versus $22 million a year ago. Management raised full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance to $805-$830 million, a $50 million increase, and highlighted record sales months and ongoing owner engagement initiatives.

negative_highlights: Offshore Pipeline Transportation segment performed slightly below expectations due to unplanned downtimes at key fields
Non-recurring margin opportunities from SPR releases and market dislocations are not expected to continue into Q3
Q2 results were broadly in line with internal estimates rather than a clear beat
positive_highlights: Retired approximately $83 million of high-cost preferred securities in the quarter
Reduced all-in annual run rate cost of capital by an estimated $25 million year-to-date
Marine Transportation segment returned to full capacity after dry docking
summary: Genesis Energy reported Q2 FY2026 results broadly in line with internal expectations but slightly below external guidance for the Offshore Pipeline segment due to operator challenges and unplanned downtimes at key fields. Management highlighted significant balance sheet optimization, including $95M asset sales, a new securitization facility, and the retirement of approximately $83 million in high-cost preferred securities, reducing total outstanding Series A by roughly 40% year-to-date. While non-recurring margin opportunities from market dislocations boosted Q2 earnings, management explicitly warned that these specific benefits are not expected to continue into Q3.

negative_highlights: Adjusted attributable net income missed Q1 levels due to lower realized gold prices ($4,447/oz vs $4,884 in Q1) and an elevated effective tax rate of 46%.

Consolidated AISC increased sequentially by $50/oz to $2,157 driven by one-time crusher costs at Lindero (~$115/oz impact), contractor mobilization at Séguéla, and external factors like Argentina macroeconomics adding ~$49/oz.
Cash balance decreased from Q1 levels due to the concentration of income tax payments ($79.3 million) in the second quarter.
positive_highlights: Generated $85 million in free cash flow from ongoing operations, bringing H1 total to $260 million despite sequential decline.
Executed significant shareholder returns via share buybacks totaling $82 million in Q2 (approx. 41% of FCF).
Séguéla plant expansion and Diamba Sud feasibility study milestones confirmed, anchoring the path to exceed half a million ounces annually by mid-2028.
summary: Fortuna Mining reported Q2 FY2026 results with revenue of $380 million and adjusted attributable net income of $75 million ($0.25/share), which was sequentially lower than the record Q1 due to lower realized gold prices, higher taxes, and increased costs. Consolidated AISC rose to $2,157/oz from a peak in Q2 before expected declines in H2 as one-time items like crusher refurbishment at Lindero and contractor mobilization at Séguéla normalize. Management reaffirmed annual production guidance of approximately 60% growth by mid-2028 driven by the Diamba Sud project and the approved 30% expansion at Séguéla.

negative_highlights: Later-line patient accrual is naturally diminishing as the company successfully captures the TKI-pretreated population.
Gross-to-net deductions remain stable at around 30% due to payer mix maturation, limiting immediate margin expansion from pricing power.
positive_highlights: IBTROZI net revenue grew 25% to $23.2 million, driven by a shift toward first-line patients which now account for approximately 85% of new starts.
The company is the number one choice for newly diagnosed advanced or metastatic ROS1-positive lung cancer patients based on IQVIA claims data from January to May 2026.
Completed an opportunistic convertible debt financing that was approximately 5x oversubscribed, allowing the retirement of higher-cost term loan debt and strengthening the balance sheet.
summary: Nuvation Bio reported Q2 FY26 net revenue of $31.7 million, a beat on the median estimate driven by IBTROZI U.S. product revenue growth of 25% to $23.2 million and collaboration/license revenue of $8.5 million. The company raised its capital position significantly via an oversubscribed convertible note offering that allowed it to retire higher-cost debt, while maintaining a cash balance of $661 million. Management highlighted strong commercial momentum with first-line new patient starts growing 30% quarter-over-quarter and IBTROZI establishing itself as the market leader in both first-line and overall settings.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened slightly to $9.3M due to a $0.6M non-cash warrant liability adjustment.
SG&A expenses increased 3% YoY despite revenue growth, indicating operating leverage has not yet fully kicked in.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 45% YoY to $3.9M, marking the second highest quarter ever.
Gross margin expanded 150 bps to 50.7%, achieving four consecutive quarters above 50%.
Cash burn improved sequentially and YoY, with cash runway extending into 2028.
summary: Second quarter revenue was $3.9 million, up approximately 45% year-over-year, with gross margin expanding to 50.7%. Management reiterated full year 2026 revenue guidance of $20 million-$22 million and cash burn guidance of $26 million-$28 million.

negative_highlights: Q3 guidance implies pre-tax income slightly below Q2 actual
Q3 and Q4 revenue expected to be more modest with a Q4 step-down
New initiatives like Exzeo Ventures may not translate into results overnight

GEICO partnership adds auto insurance, enabling home and auto bundling
summary: Exzeo reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $58 million, up from $56 million sequentially, with adjusted revenue exceeding $56 million, up $4 million YoY. Managed Premium grew to $1.4 billion, Adjusted EBITDA margin was above 53%, pre-tax income was over $31 million (above guidance), and EPS was $0.26. Full-year guidance remains unchanged, with Q3 pre-tax income expected between $28-$31 million and Managed Premium around $1.4 billion. The company also signed GEICO as its eighth carrier, doubled agent count and quote volume year-to-date, and launched Exzeo Ventures for AI-driven initiatives.

negative_highlights: Elevated investment in strategic growth initiatives partially offset margin expansion
Higher effective tax rate offset EPS benefits
No explicit FY2027 enrollment growth guidance by segment

Fourth consecutive quarter of positive total enrollment growth at Chamberlain
New Advocate Health partnership expected to serve hundreds of students annually
summary: Covista reported Q4 FY2026 revenue up 9.7% to $501.4 million and full-year revenue up 9.3% to $1.954 billion, exceeding the high end of raised guidance. Full-year adjusted EPS of $8.25 grew 23.7%, also above the high end. Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 100 bps to 26.7% for the year. Management initiated FY2027 guidance and highlighted new partnerships, including Advocate Health, and expects continued momentum across segments.

negative_highlights: Normalized FFO down 4.5% YoY due to hotel dispositions
Hotel results declined $20M YoY from exit activity
Expected displacement from renovations, notably Nautilus
positive_highlights: RevPAR up 6.6% YoY and 9% excluding Nautilus; July up 7.1%
Net lease NOI up 2.2% QoQ with stable occupancy
Reduced debt and interest expense; equity raise proceeds used to redeem $550M
summary: SVC reported Q2 2026 Normalized FFO of $55M, down 4.5% YoY, in line with consensus; per-share FFO was $0.43. RevPAR for retained hotels grew 6.6% YoY and 9% excluding Nautilus disruption; July RevPAR grew 7.1%. Net lease NOI increased 2.2% QoQ, occupancy at 96.6%, TA rent coverage improved to 1.34x. Management maintained full-year guidance and continues capital recycling with hotel dispositions and debt reduction.

negative_highlights: Adjusted gross margin decreased 100 basis points to 45.4% YoY due to normalized ocean freight and fuel pressures.

SG&A expenses increased approximately 20 bps as a percentage of revenue due to incremental marketing spend for expansion.

E-commerce sales grew nearly 25% year-over-year with penetration rising to 17.3% of total sales, driven by omnicart adoption.
New stores opened in Q2 performed at or ahead of expectations, validating the expansion strategy into new markets like South Carolina.
summary: Bob's Discount Furniture reported Q2 FY26 net revenue of $619.6 million (up 8.8% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA margin of 9.8%, missing the prior year due to a gross margin contraction of 100 bps offset by mix shifts. Management reiterated full-year guidance for net revenue between $2.6 billion-$2.625 billion, implying flat gross margins despite Q2 pressures from fuel and freight costs. While comparable sales grew 2.3% driven by higher average order value and conversion, in-store traffic remained a headwind that outpaced the industry decline.

negative_highlights: Global real estate fundraising in first half of calendar year at a nine-year low, a headwind
Net impairment charge of $19 million related to OPI contract asset write-off
Equity-based compensation expected to add ~$600,000 incremental expense next quarter
positive_highlights: Distributable earnings and adjusted EBITDA met guidance; sequential growth in recurring service revenues
DHC and ILPT among best performing REITs over past three years; ILPT doubled quarterly dividend to $0.10
Wholly owned multifamily assets nearly 92% occupied with 3-4% rent growth on renewals
summary: RMR reported fiscal Q3 2026 distributable earnings of $0.48 per share and adjusted EBITDA of $19.7 million, both in line with guidance. Recurring service revenues rose sequentially to $45.5 million, boosted by higher enterprise values at managed REITs and the Greenwich JV acquisition fee. Management noted continued improvement at managed REITs, including DHC and ILPT, and highlighted opportunities in private capital and multifamily despite a global fundraising slowdown. Next quarter guidance implies adjusted EBITDA of $19-21 million and distributable earnings of $0.48-0.50 per share; full-year adjusted EBITDA is expected at $76.5-78.5 million, excluding incentive fees.

Q3 ECS sales guidance reflects growth over a large partner addition last year rather than an acceleration of underlying demand trajectory.

Global Components backlog continues to build into the first half of 2027 with book-to-bill ratios well above parity.
summary: Arrow Electronics reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $10 billion (up 32% YoY) and non-GAAP EPS of $5.45 (up 124% YoY), both exceeding expectations. Operating margin expanded 120 bps to 4%, driven by volume growth, price inflation, and value-added services, though ECS margins were impacted by a one-time charge related to partner contract restructuring. Management raised Q3 sales guidance slightly above the prior range midpoint while maintaining EPS guidance within its previous band.

The company reaffirmed its fiscal 2026 guidance despite challenging category conditions, cost inflation (including $40 million higher COGS from Midwest premium), and a U.S. industry decline of 4.2%. Management highlighted progress in portfolio transformation, with Monaco and Fever-Tree each on track to contribute 1-2% of NSR, while noting continued share pressure in core brands and heightened competition in EMEA-APAC.

Core Business Services is expected to be flat or slightly down for full year 2026 after accounting for transition impacts.

Record quarterly bookings with nearly 40% coming from Advanced Technology Solutions; pipeline increased meaningfully.
summary: Genpact reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $1.343 billion (up 7.1% YoY) and Adjusted diluted EPS of $1.00 (up 13.6% YoY). Advanced Technology Solutions grew at an accelerated rate, while management announced a strategic transition away from non-aligned work that will impact total revenue growth by nearly two points in the second half of 2026. Management raised full-year guidance for Advanced Technology Solutions to accelerate to at least 25%, and maintained its outlook for Core Business Services despite the planned headwinds.

negative_highlights: U.S. call center closures and cost reductions implemented

Management raised no explicit guidance but signaled improved forecasting and record ERC of $8.9 billion.

The company achieved its first non-GAAP operating profit since late 2024, at $635,000, and executed $20 million in annualized spending reductions. Announced partnerships with NVIDIA and Dassault Systèmes, plus a $10 million convertible note investment from Micron. Guidance calls for Q3 revenue of $17 million ±10%, record Q4 revenue, full-year revenue above $70 million, and double-digit revenue growth in 2027.

negative_highlights: Operating margin contracted significantly from 21.7% in Q2 FY25 to 8.7%, landing at the lower end of the previously guided range.
World Cup event reduced June load factors by 230 bps, putting modest pressure on unit revenues and RASM for the quarter.
All-in fuel prices surged 85% YoY (from $2.32 to $4.28 per gallon), increasing total CASM by 26%.

Strong demand trends across the network supported an operating margin recovery, recovering approximately 40% of increased fuel expenses via higher yields and RASM growth.
Board ratified a quarterly dividend of $1.71 per share to be paid on September 15th.
summary: Copa Holdings reported Q2 FY26 operating profit of $91.7 million and net profit of $68.2 million ($1.67/share), resulting in an operating margin of 8.7% compared to the prior year's 21.7%. Revenue grew 25.7% YoY, but margins were pressured by a significant World Cup headwind in June (load factors down 230 bps) and elevated fuel costs which increased all-in CASM by 26% despite strong yield recovery of ~40%. Management updated full-year guidance to an operating margin range of 17%-19%, maintaining capacity growth expectations at 14%-15%.

negative_highlights: Third-quarter guidance was lowered for both revenue and loan volumes due to the persistent elevated rate environment affecting refinancing.
Management explicitly stated they will fall note weakness in of their previously guided goal of reaching adjusted EBITDA breakeven by September.
No new HELOC partnership launches are expected in Q3, with impact anticipated only starting in Q4.

summary: Better Home & Finance Holding Company reported Q2 FY26 loan volume growth of 38% year-over-year to $1.67 billion and total net revenues increasing 28% YoY to $54.7 million, though adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed by only 39%. Management lowered third-quarter guidance for revenue ($49M-$52M) and loan volume compared to prior expectations due to a muted refinancing environment and delayed enterprise partnership launches.

negative_highlights: Coal tar costs increased approximately 12% year-over-year and 15% sequentially, impacting profitability in Carbon Materials and Chemicals.
Railroad Products and Services segment faced headwinds from Class 1 railroad capital budget tightening and price concessions to secure volume commitments.
Carbon Markets remain volatile with global prices for carbon pitch declining by 2%, driven largely by market dynamics in Australasia.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA reached $71 million with an adjusted margin of 13.7%, supported by volume growth in Performance Chemicals and utility poles.
Operating cash flow for the first half of the year hit a record $96 million, compared to $28 million in the prior year period.
Performance Chemicals delivered strong results with sales up 10% excluding currency, driven by market share gains despite flat overall demand.
summary: Koppers reported Q2 FY2026 sales of $520 million (up 3% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $71 million, though GAAP EPS was impacted by non-cash charges from the accelerated closure of Stickney distillation operations. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance for both sales ($1.9B-$2B range maintained but with segment adjustments reflecting volatility) and adjusted EBITDA (raised to $240M-$250M), while maintaining an EPS outlook of $3.80-$4.20. The quarter highlighted record year-to-date cash flow driven by working capital improvements, offset by higher raw material costs including a 12% YoY increase in coal tar.

negative_highlights: Operating expenses rising due to variable incentive compensation
Visibility limited; management cautious on full-year 2027 outlook
Global supply chain constraints acknowledged
positive_highlights: Revenue increased 36% sequentially, well above guidance
Advanced solutions segment revenue up 20% over prior record

summary: Kulicke & Soffa delivered a strong fiscal Q3 2026 with revenue up 36.2% sequentially and 123% year-over-year, beating expectations. Gross margin was 47.8%, with non-GAAP EPS of $1.20. The company guides Q4 revenue to $375 million (up 13.5% sequentially) and non-GAAP EPS of $1.42. Management highlights broad-based recovery, record advanced solutions revenue, and expects strength to continue into fiscal 2027, with TCB revenue potential of $150-200 million next year.

B2C replatforming activity remains softer than historical norms with longer sales cycles

BigCommerce Payments adoption is running more than 30% ahead of internal plans
summary: Commerce reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $84.5 million and non-GAAP operating income of $8.1 million, which beat the high end of its prior guidance range ($4M-$5M). Management revised full-year 2026 guidance downward by approximately $17-19 million at the midpoint to reflect deliberate decisions including partner ecosystem concentration, higher AI infrastructure costs, and a more cautious view on B2C replatforming bookings. Despite the lower revenue outlook, management highlighted strong GMV growth of 14% YoY, sequential improvement in net revenue retention for three consecutive quarters, and GAAP profitability.

negative_highlights: Glucagon sales declined sharply by 42% YoY to $11.9 million due to increased competition.
IMS facility received an FDA warning letter, leading management to expect remediation expenses of $2M-$3M per quarter for several quarters and potential batch delays.
BAQSIMI net sales decreased 3% primarily due to pricing pressure from higher rebates and 340B discounts.

Gross margins expanded to 51%, up from 50% in the prior year period.
BAQSIMI triggered its first $100 million milestone payment to Eli Lilly due to exceeding annual sales thresholds.
summary: Revenue increased to $183.9 million (up 5% YoY) driven by the launch of ipratropium bromide and new products like iron sucrose and teriparatide, partially offset by declines in BAQSIMI (-3%) and glucagon (-42%). Gross margins expanded to 51%, but management issued a cautious outlook for H2 due to expected remediation expenses at the IMS facility ($2M-$3M/quarter) and continued competitive pressure on key franchises.

Operating loss of $6.9 million and net loss of $7.7 million, though improved year-over-year
New CPT code transition to 2027 creates potential near-term air pocket risk
positive_highlights: Revenue of $21.7 million up 18% YoY and 13% sequentially, first time crossing $20 million in a quarter
Raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $86-89 million, up from $80-85 million

summary: AVITA Medical reported Q2 2026 revenue of $21.7 million, up 18% year-over-year and 13% sequentially, exceeding $20 million for the first time. The company raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $86-89 million (20-24% growth) and introduced new guidance to achieve cash flow breakeven in Q4 2026. Gross margin improved to 81.9%, operating loss narrowed to $6.9 million, and net cash use improved to $3.2 million. RECELL U.S. volumes grew over 10% sequentially to 2,600 units, with strong RECELL GO mini adoption in smaller wounds, and CMS has proposed 2027 RVUs for new Category 1 CPT codes.

negative_highlights: Federal government revenues declined 9.5% year-over-year due to contract cancellations and constrained award activity.
State and local government revenues were down 1.9% sequentially, impacted by fewer major disasters and funding delays.
Book-to-bill ratio fell below 1 (0.85) in the quarter as federal procurement cycles remained sluggish.
positive_highlights: Non-federal revenues increased just under 7% year-over-year driven by commercial energy (6.7%) and international government clients (+35%).
Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to 11.2%, up from the prior year quarter.

summary: Second quarter revenues were $474.5 million, flat year-over-year and in line with expectations but missing the prior sequential growth trend due to a specific decline of 9.5% from federal clients caused by contract cancellations. Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 10 basis points sequentially to 11.2%, while non-GAAP EPS rose 12%. Management reaffirmed full-year revenue guidance and lowered share count expectations, noting that more than 90% of the required growth is already in backlog.

negative_highlights: Smelting zinc sales volume fell 7% YoY due to the fire at Cajamarquilla in May which affected casting operations.
Free cash flow closed slightly negative ($10M) primarily reflecting a $131 million tax settlement payment related to Cerro Lindo Stability Agreement.
Conversion costs were above guidance range, driven by lower volumes and temporary higher operating costs from the Cajamarquilla fire.

Aripuanã mining operations recovered with production up 44% YoY, aided by the fourth tailings filter now fully operational at >90% capacity utilization.
Cerro Lindo block caving implementation is underway to lower unit costs and access higher-grade areas.
summary: Nexa reported Q2 FY26 net revenues of $908 million (up 28% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $286 million ($186M mining / $66M smelting), driven by higher metal prices but offset by a fire at Cajamarquilla. Free cash flow was slightly negative due to a one-time $131 million tax settlement payment in Peru, though excluding this item it would have been positive. Management maintained full-year guidance for CapEx and production despite the operational setbacks.

negative_highlights: World Cup-related demand added approximately 100 bps to Q2 results and will likely fade in the back half of the year.
Total operating expenses increased 4% year-over-year, though management expects tighter growth (approx. 3%) for the full year.

summary: Summit Hotel Properties reported a strong Q2 FY26 with pro forma RevPAR growth of 5% and Adjusted EBITDAre increasing 7.7% to $54.8 million. Management raised full-year guidance for RevPAR (1.75%-3.25%), Adjusted FFO ($95.5m-$103m), and EPS, citing better-than-expected Q2 results and durable demand trends outside of World Cup markets. The company also highlighted a successful asset sale in Dallas/Arlington that eliminated $7.6 million in capital needs.

negative_highlights: Non-GAAP diluted earnings per share decreased year-over-year due to higher operating expenses from the Amicus acquisition, increased interest expense on new debt financing, and lower investment income.
Approximately $84 million of transaction and integration-related charges were recorded in GAAP SG&A for the quarter.

VOXZOGO maintained commercial momentum with double-digit growth in both U.S. and international markets despite competitor entry.
summary: BioMarin reported a standout Q2 FY26 with total revenue reaching nearly $1 billion and growing 20% year-over-year, driven by strong performance in its Metabolic Conditions portfolio following the Amicus acquisition integration. Management raised full-year guidance for total revenues, VOXZOGO revenue, and non-GAAP diluted EPS based on robust second-half expectations including a successful international price negotiation closure. The company highlighted significant cost synergies of approximately $220 million expected by 2028 from the deal.

The company raised full-year retail revenue and adjusted EBITDA guidance to $5.87 billion and $1.963 billion at the midpoint, while fine-tuning interactive revenue guidance down to $1.57 billion and reiterating an interactive adjusted EBITDA loss of $20 million. Management highlighted strong development project performance, balance sheet improvements, and a disciplined approach to capital allocation.

negative_highlights: Variable license revenue down 15% YoY

summary: Cerence reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of approximately $70 million, within guidance and up 12% year-over-year, with adjusted EBITDA of $13.5 million beating the high end of guidance and free cash flow of $20 million.
