Variable license revenue declined 15% YoY due to a tough comparison, but xUI ramp and non-auto growth are expected to support FY2027 growth.

negative_highlights: Commercial relevance for gate model systems not expected until 2032
Annealing system sales limited to roughly 2-3 systems per year, with revenue recognized over two quarters
No concrete financial guidance for revenue or EPS provided in the transcript
positive_highlights: Peer-reviewed Nature paper validated fast, high-fidelity two-qubit gate with ~99.9% fidelity and ~500 ns gate times
Expanded AT&T agreement; D-Wave reduced processing time from ~1 hour to less than 15 seconds in one application
Optum moved directly to production after initial proof-of-technology, running ~30,000 jobs by mid-June
summary: D-Wave reported expanding commercial momentum with new and expanded customer engagements (AT&T, Optum, NTT) and a Nature-published validation of its dual-rail gate model architecture. The company reiterated its roadmap: 17 physical qubit system by end of 2025, 49 qubit in 2026, 181 qubit in 2028, 10 logical qubits by 2030, and 100 logical qubits by 2032. Management guided to roughly 2-3 annealing system sales per year at $20M-$40M each, with revenue recognized over two quarters per system. No specific financial figures for revenue, EPS, or margins were provided in the transcript excerpt.

negative_highlights: Management explicitly stated it is uncertain if favorable conditions (consumption/supply mix) will continue through the remainder of 2026.
Earnings face future volatility from consumption fluctuations, climate change effects like El Niño/La Niña, and water supply quality issues.
positive_highlights: Consolidated EPS increased $0.22 (25.3%) year-over-year driven by new rates and higher consumption.
Board approved an 8.2% dividend increase, raising the annualized rate to $2.182 per share.
ASUS segment earnings grew due to higher construction activities and management fee revenues.
summary: American States Water reported Q2 FY2026 consolidated earnings of $1.09 per share and revenue up by $18.2 million compared to the prior year quarter. The beat was driven primarily by new customer rates implemented in January 2026, a 4% increase in water consumption, and favorable supply mix changes including wells returning online. Management raised guidance for ASUS segment earnings ($0.63-$0.67) while noting uncertainty regarding whether the current strong performance will persist due to potential weather or conservation impacts.

negative_highlights: Impact of Middle East conflict and higher fuel prices estimated at 300-400 basis points
Airline Technology revenue broadly in line, but continued to expect growth in future quarters
Free cash flow remains negative at approximately -$65 million for the year
positive_highlights: Revenue up 4% year-on-year, exceeding expectations of flat to nominal growth
Normalized adjusted EBITDA up 19% to $151 million, outperforming guidance by $21 million
Full-year pro forma adjusted EBITDA and free cash flow guidance increased
summary: Sabre's Q2 FY2026 revenue grew 4% to $712 million, with normalized adjusted EBITDA up 19% to $151 million, exceeding guidance. Full-year pro forma adjusted EBITDA guidance was raised to approximately $600 million and free cash flow to -$65 million. Air distribution bookings grew 1%, ahead of expectations, with noted resilience in corporate volumes and ongoing impacts from Middle East conflict and fuel prices. The company reported strong growth in hotel revenue, payments gross spend, and NDC, while highlighting agentic AI progress with doubling of active partners to 60.

negative_highlights: Clear Eyes supply remained volatile and constrained, leading to a decline in brand revenue
International segment revenue decreased 2.1% organically due to distributor order timing
Gross margin down 120 basis points YoY due to higher transportation costs and mix
positive_highlights: Q1 revenue up 6.5% to $265.7 million, exceeding expectations
Adjusted free cash flow reached a quarterly record of $83.7 million
Breathe Right integration largely complete, with new products like Breathe Right Sport launching
summary: Prestige Consumer Healthcare reported Q1 FY2027 revenue of $265.7 million, up 6.5% YoY, with organic growth of 3.2%, and adjusted EPS of $0.98, up from $0.95. The company raised its full-year guidance to include the Breathe Right and LaCorium acquisitions, expecting adjusted gross margin of just over 57% and at least $270 million in adjusted free cash flow. Growth was driven by GI and dermatological categories, while Clear Eyes remained supply constrained and international revenue fell 2.1% organically due to order timing.

negative_highlights: Experiences adjusted EBITDA margin down 290 bps to 11% due to marketing and channel mix
Hotels revenue declined 21% with sustained volume headwinds
SEO headwinds and weather-related cancellations pressured growth; Q3 guide reflects uneven July
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA above expectations at $76M for continuing operations
Viator bookings grew 10% and paid channels growing double digits
Announced sale of TheFork for $700M to unlock value and focus on experiences
summary: In Q2 FY2026, TripAdvisor's continuing operations (experiences and hotels) reported revenue of $442M and adjusted EBITDA of $76M, with revenue in line and EBITDA above expectations. Experiences bookings grew 5% overall, with Viator up 10%, but TripAdvisor POS faced SEO headwinds (~5 pts of growth drag). Hotels revenue declined 21% due to sustained volume headwinds. Management announced the sale of TheFork for $700M, expects to close before year-end, and reiterated long-term confidence in experiences while remaining cautious on macro and Q3 guidance.

negative_highlights: Adjusted OIBDA declined 11% year-over-year to $96 million
Consumer revenue fell 2% due to video business shutdown and organic broadband churn
Operating costs increased, including a $3 million public company cost addition and higher distribution expenses from Quintillion network restoration
positive_highlights: Consumer gross margin expanded to 71.8% driven by lower video programming costs following business exit
Business revenue grew 1% YoY supported by data upgrades in healthcare and education sectors
GCI net leverage stands at 2.1x with $447 million of undrawn credit capacity
summary: Liberty Capital reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $261 million (flat YoY) and Adjusted OIBDA of $96 million (down 11% YoY). The quarter was impacted by the shutdown of the video business, a decline in consumer broadband subscribers offset partially by an acquisition, and increased distribution costs from restoring service on the Quintillion network. Management announced plans to initiate a quarterly dividend starting December with $60 million annually.

negative_highlights: Private payroll loans contributed over half of the yearly increase in NPLs due to operational maturity taking longer than expected with Dataprev linkages.
Credit card delinquency increased as a result of a deliberate strategy shift towards growing an interest-earning portfolio in an unsecured segment facing macro headwinds.
Stage 3 formation increased by approximately 15 basis points due to the inclusion of credits renegotiated under Desenrola and those past-due beyond 360 days.
positive_highlights: Total net revenue grew 32% year-over-year with NIM reaching a record high of 10.1%, crossing double digits for the first time.
Private payroll loans surpassed 600,000 clients and generated interest income growth of 64% year-over-year despite higher delinquency levels.
The company achieved capital neutrality, generating more capital than it consumes to fund its own loan book.
summary: Inter reported Q2 FY26 results with total net revenue growing 32% year-over-year to BRL 4.8 billion and record ROE of 16.3%. The NIM expanded to a milestone high of 10.1%, driven by strategic repricing, inflation tailwinds, and capital deployment into higher-yielding products like private payroll loans which surpassed 600k clients. While asset quality metrics showed expected increases in delinquency for the new private payroll book due to operational maturity timing rather than deterioration, management maintains confidence in its flywheel model.

negative_highlights: Gross margin expansion was modest at ~50 bps sequentially, partially offset by COGS increases from ramping new products like Fetal Focus and Latitude.
Management noted that Q2 sequential volume growth for Signatera was exaggerated by weather-related suppression in Q1 2026.
positive_highlights: Record quarterly test processing of approximately 1,044,000 units with Oncology MRD growing ~56% YoY to 283,000 units.
Signatera received FDA approval as a companion diagnostic for muscle-invasive bladder cancer and Japanese PMDA approval for colorectal cancer.
NCCN issued its highest Category 1 recommendation for Signatera in adjuvant treatment of muscle-invasive bladder cancer.
summary: Natera reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of approximately $753 million (up ~38% YoY) and processed a record 1,044,000 tests with Oncology MRD volumes surging 56% year-over-year. Management raised the full-year revenue guidance range to $2.85-$2.91 billion at the midpoint, implying roughly 31% growth ex true-ups while holding OpEx steady. The quarter was driven by strong sequential volume acceleration in Signatera and ASP improvements across Women's Health and Organ Health.

negative_highlights: Q3 segment EBIT fell to $58M from $72M, driven by warmer weather and AmeriGas weakness
AmeriGas Q3 EBIT down $25M on lower retail volumes and customer attrition
Year-to-date adjusted EPS declined to $3.17 from $3.55 due to lost tax credits and higher interest
positive_highlights: Year-to-date segment EBIT up to $1.187B, modestly ahead of prior year
Utilities segment EBIT increased by $10M in Q3 on higher gas base rates
AmeriGas leverage at 4.3x, lowest in 10 years, with expected distributions to parent in 2027
summary: In Q3 FY2026, UGI's reportable segment EBIT fell to $58M from $72M a year ago, driven by warmer weather and continued customer attrition at AmeriGas, partially offset by utility growth. Year-to-date, segment EBIT rose modestly to $1.187B, but adjusted diluted EPS declined from $3.55 to $3.17 due to lost investment tax credits and higher interest. Management reaffirmed FY2026 EPS guidance of $2.75-$2.90, despite a noted guidance cut for midstream growth investments. AmeriGas is expected to resume distributions to the parent in 2027.

negative_highlights: Management noted that some large potential engagements in the pipeline are not yet factored into guidance until they reach 100% certainty.
Gross margin may face downward pressure on a weighted basis if the company wins lower-margin projects, though strategic mix is expected to trend upward over time.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 58% YoY with adjusted gross margin expanding two points sequentially to 49%, nine points above the public target.
Adjusted EBITDA surged 92% YoY, exceeding consensus by $8.5 million or 50%. Fully diluted EPS of $0.41 nearly doubled analyst estimates.
Customer diversification accelerated as the largest customer's share fell to 37% while a new big tech partner scaled from 17% to 34%.
summary: Innodata reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $92.1 million (up 58% YoY) and adjusted gross margin expansion to 49%, significantly beating analyst consensus on all key metrics including EPS ($0.41 vs $0.21). Management reiterated guidance for over 40% year-over-year revenue growth, citing a broadening customer base where the largest client dropped to 37% of revenue while new frontier lab partnerships scaled. The company highlighted strong cash generation and announced an ATM program alongside leadership transitions.

negative_highlights: Three multifamily loans downgraded to 4-rated during the quarter
Recorded $30 million increase in reserves due to macroeconomic conditions
Realized loss of $47 million expected on Q3 asset sales
positive_highlights: No new non-accrual or 5-rated loans in the quarter or year
Deployed $6.7 billion year-to-date, near-record pace
Expecting to resolve $800 million or 40% of non-accrual/REO by year-end
summary: STWD reported Q2 2026 distributable earnings of $152 million or $0.40 per share, with no new non-accrual or 5-rated loans. The company deployed $2.5 billion in the quarter and another $1.7 billion in July, bringing year-to-date investments to $6.7 billion. Management expects to resolve approximately $800 million of non-accrual and REO assets by year-end, and anticipates the strongest origination quarter in Q3. Guidance was not explicitly provided, but management signaled continued recovery and growth.

negative_highlights: OUS revenue grew only 12% due to European tender timing delays
Revenue shift to Q3/Q4 from Europe could impact quarterly phasing
R&D expenses up $3.9M YoY to $11.6M
positive_highlights: Revenue up ~120% YoY; U.S. revenue up >150%
Gross margin 59%, second consecutive quarter at/near high end of guidance
Raised full-year revenue and gross margin guidance
summary: Senseonics reported Q2 2026 revenue of $14.5 million, up ~120% YoY, with U.S. revenue up >150% to $12.6 million. Gross margin was 59%, above guidance and the highest organic performance in company history, leading to raised full-year revenue guidance to $62-66 million and gross margin guidance to 58-61%. The Eon Care Network added 28 providers, surpassing 90 total and on track to exceed the 100-provider goal by year-end. European transition caused some revenue timing delays but full-year outlook unchanged.

negative_highlights: Incremental U.S. carrier pass-through fees of $71M pressured gross margin
Q3 organic revenue guidance decelerates to 11%-12% growth
GAAP operating income impacted by $33M prepaid asset impairment
positive_highlights: Record revenue of $1.5B, up 22% reported and 17% organic YoY
Raised full-year organic revenue growth guidance to 13%-13.5%
Record Q2 free cash flow of $353M
summary: Twilio delivered record Q2 revenue of $1.5 billion, up 22% reported and 17% organic year-over-year, with non-GAAP gross profit growth accelerating to 18%. The company raised its full-year organic revenue growth guidance to 13%-13.5% from 9.5%-10.5% and raised full-year non-GAAP operating income and free cash flow guidance. Management highlighted strong growth in messaging, voice, and software add-ons, plus early customer wins for the new Conversations Layer.

negative_highlights: Gross margin declined to 73% in Q2, down from Q1
CapEx expected to be incrementally higher in Q3 and Q4
eProbe customer eval conversion uncertain; could take close to a year
positive_highlights: Q2 revenue up 19% YoY; H1 revenue up 22% YoY
Backlog grew to $271 million, up 10% QoQ and 16% YoY
Reaffirmed 20% full-year revenue growth guidance
summary: PDF Solutions reported Q2 FY2026 revenues of $61.5 million, up 19% year-over-year, with first-half revenues up 22%. Backlog grew to $271 million, up 10% sequentially and 16% year-over-year, driven by multiple eight-figure contracts (secureWISE and DirectScan) and record Cimetrix bookings. Gross margin was 73%, down sequentially due to higher perpetual licenses in Q1, but management expects expansion toward the 77% target. The company reaffirmed 20% full-year revenue growth guidance, despite increased CapEx for eProbe tools.

negative_highlights: Terminal shipments fell to about 2,500 from a record 3,100 in Q1, and management guided the go-forward range to 2,000-3,000 per quarter
Operating expenses rose to $10.4M from $9.7M in Q1, including $0.2M in severance
Cash fell about $1.4M to $57.7M, driven by $2.3M in stock repurchases, and the buyback program will be exhausted this month
positive_highlights: Service revenue grew 29% year-over-year to $29.7M and 6% sequentially
Subscribing vessels rose to about 10,700, an 11% sequential gain versus 7% in Q1, and up 18% year-to-date
Service gross margin expanded to 36% from 35%, with adjusted EBITDA of $3.0M up from $2.8M in Q1
summary: KVH reported Q2 FY2026 total revenue of $33.7M, up 4% sequentially and 27% year-over-year, with service revenue of $29.7M up 6% sequentially and 29% YoY. Service gross margin was 36% versus 35% in Q1, adjusted EBITDA was $3.0M (up from $2.8M), and subscribing vessels reached roughly 10,700, up 11% sequentially. Terminal shipments of about 2,500 fell from Q1's record 3,100, which management called a high watermark and guided to a 2,000-3,000 per-quarter go-forward range. No formal revenue or EBITDA guidance was issued; management noted the $15M buyback authorization will be complete within the current month.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA loss widened to $7.1 million from $5.3 million due to deliberate investment in the expanded sales organization.
Sales and marketing expenses increased significantly to $11.4 million from $7.2 million as the company ramps up its commercial footprint.
positive_highlights: Revenue beat expectations with $11.4M reported, reflecting sequential and year-over-year growth.
Gross margin expanded to 86.8% from 83.9% due to lower unit costs and manufacturing improvements.
Received CMS G-code extending reimbursement into office-based labs (OBL), removing a key barrier for TriNav adoption.
summary: TriSalus reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $11.4 million, a 1.7% increase year-over-year and sequential growth, with gross margins expanding to 86.8%. Management reiterated full-year 2026 revenue guidance of $54-$57 million (19%-26% growth over FY2025) despite elevated sales and marketing expenses driven by commercial expansion. A significant positive development was the receipt of a CMS G-code extending reimbursement into office-based labs, expanding the addressable market for liver embolization and other indications.

negative_highlights: Gold Bar production missed targets due to carbonaceous material absorbing dissolved gold during leaching
AISC rose significantly in Q2 primarily driven by the shortfall in production ounces at Gold Bar
No dividend expected from San José JV for the remainder of FY2026
positive_highlights: Los Azules FID work program on track to conclude in Q4 with major process packages awarded
Geotechnical campaign allows consolidation of pit design, increasing mineable ore and reducing stripping by roughly 22%
Enhanced financing proposal from Finland's Export Credit Agency (Finnvera) advancing alongside other ECA engagements
summary: The company reported a disappointing quarter with production falling short of expectations at the Gold Bar mine due to unexpected carbonaceous material reducing recoveries and higher costs driven by lower volume. Management explicitly stated this was not a quarter they wanted and admitted execution fell short, though they raised Los Azules progress as a long-term offset. Guidance for San José dividends is paused until next year.

negative_highlights: Lower-than-planned grades at Kensington, Rochester, and Palmarejo operations are expected to rebound in H2 but impacted Q2 production.
New Afton's partial year guidance was refined downward as the ramp-up to target throughput of 16,000 tonnes per day is now pushed from end-Q2 to early Q4.
$140 million non-cash fair value uplift expense related to Rainy River stockpile inventory reduced reported EPS and EBITDA.
positive_highlights: Record quarterly revenue of $1.1 billion and record free cash flow of $388 million despite lower realized metal prices.
Ending cash balance exceeded $1 billion for the first time in company history, doubling year-end 2025 liquidity to over $2 billion by Q4 expectations.
Rochester achieved a new quarterly crushing record of 6.8 million tonnes with Phase 2A Leach Pad expansion progressing ahead of schedule.
summary: Coeur reported record quarterly revenue of $1.1 billion and adjusted EBITDA of $478 million in Q2 FY26, driven by the first full quarter contributions from acquired New Afton and Rainy River assets despite lower-than-planned grades at three operations. Management recalibrated guidance for 2026 to reflect a slower ramp-up timeline for underground production at both Canadian mines compared to original assumptions, while maintaining confidence in strong second-half cash flow generation once non-cash acquisition accounting impacts ($140M) are removed.

negative_highlights: Extended warranty revenue declined 3.1% to $17.1 million and the segment lost Trinity to an $8 million management buyout
Roundhouse and Kingsway Skilled Trades both reported flat QoQ adjusted EBITDA from Q1 to Q2, with Southside taking a low six-figure write-down on a legacy construction project
Three operating subsidiaries representing under 10% of LTM Portfolio EBITDA were out of covenant compliance during the quarter
positive_highlights: KSX adjusted EBITDA hit a record $4.3 million, up 77.9% YoY, with KSX revenue up 68.3% to $22.3 million
Consolidated adjusted EBITDA rose to $5.2 million from $1.7 million and net income turned positive at $200,000 versus a $3.2 million loss
Portfolio EBITDA reached a record $7.2 million and net debt declined to $59.9 million from $62.4 million at December 31, 2025
summary: Kingsway reported Q2 FY2026 consolidated revenue up 27.6% to $39.4 million and swung to net income of $200,000 from a $3.2 million loss a year ago, with adjusted EBITDA of $5.2 million versus $1.7 million. KSX revenue rose 68.3% to $22.3 million and segment adjusted EBITDA jumped 77.9% to a record $4.3 million, while extended warranty revenue fell 3.1% to $17.1 million (up 6.5% pro forma for the Trinity sale) with segment EBITDA of $1.1 million. Portfolio LTM EBITDA held at $22-23 million, management reaffirmed 3-5 acquisitions and double-digit organic growth targets for 2026, and net debt fell to $59.9 million from $62.4 million at year-end. Offsets include flat QoQ adjusted EBITDA at Roundhouse and Kingsway Skilled Trades, covenant non-compliance at three subsidiaries under 10% of LTM Portfolio EBITDA, and the Trinity divestiture and SNS CEO departure.

negative_highlights: Cash at quarter-end was only $1 million against a balance sheet carrying significant current debt with Third Eye Capital
India biodiesel revenue fell sequentially to $2.5 million as the OMC tender process ran into late July; the $17 million allocation only begins shipping now

45Z credit value is uncertain: current $15.20 per MMBtu at a -42 emissions rate versus a possible -375 to -420 rate, with management unable to quantify the outcome and the DOE process described as not open
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 20% to $62.7 million and adjusted EBITDA swung positive by $15.5 million to $9.7 million year-over-year
Excluding all 45Z credits, gross profit of $13.8 million still improved by more than $8 million on lower corn cost, 12% higher ethanol volume and 38% higher RNG volume
Seven LCFS pathways approved averaging negative 380 CI versus the negative 150 default, with six more digesters in the CARB process and $17.6 million of 45Z credit proceeds received July 9
summary: Q2 FY2026 revenue rose 20% to $62.7 million from $52.2 million, operating income swung to $5.8 million from a $10.7 million loss, and adjusted EBITDA improved $15.5 million to $9.7 million. Results were aided by $8.6 million of Section 45Z credits ($6.4 million ethanol, $2.2 million dairy RNG); excluding 45Z, gross profit of $13.8 million still improved more than $8 million on cheaper corn ($6.07 vs $6.42/bushel), 12% higher ethanol volume, 9% higher ethanol pricing, and 38% RNG volume growth. Net loss narrowed $14 million to $9.4 million, but cash ended the quarter at just $1 million, with $17.6 million of net 45Z credit proceeds received July 9. No formal numeric guidance was given; management outlined milestones (two digesters within a month, third corn oil unit in fall, MVR operational by end-2026) and flagged wide uncertainty on pending DOE 45Z emissions-rate revisions and six CARB LCFS pathways.

negative_highlights: Consolidated Adjusted FCF before distributions for H1 was only $19M, significantly lower than the prior year's H1 due to a one-time $81M weather derivative receipt.
Liberty Costa Rica revenue declined sequentially compared to Q1 despite top-line improvement over last year.
Hurricane Melissa headwinds in Jamaica impacted Liberty Caribbean results by roughly $6 million net across both revenue and Adjusted OIBDA.
positive_highlights: Adjusted OIBDA grew 3% year-over-year to $436 million, driven by strong postpaid mobile trends across the group.
Liberty Puerto Rico Adjusted OIBDA margin expanded significantly to 32%, up from 29% last year, with churn stabilizing at healthy levels.
Announced an AI-driven IT services deal with Amdocs valued at north of $250 million NPV expected to drive OpEx reductions starting in Q4.
summary: Q2 FY2026 revenue was $1.1 billion (up 1% reported) and Adjusted OIBDA grew 3%, though consolidated Adjusted FCF before distributions ($83M in Q2) remains significantly weighted to the fourth quarter due to weather derivative receipts from last year's hurricane season. Management highlighted strong operational progress in Puerto Rico with margin expansion, but noted that H2 free cash flow momentum will likely be less robust than 2025 as they lap a large $81 million insurance payout and face higher P&E spending.

negative_highlights: Total revenue declined year-over-year despite strong New Expensify growth
Classic customer base is shrinking as the company migrates users to New Expensify
Management noted uncertainty regarding which business strategy (New growth vs Classic churn mitigation) will win out first
positive_highlights: Free cash flow reached $6.4 million, up 162% sequentially from Q1
New Expensify net new revenue grew over 250% year-over-year to exceed $10M in ARR
Raised full-year free cash flow guidance by approximately $3-5M
summary: Q2 revenue declined year-over-year to $33.9 million as the company navigates a transition between its cash-generating Classic product and rapidly growing New Expensify cohort. Management raised full-year free cash flow guidance from $6-9M to $12-14M, citing improved profitability despite top-line pressure and resolved legal settlements. The business executed significant capital allocation with approximately 7% share repurchases while investing in AI features that drove a Platform of the Year award.

negative_highlights: The holding unit recorded a loss of BRL 46.2 million, representing an deterioration of BRL 8.7 million compared to the prior year.
Curtailed energy impact rose from 15.7% to 23.7%, resulting in a negative revenue impact of approximately BRL 34.8 million.
positive_highlights: EBITDA reached BRL 1.6 billion, representing a 21% increase compared to the same period last year.
Recurring net income grew significantly by 42.6%, reaching BRL 645 million driven by operational improvements and tax benefits.
Copel Distribuição's billed market expanded by 7.2%, contributing directly to boosting second quarter results.
summary: Copel reported a strong Q2 FY2026 with consolidated recovery EBITDA of BRL 1.6 billion (up 21% YoY) and recurring net income of BRL 645 million (up 42.6%). The quarter was highlighted by the completion of the tariff review for Copel Distribuição, which recognized investments exceeding double the 2021 base level. Management maintained its dividend policy with a minimum payout ratio of 75% and declared interest on equity totaling BRL 706 million.

negative_highlights: Q2 sales were partially inflated by a one-time inventory stocking event of approximately $6 million, which will create a headwind for Q3.
Management described growth trajectory as 'moderating' due to high market penetration (over 70% in major markets) and the natural lifecycle dynamics of an established product.
R&D expenses increased year-over-year from $69M to $74M primarily driven by advancement of three phase III trials.
positive_highlights: KIMMTRAK demonstrated a landmark doubling of the likelihood of being alive at five years (16% OS rate vs. 8%) in metastatic uveal melanoma patients treated with KIMMTRAK as their only therapy.
Q2 net sales reached $116 million, representing an 18% increase over Q2 FY25 and a sequential growth of approximately 3% when normalized for the stocking event.
The company holds a strong balance sheet with $880 million in cash and marketable securities as of June 30th.
summary: Immunocore reported Q2 FY26 net sales of $116 million (up 18% YoY) and H1 revenue of $223 million (up 16% YoY), driven by strong U.S. growth despite a one-time $6M inventory stocking headwind in the quarter. Management reiterated that top-line data for the TEBE-AM trial is expected as early as year-end, though enrollment remains ongoing with minimal impact from remaining patients. The company highlighted exceptional five-year overall survival data for KIMMTRAK and maintained its strategic focus on advancing three phase III melanoma trials.

negative_highlights: Delivery and other cloud applications revenue declined 6% YoY to $396 million, dragging overall top-line.
Q2 CapEx of $347 million was below guidance due to delayed GPU shipments arriving in Q3.
Full-year EPS guidance lowered by approximately $0.15-$0.20 compared to prior expectations.
positive_highlights: Announced total volume of multi-year commitments for cloud infrastructure services exceeds $2.8 billion this year.
Cloud Infrastructure Services (CIS) revenue grew 39% YoY, driven by strong demand and a new robotics customer win.
Security revenue maintained momentum with growth of 10% YoY ($604M), led by WAF upgrades from major enterprises.
summary: Akamai reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $1.1 billion (up 5% YoY) and non-GAAP EPS of $1.59, missing the implied consensus due to a decline in delivery services (-6%) and lower-than-expected CapEx ($347M vs guidance). Management raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance slightly but lowered Q3 specific guidance by approximately $8 million YoY due to foreign exchange headwinds. The company announced significant multi-year cloud infrastructure commitments totaling over $2.8 billion, with a new robotics deal worth more than $600 million expected to ramp in 2027.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA margin compressed ~500 bps YoY
Headwinds in transactional product lines and portable storage units on rent
World Cup benefit creates sequential step-down into Q3
positive_highlights: Revenue up 4% YoY and adjusted EBITDA exceeded outlook
Modular activations up 16% YoY, pending orders up 13%
Enterprise account revenue up 21% YoY
summary: WSC reported Q2 FY2026 total revenue of $612M, up 4% YoY and above the ~$585M expectation, with leasing and services revenue up 6% and D&I revenue up 25%. Adjusted EBITDA was $228M, exceeding the $223M outlook, though margins compressed ~500 bps YoY to 37.2% due to upfront activation costs and mix. Management modestly raised full-year revenue and adjusted EBITDA guidance, citing strong modular activations (up 16% YoY), order book growth (up 13% YoY), and enterprise account revenue up 21%, while noting headwinds in transactional product lines and a step-down from World Cup activity in Q3.

negative_highlights: I&M revenue down 5.5% YoY due to site losses and outage timing
Adjusted SG&A up to 22.1% of revenue from 21.2%
positive_highlights: C&E revenue up 16.8%, record segment revenue of $207 million
Combined C&E & Geo backlog up 20% YoY to $1.18 billion
Consolidated adjusted gross margin up 135 bps to 38.2%
summary: TIC Solutions reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $584 million, up 3.3% year-over-year (organic growth 2.5%). Adjusted gross margin expanded 135 basis points to 38.2%. C&E grew 16.8% to $207 million, Geo grew 7.9% to $81 million, but I&M declined 5.5% to $297 million due to site losses and outage timing. Combined backlog rose 20% to a record $1.18 billion, and the company expects improved growth in the second half.

negative_highlights: Oil and gas royalties contributed only approximately 5% of total Q2 revenues.
Management noted that converting the digital infrastructure opportunities into firm revenue depends on diligence timelines and power availability ramp-up, which may take time to finalize.
positive_highlights: Revenue hit an all-time high of $66.8 million driven by strong sequential growth in surface use royalties and produced water handling volumes.
Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to a robust 89% with free cash flow reaching $40.2 million (60% margin).
Digital infrastructure pipeline advanced significantly, moving from initial discussions to late-stage negotiations or signed LOIs.
summary: LandBridge reported record Q2 FY26 revenue of $66.8 million (up 41% YoY) and Adjusted EBITDA of $59.8 million with an 89% margin. Management reaffirmed full-year 2026 guidance for Adjusted EBITDA between $210M-$230M, which was previously raised last quarter. The company highlighted a robust digital infrastructure pipeline involving seven counterparties representing over 10 gigawatts of potential.

negative_highlights: Total quarterly investment income decreased by $14 million quarter-over-quarter driven by portfolio size reduction and non-accruals
New deal activity remained light due to geopolitical uncertainty, specifically tensions in the Middle East/Iran situation
NAV per share declined 2.8% from Q1 levels
positive_highlights: $4 million in share repurchases completed during the quarter under a $300M program
KKR waived its portion of subordinated income incentive fee, providing an $11 million positive impact on Q2 net investment income
Portfolio rotation continued with sales of approximately $500 million to third parties and capital return from legacy asset Global Jet
summary: FSK reported Q2 FY2026 net investment income of $0.44 per share and adjusted net investment income of $0.43 per share, resulting in a NAV decline to $18.30 due to portfolio value decreases exceeding earnings. Management reiterated guidance for annualized yield between 8%-9% but noted that loan sales were muted by geopolitical tensions (specifically Iran) which impacted repayment activity and new deal origination volumes.

negative_highlights: China revenue declined 23% as IVD pricing guideline uncertainty impacted note
Respiratory season forecast revised down; assuming below-average season for 2026-2027
Free cash flow guidance withdrawn; Q2 operating cash flow was negative $111 million
positive_highlights: Ex-China revenue grew 6%, with Labs ex-China up 9% and TRIAGE up 9%
Adjusted EBITDA increased 21% to $129 million, margin up 310 bps to 20%
North America grew 6% and JPAC grew 10%
summary: Q2 FY2026 revenue grew 2% constant currency, with ex-China growth of 6%; adjusted EBITDA rose 21% to $129 million with margin up 310 bps to 20%. China revenue declined 23% and respiratory season is expected to be soft, leading to guidance cuts for FY2026 revenue ($2.52B-$2.60B), adjusted EBITDA ($540M-$560M), and adjusted EPS ($0.65-$0.90). Free cash flow guidance was withdrawn, and operating cash flow was negative $111 million for the quarter.

negative_highlights: Specialty market conditions more competitive; rates continuing to soften
Established $30 million reserve for Middle East developments
GAAP net income per share only $0.87 due to one-time costs
positive_highlights: Total revenues increased 93% year-over-year to $575 million
Adjusted net operating EPS grew to $1.14, with ROE of 13%
Share repurchase guidance tracking to upper end of $200-250 million range
summary: Radian reported Q2 2026 with total revenues of $575 million, up 93% year-over-year, driven by the Inigo acquisition, and net earned premiums up 116% to $504 million. Adjusted net operating EPS grew to $1.14, with adjusted net operating ROE of 13%. Mortgage segment new insurance written rose 14% to $16.3 billion, and persistency improved to 82%. Specialty net premiums earned increased 9% to $267 million, with plans for second-half earned premiums to be about 20% higher than first-half. Guidance for full-year share repurchases was raised to the upper end of the $200-250 million range, and expected Radian Guaranty dividends increased to $650 million or more. Market conditions in specialty insurance are more competitive, and a $30 million Middle East reserve was established.

negative_highlights: F1 revenue declined 15% YoY due to a calendar variance reducing the race count from nine to five races in Q2 and eight vs eleven YTD
Adjusted OIBDA for F1 decreased year-to-date because of lower event counts, with team payments as % of Adjusted OIBDA at 61.7%
F3 revenue declined due to the sale of cars at the beginning of the new cycle last year
positive_highlights: F1 viewership up 13% year-over-year, with Apple TV attracting a younger and more female audience
MotoGP attendance increased +4% through Mugello with record numbers in Thailand and Germany
Las Vegas Grand Prix ticket sales trending well ahead of last year's levels as of July
summary: Liberty Media reported Q2 FY26 results where F1 revenue declined 15% YoY and Adjusted OIBDA fell 30%, primarily driven by a calendar variance that reduced the race count to eight events compared to eleven last year. MotoGP showed growth in constant currency due to event mix changes, but overall consolidated performance was weighed down significantly by the absence of Saudi Arabia and Bahrain races held earlier in the quarter. Management noted that F1 revenue recognition is based on season-based accruals tied to the specific race count staged.

negative_highlights: Southwest Steel Processing expected to generate a net loss of $0.50 per diluted share in 2026
SG&A expenses increased to 12.1% of sales versus 11.7% a year ago
Interest expense rose $1.1 million year-over-year due to higher rates on senior notes
positive_highlights: Record consolidated revenues of $440 million, up 10% year-over-year
Raised full-year 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $3.10-$3.30
Engineered Products operating income up 50% year-over-year
summary: Park-Ohio reported record Q2 FY2026 revenue of $440 million, up 10% year-over-year, with record revenues in Supply Technologies and Engineered Products. Adjusted EPS rose 24% to $0.93, and operating income increased 22% year-over-year. The company raised full-year 2026 guidance for net sales to $1.7-1.73 billion and adjusted EPS to $3.10-3.30, citing strong demand across multiple end markets. Management also noted strong backlogs and continued operational improvements, while reviewing strategic alternatives for Southwest Steel Processing, which is expected to be a drag this year.

negative_highlights: Consolidated gross margins faced pressure, with Payables segment margins contracting significantly due to a mix shift toward lower-margin buyer-funded revenues and higher interchange costs.
Treasury Solutions saw margin compression as high-growth segments like Passport (125% growth) and Priority Tech Ventures expanded at lower margins than the core CFTPay platform.
Merchant Solutions revenue included 3.6% of volume from acquisitions, with organic merchant growth slowing to mid-single digits amid macro headwinds in construction and restaurants.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 9% YoY driven by strong organic growth (7.2%) across segments, particularly a 21.6% increase in Payables and 14.9% in Treasury Solutions.
Adjusted EPS increased 12% year-over-year to $0.29 despite margin headwinds.
Total customer accounts on the platform grew nearly 13% YoY to reach 1.8 million.
summary: Priority Commerce reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $262.3 million (up 9% YoY) and adjusted EPS of $0.29 (up 12% YoY). Management maintained full-year guidance for revenue ($1.01B-$1.04B), gross profit, and adjusted EBITDA but expects results to be at the lower end of their respective ranges due to margin pressures from business mix shifts and higher interchange costs. The company ended with $120.3 million in cash on hand.

negative_highlights: Company remains in a net loss position with cash burn of approximately $15 million annually
positive_highlights: Revenue beat expectations with a significant year-over-year increase to $13.4 million
Net loss improved materially from the prior period's $15.9 million to $5.9 million
Raised full-year revenue guidance range and narrowed ranges for operating expense
summary: OmniAb reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $13.4 million (up from $3.9M in the prior year) and a net loss narrowing to $5.9 million ($0.05/share). Management raised full-year 2026 guidance for both total revenue and cash balance, citing strong momentum driven by milestone payments and two xPloration instrument sales.

negative_highlights: Total revenue and adjusted net income declined 1% and 2% organically, missing expectations.
U.S. revenue declined 7%, with companion animal portfolio down 6%.
Management lowered full-year guidance due to intensified competitive pressure and softer clinic visits.
positive_highlights: Livestock revenue grew 11% in the quarter, led by strong U.S. performance.
Companion animal diagnostics revenue grew 12%, with sustained demand in urgent and emergency care.
International revenue grew 6% organically, supported by broad-based emerging market growth.
summary: Zoetis reported Q2 FY2026 organic revenue and adjusted net income declines of 1% and 2% respectively, with U.S. revenue down 7% and companion animal portfolio down 6%, while international grew 6% and livestock grew 11%. The company cited intensified competitive pressure and softer clinic visits, leading to increased promotional spending and a revised full-year outlook reflecting continued near-term headwinds. Management highlighted strength in diagnostics (revenue up 12%) and livestock, but acknowledged price realization could be flat to -2% for the year due to gross-to-net adjustments.

negative_highlights: FY2026 EPS guidance narrowed to $1.29-$1.32 with a projected small Q4 loss
LNG storage tank remains out of service after structural damage, not expected back until the 2027-2028 winter season
$15M note refinanced at 5.13%, up from a 2% rate, raising interest costs
positive_highlights: Nine-month diluted EPS up 4.6% to $1.37 from $1.31 on the non-gas base rate increase
Rate case settled at $3.85M of incremental annual revenue, resolving all issues, with rates effective August 1
Industrial volumes up more than 25% in the quarter, though at the lowest margin tier
summary: Q3 FY2026 net income was ~$550,000, or $0.05 per diluted share, nominally ahead of the prior-year quarter, driven by interim rate increases partially offset by the loss of a large industrial customer and higher O&M. Nine-month EPS rose 4.6% to $1.37 from $1.31. FY2026 EPS guidance was narrowed to $1.29-$1.32 from the prior range, with a small physical Q4 loss expected. The ~$4.3M expedited rate case settled at $3.85M in incremental revenue effective August 1, and the LNG storage tank remains out of service due to structural damage with a target return by the 2027-2028 winter season.

negative_highlights: Cortrophin guidance modestly revised down to $520-540M from prior (not stated)
ILUVIEN revenue down 16% YoY on international shipment timing
Gout sales force expansion adds costs, limiting near-term operating leverage
positive_highlights: Record Q2 revenues of $266M and record adjusted EBITDA of $71.6M
Cortrophin up 43% YoY with July record new cases and gout expansion off to strong start
Total revenue guidance of $1.1B and EBITDA growth of 27% reiterated
summary: ANI Pharmaceuticals reported record Q2 2026 revenue of $266M (up 26% YoY) and record adjusted EBITDA of $71.6M (up 32% YoY). Cortrophin Gel revenue was $117.1M, up 43% YoY and 56% QoQ; management revised full-year Cortrophin guidance modestly to $520-540M, still representing 50-55% growth. The gout sales force expansion is fully operational with strong leading indicators, and generics revenue grew 10% YoY. The company reiterated total revenue guidance of $1.1B and adjusted EBITDA guidance of $285-300M.

negative_highlights: Fuel hedges offset ~$20 million in the quarter, trading upside for certainty
Over $40 million of foregone margin at Montana Renewables due to turnaround
Working capital built $70 million, including $30 million crude inventory and $30 million receivables
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA with tax attributes of $175 million despite turnarounds
Restricted group leverage below 4x, expected to surpass 3x next quarter
MaxSAF catalyst test met or exceeded expectations; SAF run rate to ramp to 120-150 million gallons by spring 2027
summary: Calumet reported Q2 2026 adjusted EBITDA of $175 million, with strong performance in both Specialties and Montana Renewables despite planned turnarounds. The company deleveraged below 4x restricted group leverage, repurchased $115 million of notes and terminated a sale-leaseback. Management guided to accelerated deleveraging, announced a novel MaxSAF 150 second-phase expansion to reach 120-150 million gallons of SAF by spring 2027, and identified ~$50 million of low-risk specialty growth capital for 2027-2028.

negative_highlights: System revenue declined 34% year-over-year due to used-device cannibalization
Operating loss of $0.3M vs. operating income of $1.4M in prior year
Withdrew FY2026 revenue guidance due to proposed CMS reimbursement cuts
positive_highlights: Applicator unit volume up 27% year-over-year, a new all-time record
Applicator revenue up 13% year-over-year, partially offsetting system sales weakness
Finalized VDAs at amounts below accrued balances, yielding a $0.9M favorable swing
summary: Q2 FY2026 revenue fell 3% YoY to $9.7M, with system sales down 34% to $2.3M due to used-device cannibalization and industry distress, while applicator revenue grew 13% YoY and unit volume rose 27% YoY. Gross margin contracted to 76.2% and the company swung to an operating loss of $0.3M, with net loss of $0.7M. Management withdrew FY2026 guidance due to proposed CMS reimbursement cuts for UltraMIST under the PFS rule, though HOPPS proposed rule includes a 14% increase. The company intends to challenge the PFS proposal during the comment period.

negative_highlights: Book value per share declined to negative $45.58, down $1.31 from year-end 2025
Holding company cash and liquid assets decreased to $337 million from $357 million at year-end 2025
Oversight board settlement offer of ~$3 billion was dismissed by bondholders as inadequate
positive_highlights: Consolidated GAAP net loss improved to $46 million from $56 million in the prior year quarter
Adjusted net loss improved to $7 million from $8 million in the prior year quarter
National's leverage ratio improved to 21:1 from 24:1 at year-end 2025
summary: MBIA reported a narrower adjusted net loss of $7 million in Q2 2026, compared to $8 million a year earlier, driven by lower loss expenses at National. National's PREPA exposure decreased by $35 million to $390 million, and the oversight board increased its settlement offer to about $3 billion, but bondholders dismissed it as inadequate. Holding company liquidity declined to $337 million, and book value per share fell to negative $45.58. Management is cautiously monitoring PREPA litigation and potential sale options, with no new guidance provided.

negative_highlights: Free cash flow was negative $258 million in Q2 due to cash taxes, prepaid deliveries, and elevated production costs
Goose production impacted by April crusher fire; remediation and phase 1 crusher upgrades expected by end of Q3
Adjusted EPS of $0.03 was hit by ~$71 million realized losses on gold collar contracts
positive_highlights: Menankoto Exploitation Permit granted, allowing Fekola Regional pre-stripping to commence
Fekola, Masbate, and Otjikoto exceeded expectations; production guidance raised for those operations
AISC guidance lowered to $2,370-$2,550/oz, with full year expected at or below low end
summary: Consolidated Q2 production of ~204,000 oz in line with expectations; adjusted net income was $41M ($0.03/sh) with ~$71M realized losses from gold collar contracts. Fekola, Masbate, and Otjikoto outperformed, while Goose was impacted by the April crusher fire. The Menankoto Exploitation Permit was granted, clearing the way for Fekola Regional pre-stripping. 2026 production guidance narrowed to 820-920k oz, cash cost guidance unchanged, AISC guidance lowered; management expects meaningful free cash flow improvement in H2 and into 2027 as prepaid contracts are complete.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined to $34.3 million from $37.3 million YoY and Adjusted EBITDA fell to $17.2 million from $18 million
Core FFO per share of $0.20 was flat YoY, with reported net income of $0.43 boosted by a $28.8 million one-time property sale gain
Occupancy of 78.1% declined sequentially from Q1, and Q2 cash rent spreads on renewals were negative 7.7%
positive_highlights: Core FFO guidance raised to $0.72-$0.77 per share from $0.69-$0.76, and net debt/Adjusted EBITDA guidance lowered to 6.0x-6.8x from 6.5x-7.3x
Net debt to annualized Adjusted EBITDA fell to 5.4x from 6.4x a year ago, with debt outstanding down to $436.6 million from $483 million
Dedicated Use Assets rose to 38.7% of annualized base rent from 32.6% a year ago, and WALT lengthened to 6.2 years from 5.5 years
summary: Orion reported Q2 2026 revenue of $34.3 million, down from $37.3 million a year ago, while net income of $24.6 million ($0.43/share) was inflated by a $28.8 million gain on two property sales. Core FFO was $11.8 million, or $0.20 per share, essentially flat YoY, and Adjusted EBITDA fell to $17.2 million from $18 million. The company narrowed and raised its 2026 Core FFO guidance to $0.72-$0.77 from $0.69-$0.76 and lowered net debt/Adjusted EBITDA guidance to 6.0x-6.8x from 6.5x-7.3x, driven partly by one-time items like lease termination income and property tax refunds. Occupancy of 78.1% was down sequentially but up from 76.8% a year ago, and net debt to annualized Adjusted EBITDA improved to 5.4x from 6.4x.

negative_highlights: Ebouri-5-8 water cut increased faster than expected, implying more reservoir connectivity
Exploration well at West Etame encountered water-bearing zone and was not commercial
Production uplift from Baobab drilling not significant until 2027
positive_highlights: Net income of $42.4 million and adjusted EBITDAX of $54.8 million in Q2
Baobab production resumed and is slightly above pre-startup forecast
Egypt drilling program expanded to 10-15 wells with no increase in CapEx guidance
summary: VAALCO reported Q2 2026 net income of $42.4 million and adjusted EBITDAX of $54.8 million. Production increased in Gabon to over 9,300 boepd, and Baobab resumed production in June with rates slightly above pre-startup forecast. The company raised full-year production guidance, expanded Egypt drilling to 10-15 wells with no CapEx increase, and maintained CapEx in line with guidance. Management expressed confidence in continued growth into H2 2026 and beyond.

negative_highlights: Adjusted NII decreased from $0.62 in Q1 to $0.50 in Q2
Total investment income decreased by $4 million quarter-over-quarter due to lower fee income
One company added to the watchlist (Grade 3+)
positive_highlights: Adjusted NII of $0.50 per share covered the base dividend
Realized net gains of $6.4 million from equity monetizations
No investments on non-accrual status as of today
summary: Fidus reported Q2 FY2026 adjusted NII of $0.50 per share, down from $0.62 in Q1, covering the base dividend. Total investment income was $43.5 million, a $4 million decrease quarter-over-quarter due to lower fee income. The company realized $6.4 million in net gains from equity monetizations and exited Virtex non-accrual with a $11 million realized loss, leaving no non-accruals. Management sees deal flow picking up in the second half, citing improved activity levels and a healthy portfolio with 6% EBITDA growth.

negative_highlights: Underlying loss ratio rose 4.4 points to 43.1% vs. exceptional prior-year quarter.
Management sees signs of softening market and increasing competition, especially in Dwelling Fire.
Competition building faster than anticipated in California.
positive_highlights: Most profitable quarter in company history; net income $15.5M, EPS $1.05.
GAAP net combined ratio improved 1.3 points to 70.2%.
Dividend increased 20% to $0.06 per share; buybacks continued.
summary: Kingstone reported record Q2 2026 results: net income of $15.5 million, diluted EPS of $1.05, and a GAAP net combined ratio of 70.2%, improving 1.3 points. Direct premiums written grew 19% to $72.5 million, with new business policy count up 35% and retention up 2 points. Management reaffirmed full-year guidance, noted a softening market and increased competition, and highlighted a strengthened reinsurance placement with 14% more capacity and lower core cat costs. Capital returns accelerated with a 20% dividend increase and ongoing buybacks.

negative_highlights: Cleaning revenue down 14% YoY
Component supply tightness noted
Cash burn expected this year due to growth investments
positive_highlights: Revenue up 36% YoY to $292.9 million
H1 orders increased 105% YoY
Received production order for panel-level horizontal plating tool
summary: ACMR reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $292.9 million, up 36% YoY, with ECP and advanced packaging growing over 150%. Orders in H1 rose 105% YoY, and the company raised its full-year revenue guidance midpoint to $1.125-$1.175 billion, implying 25-30% growth. Gross margin was 46% and net cash exceeded $1 billion. The company also announced panel-level plating order wins and progress on PECVD and track platforms.

negative_highlights: Lexington property retention down 9 points due to pricing pressure
North American property growth reduced by over 3 points from disciplined actions
Property pricing competitive, challenging environment
positive_highlights: Adjusted EPS up 10% YoY to $2.00
New business up 37% YoY to $1.9 billion
Global personal combined ratio improved 490 bps
summary: AIG reported Q2 2026 adjusted EPS of $2.00, up 10% YoY, with adjusted after-tax income of $1.1 billion. Underwriting income rose 10% to $686 million, and the accident-year combined ratio improved 30 bps to 88.1%. Net premiums written grew 9% (11% ex-North America property), with global commercial up 9%. Management remains on track for sub-30% expense ratio by 2027, but is cautious on property pricing pressure, reducing Lexington retention by 9 points. Capital returned to shareholders was $904 million including $641 million in buybacks.

negative_highlights: Organic revenue growth was modestly below expectations.
Full-year revenue guidance lowered to 6.9%-7.7% growth.
Revised go-to-market approach did not deliver full expected benefits.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA margin of 43% demonstrates strong profitability.
CARFAX subscription revenue grew 8%, showing durable demand.
Launched new products including CARFAX Homegrown, Showroom, and CARFAX Germany.
summary: Mobility Global reported Q2 FY2026 organic revenue growth of approximately 7%, modestly below expectations, with CARFAX growing 8% and B2B growing 4%. Adjusted EBITDA margin was 43%, reflecting disciplined cost management. Due to first-half top-line performance, full-year revenue guidance was lowered to 6.9%-7.7% growth. Management noted adjustments to the go-to-market approach and softer non-U.S. automotive activity as key factors.

negative_highlights: Total telecom revenue guidance lowered due to copper and cable headwinds
Total operating revenues declined 6% YoY
Legacy revenue pressures largely falling to bottom line, narrowing EBITDA range
positive_highlights: Record first half fiber address delivery, exceeding 2025 second half pace
Residential fiber net adds up 47% YoY
Array cash site rental revenue up 65% YoY
summary: TDS Telecom delivered record first-half fiber address construction, raising 2026 fiber address guidance but lowering total revenue guidance due to legacy copper/cable pressures. Array grew cash site rental revenue 65% YoY and closed spectrum transactions with T-Mobile and Verizon. Overall adjusted EBITDA guidance was narrowed as legacy declines hit the bottom line, while CapEx guidance was increased to fund accelerated fiber builds.

negative_highlights: Book value per share declined 8.1% to $6.83, still down
Non- and sub-performing loans and REO created $0.29 per share earnings drag
SBA 7 originations at $82 million in Q2, well below capacity
positive_highlights: GAAP loss per share improved to $0.63 from $1.25 in Q1
Liquidity plan achieved 81% of target; $1.9 billion cash raised, $1.7 billion debt paid down
Hotel RevPAR increased 20% and occupancy rose 10% to 52%
summary: Ready Capital reported Q2 FY2026 GAAP loss from continuing operations of $0.63 per share, improving from a $1.25 loss in Q1, and distributable earnings loss of $0.47 per share (or $0.24 excluding realized losses), versus a $1.33 loss in Q1. Book value per share fell 8.1% to $6.83, a deceleration from prior quarters. Management emphasized progress on liquidity, raising about $1.9 billion and paying down $1.7 billion of debt, and expects to meet 2026 maturities without further large loan sales, relying on financing optimization, runoff, and asset sales. SBA 7 origination volume was $82 million in Q2, well below capacity, but the company expects growth toward a $1.5 billion annual target following a securitization.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened sequentially to $4.19 million despite expense cuts due to an unrealized digital asset loss of $984k and continued investments in platform commercialization.
Liquidity remains constrained with only $577,000 in cash equivalents; the company explicitly stated it is not providing full-year guidance figures.
Revenue recognition for RoboShare pilot activity is targeted to begin August 2026 subject to operational readiness and revenue recognition requirements.
positive_highlights: Total operating expenses declined substantially to $2.96 million from Q1's $4.33 million, reflecting reduced marketing spend ($86k vs $638k) and lower legal/accounting costs.
Shares outstanding remained unchanged at approximately 20.2-20.3 million shares with no new issuances or debt conversions during the quarter.
Current liabilities decreased significantly to $1.72 million from year-end levels of $3.32 million, aided by a reduction in related party payables.
summary: AIXC reported a net loss of $4.19 million for Q2 FY2026 compared to $1.68 million in the prior year quarter and an improvement from the first quarter's $6.08 million, driven by total operating expenses declining significantly to $2.96 million from $4.33 million in Q1. The company has no specific full-year revenue or loss guidance provided due to liquidity constraints but targets initial RoboShare marketplace activity in Los Angeles beginning August 2026. Management emphasized disciplined capital allocation and a focus on converting the platform foundation into product delivery while noting that digital asset holdings of $5.2 million are volatile.

negative_highlights: Higher-than-expected freight, diesel, and raw material costs due to oil price-driven inflation
Price over cost gap turned positive only in Q4, with Q3 still negative
Residential new construction remains soft in Q2
positive_highlights: Revenue growth 8.6%, organic growth 6.7% with industry-leading volume growth
Cement volumes up 5%, aggregates up 6.5%, with aggregates pricing growth leading
PB Materials exceeding expectations and $1 billion share repurchase program launched
summary: Amrize reported strong Q2 2026 results with revenue growth of 8.6% and organic growth of 6.7%, driven by mega projects in data centers, energy, and infrastructure. Adjusted EBITDA grew 5.8% to $986 million, net income up 14.4%, and adjusted EPS up 8.6%. The company faces oil-driven cost inflation and higher freight rates, but expects price over cost gap to improve in H2 and turn positive in Q4. Full-year guidance was maintained, reflecting confidence in margin recovery. Capital returns included $502 million to shareholders, with a $1 billion buyback program and a quarterly dividend of $0.11 per share.

negative_highlights: Core EPS down 35% year-over-year to $0.13
Higher O&M driven by vegetation management, overhaul costs, and storm response
Expect to accrue a loss from PIMs and SSMs for full-year 2026
positive_highlights: S&P upgraded HEI and Hawaiian Electric to BB-; Moody's upgraded both in April
PUC approved recovery of $350 million WMP spending via EPRM, with plan to use securitization
Commission approved additional solar plus storage PPAs; credit ratings show positive trajectory
summary: HEI reported Q2 2026 core EPS of $0.13, down from $0.20 a year ago, with utility core net income down to $32.6 million from $42.5 million. Results included a non-cash gain from remeasuring the Maui wildfire settlement liability, but core operations were hurt by higher interest expense, O&M costs, and lower interest income. Management reiterated FY2026 O&M headwinds, including no further deferral of wildfire costs and expected PIM/SSM losses, while progressing on rate rebasing and securitization of WMP costs. The company received credit upgrades from S&P and Moody's, but faces regulatory uncertainty around JERA's proposed regulated GenCo and a large new generation RFP.

negative_highlights: Canadian medical impacted by reduced Veterans Affairs reimbursement rates
Adjusted EBITDA still negative at CAD 3.2M
Cash used in operating activities of CAD 25M in Q1
positive_highlights: Net revenue up 13% YoY to CAD 81.2M, with growth across all business lines
Adjusted gross margin up 600 bps YoY to 31%
Adjusted EBITDA loss improved 59% YoY to CAD 3.2M
summary: Canopy Growth reported Q1 FY2027 net revenue of CAD 81.2 million, up 13% year-over-year, with cannabis segment growth of 14% and Storz & Bickel up 6%. Adjusted gross margin expanded 600 basis points to 31% (cannabis segment 26%), and adjusted EBITDA loss improved 59% to CAD 3.2 million. Management reiterated expectations for positive adjusted EBITDA during fiscal 2027 and noted a headwind from Veterans Affairs reimbursement changes, partially mitigated by cost actions. They expect cultivation improvements to impact from late Q2/early Q3.

negative_highlights: Persistency declined slightly from 84.7% to 84% quarter-over-quarter
Mortgage insurance provision for losses increased from $15.3M a year ago to $29.4M
Title and P&C remain modest headwinds due to high rates and soft market
positive_highlights: EPS of $2.08 exceeded both last quarter and year-ago quarter
Reinsurance net premiums written increased eightfold year-over-year
PMIERs sufficiency ratio strong at 172% with $1.5 billion excess assets
summary: Essent Group reported Q2 FY2026 net income of $190 million or $2.08 per diluted share, up from $1.82 last quarter and $1.93 a year ago, with an annualized ROE of 13.4% and book value per share of $63.01 growing nearly 13% year-over-year. The mortgage insurance in-force grew 1.2% year-over-year to $249.7 billion, persistency was 84%, and the default rate was stable at 2.53%. The reinsurance segment saw net premiums written jump to $249 million in H1 2026 from $31 million in H1 2025, with the combined ratio at 77.9% for the quarter, and management maintained its 2026 P&C written premium guidance of approximately $320 million. Capital returns were strong with $350 million in share repurchases year-to-date and a quarterly dividend of $0.35 per share declared.

negative_highlights: Net bookings guidance for Q2 implies a decline vs last year ($1.62-$1.67B vs $1.96B)
Mobile net bookings declined 7% year-over-year, with UA cost pressures noted
Cost of revenue rose 17% due to $43M impairment on an unannounced title
positive_highlights: Net bookings exceeded guidance and recurrent spending beat expectations
GTA VI pre-orders described as exceptional with strong deluxe mix
Full-year guidance reiterated with high confidence in GTA VI launch
summary: Take-Two delivered Q1 FY2027 net bookings of $1.39 billion, slightly above guidance of $1.32-$1.37 billion, driven by NBA 2K and GTA. Recurrent consumer spending declined 1%, better than the guided 3% decline. The company reiterated its full-year net bookings outlook of $8-$8.2 billion, representing ~20% growth, and is confident in the November 19 GTA VI launch. They also raised capex forecast to $290 million due to a real estate purchase and expect to be net cash by year-end.

negative_highlights: Second quarter revenue in line with guidance, not above
Slight sequential decline in average basket in medical-only markets
Flower sold out in Georgia due to capacity ramp not yet fully online
positive_highlights: Medical-only revenue up 4% sequentially
Adjusted EBITDA of $98 million with 36% margin
Georgia traffic tripled in first two weeks of July
summary: Q2 revenue was $271 million, in line with guidance, while medical-only revenue rose 4% sequentially to $222 million. Gross margin was 60% company-wide and 63% for medical-only, with adjusted EBITDA of $98 million (36% margin). Cash balance was $325 million with $53 million operating cash flow. Management raised CapEx guidance by $10 million, noting growth in Georgia and Texas, and flagged positive patient growth trends in Florida, Georgia, and Pennsylvania.

negative_highlights: $115M EBITDA was impacted by customer-friendly sports outcomes
Higher-than-expected customer acquisition spend reduced near-term profitability
Cost discipline remains a major focus
positive_highlights: Customer acquisition grew 75% YoY with best CAC since Q1 2025

Management highlighted production capacity still to ramp up (270,000 bpd) and reaffirmed capital discipline, with no change to guidance.

summary: Galiano Gold reported Q2 fiscal 2026 production of 34,400 ounces, bringing first-half output to 69,000 ounces, near the upper end of guidance. Full-year guidance was maintained at 140,000-160,000 ounces and $2,300-$2,600 AISC. The company continued investing in Nkran Cut 3 pre-stripping and exploration at Esaase and Abore, with a planned hedge roll-off and higher-grade ore expected to improve results in 2027 and beyond.

Management noted strong demand for high-horsepower engines, with AI data center sales reaching 1,800 units, and reiterated a full-year AIDC volume target of 3,500 units. The company raised its 2025 dividend to $0.87 per share and is planning capacity expansion to 5,000 units for high-horsepower engines.

Management noted soft April volumes due to heavy rains, maintained a cautiously optimistic outlook for H2, and highlighted new RIGI projects and road concessions as potential supports.

Management noted continued weak global steel demand and tightness in the Australian PLV spread, while highlighting the ramp-up of the new Wildcat low-vol mine as a positive mix shift.

Guidance was raised, and management expressed confidence in achieving at least 50% ACV bookings growth for the year.

Management highlighted strong free cash flow of $159 million, a 3% share repurchase, and a raised buyback authorization. They remain confident in asset value, with internal estimates of $7 billion+ versus a $4.6 billion enterprise value.

Array's cash site rental revenue rose 65% YoY, and it closed spectrum transactions with T-Mobile and Verizon, while the TDS offer for Array's minority interest remains under review.

Cash receipts from existing home sales rose 15% and 16% in May and June and 8% in July, with the May-July weighted average up 13%. No formal guidance was given; the company cited $105M cash at June 30 and $121M at July 31, aided by a $13M derivative settlement, and described a self-funded AI/Google Cloud and Elius initiative.

Pennsylvania rate case settlement effective July 1st, with Rhode Island rates expected September 1st. Data center pipeline in Pennsylvania grew to ~32 GW signed agreements, with over 11 GW under ESAs, and Invitium JV progressing with over 5 GW CCGT reservations.

Leverage was reduced to 3.3x following the Canadian NGL sale, with $1.75 billion in expected free cash flow for 2026. The tone is optimistic about 2027 momentum and macro tailwinds from Middle East volatility.

The quarter included the closing of the $4.3B Antamina silver stream with BHP, the largest streaming deal ever. Management reaffirmed 2026 production guidance of 860,000-940,000 GEOs and the 50% growth target to 1.2M GEOs by 2030. New assets and Antamina contributed, while Salobo grades were lower. Balance sheet remains strong with net debt of ~$1.9B and liquidity of ~$2.6B.

Orders surged 56% to $709 million, backlog rose to $1.05 billion, and net leverage fell to 2.6x. Full-year guidance was raised to $2.3-$2.4 billion sales, $150-$170 million adjusted EBITDA, and $0.80-$1.20 EPS, reflecting a $22.5 million midpoint EBITDA uplift from revenue and tariff refunds. Non-new machine sales reached a record $706 million on a trailing-twelve-month basis, and July orders exceeded $200 million despite seasonality.

Revenue guidance was raised by $30 million, but adjusted EBITDA, free cash flow, and operating cash flow guidance were reaffirmed. Management highlighted strong pricing, landfill volume growth, and M&A integration, but noted fuel and resource solutions margin headwinds.

NAV per share fell to $15.61 from $15.89, partly due to $24 million in net realized and unrealized losses, including markdowns on SPF and US Infra. Management expects Q2 to be the earnings trough and anticipates increased earnings and supplemental dividends over the next four to six quarters as JVs ramp. Platform originations reached $1.5 billion, up over 20% quarter-over-quarter, but M&A activity remains muted due to geopolitical and macro uncertainty.

They also noted the DOE Genesis Mission award of $60 million for the Prometheus project and the acquisitions of ARMEC and Creative Engineers to strengthen manufacturing capabilities.

U.S. net earned premiums grew 2.3%, but guidance for 2026 net earned premium growth was lowered to just below the 3%-6% range. Management raised its expected Japan benefit ratio to the high end of the 60%-63% guidance range, due to an unfavorable mix of lapses, and reaffirmed strong capital returns and strategic reinsurance expansion.

Management guided Q3 billings growth of 4%-6% and maintained full-year outlook, citing July momentum with mid-single-digit growth and continued AI-driven initiatives.

Management also announced plans to redomicile to the U.S., expecting $0.02-$0.03 EPS benefit, and reiterated no equity issuance through 2027.

U.S. revenue declined 24.6% year-over-year, while international revenue grew 11.5% on a reported basis. The company reiterated its fiscal 2026 guidance and highlighted the successful close of the Owen Mumford acquisition, which contributed modestly in the quarter. Management noted sequential improvement in revenue and profitability, but cited persistent U.S. headwinds and macro factors such as ACA/Medicaid enrollment and GLP-1 adoption.

The company generated $893.5 million in mine-site free cash flow year-to-date, repurchased over $500 million in shares, and ended with net cash. Côté is set to release an updated mine plan by year-end, targeting throughput expansion to 40,000 tons per day and a longer mine life.

Management expressed confidence in future margin expansion and AI-driven efficiencies, but acknowledged the disappointing quarter.

Net debt-to-equity was 1.35x at quarter end, below target of 1.25x post quarter end, and management plans to reactivate share buybacks. Non-accruals improved to 2.9% (from 3.2%), with a net reduction in non-accrual companies to 10. New commitments were modest at $12.9 million, with a wide spread increase of 511 bps versus six months ago. Management noted subdued M&A activity, but a pickup post quarter end, and remains selective in deployment.

Preliminary FY2027 adjusted EBITDA outlook is roughly flat versus a comparable base of ~$1.48 billion, facing volume pressure, inflation, and normalized food service earnings. Management also announced closing two peanut butter plants, impacting FY2028, and expects to pursue cost opportunities in pet food as market share stabilizes.

Management still expects second-half earnings and cash flow improvement, with $45Q credits and CapEx reductions supporting cash.

Management noted that full-year 2026 manufacturing results are expected to remain below last year's record level, though they expressed cautious optimism regarding future quarters supported by new orders.

negative_highlights: Total Non-GAAP gross margin declined 120 bps YoY to 18.6%.
Public Cloud revenue fell 2% YoY reflecting lower infrastructure and services demand.

Strategic partnerships with AMD and Palantir are advancing, targeting 15 MW cumulative AI capacity by end of 2027.

Gross margins expanded sequentially, with non-GAAP gross margin reaching 25.6%, while operating income grew significantly due to favorable project mix in the U.S. and Israel inventory replenishments. Management highlighted strong demand visibility from Europe and North America, noting that customers are increasingly willing to fund capacity expansion directly.

note, general, and administrative expenses rose to $9.2 million due to stock-based compensation
Durability data not expected until after the safety follow-up period following the 13-week or 26-week readouts

Management anticipates an interim proof-of-concept readout later in the year and plans to initiate a Phase II endometriosis trial in Q4.

positive_highlights: EBITDA excluding one-off gain increased 94% year-to-date driven by tariff adjustments and cost reductions.
Operating expenses decreased 8% in the first six months due to workforce optimization and inventory management.
Binding offer for MetroGAS acquisition accepted, subject to regulatory approval expected before year-end.
summary: Edenor reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of ARS 918 billion, a 10% real increase year-over-year driven by tariff adjustments and reduced subsidies. Excluding a one-off gain from a CAMMESA settlement recognized in the prior period, EBITDA increased 94% year-to-date due to higher tariffs and an 8% reduction in operating expenses. The company highlighted strong service quality with record-low outage durations and announced the acceptance of its binding offer to acquire MetroGAS.

negative_highlights: Distributable earnings of $0.44 per basic share fell note weakness in of the $0.47 quarterly dividend
Net interest income declined 2.2% quarter-over-quarter to $12.8 million on prepayment redeployment timing and lower one-time fee income ($0.8 million vs $1.1 million)
Total leverage rose to 47% of book equity from 38%, and available liquidity on the senior credit facility is now approximately $15 million
positive_highlights: Non-accrual loans declined to 3.7% of principal from 4.8% in Q1 2026
Weighted average yield to maturity held steady at 15.8%, with only 3.6% of principal exposed to further rate declines
Koach Capital transaction issued ~4.3 million shares at $14.53, a 1% premium to March 31 book value, adding $62.5 million of notes at a 12% blended rate
summary: REFI reported Q2 FY2026 distributable earnings of $0.44 per basic share, below the $0.47 quarterly dividend, with net interest income of $12.8 million down 2.2% from $13.1 million in Q1 due to a timing gap between $16.3 million of early prepayments and later capital redeployment. Portfolio principal rose to $453 million across 26 companies with a 15.8% weighted average yield, total leverage increased to 47% of book equity from 38%, and non-accruals declined to 3.7% from 4.8%. Management announced the Koach Capital transaction ($62.5 million of second-lien notes at a 12% blended rate in exchange for ~4.3 million shares at a 1% premium to book) and reaffirmed the expected Q4 2026 close of the LIEN merger, while guiding to a 90-100% dividend payout ratio for 2026 and distributing all or nearly all taxable income through the merger date.

negative_highlights: Revenue missed expectations due to extended protest periods and low-margin material volume impacting near-term dynamics.
Preliminary FY2027 outlook includes a specific revenue impact of approximately 3% from NASA's workforce insourcing directive.
Company is exiting several domestic-based operations representing roughly 1% of total revenue that are no- or low-margin.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA increased to $290 million with record quarterly margins of 8.3%, up 60 bps year-over-year.
Net bookings reached $3.9 billion, resulting in a trailing twelve-month book-to-bill ratio of 1.3x.
Raised full-year fiscal 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance by approximately $50 million to the range of $1.115B-$1.14B.
summary: Third quarter revenue of $3.5 billion came in slightly below expectations due to protest delays and low-margin material volume, though adjusted EBITDA hit a record $290 million with margins expanding to 8.3%. Management raised full-year fiscal 2026 guidance for adjusted EBITDA ($1.115B-$1.14B) and EPS ($2.40-$2.50), while maintaining free cash flow expectations, despite acknowledging a preliminary FY2027 revenue headwind of approximately 3% from NASA workforce directives.

negative_highlights: Q2 revenue was at the low end of guidance due solely to a delayed seven-figure customer contract extension.
A commercial ASIC design targeting Intel 18A is being removed from H2 forecast with potential shift to 2027.
Mature product revenue growth slowed, expected to be flat for full year FY26 compared to prior years.
positive_highlights: Non-GAAP gross margin expanded to 46.8%, significantly above the midpoint outlook.
Net loss narrowed to $1.1 million (vs $1.5M prior year), with cash balance increasing to $13.5 million.
Government contract ceiling increased to $89 million, expected to drive significant Q4 revenue.
summary: QuickLogic reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $5.5 million (up 48.7% YoY), which missed the midpoint of guidance due to a delayed contract extension and an uncertain commercial ASIC design targeting Intel 18A, leading management to narrow full-year growth outlook to 70%-80%. Management forecast flat Q3 revenue but raised confidence in securing new contracts for late-stage negotiations and government work. The company expects non-GAAP profitability and cash flow positive operations for the second half of FY26.

negative_highlights: Net sales declined to $102.9 million from $113.1 million in the prior year, primarily due to the closure of the U.K. cast roll facility.
Q2 results reflect a one-time decline rather than organic weakness; however, revenue is down compared to the same period last year.
positive_highlights: Customer orders increased approximately 50% versus the prior year to $144 million, indicating accelerating demand across segments.
Backlog grew from Q1 levels ($38.5M) to $39.9 million in Air and Liquid Systems alone (total backlog implied higher), reflecting record order activity.
Adjusted EBITDA improved 22% sequentially versus Q1 of the current year as restructuring impacts fade.
summary: Ampco-Pittsburgh reported Q2 FY2026 net sales of $102.9 million and adjusted EBITDA of $9.8 million (margin expanding to 9.5%), representing a significant sequential improvement as the impact from prior U.K. facility closure flows through results. Customer orders surged by approximately 50% year-over-year, with backlog growing substantially to $385.4 million driven by strong demand in Air and Liquid Systems and recovering roll shipments in Forged and Cast Engineered Products. Management expects a significantly stronger second half of the year despite normal seasonal outages.
