negative_highlights: GAAP net loss widened slightly to $29.7 million due to increased operating expenses associated with scaling commercial support and project development.
Adjusted EBITDA remains a loss of $17 million, though the company notes this is an inflection point as it transitions from build-to-transfer models.
positive_highlights: Revenue doubled year-over-year driven by Australian project progress and new US contracts.
Backlog increased approximately $650 million quarter-over-quarter to roughly $2 billion, more than doubling from a year ago.
Raised full-year revenue guidance range significantly while narrowing the gross margin outlook to 20%-25%.
summary: NRGV reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $17.4 million (up 104% YoY) and GAAP gross margin expanding to 31%. Management raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to a range of $270-$310 million from the prior $225-$300 million, citing strong backlog growth to roughly $2 billion. The company highlighted its largest-ever contract (1.25 GW) and improved liquidity with cash ending at $148 million.

negative_highlights: Results were essentially flat versus expectations due to late Q2 white space and volatile commodity prices muting customer response.
Drilling-focused revenue mix (approx. 23%) limited incremental margins compared to higher-margin service lines like completions.
Company elected PIK interest on senior notes for the second quarter, adding $8.2 million to principal rather than paying cash.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA increased 68% sequentially to approximately $19 million due to operating leverage and WolfPack contribution.
Q3 revenue guidance raised significantly with a midpoint of $182 million implying mid-single digit growth in the base business excluding acquisitions.
WolfPack acquisition integration progressing smoothly, contributing $3.4M in June with an annual run rate of ~$41 million.
summary: Second quarter revenue was $167.3 million (up 15.6% sequentially) and adjusted EBITDA was $18.7 million, with results coming in at the midpoint of guidance despite late June white space. Management raised Q3 revenue guidance to a range of $176-$188 million ($182m midpoint), citing improved activity levels driven by WolfPack integration and seasonal normalization. The company announced a proactive $125 million backstop equity rights offering designed to reduce leverage, improve liquidity, and strengthen the balance sheet.

negative_highlights: Free cash flow was an outflow of CAD 3.9 million due to working capital investments supporting scale and inventory buildup
Canadian vape share gains were limited to a single month (June) before declines reversed, indicating early-stage recovery rather than sustained trend yet
positive_highlights: Record net revenue of CAD 105.8 million driven by Sanity Group contributions exceeding EUR 24.5M in Q1 post-acquisition
Adjusted gross margin expanded to 37% (up 300 bps YoY) and adjusted EBITDA reached record CAD 13.4 million
Sanity revenue for the full quarter exceeded EUR 25M, meeting acquisition expectations with growth expected in Q4
summary: OrganiGram reported record Q3 FY2026 net revenue of CAD 105.8 million (up 49% YoY) and adjusted gross margin expansion to 37%, driven by Sanity Group contributions which exceeded EUR 25M expectations for the full quarter. Adjusted EBITDA hit a new high of CAD 13.4 million, while Canadian share recovery in vapes and pre-rolls offset slightly lower domestic market share due to portfolio rationalization. Management raised guidance expecting revenue above CAD 350M for FY26 and meaningful margin expansion.

negative_highlights: Reported adjusted EBITDA margin diluted by 60 bps due to elevated metal cost inflation, specifically regarding hafnium prices rising from ~$5k/kg to $12.5k-$13k/kg.
Turbo Wheels division reported an Adjusted EBITDA fall of $0.6 million YoY largely attributable to the sale of Ivostud business.
CapEx expected to remain at elevated levels during this investment phase, impacting near-term cash flow conversion.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 34% YoY to a record $269 million, with Engine Products growing 39% overall (Europe +49%, North America +29%).
Adjusted EBITDA margin improved 180 bps QoQ to 17.8%; excluding metal pass-through impact, the underlying organic margin expansion was robust.
Signed fourth strategic partnership with an aerospace OEM underpinning a new greenfield superalloy site in Alabama.
summary: DPC Holdings reported record Q2 FY26 revenue of $269 million (up 34% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $48 million (up 33%), driven by strong growth in Engine Products segments. Adjusted EPS was $0.05, representing a significant recovery from the prior year's loss as net income moved into profit. Management initiated full-year guidance for revenue between $1 billion-$1.04 billion and adjusted EBITDA of $182 million-$187 million.

negative_highlights: Loan growth expectations lowered significantly for the year, with real growth now projected between 10% and 15%.
Net fee income is expected to decline between 5% and 8% in real terms due to softer activity.
Cost of risk remains elevated at a run rate around 5.6%, though guidance suggests it will stay within the challenging range of 5.3%-5.8%.
positive_highlights: Attributable net income turned positive at ARS 13 billion, a swing of more than ARS 31 billion from Q1 loss.
Structural ROE reached 14.4% after incorporating full quarterly salary savings and excluding extraordinary severance charges.
NIM expanded sequentially by 250 bps to 20.3%, driven by funding costs declining faster than asset yields.
summary: Grupo Supervielle returned to profitability in Q2 FY2026 with attributable net income of ARS 13 billion and adjusted net income of ARS 36 billion following a loss in the prior quarter. Management updated full-year guidance, lowering real loan growth expectations to 10%-15% from previously higher targets due to subdued retail demand, while raising NIM guidance to 17%-19%. The rightsizing program is largely complete with structural ROE reaching 14.4%, though management notes margin pressure in the second half as asset repricing begins.

negative_highlights: Reported net income declined year-over-year due to approximately $3.3 million in transaction costs associated with the Flatrock acquisition.
The second quarter effective tax rate was elevated at 30.9% compared to a full-year expectation of roughly 25%-26%, driven by discrete state tax items.
positive_highlights: Rental revenue reached a record $49.4 million, up approximately 25% year-over-year.
Adjusted gross margin expanded to 61.1%, an increase of roughly 36 basis points despite inflationary cost pressures.
Full-year Adjusted EBITDA guidance was raised from the prior range of $92.5M-$97.5M to a new record high of $103M-$108M.
summary: NGS reported record Q2 FY26 results with rental revenue of $49.4 million (up ~25% YoY) and adjusted gross margin expanding to 61.1%. The company increased full-year Adjusted EBITDA guidance to $103-$108M from the prior range of $92.5-$97.5M, driven by a Flatrock acquisition contribution that added roughly half a month in Q2 and contracted organic growth raising expectations for 2026 deployments.

negative_highlights: Management explicitly stated they are not providing clear production guidance for H2 of the year due to a desire to maintain flexibility after deferring deliveries.
The company confirmed it is not interested in spot sales, preferring to protect inventory for future opportunistic pricing or loan repayment.
Shirley Basin operations were limited until late June as they awaited regulatory authorization from the state.
positive_highlights: Production increased significantly to 141,000 pounds (up 26% YoY) following the installation of a sand filtration system that removed flow constraints at Lost Creek.
Shirley Basin is now in full operation with six of ten production columns online and first shipments imminent after receiving regulatory authorization.
Cash cost per pound remained low at $40.20, including ad valorem and severance taxes.
summary: Ur-Energy reported Q2 FY2026 production of 141,000 pounds at Lost Creek and initial capture of 10,634 pounds at Shirley Basin, resulting in $14.4 million in sales revenue from contracted deliveries totaling 215,000 pounds. Management proactively deferred 300,000 pounds of 2026 deliveries to later years to manage ramp-up risk and maintain flexibility rather than providing specific volume guidance for the remainder of the year. While operational execution improved with sand filtration installation increasing flow rates at Lost Creek, the company explicitly stated it is not interested in spot sales and will prioritize inventory protection.

negative_highlights: Non-GAAP gross margin contracted to 32.2% (down from 35.2% YoY) due to geographical mix and cost pressures.
Full-year non-GAAP operating income guidance was lowered, with margins expected between 5%-6% versus a previous midpoint of 6.5%-7.5%.
Supply chain challenges regarding component availability are expected to persist through the remainder of FY2026.
positive_highlights: India bookings reached $120 million year-to-date, representing the highest level since Q1 FY2024.
North America revenue from a key Tier 1 carrier exceeded initial expectations despite some shipment timing shifts.
Record private network bookings were secured in North America with diverse use cases.
summary: Ceragon reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $93.9 million (up 14% YoY) and non-GAAP EPS of $0.02, driven by strong bookings in India ($120M YTD). Management reiterated full-year 2026 revenue guidance but lowered the gross margin outlook to a range of 33.5%-34.5% (from previously implied higher levels) and operating income guidance due to persistent supply chain cost pressures.

negative_highlights: Company explicitly stated it expects its first commercial revenue in 2027, indicating no current or near-term sales
Management declined to disclose the size of the drone order due to customer confidentiality concerns
No GAAP financial results (revenue/EPS) were reported as this is an inaugural call for a newly public company
positive_highlights: Achieved the first commercial battery order from a separate leading U.S. drone manufacturer
Demonstrated >30% increase in flight range for customer drones using solid-state technology before engineering optimization
Reached an automotive integration milestone with Stellantis, becoming the first solid-state battery maker to achieve successful vehicle integration with two top 10 global OEMs
summary: Factorial Energy reported Q2 FY2026 operating expenses of $13 million and non-GAAP operating expenses of $14.5 million for the six months ended June 30, which were in line with expectations; capital expenditures totaled $0.6 million for the half-year against a full-year expectation of approximately $13 million. The company announced its first commercial battery order from a U.S. drone manufacturer and achieved an automotive integration milestone with Stellantis, but explicitly stated that it expects to generate its first commercial revenue in 2027.

negative_highlights: Piceance segment adjusted EBITDA decreased $0.9M quarter-over-quarter due to a 5.7% decline in volume throughput from temporary shut-ins.
Full-year guidance was tightened (narrowed) despite strong first-half performance, reflecting uncertainty on second-half commodity pricing assumptions.
Piceance segment expects cash flow step-down starting Q4 as roughly $4M/quarter of shortfall payments expire.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA increased 12% quarter-over-quarter to $60.7 million driven by volume growth in Rockies ($30.4M) and Mid-Con ($21.4M).
Realized crude oil prices rose approximately 30% quarter-over-quarter, benefiting percentage-of-proceeds contracts.
Secured two new gathering agreements in Divide County adding visibility to ~30 new well connections not previously contemplated.
summary: Summit Midstream reported Q2 FY2026 adjusted EBITDA of $60.7 million (a 12% increase vs Q1), driven by volume growth in Rockies and Mid-Con segments alongside a ~30% quarter-over-quarter rise in realized crude oil prices. Management tightened full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance to a range of $235-$255 million while raising capital expenditure guidance to $100-$120 million, citing new well connections and Double E expansion projects.

negative_highlights: Consolidated occupancy growth (82.4%) came in slightly below expectations with only an 110 bps increase on a same-community basis.
Revenue declined 8.7% YoY due to a 15.7% reduction in average units from portfolio optimization activities, partially offset by higher RevPAR.
Other facility operating expenses were elevated during the quarter due to variability including repairs and maintenance.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA of $122.1 million beat consensus estimates and grew 4.3% year-over-year.
RevPAR growth of 8.2% met the full-year guidance target, with RevPOR increasing 5.2% YoY as price concessions from last year are lapped.
Labor expense declined to 45.2% of revenue on a same-community basis, improving 90 bps YoY due to operational focus and hiring discipline.
summary: Brookdale Senior Living reported Q2 FY2026 adjusted EBITDA of $122.1 million (up 4.3% YoY) and RevPAR growth of 8.2%, meeting the full-year guidance range but missing occupancy expectations which grew only 230 bps to 82.4%. Management reaffirmed its annual guidance for adjusted EBITDA ($502M-$516M) and RevPAR (8%-9%), noting that Q3 growth will be similar to Q2 before accelerating in Q4 due to disposition timing, while acknowledging a slight occupancy shortfall driven by move-outs.

negative_highlights: GAAP net loss was substantial at $596.5 million, primarily due to one-time IPO-related costs including a catch-up stock-based compensation expense of roughly $447.5 million.
Adjusted EBITDA remained in the red with a non-GAAP net loss of $73 million for the quarter compared to a prior year loss of $43.5 million.
R&D expenses were elevated at $367 million, including significant stock-based compensation related to IPO triggers.
positive_highlights: Revenue surged 279% year-over-year driven by significant growth in the cloud business, reaching $8 million for Q2 FY26.
Year-to-date bookings reached approximately $81 million, with management expecting full-year 2026 revenue between $28-$32 million.
Achieved a major technical milestone on Sol system components via Honeywell Aerospace validation without showstoppers and demonstrated near five-nines logical fidelities on Helios.
summary: Quantinuum reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $8 million (up 279% YoY) and bookings of $4.3 million, with year-to-date bookings reaching approximately $81 million against a full-year guidance range of $28-$32 million for 2026. The company highlighted significant progress on its Sol system roadmap via Honeywell Aerospace validation and secured major strategic partnerships including an LOI from the U.S. Department of Commerce, agreements with Oracle and HPE, and new manufacturing alliances to scale supply chains. Management expressed high confidence in their technology leadership and commercial momentum despite acknowledging that quarterly results may remain volatile as they transition into a public company.

negative_highlights: Management characterized Q2 growth as 'modest' rather than a strong beat.
Retail channel take-up remains poor with limited visibility into refill dynamics outside the e-pharmacy segment.
Net loss of $31.9 million and no positive EPS reported.
positive_highlights: July script volume increased over 45% month-over-month following the launch of telehealth and national TV campaigns.
60% of e-pharmacy patients have purchased more than one monthly pack, indicating strong early refill behavior compared to competitors like VUITY (10-12%).
Over 75% of prescribing physicians (>13,000) are repeat prescribers.
summary: LENZ reported Q2 FY2026 total revenues of $5.5 million ($1.7M product revenue) and a net loss per share of $1.02 on a net loss of $31.9 million, with no GAAP or adjusted EPS provided in the text. Management highlighted an over 45% month-over-month increase in July prescriptions driven by new telehealth initiatives and national TV advertising, but explicitly stated that Q2 results were 'modest' growth rather than a significant beat. Guidance for H2 remains focused on assessing patient persistence data to align capital allocation with demonstrated performance.

negative_highlights: ReMEDy2 interim analysis readout moved to Q1 2027 from the previously indicated Q4, after enrollment slowed in July
Cash and investments declined to $43.5M from $59.9M at Dec 31, 2025, with H1 operating cash use up to $17.2M from $14.7M
R&D expense rose to $8.2M from $5.8M a year earlier (H1 $16.1M vs $11.5M) and management guided to a further moderate increase
positive_highlights: Part 1a extension cohort: mean systolic BP fell 29.1 mmHg from a 169.3 mmHg baseline (p<0.001) and diastolic fell 17 mmHg (p<0.01), with systolic holding below 160 at all time points over 24 hours
Mid-dose cohorts 4-8 produced clinically meaningful reductions in both maternal blood pressure and uterine artery pulsatility index, supporting the 5-10 mcg/kg dose range for the next studies
Cash of $43.5M with stated runway through 2027, covering the ReMEDy2 interim analysis, preeclampsia/FGR readouts, and Canada/U.K. Phase II expansion
summary: Pre-revenue clinical-stage biotech: no product revenue or EPS; R&D rose to $8.2M in Q2 2026 vs $5.8M a year earlier, G&A was $2.3M, and net cash used in operations was $17.2M for H1 vs $14.7M. Cash and investments fell to $43.5M from $59.9M at Dec 31, 2025, with management stating runway extends through 2027, covering the ReMEDy2 interim analysis and preeclampsia/FGR readouts. Operationally, the first FGR cohort (6 patients at 5 mcg/kg) completed enrollment, the Part 1a late-onset preeclampsia extension cohort (12 patients at the highest dose) was completed with statistically significant blood pressure reductions (systolic -29.1 mmHg, p<0.001), and ReMEDy2 surpassed 85% of the 200 patients needed to trigger the interim analysis, though the readout slipped from Q4 2026 to Q1 2027 after enrollment slowed in July. Still running a rat PK/pharmacologic study (data ~October) to support a U.S. IND.

negative_highlights: Asset quality is 'slightly below plan' with nonaccruals comprising 8.5% of total cost and 26% of the portfolio marked at investment category three or below.
Other income was lower than historical levels due to reduced cash balances available for sweep, rather than operational issues.
Dividend payments exceeded earnings by $0.08 per share as management distributed remaining spillover income from prior periods.
positive_highlights: Portfolio received five full repayments totaling $38.7 million plus $10 million in other par repayments during the quarter.
Realized and unrealized gains contributed $0.30 per share, driven by specific company performance improvements and a reversal of prior realized losses.
External advisor Stellus Capital Management officially joined Ridgepost Capital platform to leverage broader sponsor relationships.
summary: Stellus Capital reported Q2 FY2026 results with GAAP net investment income of $0.26 per share and core NII also at $0.26, resulting in a NAV increase driven by realized/unrealized gains rather than organic earnings growth. Management lowered the quarterly dividend to $0.25 due to reduced spillover cash balances but expects to return to higher distributions as income normalizes. The portfolio fair value decreased slightly from Q1 despite new investments and repayments, with asset quality noted as 'slightly below plan' due to elevated nonaccruals.

negative_highlights: Q4 revenue of $11.1B was near the low end of guidance due to customer delays regarding power shortage and cooling readiness, pushing recognition into subsequent quarters.
AI solutions contribution dropped from over 80% in Q3 to approximately 60% in Q4 as large AI project ramps were delayed.
Cash conversion cycle deteriorated significantly by 43 days (from 106 to 149) and inventory days increased due to building stock for anticipated FY27 growth.
positive_highlights: Non-GAAP gross margin expanded significantly to 17.6%, beating guidance by over 9 percentage points due to favorable customer/product mix and lower inventory reserves.
Fiscal year 2026 revenue reached a record $39 billion, up 78% from the prior fiscal year.
Backlog surged with over $60 billion in new orders received during Q4.
summary: Supermicro reported Q4 FY26 revenue of $11.1 billion and non-GAAP EPS of $1.70, both missing the company's own guidance due to customer delays in power readiness and cooling that pushed shipments into subsequent quarters. While gross margins expanded significantly to 17.6% (beating guidance) driven by favorable mix and one-time inventory/tariff benefits, management explicitly warned that Q4 results were not fully comparable year-over-year because of these timing shifts. The company raised its full fiscal year 2027 revenue outlook to a range of $65 billion-$72 billion despite the near-term shipment delays.

negative_highlights: note weakness in-term disruption in GEO satellite connectivity business estimated at approximately $60M annualized due to LEO transition
Test systems segment operating profit was only $600,000 impacted by zero-margin revenue from raw material purchases for Army programs
positive_highlights: Record Q2 revenue of $260M representing a 27% year-over-year increase
Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to 19.8%, more than double the prior year quarter's level
Aerospace bookings reached an all-time high of $306 million with a book-to-bill ratio above one
summary: Astronics reported record Q2 FY26 revenue of $260 million (up 27% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA margin expansion to 19.8%, driven by volume leverage and a one-time tariff refund. Management raised full-year revenue guidance to the range of $1.02 billion-$1.04 billion, crossing the billion-dollar threshold for the first time. The company highlighted strong momentum in aerospace bookings ($306 million) and significant progress on margin improvement levers including pricing adjustments and workforce stability.

negative_highlights: Total revenue declined 1.8% year-over-year due to a 4.5% reduction in pounds processed
Field segment remains the only growth driver not yet showing improvement, requiring correction
Significant margin gap exists between top-performing and lowest-performing market centers
positive_highlights: Revenue per pound grew by $0.04 (3%) year-over-year for the first time since becoming a public company
Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to 12.2% from 9.8%, with Adjusted EBITDA up $15 million YoY
Full-year free cash flow guidance raised by $40 million, now expecting range of $160M-$170M
summary: Vestis reported Q3 FY26 revenue of $662 million (down 1.8% YoY) and Adjusted EBITDA of $81 million (up 23% YoY), driven by a return to positive Revenue Per Pound growth for the first time as a public company despite volume declines from exiting low-quality linen business. Management raised full-year free cash flow guidance midpoint to $165 million, citing strong working capital execution and transformation benefits realized in Q4.

negative_highlights: Leadership transition with Dr. Ying Huang stepping down as CEO and Alan Bash serving as Interim CEO.
Gross margin variability expected in the near term, specifically a dip into the lower 50% range for Q3 before rebounding to mid-50s in Q4 due to outpatient mix shifts.
positive_highlights: Adjusted net income reached $63 million ($0.16/diluted share), marking the first quarterly profit in history.
CARVYKTI global sales grew 50% year-over-year to $657 million, driven by strong ex-U.S. growth of 128% and accelerating adoption in earlier lines (now >70% volume).
Gross margin on net product sales improved significantly to 58%, up from Q1's artificially low level due to unwinding one-time manufacturing costs.
summary: Legend Biotech reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $341 million (implied from context) with total revenue growing 52% year-over-year to reach a new milestone in profitability. Adjusted net income was $63 million, representing an adjusted EPS of $0.16 per diluted share compared to $0.03 last year. The company achieved its first quarter of company-wide profitability on both IFRS and adjusted bases.

negative_highlights: Net revenue growth slowed to just 2% YoY, missing consensus expectations and falling note weakness in of management's internal guidance range.
Management explicitly stated that H1 performance was worse than expected due to a tough comparison from the previous year following massive repricing in Q3/Q4 FY25.
High Selic rates continue to create pressure on profitability, with rate cuts not coming at the magnitude initially expected.
positive_highlights: Total credit portfolio grew impressively by 31% year-over-year to BRL 52 billion, driven by working capital and credit cards.
Non-GAAP EPS increased 10% YoY supported by earnings resilience and share buybacks reducing the average shares outstanding.
NPL90 remained low at 3.4%, significantly below the Brazilian market average of 6.2%.
summary: PagSeguro reported Q2 FY26 net revenue of BRL 3.4 billion (up 2% YoY) and non-GAAP EPS of BRL 2.06 (up 10% YoY), beating expectations but missing the top end of its full-year guidance range due to a challenging macro environment and elevated interest rates. Management maintained its full-year gross profit guidance despite headwinds, citing expected sequential improvements in financial costs during H2 as key drivers for meeting targets.

negative_highlights: Silver production decreased 17%, lead by 15%, and zinc by 15% due to lower grades and voluntary suspension for safety upgrades.
Cash cost per ounce of silver net of byproduct credits surged to $2.45 from $1.26 in the prior year quarter, a 94% increase.
Management indicated full-year production guidance is premature and may need review as operations resume.
positive_highlights: Revenue rose 70% year-over-year to CAD 139 million driven by a 135% increase in realized silver note price averaging above $69/oz.
Free cash flow reached nearly CAD 29 million, up 27% from the prior year quarter.
Production costs at Ying remained below annual guidance range of $88-$90 per ton despite currency headwinds.
summary: Silvercorp reported Q1 FY2027 revenue of CAD 139 million (up 70% YoY) and net income of CAD 59.4 million, driven by a 135% increase in realized silver prices despite production declines at its Chinese operations due to safety upgrades. Management explicitly stated that full-year guidance is premature given the temporary shutdowns affecting Ying and GC mines, with current output running at only 40-50% of target for Q2.

negative_highlights: Q2 revenue of $14.9M missed prior year Q2 ($15.3M) and implied expectations following a recent capital raise
Cash balance declined from $78.2M at end-2025 to $54.9M before the financing, indicating cash burn despite margin improvements
Management described revenue cadence as 'lumpy' and unpredictable due to customer stocking behaviors for newly approved products
positive_highlights: Gross margin expanded to 73%, an improvement over Q1 FY26 and full-year 2025 levels driven by higher sales of more profitable products
Net loss narrowed from $13.3M in the prior year quarter to $12.0M, reflecting lower R&D ($11.7M vs $13.8M) and SG&A expenses ($10.9M vs $12.3M)
Equity financing closed two weeks ago raising approximately $25 million in net proceeds, extending the cash runway projection through 2028
summary: Total revenue was $14.9 million in Q2 FY26, down from $15.3 million the prior year quarter and below implied consensus given recent financing news; management raised full-year guidance to a range of $72-76M (back-half weighted) despite missing quarterly targets. Gross margin improved sequentially to 73% driven by higher sales of profitable products following four new regulatory approvals in 2026, while R&D and SG&A declined due to headcount reductions and lower stock-based compensation.

negative_highlights: Food costs increased by 50 basis points YoY due to input price inflation associated with the new salmon launch.

Same-restaurant sales were pressured for a portion of the quarter by Cyclospora outbreak concerns, requiring management to maintain a prudent full-year outlook that includes potential lingering headwinds.
Labor costs rose 30 basis points YoY due to incremental wage investments in team members.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 31.3% YoY driven by a robust 9% increase in same-restaurant sales and strong new unit productivity above 100%.
Same-restaurant sales recovered from flat-to-positive levels to mid-single digits as Cyclospora consumer concerns eased during the quarter's final weeks.
New restaurant openings continued to outperform expectations, reinforcing brand portability in markets like Indiana and Ohio.
summary: CAVA reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $365.4 million (up 31.3% YoY) and Adjusted EBITDA of $54.7 million (up 30%), driven by a 9% same-restaurant sales increase on 5.3% traffic growth, though food costs rose 50 bps due to salmon launch input prices. Management reiterated full-year guidance for 75-77 net new openings and mid-single-digit SSS, explicitly incorporating the lingering impact of Cyclospora outbreak concerns which caused same-store sales to dip before recovering sequentially in July.

negative_highlights: iGaming revenue was essentially flat year-over-year to $17 million, impacted by a significant increase in the U.K. gambling tax rate.
Average monthly revenue per payer declined from $286 to $218 due to the inclusion of WHOW Games metrics and market dynamics.
Operating expenses increased 10% year-over-year primarily due to the acquisition integration costs for WHOW Games.
positive_highlights: Consolidated revenue grew 11% year-over-year to $94.3 million, outperforming the industry forecast of a market decline over 5% for social casino.
Direct-to-consumer (DTC) contribution in social casino surged from ~15% last year to 52% this quarter, significantly improving margin dynamics.
Adjusted EBITDA expanded by $5.8 million sequentially and reached an all-time quarterly high of $39.3 million.
summary: DoubleDown Interactive reported Q2 FY2026 consolidated revenue of $94.3 million, an increase of approximately 11% year-over-year compared to $84.8 million in the prior period. Adjusted EBITDA reached a record contribution for the quarter at $39.3 million (up 17%), driven by strong social casino growth and improved profitability from direct-to-consumer initiatives, which now account for over half of that segment's revenue. Management maintained its strategic focus on operational excellence and DTC migration while noting sequential flatness in iGaming due to U.K. tax adjustments.

negative_highlights: Total operating expenses increased compared to Q2 FY2025 driven by clinical operations and development costs
Personnel-related costs including stock-based compensation rose as the workforce grew in support of clinical functions
Operating expenses are expected to increase quarter-over-quarter for the remainder of 2026 due to continued investment in clinical operations
positive_highlights: Three-year follow-up data showed FICERA nearly doubled overall survival versus standard of care in HPV-negative head and neck cancer
Company has approximately $497 million in cash equivalents providing runway into the first half of 2029
FORTIFI-FLEX alternative dosing study was successfully initiated to support a streamlined regimen
summary: Bicara Therapeutics reported Q2 FY2026 results with total operating expenses increasing compared to the prior year quarter due to clinical operations and development costs for its pivotal FORTIFI-HN01 study. The company ended the period with approximately $497 million in cash, providing a runway into the first half of 2029. Management highlighted strong momentum from recent ASCO data but noted that operating expenses are expected to increase quarter-over-quarter through year-end as they prepare for potential commercialization.

negative_highlights: Natural gas production averaged 37.3 MMcm per day, down 6% year-over-year due to the exit from conventional fields.
CapEx increased by 16% interannually and 37% sequentially compared to prior periods.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA reached a record high of $2.8 billion, representing the best quarterly performance in YPF history.
Shale oil production hit an all-time high of 213,000 bpd, with shale now comprising roughly 95% of total oil output excluding divested conventional assets.
Refinery processing set a new record at 351,000 bpd, generating surplus gasoline and middle distillates for export.
summary: YPF reported a record-breaking Q2 FY2026 with revenues of $6.6 billion (up 42% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA reaching $2.8 billion, marking the best quarter in company history. Management raised full-year guidance for adjusted EBITDA to approximately $8 billion from a previous expectation of around $6 billion, driven by higher Brent price assumptions ($75/bbl vs prior $63). The company also increased its CapEx forecast range to $5.8-$6.2 billion and expects net leverage to decline significantly to nearly 1x.

negative_highlights: Input costs for soybean oil remain elevated, partially offsetting favorable pricing in the biofuels segment.
Biofuel capacity utilization was only 56%, with production expected to ramp higher in Q3 following a three-week outage earlier in the period.
positive_highlights: Total revenue surged 120% YoY to $78.7 million driven by volume increases of 40% and price realizations up 80%.
summary: FutureFuel reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $78.7 million, a 120% increase year-over-year driven by volume growth and pricing improvements across its specialty chemicals and biofuels segments. The company returned to profitability with gross profit of $15 million (up from a loss in the prior period) and adjusted EBITDA of $11.8 million versus an annualized run-rate loss previously reported, marking a return to profitable growth for 2026. Management highlighted improved plant reliability, regulatory clarity on biofuels mandates, and elevated input costs as key drivers.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened significantly from $5 million to $6.6 million due to increased R&D ($3.9M) and G&A expenses.
Cash burn accelerated, with operating cash flow usage rising to approximately $10 million in the first half of FY26 compared to $7.3 million prior year.
No revenue recognized from new customers yet; income remains entirely dependent on future milestone achievements.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew year-over-year to approximately $33 million, driven by commercialization efforts.
Expanded Stage 3 customer base to five programs, including a new Fortune Global 500 client focused on scale-across applications.
Secured multiple foundry runs with wafers expected for delivery in August and Q4.
summary: Lightwave Logic reported Q2 FY26 revenue of approximately $33 million (up from $26M prior year) and a net loss widening to $6.6 million ($0.04/share). The company expanded its commercial pipeline with five Stage 3 customers, including one Fortune Global 500 firm moving into execution phase for scale-across transceivers. Management highlighted progress on foundry wafers expected in August but noted that revenue recognition remains contingent on future milestones and qualification.

negative_highlights: Antimony average note price fell approximately 52% from $28.32 per pound to $13.70 per pound
Operating loss for the quarter was about $7 million, including roughly $3.4 million in non-cash items
Full-year revenue guidance lowered due to depressed antimony pricing environment
positive_highlights: Antimony volume increased approximately 26% year-over-year to 428,425 lbs sold
Zeolite segment revenue surged 110% year-over-year driven by a 114% increase in tons sold
Cash and cash equivalents strengthened significantly to $41.4 million at quarter end
summary: Second quarter revenue declined approximately 25% year-over-year to $7.9 million due to a roughly 52% drop in realized antimony prices despite higher volumes; gross margin compressed from 27% to 7%. Management lowered full-year guidance to $60-$75 million citing the significant decline in commodity pricing, while noting that DLA deliveries will begin recognizing revenue starting in Q3.

negative_highlights: Management declined to reinstate guidance citing the ongoing wind-down of Abilene operations as a prerequisite for future outlooks.
Gross margins are expected to adjust down from current elevated levels toward more typical ranges in subsequent periods due to mix changes.
positive_highlights: Consolidated revenue surged 67% year-over-year to $24.3 million driven by both segments.
Adjusted EBITDA improved significantly from a loss of $1.1M in the prior period to positive $1.6M.
Industrial Solutions booked record orders of $17.2 million, extending its backlog growth streak to eight consecutive quarters.
summary: Broadwind reported Q2 FY26 consolidated revenue of $24.3 million (up 67% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA turning positive at $1.6 million from a loss in the prior year period. Management highlighted record backlog growth across both segments, with Industrial Solutions orders reaching $17.2 million and Gearing orders rising to $16 million. While results were strong on all metrics, management explicitly declined to reinstate guidance pending the completion of their wind tower divestiture scheduled for Q3.

negative_highlights: Sequential revenue decline of $1.6M compared to Q1 ($5.1M vs $6.7M)
GAAP net loss widened sequentially from $12.1M in Q1 to $17.8M
Non-GAAP net loss increased due to lower revenue and a bad debt provision
positive_highlights: Gross margin expanded to 22.6% from Q1's 18.1%
Secured Sol-Ark certification reducing competition in U.S. residential market
Korea plant ramping NDAA-compliant cell production to one million units/year starting September
summary: Q2 FY2026 revenue was $5.1 million (down from Q1's $6.7M), with GAAP gross margin improving to 22.6% driven by ESS mix and pricing discipline. Management reaffirmed full-year 2026 guidance of $30-35 million despite the sequential decline, citing a backlog extending into 2028 for drone cells.

negative_highlights: NAV declined for the eighth consecutive quarter, primarily driven by unrealized losses on non-accrual investments
Watchlist increased modestly from 14% to 15% of the portfolio due to businesses indexed to deferrable consumer spending
Net investment income dropped $0.02 per share sequentially excluding one-time fee waiver impacts
positive_highlights: Completed three restructurings resulting in minimal net impact on NAV by offsetting realized losses against reversal of unrealized losses
Watchlist investments declined from 5.7% to 4.8% of debt investments at cost following restructuring and exits
summary: Net investment income declined to $0.36 per share from the prior quarter's adjusted $0.38 due to lower dividend and realization activity, while NAV fell to $17.82 driven by unrealized losses on non-accrual investments. Management raised concerns about eight consecutive quarters of NAV declines concentrated in a limited set of challenged credits but emphasized progress in rotating legacy assets from over 70 to 27 holdings. The company maintained liquidity with approximately $200 million available borrowing capacity and declared the third quarter dividend at $0.34 per share.

negative_highlights: Q2 cash operating costs came in modestly higher due to a planned shutdown reducing output by a few hundred tons (operating at ~93% capacity), energy cost pressures, and currency impacts.
Stage 2 scoping study timeline shifted from mid-year expectation to end of Q3 as management aligns with partner Ganfeng on immediate execution details.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA increased 4% sequentially to approximately $110 million driven by stronger realized prices averaging around $19,500 per ton.
Free cash flow from operations reached $141 million in Q2 while simultaneously reducing net debt at the JV level by $114 million to $142 million.
Operation averaged 93-95% of design capacity for FY26, demonstrating reliability and low-cost production below $6,000 per ton.
summary: Lithium Argentina reported Q2 FY2026 adjusted EBITDA of approximately $110 million (up 4% sequentially) and free cash flow from operations of $141 million driven by realized prices averaging around $19,500 per ton. The operation averaged 93-95% design capacity for the year with costs remaining under $6,000 per ton despite a planned shutdown impacting Q2 production volume. Management reaffirmed full-year guidance of 35,000-40,000 tons and highlighted significant balance sheet strength following debt reductions to $142 million at the JV level.

negative_highlights: Wholesale note-out in everyday running franchises tracked below ambitions in the Americas due to a highly promotional multi-brand marketplace.
Management explicitly chose not to build channel inventory or participate in promotions in key regions like the U.S. and Tmall, capping wholesale growth at 4.8% reported.
Inventory levels rose by CHF 149 million (31%) year-over-year due to volume-led sales and FX movements.
positive_highlights: DTC net sales surged 34.3% at constant currency, lifting the channel's contribution to total sales to a record 45.7%.
Gross margin expanded significantly to 65.4%, allowing the company to absorb external pressures and tariffs while maintaining premium pricing integrity.
Apparel growth accelerated dramatically with net sales up 56.2% at constant currency, establishing itself as a major diversification driver.
summary: On Holding reported Q2 FY26 net sales of CHF 850 million (up 13.5% on a reported basis), driven by strong DTC growth but moderated wholesale performance in the Americas due to deliberate watch-in restraint. Management maintained full-year guidance for adjusted EBITDA margin at 19.5%-20%, while raising gross margin expectations to 'at least' 65%. The company reiterated its commitment to premium positioning and disciplined execution, noting that lower Q3 growth is expected before a re-acceleration in H2.

negative_highlights: Chile business remains excluded from 2026 revenue forecasts due to a government funding gap.
Management noted that future profitability timelines cannot be accurately predicted as spending may accelerate to capture new opportunities.
Frenel and other federal/defense contracts are not included in current guidance despite active pursuit.
positive_highlights: Revenue doubled quarter-over-quarter driven by expanded sales into private security and state/local markets.
ATF determination confirmed BolaWrap is not a firearm or weapon, unlocking the $1.2M+ licensed private security officer market.
Gross margin improved to 75% from 48%, reflecting operational efficiency gains.
summary: Wrap Technologies reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $2.1 million, representing a 103% increase year-over-year and doubling compared to the prior quarter. Gross margin expanded significantly to approximately 75%, while net loss narrowed by 39% to $2.3 million due to non-recurring warrant liability losses in the prior period. Management maintained its full-year revenue growth guidance of approximately double, citing new market access from ATF declassification and federal funding returns.

negative_highlights: Reported GP&T expenses increased due to firm transportation costs from the Antero acquisition and higher overall volumes, though excluding these costs showed a decline.
Midstream system utilization remains at approximately 35%, with management noting third-party revenues will be small in the near term as they focus on internal development first.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDAX hit a company record high of $115 million with margins roughly double the Appalachian peer group average.
Oil production surged to approximately 12,400 bpd (up 102% YoY) and NGL realizations increased 70% YoY to $32.27/bbl.
Drilling efficiency improved with lateral feet drilled per day increasing by 15% compared to the 2025 average.
summary: Infinity Natural Resources reported Q2 FY26 net production of 348 Mcfe/d (up 75% YoY) and adjusted EBITDAX of $115M, a company record driven by strong oil growth (+102%) and NGL realizations up 70%. Management reaffirmed full-year 2026 guidance for net production between 345-375 Mcfe/d and development capex of $450-$500M. The quarter highlighted operational efficiency gains, including a step change in drilling speed (+15%) and completion cost reductions ($/ft), alongside the integration of Antero assets.

negative_highlights: Net revenue declined year-over-year to $19.7 million due to a combined decrease of over $6 million in sales from ASA and ASE.
Bookings decreased quarter-over-quarter to $21.8 million, reflecting lower demand for mature titles like ASE as consumer interest shifted toward ASA.
positive_highlights: Net loss improved substantially from $16.6 million last year to a current loss of $3 million due to the absence of an income tax provision and improvement in gross profit.
Gross profit increased despite lower revenue, aided by approximately $500,000 monthly savings on licensing fees which are being reinvested into future game development.
summary: Net revenue decreased to $19.7 million in Q2 FY26 from $22.2 million a year ago due to lower sales of ASA and ASE titles, while net loss improved significantly to $3 million primarily driven by the absence of an income tax provision recorded in the prior period. Management noted that major DLC launches scheduled for early July shifted revenue recognition into Q3 rather than Q2, resulting in fewer blockbuster releases during this quarter compared to historical norms.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to $626 million due to interest expense of $640 million and high CapEx.
Operating expenses increased significantly as the company scaled active power from backlog conversion.
positive_highlights: Record revenue of $2.6 billion driven by strong demand and capacity ramp, up 112% YoY.
Adjusted operating income grew to $128 million with sequential margin expansion despite significant CapEx scaling.
Raised full-year guidance on both revenue ($12.4B-$13.2B) and adjusted operating income ($960M-$1.15B).
summary: CoreWeave reported record Q2 FY26 revenue of $2.6 billion (up 112% YoY) and adjusted operating income of $128 million with expanding margins. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance to $12.4B-$13.2B in revenue and $960M-$1.15B in adjusted operating income, while also raising Q3 estimates for both metrics. The company added approximately 500 MW of active power (including a record 300 MW in June) to reach 1.85 GW by year-end.

negative_highlights: $337 million pre-tax charge recorded due to delays in two Construction Management projects, impacting cash flow and NSR.
Full-year free cash flow guidance lowered from $400 million to $300 million due to expected cash burn of ~$500 million through H1 FY2027.
Americas total NSR declined 29% primarily reflecting the Construction Management charge and slower ramp-up of new wins.
positive_highlights: Backlog increased 13% to an all-time high on record quarterly wins and a 1.6x book-to-burn across the business.
International NSR grew 4%, led by double-digit growth in Australia (backlog up >40%) and U.K., with margin expansion realized.
Americas design business returned to growth, increasing 5% adjusted for one less working day.
summary: AECOM reported Q3 FY2026 results impacted by a $337 million pre-tax charge related to delays in two Construction Management projects, causing NSR growth to fall below expectations despite strong wins and backlog increases. Adjusted EBITDA and EPS improved year-over-year excluding the charge but missed full guidance due to lower-than-expected revenue growth and cash burn from project completion costs. Full-year 2026 guidance was lowered for free cash flow (to $300 million) while maintaining adjusted earnings expectations, with a raised margin outlook driven by International segment performance.

negative_highlights: Company remains GAAP net loss of $11.5 million for the quarter (though improving YoY).
Management notes significant capacity constraints with a need to build ~20-30 more machines by end of 2027.
Livermore Production Campus is not expected to be fully operational until later in Q4 FY26.
positive_highlights: Revenue increased 52.3% year-over-year driven by RPS growth and higher average note prices.
Gross margin expanded significantly from -11.7% to 21.5%, reflecting improved utilization and cost reallocation.
Backlog grew substantially to $31 million, up from $16 million in the prior year quarter.
summary: Velo3D reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $20.7 million (up 52% YoY) and gross margin expansion to 21.5%. The company raised its full-year 2026 revenue guidance from a range of $60M-$70M to $65M-$75M, citing strong demand in aerospace, defense, and energy sectors.

negative_highlights: Net loss of $102 million with negative EPS of -$0.10 due to significant non-recurring charges.
U.S. beef industry faces tight supplies and historically high costs, though margins are stabilizing.
positive_highlights: Net sales reached an all-time record of $24 billion for the quarter.
Free cash flow improved significantly year-over-year, turning positive at $130 million driven by working capital and higher receivables discounts.
U.S. beef EBITDA margin improved sequentially from Q1 to -1.3% despite a challenging cattle cycle.
summary: JBS reported record net sales of $24 billion in Q2 FY2026 with Adjusted EBITDA reaching $1.3-1.4 billion depending on accounting standards (5.3% GAAP margin). While the company delivered a solid quarter and raised its full-year cash flow guidance to $5.1 billion, profitability was significantly impacted by non-recurring items including bond tender costs ($172M) and antitrust settlements ($133M), resulting in a net loss of $102 million. Management highlighted strong demand resilience but noted challenging U.S. beef margins due to high cattle costs and warned that the second half leverage will likely finish slightly above their 2x-3x target.

negative_highlights: Total investment income decreased from $66.2 million in Q1 to $62.3 million in Q2 due to lower interest on one JV and new non-accruals
Non-accrual investments increased quarter-over-quarter, rising from 0.6% at fair value in Q1 to 2.2% in Q2
Realized losses of $14.6 million ($0.22 per share) were driven by a restructured investment and an exit
positive_highlights: Credit quality across the portfolio remained healthy overall despite a modest decline in NAV
Median net leverage across borrowers was stable at 4.7x and interest coverage remained healthy at 2.1x
New deal activity picked up meaningfully following a slower start to the quarter
summary: BCSF reported Q2 FY2026 net investment income of $0.44 per share and EPS of $0.22, resulting in a NAV decline to $16.65 due to realized losses driven by an exit and restructuring activity. Management maintained the base dividend at $0.42 but declined to provide specific forward guidance on payout levels or ROE targets, citing variables like interest rates and debt maturities as factors for future reevaluation. While credit fundamentals remained healthy with median leverage of 4.7x, non-accruals increased slightly quarter-over-quarter.

negative_highlights: Operating and maintenance costs were $118 million higher year-over-year due to commissioning work at Plaquemines and more owned ships in operation.
Management maintained a broader-than-usual guidance range for the remainder of 2026 citing outsized LNG price volatility related to Middle East events.
positive_highlights: Record consolidated adjusted EBITDA of $2.5 billion driven by volume growth (466 TBtu) and higher net sales prices.
Contracted position increased markedly to over 91% of the portfolio from 84% previously reported in Q1.
Completed significant planned maintenance, including hot gas path inspections at Calcasieu Pass, without production downtime.
summary: Venture Global reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $4.6 billion (up 48% YoY) and consolidated adjusted EBITDA of $2.5 billion (a record high). Management raised full-year 2026 EBITDA guidance to a range of $8.7-$9.1 billion from the prior $8.2-$8.5 billion, citing strong execution and production at Calcasieu Pass despite summer seasonality. The company also increased its quarterly dividend by 122% to $0.04 per share.

negative_highlights: Consolidated EBITDA growth (17%) trailed revenue growth (25%) due to one-time incremental costs of operating as a public company.
Q2 same-store sales grew only 4.2% YoY, significantly lower than the prior year's 10.9%, creating a tough comparison for Q3 and H2.
Transactions declined by 2% in the quarter due to loyalty platform transition effects.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 25% YoY to $63 million, driven by store-level profit expansion of 28% and margin improvement to 30.2%.
Management raised full-year new store guidance from 36 to at least 38 units as development outpaces projections.
Same-store transactions turned positive in July (+1.7%) following the structural changes associated with the loyalty platform launch.
summary: Black Rock Coffee Bar reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $63 million (up 25% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA growth of 17%, though consolidated earnings were impacted by incremental public company costs. Management raised full-year new store guidance to at least 38 units from 36, citing strong momentum in the California market and a robust pipeline for 2027. The quarter featured same-store sales growth of 4.2% despite lapping a high prior year period.

negative_highlights: $5 million of high-voltage system deliveries originally anticipated for FY2026 were deferred into Q1 FY2027 due to supply chain constraints.
Operating profit decreased by roughly 58% year-over-year from $1.9 million to $0.8 million, driven by increased SG&A and stock-based compensation.
Quarterly revenue missed internal targets as implementation delays in material handling projects impacted order timing.
positive_highlights: Gross margins hit a record 34.9%, up 410 bps year-over-year, driven by product mix and supplier pricing power.
Adjusted EBITDA margin reached approximately 20% for the first time in company history with positive cash flow of $8.6 million.
summary: Q3 FY2026 revenue was $17.7 million versus $17.1 million in the prior year, while gross margins expanded to a record 34.9% and adjusted EBITDA reached approximately 20%. Management attributes the lower-than-expected quarterly sales primarily to timing shifts of high-voltage deliveries into FY2027 due to supply chain constraints rather than lost business or demand deterioration.

positive_highlights: Enrollment in OVATION 3 exceeds internal assumptions at 0.5 patients per site per month compared to the planned 0.3.
summary: Imunon reported Q2 FY2026 results with R&D expenses of $1.5 million and G&A expenses down approximately 20% to $1.3 million due to cost containment initiatives. The company highlighted strong enrollment momentum in the pivotal OVATION 3 study, currently enrolling at 0.5 patients per site per month versus a plan assumption of 0.3, exceeding industry benchmarks for ovarian cancer trials. Management confirmed no guidance updates were provided but expressed high confidence that execution remains on track with their target timeline.

negative_highlights: Q2 results impacted by approximately $30/barrel discount composed of sulfur, demurrage, and transportation costs.
Platform Hondo restoration required about 50% more work than originally anticipated due to the platform being in bad need of structural repair.
Production constrained by pump capacity at Heritage and lack of gas lift compressors running on Harmony/Heritage.
positive_highlights: Completed refinancing of $675 million Senior Secured Term Loan B and issued $345 million convertible notes to retire the restrictive ExxonMobil seller note, lowering weighted average cost of debt.
Production ramped significantly with exit rate oil sales reaching 40,000 bpd in Q2 FY2026.
Implemented commodity hedging program starting July 2026 providing floor protection at $65/bbl for a significant portion of production.
summary: Sable Offshore Corp reported Q2 FY2026 results where production ramped to 40,000 bpd but faced significant marketing constraints and a $30/bbl discount due to sulfur content and demurrage charges. Management completed the refinancing of the senior secured term note in July 2026 to retire seller financing, providing more flexibility despite not raising guidance for the back half of the year which includes elevated deducts. The company expects production constraints to alleviate by Q4 2026 with Platform Hondo coming online and a full 3P reserve report expected in Q1 2027.

positive_highlights: FY2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance raised to approximately $15 million from approximately $14 million
Cash rose $17.5 million to $55.6 million since fiscal year end; net debt cut $17.6 million to $29.8 million
Completed $10 million share repurchase program (245,399 shares) while still building cash; approximately 98% of farmable acreage leased
summary: Alico reported Q3 FY2026 total revenue of $9.0 million, up 7.7% YoY, with net income of $2.1 million ($0.29/diluted share) versus a $18.3 million loss ($2.39) a year ago, aided by completed accelerated depreciation and higher lease income. Adjusted EBITDA was $4.6 million versus $19.3 million prior year, though management attributed the decline to lower crop insurance proceeds and a smaller asset-sale gain rather than operations. FY2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance was raised to approximately $15 million from approximately $14 million, with year-end cash of approximately $48 million and net debt of approximately $37 million. The company ended the quarter with $55.6 million cash, $29.8 million net debt (down $17.6 million from fiscal year end), completed $10 million of buybacks, and struck a 3,280-acre agricultural lease with a $29.5 million purchase option.

negative_highlights: Oil and gas revenue declined 8.2% YoY ($8.5M) primarily due to customer program exits in 2025 and deferred maintenance activity amid elevated commodity prices.
Management anticipates oil & gas will remain flat-to-down through H2, contributing headwinds despite growth elsewhere.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 4.2% YoY driven by strategic end markets which were up 28% in aggregate, specifically Aerospace & Defense (+13.2%) and Infrastructure (+76.5%).
Record Q2 adjusted EBITDA of $25.8 million achieved with a gross margin expansion of 10 basis points.
Free cash flow improved significantly by $23.9 million quarter-over-quarter due to working capital dynamics.
summary: Mistras Group reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $193 million (up 4.2% YoY) and record adjusted EBITDA of $25.8 million ($25.8m vs prior year). Gross margin expanded by 10 basis points to a non-GAAP level implied around 73-74%, while operating income surged 53.6%. Management raised full-year guidance ranges for revenue (up to $740-$755M) and adjusted EBITDA (up to $92-$95M), citing strength in aerospace/defense and infrastructure offsetting a flat-to-down outlook for oil & gas.

negative_highlights: Adjusted segment EBITDA margin in production solutions decreased by 229 basis points quarter-over-quarter due to revenue mix shifts and higher operating expenses.
Natural Gas Systems segment saw both revenue and Adjusted Segment EBITDA decline sequentially, primarily driven by lower vapor recovery system sales offsetting rental growth.
Management lowered Q3 guidance range to $92 million-$98 million citing continued cost pressures from lube oil prices tied to high crack spreads and elevated O&M expenses.
positive_highlights: Revenue increased 13% sequentially driven by growth in production solutions, specifically downhole components including the recently acquired Valiant business.
Adjusted EBITDA grew 10% quarter-over-quarter to approximately $94 million while maintaining top-quartile margins of roughly 40% despite cost headwinds.
Free cash flow generation remained strong at approximately $50 million, supporting a conservative balance sheet with leverage reduced below one times.
summary: Flowco reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $236 million (up 13% sequentially) and Adjusted EBITDA of approximately $94 million ($93.9m GAAP), maintaining roughly 40% margins despite a 229 bps margin contraction in production solutions due to Valiant integration costs and higher O&M expenses including lube oil and fuel. Management stated results were within original guidance but explicitly noted that cost pressures will continue into Q3, leading them to reflect these headwinds by lowering their third-quarter Adjusted EBITDA guidance range from the prior $92m-$105m (implied) down to a new range of $92 million-$98 million. The company generated $50 million in free cash flow and declared a one-time special dividend alongside its regular quarterly payout.

negative_highlights: NeuroStar total revenue declined slightly by 2.7% due to double-digit drop in treatment session revenue
Full-year guidance narrowed from a range of $160M-$166M down to $160M-$164M
positive_highlights: Greenbrook revenue grew 17% YoY to $26.9M driven by provider growth and pricing improvements
Gross margin expanded significantly from 46.6% in the prior year to 61.1%
Cash burn reduced substantially with cash used for operations/investing falling to $1.4 million
summary: Total revenue was $41.6 million, up 9% year-over-year driven by a 17% increase in Greenbrook to $26.9 million and double-digit growth in NeuroStar capital sales offsetting session declines. Gross margin expanded significantly to 61.1%, while the company reduced its cash burn from operations and investing to just $1.4 million compared to $3.8 million last year. Management narrowed full-year revenue guidance slightly but raised gross margin expectations, reflecting improved operational discipline.

negative_highlights: Same-store NOI on legacy Holiday properties declined 6.3% year-over-year due to move-outs and unit offline pressures.
General and administrative expenses increased significantly by 44% YoY driven by CFO transition costs and ramping SHOP personnel.
Full-year same-store guidance remains at the lower end of expectations (1%-3%) with H2 growth expected only after addressing occupancy pressure from a specific building.
positive_highlights: Completed sale of NHC portfolio for $560 million cash, reducing leverage and providing significant liquidity to pursue future investments.
Same-store SHOP NOI increased sequentially by 18.9% from Q2 FY2025 to Q2 FY2026 as the company ramps its private pay senior housing platform.
Board declared a quarterly dividend increase of $0.02 per share, raising it to $0.94.
summary: NHI reported Q2 FY2026 results in line with expectations following the sale of its NHC portfolio for $560 million and a gain on property dispositions totaling approximately $137 million ($98.5M proceeds + $22M gain). While net income per share beat due to these one-time gains, core FFO metrics were flat or slightly down compared to the prior year period. Management maintained full-year guidance unchanged despite same-store SHOP NOI growth being below the midpoint of their 1%-3% range in H1.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to $2.1 million from $1.7 million YoY, with Q2 operating expenses up 53% to $3.8 million
Management said it is 'not happy' with these numbers and is 'basically treating no one' due to lack of insurance policy coverage
Outstanding going concern remains until cash flow breakeven, and cash burn is expected to tick up in H2 2026 from the $1.1 million average YTD
positive_highlights: Revenue rose 116% YoY to a record $1.928 million, the eighth straight quarter of double-digit YoY growth
Gross margin expanded 230 bps to 85.9% and ASP rose 28% to $992 on mix shift from discounted financial assistance to full-reimbursement payers
Year-to-date prior authorization approval rate rose to 31% from 12%, and revenue per ordering account rose 68% to $40,000
summary: Q2 FY2026 revenue was $1.928 million, up 116% YoY and a record quarterly high, with gross margin expanding 230 bps to 85.9% and ASP rising 28% to $992 as mix shifted toward reimbursed procedures. Net loss widened to $2.1 million ($0.19 per share) from $1.7 million ($0.22) due to 53% higher operating expenses, and the company reported no explicit revenue or EPS guidance. Management stated it is 'not happy' with current treated-patient volumes, citing lack of insurance policy coverage, and said monthly revenue may fluctuate with payer timing expected in H2 2026 or early 2027, while expanding VA efforts with 10 new 1099 reps.

negative_highlights: Absorbed approximately $55 million of net cash hedge losses during the quarter, though management views this as a prudent risk management step.
Oil cut dropped to 64% from guided 67-68% due to accelerated completions stimulating high-oil wells and workovers on older gas-heavy assets.
positive_highlights: Production averaged 45,500 BOE/d during H1 FY26, exceeding the high end of guidance range.
Unit LOE came in approximately 13% below full-year guided levels at $7.56/BOE due to operational improvements and electrification.
Accelerated completion schedule allowed capital deployment against productive work while capturing favorable service costs.
summary: HighPeak Energy reported Q2 FY26 production of approximately 45,500 BOE/d, exceeding the high end of guidance despite accelerating completions which caused some frac-impacted volumes. The company generated $281 million in EBITDAX for H1 and absorbed roughly $55 million in net cash hedge losses while maintaining disciplined capital execution with first-half spending at 60%+ of budget. Management expects meaningful declines in second-half capital spend, positioning the business to generate stronger free cash flow as production remains supported by strong well performance.

negative_highlights: Full-year EBITDA guidance explicitly excludes incremental revenue from the Intrepid Ranch acquisition announced post-quarter end.
General and administrative expenses were noted as 'a little bit light' in H1 relative to normalized public company costs, suggesting potential for higher spend later.
positive_highlights: Normalized revenue grew ~32% quarter-over-quarter to $46.8M, exceeding internal forecasts across all metrics.
Adjusted EBITDA margins expanded to 77.5%, demonstrating the benefit of high-margin surface use royalties and low operating costs.
Free cash flow conversion improved to approximately 96% after adjusting for interest expense on the predecessor credit facility.
summary: EagleRock reported Q2 FY2026 normalized revenue of $46.8 million (up ~32% vs Q1) and adjusted EBITDA of $36.2 million (up ~32%), driven by strong brackish water sales, surface use royalties, and resource sales. The company initiated full-year 2026 guidance for normalized adjusted EBITDA between $129M-$133M, which is above original expectations but explicitly excludes the recently announced Intrepid Ranch acquisition. Management highlighted a robust balance sheet with $261.8 million in available liquidity and high free cash flow conversion of approximately 96% after adjusting for interest expense.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to $53 million due to non-cash revaluation impacts on financial instruments, financing costs from the recapitalization, and increased pre-development expenses.

Cash used in operating activities surged to $50 million for the quarter compared to $11 million last year, driven by inventory buildup at third-party processing facilities and higher exploration outflows.
Drilling progress was slower than planned at Archimedes and Mineral Point due to drill rig availability issues and contractor staffing constraints.
positive_highlights: Gold production increased to approximately 8,600 ounces in Q2 compared to the prior year period as Granite Creek ramps up.
Gross profit expanded significantly due to a realized gold price of nearly $4,800/oz and higher sales volume from ramp-up activities.
Balance sheet strengthened with cash ending at approximately $465 million following recapitalization proceeds and restricted cash release.
summary: i-80 Gold reported Q2 FY26 revenue of approximately $24 million and a net loss of $53 million ($0.06/share), driven by higher non-cash accounting impacts from financial instrument revaluations, financing costs, and increased pre-development expenses despite gross profit rising to $9 million due to gold price increases and production ramp-up at Granite Creek (8,600 ounces). Management reiterated 2026 guidance for annual output of 30,000-40,000 ounces but noted that growth capital expenditures will be below the prior range due to timing on Lone Tree refurbishment accruals and lower exploration spend. The company remains focused on executing its development plan with a strong balance sheet ($465M cash) while acknowledging moderate delays in drilling campaigns at Archimedes and Mineral Point.

negative_highlights: GAAP gross margin contracted by 130 basis points to 20.3% due to specific FORGE hardware purchases for a government program.
Free cash flow outflow widened from $78.9 million in Q1 to $106.3 million in Q2, primarily driven by the final SciTec acquisition payment of approximately $24 million.
positive_highlights: Record quarterly revenue crossing the $100 million threshold for the first time in company history.
Backlog grew sequentially by approximately $200 million to a record high of $1.5 billion, indicating strong order conversion.
Non-GAAP net loss per share improved from $0.46 to $0.42 as revenue scale increased.
summary: Firefly reported record Q2 FY26 revenue of $117.7 million (up 46% sequentially and 659% YoY) driven by five parallel lunar missions and strong spacecraft demand. The company closed the quarter with a historic backlog of $1.5 billion, up from $1.3 billion previously. GAAP gross margin declined slightly to 20.3% due to specific government program hardware purchases, while non-GAAP operating loss narrowed significantly as revenue scaled.

negative_highlights: GAAP net income was impacted by significant unrealized losses on bunker fuel hedges in Q2
Total G&A expenses increased 25% YoY due to incentive compensation and added headcount
Charter-in costs rose 24% YoY as market rates for chartered vessels increased
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA grew nearly $20M YoY to $35M driven by robust market rates
TCE rates averaged a premium of 10% over the prevailing Panamax, Supramax, and Handysize indices
Unrestricted cash balance reached $105 million following vessel sales
summary: Pangaea Logistics Solutions reported strong Q2 FY2026 results with adjusted EBITDA of $35 million (up nearly $20M YoY) driven by a 50% increase in TCE rates to an average of $18,153/day. The company raised its quarterly dividend to $0.10 per share and ended the quarter with unrestricted cash of $105 million following asset sales. Management maintains a positive outlook for H2 2026 citing seasonal tailwinds from Arctic trades and continued demand momentum.

negative_highlights: Net loss from continuing operations was $11.9M, though improved from prior year.
Adjusted EBITDA remains negative at -$1.9M despite a significant improvement.
The AVCAD program revenue has been excluded from core full-year guidance pending government next steps.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 23% YoY to $16.1M driven by handheld product revenue up 24%.
Adjusted gross margin expanded approximately 85 basis points to 57% due to volume and channel mix improvements.
Secured a specific $6 million ProtectIR order for corrections agencies in the Asia-Pacific region.
summary: 908 Devices reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $16.1 million (up 23% YoY) and adjusted gross margin expansion to 57%. The company raised its full-year 2026 guidance range to $68-$70 million, citing strong execution on FTIR modernization, the new NIRLab acquisition integration, and a specific $6 million ProtectIR order. Adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed by over half year-over-year.

negative_highlights: Net loss increased significantly due to $200 million upfront royalty payment to Tanabe Pharma Corporation
R&D expenses rose from $38.3M in Q2 FY25 to $221.4M in Q2 FY26 primarily due to the one-time payment and headcount growth
positive_highlights: $500 million committed senior secured term loan facility entered into in June 2026
$150 million equity offering completed to expand capital access
Post hoc analysis of Launch-HTN trial showed statistically and clinically meaningful blood pressure reductions comparable to broader population despite severe hypertension
summary: Mineralys Therapeutics reported a net loss of $241.1 million for Q2 FY2026 compared to $43.3 million in the prior year quarter, driven by a one-time $200 million upfront payment to Tanabe Pharma Corporation and increased R&D expenses totaling $221.4 million. The company ended the period with cash equivalents and investments of $661.4 million, sufficient to fund operations through 2028 while awaiting FDA approval for lorundrostat expected by December PDUFA date.

negative_highlights: Third-quarter adjusted EBITDA margin guidance was lowered by 30 bps to reflect tougher comparisons and timing of end-market recoveries in the back half.
Recreational marine market remains soft with interest rates suppressing growth for financed products.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EPS beat high-end of outlook by $0.05 per share driven by strong volume growth and operational leverage.
Gross margins expanded 280 bps to 34.6%, marking the fourth consecutive quarter of expansion.
Order intake grew double-digits for a fourth straight quarter, signaling robust demand visibility.
summary: Helios Technologies reported Q2 FY26 sales of $232 million (up 9% YoY) and adjusted EPS of $0.88, which exceeded the high-end of its prior guidance by $0.05 per share. Gross margin expanded 280 bps to 34.6%, driven by volume growth, mix shifts, operational initiatives, and a one-time IEEPA tariff refund benefit. Management raised full-year sales guidance to an implied range of $880-$900 million (up from the prior midpoint) and increased adjusted EBITDA margin expectations for the year.

negative_highlights: Industry growth is expected to moderate relative to historical norms as job growth slows despite stable unemployment rates.
Canadian tax season performance was not great due to regulatory changes with the CRA, though Australia performed well.
$8.3 million severance charge in Q1 fiscal 2027 related to transitioning from a seasonal office leadership model to a year-round structure.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 4.9% with a healthy balance of volume, price (up ~3%), and mix (up 1%) in the assisted category.
Conversion improved 200 basis points, marking the largest single-year improvement in recorded history due to customer journey refinements.
Wave small business services delivered its second consecutive year of double-digit revenue growth driven by paid pro tier subscriptions.
summary: H&R Block reported fiscal year 2026 revenue of $3.95 billion (up 4.9%) and adjusted EPS of $5.31 (up 13.9%), driven by higher net average charge, volume growth in assisted tax preparation, and momentum from Wave small business services. Management raised the full-year fiscal 2027 revenue guidance to a range of $4.11 billion-$4.16 billion while maintaining adjusted EBITDA between $1.11 billion-$1.14 billion and raising the quarterly dividend by 10% to $0.46 per share.

negative_highlights: Gross margin faces near-term pressure from a higher mix of purchase subscriptions (60% vs prior guidance) and costs associated with redeploying Gen1 units.
Component and supply chain costs are running modestly higher than anticipated, creating approximately half a point of gross margin headwind.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 34% year-over-year driven by new customer wins (70 added) and expansion within existing customers.
Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to 10.1%, up from 6.5% in the prior year quarter, demonstrating operating leverage despite investments.
Net revenue retention remained above 100% with ARR growing 20% YoY to $132.7 million.
summary: Evolv Technology reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $43.8 million (up 34% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA margins expanding to 10.1%. Management raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to a range of $180-$185 million from the prior forecast of $175-$180 million, citing strong demand for Gen2 upgrades and multi-product adoption.

negative_highlights: Total revenue declined to $296.8 million from $299.9 million, with pre-owned retail units down 6.8% to 4,924
Early Q3 same-store sales are down low single digits year-over-year per management
Cash used in operating activities was $28.2 million for the first half, and non-vehicle net debt stood at $174.4 million pending refinancing
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA rose 19.2% to $20.5 million from $17.2 million a year ago
Same-store revenue grew 3% to $291.5 million, the fourth consecutive quarter of same-store revenue and unit growth
Adjusted SG&A fell to 74.1% of gross profit from 77.4%, and first-half adjusted free cash flow improved to $20.8 million from $2.9 million
summary: RideNow reported Q2 FY2026 total revenue of $296.8 million versus $299.9 million a year ago, a decline attributed to operating five fewer stores, while adjusted EBITDA rose 19.2% to $20.5 million on adjusted SG&A falling to 74.1% of gross profit from 77.4%. Same-store revenue grew 3% to $291.5 million on 16,626 total units, down 2.9% (pre-owned units off 6.8%), with new unit gross margin up to 14.8% from 13.2% and pre-owned margin down to 18.0% from 18.8%. Management noted July-to-date same-store sales down low single digits and said the refinancing is progressing with details expected in coming weeks; no formal full-year guidance figures were provided, though continued adjusted EBITDA and free cash flow growth is expected. First-half adjusted free cash flow was $20.8 million versus $2.9 million a year ago, helped by floor plan draws, and liquidity totaled $158.2 million.

negative_highlights: FDA communication regarding IGE PMA supplement was not approvable in its current form, requiring additional clinical evidence and an amendment process via the SIR.
Service revenue declined significantly to $0.3 million from $0.9 million a year ago due to discontinued operations with DIXI Medical.
positive_highlights: Total revenue grew 17% year-over-year driven by a 21.3% increase in RNS System revenue ($22.5M).
Full-year total revenue guidance was raised to $99.5 million-$101.5 million, up from the previous range of $99 million-$101 million.
Adjusted gross margin remained strong at 83.4% despite a slight year-over-year decline.
summary: NeuroPace reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $22.8 million (up 17% YoY) and adjusted gross margin of 83.4%, slightly down from the prior year due to material costs but supported by favorable pricing. Management raised full-year total revenue guidance to $99.5M-$101.5M, reflecting improved visibility into service revenue which is now expected at approximately $1 million for the full year versus a previous expectation of $500k.
