Raised full-year guidance to ~$43M citing improved visibility into H2 demand
Secured major government validation including a Commerce LOI for up to $100 million and three DOE Genesis Mission projects
summary: Infleqtion reported record Q2 FY26 revenue of $12.6 million, representing an 116% year-over-year increase driven by organic growth in quantum computing and sensing. The company raised its full-year 2026 revenue guidance to approximately $43 million from prior expectations. Management highlighted significant government validation including a Department of Commerce letter of intent for up to $100 million, three Genesis Mission projects with the DOE, and delivery of the UK's first operational neutral atom quantum computer.

negative_highlights: R&D and SG&A expenses increased to support the expanded sales team, patient support services, and upcoming clinical trials like RESPIRE.
Management noted that R&D expense is expected to double in H2 FY2026 compared to H1 due to ramping enrollment.
positive_highlights: Net product sales reached $170.4 million, up 31% QoQ and more than tripling since launch began last June.
YUTREPIA has started over 5,000 patients with approximately 5,900 unique prescriptions received as of July 31.
The company achieved four consecutive quarters of increasing profitability after reporting a net loss in Q2 FY2025.
summary: Liquidia reported Q2 FY2026 net product sales of $170.4 million for YUTREPIA, representing a 31% quarter-over-quarter increase and over-tripling growth since launch initiation in June 2025. The company moved from a net loss to profitability with approximately $74.7 million in net income and $96.3 million in non-GAAP Adjusted EBITDA for the quarter, driven by strong patient starts exceeding 5,000 as of July 31. Management expressed confidence that YUTREPIA is capturing a growing share of the expanding inhaled prostacyclin market while maintaining its trajectory toward over $1 billion in net revenue for 2027.

negative_highlights: Consolidated revenue declined 9.6% year-over-year on a same-station basis
National agency revenue fell approximately 21%, and local agency revenue dropped 12%
Digital profitability was below expectations despite audience growth
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA turned profitable at $5.3M compared to Q1 loss of negative $0.4M
Local direct revenue increased 9% year-over-year, reflecting improved client retention
summary: Consolidated revenue declined approximately 9.6% year-over-year to $44.1 million due to significant pressure in national and local agency channels (down ~21% and ~12%, respectively), though local direct revenue grew by 9%. Adjusted EBITDA improved sequentially from a Q1 loss of negative $0.4 million to positive $5.3 million, driven largely by the completion of a debt restructuring that generated a gain on debt of approximately $91.8 million and reduced interest expense.

negative_highlights: Inorganic revenue contribution is likely to be lower than the original $55M plan due to slower deal closing timelines in regulatory-heavy markets like Canada.
GAAP net loss widened slightly compared to Q2 FY25, though this was expected and driven by non-cash equity-based compensation of ~$48.2M.
Attrition rates increased modestly, with 70% occurring at lower performance ratings (1-3), which management views as a positive filter but indicates ongoing headcount challenges.
positive_highlights: Revenue beat guidance by approximately $12M-$17M with a total increase of 23.7% versus the prior period.
Organic revenue growth accelerated to 20.5%, significantly outpacing initial expectations and demonstrating strong underlying demand.
Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded materially, reflecting favorable operating leverage and reduced cost of services.
summary: The company reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $217.7 million, beating the prior guidance range of $190M-$205M by approximately 10% and exceeding expectations with a 23.7% year-over-year increase driven primarily by organic growth of 20.5%. Adjusted EBITDA came in at roughly $46 million (up ~55%), while management reaffirmed full-year FY26 revenue guidance of $980M-$1B despite acknowledging that the pace of M&A deal closures is slower than anticipated, resulting in lower-than-planned inorganic contribution. Management expressed strong confidence in organic momentum and pricing power but noted ongoing investments in Global Mobility and consulting which currently suppress margins.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to $8.5 million due to a down pistachio crop (yields affected by heat/pollination issues) and higher property operating expenses.
Demand for fresh produce decreased following the Cyclospora outbreak, causing markets to soften across berries and leafy greens.
positive_highlights: Adjusted FFO improved to -$1.6 million from -$3.5 million year-over-year driven by higher cash rents and lower interest costs.
Almond prices reached $2.70/lb for the split in shell, significantly above projections, with initial 2026 pricing at $2.50/lb (two-thirds higher than last year).
Water allocation increased by 3% recently, which is expected to lower water deal pricing and reduce operating expenses heading into winter.
summary: The company reported a net loss of $8.5 million and an adjusted FFO loss of $1.6 million for the second quarter, representing significant improvement over last year's losses but still missing expectations for profitability. Management highlighted strong almond prices ($2.70/lb final pricing expected) which will drive revenue recognition in Q4 2026 following a down pistachio crop and disappointing water allocations that increased operating expenses.

negative_highlights: Free cash flow turned negative at -$7 million due to increased memory inventory buildup.
Days Inventory on Hand rose significantly from 80 days in Q1 to 95 days as the company front-runs supply for growth.
Gross margin guidance was lowered slightly (implied) or held steady at 51%-52% to account for elevated memory costs not expected to be passed through.
positive_highlights: Broadband revenue grew 54% year-over-year to $133.5 million, exceeding guidance by approximately $20M-$18.5M.
Rest-of-market bookings represented ~60% of total bookings in the quarter with a book-to-bill well over 1.5.
Full-year revenue guidance was raised from a midpoint of roughly $485 million to a new range of $505 million-$525 million.
summary: Harmonic reported Q2 FY26 broadband revenue of $133.5 million (up 54% YoY), significantly beating the high end of guidance ($115M-$125M) and EPS of $0.21, which beat the range of $0.15-$0.19. Management raised full-year revenue guidance to a new range of $505 million to $525 million (up from prior $475M-$495M), citing record backlog and strong rest-of-market growth. The company completed its transformation into a pure-play broadband entity following the sale of its video business.

negative_highlights: Contribution ex-TAC declined in desktop (-13%) and non-programmatic business lines.
Softness observed within the travel vertical during Q2.
positive_highlights: Programmatic revenue hit a Q2 record at $95.2M, representing an 11-12% year-over-year increase driven by CTV ($37.8M) and mobile in-app (up 23%).
Full-year guidance was raised for the third time this year on contribution ex-TAC and programmatic revenue.
Enterprise spend increased over 25% YoY, with the number of advertisers activated growing from under 400 to over 750.
summary: Nexxen reported record Q2 results with programmatic revenue of $95.2 million (up 12% YoY) and contribution ex-TAC of $97.8 million (up 11% YoY). The company raised its full-year guidance for both contribution ex-TAC ($388M-$402M, up from prior midpoint) and programmatic revenue ($380M-$393M, up from prior midpoint), marking the first top-line guide raise of the year. Management highlighted record CTV revenue growth of 33% YoY to $37.8 million and strong enterprise spend increases.

negative_highlights: CEO explicitly stated they are not adjusting expectations for data availability, maintaining guidance despite accelerated site activation
Solid tumor program ALLO-316 faced real safety challenges and the team had to develop a management algorithm after toxicity emerged
ALPHA3 primary analysis requires overwhelming efficacy to achieve statistical significance at the interim EFS point
positive_highlights: FDA granted RMAT and Fast Track designations for cema-cel in first-line consolidation based on interim MRD clearance data
Enrollment accelerated to meet the goal of activating over 80 sites by year-end, now expecting approximately 100 active sites with a majority in the U.S.
ALPHA3 trial achieved rapid MRD clearance in a majority of patients with no treatment-related hospitalizations
summary: Allogene provided a business update for Q2 FY2026 focusing on clinical progress rather than financial results, highlighting the receipt of RMAT and Fast Track designations for cema-cel in first-line consolidation based on interim MRD data. The company reported accelerating enrollment to reach its goal of 100 active sites by year-end but maintained guidance that the primary EFS analysis will occur mid-2027 without raising expectations despite faster site activation.

negative_highlights: SG&A expenses were $10.9 million with no specific guidance raised despite strong top-line growth.
Qbrexza revenue was down slightly due to patient mix and payer deductible resets.
Eurax Cream is a new niche product launched late in the quarter with no established sales trajectory yet.
positive_highlights: Emrosi net product revenues reached $8.1 million in Q2, up significantly year-over-year.
Total prescriptions for Emrosi grew by approximately 20% sequentially to ~36,000 units.
The unique prescriber base expanded from 3,700 at end of Q1 to over 4,500 in Q2.
summary: Journey Medical reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $18.5 million, a 23% year-over-year increase driven by Emrosi net product revenues of $8.1 million and improved ASPs. The company achieved positive GAAP EBITDA ($1.4M) and adjusted EBITDA ($2.9M), narrowing its loss to $0.01 per share compared to a prior period loss of $3.8M. Management highlighted accelerating prescription growth for Emrosi (up 20% sequentially) but noted that SG&A expenses remained elevated due to launch-related spending and upcoming marketing programs, with no specific guidance raised.

negative_highlights: Q2 GAAP gross margin declined to 14.4% due to product mix shifts in South Korea operations rather than execution issues.
Smart eyewear revenue remains nominal with Q3 expected to be negative on margins as overheads are absorbed before scale is reached.
Revenue of $9 million was at the high end of guidance but did not explicitly beat consensus estimates mentioned by management.
positive_highlights: Smart eyewear entered commercial production with first product revenue and delivery orders for ~19,000 packs in Q3 (nine-fold increase from Q2).
Defense drone pipeline grew by 41% to $183 million, exceeding $100 million specifically on drones.
Smartphone qualification passed critical milestone with lead customer confirming >1,000 cycles under the new hybrid protocol.
summary: Enovix reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $9 million (up 21% YoY), which landed at the high end of guidance but missed analyst consensus expectations due to a lack of specific beat confirmation in the text. The company recorded its first smart eyewear product revenue and advanced smartphone qualification milestones, though gross margins were pressured by South Korea mix shifts resulting in GAAP margins of 14.4%. Management maintained Q3 revenue guidance between $9-10 million but did not raise it despite strong pipeline growth.

negative_highlights: Customer traffic declined 4.9% due to deferrals among value-seeking consumers following an e-commerce re-platform that impacted sales by approximately 150 basis points.
Full-year comparable store sales guidance was narrowed at the top end (by about 1%) reflecting a more measured view on when lower-value customers will return.
Inventory increased approximately 37% year-over-date to support segmentation strategy, creating potential working capital pressure if note-through slows.
positive_highlights: Adjusted operating margin expanded 140 basis points to 6.3% driven by higher value customer mix and product attachment.
Average ticket increased 7.1%, offsetting a 4.9% decline in traffic, with strong performance from premium lenses like Nikon Eyes.
Management raised the full-year adjusted operating income outlook despite narrowing top-line revenue expectations.
summary: Net revenue grew 2.5% to $499 million while adjusted comparable store sales increased 2.2%, driven by a 7.1% average ticket expansion that offset a 4.9% decline in traffic. Adjusted operating margin expanded 140 basis points to 6.3% and adjusted EPS rose to $0.25 per share, though management narrowed the full-year top-line guidance range due to persistent deferrals from lower-value transactions following an e-commerce re-platform.

negative_highlights: Net sales declined 4% YoY, including approximately 220 bps of impact from the store closure program.
EMEA region faced headwinds due to geopolitical climate in the Middle East impacting travel retail.
Full-year guidance still anticipates a top-line decline rather than growth.
positive_highlights: Adjusted operating income doubled year-over-year, reaching $9 million ($8.6m constant currency).
Traditional watch business delivered impressive global wholesale growth of 12%.
Americas region stabilized with mid-single digit U.S. growth and Asia grew 4% led by double-digit India performance.
summary: Fossil Group reported Q2 FY26 net sales of $211 million (a 4% decline YoY) and gross margins expanding to 62.4%. Management raised full-year guidance for worldwide net sales to a 3%-5% decline range from the prior 4%-6%, while also raising adjusted operating margin expectations to 4%-6%.

negative_highlights: R&D expenses increased compared to prior year driven by higher external spend on HCV phase III program
Over 10% of patients prematurely discontinued treatment or were lost to follow-up, highlighting adherence challenges
positive_highlights: C-BEYOND trial met primary endpoint with bemnifosbuvir achieving 93.9% SVR rate in MITT population
Phase III C-FORWARD fully enrolled with >880 patients and on track for early Q1 2027 readout
Initiated first-in-human Phase I trial of AT-587 for Hepatitis E in July
summary: Atea Pharmaceuticals reported positive top-line results for its Phase III C-BEYOND trial in Q2 FY2026, demonstrating statistical non-inferiority to the standard of care EPCLUSA with an SVR rate of 93.9% versus 94.8%. The company has $219.5 million in cash and marketable securities as of June 30, 2026, providing a runway anticipated through 2027 while R&D expenses increased due to Phase III advancement.

negative_highlights: Group revenue includes investments in early-stage companies Avride and TripleTen which suppress overall margins compared to the core AI business.
Vineland site approval process remains pending a public hearing, though management expects no significant impact on timeline.
positive_highlights: Group revenue surged 454% YoY to $582 million driven by Nebius AI business growth of 514%.
Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded significantly to 41%, with the core Nebius AI business achieving a 50% margin.
Customer prepayments reached an all-time high, covering approximately 50%-60% of associated CapEx for new deals.
summary: Nebius Group reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $582 million (up 454% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $236 million with a margin expansion to 41%. Management reaffirmed full-year guidance for group revenue between $3 billion-$3.4 billion, annualized run-rate revenue of $7 billion-$9 billion, and an adjusted EBITDA margin of approximately 40%, citing strong momentum from new capacity additions and high-margin asset-light models.

negative_highlights: Net income includes a $2.7 million non-cash gain on derivative instruments which does not reflect underlying operating performance.
Sustaining capital expenditures are weighted toward the back half of the year, potentially impacting H2 cost metrics versus current Q2 run rate.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 57% year-over-year driven by zinc production up 23% sequentially compared to Q1.
Adjusted EBITDA reached $9.6 million, nearly 4x higher than the comparable quarter in 2025.
Secured first two customer agreements for Kilbourne Graphite and a conditional supply agreement with RHI Magnesita.
summary: Titan Mining reported record Q2 FY2026 results with revenue of $25.7 million (up 57% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $9.6 million. The company reaffirmed full-year zinc guidance for production between 62-66 million payable pounds, noting that current cost performance is ahead of the annual run rate due to recovering from a Q1 outage. Management highlighted significant commercial progress in graphite with two new customer agreements and confirmed district-wide germanium enrichment.

negative_highlights: Operating expenses increased $2.1 million YoY due to conference costs and approximately $1.9 million in foreign exchange headwinds.
Overall apparel market growth remains modest with ups and downs, though Kornit is gaining share via note weakness in-run demand.
positive_highlights: Revenue beat high end of guidance at $55.3M with positive adjusted EBITDA above the upper range.
Annual Recurring Revenue (ARR) grew to $33.8 million, representing a 79% year-over-year increase driven by the all-inclusive click model.
Approximately 60% of system sales in Q2 and H1 were directed toward traditional screen printers, signaling strong adoption.
summary: Kornit reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $55.3 million (up 11.2% YoY), exceeding the high end of guidance with positive adjusted EBITDA and operating cash flow for the 11th consecutive quarter. Management raised full-year growth expectations to 'high single-digit' from low single-digits, citing a structural shift in screen printing toward digital production where approximately 60% of system sales went to traditional printers. The company highlighted an increase in annual recurring revenue (ARR) by $7 million and noted that roughly 80% of total revenue is now recurring or highly recurring.

negative_highlights: AI-related revenue share increased from 11% in Q4 FY25 to only 13% of total revenue in Q2 FY26.
Visitor traffic to websites is down broadly due to market-wide changes, though Average Order Value (AOV) remained stable.
positive_highlights: Achieved positive GAAP operating profit for the first time in company history with normalized free cash flow of $8.7 million (11% margin).
Signed three large multi-year enterprise contracts representing more than $60 million of accumulated contract value.
Net new ARR reached a record quarter, while NRR improved to 100% across all customers and 107% for customers above $100k ARR.
summary: Similarweb reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $77.2 million (up 9% YoY), exceeding the top end of guidance and delivering positive GAAP operating profit for the first time in company history with normalized free cash flow of $8.7 million. Management raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to a range of $340-$380 million and non-GAAP operating profit guidance to $24-$26 million, citing strong enterprise demand and AI-driven data consumption as key drivers.

negative_highlights: Net income declined quarter-over-quarter due to normalization from an unusually strong first quarter and fading excess liquidity effects.
Funding costs increased 20 basis points, driven by higher Treasury funding for arbitrage strategies and a shift in deposit mix as pension fund withdrawals decreased.
Management explicitly stated they are not raising guidance despite ROE exceeding targets due to prudent monitoring of El Niño risks.
positive_highlights: Higher-yielding loans accelerated with consumer lending growing 9% YoY and small business expanding at a double-digit rate (31%).
Assets under management reached a new record high close to $10 billion, up 14% year-over-year.
Cost of risk normalized to 2.1%, remaining well below the company's risk appetite despite portfolio growth.
summary: IFS reported Q2 FY2026 net income of PEN 585 million and ROE of 18.5%, representing a decline from the prior quarter due to normalizing investment results and cost of risk following an exceptionally strong first quarter, though earnings recovered 23% year-over-year. Revenues increased 9% year-over-year but declined slightly quarter-over-quarter as funding costs rose 20 bps and yield on assets fell 10 bps. Management maintained full-year ROE guidance above 17% while expressing caution regarding potential El Niño impacts in the second half of the year.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA remains negative at -$110 million as capital deployment continues to focus on manufacturing capability and production readiness.
Full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance is lowered slightly compared to prior expectations due to anticipated acceleration of investment in vertical integration.
positive_highlights: Revenue beat guidance by approximately $3.7M driven by EPFD program revenue and Florida Department of Transportation charger deliveries.
Full-year revenue guidance raised to a new high-end target of $42-$50 million, reflecting increased visibility into the balance of the year.
Backlog stands at 1,001 aircraft ($3.9 billion), nearly reaching the set year-end target of $4 billion.
summary: BETA Technologies reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $14.7 million, significantly beating the guidance range of $8-$11 million and showing year-over-year growth of 146%. The company raised its full-year revenue guidance to a new high-end range of $42-$50 million following strong execution on eIPP operations, charger deliveries, and defense programs like EPFD. Adjusted EBITDA was -$110 million, landing at the midpoint of the guided range.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined 30% year-over-year to $20.5 million due to large customer disruptions and macro factors
Net loss of $0.7 million ($0.04 per share) compared to net income in the prior period
Net revenue retention rate dipped below prior levels to 90%, driven by account optimization
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA of $4.9 million exceeded consensus expectations despite revenue miss
Gross margins expanded with non-GAAP net income at $3.1 million driven by favorable channel mix
New AI-enabled product launches (DeepIntent, NLAB, CopayCue) announced to strengthen platform and recurring revenue
summary: Second quarter revenue declined 30% year-over-year to $20.5 million due to a limited number of large customers and macroeconomic factors including MFN pricing dynamics, while adjusted EBITDA was $4.9 million. Management reiterated full year 2026 guidance for revenue between $95-$100 million and adjusted EBITDA between $21-$25 million despite the miss on top-line growth. The company highlighted margin expansion to a normalized high 60%-low 70% range, debt paydown progress, and new product launches including DeepIntent integration.

negative_highlights: Total revenue fell to $24.9 million from $27.9 million, with product revenue down to $13.0 million from $15.7 million on lower shipment volume
Rental revenue dropped to $2.2 million from $4.2 million on lower fleet utilization amid oil price uncertainty
Parts and service gross margin declined to 41% from 53% on higher Factory Protection Plan claims and warranty-related parts costs; rental gross margin fell to 36% from 52%
positive_highlights: Gross margin expanded approximately 8 points to 35% from 27%, and product and accessories gross margin jumped to 31% from 8%
Operating cash flow was $5.4 million versus $1.6 million used in the prior year, and it was the fourth consecutive quarter of positive net income and ninth consecutive of positive adjusted EBITDA
Parts and service revenue grew 14% to $9.7 million from $7.9 million
summary: Capstone Energy+ reported Q1 FY2027 revenue of $24.9 million, down from $27.9 million a year ago, on lower product shipments ($13.0M vs $15.7M) and rental revenue ($2.2M vs $4.2M) due to lower fleet utilization, partially offset by a 14% increase in parts and service revenue to $9.7 million. Despite the lower top line, gross profit rose 16% to $8.8 million and gross margin expanded roughly 8 points to 35%, driving operating income of about $1 million and positive net income of roughly $37,000, though a $1 million PIK preferred dividend accrual left EPS at a loss of $0.03. Adjusted EBITDA was flat at $2.7 million, operating cash flow improved to $5.4 million (including a $3.7 million customer deposit), and no formal guidance was provided; management flagged oil and gas softness, deal timing delays, and the need to refinance or repay $25.3 million of exit notes maturing December 2026.

negative_highlights: Company remains in net loss with operating expenses exceeding gross profit by over $5 million
Q3 expected to be seasonally slower due to the Israeli holiday calendar, pushing weight toward Q4 deliveries
positive_highlights: Smart Cart deliveries nearly doubled sequentially from 500 to 950 units
Gross margin expanded significantly to 42.6% due to efficient Chinese manufacturing and scale
Operating loss narrowed to $7.6 million from a Q1 loss of $8 million
summary: Second quarter revenues reached $5.9 million, a significant sequential increase from Q1's $3.3 million driven by Smart Cart deliveries rising to $4.4 million (up from $2.5M). Gross margin expanded materially to 42.6% as the new Chinese manufacturing facility came online and production costs decreased. Management raised full-year delivery guidance, targeting at least 10,000 units delivered by year-end.

negative_highlights: Industrial segment revenue remained flat due to weakness in broader industrial markets, though semiconductor capital equipment grew sequentially.
Capital expenditures accelerated significantly by $556 million quarter-over-quarter as capacity expansion outpaces current production needs.
positive_highlights: Q4 revenue grew 34% year-over-year to a record $2.05 billion with non-GAAP EPS increasing 74% YoY to $1.74.
Six-inch indium phosphide capacity ramp is one quarter ahead of original plan, doubling output by end of Q4 FY26.
summary: Coherent reported record Q4 FY26 revenue of $2.05 billion (up 34% YoY) and non-GAAP EPS of $1.74 (up 74% YoY), driven by exceptional demand in data center transceivers, OCS, and CPO ramping ahead of schedule. Management raised Q1 FY27 guidance to revenue between $2.2B-$2.4B with a non-GAAP EPS range of $1.85-$2.05, citing record bookings extending into 2028 and accelerated capacity expansion on the six-inch indium phosphide platform.

negative_highlights: Foodservice inflation accelerated sequentially to 2.7%, with beef prices normalizing from mid-teens
Convenience segment case growth slowed slightly due to competitive losses in the quarter
Diesel expense impact was approximately $16 million, though hedging strategy is being evaluated
positive_highlights: Total net sales grew 6.4% in the fourth quarter with growth across all three segments
Adjusted EBITDA increased 7.4% to $587.5 million, hitting the upper end of guidance range
Net income rose 23.4% year-over-year to $162.3 million driven by strong gross profit and mix
summary: PFG reported Q4 FY26 net sales growth of 6.4% and adjusted EBITDA increasing 7.4%, with full-year revenue up nearly 9%. Management raised guidance for fiscal 2027 to $72.5B-$73B in sales (midpoint +7.2%) and $2.125B-$2.225B adjusted EBITDA, citing momentum from new accounts like Love's Travel Stops & RaceTrac and procurement synergies.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened slightly year-over-year from $13.4 million in Q2 FY2025 to $13.9 million.
Existing military R&D contracts are expected to wind down significantly during the second half of the year as work nears completion.
positive_highlights: Awarded largest military contract to date for $41.7 million with the U.S. Navy, securing multi-megawatt power module delivery targets.
Raised full-year revenue guidance by 50% from prior outlook of $10-$15M to approximately $15M due to accelerated R&D services ramp-up.
Identified additive manufacturing speed improvements with potential to increase printer throughput by up to three times.
summary: Hyliion reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $4.9 million and a net loss of $13.9 million, driven by increased R&D services work for the U.S. Navy. Management raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance from $10-$15 million to approximately $15 million following the award of a new $41.7 million military contract and faster-than-expected ramp-up on existing programs.

negative_highlights: Precious metal GEOs sold were down slightly compared to Q2 2025 levels due to the shift from using actual high gold prices back to the fixed conversion price of $4,500/oz.
Candelaria production was lower than prior year as Phase IA higher-grade ore depleted; Cobre Panama restart timeline remains uncertain pending government commission evaluation.
Energy revenue recognition lagged due to delays in receiving actual wellhead data for May and June.
positive_highlights: Revenue and adjusted net income increased 46% year-over-year due to record gold prices (+38%) and strong production growth at Antamina ($23.3M -> $57.4M revenue) and South Arturo.
Total GEOs sold rose 18% YoY to 132,405 units with diversified commodity revenue up 31% despite lower unit volume due to higher gold prices used for conversion.
Company maintains a robust balance sheet with $4.3 billion in available capital and remains debt-free.
summary: Franco-Nevada reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $348 million (implied by context) with adjusted net income and EPS up 46% year-over-year driven by record gold prices (+38%) and higher production at Antamina, South Arturo, Côté Gold, Casa Berardi, and Valentine. The company sold 132,405 total GEOs (up 18%), tracking toward the upper half of its full-year guidance range of 510,000-570,000 units despite a slight pullback in precious metal prices from Q1 highs.

negative_highlights: Non-GAAP gross margin contracted by 210 bps YoY (to 66.3%) due to higher hardware mix and memory costs.
Services revenue was flat year-over-year at $3.8 billion, though services margins expanded.
positive_highlights: Record Q4 revenue of $17.3B with product orders up 35% YoY, led by triple-digit hyperscale AI infrastructure orders ($9.3B total for FY26).
Non-GAAP EPS grew 23% to a record level in the quarter and 14% for the full year.
Hyperscaler revenue projected to reach $7.5 billion in fiscal 2027, up from less than 2% of total revenue in FY25.
summary: Cisco reported record Q4 FY26 revenue of $17.3 billion (up 18% YoY) and non-GAAP EPS growth of 23%, driven by strong networking orders up 35%. The company exceeded the high end of its guidance for both the quarter and fiscal year, with full-year revenue reaching a record $63.3 billion. Management raised FY27 revenue guidance to a range of $72.2-$73.4 billion (implying ~15% growth) and increased EPS guidance to $5.05-$5.11.

negative_highlights: Non-GAAP gross margin contracted slightly from 46.5% to 45.3%, primarily due to increased fuel costs and a decision not to update pricing frequently amidst volatility.
Service fee revenue growth (36%) trailed fulfillment services growth (42%), reflecting the one-time decrease in service fees baseline as Managed Markets V1 merchants migrated to V2.
positive_highlights: GMV increased by 44% YoY to nearly $2.1 billion, marking the first time GMV exceeded this threshold in a non-peak quarter.
Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded over 300 basis points year-over-year to approximately 21%, driven by operating leverage and AI efficiency gains.
The company successfully closed on the acquisition of Passport, adding logistics capabilities expected to contribute $60 million-$59 million in revenue for full-year 2026.
summary: Global-E reported Q2 FY26 results with GMV of $2.1 billion (up 44% YoY) and revenue of $299 million (up 39% YoY), significantly beating the high end of prior guidance. The company raised its full-year 2026 outlook for GMV, revenue, and adjusted EBITDA to reflect strong momentum from new brand launches, Managed Markets V2 adoption, and the recently closed acquisition of Passport. Adjusted EBITDA reached $62.4 million (a margin of ~21%), representing a more than 300 bps expansion compared to Q2 FY25.

negative_highlights: Maggiano's comp sales declined -5.3% driven by traffic contraction, with management assuming flat profits for FY27.
Food and beverage costs increased 80 basis points due to commodity inflation (beef) and elevated tomato prices from a Florida freeze.
Alcohol category faces macro pressure despite the success of specific promotions like Margarita of the Month.
positive_highlights: Chili's achieved +6% same-store sales for the quarter, marking its 21st consecutive quarter of growth.
The Big Crispy chicken sandwich launch exceeded estimates, driving unit volume to 55 sandwiches per restaurant per day by end of Q4 (up from 20 pre-launch).
Management raised fiscal 2027 guidance for revenue and EPS following the inclusion of a 53rd operating week in Q4.
summary: Brinker reported Q4 FY26 revenue of $1.536 billion with consolidated comp sales growth of +5% and adjusted diluted EPS of $3.07 (up from $2.49 last year). Management provided fiscal 2027 guidance for revenues between $6.15B-$6.27B and adjusted EPS between $12.60-$13.40, which represents a raise compared to prior expectations given the inclusion of an additional operating week in Q4. While Chili's delivered strong same-store sales growth driven by traffic and price, Maggiano's reported comp sales declines of -5.3% with flat profit assumptions built into next year.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA was approximately -$0.9 million in Q2, driven by non-cash ground lease accruals and stock compensation.
Leasing pace has been slower than expected at Denver Centennial (APA1) due to market dynamics rather than execution issues.
Re-lease step-ups decreased slightly from last quarter as leases move into their third turn with smaller bumps.
positive_highlights: Revenues grew 13% sequentially to reach a new quarterly high, driven by the opening of Miami-Opa Locka Phase II and other campuses.
Cash flow from operations reached almost $3 million in Q2, marking ten consecutive quarters of positive cash flow for the obligated group.
Management reaffirmed full-year 2026 revenue guidance ($42M-$46M) despite a negative EBITDA quarter due to ongoing construction costs.
summary: Q2 revenues increased 13% sequentially and 50% year-over-year to an annualized run rate of $46 million (up from Q1's $39.4M), driven by new campus openings in Miami-Opa Locka Phase II, Dallas, Phoenix, Denver, and Addison. Adjusted EBITDA remained negative at approximately -$0.9 million for the quarter but is expected to turn positive upon opening of Bradley and Addison Phase II later this year. Management reaffirmed full-year 2026 guidance with an annualized revenue run rate between $42M-$46M and adjusted EBITDA between $4M-$6M.

negative_highlights: No specific negative highlights were reported; management emphasized a diversified revenue mix reducing dependence on any single market.
positive_highlights: Revenue reached an all-time quarterly high of approximately $8.3 million, increasing 26% year-over-year.
Gross margin expanded to 26%, up from 15% in Q1 and 24% the prior year quarter.
The company returned to profitability with positive operating income ($0.3M) and net income of $0.01 per share.
summary: Syntec Optics reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $8.3 million, a 26% year-over-year increase driven by growth across defense, space, AI infrastructure, and biomedical segments. Gross margin expanded to 26%, returning the company to positive operating income ($0.3M) after an operating loss in Q1 FY2025. Management raised full-year guidance expectations for sequential revenue growth in both Q3 (guidance $8.3M-$9.0M) and Q4 (guidance $8.75M-$9.25M).

negative_highlights: Gold prices realized in Q2 were slightly below the $4,500/oz price used for full-year GEO guidance calculations.
G&A expenses remained elevated at $5.6 million due to busy first-half integration activities and corporate initiatives.
positive_highlights: Q2 revenue reached $24 million, representing a 127% increase over the prior year period.
Adjusted EBITDA surged to $17.4 million, up nearly 100%, with operating cash flow hitting an all-time record of $15.5 million.
GEO sales hit a company record at 5,250 units, tracking towards the upper end of annual guidance.
summary: The company reported Q2 revenue of $24 million (a 127% YoY increase) and Adjusted EBITDA of $17.4 million (up nearly 100%), driven by record GEO sales at the higher end of guidance. Management stated they are tracking towards the upper end of their annual GEO guidance range, with cash flow supporting a maiden dividend and share repurchases while preparing for the Vizsla acquisition closing in Q3.

negative_highlights: Q2 gross margin of 19% (annualized) or implied single-quarter pressure is below historical ranges due to one-time retooling and supply chain costs.
Management explicitly stated they are not providing specific guidance for the remainder of the year, citing a focus on demonstrating quarterly revenue growth rather than committing to targets.
Supply chain disruptions forced sourcing from alternative suppliers at higher-than-normal costs.

Gross margin for the six-month period improved 176% versus prior year, though Q2 specifically was lower due to one-time transition costs.
FCC certification achieved in July for PowerBridge Pro+ enables simplified deployment architectures driving customer demand.
summary: Energous reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $3.1 million (up from ~$1M prior year) and a gross margin of 19% for the six months ended June 30, which was below recent levels due to temporary U.S.-based capacity retooling costs and higher-priced alternative component sourcing. Management explicitly declined to provide specific revenue guidance but emphasized that Q2 margins were depressed by strategic decisions to prioritize customer delivery timelines over short-term profitability. The company highlighted strong pipeline expansion with Fortune 10 customers, a new FCC certification for the PowerBridge Pro+, and an end-to-end solution launch expected in H2.

negative_highlights: Total revenue declined 4% on an as-reported basis and 1% organically due to lower perpetual license deals
Full-year total revenue guidance was lowered from March expectations (3%-4%) to a range of 0%-2%
Adjusted operating margin decreased by roughly 100 bps year-over-year due to public company launch costs and reduced R&D capitalization
positive_highlights: ARR grew 7% organically on an organic constant currency basis to $1.143 billion
SaaS revenue accelerated with 21% year-over-year growth to $87 million in the quarter
Free cash flow margin was strong at 23% for the quarter, supporting a full-year target of approximately 20%
summary: Octave reported Q2 FY26 total revenue of $398 million, down 1% organically due to a shift toward recurring models and timing delays in public safety perpetual deals totaling approximately $5 million that slipped into the next year. Adjusted operating margin was 29%, slightly lower than the prior year's 31% primarily driven by incremental public company launch costs (listing/audit fees) and reduced R&D capitalization of roughly 7%. Management lowered full-year total revenue guidance to a range reflecting these deal timing uncertainties, while reiterating ARR growth targets.

negative_highlights: DeFi monetization revenue declined 36% q/q from $245k in Q1 to $158k in Q2 due to the termination of HAUS agreements with Native Markets and Felix following the USDH sunset.
Ecosystem rewards dropped significantly quarter-over-quarter, falling from $150k in Q1 to $90k in Q2, attributed to volatile airdrop timing rather than structural decline.
The company explicitly stated that financial impact of product wind-downs was 'immaterial' but acknowledged the specific revenue loss and redeployment timeline.
positive_highlights: Adjusted gross profit grew 20% quarter-over-quarter to $1.2M as DeFi businesses ramped up following the wind-down of legacy segments.
Operating expenses declined significantly from Q3 FY2025 levels, dropping from $4.3 million in H1 to $2.3 million in Q2 due to winding down biotech operations and cost optimization.
New partnerships with Skew Technologies (Partner Markets) and Entropy were announced immediately after quarter end to replace terminated USDH agreements.
summary: Hyperion DeFi reported Q2 FY2026 adjusted gross profit of $1.2 million (up 20% q/q) and net income of $31.0 million driven by a $54.8M unrealized gain on HYPE treasury, though this masks an operating decline in the 'DeFi monetization' segment which fell 36% to $158k due to USDH stablecoin wind-downs. Management maintained its full-year adjusted gross profit guidance of $5 million-$7 million despite these headwinds and a shift from legacy biotech operations, citing rapid redeployment into new partners like Skew and Entropy.

negative_highlights: China revenue growth is constrained by significant tariff costs on U.S.-manufactured products until manufacturing shifts are complete.
APAC reported sales growth was dampened by currency headwinds, resulting in only 2% year-over-year reported growth despite a 14% rise in unit volume in Japan.
Supply chain constraints previously limited the ability to fully meet demand for EVO+ and other products during Q1 and Q2.
positive_highlights: Net sales surged 111% year-over-year to $93.5 million, driven by double-digit growth across Americas and EMEA (excluding Middle East) and a return of China revenue.
Gross margin expanded to 74.5%, reflecting lower ramp-up costs in Switzerland and reduced freight expenses despite tariff impacts on U.S.-manufactured goods shipped to China.
EVO+ adoption in China has outstripped initial supply expectations, with the product representing close to a third of units sold by quarter-end.
summary: Second quarter net sales were $93.5 million, representing an 111% year-over-year increase driven by strong performance in China and the U.S., while excluding a one-time order of $25.9 million recognized in Q3 2025 that will not repeat. The company returned to profitability with net income of $8.1 million ($0.16 per diluted share) compared to a loss last year, supported by gross margin expansion to 74.5%. Management highlighted the successful launch and adoption of EVO+ in China as well as back-to-back record quarters in the U.S., though they declined to provide specific numerical guidance for Q3 or full-year targets.

negative_highlights: Operating loss of approximately $3.4 million in the quarter, with net loss per share of $0.06

Break-even operations not anticipated until Q4 2027, tied to reaching an approximate $5 million quarterly revenue run rate
positive_highlights: Record Q2 revenue of $909,000, up ~61% sequentially and ~115% year-over-year
Full-year 2026 revenue guidance raised and tightened to $3.75-$4.25 million from $3-$4 million
Active commercial cancer centers grew to 21 from 16, with 42 additional centers in the pipeline and a year-end target of 36 or more
summary: RenovoRx reported record Q2 FY2026 revenue of $909,000, up approximately 61% sequentially from $563,000 and approximately 115% year-over-year from $422,000, with gross margin of roughly 84% and a net loss per share of $0.06 that improved from a $0.08 loss a year ago. The company raised and tightened full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $3.75-$4.25 million from a prior $3-$4 million, implying 241%-286% year-over-year growth. Active commercial cancer centers rose to 21 from 16 at the May call, and management targets 36 or more by year-end 2026. The quarter's key new development was full enrollment of the Phase III TIGeR-PaC trial, with 78 of 86 events observed as of August 11, 2026, trial completion expected in the first half of 2027, and top-line data expected in the back half of 2027.

negative_highlights: Six-month commercial sales were heavily impacted by a $2.3 million inventory reserve and expenses related to unused production capacity.
Net loss widened to $54.4 million for the six months ended June 30, 2026 compared to net income of $1.5 million in FY2025 due to non-cash liability remeasurement.
Q2 sales were described as a 'rebuilding quarter' with no contract revenue generated.
positive_highlights: Interim results from V012 Phase III trial showed ATEV achieved 91 more catheter-free days than autologous fistula (p-value of 0.0007).
Infection rates were significantly lower with ATEV at six per 100 patient-years versus 23 for AV fistula.
Total net cash provided was $29.4 million in the first half of FY2026, a turnaround from cash used in operations last year.
summary: Commercial sales for the quarter were $0.4 million compared to $0.1 million in Q2 FY2025, while six-month commercial sales reached $0.9 million versus $0.2 million last year due to a rebuilding of the commercial team and inventory write-downs totaling $2.3 million over the half-year. The company reported a net loss of $36.8 million for Q2 FY2026, driven by non-cash remeasurement of contingent earnout liabilities rather than operational cash burn which remained positive at $29.4 million in H1. Management provided no updated financial guidance but reaffirmed the plan to file a supplemental BLA for dialysis access in November 2026 with an anticipated launch target in Q2 FY2027.

negative_highlights: Q2 2026 revenue fell to $7.8 million from $10.1 million a year ago, a decline of about 23%.
The company was not in compliance with certain financial covenants under its credit facility as of quarter-end and is requesting a waiver from its lender.
Q2 2026 adjusted EBITDA loss widened to $2.3 million from $1.5 million in Q2 2025, and cash and cash equivalents fell to $500,000 from $700,000 at year-end 2025.

Client retention rate was approximately 80% among clients representing roughly 80% of revenue for the six months ended June 30, 2026.

The company posted a net loss of $3.6 million and an adjusted EBITDA loss of $2.3 million, both wider than the prior-year quarter, with gross margin slipping to 34% from 35%. Management disclosed non-compliance with certain financial covenants on its credit facility and said it is negotiating a waiver with its lender, calling discussions constructive but ongoing. Positively, management noted that excluding the DSP decline, first-half revenue grew about 5% year-over-year, and roughly 80% of revenue came from clients with an 80% retention rate.

negative_highlights: Management explicitly stated they do not provide financial guidance, limiting forward visibility on revenue or earnings targets.
Operating expenses of $9.5 million remain elevated relative to GAAP revenue due to spectrum clearing investments and license exchange activity.

Company ended Q1 with a robust balance sheet of approximately $116 million cash and no debt.
Active commercial discussions accelerated over the last two months involving nearly a dozen utility opportunities.
summary: Anterix reported Q1 FY2027 GAAP revenue of $2 million and operating expenses of $9.5 million, including an approximately $11 million gain from broadband license exchanges that significantly improved the income statement. Management highlighted a strong balance sheet with no debt and cash reserves exceeding $116 million while noting active engagement on nearly a dozen utility spectrum opportunities. The company reiterated it does not provide formal financial guidance but expects single-digit million gains in subsequent quarters.

Management confirmed they are undertaking a strategic review of the Transportation and Logistics business following credible inbound interest from multiple parties.

AECO ARR grew 14% year-over-year, reaching a record $1.577 billion driven by cross-note and AI adoption.
Trimble Connect added over one million projects in Q2 alone with nearly 30 billion API calls.
summary: Trimble reported Q2 FY26 organic revenue growth of 10% and EBITDA margins expanding to 28.6%, both beating the high end of guidance. Management raised full-year EPS guidance by $0.10 (to a midpoint implying ~$3.75) and revenue guidance by $50 million, citing strong momentum in AECO (+9%) and Field Systems (+12%). The company announced a new $1 billion share repurchase authorization while undertaking a strategic review of its Transportation business amid inbound interest.

negative_highlights: Gross margin was compressed to approximately 82% in the quarter due to incremental World Cup-related customer support investments and event-driven pricing dynamics.

Management noted that GMS growth outlook for the remainder of the year is being viewed with discipline following the concentration of demand from the World Cup, implying potential normalization or slowdown post-event.
A small subset of orders experienced fulfillment issues during the complex 75-match World Cup tournament period.

Management raised full-year GMS guidance range from $9.7-$9.9 billion (implied) to $10.1-$10.3 billion, reflecting strong second quarter performance.
summary: StubHub reported Q2 FY26 GMS of $3.1 billion (up 34% YoY) and revenue of $573 million (up 33%), driven by the World Cup but with gross margins compressed to ~82%. Adjusted EBITDA nearly doubled year-over-year to approximately $106 million, expanding margin to 18%, while free cash flow reached a trailing twelve-month total of $598 million. Management raised full-year GMS guidance to $10.1-$10.3 billion (representing 10-12% growth) from the prior outlook of 8-10%, maintaining EBITDA guidance at $400-$420 million.

negative_highlights: Core gross margin declined sequentially from Q1's 46.5% to 40.6% due to higher costs associated with renting systems for private cloud demand.
Operating loss widened slightly as the company invests heavily in capacity expansion ahead of massive revenue growth expected in FY27.

Full-year 2026 core gross margin guidance raised to a range of 41%-43% as the company rolls off higher-cost rented systems for owned capacity.
Secured over 600 MW of data center capacity globally, with manufacturing capacity expected to increase more than 10x in FY26.
summary: Cerebras Systems reported Q2 FY26 core revenue of $209.9 million (up 103% YoY) and record gross margins at 40.6%, beating guidance on all metrics despite a sequential margin dip due to temporary rented capacity costs for OpenAI ramp-up. Management raised full-year 2026 core revenue guidance to the range of $880-$890 million, along with adjusted gross and operating margin targets. The company highlighted significant progress in securing over 600 MW of data center capacity by end-2027 and expanding manufacturing capabilities.

negative_highlights: Unfavorable win rate at City of Dreams Macau negatively impacted property EBITDA by approximately $9 million.
VIP win rate declined significantly from a prior year norm, dropping to 2.7% in Q2 FY26 compared to 3.4%-3.7% previously.
Lower than expected visitation and hold relative to prior quarters placed pressure on margins.
positive_highlights: City of Dreams Manila delivered property EBITDA of $31 million, representing a 9% year-over-year growth.
Cyprus operations rose 60% year-over-year in the second quarter despite regional conflicts.
Sri Lanka casino operations recorded positive EBITDA of $3.5 million during ramp-up.

Management noted lower than expected visitation and hold relative to prior quarters placed pressure on margins in Macau, though international properties showed resilience with Manila EBITDA up 9% and Cyprus rising 60%. For the remainder of FY26, total depreciation is guided at $140-$145 million while OpEx per day remains steady at approximately $3.4 million.

negative_highlights: U.S. drinkware sales were flat due to a significant headwind from three cycling SKUs tied to past trend-driven momentum.
Adjusted operating income decreased 7% year-over-year as margin expansion was partially offset by higher SG&A and incentive compensation accruals.
Canada growth remained below expectations with softer wholesale note-in despite healthy underlying consumer demand.
positive_highlights: Adjusted gross margins expanded 170 basis points year-over-year driven by product cost management and commercial team profitability initiatives.
International sales grew 19% to $93 million, led by strong performance in Europe (digital/wholesale) and Japan's first full year as a direct business.
Coolers and equipment category surged with 16% growth driven by innovation resonance across bags, soft coolers, cases, and storage.
summary: YETI reported Q2 FY26 sales of $484 million (up 9% YoY) and adjusted EPS of $0.67 (up 2%), with gross margin expanding 170 bps to 59.5%. Management raised full-year operating margin guidance by 30 bps to approximately 14.9%, citing strong operational execution, pricing discipline, and the benefit from IEPA tariff refunds partially offsetting inflationary pressures.

R&D expenses increased by 20% compared to the prior year quarter.
Net cash used in operating activities rose from $4.8 million to $6.6 million.

summary: Vuzix reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $1.1 million, a decrease of 14% year-over-year from $1.3 million in the prior period. The company posted a net loss attributable to common shareholders of $7.7 million ($0.09 per share), compared to $7.7 million and $0.10 per share respectively in Q2 FY2025, with gross losses narrowing by 15% despite higher R&D expenses driven by new product development costs.

negative_highlights: Sales declined 4% in Japan as expected due to an intentional pullback in promotions.
Fiscal year 2027 guidance for Kate Spade incorporates a high single-digit decline while Coach is guided at mid-single digits.
Q1 FY27 operating margin projected to be flat versus prior year due to higher SG&A from continued marketing investments.

Coach delivered strong Q4 performance with constant currency revenue up 14%, driven by new customer acquisition (over 9 million for the full year) and Gen Z growth.
Kate Spade welcomed approximately 2 million new customers in FY26, transacting at higher AURs than the balance of the base.
summary: Tapestry reported Q4 FY26 revenue growth of 11% and EPS of $1.32 (up 28%), exceeding expectations despite a higher tax rate headwind. The company achieved its three-year commitments two years ahead of plan, delivering record results with operating margin expansion to over 23%. Management raised the dividend by 16% and maintained full-year FY27 guidance for mid-single-digit revenue growth.

negative_highlights: Net revenue declined 29% sequentially to $2.9 million due to intentional transformation away from legacy business.
First half top line missed prior year guidance of $10 million, dropping to $7 million.
Pace of gross margin improvement has not been as fast as planned despite narrowing losses.
positive_highlights: Gross loss narrowed meaningfully from $0.6 million in Q1 2026 to $0.3 million in Q2 2026.
New distribution added nearly 150 high visibility store locations in Metro New York and Northern New Jersey.
Company ended the quarter with $6.1 million in cash and no outstanding debt.
summary: Q2 FY2026 net revenue declined 29% sequentially to $2.9 million and fell year-over-year to $7 million for the first half versus $10 million in H1 2025, reflecting a deliberate shift away from legacy contract manufacturing. Gross loss narrowed from $0.6 million in Q1 2026 to $0.3 million in Q2 2026, though operating and net losses remained at $3.3 million. Management raised the full-year retail store target to approximately 5,000 outlets by year-end across 35 states.

EBITDA loss works out to roughly half a million USD per month in line with adjusted cash burn
U.S. manufacturing footprint selection narrowed to two candidates, still in final stages
positive_highlights: Q2 revenue of ~$1.2M achieved via monthly delivery cadence under U.S. Marine Corps program

Won two new design wins including an AI-enabled autonomous weapon system platform
summary: Mobilicom reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of approximately $1.2 million driven by a shift to monthly delivery cadence under the U.S. Marine Corps program of record. The company maintains an EBITDA loss of roughly half a million USD per month, funded by a strong balance sheet with nearly $16 million in cash and no debt. Management highlighted progress on design wins for new products like SkyHopper Multiband but noted that backlog is lower than the prior quarter due to increased throughput.

negative_highlights: Civil adjusted segment operating income contracted by 13.7% YoY due to credit charges and Middle East conflict impacts.
Management explicitly stated they are 'cautious' on the Civil outlook for the remainder of the fiscal year, expecting seasonality headwinds in Q2/Q3.
Defense adjusted segment operating income was offset by higher SG&A expenses related to increased bid and proposal activity.
positive_highlights: Defense segment delivered a solid beat with revenue up 8.3% YoY to CAD 531.8M and adjusted operating income expanding margins to 9.5% (up from prior year).
Civil business maintained customer retention at less than 1% attrition during the network rationalization of retiring simulators.
Free cash flow generation improved significantly, turning positive with CAD 104 million compared to negative CAD 135 million in Q1 last year.
summary: CAE reported Q1 FY2027 consolidated revenues of CAD 1.2 billion (up 6.8% YoY), while adjusted segment operating income declined to CAD 156.6 million (-7.5%) and EPS remained flat at CAD 0.26 due to higher SG&A, credit charges in Civil, and defense bid costs. Management maintained its full-year fiscal 2027 outlook unchanged despite the quarter's mixed results, citing expected seasonality impacts on Civil margins later in the year. The company generated strong free cash flow of CAD 104 million and repurchased shares.

negative_highlights: Full-year revenue guidance cut by nearly $10 million to a range of $99-$100M due to delays and slower sales growth.
ShotSpotter segment underperformed on both bookings and go-lives, with sales cycles elongating significantly due to political pushback and ARPA funding slowdowns.
SafePointe deployments are lumpy and delayed by customer facility readiness issues, pushing expected revenue into 2027.

Secured multi-year renewals including a five-year ShotSpotter deal with Albuquerque and a new Texas Anti-Gang CrimeTracer contract worth ~$2.5M ARR.
Deferred revenue stands strong at approximately $36 million with over 100 SafePointe lanes in flight providing visibility.
summary: SoundThinking reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $23.9 million (down from $25.9M prior year) and GAAP net loss widening to $4.8 million ($0.37/share), though Adjusted EBITDA turned positive at $1.2 million due to cost reductions. Management revised full-year 2026 revenue guidance down significantly to a range of $99-$100 million (from prior expectations near $110M) citing delays in SafePointe deployments, Puerto Rico contract issues, and ShotSpotter sales cycle elongation driven by political scrutiny and funding constraints. The company maintains confidence in its long-term recurring revenue base but acknowledges the need to underwrite a longer sales cycle.

Shuttered the Treasury Accelerator program in the UK, citing unnecessary complexity rather than thesis failure
Management explicitly stated they are not de-levering currently but waiting for better market terms

Solana achieved two and a half years without outages, processing nearly $9 billion in tokenized equity volume QoQ (+350%)
summary: Management provided no specific financial results for Q2 FY2026 in this transcript, instead focusing on strategic updates regarding their convertible debt structure and capital stack simplification. They maintained a long-term target of one SOL per share by December 2028 but explicitly downgraded precision on short-term guidance due to market volatility. The company highlighted Solana network upgrades like Alpenglow and increased TPS while noting that preferred equity issuance is currently gated by low SOL prices.

Canadian sales faced significant pressure in both wholesale and retail channels

summary: FGI reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $31.9 million (up 2.9% YoY) and gross margin expansion to 33.4%, driven by trade-related recoveries that improved GAAP operating gain to $1.4M from a prior year loss. Management reaffirmed full-year guidance for adjusted net income ranging from a loss of $0.3 million to a gain of $1.1 million, explicitly stating they are looking toward the lower end of this range due to soft market conditions and cautionary inventory sentiment.

summary: Nektar Therapeutics reported Q2 FY26 non-cash royalty revenue of $10.1 million and a net loss of $40.6 million ($1.23 per share). Management raised full-year cash guidance to end at approximately $815-$840 million, extending the runway into late 2028 past mid-2028 data readouts. The company initiated its Phase III ZENITH AD program in July and received FDA alignment for a single registrational study (ZENITH AA) in alopecia areata to be initiated in early 2027.

R&D expenses increased sequentially and are expected to rise further in Q3 due to $3M upfront licensing payment for ASN-001.
positive_highlights: Record Q2 revenue reached $37.6M with a massive 99% YoY increase driven by the successful commercialization of HEMANGEOL.
Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded significantly to 43%, exceeding prior guidance and demonstrating strong operating leverage despite new transaction costs.
Full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance raised to exceed $52.7M (implied from >$145M revenue at >35% margin), up from the previous expectation of over $36M.
summary: Eton Pharmaceuticals reported record Q2 FY26 revenue of $37.6 million (up 99% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $16.2 million (43% margin). Management raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to exceed $145 million from the prior expectation of over $120 million, citing strong performance across its pediatric dermatology franchise following HEMANGEOL's relaunch and momentum in endocrinology products.

Operating loss increased significantly to $5.1M driven by headcount and OpEx related to ExoDx acquisition integration not present at this time last year.

Successful transition of all Resolve customers to GPS, eliminating a significant contingent liability and de-risking operations ahead of year-end profitability targets.
summary: Q2 FY2026 revenue was $27.2 million (up 16% YoY), but gross margins contracted to 65.7%, operating loss widened to $5.1 million, and adjusted EBITDA missed at -$2.3M versus prior year profit of +$1.1M due to ExoDx integration costs. Management reaffirmed full-year revenue guidance of $110-115M but warned that Q4/Q1 will face headwinds from tissue-based business restructuring and the wind-down of discontinued Resolve operations.

negative_highlights: Company explicitly stated it will not accelerate automotive business until sufficient funding is secured, indicating liquidity constraints on that segment.
Total liabilities remain high at approximately $278 million despite recent reductions and debt resolution efforts.
Net cash used in operating activities for the first six months was $56.5 million.

Net loss narrowed substantially by 69% YoY due to structural cost optimization and strict financial discipline.
Successfully completed $20 million in debt resolution during the quarter while securing new institutional commitments.
summary: FFAI reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $836k (up over 1,500% YoY) and narrowed its net loss to $36M from a prior year's $124.7M due to significant cost reductions ($11.54M COGS vs $26.91M in Q2 FY25). The company raised its annual shipment target for EAI robotics units to 2,000 based on cumulative shipments of 394 through July and plans to reduce total liabilities below $100 million within the next three to four quarters.

negative_highlights: Management explicitly stated it is very hard to forecast accurately due to third-party dependencies on large institutions

Tokenization revenue remains volatile as it depends heavily on new issuances rather than recurring flows

The company executed all five objectives of its 90-day plan, including securing EPC partnerships with Primoris and TSK, forming a strategic alliance with Hillcore to add 2.6 GW of incremental power capacity by 2028, and delivering major on-site milestones like the arrival of Siemens turbines at Port of Houston.

Higher education delivered $200 million in revenue (up 10%) driven by a mix of ~4% enrollment growth, price realization (~2%), and share gains; trailing 12-month market share increased 140 bps to above 30%. Recurring HE revenue grew 14%.

Management reaffirmed full-year guidance, citing strong momentum in K-12 ELA adoption driven by the science-of-reading mandates and higher education share gains despite awaiting final enrollment data for H2 visibility.

Life segment revenue fell to $49.5 million from $53.4 million with pre-tax earnings of $8.5 million versus $10.6 million, driven by lower single-premium sales and a $2.5 million drop in builder profit-share income. Cemetery and Mortuary pre-tax earnings rose 69.5% to $3 million, but operating earnings excluding investments fell 4.8%, and no formal forward guidance was given.

Company trades at significant discount (up to 43%) to NAV despite active strategy

Management highlighted strong operating cash flow growth but noted the market continues to value the company as a passive treasury despite active capital allocation strategies like WhiteFiber expansion and bridge financing.

Q3 procedure volume is historically lower in various regions, creating a seasonal headwind

summary: LENSAR reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $16.5 million (up 18% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $3.6 million, its strongest quarterly performance to date driven by recurring revenue growth to $13.7 million and a one-time tariff refund benefit. The company raised guidance implicitly through strong execution despite noting that operating expenses will normalize higher in future quarters as commercial investments resume following the terminated merger with Alcon.

Free cash flow conversion reached an exceptional 187%, generating $218 million in the quarter versus a loss of $32 million in Q1 FY2026.
Data center orders expanded over 80% year-over-year, providing strong visibility into project-based demand for lead-acid and upcoming lithium offerings.
summary: EnerSys reported Q1 FY2027 net sales of $936 million (up 5% YoY) and adjusted diluted EPS of $4.20 per share (excluding one-time tariff refunds), driven by strong growth in Network Infrastructure Solutions (+9%) and Precision Power Solutions (+24%). Management raised second-quarter guidance, expecting revenue between $955-$995 million and excluding-45X adjusted EPS up 21% YoY at the midpoint. The company highlighted record free cash flow of $218 million and secured a DOE grant for a new defense-focused lithium manufacturing facility.

Q2 adjusted operating expenses were elevated by $2.5 million in one-time compensation costs.

CoinDesk media metrics showed strong growth with page views up 38% YoY and unique visitors up 83%.

Management reaffirmed full-year operating ranges but lowered Q3 gold expectations and noted higher tax expenses ($179M) impacting net earnings compared to consensus estimates. The company returned a record $300 million to shareholders via buybacks and dividends, maintaining strong liquidity of approximately $3.2 billion.

Global region delivered over 18% net revenue growth driven by double-digit organic expansion in water (over 20%) and energy/resources.
summary: Stantec reported Q2 FY26 net revenue of CAD 1.8 billion (up ~12% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA margin expansion to a record 18.7%. Management raised the full-year adjusted EBITDA margin outlook to 17.8%-18.3%, citing strong backlog growth, particularly in water and global regions, while noting Q2 U.S. organic growth was impacted by timing issues rather than demand weakness.

IXCHIQ locally manufactured vaccine approved by Brazil's health authorities and expected to be incorporated into the public system in the near future after vaccinating over 50,000 people.

The company reaffirmed its full-year guidance despite these headwinds but noted that operating loss widened to EUR 49.9 million due to one-off restructuring costs (EUR 3.2M) and non-recurring inventory/write-down impacts totaling over EUR 10 million in the first half.

negative_highlights: Operating expenses surged from $1.5 million in Q2 FY2025 (pre-public) to $5.7 million in the current quarter due to public company costs and growth investments.
Net loss widened to $1.8 million compared to net income of $0.8 million in the prior year period, primarily driven by higher G&A expenses.
Ammunition demand remained soft despite core business strength.

PEW Logistics processed over $1.9 million in gross merchandise value with the addition of a third manufacturer, Backwoods Suppressors.

Gross margin expanded significantly from 10.6% to approximately 13.5%, while operating expenses rose sharply due to incremental costs associated with becoming a public company and scaling PEW Logistics. The quarter ended the transition period for like-for-like expense comparisons, resulting in an adjusted EBITDA loss of $1.7 million compared to prior year income.

summary: DLocal reported Q2 FY26 TPV of $17.7 billion (up 92% YoY) and gross profit of $127 million (up 29% YoY), driven by record performance in Brazil ($40M GP) and Argentina ($20M GP). Management raised full-year guidance for TPV growth to 60%-70% and gross profit growth to 25%-30%, while maintaining operating profit growth at 27.5%-32.5%. The company highlighted strong net revenue retention of 153% and a sequential improvement in operating leverage, though it noted some FX headwinds and one-off tax impacts affecting the full-year outlook.

summary: Epsilon reported Q2 2026 as its production trough for the year, with crude from the Powder River Basin and Permian contributing only late in the quarter; CFO stated Q2 was the low point and growth escalates from Q3 through year-end. For the first time the company issued H2 2026 production guidance, with full-year 2026 midpoint implying high-teens total production growth and almost 200% year-over-year oil growth, driven mainly by Q4 Parkman volumes. Adjusted net income and EPS in the summary table required a press release correction, though GAAP results, cash flows and business economics were unaffected. Debt was paid down $10 million in H1, and the company expects to use the revolver to partly fund the Q3 capital ramp while staying within a 1.5x EBITDA leverage target.

summary: Soluna reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $15.1 million (up 145% YoY) and a net loss of $22.6 million compared to $7.8 million in the prior year, driven by non-cash stock-based compensation ($9.4M), interest expense increases, and debt extinguishment losses following capital raises totaling ~$183M. Management raised guidance for operating capacity from 192 MW at quarter-end to an expected 206 MW by summer end due to the energization of Kati 1 Phase 3. The company acquired a $53M wind farm and consolidated ownership of Project Dorothy, while advancing two major AI campuses (Kati 2 and Dorothy 3) toward construction.

CapEx execution remains strong with BRL 7.5 billion invested YTD and a contracted backlog of over BRL 40 billion through 2029.

Management provided a cautious outlook on underlying cost normalization for the second half of the year, noting that roughly 75-80% of current elevated OpEx is expected to be recovered through future tariff cycles or productivity gains by 2027.

summary: ARS Pharma reported Q2 FY26 net product revenue of $26.2 million and total operating expenses of $95.1 million with gross margins at approximately 62%. Non-GAAP operating loss for the first half narrowed to $8.8 million from $14.9 million in the prior year period, demonstrating operational leverage.
Cash position strengthened with cash on hand rising 35% quarter-over-quarter following capital raises.

GAAP gross margin was 12.1% for the quarter but improved significantly in H1 with a record 31%, while operating loss narrowed sequentially despite lower volumes. Management revised full-year guidance downward, projecting revenue between $35 million and $43 million.

negative_highlights: Leverage ratios declined to 1.29x from 1.43x due to debt paydowns and higher NAV.
Credit hedge portfolio reduced by approximately $56 million (from $188m to $132m) creating earnings drag in April.
CLO equity market remains unattractive for new issues, limiting that specific growth avenue.
positive_highlights: Economic return of 8.1% non-annualized driven by NAV increase and distributions.
Adjusted NII run rate in July is approximately 20% higher than the second quarter figure.
Portfolio repositioning improved credit quality and yield potential without reaching for yield.
summary: For the quarter ended June 30, 2026, EARN reported GAAP net income of $0.33 per share and adjusted net investment income (NII) of $0.15 per share, while NAV increased to $4.18 per share. The company reduced leverage from 1.43x to 1.29x while growing the CLO portfolio by 8.5% through active rotation and capital deployment.

summary: Figure reported Q2 FY26 consumer loan marketplace volume of $4.3 billion (up 132% YoY), beating the top end of guidance by 4%. Adjusted net revenue reached $218 million with adjusted EBITDA margins expanding to 55%, driven largely by Figure Connect now representing 65% of total volume and ecosystem fees becoming the largest P&L line item. Management raised Q3 volume guidance expectations, citing strong July performance ($1.7B) and a confident outlook for August/September.

GAAP net loss from continuing operations was $4.1 million, an improvement of 40% year-over-year to a smaller absolute loss compared to the prior period. Management highlighted a debt-free balance sheet with no repurchases made under the newly authorized program due to blackout periods.

Two scheduled biopsies were cancelled last-minute in Q2 due to patient health deterioration.
Manufacturing yields remain variable with a rare event of an out-of-spec test failure requiring FDA specification review.

Management highlighted operational bottlenecks including scheduling disruptions, patient health deterioration leading to cancellations, and manufacturing yield variability as key headwinds.

negative_highlights: Total revenues declined 2.9% YoY, with electronics and home appliances revenue moderated by a high trading base and upstream price increases.
General merchandise growth was impacted by the same high comparison base effects seen in other categories during Q2.

JD Retail gross margin expanded 130 bps YoY to a record high of 18.5%, marking the 17th consecutive quarter of expansion.
JD Food Delivery narrowed total losses by over 50% YoY while maintaining healthy order volume momentum.

Non-GAAP net income surged by 20.8% YoY to RMB 8.9 billion as JD Retail gross margin expanded to 18.5% and JD Food Delivery losses narrowed significantly. Management raised the outlook for H2, expecting top-line growth re-acceleration in electronics/home appliances once base effects normalize.

Management announced a new $20 million share repurchase program initiated July 1st but provided no specific guidance for the full year.

Management confirmed sufficient capital runway extending into Q4 2028 following the reduction in force.
