Sequential cash burn decreased to $1.7 million from Q1 levels as working capital timing normalized.
summary: Q2 FY2026 revenue increased 57% year-over-year to $2.6 million while net loss declined by 24% from the prior quarter and cash burn decreased to $1.7 million. Management highlighted a shift toward higher-margin non-QM products, resulting in July margins reaching company records and sequential improvements across operating expenses and adjusted EBITDA. However, management explicitly stated they are not providing formal financial guidance for Q3 due to market uncertainty.

negative_highlights: Engineering and design revenues declined 4%, primarily due to soft demand in sustainability consulting for mixed-use clients.
Consolidated gross margin was impacted by a revenue mix shift toward lower-margin installation services following the Bowers acquisition.
Sustainability consulting business experienced softer market conditions reflecting broader commercial real estate challenges.
positive_highlights: Organic revenue growth was nearly 60%, with total revenue more than doubling when including acquisitions.
Full-year 2026 guidance raised significantly on both top-line ($4.7B-$4.8B) and bottom-line (~$565M-$585M).
Backlog reached a record $5.7 billion, up 105% year-over-year.
summary: Legence reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $1.3 billion (up 111% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA growth of 114%, driven by organic expansion in data centers/technology and the Bowers acquisition. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance for both revenue ($4.7B-$4.8B, up ~13%) and adjusted EBITDA (~$565M-$585M, up ~20%), citing strong backlog growth of $5.7 billion (up 105% YoY) and accelerating project execution speeds.

negative_highlights: Consolidated revenue declined year-over-year, with the GEO segment down 26% due to non-renewals and lower capacity renewals.
Two legacy satellites (Anik F4 and Telstar 14R) were retired during the quarter, creating a headwind for cash flow visibility.
Net loss widened significantly to CAD 559 million compared to prior periods.
positive_highlights: Secured the first contract in the ESCP-P program, adding significant backlog and funding for Lightspeed acceleration.
GEO segment backlog increased to CAD 900 million due to a five-year extension of a broadcast video contract.
FCC report confirmed eligibility for $189 million in incentive payments related to C-band spectrum repurposing.
summary: Telesat reported Q2 FY26 consolidated revenue of CAD 79 million and a net loss of CAD 559 million, driven by lower GEO segment revenue (down 26% YoY) due to contract expirations and satellite retirements. Management reiterated its guidance for the legacy GEO business but raised full-year investment guidance for Lightspeed from CAD 1-1.2 billion to CAD 1.3-1.5 billion following a decision to accelerate constellation expansion to 225 satellites funded by new government contracts.

negative_highlights: Revenue fell to $3.1M from $5.7M and gross margin contracted to 10.9% from 23.5% on a one-time facility scale-up impact
Adjusted EBITDA loss widened to $8.3M from $4.5M and R&D rose to $5.9M from $3.5M on the EscharEx VALUE trial
Cash declined to about $36M from $54M at year-end 2025 with $20M of first-half burn, and management declined to detail the components of the BARDA/MSA revenue
positive_highlights: NexoBrid posted its strongest quarter since launch at Vericel, with record quarterly revenue, hospital unit sales and ordering centers, and roughly 80 burn centers ordering since launch
Updated U.S. market assessment for EscharEx, now including pressure ulcers, raised estimated peak sales to $1.05 billion from about $800 million
Full-year 2026 revenue guidance of $24M-$26M was reaffirmed, with management noting the facility timing is not expected to materially affect it
summary: Q2 2026 revenue fell to $3.1M from $5.7M a year ago, gross margin compressed to 10.9% from 23.5%, operating loss widened to $9.5M from $5.7M and adjusted EBITDA loss widened to $8.3M from $4.5M, all attributed to timing of BARDA-funded development revenue and a one-time facility scale-up impact. The company reaffirmed full-year 2026 revenue guidance of $24M-$26M, implying a heavy second-half weighting from the Vericel MSA, Department of War programs and product supply. Net loss narrowed to $7.4M from $13.3M on non-cash financial income, cash fell to about $36M from $54M at year-end with $20M of first-half burn. Operationally, the EscharEx VALUE Phase III interim reassessment and enrollment completion remain targeted for Q1 2027 and the expanded NexoBrid facility approval is expected as early as 2H 2027.

negative_highlights: Inflation proved more persistent than anticipated at over 32%, impacting macroeconomic conditions and FX dynamics.
Net income was impacted by increased depreciation associated with the commercial launch of 5G assets.
Paycell margins faced volatility due to erosive POS transaction profitability, though total revenue grew 22%.
positive_highlights: Group revenue achieved genuine real growth of 2.5% YoY in an environment where inflation exceeded 30%.
Digital Business Services delivered outstanding performance with revenue up 33% to TRY 8.7 billion, supported by a system integration backlog of TRY 16 billion.
Turkcell crossed the historic milestone of 40 million mobile subscribers for the first time in company history.
summary: Turkcell reported Q2 FY2026 group revenue of TRY 71.8 billion (up 2.5% YoY) and net income of TRY 5.2 billion, driven by real growth despite inflation exceeding 30%. Management maintained full-year guidance unchanged after revising year-end inflation expectations to around 28%, citing disciplined pricing and strong momentum in Digital Business Services (+33%) and FWA (+64k subscribers). The company crossed the 40 million mobile subscriber milestone with a postpaid base of 32.5 million, while EBITDA margin remained steady at 41.8%.

negative_highlights: Management explicitly declined to provide quantitative guidance on YUVIWEL patient starts or sales ranges, citing insufficient time in market for analytical trends.
SG&A expenses increased significantly from EUR 145 million in Q1 to EUR 173 million in Q2 due to investments accelerating global launches.
positive_highlights: Total product revenue more than doubled year-over-year, with YORVIPATH reaching blockbuster status on a run-rate basis in its second launch year.
YUVIWEL enrollment accelerated rapidly to over 220 unique patients by end of July, capturing >65% reimbursement approval rate and demonstrating strong market expansion beyond switches.
COACH trial data showed unprecedented arm span improvements (+9.4 cm) with combination therapy compared to limb lengthening surgery.
summary: Ascendis Pharma reported Q2 FY26 total revenue of EUR 339 million (up from EUR 145m in the prior quarter), driven by YORVIPATH sales of EUR 252 million and SKYTROFA at EUR 55 million. The company achieved a significant non-product milestone gain of EUR 17 million related to TransCon CNP, resulting in net profit of EUR 207 million. Management raised full-year cash flow guidance expectations from greater than EUR 300m (implied prior) to greater than EUR 500 million for the remainder of 2026.

negative_highlights: Operating expenses rose sequentially to $806 million as timing effects reversed from Q1 and international expansion investments accelerated.
Overall NPLs deteriorated slightly by 40 basis points due to portfolio mix shifts rather than fundamental credit quality issues in core segments.
positive_highlights: Net income reached a milestone $1.1 billion, up 49% year-over-year and marking the first time exceeding $1B.
Risk-adjusted net interest margin expanded to a record 12.4%, driven by lending growth and disciplined risk expansion rather than portfolio deterioration.
Mexico banking license approved with deposits at $5.7 billion, demonstrating successful transformation into a full-scale digital bank.
summary: Nu Holdings reported a historic quarter with net income exceeding $1 billion for the first time ($1.1B), driven by gross revenue of nearly $5.9 billion and record risk-adjusted NIM expanding to 12.4%. The company achieved this while maintaining an efficiency ratio near its long-term target of 20% despite sequential operating expense increases due to international expansion investments.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined year-over-year due to the end of Menarini's reimbursement ($6.5M impact)
Phase III XPORT-EC-042 study failed to achieve statistical significance in endometrial cancer, leading to a strategic pivot away from that program
Cash runway extends only to September 2026 without additional financing or lender waivers
positive_highlights: U.S. XPOVIO net product revenue of $30.8M showed consistent underlying demand despite competition
Strong clinical momentum for selinexor in myelofibrosis with FDA feedback supporting SVR35 as a surrogate endpoint
Planned sNDA submission remains on track for August 2026
summary: Karyopharm reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $33.4 million (down from $37.9M prior year) and a net loss of $67 million due to the conclusion of Menarini's reimbursement, though underlying operating performance improved with disciplined expense reductions. Management reaffirmed full-year 2026 guidance for total revenue between $130-$150 million but highlighted an urgent liquidity constraint requiring financing or strategic alternatives by September 10th to avoid a default on their term loan.

negative_highlights: Total Q2 revenue declined 5% year-over-year as a $10M drop in SEO revenue offset data growth.
Marketing revenue fell 10% to $26.5 million due to declines in both international markets and organic search channels.
Full-year guidance implies only low-single-digit growth, suggesting the business has not yet recovered its prior high-growth trajectory.
positive_highlights: Data services revenue grew 12% year-over-year to $11.2M driven by enterprise subs and B2B OpticOdds solutions.
Adjusted free cash flow of $9.6 million was generated, with a strong conversion rate of 81% in the quarter.
Non-SEO marketing revenue now accounts for 67% of total marketing business, diversifying away from organic search.
summary: Grandstand reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $37.8 million and adjusted EBITDA of $7.7 million, both in line with expectations but representing a 5% year-over-year decline due to lower marketing revenue offsetting strong data growth ($11.2M). The company reiterated full-year guidance for revenue between $165-$170 million and adjusted EBITDA between $45-$50 million, noting that the current run rate implies modest flat-to-low-single-digit annual growth rather than a significant beat or raise.

negative_highlights: Adjusted gross margin contracted 130 bps year-over-year due to a combined 280 bps drag from FX and U.S. tariffs.
Net leverage increased to 1.8x following the accelerated share repurchase (ASR) and debt refinancing activities.
Middle East conflicts continue to impact demand in key markets like the UAE, though mitigated by strength elsewhere.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 15% in constant currency, hitting the high end of guidance with double-digit growth across Americas (14%), EMEA (15%), and APAC (23%).
D2C channel accelerated to 16% growth while retail revenue surged 50%, driven by new store openings.
Full price realization remained strong at 93% in Europe, demonstrating brand resilience against promotional pressure.
summary: Birkenstock reported Q3 FY26 revenue of EUR 720 million (up 15% in constant currency) and adjusted EBITDA of EUR 242 million. Management raised full-year guidance for revenue growth to the high end of its range at 15% and increased the minimum adjusted EBITDA target to at least EUR 710 million, citing strong momentum across all regions despite FX headwinds and tariffs.

negative_highlights: R&D expenses increased by $0.9 million YoY due to investments in clinical development for PTSD and alcohol use disorder research.
G&A expenses rose approximately $0.7 million driven by higher professional fees and administrative costs.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 35% YoY to $17.1 million driven by a 42% increase in system shipments (125 units).
Operating income surged over 300% year-over-year, marking the 12th consecutive quarter of profitability.
Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded significantly from 11% to 20%, reflecting strong operating leverage.
summary: BrainsWay reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $17.1 million (up 35% YoY) and operating income increasing over 300% to $2.4 million. The company raised its full-year 2026 guidance from a range of $66M-$68M to $68M-$70M, citing strong demand for the SWIFT protocol and growing remaining performance obligations of $80.4 million.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to $35.1M from $8.1M YoY due to heavy non-cash charges
$29.8 million unrealized loss in the change in market value of digital assets
$2.6 million impairment of Treehouse liquid staking tokens
positive_highlights: Revenue increased significantly to $2.8M from $0.5M YoY due to new treasury strategy
Completed debt restructuring reducing principal balance by $6.8M, strengthening the balance sheet
Staking activities produced an annualized yield of approximately 5.3%
summary: AVAX One reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $2.8 million, a significant increase from $500,000 in the prior year quarter driven by a transition to an Avalanche digital asset treasury strategy. The company recorded a net loss of $35.1 million ($4.41 per diluted share) due to $33 million in non-cash charges, including a $29.8 million unrealized loss on digital assets and a $2.6 million impairment of Treehouse tokens. Management highlighted the restructuring of convertible debentures reducing liabilities by $6.8 million and maintained liquidity at $21.1 million.

negative_highlights: NAND growth is expected to be slower next year as the market focuses primarily on upgrades rather than wafer capacity additions.
Q1 FY27 will be a 14-week quarter, which may result in higher-than-average step-up in operating expenses compared to standard quarters.
positive_highlights: Record Q3 revenue of $9.1 billion driven by double-digit sequential growth across all segments.
Non-GAAP gross margin expanded to a record 50.4% (up 40 bps sequentially) and operating margin hit a record 34%.
DRAM revenue grew 52% YoY, while Applied Global Services delivered record $1.8 billion in revenue.
summary: Applied Materials reported record Q3 FY26 revenue of $9.1 billion (up 15% sequentially and 25% YoY) with non-GAAP EPS of $3.50 (up 41% YoY). Management raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance, citing strengthened demand visibility from customers providing eight-quarter rolling forecasts through to 2030. The company expects particularly strong growth in DRAM and leading-edge foundry logic for the second half of calendar 2027.

negative_highlights: A weaker yen acted as a reported-results headwind given the mostly yen-denominated business
SG&A rose more than expected, attributed in part to a one-time cost from a secondary offering
The roughly JPY 15 million of fee upside is only about half-realized in H2 FY2026 and not fully reflected until next fiscal year
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA rose 32% to $20 million, outpacing 13% revenue growth and lifting the adjusted EBITDA margin to 41%
Average spend per visit increased 9% while trailing-12-month customer visits rose 10% to 6.92 million, with volume and price rising together
Locations reached 287, up 34 year-on-year, and first-half transaction value grew 19% year-on-year
summary: SBC reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $49 million, up 13% year-on-year, and adjusted EBITDA of $20 million, up 32%, for a 41% adjusted EBITDA margin, with profit growth outpacing revenue. Same-clinic revenue rose 6%, average spend per visit rose 9%, and locations reached 287, up 34 year-on-year, despite a weaker yen acting as a headwind. Management did not provide quantitative full-year guidance but said roughly JPY 15 million of annual fee increases (Gorilla and call center) would be about half-reflected in Q3/Q4 and fully reflected next fiscal year, and characterized the quarter as completing 2025 structural reforms and entering a re-acceleration phase.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA was a loss of approximately $51 million as the company front-loaded investments in operating expenses.
Cash operating expenses were elevated at ~$93 million due to integration costs and growth investments, though management expects moderation later in the year.
positive_highlights: Record quarterly revenue of $83.8 million representing more than 13-fold growth versus the prior year period.
Pro forma organic revenue grew approximately 85% year-over-year, validating underlying business execution beyond acquisition impacts.
Backlog increased approximately 33% sequentially to roughly $757 million with a two-year strategic pipeline exceeding $1.4 billion.
summary: Ondas reported record Q2 FY26 revenue of $83.8 million (up >13x YoY) and adjusted gross margin stable at 50.4%. Management raised the full-year 2026 revenue guidance to a range of $525-$550 million, citing strong organic growth drivers including Sentrycs (+298% pro forma), Airobotics (+112%), and 4M (+258%). The company ended with approximately $1.4 billion in cash equivalents after deploying capital for new acquisitions.

negative_highlights: Public sector revenue declined YoY due to temporary budgetary shifts in late Q2 driven by conflict spending priorities.
VDR deal timing remains uncertain, causing some large hyperscaler transactions to be under active review rather than fully processed.
Fiscal 2026 guidance was lowered from prior expectations with a new range of $100-$150 million.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew sequentially by 20% to $24.3M driven by VDR and licensing services which were up 40% QoQ.
Executed approximately $11.3 million in annualized cost reductions, with a target of reaching $15-$20 million total savings by end of FY26.
Secured major public sector wins including multi-year renewals with the Pac-12 Conference and CHP for document redaction.
summary: Veritone reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $24.3 million (up 20% sequentially and 5% YoY), but missed expectations due to delayed public sector budget shifts related to the conflict in Iran and timing issues with hyperscaler VDR deals. Management lowered fiscal 2026 full-year guidance to a range of $100-$150 million, citing reduced visibility on government contracts and specific VDR deal closures. The company executed significant cost reductions totaling approximately $11.3 million annually as of June 30, positioning for potential breakeven in the first half of fiscal 2027.

negative_highlights: Full-year revenue growth implies ~28% in H2 against an exceptionally strong prior year of ~36%, indicating a conservative outlook.
Rental segment margins faced an approximate 50 basis point headwind from increased fuel costs, though partially offset by pricing power.
positive_highlights: Rental segment revenue surged >39% YoY driven by fleet absorption ahead of plan on large-scale mega projects.
Adjusted core EBITDA reached $531 million, reflecting a robust margin mix between rental and sales segments.
Management raised OWN program contribution guidance for the full year by approximately $11M due to strong institutional demand.
summary: EquipmentShare reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $1.4 billion (up 26% YoY) and rental segment revenue of $908 million (up >39% YoY). Adjusted core EBITDA grew to $531 million, representing a beat on the prior period's implied growth trajectory despite management noting that full-year guidance remains conservative for the back half. Management raised specific OWN program contribution guidance by approximately $11M and highlighted strong demand visibility in mega projects.

negative_highlights: Telco core income declined 2% YoY to PHP 16.6 billion, primarily due to a 6% increase in depreciation and amortization.
Home revenues dropped 1% to PHP 30 billion as the business continues to lag from Q1 installation constraints carried into H1.
Maya's contribution to core income was lower than expected for the quarter due to one-time accounting adjustments, though underlying growth remains strong.
positive_highlights: Enterprise revenues grew 5% to PHP 24.8 billion, driven by ICT revenue expansion of 22%.
Wireless top-ups turned positive in June (+1%) and improved further in July (+3%), indicating a recovery trend after Q1 constraints.
Home fiber net adds accelerated significantly in the second quarter with postpaid churn improving to 1.4%.
summary: PLDT reported first-half FY26 service revenues of PHP 108.7 billion (up 2% YoY) and EBITDA of PHP 56.1 billion at a stable 52% margin, though Telco core income declined 2% to PHP 16.6 billion due to higher depreciation. Wireless revenue was broadly flat while Home revenues fell 1% following Q1 installation constraints that are now recovering in the second quarter with positive net adds starting in May. Enterprise remained a strong growth driver up 5%, and management reiterated full-year CapEx guidance of mid-PHP 50 billion despite elevated depreciation from network upgrades.

negative_highlights: Consolidated net loss widened year-over-year from $3.9M to $4.3M driven by increased costs for Coosa permitting, stock-based compensation, and product development.
Graphite flake input prices remain at historic lows ($500-$600/ton), which management notes is suboptimal compared to the higher price environment desired when Coosa comes online in 2028-2029.
positive_highlights: Received formal EXIM approval for a $25 million loan to support Kellyton Phase I development, representing non-dilutive capital with single-digit cost of capital expectations versus mid-teens private market rates.
summary: Westwater Resources reported a Q2 FY2026 consolidated net loss of $4.3 million ($0.03/share), an increase from the prior year's loss of $3.9 million due to higher permitting costs, stock-based compensation, and product development expenses. The company received a significant non-dilutive milestone in the form of a formal EXIM approval for a $25 million loan dedicated exclusively to advancing Phase I construction at the Kellyton Graphite Plant. Management maintains a target timeline for commercial production starting as soon as next year (late 2026/early 2027), contingent on securing remaining capital and closing documentation.

negative_highlights: Operating expenses increased significantly by 46% YoY due to higher court costs and stock-based compensation from the IPO.
Management explicitly stated they do not provide guidance on deployments or earnings, limiting forward visibility.
Cash efficiency ratio excluding Bluestem/Conn's portfolios was lower at 67.8%, reflecting one-time portfolio impacts.
positive_highlights: Record deployments in July of $185 million across the spectrum including new auto finance portfolios.
Strong growth in legal channel collections, up 54% YoY to $64 million.
Forward flow commitments reached a record $480.7 million as of June 30th.
summary: Jefferson Capital reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $178 million (up 16% YoY) and collections of $301 million (up 18% YoY), driven by strong deployments including a record July figure. Adjusted EPS was $0.77, with cash efficiency at 72.2%. The company raised its estimated remaining collections to $3.4 billion (+18%) but did not provide specific forward guidance for revenue or earnings.

negative_highlights: Revenue from Remini declined, attributed partly to market saturation rather than AI disruption.
Splice revenue also contributed negatively to the overall portfolio growth rate.
Organic growth of 3% was lower than Q1's 6%, reflecting a blended impact from low single-digit growth in newer acquisitions like AOL and Vimeo.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 126% YoY with organic revenue growth of 3%, exceeding internal expectations.
AOL Advertising performance was better than anticipated following price experiments and infrastructure upgrades.
Management successfully closed the acquisition of Tractive ($759M EV) and reached an agreement to acquire Airtable for $1.29 billion.
summary: Bending Spoons reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $704 million (up 126% YoY) and adjusted operating income of $381 million (up 150%), driven by strong performance in AOL Advertising, WeTransfer, and Tractive. Management provided full-year guidance for revenue between $2.78 billion-$2.82 billion and adjusted operating income between $1.46 billion-$1.51 billion, which excludes the pending Airtable acquisition expected to close later this year.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened significantly to $78.9 million compared to a prior year loss of $45.3 million.
SG&A expenses surged by $27.4 million quarter-over-quarter, primarily due to hiring for the commercial function and pre-launch activities.
No revenue reported in Q2 as product shipments are not expected until late third quarter 2026.
positive_highlights: FDA approved REVTORPYK for HR-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer without PIK3CA mutation following progression on endocrine therapy.
NCCN updated guidelines recommending gedatolisib regimens as preferred Category 1 options in the second-line setting.
Positive efficacy data from VIKTORIA-1 showed median PFS of 11.1 months for the triplet regimen versus 5.6 months with alpelisib.
summary: Celcuity reported a Q2 FY2026 net loss of $78.9 million ($1.44/share) and an adjusted net loss of $58.7 million ($1.07/share), representing significant year-over-year deterioration in profitability driven by a $35 million increase in SG&A expenses to support commercial launch preparations. While the company achieved major regulatory milestones including FDA approval for REVTORPYK (gedatolisib) and positive Phase III data, it has not yet generated any revenue from product sales as shipments are expected only late in Q3 2026.

negative_highlights: Total revenue fell 20% due to a significant pullback in procurement services, which dropped 45% compared to the prior-year quarter.
Net income per diluted share decreased from $0.06 to $0.05 primarily because of higher tax expenses following the full release of the valuation allowance on deferred tax assets.
Systems integration revenue was slightly below recent quarterly averages, with management noting a downturn in mainstream business demand.
positive_highlights: Systems integration revenue increased 46% year-over-year to $13.9 million as the business mix shifts toward higher-margin offerings.
Facilities management revenue surged 84% to $2.7 million, offsetting declines in maintenance agreements with discrete project work.
Blended gross margin expanded significantly from 16.4% last year to 22.8%, reflecting the structural improvement in earnings quality.
summary: Total revenue declined 20% year-over-year to $35.1 million due to a sharp drop in procurement services ($18.2M vs $33M prior year), though higher-margin systems integration grew 46%. Gross profit increased 11% and Adjusted EBITDA rose 12%, driven by the shift toward high-margin segments, but net income fell slightly to $0.05 per share due to a one-time tax valuation allowance release in Q4 FY2025 affecting comparability.

negative_highlights: Management explicitly stated they are not reaffirming prior revenue guidance and declined to provide specific numbers due to deployment timing uncertainty.
Operating loss widened significantly in Q2 compared to the same period last year as expenses rose sharply ahead of commercialization.
Sequential gross margin contracted from 48% in Q1 to approximately 28% in Q2, attributed to product mix and pre-revenue engineering investments.
positive_highlights: Sequential revenue growth accelerated by approximately 51%, reaching $8.1 million.
Gross margin expanded significantly year-over-year from roughly 7.8% to 27.9% due to a shift away from lower-margin acquired product sales.
Series A rights exercise generated net proceeds of approximately $20.12 million, strengthening the balance sheet for larger customer engagements.
summary: AmpliTech Group reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of approximately $8.1 million (up 51% sequentially but down year-over-year) and a net loss of roughly $3.09 million driven by elevated investments in R&D, marketing, supply chain readiness, and cybersecurity to support larger customers. Gross margin improved significantly from the prior year period due to product mix changes following an asset acquisition, rising from 7.8% YoY but declining sequentially from Q1's 48%. Management explicitly declined to reaffirm or provide specific revenue guidance for the remainder of FY2026, citing timing uncertainties in large telecom deployments.

negative_highlights: Retail revenue declined approximately 2% year-over-year due to consumer sentiment issues
Automotive scanning volumes are trending lower, though a reversal is anticipated
Full-year FY2026 total revenue expected to be slightly lower than FY2025 if the customer's vendor review plan proceeds
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 7% sequentially to $5.9 million despite macro headwinds
Adjusted EBITDA remained positive for the fifth consecutive quarter at $1.1 million
Major customer volume reduction fears have not materialized as expected; new purchase order signed
summary: Q2 FY26 revenue was $5.9 million (up 16% YoY), with gross margin at 91%, adjusted EBITDA of $1.1M, and net income of $633k. Management noted that a major customer's vendor review is not yet causing the volume reductions previously feared, though full-year revenue for FY2026 may be slightly lower than FY2025 if plans proceed as communicated. The company maintains a strong balance sheet with $11.8M in cash and no debt.

negative_highlights: Ending ARR fell to $11.6M from $15.9M a year ago; management said it no longer expects to hit its original significant ARR growth target by year-end 2026
Total revenue declined to $7.4M from $8.0M and subscription revenue fell $0.9M to $3.7M
GAAP net loss per share widened to $0.54 from $0.38, with opex up to $16.7M from $13.1M including $5.4M stock comp and $0.7M CEO severance
positive_highlights: Subscription gross profit margin rose 4 points to 89% on $300K lower platform costs; service gross margin up 1 point to 60%
Non-GAAP net loss per diluted share improved to $0.08 from $0.11; non-GAAP opex fell 9% to $8.1M
Secure Gift Card pipeline grew over 30x since start of year to more than 31 retailers engaged, with two additional retailers committing to deployments starting August and October
summary: Total revenue fell to $7.4M from $8.0M a year ago, with subscription revenue down $0.9M to $3.7M (51% of total) and service revenue up $0.3M to $3.6M. Ending ARR dropped to $11.6M from $15.9M, driven by a $3.1M contract expiry and a $2.6M contract reduction, partially offset by $1.5M net ARR growth; management explicitly withdrew its original year-end ARR growth target. Subscription gross margin improved 4 points to 89% and non-GAAP EPS narrowed to -$0.08 from -$0.11, but GAAP net loss per share widened to $0.54 from $0.38 on $5.4M stock comp and $0.7M severance. The new CEO outlined a go-to-market rebuild around retail and CPG, with gift card ARR largely deferred to Q4 2026/Q1 2027.

negative_highlights: Pulp sales volumes were lower compared to Q2 FY25 due to concentrated maintenance downtimes at Pine Bluff and Três Lagoas mills.
EBITDA from Brazilian operations declined 20% year-over-year driven by lower prices, export volume contraction, and unfavorable FX effects.
positive_highlights: Free cash flow remained strong despite volatile geopolitical conditions.
summary: Suzano reported Q2 FY26 results with solid free cash flow and the successful closing of the Arbex acquisition on July 1st, though paperboard volumes were impacted by customer inventory build-up ahead of price increases. Pulp sales reached 2.9 million tons driven by higher export prices to $601/ton despite constrained production from maintenance downtimes in Pine Bluff and Três Lagoas. Management reiterated a focus on deleveraging the business following Arbex consolidation, with cash costs expected to decline below BRL 800/ton in H2 due to reduced downtime and wood consumption.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened due to an incremental operating loss of $1.4M and unfavorable FX impact of $400k, alongside non-cash warrant charges
Discontinued operations revenue declined 34% year-over-year as the company winds down ESWL and distribution businesses
positive_highlights: HIFU capital system sales reached an all-time high of 13 units globally with U.S. volumes growing 47% year-over-year
Gross margin expanded significantly to 55.6%, up from 51.1% in the prior period, driven by pricing and cost reductions
Management secured a $40 million equity offering to fortify balance sheet for growth initiatives
summary: FocalTherics reported Q2 FY26 HIFU revenue of $13.2 million, a 39% year-over-year increase driven by 13 capital system sales and strong procedure volume growth in the U.S. Gross margin expanded to 55.6%, while operating expenses rose due to strategic investments and non-cash warrant charges. Management reiterated full-year 2026 guidance for core HIFU revenue between $50 million-$54 million, maintaining their previously announced targets despite a change in financial reporting classification.

negative_highlights: GAAP gross margins contracted from 43.6% to 41.2%, impacted by a $1.0 million non-cash stock-based compensation charge related to the accelerated vesting of the 2025 annual bonus.
EPS decreased year-over-year despite net income growth due to an increase in weighted shares outstanding from April's rights offering.
Management expects gross margins to contract slightly further in H2 FY2026 as new programs ramp up, with a realistic range of 41.5%-43.5%.
positive_highlights: Total revenues increased 13.8% YoY to $15.1 million driven by strong aerospace and defense program shipments.
Backlog grew significantly, increasing 37.2% year-over-year to $84 million with three consecutive quarters of book-to-bill ratios well above one.
Company received heavy order volume in counter-drone areas for phased array radar systems used in military and border control applications.
summary: M-tron reported Q2 FY2026 revenues of $15.1 million (up 13.8% YoY) and net income of $1.9 million ($0.43 diluted EPS), though GAAP gross margins contracted to 41.2% from 43.6%. Management noted a one-time non-cash stock-based compensation charge in the current quarter but expects guidance for H2 FY2026 gross margins between 41.5%-44%, citing margin pressure as new programs ramp up.

negative_highlights: Accelsius removed DarkNX from its 2026 forecast due to a site becoming unavailable, likely related to power envelope constraints.
Management explicitly suspended revenue targets and guidance for Accelius until structural market constraints ease or foundational KPIs are met.
Cash balance decreased quarter-over-quarter as the company used $59.5 million in operating cash flow while raising only $13 million via equity draws.
positive_highlights: AeroFlexx commercial pipeline grew close to $35 million (up 9% QoQ) with new partnerships in Latin America and Europe.
Accelsius completed a major third-party benchmark showing NeuCool cold plates running GPUs 9-14 degrees cooler than single-phase systems, validating the technology for high-density AI workloads.
Refinity engineering design for its 10 kt demonstration plant is on track for delivery by year-end.
summary: Consolidated revenue for Q2 FY26 was $1 million (up from $0.5M last year), while the net loss widened to $34.9 million and adjusted EBITDA remained a loss of $22.6 million. Management suspended consolidated positive cash flow targets for 2028 due to delays in Accelsius reaching breakeven, citing constraints on power availability and GPU access that are sidelining smaller early adopters like DarkNX. Consequently, the company is suspending specific revenue guidance until market adoption dynamics shift.

negative_highlights: No commercial revenue reported; the company remains in a cash-burn phase with no orders or bookings disclosed for the aircraft.
Certification timeline pushed back significantly, targeting type certification only by 2029 via UK CAA and EASA pathways.
Hybrid electric flight testing is delayed until first half of 2027 after installing powertrain in a third prototype.
positive_highlights: Completed historic two-way piloted transition flights with a full-scale prototype at Farnborough Airshow, demonstrating system maturity to regulators and the public.
Secured additional U.K. government grant of up to $30.5 million for aircraft assembly and battery manufacturing sites, bringing total support to approximately $100 million.
Announced partnership with Near Earth Autonomy to integrate autonomy capabilities into VX4 using existing Honeywell Anthem avionics architecture.
summary: Vertical Aerospace reported a cash burn of $112 million for the first half of FY26 and projects approximately $150 million in net outflows over the next 12 months to fund Critical Design Review (CDR) by Q4 2026. The company raised or accessed roughly $185 million since March via equity, convertible notes, and preferred equity facilities, bringing total available cash on hand to approximately $134-$148 million depending on drawdown timing. Management confirmed the aircraft is not yet certified for commercial service (targeting 2029) but highlighted progress in flight testing, ecosystem partnerships like Near Earth Autonomy, and UK government support totaling over $100 million.

negative_highlights: Estimated standalone adjusted EBITDA margin declined sequentially from Q1 due to delayed equipment shipments in snacks and cost inflation including tariffs
Organic net sales growth of only 1% masks a significant portion of top-line growth which was driven by an $8m one-time public company cost adjustment
positive_highlights: Net sales beat high-end guidance at $245m with estimated standalone adjusted EBITDA of $41.8m including ~$8m public company costs
Backlog reached a record $446 million, up approximately 51% year-over-year providing visibility to over 80% of H2 sales assumptions
Organic net sales growth was positive at 1%, driven by strong aftermarket parts and service across the installed base
summary: Midera reported Q2 FY26 net sales of $245 million (up 13% YoY) and estimated standalone adjusted EBITDA of $41.8 million, beating the high end of prior guidance by including ~$8m in public company costs. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance midpoints for both revenue ($935-$965M) and EBITDA ($160-$176M), citing strong backlog health and organic demand despite tariff headwinds. The quarter included a record $446 million backlog, up 51% YoY.

negative_highlights: Same-practice revenue growth decelerated to 2.3% in Q2 from 3.2% year-to-date, attributed to provider scheduling, timing shifts, and a tougher 2025 comp.
Share-based compensation of ~$3 million in Q2 (~$7.1 million YTD) continues to weigh on GAAP results and is the largest driver between reported and adjusted figures.
GAAP net income was only ~$1.3 million for the quarter (~$1.0 million YTD), reflecting margin pressure from public-company and stock-comp costs.
positive_highlights: Revenue rose 5.1% year-over-year to $66.2 million, with H1 revenue up 5.6% to $128.9 million.
Full-year revenue outlook raised for the existing business after H1 results came in modestly ahead of expectations.
Announced acquisition of Village Family Dental adds approximately 48 doctors across 12 locations and establishes a presence in a new market (Eastern North Carolina).
summary: Park Dental Partners reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $66.2 million, up 5.1% year-over-year, with same-practice revenue growth of 2.3% (down from 3.2% year-to-date and last quarter). GAAP net income was approximately $1.3 million ($0.22 per diluted share), while adjusted EBITDA was $7.4 million (11.2% margin) and adjusted diluted EPS was $0.66. Management increased its full-year revenue outlook for the existing business, excluding the recently announced Village Family Dental acquisition, and said first-half results were modestly ahead of expectations. The company announced a definitive agreement to acquire Village Family Dental (48 doctors, 12 locations, ~$39.1 million base consideration plus $6.9 million contingent) and completed five acquisitions over the past year contributing ~$1.3 million of Q2 revenue.

negative_highlights: Full-year revenue guidance cut drastically from ~$130M to a range of $40-43M due to failed commercial conversions and timing delays.
Gross margin contracted significantly to approximately 8% in Q2 compared to 58% in Q1, driven by third-party hardware mix and memory cost inflation.
$7.1 million provision recorded for the balance of Starshine receivable after deciding not to engage further until payment is received.
positive_highlights: Revenue increased sequentially by over 340% driven by NeoTensor adoption and hybrid server deliveries.
Secured a committed agreement covering 2,000 servers worth approximately $70 million at current memory prices for future conversion.
Opened Europe with the first purchase order for several thousand units after successful qualification.
summary: Blaize reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $12 million (up from $2.7M prior quarter) but significantly reduced its full-year 2026 guidance to a range of $40-43 million, down from the previous expectation of ~$130 million. The revision was driven by failed commercial conversions despite successful pilots, customer order deferrals in regions like the Middle East and US, and material increases in memory pricing that eroded margins to 8% for the quarter (down from Q1's 58%). Management maintains a backlog of approximately $70-90 million secured via signed agreements but expects only partial revenue recognition this year.

negative_highlights: Admin expenses increased by 57 basis points due to continued investment in talent and expansion into new regions.
Logistics expense may face pressure in Q3 as three additional distribution centers are opened, potentially offsetting prior efficiencies.
Gross margin improvement is attributed to scale and mix rather than pricing power or inflation pass-through.
positive_highlights: Same-store sales grew 20%, significantly outperforming the market with a gap of over 20 percentage points versus ANTAD.
155 net new stores opened in Q2, bringing total store count to 3,624 and expanding distribution network to 21 regions.
Operating cash flow from activities grew 119% YoY to MXN 4.3 billion for the first half of the year.
summary: Tiendas 3B reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of MXN 26 billion (up 39% YoY) and same-store sales growth of 20%. Adjusted EBITDA reached MXN 1.6 billion, reflecting a 44% increase driven by volume expansion and operational efficiencies despite one-time cash expenses related to an equity offering.

negative_highlights: FDA expressed substantial concerns regarding the benefit-risk verification observed in the LOTIS-5 trial, requiring assessment of the regulatory path forward.
Cost of product sales increased to $2.3 million from $0.8 million year-over-year due to a shift in personnel focus from R&D clinical supply to commercial manufacturing.
Management is assessing whether additional data, risk management options, or label modifications are needed to address FDA feedback on LOTIS-5.
positive_highlights: Net loss narrowed substantially to $16.6 million from $56.6 million year-over-year driven by lower operating expenses and cost savings from the strategic reorganization.
ZYNLONTA commercial performance remained consistent with prior quarters, indicating stable demand in the third-line plus DLBCL setting.
LOTIS-7 trial completed enrollment of 100 patients at the selected dose level with a safety profile generally consistent with prior disclosures.
summary: ZYNLONTA net product revenues increased to $18.6 million in Q2 2026 from $18.1 million in the prior year quarter, while GAAP net loss narrowed significantly to $16.6 million from $56.6 million due to lower operating expenses and a one-time reorganization charge. Management noted that commercial performance remains consistent with prior quarters despite FDA concerns regarding LOTIS-5 data, which are being assessed for potential label modifications or additional data requirements. The company maintains a cash balance of $219.1 million providing a runway into 2028.

negative_highlights: Infrastructure deployment activity slowed due to a cold winter causing construction delays and slower spring ramp-up.
Adjusted EBITDA margin declined sequentially from Q1 (10.9%) to the quarter's reported level of 12.9% before year-over-year comparison, reflecting new business startup costs.
Second quarter identified as the slowest growth quarter of the year due to weather impacts and project timing.
positive_highlights: Revenue increased 38% year-over-year ahead of plan driven by acquisitions and double-digit core growth in E&M.
Adjusted EBITDA was $52.2 million, up 21% from the prior year period.
Data center revenue expected to reach north of $65 million this year with multiples growth anticipated over next few years.
summary: ITG reported Q2 FY26 revenue growth of 38% year-over-year and adjusted EBITDA up 21%, both ahead of plan despite slower core infrastructure deployment activity driven by weather timing. Management provided full-year guidance expecting mid-30s top-line growth (approx $1.5B-$1.6B) and margin expansion in the back half as startup costs abate, though they did not raise specific prior guidance figures but rather confirmed a strong outlook consistent with IPO expectations.

negative_highlights: Interest expense increased to CAD 18.9M from CAD 14.1M year-over-year
Net debt rose CAD 191M to CAD 1.1B due to IMC acquisition and growth capital
Q2 gross margin in Australia was 13.6% and Canada adjusted margin ~7%, reflecting difficult seasonal conditions
positive_highlights: Revenue guidance midpoint raised to CAD 1.7B, CAD 100M above prior midpoint and ~14% above 2025 result
Record contractual backlog of approximately CAD 3.8B as of June 30
Australia revenue up ~31% CAGR from first half 2024 to first half 2026
summary: NACG reported Q2 2026 combined revenue of CAD 456M, up from CAD 370M a year ago, with EBITDA of CAD 93M and adjusted EPS of CAD 0.32. Australia grew organically 15% excluding IMC, and the company raised its full-year 2026 revenue guidance midpoint by CAD 100M to CAD 1.7B. Management reiterated adjusted EBITDA guidance of CAD 380-420M and free cash flow of CAD 110-130M, highlighting record backlog of CAD 3.8B and a strong bid pipeline.

negative_highlights: Consumer spending remained under pressure across most markets, with Argentina seeing a 3% decline in the overall retail sector.
NOLAD margin faced 110 basis points of pressure due to reduced operating leverage compared to last year's transaction income.
In SLAD, sales were slightly below inflation while weighted average inflation was around 46%-47%.
positive_highlights: Total revenue reached $1.3 billion, a record quarterly figure up more than 14% in USD terms.
Adjusted EBITDA totaled $126.8 million, which was more than 20% higher than last year's second quarter results.
Digital sales grew by more than 25% YoY and generated about 66% of total sales.
summary: Total revenue reached $1.3 billion (up >14% YoY in USD), with adjusted EBITDA of $126.8 million representing a record quarter and more than 20% growth versus last year's second quarter. The company delivered its highest ever quarterly net income, driven by margin expansion in Brazil (+70 bps excluding FX) and strong digital sales penetration (>25% YoY). Management raised the bar for expectations citing resilience despite challenging consumer dynamics.

negative_highlights: Standalone adjusted EBITDA of $86 million was down $9 million year-over-year due to higher SG&A, freight costs, and tariff-related product costs.
Gross margin expanded only 50 bps sequentially but faced significant headwinds from a supplier transition expected to impact second-half margins by approximately $6 million.
Residential audiovisual market remains soft with no signs of meaningful recovery anticipated in the second half.
positive_highlights: Record quarterly revenue of $1.29 billion on a carve-out basis, exceeding the high end of Resideo's segment guidance range.
Average daily sales increased 2% year-over-year despite one fewer note day and soft residential demand.
Commercial security growth in mid-single digits offset weakness in residential audiovisual.
summary: ADI reported record quarterly revenue of $1.29 billion and segment adjusted EBITDA of $103 million on a carve-out basis for Q2 FY26, beating the high end of prior guidance provided by Resideo. However, standalone adjusted EBITDA was $86 million with margins pressured by higher operating expenses, freight costs, tariff impacts, and an exclusive brands revenue decline of nearly 3%. Management initiated full-year 2026 guidance expecting mid-single-digit second-half growth but noted continued gross margin headwinds from supplier transitions and difficult prior-year comparisons.

negative_highlights: GAAP EPS declined to $0.79 from $0.96 in the prior year quarter due to a higher tax provision
Operating income dropped sequentially as R&D investments increased SG&A expenses by over $2M YoY
Non-GAAP adjusted EBITDA margin contracted slightly compared to the same period last year
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 10.6% YoY to $23.4M driven by strong demand for BKR series radios from state/local agencies
Gross margin expanded significantly to 51.9%, reflecting favorable product mix and adoption of higher-margin BKR 9000
Trailing 12-month after-tax free cash flow reached $19M, up 49% YoY
summary: Second quarter revenue grew 10.6% to $23.4 million with gross margin expanding 445 bps to 51.9%, but GAAP EPS of $0.79 missed the prior year's $0.96 due primarily to a $560,000 increase in income tax provision and higher SG&A expenses driven by R&D investments. Management reiterated full-year guidance for revenue of at least $90 million and non-GAAP adjusted EPS of $3.55 despite the sequential decline in profitability metrics.

negative_highlights: Production and operating expense rose 24% to $8.90 per BOE, including $0.59 per BOE from a non-operated workover and higher water hauling costs
Management declined to quantify the higher cost of the Clifton Mack wells, which required extra casing strings due to higher pressures
Management would not endorse the high end of guidance, saying results depend on four high-IP wells coming online at once and that Q3 will be the lowest production quarter
positive_highlights: Revenue rose 109% YoY to a record $22.5 million, with production up 46% to 4,690 BOE/d and average prices up 41%
Adjusted EBITDA increased 114% to $16.4 million and basic EPS rose to $0.24 from $0.08
Netback from operations expanded 48% to $43.92 per BOE, and the credit facility borrowing base was raised 15% from $65 million to $75 million
summary: Kolibri reported record Q2 FY2026 results: revenue of $22.5 million (up 109% YoY on a 46% production increase to 4,690 BOE/d and 41% higher realized prices), net income of $8.5 million, and basic EPS of $0.24 versus $0.08 a year ago; Adjusted EBITDA rose 114% to $16.4 million. Netback from operations increased 48% to $43.92/BOE, though production and operating expense per BOE rose 24% to $8.90 on non-operated workover costs and higher water hauling. Guidance was updated in late June and left unchanged; management said the four 2026 wells will primarily drive growth in Q4, with Q3 expected to be the low production quarter. The borrowing base was redetermined upward 15% to $75 million.

negative_highlights: GAAP net loss widened significantly from $16.3 million to $28.4 million year-over-year
R&D expenses increased by over 60% due to a one-time royalty payment for phase III completion and milestone achievement
positive_highlights: FDA accepted New Drug Application (NDA) for tinlarebant with priority review and a PDUFA date of February 12, 2027
Phase III DRAGON study data showed subjects treated exhibited decreased QAF values by approximately 2% at month 25 compared to baseline versus ~20% increase in placebo group
summary: Belite Bio reported a GAAP net loss of $28.4 million in Q2 FY26 compared to $16.3 million last year, driven by R&D expenses rising from $11M to $18.2M due to phase III milestone royalties and SG&A increasing from $6.5M to $16.7M due to team expansion. The company ended the quarter with $780 million in cash equivalents but provided no revenue guidance as it remains pre-commercial, focusing entirely on FDA approval for tinlarebant by February 2027.

negative_highlights: Management noted significant supply chain pressure and cost increases (up to 60%) on critical components like turbines and cold boxes.
positive_highlights: Signed firm order for fourth FLNG unit (Mark II) delivering in 2029, becoming the earliest available capacity globally.
Secured options for incremental units at CIMC Raffles and Seatrium shipyards to support a potential fleet of seven vessels.
Hilli delivered final cargo with 100% economic uptime over its eight-year contract; Gimi produced 15% above contractual volume.
summary: Golar LNG reported Q2 FY2026 operating revenue of $130 million and EBITDA of $127 million (up ~20% q/q), driven by Hilli's commodity-linked earnings which rose to $37M from $10M in the prior quarter. The company announced a firm order for its fourth FLNG unit, securing an option for a fifth at CIMC and signing an LOI with Seatrium for further growth units. Management highlighted strong operational performance including 15% overproduction on Gimi and 100% economic uptime on Hilli.

negative_highlights: F-16 revenue was lower ($5.7M) due to prior year pull-forward of $12.6M
R&D expenses increased by approximately $1 million as investments in NextGen capabilities accelerate
positive_highlights: Organic growth excluding F-16 timing effects was over 40% YoY
Gross margin expanded to 51.7%, marking four consecutive quarters above 50%
Secured first major OEM contract for Liberty Flight Deck with a leading eVTOL developer
summary: Innovative Aerosystems reported Q3 FY26 revenue of $26.7 million (up ~11% YoY) and net income of $4.5 million ($0.25 diluted EPS), driven by strong organic growth in commercial/business aviation excluding a difficult F-16 comparison. Gross margin expanded to 51.7%, the fourth consecutive quarter above 50%. Management raised guidance for Q4 revenue to $28-$30M and highlighted strategic wins including an eVTOL contract win, Aydin acquisition integration, and inclusion in the Russell 2000 Index.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened slightly year-over-year due to increased R&D and G&A expenses associated with clinical trial expansion
No revenue or earnings guidance provided as the company remains in a pre-revenue, cash-burn phase
Subcutaneous formulation development is ongoing but no specific timeline for commercial availability was given
positive_highlights: Zero cases of ARIA-E observed across all genotypes, including high-risk ApoE4 homozygotes
Blinded interim data showed ~15% decline in plasma p-tau217 and ~13.3% decline in CSF MTBR-tau243 biomarkers
Company raised cash via private placement to CAD 53.4 million, extending runway through Q1 FY27 readout
summary: ProMIS Neurosciences reported a net loss of CAD 11.7 million (CAD $1.28 per share) for Q2 FY26, compared to a prior year loss of CAD 10.1 million, driven by increased R&D and G&A expenses as the company advanced its clinical programs. The quarter was defined by positive blinded interim data from the Phase I-B PRECISE-AD trial showing zero ARIA-E cases across all genotypes (including ApoE4 homozygotes) and early biomarker declines consistent with target engagement, though no financial guidance or revenue beat exists as this is a clinical-stage company. Management indicated cash on hand of CAD 53.4 million provides runway through late 2027 to fund operations until the anticipated Q1 FY27 top-line readout.

negative_highlights: System revenue declined sequentially, dropping $4.2 million year-over-year as the company shifts toward larger manufacturing deals.
GAAP gross margin contracted slightly to 42.3% due to a strong Israeli shekel impacting expenses and lower system mix.
Full-year operating cash flow guidance was lowered from positive expectations given Q2 usage of $18.7 million driven by legal costs.
positive_highlights: Consumables revenue reached a quarterly record of $66.3 million, up sequentially driven by manufacturing material sales.
Stratasys Direct grew 12.1% year-over-year fueled by defense demand for drone production and munitions.
Aerospace & Defense business grew 17% relative to the prior quarter with large multi-year orders from major customers.
summary: Stratasys reported Q2 FY2026 consolidated revenue of $137.6 million, which was flat year-over-year despite a sequential increase driven by record consumable sales ($66.3M). Management reaffirmed full-year guidance but lowered the operating cash flow outlook for the year due to non-routine legal expenses in Q2 and expects positive cash flow only from H2 2026.

negative_highlights: Digital revenues declined 1.3% YoY due to lower subscription revenue and product sales despite digital ad growth.
Advertising revenues decreased 3.5% YoY primarily due to a challenging comparison from election-related demand in the prior year.
positive_highlights: Record quarterly revenue of $54.1 million representing a 16.5% year-over-year increase.
First profitable quarter as a public company with net income of $2.9 million and adjusted EBITDA of $5.7 million.
Gross margin expanded to 43.1%, up from 38% in the prior year, driven by affiliate fee growth.
summary: Newsmax reported record Q2 FY26 revenue of $54.1 million (up 16.5% YoY) and achieved its first quarterly net income as a public company at $2.9 million ($0.02/share). Gross margin expanded significantly to 43.1%, driven by high-margin affiliate fees which grew 81.9% and international licensing revenue surging from $0.7M to $4.6M in the quarter. Management reiterated full-year FY26 guidance of $212-$216 million, citing structural growth led by these expanding streams.

negative_highlights: Full-year revenue guidance was cut by $180 million to a range of $375M-$405M.
Backlog decreased 8% quarter-over-quarter from Q1 levels despite new wins, indicating recognition timing issues.
Supply chain constraints and the shift in government acquisition strategy (slow-start IDIQs) are delaying revenue realization into FY27.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 10% year-over-year driven by acquisitions (ALL.SPACE, Solestial) and a new commercial constellation win.
Gross margin expanded significantly to 24%, up 13 percentage points from the prior year quarter due to mix shift away from EAC adjustments.
Company achieved an 88% win rate on eight contracts secured in H1 FY26, including task orders converting quickly into funded delivery.
summary: York Space Systems reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $92.5 million (up 10% YoY) and a gross margin expansion to 24%, but adjusted EBITDA remained at an $8.9M-$9.5M loss due to increased SG&A from acquisitions. Management revised full-year 2026 revenue guidance down significantly, lowering the midpoint by $180 million to $375M-$405M as IDIQ contract awards shifted recognition into 2027 and supply chain delays pushed out delivery.

negative_highlights: PSUS shares are trading at approximately an 80% discount to NAV, which management admits is 'absurd' and plans to address with significant marketing
Hyperscalers (Amazon, Microsoft) have increased CapEx significantly over the last two years without immediate near-term revenue uplift from AI investments
No specific financial results or guidance were provided for Q2 FY26 in this transcript
positive_highlights: PSUS portfolio is 95% invested with capital deployed at attractive valuations during market volatility
SPARC vehicle offers a unique structure for taking private companies public without founder stock or warrants
summary: Pershing Square Inc reported its first quarter earnings for FY26 but provided no specific revenue or EPS figures in the transcript, focusing instead on strategic updates regarding its IPO vehicle PSUS and future fund launches. Management acknowledged that PSUS is trading at a significant discount to NAV (approximate $50 vs high 30s) due to low volume and retail over-subscription issues they intend to fix with increased marketing efforts. The company confirmed plans for Pershing Square Ventures in late Q4 FY26 and discussed the SPARC vehicle as an efficient way to take private companies public, though no specific deal has been closed yet.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA loss of $42.7 million driven by one-time event build costs ($52M) that are not expected to recur.
Revenue was only $17.7 million in Q2, with Live Enhanced contributing just a few weeks of activity after launching in May.
Management explicitly stated the current cost structure does not represent a run rate and requires significant capital investment.
positive_highlights: Secured approximately $32 million in sponsorship deal value, with significant revenue recognized from Rezolve and Rumble partners.
Inaugural Enhanced Games engaged over 1 billion people globally and generated more than 4 million live views on Twitch alone.
Live Enhanced platform is fully operational across the U.S. and 33 international markets.
summary: Enhanced Group reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $17.7 million driven by inaugural Enhanced Games sponsorships and early Live Enhanced activity against a backdrop of no prior-year comparable. The company posted an adjusted EBITDA loss of $42.7 million, with total net loss at $61.9 million due to one-time event build costs ($52M) and transaction expenses ($10.9M). Management raised the near-term outlook for consumer growth but maintained that current results reflect a heavy investment phase rather than sustainable run rates.

negative_highlights: FDA Advisory Committee voted against approval (3-9) on the requested cardiomyopathy indication, citing that efficacy was measured as a secondary endpoint rather than primary.
Statistical model reversion in The Lancet publication changed the P value for left ventricular ejection fraction from 0.04 to 0.09 and reduced treatment difference from 2.4% to 1.8%.
Commercial readiness activities are being conducted at a slower pace pending regulatory clarity, delaying potential revenue recognition.
positive_highlights: HOPE-3 primary endpoint (upper limb function) remained statistically significant with a P value of 0.029 and an absolute change of 1.2 points, unaffected by the statistical model reversion.
The full Phase III dataset was published in The Lancet following independent peer review, highlighting efficacy data for deramiocel.
In-house GMP manufacturing facility is operational with expansion continuing toward validation estimated for 2027.
summary: Capricor reported zero revenue and a net loss of $40.7 million ($0.70 per share) for Q2 FY26, driven by increased operating expenses of $42.9 million as the company continues to invest in its deramiocel program despite regulatory setbacks. The FDA Cellular, Tissue, and Gene Therapies Advisory Committee voted against approval for the cardiomyopathy indication (3-9), though management plans to resubmit an amended BLA focusing on upper limb skeletal muscle efficacy supported by HOPE-3 data published in The Lancet. Commercial readiness activities are being paced until regulatory clarity is achieved.

negative_highlights: Leverage ratios declined to 1.29x from 1.43x, reducing immediate earnings leverage despite excess liquidity.
Credit hedge portfolio reduced by approximately $56 million (from $188m to $132m) due to market recovery and deployment timing, creating a drag on P&L in April.
CLO equity new issue market remains unattractive, resulting in no purchases of new issue equity during the quarter.
positive_highlights: Adjusted NII run rate in July is approximately 20% higher than the second quarter figure, indicating immediate earnings capacity realization.
Portfolio repositioning improved credit quality and reduced risk while increasing income potential without reaching for yield.
Weighted average purchase yield in Q3 reached approximately 16.8%, driven by improving loan market fundamentals and attractive entry points.
summary: For the quarter ended June 30, 2026, EARN reported GAAP net income of $0.33 per share and adjusted net investment income (NII) of $0.15 per share, while NAV increased to $4.18 per share. Management noted that Q2 results did not fully reflect the earnings capacity of the expanded and repositioned portfolio, with July adjusted NII already showing a run rate approximately 20% higher than the second quarter figure. The company reduced leverage from 1.43x to 1.29x while growing the CLO portfolio by 8.5% through active rotation and reinvestment of distributions.

negative_highlights: Net loss increased year-over-year from $3.7 million to $3.9 million driven by financing-related costs
Cash and cash equivalents declined significantly to $0.5 million from $3.5 million at end of Q1 FY2026
Company explicitly stated it will not provide forward-looking guidance or estimates
positive_highlights: Established a new $10 million equity line of credit (ELOC) with B. Riley Principal Capital II
Secured additional financing tool: $5 million at-the-market (ATM) equity program with B. Riley Securities
Successfully utilized ELOC to generate approximately $1.35 million in capital proceeds during the quarter
summary: Stardust Power reported a net loss of $3.9 million for Q2 FY2026 compared to $3.7 million in the prior year period and remains pre-revenue as it advances development activities at its Muskogee refinery site. The company clarified that no forward-looking guidance or estimates would be provided during this call, focusing instead on past performance and current financial position including cash of approximately $0.5 million. Management highlighted recent capital raises via an ELOC and ATM facility to support working capital needs while maintaining disciplined liquidity management.

negative_highlights: Non-interest expenses increased to $8.38 million reflecting continued investment in personnel, technology, and infrastructure for growth.
Diluted EPS calculation included preferred stock conversions mid-quarter; normalized common equity share count will fully apply starting Q3 FY2026.
positive_highlights: Record quarterly net income of $6.7 million achieved with a clean quarter containing no non-recurring items.
Net interest margin expanded to 4.57% as loan growth outpaced funding costs, yielding approximately $14.7 million in NII.
Credit quality remained strong with zero net charge-offs and a reversal of credit loss expense during the quarter.
summary: OptimumBank reported record quarterly net income of $6.7 million and diluted EPS of $0.28 for Q2 FY2026, representing a significant increase over the prior quarter and year-ago period driven by loan growth and NIM expansion to 4.57%. Management raised its forward-looking annual earnings estimate range from approximately $1 per share to between $1 and $1.15 per share based on the current quarterly run rate of $0.28, which they believe is easily replicable going forward.

negative_highlights: Cash, cash equivalents declined substantially from $11.9 million at year-end to $3.6 million at quarter-end.
Gross profit contracted by approximately $10,000 (from $131k to $121k) despite revenue growth due to cost variability.
The company explicitly states it anticipates continued operating losses in the near term.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew year-over-year by approximately $3,000 (from $163k to $166k).
Net loss narrowed significantly to $6.3M from a prior period net loss of $7.7M.
Successfully completed analytical and clinical performance studies for the upper respiratory multiplex assay.
summary: For the second quarter of FY2026 ending June 30, Co-Diagnostics reported total revenue of $166,000 compared to $163,000 in the prior year period. The company achieved a significant regulatory milestone by submitting its Dual 510(k) and CLIA Waiver for an upper respiratory assay but continues to operate at low revenue levels with net losses narrowing from $7.7 million to $6.3 million due to reduced operating expenses.

negative_highlights: Adjusted gross margin guidance was lowered from a prior range of 16.4%-17% to an updated range of 16%-16.6%, primarily due to a prospective accounting change reclassifying incentive-based cash compensation expense.
O&M attachment rates contracted quarter-over-quarter, though management noted this is subject to project mix and timing.
positive_highlights: Revenue surged 77% year-over-year to $951 million driven by new construction and M&A activity.
Adjusted EBITDA margin reached nearly 13% for H1, reflecting strong profitability despite a prospective accounting change reducing reported adjusted gross margin guidance range slightly.
Backlog grew significantly to approximately $8.9 billion (44% YoY growth) with the majority of projects classified as safe harbors.
summary: SOLV Energy reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $951 million (up 77% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $117 million, contributing to record first-half results with total H1 revenue near $1.63 billion. negative_highlights: Net loss widened slightly from $2.8 million to $4.1 million, primarily due to a non-cash interest expense of $0.9 million related to convertible notes.
Cash balance decreased year-over-year despite the recent capital raise, ending at $1.7 million compared to $3.8 million as of December 31, 2025.
positive_highlights: Revenue doubled year-over-year with gross margin expanding significantly from 43% to 64% driven by volume absorption of fixed costs.
FDA received clearance for the Catamaran SI Joint Fusion System, enabling instrument upgrades and a shift to reusable status expected to improve margins in Q3.
Physician training events increased 98% year-over-year following the opening of the new Tampa sales and training office.
summary: Tenon Medical reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $1.3 million (up 127% YoY) and gross profit of $0.8 million with a margin expansion to 64%. The company achieved record quarterly figures driven by increased case volumes on both Catamaran and SImmetry+ platforms, while operating expenses rose due to sales/marketing spend and R&D investments in upcoming product launches.

negative_highlights: Legacy U.S. business revenue declined by $3.2 million due to government shutdowns and continuing resolutions causing contract delays.
Adjusted EBITDA decreased from $7.8M in Q1 FY25 (implied prior) or previous periods as the company incurred higher operating expenses related to its transition to a public company.
Net loss widened significantly to $15.3 million compared to net income of $1.6 million in the prior year period.
positive_highlights: Revenue increased 87% year-over-year to $49.8 million driven by the acquisition of ISA and strong international demand (134% organic growth).
International revenue reached record levels at $21 million, with backlog growing from $285M in Q1 to $292M in Q2.
Successfully completed IPO raising approximately $437.5 million of net proceeds and secured launch slots through 2028.
summary: HawkEye 360 reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $49.8 million (up 87% YoY) and Adjusted EBITDA of $7.0 million, driven by the acquisition of ISA but offset by a decline in legacy U.S. business due to government shutdowns. The company completed its IPO with net proceeds of approximately $437.5 million and ended the quarter with $292 million in backlog. Full-year 2026 guidance for revenue ($215M-$220M) and Adjusted EBITDA ($30M-$36M) was provided, though no specific prior period guidance figures were explicitly compared to determine a raise or cut.

negative_highlights: Same-store inside merchandise traffic was modestly lower than the prior year period due to higher fuel prices.
The company is note a portfolio of 29 stores in Iowa and Kansas by year-end, which will impact reported store count metrics.
Fuel margin outlook for H2 assumes moderation to the low $0.40 per gallon range.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA reached $71 million, marking the strongest performance in the company's history.
Same-store fuel gallons increased 1.8% excluding sold stores, while diesel mix grew to approximately 38% of total volume.
Inside merchandise sales rose 4.4% year-over-year with margin expansion of roughly 50 basis points.
summary: Yesway reported a record second quarter with adjusted EBITDA of $71 million (up 35% YoY) and store contribution rising to $88 million. Management raised the full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance range from $210-$220 million to $235-$245 million, driven by strong fuel volume growth of 1.4% same-store (excluding sold stores) and inside merchandise sales up 4.4%. The company ended the quarter with a store count of 450 after opening one new location.

summary: Nauticus Robotics reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $0.9 million, up $0.7 million sequentially but down $1.2 million year over year. The company gave no quantitative guidance but emphasized cost cuts, balance sheet actions (debt reduced $5.5 million via debt-to-equity exchanges), a first formal Nauticus ToolKITT software release, and a pivot toward defense and international opportunities.

Cash burn remains high at $11.3 million per quarter with no immediate path to profitability until reimbursement landscape stabilizes.

Test volume remained within target range of 2,500 to 3,000 tests despite revenue recognition lag due to reimbursement uncertainty.
Concert's client plans cover nearly 10 million lives with three already adopting the policy and several more expected.
summary: Lucid Diagnostics reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $1.5 million (up ~17% sequentially) on a test volume of 2,770 units that remained within the targeted range but did not beat prior quarter levels due to pending Medicare reimbursement status. Management highlighted significant progress in commercial coverage with Concert and VA contracting milestones while noting cash burn remains elevated at $11.3 million per quarter as they build infrastructure ahead of expected Medicare approval.

negative_highlights: Management stated they are being patient on pension pricing in the U.K. because current bid values drive returns below their comfort level.
The Just Group business is still undergoing integration, with a focus on reducing costs and exiting early-stage initiatives to improve its cost structure.

Completed the acquisition of Oaktree to create one of the most comprehensive credit businesses globally.

The company reported record fundraising of $77 billion and completed strategic initiatives including the acquisitions of Oaktree and Just Group, alongside a simplification transaction approved by shareholders. Management highlighted strong leasing momentum with net rents 25% above expiring levels in the U.S., though they noted patience on pension pricing due to current market rates.

negative_highlights: ARR missed bottom-end guidance due to four large transactions slipping beyond anticipated timelines related to foreign entity status procurement requirements
Insysets conversion ARR uplift was lower than expected, particularly in U.S. state and local government where growth dropped below the mid-20% range seen last year

positive_highlights: Defense and intelligence ARR grew 25% driven by strong platform adoption

Gross revenue retention rate continued to climb in the first half as customers convert to Inseyets
summary: Cellebrite reported Q2 FY26 ARR of $508 million (up 21%) and revenue of $131 million (up 16%), but missed the bottom end of guidance due to delayed large transactions involving cloud/AI procurement requirements. Management lowered full-year ARR guidance by approximately $15 million at the midpoint, citing moderation in Insights conversions and elongated sales cycles for federal deals requiring new permits like FEPs. Conversely, adjusted EBITDA targets were raised to reflect continued cost discipline despite lower revenue expectations.

negative_highlights: Same center occupancy declined significantly by 240 basis points to 68.6%, primarily due to lower enrollment and consolidation impacts

Marketing initiatives successfully drove a week-over-week increase in inquiries across the portfolio
summary: KinderCare reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $698 million, down slightly from the prior year's $700 million and missing expectations due to a 4% decline in total enrollment driven by footprint optimization. Adjusted EPS was $0.08 compared to $0.22 last year, while adjusted EBITDA fell to $63 million as management updated full-year guidance downward to reflect the impact of closing approximately 80-85 centers and a reduced tuition contribution assumption from state subsidies.

negative_highlights: Ipiranga expects margins in Q3 to decline from current levels as they normalize toward first-quarter figures due to Middle East conflict impacts.

Hidrovias adjusted EBITDA fell 8% compared to Q2 FY2025 primarily due to the sale of its coastal navigation operation.

Leverage ratio improved significantly to 0.9x, the lowest level since 2008.
summary: Ultrapar reported record net income of BRL 1,677 million (up 46% YoY) and recurring adjusted EBITDA of BRL 3,657 million for Q2 FY2026. The company achieved a significant working capital release at Ipiranga driven by diesel imports amid Middle East volatility, resulting in record operating cash flow generation of BRL 4.8 billion. Management anticipates margins will normalize to first-quarter levels due to the offsetting effects of fighting illegal practices and ongoing supply disruptions.

negative_highlights: Full-year revenue/EBITDA growth is capped at a modest implied rate of 6.5% due to pro-forma adjustments.

Management raised its full-year sales target to 1 GW from the prior guidance, alongside raising CapEx paid guidance from RMB 9 billion to RMB 10 billion. Pro forma adjusted EBITDA growth is now implied at 6.5% for FY26 following pro-forma adjustments that deduct one-time items and restructured recurring income.

negative_highlights: Platform revenue decreased approximately 10% year-over-year to $3.7 million.

Management maintained full-year ROAE guidance at 9.25% despite a first-half performance near 10%, citing caution regarding second-half NIM pressures from further rate hikes, earthquake impacts on asset quality, and potential local tax increases in Bogotá.

negative_highlights: FY2026 revenue guidance lowered to $9.2M-$10.5M from prior guidance of at least $10.5 million due to manufacturing constraints

positive_highlights: Product gross margin expanded to 59.9% from 53.9% YoY on a favorable product mix

summary: Q3 FY2026 product revenue rose 16% YoY to $2.0 million, with gross margin expanding to 59.9% from 53.9% on favorable mix, and new orders of $2.7 million (+43% YoY). Net loss widened to $2.0 million ($0.23 basic) from $1.5 million, and cash fell to $2.0 million from $6.6 million at Sept 30, 2025, with $1.0 million raised post-quarter via ATM and no debt. Operationally, the company received ISO 13485 certification for international market entry and advanced its StereoCED drug delivery platform toward human studies by end of September.
