positive_highlights: Gross margin improved to 41% sequentially, up from 36% in Q1
Adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed approximately $0.4M YoY to ~$1.7 million despite flat revenue
Weighted pipeline per seller increased significantly to ~$2.8 million driven by new leadership and acquired assets
summary: Super League reported Q2 FY26 gross revenue of approximately $3 million (flat YoY and sequentially) with net revenue increasing to ~$1.24M (+16% seq). Gross margin expanded to 41%, while Adjusted EBITDA remained a loss of ~$1.7M, improving from the prior year quarter but missing profitability targets for H1. Management reaffirmed guidance for adjusted EBITDA breakeven in Q4 and highlighted pipeline growth driven by new sales leadership and Misfits integration.

negative_highlights: Management explicitly declined to provide full-year guidance for 2026, citing parabolic volatility in fuel prices that makes forward-looking statements unreliable.
CASK increased significantly year-over-year due to a 61.8% rise in fuel costs and temporary deleveraging of fixed costs over reduced capacity.
Recurring free cash flow was nearly breakeven (negative BRL 80 million) hindered by non-recurring restructuring payments totaling approximately BRL 794 million.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to a record 10.2%, recapturing approximately BRL 448 million of the fuel headwind through disciplined capacity management and pricing actions.
Operating revenue reached a quarterly record, supported by RASK growth of 12.7% YoY despite significant volume reductions.
NPS increased 26 points since December 2025 as operational reliability improved to make Azul the most on-time airline in Latin America.
summary: Azul reported Q2 FY2026 operating revenue of BRL 5 billion (up 0.7% YoY) and Adjusted EBITDA of BRL 510 million in a seasonally weak quarter impacted by fuel prices up 61%. Management declined to provide full-year guidance due to extreme volatility in the fuel curve, noting that capacity was reduced proactively by 10.6% to protect liquidity while maintaining record RASK.

negative_highlights: GAAP net loss was $12.8M for the quarter and Adjusted EBITDA was -$3.2M due to merger-related stock-based compensation charges ($9.4M) and legacy business wind-down costs.
Material weaknesses in internal controls remain unremediated with a multi-step remediation plan underway involving an external accounting firm.
positive_highlights: Contracted annualized recurring revenue on live compute reached $22 million as of August 4th, inclusive of new Blackwell cluster deliveries announced last week.
summary: Corvex reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $3.8 million entirely from its newly integrated AI platform business following a March merger with Corvex Legacy Holdings; the legacy healthcare segment was fully wound down and transferred to lenders, resulting in no meaningful year-over-year comparisons. Management highlighted that contracted annualized recurring revenue on live compute reached approximately $22 million as of August 4th, driven by new cluster deliveries including Blackwell expansion funded via debt financing and customer prepayments. The quarter included significant non-cash stock-based compensation charges ($9.4M) related to merger equity awards and disclosed unremediated material weaknesses in internal controls.

negative_highlights: Revenue was constrained by a temporary suspension of mining and processing operations due to TAC negotiations in Brazil.
Not all produced material (low-grade fines) could be sold within Q2, resulting in lower revenue than production volume might suggest for the period.
Operational timeline pushed forward by three months regarding full capacity ramp-up.
positive_highlights: Production volume increased significantly by 52% quarter-over-quarter to deliver 35,400 tons of lithium oxide concentrate.
Company maintained high gross margins at 60% and achieved record EBITDA margin of 47%. All-in sustaining costs decreased over 30% year-over-year to $668/ton.
Deleveraged balance sheet significantly, repaying 43% of total debt over the last two years.
summary: Sigma Lithium reported Q2 FY2026 net revenues of $55 million and generated approximately $30-32 million in cash flow from operations for the quarter. While production volumes increased by 52% to 35,400 tons due to a ramp-up that surpassed guidance, revenue was impacted by lower sales volume compared to total production as low-grade material produced but not sold during the quarter is being monetized later. Management adjusted its full-year cost guidance downward based on executed costs of $668/ton and pushed forward certain operational timelines by three months due to a temporary suspension related to TAC negotiations.

negative_highlights: Net loss of $32.7 million in Q2 FY2026, with $43.8 million of pre-tax one-time and asset resolution charges driving the $44 million pre-tax loss.
Company restated FY2024, FY2025, and Q1 2026 financial statements for material misstatements in deferred origination costs, accrued interest, and gain-on-sale accounting.
Tangible book value per share dropped to $4.82 from $14.22 at March 31, 2026, and loans fell 4% QoQ to $882.8 million with deposits down 9% to $989 million.
positive_highlights: Normalized net interest margin was 4.07% versus reported 3.48%, with cost of funds down 24 bps QoQ to 2.66% and down 49 bps year-to-date.
Tier 1 leverage ratio improved to 8.3% from 5.89% at March 31, 2026, and total capital ratio rose to 12.77% from 9.0%, reflecting the $80 million capital raise.
Total non-performing loans excluding government guaranteed balances declined to $14.4 million from $15.9 million QoQ, with the ratio down 10 bps to 1.72%.
summary: BayFirst reported a Q2 FY2026 net loss of $32.7 million, with the quarter dominated by a $41.5 million asset resolution plan charge tied to legacy unguaranteed SBA 7 loans, plus $2.2 million of one-time items, together equaling $43.8 million of the $44 million pre-tax loss. The company also restated FY2024, FY2025, and Q1 2026 financials for material misstatements in deferred origination costs and accrued interest. Core/pre-tax operating loss was roughly $200,000, normalized NIM was 4.07% versus reported 3.48%, and tangible book value fell to $4.82 per share from $14.22. Loans fell 4% QoQ to $882.8 million and deposits dropped 9% to $989 million, while the Tier 1 leverage ratio improved to 8.3% after an $80 million capital raise.

negative_highlights: Segment NOI decreased by $510,000 due to a $1.5 million hit from fair value adjustments on unconsolidated office entities.
GAAP FFO remained negative at -$3.5 million, compared to -$7.9 million in the prior year.
The company incurred a $455,000 casualty loss due to water damage at the hotel property.
positive_highlights: Core FFO improved by $3.6 million compared to the prior year period, narrowing from a loss of $7.0 million to $3.4 million.
Multifamily NOI surged 238% year-over-year driven by occupancy reaching 95.3% in the Bay Area and rent growth of 11%.
Hotel segment NOI increased 11% year-over-year following the completion of renovations.
summary: CMCT reported Q2 FY2026 segment NOI of $9.3 million, a decrease from $9.8 million in the prior year period, primarily driven by a $1.5 million decline in office NOI due to non-cash fair value adjustments on unconsolidated entities. While Core FFO improved by $3.6 million compared to the prior year, this was largely attributable to a reduction in preferred dividends rather than operational growth. Management highlighted strong recovery trends in multifamily and hotel segments but noted they elected not to refinance an Oakland office mortgage due to capital constraints.

negative_highlights: No revenue, EPS, or margin figures disclosed for Q2, and no formal guidance issued
A previously announced ~$3 million government contract declared effectively dead due to contract-term impasses
Quarter ended with only $5.2 million of cash and management acknowledged a Nasdaq $1 minimum-price compliance issue
positive_highlights: Operating expense down 41% sequentially and net loss improved 28% sequentially
Jerusalem contract signed and onboarding started for 10,000 city workers, with a 270,000-resident city deal signed and ~50-70% adoption reported when residents are informed
Debt reduced $4.3 million ($3.3 million equity conversion at a 4x premium to market, ~$1 million pushed from 2026) plus a $3 million non-dilutive revolver available at just under 4%
summary: Q2 FY2026 was reported with a 41% sequential reduction in operating expense, a 28% sequential improvement in net loss, and $5.2 million of cash, alongside a $4.3 million debt reduction ($3.3 million converted to equity at a 4x premium and roughly $1 million pushed from 2026) plus a $3 million non-dilutive revolver. No revenue, EPS, or margin figures were disclosed, and no formal forward guidance was given; management said most growth investment yield would land in H2 2026 and more in 2027. The Jerusalem contract (10,000 city workers) was signed and onboarding started, while a previously announced ~$3 million government deal was declared effectively dead over contract terms, with management stating that deal would have had no 2026 cash flow impact. Cash is only $5.2 million and management acknowledged a Nasdaq $1 compliance issue, saying it expects the stock price to resolve it.

negative_highlights: Average note price for Zgounder was $68.29/oz, which is below the quarter's average due to a precipitous drop in June prices.
positive_highlights: Production of 1.7 million ounces (silver equivalent), representing a 61% year-over-year increase driven by record mining rates at Zgounder.
Cash flow generation reached $48 million, up 522% from the prior year quarter, with total H1 operating cash flow hitting $119 million.
Discovery of a new high-grade zone parallel to the main structure at Boumadine (intercept of 51m @ 890 g/t silver equivalent) and completion of Phase 2 tailings facility.
summary: Aya reported Q2 FY2026 production of 1.7 million ounces (silver equivalent), a 61% year-over-year increase and 12% quarter-over-quarter rise, driven by record performance at the Zgounder mine where mining rates reached 4,900 tonnes per day against a plant nameplate capacity of 2,700 tonnes. Revenue surged to $97 million (up 151% YoY) and net income hit $35 million due to strong cash costs ($17.69/oz at Zgounder) despite silver prices averaging below the quarter's low-water mark. Management confirmed full alignment with H1 guidance for production, cash cost, and CapEx while highlighting a successful Nasdaq listing as a major catalyst.

negative_highlights: Significant net loss of $30.3 million driven by high G&A expenses ($11.1M) including $6.8M severance.
Realized loss on digital assets of $25.4 million due to strategic sales.
No specific revenue guidance provided for Q3 regarding validator monetization.
positive_highlights: Revenue beat prior year period significantly ($2.5M vs $43k) due to new staking strategy.
Net staking yield outperformed network average by 46 bps at 6.14% APY.
Executed accretive capital allocation with $2.3M buybacks and $8M institutional raise.
summary: Solana Company reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $2.5 million (up from $43k in Q2 2025) driven by $2.5 million in staking revenue, but posted a net loss of $30.3 million ($0.38/share) due to $11.1 million in G&A expenses including $6.8 million of non-recurring severance costs from the Ponce divestiture. The company executed share repurchases of $2.3 million and completed an $8 million institutional raise, while holding a treasury of 2.3 million SOL valued at $170.6 million. Management highlighted operational milestones including the launch of a Tokyo validator cluster and acquisition of a Hong Kong trust company, but provided no specific revenue guidance for the next quarter.

negative_highlights: Hardware revenue decreased 19% YoY due to a specific large order delay that prevented meeting proposed expectations for the quarter.
Service revenue declined 28% YoY as non-recurring customization revenues and recurring service renewals lagged timing assumptions.
positive_highlights: Gross margin expanded sharply to 87% from 73%, driven by high-margin license revenue mix and inventory liquidation.
Net loss improved 51% YoY to $0.56 per share, with cash position strengthened to over $4.5 million following warrant exercises.
Significant pipeline growth identified in EMEA (Saudi Arabia, Jordan, Portugal) and new opportunities in AI agent governance.
summary: Q2 FY26 revenue grew 13% YoY to $1.92 million driven by a 53% increase in license fees, but the quarter missed proposed expectations due to a delayed hardware shipment shifting into H2. Gross margin expanded significantly to 87%, while net loss improved 51% to $0.56 per share on an adjusted basis of shares post-reverse split. Management targets profitability for the second half of 2026, citing strong pipeline growth in EMEA and new AI governance opportunities.

negative_highlights: Revenue was flat at $9.0M versus $9.1M and gross profit fell to $1.8M (~20% margin) from $2.9M as cost of revenue rose to $7.2M
Joint development and contract research revenue declined to $1.3M from $2.3M on project completions, and CarbonSmart product revenue was flat at $3.8M
ISCC EU certification, the stated near-term revenue catalyst, has taken longer than expected and certified sales are only anticipated beginning in Q4
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed to $7.6M from $29.7M a year ago on a 67% cut in operating expenses to $11.7M
R&D expense fell to $2.0M from $14.9M and SG&A fell 54% to $8.8M, establishing a structurally lower cost base
Cash and equivalents plus restricted cash rose to $48.9M from $17.1M at December 31, 2025, primarily on common stock proceeds
summary: Q2 revenue was $9.0M versus $9.1M a year ago, essentially flat, with gross profit of $1.8M (~20% margin) down from $2.9M, partly offset by cost of revenue rising to $7.2M. Operating expenses fell 67% to $11.7M and the adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed to $7.6M from $29.7M, reflecting the 2025 restructuring (R&D $2.0M vs $14.9M; SG&A $8.8M vs $19.1M). The company reintroduced full-year 2026 guidance: revenue $50-55M, adjusted EBITDA loss $22-26M, and opex $51-55M, with cash of $48.9M at June 30. The key forward catalyst is the world's first ISCC EU recycled-carbon-fuel certification at the China plant, with management expecting certified ethanol sales and improved pricing beginning in Q4.

negative_highlights: Full-year cash spend guidance increased slightly to $27-$28 million reflecting accelerated commercialization activities.
Net loss of $8.5 million includes significant non-cash charges related to earn-out shares and vesting liabilities.
Modest pay deployment revenue expected for the JV in 2026, with more meaningful commercial revenue anticipated only beginning in 2027.
positive_highlights: Signed an exclusive sales agreement with Kubota Corporation to deploy AirJoule systems in water-constrained regions of Texas and California.
First full-scale Prime system commissioned in Newark is operating outdoors at high uptime and tracking toward the expectation of 2,000 liters per day.
Awarded one of the UAE's first Expo City green licenses, providing access to business missions and a seat in the Green Majlis Leadership Forum.
summary: AirJoule Technologies reported a net loss of $8.5 million for Q2 FY26, driven by non-cash losses on earn-out shares and an increase in full-year cash spend guidance to approximately $27-$28 million from the prior expectation. Management highlighted significant commercial milestones including an exclusive partnership with Kubota Corporation for residential development in Texas and California, a deployment at GE Vernova's Frontier Campus, and regulatory validation via UAE green licenses.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to $17.2 million due to a $13.1M unrealized fair value change on digital asset holdings (primarily Ether).
All Q2 revenue came from the 'Access' model; no revenue was recognized yet from the primary 'Build' clusters.
Adjusted EBITDA remained negative at -$4.9 million for the quarter.
positive_highlights: Signed over $3 billion in total contract value (TCV) with more than half added incrementally since April, significantly exceeding initial projections.
Generated positive operating cash flow of $17.4 million driven by customer prepayments totaling $60.8 million at quarter end.
Active qualified pipeline reached $5.9 billion in August, nearly double the current signed book.
summary: Axe Compute reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $3.2 million (up from $35k in Q1) and a net loss of $17.2 million driven by $13.1M in unrealized digital asset losses, though adjusted EBITDA was -$4.9M excluding those non-cash items. Management highlighted the signing of over $3 billion in total contract value (TCV), including an incremental $2.9B in H1 Q3, with a projected annualized run rate exceeding $696 million upon full deployment by early 2027. The company announced its first customer prepayment of $317M and signed a new agreement for additional power capacity.

negative_highlights: Operating expenses increased by two percent due to deliberate investments in growth hiring and public company costs ahead of the second half ramp.
Revenue recognition for hosting is just beginning, while related party services revenues are winding down as APR agreements conclude.
Adjusted EBITDA guidance remains conservative at $8M-$10M for Q4 2026 due to assumptions regarding no acceleration in GPU energization.
positive_highlights: Revenue increased 30% YoY to $6.18M driven by Technology Solutions ($3.23M) as the legacy rail business was divested.
Net income from continuing operations surged to $48.7M, compared to a loss of $1.6M in Q2 2025.
Signed new agreements adding up to 55 megawatts with Axe Compute Inc., valued at over $500 million in contracted revenue.
summary: Duos Technologies reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $6.18 million (up 30% YoY) and net income from continuing operations of $48.7 million following the divestiture of its rail business and a gain on investment sales. The company reconfirmed full-year 2026 guidance to exceed $50M in revenue, citing approximately $17-18M annualized recurring revenue expected by Q4 exit run rate. Management highlighted significant progress in AI infrastructure deployment with new multi-megawatt contracts and a strengthened balance sheet of $112.3 million cash.

negative_highlights: Solutions revenue declined 4% YoY due to execution gaps and pricing pressure on renewals
Full-year revenue guidance narrowed slightly despite the Q2 beat, reflecting weaker solutions outlook for H2
Middle East conflict continues to weigh on booking volumes in affected corridors
positive_highlights: Record revenues of $7.7 million achieved ahead of expectations
Platform revenue grew 19% YoY to $2.9 million, driven by Clearit refund claims and Korean Air addition
Adjusted EBITDA loss improved significantly to a record low -$2 million
summary: Freightos reported record Q2 revenue of $7.7 million (up 3% YoY), driven by a strong platform beat but offset by a solutions decline of 4%. Adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed to -$2 million due to cost discipline, with cash ending the quarter at $21.4 million. Management raised full-year transaction growth guidance slightly while narrowing revenue expectations and maintaining an adjusted EBITDA breakeven target for Q4.

negative_highlights: One surface waiver signature remains pending from a single leasehold operator, though management expects it soon.
Phase Three expansion potential is capped at the standard air permit limit of roughly 757 MW; further growth requires switching to an PSD permit process which typically takes 18 months.
positive_highlights: Secured two key development permits from Ector County and received approval of Notice of Intent to commence grading for Phase One.
Successfully closed the acquisition of the flagged 54-acre corridor, securing all necessary land for planned development.
Expanded total gross capacity across Phases One and Two to roughly 757 MW by finalizing a PPA in New Era's own name.
summary: New Era delivered significant de-risking progress in Q2 FY2026 by securing construction permits and closing the acquisition of a critical land corridor at its flagship TCDC site. The company expanded Phase Two power capacity from 450 MW to approximately 550 MW, bringing total gross capacity for Phases One and Two to roughly 757 MW against previously contemplated levels. Management reaffirmed the target timeline for Phase One delivery in Q4 FY2026 (late 2027 calendar), citing that power availability is now secured via a finalized PPA structure.

negative_highlights: Net loss of $143 million was driven by non-cash items including a $54M depreciation charge and an $85M provision for Swedish VAT tax liability which management intends to contest.
Bitcoin mining revenue grew only modestly (7% q/q) as the business navigates rising difficulty, though this is offset by strong HPC growth.
positive_highlights: Announced a new five-year GPU cloud deal adding $70M in annualized recurring revenue (ARR) alongside an existing Cohere contract, reaching $180M total contracted HPC ARR ahead of schedule.
HPC business grew significantly with quarterly revenue rising from roughly $5 million to $7.1 million driven by the May B200 cluster go-live and new GB300 contracts.
Management confirmed strong demand for GPU clusters, noting willingness to rent additional capacity at higher prices per token than previously forecast.
summary: HIVE reported Q1 FY2027 revenue of $79 million (up 10% q/q and 74% y/y) with earnings from operations growing to $15.2 million despite a net loss driven by non-cash depreciation ($54M) and a Swedish tax provision ($85M). Management highlighted the closing of two major GPU cloud deals adding $95 million in annualized recurring revenue, pushing total contracted HPC ARR past $180 million ahead of their year-end target. The company emphasized strong demand for its compute power and plans to deploy additional capacity via partnerships with Bell Canada.

negative_highlights: Gross margin declined 30 bps YoY to 12.2%, though improved sequentially by 10 bps due to mix and efficiencies
Free cash flow was an outflow of $37 million in Q4 due to increased CapEx for capacity expansion
positive_highlights: Q4 revenue of $1.316B beat the top end of guidance range
Non-GAAP EPS of $4.10 exceeded expectations, driven by operating leverage with expenses at just 1.3% of revenue
DCI business reached a near-$1 billion annualized run rate in Q4
summary: Fabrinet reported Q4 FY26 revenue of $1.316 billion (up 45% YoY) and non-GAAP EPS of $4.10, both exceeding the top end of guidance. The company raised its full-year fiscal 2026 revenue to a record $4.6 billion (+36%) and is entering FY27 with strong momentum across data center, communications infrastructure, and automotive segments. Management highlighted significant capacity expansions in Thailand and Santa Clara to support accelerating demand.

negative_highlights: Total and cloud mining revenue declined sharply YoY, with cloud mining net dollar retention at just 24.1% as customers cut order volumes
Net loss of $20.5 million, including $16.9 million of fair value losses, and adjusted EBITDA of approximately negative $1.5 million
Cash and digital assets fell to $119.5 million from $177.1 million at year-end, driven by Bitcoin depreciation and hash rate prepayments
positive_highlights: Self-mining hash rate grew 9.3% QoQ to approximately 3.5 EH/s, with monthly self-mining production nearly tripling from 32 to a peak of 90 Bitcoin
Hosting and other services rose to $3.9 million, with hosting revenue up 254% YoY on note and Host traction
Bitcoin-backed loans were repaid down to $5.4 million from $15 million, and pledged Bitcoin fell to 54 from 357, alongside a $5 million buyback authorization
summary: Total revenue and cloud mining revenue declined sharply YoY, with cloud mining revenue of $24.9 million (58.3% of total) and self-mining $14.0 million; cloud mining net dollar retention fell to 24.1%. Net loss was $20.5 million, including $16.9 million of fair value losses on Bitcoin holdings and digital asset receivables/payables, leaving adjusted EBITDA of roughly negative $1.5 million. No formal guidance was given; management cited a 27% drop in average Bitcoin price, repayment of $10 million in Bitcoin-backed loans (loans down to $5.4 million), a $5 million buyback authorization, and self-mining hash rate up 9.3% QoQ to about 3.5 EH/s with a target of roughly 20 EH/s total managed hash rate by mid-August.

negative_highlights: Net income was negative BRL 320 million due to an impairment charge of BRL 233 million related to the TDUP São Luís port.
Debt service coverage ratio remained low at 0.2x LTM, negatively impacted by seasonality and not yet fully reflecting debt reduction benefits.
Radar's performance was impaired by lower ATR prices reducing lease contributions.
positive_highlights: Expanded net debt reduced significantly to BRL 9.2 billion via IPO proceeds (BRL 2.3b) and prepayments, a 20% drop from Q1.
Rumo EBITDA reached BRL 2.3 billion with volume up 9%, while Compass delivered higher margins in residential/commercial segments despite lower industrial consumption.
Raízen's out-of-court reorganization plan approved by 81.6% of financial creditors, marking a key turnaround step.
summary: Cosan reported a negative net income of BRL 320 million for Q2 FY2026, showing significant improvement over the prior year but missing profitability expectations due to an impairment charge and seasonality in investee dividends. The company highlighted strategic progress including Compass' IPO proceeds (BRL 2.3 billion), debt prepayments totaling nearly BRL 9 billion reducing expanded net debt by 20% to BRL 9.2 billion, and a projected Debt Service Coverage Ratio range of 0.8x-1.2x for year-end 2026.

negative_highlights: Pathology business growth was modest at only about $100,000 sequential increase to ~$6.1 million
positive_highlights: Quarterly revenues surpassed $7 million for the first time in company history
Adjusted EBITDA swung to positive approximately $400,000 from a loss of -$200,000 in Q1
Product revenue reached an all-time quarterly record of approximately $900,000
summary: Precipio reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of approximately $7 million, a sequential increase from $6.7 million in Q1 and a year-over-year growth of roughly 22% to $5.7 million. The company returned to positive adjusted EBITDA with approximately $400,000 (up from -$200,000 in Q1) and generated about $700,000 in operating cash flow while ending the quarter with over $3 million in cash on hand without raising capital. Management highlighted record product revenue of roughly $900,000 driven by a new commercial team and distributor partnerships.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA loss exceeded CAD 1.1 million for the nine-month period due to non-cash expenses and asset revaluation losses
Digital asset treasury value of approximately CAD 48 million is subject to significant volatility in crypto markets
Management explicitly stated that current market conditions have not rewarded their efforts yet
positive_highlights: Houdini Swap contributed CAD 1.2 million revenue and CAD 685,000 operating income with a 60% margin in its first month of inclusion
All validators maintained 100% uptime during Q3 FY2026
Company successfully financed Houdini acquisition using balance sheet rather than note treasury SOL
summary: For the nine months ended June 30th, 2026, Sol Strategies reported an EBITDA loss of CAD 1.1 million after adjusting for significant non-cash items including over CAD 6 million in impairment and revaluation losses on its digital asset treasury valued at approximately CAD 48 million. The company acquired Houdini Swap which contributed one month of revenue (CAD 1.2M) but the overall financials reflect a challenging macro environment with volatile crypto markets impacting the balance sheet. Management expressed confidence in long-term growth and team execution despite acknowledging that current market conditions have not yet rewarded their efforts.

negative_highlights: Fatal incident occurred at BMA's Peak Downs mine in Queensland within CEO Brandon Craig's first month
CEO stated ambition to work through tenure without a fatality was not met, requiring immediate learnings and response
Fuel prices elevated impacted financials by approximately AUD 200 million
positive_highlights: Record production numbers achieved in iron ore business in Western Australia
Escondida performed incredibly well with copper contributing over 50% of EBITDA
Net debt ended the year below target range at less than $9 billion
summary: BHP reported strong financial results for FY26 driven by record production in iron ore and Escondida copper amidst resilient prices. The company ended the year with less than $9 billion of net debt and paid a highest-in-four-years dividend of $8.7 billion, though management immediately pivoted to address a fatal incident at Peak Downs mine which halted momentum on safety goals.

negative_highlights: Fixed income primary market offerings were significantly reduced in Q2, with management noting they did less in the quarter than in an average month.
Mark-to-market losses on investment banking books and secondary trading flows impacted top-line growth by approximately BRL 400-420 million for the half-year.
Equities revenue declined sequentially by 2% due to lower ADTV, while fixed income fees were pressured by a shift in client mix toward low-yield daily liquidity products.
positive_highlights: Corporate segment revenues surged 117% year-over-year to BRL 8 billion driven by cross-note derivatives, FX, and credits despite lower fixed income offerings volume.
Retail revenue grew 8% YoY with equities up 11%, funds platform growing 23% YoY on performance fees, and retail net new money meeting the soft target of BRL 20 billion.
Adjusted EBT margin expanded to 32% sequentially due to operating leverage from controlled expenses against a resilient underlying business.
summary: XP reported Q2 FY26 gross revenue of BRL 5.1 billion (up 8% YoY) and adjusted EPS growth of 9%, driven by strong corporate segment performance (+32%) despite a challenging fixed income primary market environment that suppressed underlying retail momentum. Management noted the quarter was impacted by mark-to-market losses on investment banking books, estimating roughly BRL 400-420 million in negative impacts compared to prior periods where such effects were lower or absent. While meeting soft guidance targets for net new money and maintaining a robust capital ratio of 20.3%, management adopted a cautious tone regarding future credit growth, emphasizing collateralized lending strategies and conservative risk approaches as they navigate geopolitical volatility.

negative_highlights: No product revenue was reported; first-half net operating loss widened to $11.3 million from $7.6 million a year earlier.
Higher R&D and SG&A were driven by launch preparation for preservative-free ketamine, which remains pending ANDA approval.
Key catalysts remain contingent: NRX-101 NDA targeted for 2027, SPARC-TMS contracting still in process, and GNK-301 first-in-human targeted for July 2027.
positive_highlights: Cash and cash equivalents rose to $26.7 million as of June 30, 2026 from $7.8 million at December 31, 2025 after a public offering of more than $22 million gross.
First-half net loss narrowed to $18.0 million from $23.1 million in the comparable 2025 period.

FDA identified a single remaining major ANDA deficiency (Luer lock vial attestation), which the company says has been provided, with 2026 approval targeted and 5 million units of launch stock ordered.
summary: NRx reported a first-half 2026 net loss of $18.0 million versus $23.1 million a year earlier, but the net operating loss widened to $11.3 million from $7.6 million on higher R&D and SG&A tied to the pending preservative-free ketamine launch. Cash rose to $26.7 million from $7.8 million at Dec 31, 2025 following a public offering of over $22 million gross, and management said resources support at least a year of operations. No product revenue was reported; the company guided to a 2026 ketamine ANDA approval with 5 million units of launch stock ordered, an NRX-101 NDA targeted for 2027, and a DARPA-funded SPARC-TMS trial of NRX-101 with robotic TMS plus the GeNeuro asset acquisition and ALS drug GNK-301 first-in-human targeted for July 2027.

negative_highlights: Net loss remained significant at $14.6 million despite expense reductions, indicating high cash burn relative to current revenue.
GLDY assets under management were broadly unchanged (3,111 ounces) in Q2 compared to the prior quarter.
Material weaknesses regarding internal controls and disclosure procedures remain unremediated as of June 30.
positive_highlights: Operating expenses decreased by $20.4 million (57.1%) driven principally by lower stock-based compensation charges.
Completed five key institutional partnerships in Q2, including custody with Inspira Financial and brokerage access via Siebert/tZERO to remove accreditation barriers.
Recognized first income from the tokenized gold platform ($134k earned in Q2) proving the yield mechanism is repeatable.
summary: Streamex reported Q2 FY2026 net loss of $14.6 million (down from $46.7M in Q1) and operating expenses reduced by $20.4M due to lower stock-based compensation, while recognizing its first income stream of approximately $134k in gold lease revenue. Management provided no specific financial guidance but indicated that institutional adoption is expected as a catalyst in the third quarter following recent partnership integrations with Siebert Financial and Inspira Financial. The company maintains a strong balance sheet with $41.8M total liquidity, zero debt, and an operating cash burn run rate of approximately $1.1M/month excluding one-time items.

negative_highlights: International revenue decreased 5.8% YoY due to lease closures in the Middle East region
HWI blended RevPAR declined 3.8% YoY impacted by geopolitical conflict and Southeast Asia ramp-up challenges
First-half operational results were below expectation in some regions affected by severe weather
positive_highlights: China revenue grew 14.9% YoY driven by steady network expansion and RevPAR recovery
Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to 38.3%, with asset-light business delivering robust growth
Hanting Inn new version achieved meaningful RevPAR improvement and strong franchisee recognition
summary: In Q2 FY2026, H World Group reported revenue of RMB 7.1 billion (up 10.8% YoY) and adjusted net income of RMB 1.7 billion (up 26.9% YoY). Management maintained full-year guidance for hotel openings despite a slower first half due to supply chain issues, while keeping the full-year RevPAR outlook unchanged amidst macro uncertainties like extreme weather and geopolitical conflicts in the Middle East.

negative_highlights: Consolidated gross margin compressed to 26.7% due to inventory sold below cost for liquidity and portfolio rationalization.
One-time direct listing costs of approximately $1.4 million in deal fees plus non-cash accounting charges from convertible note conversion.
Wine and spirits revenue declined 3% YoY as the company deprioritizes legacy brands.
positive_highlights: Non-alcoholic and functional segment revenue increased 132% YoY to approximately $409,000 in Q2.
Core brands grew 12% YoY with product margins of 43.7%, significantly higher than legacy lines.
DTC and e-commerce revenue expanded more than fourfold (480%) year-over-year.
summary: Q2 FY26 net revenue was approximately $5.6 million (up 2% YoY), while core brands grew 12% and the non-alcoholic/functional segment surged 132%. The company reported a GAAP loss of $7.5M driven by one-time direct listing costs ($4.3M) and intentional inventory write-downs below cost to simplify the portfolio, resulting in compressed gross margins (26.7%). Management provided full-year guidance with net revenues at no less than $18.5 million.

negative_highlights: Total revenue decreased 4% year-over-year, missing expectations for broad-based AI-led expansion.
General business revenue fell 3% quarter-over-quarter and 4% year-over-year.
Management explicitly stated advertising businesses will remain under pressure in the second half due to deliberate monetization hold-back.
positive_highlights: AI Cloud Infra revenue increased 50% year-over-year, outpacing industry averages.
GPU cloud revenue accelerated sharply with +283% YoY growth and improved margins due to mix shift.
Apollo Go achieved a major milestone in Hong Kong as the first fully driverless testing provider in that market.
summary: Baidu reported Q2 FY2026 total revenue of CNY 31.3 billion, a decrease of 4% year-over-year and 2% quarter-over-quarter, driven by declines in general business (CNY 25.2b) and iQIYI (down 5%). While AI Cloud Infra grew strongly at +50% YoY with GPU cloud revenue surging 283%, the overall miss on top-line growth resulted from pressure in advertising-related segments, leading to a net decline in total earnings.

negative_highlights: Q4 GAAP EPS declined from $0.27 to $0.01 due to lower net income
International sales down approximately 15% attributed to temporary contract manufacturer ramp-up issues
positive_highlights: Record Q4 bookings of $660 million, up 93% year-over-year
Full-year FY26 organic revenue growth accelerated to 7.9%
FY26 adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 217 bps YoY to 15.3%
summary: Mercury Systems reported record Q4 FY26 revenue of $290 million and full-year organic growth of 7.9%, driven by a massive 93% year-over-year increase in bookings to a new quarterly record of $660 million. Management raised its outlook for FY27, targeting low double-digit organic revenue growth while maintaining an adjusted EBITDA margin profile in the high teens and full-year FCF conversion near 35%. The company highlighted strong domestic demand (up 13%) and expanded backlog visibility to over $1.9 billion.

negative_highlights: Supply chain remains a governor on near-term revenue conversion due to incoming parts constraints
One-time tariff impact artificially inflated FY26 profitability which will not repeat in future periods
positive_highlights: Revenue of $1.846B beat expectations with 36% YoY growth; EPS of $3.70 up 79%
Wireline revenue in Communications Solutions Group hit a record billion-dollar quarter, surpassing wireless for the first time
summary: Keysight reported record Q3 FY26 results with revenue of $1.846 billion (up 36% YoY) and EPS of $3.70 (up 79%), both exceeding the high end of guidance. Operating margin expanded to 33.2%, up 820 bps, driven by strong core growth in Communications Solutions Group where wireline revenue hit a record billion-dollar quarter for the first time. Management raised full-year and Q4 outlooks citing robust demand across AI infrastructure, defense modernization, and semiconductor markets.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA declined 4.5%, primarily driven by a 21% drop in Argentina due to lower domestic passenger volumes and normalized cargo storage revenues.
Uruguay adjusted EBITDA fell 16% as non-recurring costs for the new ILS system implementation weighed on results before revenue recognition began in August.
Domestic traffic in Argentina declined approximately 8-12%, constrained by Flybondi's significantly reduced operating fleet and higher fuel prices.
positive_highlights: Total revenues grew 8% year-over-year outpacing traffic figures with revenue per passenger rising nearly 9% to $22.9.
Four of six segments delivered double-digit EBITDA growth led by Armenia (up 21%), Brazil, Italy, and Ecuador.
International demand remained healthy across the portfolio including a 6% increase in Argentina's international traffic.
summary: Total revenues excluding IFRIC 12 grew 8% year-over-year to outpace traffic figures, driven by double-digit growth in Armenia and Brazil despite a decline in Argentina's cargo business due to an exceptionally bad prior-year comparison base. Adjusted EBITDA fell 4.5%, with the majority of the miss concentrated in Argentina (down 21%) and Uruguay (down 16%), while four other segments delivered strong double-digit growth. The board approved a $150 million cash dividend for 2026, marking an important milestone in capital allocation.

negative_highlights: Total revenues decreased from $84.6 million in the prior period due to a decrease in paying users attributable to geopolitical events
Operating income declined significantly to $19.4 million compared with $30.6 million last year, driven by higher marketing spend and lower core business revenue
Management expects overall revenues for 2026 to remain broadly in line with last year despite the strong Q2 beat
positive_highlights: Revenues of $82.6 million exceeded the upper end of management's prior guidance
Non-GAAP net margin remained healthy at 41.7% despite a 106% increase in note and marketing expenses YoY
Game services revenue grew by 11.6% year-over-year to $34.2 million
summary: Yalla reported Q2 FY2026 revenues of $82.6 million, which beat the upper end of guidance but represented a decline from last year due to geopolitical impacts on paying users. Non-GAAP net margin remained healthy at 41.7% despite doubling watching and marketing expenses YoY. Management maintained full-year revenue guidance broadly in line with expectations while noting potential for updates if new games perform strongly.

negative_highlights: Ball and Racket segment guidance was lowered for full-year sales growth from 12%-14% to approximately 14%, with management noting Q2's 24% pace is not sustainable.

Adjusted net finance costs of $21 million exceeded the prior guidance range due to higher hedging costs and currency losses, impacting bottom-line EPS by roughly $0.08 per share from tariff refunds only.
Corporate expenses increased significantly to $68 million versus $45 million last year due to higher IT investments and deferred compensation.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 32% on a reported basis and 30% ex-currency across all segments with double-digit growth in every region including Asia Pacific (+60%) and China (+36%).
Adjusted gross margin expanded to 65.8%, driven by underlying mix benefits of over 300 bps excluding the one-time tariff refund.
Salomon Softgoods led Outdoor Performance with strong footwear momentum, while Wilson Tennis 360 saw racket growth exceed 50% due to the Blade v10 launch.
summary: Amer Sports reported Q2 FY26 revenue growth of 32% (ex-currency) and adjusted EPS of $0.22 vs prior year's $0.06, driven by strong performance across Arc'teryx, Salomon Softgoods, and Wilson Tennis 360 segments with double-digit growth in all regions. Management raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to approximately 24% from the previous 20%-22%, along with increases in adjusted operating margin guidance to 14.2%-14.5%. The quarter featured significant one-time net tariff refund benefits of $64.3 million, which inflated reported margins but management clarified that underlying organic expansion remains robust.

negative_highlights: Total revenue declined 5.9% to $18.2 million, driven by a 13.1% drop in the MeowGo business
Gross margins contracted from 52.8% to 50.2%, with service gross margins falling sharply from 56.6% to 39.1%
Full-year revenue guidance was lowered by $10M-$15M due to macroeconomic headwinds and geopolitical tensions
positive_highlights: GlocalMe IoT revenue surged 392.4% year-over-year, growing from $0.2 million to $0.8 million
GlocalMe SIM business grew by 78%, increasing revenue contribution significantly
New product lines including PetPhone and CPE R50/R55 demonstrated strong momentum with positive market feedback
summary: Total revenue decreased by 5.9% to $18.2 million in Q2 FY26 due to macroeconomic headwinds and a significant surge in chip costs affecting the uCloudlink 1.0 business line, while new growth engines like GlocalMe IoT showed strong YoY expansion of 392.4%. Management revised full-year guidance downward from $85M-$100M to $75M-$85M citing persistent macroeconomic challenges and global trade headwinds.

negative_highlights: Gross margin expansion was largely offset by incremental cost pressures related to fuel, energy, and product inputs (approx. 60 bps).
Larger discretionary projects remain under pressure due to consumer uncertainty and housing affordability issues.
Inventory turns declined from 4.6x to 4.5x as merchandise inventories rose by approximately $2 billion.
positive_highlights: Sales increased $2.6 billion or 5.7% YoY to $47.9B driven by broad-based demand across the business.
Adjusted EPS of $4.92 beat expectations, aided by a one-time tariff refund benefit that reduced COGS by $685 million.
International performance was strong with Canada and Mexico out-competing the company average.
summary: Home Depot reported Q2 FY2026 sales of $47.9 billion (up 5.7% YoY) and adjusted EPS of $4.92 (up 5.1%), exceeding expectations driven by a one-time IEEPA tariff refund benefit that boosted gross margin to 33.7%. Management reaffirmed full-year guidance, projecting comp sales growth between flat to 2%, with the Q2 tariff windfall expected to be fully offset in Q3 and Q4 by incremental fuel, energy, and commodity cost pressures. While international (Canada/Mexico) and Pro segments showed strength, management noted continued pressure on larger discretionary projects and a frozen housing market.

negative_highlights: U.S. cinema revenue declined 3% year over year, attributed to the strong prior-year titles and the closures of the San Diego Grossmont and Town Square theaters.

Liquidity is limited, with cash and cash equivalents of $5.7 million and $183.1 million of gross borrowings, while the Santander and Bank of America maturities were extended only to October 1, 2026 and December 21, 2026.
The Newberry Yard sale stalled as the buyer requested changes to the purchase agreement and leaseback and the deal is described as no longer acceptable to the company.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA rose 79% to $11.3 million, the best second-quarter result in seven years, and global operating income improved 159% to $7.5 million.
Australian cinema revenue increased 31% to a record AUD 30 million, with segment operating income up 91% to AUD 5.6 million.
Net income attributable to Reading swung to $2.3 million from a $2.7 million loss and basic EPS rose $0.22 to $0.10.
summary: Q2 2026 consolidated revenue rose $6.5 million to $66.9 million, net income attributable to Reading swung to $2.3 million from a $2.7 million loss, and basic EPS turned positive at $0.10 versus a $0.12 loss; adjusted EBITDA rose 79% to $11.3 million and global operating income improved 159% to $7.5 million. The improvement was led by an Australian cinema circuit revenue gain of 31% to AUD 30 million, an 11% Australian dollar tailwind, and higher U.S. live theater revenue, partly offset by a 3% decline in U.S. cinema revenue. The company cited a strong upcoming film slate (Spider-Man: Brand New Day, The Odyssey, plus the December releases) and reaffirmed its two-business, three-country strategy while pursuing the Cinema 123 sale. Liquidity remains tight at $5.7 million of cash, and the Santander and Bank of America facility maturities were extended to October 1, 2026 and December 21, 2026, respectively, with a replacement lender in the due diligence process.

negative_highlights: SGI segment recorded an operating loss of RMB 64 million as the company continues heavy investment in product development for actuation modules and Kosmo.
Kosmo revenue contribution is expected to be small (low eight digits) this year, with significant ramp-up anticipated only starting Q3.
positive_highlights: SGI segment recorded first-ever revenue contribution of RMB 45 million driven by robotic actuation module sales to Sharpa.
Management raised full-year 2026 SGI guidance from RMB 100M to a range of RMB 200-300M due to demand exceeding expectations.
Robotics LiDAR shipments surged approximately 193% YoY, while total ADAS and robotics combined growth was nearly 80%.
summary: Hesai Group reported Q2 FY26 net revenues of RMB 861 million (up ~22% YoY), driven by a core LiDAR business generating RMB 816 million and the debut of Strategic Growth Initiatives (SGI) at RMB 45 million. Management raised full-year 2026 SGI revenue guidance from RMB 100 million to RMB 200-300 million, citing faster-than-expected commercialization of robotic actuation modules and Kosmo spatial intelligence platform revenues expected in Q3.

negative_highlights: Intelligent solutions revenue growth moderated to just 4% due to delivery fluctuations from domain controllers.
Net cash used in operating activities increased slightly year-over-year, though attributed to normal working capital and strategic inventory investment for fleet expansion.
positive_highlights: Robotaxi revenue surged 691% year-over-year to a record $12.1 million.
Fare charging revenue jumped nearly 8x compared to the prior year period.
Operating loss narrowed by over 30% YoY as non-GAAP operating expenses grew at only 9.6%, significantly outpaced by top-line growth.
summary: Pony.ai reported Q2 FY26 total revenue of $36.2 million, a 69% year-over-year increase driven by robotaxi revenues reaching a record high of $12.1 million (up 691%) and fare charging revenues surging nearly 8x to over 40%. Operating loss narrowed significantly from -$75M in Q2 FY25 to -$45.4M, with non-GAAP operating expenses growing at only 9.6% while revenue grew by 69%, demonstrating strong operating leverage.

negative_highlights: Q2 revenue decreased by approximately $0.2 million (40% YoY) primarily due to the conclusion of AgPlenus' agreement with Bayer in May.
First-half revenues declined significantly from $2.9 million in H1 2025 to $0.7 million, largely attributable to lower Casterra sales following significant seed revenue last year.
APH1 herbicide program was discontinued by partner Bayer because the target protein proved non-essential for weed survival.
positive_highlights: Net loss improved by approximately $2.9 million (nearly 62%) compared to Q2 2025 due to lower operating expenses.
Successfully completed hit-to-lead milestones on two of six active drug development collaborations with results exceeding partner expectations.
Reduced consolidated cash usage in the quarter to approximately $2.1 million, aligning with a full-year burn expectation range of ILS 8.5M-$9.5M.
summary: Evogene reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of approximately $0.3 million compared to $0.5 million in the prior year period, a decrease driven by the conclusion of an agreement with Bayer and lower sales from Casterra. The company's net loss narrowed significantly to approximately $1.8 million from $4.7 million in Q2 2025 due to reduced operating expenses and discontinued operations losses. Management highlighted strategic progress including six active drug development agreements, successful hit-to-lead milestones on two programs, and a reduction in cash burn expectations for the full year.

negative_highlights: Full-year GMV guidance was lowered to $149-151 billion (from above $155 billion) due to a measured view of German volumes where retail sales grew less than 1% in real terms.
U.S. revenue growth slowed sequentially compared to Q2 as the company completed back book receivable sales that were not repeated, causing reported take rates to dip slightly.
German consumer discretionary spending remains soft with no immediate recovery expected for H2.
positive_highlights: Transaction margin dollars grew at 42%, significantly outpacing revenue growth of 27% and volume growth of 18%.
Fair Financing (big-ticket spend) GMV surged 82% year-over-year to $4.7 billion, now representing 13% of total volume.
Klarna membership reached 2 million paying subscribers with subscription revenue growing over 600%, decoupling growth from pure transaction volume.
summary: Klarna delivered a strong quarter with revenue of $1.04 billion (up 27%) and transaction margin dollars rising 42% to $446 million, beating the high end of guidance on every line item for two consecutive quarters. Management raised its full-year adjusted operating income outlook by approximately $35-40 million due to stronger unit economics, despite a downward revision to the GMV forecast driven primarily by softer-than-expected consumer sentiment in Germany.

negative_highlights: Membership services revenue declined sequentially by 4% to RMB 4.0 billion due to seasonality and lack of blockbuster content.
Online advertising revenue remained flat at RMB 1.2 billion sequentially with no year-over-year growth mentioned for the quarter.
Other revenues fell 17% sequentially, indicating weakness in non-core business segments.
positive_highlights: Non-GAAP operating loss narrowed by 8% sequentially to RMB 130.3 million due to disciplined marketing spend and improved content efficiency.
Overseas membership revenue surged with Brazil up 215%, Mexico up 150%, and Thailand showing steady growth on a profitable basis.
Brand advertising delivered double-digit year-over-year growth, particularly in beauty, personal care, healthcare, and AI application sectors.
summary: Total revenues were RMB 6.3 billion, up 1% sequentially but down year-over-year due to a 4% decline in membership services revenue driven by seasonality and the absence of major hits like 'The Legend'. Non-GAAP operating loss narrowed substantially from Q1 (RMB 148.6 million) to RMB 130.3 million, approaching breakeven as AI-driven cost efficiencies began materializing.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA remained negative at -$19 million for the quarter due to high marketing investment.
Net loss per share was $0.52, down from a prior year loss of $0.94 but still representing an operating deficit.
positive_highlights: Revenue beat guidance of $46M-$48M with total revenue at $45 million for IM8 and $46.5 million consolidated.
Gross margin expanded significantly to 65% in Q2, up from prior periods.
Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC) improved by roughly 21% sequentially despite doubling acquisition spend.
summary: The company reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $46.5 million (up 3.9x YoY), with IM8 contributing $45 million at a gross margin expansion to 65%. Management raised full-year total revenue guidance to $220-$230 million and initiated 2027 projections, citing record July performance where CAC fell 21% despite doubled acquisition spend. The business crossed into positive adjusted free cash flow in Q2 due to a new funding facility.

negative_highlights: Cash on hand of $1.8 million is explicitly stated as insufficient to fund operations for the next 12 months without additional financing.
The company faces substantial doubt regarding its ability to continue as a going concern due to liquidity constraints and accumulated deficit of $138 million.
Vivos is not in compliance with Nasdaq minimum stockholders' equity requirements ($2.5 million) and faces potential delisting proceedings.
positive_highlights: Revenue increased 35% year-over-year to $5.2 million, driven by a $1.9 million increase in service revenue from SCN diagnostic services and treatment.
Gross margin expanded to 57% for the quarter as revenue growth outpaced cost increases associated with new staff and facilities.
Referral volume from SCN physicians to SAMC centers has increased three to four times since the end of Q2, indicating strong operational synergy.
summary: Vivos Therapeutics reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $5.2 million, a 35% year-over-year increase driven by service revenue growth from the Sleep Center of Nevada (SCN) acquisition, while product revenue declined due to a strategic pivot away from VIPs. The company incurred a net loss of $5.5 million and ended the quarter with only $1.8 million in cash, explicitly stating that existing funds are insufficient to fund operations for the next 12 months without additional financing. Management highlighted significant headwinds including non-compliance with Nasdaq minimum equity requirements and substantial doubt regarding the company's ability to continue as a going concern.

negative_highlights: Solar PLF declined due to a mix of curtailment (approx. half) and adverse weather patterns, impacting capacity utilization
Manufacturing margins contracted from last year's Q1 level of 40% down to the current quarter's 34%
Grid connectivity issues in Rajasthan continue to cause temporary curtailments for certain projects
positive_highlights: Operating portfolio grew 26% YoY to 13.5 GW with over 1 GW commissioned in Q1 FY27
Profit after tax increased by 16% year-over-year to INR 6 billion, aided by a significant one-time cash inflow of INR 57 billion from Andhra Pradesh DISCOM post-quarter end
Manufacturing business delivered strong external sales with adjusted EBITDA margin at 34%
summary: ReNew reported Q1 FY2027 revenue of INR 44.6 billion (up 14% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of INR 30.4 billion (up 12% YoY), driven by a 26% growth in its operating portfolio to 13.5 GW. Management reiterated full-year FY2027 consolidated adjusted EBITDA guidance of INR 103-109 billion, maintaining the range despite acknowledging margin contraction in manufacturing and curtailment impacts on solar PLF.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA loss widened significantly from negative $21 million to negative $34.6 million due to heavy R&D and corporate infrastructure spending.
R&D expenditure rose sharply to SEK equivalent of roughly $20.4 million in H1, up from $13 million the prior year.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 26% YoY on a constant currency basis driven by expansion within existing customers and new deployments.
Signed partnership to deploy 500 Tesla Semi trucks which will triple the fleet size upon completion in late 2027.
Sales pipeline increased three-fold following concerted sales team investments.
summary: Einride reported H1 FY26 revenue of EUR 27 million (up 26% YoY), but Adjusted EBITDA widened to a loss of $34.6 million from negative $21 million in the prior year due to increased R&D and IPO preparation costs. Management guided for constant currency revenue growth to double in H2, expecting EUR 39-42 million (driven by Amazon and Tesla Semi ramp), which would result in an annualized run rate of EUR 85-95 million by December. The company reiterated a path to cash flow breakeven in late 2028 with a deployed fleet of 1,500-2,000 vehicles.

negative_highlights: Cash gross margin decreased slightly to 41.8% from 43.6% YoY, primarily due to higher utility costs passed through to customers.
Wholesale revenue growth (29.3%) was lower than the total net revenue growth rate of 14.2%, indicating retail and non-IDC segments contributed less aggressively.
positive_highlights: Wholesale capacity in service rose by 49.4% year-over-year to surpass the 1 GW milestone at 1,007 MW with a utilization rate of 73.9%.
Secured 345 MW in new order wins during Q2 from leading cloud providers and AI-native companies, bringing total H1 orders to 862 MW.
Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to 33.0%, reflecting ongoing operational efficiency enhancements.
summary: VNET reported Q2 FY2026 net revenues of RMB 2.78 billion (up 14.2% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of RMB 918.3 million (up 25.4% YoY), driven by a robust wholesale IDC business that surpassed the 1 GW capacity milestone in service. Management reiterated full-year guidance for net revenues between RMB 11.5 billion-RMB 11.8 billion and adjusted EBITDA of RMB 3.55 billion-RMB 3.75 billion, maintaining unchanged estimates despite a slight sequential decline in cash gross margin attributed to higher utility pass-through costs.

negative_highlights: Adjusted operating margin contracted significantly due to the exit of Homestyles ($1.8M sales decline) and lack of prior year foreign currency gains.
Q4 guidance for Q1 FY27 (6.5%-7% margins) is lower than current performance, citing rising energy prices and supply chain inflation pressures.
Demand environment weakened significantly following geopolitical events, with consumer confidence remaining subdued.
positive_highlights: Net sales grew 4% over FY26 and delivered record adjusted EPS of $4.94 despite a challenging macro environment.
Free cash flow generation exceeded $47 million, enabling a 25% dividend increase and share repurchases.
Health and wellness category continued to deliver positive year-over-year growth.
summary: Flexsteel reported Q4 FY26 net sales of $115.4 million (up 0.7% YoY) and adjusted operating margins of 7.1%, down from the prior year's 9.0%. The quarter included a one-time benefit of tariff refunds but also reflected costs associated with exiting the Homestyles ready-to-assemble category, which contributed roughly $12 million in sales for the fiscal year.

negative_highlights: Management explicitly warned that the annualized revenue figure of $414 million is a mathematical equivalent only and should not be treated as a full-year forecast.
The Q&A session focused heavily on explaining why market capitalization remains low despite high revenues, citing a lack of retail support from investment banks following their direct listing.
No specific guidance was provided for the second half of FY26 or FY27; management only stated they are pursuing a previously announced $430M objective without confirming if it is achievable.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew approximately 59% year-over-year to $207 million for the first half of FY26.
Adjusted EBITDA run rate increased significantly from ~$190k in Q1 to over $700k in Q2 due to gross margin expansion and integration efficiencies.
Gross profit expanded by approximately 26% year-over-year, improving the company's profitability profile.
summary: For the first half of FY26 (Q1+Q2), iQSTEL reported $207 million in revenue versus approximately $130 million year-ago, representing a 59% increase. The company highlighted that its annualized run rate is now roughly $414 million but explicitly stated this figure should not be considered a forecast for the full fiscal year. Management noted significant margin expansion with gross profit growing from $3.8M to $4.8M and adjusted EBITDA rising from ~$0.2M in Q1 to over $0.7M in Q2, driven by integration synergies.

negative_highlights: Product revenue fell sharply by 42% to $40.8 million, primarily due to lower sales in China and unfavorable mix.
Full-year operating income turned into a loss of $26.4 million compared to $7.8 million profit the prior year.
Management declined to provide fiscal 2027 revenue or EBITDA guidance citing significant uncertainty from tariffs, geopolitical tensions, and macroeconomic conditions.
positive_highlights: Gross margins expanded 420 bps to 34.8% in the quarter, driven by $5.8 million of tariff favorability and operational efficiencies.
Service revenue grew 6% year-over-year to $60.1 million, supported by pricing actions and an expanding installed base.
Transformation initiatives exceeded targets, realizing over $20 million in cost improvements versus a target of $12 million.
summary: Net revenue for the fourth quarter was $100.9 million, down 21% year-over-year, while full-year revenue declined 12%. Gross margins expanded to 34.8% in the quarter due to tariff favorability and restructuring benefits, but operating income dropped significantly with a full-year loss of $26.4 million compared to prior year income. Management explicitly stated they are not providing formal guidance for fiscal 2027 due to geopolitical uncertainty and macroeconomic factors.

negative_highlights: Global Solutions segment revenue decreased 5% year-over-year to $27.6 million due to the non-repetition of a specific aircraft sale.
Backlog coverage ratio declined from 86% in Q1 to 71% in Q2 as note weakness in-cycle orders were delivered, reducing funded visibility.
positive_highlights: Revenue surged 100% year-over-year to $201.8 million driven by the Deep Strike program execution.
Net income swung from a loss of $11.8 million in Q2 FY2025 to a profit of $6.7 million in Q2 FY2026.
Adjusted EBITDA margins expanded significantly year-over-year, with the tactical systems segment reaching 17% margin.
summary: AEVEX reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $201.8 million, representing a 100% year-over-year increase driven by the tactical systems segment and the Deep Strike program. Net income turned positive at $6.7 million compared to a loss in the prior year, with adjusted EBITDA margins expanding significantly. The company announced a definitive agreement to acquire BlackSea Technologies for up to $650 million and raised its full-year 2026 revenue guidance to a midpoint of $710 million.

negative_highlights: Equity notional volume showed softness compared to June, attributed to the SpaceX event rather than a structural trend.
Crypto revenue remains low at approximately $2.25 million (just over 1% of total Q2 revenue), though prediction markets are growing rapidly.
positive_highlights: Record quarterly revenue of $198.8 million and record adjusted operating profit of $62.6 million driven by the PDT Rule elimination tailwind.
Customer assets surged to a record $28.5 billion, representing 79% year-over-year growth with average account size doubling to over $5,500.
Options volume reached 213 million contracts (up 68% YoY) and Webull secured its first-ever top-five position among retail brokers in options.
summary: Webull reported record Q2 FY26 revenue of $198.8 million (up 51% YoY) and adjusted operating profit of $62.6 million (up 169% YoY), driven by the successful navigation of the SEC's elimination of the Pattern Day Trader Rule which boosted options volume to a top-five industry position. Adjusted operating margin expanded significantly to 31.5%, while customer assets grew 79% year-over-year to $28.5 billion, with net deposits reaching $1.6 billion.

negative_highlights: Comparable average transactions declined 2.1%, primarily due to pressure in weather-sensitive outdoor categories during Memorial Day weekend.
Gross margin contracted 80 bps YoY, with elevated fuel and transportation costs largely offsetting the $30 bps tariff refund benefit.
Full-year outlook revised down as residential construction pressures impact acquisitions FBM (45% exposed) and ADG.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EPS exceeded expectations even excluding $0.11 benefit from IEEPA tariff refunds ($96M pre-tax charges).
Delivered five consecutive quarters of positive comparable sales, demonstrating strategy resilience across changing economic conditions.
Online sales grew 15.7% driven by digital experience investments and the Mylow AI agent which triples conversion rates for users.
summary: Lowe's reported Q2 sales of $26 billion (up 8.3% YoY) and adjusted EPS of $4.40, beating expectations despite a soft comparable sales increase of only 0.2%. Management updated full-year guidance to the low end of the previous range ($92B sales, ~11.6% operating margin), citing elevated fuel/transportation costs offsetting tariff benefits and persistent pressure on DIY demand from weather and macro uncertainty.

negative_highlights: Enterprise cloud services declined slightly by 1% year-over-year to RMB 740 million due to upstream supply pricing hikes affecting SOE/government customers.
Capital expenditures were high at RMB 3.3 billion in the quarter, with full-year CapEx remaining fixed at RMB 15 billion despite volatile monthly purchasing patterns.
positive_highlights: Total revenue reached a record RMB 3.07 billion, up 31% year-over-year and 40% quarter-over-quarter.
AI cloud gross billings surged to RMB 1.33 billion (+82%), accounting for over half of public cloud revenue.
Adjusted operating profit turned positive at RMB 124 million, marking a turnaround from an adjusted loss in the prior year.
summary: Kingsoft Cloud reported Q2 FY26 revenue of RMB 3.07 billion (up 31% YoY), driven by a record AI cloud gross billing of RMB 1.33 billion (+82% YoY). Adjusted operating profit turned positive for the first time with an adjusted margin of 4%, while full-year CapEx guidance remains unchanged at RMB 15 billion despite high quarterly spend.

negative_highlights: Management expects Q3 lithium gross margins to be similar to Q2, implying no immediate expansion despite volume strength.
Supply constraints in certain markets are expected to gradually normalize toward the end of the year, potentially dampening price premiums.
BESS inventory builds and project implementation delays may lead to a slowdown in battery storage demand growth over the next 12-18 months.
positive_highlights: Record quarterly lithium sales volumes of more than 84,000 metric tons achieved from operations in Chile and Australia.
Lithium prices increased during the second quarter supported by stronger-than-expected market demand.
Iodine business delivered good results with robust market demand and favorable pricing.
summary: SQM reported a strong second quarter of FY26 with record quarterly lithium sales volumes exceeding 84,000 metric tons and robust iodine results supported by favorable pricing. Management raised full-year global demand expectations to over 2.1 million metric tons and updated capital expenditure guidance to approximately $3 billion for the 2026-2028 period to support growth initiatives like Salar Futuro. While Q3 lithium prices are expected to be flat, volumes remain strong with a potential upside in Q4.

negative_highlights: Q2 revenue declined sequentially from Q1 due to lower solar cell sales volume despite strong module growth.
Shipment timing was affected by CBP reviews and detentions of Ethiopian facility products during the quarter.
Management explicitly stated that previously issued full-year guidance is no longer relevant until clarity emerges on regulatory issues.
positive_highlights: First-half revenue surged 87.6% year-over-year to $261 million driven by higher solar cell, module sales, and OEM services.
Gross margin nearly doubled in the first half from 16.6% to 32.5%, reflecting improved production consistency and mix shifts.
Management confirmed that Section 232 policy is viewed as a positive risk development supporting U.S. manufacturing strategy.
summary: TOYO reported strong first-half revenue of $261 million (up 87.6% YoY) and Q2 revenue of $118.2 million (up 35% YoY), driven by module sales, though Q2 saw a sequential decline due to lower cell mix. Gross margins expanded significantly in the first half to 32.5%, but management explicitly declined to reaffirm full-year guidance citing near-term uncertainties regarding CBP detentions and Section 232 tariff negotiations.

negative_highlights: Gross margin contracted to 34% from 55% in Q2 2025 due to a higher reduce exposure note mix and elevated costs.
Revenue missed the original full guidance of $55 million-$60 million because retail revenue was deconsolidated.
Adjusted EBITDA fell sharply to $5.7 million from $18.1 million in Q2 2025.
positive_highlights: Revenue of $47 million beat the adjusted guidance range excluding retail revenue.
Cost of production improved significantly to $122 per pound from $175 in Q1 and $129 last year.
Wholesale note price increased to $211 per pound, exceeding the original guidance of $185-$190.
summary: Second quarter revenue was $47 million, missing the prior guidance of $55 million-$60 million due to a deconsolidation of retail operations and unfavorable product mix. Gross margin declined from 55% in Q2 2025 to 34% in Q2 2026 driven by a higher proportion of low-value trim in the production mix and elevated costs of $122 per pound. Adjusted EBITDA was $5.7 million, significantly below last year's $18.1 million but an improvement from the first quarter loss.

negative_highlights: Adjusted non-GAAP gross margin remained negative at -19.9%
Operating cash flow was -$54 million with significant outflows for R&D
Automotive results were softer, offsetting gains in data centers and materials
positive_highlights: AI data center revenue more than doubled from fiscal 2025 versus fiscal 2026
Power segment grew approximately 20% sequentially in Q4 driven by AI demand
Debt conversion of $46 million reduced net debt to ~$600M and saved annual interest
summary: Wolfspeed reported Q4 FY26 revenue of $150 million, meeting the midpoint of guidance and showing a 6% sequential increase driven by AI data center growth which more than doubled from fiscal 2025. Adjusted non-GAAP gross margin was -19.9%, reflecting continued underutilization despite product mix improvements, while operating cash flow remained negative at -$54 million due to debt service and R&D investments.

negative_highlights: Q4 net new customer additions of ~1,800 were below recent trends due to deliberate prioritization of higher-quality customers and organizational restructuring.
S&E revenue faces a specific headwind from card acceptance challenges with large ad providers (Meta/Google) impacting volume growth by approximately 2 points YoY in Q4 FY2027 guidance.
TPV mix contraction compressed the AP/AR take rate to 16.0 bps, down 0.5 bps sequentially.
positive_highlights: Core revenue grew 16% year-over-year to $400.5 million with non-GAAP operating margin expanding 370 bps sequentially to 23%.
Customer spend on AI increased over 50% year-over-year, and TPV from AI-first customers nearly doubled quarter-over-quarter.
Invoice financing volume and revenue grew approximately 30% YoY with expected loss rates improving by more than 50%.
summary: BILL reported Q4 FY2026 core revenue of $400.5 million (up 16% YoY) and non-GAAP operating margin expanding to 23%. Management raised full-year FY2027 guidance for total revenue ($1.807B-$1.857B, +9%-12%) and EPS ($3.56-$3.79), while explicitly noting headwinds from S&E card acceptance dynamics and go-to-market restructuring that will impact Q1 FY2027.

negative_highlights: Haircare did not return to organic sales growth yet, though evidence of Aveda's turnaround in the U.S. is emerging.
Middle East conflict disruptions reduced EUKEM (Europe, UK, Middle East) growth by approximately 2%.
positive_highlights: Organic sales grew 3% with broad-based performance across categories; makeup trend improved by 500 bps to stabilize.
Gross margin expanded 150 basis points while operating margins rose significantly, funding additional consumer-facing investments.
Fiscal 2027 guidance was raised on profitability (operating margin) and sales growth acceleration is expected in North America.
summary: The company reported a strong beat with organic sales rising 3% and diluted EPS growing 66%, significantly exceeding the initial outlook from August. Operating margins expanded by 320 basis points to reach an annualized run-rate that prompted management to raise their fiscal 2027 operating margin guidance range to 12.7%-13.5%. Management expressed high confidence in accelerating growth for fiscal 2027, citing a diversified portfolio of billion-dollar brands and successful execution across all regions.

negative_highlights: Consolidated delivered sales were down 1% excluding divestitures due to lower wholesale performance
Joybird business experienced a significant decline with written sales decreasing 17%
Adjusted operating margin contracted to 3.9% from 4.8% last year driven by fixed cost deleverage and friction costs
positive_highlights: Retail written sales increased 16% driven by new/acquired stores and positive same-store growth
Company returned $35 million to shareholders via buybacks and dividends, a 62% increase versus the prior year
Wholesale backlog remains solid entering Q2 despite choppy order patterns
summary: Fiscal Q1 FY27 consolidated delivered sales declined 3% reported (down 1% excluding case goods divestitures) while retail same-store sales slipped slightly despite a strong 16% growth in written sales. Adjusted operating income was $19 million, down from the prior year due to deleverage on lower wholesale and Joybird volume alongside friction costs from strategic investments like plant consolidations. Management provided cautious guidance for Q2 adjusted margins of 4%-5.5%, citing uneven demand patterns and ongoing supply chain transformation expenses.

negative_highlights: Advertising revenue declined 1% YoY due to softer demand in key verticals like handsets and cosmetics.
Operating margin contracted significantly from 36% last year to 28% primarily driven by higher ad production costs and marketing expenses.
Management warned of pressure on Q3 advertising growth due to a high revenue base established during the previous food delivery price war.
positive_highlights: Value-added service revenue surged 19% YoY driven by membership services and one-off ticket purchases.
Ad revenues from Automobile (+NEV launches) and Internet Services (AI demand) delivered solid growth despite broader market softness.
Video consumption metrics showed double-digit year-over-year growth with improved high-quality content supply.
summary: Weibo reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $453.8 million (up 2% YoY) and ad revenue of $381 million (down 1% YoY), while value-added services grew to $72.9 million (+19%). Operating income was $125.4 million with a margin of 28%, down from 36% last year due to higher costs, though net margins remained at 23%. Management expressed caution regarding the second half outlook, citing persistent macro headwinds in consumption and advertising budgets for sectors like handsets and e-commerce.

negative_highlights: Marmaxx comparable sales increased only 1% and were below expectations, driven by a small decrease in customer transactions.
Adjusted SG&A was unfavorable by 20 basis points versus last year due to incremental store wage and payroll costs.
Full-year adjusted gross margin guidance is down 40-50 bps for the back half primarily due to higher fuel costs.
positive_highlights: Consolidated comparable sales increased 4%, driven by higher average basket size across all banners except Marmaxx.
HomeGoods delivered an outstanding 7% comp sales increase, while TJX Canada and International divisions grew comps by 6%-7%.
Adjusted pre-tax profit margin expanded to 11.9%, up 50 basis points versus last year due to merchandise margin favorability from tariff changes.
summary: TJX reported Q2 FY2027 adjusted diluted EPS of $1.22 (up 11% YoY) and consolidated comparable sales growth of 4%, both significantly above plan despite a miss at the Marmaxx division which was attributed to self-inflicted execution issues regarding merchandise mix. Management raised full-year guidance for pre-tax profit margin, gross margin, and EPS, citing strong performance in HomeGoods (7% comp), TJX Canada (6%), and International divisions offsetting the weaker US apparel results.

negative_highlights: Management maintained full-year revenue guidance despite Q2 strength, indicating caution regarding H2 seasonality or potential Lantheus TruVu launch impacts.
R&D investment increased significantly to AUD $130 million (up from prior periods) as the company prioritizes late-stage clinical programs over maximizing near-term earnings.
positive_highlights: Precision medicine revenue grew 27% YoY with gross margins expanding 100 bps to 65% due to pricing discipline and manufacturing efficiencies.
BiPASS study enrollment is proceeding rapidly, with the Melbourne site alone enrolling a significant proportion of patients before other sites opened.
Zircaix received Breakthrough Therapy designation in the U.S. and remains on track for resubmission following an administrative FDA delay.
