GPU fleet grew 224% to 3,088, and the company signed 21 new contracts totaling $169.7M, bringing total signed contract value to $282.5M. Operating loss widened to $7.7M from $2.2M YoY due to higher D&A, while adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed sequentially to $0.8M. Management did not reaffirm the $300M ARR target but noted they are not demand constrained, with land/power being the primary gating factor.

negative_highlights: AI application segment revenue growth slowed to 3.9% from 17% in Q1, with B2B project work dampening growth.
Gross margin declined YoY to 46.3% due to semiconductor supply cost increases and business mix changes.
Middle East demand remains paused due to military conflict, and North America shows price sensitivity from supply-chain price increases.
positive_highlights: Total revenue growth accelerated to 16% YoY, up from 8.3% in Q1.
PaaS revenue grew 16.9% to $67.9M, with 318 premium customers contributing 89.5% of PaaS revenue.
Smart home and robot products revenue grew 23.2% to $13.5M, driven by smart security and energy demand.
summary: Tuya reported Q2 2026 revenue of $92.9M, up 16% YoY, accelerating from 8.3% in Q1. PaaS revenue grew 16.9% to $67.9M, while AI application and other segments grew only 3.9% to $11.5M. Blended gross margin was 46.3%, with PaaS margin at 46.8%, down YoY due to semiconductor cost increases. Non-GAAP operating margin held at 10.3%, and net cash from operations was $6.2M. Management expects gradual demand recovery with continued growth, but did not provide specific guidance.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA margin guidance was lowered to 6-9% from prior 'more than 12%' for the full year.
Gross margin was 21.2%, lower than expected due to lower scale and a mix shift toward China, with expectations for reversal in H2.
H1 operating cash flow was an outflow of EUR 29.3 million, driven by EUR 26 million of working capital investment; working capital rose to about 14% of LTM sales.
positive_highlights: Q2 revenue rose to EUR 27.8 million from EUR 18.2 million in Q1, and equipment revenues surged to EUR 39.4 million in H1 2026 from EUR 10.7 million in H1 2025.
Order intake reached EUR 52.3 million in the last eight weeks and EUR 96.6 million year-to-date, with guidance raised to EUR 125-150 million and management expecting the upper half.
Order backlog reached a record EUR 89 million, with most 2026 orders flowing into 2027 and a strong second-half and 2027 outlook.
summary: Schmid's H1 2026 revenue rose to EUR 46.0 million from a weak prior-year half, with equipment revenues jumping to EUR 39.4 million from EUR 10.7 million. Order intake accelerated sharply to EUR 96.6 million year-to-date, including EUR 52.3 million in the last eight weeks, leading management to raise full-year order intake guidance to EUR 125-150 million and expect the upper half. However, adjusted EBITDA margin guidance was cut to 6-9% from prior >12%, reflecting lower scale and margin mix; revenue guidance of at least EUR 100 million was maintained. The balance sheet was repaired via a EUR 30.75 million debt-to-equity swap and EUR 33 million raised, with total debt reduced from EUR 53 million to about EUR 23 million.

negative_highlights: Gross loss of $2.37 million and operating loss of $4.6 million due to expanded cost base before utilization ramped.
Cash position of only $2.85 million, and company acknowledges need for additional capital.
Revenue guidance of $5 million for 2026 requires significant ramp, with only $949,000 recognized in H1 and revenue recognition criteria still pending.
positive_highlights: Committed customer orders of $3.1 million as of August 16, with $2.1 million already invoiced, indicating commercial traction across both sites.
Expanded U.S. clinical manufacturing engagement with $650,000 in cash payments/advances received after June 30.
Revenue grew 22.8% year-over-year to $949,000 in H1 2026 from $773,000 in H1 2025.
summary: Scinai reported H1 FY2026 revenue of approximately $949,000, up from $773,000 in H1 FY2025, but posted a gross loss of $2.37 million and an operating loss of $4.6 million as the expanded CDMO footprint added costs before utilization ramped. A $6.4 million non-cash bargain purchase gain from the Recipharm acquisition led to reported net income of $1.57 million, which management stressed does not reflect operating profitability. As of June 30, cash and restricted cash were $2.85 million. Management reiterated the $5 million CDMO revenue objective for 2026 and highlighted $3.1 million in committed customer orders as of August 16, with $2.1 million already invoiced.

negative_highlights: Memory availability is tight and prices have increased, with potential industry-wide cost pressure.
SOM margins in Europe may be slightly more challenged than U.S. business.
GAAP net loss of $269,000 in Q4, though improved from prior year.
positive_highlights: Unmanned systems revenue reached $12.6 million in FY2026, above the midpoint of guidance, and is expected to reach $25 million-plus in FY2027.
Gross margin expanded to 44.1% non-GAAP, up from 40.6% YoY, with guidance for stability or modest improvement.
Completed Nero acquisition, adding ~$5 million ARR revenue with gross margins in the mid-to-high 60s, and increased software/services mix above 10%.
summary: Lantronix reported Q4 FY2026 revenue of $31.2 million, up 8% YoY, with non-GAAP EPS of $0.04, a 300% increase YoY. Embedded IoT solutions grew 34% YoY, and unmanned systems revenue reached $12.6 million for the fiscal year, above guidance. The company issued Q1 FY2027 guidance of $31-33 million revenue and $0.04-$0.06 non-GAAP EPS, and expects double-digit revenue growth for the full year. Net cash was $60 million, and the company closed the Nero acquisition for $11.7 million.

negative_highlights: Sephora at Kohl's sales declined 4% due to expanded distribution of key brands, and management expects this softness to persist.
Women's business declined 1.5%, with underperformance in intimates and proprietary brand note-through constraints.
Management remains cautious on consumer demand, citing pressure on low-to-middle income customers.
positive_highlights: Comparable sales improved sequentially to -0.9% from -1.0% in Q1, with Kohl's Card sales up 1%.
Gross margin expanded 305 basis points in Q2, partly due to tariff refunds.
Marketplace GMV grew 88% in the quarter and 75% year-to-date.
summary: Kohl's reported Q2 FY2026 comp sales down 0.9% (improving from Q1's -1.0% and prior year's -5.1%), with net income of $151 million and EPS of $1.28, beating guidance. Gross margin expanded 305 bps, but excluding $150 million in tariff refunds, it was roughly flat. The company raised its full-year comp guidance to -1.5% to flat, and adjusted EPS to $1.80-$2.40, which includes a $0.65 tariff benefit. Management noted a challenging consumer environment and Sephora headwinds, but highlighted strength in proprietary brands, home, and kids, and announced a resumption of share repurchases.

negative_highlights: Fiscal 2027 production forecast down ~2% in North America and ~6% at top three customers
FX headwinds: peso at 16.90 vs. $18 average last year, a 5% peso change could swing manufacturing costs ~$4M
Q4 GAAP EPS fell to $0.95 from $2.01, impacted by transformation costs and $2.9M discrete tax adjustments
positive_highlights: Record annual revenue of $579.4M, up 2.5% YoY, with full-year gross margin expanding 150 bps to 16.5%
Full-year adjusted EBITDA up 15% to $50.5M, margin improving 100 bps to 8.7%
Q4 sales beat initial guidance (flat vs. expected down 3%-4%), and $40M new buyback authorized
summary: Q4 FY2026 sales were $151.8M, flat YoY and better than the guided down 3%-4%, with adjusted EPS of $2.06 unchanged YoY. Full-year revenue rose 2.5% to a record $579.4M, gross margin expanded 150 bps to 16.5%, and operating cash flow was $46.3M, ending with $108.2M cash and no debt. Fiscal 2027 guidance is cautious: North American production expected down ~2% and top-three customers down ~6%, with FX headwinds but partial offsets from pricing and cost actions. Management reiterated long-term gross margin target of 18%-20% and a new $40M buyback authorization.

negative_highlights: Second-half gross margin guidance of 55%-56% implies a step-down from Q2's 57.5%, due to temporary benefit from low-duty inventory.
Higher shipping costs partially offset margin gains in Q2.
Middle East sales declined due to regional headwinds and reduced international tourism.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EPS more than doubled to $0.54 from $0.23, including $0.11 from IEEPA refunds.
Gross margin improved 340 bps excluding IEEPA refunds to 57.5%, driven by channel/product mix and pricing actions.
Sales grew 4.9% with strong international growth in Latin America and India, and U.S. note-through increases.
summary: Q2 FY2027 sales rose 4.9% to $169.8M, in line with prior momentum. Adjusted EPS climbed to $0.54 from $0.23, including a $0.11 benefit from IEEPA duty refunds; excluding refunds, gross margin expanded 340 bps to 57.5% on mix and pricing. Management discontinued annual guidance but expects mid-single-digit top-line growth and 55%-56% gross margin in the second half. The company maintained a strong balance sheet with $211.6M cash and no debt, and returned over $16M via dividends year-to-date.

negative_highlights: Business user growth was negatively impacted by 4,000 churn from IWG and a small correction.
Product and other gross margin remained negative at -25% (or -30% excluding tariff recovery).
Cash and investments declined to $17.5 million, with $47 million debt remaining.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 25% YoY to $83.2 million, with business subscription and services revenue up 38% YoY.
Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to 15% of revenue, up from 10% six quarters ago.
Residential users grew by over 3,000, reversing historical decline, driven by MyPhone launch.
summary: Ooma reported Q2 FY2027 revenue of $83.2 million, up 25% YoY, with non-GAAP net income of $10.2 million and adjusted EBITDA of $12.4 million, up 58% and 74% respectively. AirDial services revenue grew 75% YoY, and business subscription and services revenue grew 38% YoY. The company raised full-year revenue guidance to $332-$333.5 million and non-GAAP EPS to $1.35-$1.38, reflecting stronger AirDial momentum and positive residential growth from MyPhone.

negative_highlights: Revenue slumped 31% YoY and gross margin collapsed to 4.2% from 8.3% sequentially, with net loss widening and operating loss margin at -11.6%.
Full-year module shipment guidance was cut to 60–70 GW (from an implied higher prior target), reflecting a deliberate shift away from scale toward profitability.
Operating expenses jumped 21% sequentially due to higher expected credit losses; cash and equivalents fell from $3.3B to $2.5B during the quarter.
positive_highlights: Module shipments grew sequentially to ~16 GW in Q2, and high-efficiency Tiger Neo 3.0 modules command a ~$0.01/W premium.
Gross margin improved 1.3 points YoY to 4.2%; operating cash flow turned positive in Q2 (improvement vs. prior quarter).
ESS shipments in H1 2026 were 3.1 GWh, more than doubling YoY, and the annual target remains unchanged; also, portfolio investments generated ~CNY 490M gains in H1.
summary: Q2 2026 total revenue fell 31% YoY to $1.82B, with gross margin contracting to 4.2% from 8.3% sequentially and operating loss margin at 11.6% (vs. 4.8% in Q1). Net loss expanded, driven by lower module ASPs, higher expected credit losses, and ramp-up costs for new capacity. Management lowered full-year 2026 module shipment guidance to 60–70 GW from prior levels and expects Q3 shipments of 15–17 GW, while maintaining that ESS shipments will more than double, although ESS revenue recognition remains in early stages. The tone is cautiously optimistic about ASP recovery and cost improvements in Q3, but acknowledges significant market headwinds from trade barriers and soft China demand.

negative_highlights: Chinese Mainland NBP decreased 4% in H1, with accelerated par mix shift compressing margins; full-year NBP expected to be similar to 2025 (i.e., no growth).
Chinese Mainland bancassurance volumes fell in Q2 due to new expense regulations, with a high Q3 comparator; guidance implies recovery only from September.
Experience variances were negative $27 million (vs. +$24 million in H1 2025), reflecting increased capability investment and startup costs.
positive_highlights: Group NBP grew 8% (10% ex-China), with strong performances in Hong Kong (+8%, margin up 7 points), Malaysia (+46%), and ASEAN (+13%).
Bancassurance NBP up 13% (18% ex-China), and management expects to hit the 2027 bancassurance objective a year early in 2026.
Underlying operating variances turned positive at $32 million for the first time since 2020, and gross OFSG grew 15% to $1.8 billion; buyback increased by ~$300 million to ~$1.5 billion for 2026.
summary: Prudential reported Q2 FY2026 new business profit of $1.4 billion, up 8% (10% ex-China), with adjusted operating EPS up 17%, gross OFSG up 15% to $1.8 billion, and dividend per share up 15%. Group NBP margin improved 2 points to 40%, with bancassurance NBP up 13% (18% ex-China) and health up 15%; Hong Kong NBP grew 8%, Malaysia 46%. Chinese Mainland NBP fell 4% due to expense regulations and a shift to participating products, with full-year NBP guided to be similar to 2025. The company reaffirmed double-digit 2026 growth guidance for NBP, adjusted EPS, gross OFSG, and DPS, and increased the 2026 buyback by ~$300 million to ~$1.5 billion.

negative_highlights: Average billing contract duration in Q4 was 3.3 years, slightly below expectations.
Supply chain constraints are expected to persist through FY2027, with higher percentage of future start-date orders assumed in guidance.
FY2027 free cash flow margin guidance of 28% at midpoint is flat YoY, partly due to restructuring charges and increased payment flexibility.
positive_highlights: Q4 revenue of $757M exceeded guidance high end of $745M; non-GAAP op margin of 26.2% beat guidance of 21%-23%.
FY2026 ARR grew 16% YoY to $2.549B, with net new ARR the highest in recent quarters.
External storage and NC2 bookings saw sharp QoQ increases, with seven-figure ACV deals in both areas.
summary: Q4 FY2026 revenue was $757M, above guidance of $725M-$745M, with non-GAAP operating margin of 26.2% versus guided 21%-23%. ARR grew 16% YoY to $2.549B, and FY2026 revenue grew 12% to $2.854B. For FY2027, the company guides revenue of $3.18B-$3.23B (12% YoY growth at midpoint), non-GAAP operating margin of 24%-25%, and free cash flow of $850M-$950M, while assuming continued supply chain constraints and increasing future start-date orders.

negative_highlights: Dealership MAU declined slightly QoQ, reflecting dealer closures; industry pressure persists with used car prices falling 10%-15% in two months and over 70% of dealers operating at a loss.
Incremental revenue carried lower gross margin, causing cost of revenue to grow faster than revenue.
Company declined to provide business outlook or quantify AI monetization targets, citing early stage.
positive_highlights: Adjusted net loss narrowed 61.5% YoY to RMB 7.4 million, driven by OPEX reductions (G&A down 14%, S&M down 14%, R&D down 29% ex-SBC).
AI adoption: over 4,100 dealerships using AI tools by June, 150 million tokens/day, 3,215 paying deployments of social media operations specialist, 295 paying deployments of management assistant.
Revenue increased 3.7% YoY and 14% sequentially, with stable used car business and growth from OEM software services.
summary: In Q2 FY2026, DSC revenue grew 3.7% YoY (14% QoQ), with adjusted net loss narrowing 61.5% to RMB 7.2 million from RMB 19.2 million (adjusted net loss was RMB 7.4 million per CFO, slight discrepancy). GAAP net loss was RMB 240.5 million including RMB 227.8 million IPO-related share-based compensation. Operating metrics: over 65,000 dealership MAU, near 200,000 user MAU, revenue from over 9,000 dealers, average revenue per dealer over RMB 6,600, 214,000 monetized transactions at RMB 259 per transaction. No guidance provided; management emphasized cautious, staged investment in AI and overseas expansion.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined 3.7% YoY, with marketing services down 10.7% YoY
Gross margin contracted to 57% from 62.5% a year ago
Adjusted net loss swung from a profit of CNY 91.3 million to a loss of CNY 10.3 million
positive_highlights: Sequential revenue growth of 5.9%, with content and IP revenue up 4.4% YoY
IP licensing revenue surged 600% YoY and 105% sequentially
Total operating expenses declined 13% YoY, with R&D down 25.4% and G&A down 22.7%
summary: In Q2 FY2026, Zhihu reported total revenue of CNY 690.1 million, down 3.7% year-over-year but up 5.9% sequentially. Adjusted net loss was CNY 10.3 million, versus adjusted net income of CNY 91.3 million in the same period of 2025. Marketing services revenue fell 10.7% YoY to CNY 199 million, while content and IP revenue rose 4.4% YoY to CNY 425.9 million. Management noted that marketing services remain in structural recovery and that IP operations will face project timing and industry filing hurdles, while new AI initiatives are still being validated for scalable revenue.

negative_highlights: Communications segment adjusted EBITDA margin declined 134 bps to 13.6%, driven by scaling investments, wireless deferral, and higher fuel costs.
Wireless program deferral of approximately $150 million of revenues from FY2027 to FY2028, causing a slight decline in Communications margin outlook for the year.
Communications organic growth expected to decelerate in second half, with Q3 revenue guidance implying lower growth versus Q2.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA margin improved 81 bps to 15.7% with strong Building Systems margin of 24.5%.
Free cash flow trailing 12-month increased nearly 200% year-over-year; DSOs improved seven days to 101 days.
summary: Q2 FY2027 revenue was a record $2.01 billion, up 45.6% year-over-year and 16.7% organic; adjusted EBITDA was $315.5 million, up 53.5% and above guidance; adjusted EPS was $5.29, up 45.3% and above guidance. Communications organic growth was 16.7% but segment adjusted EBITDA margin fell 134 bps to 13.6% on investment costs, wireless deferral, and higher fuel costs. Building Systems revenue was $397.5 million, with adjusted EBITDA margin of 24.5%, and backlog hit a record $12.2 billion at 1.2x book-to-bill. Company raised full-year revenue outlook to $7.48-$7.66 billion, but is also deferring $150 million of wireless revenues into FY2028.

negative_highlights: R&D segment experiencing S-curve transitions as old products mature and new products are early
Falcon product still in early adoption, with only five early adopters and first go-lives expected this year
Some customers migrating to Salesforce, but Veeva sees potential win-backs in 2027-2028
positive_highlights: Total revenue of $928 million, above guidance
Commercial subscription revenue grew 13% year-over-year, excluding Crossix
Two top-20 biopharma wins for Vault CRM (Lilly, Biogen) plus Regeneron
summary: Veeva reported Q2 FY2027 revenue of $928 million, ahead of guidance, with non-GAAP operating income of $416 million. Commercial subscription revenue grew 13% year-over-year, driven by broad-based strength. The company reported two top-20 biopharma wins for Vault CRM, raising full-year guidance. Management highlighted strong demand for Falcon, but noted early adoption and product readiness as near-term constraints.

negative_highlights: Customer spending from AI companies up 435% year-over-year, but not all customers are upgrading yet; only 5% of knowledge workers upgraded to premium editions.
Headless monetization is still being figured out, with management acknowledging they are 'trapped in old per-user pricing models'.
Management noted that many customers have not started AI transformations, indicating limited penetration beyond early adopters.
positive_highlights: Net new AOV growth strongest in four years, outpacing AOV growth.
Free cash flow $1.1 billion, up 81% year-over-year.
Agentforce ARR hit $1.5 billion; AI/data ARR nearing $4 billion.
summary: Salesforce reported record revenue and EPS, with CRPO up ~14% and free cash flow of $1.1 billion, up 81% year-over-year. Net new AOV growth was the strongest in four years, Agentforce ARR reached $1.5 billion, and AI/data ARR is approaching $4 billion. The company raised FY2027 revenue guidance by about $300 million in constant currency and announced a partnership with Anthropic to launch Claudeforce. Management expressed strong confidence in re-accelerating organic revenue in H2, backed by record pipeline and continued hiring of AEs.

negative_highlights: Gross margin declined 160 bps YoY to 45.5%, driven by 230 bps of merchandise margin pressure from tariffs.
The company cited ongoing volatile environment including war, changing tariffs, rising interest rates, and macro uncertainty, with no housing recovery assumed in guidance.
No share repurchases in Q2 despite $1.1 billion remaining in authorizations.
positive_highlights: Acceleration in comp to 6.2% from 4.8% in Q1, with all brands positive and industry essentially flat, implying broad market share gains.
Raised full-year guidance on both top and bottom lines: comps to 4%-6.5% (from 2%-6%) and operating margin to 17.8%-18.2% (up from prior).
B2B grew 14.5% to a record volume quarter, with contract up 20% and trade up 12%.
summary: Q2 FY2026 (calendar Q2) net revenues were $1.96 billion, up 6.7% YoY, with comparable brand revenue growth accelerating to 6.2% from 4.8% in Q1. All brands posted positive comps, including Pottery Barn up 5.1%, Williams Sonoma up 7.6%, West Elm up 6.4%, and B2B up 14.5%. Non-GAAP operating margin was 17.3% and non-GAAP EPS was $2.10, up 5% YoY, despite peak tariff pressure. Management raised full-year guidance: comp growth now 4%-6.5% (up from 2%-6%) and operating margin 17.8%-18.2% (up from prior range), with the raise driven by operational strength rather than IEEPA tariff refunds.

negative_highlights: Fuel surcharges related to Middle East conflict negatively impacted IMU by 50 bps and outbound delivery/freight by 20 bps; expected to continue for the rest of the year
Anthropologie comp slowed to 3% from 2% in Q1, with elevated markdowns during Q2; management aiming for low-to-mid single digit comps in Q3
Tariffs remain a headwind in Q2, though expected to ease in the second half
positive_highlights: Record Q2 sales of $1.7 billion, up 10% YoY; EPS of $1.72, up 9% YoY
Nuuly revenue grew 29% to $179 million with operating income margin of 10% for the first time; average active subscribers up 30% to 484,000
FP Group delivered 15% revenue growth with a 10% retail segment comp; FP Movement grew 26% with 13% comp
summary: URBN delivered record Q2 FY2027 results with net sales up 10% to $1.7 billion and EPS up 9% to $1.72, marking the eighth consecutive quarter of record sales and profits. All retail brands posted positive comps, with Nuuly revenue up 29% to $179 million and operating income margin reaching 10% for the first time. Management guided Q3 total sales growth in the high single digits and reaffirmed full-year high single-digit sales growth, with gross margin expected to improve 25-50 bps in Q3. The company also highlighted a favorable tariff environment for the second half and continued strong consumer demand.

negative_highlights: Net sales declined 2.3% YoY, with store sales down 5.4% due to lower clearance inventory and channel shift to digital.
Store traffic remains pressured, and management expects no macro improvement in the back half.
Body care declined mid-single digits, though improved sequentially; full-year gross margin expected down to 43.3%.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EPS of $0.62 beat guidance of $0.20-$0.25; excluding $80M tariff refunds, EPS of $0.31 was still $0.06 above the high end.
Digital channel returned to growth, up 3% YoY, with improvements in new, existing, and reactivated customers.
Amazon net sales more than tripled sequentially, and Fruit Fusion launch exceeded sales expectations with higher AUR.
summary: Net sales declined 2.3% to $1.5B, ahead of the down 5%-3% guidance, with adjusted EPS of $0.62 exceeding the $0.20-$0.25 range, aided by $80M tariff refunds. Excluding refunds, adjusted EPS was $0.31, above the high end. Management narrowed FY net sales guidance to down 4%-2.5% and raised FY adjusted EPS to $2.60-$2.80. Digital returned to growth, up 3%, and Amazon sales more than tripled sequentially, though store traffic and body care remain pressured.

negative_highlights: Net revenue fell 31.6% YoY to RMB 3.57 billion; non-GAAP net profit fell 75.4% YoY to RMB 455 million, partly due to a one-off tax expense of ~RMB 500 million.
C-M2 for August expected to rise ~25% sequentially; risk deterioration may take two to three quarters to resolve.
Q3 guidance of RMB 400-500 million non-GAAP net income implies a 67-73% YoY decline; management expects funding costs to rise ~25bps already seen in July-August.
positive_highlights: Risk metrics improved in Q2: C-M2 fell 17% sequentially to 0.66%, 30-day collection rate rose 2.3pp to 88.1%, and 90-day delinquency fell from 3.5% to 2.83%.
Tech solutions business grew sharply: loan volume up 515% YoY to RMB 10.5 billion, outstanding balance up 313% to RMB 16.1 billion.
Funding costs declined ~10bps sequentially, with ABS issuance up 90% to RMB 5.5 billion and issuance costs down ~20bps.
summary: Q2 2026 net revenue was RMB 3.57 billion, down from RMB 3.91 billion in Q1 and RMB 5.22 billion a year ago, with non-GAAP net profit of RMB 455 million versus RMB 946 million in Q1 and RMB 1.85 billion a year ago. The company guided Q3 non-GAAP net income between RMB 400-500 million, implying a 67-73% YoY decline. Management cited a late-June industry liquidity crisis and a nationwide collections crackdown, causing a sharp reversal in risk metrics in August with C-M2 expected to rise ~25% sequentially. They plan to maintain strict risk controls, expecting volume not to return to Q2 levels for two to three quarters.

negative_highlights: Industrial Solutions pre-tax margin fell 450 bps YoY, pressured by Facet costs, organic deleveraging, and power generation disruptions
Power generation gross margin hit by ~40 bps due to Mexico plant stabilization; full recovery not expected until mid-fiscal 2027
IFS new equipment volumes declined 2% YoY on dust collection weakness; aerospace & defense organic sales fell 3%
positive_highlights: Q4 sales surpassed $1 billion for the first time, up 8% YoY with record operating and gross margins (17.5% and 36.7%, respectively)
Mobile Solutions pre-tax margin hit a record 21.3%, up 220 bps YoY on aftermarket strength; China sales up 27%
Fiscal 2027 guidance calls for record sales of $4.1B (up 7.5%), EPS of $4.22-$4.38 (up 8% at midpoint), and 90 bps operating margin expansion
summary: Donaldson reported a record Q4 FY2026 with sales surpassing $1 billion for the first time (up 8% YoY), adjusted EPS of $1.15 (up 12%), and operating margin of 17.5% (up 110 bps). Fiscal 2027 guidance implies record sales over $4.1 billion (up 7.5% at midpoint), EPS of $4.22-$4.38 including $0.12 Facet dilution, and operating margin expansion of 90 bps to 16.9%. Management highlighted robust demand, improved operational efficiency, and growth across all segments, but noted continued pressure in power generation and industrial first-fit softness.

negative_highlights: Cash equity take rate fell sharply from 5.9 bps to 3.6 bps, primarily due to zero-commission trading in the US and higher-priced stocks.
Operating costs jumped 47% YoY, with marketing spend up 87% YoY and employee comp up 39% due to severance costs.
Effective tax rate spiked to ~28% due to non-deductible penalty costs and deferred tax adjustments; normalized is expected at 10-15%.
positive_highlights: Total revenue reached an all-time high of $182 million, up 31.4% YoY, with record quarter.
Client assets grew in every market; Hong Kong assets up ~30% QoQ, Australia/NZ up >30%, US up ~50%.
New funded accounts rose 12.7% QoQ to 32,600, with average net asset inflow per new funded user of ~$25,000 in Q3 QTD.
summary: UP Fintech reported record total revenue of $182 million in Q2 2026, up 31.4% YoY and 17.7% QoQ, with GAAP net income of $39.4 million and non-GAAP net income of $42.8 million, returning to profitability from a Q1 loss (which included a $59.7 million one-off penalty). Commission income was $78.3 million, interest income $79.8 million. Operating costs rose 47% YoY, with marketing up 87%, comps up 39%. Mainland retail client assets have fallen to under 10% of total, and revenue contribution dropped to a 15-20% range; management expects Q3 client assets to grow high single-digits, but trading activity is running slightly below Q2 levels.

negative_highlights: Component repair organic growth was only 5%, impacted by supply chain bottlenecks and a deliberate shift to lower-revenue but higher-margin PMA repairs
Expectation of $70-75M operating cash flow drag in Q4 from a legacy estate payment
Working capital will continue to be a use of cash as the company invests in inventory to meet backlog
positive_highlights: Consolidated net sales up 23% YoY to a record $1.41B, with net income up 33% to $235.4M
ETG sales up 36% and FSG sales up 18%, with operating margins expanding to 26.0% and 25.9% respectively
Operating cash flow up 49% to $345.3M, representing ~150% of net income
summary: HEICO reported record Q3 FY2026 results: consolidated net sales up 23% to $1,413.1M, operating income up 34% to $355.2M, and net income up 33% to $235.4M ($1.67 diluted EPS). Both segments delivered record sales and operating income with strong organic growth (FSG 12%, ETG 18%) and margin expansion (FSG operating margin 25.9%, ETG 26%). Cash flow from operations surged 49% to $345.3M, and the company strengthened its balance sheet with a $1.2B notes offering and expanded credit capacity to $3B. Management remains bullish on demand, citing strong backlogs and a robust acquisition pipeline, with no guidance change but continued optimism.

negative_highlights: Print revenue declined 2% YoY in a competitive market; supplies revenue down 4% in constant currency.
Expects Q4 margins to be 'low point' with PS margins pressured by rising input costs.
positive_highlights: Record Q3 revenue of $15.7B, up 13% YoY, with ninth consecutive quarter of top-line growth.
Personal Systems revenue grew 18% YoY to $11.8B, with double-digit growth in AI PCs and premium categories.
Raised FY2026 EPS guidance to $3.19-$3.29 and free cash flow outlook to $3.0-$3.2B.
summary: HP reported record Q3 FY2026 revenue of $15.7 billion, up 13% YoY, with non-GAAP EPS of $0.83, up 11%, including $0.11 of tariff refunds; even without that benefit, EPS exceeded guidance. Personal Systems revenue grew 18% to $11.8 billion, while Print declined 2%. Management raised FY2026 EPS guidance to $3.19-$3.29 (from $2.90-$3.10) and provided Q4 EPS guidance of $0.69-$0.79, with expectations of continued input cost pressure but improving margins into FY2027.

negative_highlights: Diagnostics and clinical grew 6%, below high single-digit guide.
Europe grew low single digits on tough compare; academic/government declined 3%.
Q4 ATD growth expected flattish due to tough compare.
positive_highlights: China grew 9% versus flat expectation, with double-digit pharma and food growth.
Q3 core growth 7.3%, 140 bps above guidance; ex-refund EPS $1.56 up 14% YoY.
GLP-1 revenue grew over 70% YoY; CDMO Advanced Therapeutics grew nearly 30%.
summary: Q3 FY2026 revenue was $1.88B, up 7.3% core, 140 bps above guidance; ex-refund EPS $1.56 beat by $0.06, operating margin ex-refund 27.2% up 210 bps YoY. China grew 9% vs flat, pharma up 12%, CDMO up nearly 30%. Full-year core growth guidance raised 65 bps to 5.8-6.0% and EPS ex-refund to $6.12-$6.15 (10% growth). Strong pricing (200 bps) and LC/GC replacement cycles drive momentum.

negative_highlights: Comparable sales were flat overall, with EMEA comparable sales down 4% and Hollister comparable sales down 3%
Hollister demand was constrained by inventory during the quarter, limiting sales growth to 2%
Freight costs are expected to offset tariff expense favorability in the back half
positive_highlights: Record Q2 net sales of $1.27 billion, up 5% YoY, above the 2%-4% guidance
EPS of $4.17 beat guidance of $1.80-$2.00 even after excluding the ~$1.75 tariff refund benefit
Raised full-year EPS guidance to $13.10-$13.60 from prior outlook, and buybacks to at least $500 million
summary: Abercrombie & Fitch reported Q2 FY2026 net sales of $1.27 billion, up 5% YoY, with operating margin of 19.9% and EPS of $4.17, beating its outlook. Results included a $100 million IEEPA tariff refund benefit; excluding this, EPS still beat guidance. The company raised full-year net sales growth to ~5% and EPS guidance to $13.10-$13.60 (including ~$2.10 refund benefit), and raised buyback plans to at least $500 million. Both Abercrombie and Hollister brands delivered record Q2 sales, with Abercrombie up 8% and Hollister up 2%, and APAC grew 19%.

negative_highlights: Core commissions fell 44.1% YoY and recurring management fees dropped 10.8% YoY in Q2, reflecting legacy run-off and continued revenue mix shift.
International segment net revenues declined 21.9% YoY in H1, driven by deliberate contraction of insurance and exit from legacy referral channels.
Overall client acquisition has yet to return to growth; regulatory headwinds heightened noticeably according to CFO.
positive_highlights: Operating margin expanded 9.2 percentage points YoY to 34.8% in Q2; half-year operating margin hit a record 36.3%.
Performance-based income (carry) reached RMB 238 million in H1 2026, up 364% YoY, with 63 consecutive quarters of Non-GAAP profitability.
US-dollar AUM grew 11.7% YoY to $6.5 billion while overseas RM headcount fell 36.2%, indicating early decoupling of asset growth from headcount.
summary: Q2 FY2026 net revenue was RMB 620 million, down 1.5% YoY, but operating income rose 34% YoY to RMB 216 million with an operating margin of 34.8%. Non-GAAP net income was RMB 238 million, up 25.9% YoY and 77.8% QoQ. First-half performance-based income surged 364% YoY to RMB 238 million, while US-dollar AUM grew 11.7% YoY to $6.5 billion despite overseas RM headcount declining 36.2%. Management maintained full-year operating margin guidance above 30% and emphasized the Singapore AI Wealth Management Department proof point (AUM from <$100M to >$400M, monthly profitability in July 2026) as evidence of a scalable model.

negative_highlights: Energy segment utilization only 50% due to one rig warm-stacked; Hercules not contributing revenue until H1 2027
Two car carrier newbuilds remain unchartered, exposing the company to market risk on spec orders
Dry bulk spot earnings remain marginal, with little aggregate revenue impact
positive_highlights: EBITDA rose 20% QoQ to $130 million; Suezmax spot TCE surged to $133k/day in Q2 vs $54k/day Q1
Charter backlog increased to $3.8 billion, with ~$233 million in new firm contracts added during the quarter
Raised $100 million in equity via ATM/DRIP at a premium to VWAP, with no further issuance planned
summary: SFL reported Q2 FY2026 revenues of $201 million (up from $174.5M Q1) and adjusted EBITDA of $130 million, up 20% QoQ. GAAP net income was $34 million ($0.25/share), with a declared dividend of $0.22/share, marking the 90th consecutive payout. The company added new car carrier charters and newbuilds, raising the charter backlog to $3.8 billion, and pointed to strong spot tanker earnings. Guidance was not formally issued, but management expressed confidence in continued cash flow visibility.

negative_highlights: Net loss of $1.93M vs profit of $16.39M last year, driven by a $20M+ FX swing
Same-store sales declined 0.8% YoY
North America and other regions saw turnover pressure; other-region revenue down 1.8%
positive_highlights: Operating profit up 118.9% YoY to $8.1M, with operating margin up 1.8 pp to 3.7%
Employee cost ratio improved ~1 pp YoY, and several fixed expense ratios declined
Delivery and other business revenue doubled, up 114.3% YoY to $21M, now 9.6% of revenue
summary: In Q2 FY2026, the company reported total revenue of $219M, up 10% YoY, with Haidilao restaurant revenue up 4.6% to $198M. Operating profit surged 118.9% to $8.1M, with operating margin expanding 1.8 pp to 3.7%, but net profit swung to a loss of $1.93M due to a $4.34M FX loss versus a $16.33M gain last year. Customer visits rose 5.2% to 8.1M, and table turnover improved to 3.9 turns, but same-store sales fell 0.8%. Management expects double-digit new store openings in H2, with a payback period of 3-4 years.

negative_highlights: Fiscal Q4 revenue guidance range of $207-$227 million implies potential sequential decline from Q3's $216 million; management widened the range due to persistent market uncertainty.
Mainstream IC revenue declined to $86 million due to node migration and competitive pressures in China.
Fiscal 2026 CapEx guidance lowered to $255-$305 million from $330 million due to timing of tool deliveries, with peak potentially shifting to 2027.
positive_highlights: Revenue of $216 million beat the high end of guidance, up 3% YoY and sequentially.
High-end IC revenue reached a record 44% of IC revenue, driven by node migration and improved conditions.
Operating cash flow of $76 million represented 35% of revenue; cash increased by $35 million to $673 million.
summary: Photronics reported fiscal Q3 2026 revenue of $216 million, up 3% year-over-year and sequentially, above the high end of guidance. IC revenue grew nearly 5% to $155 million, with high-end IC reaching a record 44% of IC revenue. GAAP EPS was $0.49, and non-GAAP EPS was $0.50. Operating cash flow was $76 million, and CapEx was $37 million. Management guided fiscal Q4 revenue between $207 million and $227 million, with operating margin of 19%-24% and non-GAAP EPS of $0.40-$0.56, while lowering fiscal 2026 CapEx guidance to $255-$305 million from $330 million due to timing.

negative_highlights: Backlog declined modestly quarter-over-quarter to $10.9 billion, though primarily due to the Processor IP divestiture.
Non-AI design activity only stabilized, not yet accelerating, in the last two quarters.
Multiphysics Fusion is not expected to contribute meaningfully to EDA growth until 2027.
positive_highlights: Q3 revenue, non-GAAP operating margin, and non-GAAP EPS all beat the high end of guidance; EDA grew 8.5% YoY against a tough 16% compare.
Full-year guidance raised: revenue +$50M, non-GAAP EPS +$0.31, FCF +$600M; EDA expected to deliver double-digit growth in Q4 and FY2026.
Design IP returned to growth (up 11% YoY), with die-to-die business on pace to double and 95%+ win rate in PCIe 7.0 opportunities.
summary: Synopsys reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $2.477 billion, up ~42% YoY, with non-GAAP EPS of $3.91 and operating margin of 41.6%, all exceeding guidance. EDA grew 8.5% YoY, design IP returned to growth (up 11% YoY), and Ansys contributed $711 million. The company raised full-year revenue guidance by $50 million to $9.69-$9.74 billion, non-GAAP EPS by $0.31 to $15.04-$15.10, and free cash flow guidance by $600 million to ~$2.6 billion. Management expects EDA growth to accelerate to double digits in Q4 and for the full year.

negative_highlights: NPL ratio deteriorated to 8.3% in Q2 from 7.7% in Q1, a 60 bps worsening
Loan growth revised down to 10-15% for the year, with peso lending expected to grow very little and most growth coming from dollar loans
Management noted NIM will face downward pressure as inflation and rates decline; full-year bank NIM guided to 16% from current ~17%
positive_highlights: Banco Galicia net income rose 211% sequentially on lower funding costs and higher financial instrument gains
Market share gains: loans up 69 bps to 15.1%, deposits up 42 bps to 14.3%
Management expects full-year bank cost of risk to decline to 8.3% from 9.3% currently, with NPLs improving to 6.3% by year-end
summary: Q2 2026 net income was ARS 258 billion, up 12% YoY, with ROAE of 11.3% and ROAA of 2.1%. Banco Galicia net income rose 211% QoQ and 21% YoY on lower funding costs, improved financial instrument results, and lower provisions. Management guided to full-year ROE around 10-12%, loan growth of 10-15% (mostly dollar-denominated), bank NPL ratio improving to 6.3% by year-end, and bank cost of risk at 8.3% for the full year, from 9.3% currently. NPLs deteriorated to 8.3% in Q2 from 7.7% in Q1, but coverage improved to 92.8%.

negative_highlights: Operating cash flow was negative $136M due to strategic component purchases to secure supply for core demand; free cash flow was negative $238M, with FY2027 FCF guidance of $600-800M implying recovery in H2.
Product gross margin remained at 66.2%, at the low end of the 65-70% range; management expects to stay there to drive share gains until component costs stabilize.
Hyperscale revenue contribution was only de minimis in Q2, with the majority expected in H2, and revenue growth from this segment not yet reflected in financials.
positive_highlights: Revenue growth of 38% YoY exceeded guidance, with product revenue up 54% and operating profit up 77% to $230M; both metrics above the high end of guidance.

Full-year FY2027 revenue guidance raised by >$500M at midpoint to $5.0-5.7B, representing 38% YoY growth (up from prior ~25% YoY); operating profit guidance raised by $110M to $940-960M (50% YoY growth).

Second top-5 hyperscaler design win and supply agreement announced; hyperscale revenue expected to grow significantly in Q3 and Q4 FY2027, with large order commitments extending into calendar 2028 (tens of exabytes).
summary: Everpure Q2 FY2027 revenue rose 38% YoY to $1.186B, exceeding guidance; operating profit surged 77% to $230M with a 19.4% operating margin. Product revenue grew 54% to $687M, while subscription services revenue increased 20% to $499M; Evergreen//One TCV run rate surpassed $1B. The company raised full-year FY2027 revenue guidance to $5.0-5.7B (38% YoY growth at midpoint, up from prior ~25% YoY) and operating profit to $940-960M (50% growth at midpoint). Management cited a second top-5 hyperscaler design win for DirectFlash with revenue expected to materialize in FY2028, ongoing pricing power, and strong demand despite supply constraints.

negative_highlights: AI product contribution remains immaterial to overall revenue in FY2027, with management expecting materiality only in 2028 and beyond.
Professional services revenue decreased to approximately 1% of total revenue, reflecting a deliberate shift to GSI partners.
Full-year revenue growth guidance of 10-11% implies no acceleration, and management remains cautious on near-term AI-driven upside.
positive_highlights: Record Q2 bookings, with pipeline conversion and deal expansions driving acceleration in ACV growth.
New products represented approximately 30% of bookings, with Okta for AI Agents closing a multimillion-dollar deal with a Fortune 50 healthcare company.
Over 20% growth in $1M+ ACV customers, reaching over 600 such customers.
summary: Okta reported Q2 FY2027 revenue growth of 10% YoY and a record Q2 bookings quarter, with 30% of bookings from new products and over 600 customers with $1M+ ACV. Current RPO growth accelerated to 11-12% for Q3 guidance, and full-year revenue growth guidance was maintained at 10-11%, with non-GAAP operating margin of 26%. AI-related products, including Okta for AI Agents, are still small but contributed multiple million-dollar deals, and management expressed confidence in secular demand for identity security, especially with AI agent governance.

negative_highlights: Third-quarter bookings secured to date average $38,600 per day, well below Q2 average of $59,301, indicating a potential sequential slowdown.
Geopolitical tensions and Strait of Hormuz disruptions create uncertainty, with oil flows still roughly 10% below pre-conflict levels as of July.
Operating expenses per day rose to $8,315, driven by higher crew change and consumable costs.
positive_highlights: Q2 TCE earnings of $512 million doubled year-over-year from $208 million, with EBITDA of $416 million versus $127 million.
Full-year TCE guidance midpoint raised from $1.3 billion to $1.5 billion, with EBITDA guidance increased to $1.0-$1.2 billion.
Fleetwide average TCE of $59,301 per day more than doubled year-over-year; LR2 rates hit approximately $67,000 per day.
summary: TORM reported record Q2 2026 results with TCE earnings of $512 million, more than doubling from $208 million in the prior year, and net profit of $338 million versus $59 million. Fleetwide average TCE reached $59,301 per day, with LR2s at approximately $67,000 per day. The company raised full-year TCE guidance midpoint from $1.3 billion to $1.5 billion, now expecting $1.4-$1.6 billion, and increased EBITDA guidance to $1.0-$1.2 billion. An interim dividend of $2.40 per share was approved, and the company continues fleet renewal with newbuild deliveries planned through 2029.

negative_highlights: Free cash flow margin guidance for Q3 is 27.5%, below the full-year target of at least 30%
XM Cyber acquisition will not contribute ARR or revenue in FY2027, potentially limiting near-term growth
GAAP net income was only $5M, reflecting ongoing stock-based compensation and other non-cash costs
positive_highlights: Net new ARR of $333M beat guidance by >$45M, up 51% YoY
FY2027 net new ARR guidance raised by 630 bps to 34% growth, a $116M increase from initial outlook
Falcon Flex ending ARR surpassed $2.29B, up 101% YoY, with >935 new Flex accounts in Q2
summary: CrowdStrike reported record Q2 FY2027 net new ARR of $333M, up 51% YoY and beating guidance by over $45M. Total revenue was $1.47B, up 26% YoY, with non-GAAP operating income of $372M (25% margin) and record free cash flow of $377M (26% of revenue). Management raised FY2027 net new ARR guidance by 630 basis points to ~34% YoY growth, citing sustained AI-driven demand and record pipeline.

negative_highlights: Vehicle margin fell sharply to 9.4% from 19.4% YoY, with gross margin down to 11% from 20.1% YoY
Net loss of RMB 1.7 billion, a reversal from net income of RMB 1.1 billion in the same period last year
Management acknowledged cost headwinds from batteries and memory chips, and decided not to pass price increases to customers, pressuring near-term margins
positive_highlights: Sequential revenue growth of 11.7% QoQ and gross margin expansion from 7.9% to 11% QoQ
Operating cash flow turned nearly positive at RMB 15 million in Q2, a significant improvement from -RMB 6.1 billion in Q1
In-house Mach M100 chip shipments exceeded 50,000 units, and BEV and EREV each accounted for 50% of sales
summary: Li Auto's Q2 2026 revenue was RMB 25.7 billion, down 15.1% YoY but up 11.7% QoQ; vehicle margin fell to 9.4% from 19.4% YoY, and the company reported a net loss of RMB 1.7 billion. Management guided Q3 deliveries to 95,000-100,000 vehicles with revenue of RMB 26.6-28 billion, reflecting cautious optimism amid cost pressures. The company acknowledged commodity cost inflation and margin pressures but maintained focus on in-house technology and new product launches.

negative_highlights: Net loss of $44.7 million was heavily impacted by a ~$35.7 million decline in AVAX fair value due to market pressure.
Bitcoin and broader digital asset indices faced significant headwinds, with Bitcoin down approximately 50% since October.
The quarter represents the initial reporting period as a public company, meaning historical comparables are unavailable.
positive_highlights: Core general and administrative expenses were low at $3.5 million, indicating lean operations post-merger.
Staking revenue reached $1.5 million in the quarter, generating recurring yield on the treasury.
The board approved a $10 million share repurchase plan to create shareholder value.
summary: AVAT reported a net loss of $44.7 million ($1.54 per share) for Q2 FY2026, driven by roughly $35.7 million in market-driven losses on AVAX holdings and $15.2 million in one-time business combination costs, while core G&A expenses were only $3.5 million. The company generated $1.5 million in staking revenue and announced a new $10 million share repurchase plan approved by the board. Management emphasized that this is the first quarter as a public company following the June 11 business combination and noted that one-time costs are now behind them.

negative_highlights: COGS inflation now mid-single digits, up 100 bps from initial expectations, driven by freight and other costs
Coffee volume outlook remains conservative (down low single digits) despite recent volume growth, due to commodity volatility and consumer dynamics
Sweet baked snacks expected to decline low single digits for the year, with weakness in convenience channel traffic and SKU rationalization lapping
positive_highlights: Achieved 3x leverage ratio in Q1, ahead of expectations, enabling consideration of share repurchases
Uncrustables full-year growth outlook raised from mid-single to high single digits
Café Bustelo grew 23% in the quarter, with continued distribution expansion plans
summary: SJM posted Q1 FY2027 results that included an $0.84 per share tariff refund benefit, offset by reinvestment in SD&A (admin, marketing, and McCalla pre-production) and debt paydown, achieving a 3x leverage ratio ahead of schedule. Coffee volumes grew in the quarter, but management maintained conservative full-year volume assumptions (down low single digits) and paused a planned list price decline, opting for promotional activity. Uncrustables outlook was raised from mid-single to high single-digit growth, while sweet baked snacks are expected to be down low single digits for the year, with a flatter back half. COGS inflation is now mid-single digits, up 100 bps from prior expectations due to freight and other costs.

negative_highlights: Company declined to provide specific FY2027 revenue guidance beyond 'double-digit growth'.
CFO would not commit to a cash-flow-positive quarter, citing R&D and manufacturing spend.
positive_highlights: RYONCIL net revenue of $115 million in first full year, with Q4 revenue of $36 million.
Net loss reduced 44% to $57.5 million; H2 cash burn cut to $13.4 million from $50 million year-over-year.
76% day-100 survival in adults with steroid-refractory GVHD who failed ruxolitinib, versus ~25% with other agents.
summary: Mesoblast reported FY2026 net revenue of $115 million from RYONCIL, its first full year post-launch, with Q4 revenue of $36 million and gross profit of $110 million. Net loss narrowed 44% to $57.5 million, cash burn halved in H2 to $13.4 million, and cash stood at $103 million. Management guided to double-digit RYONCIL revenue growth next year, with a phase III chronic low back pain trial readout in H2 2027 and an adult GVHD interim analysis expected in Q4 2027.

negative_highlights: Gross margins guided down to 74% in Q3 and bottoming at 71%-72% in Q4 due to memory price hikes.
Supply constraints will persist at least through end of FY2028, limiting growth below demand.
China data center revenue excluded from forward outlook due to geopolitical uncertainty.
positive_highlights: Revenue of $96 billion more than doubled YoY, with data center up 18% QoQ to $89 billion.
Issued first-ever annual guidance of ~70% revenue growth for FY2028, with demand potentially doubling.
Announced expanded AWS partnership for 2 million GPUs and Vera CPUs through FY2029.
summary: NVIDIA reported record Q2 FY2027 revenue of $96 billion, more than doubling year-over-year, with data center revenue of $89 billion growing 18% sequentially. Non-GAAP EPS was $2.92, up 96% YoY. The company guided Q3 revenue to $108 billion ±2% and initial FY2028 revenue growth of approximately 70%, driven by strong demand but constrained by supply. GAAP and non-GAAP gross margins were both 75%, with guidance reset lower to 74% ±50bps in Q3 and 72%-73% in FY2028 due to memory price increases. Management announced expanded partnership with AWS (2 million GPUs through Q2 FY2029) and investments like $50 billion in frontier AI labs and $500 billion financing platforms.

negative_highlights: Non-GAAP net income fell YoY due to a $14M FX loss from U.S. dollar weakness.
SHOPLINE gross margin pulled back sequentially due to mix shift toward lower-margin value-added services.
BIGO Ads gross margin decreased QoQ due to higher contribution from lower-margin third-party advertising.
positive_highlights: Total revenue grew 16.3% YoY to $591M, with accelerated QoQ growth of 6.3%.
BIGO Ads revenue up 53.1% YoY, with third-party BIGO Audience Network growing 74.1% YoY.
Full-year non-GAAP operating income guidance raised to ~20% YoY growth, up from previous teens level.
summary: JOYY reported Q2 2026 revenue of $591M, up 16.3% YoY and 6.3% QoQ, with non-GAAP operating profit of $49M, up 28.2% YoY. Social entertainment revenue grew 7.4% YoY, BIGO Ads grew 53.1% YoY, and SHOPLINE grew 28.6% YoY. Management raised full-year non-GAAP operating income growth guidance to around 20% (from teens), driven by better-than-expected H1 performance. Q3 revenue guidance of $602-622M implies 11.4%-15.2% YoY growth.

negative_highlights: Net income fell from $2 million to $1.6 million YoY in Q2
Geopolitical disruptions increased logistics costs and the weaker U.S. dollar created FX headwinds
positive_highlights: First-half revenue grew 3% YoY to $108.8 million and net income rose 28% to $2.7 million
Gross margin remained stable at 66.1% in Q2 despite revenue decline
Operating expenses decreased 4% YoY in Q2, with G&A down 5%
summary: Q2 revenue declined 4% YoY to $57 million, with gross margin stable at 66.1%. Net income fell to $1.6 million from $2 million a year earlier, while adjusted EBITDA was $1.9 million. Management cited a challenging external environment including geopolitical logistics pressures and FX headwinds, but maintained profitability through disciplined expense management. First-half revenue grew 3% to $108.8 million with net income up 28% to $2.7 million.

negative_highlights: Management declined to give exact GAAP EPS guidance due to tax rate volatility
Affirm Card attach rate is only 19% of actives, indicating room for improvement
No major competitive response in the U.K. yet, but competitive landscape remains a watch item
positive_highlights: Most profitable quarter ever, excluding tax allowance release
Pay in X grew 41% year-over-year
Guidance for fiscal 2027 revenue less transaction costs at 4.16%, above midterm target
summary: Affirm reported its most profitable quarter ever, even without a tax allowance release, with strong growth across products including 41% growth in Pay in X and robust card adoption. The company guided to fiscal 2027 revenue less transaction costs above the midterm target at 4.16%, supported by solid funding costs and stable credit. Management emphasized network effects, expanding merchant adoption, and ongoing innovation in in-store and Affirm Edge, while noting consumer credit remains stable with no signs of stress.

negative_highlights: July comps were approximately flat, reflecting a pullback after strong May and June results.
Computing ASPs rose mid-teens due to memory cost increases, with units down high single digits.
Full-year SG&A expected to increase ~20 bps as a percentage of revenue, driven by incentive comp and investments.
positive_highlights: Enterprise comparable sales growth of 4.1% significantly exceeded guidance of ~1%.
Domestic TV sales grew more than 10% YoY, the highest growth since Q2 FY2022.
Emerging categories (AI glasses, trading cards, health rings) more than doubled YoY and contributed ~1 point to comp.
summary: Best Watch reported Q2 FY2027 revenue of $9.8 billion, up 3.6% YoY, with enterprise comparable sales up 4.1%, versus guidance of ~1%. Adjusted operating income rate was 4.3%, up ~40 bps YoY, and adjusted diluted EPS of $1.47 was up 15% YoY. The company raised its full-year guidance, now expecting comparable sales growth of 1.9%-3% and adjusted EPS of $6.70-$6.90. Management highlighted strength in computing, home theater, and emerging categories, while acknowledging memory-cost-driven price increases and a slower back half in computing.

negative_highlights: U.S. sales moderated due to competitors offering free product through clinical trials, though temporary.
AUD 4 million unrealized translation loss from strengthening Australian dollar impacted reported EBIT.
Total expenditure of AUD 53.5 million included CBM, underlying ~AUD 45 million; R&D slightly reduced as CUV105 winds down.
positive_highlights: Revenue exceeded AUD 100 million for the second year, with 10th consecutive year of profitability and 36% net margin.
Global treatment volumes up 6% (Europe +13%) despite U.S. moderation from competitor free-product trials.
Cash reserves increased AUD 28 million to AUD 252 million, with term deposits yielding 6.23% and no debt for 20 years.
summary: CLINUVEL reported its 10th consecutive year of profit, with total revenue exceeding AUD 100 million for the second consecutive year, driven by a 6% increase in global SCENESSE treatments and a 13% rise in European volumes. Gross margin was 83% and net margin 36%, with cash reserves growing AUD 28 million to AUD 252 million despite an AUD 4 million FX translation loss. Management announced a planned Nasdaq listing and exit from the ASX, citing the U.S. as the largest future market and higher valuation multiples. Guidance for vitiligo phase III results (CUV105) and start of CUV107 remain on track for Q4, with total expenditure of AUD 53.5 million below the AUD 55 million five-year average target.

negative_highlights: Software revenue declined 3% YoY due to cautious customer spending and extended sales cycles
Medical software revenue declined 4% YoY, partly due to reduced U.S. research grants
Manufacturing adjusted EBITDA remained negative at EUR -0.3 million, though improved from EUR -4.8 million
positive_highlights: Medical segment revenue grew 12% YoY, with medical devices up 19%
Adjusted EBIT margin expanded to 5.5% from 4.7% in the prior year quarter
Free cash flow nearly doubled to EUR 11.4 million in H1 2026, with net cash position at EUR 74.2 million
summary: In Q2 2026, Materialise reported EUR 70.1 million revenue, up 8% YoY, with Medical up 12% and Manufacturing up 7%, while Software declined 3%. Adjusted EBITDA rose 16% to EUR 9.6 million (13.7% margin), and adjusted EBIT increased to EUR 3.9 million (5.5% margin). The company reaffirmed its full-year revenue guidance of EUR 273-283 million and raised its adjusted EBIT guidance range to EUR 12-14 million from EUR 10-12 million, driven by strong execution and cost control.

negative_highlights: Organic net sales declined 2% in Q3, with retail volume down sharply due to portfolio shaping, pricing elasticities, and a challenged consumer.
Full-year organic net sales guidance cut to 1%-2% from 1%-4%.
International segment was hit by a Brazil divestiture loss, an impairment on an Indonesia investment, and a one-time legal entity transition delaying SPAM export sales.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EPS grew 6% YoY to $0.37, with adjusted operating margin up 60 bps to 9%.
Full-year adjusted EPS guidance raised and narrowed to $1.45-$1.51, implying 6%-10% growth.
Foodservice delivered 12th consecutive quarter of organic net sales growth, with profit growth outpacing sales.
summary: Hormel Foods reported Q3 FY2026 adjusted EPS of $0.37, up 6% YoY, with organic net sales down 2%. Adjusted operating margin improved 60 bps to 9%. The company raised and narrowed its full-year adjusted EPS guidance to $1.45-$1.51 (from $1.43-$1.51) and tightened organic net sales growth to 1%-2% (from 1%-4%). Retail volumes declined due to portfolio shaping and consumer pressure, while Foodservice delivered its 12th consecutive quarter of organic growth.

negative_highlights: Net new ARR growth of 4% year-over-year is modest, with management expecting low-to-mid single-digit growth for the full year, a potential deceleration versus the first half's 22% growth.
Customer count growth slowed (13% for $100k+ customers vs. 17% prior quarter), partly due to a strategic shift toward larger deals.
Margin expansion expected to slow in the second half as the company reinvests in growth.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 21% to $292 million, beating guidance, with a record 10% operating margin (820 bps expansion YoY).
AI security ARR (Prompt and Purple AI) tripled year-over-year, and RPO grew 45% to a record $1.7 billion.
Raised FY2027 revenue and operating income guidance; sales and marketing efficiency improved by 900+ bps YoY.
summary: SentinelOne reported Q2 FY2027 revenue of $292 million, up 21% year-over-year, exceeding guidance. ARR grew 22%, with record net new ARR of $56 million, up 4% year-over-year. Operating margin hit a record 10%, up 820 basis points year-over-year, and EPS of $0.08 doubled. The company raised its full-year revenue guidance to $1.202-1.207 billion and operating income to $124-128 million, reflecting heightened confidence in demand, particularly in AI security products where ARR tripled year-over-year.

negative_highlights: Realized gold hedge loss of ZAR 9.6 billion within revenue, though net derivative liabilities reduced to ZAR 2 billion.
Moab Khotsong is entering an ore gap expected to last ~5 years, pressuring unit costs (Mponeng costs up 17%, Moab up 20% per the Q&A).
FY2027 capital expenditure guided sharply higher (gold ZAR 14.4bn + CSA ZAR 2.1bn + Eva Copper $650-680m), and dividend is tied to free cash flow; management did not commit to maintaining payout.
positive_highlights: Record revenue of ZAR 99.2 billion, up 34% YoY; net profit up 102% to ZAR 30 billion.
Headline EPS up 87% to ZAR 43.63; record final dividend of ZAR 7.50/share, bringing total FY26 dividend to ZAR 12.80/share at ~3.5% yield.
Adjusted free cash flow up 54% to a record ZAR 17 billion; net debt/EBITDA at 0.02x (near net cash).
summary: Harmony Gold reported record FY2026 results: revenue up 34% to ZAR 99.2 billion, net profit up 102% to ZAR 30 billion, and headline EPS up 87% to ZAR 43.63. Gold production was 1.43 million ounces at an AISC of ZAR 1.19 million/kg; copper production was 18,200 tons at C1 cost of $2.47/lb, both within guidance. FY2027 gold production guidance is 1.3-1.4 million ounces with AISC of ZAR 1.3-1.395 million/kg, and CSA copper guidance is 28,000-30,000 tons at C1 of $2.55-2.65/lb.

negative_highlights: Impaired provisions rose to CAD 612 million, up CAD 64 million QoQ, above initial guidance range.
U.S. segment NIM fell 14 bps QoQ to 376 bps due to mix and pricing pressure.
Canadian deposit growth remains flat to down (down 1% YoY), with GIC outflows of ~10% YoY.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EPS grew 26% YoY to CAD 2.73, ninth straight quarter of double-digit growth.
Revenues rose 15% YoY to CAD 8 billion, with broad-based momentum including 20% growth in non-interest income.
Efficiency ratio improved 200 bps YoY, and ROE reached 16.8%, up 260 bps.
summary: CIBC reported adjusted Q3 FY2026 EPS of CAD 2.73, up 26% year-over-year (ninth consecutive double-digit growth), with revenues up 15% to CAD 8 billion and adjusted net income of CAD 2.6 billion. The CET1 ratio was 13.4% after watching back 7.5 million shares, and ROE rose 260 bps to 16.8%. Management expects adjusted expenses to rise quarter-over-quarter in Q4, with stable to gradually positive NIM, but noted trade uncertainty and no formal guidance raise.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to $9.2 million ($0.40 per share) from $6.0 million ($0.26 per share); adjusted EBITDA declined to $4.6 million from $5.6 million
Europe revenue fell ~34% in constant currency to $66.1 million and swung to a $1.3 million pre-tax loss from $5.1 million income, prompting a guidance cut to down 30%-40%
Domestic ag same-store sales fell 8.4% and the segment posted a $3.3 million pre-tax loss; second-half domestic ag equipment sales are guided down ~20% versus -13.5% in the first half
positive_highlights: Gross margin expanded 150 bps to 18.6% and equipment margin rose 190 bps to 8.5%, with domestic ag equipment margin up 360 bps to 6.7% in the first half
Floor plan and other interest expense fell 30% to $8.1 million, reflecting reduced interest-bearing inventory, and adjusted debt to tangible net worth of 1.6x sits well below the 3.5x covenant
Construction same-store sales rose 9.2% to $78.6 million with pre-tax income of $0.4 million versus a $1.2 million loss; Australia constant-currency revenue rose 22.5%
summary: Titan reported Q2 FY2027 revenue of $496.4 million, down from $546.4 million a year ago (same-store sales -6.2%), with a net loss of $9.2 million or $0.40 per share versus a $6.0 million loss or $0.26 per share last year. Consolidated gross margin expanded 150 bps to 18.6% and equipment margin rose 190 bps to 8.5%, while floor plan interest expense fell 30% to $8.1 million. Full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance of $17-$29 million and adjusted loss per share of $1.25-$1.75 were reaffirmed, but Europe revenue guidance was cut to down 30%-40%, with construction raised to +5%-10% and Australia raised to +15%-20%. Domestic ag remains guided down ~15%-20%, with a sharper second-half equipment sales decline (~20%) following earlier-than-anticipated factory shipments that pulled first-half deliveries forward.

negative_highlights: Net loss of $77 million ($1.40 per share) driven by elevated freight costs and Jeffersonville ramp-up expenses
Gross margin fell to 13.9% from prior periods, impacted by tariff refund benefits and unrealized profit release in prior year
Operating cash flow used $181 million in the quarter, with total debt rising to $7.1 billion, partly due to Recurrent Energy construction financing
positive_highlights: Storage shipments of 3.7 GWh exceeded guidance, with 3.3 GWh revenue recognized
CS PowerTech has secured over 13 GW in contracted backlog for U.S. HJT/TOPCon modules, valued above $4.5 billion, with deliveries through 2029
Jeffersonville HJT cell facility is now the first commercial U.S. HJT manufacturer, with phase I ramping to full production by October 1
summary: Q2 2026 revenue of $1.2 billion was at the high end of guidance, with 3.1 GW modules and 3.3 GWh storage recognized; storage beat guidance. Gross margin of 13.9% was in line but down sequentially and YoY due to elevated freight costs and Jeffersonville ramp-up costs, leading to a net loss of $77 million ($1.40 per share). Q3 revenue guidance is $1.3-$1.5 billion with gross margin 13.5%-15.5%, and U.S. volume guidance for 2026 maintained at 6.5-7 GW modules and 4.5-5.5 GWh storage. Management expressed confidence in the new Section 232 policy as net positive for the company, and highlighted a 13 GW U.S. manufacturing backlog valued over $4.5 billion.

negative_highlights: Headline price erosion continues as a headwind to service revenue, with management noting the need to balance sharing cost saves with clients
Hedge program locks yields at approximately 3.9% net, below current five-year treasury yields, limiting upside from rising rates
Marketplace revenue remains immaterial to overall results, with early-stage monetization
positive_highlights: Record adjusted EBITDA margin of 48%, up 200 bps from 46% last year
New HSA sales grew 24% YoY, a Q2 record and strongest outside Q4 open enrollment
AI-driven automation resolved 85% of routine chat inquiries and reduced human-handled calls 25% YoY
summary: HealthEquity Q2 FY2027 revenue grew 8% YoY to a record with service revenue up 6% to $124.4M, custodial revenue up 10% to $175.9M, and interchange up 5% to $50.4M. Adjusted EBITDA margin hit a record 48%, up from 46% last year, with adjusted EBITDA of $167M up 11%. Non-GAAP EPS was $1.24. The company raised its FY2027 guidance for revenue, non-GAAP EPS, and adjusted EBITDA, citing strong first-half performance and AI-driven efficiency gains.

negative_highlights: Q4 gross margin is expected to decline YoY due to higher freight and fuel costs and broad-based inflation, partially offset by lower tariffs.
Helium shortages reduced Q2 sales by ~$15 million (30 bps of comp), with no recovery assumed in the back-half guidance.
Q3 EPS guidance of $0.80-$0.95 includes a ~$0.50 negative impact from tariff refund reinvestments, marking a significant sequential decline.
positive_highlights: Comp sales of 3.7% exceeded the high end of guidance, with traffic up 0.4% and improving sequentially, returning to positive a quarter earlier than planned.
Adjusted EPS of $2.70 (or $1.39 underlying) beat the $1.00-$1.15 outlook; full-year EPS guidance raised to $7.70-$8.05 from prior $6.70-$7.10.
Gross margin expanded 850 bps to 42.9%, including a one-time net benefit from tariff refunds; shrink was favorable and contributed to profitability.
summary: Dollar Tree reported Q2 FY2026 net sales of $4.9 billion, up 7% YoY, with comp sales growth of 3.7% (traffic +0.4%, ticket +3.3%). Adjusted EPS was $2.70, including a $1.31 net tariff refund benefit; underlying EPS was $1.39, ahead of the prior outlook of $1.00-$1.15. The company raised FY2026 EPS guidance to $7.70-$8.05 (from prior $6.70-$7.10) and initiated Q3 guidance of $0.80-$0.95, reflecting ~$0.50 headwind from reinvestments. Gross margin expanded 850 bps to 42.9%, largely on a one-time $383 million tariff refund. Management reiterated confidence in the long-term algorithm, with traffic turning positive a quarter early, but guided to gross margin pressure in Q4 on freight and inflation.

negative_highlights: Net expansion rate (NER) declined sequentially to ~111% from 112% in Q4, though management expects improvement within four quarters.
Gross margins were slightly lower quarter-over-quarter, though management attributed no specific trend.
Restructuring charges of $20M in Q1, with an additional $2M-$5M expected for the remainder of the year.
positive_highlights: Added more than 80 net new customers in the $100K+ ACV cohort, the largest quarterly net add ever; cohort now represents 90% of sales-led subscription revenue.
AI usage in $100K+ customers jumped to over 37% from ~21% a year ago, with 70 net additions in Q1.
Constant currency revenue growth accelerated to 15% from 14% in Q4, and sales-led subscription growth accelerated to 17% from 16% in Q4.
summary: Q1 FY2027 total revenue was $478M, up 15% YoY, and sales-led subscription revenue grew 18% to $399M. Non-GAAP operating margin was 16.2%, above guidance. CRPO grew 21% to $1.2B, and RPO grew 27% to $1.9B. Management raised full-year revenue guidance to $1.998B-$2.010B and EPS to $3.29-$3.37, citing strong pipeline and consumption.

negative_highlights: Revenue growth is sluggish at 1% YoY, with Q3 guidance midpoint roughly flat YoY
Workforce restructuring impacts about 15% of employees, concentrated in support functions
Management notes 'rough couple of quarters' and that work is not yet over
positive_highlights: ARR crossed $500 million milestone to $501 million
Dollar-based net retention improved sequentially to 98%
Operating margin came in at 24%, above high end of guidance, and FY guidance raised to 25%-26%
summary: PagerDuty reported Q2 FY2027 revenue of $124.4 million, up 1% YoY and above guidance, with non-GAAP operating margin of 24% and GAAP net income of $4.7 million. ARR crossed $500 million to $501 million, up $6 million sequentially, while DBNR improved to 98%. The company completed a 15% workforce restructuring and raised FY2027 revenue guidance at the low end, operating margin guidance to 25%-26%, and EPS to $1.33-$1.37. Management sees stabilization and improving retention but notes ongoing work needed.

negative_highlights: Core low-income customers remain financially strained, with higher fuel prices forcing them to note less per trip despite increased shopping frequency.
Fuel costs are expected to remain elevated in the second half, pressuring gross margin and requiring offsetting actions.
Full-year same-store sales guidance of 2.5%-2.9% implies a moderation from the 3.5% Q2 comp, partly due to lapping strong prior-year periods.
positive_highlights: Same-store sales grew 3.5% in Q2, the fifth consecutive quarter of traffic growth, with all four merchandising categories positive for the sixth straight quarter.
EPS of $2.48 increased 33% year-over-year, beating expectations even before the $0.25 tariff refund benefit.
Gross margin expanded 127 basis points to 32.6%, with improvement in shrink and damages exceeding expectations.
summary: Dollar General reported Q2 FY2026 net sales of $11.3 billion, up 0.2% year-over-year (slight discrepancy with stated $10.7 billion prior year, but transcribed as such), with same-store sales up 3.5% and traffic up 2%. GAAP EPS of $2.48 came in ahead of expectations, including a $0.25 benefit from tariff refunds. The company raised its full-year guidance: net sales growth of 4%-4.3%, same-store sales growth of 2.5%-2.9%, and EPS of $7.80-$8.00, while also announcing a $700 million share repurchase program for the second half. Management expressed confidence in continued gross margin expansion and top-line momentum, though it noted persistent pressure on its core low-income customer from elevated fuel prices and inflation.

negative_highlights: FY2028 subscription revenue growth target (~11%) is a deceleration from current 13%
Q3 cRPO growth guide of 11%-12% reflects lapping the Paradox acquisition
Free cash flow declined YoY due to payroll calendar timing
positive_highlights: AI ARR grew over 200% YoY to ~$600 million
AI products drove more than $100 million of new ACV, over 25% of total
5,500 customers using organic agents, up over 35% from last quarter
summary: Workday reported Q2 FY2027 subscription revenue of $2.471B, up 14% YoY, and total revenue of $2.649B, up 13%. Non-GAAP operating margin was 31.1%, and cRPO grew 14.2% to $9.03B. AI-driven ARR reached ~$600M, up over 200% YoY, and AI products contributed more than $100M in new ACV, over 25% of the total. Management slightly raised FY2027 subscription revenue guidance to $9.94-$9.95B (13% growth) and increased non-GAAP operating margin guidance to 31%, while providing an early FY2028 target of ~11% subscription revenue growth and at least 200bps margin expansion.

negative_highlights: Non-GAAP operating margin guidance for FY2027 remains flat at 39%, with dilution from MaintainX acquisition.
MaintainX acquisition contributes $45 million in transaction expenses and a drag on operating margin.
Sales reorganization impact still within expected range, with Western Europe normalizing slower.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 16% as reported, above the high end of guidance.
Raised full-year billings and revenue guidance by 1 percentage point each.
Construction business growing north of 20%, with new enterprise wins like a major retailer selecting Forma.
summary: Autodesk reported Q2 FY2027 revenue of $8.3 billion, up 16% as reported and 14% in constant currency, with billings up 10% and non-GAAP operating margin at 41%. The company raised full-year billings guidance to $8.575-$8.65 billion and revenue guidance to $8.295-$8.345 billion, including MaintainX contribution, reflecting outperformance and stronger second-half expectations. MaintainX is expected to contribute $60 million to second-half revenue and $70 million to billings.

negative_highlights: Net loss of $684 million in the quarter due to non-cash impairments and fair value decreases from mining transition
Revenue declined $7.6 million sequentially as mining hardware was decommissioned ahead of GPU installations
Mining operations expected to be fully decommissioned by end of December 2026, indicating ongoing transition costs
positive_highlights: New multi-year contracts with frontier AI lab, Cohere, Prometheus, Perplexity, Figure AI, Fal.ai, Higgsfield AI, plus renewals from Together AI and Fireworks AI
Three-year contract pricing up ~125% and five-year up ~70% since November, with recent prepayments funding 45-55% of GPU CapEx
$6.5 billion of GPU financing raised in three months, including $2.8 billion for non-investment grade at single-digit rates
summary: IREN reported Q4 FY2026 revenue of $137.2 million, including $70.5 million AI Cloud, down $7.6 million sequentially due to mining decommissioning. Net loss was $684 million, driven by $450.4 million impairments and $102.1 million fair value decrease on mining hardware. FY27 CapEx guidance of $25-30 billion with $4 billion ARR contracted by December 2026. Horizon 1 delivered to Microsoft, with Horizon 2-4 targeted for December quarter.

negative_highlights: Tanker order book to fleet exceeds 30% on VLCCs and Suezmaxes, with deliveries increasing in 2027-2028 potentially leading to oversupply.
For Q3, tanker rates booked slightly below Q2 on Suezmaxes (under $120,000 vs. $123,000 in Q2), with VLCC Q3 rates essentially flat.
Management expressed low expectations for an IMO decarbonization agreement in November, citing US pressure.
positive_highlights: Net profit of $364.4 million on revenue over $700 million, with EBITDA of $552 million.
Forecast 2027 operational cash flow of $700 million to $1 billion after all CapEx, based on FFA and rate assumptions.
Sold vessels at historic high prices, booking $127 million gain in Q2 and expected additional gains of $100 million and $130 million in Q3 and Q4, respectively.
summary: CMB.TECH reported a net profit of $364.4 million in Q2 FY2026 on revenue above $700 million and EBITDA of $552 million, including $127 million in asset-sale gains. The company declared a $0.64 per share distribution ($0.21 interim and $0.43 from share premium). Contract backlog was stable at $3.3 billion; cash flow for 2027 is forecast at $700 million to $1 billion after CapEx. The board maintained a cautious stance on tankers due to an order book over 30% on VLCCs and Suezmaxes, while dry bulk and offshore energy outlooks are positive.

negative_highlights: Non-GAAP gross margin is expected to decline slightly in Q3 due to custom product mix, guided to 57.5%-58.5% versus 58.9% in Q2.
Communications and other end market revenue declined 3% sequentially and is expected to decline low-to-mid teens sequentially in Q3.
Supply chain constraints remain pervasive, leading to ~$1 billion in capacity prepayments in FY2027.
positive_highlights: FY2027 revenue guidance raised by ~$500 million to ~$12 billion; FY2028 guidance raised by ~$1.5 billion to ~$18 billion.
Data center revenue grew 46% YoY and is expected to grow over 20% sequentially in Q3, with FY2027 data center growth raised to ~60% from ~50%.
Non-GAAP gross margin expanded 180 bps YoY to 58.9%, and operating margin expanded 180 bps YoY to 36.6%.
summary: Marvell reported record Q2 FY2027 revenue of $2.739 billion, up 37% year-over-year and 13% sequentially, with non-GAAP EPS of $0.94 beating guidance by a penny. Data center revenue hit $2.17 billion, up 46% year-over-year. Management raised FY2027 revenue outlook to approximately $12 billion (45% growth, up from $11.5 billion prior) and FY2028 to approximately $18 billion (50% growth, up from $16.5 billion prior). The company expects Q3 FY2027 revenue of $3.15 billion at the midpoint (15% sequential growth), with data center growth exceeding 20% sequentially and roughly 75% year-over-year.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened YoY to $3.4 million (from $1.6 million) due to increased G&A and R&D investments
Non-recurring costs related to IPO and public company readiness inflated G&A; costs expected to stabilize but no financial guidance provided
