Process yield was 63.3%, implying significant cost improvement potential yet to be realized
positive_highlights: Revenue increased ~8x YoY to $4.7 million, with 67% gross margin as the model scales
Total contract backlog grew from $91.3 million to $576.9 million (over 6x) in the quarter, with funded backlog reaching $119.3 million after the Antares agreement
First commercial full core load of TRISO fuel delivered to Radiant, demonstrating core-to-reload model
summary: Standard Nuclear reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $4.7 million, up from $0.6 million YoY, driven by first commercial fuel deliveries and service revenue. Gross margin was 67%, with net loss narrowing to $3.4 million from $7.7 million in Q1. Total contract backlog surged to $576.9 million (from $91.3 million at March 31) including funded backlog of $119.3 million after the Antares agreement, reflecting strong demand conversion. Management reiterated targeted Q4 2026 authorization for two new facilities and 2027 Richland production, but did not provide financial guidance.

negative_highlights: Trade tensions add uncertainty to Canada-U.S. relations, acknowledged by CEO
Expenses up 4% YoY, with 3% from variable comp, FX, and strategic cards portfolio
CET1 increased only 3 bps sequentially despite strong organic accretion, due to buybacks and model updates
positive_highlights: Record earnings of CAD 4.7 billion and EPS of CAD 2.77, with revenue up 8% YoY
ROE improved 280 bps YoY to 16%, in line with medium-term target
U.S. Banking loans turned positive sequentially; bank card balances up 20% YoY
summary: TD reported record Q3 FY2026 earnings of CAD 4.7 billion and EPS of CAD 2.77, with revenue up 8% YoY. ROE reached 16%, up 280 bps YoY, and CET1 ratio was 14.3%. Management expects total PCLs near the lower end of the prior 40-50 bps range, and reiterated a 13% CET1 target by H2 FY2027 with potential CAD 13 billion in buybacks in FY2027. U.S. Banking saw total loans positive sequentially, with bank card balances up 20% YoY.

negative_highlights: Old Navy comps declined 4%, with a traffic slowdown and seasonal assortment miss, leading to a modest miss versus expectations.
Athleta comps declined 12%, with management noting a measured approach that may limit top-line improvement in the near term.
Total company net sales declined 2% YoY, below the prior year's growth.
positive_highlights: Gap brand comps increased 10%, marking the 11th consecutive quarter of positive comps.
Full-year adjusted EPS guidance raised to $2.35-$2.45 (up 10%-15%) and operating margin raised to 7.4%-7.6%.
Year-to-date share repurchases totaled over $600 million (26 million shares), driving mid-single-digit EPS accretion.
summary: Gap Inc. reported Q2 FY2026 net sales of $3.7 billion, down 2% YoY, with comparable sales down 1%. Adjusted EPS was $0.52 versus $0.57 last year. Gross margin expanded 20 bps to 41.4%, driven by Gap brand strength, but Old Navy comps fell 4% due to seasonal assortment and traffic issues, while Athleta comps declined 12%. Full-year revenue guidance was narrowed to 1%-1.5% growth, but adjusted operating margin outlook was raised to 7.4%-7.6% and adjusted EPS to $2.35-$2.45, up 10%-15% YoY.

negative_highlights: Quarterly revenue from Hyperliquid has declined since Q3 2025 due to a crypto winter and growth-mode fee discounts on real-world assets, though RWA volumes are replacing some.
NAV has been volatile, ranging from 0.75x to 1.3x, which management acknowledges has caused stress.
Deferred tax liability of ~$184 million, a non-current obligation recognition under GAAP.
positive_highlights: Treasury-related income of ~$553 million for the year, driven by token appreciation and 16.5 million HYPE tokens purchased at favorable prices.
Staking and validator revenues of $9.5 million, recognized primarily in Q4.
Hyperliquid's new stablecoin agreement now returns 90% of reserve yield to the ecosystem, directly boosting buybacks.
summary: Hyperliquid Strategies (PURR) reported a strong fiscal year 2026, with treasury-related income of approximately $553 million, primarily driven by unrealized gains on HYPE tokens and an effective token acquisition strategy. The company holds 29.3 million HYPE tokens valued at ~$1.9 billion plus ~$150 million in cash-like instruments, with no debt. Management highlighted a growing ecosystem, including new stablecoin revenue sharing (90% now to Hyperliquid), real-world asset trading volumes, and the upcoming permissionless prediction markets. Guidance was not explicitly provided, but management expressed a bullish long-term view on HYPE token value and the potential for continued NAV accretion.

negative_highlights: Game revenue declined 14% YoY to RMB 1.4B due to a high base from Sanmo.
User growth slowed: DAU up 7% YoY, MAU up to 371M, but the company noted macro pressure on consumer spending.
R&D expenses increased 16% YoY due to AI investment, pressuring near-term margins.
positive_highlights: Advertising revenue grew 28% YoY to RMB 3.13B, marking 14 straight quarters of 20%+ growth and 39% of total revenue.
Adjusted net profit margin expanded to 8.9% from 8.1% YoY, with net profit up 55% YoY.
AI-related CapEx is on track: 70%-80% of the RMB 1B target deployed in H1, with R&D expenses expected to hit RMB 500M for the year.
summary: Q2 FY2026 total revenue rose 8% YoY to RMB 7.9B, with gross margin up to 37.2% and adjusted net profit of RMB 704M, up 25% YoY, reaching an 8.9% margin. Advertising grew 28% YoY to RMB 3.1B, while games declined 14% YoY to RMB 1.4B. Management expects gaming revenue to resume YoY growth in Q4 and maintains a 40%-45% gross margin target, with AI CapEx on track at 70%-80% of the RMB 1B target for the first half.

negative_highlights: European deliveries down 17% YoY amid intense competition
Chip price volatility drove nearly 2% increase in BOM costs
Near-term consolidation of Lotus UK expected to widen group-level losses
positive_highlights: Deliveries up 39% YoY to 3,904 units; revenue up 23% YoY to $268 million
Gross margin expanded 160 bps to 10%
Eletre X PHEV had 2,200 orders in China by June 30; deliveries over 1,800 units
summary: Lotus reported a 39% YoY increase in deliveries to 3,904 units and revenue of $268 million, up 23% YoY, despite ASPs down 3%. Gross margin expanded 160 bps to 10%, and operating loss narrowed 63% YoY to $95 million (or 26% lower to $195 million ex one-offs). Management provided a Focus 2030 roadmap targeting 30,000 annual sales and >20% gross margins by 2030, and highlighted strong early demand for the new Eletre X PHEV with 2,200 orders in China. However, European deliveries fell 17% YoY, and the company expects near-term consolidation of Lotus UK to widen group-level losses before synergies materialize.

negative_highlights: MR2 product tanker rates fell sharply from over $70,000 per day in April to around $30,000 per day by July.
Recorded a non-cash unrealized loss on warrants of $2 million for the first half of 2026.
Stock trades at a steep discount to net asset value per share ($2.67 vs $12.83 NAV), reflecting market skepticism.
positive_highlights: Voyage revenues grew 124% YoY to $24 million; net income swung from a $5.3 million loss to a $10.0 million profit.
Adjusted net income jumped 755% to $9.8 million in Q2; adjusted EBITDA up 325% to $11.8 million.
Cash balance reached $48 million by end-July, up 222% from year-end 2025, fully covering the $39.78 million CapEx due January 2027.
summary: C3is reported Q2 2026 voyage revenues of $24.0 million, up 124% YoY, and net income of $10.0 million versus a $5.3 million loss in Q2 2025. Adjusted net income rose 755% to $9.8 million, and EBITDA reached $12.0 million. Fleet TCE increased 145% to $40,300, led by the Aframax at $133,500. Management expressed confidence that H2 will mirror H1, supported by fleet expansion and no Chinese-built vessels.

negative_highlights: Mass makeup comps declined low single digits due to lack of newness and lapping prior-year strength.
Skincare and wellness comps declined modestly, dragged by body care lapping big brand expansions.
Macro uncertainty and elevated fuel costs cited, leading to cautious second-half guidance of 4%-5% net sales growth and 2%-3% comps.
positive_highlights: Raised FY EPS guidance to $28.70-$29.00 (11.9%-13.1% growth) from prior 10.6%-12.3%.
Fragrance comps grew high-teen, haircare high-single-digit, and e-commerce delivered sixth consecutive quarter of double-digit growth.
Increased share repurchase target to $1.8B for fiscal 2026, with $1B remaining under authorization.
summary: Q2 FY2026 net sales grew 8.9% to $3.0B, with comparable sales up 3.8%; diluted EPS rose 13.3% to $6.55. Gross margin was 39.1%, down 10 bps, while operating margin improved 10 bps to 12.5%. The company raised full-year guidance: net sales growth now 6.7%-7.2%, comps 3.2%-3.7%, EPS $28.70-$29.00, and increased buyback target to $1.8B. Management noted consumer resilience but cited macro uncertainty and elevated fuel costs as reasons for prudence in second-half guidance.

negative_highlights: Q3 revenue guidance of 16.4%-17.7% growth implies a deceleration from Q2's 20.2% growth
Still net loss of CNY 135.8 million, though improved
Offline business remains in early-stage investment phase, with management emphasizing selective expansion over footprint growth
positive_highlights: Non-academic tutoring revenue grew over 30% year-over-year, accounting for over 40% of total revenue
Adjusted operating loss narrowed 38.5% year-over-year, with operating expenses as % of revenue down 7 percentage points
Net operating cash flow increased 46.3% to CNY 861.2 million
summary: Gaotu reported Q2 2026 net revenues of nearly CNY 1.7 billion, up 20.2% year-over-year, with gross margin expanding to 66.5% from 65.8%. Adjusted net loss narrowed 37.6% to CNY 129.1 million, and operating cash flow rose 46.3% to CNY 861.2 million. The company guided Q3 2026 revenue to CNY 1,838-1,858 million, implying 16.4%-17.7% growth, a slowdown from Q2's 20.2%. Strong growth in non-academic tutoring (30%+ revenue growth) and offline business (high double-digit revenue growth in H1) was offset by still-negative operating profitability, though losses narrowed significantly.

negative_highlights: Acquired Zoetis MFA portfolio declined 11% in Q4 due to a tough comparison.
FY27 guidance assumes essentially no sales of virginiamycin in Brazil after Q1; FY26 Brazil virginiamycin sales were $27M.
Free cash flow was only $10M in FY26, impacted by an $86M inventory build related to the acquired MFA business.
positive_highlights: FY26 adjusted EBITDA increased 39% to $255M; Q4 adjusted EBITDA grew 29%.
Legacy Animal Health grew 8% in Q4; full-year legacy MFA up 4%, Nutritional Specialties up 9%, vaccines up 14%.
Mineral Nutrition sales grew 20% in Q4, driven by demand and higher commodity prices.
summary: Q4 FY2026 revenue was $396.7M, up 5% YoY, with adjusted EBITDA up 29% to $255M (FY26) and adjusted EPS up 35% in the quarter. Animal Health legacy MFA grew 11% in Q4, while the acquired Zoetis MFA portfolio declined 11% on a tough comp. FY27 guidance calls for net sales of $1.55B-$1.6B and adjusted EBITDA of $258M-$268M, reflecting a prudent view on Brazil virginiamycin regulatory uncertainty; full-year adjusted EBITDA grew 39% to $255M.

negative_highlights: BEC product sales fell 10% YoY as management deliberately scaled back low-margin categories.
BBM still reported a non-GAAP operating loss of RMB 33M, though it narrowed from RMB 35M a year ago.
Management noted weak consumption data in July 2026, though did not see significant budget shifts from brand partners.
positive_highlights: Group non-GAAP operating income grew 25% YoY to RMB 74M, exceeding prior-year rebased RMB 59M.
BEC achieved record Q2 non-GAAP operating income of RMB 107M, with service revenue up 10% YoY.
BBM gross margin expanded 383 bps YoY to 56.1%, and Gap same-store sales grew in the 20s.
summary: Q2 FY2026: Group revenue grew 7% YoY to RMB 2.7B; non-GAAP operating income reached RMB 74M vs RMB 59M rebased a year ago (25% improvement). BEC revenue grew 5% with record Q2 non-GAAP operating income of RMB 107M; BBM revenue grew 22% with gross margin expansion to 56.1%. Management raised the 2028 non-GAAP operating profit target from RMB 550M to RMB 700M, citing AI-driven productivity gains and strong BBM momentum. Gap same-store sales grew in the 20s for the quarter; full-year BBM top-line growth expected at 20%-25%.

negative_highlights: Full-year gross margin declined 180 bps to 16% due to higher material and labor costs.
Saxdor's Q4 adjusted EBITDA margin was below the 10%-11% guidance due to investment and input costs.
Registrations for the April-June period were down roughly 3% YoY, indicating soft industry demand.
positive_highlights: Q4 legacy sales grew 13.2% with Cobalt segment net sales up 31% and Saltwater up 11.1%.
Q4 adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 200 bps YoY to 11.5%.
Full-year net sales exceeded the raised guidance top end by $29 million.
summary: Malibu Boats reported Q4 FY2026 net sales of $295.5 million, up 42.7% YoY, with adjusted EBITDA of $33.9 million, up 72.7% and margin expanding 200 bps to 11.5%. Legacy sales grew 13.2% to $234.3 million, driven by strong Cobalt and Saltwater unit growth. Full-year net sales of $914.6 million exceeded guidance top end by $29 million. For FY2027, the company guides net sales of $1.080-$1.120 billion and adjusted EBITDA of $101-$109 million, with Saxdor expected to grow mid-teens and legacy brands low to mid-single-digit.

negative_highlights: Non-GAAP gross margin declined 60 bps to 81%, due to lower material-rights revenue and mix.
Reported revenue growth faces a headwind from materially lower material-rights revenue in FY2027.
RAC revenue contribution remains minimal this year, with only 15 paying customers.
positive_highlights: Subscription ARR grew 33% to $1.66B, with net new ARR of $96M accelerating to 35% YoY growth.
Full-year guidance raised by $24M-$25M in subscription ARR, with net new ARR growth rate implied up 700 bps.
Subscription ARR contribution margin improved 460 bps to 14%, and free cash flow was $65.7M.
summary: Rubrik's Q2 FY2027 results exceeded guidance with subscription ARR of $1.66B, up 33% YoY, and net new subscription ARR of approximately $96M. Subscription revenue grew 37% to $407.2M, and total revenue was $427.3M, up 38%. Free cash flow reached $65.7M. The company raised its full-year outlook for subscription ARR to $1.88B-$1.885B, reflecting a 29% growth rate, and expects non-GAAP EPS of $0.47-$0.53. Management noted accelerating net new ARR growth and is investing in R&D and go-to-market for identity and agentic AI products.

negative_highlights: Comp sales growth of 2% was at the midpoint of guidance, with July representing the toughest comparison; management candidly noted expectations for a slightly stronger comp.
New store cannibalization was elevated at 1.5 percentage points of comp in Q2 (vs. typical 1 point), expected to persist for the rest of the year.
Management expressed increased caution on the consumer due to persistent gas price increases and underwhelming sector-wide Q2 comps, leading to maintaining rather than raising sales guidance.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EPS grew 38% in Q2, excluding tariff refunds, on top of 39% growth last year, with the beat driven by 70 bps merchandise margin expansion, supply chain leverage, and SG&A savings.

Total sales grew 11% (on top of 10% last year), supported by record new store openings (178 gross, 149 net in trailing 12 months) with each new store expected to generate over $7 million in annual sales and payback in less than two years.

Company raised full-year EPS guidance to $11.77-$11.97 (16%-18% growth), passing through the entire Q2 earnings beat, while reiterating back-half sales guidance and reaffirming 2027 and 2028 new store targets.
summary: Burlington Stores reported Q2 FY2026 total sales growth of 11% (matching prior year's 10% growth) and comp sales up 2% (at the midpoint of guidance) on top of a 5% comp increase last year. Excluding $55 million in tariff refunds and the resulting $0.64 EPS benefit, adjusted EPS grew 38% to $2.37, exceeding the $2.05-$2.20 guidance, while adjusted EBIT margin expanded 100 bps to 7%, above the 30-60 bps guidance. The company raised full-year EPS guidance to $11.77-$11.97 (up 16%-18%) and reiterated back-half sales guidance, planning to reinvest all tariff refunds into sharper customer values. Management expressed confidence in back-half opportunities but acknowledged consumer caution and weather risks, maintaining disciplined off-price execution.

negative_highlights: Gross margin declined meaningfully: Q4 non-GAAP gross margin fell to 30.9% from 34.7% a year ago, partly due to component price inflation and supply shortages.
Full-year international revenue declined to $219.6 million from $227 million in fiscal 2025, though management expects growth in fiscal 2027.
Q1 fiscal 2027 revenue is expected to be the lowest of the year, with gross margin pressure continuing into Q1 before improving.
positive_highlights: Q4 revenue of $120.9 million, up 4.8% year-over-year, and full-year revenue of $439.7 million, up 1.2%, marking sixth consecutive year of growth.
Backlog up 14% year-over-year to $367 million, with record Q4 bookings.
EMEA revenue up 53% in Q4 and 33% for fiscal 2026, driven by private network wins including defense and energy customers.
summary: Q4 fiscal 2026 revenue was $120.9 million, up 4.8% year-over-year, with non-GAAP EPS of $0.64 and adjusted EBITDA of $11.9 million. Full-year revenue was $439.7 million, up 1.2%, and backlog hit $367 million, up 14% year-over-year. FY2027 guidance was set at $455-$470 million revenue and $50-$55 million adjusted EBITDA, up from FY2026 levels. Gross margin declined due to component cost inflation, but management expects to offset this with price increases and see improvement in the second half of fiscal 2027.

negative_highlights: Full-year revenue guidance reduced by $30 million at the midpoint; pre-tax guidance reduced by $9.5 million at the midpoint
Q2 gross margin contracted 340 basis points to 54.2% due to occupancy deleverage and promotional activity
Commercial segment guidance cut from +20% to flat, driven by the non-repeat of the Walmart program and slower wholesale development
positive_highlights: Halloween launch week was the highest non-fourth quarter sales week in company history and third highest U.S. e-commerce sales week ever
DTC revenue still grew 3% versus 2024, representing the second-highest Q2 DTC sales in company history
Dollar per transaction exceeded last year with strong attachment rates on Promise Pets, and share count reduced over 5% in the past 12 months
summary: Q2 FY2026 revenue declined 7.2% to $115.3 million, with DTC sales down on weaker traffic and summer trend underperformance; pre-tax income fell 24.1% to $11.6 million. Management cut full-year revenue guidance to $500-$525 million (from $530-$550 million) and pre-tax income to $60-$68 million (from $72-$78 million), citing traffic uncertainty, summer product miss, and the non-repeat of the Walmart program. Early Q3 momentum from the Halloween launch showed sequential improvement, but August comparisons remain challenging and performance is still below prior expectations.

negative_highlights: Canadian Banking segments reported 3% negative operating leverage this quarter
Capital Markets provisions increased CAD 148 million QoQ, including an additional CAD 120 million on a legacy utility exposure
Insurance net income down 20% YoY on prior-year favorable items
positive_highlights: Record earnings of CAD 6 billion, up 11% YoY, with revenue growth of 9%
Investment banking revenue up 23% YoY and Wealth Management net income up 32%
Commercial Banking record net income of CAD 936 million, up 12% YoY, with deposit growth of 9%
summary: RBC reported record earnings of CAD 6 billion, up 11% YoY, with diluted EPS of CAD 4.23 (adjusted CAD 4.28, up 11%). Revenue grew 9% YoY, with record revenues across most segments; adjusted operating leverage was 2.4% and the efficiency ratio was 52%. The bank reiterated full-year guidance, expecting positive all-bank operating leverage and mid-single-digit NII growth, while CET1 remains at 13.5%. Credit performance was stable but with a notable CAD 120 million incremental provision on a previously impaired utility borrower.

negative_highlights: Transaction volume fell 74.4% year-over-year to CNY 9.5 billion and net revenue declined 50.9% to CNY 636.9 million
Net loss of CNY 183.6 million versus CNY 519.1 million net income a year earlier; non-GAAP operating loss of CNY 225.7 million
Dividend for the fiscal year suspended and no Q3 guidance issued due to macroeconomic uncertainty
positive_highlights: Cash and cash equivalents increased to CNY 504 million from CNY 43.4 million at the end of the previous quarter
Indonesia partner business volume rose 58% year-over-year and 10% sequentially, while Mexico volume grew 36% sequentially
30-day collection rate improved consecutively quarter-over-quarter and the 90+ day delinquency rate held stable at 2.21%
summary: Jiayin Group reported Q2 FY2026 transaction volume of CNY 9.5 billion, down 74.4% year-over-year, and net revenue of CNY 636.9 million, down 50.9% year-over-year, swinging to a net loss of CNY 183.6 million from CNY 519.1 million net income a year ago, with basic and diluted net loss per share of CNY 0.89. The company suspended its dividend for the fiscal year and declined to issue Q3 guidance, citing industry-wide liquidity tightening and regulatory compliance effects. Non-GAAP loss from operations was CNY 225.7 million versus CNY 737.6 million income a year earlier, while cash and cash equivalents rose to CNY 504 million from CNY 43.4 million at the end of the prior quarter. The 90+ day delinquency rate was 2.21%, stable sequentially, and the 30-day collection rate improved quarter-over-quarter.

negative_highlights: China loan volume down roughly 50% in July due to industry funding tightening following the Jizi incident.
Early risk indicators up around 20% versus Q2, with collection capacity weakened by regulatory actions.
Funding costs rose 30 bps sequentially to 3.7% in Q2 and are expected to tick up further in the coming quarters.
positive_highlights: Overseas operating profit rose 17% sequentially to RMB 154 million, doubling YoY.
Overseas unique borrowers more than doubled YoY to 5.3 million; Australia unique borrowers up 22% sequentially.
Group cash and note weakness in-term investments remained strong at RMB 7.5 billion as of latest data, providing liquidity cushion.
summary: Q2 2026 group revenue rose 6% sequentially to RMB 3.4 billion, with net profit of RMB 427 million up 1% sequentially. Overseas revenue grew 18% YoY to RMB 930 million, and overseas operating profit rose 17% sequentially to RMB 154 million. Management reiterated full-year revenue guidance of RMB 11.5-12.9 billion but now expects to land in the lower half due to funding and credit tightening that began in July, with China loan volume down ~50% in July. Overseas volume is expected to grow double-digit YoY for 2026.

negative_highlights: Overseas revenue grew only 15% versus guided high-double-digit, with distributor revenue down 10% and Asia and Latin America revenue declining low single digit and low double digit respectively
Adjusted operating profit fell 6% YoY to RMB 1.49 billion and adjusted net profit fell 1.7%, with overseas profit contribution falling from 35%-40% in 2023 to 10%-15% in H1
H2 guidance implies sharp deceleration to high single-digit group revenue growth and flat TOP TOY, with a net reduction of 50-70 overseas stores planned
positive_highlights: H1 revenue grew 22.4% to RMB 11.5 billion, slightly ahead of the 20%-22% guidance, with China growing 26.2% (fastest H1 in three years) versus Q2 guidance of only low double digits
Proprietary IP reached the RMB 1 billion full-year target by end-July; YOYO generated nearly RMB 500 million in H1 and TOP TOY's NOMI surpassed RMB 300 million cumulative GMV
Shareholder returns of RMB 1.31 billion in H1, with buybacks of RMB 520 million already exceeding the full-year 2025 total
summary: H1 revenue rose 22.4% to RMB 11.5 billion and China revenue grew 26.2% with mid-single-digit same-store growth, but overseas revenue grew only 15% against guided high-double-digit and distributor revenue fell 10%. H1 adjusted operating profit fell 6% YoY (up 5% ex-forex) and adjusted net profit fell 1.7%, with gross margin flat at 44.3% diluted by about 0.6pp of one-off U.S. tariff refunds. For H2 management guided group revenue to high single-digit growth (mid-double-digit full year), China mid-double-digit, overseas low single-digit, and TOP TOY flat; they plan to slow overseas store openings and take a net reduction of 50-70 overseas stores. Company repurchased RMB 520 million in H1, exceeding all of 2025's total, and declared no interim dividend, prioritizing buybacks at current valuation.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to RMB 316.7 million ($46.5 million) from RMB 11.8 million a year earlier; loss per share was RMB 13.65 versus RMB 0.43
Cryptocurrency fair-value loss of RMB 250.5 million versus a RMB 48.6 million gain in the prior-year period, tied to lower BNB prices
Revenue fell to RMB 2.8 million from RMB 8.3 million and gross loss was RMB 5.8 million, driven by lower iPollo V Series sales volume
positive_highlights: Cash and cash equivalents rose modestly to RMB 9.0 million at June 30, 2026 from RMB 8.5 million at December 31, 2025
Completed $3.2 million of buybacks as of August 26, 2026 under the up-to-$25 million repurchase program, with 1,117,401 shares repurchased as of June 30, 2026
Launched the iPollo ClawPC A1 Mini and continued developing the OpenClaw ecosystem as a new AI-focused product line
summary: Nano Labs reported a first half 2026 net loss of RMB 316.7 million ($46.5 million), or RMB 13.65 per share, versus RMB 11.8 million (RMB 0.43 per share) a year earlier, driven by a RMB 250.5 million fair-value loss on cryptocurrencies from lower BNB prices. Revenue fell to RMB 2.8 million from RMB 8.3 million as iPollo V Series volumes dropped, producing a gross loss of RMB 5.8 million and an operating loss of RMB 291.7 million versus prior-year operating income of RMB 10.6 million. Operating expenses swung to RMB 285.8 million from prior-year operating income of RMB 21.3 million, with G&A up 29.5% and R&D up 39.8%. Cash stood at RMB 9.0 million at June 30, 2026; management outlined strategic AI/Web3 and digital-asset initiatives but gave no quantitative guidance for the second half.

negative_highlights: VLCC order book at ~33.5% of the existing fleet and close to 40% of the efficient fleet, approaching 2008-2009 cycle levels
Suezmax cash break-even rose to $25,700/day, above the VLCC break-even, due to increased dry dock costs and drawn revolver capacity
positive_highlights: Best-ever quarterly profit of $659.2 million and adjusted profit of $580.2 million, with adjusted profit up $235.3 million from Q1 2026
VLCC Q3 2026 bookings at $156,900/day on 86% of days, above the $152,700/day Q2 average
Weighted average interest margin reduced ~52 bps from 178 bps at Q1 2026 to 126 bps, with no meaningful debt maturities until 2030
summary: Frontline reported its best quarterly results ever, with Q2 2026 profit of $659.2 million ($2.96 per share) and adjusted profit of $580.2 million ($2.61 per share), up $235.3 million from Q1 on stronger TCE earnings. VLCC TCE averaged $152,700/day, Suezmax $111,400/day, and LR2/Aframax $92,400/day, with Q3 bookings so far at $156,900 (86% of VLCC days), $117,400 (79% of Suezmax days), and $81,000 (70% of LR2 days). Liquidity stands at $1.2 billion with no meaningful debt maturities until 2030 and a 52bp reduction in financing margins. Management described an exceptional tanker market driven by inefficiencies and inventory draws, but flagged the VLCC order book near 40% of the efficient fleet as a longer-term concern.

negative_highlights: Reported TCE of $74,000 per available day came in below company guidance of $81,000 per available day.
Product Services reported a net loss after tax of $31 million, driven by a $145 million negative mark-to-market movement, despite a $127 million realized trading gain.
Spot VLGC trade flows remain highly exposed to the ongoing closure of the Strait of Hormuz, with 30+ vessels idling in the Arabian Gulf/Indian Ocean.
positive_highlights: Q3 2026 guidance of ~$88,000 per available day for 92% of days is far above the $24,900 per day all-in cash breakeven.
Dividend declared at $0.95 per share, representing 100% payout of quarterly shipping NPAT, above the 75% policy minimum.
Net leverage fell to 23.5% from 26.3% at the end of Q1, with liquidity of $773 million and ROE of 27%.
summary: BW LPG reported Q2 2026 TCE income of $74,000 per available day, below the prior company guidance of $81,000 per day, with the shortfall attributed to negative IFRS 15 and FFA adjustments of $16.4M and $12M respectively. Profit after minority interest was $120M, or $0.79 per share, and the board declared a $0.95 dividend equal to 100% of shipping NPAT, exceeding the 75% minimum payout policy. For Q3 2026, the company guided to about $88,000 per day fixed for 92% of available days, well above its all-in cash breakeven of $24,900 per day, as Middle East disruptions, the Panama Canal drought, and longer Cape of Good Hope routes tighten effective vessel supply.

negative_highlights: Q3 coverage of 80% of earning days at $30,716/day is materially below Q2 fleet-wide TCE of $44,093/day and spot rates near $50,000/day
Dirty loadings East of Suez still roughly 30% below pre-crisis levels and clean products on water 12% below pre-conflict levels, equivalent to 180 MRs of displaced demand
Order book of about 60 million deadweight tons for 2026-2029, with a potentially stronger net impact from 2028, plus a stated risk of losing inefficiency effects if Hormuz and the Red Sea normalize
positive_highlights: Net profit of $277.8 million, the strongest quarter since Q3 2022, up from $75.3 million a year ago
Net LTV improved to 13% from 20.2% in Q1, supporting a $250 million dividend at the maximum 90% payout ratio
$39.3 million gain on sale from divesting one LR1, two MRs and three Handy vessels, with a further $13.3 million JV gain in Q3
summary: Hafnia reported Q2 FY2026 net profit of $277.8 million, its strongest quarter since Q3 2022, versus $75.3 million a year ago, with TCE income of $372.9 million and adjusted EBITDA of $287.3 million. The result included a $39.3 million gain on vessel disposals, bringing half-year net profit to $457.5 million, while net LTV fell to 13% from 20.2% and a $250 million dividend ($0.5003/share) was declared at the 90% payout ratio. Q3 guidance was framed through coverage: 80% of Q3 earning days booked at $30,716/day and 53% of H2 2026 days at $28,917/day, both below the exceptional Q2 spot rates of roughly $50,000/day but well above cash breakeven. Management described the market as easing but constructive into Q4, supported by inventory restocking (about 260 million OECD barrels by mid-2027), Red Sea and Hormuz disruption, and a clean fleet down 3% year-to-date, with CEO Mikael Skov handing over to Søren Steenberg Jensen on September 1 and no formal numerical guidance provided.

negative_highlights: Total revenue fell 3.7% sequentially to RMB 3,415 million, with total GMV down 3.3% sequentially
Greater China GMV declined 4.5% sequentially and average monthly GMV per Greater China tea house fell to RMB 338,259 from RMB 356,080
Non-GAAP net margin compressed to 14.3% from 18.9% a year ago, and non-GAAP operating margin slipped to 16.1% from 17.1% in Q1
positive_highlights: Overseas GMV reached RMB 504 million, up 114.3% year-over-year and 18.2% sequentially
GAAP net income margin rose to 13.6% from 2.3% a year ago; non-GAAP G&A ratio fell to 9.1% from 13.2%
Same-store sales improved in Q3 with July down low single digits and August expected to turn positive year-over-year
summary: Chagee reported Q2 FY2026 total revenue of RMB 3,415 million, up 2.5% year-over-year but down 3.7% sequentially, with total GMV of RMB 7,660 million down 3.3% sequentially and Greater China GMV down 4.5%. GAAP net income was RMB 465 million (13.6% margin, up from 2.3% a year ago), and non-GAAP net margin was 14.3%, flat sequentially but down from 18.9% a year ago. Margins and cost ratios improved sharply (non-GAAP G&A 9.1% vs 13.2% a year ago), while overseas GMV grew 114.3% year-over-year; same-store sales in July fell low single digits with August expected to turn positive. No formal financial guidance was given, but management cited same-store recovery and continued buybacks ($30 million of the $150 million program executed as of August 24).

negative_highlights: NPL ratio rose 49 bps QoQ to 6.09%, exceeding the system's 54 bp increase
Cost of risk at 7.13% remains elevated, with full-year guidance of 6.5% implying only gradual improvement
Management expects activity NIM in pesos to face moderate pressure as interest rates decline
positive_highlights: Net income of ARS 131.6 billion rose 44.6% QoQ, driving ROE to 12.2% from 8.3% in Q1
NIM net of monetary position loss improved to 14.7% from 14% QoQ
Net fees grew around 35% YoY and early-stage delinquencies are improving with new vintages performing better
summary: BBVA Argentina reported Q2 2026 inflation-adjusted net income of ARS 131.6 billion, up 44.6% QoQ, lifting quarterly ROE to 12.2% from 8.3% in Q1. NIM net of monetary position loss improved to 14.7% from 14% and the efficiency ratio reached 45%. However, the NPL ratio rose 49 bps QoQ to 6.09% and cost of risk was 7.13%, though management guided to NPL stabilization around 5.5% and cost of risk of 6.5% for full-year 2026. Full-year guidance includes real loan growth of around 10%, deposits growing 5%–10%, an efficiency ratio below 45%, and a real ROE in the low teens, consistent with prior guidance.

negative_highlights: Q3 aesthetic revenue guidance of RMB 352-362 million implies ~91.7%-97.2% YoY growth, a marked slowdown from Q2's ~130%
Information and reservation services revenue fell 35% YoY to RMB 87.9 million on fewer subscribing medical service providers
Other services revenue dropped 48.2% YoY and sales of medical products fell 2.8% YoY; GAAP net loss of RMB 22.7 million persists with cost of revenues up 53% YoY
positive_highlights: Aesthetic treatment revenue of RMB 331.4 million grew ~130% YoY and beat the upper end of guidance by ~5%, the fifth straight quarter above the guidance top end
Clinic gross margin expanded 3.8pp YoY to 28.1% and 1pp QoQ; profitable centers rose to 47 and 51 generated positive operating cash flow
Same-store sales growth improved to 52% from 14% in the prior-year period, with referrals over 50% of new customers and acquisition cost under 10% of revenue
summary: Aesthetic treatment services revenue reached RMB 331.4 million, up ~130% YoY and exceeding the upper end of guidance for the fifth consecutive quarter (5% above the top end), lifting group revenue 33% YoY to a record ~RMB 510 million. Net loss attributable to So-Young narrowed 37% YoY to RMB 22.7 million, with clinic gross margin up 3.8pp YoY to 28.1% and 47 of 65 centers profitable. Q3 guidance of RMB 352-362 million implies ~91.7%-97.2% YoY growth, a sharp deceleration from Q2's ~130%, and the legacy information/reservation segment fell 35% YoY while other services dropped 48.2% YoY. Same-store sales growth accelerated to 52% from 14% a year earlier, and the loyalty program creates a 3-5pp deferral between service delivery and recognized revenue.

negative_highlights: Net income of CNY 101 million fell 49.7% or about CNY 100 million quarter-over-quarter, and management guided to a net loss in Q3
Credit facilitation service income dropped 43.6% to CNY 508 million as loan volume declined 4.3% sequentially amid industry-wide funding tightening
Day-1 delinquency rose roughly 9.5% QoQ and 90+ day delinquency rose from 3.5% to 3.6%, with further increases and declining collection rates expected in Q3
positive_highlights: Installment e-commerce gross profit rose 58.7% to CNY 329 million with gross margin expanding from 9.4% to 14.1% quarter-over-quarter
Fintech empowerment loan volume grew 8% sequentially, lifting combined fintech empowerment and e-commerce volume contribution to 45%
Operating expenses fell 17.6% or CNY 244 million quarter-over-quarter, and cash position stood at CNY 2.5 billion
summary: Lexin reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of CNY 3.19-3.2 billion with net profit of CNY 101 million, down 49.7% or about CNY 100 million quarter-over-quarter, on loan volume of CNY 55.43 billion (down 4.3% sequentially). Credit facilitation service income fell 43.6% to CNY 508 million and tech empowerment service income fell 14.4% to CNY 473 million, partly offset by installment e-commerce gross profit rising 58.7% to CNY 329 million with gross margin expanding from 9.4% to 14.1%. Management guided to a net loss in Q3, citing sharply lower loan originations, higher credit costs and one-time severance costs, and declined to provide specific full-year guidance; the board also changed the dividend policy from semi-annual to annual. Day-1 delinquency rose about 9.5% QoQ and 90+ day delinquency rose from 3.5% to 3.6%, with further increases expected in Q3.

negative_highlights: Revenue flat at $0.3 million versus Q2 2025 and net loss widened to $4.3 million from $3.9 million
Company raised an additional $3.75 million via a registered direct offering, with cash of $13.1 million funding operations only into the first half of 2027
No APHEXDA sales guidance provided and management acknowledged a new pancreatic cancer approval (Revolution Medicines' daraxonrasib) could change the CheMo4METPANC treatment landscape
positive_highlights: GLIX1 Phase I/IIa enrollment progressing on plan, with dosing in the second of five cohorts and the third cohort expected to start in September
New preclinical data showed the low-dose GLIX1 plus olaparib combination produced tumor reduction comparable to cisplatin in an HR-proficient ovarian cancer PDX model
Phase I data for GLIX1 remains guided to the first half of 2027, and abstracts were accepted at EANO 2026, SNO 2026 and ESMO
summary: BioLineRx reported Q2 2026 revenue of $0.3 million from APHEXDA royalties, flat versus Q2 2025, with a net loss of $4.3 million versus $3.9 million a year earlier and R&D rising to $2.9 million on GLIX1 spending. Cash and equivalents stood at $13.1 million, sufficient into the first half of 2027, supplemented by a $3.75 million registered direct offering announced the prior Friday. Management highlighted GLIX1 Phase I/IIa enrollment tracking to plan with the third cohort dosing in September and Phase I data expected in the first half of 2027, alongside new preclinical PARP-inhibitor synergy data, while giving no APHEXDA sales guidance and noting the Revolution Medicines pancreatic approval could alter the CheMo4METPANC landscape. No financial guidance was issued and no specific beat or raise was cited.

negative_highlights: Quarterly book-to-bill of 0.6 (0.8 trailing twelve months), with large recompete awards slipping to the right on slower procurement and new fixed-price directives
Second-half margins guided down to the high 9% range from 11% in the first half on planned investments
Adjusted EPS of $3.01 declined year-over-year due to the prior-year favorable legal settlement
positive_highlights: Guidance raised across revenue, EBITDA, and EPS: revenue midpoint lifted 2% to $7.25 billion and EBITDA margin guide lifted 20 bps to 10.3%-10.5%
Q2 organic revenue growth ~5%, with on-contract growth of 9%, roughly double the prior-year rate, on an improving outlay environment
Free cash flow of $131 million in the quarter; net leverage declined to 3.0x and recompete win rate exceeded 90%
summary: SAIC reported Q2 FY2027 revenue of $1.9 billion, up ~5% organically, adjusted EBITDA of $193 million (10.3% margin) up modestly year-over-year ex a prior-year legal settlement, and adjusted EPS of $3.01, down year-over-year on the prior-period settlement offset by lower share count. Free cash flow was $131 million and net leverage fell to 3.0x. Management raised FY2027 guidance for revenue (midpoint $7.25 billion), EBITDA (10.3%-10.5% margin, +20 bps), and EPS, while noting a book-to-bill of 0.6 for the quarter (0.8 trailing twelve months) on procurement delays and an expected second-half margin step-down to the high 9% range. The company also quantified Project ORBIT at ~$150 million in annual run-rate savings by the end of a three-year implementation, with a path to ~11% margins in FY2030.

negative_highlights: U.S. PGM adjusted EBITDA fell 56% YoY to $66 million, partly on the prior-year Section 45X credit that was not repeated
Stillwater union labor agreements for two bargaining units remain unresolved after two months of negotiation
SA gold H2 cost guidance of ZAR 1.75-1.84 million/kg reflects infrastructure and electricity cost pressure, with Kloof at ZAR 2.4 million/kg
positive_highlights: SA PGM adjusted EBITDA up 302% to ZAR 19.2 billion at a 44% AISC margin on a 67% higher basket
SA gold adjusted EBITDA a record ZAR 9 billion, up 87% at a 39% margin, with cash generation up 267%
Recycling adjusted EBITDA of $164 million at a 13% margin with 63% cash conversion and 2.8 million ounces gold equivalent produced
summary: Sibanye reported record 1H revenue and EBITDA more than doubled, with South Africa PGM AISC margin of 44% on a 67% higher basket and SA gold adjusted EBITDA a record ZAR 9 billion, up 87% at a 39% margin. Group net operating cash was a record, debt was reduced, and a dividend was maintained at a 25-35% payout. U.S. PGM adjusted EBITDA fell 56% YoY to $66 million on the prior-year 45X credit, while recycling and Century zinc delivered strong cash conversion. The board approved Burnstone and Mt Lyell projects, but Stillwater union labor agreements remain unresolved and gold costs were guided to ZAR 1.75-1.84 million/kg for the second half.

negative_highlights: Gross margin rate of 21.1% declined sequentially due to higher AI server mix
CSG operating margin expected to moderate to roughly 6% in Q3
Significant supply constraints persist across DRAM, NAND, CPUs, and other components
positive_highlights: Revenue up 58% to $47 billion and EPS up 203% to $7.04, both records
Full-year revenue guidance raised by $25 billion to $192 billion
AI orders of $60.9 billion and AI backlog of $95 billion, with customer count surpassing 6,500
summary: Dell reported Q2 FY27 record revenue of $47 billion, up 58% year over year, and record non-GAAP EPS of $7.04, up 203%. ISG revenue rose 89% to $31.8 billion with a 15% operating margin (up 620 bps), AI server revenue was $16.4 billion, and AI orders hit a record $60.9 billion with backlog at $95 billion. Management raised full-year guidance by $25 billion to $192 billion in revenue, with EPS of $25.50 (up ~150%), and guided Q3 revenue to $49 billion (up ~80%) with AI server revenue of $19 billion. Key change versus prior period: the company cited continued supply constraints (DRAM, NAND, CPUs) but expects a stronger second half, driven by AI and traditional infrastructure demand.

negative_highlights: Flex adoption is expected to shift approximately $13 million of revenue out of FY2027 into future periods due to timing of revenue recognition.
CRPO saw a three-point headwind relative to RPO from the absence of Flex commitments, which are excluded from current RPO.
Adjusted free cash flow was $9.8 million, a 3% margin, with the timing of collections weighing on the number this quarter.
positive_highlights: Revenue of $286.3 million beat guidance by roughly five points, with 21% year-over-year growth.
Net ARR grew 42% year-over-year, the second-highest growth quarter in four years, and gross bookings were the largest in company history.
Full-year revenue guidance raised to $1.129-$1.133 billion and Non-GAAP EPS guidance raised to $0.85-$0.87.
summary: GitLab reported Q2 FY2027 revenue of $286.3 million, up 21% year-over-year and roughly five points ahead of guidance, with Non-GAAP operating income of $42.6 million (15% margin). Net ARR grew 42% year-over-year, the strongest gross bookings quarter in company history, and dollar-based net retention rose to 117%. Management raised full-year revenue guidance to $1.129-$1.133 billion (18%-19% growth) and Non-GAAP EPS to $0.85-$0.87, citing broad-based strength and public sector recovery. The quarter included the launch of the Flex consumption model, which is expected to introduce near-term revenue recognition timing noise but is not included in guidance.

negative_highlights: Extra note week added ~670 bps to organic growth, making the underlying 52-week trend materially lower than the 13.7% headline
Neuromodulation grew only 3% globally on ongoing SCS market softness and DBS replacement headwinds
Gross margin mix was unfavorable by 50 bps, largely from diabetes and CAS, and FY operating margin expansion guidance was trimmed to ~50 bps (from the prior ~60 bps cited by an analyst)
positive_highlights: Organic revenue growth of 13.7% with revenue of $9.8B, aided by a $570M (670 bps) extra-week benefit; management said ex-extra week it was the strongest quarter in nearly eight years
Cardiac Ablation Solutions grew 88% worldwide (139% in the U.S.) and surpassed $2B in trailing 12-month revenue ahead of schedule
FY2027 guidance raised: organic revenue growth to 7.25%-7.75% (+50 bps) and adjusted EPS to $5.94-$6.00, with adjusted EPS of $1.45 beating guidance midpoint and consensus by $0.06
summary: Medtronic reported Q1 FY2027 revenue of $9.8 billion, up 13.7% organic, and adjusted EPS of $1.45, $0.06 above the midpoint of guidance and consensus. The quarter benefited from an extra watching week that added roughly $570 million, or 670 bps, to organic growth; excluding it, management called it the strongest quarterly performance in nearly eight years. Guidance was raised: FY2027 organic revenue growth to 7.25%-7.75% (up 50 bps) and EPS to $5.94-$6.00, with Q2 organic growth of ~6% and EPS of $1.32-$1.34. Adjusted gross margin was 65.2% (+10 bps) and adjusted operating margin 23.7% (+10 bps), with FY operating margin expansion guided to ~50 bps.

negative_highlights: Material and chip costs rose about RMB 14,000 per car versus late last year and are expected to add another RMB 2,000-3,000 per car in the second half
SG&A expenses increased 22.5% quarter-over-quarter to RMB 4.4 billion, including roughly RMB 500 million of one-off new-product launch costs
Onvo's customer conversion and order momentum were described as relatively moderate, with brand awareness lagging NIO's level from five to six years ago
positive_highlights: Vehicle margin expanded to 18.5% from 10.3% in Q2 last year, with total gross margin at 18.4% versus 10.0% a year ago
Total revenue rose 69.1% year-over-year to RMB 32.1 billion and vehicle sales rose 80.1% year-over-year
Cash position increased to RMB 56.7 billion with positive operating cash flow and free cash flow, plus adjusted net profit of RMB 26.1 million
summary: NIO reported Q2 FY2026 total revenue of RMB 32.1 billion, up 69.1% year-over-year and 25.9% quarter-over-quarter, with vehicle sales of RMB 29.1 billion (up 80.1% YoY) on 107,658 deliveries (+49.4% YoY). Vehicle margin was 18.5% versus 10.3% a year ago and 18.8% last quarter, and overall gross margin was 18.4% versus 10.0% last year and 19.0% last quarter. Adjusted net profit was RMB 26.1 million and cash rose to RMB 56.7 billion with positive operating and free cash flow. Q3 delivery guidance is 108,000-111,000 units and Q4 is targeted at over 40,000 units per month, while management expects Q3/Q4 vehicle margin to hold near Q2 levels despite RMB 2,000-3,000 per car of additional material cost pressure.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA margin of 9.9% fell well below the approximately 16% full-year guidance rate, held down by a $12 million FX remeasurement charge and $8 million accelerated investment
Free cash flow was a use of $90 million, with operating cash flow negative $49 million and separation/stand-up activities consuming $111 million
Q1 new pumps sold rose only 7.7% year over year to 34,000, and were down sequentially
positive_highlights: Organic revenue growth of 15.8% (low double digits ex-extra week) accelerated from 8.7% in Q4, with U.S. growth up to 13.1% from 1.5%
FY2027 organic revenue growth guidance raised to approximately 10.5% from approximately 10%
Adjusted gross margin of 55.9% came in ahead of expectations, with Simplera yields trending better than modeled helping offset FX headwinds
summary: Q1 FY2027 revenue was $843 million, up 15.8% organic, with U.S. growth accelerating to 13.1% from 1.5% in Q4 and international up 16.9%; the extra week added about 4.6 points, leaving low-double-digit underlying growth versus 8.7% in Q4. Adjusted EBITDA was $83 million (9.9% margin), depressed about 230 bps by an $8 million pull-forward of Flex/Fit investment and a $12 million FX remeasurement charge; excluding these, margin was 12.2%, with adjusted gross margin at 55.9% and Simplera yields trending better than modeled. Management raised FY2027 organic revenue growth guidance to approximately 10.5% from approximately 10% and reaffirmed FY2027 adjusted EBITDA margin guidance of approximately 16%, with margin expansion weighted to the second half. Flex launched in the U.S. in late June, Fit was filed with FDA ahead of plan for a summer 2027 launch, Vivera pivotal enrollment completed early, Flex received CE mark ahead of target, and the next-generation extended-wear sensor received IDE approval for an October pivotal start.

negative_highlights: Total revenue fell ~50% QoQ to $50.8 million, as self-mining hash rate was deliberately reduced and capacity shifted to leasing.
Net loss of ~$81.6 million, including ~$51 million of non-cash mining machine impairment and disposal losses, and adjusted EBITDA was negative $10.7 million.

No formal Q3 guidance; management only expects mining revenue to be roughly stable, with risk of summer power curtailment, and the AI revenue contribution expected to be small and starting from a limited signed contract base.
positive_highlights: Average cash mining cost fell ~35% sequentially to $73,313 per Bitcoin, with month-by-month decline, aided by power-price reduction clauses in hosted contracts.
Signed first AI infrastructure customer contract after June 30; revenue recognition expected to begin in Q3, moving the segment from build-out to commercialization.
Implemented a Bitcoin hedging program (note weakness in-term BTC loan ~$8 million) to reduce cash flow sensitivity, and cut Q2 cost of revenue to $50.7 million from $99.6 million in Q1.
summary: Cango reported Q2 FY2026 total revenue of ~$50.8 million, with ~$47.4 million from Bitcoin mining (656 BTC mined), roughly 50% lower sequentially versus Q1's ~$100M+ due to a deliberate hash rate reduction. Net loss was ~$81.6 million, driven mainly by a $42.9 million mining machine impairment and an $8.5 million disposal loss. Cash mining cost fell to $73,313 per Bitcoin (down ~35% QoQ), with all-in cost of $98,405, and adjusted EBITDA was a loss of $10.7 million. Management gave no formal guidance but expects AI-related revenue (first customer contract signed post-June 30) to begin in Q3 and said mining hash rate should be roughly stable in Q3, aside from possible summer power curtailment.

negative_highlights: Working capital was 18.3% on a 12-month basis, above the 15.5%-16.5% target, and management flagged it as the primary headwind to cash conversion
Chemical markets remain challenging with excess capacity and weak demand; full-year US ethylene margins were still 8% below FY2025
Free cash flow of ZAR 11.9 billion was 5% lower than the prior year including the Transnet benefit, and impairments were booked on the Secunda liquid fuels refinery CGU and SA polyethylene CGU
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA rose 17% to ZAR 61 billion, with H2 EBITDA of roughly ZAR 40 billion versus ZAR 21 billion in H1
Net debt reduced 11% to $3.3 billion, the lowest in 10 years and ahead of the below $3.7 billion FY2026 target
Secunda production reached a five-year high of 7.26 million tons, helping cut the SA oil breakeven to $49/bbl and lifting free cash flow 26% excluding the prior Transnet benefit
summary: Sasol reported FY2026 adjusted EBITDA up 17% to ZAR 61 billion, with sales volumes up 4%, cash fixed costs flat, capex down 18% to ZAR 21 billion, and free cash flow of ZAR 11.9 billion (up 26% excluding the prior-year Transnet benefit). Net debt fell 11% to $3.3 billion, ahead of the below $3.7 billion target, and the Southern African oil breakeven improved to $49/bbl on a five-year-high Secunda production of 7.26 million tons. Guidance remains unchanged on the path to net debt below $3 billion sustainably between FY2027 and FY2028, though working capital came in above target at 18.3% and chemical markets remain below historical levels.

negative_highlights: Cash and equivalents fell $679 million sequentially to $764.3 million due to the DustPhotonics acquisition outlay
Operating cash flow fell $92 million sequentially to $90.2 million on working capital changes, with inventory up $62.2 million to $313.1 million
Customer concentration remains high with top four end customers at 33%, 28%, 13%, and 10% of revenue
positive_highlights: Revenue of $479 million rose 10% sequentially and 115% year over year, above the high end of guidance
Non-GAAP net income of $236.3 million more than doubled year over year and non-GAAP operating margin was 48.2%
Full-year FY2027 outlook reiterated for more than 85% revenue growth and more than $600 million in optical revenue, with Q2 revenue guidance of $525-535 million
summary: Credo reported Q1 FY2027 revenue of $479 million, up 10% sequentially and 115% year over year, above the high end of guidance, with non-GAAP gross margin of 68%, non-GAAP net income of $236.3 million (up 4% sequentially and more than doubling YoY), and a 48.2% non-GAAP operating margin. Q2 guidance is $525-535 million with gross margin of 67-69%, and full-year FY2027 revenue growth is reiterated at more than 85% with optical revenue exceeding $600 million. The key change versus prior periods is the emergence of optics as a second growth engine via DustPhotonics PIC revenue and ZeroFlap ramp, while cash fell $679 million on the DustPhotonics acquisition and Q1 operating cash flow declined $92 million sequentially to $90.2 million on working capital.

negative_highlights: Gross margin of 48.9% is pressured by lower-margin loyalty and professional services revenue mix.
Reported operating loss widened to $128.1 million from $32.4 million, and net loss widened to $139.5 million from $57.9 million.
Operating cash burn increased to $96.1 million from $19.8 million, with only $33.2 million of unrestricted cash remaining.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew ~1,970% YoY to $130.8 million, nearly 3x the full-year 2025 total.
Customer base expanded to more than 1,640 from just over 950 at year-end.
Google selected Rezolve's proprietary distributed database technology for infrastructure deployment covering ~100 TB across 10 blockchain networks.
summary: Rezolve Ai reported H1 FY2026 revenue of $130.8 million, up approximately 1,970% from $6.3 million in H1 2025, with a customer base expanding to over 1,640 from roughly 950 at year-end. Gross profit was $63.9 million (48.9% margin), while the reported operating loss widened to $128.1 million and adjusted EBITDA loss was $32.6 million. Management reaffirmed full-year 2026 revenue guidance of approximately $360 million—implying roughly $229 million in H2—and reiterated its target of at least $500 million in ARR exiting the year, citing seasonal H2 weighting, a larger customer base, and partner-led distribution. The company ended the period with $33.2 million in cash plus $67.4 million restricted cash, after raising approximately $250 million in gross equity capital during the half.

negative_highlights: Q3 total revenue guidance of $756-761M implies just 20-21% YoY growth, a deceleration from 30% in Q2, partly due to Atlas comps and prudence on Q4 consumption.
EA and other revenue growth, while strong this quarter at 36%, is guided roughly flat in the second half, highlighting the unpredictability of multi-year deals.
positive_highlights: Total revenue grew 30% YoY to $772M, the highest quarterly growth since FY2024, with Atlas up ~29% and EA/other up 36% YoY.
Full-year Atlas growth guidance raised to ~27% (a 300 bps increase) and EA/other raised to ~11% from mid-single digits.
Net ARR expansion rate increased to 122% from 119% a year ago, with a record 2,900 net new customers added.
summary: MongoDB reported Q2 FY2027 total revenue of $772M, up 30% YoY (vs 24% a year ago), with Atlas revenue up ~29% (fifth straight quarter near that level) and EA and other up 36% YoY; non-GAAP operating margin was 24% and non-GAAP EPS was $1.90. Net new customers hit a record 2,900, net ARR expansion rose to 122%, and RPO grew 91% YoY to $1.52B. Management raised full-year Atlas growth guidance to ~27% (up 300 bps) and EA/other full-year growth to ~11% (from mid-single digits), while Q3 total revenue guidance of $756-761M implies a sharp deceleration to 20-21% growth. The prior-quarter trend of accelerating total revenue and consistent Atlas growth continued, but the Q3 guide reflects a meaningful step-down that management framed as prudence.

negative_highlights: Q4 gross margin declined 100 basis points year over year to 74.8%, and full-year gross margin fell 60 basis points to 75.8%.
Management expects rising commodity costs, particularly memory and storage, to persist in the hardware business, and cloud hosting costs to grow faster than total revenue in FY2027.
positive_highlights: Q4 revenue grew 34% year over year to $3.41 billion, with full-year revenue of $11.5 billion, up 24%.
NGS ARR reached $9.1 billion, up 63%, with net new NGS ARR of nearly $1 billion in Q4, almost double the prior year.
Non-GAAP EPS of $1.02 exceeded the high end of guidance by $0.04, and Q4 adjusted free cash flow grew 35% to $1.29 billion.
summary: Palo Alto Networks reported Q4 FY2026 revenue of $3.41 billion, up 34%, and full-year revenue of $11.5 billion, up 24%. Non-GAAP EPS was $1.02, exceeding the high end of guidance by $0.04, and Q4 RPO reached $21.2 billion (up 34%) with NGS ARR at $9.1 billion (up 63%). The company exceeded guidance across all metrics and management said FY2027 guidance is set to exceed consensus, but gross margin declined 100 bps to 74.8% on SaaS mix and rising memory/storage costs.

negative_highlights: Total revenue declined about 1% sequentially, driven by legacy payment processing seasonality
Total revenue per AHSC fell about 2% sequentially
Subscription pricing is being moderated, with some second-half revenue shifted toward Network Solutions
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA rose $10.8 million year-over-year to $32.9 million, a 25% margin
Fifth consecutive quarter of positive net income at $1.9 million
Ninth consecutive quarter of positive operating and free cash flow; FCF of $13.8 million up $4.2 million year-over-year
summary: Phreesia reported Q2 FY2027 revenue of $129.5 million, up 10% year-over-year but down about 1% sequentially, with Adjusted EBITDA of $32.9 million (25% margin) and net income of $1.9 million, its fifth consecutive positive net income quarter. Average healthcare services clients rose to 4,744, up 36 sequentially and 277 year-over-year, while total revenue per AHSC of $27,289 rose 4% year-over-year but fell about 2% sequentially on payment processing seasonality. Management maintained its FY2027 revenue outlook of $510-$520 million and Adjusted EBITDA outlook of $125-$135 million, and continued to expect mid-single-digit AHSC growth and low-single-digit revenue per AHSC growth. The company reduced debt principal by over $23 million and generated $18.3 million in operating cash flow and $13.8 million in free cash flow, though commentary indicated some subscription revenue is being moderated to support downstream network and payments growth.

negative_highlights: SG&A jumped to $15.6 million from $6.2 million on higher incentive compensation and restricted stock awards
Management said it lacks clarity on Illinois Commerce Commission approval of the roughly five-mile connector pipeline, which it expects will cause the longest delay
No imminent third-party CO2 project despite excess injection well capacity
positive_highlights: Net income of $34.9 million, or $1.06 per diluted share, was a record second-quarter EPS versus $0.22 a year ago
Gross profit rose to $53.3 million from $14.3 million, and grew roughly 144% year-over-year even excluding 45Z tax credits
Balance sheet carries no bank debt with $379.5 million in cash, equivalents, and note weakness in-term investments
summary: REX reported Q2 net sales of $168.5 million versus $158.6 million a year ago, with gross profit of $53.3 million versus $14.3 million, aided by $18.4 million in 45Z production tax credit income. Net income attributable to REX was $34.9 million or a record second-quarter $1.06 per diluted share, compared to $7.1 million or $0.22 per share. Management said it expects to remain profitable in Q3 and for results to be better than the prior-year period, while the One Earth ethanol expansion stays on track for completion by end-2026 and the carbon capture project received draft EPA Class VI well permits in August. Versus the prior period, margins expanded sharply on stronger crush margins and tax credits, though SG&A rose to $15.6 million from $6.2 million on higher incentive compensation and restricted stock awards.

negative_highlights: Net new ARR of $54 million grew only 9% YoY, a deceleration highlighted in the analyst discussion compared to prior-quarter ARR growth
Q3 revenue guidance implies ~24% growth, a deceleration from Q2's 29%, and net new ARR growth expectations in H2 depend on a seasonally stronger Q4
Company is reducing ~5% of its workforce and transition to annual billings is temporarily deferring cash collections, with negative free cash flow of $29.8 million in Q2
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 29% YoY to $220.5 million, ahead of guidance, with full-year guidance raised to $888-892 million (~26% growth), a raise larger than the Q2 beat
Operating margin improved 11 percentage points YoY to -9%, significantly ahead of the guided range, driven largely by R&D leverage
NRR rose to 114% and GRR hit an all-time high, with customers using 4+ products rising to 59% from 51% a year ago and $100K+ ARR customers up 23% to 1,686
summary: Netskope reported Q2 FY2027 revenue of $220.5 million, up 29% year-over-year and ahead of guidance, with ARR of $899 million (up 27%), net new ARR of $54 million (up 9%), and NRR rising to 114%. Gross margin was 77% (up ~2 points), operating margin improved 11 points year-over-year to -9% versus guidance, and EPS loss of $0.03 beat. Full-year revenue guidance was raised to $888-892 million (~26% growth), with the raise slightly exceeding the Q2 beat, though Q3 revenue growth is guided to decelerate to ~24%. The company also announced a ~5% workforce reduction and is transitioning customers to annual billings.

negative_highlights: Comparable store sales declined 1.8%, missing the original Q2 plan
Full-year top-line guidance was lowered, with comps now expected flat to +0.5%
SG&A deleveraged 80 bps to 26.6% due to lower comps and increased marketing
positive_highlights: Adjusted EPS increased 43% to $1.42 and adjusted EBITDA rose 36% to $127 million
Gross margin expanded 360 bps to 43.5%, aided by 380 bps of IEEPA tariff refunds
New store openings remain on track, with 42 opened in the first half toward a full-year target of 75
summary: Ollie's reported Q2 FY2026 net sales up 9.1% to $741 million on 15 new stores, but comparable store sales fell 1.8% against a challenging multiyear stack due to weather, promotional pressure, and a cautious consumer. Gross margin rose 360 bps to 43.5%, though the entire increase—and more—came from 380 bps of IEEPA tariff refunds; adjusted EPS jumped 43% to $1.42 and adjusted EBITDA rose 36% to $127 million. Management lowered full-year sales and comp guidance (comp now flat to +0.5% vs prior expectations) while raising the buyback authorization to $175 million and planning about $50 million in price investments for the year. The quarter's earnings strength was largely refund-driven, and the forward outlook is more measured than previously communicated.

negative_highlights: Consolidated backlog declined to $2.5 billion at July 31, 2026 from $2.9 billion at the start of fiscal 2027

Industrial gross margin was 7.3%, below expectations due to cost overruns on a couple of non-data-center projects, and management said industrial margins may run below historical norms for a quarter or two
Consolidated gross margin stepped down from 25% in Q4 FY2026 to 21% in Q1 FY2027 to 19.3% in Q2 FY2027, reflecting earlier-stage power project revenues
positive_highlights: Record quarterly revenue of $384 million, up 62% YoY, with record net income of $53.3 million or $3.76 per diluted share versus $2.50 a year earlier
Adjusted EBITDA reached a record $70 million at an 18.2% margin, and gross margin expanded 70 bps YoY to 19.3%
Power segment revenue grew 53% to $301 million and industrial revenue grew 111% to $76 million, with $260 million-plus of backlog additions from scope increases and smaller jobs
summary: Argan reported record Q2 FY2027 revenue of $384 million, up 62% YoY, with record net income of $53.3 million ($3.76 per diluted share) and record adjusted EBITDA of $70 million (18.2% margin). Gross margin was 19.3% versus 18.6% a year ago but down from 21.0% in Q1 and 25% in Q4 FY2026, reflecting earlier-stage power project revenues; power gross margin was 22.4% and industrial 7.3% on cost overruns. Consolidated backlog fell to $2.5 billion from $2.9 billion at the start of fiscal year, though management cited a strong pipeline and expects to add a handful of new projects over the next 7-15 months, with full-year FY2027 revenue significantly above FY2026. The quarter included the ValCor Communications acquisition, a quarterly dividend of $0.50 per share, and approximately $1 billion in cash and investments with no debt.

negative_highlights: Professional services revenue of $18.9 million missed expectations on managed services softness and partner cost overruns in one region, with services gross margin at -22%
Q3 total revenue guidance of $215-$216 million implies a year-over-year decline, with professional services guided down 34% to $19 million
Net dollar expansion rate was 102% overall, and full-year total revenue growth of 1% remains minimal despite subscription growth
positive_highlights: Subscription revenue grew 3% year-over-year to $194.8 million, with total RPO up 11% to $1.03 billion for a second consecutive quarter of double-digit growth
GNAR grew more than 50% year-over-year and AI-native SKU ARR was up 40% year-over-year, with 200+ AI engagements and four $1 million+ ARR deals closed
Completed $125 million accelerated share repurchase, retiring ~22 million shares, with $453 million in cash and no debt
summary: Sprinklr reported Q2 FY2027 total revenue of $213.7 million, up 1% year-over-year, with subscription revenue up 3% to $194.8 million and non-GAAP operating income of $31.3 million (15% margin, $0.11 EPS). Professional services revenue of $18.9 million came in below expectations on managed services softness and partner cost overruns, driving services gross margin to -22% and total non-GAAP gross margin to 66%. For FY2027, the company raised its subscription revenue guide to $782.5-$784.5 million (4% growth) while keeping total revenue at $866.5-$868.5 million (1% growth) and non-GAAP operating income at $139-$141 million; Q3 total revenue is guided to $215-$216 million, slightly down year-over-year on a 34% decline in professional services. Total RPO was $1.03 billion, up 11% year-over-year, and the $125 million accelerated share repurchase was completed with $75 million remaining under the authorization.

negative_highlights: Q4 gross margin compressed to 2.2% of revenue from 3.25% a year ago, and Q4 EBITDA declined 3% to $28.2 million versus $29.2 million
New DTC customers fell 38% year over year to 67,900 in Q4, and full-year new DTC customers were down 53% to 526,300

Management said the demand slowdown that began mid-March to early April continued through Q4 and into the first two months of fiscal Q1 2027, with higher rates sapping gold and silver spot momentum and no dip-note enthusiasm from retail customers
positive_highlights: Q4 revenue nearly doubled to $5.0 billion from $2.5 billion, with full-year revenue up 132% to $25.5 billion
Full-year net income of $82.3 million or $3.02 per diluted share versus $17.3 million or $0.71 a year ago; full-year adjusted net income rose 164% to $139.9 million
Declared a $1.00 per share special dividend in addition to the regular $0.20 dividend, with cash of $578 million versus $77.7 million at fiscal 2025 year-end
summary: Gold.com reported fiscal Q4 2026 revenue up 99% to $5.0 billion (about $0.9 billion from forward sales) and gross profit up 35% to $110.3 million, or 2.2% of revenue versus 3.25% a year ago, while net income was $12.2 million and diluted EPS was $0.41, flat versus the prior year. Full-year revenue rose 132% to $25.5 billion, gross profit rose 115% to $453.1 million, and net income was $82.3 million or $3.02 per diluted share; Q4 EBITDA fell 3% to $28.2 million even as adjusted net income rose 29% to $24.7 million. Management disclosed a mid-March to early-April demand slowdown that continued through Q4 and into the first two months of fiscal 2027, noted higher rates pressuring metal prices and silver premiums narrowing, and said new DTC customers fell 38% year over year to 67,900. No explicit fiscal 2027 revenue or EPS guidance was provided; management announced a $1.00 special dividend alongside the regular $0.20 dividend and left M&A and buybacks open-ended.

negative_highlights: Non-GAAP product gross margin guidance lowered to 74% due to higher mix of lower-contribution-margin AI workloads
Net revenue retention rate of 126% indicates expansion deceleration versus historical levels
Bookings increasingly weighted toward Q4 renewals, concentrating RPO growth in the fourth quarter
positive_highlights: Product revenue growth accelerated to 37% YoY, marking a third straight quarter of acceleration and second consecutive quarter of record sequential dollar growth
FY2027 product revenue guidance raised to $6.07 billion (36% YoY growth), a 500+ bps increase
Non-GAAP operating margin expanded over 400 bps YoY to 15%; FY2027 operating margin guidance raised to 14.5% from 13.5%
summary: Snowflake reported Q2 FY2027 product revenue of $1.49 billion, up 37% year-over-year — its third consecutive quarter of acceleration — and non-GAAP operating margin of 15%, expanding over 400 basis points year-over-year. Net revenue retention was 126%, RPO grew 30% to $9 billion, and the company added 692 net new customers (up 32% YoY). Management raised FY2027 product revenue guidance to $6.07 billion (36% YoY growth, a 500+ bps increase), lifted non-GAAP operating margin guidance to 14.5% from 13.5%, and guided Q3 product revenue to $1.588–1.593 billion (37–38% YoY). Non-GAAP product gross margin guidance was lowered to 74% due to a higher mix of lower-margin AI workloads, and adjusted free cash flow margin guidance was reiterated at 23%.

negative_highlights: The Petco Perks relaunch drove point redemption volumes that exceeded projections, reducing Q2 net sales by a mid-single-digit-million amount and leaving reported sales roughly flat versus a pre-launch run rate tracking above the ~0.3% outlook
The dog business remains soft with industry adoptions down slightly, and the category is not expected to rebound until 2027; supplies and companion animal sales remain in decline though moderating
Q3 Adjusted EBITDA guidance of $100-$103 million is below the Q2 level of $122 million, and ongoing supply chain and fuel headwinds are expected in the second half
positive_highlights: Q2 comps were +0.6%, the second consecutive quarter of positive comps, and normalized Adjusted EBITDA of $115 million exceeded the prior-year level and prior outlook
Consumables returned to positive comp growth, with cat, companion animal, and vet diet (double-digit growth in dog and cat) cited as standout areas

Total debt fell $113 million year over year to $1.48 billion; free cash flow rose $51 million year to date and an additional $75 million debt prepayment was announced, bringing nine-month paydown to $170 million
summary: Petco reported Q2 net sales of $1.5 billion, up slightly year over year, with a 0.6% comp representing a second consecutive quarter of positive comps. Adjusted EBITDA was $122 million (8.2% of sales), including a $6.8 million net tariff refund; normalized Adjusted EBITDA of $115 million came in above the prior-year level and above the company's outlook. Gross margin expanded 37 basis points to 39.7% but was roughly flat excluding the tariff benefit, and full-year guidance was affirmed at flat to +1.5% net sales and $415-$430 million Adjusted EBITDA, with Q3 sales growth guided to 0.4%-1% and Q3 Adjusted EBITDA of $100-$103 million. The membership relaunch drove point redemptions that exceeded projections and reduced Q2 net sales by a mid-single-digit-million amount, which management said is now behind them.

negative_highlights: Q3 revenue guidance of $68-73 million implies a 4-10% year-over-year decline against the $75.8 million prior-year base
Adjusted operating loss widened to $11.1 million from $4.9 million a year ago as total adjusted OpEx rose $8.4 million year over year
Supply constraints on Bip, Balance 3, and Helio Strap persisted in Q2, with Helio Strap not expected to reach full supply until Q4
positive_highlights: Gross margin improved 120 bps year over year to 37.4% despite higher memory and component costs and RMB appreciation

Balance 3 and Balance Ultra rose from ~3% of global Balance family activations in Q2 to ~26% in July and ~30% through August 25, with July total Balance activations up more than one-third versus the Q2 monthly average
Cash and cash equivalents increased to $106.3 million, up $11 million year over year; inventory fell $17.5 million versus the prior-year quarter
summary: Q2 FY2026 revenue was $63.5 million, up 6.9% year over year and in line with guidance, with gross margin of 37.4%, up 120 basis points from 36.2% a year earlier despite higher memory costs. Adjusted operating loss widened to $11.1 million from $4.9 million a year ago, driven by an $8.4 million OpEx increase (including $2.9 million of product-launch marketing) and FX headwinds. Q3 revenue guidance of $68-73 million implies a 4-10% year-over-year decline against a $75.8 million prior-year base, attributed to supply constraints on Helio Strap/Balance 3/Bip, launch timing, and macro softness, though the company expects to return to growth in Q4. Management also announced Bip family price increases starting January 2027 to offset entry-level cost pressure.

negative_highlights: Q3 revenue guidance of $105-$115 million implies only ~4% YoY growth at the midpoint, a sharp deceleration from 18% in Q2
The Q2 revenue beat was partly driven by higher home charging sales tied to lumpy events like Prime Day, which management does not expect to repeat in Q3
Normalized gross margin, roughly 35% and guided to remain there, still trails the company's stated 40% target with no near-term timeline given
positive_highlights: Revenue of $116 million exceeded the $100-$110 million guidance range and grew 18% YoY, the fourth consecutive quarter of YoY growth
Non-GAAP gross margin hit a record 38% (35% normalized excluding ~$4 million tariff refunds), up 7 points sequentially and 5 points YoY
Adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed to $5 million from $19 million in Q1 and $22 million a year ago, with essentially zero cash burn and inventory down to $179 million from $204 million
summary: ChargePoint reported Q2 FY2027 revenue of $116 million, above its $100-$110 million guidance range, up 18% year-over-year and 14% sequentially, marking a fourth consecutive quarter of YoY growth. Non-GAAP gross margin was 38%, including ~$4 million of one-time tariff refunds; normalized gross margin was 35%, up 3 points sequentially and 2 points YoY. Non-GAAP adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed to $5 million from $19 million in Q1 and $22 million a year ago, with cash of $96 million and essentially zero cash burn. Q3 guidance is $105-$115 million revenue (about 4% YoY growth at the midpoint), with gross margin expected to remain near normalized levels and OpEx below $50 million per quarter; management noted the Q2 revenue beat was partly driven by lumpy higher home sales not expected to repeat.

negative_highlights: Used barrel sales fell more than 60%, with the non-branded/bulk business dropping from over $100 million two years ago to roughly $30 million.
Developed international markets declined 8% organically, with Germany, France, and the U.K. described as very weak, and Canada still withholding U.S.-produced spirits.
The full-strength tequila portfolio (Herradura and el Jimador) declined in the low teens, and U.S. shipments trailed depletions by about 4 points.
positive_highlights: Gross margin expanded 40 bps to 60.2%, and EPS rose 6% to $0.38 with organic operating income up 4%.
New Mix, the RTD portfolio, and Jack Daniel's Tennessee Blackberry drove growth, with Blackberry contributing more than 2 points of U.S. value growth and now in 30+ international markets.
Emerging international markets grew 9% organically, led by Mexico and the UAE, and cash flow from operations rose $13 million to $173 million.
summary: Brown-Forman reported Q1 FY2027 organic net sales declined about 1%, following roughly 9% growth in the trailing Q4, with gross margin up 40 bps to 60.2%, reported operating income down 3% but organic operating income up 4%, and EPS up 6% to $0.38. Management reaffirmed full-year guidance of approximately flat organic net sales and a 3%-5% organic operating income decline, but said confidence has increased that results will trend toward the more favorable end of the operating income range. Growth from New Mix, the broader RTD portfolio, and Jack Daniel's Tennessee Blackberry was offset by a more than 60% decline in used barrel sales, a low-teens decline in the full-strength tequila portfolio, and an 8% organic net sales decline in developed international markets, with U.S. shipments trailing depletions by about 4 points. Because it is early in a rocky year, management gave no quantitative raise despite the improved operating income confidence.

negative_highlights: Non-GAAP operating loss remained large at $36.2 million and non-GAAP net loss was $30.7 million ($0.20 per share).
Gross margin is guided to moderate to the mid-40s next quarter on selective forward-deployed engineering investment.
FY2027 revenue guidance of $210-240 million and operating loss of $123-155 million imply continued losses for the full year.
positive_highlights: Revenue of $52.4 million came in above guidance, with subscription and PES revenue at 97% of total.
Non-GAAP gross margin improved sequentially to 50% from 37% last quarter.
