Free cash flow turned positive at $2.1 million versus negative $34.3 million in the year-ago quarter; bookings grew 73% and federal bookings grew 138%.
summary: C3.ai reported Q1 FY2027 total revenue of $52.4 million, with subscription revenue of $49.2 million (94% of total), non-GAAP gross margin improving sequentially to 50% from 37%, non-GAAP operating loss of $36.2 million ($8.3 million better than the midpoint of guidance), and positive free cash flow of $2.1 million versus negative $34.3 million a year ago. Bookings grew 73% with federal bookings up 138%, and restructuring delivered roughly $135 million in annualized cost savings including a ~40% headcount reduction. Guidance was set at $51-55 million revenue and a $34.5-42.5 million non-GAAP operating loss for Q2, and $210-240 million revenue with a $123-155 million non-GAAP operating loss for FY2027; gross margin is expected to moderate to the mid-40s next quarter on forward-deployed engineering investment. Revenue was above guidance but the forward outlook was not raised and the CEO emphasized consistent quarter-over-quarter growth over hitting the high end of the range.

negative_highlights: Q3 gross margin fell 210 bps sequentially to 75% and is guided to ~73% in Q4 due to increasing XPU/memory content mix.
Q3 non-AI semiconductor revenue of $4.2B was flat sequentially, with wireless declining.
Q4 infrastructure software revenue is guided to ~$8.7B, essentially flat versus Q3's $8.8B, indicating no sequential growth.
positive_highlights: Q3 AI semiconductor revenue rose 221% YoY to $16.7B, with XPU shipments up over 3.5x YoY and 73% of AI revenue.
Q4 revenue guided to $34.8B (+93% YoY) with AI revenue of $21.7B (+236% YoY); FY2026 AI revenue guidance raised to $58B from $56B.
Record free cash flow of $13.7B (46% of revenue) and operating income of $20.1B (+92% YoY) with operating margin up 240 bps YoY to 67.9%.
summary: Broadcom reported record Q3 FY2026 revenue of $29.6B, up 86% YoY, with AI semiconductor revenue of $16.7B up 221% YoY and 54% sequentially; non-GAAP EPS was $3.32, up 96% YoY, and operating margin hit a record 67.9%, though gross margin fell 210 bps sequentially to 75% on AI mix. Q4 guidance calls for $34.8B revenue (+93% YoY) and AI revenue of $21.7B (+236% YoY), and management introduced multiyear AI revenue targets of ~$115B in FY2027 and ~$230B in FY2028, citing secured supply. Fiscal 2026 AI revenue guidance was lifted to $58B from a prior $56B, the key change versus the prior period, alongside an agreement with Google to supply tens of billions of dollars of TPUs annually. Non-AI semiconductor revenue was $4.2B, up 5% YoY, and infrastructure software was $8.8B, up 29% YoY, with Q4 software guided to ~$8.7B.

negative_highlights: Net sales of $555 million fell 10% YoY and came in below plan
Q3 revenue guided to ~$870 million versus $989 million in the prior-year quarter, the largest YoY PVH revenue reduction this fiscal year
Q3 non-GAAP EPS guided to $1.34-$1.45 versus $1.90 last year, with Marc Jacobs slightly dilutive for remaining FY2027
positive_highlights: Non-GAAP EPS of $0.26 exceeded the $0.15-$0.25 guidance range
Gross margin expanded 440 bps to 45.2%, with wholesale gross margin up to 43.3% from 38.9%
Full-price wholesale sales in the go-forward portfolio rose more than 20%, while the go-forward portfolio grew high single digits
summary: G-III reported Q2 FY2027 net sales of $555 million, down 10% YoY and slightly below plan, with non-GAAP EPS of $0.26 ahead of the $0.15-$0.25 guidance range; gross margin expanded 440 bps to 45.2% on price actions and a mix shift to owned brands. Full-year net sales guidance was reiterated at approximately $2.71 billion, while non-GAAP EPS guidance was raised to $2.20-$2.30 from a prior range, as Q3 revenue is guided to about $870 million versus $989 million last year due to the largest PVH license exit. The company closed the Marc Jacobs acquisition and owns 100% of the operating company plus a 50% stake in the IP joint venture with WHP; it guides to ~$360 million in Marc Jacobs sales this year and expects the deal to be dilutive for the first 12 months before turning accretive. Balance sheet is strong with $529 million in cash, aided by $134 million in tariff refunds, and inventories down 13% YoY.

negative_highlights: Gross margin expected to moderate toward historical levels going forward, driven by higher mix of AI systems, normalization in traditional server margins, and pricing
Supply constraints continue to limit revenue conversion, with orders growing 3.5x faster than networking revenue and data center networking revenue declining 6% due to shipment timing
Operating expense rose 17% sequentially on higher variable compensation, and inventory ended at $11.8B, up YoY and sequentially, reflecting higher commodity costs and purchases
positive_highlights: Record revenue of $12.2B, up 34% YoY, exceeding the high end of guidance, with non-GAAP operating profit of $2B (2.5x YoY) and record non-GAAP EPS of $1.11
Record non-GAAP gross margin of 40% and operating margin of 16.2%, up 290 bps sequentially, driven by disciplined pricing and networking mix

FY2026 EPS guidance raised to $3.75-$3.85 and FY2027 framework raised to 13%-17% revenue growth with EPS of $4.40-$4.60; networks for AI orders hit a record $700M, bringing cumulative orders to $2.2B and raising the year-end target to $2.5B-$3B
summary: HPE reported record Q3 FY2026 revenue of $12.2B, up 34% YoY, exceeding the high end of guidance, with record non-GAAP gross margin of 40%, record operating profit of $2B, 16.2% operating margin (up 290 bps sequentially), and record non-GAAP EPS of $1.11, the first time above $1. Free cash flow was a Q3 record $958M, and management raised FY2026 EPS guidance to $3.75-$3.85 and the FCF target to at least $3.75B. The company also raised its FY2027 framework to revenue growth of 13%-17% and EPS of $4.40-$4.60, supported by record backlog, orders up 42% normalized, and strong AI and networking demand, though supply constraints persist and gross margin is expected to moderate toward historical levels.

negative_highlights: Gross margin contracted to 73.9% from 78.3% on higher color-cosmetics inventory provisions
Q3 2026 guidance implies 0-10% YoY revenue decline, versus 5.1% growth in Q2
Swing to net loss of RMB 90.8 million from a RMB 19.5 million loss last year, with non-GAAP net loss of RMB 99.4 million versus prior-year non-GAAP income of RMB 11.5 million
positive_highlights: Skincare revenue grew 40.4% YoY and reached 71.5% of total net revenues
Fulfillment expenses fell to 4.9% of revenue from 5.8% on logistics efficiency gains
G&A fell to 6.6% of revenue from 7.7%, helped by lower share-based compensation
summary: Total net revenues rose 5.1% YoY to RMB 1.14 billion, driven by a 40.4% increase in skincare (now 71.5% of revenue) but offset by a 35.8% decline in color cosmetics. Gross margin fell to 73.9% from 78.3% on higher color-cosmetics inventory provisions, watching and marketing rose to 70.7% of revenue from 66.5%, and the company swung to a net loss of RMB 90.8 million from a RMB 19.5 million loss, with non-GAAP net loss of RMB 99.4 million versus prior-year non-GAAP income of RMB 11.5 million. Q3 2026 guidance calls for revenue of RMB 898.6-998.4 million, a 0-10% YoY decline, following the more moderate-than-expected Q2 growth.

negative_highlights: Gross margin declined 50 bps YoY to 70.6% due to higher product revenue mix, and Q2 gross margin is guided lower to 67%-68%
Product gross margin fell 150 bps sequentially to 54.6% on higher component costs, and the Q2 product margin trajectory implies a sequential decline
Back-half revenue growth is projected to decelerate to roughly 9-10% YoY from 23-26% in the first half, and management noted some pull-forward of purchases that may not repeat
positive_highlights: Revenue of $2.03B grew 30% YoY, exceeding the high end of guidance, with broad-based strength across products, customer types, and geographies
Non-GAAP EPS of $2.58 rose 66% YoY, and FY27 EPS guidance was raised to $9.73-$10.03 (22% YoY growth at midpoint)
All-flash array revenue reached $1.31B, up 47% YoY, and public cloud revenue grew 28% YoY to $206M
summary: NTAP reported Q1 FY27 revenue of $2.03B, up 30% YoY (26% ex-extra week) and 4% sequentially, with non-GAAP EPS of $2.58, up 66% YoY, exceeding the high end of guidance on every metric. Gross margin was 70.6%, down 50 bps YoY on product mix but above guidance, and operating margin reached 31.9%, up 6.1 points YoY. The company raised FY27 revenue guidance to $7.975B-$8.225B (17% YoY growth at $8.1B midpoint, an increase of $650M vs prior guidance) and raised EPS guidance to $9.73-$10.03 (22% YoY growth at $9.88 midpoint). Management cited broad-based momentum in public cloud (+28% YoY), all-flash arrays (+47% YoY), and AI-related deals (approximately 350 deals), while acknowledging some accelerated purchases and improved pricing that are not expected to repeat at the same level.

negative_highlights: Q3 comp guidance of 8-10% decelerates from Q2's 14%
Gross margin faces headwinds from higher fuel costs and an unfavorable shrink comparison in Q3
positive_highlights: Net sales up 23% YoY to $1.3 billion with comps up 14% and unit growth of 9%
Adjusted EPS more than doubled to $1.68 from $0.68 a year earlier
Full-year FY2026 guidance raised to $10.07 adjusted EPS (51% growth) on 19% sales growth
summary: Five Below reported Q2 FY2027 net sales up 23% to $1.3 billion, with comparable sales growth of 14% and adjusted diluted EPS of $1.68, more than double last year's $0.68. Adjusted operating margin expanded 360 basis points to 9.0%, and gross margin rose 220 basis points to 35.6%. Management raised full-year fiscal 2026 guidance to sales of $5.63-$5.71 billion (19% growth) and adjusted EPS of $10.07 (51% growth), up from prior outlook. A new $600 million share repurchase authorization was approved, and Q3 guidance was set at $1.21-$1.23 billion in sales with 8-10% comps and EPS of $1.07.

Daktronics reported Q1 FY2027 net sales up 7.1% and EPS of $0.40, up 21.2% and the highest quarterly EPS in three years, despite the quarter having one fewer week than the prior-year period. Gross margin rose 80 bps to 30.5% and operating income grew 7.2% to $24.9 million, aided by about $3 million in tariff refunds largely offset by rising raw material costs. Order bookings were down year over year and backlog fell to $311 million from $356 million, which management attributed to order timing and said sizable projects would book in Q2. FY2028 targets (7%-10% revenue CAGR, 10%-12% operating margin, 17%-20% ROIC) were reaffirmed, and the company disclosed NBA and SEC information requests.

negative_highlights: Q3 EPS guidance of $0.07–$0.12 assumes September comps may slow roughly 8 points from August, as occurred in three of the last four years
SG&A excludes meaningful leverage as bonus accruals added $1.5 million in Q2 and are expected to persist in Q3
The Q4 comp comparison is the toughest of the year (last year's Q4 comp was 10.1%) with no Q4 guidance provided
positive_highlights: Comparable net sales rose 12.1%, a third straight quarter of double-digit growth, with fiscal August comps accelerating to 14.6%
Gross margin expanded 300 basis points to 35.5% of net sales, including 140 bps of product margin improvement
Net income improved $5.2 million or $0.17 per diluted share to $0.27, and the company is profitable on a trailing four-quarter and year-to-date basis for the first time since 2022
summary: Tilly's reported Q2 FY2026 total net sales of $163.5 million, up 8.1%, with comparable net sales up 12.1% — a third consecutive quarter of double-digit comps. Gross margin expanded 300 basis points to 35.5%, net income was $8.4 million or $0.27 per diluted share versus $0.10 last year, and the company returned to trailing-four-quarter and year-to-date profitability for the first time since 2022. Management guided Q3 net sales to $150–$155 million (10–14% comps) and EPS of $0.07–$0.12 versus last year's $0.05 loss, while noting bonus accrual headwinds and that September comps decelerated about 8 points after back-to-school in three of the last four years.

negative_highlights: Q3 revenue fell 29% to $33 million from $46.7 million, with products revenue down to $18 million from $26 million and generation revenue down to $8.8 million from $12.4 million

Gross loss widened to $24.5 million from $5.1 million, including $17 million of Fit Energy Phase Zero charges ($4 million inventory write-down, $13 million firm purchase commitment losses) as current costs exceed contractual pricing
Adjusted EBITDA worsened to -$36.7 million from -$16.4 million, with production at roughly 37 MW annualized versus the 100 MW target needed to align cost structure with pricing
positive_highlights: Total committed and awarded capacity backlog reached $3.6 billion as of July 31, 2026, including $1.3 billion committed backlog up 4.1% year-over-year and a new $2.4 billion awarded capacity category
Cash, equivalents, and restricted cash rose to $737.3 million from $440.9 million at April 30, 2026, with $658.1 million unrestricted, and $298 million of net equity proceeds raised in the quarter

First FuelCell Energy Blocks order for data center baseload power signed (up to 380 MW across four phases with Fit Energy) and a 75 MW capacity reservation agreement with a colocation data center operator closed after quarter end
summary: Total Q3 FY2026 revenue was $33 million, down 29% from $46.7 million a year ago, with a gross loss of $24.5 million versus a $5.1 million gross loss prior year, driven by $17 million of Fit Energy Phase Zero charges ($4 million inventory write-down plus $13 million firm purchase commitment losses). Net loss attributable to common stockholders was $45.3 million, or $0.64 per share, versus $92.5 million, or $3.78 per share, and adjusted EBITDA was -$36.7 million versus -$16.4 million. Committed backlog was $1.3 billion, up 4.1% year-over-year, with a new $2.4 billion awarded capacity backlog category (Fit Energy phases 1-3, 350 MW) for total $3.6 billion, and a 75 MW capacity reservation with a colocation data center operator was closed after quarter end. Management set a new target of positive adjusted EBITDA in Q4 FY2027, dependent on converting awarded capacity to committed contracts, reaching 100 MW annualized production by October 2026, and cost reductions; no revenue or EPS guidance was given.

negative_highlights: NIM on credit assets fell 27 bps sequentially to 2.44%, attributed to higher liquidity, deposit mix shift, and lower asset yields.
Q3 included CAD 4.6 million in non-core and transitory costs (CAD 3.1 million non-core, CAD 1.5 million transitory), making core earnings noisier.
Canadian digital banking revenue grew only 4% YoY, with Canada net income dampened by CAD 1.8 million after-tax reorganization costs.
positive_highlights: Net income up 53% YoY to CAD 10.1 million and adjusted net income up 27% YoY to CAD 12.3 million (CAD 0.38 per share).
U.S. banking revenue grew 199% YoY to CAD 9.3 million, with U.S. net income up 803% YoY to CAD 3.9 million.
New U.S. SRP target of at least $3 billion in fiscal 2027, representing ~60% growth in credit assets, with management noting half is already aligned with existing partners.
summary: VersaBank reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of CAD 38.8 million (up 23% year-over-year, 1% sequentially), net income of CAD 10.1 million (up 53% YoY), and adjusted net income of CAD 12.3 million or CAD 0.38 per share (up 27% YoY). U.S. banking revenue grew 199% YoY and 18% sequentially to CAD 9.3 million with net income up 803% YoY to CAD 3.9 million. NIM compressed to 2.44% on credit assets (down 11 bps YoY, 27 bps sequentially), with management guiding NIM back to ~2.30% next quarter and reiterating a U.S. SRP target of $3 billion in fiscal 2027. Total assets surpassed CAD 7 billion post-quarter, and the company expects core non-interest expenses to remain flat in fiscal 2027 despite significant asset growth.

negative_highlights: Full-year volume guidance cut to low to mid single-digit growth, with Q2 retail sales down 4% YoY to ~17,300 cars and revenue down 8% YoY to $727 million
Adjusted gross margin deteriorated to negative 13% in Q2 from negative 6% a year ago; adjusted EBITDA loss widened to $286 million from $206 million

Net loss narrowed 55% YoY in Q2 to $459 million and operating loss improved 43% in H1, with no impairment expense versus $724 million recognized in H1 2025

Capital structure strengthened via ~$640 million debt-to-equity conversion, Volvo Cars loan maturity extended to Dec 2031, $700 million new equity, and $1.7 billion of banking facilities renewed or increased in H1
summary: Polestar Q2 2026 retail sales fell 4% YoY to ~17,300 cars and revenue dropped 8% YoY to $727 million, with adjusted gross margin deteriorating to negative 13% from negative 6% and adjusted EBITDA loss widening to $286 million from $206 million. On a reported basis the net loss of $459 million improved 55% YoY and operating loss fell 43% in H1, but largely because the prior period included $724 million of impairment charges. Management cut its full-year volume outlook to low to mid single-digit growth, absorbing a roughly $130 million hit from the U.S. BIS decision (which will halt sales of model-year 2027 vehicles in the U.S.) and continued pricing pressure, while pointing to Polestar 4 SUV and Polestar 5 launches as H2 drivers.

negative_highlights: Q3 revenue guidance of RMB 2.4-2.5 billion implies a 5.7% to 9.4% YoY decline with domestic revenue worsening to high-teens decline versus a 17% drop in Q2

Full-year group revenue now expected to decline at a mid-single-digit rate, down from prior expectation of a couple percent, and the RMB 3 billion overseas revenue target for 2026 is likely RMB 100-200 million lower
Non-GAAP operating margin fell to 11.1% from 17.1% a year ago, and the low-teens adjusted operating margin target for 2026 is described as more challenging to achieve

Two newer MENA products, YahaLand and Amar, had combined Q2 revenue approaching SoulChill's scale, with YahaLand reaching net income breakeven and combined Q3 revenue expected to surpass SoulChill
Q2 net cash provided by operating activities was RMB 642.3 million, and Momo paying users rose 200,000 sequentially to 3.9 million
summary: Hello Group reported Q2 2026 total revenue of RMB 2.49 billion, down 5% year-over-year but up 4% sequentially, with domestic revenue down 17% YoY to RMB 1.81 billion and overseas revenue up 52% YoY to RMB 673 million (27% of total). Non-GAAP net income was RMB 273.9 million versus a RMB 96 million loss a year ago, while non-GAAP operating margin fell to 11.1% from 17.1%. Management guided Q3 revenue to RMB 2.4-2.5 billion (down 5.7% to 9.4% YoY, with domestic down high-teens and overseas up high-30s), revised its full-year group revenue decline to mid-single digits from a couple percent, and said the original RMB 3 billion 2026 overseas revenue target looks a stretch, likely RMB 100-200 million lower. The main negative change was a wider domestic revenue decline than previously expected due to weaker spending among top-tier live-streaming users.

negative_highlights: Gross margin declined 90 basis points year-over-year to 24.0% from 24.9%, though it improved from 23.6% in Q1
Management noted some Walmart items (sausage and peppers, meatloaf) show lower velocities and may be replaced, indicating mix risk
No explicit financial guidance for Q3/Q4 was provided; commentary only reaffirmed double-digit revenue growth and sequential margin improvement
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 55% to $54.6 million and adjusted EBITDA rose 68.9% to $5.5 million, with adjusted EBITDA margin expanding 80 basis points to 10.1%
Net income increased 100.9% to $2.6 million, or $0.06 per diluted share, and operating expenses declined 160 basis points to 18.5% of revenue
Balance sheet strengthened to $138.6 million in cash (from $20 million at January 31, 2026) with total debt reduced to $4.8 million, following a $108.6 million net equity raise
summary: Mama's Creations reported Q2 FY2027 revenue up 55% to $54.6 million and adjusted EBITDA up 68.9% to $5.5 million (10.1% margin), with net income more than doubling to $2.6 million or $0.06 per diluted share. Gross margin of 24.0% improved sequentially from 23.6% but declined from 24.9% a year ago, while operating expenses fell 160 basis points to 18.5% of revenue. Management cited new Kroger distribution (Louisville division, 100+ stores, four items starting next month) and a larger Costco MVM across all eight regions as forward drivers, and reaffirmed a mid-to-high 20% gross margin target. The company ended the quarter with $138.6 million in cash and $4.8 million of total debt; explicit EPS guidance was not provided.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined 3% in both reported and constant currency, with EMEA down 6% and Calvin Klein down 7%
Excluding tariff refunds, Q2 EBIT fell to $126 million and operating margin was 6%, versus $178 million and 8.2% in the prior year
Spring 2027 EMEA wholesale order book is down mid-single digits and Q4 gross margin is expected lower year-over-year; a $439 million non-cash goodwill impairment was recorded
positive_highlights: Q2 EPS of $3.70 and operating margin of 11.1% exceeded guidance on both gross margin and SG&A

Gross margin expanded roughly 20 basis points excluding tariff refunds, with expansion in both APAC and the Americas on higher DTC AURs, and Q3 gross margin guided up ~100 basis points with expansion in all three regions
Confirmed annualized run-rate cost savings of approximately $45 million across nearly a dozen categories, with full realization in 2027
summary: PVH reported Q2 revenue down 3% in both reported and constant currency, at the high end of guidance and in line with all three regions, with operating margin of 11.1% and EPS of $3.70 ahead of plan; however, the quarter included approximately 510 basis points of operating margin benefit and about $1.80 of EPS from $107 million in tariff refunds, and excluding those refunds operating margin was 6% with EBIT of $126 million versus $178 million last year. Gross margin of 63% rose 530 basis points but was up only about 20 basis points excluding tariff refunds, and inventories fell 3%. Full-year guidance was reaffirmed at roughly flat reported revenue, ~8.8% operating margin, and $11.80-$12.10 EPS, with Q3 revenue guided down low single digits and Q3 operating margin of ~7.5%; EMEA remains pressured with the spring 2027 wholesale order book down mid-single digits, while Americas and APAC are expected to grow for the full year.

negative_highlights: PLG headwind pressure on revenue growth widens to ~100 bps in Q3 and ~150 bps in Q4, with no FY2027 recovery assumed
Gross margin fell to 87%, down ~120 bps sequentially, with ~150 bps of further COGS pressure across Q3-Q4 and gross margin exiting the year in the mid-80s
Q3 revenue guidance of $217-219 million implies 8-9% growth, decelerating from Q2's 10%
positive_highlights: Revenue of $216.4 million rose 10% YoY, above the high end of guidance, an acceleration from Q1
Overall NRR improved to 97% from 96%, with core and $100,000+ cohorts both at 98% (large-customer cohort up from 96%)
AI Studio and AI Teammates drove ~25% of net new ARR, above the 15% full-year target, with full-year AI mix target raised to ~20%
summary: Q2 FY2027 revenue was $216.4 million, up 10% year-over-year and above the high end of guidance, with non-GAAP operating margin of 10% (up ~300 bps YoY) and non-GAAP EPS of $0.10. NRR improved to 97% overall and 98% in both core ($5,000+) and $100,000+ cohorts, and AI Studio/AI Teammates drove ~25% of net new ARR. Q3 guidance of $217-219 million (8-9% growth) and full-year revenue of $858.5-863.5 million (9% growth) were framed against a rising PLG headwind (~100 bps in Q3, ~150 bps in Q4), a $1.2 million AWM revenue-timing impact, and ~150 bps of gross margin pressure as AI products are seeded into tiers. Full-year AI net-new-ARR target was raised to ~20% from ~15%, while FY2027 contribution from Client Management, Service Management and Command is assumed minimal.

negative_highlights: Full-year revenue growth guidance left unchanged at 5%-7% despite 32% Q1 growth, implying a sharp back-half deceleration
Q2 sales guided to only roughly 10% above last year, well below Q1's 32%

Cash used in operations was $8.8 million and internal inventory rose to $181 million from $156 million at the end of Q4; operating expenses rose $3 million YoY on legal, profit-related compensation, freight, and advertising costs
positive_highlights: Net sales rose 32.3% YoY to $112.6 million, and EPS swung to $0.06 from a $0.08 loss last year
Adjusted EBITDAS grew 86% YoY; gross margin of 28.7% rose 2.8 points, aided by $2.9 million of tariff refunds (260 bps)
summary: Smith & Wesson reported Q1 FY2027 net sales of $112.6 million, up 32.3% YoY, with gross margin of 28.7% (up 2.8 points, 260 bps from $2.9 million of tariff refunds) and EPS of $0.06 versus a $0.08 loss last year; adjusted EBITDAS grew 86%. Q1 shipments grew roughly 20% against 7.7% adjusted NICS growth, with channel inventories flat and long-gun inventories down 5,000 units, indicating share gains. Management guided Q2 sales to roughly 10% above last year and Q2 gross margin 200-300 bps higher YoY, but left the full-year revenue growth outlook unchanged at 5%-7%, implying a back-half deceleration versus the 32% Q1 growth. Capital spending is expected at $45-$50 million for the year, and the board declared a $0.13 quarterly dividend.

negative_highlights: Non-GAAP gross margin of 59.3% came in below the 59%-60.5% guidance midpoint
Memory price inflation and supply scarcity are described as 'dire for everybody,' creating Q4 revenue uncertainty as customers may cut volumes

Operating cash outflow of $260,000 and free cash outflow of $7.1 million; days of inventory rose to 157 from 145 and no shares were repurchased in the quarter despite the new $50 million authorization
positive_highlights: Revenue of $108.1 million came in slightly above the midpoint of the $105-111 million guidance range, up 13.2% year-over-year and 7.7% sequentially
Q3 revenue guidance of $115-124 million implies roughly 10.5% sequential growth at the midpoint, led by Physical AI demand in IoT
Five-year rolling SAM raised to $22.9 billion in FY2032 from $8.5 billion in FY2027, a ~20% CAGR versus the prior ~18% projection; automotive set a new revenue record
summary: Fiscal Q2 FY2027 revenue was $108.1 million, slightly above the $105-111 million guidance midpoint and up 7.7% sequentially and 13.2% year-over-year, with non-GAAP gross margin of 59.3% below the 59%-60.5% guidance midpoint and non-GAAP EPS of $0.18. Q3 guidance is $115-124 million (midpoint $119.5 million, roughly 10.5% sequential growth), with non-GAAP gross margin of 59%-60% and OpEx of $56.5-59.5 million. The company raised its five-year SAM to $22.9 billion by FY2032 (about 20% CAGR) and announced Capgemini and Macnica indirect-channel partnerships plus a new X7 AI accelerator sampling now, while flagging industry-wide memory cost inflation and supply scarcity as an uncertainty mainly for Q4. Automotive set a revenue record and the board authorized a new $50 million repurchase program.

negative_highlights: Previously issued financial guidance was withdrawn, with no updated guidance given until more operating history is built
The strategic review of parts of the legacy financial services business introduces uncertainty about the portfolio's future structure
Revenue mix is not yet from agents being paid directly for outcomes; A-MM revenue is still mostly platform/capability monetization rather than outcome-based agent compensation
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 38.8% quarter-over-quarter to $13.9 million from $10 million
Gross margin expanded to 79.5% from 67.7%, driven by higher-margin agentic revenue
Operating income turned positive at $1 million, versus a $3.2 million operating loss in Q1, while opex stayed roughly flat at ~$10 million
summary: Q2 FY2026 revenue was $13.9 million, up 38.8% from $10 million in Q1, with gross margin expanding to 79.5% from 67.7%. Operating income turned positive at $1 million versus a $3.2 million loss in Q1, net income from continuing operations was $1.5 million, and adjusted EBITDA improved to $1.9 million from -$3.2 million. The $10.1 million digital assets platform plus A-MM revenue was slightly above the prior $9-$10 million outlook, but the company withdrew its previously issued financial guidance due to the strategic transition toward an agentic AI company, and will not provide updated guidance until it has more operating history. Management also said it is reviewing the structure and ownership of parts of its legacy financial services business, with nothing to announce.

negative_highlights: Free cash flow margin guidance lowered to ~100bps below FY2026 due to inventory pre-note and elevated supply chain costs, with management noting temporary FCF lag vs operating margin
Full-year FY2027 revenue guidance implies a deceleration from Q2's 30% YoY growth to 24% in Q3, suggesting moderating top-line momentum ahead
positive_highlights: Net new ARR of $134 million grew 28% YoY in constant currency, the second-highest growth rate over the past 10 quarters and accelerating both sequentially and vs Q2 last year
Non-GAAP operating margin expanded 6 percentage points YoY to 21%, with GAAP EPS positive at $0.03 for the fourth consecutive quarter of GAAP profitability
$100k+ ARR customers reached 3,605 with a record 242 net additions, driving 38% YoY ARR growth in that cohort (fourth consecutive quarter of sequential acceleration)
summary: Samsara reported Q2 FY2027 revenue of $508 million, up 30% year-over-year, with ending ARR of $2.1 billion (also +30% YoY) and net new ARR of $134 million, up 28% YoY in constant currency. GAAP EPS turned positive at $0.03 (fourth consecutive GAAP profitable quarter) and non-GAAP operating margin reached 21%, up 6 percentage points YoY. The company guided Q3 revenue to $514-516 million (24% YoY growth) and FY2027 revenue to $2.043-2.047 billion (26% YoY growth), while noting FCF margin will be ~100bps lower than FY2026 due to inventory pre-buys and supply chain costs. summary: Oxford Industries reported Q2 FY2026 net sales of $394M versus $403M a year ago, near the high end of the $380-400M guidance range, with adjusted EPS of $1.34 and adjusted gross margin expanding 140 bps to 63.1%; adjusted EBITDA was $45M (11.4% margin) versus $43M (10.7%). The company narrowed full-year sales guidance to $1.43-1.47B (down 3% to flat) from a prior slightly negative to slightly positive comp view, and cut adjusted EPS guidance to $1.60-2.00 from prior expectations, versus $2.11 last year, citing continued Lilly Pulitzer weakness and softer discretionary demand. The quarter marked the first earnings call under new CEO Charlie Cole, with a $100 million buyback authorization (about $11 million repurchased, $89 million remaining) and a 13% inventory increase described as normalized.

summary: Docusign reported Q2 FY2027 revenue of $876M (up 9% YoY, with a 1.3pp FX tailwind) and non-GAAP operating income of $277M (32% margin, up 180bps YoY, beating the guidance midpoint by 160bps). Full-year revenue guidance of $3.499–$3.507B incorporates the Q2 beat plus second-half outperformance, partially offset by a $4M FX headwind, while full-year ARR growth guidance was raised to 8.5–9.0% (from 8.0% prior) and IAM is now expected to represent 18–19% of exiting Q4 ARR versus 15.1% in Q2. summary: Zscaler reported Q4 FY2026 revenue of $898M, up 25% YoY and above the high end of guidance, with total ARR of $3.8B also up 25% and a record non-GAAP operating margin of 24.3% (up 220 bps YoY). Net new ARR was $246M (up 24%), or $232M (up 17%) excluding Red Canary, which marked a sequential acceleration from 7% in FY2025 and 10% in the first half of FY2026. FY2027 guidance calls for revenue of $3.908B-$3.938B (16.6%-17.5% growth), ARR of $4.396B-$4.426B (~16.6%-17.4%), an operating margin of ~23.7%, EPS of $4.86-$4.90, and a free cash flow margin of 23%-23.5%; the ARR growth guide implies a step-down from Q4's 25% pace, reflecting the sales leadership transition and timing of the new Agentic SecOps launch. Management also announced a restructuring affecting ~3% of employees with $30M-$33M in charges, and expects elevated CapEx in FY2027 on higher memory and component pricing.

The company also initiated a regular quarterly dividend of $0.13 per share (~5.6% annualized yield) and reduced net leverage to 3.6x from 3.8x. Positives were broad-based U.S. growth led by data centers and infrastructure plus 14% Eco-Pan growth; offsets included flat-to-down gross margin (38.7% vs. 39.0%), soft U.K. underlying demand, and continued weakness in residential and light commercial construction.

positive_highlights: Record Q2 revenue of $116M, up approximately 58% YoY, with non-GAAP gross margin of 59% and adjusted EBITDA of $13.9M, both better than expected.
Full-year revenue guidance raised at the low end to $430-441M and gross margin guidance lifted to 55-57%, above the prior high end.
Defense and intelligence revenue grew over 90% YoY, with a new $8M NGA contract and a German government constellation services tender with a maximum value of EUR 25M over five years.
summary: Planet reported record Q2 FY2027 revenue of $116M, up roughly 58% YoY, with non-GAAP gross margin of 59% and adjusted EBITDA of $13.9M, both above expectations; the beat was driven largely by point-in-time revenue from the Swedish Armed Forces satellite handover, which shifted revenue from Q3 into Q2. Full-year revenue guidance was raised at the low end to $430-441M (40-43% growth), gross margin guidance was lifted to 55-57%, and adjusted EBITDA guidance was also increased at the low end to $3-10M. Defense and intelligence grew over 90% YoY, commercial over 15%, and civil government over 5%, with EMEA revenue up over 130%. Q3 revenue guidance of $101-105M implies a sequential decline due to the timing of satellite services revenue, which management attributed to point-in-time recognition variability.

negative_highlights: Net sales fell to $231.7 million from $262.8 million a year ago, with comparable sales down 6.3%
Gross margin excluding the tariff refund was 33.9%, down 170 basis points year over year on targeted promotions
Adjusted EBITDA excluding the tariff refund was $12.1 million, a 5.2% margin, and full-year guidance net of the refund is unchanged at $65-$75 million
positive_highlights: July comparable sales inflected positively, with all 11 marketing channels improving sequentially and momentum continuing into August
Sub-brands are tracking to roughly $110 million in 2026, up 60% year over year and about 12% of total net sales versus 7% last year
SG&A fell $8.6 million to $61.9 million and first-half cash from operations was $10.1 million versus a $2.3 million use last year
summary: Torrid reported Q2 net sales of $231.7 million, down from $262.8 million a year ago, with comparable sales down 6.3%; adjusted EBITDA was $23.3 million, but only $12.1 million (5.2% margin) excluding an $11.1 million IEEPA tariff refund, within guidance. Gross margin was 38.7% versus 35.6% a year ago, but 33.9% excluding the tariff refund, down 170 basis points on targeted promotions. GAAP net income was $5.2 million, or $0.05 per share, versus $1.6 million or $0.02 last year, and SG&A declined $8.6 million to $61.9 million on store-optimization savings. Full-year net sales guidance was maintained at $940-$960 million, while adjusted EBITDA guidance was raised to $76-$86 million solely to reflect the tariff refund; excluding it, the $65-$75 million outlook is unchanged, and management expects a return to positive comparable sales in the second half.

negative_highlights: Full-year volume guidance cut to low to mid single-digit growth from prior outlook, citing market pressure and portfolio transition
U.S. Department of Commerce denied the Connected Vehicle Rule authorization, barring model year 2027 U.S. sales and driving approximately $130 million in U.S. restructuring adjustments
Q2 revenue fell 8% year-on-year to $727 million on lower volume, pricing pressure, and lower carbon credit sales ($36 million vs $42 million)
positive_highlights: Retail sales reached a record first half of 30,423 cars, with Polestar 4 coupe representing two-thirds of volume
Operating loss narrowed 43% and net loss narrowed 29% year-on-year, aided by the absence of the prior year's $724 million impairment
Capital structure strengthened via $640 million debt-to-equity conversion with Geely Sweden and Volvo Cars and extension of a $660 million shareholder loan to December 2031
summary: Polestar reported Q2 2026 revenue of $727 million, down 8% year-on-year, with retail sales of roughly 17,300 cars down 4%, and a net loss of $459 million. Full-year volume guidance was cut to low to mid single-digit growth, and the company accepted the U.S. Department of Commerce decision barring model year 2027 sales in the U.S., triggering about $130 million in material adjustments tied to U.S. restructuring. Gross margin was negative 13% (adjusted negative 13%) versus negative 97% a year earlier, which was distorted by a $724 million impairment; operating and net losses narrowed largely because no such impairment recurred. Cash fell to $888 million from $1.159 billion at year-end 2025, with H1 operating cash outflow of $850 million.

negative_highlights: Gross margin benefited from a one-time tariff refund of about 70 basis points that is not expected to continue.
Supply constraints are limiting revenue growth, with management stating FY2027 and likely 2028 revenue would be higher if more supply were available.
Potential new Canadian tariffs could impose a headwind of roughly $10 million per quarter, though mitigation actions are being explored.
positive_highlights: Revenue of $1.67 billion grew 37% year-on-year, a quarterly record, and direct cloud provider revenue grew over 80%.
Adjusted EPS of $2.11 rose 215% year-on-year to a record; adjusted operating margin of 22.5% more than doubled year-on-year.
Backlog increased $800 million to $8.5 billion, with orders in the first month of Q4 nearly matching all of Q3 and projected year-end backlog above $10 billion.
summary: Ciena reported record Q3 FY2026 revenue of $1.67 billion, up 37% year-on-year, at the top end of guidance. Adjusted gross margin reached 46.4% (up 450 basis points year-on-year, with a 70-basis-point tariff-refund benefit), adjusted operating margin hit a record 22.5% (250 basis points above the guide and more than double the year-ago level), and adjusted EPS was a record $2.11, up 215% year-on-year. The company raised its full-year revenue midpoint to $6.42 billion (up $120 million from last quarter) and issued preliminary FY2027 guidance for at least 30% revenue growth ($8.3-$8.4 billion), gross margin of at least 45%-46%, and adjusted operating margin of 25%-27%. Backlog rose $800 million to $8.5 billion, with management projecting over $10 billion by fiscal year-end and visibility extending into 2028.

negative_highlights: Net sales declined 7.8% year-over-year to $121.4 million
Women's product sales fell 15% and AKHG brand sales fell 26%
SG&A deleveraged 510 basis points to 57.3% of sales on the sales decline
positive_highlights: Underlying gross margin, excluding tariff refunds, expanded 490 basis points to 59.6%
Free cash flow improved $41 million year-over-year to $13 million, with zero ABL debt versus $32.5 million last year
Inventory reduced 15.5% to $125.2 million and clearance inventory down 43.1%, with current products at 85.4% of mix
summary: Duluth Trading reported Q2 FY2027 net sales of $121.4 million, down 7.8% year-over-year, with reported and adjusted diluted EPS of $0.50 including $16.3 million in tariff refunds that contributed $0.44 per share. Excluding tariff refunds, underlying gross margin expanded 490 basis points to 59.6%, adjusted EBITDA was $10.7 million (8.8% of sales), and free cash flow improved $41 million to $13 million, with inventory down 15.5% and clearance inventory down 43.1%. Full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance was raised to $38-$42 million from $28-$32 million, but that increase is driven by the $16.3 million tariff refund; net sales guidance was reaffirmed at $540-$560 million, with Q3 expected to soften as the company laps prior-year clearance events and Q4 improving sequentially. The top-line decline reflects the intentional promotional reset and SKU rationalization, with women's product sales down 15% and AKHG down 26%.

negative_highlights: GAAP EPS was a loss of $0.23 compared to earnings of $0.22 in the prior year, impacted by restructuring and acquisition costs.
Learning revenue fell 20% to $93M, with Professional down 20% on softer consumer demand and corporate assessments, and segment Adjusted EBITDA margin compressed to 15.1% from 27.4%.
Free cash flow was a use of $70M, though improved from a $100M use last year; net debt-to-EBITDA rose to 2.7x from 1.9x due to the Emerald acquisition.
positive_highlights: Research Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 130 basis points to 29.6% on cost savings and Emerald accretion.
AI revenue of $14M was realized in Q1, ahead of the pace needed for the full-year target, with a further $14M already contracted for Q2 and Q3.
Emerald integration is ahead of schedule; revenue synergies and cost synergy capture are tracking ahead of plan, with full $30M synergies expected by year three.
summary: Wiley reported Q1 FY2027 revenue with research up 4% to $293M (Research Publishing +12%, including $13M from Emerald) but learning down 20% to $93M. Adjusted EPS fell 10% and GAAP EPS was a loss of $0.23 versus $0.22 prior year, largely due to restructuring and acquisition costs. The year-over-year decline was driven by a known $29M prior-year AI licensing comparison, though AI revenue of $14M was realized and the company reaffirmed full-year guidance of low-to-mid single-digit organic growth and adjusted EPS of $4.60-$5.05. Management highlighted strong publishing KPIs, margin expansion in research, and early momentum in new partnerships, while acknowledging continued softness in learning.

negative_highlights: Reported a net loss of BRL 90 million for FY2026.
Sugarcane was hit by frost, fires, and excess rain, cutting commercialized volume by roughly 650,000 tons versus prior year and hurting crushing estimates.
Cotton quality/operational issues in Mato Grosso prompted area reductions and negatively impacted results.
positive_highlights: Soy production rose ~19% and corn production rose ~30% year-over-year, lifting grains results.
FY2027 soy is already locked in above $12/bu versus $11 last harvest, a >10% price improvement.
Portfolio value increased to BRL 3.34 billion from BRL 3.1 billion, with area maturity adding ~BRL 95 million.
summary: BrasilAgro reported FY2026 net revenue of BRL 926 million with adjusted EBITDA of BRL 100 million and a net loss of BRL 90 million, compared to a BRL 138 million loss in the prior year. Results were hurt by sugarcane fire/frost impacts and cotton quality issues, while soy and corn delivered volume and margin gains. Management did not provide explicit numeric guidance for FY2027 but pointed to backlog/pricing improvements (soy already locked above $12 versus $11) and expected farmland sales to recover recurring operational results. The company proposed BRL 30 million in dividends while prioritizing debt reduction given a high cost of capital (~14%).

negative_highlights: Single-family housing data deteriorated: starts down ~16% YoY to 808,000 and completions down ~13% YoY to 878,000, both described as weaker than anticipated
Adjusted EBITDA declined in Extruded Solutions (to $35.6 million from $37.1 million) and Custom Solutions (to $12.0 million from $12.9 million) on inflation
Revenue growth of 1.3% was held back by a ~2% tariff reimbursement headwind (~$9 million in Hardware Solutions), with volumes flat and demand still soft in the U.K., Germany, France, and Italy
positive_highlights: Adjusted EPS rose to $0.79 from $0.69 a year earlier and adjusted EBITDA increased to $72.7 million from $70.3 million
Free cash flow grew 3.5% to $47.8 million, funding $42.25 million of debt repayment and $1.7 million of share repurchases; leverage fell to 2.8x
Custom Solutions revenue rose 8.5% to $111 million on 3% volume and 5.5% pricing, aided by roughly $10 million/year of previously won Wood Solutions business
summary: NX reported Q3 FY2026 net sales of $501.8 million, up 1.3% YoY, with volumes flat, pricing up ~3%, and a ~2% drag from IEEPA tariff reimbursements. Adjusted EPS rose to $0.79 from $0.69 and adjusted EBITDA edged up to $72.7 million from $70.3 million, though Extruded and Custom segment adjusted EBITDA both declined on inflationary pressure. Management guided Q4 revenue growth of 2%-3% and adjusted EBITDA margin expansion of 50-75 bps, while flagging mixed housing data: single-family completions down ~13% YoY but permits up 3% and authorized-not-started homes up ~10%.

negative_highlights: No quantitative fiscal 2027 guidance or Q4 revenue/EPS figures were provided on the call
Fourth quarter margin commentary relied on Adjusted EBITDA before corporate expense, with corporate expense described as deliberate infrastructure investment rather than a scalable cost
Consumer garment care division is early-stage; management gave no financial contribution or scale figures for the new Sudsies-led unit
positive_highlights: Record fiscal 2026 revenue of approximately $447 million and record gross profit of approximately $141 million, with gross margin at a record 31.5%
Gross profit grew faster than revenue, which management framed as improving earnings quality
Roughly $21 million of operating cash flow with net debt essentially unchanged at about $44 million despite two acquisitions completed in the year
summary: EVI reported record fiscal 2026 revenue of approximately $447 million and record gross profit of approximately $141 million, with record gross margin of 31.5% as gross profit grew faster than revenue. The company generated roughly $21 million of operating cash flow and ended June with about $44 million of net debt, essentially unchanged from the prior year. Management disclosed no formal quantitative guidance for fiscal 2027, instead citing a substantial acquisition pipeline, a new consumer garment care division anchored by Sudsies, and continued investment in technology including a CRM. The fourth quarter showed commercial laundry Adjusted EBITDA margin above 10% before corporate expense, but no Q4 revenue, EPS, or prior-period comparisons were given on the call.

negative_highlights: Tenant sales declined 8.5% in real terms for the year as prices fell relative to inflation, with tickets and traffic roughly flat
Shopping-mall EBITDA margin compressed to 66% from 67.9% in the quarter on one-off costs and management-program implementation investments
FY2026 income tax was a negative ARS 150 billion and management said Net Debt/EBITDA (currently 1.4x) is expected to increase next year with the CapEx peak
positive_highlights: Rental-segment adjusted EBITDA reached a record high of almost $200 million, up about 4% year over year in dollar terms
Office portfolio reached 100% occupancy; hotel occupancy rose to almost 65% with an average rate of $218
Ramblas del Plata has completed 20 transactions (18 swaps, 2 sales) worth about $130 million, with the Zetta expansion adding 15,000+ sq m leased largely to Mercado Libre
summary: IRSA reported FY2026 net income of ARS 420.9 billion versus ARS 261.9 billion a year earlier, driven largely by a positive ARS 193.7 billion swing in fair value change, and record rental-segment adjusted EBITDA of almost $200 million. Tenant sales fell 8.5% in real terms while mall revenues rose 1.5% on inflation-adjusted fixed rents, occupancy held near 97%, and shopping-mall EBITDA margin slipped to 66% from 67.9% on one-off costs. Management guided to roughly $150 million of FY2027 CapEx excluding new acquisitions, a Net Debt/EBITDA that will rise above the current 1.4x, and a coming dividend proposal, while not giving explicit EBITDA guidance for the development segment.

negative_highlights: Q4 revenue fell 20.8% YoY to $24.3 million and the $20-23 million Q1 FY2027 guide implies further sequential decline
Q4 swung to an operating loss of $0.8 million (operating margin -3.1%) from operating income of $1.4 million (4.6%) a year ago
Full-year G&A expenses rose 36.5% to $6.4 million and management said legacy revenue will 'continue to contract' with the AI business not yet generating revenue
positive_highlights: ARPDAU rose 11.6% to $0.577 from $0.517 and daily payer conversion improved to 2.5% from 2.3%
Company-wide DTC revenue mix reached 16.2%, up from the prior quarter, with a stated goal of exceeding 20% by December 31, 2026
Cash and cash equivalents increased to $17.6 million from $15.2 million a year earlier, and the $5 million buyback was extended through August 28, 2027
summary: Gamehaus reported Q4 FY2026 revenue of $24.3 million, down 20.8% year-over-year and at the low end of its $23-26 million outlook, with net income of $0.9 million versus $1.5 million a year ago and an operating loss of $0.8 million (operating margin -3.1% versus +4.6%). Full-year revenue fell 11.4% to $104.7 million while net income was roughly flat at $3.9 million, aided by $2.5 million of other income. Management guided Q1 FY2027 revenue to $20-23 million, implying further sequential decline, as it shifts the legacy casual and social casino portfolio to a cash-flow/profitability focus and redirects resources toward generative AI. Offsets included ARPDAU up 11.6% to $0.577, payer conversion of 2.5% versus 2.3%, DTC mix reaching 16.2% with a target above 20% by December 31, 2026, and cash rising to $17.6 million.

negative_highlights: Q4 reported sales declined slightly and total company sales are guided to decline in Q1 FY2027 before returning to growth in H2, with ~500 bps of optimization and ~150 bps of project-work headwinds still to cycle
Conventional product segment underlying sales declined mid-single digits and retail sales fell 8%, reflecting planned store actions and a still-early comp turnaround

FY2027 free cash flow guidance of $275–$325 million is below the $323 million delivered in FY2026 as CapEx steps up to ~$300 million, and management flagged low single-digit inflation plus a ~$5 million per quarter net fuel headwind
positive_highlights: Full-year adjusted EBITDA of $701 million grew 27% and came in near the top of guidance; Q4 adjusted EPS of $0.69 and FY adjusted EPS of $2.65 exceeded the high end of guidance

Free cash flow of $323 million for the year was the highest ever and $84 million above FY2025; net leverage reduced to 2.2x, a 1.1-turn improvement, with net debt below $1.6 billion for the first time since fiscal 2018

FY2027 adjusted EBITDA midpoint of $755 million is $25 million above the Investor Day target and implies 10 bps of margin expansion, positioning the company to hit its FY2028 margin target a year early; a new $200 million buyback was authorized
summary: UNFI reported Q4 FY2026 sales of over $7.6 billion (down less than 1% YoY) and full-year sales of approximately $31.2 billion, in line with the updated June outlook. Full-year adjusted EBITDA reached $701 million (up 27%) and adjusted EPS of $2.65 came in above the high end of guidance, while free cash flow of $323 million was the highest ever and net leverage fell to 2.2x from 4x two years ago. For FY2027, management guided sales to $31.2–$31.8 billion (up ~1% at the midpoint, with Q1 down before a return to growth in H2), adjusted EBITDA of $730–$780 million (high single-digit growth, $25 million above the Investor Day target), and adjusted EPS of $3.00–$3.50 (~23% growth at the midpoint). The quarter reflected continued underlying sales growth in line with the $90 billion target market, offset by ~500 bps of optimization headwinds and ~150 bps from cycling short-term project work.

negative_highlights: Technical Solutions organic growth only 2% on ~$15M of project deferrals from an important client, with revenue below expectations
Aviation margin fell 120 bps YoY to 5.6% as airline clients sought cost relief from elevated fuel costs
Segment operating margin was flat YoY at 7.7%, with FY margin outlook trimmed to 7.7%-7.8% on higher WGNSTAR amortization
positive_highlights: Adjusted EPS grew 27% YoY to $1.04 and adjusted EBITDA rose 11% to $139.6M
Company raised FY free cash flow outlook to ~$210M reported from ~$185M prior, after YTD FCF of $199.6M vs $42.4M a year ago
Semiconductor, microgrid and data center businesses generated nearly $775M YTD, growing 26% organically (40% with WGNSTAR) at double-digit margins
summary: ABM reported Q3 FY2026 record revenue of ~$2.3B, up 4.2% YoY (2.1% organic, 2.1% from WGNSTAR), with adjusted EPS up 27% to $1.04 and adjusted EBITDA up 11% to $139.6M. The company raised the midpoint of full-year adjusted EPS to $3.95-$4.10 and raised reported free cash flow guidance to ~$210M from ~$185M, based on $199.6M of YTD FCF versus $42.4M a year ago. Segment margin was 7.7%, up 40 bps sequentially but flat YoY, with B&I down 2.6% as expected and Technical Solutions organic growth at just 2% on ~$15M of client project deferrals that management expects to shift into Q4. Aviation grew 12% but margin fell to 5.6% from 6.8% on airline cost-relief requests tied to higher jet fuel.

negative_highlights: Gross margin contracted 270 bps to 9.9% and gross profit fell to $44.7 million from $45.1 million
Adjusted EPS declined to $0.18 from $0.26 while GAAP net loss was $6.5 million, or $0.08 per diluted share
International farming segment Adjusted EBITDA fell to $7.6 million from $12.1 million on lower average note prices
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA of $32.4 million exceeded the high end of the $28-$32 million guidance range
Annualized Calavo cost synergy estimate raised to more than $30 million from at least $25 million
Avocado volume rose 38% to approximately 253 million lbs and U.S. retail market share gained about 60 bps year to date
summary: Q3 FY2026 revenue rose 26% to $450 million on 38% higher avocado volume (253 million lbs), but GAAP EPS was -$0.08 with adjusted EPS of $0.18 versus $0.26 last year; adjusted EBITDA of $32.4 million exceeded the high end of the $28-$32 million guidance but was roughly flat versus $32.6 million a year ago. Gross margin fell 270 bps to 9.9% and the international farming segment Adjusted EBITDA dropped to $7.6 million from $12.1 million on lower average watching prices. Management reaffirmed its second-half Adjusted EBITDA range of $84-$88 million, implying a Q4 jump to $52-$55 million on the Peru harvest, blueberry seasonality, a full Calavo quarter and initial synergies, and raised its annualized Calavo synergy estimate to more than $30 million from at least $25 million.

negative_highlights: Q4 adjusted EBITDA fell to $24.3 million from $30.5 million in Q3 FY2026
Q4 center-level contribution margin contracted ~30 bps sequentially to 23.9%
FY2027 Medicare net rate increase of just 1.5%-2.0% (including V28 transition) versus the more favorable FY2026 rate environment
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA rose ~175% to $94.6 million in FY2026 from $34.5 million in FY2025
Center-level contribution margin expanded 500 bps to 23.0% for the full year
FY2027 guidance implies adjusted EBITDA margin of ~10.3% versus 9.6% reported in FY2026
summary: InnovAge reported FY2026 revenue of $989.7 million, up 15.9%, with adjusted EBITDA of $94.6 million versus $34.5 million in FY2025 (a ~175% increase) and center-level contribution margin up 500 bps to 23.0%. Q4 revenue rose 4.0% sequentially to $262.0 million and Q4 adjusted EBITDA was $24.3 million, down from $30.5 million in Q3, though net income turned positive at $9.8 million versus a $29.9 million loss in Q3. FY2027 guidance targets revenue of $1.05-$1.085 billion and adjusted EBITDA of $105-$115 million on census growth of 5%-7.5%, implying margin expansion to roughly 10.3% despite a more tempered Medicare rate increase of 1.5%-2.0% and final Medicaid rate outcomes still unresolved in California and Colorado, which represent ~70% of census.

negative_highlights: Net profit attributable to shareholders fell 10.3% YoY to CNY 126-130 million despite revenue growth, due to tax items and non-recurring losses
Sales and marketing expenses surged to ~CNY 638 million from CNY 199 million a year ago, with third-party traffic costs up ~CNY 450 million
Total operating costs and expenses rose 80.5% YoY to CNY 1.337 billion, outpacing the 72.8% revenue growth
positive_highlights: Total revenue grew 72.8% YoY to CNY 1.448 billion, with insurance revenue up 80.5% YoY to CNY 1.333 billion and 15.4% QoQ
Operating profit rose 39.2% QoQ to CNY 111 million and 14.3% YoY; profitability maintained for 18 consecutive quarters since Q1 2022
Board approved a sixth buyback of up to $50 million over 12 months and a ~$10.8 million cash dividend ($0.03 per ADS); 62.9 million ADS repurchased for ~$121 million to date
summary: Waterdrop reported Q2 FY2026 total revenue of CNY 1.448 billion, up 72.8% year-over-year, with insurance revenue of CNY 1.333 billion, up 80.5% YoY and 15.4% QoQ, and operating profit of CNY 111 million, up 14.3% YoY and 39.2% QoQ. Net profit attributable to shareholders was CNY 126-130 million, down 10.3% YoY but up 27.9% QoQ, with the YoY decline attributed to tax-related items and non-recurring gains/losses. Management guided for full-year 2026 revenue growth of more than 40% YoY and operating profit growth of over 10% YoY, and announced a sixth buyback program of up to $50 million over 12 months plus a ~$10.8 million cash dividend. Total costs and expenses rose 80.5% YoY to CNY 1.337 billion, driven by a CNY 450 million increase in third-party traffic marketing spend.

negative_highlights: Non-GAAP gross margin declined to 68.6% from 69.3% year-over-year on high premium messaging volumes and Decisioning Studio headcount costs
Professional services revenue mix shift and ongoing customer migration to new pricing/packaging creates year-over-year comparability headwinds
Q3 revenue growth guidance of ~20% at the midpoint implies a sequential deceleration from Q2's 26%
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 26% year-over-year to $227 million with non-GAAP operating margin expanding over 600 basis points year-over-year to 9.7%
Management raised Q3 and full-year revenue guidance and increased full-year operating income guidance to $75.5-76.5 million
Large-customer dollar-based net retention inflected up 100 basis points sequentially to 112%, with large customers growing 28% year-over-year
summary: Braze reported Q2 FY2027 revenue of $227 million, up 26% year-over-year and 8% sequentially, with non-GAAP operating income of $22 million (9.7% margin) versus $6 million (3.4%) a year ago. Non-GAAP EPS was $0.19 versus $0.15, and record Q2 free cash flow was $22 million. Management raised Q3 revenue guidance to $229-230 million (~20% growth) and increased full-year revenue and operating income guidance, while gross margin declined to 68.6% from 69.3% on premium messaging and Decisioning Studio costs. The company completed a $50 million accelerated share repurchase and reported large-customer DBNR improving to 112%.

negative_highlights: Q2 revenue of ~$32 million missed the prior guidance range of $35-45 million.
Q3 revenue guidance of $11-15 million implies a severe sequential decline from Q2.
Adjusted EBITDA loss of $74.9 million, including $9.2 million PP&E impairment and $2.7 million credit losses, with inventory write-downs and digital asset fair value losses.
positive_highlights: Cash position improved to $66 million at Q2 end from $43 million at Q1 end despite lower revenue.
Project ABC installed hashrate reached 4.85 EH/s at end of July, up 10% from end of March, and cumulative cash received reached $8.4 million as of August 31.
Year-to-date share repurchases totaled 16.4 million ADSs for $7.4 million, funded partly by digital asset monetization.
summary: Canaan reported Q2 FY2026 total revenue of approximately $32 million, below its prior guidance range of $35-45 million, with product revenue of $14 million, mining revenue of $18 million, 2.5 EH/s of computing power sold, and 243 Bitcoin mined. Adjusted EBITDA was a loss of $74.9 million, including non-cash inventory write-downs, PP&E impairments, and digital asset fair value losses, while cash rose to $66 million from $43 million at the end of Q1. Management guided Q3 FY2026 revenue to $11-15 million, well below the Q2 level, citing cautious miner procurement, elevated industry inventory, and aggressive competitor pricing; Q2 product revenue declined sharply from $40 million cited in the CEO's remarks referenced as product revenue for the quarter. The company also sold all Ethereum and 54 Bitcoins in late August to fund $5.4 million of ADS repurchases.

negative_highlights: GTV growth of 17% was about 200 basis points below recent quarters, driven by lower job growth and softer lead volumes in May and June, especially in HVAC.
The shift to Max creates an estimated $4-$5 million near-term revenue headwind in FY2027, comprising $2-$3 million in subscription and about $2 million in professional services.
Guidance was adjusted to reflect more moderate GTV growth and the Max mix shift, contributing to implied back-half growth in the mid-teens.
positive_highlights: Q2 total revenue grew 21% year-over-year to $292.8 million, with subscription revenue up 22% to $212.4 million and usage revenue up 24% to $72.1 million.
Operating margin expanded 310 basis points year-over-year to 15.2%, and FY2027 incremental margins are now expected at 33% versus a prior 25% floor framework.
Max locations exceeded the doubling goal in Q2 and are now expected to exceed 700 by fiscal year-end; Virtual Agent revenue more than doubled sequentially.
summary: ServiceTitan reported Q2 FY2027 total revenue of $292.8 million, up 21% year-over-year, with platform revenue of $284.5 million (+22%), non-GAAP operating income of $44.4 million (15.2% margin, up 310 bps), and record free cash flow of $50.5 million (+47%). GTV grew 17% to $26.8 billion, about 200 bps below recent quarters due to lower existing-customer job growth, particularly in HVAC. Guidance for Q3 is $285-$287 million revenue and $29-$30 million operating income, with FY2027 revenue of $1.139-$1.144 billion and operating income of $152-$154 million, reflecting roughly $4-$5 million of near-term revenue headwinds from the Max mix shift and a more moderate GTV forecast. Management also narrowed its trade-expansion focus to existing trades and reported the CRO transition from Ross Biestman to Rikus Pretorius.

negative_highlights: Net revenue declined 25% YoY to $181 million, driven by IL MAKIAGE ad-account dislocation and sharply higher CPA
Gross margin compressed ~360 bps YoY to 68.7% on lower AOV and product mix
First-order net revenue fell ~40% YoY and repeat-order revenue fell ~20%, indicating compounding pressure into 2027
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA of $13 million beat guidance of $8-10 million
SpoiledChild on track to grow at least 35% and approach $350 million in 2026 net revenue, with 12-month net revenue repeat rates well above 100%
Q3 guidance implies a ~20-point sequential improvement, with net revenue down ~5% YoY
summary: Oddity Q2 FY2026 net revenue fell 25% YoY to $181 million, at the favorable end of guidance for a 25-30% decline, with adjusted EBITDA of $13 million beating the $8-10 million outlook and adjusted diluted EPS of $0.20. Gross margin compressed ~360 bps to 68.7% and first orders fell ~40% amid an ongoing ad-account algorithm dislocation at IL MAKIAGE, partly offset by SpoiledChild tracking to ~$350 million in 2026 revenue and METHODIQ's early ramp. Q3 revenue is guided to decline ~5% YoY with adjusted EBITDA of $18-20 million, while FY2026 revenue is guided down ~19% with EBITDA of $30-32 million. The company repurchased 5.6 million shares for $80 million in the quarter and repurchased $50 million face value of its June 2030 exchangeable notes for $35 million.

negative_highlights: Residential lot development remained challenged, down high single digits in the quarter (after a low-double-digit decline in Q1), with full-year residential expected down mid-single digits
Gross margin was approximately 26.7%, flat year over year and down sequentially from Q1, with benefits from private label offset by project mix and PVC price increases failing to stick

Smart Utility growth was only about 1% with volume flat, as large project start timing (including Miami-Dade, expected at only 5%-10% of project volume late this year) pushed meaningful ramp into 2027
positive_highlights: Adjusted Diluted EPS rose 8% to $0.94 versus $0.87, aided by a lower share count from repurchases
SG&A held roughly flat at ~$301 million while sales grew 2.5%, improving ~40 bps as a percentage of sales and driving 10 bps of Adjusted EBITDA margin expansion to 12.8%

Fire protection sales increased 14% on share gains and higher steel pricing, and the company deployed $169 million to repurchase 3.7 million shares, a second consecutive quarter of record open market buybacks
summary: Core & Main reported Q2 net sales of approximately $2.1 billion, up 2.5% year over year, with volume, price, and acquisitions each contributing slightly. Adjusted EBITDA rose about 3% to $274 million as Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 10 basis points to 12.8% on roughly flat SG&A of $301 million, and Adjusted Diluted EPS increased 8% to $0.94. Full-year guidance was affirmed at net sales of $7.8-$7.9 billion, Adjusted EBITDA of $950-$980 million, and operating cash flow conversion of 60%-70%, unchanged from prior guidance. Fire protection sales rose 14% (about two-thirds price/steel), treatment plant grew double digits to a mid-single-digit share of sales, data center contribution nearly doubled year over year, while residential lot development fell high single digits and PVC pricing stayed flat with announced increases failing to stick.

negative_highlights: CooperVision revenue was flat year-over-year at $717 million, with the Americas growth of ~5% reduced to ~0% by channel inventory actions; similar impact expected in Q4
Q4 guidance implies consolidated organic growth of 0%-2%, with CooperVision down 2% to flat organically, a sharp deceleration from earlier expectations of ~4% growth in 2H 2026
FY2027 headwind from GILTI increase expected to lift the non-GAAP effective tax rate to ~17.5% from ~15.5%, and margin pressure from commercial investments in CooperVision and R&D in fertility
positive_highlights: Record quarterly free cash flow of $273 million, up 86% year-to-date to $528 million, supporting the $2.2 billion cumulative FCF goal for FY26-FY28
Non-GAAP EPS rose 4% to $1.15, the 11th consecutive quarter exceeding consensus, and the board raised the buyback authorization by $1 billion to ~$1.5 billion remaining
$307 million discrete tax benefit from favorable HMRC resolution, expected to extend non-GAAP tax benefits for at least 10 additional years
summary: Cooper reported Q3 FY2026 consolidated revenue of $1.066 billion, up ~1% reported and organic, with non-GAAP EPS up 4% to $1.15 and record quarterly free cash flow of $273 million. CooperVision revenue was $717 million, essentially flat, due to a proactive U.S. channel inventory reduction that will also pressure Q4; CooperSurgical grew 3% organically with fertility up 5%. Q4 guidance implies consolidated organic growth of 0%-2% and EPS of $1.05-$1.09, below the prior Q3 run rate, while the company also announced a $307 million tax benefit and a $1 billion increase to its buyback authorization. The strategic review concluded with the board deciding to retain CooperSurgical rather than watch.

negative_highlights: Space, Cyber and Directed Energy revenue fell 21% year-over-year to $134 million, and the segment posted negative $9 million adjusted EBITDA on under-absorption of fixed costs.
Adjusted service gross margin declined to 8% from 13% a year ago, and adjusted SG&A rose to 18% of revenue from 14%, including an unexpected $4.2 million bad debt reserve.
Full-year FY2027 free cash flow is still targeted to be negative, with Q1 free cash flow at negative $36 million on elevated CapEx.
positive_highlights: Funded backlog reached a record $1.5 billion, up 37% year-over-year and 23% from the prior quarter, with total backlog approximately $2.8 billion.
Adjusted EPS rose 84% year-over-year to $0.59, and Q1 adjusted product gross margin improved to 40% from 36% a year ago.

Landmark counter-UAS wins: nearly $465 million U.S. Army EHEL/LOCUST directed energy contract, a sole-source $500 million Titan IDIQ (with $80 million initial award), plus a first international LOCUST order.
summary: AV reported Q1 FY2027 revenue of $480 million with adjusted EBITDA of $53 million (11% of revenue) and adjusted EPS of $0.59, up 84% year-over-year from $0.32. Bookings were $683 million (1.4x book-to-bill) and funded backlog hit a record $1.5 billion, up 37% year-over-year and 23% sequentially, while total funded and unfunded backlog was approximately $2.8 billion. The company reaffirmed full-year FY2027 guidance: revenue of $2.125-$2.225 billion (~10% growth at midpoint), adjusted EBITDA of $305-$325 million, and non-GAAP EPS of $3.02-$3.34, with a 45/55 first-half/second-half revenue split. Segment results were mixed: Autonomous Systems revenue rose 21% to $346 million, but Space, Cyber and Directed Energy revenue fell 21% to $134 million on the SCAR contract termination and discontinued programs, producing a negative $9 million segment adjusted EBITDA.

negative_highlights: SG&A rose to $7.0 million from $5.7 million, with management declining to model where SG&A settles as a percentage of sales at higher revenue levels.
Management cited ongoing industry-wide optical fiber shortages and longer lead times for certain raw materials as the primary impediments to ramping manufacturing.
Working capital of $19.2 million and a daily-swept credit revolver are relied on for growth funding, with no equity or expanded-facility plans disclosed.
positive_highlights: Net sales rose 22% YoY to $24.3 million and nine-month sales rose 18.3% to $62.9 million.
Gross margin expanded 570 bps YoY to 37.4% in Q3, with gross profit up 43.9% to $9.1 million.
Backlog and forward load grew to $13.5 million from $7.3 million at October 31, 2025, and the prior expectation that the second half of fiscal 2026 would be very strong was reaffirmed.
summary: OCC reported Q3 FY2026 net sales up 22% YoY to $24.3 million and net income of $1.9 million, or $0.21 per diluted share, versus $302,000, or $0.04, a year earlier, with gross profit up 43.9% to $9.1 million and gross margin expanding to 37.4% from 31.7%. Backlog and forward load rose to $13.5 million from $13.3 million at April 30, $10.4 million at January 31 and $7.3 million at October 31, and the company said demand is strong across enterprise, data center and specialty markets, including military. Management reaffirmed its prior expectation that the second half of fiscal 2026 would be very strong and said optical fiber shortages and longer lead times for certain raw materials remain the primary impediments to ramping manufacturing, though the company does not provide forward guidance.

negative_highlights: Comparable sales fell 0.4%, with May and June comps down 1% before July inflected positive
Traffic from households under $50,000 was down high single digits, a larger decline than Q1
Footwear, approximately 20% of sales, was the softest category at down 1%
positive_highlights: Gross margin expanded roughly 440 bps to 40.4%, driven by 510 bps from tariff refunds
E-commerce sales grew 12.8% in Q2 and 14% in the first half, with penetration up 110 bps
Full-year gross margin and EPS guidance raised, with adjusted EPS now $6.50-$6.90
summary: Academy reported Q2 FY2026 net sales of $1.6 billion, up 3% with comparable sales down 0.4%, as July turned positive but May/June ran down 1% on a comp basis. Gross margin rose roughly 440 bps to 40.4% on tariff refunds, diluted EPS rose 17.3% to $2.17 and adjusted EPS rose 19.1% to $2.31, though the tariff refund contributed only $0.06 to EPS after reinvestment into price, labor, and marketing. Full-year sales guidance was affirmed at 3%-5% growth with comps flat to +2%, gross margin guidance was raised to 35.5%-36.0%, and EPS guidance was raised to $6.05-$6.45 (adjusted $6.50-$6.90) on a lower share count. Management flagged a challenged consumer, with under-$50,000 household traffic down high single digits and footwear down 1%, while e-commerce grew 12.8% and new stores comped mid-single digits.

negative_highlights: No explicit forward revenue or margin guidance was provided; management declined to extrapolate any single quarter into a specific growth trajectory
Sales and marketing expenses rose 92.2% year-over-year to RMB 26.9 million and R&D rose 66.8% to RMB 20.0 million
Operating income remained slightly negative at RMB -0.6 million, so GAAP profitability depended on non-operating items rather than full operating break-even
positive_highlights: Net revenues grew 254.6% year-over-year to RMB 90.1 million, with first-half 2026 revenues of RMB 189.5 million up 302.6%
Gross margin expanded 11.7 percentage points to 69.2% from 57.5% a year ago and rose from 61.9% in Q1 2026
Achieved first quarterly GAAP net profit of RMB 1.1 million and adjusted non-GAAP net income of RMB 4.7 million, with operating loss narrowed to RMB 0.6 million from RMB 28.5 million
summary: 17EdTech reported Q2 FY2026 net revenues of RMB 90.1 million, up 254.6% year-over-year from RMB 25.4 million, with gross margin expanding 11.7 percentage points to 69.2% from 57.5% and up from 61.9% in Q1. The company posted its first quarterly GAAP net profit of RMB 1.1 million and adjusted non-GAAP net income of RMB 4.7 million, versus a GAAP net loss of RMB 26.0 million a year ago, while operating loss narrowed to RMB 0.6 million from RMB 28.5 million. Cash rose to RMB 456.9 million from RMB 407.0 million at year-end 2025, and the board authorized a new up-to-$10 million share repurchase program. Management cited expansion of the Yiqi Aixue consumer AI membership and district/school subscription projects, and pointed to the Minhang District shift from SaaS toward agentic services, but declined to provide explicit forward revenue or margin guidance and cautioned against extrapolating any single quarter.

negative_highlights: Full-year operating income guidance trimmed to $540-$550 million from prior ~$555 million implied, with American Eagle now guided flat for the back half versus prior low-single-digit positive
Merchandise margins deleveraged 330 bps, with American Eagle markdowns offsetting Aerie improvement; further AE markdowns expected in Q3 for inventory rebalancing
Consolidated inventory cost up 14% and units up 9%, with seasonal note weakness in and older denim fits still needing to be cleared
positive_highlights: Aerie total revenue grew 25% to $536 million with comparable sales up 19%, showing breadth across channels and categories
Q3 comp guidance of mid-to-high single digits keeps Aerie in the high-teens to 20% range, sustaining growth against tougher comparisons
Full-year gross margin expected up year-over-year and Q3 gross margin guided roughly flat despite markdown placeholders
summary: Q2 FY2027 revenue of $1.4 billion rose 8% with comparable sales up 6%, and operating income of $211 million versus $103 million last year included a $161 million net tariff refund benefit; gross margin of 48.7% was up 980 bps, driven 1,300 bps by $179 million of tariff refunds while merchandise margins deleveraged 330 bps. Aerie total sales grew 25% with comps up 19%, while American Eagle total sales rose 1% with comps down 1%. Full-year operating income guidance was trimmed to $540-$550 million from roughly $555 million, driven by American Eagle now guided flat for the back half versus prior low-single-digit positive, plus markdown placeholders; Q3 operating income is guided to $110-$115 million on mid-to-high single-digit comps.

negative_highlights: Excluding tariff refunds, gross margin of 68.3% was roughly flat YoY as a higher full-price rate was offset by greater markdown mix.
Store sales declined 0.7% YoY as markdown note in stores fell, and direct sales growth of 1.9% was driven by higher markdown sales.
Second-half tariff rates are now estimated at 10%-12.5% for goods landed, and management cited emerging shipping fuel surcharge cost pressures.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EPS rose to $1.24 from $0.81 last year and adjusted EBITDA was $20.1 million excluding tariff refunds and ~$600,000 of strategic investments/costs.
Full-year guidance was raised: sales now expected flat to up 2% (vs prior outlook) and adjusted EBITDA guided to $75-80 million, with Q3 sales guided up 3-5% and comps up 1-3%.
Customer file is stabilizing with new-to-brand acquisition accelerating, a younger new customer profile, higher retention and higher spend, and positive store traffic in the quarter.
summary: J.Jill reported Q2 net sales of $154.8 million, up 0.5% YoY, with comps up 0.5%; adjusted EPS was $1.24 versus $0.81 last year and adjusted EBITDA excluding tariff refunds and investments was $20.1 million. Reported gross margin was 76.8% (up ~840 bps) including $13.3 million of net tariff refunds, but was roughly flat at 68.3% excluding refunds. Management raised full-year sales guidance to flat to up 2% and adjusted EBITDA to $75-80 million, and guided Q3 sales up 3-5% with comps up 1-3%, while deploying most tariff refunds into second-half marketing and technology investments.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA grew only 7% to $114 million, with a $10 million advertising expense timing difference reducing growth by approximately 11 points.
Advertising expenses exceeded revenues by $7 million in the first half, and the imbalance is expected to largely remain through the rest of the year.
Full-year same-store sales guidance of 2.5%-3% implies a deceleration from Q3's 3%-4% range.
positive_highlights: Same-store sales accelerated to 2.3% in Q2 from 1.7% in Q1, and management said Q3 is currently tracking above 3%.
System-wide sales grew 10% to ~$1.21 billion and total revenues grew 10% to $208 million, supported by 8.1% net unit growth.
Digital channels expanded ~200 basis points to 43% of sales mix, with loyalty registrations up 22% year to date.
summary: Jersey Mike's reported Q2 FY2026 same-store sales growth of 2.3%, accelerating from 1.7% in Q1, with system-wide sales up 10% to ~$1.21 billion and total revenues up 10% to $208 million; adjusted EBITDA rose 7% to $114 million, pressured by a $10 million advertising expense timing swing that reduced EBITDA growth by ~11 points (ex-timing, EBITDA would have grown 18%). The company guided full-year 2026 same-store sales to 2.5%-3% (including 3%-4% in Q3), net unit growth of at least 8%, and adjusted EBITDA growth of at least 20% (at least 13% in Q3). Key changes included the completion of a $300 million IPO used to repay debt, reducing leverage to ~4.4x, and the ongoing shift to digital marketing representing over 20% of spend, with digital mix reaching 43% of sales.
