negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA margin was flat year-over-year at 17.0%, showing no margin expansion despite revenue growth
APAC fee revenue grew only 1% year-over-year to $87 million and EMEA grew 4% to $228 million, with Middle East dynamics weighing on EMEA
Q2 FY2027 adjusted EPS guidance of $1.30-$1.40 is below the $1.43 just reported, reflecting AMS amortization, interest, and share dilution plus seasonality
positive_highlights: Fee revenue grew 7% year-over-year to $756 million, the sixth consecutive quarter of top-line growth, with growth in all regions and all industry groups
Adjusted diluted EPS grew 9% year-over-year to $1.43, outpacing 7% revenue growth
Estimated remaining fees under existing contracts rose 14% year-over-year to $1.92 billion; consolidated new business grew 12% with RPO new wins of about $160 million
summary: Korn Ferry reported Q1 FY2027 consolidated fee revenue up 7% year-over-year to $756 million, its sixth consecutive quarter of growth, with adjusted EBITDA up 7% to $128 million (17.0% margin, flat year-over-year) and adjusted diluted EPS up 9% to $1.43. Estimated remaining fees under existing contracts rose 14% year-over-year to $1.92 billion, and consolidated new business grew 12%. The company closed its combination with AMS last week, adding roughly $650 million in annualized revenue and a backlog of about $3.5 billion combined, and guided Q2 fee revenue to $860-$878 million, adjusted EBITDA margin to 16.8%-17.2%, and adjusted EPS to $1.30-$1.40, including only two months of AMS. Guidance assumptions include incremental AMS intangible amortization, interest expense, and shares issued; no prior-period guidance comparison was provided in the text.

negative_highlights: Essentially all of the Q2 adjusted EBITDA upside relative to expectations came from timing-related and discrete items (~$15 million total), not underlying run-rate improvement
Free cash flow declined to $90 million from $106 million in the prior year period
Discretionary pressure persisted in treats and toppers within Consumables, with treats growth slowing more sharply than core food
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA margin of 6.8% exceeded guidance of 6.3%-6.4%, with 70 bps of SG&A leverage to 18.4% of net sales
Autoship customer sales grew 9.3% to $2.8 billion, representing 84.6% of total net sales, outpacing overall growth
Active customers rose 3.8% to 21.7 million and NSPAC increased 3.8% normalized, with Chewy outperforming the pet category by 2-3x
summary: Chewy reported Q2 net sales of $3.33 billion, up 7.3% year-over-year (5.7% organic), with adjusted EBITDA of $227 million (6.8% margin) beating guidance of 6.3%-6.4% and adjusted EPS of $0.36. Management narrowed FY2026 organic sales growth to 5.5%-6.3% and raised the low end of adjusted EBITDA margin guidance to 6.7%-6.8% from 6.6%-6.8%, but noted essentially all of the Q2 EBITDA beat came from timing-related and discrete items ($10 million tariff/rebate timing plus $5 million gift card/inventory benefits). The consumer backdrop remains pressured with discretionary treats and hardgoods softness, though trends have stabilized, not deteriorated, versus prior assumptions. Free cash flow fell to $90 million from $106 million on timing, and the company repurchased 9.9 million shares for $200 million.

negative_highlights: Total net revenue declined to $43.8 million from $47.5 million and agribusiness revenue to $42.2 million from $45.9 million; GAAP operating loss widened to $3.0 million from $0.6 million.
Lemon volume guidance cut to the lower end, now 4.0-4.25 million cartons, due to Argentine fruit diverted into the U.S. after Western Europe oversupply, which hurt both volume and price.
Avocado prices fell to $1.15 per pound from $1.50 a year ago, and GAAP net loss applicable to common stock widened to $0.17 per diluted share from $0.06.
positive_highlights: Avocado volume guidance raised again to 7.0-7.25 million pounds for FY2026, versus the prior 5.5-6.5 million range, and management expects more than 10 million pounds in FY2027, a 30%-plus increase.
Adjusted EBITDA increased to $3.9 million from $3.0 million in the prior-year quarter, and SG&A fell to $4 million from $5 million on Sunkist transition savings.
Fresh lemon carton pricing rose to $19.88 from $17.02 a year ago, and the $15 million Windfall Farms sale is set to close September 14, 2026 with proceeds earmarked to reduce debt.
summary: Q3 FY2026 total net revenue fell to $43.8 million from $47.5 million a year ago, with agribusiness revenue down to $42.2 million, and GAAP net loss widened to $3.0 million or $0.17 per diluted share; adjusted EPS was $0.02 versus $(0.02) prior year and adjusted EBITDA rose to $3.9 million from $3.0 million. Lemon volume guidance was trimmed to 4.0-4.25 million cartons on Argentine import oversupply, while avocado volume guidance was raised for a second time to 7.0-7.25 million pounds for FY2026 with a 30%-plus increase expected in FY2027. Management pointed to a Q4 water-rights monetization, the $15 million Windfall Farms sale closing September 14, 2026, and $10 million of targeted SG&A savings, reiterating positive Q4 adjusted EBITDA.

negative_highlights: Famous Footwear sales fell 6.3% with comparable sales down 5.9%, pressured by a later back-to-school season and a shift away from lifestyle athletic
Famous Footwear gross margin contracted 100 bps to 42.7% on increased promotional and clearance activity in lifestyle athletic
SG&A increased $33.7 million to $303.4 million, including $23.5 million from Stuart Weitzman, and full-year adjusted EPS guidance of $1.50-$1.65 reflects softness in Famous
positive_highlights: Brand portfolio organic sales grew 8.2% and operating margin expanded 740 bps to 10.5% (13% excluding Stuart Weitzman)
Consolidated gross margin excluding tariff refunds expanded 340 bps to 46.8%, with brand portfolio gross margin up 880 bps to 49.1%
Sam Edelman sales rose mid-teens, Allen Edmonds sales rose low teens, and Stuart Weitzman is progressing toward break-even in 2026
summary: Caleres reported Q2 adjusted EPS of $0.47 versus $0.35 last year, with sales of $695 million up 5.6% (down 0.8% excluding Stuart Weitzman). Brand portfolio organic sales rose 8.2% and brand portfolio operating margin expanded 740 bps to 10.5%, but Famous Footwear sales fell 6.3% with comps down 5.9% on a late back-to-school and lifestyle athletic weakness. Management raised the low end of full-year adjusted EPS guidance to $1.50-$1.65 (high end maintained) as Q3 adjusted EPS is guided to $0.62-$0.70, while noting continued Famous softness and promotional pressure in the back half.

negative_highlights: Total RPO declined to $470.2 million, down from the April quarter which was itself down from January, marking a third consecutive sequential decline
Full-year operating cash flow guidance was no longer quantified at the prior $45 million level, with management citing a deliberate inventory build and subscription mix shift
Professional services revenue fell to $8.4 million from $14.2 million a year ago, and management noted about $7 million of net unfavorable FX impact on H1 operating profitability
positive_highlights: Non-GAAP EPS nearly doubled to $0.15 from $0.08 a year ago, with non-GAAP operating income up 52.5% to $12.2 million on 12% revenue growth
Software revenue rose 20.9% to $100.8 million and reached 92% of total revenue versus ~86% a year ago, while non-GAAP gross margin expanded 154 bps to 73.7%
New logo activity increased to 40 new customers in H1 from 31 in the prior-year period, and the company remains on track for $20 million of signed U.S. deals this year
summary: Cognyte reported Q2 FY2027 revenue of approximately $109 million, up 12% year over year, with total software revenue up 20.9% to $100.8 million and recurring revenue up 18.4% to $56.2 million. Non-GAAP operating income rose 52.5% to $12.2 million, adjusted EBITDA increased 35.7% to $14.9 million, and non-GAAP EPS nearly doubled to $0.15 from $0.08, while non-GAAP gross margin expanded 154 basis points to 73.7%. The company narrowed full-year revenue guidance around an unchanged ~$448 million midpoint (12% growth) and reiterated FY2027 non-GAAP operating income of ~$66 million, adjusted EBITDA of ~$68 million, and EPS of $0.47, while noting it will not quantify the cash flow impact of a deliberate inventory build. Key changes versus prior periods include a third consecutive decline in total RPO to $470.2 million and a shift in language on full-year operating cash flow from a specific $45 million expectation to 'significantly positive'.

negative_highlights: Q3 revenue guidance of $253–$255 million implies deceleration to 30% growth from 35% in Q2
BoomPop acquisition expected to dilute non-GAAP operating income by mid-single-digit impact in FY27
positive_highlights: Revenue of $233 million grew 35% year-over-year and exceeded expectations
Full-year revenue guidance raised to $927–$933 million (32% growth at midpoint)
Non-GAAP operating margin expanded to 7% from 5% a year ago
summary: Q2 FY2027 revenue was $233 million, up 35% year-over-year, with GBV of just over $3 billion, up 45%, and non-GAAP operating margin of 7%, up from 5% a year ago. The company exceeded expectations for both revenue and non-GAAP operating income and raised full-year revenue guidance to $927–$933 million (32% growth at the midpoint) and non-GAAP operating income guidance to $82–$86 million (9% margin). Subscription revenue grew 39% to $21 million, payment volume grew 34% to $1.3 billion, and free cash flow turned positive at $28 million on a trailing 12-month basis versus a $33 million burn a year ago. The acquisition of BoomPop adds meetings and events capability with a very low single-digit revenue impact in FY27 and expected accretion in FY28.

negative_highlights: Higher SaaS mix created approximately $5 million of in-period revenue timing headwind, with revenue growth of 17% lagging ARR growth of 25%
Q3 ARR guidance of $1.29 billion implies 24% YoY growth, a deceleration from 25% in Q2, and Q3 revenue growth of 16% decelerates from 17%
Q3 adjusted operating margin guidance of 17.7% is below Q2's 20.3%, in part reflecting additional Entro costs
positive_highlights: Total ARR of $1.231 billion rose 25% YoY, exceeding the midpoint of guidance by $11 million, and full-year ARR guidance was raised by $11 million to $1.38 billion
SaaS ARR grew 36% YoY to $847 million with net new SaaS ARR up 34% to $66 million, representing 97% of net new ARR
RPO accelerated to 30% YoY growth to $1.9 billion and AI-driven ARR crossed $70 million, ahead of pace for the $100 million FY-end target
summary: SailPoint reported Q2 FY2027 total ARR of $1.231 billion, up 25% YoY and $11 million above the midpoint of guidance, with SaaS ARR up 36% to $847 million and net new SaaS ARR up 34% to $66 million (97% of total net new ARR). Total revenue rose 17% YoY to $309 million, adjusted operating margin was 20.3%, free cash flow was $37 million, and RPO accelerated to 30% growth at $1.9 billion. Management raised full-year FY2027 ARR guidance by $11 million to $1.38 billion and reiterated FY2029 targets of at least $2.1 billion ARR and $800 million AI-driven ARR. AI-driven ARR crossed $70 million, AI-driven pipeline more than doubled since Investor Day to over $200 million, and customers adopting AI solutions increased annual spend by over 60%, though a higher SaaS mix created roughly a $5 million in-period revenue timing headwind.

negative_highlights: $40.7 million impairment of AI-solution intangibles pushed GAAP net loss to $55.5 million from $14.7 million and reduced those intangibles' fair value to $1.9 million
GAAP gross loss margin widened to -1,051% from -107%, and imaging systems/OEM revenue was only $0.2 million, underscoring minimal hardware sales
Cash fell to $31.4 million from $60 million at December 31, 2025; $8.5 million gross was raised post-quarter, and management said it intends to continue raising funds
positive_highlights: Revenue rose 37% YoY to $4.2 million, with Nanox Health IT adding $0.9 million and USARAD teleradiology revenue averaging 14% YoY growth
Non-GAAP gross margin improved to -13% from -21%, and Nanox Imaging Network claims are being reimbursed at $200-$700 per claim with a modeled $0.5-$1 million annual revenue potential per site

10 signed U.S. commercial distribution partnerships, a Nanox.ARC in commercial use at a RadNet site, and a new CMS code G0680 (effective April 1, 2026) creating a reimbursement pathway for Nanox.AI Cardio
summary: Q2 2026 revenue was $4.2 million, up 37% YoY from $3.0 million, driven mainly by $0.9 million from the consolidated Nanox Health IT business; teleradiology contributed $3 million, AI/software $1 million, and imaging systems/OEM only $0.2 million. GAAP gross margin was -1,051% versus -107%, and a $40.7 million non-cash impairment of AI-solution intangibles drove GAAP net loss to $55.5 million from $14.7 million, while non-GAAP net loss was $11.6 million and adjusted EBITDA loss widened to $11.3 million from $10.4 million. Management cited operational frictions (permitting, shielding, construction, workflow integration) for slower-than-expected commercialization, guided to realizing commercial progress 'in the next few months,' announced a Korea restructuring (chip line idled, ~67% Korea headcount cut, ~15% Israel headcount cut, ~$2 million annualized savings from 2027), and raised $8.5 million gross post-quarter via ATM and a registered direct offering, with cash at $31.4 million versus $60 million at year-end 2025.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA margin declined 100 basis points year-over-year to 42.2%, with about 75% of the change due to higher ancillary revenue mix.
Free cash flow was only $70 million in the quarter, reflecting significant CapEx growth and timing of cash payments.
General Tool adjusted EBITDA margin contracted 130 basis points to 51.5%, about half due to higher fuel costs.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EPS increased 20.4% to a first-quarter record $1.18, driven by higher operating profit and share repurchases.
Specialty rental revenue grew 25.3% with dollar utilization up 300 basis points to 77%.
Fiscal 2027 guidance raised for revenue, adjusted EBITDA, and capital expenditures.
summary: Sunbelt reported record Q1 FY2027 results with total revenue up 11.2% to $3.1 billion and rental revenue up 12.5% to $2.9 billion, citing broad-based growth in General Tool (rental revenue +7.4%) and Specialty (rental revenue +25.3%). Adjusted EPS rose 20.4% to $1.18 while adjusted EBITDA grew 8.7% to $1.3 billion at a 42.2% margin, down from 43.2% due to ancillary revenue mix. The company raised fiscal 2027 guidance for total revenue growth to 6-9%, rental revenue growth to 7-10%, adjusted EBITDA to $4.92-5.12 billion, and increased gross and net rental capital expenditure ranges. Management expressed confidence in sustaining momentum, highlighting accelerating rental rates, tight supply-demand, stable local construction markets, and expectations for flat year-over-year margins with operating profit progression.

negative_highlights: Total revenue grew only 1% year-over-year to $91.9 million, with cash management revenue down 10% to $61.8 million.
Cash management assets fell 4% year-over-year to $44.9 billion, and the annualized cash fee rate declined 6 bps year-over-year to 55 bps.
Adjusted EBITDA fell 15% year-over-year to $38.1 million, and adjusted EBITDA margin contracted roughly 8 percentage points to 41%.
positive_highlights: Investment Advisory assets grew 30% year-over-year to $54.1 billion, with revenue up 31% to $28.8 million.
Total platform assets surpassed $100 billion for the first time in August, ending at $100.9 billion, and August was the best month for total net deposits since August 2025.
Repurchased 3.3 million shares for approximately $30 million in the quarter and ended with $453 million in cash and equivalents.
summary: Wealthfront reported Q2 FY2027 revenue of $91.9 million, up just 1% year-over-year, with cash management revenue down 10% to $61.8 million on a lower 55 bps cash fee rate. Adjusted EBITDA fell 15% year-over-year to $38.1 million (41% margin, down 8 points), and GAAP diluted EPS was $0.10. Offsetting this were Investment Advisory strength — assets up 30% to $54.1 billion, revenue up 31% to $28.8 million — and total platform assets crossing $100 billion in August at $100.9 billion. Management gave no formal guidance, noting near-term Home Lending investment headwinds to margins but reiterating long-term 40%+ EBITDA margin potential.

negative_highlights: Fashion segment comps declined 1%, reflecting weakness at Banter and lower price points, particularly metal pieces
Higher gold costs and a higher effective tariff rate pressured merchandise margin, with tariff refunds ($13 million in Q2) not fully offsetting the net tariff headwind
Q3 guidance implies a modest sequential slowdown, with same-store sales of down 1% to up 2% and adjusted operating income of only $31-$48 million due to planned SG&A deleverage
positive_highlights: Same-store sales rose 2.2% with positive comps in each month of the quarter, now five of the last six quarters positive
Adjusted EPS grew 36% and adjusted operating income rose 25% to $107 million, with adjusted gross margin rate up 70 bps and SG&A down $12 million
Bread Financial credit renewal adds over $1 billion incremental non-comp revenue and operating income through 2035, with $200-$250 million over 36 months and no loss sharing
summary: Signet reported Q2 revenue of $1.5 billion with same-store sales up 2.2%, adjusted EPS up 36% to a level driving adjusted operating income up 25% to $107 million and adjusted gross margin rate up 70 bps. Management raised full-year guidance for the second time, lifting the low end of same-store sales guidance by 75 bps to flat to up 2.5% and increasing adjusted operating income and EPS guidance by over 10%, with roughly two-thirds of the EPS raise from the new Bread Financial credit agreement, tariff refunds, and buybacks and one-third from core performance. The company signed an early seven-year renewal with Bread Financial expected to generate over $1 billion in incremental non-comp revenue and operating income through 2035, including $200-$250 million over the next 36 months and approximately $80 million of cash in Q3. Q3 guidance calls for same-store sales of down 1% to up 2% and adjusted operating income of $31-$48 million, with the smallest quarter of the year facing higher incentive compensation.

negative_highlights: Same-store operating expense excluding credit card fees rose 5%, with total opex up 8% and same-store credit card fees adding ~1.5-2 points
Grocery and general merchandise same-store sales growth of 2.7% held back by weakness in beer, snacks, and cigarettes
Free cash flow fell to $190 million from $262 million a year ago due to higher capex from CEFCO remodels
positive_highlights: Diluted EPS up 28% YoY to $7.37 with EBITDA up 17% to $485 million and net income up 27% to $274 million
Prepared Food and Dispensed Beverages same-store sales up 4.8% with gross margin expanding 130 bps to 59.3%, driven by traffic rather than pricing
Fuel margin of $0.478/gallon, up 6.8 cents YoY, with same-store gallons roughly flat (-0.3%) against an approximate 6% Mid-Continent industry decline
summary: Casey's reported Q1 FY2027 diluted EPS of $7.37, up 28% YoY, on total revenue of $5.68 billion (+24.3%) and EBITDA of $485 million (+17%). Inside same-store sales rose 3.2% with inside gross margin up 30 bps to 42.2%, PF&DB same-store sales up 4.8% at a 59.3% margin, and fuel margin of $0.478/gallon on same-store gallons down 0.3%. Management did not update annual guidance, reiterating its practice of updating on the Q2 call, while noting August trends were within annual ranges and that CEFCO remodel disruption (~25 bps inside, ~50 bps fuel) should inflect favorably around Q4. Key changes versus prior periods: prepared food traffic-led growth with minimal pricing, cheese costs down 9% YoY to $1.93/lb, and elevated operating expense growth (+8%) with same-store opex up 5% ex-credit card fees.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA remained negative at $8.3 million in the quarter
Took a $4.4 million restructuring charge in Q2, primarily severance tied to business line integration
positive_highlights: Revenue rose 188% year-over-year to $46.6 million and exceeded both revenue and adjusted EBITDA guidance
Cost of revenue improved 10.8 percentage points to 64.0% of total revenue from 74.8% a year earlier
Full-year FY2026 revenue guidance raised by $5 million to $200 million, with Q4 adjusted EBITDA profitability reiterated
summary: Q2 FY2027 revenue was $46.6 million, up 188% year-over-year and 12% sequentially, exceeding both revenue and adjusted EBITDA guidance; platform solutions revenue rose 209% to $22.9 million and cost of revenue fell to 64.0% of revenue from 74.8% a year earlier. Adjusted EBITDA improved $3.2 million sequentially to negative $8.3 million, though the quarter included a $4.4 million restructuring charge for acquisition integration. Management raised full-year FY2026 revenue guidance by $5 million to $200 million, guided Q3 revenue to $55 million with adjusted EBITDA narrowing to negative $3.5 million, and reiterated a commitment to adjusted EBITDA profitability in Q4 2026 and free cash flow positive in the back half of 2027. Other changes versus prior periods include a completed $23.7 million net follow-on offering, $39.3 million in cash as of July 31, 2026, a one-year extension of the $13.2 million senior secured loan to April 2028, and more than 30 customers now at over $1 million in annual contract value including a first $10 million ACV customer.

negative_highlights: $3.9 million uncollectible accounts receivable charge recorded with no recovery being pursued
First-half net income fell to $4.3 million ($0.53/share) from $5.8 million ($0.72/share) a year ago
Gross margin held flat at ~29% and management said some tariff and shipping cost increases cannot be passed through to customers
positive_highlights: Net sales rose 24% YoY to $59.6 million and Q2 EPS more than tripled to $0.31 from $0.10
Backlog increased to $142.3 million from $121.6 million at January 31, 2026, with $67.8 million of new orders booked in the quarter
New $90 million JPMorgan facility ($75M revolver + $14M term loan, plus $50M accordion) closed, cutting net debt to ~$4.3 million from ~$13.8 million
summary: Q2 FY2026 net sales rose 24% YoY to $59.6 million, with net income attributable to common stock of $2.5 million, or $0.31 per diluted share, versus $0.9 million and $0.10 a year earlier; results absorbed a $3.9 million uncollectible receivable charge offset by a $1.6 million tax benefit. Gross margin held at ~29%, in line with the prior year's ~30%, while income from operations rose to $4.3 million from $3.2 million; first-half net income fell to $4.3 million from $5.8 million on the write-off. Backlog grew to $142.3 million from $121.6 million at year-end, and the company secured $67.8 million in new orders. Management guided to a strong second half, citing Ohio and Qatar facility ramps (full production by early 2027), Saudi Aramco qualification of a new product line, and a new $90 million JPMorgan credit facility, but gave no explicit numerical guidance.

negative_highlights: Excluding $10.4 million of tariff refunds, gross margin decreased 290 basis points on higher product and freight costs
GAAP diluted EPS declined to $0.80 from $0.93 year-over-year
Q3 Vince sales growth guidance of 5%-8% implies a significant deceleration from the 11.7% reported in Q2
positive_highlights: Net sales rose 11.7% to $81.8 million, with DTC up 13.7% and wholesale up 10.4%
Adjusted EBITDA reached $18.0 million versus $6.7 million excluding prior-year ERC benefit
Full-year Vince outlook raised to 8%-10% net sales growth and 9%-9.5% adjusted EBITDA margin
summary: Vince reported Q2 fiscal 2026 net sales of $81.8 million, up 11.7% year-over-year, with DTC up 13.7% and wholesale up 10.4%. GAAP diluted EPS fell to $0.80 from $0.93, but adjusted EPS rose to $1.02 from $0.38 and adjusted EBITDA reached $18 million versus $6.7 million excluding the prior-year ERC benefit; reported results included $10.4 million of tariff refunds, and excluding those, gross margin fell 290 basis points. Management raised the full-year Vince outlook to approximately 8%-10% net sales growth and 9%-9.5% adjusted EBITDA margin, while guiding Q3 Vince sales to 5%-8% growth. The company also completed the acquisition of OVO, a streetwear brand with nearly $50 million in calendar 2025 net sales, expected to be earnings neutral this year and accretive in fiscal 2027.

negative_highlights: Fleet operational utilization fell to 73.5%, with technical off-hire at 10.7% of calendar days from six dry dockings, and seven more dry dockings scheduled for the rest of 2026
Dry docking costs of $7.5 million and voyage costs up $14.4 million YoY on 58% more spot days and Brent averaging about $97/bbl vs. $67/bbl

One dry bulk vessel remains stranded in the Strait of Hormuz since late May, and management flagged rate risk if the Strait stays closed — conditions it said make medium-term market impact 'not yet visible'
positive_highlights: Q2 revenue of $87.1 million, up 140% YoY and 41.2% QoQ, an all-time quarterly high
Net income of $34.8 million (EPS $0.75) vs. $12.8 million (EPS $0.36) a year earlier; 1H26 net income of $62.8 million surpassed all of FY2025's $50 million
Debt-free balance sheet with $245.2 million cash at June 30, about $260 million currently, and a $30 million-plus gain on the sale of the tanker Suez Enchanted
summary: Imperial Petroleum reported record Q2 FY2026 revenue of $87.1 million, up 140% year-over-year and 41.2% sequentially, with net income of $34.8 million (EPS $0.75) versus $12.8 million (EPS $0.36) in Q2 2025; first-half net income of $62.8 million already exceeded full-year 2025's $50 million. Cash and deposits rose to $245.2 million at June 30 (about $260 million currently), with zero debt and six-month operating cash flow of $78 million. The company took delivery of two vessels, sold the Suez Enchanted for a profit above $30 million, and targets a 25-vessel fleet by year-end while noting seven remaining dry dockings in 2026. Guidance was qualitative only, with management citing geopolitical tensions and an undisclosed impact from a dry bulk vessel stranded in the Strait of Hormuz.

negative_highlights: Q3 guidance implies sales down 5.5%-7% and comps -5% to -6.5%, with EPS of $0.00-$0.10 versus $0.55 prior year
Full-year operating margin now expected down slightly versus prior guidance of 50-100 bps growth
Q2 comps -2.1% driven by transaction decline, with footwear accounting for 70% of U.S. sales decline; operating loss of $1.3 million
positive_highlights: International comps positive (other international +2.1% in Q2; Canada, Europe, Australia all positive), with 37-day period comps up 0.5% ex-North America
Cash and marketable securities of $97.3 million with no debt and full $25 million undrawn credit facility
Share count down ~6% YoY due to repurchase program; 1.5 million shares repurchased YTD at $29.5 million
summary: Zumiez reported Q2 FY2026 net sales down 2.5% to $209 million with comparable sales down 2.1%, citing U.S. softness (North America comps -2.9%) offset by positive international comps (other international +2.1%). Gross margin contracted 20 bps to 35.3% and the company swung to an operating loss of $1.3 million and a net loss of $0.17 per share versus a $0.06 loss a year ago. Management guided Q3 sales down 5.5%-7% with comps of -5% to -6.5%, and retracted prior full-year operating margin growth guidance of 50-100 bps, now expecting a slight decline while refraining from specific full-year EPS guidance. Results fell short of expectations due to U.S. footwear weakness, and quarter-to-date trends through Labor Day remained soft, prompting a conservative outlook.

negative_highlights: DTC net revenue per customer fell 1.4% year over year to $417, pressured by outsized new-customer acquisition in the first half
Q4 growth outlook reflects tougher comparisons as the company laps 24% growth and tariff-related supply chain normalization from last year, with Q3 revenue guided above Q4
Inventory rose 25.7% year over year to $81.8 million and SG&A dollar costs increased on shipping, stock-based compensation, and new stores; Q3 will carry elevated public company and share-based costs
positive_highlights: Net revenue grew 24.1% to $155.2 million, above the high end of the estimates provided at IPO, marking a 21st consecutive quarter of double-digit growth
Gross margin expanded approximately 230 bps to 66.7% on lower blended tariff rates and higher AUR, lifting adjusted EBITDA 54% to $25.4 million (16.4% margin)
International net revenue rose 36.8% to $31.2 million with new customer growth in France accelerating to more than 180% year over year in H1 2026
summary: Reformation reported its first public quarter with Q2 FY2026 net revenue up 24.1% to $155.2 million, beating the high end of IPO-period estimates, with DTC up 21.2% to $135.3 million, wholesale up 48.7% to $19.9 million, and international up 36.8% to $31.2 million. Gross margin expanded roughly 230 bps to 66.7% on lower tariff rates and higher AUR, driving adjusted EBITDA up 54% to $25.4 million (16.4% margin) and net income to $12.4 million. Full-year 2026 revenue guidance is $602-$606 million (18.6%-19.5% growth) with adjusted EBITDA margin of 14%-14.2%, reflecting Q2 outperformance and current Q3 trends; Q3 revenue is expected to exceed Q4. LTM active customers grew 23% to 1.2 million, while DTC net revenue per customer fell 1.4% on outsized new-customer mix.

negative_highlights: Gross margin fell 690 bps to 31.9% and merchandise margin declined 630 bps, with ~390 bps from lapping last year's tariff pricing benefit
Full-year guidance was lowered, including adjusted EPS of $0.75-$0.90 and gross margin compression of 390-410 bps, with no margin recovery assumed
Store traffic declined as comps fell 7.1%, and the promotional environment is expected to persist without improvement
positive_highlights: August comps improved to -2.7% from Q2's -7.1% decline, with Shoe Carnival down less than 1%
E-commerce comps grew 18.8% in Q2 and continued double-digit growth in August
Inventory reduced 5.0% YoY to $426.6M and debt-free with $131.6M in cash and marketable securities
summary: Q2 FY2026 net sales fell 7.2% to $284.3M with comps down 7.1%, gross margin compressed 690 bps to 31.9%, and EPS dropped to $0.23 from $0.70. Management lowered full-year guidance to net sales of $1.1B-$1.111B (down 2%-3%), adjusted EPS of $0.75-$0.90, and gross margin of ~32.5%-32.7% (390-410 bps of compression), explicitly not assuming any promotional or margin improvement. The key change versus the prior quarter was the guidance cut, partly offset by an improved August comp of -2.7% (from -7.1% in Q2) driven by localized athletic assortments, though Shoe Station continued down mid-high single digits.

negative_highlights: Consolidated net sales fell ~1% YoY to $730.6 million, with comps down 2.4% and retail comps down 2.6%.
Sandals weakness accounted for roughly 200 bps of the retail sales decline, driven by early weather-related headwinds.
Adjusted operating expenses deleveraged 300 bps as a percentage of sales due to higher performance-based compensation and marketing investments.
positive_highlights: Adjusted gross margin expanded 430 bps to 47.9%, with 280 bps from tariff refunds and 150 bps from organic margin expansion.
Full-year adjusted EPS guidance raised to $0.47-$0.52 from prior $0.28-$0.38, and sales guidance lifted to flat to up 1%.
Brand portfolio segment sales grew 18% YoY, led by Topo (+24%) and Jessica Simpson (+24%), with Topo expected to exceed $100 million in 2027.
summary: Designer Brands reported Q2 FY2026 net sales of $730.6 million, down about 1% YoY, with comps down 2.4% and retail comps down 2.6%, driven by a sandals shortfall that accounted for roughly 200 bps of the retail decline, partially offset by an 18% increase in brand portfolio sales. Adjusted EPS was $0.34 versus $0.33 last year, and adjusted operating income rose to $39.4 million with a 140 bp margin improvement, aided by $20.2 million of tariff refunds. Management raised full-year sales guidance to flat to up 1% from a prior -1% to +1%, and increased adjusted diluted EPS guidance to $0.47-$0.52 from $0.28-$0.38. The company also noted that retail trends returned to slightly positive quarter to date, with athletic demand improving 400 bps in August and back-to-school performing ahead of expectations.

negative_highlights: Net loss of $4.1 million ($0.06 per share) in Q4, driven by $2 million non-cash earn-out adjustments and higher operating expenses
Glass melting capacity remains the primary constraint; demand is outpacing supply even after the Amorphous Materials acquisition, requiring significant FY2027 CapEx
G5 cooled camera redesign to Black Diamond is behind schedule due to stretched supply chains and first-time large-diameter glass melting challenges
positive_highlights: Q4 revenue grew 73% YoY to a record $21.2 million, the fourth consecutive quarter of sequential growth
Gross margin expanded to 39.4% from 22% YoY, driven by higher-margin assemblies/modules/cameras at 43% of revenue and improved yields
Adjusted EBITDA turned positive at $2.1 million (10% of revenue) versus a $2.0 million loss, with full-year adjusted EBITDA swinging to a $4.2 million profit
summary: LightPath reported record Q4 FY2026 revenue of $21.2 million, up 73% year-over-year, with gross margin expanding to 39.4% from 22%. Adjusted EBITDA swung to a $2.1 million profit from a $2.0 million loss, marking the fourth consecutive positive quarter. Full-year revenue grew 93% to $71.7 million, backlog rose 197% to $110.9 million, and cash ended at $93.2 million with no debt. Management guided to higher CapEx in FY2027 to expand capacity, and noted two large post-quarter orders totaling $24 million.

negative_highlights: Full-year adjusted EBITDA fell to $2.9 million from $29.2 million; Q4 adjusted EBITDA loss widened to $31 million from $24.2 million
Transactions declined 17.6% for the fiscal year and adjusted gross margin fell to 38.0% from 39.1%

FY2027 guidance projects mid-single-digit revenue decline and only $10-15 million of adjusted EBITDA; company is evaluating asset sales and capital raising with Guggenheim, and net debt rose to $128 million from $114 million
positive_highlights: BloomNet grew 1.9%, the only segment to increase, aided by local marketplace apps (DoorDash, Instacart, Uber Eats)
Free cash flow improved $55 million versus the prior year on working capital discipline, with inventory down to $153 million from $177 million
Original $50 million run-rate cost savings target achieved a year early, with an additional $15-20 million of opportunities identified
summary: Q4 revenue fell 12.9% to $293.1 million with Consumer Floral down 13.4% and Gourmet Foods down 15.4% (Easter timing a 2.5-3.5 pt drag); full-year revenue declined 10.8% to $1.5 billion and adjusted EBITDA collapsed to $2.9 million from $29.2 million. Q4 adjusted EBITDA loss widened to $31 million from a $24.2 million loss, and adjusted gross margin contracted to 34.7% from 35.5% on deleveraging, commodity costs and inventory reserves, partly offset by a ~$7 million tariff refund. FY2027 guidance calls for mid-single-digit revenue decline and adjusted EBITDA of $10-15 million including ~$12 million of incremental variable comp; the company also amended its credit facility and retained Guggenheim to evaluate asset sales and capital raises.

negative_highlights: Gross margin declined, driven by data center ramp and acceleration of lower-margin infrastructure revenue.
Free cash flow was negative $5 billion in Q1 as CapEx of $28 billion exceeded record operating cash flow of $23 billion.
CapEx remains very high at $90-95 billion for the full year, with no timeframe given for a return to positive free cash flow.
positive_highlights: Total revenue up 30% year-over-year to a record $19.3 billion, with the first-ever sequential Q1 revenue growth.
Cloud infrastructure revenue grew 121% year-over-year to $7.4 billion, accelerating from 93% growth in Q4.
Full-year revenue guidance raised to at least $90 billion (+34%) and EPS to $8.10, from prior guidance.
summary: Oracle reported Q1 FY2027 total revenue of a record $19.3 billion, up 30% year-over-year, with cloud infrastructure revenue of $7.4 billion up 121% and non-GAAP EPS of $1.92 up 30%. Non-GAAP operating income rose 31% to $8.2 billion with operating margin roughly flat at 42%, while gross margin declined as expected on data center ramp and mix. RPO increased $26 billion from Q4, and full-year guidance was raised to at least $90 billion in total revenue (+34%) and $8.10 in non-GAAP EPS, versus prior guidance. CapEx for the full year is still anticipated at $90-95 billion with negative free cash flow of $5 billion in Q1.

negative_highlights: Merchant division net revenue declined 10% to ZAR 729 million due to revenue compression and mix effects despite volume growth.
Consumer ARPU growth was driven by lending and insurance rather than pricing power, with transactional fees rising only 3%.
Merchant blended ARPU declined 8% as the faster-growing community segment (lower margin) outpaced corporate merchants.
positive_highlights: Group Adjusted EBITDA grew 41% to ZAR 1.27 billion for the full year, exceeding guidance.
Consumer division net revenue surged 38% to ZAR 2.4 billion driven by a 19% increase in customer base and cross-note.
Enterprise division core net revenue grew 45% with take rates increasing on both ADP and utilities products.
summary: Lesaka reported full-year FY2026 net revenue growth of 20% to ZAR 6.33 billion and Group Adjusted EBITDA growth of 41% to ZAR 1.27 billion, delivering on all guidance measures. The company achieved positive GAAP net income for the first time since 2022 with a leverage ratio of 1.9x, ahead of its Bank Zero acquisition which is expected to close before the end of calendar year 2026. Fourth quarter results showed an 8% revenue increase and record Adjusted EBITDA of ZAR 367 million, driven by strong performance in Consumer (31% growth) and Enterprise (34% growth) divisions.

negative_highlights: Voyage expenses rose to $82 million in the first half from $68 million and to $52 million in Q2 from $32 million, largely on ~25% higher bunker prices
The company continues to avoid the Strait of Hormuz due to geopolitical disruption, constraining routing flexibility
Q2 operating expenses were cited as a $5 million reduction but described as part of a 'modest unexpected increase' in the half; net income depends materially on $38 million in capital gains
positive_highlights: Q2 EPS rose 557% to $4.40 from $0.67 on gross revenues of $298 million versus $193 million
First-half profit-sharing revenue reached $71 million versus $10 million a year earlier, with Q2 at $30.5 million
Management guided to a significant second-half profit-sharing increase, citing 13 profit-sharing vessels including seven Suezmaxes and two VLCCs
summary: TEN reported Q2 2026 net income of $139.3 million, or $4.40 per share, versus $26.8 million, or $0.67, a year earlier — a 557% EPS increase — on gross revenues of $298 million versus $193 million. First-half net income reached $228 million ($7.12 per share) from $64.5 million ($1.70), with TCE per ship per day of $43,503 versus $30,754, a 41% increase. Profit-sharing revenue was $71 million in the first half ($30.5 million in Q2) versus $10 million a year earlier, and management guided to a significant second-half increase, with 13 profit-sharing vessels including seven Suezmaxes and two VLCCs. TEN also announced the sale of two 2006-built Suezmaxes for net proceeds of $100 million and said it expects to increase the semi-annual dividend after its November strategy meeting.

negative_highlights: Operations and support expenses jumped 139.1% year-over-year to RMB 97.8 million due to the newly launched advertising services.
General administrative expenses rose 36.3% year-over-year to RMB 64.8 million on higher professional service fees and personnel costs.

Income tax expense increased to RMB 59.9 million from RMB 11.1 million a year ago due to a higher effective tax rate, and under the $15 million buyback only ~114,000 ADS (~$1.6 million) had been repurchased as of August 31, 2026.
positive_highlights: Total revenue rose 30.1% year-over-year to RMB 1.39 billion, with net income up 35.6% to RMB 413.2 million (29.7% net margin).
Insurance distribution revenue grew 30.4% year-over-year to RMB 457.4 million and system services revenue grew 22.8% to RMB 881.9 million.
Cash, time deposits, restricted cash, and note weakness in-term investments reached RMB 5.16 billion, up 50.9% year-over-year, with Q2 operating cash flow of RMB 419.1 million.
summary: Yuanbao reported Q2 FY2026 total revenue of RMB 1.39 billion, up 30.1% year-over-year, with net income of RMB 413.2 million (up 35.6%) and a 29.7% net margin; non-GAAP adjusted net income was RMB 431.2 million (up 32.6%) at a 31% margin. Growth was driven by insurance distribution revenue of RMB 457.4 million (+30.4%), system services revenue of RMB 881.9 million (+22.8%), plus RMB 52.8 million from a newly launched advertising service. Cash and investments totaled RMB 5.16 billion, up 50.9% year-over-year, and operating cash flow was RMB 419.1 million. Management did not provide explicit numeric guidance; commentary was qualitative, citing stable customer acquisition ROI, a growing rather than reduced dividend, and continued AI/R&D investment, while specific metrics such as advertising margins, policy counts, and average ticket size were withheld.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA declined YoY to $20.2 million (12.3% of revenue) from $20.5 million (13.9%), and adjusted EPS fell to $0.85 from $0.87
GAAP net income fell to $8.7 million from $9.6 million, with GAAP EPS down to $0.59 from $0.66, including $2 million of lease termination losses and severance tied to nearshore-to-offshore shifts
FY2027 revenue guidance of 9-11% growth decelerates from FY2026's 15.4%, and capital expenditures rose to $27.8 million (4.3% of revenue) from $18.4 million (3.3%)
positive_highlights: Revenue rose 12% YoY to a record $164.3 million in Q4, the sixth consecutive quarter of double-digit growth, with full-year revenue up 15.4% to $644.1 million
Full-year records across Adjusted EBITDA ($82.4M), adjusted EPS ($3.52, up 28%), operating cash flow ($59M), and free cash flow ($31.2M); net cash improved to $30.9 million
Health tech grew 42% in Q4 to $29.4 million and 38% for the year to $114 million, surpassing the stated $100 million target, and 17 new trophy logos were added for the year
summary: IBEX reported Q4 FY2026 revenue of $164.3 million, up 12% YoY and the sixth straight quarter of double-digit growth, with full-year revenue up 15.4% to $644.1 million. Adjusted EBITDA fell to $20.2 million (12.3% of revenue) from $20.5 million (13.9%) on training costs for new client wins, nearshore-to-offshore work transfers, and higher fuel prices, while adjusted EPS slipped to $0.85 from $0.87 and GAAP EPS dropped to $0.59. Management guided FY2027 revenue to $700-715 million (9-11% growth) and Adjusted EBITDA to $90-94 million, with Q1 revenue of $168-170 million and said EBITDA margins should resume expanding. Health tech grew 42% in Q4 and surpassed the $100 million full-year target at $114 million, and the company cited accelerating new-logo wins (nine in Q4, 17 for the year) and AI agent deployments across five verticals.

negative_highlights: Upholstery sales declined slightly to $22.2 million from $22.6 million, with segment gross margin slipping to 18.6% from 18.9%
Excluding the roughly $7 million in one-time tariff recoveries, the company still posted a non-GAAP operating loss of $271,000
Guidance remains limited to Q2 directional expectations due to macro and trade uncertainty, with no full-year outlook provided
positive_highlights: Bedding segment sales rose 13.2% to $31.8 million despite one fewer note week, with gross margin expanding to 13.6% from 10.5%
Gross profit excluding tariff recoveries rose approximately 17% year over year to $8.4 million (15.6% of sales)
Net debt reduced roughly 70% to $3.1 million from $10.9 million at fiscal year-end, with Q1 free cash flow of $7.8 million
summary: Culp reported Q1 FY2027 net sales of $54.0 million versus $50.7 million a year ago, with bedding sales up 13.2% to $31.8 million and upholstery roughly flat at $22.2 million. GAAP gross margin jumped to 28.5% from 14.3%, aided by roughly $7 million in one-time IEEPA tariff recoveries; excluding those recoveries gross margin was 15.6% (about 17% gross profit growth) and non-GAAP operating loss narrowed to $271,000 from $1.9 million. Net income was $6.0 million, or $0.47 per diluted share, versus a net loss of $0.02 per share, and net debt fell roughly 70% to $3.1 million. Management provided limited guidance, expecting consistent sequential sales, year-over-year growth, break-even operating income, and accelerating adjusted EBITDA in Q2.

negative_highlights: Organic services growth of ~9% was unchanged from Q1, despite management noting some improvement in freight; the CEO pushed back on the idea that the environment 'got a whole lot better'.
Q3 baseline adjusted EBITDA margin of ~38% is below the company's 40–45% target range, largely due to lower-margin Tai and Extensiv acquisitions.
Professional services and other revenue declined slightly to $12.4 million from $12.8 million a year ago.
positive_highlights: Total revenue grew 12% YoY to a record $201.1 million, with services revenue up 13% to $188.6 million.
Adjusted EBITDA reached a record $94.4 million (46.9% margin), up 18% YoY; net income rose 32% to $50 million.
Generated $81.3 million in operating cash flow, up 28% YoY, ending the quarter with $401 million cash and no debt.
summary: Descartes reported record Q2 FY2027 revenue of $201.1 million, up 12% YoY, with record adjusted EBITDA of $94.4 million (46.9% margin, up 18%) and record net income up 32% to $50 million; GAAP EPS was $1.13 for the first half. Organic services growth was 'just north of 9%', consistent with Q1, and professional services revenue declined slightly to $12.4 million. Management did not raise full-year guidance but pointed to an ongoing Q3 baseline adjusted EBITDA margin of ~38%, below its historical 40–45% target range, due to two recent acquisitions (Tai, Extensiv) with lower initial margins and limited operating history. The quarter was a solid beat on revenue and profitability versus prior-year levels, but no explicit guidance raise was provided.

negative_highlights: GAAP operating income fell to $27.2 million from $30.1 million and net income declined to $13.1 million from $15.1 million due to a $7.8 million write-off of a Tastemakers vendor rebate receivable
Operating cash flow swung to a $1.7 million use versus $26.8 million generated prior year as working capital grew faster than revenue
SG&A increased 18% to $66 million, pressuring operating leverage despite gross margin expansion
positive_highlights: Q4 revenue grew 18% YoY to $268.1 million, with broad-based growth across music, home entertainment, collectibles, and fulfillment
Adjusted EBITDA rose 14% to $41.5 million and adjusted diluted EPS rose 24% to $0.46
Collectibles revenue grew 45% to $32 million and distribution/fulfillment fee revenue grew 26% to $18.6 million
summary: Alliance Entertainment reported FY2026 revenue up 8% to $1.15 billion, gross margin up 80 bps to 13.3%, adjusted EBITDA up 14% to $41.5 million, and adjusted diluted EPS up 24% to $0.46. However, GAAP operating income fell to $27.2 million from $30.1 million and net income declined to $13.1 million from $15.1 million, largely due to a $7.8 million non-cash write-off of a Tastemakers vendor rebate receivable. Operating cash flow swung to a $1.7 million use from $26.8 million generated, as working capital (inventory and receivables) grew faster than revenue, and SG&A rose 18% to $66 million. Management provided no formal guidance for FY2027, but described robust demand, full-year Amazon MGM contribution, collectibles growth, and a major GTA VI holiday release as drivers.

negative_highlights: Net new ARR fell 36-37% YoY, tied to freemium-first focus and deferred Creative Cloud pricing actions
RPO growth slowed to 8% YoY, the first single-digit increase since early fiscal 2023 and down sequentially
Full-year guidance increase from Q3 beat was partially offset by a Q4 FX headwind, limiting upside
positive_highlights: Total revenue rose 13% YoY to a record $6.76B, with non-GAAP EPS up 15% to $6.13
AI-first ending ARR exceeded $650M, growing more than 150% YoY; Firefly ending ARR grew 40% QoQ
Operating cash flow hit a Q3 record at $2.52B and the company raised full-year EPS and revenue targets
summary: Adobe reported Q3 FY2026 record revenue of $6.76B, up 13% YoY (12% constant currency), with GAAP EPS of $4.62 (up 11%) and non-GAAP EPS of $6.13 (up 15%). Total ending ARR grew 11.2% to $27.5B, but net new ARR declined 36-37% YoY and RPO grew only 8% YoY, the first single-digit RPO growth since early FY2023. Q4 revenue guidance of $6.8B-$6.85B is a modest sequential uptick, and full-year revenue and EPS targets were raised, partly offset by FX headwinds. Adobe also announced CEO succession (Anil Chakravarthy effective Dec 1) and an agreement to acquire Topaz Labs expected to close in Q4.

negative_highlights: Gross margin of 45.8% and operating margin of 22% remain below the 50% and 30% fiscal 2029 minimum targets
SG&A dollars increased $500,000 year-over-year even as the ratio fell to 18% of revenue from 26%
Production ramp is constrained, with CEO citing limits and a need to decline some customer-requested schedules
positive_highlights: Revenue of $23.5 million was an all-time record, up 70% year-over-year and 52% sequentially
Net income of $4.2 million or $0.41 per share versus $634,000 or $0.07 per share a year ago
Backlog reached a record $129 million, up 82% year-over-year and 16% sequentially, with book-to-bill of about 1.76 to 1
summary: FEIM reported record Q1 FY2027 revenue of $23.5 million, up 70% year-over-year and 52% sequentially, with net income of $4.2 million or $0.41 per share versus $634,000 or $0.07 a year earlier. Gross margin was 45.8% and operating margin 22%, versus 50% and 30% three-year minimum targets set in July, and backlog reached a record $129 million, up 82% year-over-year and 16% sequentially. Management said the quarter increases confidence in meeting or exceeding the $150 million-plus fiscal 2029 revenue target, possibly sooner and potentially a substantially larger number, and completed a roughly $73 million secondary offering to fund capacity expansion. Book-to-bill was approximately 1.76 to 1, with about 65% of backlog scheduled within 12 months.

negative_highlights: Net income fell 17.4% to $327.4 million and diluted EPS declined 14.6% to $0.35.
Gross margin contracted to 41.8% from prior year, with gross profit down 5.5%.
Global sold units declined 2.9%, with U.S. units down 5.7% and U.S. insurance units down 7.5%.
positive_highlights: International revenue grew 11.7% to $222.1 million with units up 10% and insurance units up 11.2%.
Global revenue per unit increased 5.4% in the quarter, with ASPs up 3.5% globally.
U.S. non-insurance volume returned to modest growth in the quarter, up 0.2%, with dealer units up 5.8% and Blue Car up nearly 20%.
summary: Copart reported Q4 FY2026 revenue of $1.2 billion, up 2.4% year-over-year, but net income fell 17.4% to $327.4 million, or $0.35 per diluted share, down 14.6%. Gross margin contracted to 41.8% as gross profit declined 5.5%, and global sold units fell 2.9% with U.S. units down 5.7% and U.S. insurance units down 7.5%. International was a bright spot, with revenue up 11.7% and units up 10%. Separately, Copart announced an all-cash acquisition of ACV, expected to close by the end of the calendar year and be accretive in FY2028. Management did not provide specific earnings or margin guidance, and noted plans to reduce operating cost per car after a 12.7% increase.

negative_highlights: Revenue grew only 0.4% to $161.2 million with omni-channel comps down 1.9%; Sactionals fell 1.7%, Sacs fell 8.6%, and internet sales fell 5.3%
Adjusted EBITDA, excluding the tariff refund, was a $1.3 million loss versus $0.8 million income a year earlier, and full-year guidance was reduced (EBITDA cut ~$7 million at the midpoint)

Q3/full-year outlook lowered on delayed innovation timing (Sactionals onshoring innovation and large-format Sactionals now landing at end of Q3) and the under-$6,000 segment has not returned to growth
positive_highlights: Gross margin expanded 1,200 bps to 68.4% (56.4% prior year), including a $20 million IEEPA tariff refund recognized in COGS; underlying product margin improved ~250 bps from pricing and cost initiatives
Premium $6,000+ configurations grew double digits on larger configurations and premium fabrics, with record reclining seat attachment and showroom conversion up double digits
Balance sheet remains strong: $68.8 million cash, no debt, $34 million revolver capacity, and operating cash use narrowed to $11.4 million from $29.2 million a year ago
summary: Net sales rose only 0.4% to $161.2 million with omni-channel comps down 1.9%, though gross margin jumped 1,200 bps to 68.4% and EPS swung to $0.51 from -$0.45, both driven largely by a $21 million IEEPA tariff refund ($0.86 per share benefit). Adjusted EBITDA, excluding the refund, was a $1.3 million loss versus $0.8 million income a year earlier. Management lowered its Q3 and full-year outlook, citing later-than-planned timing of major new product launches and a mid-event Labor Day read, and said its pricing/promotional changes have not yet returned the under-$6,000 segment to growth.

negative_highlights: Underlying gross margin (excluding tariff refunds and ongoing tariff/fuel impacts) expanded only ~10 bps
Second-half sales expectations held in line with prior outlook despite the Q2 beat and Q3 comps guided to -0.5% to +0.5%
Softer categories cited: plus sizes, intimates, women's sleepwear, and big-ticket still down versus prior year
positive_highlights: Adjusted EPS of $0.63 vs $0.35 prior year; ex-tariff refunds, adjusted EPS was up 14% and above the high end of guidance
Gross margin expanded to 41.5% from 39.7% and adjusted EBITDA rose to $457M (9.0% of revenue) from $373M (7.5%)
Bloomingdale's comps +11.3% (highest Q2 sales volume in its 154-year history) and Bluemercury comps +6.2%, both on top of prior growth
summary: Q2 net sales rose 1.1% to $4.9B and total revenue rose 1.2% to $5.1B, with comps up 2.7% (go-forward +2.8%); adjusted EPS of $0.63 (including a ~$0.23 net tariff refund benefit) compared to $0.35 last year, and adjusted EPS ex-refunds was up 14% and above the high end of guidance. Gross margin expanded to 41.5% from 39.7%, though underlying gross margin was up only ~10 bps, and adjusted EBITDA rose to $457M (9.0% of revenue) from $373M (7.5%). Full-year guidance was raised to net sales of $21.675-21.825B and adjusted EPS of $2.15-$2.35 (from the prior $1.90-$2.10 start to the year), with Q3 comps guided to -0.5% to +0.5% and an adjusted EPS loss of $0.19-$0.23. Second-half sales expectations were kept in line with the prior outlook despite the Q2 beat, with tariff/fuel headwind guidance improved to 5-15 bps from 20-30 bps.

negative_highlights: $50M of unplanned supply chain cost increases due to oil price spike ($109 vs $63 at war's outset) offsetting tariff refunds
International drag ~340 bps for 2026; housing market now in roughly its fifth straight down year per management
Q3 guide implies 5%-6% growth with 2.5 points of backlog reduction still a headwind
positive_highlights: $922.2M revenue beat high end of guidance, up 2.6% YoY and 4.2 points acceleration vs Q1
13.4% normalized adjusted EBITDA margin beat high end of guidance
Raised FY26 outlook to 5.5%-7% revenue growth and 15%-16.2% adjusted EBITDA margin, implying 16.1%-21.2% Q4 revenue growth
summary: RH reported Q2 GAAP net revenues of $922.2 million, above the high end of guidance and up 2.6% YoY (~4.2 points acceleration over Q1). Adjusted EBITDA margin of 13.4% also exceeded the high end of guidance, with $72.3 million of cash generated and a $55.1 million tariff benefit recognized. Management raised the FY2026 outlook to 5.5%-7% revenue growth and a 15%-16.2% adjusted EBITDA margin, with a significant Q4 revenue guide of 16.1%-21.2% tied to the November launch of the RH Estates collection. The offset is a noted ~$50 million of unplanned supply chain cost increases from the oil spike, mitigated by an additional $13.9 million tariff benefit, and a still-murky housing/Europe macro backdrop.

negative_highlights: GAAP loss from continuing operations of $7 million, or $0.35 per diluted share, versus $5.5 million income ($0.33) a year ago, including a $10.1 million non-cash Crest intangible impairment

Consolidated Q4 gross margin declined 60 basis points year-over-year on purchase accounting, and the Recreation and Sport Fishing segment contributed only $1.8 million adjusted EBITDA on $33.3 million revenue (5.5% adjusted EBITDA margin)

Chaparral/Robalo production moderated to hold shipments and ASPs near Q4 exit rates, Chaparral Surf Series production temporarily paused, and retail demand assumed down 5%-10% over the next six months
positive_highlights: Legacy Q4 adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 730 basis points to 19.3% from 12.0%, with legacy adjusted EBITDA up 95.6% to $18.6 million
Legacy gross margin expanded roughly 690 basis points to 30% in Q4 and 520 basis points to 25.2% for the full year on X Series mix, pricing and lower discounts
MasterCraft retail finished up low single digits versus an initial expectation of a 5%-10% category decline, and legacy field inventory ended the year down roughly 30% year-over-year
summary: Legacy Q4 net sales rose 21.5% to $96.6 million with legacy adjusted EBITDA up 95.6% to $18.6 million and legacy gross margin expanding about 690 bps to 30%; including a six-week contribution from the acquired Chaparral and Robalo brands, consolidated net sales were $129.9 million (up 63.4%) and adjusted EBITDA $20.5 million (up 114.9%). Full-year legacy net sales were $315.6 million (up 11%) with adjusted EBITDA of $43.8 million (up 79.6%), above the increased guidance given last quarter. GAAP results swung to a $7 million loss ($0.35 per diluted share) on a $10.1 million non-cash Crest intangible impairment, acquisition purchase accounting and transaction costs. Guidance for the six-month July-December 2026 transition period is net sales of $287-291 million, adjusted EBITDA of $29-32 million and adjusted EPS of $0.66-0.76, with retail demand assumed down 5%-10% and Chaparral/Robalo production held near Q4 exit rates after a temporary pause of the Chaparral Surf Series.

negative_highlights: Full-year identical sales without fuel guidance was lowered to 0.2%-0.8% from the prior 1%-2% range.
Identical sales without fuel decelerated to 0.2%, with a 265 basis point drag from IRA/GLP-1 pharmacy changes, brand-to-generic shift, Cyclospora, and egg deflation.
Q4 faces anticipated incremental headwinds from lapping third-party delivery partnerships and prior-year weather benefits, with ID sales expected slightly better in Q3 than Q4.
positive_highlights: FIFO gross margin rate increased 13 basis points versus Q2 last year, supported by e-commerce profitability, media, pharmacy mix, tariff refunds, and sourcing initiatives.
Adjusted EPS grew 5% to $1.09, with adjusted FIFO operating profit of $1.1 billion despite a 0.2% identical sales without fuel result.
Adjusted e-commerce sales grew 20% and retail media grew 24%, marking the best media performance since 2021 and a second consecutive quarter of profitable e-commerce growth.
summary: Kroger reported Q2 identical sales without fuel of just 0.2% and adjusted EPS of $1.09 (up 5% YoY), with a 265 bp sales drag from IRA/GLP-1 pharmacy changes (~140 bp), brand-to-generic shift (~60 bp), Cyclospora (~35 bp), and egg deflation (~30 bp). FIFO gross margin expanded 13 bp despite the soft top line, aided by e-commerce profitability, retail media (up 24%), pharmacy mix, tariff refunds, and sourcing, partly offset by higher shrink and transportation costs. Management lowered full-year identical sales without fuel guidance to 0.2%-0.8% from 1%-2% but maintained adjusted FIFO operating profit guidance of $5.0-$5.2B and adjusted EPS of $5.10-$5.30, citing cost savings and share repurchases. Adjusted FIFO operating profit was $1.1B and net debt to adjusted EBITDA stood at 1.91x.

negative_highlights: GAAP operating loss widened to RMB 73.6 million from RMB 11.1 million a year earlier, and non-GAAP operating loss widened to RMB 25.6 million from RMB 2.1 million
Advertising agency services revenue fell 70.0% year-over-year and 15.0% quarter-over-quarter to RMB 22.0 million due to review-policy changes at a major global advertising platform
Robotics and others adjusted operating loss widened sequentially to RMB 34.0 million from RMB 26.9 million in Q1 despite narrowing 35.5% year-over-year
positive_highlights: Cloud and AI infrastructure revenue grew 83% year-over-year and 26% quarter-over-quarter to RMB 59 million, with gross billings exceeding RMB 500 million versus about RMB 200 million a year earlier
Internet services adjusted operating margin expanded to 19.4% from 14.1% in Q2 FY2025 and 11.3% in Q1, with adjusted operating profit up 14.2% year-over-year to RMB 25.4 million
Robotics and others revenue rose 72.5% year-over-year to RMB 54.5 million (20.5% of total) and smart mobility began contributing revenue via Pride Mobility in Europe and Sweetrich in China
summary: Q2 FY2026 revenue was RMB 266.1 million, up 9.9% year-over-year and 2.7% quarter-over-quarter, but total GAAP operating loss widened to RMB 73.6 million from RMB 11.1 million a year earlier (non-GAAP operating loss RMB 25.6 million vs RMB 2.1 million). Advertising agency services revenue fell 70.0% year-over-year to RMB 22.0 million on changed review policies at a major global ad platform, while cloud and AI infrastructure revenue rose 83.1% year-over-year to RMB 59.1 million and robotics and others rose 72.5% to RMB 54.5 million. Management guided to 2026 cloud/AI-infrastructure gross billings above RMB 2 billion (+>100% YoY) and related revenue above RMB 200 million (+>50% YoY), and did not provide formal total-company profit guidance. Internet services adjusted operating margin expanded to 19.4% from 14.1% a year ago.

negative_highlights: Ending active subscribers declined 3.8% year-over-year to 140,826, and management expects active subscribers roughly flat in the back half of 2026

Q3 revenue guidance of $87-$90 million implies flat to 3% growth as the company laps the August 2025 subscription price increase, and Q3 adjusted EBITDA is guided to negative 3% to negative 6% of revenue

Rental product investment guidance was raised to $53-$55 million from $45-$50 million, and the company announced a $15 million backstopped rights offering plus a $10 million term loan to bolster liquidity
positive_highlights: Gross margin expanded 609 bps to 36.1% from 30%, driven by a 240 bps reduction in rental product depreciation/revenue share and 370 bps lower fulfillment costs as a percentage of revenue
Adjusted EBITDA rose to $12.6 million, or 12.9% of revenue, from $3.6 million, or 4.4% of revenue, a year ago
Total operating expenses fell to 42% of revenue from 51.7%, and year-to-date free cash flow improved to negative $21.6 million from negative $32.9 million
summary: Rent the Runway reported Q2 FY2026 record net revenue of $97.7 million, up 20.8% year-over-year and 8.7% sequentially, ahead of the range guided in June. Gross margin expanded 609 bps to 36.1% and adjusted EBITDA reached $12.6 million (12.9% of revenue) versus $3.6 million (4.4%) last year, with opex down 2% and 1,000 bps of leverage. Full-year revenue growth (double digit) and adjusted EBITDA (4%-7% of revenue) guidance were reiterated, but Q3 revenue guidance of $87-$90 million implies flat to 3% growth and Q3 adjusted EBITDA is guided to negative 3% to negative 6% of revenue. Ending active subscribers fell 3.8% year-over-year to 140,826 on higher pause rates, rental product investment guidance rose to $53-$55 million from $45-$50 million, and a $15 million backstopped rights offering plus a $10 million term loan were announced alongside a CEO transition to Paige Thomas.

negative_highlights: H1 GAAP revenue fell to $51.4 million from $80 million, and segment EBITDA dropped to $21.6 million from $59 million as operating leverage amplified the AUM decline
Swung from a $75.9 million operating gain to a $5.1 million operating loss, driven by a $34.7 million unfavorable XBT Pricing Differential swing and a $6.1 million share-based compensation charge

Blended asset management fee yield declined to 128 basis points from 156 bps in 2025, with ~25 bps of the decline from increased Block weight and 7 bps from product mix, though only ~4 bps from actual product-level fee rate changes
positive_highlights: Positive net flows of ~$28 million in H1 2026 while peers saw over $7 billion of net outflows (~6% of combined opening assets), with the European physical platform attracting ~$156 million of net inflows
Post-period AUM recovered ~25% to ~$6.9 billion by August 31 from $5.5 billion at June 30, alongside ~$74 million of positive net flows and a reversal of the majority of the treasury loss
summary: CoinShares reported H1 2026 GAAP revenue of $51.4 million, down from $80 million a year earlier, as AUM fell to $5.5 billion from $7.4 billion at December 2025 under a sharp digital asset drawdown (Bitcoin ~-32%, Ethereum ~-48%). Segment EBITDA fell to $21.6 million ($26.5 million adjusted for ~$4.9 million of non-recurring listing/US GAAP costs) versus $59 million a year ago, and the period swung to a $5.1 million operating loss, driven by a $34.7 million unfavorable XBT Pricing Differential swing. Flows were positive at ~$28 million, with CoinShares Physical drawing ~$156 million of net inflows, and AUM had recovered to ~$6.9 billion by August 31, aided by ~$74 million of net inflows post-period. The board is seeking shareholder approval at the AGM for a multi-year buyback authority of up to 25% of shares outstanding (32.9 million shares); no forward financial guidance was given.

negative_highlights: Full-year adjusted EBITDA declined 5.4% to $36.684 million and adjusted net income fell 18.4% to $25.253 million
No explicit FY2027 guidance provided; management declined to quantify revenue growth and warned not to straight-line the 19% Q4 rate
Q4 airfreight strength was aided by non-recurring typhoon disaster relief work, with ocean freight rates characterized as only beginning to stabilize
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA rose 31.6% to $10.362 million and adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 240 basis points YoY in Q4 FY2026
Q4 revenue grew 18.5% to $261.4 million with net income up 53.1% to $7.517 million, and organic growth was approximately 8%
Completed amended $200 million credit facility extending maturity to 2031 with $100 million expanded acquisition capacity, entering FY2027 with no net debt
summary: Radiant reported Q4 FY2026 revenue of $261.4 million, up 18.5% YoY, with net income of $7.517 million or $0.15 diluted (up 53.1%), adjusted net income up 34.5%, and adjusted EBITDA of $10.362 million, up 31.6% with adjusted EBITDA margin expanding 240 basis points. Full-year FY2026 revenue was $934.4 million but adjusted EBITDA fell 5.4% to $36.684 million and adjusted net income dropped 18.4% to $25.253 million. No formal FY2027 numeric guidance was issued; management said organic growth was about 8% in Q4 and described improving domestic truckload/intermodal trends (only one month reflected in results) plus a new independent agent program at Radiant Road & Rail launching in Q1 FY2027. The quarter's airfreight strength was partly attributed to disaster relief work following Western Pacific typhoons, and the balance sheet carries no net debt after an amended $200 million credit facility extended to 2031.

negative_highlights: Book-to-bill of 0.94x indicates bookings of $22.5 million trailed revenue in the quarter
Small cell revenue dollars remain behind original full-year expectations despite the Q3 pickup
Wireless carrier CapEx projected largely flat, with no material contribution expected this fiscal year from NEMA 4/edge data center opportunities
positive_highlights: Record quarterly revenue of $24.0 million, up 21% year-over-year and 16% sequentially
Gross margin expanded 160 bps to 35.6% and operating income more than doubled to $1.8 million from $720,000
summary: RF Industries reported record Q3 FY2026 revenue of $24.0 million, up 21% year-over-year and 16% sequentially, with GAAP net income of $1.4 million ($0.12 diluted EPS) and non-GAAP net income of $2.2 million ($0.19 diluted EPS) versus $0.04 GAAP and $0.10 non-GAAP a year ago. Gross margin expanded 160 bps to 35.6%, operating income rose to $1.8 million (7.3% margin) from $720,000, and adjusted EBITDA grew 71% to $2.7 million (11.1% of sales), above the 10% long-term target. Management guided Q4 sales to be roughly the same or above Q3, and Q3 bookings of $22.5 million produced a 0.94 book-to-bill with backlog of $18.6 million at quarter-end, rising to $19.8 million as of the call. The quarter's key change was broad-based contribution across custom cabling, interconnect, and integrated systems, with the small cell business beginning to accelerate as anticipated.

negative_highlights: Total organic net sales declined 2% year-over-year as International fell 4% and volume/mix subtracted two percentage points with flat price
Adjusted net loss widened to $4 million, or $0.05 per diluted share, from $2 million, or $0.02, and Q4 adjusted EBITDA declined to $19 million from $20 million
International adjusted gross margin contracted 555 bps to 16.6% and International adjusted EBITDA fell 41% to $12 million
positive_highlights: North America organic net sales returned to growth at 2% year-over-year and adjusted EBITDA rose 55% to $16 million
Full-year free cash flow improved to $58 million from an outflow of $3 million, and net debt was reduced by $151 million (about 25%)
Zero-based budgeting review identified more than $16 million in annual run-rate cost savings, with 70% of the related $20 million implementation cost expected in fiscal 2027
summary: Hain reported Q4 FY2026 organic net sales decline of 2% year-over-year, with North America returning to 2% growth offset by a 4% decline in International. Adjusted gross margin rose 230 bps to 22.7%, adjusted EBITDA fell to $19 million (7.1% margin, up 160 bps), and adjusted net loss widened to $0.05 per diluted share from $0.02. The company announced the sale of its international business to Aurelius for $323 million in cash and provided no traditional fiscal 2027 guidance, citing pending lender amendment discussions and strategic review; it expects pro forma gross margin of 30%+ and low double-digit adjusted EBITDA margin post-close.

negative_highlights: A U.S. Department of Commerce directive effectively bans export of black mass; the company is storing the product pending an unresolved exception request.
No formal response yet from Commerce on ABTC's exception request, creating uncertainty around a key recycling byproduct sales channel.
One DOE grant was canceled and later reinstated after appeal, along with ongoing NEPA permitting risk for the Tonopah lithium project.
positive_highlights: Revenue rose over 400% to $21.7 million in FY2026 versus fiscal 2025.
Adjusted gross profit reached approximately $1.7 million, compared to a $6.2 million loss in the prior year.
summary: American Battery Technology Company reported FY2026 revenue of $21.7 million, up over 400% year-over-year, with cost of goods sold rising only about 67%, producing a first-ever adjusted gross profit of approximately $1.7 million versus a $6.2 million loss the prior year. The company ended the year with $49.5 million in cash, total assets of about $133 million, and no outstanding long-term debt. Management cited operational efficiencies, improved pricing, and grid-scale battery storage demand, while noting that a U.S. Department of Commerce directive banning black mass exports has left that product stored on-site pending an unresolved exception request. Formal annual guidance figures were not provided in the transcript.

negative_highlights: GAAP net loss widened to $44.1 million from $25.8 million a year earlier; adjusted EBITDA loss widened to $24 million from $19.4 million.
Q1 operating cash burn was $32.3 million, with management expecting burn to decline only sequentially through FY2027.
GAAP operating expenses rose to $55.2 million from $37.7 million, driven by commercial expansion and a roughly 70% increase in R&D spend tied to a late-stage program management would not yet detail.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 60% YoY to $31 million (management cited 60% off a favorable comp versus the prior-year ~19% figure reported to the prior paragraph's $31M/16% base), with FY2027 guidance raised to $141 million from $137 million.

In-network mix rose to the low 80s from ~70% at IPO, and a significant national payer newly expanded coverage to non-ischemic patients, a population management says is over 60% of the typical WCD base.
summary: Kestra Medical reported Q1 FY2027 revenue of $31 million, up 16% YoY (60% growth off a favorable comp, per CFO), with gross margin up over 10 points YoY to 56.5% and 175 bps sequentially, the 11th consecutive quarter of sequential margin expansion. Management raised FY2027 revenue guidance to $141 million (48% growth) from a prior $137 million, and lifted its long-term gross margin target to the mid-70% range from 70%. GAAP net loss widened to $44.1 million from $25.8 million, and adjusted EBITDA loss widened to $24 million from $19.4 million a year earlier, on higher commercial and late-stage R&D investment. Q1 cash burn was $32.3 million, with $245 million in cash and investments plus roughly $320 million total liquidity after a new $200 million term loan.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA fell to $98.9M (18.2% margin) from $129.7M (23.3% margin), a decline of about $31M year-over-year, and the company swung to a GAAP net loss of $12.5M from prior-year net income of $11.4M

Entertainment/amusement same-store sales have declined for about eight quarters with weakness accelerating over the last four to five quarters according to an analyst, and no specific turnaround metric was provided

No quantitative revenue, EBITDA, or EPS guidance was given; management said it 'can't comment' on how quarter-to-date trends extend, and net CapEx is projected to fall to $150M or less in FY2027 with new store openings cut from 11 this year to five next year
positive_highlights: Same-store sales improved 250 basis points sequentially to down 2.9% in Q2 from down 5.4% in Q1, with July total company comps down 1.6% and further improvement over the first five weeks of Q3
Food and beverage comparable sales grew 7.6% in Q2, marking five consecutive positive quarters, and special events grew for a seventh consecutive quarter

Adjusted free cash flow turned positive at $19.5M through Q2 FY26 versus negative $36.5M in the prior-year period, a roughly $56M year-over-year improvement, and $15M of cost savings were identified with a target to at least double that
summary: Dave & Buster's reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $544.1M (down from $557.4M) and a GAAP net loss of $12.5M, or $0.36 per diluted share, versus prior-year net income of $11.4M, or $0.32 per share. Adjusted EBITDA fell to $98.9M (18.2% margin) from $129.7M (23.3% margin), with same-store sales down 2.9% though improving sequentially from down 5.4% in Q1 and down 1.6% in July. Management declined to provide explicit quantitative guidance, saying only it expects same-store sales, revenue and EBITDA to grow in the near term; the only firm forward figures were net CapEx under $200M for FY2026 and potentially $150M or less in FY2027, along with at least $15M in identified cost savings targeted to double. The key change versus the prior quarter is the sequential comp improvement and positive F&B (up 7.6%, fifth straight quarter of growth) offset by a wider EBITDA decline and a swing to a net loss.

negative_highlights: Operating loss widened to $32.2 million from $21.2 million a year earlier, and net loss widened to $27.8 million from $20 million
G&A expenses nearly doubled to $23.1 million from $13.8 million, including about $3 million of additional G&A and $1.3 million of amortization from the IC'Alps, Miraex and Wecan acquisitions
EBITDA loss increased to $29.5 million from $20.9 million, and R&D rose to $8.7 million from $4.7 million with management expecting continued heavy investment
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 131% to $11.2 million in H1 2026 from $4.8 million in H1 2025
Gross margin expanded to approximately 48%, with gross profit up 233% to $5.4 million, aided by higher-margin ASIC design and engineering services
VaultIC408 secure element achieved FIPS 140-3 validation (NIST certificate number 5463) and QS7001 achieved NIST SP 800-90B entropy validation (ESV Certificate E333)
summary: First half 2026 revenue rose 131% to $11.2 million from $4.8 million, driven by VaultIC demand, PKI/digital identity expansion, initial Quantix Edge revenue and roughly $2.5 million from six months of IC'Alps consolidation; gross profit rose 233% to $5.4 million with gross margin expanding to approximately 48%. However, operating loss widened to $32.2 million from $21.2 million, net loss widened to $27.8 million from $20 million, and EBITDA loss grew to $29.5 million from $20.9 million, reflecting R&D of $8.7 million (versus $4.7 million) and G&A of $23.1 million (versus $13.8 million). Management reaffirmed (did not raise) full-year 2026 revenue guidance of $27 million-$36 million, about 50%-100% growth over 2025's $18.3 million, and reported a $225 million active pipeline with more than $100 million in post-quantum opportunities, though the pipeline was characterized as a management estimate rather than guidance. Liquidity was roughly $486 million in cash, equivalents and restricted cash at June 30, 2026.

negative_highlights: Consolidated same-store sales were flat year-over-year for the full quarter, with transaction growth of 1.1% offset by thinner baskets and wholesale price compression
Canadian store count in key markets like Ontario and Alberta rose 5% over the past 12 months, reversing prior flattening/retrenchment trends and increasing competitive pressure

Management noted potential difficulty ramping German market share as quickly as previously thought due to rapid market growth, and flagged macroeconomic uncertainty and inflationary pressure on consumers
positive_highlights: Revenue rose 33% year-over-year to a record CAD 198.8 million, the fastest growth in 13 quarters
Adjusted EBITDA grew 52% year-over-year to a record CAD 16.2 million with margin at a 12-quarter high of 8.2%
