Remexian sold 10.2 tons of medical cannabis in Germany, up 35% sequentially, with adjusted EBITDA up 38% sequentially to CAD 4.4 million
summary: High Tide reported Q3 FY2026 record revenue of CAD 198.8 million, up 33% year-over-year (fastest growth in 13 quarters) and 11% sequentially, with record adjusted EBITDA of CAD 16.2 million (up 52% YoY), record operating income of CAD 8.7 million (up 133% YoY), and record net income of CAD 12.7 million (adjusted net income CAD 2.2 million, up 157% YoY). Gross margin held at 27% consolidated, and salaries/wages (11.4% of revenue) and G&A (3.9% of revenue) hit multi-quarter lows. Remexian sold 10.2 tons in Germany, up 35% sequentially, generating CAD 38.2 million revenue and 12% adjusted EBITDA margin. Guidance was issued one business day after quarter-end with the low end exceeding the most aggressive analyst estimates, and results came in near the high end; no formal raised guidance was quantified for the forward quarter, though management reiterated confidence in reaching a CAD 1 billion revenue run rate and noted same-store sales turned positive in June and July.

negative_highlights: Indirect segment revenue fell 39% YoY to $6.3 million due to marketplace strategy shifts and reduced liquidation sales.
SG&A rose to $38.7 million, or 54% of net revenue, from $36.3 million, driven by higher variable compensation and lapping prior-year stock forfeitures.
Total revenue growth slowed to 1.1% from nearly 8% in Q1, and 14 fewer stores reduced total growth by about 100 bps.
positive_highlights: Direct segment revenue rose 8% YoY to $65.4 million, the fifth consecutive quarter of sequential improvement, with comparable sales up 9.2%.
Gross margin expanded to 59.8% from 49.9%, including $8 million in tariff refunds; underlying gross margin improved more than 40 bps.
Inventory declined 28.4% YoY to $69.3 million and the company ended with $34.2 million in cash, double last year, and no debt.
summary: Vera Bradley reported Q2 FY2027 revenue of $71.6 million, up 1.1% YoY, with Direct segment revenue up 8% to $65.4 million and comps up 9.2%, while Indirect revenue fell 39% to $6.3 million on strategic marketplace shifts and reduced liquidation. Gross margin expanded to 59.8% from 49.9%, though roughly 980 bps of the increase came from $8 million in tariff refunds; underlying gross margin improved more than 40 bps. Net income swung to $3.3 million, or $0.11 per diluted share, from a $0.5 million loss, and inventory fell 28.4% YoY. Management reiterated full-year guidance for sales of $255-$270 million and at least 50% operating profit improvement, with the Direct business momentum and margin discipline offsetting Indirect weakness.

negative_highlights: Net loss attributable to ordinary shareholders was $3.1 million with GAAP EPS of negative $0.51 per ADS
Sales and marketing expenses rose 48.8% to $19.3 million and product development expenses rose 96.6% to $2.4 million, outpacing revenue-driven margin improvement
Q3 FY2026 gross billings guidance of $41-43 million implies sequential growth deceleration from the Q2 level, with management referencing a tougher comparison to an exceptionally strong Q3 2025
positive_highlights: Gross billings of $39.3 million, up 38.1% YoY, exceeded the high end of the June guidance
Net revenues rose 58.8% YoY to $32.4 million, with gross margin at 73.9%
Operating loss narrowed to $2.1 million from $3.2 million in the prior-year quarter, and Q2 net operating cash inflow was $4.9 million
summary: 51Talk reported Q2 FY2026 gross billings of $39.3 million, up 38.1% YoY and above the high end of June guidance, with net revenues of $32.4 million up 58.8% YoY and gross margin of 73.9%. Operating loss narrowed to $2.1 million from $3.2 million, and net loss attributable to ordinary shareholders was $3.1 million, or GAAP EPS of negative $0.51 and non-GAAP negative $0.43 per ADS. Q3 FY2026 gross billings guidance is $41-43 million, and management described prioritizing more efficient investment toward profitability while noting the prior exceptionally strong Q3 2025 base. Sales and marketing expense rose 48.8% to $19.3 million and product development rose 96.6% to $2.4 million, offsetting much of the top-line improvement.

negative_highlights: Standard products revenue grew only 3% year over year to $11 million, a laggard versus other segments
Industrial and other revenue grew just 11% and customer count declined as the company high-graded its mix
Guidance incorporates early-year under-absorption and startup costs from the new Tijuana Powertrain Solutions facility, which comes online in Q4 FY2027
positive_highlights: Q4 revenue of $462 million grew 94% year over year, and each KPI exceeded the high end of guidance that was raised in May
Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 640 basis points year over year and 200 basis points sequentially to 24.4%, the second consecutive quarter of 200 bps sequential expansion
Backlog reached a record $3 billion, up 256% year over year, with Q4 bookings of $1.5 billion and a record 3.3x book-to-bill; FY2027 guidance implies 76% revenue growth
summary: Forgent Power Solutions reported Q4 FY2026 revenue of $462 million, up 94% year over year and 22% sequentially, with adjusted EBITDA of $113 million (up 163%) and adjusted EBITDA margin of 24.4%, up 200 basis points sequentially and 640 basis points year over year. Full-year revenue rose 89% to $1.42 billion and adjusted EBITDA rose 91% to $323 million, exceeding both the IPO forecast and the guidance raised in May. Management issued FY2027 guidance for revenue of $2.4–2.6 billion (76% growth at the midpoint), adjusted EBITDA of $575–625 million, and adjusted EPS of $1.26–1.40. Q4 bookings reached a record $1.5 billion and backlog grew to $3 billion, up 256% year over year, with Powertrain Solutions representing approximately 40% of backlog.

negative_highlights: Total net revenue growth slowed to 6% year-over-year, and transportation ticketing revenue declined 1% to RMB 5.4 billion.
Adjusted EBITDA decreased to RMB 4.6 billion from RMB 4.9 billion in the prior-year period.
The SAMR anti-monopoly decision resulted in a one-time RMB 5.18 billion expense and RMB 122 million contra-revenue, and management expects near-term domestic operational volatility.
positive_highlights: International OTA platform revenue increased over 50% year-over-year, with inbound travel revenue up high double digits.
Accommodation reservation revenue rose 6% year-over-year to RMB 6.6 billion, or 8% excluding the SAMR contra-revenue item.
AI-assisted orders through TripGenie increased approximately 400% year-over-year, with nearly 60% of interactions booking-related.
summary: Trip.com reported Q2 FY2026 total net revenue of RMB 15.7 billion, up 6% year-over-year, with accommodation revenue up 6% to RMB 6.6 billion (8% ex-contra-revenue item) and transportation ticketing revenue down 1% to RMB 5.4 billion on softer demand, elevated fuel prices, and compliance-related operational adjustments. Adjusted EBITDA fell to RMB 4.6 billion from RMB 4.9 billion a year earlier, while non-GAAP diluted EPS rose to RMB 7.27 from RMB 7.20. The quarter included a one-time RMB 5.18 billion expense and RMB 122 million contra-revenue related to the SAMR anti-monopoly penalty, and management guided to near-term volatility in domestic performance as partners transition to a new operating model. International OTA revenue grew over 50% year-over-year, with inbound travel up high double digits, but no explicit quantitative guidance for Q3 was provided.

negative_highlights: FY2027 adjusted EBITDA margin guidance of 2%-3% remains modest relative to the 7%-9% medium-term target
YOOX adjusted EBITDA margin remained negative at -10.5% in Q4, with FY2027 guidance still mid-single-digit negative
Greater China demand was disappointing over the summer, and France/Germany domestic luxury demand remained sluggish
positive_highlights: Q4 group net sales grew +7.6%, the strongest quarter of FY2026, with adjusted EBITDA margin of +2.1%
Mytheresa net sales +10.2% in Q4 with adjusted EBITDA margin up 20 bps to 6.6% and gross margin up 150 bps to 49.7%
NAP/MRP achieved its first positive adjusted EBITDA (2.7% margin, up 230 bps YoY) and Q4 net sales +5.6%
summary: LuxExperience delivered on FY2026 guidance with GMV growth of +2.9% constant currency and a positive group-adjusted EBITDA margin of +0.4%. Q4 net sales grew +7.6% (the strongest quarter of the year) with a +2.1% adjusted EBITDA margin, the third consecutive positive quarter; all three segments grew, with Mytheresa +10.2% and a 6.6% adjusted EBITDA margin, NAP/MRP +5.6% and its first positive adjusted EBITDA at 2.7%, and YOOX +6.6% with losses nearly halved to -10.5%. FY2027 guidance is for mid-to-high single-digit group net sales growth and a 2%-3% adjusted EBITDA margin, with segment-level indications and a stated path to 7%-9% medium-term. Management also noted a EUR 442 million cash balance, no bank debt, an ADS buyback authorization, and an expected EUR 150-250 million remaining transformation cash burn.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA declined to $6.5 million from $8.6 million in the prior-year quarter, and the company posted an adjusted net loss of $0.6 million versus adjusted net income of $1.1 million a year ago
Q4 production fell 4% YoY to 6,901 BOE per day, and full-year operating cash flow dropped to $23.6 million from $33.1 million in fiscal 2025

Total liquidity of roughly $19 million as of August 20 includes a borrowing base temporarily raised from $65 million to $73 million that is only effective through October 20, with redetermination on or about October 1
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA more than doubled sequentially to $6.5 million from $3.1 million, driven by a 20% sequential revenue increase to $24.2 million
Fiscal Q4 SCOOP/STACK production averaged 1,275 BOEPD, up ~14% YoY, while per-unit lease operating costs fell to $10.33 per BOE from $11.05
Realized oil price before hedge settlements rose 49% YoY to $90.74 per barrel and NGLs realized $32.49 per barrel, up 27%
summary: Evolution Petroleum reported Q4 FY2026 revenue of $24.2 million (up 20% sequentially, 15% YoY), net income of $4.6 million or $0.13 per diluted share, and adjusted EBITDA of $6.5 million that more than doubled from $3.1 million in fiscal Q3 but declined from $8.6 million a year ago. Production averaged 6,901 BOE per day, up 3% sequentially but down 4% year-over-year, with adjusted net loss narrowing to $0.6 million from $2.9 million sequentially while remaining below the prior-year adjusted net income of $1.1 million. Full-year production was essentially flat at 7,077 BOE per day versus 7,074, proved reserves were roughly unchanged at 27.2 million barrels of oil equivalent, and the board maintained the quarterly dividend at $0.12 per share for a 52nd consecutive payment. Management gave no production or LOE guidance and set fiscal 2027 CapEx at $4 million-$6 million, excluding potential Chaveroo drilling, while highlighting a post-quarter ~$16 million Permian Midland mineral acquisition adding ~3,420 net royalty acres and over 200 BOE per day.

negative_highlights: FY2026 revenue of $4.5 million was roughly flat versus $4.7 million in FY2025, with Q4 revenue of only $582,000.
FY adjusted EBITDA turned negative $5.2 million from positive $186,000 in FY2025; full-year net loss widened to $9.2 million from $3.0 million.
No formal FY2027 revenue guidance; only ~$2.3 million of booked government revenue disclosed against $10-$12 million planned capex.
positive_highlights: Signed letter of intent with the Department of Commerce CHIPS R&D office for up to $30 million to accelerate photonics commercialization.
New agreement with Sumitomo Chemical Advanced Technologies to increase wafer production capacity, plus procurement of AIXTRON G10-AsP MOCVD systems.
Headcount grew from 14 employees at June 30, 2025 to more than 30, with key hires including VP of Engineering Dr. Brendan Moran.
summary: Q4 revenue was $582,000, bringing FY2026 total to $4.5 million, near the high end of the prior range but roughly flat versus $4.7 million in FY2025. GAAP net loss widened to $4.0 million ($0.22/share) in Q4 and $9.2 million ($0.52/share) for the year, with FY adjusted EBITDA swinging to negative $5.2 million from positive $186,000 in FY2025. Management did not provide formal FY2027 revenue guidance, citing a handful of contracts that could swing the range, but disclosed ~$2.3 million of booked government revenue plus potential for ~$2 million more, and guided FY2027 capex to $10-$12 million for two MOCVD reactors. The main change is a strategic pivot from government R&D revenue toward commercial AI datacom NRE programs, alongside a CHIPS R&D letter of intent for up to $30 million likely to be structured as an equity investment rather than revenue.

negative_highlights: No financial results beyond the balance sheet were disclosed in this business update; no revenue, EPS, or margin figures were reported.
NSCLC enrollment in the IPH4502 expansion cohorts was 'somewhat lower' than the approximately 15 patients each in post-EV urothelial and head and neck cohorts.
positive_highlights: Sobi deal closed with a $75 million upfront, plus up to $40 million near-term Sézary syndrome milestones, up to $465 million in additional milestones, and tiered double-digit royalties.
IPH4502 produced objective responses in post-enfortumab vedotin urothelial cancer, NSCLC, and head and neck cancer with a favorable safety profile and limited hematological toxicity.
Combined Sobi upfront and EUR 30 million equity offering extend projected cash runway through the end of Q1 2028, versus EUR 21.4 million cash at June 30, 2026.
summary: The first half 2026 update was a business and pipeline progress report rather than a quarter with reported revenue or EPS figures. Key events: the Sobi lacutamab partnership closed with a $75 million upfront, the TELLOMAK-3 phase III was initiated with first patient targeted Q1 2027 and an accelerated-approval filing planned H2 2027, and a EUR 30 million equity financing closed. IPH4502 completed phase I dose escalation with objective responses in post-enfortumab vedotin urothelial, NSCLC, and head/neck cancer, with data due at EORTC-NCI-AACR on November 18, 2026; PACIFIC-9 monalizumab phase III enrollment is complete with readout still expected in H2 2026. Cash was EUR 21.4 million as of June 30, 2026, excluding the Sobi and equity proceeds, which are expected to extend the runway through the end of Q1 2028.

negative_highlights: New orders of 20,879 fell below the 21,000-22,000 guidance range and were down from 23,000 in the prior year
SG&A of 9.2% exceeded the 8.7%-9% expected range, which management attributed to lower revenue leverage on a below-guidance ASP of $372,000 and higher brokerage commissions

Land cost per homesite is up approximately 6% and option maintenance fees are rising as deal duration extends, which management identified as the entire gross margin gap and a headwind 'still in front of us for a while'
positive_highlights: Gross margin improved sequentially to 15.8% from 15.6%, with sales incentives on deliveries down to 12%
Construction cycle time set a record low of 116 days, down from 121 days last quarter and 126 days a year ago
Completed unsold inventory fell to 1.8 homes per community from 2.1 last quarter and 3.0 in Q1, with land only 2% owned and 86% of deliveries from land-bank land
summary: Lennar delivered 20,840 homes within its 20,500-21,500 guidance range but new orders of 20,879 fell below the 21,000-22,000 range, down from 23,000 a year ago, as interest rates rose to ~7% and consumer confidence weakened. Gross margin improved sequentially to 15.8% from 15.6% and sales incentives fell to 12%, but SG&A came in at 9.2% above the 8.7%-9% expected range, producing EPS of $1.19 GAAP / $1.23 adjusted on net margin of 6.6%. Q4 guidance calls for 19,500-20,500 new orders, 22,000-23,000 deliveries, 15.5%-16% gross margin, and EPS of $1.30-$1.65. Management flagged a rising land cost basis (up ~6% per homesite) and lengthening land-bank durations as a persistent gross margin headwind, alongside building labor pressure and heavier resale competition in Texas and Florida.

negative_highlights: FY2026 net loss of $246.1 million ($3.87/share) versus $13.7 million ($1.73/share) in FY2025, driven by $195.1 million unrealized and $11.7 million realized digital asset losses
Stockholders' equity fell to negative $53.8 million from positive $90.1 million a year earlier
Solana holdings of ~2.34 million tokens carry a $360.3 million cost basis against $165.3 million in reported value at quarter end
positive_highlights: Cash rose 65% quarter-over-quarter to $5.8 million as of June 30, 2026
Extinguished roughly $20 million in debt in June and refinanced the credit facility, cutting the rate from 11.5% to 7.5%
Reduced full-time employees from 59 a year ago to 10, with management stating staking revenue should cover ongoing cash expenses going forward
summary: Upexi's fiscal Q4/FY2026 results were dominated by digital asset losses: net loss for the year was $246.1 million, or $3.87 per share, versus a $13.7 million loss ($1.73) in FY2025, driven by $195.1 million of unrealized and $11.7 million of realized digital asset losses and $21.9 million in stock-based compensation. Total stockholders' equity swung to negative $53.8 million from positive $90.1 million a year earlier, while the Treasury held roughly 2.34 million Solana tokens at a $360.3 million cost basis versus $165.3 million in reported Solana value, generating approximately $17.4 million of annualized digital asset (staking) revenue. Management did not provide explicit forward financial guidance beyond stating that cost cuts (headcount from 59 to 10, outsourced operations) should let staking revenue cover ongoing cash expenses beginning in the September 30 quarter, and it highlighted balance-sheet actions including roughly $20 million of debt extinguished, a credit facility refinance to 7.5% from 11.5%, and a $2.8 million share repurchase.

negative_highlights: Domestic DIY same-store sales declined 0.6% YoY, driven by traffic declines and milder temperatures.
International same-store sales growth slowed to +1.3% on a constant currency basis due to macro softness in Mexico.
LIFO charge of $15 million negatively impacted EPS, compared to an $80 million charge last year.
positive_highlights: Domestic commercial sales grew +8.6% YoY, finishing the year up nearly 11% versus FY2025.
Opened 175 new stores in Q4, contributing to a record 374 total store openings for FY2026.
Gross margin expanded 182 bps to 53.3%, aided by a $96 million IEEPA tariff refund.
summary: AutoZone reported Q4 FY2026 total sales of $6.6 billion (+5.6% YoY) and EPS of $56.05 (+15.1% YoY), driven by strong commercial growth (+8.6%) and a $96 million tariff refund benefit. Domestic DIY same-store sales declined 0.6% due to traffic issues and milder temperatures, while international comps grew 1.3% on a constant currency basis. Management raised FY2027 guidance for domestic same-store sales to flat to low single digits and maintained an outlook of high single-digit commercial growth.

negative_highlights: Sequential revenue decline attributed to a challenging market environment and lower sales through traditional wholesale channels.
Gross margin contracted significantly to 25.8% from 34.7% a year ago due to higher IP product costs and increased logistics/labor expenses.
Adjusted net loss widened to CNY 37.7 million compared to CNY 19.3 million in the prior year quarter, exacerbated by a CNY 124.1 million goodwill impairment.
positive_highlights: Revenue surged 94.1% year-over-year driven by higher sales of existing and newly launched IP product lines.
New IP SIINONO delivered a phenomenal trajectory, generating CNY 27.3 million in Q4 alone and representing 21.4% of total quarterly revenue.
The 'others' IP category surged 661% year-over-year to CNY 39.8 million, indicating successful diversification beyond the flagship WAKUKU.
summary: Here reported Q4 FY2026 revenue of CNY 127.7 million, representing a robust 94.1% year-over-year increase but a sequential decline driven by challenging market conditions and lower channel sales. The company recorded an adjusted net loss of CNY 37.7 million, impacted by a one-time non-cash valuation adjustment and a goodwill impairment charge of CNY 124.1 million related to the Fastone acquisition. Management emphasized a strategic pivot toward a self-operated closed loop model with disciplined capital allocation, noting that revenue scale was affected by lower sales through traditional wholesale channels while they work to optimize inventory and unit economics.

negative_highlights: Full-year net sales guidance was reduced to a midpoint of 3% growth due to lower-than-expected Q1 sales and orders.
North America Contract orders were softer than anticipated, with specific weakness in healthcare and federal/state/local government sectors.
International Contract adjusted operating margin declined 390 basis points year-over-year due to deleverage on lower sales and higher incentive compensation.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EPS of $0.53 beat the guidance range, driven by a $0.11 per share net benefit from IEPA tariff refunds.
Global Retail orders grew 7.5% year-over-year in North America, marking the eighth consecutive quarter of growth.
August sales and orders strengthened significantly across channels and geographies, offsetting softer June and July performance.
summary: First quarter sales were $923 million, down 3.4% year-over-year, while adjusted EPS of $0.53 beat the guidance range due to a one-time $0.11 per share benefit from IEPA tariff refunds. Management reduced its full-year net sales guidance to a midpoint of 3% growth and maintained the EPS range at $1.85-$2.15, explicitly including an estimated $0.07 per share unfavorable impact from new U.S.-Canada tariffs. While North America Contract orders were softer than anticipated and International Contract margins declined due to mix and inflation, Global Retail delivered order growth and margin improvement.

negative_highlights: Fourth-quarter ASP guidance was lowered by roughly $20,000 due to slower sales in Southern California and a shift in community mix.
Housing gross profit margin is expected to decline sequentially in Q4 as pricing pressures and higher land costs offset leverage benefits.
Full-year housing revenue guidance range was narrowed from the prior outlook to reflect current market conditions.
positive_highlights: Built-to-order homes comprised 74% of deliveries, up from 60% a year ago, contributing to sequential margin improvement.
Backlog conversion rate improved to 60% sequentially as the company successfully pivoted its business model.
Average build time decreased to 99 days, representing a 19% reduction compared to the prior year.
summary: KB Home reported Q3 FY2026 housing revenues of $1.3 billion and diluted EPS of $1.05, meeting full-year guidance despite a 20% year-over-year decline driven by lower delivery volume and pricing pressure. Management maintained full-year delivery and revenue guidance ranges but lowered the fourth-quarter ASP outlook by approximately $20,000 and reduced Q4 gross margin expectations by one percentage point due to softer Southern California demand and higher costs. The company returned over $65 million to shareholders via buybacks and dividends while investing nearly $725 million in land acquisition.

negative_highlights: Continued decline in dry dog food, specifically the Wilderness brand, requiring a re-look at the proposition.
Consumer stress persists with middle/lower-income shoppers waiting for sales rather than note at everyday prices.
Fruit snacks category facing pressure from insurgent brands despite overall category growth.
positive_highlights: Sequential improvement in retail trends with a 2-point improvement in dollar sales.
Significant improvement in Love Made Fresh pet business and strong growth in Tiki Cat.
Core brands like Lucky Charms, Reese's Puffs, and Cinnamon Toast Crunch returned to growth driven by innovation.
summary: Management reported sequential improvement in retail trends and a 2-point improvement in dollar sales, though the business remains below growth levels. While specific revenue and EPS figures were not explicitly stated in the Q&A transcript, management confirmed that inflation came in at the low end of the 4%-5% range for Q1 and reiterated full-year guidance assumptions. The primary focus for the remainder of the year is on driving positive price mix through innovation and renovation rather than base price increases.

negative_highlights: Q4 revenue declined to approximately $13 million from $4.8 million prior year due to residential market headwinds.
GAAP net loss increased significantly to $21.5 million for FY2026 and $11.7 million in Q4.
Q4 loss driven by a $3.9 million provision for credit losses/bad debt and $1.1 million in residential inventory reserves.
positive_highlights: Fiscal year 2026 revenue increased 58% YoY to $13.3 million reflecting expansion beyond residential base.
Pendergrass manufacturing facility officially opened and transitioning from commissioning to production ramp.
Secured a five-year agreement with SK On for 9 GWh of U.S.-manufactured LFP cells (2027-2031) and potential additional 9 GWh.
summary: Fiscal year 2026 revenue grew 58% to $13.3 million, but Q4 revenue declined to approximately $13 million due to a sharp slowdown in the residential market following federal incentive changes. GAAP net loss widened to $21.5 million for the full year and $11.7 million in Q4, driven by credit losses, inventory reserves, and facility build-out costs. Management highlighted the official opening of the Pendergrass manufacturing facility and a strategic collaboration with SK On for cell supply, though commercial terms for the pack deal remain to be finalized.

negative_highlights: Comparable store restaurant sales decreased 2.1%, driven by a 6.1% decline in traffic.
Labor and related expenses rose 100 basis points to 37.5% of revenue due to sales deleverage and the reversal of prior year kitchen labor initiatives.
Retail cost of goods sold increased 60 basis points excluding tariff refunds, primarily due to higher markdowns.
positive_highlights: Comparable store retail sales increased 0.7%, driven by a 4.2% increase in average check and higher units per transaction.
Adjusted EBITDA of $62.1 million exceeded expectations, reflecting continued momentum despite the difficult prior-year comparison.
Google star rating increased 2% year-over-year to remain near an all-time high.
summary: Cracker Barrel reported Q4 FY2026 revenue of $849.3 million with comparable store restaurant sales declining 2.1% (traffic down 6.1%) and retail comp sales up 0.7%. Adjusted EBITDA was $62.1 million, exceeding expectations despite the challenging prior-year comparison. Management provided FY2027 guidance for total revenue of $3.325-$3.4 billion and adjusted EBITDA of $180-$200 million, assuming 3%-5% same-store restaurant sales growth with no new stores.

negative_highlights: Management solutions revenue growth (4%) was slightly below expectations due to the mix shift to PEO.
Q2 outlook assumes flat employment levels and stable demand, requiring back-half acceleration to hit full-year targets.
CFO noted caution regarding upcoming annual renewals in October and January.
positive_highlights: PEO and insurance solutions delivered record retention and high-single-digit worksite employee growth.
ASO-to-PEO upgrades exceeded expectations, driven by strong referrals from HCM sales teams.
WISE AI platform prevented approximately 90% of payroll errors in a pilot with over 50,000 businesses.
summary: Paychex reported Q1 FY2027 revenue of $1.6 billion (up 6% YoY) and adjusted EPS of $1.34 (up 10%), driven by strong PEO growth of 12%. Operating margins expanded 280 bps to 38%, while management solutions grew 4% despite a mix shift from ASO to PEO. Management reaffirmed full-year FY2027 revenue guidance of 5%-6% but raised the specific outlook for PEO and insurance solutions to 7%-8%.

negative_highlights: Building Performance Solutions faced headwinds with organic sales growth of only 6% due to A2L transition and muted housing demand.
Gross margin contracted to 26.4% from 27.1% primarily reflecting lower volumes and less favorable mix in cooling and construction.
Steel availability remained tight, extending lead times and causing production disruptions for Balloon Time.
positive_highlights: Trade & Specialty Solutions delivered strong sales and EBITDA growth with margin expansion to 18.6%.
Free cash flow reached $54 million, nearly double the prior year quarter, supported by working capital improvements.
Data center ASME tank revenue matched the full fiscal 2026 run rate of $13 million in just one quarter.
summary: Worthington Enterprises reported Q1 FY2027 consolidated sales growth of 13% to $344 million and adjusted EPS of $0.82, beating the prior year period. Adjusted EBITDA increased 10% to $74 million, driven by strong performance in Trade & Specialty Solutions and joint ventures, though Building Performance Solutions faced headwinds from A2L refrigerant transition comparisons and steel supply constraints. Management raised guidance for organic growth in data center ASME tanks, projecting sequential increases through the fiscal year.

negative_highlights: Operating income was impacted by $6 million in UniFirst transaction-related expenses, though these are non-recurring.
Fire Protection Services margin faces near-term pressure from investments in new technicians and national footprint expansion (new flags).
Energy costs are expected to be slightly higher than Q4 levels for the remainder of the year due to volatile fuel prices.
positive_highlights: Total revenue grew 10.9% YoY to $3.01 billion, marking the first quarter exceeding $3 billion.
Gross margin reached an all-time high of 51.5%, with Operating Income increasing 17.6% excluding transaction costs.
Management raised full-year revenue and EPS guidance following a strong start to the fiscal year.
summary: Cintas reported Q1 FY2027 revenue of $3.01 billion (up 10.9% YoY) and diluted EPS of $1.36 (up 13.3% YoY), with adjusted EPS of $1.39. Management raised full-year fiscal 2027 revenue guidance to $12.15-$12.27 billion and adjusted EPS guidance to $5.45-$5.54, citing strong new business conversion and volume growth. Gross margin expanded to an all-time high of 51.5%, driven by segment performance and operational leverage.

negative_highlights: Active clients declined 1.4% sequentially and year-over-year in Q4 due to higher client acquisition costs.
FY2027 revenue guidance was lowered to a range of $1.31-$1.36 billion, reflecting macro headwinds.
Q1 FY2027 outlook includes drags from shifted Fix volume and an unintended post-checkout offer flow change.
positive_highlights: Q4 adjusted EBITDA of $10.8 million exceeded expectations driven by lower fixed operating expenses.
Revenue per active client (RPAC) set a new record at $592 for the third consecutive quarter.
The business outperformed the total U.S. apparel market, which was flat, with 6.4% full-year growth.
summary: Stitch Fix reported Q4 FY2026 revenue of $324.4 million (up 4.2% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $10.8 million (3.3% margin), exceeding expectations due to lower fixed costs. Full-year FY2026 revenue grew 6.4% to $1.35 billion with a net loss narrowing to $12.6 million. For FY2027, management lowered the full-year revenue guidance range to $1.31-$1.36 billion and adjusted EBITDA to $27-$42 million, citing higher client acquisition costs and temporary Q1 volume shifts.

negative_highlights: Hyve non-GAAP operating margin declined to 3.61% from 5.04% in the prior year period due to large AI server programs.
Free cash flow consumption for the quarter was approximately $1 billion driven by increased inventory and working capital investments.
Distribution gross margins were slightly impacted by customer and product mix, with Advanced Solutions facing margin pressure from larger transactions.
positive_highlights: Non-GAAP gross billings of $31.8 billion increased 40% year-over-year, exceeding the high end of guidance.
Distribution delivered strong growth with non-GAAP gross billings reaching $24.8 billion, up 27% year-over-year.
Hyve gross billings surged 117% to $7 billion driven by manufacturing and supply chain services.
summary: TD SYNNEX reported a record quarter with non-GAAP gross billings of $31.8 billion, up 40% year-over-year, and non-GAAP EPS of $5.68, beating the high end of guidance. Both Distribution ($24.8B) and Hyve ($7B) grew above market, though Hyve's operating margin contracted to 3.61% due to large AI server programs with lower initial margins. Management raised Q4 guidance for gross billings to approximately $31.9 billion plus or minus $500 million.

negative_highlights: Volume declined year-over-year as pricing gains offset lower sales volume.
Electronics segment softened due to chip shortages weighing on mobile phone production in Asia-Pacific.
Construction markets remain sluggish with high interest rates impacting residential demand.
positive_highlights: Organic revenue grew 4.4% driven by pricing actions that offset higher raw material costs.
EBITDA margin expanded 80 basis points to 19.9%, with all three GBUs contributing to profitability growth.
Quantum Leap program is on track, with $25 million of annualized savings realized through end of 2026.
summary: H.B. Fuller reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $1.8B (implied by context) with organic growth of 4.4% driven by pricing of 7.4%, partially offset by lower volume. Adjusted EBITDA was $187 million, up 9% year-over-year, expanding margins to 19.9%. Management maintained full-year 2026 guidance for mid-single digit revenue growth and adjusted EBITDA between $655M-$670M, noting the quarter came in slightly above the midpoint of the range.

negative_highlights: Gross margin deteriorated sharply to negative 0.7% in the quarter compared to 5.2% last year due to rapid new ICE car price declines.
Adjusted EBITDA loss widened to RMB 120 million, primarily reflecting the temporary impact of lower growth margins and inventory adjustments.
Broader market demand remains weak with nationwide used car transactions declining 6-11% in July-August following a severe Q2 adjustment.
positive_highlights: Retail transaction volume surged 89% year-over-year to 19,610 units, significantly outperforming the broader market which saw new car sales decline by over 20%.
Inventory turnover shortened from approximately 30 days to 20 days through AI-driven pricing and operational integration.
Management raised Q3 guidance for retail volume (expecting ~50% YoY growth) and revenue, with a clear path to gross margin recovery above 6%.
summary: Uxin reported Q2 FY2027 retail revenue of RMB 1.08 billion (up 78% YoY) and total revenue of RMB 1.151 billion (up 75% YoY), driven by a massive 89% increase in retail transaction volume to 19,610 units. However, gross margin contracted significantly to negative 0.7% due to rapid new car price adjustments impacting existing inventory, resulting in an Adjusted EBITDA loss of RMB 120 million. Management raised Q3 guidance for retail volume (expecting 20,500-21,000 units) and revenue (RMB 1.16-1.19 billion), projecting a gross margin recovery to above 6% as inventory turnover accelerates.

negative_highlights: Secure Communications full-year revenue guidance lowered due to geopolitical uncertainty and trade tensions affecting deal timing.
Licensing revenue of $22 million was significantly above expectations but management noted it is not a new quarterly run rate.
Full-year Secure Communications outlook revised down to $260-$270 million with Q3/Q4 guidance tightened due to caution on government deal cycles.
positive_highlights: QNX revenue reached a record $80 million, growing 27% YoY and exceeding the high end of guidance.
Adjusted gross margin expanded 3 percentage points YoY to 78%, driven by higher-margin royalty mix.
Secured first Alloy Kore design win with Coretura, estimated to generate over $100 million in future royalties.
summary: BlackBerry reported Q2 FY2027 revenue of $163 million (up 26% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $47 million (up 81% YoY), beating the high end of guidance. Management raised full-year revenue and adjusted EBITDA outlooks by $19 million and $21 million respectively, while also increasing QNX revenue guidance to a midpoint of $315-$325 million. The company delivered its sixth consecutive quarter of positive GAAP net income ($34 million) and generated $29 million in operating cash flow.

negative_highlights: Operating loss widened to EUR 59.2 million from EUR 19.8 million in the prior year period.
Cryostat revenues declined to EUR 0.9 million due to fewer deliveries, and government grant income fell to EUR 3.1 million.
Net cash used in operating activities increased to EUR 25.2 million compared to EUR 20 million in the prior year.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 14% year-over-year to EUR 4.9 million, with QPU-related services revenue increasing 34% to EUR 3.9 million.
Booked and awarded business reached EUR 70.4 million as of June 30, 2026, indicating strong commercial traction.
Demonstrated quantum advantage in material simulation (TMGO) with results verified experimentally across five independently deployed QPUs.
summary: Pasqal reported first-half 2026 revenue of EUR 4.9 million, representing a 14% year-over-year increase driven by QPU-related services growth of 34%. The company highlighted the commissioning of the Aramco system and a booked order book of EUR 70.4 million, though it noted an operating loss of EUR 59.2 million largely due to one-off share-based compensation and listing expenses. Management maintained its roadmap targets for fault-tolerant quantum computing by 2029 while emphasizing commercial progress in energy and financial services.

negative_highlights: Reported gross margin rate was lower year-over-year by 11 basis points to 11.02%, impacted by a $152 million LIFO charge.
Membership growth has slowed for eight consecutive quarters, with the spread between membership and unit growth narrowing.
Inflation in non-foods increased due to memory costs in consumer electronics and geopolitical impacts on gas/petroleum items.
positive_highlights: Comparable sales excluding gas price inflation and FX were up 6.7%, demonstrating underlying demand strength.
Non-foods comparable sales were the highest-performing category overall, with top departments including gold/jewelry and home furnishings.
Executive membership penetration reached an all-time high, contributing to improved renewal rates of 92.3% in the U.S. and Canada.
summary: Costco reported Q4 FY2026 net sales of $93.87 billion, an increase of 11.2% year-over-year, with comparable sales up 9.4%. Net income was $2.998 billion ($6.75 per diluted share), including a non-recurring tariff refund benefit of $0.15 per share; excluding this item, net income grew 12.3%. Membership fee income rose 7.3% to $1.849 billion, driven by higher executive membership penetration and base growth.

negative_highlights: Operating loss widened to $9.8 million from $4.9 million due to sharply higher variable compensation ($11.7 million) and data processing costs.
Cash used in operating activities was $6.2 million, reversing the cash flow provided in the prior year.
Six new correspondent broker-dealers signed contributed no meaningful revenue during fiscal 2026 as they were still onboarding.
positive_highlights: Revenue increased 85% to $20.1 million, significantly outpacing prior year growth.
Stock locate revenue expanded rapidly from approximately $300,000 to $6.8 million.
Balance sheet strengthened with cash ending at $15.4 million and stockholders' equity improving to a surplus of $21.1 million.
summary: Fiscal 2026 revenue surged 85% to $20.1 million driven by a breakout in stock locate fees ($6.8 million) and existing correspondent growth (67%), though total expenses rose sharply to $29.8 million due to variable compensation and new cost categories. The company reported a GAAP net income of $2 million, primarily supported by an $11.1 million non-cash gain on warrant earn-out liabilities, while operating cash flow turned negative at -$6.2 million as the business invested in growth. Management raised no specific financial guidance but highlighted strategic milestones including the Dawson James transaction and a refiled application for Commercial Bancorp.

negative_highlights: Olive Garden faced a net negative impact to same-restaurant sales of approximately 80 basis points due to the World Cup and consumer concerns about lettuce.
Olive Garden segment profit margin declined 20 basis points year-over-year, partly due to menu mix changes including lighter portion sections.
The Other Business Segment margin contracted 30 basis points primarily due to costs associated with winding down Bahama Breeze.
positive_highlights: All segments delivered positive same-restaurant sales growth in the quarter.
LongHorn Steakhouse achieved a 6.8% comparable calendar same-restaurant sales increase, marking its 22nd consecutive quarter of growth.
Olive Garden's Never-Ending Pasta Bowl promotion saw all 10,000 passes sold out immediately upon launch.
summary: Darden reported Q1 FY2027 total sales of $3.2 billion, a 5.1% increase year-over-year driven by positive same-restaurant sales growth across all segments and the addition of 53 net new restaurants. Diluted net earnings per share from continuing operations were $2.05, representing a 4.1% increase over the prior year. Management reaffirmed full-year fiscal 2027 diluted EPS guidance between $11.10 and $11.35, maintaining expectations despite headwinds including World Cup impacts and consumer concerns regarding lettuce.

negative_highlights: Consolidated revenues decreased 4% to $216.8 million, primarily reflecting lower education and children's book publishing revenues.
Education segment revenues fell $9.7 million year-over-year as districts managed higher costs and ESSER funding concluded.
Adjusted operating loss widened to $88.7 million on a comparable basis due to higher overhead costs.
positive_highlights: Entertainment segment revenues increased $6.5 million year-over-year to $20.1 million driven by higher production activity.
Book fair bookings and fair count are ahead of the prior year with strong early indicators for the fall season.
International adjusted operating loss improved to $2.7 million from $4.1 million due to cost management.
summary: Scholastic reported Q1 FY2027 revenue of $216.8 million, a 4% decrease year-over-year, driven by lower education and children's book publishing revenues and the elimination of rental income from sale-leaseback transactions. The company recorded an operating loss of $92.2 million and reaffirmed its full-year fiscal 2027 guidance for revenue growth of 2%-4% and adjusted EBITDA of $135 million-$145 million. Management noted that while the first quarter is seasonally light, they remain confident in the trajectory ahead due to strong entertainment production activity and upcoming franchise launches like Harry Potter.

negative_highlights: Gas volumes currently limited by market demand and Northern Territory Government nominations at 25 terajoules per day
Expansion of the SPCF remains contingent on certainty regarding surrounding infrastructure network to move incremental volumes
positive_highlights: Completed Sturt Plateau Compression Facility on time at approximately $9 million below forecasted budget
Raised US$186 million net of fees via public offer and entitlement, solidifying the balance sheet with US$240 million pro forma cash position
Successfully completed stimulation campaign on SS-2 pad utilizing local Beetaloo Red Sand with no impact to pump pressures or fracture initiation
summary: Tamboran Resources delivered first gas sales to the Northern Territory market after completing the Sturt Plateau Compression Facility on time and approximately $9 million below budget. The company raised US$186 million in equity in April, bringing pro forma cash to US$240 million, while currently operating under a 25 terajoules per day nomination limit due to seasonal demand constraints. Management is prioritizing two wells to generate long-term production history before ramping up to the full 40 terajoule per day take-or-pay contract quantity.

negative_highlights: Revenue from the retailer agent channel declined 17% YoY as customers migrated to digital alternatives.
Net2phone budgeted a small increase in Adjusted EBITDA for FY2027, though management noted they previously underestimated growth.
positive_highlights: Consolidated revenue increased 7% YoY in Q4 and full-year growth accelerated to 5% from 2% in FY2025.
NRS Adjusted EBITDA surged 47% YoY to $14.3 million (implied) driven by a 31% revenue increase and advertising/data revenue up 49%.
Fintech segment Adjusted EBITDA grew 41% YoY, while net2phone Adjusted EBITDA expanded 33% despite AI investment.
summary: IDT reported a strong Q4 FY2026 with consolidated revenue up 7% YoY and full-year revenue accelerating to 5% growth. The company generated record quarterly gross profit and Adjusted EBITDA, with the three high-margin segments (NRS, Fintech, net2phone) driving the majority of earnings growth. Management raised fiscal 2027 Adjusted EBITDA guidance to a range of $176 million-$180 million, representing a 15% increase from the prior year's record.

negative_highlights: Pass units declined 12%, days sold declined 10%, and sales dollars were down 6% through September 18.
Implied resort EBITDA margin for FY2027 is expected to be approximately 200 basis points below the original fiscal 2026 outlook due to inflation outpacing revenue growth.
Visitation in the upcoming season is expected to remain modestly below original fiscal 2026 expectations despite a meaningful recovery from last year's weather impacts.
positive_highlights: Resort-reported EBITDA for fiscal 2026 landed in line with the midpoint of the range provided in June ($746 million).
Management expects total revenue to increase approximately 3% compared to fiscal 2026 expectations driven by stronger ancillary revenue growth.
The company remains confident in cash flow generation capabilities even at the low end of guidance, supporting capital spending and dividends.
summary: Fiscal 2026 Q4 resort net revenue was flat year-over-year, while full-year lift revenue decreased 3.5% despite a 13% decline in skier visitation due to severe weather. Management provided FY2027 guidance for net income of $158M-$233M and EBITDA of $805M-$865M, noting that total revenue is expected to increase approximately 3% versus the prior year's expectations driven by ancillary growth, though implied margins are projected to be lower than the original FY2026 outlook. Pass sales remain down through the current watching period, with management attributing the weakness to delayed decision-making rather than structural demand changes.

negative_highlights: Gross margin compressed slightly to 43.4% from 45.2% in the prior year
Cost of goods sold increased 62.3% YoY, outpacing revenue growth
Intelligent robotics business remains in an early R&D stage with no immediate revenue contribution
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 57.4% YoY to $57.1 million
Return to operating profitability with income of $5.5 million vs. a prior period loss of $1.9 million
Battery swapping subsidiary secured two consecutive batch orders from CATL's Qiji Energy
summary: First half 2026 revenue grew 57.4% year-over-year to $57.1 million, driven by a 59.4% increase in core off-road EV sales and the acquisition of Rawrr. The company returned to operating profitability with income from operations of $5.5 million compared to a loss of $1.9 million in the prior period. Management expressed confidence in the dual-engine strategy, citing tangible progress in battery swapping equipment orders and strong sales momentum in North America.

negative_highlights: Substantial doubt exists about the ability to continue as a going concern; existing cash is insufficient for at least 12 months.
Operating expenses increased to $21.9M in FY2026 from $17.5M in FY2025, with G&A rising due to higher professional fees.
Net loss widened to $8.4M in FY2026 compared to $17.3M in FY2025 (excluding prior year gains).
positive_highlights: Full-year collaboration revenue of $13.2M, including $9.4M from Boehringer Ingelheim and $3.8M non-cash debt cancellation from Altanispac.
Preclinical data supports potential for dosing less frequently than once-weekly (e.g., every two weeks) for the lipidated peptide series.
PL7737 oral program lessons learned have led to multiple new scaffolds with improved potency and selectivity.
summary: Palatin reported Q4 FY2026 collaboration revenue of $300,000 and full-year revenue of $13.2M, offset by a net loss of $8.4M ($2.96/share) driven by operating expenses rising to $21.9M. Management indicated substantial doubt about the company's ability to continue as a going concern due to insufficient cash reserves for 12 months, necessitating additional financing. Forward guidance targets Phase I initiation for lipidated and oral MC4R candidates in H2 2027.

negative_highlights: Cash balance decreased by CHF 0.8 million to CHF 0.8 million due to operating costs.
Net loss remained stable at CHF 3.4 million, indicating no improvement in profitability despite reduced outsourced R&D.
Share of net loss from Neurosterix spin-out increased to CHF 2.3 million compared to CHF 2.1 million in the prior period.
positive_highlights: Regained full rights to the GABAB PAM substance use disorder and cough programs following Indivior's termination of the license.
Raised $2.8 million in Q3 through ATM facility, securing cash runway into Q4 2027.
GABAB PAM clinical candidate demonstrated a 60-fold safety margin based on respiratory depression biomarkers in non-human primate studies.
summary: Addex Therapeutics reported a net loss of CHF 3.4 million for H1 FY2026, which remained stable compared to the prior year period. The company raised $2.8 million via its ATM facility in Q3, extending its cash runway to Q4 2027, but cash on hand decreased from CHF 1.6 million at year-end 2025 to CHF 0.8 million at June 30, 2026 due to operating costs. Management highlighted the regaining of rights to the GABAB PAM program from Indivior and progress in preclinical studies for SUD and cough indications, noting that IND-enabling studies are ready pending financing.

negative_highlights: No specific revenue or EPS figures were disclosed for the first half of 2026 in the provided transcript.
Management explicitly stated they are not guiding on future raises or specific top-line data readout details until Q4.
Weight gain and edema remain potential tolerability concerns, though management argues they are attenuated compared to full PPAR gamma agonists.
positive_highlights: Cash runway extended to Q2 2027 with current resources, potentially to Q1 2028 if Tranche 3 warrants are exercised following positive top-line data.
NATiV3 trial last patient completed their final 72-week visit earlier in the month, positioning for Q4 2026 top-line readout.
Phase II-B data showed lanifibranor delivered an 18% placebo-adjusted improvement in fibrosis and 26% on MASH resolution after six months.
summary: Inventiva reported first half of 2026 financial results with EUR 233.9 million in cash equivalents and short-term deposits as of June 30, 2026. The company strengthened its balance sheet through capital structure optimization, including the buyback of EIB warrants for EUR 50 million and repayment of EIB loans for EUR 63 million, alongside new debt financing and an ADS offering generating EUR 103 million in gross proceeds. R&D expenses were EUR 46.2 million, while marketing and G&A expenses increased to EUR 2.6 million and EUR 22.2 million respectively.

negative_highlights: Q4 revenue declined 3% YoY to $5.6M, which management attributed to prior-year pull-forward of traceability activity before the FDA deadline
Full-year revenue growth of 3% was moderated by deliberate de-emphasis of high-touch, low-margin revenue streams
The FDA traceability compliance date was extended to July 2028 with a congressional directive against enforcement before then, pushing the expected revenue inflection into 2027
positive_highlights: Full-year operating margin expanded ~620 bps to 33.7% from 27.5%, with operating income up 26% to $7.8M
Q4 diluted EPS rose ~20% YoY to $0.11 despite income tax expense nearly tripling, with Q4 opex down 11% to $3.7M
Touchless Merchandising went from press release to signed contracts and initial revenue in about 45 days, with management expecting meaningful contribution in 2027
summary: Full-year FY2026 revenue rose 3% to $23.3M with opex down 6% to $15.4M, lifting operating margin to ~33.7% from 27.5% and diluted EPS 13% to $0.39. Q4 revenue fell 3% YoY to $5.6M due to the prior-year pull-forward of traceability activity ahead of the original FDA deadline, now extended to July 2028, while Q4 EPS rose ~20% to $0.11 on 19% operating income growth and an 11% opex cut. No formal guidance was issued beyond qualitative expectations that traceability revenue accelerates into 2027 and Touchless Merchandising, launched ~45 days ago with SPAR Group, produces little revenue this quarter but becomes significant in 2027. Cash was $27.3M plus a $3M SPAR note, with $1.8M of buybacks and preferred redemptions continuing.

negative_highlights: Full-year GPU reduction outlook improved to less than the previously guided $200 per unit decrease.
Wholesale gross profit per unit declined $135 year-over-year, though volume was up 16%.
CarMax Auto Finance penetration declined year-over-year due to lower tier one financing.
positive_highlights: Total sales grew 19% year-over-year to $7.9 billion, with used unit comps up 13%.
EPS increased 81% year-over-year to $1.16, supported by strong comp growth and SG&A leverage of 9%.
Extended Protection Plan (EPP) margins expanded materially, reaching $46 per unit in Q2 against a full-year guidance of $35.
summary: CarMax reported Q2 FY2027 total sales of $7.9 billion, up 19% year-over-year, with used unit comps growing 13%. Earnings per share surged 81% to $1.16, driven by robust comp growth and SG&A leverage, though management noted that full-year GPU reductions will be less than the previously guided $200 per unit due to better-than-expected execution. Management indicated a plan to resume share repurchases at a modest pace in Q3.

negative_highlights: Constant currency revenue decreased 0.5%, missing the lower end of guidance.
A 3% headwind from shore mix impacted results, with additional hyperscaler spend priority impacts expected in Q4.
No share repurchases were made in the quarter despite strong cash generation.
positive_highlights: Non-GAAP operating income of $309 million beat the high end of guidance.
New business revenues grew at an expected 30% year-over-year rate.
Adjusted free cash flow reached a record $218 million for the third quarter.
summary: Concentrix reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $2.45 billion, a 0.5% decrease on a constant currency basis, missing the lower end of guidance due to client decisions to reduce support and AI deployment acceleration. Non-GAAP operating income was $309 million, exceeding the high end of guidance, with margins expanding 30 bps year-over-year. Management noted a 3% headwind from shore mix and warned that hyperscaler spending priorities will create a larger-than-expected revenue impact in Q4.

negative_highlights: Management explicitly stated there is no formal guidance for FY2027 due to reliance on external regulatory approvals.
Regulatory delays remain a key variable impacting the ramp-up timeline for new header houses at Christensen Ranch and Ludeman.
Burke Hollow production was limited to a small section of the first production area to establish operating parameters before full expansion.
positive_highlights: Production surged 157% quarter-over-quarter to nearly 83,000 pounds driven by new header houses at Christensen Ranch and full commissioning at Burke Hollow.
Total cost per pound dropped 33% to $36.50 as higher volumes moved through the Hobson plant.
Company ended the year with $753 million in liquid assets and no debt, providing flexibility to hold inventory for upside pricing.
summary: Fiscal Q4 FY2026 production rose 157% to nearly 83,000 pounds of U3O8 with total costs falling 33% to $36.50 per pound. The company generated $37.3 million in revenue and $16.9 million in gross profit by watching 400,000 pounds at a weighted average realized price of $93.13 per pound while holding significant inventory. Management provided no formal guidance for FY2027 due to regulatory timing variables but expressed strong confidence in scaling operations.

negative_highlights: Higher fuel prices created an $0.11 per share headwind for the full year, though mitigated by consumption reductions.
The new loyalty program creates a temporary accounting-driven yield headwind in Q4 2026 and FY2027 before turning positive in 2028.
positive_highlights: Net income exceeded June guidance by over $100 million or $0.08 per share.
Yields increased nearly 2.5% year-over-year, with strong close-in demand translating into higher revenues.
Customer deposits reached a record of approximately $7.6 billion, up about 7% despite flat capacity growth.
summary: CCL reported a strong Q3 FY2026 with revenues and yields reaching new highs, exceeding June guidance by approximately $100 million ($0.08 per share). The outperformance was driven by yield increases of nearly 2.5% year-over-year and cost discipline that delivered unit costs better than expected despite higher fuel prices. Management raised full-year 2026 EPS guidance to $2.24 from the prior level, citing operational improvements of more than $150 million.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA margin in Repair, Engineering, and Software declined 120 bps to 11.9% due to expected note weakness in-term dilution from the HAECO Americas integration.
The full-year outlook excludes any impact from the MRO Holdings acquisition until it closes later in the fiscal year.
positive_highlights: Total sales grew 24% year-over-year driven by broad-based growth across all three key segments.
Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 100 bps to 12.7%, excluding Legacy Commercial Programs it reached 13.3% within the target range.
Record first-quarter cash flow of $57 million reduced net leverage to 1.81x.
summary: AAR reported Q1 FY2027 total sales of $918 million, up 24% year-over-year (11% organic), with Adjusted EBITDA margin expanding 100 bps to 12.7%. The company announced an agreement to acquire a 65% controlling interest in MRO Holdings for an implied enterprise value of $4 billion, which is expected to close in Q3 FY2027. Management raised the full-year sales outlook excluding Legacy Commercial Programs to the low teens and maintained Q2 guidance.

negative_highlights: Mobile and client segment saw a sequential bit decline in the quarter.
Supply growth expected to decelerate in 2027 due to HBM trade ratio increases and cleanroom constraints.
NAND bit shipments tracking below industry average, with limited visibility on 2027-2028 growth rates.
positive_highlights: Server units growing in the high teens driven by agentic AI workloads.
HBM pricing increased significantly for calendar year 2027 to narrow profitability gaps.
Micron maintains technology leadership at least two nodes ahead of China competition.
summary: Micron's Q4 FY2026 call focused on forward guidance for fiscal 2027 and beyond rather than reporting specific quarterly financial results. Management confirmed single-digit sequential bit growth and double-digit cost increases for the first quarter of fiscal 2027, while raising expectations for server unit growth into 2028 driven by agentic AI and CPU demand. The company reiterated that supply constraints will persist through 2028 due to HBM trade ratio shifts and cleanroom space limitations.

negative_highlights: Healthcare and Packaging segment revenue was lower than expected due to automation equipment delays and timing shifts in a customer program.
Connected Living (now Intelligent Devices) revenue was flat year-over-year, with management noting a 15% decline in the Connected Living sub-segment specifically.
positive_highlights: Revenue beat exceeded the high end of guidance by more than $1 billion above the June outlook midpoint.
Intelligent Infrastructure revenue grew 56% year-over-year, driven by AI demand acceleration and early capacity ramping.
Core operating margin expanded to 6.4%, reflecting improved mix and contribution from the Hanley Energy acquisition.
summary: Jabil reported Q4 FY2026 revenue of $10.6 billion, up 29% year-over-year, and core EPS of $4.40, up 34% year-over-year, both exceeding the high end of guidance. Management raised full-year fiscal 2027 revenue guidance to approximately $8.5 billion (up from over $6 billion in FY2026) and increased Q1 2027 revenue guidance to a range of $10.6-$11.4 billion, driven by strong AI infrastructure demand and capacity ramping. The company maintained its asset-light capital model with CapEx expectations of 1.5%-2% of revenue.

negative_highlights: Net revenue declined 46% year-over-year and 3% sequentially due to lower loan facilitation volume under new regulatory requirements.
Allowance for contract assets receivable and others increased significantly to RMB 502.8 million following a reassessment of recoverability on aging balances.
Fair value adjustment loss of RMB 97.8 million recorded due to Ethereum price fluctuations, offsetting potential gains.
positive_highlights: Credit environment recovery with the outstanding balance of performing loans declining 30% to RMB 15.1 billion.
Insurance brokerage revenue grew 16% year-over-year supported by a 281% increase in insurance clients to approximately 453,000.
Technology service revenues increased 5.9% year-over-year as the company begins generating external commercial traction from AI capabilities.
summary: Yiren Digital reported Q2 FY2026 net revenue of RMB 890 million, down 3% sequentially and 46% year-over-year, driven by a 29% decline in loan facilitation volume. Net loss narrowed by 9% sequentially to RMB 449.6 million due to lower provisions for contingent liabilities, though this was partially offset by higher allowances for credit losses on aging receivables and a fair value loss of RMB 97.8 million on Ethereum. Management emphasized a strategic transition toward an asset-light, technology-driven model while maintaining capital discipline.

negative_highlights: Q4 adjusted operating margin compressed to 33% from 33.8% due to structural investments and performance-based compensation expenses.
FY2027 EPS growth faces a headwind of approximately 2% driven by higher assumed tax rates and incremental interest expense on maturing notes.
Revenue growth for FY2027 is expected to be lower than ASV growth (5%-6% vs 5%-6.5%) due to the exit from ESG Signals attribution business and FX impacts.
positive_highlights: Q4 organic ASV accelerated to 7% YoY, representing the largest quarter ever at $86 million.
Full year FY2026 organic ASV exceeded guidance by $168 million, a more than 30% increase over FY2025 levels.
AI-related solutions contributed double-digit share of new ASV this quarter, exceeding the total AI contribution of fiscal 2025.
summary: FactSet reported Q4 FY2026 revenue of $634 million (up 6% YoY) and adjusted EPS of $4.52 (up 11% YoY), both exceeding the high end of guidance. Full year FY2026 organic ASV grew 7% to $2.56 billion, also beating the high end of guidance. Management raised FY2027 organic ASV guidance to a range of 5%-6.5% and expects operating margin expansion of 25-75 bps in FY2027.

negative_highlights: Conventional shell egg net sales dropped 59.5% to $201.7 million, resulting in a segment operating loss of $71 million.
Net cash used in operating activities was $101.4 million compared to $278.6 million provided in the prior year period.
Feed costs increased 4.3% quarter-over-quarter, with management warning that higher grain prices could persist through the balance of the year.
positive_highlights: Specialty shell eggs generated operating income of $14.9 million with a 6.3% margin, outpacing overall category growth trends.
Prepared foods segment delivered operating income of $7.8 million and a 12.4% margin despite volume declines.
Company maintained a strong balance sheet with $767.6 million in cash and temporary investments while remaining virtually debt-free.
summary: Consolidated net sales fell 41.5% to $539.6 million and operating income swung to a loss of $82.2 million due to a severe decline in conventional shell egg volumes and prices. While specialty shell eggs and prepared foods segments remained profitable, the company's overall earnings were heavily impacted by market timing lags and elevated feed costs. Management emphasized that current results reflect a trough in the commodity cycle and ongoing investments in prepared foods capacity that have not yet fully realized earnings potential.

negative_highlights: Q2 organic sales guidance lowered to a 2% decline, heavier than consensus expectations.
Transportation inflation has doubled compared to planning assumptions, offsetting protein favorability.
Frozen business volumes expected to be down approximately 10% in the coming quarters.
positive_highlights: Q1 EPS beat driven by favorable SG&A timing and lower-than-forecasted inflation in proteins.
Ardent Mills provided a $0.03 benefit to the quarter due to wheat price volatility trading opportunities.
Sweet treats portfolio (Snack Pack, Swiss Miss) continues to perform very well with strong Q1 results.
summary: Conagra Brands reported a Q1 FY2027 EPS beat driven by SG&A timing benefits and lower-than-expected inflation in proteins, though operating margin guidance for the full year was held flat at high single digits. Management reaffirmed its Q2 organic sales outlook of a 2% decline, citing Thanksgiving timing and higher transportation inflation offsetting protein favorability. The company maintained its full-year inflation guidance range of 5%-6%, noting that Q4 is expected to see lower inflation as they wrap on material costs.

negative_highlights: Domo's top line is expected to settle at a steady state of $280-$290 million, implying churn in its legacy seat-based and services revenue streams.
Full-year 2027 operating margin is expected to compress to the high 30s (approx. 36%-37%) due to integration timing and Domo's lower initial margins.
positive_highlights: EPS of $1.69 exceeded the high end of guidance, growing 13% year-over-year.
Operating margin expanded significantly to 43%, up 300 basis points from a year ago.
Full-year 2026 revenue guidance was raised by more than $50 million due to Domo's partial quarter contribution and strong base performance.
summary: Q3 revenue of $246 million met the midpoint of guidance, while EPS of $1.69 exceeded the high end of the range and ARR grew over 1% to $873 million. The company closed its acquisition of Domo's AI and data platform business for $400 million, raising full-year 2026 revenue guidance by more than $50 million to a range of $1 billion-$1.044 billion. Operating margins expanded to 43%, driven by cost discipline and improved collections following the integration of ShareFile.

negative_highlights: Direct impact from the Middle East market worsened in Q4, though indirect impacts stabilized.
Days services outstanding increased to 50 days from 48 days in the prior quarter.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 7% in local currency, beating the top end of the guided range.
Adjusted operating margin expanded 20 basis points to 15.3%.
Free cash flow reached $2.8 billion for the quarter and $11.6 billion for the full year.
summary: Accenture reported Q4 FY2026 revenue of $18.7 billion, growing 7% in local currency above the top end of its guided range, with adjusted EPS rising 9% to $3.29. The company delivered strong margin expansion and free cash flow while returning a record amount of cash to shareholders through dividends and buybacks. Full-year FY2026 revenue reached $74 billion with approximately 5% growth in local currency, exceeding original guidance.

negative_highlights: Operating loss widened to $40.9 million from $27.3 million in the prior year period.
Net loss increased to $36.4 million compared to $22.3 million in the prior year.
R&D expenses rose by $5.1 million net of stock-based compensation due to acquisitions and strategic investments.
positive_highlights: Revenue increased 116% YoY to $11.4 million driven by core semiconductor and PKI lines.
Gross margin expanded 1300 bps to approximately 48% due to higher-value technology mix.
Post-quantum commercial pipeline exceeded $225 million through 2029 with over 150 customers engaging.
summary: WISeKey reported preliminary unaudited revenue of $11.4 million for H1 FY2026, representing an 116% increase year-over-year to $5.3 million in the prior period. Gross margin expanded significantly to approximately 48% from 35%, driven by improved product mix and higher-value semiconductor contributions. Management reaffirmed full-year 2026 revenue growth guidance of 50%-100% compared to 2025, citing strong liquidity of $495 million at June 30.

negative_highlights: Nike Sportswear declined low double digits, with a deliberate Dunk revenue reduction creating a roughly $200 million headwind.
Jordan Brand revenue fell mid-teens globally as the company reduces volume of iconic retro products to restore scarcity.
Greater China revenue declined 26% due to digital cleanup actions and broader marketplace pressure.
positive_highlights: Nike performance portfolio grew high single digits, driven by double-digit growth in running, global football, tennis, and golf.
Gross margin improved 60 bps to 42.8% due to supply chain cost management and FX tailwinds.
North America revenue grew 2%, led by performance categories including running and basketball.
summary: Nike reported Q1 FY2027 revenue of $11.2 billion, a decline of 4% on a reported basis and 5% currency neutral, with EPS down 2% to $0.48. Gross margin expanded 60 bps to 42.8%, driven by supply chain discipline and FX, partially offset by increased discounts. Management provided full-year FY2027 guidance expecting revenue decline in the high single digits and adjusted EPS between $1.15-$1.35, noting that deliberate actions in Sportswear, Jordan Brand, and Greater China will dampen near-term results.

negative_highlights: Full-year production guidance lowered to 26,500-27,000 ounces due to lower grades (1.7 g/t vs 1.9 g/t) and mill expansion delays.
Group all-in sustaining costs rose to $3,078/oz in H1, exceeding the guidance range of $2,400-$2,700/oz.
Production at How Mine fell 11% YoY to 11,373 ounces as the existing mill reached capacity constraints.
positive_highlights: Revenue increased 40% to $50.8 million driven by a 48% rise in average net realized gold price to $4,195/oz.
Adjusted EBITDA surged 76% to GBP 19 million, with gross profit doubling to GBP 27 million (53% margin).
Red Wing dewatering completed ahead of schedule, enabling an earlier restart target of January 2027.
summary: Namib Minerals reported H1 FY2026 revenue of $50.8 million (up 40% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of GBP 19 million (up 76%), driven by a significantly stronger gold price despite lower production volumes. Management revised full-year 2026 production guidance down to 26,500-27,000 ounces from the prior range of 28,000-31,500 due to lower grades at How Mine and delayed commissioning of the expanded milling plant until mid-October. The company maintained its C1 cash cost guidance of $1,400-$1,650 per ounce while funding expansion via bank debt rather than equity.

negative_highlights: U.S. consumer organic sales were flat due to a volume decline offset by pricing, with softer demand from CPG and QSR customers.
A note weakness in-term industry supply constraint on specific packaging material may negatively impact total company volume growth for the fourth quarter by up to one point.
QSR volumes in EMEA were pressured by softer foot traffic, particularly in the U.K.
positive_highlights: Total net sales grew 17% in constant currency with 2% organic growth.
Adjusted gross profit margin expanded 180 basis points driven by acquisition accretion and productivity initiatives.
McCormick de Mexico delivered robust volume-led quarterly growth fueled by strength in mayonnaise and herbs/spices.
summary: Total net sales grew 17% in constant currency with 2% organic growth, driven by the McCormick de Mexico acquisition and solid performance in EMEA and Asia Pacific. Adjusted gross profit margin expanded 180 basis points to support a 22% increase in adjusted operating income, though U.S. consumer volumes faced pressure from macro factors and a packaging supply constraint. Management maintained its full-year guidance range while noting that fourth-quarter volume improvement will be more gradual due to these headwinds.

negative_highlights: ABL sales declined slightly by less than 1% due to an elevated backlog from accelerated orders in the prior year.
Adjusted operating profit margin decreased 10 bps to 18.7% impacted by a $15 million special charge and technology investments.
AIS margins face an anticipated headwind of approximately 200 basis points from memory cost increases starting in Q1 FY2027.
positive_highlights: Adjusted diluted earnings per share increased 11% to $5.77 driven by higher profitability and lower shares outstanding.
Acuity Intelligent Spaces (AIS) sales grew 17% to $298 million with adjusted operating profit margin expanding 350 bps to 24.9%.
Company generated $826 million in fiscal year cash flow from operations, a $225 million increase over the prior year.
summary: Acuity Brands reported Q4 FY2026 net sales of $1.2 billion (up 3% YoY) and adjusted diluted EPS of $5.77 (up 11% YoY). The company delivered solid execution with gross margin expansion to 50.2%, though operating margin dipped slightly due to a $15 million special charge and memory cost headwinds anticipated in the next fiscal year. Management provided FY2027 guidance for net sales between $4.7 billion and $4.9 billion and adjusted EPS between $20.50 and $22, maintaining the prior trajectory without raising or lowering expectations.

negative_highlights: Operating loss widened to $40.9 million from $27.3 million in the prior year period.
Net loss increased to $36.4 million from $22.3 million, reflecting heavy investments in R&D ($9.1M) and strategic platforms.
Revenue guidance relies on future commercialization of post-quantum products expected in Q4 2026 and beyond.
positive_highlights: Revenue increased 116% YoY to $11.4 million driven by core semiconductor lines and acquisitions (IC'ALPS, Miraex, Wecan).
Gross margin expanded 1300 bps to approximately 48% due to improved product mix.
Post-quantum commercial pipeline exceeded $225 million through 2029 with over 150 customers engaging.
summary: WISeKey reported preliminary unaudited revenue of $11.4 million for H1 FY2026, representing a 116% increase year-over-year to $5.3 million in the prior period. Gross margin expanded significantly to approximately 48% from 35%, driven by improved product mix and higher-value semiconductor contributions. The company reaffirmed its full-year 2026 revenue growth guidance of 50%-100% compared to 2025, citing strong progress in post-quantum commercialization and sovereign infrastructure initiatives.

negative_highlights: Currency headwinds moderated revenue growth as the US Dollar Index strengthened.
First-half core growth is expected to be lower (approx. 3.5%) compared to Q1 due to timing of orders previously recognized in Q2.
Petrifilm transition involves duplicative costs that are expected to peak before subsiding, with full margin benefits not realized until FY2029.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 8.1% core, marking the fifth consecutive quarter of core growth.
Food safety segment revenue increased 8.1%, led by an 11% increase in Petrifilm and double-digit growth in pathogen detection.
Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 170 bps to 18.7%, with free cash flow improving $18 million year-over-year.
summary: Neogen reported Q1 FY2027 revenue of $222.8 million, representing an 8.1% core growth driven by food safety and animal safety segments. The company raised its full-year 2027 revenue guidance to $885-$890 million and adjusted EBITDA guidance to $181-$183 million. Management highlighted a successful milestone in the Petrifilm manufacturing transition with full validation of the first SKU.

negative_highlights: Gross margins declined 100 basis points as the rate of raw material inflation outpaced pricing and MAP benefits.
Construction Products Group sales were dragged down by polyurethane feedstock shortages and a slowdown in education and healthcare markets.
Full-year guidance was narrowed from a previous outlook of 3%-7% sales growth to mid-single digits.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EPS increased 5.3% to a first quarter record of $1.98.
Performance Coatings Group delivered record results with broad-based growth led by engineered solutions for high-performance buildings and emerging markets.
Consumer Group achieved 5.2% organic growth driven by shelf space wins, new products, and pricing.
summary: RPM reported record first quarter sales and adjusted EBITDA, with adjusted EPS increasing 5.3% to $1.98. However, consolidated gross margins declined 100 basis points as raw material inflation outpaced pricing, while the company lowered its full-year guidance for both sales and EBITDA due to higher-than-expected inflation in polyurethane feedstocks and other commodities. Management noted that Construction Products Group sales were negatively impacted by temporary supply shortages and a slowdown in education and healthcare markets.

negative_highlights: International segment net sales declined 8% due to a 6% drop in sales volume, primarily in Europe.
European crop yields were negatively impacted by heat and dry conditions, reducing tonnage by an estimated 15-20%.
Adjusted EBITDA for the International segment declined 5% YoY due to carry-in of prior year potato costs.
positive_highlights: North America sales volume grew 7% for the seventh consecutive quarter, exceeding end market growth.
Price mix improved sequentially by 70 basis points to a 1.7% decline from Q4 levels.
Adjusted EBITDA in North America grew 11% driven by volume and cost savings initiatives.
summary: Lamb Weston reported Q1 FY2027 net sales of $1,670 million (up 1% YoY) and adjusted EPS of $0.75 (up 1% YoY), beating expectations. Management raised the full-year fiscal 2027 outlook for net sales to low-single-digit growth and increased the adjusted EBITDA range to $1.125-$1.215 billion. North America delivered strong volume growth, while International results were in line with guidance but below long-term aspirations.

negative_highlights: Advanced Computing full-year FY2026 net sales declined 14% due to the wind-down of Penguin Edge and lower hyperscale hardware sales.
Services net sales in Q4 were down 11% year-over-year, reflecting lower hyperscale services volumes.
Gross margin for the full year was 29.3%, down 170 basis points from the prior year, primarily due to a greater contribution from AI infrastructure hardware.
