positive_highlights: Net sales grew 68% year-over-year to a record $567 million, with EPS growing at 133% due to operating leverage.
Integrated Memory achieved record Q4 net sales of $341 million (up 158% YoY) and ended the quarter with a backlog extending at least four quarters.
Fiscal 2027 guidance was raised from a preliminary view of ~30% growth to a midpoint of ~40% for net sales and ~55% for EPS.
summary: Penguin Solutions reported record Q4 FY2026 results with net sales of $567 million (up 68% YoY) and diluted EPS of $1.00 (up 133% YoY). The company raised its fiscal 2027 guidance, projecting net sales growth of approximately 40% at the midpoint and diluted EPS growth of approximately 55%. Full-year FY2026 net sales reached $1.73 billion, up 26% YoY, driven by strong performance in AI infrastructure and Integrated Memory segments.

negative_highlights: Lower volume in Metals and Glass segments offset by price gains.
Glass segment margin declined year-over-year to 14.9% due to lower prices and higher costs, though improved sequentially from Q1.
Services segment margin decreased to 5.8% due to project mix impacts despite volume growth.
positive_highlights: Revenue beat expectations with a 9.2% year-over-year increase to $391 million.
Adjusted EPS improved 19% year-over-year to $1.17, exceeding internal expectations.
Management raised full-year guidance for both net sales and adjusted diluted EPS following strong first-half performance.
summary: Apogee Enterprises reported Q2 FY2027 revenue of $391 million (up 9.2% YoY) and adjusted EPS of $1.17 (up 19% YoY), driven by pricing actions, productivity gains, and acquisitions. Management raised full-year fiscal 2027 guidance for net sales to $1.46-$1.5 billion and adjusted diluted EPS to $3.00-$3.40, citing strong first-half momentum and successful integration of Kalwall.

negative_highlights: Consulting segment revenue fell 25.8% year-over-year driven by lower project volume and utilization.
On-Demand Talent revenue declined 13.2% due to volume pressures despite solid pricing.
Salaried consultant utilization dropped to high 50%s, impacting operating leverage.
positive_highlights: Adjusted SG&A expense of $40.3 million was better than the July outlook.
On-Demand Talent average bill rate increased to $145 from $140 year-over-year.
Strong performance observed in largest strategic client relationships with sequential growth.
summary: RGP reported Q1 FY2027 revenue of $98.1 million, an 18.5% decline year-over-year, with gross margin contracting to 37.4%. Adjusted SG&A expense was $40.3 million, which beat the outlook, but segment Adjusted EBITDA declined across all units due to lower volume and utilization. Management reiterated Q2 revenue guidance of $95-$100 million and maintained a cautious stance on the recovery timeline.

negative_highlights: GAAP net loss of $221 million ($0.76/share) due to non-cash warrant losses and stock-based compensation.
Adjusted EBITDA remains low at $64.4 million, significantly below the prior-year quarter's adjusted metrics.
Financing for future campuses (Polaris Forge 3, Delta Forges) is still in active discussions.
positive_highlights: Revenue surged 322% YoY to $341.9 million driven by HPC Hosting segment growth.
Successfully refinanced first campus debt at 7%, down from 9.25% on previous tranches, signaling improved credit confidence.
Projected to place over 600 MW into service in the next 12 months versus 250 MW previously.
summary: Applied Digital reported Q1 FY2027 revenue of $341.9 million, a 322% increase year-over-year driven by HPC Hosting growth to $262.6 million. The company completed financing for its first campus with a new tranche at 7%, reducing the cost of capital on existing debt. Management raised full-year guidance expectations, projecting over 600 MW placed into service over the next 12 months compared to 250 MW in the prior year.

negative_highlights: Reported net loss from continuing operations was $7 million ($0.14 per share) compared to earnings of $36.8 million a year ago.
Legacy shipments declined 1% year-over-year due to lower energy and construction volumes.
Manufacturing expenses increased 6% primarily due to higher labor, benefits, and freight costs.
positive_highlights: Legacy direct sale volumes increased 3% year-over-year, with automotive shipments up 4% and agriculture up 40%.
Heavy truck and trailer shipments increased 39% due to share gains and new business wins.
Supply remains tight in the U.S. with imports down, supporting pricing sustainability for contractual business.
summary: Worthington Steel reported Q1 FY2027 net sales of $2.7 billion and adjusted EPS of $0.57, which includes the full impact of the Kloeckner acquisition and a $43 million purchase accounting inventory step-up that reduced margins. Legacy Worthington Steel net sales grew 9% year-over-year to $954 million driven by volume gains in automotive, agriculture, and heavy truck, while energy shipments declined 31%. Management noted that reported earnings were significantly weighed down by acquisition-related expenses ($22.6M) and interest costs ($38.8M), with no specific guidance provided for the combined entity yet.

negative_highlights: DTC performance fell note weakness in of expectations due to softer traffic in the U.S. and Europe
Back-to-school campaign did not drive anticipated traffic or demand
Distribution costs were higher than expected, delaying benefits from network transformation until 2027
positive_highlights: International business grew 8% led by Asia's double-digit growth
Wholesale business increased 6% with strength across all segments
Blue Tab delivered strong double-digit growth driven by premium knitwear and elevated products
summary: Levi Strauss & Co. reported Q3 FY2026 organic revenue growth of 5% and adjusted EPS of $0.48, though DTC performance fell short due to soft U.S. traffic and weather impacts in Europe. Management noted that while recent trends have improved, the quarter's results were mixed, with specific challenges in the U.S. back-to-school campaign and distribution network transition costs. Full-year guidance was maintained at mid-single-digit revenue growth, though Q4 revenue guidance was lowered slightly due to foreign exchange headwinds.

negative_highlights: NAV per share declined $1.08 sequentially due to $8.4 million in share repurchases and markdowns on three specific credits (Exigo, Chronus, Madison Logic).
Adjusted NII decreased 2.6% quarter-over-quarter primarily due to increased interest expense from the capital structure reset.
Portfolio credit quality decreased slightly to 96% of credits in the highest category due to downgrades of Exigo, Chronus, and Madison Logic.
positive_highlights: AUM reached a record level of $1.15 billion with net positive originations of $37.1 million.
Non-accrual investments were resolved to zero following the sale of Pepper Palace and CLO F-Note.
Core BDC portfolio fair value remains within 1.6% of cost, demonstrating solid credit quality.
summary: Saratoga Investment Corp reported a sequential decline in NAV per share of $1.08 and adjusted NII of $7.4 million (down 2.6% QoQ), driven by higher interest expense from recent refinancing, excess dividend distributions exceeding net investment income, and specific portfolio markdowns totaling $15.4 million. Management highlighted record AUM of $1.15 billion and the successful refinancing of legacy debt to reduce near-term risk, while acknowledging competitive market dynamics and a challenging macroeconomic environment.

negative_highlights: Q2 pricing net of mix was roughly flat due to mix headwinds and carryover from high-end light beer portfolio repositioning.
Veracruz facility is approximately 85% complete with an expected annualized depreciation impact of $75 million (90 bps) starting in FY2028.
positive_highlights: Company was the number one dollar share gainer in beverage alcohol this quarter.
Pacifico achieved top 10 beer brand status with approximately 20% year-to-date growth rate.
summary: Constellation Brands reported Q2 FY2027 results that beat expectations, with the CEO reiterating full-year fiscal 2027 guidance of $11.20-$11.90 per share in comparable EPS. Management highlighted strong September trends driven by non-timing factors like college football and healthy distributor inventory depletions, expecting to land at the high end of the guide if these continue. The company remains disciplined on marketing spend and pricing while executing a multi-year cost improvement program.

negative_highlights: Beauty & Wellness sales declined 4.5% YoY, with declines in Revlon, Hot Tools, Honeywell, and Curlsmith offsetting growth in wellness and nail care.
Management lowered the full-year Home & Outdoor outlook due to saturation in the beverageware category and promotional pressure from competitors.
SG&A ratio increased 540 basis points to 46.4% as the company reinvested tariff refunds into packaging, inventory cleanup, and organizational restructuring.
positive_highlights: Consolidated sales grew 2.1% YoY, with Home & Outdoor sales increasing 9.2% driven by Osprey, OXO, and Hydro Flask.
Adjusted diluted EPS beat expectations due to a net pre-tax tariff refund benefit of approximately $4 million ($0.12 per share).
International sales grew 3.7%, led by new distributor partnerships in Australia and improved execution in select markets.
summary: Consolidated sales increased 2.1% to meet full-year outlook expectations, while adjusted diluted EPS came in ahead of guidance due to a net tariff refund benefit of approximately $0.12 per share. Management narrowed the full-year revenue guidance range slightly and raised consolidated EBITDA and EPS expectations to reflect the tariff benefits, though they noted pressure on discretionary categories and inventory correction needs in the second half. The company improved its net leverage ratio to 3.0x and generated $38 million in free cash flow for the first half of the fiscal year.

negative_highlights: Operating expenses rose to $17.4 million, primarily due to higher employee compensation and travel costs.
Canvys regional performance was mixed, with lower revenue in Europe offset by North American growth.
Management indicated that the IEEPA tariff refund benefit is sporadic and unlikely to repeat at the same level.
positive_highlights: Operating income improved 5x year-over-year to $5.1 million due to higher sales growth and expanded gross margin.
GES sales grew 27.1% driven by wind product adoption and a new $2 million BESS program booking.
PMT sales increased 23.1% with strong demand from semiconductor wafer fab customers.
summary: Consolidated net sales increased 18.9% to $64.9 million, driven by a 19.7% rise in Power & Microwave Technologies (PMT) and a 27.1% increase in Green Energy Solutions (GES). Gross margin expanded 360 bps to 34.6%, aided by an IEEPA tariff refund of 170 bps, while operating income surged 5x year-over-year to $5.1 million. Backlog grew to $184.4 million, up $20 million from the prior year end.

negative_highlights: Net revenue declined approximately 46% year-over-year to $15.3 million due to substantial restocking in the prior period and slower note-through.
Operating expenses increased 7% to $15.1 million, including $1.7 million in bad debt expenses related to two large international customers.
Wholesale business faced significant headwinds with reorder activity lagging behind expectations despite new retail partnerships.
positive_highlights: Adjusted gross margin expanded to approximately 65%, up from 62% in Q2, driven by operational efficiency and favorable mix.
Website sessions averaged approximately 29,000 per day in August, the highest since March, with sequential improvement in conversion rates.
Social creator ecosystem engagement increased by 95% compared to Q1, exceeding September sales targets by approximately 300%.
summary: Net revenue for the third quarter was $15.3 million, down approximately 46% from the prior year period due to declines in e-commerce sales and slower wholesale reorder activity. Adjusted gross margin improved to approximately 65%, driven by operational efficiency gains and a shift to an outsourced ammunition model, while operating expenses increased 7% to $15.1 million primarily due to new marketing investments and bad debt. Management provided no specific numerical guidance for the current quarter but expressed cautious optimism about early progress in conversion rates and inventory normalization ahead of the holiday season.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to $36 million due to increased Donlin Gold expenditures and higher G&A expenses related to the transaction.
Corporate G&A guidance was raised by $11.5-$31.2 million for the balance of FY2026, reflecting elevated legal and professional fees.
Cash on hand decreased by $26.8 million during the quarter due to funding Donlin Gold activities and corporate costs.
positive_highlights: Treasury cash balance remains robust at $343.4 million, enabling completion of the bankable feasibility study and prepayment of the Barrick promissory note.
Donlin Gold ownership consolidated to 100% via a definitive agreement with John Paulson, projected to add 16 million ounces of resources and 520,000 ounces of annual production.
Permitting status remains constructive with federal permits in place and state-level Clean Water Act certification anticipated within the coming year.
summary: NovaGold reported a Q3 FY2026 net loss of $36 million ($0.08 per share), an increase of $20.4 million from the prior year driven by higher Donlin Gold expenditures and elevated legal fees related to the proposed acquisition of 100% of Donlin Gold. Management raised corporate G&A guidance for the remainder of FY2026 by $11.5-$31.2 million to support the transaction closing, while maintaining a robust cash position of $343.4 million. The company advanced permitting and technical milestones for the Donlin Gold project, with a bankable feasibility study expected in 2027.

negative_highlights: AngioVac revenue decreased 5.9% year-over-year to $7.5 million due to tougher competition.
NanoKnife disposables declined sequentially by 20% compared to the prior quarter, attributed to seasonality following a strong Q4.
GAAP net loss widened to $7.1 million from $10.9 million in the prior year quarter.
positive_highlights: Med Tech revenue grew 13.2% to $39.9 million, now comprising 49% of total revenue.
Auryon delivered double-digit growth for the 21st consecutive quarter at $18.9 million.
NanoKnife revenue surged 29% to $8.3 million driven by record procedure volumes and a 53.5% increase in capital sales.
summary: AngioDynamics reported Q1 FY2027 revenue of $80.9 million, a 6.9% increase year-over-year driven by strong Med Tech growth (13.2%) and NanoKnife disposables (29%). Gross margin expanded 410 bps to 59.4%, aided by tariff refunds, with management maintaining full-year guidance of $336-$341 million in net sales and 54%-55% gross margin. The company also announced a leadership transition with Eric Honroth joining as CEO effective November 2nd.

negative_highlights: Sports school membership declined 0.9% year-over-year to 68,873.
Net cash provided by operating activities decreased to $1.6 million from $1.9 million in the prior year period.
Acquisition-related costs of $0.3 million impacted GAAP adjusted income from operations.
positive_highlights: Adjusted income from operations surged 105.6% year-over-year to $0.9 million.
Social business revenue grew 18.0% to $11.3 million, driven by new local government contracts.
Sports school business achieved growth in net revenue and segment profit despite a 0.9% decline in membership due to higher monthly fees.
summary: Leifras reported first-half FY2026 net revenue of $36.8 million, an 8.9% year-over-year increase, with adjusted income from operations rising 105.6% to $0.9 million. The company achieved record highs for five key metrics including net revenue and operating margin, driven by strong growth in the social business (revenue up 18.0%) and pricing adjustments in the sports school segment. Full-year FY2026 guidance remains unchanged with expected net revenue of $82.9 million-$95.7 million.

negative_highlights: Q4 guidance was lowered due to margin performance below expectations driven by higher input costs and mix headwinds.
North American beverage business faces underlying pressure as tariff benefits expire and commodity inflation ramps up.
Management expressed dissatisfaction with U.S. soft drink performance, citing a need for improved execution and increased investment.
positive_highlights: International organic revenue accelerated to 8% with global beverage volume up 3% and food volume up 1%.
North American snacks business achieved a major turnaround, moving from low single-digit negative volume growth to positive volume growth.
Hydration category in the U.S. successfully accelerated in both volume and net revenue.
summary: PepsiCo reported Q3 FY2026 organic revenue growth of 3.1% and core operating profit up 3%, driven by strong international performance (8% organic revenue growth) and a turnaround in North American snacks volume. However, management lowered Q4 guidance due to margin pressures from rising input costs, the expiration of tariff benefits in North America beverages, and higher commodity inflation as hedges roll off. Management emphasized a sense of urgency to invest in growth platforms while cutting non-growth costs and exploring strategic options like refranchising.

negative_highlights: Full-year fiscal 2027 forecast for GE engine programs was lowered to $32M-$35M after Q1 and Q2 data showed slower ramping.
Management explicitly stated the original build plan from customers is likely not being achieved as quickly as hoped.
The A320neo program delivery rate has stabilized at 27 per month rather than the target of 70-75 per month by end of 2027.
positive_highlights: Sales of $20.8 million came in within the upper end of the $19.5M-$21M guidance range.
Adjusted EBITDA of $5.3 million exceeded the $4.3M-$5.1M guidance range.
Missile system backlog and production are described as sustainable with a frenetic pace.
summary: Park Aerospace reported Q2 FY2027 sales of $20.8 million and gross margins of 34.3%, beating the upper end of guidance for both metrics. While management described missile system growth as sustainable, they lowered their full-year fiscal 2027 forecast for GE engine programs to a range of $32-$35 million after two quarters of data indicated a slower ramp than the original build plan suggested.

negative_highlights: GAAP net loss of $40 million compared to net income of $1.5 million in the prior year quarter.
International cannabis revenue declined sequentially due to disciplined prioritization of profitable growth over volume and price compression of $8.8 million.
Wellness segment margins were compressed by a one-time organic hemp seed shortage affecting e-commerce channels.
positive_highlights: Record first quarter gross profit of $77.5 million and gross margin expansion of 300 bps to 30%.
Beverage revenue increased 82% year-over-year to $101.5 million, with BrewDog becoming profitable in Q1.
International cannabis revenue grew 21% year-over-year, with EU GMP medical cannabis shipments accelerating (flower +110%, oil +150%).
summary: Tilray reported record Q1 FY2027 revenue of $257 million, up 23% year-over-year, driven by the BrewDog acquisition and strong international cannabis growth. Gross profit hit a record $77.5 million with gross margin expanding 300 bps to 30%, while beverage revenue surged 82% to $101.5 million. Management reaffirmed its fiscal 2027 adjusted EBITDA guidance of $68-$75 million despite a GAAP net loss of $40 million.

negative_highlights: Gross margin remained steady at 27.8% under pressure from a 3% increase in domestic cost of goods sold due to higher freight and transportation expenses.
Retail and Wholesale segment operating income declined 5% due to significantly higher transportation costs for cat litter products.
Fluids purification sales declined 5% year-over-year, though the CEO attributed this to volatile demand in an early-stage market rather than customer losses.
positive_highlights: Record full-year sales and net income achieved after a tough first-half comparison.
Fourth quarter revenue was record-breaking, driven by improved product mix and strong growth in animal health and agricultural products.
Co-packaged cat litter sales surged 47% for the year and 60% in Q4.
summary: Oil-Dri reported record full-year sales and net income for fiscal 2026, driven by a record fourth quarter where business-to-business sales rose 4% to $50 million and retail/wholesale increased 3% to $79 million. Gross margin remained steady at 27.8% despite higher freight costs, while operating income grew 17% year-over-year. The company highlighted historic cash generation with cash equivalents reaching $74 million and doubled its dividend payout.

negative_highlights: Fuel expense increased by $1.6 billion YoY, exceeding guidance by more than $500 million.
Non-fuel unit costs increased 7.3% over the prior year on flat capacity due to higher crew/revenue-related costs and disruptions.
The quarter faced a challenging operating environment with persistent weather and ATC delays, resulting in more than twice the historical average disruption days.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 16% YoY on flat capacity, with unit revenue growth accelerating three points sequentially to 15.4%.
Main Cabin unit revenue grew high teens for the third consecutive quarter, reflecting strong demand and pricing power.
Forward cash sales grew nearly 20% in the September quarter, the highest quarterly growth since 2022.
summary: Delta reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $17.6 billion (up 16% YoY) and earnings of $1.72 per share on an operating margin of 9.4%. Pre-tax profit of $1.5 billion was in line with last year despite a $1.6 billion increase in fuel costs, which exceeded guidance by more than $500 million. Management raised full-year pre-tax profit expectations to roughly $4.5 billion and fourth-quarter earnings guidance to $1.15-$1.65 per share.

negative_highlights: R&D expenses rose sharply to CAD 7.4 million, driven by engineering costs of CAD 5.3 million.
Net cash used in operations increased to CAD 7.2 million compared to CAD 2.4 million last year.
Certification timeline remains uncertain with a target goal set for early 2030.
positive_highlights: Net loss narrowed significantly from CAD 10.9 million in the prior year to CAD 4.1 million.
Company maintains a strong liquidity position with over CAD 70 million in cash.
Secured non-binding LOIs covering up to 200 X7s with potential value exceeding $1 billion.
summary: Horizon Aircraft reported a net loss of CAD 4.1 million (CAD 0.06 per share) for Q1 FY2027, representing an improvement from the prior period's loss of CAD 10.9 million due to lower G&A expenses and non-cash warrant gains. R&D expenses increased significantly to CAD 7.4 million as the company advanced the full-scale X7 demonstrator design, while cash on hand remains strong at over CAD 70 million. Management reiterated a target to complete the demonstrator by the end of Q1 2027 and maintain focus on engineering milestones.

negative_highlights: U.S. same-store sales growth guidance lowered to the low end of low single digits for the remainder of 2026.
U.S. unit growth outlook reduced to 125-150 stores due to pressure on franchisee profitability and a constrained development pipeline.
International same-store sales expected to be flat in 2026 due to continued pressures at Domino's Pizza Enterprises (DPE).
positive_highlights: Order count growth remained strong across delivery and carryout channels, driving global retail sales up 3.2%.
Supply chain gross margins expanded due to procurement productivity and route optimization.
Domino's maintains the number one position on DoorDash and Uber within the pizza category.
summary: Domino's reported Q3 FY2026 global retail sales growth of 3.2% (U.S. +2.1%, International +4.3%), driven by net store growth and order count expansion despite a challenging macro environment that pressured items per order. Management lowered the full-year U.S. same-store sales guidance to the low end of low single digits and reduced the annualized U.S. unit growth outlook to 125-150 stores due to franchisee profitability pressures, while maintaining long-term potential at 8,500+ stores. Operating income increased 8.5% excluding FX and one-time items, supported by strong supply chain margins and higher royalties.

negative_highlights: Net investment securities losses of $658 million in Corporate reduced reported revenue.
Expenses increased 12% year-over-year to $27.3 billion due to higher volume-related costs and wage inflation.
Management noted that evolving market conditions have recently slowed activity slightly, particularly in the Investment Bank.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 8% year-over-year to $50.9 billion, driven by markets revenue, higher deposit balances, and asset management fees.
Equities revenue surged 49% year-over-year due to continued outperformance in prime and derivatives.
Consumer deposit growth of 4% year-over-year was stronger than prior quarters, supported by a net new checking account acquisition of approximately 650,000.
summary: JPMorgan reported Q3 net income of $15.3 billion and EPS of $5.57, with revenue of $50.9 billion up 8% year-over-year. Management provided a central case full-year NII ex markets guidance of approximately $107 billion for 2027, noting that the outlook remains constructive despite recent market volatility and evolving global conditions. While business performance was strong across the franchise, executives emphasized caution regarding macro uncertainty and potential shifts in deposit betas.

negative_highlights: Commercial medical cost trends exceed initial expectations at over 11%, driven by No Surprises Act arbitration and specialty drug costs.
Medicaid margins expected to be moderately better than -1% for full year 2026, indicating continued pressure in that segment.
Optum Health Q4 outlook implies negative performance due to risk seasonality and additional investments in AI and workflow improvements.
positive_highlights: Revenue of $113 billion and adjusted EPS of $4.69 beat consensus expectations.
Full-year 2026 adjusted EPS guidance raised to at least $20.50.
Medicare Advantage Star Ratings expected to approach 75% of members in 4+ Star Plans by 2028, exceeding the industry average of 70%.
summary: UnitedHealth Group reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $113 billion and adjusted EPS of $4.69, beating expectations with a consolidated medical care ratio improvement to 88.4%. Management raised full-year 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to at least $20.50 and reaffirmed the long-term growth target of 13%-16%. While commercial trends remain elevated above initial expectations, Medicare fundamentals are strengthening and Medicaid margins are expected to be moderately better than -1% for the year.

negative_highlights: Identical sales declined 0.8%, driven by a 210 basis point headwind from pharmacy IRA impacts and brand-to-generic mix shifts.
Gross margin contracted to 26.8% (down 17 bps YoY) due to e-commerce mix shift, higher shrink from the Cyclospora outbreak, and fuel price inflation.
Management explicitly stated that current performance does not reflect the quality of assets or team capabilities, necessitating a comprehensive business review.
positive_highlights: E-commerce sales increased 11% sequentially, reflecting continued customer adoption.
Pharmacy script count growth remained strong despite headwinds from the Inflation Reduction Act and brand-to-generic mix shifts.
Operating cash flow was $1.2 billion in the first half of 2026, with free cash flow exceeding $300 million.
summary: Identical sales declined 0.8% in Q2 FY2026, while Adjusted EBITDA was $784 million and Adjusted EPS was $0.36 per share. Management stated the business performed in line with revised guidance but emphasized that results have not met expectations for sales growth, earnings, or shareholder return. Consequently, leadership paused providing an incremental financial outlook until a comprehensive turnaround plan is delivered by the fourth quarter earnings call.

negative_highlights: U.S. Consumer Cards revenues were flat due to higher partner payments and a 62% decline in non-interest revenue.
Markets revenues faced pressure from the trading environment, with derivatives revenues declining despite equities growth.
Expenses increased 3% excluding prior year notable items, driven by severance and volume-related costs.
positive_highlights: Net income rose 17% year-over-year to $5.2 billion with ROTCE improving 180 bps to 11.5%.
Services revenues surged 15% driven by broad-based growth across deposits, commercial cards, and trade loans.
Management raised full-year ROTCE guidance from the high end of 10%-11% to above 11%.
summary: Citi reported Q3 FY2026 net income of $5.2 billion and EPS of $2.85, with revenues up 8% year-over-year to $23.8 billion. Management raised full-year ROTCE guidance from the high end of 10%-11% to above 11%, citing disciplined execution and positive operating leverage despite pulling forward investments. The firm returned over $4 billion to shareholders via buybacks and dividends, while maintaining a CET1 ratio of 12.8%.

negative_highlights: MedTech operational sales growth was only 2.5%, missing internal expectations.
Adjusted EPS decreased 7.5% YoY due to approximately $7 billion in transaction costs from Firefly Bio and Sail Biomedicines.
Innovative Medicine margin declined from 44.3% to 35.4% primarily due to acquired IPR&D expenses.
positive_highlights: Innovative Medicine delivered 7.9% operational sales growth with eight brands growing double digits.
Oncology business grew approximately 17%, led by RYBREVANT (+64%) and TREMFYA (+68%).
Management raised full-year 2026 operational sales guidance to a midpoint of $100.7 billion.
summary: J&J reported Q3 operational sales of $25.4 billion (6% growth) and adjusted EPS of $2.59, beating consensus expectations driven by strong Innovative Medicine performance. Management raised full-year 2026 operational sales guidance to a range of 6.7%-7.1% (midpoint $100.7B) and tightened the earnings outlook, citing specific transaction costs from Firefly Bio and Sail Biomedicines. While MedTech missed internal expectations due to Middle East disruptions and VBP, management remains confident in long-term growth drivers like OTTAVA and new oncology launches.

negative_highlights: Equities intermediation revenues declined 7% due to lower results in mortgages, rates, and credit.
FICC intermediation revenues fell 7% as declines in mortgages and rates offset gains in currencies and commodities.
Provision for credit losses increased to $368 million due to portfolio growth and specific idiosyncratic impairments.
positive_highlights: Advisory revenues reached a quarterly record of $1.7 billion, up 18% year-over-year.
Equities financing revenues rose 96% to a record level driven by strength in Asia.
summary: Goldman Sachs reported Q3 FY2026 net revenues of $18.7 billion and EPS of $17.01, excluding a one-time charitable contribution of approximately $450 million that reduced adjusted EPS to roughly $18. The firm maintained its number one position in M&A with record advisory revenues of $1.7 billion and achieved record year-to-date financing revenues driven by strong activity in Asia. Management noted the quarter was impacted by deleveraging in equities financing, though they remain confident in their durable revenue base and strategic growth trajectory.

negative_highlights: Core net interest margin compressed 12 bps to 3.83%, down from 3.95% in Q2.
Mortgage banking revenue declined $1.3 million due to higher rates and a one-time transition expense of $719,000.
Deposit costs increased six basis points to approximately 3% on new production.
positive_highlights: Loan growth accelerated to 9.7% annualized, hitting the high end of the forecasted range.
Customer deposit growth remained robust at 11.2% annualized before broker decline.
Credit quality remains stable with an allowance coverage ratio of 1.47% and limited loss content on non-accruals.
summary: FB Financial reported Q3 FY2026 EPS of $1.20 (GAAP) and $1.21 (adjusted), with net income of $60.2 million, beating expectations driven by strong loan growth at an annualized rate of 9.7% and deposit growth of 8.8%. Management maintained a positive outlook for the franchise despite margin compression of 12 bps to 3.83% due to deposit repricing and a one-time interest income reversal on a non-accrual loan. Full-year guidance remains within the mid-to-high single-digit range for balance sheet growth, with Q4 expected to see moderated growth due to normal seasonality.

negative_highlights: Markets revenue declined modestly due to late-quarter slowdown in fixed income valuations and client activity
Non-interest income declined 1% YoY, offset by lower trading gains and lease income from the railcar business sale
Equity securities gains were minimal in Q3, expected to remain low in Q4
positive_highlights: EPS grew 13% year-over-year to $1.87
Revenue grew 2% YoY across all operating segments
Commercial Banking efficiency ratio improved to 43% from 48% a year ago
summary: Wells Fargo reported Q3 FY2026 EPS of $1.87 (up 13% YoY) and revenue growth of 2% YoY, driven by broad-based segment expansion including Wealth & Investment Management (+12%) and Commercial Banking (+6%). While Markets revenue was modestly down due to a late-quarter slowdown in fixed income valuations and client activity, the company maintained strong credit performance with charge-offs at 38 bps. Full-year 2026 net interest income guidance remains at approximately $50 billion, with Q4 expected to be slightly higher than Q3.

negative_highlights: Gross margin declined 40 basis points year-over-year to approximately 45%, primarily due to a customer mix headwind.
Pricing contribution slowed to approximately 2.4% as the company laps strong pricing actions from Q4 FY2025 and Q1 FY2026.
Receivables increased significantly with strong sales growth, particularly from larger customers with longer payment terms.
positive_highlights: Operating income increased by $90 million, marking the largest single-quarter increase in Fastenal's history.
Daily sales growth accelerated to 15.5% from 14.7% in the prior quarter.
Digital footprint reached 61.4% of sales with digital daily sales growing approximately 16%.
summary: Fastenal reported Q3 FY2026 net sales of $2.46 billion, a 15.5% year-over-year increase driven by share gains and new contract wins. Operating margin expanded 90 basis points to 21.5%, while earnings per share grew roughly 20%. Management noted that pricing contributions are slowing as the company laps strong actions from earlier in the year, but emphasized continued structural efficiency gains.

negative_highlights: Market volumes slowed in September following Labor Day due to renewed Middle East tensions and higher global interest rates.
Fixed income underwriting revenues declined compared to the prior year despite strong fixed income underwriting at $747 million.
Net interest income decreased modestly as deposits grew by nearly $30 billion sequentially, shifting the asset mix.
positive_highlights: Wealth Management delivered record revenues of over $9 billion with net new assets of $232 billion and fee-based flows of $80 billion.
Institutional Securities revenue increased 18% YoY to $10 billion, driven by a leading equities franchise at $5.8 billion.
The firm maintained a healthy excess CET1 ratio of 300 basis points, providing substantial flexibility for capital allocation.
summary: Morgan Stanley reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $20.3 billion and EPS of $3.03, beating expectations with Wealth Management delivering record revenues of over $9 billion and Institutional Securities up 18% YoY. While the quarter ended on a softer note due to geopolitical tensions and higher rates in September, management raised full-year guidance for tax rates and reiterated that overall full-year guidance remains unchanged. The firm highlighted a robust pipeline and strong client engagement across its integrated franchise.

negative_highlights: Sales and trading revenue declined due to reduced client activity and a major shift in interest rates affecting FICC micro businesses.
Investment banking revenue was lower than prior periods, with advisory and debt underwriting fees down from a strong year-ago period.
A non-tax-deductible regulatory settlement charge of $1.2 billion impacted the quarter's reported earnings.
positive_highlights: Net Interest Income grew 8% year-over-year to $16.6 billion, with the yield improving 8 basis points sequentially.
Consumer deposits increased by $31 billion quarter-over-quarter to $2 trillion, driven by non-interest-bearing growth.
Commercial loans grew across every segment, including a 22% increase in GWIM custom lending and 10% in global corporate.
summary: Bank of America reported Q3 net income of $6.9 billion ($0.91 EPS) and adjusted net income of $8.1 billion ($1.08 EPS), driven by an 8% year-over-year increase in Net Interest Income (NII) to $16.6 billion. Revenue was approximately $30 billion, up 3% year-over-year, though sales and trading revenue declined due to reduced client activity and interest rate shifts. Management raised full-year NII growth guidance to approximately 8% from a prior range of 5%-7%, citing strong deposit growth and loan expansion.

negative_highlights: HVAC and appliance end markets declined 10% due to weakness in new residential construction.
Substrate availability remains tight with lead times extending to approximately nine weeks for flat roll steel.
Q4 margins expected to face seasonal pressure as volumes typically decline during the winter months.
positive_highlights: Record quarterly sales of $486.9 million representing a 16.7% year-over-year increase.
Metal Coatings segment sales surged 22.9% driven by construction and industrial infrastructure demand.
Precoat Metals adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 100 bps to 21.2% due to facility ramp-up and pricing initiatives.
summary: AZZ reported record Q2 FY2027 sales of $486.9 million, up 16.7% year-over-year, with gross margins expanding 80 bps to 25.1%. Adjusted diluted EPS rose 29% to $2.00, driven by volume growth in Metal Coatings and Precoat Metals segments alongside pricing actions. Management raised full-year fiscal 2027 guidance for sales ($1.825B-$1.875B), adjusted EBITDA ($380M-$420M), and EPS ($7.00-$7.30) citing strong execution, the recent Seattle Galvanizing acquisition, and robust demand in infrastructure and industrial markets.

negative_highlights: Institutional index net outflows of $27 billion were concentrated in low-fee index equities.
positive_highlights: Revenue of $7.8 billion was 19% higher year over year, reaching a new record.
Operating margin reached 47.8%, up 320 basis points year over year.
Organic base fee growth of 11% marks the ninth consecutive quarter at or above the 5% target.
summary: BlackRock reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $7.8 billion (up 19% YoY) and EPS of $15.93 (up 38% YoY), driven by $205 billion in net inflows and 11% organic base fee growth. Operating margin expanded to 47.8%, up 320 bps YoY, while management raised guidance for full-year G&A expense and reiterated confidence in the 2030 plan. The company highlighted record revenue, operating income, and EPS across all segments, with strong momentum heading into the seasonally strong fourth quarter.

negative_highlights: Other fee revenue was lower due to an approximately $30 million year-over-year impact from market-related gains on strategic investments in the prior quarter.
Average non-interest-bearing deposits declined slightly sequentially, though they remained in the 10% range of total deposits.
positive_highlights: Total revenue grew 13% year-over-year to $4 billion, driven by double-digit growth in fee revenue and net interest income.
Pre-tax margin expanded 350 basis points year-over-year to 35%, reflecting strong operating leverage.
Assets under custody administration reached a record $59.2 trillion, while investment management AUM hit a record $6.3 trillion.
summary: State Street reported Q3 FY2026 results with total revenue of $4 billion (up 13% YoY) and EPS of $3.69 (up 33% YoY). The company delivered record servicing fees, management fees, and FX volumes, while expanding pre-tax margins to 35%. Management raised full-year fee revenue guidance to 13%-14% and NII growth to 15%-16%, citing strong organic momentum.

negative_highlights: Q4 gross margin guidance lowered slightly to around 57% due to ramp costs associated with capacity expansion.
Management indicated that current planned output levels for 2027 and 2028 will not fully meet customer demand, necessitating further capacity investigation.
positive_highlights: Total net sales hit a record EUR 11.7 billion, beating the high end of guidance.
Gross margin expanded to 57.5%, driven by high-margin installed base management sales exceeding guidance by EUR 0.4 billion.
Management raised full-year 2026 guidance to EUR 44-45 billion and confirmed strong demand visibility extending to 2028.
summary: ASML reported record Q3 FY2026 net sales of EUR 11.7 billion and gross margins of 57.5%, both exceeding guidance. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance to EUR 44-45 billion, citing strong demand for EUV systems (over 45% growth) and installed base management sales (50% growth). The company highlighted robust order momentum with customers securing visibility through 2028 and announced a share buyback of EUR 4.1 billion.

negative_highlights: Share repurchases are currently inactive due to SEC filing blockout period.
Lincoln acquisition is expected to degrade run-rate margin by 8-10 bps (2-3 bps for a single month).
Management declined to provide specific expense growth run rates or detailed technology cost-saving figures.
positive_highlights: Dividend was increased in Q3.
Management is confident the combined company will be better than the two separated entities.
Organic growth of checking accounts in legacy markets is described as exceptional.
summary: Management confirmed the dividend hike in Q3 but noted share repurchases are currently blocked by an SEC filing (S-4) for the Lincoln acquisition. Regarding forward guidance, management reiterated a pro forma EPS expectation of $0.27 pending transaction closure, while projecting a 2-3 bps margin impact from Lincoln if it closes in December. Management expressed confidence in organic growth capabilities and stated they do not need M&A to remain meaningful, though they remain open to strategic deals within their current footprint.

negative_highlights: Experienced substantial loan paydowns during the quarter, requiring conservative liquidity management.
Pending merger with Century Financial is currently viewed as neutral to NIM rather than an immediate accretive driver.
One-time transaction expenses of approximately $16.2 million remain to be realized in Q4.
positive_highlights: Very strong loan growth achieved despite overcoming substantial unscheduled paydowns from large customers.
Core loan yields ticked up two basis points quarter-over-quarter amidst consistent competition.
Management expressed confidence that at least 75% of merger cost savings will be realized immediately in Q4.
summary: Bank7 reported a strong Q3 FY2026 quarter characterized by very strong loan growth that exceeded appearances due to overcoming substantial unscheduled paydowns from large customers. Management highlighted disciplined pricing and balance sheet management resulting in a consistent Net Interest Margin (NIM), while noting the pending merger with Century Financial is currently viewed as neutral to margin. The company held excess liquidity higher than usual to prepare for the merger closing in November and subsequent cash deployment.

negative_highlights: Gross margin decreased 130 bps sequentially to 66.4% due to initial ramp-up of 2 nm technology.
Overseas fabs expected to cause gross margin dilution widening to 3%-4% in the next few years.
Management noted consumer and price-sensitive end markets are being challenged by rising component prices.
positive_highlights: Revenue beat high end of guidance at $46.7 billion driven by strong demand for leading-edge technologies.
Full-year 2026 revenue growth raised to ~44% YoY in U.S. dollar terms.
AI demand described as 'extremely robust' with no signs of slowdown, fueled by agentic AI adoption.
summary: Third quarter revenue increased 16.2% sequentially to $46.7 billion in U.S. dollar terms, beating the high end of guidance, though gross margin decreased 130 bps to 66.4% due to 2 nm ramp-up dilution. Management raised full-year 2026 revenue growth expectations to approximately 44% year-over-year and reiterated a capital budget of $60-64 billion for the year. Fourth quarter guidance was set between $52.3 billion and $54.3 billion, representing a 14% sequential increase.

negative_highlights: Reinsurance revenue declined 6% year-over-year due to continued softness in property reinsurance rates and a tough comparison to last year.
Primary commercial insurance rates decreased 5% globally, with double-digit declines in the Pacific region and high single-digit drops in the U.K. and Latin America.
Workforce and rewards revenue was down 1%, impacted by a challenging environment in the Middle East.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EPS grew 10% year-over-year to $2.03 driven by double-digit growth in Management Consulting (14%) and strong performance in People and Investments.
Management raised the Thrive efficiency program savings target from $400 million to $600 million, enabling increased investment in sales and technology.
Marsh accelerated the brand transition of Guy Carpenter and Mercer several months ahead of schedule due to favorable market research.
summary: Marsh reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $6.9 billion, an 8% increase year-over-year, with adjusted operating income growing 6% to $1.5 billion and adjusted EPS rising 10% to $2.03. Management raised the Thrive savings target from $400 million to $600 million by end of 2028 while maintaining full-year guidance for underlying revenue growth similar to 2025 levels and continued margin expansion. The company repurchased $500 million in stock during the quarter, bringing year-to-date buybacks to $2 billion.

negative_highlights: Cross-border take rate reduced by one basis point to 49 bps, reflecting price reductions and lower high-volume U.S. transactions due to dollar depreciation.
Gross yields on customer balances fell from 3.1% to 2.9% year-over-year due to central bank decisions.
One-off expenses of approximately $15 million related to the dual listing are included in the full-year margin guidance.
positive_highlights: Active customer base increased by 20% year-on-year to 12.5 million, with business customers growing by 32%.
Cross-border volume grew 22% year-on-year to $72 billion, while card spend rose 30% to $14 billion.
Management raised full-year net revenue guidance to the upper half of the 15%-20% range on a constant currency basis.
summary: Wise reported Q2 FY2027 net revenue of $739 million, up 21% year-over-year, driven by a 22% increase in cross-border volume to $72 billion and strong growth in cards and other revenues. Management raised full-year net revenue guidance to the upper half of the 15%-20% range on a constant currency basis, citing continued rapid growth in active customers (up 20% YoY) and business volumes. The company reiterated its investment framework targeting medium-term income before tax margins of 15%-20%, with full-year PBT margin expectations around the top of the 20-25% range.

negative_highlights: Adjusted expenses increased 9% year-over-year to $3.2 billion due to higher volume-related costs and performance-based compensation.
Cash balances decreased quarter-over-quarter by $7.1 billion as clients reinvested in markets following improving sentiment.
positive_highlights: Total net revenues reached a record $7.2 billion, up 17% year-over-year.
Adjusted EPS increased 29% year-over-year to a record $69.
Core net new assets grew 38% YoY to $190 billion, with managed investing net flows hitting a quarterly record of $24 billion.
summary: Schwab reported record Q3 FY2026 results with total net revenues of $7.2 billion and adjusted EPS of $69, representing a 17% YoY revenue increase and a 29% YoY EPS increase. Management raised full-year guidance expectations for revenue growth and NIM expansion, projecting approximately 800 bps of positive operating leverage for the year. The company highlighted strong client engagement, with 1.2 million new brokerage accounts opened and $190 billion in core net new assets attracted.

negative_highlights: Third quarter revenue declined sequentially primarily due to lower metal prices.
Aluminum shipments were lower than expected following Q2 inventory repositioning, with no repeat of the ~30,000 metric ton note-off in Q3.
Carbon costs exceeded guidance by approximately $5 million, rising from an estimated $15 million impact to just over $20 million.
positive_highlights: Achieved six year-to-date production records and increased aluminum production by approximately 15,000 metric tons sequentially.
Completed the Alumar smelter restart and delivered a significant performance recovery at the Pinjarra refinery.
Secured $2.6 billion in debt financing for the AliGroup acquisition, reducing execution risk ahead of H1 2027 closing.
summary: Third quarter revenue was $3.7 billion with net income of $483 million and adjusted EPS of $1.81, beating prior quarter earnings despite lower metal prices. Management provided a full-year outlook expecting strong operating performance in Q4 with higher production and shipments, though alumina guidance remains flat on a performance-only basis excluding market price impacts. The company secured $2.6 billion in debt financing for the AliGroup acquisition and expects to close the deal in H1 2027.

negative_highlights: Total revenue declined $313 million (5%) quarter-over-quarter as higher net interest income was more than offset by lower non-interest income.
Net interest margin decreased 2 basis points to 2.94% due to mix shifts toward lower spread, high-quality loans and increased funding costs.
Non-interest expense decreased $347 million (8%) QoQ, but excluding integration costs, underlying expenses still declined, indicating a potential slowdown in organic cost growth or one-time benefits.
positive_highlights: Adjusted diluted EPS of $5.09 beat expectations for an ordinary quarter, supported by strong organic loan growth exceeding initial year-end forecasts.
Net interest income increased $100 million (2%) driven by commercial loan growth and higher yields on assets.
Capital markets fees are up 40% year-to-date, and the company expects Q4 fee income to be up approximately 3.5% with capital markets specifically up 15% QoQ.
summary: PNC reported Q3 FY2026 adjusted net income of $2.1 billion ($5.09 per diluted share) and total revenue of $6.6 billion, which was a decrease of $313 million or 5% compared to the prior quarter due to lower non-interest income offsetting higher net interest income. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance expectations for loan growth (approx. 13.5%), net interest income (up 15.5%), and non-interest income (up 10.5%) despite a modest QoQ decline in revenue. The company returned $1.4 billion to shareholders via dividends and share repurchases, with plans to continue similar repurchases in the fourth quarter.

negative_highlights: Operating income decreased 5% sequentially from Q2 due to over $50 million in cost pressures including driver wages, fuel volatility, and medical claims.
Dedicated Contract Services results were below expectations as growth-related expenses offset solid demand.
Intermodal volume growth slowed in the West (1% transcon) due to competitive dynamics and capacity bottlenecks.
positive_highlights: Total revenue increased 20% year-over-year driven by strong demand across services.
Dedicated Contract Services (DCS) sold approximately 425 new trucks in the quarter, bringing year-to-date sales to 970 against a full-year target of 1,000-1,200.
Intermodal volumes increased 8% year-over-year with record quarterly volume despite capacity constraints.
summary: Total revenue increased 20% year-over-year, but operating income fell 5% sequentially due to over $50 million in cost headwinds from driver investments, volatile fuel prices, and higher claims/medical costs. Management noted that Q3 results were below expectations as these near-term pressures offset strong demand and growth-related expenses. While the company raised its full-year CapEx guidance to approximately $700 million due to replacement needs and growth investments, it maintained a disciplined capital allocation stance.

negative_highlights: Stock share volumes declined 24% YoY, primarily due to low-priced stocks underperforming relative to major indices.
G&A expenses increased, driven predominantly by higher advertising spend for digital customer acquisition.
Options volumes were down slightly compared to the prior year.
positive_highlights: Commissions rose 12% YoY to $602 million, marking the third consecutive quarter exceeding $600 million.
Net interest income increased 19% YoY to over $1.1 billion, driven by higher margin lending and segregated cash balances.
Pre-tax margin expanded to a record 78%, with the eighth consecutive quarter above 70%.
summary: Interactive Brokers reported near-record adjusted net revenues and record pre-tax income for Q3 FY2026, driven by a 12% rise in commissions to $602 million and a 19% increase in net interest income to over $1.1 billion. The company raised its annual dividend from $0.35 to $0.60 per share, citing confidence in its capital base and business model. Management noted that while stock share volumes were down 24% year-over-year due to a shift toward larger names, overnight trading volumes rose significantly to over 10 million trades.

negative_highlights: RAN market is broadly flat with component costs increasing due to the AI boom.
Americas sales declined 1%, driven by lower performance in Latin America.
Enterprise segment adjusted EBITA was negative SEK 0.5 billion following the divestment of iconectiv.
positive_highlights: Organic sales grew 7% year-over-year with growth in all segments except Americas.
Networks segment sales increased 9% to SEK 38.7 billion, driven by share gains in strategic markets.
Adjusted EBITA margin of 23.1% in Networks demonstrates strong operating leverage.
summary: Ericsson reported Q3 FY2026 organic sales growth of 7% driven by strong demand in strategic markets like Japan and India, though the Americas segment declined slightly. Gross margin remained stable at 48%, while EBITA margin was 17%, reflecting earnings leverage despite rising component costs. Management raised concerns about a broadly flat RAN market and increasing input costs, noting that structural price increases will take time to flow through as they are embedded in multi-year contracts.

negative_highlights: Americas 1 business declined 2.1% sequentially due to client-specific issues.
Healthcare sector declined 3.8% sequentially and 6.5% year-on-year due to U.S. policy changes.
Q3 guidance explicitly includes a sequential decline of up to -1.5% due to seasonal furloughs.
positive_highlights: Operating margin expanded 50 bps sequentially to 16.5%.
BFSI sector grew 1% sequentially and 1.3% year-on-year.
APMEA region delivered strong sequential growth of 3.1%.
summary: Wipro reported Q2 FY2027 IT services revenue of $2.61 billion, which was flat sequentially and up 0.6% year-on-year in constant currency. Operating margin expanded 50 bps to 16.5%, driven by operational improvements and rupee depreciation despite sequential declines in Americas 1 (-2.1%) and Health (-3.8%). Management provided Q3 guidance of -1.5% to +0.5% sequential growth, citing seasonal furloughs and client-specific issues as primary headwinds.

negative_highlights: Average occupancy guidance narrowed to a lower midpoint of 95.25%-95.5% due to fourth-quarter visibility.
Strategic capital revenue guidance revised down to $650 million-$660 million reflecting tempered asset management fee views.
Acquisition guidance lowered slightly to $2.1 billion-$2.3 billion and contributions/dispositions narrowed to $3.5 billion-$4.75 billion due to market caution.
positive_highlights: Same-store NOI growth of 5.7% on a net effective basis and 5.9% on a cash basis.
Rent change on rollover was 38% on a net effective basis, adding $85 million of incremental NOI.
U.S. net absorption totaled 63 million square feet in the quarter, consistent with normalized annual range.
summary: Prologis reported Q3 FY2026 core FFO of $1.60 per share and same-store NOI growth of 5.7% on a net effective basis. Management raised full-year guidance for same-store NOI growth to 5.5%-6% (cash basis 7%-7.5%) and increased development starts guidance to $6 billion-$6.75 billion, while narrowing the occupancy forecast range to 95.25%-95.5%. The company also announced that SEGRO shareholders approved the combination, with completion expected in H1 2027.

negative_highlights: Loan production softened slightly to $850 million due to conservative underwriting and late payoffs of approximately $1.01 billion.
Non-performing loans ticked up 11 basis points quarter-over-quarter, primarily driven by a single CCFG loan expected to be resolved soon.
Legacy deposit balances declined by $358 million in the quarter due to municipal outflows and acquisition-related reductions.
positive_highlights: Record adjusted earnings of $129.1 million representing an increase of $1 million from the prior quarter.
Core net interest margin expanded to 4.50%, up 3 basis points sequentially, with total NIM at 4.53%.
Tangible book value per share grew $0.03 to $15.35 despite a $65 million AOCI increase and significant buybacks.
summary: Home Bancshares reported record Q3 FY2026 adjusted earnings of $129.1 million ($0.65/share), driven by a core net interest margin expansion to 4.50% and reduced funding costs. Management highlighted stability in loan balances despite late payoffs, strong capital levels with TCE growth, and continued shareholder returns via a new dividend and active buybacks. Forward guidance remains positive with expectations for further rate-driven NII benefits and resolution of large non-performing loans.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EPS declined sequentially due to lower fee income and slightly higher provision expense.
Period-end loans decreased $5.5 billion driven by the reclassification of mortgage loans for the portfolio sale.
NIM compressed by one basis point to settle in the high 340s, with deposit costs increasing 12 bps.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EPS increased 4% year-over-year to $0.53 despite a sequential decline.
Client deposits grew by approximately $1.5 billion, offsetting a decrease in brokered CDs.
Net charge-off ratio remained stable at 22 basis points with NPLs flat at 81 bps.
summary: First Horizon reported Q3 FY2026 adjusted EPS of $0.53, a decline from the prior quarter due to lower fee income and slightly higher provision expense, though representing a 4% year-over-year increase. The company executed a strategic restructuring involving the sale of approximately $4.5 billion in residential mortgage loans, which reduced period-end loans by $5.5 billion and lowered the loan-to-deposit ratio to roughly 88%. Management provided refinements to the 2026 outlook, noting that NIM is expected to improve into the 3.50s following the transaction.

negative_highlights: Sequential loan growth was flat (1.0%) due to runoff in NDFI balances and muted commercial real estate demand.
Deposit costs increased seven basis points sequentially, though total funding costs rose only one basis point due to mix improvements.
Buyback program remains paused pending clarity on Basel III tailoring rules and loan demand.
positive_highlights: Record net revenue of $8 billion driven by an 8.7% year-over-year increase.
Capital markets revenue surged 69% year-over-year following the BTIG acquisition, contributing $226 million in fees.
Net interest margin expanded five basis points sequentially to 2.84%, with expectations for similar expansion in Q4.
summary: U.S. Bancorp reported record net revenue of $8 billion and diluted EPS of $1.34, representing an 8.7% year-over-year increase and a 10% beat on the prior quarter. Management raised full-year 2026 total net revenue guidance to 8%-9% growth (up from 5%-7%) and increased the operating leverage outlook to 300 basis points for the full year. The bank highlighted strong execution in payments, capital markets (driven by BTIG), and small business banking, while noting that loan growth was flat sequentially due to runoff in NDFI balances.

negative_highlights: Tier 1 leverage ratio declined 24 basis points sequentially to 5.7% due to capital returns.
Average deposit balances decreased 1% sequentially, with non-interest-bearing deposits down 3%.
Net interest income was down 2% quarter-over-quarter due to seasonally lower deposit balances.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 12% year-over-year to $5.7 billion, with fee revenue also up 12%.
Pre-tax margin expanded by approximately 390 basis points to 39%, generating positive operating leverage.
Securities Services revenue increased 15% year-over-year, while Issuer Services fees surged 43% driven by corporate trust and Trump Accounts.
summary: BNY reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $5.7 billion, up 12% year-over-year, with EPS of $2.34 representing a 24% increase. Pre-tax margins expanded by approximately 390 basis points to 39%, driven by strong fee growth across segments and net interest income rising 15%. Management raised its full-year 2026 outlook for operating leverage to nearly 500 bps and revenue growth to the middle of a 12%-13% range.

negative_highlights: France revenue declined 2% on a constant currency basis due to softer permanent recruitment and Right Management outplacements
Free cash flow was negative $17 million in the quarter, impacted by timing of MSP payments
No share repurchases were made in Q3
positive_highlights: Manpower brand delivered ninth consecutive quarter of growth with double-digit revenue growth in the U.S.
Experis U.S. crossed to growth in the quarter, improving from a flat result in Q2
SG&A expenses decreased 2% on a constant currency basis while revenue grew
summary: ManpowerGroup reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $4.8 billion, representing organic constant currency growth of 6% at the midpoint of guidance. Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 10 basis points year-over-year to 2.2%, also landing at the midpoint of guidance. Management raised full-year outlook expectations for Q4, projecting a 20 bps YoY EBITDA margin expansion compared to the prior run rate.

negative_highlights: Construction Solutions Group fourth quarter results were below expectations due to residential softness in certain southeastern markets.
Precast generated adjusted EBITDA of $57.1 million, which was approximately $20 million note weakness in of the number intimated on the last call.
Performance Reinforcing Steel results were lower due to an unplanned outage at the GalvaBar facility.
positive_highlights: Core EBITDA increased 35.1% year-over-year to approximately $394 million in the fourth quarter.
North America Steel Group shipments increased 7.1% sequentially with metal margin expanding $42 per ton to $652.
Construction Solutions Group net sales surged 94.5% year-over-year, and adjusted EBITDA more than doubled.
summary: CMC reported Q4 FY2026 core EBITDA of approximately $394 million (up 35.1% YoY) with a margin expansion to 14.8%, driven by strong North America Steel Group performance and Precast integration. While Construction Solutions Group results were below expectations due to residential softness in the Southeast, non-residential demand remains healthy with backlog up 3%. Management raised guidance for Q1 FY2027, expecting adjusted EBITDA to be nearly flat sequentially despite seasonal factors.

negative_highlights: A significant impairment on a large private equity-owned manufacturer resulted in $39.2 million in net charge-offs for the quarter.
Total non-interest expense rose to $121.5 million, driven by $6.2 million in merger-related costs and strategic investments.
The effective tax rate increased to 22.17% due to nondeductible merger expenses.
positive_highlights: Net interest income increased $1 million quarter-over-quarter despite a 7-point increase in deposit costs.
Adversely classified loans decreased to 2.56% of net loans, and non-performing assets fell to $86 million following the resolution of a large C&I relationship.
The bank expects its net interest margin to expand modestly over the next couple of quarters as earning assets reprice faster than liabilities.
summary: WaFd reported Q4 FY2026 net income of $56.3 million ($0.76 EPS), missing the prior quarter's $0.84 EPS due to a large $39.2 million in charge-offs and $6.2 million in merger expenses, though revenue remained stable with NII up $1 million. Management noted that excluding these one-time items, adjusted EPS would have been up 5% sequentially. The company sold $543 million of single-family loans and reclassified $429 million of multifamily loans as held for sale, reducing the loan portfolio by roughly $1 billion.

negative_highlights: Fee income declined 1% sequentially due to volatile capital markets conditions and deals pushing into Q4.
Commercial period-end loans decreased $1.5 billion (2%) sequentially, driven by planned reductions in CRE multifamily and general office paydowns.
Mortgage fees were lower due to a negative net MSR valuation result of $13 million caused by high mortgage rate volatility.
positive_highlights: Record revenue performance driven by NII growth of 2.7% sequentially and a 2 basis point expansion in Net Interest Margin to 3.19%.
Private Bank delivered strong deposit growth, ending the quarter at $18.5 billion with Client Assets increasing by $1.2 billion to $12.4 billion.
M&A fee pipeline is at record levels, and management feels very strongly about capital markets activity entering Q4.
summary: Citizens Financial Group reported Q3 FY2026 EPS of $1.41 (up 8.5% sequentially) and record revenue driven by a 2.7% sequential increase in Net Interest Income (NII). Management reiterated full-year guidance for NIM expansion to 3.23%-3.26% in Q4 and projected fee income growth of 4%-5%, citing strong M&A pipelines. The company returned $322 million to shareholders via dividends and buybacks, with the board increasing the share repurchase capacity by $1.3 billion.

negative_highlights: Net unrealized investment loss increased from $2 billion to $6.4 billion due to a significant rise in interest rates.
Business Insurance recorded a $295 million charge related to the annual asbestos review.
Renewal premium change in Personal Insurance auto was slightly negative as pricing was moderated.
positive_highlights: Core return on equity of 22.1% for the quarter and 24.1% trailing twelve months.
Net written premiums grew to a record $5.9 billion in Business Insurance, excluding property.
After-tax net investment income increased 7% to $908 million, surpassing $900 million for the first time.
summary: Travelers reported excellent Q3 FY2026 results with core income of $1.95 billion and a combined ratio improving to 86.8%. Net written premiums reached $11.5 billion, driven by strong growth in Business Insurance (4% YoY ex-Canada) and Bond & Specialty (12% YoY). Management reiterated the durability of underlying underwriting income despite moderating pricing and the sale of Canadian business.

negative_highlights: Net interest margin contracted 5 basis points to 3.65%, reflecting higher funding costs and muted asset growth benefits.
Non-interest expenses increased $44 million quarter-over-quarter, pushing the efficiency ratio up to 54.4% from 52.8%.
Criticized loans increased $245 million to $6.1 billion, with non-accrual loans rising to a 90 basis point ratio.
positive_highlights: Loan growth remained solid with average loans increasing $2.6 billion, driven by commercial real estate and consumer portfolios.
Deposit growth of $3.3 billion allowed the bank to reduce reliance on note weakness in-term borrowings by $2.8 billion.
summary: M&T Bank reported Q3 FY2026 diluted GAAP EPS of $5.04 and net income of $775 million, both missing the prior quarter's levels of $5.32 and $818 million respectively. Net interest margin declined 5 basis points to 3.65% due to higher funding costs and lower non-accrual interest, while loan growth was solid but C&I loans remained flat. Management provided Q4 guidance for taxable equivalent NII of $1.83-$1.85 billion and an efficiency ratio expected to remain elevated at 54.4%.

negative_highlights: GAAP EPS was reduced by a net $0.60 per share due to losses from AFS securities repositioning ($0.90/share) and RAC-related costs/losses.
Average loans declined $3.6 billion (1.1%) quarter-over-quarter due to the strategic sale of RAC and reduced originations in Marine, RV, and other non-core segments.
Non-interest income fell 2.9% adjusted quarter-over-quarter primarily due to a $1.4 billion loss on AFS securities sold and lower trading activity.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EPS grew 12% year-over-year to $1.16, driven by higher wealth management income ($407M, a record quarter) and improved client deposit growth (+3.6% YoY).
Strategic sale of RAC portfolio reduced consolidated non-performing loans by 28% and generated approximately $1 billion in CET1 capital.
Wealth management income reached an all-time high of $407 million, offsetting declines in investment banking and trading revenue.
summary: Truist reported Q3 FY2026 adjusted EPS of $1.16 (up 12% YoY) and revenue in line with expectations, though GAAP EPS was significantly impacted by a $0.60 per share drag from the sale of the RAC auto loan portfolio and LightStream agreement. Management executed strategic balance sheet repositioning, watching $5.5B in RAC loans and agreeing to watch $7.7B in LightStream assets, which reduced average loans but improved credit risk and capital ratios. The company provided Q4 2026 guidance for revenue of approximately $5.35 billion and expects non-interest expense to rise 2.5% YoY.

negative_highlights: No revenue or earnings reported; call focused entirely on capital raising efforts.
Total available liquidity is low at $1.9 million as of August 31st.
Financing timeline remains uncertain with no definitive commitment date provided.
positive_highlights: Cash operating expenses reduced year-over-year to $1.6 million via targeted personnel and insurance cuts.
Over 50% of the downsized India facility capacity is already committed via signed contracts and LOIs.
Total output of two facilities remains at 170,000 tons with potential for a larger second plant.
summary: Loop Industries reported Q2 FY2027 with no revenue or EPS figures disclosed in the transcript, focusing instead on a strategic reduction of its India facility capacity from 70,000 to 45,000 kilotonnes per annum. Management highlighted a year-over-year reduction in cash operating expenses to $1.6 million and stated total available liquidity stands at $1.9 million as of August 31st. The company is actively seeking financing for the downsized project with a target start date in Q1 2027, though specific funding amounts remain pending.

negative_highlights: Loan production declined significantly due to a high level of maturities and paydowns, particularly from low-rate fixed loans.
Risk spreads compressed meaningfully in several instances, leading management to decline certain deals rather than dilute standards.
No share repurchases were executed in the quarter as capital was earmarked for one-time investments and efficiency initiatives.
positive_highlights: NIM expanded 8 basis points quarter-over-quarter driven by de-leveraging and core profitability strategy.
Non-interest revenue grew faster due to successful investments in the wealth management team.
Core customer transaction account balances grew year-over-year every single quarter this year.
summary: Management acknowledged a significant decline in loan production and balance sheet contraction due to high maturities, paydowns of low-rate fixed loans ($2.1B book), and compressed risk spreads that made certain deals unattractive. While the bank successfully expanded its Net Interest Margin (NIM) by 8 bps and grew NII linked quarter through de-leveraging and repricing, immediate-term growth outlook is tempered by these environmental factors. The company maintained discipline on share repurchases to fund one-time investments in efficiency and deposit growth initiatives.

negative_highlights: Loan origination pipeline slowed in September due to higher interest rates and buyers requesting lower prices.
Recognized a $4.5 million loss on a legacy fixed-rate CMBS with no impact to book value.
Two loans on nonaccrual totaling $61 million, including one office property in Minneapolis expected to be taken into ownership.
positive_highlights: Generated distributable earnings of $44.7 million ($0.35 per share) with modest adjusted leverage of 2.5x.
Completed sale of Jacksonville office campus contributing a $31 million gain to distributable earnings.
Undepreciated book value per share increased to $13.50 from $13.44.
summary: Ladder Capital Corp reported distributable earnings of $44.7 million ($0.35 per share) for Q3 FY2026, driven by a $31 million gain on the sale of its Jacksonville office campus and continued loan growth. Management raised guidance implicitly by stating their plan is unchanged despite higher rates slowing origination pipelines, while maintaining modest adjusted leverage of 2.5x. The company repurchased $8 million of stock at a discount to book value and declared a quarterly dividend.

negative_highlights: Total non-performing assets increased to $126.2 million (0.5% of total assets) driven by one office loan entering workout status.
Fee income decreased approximately 3% quarter-over-quarter due to elevated tax prep fees in the prior period and softer mortgage banking demand.
A systems conversion project was delayed from October to February, with additional one-time expenses of $1.5 million-$2 million anticipated in Q4.
positive_highlights: Diluted EPS increased 12% year-over-year to $1.90, driven by a $15 million increase in interest income versus the prior quarter.
Non-time deposits grew by over $230 million (5.4% annualized) despite heightened competition and rising rates.
C&I loans rose 5% annually excluding runoff from an exited dealer floor plan business, supported by a healthy pipeline of $574 million.
summary: Third quarter net income was $89.7 million with diluted EPS of $1.90, representing a 12% increase over the prior quarter. The bank reported solid loan growth of $158 million and deposit growth of over $230 million in non-time deposits, while maintaining an adjusted core net interest margin of 3.76%. Management provided fourth quarter guidance anticipating modest increases in net interest income and a margin slightly north of 3.9% assuming no further Federal Reserve rate hikes.

negative_highlights: Total AUM decreased to $95.9 billion from $100 billion due to negative market movement, primarily in September.
Notified of approximately $400 million in partial account rebalancing outflows from two institutional clients unrelated to investment performance.
positive_highlights: Generated $1.6 billion of net inflows, the strongest flow period since Q4 2021.
Operating margin expanded to 37.2% driven by higher revenues and controlled expenses.
Institutional pipeline increased to $1.9 billion from $1.6 billion in the prior quarter.
summary: Cohen & Steers reported adjusted EPS of $0.89 and net income of $46.5 million for Q3 FY2026, representing a beat on the prior quarter and an 11% increase year-over-year. The company generated $1.6 billion in net inflows, marking its fifth consecutive quarter of organic growth despite a decline in total AUM to $95.9 billion due to market depreciation. Management maintained expense guidance and highlighted broad-based strength across wealth, institutional, and strategy lines.

negative_highlights: Consumer loan balances declined modestly during the quarter due to softness in residential mortgage and Regions Home Improvement Financing.
Wealth management revenue moderated from record second quarter levels, though it remained strong relative to the prior year.
A $28 million decline in market value on employee benefit assets partially offset fee revenue growth.
positive_highlights: Adjusted pre-tax, pre-provision income of $870 million delivered an adjusted return on tangible common equity of 22%.
Capital markets and treasury management each delivered record revenue during the quarter, with capital markets income increasing 23% linked quarter.
Annualized net charge-offs declined 13 basis points to 29 basis points of average loans, while business services criticized and non-performing loans continued to decline.
summary: Regions Financial reported Q3 FY2026 earnings of $611 million ($0.71 EPS) and adjusted earnings of $622 million ($0.73 EPS), beating expectations with a solid beat on revenue and margins. Management maintained full-year guidance for non-interest income growth of 3%-5% and net interest margin exit at 3.70%, while noting loan growth moderated to low single digits. The company highlighted record capital markets revenue, strong credit quality with declining charge-offs, and disciplined deposit cost management despite a higher rate environment.

negative_highlights: Net interest margin contracted to 4.18% from 4.36% QoQ, and management guided to further moderation in Q3 before recovery from Q4
Credit card portfolio declined 9.7% YoY and jewel loan sequential growth slowed amid RBI guideline realignment
Treasury recorded a loss of INR 2.3 billion versus a INR 1.5 billion gain in the prior quarter
positive_highlights: Profit after tax rose 20.1% YoY to INR 148.43 billion and PBT excluding treasury rose 23.4% to INR 199.54 billion
Net NPA ratio improved to 0.3% from 0.5% at June 30, 2026, with retail net NPA additions down to INR 11.05 billion from INR 14.39 billion a year ago
Fee income grew 20.1% YoY to INR 77.95 billion and non-interest income excluding treasury rose 12.5% YoY
summary: ICICI Bank reported Q2 FY2027 profit after tax of INR 148.43 billion, up 20.1% YoY, with profit before tax excluding treasury up 23.4% to INR 199.54 billion and core operating profit up 21.8% to INR 208.05 billion. Total deposits grew 27.1% YoY (17% excluding FCNR), loans grew 30% YoY (24.1% excluding FCNR-linked international loans), and net NPA improved to 0.3% from 0.5% QoQ. Net interest margin fell to 4.18% from 4.36% QoQ on the overseas asset mix and term deposit build, with management guiding to further moderation in Q3 before recovery from Q4. No formal earnings or revenue guidance was issued; credit cost guidance held at up to 50 bps.

negative_highlights: NIM declined to 3.32% with no outperformance versus peers despite slower corporate growth; cost of funds flat at 4.4% only because of FCNR deposit mix
