LCR at ~113% against a stated 110-120% operating band, with management acknowledging deposit outflows and reliance on non-retail deposits and CD issuance
Draft insurance norms flagged as high-impact on commission income, and PSL small/marginal farmer shortfall remains a recurring gap
positive_highlights: GNPA at 1.11%, 13 bps lower YoY, with agri GNPA broadly flat versus June and credit costs at 44 bps
Retail ex-agri EOP loan growth accelerated to 11.2% vs 9.1% in June 2026 and 7.4% in March 2026; MSME/mid-market growth at 23.5% YoY
Management called Q2 the margin bottom, guiding neutral-to-positive NIM from Q3; Kaizad Bharucha stated the trajectory is upward from next quarter
summary: HDFC Bank reported Q2 FY27 PAT of INR 19.5 billion, up 12.7% excluding trading gains, with ROA of 1.8%, GNPA of 1.11% (down 13 bps YoY) and credit costs of 44 bps. Deposits grew 18.8% YoY including a ~4pp lift from the special FCNR window and AUM grew 15.3%, while NIM fell to 3.32% and cost of funds stayed flat at 4.4%. Management called Q2 the bottom for margins and guided to a neutral-to-positive trajectory from Q3 as 70% floating-rate repricing offsets the full-quarter FCNR cost drag; retail/asset growth momentum accelerated (retail ex-agri EOP growth 11.2% vs 9.1% in June; MSME 23.5%). Leadership transition dominated the call, with Sashi Jagdishan departing, Anup Bagchi taking over and Kaizad Bharucha announcing early retirement, and the new CEO deferred strategy detail to a presentation in about a month.

negative_highlights: Reinsurance and monoline excess net premiums written declined 11.6% to $369 million, with management guiding further 10-20% shrinkage
Pre-tax cat losses of $86 million (2.7 loss ratio points) rose $7 million despite nearly double the PCS-named storm events quarter-over-quarter
Stockholders' equity was roughly flat versus year-end 2025 as unrealized investment losses rose $800 million on higher rates, and capital return was light in the quarter
positive_highlights: Current accident year loss ratio ex-cats improved 40 bps to 59.5%, bringing the accident year combined ratio ex-cats to 88.1%
Insurance segment current accident year combined ratio ex-cats improved one point to 88.3%, with pre-tax underwriting income up 10.6% to $238 million
Pre-tax net investment income rose 12% to $384 million, with new money yields 80-100 bps above the 4.7% book yield on the ~$24 billion domestic fixed income portfolio
summary: W.R. Berkley reported record Q3 underwriting profit of $296 million and operating earnings of $456 million, or $1.17 per share, with an annualized operating ROE of 18.8%. The accident-year combined ratio ex-cats improved to 88.1% as the loss ratio fell 40 bps to 59.5%, while insurance segment net premiums written grew 3.2% to $2.9 billion and reinsurance net premiums written fell 11.6% to $369 million on disciplined casualty retrenchment. Management guided insurance growth to mid-single digits or better and reinsurance to shrink 10-20% for the foreseeable, with no formal numerical guidance issued versus a prior period.

negative_highlights: Loan growth slowed to $259 million (7.1% annualized) from the prior quarter on unexpected payoffs and deals not closing, with payoff timing described as hard to estimate
Non-interest expense rose 8.8% year-over-year to $52.2 million, pushing the efficiency ratio to 30.20% from 29.65%, including ~$2 million of non-recurring costs
Large municipal deposits rolled off due to G-SIB rate competition, and a $7 million charge-off was taken on the multifamily portfolio with two-to-four quarters of liquidation expected
positive_highlights: Adjusted EPS grew 23% year-over-year to $0.80 with pre-provision net revenue up 26% on an adjusted basis
Net interest margin expanded ~5 bps excluding the prior-quarter recovery and is up 54 bps from 3.09% a year ago, with 5-7 bps of quarterly expansion guided ahead
Nonaccrual loans fell $9.6 million to $161.8 million and allowance coverage rose to 118% from 107%; non-interest-bearing deposits grew 12% year-over-year
summary: ServisFirst reported Q3 2026 net income of $87.3 million, or $0.80 per diluted share on a split-adjusted basis, up 2.6% linked-quarter and up 23% year-over-year on an adjusted basis versus $0.65. Net interest income rose 2.7% sequentially to $159.8 million, margin held at 3.63% GAAP but expanded ~5 bps excluding a prior-quarter recovery, and the efficiency ratio was 30.20%. Loans ended at $14.7 billion, up only $259 million (7.1% annualized) as payoffs ran high, though year-to-date growth topped $1 billion and the sub-90-day pipeline rose 58% sequentially. Management guided to 5-7 bps of quarterly margin expansion, a normalized expense run rate of $50-51 million per quarter, and said Houston startup losses should decline with break-even targeted in Q1-Q2 2027.

negative_highlights: Book value fell 15.4% to $10.91 from $12.90 and total economic return was negative 11.4%
Spread widening accounted for over 80% of the quarter's return drag as current coupon spreads widened nearly 20 bps to about 162 bps to seven-year swaps
Leverage rose to 9.0x shareholders' equity, largely reflecting the decline in book value
positive_highlights: Estimated book value recovered modestly to $10.95 as of late October, above the $10.91 quarter-end figure
Economic net interest spread held stable at approximately 1.18% as asset yields rose to 5.0% from 4.9%
Modeled sensitivity to a 50 bp rate rise fell to about 0.5% of common equity from 3.5% at June 30
summary: Dynex reported a 15.4% decline in book value per share to $10.91 from $12.90, with a total economic return of negative 11.4% (comprehensive loss of $1.49 per share versus income of $0.80 last quarter). Spread widening drove over 80% of the quarter's return impact, though management held positions and did not de-lever, and economic net interest spread stayed at roughly 1.18% (asset yields 5.0%, financing cost 3.82%). Management guided qualitatively toward static ROEs of about 20% in lower coupons and 25% in current coupons at wider spreads, and noted estimated book value of $10.95 as of late October. Leverage rose to 9.0x equity from the book value decline, and the company raised $384 million net of capital including a first preferred offering since 2020 ($116 million).

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to $1.3 million (-$0.14 per share) from $0.7 million (-$0.09) year-over-year
Total revenue declined slightly to $6.7 million from $6.8 million, with lower Durango product sales and royalty and marketing fees reflecting fewer franchise stores
Cash fell to $0.4 million from $1.2 million at fiscal year-end 2026, while total debt stood at $6.9 million; strategic alternatives including a potential sale are under review
positive_highlights: Gross margin improved to 8% from -0.6% year-over-year, with product and retail gross profit rising to $2.4 million from roughly breakeven
Revenue grew 9% sequentially from Q1, and August was the highest production and shipping month of the calendar year
Durango sale leaseback raised approximately $6.6 million, used to repay $6.6 million of 12% promissory notes
summary: Q2 FY2027 revenue was $6.7 million, down from $6.8 million year-over-year, though up 9% sequentially. Gross margin improved to 8% from -0.6%, but net loss widened to $1.3 million (-$0.14 per share) from $0.7 million (-$0.09). The company is conducting a strategic review of alternatives including a possible sale or merger, completed a $6.6 million Durango sale leaseback to repay 12% notes, and added a $2 million Alpine Bank loan. No formal forward guidance was provided.

negative_highlights: Net interest margin fell 4 bps QoQ to 3.23% on higher deposit costs and lower-yielding money market asset growth
Full-year 2026 operating leverage guidance cut to ~40-50 bps from 100-150 bps after the Basis acquisition
Ending loan balances declined slightly and loan growth outlook was tempered to 2%-4%, with CRE softer on competition and rates
positive_highlights: EPS of $1.78 rose 20% from $1.48 a year ago on NII and customer fee income growth
Net charge-offs were just 2 bps annualized of average loans, with classified and criticized balances down 12% and 8%
Customer deposits grew 8.8% annualized ($1.7 billion), funding a paydown of note weakness in-term FHLB borrowings
summary: Zions reported Q3 FY2026 net earnings to common of $262 million, or $1.78 per share, up 20% YoY from $1.48 and 2% sequentially on an adjusted basis. Net interest income was $684 million (up 1% QoQ, 2% YoY) while NIM fell 4 bps to 3.23% on higher deposit costs (1.59%, +11 bps) and lower-yielding asset growth; credit was exceptionally clean at 2 bps of net charge-offs. Full-year 2026 operating leverage guidance was cut to roughly 40-50 bps from 100-150 bps due to the Basis multifamily acquisition, and the loan growth outlook was tempered toward 2%-4% with CRE specifically softer. Management provided 3Q 2027 guidance of NII up 8%-12%, fee income up 6%-9%, and expenses up 4%-6%.

negative_highlights: Shipments rose only ~125,000 tons versus the ~300,000 tons outlined last quarter, hurt by automotive customer scheduling
Stelco Galvanneal line remains idled with temporary layoffs as Canadian import protection never materialized, and CAD 3.4 billion Stelco acquisition turned a negative contributor
Q3 working capital build of $160 million limited cash inflow, and 2027 CapEx steps up to just over $1 billion from $700 million
positive_highlights: Q3 adjusted EBITDA of $612 million beat the $575 million guide and more than doubled Q2's $286 million
Guidance raised: Q4 EBITDA expected at $715 million (+~$100 million) and a stated path to >$4 billion EBITDA in 2027
Unit cost fell $17/ton versus a $10/ton guide, and 2027 contract resets are expected to add more than $1 billion of year-over-year EBITDA
summary: Q3 2026 adjusted EBITDA of $612 million beat guidance of $575 million and more than doubled Q2's $286 million, driven by shipments of 4.2 million tons (up from 4.0 million), ASP of $1,177/ton (+$53 sequentially), and unit cost down $17/ton versus a $10 guide. Q4 EBITDA is guided to $715 million, and management outlined a path to more than $1 billion per quarter and over $4 billion for 2027, with contract resets contributing more than $1 billion of year-over-year EBITDA. The Burns Harbor C reline was pushed to April 2028, preserving ~500,000 tons of 2027 production, while the Stelco Galvanneal line remains idled and the USW contract and POSCO discussions are unresolved.

negative_highlights: Net interest margin fell 2 bps to 3.34% (up ~2 bps excluding the $3.1B Comerica sweep cash build that cost ~4 bps)
Capital markets fees fell 5% ($147M) on lower M&A advisory and loan syndication, and the $1.6B AOCI hit from higher rates deferred the restart of buybacks until Q4
TCE ratio was flat and tangible book value per share grew only 2% year-over-year despite the merger
positive_highlights: Adjusted PPNR grew 8% QoQ to $1.5B, with adjusted efficiency ratio improving 250 bps to 54.6%
Adjusted ROTCE of 20.6% and ROA of 1.41% already exceed the 19% ROTCE and 53% efficiency targets set at the deal announcement for 2027
Core deposits grew 3% QoQ to $236B and commercial loan production doubled year-over-year, with gross production pipelines at record levels entering Q4
summary: Fifth Third reported Q3 FY2026 EPS of $0.90 ($1.13 adjusted) with adjusted PPNR up 8% to $1.5B, adjusted revenue up 2%, and adjusted expenses down 2%. Core deposits grew 3% QoQ and loans 1%, NCOs held at 31 bps, and adjusted ROTCE reached 20.6% vs. the 19% deal target, with adjusted efficiency at 54.6% already beating the 53% target. Q4 guidance calls for 2.5%-3.5% NII growth, 9%-10% adjusted PPNR growth, NCOs of 30-35 bps, and $200-300M of buybacks; management framed Q4 as the first full-quarter baseline for the combined company and deferred 2027 guidance to January.

negative_highlights: GAAP gross margin deteriorated to -62.8% from -21.8% a year ago, and underlying gross margin excluding one-offs was still -28.7%
Adjusted EBITDA loss widened to -$1.1 billion from -$362 million a year ago, with adjusted EBITDA margin at -53.2% versus -44.3%
Liquidity is heavily reliant on a $968 million Yorkville facility expiring November 1, 2026 and about $1 billion of related-party commitments, while cash and equivalents were only $281 million
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 85.5% YoY and 32.9% QoQ to $1.2 billion, with four-wheeler deliveries up 96% YoY and two-wheeler deliveries up 311% YoY
VF 2 pre-orders exceeded 28,700 in the first three days and all-new VF 8 pre-orders exceeded 12,700 in eight days
VinFast holds approximately 38% of the Vietnam automotive market and has ranked number one for 22 consecutive months
summary: VinFast reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $1.2 billion, up 85.5% YoY and 32.9% QoQ, with deliveries of 70,085 four-wheelers (+96% YoY) and 286,000 two-wheelers (+311% YoY). GAAP gross margin was -62.8% versus -21.8% a year ago, and adjusted EBITDA was -$1.1 billion versus -$362 million a year ago, driven by an $88 million free-charging revenue deduction, revenue deferrals, and overseas sales incentives. The company did not provide formal financial guidance but stated no change to its EBITDA break-even plan and reaffirmed its 300,000 four-wheeler target, having delivered 43% of that target in H1. Liquidity of $2.3 billion includes $968 million from a Yorkville facility expiring November 1, 2026 and about $1 billion of related-party commitments, with cash and equivalents of $281 million.

negative_highlights: Nonperforming loans rose to $42.2 million, or 1.52% of loans, from $26.4 million (0.95%) as six relationships totaling $19.5 million moved to nonaccrual
EPS fell to $1.28 from $1.48 in Q2; foreclosed asset expense rose $1.7 million to $2 million and total non-interest expense increased $1.8 million to $26.3 million

Loans decreased $4 million with payoffs elevated, and management expects problem-loan paydowns to temper net loan growth near term; net charge-offs may be somewhat elevated over the next couple of quarters
positive_highlights: Net interest income reached a record $35.9 million, up $1.8 million or 5% from a year ago
NIM would have been 4.28%, up 4 bps from Q2, excluding $862,000 in nonaccrual interest reversals; management guided to a 4.27%-4.28% starting point
Loan pipeline of roughly $440 million, including $132 million committed, with most expected to close by year-end and early Q1
summary: Q3 net income was $10.1 million, or $1.28 per share, down from $1.48 in Q2, with ROA of 1.12%; nonperforming loans jumped from $26.4 million (0.95% of loans) to $42.2 million (1.52%) after six relationships totaling $19.5 million were placed on nonaccrual. Net interest income hit a record $35.9 million (+5% YoY) but NIM fell 5 bps to 4.19%, pressured by $862,000 of interest reversals; non-interest expense rose $1.8 million to $26.3 million, driven by $2 million in foreclosed asset expense. Loans declined $4 million with payoffs elevated, deposits fell $15.4 million (<1%), and guidance was largely qualitative: NIM starting point of 4.27%-4.28%, non-interest expense of $24.2-$24.6 million ex-foreclosed costs, non-interest income of $4.0-$4.2 million, and a possible slight elevation in charge-offs over the next couple of quarters. CEO John Bordelon announced retirement in January 2027 with President Darren Guidry named successor.

negative_highlights: Full-year NII growth guidance lowered to 11%-12% from 12%-14%
Loan growth outlook cut by $1 billion and total deposit growth revised down from $6 billion to $3.5-$4 billion
Mortgage banking revenue guided to ~$70 million in Q4 from $80 million, with rate lock volume down 14% YoY
positive_highlights: Non-accrual loans declined 14% ($77 million) to $485 million, driving ACL coverage of non-accruals up 22 percentage points to 118%
Non-interest income guidance raised to 18%-21% growth from 13%-17% on commercial banking fee momentum ($26 million YoY increase)
Adjusted NIM expanded 10 bps with deposit costs down $14 million; $92 million of shares repurchased in Q3 at an average of $79.78
summary: Western Alliance reported Q3 FY2026 net income of $277 million, up 6% YoY, with EPS of $2.45 (up 7.5%), PPNR up 6% to $419 million, NII up 8% to $808 million, and non-interest income up 10% to $207 million. NIM expanded 4 bps to 3.57% and adjusted NIM rose 10 bps on lower deposit costs, while non-accrual loans fell 14% to $485 million and net charge-offs declined to 30 bps. Guidance was mixed: full-year NII growth was cut to 11%-12% from 12%-14% and loan growth lowered by $1 billion, but non-interest income guidance rose to 18%-21% from 13%-17% and deposit cost guidance was trimmed to $650-$675 million. Q4 NIM is guided down 3-4 bps seasonally on warehouse deposit outflows.

negative_highlights: About $0.25 of the $0.55 EPS guidance raise and roughly $300M of Q3 free cash flow came from IEEPA cost recovery, a non-operating item
Pratt commercial OE sales fell 5% on large commercial engine mix, and Pratt margins of 10.5% included 170 bps of IEEPA benefit
Management flagged supply-chain bottlenecks (printed circuit boards, castings, rocket motors, critical minerals) as the key constraint to achieving 2x-4x munitions rate increases
positive_highlights: Full-year adjusted EPS guidance raised to $7.65-$7.75 from $7.10-$7.25, and sales guidance lifted $1.5-2B to $97-97.5B
Adjusted EPS of $2.26 rose 33% YoY and segment operating profit grew 39%, with margins expanding 310 bps
Record backlog of $340B, up 36% YoY, including ~$70B of converted multi-year munitions contracts (Tomahawk ~$23B, AMRAAM >$14B) with book-to-bill of 4.57 at defense
summary: RTX reported Q3 adjusted sales of $25B, up 12% organically with double-digit growth across commercial OE (+10%), commercial aftermarket (+16%), and defense (+10%), and adjusted EPS of $2.26, up 33% YoY (including $0.25 from IEEPA cost recovery); segment margins expanded 310 bps. Management raised full-year adjusted sales to $97-97.5B from $95-96B, adjusted EPS to $7.65-7.75 from $7.10-7.25, and free cash flow to $9-9.2B from $8.5-8.75B, with organic growth now 10-11% versus a prior 8-9%. Backlog reached a record $340B, up 36% YoY, aided by converting Tomahawk (~$23B) and AMRAAM (>$14B) framework agreements into multi-year contracts (~$70B combined), though roughly $0.25 of the EPS raise and much of the FCF lift came from IEEPA recovery rather than operations.

negative_highlights: EPS growth of 3% trailed sales growth of 7%, helped by tax benefits and offset by lower returns on marketable securities
Mission Systems and Space Systems sales grew only 2% each, well below the company average
The $68M favorable EAC adjustment in the prior-year period at MS was not repeated this year
positive_highlights: Record backlog of $110B, up 20% YoY on $16B of bookings and a 1.5x book-to-bill
Segment operating income guidance midpoint raised $65M and EPS guidance raised $0.70
Adjusted free cash flow of $1.8B, up over 40% YoY, and Aeronautics margins expanded to 10.5%
summary: Northrop reported Q3 FY2026 sales of $11.1B, up 7% YoY with growth in all four segments, and diluted EPS of $7.89 (up 3%). Segment operating income rose 5% to a 12.1% margin, and book-to-bill of 1.5x drove record backlog of $110B, up 20% YoY. Full-year sales guidance was maintained at $43.75-44.25B, but segment operating income midpoint was raised $65M to $4.94-5.04B and EPS guidance increased $0.70. 2027 outlook calls for 5-7% sales growth and 10-20 bps of margin expansion beyond the 2026 midpoint, with adjusted free cash flow of $3.3-3.7B against roughly $2.1B of CapEx tied to B-21 acceleration.

negative_highlights: Total fees and commissions declined $14 million sequentially to $188 million, driven by markets and securities revenue falling $15.2 million to $36.2 million.
Total trading revenue fell to $15 million from $25 million in Q2, with trading fees at negative $6.3 million, as an ~80 bp rise in the 10-year Treasury curtailed fixed income and mortgage activity.

Loan growth guidance of over 10% was maintained but NII growth is expected to slow materially quarter-over-quarter based on the $1.43-1.44 billion full-year guide, with management describing near-term NIM as stable.
positive_highlights: Total loans grew $646 million, or 2.4% linked quarter (9.5% annualized) and 11.5% year-over-year, led by energy lending up $264 million (8.6%) and mortgage warehouse balances up $137 million to $589 million.
Net interest margin rose 9 bps to 3.0%, with securities runoff of $770 million reinvested at ~5.1% versus ~3.3%, a yield pickup of more than 180 bps.

Credit quality remained exceptionally strong: net charge-offs of $886,000 (averaging two bps over 12 months), non-performing assets up only $3.3 million to $58 million (21 bps of loans), and no provision required.
summary: BOK Financial reported Q3 earnings of $159.9 million, or $2.64 per diluted share, with total loans up 2.4% linked quarter (9.5% annualized) and 11.5% year-over-year. Net interest margin expanded 9 bps to 3.0%, with core NIM up 8 bps, and no provision was required. However, total fees and commissions fell $14 million sequentially to $188 million as a rapid ~80 bp rise in the 10-year Treasury pressured fixed income trading (total trading revenue $15 million vs $25 million in Q2) and mortgage banking. Full-year guidance was maintained: revenue growth mid-single digits, loan growth over 10%, and NII of $1.43-1.44 billion, while expense growth guidance was tightened to ~1% from prior levels.

negative_highlights: North America revenue fell 9% YoY and 5% sequentially to $2.2 billion as the frac market did not recover as anticipated; crew moves created more downtime than expected
C&P division revenue and operating margins were both below expectations on lower North America frac and Argentina activity and a slower Saudi contract start-up
Full-year 2026 free cash flow guided to about $1.6 billion with Q3 free cash flow down from Q2, and management noted persistent Middle East logistics inflation built into 2027
positive_highlights: International revenue of $3.5 billion grew 9% YoY and 3% sequentially, with D&E beating expectations and improving operating margins 150 bps sequentially
Early 2027 outlook calls for mid-single-digit revenue growth and ~200 bps of operating margin expansion to about 15%, with roughly $250-300 million from cost savings including S/4 ramp-down
Q4 EPS guided to $0.62-$0.64, up from $0.60, on margin improvement of about 70 bps; management noted about $14 billion of work won year-to-date and ~$4 billion offshore
summary: Halliburton reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $5.7 billion with adjusted operating margin of 12.8% and adjusted EPS of $0.60; revenue exceeded expectations but C&P revenue and margins came in below plan on weaker North America frac and Argentina activity and a slower Saudi contract start-up, while D&E beat. International revenue rose 9% YoY to $3.5 billion while North America fell 9% YoY to $2.2 billion, and the company repurchased about $250 million of stock. Management issued an early 2027 view of mid-single-digit revenue growth and roughly 200 bps of operating margin expansion to about 15%, assuming flat North America and Middle East activity in line with H2 2026. For Q4, revenue is guided roughly flat near $5.7 billion with margin up about 70 bps and EPS of $0.62-$0.64.

negative_highlights: Ads business is 'a bit behind' its aggressive full-year target due to delayed partner integrations and product rollouts
U.S. engagement and slate called 'not growing as fast as it could'; management says it can 'do better'
120 bps of Q4 cost tied to largest headcount reduction since 2022; 2027 expense and margin quantification deferred to January
positive_highlights: Q3 churn improved year-on-year globally and in the U.S., and came in better than forecast
Ads business still growing over 80% this year, with demand described as strong and advertiser breadth expanding
India view hours grew 24% YoY and drove nearly 20% revenue growth; local titles cited across APAC, LATAM, EMEA
summary: Netflix reiterated full-year 2026 guidance and said all three revenue levers (member growth, pricing, ads) are working, with Q3 churn improved YoY and better than forecast globally and in the U.S. Ads growth remains above 80% for the year, but management said it is 'a bit behind' its aggressive target due to delayed rollout and partner integrations for new ad products. Headcount reductions produced about 120 bps of Q4 cost tied to restructuring, but 2027 guidance (including margin) was deferred to January; India view hours grew 24% with nearly 20% revenue growth, while U.S. engagement was called solid but needing better execution. Peter Rice was named Chief Content Officer, and management flagged the U.S. slate as the main area to improve.

negative_highlights: Overall combined ratio deteriorated to 86.2% from 85.1% as the loss ratio rose 1.3 points to 47.4%
Multiple segments contracted on competition: E&S property premium -17%, E&S casualty -10%, transportation -9% with renewal retention down nearly 10 points
GAAP net EPS fell to $0.88 from $1.35 and comprehensive earnings swung to a $36.8 million loss from $152 million of income a year ago
positive_highlights: Favorable prior-year reserve development rose to $22.9 million from $15.5 million in Q3 2025, with casualty, property and surety all contributing
Net investment income grew 13% to $46.7 million and operating cash flow rose 9% to $195 million, with new fixed-income purchases yielding 5.5%, roughly 100 bps above book yield
Surety combined ratio improved to 79.8% from 85.0% and underwriting income rose $7.3 million to $12.9 million; marine premium grew 11% and Personal Umbrella premium grew 22%
summary: RLI reported Q3 operating EPS of $0.86 vs $0.82 a year ago, a combined ratio of 86.2% (vs 85.1%), 2% gross premium growth and a 13% increase in net investment income to $46.7 million. GAAP net EPS fell to $0.88 from $1.35 on mark-to-market swings in equity securities, and a comprehensive loss of $36.8 million was recorded versus prior-year comprehensive income of $152 million. Underwriting income was $58.8 million with $22.9 million of favorable prior-year reserve development; through nine months operating EPS of $2.52 was roughly flat year over year. Management gave no formal numeric guidance but pointed to a positive 2027 reinsurance renewal and continued soft-market discipline, while flagging premium declines in E&S property (-17%), E&S casualty (-10%) and transportation (-9%).

negative_highlights: North America Automotive segment EBITDA margin fell 40 bps to 7.6%, with a $6 million absolute EBITDA decline driven by $15 million of higher freight, fuel, and rent costs plus summer merit increases.

Full-year adjusted EPS guidance was narrowed to $7.50-$7.75 (up 3.5% at midpoint) and incremental Iran conflict costs for the remainder of 2026 were raised to $30 million-$40 million from the prior $20 million-$30 million, with diesel up ~50% year-over-year.
Adjusted SG&A rose 70 bps to 29.5% of sales, with U.S. healthcare costs up ~15% and freight costs up 12%.
positive_highlights: Industrial sales rose 6% to $2.4 billion with comps up 5.5%, and Industrial segment EBITDA grew ~11% to $317 million with margin up 60 bps to 13.2%.
Gross margin expanded 70 bps to 38.1% on pricing and sourcing initiatives.
Year-to-date cash from operations was $817 million and free cash flow approximately $500 million, with $434 million returned via dividends.
summary: GPC reported Q3 FY2026 total sales of $6.5 billion, up 4.2% with a 290 bp comparable sales benefit, adjusted EPS of $2.07 (up ~5%), and adjusted EBITDA margin of 8.4% flat versus prior year. Industrial outperformed with sales up 6% (comps +5.5%) and EBITDA margin up 60 bps to 13.2%, while North America Automotive EBITDA margin fell 40 bps to 7.6% on freight, fuel, rent, and merit-wage cost inflation tied to the Iran conflict ($16 million, or $0.09 per share, in the quarter). Full-year adjusted EPS guidance was narrowed to $7.50-$7.75 from the prior range and the prior revenue outlook for Global Automotive was maintained as revised in July; incremental Iran conflict costs for the rest of the year were raised to $30 million-$40 million from the earlier $20 million-$30 million. Management flagged persistent macro pressure, heightened fuel/diesel assumptions, and cautious Q4 trading, partially offset by Industrial momentum and separation progress on track for Q1 2027.

negative_highlights: Q4 earnings and margins expected to moderate on accelerating input cost pressure and mix
North America telecom sales fell 33.8% with soft conditions expected into 2027
Agriculture international sales dropped 25.3%, with no near-term return to normal in the Middle East
positive_highlights: North America utility sales increased 23% on volume-led growth with pricing in double digits
Operating margin expanded 220 bps to 15.7% and diluted EPS rose 25.3% to $6.24
Adjusted diluted EPS guidance raised to $22.75-$23.75 and infrastructure backlog reached $1.8 billion
summary: Valmont reported Q3 FY2026 net sales of $1.1 billion, up 5.5% YoY, operating margin expanded 220 bps to 15.7%, and diluted EPS rose 25.3% to $6.24. The company reaffirmed net sales guidance of $4.3-$4.45 billion and raised adjusted diluted EPS guidance to $22.75-$23.75. North America utility sales grew 23% and coatings 13.8%, but telecom fell 33.8% and total agriculture declined 6.4% on a 25.3% international drop; management flagged accelerating steel cost inflation and expects Q4 earnings and margins to moderate from Q3 levels.

Peoples Bancorp reported Q3 2026 diluted EPS of $0.91 ($1.04 adjusted), beating the $0.93 consensus, with net interest income up 1% ($1.1 million) and NIM up 8 bps; fee-based income rose 5% and the provision for credit losses fell 24% to $3.6 million. Adjusted results exclude a $4.5 million securities loss ($0.10) and $1.5 million of acquisition costs ($0.03). Full-year 2026 guidance calls for a 4.2%-4.3% NIM, $28M-$30M quarterly fee income, $78M-$80M quarterly expense, and 6%-8% loan growth including Citizens, with 2027 NIM guided to 4.3%-4.5% and loan growth to 3%-5%. Loan balances grew only 1% annualized as $160 million of commercial payoffs offset production, and net charge-offs rose to 35 bps from 31 bps.

negative_highlights: Q3 results came in just shy of the earlier guidance range due to roughly $30M of unrealized FX and aluminum hedging mark-to-market adjustments
Aluminum operations posted a $26M operating loss; a hot strip mill coolant/surface-quality issue caused significant yield losses and several weeks of lower production
Management said second-half aluminum EBIT positive is not likely, and the hot strip mill was at 75% utilization in October against a 90% target by year-end
positive_highlights: Record quarterly steel shipments of 3.8 million tons with steel operations operating income of $1.0B, up 43% sequentially, and average note prices rising to $102/ton
Value-add spreads over hot-rolled coil recovered to over $230/ton, with roughly 80% of flat-rolled volume on contractual pricing that lags by two months, supporting expected Q4 and 2027 improvement
Fabrication operating income rose to $91M from $85M sequentially, with joist and deck order backlog 50% higher than a year ago; cash flow from operations was $846M
summary: Q3 2026 net income was $756M ($5.26/diluted share), adjusted EBITDA $1.2B on revenues of $6.5B, with record steel shipments of 3.8 million tons and steel operations operating income of $1.0B, up 43% sequentially as average watching prices rose to $102/ton. Results came in just shy of the earlier guidance range due to roughly $30M of unrealized mark-to-market aluminum hedging and FX adjustments, and aluminum operations posted a $26M operating loss as a hot strip mill surface-quality issue caused yield losses and several weeks of lower production. Management expects favorable flat-rolled pricing and value-add spreads (over $230/ton) to lift Q4 and 2027 results, but said second-half aluminum EBIT positive is not likely, with the hot strip mill at 75% utilization in October versus a 90% target by year-end. The company repurchased $591M of stock in 2026 with $216M remaining under the current program.

negative_highlights: CET1 ratio fell to 13% and TCE to 9%, both down from Q2 due to strategic actions
Mortgage business forecast down 10%-20% given higher-for-longer rate environment
Deposit costs increased modestly (total 1.69%, interest-bearing 2.31%) and could rise further with additional rate hikes
positive_highlights: Core loan growth of 10% annualized, the strongest since 2022, with production exceeding $1 billion for the second consecutive quarter
Net charge-offs of 9 basis points, improved from 7.9 million in Q2, aided by the Navitas sale
Q4 EPS guidance of $0.80-$0.83 and NIM expansion to the mid-370s, supported by securities repositioning and asset sensitivity
summary: United Community Banks reported Q3 operating EPS of $0.77, up from $0.71 in Q2, with core loan growth of 10% annualized (ex-Navitas, ex-Peach State) and core deposit growth of 8% annualized. Net interest margin held stable at 3.68% and net interest revenue rose $10.3 million sequentially; net charge-offs were just 9 basis points. Management guided Q4 EPS to $0.80-$0.83 and NIM to expand to the mid-370s, contingent on a 25bp December rate hike, reflecting a full quarter of Peach State and the securities portfolio restructuring. The quarter featured major strategic actions (Navitas sale, Peach State acquisition, securities repositioning) and an efficiency ratio of 53.1%, with capital ratios down modestly (CET1 13%, TCE 9%) but still strong.

negative_highlights: Reported EPS included roughly $0.12 from the Brooklyn building sale and margin benefited about 7 bps from non-accrual interest recoveries, so core earnings were below the headline
Non-interest income excluding the building gain declined $600,000 from Q2 on lower payoffs and loan sales
CFO said deposit betas near term will run above the roughly 50% historical level and 'funding costs will go up,' with time deposit and brokered pricing competing above 4%
positive_highlights: Net income rose 25% sequentially to $12.6 million and EPS reached $0.74, with pre-tax pre-provision income up 23% from Q2 and 25% year over year
Net interest margin expanded 10 bps to 3.16% and loan yields rose 10 bps to 6.23% while cost of funds fell 3 bps to 2.97%
Non-performing assets declined 11% in the quarter to $38.7 million (91 bps of assets), NPAs down 36% over two years, and allowance coverage of NPLs rose to 234%
summary: RBB reported Q3 FY2026 net income of $12.6 million, or $0.74 per diluted share, up 25% from the prior quarter, with return on average assets of 1.17%. Results included a $2.7 million pre-tax gain on the Brooklyn office building sale that added about $0.12 to EPS, while net interest income rose 6% sequentially to $31.8 million and NIM expanded 10 bps to 3.16%, aided by roughly 7 bps of non-accrual interest recoveries and 3 bps from an FHLB special dividend. Loans grew $90 million (11% annualized), NPAs fell 11% to 91 bps of assets, and the efficiency ratio improved to 53%. Management guided the quarterly non-interest expense run rate to about $19 million and the full-year effective tax rate to 27%, and said it expects payoffs to remain tempered while loan sales pick up in Q4.

negative_highlights: U.S. da Vinci procedure growth slowed to 10%, the lowest in some time per analyst framing, against a 16% prior-year comparison
Instrument pricing actions and China charge-code cuts expected to reduce da Vinci I&A revenue per procedure by ~3%-5% on a constant-mix basis once fully implemented
GAAP net income fell to $523 million ($1.49/share) from $704 million ($1.95) on a $450 million litigation settlement
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 22% to just over $3 billion with 84% recurring revenue, ahead of 15% total procedure growth
Non-GAAP gross margin rose 90 bps year-over-year to 68.9% excluding the $28 million tariff refund benefit
da Vinci placements rose 28% to 546 systems, including 315 da Vinci 5 units, and OUS placements grew 29% with Europe up 83%
summary: Q3 FY2026 revenue rose 22% to just over $3 billion, with 84% recurring, non-GAAP operating margin of 42% (41% excluding a $28 million tariff refund), and non-GAAP EPS up 25% to $3; total procedures grew 15% (da Vinci +14%, Ion +31%) and da Vinci placements rose 28% to 546 systems, including 315 da Vinci 5. GAAP EPS fell to $1.49 from $1.95 on a $450 million litigation settlement. The full-year procedure outlook narrowed to 14%-15% from 13.5%-15.5%, gross margin guidance rose to 68.7%-69.3% from 68%-69%, and opex growth guidance held at 11%-13%. Management quantified planned instrument pricing actions (Extended Use Program expansion plus China charge-code cuts) as a ~3%-5% constant-mix reduction in da Vinci I&A revenue per procedure, building mainly through 2027.

negative_highlights: GE9X mid-seal FAA certification still pending (targeted by end of 2026) forced fewer units assumed in the year, and GE9X losses are expected to add roughly $300 million of year-over-year headwind in 2027
Spare parts delinquency increased sequentially even as material availability improved
High fuel prices and airline capacity reduce exposure note (schedules being cut though Q3 departures up 1%) create macro pressure management flagged as a risk for the aftermarket
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 18% with operating profit up 30% and margins expanding 220 bps to 22.5%
Orders rose 49% (CES +58%) and backlog exceeded $170 billion, supporting a raised 2026 outlook and low double-digit services growth expectation for 2027
Free cash flow of $2 billion in the quarter and $6.7 billion year-to-date at 105% conversion, with full-year FCF guidance raised to $9.1-9.4 billion
summary: GE Aerospace reported Q3 2026 revenue up 18% with CES up 21% and DPT up 7%; operating profit rose 30% to $3 billion with margins expanding 220 bps to 22.5%, EPS up 36% to $2.25, and free cash flow of $2 billion. Orders grew 49% (CES +58%), backlog exceeded $170 billion. Management raised 2026 guidance across the board: revenue growth to 19-20% from high teens, operating profit to $10.9-11.0 billion (up $300 million at midpoint), EPS to $8.00-8.10 (up $0.30), and FCF to $9.1-9.4 billion; it also introduced a low double-digit commercial services growth expectation for 2027. The quarter marked the sixth consecutive period of at least 20% CES growth and the fifth consecutive quarter of at least 500 LEAP deliveries, while GE9X mid-seal certification timing pushed some units out of the year.

Atlantic Union reported Q3 2026 diluted EPS of $0.94 and adjusted operating EPS of $0.96, with ROATCE of 19.59% and an efficiency ratio of 52.7%. Average loans rose about 9.6% annualized to $28.9 billion and period-end deposits grew 6.5% annualized to $31.0 billion, but FTE NIM fell six basis points to 3.88% on higher funding costs and loan-to-deposit ended at 94.6%. Guidance moved to the low end across the board: FY NIM at the low end of 3.90%-3.95%, NII at the low end of $1.32-$1.33 billion, non-interest income at the low end of $220-$230 million, and loan growth toward the lower end of high single digits, while the net charge-off outlook was cut to under 5 basis points. Management cited higher rates slowing new construction and mortgage/swap fees, partially offset by a full quarter of the September Fed hike benefit in Q4; no 2027 outlook was given.

negative_highlights: Revenue retention over the last 12 months was ~89%, down from low-90s a year ago per analyst question
Housing market remains weak with two consecutive years without a major hurricane demand event
Premium per policy up only 2% year-over-year, partly from A-zone/X-zone mix shift
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 34% to $59.6 million and Adjusted EBITDA grew 38% to $36.8 million, a 62% margin expanded 147 bps
FY2026 revenue guidance raised for the fourth time to $204 million from $186-189 million, implying ~28% growth
New business premium up 51% year-over-year and net leverage cut to ~1.7x from ~2.9x a year ago
summary: Neptune reported Q3 revenue of $59.6 million, up 34% year-over-year, with Adjusted EBITDA of $36.8 million (up 38%) at a 62% margin, expanded 147 bps, and premium in force of $450 million, up 32%. Management raised FY2026 revenue guidance for the fourth time to $204 million (~28% growth, >61% EBITDA margin) from a prior $186-189 million, and issued initial FY2027 guidance of ~$238 million at ~61% margin, both assuming no housing recovery or above-average hurricane season. New business premium rose 51% year-over-year and net leverage fell to 1.7x from 2.9x a year earlier, while revenue retention slipped to ~89% from low-90s. Other items included a CFO transition (Cristian Melej succeeding Jim Steiner, who becomes COO) and a planned Q4 earthquake product launch.

negative_highlights: Efficiency ratio rose to ~63% from 60%, with operating non-interest expense up $2.4 million to $36.4 million including ~$1 million of Fountain equipment sale losses/write-downs
Q4 fee income guided to ~$7.5 million, softer than Q3's $8.1 million on mortgage seasonality
Delinquencies ticked up in the ~$145 million Fountain Equipment Finance book as higher diesel prices strained transportation borrowers; TCE ratio slipped to 7.8% from 8.0% on AOCI from rising rates
positive_highlights: Record operating revenue of $57.5 million and operating EPS of $1.10 on 15% annualized organic loan growth and 12% annualized core deposit growth
Operating ROA of 1.20% and operating ROATCE of 15.1%; tangible book value excluding AOCI grew 15% annualized to $30.03
New loan production yields of 6.37% for the quarter and 6.78% in September, with renewals repricing ~100-110 bps over original rates and 80-85% retention
summary: SmartFinancial reported record operating revenue of $57.5 million and operating EPS of $1.10 ($18.6 million), with 15% annualized organic loan growth ($174 million) and 12% annualized core deposit growth ($163 million). Operating ROA rose to 1.20% and operating ROATCE to 15.1%, though the quarter was aided by a $2.6 million tax benefit from purchased energy tax credits and net release items. NIM held at 3.45%, in line with guidance, and Q4 NIM is guided to remain near that level with NII growth around 3%; Q4 fee income is guided to ~$7.5 million (softer) and operating expense to $35-35.5 million. Management reiterated high-single-digit-plus loan growth guidance despite expecting higher rates to pose challenges into 2027, and flagged an efficiency ratio uptick to ~63% from 60% and a TCE ratio dip to 7.8% from 8.0% on AOCI.

negative_highlights: Q2 free cash flow was only ZAR 41 million, reflecting a ZAR 966 million H1 investment in in-vehicle IoT devices and memory plus higher receivables
Adjusted EPS grew just 12% versus 18% GAAP EPS growth, held back by a higher tax rate and finance expense
Europe subscription revenue growth slowed to 4% reported (14% constant currency) from 7%/13% in Q1, and Cartrack operating margin dipped to 28%
positive_highlights: Constant-currency Cartrack subscription revenue growth accelerated to 23% from 21% in Q1, with acceleration in every region including South Africa at 25% and Asia at 25%
Record Q2 net subscriber additions of 94,516, up 34%, driving total subscribers to ~2.9 million (+18%)
Record quarterly operating profit of ZAR 422 million (+19%) at a 46% adjusted EBITDA margin, with sales and marketing expense growth moderating to 16% from 33% in Q1
summary: Karooooo reported Q2 FY2027 total revenue up 22% to ZAR 1,640 million, subscription revenue up 20% to ZAR 1,418-1,480 million (figures vary by segment in the transcript), and record operating profit of ZAR 422 million, up 19%. Cartrack constant-currency subscription revenue growth accelerated to 23% from 21% in Q1, with acceleration across all regions and a record Q2 net adds of 94,516 (+34%). EPS rose 18% to ZAR 9.28 but adjusted EPS rose only 12% on a higher tax rate and finance expense, and Q2 free cash flow was just ZAR 41 million against a ZAR 966 million H1 investment in in-vehicle IoT devices and memory. Guidance for FY2027 was reiterated, not raised, implying accelerating constant-currency subscription revenue growth at the midpoint.

negative_highlights: Consumer electronics fell mid-teens, dragging TEBG to just 0.5% organic growth and China to down high single digits
Oil inflation estimate rose to $185 million from the prior $150-$175 million range, about 20 bps dilutive to margin rate
Q3 organic growth of 3.3% is below the 3.5%-plus full-year target, relying on just over 4% Q4 growth
positive_highlights: Adjusted EPS of $2.50 rose 12% YoY and FY26 guidance was raised to $9.10-$9.15 from $8.95-$9.10
Order trend grew high single digits with backlog up high teens YoY, and SIBG delivered 7% organic growth with orders and backlog up double digits
Gross margin expanded 230 bps YoY on productivity and pricing; pricing now expected slightly above 1.5% for the year with the back half above 2%
summary: 3M reported Q3 organic growth of 3.3% with adjusted operating margin of 26.2% (up 110 bps) and adjusted EPS of $2.50, up 12%, alongside free cash flow of $1.2 billion and $600 million returned to shareholders. Full-year EPS guidance was raised to $9.10-$9.15 from $8.95-$9.10 (about $0.10 above the prior midpoint), with organic growth still expected above 3.5% and margin of about 24.6% on the new basis. Oil inflation guidance rose to $185 million from the prior $150-$175 million range, fully offset by price but roughly 20 bps dilutive to margin rate. Organic growth of 3.3% sits below the guided full-year pace, requiring just over 4% in Q4, and consumer electronics weakened to down mid-teens within TEBG's 0.5% growth.

negative_highlights: TCE fell 173 bps to 8.05% (111 bps from the OFB cash purchase, 59 bps from OCI, 22 bps from buybacks), and management said it will likely stay on the sidelines on repurchases with 1 million shares remaining
Deposit costs rose 12 bps to 1.55% and management guided to a similar or slightly larger increase in Q4, with betas running higher than historically seen
NIM expansion of 5 bps was mostly non-core, with 4 bps from purchase accounting accretion; non-accrual loans rose $19 million to $133 million and DDA balances fell about $200 million
positive_highlights: Adjusted EPS of $1.66 rose 17% year-over-year and PPNR grew 8% year-over-year, with adjusted ROA of 1.41% and ROTCE of 16.4%
Criticized commercial loans fell $7 million to $485 million, the seventh consecutive quarterly improvement, with net charge-offs flat at 16 bps and reserves at 1.42% of loans
New bankers hired since early 2025 drove 55% of year-to-date 2026 loan growth and 77% of Q3 loan growth, with headcount at 42 net hires versus a ~50 year-end target
summary: Hancock Whitney reported Q3 FY2026 adjusted net income of $134 million or $1.66 per share, up from $127 million or $1.55 in Q2, with PPNR up 6% linked quarter to $189 million and net interest income up 7%. NIM rose 5 bps to 3.61%, though 4 bps came from One Florida purchase accounting accretion, and loan and deposit growth of 4% and 9% annualized (ex-OFB) was funded by promotional-rate deposit campaigns that pushed deposit costs up 12 bps to 1.55%. Full-year 2026 guidance was revised for NII (up 9-9.5%), fee income (up 5.5-6%), and both operating expenses and PPNR (up 8-8.5%), while loan and deposit growth guidance held at low double digits. TCE fell 173 bps to 8.05% on the OFB cash purchase, buybacks, and a 59 bp OCI hit, and management signaled it will likely pause buybacks with 1 million shares of authority remaining until rate clarity improves.

negative_highlights: Legacy Discover Card loans shrank 2.9% YoY and management expects continued contraction for several quarters before growth turns positive
Marketing expense rose 14% YoY to about $1.6 billion and management expects to lean harder into marketing in 2027, pressuring efficiency
Management flagged a likely Visa/Mastercard interchange reduction from the settlement it will plan for, with wide error bar, as an offset to remaining synergies
positive_highlights: Pre-provision earnings grew 10% linked-quarter as revenue rose 3% and non-interest expense fell 2%
Domestic card charge-off rate fell to 3.98%, down 73 bps QoQ and 65 bps YoY, aided by allowance release of $250 million in domestic card
Purchase volume grew 11% YoY and combined Discover synergies reached about $1.8 billion annualized, ahead of schedule
summary: Capital One reported Q3 2026 GAAP EPS of $5.61 ($6.69 adjusted net of Discover/Brex items), with revenue up 3% linked-quarter and non-interest expense down 2%, driving 10% pre-provision earnings growth. Domestic card purchase volume rose 11% YoY, card charge-offs fell to 3.98% (down 73 bps QoQ), and a $225 million allowance release helped results; CET1 was 13.8% with $2.6 billion of buybacks. Management flagged heavier marketing in 2027 and Q4, Discover Card loans still contracting (-2.9% YoY, brownout to persist several quarters), and a Visa/Mastercard settlement interchange hit it sees as roughly offsetting remaining synergies. No formal company-wide guidance beyond directional commentary on marketing, NIM, and discover growth timing.

negative_highlights: Commodity, logistics, and DRAM costs now expected to be a ~$2 billion full-year headwind; annualizing recent inflation implies an additional $1-$1.5 billion EBIT headwind for 2027
Full-year EBIT adjusted guidance narrowed to $14.5-$15.5 billion from $14-$16 billion, lowering the top end
GM International ex-China EBIT breakeven, down $200 million year-over-year, on a -$100 million Momenta mark-to-market and higher manufacturing and logistics costs
positive_highlights: EBIT adjusted rose 22% year-over-year to $4.1 billion and EPS diluted adjusted rose more than 30% to $3.70
North America margin expanded 2.5 points to 8.7%, returning within the 8%-10% target
Adjusted automotive free cash flow guidance raised to $11.5-$12.5 billion from $9.5-$11.5 billion, plus a new $20 billion buyback authorization
summary: GM reported record Q3 revenue of $50 billion, up 3% year-over-year, with EBIT adjusted of $4.1 billion (+22%), EPS diluted adjusted of $3.70 (+30%), and North America margin of 8.7% (+2.5 pts). Full-year EBIT adjusted guidance was narrowed to $14.5-$15.5 billion from $14-$16 billion and EPS to $12.75-$13.75 from $12-$14, while adjusted automotive free cash flow guidance was raised to $11.5-$12.5 billion from $9.5-$11.5 billion. Offsetting this, management flagged intensifying commodity, logistics, and DRAM inflation (~$2 billion full-year headwind, with a potential additional $1-$1.5 billion into 2027) and said the path forward is more challenging, conditioning 2027 growth on cost moderation. The company announced a new $20 billion multi-year buyback authorization and repurchased $2.5 billion in the quarter.

negative_highlights: About $40M of Magic sales shifted into Q3 out of Q4, so Q4 Magic is now expected to be down low-to-mid single digits
Consumer products Q3 profit included ~$48M of one-time tariff refunds, and the benefit is fully recognized in Q3 with Q4 margins stepping down
Licensing revenue of $417M year-to-date was down 4% on $26M of prior-year non-recurring items and tough Kayou My Little Pony comps
positive_highlights: Magic revenue topped $600M for the first time, up 34% to $616M, with The Hobbit the fourth best-note set in Magic history
Adjusted operating margin expanded 830 bps to 33.9% and adjusted EPS rose 73% to $2.90
Full-year outlook raised, with share repurchase target increased from $200M to $400M ($149M executed through nine months)
summary: Hasbro reported Q3 revenue of $1.6B, up 15% YoY, with adjusted operating profit of $541M (+52%), adjusted operating margin of 33.9% (+830 bps), and adjusted EPS of $2.90 (+73%). Wizards revenue rose 31% to $747M (Magic up 34% to $616M, topping $600M for the first time) and consumer products grew 4% to $828M with adjusted operating profit doubling to $178M (including ~$48M of tariff refunds). Full-year guidance was raised: consolidated revenue +7%-9% cc and Adjusted EBITDA of $1.575B-$1.625B, with Wizards revenue now +16%-18% and CP margin up to 8%-10%. Management flagged a Q4 shift of roughly $40M of Magic sales pulled into Q3, which will make Q4 Magic down low-to-mid single digits, and 2027 Wizards margins stepping to the high 30%s on video-game amortization.

negative_highlights: NPAs rose, driven by a $6 million specific C&I reserve and a multifamily charge-off; provision held at $13.8 million with $13-15 million expected for the next couple of quarters
Multifamily runoff continues at ~$500 million expected, with ~$150 million/quarter of CRE paying off, tempering overall loan growth to low-to-mid single digits
Deposit cost of funds has drifted up to ~1.72% from 1.68% at quarter end, with more creep expected on additional rate hikes
positive_highlights: NIM increased for a 10th consecutive quarter to 3.35%, with the run-rate guide raised to over 3.60% by year-end 2027 from over 3.50% previously
Revenue hit a record $135 million with core EPS of $0.91, up 53% YoY, and business loans grew ~$929 million (30% YoY)
Core efficiency ratio below 48% with ROA of 1.10%; CRE concentration reduced to 338% while repurchasing ~1% of shares
summary: Dime reported record Q3 revenue of $135 million with core EPS of $0.91, up 53% YoY, and NIM expanding 7 bps linked-quarter to 3.35% (3.32% run-rate ex purchase accounting). Management raised its out-year NIM target to over 3.60% by year-end 2027 from over 3.50% previously, on a clearer line of sight from loan repricing and a strong $1.4 billion pipeline at ~6.5%. Guidance for Q4 includes core cash opex of ~$66 million and a 28.5% tax rate, with the Empire State Bank acquisition ($600 million assets, ~3.5% EPS accretive, ~35 bps capital impact) announced concurrently. Credit showed some noise: NPA increases tied to a $6 million C&I specific reserve and a multifamily charge-off, with provisioning expected to stay elevated (~$13-15 million) for a couple more quarters, though substandard loans fell 7% linked-quarter.

negative_highlights: Lease yields included a $16 million loss on lease terminations tied to Stellantis auction prices and residuals, with pressure expected to persist into 4Q
Retail auto net charge-offs rose 32 bps QoQ to 189 bps and 30+ day delinquencies increased 6 bps YoY to 4.96%
CECL reserve builds from retail auto growth ($2.4 billion) created a ~$0.20 EPS and ~200 bps ROTCE headwind in the quarter
positive_highlights: Adjusted EPS of $1.34 rose 16% YoY and adjusted net revenue of $2.3 billion rose 9% YoY with non-interest expenses flat, producing 9% operating leverage
Average earning asset growth outlook raised to 5%-6% from 3%-5%, driven by retail auto assets up 8% and corporate finance loans up 40% YoY
Quarterly dividend increased to $0.35, the first raise since 2022; adjusted non-interest expense guide lowered to flat to up 1%
summary: Ally reported Q3 FY2026 adjusted EPS of $1.34, up 16% YoY, on adjusted net revenue of $2.3 billion, up 9% YoY, with flat non-interest expenses delivering 9% operating leverage. Net interest margin ex-OID of 3.66% rose 3 bps QoQ, and CET1 was 10.2%, up 10 bps YoY. Full-year guidance was refined rather than broadly raised: NIM now expected at 3.6%-3.65%, other revenue tightened to up 2%-4% from flat to up 5%, adjusted non-interest expense lowered to flat to up 1%, and average earning asset growth raised to 5%-6% from 3%-5%. Headwinds included a $16 million lease termination loss tied to Stellantis residuals and elevated early-life delinquency in late 2025/early 2026 vintages, while the quarterly dividend was raised to $0.35, the first increase since 2022.

Wintrust reported a seventh consecutive quarter of record net income at $239 million, up from $234 million in the prior quarter, with net interest income rising $24.2 million to $621.6 million on $2.1 billion of average earning-asset growth. Loans and deposits each grew at an 8% annualized rate (deposits up ~$1.3 billion, loans up ~$1.1 billion), NIM slipped 1 bp to 3.51%, and non-interest income fell $5.0 million to $136.3 million on lower mortgage banking revenue and a swing to securities losses. Fourth-quarter targets were unchanged: mid-to-high single-digit loan and deposit growth, stable NIM near 3.50%, and expenses roughly flat sequentially, with mid-single-digit annual expense growth reiterated for 2027. Credit stayed benign with NPLs at 0.31% of loans and charge-offs of 15 bps.

SpaceX reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $14.6B, up 161% YoY from $5.6B, with net income of $4.4B (a $5.5B swing from a $1.1B loss) and adjusted EBITDA of $8.8B, up 306% YoY. SI segment revenue reached $7.6B (up $5B QoQ and $6.7B YoY), connectivity grew 69% YoY to $5.2B, and space rose 6% YoY to $1.8B. Management reiterated its $100B ARR goal by end of 2026 and set Q1 2027 revenue guidance of $33B-$37B, while flagging Q4 capex of $35B-$40B and Q4 gross margins more consistent with Q2 due to one-time Q3 benefits. Backlog stood at $63B as of September 30, with $42B expected to be recognized within a year.

negative_highlights: Fuel costs came in ~$93M above prior guidance and ~$170M above plan for Q4, forcing a reset of the outlook; total operating expenses rose 22% YoY.
Q4 guidance implies operating margin of only 7.5%-9.5%, a sharp step down from Q3's 12% and from prior expectations, as revenue guidance fell despite higher fuel.
The stronger Mexican peso clipped ~2 percentage points of Q4 revenue growth, and CASK ex-fuel rose ~7% in Q3 after ~15% in H1, keeping non-fuel cost pressure in place.
positive_highlights: Total revenue reached a record $1.62 billion, up 13.6% YoY, with TRASM up 12% and revenue growth of $194M more than offsetting a $171M fuel increase.
Adjusted EBITDAR margin of 24% ($389M) and operating margin of 12% were delivered despite fuel prices averaging nearly $4/gallon versus $2.50 in Q3 2025.
Loyalty penetration hit a record 40% (up 8 points YoY) with redemption revenue up 27%, and a $49M breakage update boosted the quarter; international revenue rose 17.4%.
summary: Aeroméxico reported record Q3 FY2026 revenue of $1.62 billion, up 13.6% YoY, with TRASM +12%, EBIT margin of 12% ($190M operating income), and adjusted EBITDAR of $389M (24% margin) despite fuel averaging nearly $4/gallon versus $2.50 a year earlier. Full-year guidance calls for 13.5%-14.5% revenue growth, 21.5%-22.5% adjusted EBITDAR margin, and 8.5%-9.5% operating margin, with Q4 EBITDAR of 19.5%-21.5% and operating margin of 7.5%-9.5%. However, Q4 revenue guidance of ~14%-16% (16%-18% adjusting for the ~2-point FX headwind) reflects a step down from prior expectations as fuel ran ~$170M above the July guidance, and the implied Q4 operating margin of 7.5%-9.5% is well below Q3's 12%.

negative_highlights: Segment income declined to $484M from $490M despite volume growth
Middle East conflict inflation impact roughly doubled to $0.20-$0.25 for the second half versus prior $0.10 guide
Transit Packaging volumes and profits fell note weakness in of expectations, with Q4 expected to be down similar to Q3
positive_highlights: Global beverage can volumes grew more than 6%, with double-digit Asia, 6% North America and 4% Europe growth
Adjusted diluted EPS rose 7% to $2.39 and adjusted free cash flow guidance raised to at least $950M from at least $900M
Year-to-date capital returns exceeded $700M including $598M of buybacks, with leverage steady at ~2.5x
summary: Crown reported Q3 FY2026 adjusted diluted EPS of $2.39 vs $2.24 (+7%) and net sales up to $3.7B from $3.2B, driven by global beverage can volume growth of more than 6% and metal pass-through. Segment income fell to $484M from $490M, as shipments were offset by elevated input costs and weaker Transit Packaging, with Middle East conflict inflation hitting segment income by roughly $17M ($0.12 EPS). H2 conflict inflation roughly doubled versus prior guidance to $0.20-$0.25 (Q2 $0.05 plus $0.10 prior H2 estimate), and full-year EPS guidance holds at $8.35-$8.45 with Q4 $1.63-$1.73, while adjusted free cash flow guidance rose to at least $950M from $900M on better working capital. Transit Packaging results missed expectations and management remained cautious pending firm orders.

negative_highlights: Sustainability and climate saw elevated cancels including a sizable down sale, with Q4 recurring net new sales guided to roughly flat to slightly positive
Expense guidance to land at top end of 2026 ranges, with acquisitions adding ~$20 million and severance $10-15 million above plan
CEO stated 'no margin expansion' as a strategy, with only marginal 20-50 bps cushion-driven increases expected
positive_highlights: Total revenue grew 12.4% with ABF revenue up 25% and adjusted EPS up 14%
Index subscription run rate accelerated to 11.7%, with hedge funds up 32% and banks/brokers up 15%; Index retention above 97%
Recurring net new sales up 88% in PCS, 63% in Analytics, and 40% in Index versus a year earlier; LTM recurring net new sales up 26%
summary: MSCI reported Q3 FY2026 total revenue growth of 12.4%, adjusted EBITDA growth of 12%, and adjusted EPS growth of 14%, with ABF revenue up 25% and subscription revenue up 8%. Total run rate grew 12% to a record ~$1 billion ABF run rate, subscription run rate rose 9% on ~$55 million of recurring net new sales, and retention improved 30 bps to 95%. Index subscription run rate accelerated to 11.7%, PCS to 19%, Analytics to 7.5%, while real assets grew 2% and sustainability/climate faced elevated cancels with flat-to-slightly-positive Q4 net new sales guided. Management expects to land at the top end of 2026 expense guidance ranges due to acquisitions (~$20 million), performance stock accruals (~$15-20 million), and higher severance, and explicitly declined to guide margin expansion.

negative_highlights: Total passenger traffic declined 1.4% with international down 4.5%; Puerto Vallarta international fell 24.8% and Montego Bay 23%
Excluding CBX, combined aeronautical and non-aeronautical revenue grew only 3.4% and EBITDA ~8.3%, showing soft underlying growth
Full-year traffic guidance of -3% to 0% requires meaningful Q4 improvement versus the year-to-date trend; duty-free revenue fell 12.3%
positive_highlights: EBITDA grew 19.2% to MXN 6.1bn and margin expanded 350bps to 67.8%, aided by CBX consolidation and TA internalization
Non-aeronautical revenue rose 37% on CBX and directly operated businesses; cargo/bonded warehouse grew 20.7% to ~MXN 674mn
CBX users up 8.4% to ~1mn, capture rate up to 32.4% from 29.7%, contributing MXN 558mn to consolidated EBITDA
summary: Revenue ex-construction rose 13.2% and EBITDA grew 19.2% to MXN 6.1bn with margin up 350bps to 67.8%, but these gains were driven largely by CBX consolidation and technical-assistance internalization; ex-CBX organic revenue rose only 3.4% and EBITDA ~8.3%. Passenger traffic fell 1.4% (improving from -5.6% in Q2), with international down 4.5% and steep declines at Puerto Vallarta (-11%, international -24.8%), Los Cabos (-6.8%), and Montego Bay (-23%). Guidance held at -3% to 0% traffic, which management acknowledged requires meaningful Q4 improvement over the year-to-date trend; a January tariff increase of ~7% is planned toward 95% maximum-tariff fulfillment.

negative_highlights: Full-year NII growth guidance tightened to approximately 10% from a 9%-11% range, narrowing the top end
NIM guided to approximately 3% in Q4, with earning asset growth and preferred capital actions diluting NIM by roughly 2-3 bps
Middle-market M&A has yet to normalize, with deals under $1 billion down 11% this year and transactional real estate deals being retraded
positive_highlights: EPS of $0.51 up 24% YoY on record revenue over $2 billion (up 8% YoY) and record PPNR
ROTCE rose 260 bps YoY to 15.1%; NIM expanded 6 bps sequentially to 2.95% and NII grew 10% YoY
Net charge-offs improved to 32 bps and NPAs fell 19 bps to 55 bps, prompting lower full-year NCO guidance of 37-39 bps
summary: KeyCorp reported Q3 FY2026 EPS of $0.51, up 24% YoY, on record revenue exceeding $2 billion (up 8% YoY) and record PPNR; ROTCE rose 260 bps YoY to 15.1%. NIM expanded 6 bps sequentially to 2.95%, NII grew 10% YoY, and net charge-offs improved to 32 bps with NPAs down 19 bps to 55 bps. Management tightened 2026 NII growth guidance to approximately 10% from 9%-11%, raised average loan growth to approximately 5% (from 4%-5%), raised commercial loan growth to approximately 10% (from 8%-10%), and lowered the NCO range to 37-39 bps from 40-45 bps; the 3.25%+ NIM and 15%+ ROTCE targets for 4Q 2027 remain intact.

Mercantile reported Q3 2026 net income of $24.1 million, or $1.39 per diluted share, versus $23.8 million and $1.46 a year ago; adjusted EPS fell about 5% YoY to $1.42 as higher non-interest expense offset a 17% revenue increase. NIM expanded to 3.73% from 3.49%, total deposits rose 17% and commercial loans grew 9% from year-end 2025, with NPAs at just 14 bps of assets. Q4 guidance projects 5%-7% annualized loan growth, a higher NIM, a ~17% tax rate, and $1.2 million of one-time costs; no 2027 expense guidance was given. The key change versus prior periods is margin-driven revenue growth being partly absorbed by personnel investment in Southeast Michigan and core-system conversion costs.

negative_highlights: Total enrollment fell to 241,400 from 247,700 YoY, with net new enrollments declining
Adjusted EPS fell to $1.37 from $1.52 and adjusted operating income declined to $78.6 million from $81.1 million
Gross margin contracted to 37.7% from 39%, with full-year gross margin guided down 100-200 bps
positive_highlights: Revenue per enrollment rose 7% YoY to $2,556 in Q1
Adjusted EBITDA increased to $111.8 million from $108.4 million
Positive in-year enrollment activity since the September count date, with guidance assuming in-year growth in Q2 and Q3
summary: Stride reported Q1 FY2027 revenue of $639.4 million, up 3% YoY, but adjusted operating income fell to $78.6 million from $81.1 million, adjusted EPS declined to $1.37 from $1.52, and gross margin contracted to 37.7% from 39%. Total enrollment as of September 30 was 241,400, down from 247,700, driven by lower net new enrollments after application declines and platform friction, with the Lone Star program loss costing roughly 3,000 students net. Full-year guidance was set at revenue of $2.53-$2.61 billion and adjusted operating income of $500-$530 million, with gross margin expected down 100-200 bps and SG&A down 10-15%; management reiterated its fiscal 2028 targets. Management described the enrollment results as disappointing and acknowledged that Launchpad enhancements created a poor user experience during the enrollment season, while noting positive in-year enrollment activity since the count date.

negative_highlights: Full-year NII guidance was revised to $1.485-$1.5 billion, with management citing heightened deposit competition
Non-interest expense guidance expected toward the higher end of the $1.01-$1.02 billion range; occupancy up 14% and outside services up 15%
Deposits expected at the low end of mid-single-digit growth for the full year, and CRE balances fell $90 million linked-quarter on payoffs
positive_highlights: Net charge-offs improved to 12 bps from 19 bps in the prior quarter, with NPLs at 33 bps, down 4 bps year-over-year
Net interest margin expanded 4 bps sequentially to 3.29% on stable deposit costs (interest-bearing up only 1 bp)
Full-year provision guidance lowered by $5 million at the high end to $80-$90 million on favorable credit performance
summary: F.N.B. reported Q3 FY2026 net income of $153 million, or $0.43 per share, with revenue of $469 million and record net interest income of $377 million. NIM expanded 4 bps sequentially to 3.29%, loans grew 8.5% annualized and deposits 9% annualized, while net charge-offs improved to 12 bps from 19 bps. Full-year NII guidance was revised to $1.485-$1.5 billion citing heightened deposit competition, NII non-interest income tightened to $370-$380 million, expense guidance held at $1.01-$1.02 billion (toward high end), and provision guidance lowered to $80-$90 million. Buybacks totaled $51 million in the quarter and $133 million year-to-date.

negative_highlights: Full-year U.S. mortgage revenue expected about $80 million below July guidance, with Q4 mortgage revenue down mid-double digits ex-FICO
2027 mortgage market transactions guided down high single digits versus 2026, concentrated in the first eight months
Q4 EPS guided to $2.07-2.17, up only about 1.7% at midpoint, with revenue growth decelerating to about 4.5% as mortgage volumes fall
positive_highlights: Adjusted EPS of $2.26 rose 11% and came in above the high end of guidance despite the $20 million mortgage headwind
EWS government signed over $550 million in annual contract value year-to-date (about $150 million new, $400 million renewals), and diversified markets revenue grew over 8%
summary: Equifax reported Q3 revenue of $1.693 billion, up 10% reported and 9% constant currency, but slightly below the midpoint of July guidance due to roughly $20 million of September mortgage-market impact; EPS of $2.26 grew 11% and landed above the high end of guidance. Diversified markets revenue rose over 8% with margins ex-FICO up 130 bps, and full-year ex-FICO EBITDA margin guidance was raised to +100 bps from +75 bps. However, full-year U.S. mortgage revenue is now expected about $80 million below July guidance (Q4 down about $60 million), with 2027 mortgage transactions guided down high single digits across the first eight months, and Q4 revenue is guided to $1.605-1.635 billion (about 4.5% growth) with EPS of $2.07-2.17, up only about 1.7%.

negative_highlights: Economic return on tangible common equity was -12.7% with a comprehensive loss of $1.28 per common share and a $1.45 decline in tangible book value per share
Net spread and dollar roll income fell $0.03 to $0.37 per share as net interest spread narrowed 14 bps on higher funding costs
Agency MBS was the worst-performing fixed income sector, underperforming Treasuries by nearly 120 bps on a duration-matched basis
positive_highlights: Company raised $992 million of common stock through its ATM at a premium to tangible net book value
Management estimated expected ROE on new business of roughly 18%-20% given ~6.5% current coupon yields and 135/165 bp spreads
Hedge ratio reached 97% and duration gap held at 0.8 years, offsetting a full year of mortgage duration extension; tangible NAV per share was up 3% since quarter end
summary: AGNC reported a comprehensive loss of $1.28 per common share and an economic return on tangible common equity of -12.7% for Q3, as tangible net book value fell $1.45 per share on mortgage underperformance versus hedges. Net spread and dollar roll income was $0.37 per share, down $0.03 from Q2, as net interest spread narrowed 14 bps. Management issued no formal guidance but framed forward returns positively, citing expected ROE of roughly 18%-20% on new business, a 6.5% current coupon yield, and spreads near the wide end of a multi-year range; tangible NAV per share was up 3% since quarter end. The company raised $992 million of common stock via ATM at a premium to book and grew the portfolio $2.5 billion while leverage rose modestly to 7.9x.

negative_highlights: Mortgage banking revenues fell 9% sequentially and 10% year-over-year to $3.2 million on a smaller pipeline and rising rates
A $6 million Class A office loan was newly placed on non-accrual despite never missing a payment
No buyback planned; management cited a high stock price and a desire to hold capital for balance sheet growth
positive_highlights: Net interest income rose 7% sequentially and 15% year-over-year to $44.7 million, with NIM up 11 bps to 2.84%
PPNR rose 20% from Q2 and 26% year-over-year
Non-accrual loans declined to 48 bps of total loans from 78 bps after resolution of a $22.3 million office loan
summary: Q3 2026 net income was $19.4 million or $1.01 per share, up $3.4 million or $0.18 from Q2. Net interest income was $44.7 million, up 7% sequentially and 15% year-over-year, with NIM expanding 11 bps to 2.84%. Q4 NIM guidance was revised to a 285-290 range, and non-interest expense is expected to rise about $1.5 million in Q4 plus a $750,000 charitable contribution. Asset quality improved as non-accrual loans fell to 48 bps from 78 bps after a $22.3 million office loan was restructured, though a $6 million Class A loan was newly moved to non-performers.

Vicor reported Q3 FY2026 product and royalty revenue of $197.1 million, up 37.5% sequentially and 78.5% year-over-year, with royalty revenue up 119.1% sequentially to $66.6 million and consolidated gross margin up 1,030 bps sequentially to 68.3%. GAAP diluted EPS was $1.33 on net income of $63.3 million, operating cash flow was $69.7 million, and cash rose $59.6 million to $513.1 million. Q4 guidance calls for roughly 10% product revenue growth and at least $43 million in royalty revenue assuming no new license deals, with management noting $100 million in bookings in the first two weeks of Q4. One-year backlog rose 7% sequentially to $406 million, though the royalty increase included a non-recurring catch-up component tied to a new licensee.

negative_highlights: NIM declined 12 bps YoY to 15.5%, driven by lower loan receivable yield, lower liquidity portfolio yield, and asset mix
Efficiency ratio rose ~330 bps YoY to 35.9% on 10% higher other expense from operational losses, technology investment, and marketing
Provision rose $120 million to $1.3 billion on a $30 million reserve build versus a $152 million release in the prior year, and management flagged Q4 reserve cadence as the gap versus consensus
positive_highlights: Purchase volume grew 8% YoY to almost $50 billion, the highest third-quarter level in company history, with growth across all five sales platforms
Net charge-off rate fell 37 bps YoY to 4.79%, with 30+ and 90+ delinquency in line with the prior year
Full-year EPS guidance set at approximately $9.50, the high end of the original $9.10-$9.50 range, above the $9.38-$9.40 consensus cited
summary: Synchrony reported Q3 net earnings of $892 million, or $2.68 per diluted share, with ROA of 2.9% and ROTCE of 25.2%. Purchase volume rose 8% to nearly $50 billion (a record third-quarter level) and ending loan receivables grew 3% to $103 billion, while net charge-offs fell 37 bps YoY to 4.79%. Full-year 2026 EPS is now guided to approximately $9.50, the high end of the original $9.10-$9.50 range, versus roughly $9.38-$9.40 consensus. Offsets included a 12 bp YoY NIM decline to 15.5%, a 330 bp rise in the efficiency ratio to 35.9% on higher operational losses and tech spend, and a guide that implies Q4 EPS below Street on reserve cadence.

negative_highlights: Provision for credit losses rose to $45 million from $33 million QoQ, with criticized C&I loans (special mention and substandard) ticking up.
Wealth management fees declined $4 million linked quarter on lower structured product sales.
C&I balances declined modestly QoQ, driven by reductions in non-depository financial institution borrowings (over $300 million in consumer and mortgage credit).
positive_highlights: Net interest margin expanded 6 bps QoQ and NII reached a record, with full-year NII growth guidance raised to 9%-10%.
Deposits grew over $1.4 billion with average deposit cost down 2 bps QoQ; non-interest-bearing deposits rose 16% year-over-year and represent over 26% of total deposits.
Net charge-offs declined to 15 bps ($22 million) from 19 bps ($27 million) prior quarter, prompting a lowered full-year charge-off guidance of 15-20 bps; efficiency ratio improved to 34.4%.
summary: East West reported record revenue, net interest income, pre-tax pre-provision income, and diluted EPS, with net interest margin expanding 6 bps QoQ to drive NII up 9.5% year-over-year for the nine months. Deposits grew over $1.4 billion with average deposit cost down 2 bps, and loans grew 7% year-over-year led by nearly $400 million of residential mortgage growth. Management raised full-year NII growth guidance to 9%-10% (from prior expectation) and lowered full-year net charge-off guidance to 15-20 bps, while narrowing tax-credit amortization expectations; expense and fee income guidance were reaffirmed. Credit showed a modest uptick with NPAs up 1 bp to 30 bps and criticized C&I loans rising alongside a $45 million provision versus $33 million prior quarter.

negative_highlights: Full-year revenue guidance midpoint cut ~$30M and adjusted gross margin guidance lowered 60 bps to roughly flat vs 2025
Cincinnati disruption impact grew to ~$7M in Q3 with an additional $15-20M expected in Q4; full manufacturing recovery not until Q2 2027
Tissue Reconstruction fell 2.2% organically on UBM/MicroMatrix competitive pressure and slower Integra Skin share recapture; base TR guided flat in 2027
positive_highlights: Operating cash flow of $96M was a record quarter, with free cash flow of $86M and 185% adjusted conversion
Neurosurgery grew 6.5% organically despite the ~$7M Cincinnati headwind; international Specialty Surgery grew 7.8%
Leverage improved to 3.8x with $46M of debt repaid, and a $2.1B refinancing extended maturities
summary: Q3 revenue of $411.2M came in at the low end of guidance (up 2.3% reported, 2.5% organic), with an ~$7M Cincinnati flood hit; adjusted EPS was $0.59 vs $0.54 a year ago and adjusted gross margin fell to 61.1% from 62.9%. Full-year guidance was cut on October 2nd, with the revenue midpoint reduced by ~$30M to $1.634-1.654B and adjusted EPS to $2.30-$2.40, driven by a larger Cincinnati impact (~$15-20M expected in Q4) and a more measured Tissue Reconstruction outlook. Tissue Reconstruction fell 2.2% organically on UBM/MicroMatrix weakness and slow Integra Skin share recapture, offset by neurosurgery up 6.5% and international Specialty Surgery up 7.8%. Operating cash flow was a record $96M and leverage improved to 3.8x, but the new refinancing adds ~$8M interest expense in Q4 and ~$24M in 2027.

negative_highlights: $61M of DISH terminations and $5M of Sprint cancellations more than offset 3.5% organic growth in Q3
Core leasing activity expected at the bottom end of the $60-70M range due to timing shifts into 2027
$275M cash paid for residual economic interest yields only ~$4M annualized AFFO accretion
positive_highlights: FY2026 guidance increased by $20M site rental revenues, $25M Adjusted EBITDA, and $5M AFFO
$65M of annualized run-rate operating cost savings realized, contributing ~50 bps of site rental revenue margin improvement since February guidance
Discretionary CapEx raised to $240M to fund >400 ground lease buyouts in 2026, more than double 2025
summary: Crown Castle raised FY2026 guidance by $20M site rental revenues, $25M Adjusted EBITDA, and $5M AFFO, driven largely by a $275M customer agreement that adds ~$20M of straight-line revenue in Q4 and $4M annualized AFFO accretion. Q3 organic growth ex-Sprint/DISH was 3.5%, offset by $61M of DISH terminations and $17M lower straight-line revenue; full-year organic growth guidance held at 3.4% but core leasing is now expected at the low end of the $60-70M range due to timing. Management reiterated 2026 as the low point for organic growth and cited spectrum deals and edge compute as longer-term catalysts without providing 2027 guidance.
