Lam reported record September-quarter revenue of $8.22 billion, up 22% sequentially and 54% year-over-year, with record gross margin of 52.4% and operating margin of 40.2% (first time above 40%) and record non-GAAP EPS of $2.20. December-quarter guidance is $8.6 billion ± $400 million revenue, 52.5% gross margin, 40.5% operating margin, and $2.33 ± $0.15 EPS, with management stating the revenue guide would have been higher absent near-term supply chain constraints. Management raised its cumulative Aether revenue expectation to roughly $2.5 billion by decade-end (about $1 billion above prior) and guided calendar 2027 WFE to more than $200 billion from mid-$150 billion in 2026, while noting China revenue will be meaningfully lower in December. Record free cash flow of $3.24 billion funded about $1 billion of buybacks and $325 million of dividends.

negative_highlights: Full-year revenue guidance held at 4%-5% anchored to the 4% base case despite the 6% Q3 print, so the beat did not translate into a top-line raise
Consulting grew only 2% and its segment profit margin declined modestly as productivity gains were reinvested
Management expects TP's double-digit growth not to continue, guiding full-year transaction processing to flat and flagging moderation from Q3 into Q4
positive_highlights: Software revenue growth accelerated four points sequentially to 9%, with over four points of organic growth and three of four sub-segments up double digits
Red Hat grew 11% with bookings reaccelerating to high teens and OpenShift ARR growth accelerating to over 30% on a $2.4 billion base
Free cash flow growth guidance raised to more than $1 billion; first-nine-month FCF of ~$8 billion, up 8% YoY, with FCF margin the highest in reported history
summary: IBM reported Q3 FY2026 revenue growth of 6% constant currency, above the 4% base case set in July, with software +9%, infrastructure +5%, and consulting +2%; operating pre-tax margin expanded 70 bps and diluted operating EPS grew 11%. Software acceleration was helped by closing about two-thirds of the ~$400M of deals that slipped in Q2, which management said accounted for roughly a quarter of the sequential improvement. Full-year revenue guidance was kept at 4%-5% anchored to a 4% base case, while free cash flow growth guidance was raised to more than $1 billion and software growth guidance was lifted to approximately 7%-8%.

negative_highlights: Life Sciences Solutions organic growth was only 1%, with management citing a still-muted biosciences and genetic sciences reagents environment
Specialty Diagnostics reported revenue declined 6% and organic was flat; reported revenue also carried a 1% drag from the microbiology divestiture
Of the $0.26 EPS beat versus guidance, $0.15 came from one-time tariff refunds ($60 million operating income) rather than operations
positive_highlights: Revenue beat prior guidance by more than $200 million, including ~2 points of stronger organic growth, and adjusted EPS beat by $0.26
Adjusted operating margin expanded 120 bps to 24.5% with adjusted operating income up 15% to $2.97 billion
Full-year guidance raised on revenue, adjusted EPS (midpoint up $0.15) and free cash flow ($7.0-$7.5 billion); Asia Pacific and China both grew low double digits
summary: Thermo Fisher reported Q3 FY2026 revenue up 9% to $12.14 billion, with organic growth of 6% and adjusted EPS up 15% to $6.68 ($4.64 GAAP, up 9%). Adjusted operating margin expanded 120 bps to 24.5%, and revenue came in more than $200 million above prior guidance with adjusted EPS $0.26 ahead, including $0.15 from tariff refunds. Full-year guidance was raised on both top and bottom lines to revenue of $47.7-$48.2 billion (7-8% reported growth, 4% organic) and adjusted EPS of $25.13-$25.43 (10-11% growth), with free cash flow guidance also increased to $7.0-$7.5 billion. Segment mix was uneven, with Laboratory Products organic growth of 10% and Analytical Instruments up 6%, while Life Sciences Solutions organic growth was only 1% and Specialty Diagnostics organic was flat.

negative_highlights: Mortgage finance period-end loans fell $942M or 15% linked quarter to $5.4B, departing from seasonal pattern, with full-year average outlook cut to ~$5.5B from ~$6B
CRE balances down 7% linked quarter and 16% YoY, guided to ~$4.4B at year-end, with higher rates likely to weigh on Q4 transaction volume
Total deposits fell $1.2B or 4% linked quarter to $27.7B as brokered deposits declined $1.6B; Q4 NII guided flat at $270-275M and non-interest expense steps up to $205-210M
positive_highlights: Adjusted EPS of $2.35 up 8% YoY and 25% linked quarter; adjusted revenue and adjusted PPNR both records at $356.6M and $157M
Non-interest income up 19% YoY to $81.6M (23% of revenue), with investment banking and trading at a third consecutive record $46.7M and treasury product fees up 16%
Full-year non-interest income guidance raised to $295-300M from $265-290M, implying ~30% YoY growth, with Q4 fees guided to $70-75M
summary: Texas Capital reported record adjusted EPS of $2.35 (up 8% YoY, 25% QoQ), record adjusted revenue of $356.6 million (up 5% YoY) and record adjusted PPNR of $157 million, with non-interest income up 19% YoY to $81.6 million. Full-year revenue growth guidance was lifted to high single digits and non-interest income guidance raised to $295-300 million from $265-290 million, while Q4 expense guidance of $205-210 million implies full-year expense growth of 6.6%-7.2%. Mortgage finance balances fell 15% linked quarter to $5.4 billion as 30-year rates approached 7%, and CRE declined 7% linked quarter with year-end balances guided to ~$4.4 billion. The $200 million buyback authorization follows exhaustion of the prior program ($103 million repurchased at $96.99).

negative_highlights: Full-year 2026 loan growth guidance of 3%-5% is about a percentage point below the guidance given at the start of the year, implying Q4 balance retracement
About $690 million of RESG payoffs/paydowns already occurred in the first 19 days of October, with near-record or record RESG payoffs expected in Q4
Management cited a noteworthy mark-to-market adjustment on the securities portfolio; the 82 bp quarterly move in the 10-year yield was the largest in roughly three and a half decades
positive_highlights: Q3 delivered a very good quarter of loan growth, led by CIB with additional contribution from Indirect RV & Marine and Community Banking
Credit trends improved: special mention declined, and the net charge-off ratio was the lowest quarterly level of the year
Loan growth guided to 10%-12% for 2027, up roughly a point from prior upside guidance, with CIB expected to surpass RESG in balances next year
summary: Q3 FY2026 featured a very good quarter of loan growth, driven by CIB plus Indirect RV & Marine and Community Banking, while RESG had moderate-to-heavy payoffs; management guided full-year 2026 loan growth to 3%-5%, about a point below the original guidance, reflecting RESG repayments pulling forward into 2026. Q4 is expected to show a modest retracement in balances given roughly $690 million of RESG payoffs already in the first 19 days of October and the prospect of near-record or record RESG payoffs in the quarter, against 2027 guidance of 10%-12% loan growth. Credit metrics improved, with special mention declining and the net charge-off ratio the lowest quarter of the year, though charge-offs are guided to remain elevated in 2026 and 2027 before improving. Net interest income guidance assumes no further Fed moves, and management flagged a large mark-to-market adjustment on the securities portfolio from an 82 bp quarterly move in the 10-year yield, while highlighting increased capital flexibility now that the CRE ratio is below 300%.

negative_highlights: RV seasonal and transient rents fell 4.4% and 5.8% respectively, and management said it hasn't seen improvement in booking pace
Q4 RV seasonal/transient now implies roughly a 7% decline, versus the prior expectation of a flat second half
Preliminary 2027 RV annual rate growth of 4.7% came in below last year's initial figure, with management citing moderation after several years of robust growth
positive_highlights: Core NOI grew 6.7% in Q3 on revenue growth of 4.4% against expense growth of 1.3%
MH new-resident mark-to-market at 12%, with 5.6% in-place rate growth outperforming guidance midpoint
August annual RV occupancy grew 444 sites; membership net contribution rose 9.5% to $52.8 million YTD
summary: Q3 2026 normalized FFO was $0.79/share, in line with guidance, with core NOI growth of 6.7% and core community-based rental income up 5.7% (MH rate growth 5.6%). Full-year 2026 normalized FFO guidance was maintained at $3.18/share midpoint ($3.15-$3.21), with core NOI growth of 6% midpoint unchanged. Management gave early 2027 rate assumptions of 5.1% for MH and 4.7% for RV annual, both excluding occupancy gains and mark-to-market, and flagged a softer RV seasonal/transient outlook that trimmed the Q4 view versus the prior flat assumption. Occupancy grew 99 sites in the quarter (166 YTD).

OFG reported Q3 EPS of $1.33, up 15% year-over-year on 1% growth in total core revenues. Core revenues fell $4.5 million to $186 million from Q2 due partly to the absence of $4.1 million in commercial loan prepayment income, while non-interest expenses dropped $6.6 million to $96 million on the absence of $5.8 million in prior-quarter operational charges. NIM came in at 5.23% and management guided to ~5.25% for the balance of 2026, with the provision moving to $18-20 million and full-year expenses near $385 million. The company resumed buybacks with $13.5 million repurchased and $180 million remaining, and reiterated low single-digit full-year loan growth.

negative_highlights: GAAP operating income fell 37% to $13 billion (20% margin) on a $9.9 billion legal charge, and free cash flow was negative $2.1 billion
Full-year 2026 expense outlook was raised to $175-179 billion, and Q3 total expenses rose 68% to $51.6 billion on infrastructure and third-party AI token costs
Reality Labs Q3 revenue fell 6% to $443 million on lower Quest headset sales, and no 2027 revenue or expense guidance was provided
positive_highlights: Total revenue rose 26% YoY to $64.6 billion with average price per ad up 14% and ad impressions up 10%
Family of apps other revenue grew 59% to $1.1 billion on WhatsApp paid messaging and subscriptions; Meta One passed 15 million subscriptions and trials
Reality Labs losses expected to narrow to about $15 billion next year, and 66,000 employees represents a 12% headcount decline from Q2
summary: Q3 total revenue was $64.6 billion, up 26% YoY on both reported and constant currency, with family of apps ad revenue of $63.1 billion (+26%) on 10% impression growth and a 14% increase in average price per ad. GAAP operating income fell 37% to $13 billion (20% margin) and net income was $9.9 billion, or $3.83 per share, driven by a $9.9 billion multi-state AG legal charge and a 68% rise in total expenses to $51.6 billion; excluding the legal charge, operating income would have risen 11%. Q4 revenue is guided to $73-76 billion (1% FX headwind), full-year expense outlook was raised to $175-179 billion to absorb the legal charge, and 2026 CapEx was narrowed to $135-145 billion; free cash flow was negative $2.1 billion against $34.9 billion of CapEx. Management also said Reality Labs losses should narrow to about $15 billion next year and announced a two-for-one non-voting stock split via stock dividend expected to trade in late January 2027.

negative_highlights: Non-performing loans and leases ratio rose to 5.61% sequentially, largely tied to renewable energy credits being worked to completion
Net charge-offs were $52 million in the quarter, including $20.3 million in commercial finance
positive_highlights: Loans and leases grew 9% year over year and originations increased from $1.3 billion to $2.2 billion, driven by credit sponsorship growth
Adjusted net interest margin improved to 551 bps in Q4 on earning-asset mix and repricing
FY2026 net income of $175.7 million, $8.14 diluted EPS, 230 bps ROA and 32.9% return on average tangible equity
summary: Pathward reported FY2026 net income of $175.7 million, or $8.14 diluted EPS, with ROA of 230 bps and return on average tangible equity of 32.9%; Q4 adjusted net interest margin improved to 551 bps and loans grew 9%, while non-performing loans rose sequentially to 5.61% and net charge-offs were $52 million (of which $20.3 million in commercial finance). Full-year loan originations rose to $2.2 billion from $1.3 billion. Management reiterated FY2027 guidance of $9.50-$10.00 per share, assuming no additional rate changes, an 18%-22% effective tax rate, and $5-$7 million of quarterly secondary market revenue, and expects credit to normalize as it works down NPLs.

negative_highlights: Non-IFRS cloud gross margin fell 0.7pp to 74.3%, with model costs, hardware prices, and acquisitions cited as headwinds
Cloud revenue growth included roughly 1 point of one-off benefit from a revenue recognition catch-up, and Q4 implied cloud growth decelerates to about 23% from 25%
Management called the 2027 revenue acceleration more challenging on macro uncertainty, a higher 2026 base, and expected further services revenue declines (services already down 5%)
positive_highlights: Cloud backlog reached EUR 24.1B, up 26% in constant currency, stable versus Q2's growth rate
Total revenue crossed EUR 10B for the first time, up 12%, with cloud ERP suite revenue up 28% and 89% of cloud revenue
Non-IFRS operating profit rose 18% to over EUR 3B and non-IFRS EPS rose 19% to EUR 1.89, with EUR 1.7B free cash flow
summary: SAP reported Q3 FY2026 cloud backlog of EUR 24.1B up 26%, cloud revenue of EUR 6.7B up 25% (roughly 1 point of one-off benefit), total revenue of EUR 10.3B up 12% (first quarter above EUR 10B), and non-IFRS operating profit above EUR 3B up 18%, with non-IFRS EPS up 19% to EUR 1.89. Guidance now aims toward the upper end of the prior 2026 cloud and cloud-plus-software revenue range while backlog, operating profit, and free cash flow guidance were reaffirmed. Management reiterated the 2027 total revenue acceleration goal but flagged it as more challenging given political/macro uncertainty skewing to the largest booking quarter, Q4, continued planned services revenue declines, and a higher 2026 bar, and said below-guidance cloud gross margin (74.3%, down 0.7pp) needs offsetting levers.

negative_highlights: Fiber ARPU declined 4% YoY and management guided to a similar decline in Q4, citing introductory pricing and converged discounts.
Net debt to adjusted EBITDA rose to 3.13x from 2.68x after the $23B EchoStar spectrum purchase, with return to ~2.5x not expected until 2029.
Q4 adjusted EBITDA growth will be pressured by higher marketing/customer acquisition costs and ~$100M of unfavorable vendor dispute settlements; legacy service revenue fell ~25% YoY.
positive_highlights: Consolidated service revenue grew 3.8% YoY, the best performance in more than four years, with total revenue up 5.3%.
Adjusted EPS of $0.65 rose 20% YoY, and full-year adjusted EPS guidance was raised to ~$2.40 from $2.25-$2.35 on lower depreciation.
Advanced Connectivity service revenue rose 6.1% and EBITDA 7.3%, with record combined advanced home internet net adds of 696,000 (416,000 fiber, 280,000 Internet Air).
summary: AT&T reported Q3 FY2026 total revenue growth of 5.3% YoY, service revenue growth of 3.8%, adjusted EBITDA growth of 5.4% and a 38.7% adjusted EBITDA margin, described as its highest third-quarter margin since refocusing on advanced connectivity. Adjusted EPS of $0.65 rose 20% YoY, and full-year adjusted EPS guidance was raised to ~$2.40 from $2.25-$2.35 on lower depreciation from held-for-sale accounting for AT&T Mexico. Management raised the adjusted EBITDA growth outlook to the upper portion of 3%-4% but flagged Q4 pressure from higher marketing costs and ~$100M of unfavorable vendor dispute settlements, while fiber ARPU fell 4% YoY and net debt/EBITDA rose to 3.13x from 2.68x after the $23B EchoStar spectrum purchase. Advanced Connectivity service revenue grew 6.1% with EBITDA up 7.3%, record combined fiber and Internet Air net adds of 696,000, and 379,000 postpaid phone net adds.

negative_highlights: A $6M increase in incentive comp accrual cut Q3 operating profit and ~100 bps of adjusted margin; adjusted EPS fell $0.02 sequentially
Institutional revenue declined 2% YoY, with management saying timing of pipeline conversion to revenue remains difficult to predict
Net investment gains in variable interest entities fell $8M QoQ and LSV assets slipped 1% on $5B of net outflows; a $32.5M Stratos/NSC termination charge hit GAAP net income
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 14% and adjusted EPS grew 24% YoY; adjusted operating margins expanded 260 bps to near record levels
Net sales events of $47M (second-highest quarter ever) lifted YTD to $157M, already exceeding the best full-year total in company history
IMS revenue and operating profit each rose 14% YoY, and private banking revenue rose 11% with operating profit up 38% on strong operating leverage
summary: SEI reported 14% revenue growth, 25% adjusted operating profit growth, and 24% adjusted EPS growth YoY, with adjusted operating margins up 260 bps to near record levels. Net sales events of $47 million were the second highest in company history and brought YTD to $157 million, already above the highest full-year total ever. Q3 results were partly dampened by a $6 million incentive comp accrual (~100 bps margin impact, $0.02 EPS drag) and an $8 million QoQ decline in investment gains; excluding the accrual, sequential operating profit would have grown ~4%. No formal guidance was issued, but management said pipelines are healthy and expects continued momentum into Q4 and 2027.

negative_highlights: Same-store revenue declined 1.4% and new vehicle revenue fell 2.6% on 2.7% fewer units, with domestic units down 8.8%
F&I per unit fell 4.7% to $1,736 as DFC penetration shifts F&I income
Adjusted EBITDA of $443.5 million grew only 1.3% year over year; SG&A at 68.5% of gross profit remains well above the sub-60% target
positive_highlights: Adjusted diluted EPS of $10.34, up 9% year over year, with share count 11% lower than a year ago
DFC finance operations income of $32 million, up nearly 70%, on managed receivables of $5 billion (up 22%) and penetration of 18.3%
Used vehicle gross profit up 9.3% and used GPU up $234 (13%), with core 3-8 year-old GPU up 44%; after-sales margin expanded 100 bps to 59.5%
summary: Lithia reported Q3 revenue just shy of $10 billion with adjusted diluted EPS of $10.34, up 9% year over year, while same-store revenue declined 1.4% against a ~8% prior-year comparison. New vehicle revenue fell 2.6% on 2.7% fewer units, offset by used vehicle gross profit up 9.3%, total vehicle GPU of $3,958 (down $63), after-sales gross profit up 2.4% with margins up 100 bps to 59.5%, and DFC finance operations income of $32 million, up nearly 70% as managed receivables reached $5 billion. Adjusted SG&A was 68.5% of gross profit, in line with Q2, with net leverage at 3.1x and $85 million of buybacks plus $1.2 billion of year-to-date acquired annualized revenue; management gave no formal numeric guidance but reiterated long-term targets of sub-60% SG&A and $2 of EPS per $1 billion of revenue.

negative_highlights: Clearing house average cash balances fell to $147 billion from $150 billion in Q2, contributing to an 8% sequential decline in net interest income
24/7 WTI oil listing was withdrawn after commercial participant pushback and a CFTC stay, delaying that product
Compute futures remain stalled pending CFTC review, with the comment period extended 45 days and no approval timeline given
positive_highlights: Q3 ADV of 29.4 million contracts set a third-quarter record, up 16% YoY, with double-digit volume growth in all six asset classes
Revenue rose 13% to a Q3 record $1.7 billion with adjusted operating margin of 69.4% and adjusted EPS up 13% to $3.02
Market data revenue hit an all-time quarterly record of $243 million, up 20%, the 34th consecutive quarter of YoY revenue growth
summary: CME reported Q3 2026 revenue of $1.7 billion, up 13% YoY, with adjusted diluted EPS of $3.02, up 13%, and an adjusted operating margin of 69.4%. Average daily volume hit a Q3 record 29.4 million contracts, up 16%, with double-digit growth in all six asset classes, and market data revenue reached a record $243 million, up 20%. Q4 volume is tracking 17% above last year's record fourth quarter, and YTD volume is 12% ahead, with management stating it is on track for another record year. No formal numeric guidance was issued, but October 1 pricing changes are expected to add 0.5%-1% annualized to clearing and transaction fees.

negative_highlights: Operating revenue rose only just under 1% to $50.4B as lower health plan membership offset fee-based growth; membership ended at ~44.9 million
Adjusted operating expense ratio rose 90 bps to 11.3%, with targeted one-time investments and Stars/dual-eligible funding a drag

Medicaid underlying cost trend remains elevated (stable vs Q2) and rates have not fully caught up with costs; ACA outlook aided by a $1.85/share non-operating gain and slower-than-expected bronze cost seasonality
positive_highlights: Adjusted diluted EPS of $6.99 exceeded the outlook, driven by ~$0.50/share of operating outperformance; 2026 adjusted EPS guidance raised to at least $29
Benefit expense ratio improved 70 bps to 90.6%, with Medicaid, Medicare Advantage, and Individual ACA all favorable to outlook
2026 earnings baseline raised $0.75 to at least $26.75, with at least 12% adjusted EPS growth reaffirmed for 2027; full-year operating cash flow guidance raised to at least $6.5B
summary: Adjusted diluted EPS of $6.99 beat the outlook, with roughly $0.50/share of operating outperformance plus a $1.85/share net non-operating benefit. Revenue rose just under 1% to $50.4B while the benefit expense ratio improved 70 bps to 90.6%, though the adjusted operating expense ratio rose 90 bps to 11.3%. Management raised 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to at least $29, lifted the 2026 baseline to at least $26.75 (up $0.75), and reiterated at least 12% adjusted EPS growth in 2027; full-year operating cash flow guidance rose to at least $6.5B. Medicaid, Medicare Advantage, and Individual ACA each came in ahead of outlook, and management called 2026 the trough for Medicaid margins.

negative_highlights: Negative 7.6% economic return and an 11.4% quarter-over-quarter decline in book value per share to $17.86
Net interest margin contracted 7 bp to 1.69% and net interest spread fell 8 bp to 1.42% as cost of funds rose to 4.03%
Economic leverage increased to 5.9x from 5.6x, with assets available for financing down about $1.1 billion to $8.5 billion
positive_highlights: EAD of $0.80 per share rose 1 cent and exceeded the $0.75 quarterly dividend for the quarter
Book value was up roughly 2% quarter-to-date (about 3% including dividend) after the Q3 decline
Onslow Bay posted record quarterly fundings of $5.8 billion with locked pipeline average FICO of 766 and LTV of 67%
summary: Annaly reported a negative 7.6% economic return for Q3 2026 as book value per share fell 11.4% to $17.86, driven by a 20 bp widening in Agency MBS spreads and elevated rate volatility after a 82 bp rise in the 10-year Treasury. EAD rose 1 cent to $0.80 per share, again covering the $0.75 dividend, but net interest margin fell 7 bp to 1.69% and economic leverage rose to 5.9x from 5.6x. Management said book value was up about 2% quarter-to-date and expects to outearn the dividend in Q4, with no formal guidance change and new money Agency returns cited in the mid-to-high teens.

negative_highlights: North America railcar build forecast cut to ~23,000 cars, a 26% decline YoY, pressuring the component/flow business
Equipment sales were only up slightly as some locomotive deliveries shifted from Q3 into Q4; revenue guidance left unchanged
Freight carload and international traffic trends described as mixed, with North American Class I note behavior unchanged
positive_highlights: Adjusted operating margin expanded 1.9 pts to 22.9% and GAAP gross margin rose 2.6 pts to 37.3%, exceeding internal expectations on mix, Integration 3.0 productivity, and cost discipline
Multi-year backlog exceeded $31 billion, up 22.9% YoY, with 12-month backlog up 8.8% and management calling order coverage the strongest it has ever been
International orders included $1 billion of locomotive and service awards in Africa and Brazil plus $600M+ of North America locomotive/modernization orders from two Class I customers
summary: Wabtec reported Q3 FY2026 sales of $3.12 billion, up 8.1% (8.3% ex-FX), with GAAP EPS of $2.42 (+33.7%) and adjusted EPS of $2.83 (+22.0%); adjusted operating margin was 22.9%, up 1.9 pts, and GAAP gross margin 37.3%, up 2.6 pts. Freight adjusted margin hit 26.4% (+1.9 pts) and Transit 18.1% (+2.6 pts), while 12-month backlog rose 8.8% to $8.99 billion and multi-year backlog topped $31 billion (+22.9%). Full-year adjusted EPS guidance was raised to $10.85-$11.05 (up 22% at midpoint) while revenue guidance was unchanged, with management noting some locomotive deliveries shifted from Q3 into Q4. Management flagged North America railcar builds cut to ~23,000 (-26% YoY) and mixed freight carload, but touted strong global locomotive/service orders ($1 billion internationally, $600M+ North America) and Integration 3.0 savings running ahead of plan.

negative_highlights: Total non-GAAP revenue of $1.43 billion was flat YoY and 1% below consensus.

Transactional revenue fell 17% YoY and came in 10% below expectations, with fixed income transactional revenue down to $80 million from ~$123 million and equity transactional down to $41 million from $59 million.
Net flows were slightly negative in the quarter amid elevated advisor competition and choppy markets.
positive_highlights: Non-GAAP EPS of $1.46 beat consensus and rose 12% YoY; year-to-date EPS up 22% excluding last year's legal charge.
Net interest income of $302 million exceeded the high end of guidance and consensus by $4 million, with loans up $1.3 billion in the quarter.
Comp ratio fell to 56.6% from 57.0% in Q2, the lowest since Q4 2022, driving a 22.5% pre-tax margin; non-comp expense declined 4% sequentially and beat estimates by 3%.
summary: Q3 FY2026 non-GAAP EPS of $1.46 beat consensus and rose 12% YoY, but total non-GAAP revenue of $1.43 billion was flat year-over-year and 1% below consensus, with transactional revenue down 17% and 10% below expectations. Net interest income of $302 million beat the high end of guidance and consensus, comp ratio fell to 56.6% from 57.0%, and pre-tax margin was 22.5%. Q4 NII is guided to $295-305 million and institutional transactional revenue to $145-150 million; management expects Q4 revenue to roughly match last year's record $1.56 billion with higher EPS. The key change versus prior periods is a more cautious near-term outlook as September's rate shock and geopolitical tension slowed investment banking activity, offset by record wealth management revenue and continued loan growth.

negative_highlights: Full-year EPS growth now seen at midpoint or lower half of the 7.5-9.5% currency-neutral range, with roughly one point of combined drag from Middle East/input inflation (~0.5 pt) and Ukraine disruption (~0.5 pt)
U.S. Q4 adjusted OCI guided to around zero or slightly negative on the 20-pouch transition (~25% less revenue per pouch) and a further ~10% sequential step-up in U.S. SG&A to roughly $370M+
U.S. adjusted OCI grew only +1.5% in Q3 despite a 23% revenue increase, and HTU shipment growth is now expected slightly below adjusted IMS growth for the full year
positive_highlights: Organic net revenue +7.1% and organic adjusted OI +10.5% in Q3, with adjusted OI above $5B for the first time and adjusted OI margin near 45% (+130 bps organic)
VEEV e-vapor shipments +62% in Q3 (+68% YTD to 4.0B units); IQOS adjusted IMS accelerated to +7.1% from +5.1% in Q2, and +10% excluding Japan/Poland
Combustibles posted flat cigarette volumes against a -1.1% industry, pricing +8.9% in Q3 with Marlboro at a record 11.4% share; dividend raised ~9% for a 19th consecutive year to $6.40
summary: Q3 organic net revenue grew +7.1% (+5.5% reported to $11.4B), organic adjusted OI rose +10.5% to over $5B with margin near 45% (+130 bps organic), and adjusted diluted EPS hit a record $2.36 (+5.4%, +6% ex-FX). Headline guidance was unchanged (organic revenue +5-7%, organic OI +7-9%, currency-neutral EPS +7.5-9.5%), but management framed full-year delivery as 'midpoint or lower half' of the EPS bracket due to a step-up in U.S. investment and geopolitical cost inflation, versus prior language. The key change is the U.S.: Q4 adjusted OCI is guided to around zero or slightly negative as ZYN shifts from 15- to 20-pouch cans (roughly 25% less revenue per pouch) plus a further ~10% sequential SG&A increase, while international smoke-free is expected to re-accelerate in Q4.

negative_highlights: Q4 NIM guided down to 4.15-4.20% (~5 bps compression from normalized), with each 25 bp hike implying ~5 bps of pressure and $1B of swaps rolling off in April/August 2027.
Deposit-related fees are expected to rise ~25% in Q4, pressuring the expense line alongside AI, branch, and payments investments.
EB-5 drove ~75% of Q3 deposit growth amid an application cutoff, and management expects non-interest-bearing deposit growth to decelerate.
positive_highlights: NIM expanded 28 bps to 4.36% and net interest income grew ~8% QoQ and more than 25% YoY, with cost of deposits down 8 bps to 2.49%.
Loans grew to $7.5B (up 10.6% YTD) and deposits to $8.3B (up ~$589M QoQ), keeping loan growth on track versus the $1B annual guidance.
Board raised the quarterly dividend 14% to $0.40 and management committed to further buybacks under a $40M authorization.
summary: MCB reported Q3 FY2026 diluted EPS of $2.58, NIM of 4.36% (up 28 bps QoQ, normalized 4.20-4.25%), net interest income up ~8% QoQ and over 25% YoY, loans of $7.5B (up 10.6% YTD, tracking toward $1B annual growth guidance), and deposits of $8.3B with ~$589M QoQ growth. The board raised the quarterly dividend 14% to $0.40 and the bank repurchased ~$10M of shares in September under a $40M authorization. Q4 NIM guidance is 4.15-4.20% (~5 bps compression from normalized), and management flagged rising deposit fee expenses (~25% higher) and swap rolloffs ($1B in April/August) as headwinds. Charge-offs were a manageable 18 bps, with recoveries expected in Q4 and credit trending toward normalization.

negative_highlights: Annualized net charge-offs rose to 0.21% on a $2.4 million charge-off on the $10 million mixed-use multifamily non-accrual loan
The $8.6 million CBD office non-accrual loan saw its specific reserve increased to $5.3 million, with management expecting some portion to migrate to charge-offs
Provision expense guided higher for Q4 versus Q3; new loan origination activity expected to slow as higher rates push deals out of the pipeline
positive_highlights: Revenue up 20% YoY to a record, with pre-provision net revenue up 36% YoY
NIM expanded 2 bps to 3.09% with loan yields up 5 bps to 5.96%, and management noted margin exceeded its own expectations (originally not expected to reach 3% until Q4)

Efficiency ratio fell below 50% for the first time since Q1 2023 as Q3 non-interest expense came in below the expected Q2 run-rate; core deposits grew $165 million (20% annualized) with non-interest-bearing deposits up $63 million and brokered deposits down $96 million
summary: Bridgewater reported record total revenue (up 20% YoY) and record pre-provision net revenue (up 36% YoY), with NIM up 2 bps to 3.09% and loan yields up 5 bps to 5.96%. Core deposits grew $165 million (20% annualized) and loans grew 7.2% annualized, pushing the efficiency ratio below 50% for the first time since Q1 2023; non-interest expense came in below the prior expectation of holding flat with Q2. Guidance is for mid-single-digit loan growth, a relatively stable NIM even assuming a December hike and two more in 1H27, and Q4 expenses back to Q2 levels. The main offsets are a $2.4 million charge-off driving net charge-offs to 0.21%, a $5.3 million specific reserve on an $8.6 million office loan, and expectations for a higher Q4 provision.

negative_highlights: Management said it does not expect to achieve its full second-half ACV plan, with only $52 million of net new ACV added through the first three quarters
FY26 free cash flow will be lower than originally modeled due to slower net new ACV and unusual legal-settlement cash expenditures
Headcount will fall to approximately 5,000 by Q1 2027, down a few hundred, as part of restructuring amid longer sales cycles and deployment challenges
positive_highlights: Q3 net new ACV of $32 million in constant currency was the strongest quarterly add of the year
Pega Cloud ACV grew 20% YoY and cloud backlog rose 25% in constant currency, with cloud at 59% of total ACV
Repurchased just under 11 million shares for roughly $430 million in the first nine months of 2026, reducing share count by 6.8 million
summary: Pega reported ACV growth of 7% YoY in constant currency to $1.66 billion, with Q3 net new ACV of $32 million, the strongest quarter of the year but still below plan; Pega Cloud ACV grew 20% and reached 59% of total ACV, and cloud backlog rose 25%. Management explicitly said it does not expect to achieve its full second-half ACV plan, and FY26 free cash flow will be lower than modeled, while reaffirming the 2028 target of $700 million or more in free cash flow. The company is cutting headcount to approximately 5,000 by Q1 2027 and restructuring go-to-market, marketing, adoption, and operations, citing longer sales cycles and customer deployment challenges rather than demand deterioration. Free cash flow for the first three quarters was $290 million, and just under 11 million shares were repurchased for about $430 million.

negative_highlights: Adjusted net income fell to $14.7 million ($0.29 per diluted share) from $22.8 million a year ago, driven by $17.2 million of realized and unrealized investment losses
GWP growth of 14.7% came in below management's stated expectation, which it attributed to casualty rate increases lowering conversion and hiring delays from the Next-Gen rollout
Book value decreased $6.7 million from Q2 on an AOCI decline from higher Treasury yields; no shares were repurchased in the quarter
positive_highlights: Combined ratio improved 4.0 points YoY to a company-record 84.7%, with loss ratio down 2.5 points to 57.5% (including 1.6 points of favorable development) and expense ratio down 1.5 points to 27.2%
Submissions grew 30% and net earned premiums rose 35.7% YoY, outpacing a relatively flat E&S market
Net investment income rose 19.1% to $13.1 million; four new specialty products launched in four weeks versus a 12-week budget
summary: Ategrity reported a combined ratio of 84.7% (down from 88.7%), underwriting income of $19.5 million (+83.7% YoY), and net earned premiums up 35.7%, but adjusted net income fell to $14.7 million ($0.29/diluted share) from $22.8 million on $17.2 million of realized/unrealized investment losses. Gross written premiums rose 14.7% and submissions grew 30%, though the quarter came in below management's own expectation as deliberate casualty rate increases and the Next-Gen platform rollout temporarily cut productivity. Q4 guidance calls for GWP growth exceeding E&S market growth by 15-20 points and a combined ratio below 87%. No shares were repurchased; $47 million remains on the buyback authorization.

negative_highlights: Net charge-offs rose to $25.3 million or 49 bps annualized, driven by three previously identified credits (~$18 million of two movie theater loans plus roughly $9 million construction exposure).

Core NIM was about 3.46% excluding roughly $3.7-$3.8 million of interest recoveries (~6 bps), and management flagged continued deposit cost pressure from $3.4 billion of CDs rolling at 3.46% and competitive pricing.
Adjusted non-interest income fell to $18.8 million from the prior quarter on lower wealth management fees.
positive_highlights: Record net interest income of $211.9 million, up $11.0 million or 5.5% linked quarter, with NIM expanding 4 bps to 3.52%.
Full-year loan growth outlook raised to 5%-6% from 3.5%-4.5% and deposit growth to 4%-5% from 3%-4%.
Non-interest-bearing deposits grew $331 million in the quarter and the net loan-to-deposit ratio improved to approximately 96%.
summary: Cathay reported Q3 FY2026 net income of $95.2 million, or $1.43 per diluted share, up 3.2% linked quarter, on record net interest income of $211.9 million (+$11.0 million, +5.5% QoQ) and NIM expansion of 4 bps to 3.52%. Loans grew 2.8% ($575 million) and deposits 3.7% ($773 million) during the quarter, and the company raised its full-year loan growth outlook to 5%-6% from 3.5%-4.5% and deposit growth to 4%-5% from 3%-4%, while leaving the NIM guide (3.40%-3.50%) and adjusted expense growth (3.5%-4.5%) unchanged. Results included notable items: a $36.1 million equity securities gain, a $15.1 million securities repositioning loss, an $8 million foundation contribution, $5.4 million of contract termination costs, and a $54.1 million trust preferred redemption. Net charge-offs rose to $25.3 million (49 bps annualized), concentrated in three previously identified credits including two movie theater CRE loans and a fully reserved construction loan.

negative_highlights: Average deposits fell 3% sequentially to $123B and average earning assets declined 2%, contributing to a 1% sequential drop in NII.
Net interest income declined 1% sequentially as lower deposit balances offset higher securities yields.
Wealth management margins may compress as management prioritizes growth investments over near-term margin expansion.
positive_highlights: Revenue excluding notable items grew 11% YoY with expenses up only 4.9%, generating more than 600 bps of positive operating leverage.
EPS rose 40% YoY and pre-tax income rose 21%, with ROE at 20.1% and pre-tax margin at 34.9%.
Asset servicing pre-tax margin reached 30%, up 6 percentage points YoY, and trust fees grew 8% YoY.
summary: Northern Trust reported Q3 2026 net income of $642.9M and EPS of $3.40, with pre-tax margin of 34.9% and ROE of 20.1%; excluding notable items, revenue rose 11% YoY and expenses 4.9%, producing over 600 bps of positive operating leverage and 40% EPS growth. Guidance calls for Q4 revenue growth of 6%-7% and NII growth of 8%-9% YoY, with positive operating leverage in Q4 and 500+ bps for the full year. Results included $48.7M of pre-tax notable gains, and the company returned $514.2M to shareholders. The CFO announced his retirement, and deposit balances declined 3% sequentially on typical seasonality.

negative_highlights: FPL weather-normalized retail sales grew only 1.4%, versus 2.8% reported, with the gap driven by weather
Virginia governor's office and staff filed intervener testimony with potentially onerous conditions on the Dominion combination, adding regulatory uncertainty to a deal still awaiting SCC orders
positive_highlights: Adjusted EPS rose 9.7% YoY in Q3 and 9.5% through nine months, with full-year guidance unchanged at $3.92-$4.02 and management targeting the high end
Energy Resources added 3.7 GW to backlog (2.4 GW storage), bringing backlog to ~36.7 GW and marking a fourth consecutive quarter above 3.5 GW
Executed a 20-year PPA for ~1 GW of Point Beach at an expected ~$0.21 average EPS contribution; YTD recontracting of ~1,400 MW priced ~$20/MWh above recent realized pricing
summary: NextEra reported Q3 2026 adjusted EPS up 9.7% YoY, with Energy Resources adjusted earnings up ~13% and FPL EPS up $0.06 on ~9.2% regulatory capital employed growth. Full-year 2026 adjusted EPS guidance of $3.92-$4.02 was unchanged, but management is targeting the high end despite expected El Nino wind impacts of 90-95% of long-term average in Q4. Energy Resources added 3.7 GW to backlog, now ~36.7 GW, marking a fourth straight quarter above 3.5 GW. The pending Dominion combination remains on track for a 2H 2027 close, with Virginia and South Carolina hearings in November-December and final orders expected January 2027.

negative_highlights: North America Commercial premiums fell 2.7%, with ~4.5 points of drag from non-renewals and additional reinsurance in property and financial lines; major accounts and specialty declined 5%
Total P&C premium growth slowed to 1.9% amid a more competitive market, with gross property pricing down 4.2% in North America
Q3 core operating earnings fell ~2% to $2.98 billion on light prior-year CAT comps, and rising rates produced $4.5 billion of net realized and unrealized investment losses
positive_highlights: Adjusted net investment income set a record $1.89 billion; new money rate averaged 6.2% vs. a 5.2% portfolio yield, with invested assets over $175 billion
YTD underwriting income of $5.8 billion, up nearly 34%, and YTD core operating EPS of $21.94, up 24.5%
Favorable prior-period development of $562 million in active companies and a global P&C ex-CAT combined ratio of 81.8%, roughly flat YoY
summary: Chubb reported core operating earnings of $2.98 billion, or a record $7.66 per share, down ~2% and up ~1% respectively on exceptionally light prior-year CAT losses. Q3 combined ratio was 84.1% with P&C underwriting income of ~$2.1 billion; YTD core operating income rose 21% to $8.6 billion and core operating EPS rose 24.5% to $21.94. Total P&C premiums grew 1.9%, with Overseas General up 6.7% and North America Commercial down 2.7% (about 4.5 points of drag from property/financial lines non-renewals and added reinsurance); net investment income hit a record $1.89 billion. No formal EPS or margin guidance was given; management reiterated confidence in medium-term double-digit tangible book value growth and expected North America Commercial growth to improve materially, while flagging a more competitive commercial P&C market spreading into casualty lines.

negative_highlights: Other segment revenue declined 6% YoY
Personal electronics was about flat YoY
Embedded recovery is running roughly a year behind Analog, and trailing-12-month free cash flow of $8.4B includes $1.6B of CHIPS Act incentives
positive_highlights: Revenue up 28% YoY to $6.1B with broad growth across all end markets and regions; data center up ~95% YoY and industrial up more than 40% YoY
Gross margin rose 280 bps sequentially to 64% of revenue on higher revenue plus pricing, loading and mix; operating profit up 73% YoY to 47% of revenue
Q4 revenue guide of $5.8B-$6.3B implies flattish seasonality versus a typical mid-to-high single-digit decline, which management attributed to industrial, automotive and data center strength
summary: TXN reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $6.1B, up 11% sequentially and 28% year over year, with Analog +32% and Embedded +21% YoY. Gross margin was 64% of revenue, up 280 bps sequentially, operating margin 47%, and EPS $2.62 (including a $0.01 discrete tax headwind). Q4 guidance is revenue of $5.8B-$6.3B and EPS of $2.45-$2.79, which management framed as above normal seasonality on continued strength in industrial, automotive and data center. The dividend was raised 7% to $1.52 per share, the 23rd consecutive annual increase; no explicit prior-quarter guidance comparison was stated in the text.

negative_highlights: High-end softness in both markets drove a weaker quarter, with MBS EBITDA at $590M and management noting customers 'didn't show up'
Lower hold at The Londoner and MBS pressured margins and EBITDA
No explicit numerical guidance provided for Q4 or FY2027; management characterized the environment as 'aberrational' without pinpointing causes
positive_highlights: Macao market share reached 26.1% of mass gaming revenue, highest since Q4 2023
Rolling volume up 31% and slot/ETG handle up 26% year-over-year in Macao
Board approved 20% increase in quarterly dividend to $0.36 per share and $950M of buybacks during the quarter
summary: LVS reported a quarter with high-end customer softness in both markets, with MBS EBITDA of $590M (would have been $594M on normal hold) and Macao EBITDA of $529M (would have been $518M on normal hold). Macao gained share, hitting 26.1% of mass gaming revenue, its best since Q4 2023, with rolling volume up 31% and slot/ETG handle up 26% year-over-year. Management characterized the quarter as 'aberrational' and reiterated its long-term view, but offered no explicit numerical guidance, while announcing a 20% dividend increase to $0.36 and $950M in buybacks. The key change versus prior quarters is the slowdown at the high end of both markets, with management unable to attribute it to a single cause.

negative_highlights: Q3 GAAP net loss of $147 million (-$1.32/share); adjusted net income only $40 million ($0.36/share)
Q4 guided to an adjusted loss of $2.00-$2.50/share and full year to a $5.00-$5.50/share loss, with Q4 fuel of $4.65-$4.85/gal versus $2.50 initial plan adding $650 million of Q4 expense
About 40% of the system is absorbing six points of unit revenue pressure from growth markets, international ramp, and Hawaii, with load factor down roughly two points
positive_highlights: Total revenue up 14% to $4.3 billion with unit revenue up nearly 12%, in line with low-double-digit expectations, and yield up 13.4%
Premium revenue up ~24.5% YoY to more than 36% of total mix, and loyalty program cash up 21% to $721 million
RASM-to-CASMex spread improved to seven points from two points in Q2, and non-fuel unit cost growth slowed to 4.4% from 6.5% sequentially
summary: Alaska Air Group reported a Q3 GAAP net loss of $147 million (-$1.32/share), with adjusted net income of $40 million and adjusted EPS of $0.36, as fuel averaged $3.94/gal versus original July guidance of $3.75. Total revenue rose 14% to $4.3 billion on 2.4% capacity growth, with unit revenue up nearly 12% and non-fuel unit costs up 4.4%. Q4 adjusted EPS is guided to a loss of $2.00-$2.50, and full-year adjusted EPS to a loss of $5.00-$5.50, with Q4 economic fuel of $4.65-$4.85/gal versus an initial 2026 plan of $2.50. Management cited at least $3-$4 of core earnings improvement next year despite the fuel headwind.

negative_highlights: Q4 gross margin fell 190 bps YoY to 52.8% on roughly 370 bps of higher specialty chemical and raw material costs

Q4 SG&A rose $9.4 million to $58.2 million, including a $3.8 million constant-currency increase in incentive compensation accrual and $1.5 million of higher freight tied to Middle East supply disruption

FY2027 net sales guidance of 4%-7% growth and EPS growth of 5%-10% decelerates from FY2026's 11% reported sales growth, with Steve Brass flagging the U.S. as heading for the lower end of the range while lapping a strong FY2026
positive_highlights: Q4 sales grew 8% to $176.8 million with maintenance products up 9% to $170.5 million; EIMEA maintenance rose 14% and Asia Pacific sales rose 13%

WD-40 Specialist grew 21% to $99 million and premiumized Smart Straw/EZ Reach grew 17% to $277.1 million; free cash flow was $97.6 million, 117% of adjusted net income, and ROIC improved to 28.6% from 26.9%
summary: FY2026 net sales rose 11% to $688 million and constant-currency net sales grew 8% to $666 million, near the high end of guidance, with full-year gross margin of 55.3% and non-GAAP EPS up 6% to $6.18. Q4 gross margin fell 190 bps YoY to 52.8% on ~370 bps of higher specialty chemical and raw material costs, partly offset by ~170 bps of lower can and fill costs; SG&A rose $9.4 million to $58.2 million on $3.8 million of incentive accrual and $1.5 million of Middle East freight. FY2027 guidance targets net sales of $715-$735 million (4%-7% constant-currency growth), gross margin of 54%-55.5%, operating income of $114-$120 million (up 5%-10%), and diluted EPS of $6.40-$6.70; management called Q4 the gross-margin low point and cited sequential improvement already seen in September.

negative_highlights: Rated issuance fell 2% YoY and MIS revenue declined 1%, with transaction revenue down 5% as high yield and bank loan revenue fell 40% and 27% respectively
MIS adjusted operating margin contracted ~80 bps YoY to 64.4%
Q4 issuance guided to decline mid-teens percent YoY, and high yield/leveraged loan expectations were tempered while overall issuance outlook stayed at mid-single-digit growth
positive_highlights: Adjusted operating margin of 52.6% and adjusted diluted EPS growth of 6% despite a 2% decline in rated issuance
MA adjusted operating margin expanded 100 bps YoY to 35.3% with ARR up ~8% to $3.7 billion and 95% trailing-12-month retention
First-time mandates rose 40% YoY to the highest quarterly total in five years, prompting a raise of the full-year outlook to 900-950
summary: Moody's reported Q3 FY2026 revenue above $2 billion for a third straight quarter with rated issuance down 2% YoY to ~$1.7 trillion, yet adjusted operating margin held at 52.6% and adjusted diluted EPS grew 6%. MIS revenue fell 1% to $1.1 billion (transaction revenue -5% on mix), with MIS adjusted operating margin 64.4% (down ~80 bps YoY), while MA grew 3% reported / 8% organic constant currency with ARR up ~8% to $3.7 billion and margin up 100 bps to 35.3%. Full-year guidance was maintained, not raised: revenue growth high single digits, adjusted operating margin 52%-53%, adjusted diluted EPS $16.50-$17, with Q4 issuance expected to decline mid-teens percent YoY; the only raise was the first-time mandates outlook to 900-950. Free cash flow was $2.2 billion YTD, up 22%, with ~$2.6 billion of shares repurchased YTD against an up-to-$3 billion full-year target.

negative_highlights: Total revenue declined 8% YoY and product sales fell 9%, with defense product sales down 95%.
Net income and diluted EPS declined YoY to $3.17M and $0.65 from $3.31M and $0.68.
Operating expenses rose 4% on a 44% increase in SG&A, and guidance is for H2 revenue only consistent with H1, implying no sequential growth.
positive_highlights: Distributor sales increased 67% YoY in Q2 (and roughly 40% in H1), which management described as broad-based demand across new and legacy products.
Gross margin was 78%, operating margin 55%, and net margin 54%, with the tax rate down to 14% from 20% on favorable tax law changes.
First-half revenue was $16.9M, up 36% YoY, and operating cash flow rose to $11.1M from $8M, while cash plus marketable securities grew to $44.4M.
summary: Q2 FY2027 revenue fell 8% YoY as product sales dropped 9%, driven by a 95% decrease in defense product sales and a short-term medical-device customer inventory adjustment; distributor sales rose 67% and contract R&D rose 25%. Net income was $3.17M ($0.65/diluted share) versus $3.31M ($0.68), with net margin up to 54% on a lower 14% effective tax rate, gross margin 78%, operating margin 55%. Management guided H2 revenue to be consistent with H1 and expects medical and defense sales to recover in the current quarter, with a 14-16% tax rate expected for the remainder of the fiscal year. H1 revenue was $16.9M, up 36% YoY, and operating cash flow was $11.1M versus $8M.

negative_highlights: Some capital markets deals slid from Q3 into Q4, with Q4 production guided to $18-20 million
Tangible common equity to tangible assets fell 28 bps to 10.43% on higher rates' AOCI impact and buybacks
Continued deposit competition and funding-mix changes expected to largely offset the near-term benefit from higher rates, leaving Q4 NIM relatively static
positive_highlights: Record adjusted EPS of $2.21 with adjusted ROA of 1.52%
NIM TEY expanded 3 bps to 3.58%, exceeding guidance, on $69 million net interest income
Asset quality: NPAs fell to 0.39% of assets (lowest since 2024) and criticized loans dropped $14 million to 1.67%, lowest since 2019
summary: QCR Holdings reported record adjusted EPS of $2.21 on $36 million adjusted net income and a 1.52% adjusted ROA. NIM TEY expanded 3 bps to 3.58%, beating guidance, net interest income rose $800K (5% annualized) to $69 million, loans grew $190 million (11% annualized ex-M2 runoff), and capital markets revenue rose to $17 million from $15 million. Management reaffirmed $60-70 million capital markets revenue over the next four quarters, reiterated 10-15% annualized Q4 loan growth and $54-57 million Q4 expense guidance, and guided Q4 capital markets production to $18-20 million; Q4 NIM is expected to be relatively static. Asset quality improved to 0.39% NPAs, the lowest since 2024, with criticized loans at 1.67%, the lowest since 2019.

negative_highlights: Revenue growth was heavily fuel-driven, with fuel contributing about half of growth as diesel prices rose nearly 50% year over year; RPU ex-fuel rose only 1%
Fertilizer volume fell 13% and remained the softest merchandise market on supply issues and low crop prices
Q4 guidance implies 200-300 bps of typical sequential margin degradation from Q3 due to winter seasonality and higher PS&O
positive_highlights: EPS of $0.57 rose 30% and operating margin expanded 420 bps to 39.1% versus prior-year adjusted results
Revenue grew 12% on 5% volume growth, and full-year revenue guidance was raised to high single digits from mid-to-high single digits
Non-fuel costs fell 3% while handling 5% more volume; total intermodal volume hit an all-time record, up 7%
summary: CSX reported Q3 FY2026 revenue up 12% and EPS of $0.57, up 30% versus prior-year adjusted results, with 5% volume growth and operating margin of 39.1%, up 420 bps on an adjusted basis. Full-year revenue guidance was raised to high single-digit growth from mid-to-high single digits, with full-year operating margin expansion above 350 bps, capex below $2.4 billion, and free cash flow growth above 80%. Management cited a tight truck market, domestic intermodal at a record, and over 100 productivity initiatives for 2027, while flagging normal Q4 seasonal cost step-ups and fertilizer softness.

negative_highlights: Full-year revenue growth guidance reduced to ~6% from prior, driven by EP and diabetes softness
EP growth pressured by LAA market headwinds and an order slowdown after the Amulet 360 CE Mark, which management expects to persist through Q4
FY2027 guidance, including whether double-digit EPS growth holds, deferred to January
positive_highlights: Comparable sales grew 7% and adjusted EPS grew 9%, representing an acceleration versus the first half
Adjusted gross margin expanded 140 bps to 57.2% and operating margin expanded 40 bps to 23.4%
Cancer diagnostics grew 14% and medical devices grew 8%, led by electrophysiology and 10% rhythm management growth
summary: Abbott reported Q3 FY2026 comparable sales growth of 7% and adjusted EPS of $1.42, described by management as in line with guidance and consensus, with adjusted gross margin up 140 bps to 57.2% and operating margin up 40 bps to 23.4%. However, the full-year revenue growth guide was reduced to about 6% (implying just over 8% in Q4), driven by softness in electrophysiology (LAA market dynamics) and diabetes. Q4 adjusted EPS was guided to $1.62-$1.67 and FX is expected to be a roughly 1% headwind to Q4 sales. The headline event was the announced tax-free spin-off of the ~$8.5 billion nutrition business, expected to complete by end of next year, which management said would leave Abbott with 50-100 bps faster sales growth, >200 bps higher gross margin, and ~100 bps higher operating margin.

negative_highlights: Non-interest income fell $9 million QoQ and $6 million YoY to $20 million, driven by a $2.3 million securities loss, a $1.1 million lease-asset loss and a $1.9 million BOLI decline
Capital markets revenue fell $1.8 million QoQ on delayed transactions and lower average revenue per transaction
positive_highlights: NIM expanded 10 bps QoQ and 16 bps YoY to 3.16%, already above the 3.15% fourth-quarter target management had previously set
Average deposit costs fell 6 bps QoQ to 1.99%, with both asset yields and funding optimization contributing to margin expansion
Net charge-offs remained low; NPA ratio improved to 77 bps from 110 bps and criticized/classified balances fell 14% YoY
summary: BankUnited reported Q3 FY2026 net income of $72 million, or $1.01 per share GAAP and $1.03 adjusted (excluding a $2.3 million securities loss), up from $0.96 last quarter and $0.94 a year ago. NIM expanded 10 bps QoQ and 16 bps YoY to 3.16%, ahead of the 3.15% fourth-quarter target management had previously guided, while deposit costs fell 6 bps to 1.99%. Guidance for Q4 calls for NIM around 3.2%, NII of $265 million, non-interest income returning toward normalized levels, expenses of ~$178 million and a $15 million provision, with CET1 at 12.1% after 2.1 million shares repurchased for ~$97 million. The main negatives were a $9 million QoQ decline in non-interest income to $20 million on a securities loss, a $1.9 million BOLI drag and lower capital markets revenue, plus flat average NIDDA as the title business was hit by higher long-end rates.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA loss of $60.7 million and GAAP net loss of $84.5 million with no revenue recognized; still pre-commercial
Guidance reiterated rather than improved: FY2026 adjusted EBITDA loss $250-275 million and CapEx $27-37 million unchanged
Customer billings flagged as variable quarter to quarter and not a substitute for GAAP revenue
positive_highlights: Announced 100-MWh mass production line with Muehlbauer targeting 2028 startup, equipment cost to QS under $100 million
Customer billings of $9.8 million included first billings from Honda and first QSAS billing from QSE-5 sample shipments
QS PowerBlock demonstrated 4x power density and 5x longer runtime than the OCP reference spec, with thermal stability above 300 degrees C validated in third-party testing
summary: QuantumScape reported Q3 FY2026 GAAP net loss of $84.5 million and an adjusted EBITDA loss of $60.7 million, in line with expectations, with customer billings of $9.8 million that included first billings from Honda and from QSAS sample shipments. Full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA loss guidance of $250-275 million and CapEx of $27-37 million were both reiterated, not raised. The main change versus prior periods was the announcement of a 100-MWh mass production line with Muehlbauer, targeting 2028 startup production with equipment cost to QS under $100 million and non-dilutive funding being pursued. Liquidity stood at $819.8 million. No revenue or EPS figures were disclosed since the company is pre-commercial, so the read rests on billings, losses, reiterated guidance, and roadmap announcements.

negative_highlights: Net income fell to $13.9 million ($0.39) from $21.3 million ($0.60) in Q2, including a $3.1 million deposit fraud loss and a combined $4.3 million fair-value decline
Residential mortgage originations dropped 26% sequentially with tightening gain-on-sale margins, and gain-on-sale is guided to near zero in 2027
MPP average yields fell to 6.27% (6.49% fee-adjusted) on competitive pricing, and MPP fees were cut to $8-9 million for 2026 from prior guidance
positive_highlights: MPP period-ending balances rose $262.7 million and average balances $237.2 million, with four new clients adding $185 million of capacity and utilization averaging 58%
Total deposits increased $210.4 million to $5.4 billion, with growth in non-interest-bearing demand deposits
Net charge-offs were just $429,000, a 2 basis point annualized ratio to average loans, and 31-89 day delinquencies fell $5.7 million
summary: Q3 FY2026 net income fell to $13.9 million ($0.39 per diluted share) from $21.3 million ($0.60) in Q2, with $7.5 million pre-tax negative impact from a $4.3 million fair-value decline on three rate-sensitive assets and a $3.1 million external deposit fraud loss. Net interest income rose $1.2 million on $157 million higher average earning assets, while NIM slipped 1 bp to 2.32%. Management announced a non-binding LOI to watch the distributed retail and consumer direct mortgage origination channels to CMG Financial, guiding 2027 non-interest expense down to $80-$95 million ($50-$55 million of expense savings) but noting gain-on-sale revenue will be virtually zero in 2027; full-year 2026 NIM guidance held at 2.3%-2.4%, rising to 2.4%-2.6% in 2027. MPP period-ending balances grew $262.7 million and the quarterly dividend was raised to $0.03 from $0.025 per share.

negative_highlights: About $225 million of 2026 outperformance came from non-recurring items (Winter Storm Fern, a terminals contract buyout, a FERC rate true-up, an unusually favorable Waha-to-Houston spread), plus $175 million from commodity prices versus a $60 WTI budget
Products segment volumes declined, with refined product volumes down 3% and crude/condensate volumes down 11% YoY, partly on the Double H NGL conversion and fewer Hiland Crude well connects
Management declined to preview 2027 guidance and noted growth will be lumpy, with only 30% of Trident's contracted EBITDA coming online in 2027 and 2026 a difficult year to replicate
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA rose 9% to $2.18 billion and adjusted EPS rose 21% to $0.35, with all four business segments delivering higher adjusted earnings YoY

Project backlog increased from $9.6 billion to $14.4 billion on $5.4 billion of additions at a 5.7x multiple, with Rich Kinder stating the backlog implies about $2.5 billion of additional EBITDA, taking the total to $11.5-$12 billion
Net debt to adjusted EBITDA improved to 3.5x from 3.8x at the start of the year, with year-end leverage now expected at 3.6x versus a 3.8x budget
summary: KMI reported Q3 FY2026 adjusted EPS of $0.35, up 21% YoY, and adjusted EBITDA of $2.18 billion, up 9%, with EPS 15% above budget and EBITDA 6% above budget; net income attributable to KMI was $764 million and GAAP EPS $0.24, up 22% and 21% respectively. Guidance was raised: full-year adjusted EBITDA now expected more than 6% above budget (well over $515 million of additional EBITDA) and adjusted EPS more than 13% above budget, though management flagged ~$225 million of one-time items and ~$175 million of commodity-price upside as unlikely to recur. The quarter's headline was commercial rather than financial: project backlog rose from $9.6 billion to $14.4 billion with $5.4 billion of additions, including the SNG Southeast Connector and NGPL Permian Link JVs, extending the growth runway into 2030-2032. Leverage fell to 3.5x from 3.8x at the start of the year, and the dividend was declared at $0.2975 per quarter, up 2%.

América Móvil reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of MXN 251 billion, up 7.6% YoY, with EBITDA margin at 40.8% (up 0.5 ppts) and operating profit up 13.9% to MXN 57 billion. At constant FX, service revenue rose 5.3% and EBITDA 6.7%, with mobile service revenue +6.3% and fixed accelerating to 3.7% from 2.7% prior quarter. Net profit reached MXN 24 billion (+7% YoY), free cash flow was 41% higher YoY, and net debt/EBITDA fell to 1.21x from 1.50x at year-end 2025. Management gave no formal numeric guidance update beyond reiterating ~$7 billion CapEx for this year and next; Mexican prepaid faces near-term pressure from the subscriber registration mandate.

negative_highlights: 2026 investment volume guidance reduced to ~$1.6B, and guidance noted a $150M decrease in net investment activity at the midpoint
Spot cost of capital cited at 6.8% versus 7.3% acquisition cap rates, a narrow ~50 bps spread management is trying to widen
Elevated dead deal costs in Q3 reduced AFFO per share by roughly a penny, and the 10-year bond was issued at 5.65% (5.36% all-in)
positive_highlights: Core FFO and AFFO per share each $1.15, up 4.9% YoY; FY2026 AFFO guidance raised to $4.58-$4.59 (~6% growth at midpoint)
Acquisition cap rates expanded 30 bps QoQ to 7.3% on 7.3% weighted average cap rate for Q3 acquisitions, with Q4 expected to expand a further ~25 bps
Portfolio at a company record 99.8% occupied with 106% recapture rate, the highest in six quarters; credit and occupancy loss assumption cut to 15 bps from 25 bps
summary: Core FFO and AFFO per share were each $1.15, up 4.9% YoY, with full-year 2026 AFFO guidance raised to $4.58-$4.59 (~6% growth at the midpoint) on portfolio strength and lower TSMM dilution, though partly offset by $150M lower net investment activity. Q3 investment volume was ~$360M across 94 properties with acquisition cap rates expanding 30 bps QoQ to 7.3%, and 2026 investment volume guidance was cut to ~$1.6B while disposition volume guidance rose to $100-150M from $50-100M. Management framed a $2B war chest raised at prior pricing, 3.9x pro forma leverage, and mid-single-digit AFFO growth in 2027, while acknowledging an elevated spot cost of capital and culling lower-yield deals.

negative_highlights: Loan growth guidance moved down: full-year 2026 now expected at the low end of the 6%-8% range on mid-single-digit 4Q growth, versus the range increase last quarter
Full-year NII now expected at the low end of the stated range, with total margin down modestly in the quarter to 352 bps as deposit costs rose 8 bps linked-quarter
Mortgage fees were soft and expected to remain soft into 4Q on the rising rate environment and seasonality, and management flagged pressure on NII and the top line
positive_highlights: Adjusted efficiency ratio hit a record-low 44.9% while adjusted non-interest expense fell to $355 million from the prior quarter
Period-end deposits grew 11% annualized, driven by about $1 billion of organic business-account increases, pushing the loan-to-deposit ratio down to 89%
Credit improved: criticized and classified loans fell 9% linked-quarter and 16% year-over-year, with net charge-offs of 27 bps (24 bps ex-PCD) and non-accruals down from 123 bps a year ago to 92 bps
summary: Old National reported record GAAP and adjusted EPS of $0.66 with ROA of 1.37% and ROTCE of 19.6%, a record-low 44.9% adjusted efficiency ratio, and 11% annualized deposit growth. Revenue came in softer, with NII of $592 million and total margin down modestly to 352 bps on higher deposit costs. Full-year 2026 guidance is unchanged (15%+ EPS growth, positive operating leverage), but loan growth is now expected at the low end of the 6%-8% range, full-year NII at the low end of its range, and mortgage fees face continued softness. The quarter was solid on efficiency, credit, and capital return but light on the top line relative to the trajectory management had guided to earlier in the year.

negative_highlights: Middle East weakened relative to July expectations; rig counts trending lower, tender cycles slipped, and no regional recovery is built into the near-term outlook
Revenue declined 7% year over year and Q4 Adjusted EBITDA margin is guided modestly below Q3 at 270-290 million on startup costs in Venezuela and equipment mix
Europe, Sub-Saharan Africa and Russia revenue fell 9% sequentially on lower activity and a Norway labor strike
positive_highlights: Adjusted free cash flow of $155 million at 61% EBITDA conversion (up from 36.8% a year ago) with year-to-date $379 million, up 55% YoY
Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 204 bps sequentially and 39 bps YoY to 22.2% on a 7% YoY revenue decline
Full-year adjusted free cash flow conversion outlook raised for the third time this year to the high 40% range; DRE revenue grew 14% sequentially with segment margins up over 700 bps
summary: Weatherford reported Q3 2026 revenue of $1.143 billion, up 3% sequentially but down 7% year over year, with Adjusted EBITDA of $254 million (22.2% margin, up 204 bps sequentially) and adjusted free cash flow of $155 million at 61% conversion. Q4 guidance calls for revenue of $1.28-$1.33 billion and Adjusted EBITDA of $270-$290 million at a modestly lower margin, while full-year free cash flow conversion guidance was raised for the third time this year to the high 40% range from mid-to-high 40% and the Adjusted EBITDA range was narrowed around a midpoint slightly below July. The company redeemed $236 million of 8.625% notes due 2030, reducing annual cash interest by about $20 million, and guided to 2027 mid-single-digit global market activity growth with Weatherford outperforming, though the Middle East has weakened versus July and is planned at status quo with no recovery assumed.

negative_highlights: Fuel expense rose $1.8 billion year-over-year and only 72% was recaptured; Q4 recapture expected similar rather than the 100% anticipated
CASM-ex rose 7.8%, including full run-rate of the flight attendant deal and closing capacity reductions
Management said reaching double-digit 2027 pre-tax margins likely requires lower fuel, lower capacity, or continued yield-over-load-factor tradeoffs, and that Starlink alone is probably not enough
positive_highlights: Revenue rose 17.4% to a record $17.9 billion, with TRASM up 15.9% and yields up 17%
Premium revenue increased 17% and business revenue rose 22%, with economy cabin RASM positive for the first time in 12 quarters in Q1 2026
Starlink rollout on track to 61% of departures by end of 2026 and fleet-wide by end of 2027; loyalty revenue up 17% with Chase remuneration up 15%
summary: United reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of a record $17.9 billion, up 17.4% year-over-year, with TRASM up 15.9% and yields up 17%; EPS came in at $2.54, within the guidance range, and pre-tax margin was 6.2%. CASM-ex rose 7.8%, which management called the high-water mark, and fuel expense increased $1.8 billion year-over-year with only 72% recaptured through pricing. Q4 EPS guidance was set at $0.50-$1.50 on an all-in fuel price of roughly $4.80 per gallon, with fuel recapture expected to remain near the Q3 level rather than the 100% previously anticipated. Management explicitly declined to assume it can reach double-digit 2027 pre-tax margins without at least one of lower fuel, lower industry capacity, or continued yield-over-load-factor tradeoffs.

negative_highlights: Electronic test and measurement sales fell 6.3% due to order timing, and Instrumentation segment margin declined modestly YoY on mix
Q4 EPS guidance of $6.60-$6.70 implies little sequential improvement from Q3, which management tied partly to absence of prior-year tax benefits
Commercial aerospace sales were lower, partially offsetting 7.4% defense electronics growth in the Aerospace & Defense Electronics segment
positive_highlights: Full-year 2026 non-GAAP EPS guidance raised to $25.45 from $23.65 in January, a $1.80 (~8%) increase and ~16% YoY growth
Digital Imaging sales up 15% (14.3% organic) with segment non-GAAP margin up 376 bps to 25.4%, targeting 225 bps of full-year margin expansion
Free cash flow of $319.5M, a third-quarter record, plus $224.6M of opportunistic buybacks at ~$607 average; net leverage at a six-year low
summary: Teledyne reported record Q3 FY2026 sales and operating earnings and raised full-year 2026 guidance for the third consecutive quarter: revenue outlook moved to $6.625B (8.3% YoY, ~7.5% organic) from January's $6.37B, and non-GAAP EPS to $25.45 from $23.65, about $1.80 higher. Digital Imaging sales rose 15% (14.3% organic) with segment non-GAAP margin up 376 bps to 25.4%, and Digital Imaging book-to-bill was ~1.22x. Funded backlog is ~$5.3B with orders exceeding sales for 12 straight quarters. Q4 guidance implies 7-8% organic growth; management did not give a 2027 figure but expects mid-to-high single-digit growth.

negative_highlights: Full-year revenue guidance held at $60-68 million despite 43% H1 growth, with management explicitly cautious on H2 due to Middle East conflict and pending deliveries awaiting import permits
Net profit grew only 38% to $3.7 million as $4.3 million of finance costs, including a $1.6 million preferred-share derivative fair value loss, offset operating gains
Cash fell to $2.9 million from $6.8 million at year-end as receivables rose to $25.7 million, though management said the Turkmengaz June delivery was fully collected since
positive_highlights: H1 revenue up 43% to $33.8 million with Adjusted EBITDA up 79% to $14.1 million versus $7.9 million
Operating profit rose 135% to $9.1 million, reflecting operating leverage on the revenue growth
Backlog grew modestly above the $22.6 million reported at December 2025 despite roughly $9 million of capital sales delivered in H1
summary: GOWell reported H1 2026 revenue of $33.8 million, up 43% year over year, driven primarily by roughly $9 million of equipment sales mostly in the Caspian, with service up about $1.2 million. Operating profit rose 135% to $9.1 million and Adjusted EBITDA grew 79% to $14.1 million, though net profit rose only 38% to $3.7 million after $4.3 million of finance costs tied to redeemable preferred shares. Full-year guidance was reiterated at $60-68 million revenue and $25-29 million Adjusted EBITDA, not raised, as management cited Middle East conflict uncertainty and pending capital-project deliveries tied to import permits. Adjusted EBITDA would have been $11.7 million (48% growth) if $2.4 million of capitalized R&D had been expensed, and backlog grew modestly from $22.6 million at December 2025 despite the deliveries.

Q3 FY2026 revenue fell 5% to $1.08 billion, pre-tax income dropped 38% to $87 million, diluted EPS fell to $2.56 from $3.92, and adjusted gross margin contracted 320 bps to 21.3% as rate-buydown costs rose. New contracts were down 2% with monthly deterioration (July +15%, August -6%, September -16%), and the cancellation rate was 12%. No explicit forward EPS or revenue guidance was given; management said only that year-end community count would be about 5% higher and that conditions 'may continue for some time.' The balance sheet is the standout: a record $3.3 billion of equity ($130 book value per share), 18% debt-to-capital, $620 million cash, and $50 million of buybacks in the quarter.

negative_highlights: All Other Segments expected to produce an operating loss in Q4 as warehousing revenue seasonally declines against a higher fixed cost base, plus ~$6.5 million of AR securitization costs shifted from interest expense
Cost per mile rose 3.5% in 2026, with driver pay and record-high diesel cited as the most acute cost pressures, limiting margin expansion despite accelerating rates
Q4 guidance of $0.78-$0.84 adjusted EPS implies a sequential step down from Q3's $0.83, reflecting expected seasonal declines in LTL and All Other Segments
positive_highlights: Adjusted EPS of $0.83 versus $0.32 a year ago, with adjusted operating income up 87.4% and consolidated adjusted operating ratio improving 450 bps to 89.3%
Truckload revenue per mile excluding fuel accelerated to 12.2% YoY growth in Q3 from 2.5% in Q1, with 68% of rate improvement flowing to margin versus 50% in Q2

Intermodal posted its highest quarterly load count in over five years, with revenue per load up 15.2% YoY, and management said it started 2027 bid talks targeting low-to-mid double-digit rate increases
summary: Knight-Swift reported Q3 FY2026 consolidated revenue up 14.2% YoY to a record, adjusted operating income up 87.4% to $93 million, GAAP EPS of $0.72 versus $0.05, and adjusted EPS of $0.83 versus $0.32, with consolidated adjusted operating ratio improving 450 bps to 89.3%. Truckload rate per mile excluding fuel accelerated to 12.2% YoY growth in Q3 from 2.5% in Q1, with 68% flow-through to margin, and one-way operating margins exceeded dedicated for the first time in several years. Q4 2026 adjusted EPS guidance is $0.78-$0.84, with Truckload operating income expected to meaningfully improve sequentially while LTL and All Other step down seasonally, including an anticipated operating loss in All Other and ~$6.5 million of AR securitization costs shifted from interest expense. Management cited record peak season project arrangements and expects to open 2027 bid season discussions at low-to-mid double-digit rate increases.

negative_highlights: Reported core growth was only 3% as respiratory revenue fell to ~$350 million, a ~250 bps headwind, and respiratory revenue is now planned at ~$1.5 billion, roughly $100 million below prior expectations with Q4 a further ~150 bps headwind
Developed market core revenue was flat, with North America down low single digits, and academic demand remains below historic levels
Discovery & Medical core revenue declined low single digits on lab consumables timing, and 2027 guidance was given only as a qualitative 4%-5% starting point with a formal outlook deferred to January
positive_highlights: Core growth excluding respiratory accelerated to 5.5%, up 100 bps sequentially, with Biotechnology +5%, Life Sciences +4.5%, and Diagnostics ex-respiratory +7%
Adjusted operating margin expanded 110 bps to 29% and adjusted EPS rose ~11.5% to $2.11; full-year adjusted EPS guidance raised to $8.57-$8.62 from $8.45-$8.60
Bioprocessing orders grew mid-teens with equipment orders in strong double digits and a building backlog; Beckman Coulter Diagnostics posted its highest core growth quarter in more than two years
summary: Danaher reported Q3 sales of $6.6 billion with core growth of 3% as reported, or 5.5% excluding respiratory revenue, a 100 bps acceleration from Q2. Adjusted operating margin was 29%, up 110 bps, adjusted EPS rose about 11.5% to $2.11, and free cash flow was $1.6 billion on a 128% YTD conversion ratio. Full-year adjusted EPS guidance was raised to $8.57-$8.62 from $8.45-$8.60, and management framed 4%-5% ex-respiratory core growth as the starting point for 2027, with respiratory planned at roughly $1.5 billion versus a prior $100 million cut. Bioprocessing orders grew mid-teens, Masimo tracked ahead of expectations, and new CEO Julie Sawyer Montgomery outlined commercial-execution, innovation, talent, and capital-allocation priorities.

negative_highlights: Q3 revenue of $479.6 million versus a Q4 midpoint guide implying roughly $60 million sequential increase, largely acquisition-driven; standalone organic momentum is modest.
SG&A rose in Q3 due to higher professional fees (legal and M&A-related) and remains within the 9.5%-10.5% range with limited near-term operating leverage.
Bad debt and workers' comp remain lumpy and unpredictable; management explicitly stated performance in any quarter does not predict the next.
positive_highlights: 2027 revenue growth outlook raised to low double digits from prior mid-single digits, supported by NEXDINE and mid-single-digit organic growth.
Cost of services at 83.2% was below the 86% target, aided by a $6.1 million Genesis recovery and strong service execution.
Q3 share repurchases of $11.7 million brought YTD buybacks to $56.6 million, with $204.3 million in cash and an unutilized $300 million credit facility.
summary: HCSG reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $479.6 million, net income of $24.9 million and diluted EPS of $0.36, with segment margins of 13.3% (Environmental) and 8.7% (Dietary). Cost of services came in at 83.2%, below the 86% target, helped by operational execution and a $6.1 million Genesis bankruptcy recovery that reduced bad debt. Q4 revenue guidance is $535-$545 million, including the NEXDINE acquisition (>$150M annual revenue, closed October 6), and 2027 revenue growth outlook was raised from mid-single digits to low double digits (including NEXDINE; mid-single-digit organic). Cash flow from operations was $30.2 million, and the company repurchased $11.7 million of stock in Q3 ($56.6 million YTD).

Tesla reported a second consecutive quarter above 480K vehicle deliveries with automotive gross margin ex-credits up sequentially from 16.3% to 18.1%, though management attributed the gain largely to APAC delivery mix and noted commodity and interest-rate cost headwinds.
