Energy storage gross margin jumped from 20.4% to 33.1%, but primarily on one-time tariff refunds and warranty true-downs, with 13.7 GWh deployed. No formal revenue, EPS, or delivery guidance was given; CapEx guidance for the year was revised to approximately $20 billion, over $1.5 billion of free cash flow was generated, and the cash balance exceeded $45 billion. Management framed demand as exceeding production with the highest backlog in four years and touted FSD attach (over 75% in North America at delivery, 1.7M paid customers) and Robotaxi/Optimus timelines, but much of the forward narrative (Optimus at scale, Terafab, 5M vehicles by 2030) was pushed a year or more out.

negative_highlights: Q1 FY2027 sales guided down mid-to-high single digits with adjusted EPS down YoY and adjusted EBITDA margin on par to slightly below prior-year Q1
Towable RV revenue fell to ~$220.3M with operating margin of only 4.2% amid cautious dealer ordering and elevated competitive intensity
Management assumes no broad RV or marine retail recovery, and expects same-SKU inflation of 2.5%-3.5% with aluminum cost escalation running above that range
positive_highlights: Motorhome RV operating margin improved more than 250 basis points YoY to 2.4% on transformation efficiencies, reduced discounts and cost discipline
Full-year free cash flow rose to $144.6M from $89.5M, and net leverage fell to 2.2x from 3.1x a year ago
Enterprise RV retail unit share reached 35.4% and U.S. dollar share 41%, with Barletta pontoon share up ~70 bps to 9.7%
summary: Winnebago reported Q4 FY2026 net revenue of ~$645.1M, adjusted EBITDA of ~$32.6M (5.1% margin) and adjusted EPS of $0.49, with revenue down YoY on lower unit volume and unfavorable mix; full-year revenue was ~$2.7B and adjusted EPS $1.79. FY2027 guidance calls for revenue of $2.65B-$2.8B and adjusted EPS of $1.65-$2.25 (midpoint $1.95, up 9% YoY), but Q1 sales are guided down mid-to-high single digits with EPS down YoY and adjusted EBITDA margin on par to slightly below prior-year Q1. Motorhome RV operating margin improved more than 250 bps to 2.4%, free cash flow rose to $144.6M from $89.5M, and net leverage fell to 2.2x from 3.1x; management assumes no broad retail recovery, relying instead on $70M-$80M of cumulative FY2027-2029 gross cost savings.

negative_highlights: Tangible common equity ratio fell to 9.1% from 9.5% and tangible book value per share declined due to a $41.6 million increase in unrealized investment losses
Fee income declined to $13.4 million from $13.8 million, with mortgage income lower on mark-to-market adjustments and swap fees down
Loan-to-deposit ratio rose to 92% as net deposit outflows required increased reliance on borrowings; deposit beta expected higher than the prior cycle's 25 bps
positive_highlights: NIM expanded 12 bps to 4.12% adjusted for the $1.6 million subordinated debt charge, with asset-sensitive positioning to benefit from further rate hikes
Loans grew $95.3 million, or 9% annualized, with core growth of 7% excluding $15.5 million of purchased HELOCs; full-year 5% growth goal already met
Efficiency ratio improved to 56% from 58.6% adjusted prior quarter, with non-interest expense down $400,000 to $37.3 million
summary: Orrstown reported Q3 2026 net income of $22.8 million, or $1.17 per diluted share, with ROA of 1.60% and ROE of 14.62%. Net interest income rose $4.5 million to $53.3 million and NIM expanded to 4.12%, up 12 bps adjusted for the prior quarter's $1.6 million charge, while loans grew $95.3 million (9% annualized). Guidance was introduced for NIM of 4.05%-4.15% through 2027, fee income of $54-56 million, and expense run rate of $153-157 million, with loan growth held at mid-single digits versus a 5% full-year goal already reached. Tangible common equity fell to 9.1% from 9.5% due to a $41.6 million increase in unrealized investment losses, and the loan-to-deposit ratio rose to 92% as borrowings funded growth.

negative_highlights: 2027 capital plan cut by $2 billion to $11.4 billion, delaying customer projects including clean energy connections, system expansion, and housing support
Fitch revised PG&E's outlook to negative during the quarter and S&P flagged heightened California utility risk; investment-grade ratings remain unattained per management
CPUC proposed decision on EUP benefit-cost ratio could sharply reduce undergrounding miles, and management is still quantifying the impact on its 5,000-mile plan
positive_highlights: Nine-month core EPS rose to $1.24 from $1.14, with customer CapEx contributing $0.12 of growth and O&M savings $0.04
2026 and 2027 core EPS guidance reaffirmed at $1.64-$1.66 and $1.78-$1.82, up 10% and 9% at the midpoints respectively
Fourth consecutive year without a major wildfire tied to company equipment; weather-normalized ignition rate down 74% since 2017, and ~174 MW of data center load connected since 2024
summary: PG&E reported Q3 2026 core EPS of $0.41 and $1.24 for the first nine months, up from $1.14 a year earlier, and reaffirmed 2026 core EPS guidance of $1.64-$1.66 (up 10% at the midpoint) and 2027 guidance of $1.78-$1.82 (up 9%). The 2027 capital plan was cut by $2 billion to $11.4 billion, with 2027 rate base guidance unchanged, and no new equity is expected through 2030. Management declined to give guidance beyond 2027 during a strategic review (corporate ring-fencing to sales/separations) targeting a conclusion by summer 2027, while comprehensive wildfire liability reform has not been enacted and Fitch revised its outlook to negative during the quarter. Results were in line, but the forward narrative is dominated by unresolved policy risk and deferred capital spending.

negative_highlights: VLCC freight Gulf Coast to Asia averaging $30-$35/bbl versus a ~$5/bbl 2025 average, dislocating global crude pricing and pressuring North Atlantic/West Coast sourcing
Q4 Gulf Coast throughput guide of 1.855-1.905 MMbpd is below the 3 MMbpd system average run rate, and the Port Arthur DHT unit is not expected back until roughly year-end at ~$250 million repair cost
Management flagged risk that a run-up in crude prices could compress diesel cracks, and demand destruction has not yet appeared despite elevated prices
positive_highlights: Net income of $6.8 billion ($23.89/share), up from $1.1 billion ($3.53) in Q3 2025, with refining operating income of $8.8 billion versus $1.6 billion
Renewable diesel operating income of $353 million versus a $28 million loss a year ago; ethanol operating income of $272 million versus $183 million
Adjusted operating cash flow of $7.3 billion; debt-to-capitalization net of cash of 4%, with $9.8 billion cash and $5.3 billion additional liquidity
summary: Valero reported Q3 2026 net income of $6.8 billion, or $23.89 per share, versus $1.1 billion ($3.53) a year earlier, with refining operating income of $8.8 billion versus $1.6 billion. Renewable diesel swung to $353 million operating income from a $28 million loss, and ethanol rose to $272 million from $183 million. Operating cash flow was $6.9 billion ($7.3 billion adjusted), and Q4 throughput guidance across the four regions totals roughly 2.88-2.98 MMbpd with refining cash opex of about $4.85/bbl; full-year capital guidance was reiterated at approximately $2 billion. Management cited record refining utilization, a quarterly ethanol production record, and record Venezuelan crude processing, while flagging that freight costs (VLCC Gulf Coast to Asia at $30-$35/bbl versus a $5/bbl 2025 average) and ULSD/D4 volatility introduce near-term noise.

negative_highlights: Neptune second-half revenue now seen slightly down versus the prior modest-growth outlook, with mechanical-heavy mix pressuring revenue and margin likely into Q4
Core EBITDA margin contracted 30 bps, with TEP segment margin down 90 bps year-over-year
Free cash flow of $805M fell 4% year-over-year on bond interest coupon timing and a collections lag at Illumia during its ERP implementation
positive_highlights: DEPS of $5.89 rose 15% and came in above the guided range of $5.75-$5.80
Full-year DEPS guidance raised and narrowed by $0.15 at the midpoint, and up $0.95 from the original guide
TEP organic revenue grew 10% on exceptional NDI growth and strong Verathon performance (BFlex, GlideScope, BladderScan)
summary: Roper reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $2.2B, up 8% total and 7% organic, with EBITDA of $864M (39.8% margin) up 7% and DEPS of $5.89 up 15%, above the guided $5.75-$5.80 range. Full-year DEPS guidance was raised and narrowed to $22.35-$22.40, a $0.15 increase at the midpoint and $0.95 above the original guide, with Q4 DEPS set at $5.95-$6.00 and full-year organic growth in the 6% area. Core EBITDA margin slipped 30 bps as TEP fell 90 bps on a mechanical-meter mix shift at Neptune, which now sees second-half revenue slightly down versus the prior modest-growth outlook; free cash flow fell 4% on interest timing and an Illumia ERP-related collections lag. Management flagged solid AI product momentum and $436M deployed across three bolt-ons, with leverage down to 2.9x and over $6B of deployment capacity.

negative_highlights: Q4 AISC guided to ~$1,900/oz, the highest of the year, driven by sustaining capital timing, lower silver credits, and fuel inflation.
2027 unit costs expected to trend higher on macro headwinds and ~30% lower Penasquito silver production versus 2026.
Red Chris Block Cave carries $4.2-4.8 billion development capital with first commercial production targeted for 2033.
positive_highlights: Adjusted net income of $2.20 per share was a Q3 record, with $1.9 billion free cash flow and $4 billion adjusted EBITDA.
Full-year gold AISC guidance improved to ~$1,520/oz, roughly 10% better than the guidance given at the start of the year.
~$1.6 billion of shares repurchased since last call under the $6 billion program; share count down >115 million (~10%) since February 2024, with $2.8 billion remaining.
summary: Newmont reported Q3 2026 gold production of ~1.3 Moz plus 23,000 tons copper and 11 Moz silver, with $1.9 billion free cash flow, $2.20 adjusted EPS (a Q3 record), and $4 billion adjusted EBITDA at a realized gold price of $4,317/oz; AISC was $1,454/oz. Full-year production, capital, and cost guidance were maintained to improved — AISC guidance was trimmed to ~$1,520/oz, ~10% better than the start of the year. Q4 production is guided to 1.4 Moz (strongest quarter) but Q4 AISC jumps to ~$1,900/oz, and 2027 unit costs are expected to trend higher on inflation and a ~30% decline in Penasquito silver output, even as 2027 production grows low-to-mid single digits.

negative_highlights: Total sales were flat year-over-year and base sales fell 2%, with utility water base sales down 3% on lower AMI-related product sales
Free cash flow fell to $40.3 million from $48.2 million a year ago, with working capital at 23.6% of sales and above-average inventory still to be worked down
Management confirmed electronic component cost and availability pressures tied to AI/data center demand have escalated further and have not abated
positive_highlights: Gross margin expanded 120 bps to 41.9% and base gross margin of 42.1% landed at the top of the 39-42% normalized range
Base operating margin rose 130 bps to 20.9% and EPS grew 4% to $1.24 despite flat total sales
Base sales rose 5% sequentially as awarded projects (including PRASA) began shipping, and management expects Q4 base sales growth both sequentially and year-over-year
summary: Q3 total sales were $235.9 million, flat year-over-year, with base sales down 2% ex-UDlive ($5.6 million contribution) but up 5% sequentially as awarded projects ramped. Gross margin rose 120 bps to 41.9% and operating margin expanded 60 bps to 20.2% (base operating margin 20.9%, up 130 bps), with diluted EPS of $1.24, up 4% from $1.19. Management guides Q4 to sequential and year-over-year base sales growth and expects low single-digit full-year organic decline, with high single-digit growth framed for 2027. Electronic component cost and availability pressures escalated but were mitigated; free cash flow fell to $40.3 million from $48.2 million.

negative_highlights: Construction costs up roughly 5%-10% and still rising, pressuring development economics
California markets (14% of NOI) remain flat to negative on absorption and rents
Cap rates on acquisitions have moved up roughly 20-30 bps, and $695 million of forward equity is outstanding to fund investment activity
positive_highlights: FFO per share of $2.45 beat guidance midpoint by $0.04 and rose 7.9% YoY, with year-to-date FFO/share up 7.7%
Full-year 2026 FFO guidance midpoint raised $0.06 to $9.65; Q4 midpoint of $2.50 is $0.02 above prior projection
Record 2.9 million sq ft of second-gen leases signed with re-leasing spreads of 36% GAAP / 21% cash, and cash same-store NOI guidance raised 70 bps to 7.5%
summary: EastGroup reported Q3 FY2026 FFO of $2.45/share, $0.04 above guidance midpoint and up 7.9% YoY, on 96.5% quarter-end occupancy and cash same-store NOI growth of 7.1%. Management raised full-year 2026 FFO midpoint by $0.06 to $9.65 (7.5% growth over 2025), lifted cash same-store NOI guidance by 70 bps to 7.5%, and increased development starts by $65 million to a record $390 million plus acquisitions guidance by $145 million to $360 million. Re-leasing spreads were strong at 36% GAAP / 21% cash, and the company set a record 2.9 million sq ft of second-generation leases. Financing activity included $485 million of forward equity agreements in the quarter, bringing outstanding forwards to $695 million at ~$202/share.

negative_highlights: PA&T segment margin contracted as expected on project mix and Johnson Matthey Catalyst dilution, with Q4 guided to ~21.5% and first half 2027 similar before expanding
Total company orders grew only 3% organically on a normalized basis, and book-to-bill was just 1.0
Industrial automation product sales were roughly flat amid utility meter deployment deferrals; inflation elevated and expected to persist into first half 2027
positive_highlights: Organic sales grew 7%, above the high end of Investor Day targets, with all three segments growing
Segment margin expanded 370 bps to 21.3% and adjusted EPS rose 34% to $2.27
Full-year guidance raised across organic growth (to 4-5% from 3-4%), adjusted EPS ($8.40-$8.45, +$0.23 midpoint) and FCF ($2.1 billion); low end of EPS range now above prior high end
summary: Honeywell's first quarter as a standalone pure-play automation company delivered 7% organic sales growth, above the high end of its Investor Day targets, with segment margin up 370 bps to 21.3% and adjusted EPS of $2.27, up 34% year-over-year. The company raised full-year 2026 guidance across all metrics: organic growth to 4-5% from 3-4%, adjusted EPS to $8.40-$8.45 (a $0.23 midpoint improvement, with the low end above the prior high end), free cash flow up $100 million to $2.1 billion, and margin tightened to the high end of 20.5%. PA&T grew 8% organically and Industrial Automation 4%, while all remaining stranded costs are now expected to be eliminated by end of 2026, roughly six months early. Q4 organic growth is guided to 5-6% and orders to high single digits excluding last year's large LNG award.

negative_highlights: Diluted EPS fell to $1.36 from $1.43 in the prior quarter and $1.54 a year ago, due primarily to M&A expenses and a $2.1 million securities sale loss.
Delinquent loans rose to 0.56% of total loans, up 5 bps linked quarter and from 0.39% a year ago.
Non-interest income fell $2.8 million sequentially on lower mortgage banking and SBA gain-on-sale activity, and non-interest expense rose $7.7 million, including $4.9 million of M&A costs.
positive_highlights: Organic loan growth of $235 million, about 8% annualized for the legacy portfolio, with originations up 61% year over year.
Organic deposit growth of $463 million, about 13% annualized, and core deposits representing 90% of total deposits; all FHLB advances repaid.
Core pre-tax pre-provision earnings rose $4.2 million, or 7%, sequentially to $68.6 million.
summary: Banner reported Q3 FY2026 diluted EPS of $1.36, down from $1.54 a year ago, with the decline attributed to merger and acquisition expenses and a $2.1 million loss on the sale of securities acquired from Pacific Financial. Core pre-tax pre-provision earnings were $68.6 million versus $67.8 million a year ago, and revenue from core operations was $179 million, up 6%. NIM was essentially flat at 4.14% versus 4.13% prior quarter; loans grew $1 billion with $766 million from the acquisition and $235 million organic (about 8% annualized). Management guided to some NIM expansion in Q4, mid-single-digit loan growth through 2026 and 2027, and 40% Pacific Financial cost synergies by mid-2027, while noting uncertain rate trajectory and fierce pricing competition.

negative_highlights: Protiviti adjusted revenue fell 3% YoY, with U.S. Protiviti down 5%
Adjusted SG&A rose to 33.8% of revenue from 33.5% a year ago
Contract Talent volumes remain down YoY, with growth driven by bill rates (+3.6%) rather than hours worked
positive_highlights: Adjusted EPS of $0.49 rose 14% YoY, the first quarterly EPS increase since 2022
Talent Solutions returned to adjusted YoY growth (+2%) for the first time since 2022, with Permanent Placement up 6%
Adjusted operating income rose to $73 million (5.3% of revenue) from $61 million (4.5%) a year ago
summary: Robert Half reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $1.359 billion, roughly flat year-over-year on an adjusted basis, with adjusted EPS of $0.49 up 14% from $0.43 — the first year-over-year EPS increase since 2022. Talent Solutions returned to adjusted growth (+2%), driven by Permanent Placement (+6%) and Contract (+1%), while Protiviti declined 3%. Q4 guidance calls for revenue of $1.285-1.385 billion (midpoint +3% adjusted) and EPS of $0.36-0.46 (midpoint $0.41, +30% YoY), with Talent Solutions guided up 1-5% and Protiviti flat to up 4%. Adjusted operating margin expanded to 5.3% from 4.5%, helped by gross margin gains and prior cost actions.

negative_highlights: Net room growth outlook narrowed to approximately 4% from 4%-4.5%, reflecting terminations and the Revo exit
International RevPAR still declined 3% constant currency and China RevPAR fell 10% on soft Tier 2 city demand
About 9,100 Revo rooms have already left the system, with only 20%-25% of the original ~22,000 expected to be retained
positive_highlights: U.S. RevPAR up 6% YoY, nearly 400 bps better sequentially and ahead of second-half expectations, with occupancy +300 bps and ADR +280 bps
Royalty and franchise fees grew 6%, back in line with the algo after prior Revo/timing noise, with Q4 expected to match Q3 growth
Raised low end of global RevPAR outlook by 50 bps to 0.5%-1% and lifted revenue and adjusted EBITDA guidance by $5M at the bottom; board added $400M to buyback authorization
summary: Wyndham reported Q3 FY2026 net revenues of $410 million, up 7% YoY, with adjusted EBITDA of $207 million (+5% comparable) and adjusted diluted EPS of $1.43 (+9% comparable). U.S. RevPAR rose 6% (roughly 400 bps of sequential improvement) while global constant-currency RevPAR grew 2%, and royalty and franchise fees grew 6%, back in line with the algo. Guidance was raised at the low end: global RevPAR outlook to 0.5%-1% (+50 bps), revenue to $1.48B-$1.5B and adjusted EBITDA to $740M-$745M (each +$5M at the bottom), with adjusted EPS of $4.84-$4.92. Net room growth was narrowed to approximately 4% from 4%-4.5% on substandard-room terminations and Revo exits, and the board added $400M to the buyback authorization.

negative_highlights: Contract volume in North America pest remains negative, with the 3.1% contract growth attributed largely to pricing
CFO Paul Edgecliffe-Johnson is retiring January 31, with an interim CFO only if a permanent successor is not in place by then
Management stepped back from the 20% North America margin target for 2027, citing reinvestment of savings into growth
positive_highlights: Residential lead flow decline narrowed to 1% in September from a mid-to-high single-digit decline in July and August, with October tracking similarly
International pest control organic growth strengthened to 5.7%, with the UK sustaining high single-digit organic contract growth
Board approved a $200m share buyback, funded by SOLitude disposal proceeds, with leverage back inside the 2x-2.5x target range at the half-year
summary: Rentokil reported Q3 group revenue of $1.9bn with 3.4% organic growth, split North America 3.2% and International 3.7%; North America pest organic growth was 2.4% with contracts +3.1% and jobbing +2.6%, while North America business services grew 9.6% organically and is guided to moderate toward mid-single digits. Management said full-year profits should be in line with current market expectations, with no change to guidance, and reiterated that it will step back from the 20% North America margin target for 2027 while investing in growth. The board approved a $200m buyback funded by the SOLitude disposal proceeds, and CFO Paul Edgecliffe-Johnson announced his retirement effective January 31. Positives on sequential lead-flow improvement (residential lead decline narrowed to -1% in September from mid-to-high single digits in July/August) are offset by still-negative contract volumes, an unresolved North America margin path and CFO turnover.

negative_highlights: Full-year guidance was only tightened, with the low end up a penny and top end unchanged, as Refuel was largely revenue-neutral to run-rate guidance
Pipeline shrank to $75 million as rapid capital-cost increases forced repricing and possible deal fallout
Net debt to EBITDA at 5.2x (5.0x including forward equity), near the top of the 4.5x-5.5x target range
positive_highlights: Year-to-date investments reached $502.3 million at a 7.2% initial cash yield, driving 21% YoY growth in annualized base rent
AFFO per share of $1.89 for the first nine months grew 5% YoY, and G&A ratio improved 85 bps to 8.9%
Portfolio occupancy was 99.7% with 10.8-year weighted average lease term and trailing 12-month rent coverage of 2.5x
summary: Getty reported Q3 2026 AFFO per share of $0.64, up 3.2% YoY, and $1.89 for the first nine months, up 5%. Full-year AFFO guidance was tightened to $2.53-$2.54 from $2.52-$2.54, and the board raised the quarterly dividend 3.1% to $0.50. Year-to-date investments reached $502.3 million at a 7.2% initial cash yield, including the $261 million Refuel sale-leaseback, but management flagged rapid increases in capital costs, a pipeline down to $75 million, and the revenue-neutral nature of Refuel to guidance. Net debt to EBITDA was 5.2x, or 5.0x including unsettled forward equity, within the 4.5x-5.5x target range.

First Merchants reported Q3 net income of $67.8M, or $1.09 per diluted share ($1.10 adjusted), up 11% YoY, with net interest margin expanding 6 bps to 3.44% and adjusted pre-tax pre-provision earnings of $83.7M (up 19% YoY). Deposits grew 4.2% annualized while loan growth was softer at 1.8% annualized; management guided to mid-single-digit loan growth in Q4 and a stable Q4 margin, with full-year net charge-offs now expected at 38-40 bps versus prior 40-45 bps. Non-interest expense of $116.3M came in above prior guidance on higher marketing and health insurance, and Q4 is expected to run at that elevated level. Credit activity remained elevated with ~$29M of charge-offs tied to previously reserved credits and two newly nonaccrual relationships totaling $22.7M that had specific reserves established in prior quarters.

negative_highlights: Book value fell 17% to $14.55 per share with a -12.9% total economic return for the quarter
GAAP net loss of $327 million ($2.26 per share) as OAS widened 20 bps, ~80% in September
Leverage rose to 8.2x at quarter-end with net duration at 0.38 years
positive_highlights: Distributable earnings of $0.71 per share covered the $0.72 quarterly dividend
Prepayment speeds averaged 8.5 CPR, down 25% from the prior quarter, improving convexity
Liquidity was ample at $1.02 billion with repo-to-SOFR spreads tight and swap hedge ratio at 89%
summary: ARMOUR reported a Q3 FY2026 GAAP net loss of $327 million, or $2.26 per common share, with distributable earnings of $0.71 per share and net interest income of $83.7 million. Book value fell 17% to $14.55 per share (est. $14.65 as of Oct 19) and total economic return was -12.9% as mortgage spreads widened sharply, ~80% of the OAS widening in September. Management kept the $0.24 monthly dividend and said earnings available for distribution should be in the range of the dividend for the coming quarter, while leverage was 8.2x at quarter-end and 7.9x as of Oct 19. The company sold ~$900 million of DUS and seasoned MBS in late September to preserve liquidity and raised ~$205.7 million of common capital via ATM earlier in the quarter.

negative_highlights: Q4 gross margin guided to ~33% from ~40% full-year level on ocean freight and cost inflation, with freight relief assumed but not guaranteed
Supply constraints cut service levels; U.S. Vita Coco shipments grew 8% against 23% retail scan growth, leaving deferred sales
Pricing to recover structural cost increases is deferred to Q1 2027, leaving gross margin exposed in the interim
positive_highlights: Net sales rose 34% YoY to $244M, with organic growth of 18% and EPS of $0.58 vs $0.40 a year ago
Full-year net sales and adjusted EBITDA guidance raised to $810-820M and $170-175M respectively
International net sales grew 48%, with Vita Coco coconut water up 57% and Germany growing over 100%
summary: Net sales rose 34% YoY to $244M (organic +18%), with Vita Coco coconut water +15% and private label +152%, Copra contributing $29M; Q3 diluted EPS was $0.58 vs $0.40 and adjusted EBITDA $53M (22% of sales) vs $32M (18%). Full-year guidance was raised to net sales of $810-820M and adjusted EBITDA of $170-175M, with gross margin held at ~40%. However, Q4 gross margin is guided to ~33% due to ocean freight and cost inflation, and pricing to return to target margins does not take effect until Q1 2027. Supply constraints reduced service levels, with U.S. branded shipments lagging 23% retail scan growth.

negative_highlights: FDA declined the DM sBLA on ALKIVIA, which missed its primary endpoint, requiring an additional registrational study of undisclosed duration and cost
UNITY Sjögren's program stopped for futility, with ~500 patients at week 24 and the dataset not yet in hand
FY2026 R&D+SG&A guidance raised to ~$4B, a 45% YoY increase including $150M Forte transaction costs and ~$50M of additional FB-102 spend
positive_highlights: Product net sales of $1.7B grew 54% YoY and 13% QoQ, with US up 16% QoQ at broadly consistent net pricing
Adjusted for $150M in Forte transaction costs, operating margin was 37% versus 28% as reported, with revenue growth outpacing the 5% underlying OpEx increase
Seronegative MG launch secured ~96% of covered lives, with ~10% of seronegative prescribers new to VYVGART and a halo driving seropositive prescribing
summary: Product net sales were $1.7B, up 54% YoY and 13% QoQ, with US net sales of $1.5B (+16% QoQ on broadly consistent net pricing) and RoW growing 70% YoY. Operating profit was $486M (28% margin; 37% adjusting for $150M Forte transaction costs), and cash stood at $3.7B after a net $2.1B Forte payment. FY2026 combined R&D+SG&A guidance rose to approximately $4B, a 45% YoY increase, with roughly half the raise tied to Forte/FB-102; CFO flagged roughly half that growth rate as a 2027 placeholder ahead of JPMorgan. On the negative side, the DM sBLA was not accepted on ALKIVIA (missed primary endpoint) and requires an additional registrational study, and the UNITY Sjögren's program hit a futility stop with data not yet in hand.

negative_highlights: PAMA's 2027 preliminary rate cuts are estimated at roughly 1% of total revenue (about $120-$125 million), with 775 of 1,550 codes facing the maximum 15% cut.
Total revenue per requisition fell 4.2% YoY due to Corewell and Fresenius mix; excluding that mix, it rose only 1.7%, down from 2.9% in Q2, partly on low-price single-test requisitions.
The company disclosed an 8-K regarding unauthorized access to a test ordering system; financial impact is not yet quantified and the investigation is in early stages.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 10% to $3.1 billion with organic diagnostic revenue up 10.1% and total volume up 14.5% (organic up 14.4%).
Adjusted EPS rose 15.4% to $3.00 and adjusted operating margin expanded 40 bps to 16.7%, driven by organic growth and Invigorate productivity.
Full-year 2026 revenue and EPS guidance was raised and narrowed, with consumer health growth expected to exceed 30% and the Apple Health partnership launching later this year.
summary: Quest reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $3.1 billion, up 10% YoY, with diagnostic information services up 10.2% (10.1% organic). Adjusted EPS rose 15.4% to $3.00 versus $2.60, and adjusted operating margin expanded 40 bps to 16.7%. Management raised and narrowed full-year 2026 guidance to revenue of $12.065-$12.105 billion (9.3%-9.7% growth) and adjusted EPS of $11.25-$11.35, citing continued momentum. The primary overhang is the 2027 PAMA preliminary rate cut, estimated at roughly 1% of revenue (~$120-$125 million), which management is working to offset and reform via the RESULTS Act.

negative_highlights: Solid waste unit volumes declined 1.2% year-over-year, with roll-off pulls down ~2.5% and declines in all regions except the Western U.S.
Higher diesel costs created a ~30 bps margin drag and drove ~$30 million in surcharges; Q4 margin guided to 33.3%, a tougher year-over-year comparison

Free cash flow guidance unchanged despite higher EBITDA, partly due to ~$40 million higher interest expense from $1 billion in buybacks; C&D and residential construction activity described as struggling
positive_highlights: Revenue of $2.638 billion beat expectations, up 7.3% year-over-year with 5.5% core price and 1.3% surcharge contribution
Underlying adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 50 bps to 34.3% excluding fuel, despite surging diesel costs; reported margin 34%
Full-year 2026 outlook raised to ~$10.09 billion revenue and ~$3.345 billion adjusted EBITDA; dividend raised 10%, 16th consecutive double-digit increase
summary: Waste Connections reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $2.638 billion, up 7.3% year-over-year, and adjusted EBITDA of $895.8 million (34% margin, up 20 bps reported, 50 bps underlying excluding a 30 bps fuel drag). Adjusted EBITDA rose 7.9%, and management raised full-year 2026 outlook to ~$10.09 billion revenue and ~$3.345 billion adjusted EBITDA (33.2% margin), citing Q3 outperformance, acquisition contributions, and commodity tailwinds. The company also authorized a 10% dividend increase (16th consecutive double-digit raise) and has repurchased over $1 billion in shares year-to-date. Preliminary 2027 framework calls for mid-to-high single-digit revenue growth, normalized margin expansion, and double-digit adjusted FCF per share growth; Q4 guidance implies revenue of ~$2.52 billion and 33.3% margin, a tougher comparison.

negative_highlights: Thom Browne revenues fell 7% to EUR 45 million, with DTC down 7% and wholesale down 11% organically
Thom Browne Q3 hit by sharp deterioration in Asian demand and the absence of the ASICS collaboration versus prior year
Management said margin moved sideways and that they are not cutting costs to stay in guidance, limiting operating leverage
positive_highlights: Zegna brand revenues rose 13% to EUR 284 million with DTC up 16% and positive performance across all regions
Group DTC grew 11% and DTC rose to 85% of branded revenues from 82% a year earlier
Zegna Chinese cluster accelerated to double-digit growth in Q3, with Hong Kong, Shanghai, Hangzhou and Chengdu cited as outperformers
summary: Group Q3 FY2026 revenues reached EUR 434 million, up 8% organic, led by Zegna brand at EUR 284 million (+13%) and Zegna DTC +16% across all regions; TOM FORD FASHION grew 5% to EUR 70 million while Thom Browne fell 7% to EUR 45 million on a challenging Greater China and wholesale environment. DTC rose 11% group-wide and now represents 85% of branded revenues versus 82% prior year. Guidance was reiterated rather than raised: Zegna wholesale expected down low-teens for the year, TOM FORD FASHION wholesale low-single-digit growth, and the prior EUR 2.2 billion revenue / EUR 250 million adjusted EBIT targets reaffirmed at the low end. Management flagged that Thom Browne's full-year loss will be smaller than the H1 loss, a modest improvement versus prior expectations, but noted margin moved sideways as the group continues investing rather than cutting costs.

negative_highlights: Full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance cut to $370-410 million from $455-495 million, driven by the $77 million in warranty charges
Adjusted free cash flow guidance reduced to $90-130 million from $170-210 million; YTD adjusted FCF was -$4 million versus $215 million in the prior-year period
Memory and other component inflation, including ~$10 million of Q3 cost leakage from PCBs and other electronics, is expected to persist and exceed Investor Day assumptions in 2027
positive_highlights: Sales grew 6% year-over-year to $970 million against customer-weighted production down ~5%, delivering ~10 points of growth over market
Excluding the $77 million warranty charges, adjusted EBITDA was $123 million or 12.7% of sales, up from 12.1% in Q2 and $119 million in the year-ago quarter
Completed $200 million accelerated share repurchase, reducing shares ~7.5%, and paid $9 million in dividends, returning $209 million in the quarter
summary: Visteon reported Q3 FY2026 sales of $970 million, up 6% year-over-year against customer-weighted production down ~5%, for roughly 10 points of growth over market. Adjusted EBITDA was $46 million (4.7% of sales) after $77 million of warranty charges on two instrument cluster programs; excluding them EBITDA was $123 million (12.7%) versus $119 million a year ago. Full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance was cut to $370-410 million from $455-495 million, and adjusted free cash flow guidance lowered to $90-130 million from $170-210 million, though sales guidance was nudged up to $3.8-3.85 billion with the midpoint $25 million above prior trending. Management flagged a second wave of PCB and electronic component inflation (~$10 million leakage in Q3), expectations that 2027 memory costs exceed Investor Day assumptions, and $6 billion full-year bookings target retained despite roughly $1 billion of Q3 bookings shifting out.

First Industrial reported Q3 2026 NAREIT FFO of $0.80/share versus $0.76 a year ago, with cash same-store NOI growth of 5.6% excluding termination fees. Management raised the full-year FFO midpoint guidance by a penny to $3.11-$3.15 (or $3.15-$3.19 excluding $0.04 of proxy advisory costs), and raised full-year cash same-store NOI growth guidance by 75 bps at the midpoint to 6.25%-6.75%. In-service occupancy of 94.1% exceeded the 93.5% forecast, but Q4 development leasing expectations were trimmed by about 150,000 sq ft and pushed into 2027. The key message shift was 2027 renewal spreads: the 16% cash increase achieved on 45% of 2027 expirations is expected to be broadly representative of the full year, well below the 40.5% commenced spreads year to date in 2026, which management framed as a reset off COVID-era peak rents.

SS&C reported Q3 FY2026 adjusted revenue of $1.691B, up 7.8% (5.2% organic), adjusted diluted EPS of $1.78 up 14.8%, and record adjusted EBITDA of $674.8M (39.9% margin, up 40 bps). Full-year 2026 guidance was raised: revenue of $6.736-6.776B with 5.5% organic growth at the midpoint, adjusted EPS of $7.11-7.17 (~16.3% growth), and EBITDA margin expansion of 90 bps for the year with a 41% exit margin. Q4 guidance implies organic growth decelerating to 4% at the midpoint, attributed to a strong prior-year Q4 comparison and timing of large mandates. The Intelligent Automation & Analytics segment declined 4.5% organically, the main soft spot against an otherwise solid quarter.

negative_highlights: Non-accrual loans rose $16.6 million to just over $32 million (0.55% of loans), driven by an $11.8 million transportation C&I relationship, lifting NPAs/assets to 0.39% from 0.19%

Commercial loan pipeline fell to $399 million from $628 million last quarter and $511 million a year ago; $103 million of affordable housing projects left the pipeline, with four lost to competitors on pricing
CRE concentration rose to 308% of total loans and TCE declined to 9.3% from 9.7% on higher unrealized securities losses; CFO expects less buyback activity in Q4
positive_highlights: Net interest margin expanded to 4.05% from 3.99% in Q2 and 3.64% in Q3 2025, with net interest income up $2.4 million QoQ
Total deposits increased $148 million and non-maturity deposits rose $190 million; cost of interest-bearing deposits fell to 1.65% from 1.67%
Non-interest expense decreased $2.4 million on $2.3 million lower merger costs, with Q4 expense guided to $55-56 million; net charge-offs were just $381,000 (0.03% annualized)
summary: Heritage reported Q3 net interest margin of 4.05% (up from 3.99% in Q2 and 3.64% a year ago) and net interest income up $2.4 million QoQ, with loans up $133 million and deposits up $148 million; non-interest expense fell $2.4 million on lower merger costs, and the Kitsap systems conversion was completed. Credit deteriorated: non-accrual loans rose $16.6 million to just over $32 million (0.55% of loans), NPAs/assets rose to 0.39% from 0.19%, criticized loans rose to 4.19%, and a $2.3 million provision was booked, about $1 million of it tied to new non-accruals. Management guided Q4 expenses to $55-56 million, expects mid-single-digit annualized loan growth for the next couple of quarters, and sees margin and NII moving higher, but the commercial pipeline fell to $399 million from $628 million and the CRE concentration rose to 308%, prompting a slower buyback pace in Q4 (341,000 shares for $10 million were repurchased in Q3, and a new 5% program was approved).

negative_highlights: International organic revenue declined slightly with adjusted operating margin down 40 bps on lower volume and unfavorable mix; Europe/Germany weakness persists with outlook unchanged at down low single digits
Residential growth was price-driven with end-market volume described as flattish, and management does not anticipate a strong recovery given inflation and high interest rates
Q4 relies on a margin step-up partly from easier comps; 2027 pricing and inflation magnitude explicitly deferred to February
positive_highlights: Adjusted EPS of $2.60 rose 13% YoY ($0.30), with adjusted operating margin up 60 bps to 24.7%
Americas organic revenue grew 9.1% with non-residential up low double digits on both price and volume; Americas organic outlook raised to 7%-8%
Full-year adjusted EPS outlook raised to $9.05-$9.10 and reported revenue raised to 9.5%-10.5%
summary: Allegion reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of approximately $1.2 billion, up 9.6% reported and 7.2% organic, with adjusted operating margin of 24.7% (up 60 bps) and adjusted EPS of $2.60, up 13% YoY. Americas revenue rose 11.7% reported / 9.1% organic on low-double-digit non-residential growth and mid-single-digit residential, while International was up 1.8% reported but down slightly organically on Western Europe weakness. Management raised full-year reported revenue guidance to 9.5%-10.5%, organic growth to 5%-6%, and adjusted EPS to $9.05-$9.10, from prior ranges. Q4 embeds a margin step-up but commentary on 2027 pricing/inflation magnitude was deferred to February.

negative_highlights: Consolidated pre-tax operating income fell to $227 million from $248 million and operating EPS dropped to $0.73 from $0.78
Consolidated combined ratio widened to 96.1% from 95.3% as favorable prior-year development fell to 1.1 points from 2.5 points; Specialty combined ratio rose to 96.0% from 94.8%
A $20 million credit loss charge added 1.4 points to the Specialty expense ratio, and commercial auto loss ratio rose to 71.0% from 68.3%
positive_highlights: Title pre-tax operating income rose to $50 million from $46 million with premium and fee revenue up 7.3% and the loss ratio improving 60 bps
Specialty net premiums written grew 10.5%, with commercial auto and general liability rate increases in the mid-teens and commercial auto retention stable near 80%
Bought back $114 million of shares in the quarter plus $60 million since quarter-end, with roughly $460 million remaining on the repurchase program
summary: Consolidated pre-tax operating income fell to $227 million from $248 million, with operating EPS of $0.73 versus $0.78 and the combined ratio widening to 96.1% from 95.3%; favorable reserve development shrank to 1.1 points from 2.5 points. Specialty pre-tax operating income slipped to $204 million from $208 million on a 96.0 combined ratio (94.8% prior year), while Title rose to $50 million from $46 million on 7.3% premium and fee growth. Net premiums written grew 10.5% in Specialty but only 4.4% excluding ECM and the auto warranty write-up. Management guides to a competitive P&C market and flagged higher mortgage rates as a risk to Title volumes, with no formal EPS or combined ratio guidance issued.

negative_highlights: Cash used in operating activities was $13.6 million, driven largely by a substantial wafer prepayment, leaving $109.9 million in cash and equivalents
Q4 guidance implies broadband and connectivity declining seasonally, with sequential revenue growth of roughly 10-19% dependent on infrastructure
Management declined to provide 2027 revenue guidance despite discussing bookings, and noted internal qual-resource constraints limit how many 1.6T programs can run simultaneously
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 72% YoY to $218.1 million and 29% sequentially; infrastructure reached ~$125 million, up 210% YoY and now larger than all other categories combined
2026 optical data center revenue outlook raised to $250 million-$270 million, with bookings extending into 2028 and 26-28 week optical lead times
Non-GAAP gross margin rose to 60.0% and non-GAAP operating margin reached 29.5%, with Q4 gross margin guided higher at 59-62%
summary: MaxLinear reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $218.1 million, up 29% sequentially and 72% year-on-year, with infrastructure revenue roughly $125 million (+210% YoY) now larger than all other categories combined. Non-GAAP gross margin was 60.0%, non-GAAP operating margin 29.5%, and non-GAAP diluted EPS $0.62 versus GAAP EPS of $0.30. Management raised its 2026 optical data center revenue outlook to $250-270 million and guided Q4 revenue to $240-260 million with non-GAAP gross margin of 59-62%. Operating cash flow was negative $13.6 million, reflecting a large prepayment for wafers tied to committed 2027 backlog.

negative_highlights: Dedicated Transportation Solutions operating revenue fell 1% on lower fleet count, and segment EBT declined versus prior year
Supply Chain Solutions revenue growth of 9% was partially offset by lost automotive business, and EBT margin of 8.1% reflects drag from new business ramping up
Free cash flow forecast of $700-$800 million held unchanged despite the EPS raise; Q3 used vehicle tractor pricing was inflated ~700 bps by retail mix shift
positive_highlights: Full-year 2026 comparable EPS guidance raised to $14.85-$15.05 from $14.40-$14.80, with ROE guidance lifted to 18%-19%
Comparable EPS up 21% to $4.33; FMS EBT up 21% to $177 million at a 13.2% margin, at the low-teens target early in the cycle
Rental utilization rose 700 bps YoY to 77% on a 12% smaller average fleet, with rental pricing up 4%; used tractor pricing up 19% YoY and retail mix at 61% of volume
summary: Ryder reported Q3 FY2026 comparable EPS of $4.33, up 21% YoY, on operating revenue of $2.8 billion, up 6%, marking an eighth consecutive quarter of comparable EPS growth. FMS EBT rose 21% to $177 million at a 13.2% margin, rental utilization hit 77% (up 700 bps) on a 12% smaller fleet, and used vehicle pricing rose 19% for tractors and 5% for trucks. Management raised full-year 2026 comparable EPS guidance to $14.85-$15.05 from $14.40-$14.80 and lifted the ROE forecast to 18%-19%, citing stronger Q3 results and higher expected cyclical upturn benefits of ~$40 million (from $20 million). Dedicated revenue fell 1% with lower EBT, and the full-year free cash flow forecast of $700-$800 million was unchanged.

negative_highlights: Engineered Products declined 2% organically on lower European vehicle services volumes
Clean Energy & Fueling margin roughly flat as cryogenic production ramp offset volume leverage
CST absorbed ~$40 million YTD in ramp and duplicate facility costs, and this figure will likely rise by year-end
positive_highlights: Orders up 16% YoY with growth in all five segments; trailing book-to-bill 1.08 and backlog up 35% YoY
Climate & Sustainability Technologies organic growth accelerated to 18%, with record CO2 systems revenue and data center liquid cooling strength
Imaging & Identification margins expanded 400 bps to 33% and Pumps & Process Solutions 770 bps to 34%
summary: Dover reported 7% organic growth with adjusted EPS of $2.88, up 10% YoY, and orders up 16% with a book-to-bill of 1.03. Backlog rose 35% YoY and management narrowed full-year guidance toward the upper end (5-6% organic growth, $10.60-$10.75 adjusted EPS). Segment margins were mixed: Imaging & Identification expanded 400 bps to 33% and Pumps & Process Solutions 770 bps to 34%, while Clean Energy & Fueling and CST margins were pressured by capacity ramp and ~$40 million in food retail transition costs expected to roll off into 2027. The company repurchased over $330 million of shares in the quarter and announced two bolt-on acquisitions.

negative_highlights: Connectivity & Platforms revenue -2.6% and EBITDA -4.4%; 144,000 broadband subscribers lost amid aggressive fiber promotions and a higher-than-typical volume of legacy promotional roll-offs
Theme Parks revenue -4% and EBITDA -17%, with Orlando softness continuing and expected to remain a headwind in Q4 and the first half of 2027
Over $1 billion in expected Q4 charges tied to the transformation, with no quantified savings target and share repurchases paused at least through the separation
positive_highlights: Peacock EBITDA of $261 million, up $478 million year-over-year, with revenue +34% and paid subscribers +7 million; subs held at 48 million despite an in-quarter price increase
Wireless lines up 18% year-over-year to 10.6 million, with 70% of free lines converting to paid and premium plans at ~40% of postpaid phone connects (up from 30% last quarter)
Free cash flow of $4.2 billion and adjusted EPS of $1.07; Convergence and broadband ARPU declines narrowed sequentially by 190 bps and C&P EBITDA decline narrowed 140 bps
summary: Pro forma revenue was flat and adjusted EBITDA rose ~1%, with adjusted EPS of $1.07 and $4.2 billion of free cash flow. Connectivity & Platforms revenue fell 2.6% and EBITDA fell 4.4%, with 144,000 broadband subscribers lost and 368,000 net wireless lines added; Peacock posted its second consecutive profitable quarter ($261 million EBITDA, revenue +34%, 48 million subs) and Media revenue rose 13%, while Theme Parks revenue fell 4% and EBITDA fell 17%. Management flagged a significant Q4 charge of over $1 billion tied to a broad operating and cost transformation, paused buybacks at least through the NBCUniversal/Sky separation, and guided Q4 Connectivity trends to only slight improvement, with Parks Orlando softness expected to persist into the first half of 2027.

negative_highlights: Offshore Solutions declined 13% organically on project delays and an equipment failure at a large customer, a few million dollar revenue hit
Industrial Solutions volumes were roughly flat, with construction markets down materially and European business weak; price-cost timing cost about $1-2 million
Higher incentive comp accruals cut more than 100 bps from margins year-over-year across both segments
positive_highlights: Organic sales grew 13% with Electronics organic up 18% and Semiconductor up 24%, marking a fourth straight quarter of double-digit organic growth in Electronics
Full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance raised to approximately $720 million, with implied adjusted EPS growth of more than 20%
Adjusted EBITDA margins ex metals expanded 50 bps to 28.2%, with underlying incrementals in the mid-40s% for the company and ~50% for Electronics
summary: Element Solutions reported record quarterly revenue, adjusted EBITDA and adjusted EPS, with organic net sales up 13%, constant-currency adjusted EBITDA up 29% and adjusted EPS up 22%. Electronics organic sales rose 18%, led by Semiconductor at 24%, and adjusted EBITDA margins ex pass-through metals expanded 50 bps to 28.2%. Management raised full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance to approximately $720 million, implying >20% adjusted EPS growth, with Q4 revenue implied around $175-176 million of EBITDA on normal seasonality. The quarter's negatives were concentrated in Specialties, where Industrial grew 3% on pricing with flat volumes and Offshore declined 13% on an equipment failure at a large customer.

negative_highlights: Higher Education performance fell below expectations on K-12 adoption delays and Advanced Placement timing drag
PTE/English Language Learning market 'proving tougher for longer than we expected'; Q4 return to growth now 'more uncertain than we thought'
A&Q growth expected to slow sharply into Q4 given tough comparatives and test-delivery phasing that favored Q3
positive_highlights: Group sales growth accelerated to 6% in Q3, with A&Q up 10% and Virtual Learning up 17% year-to-date
Anthropic certification program delivered over 230,000 secure tests since July launch; Google Cloud, ServiceNow and Salesforce cited as partners
Full-year EBIT range narrowed to GBP 650-675m from GBP 640-685m while retaining the same midpoint
summary: Pearson reported Q3 group sales growth accelerating to 6%, with 5% growth for the nine months year-to-date, driven principally by Assessment & Qualifications at 10% growth in Q3 (new contracts including Google Cloud and Anthropic) and Virtual Learning at 17% year-to-date. Full-year guidance was reiterated (mid-single-digit revenue growth), while the EBIT range was narrowed to GBP 650-675m from GBP 640-685m, keeping the same midpoint. Higher Education came in below expectations on K-12 adoption delays, and PTE/English Language Learning remained challenged with Q4 growth now 'more uncertain' than previously expected. The company announced a restructuring into four customer-led business units effective January 1 and two acquisitions (ITS and Workera) totaling roughly GBP 200m.

negative_highlights: Q4 EBITDA guided to $85-95 million, roughly 24-29% below Q3's $119 million, on SSR geographic mix, rig mobilization costs, and lower-margin OPG work
Net income fell 26% to $52.6 million ($0.52/share) on a one-time refinancing loss, and ADTech operating income fell 11% with margin down to 11%
Manufactured Products book-to-bill was 0.77 trailing twelve months, and 2027 guidance of $430-480 million implies a limited increase at the low end versus 2026
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA of $119 million, up 7% and the highest quarterly level since Q4 2015, in line with guidance
SSR EBITDA margin reached 39%, its highest since the 2020 resegmentation, with average ROV revenue per day up to $11,781 from $11,254
Bookings included ~$180 million of ROV/survey contracts extending to 2031, ~$160 million of Manufactured Products awards, and Navy contracts worth up to $154 million and $67 million
summary: Oceaneering reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $785 million, up 6% YoY with growth in every segment, operating income of $92 million (+7%), and adjusted EBITDA of $119 million (+7%), in line with guidance and the highest level since Q4 2015. GAAP EPS fell 26% to $0.52 on a one-time debt refinancing loss, and free cash flow of $142 million benefited from lower cash taxes and deferred capex expected to shift into Q4. Q4 EBITDA guidance is $85-95 million, well below Q3, on SSR mix and mobilization costs plus OPG project mix. Initial 2027 EBITDA guidance of $430-480 million was framed as wide and timing-driven, with management explicitly citing caution on how fast offshore spending ramps.

negative_highlights: Free cash flow fell to $261 million from $303 million a year ago, and operating cash flow declined to $268 million from $308 million, on higher cash taxes and vendor/employee payments
Expected Q3 renewal rate declined to 74.3% from 75.4% a year ago, with first-time renewing names in the mid-40% range versus previously renewed names in the mid-80% range
A $7.5 million pre-tax loss on assets held for sale lifted operating expenses to $147 million from $135 million a year ago and reduced EPS by $0.06
positive_highlights: Record 13.1 million new registrations in Q3, up from 12.7 million last quarter and 10.6 million a year ago, with the .com/.net base up 6.1% year-over-year to 182.5 million names
Domain name base growth guidance raised and narrowed to 6.5%-7% for 2026 from prior expectations
$1.14 billion returned to shareholders over the trailing 12 months, with $1.36 billion remaining authorized for buybacks and a $0.81 per share quarterly dividend declared
summary: VeriSign reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $443 million, up 5.7% year-over-year, with GAAP diluted EPS of $2.35 versus $2.27 a year ago, a figure dampened by a $7.5 million pre-tax loss on assets held for sale that cut EPS by $0.06. The combined .com/.net base reached 182.5 million names, up 6.1% year-over-year, on a record 13.1 million new registrations, and management raised and narrowed full-year domain name base growth guidance to 6.5%-7%. Full-year revenue guidance of $1.755-$1.760 billion and operating income of $1.188-$1.192 billion were updated, with the latter reflecting the $7.5 million charge. The expected Q3 renewal rate slipped to 74.3% from 75.4% a year ago on mix, and free cash flow fell to $261 million from $303 million on higher cash taxes and payments.

negative_highlights: 2027 EPS guidance of $1.75-$1.83 was reset lower at the September conference, with management citing a more competitive, higher-rate, higher-inflation environment.
Full-year fee growth was trimmed to ~31% (from an earlier range) as Q3 fee revenue of ~$730 million came in slightly below the prior target, attributed to the rate-driven capital markets impact.
Net charge-offs rose 6 bps to 31 bps on an idiosyncratic commercial charge-off; criticized assets ticked up to 4.26% and NPAs rose to 90 bps from 85 bps.
positive_highlights: NII of ~$2.1 billion rose 0.9% QoQ and 37% YoY, with NIM up 4 bps to 3.25%.
Value-added fee revenue grew more than 15% YoY; treasury management revenue up 42% YoY and debt/equity capital markets revenue up 35% YTD.
Adjusted ROTCE was 16.6% for the quarter; ~$460 million of buybacks completed YTD including $100 million in Q3.
summary: Huntington reported Q3 FY2026 with NII of ~$2.1 billion (up 0.9% QoQ, 37% YoY), NIM of 3.25% (up 4 bps QoQ), and period-end loans up 1.1% while average loans fell 0.4% QoQ. Fee revenue of roughly $730 million came in just below the prior ~$730 million target, and the full-year fee growth guide was trimmed to ~31% from an earlier 26.5%-29.5% range. Management had reset 2027 EPS guidance at a September conference to $1.75-$1.83 and on the call framed it as "tracking," citing a more competitive environment and higher-for-longer rates. Net charge-offs rose 6 bps to 31 bps on an idiosyncratic commercial credit, and criticized assets edged up to 4.26% from 4.18%.

negative_highlights: Q4 EBITDA guided to approximately $1.5 billion, roughly flat sequentially, with normal year-end seasonality offsetting self-help and lower turnarounds

Reported total volumes were down 1% YoY due to Middle East supply constraints, and Q3 self-help benefits of more than $150 million were mainly offset by margin pressure in Packaging & Specialty Plastics

MDI demand remains weak with building and construction the softest end market, and the segment is expected to move back to a longer market as industry supply disruptions resolve and new North American capacity starts up
positive_highlights: Net sales up 13% YoY with growth in all three operating segments, and Packaging & Specialty Plastics EBIT up more than $385 million YoY to about $585 million
Free cash flow of $1.1 billion in Q3 with roughly $1.3 billion sequential working capital improvement and over $400 million released against a $500 million second-half target
Additional polyethylene price nominations of $0.07 per pound in October and $0.05 in November could add about $200 million of upside to the Q4 guide
summary: Dow reported Q3 FY2026 net sales up 13% YoY with growth in every operating segment and operating EBITDA above $1.5 billion, driven by polyethylene pricing, self-help savings, and the Transform to Outperform program. Packaging & Specialty Plastics net sales rose 18% to $5.8 billion with operating EBIT of roughly $585 million, up more than $385 million YoY; Industrial Intermediates & Infrastructure sales rose 8% to $3.1 billion on 16% higher local price with EBIT of $176 million; Performance Materials & Coatings sales rose 8% to $2.3 billion with EBIT of $154 million. Q4 guidance calls for EBITDA of approximately $1.5 billion, roughly flat sequentially, as polyethylene integrated margins improve about $0.02 per pound and more than $100 million of lower turnaround spending and $100 million of sequential self-help offset normal seasonality. Free cash flow was $1.1 billion with over $400 million of working capital released, and Dow repurchased about $300 million of debt in the quarter.

negative_highlights: Loan growth was muted by $47 million of early payoffs, limiting net growth to $38 million or 4.7% annualized
Subordinated debt repricing from 3.25% fixed to SOFR+219 bps on December 1 will cost 5-6 bps per quarter of NIM
Securities portfolio carried $59.9 million, or 9.3%, of unrealized losses, and the quarter included a $1.6 million loss on securities sales
positive_highlights: EPS of $0.77 rose 26% YoY; net income up $3.3 million and pre-provision net revenue up $5.3 million or 33% YoY
NIM expanded 4 bps QoQ to 3.93% as non-interest-bearing deposits grew $30.3 million and brokered funding was reduced $25 million
Efficiency ratio improved to 55.3% from 58.2% linked-quarter, with non-interest expense down 2.4% QoQ to about $28 million, below the prior $29.6-30 million outlook
summary: Civista reported Q3 FY2026 net income of $16 million, or $0.77 per diluted share, up 26% YoY and 12% linked-quarter, with pre-provision net revenue up 33% YoY. Net interest income rose 2% QoQ to $39.4 million and NIM expanded 4 bps to 3.93%, while non-interest expense fell 2.4% QoQ and the efficiency ratio improved to 55.3% from 58.2%. Management guided to mid-single-digit loan and deposit growth into 2027, Q4 fee income of $9.0-9.5 million and Q4 expenses of $28.7-29.5 million, and flagged a sub-debt repricing costing 5-6 bps per quarter starting December. The quarter also included $1.8 million of insurance proceeds and a $1.6 million securities loss.

negative_highlights: Cost per terabyte will decline less than 10% YoY near-term due to DRAM and NAND input cost increases not yet offset by value engineering
CapEx is expected to run modestly above the 4%-6% of revenue range over the next two years for heads, media, and factory automation
positive_highlights: Revenue rose 55% YoY to $4.4 billion with Q2 guided to $5.1 billion ± $100 million, a 69% YoY increase at the midpoint
Gross margin expanded 1,420 bps YoY to 58.1% with incremental gross margins above 80%, and Q2 gross margin guided to 60%-61%
EPS of $4.64 grew 161% YoY with $1.4 billion free cash flow, a 17% dividend raise to $0.175, and $1.1 billion returned to shareholders
summary: Western Digital reported Q1 FY2027 revenue of $4.4 billion, up 55% year-over-year, with non-GAAP EPS of $4.64 (+161%), gross margin of 58.1% (+1,420 bps), and operating margin of 49.1%; free cash flow was $1.4 billion. Guidance for Q2 was guided well above the just-reported quarter at $5.1 billion ± $100 million (69% YoY at midpoint) with gross margin of 60%-61% and EPS of $5.80 ± $0.20, plus a 17% dividend increase to $0.175 per share and $1.1 billion returned to shareholders. Exabytes shipped were 248, up 22% YoY and 8% sequentially, which management called the floor with acceleration expected through FY2027 and FY2028 as the 40TB ePMR and HAMR platforms ramp. Average price per terabyte rose 28% YoY versus high-teens in the prior quarter, though cost per terabyte declined less than 10% near-term due to DRAM/NAND input cost inflation.

negative_highlights: Cost of capital has increased on both equity and debt, raising unlevered IRR expectations for new acquisitions
Lease rate slipped 10 bps sequentially to 96.4%
Management noted an uptick in national retail bankruptcies (Sleep Number, Leslie's Pool Supplies) though not in its own portfolio
positive_highlights: Raised 2026 OFFO guidance to $1.25-$1.27 per share, just over 18% growth at the midpoint
Same-property NOI accelerated to 3.4% in Q3 from 3.3% in 2025, with base rent growth of 2.8%
Full-year investments now expected to exceed the prior $1 billion target, with over $800 million acquired through last Friday
summary: Curbline raised 2026 OFFO guidance to $1.25-$1.27 per share, implying just over 18% growth at the midpoint, and now expects to exceed its prior $1 billion full-year investment target. Q3 total NOI rose 11% sequentially and over 50% year-over-year, same-property NOI accelerated to 3.4% from 3.3% in 2025, and occupancy improved to 96.4% leased and up 60 bps year-over-year. Management flagged that its cost of capital has risen and unlevered IRR hurdles have increased as borrowing rates moved higher, though it described cap rates on growth-quality assets as stickier and the deal pipeline as robust through early 2027. Liquidity stood at $895 million with net debt to EBITDA expected under 2.5x at year-end.

negative_highlights: Revenue landed in line at ~EUR 5B with no top-line beat, and Q4 revenue guide of EUR 5.2B reflects ARPU growth decelerating to 4.5%-5% on lapping prior pricing actions across 150+ markets
Social charges of EUR 22M came in EUR 13M above forecast due to share price movements
Q4 MAU guide of 818M reflects growth below last year's all-time high tied to the free-tier rollout; management declined to give 2027 guidance
positive_highlights: Subscribers reached 306M, beating guidance by 1M with net adds of 6M across all regions
Gross margin of 33% exceeded guidance by 10bps and expanded ~140bps YoY, with Q4 guided to 33.8% and full-year expansion of ~130bps
Ad-supported revenue growth accelerated to 9% from 3% in each of the first two quarters, driven by automated biddable sales
summary: Spotify reported Q3 revenue of ~EUR 5.0B, up 14% constant currency and in line with guidance, with 306M subscribers (+6M net, 1M above guidance) and MAU of 788M in line. Gross margin came in at 33%, 10bps above guidance and up ~140bps YoY, with operating income of EUR 672M (13.5% margin) and EUR 735M of quarterly free cash flow. Ad-supported revenue accelerated to 9% growth from 3% in the prior two quarters. Q4 guidance calls for 316M subscribers, EUR 5.2B revenue, and 33.8% gross margin, implying ~130bps full-year margin expansion, with OpEx growth moderating from Q3 into 2027.

negative_highlights: Organic growth of 4.4% missed the prior 6% full-year target, forcing a guidance cut to 4%-6%
Residential organic growth decelerated to 2.3% as digital lead flow weakened further; organic website traffic was down 13% in August
Gross margin contracted 90 bps to 53.5% and adjusted EBITDA margin fell to 23.5%; adjusted EPS declined 2.9% to $0.34
positive_highlights: Commercial pest control grew 7.7% (6.6% organic) with Orkin's core commercial business up over 8%
Door-to-door and relationship-driven brands performed strongly, with Fox delivering double-digit growth
Free cash flow of $235 million and 149% conversion (109% excluding the $63 million tax refund), plus a 10% dividend increase
summary: Rollins reported Q3 FY2026 total revenue growth of 6.2% with organic growth of 4.4%, below its prior 6% expectation, driven by continued deterioration in residential digital lead flow amid AI/LLM-driven search changes. Adjusted EPS fell 2.9% to $0.34, gross margin contracted 90 bps to 53.5%, and adjusted EBITDA declined 0.7% to $257 million (23.5% margin). Management cut full-year organic growth guidance to 4%-6% from 6% and now sees incremental margins of slightly positive to 10%, blaming further lead-volume declines and macro uncertainty. The company raised its dividend 10% and repurchased $120 million of shares.

negative_highlights: Non-GAAP expense guidance raised to $2.550-$2.580 billion from $2.530-$2.570 billion
Market Services operating margin fell 5 points YoY to 61%, and revenue grew only 2%
Management noted a modest softening in the IPO environment in recent weeks as some companies reassess timing
positive_highlights: Solutions revenue rose 18% to $1.2 billion and ARR grew 14% to $3.4 billion, with record Fintech ARR growth of 18%
Diluted EPS up 19% to $1.04, with operating margin at 57% and EBITDA margin at 60%, each up 1 point YoY
Index revenue up 39% on record average ETP AUM above $1.1 trillion and $141 billion in trailing-12-month net inflows
summary: Nasdaq reported Q3 2026 net revenue of $1.5 billion, up 14% YoY, with solutions revenue up 18% to $1.2 billion and ARR up 14% to $3.4 billion; diluted EPS rose 19% to $1.04 on operating and EBITDA margins of 57% and 60%, each up 1 point. Fintech delivered 16% revenue growth and record 18% ARR growth, while Capital Access Platforms grew 20% and Market Services rose 2% to a Q3 record $309 million. Full-year non-GAAP expense guidance was raised to $2.550-$2.580 billion from $2.530-$2.570 billion, reflecting the LeveL and Dasseti acquisitions plus strong year-to-date revenue. Management flagged a modest softening in the recent IPO environment, though the listings pipeline remains robust, and noted a tough Calypso comparison in Q4.

negative_highlights: Capital markets slowed notably in September; capital markets revenue expected roughly flat in Q4 and into the first half of 2027, with refinancings replacing sales and deals being retraded
Advisory growth is now expected to moderate more than anticipated 90 days ago, and 2027 growth hinges partly on the wide range of outcomes from development asset monetizations

Two enterprise facilities management accounts are being restructured in Q4, pressuring earnings, and mortgage origination grew only 1% as agency lending declined; buybacks are being slowed in anticipation of M&A
positive_highlights: Critical infrastructure services revenue grew 80%, with total infrastructure services revenue expected to reach nearly $7 billion in 2027, up more than 40% from this year
Global property sales revenue rose 28%, led by the U.S. up 37%, and advisory segment operating profit grew 16%
REI segment operating profit rose to $166 million from $73 million on data center land sales and asset monetizations; free cash flow totaled $1.8 billion on a trailing 12-month basis
summary: CBRE reported Q3 FY2026 core EPS growth of 28% on a 13% revenue increase, with advisory revenue up 11%, property sales up 28%, and BOE segment revenue up 17% (critical infrastructure services up 80%); segment operating profit in Real Estate Investments rose to $166 million from $73 million. Management maintained its 2026 core EPS guidance of $7.80-$7.90 (23% growth at midpoint) and reiterated a path to 15% core EPS growth in 2027. However, capital markets activity slowed materially in September amid higher and volatile rates, with capital markets expected roughly flat in Q4 and into the first half of 2027, advisory growth moderating versus expectations 90 days ago, and two problematic enterprise facilities accounts requiring restructuring in Q4.

negative_highlights: Full-year 2026 EPS guidance lowered to $1.95-$2.05 due to cancelling the planned ~$1 billion Q4 whole loan sale
Full-year net charge-off guidance raised to $400-$420 million from $345-$385 million, with the third-party debt resolution impact estimate up from $25 million to $45 million
Net interest income fell $34 million YoY to $339 million and provision for credit losses was $214 million, with 30+ day delinquencies up to 4.2% from 4.0% a year ago
positive_highlights: Q3 originations of $3.4 billion were the highest quarterly volume in company history, up 15% YoY, with graduate originations up 119%
NIM expanded 10 bps QoQ to 4.85% and deposit weighted average life extended to 37 months from 23 months at year-end 2025
New Sixth Street partnership commits to at least $1.5 billion in annual loan purchases for an initial three-year term, following the KKR deal
summary: Sallie Mae reported Q3 FY2026 net interest income of $339 million (down $34 million YoY) and other income of $46 million (up $15 million), with NIM of 4.85%, up 10 bps QoQ. Originations hit a record $3.4 billion, up 15% YoY, with graduate originations up 119%, and October month-to-date disbursements up 35%. Management lowered full-year 2026 EPS guidance to $1.95-$2.05 primarily because it will not execute a planned ~$1 billion loan sale in a volatile, higher-rate market, and raised full-year net charge-off guidance to $400-$420 million from $345-$385 million, citing a bigger $45 million impact (up from $25 million) from third-party debt resolution practices. Non-interest expense and origination guidance were reaffirmed, and a new Sixth Street partnership ($1.5 billion annual purchase commitment, including a $600 million seasoned seed portfolio) was announced.

negative_highlights: Company-wide revenue and EBITDA declined approximately 1% on a reported basis in Q3
Destination softness to Las Vegas intensified versus the prior four quarters, concentrated at the Orleans, where 300+ rooms were out of service daily for the past year
Guidance is only qualitative: modest Las Vegas Locals EBITDA growth depends on destination trends improving, and Suncoast is expected to contribute only very modestly in Q4
positive_highlights: Midwest & South adjusted revenue grew nearly 3% and EBITDA ~2.5% (~$5 million), with segment margins steady at 38%
Las Vegas Locals excluding Orleans and Suncoast grew revenue and EBITDA 3% with gaming revenue up 3.5% and margins at 47%
Returned ~$180 million to shareholders in Q3; share count down 9.4% YoY to 71.2 million, with leverage at 2.2x traditional / 2.7x lease-adjusted
summary: Reported company-wide revenue and EBITDA fell roughly 1% YoY; management said adjusted for the Tunica closure, Shreveport sale, Kansas Star property taxes and reduced tax pass-throughs, revenue grew 2% and EBITDA 1%. Midwest & South adjusted revenue rose ~3% with EBITDA up ~2.5% and 38% margins, and Las Vegas Locals ex-Orleans/Suncoast grew revenue and EBITDA 3% at 47% margins, but destination weakness intensified in Q3, primarily at the Orleans, alongside Hawaii storm and airfare impacts downtown. Q4 guidance is qualitative: modest Locals EBITDA growth depends on destination trends reverting to pre-Q3 levels, Suncoast rooms are out of service in Q4/Q1, while online and Managed & Other are guided to the high end of prior ranges. Capital returns continued with ~$180 million in Q3 buybacks and dividends, a 9.4% share count reduction YoY, and 2.2x traditional leverage.

negative_highlights: Investment Bank Q3 RoTE of 9.5% with income broadly flat year-on-year and income to average RWAs down 20bp to 6.1%
FICC intermediation called out as disappointing, with lower client activity in rates and credit and GBP 39m of leveraged finance marks
Barclays UK costs rose 6% on GBP 110m of SCAs, and management no longer expects UK costs to fall in 2026 versus 2025
positive_highlights: EPS up 18% year-on-year in Q3, on track for a third consecutive year of 20% EPS growth, with profit before tax up 12% to GBP 2.3bn
New GBP 500m buyback announced, taking year-to-date distributions to GBP 2.8bn, up 47% year-on-year
2027 statutory costs guided to fall to circa GBP 18.4bn with more than GBP 1.1bn of gross efficiency savings, and a 59bp MDA reduction more than offsetting 30-55bp Basel 3.1 RWA headwind
summary: Barclays reported Q3 2026 income of GBP 7.4bn, up 3% year-on-year, with profit before tax up 12% to GBP 2.3bn, EPS up 18%, and RoTE of 11.7% in the quarter and 13.8% year-to-date. It announced a GBP 500m buyback, taking year-to-date distributions to GBP 2.8bn (up 47%), and reiterated full-year targets (circa GBP 31.5bn income, high-50s cost-income ratio, >12% RoTE) with 2027 statutory costs guided down to circa GBP 18.4bn and >GBP 1.1bn of gross efficiency savings. Soft spots included flat Investment Bank income (equities +47% offsetting weaker FICC intermediation), a 9.5% IB quarterly RoTE, and a GBP 39m leveraged finance mark; management also narrowed disclosure on unquantified October structural hedge growth. The quarter roughly met plan on income while cost trajectory and capital flexibility (59bp MDA reduction) improved versus prior guidance.

negative_highlights: Q4 CASM-X guided up 4%-4.5% YoY, accelerating from Q3's 3.8%
Full-year 2026 adjusted EPS of $2.60-$2.85 implies Q4 EPS of $0.55-$0.80, a step down from Q3's $0.66
On-time performance below targets is adding cost pressure, with remediation not fully in place until 2027 schedules
positive_highlights: RASM rose 21.6% YoY, exceeding the high end of the 17.5%-19.5% guidance range and setting an all-time record
Adjusted operating margin expanded 4.8 points YoY to 5.4% despite an $820 million fuel headwind
Managed business revenue grew 29% YoY on roughly flat capacity, with passengers up about 9%
summary: Southwest reported Q3 FY2026 record operating revenue of $8.4 billion, adjusted EPS of $0.66 (up 500% YoY, above guidance midpoint), and RASM growth of 21.6% that exceeded the 17.5%-19.5% guidance range, driving a 5.4% adjusted operating margin (up 4.8 points YoY) despite an $820 million fuel headwind. Q4 guidance calls for RASM growth of 19%-21% and adjusted EPS of $0.55-$0.80, with full-year EPS of $2.60-$2.85. Q4 CASM-X is guided up 4%-4.5% on 3%-4% capacity growth, with unit cost growth expected to moderate into 2027. No full-year 2027 guidance was given, though management expressed confidence in continued margin expansion and higher aircraft deliveries next year.

negative_highlights: Loan balances essentially flat and C&I declined about $50 million on lower originations, reduced line utilization, and exits of several credits
Deposits declined modestly in the quarter; criticized and classified assets rose about 7% (criticized loans up, classified stable)
Guidance for flat-to-low-single-digit loan growth in Q4 and a delay past the $10 billion threshold to mid-2028 Durbin impact
positive_highlights: Record EPS of $1.09, up nearly 20% YoY and about 7% QoQ, on record revenue of nearly $108 million
NIM expanded 7 bps to 4.06% on higher loan yields and improved funding mix; cost of funds up just 1 bp
Net charge-offs of $2.1 million (10 bps) and NPAs fell $3.7 million to about $36 million (0.45%); no brokered deposits remain after a $180 million reduction YTD
summary: ST Bancorp reported record Q3 EPS of $1.09, up nearly 20% YoY and about 7% QoQ, on record revenue of nearly $108 million. NIM expanded 7 bps to 4.06%, ROA was 1.55%, and PPNR rose to 2.01%, with net charge-offs of $2.1 million (10 bps) and NPAs down $3.7 million to about $36 million (0.45%). However, loans were essentially flat and deposits declined modestly, with C&I balances down about $50 million; management guides to flat-to-low-single-digit loan growth in Q4 and now expects not to cross $10 billion before year-end. NIM is expected to stay north of 4% into 2027 and 2027 non-interest expense growth is targeted near 3%, but competitive pricing pressure on both loans and deposits is building.

negative_highlights: Full-year 2026 net operating EPS guidance cut to $15.35-$15.65, reflecting Q3 results and lower Q4 United American margin estimates
United American health underwriting margin fell to -$6M from $16M a year ago, driven by $7M of prior-period CMS Medicare Supplement claims and about $16M of high-severity claims at Evry
Normalized health underwriting margin fell to 20.5% from 27.2% a year ago, and management expects elevated loss ratios to persist through year-end
positive_highlights: Health premium revenue grew 16% to $447M and United American net health sales rose 95% to $48M on Medicare Supplement tailwinds
Book value per share excluding AOCI rose 11% to $103.62 and GAAP ROE was 19.7% through September 30
2026 share repurchase guidance raised to $725M-$775M, a $65M increase at the midpoint
summary: Q3 net income fell 2% YoY to $361M ($4.62/share) while net operating income rose 1% to $379M ($4.84/share). Total premium revenue grew 7%, but United American health underwriting margin swung to -$6M from $16M on a $7M CMS Medicare Supplement processing delay and roughly $16M of high-severity claims at Evry. Full-year 2026 net operating EPS guidance was cut to $15.35-$15.65 (from prior guidance) and 2027 is guided to $16.10-$17.10, up 7% at the midpoint; 2026 health margin guidance is 22%-24% with a 20%-22% Q4 range. Buyback plans were raised to $725M-$775M for 2026, and normalized EPS growth is estimated at 8% for the full year.

negative_highlights: The loan sale triggered a $23 million non-operating pre-tax charge in Q3, plus $7-8 million of Q4 transaction costs, and tangible book value per share fell 1.9% sequentially to $24.19
Management expects further charge-offs of $3-5 million per quarter tied to exiting remaining rent-stabilized credits
Deposit cost pressure is tempering margin widening, with the pace limited to roughly 3-5 bps per quarter, and the preferred stock may stay outstanding another quarter at an ~8.8% rate
positive_highlights: Operating EPS of $0.95 rose 13% sequentially and 35% YoY, with operating PPNR at 2.01% of average assets and ROTCE above 15%
NIM widened 2 bps to 3.44%, the eighth straight quarterly expansion, with Q4 guided to 3.50% and further widening modeled through 2027
Expenses came in flat versus 1.5% growth guidance, improving the efficiency ratio to 41% from 43% last quarter and 48% a year ago
summary: ConnectOne reported Q3 FY2026 operating EPS of $0.95, up 13% sequentially from $0.84 and up 35% YoY, with operating PPNR at 2.01% of average assets, ROA of 1.35%, and operating ROTCE above 15%. NIM widened 2 bps for an eighth consecutive quarter to 3.44%, with management guiding to 3.50% in Q4 and continued widening through 2027. The quarter included a $23 million non-operating pre-tax charge tied to a definitive agreement to watch up to ~$750 million of non-relationship multifamily loans at just over 90% of par, cutting rent-stabilized exposure to 2% of loans from 6% and lowering the CRE concentration to 397% from 439% pro forma. Expenses were flat versus prior guidance of 1.5% growth, charge-offs were 7 bps, non-accruals fell to $64 million from $80 million, and the dividend was held at $0.195 while 50,000 shares were repurchased.

negative_highlights: Q4 guidance of $2.81 is roughly $0.20-$0.25 below Q3, with Q4 outage expense of $0.72 versus $0.28 in Q3
Legacy corrugated shipments fell 0.5% year-over-year, with agriculture end-market volumes still depressed
