Input costs are expected to keep climbing across recycled fiber, freight, chemicals, and energy, and management assumes these stay elevated
positive_highlights: Adjusted EPS of $3.04 exceeded the $2.91 guidance on price realization and a stronger-than-expected Greif contribution
Packaging EBITDA margin expanded to 23.9% from 23.1% a year earlier, with legacy mills producing 1,286,000 tons of containerboard, up 77,000 tons sequentially
Nearly all of the first $50/ton and about half of the second $50/ton containerboard increases were realized, with the $70 increase set to flow through Q4 and Q1
summary: Q3 FY2026 adjusted EPS of $3.04 beat prior guidance of $2.91, up from $2.73 a year ago, on net sales of $2.6 billion versus $2.3 billion. Packaging EBITDA rose to $578 million at a 23.9% margin (from 23.1%), and roughly $0.24 of the $0.31 EPS improvement came from the acquired Greif business. Q4 guidance was set at $2.81 per share, about $0.20-$0.25 below Q3, driven by significantly higher outage expense ($0.72 in Q4) despite continued price realization from the second and third containerboard increases. Management flagged rising recycled fiber, freight, energy, and chemical costs across the business.

negative_highlights: NIM contracted 4 bps linked quarter to 3.40%, and management expects only slight expansion in Q4 with slight pressure through 2027 from HQLA build and wholesale-funded growth
Loan yields rose just 1 bp to 6.12%, with PAA and loan fees at the low end of the modeled range; a premium-priced payoff cost $2 million of PAA in the quarter
Adjusted non-interest expense rose 4% to $690 million on higher incentive accrual and continued hiring investment
positive_highlights: Adjusted non-interest revenue rose 19% linked quarter, driven by a record BHG production quarter and a $23 million equipment leasing gain
BHG full-year income guidance raised to $150-160 million from the prior $110-120 million range provided in July
Net charge-offs of 23 bps stayed inside the 20-25 bp range for a third straight quarter and the NPAs ratio held flat at 0.50%; CET1 rose 8 bps to 10.01%
summary: PNFP reported Q3 FY2026 diluted EPS of $2.40 and adjusted diluted EPS of $2.69, up 19% YoY and 8% linked quarter, with year-to-date adjusted EPS up 23%. Loans grew $1.7 billion (8% annualized) and deposits $2.1 billion linked quarter; NII rose 3% to $986 million while NIM contracted 4 bps to 3.40%, and the adjusted tangible efficiency ratio improved 95 bps to 48.9%. Full-year guidance ranges were left unchanged, with loan growth still at the top end of 9-11%, but the BHG income outlook was raised to $150-160 million from a prior $110-120 million range, and the NIM guide was nudged slightly lower at the top end. Credit stayed clean with charge-offs of 23 bps and the NPAs ratio flat at 0.50%; CET1 built 8 bps to 10.01%.

negative_highlights: Loans declined $170M and deposits fell $303M, with total assets down $375M to $21.9B sequentially
GAAP EPS fell to $0.73 from $0.77 and ROTCE dropped 82 bps to 12.02%, with management stating it has not yet achieved merger-plan performance levels
NPLs rose ~$8M to 91 bps of loans and management expects elevated charge-offs ahead as specific reserves are worked through
positive_highlights: NIM expanded 4 bps to 3.85% on loan yields up 14 bps to 6.13% and funding costs up only 1 bp
ICRE concentration reached 295% of risk-based capital, ahead of the 300% merger goal after over $500M of runoff
Board added $75M to buybacks for a $125M authorization (~5% of market cap) and kept the $0.3225 dividend
summary: Beacon reported Q3 GAAP EPS of $0.73 versus $0.77 in Q2 and operating EPS of $0.77, with net income of $61.2M down from $64.4M sequentially. NIM expanded 4 bps to 3.85% and net interest income rose $3.9M to $197.2M, but total assets fell $375M to $21.9B and loans declined $170M to $17.7B on CRE, consumer and equipment finance runoff. Management guided NIM to 3.85%-3.9% but deferred 2027 plan details, expense targets and buyback pace to the January call, while flagging elevated charge-offs ahead and a mid-teens ROTCE goal against current 12.02%. The board added $75M to buybacks for $125M total authorization and maintained a $0.3225 dividend.

negative_highlights: NIM contracted 14 bps to 4.73% on higher funding costs (CD repricing, government market-linked accounts up ~12 bps)
Non-interest income fell $3.1M and non-interest expenses rose $2.9M, including a $2.8M contingency reserve on an adverse USVI OREO court ruling
Annualized net charge-offs rose to 55 bps on higher consumer/auto losses, and loan growth guidance was narrowed to the low end of the 3%-5% range
positive_highlights: Board approved a 25% increase to the quarterly common dividend and a $350M stock buyback authorization, with CET1 at 16.9%
Return on assets of 1.98%, the 19th consecutive quarter above 1.5%; efficiency ratio of 50% versus a 52% target
Loan growth of 3.3% annualized linked-quarter, led by commercial and construction, with NPA ratio unchanged at 0.59%
summary: Net income of $96.1M ($0.63/share) was essentially flat QoQ, with EPS up 14% YTD; NII fell $1.6M and NIM contracted 14 bps to 4.73% on higher funding costs, partly offset by the absence of prior-quarter purchase discount benefits. Non-interest income fell $3.1M and expenses rose $2.9M (including a $2.8M legal contingency reserve), while loan growth ran at a 3.3% annualized rate and credit stayed stable (NPA ratio 0.59%). Management guided FY loan growth to the low end of 3%-5% and expects core margin near current levels in Q4, deferring a 2027 forecast to the next call. The board approved a 25% dividend increase and a $350M buyback authorization, with CET1 at 16.9%.

negative_highlights: Defense, space, and other sales fell 9% YoY to $166 million on soft launchers, rocket motors, F-35 and Rafale timing, and divested industrial businesses
Engineered products segment adjusted operating margin fell to 11.8% from 15.5% a year ago
Free cash flow of $103 million for the nine months despite improved operating cash; leverage at ~2.1x net debt/EBITDA, above the 1.5x-2x target
positive_highlights: Commercial aerospace sales rose 21% YoY to $330 million, with volume growth on the A350, 787, A320neo, and 737 MAX
Adjusted EPS of $0.50 rose 35% YoY from $0.37, and adjusted operating margin expanded to 11% from 9.8%
Gross margin improved to 23.3% from 21.9% on operating leverage and price realization
summary: Q3 FY2026 sales of $496 million rose 8.8% YoY, with adjusted operating margin of 11% (up from 9.8%) and adjusted EPS of $0.50 versus $0.37 (up 35%, partly aided by a lower tax rate). Commercial aerospace sales of $330 million grew 21% YoY on all four primary platforms, but defense/space/other fell 9% to $166 million on lower space launchers, soft F-35 and Rafale timing, and divested industrial businesses. Full-year 2026 guidance was reaffirmed and unchanged: revenue $2.025-2.15 billion, EPS $2.30-2.40, and free cash flow >$195 million. Management gave an initial 2027 A350 outlook of ~100 shipsets (about +25% over 2026) and reiterated a path to ~18% operating margin, with potential upside to ~20%, while noting hiring and training costs pressure near-term margins.

SouthState reported Q3 FY2026 loans and deposits each up 9% annualized, NIM flat at 3.78% and within the 3.75%-3.80% guide, and net charge-offs of just 9 bps. Noninterest income fell $3 million to $94 million on weaker capital markets (correspondent income $20.1 million vs. the $25 million guide after an 87 bp five-year Treasury move), and NIE rose $17 million to $375 million. Management raised the NIM range to 3.75%-3.85% through 2027 but guided Q4 loan growth to mid-single digits from 9.5% YTD, and pointed 2027 total payout to the low end of the 40%-60% range after trailing payouts of 67%-75%. FY26 NIE growth stays near the ~4% guide, with 2027 seen at 3.5%-4%.

negative_highlights: Exhibitions growth of 4% was cut by about 3 percentage points from Middle East disruption, and management expects a similar Q4 impact
LeapSpace rapid usage growth has no material revenue impact at this stage
Insurance shopping and switching volumes no longer growing at the strong pace of the last two years, though still elevated
positive_highlights: Legal underlying revenue growth of 10%, with law firms and corporate legal (70% of the division) growing at double digits
Risk grew 8% with over 90% of revenue from machine-to-machine interactions; article submissions up over 20% year-to-date in STM
Lexis+ Protégé adoption passed 50% of U.S. revenue, with the vast majority of new sales and a comfortable majority of renewals on the new platform
summary: RELX reported 7% underlying revenue growth for the first nine months, with Risk at 8%, STM at 6%, Legal at 10% and Exhibitions at 4%. Risk, STM and Legal were each described as in line with the first half, while Exhibitions was moderated by roughly 3 percentage points of Middle East disruption. Full-year outlook is unchanged, with management still expecting strong underlying growth in revenue, adjusted operating profit and constant-currency adjusted EPS. The main change versus prior periods is qualitative: LeapSpace usage growth is running at or slightly faster than the prior 90-day doubling, but revenue impact is not material yet.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA margin contracted to 11.1% from 12.7%, with ~one-third of the decline from unrecovered material inflation and accelerating freight costs
Adjusted diluted EPS fell to $0.33 from $0.73, driven by a higher tax rate from M&A expense timing; GAAP diluted loss was $0.08
Adjusted free cash flow declined to ~$59 million from $72 million, and Q4 Modine EBITDA guidance (~$28 million on ~$275 million revenue, ~10% margin) came in below the ~11% acquisition-time level
positive_highlights: Automotive climate and comfort revenue grew 8.8% YoY, outpacing light vehicle production in key markets by 12 percentage points
China domestic OEM sales exceeded global OEM sales in China for the first time in company history
Lumbar and massage comfort solutions revenue grew more than 25% YoY and $555 million of new automotive awards were booked, with YTD awards above $1.6 billion
summary: Gentherm reported Q3 revenue of $405 million, up 4.7% YoY (4.4% ex-FX), with automotive climate and comfort revenue up 8.8% and outperforming light vehicle production by 12 points. Adjusted EBITDA fell to $45 million (11.1% of sales) from 12.7% a year ago, adjusted diluted EPS dropped to $0.33 from $0.73, and GAAP was a $0.08 loss including ~$0.37 of merger/restructuring costs. Full-year 2026 guidance was updated to include ~$275 million revenue and ~$28 million adjusted EBITDA from Modine in Q4, with legacy Gentherm revenue trending to the higher end of prior range but EBITDA near the midpoint due to accelerated inflation; 2027 detail deferred to February. The quarter closed the Modine acquisition on October 1 and included ~2 million shares repurchased for $60 million since then.

negative_highlights: PD is close to capacity constraints, with sequential revenue expected roughly flat in the first half of 2027 until added capacity comes online late Q1 and fully by H2 2027
MSA faces a 2-3% revenue headwind in 2027 from the end of a stamping supplier last-time note, concentrated in the first half
Capex expected to rise to 5-7% of revenues in 2027 from the historical 3-5% range to fund capacity additions
positive_highlights: Revenue of $184 million rose 20% YoY and exceeded the high end of the guided range, with EPS of $0.38 at the high end
Precision Devices revenue grew 33% YoY to $117 million with a book-to-bill of 1.5 and Q3 orders near $180 million, well above Q2
Full-year 2026 revenue growth guided to 16% and adjusted EBITDA growth to 24%, both above the high end of May 2025 Investor Day targets
summary: Knowles reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $184 million, up 20% YoY and above the high end of guidance, with EPS of $0.38 (up 15% YoY) and operating cash flow of $45 million, both at the high end of the guided range. Precision Devices revenue grew 33% YoY to $117 million with segment gross margin of 41.6% (up 10 bps), while Med Tech & Specialty Audio grew 4% to $67 million at 51.9% gross margin. Q4 guidance calls for revenue of $180-190 million (up 14% YoY at the midpoint), EPS of $0.39-0.43, and adjusted EBIT margin of 23-25%. Management noted PD is near capacity constraints, with sequential PD revenue expected roughly flat in the first half of 2027, and 2026 revenue growth guided to 16% at the midpoint, above the May 2025 Investor Day targets.

negative_highlights: Pipeline close probability fell from a typical 90-95% to ~65-70% amid capital markets choppiness
Incremental spread on new dollars has compressed to 100-150 bps (mid-to-high 6s cost of capital vs ~8% pipeline cap rates), toward the low end of the historical 100-300 bps range
Management plans a slower deployment pace over the next two to three quarters and 2027 volume is back-end loaded to preserve capital capacity
positive_highlights: AFFO per share of $0.51 rose 6% YoY and nominal AFFO grew 16% to $112 million, ahead of internal expectations
2026 AFFO/share guidance raised to $2.02-$2.05 (~8% growth at midpoint) and investment volume raised to $1.3-$1.5 billion
Portfolio metrics steady: same-store rent growth 1.4%, occupancy 99.6%, rent coverage 3.5x, and watchlist down 50 bps QoQ to 1.1%
summary: EPRT reported Q3 FY2026 GAAP net income of $60.7 million and AFFO of $111.9 million ($0.51/share, +6% YoY, nominal AFFO +16% to $112 million), ahead of expectations, with $342 million invested at a 7.7% cash / 9.4% GAAP yield. Management raised 2026 AFFO/share guidance to $2.02-$2.05 (~8% growth at midpoint) and investment volume guidance to $1.3-$1.5 billion, and initiated 2027 AFFO/share guidance of $2.10-$2.18 with a back-end-loaded $1-$1.5 billion volume range. Offsetting the raise, management flagged a deliberately slower deployment pace over the next two to three quarters to preserve balance sheet capacity amid a higher cost of capital, with pipeline close rates falling to ~65-70% and incremental spreads compressing to 100-150 bps.

negative_highlights: Gross CapEx guidance raised by $300 million to $5.2B-$5.5B, contributing to higher net CapEx of $3.75B-$4.05B.
Management flagged persistent above-trend cost inflation (merit increases, parts, diesel, freight) that must be offset through productivity and rate.
Used equipment recovery rate of 51.4% remains in a normalized low-50s range, with management cautioning against expecting material variability.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EPS grew 33% YoY to $15.55 and adjusted EBITDA rose $385 million to a record $2.3 billion at a 47.6% margin (up 160 bps).
Full-year revenue guidance raised by $450 million at the midpoint to $18.0B-$18.2B, with adjusted EBITDA guidance up $300 million to $8.3B-$8.4B.
Total revenue up 16% and rental revenue up 18% YoY, both quarterly records, with specialty rental growth of 35%.
summary: United Rentals reported Q3 revenue of $4.9 billion, up 16% YoY, with rental revenue up 18% to $4.3 billion; adjusted EBITDA was a record $2.3 billion at a 47.6% margin (up 160 bps), and adjusted EPS rose 33% to $15.55, also a record. The company raised 2026 revenue guidance by $450 million at the midpoint (to $18.0B-$18.2B) and adjusted EBITDA guidance by $300 million (to $8.3B-$8.4B), now implying over 13% total revenue growth ex-used versus prior guidance of ~6%, and raised gross CapEx guidance to $5.2B-$5.5B. Specialty rental revenue grew 35% YoY, power and metals/minerals both posted double-digit growth, and management noted customers remain consistently positive, underpinning the raised outlook.

negative_highlights: Cash flow from operations was a use of $27 million in the quarter, driven by increases in inventory, contract assets, and receivables.
Free cash flow was a use of $181 million in the quarter, though positive $42 million year to date.
Gross margin outlook maintained at approximately 34% despite higher revenue, as new production line start-up costs and expedited deliveries carry near-term cost.
positive_highlights: Revenue of $1.24 billion grew 138% YoY and 16% sequentially, with product revenue up 179% YoY to $1.07 billion, crossing $1 billion for the first time.
Non-GAAP operating income of $286 million grew over 500% YoY, expanding operating margin to 23.1% from 8.9% a year ago as opex grew only 26%.
Full-year guidance raised for the third time in 2026: revenue to $4.4-4.6 billion, operating income to $960 million-$1.03 billion, and EPS to $3.10-$3.40.
summary: Bloom Energy reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $1.24 billion, up 138% YoY and 16% QoQ, with non-GAAP operating income of $286 million (23.1% margin, up from 8.9%) and non-GAAP diluted EPS of $0.94 versus $0.15 a year ago. Product revenue crossed $1 billion for the first time at $1.07 billion (up 179% YoY). The company raised full-year revenue guidance to $4.4-4.6 billion (about 122% growth at midpoint), raised operating income guidance to $960 million-$1.03 billion, and raised EPS guidance to $3.10-$3.40, while maintaining its non-GAAP gross margin outlook of approximately 34%. Cash flow from operations was a use of $27 million in the quarter due to working capital build, though free cash flow was positive $42 million year to date.

negative_highlights: Net realizations fell 20% quarter-over-quarter, and Q3 DE of $1.32 per share was underpinned by FRE rather than realizations
BCRED purchase requests hit 10% of NAV versus the 5% quarterly limit, resulting in $1.4 billion of net outflows
Opportunistic real estate funds (BREP) declined 3.2% in Q3 as valuation cap rates were raised in response to higher base rates, and total real estate AUM declined
positive_highlights: Total AUM rose 10% YoY to ~$1.4 trillion with $63 billion of Q3 inflows and $270 billion over the last 12 months, the highest in four years
Base management fees reached a record $2 billion and fee-related earnings grew 6% YoY to $1.6 billion, with transaction and advisory fees up 34% to $210 million
Net accrued performance revenue receivable stands at $7.3 billion, up 12% YoY (~$6 per share), with infrastructure platform appreciation of 6.4% in Q3 and 29% LTM versus a 4% index return
summary: Blackstone reported Q3 FY2026 GAAP net income of $1.3 billion, DE of $1.7 billion or $1.32 per share, with a declared dividend of $1.12. Total AUM rose 10% YoY to ~$1.4 trillion, fee revenues rose 8% to $2.7 billion, FRE rose 6% to $1.6 billion ($1.26/share), and inflows were $63 billion; net realizations fell 20% QoQ, as previously guided. For Q4 management expects a significant step-up in net realizations and BXMA crystallizations, with base management fees returning to low double-digit growth in 2027; real estate base fees seen broadly stable. Offsets include opportunistic real estate depreciation of 3.2% from cap-rate increases and $1.4 billion of BCRED net outflows after 10% of NAV purchase requests versus a 5% quarterly limit.

negative_highlights: CRE loans declined $9.9M on elevated July-August payoffs, with a return to normal run rate expected only in Q4
Interest-bearing deposit costs are expected to trend higher from here, with non-time betas of 30%-40% assumed
Net charge-offs of $1.2M (10 bps) were modestly higher than the prior quarter
positive_highlights: ROA above 1.7%, ROTCE over 20%, and CET1 up 44 bps to 11.53% in the quarter
Deposits grew ~$81M (~6% annualized), with total deposit costs rising only 3 bps
Substandard loans improved to ~$60M from $65M, and year-to-date annualized net charge-offs were 6 bps
summary: Horizon reported Q3 with NIM flat at 4.37%, ROA above 1.7%, and ROTCE over 20%; loans grew ~$47M (~4% annualized) to just over $5B and deposits rose ~$81M (~6% annualized), with CET1 up 44 bps to 11.53%. Expenses fell to $41.5M from $43.8M in Q2 (which included a $3.1M legal charge), and fee income was ~$12M with mortgage up 52% YoY. Full-year 2026 guidance was largely unchanged, save for Q4 specifics: NII of $66M-$67M with modest NIM expansion, mid-$40M fee income, low-to-mid $160M expenses, and an 18%-19% tax rate, with the outlook assuming one additional 25 bps Fed hike in December. Credit was stable, with net charge-offs of $1.2M (10 bps annualized) and substandard loans improving to ~$60M from $65M.

negative_highlights: Asset management recorded net outflows of $2.3 billion in the quarter, with AUM of $284 billion only roughly flat sequentially
Adjusted compensation ratio held at 69.9% for a third straight quarter, with a potential deferral change set to raise the reported ratio by a few points this year
Private equity M&A remains stalled on valuation disconnect, a segment management called out as the missing piece of deal flow
positive_highlights: Financial advisory posted record third-quarter revenue of $465 million with record Americas and U.K. results for both the quarter and nine months
Management fees rose 18% YoY to a record $321 million, marking a sixth consecutive quarter of sequential growth
2027 weighted pipeline is more than double the 2026 pipeline at the same point last year, and conflict clearances are up over 30% YoY
summary: Lazard reported firm-wide adjusted net revenue up 11% YoY, with record third-quarter financial advisory revenue of $465 million and record asset management management fees of $321 million, up 18% YoY. Asset management adjusted net revenue was $330 million but faced net outflows of $2.3 billion, though gross inflows hit a record $54 billion for the first nine months. Management expects the Campbell Lutyens acquisition to close in early November and generate roughly $500 million of revenue, accretive in 2027, and flagged a potential year-end deferral-rate cut that would lift this year's comp ratio by a few points before lowering it thereafter. Forward indicators include a 2027 weighted pipeline more than double the year-ago level and conflict clearances up over 30% YoY.

negative_highlights: Greater China RevPAR fell 3% with Tier 2-4 cities down 7.5% and occupancy down 1.6pp to 62.3%
GCC countries saw a 12% RevPAR decline in Q3, and management said the Middle East could stay down until the conflict resolves
Adjusted interest expense is expected to rise $40-60m pre-tax in 2027
positive_highlights: Global RevPAR grew 5.3% in Q3, up from 4.6% year-to-date, with rate up 3.9% and occupancy up 0.9pp
Americas RevPAR accelerated to 6.8% and U.S. occupancy of 73.9% was the highest since 2017
Signings of 21,100 rooms across 164 hotels were almost double the 12,900 rooms opened, and pipeline is 33% of current system size
summary: IHG reported global Q3 RevPAR growth of 5.3%, accelerating from 4.6% year-to-date, with Americas RevPAR up 6.8% and U.S. up 6.9%, while EMEAA improved to 5% from 0.6% in the prior quarter. Greater China eased 3% on adverse weather and holiday timing, with Tier 2-4 cities down 7.5%. Net system growth was 4.9%, signings of 21,100 rooms nearly doubled openings of 12,900 rooms, and management said it is confident in 2026 consensus and expects consensus to rise modestly given the stronger Q3; it flagged $40-60m higher adjusted interest expense for 2027 but reiterated the 12-15% EPS algo.

negative_highlights: International sales fell 4% in the quarter (though up 7% YTD) as Europe was only marginally up
Management cited higher resin prices pressuring product cost and higher diesel prices hitting ocean and land freight, with definitive U.S. tariff guidance still pending
Costume business at $62 million for the quarter is only slightly ahead of 2024 as it recovers from last year's disruptions
positive_highlights: Net sales of $254 million, up 20% YoY, with North America up 28% and toys/consumer products shipping up 23%
Adjusted EBITDA of $44.4 million versus $36.5 million in Q3 last year; adjusted EPS $2.68 versus $1.80
Gross margin held at 32.1% versus 32.0% despite higher resin and diesel/freight costs, and cash rose to $45 million from $28 million a year ago
summary: JAKKS reported Q3 FY2026 net sales of $254 million, up 20% YoY, with North America up 28% and toys/consumer products shipping up 23%. Adjusted EBITDA rose to $44.4 million from $36.5 million, adjusted EPS was $2.68 versus $1.80, and gross margin held at 32.1% (vs 32.0%) despite resin and freight cost pressure. Management did not provide explicit quantitative FY guidance but said results are tracking to plan ('coloring within the lines'), noted some Q4 sales pulled into Q3, and approved a $0.25 quarterly dividend. Pressure points: international sales fell 4% in the quarter and product/freight costs and pending tariff clarity remain unresolved.

negative_highlights: Unit expansion among existing customers is pacing slower than last year and is expected to stay below last year's Q4 pace and comparable to Q3
Subscription services revenue grew only 14% year-over-year to $62 million, lagging total company growth of 19%
Q4 outlook notes a prior-year one-time Stack partnership revenue that will not recur, and sales and marketing rose to 15% of revenue from 13% on deliberate added investment
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 19% year-over-year to $296 million; full-year revenue guidance raised to $1.122–$1.127 billion, lifting midpoint growth to 18.3%
Non-GAAP operating margin expanded to 27.3% from 23.5% a year ago; GAAP operating income grew 64% to $57 million (19.4% margin)
Value-added services revenue grew 21% to $232 million and units on platform rose 8% to 9.8 million; operating cash flow was $97 million with $307 million in cash and investments
summary: AppFolio reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $296 million, up 19% year-over-year from $249 million, with GAAP operating income up 64% to $57 million (19.4% margin) and non-GAAP operating income up 38% to $81 million (27.3% margin). Full-year revenue guidance was raised to $1.122–$1.127 billion (midpoint growth 18.3%) and full-year non-GAAP operating margin guidance set at 26.5%–27.5% versus 24.7% in 2025. The key negative noted was that unit expansion among existing customers is pacing slower than last year and is expected to remain below last year's Q4 pace. Margin gains were partly aided by a prior-year bonus accrual and the timing shift of the FUTURE conference into Q3.

negative_highlights: Deposits of $21.6 billion were roughly flat sequentially, below management's prior positive commentary, with loan growth outpacing deposits
Q4 NIM guided potentially 1-2 bps below the 360 bps reported, reflecting heavier use of higher-cost wholesale borrowings to fund loan growth
CRE payoffs totaled approximately $370 million in Q3, a nearly 1% headwind to loan growth, and mortgage banking income fell almost $2 million YoY
positive_highlights: Adjusted EPS rose nearly 7% year-over-year to $2.72 year-to-date, with return on average tangible common equity near 17%
Total loans increased 5.1% year-over-year and 8.7% annualized sequentially, with C&I up 11% YoY and 16% QoQ annualized
Criticized and classified loans decreased $93 million, or 55 bps, from Q2 to 3.19% of total loans, driving a 4 bp reduction in the allowance to 1.08%
summary: WesBanco reported Q3 FY2026 GAAP EPS of $0.88 and adjusted EPS of $0.89, with adjusted EPS up nearly 7% year-over-year; net interest income rose 4.7% to $227 million and NIM improved 7 bps YoY to 3.60%. Total loans grew 5.1% YoY and 8.7% annualized sequentially, with C&I up 11% YoY, while deposits of $21.6 billion were roughly flat sequentially. Management reiterated mid-single-digit 2026 loan growth and Q4 fee income growth of 3%-5% with expenses near $153 million, but guided Q4 NIM potentially 1-2 bps below the 360 bps reported. Criticized and classified loans fell $93 million to 3.19% of total loans.

negative_highlights: Revenue of $1.48B came in slightly below expectations, with ~$22M of EMEA 3PL shipment delays and some of that amount at risk of cancellation
Full-year revenue guidance reset to $5.70-5.725B with HOKA cut to high-single-digit growth; Q3 HOKA guided to only low-to-mid-single digits
UGG DTC fell 8% to $146M and HOKA DTC grew only 4%, with U.S. e-commerce pressured by a heavily promotional athletic footwear market
positive_highlights: Ex-refund diluted EPS of $2.03 rose 11.5% YoY and came in above the high end of the guidance range
Gross margin expanded 430 bps to 60.5%, with a 120 bp underlying improvement from full-price note and favorable product mix
Repurchased $637M of shares over the first six months (~5% of shares outstanding), with $4.4B remaining on the authorization
summary: Deckers reported Q2 FY27 revenue of $1.48B, up 3.5% YoY, slightly below its own expectation due to ~$22M of EMEA 3PL shipment delays and softer U.S. DTC; HOKA grew 7% to $677M and UGG 4% to $786M. Gross margin rose 430 bps to 60.5% (310 bps from IEEPA tariff refunds), operating margin was 26.3% (23.2% ex-refunds), and diluted EPS was $2.31 ($2.03 ex-refunds, up 11.5% and above the high end of guidance). Full-year revenue guidance was reset to $5.70-5.725B with HOKA now high-single-digit and UGG low-single-digit growth, while EPS guidance rose to $7.80-$7.95 largely on ~$88M of tariff refunds; Q3 revenue is guided to low-single-digit growth with EPS of $3.52-$3.60. The key change versus prior outlook is a more measured revenue trajectory, with management prioritizing full-price watching and margin over incremental volume amid a more promotional U.S. athletic footwear market.

negative_highlights: GAAP EPS of $0.52 versus $0.76 excluding the $17 million distillery provision, a ~$0.27 drag
Commercial banking net charge-offs of 86 bps reflecting six new impairments and distillery actions
Management declined to replace the prior $20-25 million provision run-rate range and said provision will not step down next quarter
positive_highlights: Record adjusted PPNR of $88 million, up 33% YoY and 16% QoQ, on 15% revenue growth versus 1% expense growth
Record originations of $2.1 billion across 34 industries, up 29% YoY, driving loans to $13.9 billion (+16% YoY)
Live Oak Express originations of $107 million, up 173% YoY, with gain on sale of $7 million, up 250% YoY
summary: Reported EPS of $0.52 was driven down by $17 million of additional provision on the exited distillery portfolio (~$0.27 EPS drag); excluding that, adjusted EPS would have been $0.76. Core operating trends were strong: adjusted revenue rose 15% YoY to $172 million against 1% expense growth, producing record adjusted PPNR of $88 million (+33% YoY), with originations of $2.1 billion (+29% YoY) and loans and deposits each up 16% YoY. Total provision was $55 million, including $16 million on record loan growth and $13 million in commercial banking impairments across six relationships. Management declined to reinstate a provision run-rate range and guided to a relatively stable NIM and modest expense growth, with commercial credit expected to remain lumpy.

negative_highlights: Adjusted loss of $0.28 per diluted share as fuel at $3.85/gallon added $1.9 billion YoY; full-year fuel expense now expected more than $7 billion higher than 2025
Q4 guided to an adjusted loss of $0.50-$1.10 per share with fuel near $4.70/gallon, roughly $2.8 billion higher YoY, and full-year adjusted loss of $1.00-$1.60
2027 capacity growth to decelerate considerably, which management said will put upward pressure on unit costs
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 19.3% YoY to $16.3 billion, above the high end of guidance, with total unit revenue up 14.5%
Premium unit revenue rose 18.5% YoY, outperforming main cabin by more than four points, and managed corporate revenue was up 28% for a sixth straight quarter of double-digit growth
Q3 CASM ex rose ~3%, better than the July guidance midpoint, with roughly $1 billion of annual run-rate savings and over $900 million of working capital improvements expected by year-end
summary: Q3 revenue rose 19.3% YoY to $16.3 billion (above the high end of guidance) with total unit revenue up 14.5%, but a $1.9 billion YoY fuel increase ($3.85/gallon, +$1.48) drove an adjusted loss of $0.28 per diluted share, ahead of the guidance midpoint but still a loss. Q4 guidance calls for revenue growth of 19.5%-22.5% yet an adjusted loss of $0.50-$1.10 per share on fuel near $4.70/gallon, taking the full-year adjusted loss to $1.00-$1.60. Management also flagged that 2027 capacity growth will decelerate considerably due to high fuel, with CASM ex rising on lower growth after Q3 CASM ex of ~+3% beat the guidance midpoint.

negative_highlights: Data Center & Networking revenue came in about 10% below prior guidance due to customer program timing, with one of three N+M programs moving right
N+M revenue tracked slightly above $200 million in Q3 but slightly below the prior $400 million Q4 expectation
Ophir acquisition financing adds roughly $20 million per quarter of interest expense, a drag on EPS
positive_highlights: Revenue of $1.2 billion grew 60% YoY and non-GAAP EPS of $1.46 rose 118% YoY, both all-time quarterly records and above guidance
Adjusted EBITDA margin reached a record 20.1%, up 400 bps YoY and over 350 bps sequentially, on favorable mix and Penang execution
Overall book-to-bill was 2.1 (commercial 2.5), 90-day backlog rose 111% YoY to $1.3 billion, and A&D backlog hit a record $2 billion
summary: TTM reported record Q3 FY2026 revenue of $1.2 billion, up 60% YoY, with non-GAAP EPS of $1.46 (up 118% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA margin of 20.1% (up 400 bps YoY), both above guidance. Full-year 2026 revenue guidance was raised to $4.47-4.49 billion with non-GAAP EPS of $4.97-5.03, and initial FY2027 guidance calls for $6.5-6.75 billion in sales and $8.10-8.90 in EPS. However, the Data Center & Networking segment came in about 10% below prior guidance on customer program timing, and N+M revenue tracked slightly below the prior $400 million Q4 target. Bookings were strong with overall book-to-bill of 2.1 and A&D backlog at a record $2 billion.

negative_highlights: Swung to a GAAP net loss of $39 million (-$0.24/diluted share) from prior-quarter net income of $43 million
Adjusted net income and adjusted EPS declined sequentially to $10 million and $0.06 from $14 million and $0.09
Drilling-related delays created unanticipated calendar gaps, and management declined to give a specific Q4 revenue outlook
positive_highlights: Record natural gas substitution above 60% of fleet fuel consumption, equating to over $1 billion of annualized fuel savings for customers
New 1.2 GW power development agreement with a frontier AI lab includes a capacity-fee prepayment 'in the hundreds of millions of dollars' and a ~500 MW ESA targeted by December 2026
11% increase in quarterly cash dividend to $0.10 per share; $669 million total liquidity with no revolver balance
summary: Q3 FY2026 revenue of $1.2 billion was roughly flat sequentially, with adjusted EBITDA of $142 million, but the quarter swung to a GAAP net loss of $39 million (-$0.24/diluted share) versus prior-quarter net income of $43 million, largely on $49 million of tax-affected unrealized investment losses. Adjusted net income fell to $10 million ($0.06/diluted share) from $14 million ($0.09) in Q2, and adjusted G&A rose $3 million ex-SBC to $69 million. Management declined to give a specific Q4 revenue outlook, citing weather/holiday seasonality partly offset by deferred Q3 activity, while expecting modest quarter-on-quarter pricing increases and reaffirming confidence in its full 3 GW of generation capacity. The strategic highlight was a new development agreement with a frontier AI lab for 1.2 GW of integrated power services, including a capacity-fee prepayment in the hundreds of millions and a target of ~500 MW ESA by December 2026.

negative_highlights: Gross margin down 60 bps to 29.0% on higher inbound freight and customer mix
Operating income fell 3% to $172 million with SG&A up 5% vs 4% sales growth, driving margin to 11.4%
New pool construction below prior year and irrigation/landscape tied to a challenging housing market
positive_highlights: Net sales up 4% YoY (3% pricing, 1% volume), accelerating from 2% in Q2
Operating cash flow YTD of $420 million, up 47% from $286 million, equal to 115% of net income
Inventory down 3% YoY against 4% sales growth; Europe sales up 8% in local currency
summary: Pool Corp reported Q3 FY2026 net sales of $1.5 billion, up 4% YoY (3% pricing, 1% volume), an acceleration from the 2% growth in Q2. Gross margin fell 60 bps to 29.0% on higher inbound freight, customer mix, and a tough mid-season pricing comparison, and operating income declined 3% to $172 million (11.4% margin); adjusted diluted EPS was $3.40 vs $3.39, with buybacks reducing share count about 3.5%. Full-year adjusted EPS guidance was reaffirmed at $10.87-$11.17 (midpoint ~3% growth) with slightly better top-line growth of 3%-4%, while Q4 faces a smaller pricing benefit and a difficult gross margin comparison. October sales were up about 2%, and the company flagged Europe up 8% in local currency and continued weakness in new pool construction and housing-linked irrigation/landscape.

negative_highlights: Non-performing loans rose to $21.1 million (0.39% of loans) from $18.5 million a year ago
Consolidated equity to asset ratio fell to 9.72% from 10.9% a year earlier
Provision for credit losses of $850,000 reflects changes in economic forecasts rather than improving credit trends
positive_highlights: Net interest margin expanded 16 bps YoY to 2.95% as cost of interest-bearing liabilities fell to 1.79% from 1.90%
Average loans grew 4.6% ($238 million) to $5.4 billion, an improvement over last quarter's $197.5 million YoY growth
Quarterly dividend raised 5.3% to $0.40 per share and 1.5 million shares repurchased in 2026, with seven straight quarters of net recoveries
summary: TrustCo reported Q3 FY2026 net income of $17.3 million, up 6.5% year over year, with ROAA of 1.05% and ROAE of 10.57%. Net interest income rose 9.1% to $47 million and net interest margin expanded 16 bps to 2.95% as cost of interest-bearing liabilities fell to 1.79% from 1.90%. Average loans grew 4.6% ($238 million) to $5.4 billion and total deposits rose $203 million sequentially to $5.7 billion; non-performing loans ticked up to $21.1 million (0.39% of loans) from $18.5 million a year ago. The bank raised its quarterly dividend 5.3% to $0.40 and repurchased 13.2% of outstanding shares in 2026, while guiding recurring non-interest expense to roughly $27.8-$28.2 million per quarter.

negative_highlights: Organic growth of only 2.3%, with Jafra revenue down 2.8% and the CEO taking over as interim Jafra Mexico managing director
Organic net revenue growth guidance narrowed to 4%-5%, lowering the midpoint of the original range
Consolidated EBITDA margin contracted to 20.9% from 21.4%, and MXN 47 million of Tupperware acquisition costs hit the quarter
positive_highlights: Tupperware core direct-note revenue rose 14% YoY (Mexico +23%), with Brazil declines moderating to 3.3% from prior 10%-15% drops
Post-acquisition net revenue growth guidance raised to 24%-26%; pro forma free cash flow reached MXN 1,059 million (105% of EBITDA)
Pro forma net debt/EBITDA improved to 1.65x, interest coverage 6.91x, and a MXN 250 million dividend was approved (27th consecutive quarter)
summary: Consolidated revenue rose 43.1% YoY to MXN 4,832 million, but organic (Betterware + Jafra) growth was only 2.3%, weighed by a 2.8% Jafra revenue decline. EBITDA grew 39.6% to MXN 1,008 million with margin of 20.9% vs 21.4% a year ago, and net income rose 24.2% to MXN 390 million. Guidance: organic net revenue growth narrowed to 4%-5% (from the original range) and post-acquisition net revenue growth raised to 24%-26%, with full-year EBITDA margin still expected at 19%. Tupperware core direct watching grew 14% and was profitable and cash generative, while Betterware Mexico grew 8.5%.

negative_highlights: Full-year 2026 loan growth guidance cut to approximately 2% on weaker auto/lease and more moderate commercial growth
Commercial NPLs rose $52 million to $466 million (NPL ratio 1.16% from 1.04%) as a $74 million C&I relationship went on non-accrual with a $34 million partial charge-off
FY net charge-off guidance raised to 80-90 bps, implying roughly 100 bps in Q4, and tangible book value per share fell $1.64 to $86.30
positive_highlights: EPS of $4.21 rose 34% year over year and ROTCE held at 15.8% versus 13.1% a year ago
Quarterly dividend raised 20% to $0.90 per share and $179 million of stock repurchased, with Q4 buybacks guided to $150-200 million
Net charge-offs fell to $73 million (73 bps annualized) from $104 million (1.05%) in the prior quarter, with consumer losses at historical lows
summary: Popular reported Q3 2026 net income of $266 million and EPS of $4.21, down $0.14 sequentially but up 34% YoY, with ROTCE of 15.8% versus 17% in Q2 and 13.1% a year ago. NII rose $6 million to $699 million while GAAP NIM slipped 3 bps to 3.63%; operating expenses rose $21 million to $506 million and non-interest income fell $5 million to $176 million but stayed above guidance. Full-year loan growth guidance was trimmed to approximately 2% on weaker auto/lease and more moderate commercial activity, while FY net charge-off guidance moved to 80-90 bps and FY expense growth to approximately 2%. Management raised the quarterly dividend 20% to $0.90, bought back $179 million of stock, and guided Q4 non-interest income to approximately $170 million.

negative_highlights: Adjusted diluted EPS fell to $1.33 from $1.64 a year ago, and GAAP EPS dropped to $0.98 from $1.55
Title segment pre-tax income declined to $47 million from $62 million as direct operations absorbed the residential slowdown
RES adjusted pre-tax margin slipped to 10.5% from 11.3% with same-store volume down 6%-7% and historical cancellations up to ~15% of transactions
positive_highlights: Commercial revenue grew 9% with closed orders up 18% across multiple asset classes
Agency net revenues rose 8% year-over-year with residential premiums up 7% and commercial premiums up 25%
Seventh dividend increase in under six years, raising the annual dividend to $2.20 from $2.10 per share
summary: Stewart reported Q3 FY2026 net income of $30 million and diluted EPS of $0.98, down from $44 million and $1.55 a year ago; adjusted EPS fell to $1.33 from $1.64, which management described as below last year's third quarter. Total operating revenue growth slowed to 13% in the quarter versus 22% year-to-date, with title pre-tax income down to $47 million from $62 million and RES adjusted pre-tax margin slipping to 10.5% from 11.3% on softer Informative Research and appraisal volumes. Management said residential market conditions will continue to decay into the next quarter as 30-year rates held above 7%, guiding RES margins to stay near current levels for the next couple of quarters, while the annual dividend was raised to $2.20 from $2.10. Commercial revenue grew 9% with closed orders up 18%, though average fee per file fell 8% to $16,300 and some closings slipped into Q4.

negative_highlights: A $42 million non-cash impairment from discontinuing the Digital Core program cut GAAP operating margin by 390 bps and GAAP EPS by $0.56 to $0.85
Gross margin of 40.6% faces a negative transactional price-cost position on tungsten and tariff-driven inflation, with another wave to work through in Q1
Q1 FY2027 adjusted operating margin guidance of 9.5%-10.1% sits below the 10.9% just reported, reflecting gross margin and OpEx pressure
positive_highlights: Adjusted operating margin expanded 170 bps to 10.9%, above the high end of the guided range, with adjusted incremental margin of 27%
Core customer daily sales grew double digits for the first time in over three years, and ADS outpaced the IP index for the fifth consecutive quarter
Free cash flow was approximately $64 million, or 133% of net income, in the quarter, with full-year FCF conversion of 102%
summary: MSC reported fiscal Q4 sales of approximately $1.1 billion, up 8.6% on an average daily sales basis, driven by 6.9% price and 1.6% volume, with adjusted operating margin up 170 bps to 10.9% and adjusted EPS of $1.45, up 33% from $1.09. GAAP results were hit by a $42 million non-cash impairment from discontinuing the Digital Core program, cutting GAAP operating margin to 6.7% and EPS to $0.85. Q1 FY2027 guidance calls for 9.5%-10.5% ADS growth and adjusted operating margin of 9.5%-10.1%, with gross margin slightly below the typical 10 bp sequential decline due to material inflation and pricing timing. Management framed the industrial recovery as taking hold, but flagged a negative transactional price-cost position and continued inflation in tungsten, freight, and medical costs entering the new year.

negative_highlights: Organic growth was only 2.1%, with roughly 6 points of the 8.2% total coming from acquisitions
About $50M of ARKA space program revenue shifted beyond the first 12 months post-close, moving from inorganic to organic timing
Management said award decision-making remains sluggish in some areas and expects it to stay that way for the next couple of quarters
positive_highlights: EBITDA margin of 13.3% expanded 160 bps YoY on strong program execution and favorable mix of higher-margin work
Funded backlog grew 15% YoY, the seventh double-digit growth in the last eight quarters; total backlog $34B
Existing business rose to 94% of revenue from 83% last quarter, the highest level at this point in the year in seven years
summary: CACI reported Q1 FY27 revenue of $2.5B, up 8.2% YoY but only 2.1% organic, with EBITDA margin of 13.3% (+160 bps YoY) and adjusted diluted EPS of $7.66, up 11.8%. Free cash flow was $133M and awards totaled $4.8B for a 2.0x book-to-bill, with funded backlog up 15% YoY. Guidance was raised: revenue +$50M to $10.7-10.9B, adjusted net income +$5M to $740-760M, and adjusted EPS to $33.18-34.08, while EBITDA margin (high 12% range) and FCF (at least $900M) were reaffirmed. Management flagged that some ARKA space program revenue shifts roughly $50M later, and that award decision-making remains sluggish, though 94% of revenue is now from existing programs versus 83% last quarter.

negative_highlights: Property NOI of $68.5 million was $1.1 million below forecast on lower retail and residential income, with Q4 NOI guided down another ~$0.5 million
Core FFO of $0.14/share was only in line, and GAAP results showed a $22.3 million net loss including $9.2 million of debt extinguishment costs
Austin at 66% occupancy drags overall occupancy ~400 bps, and the 2027 IBM expiration removes ~$11 million of net NOI; CAD payout ratio was 103%, above the 70%-90% target
positive_highlights: Sales guidance raised to $681 million (from $305 million), 100% achieved and funded, including the $240 million 3151 Market sale at $544/sq ft that eliminated ~$80 million of forward capital spend
Debt reduced by $390 million (over 13% of combined debt), cutting quarterly net debt/EBITDA from 9.0x to 7.6x and lowering the year-end midpoint to 7.8x-8.0x from 8.4x-8.8x
Leasing of 558,000 sq ft was the highest of the year, with One Uptown reaching 97% leased and retention guidance raised to a 54% midpoint
summary: Q3 2026 core FFO of $0.14 per share was in line with guidance and consensus, with a GAAP net loss of $22.3 million ($0.13/share) driven largely by debt extinguishment charges; property NOI of $68.5 million came in $1.1 million below forecast. Full-year FFO guidance midpoint was maintained at $0.55 with a narrowed range, and the sales target was raised to $681 million (wholly owned $545 million), 100% achieved and funded, including the $240 million sale of 3151 Market at $544/sq ft. Deleveraging exceeded plan: debt reduced $390 million (over 13%), year-end net debt/EBITDA midpoint lowered from 8.4x-8.8x to 7.8x-8.0x, and quarterly net debt/EBITDA fell from 9.0x to 7.6x. Same-store was -0.6% GAAP and +1.7% cash, occupancy was 89% (90.5% leased), leasing of 558,000 sq ft was the highest of the year, and retention guidance was raised to 54%, though Austin at 66% occupancy remains a drag and the ~$11 million 2027 IBM NOI loss looms.

negative_highlights: Non-performing assets increased $52.9 million to $166 million, or 1.75% of total assets, driven by a $56 million Maryland affordable multifamily relationship
PPNR fell to $23.8 million from $29.1 million in Q2, with non-interest expense up $3.1 million to $47.1 million and no loan sale gains versus $2.3 million prior quarter
Total loans declined 0.9% to $6.6 billion and total deposits fell $151 million as brokered deposits were cut $348 million
positive_highlights: Provision expense fell to $2.8 million from $21.4 million in Q2 and net charge-offs dropped to $4.2 million (25 bps annualized) from $47.9 million
Criticized and classified loans declined $111 million to $648.4 million, or 54% of Tier 1 capital, from roughly 90% a year ago, with new inflows down 74% to $55.7 million
Net interest margin expanded 8 bps to 2.6%, a third straight quarterly increase, as cost of funds fell to 2.75% and CET1 rose to 14.99%
summary: Eagle Bancorp reported Q3 FY2026 net income of $24.2 million, or $0.79 per diluted share, versus $6.9 million and $0.23 in Q2, driven mainly by an $18.6 million drop in provision expense to $2.8 million and a $5.3 million state tax refund benefit. Net interest margin expanded 8 bps to 2.6%, the third consecutive increase, while net interest income fell about $1 million to $61.3 million on a smaller earning asset base and PPNR declined to $23.8 million from $29.1 million. Criticized and classified loans fell $111 million to $648.4 million (54% of Tier 1 capital) and new inflows dropped 74%, but non-performing assets rose $52.9 million to $166 million on a $56 million multifamily relationship. Management guided to Q4 average loan and deposit growth and higher PPNR versus Q3, and gave an initial 2027 NIM range of 2.77%-3.05% with a criticized-and-classified target near $400 million by around mid-2027.

negative_highlights: Guidance implies Q4 NII roughly flat to Q3 and PPNR down quarter-over-quarter as the election-cycle deposit remix pressures the margin
DDA expected to fall from 42% to about 36% of total deposits by year-end, driving modest Q4 margin compression
Political deposits already declined from about $2 billion to roughly $1.7 billion as of 10/15, and the D.C. multifamily credit saw no recorded resolution activity this quarter
positive_highlights: Core net income hit a record $34.6 million, or $1.14 per diluted share, with net revenue exceeding $100 million for the first time
Full-year NII guidance raised to $341-$342 million and core pre-tax pre-provision guidance raised to $193-$194 million from a $190 million high end
Net charge-offs declined to 20 basis points annualized with pass-rated loans at approximately 97% of the portfolio; core efficiency ratio held near 49%
summary: Amalgamated reported record core net income of $34.6 million ($1.14 per diluted share), record net interest income of $87.9 million, and net revenue above $100 million for the first time, with NIM at 3.77%, core ROA of 1.44%, and core efficiency near 49%. The company raised its 2026 NII outlook from a $340 million high end to $341-$342 million and lifted core pre-tax pre-provision earnings guidance from $190 million to $193-$194 million, citing Q3 outperformance. Management guided to modest Q4 margin compression from a DDA/IBA deposit remix as the election cycle concludes, with DDA expected to fall from 42% to roughly 36% of deposits and provision expense of $5.0-$5.5 million in Q4. Deposits rose $256 million to $8.7 billion, commercial loans grew about $93 million, CPACE assessments rose about $54.2 million, and net charge-offs fell to 20 basis points annualized.

negative_highlights: Traffic fell 14% YoY and 11% sequentially, with the slowdown accelerating in September and continuing through early October per management
Q4 gross margin guided to 24.0%-24.5% from 24.8% in Q3, and full-year SG&A guidance raised to 10.3%-10.5% of revenues on lower closing volume and lost leverage
First-time and move-up orders fell 9% and 14% YoY respectively, and the company walked away from roughly 8,000 optioned lots in the quarter
positive_highlights: Cancellation rate fell to 10% of starting backlog from 12% a year ago and 50 bps sequentially, suggesting contracted buyers remain committed
Build costs of $75/sq ft were down 5% YoY, the third straight quarter of that decline, with low-single-digit YoY reduction expected again in Q4
Active-adult net new orders rose 11% YoY and backlog grew to 10,298 homes/$6.4B from 9,888/$6.2B, with cycle time below 100 days for the first time since pre-COVID
summary: PulteGroup reported Q3 home sale revenues of $3.9B, down 9% YoY on a 9% decline in closings to 6,876 homes, with EPS of $2.53 versus $2.96 a year ago. Net new orders fell 6% to 6,208 as absorption dropped 13% to 1.9 homes/month and traffic fell 14% YoY, slowing further in September and continuing into October. Q3 gross margin of 24.8% was down 140 bps YoY including $26M (70 bps) of impairments and 10.4% incentives. Management guided Q4 closings of 7,000-7,500 and full-year 27,000-27,500 homes, Q4 gross margin of 24.0%-24.5%, and raised the full-year SG&A guide to 10.3%-10.5% of revenues on lost leverage, while noting willingness to cut 2027 land spend.

negative_highlights: Deposits of $21.6 billion were roughly flat sequentially versus prior expectations for growth, which management attributed to competition and 37 branch closures.
Q4 NIM guided 1-2 bps below the 360 bps reported, as deposit betas run ~50% and new loans are funded with higher-cost wholesale borrowings.
Q4 operating expenses guided to ~$153 million, above the $150 million Q3 level after adding back $2 million healthcare rebate and ~$1 million deferred comp benefit.
positive_highlights: Total loans grew 5.1% year-over-year and 8.7% annualized sequentially, with C&I up 11% YoY and 16% QoQ annualized.
Criticized and classified loans fell $93 million (55 bps) from Q2 to 3.19% of total loans, driving a 4 bps reduction in the ACL ratio to 1.08%.
Adjusted EPS rose ~7% YoY, NIM improved 7 bps YoY to 360 bps, and deposit funding costs declined 12 bps YoY to 180 bps.
summary: WesBanco reported Q3 2026 GAAP EPS of $0.88 and adjusted EPS of $0.89, with GAAP net income of $85 million. Loans grew 5.1% year-over-year and 8.7% annualized sequentially, NIM was 360 bps (up 7 bps YoY, flat QoQ ex-accretion), and the efficiency ratio was 52% with CET1 at 10.6%. Management guided Q4 NIM down 1-2 bps to ~358-359 bps, Q4 fee income up 3%-5% YoY, Q4 opex ~$153 million (up from $150 million), and reiterated mid-single-digit full-year loan growth. Deposits were flat sequentially against expectations, which management attributed to branch closures and competition, while CRE payoffs of ~$370 million remained a ~1% loan growth headwind.

negative_highlights: Revenue of $586 million finished slightly below the $580-$600 million guide excluding Valco Melton, reflecting Industrial project delays and longer decision cycles
Adjusted operating margin contracted about 180 bps to 27% on unfavorable product and channel mix, including higher powder finishing systems
Industrial legacy bookings were only up about 1% year to date and home center channel was down slightly, with Q4 guidance assuming no demand acceleration
positive_highlights: Organic incoming orders rose 7% in the quarter and backlog increased $51 million, or 18%, from the start of the year
Expansion Markets bookings jumped 62% in Q3 and 44% year to date, with semiconductor posting its strongest quarterly revenue in several years
Year-to-date operating cash flow of $463 million represented 116% of adjusted net earnings, alongside $467 million of buybacks and $145 million of dividends
summary: Graco reported record Q3 revenue of $586 million, up 8% (4% organic), with adjusted EPS up 5% to $0.81. However, revenue came in slightly below the prior $580-$600 million guidance range excluding Valco Melton, driven by Industrial project delays, and adjusted operating margin fell about 180 bps to 27% on product and channel mix. Q4 guidance of $610-$640 million implies little organic acceleration, and management explicitly said the outlook assumes no demand acceleration; organic orders rose 7% in the quarter with backlog up $51 million (18%) year to date.

negative_highlights: Net interest margin fell 13 bps sequentially to 3.70%, missing prior flat-to-up guidance, which the CFO called a surprise and partly attributed to an $800,000 premium amortization from one Keystone loan payoff
Net income of $19.0 million and diluted EPS of $0.93 declined from $22.0 million and $1.08 in Q2, and the adjusted efficiency ratio rose to 58.63% from 56.5%
Non-performing loans rose to $29 million, or 0.53% of total loans, from $27.1 million and 0.50% at June, driven by $2.3 million of SBA loans placed on non-accrual
positive_highlights: Non-interest-bearing demand deposits rose $78 million to $721 million, or 12.2% of total deposits, from 11% at June, and were up 60.3% over 12 months versus 35.5% total deposit growth
Underlying loan growth exceeded $144 million in the quarter excluding the $87 million securitization sale, and loans were up roughly $80 million early in Q4
Tangible book value per share reached a new high of $33.31, up from $33.08 at June and $30.91 a year ago; credit recorded $27,000 of net recoveries, the third consecutive quarter of net recoveries
summary: Third Coast reported Q3 FY2026 net income of $19.0 million and diluted EPS of $0.93, down from $22.0 million and $1.08 in Q2 and $1.03 a year ago, though adjusted net income excluding $3.2 million of merger costs was $21.6 million or $1.06 per share. Net interest margin fell 13 bps sequentially to 3.70%, below the prior flat-to-up guidance, which the CFO called a surprise and attributed largely to an $800,000 premium amortization on a single Keystone loan payoff plus a low-yield securitization. Management guided Q4 NIM to about 3.80% and raised the quarterly fee income range to roughly $5 million from $4-4.5 million while holding loan growth guidance unchanged; the pending Great Plains merger is expected to close between February 1 and April 1, 2027. Underlying loan growth exceeded $144 million excluding an $87 million securitization sale, and tangible book value per share reached a new high of $33.31.

negative_highlights: Aeronautics full-year 2026 sales and profit guidance trimmed slightly on revised F-35 next-lot award timing, with the top-end sales bump pushed to 2027
F-16 and C-130 unfavorable profit adjustments partially offset higher Aeronautics volume
Pension contribution in excess of $1 billion required next year, plus a $0.15 quarterly dividend increase to $3.60 per share
positive_highlights: Sales rose 11% YoY to $20.7 billion with all four segments growing, led by MFC up 24% on munitions ramps
Full-year 2026 guidance raised again: sales to $80-82 billion, segment operating profit to $8.575-8.675 billion, and free cash flow to $7.8-8 billion
Record backlog of $292 billion, up $113 billion YoY, with 4x book-to-bill, including the PAC-3 seven-year contract worth up to $58.6 billion
summary: Lockheed Martin reported Q3 FY2026 sales up 11% YoY to $20.7 billion, segment operating profit of $2.2 billion at a 10.8% margin, and EPS of $7.97 versus $6.95, a 15% increase. Free cash flow was $3 billion in the quarter and $5.6 billion year to date, with backlog reaching a record $292 billion on 4x book-to-bill. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance for sales to $80-82 billion, segment operating profit to $8.575-8.675 billion, and free cash flow to $7.8-8 billion, citing MFC munitions ramps and improved execution. The main wrinkle is Aeronautics, where full-year guidance was trimmed slightly on revised F-35 Lot 20 award timing, shifted into 2027.

negative_highlights: Net income fell 17% YoY to $156M and EPS was $3.82, with the decline attributable to a prior-year $38M favorable discrete tax item
Full-year average loan growth guidance narrowed to ~4% from low- to mid-single digits, and management said growth will not accelerate from Q3 levels
Management guided 2027 NIM flat to slightly down and flagged next year as potentially a 'thin year' for positive operating leverage
positive_highlights: Net loss rate improved 99 bps YoY to 6.40% and full-year guidance raised to 6.9%-7.0% from 7.0%-7.1%, the second consecutive quarterly improvement
Revenue up 5% ($46M) and pre-tax income up 6% ($13M) on 7% end-of-period loan growth to $18.9B and 9% credit sales growth
summary: Bread Financial reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $1.03B implied by $46M/5% YoY growth, net income of $156M and diluted EPS of $3.82, down 17% YoY only because the prior year included a $38M discrete tax benefit; pre-tax income rose 6%. End-of-period loans grew 7% to $18.9B and credit sales 9%, while the net loss rate improved 99 bps YoY to 6.40% and delinquency fell 47 bps to 5.57%. Full-year net loss rate guidance was improved for the second consecutive quarter to 6.9%-7.0% from 7.0%-7.1%, but average loan growth guidance was narrowed to ~4% from low- to mid-single digits and management flagged NIM flat to slightly down in 2027 and a potentially thin year for operating leverage. Capital return was $75M of buybacks plus a 9% dividend increase, with minimal buybacks expected in Q4 absent a preferred issuance.

negative_highlights: Non-performing loans rose to 40 bps of total loans, driven by Bank of Houston acquired credits
Non-interest income slipped to $13.8 million from $14.1 million on lower bank card and interchange revenue
Tangible book value per share fell to $29.23 from $29.60 as AOCI dropped $25.5 million on rising interest rates
positive_highlights: EPS rose to $1.06 from $0.96 in the linked quarter, with net income up to $20.8 million from $19.0 million
Efficiency ratio improved 350 bps to 58.1% as non-interest expense fell $1.8 million to $38.1 million
Loans grew $60 million, or 6.3% annualized, to $3.83 billion despite a $25 million secured payoff, and NIM held stable at 4.00%
summary: South Plains reported Q3 FY2026 net income of $20.8 million versus $19.0 million in the linked quarter, with diluted EPS of $1.06 versus $0.96. ROA improved to 1.53% and the efficiency ratio improved to 58.1% from 61.6%, helped by lower personnel costs and the absence of Bank of Houston acquisition expenses. Loans grew $60 million (6.3% annualized) to $3.83 billion despite a $25 million deposit-secured payoff, and NIM held stable at 4.00%. Management reiterated full-year loan growth guidance in the mid-single digits; no EPS guidance was provided.

negative_highlights: Net charge-offs came in at 36 bps annualized versus the 15-20 bps run rate management guided to on the Q2 call, driven by a $7 million private club charge and $2.6 million hotel write-down
EPS of $1.14 fell from $1.19 a year ago, ROAA was 95 bps, and non-performing assets to total assets rose 11 bps linked-quarter with $18 million of agricultural loans newly added
Tangible book value per share fell to $39.45 from $42.30 and the TCE ratio dropped to 8.13% from 9.04% on AOCI/hedge fair-value declines; Laguna OREO monetization now pushed to Q1 2027
positive_highlights: Net interest income grew $5.9 million to $175 million with NIM held stable at 4.30% despite competitive pricing pressure
Loans grew $452 million (nearly 4% sequentially) and deposits rose $624 million (4.3% linked-quarter), bringing total deposits to $15.1 billion
Core efficiency ratio improved to 58.9% from 61.1% in the linked quarter, and capital management included $34 million of buybacks and a $0.01 dividend increase to $0.36
summary: EFSC reported Q3 FY2026 net income of $42 million, or $1.14 per diluted share, down from $1.19 a year ago but up from $1.09 in the linked quarter; adjusted EPS was $1.17 versus $1.13 in Q2. Net interest income rose $5.9 million to $175 million with NIM stable at 4.30%, and loans grew $452 million (nearly 4% sequentially) while deposits rose $624 million to $15.1 billion. Provision expense of $18.1 million and net charge-offs of 36 bps annualized came in well above management's prior 15-20 bps charge-off expectation stated on the Q2 call, driven by a $7 million St. Louis private club credit and a $2.6 million Southern California hotel write-down; ROAA was 95 bps. Management guided to Q4 margin up a couple basis points and mid-to-high single-digit loan growth for the rest of 2026, with criticized/classified levels (currently ~6.3%) targeted to return to 4.5%-5% and NPA normalization slipping into Q1 2027.

negative_highlights: Net income fell to $14.0 million ($1.27/share) from $17.8 million ($1.56/share) a year ago, including a $3.5 million pre-tax non-cash hedge accounting charge ($0.23/share after tax)
Net loans declined $59.3 million sequentially and $108.4 million year to date to $4.25 billion, with CRE down $95.8 million and multifamily down $105.6 million over nine months
Management guided NIM to roughly 3.65%-3.70%, down from 3.75%, as the $400 million securities purchase carries a spread near 100 bps or less over FHLB borrowings
positive_highlights: Net interest margin expanded to 3.75% from 3.72% in the prior-year quarter and 3.76% sequentially despite a $2 million quarterly swap income headwind
Credit metrics remain minimal: non-performing loans at 0.03% of total loans, net charge-offs of $397,000 (0.04% annualized), and no provision on the loan portfolio
Branch consolidation and 66 position eliminations completed October 1 are expected to deliver $4.4 million-$4.8 million in annual expense savings starting in Q4
summary: GSBC reported Q3 FY2026 net income of $14.0 million, or $1.27 per diluted share, down from $17.8 million and $1.56 a year ago, with a $3.5 million pre-tax non-cash hedge accounting charge; operating net income was $16.5 million, or $1.50 per share. Net interest income of $50.3 million was down $504,000 YoY on the absence of roughly $2 million quarterly income from a terminated swap, while NIM expanded to 3.75% from 3.72%. Net loans fell $59.3 million sequentially and $108.4 million year to date to $4.25 billion on CRE and multifamily payoffs, and management guided NIM toward 3.65%-3.70% going forward, citing a narrower spread on $400 million of securities purchases. Branch consolidations and 66 position eliminations, effective October 1, are expected to yield $4.4 million-$4.8 million in annual expense savings beginning in Q4.

negative_highlights: Core gross margin fell 150 bps and core operating margin fell 80 bps (down 90 bps currency-neutral); core EPS of $2 was up only 1% and flat currency-neutral

Full-year cost headwind raised to about $1.4 billion after tax at $100 Brent, with combined input cost, FX and below-the-line headwinds of $1.9 billion or $0.79 per share versus $0.56 expected in July
Guidance held rather than raised even after the 4% start, with first-half organic growth of about 3% implying deceleration in Q2 and free cash flow productivity guided to 85-90% (93% in Q1)
positive_highlights: Organic sales rose 4.0% with volume up 2.4 points, mix up over a point, and all 10 product categories and all six regions growing
Over 70% of top U.S. customers holding or growing share, up from less than 10% in the first half of fiscal 2026 and 50% in the second half
Greater China organic sales grew 8% (SK-II +12%, Pampers up close to 50%) and productivity delivered about 250 bps improvement, with $500-550 million of productivity in Q1
summary: P&G reported Q1 FY2027 organic sales growth of 4.0% (volume +2.4 pts, pricing +0.4 pts, mix +1 pt), with all 10 categories and all six regions growing, but core EPS of $2 was up only 1% (flat currency-neutral) and core gross margin fell 150 bps with core operating margin down 80 bps. Fiscal 2027 guidance was maintained rather than raised: organic sales +1-3% and core EPS growth of 0-3% ($6.89-$7.11), despite starting the year above the sales range. The key change versus the prior outlook is a larger cost headwind, now roughly $1.4 billion after tax (assuming $100 Brent) and $1.9 billion/$0.79 per share combined with FX and below-the-line items, up from $0.56 per share, with management flagging materially higher cost pressure in Q2 and the second half and guiding first-half organic growth of about 3%.

negative_highlights: Full-year guidance cut to adjusted EPS of $5.30-$5.50 and EBITDA of $1.2-1.25 billion, with Q4 range left wide due to macro/input-cost uncertainty
$829 million non-cash goodwill impairment on the consumer EMEA business, which Paul said had been passing its annual goodwill test by only a 3% margin
Consumer volume mix down 3% YoY and Consumer EBITDA down 9%; OCC up 90% YoY and total URB production costs up more than $60/ton
positive_highlights: PPP program delivered $60 million of savings, its largest quarterly contribution to date, with annualized savings of $51 million
Industrial sales rose 5% to $646 million; URB trade ton sales up 10% YoY in North America and mill utilization at 94%
Free cash flow rose 2% YoY and total debt was reduced by $162 million while an $800 million term loan was refinanced
summary: Sonoco reported Q3 FY2026 net sales of $2 billion, down 4% YoY (flat excluding the ThermoSafe divestiture), adjusted EBITDA of $352 million (17.2% margin, down 9% YoY / 4% ex-ThermoSafe) and adjusted EPS of $1.67, down 13% YoY / 7% ex-ThermoSafe. Consumer volume mix fell 3% on drought-driven food-can demand and price-cost lag, while Industrial sales rose 5% on URB pricing and reels. Management lowered full-year guidance to sales of $7.2-7.4 billion, adjusted EBITDA of $1.2-1.25 billion, EPS of $5.30-5.50 and operating cash flow of $600-650 million, and recorded an $829 million non-cash goodwill impairment tied to the consumer EMEA business. Input costs (freight +$17 million YoY, OCC +$25/ton, diesel above $6.50/gal) ran ahead of price recovery, with full URB price realization deferred into 2027.

negative_highlights: Higher fuel negatively impacted the operating ratio by ~250 bps versus prior expectations, a swing from the expected tailwind
Costs rose 17% with over half from fuel; guidance now embeds ~$700 million incremental fuel expense versus start of year
Management said most truck-to-rail conversion gains are temporary and could revert to highway over a year or two without structural change
positive_highlights: Revenue less fuel rose 6% to an all-time record; intermodal revenue less fuel up 7% and merchandise up 5%
Adjusted EPS grew 10% to $3.62 and net income rose 10% despite the fuel headwind
Record workforce productivity with on-time originations up 12 percentage points and a train accident rate of 1.74, a historical best
summary: Norfolk Southern reported 14% revenue growth (6% revenue less fuel to a record) with 3% volume growth in every business group and adjusted EPS up 10% to $3.62; adjusted operating ratio was 65.4%. The positive occurred despite higher fuel that management said hurt the operating ratio by ~250 bps versus prior expectations, and operating income rose 7% while costs increased 17% (over half from fuel). Full-year adjusted OpEx guidance is now just north of $9 billion including ~$700 million incremental fuel versus the start of the year, and 2026 CapEx guidance was raised to ~$2.1 billion from $1.9 billion; management kept core operating costs within the original guide. Management was candid that most current truck-to-rail conversion is temporary and framed the UP merger as the structural fix.

negative_highlights: Depletions and shipments each declined about 5%, trailing a category down roughly 3%, with full-year volume guidance narrowed to the low end of the prior range
Non-GAAP operating profit fell 6% YoY as freight rates rose over 50%, and the $9.5M higher freight costs more than offset lower shipment volumes
Twisted Tea, Truly and Samuel Adams all declined; Truly remains under strategic review and management is cutting advertising behind the brand
positive_highlights: Gross margin of 51.7% rose 90 bps YoY to the highest quarterly rate since 2017, absorbing higher aluminum, energy and tariff costs
Low end of full-year gross margin and non-GAAP EPS guidance raised to $9-$10.50 from $8.50-$10.50, with tariff cost outlook cut to $18M-$22M from $20M-$30M
Sun Cruiser grew approximately 60% in tracked channels and Angry Orchard grew for a sixth consecutive quarter; internal production reached 98% of domestic volume versus 89% a year ago
summary: Depletions fell 5% and shipments 4.9% in Q3, with revenue down 3.2% as volume declines in Twisted Tea, Truly and Samuel Adams offset Sun Cruiser and Angry Orchard growth. Gross margin reached 51.7%, up 90 bps YoY and the highest since 2017, while non-GAAP operating profit declined 6% and non-GAAP EPS was $4.37. Full-year depletion and shipment guidance was narrowed to down mid-single digits at the low end of the prior range, but the low end of gross margin (49%-50%) and non-GAAP EPS ($9-$10.50, from $8.50-$10.50) guidance was raised on productivity savings and lower tariff costs of $18M-$22M versus $20M-$30M prior. The company repurchased $80 million of shares year to date through October 16 and cut 2026 capex to $55M-$70M from $60M-$80M.

Old Second reported Q3 2026 GAAP net income of $28.9 million, or $0.56 per diluted share, with ROA of 1.69% and an adjusted efficiency ratio of 52.06% versus 50.8% last quarter. Results included $12.7 million of net charge-offs, $9.2 million from one previously reserved C&I warehousing credit, partly offset by a 38% ($61.3 million) decline in criticized loans and lower classifieds. NIM rose 4 bps to 5.27%, but management guided to roughly 5 bps of NIM giveback in Q4 and low single-digit loan growth, and raised the common dividend 14% while continuing buybacks. Tangible book value per share slipped to $14.75 from $14.77 on $39.5 million of repurchases.

negative_highlights: CFO guided 2027 revenue roughly flat versus 2026, residential down, and said 'I don't see margin expansion next year' with title pre-tax margin only stable to slightly lower
First three weeks of October: open purchase orders down 8%, refinance down 35% and commercial down 7%, with the 30-year mortgage rate up about 100 bps over six months to 7.5%
Home Warranty pre-tax income fell 30% to $11 million on higher marketing spend; CFO flagged that prior-year reserve releases (75 bps of the 3.0% loss provision) will likely slow or cease
positive_highlights: Commercial revenue rose 21% to $297 million with a record Q3 for National Commercial Services, eight of 11 asset classes growing and average revenue per order up 13%
Title investment income grew 11% to $169 million, with First American Trust deposits up almost 38% YoY and ServiceMac fee revenue up 31%
Dividend raised 11% to an annual rate of $2.44 per share; Endpoint automation rate climbed from 30% in Q1 to 42% in Q3
summary: Title segment revenue rose 7% to $2.0 billion with adjusted EPS of $1.78, up 5% YoY, driven by commercial revenue up 21% to $297 million (record Q3 NCS revenue, 13% higher average revenue per order) while purchase fell 3% and refinance fell 1%. Management guided 2027 total revenue to be roughly flat versus 2026, with residential down, commercial modestly up, and explicitly said it does not see title margin expansion next year, citing continued pressure. Early Q4 order trends were soft: open purchase orders down 8%, refinance down 35% and commercial down 7% in the first three weeks of October, against a 30-year mortgage rate near 7.5%. Offsets included an 11% dividend increase to $2.44 annualized and title investment income up 11%, but the release of prior-year loss reserves (75 bps of the 3.0% provision) is expected to slow or stop.

Medpace reported Q3 2026 revenue of $716M, up 8.5% YoY, with EBITDA of $172.1M (up 16%) at a 24% margin versus 22.5% prior year, and diluted EPS of $4.84 versus $3.86. Net new business awards hit an all-time high of $873.4M (up 10.6% YoY), and trailing-12-month awards grew 23.9% to $3.02B. Full-year 2026 guidance was updated to revenue of $2.835-2.855B (12-12.8% growth) and EBITDA of $638-652M, with EPS of $17.97-18.32; management declined to guide 2027 until February but said consensus looks reasonable versus current modeling. Cancellations ran toward the higher end of the expected range this quarter, cited as primarily product failure rather than funding.

negative_highlights: 2027 premium outlook cut to at least $45 billion from a prior $46.5 billion as Georgia and Texas STAR/CHIP implementation delays $1.3 billion of premium.
2027 embedded earnings harvest reduced by $0.50 per share to ~$4.00 per share due to potential timing of Georgia and Texas operating leverage.
MAPD business expected to lose $1 per share in 2026 and Marketplace expected to lose $0.75 per share, with Q4 Marketplace MCR guided to 96.1%.
positive_highlights: Q3 results in line across all segments: Medicaid MCR 93%, Medicare MCR 93%, Marketplace MCR 92.5%, with consolidated adjusted EPS of $0.89 on ~$10.5 billion premium revenue.
January 1 renewal cohort rates averaging ~7% on 80% of that cohort known, with known rates covering 70% of full-year 2027 premium.
Legacy Medicaid business delivering a 1.6% pre-tax margin for full year 2026, and duals contributing $1.25 per share at a 1.4% pre-tax margin.
summary: Molina reported Q3 2026 premium revenue of ~$10.5 billion with adjusted EPS of $0.89, a 92.9% consolidated MCR, 6.3% adjusted G&A ratio, and 0.6% adjusted pre-tax margin. Full-year 2026 guidance was reaffirmed at premium revenue of ~$42 billion and adjusted EPS of at least $5.25, with the annual rate outlook raised to 4.5% and trend raised to 5.5%. Preliminary 2027 premium outlook was cut to at least $45 billion from $46.5 billion and embedded earnings realization trimmed by $0.50, both due to Georgia and Texas contract delays, though 2027 EPS building blocks were disclosed at more than $9.50 per share. Management framed Medicaid margins as troughing and cited January 1 rate renewals averaging ~7% on known cohorts.

negative_highlights: Loans declined to $46.9 billion from $47.2 billion at June 30 as CRE payoffs and competitive pricing weighed; management expects flat to slightly down into Q1 2027
Tangible book value fell to $18.10 on higher AOCI from rising rates; CET1 declined to 11.5% as buybacks outpaced capital generation
Guidance implies Q4 NIM of about 4.05%, below the 4.11% reported, and total risk-based capital is expected to decline roughly 50 bps from TruPS redemptions
positive_highlights: Adjusted NIM expanded 12 bps sequentially to 4.11%, with management guiding to about 4.05% in Q4 and a low-4% starting point for 2027
New $1.2 billion share repurchase authorized after the prior plan completed, having returned over $1 billion to shareholders over the past year and reduced share count 8%
Operating non-interest income of $87 million landed at the high end of guidance, with treasury management, card, and wealth fee momentum
summary: Columbia reported Q3 2026 EPS of $0.78 GAAP and $0.82 operating, with operating pre-provision net revenue up 7% QoQ and 25% YoY. NIM was 4.11%, up 12 bps sequentially after adjusting for one-time items, while non-interest income of $87 million operating came in at the high end of guidance. Management guided Q4 NIM to about 4.05% and Q4 operating non-interest expense to $330-$335 million, and announced a new $1.2 billion buyback after completing the prior authorization with an 8% share count reduction. Loans declined to $46.9 billion from $47.2 billion as commercial and CRE mix improved and deposits grew to $52.7 billion.
