negative_highlights: The intelligence business did not ramp as anticipated, with customer churn among acquired customers and a shift from data products to a data platform still underway.
Revenue per invoice growth is expected to slow materially going forward as the repricing effort is largely complete.
ROA was 70 basis points with episodic credit noise, and the company declined to accrue the previously signaled $6 million of back-half incentive comp, giving only $100 million of Q4 expense guidance.
positive_highlights: Factoring added 706 new customers year to date despite a contracting carrier population, with management citing 8,000 carriers paid in factoring and 134,000 carriers paid last quarter.
Payments revenue per invoice rose about 3% on the repricing effort, and management called high-single-digit invoice volume growth very attainable now that repricing is largely complete.

LoadPay is expected to exit the year around 14,000 accounts, with accounts open over 120 days generating north of $1,200 annualized revenue, and management sees potential to move from 1.1% to 5%-10% of payment volumes over the next couple of years.
summary: Triumph Financial reported Q3 FY2026 with transportation revenue growth, factoring and payments margin expansion, and LoadPay scaling to roughly 14,000 accounts exiting the year. Management set a 2027 sub-$400 million expense target requiring at least $20 million of efficiencies and a 2027 earnings bridge to around 1.0%-1.2% ROA assuming flat invoices, reiterating it does not provide formal revenue guidance. The intelligence business underperformed with customer churn and a slower-than-expected start, which management owned, while factoring added 706 new customers year to date and revenue per invoice growth is expected to slow as the repricing effort is largely complete. ROA was 70 basis points with episodic credit noise, and no specific Q4 incentive compensation accrual was given.

negative_highlights: EPS fell to $1.73 from $1.83 in the linked quarter, and adjusted NIM of 3.65% represented modest compression
Management guided to softer second-quarter net loan growth and a potential exit margin in the low 360s amid liability sensitivity
Non-interest expense rose 4% ($1 million) to $26.6 million, above the analyst's expectation, and the allowance rose $3.4 million to 1.31% of loans partly for an evolving economic environment
positive_highlights: NIM expanded 3 bps to 3.70% and net interest income rose 3.5% from the linked quarter
Non-performing assets declined to $32 million or 0.61% of total assets from 0.64%, and adversely classified loans fell nearly $1 million to $53 million
New business deposit accounts reached $42 million at September 30 and core CDs grew $95 million while brokered CDs were cut $35 million
summary: Southern Missouri Bancorp reported Q1 FY2027 diluted EPS of $1.73 versus $1.83 in the linked June quarter, with ROAA of 1.44% and ROCE of 12.7%; net interest margin expanded 3 bps to 3.70% but would have been 3.65% excluding fair value accretion and a $200,000 interest recovery, implying modest core compression. Loans grew $64 million (1.5%) and deposits $66 million (1.5%), while non-interest expense rose $1 million (4%) to $26.6 million. Management reiterated mid-single-digit expense growth and mid-single-digit FY2027 loan growth, but flagged softer net loan growth in the December quarter and near-term margin pressure given liability sensitivity, with an exit margin in the low 360s noted as a possibility. Credit improved modestly with NPAs down to 0.61% of assets, though an elevated $21 million C&I modification lifted performing modifications to $51 million.

negative_highlights: Americas Adjusted EBITDA fell 3% to $122M on lower volumes, higher operations/overhead costs, and lower input cost recovery.
Brazil shipments declined 5% due to customer mix and a contract reset, lagging improved industry growth.
Q4 EBITDA guidance implies a decline of roughly 4-5% at the midpoint versus prior year on FX headwinds, inflation (notably coatings), and lapping strong prior-year shipments growth of 4%.
positive_highlights: Europe shipments grew 6% and segment Adjusted EBITDA rose 11% to $91M on strong volume and input cost recovery.
Announced acceleration and upscaling of European investments (two new can lines in the U.K. and Spain) expected to drive material EBITDA growth from 2028.
summary: AMBP delivered Q3 FY2026 with global beverage can shipments up 2% (Europe +6%, Americas -1%, Brazil -5%) and Adjusted EBITDA of $213M that exceeded guidance, leading management to upgrade FY2026 Adjusted EBITDA guidance to $785-795M. Europe revenue rose 11% to $693M with segment EBITDA +11% to $91M, while Americas revenue rose 25% to ~$1B but segment EBITDA fell 3% to $122M on lower volumes and costs. The company is accelerating and upsizing European capacity investments (two new lines in the U.K. and Spain), lifting growth CapEx from $90M in 2026 to ~$250M in 2027, and expects 2027 constant-currency EBITDA growth to be only moderate given a more inflationary environment and lapping a strong Q4. Net leverage was 5.1x, down from 5.2x, with liquidity of $736M and an unchanged $0.10 quarterly dividend.

negative_highlights: FirstService Brands EBITDA margin compressed 80 bps to 11.3%, with roofing hit by both a 4% reported revenue decline and gross margin compression from competitive pricing, and Brands margin guided down again in Q4

Roofing organic revenue fell high single digit and Q4 organic is guided flat to slightly down, with Florida still 'very difficult' and management citing limited forecasting visibility across 12 separate systems

Home Services faced worsening housing and consumer sentiment, with Q4 revenue guided flat in aggregate and down low single digit organically; leverage rose to 2.4x from 1.8x, limiting buyback pace to free cash flow
positive_highlights: FirstService Residential delivered 7% EBITDA growth to $71 million with 30 bps of margin expansion to 11.3%, and Q4 margin improvement expected at least double that 30 bps pace after exiting non-core aquatics
Century Fire revenue grew over 10% including high single-digit organic, with backlog ticking up sequentially and 10%+ growth expected for the full year
Restoration Brands revenue rose 10% year-over-year, better than expectation, and roofing backlog finished at the highest level in a year, up sequentially
summary: FirstService reported Q3 revenue of $1.53 billion, up 6% (4% organic), adjusted EBITDA of $170 million up 3% with margin compressing to 11.1% from 11.4%, and adjusted EPS of $1.89 up 7% aided by 2.2 million shares repurchased for roughly $300 million. CEO called results in aggregate in line with expectations, though organic growth exceeded expectations; Full-year guidance was maintained at mid-single-digit revenue and EBITDA growth with margins roughly in line, and revenue is now seen at the upper end of the range set mid-year. FirstService Residential grew 5% with 30 bps of margin expansion, Century Fire grew over 10% with high single-digit organic, but FirstService Brands margin compressed 80 bps as roofing revenue fell 4% on competitive pricing and weak Florida demand, with Brands margin expected down again in Q4. Leverage rose to 2.4x from 1.8x due to buybacks, tempering future repurchase pace.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA of $84 million was down ~$82 million (~50%) sequentially, with ~$29 million unfavorable metal price lag swing versus the prior year quarter
Packaging shipment growth outlook cut to 5-10% from 10-15% and automotive cut to a -5% to -10% decline from 0% to -5%, with full-year EBITDA now trending toward the low end of the ~45% growth guide
Incremental costs from the Bellwood outage, Roll Coat 4 startup, and furnace rebuilds represented ~640 bps of margin impact, and management acknowledged the Bellwood comeback was not handled well
positive_highlights: Aerospace and high strength conversion revenue rose 31% YoY to $131 million on a 42% shipment increase; management declared commercial aerospace plate destocking over
General engineering conversion revenue up 21% to $99 million with record conversion revenue per pound of $1.47 in the quarter
Full-year 2026 free cash flow now expected to exceed $200 million (prior outlook already surpassed), and net debt leverage improved to 2.0x from 3.4x at year-end
summary: Q3 FY2026 conversion revenue rose 25% YoY to $439 million ($1.46/lb, +12%), adjusted EBITDA $84 million was up only $3 million YoY, and adjusted EPS of $1.89 was roughly flat versus $1.86. Results landed in line with management expectations, but guidance shading moved to the lower end of the ~45% YoY EBITDA growth outlook, with packaging shipment growth cut to 5-10% from 10-15% and automotive shipments cut to a -5% to -10% decline from 0% to -5%. The sequential EBITDA decline of ~$82 million (~50%) reflected a $28 million metal price lag swing plus $54 million of tighter scrap spreads and lower scrap utilization, and free cash flow guidance was raised to exceed $200 million with leverage improving to 2.0x.

negative_highlights: No large MENA project award is expected to begin delivery in fiscal 2027 versus the ~$70M recognized in fiscal 2026; management said it expects to cover only about half of that hole with smaller projects and growth initiatives.
Full-year irrigation operating margin fell to 14.8% from 17.1% on lower volume, weaker fixed-cost absorption, and higher input costs; Q4 margin slipped to 12.9% from 13.7%.
Management said price realization lags rising material and freight costs by a couple of quarters and that North America demand remains subdued until net farm income improves.
positive_highlights: North America irrigation revenue grew 11% to $55.4M in Q4, with management noting demand response to $5+ corn and volumes outside storm-replacement business.
Infrastructure segment Q4 revenue rose 13% to $27.8M and operating income rose 41% to $5.0M, with margin at 17.9% versus 14.4% on favorable mix.
Agricultural technology annual recurring revenue grew ~11% year-over-year, extending the five-year CAGR to more than 15%, and $96.1M (about 173% of net earnings) was returned to shareholders.
summary: Q4 revenue rose 5% to $161.6M and EPS rose to $1.10 from $0.99, with North America irrigation up 11% and infrastructure revenue up 13% at a 17.9% margin, but irrigation segment margin contracted to 12.9% from 13.7% on higher input costs. Full-year revenue fell 6% to $635.9M and EPS fell 21% to $5.33. Management guided that no large MENA project award is expected to begin delivery in fiscal 2027, leaving roughly half of the prior year's ~$70M to be covered by smaller projects and self-help, and said North America irrigation demand remains subdued absent sustained net farm income improvement. A global restructuring is expected to yield $8M in net annualized cost savings, and a small Brazilian acquisition (Setorial) was signed.

negative_highlights: Total operating expenses rose to 35% of revenue from 31% a year ago, with marketing at 23% of revenue ($230M) versus 18% ($147M)
Consolidated 30-plus day delinquency rose sequentially to 8%, including a 40 bp sequential increase in SMB delinquency
Q4 net revenue margin guided to 55%-60%, below Q3's 61%, as consumer margin is expected to revert toward ~50%
positive_highlights: Revenue crossed $1 billion for the first time, up 26% YoY, with originations up 31% to $2.6B
Adjusted EPS rose 33% to $4.48 with annualized ROE above 30%; consolidated net charge-off ratio improved to 8.1% from 8.5%
Cost of funds fell 60 bps YoY to 8% and buybacks more than doubled sequentially to $46M, with October already matching Q3's total
summary: Enova reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of roughly $1 billion, up 26% YoY and the first $1B quarter in company history, with originations up 31% to $2.6B, a consolidated net charge-off ratio improving to 8.1% from 8.5%, and adjusted EPS up 33% to $4.48. Q4 guidance calls for revenue around 25% higher YoY, a net revenue margin of 55%-60%, and adjusted EPS 30%-35% above Q4 FY2025, consistent with the growth trajectory rather than a formal raise. The company withdrew its bank charter applications but said the decision does not diminish growth plans, added new product ambitions, and more than doubled buyback pace to $46M in Q3, matching that amount already in October. Total operating expenses rose to 35% of revenue from 31% a year ago, driven by marketing at 23% of revenue versus 18%.

negative_highlights: Elevated commercial loan payoffs constrained balance sheet growth, with total loans up only $53 million QoQ
Non-accrual balances increased $183 million (up $33 million QoQ), driven largely by a $30 million C&I reclass following an SNC exam
Non-interest expense guidance of 19%-20% growth for 2026 reflects continued cost pressure from acquisition integration and strategic investments
positive_highlights: Net interest margin expanded 3 bps to 3.20%, described as the second-best quarter in over a decade, despite lower purchase accounting accretion
Non-interest income grew 8% QoQ to $87 million, led by capital markets, asset gains, and service charges
Commercial pipelines are up 36%-40% YoY, supporting confidence in future C&I production
summary: Associated reported Q3 FY2026 GAAP EPS of $0.76 ($0.81 adjusted), with net interest income up $7 million to $377 million and NIM expanding 3 bps to 3.20%. Core customer deposits grew ~2% (~$700 million), non-interest income rose 8% to $87 million, and non-interest expense fell $12 million to $260 million including $13 million of one-time acquisition costs. Full-year guidance was reaffirmed for loan growth of 18%-20% and C&I growth of 20%-22%, while acquisition cost guidance was lowered to ~$48.5 million from $52.5 million. The company executed $100 million of buybacks, its first major repurchase since 2021, and management struck a confident tone on pipeline growth and future strategic initiatives.

negative_highlights: Higher interest rates drove a $0.25 back-half earnings impact, of which about $0.05 is fee income and the balance interest expense
Some remaining dispositions, including JV stakes with associated fees, may slip into the first half of 2027, below the self-imposed $2.5 billion target timing
Summit One Vanderbilt operating loss widened year over year on percentage-rent timing and pre-opening Paris costs, with management calling 2026 tourism below expectations
positive_highlights: Leased occupancy reached 95%, with more than 2 million sq ft leased year to date and a 1.3 million sq ft pipeline, of which ~840,000 sq ft are active lease negotiations
Mark-to-market rents averaging around 15% above prior rents, with leasing mark-to-market cited at north of 20% and 4%+ same-store NOI growth
Completed over $7 billion of 2026 financings, including the $2 billion 245 Park refinancing, plus a $40 million hospitality-business sale at a $200 million valuation (20x FFO)
summary: SL Green reported leased occupancy of 95% and surpassed 2 million sq ft of leasing year to date, with mark-to-market rents running roughly 15% above prior rents on average and same-store NOI growth above 4%. Management said 2026 earnings guidance is up more than $2 per share versus original December estimates, though a $0.25 back-half hit from higher interest rates and delayed dispositions pushed the near-term estimate below raised analyst expectations, prompting management to argue no miss occurred. The company has completed over $7 billion of 2026 financings, including the $2 billion 245 Park refinancing, and about $1 billion of pro-rata dispositions against a $2.5 billion target, with some remaining sales possibly slipping into 2027. Management reiterated a 2027 same-store cash NOI objective north of 10% and flagged a $40 million hospitality-platform sale at a $200 million valuation (20x FFO).

negative_highlights: Free cash flow was EUR -99m and 2026 FCF conversion guidance cut to 35%-55%
Network Infrastructure gross margin fell 150 bps to 41.2% on product mix and new-product ramp
Fixed Networks declined 22% and Core Software declined 13% on portfolio actions and server supply constraints
positive_highlights: Operating margin expanded 220 bps to 11.7% on operating leverage from higher sales
AI & Cloud net sales grew 123% YoY to 12% of group; order intake up 118% to EUR 1.5bn
2027 combined IP Networks and Optical Networks growth outlook set at 25%-30%, above the prior 18%-20% assumption for the current year
summary: Nokia grew Q3 net sales 9% with gross margin roughly stable at 44.6% and operating margin up 220 bps to 11.7% (operating profit EUR 605m). AI & Cloud net sales rose 123% and IP Networks 43%, while Fixed Networks fell 22% and Core Software 13%. Guidance for comparable operating profit was unchanged but the company now tracks above the midpoint and raised the 2027 combined IP/Optical growth outlook to 25%-30%. Free cash flow was EUR -99m and 2026 FCF conversion guidance was cut to 35%-55% on a EUR 400m working-capital build.

negative_highlights: Gross margin contracted about 90 bps to approximately 36.4%, with transportation pressure greater than anticipated entering the quarter
Operating margin of approximately 7.9% is below the 9% floor management says it is not comfortable operating under
Comps of just +0.4% reflected a 0.3% decline in transactions, with big ticket and companion animal still soft
positive_highlights: Comps improved sequentially through the quarter, from a decline of less than 1% in July to solid growth in September, with October run-rate in line with September
Digital sales grew approximately 16% with growth in both traffic and conversion; total pet business grew 5% including Allivet and VIP Petcare
Management sized 2027-2028 offsets: $50M+ annualized vendor support benefit (~30 bps), $75M+ SG&A reductions, and depreciation growth moderating to mid-single digits or lower
summary: TSCO reported Q3 FY2026 net sales up 5.1% to $3.91 billion with comps of just +0.4% (0.7% ticket, -0.3% transactions) and diluted EPS of $0.43. Gross margin fell roughly 90 bps to about 36.4% on higher transportation and price investment, SG&A rose 43 bps to 28.6% of sales, and operating margin was about 7.9%. Management reaffirmed full-year 2026 guidance and expects positive Q4 comps, with Q4 gross margin modestly down 10-30 bps versus the prior year and 15-20 bps of Nampa DC benefit. Leadership flagged that operating margin is below the 9% level it deems acceptable and outlined 2027-2028 offsets: $50M+ in vendor support (~30 bps), $75M+ in SG&A reductions, and moderating depreciation.

negative_highlights: Total deposits and customer repos fell $550 million to $16.3 billion from June 30, with interest-bearing down $360 million and non-interest-bearing down $190 million
Loan originations declined 15% QoQ and management said demand is slowing as higher rates push customers to use internal cash
Non-performing assets rose to $18.7 million from $16.8 million and classified loans increased $4.2 million to $113.9 million on two new classified CRE loans
positive_highlights: EPS of $0.44 rose 16% YoY and 52% from Q2's $0.29, with pre-tax income up to $106.1 million from $65 million sequentially
Adjusted ROA of 1.59% (1.48% reported) already exceeds the 150 bps target set for 2027, with return on average tangible common equity of 16.2%
Adjusted efficiency ratio improved to 42.1% from 43.9% in Q2 and 45.2% a year ago, and cost of deposits fell to 83 bps from 86 bps
summary: CVBF reported Q3 2026 net earnings of $78.1 million, or $0.44 per share, up from $48.3 million/$0.29 in Q2 and $52.6 million/$0.38 a year ago, with pre-tax income of $106.1 million versus $65 million sequentially. The quarter was the first full quarter including Heritage; EPS rose 16% YoY and adjusted ROA was 1.59% (1.48% reported) versus the 150 bps 2027 target, but $8.1 million of acquisition expense remained. Loans grew $105 million to $12.1 billion, but originations fell 15% QoQ and management said loan demand is slowing on higher rates; deposits and repos fell $550 million to $16.3 billion, with non-interest-bearing at 53.5%. Adjusted efficiency ratio improved to 42.1% from 43.9%, net interest margin was 3.89%, and the company repurchased 775,000 shares for $17.5 million; no explicit forward EPS or revenue guidance was given beyond the 2027 merger targets.

negative_highlights: Gross margin fell 610 bps to 10.0% from 16.1% as note price increases did not fully recover higher wire rod, freight and conversion costs

Net earnings dropped to $7.7 million ($0.40/share) from $14.6 million ($0.74), and management guided that elevated input costs and seasonally lower demand will continue pressuring margins in Q1 FY2027
A 1.3 million-ton U.S. hot-rolled wire rod supply deficit forced offshore purchases after Section 232 tariffs rose to 50% and Canada/Mexico were added, driving inventory to ~3.4 months of shipments
positive_highlights: Net sales rose 17.9% YoY to $209.3 million and average note prices increased 6.6% YoY and 3.3% sequentially on pricing actions
Operating cash flow was $18.2 million in the quarter versus a $17.0 million use a year ago; full-year operating cash rose $36.6 million to $27.2 million
Balance sheet closed with $37.5 million cash and no borrowings on the $100 million revolver, and the company returned $1.12/share in total dividends plus ~114,000 shares repurchased for $3.2 million
summary: Insteel reported Q4 FY2026 net sales of $209.3 million, up 17.9% YoY, but the 14-week quarter inflated the comparison; on a 13-week basis shipments rose only 2.2% YoY and fell 5.4% sequentially. Gross margin contracted 610 bps to 10.0% and net earnings fell to $7.7 million ($0.40/share) from $14.6 million ($0.74), with $700,000 of restructuring charges ($0.03/share). Management said elevated input costs and seasonally lower demand will keep pressuring margins in Q1 FY2027, with support only from a recently announced price increase and savings from the Upper Sandusky closure; fiscal 2027 capex is guided to roughly $30 million, including about $20 million for a new engineered structural mesh line.

negative_highlights: Full-year AFFO guidance held at $1.37-$1.39 despite Q3 AFFO of $0.35; settling 2.4M forward shares added 2.0M-2.3M to the 2026 weighted share count for a $0.025-$0.03 dilutive impact

Cap rates are expected to rise near-term; 10-year Treasury moved from under 4.5% to 5.3% during Q3, and management described the demand side of the transaction market as having 'weakened substantially'

Only 30 bps of average cap-rate expansion was achieved on 10 repriced deals, taking the quarterly blended yield from 7.3% to just 7.4%, with Q4 acquisitions expected to be back-end loaded on pricing uncertainty
positive_highlights: Year-to-date gross investments of $811M at a 7.4% blended cash yield already exceed the $657.1M completed for all of 2025
Occupancy at 99.9% with a single vacant asset, weighted average lease term of 10.1 years, and top-10 tenant concentration down to 29.2% of ABR from 37.9% a year ago
Recurring G&A fell to 9.1% of total revenues from 10.6% in the prior-year quarter, and leverage of 3.7x sits well below the 4.5x-5.5x comfort zone with $1.3B of liquidity
summary: NETSTREIT reported Q3 FY2026 net income of $8.5M ($0.08/share), core FFO of $36.6M ($0.34/share) and AFFO of $37.5M ($0.35/share, up 6.1% YoY). Full-year 2026 AFFO guidance was maintained at $1.37-$1.39, while net investment activity guidance rose to at least $800M from a prior $700M-$800M range. Gross investments of $273.1M closed at a 7.4% blended cash yield, and only 30 bps of repricing was achieved on 10 late-quarter deals as the 10-year moved from under 4.5% to 5.3%. Management flagged that settling 2.4M forward shares in Q3 lifted the 2026 weighted share count by 2.0M-2.3M and created a $0.025-$0.03 dilutive impact that more than offset reduced treasury-stock-method dilution, leaving guidance unchanged.

negative_highlights: Total sales ex-surcharge fell 7% sequentially to ~$656.5M and defense sub-market bookings declined both sequentially and YoY on funding gaps
PEP sales fell 5% YoY and 15% sequentially to $83M on lower medical titanium, with Q2 PEP operating income guided to ~$7M, flat
Free cash flow was negative $24.8M in the quarter as capex of $77.7M and inventory build outran $52.8M of operating cash flow
positive_highlights: Operating income of $196.4M rose 28% YoY to a first-quarter record, with SAO adjusted margin holding at 37.7% despite planned outages
Aerospace distribution and structural bookings rose 23% sequentially and 49% YoY, and total aerospace bookings rose 25% YoY
Management stated volume, productivity and pricing assumptions now carry upside to the FY27 guide, with a reiterated FY29 operating income target of $1.2B-$1.3B and 20%+ CAGR
summary: Carpenter reported Q1 FY27 net sales ex-surcharge of $5.37B-equivalent? No — sales ex-surcharge rose 5% YoY but fell 7% QoQ to ~$656.5M, with operating income of $196.4M (up 28% YoY, down 5% QoQ, a first-quarter record) and diluted EPS of $3.25. SAO adjusted operating margin held at a record-matching 37.7% despite planned maintenance and fewer operating days, and SAO sales rose 7% YoY to $573.5M. Q2 FY27 operating income guidance of $192M-$197M is roughly flat sequentially but implies 24%-27% YoY growth, and management said volume, productivity and pricing assumptions now offer upside to the FY27 guide; FY29 operating income target of ~$1.2-1.3B was reiterated with a stated goal to overachieve. Free cash flow was negative $24.8M on $77.7M of capex, offset by $133.9M of buybacks, and full-year FCF guidance of $400M-$430M was maintained.

negative_highlights: Full-year LIFO expense outlook jumped to $450M from $300M, with Q3 LIFO of $187.5M versus a $75M estimate
Gross margin fell 20 bps sequentially to 27.9% on the higher LIFO and the lower-margin border wall mix
Border wall accounted for 3.7 points of the 4.3% sequential ton growth, and management flagged supply availability as a possible constraint on 2027 organic growth
positive_highlights: Non-GAAP EPS of $8.02 beat guidance of $6.40-$6.60 by a wide margin and rose 120% YoY despite an incremental $1.64/share LIFO headwind versus guidance
Record tons sold rose 4.3% sequentially and 15.6% YoY, outrunning the 10.1% industry increase reported by MSCI
Average note price rose 8.2% QoQ, well above the expected flat-to-up-2%, and FIFO gross margin expanded to 31.6% from 30.5% sequentially and 29% a year ago
summary: Reliance reported record Q3 net sales up 43% YoY and non-GAAP EPS of $8.02, up 120% YoY, crushing its $6.40-$6.60 guidance despite $2.74/share of LIFO expense vs $1.10 guided. Tons sold hit a record, up 4.3% sequentially and 15.6% YoY versus 10.1% industry growth, with average watching price up 8.2% QoQ versus a flat-to-up-2% expectation. Q4 EPS guidance of $7.40-$7.60 includes $112.5M ($1.64/share) of LIFO and ~$0.70 from the border wall. Full-year LIFO outlook rose to $450M from $300M, and gross margin fell 20 bps sequentially to 27.9% on LIFO and border-wall mix, though FIFO margin expanded to 31.6%.

negative_highlights: Advertising revenue declined mid-single digits and health was marginally negative
U.K. organic revenue was negative low single digit and Middle East/Africa declined mid-single digits on conflict
Net interest expense rose to $104 million from $43 million on Interpublic debt, and full-year organic guidance of ~5% implies a Q4 deceleration from 7.2%
positive_highlights: Organic revenue grew 7.2% in Q3 with U.S. up 10% and integrated media up over 10%
Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 200 bps to 18.2% and adjusted EPS rose 22% to $2.73
$900 million cost synergy target on track and $3.2 billion of the $5 billion buyback completed
summary: Core organic revenue grew 7.2% in Q3 (5.8% year to date), with adjusted EBITDA up 21.1% to a 18.2% margin (up 200 bps) and adjusted EPS up 22% to $2.73. Management now guides full-year 2026 organic growth of approximately 5% and expects Q4 margins similar to the 200-210 bps of year-to-date expansion, with $900 million of cost synergies on track. U.S. organic growth of 10% and integrated media up over 10% offset mid-single-digit advertising declines and negative U.K. growth. $3.2 billion of the $5 billion buyback is complete, with the remainder targeted by April 2027.

negative_highlights: Operating profit fell 42% YoY to KRW 250.6 billion (4% margin) as a 6% weaker won/USD rate and chipflation limited ASP management
Revenue declined 10% YoY on reduced mid-sized LCD shipments from portfolio realignment, and IT share of revenue fell 7pp QoQ to 29%
Q4 ASP is guided up only low single digits and management said mobile profitability improvement will be limited relative to volume growth; auto order backlog was not disclosed
positive_highlights: Revenue rose 12% QoQ to KRW 6.277 trillion as large and mobile OLED seasonality began
OLED share of revenue reached a record quarterly 67%, up 10pp QoQ and 2pp YoY
Price per square meter rose 16% QoQ to $1,250 on mobile OLED mix, and net income hit KRW 755.6 billion on FX translation gains
summary: Q3 FY2026 revenue was KRW 6.277 trillion, up 12% QoQ on large and mobile OLED seasonality but down 10% YoY, with mid-sized LCD shipments reduced by a profitability-focused portfolio realignment. Operating profit was KRW 250.6 billion (4% margin), roughly flat QoQ but down 42% YoY as a 6% weaker won/USD rate and chipflation constrained ASPs; net income of KRW 755.6 billion was driven by FX translation gains. Q4 guidance calls for area shipment up about 10% with price per square meter up only low single digits, citing softer consumer demand, chipflation and rising raw material costs; no explicit profit guidance and no update to the auto order backlog, which management declined to disclose.

negative_highlights: Total loans grew only $44 million as commercial balances declined $63 million, driven by accelerated multifamily CRE payoffs above expectations in a competitive market
Net interest margin narrowed to 3.58% from 3.60%, with roughly 2 bps of drag from average cash balances rising to $1.1 billion from $842 million
The low end of operating non-interest expense guidance was raised to $820 million as salaries and benefits rose $5.6 million on higher incentive accruals and recruiting expense
positive_highlights: Operating EPS rose to $0.62 from $0.60 and operating PPNR reached a record $156 million, with operating ROTCE of 15.94% and efficiency ratio at 56.8%
Guidance raised on three fronts: low end of NII up $5 million to $1.125 billion, non-interest income raised to $295-305 million, and provision range lowered to $30-40 million
Net charge-offs fell to 0.14% of average loans from 0.34%, NPAs improved to 0.52% of assets, and wealth management revenue grew more than 9% linked quarter to a record $18.6 billion in AUM/A
summary: Fulton reported Q3 operating EPS of $0.62 versus $0.60 in Q2, with operating net income of $119.8 million and record operating PPNR of $156 million; net interest income rose $5.8 million (~2%) to $290 million while NIM slipped to 3.58% from 3.60% on lower purchase accounting accretion and higher cash balances. Guidance was raised: the low end of NII was lifted $5 million to $1.125 billion, non-interest income was raised to $295-305 million, and the loan loss provision range was lowered to $30-40 million, while the low end of operating expense was raised to $820 million. Deposits grew $571 million to $28.8 billion (customer deposits up roughly $1 billion) as brokered deposits fell $428 million and FHLB advances of $553 million were fully paid off, but loan growth was modest at $44 million as commercial balances fell $63 million on accelerated multifamily CRE payoffs. Net charge-offs improved to 0.14% from 0.34% and the company repurchased $56.1 million of stock at an average of $24.14.

negative_highlights: Subscription revenue growth of only 6% YoY and total revenue growth of 5.9%, still a single-digit growth profile
GAAP EPS of $6.50 was inflated by a $545M non-cash deferred tax valuation allowance release; diluted EPS excluding the benefit was just $0.28
Core UCaaS remains the bulk of the business and AI, while growing fast, is still a small percentage of network traffic and grows off a smaller base
positive_highlights: Full-year guidance raised: non-GAAP EPS to $5.07-$5.12 (up ~17%), free cash flow to $620-630M, and total revenue to $2.650-2.657B
Record non-GAAP operating margin of 24.7% (up ~200 bps) and record GAAP operating margin of 8% (up 320 bps)
RingCentral AI cohort reached ~15% of total ARR or over $400M, doubling year-over-year, with higher ARPU and net retention above 100%
summary: RingCentral reported Q3 FY2026 subscription revenue of ~$653M (up 6% YoY) and total revenue of ~$676M (up 5.9%), both above the high end of guidance. Non-GAAP operating margin reached a record 24.7% (up ~200 bps) and GAAP operating margin hit a record 8% (up 320 bps), while free cash flow rose 21% to $157M. Management raised full-year guidance across subscription revenue ($2.563-2.569B), total revenue ($2.650-2.657B), non-GAAP operating margin (24-24.2%), non-GAAP EPS ($5.07-5.12), and free cash flow ($620-630M). Gross debt was reduced below $1B ahead of schedule, and the RingCentral AI cohort reached ~15% of ARR (~$400M), doubling YoY.

negative_highlights: Organic sales fell 2.8% and reported sales were down $7.1 million, with EPS of $4.64 versus $5.02 (or $4.71 as adjusted) last year
Tools Group organic sales dropped 7% and operating margin contracted 370 bps to 18.0%, with operating income down to $84.8 million from $109.9 million
RS&I organic sales declined 5.5% on sharply lower OEM program activity tied to reduced new-vehicle launches, and management described visibility on program timing as limited
positive_highlights: C&I organic sales rose 7.4% to a record $404.3 million, with operating income up 29.9% to $74.7 million and a segment-record 18.5% operating margin, up 290 bps
Consolidated gross margin was 51.0%, up 10 bps year-over-year, attributable to RCI savings offsetting higher material costs
RS&I gross margin improved 110 bps to 48.1% and adjusted operating margin held roughly flat (down only 10 bps) despite a 5.5% organic sales decline
summary: Snap-on reported Q3 FY2026 net sales of $1,183.7 million, up 0.6% as reported but down 2.8% organically, short of prior-year levels as diesel-price turbulence drove franchisee van destocking. EPS fell to $4.64 from $5.02, though the prior year included a $0.31 legal-settlement benefit; gross margin held at 51.0%, up 10 bps. C&I was the bright spot with sales of $404.3 million (7.4% organic), OI up 29.9% to $74.7 million and a record 18.5% margin. Tools Group organic sales fell 7% and RS&I fell 5.5%; management gave no formal full-year revenue or EPS guidance beyond capex (~$100 million) and a ~22% tax rate.

negative_highlights: Net charge-offs rose to 28 bp of average loans from 17 bp, driven by a single C&I loan charge-off, with YTD 20 bp at the high end of guidance
Allowance coverage declined to 1.13% from 1.16% as C&I growth carries a higher reserve than CRE
Non-accrual loans rose to 0.96% of total loans on migration of a single construction (land) loan; CRE concentration at 312% remains above the sub-300% target
positive_highlights: NIM expanded ahead of the 5-7 bp quarterly guide, with September exit margin at 3.33% and Q4 expansion guided to another 5-7 bp
Efficiency ratio fell below 50%, its lowest since Q3 2021 and a quarter ahead of schedule
Core customer deposits rose $1.1 billion and criticized/classified loans fell to 7.1% of loans from 8.8% a year ago
summary: Valley National reported Q3 2026 results that put it at the high end of full-year guidance ranges, with NIM expanding beyond the 5-7 bp guide (September exit margin 3.33%) and the efficiency ratio falling below 50% a quarter ahead of schedule. Core deposits grew $1.1 billion, CRE concentration fell to 312% from 317%, and criticized/classified loans declined to 7.1% from 8.8% a year ago. Offsets included net charge-offs rising to 28 bp from 17 bp on a single C&I loan and an expected Q4 normalization of tax credit advisory and fintech valuation benefits; NII guidance remains the high end of 11-13% and a 2027 loan growth framework of 4-6% was floated.

negative_highlights: Fuel expense grew 69% on average price per gallon rising from $2.56 to $4.21, adding 140 bps to the operating ratio
Pricing gains were masked by business mix, with nearly 75% of volume growth from intermodal, leaving freight revenue ex-fuel up only 6%
Coal and renewables volume declined 3%, with lower natural gas prices and elevated inventories cited as continuing challenges
positive_highlights: Adjusted EPS grew 15% to $3.53 on 6% volume growth, and core operating ratio improved 110 bps excluding fuel and merger costs
Freight revenue ex-fuel rose 6% to a record $5.6 billion; domestic intermodal delivered a fifth consecutive record quarter with 13% volume growth
Ninth consecutive quarter of record workforce productivity, with 1% lower headcount against 6% volume growth, and the dividend raised 3% for a 20th consecutive year
summary: Union Pacific reported Q3 FY2026 record revenue of $7.2 billion, up 15%, with freight revenue of $6.8 billion up 15% on 6% volume growth; adjusted EPS rose 15% to $3.53 (reported $3.49) and the operating ratio was 58.8%, with core OR improving 110 bps excluding fuel and merger costs. Management affirmed its 2026 outlook of reported EPS growth in the high single digits and continued core operating ratio improvement, while fuel prices (expected ~$4.85/gal in Q4) remain a headwind; capital spend was raised to $3.5 billion for 2026. Volume growth was heavily skewed to intermodal (nearly 75% of growth), which masked pricing contribution, and freight revenue ex-fuel grew 6%. The Norfolk Southern merger remains on track with a procedural schedule targeting a close in the second half of 2027.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to $47M ($1.76/share) from $28M ($1.10) a year ago, including ~$14M of Monterrey restructuring charges
Adjusted EBITDA declined to $9M from $13M YoY on lower realized pricing
Production fell 19% sequentially to ~27,000 mt with utilization of 64%, and preliminary U.S. antidumping determinations on India were below expectations
positive_highlights: Q4 realized pricing expected up mid-single-digit percent, with a step change higher in 2027 as higher-priced commitments flow through
Monterrey closure expected to deliver ~$20M-$25M annual cash cost savings, ~$5M lower annual capex, and ~$20M-$25M working capital release
Adjusted free cash flow improved to -$16M from -$75M in Q2, with $242M total liquidity and no debt maturities until December 2029
summary: GrafTech reported Q3 FY2026 net sales of $140M, down ~3% YoY, on realized pricing of ~$3,900/mt (down ~7% YoY, flat QoQ), and a net loss of $47M ($1.76/share) versus a $28M loss ($1.10) a year ago, which included ~$14M of Monterrey closure charges. Adjusted EBITDA fell to $9M from $13M, and adjusted free cash flow was -$16M, improved from -$75M in Q2. Sales volume of ~29,000 mt was flat YoY but up ~7% YTD, with full-year volume growth guidance of 5%-10% and a low-single-digit cash COGS per ton decline maintained. Management guided to a mid-single-digit realized price increase in Q4 and a 'step change' higher in 2027, backed by the March and September price increases and a ~$20M-$25M annual cost saving from closing Monterrey, though initial U.S. antidumping preliminary determinations on India were disappointing.

negative_highlights: Q3 non-interest income declined 7.6% QoQ to KRW 581.4bn on securities valuation losses and a sharp drop in capital market fees
Card delinquency rate rose on higher write-offs, which management attributed partly to rate-cycle pressure on vulnerable customers
positive_highlights: Net income of KRW 1,049.2bn exceeded KRW 1 trillion for a second consecutive quarter, up 4.4% QoQ
CET1 ratio at 13.8%, up ~90 bps YTD and 170 bps over two years, with management citing ~13.95% on an adjusted basis
Q3 credit costs fell 28.5% QoQ to KRW 314bn and the YTD credit cost ratio declined to 42 bps
summary: Woori Financial reported Q3 FY2026 net income of KRW 1,049.2bn, up 4.4% QoQ and above KRW 1 trillion for a second straight quarter; YTD net income of KRW 2,658.1bn was up 19% YoY excluding last year's ~KRW 550bn bargain purchase gains. YTD net operating revenue hit a record KRW 8,680.3bn (+6.2% YoY) and CET1 rose ~90 bps this year to 13.8%, with Q3 credit costs falling 28.5% QoQ to KRW 314bn. Offsets: bank NIM fell 7 bps QoQ to 1.43% on funding-cost and CD-linked loan spread pressure, and Q3 non-interest income dropped 7.6% QoQ to KRW 581.4bn on securities valuation losses. Management guided NIM to stop declining in Q4, reaffirmed the 15% credit-cost reduction target (low-40bp ratio), and signaled a nominal TSR above 50% for 2027.

negative_highlights: Total revenue declined 3.9% YoY to $2.8 billion on a 10.6% drop in billable expenses
Civil revenue fell 15% YoY and is now guided to a low-double-digit decline for the year, softer than the prior high-single-digit expectation
Second-half margins are guided to step down on lower civil volumes and the timing of investment spending
positive_highlights: Adjusted EPS rose 18% YoY to $1.76, and the full-year adjusted EPS range was raised to $6.50-$6.70
Funded backlog increased 5% YoY to $5.7 billion, with national security funded backlog up 10%; book-to-bill was 1.5x
Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 10 bps to 11.3%, and free cash flow was $263 million in the quarter
summary: Revenue declined 3.9% YoY to $2.8 billion, driven by a 10.6% drop in billable expenses; revenue ex-billables fell less than 1%, national security grew 1% (6% ex-billables) while civil fell 15%. Adjusted EBITDA was $313 million at an 11.3% margin, up 10 bps, and adjusted EPS rose 18% YoY to $1.76, aided by a $10 million DARPA earn-out and a lower tax rate. FY27 guidance now calls for revenue of $11.3-$11.6 billion (1%-3% growth) with the bottom end of adjusted EBITDA raised to a $1.26-$1.29 billion range and adjusted EPS raised to $6.50-$6.70; civil is now guided to a low-double-digit decline versus the prior high-single-digit expectation. Book-to-bill was 1.5x, total backlog rose 2% to nearly $41 billion, and funded backlog rose 5% to $5.7 billion.

negative_highlights: Revenue came in ~$35M below the beginning-of-quarter forecast; automotive sales fell to $552.5M from $573.7M, with units down ~1M
Gross margin fell 100 bps to 33.4% and full-year revenue guidance was lowered to ~$2.65B with FY gross margin of 34%-34.5%; management flagged 2027 gross margin likely in the 33%-34% range
Electronic component costs are up 8x-10x on some parts, Q4 carries $10-15M of unrecovered cost with recovery delayed to H1 2027, and CFO cash flow fell to $83.5M from $147M on working capital
positive_highlights: Premium audio revenue rose ~27% to $54.7M and non-automotive reached 15% of total revenue vs 12% a year ago
Automotive revenue excluding China and VW headwinds grew ~2% against a global light vehicle production decline of more than 2%, with Europe ex-VW up ~13%
Repurchased 5.7M shares for $132.6M in Q3 (11.6M shares / $270.2M year to date), and secured a first PCBA award annualized at roughly $180M
summary: Q3 net sales were $647.7M vs $655.2M a year ago, roughly $35M below the beginning-of-quarter forecast due to customer launch delays and the Hyundai-Kia strike; diluted EPS fell to $0.43 from $0.46 (adjusted EPS flat at $0.47). Gross margin contracted to 33.4% from 34.4% on higher precious metals costs, unfavorable mix, and lost operating leverage. Full-year 2026 revenue guidance was cut to ~$2.65B with gross margin of 34%-34.5%, a range that embeds $10-15M of incremental Q4 component costs with recoveries not expected until H1 2027, while the 2027 revenue outlook of $2.8-2.9B was maintained.

negative_highlights: Non-interest income decreased $600,000 sequentially on lower mortgage gain-on-sale and bank fees
Allowance coverage slipped to 74 bps from 75 bps while a $600,000 provision was taken on higher loan volume
Mortgage production was described as having 'fallen off a cliff' nationally amid higher rates
positive_highlights: Net income of ~$6 million ($0.60 per diluted share) was up 88% from Q3 2025
Net interest margin expanded 5 bps QoQ to 2.95% and 41 bps YoY, with new loan production yielding 6.79% versus 6.26% on payoffs
Non-performing asset ratio fell to 39 bps and the efficiency ratio improved to 72% from 74% prior quarter
summary: First Western reported Q3 FY2026 net income of about $6 million, or $0.60 per diluted share, both up 88% year over year, with pre-tax pre-provision net income up 15% sequentially and 27% YoY. NIM rose 5 bps QoQ to 2.95% and 41 bps YoY, loans held for investment grew $95 million (sixth consecutive quarterly increase, +8% YoY), deposits rose 2.5% QoQ, and the efficiency ratio improved to 72% from 74%. Management offered only qualitative Q4 guidance, expecting further improvement, continued NIM expansion, and a path to 1% ROA during 2027; no formal numeric guidance was raised. Non-interest income fell $600,000 QoQ on lower mortgage gains and bank fees, partly offset by a 2.6% rise in trust and investment management fees.

negative_highlights: Core FFO per share of $0.60 was flat YoY and declined $0.03 sequentially on timing of redeploying proceeds
Cash leasing spreads expected to average negative low-to-mid teens over the next couple of years as 2022-2023 peak leases reset
Total portfolio occupancy of ~91% remains well below the 96%-97% same property level, with a $40 million NOI lease-up gap
positive_highlights: Full-year Core FFO per share guidance midpoint raised $0.02 to $2.41-$2.44, the third consecutive increase
Same property occupancy rose 200 bps sequentially to ~97%, with 3.7 million sq ft leased (second highest ever) and ~87% of expiring space renewed or backfilled
3000000 sq ft of repositioning/development leases signed contributing $14 million of annualized NOI once commenced
summary: Rexford reported Q3 FY2026 Core FFO of $0.60 per share, flat YoY and down $0.03 QoQ on the timing of redeploying disposition proceeds. Management raised the full-year Core FFO per share midpoint by $0.02 to $2.41-$2.44, lifted Same Property NOI growth outlook by 75 bps at the midpoint on net effective and cash basis, and raised average same property occupancy by 40 bps to 95.9%. The company closed $1.3 billion of dispositions, including a $1.2 billion 22-property sale at an estimated 2027 cash NOI yield of ~5.5%, leaving $500 million remaining in the $2 billion realignment. Leverage fell to 3.8x, $425 million of 2027 maturities were repaid, and $409 million of stock was repurchased in and since Q3.

negative_highlights: $0.51 per-share legal reserve tied to the OCC civil money penalty and an unrelated matter settlement
$336 million restructuring charge with ~5% of global positions eliminated
Commercial spend up just 3% (5% ex-co-brand exits) and international spend decelerated from 13% to 11%
positive_highlights: Adjusted EPS of $4.68 up 13% YoY; EPS guidance raised to $18.30-$18.60 reported / $17.60-$17.90 adjusted
Net card fees grew 17% FX-adjusted, the fastest-growing revenue line, and T&E spend rose 10% with airline up 13%
Returns: $2.2 billion returned to shareholders ($1.6 billion buyback, $0.6 billion dividends); ROE roughly 35%
summary: Revenue rose 9% to $20.1 billion (about a point higher ex-co-brand exits), with net card fees accelerating to 17% FX-adjusted. GAAP EPS of $5.42 included a $1.11 GBTG gain; adjusted EPS of $4.68 rose 13% and absorbed a $0.51 legal reserve (including the OCC penalty) offset by a $0.29 tax benefit and $0.24 CECL benefit. Guidance: 10% revenue growth reaffirmed and EPS guidance raised to $18.30-$18.60 reported / $17.60-$17.90 adjusted. The quarter also carried a $336 million restructuring charge (~5% of positions eliminated); credit remained strong with write-offs up only 3% on 8% balance growth.

negative_highlights: $100 million SOFR swap at 2.05% rolls up about 150 bps in January 2027, with a $60 million swap also expiring
Two loans totaling $17.9 million repaid early, cutting interest income and pushing the loan book below its ~20% target, so Q4 run rate steps down to about $0.53 before acquisitions
Pro forma leverage rises to roughly 7.3x from the mid-6x level to fund the industrial deal
positive_highlights: AFFO per diluted share grew 19.6% YoY to $0.55 with no one-time or non-recurring income in the quarter
FY2026 AFFO guidance raised to $2.20-$2.22 from $2.12-$2.15 (midpoint roughly 17% YoY growth)
Pending $117.3 million industrial acquisition adds roughly 1.9 million sq ft with a 10.2-year WALT and no expirations before late 2031
summary: Alpine reported Q3 FY2026 total revenue of $20.5 million, with FFO and AFFO both $0.55 per diluted share, up about 20% YoY (AFFO/share +19.6%), and raised FY2026 AFFO guidance to $2.20-$2.22 from $2.12-$2.15 and FFO to $2.19-$2.21 from $2.10-$2.13. The raise is driven by an increased investment volume assumption of $310-$350 million, with closed and under-contract investments YTD exceeding $300 million (a record vs FY2025's $277 million), including a pending $117.3 million, 13-property industrial portfolio acquisition at roughly an 8.5% yield and $63/sq ft. Occupancy was 99.6% with a WALT of 8.7 years; a new $100 million four-year term loan plus a $75 million revolver upsize adds $175 million of liquidity and lifts leverage to roughly 7.3x pro forma.

negative_highlights: Direct premiums written grew just 2.7% to $608.9 million, with Florida down 3.3%
Net expense ratio rose 0.2 points to 26.4% on higher policy acquisition costs outside Florida and higher operating costs
Hurricane Isaias struck the western Florida Panhandle after quarter end, adding Q4 catastrophe exposure
positive_highlights: Adjusted diluted EPS of $1.93 versus $1.36 in the prior year quarter
Net combined ratio improved 5.4 points to 91.0%, with the net loss ratio down 5.6 points to 64.6%
Annualized return on common equity of 32.7% with policies in force up 8%
summary: Adjusted diluted EPS rose to $1.93 from $1.36 a year ago on core revenue of $444.3 million, up 11.1% YoY, with net premiums earned up 12.1% to $403.2 million. The net combined ratio improved 5.4 points to 91.0% as the net loss ratio fell 5.6 points to 64.6%, partly offset by a 0.2-point rise in the net expense ratio to 26.4%. Direct premiums written grew only 2.7% to $608.9 million, with 18.5% growth in other states offset by a 3.3% decline in Florida; annualized ROE was 32.7% and policies in force grew 8%. No explicit forward guidance was given; management flagged post-quarter Hurricane Isaias as manageable based on claims activity to date and noted the buyback authorization has about 1.1 million shares remaining.

negative_highlights: Net loss of $0.90 per share in Q3 versus net income of $0.44 in Q2
Book value declined to $6.02 per share from $7.22 at June 30, with total return of -12.5% for the quarter
Leverage rose to 8.6x from 7.3x while liquidity fell to 44% from 54%
positive_highlights: Book value up approximately 4.5% month-to-date through October 22 inclusive of the dividend accrual
Repurchased 6.62 million shares since the end of Q2, with shares trading at more than a 20% discount to estimated current book value
Unwound the three-month into five-year payer swaption near max value for a realized return of roughly 200% on premium paid
summary: Orchid Island Capital reported a Q3 net loss of $0.90 per share versus net income of $0.44 in Q2, with book value falling to $6.02 from $7.22 and total return of -12.5% versus +6.2% in Q2. The loss was driven by the late-quarter rates watch-off and mortgage basis widening; leverage rose to 8.6x from 7.3x and liquidity fell to 44% from 54%, though three-month CPR declined to 8.4% from 10.9%. Management kept the $0.30 dividend unchanged and said taxable income is roughly in line with the pay rate, and noted book value has rebounded about 4.5% month-to-date through October 22. The company repurchased 6.62 million shares since quarter-end Q2 at a discount to book and intends a mix of further buybacks and reinvesting paydowns, with leverage now at 8.12x.

negative_highlights: Net interest margin declined 4 bps to 3.62% as deposit costs rose 8 bps; CFO conceded they 'underestimated deposit pricing in Q3'
Operating non-interest income fell 16% ($5.2 million) linked quarter on weaker retirement-benefit investment income and non-recurring Q2 loan-sale gains
Management flagged that elevated deposit competition and higher rates may slow the pace of loan and earnings growth in 2027, with loan closings already slower than anticipated
positive_highlights: Record operating net income of $111 million, or $0.51 per diluted share, up 50% from a year ago
Operating efficiency ratio improved to 47.5% as non-interest expense fell 5% linked quarter, producing positive operating leverage
Net charge-offs fell to 9 bps from 17 bps and NPLs improved $24.6 million to 36 bps of loans; $89.1 million of capital returned via dividends and buybacks
summary: Eastern reported record operating net income of $111 million, or $0.51 per diluted share, up 4% linked quarter and 50% year over year, on total revenue of $306.6 million (+1% QoQ). Net interest margin fell 4 bps to 3.62% as higher deposit costs more than offset asset repricing, and non-interest income dropped 16% linked quarter to $5.2 million on weaker retirement-benefit investment income. Expenses fell 5% QoQ and credit improved with net charge-offs of 9 bps versus 17 bps in Q2. Full-year 2026 guidance was unchanged from July, with NIM expected stable in Q4 and to modestly improve into 2027, though management said higher rates may slow loan growth and earnings into 2027; new guidance comes in January.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EPS of $0.64 fell $0.05 year-on-year, and GAAP results included a $0.12 ($187M) non-cash pension settlement charge plus $0.03 of ChampionX merger charges
Q4 revenue guidance of ~$10B hinges on assumed flat Middle East activity (~$1.9B, only 83% of Q1 2025 levels), with management flagging continued geopolitical uncertainty
All Other pre-tax operating income declined on ramp-up costs for new data center projects; Kelvion closing not expected until first half of 2027
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 5% sequentially to $9.45B with all four divisions and every geography expanding; adjusted EBITDA margin up 71 bps to 21.9%
Middle East revenue rebounded 13% sequentially to $1.9B, and Saudi Aramco awarded four integrated Well Construction contracts covering more than 450 wells over an initial three-year term

Digital revenue up 11% year to date with full-year adjusted EBITDA margin expected above 35%; ChampionX delivered its highest quarterly revenue and margin since acquisition, with margins up a fourth consecutive quarter
summary: SLB reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $9.45B, up 5% sequentially, with adjusted EPS of $0.64, up $0.09 sequentially but down $0.05 year-on-year. Adjusted EBITDA margin was 21.9%, up 71 bps sequentially, and pre-tax segment operating margin rose 104 bps with expansion across all four divisions; Middle East revenue recovered 13% sequentially to $1.9B. Q4 guidance calls for revenue of approximately $10B (up 5-7% sequentially) and adjusted EBITDA margin expansion of 100-150 bps, assuming Middle East revenue stays flat. For 2027, management assumes a flat Middle East and mid-single-digit global OFS market growth, with SLB expected to outperform, though no formal 2027 guidance was given.

negative_highlights: Deposit costs are expected to drift higher as the Fed hikes, with a 20-25% deposit beta that could eat into the recent 10-12 bp quarterly margin lift
Loan growth is guided to low-to-mid single digits and Q4 enters a seasonally slower period
Core operating expenses of $190.8 million came in at the high end of the $187-192 million guide, with management flagging continued caution on expenses
positive_highlights: Net interest margin reached 4.01%, up 11 bps QoQ and 62 bps YoY, the 11th consecutive quarter of margin expansion
Non-interest-bearing deposits rose $279 million or 15% annualized to $7.7 billion, 30% of total deposits, while total deposits grew 10% annualized
Record net income of $105 million, up 54% YoY, with efficiency ratio improving to 56.08% and ROA rising to 1.31%
summary: Glacier reported record quarterly net income of $105 million, up 7% QoQ and 54% YoY, with diluted EPS of $0.80 and operating EPS of $0.81. Tax-equivalent NIM expanded 11 bps QoQ and 62 bps YoY to 4.01%, marking an 11th consecutive quarter of margin expansion, on net interest income of $290 million (up 5% QoQ, 29% YoY) and total deposits of $25.3 billion (up 10% annualized QoQ). Credit stayed clean with net charge-offs of $6 million and NPAs at 0.28% of subsidiary assets. Guidance is supportive: management reiterated low-to-mid single-digit loan growth, kept the Q4 expense guide at $187-192 million (high end), pointed to further margin expansion through 2027 from ~$3.5 billion of loans repricing 125-150 bps higher, and said buybacks and special dividends are now in scope.

negative_highlights: Wireless service revenue fell 1% and mobile phone ARPU dropped 2.6% to CAD 55.22, predominantly from the CRTC fee prohibition with more cost-recovery work still to do
Total mobile phone net adds were just 17,000 (6,000 postpaid) as industry net adds fell an estimated 30-40% YoY in Q3
Postpaid churn rose 4 bps YoY to 1.03% following a substantial in-quarter price action, with possible carryover into Q4
positive_highlights: Free cash flow rose 65% YoY to roughly CAD 1.4 billion in the quarter and 34% YTD to over CAD 3.1 billion on a 46% capex cut
Adjusted EBITDA margins expanded in all three segments: wireless +130 bps to 68%, cable +40 bps to 59%, with media EBITDA up 12% to CAD 84 million
Incoming ARPU for customers added in Q3 and October is up 8% YoY, and leverage improved 0.1x sequentially to 3.7x
summary: Rogers reported Q3 FY2026 consolidated service revenue and adjusted EBITDA each up 1%, with wireless service revenue down 1% and mobile phone ARPU down 2.6% to CAD 55.22 largely from the CRTC fee prohibition, while cable service revenue grew for a sixth consecutive quarter (+1% organic) and media revenue rose 9% with EBITDA up 12%. Margins expanded across all three segments (wireless +130 bps to 68%, cable +40 bps to 59%), capex fell 46% to CAD 524 million driving capital intensity to 9.6%, and free cash flow rose 65% to roughly CAD 1.4 billion with leverage improving to 3.7x. The full-year 2026 outlook was reaffirmed (service revenue +3-5%, EBITDA +1-3%, capex CAD 2.5-2.7 billion, FCF CAD 4.1-4.3 billion), and the minority sale of consolidated sports assets is targeted for H1 2027. The key negative versus prior periods is wireless: total mobile phone net adds of only 17,000 (6,000 postpaid), market net adds down an estimated 30-40% YoY, and postpaid churn up 4 bps to 1.03%.

Byline reported record net income of $41.8 million ($0.94/diluted share), up from $40.2 million ($0.90) in Q2 and roughly 15% YoY on EPS, with record revenue of $121 million (+3% QoQ). NIM expanded 5 bps to 4.33% (up 10 bps ex-accretion), deposits grew 8.5% annualized to $8 billion, but loans fell ~1% to $7.5 billion as $396 million of payoffs outpaced $362 million of originations. Q4 guidance calls for flat loan balances, NII of $103-105 million, non-interest income of $14-15 million (down on a one-time BOLI item) and expenses of $62-64 million, with full-year efficiency at or below 50%. Management also announced the Illinois State Bancorp acquisition and expects to cross $10 billion in 2027.

negative_highlights: Over-90-day NPL rose to 4.6% from 4.3% in the prior quarter and 4.1% a year earlier, with half the increase from FGI/FGO portfolios and ~10 bps from John Deere Bank seasonality
NII net of provisions was nearly flat as cost of credit rose, and full-year guidance of BRL 42-48 billion is tracking at the low end
Management flagged continued pressure on cost of risk and over-90 NPL in rural individuals/SMEs, personal loans and credit cards, with no curve inflection expected until Q2/Q3 of next year
positive_highlights: Loan portfolio reached BRL 1.15 trillion, up 11.1% year-over-year, with large corporates growing 14.8% and private payroll loans up 102% year-over-year
Total NII grew 14% year-over-year and 2.4% quarter-over-quarter, with fee income, insurance premiums and liability NII all expanding
Completed a BRL 10 billion capital increase, with CET1 at 12.1% and Tier 1 at 13.7%
summary: Bradesco reported Q3 FY2026 with a loan portfolio of BRL 1.15 trillion, up 11.1% year-over-year and 1.1% quarter-over-quarter, with NII up 14% year-over-year and 2.4% quarter-over-quarter and fee income growing. However, the over-90-day NPL rose from 4.3% to 4.6% in the quarter (from 4.1% a year ago), half of the increase attributed to FGI/FGO guaranteed portfolios, and NII net of provisions was described as almost flat due to higher cost of credit. Management said the full-year NII net of provisions guidance of BRL 42-48 billion will land in the lower range, with performance 'within expected.' The bank completed a BRL 10 billion capital increase, ending with CET1 of 12.1%, and management guided to a higher NIM and client NII in Q4 while flagging continued pressure on cost of risk.

negative_highlights: A $2.1 million reversal of interest income reduced reported NIM to 3.49% from 3.60% excluding the item
Loans decreased $14 million in the quarter after a large credit was placed in held-for-sale status
Nonaccrual resolution is slower than expected, with several credits stuck in court proceedings delayed to 3Q-4Q next year; classified loans were $177.6 million including $11.5 million OREO
positive_highlights: Deposits grew $77 million, or 1.2% linked-quarter, with the quarter-end balance cited as a good launch point into Q4
Non-interest expense fell on lower legal and incentive accruals, with Q4 guided to $23-24 million
Total deposit cost declined 3 basis points to 3.06% for September despite a difficult rate environment
summary: Preferred Bank reported Q3 FY2026 net income of $32.9 million, or $2.73 per share, with results dinged by a $2.1 million reversal of interest income that cut reported NIM to 3.49% versus 3.60% excluding the adjustment. Deposits grew $77 million (1.2% linked-quarter) but loans fell $14 million after a large credit was moved to held-for-sale, and nonaccrual resolution slipped as court proceedings pushed recoveries into 3Q-4Q next year. Management guided Q4 expense to $23-24 million and said the loan pipeline is solid for Q4 growth, while flagging a persistently competitive deposit market extending into 2027.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined 1.5% YoY and EBITDA margin fell 614 bps YoY to 20.6% on lower lenalidomide sales
North America generics revenue fell 29% YoY to $264 million and PSAI fell 19% YoY on lower API volume uptake
Europe declined 6% YoY on generic price erosion and NRT model change; input cost inflation (KSM, solvents, freight) is expected to persist at roughly 100 bps of EBITDA drag into Q3 and Q4
positive_highlights: Base business excluding lenalidomide delivered double-digit growth, with India up 17% YoY and emerging markets up 24% YoY
Gross margin recovered 562 bps sequentially to 52.1%, helped by new launches (sugammadex, bosentan, nivolumab) and a 53%-of-revenue branded/consumer mix
Semaglutide API scale-up issue described as solved with validation on track for a November 2026 relaunch, backed by existing orders and 89 approved markets
summary: Revenue fell 1.5% YoY to INR 8,671 crore ($905 million) but rose 7.4% QoQ; EBITDA margin was 20.6%, down 614 bps YoY, and gross margin 52.1% fell 254 bps YoY, both driven by the loss of lenalidomide sales. North America generics revenue dropped 29% YoY to $264 million while the base business excluding lenalidomide grew double digits; India grew 17% and emerging markets 24%, while Europe fell 6% and PSAI fell 19%. Management gave no formal numeric guidance but said gross margin stays in the 50-55% band, EBITDA of 20%+ is sustainable with a 25% target, R&D returns to 7-8% of sales, and semaglutide relaunch is expected in November 2026 pending validation. Profit after tax was INR 925 crore at a 10.7% margin with diluted EPS of INR 11.1.

negative_highlights: Adjusted non-interest income fell $11 million sequentially, driven by a $37 million swing in warrant income from valuation adjustments.
Management cautioned Q3's exceptional loan growth will moderate, with utilization at ~40% expected to normalize.
Replacing the FDIC Purchase Money Note with FHLB/brokered/debt funding is acknowledged as a marginal NIM drag; prepayments guided to $3.5-4 billion per quarter through 2027.
positive_highlights: Loans rose $6.2 billion (4.1%) sequentially, led by fund banking up $4.4 billion (11%), and Q4 loan guidance was raised to $158-161 billion.
Deposits grew $11.8 billion period-end (6.8%), including ~$4.9 billion from the BMO branch acquisition and $3.2 billion of direct bank inflows.
Full-year NII guidance raised to $6.68-6.75 billion and non-interest income to $2.22-2.26 billion; net charge-off ratio improved 2 bps to 0.27%, beating guidance.
summary: First Citizens reported Q3 FY2026 adjusted net income of $652 million and adjusted EPS of $55.37, with ROE of 12.24% and ROA of 1.08%. Loans grew $6.2 billion (4.1%) sequentially and deposits $11.8 billion (6.8%), aided by roughly $4.9 billion of BMO branch deposits. Management raised Q4 loan guidance to $158-161 billion and full-year NII guidance to $6.68-6.75 billion and non-interest income to $2.22-2.26 billion, while tightening full-year net charge-off guidance to 29-31 bps. Net charge-offs fell 2 bps to 0.27%, nonaccrual loans declined $80 million to 0.87% of loans, and $600 million of buybacks brought CET1 to 10.24%, within target range.

negative_highlights: Gross margin percentage was flat at 24.8% and electrical segment margins slipped to 24.3% from 26.2% on a higher equipment/material cost mix and ~$12 million of higher acquisition purchase adjustments
Same-store revenue growth is guided to decelerate from mid-40% in 2026 to mid-20% in 2027
CFO Bill George is retiring, with Julie Shaeff promoted as successor shortly after 2026 results are reported
positive_highlights: Revenue rose 54% YoY to $3.8 billion with electrical segment revenue up 85% and mechanical up 43%
Backlog reached a record $17.8 billion, up $8.4 billion or 90% YoY and 27% sequentially, the eighth consecutive sequential increase
Operating income grew 65% to $625 million and EBITDA rose 61% to $668 million, with quarterly free cash flow of $806 million
summary: Comfort Systems reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $3.8 billion, up 54% YoY, with electrical segment revenue up 85% and mechanical up 43%. EPS reached $13.91 versus $8.25 a year ago, operating margin expanded to 16.6% from 15.5%, and EBITDA rose 61% to $668 million with quarterly free cash flow of $806 million. Backlog hit a record $17.8 billion, up 90% YoY and 27% sequentially, and management guided to mid-40% same-store revenue growth for full-year 2026 and mid-20% for 2027, alongside a $0.10 dividend increase to $1.00 per share and active share repurchases. The main blemish was a sequential gross margin slip driven by a higher equipment/material cost mix and roughly $12 million of higher acquisition purchase adjustments, plus a CFO transition with Bill George retiring and Julie Shaeff named successor.

negative_highlights: Adjusted non-interest income declined $11 million sequentially, driven by a $37 million swing in warrant income
Replacing the FDIC Purchase Money Note with FHLB, brokered, and debt funding carries a higher marginal cost than the note, a drag management expects to offset with asset yields
Share repurchases are expected to moderate to about $300 million in Q4 from $600 million in Q3 now that CET1 is inside the target range
positive_highlights: Period-end deposits grew $11.8 billion, or 6.8% sequentially, with the BMO branch acquisition contributing about $4.9 billion
Fund banking loans expanded $4.4 billion, or 11% sequentially, and innovation banking loans rose 6.6% to $10.1 billion
Net charge-off ratio improved 2 bps to 0.27%, the lowest since Q1 2023, and full-year NCO guidance was tightened to 29-31 bps
summary: First Citizens reported Q3 FY2026 adjusted net income of $652 million and adjusted EPS of $55.37, with ROE of 12.24% and ROA of 1.08%. Loans rose $6.2 billion (4.1%) sequentially to lead a period of strong balance sheet expansion, while period-end deposits grew $11.8 billion (6.8%), including roughly $4.9 billion from the BMO branch acquisition. Management raised Q4 loan guidance to $158-$161 billion, raised full-year NII guidance to $6.68-$6.75 billion, and raised full-year non-interest income guidance to $2.22-$2.26 billion, while tightening full-year net charge-off guidance to 29-31 bps. The quarter also included $600 million of buybacks that brought CET1 to 10.24%, within the target range, implying a moderation in repurchase pace ahead.

negative_highlights: Full-year loan growth guidance cut to 1%-2% from 3%-4% after total loans declined $115M on unexpected CRE payoffs
Net charge-offs of $21.9M (60 bps) included a $12.5M partial charge-off of a downtown Seattle office loan; criticized assets rose 72 bps
Non-performing assets and 90-day past dues rose to 45 bps of loans, partly from operational issues from the residential mortgage servicing outsourcing
positive_highlights: NIM expanded 5 bps to 3.30%, lifting NII to $174.1M, up $3.1M linked quarter, with deposit costs down 3 bps
Full-year NIM outlook raised to 3.26%-3.27% and Q4 NIM guided to 3.34%-3.35%; spot NIM was 333 bps in September
Full-year non-interest expense outlook lowered to $510M-$515M, with Q3 operating expenses below expectations excluding merger and tax items
summary: First Hawaiian reported Q3 FY2026 NII of $174.1M, up $3.1M linked quarter, with NIM of 3.30% (+5 bps QoQ) and non-interest income of $56.1M, in line with outlook. Non-interest expense of $160M included $6.7M merger costs and a $24.3M California tax settlement, more than offset by a $31M tax benefit. Management cut the full-year loan growth outlook to 1%-2% from 3%-4% after total loans fell $115M on unexpected CRE payoffs, while raising the full-year NIM outlook to 3.26%-3.27% and lowering the expense outlook to $510M-$515M. Credit noise included $21.9M of net charge-offs (60 bps) driven by a $12.5M Seattle office partial charge-off and a 72 bps rise in criticized assets.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA margin contracted 7.4 percentage points to 60.3% and Mexico EBITDA fell 10% on softer traffic
Mexico traffic declined nearly 5% and U.S.-Mexico, Europe and South America passenger volumes fell 14.9%, 14.4% and 7.9% respectively; management said winter schedules are not encouraging
Net debt to LTM EBITDA jumped to 2.6x from 0.2x following the acquisition financing
positive_highlights: Revenues rose nearly 13% to MXN 7.8 billion, with non-aeronautical revenues up just under 27% including MXN 456 million from U.S. operations and MXN 362 million from Brazil and Others
Colombia traffic grew just over 5% and Colombia commercial revenue per passenger reached MXN 65.2 with double-digit growth
Two extraordinary dividends of MXN 10 per share each payable November 30 and December 23, and the $1.8 billion Cancún senior notes refinancing extended average debt maturities by seven years
summary: ASUR reported Q3 FY2026 revenues up nearly 13% to MXN 7.8 billion, aided by the first month of CPC Aeroportos consolidation and U.S. commercial operations, but consolidated adjusted EBITDA rose only 1.7% to MXN 4.7 billion and the adjusted EBITDA margin fell 7.4 percentage points to 60.3%. Total traffic declined 1.2% to 20.9 million passengers as Mexico traffic fell nearly 5% on weaker Cancún international demand, while Colombia grew over 5% and Brazil and Others added nearly 4 million passengers in September. Management guided no near-term improvement, noting airline winter schedules show only December capacity up year-on-year, and flagged higher 2027 Mexico costs from the 38-hour workweek and Terminal 1 start-up. Net debt to LTM EBITDA rose to 2.6x from 0.2x following the BRL 5.5 billion CPC acquisition, though management said next year's MXN 11 billion capex will be funded from operating cash flow with no further leverage expected.

negative_highlights: Total non-interest expense is guided to $460-465 million with an expected step-up in Q4 due to incentive compensation and technology investments, leaving less clarity on the 2027 expense base.
Net charge-offs remain at 28 bps and management flagged potential borrower stress from rate resets in 2027 that could lead to restructurings.
The Q3 NIM expansion was limited to 2 bps (to 3.19%) due to timing of deposit growth versus loan funding, with the full benefit not yet reflected.
positive_highlights: Total deposits grew 4% QoQ and 11% YoY to a record $22.6 billion, with non-interest-bearing deposits up $300 million to a record $7.2 billion (32% of total).
EPS rose 10% QoQ to $2.25 and ROE reached 14%, up more than 70 bps QoQ, while the efficiency ratio improved approximately 340 bps.
Loan growth guidance was raised to 12% or higher and deposit growth guidance to 9% or more; September run-rate NIM was 3.25% with new loan yields at 6.83% (50 bps above the quarterly average).
summary: Customers Bancorp reported Q3 2026 EPS of $2.25 (up 10% QoQ), NII of $208 million (up 8% QoQ), and ROE of 14% (up >70 bps QoQ). Deposits reached a record $22.6 billion (up 4% QoQ, 11% YoY) and loans a record $18.5 billion (up 3% QoQ, 14% YoY), with non-interest-bearing deposits up $300 million to $7.2 billion. Guidance was raised for loan growth to 12%+ (from prior) and deposits to 9%+, while NII was tightened to $805-810 million and expenses updated to $460-465 million. The efficiency ratio improved ~340 bps QoQ and the September run-rate NIM was 3.25%, with management pointing to further NIM expansion in Q4.

negative_highlights: Management expects no dramatic change in growth trajectory near term given cautious lending
Credit card pilot still a quarter or two from a decision on scaling, limiting near-term visibility
No formal forward guidance or consensus comparison provided in the transcript
positive_highlights: Adjusted EPS of $1.92 on revenue growth of 3.2%
Provisioning expense fell 7.7% as credit quality improved
Front-end delinquency declined from 20% to 18.9%
summary: World Acceptance reported Q2 FY2027 adjusted EPS of $1.92, with revenue up 3.2% and provisioning expense down 7.7% year over year. Credit quality improved, with front-end delinquency falling from 20% to 18.9%, and G&A expense also improved. Management guided to a cautious lending posture, saying it remains much tighter than a year ago and expects no dramatic change in growth trajectory near term, while the credit card pilot is still a quarter or two from a scale decision. No formal revenue or EPS guidance or consensus comparison was provided in the transcript.

Selective reported Q3 FY2026 diluted EPS of $2.11 and operating EPS of $2.37, a 16.9% operating ROE and 15.1% ROE, with a GAAP combined ratio of 96.8 (5.4 points of cats), improving 1.8 points YoY. Net investment income rose 16% to $127 million after tax, and the company raised full-year NII guidance to $490 million from $480 million while holding the combined ratio guide at 96.5-97.5% and lowering the cat assumption to 5.5 points. Standard Commercial renewal pure price was 5.7% (6.4% ex-workers' comp), but net premiums written fell 8%, with about five points of the decline from deliberately lower retention in the worst-performing 10% of cohorts (retention 52% vs 79% a year ago). Management framed the reduced near-term growth as intentional mix and pricing discipline, and announced a 12% dividend increase and a new $200 million buyback authorization.

negative_highlights: Adjusted operating margin narrowed to ~10.5%, the low end of the 10.5%-11% range, on ~170-180 bps of incremental raw material and logistics headwinds
Gross margin fell 90 bps to 18.4% and adjusted operating income declined 3% to $262M; adjusted EPS fell $0.13 to $2.19
Global organic sales declined 1% while light vehicle production fell 1.9%; Q4 production is forecast to drop ~4.5% and raw material is expected to stay as challenging in 2027
positive_highlights: Outperformance with Chinese OEMs of nearly 20 percentage points, lifting their share of China sales to 58% from 46% a year earlier
Adjusted operating margin of 9.7% came in ahead of earlier indication, with operational drivers contributing $34M despite slightly lower sales
Completed buybacks of over 1.2 million shares for $150M plus $63M in dividends, and CapEx guidance trimmed to ~4% of sales
summary: Autoliv reported Q3 net sales of $2.7B, down 0.5% (organic -1%), with adjusted operating income down 3% to $262M and adjusted operating margin down 30 bps to 9.7% despite beating the company's own earlier indication. Adjusted diluted EPS fell $0.13 to $2.19, driven by a $0.16 higher tax hit. Full-year 2026 adjusted operating margin guidance was narrowed to around 10.5%, the low end of the prior 10.5%-11% range, citing ~170-180 bps of incremental raw material and logistics headwinds, while organic sales guidance stays flat and cash flow guidance is unchanged; CapEx was cut to ~4% of sales from less than 5%. Management framed Q4 as sequentially stronger on engineering income, tariff/raw material recoveries and cost actions, though it flagged raw materials as equally challenging into 2027.

negative_highlights: Full-year constant-currency revenue growth guidance cut to 1%-2%, with H2 facing seasonal weakness and management noting H1 growth of 1.9% was below expectations on softer volume and lower pricing
Operating margin guidance maintained but H2 margins face headwinds from compensation hikes, softer seasonality, AI productivity sharing, and large-deal ramp-up
High-tech and retail verticals softened, with manufacturing under near-term pressure from a large client, and high competitive intensity pressuring pricing
positive_highlights: Large deal TCV of $5.2 billion, second highest quarterly TCV in five years, with 62% net new and a net-new $2 billion-plus seven-year mega deal expected to contribute over 1% to FY28 revenue
AI revenue reached 10.5% of total revenue with 29% sequential growth, up from 8.2% last quarter
Free cash flow of $928 million at 113% of net profit; interim dividend raised 13% to INR 26 and Q2 EPS up 8.7% YoY to INR 19.32
summary: Infosys reported Q2 FY27 revenue of $5.145 billion, up 1.2% sequentially and 1.5% YoY in constant currency, with management stating growth was below expectations due to softer volume and lower-than-anticipated price increases amid high competitive intensity. Operating margin was 21%, down 0.1% sequentially, and free cash flow was $928 million (113% of net profit). Full-year revenue growth guidance was cut to 1%-2% in constant currency from the prior outlook, while the 20%-22% operating margin guidance was maintained. Offsets included AI revenue at 10.5% of total (up over 29% sequentially) and large deal TCV of $5.2 billion, including a net-new $2 billion-plus seven-year mega deal expected to add over 1% to FY28 growth.

negative_highlights: Q4 NIM guided down to 3.65%-3.70% from 3.77%, partly as the NPL recovery benefit and early exit fees do not recur
