Total deposits fell $109.6M to $8.2B; Q4 deposit guidance revised down on large commercial fund-provider exits
Provision rose to $6.2M from $4.8M on $12.6M of specific reserves across four commercial relationships; gross charge-offs guided to 30-35 bp in Q4
positive_highlights: NIM expanded 25 bp to 3.77% from 3.52%, driven by 18 bp from loan repricing and 6 bp of NPL recovery interest
Net interest income rose $7.9M to $90.5M and pre-tax pre-provision net revenue hit $39.7M, the highest since 4Q22
Non-performing loans fell $21.6M, or 12.6%, to $149.5M (1.46% of assets); a $5M downgraded loan paid off post-quarter
summary: Amerant reported Q3 FY2026 net income of $25.7M ($0.65 diluted EPS) versus $0.53 in Q2, with NIM expanding 25 bp to 3.77% and NII up $7.9M to $90.5M. ROA reached 1% and ROE 11.29%, the best quarterly results since 3Q22 and 4Q21 respectively, while the efficiency ratio improved to 63.51% from 68.37%. The board authorized a $50M share repurchase program through 2027. Q4 guidance calls for NIM of 3.65%-3.70% (down from 3.77%), loans of ~$7.3B (up from $7.1B), deposits of ~$8.5B (revised lower from prior guidance on large commercial fund-provider exits), and non-interest expense of ~$68M; early 2027 expense run-rate guided to $69.5-70M.

negative_highlights: Gross written premium fell 4.8% and net written premium 1.5%, with pricing down about 3.1% per the Amwins index and commercial property showing double-digit premium declines
GAAP diluted EPS fell 28.4%, including a $37.6 million ($1.67/share) pre-tax loss on fixed maturity sales

Combined ratio deteriorated to 75.4% from 74.9% as the expense ratio rose a point to 22% on higher reinsurance retentions; management said loss cost trends are running slightly ahead of rates in some divisions
positive_highlights: Diluted operating EPS rose 9.4% to $5.70 and annualized operating ROE was 25.6% through nine months
Loss ratio improved to 53.4% from 53.9% on higher favorable prior-year development, and the other underwriting expense ratio held flat at 10.2%
Net investment income grew 17.5% to $58.3 million; $130 million of sub-2% bonds were replaced with bonds yielding above 5.5%, adding roughly $5.5-6 million of annual income
summary: Kinsale reported Q3 diluted operating EPS of $5.70, up 9.4% YoY, with a 75.4% combined ratio versus 74.9% a year earlier; GAAP diluted EPS fell 28.4%, driven by a $37.6 million ($1.67/share) pre-tax loss on bond sales as the investment portfolio was repositioned. Gross written premium fell 4.8% and net written premium 1.5%, though excluding the commercial property division GWP was down only 0.5%, and submissions, quotes and binds grew mid-single digits. Annualized operating ROE was 25.6% through nine months, net investment income rose 17.5% to $58.3 million, and the company repurchased 269,000 shares for $100 million, which management expects as a quarterly run rate. Management described E&S competition as the most intense in 10 years and gave no formal forward guidance, but said the premium decline stems largely from a mix shift away from large accounts that should correct near term.

negative_highlights: NIM fell 12 bps quarter over quarter to 3.37%, with seven bps from lower loan fee income tied to payoffs
Non-performing loans rose to $7.7 million, or 33 bps of total loans, from $2.1 million (9 bps) prior quarter, driven primarily by one loan; classified loans rose to 44 bps from 20 bps
Non-interest income of $2.7 million was below plan, with swap activity 'nearly negligible' in Q2 and Q3 versus $1.4 million in Q1, and SBA gain-on-sale lighter than planned
positive_highlights: Net income of $9.5 million, or $0.51 per diluted share, was the highest quarterly earnings since IPO and up 13.3% year over year
September NIM exit rate of 3.41% and guidance to hold/improve at the 340 level in Q4, supported by $610 million of loans repricing at a 6.37% weighted average yield
New loan production of $156 million was up 18% year over year and the average coupon on new loans rose 12 bps to 6.02% (6.29% excluding correspondent)
summary: USCB reported record quarterly net income of $9.5 million, or $0.51 per diluted share, up from $0.49 last quarter and 13.3% year over year, with NII of $24.3 million (up 14.2% YoY) and ROE of 16.03%. However, NIM compressed 12 bps to 3.37% from 3.49% (mostly lower loan fee income tied to payoffs), non-interest income of $2.7 million came in below plan on weak swap and SBA activity, and non-performing loans jumped to $7.7 million (33 bps) from $2.1 million (9 bps) on one loan. Guidance was largely maintained: Q4 NIM guided to the 340 range, loan growth still high single to low double digit (near term lower end), Q4 expenses ~$15 million or slightly higher, and fee income recovery described as measured.

negative_highlights: Total origination funded volume fell 19% quarter-over-quarter to $12.9 billion, and management expects about a 25% production decline from September to October
Wholesale gain-on-sale margins face continued pressure, with Baron Silverstein flagging more margin pressure coming in the fourth quarter
Agency and Ginnie delinquencies rose slightly quarter-over-quarter, attributed to seasonality
positive_highlights: Newrez pre-tax income ex-mark-to-market of about $330 million rose 7% quarter-over-quarter at a 24% annualized operating ROE
Non-agency originations rose 8% quarter-over-quarter and 30% year-over-year, with year-to-date non-agency volume of $5.1 billion a Newrez record
Sub-servicing added 15 new clients and about $80 billion in new loan boardings year to date, and year-to-date gross asset management inflows were just under $3 billion
summary: Rithm reported Q3 2026 EAD of $0.55 per diluted share and $315 million, with GAAP net income of $217 million ($0.38 per diluted share) and book value roughly flat quarter-over-quarter at about $12.50 per share. Newrez pre-tax income excluding mark-to-market was approximately $330 million, up 7% quarter-over-quarter, at a 24% annualized operating ROE; Genesis pre-tax income was $33 million, up 14% year-over-year. Origination funded volume fell 19% quarter-over-quarter to $12.9 billion, and management guided to roughly a 25% production decline from September to October on higher rates. No formal guidance was raised; management reiterated $125 million of expected Newrez savings from AI and technology and a $75-80 billion AUM target by end-2028.

WSFS reported Q3 FY2026 core EPS of $1.75, core ROA of 1.58%, and core ROTCE of 20.7%, all above the prior quarter, with core PPNR up 15% YoY and core EPS up 25% YoY. NIM expanded 1 bp linked quarter to 3.88%, gross loans grew 1% linked quarter (5% annualized, 7% YoY ex-Spring EQ runoff), and wealth and trust fees rose 30% YoY on broad-based growth. Guidance was largely unchanged: mid-single-digit loan and deposit growth, efficiency ratio grinding lower from 56.1%, a 35% up-cycle deposit beta for 2026 with a normalized 45-50% outlook, and net charge-offs expected to come in a bit better than prior guidance. The quarter was tempered by a $57.5 million (12%) linked-quarter increase in problem assets and an $8 million specific reserve on a student housing loan, while buybacks slowed to about 80% of net income from roughly 100% due to rate-driven AOCI/TCE considerations.

Eni reported Q3 FY2026 net income of EUR 2.8 billion, up 20% QoQ despite lower oil prices and 2.2x YoY, with CFFO before working capital of EUR 4.3 billion (up 30% YoY). E&P production grew 4.2% and pro forma EBIT was EUR 4.6 billion; full-year underlying production guidance was raised to 6-7% and 2026 CFFO guidance lifted to EUR 16.5 billion, 43% above initial guidance. The buyback was raised to EUR 3.8 billion from EUR 3.4 billion plus a EUR 1.3 billion exceptional dividend, taking total payout to EUR 8.2 billion, while gearing fell to a record 10% reported (9% pro forma). Offsets include a Plenitude EBITDA guidance cut to EUR 1.2 billion from EUR 1.3 billion on retail competition and weaker renewables, continued Versalis losses, and a fuel price cap costing a few hundred million per quarter.

negative_highlights: FFO ex-current tax was flat at $47.1 million, down 0.7% YoY, despite double-digit revenue and NOI growth
Adjusted EBITDA margin contracted 123 bps YoY to 84.1% and adjusted NOI margin fell 33 bps to 94.1% on higher operating property, administrative and other costs
Development pipeline grew ~80% QoQ to ~3.3 million square feet (~$282.5 million investment), largely on a speculative basis, creating lease-up exposure
positive_highlights: Record 1.6 million square feet of new leases drove total Q3 leasing to ~2.3 million square feet, with portfolio and stabilized occupancy up 220 bps QoQ to 93.9%
FY2026 revenue growth guidance raised to 11.5%-12.5% from 10%-11%, and adjusted NOI/EBITDA margin targets raised to 94%/84% from 93.5%/83%
summary: Vesta reported Q3 FY2026 total revenue of $79.6 million (up 9.9% YoY), rental revenue ex-energy of $77.5 million (up 10.8% YoY), adjusted NOI of $72.9 million (up 10.4%, 94.1% margin) and adjusted EBITDA of $65.2 million (up 9.2%, 84.1% margin), while FFO ex-current tax was flat at $47.1 million and pre-tax income jumped to $104 million from $52.4 million on investment property revaluations. Management raised FY2026 revenue growth guidance to 11.5%-12.5% from 10%-11% and lifted year-end adjusted NOI/EBITDA margin targets to 94%/84% from 93.5%/83%. Leasing was the standout, with a record 1.6 million square feet of new leases within ~2.3 million square feet signed, portfolio and stabilized occupancy at 93.9% (up 220 bps QoQ) and same-store occupancy at 95.5%. The negative offsets were the flat FFO, year-over-year margin contraction in both NOI and EBITDA, and a materially larger mostly spec development pipeline (~3.3 million square feet, ~80% QoQ growth) that carries lease-up risk.

negative_highlights: Raw material inflation is running all year and pass-through is only roughly break-even year-to-date, described as slightly margin-dilutive
Inventory climbed to $177 million, which management called high versus history, driven by inflation, growth, safety stock and pre-launch build

High oil prices were characterized as a net negative via logistics, utilities and petrochemical inputs, with the fracking choline business only around an $8 million run rate versus $5 million last year
positive_highlights: Revenue rose 8.6% to a record $291 million with growth in all three segments
Gross margin expanded 70 bps to 36.4% and adjusted EBITDA rose 12.4% to a record $80 million (27.6% margin)
Animal Nutrition & Health operating earnings jumped 82.8% to $6.8 million on 11.7% sales growth
summary: Balchem reported record Q3 FY2026 revenue of $291 million, up 8.6% YoY, with GAAP EPS of $1.46 (+17.7%) and adjusted EPS of $1.57 (+16.3%). Gross margin expanded 70 bps to 36.4% and adjusted EBITDA rose 12.4% to a record $80 million; all three segments grew, with Animal Nutrition & Health sales up 11.7% and segment operating earnings up 82.8%. Management gave no formal numeric guidance but said it expects Q4 to be sequentially lower on normal seasonality while still delivering year-over-year growth. Free cash flow was $58 million, with $28 million of buybacks and $28 million of debt reduction taking net leverage to 0.2x.

negative_highlights: Cash same-property NOI decreased 1.5%, with lower settlement/restoration fees and tax refunds a 170 bps drag
Portfolio occupancy including KOP 2 fell 10 bps sequentially to 76.9%

2027 headwinds: ~$395 million of debt maturing at ~3.8% likely to refinance higher (~$4 million annualized per 100 bps), DIRECTV downsize/vacate of 484,000 sq ft in Q4 2027, and ~$37 million annualized added cost when Flower Mart capitalization stops in January 2027
positive_highlights: GAAP re-leasing spreads of +30.6% and cash spreads of +9.7%, among the strongest reported since before the pandemic, on ~815,000 sq ft of Q3 leasing
Leased occupancy rose 150 bps to 83%, with all five regions posting sequential leased-occupancy gains of more than 100 bps
SNO pipeline grew to 1.4 million sq ft and ~$101 million ABR, with ABR per square foot ~$72, roughly 22% above the portfolio average
summary: KRC reported Q3 FY2026 FFO of $0.88/diluted share (including ~$0.01 of settlement and restoration fee income) and raised the low-to-mid-point of full-year FFO guidance by $0.01 to $3.55-$3.59 (midpoint $3.57), driven by +$0.01 same-property NOI, +$0.02 development NOI, and +$0.01 net interest, offset by -$0.02 lower termination fees and -$0.01 higher G&A. Leasing was the standout: ~815,000 sq ft executed in Q3, YTD volume over 1.75 million sq ft (+44% vs. first nine months of 2025), GAAP re-leasing spreads +30.6% and cash +9.7%, with leased occupancy up 150 bps to 83% and the SNO pipeline at 1.4 million sq ft / ~$101 million ABR. Offsets include cash same-property NOI down 1.5% and portfolio occupancy including KOP 2 down 10 bps to 76.9%. Management flagged 2027 headwinds: ~$395 million of debt maturing at ~3.8% likely refinanced higher, DIRECTV's 484,000 sq ft El Segundo lease expiring in Q4 2027 (~$4 million/quarter ABR), and ~$37 million annualized cost from ceasing Flower Mart capitalization in January 2027.

negative_highlights: 90-day NPL rose to 4.6% from 4.3% in the prior quarter and 4.1% a year earlier, with half of the increase from FGI/FGO portfolios and about 10 bps from John Deere Bank seasonality
NII net of provisions was nearly flat as cost of credit increased; management placed the year at the lower end of the BRL 42-48 billion guidance range
Large corporate portfolio growth of 14.8% diluted NIM; excluding roughly BRL 50 billion of large corporate growth, NIM would be 9.3% rather than the reported level
positive_highlights: Loan portfolio grew 11.1% year-over-year to BRL 1.15 trillion, above the national financial system's 9.2% growth through August
Total NII rose 14% year-over-year and 2.4% quarter-over-quarter, supported by growth in NII, fee income, and insurance premiums
Completed a BRL 10 billion capital increase, leaving CET1 at 12.1% and Basel level 1 at 13.7%
summary: Bradesco reported loan portfolio growth of 11.1% year-over-year to BRL 1.15 trillion (1.1% QoQ), with total NII up 14% YoY and 2.4% QoQ, but NII net of provisions roughly flat as cost of credit rose. The 90-day NPL ratio rose to 4.6% from 4.3% in the prior quarter and 4.1% a year earlier, with half of the increase attributed to FGI/FGO guaranteed portfolios and about 10 bps to John Deere Bank seasonality. Management kept the NII net of provisions guidance at BRL 42-48 billion, stating the bank is in the lower range and performance is within expectations, while flagging that cost of risk and 90-day NPL will remain under pressure until a curve inflection expected in Q2/Q3 2027. CET1 reached 12.1% following a completed BRL 10 billion capital increase.

negative_highlights: 2026 EPS guidance cut to $0.10-$0.15 and 2027 to $0.85-$0.95, pushing peer-like profitability to 2028 from 2027
Provision rose to $76M and criticized/classified loans increased $670M or 6%, with substandard up $248M, on an 18-month look-forward at higher rates
Deposit growth forecast cut and mortgage gain-on-sale fee income reduced by roughly $80M-$100M; buybacks paused for Q4
positive_highlights: NIM expanded 4 bps QoQ to 2.17%, with September NIM at 2.23% and Q4 guided to 2.20%-2.25%
Net charge-offs fell $25M to $74M, or 0.49% of average loans, with nonaccruals roughly flat at $2.8B
C&I loans grew $2B (11% QoQ) to $20.6B on a $2.7B pipeline; CRE par payoffs of $1.2B reduced concentration, and CET1 at 12.38%
summary: Flagstar cut its 2026 and 2027 EPS guidance, with 2026 now at $0.10-$0.15 and 2027 at $0.85-$0.95, and pushed the timeline for peer-like profitability out roughly 12 months to 2028, which it guided at $1.60-$1.70. Q3 showed operating improvement (NIM up 4 bps to 2.17%, PPNR positive, C&I loans up $2B or 11% QoQ to $20.6B, net charge-offs down $25M to $74M or 49 bps), but provision rose to $76M on higher rates and NYC rent-regulation pressure, and criticized/classified loans rose $670M or 6%. The guidance cut was attributed to a forward curve now implying four rate hikes, a more competitive deposit environment, slower nonaccrual resolution (YE26 ~$2.6B vs prior $2.3B), and lower mortgage fee income ($80M-$100M reduction). Management said no buybacks in Q4 but expects to resume in 2027.

negative_highlights: About $16 million of pre-tax mark-to-market losses hit results across the mortgage pipeline and trading assets, alongside a $21 million negative AOCI impact
PrimeLending pre-tax loss of $10.8 million with lock volume down 18% to $2.2 billion and gain-on-sale margin down 26 bps to 200 bps; Q4 and 2027 remain challenged
Credit provision of $10.1 million drove a $9 million ACL build to $94 million (1.07% coverage), and deposit betas are expected to revert to 55%-60%, pressuring future NIM
positive_highlights: Net interest income rose 9% YoY to $122 million on commercial loan and deposit growth
Net interest margin expanded 12 bps QoQ to 3.33% and over 25 bps YoY to 3.49% on stable deposit costs and loan repricing
Deposits grew $500 million in the quarter, including $100 million swept in from HilltopSecurities, and full-year bank loan growth is guided to 7%-8%
summary: Hilltop reported Q3 2026 net income of $24.9 million, or $0.44 per diluted share, with ROA of 0.67% and ROE of 4.7%, as roughly $16 million of pre-tax mark-to-market losses and a $10.1 million credit provision weighed on results. PlainsCapital grew core loans 7% YoY to $8.7 billion and expanded NIM 12 bps QoQ to 3.33%, while PrimeLending posted an $11 million pre-tax loss on an 18% decline in rate lock volume to $2.2 billion and a 26 bp drop in gain-on-sale margin to 200 bps. Management guided fourth-quarter mortgage results to remain challenged and said mortgage conditions will pressure activity into 2027, and it expects NIM to level out or trend modestly lower, while the expense outlook improved slightly.

negative_highlights: Net income fell to $62.2 million, or $0.65 per diluted share, from $83.9 million, or $0.87, in Q2, and non-interest income dropped $18.4 million largely on the prior quarter's $19.5 million branch-sale gain
Loans decreased $296 million in the quarter, with management guiding to further meaningful commercial payoffs and continued mix pressure in Q4
Management guided to a smaller sequential margin benefit in Q4 than in Q3, noted a slightly reduced deposit guide, and declined to provide a 2027 outlook
positive_highlights: Net interest margin expanded to 3.55% from 3.48% in Q2 and 3.36% in Q3 2025, the 10th consecutive quarter of expansion, with a 5 bp rise in loan yields to 5.67% and a 4 bp decline in funding costs
Non-interest-bearing deposits increased for a second consecutive quarter, and criticized loans fell 19% year over year while non-performing assets declined 6% sequentially
Repurchased approximately 2 million shares for about $76 million, bringing program-to-date repurchases to $347 million, while CET1 remained strong at 14.36%
summary: FIBK reported Q3 FY2026 net income of $62.2 million, or $0.65 per diluted share, down from $83.9 million and $0.87 in Q2, which included a $19.5 million gain on the Nebraska branch transaction. Net interest income rose 2% sequentially to $206.2 million and the FTE net interest margin expanded to 3.55% from 3.48% (3.36% a year ago), the 10th consecutive quarter of expansion, but non-interest income fell $18.4 million on the absence of the prior-quarter gain and loans declined $296 million. Management cited more meaningful commercial payoffs in Q4, a smaller sequential margin benefit than in Q3, a slightly reduced deposit guide, and did not provide a 2027 outlook, while repurchasing about 2 million shares for roughly $76 million and declaring a $0.47 dividend.

negative_highlights: Management guided to possible NIM compression over the next few quarters from higher deposit costs and competitive pricing.
Mortgage production fell 13.7% QoQ and adjusted non-interest income declined about $2 million, mostly on lower mortgage revenue.
Criticized/classified and NPAs ticked higher; the CFO noted new interest-bearing-funded loan growth would be about 25 bps margin dilutive.
positive_highlights: EPS of $1.73 per diluted share marked a five-year record high for the company.
Adjusted efficiency ratio improved to 49.15% from 50.42% last quarter on higher revenue and lower expenses.
Net charge-offs fell to 19 bps annualized, with reserve coverage at 162% of loans and 315% of NPAs; board approved a new $200 million repurchase authorization.
summary: Ameris reported Q3 net income of $116.1 million, or $1.73 per diluted share, which the CEO called a five-year record high EPS. NIM held at 3.87% (down 1 bp QoQ), the adjusted efficiency ratio improved to 49.15% from 50.42%, ROA was 1.61%, and net charge-offs fell to 19 bps. Management guided to mid-single-digit loan and deposit growth near term but flagged possible NIM compression over the next few quarters from higher deposit costs and competition. The board approved a new $200 million buyback authorization; no shares were repurchased this quarter.

negative_highlights: Mortgage banking revenue fell to $8 million from $11.4 million in Q2 and $8.9 million a year ago amid the rate spike
Management expects mortgage volume to fall from ~$1.6 billion to ~$1.1 billion annually if high rates persist, with ~$4 million of cost cuts in response
Mortgage Warehouse balances fell $43 million to $501 million and the division lost about $200,000 in the quarter; core net charge-offs rose to 17 bps from 3 bps a year ago
positive_highlights: Reported NIM rose 21 bps linked quarter to 3.66% and 48 bps year over year, with core NIM up 14 bps to 3.59%
Operating EPS of $0.35 versus $0.23 in Q2 and $0.28 a year ago; pre-tax pre-provision operating income up 38% year over year to $12 million
Tangible book value $13.81, up 18% year over year, and TCE ratio improved to 8.14%
summary: Primis reported Q3 net income of $8.7 million, or $0.35 per diluted share, up 28% year over year but down from $9.4 million ($0.38) in Q2; operating EPS of $0.35 rose from $0.23 linked quarter and $0.28 a year ago. Reported NIM expanded to 3.66% (core 3.59% ex-recovery), up 21 bps linked quarter, on 9% loan growth and stable funding costs. Mortgage banking revenue fell to $8 million from $11.4 million last quarter as the 10-year rose nearly 100 bps; management expects annual mortgage volume to drop from ~$1.6 billion to ~$1.1 billion if rates persist and has cut ~$4 million of annualized fixed costs. Guidance points to full-year loan growth of ~8%-8.5% and incremental NIM expansion of 4-5 bps ahead.

negative_highlights: Gross margin declined 40 bps to 45.7% on higher material costs, depreciation, and freight; wood product gross margin fell to 44.9% from 46.2%
Europe net sales fell 3.4% to $129.9 million on a 5% volume decline, with gross margin down to 36.1% from 37.9%
Management expects full-year operating margin of 20.0%-20.5% and Q4 operating income in the 14% range, implying a sequential step-down
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA rose 7.4% to $167.2 million, a 26.2% margin
North America operating margin improved to 27.3% from 25.9%, with segment sales up 3.8% to $502 million
Operating expenses fell 6.3% to $150.5 million and SG&A headcount dropped about 6% year-over-year
summary: Simpson reported Q3 FY2026 net sales of $638.1 million, up 2.3% year-over-year, with pricing contributing 2.5% and volumes roughly flat; GAAP diluted EPS was $2.68 versus $2.58. Gross margin fell 40 bps to 45.7% and operating margin slipped 50 bps to 22.1%, partly due to a prior-year $12.9 million Gallatin facility gain, while adjusted EBITDA rose 7.4% to $167.2 million. Full-year operating margin guidance is now 20.0%-20.5%, and management expects volumes down slightly for the remainder of the year amid decelerating housing starts and steel up over 50% year-over-year, with additional pricing actions to be announced.

negative_highlights: Non-interest income of $12.5M came in below expectations on weaker SBIC and swap fee revenue
NPLs fell only 2 bps to 1.24% and NPAs 1 bp to 1.22%; NCO uptick came from a single previously identified, fully reserved commercial relationship, with resolution timing slipping into Q4
New and renewed loan yield of 6.99% for the quarter versus 7.13% in September, and management flagged emerging competitive pressure on deposit rates near one-year brokered levels
positive_highlights: Core NIM expanded 12 bps linked quarter to 3.80% and GAAP NIM rose 13 bps to 3.86%, on loan yields up 10 bps against deposit costs down 2 bps
Deposits grew $141.2M (7.7% annualized) and loans grew $21.4M (7.2% annualized), enabling paydown of ~$66M brokered deposits and $108M of FHLB borrowings
Core non-interest expense fell $1.4M to $56.9M, below expectations, on accelerated Progressive cost saves; core pre-tax pre-provision earnings of $36.3M exceeded expectations
summary: Business First Bancshares reported Q3 FY2026 GAAP net income of $23.2M ($0.71/share) and core net income of $26M ($0.79/share), with core ROAA of 1.17% and a core efficiency ratio of 61.1%. Core NIM expanded 12 bps linked quarter to 3.80% (GAAP NIM 3.86%, +13 bps), loans grew $21.4M or 7.2% annualized, and deposits rose $141.2M or 7.7% annualized, funding a $66M brokered deposit paydown and $108M of FHLB repayment; core non-interest expense fell $1.4M to $56.9M. Management guided Q4 to continued mid-to-upper single-digit loan growth, further margin expansion, ~$57M core expense run-rate, and NPA reductions of roughly $15M, with a stated path to a 1.25% ROAA. The main soft spot was non-interest income ($12.5M, below expectations on lumpy SBIC and swap revenue) and credit progress that lagged, with NPLs down only 2 bps to 1.24%.

negative_highlights: Q4 adjusted EBITDA guided to $10M-$20M, well below Q3's $24M, on seasonal declines, $5M-$7M Cypress Bend outage, $4M seasonal energy, and continued Augusta challenges
Net sales fell 4% YoY to $385M with a 4% pricing decline; reported a $2M net loss, or $0.10 per diluted share

Augusta is running 10%-15% below needed production; January 2027 outage costs $12M-$15M with a likely additional Q2/Q3 2027 outage at $7M-$10M, and additional capital investment needed to address undisclosed asset conditions
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA of $24M came in at the midpoint of the $20M-$30M guidance range despite Augusta disruptions
First $60/ton price increase fully implemented, expected to deliver more than $70M in annual benefit with $8M-$12M sequential contribution in Q4; second $60 increase making good progress
Debt refinancing closed in September extends maturities five years to 2031; year-to-date net debt reduced by $56M, and full-year free cash flow now expected to be positive
summary: Adjusted EBITDA of $24M landed at the midpoint of the $20M-$30M guidance range, but net sales fell 4% YoY to $385M on a 4% price decline and 1% lower shipments, producing a $2M net loss ($0.10/diluted share). Q4 guidance of $10M-$20M adjusted EBITDA is a sharp step down, reflecting $5M-$7M Cypress Bend outage costs, $4M seasonal energy, $1M-$2M incremental conflict costs, and continued Augusta operational challenges. Offsets include a fully implemented first $60/ton price increase (worth $70M annualized, $8M-$12M sequential Q4 contribution), a second increase in progress, and completion of a debt refinancing extending maturities to 2031. Augusta electrical and mechanical failures drive a January 2027 outage ($12M-$15M) and a likely Q2/Q3 2027 outage ($7M-$10M), with the mill running 10%-15% below needed production.

negative_highlights: Recurring revenue growth decelerated to 18% from 20% last quarter, partly on prior-year China revenue timing
Non-GAAP operating margin of 44.1% and full-year guide of ~44.7% is only slightly above last year, as Hexagon D&E integration drags incremental margins
G&A expense spiked in Q3 on timing of annual charitable contributions (moved from Q4), a one-time shift
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 22% YoY to $1.633 billion, exceeding guidance on every key metric, with record backlog of $8.2 billion
Full-year 2026 revenue outlook raised to ~21% growth and non-GAAP EPS raised $0.30 to $8.40
All product groups grew double digits: core EDA +20%, IP +24%, SDA +30%, with recurring revenue up 18% YoY
summary: Cadence reported Q3 revenue of $1.633 billion, up 22% YoY with double-digit growth in every product group (core EDA +20%, IP +24%, SDA +30%), and exceeded guidance on every key metric. Non-GAAP operating margin was 44.1% and non-GAAP EPS was $2.11, with record backlog of $8.2 billion and 18% recurring revenue growth. The company raised its full-year 2026 outlook to ~21% revenue growth and non-GAAP EPS of $8.40 (up $0.30), and authorized an additional $2.5 billion buyback alongside $400 million repurchased in the quarter. Momentum was underscored by the Maestro domain-specialized AI model launch and over 100 active agentic AI engagements.

negative_highlights: Communications revenue declined 8% sequentially and is guided down high single digits in Q4, with both iOS and Android ecosystems declining
Consumer revenue expected to decline more than seasonal, into the mid-teens percent sequentially, on component shortages in premium smartphones and IoT wearables
Q4 EPS guidance of $0.65-0.75 is below the $0.76 reported in Q3; 2027 CapEx expected to step up significantly with depreciation rising mid-teens percent in 2026
positive_highlights: Gross margin expanded 150 bps sequentially and 400 bps year-on-year to 18.3% on richer advanced packaging mix
Computing revenue up 25% sequentially to a record, with a second HDFO CPU hyperscaler program ramping in Q3 and two new 2.5D programs expected in Q4
Q4 revenue guided to low double-digit sequential growth and over 50% year-on-year, with computing guided to over 30% growth in 2026 and similar or higher in 2027
summary: Amkor reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $1.99 billion, up 5% sequentially, with gross margin of 18.3% (up 150 bps QoQ and 400 bps YoY) and operating margin of 11.3%; EPS was $0.76 and EBITDA $435 million. Computing and automotive/industrial each hit records, up 25% and 7% sequentially, while communications fell 8% QoQ on SiP migration, memory constraints, and component shortages. Q4 guidance calls for revenue of $1.9-2.0 billion (low double-digit sequential growth, over 50% YoY), gross margin of 18-19%, and EPS of $0.65-0.75. Management raised the CapEx profile with 2027 step-ups for Arizona, Korea, and Vietnam, supported by customer advance payments from a dozen customers.

negative_highlights: AOCI declined $24.8 million on rising rates, lowering the tangible common equity ratio to 8.05% and tangible book value per share to $18.81
New loan fundings of $63.6 million were roughly flat sequentially, requiring a $31 million residential pool purchase to supplement growth
positive_highlights: EPS rose 7% sequentially to $0.62 and net income was up 32% versus Q3 2025
Net interest margin expanded 10 bps on loan yields rising to 5.23% and deposit costs falling to 1.24%
Non-interest-bearing deposits grew $45 million and reached 37.8% of total deposits
summary: Bank of Marin reported Q3 net income of $9.9 million, or $0.62 per share, up from $9.2 million or $0.58 in the prior quarter, with ROAA of 1.05%, ROTCE of 12.26%, and efficiency ratio improving to 58.65%. NIM expanded 10 bps, loan yields rose to 5.23% from 5.12%, and deposit costs fell to 1.24% from 1.28%, driving a 17% sequential increase in pre-tax pre-provision income. NIB deposits grew $45 million to 37.8% of total deposits, but AOCI losses of $24.8 million from rising rates cut TCE ratio to 8.05% and tangible book value to $18.81. No formal guidance was issued; management pointed to a Q4 expense run-rate similar to Q3 and continued NIM tailwinds from ~25 bps of annual loan repricing, while noting a $14 million CRE downgrade and no share repurchases.

negative_highlights: FAA Chicago move-out and Loma Linda refinancing pressure baked into 2027 outlook
Medford, Oregon courthouse completion pushed to first half of 2028 from prior timing due to slower government design process
positive_highlights: Revenue rose 8.7% YoY to $93.6 million and EBITDA grew 8.9% to $59 million
Low end of 2026 core FFO guidance raised to $3.08 from $3.07 (range $3.08-$3.13)
Portfolio 98% leased with 9.2-year weighted average lease term; soft term cut to 2.3% of ALI from 5.2% at year-end 2024
summary: Q3 FY2026 revenue rose 8.7% YoY to $93.6 million and EBITDA grew 8.9% to $59 million; core FFO per share was $0.78 (+2.6% YoY) with FFO at $0.79. Management raised the low end of 2026 core FFO guidance to $3.08-$3.13 (from $3.07-$3.13), driven by the FAA Chicago nine-month lease extension, partly offset by the $35.6 million Bedford loan repayment. Initial 2027 guidance of $3.09-$3.17 implies only ~1% growth at the midpoint, with FAA Chicago move-out and the Loma Linda refinancing cited as headwinds. Net debt to annualized EBITDA was 7.1x, improved from Q2.

negative_highlights: Product gross margin of ~60.4% landed at the low end of the 60-63% range, attributed to supply-chain input cost inflation
MRDIMM ramp expected to be shallower than prior RCD generations; 2028-timed SOCAMM2 remains a niche opportunity
Supply lead times are lengthening and supply is expected to remain tight into 2027, with customers placing backlog earlier
positive_highlights: Record revenue of $218M and non-GAAP EPS of $0.84 both exceeded the top end of guidance, with EPS up 35% YoY
Record product revenue of $114M and Q4 product guidance of $127-133M implies ~34% YoY growth at the midpoint
Record cash flow from operations of $102M and a completed $100M accelerated share repurchase
summary: Rambus reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $218M, up 22% YoY and 5% QoQ, with non-GAAP EPS of $0.84, up 35% YoY and 10% QoQ, both above the top end of guidance. Product revenue hit a record $114M (+22% YoY, +15% QoQ), and Q4 guidance of $227-233M total revenue and $127-133M product revenue implies roughly 34% YoY product growth at the midpoint. Management flagged a shallower-than-usual MRDIMM ramp and supply-chain cost pressure pushing product gross margin to the low end of the 60-63% band, while demand into 2027 is described as strengthening with tight supply.

negative_highlights: Revenue fell 19.4% YoY to $72 million and active earning coaches dropped to about 10,200 from 19,500
GAAP operating loss widened to $19.4 million (26.9% of revenue) from $4.1 million, driven by $13.8 million of Catalyst restructuring charges
Management expects active earning coach count to keep declining through year-end and into the near term
positive_highlights: Revenue per active earning coach rose 54.1% YoY to $7,064, the highest level in many years
Adjusted gross margin expanded 220 bps to 71.7% on a non-GAAP basis
Adjusted EBITDA increased 29.7% to $0.4 million; 95% of active earning coaches were offering the new Trilivy Reset line by September
summary: Medifast reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $72 million, down 19.4% YoY, with GAAP net loss of $17.5 million (-$1.57 per diluted share) versus a $2.3 million loss a year ago; adjusted net loss was $2.1 million (-$0.19). Active earning coaches fell to roughly 10,200 from 19,500, though revenue per coach rose 54% to $7,064. Guidance calls for Q4 revenue of $55-75 million and EPS of $0-0.25, with full-year revenue of $280-300 million and adjusted EPS loss of $0.45-0.70; management reiterated the target of Q4 profitability.

negative_highlights: Six recordable injuries versus four in the previous two quarters, lifting the injury frequency rate
Two cargoes provisionally priced, so realized price of $1,276/t FOB may change in the December quarter
Management flagged negative lithium sentiment and softer China battery production data even as it called the physical market tight
positive_highlights: Revenue rose 137% to $74 million on 58,134t sold, up 71% QoQ
Unit operating costs fell 14% to $780/t sold from $907, with processing costs down 14%
Two binding offtakes signed, including LG Energy Solution at 240,000t over three years, and PFS raised post-expansion output to 373,000t/yr with C1 costs of $630/t
summary: Elevra reported Q1 FY27 revenue of $74 million, up 137% QoQ, on record ore mined (466,000t, +25%) and record mill throughput (just under 365,000t), with 54,907t of spodumene concentrate produced at 5.1% grade. Unit operating costs fell 14% to $780/t sold from $907, and the company ended with $319 million in cash after generating $34 million from NAL operations plus a $46 million convertible note. Realized price was $1,276/t FOB ($1,524/t SC6 equivalent) with two cargoes provisionally priced, so the reported price may change in the December quarter. Safety was a clear negative with six recordable injuries versus four across the prior two quarters, and the NAL PFS targets 373,000t/yr average production with C1 costs falling to $630/t.

negative_highlights: Excluding the MXN 1.1 billion Brazil insurance recovery, consolidated operating margin contracted 40 bps to 13.6% and operating income grew only 7.4%
Mexico operating income fell 3.1% and margin contracted 170 bps to 14.3% on multi-serve mix, labor, freight, and an operating FX loss
Operating capacity strained in Colombia and Venezuela with very low inventories amid high-double-digit volume growth
positive_highlights: Consolidated volumes up 5.3% to a record 1.1 billion unit cases, with growth in every region
Gross margin expanded 140 bps to 46.5% on lower sweetener and PET costs plus operating-currency appreciation
South America volumes +6% and reported operating margin +380 bps to 15.7% (29% underlying EBIT growth excluding insurance, per IR)
summary: KOF reported record Q3 volumes up 5.3% to 1.1 billion unit cases and revenue up 10.9% to MXN 79.7 billion (+11.3% FX-neutral), with gross margin expanding 140 bps to 46.5% on lower sweetener/PET costs. Reported operating income rose 15.4% and margin expanded 60 bps to 14.9%, but MXN 1.1 billion of Brazil insurance recoveries drove that; excluding it, operating income grew 7.4% and margin contracted 40 bps to 13.6%. Mexico volumes rose 4.8% off a low base against a 170 bps operating margin contraction to 14.3%, while South America volumes grew 6% with 380 bps of reported margin expansion. Management gave no formal numeric guidance but characterized 2027 as a more normalized year and said a capital-return mechanism would be announced early next year.

negative_highlights: Full-year results came in below the company's own start-of-year expectations, with FY2026 core EPS of $2.60, aggregate gross margin of 13.6%, and ROIC below the targeted range
Q4 EPS of $0.27 included ~$0.12 per share of facility rationalization costs tied to exiting the Omaha maintenance and repair facility, and operating margin was only 4.3%

European demand remains muted, with industry freight wagon deliveries falling from nearly 14,000 two years ago to under 10,000 in 2026 and a similar 2027 outlook, and tank car demand is pressured by competitor anti-dumping/countervailing duty petitions
positive_highlights: Q4 orders of 3,400 railcars worth ~$600 million drove a book-to-bill ratio of nearly 1.0, the highest since Q3 fiscal 2024, and backlog rose sequentially to 14,000 cars ($2.1 billion), the first increase since fiscal 2024
Lease fleet grew ~23% to approximately 21,000 railcars at 98% utilization, with recurring revenue at $175 million versus $113 million when the doubling goal was set
FY2027 EPS guidance of $2.75-$3.75 brackets FY2026 core EPS of $2.60, with aggregate gross margin guided to 14%-15% versus 13.6% in FY2026
summary: Q4 FY2026 revenue was $591 million, up ~3% sequentially, with aggregate gross margin of 13.5%, operating margin of 4.3% ($26 million, including $4 million in facility rationalization costs), GAAP EPS of $0.27 and core EPS of $0.39. Full-year revenue was $2.5 billion with core EPS of $2.60 and core EBITDA of $300 million (12% of revenue), results management said were below what it expected at the start of the year. FY2027 guidance calls for revenue of $2.8-$3.2 billion, operating margin of 7%-7.5%, EPS of $2.75-$3.75, and North American industry deliveries of 26,000-28,000; Greenbrier is replacing company-specific delivery guidance with an industry delivery outlook. Q4 orders of 3,400 cars (~$600 million) produced a book-to-bill near 1.0 and the first sequential backlog increase since fiscal 2024, to 14,000 cars valued at $2.1 billion.

negative_highlights: Adjusted operating margin fell to 1.7% of gross bookings from 1.8%, with air fare inflation of 25-30% raising payment processing costs without matching revenue per ticket
Air segment under pressure: domestic departures -7% and international -4% YoY, high ATF prices and INR depreciation weighing on demand
International hotel growth muted; outbound demand hit by geopolitical headwinds and high fares
positive_highlights: Gross bookings +20.9% YoY in constant currency to $2.7bn with all key segments in double digits
Bus ticketing adjusted margin +29% cc to $45.1mn with 24.7% volume growth; other segment +29.8% cc
Non-air business mix reached 63.2% vs 61.5% a year ago; domestic hotel room nights +20.4%
summary: Gross bookings grew 20.9% YoY in constant currency to $2.7bn, with hotels/packages adjusted margin up 20.2% cc to $116.8mn, bus ticketing up 29% cc to $45.1mn, and other segment up 29.8% cc to $24.4mn. Air ticketing adjusted margin rose 14.3% cc to $108.6mn even as domestic departures fell 7% and international 4%, with fares up 25-30%, and total adjusted operating profit grew 13.8% cc to $46.2mn. Adjusted OPM slipped to 1.7% of gross bookings from 1.8% a year ago on air revenue/processing-cost divergence tied to higher fares. No explicit forward guidance was issued; management flagged near-term macro caution, retains its long-term India view, and the India IPO awaits regulatory approval.

negative_highlights: U.S. sequential cement prices declined 3%, with price erosion in Texas and northern Florida cited, and EBITDA was hit by an unplanned outage at the Brooksville plant
For the first time in six quarters, total year-on-year costs increased, reflecting a pickup in inflation, with management flagging mid-to-high single-digit energy inflation for 2027
U.S. aggregates volumes rose less than initially anticipated due to project delays, now expected to contribute incremental volumes only in 2027, and residential demand is not expected to improve
positive_highlights: EBITDA grew 12% to $990 million with margin up 80 bps, and EBIT rose 19%, both outpacing ~8% net sales growth
Free cash flow from operations reached $723 million in the quarter, up 34%, and year-to-date nearly tripled to $1.4 billion; adjusted TTM conversion hit 62%
Project Cutting Edge delivered ~$60 million in recurring savings in the quarter, reaching 80% of the $475 million target, and net leverage fell to 1.8x, nearly half a turn lower since December
summary: CEMEX reported Q3 FY2026 net sales growth of approximately 8%, with EBITDA up 12% to $990 million (margin +80 bps) and EBIT up 19%, marking a fifth consecutive quarter of double-digit EBITDA and EBIT growth and margin expansion. Free cash flow from operations reached $723 million in the quarter, up 34%, and year-to-date nearly tripled to $1.4 billion; adjusted trailing 12-month conversion was 62%. Management reaffirmed full-year EBITDA guidance of 16%-17% YoY growth and said it expects to land near its 21% EBITDA margin target, while flagging Q4 headwinds of roughly $18 million in maintenance and $17 million in energy costs and noting higher 2027 energy inflation of mid-to-high single digits.

negative_highlights: Average coal sales price per ton fell 8.3% YoY to $53.93, with Appalachia pricing down 25.1% YoY to $62.35 on a higher Tunnel Ridge mix
Oil and gas average sales price per BOE declined 16.6% sequentially to $41.21 on lower realized crude and higher gas weighting
Barge and ocean freight logistics constraints could impede export volume growth beyond 2026; management said $125 API2 threshold needs to stabilize
positive_highlights: Coal segment adjusted EBITDA expense per ton improved 13.1% YoY and 7.9% sequentially to $35.64, widening the price-minus-expense spread to $18.29 from $16.19
Oil and gas royalty revenue hit a record $59.8 million with record BOE volumes of 1.45 million, up 61.3% YoY and 54.9% sequentially on AllDale III/IV
Distribution coverage rose to 1.76x with free cash flow of $198.6 million and net leverage of 0.78x; Mettiki reopening adds ~550,000 tons of 2027 production
summary: ARLP reported Q3 2026 revenue up 5.5% YoY to $603 million, net income up 46.8% to $139.6 million ($1.08/unit), and adjusted EBITDA up 26.3% to $233.9 million, with coal segment EBITDA up 18.6% YoY on 9.3 million tons sold (+7.4%). Cost performance drove the beat: segment adjusted EBITDA expense per ton fell 13.1% YoY to $35.64, widening the per-ton spread to $18.29 from $16.19 sequentially, and royalty revenue surged 52.5% YoY to $87.5 million on the first full quarter of AllDale III/IV. Full-year coal volume guidance was tightened to 34.5–35.5 million tons, raising the midpoint of the prior range, with price at $54.25–$54.75 and EBITDA expense per ton at $37.50–$38.50; 2027 guidance comes in February. The Mettiki mine is reopening under a new multi-year supply agreement with 2027 production ~550,000 tons above 2026.

negative_highlights: Net loss of $25.4 million and operating loss of $25.8 million with no product revenue
Cash of ~$79 million funds operations only into early 2027, before any phase III spend
All value hinges on the November ALTITUDE-AD readout; no efficacy or biomarker data disclosed this quarter
positive_highlights: R&D expense fell to $21.1 million from the prior year on lower manufacturing, materials and CRO costs tied to ALTITUDE-AD
OLE rollover of >95% of eligible patients and retention in the primary study exceeding expectations
ACU401 EBD bispecific showed up to 40-fold greater frontal cortex exposure in non-human primates versus unmodified ACU234
summary: Acumen reported a Q3 FY2026 net loss of $25.4 million and loss from operations of $25.8 million, with R&D of $21.1 million (down YoY on lower ALTITUDE-AD manufacturing, materials and CRO costs) and G&A of $4.7 million. Cash and marketable securities ended at approximately $79 million, expected to fund activities into early 2027. No revenue or EPS guidance was given; the key event is the ALTITUDE-AD phase II top-line readout expected in November, with management reiterating a ~30% iADRS slowing bar and low double-digit ARIA-E expectation. Management was confident on execution, citing >95% OLE rollover and high retention, but the quarter's substance is a pre-readout financial update.

negative_highlights: Wireless service revenue of just over $20.9 billion did not grow YoY in the quarter, with a return to growth only expected in Q4
positive_highlights: Raised FY2026 adjusted EPS growth guidance to 7%-7.5% from 6%-7% and free cash flow growth to approach 12% from 9%-10%
Adjusted EBITDA margin of 40.2% expanded 240 bps YoY to a reported high; adjusted EBITDA up 8% to $13.8 billion
Postpaid phone net adds up 820% YoY to 406,000 with cost of acquisition down 41% and retention cost down 30%, no free lines
summary: Verizon reported Q3 FY2026 total revenue of $34.3 billion, up 1.5% YoY, with mobility and broadband service revenue growth of 2.9% partially offset by a 9% decline in equipment revenue. Adjusted EPS of $1.31 rose 8.3% YoY and adjusted EBITDA margin hit a reported high of 40.2%, up 240 bps. Management raised FY2026 guidance on multiple fronts: adjusted EPS growth to 7%-7.5% from 6%-7%, free cash flow growth to approach 12% from 9%-10%, and postpaid phone net adds to 1.1-1.2 million. Free cash flow of $7.8 billion was the highest quarterly figure since 2020, and the company disclosed roughly $4 billion in signed AI Connect contracts, including a >$2 billion dark fiber deal with AWS.

negative_highlights: Interest expense rose 19% to $70 million and management flagged rising rates as a margin drag it offsets via APRs and fees
Return on managed assets only edged up to 0.9% from 0.8% despite the 28% portfolio growth
No numeric guidance provided, with the CEO noting Q4 is 'a little bit lighter' and only qualitative intent to grow strategically
positive_highlights: EPS up 50% YoY to $0.30 on net income up 42% to $7.0 million, with revenue rising 22% to $131.9 million
Originations of $815 million, a 35-year record and 108.5% above the $391 million prior-year quarter; nine-month volume of $2.11 billion already exceeds the prior full-year record of $2 billion
Total delinquency fell to 12.26% from 13.9% and annualized net charge-offs to 7.26% from 8.01%, with recovery rates rising to 32% from 28%
summary: Revenue rose 22% YoY to $131.9 million and Q3 EPS jumped 50% to $0.30 as pre-tax income grew 44% to $10.1 million. Originations of $815 million were a record, up 108.5% from $391 million, lifting the fair value portfolio 28% to $4.6 billion; delinquency fell to 12.26% from 13.9% and net charge-offs to 7.26% from 8.01%. Management gave no numeric guidance, citing a seasonally lighter Q4, but said it intends to keep growing strategically in 2027 and highlighted more than $1 billion of warehouse capacity for the first time. The quarter primarily reflects a much higher origination and portfolio base with improving credit, not a formal beat-and-raise against stated targets.

negative_highlights: Q4 EPS guidance of $0.62-0.70 is well below Q3's $0.90 (which included the $0.12 COLI gain), reflecting seasonal costs and holiday PTO.
Operating cash flow was $9.5 million, below expectations, due to a large client's payment delay, though management said it was resolved in early October.
Sequentially, gross margin declined 30 bps on lower direct-hire mix and higher healthcare costs; management also cited modest job declines in information and professional services per BLS data.
positive_highlights: Revenue of $357.8 million exceeded the high end of guidance, with technology revenue up 7.8% year-over-year and 2.5% sequentially on a billing-day basis.
Gross margin expanded 50 bps to 28.2% and flex gross margin rose 60 bps year-over-year, with the average technology bill rate at $91/hour and up for a second consecutive quarter.
Consulting Solutions reached record new contract award value and the highest pipeline conversion rate in its history, with AI-related pipelines up about 20% year-over-year.
summary: Kforce reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $357.8 million, up 7.5% year-over-year and above the high end of guidance, with technology revenue up 7.8%. EPS of $0.90 included a $0.12 COLI gain; excluding it, EPS was near the high end of guidance and up roughly 24% year-over-year. Gross margin expanded 50 bps to 28.2% and flex gross margin rose 60 bps year-over-year. Q4 guidance is $352-360 million revenue and $0.62-0.70 EPS, implying 7.2% year-over-year growth at the midpoint, roughly stable with Q3's growth rate against a tougher comp.

negative_highlights: Revenue grew only 7% YoY to ~$11M, and enterprise channel revenue was relatively flat YoY, reflecting reduced non-recurring revenue.
Q4 revenue guidance of $11.4M-$11.6M implies modest sequential growth as full-year range was narrowed rather than raised.
New Agentic Audits and SDK MCP products launched only in October with revenue impact not yet quantifiable, and management flagged needed customer education.
positive_highlights: Full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance raised to $13.4M-$13.6M from at least $12.7M, with Q4 annualized adjusted EBITDA run rate now expected above $17M versus prior $15M expectation.
Gross margin expanded over 550 bps to 83% (adjusted 88%) and adjusted EBITDA rose 58% YoY to $3.9M at a 35% margin.
Free cash flow of $3.5M, up $1.5M YoY, cash up $600K sequentially to $9.3M, plus a $15M buyback authorized.
summary: AudioEye reported Q3 FY2026 record revenue of ~$11M (up 7% YoY) with adjusted EBITDA of $3.9M, up 58% YoY at a 35% margin, GAAP net income of $1M or $0.08 per diluted share, and free cash flow of $3.5M. Gross margin expanded over 550 bps to 83%. Q4 revenue guidance is $11.4M-$11.6M and full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance was raised to $13.4M-$13.6M from at least $12.7M, implying ~50% growth and a Q4 annualized adjusted EBITDA run rate above $17M versus prior expectations of $15M. ARR grew 12% YoY to $43.3M with 130,000 customers, and the company announced a $15M share repurchase program.

negative_highlights: Q3 adjusted EBITDA is guided to only slightly above 22% of revenue versus 25.9% in Q2, due to unfavorable timing of costs including professional fees
Marriott PMS rollout is past 2,000 live properties but management said it has not reached the halfway mark on properties, rooms or revenue
Professional services revenue grew only 5.3% to $19.2 million and is expected to stay roughly flat in the second half
positive_highlights: Full-year revenue guidance raised to $374-$378 million from $368-$373 million, and subscription growth guidance raised to at least 34% from at least 32%
Subscription revenue grew 32.6% YoY to a record $44.2 million, the 20th consecutive quarter of at least 23% growth, with Q4 exit rate guided to 38%-39%
Adjusted EBITDA hit a record $24.1 million, or 25.9% of revenue, versus $16.4 million a year ago, and gross margin expanded to 64.6% from 61.7%
summary: Agilysys reported record Q2 FY2027 revenue of $93.4 million, up 17.7% YoY and 6.5% QoQ, with subscription revenue up 32.6% to a record $44.2 million (71% of recurring revenue). Adjusted EBITDA was a record $24.1 million at 25.9% of revenue, adjusted diluted EPS rose to $0.67 from $0.40, and gross margin expanded to 64.6% from 61.7%. Management raised full-year revenue guidance to $374-$378 million from $368-$373 million and subscription growth to at least 34% from at least 32%, with adjusted EBITDA guidance lifted to 25% of revenue from 24%. The Marriott PMS rollout is past 2,000 live properties and nearly complete on select service, but management said it is not yet at the halfway mark; the company booked a seven-figure multi-property competitive replacement win in HRC resort.

Bank of Hawaii reported Q3 FY2026 diluted EPS of $1.49 and net income of $64.3 million, up 0.7% and 1.4% linked quarter and up 24.2% and 20.5% YoY, with ROACE of 15.4%. NII rose $2.5 million to $156.1 million and NIM expanded 4 bps to 2.82%, the tenth consecutive quarter of expansion, though the deposit mix shift was negative for a second quarter and accelerated. Average deposits fell 0.8% (including an intentional ~$200 million runoff of high-cost public funds) while loans grew 0.6% (2.4% annualized); Q4 guidance is for normalized non-interest income of ~$44 million and expense of ~$112.5 million, with modest deposit growth expected to return. NPAs rose to 30 bps from 8 bps on a single commercial credit expected to resolve within a quarter with immaterial loss, and the board added $200 million to the buyback authorization alongside a $0.70 dividend.

negative_highlights: Reported VPG fell 1% to $3,286 on acquisition mix dilution, with Spinnaker closing early and contributing more tours at lower VPG
Travel and Membership EBITDA relies on cost cuts: $16 million annualized savings and ~300 employee reductions amid structural decline in exchange transaction propensity
2027 outlook points to higher ABS funding costs and a modest margin headwind from new-brand investment partially offsetting acquisition and G&A tailwinds
positive_highlights: Adjusted EPS of $2.21 rose 23% year-over-year and net income grew 16%
Full-year EBITDA guidance midpoint raised again, with gross VOI sales narrowed to the top of the range ($2.625-$2.675 billion)
Loan loss provision rate declined ~150 bps year-over-year and full-year provision outlook improved to ~20% from ~21%, with 2027 expected lower than 2026
summary: Revenue rose 5% to $1.1 billion, adjusted EBITDA grew 6% to $283 million with 20 bps of margin expansion, and adjusted EPS of $2.21 rose 23% year-over-year. Gross VOI sales increased 6% and tours rose 7%, though reported VPG of $3,286 declined 1% due to dilutive mix from the August 1 Spinnaker acquisition; organic VPG was up low single digits, in line with guidance. Management narrowed full-year gross VOI sales guidance to the top of the range ($2.625-$2.675 billion) and raised the EBITDA midpoint again ($1.07-$1.085 billion) and EPS guidance, while lowering the full-year loan loss provision outlook from ~21% to ~20%. The main offset was Travel and Membership, where revenue was flat at $150 million, segment EBITDA was $51 million, and a $16 million annualized cost program affecting roughly 300 employees was taken to align with ongoing exchange-to-travel-club mix shift.

negative_highlights: Levered free cash flow guidance cut to slightly positive from more than $50 million as net rental fleet investment rises $35 million at the midpoint to $210-$230 million

STEM third-party revenue fell 5% YoY, with more than $20 million of sales delayed by a chassis vendor recall and hailstorm damage, and backlog of $342 million at 3.8 months sits below the 4-6 month target range
Total revenue grew only 3% YoY to $495 million, well below the 16% EBITDA growth as STEM margins compressed to 8.3% on mix
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA of $111 million rose 16% YoY and margin expanded ~250 bps to 22.4%, the fourth consecutive quarter above 20%
Full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance raised for the third time to $447.5-$460 million (17%-20% YoY growth), with SER revenue guidance lifted to $870-$890 million
Rental KPIs at records: utilization 81.5% (+220 bps YoY), average OEC on rent up more than 10% to ~$1.39 billion, and rental gross margin ~79% versus a mid-70s prior expectation
summary: Q3 revenue was $495 million, up 3% YoY, with adjusted EBITDA of $111 million up 16% and margin of 22.4% (up ~250 bps); GAAP EPS was $0.01 versus a year-ago loss. SER revenue rose 18% to $223 million with 54.6% segment margin and record rental KPIs (81.5% utilization, $1.39 billion average OEC on rent, 39.4% yield), while STEM third-party revenue fell 5% due to capacity redirected to the rental fleet, a chassis recall, and hailstorm damage that delayed $20 million-plus of sales. Management raised full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance for the third time to $447.5-$460 million and lifted SER revenue guidance to $870-$890 million, but cut the levered free cash flow outlook to slightly positive from more than $50 million on a $35 million increase to net rental fleet investment ($210-$230 million). Net leverage improved to 3.7x and management reiterated a below-3x target for 2027 with double-digit EBITDA growth expected.

negative_highlights: Net interest margin fell 19 bps to 407 bps, with 17 bps attributed to $205 million of higher average cash balances from temporary deposits
Non-performing loans increased to 70 bps of total loans after a $1.5 million land loan was placed on non-accrual

Non-interest income dropped to $1.7 million from $3.1 million in Q2, which had included $1.3 million of BOLI death benefit proceeds; expenses rose $1.3 million excluding the prior-quarter litigation settlement
positive_highlights: Diluted EPS rose to $0.94 from $0.71 in Q2; net income increased to $10.2 million with ROA of 1.42%
Loans grew approximately $58 million, or 10% annualized, and were up 17% over the past year, driven by C&I, multifamily, and owner-occupied CRE
Core deposit growth of approximately $76 million excluding temporary and brokered deposits, with cost of interest-bearing deposits down 9 bps to 97 bps
summary: Avidbank reported Q3 FY2026 net income of $10.2 million and diluted EPS of $0.94, up from $0.71 in Q2, with ROA of 1.42% and an efficiency ratio below 50%. Net interest income rose $2 million to $28.7 million, but NIM fell 19 bps to 407 bps, largely due to $205 million of higher average cash balances from a temporary $270 million deposit. Loans grew about $58 million (10% annualized, +17% YoY) with broad-based C&I, multifamily, and owner-occupied CRE contributions; non-performing loans ticked up to 70 bps after a $1.5 million land loan was placed on non-accrual, though net charge-offs were near zero. Management gave limited explicit guidance, expecting Q4 expenses flattish to slightly up, Q4 loan pipelines healthy but construction payoffs a wild card, and an asset-sensitive balance sheet to benefit from the September rate increase.

negative_highlights: Reported operating income fell 61% and net income fell 71% to $1.2 billion, including a $1.9 billion del-desiran partial impairment after the HARBOR Phase III miss
Pelacarsen ORION-4 Phase III did not meet its primary endpoint, and the company flagged pressure in IgAN positioning against anti-APRILs with Vanrafia and Fabhalta 'in a state of flux'
Q4 core margin guided to decline versus Q3 on year-end spend phasing, higher royalties, and lower Xolair-related other income from U.S. biosimilars; Pluvicto HSPC launch uptake pushed into 2027
positive_highlights: Core operating margin expanded 2 percentage points to 41.6% of net sales on gross margin improvement and SG&A productivity, with SG&A down 7% while sales grew 4%
Full-year 2026 core operating income guidance raised to in line to low double digit growth from a prior low single-digit decline
Priority brands up 29% with Kisqali +37%, Scemblix +67%, Leqvio +63%, Kesimpta +22%; Rhapsido peak sales guidance raised to over $4 billion
summary: Q3 FY2026 net sales rose 4% in constant currency to $14.5 billion, core operating income grew 10% to $6 billion, and core operating margin expanded 2 points to 41.6% of sales, while core EPS rose 8% to $2.46. Full-year 2026 core operating income guidance was raised to in line to low double-digit growth from a prior low single-digit decline, with net sales guidance unchanged at low single-digit growth. Reported operating income fell 61% and net income fell 71% to $1.2 billion, driven by a $1.9 billion del-desiran impairment after the HARBOR Phase III miss and by the pelacarsen ORION-4 primary endpoint failure. Priority brands grew 29%, led by Kisqali +37%, Scemblix +67%, Leqvio +63%, Kesimpta +22%, and Pluvicto +20%.

negative_highlights: Q4 revenue guided to $225M-$255M, with note-through expected to decline ~10% QoQ and an intentional ~$20M undershipment into channel.
Non-GAAP gross margin down to 45.0% in Q3 from 46.8% in Q2 and guided to 40-43% in Q4 on mix, battery price adjustments, and freight.
U.S. note-through down ~35% YoY and management stated it sees no meaningful recovery in U.S. demand; Q3 free cash flow was negative $11.4M due to working capital timing.
positive_highlights: U.S. commercial note-through grew ~50% QoQ as IQ9 commercial microinverters ramped; commercial revenue expected to grow from ~$30M in 2026 to over $100M in 2027.
Netherlands battery activations rose 23% QoQ after 102% QoQ growth in Q2, with ~$2B retrofit opportunity across ~500K Enphase solar-only customers as net metering ends in 2026.
Propel prepaid lease expanded to 13 states with ~350 installers (from 290 in Q2) and weekly originations above 300 (from ~200), with SolSource raising $300M of capital at ~71% battery attach.
summary: Q3 revenue of $293.3M (up ~1% QoQ, including $85M of safe harbor) came in at the low end of guidance, and non-GAAP gross margin fell to 45.0% from 46.8%. Q4 guidance of $225M-$255M was deliberately set ~$20M below expected ~$210M of watch-through to reduce channel inventory, and implied non-GAAP gross margin steps down further to 40-43% on product mix, battery price adjustments, and freight costs. U.S. watch-through rose 5% QoQ but fell ~35% YoY; Europe revenue declined ~11% QoQ. Management leaned heavily on 2027 growth drivers (G5 battery +50%, commercial to over $100M), while stating it sees no meaningful recovery in U.S. demand.

negative_highlights: Personal Insurance written premium declined 4%, with auto down 9% amid intense new-business competition
Middle and large business underlying combined ratio rose to 99.5, with workers' comp frequency and non-cat property each contributing just under 4 points to the increase
Group disability loss ratio increased 5.7 points to 76.3 on higher claim incidence and less favorable LTD recoveries; group life rose 3.6 points to 77.8
positive_highlights: Small business written premium grew 7% at an 85.2 underlying combined ratio, improving 4.6 points YoY on lower non-cat property losses and a lower expense ratio
Net investment income rose 13% to $850M, helped by 10.2% annualized limited partnership returns
Common quarterly dividend raised 12% to $0.67 per share; 3.4M shares repurchased for $475M with $4.37B remaining authorization
summary: Core earnings of $956M ($3.50/diluted share) with a trailing 12-month core earnings ROE of 17.9%; Business Insurance written premium grew 6% with an underlying combined ratio of 90.1, and book value per share ex-AOCI rose 12% from year-end. Results carried real blemishes: Personal Insurance written premium fell 4% (auto down 9%), middle-and-large underlying combined ratio deteriorated to 99.5 on higher non-cat property and workers' comp frequency, and group disability loss ratio rose 5.7 points to 76.3. Management framed the workers' comp frequency increase as a 2026 step change rather than a persistent trend, flagged incremental competition in small and middle market (small new business non-positive for the first time in ~20+ quarters), and announced a 12% dividend increase to $0.67 plus a $475M buyback. No explicit EPS or combined-ratio guidance was given; the Equitable Employee Benefits acquisition closed with ~$500M annual premium and is expected to be modestly dilutive in 2027 ex-amortization.

negative_highlights: Q3 cash flow used by operations was $3.7 billion, reflecting over $3 billion of Medicaid pass-through payouts
2026 earnings include $0.50 not expected to recur, and 2027 faces Medicaid OB3 membership attrition, California UIS population removal, and a PDP margin reset toward 2%-3%
Medicare Advantage membership expected down year-over-year in 2027 as footprint is narrowed; Stars at ~42% of members at/above 3.5 Stars with only 10% in four stars
positive_highlights: FY2026 adjusted EPS guidance raised to >$5.20 from >$4.80
Medicare Advantage now on track for breakeven in 2026, a year ahead of plan; Medicare HBR 93.8% with PDP pre-tax margin guided to mid-to-high 3% from >3%
Marketplace pre-tax margin guided to top of 4.5%-5% range (5%), a ~600 bps improvement from -1% in 2025; adjusted SG&A ratio fell to 6.5% from 7.0% a year ago
summary: Centene reported Q3 FY2026 premium and service revenue of $45.1 billion and adjusted diluted EPS of $0.58, ahead of expectations, with consolidated HBR of 92.7% better than planned. Full-year 2026 adjusted EPS guidance was raised to greater than $5.20 from greater than $4.80, driven by Medicare/PDP strength, Marketplace margin at the top of the 4.5%-5% range, and lower interest expense (~$610M midpoint). Medicare Advantage is now expected to reach breakeven in 2026, a year early, and management guided to 2027 EPS growth off both a ~$4.70 jump-off point and the revised $5.20 base. Marketplace moved from a -1% pre-tax margin in 2025 to a forecasted 5% in 2026.

negative_highlights: Active equities posted more than $12 billion of net outflows concentrated in the largest mutual funds
Taxable fixed income retail saw more than $3 billion of net outflows, and management said it may take several quarters for retail to return at scale
Bernstein Private Wealth net flows were negative in the quarter, though net new assets still grew 2% annualized
positive_highlights: FY2026 performance fee outlook raised to $135-$150 million from $115-$135 million, with private markets now $60-$65 million and public markets $75-$85 million
Private markets AUM exceeded $105 billion, surpassing the $90-$100 billion target more than a year ahead of the original 2027 commitment
Institutional net inflows hit a record ~$16 billion, the second consecutive positive quarter, with flows positive even excluding the ~$12 billion CML mandate
summary: Adjusted EPU of $0.88 rose 2% YoY and 7% sequentially on adjusted net revenues of $904 million (+2% YoY and QoQ), with base fees up 3% YoY to $845 million and adjusted operating margin of 33.5%, up from 33.0% in Q2. Full-year performance fee guidance was raised to $135-150 million from $115-135 million, and the non-compensation expense outlook was narrowed to $620-635 million from $620-640 million, while the 48.5% comp ratio and 5-6% tax rate were reaffirmed. Firm-wide net inflows approached $7 billion (3% annualized organic growth) on roughly $12 billion of Equitable CML onboarding, but active equities saw over $12 billion of net outflows and taxable fixed income retail lost more than $3 billion. Private markets AUM surpassed $105 billion, ahead of the 2027 target, and $100 billion of Corebridge assets remain to be onboarded over time.

negative_highlights: Device Solutions and Networked Solutions revenue each declined 1% on a constant currency basis
Free cash flow fell to $96 million from $113 million a year ago on working capital growth and higher tax payments
Full-year revenue range was narrowed to $2.37-$2.385 billion with segment revenue declines in two of four segments
positive_highlights: Non-GAAP operating income grew 20% while revenue grew only 3%, and adjusted gross margin expanded 350 bps to 41.3%
Full-year EPS outlook was raised to $6.72-$6.82 with Q4 revenue guided up 10% year-over-year at the midpoint
Bookings rose 27% year-over-year to $482 million, and annual recurring revenue grew roughly 25%, accelerating from 21% last quarter
summary: Itron reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $599 million, at the top end of its outlook and up 3% year-over-year, with adjusted gross margin of 41.3% (up 350 bps) and record adjusted EBITDA of $115 million (19% of revenue). Non-GAAP EPS of $1.94 rose from $1.54, and non-GAAP operating income grew 20% on the 3% revenue growth. The company narrowed full-year revenue guidance to $2.37-$2.385 billion and raised full-year non-GAAP EPS to $6.72-$6.82, with Q4 revenue guided to $621-$636 million (up 10% at the midpoint) and Q4 EPS of $1.70-$1.80. Bookings were $482 million, up 27% year-over-year, with backlog of $4.3 billion; free cash flow of $96 million was down from $113 million a year ago on working capital and higher taxes.

negative_highlights: In-line leased occupancy slipped ~40bps to 95.1%, attributed to newly acquired assets running in the low-90s
Q4 same-center NOI faces a tougher recovery-income comparison versus the prior-year quarter, implying moderation from the 5.3% Q3 pace
Higher G&A expected in Q4 versus Q3, weighing on NAREIT and core FFO growth in the quarter
positive_highlights: Record high comparable renewal rent spreads of 25.2%, with new lease spreads of 26.3%
Full-year guidance midpoints raised: same-center NOI to 3.75% (top of 3%-4% range), core FFO per share growth to 6.5%, NAREIT FFO growth to 6.3%
New $350M three-year unsecured term loan priced at SOFR+80bps, 30bps below the repaid loan, with ~$950M total liquidity and no meaningful maturities until 2030
summary: PECO reported Q3 FY2026 same-center NOI growth of 5.3% and core FFO per share of $0.71, up 9.2% YoY, with NAREIT FFO of $0.69 per share up 7.8%. Management raised the midpoint of full-year core FFO per share guidance to reflect 6.5% growth and NAREIT FFO to 6.3%, and now expects same-center NOI at 3.75% (top end of the original 3%-4% range). Renewal rent spreads hit a record 25.2%, new lease spreads were 26.3%, portfolio retention was 92.2% and leased occupancy 97.5%. Gross acquisition guidance was previously raised on October 1 to $600M-$700M, with $519M acquired YTD and $250M under contract or awarded.

negative_highlights: First-time R&D ($160–170M) and SG&A ($270–280M) guidance implies materially elevated fourth-quarter spend, including pre-commercial KPL-387 manufacturing costs.
Company declined to share first-time versus repeat prescriber breakdown and has not updated the 80/20 first-versus-second recurrence prescription split.
positive_highlights: ARCALYST revenue grew 58% year-over-year to $286 million, up roughly $42.5 million quarter-over-quarter.
Full-year 2026 revenue guidance raised to $1.045–1.050 billion, now above the $1 billion threshold.
Penetration into the 14,000 multiple-recurrence population rose to 23% at quarter-end from 18% at end of Q4 of the prior year.
summary: ARCALYST revenue grew 58% year-over-year to $286 million in Q3, with penetration into the 14,000 multiple-recurrence population rising to 23%. Kiniksa raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $1.045–1.050 billion, exceeding the $1 billion milestone, and provided first-time R&D ($160–170M) and SG&A ($270–280M) guidance. Operating income reached $54.2 million and net income $47.3 million, with $568.8 million in cash after roughly $43 million in quarterly net cash generation; the KPL-387 phase III pivotal data readout is guided to H2 2027.

negative_highlights: Specialty Distribution organic revenue fell 0.8% versus prior guidance of +2% to +4% for the second half, and Q4 organic is guided down 2%-4%
Adjusted EBITDAC margin contracted 200 bps to 34.6%, with over half from ~$29 million lower interest income versus the prior-year cash-held-for-Accession period
Specialty faces structural pricing pressure: commercial earthquake terms down further, E&S property rates down 15%-35%, and management sees CAT property rates potentially down 10%-20% into 2027
positive_highlights: Accession EBITDAC synergy estimate for 2026 raised to approximately $50 million from $30-40 million, with the 2028 run-rate target lifted to $175 million from $150 million
Retail organic growth of 2.6% came in above the top end of expectations and retail EBITDAC margin expanded 10 bps
Board raised the dividend 9%, the 33rd consecutive annual increase; $750 million of shares repurchased through nine months including $250 million in Q3
summary: Brown & Brown reported Q3 revenue of $1.7 billion, up 7.4%, but organic growth was just 1.2% (1.5% including contingents), adjusted EBITDAC margin fell 200 bps to 34.6%, and adjusted EPS rose only 1.9% to $1.07. Retail outperformed with 2.6% organic growth, while Specialty Distribution organic revenue fell 0.8%, below the previously stated +2% to +4% second-half expectation, on admitted-market encroachment, commercial earthquake pricing pressure, lender-placed onboarding delays, and light flood claims. Q4 guidance calls for Specialty organic decline of 2%-4% (including $8-12 million of non-recurring/timing items) and Retail organic of 2%-3%, with 2027 guided to 2%-4% Retail and 1%-3% Specialty. Accession synergies were raised to ~$50 million for 2026 from $30-40 million and the 2028 run-rate target lifted to $175 million from $150 million, and the dividend was raised 9%.

negative_highlights: Management acknowledged shares trade at a meaningful discount to book and that the market appears to price in an earnings or dividend cut
SFR pilot is only ~10% leased with ~6 months projected to rent the portfolio, and the ~5% as-rented yield sits roughly at the financing cost, with peak carry friction in Q4
Leadership repeatedly declined to quantify freed Lennar priority capital ('rather not give you a number because it is still fluid') and gave no AFFO extrapolation from the 90% payout
positive_highlights: Pro forma AFFO guidance of $0.82-$0.84 for Q4 and year-end AFFO run rate above the $3.30 per share prior guidance, a sixth consecutive quarterly AFFO increase
Weighted average yield on non-Lennar agreements rose to 10.8% from 10.6%, with ~11% expected in Q4 on higher SOFR and Dream Finders yields
$250 million share repurchase authorized, to be funded from earnings otherwise distributed plus unused Lennar priority capital, with no borrowing to fund buybacks
summary: Millrose reported Q4 AFFO guidance of $0.82-$0.84 per share and a year-end AFFO run rate above the prior $3.30 per share guidance, marking a sixth consecutive quarterly AFFO increase; Q3 included roughly $1.3 billion of new investments and development funding and $800 million of net homesite takedown proceeds. Invested capital outside the Lennar Master Program Agreement rose $521 million to about $3.4 billion, with other-agreement yields up to 10.8% from 10.6% and expected at about 11% in Q4, and the October Dream Finders/Beazer deal added roughly $1.1 billion of funding. Management spent most of the call defending a ~$120 million net SFR pilot (1,233 homes, ~10% leased, ~10% above underwritten rents) against conflict-of-interest criticism, and announced a shift to distributing 90% of earnings with the remaining 10% directed to a new $250 million buyback authorization. The dividend/buyback change and repeated pushback on market skepticism are the main tone-setting changes versus the prior period.

negative_highlights: Net income fell 5% QoQ due to normalization of transaction-driven fee income, higher operating expenses (+7% QoQ to $26.6 million), and increased provisions ($10.4 million vs. $8.6 million).
NIM of 2.30% included a temporary benefit from early loan prepayments about 2x-3x higher than in prior periods, and the Panama transaction is expected to dilute NIM in Q4.
Underlying lending spreads remain under pressure amid competition for high-quality assets, with full-year NIM guided to ~2.25% (roughly 5 bps compression).
positive_highlights: Net interest income reached a record $79.8 million, up 9% QoQ and 18% YoY.
Commercial portfolio hit a record $15 billion, up 15% QoQ and 38% YoY; even excluding the $1 billion Panama sovereign loan, growth was 7% QoQ and 29% YoY, versus original guidance of 13-15%.
Stage 2 exposures declined to $82 million (0.5% of the portfolio) from $162 million, with no new impaired migrations and reserve coverage rising to 1.4x.
summary: Bladex reported Q3 2026 net income of $63.2 million, up 15% YoY but down 5% QoQ, with record net interest income of $79.8 million (up 9% QoQ, 18% YoY) and a commercial portfolio of $15 billion (up 15% QoQ). NIM expanded six basis points to 2.30%, aided by a temporary prepayment benefit and lower funding costs. Full-year commercial portfolio growth guidance is now ~35% (~25% excluding the one-off $1 billion Panama sovereign loan), well above the original 13-15%; NIM guidance is ~2.25% with ~5 bps compression, and the efficiency ratio is expected near 27%, slightly better than prior guidance. The quarter showed strong volume-led growth with stable asset quality (stage 2 down to $82 million), but underlying lending spreads remain under pressure and Q4 NIM will be diluted by the Panama transaction.

negative_highlights: Total company net cash flow was negative $11 billion, driven by select active equity strategies, and management expects near-term pressure to continue
Significant variances (variable investment income and encaje) cut after-tax earnings by $59 million or $0.27 per share, holding GAAP-basis operating EPS growth to 6%

SMB Well-Being Index sentiment fell to levels similar to the April 2025 tariff shock, and the Beam acquisition is running at a modest loss (~$1-2M headwind) with earnings drag expected to persist into 1H 2027
positive_highlights: Year-to-date adjusted EPS growth of 12% at the high end of the 9%-12% target range, with 10% YTD pre-tax operating earnings growth on 5% revenue growth and 120 bps of margin expansion
