Life operating margin expanded 420 bps YoY to 16.4%, above the top end of the target range, on improved mortality frequency and severity; RIS operating margin of 42% exceeded the high end of range

Returned $429 million to shareholders in the quarter ($250M buybacks, $179M dividends), over $1.2 billion YTD, with $1.5 billion of excess and available capital and a dividend raised $0.01 to $0.85 (8% higher YoY)
summary: PFG reported Q3 FY2026 non-GAAP operating earnings of $482 million, up 2% YoY, with EPS of $2.22 up 6%; excluding $59 million ($0.27/share) of significant variances from variable investment income and encaje, EPS was $2.49, up 7%. Year-to-date adjusted EPS growth of 12% sits at the high end of the 9%-12% target, and management reaffirmed full-year capital deployment of $1.5-$1.8 billion with buybacks trending to the low end due to the Beam acquisition. The clear negative was total company net cash flow of negative $11 billion, concentrated in active equity, with management flagging continued near-term pressure, partially offset by $800 million of private markets and $500 million of active ETF inflows. Segment margins were solid (RIS 42%, Life up 420 bps to 16.4%, International Pension up 240 bps to the high end of range), but an SMB sentiment survey showed caution similar to April 2025 tariff-era lows.

HSBC reported Q3 revenue up 5% YoY to $18.7bn and profit before tax up 10% to $10bn excluding notable items, with EPS ex-notables up 17%, cost growth of 1% on a target basis and annualized ROTE of 18.8% year to date. Banking NII rose $0.6bn YoY to $11.7bn, helped by $0.1bn of one-offs, hedge reinvestment and day count, and the full-year NII guidance of at least $46bn plus the ~45bp cost-of-risk guidance and ~1% cost growth target were all reiterated unchanged. The bank announced a further buyback of up to $1bn and flagged an estimated 40-50bp Basel 3.1 capital benefit from January 2027, while CET1 slipped 20bp QoQ to 13.9%. The key change versus prior periods was deposit mix pressure, with Hong Kong time deposits rising about 2pp to 38% and U.K. deposit competition intensifying, plus a $2.2bn cumulative revenue drag from disposals split across 2026-2028.

negative_highlights: Same-property NOI declined 6.7% GAAP and 2.8% cash in the quarter, with 2027 same-property performance guided to remain negative on occupancy.
Recognized $638 million of real estate impairments, with the two largest totaling 75% of the balance, tied to lab conversion projects at 421 Park Drive and a four-building Palo Alto office project.

Guidance points to temporary occupancy pressure in the first half of 2027 from 1.4 million sq ft of lease expirations with 9-24 months of downtime and $101 million of expiring rent, plus potential tenant wind-downs.
positive_highlights: Leasing volume of 1,236,000 sq ft was the highest in seven quarters, including 451,000 sq ft of previously vacant space, the second largest quarterly total in company history.
Delivered 529,000 sq ft of development and redevelopment space that was 84% occupied, expected to generate $40 million of incremental annual NOI.

$1.7 billion of capital was raised since June 30, including $1 billion of 7.25% junior subordinated notes that received 50% equity credit, and $2.6 billion of completed plus pending dispositions exceed the $1.9 billion midpoint target by $720 million.
summary: Alexandria reported Q3 2026 FFO per share as adjusted of $1.54 and reaffirmed the midpoint of 2026 FFO guidance at $6.40, tightening the range to +/- $0.02, while lowering the realized investment gains guidance by $10 million at the midpoint to $65 million. Leasing volume was 1.236 million sq ft, the highest in seven quarters, including 451,000 sq ft of previously vacant space, but same-property NOI fell 6.7% GAAP and 2.8% cash, with occupancy at 87.1%, up 20 bps sequentially. The company recorded $638 million of real estate impairments, largely tied to lab conversion projects at 421 Park Drive and Palo Alto, and guided to temporary occupancy pressure in the first half of 2027 from 1.4 million sq ft of expirations with 9-24 months of downtime, with same-property performance expected to remain negative in 2027 and occupancy growth only expected in 2028.

negative_highlights: Commonwealth retention cut to ~83% from ~85% last quarter (original underwriting 90%), reducing run-rate EBITDA to ~$415 million
Client cash balances fell $300 million QoQ to $56.6 billion, with October organic growth guided to ~3% and cash down ~$1.2 billion on advisory fee timing
Payout rate rose ~50 bps to 88% and is guided up another ~40 bps in Q4; TA rates remain elevated from sustained competitor aggression
positive_highlights: Record adjusted EPS of $5.97, up 15% from a year ago, with adjusted pre-tax margin of ~38.6%
Organic net new assets of $29 billion (5% annualized), the best core growth rate in over a year, plus $24 billion in recruited assets
Core G&A of $532 million came in below the low end of the outlook range, and full-year guidance range was narrowed to $2.140-$2.160 billion
summary: LPL reported record adjusted EPS of $5.97, up 15% YoY, with gross profit of $1.662 billion (up $44 million sequentially) and an adjusted pre-tax margin of ~38.6%. Organic net new assets were $29 billion (5% annualized), the best core rate in over a year, with total client assets of $2.6 trillion up slightly QoQ as market headwinds offset organic growth. Commonwealth retention now expected at ~83% (down from ~85% last quarter), yielding run-rate EBITDA of ~$415 million (~8x multiple) by Q4 2027. Management narrowed 2026 core G&A to $2.140-$2.160 billion and repurchased ~$300 million of stock, with another $300 million planned in Q4.

negative_highlights: Automotive OEM organic revenue fell 2% with operating margin down 170 bps on resin inflation and price-cost timing lag
Construction Products organic revenue fell 1% and operating margin declined 170 bps to 29.9% on near-term price-cost headwinds
Management declined to quantify Q3/Q4 price-cost basis points citing a dynamic 4%-5% raw material inflation environment
positive_highlights: Test & Measurement and Electronics organic growth of 16% with electronics up 31% and segment operating margin expanding 330 bps to 28.7%
Full-year GAAP EPS guidance raised $0.05 to a midpoint of $11.50, the third increase of the year, with total revenue growth guidance up 50 bps to 4.5%-5.5%
Welding grew 7% organic (15% ex-tornado) with orders running well ahead of revenue, and Polymers & Fluids grew 8% with margin up 280 bps to 31.3%
summary: ITW reported Q3 organic growth of 3.8% (about 4.8% ex-tornado) with total revenue up 4.4%, operating margin expanding 40 bps to 27.8%, and GAAP EPS of $3.00, up 7% despite a ~$0.10 tax headwind. Full-year GAAP EPS guidance was raised $0.05 to a narrowed $11.45-$11.55 midpoint of $11.50 (10% growth), the third raise of the year, while operating margin guidance held at 26.5%-27.5% and organic growth stayed 3%-4% (implying 5%+ in Q4). Key drivers were Test & Measurement and Electronics up 16% (electronics +31%) and Welding up 7% (15% ex-tornado), offset by declines in Automotive OEM (-2%), Construction Products (-1%), and Specialty Products (-1%).

negative_highlights: Concrete, pavement and mortar revenue fell 19.7% to PEN 65.6 million as Yanacocha, Motupe and Piura Airport deliveries ended
2027 volume growth guided to only about 4% and explicitly contingent on El Niño strength
No dividend decision from the Board and no buyback plan, versus dividends announced in October in each of the prior two years
positive_highlights: EBITDA rose 45.1% to PEN 233.1 million with margin expanding 7 percentage points to 34.9%
Net income increased 69.8% to PEN 131 million and cement gross margin reached 50%
summary: Pacasmayo reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of PEN 667.4 million, up 16.3% YoY, on a 14.2% volume increase in cement, concrete and precast. EBITDA rose 45.1% to PEN 233.1 million with margin expanding 7 percentage points to 34.9%, net income up 69.8% to PEN 131 million, and cement segment gross margin at 50%. Concrete/pavement/mortar revenue fell 19.7% to PEN 65.6 million after the Yanacocha, Motupe and Piura Airport deliveries concluded, though segment margin expanded 21 points to 19.8%. Management guided to roughly 4% volume growth in 2027, contingent on El Niño strength, and stated no dividend decision, no buyback plan, and no Holcim synergy benefits yet reflected in results.

negative_highlights: Q4 EBITDAR margin guided to ~20%, down from 25.3% in Q3, on a fuel assumption of $4.40/gal versus $3.67 in Q3, with fuel recapture described as continuing at the same trend
CASM rose 26% YoY to 9.97 cents, driven by a 57% increase in economic fuel cost per gallon, and Q4 CASM ex fuel is guided up to ~6.50 cents including ~0.4 cents of non-recurring costs
Net loss of $26 million in the quarter; full-year 2026 EBITDAR margin guided to ~21%, below the Q3 level, primarily on higher fuel
positive_highlights: EBITDAR margin of 25.3% beat the 22% guidance by more than three percentage points despite fuel averaging $3.67/gal versus the $3.50 assumption
TRASM rose 19% YoY to 10.31 cents, above guidance, with average base fares up 26% and consolidated revenue up 32% to over $1 billion
CASM ex fuel of 6.23 cents outperformed the 6.35 cent guidance; fleet plan reduce exposure note lease liabilities by ~$360 million and cuts 2027 lease payments by ~$50 million
summary: Volaris exceeded Q3 FY2026 guidance: TRASM rose 19% to 10.31 cents (above guidance) and CASM ex fuel came in at 6.23 cents versus 6.35 cents guided, driving an EBITDAR margin of 25.3% versus 22% guidance despite fuel at $3.67/gal versus $3.50 assumed. Revenue surpassed $1 billion for the first time, up 32% YoY, with transborder revenue up 53%, positive EBIT of $34 million (3.3% margin), and a net loss of $26 million narrowed nearly 80% sequentially. Q4 guidance calls for ~4% ASM growth, TRASM of ~10.90 cents, CASM ex fuel of ~6.50 cents, and EBITDAR margin of ~20%, driven by a higher $4.40/gal fuel assumption; full-year 2026 EBITDAR margin is now ~21%. Management also detailed a fleet rightsizing to ~137 aircraft by end-2027, cutting lease liabilities roughly $360 million and lease payments about $50 million in 2027, alongside a $300 million undrawn revolver.

negative_highlights: Total company retail consumption declined 8.4% in Q4; net sales fell 9.7% to $333.3 million
Atkins retail takeaway fell 22.6% and household penetration dropped ~210 bps to 8.3%; OWYN takeaway fell 7% versus -1.3% last quarter
FY2027 net sales guided down 13%-17% and adjusted EBITDA down 9%-14%, with Q1 net sales down 19%-22% and Q1 adjusted EBITDA down 28%-33%
positive_highlights: Gross margin of 34.0% was the strongest of the fiscal year despite ongoing inflation and was guided up 250-300 bps in FY2027
Quest salty consumption grew ~13% with Dill Pickle launch exceeding expectations; Quest household penetration rose ~50 bps to 20.2%
Cash flow from operations was ~$181 million versus $178.5 million prior year; net debt/EBITDA ~0.9x after $50 million debt reduction and $213 million of FY2026 buybacks
summary: Q4 FY2026 net sales fell 9.7% to $333.3 million with GAAP gross margin down 30 bps to 34.0% and adjusted EBITDA down 13.2% to $57.5 million; management called results modestly ahead of plan but well below long-term expectations. FY2027 guidance calls for net sales to decline 13%-17% and adjusted EBITDA to decline 9%-14%, with Q1 net sales down 19%-22% and Q1 adjusted EBITDA down 28%-33%, the weakest quarter of the year. Gross margin is guided up 250-300 bps on pricing and productivity, and watching/marketing is guided up ~80 bps as marketing rises ~90 bps toward the ~10% of sales aspiration. The sequential step-down from Q4 to the FY2027 outlook is the key change, driven by a near-double-digit price increase, elasticities above one, and distribution losses including lower club rotations.

negative_highlights: Revenue of $236.1 million came in slightly below the midpoint of prior guidance (~$2 million miss) on supply constraints and pushouts
Q4 revenue guided to $215-225 million, a sequential decline from Q3
Higher commodity costs continue as a gross margin headwind versus prior year
positive_highlights: Adjusted EPS of $1.39 rose 54% YoY and exceeded the high end of guidance
Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 300 bps to 20.2%, the highest in five years
Free cash flow of $35.4 million and $9.3 million of share repurchases in the quarter
summary: Q3 FY2026 sales were $236.1 million, up 9% YoY (including a $2.4 million FX benefit), with adjusted EPS of $1.39 (+54%, above the high end of guidance) and adjusted EBITDA of $47.7 million at a 20.2% margin, up 300 bps and the highest in five years. Gross margin was 34.2%, up 70 bps despite higher commodity costs, and free cash flow was $35.4 million with $9.3 million of buybacks. Q4 guidance calls for sales of $215-225 million (~9% YoY growth at the midpoint, down sequentially on seasonality), gross margin of 32.5-33.5%, and adjusted EPS of $0.90-$1.10 versus $0.89 a year ago. Management noted a slight revenue miss to the prior guidance midpoint (~$2 million) from supply constraints and pushouts, while design-win momentum and commentary on data center, battery, and EMI opportunities were positive.

negative_highlights: Reported 45.0% gross margin includes a $2.5 million IEEPA refund and $3.5 million free-trade-zone benefit that will not recur, leaving underlying margin roughly flat
Wholesale gross margin declined 90 bps to 39.2% on product and brand mix, and container pricing worsened in Q3
Georgia Boot sales declined YoY on difficult comparisons and cautious field conditions; commercial military sales were below plan on raw-material shortages
positive_highlights: Revenue rose 13.3% to $138.8 million, an acceleration from Q2's 12% and highest growth in more than three years
Full-year revenue guidance raised to approximately +10.5% from +8.5%, with reported EPS guidance raised to approximately $5.30 from approximately $5
Retail segment sales up 20% to $35.4 million and gross margin expanded 480 bps to 45.0%; excluding $6.0 million of one-time tariff and FTZ benefits, gross margin was still 40.7% vs. 40.2% prior
summary: Rocky Brands reported Q3 FY2026 net sales up 13.3% YoY to $138.8 million, with wholesale +11.8% to $99.6 million and retail +20% to $35.4 million, and GAAP diluted EPS of $1.69 versus $0.96 a year ago. Gross margin expanded to 45.0% from 40.2%, though $6.0 million of one-time tariff and free-trade-zone benefits lifted the result; excluding those, Q3 gross margin was 40.7%. Management raised full-year revenue guidance to approximately +10.5% from +8.5% and lifted reported EPS guidance to approximately $5.30 from approximately $5, while normalized EPS remains approximately $4.00. Guidance implies roughly 8% Q4 revenue growth with retail moderating on tough prior-year DTC comparisons and contract manufacturing down a couple million dollars as military contracts wind down.

Intapp reported FQ1 FY2027 subscription revenue of $125.5M, up 29% YoY and accelerating from 27% in FQ4, with total revenue of $161.3M, up 16% YoY, dampened by license revenue of $23M, down 21% YoY on shortening on-prem contract durations. Non-GAAP operating margin was 22%, up roughly seven points, non-GAAP EPS was $0.44 versus $0.24, and free cash flow of $28.1M more than doubled; cloud ARR grew 28% to $515.3M at 85% of total ARR and cloud NRR held at 123%. FY2027 guidance calls for total revenue of $658.2M-$662.2M and non-GAAP EPS of $1.64-$1.68, but the FQ2 total revenue guide of $158.8M-$159.8M implies a sequential decline driven by the on-prem-to-cloud license transition. Management flagged Celeste pipeline up roughly 2.5x QoQ and Firm AI at more than 40% of net new bookings, up from over 20% last quarter, while noting demand is outrunning deployment capacity.

negative_highlights: Same-store new units fell 8% year-over-year, with BEV sales down 76% and the EV decline accounting for 5 points of the drop.
Parts and service was below plan: customer pay revenue up 2% but gross profit flat and warranty gross profit down 1%, with customer pay repair orders down 1.9%.
Same-store adjusted SG&A as a percentage of gross profit was 67%, reflecting the peak of Tekion conversions, and adjusted EPS carried a $0.69 non-cash TCA deferral headwind.
positive_highlights: Used retail gross profit grew 3% year-over-year and GPU rose 10% to $1,777, with all-store used retail volume up 4.5% sequentially.
Stores on Tekion for six months or more outperformed: Georgia and Koons customer pay gross profit grew 7%, and Florida fixed ops gross profit was up 3% in September.
FTC administrative proceeding against the company was dismissed in early October.
summary: Asbury reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $4.4 billion, gross profit of $732 million (16.6% margin), adjusted operating margin of 4.9%, adjusted EBITDA of $218 million, and adjusted EPS of $6.16 ($6.85 excluding a $0.69 non-cash TCA deferral). Same-store new units fell 8% (5% from BEV volume declines), parts and service gross profit was flat with customer pay revenue up 2%, and same-store adjusted SG&A was 67% of gross profit, elevated by the peak 47-store Tekion conversion. Management expects SG&A to reach the low 60% range by the end of 2027 and targets transaction-adjusted net leverage of 3.0x by mid-2027, with parts and service growth expected to resume mid-single-digit next year. The quarter completed the Tekion and TCA rollouts, and the FTC administrative proceeding against the company was dismissed in early October.

negative_highlights: NIM fell to 5.74% from 5.96% in the trailing quarter (5.68% normalized) on the combined asset/funding mix, with 2027 guided to 5.70%-5.75%, below prior expectations of the high-540s/low-550s.
GAAP EPS of $1.57 was burdened by $8.9M pre-tax merger expenses; operating expenses jumped 71% to $36M, including $1.8M of core deposit intangible amortization.

Management called the $500M 2027 loan growth target (~14%) realistic rather than conservative, citing a heavy integration lift with two different core systems (Fiserv vs. Jack Henry) and a conversion targeted for April 2027.
positive_highlights: Adjusted diluted EPS of $2.12 rose 69% from $1.60 on a linked-quarter basis and exceeded consensus, per management.
Organic growth ex-Signature stayed strong: litigation loans +$160M (49% annualized) in the quarter and organic loans +$497M (+32%) year over year, with organic deposits +$447M (+24%).
Management guided 2027 to ~$9.00 diluted EPS and said it expects to exceed the earnings expectations set when the deal was announced in March 2026.
summary: First post-merger quarter (Signature closed Aug 1, 2026, two months included): GAAP net income $17.5M or $1.57/diluted share; adjusted net income $23.6M or $2.12/diluted share versus $1.60 adjusted a quarter ago (+69%), which management said exceeds consensus. Adjusted ROA and ROA-TE were 2.34% and 23.1%, NIM 5.74% (5.68% normalized), and adjusted efficiency ratio 41.1%. Organic growth remained strong ex-merger: loans +$160M (49% annualized) in the litigation vertical, deposits +$147M organically, and year-over-year organic loan growth of $497M (+32%). For 2027, management guided to ~$500M loan growth (~14%), a 5.70%-5.75% NIM, $33-34M fee income, $138-140M non-interest expense, a 28.5% tax rate, and ~$9.00 diluted EPS, stating they expect to exceed the initial merger guidance from March 12, 2026.

negative_highlights: Insurance and claims costs rose to $39.4 million from $30.4 million, including ~$10.5 million of net unfavorable prior-year claim development tied to five claims
Variable contribution margin compressed to 13.9% from 14.1% as truck brokerage carrier pay rose 136 basis points
Free cash flow was negative in Q2, only the third negative FCF quarter in the past decade, and no formal Q3 guidance was issued
positive_highlights: Truck revenue per load rose 17% YoY and 14.4% sequentially, the largest sequential increase in 15 years
Heavy haul revenue reached ~$164 million, up 18% YoY on 9% volume growth and 8% higher revenue per load
Net BCO truck count rose by 68 trucks, the strongest quarterly improvement since Q1 2022, with turnover falling to 28.3% from 31.4% at FY2025 year-end
summary: Landstar reported Q2 FY2026 revenue up 18% year-over-year, driven by truck revenue per load up 17% and loads hauled up nearly 2%, with heavy haul revenue of ~$164 million (+18%). Gross profit rose to $132.3 million from $109.3 million and gross margin edged up to 9.2%, but variable contribution margin slipped to 13.9% from 14.1% and insurance/claims costs jumped to $39.4 million from $30.4 million on ~$10.5 million of unfavorable prior-year claim development. Management declined formal Q3 guidance, citing fluid freight, geopolitical, and litigation environments, instead providing commentary: July truck loads ~5% above prior year and revenue per load ~26% above, both slightly ahead of normal seasonality. Capital returns continued with a $0.44 quarterly dividend (10% increase) and ~$120 million returned in the first half.

negative_highlights: Full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance midpoint was lowered to 8%-10% growth from 9%-12%, with adjusted EPS growth cut to 12%-13% from 12%-15%.
Rapid freight and raw material inflation created pricing lags, and Mineral Fiber full-year margin is now expected roughly flat versus the record 43.5% prior year.
The Parallel acquisition is ramping slower than expected on operational leverage, and lower-than-expected acquisition contributions partly offset the sales guidance raise.
positive_highlights: Architectural Specialties organic growth of 16% was the highest quarterly rate on record, with segment adjusted EBITDA up 25% and margin expanding 60 bps to 19.4%.
Mineral Fiber expanded adjusted EBITDA margin 40 bps to 44% even amid the highest input cost inflation since 2022, and delivered its third consecutive quarter of volume growth.
AS order intake grew at a double-digit rate again, and the dividend was raised 10% (eighth consecutive annual increase), with $75M of Q3 buybacks and $210M year to date.
summary: Q3 net sales rose 12% with adjusted EBITDA up 11% and adjusted diluted EPS up 10%; Mineral Fiber sales grew 7% (AUV +6%, margin +40 bps to 44%) and Architectural Specialties grew 22% (16% organic, margin +60 bps to 19.4%). Management raised the total company sales outlook to 10%-11% growth from 9%-11% on stronger AS organic growth (now low teens, AS segment 18%-19% from 15%-17%), but modestly lowered the adjusted EBITDA midpoint to 8%-10% from 9%-12% and cut adjusted EPS growth to 12%-13% from 12%-15% and free cash flow growth to 10%-13% from 10%-14%. The reduction reflects accelerated freight and raw material inflation, tariffs, a timing-related low-AUV channel mix in Mineral Fiber, and slower ramp at the Parallel acquisition. Mineral Fiber full-year margin is now guided to roughly flat versus the prior year's record 43.5%, while AS margin expansion holds at about 19% (~20% organic).

negative_highlights: Mortgage revenues declined in the quarter, with core fee income only 4% YoY as reported
Commercial non-performers increased, though attributed to isolated situational credits
Loan growth was 3% linked-quarter annualized (4% ex-other consumer), and management flagged some borrower moderation in certain markets
positive_highlights: NIM expanded 12 bps YoY to 4.51% and net interest income rose $20 million YoY to $218.9 million
Non-interest-bearing deposits grew 6% YoY, with cost of deposits down 8 bps YoY
About $2.2 billion of fixed loans rolling off in 2027 at ~6.0% with ~100 bps of reinvestment yield improvement, plus a ~$27 million Q4 pension termination gain
summary: Central Bancompany reported Q3 FY2026 net income of $116.2 million, or $0.48 per share, with ROA of 2.27%. Net interest income rose $20 million YoY to $218.9 million and the FTE NIM expanded 12 bps to 4.51%, while core fee income grew 4% (8% ex-mortgage) and the efficiency ratio was 45.4%. Credit stayed benign at 12 bps of net charge-offs, and management flagged $700 million of fixed loans repricing in Q4 ($2.2 billion next year) at roughly 6.0% plus a pension termination gain of about $27 million in Q4. No formal guidance was issued, but management said NIM and NII should grind higher into 2027-2028 under a static curve and balance sheet.

negative_highlights: Adjusted gross margin fell 50 bps to 11.2%, attributed to mix in the CCS segment
2026 free cash flow outlook cut to $460M from $600M on targeted working capital investment
Inventory rose $1.1B sequentially and $2.5B YoY to $4.5B; capex of $274M was 4.7% of revenue versus 1.2% a year ago
positive_highlights: Revenue of $5.83B rose 83% YoY and came in above the high end of guidance, with both CCS and ATS ahead
Adjusted EPS of $3.30 beat the high end of guidance and rose 109% YoY; non-GAAP operating margin hit a record 8.5%, up 90 bps
Full-year 2026 outlook raised to $21B revenue and $11.55 adjusted EPS (from $20.5B and $11.30)
summary: Celestica reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $5.83B, up 83% YoY and above the high end of guidance, with adjusted EPS of $3.30 up 109% and also above the high end. Non-GAAP operating margin reached a record 8.5% (up 90 bps), though adjusted gross margin fell 50 bps to 11.2% on CCS mix. Guidance for Q4 is $6.275-6.575B revenue and $3.37-3.57 adjusted EPS, and the full-year 2026 outlook was raised to $21B revenue (from $20.5B) and $11.55 adjusted EPS (from $11.30), while the 2026 free cash flow outlook was cut to $460M from $600M on working capital investment. Inventory rose $1.1B sequentially to $4.5B and capex is tracking near $1B for 2026, supporting the accelerating 2027 growth outlook.

negative_highlights: P&C combined ratio rose 2.7 points to 90.9% including 7.0 points from higher catastrophe losses, and operating income fell $6 million YoY despite $146 million more after-tax cat losses
Consolidated net written premiums grew only 2%, with commercial lines below 1% and personal lines 1% as renewal price increases moderated versus Q2
Third quarter value creation ratio was -2.1% as the bond portfolio carried a $1.5 billion net unrealized loss after a ~$1.2 billion pre-tax markdown from rising rates
positive_highlights: Nine-month accident year combined ratio before catastrophes improved to 86.5% from 86.7% a year ago
Cincinnati Global grew net written premiums 13% at a 70.7% combined ratio and Cincinnati Re grew 34%
Net investment income rose 10% with bond interest income up 11% and $1.1 billion of fixed maturity purchases in the quarter
summary: Q3 2026 non-GAAP operating income of $443 million was down $6 million YoY despite after-tax catastrophe losses $146 million higher; the P&C combined ratio rose 2.7 points to 90.9% including 7.0 points from cat losses. Consolidated P&C net written premiums grew only 2%, with commercial lines under 1% and personal lines 1% on softer new business, while Cincinnati Re grew 34% and Cincinnati Global 13%. Nine-month accident year combined ratio before cats improved slightly to 86.5% from 86.7%, investment income rose 10%, and no explicit forward guidance was given; management repeatedly framed slowing growth as normalization from an exceptionally hard market rather than a reversal. Third quarter VCR was -2.1% on a $1.2 billion pre-tax bond portfolio loss from rising rates.

negative_highlights: China multinational OEM share loss and pricing pressure; domestic China market ex-exports down roughly 25%, and Q4 global light vehicle production expected down 4%
Aerospace, defense and commercial equipment segment margin contracted to 26.7% from 27.4% on growth investments and product mix
Q4 revenue guide midpoint of ~$957M is roughly 2% below Q3 excluding the one-time payment, and management does not expect sequential revenue growth into Q1 2027
positive_highlights: Adjusted operating margin expanded year-over-year for a fifth consecutive quarter, up 160 bps to 28.8% in Industrials and 20 bps to 19.5% ex-payment overall
Free cash flow of $198M rose 46% YoY with conversion of 119%, and YTD free cash flow of $489M already matches full-year 2025's record $490M
Data center revenue expected to grow 76% to $48M in 2026, with hyperscaler wins up to seven across six hyperscalers from one at the start of the year
summary: Sensata reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $1.004B, up 8% reported and 7% organic, including a $24M EV program termination payment; excluding it, revenue was $980M (5% reported, 4% organic) and results met or exceeded guidance midpoints across key metrics. Adjusted operating margin was 21.5%, or 19.5% ex-payment (up 20 bps YoY), adjusted EPS was $1.13 (up 27% YoY, $0.16 above the high end as reported), and free cash flow conversion was 119%. Q4 guidance is $942-972M revenue and $0.95-0.99 EPS (~5% revenue growth, ~10% EPS growth at midpoint), with management flagging softer China auto production and no sequential revenue growth into Q1 2027. Data center revenue is expected to grow 76% to $48M in 2026, with seven hyperscaler wins ramping from mid-2027.

negative_highlights: Q4 guidance of $154-164 million in sales and $10-13 million adjusted EBITDA implies sequential declines from Q3's $172.8 million and $13.6 million ex-refund EBITDA
DynaEnergetics volumes declined in the Americas in Q3, with management saying margins should be modeled 50-100 bps lower and no further step-up expected
CEO described construction markets as 'truly terrible' and the worst since 2008-2009, with no expectation of a permit pickup
positive_highlights: NobelClad sales rose 38% YoY and adjusted EBITDA 120% YoY on a record petrochemical order and resolution of defense-order supply delays
Backlog rose to $72.4 million from $63.5 million at Q2 end, including a record $16 million in quarterly U.S. Navy vessel construction orders
Net debt fell to $13.7 million from $30.5 million at Q2 end on $16.6 million of quarterly free cash flow
summary: DMC reported Q3 sales of $172.8 million, up 14% YoY and 10% sequentially, with adjusted EBITDA attributable to DMC of $13.6 million excluding $5.4 million of DynaEnergetics tariff refunds, up 59% YoY. All three segments grew: Arcadia sales +25% YoY, NobelClad sales +38% YoY with adjusted EBITDA +120%, and DynaEnergetics margins expanded to 9.7% ex-refunds from 7.1%. Q4 guidance calls for sales of $154-164 million and adjusted EBITDA of $10-13 million, reflecting seasonal moderation, a two-week California anodizing facility shutdown, and declining large long-cycle project activity; management said construction markets are the worst since 2008-2009.

negative_highlights: 737 deliveries came in shy of the ~500 target and stability at Rate 47 will slip into next year, with Rate 52 now targeted for H2 2027
787 deliveries tracking toward the low end of the 90-100 range on delays reaching Rate 10; 777 and 767 lines disrupted by a wing-component supplier
BCA operating margin -6.5% with higher supply chain costs and lower booking rates; 2027 FCF of ~$3B is largely the absence of the $700M DOJ payment plus modest improvement
positive_highlights: Record total backlog of $745B, with BCA at $612B and BDS at $101B after $23B of Q3 defense orders
F/A-XX sixth-generation Navy win and FAA certification of the 737-7 in July and 737-10 last week
BGS revenue up 4% to $5.6B (up 11% ex-divestiture) and operating margin of 18.3%
summary: Q3 FY2026 revenue of $24.2B rose 4% on higher defense and services volume, with operating margin improving to 1.5% and core EPS a loss of $0.34; free cash flow was positive $464M. BCA revenue fell 3% to $10.7B with a -6.5% operating margin on delivery mix, rate adjustments and higher supply chain costs, and 737 output came in shy of the ~500 delivery target due to slower-than-expected stability at Rate 47. Management issued a multi-year FCF path of ~$2B in 2026, ~$3B in 2027, ~$6B in 2028 and $10B in 2029, assuming 777X certification by mid-2027, and set Rate 52 on the 737 for the back half of 2027. Record backlog reached $745B, with BCA at $612B and BDS at $101B, and BDS booked the F/A-XX win, which was not yet in Q3 backlog.

negative_highlights: Adjusted free cash flow conversion is guided to decline to approximately 95% in FY2027 from 103% in FY2026, reflecting higher capex of ~$900 million.
The global intrusion divestiture (~$500 million annual revenue) is expected to be slightly dilutive at about $0.15 annualized once it closes in Q2 FY2027.
Service growth of 8% lagged systems growth of 13%, with management noting security service remains subdued and may need another one or two quarters before recovering.
positive_highlights: Orders increased 44% and backlog grew 43% to a record $23 billion.
Organic revenue rose 12% in Q4 with adjusted EPS up 32% to $1.66 and adjusted EBIT margin expanding 300 bps to 18%.
Margin expanded in all three regions: Americas +210 bps to 22%, EMEA +80 bps to 16.4%, APAC +110 bps to 19%.
summary: JCI reported Q4 FY2026 organic revenue growth of 12% with systems up 13% and service up 8%, adjusted EPS up 32% to $1.66, and adjusted EBIT margin expansion of 300 bps to 18%. Orders rose 44% and backlog grew 43% to a record $23 billion, with 70%-80% expected to convert over the next 12 months. FY2027 guidance calls for 11%-12% organic revenue growth, adjusted EPS of $6.15-$6.30 (21% growth at midpoint), operating leverage above 30%, and adjusted free cash flow conversion of approximately 95%, alongside $900 million of capex and a new $400 million restructuring program targeting $600 million in annualized savings by FY2029. This follows a full year in which organic revenue rose over 8% and adjusted EPS rose 37%, exceeding both initial and raised FY2026 guidance.

positive_highlights: Revenue rose 19% YoY to $7.94 billion and net income rose 44% YoY to $847.5 million
Paccar Parts set a record quarterly revenue of $1.78 billion, with 3%-5% full-year growth reiterated
Price cost remained favorable in the quarter on strong truck price realization, and truck gross margin held at 14.5% despite 40,100 deliveries constrained by supply
summary: Paccar reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $7.94 billion (up 19% YoY) and net income of $847.5 million (up 44% YoY), with truck/parts/other gross margin of 14.5%. Q4 deliveries are guided to 41,000-43,000 (up from 40,100) with gross margin of 14%-15%, roughly flat sequentially due to supplier-related production inefficiencies; management flagged Q3 deliveries were held back by supply constraints. Paccar Parts posted a record $1.78 billion and PFS earned $138 million (up 9.4%), though parts margin slipped on mix. Guidance is essentially intact with 2027 market outlooks raised modestly (NA Class 8 to 240,000-280,000; South America up slightly), but 2027 pricing awaits unresolved NCP levels.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to $61.9 million from $53.9 million a year ago as R&D rose to $53.8 million and G&A to $25.4 million
Cash of $431 million with runway into Q3 2028 excludes future GSK milestones, leaving funding dependent on partnership inflows
Key value drivers, including WVE-007 600 mg data, the post-incretin maintenance trial start, and the WVE-008 CTA, all remain pending in Q4 2026 with no readouts delivered this quarter
positive_highlights: Revenue rose to $13.2 million from $7.6 million in the prior-year quarter on the GSK collaboration
FDA meeting supports a single two-year WVE-006 registrational trial with a one-year interim analysis for potential accelerated approval, without a separate confirmatory trial
GSK selected an siRNA development candidate, triggering a $12 million milestone payable in Q4, with three additional GSK programs advancing toward development candidates
summary: Q3 FY2026 revenue was $13.2 million versus $7.6 million a year ago, driven by the GSK collaboration, while R&D rose to $53.8 million from $45.9 million and G&A to $25.4 million from $18.1 million, widening the net loss to $61.9 million from $53.9 million. The company ended the quarter with $431 million in cash and guided to runway into Q3 2028, plus a $12 million GSK milestone due in Q4. No formal financial guidance was given; the key clinical updates were an FDA-aligned single two-year registrational trial for WVE-006 with a one-year interim for accelerated approval, and timeline confirmations for WVE-007 600 mg data, a post-incretin maintenance trial start, and a WVE-008 CTA, all in Q4 2026. The quarter was a pipeline-progress update rather than a financial beat or miss, with expenses rising on advancing programs.

negative_highlights: Full-year adjusted operating margin guidance cut to -4.5% to -6.5%, with higher fuel creating 3.5 points of pressure versus the July outlook.
Q3 CASM ex-fuel rose 7% YoY, including roughly 4 points of pressure from summer weather and ATC disruptions.
Q3 fuel was $3.91/gal, up 57% YoY, with Q4 fuel guided to approximately $4.64/gal, up 85% YoY.
positive_highlights: Revenue rose 18.4% YoY, about 4 points above the midpoint of initial guidance, with Q4 RASM guided up 18%-22%.
Fuel recapture reached 87% in Q3 versus an initial 70%-80% expectation, with management targeting 100% by early 2027.
Q4 CASM ex-fuel guided to -1% to +1% YoY, a sharp step-down from +7% in Q3, after over $30 million of controllable cost savings.
summary: JetBlue reported Q3 total revenue up 18.4% YoY, roughly 4 points above the midpoint of initial guidance, with unit revenue up 18.4% and 87% fuel recapture versus an initial 70%-80% expectation. Q4 RASM is guided up 18%-22%, a fifth consecutive quarter of accelerating YoY RASM growth, with full-year RASM now 13.5%-14.5%, but full-year adjusted operating margin was cut to -4.5% to -6.5%, reflecting 3.5 points of pressure from higher fuel ($3.91/gal, up 57% YoY). CASM ex-fuel rose 7% in Q3 including ~4 points of summer disruption, with Q4 guided to -1% to +1%. Liquidity was $2.2 billion with ~$7 billion of unencumbered assets, and management reiterated 2027 operating profitability and 2028 targets of at least $1 EPS and positive free cash flow.

negative_highlights: North Italia comparable sales declined 3% and restaurant-level margin fell to 13.2% from 15.7% on sales deleverage
Q4 guidance models the last three weeks at only ~3% pricing with flat traffic and a 1% holiday-shift deduction, implying deceleration from Q3 trends
positive_highlights: Cheesecake Factory comparable sales rose 15.2% with traffic up 9.5%, outperforming the Black Box Casual Dining Index by 940 bps
Cheesecake Factory restaurant-level profit margin expanded 240 bps year-over-year to 18.7%, with labor down 80 bps and cost of sales down 60 bps as a percent of sales
Flower Child comparable sales increased 11% (two-year comps accelerating to 18%), with restaurant margin up 280 bps to 20.2% and 2027 unit growth planned at 11-13
summary: Total revenue exceeded $1.033 billion, above the high end of guidance, with Cheesecake Factory comparable sales up 15.2% on 9.5% traffic growth and adjusted diluted EPS of $1.02, well above expectations. Adjusted EBITDA rose 38% to $98.7 million and Cheesecake Factory restaurant-level margin expanded 240 bps to 18.7%. Q4 revenue guidance is $1.04-$1.05 billion with adjusted net income margin of about 5.8% at the midpoint, while initial 2027 targets ~$4.425 billion revenue and 6.0%-6.1% net income margin. Management explicitly characterized the sales inflection as early and kept 2027 assumptions aligned to its historical algorithm; North Italia comps fell 3% with restaurant margin down to 13.2% from 15.7%.

negative_highlights: Q4 revenue is targeted at about $291 million, a sequential decline from Q3's $306 million, reflecting retail peak-seasonality dynamics
Services revenue grew only 1% to $134 million, and full-year services growth is guided to low single digits amid faster deployment offsetting volume

Linda noted roughly half the quarterly beat was tied to upsells that management deliberately excludes from forward guidance due to timing and amount variability, and declined to break out AI revenue contribution
positive_highlights: Cloud revenue grew 28% to $134 million, marking the fourth consecutive quarter of record bookings and accelerating from 26% in Q2 and 24% in Q1
Full-year RPO outlook raised to 21% growth from a prior 18%-20% range, with RPO up 25% to $2.59 billion and year-to-date deal volume already surpassing full-year 2025

Guidance raised on total revenue ($1.177 billion midpoint), adjusted operating margin (35.3% midpoint from 35.1%), and adjusted EPS ($5.54-$5.56); $325 million in year-to-date buybacks including $50 million in Q3
summary: Manhattan reported Q3 revenue of $306 million, up 11% (12% excluding license and maintenance), with cloud revenue up 28% to $134 million and adjusted EPS of $1.55, up 14%, both ahead of expectations. RPO rose 25% to $2.59 billion on a fourth consecutive record bookings quarter, and adjusted operating margin came in at 37.6%. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance across the board: total revenue to $1.176-$1.178 billion, RPO growth to 21% (from 18%-20%), adjusted operating margin midpoint to 35.3% (from 35.1%), and adjusted EPS to $5.54-$5.56. Preliminary 2027 commentary said consensus estimates are generally appropriate, including 20% cloud revenue growth.

positive_highlights: Consolidated EBITDA margin of 20.2% was the highest since Q2 2023, with North America at 27.7%, the highest in four years
Free cash flow of BRL 1.4 billion in Q3 was 6x the Q2 level, and nine-month FCF swung to BRL 1.7 billion from a BRL 1 billion consumption a year earlier
S&P revised its outlook to positive on the BBB rating, and leverage stood at 0.58x net debt to EBITDA
summary: Gerdau reported Q3 FY2026 EBITDA of BRL 3.8 billion at a 20.2% margin, the highest since Q2 2023, with North America EBITDA margin of 27.7%, the highest in four years. Adjusted net income reached BRL 1.5 billion and EPS rose to BRL 0.79 from BRL 0.74. Free cash flow was BRL 1.4 billion, 6x Q2, and the company declared BRL 0.34 per share at Gerdau S/A plus buybacks totaling more than BRL 1.850 billion returned in 2026, with leverage at 0.58x net debt/EBITDA. Brazil remains pressured by imports and oversupply, with management flagging a restructuring plan to be detailed at the December 4 Investor Day and no formal guidance update; CapEx is now tracking closer to BRL 4 billion versus the prior BRL 4.5-4.7 billion.

negative_highlights: Net loss of $91.9 million ($0.19/share) versus net income of $2.5 million a year ago, driven by a $76.7 million non-cash goodwill impairment
Adjusted EBITDA remained negative at -$9.1 million, only a modest improvement from -$9.4 million a year ago
Revenue of $43.6 million at the 31% growth rate still implies a low run-rate against the $150-$165 million full-year guide, with about $17 million of convertible debt maturing in December
positive_highlights: Full-year 2026 revenue guidance raised to $150-$165 million, a 5% increase at the midpoint over prior guidance, implying 23% growth at the midpoint
Revenue grew 31% year-over-year to $43.6 million and 18.6% quarter-over-quarter, accelerating from 6.7% in Q2
Gross margin expanded 878 bps to 31.2%, and backlog rose 22% sequentially to $330 million on 25+ wins worth over $225 million
summary: Q3 FY2026 revenue was $43.6 million, up 31% year-over-year and 18.6% quarter-over-quarter (accelerating from 6.7% in Q2), with gross margin at 31.2%, up 878 bps. Management raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $150-$165 million, a 5% increase at the midpoint versus prior guidance and implying 23% growth at the midpoint. Backlog rose 22% sequentially to $330 million on 25+ new contracts worth over $225 million, against a $91.9 million net loss ($0.19/share) driven by a $76.7 million non-cash goodwill impairment. Adjusted EBITDA was -$9.1 million versus -$9.4 million a year ago, and cash and investments were nearly $400 million with about $17 million of convertible debt maturing in December.

negative_highlights: Q4 operating margin fell to 3.8% from 4.0% as SG&A rose to 13.8% of revenue from 13.5%, with G&A to 3.9% from 3.6% on technology and executive comp
RELEX forecasting/replenishment rollout will not finish by Q2 FY2027 as previously communicated, with no new completion date given
Trinidad dollar liquidity remains challenging, with $53.8 million of cash and note weakness in-term investments in TTD not readily convertible
positive_highlights: Net merchandise sales +13.8% (7.8% cc) with comps +12.2%, and average ticket +7.5% alongside transactions +5.9%
EPS +19% to $1.21 for Q4; FY adjusted EBITDA up 12.4% to $360.5 million
Membership: renewal rate 90.4% vs 88.8%, accounts +8.7% to almost 2.2 million, membership income +17.8% to $100.8 million, Platinum 23.4% from 17.9%
summary: Q4 FY2026 net merchandise sales rose 13.8% (7.8% constant currency) to almost $1.5 billion, with comps up 12.2% (6.2% cc). EPS rose 19% to $1.21 on net income of $37.6 million, aided by a lower 25% tax rate from discrete items; operating income rose 8.1% to $57 million but operating margin slipped to 3.8% from 4.0% on higher G&A, and gross margin was up 10 bps to 15.8%. FY net merchandise sales grew 11.7% with EPS up 12% to $5.40; Q1 FY2027 comps through eight weeks were up 11.8% (6% cc). Management flagged a converging risk scenario of higher fuel, freight, and food costs and delayed the RELEX rollout beyond Q2 FY2027 without a new date.

negative_highlights: Core rental REBITDA margin fell 70 bps to 45.2%, with fuel and freight pressures costing ~100 bps
CFO acknowledged rental rate is not keeping pace with inflation on a one-year view
Local market activity remains stable but soft, with commercial construction still pressured by interest rates
positive_highlights: Equipment rental revenue grew nearly 12% on average OEC fleet growth of less than 2%, with dollar utilization up 360 bps
Full-year adjusted REBITDA guidance raised ~2% at the midpoint to $2.13 billion, with rental revenue guidance to $4.513 billion
Specialty returned to 20% of total fleet at OEC from 17% a year ago, with specialty revenue up double digits
summary: Herc reported Q3 FY2026 equipment rental revenue up ~12% on average OEC fleet growth of under 2%, with dollar utilization up 360 bps and adjusted net income of $131 million ($3.91 per diluted share). Total revenue rose ~5% (held back by lower equipment sales), adjusted REBITDA grew ~9% and adjusted REBITDA margin expanded 190 bps to 44.2%, though core REBITDA margin fell 70 bps to 45.2% on fuel, freight and cost inflation. Management raised full-year guidance at the midpoint to $4.513 billion rental revenue and $2.13 billion adjusted REBITDA (~2% above prior), and increased net fleet CapEx to ~$1.05 billion, framing ~$150 million of that as pulled forward from the 2027 budget. The quarter was the first with H&E in both comp periods; CEO Larry Silber transitions to Executive Chairman and Aaron Birnbaum becomes CEO on January 1.

negative_highlights: Services revenue growth of 20% to $390 million is well below equipment growth, and management guided to high single-digit services growth for the next couple of years before accelerating in the early 2030s.
Equipment segment Adjusted EBITDA margin of 17.1% in Q3 remains well below the 32% services margin, reflecting dilution from the growing equipment mix.
positive_highlights: Revenue up 57% YoY to a record $1.2 billion with Adjusted EBITDA up 70% to $245 million and margin expanding 160 bps to 21%.
Full-year Adjusted EBITDA guidance raised by $60 million at the midpoint to $780-800 million, with revenue guidance also raised to $3.9-4.0 billion.
Equipment backlog reached a record $8 billion, up 142% YoY, with a last-12-month book-to-bill of 3.3x and $6.1 billion year-to-date equipment order intake up 91%.
summary: INNIO reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $1.2 billion, up 57% YoY, with equipment revenue up 86% and services up 20%, while Adjusted EBITDA rose 70% to $245 million and margin expanded 160 bps to 21%. The company raised full-year revenue guidance to $3.9-4.0 billion from $3.8-3.9 billion and Adjusted EBITDA guidance by $60 million at the midpoint to $780-800 million, versus approximately 19% prior margin guidance now approximately 20%. Equipment backlog reached a record $8 billion, up 142% YoY, with book-to-bill at 3.3x and 19 GW of combined backlog and slot reservations, up from over 15 GW last quarter.

negative_highlights: Gross margin from operations declined 19 bps on roughly 190 bps of commodity, logistics and tariff cost headwinds
About $0.30 of EPS shifted from Q4 into Q3, leaving Q4 adjusted EPS guidance of just $0.32-$0.42
Marine pontoon retail down low double digits and Aixam/Goupil sales down 12% on planned shipment reductions
positive_highlights: Operational adjusted EPS of $0.95, up from $0.41 a year ago and well above expectations
Full-year operational adjusted EPS guidance raised to $2.40-$2.50 from $2.05-$2.15, the third raise this year
Sixth consecutive quarter of ORV share gains with ORV North American retail up 2% against a 9% prior-year comparison
summary: Polaris reported Q3 FY2026 sales up 11% (17% organic, excluding Indian Motorcycle) with operational adjusted EPS of $0.95 vs $0.41 last year, well above expectations; reported adjusted EPS was $1.08 including $10M of IEEPA tariff refunds. Operational adjusted EBITDA margin expanded ~85 bps, though gross margin from operations slipped 19 bps as ~190 bps of commodity, logistics and tariff headwinds offset net price and efficiency gains. Management raised full-year operational adjusted EPS guidance to $2.40-$2.50 from $2.05-$2.15 (third raise this year), raised sales guidance to $7.55-$7.60B, and narrowed adjusted EBITDA margin expansion to 270-275 bps. About $0.30 of EPS shifted from Q4 into Q3 on earlier snowmobile shipments and faster-than-planned Huntsville RANGER ramp, implying a soft Q4 EPS guide of $0.32-$0.42.

negative_highlights: Q3 adjusted diluted EPS of $1.04 versus $1.27 a year ago, and YTD $2.30 versus $2.53, with $0.44 of YTD dilution from the higher share count
YTD operating cost headwinds of $0.28 higher depreciation and $0.13 higher A&G not yet reflected in rates; effective tax rate fell to 14% from 16%
Texas SICC PFD adopted a $238,000 annual revenue decrease, and the Texas GRC filing slipped to first half 2027 from early 2027
positive_highlights: Quadvest closed October 1 with active connections up 14% in 2026 and 98,300 connections under contract, 13% above year-end 2025
2026 dilution from the Texas acquisitions now ~6% versus the prior 10%-20% expectation due to the October 1 close timing
summary: Q3 FY2026 adjusted diluted EPS of $1.04 fell from $1.27 a year earlier, and year-to-date adjusted EPS of $2.30 was below the $2.53 prior-year figure, driven by a roughly 20% higher share count ($0.44 YTD dilution), $0.28 of higher depreciation and $0.13 of higher A&G, partly offset by rate relief. Standalone 2026 adjusted EPS guidance was narrowed to $3.10-$3.16 from $3.08-$3.18, preserving the $3.13 midpoint, and guidance including the Texas acquisitions is $2.91-$2.97, about 6% dilution versus the previously flagged 10%-20%. Quadvest closed October 1 (Cibolo expected next week), and 2026 company-funded CapEx was cut to about $465 million from $483 million on higher developer-funded spend in Texas, with the five-year $2.7 billion plan unchanged. Management reiterated the 6%-8% long-term EPS CAGR and 13% rate base CAGR, and 2027 guidance comes in February.

negative_highlights: Q3 gross margin guided to 41%-42%, ~200 bps YoY decline, with ~150 bps from freight and material cost inflation
Tablet accessories fell 30% on a tough Japan education comparison, with Q3 also affected
EMEA declined 6% on weak European consumer/business confidence and Middle East conflict (~50 bps company-level drag)
positive_highlights: Non-GAAP gross margin of 45.2%, up 140 bps YoY and the fifth consecutive quarter above 43%
Video collaboration net sales grew 12% cc with a 60/40 price/unit split
Q3 supply-incident impact cut to $70M-$80M from up to $200M previously flagged; largely resolved by Q4
summary: Logitech reported Q2 FY2027 net sales of $1.2B, up 3% in USD and 2% in constant currency, its 11th consecutive quarter of growth, with non-GAAP gross margin of 45.2% (up 140 bps YoY) and non-GAAP operating income of $231M at an 18.9% margin. Growth was led by video collaboration (+12% cc), gaming (+7%), and AMR (+13%), while tablet accessories fell 30% and EMEA declined 6%. Guidance calls for Q3 constant-currency net sales of -5% to flat, reflecting a $70M-$80M supply-incident impact (down from up to $200M previously flagged), with Q3 gross margin of 41%-42% (~200 bps YoY decline on freight, materials, and promo), though FY2027 non-GAAP operating margin is now expected at the high end of the 15%-18% range, even excluding prior tariff refunds. The key change versus prior communication is the materially reduced supply-incident sales hit, offset by a sharper near-term gross-margin outlook due to broad component and freight inflation.

negative_highlights: Net revenue yield of 21.5 bps was pressured by strong low-fee money market and ETF flows, with exit yield of 21.3 bps
Fundamental fixed income saw $2.6 billion of net outflows and private markets posted $400 million of outflows, including nearly $700 million out of the U.S. bank loan ETF
positive_highlights: Adjusted operating margin expanded 650 bps YoY to 40.7%, the highest level since 2021, on 11 points of positive operating leverage
Additional $1.5 billion preferred repurchase brings total to $3 billion since May 2025, saving $88.5 million in annual dividends and lifting total preferred dividend savings to $177 million
summary: Invesco reported Q3 net revenue of $1.4 billion, up 16% YoY and 4% sequentially, with adjusted operating income of $562 million (+38% YoY) and adjusted operating margin of 40.7%, the highest since 2021, expanding 650 bps YoY. Adjusted diluted EPS rose to $0.72 from $0.61 a year ago, and net long-term inflows of $35.1 billion marked a 6.3% annualized organic growth rate and a 13th consecutive inflow quarter. The company announced an additional $1.5 billion preferred stock repurchase from MassMutual, bringing total repurchases to $3 billion and expected 2027 EPS accretion of $0.17 with a $0.41 run-rate once term loans are repaid. Q4 adjusted operating expense guidance is $830-840 million, and management framed long-term margins in the high 30s despite the 40.7% third-quarter level.

negative_highlights: Q4 same property NOI growth expected to moderate as the company laps elevated prior-year ancillary and other income tied to a large redevelopment incentive
2027 flagged as 'not business as usual' due to Slate closing and $500 million term loan swaps burning off in July, with 2027 guidance deferred to year-end
Signed-but-not-yet-commenced pipeline compressed to $69 million after $17 million of rent commenced in the quarter
positive_highlights: Full-year guidance raised: same property NOI growth to 5.5%-5.75% and FFO per share to $2.36-$2.38, supported by 6.2% YTD same property NOI growth
Total leased occupancy reached a record 95.6%, up 80 bps sequentially and 150 bps YoY, with small shop occupancy at a record 92.8% and anchor at 97%
Leasing economics remained strong: ~1.6 million sq ft executed at a 25% blended rent spread, with 43% new lease spreads including anchor spreads above 70%, plus a greater-than-7% dividend increase
summary: Brixmor reported Q3 FY2026 same property NOI growth of 6.6% and NAREIT FFO per share up 7% to $0.60, with total leased occupancy at a record 95.6% (up 80 bps sequentially, 150 bps YoY) and small shop occupancy at a record 92.8%. Management raised full-year guidance to same property NOI growth of 5.5%-5.75% and FFO per share of $2.36-$2.38, and the board increased the quarterly dividend by more than 7%. Leasing remained strong at a 25% blended comparable rent spread (43% new, 19%+ renewal), though management flagged that Q4 growth will moderate on lapping elevated ancillary income and 2027 will not be 'business as usual' given the pending Slate acquisition.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA was down three percentage points year over year in Q3
Management declined to provide a specific revenue growth target or a Q4 margin run rate, citing seasonality and variability
Fewer Experience Management RFPs were seen this year amid the Press Ganey-Qualtrics merger, and the CFO seat is vacant mid-search
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 11% YoY to $38 million, up from 4% growth in the first half of 2026
Adjusted EBITDA margin improved sequentially to 28% from 27% in H1 despite a 4-point HUB conference timing drag
TRCV grew 9% YoY to $154 million with several longstanding customers moving from annual to multi-year agreements
summary: Revenue grew 11% YoY to $38 million, accelerating from 4% growth in the first half, with less than half of Q3 growth from the large customer implementation that went live on schedule in July. TRCV rose 9% to $154 million and adjusted EBITDA margin improved sequentially to 28% from 27% in H1, though it was down three points YoY and HUB conference timing cost about 4 points of margin. Management expects further sequential margin improvement in Q4 plus seasonal revenue, but explicitly declined to give a specific growth target or treat Q4 margin as a run rate. No formal revenue or EPS guidance was issued, and a CFO search is underway following Shane Harrison's departure.

negative_highlights: Exchange equivalent admissions fell ~19% YoY and the exchange-to-uninsured shift drove an estimated ~$400M unfavorable Adjusted EBITDA impact in the quarter
Uninsured volume rose to ~10.5% of equivalent admissions from 8.5% a year ago; full-year payer mix hit now expected at or slightly above the top of the prior range
Inpatient surgeries fell 1.4% and outpatient surgeries fell 3.7%, with ASC surgery volumes down 5.4%
positive_highlights: Same-facility adjusted admissions grew 3% versus 2.3% year to date, marking the 22nd consecutive quarter of volume growth
Same-facility cost per equivalent admission excluding Medicaid supplemental programs was essentially flat YoY and improved 40 bps sequentially despite normal Q3 merit increases
2026 guidance reaffirmed with expectation to land in the upper half of ranges; Medicaid supplemental net benefit range raised to $600-800M from prior
summary: HCA reported Q3 2026 same-facility adjusted admissions growth of 3% (22nd consecutive quarter of volume growth) and adjusted diluted EPS up almost 4%, with results slightly above expectations; core growth was cited at roughly 10%. Full-year 2026 guidance ranges were reaffirmed with an expectation to land in the upper half, helped by a raised Medicaid supplemental payment net benefit range of $600-800M (up ~$300M). Offsets include a ~$400M quarterly Adjusted EBITDA hit from the exchange-to-uninsured payer mix shift, exchange equivalent admissions down 19% YoY, and a preliminary 2027 view of earnings generally consistent with 2026 given $550-650M less in Medicaid supplemental net benefits.

negative_highlights: Branded checkout TPV growth remained at 1%-2% for a fourth straight quarter, and Q4 is guided at the same 1%-2% with EU de minimis headwinds persisting
Q4 non-GAAP EPS guided to ~$1.43 versus $1.45 in Q3, with transaction margin dollars only slightly positive
2027 framed as an investment year with EPS growth only similar to 2026; management said not to annualize the 1% Q3 non-transaction OpEx growth
positive_highlights: Non-GAAP EPS of $1.45 grew 8% and came in above guidance, driven by transaction margin dollars beating expectations and OpEx below forecast
Full-year guidance raised to ~$15.7 billion transaction margin dollars and ~$5.60 non-GAAP EPS, with adjusted free cash flow of at least $6.5 billion
Venmo TPV grew double-digits for an eighth consecutive quarter and Braintree TPV grew 10%, with Pay with Venmo up 43% and Pay Later up 25%
summary: PayPal reported Q3 FY2026 revenue growth of 2% (1% currency-neutral), transaction margin dollars up 2% (3% ex-interest on customer balances), and non-GAAP EPS of $1.45, up 8% and above guidance, with adjusted free cash flow of $2 billion and $1.5 billion of buybacks. Full-year guidance was raised to ~$15.7 billion transaction margin dollars, ~$5.60 non-GAAP EPS, and at least $6.5 billion adjusted free cash flow, with Q4 EPS guided to ~$1.43 and low-double-digit currency-neutral revenue growth. Branded checkout TPV growth stayed in the 1%-2% range, with the EU de minimis removal creating ~70 bps of headwind expected to persist through Q4, while Venmo and Braintree grew TPV double-digits. Management targets 2027 EPS growth similar to 2026 as it increases investment, with mid-single-digit transaction margin dollar growth as a medium-term target.

negative_highlights: Operating cash flow was -$42.3M, with inventory up $93.4M to $723.3M, reflecting heavy working capital build to fund the ramp
Customer concentration remains high, with the two largest customers at 61% of total revenue
Gross margin of 17.3% is still well below the 20% target at $4B revenue, and management flagged capacity expansions as a temporary margin headwind as phases come online
positive_highlights: Revenue of $759M rose 48.8% YoY and 17.7% sequentially, above the high end of guidance, with Q4 guided to $800M-$860M (up 9.4% sequentially at midpoint)
Operating margin expanded 200 bps to 9.0% from 7.0% in Q2, with products gross margin up to 15.9% from 15.1% and services margin up to 30.1% from 28.9%
Management raised its 2027 WFE outlook to above $200B and guided to roughly $4B of capacity by Q1 with 15%-20% burst capacity, citing healthy customer forecasts and fab utilization
summary: UCT reported record Q3 FY2026 revenue of $759M, up 17.7% sequentially and 48.8% year-over-year, with non-GAAP EPS of $1.15 (up $0.45 QoQ), gross margin of 17.3% (+60 bps) and operating margin of 9.0% (up 200 bps from 7.0%). Both top and bottom line came in above the high end of guidance. Q4 guidance is $800M-$860M revenue (up 9.4% sequentially at midpoint) and EPS of $1.11-$1.35; management now expects 2027 WFE above $200B. Operating cash flow was -$42.3M and inventory rose $93.4M to $723.3M to fund the ramp, alongside $203M raised via the ATM program (including $169.1M post-quarter).

negative_highlights: Total U.S. average daily volume fell 3.3% year-over-year, and Q4 U.S. ADV is guided down 1.3% as Amazon volume wraps
International total ADV declined 8.7% year-over-year, attributed to geopolitical tensions and the de minimis change
SCS operating profit of $274 million compares against a prior-year quarter that included a $330 million sale-leaseback gain
positive_highlights: U.S. Domestic operating profit rose 14.3% year-over-year to over $1 billion, with operating margin up 60 bps to 7%
Full-year 2026 guidance raised to approximately $92.6 billion revenue and approximately $8.75 billion operating profit, implying approximately $7.28 EPS
International returned to year-over-year operating profit growth for the first time in six quarters, with a 14.9% margin on 7.1% revenue growth
summary: UPS reported Q3 FY2026 consolidated revenue of $22.9 billion, up 6.7% year-over-year, with operating profit of $2.1 billion, a 9% operating margin, and diluted EPS of $1.69. All three segments grew revenue: U.S. Domestic rose 4.5% with operating profit up 14.3% and margin up 60 bps to 7%, International rose 7.1% with operating profit of $746 million and a 14.9% margin, and Supply Chain Solutions rose by $459 million to $3 billion. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance to approximately $92.6 billion in revenue, approximately $8.75 billion in operating profit, and approximately $7.28 in EPS, and lifted Q4 expectations to approximately $25.7 billion in revenue and approximately $3.3 billion in operating profit. Total U.S. average daily volume fell 3.3% due to deliberate Amazon reductions, and Q4 U.S. ADV is expected to be down 1.3% year-over-year, though core ex-Amazon volume grew nearly 2%.

negative_highlights: FY2027 non-GAAP gross margin guided to 80.5%-82.5%, reflecting higher component costs, versus 84% non-GAAP gross margin reported in Q4
FY2027 revenue growth guidance of 8%-9% decelerates from FY2026's 11% total and 19% product growth
Replacement bookings expected to be down YoY in the second half of FY2027 as refresh-driven expansion shifts to net-new timing, and Americas grew only 5% in Q4
positive_highlights: Q4 revenue of $917 million grew 13% YoY and exceeded the top end of guidance, with product revenue up 23% and systems up 29%
FY2027 systems growth target raised to upper single-digit from the mid-to-upper single-digit outlined at the May investor event
Direct AI use-case bookings topped $100 million in FY2026, up nearly 300% YoY, with active direct AI customers growing 4x to more than 200
summary: Q4 FY2026 revenue of $917 million rose 13% YoY and came in above the top end of guidance, with product revenue up 23% to $510 million and systems up 29%; non-GAAP EPS of $4.42 and non-GAAP operating margin of 33.7% also exceeded guidance. FY2027 revenue guidance of 8%-9% growth was set against an FY2026 baseline that finished above May investor-event expectations, with systems now seen at upper single-digit growth (improved from mid-to-upper single digit) and software at solid double digits. FY2027 non-GAAP gross margin is guided to 80.5%-82.5% on higher component costs, non-GAAP operating margin 33%-35%, and EPS $18.00-$18.30, with a new $1.5 billion buyback authorization added to $322 million remaining. Direct AI use-case bookings more than doubled from H1 to over $100 million for the year, up nearly 300% YoY, while Americas growth lagged at 5% versus EMEA's 31%.

negative_highlights: Consolidated revenue grew only 2% YoY and adjusted EBITDA fell $2 million YoY despite the strong sequential improvement
Consolidated non-GAAP gross margin of 50.3% declined 230 bps YoY, with IP Optical gross margin down 390 bps YoY on higher component costs and unfavorable geographic mix

IP Optical book-to-bill was about 0.82 in Q3, and management said the company expects to be supply limited to some extent in Q4, potentially pushing $5-$10 million of demand into the next quarter; cash flow from operations was a $14 million use with net debt leverage at 4.4x
positive_highlights: Q4 revenue guidance of $233-$247 million implies roughly 10% sequential growth, with adjusted EBITDA guided to $40-$47 million versus $27 million in Q3
IP Optical Networks posted a record third quarter at $96 million, up 17% sequentially, with U.S. sales up more than 150% YoY and routing shipments growth of about 35%
Total bookings rose 8% YoY and backlog increased 9% from a year ago, while the first nine months of IP Optical delivered a 1.24x book-to-revenue ratio
summary: Ribbon reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $219 million, up 14% sequentially but only 2% year over year, with non-GAAP EPS of $0.07 (up $0.03 YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $27 million (up $15 million sequentially, down $2 million YoY). IP Optical Networks revenue rose 17% sequentially and 5% YoY to $96 million, while Cloud and Edge revenue was $123 million, up 11% sequentially but down 1% YoY; consolidated non-GAAP gross margin was 50.3%, down 230 bps YoY on product and customer mix. Q4 guidance was set at revenue of $233-$247 million and adjusted EBITDA of $40-$47 million, with management citing growth led by Cloud and Edge, software and professional services mix, and about $2 million per quarter of higher component and logistics costs. Bookings rose 8% YoY and backlog was up 9% from a year ago, though IP Optical book-to-bill was about 0.82 and management flagged some Q4 supply limitation.

negative_highlights: About $400,000 of the quarter's NIM came from a one-time bankruptcy-related interest and fee recovery
Management said it would not expect a lot of margin expansion going into the rate-hike cycle
Tangible book value per share slipped to $22.35 from Q2 on lower AOCI as rising rates hit the AFS securities portfolio
positive_highlights: Net interest income rose 37% YoY to $28 million and NIM expanded 38 bps YoY to 4.01%
Pre-provision net revenue reached $15.4 million, up 53% from $10 million a year ago
Provision fell to $100,000 from $1.9 million in Q2 as the bankruptcy resolution cut non-performing loans and de-risked the balance sheet
summary: Norwood reported record net income of $11.8 million, or $1.08 per diluted share, versus adjusted $8.9 million or $0.94 a year ago, with net interest income up 37% to $28 million and NIM at 4.01%, up 38 bps YoY and 11 bps QoQ. ROAA was 1.60% and return on average tangible equity approximately 18.5%; PPNR rose 53% YoY to $15.4 million and the provision fell to $100,000 from $1.9 million in Q2. Results included roughly $400,000 of one-time interest benefit from the borrower bankruptcy resolution, and management said it would not expect much further NIM expansion in the current rate-hike cycle. No formal forward guidance was given; merger costs are essentially complete and the tax rate is guided to 21.5%-22%.

negative_highlights: RV same-property NOI declined 1.3% for the quarter, with RV growth range narrowed on higher-than-expected property-specific utility expense
2027 will face the loss of U.K. contribution, the approximately $10 million of Fort Myers Hurricane Ian business interruption income that will not recur, and lower Sungenia JV contribution
Management declined to give 2027 guidance or commit to a 2027 growth outlook, citing moving pieces from portfolio transformation
positive_highlights: Core FFO per share of $2.35 exceeded the high end of guidance by $0.02, the third consecutive quarter above guidance
Manufactured housing same-property NOI rose 6.9% on 5.8% revenue growth with occupancy of approximately 98%
2027 rent increases set above 2026 levels: approximately 5.4% for MH (about 40 bps higher than last year) and 4.4% for annual RV
summary: Sun Communities reported Q3 FY2026 Core FFO per share of $2.35, $0.02 above the high end of guidance, its third consecutive quarter of outperformance. MH same-property NOI rose 6.9% on 5.8% revenue growth and roughly 98% occupancy, while RV same-property NOI fell 1.3% on higher property-specific utility costs. Full-year Core FFO guidance is now $6.97-$7.05 per share, but the range is not comparable to the prior range because it removes U.K. contribution after the September 22 closing; MH NOI growth guidance was raised and RV narrowed. Management pointed to 2027 rent increases above 2026 levels (approximately 5.4% MH, 4.4% annual RV) as a positive, while flagging lost U.K., Fort Myers business interruption income (~$10 million in 2026), and lower Australia JV contribution as 2027 headwinds.

negative_highlights: Operating margin of 6.0% missed the 6.5%-7.0% guidance range on a $0.8 million FX translation loss
Gross margin contracted to 22.0% from 23.5%, a 130 bps FX-driven decline
Incremental inflation of $1.5-$2 million expected to repeat in Q2; ocean freight rates nearly doubled in six months and Section 232 upholstery tariff rises from 25% to 30% in January 2027
positive_highlights: Orders rose about 5% and ending backlog grew 8.2% YoY to $77.7 million
12th consecutive quarter of YoY sales growth, continuing branded business up about 5% excluding Homestyles
Balance sheet has no bank debt, with $4.4 million cash and $80.5 million working capital
summary: Net sales rose 3.2% YoY to $114.0 million, near the high end of the 1%-4% guidance, with continuing Flexsteel branded sales up about 5% excluding the Homestyles exit. GAAP operating margin was 6.0%, below the 6.5%-7.0% guided range, though roughly $0.8 million (70 bps) of peso translation loss was the cause; excluding it results were in line. Gross margin fell to 22.0% from 23.5%, and Q2 guidance calls for 1%-4% sales growth to $119.5-$123.0 million and 6.5%-7.0% operating margin. Incremental inflation of $1.5-$2 million is expected again in Q2, with ocean freight nearly doubling over six months and a Section 232 upholstered furniture tariff rising to 30% on January 1, 2027.

negative_highlights: Full-year ongoing EBIT margin guidance cut to 2.0%-2.2% after Q3 fell note weakness in of the expected step-up
Net cost take-out now below $150 million despite ~$250 million gross savings, hit by volume deleveraging and fuel/logistics costs
Free cash flow consumption of ~$1.1 billion in Q3, including a ~$150 million Grupo Casas Bahia receivable write-off, with only ~$100 million expected to be collected in Q4
positive_highlights: Sequential ongoing EBIT margin improvement of 80 bps to 2.6%, with pricing adding 250 bps and net cost a 100 bps tailwind
New 7%-10% pricing actions announced (7% U.S. effective December 3, Canada November 1, up to 10% in Latin America) that largely carry into 2027
$290 million of identified structural cost benefits from Amana, Perrysburg, and Mexico footprint actions, plus a 25% cut in U.S. local distribution centers
summary: Q3 net sales were $3.7 billion with ongoing EBIT margin of 2.6% and ongoing EPS of -$0.21; margin improved 80 bps sequentially but management explicitly said it 'did not deliver the margin step-up we had expected.' Full-year guidance was cut: ongoing EBIT margin now 2.0%-2.2%, like-for-like revenue down ~1.5%, net cost take-out below $150M versus ~$250M gross savings, and Latin America margin to ~3%. Free cash flow was a ~$1.1B consumption in the quarter (including a ~$150M Grupo Casas Bahia receivable write-off) against a ~$300M full-year target, offset by a higher net debt outlook (below $4.5B from below $5B) and 7%-10% new pricing actions in North America and Latin America that mostly ramp in 2027.

negative_highlights: Revenue of just $200,000 in the quarter, entirely grant and early access service revenue with no instrument or kit product revenue yet.
Net loss widened to $15.6 million ($0.12/share) from $13.6 million ($0.11) as opex rose 10% to $16.9 million and SG&A grew 15%.

Company is exploring an equity raise between now and mid-2027 despite runway into Q1 2028, and noted S10 grant funding for 2027 instrument purchases is largely behind, pushing institutional placements toward 2028.
positive_highlights: Three oncology assays (AKT1, EGFR, P53) delivered median CVs of 8.8%, 3.6%, and 6.6% after about a year of development, all below the 10% target and in line with the five-year tau assay.
2026 revenue outlook raised to exceed the prior ~$500,000 guide, with Q4 sequential growth expected excluding SEEDS.
SEEDS/ARPA-H consortium participation worth up to $6 million over four years, plus tau proteoform work published in Nature Methods with an accompanying News & Views.
summary: Nautilus reported Q3 FY2026 total revenue of $200,000, all from MJFF grant funding and early access service revenue, with no product revenue yet ahead of the Voyager launch. Operating expenses rose ~10% YoY to $16.9 million and net loss widened to $15.6 million ($0.12 per share) from $13.6 million ($0.11), with cash of $114.3 million and runway into Q1 2028. Management now expects total 2026 revenue to exceed its prior ~$500,000 outlook and sees Q4 revenue growing sequentially excluding any SEEDS/ARPA-H contribution; Voyager commercial launch is targeted for early 2027 with shipments mid-2027. The company disclosed it is exploring raising funds between now and mid-2027, and early oncology assay data (AKT1, EGFR, P53 median CVs of 8.8%, 3.6%, 6.6%) showed performance in line with tau.

negative_highlights: Gross margin of 26.4% reflected mix headwinds, including new construction-related equipment rising double digits and Jackson Supply running below the 27% range
Same-store SG&A grew faster than same-store sales, with quarterly variable expenses up roughly 10% and fixed costs up 3% in the quarter
Replacement units remain roughly 10-15% below levels of two years ago, and management described the consumer as uncertain
positive_highlights: Sales grew 7% to a record $2.22 billion, with same-store sales up 4% versus a year-ago quarter in which same-store sales were down
Year-to-date operating cash flow rose 79% to $304 million, and the company ended the quarter with $649 million cash and no debt
Jackson Supply grew 16% in its first quarter as part of Watsco; e-commerce sales up 12% year-to-date and reached 37% of sales over the last 12 months
summary: Watsco reported Q3 FY2026 sales up 7% to a record $2.22 billion (4% same-store), operating income of $225 million at a 10.1% margin, and EPS of $3.77, with gross margin at 26.4%; residential HVAC equipment rose 7% on both volume and price. Management made no explicit guidance revision, but cited improving monthly momentum since May, October revenue up double digits including acquisitions, and an expectation of more 'ordinary' OEM pricing in the coming 12 months. The largest change was continued M&A expansion, with Jackson Supply (up 16%) in the quarter and the roughly $500 million Granite Group acquisition closing in October. Gross margin absorbed mix headwinds (new construction up double digits, Jackson below the 27% range) of roughly 10-20 bps each.

negative_highlights: Full-year 2026 loan growth guidance cut to 5%-5.5%, with Q4 moderation from seasonal consumer softness and larger commercial payoffs
Employee benefit services pre-tax earnings fell 3.5% YoY on elevated startup legal costs tied to new collective investment trust fund launches
Net charge-off ratio rose 6 bps on $2.7 million of charge-offs on two individually assessed business lending relationships; NPL ratio up 2 bps and 30-89 day delinquencies up 9 bps
positive_highlights: Operating EPS of $1.27 up 16.5% YoY and 9.5% QoQ; operating PPNR per share of $1.77 up $0.21 YoY
NIM expanded 7 bps to 3.56% and net interest income rose 12% YoY to $143.5 million, the tenth consecutive quarter of NII expansion
Wealth management revenue +41% and insurance services pre-tax earnings +41% on revenue up 8.9% with expenses roughly flat
summary: Operating EPS of $1.27 rose from $1.09 a year prior and $1.16 linked quarter, a sixth consecutive quarter of record operating results, with net interest income up 12% YoY to $143.5 million and NIM expanding 7 bps to 3.56%. Wealth management revenue rose 41% YoY (ClearPoint added $2.1 million) and insurance services pre-tax earnings rose 41%, partly offset by employee benefit services pre-tax earnings down 3.5% on startup legal costs. Full-year 2026 loan growth guidance was lowered to 5%-5.5% from prior expectations on Q4 seasonal consumer softness and larger commercial payoffs, while NII growth guidance rose to 11%-11.5% and NIM is expected to exit at mid-to-high 3.5% after the accretive August securities sale. Core noninterest expense guidance is $553-$557 million (7%-8% growth), and expense growth ex-acquisitions is targeted at 4%-5% for 2027.

negative_highlights: Ratings revenue growth decelerated to 2% with margins contracting approximately 130 bps, and Q4 implies a slight year-over-year decline in transaction revenue
Billed issuance grew 8% but transaction revenue only 1%, a wider-than-usual mix-driven variance as investment grade (+28%) offset declines in high yield, bank loans, and structured finance
Q4 faces a wider organic-to-reported gap in Energy from the full-quarter Upstream Software divestiture impact, plus non-recurring one-time sales in Q3 unlikely to repeat
positive_highlights: Full-year guidance raised: organic constant currency growth to 7.5%-8.5%, adjusted operating margin expansion to 75-100 bps, and adjusted EPS to $17.70-$17.95
