Indices posted a 14th consecutive record revenue quarter, +20% with ETF AUM at $6.5 trillion (up 26%) and ETD revenue +19%
Energy returned to 6% organic growth with 190 bps of margin expansion to 48.1%, and Market Intelligence accelerated to 7% with 110 bps of margin expansion to 36.2%
summary: S&P Global reported Q3 FY2026 revenue growth of 7% organic constant currency and all-in, with adjusted operating margin expanding 60 bps to 53.5% (120 bps excluding OSTTRA), adjusted operating profit up 8% and EPS up 9%. Three of four divisions accelerated — Indices revenue +20% (margin +150 bps to 71.9%), Energy +6% (margin +190 bps to 48.1%), Market Intelligence +7% (margin +110 bps to 36.2%) — while Ratings decelerated to +2% with margin contraction of ~130 bps. Management raised full-year guidance: organic constant currency growth to 7.5%-8.5%, adjusted operating margin expansion to 75-100 bps, and adjusted EPS to $17.70-$17.95. The company also announced a strategic review of Capital IQ and associated data businesses, including potential separation, with no definitive timetable and the earliest meaningful update on the February call.

negative_highlights: RUCONEST's 14% growth included ~9 points from earlier-than-expected seasonal channel inventory, which management says may reverse in Q4
Full-year revenue guidance implies Q4 revenue of roughly $100-110 million, below Q3's $117.6 million, partly on inventory timing and $2-3 million Joenja revenue pulled forward
FALCON enrollment now expected to complete in H1 2027, with 145 of 180 patients by year-end, pushing top-line data a year beyond enrollment
positive_highlights: Total revenue grew 21% to $117.6 million, above analyst consensus, with operating profit up 89% to $29.9 million
Joenja global revenue rose 58% YoY to $23.8 million, U.S. patients on paid therapy up 17% to 136
Operating expense guidance lowered to $310-315 million (0-1% growth) with operating expenses flat YoY in the quarter
summary: Q3 FY2026 revenue rose 21% YoY to $117.6 million (above consensus), with Joenja up 58% to $23.8 million and RUCONEST up 14% to $93.8 million; operating profit rose 89% to $29.9 million and adjusted operating profit was $35 million versus $16 million a year ago. Full-year revenue guidance was tightened to $380-390 million (1-4% growth) and opex guidance lowered to $310-315 million. Management flagged that ~9 points of RUCONEST's 14% growth came from earlier-than-expected channel inventory, and $2-3 million of Joenja's international revenue was pulled forward from Q4, implying roughly $100-110 million in Q4 revenue. A CEO transition is underway with interim co-CEOs.

negative_highlights: Core EPS declined sequentially to $0.46 from $0.47, driven by lower capital structuring fees from longer transaction timelines
Origination pace was more measured with a closing ratio moderately below the ~5% historical average; total portfolio slipped to $29.2 billion from $29.3 billion
NAV per share decreased $0.04 sequentially to $19.31
positive_highlights: Announced agreement to acquire MFIC, expected to be modestly accretive to Core EPS, hold 200+ positions and expanding the portfolio to over 800 companies
Portfolio companies generated weighted average LTM organic EBITDA growth of ~7%, and first lien spreads on new originations widened 50 bps from the prior quarter

Issued $750 million of seven-year unsecured notes at 185 bps over Treasuries, the lowest new-issue spread and longest duration in the BDC sector during the quarter; non-accruals held flat at 2.4% of cost
summary: Core EPS of $0.46 fell from $0.47 in Q2, with GAAP net income per share of $0.44 versus $0.24 prior quarter on unrealized appreciation. NAV per share dipped $0.04 to $19.31, net leverage fell to 1.06x from 1.12x, and non-accruals held flat at 2.4% of cost (1.4% at fair value). Originations of $2.1 billion came in at a close rate moderately below the ~5% historical average, though post-quarter commitments of $1.1 billion and a $2.5 billion backlog were cited as historically strong. The company announced the acquisition of MFIC, expected to be modestly accretive to Core EPS, and declared a $0.48 Q4 dividend with $983 million ($1.37/share) of spillover income.

negative_highlights: Adjusted diluted EPS grew only ~1% and adjusted EBITDA rose just 3.3% on high single-digit sales growth, with management conceding sales-to-earnings conversion was below its standards
Gross margin pressured by raw material, supply chain and fuel costs plus Suvinil dilution; CBG adjusted segment margin fell 430 bps with Suvinil accounting for roughly 70% of the decline

2027 outlook calls for continued 'softer for longer' demand with few positive catalysts and low-to-mid-single-digit raw material inflation, and management declined to quantify 2027 pricing, citing timing mismatch between price and cost
positive_highlights: Consolidated sales grew high single digits with volume growth in every quarter of the year and sales at or above guidance in all three segments

Performance Coatings grew in every division and region, with general industrial up mid-teens, packaging and coil up low double digits, and Protective & Marine up mid-teens for a ninth straight quarter of at least high single-digit growth
Returned $749 million to shareholders in the quarter and $3 billion year-to-date; net debt to adjusted EBITDA at 2.4x and year-to-date operating cash up 10% ($232 million)
summary: Consolidated sales grew high single digits in Q3 (mid-single-digit price mix, low single-digit volume and acquisition contribution), with sales at or above guidance in all three segments, but adjusted diluted EPS rose only ~1% and adjusted EBITDA margin of 20.5% held within the target range. Full-year adjusted EPS guidance was narrowed to $11.85-$12.15 with the prior $12 midpoint unchanged (it had been raised in July), so the quarter is effectively in line on earnings despite the top-line beat. Gross margin came under pressure from higher raw material and supply chain costs, Suvinil dilution (~70% of the CBG margin decline), and mix toward lower-margin segments. Management framed 2027 as 'softer for longer' with few positive catalysts, low-to-mid-single-digit raw material inflation, and ~$75 million of expected cost savings, while declining to size 2027 pricing.

negative_highlights: Same-store revenue and NOI grew only 0.5% each and full-year same-store NOI guidance remains negative at -0.3%
New supply continues to pressure Sun Belt markets including Houston, Tampa and Charlotte, with west Florida likely to see more note weakness in-term pressure
NSA integration is creating near-term noise, including elevated bad debt and repair and maintenance activity
positive_highlights: Core FFO guidance raised $0.10 to $16.90-$17.10, the second raise this year, with same-store revenue outlook up 45 bps and NOI up 85 bps
Average move-in rents improved 9% YoY, strongest since 2Q 2022 and up 28% from Q4 2025
Non-same-store NOI grew 22% and ancillary NOI grew 21%, both ahead of expectations, while expense growth was roughly flat
summary: PSA reported Q3 FY2026 core FFO of $4.34/share, up 0.7% YoY, with same-store revenue and NOI each up 0.5% and same-store revenue accelerating 110 bps sequentially into positive territory. Management raised full-year core FFO guidance by $0.10 to $16.90-$17.10 (midpoint $17) for the second time this year, lifting same-store revenue growth to +0.25% and NOI to -0.3%, improvements of 45 bps and 85 bps versus the prior outlook. Average move-in rents rose 9%, the strongest since 2Q 2022, and occupancy remained ahead of the prior year, while October trends were consistent but below the 9% move-in rate mark. The company closed NSA and Public Storage Canada, guiding both to a neutral 2026 impact with tenant cleanup driving near-term bad debt and R&M noise.

negative_highlights: ROAE declined to 15.04% from 16.67% on the 11% increase in weighted average shares from the offering
Non-interest income fell to $1.7 million from $1.9 million on lower loan referral income and weaker venture-fund earnings
Non-interest expense rose $1 million sequentially and average cost of deposits increased 3 bps to 2.19%
positive_highlights: Net income rose 13% to $21.9 million and pre-tax pre-provision income rose 13% to $32 million sequentially
Loans held for investment grew $184.5 million, or ~16% annualized, reaching $4.7 billion
NIM expanded 6 bps to 3.69% and the efficiency ratio improved to 39.13% from 40.91%
summary: Net income rose to $21.9 million from $19.4 million in Q2 2026, with basic EPS of $0.92 despite an 11% increase in weighted average shares from the July offering. Loans held for investment grew $184.5 million (~16% annualized) to $4.7 billion, NIM expanded 6 bps to 3.69%, and the efficiency ratio improved to 39.13% from 40.91%. Management guided to 10%-12% loan growth in Q4 and 2027, a NIM range of 3.65%-3.75%, and roughly $200,000 of added Q4 expense; the $130 million net offering lifted CET1 to 12.52%, up 255 bps, while ROAE fell to 15.04% from 16.67%. A $2.5 million provision was recorded and non-performing loans eased to 0.28% of total loans from 0.30%, tied mainly to one CRA credit of $11.4 million.

Robinhood reported record Q3 FY2026 revenue of $1.4 billion, up 12% year-over-year, with record adjusted EBITDA of $808 million (up 9%, 57% margin). GAAP EPS was $0.51 including a -$0.07 investment mark; adjusted EPS was $0.60, a newly introduced metric. Transaction revenue set a record on ~50% YoY growth in equities, options, and margin volumes, event contracts grew 7x YoY, and platform assets reached nearly $400 billion. Management trimmed the top end of full-year adjusted OpEx guidance by $25 million to $2.675-$2.75 billion and noted October net deposits above $13 billion, already exceeding the 20% annual growth goal, while flagging Q4 ADVs about 5% lighter than the record Q3.

negative_highlights: Gross margin of 57.3% was below expectations, down 178 bps QoQ, on lower high-margin DME iLet revenue from distributor destocking
Withdrew the 3D Intelligence 510(k) at FDA's request over simulator validation, pushing launch to ~mid-2027 and lowering the near-term pipeline visibility
Operating expenses rose 46% YoY to $46.9M, and Mint gross margin is expected to be dilutive in 2027
positive_highlights: Record Q3 net sales of $35.5M grew ~30% YoY, driven by new patient starts and a growing pharmacy installed base
Raised the low end of FY2026 revenue guidance to $124-126M from $121-126M, with Q4 revenue expected at $29-31M
Gross margin expanded 179 bps YoY to 57.3%, and ~69% of new patient starts came from multiple daily injections, with >30% estimated Type 2
summary: Beta Bionics reported record Q3 revenue of $35.5M, up ~30% YoY, with gross margin of 57.3% down 178 bps QoQ but up 179 bps YoY, and it raised the low end of full-year revenue guidance to $124-126M from $121-126M while maintaining full-year gross margin guidance of 58.5-59.5%. Q3 gross margin missed expectations due to unfavorable DME mix, which management expects to reverse in Q4. The company disclosed that it withdrew its 3D Intelligence 510(k) at FDA's request over simulator validation questions, pushing the expected launch to mid-2027, and it now expects the Q4 Mint-related revenue deferral to be up to $8.5M rather than $10M. It also completed a $161M net capital raise, ending the quarter with ~$374M in cash and investments, and expects Mint U.S. commercialization in Q1 2027.

negative_highlights: Non-performing loans rose to $39.2 million or 80 bps of loans from 74 bps at 6/30, with problem assets up a tenth consecutive quarter
Provision of $4.8 million (~0.4% of loans annualized) exceeded the 0.2-0.25% forecast range on a specific reserve for one commercial relationship

Non-interest expense of $44.8 million including $3.5 million merger costs came in slightly above the forecast range ($37.3 million ex-Highpoint and merger costs vs. $36-37 million), and 2026 cost saves are tracking below the earlier 50% target
positive_highlights: Net interest income grew 15.4% linked quarter and 21.8% year over year, the 13th consecutive quarter of NII growth
Net interest margin expanded 11 bps to 3.82% and 5 bps ex-purchase accounting accretion, with ~$737 million of loans and securities repricing over six quarters at a 4.74% weighted yield
Organic commercial loan growth of $123 million (nearly 21% annualized) and deposits up $115.8 million (9.4% annualized), both above the original outlook ranges
summary: Q3 2026 net income was $17.9 million ($0.80 diluted EPS) versus $17.5 million ($0.84) a year ago; excluding $2.7 million after-tax merger costs, adjusted net income was $20.6 million ($0.92). Net interest income rose 21.8% YoY to a 13th straight quarterly increase and NIM expanded 11 bps to 3.82% (3.76% ex-purchase accounting); organic loans grew $116.6 million (10.5% annualized) and deposits $115.8 million (9.4% annualized), both above the original outlook ranges. Provision of $4.8 million (~0.4% of loans) exceeded the 0.2-0.25% forecast on a specific reserve for one commercial relationship, and non-performing loans rose to 80 bps from 74 bps. The Highpoint conversion remains set for November 9, with roughly $3 million of remaining merger costs in Q4 and cost savings largely landing in the 2027 expense run rate; no formal updated full-year guidance was issued beyond confirming prior margin and loan-growth trends.

negative_highlights: Fresh pork swung to an $89 million operating loss from a $10 million profit, with processing spread down about 35% year-over-year and 28% sequentially
Hog production operating profit fell to $34 million from $89 million on lower realized hog prices and $74 million lower sales to joint venture partners
Full-year sales outlook cut to down low single digits from roughly flat and total company adjusted operating profit reset to $900 million-$1 billion
positive_highlights: Packaged meats operating profit rose $4 million to $230 million and margin expanded 80 bps to 11.6%, the second-highest third quarter on record
Packaged meats volume grew about 1% against a 3.3% industry decline across top 25 categories, with volume share up 0.4 points and gains in all five largest categories
Net debt to adjusted EBITDA of 0.5x, $3.5 billion liquidity including $1.2 billion cash, and nine-month operating cash flow of $365 million, up $244 million year-over-year
summary: Smithfield reported Q3 FY2026 adjusted operating profit of $145 million (4.2% margin) versus $310 million (8.3%) a year ago, on consolidated sales of $3.4 billion, down 8.3%. Adjusted diluted EPS fell to $0.26 from $0.58 and adjusted net income to $103 million from $230 million, driven by a fresh pork operating loss of $89 million (versus $10 million profit) and hog production profit falling to $34 million from $89 million. Full-year total company sales guidance was cut to down low single digits from roughly flat, and total company adjusted operating profit is now guided to $900 million-$1 billion, while packaged meats was narrowed to $1.09-$1.14 billion with a modest midpoint increase from two months of Nathan's Famous. Packaged meats was the bright spot, with operating profit up $4 million to $230 million and margin up 80 bps to 11.6% on 0.2% volume growth.

negative_highlights: Annualized net new bookings were $37 million, down from $84 million in Q3 last year, with the decline concentrated in residential (Apartments.com and Homes.com) amid insufficient sales capacity.
Full-year revenue guidance excluding Zonda is $35 million or 1% lower than in July, and revenue ex-Zonda came in $7 million below the guidance midpoint.
Apartments.com revenue growth slowed to 6% from 9% in Q2, paid properties fell 2% sequentially to 91,155, and Domain revenue declined 5% pro forma in a weak Australian market.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA reached a record $229 million, up $45 million or 25% QoQ and $16 million above the top end of the $190-210 million guidance range; margin of 24% marked a seventh consecutive quarter of expansion.
Adjusted EPS was $0.38, up 65% YoY and above the $0.31-0.34 range, with adjusted operating expenses down 2% YoY.
Full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance midpoint raised to $830 million, and management identified ~$200 million of incremental efficiency opportunities on top of $150 million in 2026 savings.
summary: Revenue rose 14% YoY to $952 million, but excluding Zonda it was $933 million, about $7 million below the guidance midpoint, with the shortfall split 60/40 between Domain transaction volume and Apartments subscription revenue. Adjusted EBITDA hit a record $229 million, ~$16 million above the top end of the $190-210 million range on cost control, and adjusted EPS of $0.38 beat the $0.31-0.34 range. Full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance was raised to a $830 million midpoint (24% above the prior record) and the 2028 $1.25 billion target reconfirmed, but full-year revenue guidance excluding Zonda is $35 million (1%) below July and annualized net new bookings fell to $37 million from $84 million a year ago. The prior-period improvement was driven by cost actions and Zonda inclusion rather than top-line acceleration.

negative_highlights: Total loans declined $110M (3.8% annualized) and total deposits fell $447M, including ~$85M of true attrition
PPNR per share declined to $1.42 from $1.50 in Q2
Service fee revenue fell ~4% QoQ to $39.4M as mortgage banking revenue weakened on higher rates
positive_highlights: NIM expanded 24 bps to 3.82% from 3.58% in Q2, with loan yields up 17 bps and funding costs improving
Cost saves reached ~70% of the original $68.8M target, with total savings expected to slightly exceed the original target
Criticized credits improved: special mention fell $23.8M and substandard fell $39.9M QoQ, with net charge-offs at 11 bps annualized
summary: Adjusted EPS was $1.03 with adjusted ROAA of 1.23%, and PPNR per share fell to $1.42 from $1.50 in Q2. NIM expanded 24 bps to 3.82% and service fee revenue was $39.4M (down ~4% QoQ, 21.9% of revenue), while total loans declined $110M (3.8% annualized) and total deposits fell $447M. Q4 guidance calls for mid-single-digit loan and deposit growth (ex-broker), NIM in the mid-380s and an efficiency ratio in the low 60s, with 2027 EPS targets reiterated only qualitatively. Adjusted non-interest expense declined $0.8M QoQ and cost saves were at ~70% of the $68.8M target.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA outlook held flat as ~$15 million lower network services contribution offset data center outperformance
Cash adjusted EBITDA margin declined ~50 bps YoY (DISH churn and lower services), and U.S./Canada organic growth was flat (~4% ex-DISH) with new leasing stepping down in Q3
Latin America organic growth declined ~2% on elevated Brazil churn; services gross margin fell to north of 40% from ~50% on construction management mix
positive_highlights: Data center revenue growth outlook raised to ~16% from 15% last quarter and 13% at the start of the year, with CoreSite leasing on track for a record year
Third guidance raise of 2026: property revenue +$55 million at midpoint and AFFO per share +$0.02, with ~4% organic growth (~7% cash FX-neutral ex-DISH)

Capital returns: ~$315 million repurchased in Q3 plus $68 million through Oct 20 (over $950 million since Q4 2025), new $2 billion authorization leaving ~$3.1 billion capacity, leverage 4.9x within target
summary: AMT raised its 2026 outlook for the third time this year: property revenue up $55 million at the midpoint (~1%), AFFO per share up $0.02, while adjusted EBITDA guidance was held flat. Q3 property revenue grew ~5% (cash FX-neutral, ex straight-line) and ~7% normalized for one-time DISH churn, with data center revenue up ~16% and total organic tenant billings growth of ~1% (~4% ex-DISH). The EBITDA hold reflected ~$15 million lower network services contribution offsetting ~$10 million data center and ~$5 million other outperformance, and cash adjusted EBITDA margins declined ~50 bps (up 10 bps ex-DISH). Management called 2026 the trough year for U.S. organic growth and AFFO per share growth, expecting an inflection in 2027, and disclosed a ~$202 million Canada sale, ~$315 million of Q3 buybacks, and a new $2 billion repurchase authorization.

negative_highlights: Reported Q3 loss of $2.6 million versus $0.5 million operating profit in the prior-year period
Non-GAAP operating loss of $2.1 million versus $1.1 million profit a year ago
Jack's Flight Club revenue declined due to lower member acquisition in Q1 and Q2
positive_highlights: Club Members grew 65% year-over-year, the largest number of additions in any quarter
Average U.S. member acquisition cost fell to $54 from $62 in Q2, improving despite higher spend
Cash and equivalents plus restricted cash rose $1.2 million sequentially to $8.8 million, and 256,898 shares were repurchased
summary: Travelzoo reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $22.9 million, up 3% year-over-year ($23.0 million in constant currency), but swung to a $2.6 million loss from $0.5 million operating profit a year earlier; non-GAAP operating loss was $2.1 million versus $1.1 million profit prior year. The loss reflects deliberate investment in Club Members, which grew 65% year-over-year at an average acquisition cost of $54 (down from $62 in Q2). Management guided to year-over-year revenue growth in Q4 and subsequent quarters and projects a positive $1.20 impact on 2027 EPS, while noting near-term earnings fluctuations are likely.

negative_highlights: Full-year underlying margin guidance was cut to flat to up 20 bps from prior 50-70 bps of expansion, and Q3 adjusted EBITDA margin contracted 90 bps to 35.4% (40 bps underlying), citing tech investment and higher legal/regulatory expense
Q4 organic constant currency growth guided to decelerate to 3%-6% (3%-5% ex-FICO) as mortgage inquiries are expected to fall more than 20% in Q4 and roughly 10% for the full year
2027 net interest expense expected to rise roughly $60M from swap replacement and higher SOFR; mortgage revenue growth (21%, or 5% ex-FICO) slowed sequentially, and consumer interactive declined 3%
positive_highlights: Adjusted diluted EPS of $1.25 rose 14% YoY and beat the high end of guidance by $0.04; revenue and adjusted EBITDA each exceeded the high end by $3M and $2M
International returned to double-digit organic constant currency growth at 10%, with India and Latin America both up 18% and Mexico tracking ahead of the acquisition case
summary: TransUnion beat the high end of Q3 FY2026 guidance on revenue ($3M above), adjusted EBITDA ($2M above), and adjusted diluted EPS ($1.25, up 14% YoY and $0.04 above the high end). Organic constant currency revenue grew 8% (5.5% ex-FICO mortgage royalties), with international re-accelerating to 10% on 18% growth in both India and Latin America and U.S. financial services up 11%. Management raised the low end of full-year revenue and EBITDA guidance and lifted EPS growth guidance by one point to 12%-13% (to $4.81-$4.88), though Q4 organic CC growth is guided to decelerate to 3%-6% on declining mortgage inquiries, and underlying margin guidance was cut to flat to up 20 bps from prior 50-70 bps expansion. Key changes versus prior periods: leverage fell to 2.5x, buyback authorization rose $1B to $2B, and 2027 net interest expense is expected to rise roughly $60M on swap replacement and higher SOFR.

negative_highlights: Mobile revenue fell 4% YoY to $411 million and is guided down mid-teens YoY in Q4

Book-to-bill and lead times signal tightness, but pricing remains only cost-offset with 2026 price declines now expected neutral (versus low single-digit decline originally planned), not a demand-driven price uplift
positive_highlights: Revenue rose 19% YoY to $3.79 billion, exceeding the outlook across all end markets, with every region growing double digits YoY
Non-GAAP operating margin expanded 330 bps YoY to 37.1% and non-GAAP EPS grew 35% YoY to $4.20, roughly 2x revenue growth
Data center revenue outlook raised to exceed $500 million this year with a path to over $1 billion in a couple of years; Q4 gross margin guided to 59% and 2027 gross margin target of 60%
summary: NXP reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $3.79 billion, up 19% YoY (22% excluding MEMS sensors), with non-GAAP gross margin of 58.6% (+160 bps YoY), operating margin of 37.1% (+330 bps YoY), and non-GAAP EPS of $4.20, up 35% YoY, exceeding guidance across all end markets. Q4 guidance is revenue of $3.85 billion (±$100 million), up 15% YoY, with non-GAAP gross margin of 59% and EPS of $4.36 at the midpoint. Management outlined 2027 expectations of double-digit revenue growth, gross margins expanding to 60%, and data center revenue reaching $1 billion by 2028, and authorized an incremental $5 billion buyback bringing total authorization to roughly $6.3 billion.

negative_highlights: Filtration revenue fell 11% and was slightly worse than expected, with full-year outlook cut to flat-to-slightly-down as system orders shift into 2027
Adjusted gross margin declined 30 bps to 53% on product mix and inflation
GAAP results included a $41M intangible asset impairment tied to a legacy IP license that did not lead to a positive outcome
positive_highlights: Revenue hit a record $209M, surpassing the prior Q2 2022 peak, with 12.5% organic growth
Chromatography grew over 50% and Proteins over 40%, with consumables up 20% and services up over 20%
Adjusted operating margin expanded 170 bps to 15.9% on only 5% adjusted OpEx growth; full-year operating margin guidance raised to 16-16.3%
summary: Repligen reported record Q3 FY2026 revenue of $209M, up 11% reported and 12.5% organic, with adjusted EPS of $0.53 versus $0.46 (+15%) and adjusted operating margin of 15.9% (+170 bps). Adjusted gross margin slipped 30 bps to 53% on mix and inflation, consistent with guidance that Q3 would be the 2026 gross margin low. The company raised full-year revenue guidance to $844-852M (14.5-15.5% reported, 12-13% organic, +50 bps at the midpoint) and lifted adjusted operating income to $135-139M and EPS to $2.05-2.09 (+$0.01 at the midpoint), incorporating ~$24M of Q4 BioLife contribution; Filtration was revised to flat-to-slightly-down with system deliveries pushed to 2027.

negative_highlights: Service Center organic growth moderated to 3.5% from 8% last quarter, and segment EBITDA margin declined 35 bps to 13.6%.
Full-year EPS guidance raise was driven by a lower diluted share count, not an improved operating outlook; sales and margin guidance were unchanged.
Q2 organic growth guidance of 6%-8% sits below October month-to-date growth of roughly 10%, reflecting anticipated November-December comparison headwinds.
positive_highlights: Engineered Solutions organic sales grew 14.1% and segment EBITDA rose 24.7%, with margin expanding 129 bps to 15.1%.
Engineered Solutions orders rose more than 30% year over year, with book-to-bill at its highest level in more than four years.
Gross margin expanded 25 bps to 30.4% (nearly 50 bps excluding LIFO) and EPS grew 12.7% to $2.97.
summary: Applied Industrial reported Q1 FY2027 sales up 7.6% (7.1% organic) with EPS of $2.97, up 12.7% year over year, and organic growth in line with the mid-August outlook. Gross margin expanded 25 bps to 30.4% and EBITDA margin rose 22 bps to 12.4%, both despite higher LIFO expense. Full-year EPS guidance was modestly raised to $11.70-$12.20 from $11.65-$12.15 solely on a lower share count, while sales guidance of up 4%-6.5% and EBITDA margin of 12.5%-12.8% were maintained. Q2 organic growth is guided to 6%-8% versus October month-to-date of roughly 10%, with management citing prudence on trade, geopolitical, and interest rate uncertainty and tougher November-December comparisons.

positive_highlights: Consolidated net income up over 80% YoY; U.S. mining operating income more than doubled YoY.
Grasberg ramp-up reached 67% of capacity; targeting 80% by mid-2027 and full capacity by end-2027.
Q4 copper sales expected +17% and gold sales nearly tripling vs Q3; 2027 copper sales growth over 20% and gold over 50%.
summary: FCX reported Q3 2026 with copper sales rising for a third consecutive quarter, consolidated net income up over 80% YoY, and U.S. mining operating income more than doubling, aided by Grasberg ramp-up to 67% of capacity and higher copper prices (~$6.58/lb vs $6.09 YTD average). However, management trimmed 2026 copper sales by ~2% (U.S. and Chile shortfalls) and 2027 by ~2.5%, while raising 2027 capex to $5.2B (up ~$400M) on equipment and inflation; 2026 unit cash cost guidance held at $1.90/lb. Q4 is expected to be the strongest of the year with copper sales +17% and gold nearly tripling QoQ. Costs remain pressured by ~$500M higher energy costs vs 2025 and acid more than doubling, partially offset by moly strength.

negative_highlights: SG&A rose to 37.6% of sales from 32%, driven by My Medic advertising and $1 million of tariff-refund-related variable compensation
Net debt increased to $29.7 million from $23.1 million a year ago; inventories were deliberately built up $8-10 million and receivables up ~20%
Management noted rising shipping and freight costs (China freight tripled) and consumer stress, and flagged easy promotional comparisons aiding the Westcott result
positive_highlights: Net sales rose 18% to $58 million and adjusted EPS grew 20% to $0.55 excluding the tariff-refund benefit
U.S. segment sales up 20% (10% ex-My Medic) with strong back-to-school and Westcott demand, and Spill Magic up 34% year to date on new capacity
Gross margin expanded to 45.3% from 39.1%, with the underlying mix helped by higher-margin My Medic DTC sales
summary: Acme United reported Q3 FY2026 net sales of $58.0 million, up 18% YoY (10% excluding the $4 million My Medic acquisition), with GAAP EPS of $0.80 versus $0.46. Results were boosted by a $6 million IEEPA tariff refund, of which $4 million was recognized in COGS; adjusted for the ~$1 million net after-tax benefit, EPS was $0.55 (+20%) and net income $2.4 million (+24%). Gross margin was 45.3% versus 39.1%, including a 690 bps refund benefit and a 310 bps DMT closure drag; SG&A rose to 37.6% of sales from 32% on My Medic advertising and $1 million of variable comp. Management guided to a seasonally strong Q4, cited new First Aid business booked for 2027, the DMT Marlborough closure (over $1 million annual savings from January 2027), and flagged rising freight and inflation being offset by automation.

Pentair reported Q3 FY2026 sales of $976 million with adjusted operating income of $242 million (24.8% ROS) and adjusted EPS of $1.18, above the $1.05-$1.08 guidance range, though core sales fell 5% on an 18% Pool decline. Flow sales rose 4% to $262 million (ROS up 250 bps to 26%) and Water Solutions rose 1% to $422 million (ROS up 370 bps to 29%), while Pool fell 18% to $291 million with ROS near 25% as the channel destock concluded. Full-year EPS guidance midpoint of $4.70 was reaffirmed, not raised, with total sales seen down ~3% and Q4 EPS guided to ~$1.15. The Taco acquisition closed October 1 (~$560M 2026 sales, >$620M expected in 2027) and Pool watch-through is framed flattish at ~$1.45 billion for a ~14% 2027 watch-in rebound, accretive in 2027.

negative_highlights: Fuel, driver investment, and claim reserve development created a $0.18 per share sequential EPS drag, leaving adjusted operating margin at just 2.2%
Q4 adjusted EPS guided to only modest sequential improvement from $0.16 as lower equipment gains, higher interest, and tax normalization offset cost abatement
TTS average truck growth guidance was tightened to 16%-17% from 16%-18%, and One-Way truck count fell 37% year over year to 1,673
positive_highlights: Dedicated revenue ex-fuel rose 52% year over year with revenue per truck per week up nearly 6% (legacy Dedicated up 7%) and retention above 95%
One-Way revenue per truck per week surged 34% and One-Way adjusted operating margin expanded more than 800 bps year over year

Logistics returned to positive adjusted operating income with gross margin up over 600 bps sequentially; FirstFleet delivered $6 million of savings in 8 months and is on track for $18 million in synergies
summary: Werner reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $951 million, up 23% year over year, adjusted operating income of $21 million (up 92%), adjusted operating margin of 2.2% (up 80 bps), and adjusted EPS of $0.16 versus a $0.19 year-over-year improvement. Results absorbed roughly $0.18 per share of sequential drag from fuel, driver recruiting investment, and adverse FirstFleet claim reserve development, which management characterized as largely temporary. Guidance was mixed: full-year TTS average truck growth was tightened to 16%-17% from 16%-18%, Dedicated revenue per truck per week guidance was raised to up 4%-5%, net CapEx was lowered to $190-$205 million from $215-$250 million on OEM timing, and used equipment gains guidance was raised to $14-$16 million. Q4 adjusted EPS is guided to only modest sequential improvement from $0.16, with lower gains and higher interest/tax offsetting cost abatement.

negative_highlights: Credit loss expense jumped to $4.5 million from $1.2 million, with annualized net charge-offs at 27 bps versus 8 bps prior quarter
Payoffs of $283 million kept loan balances flat despite strong production; year-to-date payoffs are up 65% and over $250 million
Two multifamily loans were downgraded following New York City rent control changes, and NIM benefited from roughly $700,000 of one-time items (~4 bps)
positive_highlights: Net interest income grew 5.8% sequentially and NIM expanded 8 bps to 3.4%, driving a 10.8% rise in pre-provision net revenue
Loan production of $544 million rose 46.2% QoQ with every loan category increasing; SBA sold at an 8.1% premium versus 7.92% in Q2
Efficiency ratio improved more than 200 bps to 52%, and 55.6% of net income was returned via dividends and $4.9 million of buybacks
summary: Hanmi reported Q3 FY2026 net income of $23.7 million, or $0.80 per diluted share, with pre-provision net revenue up 10.8% sequentially on 5.8% NII growth and an 8 bp NIM increase to 3.4%. The efficiency ratio improved over 200 bps to 52%, deposits rose 1.4% (core +1.9%), and loan production hit $544 million, up 46.2% QoQ, though payoffs of $283 million kept loan balances roughly flat. Credit loss expense rose to $4.5 million from $1.2 million on a $3.2 million partial charge-off tied to a CRE loan sale, lifting annualized net charge-offs to 27 bps. Management guided to low single-digit loan growth for 2026 and low-to-mid single-digit for 2027, and expects Q4 buybacks at the same dollar run rate as prior quarters.

negative_highlights: $13 million realized loss on the multifamily loan converted to REO drove distributable earnings down to $0.07 per share from $0.24 before realized losses
Book value per common share declined $0.10 to $10.85, reflecting credit loss expense from portfolio growth and macroeconomic conditions
Total leverage rose to 4.03x from 3.32x at June 30, reducing capacity for further balance sheet growth as management described the book shifting to one-in, one-out
positive_highlights: Net interest income increased approximately 13% quarter-over-quarter, with Q3 originations of $772.7 million not yet contributing a full period
Net earning assets grew 14% quarter-over-quarter to $4.9 billion and 36% year-over-year; portfolio 100% performing with weighted average risk rating unchanged at 3.0
Closed $1 billion TRTX 2026-FL8 CRE CLO, pushing non-mark-to-market financing to approximately 85% and weighted average cost of funds down to 1.81% from 1.95% a year ago
summary: TRTX reported Q3 2026 GAAP net income of $5.8 million or $0.08 per diluted share and distributable earnings of $5.1 million or $0.07 per share after a $13 million realized loss on a multifamily loan conversion to REO; DE before realized losses was $18.1 million or $0.24 per share, covering the dividend. Net interest income rose 13% quarter-over-quarter and net earning assets grew 14% to $4.9 billion, while book value per share slipped $0.10 to $10.85 and the CECL reserve fell to $76.1 million (147 bps of commitments) from 179 bps. No explicit forward guidance was provided; management noted Q3 originations closed late in the quarter and have yet to contribute fully to earnings. Leverage rose to 4.03x from 3.32x and the board approved a new $50 million buyback after exhausting the prior $25 million plan.

negative_highlights: Institutional and specialty performance was only consistent as North American restaurant food traffic declined mid-single digits, with management stating it is 'not satisfied' with results and should be outperforming by a wider margin
Commodity costs are expected to remain high through the end of next year, with raw material assumptions of elevated levels persisting
CoolIT creates roughly a 12% EPS drag in Q4 (up from ~10% in Q3) and a 5-point EPS headwind in H1 2027 from amortization and interest
positive_highlights: Global High-Tech organic sales grew 63%, with CoolIT more than doubling sales since acquisition and Ovivo delivering strong double-digit growth versus pre-acquisition levels
Organic OI margin expanded to 19.6% while organic OI growth accelerated to 11%, maintaining organic gross margin despite significant commodity cost inflation
Life Sciences organic sales grew 17% with Q3 margins around 23% versus prior high-teens guidance, and management reiterated a path to 30% OI margin
summary: Ecolab reported 7% organic sales growth with organic OI margin expanding to 19.6% and organic OI growth accelerating to 11%, as every business outperformed its end market despite significant commodity cost inflation. Growth engines accelerated sharply — Global High-Tech organic sales up 63%, Life Sciences up 17%, Digital up 34%, and Pest up 8% — though Institutional growth remained under pressure from mid-single-digit declines in North American restaurant traffic. For 2027, management guided organic growth to the upper end of the 5%-7% range, adjusted OI margin to 20%, and adjusted EPS growth of 12%-15% (mid-teens underlying) with a 5-point headwind in H1 and 5-point tailwind in H2 from M&A amortization and interest. The quarter marked an inflection from Q2's commodity cost transition, with pricing running at 5%-6% versus a 2%-3% steady state.

Nucor reported Q3 net earnings of $1.3 billion or $5.80 per share, exceeding the midpoint of guidance by ~3.5% on higher shipments and average watching prices, with EBITDA of approximately $2.3 billion (margin above 20%, highest in three years). Steel mills pre-tax earnings rose $232 million sequentially to $1.8 billion on record shipments above 7.2 million tons (up 2%), while steel products pre-tax earnings rose $112 million to $465 million with EBITDA margin up ~200 bps. Q4 guidance is for consolidated earnings in line with or modestly higher than Q3, with steel mills and steel products stable and raw materials slightly lower; the full-year shipment growth outlook holds near the high end of the 5%-10% range. Free cash flow was $1.6 billion in the quarter, capital spending is moderating toward or slightly below the $2.5 billion full-year estimate, and startup costs at the West Virginia sheet mill are expected to stay elevated in 2027 similar to or higher than 2026.

negative_highlights: No Helios II lease signed: advanced summer discussions were abandoned on terms, pushing a major contracted-cash-flow catalyst out with delivery not before 2028
Digital assets segment EBITDA still negative despite $71 million of adjusted gross profit, which management attributed partly to a one-time accounting adjustment
ERCOT reclassified Caspian from base load to studied load and Galaxy's reconsideration request was denied, with clarity on 2.6 GW of expansion projects not expected until April 2027
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA of $455 million and net income of $323 million versus a $42 million treasury segment loss in Q2

Operating businesses adjusted gross profit rose more than 75% to ~$150 million, with data centers contributing ~$79 million of adjusted gross profit and $69 million of adjusted EBITDA in the first full Helios phase I quarter
Assets under stake grew 64% to $4.6 billion with over $400 million of gross new ETH/SOL inflows from large ETF providers; AUM rose over 30% to $5.9 billion
summary: Galaxy reported Q3 net income of $323 million, adjusted gross profit of $569 million and adjusted EBITDA of $455 million, a sharp swing from Q2 driven by market appreciation of the investment portfolio and the first full quarter of Helios phase I leasing revenue. Operating businesses generated ~$150 million of adjusted gross profit (up over 75% from $86 million) and $60 million of adjusted EBITDA versus ~$1 million in Q2; digital assets produced $71 million of adjusted gross profit but remained EBITDA-negative. Helios I phase II remains on schedule and fully funded, with management targeting an annualized leasing revenue run rate of $800-850 million exiting 2027, but no Helios II lease was signed after summer talks were abandoned on terms. The board authorized an additional $200 million buyback after completing the prior $200 million authorization.

negative_highlights: Utility Solutions organic growth outlook lowered to +6-7% for the full year, driven by a meter component shortage and slower substation control house ramp
Grid Automation declined 4% organically in Q3 on the temporary component availability headwind
Q4 segment margins implied down YoY, primarily in Utility, with higher inflation and about $5M of IEEPA customer considerations spilling into Q4
positive_highlights: Electrical Solutions adjusted operating margin expanded 400 bps YoY to 24.8%, with adjusted operating profit up 80%
Data center sales grew over 80% organically in Q3, with data center expected to be about 15% of Electrical segment revenue exiting the year
Full-year 2026 adjusted EPS guidance raised to $20.40-$20.60, implying 12-13% YoY growth, alongside $500M+ YTD backlog build (up ~30%)
summary: Hubbell reported Q3 FY2026 net sales of $1.873B, up 25% YoY (11% organic, 13% acquisition), with adjusted operating profit up 33% to $477M at a 25.5% margin (up 160 bps) and adjusted EPS of $5.91, up 14%. Electrical Solutions led with 51% sales growth including 22% organic and data center organic sales up over 80%; Utility grew 5% organically with a meter component shortage shifting roughly $15M of revenue into Q4. The company raised full-year 2026 guidance to +18-19% sales growth (10-11% organic) and adjusted EPS of $20.40-$20.60, with over 20% adjusted operating profit growth, though it slightly lowered its Utility organic outlook to +6-7%. Management cited $500M+ year-to-date backlog build (up about 30%) and 2027 capacity investment roughly doubling to about $50M per quarter.

negative_highlights: Gross margin remained negative at -31% versus +4% in the year-ago quarter; net loss of $52.9 million and adjusted loss of $0.78 per ADS
Q4 production guided down to 35,000-45,000 MT from 53,469 MT in Q3 amid weak demand and ~700,000 MT industry inventory
Share repurchase deferred pending policy clarity; operating cash flow was -$215 million for the nine months
positive_highlights: Sales volume rose to 46,910 MT from 15,190 MT in Q2; revenue of $194.2 million vs $62.7 million sequentially
Average total production cost and cash cost fell 9.7% and 7.4% QoQ to record lows of $5.37/kg and $4.23/kg
Liquid assets rose to $2.06 billion from $1.92 billion at Q2-end with zero debt
summary: Daqo reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $194.2 million, up sharply from $62.7 million in Q2 and $44.6 million a year ago, driven by sales volume jumping to 46,910 MT from 15,190 MT as the company shifted to a market-oriented sales strategy. However, gross margin remained deeply negative at -31% (vs -132% in Q2 and +4% a year ago), operating loss was $78.6 million, and net loss per ADS was $0.78, versus adjusted EPS of $0.05 a year earlier. Q4 production is guided to 35,000-45,000 MT (down from Q3's 53,469 MT) as management cuts utilization to support de-stocking, with full-year 2026 output of 175,000-185,000 MT. Management flagged continued policy uncertainty on anti-involution enforcement, elevated industry inventory of about 700,000 MT, and a possible industry-wide utilization cut to ~35%, while outlining an AIDC diversification with ~CNY 1 billion 2027 capex and a buyback being considered but not committed.

negative_highlights: Year-to-date O&M was $0.16 unfavorable, driven by additional storm activity plus reinvestments
Parent and other was $0.16 unfavorable year-to-date, primarily from NorthStar performance
Weather was a $0.05 unfavorable variance versus last year, and year-to-go assumptions embed a $0.09 unfavorable normal-weather variance
positive_highlights: Year-to-date adjusted EPS of $2.95 is $0.29 favorable to last year, with full-year guidance reaffirmed toward the high end
Gas rate order approved $139 million (~60% of the final ask) at a 9.8% ROE and 50% equity ratio; Staff recommended $265 million, or 60% of the $443 million electric ask
NorthStar restructuring is more than 35% signed or closed, on track to complete by year-end, with management indicating the funding benefit could exceed the $500 million target
summary: CMS reported year-to-date adjusted EPS of $2.95, $0.29 favorable to last year, on adjusted net income of $915 million, and reaffirmed full-year 2026 guidance of $3.83-$3.90 with confidence toward the high end. 2027 guidance of $4.08-$4.17 was also reaffirmed, incorporating the NorthStar restructuring, with long-term 6%-8% EPS growth still framed as toward the high end (7% or better). The gas rate case produced a $139 million order (~60% of the final ask, 9.8% ROE); Staff context $265 million (~60% of the revised $443 million electric ask, 9.85% ROE, 50% equity). NorthStar sales are more than 35% signed or closed with restructuring on track by year-end, and the new IRP carries roughly $27 billion of capital opportunity, though it is not yet in the five-year plan.

negative_highlights: Price mix of only 1% reflects three points of unfavorable mix, and management called it potentially one of the lower price mix years in about a decade
North America volume was flat, held back by the July 4th timing shift and cycling strong prior-year Topo Chico/BODYARMOR finished-goods comparisons
Cost pressures accelerated with elevated logistics and transportation costs, and Q4 faces slight destocking plus six fewer days
positive_highlights: Organic revenue +7% with unit case volume +5%, and price mix positive at +1% despite a three-point mix drag
Comparable gross margin up ~170 bps and operating margin up ~110 bps, with management stating expansion did not come at the expense of investment
Full-year guidance raised to at least 5% organic revenue, at least 9% currency-neutral EPS growth and at least $13 billion free cash flow; 22nd consecutive quarter of value share gain
summary: Q3 FY2026 organic revenue grew 7% on unit case volume of +5%, with price mix up 1% (four points of pricing partly offset by three points of unfavorable mix). Comparable gross margin rose ~170 bps and operating margin ~110 bps, and comparable EPS of $0.91 was up 11% including a two-point FX benefit. Full-year 2026 guidance was raised to organic revenue growth of at least 5%, currency-neutral comparable EPS growth of at least 9% (comparable EPS growth of at least 11% vs $3 in 2025) and at least $13 billion of free cash flow, though Q4 carries slight destocking and six fewer days. Management flagged elevated cost pressures in logistics and transportation and a modest FX headwind for 2027, with CCBA refranchising an eight-point revenue and two-point EPS headwind next year.

negative_highlights: FY2027 revenue guide of low double digits implies deceleration from 15% in FY2026, with Q2 flagged as the growth low point
Client incentives grew 21% in Q4, a step-up of nearly three points from Q3, and are expected to step up further in FY2027 given ~25% of payments volume up for renewal
International transaction revenue rose only 8% versus 14% cross-border volume growth, due to lower volatility levels and mix
positive_highlights: Q4 net revenue up 13% to $12.1 billion and full-year revenue up 15% to $46 billion, the strongest growth in over 15 years excluding post-pandemic recovery and acquisitions
Value-added services revenue grew 31% in constant dollars to $4 billion in Q4, with management guiding to low-to-mid-20s VAS growth in FY2027
Cross-border volume ex-intra-Europe accelerated to 14% growth, two points above Q3, with travel up 13% and e-commerce up 17%
summary: Visa reported Q4 FY2026 net revenue of $12.1 billion, up 13% year-over-year in nominal and constant dollars, described as in line with expectations, with EPS of $3.48 up 17% and better than expected primarily due to an 18.4% tax rate versus guidance. Full-year net revenue rose 15% to $46 billion with EPS up 16% to $13.27; VAS grew 31% in constant dollars in Q4 and 30% for the year. FY2027 guidance calls for low-double-digit adjusted net revenue growth and low-double-digit to low-teens adjusted EPS growth, with opex growth modestly below revenue growth, a 16% dividend increase, and roughly 25% of payments volume up for renewal versus about 20% in 2026.

negative_highlights: Consolidated net revenue declined 2.5% to CAD 238 million and gross profit fell 9.8% with gross margin down 200 bps to 24.3%.
Cannabis Operations revenue fell 27.7% to CAD 27.0 million with a negative 6% gross margin and adjusted operating loss widening to CAD 11.4 million.
Operating loss of CAD 48.3 million driven by a CAD 52 million goodwill impairment, and same-store sales declined 6% in Liquor Retail and 3.8% in Cannabis Retail.
positive_highlights: Record free cash flow of CAD 20 million, up 19.5% year-over-year, though including a CAD 10.6 million one-time captive insurance unwind benefit.
Adjusted operating income swung to positive CAD 5.2 million from a CAD 9.5 million loss, a CAD 14.8 million improvement.
Both retail segments set record gross margins at 27.0%, with Cannabis Retail revenue at a record CAD 85.6 million and Liquor Retail gross margin up 70 bps.
summary: SNDL reported Q3 2026 net revenue of CAD 238 million, down 2.5% year-over-year, with gross profit down 9.8% to CAD 57.9 million and gross margin contracting 200 bps to 24.3%. Reported operating loss was CAD 48.3 million on a CAD 52 million goodwill impairment in Cannabis Operations, partly offset by positive adjusted operating income of CAD 5.2 million (a CAD 14.8 million improvement) and record free cash flow of CAD 20 million, which included a one-time CAD 10.6 million captive insurance benefit. Cannabis Retail posted record revenue and margin (27.0%) and Liquor Retail hit a record 27.0% margin despite a 6% same-store sales decline, while Cannabis Operations revenue fell 27.7% to CAD 27.0 million with negative gross margin of 6%, prompting a strategic review. Management outlined capital returns via buybacks and a potential up-to-CAD 50 million substantial issuer bid, plus U.S. investment in Parallel (indirect ownership rising to ~92%) and an expected deconsolidation of Ontario franchise operations reducing reported revenue by ~CAD 105 million.

negative_highlights: Glass Innovations sales fell 3% YoY to $1.5 billion with net income down 10%, as TV units fell 4% and notebooks/handhelds fell about 20%.
Solar reported a $7 million net loss and production ramp is slower than anticipated, remaining a drag on corporate margins.
Carrier sales grew only 4% YoY, and optical segment margin improvement lacks a new forward target.
positive_highlights: Sales grew 19% YoY to $5.1 billion and EPS grew 36% to $0.91, both above guided ranges.
Optical Communications sales rose 44% YoY to $2.4 billion with net income up 80%, and Enterprise sales grew 84% with Gen AI products up over 100%.
Q4 guidance of $5.2-$5.3 billion sales and $0.96-$1.00 EPS implies continued ~19% and ~36% YoY growth, and the company is already exceeding its $20 billion end-2026 run-rate target.
summary: Corning reported Q3 FY2026 sales up 19% YoY to $5.1 billion and EPS up 36% to $0.91, both above guided ranges, with gross margin expanding 150 bps to 40.5% and operating margin up 310 bps to 22.7%. Optical Communications led with sales up 44% to $2.4 billion and net income up 80%, while Glass Innovations fell 3% and Solar posted a $7 million net loss on a slower production ramp. Q4 guidance calls for sales of $5.2-$5.3 billion and EPS of $0.96-$1.00, both roughly 19% and 36% YoY growth, extending the acceleration and putting the company ahead of its $20 billion 2026 Springboard run-rate target. The main changes versus prior periods are the raised growth trajectory and new Carrier long-term agreements with Verizon, AT&T, and Zayo, partly offset by margin drag from Solar and soft display/consumer end markets.

negative_highlights: Technology Platform revenue fell ~20-24% YoY to $87M on a large client transition
SoFi Plus subscriber growth came in below expectations due to what management described as nefarious actors, requiring sign-up changes
Total capital ratio declined 180 bps sequentially to 17% as excess capital was deployed into balance-sheet loans
positive_highlights: Full-year 2026 revenue guidance raised to $5.04B from a prior $4.75-4.85B range, with EBITDA, net income, and EPS all lifted
Adjusted net revenue grew 44% YoY to $1.4B with adjusted EBITDA up 70% to a record $470M at a 34% margin
Personal loan all-in annualized net charge-offs fell ~80 bps YoY to 3.4% while NIM expanded 16 bps sequentially to 6.14%
summary: SoFi reported Q3 2026 adjusted net revenue of $1.4B, up 44% YoY, adjusted EPS of $0.18 (up 64% YoY), adjusted EBITDA of a record $470M (34% margin), and adjusted net income of $243M (18% margin). Management raised full-year 2026 guidance to $5.04B revenue (from a prior $4.75-4.85B range), $1.66B EBITDA, $840M net income, and $0.61 EPS, and issued preliminary 2027 guidance of $6.4B revenue (27% growth), ~35% EBITDA margin, and $0.90 EPS, funded organically without a capital raise. Members grew 35% to 17.1M and products 44% to 26.7M, personal loan net charge-offs improved to 3.4%, and NIM rose 16 bps sequentially to 6.14%. The main blemish was Technology Platform revenue down ~20-24% YoY on a large client transition (up 18% excluding it) and SoFi Plus growth coming in below internal expectations due to fraud-related sign-up issues.

negative_highlights: Cost per terabyte decline slowed to mid-single digits in the quarter versus roughly 15% over the prior four quarters, partly on higher external component costs
Nearline exabyte shipments were relatively flat sequentially in September (data center 198 EB) versus a large June step-up, with the meaningful increase deferred to December
positive_highlights: Revenue of $4.2B rose 61% YoY and 17% QoQ, exceeding the high end of guidance, with non-GAAP EPS of $7.68 up 194% YoY
Non-GAAP gross margin expanded 510 bps sequentially to 67.8% and operating margin rose 610 bps to 50.7%
Record free cash flow of $1.5B (up 32% QoQ, more than tripling YoY) alongside a dividend increase to $0.76 per share and $4.4B remaining repurchase authorization
summary: Seagate reported September quarter revenue of $4.2B, up 61% YoY and 17% QoQ, exceeding the high end of guidance, with record non-GAAP EPS of $7.68 (up 194% YoY) and record non-GAAP gross margin of 67.8%, up 510 bps sequentially. December quarter guidance calls for revenue of $4.8B ±$100M (17% YoY at midpoint), operating margin expanding toward the mid-50% range, and EPS of $9.20 ±$0.20. Management reiterated expectations for sequential revenue growth and gross margin expansion throughout fiscal 2027, with HAMR representing roughly 50% of nearline exabyte shipments exiting calendar 2026. The dividend was raised approximately 3% to $0.76 per share and share repurchases are expected to increase significantly starting calendar 2027 after debt reduction to $1.6B in principal.

negative_highlights: Full-year organic revenue guidance cut to roughly flat from prior 2%-3% growth
Full-year EPS guidance lowered to $5.40-$5.45 from $5.55-$5.70
MCS revenue declined 5% and management guided MCS to decline sequentially in Q4, with note weakness in-cycle water metering demand slowing
positive_highlights: EBITDA margin expanded 70 bps to 23.9% despite lower volume, driven by productivity and price
Orders grew 10% with backlog up 13% to $5.5 billion and book-to-bill above 1
Applied Water orders grew 15% with data center orders up over 200% for the second consecutive quarter
summary: Xylem reported Q3 FY2026 organic revenue roughly flat year-over-year, below expectations, with revenue declining in MCS (-5%), Water Infrastructure (-1%), and WSS (-2%), while Applied Water grew 9%. EPS rose 5% to $1.44 and EBITDA margin expanded 70 bps to 23.9%, but the company lowered full-year revenue guidance to roughly flat organic from prior 2%-3% growth and cut EPS guidance to $5.40-$5.45 from $5.55-$5.70. Orders grew 10% with backlog up 13% to $5.5 billion, but management cited timing delays in MCS book-and-ship metering and WSS capital projects. The company also announced divestitures of Applied Water International and Specialty Flow Control (9% of revenue, <5% of EBITDA) and a move to three segments in 2027.

negative_highlights: A ~$2.1B backlog adjustment removed inactive trials (>18 months) from R&D contracted backlog; backlog now $32.6B with $9.4B next-12-month revenue
Reported adjusted EBITDA margin held roughly flat YoY at ~23.2% for the full year, with pass-through revenue mix diluting gross margin by ~70 bps
Guidance embeds a ~70 bps FX headwind to Q4 revenue and difficult Q4 comparisons management flagged
positive_highlights: Revenue, adjusted EBITDA, and adjusted EPS all exceeded the high end of Q3 guidance, with EPS up 11.3% YoY to $3.34
R&D net new bookings of $3.2B rose 15% YoY for a 1.2 book-to-bill, the strongest in four years; LTM bookings of $11.7B up 14% for a fifth straight quarterly increase
Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 20 bps despite ~70 bps of pass-through and ~10 bps of FX headwind, as ~80 bps of operational improvement more than offset them
summary: IQVIA reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $4.428B, up 8.0% reported and 8.6% constant currency, with organic growth of ~6%—about 2x last year. Adjusted EBITDA of $1.032B grew 8.7% with margin expanding 20 bps, and adjusted diluted EPS of $3.34 rose 11.3%; revenue, EBITDA, and EPS all exceeded the high end of guidance. R&D net new bookings were $3.2B (up 15% YoY, 1.2 book-to-bill), the highest in four years, and LTM net new bookings of $11.7B rose 14% for a fifth consecutive quarterly increase. Full-year 2026 guidance was raised for revenue ($17.35B–$17.5B), adjusted EBITDA ($4.025B–$4.055B, flat ~23.2% margin), and adjusted EPS ($12.90–$13.00). A ~$2.1B backlog adjustment for inactive trials was booked with no impact to guidance or historical results.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA fell 5% sequentially to $201 million as the BlackRhino, Discoverer, Venturer and Globetrotter I had fewer contract days in Q3
Full-year Adjusted EBITDA guidance narrowed to the lower end at $850-$900 million from $850-$925 million on later Voyager and Valiant starts
Free cash flow was -$48 million with capex of $192 million, and full-year capex guidance rose to $680-$705 million from $615-$665 million
positive_highlights: New contract awards totaling approximately $560 million, lifting backlog to $6.7 billion with about $2.6 billion scheduled for 2027 conversion
Contracted UDW utilization of 99% (109 of 110 marketed rigs), exceeding the 2024 high watermark of 105 contracted rigs
Four of five CJ70 jackups now contracted in Norway at leading-edge day rates of $230,000-$300,000, with about 20% more contracted capacity in H2 2027 versus H1
summary: Noble reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $684 million, Adjusted EBITDA of $201 million (28% margin, down 5% sequentially), and negative free cash flow of -$48 million on capex of $192 million. Full-year 2026 revenue guidance was narrowed to $2.85-$2.9 billion (from $2.8-$2.9 billion) driven by higher reimbursables, while Adjusted EBITDA was narrowed to the lower end at $850-$900 million (from $850-$925 million) on later starts for the Voyager and Valiant; capex guidance rose to $680-$705 million. Backlog stands at $6.7 billion with about $2.6 billion converting in 2027, and management guided Q1 2027 EBITDA broadly flat with Q4 2026 before building meaningfully higher each quarter, citing roughly 20% more contracted capacity in H2 2027 versus H1. Management was upbeat on market tightening (99% marketed UDW utilization, mid-$400s to $500k day rates) and announced roughly $560 million of new awards, though the quarter itself showed sequential EBITDA decline, negative free cash flow, and a lower EBITDA guide.

negative_highlights: Management described the macroeconomic environment as continued to deteriorate: the Fed raised rates in September, inflation re-accelerated to 3.7%, and the 10-year touched 5.36%
Private credit defaults near 6% vs 2%-2.5% historic, CMBS delinquencies above 8%, and $8B of U.S. seniors housing debt maturing in 2026 with $10-12B annually in 2027-2028
Higher expected G&A partially offset the FFO guidance raise, and net debt to adjusted EBITDA is expected to end the year in the low threes
positive_highlights: Normalized FFO per share of $1.67 grew 24.6% YoY, and full-year FFO guidance midpoint was raised $0.10 to $6.50
SHOP same-store NOI margin expanded 310 bps to 31.7%, with record flow-through of 66% of incremental revenue to NOI
RevPOR growth accelerated to 5.3% (5.8% in traditional senior living) while ExpPOR rose only 80 bps, driving a 300 bps margin expansion
summary: Welltower reported Q3 FY2026 normalized FFO of $1.67/share, up 24.6% YoY, on 38% revenue growth and 35% adjusted EBITDA growth. Total same-store NOI rose 15.8%, driven by 21% SHO NOI growth, 9.1% organic revenue growth, 320 bps occupancy gain, and 5.3% RevPOR growth, with SHOP margin up 310 bps to 31.7%. Management raised the midpoint of full-year normalized FFO guidance by $0.10 to $6.50 (23% YoY growth), citing $0.03 from SHO NOI, $0.055 from investment/financing activity, and favorable FX/tax, slightly offset by higher G&A. The quarter showed margin expansion and accelerating pricing power, but management flagged a deteriorating macro backdrop with Fed rate hikes, 3.7% inflation, and elevated credit stress.

negative_highlights: Same-store NOI guidance midpoint implies moderation from Q3's ~8% cash growth to full-year 7.5%-8.5% range
New York Citi renewal pushed to Q1 2027 from prior expectation, delaying some leasing volume
Dividend increase not expected imminently in 2027 per CFO commentary; board to evaluate as year progresses
positive_highlights: Record net effective rents after capex of $29.31/sq ft, up more than 30% from the trailing 12-month average
Cash and accrual leasing spreads of 26% and 35%, the second highest in company history
Core FFO guidance raised and narrowed to $1.55-$1.57 for the third consecutive quarter, now $0.06 above original 2026 midpoint
summary: Piedmont reported Q3 2026 core FFO of $0.39 per diluted share, $0.04 above Q3 2025, driven by higher rental rates and commenced occupancy. The company raised and narrowed 2026 core FFO guidance to $1.55-$1.57 per share for the third consecutive quarter, now $0.06 above the original outlook at the midpoint, implying over 10% earnings growth. Leasing momentum was strong with cash/accrual spreads of 26%/35%, net effective rents after capex hitting a record $29.31/sq ft (up >30% from the trailing 12-month average), and same-store NOI growing ~8% cash and ~7% accrual. The balance sheet was repositioned via $230 million exchangeable notes redeeming the 2028 unsecured bonds, reducing weighted average cost of debt by 70 bps to 4.8% and extending maturities with no maturities until late 2028.

negative_highlights: Full-year 2026 guidance was cut to about $4.375 billion revenue, $725 million adjusted EBITDA, and roughly 10% adjusted EPS growth, revising the May Investor Day framework
Cross-border payments revenue fell 4% with operating income down 35% and adjusted EBITDA down 32%, reflecting flow-through of revenue declines and about $6 million of incremental advertising spend
Adjusted EPS of $3.55 declined 2% year-over-year, and Steam's discontinuation of physical gift card sales at end of October is expected to be a headwind to epay's fourth quarter
positive_highlights: Digital accelerators grew approximately 33% year-to-date, ahead of the 2026 growth rate outlined at the May Investor Day, and now represent about 26% of payment channel revenue versus 21% in 2025
Payments infrastructure revenue grew 9% on merchant acquiring growth and CoreCard contribution, with epay revenue and operating income each up 5% and adjusted EBITDA up 6%
Repurchased approximately 690,000 shares for $50 million in the quarter, and cross-border digital transactions rose 34% with Ria Digital revenue up 30%
summary: Euronet reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $1.2 billion, operating income of $171.6 million, adjusted EBITDA of $226.1 million, and adjusted EPS of $3.55, down 2% year-over-year. The company cut its full-year 2026 outlook to approximately $4.375 billion revenue, $725 million adjusted EBITDA, and about 10% adjusted EPS growth, versus the May Investor Day framework it is now revising. Cross-border payments were the weak spot, with revenue down 4% and adjusted EBITDA down 32%, driven by U.S. immigration policy and macro pressure, while payments infrastructure grew revenue 9% and epay grew revenue and operating income 5%. Management pointed to digital accelerators growing roughly 33% year-to-date, $50 million of buybacks (about 690,000 shares), and upcoming headwinds including Steam discontinuing physical gift cards at the end of October.

negative_highlights: Coke sales volumes fell to 875,000 tons from 951,000 due to the Haverhill I shutdown
GAAP EPS slipped $0.01 YoY to $0.25 on loss of prior-year capital investment tax credits
Q4 Industrial Services expected to soften toward Q1 levels as steel mills slow for holidays
positive_highlights: Consolidated Adjusted EBITDA rose $17.8 million YoY to $76.9 million, with guidance now expected to modestly exceed the $250-$265 million range
Industrial Services EBITDA more than doubled to $32.1 million from $18.2 million on higher terminals volumes and a full Phoenix contribution
Domestic Coke EBITDA per ton reached $58.40, described as the strongest in recent quarters, aided by contract/spot mix and favorable coal-to-coke yields
summary: SunCoke reported Q3 2026 consolidated Adjusted EBITDA of $76.9 million, up $17.8 million YoY, with Domestic Coke EBITDA of $51.1 million (on 875,000 tons, down from 951,000) and Industrial Services EBITDA of $32.1 million versus $18.2 million. GAAP EPS was $0.25, down $0.01 YoY due to absence of prior-year tax credits, though underlying earnings improved. Management now expects full-year consolidated Adjusted EBITDA to modestly exceed the $250-$265 million range, Domestic Coke to reach the high end of $172-$178 million, Industrial Services to exceed $110-$115 million, and raised free cash flow guidance to $180-$185 million. The Algoma settlement was executed in October with SunCoke 'made whole,' while Middletown turbine insurance proceeds are now excluded from guidance and may slip into 2027.

OrthoPediatrics reported record Q3 FY2026 revenue of $72.7M, up 19% YoY (U.S. $57.9M +19%, international $14.8M +18%), with Trauma & Deformity $52.6M +19% and scoliosis $19.2M +18%. Gross margin held at 74%, operating expense rose 6% to $58.2M, adjusted EBITDA hit a record $6.9M (~10% margin), GAAP net loss was $0.25/share vs $0.50, and free cash flow turned positive at $1.6M from a $3.4M use a year ago. Full-year revenue guidance was raised to $270-273M (+14% to +16%), with adjusted EBITDA reiterated at ~$25M and cash flow breakeven-or-better reaffirmed. Management deliberately declined to extrapolate, noting Q4 comparisons lack last year's Brazil set sales and 7D unit sales, and that many Super Cycle products remain in limited launch with real contribution pushed to 2027 and beyond.

negative_highlights: Gross margin compressed 190 bps to 34.8% due to the timing of price increases and unfavorable mix, with year-to-date price-cost lagging the neutral target by 100 bps
International Welding adjusted EBIT fell 7% to $24 million with margin down 100 bps to 10.3% on lower volume and weak European capital spending, plus a $5 million Middle East conflict headwind
Harris Products adjusted EBIT margin declined 100 bps to 17.3%, below the expected range on unfavorable mix and operational inefficiencies; 2027 faces a looming silver-price comp issue
positive_highlights: Sales rose 15% to $1.221 billion on 9% volume growth and 6% price, with adjusted EPS up 21% to a record $2.98
Organic growth was broad-based across all three segments and all five end markets, with U.S. sales up over 20% and Americas Welding adjusted EBIT up 27% to $167 million at a 20.1% margin (up 190 bps)

Automation sales reached $232 million on high-teens organic growth, backlog hit a record, and the company raised full-year sales growth guidance to low teens percent and its dividend 10% to $3.48 annualized
summary: Lincoln Electric reported Q3 FY2026 sales of $1.221 billion, up 15% (9% volume, 6% price), with adjusted EPS up 21% to a record $2.98 and adjusted operating margin up 60 bps to 18% at a 22% incremental margin. However, gross margin compressed 190 bps to 34.8% on late-quarter pricing and unfavorable mix, and International Welding adjusted EBIT fell 7% with margin down 100 bps to 10.3%. The company raised full-year sales growth guidance to low teens percent and increased its 2026 CapEx range to $140-$150 million from $110-$130 million, while maintaining its September price-cost and incremental margin assumptions and expecting price-cost neutrality in Q4. Management flagged persistent inflation from AI data-center-driven material shortages and said it has been 'one step behind' on pricing, though volume momentum remains robust through October and backlog hit a record.

negative_highlights: Medical book-to-bill was 0.66 on order timing, and medical revenue fell 4% sequentially despite 21% YoY growth
A&D sales of $24 million were 7% below prior year, reflecting lumpy program funding and order timing
Management expects gross margin normalization from the 42% level, citing unusually favorable mix and ~$1.4 million FX benefit
positive_highlights: Adjusted gross margin hit a record 42.2%, up 330 bps YoY, and adjusted diluted EPS rose to a record $0.77 from $0.60
Full-year 2026 sales guidance raised to $580-590 million and adjusted EPS to $2.78-2.88
Diversified end markets grew 7% YoY with total book-to-bill of 1.18 and diversified book-to-bill of 1.3; industrial book-to-bill 1.36 and A&D 1.91
summary: CTS reported Q3 sales of $149.6 million, up 5% YoY and 3% sequentially, with record adjusted gross margin of 42.2% (up 330 bps YoY) and record adjusted diluted EPS of $0.77 versus $0.60 a year ago. Diversified end markets grew 7% YoY to 60% of sales, led by medical up 21% and industrial up 7%, while transportation rose 2% and A&D fell 7% YoY despite a 1.91 book-to-bill. Full-year 2026 guidance was raised to $580-590 million in sales and $2.78-2.88 in adjusted EPS, supported by the Millar acquisition (~$30 million annual revenue, expected accretive in H2 2027). Management flagged that the margin strength included an unusually favorable mix and ~$1.4 million FX benefit, and expects some normalization in profitability over the next few quarters.

negative_highlights: Q3 subscription revenue guidance of $293-$297 million implies deceleration to ~15% year-over-year growth from 21% in Q2
Second-half EBIT margin guidance of 20.5%-21.0% for Q3 reflects a step down from the 21.9% reported in Q2, partly on SHIFT conference costs

Subscription NRR of 113% reflects stronger new-customer contribution than expansion across the install base, and identity ARR growth of ~100% is off a small base with cross-note acceleration pushed to the second half
positive_highlights: Full-year subscription ARR guidance raised to $1.205-$1.215 billion, implying ~$195 million in net new subscription ARR and ~19.2% growth at the midpoint
SaaS ARR grew 35% year-over-year to $454 million, with management expecting to exceed $500 million by fiscal year-end
Non-GAAP EBIT margin expanded 330 bps to 21.9% and SaaS gross margin expanded 650 bps to 70%
summary: Commvault reported Q2 FY2027 total revenue of $312 million, up 13%, with subscription revenue up 21% to $269 million and subscription ARR up 20% to $1.104 billion; SaaS ARR grew 35% to $454 million. Non-GAAP EBIT margin expanded 330 bps to 21.9% and gross margin rose 110 bps to 81.6%, with free cash flow of $71 million. Management raised full-year guidance: subscription ARR to $1.205-$1.215 billion (~19.2% growth), subscription revenue to $1.127-$1.133 billion, total revenue to $1.30-$1.31 billion and EBIT margins to 21.0%-21.5%. The quarter beat on go-to-market execution with higher close rates, and the raise is anchored on expected second-half cross-watch and a larger renewal pool.

CenterPoint reported Q3 2026 GAAP EPS of $0.50 and non-GAAP EPS of $0.53, with rate recovery contributing $0.09 and weather/usage $0.03, partly offset by $0.05 of unfavorable other items and $0.04 of higher financing costs. Management raised 2026 non-GAAP EPS guidance to $1.90-$1.92 from $1.89-$1.91 (nearly 9% growth at the midpoint) and initiated 2027 guidance of $2.07-$2.09, 9% growth at the midpoint. The 10-year capital plan rose $4 billion to $70.7 billion with $1.5 billion accelerated, supporting enterprise rate base CAGR above 14% through 2030, funded with a $1.6 billion increase to equity needs and about $500-700 million of common equity in 2027. The quarter came in near 80% of the original full-year guide with O&M flat and on track for a 1-2% reduction.

negative_highlights: Non-interest income fell 8% QoQ and 6% YoY to $13.2 million on lower BOLI and mortgage banking income
Provision expense jumped to $1.9 million from $710,000 prior quarter on economic outlook and unfunded reserves
Net income and EPS fell just note weakness in of last quarter's record results; total loans flat YoY and QoQ
positive_highlights: NIM rose 15 bps QoQ to 3.41%, exceeding the prior guidance range, with funding costs down to 1.63% from 1.70%
Total deposits increased 5% QoQ and 8% YoY to $5.8 billion, improving funding mix
Non-performing loans declined to 16 bps from 24 bps and past due loans fell to 14 bps from 15 bps
summary: Q3 FY2026 net income of $22.8 million (EPS $1.34) rose 8% and 7% respectively YoY but fell just short of last quarter's record. NIM expanded 15 bps QoQ to 3.41%, exceeding guidance, and deposits grew 5% QoQ/8% YoY to $5.8 billion, though total loans were flat at $5 billion. Q4 NIM guided flat, non-interest income guided to $13.5-14.5M, and non-interest expense to $37.5-38M. Credit improved (NPLs 16 bps vs 24 bps) but provision rose to $1.9M from $710K.

negative_highlights: Adjusted diluted EPS fell 21% YoY to $2.08 from $2.62 and adjusted gross margin contracted 500 bps to 39.4%
Light-duty operating margin fell 520 bps YoY to 18.5% and heavy-duty posted breakeven operating margin on higher tariff and shipping costs
Full-year EPS guidance narrowed to $8.50-$8.70 from $8.50-$8.80, with Q4 POS pressure from DIY softness and further tariff-related price reductions
positive_highlights: Net sales reached a record $562 million, up ~3% with growth in all three segments
Full-year adjusted operating margin guidance narrowed to the top end of the prior range, now 16%-16.5%
Year-to-date share repurchases of $112 million set a company record, with $348 million remaining on the authorization through 2027
summary: Q3 net sales were a record $562 million, up ~3% YoY, with growth in all three segments (light-duty $444M +3%, heavy-duty $66M +5%, specialty $52M +3%). Adjusted diluted EPS fell 21% to $2.08 from $2.62, adjusted gross margin contracted 500 bps to 39.4% and light-duty operating margin dropped 520 bps to 18.5%, both attributed to lapping last year's tariff-related pricing without the associated costs. Full-year EPS guidance was narrowed to $8.50-$8.70 from $8.50-$8.80 and sales growth to 2%-3%, reflecting continued DIY softness and additional tariff-related price reductions in Q4, while adjusted operating margin guidance was narrowed to the top end at 16%-16.5%.

negative_highlights: Middle East and Africa RevPAR fell 5.6% with full-year now expected to decline low double digits on conflict
China RevPAR declined 5.4% with soft consumer sentiment and government business-travel restraints
Flow-through was dampened: management said flow-through 'would have been 30' absent Middle East pressure and weaker timeshare license fees, roughly splitting the shortfall
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA of $1.058 billion rose 8.4% YoY and exceeded the high end of guidance
System-wide RevPAR up 5.8% with business transient +8.3% and group +8.2%; U.S. RevPAR +7%
Record quarter of 27,000 organic room openings, NUG of 6.0%, and record 543,000-room pipeline with construction starts up over 40% YoY
summary: Hilton reported Q3 FY2026 system-wide RevPAR growth of 5.8% YoY on both rate and occupancy ahead of expectations, with adjusted EBITDA of $1.058 billion up 8.4% and exceeding the high end of guidance; management franchise fees grew 9.5%. Full-year RevPAR guidance was set at 4%-4.5%, with Q4 RevPAR guided to 3%-3.5% (down sequentially due to election and calendar shifts), FY adjusted EBITDA of $4.06-$4.08 billion and adjusted EPS of $9.07-$9.13. Net unit growth was 6.0% with a record 27,000 organic room openings and a record 543,000-room pipeline; Middle East RevPAR fell 5.6% and China declined 5.4%. Management framed 2027 global RevPAR at 3%-4% and reiterated confidence in algorithm growth.

negative_highlights: Q4 net yield guidance of 4.2%-4.7% was unchanged from July expectations, so the raise was driven by Q3 rather than a stronger H2 outlook
Full-year EPS guide of $17.85-$17.95 is roughly in line with the initial January midpoint of $17.90, as higher fuel and unfavorable FX offset the stronger Q3
2027 Q1 faces ~200bps of structural yield headwinds from dry dock timing, with yield growth weighted to the second half
positive_highlights: Adjusted EPS of $6.57 came in $0.26 above the guidance midpoint, with revenue up 9% YoY
Net yields beat guidance by ~60bps, driven by stronger close-in demand in Europe and the Caribbean and strong onboard revenue
Bookings since the last call rose mid-teens YoY and 2027 sailings are up high teens, with record book positions for both 2026 and 2027
summary: Q3 revenue grew 9% YoY with capacity up 8% and net yields up 0.6%, about 60bps above guidance, driving adjusted EPS of $6.57, $0.26 above the guidance midpoint. Net cruise costs ex-fuel fell 1.8% YoY (40bps better than expected on timing) and adjusted EBITDA was $2.5 billion at a 45% margin. Full-year adjusted EPS guidance rose to $17.85-$17.95 (~14% YoY growth) on full-year net yields of ~2.1% and capacity growth of 6.6%, though Q4 yield guidance of 4.2%-4.7% was unchanged from July. Bookings since the last call rose mid-teens YoY and 2027 sailings are up high teens, with book position for 2026 and 2027 ahead of prior year at record rates; separately, the company announced a ~$3 billion deal for a 50% Sandals and Beaches stake, expected to be immaterial to 2027 earnings.
