negative_highlights: GAAP and adjusted EPS of $0.34 and $0.35 each declined $0.02 from the prior quarter
NIM contracted 5 bps to 370 bps on a 4 bp borrowing drag and 2 bp lower purchase accounting accretion
The adjusted efficiency ratio rose quarter-over-quarter to 57.8%, and non-interest expense is guided to the high end of the range
positive_highlights: Revenue reached a record $185 million (+9.9% YoY) and net interest income hit a record $149 million (+9% YoY)
Average C&I loans grew $201 million QoQ (7.2%) and $702 million YoY (30.8%), with national verticals now ~30% of the commercial portfolio
Non-interest income rose $3.7 million YoY (11.6%), with trust and other financial services income up 25.7% YoY
summary: Northwest Bancshares reported record Q3 FY2026 revenue of $185 million (+2% QoQ, +9.9% YoY) and record net interest income of $149 million (+9% YoY), with GAAP EPS of $0.34 and adjusted EPS of $0.35, down $0.02 from the prior quarter. NIM fell 5 bps to 370 bps on higher borrowing costs and lower purchase accounting accretion, and the adjusted efficiency ratio rose to 57.8% QoQ though it improved 184 bps YoY. Guidance was reiterated to the high end of the revenue and expense ranges, NIM guided to 373 bps in Q4 and 371 bps for the full year, fee income expected to exceed the high end of the range, and net charge-offs at the low end of guidance.

negative_highlights: Full-year revenue guidance of $90-92M merely reiterated, not raised, despite the return to growth
US sales force tenure remains note weakness in: mean ~1.8 years and median ~1.2 years, with 'high degree of variability' in rep ramp
Cash balance fell $3.2M sequentially to $52.7M, with ~$22M full-year 2026 burn expected
positive_highlights: Returned to year-over-year growth: total revenue +6% to $22.8M, US +7% to $14.9M, international +5% (+9% ex-China)
Adjusted EBITDA loss cut nearly 60% to $3.5M from $8.2M, with OpEx down 18% to $24.9M
Gross margin up to 76% from 75%, with full-year 2026 gross margin guidance now ~77%
summary: Pulmonx reported Q3 FY2026 worldwide revenue of $22.8 million, up 6% YoY (7% US to $14.9M, 5% international to $7.9M), marking the first return to global YoY growth since the CEO/CFO rejoined. Gross margin rose to 76% from 75%, operating expenses fell 18% to $24.9M, net loss narrowed 40% to $8.4M ($0.19/share), and adjusted EBITDA loss improved nearly 60% to $3.5M. Full-year 2026 revenue guidance of $90-92M was reiterated (not raised), while gross margin guidance is now ~77% and OpEx now $108-109M; cash burn is expected at ~$22M, a 30% reduction from 2025. The most important change is the inflection back to positive growth after prior declines, though the FY revenue range itself was not increased.

negative_highlights: Brazil NII came under pressure from deliberate de-risking and mix shift, with NPLs at 4.1% versus system deterioration to near 5%, and management said it was too early to say when the de-risking ends or loan growth resumes
CET1 of 12.7% absorbed a 147bp hit from Webster, with further regulatory charges and integration impacts still to come in Q4
U.S. loan yields fell and Q3 reflected CIB normalization after a record Q2 plus typical auto provision seasonality; Openbank motor finance was hurt by the end of U.S. EV tax incentives
positive_highlights: 9M underlying profit hit a record EUR 11.2bn, with Q3 underlying profit up 14% YoY in constant euros and guidance of >EUR 14.1bn for 2026 positioned to be exceeded
Efficiency ratio improved 2.8pp to 42.6%, the best in 17 years, with costs flat YoY ex-M&A and down 4% QoQ ex-M&A
Underlying EPS grew 21% and underlying RoTE reached 16% (close to 17% at normalized CET1 of 13%), with total buybacks reaching around EUR 9bn
summary: Santander reported record underlying profit of EUR 11.2bn for 9M 2026, with Q3 profit up 14% YoY in constant euros, revenue up 7% (NII +8%, fees +7%), and efficiency at 42.6%, its best level in 17 years. Management said it is in a strong position to exceed its 2026 guidance of more than EUR 14.1bn profit excluding M&A, and confirmed a CET1 target at or above 12.8% after absorbing the 147bp Webster impact. The main negative was Brazil, where NII fell on de-risking and mix shift, NPLs rose to 4.1%, and management said it was too early to say when loan growth resumes given the abrupt rate outlook change post-election. The first-time consolidation of TSB and Webster added roughly 1.3pp to P&L lines and drove the US RoTE to 12.6%, on track for 18% by 2028.

negative_highlights: Material sales declined to $80 million from $83 million, with green emitter sales down to $61 million from $65 million
Total gross margin fell to 73% from 75%, and management now expects full-year margin at the low end of 74%–76%
Full-year revenue guided toward the low end of the $630M–$670M range, with management citing continued macro uncertainty and tight memory pricing into 2027
positive_highlights: Royalty and license revenue rose to $75 million from $53 million, aided by the absence of last year's $9.5 million out-of-period reduction
Operating margin expanded to 33% from 31% with operating income of $54 million vs $43 million
Repurchased ~963,000 shares for ~$79 million in the quarter; ~2.1 million shares for ~$193 million year-to-date, cutting share count more than 5% over 12 months
summary: Q3 FY2026 revenue was $160 million vs $140 million a year ago, but the year-ago period was depressed by a $9.5 million out-of-period royalty adjustment. Material sales fell to $80 million from $83 million, total gross margin contracted to 73% from 75%, and management guided full-year revenue toward the low end of the $630M–$670M range and gross margin toward the low end of 74%–76%. GAAP EPS was $1.72 but included a $29 million non-cash UDC Ventures gain; adjusted EPS was $1.23, and operating income rose to $54 million (33% margin) from $43 million (31%). For 2027 management flagged tight memory conditions, higher input costs, and gross margin pressure, with only mid-single-digit OLED area growth expected.

negative_highlights: HETLIOZ's $21.7 million quarter (+289% QoQ) was driven by shipment timing, including ~$7 million of orders shipped June 29, and specialty pharmacy stocking; management warned sales may decline, potentially significantly, as inventory unwinds
NEREUS full-year 2026 revenue now guided to less than $10 million, with management saying initial growth is likely to progress slower than expected
2026 cash burn expected to exceed 2025, with cash down $123.4 million since December 31, 2025 to $140.5 million
positive_highlights: Fanapt net sales rose 24% YoY to $38.8 million with TRx up 25% and weekly TRx hitting an 11-year high of nearly 2,800 in the week ending September 25, 2026
Operating expenses fell 18% to $93.3 million from $114.3 million in Q2, narrowing the net loss to $22.6 million from $62.5 million, with further opex decreases expected
Positive Phase III results for NEREUS in GLP-1-induced vomiting (80% reduction in severe vomiters) and HETLIOZ in DSWPD, plus a December 12, 2026 PDUFA date for Quimilza
summary: Q3 2026 total revenue was $69.8 million, up 24% YoY and 38% QoQ, but the sequential jump was largely due to HETLIOZ timing—including ~$7 million of orders shipped June 29 that landed July 1—and specialty pharmacy stocking, with HETLIOZ sales of $21.7 million up 289% QoQ despite ongoing generic erosion. Fanapt net sales rose 24% YoY to $38.8 million on 25% TRx growth, while NEREUS contributed just $1.6 million. The quarter's net loss of $22.6 million improved by ~$40 million from Q2 on a $21 million opex reduction, with more opex decline expected; full-year revenue guidance is now greater than $240 million, with NEREUS explicitly guided to under $10 million for 2026 and 2026 cash burn expected to exceed 2025's. Management flagged that HETLIOZ sales may decline, potentially significantly, as elevated specialty pharmacy inventory unwinds, and acknowledged NEREUS growth will progress slower than initially hoped.

negative_highlights: 2026 capex guidance raised to ~$3.5B from ~$3.2B
Crude volumes came in light, attributed to lower-margin Houston distribution system
Waha to Katy optimization moderated sequentially and expected to fall further in Q4
positive_highlights: 2026 adjusted EBITDA midpoint raised $200M to ~$8.55B, the third guidance increase this year
Gulf Coast Permian NGL volumes up 16% YoY and 9% QoQ; total raw feed throughput up 6% to nearly 1.7 million bpd
Balance sheet strengthened via $9B minority equity investment, ~$5.5B debt extinguishment, and S&P/Fitch upgrades to BBB+
summary: ONEOK reported Q3 2026 net income of $1.35B ($2.13/diluted share) and adjusted EBITDA of $2.24B, up 6% YoY, with EPS including a $336M one-time non-cash tax benefit and EBITDA including a $53M net transaction benefit. The company raised 2026 adjusted EBITDA midpoint guidance to approximately $8.55B, a $200M increase over last quarter and $450M above original February guidance, driven by ~$75M Brazos contribution, $50M transaction benefits, and $100M of stronger base business. 2026 capex guidance rose to ~$3.5B from ~$3.2B, and leverage target was lowered to approximately 3.25x or below versus the prior 3.5x. Management did not provide 2027 guidance but cited constructive producer plans, completed projects, and hedging as supporting momentum into 2027.

negative_highlights: Vans revenue fell 9.8%, about $3-4 million softer than indicated, with Q2 wholesale down more than Q1 on continued destocking
Net inventory rose 7% YoY as a deliberate build, and first-half free cash flow was negative $323 million
APAC declined 7% overall, with Timberland APAC down roughly 20% (~$12 million) and North Face APAC down 4%
positive_highlights: Operating income of $364 million came in about $50 million above the $315 million guidance, with gross margin up 290 bps to 55.4% (180 bps structural, 110 bps FX)
EPS of $0.70 rose over 40% YoY, more than twice operating income growth, aided by lower interest expense ($24 million) and an ~18% effective tax rate
Altra grew over 40% with growth in every region and channel, and 75% of the portfolio by revenue is now growing versus 43% in fiscal 2024
summary: Revenue grew 1% versus guidance of flat, operating income of $364 million came in roughly $50 million above the $315 million guide, gross margin expanded 290 bps to 55.4% and EPS rose over 40% to $0.70 from $0.49. Full-year FY2027 guidance was reaffirmed (revenue up 2% or better, ~8% operating margin) along with medium-term targets, while The North Face and Timberland were tightened to up mid-single digits and Vans confirmed at down 2% or better in the second half. Q3 guidance calls for revenue growth of ~3% or better and operating income of ~$390 million or better; FY tax rate was lowered to the high 20s from the low 30s. Vans remained the weak spot, down 9.8% versus a guided ~9%, with wholesale softer, partly offset by the first positive global DTC quarter in almost five years.

negative_highlights: AS&I Adjusted EBITDA fell 36% to $21 million on lower automotive and industry volumes and a $23 million price/mix headwind
Implied Q4 EBITDA down high-single-digits YoY, with Section 338 tariffs, a Q4 recycling outage, and tapering Oswego automotive benefits
Working capital and other expected to be a larger use of cash than prior guidance
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA rose 17% to $276 million, or $280 million excluding a $4 million metal price lag, a Q3 record and up 43% ex-lag versus $196 million last year
Full-year Adjusted EBITDA guidance raised to $1.03-1.06 billion excluding metal price lag, with FCF above $300 million
A&T Adjusted EBITDA up 13% to $102 million on aerospace shipments +10% and TID shipments +24%; P&ARP Adjusted EBITDA up 98% to $162 million on a $70 million cost tailwind
summary: Constellium reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $2.6 billion, up 22% YoY, net income of $119 million versus $88 million last year, and Adjusted EBITDA up 17% to $276 million (or $280 million ex-metal price lag, a Q3 record). It again raised full-year 2026 Adjusted EBITDA guidance, now $1.03-1.06 billion excluding metal price lag, with free cash flow expected above $300 million. Management flagged a softer implied Q4 versus an exceptional Q4 2025, citing seasonality, a recycling outage moved into Q4, tapering Oswego auto benefits, and Section 338 tariff headwinds, while pointing to significantly stronger aerospace demand and repricing in 2027.

negative_highlights: Q4 EBITDA margin guided to 49%-50%, down from 51.4% in Q3 on seasonality of spend
Management flagged industry headwinds from power availability, legislation, and community sentiment
Churn guidance held at 2%-2.5% for the remainder of the year despite the 1.7% print, with selective intentional churn possible
positive_highlights: Full-year 2026 guidance raised: revenue +$100M, adjusted EBITDA +$70M, AFFO +$90M
Record annualized gross bookings of $533M, up 35% YoY, with sales activity up 38%
Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 180 bps YoY to 51.4% and stabilized assets generated 27% cash-on-cash returns
summary: Equinix raised full-year 2026 guidance: total revenue up $100M to ~12% YoY growth, adjusted EBITDA up $70M to ~51% margin, and AFFO up $90M (including $31M from atNorth), with AFFO per share growth of 11%-12%. Q3 delivered 12% total revenue and 11% MRR growth (normalized, constant currency), adjusted EBITDA margin of 51.4% (up 180 bps YoY), AFFO per share up 12% normalized (18% including atNorth), and record annualized gross bookings of $533M, up 35%. New deal pricing rose 12% YoY with churn at 1.7%, and the retail capacity plan for the year was raised to nearly 40% above initial expectations with over 13,000 cabinets slated for Q4.

negative_highlights: Reported combined ratio widened to 59.3% from 48.5% on $34.2M of catastrophe losses versus none in the prior-year quarter
Favorable prior-period reserve development fell to $18M from $32.5M a year earlier
Gross written premium growth of 9.3% is modest, and 2027 growth is guided to a similar 8%-9% with a back-end-loaded ramp
positive_highlights: Full-year net income guidance raised to $500M-$520M from $455M-$470M, with FY ROE expected above 40%
Accident-year ex-cat combined ratio improved to 54.4% from 62.3% and the expense ratio improved 590 bps to 28.9%
Board declared a $1.50/share special dividend; roughly $423.1M returned to shareholders since the June 2025 IPO
summary: Slide reported Q3 FY2026 gross written premiums up 9.3% to $506.5M and net income up 24.5% to $138.2M, or $1.09 diluted EPS, with total revenue up 35.9% to $361.1M. The reported combined ratio of 59.3% widened from 48.5% on $34.2M of convective storm cat losses, but the accident-year ex-cat combined ratio improved to 54.4% from 62.3% and the expense ratio improved 590 bps to 28.9%. Management raised the low end of full-year GWP guidance to $1.9B-$1.95B from $1.85B-$1.95B and lifted net income guidance to $500M-$520M from $455M-$470M, including up to $50M of pre-tax Hurricane Isaias retention. The board also declared a $1.50/share special dividend alongside the $0.07 regular dividend.

negative_highlights: SG&A guidance raised to $585M-$590M from a prior $540M-$580M range, driven by higher-than-usual claims expense in Q3
Q3 SG&A of $161M ex-charges rose $25.1M YoY; total SG&A of $176.3M included $15.4M of other charges, primarily a $12.5M real estate impairment
Share repurchases paused and net debt/EBITDA up to 1.71x from 1.64x, with leverage expected to rise further on the RXO acquisition
positive_highlights: NAST operating margin up 110 bps YoY to 40.3% and Global Forwarding margin up 660 bps YoY to 36.6%, again exceeding mid-cycle targets
Truckload AGP per shipment up 17% YoY and NAST volume up 3.5% versus a 0.3% Cass index decline, 14th straight quarter of market outgrowth
Average headcount down 10.4% YoY while volumes grew, with NAST shipments per person per day up over 15% YoY
summary: C.H. Robinson reported Q3 revenue growth of 29.5% and adjusted gross profit growth of 14.5% year-over-year, with NAST operating margin up 110 bps to 40.3% and Global Forwarding margin up 660 bps to 36.6%. Truckload AGP per shipment rose 17% YoY and NAST volumes grew 3.5% versus a 0.3% decline in the Cass index, the 14th consecutive quarter of outgrowth. Guidance was mixed: personnel expense guidance was tightened to $1.36B-$1.37B, but SG&A guidance was raised to $585M-$590M from a prior $540M-$580M on higher claims, while the full-year operating income target (at least $6 diluted EPS) held unchanged. The quarter included elevated claims and a $12.5M real estate impairment, and buybacks were paused pending the RXO acquisition, with leverage guided higher on closing.

negative_highlights: Recurring revenue grew only 7% YoY as legacy support contracts are subsumed into Platform ONE, with re-acceleration pushed to FY2028
Revenue in Asia Pac declined on elevated prior-year comparisons
Rising memory component costs are embedded in the gross margin results and guide, with management citing a fluid pricing environment
positive_highlights: Revenue of $341M grew 10% YoY and exceeded both consensus and the high end of guidance, with product revenue up 12%
FY2027 revenue guidance raised to 10% growth at the midpoint from the prior 8%, alongside EPS of $1.35-$1.39
Operating margin expanded 410 bps YoY to 17.4% and adjusted EBITDA rose 47% to $66M; SaaS ARR grew 22% to ~$265M
summary: Extreme reported Q1 FY2027 revenue of $341M, up 10% YoY, above consensus and the high end of guidance, with product revenue of $218M up 12%. Non-GAAP EPS of $0.33 rose 50% YoY and beat the high end, gross margin was 62.6% (up 130 bps YoY), and operating margin expanded 410 bps to 17.4%. FY2027 revenue guidance was raised to $1.402B-$1.412B (10% growth at the midpoint, up from a prior 8% guide), with EPS of $1.35-$1.39, and Q2 revenue guided to $345.8M-$350.8M. Free cash flow was $39M, cash reached $245M, and $25M of shares were repurchased.

negative_highlights: OXXO México gross margin contracted 120 bps (70 bps normalized) and operating margin 40 bps, with a further similar closure impact expected in Q4
Health operating income fell 63.2% on a MXN 430 million additional Colombia credit provision; Europe operating income fell 24.8% on weak Valora US B2B and German traffic
Net new stores will fall note weakness in of the 1,000 annual run-rate this year (734 opened, 272 closed YTD), and management guided to a tougher comparison base and soft Mexico consumer
positive_highlights: OXXO México same-store sales +9.2% with traffic +3.5%, 150 bps above Q2 despite only a small World Cup benefit
Consolidated operating income +13.4% currency-neutral and net income +81% to MXN 10.6 billion
Bara same-store sales +10.3% with 112 net new stores; Coca-Cola FEMSA South America delivered double-digit operating income growth
summary: FEMSA reported Q3 FY2026 total revenues up 9.8% YoY and operating income up 9.9% (9.4% and 13.4% respectively on a currency-neutral basis), with net consolidated income of MXN 10.6 billion, up 81% on an easy base including last year's MXN 3.1 billion discontinued-ops loss and a MXN 1.1 billion FX gain. OXXO México same-store sales rose 9.2% on 5.5% ticket and 3.5% traffic growth (traffic up 150 bps sequentially despite minimal World Cup benefit), while OXXO gross margin contracted 120 bps and operating margin 40 bps; excluding 140 store closures, operating income grew 8%. Coca-Cola FEMSA grew revenue 10.9% and operating income 15.4% (7.4% ex a one-time insurance benefit); Health operating income fell 63.2% on a MXN 430 million Colombia credit provision and Europe fell 24.8%. No formal guidance was issued; management said net new stores will come 'a bit short' of the 1,000 run-rate this year but the target stands for next year, and flagged a soft Mexico consumer, Brazil volatility, and a harder comparison base ahead.

negative_highlights: Gross margin fell 180 bps YoY to 74.8% on 3% higher product cost, and management expects further sequential decline in Q4 with 2027 similar to 2026.
G&A expenses jumped 51.9% to $16.5 million (21.7% of revenue), including $2 million of BioCircuit acquisition costs.
Aetna initially extended coverage only for note weakness in to medium sensory gaps of 30 mm or less in the upper extremity, a utilization-management constraint management will work to resolve.
positive_highlights: Revenue rose 26.2% to $75.8 million with growth in all markets; breast grew more than 50% and extremities/OMF/head and neck combined grew 10.7%.
Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 2.3 percentage points to 17.7%, with adjusted net income of $13.1 million ($0.21/share) versus $6.1 million ($0.12/share) a year ago.
Full-year revenue guidance raised to at least $290 million (at least 29% growth) including at least $7 million from BioCircuit, with at least 26% organic growth.
summary: Q3 FY2026 revenue was $75.8 million, up 26.2% YoY, with breast up more than 50% and extremities/OMF/head and neck combined up 10.7%. GAAP net income was $2.3 million ($0.04/share), adjusted net income $13.1 million ($0.21/share), and adjusted EBITDA $13.4 million (17.7% margin, up 2.3 points YoY); gross margin was 74.8%, down 180 bps YoY on 3% higher product cost. Full-year 2026 guidance was revised to revenue growth of at least 29% (at least $290 million, including at least $7 million from BioCircuit), organic growth of at least 26%, gross margin of at least 73%, and positive free cash flow. Guidance embeds a step-down in gross margin sequentially in Q4 tied to production-plan changes for long-length Avance and possible BioCircuit inventory step-up.

negative_highlights: Truck gross margins ~8.1%, down from ~8.5% a year ago, attributed to mix toward higher fleet business and competitive pressure
Quoting and new order activity slowed as customers wait for EPA 2027 final rules and manufacturer pricing, leaving Q2 visibility limited and backlog declining daily
Tier 2/3 supplier constraints could push some Q4 deliveries into Q1, and management declined to guarantee Q4 numbers
positive_highlights: Revenue up 12.4% to ~$2.1 billion and net income up 18.2% to $78 million ($0.65 per diluted share)
New Class 8 truck sales up 24.4% versus industry growth of just over 10%, lifting Class 8 market share to 6.5%
Aftermarket revenue up 5.8% to ~$680 million with a 128.3% absorption ratio; August and September were the best and second-best gross-profit-per-day months of the year
summary: Rush reported Q3 revenue of roughly $2.1 billion, up 12.4% YoY, and net income of $78 million ($0.65 diluted), up 18.2%, with new Class 8 truck sales up 24.4% and Class 4-7 up 9.6%. Parts, service, and collision revenue rose 5.8% to about $680 million and generated nearly 63% of gross profit at a 128.3% absorption ratio. Management guided qualitatively to a strong Q4 and Q1 on backlog but flagged slower quoting/orders amid EPA 2027 emission-rule and pricing uncertainty, tier 2/3 supply constraints that could push deliveries into Q1, and truck margins down to ~8.1% from ~8.5% on mix toward lower-margin fleet business.

negative_highlights: Ford Blue EBIT declined 10% to $1.4 billion on lower volume from Escape/Corsair sunsets and Middle East conflict; Ford Pro EBIT fell 16% to $1.7 billion on higher commodities and Oakville launch costs
FY2026 commodity headwinds raised to approaching $2.5 billion YoY (about $500 million higher than prior assumption), with rising fuel prices pressuring freight and energy costs
2027 outlook targets profitability roughly in line with 2026 against a ~$2 billion commodity/memory/logistics headwind, and Model e expects higher 2027 expenses before a step change in H1 2028
positive_highlights: Raised low end of FY2026 adjusted EBIT guidance to $10.5–$11 billion, versus prior $10–$11 billion, with adjusted EBIT up 3% YoY to $2.7 billion despite revenue down 2%
Software services and parts hit record quarterly revenue, contributing ~10% of total revenue at accretive margins, with BlueCruise and Connectivity leading growth
Ford Energy has contracts and late-stage negotiations covering more than 80% of 2028 capacity, with 20 GWh capacity on track for end of next year
summary: Ford reported Q3 FY2026 adjusted EBIT of $2.7 billion (up 3% YoY) on revenue of $49.5 billion (down 2% YoY), with company adjusted free cash flow of $4.7 billion and cash of $25.3 billion. Ford Blue EBIT fell 10% to $1.4 billion on lower volume from product sunsets and Middle East conflict, Ford Pro EBIT fell 16% to $1.7 billion on commodities and Oakville launch costs, Model e loss narrowed to $1.1 billion, and Ford Credit EBT rose to $803 million. The company raised the low end of full-year adjusted EBIT guidance to $10.5–$11 billion from a prior $10-11 billion, while 2027 profitability is targeted roughly in line with 2026 against a ~$2 billion commodity/memory/logistics headwind and higher 2027 Model e investment.

NOV reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $2.23 billion, up 4% sequentially and 2% year-over-year, with GAAP net income of $90 million ($0.25 per diluted share), adjusted operating profit of $188 million (8.4% of sales), and adjusted EBITDA of $281 million (12.6% of sales). Energy Equipment revenue was $1.22 billion, flat sequentially and down 2% year-over-year, at 15.3% EBITDA margin, while Energy Products and Services revenue rose 9% both sequentially and year-over-year to $1.06 billion at 14.5% margin. Free cash flow was a $47 million use on Middle East milestone billing delays and inventory buffers, though management guided to roughly 50% EBITDA-to-FCF conversion in 2027, and Q4 guidance is mixed: Energy Equipment revenue down 4%-6% year-over-year with $175-205 million EBITDA, Energy Products and Services revenue up 6%-8% with $140-160 million EBITDA. Management raised confidence in a $1.5 billion annualized EBITDA capacity path but gave no explicit 2027 guidance beyond an expectation to outpace mid-single-digit industry growth, with Middle East activity moderating through year-end.

Alphabet reported Q3 FY2026 consolidated revenue of $127.6 billion, up 25% year over year in both reported and constant currency, with operating income up 30% to $40.6 billion and operating margin at 31.8%. Google Cloud grew 103% to $30.7 billion with operating margin expanding to 36.2% from 23.7%, while Google Services revenue rose 11% to $96.3 billion and Search grew 12% to $63.3 billion. However, net income and EPS declined due to an $8.2 billion negative swing in other income/expense from an unrealized SpaceX loss, and free cash flow was negative $9.1 billion on $51.4 billion of CapEx. Full-year 2026 CapEx guidance of $195-205 billion was unchanged, with CapEx expected to increase significantly in 2027 and near-term Cloud margin headwinds from third-party capacity.

negative_highlights: Europe segment operating profit fell to $2 million from $95 million a year ago on ~4% lower price and volume and competitive pricing pressure
2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance cut to $925-950 million from a prior implied ~$1 billion floor, with free cash flow guided to ~$300 million of usage
Adjusted EPS swung to a loss of $0.09 from $0.48 profit, driven by lower net price, elevated European energy/freight, and an unusually high tax rate
positive_highlights: Americas net sales rose more than 3% YoY to $970 million with segment operating profit of $137 million, roughly flat after a $6 million prior-year insurance recovery
Fit to Win delivered ~$50 million in Q3 and $135 million year-to-date, with cumulative benefits of $460 million since inception
New business wins represent ~4% of annual sales volume, and Q4 enterprise shipments are guided flat to up low single digits
summary: Q3 FY2026 net sales were roughly stable at ~$1.6 billion but adjusted EPS swung to a loss of $0.09 from $0.48 profit a year ago, with adjusted EBITDA down YoY. Europe segment operating profit collapsed to $2 million from $95 million on ~4% lower price and volume plus ~$15 million of energy/freight above expectations, while Americas held up with sales up over 3% to $970 million and segment profit down ~2% to $137 million. 2026 guidance was cut to adjusted EBITDA of $925-950 million and free cash flow usage of ~$300 million, with year-end leverage of 4.5x-5x, reflecting lower volume (including the U.S.-Canada tariff), higher energy/freight, and reduced Fit to Win benefits now seen at $180 million. Management framed 2027 as higher sales, EBITDA, and free cash flow with at least $170 million of Fit to Win benefits, but deferred formal 2027 guidance to the next call and said Europe stays pressured through Q1 2027.

negative_highlights: Full-year 2026 revenue, Adjusted EBITDA, and non-GAAP EPS outlook ranges revised down; Q3 Adjusted EBITDA landed at the low end of its range.
Progressive Leasing revenue fell 0.7% YoY and gross margin contracted 20 bps to 31.8%, with write-offs at 8.3% of leasing revenue (near the high end of the 6-8% target) versus 7.4% a year ago.
Approval rates down nearly 300 bps YoY, the consumer remains stressed by persistent inflation and higher gas prices, and management explicitly took a more cautious near-term macro view.
positive_highlights: Four grew GMV 103% to $330.4M and revenue 113.8% to $37.2M, with Adjusted EBITDA of $11.4M (30.6% margin) and loss provision as a percentage of GMV improved ~100 bps YoY.

Progressive Leasing gross lease asset balance turned positive YoY for the first time since April 2025, with GMV up 2.3% and September the strongest month; Q4 leasing revenue expected to comp positively.
$100M ASR announced with initial delivery of ~2.7M shares, plus $500M total buyback capacity; recourse debt paid down $260M since January, net leverage at 1.5x.
summary: PROG delivered Q3 FY2026 revenue up ~26% to $725.8M and non-GAAP EPS of $1.06 (up 21.8%), with consolidated Adjusted EBITDA of $80M (11% margin) at the low end of the range, driven by leasing portfolio pressures. The company revised down its full-year 2026 outlook to revenue of $3.015-3.05B, Adjusted EBITDA of $345-355M, and non-GAAP EPS of $4.70-4.85, citing a stressed consumer. Progressive Leasing GMV grew 2.3% to $420.4M but revenue fell 0.7% and gross margin contracted 20 bps to 31.8%; Four grew GMV 103% and Purchasing Power grew GMV 12.3%. The company announced a $100M accelerated share repurchase and a replenished $500M buyback authorization, while net leverage fell to 1.5x.

negative_highlights: AUM fell 8% sequentially and 7% YoY to $169 billion, with $10.6 billion of net outflows including $7.8 billion from two discrete equity events
Adjusted operating margin declined 70 bps YoY and adjusted EPS rose only 1% YoY

note weakness in-term relative underperformance in larger equity strategies (International Value, Global Value) pressured one- and three-year numbers, and Q4 begins with lower AUM plus an estimated $2.5 billion distribution reduction
positive_highlights: Adjusted operating margin expanded 260 bps sequentially to 35.5% and adjusted operating income rose 9% QoQ
Credit and alternatives generated $1.1 billion of net inflows in the quarter and $3.2 billion YTD; credit marked its 17th consecutive positive flow quarter
Combined credit and alternatives AUM nearly doubled over five years to over $26 billion, rising from 8% to 15% of firm-wide AUM; dividend raised 10% QoQ to $0.88
summary: Artisan reported Q3 revenue of $313 million, up 1% sequentially and 4% YoY, with adjusted operating margin expanding 260 bps sequentially to 35.5% and adjusted EPS of $1.03 (up 1% YoY). But AUM fell 8% sequentially and 7% YoY to $169 billion on $10.6 billion of net outflows, of which ~$7.8 billion came from the US value team wind-down and a large Global Value client rebalancing. Management flagged short-term relative underperformance in International Value and Global Value, though it noted 75% and 84% of AUM outperforming over one and three years as of October 26. Q4 starts with lower AUM and an estimated $2.5 billion distribution-driven AUM reduction, with performance fees projected similar to last year's ~$29 million.

negative_highlights: Core EPS grew only 1% versus 5% sales growth, due to higher interest costs following the Nuvalent acquisition and a higher tax rate.
Vaccines sales fell 2%, with a drag from Shingrix China destocking; general medicines were flat, with Trelegy's U.S. business facing continued price pressure.
R&D spend rose 22% at CER, well ahead of sales, and Accelerate Growth charges are now expected at up to GBP 1 billion in 2026, above the prior GBP 0.7 billion.
positive_highlights: Specialty medicines sales grew 15% at CER, led by Cabenuva up 35% and APRETUDE up 21%, while Nucala rose 18% on COPD launch.
Gross profit rose 7% at CER, ahead of the 5% sales growth, supported by product mix and efficiencies; core operating profit grew 5%.
Free cash flow increased by GBP 1.8 billion year-to-date and GSK remains on track for around GBP 10 billion CGFO at constant rates.
summary: GSK reported Q3 FY2026 sales up 5% to GBP 8.9 billion at CER, core operating profit up 5% and core EPS up 1%, with strong cash generation of GBP 7.4 billion year-to-date and free cash flow up GBP 1.8 billion. Full-year 2026 guidance was reconfirmed rather than raised: sales and core operating profit expected in the upper half of the range, core operating margin above 31%, EPS growth in the low half of the range, and FX headwinds of -1% on sales and -3% on operating profit. The quarter was ordinary on the numbers, with specialty sales up 15% offset by vaccines down 2% and general medicines flat; management commentary was mixed, highlighting launch momentum and a large late-stage pipeline ramp but also acknowledging U.S. price pressure in the inhaled respiratory class, ViiV management changes, and an EXTEND 4M PK analysis still pending.

negative_highlights: International plumbing sales fell 5% in local currency (down 1% ex-divestiture) on difficult European comps and continued China weakness.
Decorative architectural sales were flat, with DIY paint down low single-digits and segment operating profit roughly flat at $126 million.
Mid-single-digit input cost inflation (copper, oil-based products, freight) plus higher employee-related costs pressure Q4, with total operating margin expected roughly flat year over year.
positive_highlights: EPS rose 23% to $1.19 and operating profit grew 13% to $351 million, with operating margin expanding 160 bps to 17.9%.
Gross margin improved 250 bps to 37.1%, aided by pricing, cost savings and lower year-over-year tariff costs.
Full-year EPS guidance raised to $4.65-$4.75 from $4.40-$4.60, with plumbing margin now expected at ~20% and decorative architectural at ~19.5%.
summary: Masco reported Q3 FY2026 net sales up 3% (4% in local currency ex-Bristan), operating profit up 13% to $351 million with margin up 160 bps to 17.9%, and EPS up 23% to $1.19. Full-year EPS guidance was raised to $4.65-$4.75 from $4.40-$4.60, and operating margin guidance increased to 18%-18.5% from ~18%, with segment margin targets also lifted (plumbing to ~20%, decorative architectural to ~19.5% from ~19%). Management flagged mid-single-digit input cost inflation and higher Q4 employee costs, and expects roughly flat year-over-year operating margin in Q4.

negative_highlights: Europe and rest of world net sales fell 6% to $34 million, with Europe down 18% on Wuxi China supply-route lead times; European segment gross margin fell 40 bps to 40%.
Year-to-date operating cash flow fell to $225 million from $283 million on higher working capital and inventory build for Early note.
Inflation for the full year is expected slightly above mid-single digits, and Q4 guidance implies gross margin below the prior-year in-season pricing mix.
positive_highlights: Adjusted diluted EPS rose 29% to $0.18 and adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 60 bps to 24.8% on operating leverage.
North America net sales grew 9% (U.S. +10%) with 7% price and 2% volume; adjusted segment income margin expanded 80 bps to 30.4%.
Full-year guidance raised to ~5%-6% sales growth and $0.86-$0.88 EPS from prior ~5% and $0.84-$0.87; net leverage at 1.5x is the lowest since the 2021 IPO.
summary: Hayward reported Q3 FY2026 net sales up 6% to $260 million with adjusted diluted EPS up 29% to $0.18 and adjusted EBITDA up 9% to $65 million (24.8% margin, +60 bps). North America grew 9% (7% price, 2% volume) while Europe and rest of world fell 6%, largely on an in-transit shipment timing shift into Q4. Full-year 2026 guidance was raised: sales growth now ~5%-6% (from ~5%) and adjusted diluted EPS $0.86-$0.88 (from $0.84-$0.87). Q4 sales implied flat to +3% with a less favorable price/mix as the mix shifts toward discounted Early Watch volume.

negative_highlights: Full-year 2026 net sales growth guidance was maintained at mid-to-high teens, not raised, despite Q3 outperformance.
Q4 gross margin is expected to moderate sequentially to 37%-38% from 39.9% in Q3 due to data center sales mix and inflationary pressures.
Residential energy storage sales declined on tougher prior-year comparison and a challenging solar/storage policy environment, weighing on the segment.
positive_highlights: Record Q3 net sales of $1.29 billion, up 16% YoY, with C&I segment sales up 28% to $553 million.
Adjusted EBITDA rose 33% to $256 million (19.8% margin), driving a 50 bps raise to full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA margin guidance of 20.5%-21%.
summary: Generac reported record Q3 FY2026 net sales of $1.29 billion, up 16% YoY, with C&I up 28% to $553 million and residential up 9% to $744 million. Adjusted EBITDA rose 33% to $256 million (19.8% margin), and GAAP EPS was $1.83 vs $1.12, with adjusted EPS $2.54 vs $1.83. The company raised full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA margin guidance to 20.5%-21% from 20%-21% but maintained net sales growth guidance in the mid-to-high teens, with data center revenue now expected near $500 million vs ~$450 million prior. A long-term Amazon supply agreement drove data center backlog to ~$4.5 billion (nearly tripling QoQ) and 2027 data center revenue is expected to exceed $2 billion.

negative_highlights: Completions margins were weighed down by higher-than-anticipated rebuilding costs (rehiring, inventory, maintenance) carried from Q2 into Q3
Net cash from operating activities fell to $46 million from $66 million, with working capital consuming about $15 million versus a prior $20 million source
Management guided to meaningful Q4 seasonality and continued margin pressure, with full cost-optimization benefit only arriving over time in 2027
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA rose 33% sequentially to $60 million (17% of revenue) on higher completions utilization and PROPWR deployments
PROPWR generated approximately $8 million of adjusted EBITDA, a meaningful sequential step-up, with contracted capacity at about 510 MW including the ~230 MW Targa award
Cash and equivalents of $729 million and total liquidity of $934 million after the $690 million convertible notes offering
summary: ProPetro reported Q3 2026 revenue of $355 million, up 16% sequentially, net income of $13 million ($0.09 per diluted share) versus a prior-quarter net loss of $8 million, and adjusted EBITDA of $60 million (17% of revenue) up 33% sequentially. PROPWR adjusted EBITDA reached roughly $8 million and contracted capacity totals about 510 MW, with 250-275 MW deployed by year-end 2026 and more than 500 MW by early 2028. Completions margins were pressured by higher-than-expected fleet reactivation and rebuilding costs, and management flagged meaningful Q4 seasonality plus continued margin pressure despite a sold-out 13-fleet position. 2026 capex guidance was narrowed for PROPWR to $400-$430 million (from prior) while per-MW cost of $1.4-$1.5 million and PROPWR guidance were reaffirmed and unchanged.

negative_highlights: Profit for the quarter was only INR 40 million despite INR 13,798 million in revenue, reflecting margin pressure from depreciation, interest, and manpower costs
Data center revenue declined sequentially, driven by absence of one-time enterprise implementation revenue and lower power pass-through revenue
Sify Infinit Spaces IPO timing remains uncertain, with a January-end deadline before the process must restart
positive_highlights: Revenue rose 31% YoY to INR 13,798 million and adjusted EBITDA rose 33% YoY to INR 3,131 million
113 MW of contracted data center capacity scheduled for delivery beginning this quarter over the next three quarters, with total design capacity approaching 300 MW
Management stated industry demand far exceeds supply, with no pricing pressure and improving returns on data center investments
summary: Sify reported Q2 FY2026-27 revenue of INR 13,798 million, up 31% YoY, with adjusted EBITDA of INR 3,131 million, up 33% YoY. Profit for the quarter was only INR 40 million despite strong top-line growth, reflecting heavy capex of INR 8,573 million and rising depreciation/interest costs. No formal guidance was issued, but management noted 113 MW of contracted data center capacity will be delivered over the next three quarters, and said data center pricing is improving with demand far exceeding supply. Data center revenue declined QoQ due to absence of one-time implementation revenue and lower power pass-through, while the Sify Infinit Spaces IPO timing remains undetermined with a January deadline before restart.

negative_highlights: Domestic same-store sales fell 5.4%, below expectations, prompting a full-year comp guidance cut to a decline of roughly 6.5%-7%.
Company-owned cost of sales rose 340 bps to 78.2% of sales on labor and operating expense deleverage, with some integration costs carrying into Q4.

Q4 adjusted EBITDA is guided below prior expectations due to a $138-140 million SG&A outlook including additional marketing spend not in the prior plan; unit growth outlook was also trimmed to 440-450 restaurants.
positive_highlights: Unit growth remained strong: 76 net new restaurants opened, bringing the system to 3,331 units, up nearly 14% year-over-year, with 544 international restaurants up more than 27%.
Club Wingstop loyalty showed early traction: new members return within 30 days at 13 points higher than non-members, and 90-day member purchase frequency is up almost 20%.
Guest complaints related to food quality and preparation declined approximately 30% year-to-date versus the prior year.
summary: Wingstop reported Q3 FY2026 domestic same-store sales down 5.4%, below management expectations, with system-wide sales up 6% to approximately $1.4 billion and net income of $29.1 million ($1.07 per diluted share). Adjusted EBITDA rose 0.5% to $64 million, but company-owned cost of sales rose 340 bps to 78.2% on sales deleverage. Management cut full-year domestic same-store sales guidance to a decline of approximately 6.5%-7% and guided Q4 adjusted EBITDA below prior expectations due to higher SG&A ($138-140 million) from incremental marketing spend; global unit growth outlook was trimmed to 440-450 net new restaurants from a timing shift in openings.

negative_highlights: Tangible book value per share fell to $16.09 from $16.44 at June 30 on a $116.1 million after-tax increase in AFS unrealized losses
Net charge-offs were $17.3 million in the quarter, and the allowance for credit losses declined to 1.10% of loans from 1.14%
CEO said economic growth would 'probably' stall with two more rate hikes, citing AI capital crowding out other investment
positive_highlights: EPS of $0.46 rose 21% YoY and PTPP income of $118.4 million rose 16% YoY, with revenue up 6% against essentially flat non-interest expense
NIM expanded 21 bps to 3.34% and the efficiency ratio improved to 59.1% from 67.2% in the prior quarter
CET1 rose 45 bps to an estimated 9.70%, exceeding the range guided last quarter, and core deposits grew about $515 million while broker deposits fell $375 million
summary: Banc of California reported Q3 FY2026 EPS of $0.46 (up 21% YoY) and pre-tax pre-provision income of $118.4 million (up 16% YoY), with revenue up 6% while non-interest expense was essentially flat. NIM expanded 21 bps to 3.34% and the efficiency ratio improved to 59.1% from 67.2%, while CET1 rose 45 bps to an estimated 9.70%, above the previously communicated range. Q4 PTPP guidance was reiterated at $125-130 million and the NIM outlook was narrowed to 3.35%-3.40%, with management citing full-quarter securities reinvestment benefits and completed loan sales as drivers of further growth into 2027.

negative_highlights: Weather-adjusted load growth was modest at 1.2% in the quarter
Guidance was reaffirmed rather than raised, with 2026 core EPS still a $2.62-$2.82 range at or slightly above the midpoint
Incremental West Virginia generation carries up to 35% equity or equity-like financing, implying further equity needs as the plan rolls forward
positive_highlights: Core EPS rose to $0.98 from $0.83 a year ago, and nine-month core EPS increased 9% to $2.20
Contracted and pipelined data center demand up nearly 60% since year-end, including a 90% increase in contracted demand to 7.9 GW
Transmission rate base growth of 14%, including 21% in the integrated transmission business, with a planned 25%+ increase to the $19 billion transmission investment plan
summary: FirstEnergy reported Q3 FY2026 GAAP EPS of $0.96 versus $0.76 a year ago and core EPS of $0.98 versus $0.83, with nine-month core EPS up 9% to $2.20. Management reaffirmed 2026 core EPS guidance of $2.62-$2.82 and expects to be at or slightly above the midpoint, with 6%-8% growth through 2030 near the top end. Weather-adjusted load rose 1.2% in the quarter, the fourth consecutive positive quarter, and contracted plus pipelined data center demand is up nearly 60% since year-end. The company signaled at least a 25% increase to its $19 billion transmission investment plan in the upcoming five-year update and expects a West Virginia order on Maidsville in Q4.

negative_highlights: Core growth decelerated to 7% from prior quarters as tariff-related price carryover was fully cycled
Q4 sales guided to $430-437 million, below Q3's $495 million, and management expects the 2027 market down a couple of points
Dodge data shows education and healthcare starts contracted at a 4% CAGR over the last four years, and management would not commit to a 2027 outlook until February
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA rose 15% to $140 million with margin up 150 bps to 28.3%
Full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance raised to $512-515 million
Board raised the annual dividend 18% and the company repurchased $35 million of stock in the quarter
summary: Q3 FY2026 sales were $495 million, up 9% reported and 7% core, landing at the high end of guidance, with adjusted EBITDA of $140 million (+15%) and margin up 150 bps to 28.3%. Full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance was raised to $512-515 million with free cash flow maintained at greater than $350 million, while Q4 sales are guided to $430-437 million and EBITDA to $120-123 million. Management flagged a 2027 market likely down a couple of points but affirmed 40%+ incremental margins plus roughly $5 million of incremental benefit, and announced an 18% dividend increase and $35 million of buybacks. Free cash flow was $110 million in the quarter and $264 million year to date.

negative_highlights: AFFO guidance implies a lower Q4, driven by ~$3M-$3.5M of Nord Anglia free rent and 2-3 cents of total rent abatement impact
Cap rates on closed and pipeline deals have moved only to the mid-to-high 7s from the low-to-mid 7s in H1, with interest expense guided higher in Q4 and into 2027
positive_highlights: AFFO per share of $1.33 rose 6.4% year-over-year; full-year 2026 AFFO guidance midpoint raised $0.03 to $5.26, implying 5.8% growth
Estimated rent loss from tenant credit events cut to $3M-$5M (25 bps of ABR) from a prior $7M-$10M, with Hellweg moved out of the top 25 tenants
Contractual same-store rent growth of 2.6% with nearly half of rents CPI-linked; quarterly dividend raised 4.4% to $0.95 at a 71% payout ratio, ~6% yield
summary: W. P. Carey reported Q3 FY2026 AFFO per share of $1.33, up $0.08 or 6.4% year-over-year, and raised and narrowed full-year 2026 AFFO guidance to $5.23-$5.29, lifting the midpoint $0.03 to imply 5.8% growth. Investment volume guidance was only moderately raised at the low end to $1.8B-$2.1B, with management citing rising long-term rates that make Q4 deal timing harder to predict, while estimated rent loss from credit events was cut to $3M-$5M from $7M-$10M. Contractual same-store rent growth was 2.6% and occupancy rose 10 bps to 98.6%; the dividend was raised 4.4% to $0.95 quarterly at a 71% payout ratio. Q4 AFFO is guided lower on roughly $3M-$3.5M of Nord Anglia free rent and 2-3 cents of total abatement impact.

negative_highlights: Total ARR growth of 11% trails subscription ARR growth of 13.5%, reflecting continued pressure in discretionary non-subscription services revenue (roughly flat for the full year).
Q4 adjusted EBITDA guidance of $62.4-$65.4 million implies a lower margin than Q3's 30%, as investment spend that came online late in Q3 ramps fully in Q4 and into 2027.
Helix/BaaS net-new activity remains slow, with management stating there is not yet enough traction with traditional FIs to report meaningful progress.
positive_highlights: Revenue of $225.8 million and adjusted EBITDA of $67.8 million both finished above the high end of guidance, with adjusted EBITDA margin reaching a record 30% (up ~580 bps year-over-year).
Full-year 2026 guidance raised on both revenue ($888-$892 million) and adjusted EBITDA ($253-$256 million), with implied margin expansion of ~500 bps versus the ~250 bps in initial guidance.
Free cash flow of $55 million (up 48% year-over-year, 81% of adjusted EBITDA) funded $39 million of buybacks while remaining debt-free, with $336 million remaining on the repurchase authorization.
summary: Q2 Holdings reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $225.8 million, up 12% year-over-year and 3% sequentially, with adjusted EBITDA of $67.8 million (30% margin) and non-GAAP gross margin of 62.6%, both above the high end of guidance. Subscription revenue grew 14% to 83% of total, subscription ARR reached $846 million (+13.5%), and total ARR was $989 million (+11%). Management raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $888-$892 million and adjusted EBITDA to $253-$256 million, implying ~500 bps of margin expansion versus prior expectations of ~250 bps, while reiterating 2027 subscription revenue growth of 12.5%-13% and 150-200 bps of margin expansion. The quarter also featured the appointment of CFO Jonathan Price as Co-CEO alongside Matt Flake.

negative_highlights: Cyber Safety revenue growth held at only 5%, and management declined to commit to more than mid-single digits, saying 'hope for doesn't make a plan'
Trust-Based Solutions margin held at 30% with management guiding to keep it there, limiting operating leverage as the higher-growth segment scales
Agentic AI products are expected to contribute no material revenue this fiscal year, leaving the new-product narrative unproven near term
positive_highlights: Revenue of $1.37 billion grew 12%, beating the high end of guidance, with bookings up 10% for a sixth consecutive quarter of double-digit growth
FY2027 revenue and EPS guidance both raised, with EPS growth now 16%-18% versus the prior 14%-18% range and above the prior 12%-15% midterm target
Cyber Safety operating margin reached a record 62% and cross-note penetration neared 30%, with up-note cohorts showing 5-10 point gains in retention and ARPU
summary: Gen reported Q2 FY2027 revenue of $1.37 billion, up 12% and above the high end of guidance, with bookings up 10% to $1.35 billion and non-GAAP EPS of $0.74, up 19% and above the $0.71-$0.73 guide. Cyber Safety grew 5% at a record 62% margin and Trust-Based Solutions grew 26% at a stable 30% margin, with blended operating margin held at 50% and free cash flow of $323 million. The company raised FY2027 revenue guidance to $5.465-$5.515 billion (10%-11% growth, from 9%-11%) and EPS to $2.93-$2.98 (16%-18% growth, from 14%-18%), with Q3 EPS guided to $0.73-$0.75. Management flagged no material agentic-AI revenue this fiscal year and stated it is not pursuing a transformative acquisition, while noting the $100 million cross-watch synergy ramp is on track for the second half into FY2028.

negative_highlights: Gross software backlog fell ~6% to $67.7 million and net backlog fell nearly 15% to $52 million YoY
Cancelable contract exclusions grew to $15.7 million from $11.2 million as customers shift to shorter terms
Software revenue flat at $16 million and wireless revenue still declining YoY, with management citing longer hospital decision cycles
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA up nearly 30% YoY to $8.6 million as expense reductions more than offset revenue decline
Adjusted operating expenses fell more than 8% to $26.1 million, with note and marketing down ~23% YoY
Narrowband spectrum sale closed and generated ~$7.6 million in cash, lifting cash to $30.1 million from $16.6 million in Q2
summary: Spok reported Q3 FY2026 GAAP net income of $9.7 million ($0.46/diluted share) versus $3.2 million ($0.15) a year ago, though adjusted for the narrowband license gain and restructuring, net income was about $4.5 million; adjusted EBITDA rose nearly 30% to $8.6 million as adjusted opex fell more than 8% to $26.1 million. Software revenue was essentially flat at $16 million with license revenue up ~30% to $1.4 million, while wireless revenue declined again (improvement of 220 bps in the YoY decline rate) and ARPU rose $0.17 to $8.36. Gross software backlog fell ~6% to $67.7 million and net backlog fell nearly 15% to $52 million, with management citing longer decision cycles and a customer preference for shorter-term contracts. Full-year 2026 revenue and adjusted EBITDA guidance was reiterated (ranges not stated on the call), and cash rose to $30.1 million, aided by ~$7.6 million from the narrowband license sale.

RSI reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $385.9 million, up 39% year-over-year, and adjusted EBITDA of $62.2 million, up 73%, with adjusted EBITDA margin of 16.1% (15% excluding a $4.3 million FX gain). North America revenue grew 14% and Latin America 218%; online casino grew 32% and online sports 70%. Full-year revenue guidance of $1.56–$1.60 billion and EBITDA of $245–$265 million was reiterated, but management said October trends put revenue near the low end of the range, citing moderating North American iCasino market growth, while EBITDA trends are near the midpoint. Positive office said 'We are encouraged by the strength of our business and the opportunities ahead, and we look forward to updating you on our progress when we share our fourth quarter and full year results.'

negative_highlights: Faster-than-anticipated roll-off of the Boost MVNO and ongoing prepaid declines are pressuring the wholesale and other service revenue line
Q4 EBITDA growth is implied to slow versus Q3 due to holiday promotional intensity and M&A timing comparisons, with Q3 inventory constraints shifting some costs into Q4
Q4 churn is expected to rise seasonally and from more 5G broadband and fiber-only accounts, which carry structurally higher churn than postpaid phone
positive_highlights: Core adjusted EBITDA guidance raised by $100 million at the midpoint to $37.35-$37.45 billion and adjusted free cash flow raised by $150 million to $18.7-$18.8 billion
Postpaid service revenue grew 9% and postpaid ARPA growth guidance was lifted to ~3.5% from 2.5%-3%
Adjusted free cash flow margin of 26% and $10.3 billion of buybacks through October 23, already above the $9.9 billion done in all of 2025
summary: T-Mobile reported Q3 with postpaid phone and 5G broadband net addition leadership, postpaid service revenue up 9% and total service revenue up 6%, core adjusted EBITDA up 11%, and adjusted free cash flow margin of 26%. Management raised full-year core adjusted EBITDA guidance by $100 million at the midpoint to $37.35-$37.45 billion and adjusted free cash flow by $150 million to $18.7-$18.8 billion, with full-year service revenue now ~$76.8 billion (+8%) and postpaid ARPA growth raised to ~3.5% from 2.5%-3%. The key change versus prior guidance is the higher ARPA and EBITDA/FCF outlook, partially offset by faster wholesale (Boost MVNO) roll-off and prepaid pressure; Q4 postpaid organic service revenue growth is guided to ~7%. No explicit EPS figures were provided in the transcript.

negative_highlights: Gross margin guidance of 62.5% for December remains below the 63%-64% target range, held back by persistently high memory costs
Management said it was supply-constrained all year and remains behind on supply ('I'm still note weakness in all year, same note weakness in now')
China revenue expected to fall to the low-20% range of the mix in calendar 2027 from roughly 27%-29% in 2026
positive_highlights: Record revenue of $4.14 billion rose 13% sequentially and 29% year-over-year, above the midpoint of guidance
Operating margin crossed 46% for the first time at 46.1%, up 240 bps sequentially, with gross margin of 62.7%
Advanced packaging process control revenue on track for approximately $1.1 billion in calendar 2026, more than 70% year-over-year growth; services revenue of $850 million rose 14% YoY
summary: KLA beat the midpoint of guidance across all key metrics with record revenue of $4.14 billion (up 13% QoQ, 29% YoY), gross margin of 62.7%, and a first-ever operating margin above 46% (46.1%, up 240 bps sequentially). Non-GAAP EPS was $1.22 and free cash flow was $1.34 billion. December quarter guidance is $4.7 billion ±$200M with non-GAAP EPS of $1.44 ±$0.11, and management raised its calendar 2026 wafer equipment market outlook to the mid-$150 billion range and guided calendar 2027 WFE above $200 billion, citing a growing backlog and unprecedented sales-funnel visibility.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA less NCI of $625 million compared to $671 million in Q3 2025, and was below internal expectations excluding $12 million of net favorable unusual items
Cedar Hill break-even pushed to 1H 2027 from prior Q4 2026 expectation; combined de novo and Laurel Ridge losses expected at $80-$100 million in 2026
2027 Medicaid supplemental payment headwind estimated at $175-$200 million, plus a $15 million exchange-related headwind from annualizing the 2H 2026 run rate
positive_highlights: Acute care same-facility adjusted admissions rose 4.9% YoY and ED visits rose 4.6%, with volume broad-based geographically
Behavioral health same-facility net revenue rose 4.0% on 2.1% adjusted patient day growth and 2.1% revenue per adjusted patient day
Operating cash flow was $637 million versus $381 million a year ago; Q3 buybacks of 1.35 million shares for $242 million brought YTD repurchases to $690 million
summary: UHS reported Q3 2026 adjusted EPS of $5.22, down 8% YoY, and adjusted EBITDA less NCI of $625 million versus $671 million a year ago. Excluding three items not in the July outlook ($47 million supplemental Medicaid benefits, $26 million added liability reserves tied to a Cumberland settlement, $8.5 million Talkspace transaction costs), adjusted EBITDA less NCI was below internal expectations on slower de novo ramps and soft surgical trends. Full-year 2026 guidance ranges were reiterated but management now expects results toward the lower end, and Cedar Hill break-even slipped to 1H 2027 from Q4 2026. Management flagged 2027 Medicaid supplemental headwinds of roughly $175-$200 million and framed 2026 losses at underperforming facilities at $80-$100 million.

negative_highlights: Q3 EBITDA of $66 million compares with $75 million in Q2, which management attributed partly to $5 million-$10 million of pulled-forward volume and margin benefit in Q2
Polymers Europe EBITDA fell $2 million due to the Germany maintenance turnaround, and Q4 faces further U.S. turnaround costs at the PA facility
Crop productivity demand declined in the quarter, and management expects lower volume growth in Q4 versus Q2 and Q3
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA rose 18% to $66.3 million and adjusted EPS nearly doubled to $0.94
Organic volume grew 7%, with Surfactants up 8%, Polymers up 3%, and Specialty Products up 20%
Project Catalyst savings now expected at $66 million-$70 million for 2026, above the prior 60% target, and above $25 million per quarter on average in 2027
summary: Stepan reported adjusted EPS of $0.94, up 98% from $0.48, and adjusted EBITDA of $66.3 million, up 18% year over year, on 7% organic volume growth across all three segments. Full-year 2026 guidance points to adjusted EBITDA growth, positive free cash flow, and continued deleveraging, with net leverage improved to 2.4x. Project Catalyst savings are now expected to exceed the 60% target, reaching $66 million to $70 million for 2026, and management says 2027 run-rate savings will average above $25 million per quarter. The key change from prior guidance is the upward revision to Project Catalyst savings and the increased dividend, though management flagged lower volume growth in Q4.

negative_highlights: Underlying cost reduction of 10% is behind schedule due to FX effects and higher energy consumption costs.
Johan Sverdrup decline of 11% year-to-date is expected to increase in 2027 versus 2026.
Empire Wind first power slipped to the first half of 2027, later than planned; safety incidents increased year-over-year with too many personal injuries.
positive_highlights: Adjusted operating income of $12.4 billion was almost double the year-ago level, driven by higher realized prices and an exceptional refining contribution.
Full-year 2026 production growth guidance raised to around 4% from 3%, with year-to-date growth of almost 5% and Bacalhau producing at plateau.
CFFO guidance lifted to around $29 billion from the $25 billion given at Capital Markets Day, based on current forward prices.
summary: Equinor reported Q3 2026 adjusted operating income of $12.4 billion (nearly double year-ago), cash flow from operations after tax of $8.1 billion, and adjusted EPS of $1.20. Production grew 2% (up almost 5% year-to-date), and management raised full-year production growth guidance from 3% to around 4%, while MMP delivered well above guidance. The board approved a $0.39 quarterly dividend and a fourth $1.125 billion buyback tranche, bringing 2026 buybacks to $3 billion; 2026 CapEx guidance held at around $13 billion and CFFO guidance raised to around $29 billion from the prior $25 billion. Management flagged a higher 2027 decline at Johan Sverdrup, cost pressure from FX, and a tax payment lag pushing year-end net debt ratio to roughly 10% on an adjusted basis versus 3.8% reported.

negative_highlights: O&M was higher year-over-year due to costs from the August 11 derecho and subsequent severe weather in northern Indiana
The storm triggered an internal after-action review expected by late November and an independent third-party review, alongside IURC proceedings
Planned $400 million-$600 million of annual maintenance equity issuance in the near term adds dilution to the funding plan
positive_highlights: Q3 adjusted EPS rose to $0.27 from $0.19 a year earlier, with YTD adjusted EPS at $1.49
2026 guidance narrowed to the upper half of the $2.02-$2.07 range, and 2027 EPS guidance initiated at $2.22-$2.30
Microsoft 20-year agreement adds roughly 1,100 MW and raises expected NIPSCO customer savings to about $1.75 billion from $1.4 billion
summary: NiSource reported Q3 FY2026 consolidated adjusted EPS of $0.27 versus $0.19 a year earlier, with year-to-date adjusted EPS of $1.49. The company narrowed 2026 EPS guidance to the upper half of the prior $2.02-$2.07 range, initiated 2027 guidance of $2.22-$2.30, and extended its capital plan through 2033 at $40 billion with a 10%-11% adjusted EPS CAGR. A new 20-year Microsoft agreement adds roughly 1,100 MW to the GenCo pool and lifts expected customer savings to about $1.75 billion from $1.4 billion last quarter. O&M rose on storm response costs tied to the August Indiana derecho, partially offsetting usage, customer-count and property-tax tailwinds.

negative_highlights: Loans held for investment declined $43.9 million (0.3%) linked quarter, with $214 million of unexpected CRE payoffs
Full-year non-interest income growth cut to low-to-mid-single-digit, with mortgage banking revenue down 11.6% linked quarter
Revenue fell 0.5% linked quarter amid treasury management fee migration to NII and slower equipment finance
positive_highlights: Record quarterly operating EPS of $1.00 per diluted share with ROATCE of 12.72% and ROA of 1.21%
Full-year 2026 NIM guidance raised to 3.83%-3.87%, with Q4 NIM expected around 4%
Credit quality strong: net charge-offs of $1 million, or 3 bps of average loans, and total deposit costs of 1.67%
summary: Trustmark reported Q3 net income of $58.1 million, or $1.00 per diluted share, a record operating EPS, with ROATCE of 12.72% and ROA of 1.21%. Revenue was $207.1 million, down 0.5% linked quarter but up 2.4% year-over-year, with NIM steady at 3.84% and non-interest expense up only 0.6% linked quarter. Management raised full-year 2026 NIM guidance to 3.83%-3.87% and expects Q4 NIM around 4%, while cutting the non-interest income outlook to low-to-mid-single-digit growth due to weak mortgage and treasury management fee migration. Loans fell $43.9 million linked quarter on elevated payoffs, though management cited a roughly $1 billion approved pipeline and reiterated mid-single-digit full-year loan growth.

negative_highlights: Q4 originations guided to $3.1-$3.2 billion, below Q3's $3.34 billion, on seasonality and coupon repricing
Higher benchmark rates drove roughly $20 million of fair value markdowns, with only about half the rate impact offset through marketplace pricing
Auto refinance is being pulled back as a thinner-margin business under rate pressure, a drag on near-term volume
positive_highlights: Diluted EPS of $0.50 came in above the $0.43-$0.48 guidance range, with full-year EPS guidance raised to $1.87-$1.92
Net charge-off ratio improved to 3.1% from 3.4%, and provision was a $16 million benefit, with a further $5-$10 million benefit expected in Q4
Originations grew 26% to $3.34 billion toward the upper end of guidance, with risk-adjusted revenue up 27% to a record $279 million
summary: Record pre-tax income of $76.8 million, up 34% YoY, with diluted EPS of $0.50 beating the $0.43-$0.48 guidance range; originations rose 26% to $3.34 billion, risk-adjusted revenue rose 27% to a record $279 million, and net charge-off ratio improved to 3.1% from 3.4%. Full-year EPS guidance was raised to $1.87-$1.92, though Q4 originations are guided down to $3.1-$3.2 billion on seasonality and higher borrower pricing. Net interest income grew 16% to a record $183 million with NIM at 6.05%, and a $15 million hedging gain and $12 million of one-time fair value benefits offset roughly $20 million of rate-driven markdowns. Management cited strong credit and a $5-$10 million expected Q4 provision benefit, but flagged a transition period as it pulls back on thinner-margin auto refinance and raises coupons through borrowers.

negative_highlights: Rig count reduced from about 12 to 10 entering Q4 in direct acknowledgement of a weakening market
About nine turn-in-lines pushed out of Q3, with Q4 production guided to a wide 7.4-7.6 Bcfe/d range
Low-to-mid single digit cost inflation expected from 2026 into 2027, with Haynesville rig counts up ~35% year-over-year
positive_highlights: Hedging improved realized prices by $0.46/Mcfe and contributed over $300 million relative to the strip in Q3
Q4 marketing and commercial guidance of ~$80 million (~$0.12/Mcfe) with line of sight to $500 million (~$0.20/Mcfe) by 2028 and $750 million longer term
Net debt of $4.7 billion at 0.8x leverage and $305 million of Q3 share repurchases
summary: Expand reported Q3 FY2026 production of roughly 7.5 Bcfe/d and repurchased $305 million of shares, with hedging adding $0.46/Mcfe to realized prices; no explicit revenue, EPS or margin figures were stated in the transcript. Management guided Q4 combined marketing and commercial EBITDA to about $80 million (~$0.12/Mcfe) and reiterated a path to $500 million (~$0.20/Mcfe) by 2028 and $750 million later, which would lower cash breakeven from ~$2.80 to ~$2.60 and then $2.50/Mcfe. Offsetting this, management cut rig count from about 12 to 10 entering Q4, deferred roughly nine turn-in-lines out of Q3, and flagged a low-to-mid single digit cost inflation factor into 2027 with a $2.80/Mcfe breakeven. Twin Eagle closed September 16 and integration is described as early-stage.

negative_highlights: Q4 revenue guidance midpoint of $1.3B is roughly flat sequentially, reflecting a digestion period in memory and a second-half compute program timing.
Gross margin guided down to 57.5%-58.5% for Q4 from 59.1% in Q3, citing product mix and new product launches.
Mobile remains below historical levels and underperforming prior model expectations, with recovery timing uncertain.
positive_highlights: Revenue of $1.3B topped the high end of guidance, up 70% YoY, with non-GAAP EPS of $2.29 up over 150% YoY.
Semi Test surpassed $1B (+77% YoY), memory set a record at $301M, and IST reached a record $95M (+~150% YoY).
Product Test posted 56% YoY growth with book-to-bill of 1.4x, and Robotics delivered its highest Q3 revenue ever while achieving profitability.
summary: Teradyne reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $1.3B, up 70% YoY and above the high end of guidance, with non-GAAP EPS of $2.29, up over 150% YoY. Semi Test revenue exceeded $1B (+77% YoY), with record memory at $301M and IST at $95M; Product Test grew 56% and Robotics 28%. Q4 guidance is $1.25B-$1.35B revenue and non-GAAP EPS of $1.95-$2.25, implying ~20% YoY growth and full-year revenue of ~$5.2B (+over 60%). Management reiterated expectations for healthy growth in 2027, citing strong backlog and compute momentum, with a more detailed model update expected in Q4.

negative_highlights: Q3 free cash flow was negative $9.1B on CapEx of $51.4B plus a $5.2B EC fine payment and TPU inventory build
Net income and EPS declined on a negative $8.2B OI&E swing from an unrealized SpaceX loss
Management flagged a slightly larger Q4 FX headwind, tougher Search comps, and near-term Cloud margin pressure from third-party capacity
positive_highlights: Cloud revenue grew 103% to $30.7B with operating margin of 36.2%, up from 23.7% a year ago, and backlog reached $561B
Consolidated revenue rose 25% to $127.6B with operating income up 30% to $40.6B and operating margin at 31.8%
Year-over-year query growth was the highest in five years, and Gemini app reached 1 billion users
summary: Alphabet reported Q3 FY2026 consolidated revenue of $127.6B, up 25% YoY in both reported and constant currency, with operating income up 30% to $40.6B and operating margin at 31.8%. Google Cloud revenue rose 103% to $30.7B with operating margin expanding to 36.2% from 23.7%, while Services grew 11% and Search grew 12% to $63.3B. Net income and EPS declined due to a negative $8.2B in OI&E from an unrealized SpaceX loss, and Q3 free cash flow was negative $9.1B on $51.4B of CapEx. FY2026 CapEx guidance of $195-205B was unchanged, Q4 faces a slightly larger FX headwind and slower Search comps, and Cloud margins face near-term pressure from ramping third-party capacity.

negative_highlights: GAAP EPS was only $0.17, diluted by $29.4 million ($0.30/share) of non-recurring merger expenses
Tangible book value per share fell slightly to $18.08 on merger costs and a $14 million after-tax AOCI hit from higher rates
Management flagged a roughly $5 million/quarter earnings gap to close to reach the 2027 EPS goal
positive_highlights: Core EPS of $0.48 rose 54% QoQ and 131% YoY; core efficiency ratio improved more than 8 points to 62%
Core operating expenses of $114 million came in below the $120-$125 million July guidance range
Total loans grew $216 million (~5% annualized) and deposits grew $319 million (1.8%); commercial originations rose 15% to $735 million
summary: OceanFirst reported Q3 FY2026 core EPS of $0.48, up 54% QoQ and 131% YoY, with GAAP EPS of $0.17 after $0.30/share of merger costs. Net interest income rose 43% QoQ to $172 million on the first full quarter of Flushing, and core operating expenses of $114 million came in below the prior $120-$125 million guidance range. NIM expanded 13 bps to 3.18% (3.08% ex the non-recurring recovery), and Q4 guidance calls for 1-2% loan and deposit growth, stable-to-modestly-higher margin, and core expenses declining to $110 million with a $105 million run-rate base into 2027. Full 2027 guidance is deferred to the January call, though the 1% ROA target is reiterated.

negative_highlights: Proposed iDose TR local coverage determinations remain unresolved; management acknowledged potential restrictions and could not commit to an iDose revenue trajectory for 2027 pending the outcome
Epioxa prior authorization timelines remain varied payer-by-payer and far from streamlined, with the operational and field support burden scaling faster than planned
Operating expenses guided to grow 25%-30% in Q4, landing full-year 2026 opex around $630 million, as disease-awareness investment ramps into 2027
positive_highlights: Full-year 2026 net sales guidance raised to $775-$785 million, an increase of $90 million at the midpoint over prior guidance of $680-$700 million
Non-GAAP gross margin expanded nearly 400 bps YoY to approximately 88%, with non-GAAP net income of $28.5 million and EPS of $0.47
Epioxa delivered approximately $53 million in its first quarter post J-code, with access pathways established for ~90% of commercial lives and ~80% of Medicaid lives
summary: Glaukos reported record Q3 FY2026 net sales of $211 million, up 58% YoY, with non-GAAP EPS of $0.47, non-GAAP gross margin near 88% (up ~400 bps YoY), and more than $50 million in cash generation. Epioxa contributed ~$53 million and iDose TR ~$76 million, driving U.S. glaucoma franchise sales of $118.6 million (+47%) and corneal health of $59 million (+154%). Management raised full-year 2026 net sales guidance to $775-$785 million from $680-$700 million (an increase of $90 million at the midpoint) and introduced preliminary 2027 revenue guidance of $1 billion. The primary risk flagged is the proposed iDose TR local coverage determinations, which management said the 2027 outlook already contemplates under downside scenarios.

negative_highlights: PFT core sales grew only 6.2% in the quarter, with chemical exposure still ~20% of the segment and flat into 2027
BS&U divestiture (~$160M revenue at fleet margin) versus Trillium (~$115M revenue at below fleet margin) implies some dilution near the end-of-Q1 close
Total growth heavily acquisition-driven (21 of 28 points), with AAT core orders up only 2% as reported
positive_highlights: Full-year adjusted EPS guidance raised $0.35 at the midpoint to $7.23-$7.38, with acquisition EPS contribution lifted to ~$0.30 from $0.20
Adjusted operating margin expanded 130 bps to a record 22.5% on 8% core growth, with adjusted operating profit up 36%
PFT core orders up 20% year-over-year and 8% sequentially, with total backlog up 9% to a record
summary: Crane reported total sales up 28% with 8% core growth and 21 points from acquisitions, adjusted operating margin expanding 130 bps to a record 22.5%, and adjusted operating profit up 36%. Core orders rose 11% (PFT +20%) and total backlog increased 9% year-over-year to a record. The company raised full-year adjusted EPS guidance by $0.35 at the midpoint to $7.23-$7.38 and lifted the acquisition EPS contribution to ~$0.30 from $0.20, while expecting the 10% ROIC hurdle ~18 months early. AAT core sales rose 9.5% with margin 26.3% (+100 bps), PFT core sales rose 6.2% with a record 24% margin, and the company announced the Trillium Pumps acquisition and BS&U divestiture.

negative_highlights: Higher risk management costs added ~$63 million year-over-year, with a $40 million hit in corporate and other.
Collection and disposal volume was modestly negative, including commercial down 1.3% and residential -3.5% year-to-date.
Diesel fuel spiked to record highs, creating a ~40 bps margin headwind and a one-month lag in surcharge recovery.
positive_highlights: Operating EBITDA grew 5.8% and revenue grew 6.3%, with all segments contributing.
Healthcare Solutions operating EBITDA rose 33% and revenue returned to growth, up 3.7%.
SG&A improved 70 bps to 9.3% of revenue; free cash flow up more than 42% year-to-date.
summary: WM reported Q3 FY2026 revenue growth of 6.3% and operating EBITDA growth of 5.8%, with core price at 5.8% and SG&A down 70 bps to 9.3% of revenue. Free cash flow rose more than 42% through the first nine months, and Healthcare Solutions revenue turned positive (up 3.7%) with operating EBITDA up 33% and SG&A at 15.2%, reaching year-end targets ahead of schedule. Full-year guidance was maintained for operating EBITDA within the original range, with revenue and free cash flow now expected at the high end of prior ranges. The quarter included a ~$63 million year-over-year increase in risk management costs, and collection and disposal volume was modestly negative (about -2.6% for the quarter).

negative_highlights: Revenue fell 20% year over year to $59.4 million on a 9% volume decline and 17% price decline
Gross margin contracted to 25% from 32% a year ago; net income fell to $2.0 million from $12.4 million
SG&A rose $1.9 million to $10.8 million on ERP costs and added personnel and consultants, and no shares were repurchased in the quarter
positive_highlights: Gross margin of 25% came in above internal expectations even as average note price fell 17%
Cash rose $10 million sequentially to $35.3 million with a debt-free balance sheet
Re-awarded the $210 million DLA contract extending the relationship through July 2031, contributing $11 million of Q3 revenue
summary: Hudson reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $59.4 million, down 20% year over year, as sales volume fell 9% and average watching price fell 17%; gross margin was 25% versus 32% a year ago, and net income fell to $2.0 million ($0.05 diluted) from $12.4 million ($0.27). Management reaffirmed its 2026 gross margin target at the low-to-mid 20% range and said it expects 2027 pricing to be roughly flat with 2026, while noting Q3 volume decline was intentional as it prioritized profitable sales. The company ended the quarter debt-free with $35.3 million in cash, up $10 million from June 30, but did not repurchase shares in the quarter despite the stock trading below book.

Q3 FY2026 revenue was $256 million, up 14% YoY, with gross profit of $33 million, GAAP net income of $5.5 million, adjusted EPS of $0.12, and adjusted EBITDA of $18 million, up 37% with margin expanding 120 bps. Marine revenue rose 13% to $161 million (11.6% EBITDA margin) and Concrete rose 16% to $95 million (11% EBITDA margin, including ~2% of favorable project write-ups). Full-year 2026 guidance was reiterated at $900-950 million revenue, $50-54 million adjusted EBITDA, $0.23-0.30 adjusted EPS, and $25-35 million CapEx, with management tracking toward the upper end of each range. Backlog was ~$645 million with book-to-bill around 0.7x, as the award cycle slowed even though submitted bids awaiting award doubled to ~$2 billion from just over $1 billion at the start of the year.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined 3.8% to $149 million and originations fell about 7% to $229 million year-over-year
Adjusted EPS fell to $0.37 from $0.46 and adjusted net income dropped 23% to about $32 million
