Full-year 2026 guidance range top end was reduced, and net charge-offs rose to roughly 53% of receivables from 47%
positive_highlights: Recoveries increased to approximately $15 million from $11 million in the prior year period
Pricing Test 5 and the upcoming Model 7 (20% improvement in pre-screening alignment) are positioned to support origination growth in Q4 and 2027
Company began repurchasing shares under the board-authorized $40 million program and holds approximately $141 million in cash and restricted cash
summary: OppFi reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $149 million, down 3.8% year-over-year, with originations down about 7% to $229 million. Adjusted net income fell 23% to roughly $32 million and adjusted EPS dropped to $0.37 from $0.46, while net charge-offs rose to about 53% of receivables from 47%. Full-year 2026 guidance was refined by trimming the top end: revenue $600-610 million, adjusted net income $115-120 million, and adjusted EPS $1.34-1.40. Management framed the quarter around strategic progress (line-of-credit launch, LOLA migration, Model 7 upcoming, BNCC deal pending regulatory approval) and an active $40 million buyback, but gave no 2027 guidance beyond saying expectations remain intact.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EPS fell 7% to $6.84 and total segment profit declined ~2% to $323 million as profitability missed expectations
Full-year adjusted EPS guidance cut to $21.00-$21.50 and revenue growth guidance lowered to ~6% from 8%

HCS organic segment profit fell $46 million as $47 million of tariff/inflation headwinds net of productivity more than offset $13 million of favorable mix and price; full-year HCS margin expected down ~350 bps
positive_highlights: Building Climate Solutions revenue up 24% (15% organic) with continued volume growth in commercial equipment and services
Operating cash flow of $395 million, up $95 million YoY, with trailing 12-month free cash flow conversion of 108%
HCS organic sales improved to down 1% from a 9% decline in Q2, and direct-to-contractor decline narrowed to 6% from 12%
summary: Lennox reported Q3 FY2026 revenue up 10.2% to $1.6 billion, but total segment profit fell about 2% to $323 million and adjusted EPS declined 7% to $6.84, with profitability missing management's expectations. Full-year adjusted EPS guidance was cut to $21.00-$21.50, revenue growth guidance lowered to ~6% from 8%, and free cash flow guidance reduced to $700-$750 million from $750-$850 million. HCS organic revenue fell 1% (improving from a 9% decline in Q2) with segment margin contraction driven by $47 million of tariff/inflation headwinds net of productivity, while BCS grew 24% (15% organic) but also saw margin pressure. Management outlined a four-part recovery plan (pricing, productivity, portfolio, promoters) and said 2027 should see sales, EBIT and EPS growth with a tougher first half.

negative_highlights: Crude charge fell to 614 Mbd from 639 Mbd, with lower MidCon volumes from the El Dorado turnaround and Q4 guidance of 560-600 Mbd
Sizable portion of refining upside tied to one-time EPA SRE waivers (~$500-600M per analyst framing) that are not monetized in cash flow and are deferred to future compliance
Refining OpEx rose sequentially on environmental accruals, employee benefit charges, and cat-chem inflation; company declined to commit to the prior $7.25/bbl target
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA of $3.0B versus $870M a year ago; refining adjusted EBITDA of $2.6B versus $661M
Adjusted EPS of $11.75 versus $2.44 in Q3 2025; net income $2.0B
Returned $572M to shareholders in the quarter ($479M buybacks, $93M dividends); net debt-to-cap of negative 4%
summary: HF Sinclair reported Q3 2026 net income of $2.0B ($11.38/diluted share) and adjusted net income of $2.1B ($11.75/diluted share), up sharply from $459M ($2.44) a year earlier; adjusted EBITDA was $3.0B versus $870M. Refining adjusted EBITDA reached $2.6B versus $661M, driven by tight fuel supply, elevated crack spreads, and EPA small-refinery RIN waivers, with capture ex-SRE at roughly 105%. Capital guidance was revised to ~$725M sustaining/turnaround plus $150M growth, Q4 crude guidance is 560-600 Mbd (reflecting the El Dorado turnaround), and the Lubes spin remains on track for H2 2027. Shareholder returns totaled $572M ($93M dividends, $479M buybacks) with a $0.525 quarterly dividend declared.

negative_highlights: CapEx guidance raised to $255-275 million from $220-250 million prior
Incumbent broadband data churn rose to 1.76% and data ARPU fell 3% YoY to ~$80 on competition and rural demand softness
Incumbent broadband revenue declined $2.8 million on a 13% drop in video RGUs and lower data ARPU
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA growth of 11.8% to $33.2 million outpaced revenue growth of 4.6%, expanding margin 200 bps YoY
Glo Fiber data net adds hit a record 8,600, up 48% YoY, with penetration reaching 21.7% (+108 bps YoY)
2026 revenue and Adjusted EBITDA guidance reiterated; management expects 300-400 bps of further EBITDA margin expansion in 2027
summary: Total revenue rose 4.6% YoY to $93.9 million and Adjusted EBITDA grew 11.8% to $33.2 million, with margin expanding 200 bps in the quarter. Glo Fiber and commercial fiber revenue grew 19.5% and reached 52% of consolidated revenue, while Glo Fiber data customers rose 32% YoY to ~109,000 on a record 8,600 net adds. Full-year 2026 revenue ($370-377 million) and Adjusted EBITDA ($131-136 million) guidance was reiterated, but CapEx guidance was raised to $255-275 million from $220-250 million for 7,000 extra passings and grant timing. Incumbent broadband remained a drag, with data churn up to 1.76% and ARPU down 3% YoY.

negative_highlights: Recent acquisitions, including 22 new operations this quarter and since (nine in Florida), are described as significantly challenged turnarounds expected to take a year or more to contribute
Texas acquisition operations remain not accretive, with only possible fourth-quarter contribution
Same-store occupancy at 84.1% still leaves meaningful runway versus mid-90s levels at the most mature operations
positive_highlights: Adjusted diluted EPS rose 23.8% to $2.03 and GAAP net income rose 24.4% to $104.3M on revenue growth of 14.5% to $1.48B
2026 EPS guidance raised to $7.94-$8.02 from $7.75-$7.85, with the midpoint up 21.5% over 2025
Same-store skilled mix revenue and Medicare revenue increased 10.7% and 11.1% respectively, with growth across all skilled payer categories
summary: Q3 FY2026 GAAP revenue and adjusted revenue both $1.48B, up 14.5% YoY; GAAP diluted EPS $1.76 (+23.9%) and adjusted diluted EPS $2.03 (+23.8%). Same-store occupancy 84.1% and transitioning 86.1%, with skilled mix revenue up 10.7% and skilled days up 7.2%, growth across all payer categories. Management raised 2026 EPS guidance to $7.94-$8.02 (from $7.75-$7.85) and lifted the low end of revenue guidance to $5.89B, midpoint EPS implying 21.5% growth over 2025. The main caveat is that recent acquisitions, including 22 new operations with nine in Florida, are characterized as challenged turnarounds that are not yet accretive and will take a year or more to contribute.

negative_highlights: Net loss of CNY 1.494 billion versus a CNY 380 million loss a year ago, driven by a CNY 721 million pre-tax loss and CNY 773 million of tax expense including a deferred tax asset writedown
Credit impairment losses rose 10.3% to CNY 4.511 billion, exceeding total income and producing total expenses of CNY 6.9 billion against CNY 6.180 billion of income
C-M3 flow rate rose to 1.2% from 1.0% sequentially, with total outstanding balance down 11.9% year-over-year to CNY 167.1 billion
positive_highlights: New loan sales rose 2.5% year-over-year and 14.1% quarter-over-quarter to CNY 58.3 billion, led by consumer finance up 25.2% to CNY 39.7 billion
Cost of funds by balance excluding consumer finance fell to 3.6%, down 20 bps sequentially and 80 bps year-over-year
DPD 30+ and 90+ delinquency rates for enabled loans improved to 5.5% from 5.8% and 3.2% from 3.7% sequentially; consumer finance NPL stable at 1.3%
summary: Lufax reported a net loss of CNY 1.494 billion versus a CNY 380 million loss a year ago, within the CNY 1.30-1.70 billion range pre-announced on October 16; the loss comprised a CNY 721 million pre-tax loss and CNY 773 million of tax expense tied to a deferred tax asset writedown and withholding tax on planned domestic-to-offshore dividends. Total income fell 4.6% to CNY 6.180 billion as technology platform income dropped 24.1% and guarantee income fell 24.6%, partly offset by 10.3% net interest income growth; credit impairment losses rose 10.3% to CNY 4.511 billion. New loan sales rose 2.5% year-over-year (14.1% quarter-over-quarter) to CNY 58.3 billion on consumer finance growth of 25.2%, but the C-M3 flow rate rose to 1.2% from 1.0% sequentially. Management gave no numeric guidance, calling the collection-enforcement-driven risk volatility temporary while flagging continued macro and regulatory pressure for a couple more months.

negative_highlights: Consolidated revenue declined 3.4% YoY to $605 million, with BetterHelp segment revenue down 12.8% on lower cash pay in U.S. and non-U.S. markets
BetterHelp EBITDA margin guidance for 2026 cut ~30 bps at the midpoint to 2.7%-4.3%, with Q4 BetterHelp revenue guided down 18.5%-31.5%
Average total BetterHelp paying users fell 12% YoY and 3% sequentially to 336,000, and management expects continued cash pay pressure into 2027 with ad spend down mid-to-high 20s%
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA of $79 million was above the high end of guidance and grew 13.5% YoY, with consolidated margin up ~200 bps to 13.1%
BetterHelp insurance revenue of $32 million beat the high end and rose $10 million sequentially; weekly sessions hit 27,000 (~$140 million annualized run rate) vs $110 million referenced last quarter
Integrated Care adjusted EBITDA margin of 18.8% was well above the high end, up ~180 bps YoY despite visit-based mix shift, and full-year IC margin guidance raised ~30 bps at the midpoint
summary: Revenue of $605 million declined 3.4% YoY but came in near the high end of guidance, with adjusted EBITDA of $79 million (up 13.5%) above the high end and margin expanding ~200 bps to 13.1%. Full-year 2026 revenue guidance was raised $13 million at the midpoint ($2.39B-$2.44B) and adjusted EBITDA guidance raised $3 million at the midpoint, with Integrated Care margin guidance raised, but BetterHelp EBITDA margin guidance was cut ~30 bps and Q4 BetterHelp revenue guided down 18.5%-31.5%. Insurance revenue of $32 million beat the high end, with 27,000 weekly sessions representing a ~$140 million run rate and a stated goal of at least $200 million exiting 2027, while cash pay pressure persists, prompting a further mid-20s% ad-spend reduction and a lower 2027 cash pay outlook.

negative_highlights: Developed markets declined 0.9% and Europe fell 1.7%, with management calling Europe 'probably the most challenged region'
Foods grew only 0.1%, with U.S. condiments performance below expectations amid avocado-oil mayo and discount-brand competition
Wellbeing declined high single digit (down 1% year to date), with Nutrafol in high single-digit decline and higher customer acquisition costs
positive_highlights: Underlying sales rose 5.2% with 2.9% volume growth, and Power Brands grew 5.8% (3.3% volume)
Emerging markets grew 9.5% with 6% volume, including India +15% and Brazil high single digit
Full-year outlook upgraded to at least 3% volume growth, and full-year currency impact eased to roughly -2% on turnover from -5.1% in H1
summary: Unilever reported Q3 FY2026 underlying sales growth of 5.2% (2.9% volume, 2.3% price) and turnover of EUR 13.3 billion, up 6.7%, led by emerging markets (+9.5%) and HPC (+7%), while developed markets declined 0.9% and Europe was down 1.7%. Management upgraded its full-year outlook to at least 3% underlying volume growth and around 5% second-half underlying sales growth, and confirmed modest underlying operating margin improvement versus 20% in 2025, despite raising full-year inflation expectations to about EUR 900 million from a prior EUR 800-900 million range. Foods grew only 0.1% and Wellbeing declined high single digit, with U.S. condiments and Nutrafol explicitly identified as below expectations, while North America returned a 0.7% decline on a tough comparator.

negative_highlights: Maggiano's comps fell 3.4%, with traffic down 5.1%
Chicken Parm Big Crispy is note about 2 per day, note weakness in of expectations, due to lack of in-restaurant merchandising until November 1
October mix turned slightly negative as consumers pulled back on alcohol and dessert purchases
positive_highlights: Chili's same-store sales +10.1% with traffic +6.4%, outpacing casual dining by 720 bps on top of a +21% lap
Adjusted diluted EPS of $2.77, up 44% from $1.93, with restaurant operating margin up 150 bps to 17.7%
FY2027 guidance raised to revenue of $6.23-6.33 billion and adjusted diluted EPS of $13.30-13.90, with $125 million of shares repurchased in the quarter
summary: Brinker reported Q1 FY2027 total revenue of $1.476 billion with consolidated comps +9.1%; Chili's comps rose 10.1% (traffic +6.4%, price +3.7%, mix flat) while Maggiano's comps fell 3.4%. Adjusted diluted EPS was $2.77 versus $1.93 a year ago (+44%), restaurant operating margin expanded 150 bps to 17.7%, and adjusted EBITDA rose 21.3% to about $209.1 million. Management raised FY2027 targets to revenue of $6.23-6.33 billion and adjusted diluted EPS of $13.30-13.90, citing Q1 outperformance and business momentum, and guided Q2 to high mid-single-digit comps with positive traffic. Constraints include consumer check management (mix turned slightly negative in October), the Chicken Parm Big Crispy watching about 2 per day versus expectations, and roughly $7 million of oil/freight inflation baked into guidance.

negative_highlights: Organic daily sales fell 1% as sales volume declined approximately 5%, more than offsetting 4% price contribution
Full-year adjusted EBITDA guide of $425-$440 million includes a $6-$8 million restructuring charge and $4-$5 million 53rd-week impact
positive_highlights: Gross margin expanded 80 bps to 35.5% on strong price realization, with adjusted EBITDA margin up 60 bps to 10.7%
Private brand products (Pro-Trade, Solstice, Portfolio) grew 23% in the quarter and over 35% year-to-date; digital sales on siteone.com up over 45% YTD
Repurchased ~646,000 shares for ~$62 million in the quarter and board added $500 million to the buyback authorization
summary: SiteOne reported Q3 FY2026 net sales up 3% to $1.29 billion, with organic daily sales down 1% as roughly 5% volume decline more than offset 4% price. Gross margin expanded 80 bps to 35.5% and adjusted EBITDA rose 8% to $138.3 million (10.7% margin, up 60 bps), while SG&A rose 20 bps to 28.6% and net income grew 8% to $63.9 million. Full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance is $425-$440 million, and management now expects to take a $6-$8 million Q4 charge for workforce reductions and branch closures, with the 53rd week an additional $4-$5 million drag, while still guiding to slight full-year margin expansion. End-market demand remains soft, with new residential seen down double digits for the year and repair and upgrade stepping down on higher rates and weak consumer confidence.

negative_highlights: Full-year same-store sales guidance of at least 2.5% implies Q4 deceleration in two- and three-year trends versus the 3% Q3 result
Management flagged continued softness in consumer confidence and a temporary late-Q3 slowdown as the basis for the Q4 outlook
The $9 million area director benefit will lap through 2027, with no year-over-year impact likely by Q3, pressuring future EBITDA growth comparisons
positive_highlights: Same-store sales accelerated to 3% from 2.3% in Q2, driven primarily by transaction growth while industry traffic was challenged
summary: Jersey Mike's reported Q3 FY2026 system-wide sales of $1.2 billion, up 11% on 9% net unit growth and a 3% same-store sales increase that accelerated from 2.3% in Q2 and was led by transactions. Total revenue rose 10% to $209 million and adjusted EBITDA grew 20% to $125 million, aided by a $9 million year-over-year benefit from the area director transition. Full-year guidance was reiterated at SSS of at least 2.5%, net unit growth of at least 8%, adjusted EBITDA growth of at least 20%, with Q4 implied comps near 3% reflecting a short-lived late-Q3 consumer softness. The board authorized a $100 million buyback and a $0.35 per-share special dividend, roughly $200 million of capital return within four months of IPO.

Q3 FY2026 sales fell 10% YoY to $117.9M, adjusted EBITDA dropped 33% to $21.5M, and adjusted EPS fell 54% to $0.39, with consolidated gross margin down ~350 bps to 34.3%. Branded Spirits sales fell 4% to $58.2M, Distilling Solutions fell 29% to $29M on a 47% brown goods decline, while Ingredient Solutions grew 5% to $30.8M. Full-year guidance was reaffirmed: net sales $480-500M, adjusted EBITDA $90-98M, adjusted EPS $1.50-1.80, with segment outlooks unchanged and Distilling Solutions still expected down ~35%. Management noted Q3 adjusted EBITDA and EPS came in ahead of internal expectations on cost savings, debt was cut $28.4M to a 3.6x leverage ratio, and the company rebrands to Sempreon (ticker CASK) on November 2.

negative_highlights: Management said it is not planning to share orders data going forward, and declined to detail 2027 CapEx, lowering transparency for lumpy demand metrics
EMEA full-year organic growth guidance remains low to mid-single digits despite the Q3 pipeline doubling, indicating regional recovery is still uneven

New-product quality questions (compressor burnouts, UPS overheating) prompted management to acknowledge 'we are not perfect' and that a higher new-product mix carries a statistically higher defect curve in the early phase
positive_highlights: Q3 net sales up 61% YoY to ~$4.3 billion with ~55% organic growth across all regions (Americas organic +66%, APAC +48%, EMEA +19%)
Adjusted diluted EPS of $2.21 beat guidance midpoint by $0.41, up 78% YoY; adjusted operating margin of 25.2% expanded ~290 bps and beat guidance by 70 bps
Full-year 2026 guidance raised across all key metrics—sales midpoint to $14.65 billion (+$650 million), EPS to $7.15 (+$0.45), adjusted operating profit to ~$3.5 billion
summary: Vertiv reported Q3 FY2026 net sales up 61% YoY to ~$4.3 billion (~55% organic, 6% acquisitions), adjusted diluted EPS of $2.21 up 78% and $0.41 above guidance midpoint, and adjusted operating margin of 25.2% (up ~290 bps, 70 bps above guidance). Organic orders grew more than 100% YoY, spread across customer types and all three regions. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance across all key metrics: net sales to $14.65 billion midpoint (+$650 million vs prior), adjusted EPS to $7.15 (+$0.45), adjusted operating profit to ~$3.5 billion, and adjusted free cash flow to $2.7 billion. Q4 guidance points to ~$4.4 billion net sales and EPS of $2.25, but management declined to detail 2027 CapEx and said they will stop disclosing orders data going forward.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA margin fell 210 bps to 23.8% and CCM margin fell 200 bps to 28.2% as raws and freight inflation outpaced price realization
Price-cost parity slipped one quarter to exit 2026 from the July expectation of neutral in Q3 and positive in Q4
Drivers cited as worsening: U.S. diesel around $6.35/gal, roughly 75% higher year-over-year, with Q3 raws and freight up high-teens versus double digits in Q2
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 9% to $1.5 billion with CCM +8% to $1.1 billion and CWT +9% to $379 million, both ahead of their end markets
Adjusted EPS rose 6% to a record third-quarter $5.92, aided by an 8% lower diluted share count
CWT adjusted EBITDA rose 13% to $68 million with margin up 60 bps to 18%; reroofing returned to mid-single-digit growth and CCM October bookings remained strong
summary: Revenue rose 9% to $1.5 billion and adjusted EPS rose 6% to a record Q3 $5.92, but adjusted EBITDA was flat at $348 million and the adjusted EBITDA margin fell 210 bps year-over-year to 23.8% as raw material and freight costs rose faster than price realization. Management pushed price-cost parity out one quarter to exit 2026 (from Q3 neutral / Q4 positive guided in July), citing unanticipated input cost escalation, and guided Q4 to high single-digit revenue growth with flat adjusted EBITDA margin and CCM flat / CWT up ~100 bps. Q4 CCM price realization is expected around 7% versus about 4% in Q3, and the pricing now in place is expected to be a tailwind into 2027, with Vision 2030 targets of $40 adjusted EPS unchanged.

negative_highlights: Management said results were 'much lower than expectations' and that the last several quarters were difficult for the bank and shareholders.
Interchange income fell after online sports betting operators disallowed credit cards, which management said had a significant effect on third-quarter results.

The SBA operating procedure change pushes December originations into January, which management said will hurt fourth-quarter gain-on-sale income; the LuckyLoads card launch slipped to Q2 2027 and the CFO search is still ongoing.
positive_highlights: NIM improved to 3.95%, about 17 bps higher quarter-over-quarter, with the prime rate increase expected to benefit the next quarter.
Early-stage delinquencies fell by more than $10 million and NPAs declined by $5 million, with about $10 million of OREO targeted for resolution.
Gain-on-sale margin rose to 5.57% from 5.04%, with management citing a normalized range of 5%-6%.
summary: GBank reported Q3 results that management itself described as 'much lower than expectations,' with net interest income and NIM improving to 3.95% (up about 17 bps) and continued expense pressure. Interchange income fell because several online sports betting operators disallowed credit cards as a payment source, and gain-on-sale income was reduced by a timing change in SBA sales rules. Guidance was minimal: loan growth of 10%-15%, a normalized gain-on-sale margin of 5%-6%, and the statement that gaming FinTech programs will not be material near term. The CEO transition to Jeff Newgard was completed, and management said credit costs should normalize by 2027 while citing a $10 million reduction in early-stage delinquencies.

negative_highlights: GAAP EPS was a loss of $0.14, including $284M of acquired IPR&D and milestone charges (~$1.70 impact to non-GAAP EPS)
VUMERITY revenue fell 11% YoY to $192M on tighter Part D formulary management, expected to persist
SPINRAZA's 23% YoY growth to $461M included a one-time high-dose conversion tailwind, with Q4 expected up only mid-single-digit YoY; core OPEX rose 27% YoY
positive_highlights: Growth portfolio revenue of ~$1.3B, up 49% YoY and 19% QoQ, now ~63% of core pharmaceutical revenue
Raised the low end of FY2026 non-GAAP diluted EPS guidance to $12.20-$13.00 on faster Apellis synergy capture
SYFOVRE revenue $191M, up 27% YoY, with commercial injection volume up 18% YoY; strongest commercial injection quarter since launch
summary: Total revenue rose 11% YoY to $2.8B, while core pharmaceutical revenue grew 18% to $2.0B, driven by a growth portfolio up 49% YoY to ~$1.3B (now ~63% of core revenue). The first full Apellis quarter contributed $243M from SYFOVRE and EMPAVELI, and management raised the low end of FY2026 non-GAAP EPS guidance to $12.20-$13.00, citing faster-than-expected integration synergies with the Apellis deal now roughly neutral on an operating basis. GAAP EPS was a loss of $0.14 due to $284M in acquired IPR&D and milestone charges tied to Reata. Offsetting the strength, VUMERITY fell 11% YoY on Part D formulary pressure, and SPINRAZA benefited from a one-time high-dose conversion tailwind expected to normalize in Q4.

negative_highlights: Net non-operating expenses of KRW 32.6 trillion (KRW 11.6 trillion FX loss plus KRW 22.9 trillion investment valuation losses) cut pre-tax income to KRW 50.7 trillion from KRW 83.3 trillion operating profit
NAND bit shipments declined slightly QoQ as sales were adjusted toward high-value 321-layer TLC enterprise SSDs

Some customers are lowering HBM stack counts (e.g., 12-stack HBM4 to 8-stack HBM4E), and 2027 achievable demand growth is guided similar to 2026 (mid-20% DRAM, high-teens NAND) rather than accelerating
positive_highlights: Revenue KRW 104.6 trillion, up 32% QoQ and 328% YoY, first quarter above KRW 100 trillion; operating profit KRW 83.3 trillion at an 80% operating margin, both all-time records
HBM4 mass production and shipments began in Q3 and are expected to surpass HBM3E in both bit and revenue share in Q4; HBM4 yield exceeded plan and the target was revised up

DRAM and HBM volume effectively sold out through 2029, with LTA-covered volume above 50% of 2027 and 2028 capacity; ~KRW 100 trillion FY2026 shareholder return plan includes a KRW 10,000/share Kioxia special dividend
summary: SK hynix reported record Q3 FY2026 revenue of KRW 104.6 trillion, up 32% QoQ and 328% YoY, the first quarter above KRW 100 trillion. Operating profit reached KRW 83.3 trillion (up 38% QoQ, 632% YoY) at an 80% operating margin, with DRAM ASP up high-20% and NAND ASP up mid-20%. Management guided Q4 DRAM bit shipments up mid-20% sequentially and NAND up mid-single digits, said DRAM and HBM volumes are effectively sold out through 2029, and announced roughly KRW 100 trillion of shareholder returns for FY2026 including a KRW 10,000 per-share Kioxia special dividend. The main negative was KRW 32.6 trillion of net non-operating expenses (KRW 11.6 trillion FX loss, KRW 22.9 trillion investment valuation losses), pulling net income to KRW 39.8 trillion at a 38% net margin.

negative_highlights: Europe AOI deteriorated by EUR 468m YoY to negative EUR 311m on unfavorable BEV mix and pricing pressure
Industrial free cash flow was negative EUR 4bn in Q3, requiring a large Q4 working-capital reversal to get to positive for the year
Q4 headwinds cited from memory chips and recall costs, with commodity costs expected to rise further in 2027
positive_highlights: Industrial cost improved by EUR 828m YoY, the largest AOI driver, reflecting VCP purchasing savings and lower CO2 compliance and warranty costs
North America AOI improved by EUR 539m YoY to EUR 64m on pricing of +EUR 421m and cost cuts
Tariff headwind trimmed to about EUR 1bn from the prior EUR 1.0-1.2bn estimate
summary: Q3 net revenue rose 1% YoY to EUR 37.6bn on shipments of 1.3m units, down 1%, which was better than expected versus soft AOI of EUR 256m at a 0.7% margin, up 50 bps YoY. Industrial free cash flow was negative EUR 4bn, though EUR 0.3bn better than last year, with the company expecting a Q4 working-capital reversal that leaves free cash flow positive for FY26 and in 2027. Europe AOI fell to negative EUR 311m, a EUR 468m YoY deterioration, but North America improved by EUR 539m to EUR 64m. Guidance for 2026 was reaffirmed, with a modest reduction in the net tariff estimate to about EUR 1bn, but the company gave no detailed 2027 bridge and flagged rising memory-chip and commodity costs.

negative_highlights: Fuel prices rose sharply since March, keeping adjusted OpEx roughly flat as a percent of revenue and muting operating leverage; management said only most, not all, of the cost is being passed through
Middle East operations remain a drag, with reported unique customer growth of 4.4% versus ~5.7% excluding the conflict impact and conservatism built into Q4 for the region
Q4 guidance implies a modest organic slowdown to ~10% from ~11% year-to-date, reflecting the lapped Italco acquisition (~50-80 bps) and a ~1% tougher comparison
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA rose to $82.2 million from $65.1 million a year ago, with full-year guidance implying reaching the 7% EBITDA margin target originally set for 2028
Gross margin expanded ~84 bps to 25%, including ~137 bps of center-of-the-plate margin improvement on product mix and procurement leverage
Organic net sales grew 10.3%, with unique item placements up 7.2% and specialty case growth of 6.1%
summary: Q3 FY2026 net sales rose 11.2% to $1.135 billion, with organic sales up 10.3% and acquisitions adding ~0.9%; adjusted EBITDA grew to $82.2 million from $65.1 million and adjusted EPS rose to $0.66 from $0.50. Gross margin expanded ~84 bps to 25%, driven by product mix and procurement scale, though fuel costs kept adjusted OpEx roughly flat versus prior year. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance to net sales of $4.56-$4.61 billion and adjusted EBITDA of $317-$321 million, while flagging some conservatism on the Middle East and a tougher Q4 comp.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to $183.2 million ($1.55/share) from $90.8 million ($0.81/share) a year earlier
R&D expenses rose to $166.8 million from $90 million and G&A to $20.3 million from $8.6 million YoY
Timing of VANQUISH maintenance/extension data in the initial filing is unresolved ('TBD'), with management expecting it more likely as a later supplement
positive_highlights: Maintenance study showed 82%-97% of weight loss retained at week 33 under every-other-week or monthly dosing versus 61% for placebo
Exploratory 17.5 mg weekly cohort reached ~22% mean weight loss at 33 weeks with no observed plateau
Cash of $960 million at quarter end, including ~$550 million net proceeds from the concurrent offerings, with guided cash use of ~$100 million per quarter
summary: Viking reported a Q3 FY2026 net loss of $183.2 million, or $1.55 per share, versus a $90.8 million / $0.81 loss a year ago, as R&D jumped to $166.8 million from $90 million and G&A rose to $20.3 million from $8.6 million. No product revenue exists (pre-commercial biotech); the balance sheet showed $960 million in cash at September 30, including roughly $550 million of net proceeds from ~$575 million gross concurrent common-stock and convertible-note offerings. Management guided to company-wide cash usage averaging roughly $100 million per quarter and described VANQUISH phase III as fully enrolled and on track, with SUNRISE oral phase III initiated in October 2026. The most important change versus the prior period was the positive maintenance dosing data — up to ~22% weight loss at 33 weeks on 17.5 mg weekly, and 82%-97% of weight loss retained under every-other-week or monthly dosing versus 61% for placebo — plus the capital raise extending runway.

negative_highlights: Coastal margins pressured by elevated Q4 shipyard days and softer 80s/100s barge pricing on reduced European import flows
Rising fuel costs only partially mitigated by escalators and rate recovery during the quarter
OEM engine availability remains constrained, limiting the pace of backlog conversion into revenue
positive_highlights: Record Q3 EPS of $2.09, up 27% year-over-year
Marine transportation operating income up 26% YoY on 17% revenue growth, with inland revenue up 21%
Power generation backlog now north of $1.5 billion with book-to-bill well above one, and KDS operating margin up 200 bps sequentially to 12%
summary: Kirby reported record Q3 EPS of $2.09, up 27% YoY, with marine transportation revenue up 17% to $569 million and operating income up 26% at a 20% margin, while Distribution & Services revenue rose 6% to $408 million with a 12% operating margin. Management narrowed FY2026 earnings growth guidance to 10%-15% and said results should land toward the upper end of that range, a modest tightening from the prior range. Inland revenue guidance was raised to low double-digit growth from mid-to-high single digits, driven by improving spot and term pricing as 35%-40% of the term book renews in Q4. Q3 free cash flow was $74 million on elevated working capital, and $112 million was returned via buybacks at an average price of $137.

negative_highlights: Service revenue grew just 13% to $1.31B, with management citing delayed service activation and ramped deployments on large new enterprise and expansion deals that pressured the FY2026 service revenue guide
Product gross margin compressed as on-hand inventory benefits from the first half faded and component costs crept up; Q4 gross margin guide of 78%-80% is below the full-year 79.7%-80.3% range
Lead times for certain components lengthened and pricing benefits stabilized rather than improved, with Q4 billings growth guided to 20% versus 29% in Q3
positive_highlights: Billings grew 29% to $2.34B and total revenue grew 20% to $2.08B, exceeding the midpoint of guidance across billings, revenue, operating margin, and EPS
Non-GAAP operating margin of 38.2% was a third-quarter record, up 130 bps and above the high end of guidance; GAAP EPS grew 39% to $0.86
Free cash flow grew 52% to $865M in Q3 and 74% year-to-date to $2.84B; board approved a ~$1.2B increase to the repurchase authorization, leaving $2B available
summary: Fortinet reported Q3 FY2026 billings up 29% to $2.34B and total revenue up 20% to $2.08B, with product revenue up 37% to $765M and non-GAAP EPS up 23% to $0.91; non-GAAP operating margin was a Q3 record 38.2%, up 130 bps, above the high end of guidance. FY2026 billings guidance was raised for the third time this year to $9.568B-$9.718B (28% growth at midpoint) and revenue to $8.125B-$8.215B (20%), with operating margin and EPS also raised, though management flagged a services revenue shortfall tied to delayed service activation on large enterprise deals. Service revenue grew 13% to $1.31B, and management now expects improved service revenue growth in 2027 versus 2026, citing 26% service billings growth and 19% deferred revenue growth as leading indicators.

negative_highlights: Commissions and related revenue of $61 million fell 4% year-over-year on lower volatility and trading volumes
Financial sponsor and middle market activity continues to run below historical levels despite gradual improvement
ECM commentary noted a slowdown in IPO activity entering Q4, with management taking a wait-and-see stance
positive_highlights: Adjusted net revenues of nearly $1.2 billion rose 13% year-over-year, the sixth consecutive quarterly record, with nine-month adjusted revenues up 38%
Adjusted EPS of $4.28 rose 23% year-over-year and nine-month adjusted EPS rose 57%
Adjusted compensation ratio fell 200 bps year-over-year to 63%, and the non-comp ratio of 14.1% declined 340 bps from last quarter
summary: Evercore reported record Q3 2026 adjusted net revenues of nearly $1.2 billion, up 13% year-over-year, the sixth consecutive quarterly revenue record, with adjusted EPS of $4.28 up 23% and adjusted operating income of $270 million up 18%. Adjusted advisory fees of $1 billion rose 14% on market share gains and higher fee events, while the adjusted compensation ratio fell to 63%, down 200 bps year-over-year, and the year-to-date non-comp ratio was 13.7% versus 14.2% last year. Year-to-date adjusted revenues of $3.6 billion were up 38% and nine-month adjusted EPS up 57%; management pointed to record backlogs and healthy replenishment without giving formal guidance or predicting backlog realization timing. The firm returned a record $189 million in Q3 and over $1 billion year-to-date, and announced Nigel Dawn and Naveen Nataraj as co-presidents effective January 1, 2027.

negative_highlights: Full-year adjusted EBITDA outlook trimmed to $930-960 million from prior guidance, with management quantifying the reduction at roughly $30-40 million driven by segment mix, freight inflation and Utilities ramp inefficiencies

Environmental Solutions sales fell 8% to $400 million and segment adjusted EBITDA margin contracted 390 bps to 15.3% on unfavorable utility mix, Waukesha ramp-up inefficiencies and lower volume absorption; full-year ES sales outlook cut to roughly flat

Aerials adjusted EBITDA margin fell 180 bps YoY to 8.7% on unfavorable customer mix and tariffs, and management declined to give timing or counterparty detail on the Aerials separation despite active strategic discussions
positive_highlights: Pro forma orders up 53% YoY to $2.3 billion with growth in all four segments; consolidated book-to-bill ~103% and backlog of $7 billion, with Materials Processing backlog nearly doubling to a two-year high of $676 million
Materials Processing adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 530 bps to 19.3% on higher volume, favorable mix and price/cost discipline; Specialty Vehicles margin up 300 bps to 16%

Free cash flow guidance raised to $360-400 million on working capital efficiency (net working capital 15% of sales vs 18.1% prior year), $209 million FCF generated in Q3, and a new $500 million buyback authorization added to $111 million remaining
summary: Terex reported Q3 sales of $2.2 billion, up 11.6% pro forma, adjusted EBITDA of $286 million (13.0% margin vs 12.8% pro forma prior year) and adjusted diluted EPS of $1.50; pro forma orders rose 53% and backlog reached $7 billion with book-to-bill of ~103%. Despite that, the full-year EBITDA outlook was trimmed to $930-960 million, with management attributing roughly $30-40 million of the cut to segment mix (~50%), higher freight inflation (~25%) and Terex Utilities ramp inefficiencies plus the Capacity/LayMor divestiture (~25%). Full-year sales are now $8.0-8.2 billion (~8% pro forma growth, ES cut to flat from low single digits, Aerials raised to mid-teens) with EPS of $4.80-5.00, while free cash flow guidance was raised to $360-400 million. Environmental Solutions sales fell 8% to $400 million with margin down 390 bps to 15.3%, offsetting strong Materials Processing (margin +530 bps to 19.3%) and Specialty Vehicles (+300 bps to 16%).

negative_highlights: Adjusted gross margin fell 80 bps year-over-year to ~63% on mix shift toward lower-margin products
AHS adjusted EBITDA fell 5% to $88 million with margin contracting 230 bps to 26% on growth investment and lapping prior-year discrete cost benefits
Q4 faces a $15-20 million revenue and 150 bps core growth headwind from four fewer note days, with AHS taking a 300 bps hit
positive_highlights: Full-year adjusted EPS guidance raised to $3.10-$3.14, up ~15% year-over-year at the midpoint
IOS core revenue growth accelerated to 9% with orders growth accelerating again and book-to-bill above one
Adjusted EBITDA up 10% to $340 million with margin expanding 50 bps to 30.6%, and $300 million of Q3 buybacks bringing cumulative repurchases to $2.3 billion
summary: Fortive reported Q3 FY2026 total revenue of $1.1 billion, up 8% reported and 7.2% core, with adjusted EPS of $0.77 up over 13% and adjusted EBITDA of $340 million up 10% (30.6% margin, +50 bps). Core growth accelerated sequentially for a fifth straight quarter, with IOS core up 9% on Fluke and FAL strength while AHS core grew only 3.1% and its adjusted EBITDA margin contracted 230 bps. Management raised full-year adjusted EPS guidance to $3.10-$3.14 (up ~15% at the midpoint) and guides full-year revenue just north of $4.4 billion with core growth just north of 5%. Adjusted gross margin fell 80 bps to ~63% on product mix, and Q4 carries a four-fewer-watching-day headwind of $15-20 million revenue and 150 bps to core growth.

negative_highlights: Adjusted operating margin contracted 110 bps to 16% and adjusted operating profit fell $3 million, with adjusted EPS flat year-over-year
New equipment operating margin fell 150 bps to 3.2% on unfavorable price and mix, with segment profit down $22 million at constant currency
Maintenance growth slowed to 2% from 3% last quarter as churn and mix created a 4% drag, and China new equipment sales declined more than 20%
positive_highlights: Organic sales rose 6%, the strongest growth in 13 quarters, with modernization organic sales up 20% and backlog up 20% at constant currency
New equipment organic sales turned positive for the first time since 2023 at 3%, with Americas up 13% and North America posting its ninth consecutive quarter of order growth
Adjusted free cash flow reached ~$272 million in the quarter and $834 million year-to-date, up 9% versus the prior year period
summary: Otis reported Q3 FY2026 net sales of $3.9 billion with organic sales up 6%, its strongest organic growth in 13 quarters, led by 7% service growth and a 3% increase in new equipment (first positive since 2023). Adjusted operating margin contracted 110 bps to 16%, adjusted operating profit fell $3 million, and adjusted EPS was flat year-over-year. Full-year guidance was unchanged: net sales $15.1-15.3 billion, adjusted operating profit down $30 million to flat, adjusted EPS $4.01-$4.05, and free cash flow around $1.5 billion. New equipment orders grew 1% (5% ex-China), modernization orders rose 10% with backlog up 20%, while China new equipment sales fell more than 20% and maintenance growth slowed to 2% on churn and mix.

negative_highlights: Free cash flow was negative $9.1 billion in Q3, driven by $51.4 billion of CapEx, a $5.2 billion EC fine payment, and TPU inventory build
Net income and EPS decreased due to a negative $8.2 billion in other income/expense from an unrealized SpaceX investment loss
Management guided to near-term Cloud margin headwinds from ramping third-party compute and continued depreciation pressure, with CapEx to rise significantly in 2027
positive_highlights: Google Cloud revenue grew 103% to $30.7 billion with operating margin expanding to 36.2% from 23.7% a year ago
Consolidated revenue rose 25% to $127.6 billion, marking the 13th consecutive quarter of double-digit growth, with operating income up 30% to $40.6 billion
Year-over-year query growth was the highest in five years and Cloud backlog reached $561 billion
summary: Alphabet reported Q3 FY2026 consolidated revenue of $127.6 billion, up 25% YoY in both reported and constant currency, with operating income up 30% to $40.6 billion and operating margin at 31.8%. Google Cloud revenue rose 103% to $30.7 billion with segment operating margin expanding to 36.2% from 23.7%, though the quarter was meaningfully aided by TPU system sales, and net income/EPS fell on an $8.2 billion unrealized loss on the SpaceX investment. Full-year 2026 CapEx guidance of $195-205 billion was unchanged and expected to rise significantly in 2027; the company flagged a slightly larger Q4 FX headwind, lapping pressure on Search growth, and Cloud margin headwinds from ramping third-party compute. Free cash flow turned negative at -$9.1 billion on $51.4 billion of CapEx, a $5.2 billion EC fine payment, and TPU inventory build, with future purchase commitments of $924 billion.

negative_highlights: Passenger vehicle organic sales declined 5% on lower global auto production and planned exits of legacy sensor lines
A one-time $28.5 million Dortmund amendment fee cut reported semiconductor sales, pulling total reported revenue below the prior guidance frame
Q4 EPS guide of $5.05-5.25 is below Q3's $5.79, implying sequential margin/earnings step-down
positive_highlights: Organic growth accelerated sequentially to 22% in Q3 from 14% in Q2 and 9% in Q1
Electronics adjusted EBITDA margin rose 910 bps to 33.1% on 27% organic growth, with protection semiconductors at record revenue and profitability
Basler full-year outlook raised to $135-140 million revenue and $0.25-0.30 EPS accretion versus original $130-135 million and $0.10-0.15 guidance
summary: Littelfuse reported record Q3 FY2026 net sales of $767 million with organic growth accelerating to 22% YoY, adjusted EBITDA of $226 million (28.4% margin, up 690 bps), and record adjusted EPS of $5.79, up 96% YoY. Reported sales were reduced by a one-time $28.5 million Dortmund contract amendment fee that was not in prior guidance, yet Electronics organic sales still rose 27% (passives +30%, semiconductors +24%). Q4 guidance calls for sales of $750-770 million (about 28% growth at midpoint) and adjusted EPS of $5.05-5.25. Bookings were a record with book-to-bill well above 1.0, Basler synergy realization is running ahead of plan, and management reaffirmed its 2030 targets of $4.5 billion revenue and $1.1 billion adjusted EBITDA.

negative_highlights: No product revenue recorded in the quarter since first commercial shipments occurred in early October, pushing first revenue recognition to fiscal Q3
Management declined to provide revenue guidance and said patient numbers and per-patient volume are difficult to track at this stage
Pending permanent J-code not expected until April 2027, with adoption breadth into community settings dependent on that timing
positive_highlights: Over 70% of the initial 200 target accounts engaged and more than 15 institutions have written TUDRIQEV prescriptions in under 20 business days
About 20 accounts placed TUDRIQEV on formulary, with sites including Moffitt and Memorial Sloan Kettering moving quickly; some bypassing standard formulary review
Cash of $307.8 million after $141 million August offering provides greater than 12 months of runway, and net loss narrowed to $57.1 million from $69.8 million sequentially
summary: Replimune reported its first post-approval quarter with no product revenue, as first TUDRIQEV shipments occurred in early October after the September 30 quarter end; net loss narrowed to $57.1 million from $69.8 million in fiscal Q1 on R&D of $34.4 million and SG&A of $21.9 million. Cash stood at $307.8 million including $141 million in August offering net proceeds, funding operations for greater than 12 months. Launch metrics in under 20 business days: over 70% engagement of the initial 200 target accounts, about 20 accounts on formulary, and more than 15 institutions having written prescriptions, with management expecting to roughly double treating accounts by year end. No revenue guidance was provided; list price is $450,000 per course before rebates and discounts.

negative_highlights: Free cash flow was negative $9.1 billion in Q3, driven by $51.4 billion of CapEx, TPU inventory build, and a $5.2 billion EC fine payment
Net income and EPS decreased due to a negative $8.2 billion in other income/expense from an unrealized SpaceX investment loss
Management guided to Q4 revenue pressure from FX headwinds and lapping Search acceleration, plus near-term Cloud margin headwinds from ramping third-party compute
positive_highlights: Google Cloud revenue grew 103% to $30.7 billion with operating margin expanding to 36.2% from 23.7% a year ago
Total revenue rose 25% to $127.6 billion with operating income up 30% to $40.6 billion and operating margin of 31.8%
Cloud backlog reached $561 billion, with just over 55% expected to be recognized as revenue over the next 24 months
summary: Alphabet reported Q3 revenue of $127.6 billion, up 25% YoY in reported and constant currency, with operating income up 30% to $40.6 billion and operating margin of 31.8%. Google Cloud revenue grew 103% to $30.7 billion with operating margin expanding to 36.2% from 23.7%, and Search and other advertising rose 12% to $63.3 billion. Net income and EPS decreased due to an $8.2 billion unrealized loss on the SpaceX investment, and free cash flow was negative $9.1 billion on $51.4 billion of CapEx. Full-year 2026 CapEx guidance of $195-205 billion was unchanged, but management flagged Q4 FX headwinds, lapping Search acceleration, and near-term Cloud margin pressure from third-party capacity.

negative_highlights: Interest expense to rise $0.10-$0.12 per share in 2027 from JV swap resets, with the $496 million tranche moving from 2.7% to 5.3%
Southern California blended rent growth only 90 bps and L.A. County same-property revenue growth decelerated to 50 bps YoY in Q3 from 1.7% in Q1
Q4 controllable operating expenses up about 5% YoY, and property taxes expected to revert to a 3%-4% historical growth rate in 2027 after a favorable 60 bps this year
positive_highlights: Full-year same-property revenue growth guidance raised 10 bps to 2.9% and NOI growth raised 20 bps to 3%, with core FFO midpoint up $0.02
Northern California blended rent growth of 7.3%, with new lease rates improving 20 bps sequentially versus the normal seasonal deceleration
Q4 earn-in improved to roughly 155-160 bps from the 150 bps originally published, versus about 85 bps last year
summary: Essex reported Q3 FY2026 core FFO per share of $4, a $0.01 beat to the midpoint of guidance, on same-property revenue growth of 3% YoY led by Northern California. Full-year same-property revenue growth guidance was raised 10 bps to 2.9%, NOI growth raised 20 bps to 3%, and the core FFO midpoint increased $0.02. Blended rent growth of roughly 2.9% came in near the high end of the range, with Northern California at 7.3%, Seattle positive at 2.1%, and Southern California at 90 bps. Higher interest expense of $0.10-$0.12 per share from JV swap resets is a 2027 headwind, and management characterized the 2027 outlook as uncertain but with better supply and earn-in versus last year.

negative_highlights: Acquisition guidance narrowed and explicitly assumes little additional activity this year due to uncertain capital markets; cap rate guidance ticked up to a 6.3%-6.4% stabilized range
G&A guidance increased to $56 million-$57 million from prior range on new hires, service provider fees, and incentive true-ups
Reno North Valleys (284,000 sq ft Mount Anderson) flagged as the project with the most leasing risk amid slow traditional fulfillment demand
positive_highlights: Same store cash NOI guidance raised to 3.5%-3.75% from 3.0%-3.5%, and Core FFO guidance lifted $0.02 at the midpoint to $2.64-$2.66
Cash leasing spreads of 23.8% (straight-line 35.7%) on 3.6 million sq ft commenced, with retention of 90.3%
Credit loss of 12 bps through Q3 versus a 50 bps initial expectation; 2027 market rent growth guided to 2%-4% from 1.6% in 2026, and ~15% leasing spreads next year
summary: Core FFO per share was $0.66, up 1.5% YoY, with same store cash NOI growth of 3.5% for the quarter and 3.9% YTD. Guidance was raised: same store cash NOI growth lifted to 3.5%-3.75% from 3.0%-3.5%, average occupancy to 96.75%-97.25%, and Core FFO to $2.64-$2.66 (up $0.02 at the midpoint). Leasing spreads were strong at 23.8% cash / 35.7% straight-line on 3.6 million sq ft, with retention of 90.3%, while credit loss tracked at 12 bps versus a 50 bps starting expectation. Management cited national net absorption of ~75 million sq ft in Q3 and expects 2027 market rent growth of 2%-4% (vs 1.6% in 2026) and ~15% leasing spreads next year.

negative_highlights: 2026 revenue guidance trimmed to approximately $9 million reflecting a production ramp about six weeks behind the prior plan
Q3 operating loss of $257 million and Q4 cash use guided to approximately $250 million, up from ~$170 million in Q3

Production ramp constrained by material availability, component quality, and end-of-line testing issues; the 20 trucks/week rate slipped to early December and the 200-truck milestone to end of February
positive_highlights: Charger Logistics MOU to own and operate 500 driverless trucks, a potential multi-year revenue stream in the hundreds of millions of dollars, with deliveries in 2027-2028
FMCSA granted a five-year exemption permitting cab-mounted warning beacons in place of manually placed roadside devices
Balance sheet over $1 billion in cash and note weakness in-term investments; the initial 200-truck fleet is fully contracted and the ~500-truck test fleet is nearly fully allocated
summary: Aurora reported Q3 2026 revenue of just $3 million, an operating loss of $257 million including $54 million stock comp, and operating cash use of roughly $170 million with $36 million of capex. Management cut its 2026 revenue outlook to approximately $9 million, citing a production ramp running about six weeks behind plan due to material availability, component quality, and end-of-line testing issues, and guided Q4 cash use up to about $250 million. The 20-trucks-per-week run rate target slipped to early December and the 200 driverless truck milestone pushed to end of February, though the company reiterated exiting 2027 with more than 1,000 trucks. Positives include a Charger Logistics MOU for 500 trucks (hundreds of millions in potential multi-year revenue), a five-year FMCSA beacon exemption, and a balance sheet with over $1 billion in cash.

negative_highlights: Full-year guidance lowered across all metrics: revenue to $3.86-$3.90B, adjusted EBITDA to $490-$510M, FCF to $190-$210M, and EPS to $4.50-$4.85
Product gross margin fell 530 bps YoY to 22.1% and total gross margin fell 90 bps to 25.3% on mix and memory cost inflation of ~$25M net for the year
Free cash flow was a $46M use in the quarter, and the company now expects FCF conversion of only 40%-45%; the prior 50 bps service margin improvement target will not be met
positive_highlights: Retail revenue grew 16% YoY, the fourth consecutive quarter of double-digit growth, with new wins including a 6,000-lane European self-checkout refresh and a ~1,200-lane North American grocer deal
Service gross margin reached 27.7%, up 230 bps YoY, including an ~$8 million one-time tax benefit (~100 bps); excluding it, margins still improved sequentially
New $250 million share repurchase authorization, the largest to date, backed by $495 million liquidity and 1.5x net debt leverage
summary: Q3 revenue rose 5% YoY to $991 million with adjusted EBITDA up 5% to $128 million, but non-GAAP gross margin fell 90 bps to 25.3% and product gross margin dropped 530 bps to 22.1% on mix and memory costs; EPS of $1.34 was down 4% YoY and free cash flow was a $46 million use. Management cut the full-year outlook to revenue of $3.86-$3.90 billion, adjusted EBITDA of $490-$510 million, FCF of $190-$210 million, and EPS of $4.50-$4.85, citing a $25 million net memory cost headwind, higher retail POS mix, and slower banking product volumes. The company also announced a new $250 million buyback and said 2027 guidance would come in February.

negative_highlights: Software revenue declined just over 4% to EUR 9.9 million, with adjusted EBITDA falling to EUR 1.5 million (15% margin) on cautious spending and extended sales cycles
Manufacturing revenue declined 6% year-over-year to EUR 21.3 million as soft prototyping demand offset series-production growth, and the segment posted a EUR 0.3 million adjusted EBITDA loss

Adjusted EBIT fell to EUR 2.5 million (3.7% margin) as higher gross profit was offset by R&D up 12% to EUR 12.8 million and one-time costs; Q4 requires a sharp sequential step-up to hit the EUR 12-14 million full-year EBIT target
positive_highlights: Medical segment revenue increased nearly 10% year-over-year, with medical devices and medical software each up around 10%, holding a 27.4% adjusted EBITDA margin
Series production revenue grew more than 30% year-over-year, driven by aerospace, semiconductor, and defense demand
Gross margin expanded 90 bps to 57.7%, and year-to-date free cash flow of EUR 22.8 million was more than double the prior-year level
summary: Materialise reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of EUR 67.7 million, up more than 2% year-over-year (almost 5% excluding divestitures), with gross margin expanding 90 bps to 57.7% and adjusted EBIT of EUR 2.5 million (3.7% margin). Medical revenue grew nearly 10% to lead the mix at 54% of sales, manufacturing declined 6% (up 1.5% ex-divestitures) on soft prototyping, and software fell just over 4% on cautious customer spending and extended sales cycles. Net profit was EUR 1.4 million (EUR 0.02 per share) and net cash rose almost EUR 12 million year-to-date to EUR 82.5 million. Full-year 2026 guidance was reconfirmed at EUR 273-283 million revenue and EUR 12-14 million adjusted EBIT, the latter the range raised in August.

negative_highlights: Memory and raw material costs increasing significantly; management expects consolidated gross margin to return to historical range in 2027 as safety stock of low-cost memory runs off
Free cash flow fell $132M sequentially to $293M and full-year FCF/capex estimates worsened on higher inventory and prepayments for strategic components
Auto OEM revenue fell 20% to $132M on declining domain controllers, with Q4 expected to decline similarly
positive_highlights: Revenue up 12% to $1.986B with gross margin expanding 420 bps to 63.3% and operating margin up 500 bps to 30.8%
Full-year revenue guidance raised $100M to ~$8.15B and pro forma EPS raised $0.80 to ~$10.80
Outdoor revenue up 20% on fēnix 9 launch and fitness up 16% with new CIRQA Smart Band demand exceeding expectations
summary: Garmin reported Q3 revenue of $1.986B, up 12% YoY, with gross margin of 63.3% (+420 bps) and operating margin of 30.8% (+500 bps), aided by $33M of tariff refunds and favorable segment mix; pro forma EPS rose 39% to $2.76. Full-year guidance was raised to revenue of ~$8.15B (from $8.05B) and pro forma EPS of ~$10.80 (from $10.00), with gross margin now ~61% and operating margin ~29%. The key change versus prior periods is a memory cost headwind that management said will pressure gross margin in Q4 and return the consolidated gross margin profile to its historical range in 2027. Fitness grew 16%, outdoor 20%, marine 16%, aviation 5%, while Auto OEM fell 20%.

negative_highlights: Banana full-year gross margin guidance cut to 2%-3% from 3%-4% on weather-related volume, production, distribution, and currency pressures
Full-year inflationary pressures now estimated at $55M-$65M, more than half in bananas, driven by fuel, energy, the stronger Costa Rican colón, and fertilizer

Fresh-cut volume declined with lower fresh-produce traffic, higher inland transportation costs, and margins below last year; operating cash flow for the nine months was only $53M amid a roughly $70M-$80M above-normal working capital build
positive_highlights: Foods segment gross margin of 17.5%, the highest among reportable segments, with Del Monte Foods net sales/EBITDA outlook raised to ~$650M/~$45M from $625M/$35M
Gross profit rose 27% to $103 million, outpacing the 7% sales growth, with gross margin expanding 150 bps to 9.4%
Customer fill rates improved from 87% to approximately 98% ahead of the holiday season, restoring retailer confidence
summary: Q3 FY2026 net sales were $1.1 billion, up 7% year-over-year (adjusted net sales up 14%), gross margin 9.4% (up 150 bps), adjusted EBITDA $61 million (up 5%, 5.6% margin), and adjusted diluted EPS $0.50. Foods segment gross margin was 17.5% on improving fill rates (87% to ~98%), and the Foods outlook was raised to ~$650M net sales and ~$45M adjusted EBITDA from $625M/$35M. Full-year adjusted net sales growth (13%-15%) and adjusted EBITDA ($230M-$240M) were reiterated, but banana gross margin guidance was cut to 2%-3% from 3%-4% on weather, cost, and currency pressure, with inflationary headwinds now $55M-$65M. The quarter was carried by Foods and a strong gross profit (+27%), offset by a weaker fresh platform and a reduced banana outlook.

negative_highlights: SANAD received suspension notices on five rigs tied to the Jafurah gas program, taking the working count from 56 to 53 with two more suspensions due, ending the year at 52 rigs
The 19th SANAD newbuild slipped from Q4 2026 to Q1 2027 on conflict-related equipment delivery delays, and suspensions plus the delay cut Q4 free cash flow by $5-$6 million
Q4 capital expenditures step up to $250-$260 million from $141 million, including $140-$150 million for SANAD newbuilds
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA of $246 million came in above the top of implied guidance, with 42% of the 7% sequential revenue growth converting to EBITDA and margin up ~100 bps to 28.2%
International daily gross margin rose more than $1,500 to a record above $19,000, driving 12% segment EBITDA growth and a 160 bps margin expansion to 32%
Full-year adjusted free cash flow guidance raised by $80 million to $100-$110 million and full-year EBITDA guided to approximately $930 million at the top of the prior range
summary: Nabors reported Q3 FY2026 adjusted EBITDA of $246 million, up $24 million or 11% sequentially on 7% revenue growth, with margin expanding ~100 bps to 28.2% and every segment meeting or exceeding guidance. International EBITDA rose 12% on record daily gross margin above $19,000, Lower 48 daily margin exceeded $14,000, and adjusted free cash flow of $75 million beat the outlook by $115 million. Full-year EBITDA is now guided to approximately $930 million at the top of the prior range despite five SANAD rig suspensions in Saudi Arabia, and full-year adjusted free cash flow guidance was raised by $80 million to $100-$110 million. The offsetting negative is the Saudi disruption, which cuts the SANAD count to 52 by year-end and delays the 19th newbuild into Q1 2027, though the fifth tranche of newbuilds was signed during the call.

negative_highlights: Second-half margins guided down to high-20s adjusted gross margin and high-teens adjusted EBITDA margin versus the 23% adjusted EBITDA margin reported in Q2
Significant cost inflation in diesel (up roughly 80% year-to-date), steel, freight and logistics expected to stay elevated through FY2027, with no clear timeline for reversion

Zimmermann acquisition expectations reduced to approximately $100 million revenue and $10 million adjusted EBITDA for the balance of the fiscal year, with deal consideration lowered to EUR 230 million all-cash; Q3 revenue guided down sequentially
positive_highlights: Revenue up 23% year-over-year to over $1.1 billion with adjusted EBITDA of approximately $250 million and record quarterly bookings driving backlog above $6 billion
FY2027 guidance raised: revenue to $4.2-4.45 billion, adjusted EBITDA to $890-940 million, adjusted EPS to $4.61-4.87, and free cash flow lifted from $450 million to over $500 million

Non-tracker products reached approximately 22% of revenue, with storage contributing roughly $100 million of revenue and over $20 million of adjusted EBITDA including a hyperscaler AI data center project; eBOS bookings exceeded $100 million
summary: Nextpower reported record Q2 FY2027 revenue over $1.1 billion, up 23% year-over-year, with adjusted EBITDA of approximately $250 million (up 12% YoY) at a 23% adjusted EBITDA margin. Record bookings drove backlog above $6 billion, and the company raised its FY2027 outlook to $4.2-4.45 billion revenue, $890-940 million adjusted EBITDA, $4.61-4.87 adjusted diluted EPS, and free cash flow above $500 million (up from $450 million). However, management guided second-half margins down, expecting high-20s gross margin and high-teens EBITDA margin versus 23% in Q2, citing inflation in diesel, steel, and freight, plus ramp costs on new products, and noted Q3 revenue will decline sequentially before a Q4-weighted finish.

negative_highlights: Recurring net income of BRL 2.9 billion with ROE of 11.9%, explicitly below the bank's target profitability
Client NII spread fell ~33 bps in the quarter on the consumer finance FIDC sale, lower CDI, and banking agent effects, with de-risking expected to keep pressuring spreads
Wholesale one-offs of ~BRL 500 million and rising 90-day NPLs for individuals (agribusiness adding ~60 bps), with new deterioration in middle-income unsecured cards
positive_highlights: Efficiency ratio improved to 38.8% with expense growth well below inflation despite the 4.6% collective bargaining agreement
Transactional deposits grew 10% and the client base reached 76.9 million, up 6% year-over-year
Mortgage loans grew 10.3% and SME loans 8.5% year-over-year, and hybrid/electric vehicles rose from 5% to 20% of financed vehicles
summary: Santander Brasil reported recurring net income of BRL 2.9 billion and ROE of 11.9%, which management explicitly called below target profitability. Client NII declined ~33 bps in the quarter and market NII also softened, with ~BRL 500 million of wholesale one-offs pressuring cost of risk. Expenses grew below inflation and the efficiency ratio improved to 38.8%, and management guided to better NII and lower agribusiness losses in 2027 versus 2026, but gave no quantitative targets and flagged continued deterioration in agribusiness, low-income, and now middle-income unsecured cards, plus concern that higher-for-longer rates pressure SMEs.

negative_highlights: Q4 gross margin is guided down to approximately 44% from 45.7% in Q3, citing longer lead times and higher input costs for certain semiconductors and specialty components.
One compute customer accounted for more than 10% of total sales in Q3, indicating customer concentration risk.
Recurring revenue from Eclipse upgrades is still early-stage; management said 'we haven't seen a lot of evidence yet because we're new in the space.'
positive_highlights: Revenue of $173 million grew 37% YoY and exceeded the midpoint of guidance; non-GAAP EPS was $0.43 with a 45.7% gross margin above guidance.
Total bookings grew 126% YoY, with systems bookings up 318%, and book-to-bill was solidly above one; HPC opportunity pipeline expanded ~18% to ~$1 billion.
Preliminary 2027 outlook calls for 30%-40% revenue growth with 46%-48% gross margin and ~50% incremental revenue falling to operating income.
summary: Cohu reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $173 million, up 37% YoY and above the midpoint of guidance, with non-GAAP EPS of $0.43, gross margin of 45.7% (above guidance), and adjusted EBITDA margin of 16.6%. Total bookings grew 126% YoY (systems up 318%, recurring up 36%), and the company raised its FY2026 revenue growth outlook to approximately 38% while guiding Q4 revenue to ~$178 million (~46% YoY growth). Management introduced a preliminary 2027 view of 30%-40% revenue growth with gross margin of 46%-48%, but noted Q4 gross margin is projected to decline to ~44% due to higher input costs and supply-chain tightness for specialty components.

negative_highlights: Fareva Amboise warning letter remains open with site-wide quality-system implications; FDA reinspection has not been scheduled
Nine-month operating expenses rose $59.4 million to $164.4 million, with sales and marketing up from $1.9 million to $15.7 million
Company confirmed a priority review voucher is not expected to apply to VIASKIN Peanut under the strict rule definition
positive_highlights: Cash of $165.7 million including $50 million gross ATM proceeds to RA Capital, with runway guided into Q3 2027
BLA for ages four to seven submitted and priority review requested on the basis of breakthrough designation
FDA agreed to a sequential review approach so the toddler BLA can benefit from learnings and CMC content overlap with the first review
summary: DBV reported Q3 2026 cash and cash equivalents of $165.7 million, including $50 million in gross proceeds from ADS sales to RA Capital under an ATM program, with runway estimated into Q3 2027 on a stage-gated, milestone-based spending plan. Nine-month operating expenses rose to $164.4 million from $107 million a year ago, with sales and marketing up from $1.9 million to $15.7 million. The quarter's focus was the BLA submission for ages four to seven, with a priority review request made and a toddler (one to three) BLA now expected in 2027 under a sequential-review approach agreed with FDA. Fareva Amboise's April 2026 warning letter remains unresolved; the FDA reinspection has not been scheduled, and DBV's stated February 1 PAI-readiness date assumes timely remediation.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBIT margin expansion guidance held at 70-90 bps despite the revenue beat and float upside
FX shifted to close to half a point of headwind in FY2027 versus a point of tailwind in FY2026
Global offerings had a softer start to the year and full-year ES retention is still forecast down 10-30 bps
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 6% with adjusted EBIT margin up 130 bps and adjusted EPS up 13%, all above expectations
FY2027 client funds interest revenue outlook raised $50 million to $1.59-1.61 billion and adjusted EPS growth guide lifted to 10%-12%
Pays per control rose 2% in Q1 and full-year outlook improved to around 1% from 0%-1%; Q1 ES bookings were a record for a first quarter
summary: ADP reported Q1 FY2027 revenue growth of 6%, adjusted EBIT margin expansion of 130 bps, and adjusted EPS growth of 13%, all ahead of expectations. Full-year guidance was raised: consolidated revenue to about 6% (from prior), client funds interest revenue lifted $50 million to $1.59-1.61 billion, pays per control now around 1% from 0%-1%, and adjusted EPS growth to 10%-12%. The adjusted EBIT margin expansion forecast was held at 70-90 bps despite the revenue lift, with management citing continued investment in AI, cloud infrastructure, and upmarket/global offerings.

negative_highlights: Next-generation HPC opportunity now expected mid-to-late 2027, a shift further out from prior late-2024/early-2027 commentary
Inventory rose roughly 16% sequentially, faster than revenue growth, with inventory turns slipping
Supply chain constraints persist in the ASIC side, an issue management says has been present for three quarters
positive_highlights: Revenue of $811 million and EPS of $0.84 both exceeded the high end of prior guidance, with EPS growth of 35% nearly double revenue growth
Full-year 2026 revenue outlook raised to exceed $3 billion (16% annual growth) with Q4 guided to $815-855 million, 19% YoY growth at midpoint
Operating margin expanded 70 bps YoY to 5.5% and cash conversion cycle improved 23 days YoY to 54 days, with $14 million free cash flow
summary: Benchmark reported record Q3 FY2026 revenue of $811 million, up 19% year-over-year, with non-GAAP EPS of $0.84 up 35%; both exceeded the high end of prior guidance. Non-GAAP gross margin was 10.5% (up 40 bps YoY) and operating margin 5.5% (up 70 bps YoY). Management raised its Q4 outlook to $815-855 million (19% YoY growth at midpoint) and now expects full-year 2026 revenue above $3 billion with 16% annual growth. One offset: next-gen HPC contribution shifted from late 2024/early 2027 expectations to mid-to-late 2027, though management frames it as upside layered on current business.

negative_highlights: Tangible book value per share fell 6% to $15.65 and the TCE ratio dropped 43 bps to 7.81% due to AOCI from higher rates
Core non-interest expense rose $7.8 million on incentive costs, healthcare claims, and credit/collection costs
positive_highlights: Adjusted EPS of $0.84 rose 11% YoY to a company record, with adjusted ROA of 1.56% and adjusted ROTCE of 20.2%
NIM expanded 9 bps to 4.07% as asset yields rose 13 bps, partially offset by a 4 bp increase in cost of funds
Adjusted fee income hit a record $77.6 million (28% of revenue) with double-digit growth in wealth, bank card, and client derivative fees
summary: First Financial reported Q3 2026 adjusted net income of $87.8 million and adjusted EPS of $0.84, up 11% YoY and the highest in company history, on record revenue of $273.9 million. NIM rose 9 bps to 4.07%, or 4.08%-4.12% guided for Q4, and record adjusted fee income of $77.6 million (28% of revenue) was driven by FX, wealth, client derivatives, and bank card. Q4 guidance calls for low-to-mid-single-digit loan growth, fee income of $75M-$78M, and expenses of $150M-$153M as incentive and healthcare costs moderate. Classified assets jumped to 1.26% of assets on a single ICRE downgrade, and TCE fell 43 bps to 7.81% on AOCI from higher rates, dragging tangible book value down 6% to $15.65.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EPS was flat YoY at $1.85 despite 5% revenue growth, and the adjusted non-comp ratio rose to 13.3% from 12.5%
Financial Restructuring revenue fell 12% to $118 million and closed transactions dropped 27% to 27
Closed Corporate Finance transactions fell to 142 from 171, and management said software revenue this year will not match last year's level
positive_highlights: Corporate Finance revenue grew 10% YoY to $481 million, with average transaction fees up on a higher mix of large-fee closings
New deal activity and backlog support an unseasonably strong second half, with restructuring backlog at a record level heading into calendar 2027
FVA revenue rose 7% to $93 million on portfolio valuation growth, a non-cyclical business management called out as growing strongly
summary: Houlihan Lokey reported Q2 FY2027 revenue of $692 million, up 5% YoY, with adjusted EPS of $1.85 flat versus the prior year. Corporate Finance revenue rose 10% to $481 million on higher average fees despite closed transactions falling to 142 from 171, while Financial Restructuring fell 12% to $118 million and FVA rose 7% to $93 million. Management guided to an unseasonably strong second half and elevated restructuring revenue into fiscal 2028, citing a record backlog and software-driven restructuring, but flagged continued headwinds from rates, geopolitics, and software, with no expectation of matching last year's software revenue. Adjusted comp ratio held at 61.5% while the non-comp ratio rose to 13.3% from 12.5%, and the company repurchased about 397,000 shares for roughly $50 million.

negative_highlights: Effective tax rate jumped to 39.0% due to Cayman holding company share-based expense that generates no tax benefit
Capitalized software development ran at 37.8% of nine-month revenue ($14.1 million), with operating cash flow covering only ~83% of platform and equipment investment
positive_highlights: Revenue growth accelerated to 90.3% YoY from 80.8% in Q2, with GMV up 144.8% to $177.5 million
Gross margin expanded 590 bps to 49.0% as cost of revenue fell to 51.0% of revenue from 56.9%
Nine-month revenue of $37.3 million (+76.4%) and net profit of $5.7 million already exceed all of full-year 2025
summary: Ticketplus reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $14.4 million, up 90.3% year-over-year and accelerating from 80.8% growth in Q2, with GMV of $177.5 million up 144.8%. Gross margin expanded 590 bps to 49.0%, Adjusted EBITDA rose 108.2% to $6.1 million (42.6% margin), and net profit was $1.6 million or $0.14 per share after a $1.2 million one-time IPO-related share-based charge. Full-year 2026 guidance calls for revenue of $51-53 million (+73.1% to 79.9%), GMV of $625-650 million (+130%+), and 80,000-85,000 events, with the midpoint implying Q4 revenue above Q3 in USD despite less favorable assumed exchange rates.

negative_highlights: Total revenue grew only 3% versus 6% organic growth, reflecting a drag from lower fiduciary investment income and other items
Fiduciary investment income fell 8% to $69 million on lower interest rates, a headwind to margin
Management flagged a challenging/softer pricing environment in P&C and reinsurance, and Q4 interest expense is expected to jump to ~$410 million on USI-related debt
positive_highlights: Organic revenue growth of 6% was the highest of the year, with all four solution lines at mid-single digits or greater and commercial risk accelerating to 7%
Adjusted operating margin expanded 70 bps to 27% and adjusted EPS grew 10% to $3.36 despite an 8% decline in fiduciary investment income
New business contributed 11 points to organic growth, extending a 10-quarter streak of 9-11 point contribution, with retention in the mid-90s
summary: Aon reported Q3 FY2026 organic revenue growth of 6% (highest of the year) with total revenue up 3% to $4.1 billion, adjusted operating income up 5% to $1.1 billion, adjusted operating margin expanding 70 bps to 27%, and adjusted EPS up 10% to $3.36; free cash flow was $1.1 billion. All four solution lines grew mid-single digits or better, led by commercial risk and reinsurance at 7% each, supported by 11 points of new business and mid-90s retention. Management reaffirmed prior standalone full-year 2026 guidance across organic revenue, margin, EPS, and free cash flow, and confirmed the USI acquisition remains on track to close in Q4 with $395 million of identified synergies. The quarter showed broad-based growth and margin expansion offsetting a softer P&C/reinsurance pricing environment and an 8% decline in fiduciary investment income.

negative_highlights: Non-performing assets rose to $193 million, or 60 bps of loans, from $130.6 million, or 52 bps, at June 30, and management said the run rate likely settles at $125-150 million rather than returning near zero
Net charge-offs increased to $4.4 million from $2.2 million in Q2

Warehouse mortgage lending fell to $1.11 billion from a $1.229 billion quarterly average, with management guiding Q4 down to $850-900 million on rates and seasonality, and deposit costs are guided to rise 6-8 bps in Q4 after a late-Q3 money market increase
positive_highlights: Tax-equivalent NIM expanded 49 bps YoY and 26 bps QoQ to 3.73%, with core NIM ex-purchase accounting up to 3.59% from 3.19% a year earlier
Board raised the quarterly dividend 6.7% to $0.64 per share and cited $850-880 million of projected total earnings and roughly $310 million of annual dividend cost as capacity for buybacks
Average monthly new loan production rose to $635 million from $454 million in Q2, and management guided to low-to-mid-teens EPS growth in 2027 plus another double-digit year in 2028
summary: Q3 FY2026 was the first full quarter including Stellar Bank: net interest income rose to $443 million from $273.4 million a year earlier, tax-equivalent NIM expanded 49 bps YoY and 26 bps QoQ to 3.73%, and adjusted EPS was $1.67 on $200 million of net income excluding merger costs, with the adjusted efficiency ratio at 48%. The board raised the Q4 dividend 6.7% to $0.64 per share. Management guided Q4 expenses to $235-238 million and reiterated a 370-375 bps Q4 margin exit rate with 380-385 bps for 2027 average, while projecting flat to slightly up 2027 loan balances offset by $65-70 million of remaining pre-tax cost savings and low-to-mid-teens 2027 EPS growth. The main blemish was credit: non-performing assets rose to $193 million, or 60 bps of loans, from $130.6 million, or 52 bps, at June 30, largely from acquired assets.

negative_highlights: Surgical equipment revenue fell 11%, reflecting a shift toward strategic system placements rather than revenue recognition
Xiidra growth slowed to 2% ($89M), lagging the broader dry eye pharma portfolio's 22% growth
Vision Care international growth of 4% trailed the U.S. at 9%, with management citing pressure on the legacy contact lens portfolio
positive_highlights: Full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance raised by $65M to $1.09B–$1.14B, implying ~20.3% margin, 130 bps above the Investor Day target
Adjusted EBITDA rose 34% to $325M and adjusted gross margin expanded 300 bps to 64.7%, driven by favorable mix and productivity initiatives
Free cash flow of $178M was the strongest quarter since the 2022 IPO, reducing net leverage to 4.1x from 5.7x a year ago
summary: Bausch + Lomb reported Q3 2026 revenue of $1.375B, up 8% constant currency, with adjusted EBITDA of $325M (up 34%) and adjusted EPS of $0.34 vs $0.18 a year ago. All three segments grew: Vision Care +6%, Surgical +9%, and Pharma +11%. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance for the third time this year, lifting revenue to $5.45B–$5.55B and adjusted EBITDA to $1.09B–$1.14B, with implied margin of ~20.3%, 130 bps above the Investor Day target. Adjusted gross margin expanded 300 bps to 64.7% (63.6% excluding a $14M tariff refund), and free cash flow of $178M was the strongest quarter since the 2022 IPO, bringing net leverage down to 4.1x from 5.7x.

negative_highlights: Revenue grew only 4.1% to $293M, with growth moderated by a 2026 renewal cohort ~40% larger than last year
Larger renewal cohort pressures gross dollar retention and contractual recurring revenue growth into 1H 2027, with GDR only returning to 91%-92% by end-2027
Global workforce transition costs raised to $8M-$10M from a prior $6M-$8M, with cash impact primarily in Q4
positive_highlights: Non-GAAP EPS rose 24% YoY to $1.36, with EPS and free cash flow guided at or above the high end of the range
