Free cash flow of $126M and debt leverage reduced from 2.7x at end of Q1 to just under 2.3x in Q3
Repurchased just over 7% of outstanding shares in the first nine months and cut shares ~16% since Q4 2023; final two co-lo data centers closing by year-end
summary: Blackbaud reported Q3 revenue of $293M, up 4.1% YoY, non-GAAP EPS of $1.36 (up 24%), adjusted EBITDA of $111M at a 38% margin, and free cash flow of $126M. Full-year guidance was reaffirmed with revenue and adjusted EBITDA expected in the upper half of the range, and EPS and free cash flow at or above the high end; no AI product revenue is included in the 2026 guide. Management flagged a 40% larger 2026 contractual renewal cohort that is moderating recurring revenue growth through 1H 2027, with gross dollar retention expected to return to 91%-92% by end-2027 as the 2027 cohort is nearly 25% smaller. The quarter reflects solid EPS/cash flow execution and heavier AI product announcements (Platform for Good, Lantern, Agents for Good) rather than a revenue beat.

negative_highlights: Total gross margin fell to 54.9% from 60.9% sequentially, and Q4 revenue is guided down sequentially to $104-107M
Systems revenue declined 15% YoY to $14.8M and is guided down sequentially in Q4 as enterprise project timing slips, forgoing the typical seasonal step-up

Back-end post-processing capacity in shared/bought process steps is tight, constraining shipments; management said it met but could not get ahead of market need, with elevated capex and cost pass-throughs flagged for 2027
positive_highlights: Endpoint IC product revenue grew 23% sequentially excluding the $17M Q2 licensing revenue, and total revenue set a record at $112.1M without licensing benefit
Product gross margin increased 130 bps sequentially driven by M800 mix, with Q4 gross margin guided up ~100 bps on specialty ICs and M800 terminal mix
Backlog is building with book-to-bill above one and some bookings already extending into Q1 2027, and modest specialty IC revenue returns in Q4 after a multi-year drought
summary: Revenue hit a record $112.1M, up 3% sequentially and 17% YoY, with record endpoint IC revenue of $97.3M (+24% YoY) and systems revenue of $14.8M (+23% QoQ but -15% YoY). Non-GAAP net income was $22.1M or $0.69 EPS, and adjusted EBITDA margin was 21.9%. Q4 guidance is $104-107M (14% YoY growth at midpoint) and EPS of $0.55-0.60, a favorable end of typical seasonality due to returning specialty IC revenue, but systems revenue will decline sequentially on project timing. Gross margin fell to 54.9% from 60.9% sequentially mostly on prior licensing revenue, though product gross margin rose 130 bps QoQ on M800 mix, and management expects Q4 gross margin up ~100 bps sequentially.

negative_highlights: Destination resorts revenue fell $1.4 million partly on hotel closures, and the Asia land-based exit completes with 12 resorts at year-end
Administrative expenses rose to $7.0 million from $4.6 million on $2.1 million of third-party fees from the U.K./Italy reorganization
Dynamic AI pricing not expected before Q4 2027, and management declined to quantify its impact
positive_highlights: Revenue of $276.5 million (+7%) and adjusted EBITDA of $39.2 million (+12%) both exceeded the high end of July guidance
Full-year 2026 revenue and adjusted EBITDA guidance midpoints raised by $7.5 million and $4 million respectively
Pre-booked revenue rose 20% and forward-booking position is up 18% YoY; new $100 million buyback and 25% dividend increase to $0.0625
summary: Q3 FY2026 total revenue rose 7% to $276.5 million and adjusted EBITDA rose 12% to $39.2 million, both exceeding the high end of July guidance, marking the 22nd straight quarter of record YoY revenue and adjusted EBITDA growth. Adjusted EPS was $0.34 versus $0.30, driven by a 3.3% increase in average guest spend, fleet expansion and higher volumes. Full-year 2026 guidance was raised at the midpoint to $1.033-$1.038 billion revenue and $138-$140 million adjusted EBITDA (midpoints up $7.5 million and $4 million), with Q4 guided to $248-$253 million revenue and $32-$34 million EBITDA. The board approved a new $100 million buyback and a 25% dividend increase to $0.0625 per share.

negative_highlights: Regency Court acquired at an approximately 4% going-in cash yield (GAAP yield expected in the 5s), dependent on below-market anchor rollover in six years to reach an 8%-9% unlevered IRR
Q4 same-property NOI acceleration relies partly on a prior-year $3.5 million snow removal expense that is not expected to recur
Net debt to EBITDA of 5.7x with $138 million drawn on the credit facility after the Regency Court draw
positive_highlights: Raised 2026 FFO as adjusted guidance by $0.01 at the midpoint to $1.52-$1.54, implying 7% growth over 2025
Raised full-year same-property NOI growth guidance to a 4.1% midpoint from 3.5%
Same-space new lease cash spreads of 28% YTD and a $21 million signed-but-not-opened pipeline equal to 7% of annualized NOI
summary: Urban Edge reported Q3 FY2026 FFO as adjusted of $0.38/share, up 6% YoY, with same-property NOI including redevelopment up 4.6% for the quarter and 3.6% YTD. Management raised 2026 FFO as adjusted guidance by $0.01 at the midpoint to $1.52-$1.54 (implying ~7% growth) and lifted full-year same-property NOI growth guidance to a 4.1% midpoint from 3.5%. Leasing remained strong with same-space new lease cash spreads of 28% YTD, same-property leased occupancy of 96.6% (up 20 bps QoQ), and a $21 million signed-but-not-opened pipeline representing 7% of annualized NOI. The company closed the $90.3 million Regency Court acquisition in Boca Raton at an approximately 4% going-in cash yield, entering Florida, funded partly by the $60.5 million sale of Briarcliff Commons.

negative_highlights: Wind remains challenged: U.S. onshore new equipment market soft and onshore backlog off a small base, with offshore execution extending through 2027
2026 gas equipment order pricing per kW expected to be ~50% above 2025 but Q4 pricing to step down sequentially due to fewer aeroderivatives
Trench close not expected until late 2027, with $4.5 billion of new debt and cost synergies only $50-100 million by 2030
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA grew 123% YoY to $1.9 billion with margin up 690 bps
Orders rose 96% to $29.3 billion at >2x book-to-bill; backlog expanded to $197 billion from $176 billion
Management raised 2026 revenue, margin, and free cash flow guidance; Q3 FCF was $5.4 billion
summary: GE Vernova reported Q3 2026 revenue up 18% with adjusted EBITDA up 123% to $1.9 billion and margin expanding 690 bps, alongside orders of $29.3 billion (up 96% YoY) and backlog growing to $197 billion. Management raised 2026 revenue, margin, and free cash flow guidance, citing strong Q3 performance and confidence in Q4. The company announced a $9 billion acquisition of Trench Group (~36% 2028 EBITDA margin, mid-teens revenue growth) to be funded with equal parts debt and cash, and doubled the buyback authorization from $10 billion to $20 billion. Power reached 21% EBITDA margins, Electrification 19%, and Wind turned profitable.

Total revenue rose 7% to $275 million and adjusted EBITDA rose 10% to $106 million, with TRS rental revenue up 26% and Enviroplex sales nearly doubling to $25.7 million. Offsetting that, Mobile Modular total revenue fell 1% to $180 million on a $5.3 million drop in new equipment sales and rental margin slid to 56% from 58%, and Portable Storage revenue fell 3% with EBITDA down 20%. Guidance was narrowed with no change to the EBITDA midpoint ($365-373 million), but the revenue outlook was cut on lower modular sales and rental CapEx was raised to $270-290 million from a $190 million February midpoint. TRS ended the quarter at 71.9% utilization, the highest in 20 years, while small local commercial construction and education demand remained weak.

negative_highlights: 2027 FFO faces ~$0.08/share dilution from completed asset sales plus ~$0.06 more if Times Square Tower closes, moderating growth
Negative leasing spreads in Boston, where Quarry renewals reset rents about 28% lower, and in San Francisco where expiring rents (~$120) exceeded new rents (~$100)
Higher net interest expense ($0.02/share drag) and expiration of the 3.6% GM Building mortgage in June 2027 imply refinancing at materially higher rates
positive_highlights: FFO of $1.89/share beat prior guidance midpoint by $0.08 and consensus; FY2026 FFO guidance raised $0.05 at the midpoint to $7.06-$7.08
In-service occupancy rose 100 bps in the quarter to 89.4%, 270 bps of gain year to date, above the 89% year-end target
Leasing spreads of +6.5% gross and +9.3% net, with Midtown office transactions up 23% net and Manhattan taking rents at 680 Folsom up over 25% in 12 months
summary: BXP reported Q3 FY2026 FFO of $1.89 per share, beating the prior guidance midpoint by $0.08 and consensus, and raised full-year 2026 FFO guidance by $0.05 at the midpoint to $7.06-$7.08 (3.2% growth). Same-property NOI growth guidance rose 35 bps to 2.35%-2.75%; in-service occupancy climbed 100 bps sequentially to 89.4%, ahead of the 89% year-end target, and management now expects to end 2026 near 90%. Leasing spreads were +6.5% gross/+9.3% net, with dispositions ($520M this year, $1.37B since the investor conference) running well ahead of the $1.9B 2028 target, though 2027 FFO faces roughly $0.08 of sale dilution plus $0.06 more if Times Square Tower closes.

negative_highlights: Consolidated same-store sales moderated to +1.4% in Q2 and turned only slightly positive in the first four weeks of Q3
Ladies' western boot comps were a modest drag and e-commerce growth slowed to 5.2% with a ~650 bps headwind from that category
FY guide implies comps of +2%, below the historical low-to-mid-single-digit algorithm
positive_highlights: EPS of $1.73 exceeded the high end of guidance by $0.08, up 26% YoY
Gross margin expanded 80 bps to 38.5% driven by 190 bps of merchandise margin expansion
Raised FY27 new store opening plan to 75-80 from 70 and lifted merchandise margin outlook to ~70 bps expansion excluding tariff refunds
summary: Q2 net sales rose 15% to $582 million with consolidated same-store sales up 1.4% and merchandise margin expanding 190 bps; gross margin improved 80 bps and EPS rose 26% to $1.73, $0.08 above the high end of guidance. Full-year guidance calls for 15% revenue growth to $2.6 billion, 2% comps, and 22% EPS growth to $9, while Q3 guidance implies ~1% comps and $3.19 EPS. Management noted comp moderation in October, driven by softer ladies' western boots and macro/weather pressure in men's, and raised the fiscal 2027 new store plan to 75-80 from 70 and lifted the merchandise margin outlook to ~70 bps expansion excluding tariff refunds. The quarter beat on EPS but forward comp trends decelerated, leaving the overall read mixed.

negative_highlights: Non-interest income fell $13.1 million sequentially to $232.4 million, driven by a $16.1 million drop in securities gains and a $7 million decline in COLI income
Average DDA balances declined 6.1% from the linked quarter on seasonal institutional disbursements, and average deposits grew only 1.1%
Management flagged that record $3.1 billion loan production is likely to moderate in Q4 toward the Q1/Q2 run rate, and said it does not yet know the new baseline
positive_highlights: Record top-line loan production of $3.1 billion drove 11.1% linked-quarter annualized average loan growth, with C&I up nearly 22% annualized
Net charge-offs of just 13 bps and NPL ratio improved to 28 bps from 31 bps, versus an industry median of 53 bps
Institutional fee income rose 3.2% linked-quarter and nearly 18% year to date, with fund services up 8.8% sequentially and year-to-date operating leverage of 11.5%
summary: UMB reported Q3 2026 net income of $272.3 million and EPS of $3.56, with an operating return on tangible common equity of 19.5%. Record loan production of $3.1 billion drove 11.1% annualized average loan growth, net charge-offs were 13 bps, and the NPL ratio improved to 28 bps from 31 bps. Core NIM was 3.10% (up 1 bp sequentially) versus 3.32% reported including 22 bps of purchase accounting accretion; management guided Q4 core margin flat, Q4 expenses of $400-405 million, and Q4 loan production to moderate toward the Q1/Q2 run rate. Separately, UMB announced the acquisition of El Dorado Savings Bank ($2.1 billion of deposits at an 88 bp cost of deposits, $500 million of loans), expected to close in Q1 2027 and be modestly accretive in 2027.

negative_highlights: Q4 revenue guidance of $277-280M implies only 6.9% YoY growth at the midpoint, a deceleration from the 9.5% delivered in Q3
Non-GAAP gross margin was roughly flat at 81.5% versus 81.6% in Q3 2025
Net dollar expansion is guided to hold steady at 107% in Q4, with no further acceleration expected
positive_highlights: Revenue of $276.4M grew 9.5% YoY and topped the high end of guidance for every guided metric
Net dollar expansion accelerated to 107% from 106%, the second consecutive quarter of improvement and first two-quarter acceleration in over four years
Tenable One hit a record 59% of new business (up from 50% in Q2 and 39% a year ago) with 5,000+ platform customers; six-figure account ACV rose 18% YoY
summary: Tenable reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $276.4M, up 9.5% YoY, above the high end of guidance for every metric, with non-GAAP operating margin of 27.1% (up 380 bps) and non-GAAP EPS of $0.63 (including a $0.03 one-time tax benefit) versus $0.42 a year ago. Net dollar expansion accelerated to 107% from 106% (second straight quarter of improvement), Tenable One reached a record 59% of new business (from 50% in Q2 and 39% a year ago), CCB grew 9%, CRPO grew 12%, and unlevered FCF rose 18.7% to $69.4M. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance for revenue to $1.084-1.087B (8.6% YoY at midpoint), non-GAAP operating income to $270-273M (25.0% margin), and non-GAAP EPS to $2.16-2.19. The main change versus the prior quarter is broad-based acceleration in leading indicators — expansion rate, platform mix, and deal sizes — alongside a debt refinancing and $170.5M+ in buybacks.

negative_highlights: Shopping center same-property NOI growth decelerated to 3.8% in Q3 from 6.2% YTD as late-2025 anchor openings entered the comparable base
Signed-not-open pipeline of $5.6M (4.6% of in-place rent) fell modestly QoQ, with only ~$3.2M commencing in 2027
Leverage expected to rise to ~6.5x debt to EBITDA after recent acquisitions, up from 5.9x at quarter end
positive_highlights: Full-year 2026 Core FFO guidance raised to $2.11-$2.14 from $2.09-$2.13, midpoint ~14% growth over 2025
Core FFO per diluted share up 10.4% YoY to $0.53 in Q3 and 13.8% YTD to $1.57
New $1B unsecured facility extended weighted average debt maturity to 4.3 years from 1.6 and added $250M of liquidity
summary: Q3 2026 Core FFO was $0.53/diluted share, up 10.4% YoY, with 9-month Core FFO of $1.57, up 13.8%. Management raised full-year 2026 Core FFO guidance to $2.11-$2.14 from $2.09-$2.13 (midpoint ~14% growth) and lifted the low end of AFFO guidance to $2.22-$2.25, while raising investment volume to ~$472M from a prior $300-400M. Shopping center same-property NOI grew 3.8% for the quarter (6.2% YTD), moderating as late-2025 anchor openings rolled into the comparable base. The company closed a $1B unsecured credit facility, extended weighted average debt maturity to 4.3 years from 1.6, and ended at 5.9x net debt to pro forma adjusted EBITDA with ~$255M liquidity.

negative_highlights: Total loans were down approximately $54 million YoY at $5.31 billion, with only ~$5 million of QoQ growth as runoff offsets production
Other operating income fell to $12.4 million from $14.6 million in the prior quarter on a $2.4 million decline in BOLI income tied to equity market volatility

Management flagged deposit costs as likely at a trough, with Q4 CD maturities of ~$410 million rolling off at 2.7% into new CDs near 3.0%, and expects repurchases at a similar Q3 pace rather than higher
positive_highlights: Diluted EPS rose 21% YoY to $0.88 (adjusted for prior-year one-time expenses), with ROA at 1.22% and ROE at 15.28%
NIM expanded 5 bps QoQ and 13 bps YoY to 3.62% as average loan yield rose 5 bps to 5.01% while total deposit cost held at 90 bps
Full-year expense growth guidance trimmed to 2%-2.5% from the prior range, and efficiency ratio improved to 58.3% from 59.6%; Q4 dividend raised 3.3% to $0.31 per share
summary: Q3 FY2026 net income was $22.8M or $0.88 per diluted share, up from $20.8M or $0.80 in the prior quarter, with diluted EPS up 21% YoY on an adjusted basis. NIM expanded 5 bps QoQ and 13 bps YoY to 3.62%, NII rose 2.6% QoQ to $64.5M, and the efficiency ratio improved to 58.3% from 59.6%. Guidance was constructive but incremental: Q4 NIM guided to the mid-3.60% range, full-year expense growth trimmed to 2%-2.5% from the prior range, and the Q4 dividend raised 3.3% to $0.31. Loan balances were roughly flat ($5.31B, down $54M YoY) with continued mix shift toward higher-yielding commercial and mainland production.

negative_highlights: U.S. daily operating margins fell to $7,653 from $8,700 YoY, hurt by six reactivations at $2,125 per utilization day
International day rates fell 14% to $46,304 with elevated Middle East operating costs and a Kuwait rig idled until mid-2027
Cash from operations declined to CAD 71 million from CAD 76 million on a working capital build; Canadian margins slipped to CAD 12,817 from CAD 13,007
positive_highlights: Revenue rose 15% YoY to CAD 532 million and net earnings swung to CAD 21 million from a CAD 7 million loss
U.S. Permian rig count doubled to 16 from 8 a year ago; U.S. Q4 margin guided to $9,500-10,500, up from $7,653 in Q3
Canadian contract book grew to 28 rigs from 16 a year ago; CMP adjusted EBITDA rose 10% to CAD 21 million
summary: Q3 FY2026 revenue rose 15% YoY to CAD 532 million, adjusted EBITDA was CAD 125 million (CAD 133 million pre-share-based comp) versus CAD 118 million prior year, and net earnings were CAD 21 million versus a CAD 7 million loss a year ago. Canadian activity averaged 73 rigs and U.S. 43, but U.S. daily margins fell to $7,653 from $8,700 due to six rig reactivations costing $2,125 per utilization day, and international day rates dropped 14% to $46,304 with elevated Middle East costs. Q4 guidance points to Canadian margins of CAD 13,500-14,500 and U.S. margins of $9,500-10,500 (a sequential step up), with full-year capex raised to CAD 275-285 million from prior levels. Management cited CAD 31 million of buybacks, CAD 75 million of debt reduction year-to-date, and over CAD 460 million of liquidity.

negative_highlights: Cumulative shareholder returns reached only 40% through Q3 versus the >50% commitment, requiring an above-50% Q4 to catch up
U.S. gasoline demand down about 2.5% and diesel down about 1.5%
Chemicals Q4 utilization guided to mid-80s, with Golden Triangle startup costs expected at CPChem
positive_highlights: Refining utilization of 98% and record Q3 distillate yield of 41%
Second 2026 dividend increase of 10.8% versus Q4 2025; $2.8 billion returned in the quarter
Debt reduced $2 billion to $18.5 billion; net debt to capital at 26%, ahead of the 2027 target
summary: Reported and adjusted earnings were $5.6 billion, or $14.08 per share, with operating cash flow of $7.3 billion ($6.2 billion excluding a $1.1 billion working capital benefit). The company returned $2.8 billion to shareholders, cut debt by $2 billion to $18.5 billion, and reduced net debt to capital to 26%, hitting its 2027 target early, while announcing a second 2026 dividend increase of 10.8% versus Q4 2025. Q4 guidance calls for mid-80s chemicals utilization and mid-90s crude utilization; cumulative shareholder return was 40% through Q3 versus the >50% commitment, with management targeting above 50% in Q4. Refining ran at 98% utilization with record 41% distillate yield, and management cited a widened WCS/WTI differential worth $140 million per dollar.

negative_highlights: U.S. domestic adjusted operating margin declined 20 bps, with fuel a 30 bps headwind and higher over-the-road line-haul purchase transportation rates accelerating into Q4
Q4 faces transitory headwinds of $130 million line-haul rates, $100 million pilot agreement, and $80 million aircraft maintenance; Q4 U.S. domestic margin expected down moderately YoY
Ground economy volume declined 4% and international domestic volume declined 11%, with international yield growth expected to moderate in 2027
positive_highlights: Adjusted EPS of $3.74 rose 28% YoY and adjusted operating income grew 16%, with CY2026 EPS guidance raised and tightened to $18.00-$18.60
Express International revenue grew 17% and adjusted operating income rose 52% with 80 bps of margin expansion on strong export volume and air freight weight
Repurchased $2 billion of stock since June with $4.3 billion remaining authorization; Network 2.0 on track for ~$1 billion savings in CY2026 and $2 billion cumulative by 2027
summary: FedEx reported calendar Q3 revenue up 12% YoY (including a 4-point fuel surcharge benefit) and adjusted EPS of $3.74, up 28%, with adjusted operating income up 16% to $164 million. Revenue grew 10% in Express U.S. Domestic and 17% in Express International, where adjusted operating income rose 52% with 80 bps of margin expansion, while U.S. domestic adjusted operating margin declined 20 bps on fuel and purchased transportation costs. Management raised and tightened CY2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $18.00-$18.60 (midpoint implying 23% growth) and introduced a ~$4 billion adjusted free cash flow outlook, with Q4 adjusted EPS embedded at $6.03-$6.63. The quarter included $2 billion of buybacks since June and portfolio actions (FedEx Freight spin-off, Supply Chain sale), with Q4 facing transitory headwinds of $130 million line-haul rates, $100 million pilot agreement, and $80 million aircraft maintenance.

negative_highlights: CET1 ratio expected to fall roughly 200 bps to approximately 10.2% following the MANUBANK acquisition
Full cost savings from MANUBANK now delayed to 2028 due to core conversion timing, with a higher near-term expense run rate
Acquired MANUBANK loan balances came in below deal announcement levels, and market now projects three rate increases in 2027 versus prior cut expectations
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 7% QoQ and 11% YoY to $157 million, with NIM expanding 6 bps to 3.02% on higher loan yields and lower deposit costs
Efficiency ratio improved to 63.6% excluding notable items, down from 67.6% a year ago, reflecting positive operating leverage
Criticized loans fell 10% YoY to $335 million and net charge-offs declined to 19 bps annualized from 24 bps
summary: Hope Bancorp reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $157 million, up 7% QoQ and 11% YoY, with diluted EPS of $0.28 (up 16% YoY) and adjusted EPS of $0.29. Net interest margin expanded 6 bps to 3.02%, and pre-provision net revenue rose 11% sequentially to $55 million. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance to 16-18% revenue growth and 23-25% PPNR growth, including the MANUBANK acquisition closed October 1. The deal adds $2.2 billion of loans and $2.6 billion of deposits, but CET1 is expected to drop about 200 bps to roughly 10.2%, and full cost savings are delayed to 2028.

negative_highlights: Distributable earnings of $0.08/share and adjusted DE of $0.14/share, with $7.5M of specific CECL reserves charged off on the Denver office loan
Undepreciated book value declined to $7.87 from $8.10 on a higher general CECL provision ($107M, 332 bps vs $100M, 327 bps) and $6M of real estate impairments
Management guided loan growth to moderate and explicitly flagged a delay to full deployment and to reaching positive dividend coverage, citing ~$0.02-$0.03/share quarterly leakage
positive_highlights: Originated $272M across seven loans; loan portfolio grew ~30% YoY to $3.1B and ~$200M QoQ, now 72% multifamily
Completed fifth CLO and second of the year; roughly two-thirds of the loan book is now non-recourse, non-mark-to-market CLO financing
Sold the Albertsons NNN investment at only 2% below undepreciated book value, booking a $60.3M GAAP gain
summary: BrightSpire reported Q3 2026 GAAP net income of $46.9M or $0.37/share, driven largely by a $60.3M gain on the Albertsons NNN sale, but distributable earnings were only $10.3M or $0.08/share (adjusted DE $0.14/share) after $7.5M of specific CECL reserves. Undepreciated book value fell to $7.87 from $8.10 on higher CECL and REO impairments, though GAAP book value rose to $7.08 from $6.81. Management explicitly said it will slow loan book growth, hold more cash, and that full deployment and positive dividend coverage may be delayed given rate and credit-spread volatility; near-term portfolio growth is guided to be modest at best.

negative_highlights: Total revenue grew only 2% YoY and organic revenue ex the confidential contract was up 2%, with Federal Solutions organic revenue down 3% including the confidential contract
Full-year guidance was narrowed, not raised, and operating cash flow guidance of $430-490M was maintained despite Q3 cash flow of $269M
CFO Matt Ofilos is stepping down; George Ball returns as interim CFO effective November 6
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA rose 6% to a record $168M and adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 40 bps to a record 10.2%
Operating cash flow was $269M versus $163M in the prior-year quarter, with trailing 12-month free cash flow conversion of 130%
Critical Infrastructure revenue of $846M, adjusted EBITDA up 9% to $94M and margin up 80 bps to 11.1%, all segment records, with a 24th consecutive quarter of book-to-bill at or above 1.0x
summary: Parsons reported Q3 FY2026 total revenue up 2% YoY to roughly $6.25-6.45B run-rate, with organic revenue ex the confidential contract up 2%, adjusted EBITDA up 6% to a record $168M and margin expanding 40 bps to a record 10.2%. FY2026 guidance was narrowed rather than raised, to revenue of $6.25-6.45B and adjusted EBITDA of $510-550M, with operating cash flow guidance maintained at $430-490M despite $269M of Q3 operating cash flow. Bookings rose 14% to $1.8B for a 1.1x book-to-bill, backlog hit a record $9.4B with 73% funded, and the company disclosed a CFO transition with Matt Ofilos departing and George Ball serving as interim CFO. Management flagged a $850M award under protest and lapping of the confidential contract as headwinds, guiding Q4 organic revenue to roughly flat.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA margin contracted to 10.0% from 11.3% YoY on higher-priced vehicle mix and customer rate give-back
Non-GAAP other GPU fell $299 YoY and wholesale GPU fell $196 as retail growth outpaced wholesale gross profit
Operations expense per unit rose $109 on higher fuel and logistics costs, and available inventory growth lagged sales growth
positive_highlights: Retail units sold rose 39% YoY to 217,385 and revenue rose 42% to $8.04 billion, both new company records
Adjusted EBITDA hit a record $800 million and GAAP operating income a record $714 million
Net debt to trailing 12-month Adjusted EBITDA fell to a record 0.8x and EBITDA/interest rose to 6.9x after refinancing $1.7 billion of notes for ~$45 million annual interest savings
summary: Carvana reported Q3 FY2026 retail units of 217,385 (+39% YoY) and revenue of $8.04 billion (+42%), both company records, with net income of $483 million and record Adjusted EBITDA of $800 million. Adjusted EBITDA margin fell to 10.0% from 11.3%, driven by mix toward higher-priced vehicles and give-back to customers in other GPU, while net income margin rose to 6.0% from 4.7%. For FY2026, management reiterated the previously communicated $2.7-3.0 billion Adjusted EBITDA range and expects sequential increases in retail units and Adjusted EBITDA in Q4, contingent on a stable environment. Balance sheet metrics hit records at 0.8x net debt/Adjusted EBITDA and 6.9x EBITDA/interest, aided by a refinancing that saves roughly $45 million annually.

negative_highlights: RWP per policy written fell to $2,384, with premium per new customer down 2% year-over-year on customer mix.
Software & Data revenue declined to $22 million, with average companies served down due to the exit of a legacy small-contractor product removing roughly 4,000 companies.

Consumer Services monetized services fell 11% year-over-year on continued housing and moving softness; Q4 Adjusted EBITDA implied around $34 million, a step down from Q3 on seasonality and expense timing.
positive_highlights: Insurance Services Adjusted EBITDA rose 98% to $50 million at a 49% margin, marking the sixth consecutive Rule of 80 quarter.
Reciprocal policies written grew 42% to 68,000, accelerating from Q2's 38%; producing agency branch locations rose 114% and quote volume rose 79%.
Full-year Adjusted EBITDA excluding the Reciprocal guidance midpoint raised to $138 million (79% growth) from the $102 million starting midpoint, with net leverage reduced to 2.4x.
summary: Porch reported Q3 FY2026 Insurance Services revenue of $103 million, up 39% year-over-year, with segment Adjusted EBITDA of $50 million at a 49% margin; total company Adjusted EBITDA excluding the Reciprocal was $44 million, up 116% year-over-year. Reciprocal policies written rose 42% to 68,000 (accelerating from Q2's 38%), and GAAP net income attributable to Porch was $12 million, up $23 million year-over-year. Management raised full-year guidance for Adjusted EBITDA excluding the Reciprocal to $135-140 million (midpoint $138 million, 79% growth) from the prior $102 million starting midpoint, and provided an initial 2027 target of more than $180 million of Adjusted EBITDA excluding the Reciprocal, including a full year of Allied Trust. The company also announced the pending ~$200 million Allied Trust acquisition, expected to add roughly $25 million of Adjusted EBITDA in the first full year.

negative_highlights: Weather-normalized load growth only ~1%, with the variance attributed to customer ramps and maintenance outages reducing usage among larger customers
New $750M ATM equity program alongside a lowered 55%-60% payout target introduces dilution and financing uncertainty
EPS CAGR guidance of 5%-7% not updated despite rate base growth of 9.6%, with management deferring any refresh to next year
positive_highlights: 2026 consolidated EPS guidance raised to $2.62-$2.68 per share
Q3 diluted EPS of $1.52 versus $1.14 in the prior-year period, with utility net income of $321M versus $243M
Horseshoe Lake units 11-12 completed ahead of schedule and $12M under budget, adding ~448 MW and avoiding up to $16M in winter capacity purchase
summary: OGE reported Q3 consolidated net income of ~$316M, or $1.52/diluted share, versus $231M or $1.14 a year ago, with the electric utility at $1.54 versus $1.20, driven primarily by significantly warmer weather (45+ days of triple-digit heat versus one last year) partly offset by higher income tax expense. Management raised 2026 consolidated EPS guidance to $2.62-$2.68, assuming normal weather for the balance of the year. Horseshoe Lake units 11-12 came in ahead of schedule and $12M under budget, adding 448 MW, while Unit 15 represents ~$1.75B of investment with a 2031 in-service date. The company established an inaugural ATM program of up to $750M and expects ~$200M of incremental equity over the planning horizon; weather-normalized load growth was ~1%.

negative_highlights: Q4 EPS guided to -$0.15 to +$0.05 as fuel is now expected at $4.75/gal, up $1.25 or over $100M from prior guidance
Load factor fell 2 points YoY even as RASM rose 30%
Fleet actions drove $134 million of non-recurring charges in Q3 (lease return costs, accelerated depreciation, prepaid maintenance write-offs)
positive_highlights: Record revenue of $1.4 billion, up 53% YoY, with RASM up 30% on 18% capacity growth
Adjusted EPS of $0.18 came in above the high end of guidance; adjusted pre-tax margin rose ~12 points YoY to 3%
Loyalty-related revenue up 37% YoY; leverage cut from 7x to just over 4x adjusted EBITDAR
summary: Frontier posted record Q3 revenue of $1.4 billion, up 53% YoY, with RASM up 30% on 18% capacity growth and adjusted diluted EPS of $0.18, above the high end of guidance. Adjusted pre-tax margin improved ~12 points YoY to 3% despite a 56% fuel price increase ($3.96/gal), and CASM ex-fuel fell ~2.5% adjusted for sale-leaseback gains. Q4 guidance calls for adjusted EPS of -$0.15 to +$0.05 on fuel of $4.75/gal (up over $100M from prior guidance) with RASM up over 20% on 5-6% capacity growth; 2027 capacity framed loosely at 5-7%. Liquidity was $1.18 billion and leverage fell to just over 4x adjusted EBITDAR from 7x at year-end 2025.

negative_highlights: EPS fell linked quarter on a $13.3 million provision; net charge-offs were $10 million, largely one C&I credit written down to realizable value
Total deposits declined $73.2 million (1.3% annualized) on public fund outflows, leaving the loan-to-deposit ratio around 90-91% and reliance on borrowings
Non-interest income fell $1.9 million to $49.3 million on weaker mortgage banking, with management guiding to more fee softness in Q4; reported NIM narrowed 6 bps to 3.77%
positive_highlights: Adjusted EPS of $0.86 up 12% YoY; adjusted ROA 1.16% vs 1.09% and adjusted ROTCE 14.5% vs 14.2% a year ago
Record loan production with loans up $555.9 million, or 11.5% annualized, linked quarter, and core deposits up roughly $300 million (about 8% annualized)
Efficiency ratio improved to 57.7% on a $1.2 million linked-quarter decline in non-interest expense; criticized/classified balances down four straight quarters
summary: Adjusted EPS of $0.86 rose 12% YoY with adjusted ROA of 1.16% (vs 1.09%) and adjusted ROTCE of 14.5%; the efficiency ratio improved to 57.7%. Linked-quarter EPS declined, which management attributed to a higher $13.3 million loan provision driven by loan growth, while reported NIM fell 6 bps to 3.77% and core NIM rose 2 bps. Loans grew $555.9 million (11.5% annualized) but total deposits fell $73.2 million on public fund outflows, and management reiterated mid-single-digit balance sheet growth rather than raising it. Separately, Renasant announced the roughly $140 million Commercial Bank & Trust merger (75% stock/25% cash), expected about 4% EPS accretive and 1.5% TBV dilutive, closing in Q1 2027.

negative_highlights: Non-accrual loans rose to $119.6 million, or 2.7% of gross loans, from 2.2% in the prior quarter, tied to Channel Islands and U.K. residential real estate.
Unrealized AFS losses widened to $187.3 million from $106.7 million QoQ as longer-term rates rose.
Roughly $500 million of deposits notified to exit within weeks, and core non-interest expenses rose 3.5% QoQ.
positive_highlights: Net interest margin improved 2 bps QoQ to 2.76% and NII rose $1.6 million to $97.2 million on higher-yielding securities reinvestment.
Non-interest income grew $1.4 million QoQ to $64.8 million, with fee-based revenue at 40% of total revenues.
Core efficiency ratio of 57.8% remained below the 60% through-cycle target; core ROTCE was 25%.
summary: Butterfield reported Q3 FY2026 net income of $61.0 million ($1.50/share) and core net income of $64.2 million ($1.58/share), with ROACE of 21.3% and core ROTCE of 25%. NIM rose 2 bps QoQ to 2.76%, NII increased $1.6 million to $97.2 million, non-interest income rose $1.4 million to $64.8 million, and the core efficiency ratio was 57.8%; the $0.50 quarterly dividend was maintained. Management guided quarterly core non-interest expenses to $93-95 million and expects NII/NIM to be roughly flat near term, despite roughly $500 million of notified deposit outflows. Non-accrual loans rose to $119.6 million (2.7% of gross loans) from 2.2%, driven by Channel Islands and U.K. residential exposures, while unrealized AFS losses widened to $187.3 million from $106.7 million.

negative_highlights: Book-to-bill of 1.03 was the lowest since Q1 2024, and organic orders grew only 4% against a 5.7% prior-year comparison.
Inflationary costs for memory chips and higher oil prices negatively impacted margins.
Implied Q4 organic growth of 3%-4% reflects a difficult comparison from a $45 million product hold benefit in Q4 2025.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EPS up 25.1% to $1.34 and adjusted EBIT margin up 180 bps to 16.6%.
Full-year 2026 guidance raised for organic revenue, adjusted EBIT margin, adjusted EPS, and free cash flow.
Backlog increased 12% year-over-year to $23.7 billion, with PDX organic growth of 13.8%.
summary: GE HealthCare reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $5.5 billion, up 6.2% organically, with growth across all segments. Adjusted EBIT margin expanded 180 bps to 16.6% and adjusted EPS rose 25.1% to $1.34, while free cash flow reached $793 million. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance for organic revenue growth (~4%), adjusted EBIT margin (15.5%-15.7%), adjusted EPS ($4.95-$5.05), and free cash flow (>1.6 billion), citing strong execution and margin expansion. Backlog grew 12% to $23.7 billion, though book-to-bill was 1.03 and Q4 growth is implied at 3%-4% due to a prior-year product hold comparison.

negative_highlights: $763M of retained mark-to-market losses drove a GAAP loss and a 2% QoQ decline in tangible book value per share, with $654M ($16/share) of unrealized fixed-maturity losses outstanding.
Gross premiums written fell 9% to $2.1B and net premiums written fell 19% on increased ceded purchases; more ceded purchasing will further reduce 2027 net written premium.
Casualty and specialty adjusted combined ratio of 109.5% with a 10.5-point large-loss impact; management flags casualty rate no longer exceeding trend and plans to cut back in U.S. general liability.
positive_highlights: Operating income of $513M with a 19% annualized operating ROE; YTD operating income over $1.6B at a 20% operating ROE.
Retained net investment income of $315M, up 4% YoY, with duration extended to 4.2 years and yield to maturity up 70 bps to 6%, guiding Q4 NII to ~$325M and full-year 2026 to over $1.25B.
$310M of Q3 buybacks (959k shares at avg $323) plus $144M in October through Oct 23; management signals an elevated pace through Q4.
summary: RenaissanceRe reported Q3 operating EPS of $12.71 and a 19% annualized operating ROE, but rising rates drove $763M of retained mark-to-market losses, a GAAP loss, and a 2% sequential decline in tangible book value per share. Gross premiums written fell 9% to $2.1B and net premiums written fell 19%, with the adjusted combined ratio at 79% after a 9-point hit from large losses (Middle East war, Ras Laffan LNG explosion, Colombia earthquake). Management expects property cat rates down less than the mid-teens YTD decline seen in 2026, casualty rates no longer exceeding trend in U.S. general liability, and further pullback in casualty. Capital return stayed aggressive with $310M of buybacks in Q3 and $144M in October.

negative_highlights: Fringe benefits rose to 42.8% of salaries and wages from 39.7% a year ago, a roughly full operating point headwind, with more pressure expected in Q4
LTL tons per day fell 0.1% for the full quarter, and October tonnage was described as below normal seasonality
Operating supplies and expenses rose as a percent of revenue on higher diesel and petroleum-based costs
positive_highlights: Revenue rose 13.1% to $1.59 billion and EPS rose 28.9% to $1.65, with operating ratio improving 280 bps to 71.5%
LTL revenue per hundredweight increased 13.3% (ex-fuel up 5.1% for the quarter), reflecting strong pricing and the earlier Oct 1 GRI
October month-to-date revenue per day up approximately 22% YoY with tons per day up 1.6%, supporting Q4 revenue guidance above normal seasonality
summary: Old Dominion reported Q3 FY2026 revenue up 13.1% to $1.59 billion and EPS up 28.9% to $1.65, with the operating ratio improving 280 bps to 71.5%. Growth was driven by a 13.3% increase in LTL revenue per hundredweight, though LTL tons per day slipped 0.1% for the quarter before turning positive (up 1.6% YoY) in September. Management guided Q4 revenue to $1.54-1.58 billion (above normal seasonality) and an operating ratio around 73.5% +/-20 bps at the low end of the seasonal range, and noted October revenue per day up roughly 22% YoY. Key headwind cited was fringe benefit cost, which rose to 42.8% of salaries and wages from 39.7% a year ago, a ~1 point OR drag expected to persist into Q4.

negative_highlights: Truck margin came in at 8.1%, down from ~8.5% a year ago, on a fleet-heavy mix and competitive parts/service pricing pressure
New order activity and quoting have slowed as customers await EPA 2027 final rules and OEM pricing clarity
Tier 2/tier 3 supply bottlenecks could delay some Q4 deliveries into Q1, and visibility beyond Q1 into Q2 is limited
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 12.4% to ~$2.1B and net income rose 18.2% to $78M ($0.65 diluted)
Class 8 sales up 24.4% vs industry growth just over 10%, lifting share to 6.5%, with medium duty up 9.6% vs a flat market
Aftermarket revenue ~$680M, up 5.8%, generating nearly 63% of gross profit at a 128.3% absorption ratio
summary: Revenue rose 12.4% YoY to ~$2.1B and net income grew 18.2% to $78M ($0.65 diluted) with Class 8 sales up 24.4% (6.5% share) and aftermarket parts/service up 5.8% to ~$680M at a 128.3% absorption ratio. Management flagged soft new order activity tied to uncertainty over EPA 2027 emission rules, but guided to a strong Q4 and solid Q1 supported by backlog, with supply constraints at tier 2/3 suppliers pushing some deliveries into Q1. Truck margins compressed (8.1% vs 8.5% a year ago) on a fleet-heavy mix, and no formal full-year guidance was provided. The company repurchased $10.3M of stock, paid $16.4M in dividends, declared $0.14/share, and held $226M in cash.

negative_highlights: Cash same-property NOI growth was just 0.2% versus GAAP +4.1%, with straight-line rent at ~$14M versus $5.5M a year ago
Leasing CapEx is north of $140M year to date; management said 2027 will be an 'okay' cash flow year with normalization not expected until 2028
New leasing volume expected to moderate to ~250K sq ft/quarter from the 300K marker as lease rate exceeds 90%, and no acquisitions have met return hurdles this year
positive_highlights: Full-year FFO outlook raised $0.025 at the midpoint to $3.51-$3.70, and up $0.065 since the start of the year despite $0.04 of disposition dilution
Occupancy up 130 bps sequentially and lease rate at 90.1% (+50 bps QoQ) on 1.2M sq ft of second-gen leases at 29% GAAP / 4% cash rent growth
Debt/EBITDA cut from 6.7x at the start of the year to 6.1x, with ~$280M cash and nothing drawn on the $750M revolver
summary: Highwoods reported Q3 FFO of $0.89/share ($100.1M) and net income of $31.8M ($0.29/share), with no land sale gains or unusual items. Full-year 2026 FFO guidance was raised $0.025 at the midpoint to $3.51-$3.70, and excluding land gains the midpoint implies Q4 FFO above $0.90/share. Occupancy rose 130 bps sequentially, the lease rate reached 90.1%, and GAAP rent growth on 1.2M sq ft of second-gen leases was 29% (cash +4%). Cash same-property NOI was roughly flat at 0.2% versus GAAP +4.1%, with the gap attributed to free rent on new leases; management expects cash NOI to accelerate as that burns off, with free cash flow normalization pushed toward 2028.

negative_highlights: Q4 GMS guidance of 5-7% growth decelerates from the 8.8% reported in Q3, with management citing less favorable prior-year comparisons and FX headwinds
Purchase frequency remains modestly down YoY, and management said it does not expect the total to comp positively in the near term
CFO Lanny Baker is departing in early March, with an executive search underway for a Brooklyn-based successor
positive_highlights: Marketplace GMS grew 8.8% YoY to $2.6B, with revenue up 10.9% to $692M and take rate up 50 bps to 26.2%
Active buyers returned to YoY growth (+1% to ~88M) for the first time in two years, and GMS per active buyer rose 3.9% YoY, a third straight quarter of growth
Adjusted EBITDA grew 14.6% YoY to $210M at a 30.4% margin, the second consecutive quarter of EBITDA growing faster than revenue; full-year margin outlook raised to ~30%
summary: Etsy marketplace GMS rose 8.8% YoY to $2.6B, revenue grew 10.9% to $692M on a 26.2% take rate (up 50 bps), and adjusted EBITDA was $210M, up 14.6% YoY at a 30.4% margin. Active buyers returned to growth (+1% to ~88M, first increase in two years) and GMS per active buyer rose 3.9%, though purchase frequency remained modestly down YoY. Q4 GMS guidance of $3.46-3.52B implies 5-7% growth with a ~25.6% take rate and ~30% EBITDA margin, and the full-year EBITDA margin outlook was raised to roughly 30%. The company repurchased ~$395M of stock, cut ~5.2M shares, and announced CFO Lanny Baker will leave in early March.

negative_highlights: Dividend coverage timing was pushed out: sustainable coverage now expected in the first half of 2027, attributed to loan closings occurring later than anticipated
Weighted average risk rating rose to 3.2 from 2.9, with one office loan downgraded to 5 and Q4 to carry an approximately $0.11 per share Carlsbad realized loss
New origination net spreads compressed, with management guiding to a steady-state net spread of 160-180 bps versus recent levels; the large Chattanooga loan carried a tighter margin
positive_highlights: Originations of $122.3 million in Q3, the highest quarterly volume since Q4 2021, with virtually 100% funded at closing

Dallas office loan resolved at ~97% of $44.2 million, beating the $6.3 million CECL reserve and unlocking ~$46 million of capacity; office exposure fell to 13% from 19%, and to 10% after the post-quarter Carlsbad sale
Q4 DE guidance of $0.25-$0.27 per share versus $0.24 in Q3, with $220 million of net portfolio growth identified as the gap to dividend coverage and capital in place to fund it
summary: Q3 Distributable Earnings were $0.17 per share including a $1.5 million realized loss on the Dallas office loan; excluding it, DE was $0.24 per share, at the midpoint of guidance and in line with consensus. The quarter included a net $3.6 million credit reserve reversal, $122.3 million of originations (highest since Q4 2021), $139 million of repayments, and office exposure fell from 19% to 13%. Q4 DE guidance is $0.25-$0.27 excluding an approximately $0.11 Carlsbad realized loss, and the company pushed its sustainable dividend coverage target to the first half of 2027 due to loan closings landing later than anticipated. Weighted average risk rating rose to 3.2 from 2.9, and the Carlsbad office loan was downgraded to risk rating 5 before its post-quarter sale recovered about 90% of principal.

negative_highlights: Chemical valves and agriculture sales declined year-over-year, with chemicals described as continuing to be very fatigued on elevated input pricing
FSDP organic orders grew only 1%, well below the segment's 6% sales growth
HST life sciences was flat as an expected legacy platform roll-off offset mid-single-digit base analytical instrument growth
positive_highlights: Organic sales grew 8%, exceeding the 5%-7% guidance range, with HST up 13%, FMT up 4%, and FSDP up 6%
Adjusted EPS of $2.33 beat the $2.20-$2.25 guide and grew 15% year-over-year on record sales
Full-year 2026 adjusted EPS guidance raised $0.16 at the midpoint to $8.91-$8.96 and organic growth raised to 6.5%-6.8% from 5%-6%
summary: IDEX reported Q3 FY2026 organic sales growth of 8% (above the 5%-7% guide), record adjusted EPS of $2.33 (above $2.20-$2.25 guidance), adjusted EBITDA margin of 27.8% (above the 27%-27.5% range), and adjusted gross margin expansion of 70 bps to 45.2%. Organic orders rose 13% to nearly $1 billion with growth in all three segments (HST +21%, FMT +11%, FSDP +1%). The company raised full-year 2026 organic growth guidance to 6.5%-6.8% from 5%-6% and adjusted EPS to $8.91-$8.96 from $8.70-$8.85, while tightening EBITDA margin to 27.1%-27.3%. Free cash flow was $214 million (124% conversion), leverage improved to 1.8x, and $75 million of shares were repurchased with plans for ~$75 million per quarter through 2026.

negative_highlights: CET1 guided down 70 bps from 14.7% to at or very close to 14% by year-end 2026, partly from intended 2027 buyback accrual
Global banking revenues fell 21% with advisory down 44% from a record prior-year quarter, and Asset Management net new money was -$5 billion
Swiss capital proposal remains unresolved; CEO called the Upper House outcome very concerning and declined to quantify contingency options or their cost
positive_highlights: Underlying pre-tax profit of $4.1 billion rose 14% with return on CET1 capital of 16.7% and a cost-income ratio of 68.7%
GWM net new assets of $55 billion (4.5% growth) brought year-to-date NNA to $128 billion, with $13 billion of net new fee-generating assets
Gross cost reductions of $13.2 billion delivered, with total now expected around $13.7 billion versus the $13.5 billion ambition
summary: UBS reported Q3 FY2026 net profit of $2.7 billion and EPS of $0.85, with underlying pre-tax profit of $4.1 billion up 14% on 10% higher revenues, a 16.7% return on CET1 capital and a 68.7% cost-income ratio. All four businesses grew profit year-over-year, GWM attracted $55 billion of net new assets (4.5% growth rate), and the Investment Bank posted record Q3 global markets revenues of $2.5 billion, up 17%. Gross cost reductions are now expected around $13.7 billion versus the $13.5 billion ambition, and management said it is increasingly confident of outperforming its 2026 exit return target while holding the sub-70% cost-income exit ambition. Offsetting this, the CET1 ratio is guided down from 14.7% to at or near 14% by year-end including an intended 2027 buyback accrual, and management struck a defensive tone on the Swiss parliamentary capital proposal, calling September's Upper House outcome very concerning and declining to discuss contingency planning.

negative_highlights: Industrial Coatings segment EBITDA fell 11% and margin contracted 260 bps to 14.4% as COGS inflation outran index-based pricing; full catch-up pushed to Q1/Q2 2027
Q4 organic growth guided to low single digits versus 5% in Q3, with the Industrial segment guided essentially flat as automotive builds were cut
Q4 COGS inflation guided to high single digits, and management explicitly said not to assume a price/cost tailwind near term
positive_highlights: Organic sales rose 5% with 2% volume growth, the seventh consecutive quarter of organic sales growth and 300 bps of industry outperformance
Performance Coatings segment EBITDA grew 21% with margin up 220 bps to 23.9%; Aerospace posted double-digit organic growth with backlog near $300 million
Commercial actions fully offset COGS inflation, and the full-year adjusted EPS midpoint was raised and narrowed to $7.90-$8.10
summary: PPG reported Q3 net sales up 7% to $4.4 billion with organic sales up 5% (2% volume), adjusted EPS up 6% to a Q3-record $2.25, and total company adjusted EBITDA margin above 18%. Company-wide commercial actions fully offset COGS inflation for the first time. Industrial Coatings was the weak spot, with segment EBITDA down 11% and margin contracting 260 bps to 14.4% on index-pricing lag. The full-year adjusted EPS midpoint was raised and the range narrowed to $7.90-$8.10, though Q4 organic growth is guided to only low single digits versus Q3's 5%, and management declined to quantify 2027 beyond themes of continued organic growth and margin expansion.

negative_highlights: ES margin expansion of 60 basis points included a large emergency response event (~$120 million revenue); underlying margin growth was more modest.
Industrial services revenue rose only 1-2% year-over-year, with continued softness in North American refineries and limited turnaround activity.
Incineration utilization declined to 87% from 88% a year ago, partly due to a pulled-forward maintenance turnaround.
positive_highlights: Total revenue increased 21% to $1.87 billion, with both segments contributing to record quarterly revenue and adjusted EBITDA.
Adjusted EBITDA rose 42% to $456 million, and consolidated adjusted EBITDA margin reached a record 24.4%, up 370 basis points year-over-year.
Full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance raised to $1.44-$1.48 billion, $80 million higher at the midpoint, and adjusted free cash flow guidance increased to $600-$660 million.
summary: Clean Harbors reported record Q3 FY2026 results, with revenue up 21% to $1.87 billion and adjusted EBITDA up 42% to $456 million, driven by a large emergency response event (~$120 million) and record SKSS performance (adjusted EBITDA more than tripled to $126 million). The company materially exceeded its July guidance and raised full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance to $1.44-$1.48 billion (midpoint up $80 million) and adjusted free cash flow to $600-$660 million. ES segment margin expanded 60 basis points to 27.4%, and consolidated adjusted EBITDA margin reached a record 24.4%. Management noted strong demand trends, including reshoring, PFAS, and data centers, while maintaining a conservative SKSS outlook due to market uncertainty.

negative_highlights: Inventory up 13% sequentially and 39% YoY, with net working capital days rising five days to 60
ITS margin expansion limited to 20 bps (5.5%) as weakness in consumer-related end markets offset communications strength
Incremental weakness in lifestyle noted for the second half, with RMS revenue guided to only low-to-mid single digit growth in Q3
positive_highlights: FY2027 revenue guide raised ~$950M to $34.9-35.9B, with about half from underlying improvement and half from EPC Power
CPI operating margin expanded 240 bps YoY to 10.7%, with power segment margins up ~550 bps to ~16%
Adjusted operating profit rose 48% to $607M and adjusted EPS hit a record $1.18, up 49%
summary: Flex reported Q2 FY2027 revenue of $8.5B, up 25% YoY, with adjusted operating margin of 7.1% (up 110 bps) and record adjusted EPS of $1.18, up 49%. CPI grew 54% YoY with operating margin up 240 bps to 10.7% (power margins ~16%, up ~550 bps), RMS grew 9% and ITS grew 22%. FY2027 guidance was raised to revenue of $34.9-35.9B (up 27% at midpoint, a ~$950M increase, roughly half organic and half EPC Power) and EPS of $4.84-5.16 (up 52%); CPI margin outlook was lifted to ~240 bps of expansion from ~100 bps prior. FCF was $261M, reduced by $61M of one-time spin costs, and inventory rose 39% YoY to 60 days to support higher-value ramps.

negative_highlights: Restaurant-level margin contracted 120 bps to 23.3% and adjusted EPS fell 7% to $0.27
Q4 margin guided to just under 22%, roughly 150 bps below last year, with October trends softening
Labor costs rose 50 bps to 25.7% and other operating costs rose about 100 bps to 16%, including discrete insurance costs
positive_highlights: Sales grew 9.6% to $3.3 billion with positive comps of 2.1% and positive transactions of 0.8%
Cost of sales fell about 50 bps to 29.5% as pricing and tariff relief offset beef and freight inflation
Loyalty share of sales rose to over 33%, an all-time high, with active Rewards membership above 24 million
summary: Chipotle reported Q3 FY2026 sales up 9.6% to $3.3 billion with comps of +2.1% and transaction comp of +0.8%, but restaurant-level margin fell 120 bps to 23.3% and adjusted EPS dropped 7% to $0.27. Management kept its 2026 low single-digit comp guidance and expects Q4 margins just under 22%, about 150 bps below last year, while flagging that October trends softened consistent with the broader industry. Cost of sales improved about 50 bps to 29.5%, but labor rose 50 bps to 25.7% and other operating costs rose about 100 bps to 16% on higher marketing and delivery mix.

negative_highlights: Adjusted gross margin contracted 300 bps to 68.0% on unfavorable manufacturing absorption, and adjusted EPS fell 3% to $0.73 versus the $0.80-$0.82 guide
WATCHMAN sales declined 6% (U.S. down 7%) and EP sales declined 5% (U.S. down 8%), with management expecting continued PFA share erosion until FARAWAVE Ultra in early 2028

Management guided Q4 to organic revenue declines of 1%-3%, said 2027 will be challenged to grow revenue and EPS, and acknowledged needing to 'rebuild confidence' in forecasts after a year of forecasting misses
positive_highlights: Interventional Cardiology grew 19%, and Interventional Cardiology plus Vascular Therapies combined grew 12%
Neuromodulation sales grew 13% with broad-based pain growth and exceptional Nalu PNS performance
WATCHMAN concomitant procedures grew approximately 35% within the U.S.; EP international grew 2%
summary: Q3 FY2026 organic revenue grew just 1.5% versus the 3%-5% guide, and adjusted EPS of $0.73 fell 3% versus the $0.80-$0.82 range, with management attributing ~300 bps of the revenue shortfall and $0.07 of EPS to a cybersecurity incident. Adjusted gross margin contracted 300 bps to 68.0% and operating margin fell 150 bps to 26.5%. Q4 guidance calls for organic revenue declines of 1%-3% and EPS of $0.77-$0.79, with full-year EPS of $3.16-$3.18 and organic growth of ~4%; management said 2027 will be 'challenged to grow' sales and EPS excluding Penumbra, citing continued EP and WATCHMAN pressure, a 2027 competitive launch, and escalating China pricing headwinds.

negative_highlights: Non-interest income fell ~10% QoQ to $20 million, with SBA sale gains permanently exited and no replacement anticipated
Rapid loan growth and deposit competition forced heavier FHLB borrowings, tempering margin benefit (NIM up only 2 bps)
Q3 EPS includes a one-time $1.8 million tax benefit that management says will not recur; loan growth expected to step back toward the 2-2-2 pace from an 'abnormally strong' Q3
positive_highlights: Core pre-tax pre-provision revenue of $32.3 million rose 76% YoY and 6% QoQ
Efficiency ratio improved to 63%, down ~1.7 pts sequentially and ~16 pts from Q3 2024
Non-performing assets fell 20% QoQ to $58 million (0.68% of assets) with allowance coverage for NPLs at 126%
summary: Peapack-Gladstone reported Q3 FY2026 net income available to common of $18.5 million, or $0.99 per diluted share, up 17% sequentially from $15.8 million/$0.86. Total revenue was $88 million, up 2% QoQ and 24% YoY, with NII of $68 million (+6% QoQ, +33% YoY) and NIM of 3.34% (+2 bps QoQ, in line with prior guidance). Loans grew $403 million to $7.1 billion and deposits $301 million to $7.4 billion, both above the $200 million/$200 million quarterly objectives, and the efficiency ratio improved to 63%. Management reiterated its 2-2-2 quarterly objectives, guided to 2-3 bps of NIM expansion per quarter into 2027, and said mid-to-upper single-digit expense growth is expected next year; the $0.99 EPS includes a one-time $1.8 million tax benefit (20.5% effective rate vs 28.4%) not expected to recur.

negative_highlights: Q4 origination guidance of $1.5-$1.6 billion is below the $2.1 billion just reported, and management set that lower level as the 2027 baseline
Management said the favorable credit results are 'unusually favorable' and not indicative of a new run rate, guiding Q4 charge-offs back up to about $4 million with $5-$7 million of NPL migration
Core non-interest expense ex-credit-enhancement rose $2.8 million to $18.4 million, and management declined to give an expense run rate
positive_highlights: Originations of $2.1 billion came in far above the roughly $1.6 billion prior guidance, driven by stronger student lending and a credit-enhanced partner finally ramping
Net interest income rose 17% sequentially to $41.9 million and credit-enhanced balances nearly doubled to $146.2 million from $74.2 million
Net charge-offs on non-credit-enhanced loans fell to $2.6 million from $5.2 million in the prior quarter, and NPAs declined to $37.1 million from $37.7 million
summary: FinWise reported Q3 FY2026 net income of $10 million, or $0.73 per diluted share, with continuing operations at $10.4 million or $0.76, including a $6.5 million one-time bargain purchase gain from the Tallied transaction. Net interest income rose 17% sequentially to $41.9 million and originations reached $2.1 billion, well above the roughly $1.6 billion prior guide, while credit-enhanced balances nearly doubled to $146.2 million. Management guided Q4 originations to $1.5-$1.6 billion (below Q3 seasonality) and set that as the 2027 run rate, guided Q4 charge-offs to about $4 million versus the unusually favorable $2.6 million this quarter, and explicitly said the strong credit results are not a new run rate. The Upstart relationship ends September 30, 2026 with immaterial impact, and two partners have signaled intent to pursue bank charters, though their agreements run into late 2028 and early 2029.

negative_highlights: Organic constant currency growth guidance high end cut to 5.5% from 6%, with Q4 implied high end trimmed to 6.8% from 8.1%
U.S. ortho declined 1.7% and U.S. general surgery grew only ~1.9%, with OEM Buffalo Filter a drag

Adjusted EPS fell to $1.04 from $1.08 YoY as interest expense rose to $10.5 million from $6.3 million; adjusted gross margin guidance and Q3 gross margin came in light (56.4%, below the 50-100 bp expansion outlook)
positive_highlights: Adjusted EPS of $1.04 exceeded the high end of guidance by $0.01 and the low end by $0.06
Full-year adjusted EPS guidance raised to $4.54-$4.61 from $4.48-$4.60 on the Q3 beat
International drove the quarter: general surgery +15.5% and ortho +12.7% constant currency, with AirSeal and Buffalo Filter direct both growing high single to low double digits
summary: Q3 FY2026 net revenue was $335.6 million, down 70 bps as-reported and 80 bps constant currency, but up 6.7% organic constant currency; adjusted EPS was $1.04 versus $1.08 a year ago, which beat the top of the company's own range by $0.01 but was still a decline YoY. Adjusted gross margin rose 40 bps to 56.4%, adjusted operating margin rose 20 bps to 15.4%, and adjusted net income fell to $31.4 million from $33.4 million due to higher interest expense ($10.5 million vs $6.3 million) after the convertible-note refinancing. Full-year organic constant currency growth guidance was narrowed to 5%-5.5% from 5%-6% (high end cut on a more measured sequential pace and Q3 international distributor order timing not rolled forward), while full-year adjusted EPS guidance rose to $4.54-$4.61 from $4.48-$4.60. Domestic ortho fell 1.7% and U.S. general surgery grew only 1.9%-2% on OEM smoke evacuation pressure, partly offset by high single to low double digit AirSeal and Buffalo Filter direct growth and BioBrace plus international strength (general surgery +15.5%, ortho +12.7% constant currency).

negative_highlights: Group net revenue fell 12% QoQ to JPY 607.5bn and net income fell 29% to JPY 103.7bn, with income before income taxes down 30% to JPY 148bn.
Wholesale income before income taxes fell 51% QoQ to JPY 46.1bn as Global Markets revenue dropped 20%, including equities down 25% and fixed income down 14%.
Wholesale expense ratio came in at 85%, above the 80% target, and management flagged a slower start to October in Wholesale and Investment Banking.
positive_highlights: Recurring revenue in Wealth Management rose 13% QoQ to a record JPY 66.7bn, with net inflows into recurring revenue assets up 40% QoQ to a record JPY 755.4bn.
Investment Banking net revenue rose 9% QoQ to JPY 54.7bn, and Nomura ranked first in Japan-related ECM and DCM league tables for April-September.
H1 ROE of 13.3% and Q2 ROE of 10.9% exceeded the company's raised 10%-12% target, with the interim dividend at JPY 35 per share (41% payout ratio).
summary: Nomura reported Q2 FY2027 group net revenue of JPY 607.5bn, down 12% QoQ, with income before income taxes down 30% to JPY 148bn and net income down 29% to JPY 103.7bn; EPS was JPY 34.61 and Q2 ROE 10.9% (H1 ROE 13.3%). All four divisions saw profit declines QoQ after a record Q1, though H1 four-division income before taxes rose 50% YoY and recurring revenue hit a record JPY 66.7bn with record net inflows of JPY 755.4bn. The interim dividend was set at JPY 35 per share (41% payout), and October trading has been slower in Wholesale with Wealth Management revenue roughly flat versus Q2 while the Investment Banking pipeline remains solid.

negative_highlights: CFO flagged low single-digit depreciation growth in 2027 and more in 2028 plus rising raw material costs, saying gross margin is 'unlikely to see near the previous high level'
Softness noted in computers, AI LCD controllers, DDI, and Wi-Fi, and management projected the mid/low-end smartphone market weaker than others
2027 shipment growth constrained by capacity near full on several technologies; management said incremental capacity is 'not enough'
positive_highlights: Gross margin expanded from 32.5% to 34.0% as utilization rose from 85% to 92%
Record wafer shipments above 1.2 million 12-inch equivalent, with 22/28nm at ~35% of revenue and 22nm alone at 18.3% of wafer sales
Guided ~10% blended ASP increase for 2027, described as a turning point from historical erosion, with pricing talks in 'very late stage'
summary: UMC reported Q3 2026 revenue of TWD 74.24 billion, up 8% QoQ and 16.1% YoY on a 9M basis, with gross margin expanding to 34% from 32.5% and EPS of TWD 1.32; utilization rose to 92% from 85% on record wafer shipments of over 1.2 million 12-inch equivalent. Q4 guidance calls for low single-digit shipment growth, firm ASP, flat gross margin, and low-90% utilization. Management guided a roughly 10% blended ASP increase for 2027 with pricing talks in late stages, while flagging higher depreciation (low single-digit growth in 2027, more in 2028) and rising raw material costs that keep gross margin below prior peaks despite a healthier EBITDA structure. The board approved an additional ~$3.2 billion capex for silicon photonics, TFLN, and DTC capacity, with a target of AI-related revenue exceeding a quarter of total sales within three years.

FormFactor reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $280.5 million, up 9% sequentially and roughly 40% year over year, coming in $10.5 million above the high end of the $260-280 million outlook range, with non-GAAP EPS of $1.04 versus $0.82 in Q2 and non-GAAP gross margin of 56.5% (up 320 bps sequentially). Management guided Q4 revenue to approximately $285 million +/- $10 million and non-GAAP EPS of $0.95 +/- $0.09, with gross margin around 54%, and raised its baseline gross margin framework to about 53% from 51-51.5% previously. Roughly $10.5 million (about 380 bps) of the Q3 gross margin came from non-recurring tariff refunds and favorable sub-component costs; 2026 Farmers Branch cash CapEx was cut to $100-110 million from a prior $140-170 million on timing only. TRITON revenue expectations rose to upwards of $30 million for 2026 from an initial $10-20 million, and the Teradyne partnership includes a $300 million investment in FormFactor.

New Oriental reported Q1 FY2027 total net revenue of $1,874.5 million, up 23.1% YoY, above the upper end of its guidance, with non-GAAP operating income up 21.2% to $406.8 million and net income up 13.5% to $273.2 million ($1.74 diluted per ADS). Group operating margin was broadly stable as faster-growing East Watch raised its revenue mix weight, though management said both core education and East Watch expanded margins individually. Full-year FY2027 revenue guidance of $6,453.9M-$6,680.3M (14%-18% growth) was reiterated rather than raised, and management flagged Q2 group revenue growth above Q1; the board also approved a $300 million dividend ($2.0 per ADS in two installments) and a new $200 million buyback. Overseas test prep (+8%) and overseas consulting (+7%) reaccelerated while new education initiatives grew 25%.

negative_highlights: Contribution margin guidance decelerates: Q4 contribution guided up ~18% YoY at the midpoint versus 26% in Q3, and revenue growth of ~25% outpaces the ~18% contribution midpoint implied by guidance.
Under-65 health remains a drag, expected at ~4% of Q4 revenue with contribution down ~$900,000 YoY.
Cash of $18.7 million is modest, and the company drew $10 million on its revolver post-quarter to fund buybacks.
positive_highlights: Revenue, contribution, and adjusted EBITDA all exceeded the high end of guidance; adjusted EBITDA grew 36% YoY to $39 million and revenue grew 23% to $376 million.
Home and renters revenue reached a record $66 million, up 116% YoY, with agent revenue up ~46% to $21 million on more than 3,000 active agents.

Cash generation and capital returns: $21 million deployed in Q3 across buybacks and a TRA repurchase at a 47% discount, plus 1.8 million shares repurchased for $18 million post-quarter; full-year free cash flow guidance maintained at $90-100 million.
summary: MediaAlpha reported record Q3 FY2026 results: revenue of $376 million up 23% YoY, contribution of $57 million up 26%, and adjusted EBITDA of $39 million up 36%, all exceeding the high end of guidance. Home and renters revenue hit a record $66 million (+116% YoY), auto grew 17%, and agent revenue rose ~46% to $21 million. Q4 guidance calls for revenue of $355-375 million (~25% YoY growth at the midpoint), contribution of $54-57 million, and adjusted EBITDA of $36-39 million; full-year free cash flow guidance of $90-100 million was maintained and operating leverage drove 69% contribution-to-EBITDA conversion. Management pointed to a broadening carrier base (three carriers above 10% of revenue) and continued soft-market ad spend as drivers into 2027.

negative_highlights: Total net sales fell 45% YoY to $62 million, with wound sales down 71% to $22 million on Medicare reimbursement changes and pricing pressure
GAAP gross profit fell to $50 million from $95 million and gross margin contracted to 80% from 84% YoY; G&A rose to $19 million on $6 million of incremental legal costs
FTC second request extends the HSR waiting period and delays the Sanara close, with no timeline provided and ticking fees now accruing on the $300 million Hayfin commitment
positive_highlights: Surgical revenue grew 9% YoY (mid-teens volume) to $40 million, now ~two-thirds of total sales, with broad-based growth in AMNIOFIX, AMNIOEFFECT, particulates and G4Derm Plus
Adjusted EBITDA returned to positive $2 million, a ~$10 million sequential improvement, and gross margin expanded ~11 percentage points sequentially to 80%
Wound care center volume grew more than 20% YoY and 7% sequentially; company ended quarter debt-free with $121 million net cash and a $25 million patent settlement
summary: Q3 FY2026 net sales were $62 million, down 45% YoY, with surgical up 9% and wound down 71% after the 2026 Medicare reimbursement reset. GAAP gross margin was 80% (down from 84% YoY but up ~11 points sequentially), Adjusted EBITDA was $2 million (3% of sales) versus $35 million a year ago, and GAAP net loss was $0.06 per share. The company now guides full-year 2026 net sales of $250-260 million, expects high-single-digit surgical growth and mid-single-digit sequential wound growth in Q4, and flagged an FTC second request that delays the Sanara acquisition. Management also noted a $25 million patent settlement, a favorable AXIOFILL court ruling, and a debt-free balance sheet with $121 million net cash.

InvenTrust reported Q3 2026 same property NOI of $50.4 million, up 3.1% YoY, with NAREIT FFO of $0.53 per diluted share, up 8.2%, and core FFO of $0.50, up 6.4%. Full-year NAREIT FFO guidance was raised to $2.05-$2.07 and core FFO to $1.94-$1.96, while same property NOI guidance was updated to 3.75%-4.25% and net investment assumptions trimmed to $190-$255 million on deal timing. Leasing was a highlight with 86 leases, blended spreads of 14% (new 42%, renewal 11%), leased occupancy up 20 bps sequentially to 96.4%, and a signed-not-open pipeline of roughly 110 bps of occupancy and $4.3 million of ABR. The main change was management raising acquisition return hurdles by 25-50 bps and slowing external growth as private-market pricing has not adjusted to higher debt costs.

negative_highlights: Group provisions for credit losses of EUR 501 million remain elevated, driven by proactive CRE de-risking and an idiosyncratic Corporate Bank event in Asia
FICC markets revenues declined year-on-year on non-recurrence of prior-year distressed credit trading strength; Investment Bank revenues only broadly matched a record prior year
Total expense guidance held at around EUR 21.3 billion, implying a significant Q4 cost step-up versus the first nine months
positive_highlights: Full-year revenue guidance raised to above EUR 33 billion versus the prior around EUR 33 billion ambition
Corporate Bank delivered record quarterly revenues of approximately EUR 2 billion, up 9% year-on-year with double-digit NII and commission growth
Private Bank net flows of EUR 17 billion and Asset Management record net flows of EUR 31 billion; group AUM near EUR 2 trillion, up roughly EUR 0.25 trillion year-on-year
summary: Q3 FY2026 net revenues of EUR 8.3 billion rose 4% year-on-year, marking 21 consecutive quarters of revenue growth, with profit before tax of EUR 2.6 billion up 8% and RoTE of 10.6%. All four divisions contributed, with the Corporate Bank posting record revenues near EUR 2 billion (+9% YoY) and the Private Bank up 8% on record EUR 17 billion net flows. Management raised full-year revenue guidance to above EUR 33 billion while keeping total expense guidance at around EUR 21.3 billion; CET1 was 14.0% and 2026 buybacks totaled EUR 1.5 billion. Loan loss provisions of EUR 501 million included proactive CRE de-risking and an idiosyncratic Asia corporate event, with the CRE run rate expected to decline gradually in 2027.

negative_highlights: Non-performers in the C&I LA loan book increased to $82 million from $46 million last quarter
Management said higher rates make it 'more challenging to make loans' and that origination volumes have been muted
Gain on sale income saw a sharp decline, per the analyst's question, requiring NII growth to carry Q4
positive_highlights: Q3 net interest income of $18.9 million was the highest in nearly four years as a financial holding company, up 26% QoQ and 30% YoY
Tangible book value per share of $12.30 rose 10% YoY and 78% since taking over the bank in January 2023
Newtek Bank ranked number one in units of SBA loans approved for fiscal year 2026, with deposits growing to $2.6 billion
summary: NewtekOne reported Q3 2026 basic/diluted EPS of $0.34 and reiterated full-year 2026 EPS guidance of $1.70-$1.80, implying a step-up in Q4 driven by seasonal lending and NII growth. Q3 net interest income of $18.9 million was the highest as a financial holding company, up 26% QoQ and 30% YoY, with NII at 26% of revenue versus 19% in Q3 2025. Tangible book value per share was $12.30, up 10% YoY and 78% since acquiring the bank, while deposits reached $2.6 billion and YTD loan originations of $1.2 billion rose 12% YoY. Credit was a concern: non-accruals in the C&I LA book rose to $82 million from $46 million last quarter, and management said higher rates are making loan growth more challenging and originations have been muted.

negative_highlights: 2028 margin target of 30% EBITDA withdrawn as too aggressive, citing AI/cyber spend, slower Paragon margin accretion and a two-year flat spot in Medical
Nuclear & Safety adjusted EBITDA margin contracted to 25.7% from 28.1% on legacy Paragon project adjustments and Sensing/NA headwinds
Q3 organic growth of 6.5% came in below the high-single-digit July guide and adjusted EBITDA high end was lowered to $292M from prior range
positive_highlights: Organic orders grew 62% to $340M, with nuclear power end-market orders up 105% (134% excluding the Chinese de-booking)
Backlog rose to $1.25B from $816M a year ago, with $735M expected to convert across Q4 2026 and FY2027, over $200M more than a year ago
Adjusted free cash flow guidance raised to $170M-$185M from $155M-$175M; YTD FCF of $107M doubled the prior year
summary: Q3 revenue rose 24.5% to $277.8M, with organic growth of 6.5% slightly below the high-single-digit July guide; adjusted EBITDA of $64.8M grew 23.7% but margins slipped to 23.3% from 23.5%. Adjusted EPS was flat at $0.12. Total revenue guidance was raised to 24%-25% (from 22%-24%) and organic to 7%-8% (from 5%-7%) with Q4 organic expected mid-to-high teens, but the adjusted EBITDA dollar range was narrowed downward at the high end to $285M-$292M and the 2028 30% margin target was withdrawn as too aggressive. Orders grew 62% organically to $340M with nuclear power orders up 105%, and free cash flow guidance was raised to $170M-$185M.

negative_highlights: Loan growth excluding consumer runoff is only 4% YTD; payoffs remain elevated and some deals are being displaced by competitors like Farm Credit
Higher rates are pressuring project economics and slowing some commercial and residential activity; management flagged potential deposit beta in a rising-rate cycle
Fee businesses face a seasonal Q4 decline, and retirement plan revenue growth is guided down to 5%-7% for 2027 from 8.7% this quarter
positive_highlights: Record net interest income of $143 million, up $5 million from Q2 and more than 5% above Q3 2025
Net interest margin expanded 5 bps to 3.78%; deposits costs fell 1 bp to 1.32%
Provision expense fell to $3.8 million from $6.1 million in Q2; reserves cover 2x non-performing loans and criticized/classified levels ticked down
summary: NBT reported Q3 2026 net income of $58 million, or $1.11 per diluted share, on record net interest income of $143 million (up $5 million QoQ and over 5% YoY) and NIM of 3.78%, up 5 bps sequentially. Loans grew 4% YTD to $11.9 billion excluding consumer runoff (3% including), core deposits rose 2.6%, and provision fell to $3.8 million from $6.1 million. Management guided to consistent Q4 loan growth, roughly flat Q4 expenses of $114-115 million, and 2027 loan growth of 3%-5%, with fee income stepping down seasonally in Q4. There was no explicit EPS or revenue beat versus consensus stated, and no formal guidance raise.

negative_highlights: Communications networks organic sales fell 28% YoY and 13% sequentially, with a further Q4 decline guided on broadband softness
Adjusted operating margin slipped 10 bps sequentially, reflecting the larger Q2 tariff-recovery benefit
IT datacom reached 48% of sales and grows toward ~50%+ next year, concentrating exposure in one end market despite positive growth
positive_highlights: Sales of $10.2 billion beat the high end of guidance, up 65% YoY and 37% organically, with IT datacom up 117% YoY (77% organic) and 30% sequentially versus a mid-teens expectation
Adjusted operating margin expanded 220 bps YoY to 29.7%, and adjusted diluted EPS rose 74% to $0.80
Record orders of $12.17 billion drove a 1.19:1 book-to-bill, with positive book-to-bill in all but one end market
summary: Amphenol reported record Q3 FY2026 sales of $10.2 billion, up 65% YoY (37% organic) and 17% sequentially, with adjusted diluted EPS of $0.80 (up 74% YoY) and adjusted operating margin of 29.7% (up 220 bps YoY, down 10 bps sequentially on tougher tariff-recovery comparison). Orders hit a record $12.17 billion for a 1.19:1 book-to-bill, and management guided Q4 to $10.3-$10.5 billion in sales and $0.81-$0.83 adjusted EPS (60-63% and 65-69% YoY growth), lifting full-year sales to ~$36.9-$37.1 billion and adjusted EPS to $2.82-$2.84. Results exceeded the high end of prior guidance, and the board raised the dividend 20% to $0.15 per share and authorized a new $4 billion buyback. The one soft spot is communications networks, where organic sales fell 28% YoY on broadband weakness, with further decline guided for Q4.
