negative_highlights: Total net revenue fell 20% to $39.6 million from $49.7 million, with U.S. product revenue down to $28.5 million from $40.9 million on lower net note prices amid generic competition
EMT2's primary progression-free survival endpoint was not met, with only the secondary overall survival endpoint showing benefit

U.S. pricing pressure expected to continue into 2027, and partner ordering timing means international product revenue (down to $3.7 million from $4.1 million in Europe) may lag in-market demand growth
positive_highlights: First profitable quarter in two years at net income of $245,000, versus a $7.7 million net loss in Q3 2025
Total operating expense declined 44% YoY (22% excluding restructuring), and operating cash flow was $9 million in Q3 and $22 million year-to-date versus a $9 million outflow
Gross margin rose about 2.3 percentage points sequentially excluding write-offs on renegotiated supply contracts; cash of $324 million, up $21 million from year-end 2025, with zero debt
summary: Total net revenue fell to $39.6 million from $49.7 million YoY, with U.S. product revenue down to $28.5 million from $40.9 million on lower net watching prices tied to generic competition, partly offset by licensing/royalty revenue rising to $2.7 million from $1.1 million. The quarter returned to a thin GAAP profit of $245,000 versus a $7.7 million net loss, driven by a 44% cut in operating expense and a 2.3-point sequential gross margin improvement excluding write-offs from renegotiated supply contracts. Operating cash flow was $9 million in Q3 and $22 million year-to-date versus a $9 million outflow, with $324 million in cash and no debt. Management expects U.S. volumes and exclusivity stable through 2026, anticipated continued U.S. pricing pressure into 2027, and reaffirmed full-year positive operating cash flow without formal revenue or EPS guidance; EMT2 missed its primary PFS endpoint but showed a 32% lower hazard of death on overall survival.

negative_highlights: Estimated ~$125M PAMA reimbursement impact expected in 2027, with management calling 2027 a 'tougher year'
Incremental foreign currency headwind of ~$10M versus prior guidance
Diagnostics organic price mix growth of 1.3% was modest relative to 3.1% volume growth
positive_highlights: Adjusted EPS grew 14.5% to $4.78 and adjusted operating margin expanded 60 bps to 15%
BLS adjusted operating margin expanded 180 bps to 18.3% on organic constant currency growth of 9.6%, with book-to-bill of 1.13
2026 guidance raised: revenue midpoint up $65M and adjusted EPS midpoint up $0.18
summary: Labcorp reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $3.8B, up 6.9% (organic 5.5%), adjusted EPS of $4.78, up 14.5%, adjusted operating margin of 15% (up 60 bps), and free cash flow of $412M. Diagnostics revenue rose 6.5% (organic 4.4%) with 40 bps of margin expansion to 16.7%, and BLS revenue rose 8.5% (organic constant currency 9.6%) with 180 bps of margin expansion to 18.3% and book-to-bill of 1.13. Guidance was raised: the midpoint of 2026 enterprise revenue guidance increased by $65M (to 5.9%-6.7% growth) and adjusted EPS midpoint by $0.18 (to $18.30-$18.70), though the company flagged an estimated ~$125M PAMA reimbursement impact for 2027. Management reaffirmed its 2026-2029 long-term outlook and noted the PAMA headwind is expected to be largest in 2027, with partial offsets from LaunchPad, business development, and underlying momentum.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA of $172 million and adjusted net income of $127 million were flattered by a $153 million one-off gain on sale of five vessels
The $2.1 billion cash balance excludes October pool hire payments of over $100 million and $145 million pending from two LR2 sales not yet closed
Refining margins have peaked and are coming off record highs, which James Doyle acknowledged may pressure margins even as runs rise
positive_highlights: Q4 booked LR2 rates of ~$181,000/day and MRs of ~$56,000/day, with November-to-date LR2s ~$215,000/day and MRs ~$70,000/day versus July LR2 $55,000 and MR $29,000
Quarterly dividend raised 67% from $0.45 to $0.75 per share, with management stating an expectation to increase it annually
Net cash position of $1.4 billion ($27/share) and cash break-even below $11,000/day, with debt cut from $3.1 billion to $655 million
summary: Scorpio Tankers reported Q3 2026 adjusted EBITDA of $172 million and adjusted net income of $127 million, with a $153 million gain on five vessel sales, $200 million of Nordic bond repayment, and a net cash position of $1.4 billion ($27/share). Q4 bookings have accelerated sharply: LR2s at ~$181,000/day and MRs at ~$56,000/day, with November-to-date LR2s near $215,000/day and MRs near $70,000/day versus July levels of $55,000 and $29,000 respectively. The board raised the quarterly dividend 67% from $0.45 to $0.75 per share and management said it expects to keep raising it annually. Cash break-even is below $11,000/day and $1.3 billion of newbuild/JV commitments can be funded without debt.

negative_highlights: 407 ETR traffic declined 7.1% in Q3, attributed to slower economic growth, tariff-exposed heavy vehicles, weather and holiday timing, with regional GDP described as almost flat in 2026

I-77 adjusted EBITDA fell 6.1% and traffic declined 5.3% in Q3 as heavy vehicles shifted to alternative routes and the revenue-share band stepped up from 25% to 50%; Dalaman revenue fell 7.1% and EBITDA 7.7%
No NTO distributions until June 2033 with no time-based fallback, and equity funding for I-24 and I-285 East is back-ended to 2033-2035, with Phase 2 of I-285 not automatically committed
positive_highlights: Construction adjusted EBIT margin improved to 4.1% from 3.7% in 9M, with a 5.1% margin in Q3, and order book reached a record EUR 19 billion, up 8.2% like-for-like vs December 2025
407 ETR revenue grew 18.4% and EBITDA 21% in 9M on higher toll rates, with total 2026 dividends approved of CAD 2.1 billion versus CAD 1.5 billion in 2025

Net cash position excluding infrastructure projects rose to roughly EUR 1.66 billion from EUR 1.3 billion at end-2025, with EUR 604 million of project dividends and EUR 591 million of construction operating cash flow
summary: Ferrovial reported 9M 2026 with double-digit like-for-like growth: construction revenue of EUR 5.8 billion (+9.1% LFL) at a 4.1% adjusted EBIT margin (up from 3.7%), an all-time-high EUR 19 billion order book (+8.2% LFL vs December 2025), and a net cash position of EUR 1.66 billion excluding infrastructure projects, up from EUR 1.3 billion at year-end 2025. Highways were two-sided: 407 ETR revenue rose 18.4% and EBITDA 21% on higher tolls despite traffic down 7.1%, while I-77 adjusted EBITDA fell 6.1% as its revenue-share band stepped up from 25% to 50%, and Dallas NTE traffic fell 2.5%. No formal group guidance was stated; the call was dominated by disclosure on the new I-24 and I-285 East awards, where equity injections are described as heavily back-ended into 2033-2035, and NTO dividends are locked up until June 2033 with no fallback.

negative_highlights: Gross margin declined 110 bps to 18.5%, with Business Solutions margin falling to 23.8% from 26.5%
Notebook and laptop revenue rose over 30% while unit count fell about 5%, indicating pricing pressure
Management flagged no Q4 budget flush, which it called uncharacteristic, and expects 2027 endpoint demand slightly down from 2026
positive_highlights: Net sales rose 23.3% to a record $874.3 million, with server storage up 45.1% and networking up 43.3%
Operating income grew 35.4% to $41 million as SG&A fell 150 bps to 13.8% of net sales, lifting operating margin to 4.7% from 4.3%
Enterprise Solutions net sales rose 27.4% to a record $407.5 million and ended the quarter with a record backlog
summary: Connection reported Q3 FY2026 record net sales of $874.3 million, up 23.3% YoY, with record gross billings of $1.3 billion (+19.4%) and record gross profit of $161.9 million (+16.7%). Gross margin contracted 110 bps to 18.5% on large-project customer mix and lower netted-down software revenue, while operating income rose 35.4% to $41 million and diluted EPS grew 27.8% to $1.24. Management gave no formal EPS or revenue guidance but said Q4 should follow the historical sequential decline of roughly 3-4% from Q3 and expects to outperform the U.S. IT market by 200 bps for the year. Management noted the endpoint device upgrade cycle is largely behind it and expects endpoint demand slightly down in 2027, while saying it has not seen the typical Q4 budget flush.

negative_highlights: Net credit loss rate of 10.9% was 20 bps above the July outlook and up 70 bps year-over-year; 30+ day delinquency rose 50 bps both sequentially and year-over-year to 7.5%

Q4 net income now expected to be lower than Q3 versus July expectation it would exceed Q3, driven by higher net credit losses, accelerated partnership costs, higher funding costs, and G&A timing shift
Cost of funds expected to rise to ~4.7% in Q4 from 4.4% as lower-cost fixed-rate securitizations amortize out of their revolving periods
positive_highlights: Record revenue of $178.8 million, up 8% year-over-year, with other income including bank partnership fees more than doubling to $12.3 million
Operating expense ratio improved 20 bps year-over-year to 12.6% despite absorbing ~40 bps of upfront bank partnership origination costs
Auto-secured portfolio grew 25% year-over-year to nearly 16% of total portfolio with just 2.2% 30+ day delinquency, and bank partnership fee income added ~120 bps to revenue yield
summary: Q3 FY2026 net income was $15.1 million, or $1.61 diluted EPS, up 5% and 13% year-over-year, on record revenue of $179 million, up 8% year-over-year, with the portfolio up 7.6% to $2.2 billion and operating expense ratio improving 20 bps to 12.6%. However, net credit losses of 10.9% came in 20 bps above the July outlook and 70 bps above prior year, with 30+ day delinquency up 50 bps to 7.5% on pressures concentrated in 2025 originations. Full-year net income growth (6%-9%), EPS growth (10%-13%), and portfolio growth (5%-7%) guidance is unchanged, but management guided Q4 net income below Q3 versus prior expectation it would exceed, citing higher credit losses, accelerated bank partnership costs, higher funding costs, and G&A timing. The bank partnership with Column now accounts for just over 40% of October originations, up from roughly 28% in July, and added about 120 bps to total revenue yield with an expected 200 bps pre-tax margin lift.

negative_highlights: Full-year North America packaging adjusted EBITDA outlook cut to $2.27-$2.31 billion, with ~$145 million of incremental headwinds lowering the midpoint by ~$110 million
Free cash flow was -$267 million in the quarter, with full-year FCF guided to only ~$100-$200 million
EMEA results came in below expectations on softer demand and higher natural gas costs, and EMEA guidance was withdrawn due to the planned separation
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded nearly 400 bps sequentially to 13.6%, with adjusted EBITDA of $843 million
Packaging Solutions North America adjusted EBITDA rose 56% sequentially to $663 million on $141 million favorable price/mix and $85 million favorable operations/costs
Management expects to outpace industry demand by ~2 percentage points for the full year, with Pine Hill restarted ahead of schedule and September price increase not yet in Q4 box prices
summary: Adjusted EBITDA rose to $843 million with margin up nearly 400 bps sequentially to 13.6%, and adjusted operating EPS was $0.37, with North America packaging EBITDA up 56% sequentially to $663 million on $141 million favorable price/mix and $85 million favorable operations. But the full-year North America packaging EBITDA outlook was cut to $2.27-$2.31 billion, with ~$145 million of incremental headwinds (diesel, distribution, volume) reducing the midpoint by ~$110 million, and Q3 free cash flow was -$267 million. Q4 North America packaging EBITDA is guided to ~$700-$740 million; EMEA guidance was withdrawn ahead of the planned separation. Management said market conditions persist into 2027 and declined to guide 2027, while noting more price realization (September increase) remains ahead.

negative_highlights: GAAP gross margin contracted 50 bps to 35.4% on plant-move inefficiencies, inflation, and acquired inventory step-up
Water Systems adjusted operating margin fell 120 bps to 17%, with international organic volume down nearly 5%
Water Systems adjusted operating income declined 2% to $60 million; EMEA and Middle East demand soft on conflict
positive_highlights: Full-year sales and adjusted EPS guidance both raised to $2.23-2.30 billion and $4.62-4.82
Energy Systems adjusted operating income up 24% with margin expanding 260 bps to 34.4%
Distribution sales up 15% to a record $226.1 million with operating margin up 80 bps to 9.1%
summary: Franklin Electric reported Q3 FY2026 sales of $633.6 million, up 9% YoY, with organic growth of nearly 5%, and adjusted diluted EPS of $1.50 versus $1.31, a 15% increase. Adjusted operating income rose 11% with margin up 30 bps to 15.1%, though GAAP gross margin fell 50 bps to 35.4% on plant-move inefficiencies, inflation, and $3.6 million of acquired inventory step-up. Management raised full-year sales guidance to $2.23-2.30 billion and adjusted EPS to $4.62-4.82, excluding the Challenge Pumps deal announced after the quarter. Segment detail was mixed: Distribution sales up 15% to a record $226.1 million with margin up 80 bps, Energy adjusted operating margin up 260 bps to 34.4%, but Water Systems adjusted operating margin fell 120 bps to 17% on site-move headwinds and EMEA softness.

negative_highlights: Full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance cut to ~$4.7 billion from earlier expectations, driven by $700 million of energy and freight headwinds
North American corrugated converting margins fell below the prior 3-4% range as paper price increases have not yet been passed into box prices
Earnings call omitted hard revenue and EPS figures; management withheld 2027 guidance, saying budgets are not yet done
positive_highlights: Paper mill system described as sold out across most grades, with order backlog still being fulfilled from April and May
Sequential pricing gains: North American pricing up ~5% and Europe up ~2% from Q2 to Q3
2030 medium-term plan reaffirmed unchanged, with Ken Bowles calling the 2026 shortfall purely a timing issue
summary: Smurfit Westrock reported Q3 adjusted EBITDA of $1,205 million, a 14.8% margin, and guided full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA to approximately $4.7 billion, citing $700 million of energy and freight cost headwinds versus earlier expectations. Management repeatedly said the cost inflation was unprecedented and greater than anticipated, and that price increases ($170/ton in North America, EUR 140 in Europe) will take until Q1 2027 to fully pass through. North American volumes were down in Q3 with the company citing Cyclospora and E. coli impacts on agricultural end markets, though October volumes were described as roughly flat year-over-year. The 2030 targets were reaffirmed but the timing bridge to get there has slipped.

negative_highlights: Non-clinical revenue of $15M declined ~10% YoY ($1.5M), with legacy pharma now expected down low double digits for the year.
Cash declined $6M to $139M, reflecting a ~$10M DOJ settlement and transient XiFin RCM implementation effects on receivables.
Q4 adjusted gross margin guided to ~48%, down from 49% in Q3, with unreimbursed MRD runs cited as a gross margin headwind.
positive_highlights: Adjusted gross margin expanded over 300 bps to 49% on mix shift, 11% AUP growth, and Lab of the Future efficiencies.
NGS revenue grew 29% YoY with 17% volume growth and large panel volumes up more than 25%.
Full year 2026 revenue guidance raised to $807-809M and adjusted EBITDA guidance raised to ~$60M from $56-58M.
summary: NeoGenomics reported Q3 total revenue of $209M, up 11% YoY and above its ~10% expectation, with clinical revenue of $195M (+13%), NGS revenue +29% (+17% volume, large panels >25%), and AUP +11%. Adjusted gross margin was 49%, up over 300 bps, and adjusted EBITDA was $18.7M, up 53% YoY and well above expectations. Management raised FY2026 revenue guidance to $807-809M from $802-806M and adjusted EBITDA to ~$60M from $56-58M, with NGS now seen growing >25% to ~$250M; non-clinical is still a headwind, guided down low double digits. A CEO transition to Warren Stone (effective January 2027) was detailed, with strategy continuity emphasized.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EPS of $0.70 grew only 2% YoY as higher interest expense from the Chart deal offset operating gains
Leverage rose to 2.5x after funding Chart; net leverage below 1.5x is not targeted until H2 2028
IET margin of 19.7% (up 90 bps) came in below the guidance midpoint on project timing, mix, and inflation; Q4 assumes Middle East declines in both OFSE and IET
positive_highlights: IET RPO hit a record $39.4B, up 6% sequentially and 23% YoY, with company book-to-bill of 1.3x and IET at 1.7x
Full-year IET order outlook raised to $21.5-23.5B, implying >1.6x book-to-bill and a record year, with YTD orders already $17.9B
Company EBITDA guidance midpoint raised to $5.265B; Q3 free cash flow of $769M rose 10% YoY despite ~$200M of Chart closing costs
summary: Revenue was approximately $8.0B, up 14% YoY with 9% net from acquisitions/divestitures, and adjusted EBITDA rose 14% to $1.42B at a 17.6% margin, flat to prior year. Adjusted EPS was $0.70, up only 2% YoY, and free cash flow was $769M after ~$200M of Chart-related transaction costs. Full-year EBITDA midpoint was raised to $5.265B and the IET order outlook lifted to $21.5-23.5B (a record year, implying >1.6x book-to-bill), with IET RPO at a record $39.4B, up 23% YoY. Q4 guidance embeds sequential Middle East declines and tougher IET logistics, with dollar-for-dollar quarter guide set at $8.25B revenue and $1.46B EBITDA.

negative_highlights: SHOP same-store NOI growth decelerated to 16% from 18% last quarter, and margin expansion slowed to 190 bps from 210 bps.
SHOP same-store margin slipped 20 bps sequentially despite occupancy gains, attributed to an extra day in the quarter and higher utility costs.
Higher interest rates and FX reduced the FFO guidance raise by $0.01, and management declined to comment on 2027.
positive_highlights: SHOP same-store cash NOI grew 16% (17% U.S.), the 17th consecutive quarter of double-digit growth, with U.S. occupancy outperforming NIC by 130 bps sequentially.
Full-year normalized FFO guidance raised to $3.87–$3.90 (midpoint +$0.01), citing $0.02 from 2026 senior housing investments, while same-store NOI guidance was reaffirmed.
Net debt/EBITDA improved to 4.4x, nearly a full turn better YoY, with $4.5 billion of liquidity and $5.2 billion of YTD senior housing investments at a 6.6% year-one yield.
summary: Ventas reported Q3 FY2026 normalized FFO of $0.99/share (up 10% YoY), total company same-store cash NOI growth of 11% (a record), and SHOP same-store cash NOI growth of 16% (17% in the U.S.), with SHOP same-store margin up 190 bps to 30.7%. Management raised full-year normalized FFO guidance to $3.87–$3.90 (midpoint $0.01 higher, +9–10% YoY), driven by $0.02 from 2026 senior housing investments offset by $0.01 from higher rates/FX, while reaffirming segment and total same-store NOI guidance. Year-to-date investments closed reached $5.2 billion versus $4.5 billion previously contemplated, funded with $4.7 billion of equity, and net debt/EBITDA improved to 4.4x. The key change was a modest sequential deceleration in SHOP NOI growth (18% to 16–17%) and margin expansion (210 to 190 bps), which management attributed to an extra day and higher utility costs.

negative_highlights: Full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance cut to $16-$20 million from the prior $25-$35 million range on fuel and freight inflation
Greater China constant-currency revenue fell 19.3% and segment adjusted EBITDA softened $3.5 million year-on-year to negative $1.9 million
Q3 free cash flow outflow widened to $18.4 million from $5.4 million, and management reiterated free cash flow will not be positive for full-year 2026
positive_highlights: Gross margin expanded 436 bps to 34.1%, with 450 bps from fixed cost absorption and supply chain efficiencies
Europe & International constant-currency revenue grew 20.4% with volume up nearly 18%, and segment adjusted EBITDA margin rose ~370 bps to 31.4%
North America market share gap narrowed to nearly two points from nearly eight points in summer 2025, with distribution points at a record high and volume growth of 8%
summary: Q3 constant-currency revenue grew 8.9% (Europe & International +20.4%, North America +2.9%, Greater China -19.3%), gross margin expanded 436 bps to 34.1%, and adjusted EBITDA was $9.4 million versus a prior-year $3.1 million. Full-year constant-currency revenue guidance was maintained at 8%-10%, but adjusted EBITDA guidance was cut to $16-$20 million from the prior $25-$35 million range, with $7 million at the midpoint attributed entirely to North America fuel and freight inflation, notably a ~70% rise in U.S. diesel since February. Free cash flow was a $18.4 million outflow versus $5.4 million last year, described as largely timing of CapEx, a more than $11 million inventory build, and payables phasing. Management repeatedly declined to quantify the North America price increase effective Q1 2027 or the Europe pricing under review, framing it as surgical and innovation-led.

negative_highlights: U.S. new vehicle same-store sales declined 4.6% and U.S. used same-store sales fell 10%
Adjusted SG&A as a percent of gross increased sequentially to 67.7% even with prior cost actions
Pro forma rent-adjusted leverage rises to ~4x from 3.3x, with share repurchases paused until a return to ~3x by mid-to-late 2027
positive_highlights: U.S. after-sales set an all-time record in customer pay revenue and RO count, with same-store RO count up over 4% and customer pay revenue up 3.2%
Hennessy acquisition adds 10 dealerships and ~$1.7 billion annualized revenue at ~7% EBITDA margin, ~75% luxury mix, and over 10% more U.S. service bays
U.K. same-store new vehicle sales up 8%, used GPU up 14% local currency, and aftersales revenue/gross profit up 7%/4% local currency
summary: GPI reported Q3 2026 revenue of $5.4 billion, gross profit of $855 million, adjusted net income of $112 million and adjusted diluted EPS of $9.36 from continuing operations. U.S. new vehicle sales fell 4.6% same-store and U.S. used same-store sales dropped 10%, partly offset by record customer pay revenue with RO count up over 4% and customer pay revenue up 3.2%. Adjusted SG&A as a percent of gross rose to 67.7% and U.S. same-store customer pay gross profit growth decelerated, with management flagging no pricing room and an expected ~12-month wait for after-sales recovery. The Hennessy acquisition closed in early Q4 adding ~$1.7 billion revenue at ~7% EBITDA margin, with $1.1-1.2 billion of dispositions targeted by mid-2027; leverage rose to ~4x pro forma from 3.3x with buybacks paused until a return to ~3x.

negative_highlights: Q4 organic revenue growth guided to 5–7%, decelerating from 11% in Q3, as take rate is pressured by Depop mix and the U.K. managed-shipping gross-to-net transition
Total take rate declined 20 bps year over year and Q4 operating margin guided to 25.7–26.2% with operating income growth slowing to 6–10%
Core active buyers excluding Depop and Tise grew just over 1%, with international soft, and management announced a ~9% workforce reduction
positive_highlights: Revenue up 13% FXN to $3.21 billion with non-GAAP EPS up nearly 12% to $1.51, both above the high end of guidance ranges
Focus category GMV grew 24%, outpacing the rest of the marketplace by 19 points, with aggregate focus/C2C/Recommerce up ~20% and now 72% of total GMV ex-Depop
Depop outperformed with U.S. GMV, MAUs and sold items more than doubling year-over-year pro forma; combined eBay+Depop U.S. fashion GMV ~$9 billion growing mid-20%
summary: eBay reported Q3 FY2026 GMV of $23.2 billion (up ~16% FXN total, 13% organic), revenue of $3.21 billion (up 13% FXN, 11% organic), non-GAAP operating income of $843 million (up 11%) and non-GAAP EPS of $1.51 (up ~12%), all above consensus and the high end of guidance ranges. Q4 guidance calls for GMV of $23.7–24.1 billion (12–14% FXN, 8–10% organic) and revenue of $3.19–3.24 billion (7–9% FXN, 5–7% organic), with EPS of $1.48–1.53 (5–9% growth) — a decelerating revenue trajectory versus Q3. Management also disclosed a ~9% workforce reduction to fund growth investments, and 2027 planning assumes trading card growth moderates off a strong 2026. Focus categories grew 24% and C2C/Recommerce each grew over 20%.

negative_highlights: Las Vegas segment adjusted EBITDA declined on lower room revenues, with ADR down high-single digits in September versus flat occupancy
MGM China reported EBITDA fell $20 million and margin eased to 26.9% from the prior quarter
Regional same-store adjusted EBITDA fell 3%, with a hold impact at two properties and prior-year $9 million business interruption proceeds
positive_highlights: Las Vegas casino revenues grew 8% on record third-quarter slot win
MGM China posted record quarterly revenue with record 3Q market share of 17.1% and Golden Week visitation up 10%
MGM Digital narrowed its EBITDA loss to $4 million, a $19 million year-over-year improvement on 6% revenue growth
summary: Las Vegas segment adjusted EBITDA declined year-over-year on lower room revenues, with ADR down mid-single digits in August and high-single digits in September against flat occupancy; consolidated revenue was described as steady with Las Vegas casino revenue up 8% on record 3Q slot win. Regional same-store revenue rose 1% and same-store EBITDA fell 3% (including a $9 million prior-year business interruption benefit), while MGM China revenue grew 5% with reported EBITDA down $20 million before a $22 million higher brand fee. MGM Digital narrowed its EBITDA loss to $4 million on 6% revenue growth, BetMGM reported 7% net revenue and 112% EBITDA growth and maintained prior full-year guidance. No formal consolidated guidance was given; October ADR trends improved toward July levels, but December convention rotation requires backfill and management cited fuel, airfare and macro headwinds.

negative_highlights: Commercial bookings decreased 12% (11% in constant currency), with management flagging material quarterly volatility.
Windows OEM revenue fell 27% on Windows 10 end-of-support comparison, OEM/channel inventory drawdowns, and weaker PC demand, with inventory still elevated.
Microsoft Cloud gross margin percentage declined year-over-year to 66% on mix shift to Azure, and Q2 is guided to roughly 65%.
positive_highlights: Microsoft Cloud revenue hit $63.9 billion with growth accelerating to 30% year-over-year, and Azure grew 48%, ahead of expectations.
Commercial remaining performance obligation grew 73% to $677 billion, with the portion recognized beyond 12 months up 98%.
Operating margin expanded slightly to 50% on 21% operating income growth, and cash flow from operations rose 29% to $58 billion.
summary: Microsoft reported Q1 FY2027 revenue of $92.3 billion, up 19% (21% operating income growth, 18% EPS growth to $4.89), with management stating results exceeded expectations on revenue, operating income, and EPS. Microsoft Cloud revenue reached $63.9 billion with growth accelerating to 30%, and Azure grew 48%, ahead of expectations despite third-party capacity delays. Guidance for Q2 calls for total revenue of $96-97.1 billion (18-19% growth) and Azure growth of 49-50% in constant currency, with operating margins guided down slightly year-over-year and CapEx expected over $50 billion in Q2. Watch items include commercial bookings down 12%, Windows OEM down 27% on elevated inventory and weak PC demand, and a small M365 execution miss in E3/standalone SKUs.

Honeywell Aerospace's first standalone quarter delivered $4.6B in organic sales, up 2.4% versus expectations of flat to slightly up, with adjusted EBIT of $1.2B (up 4%) and adjusted EPS of $2.21; adjusted EBIT margin of ~25% included ~$50M of IEEPA tariff refunds worth over 100 bps. Full-year organic growth guidance was maintained at 4%-5% and pro forma adjusted EBIT narrowed around the same $4.4B midpoint, but Q4 organic sales are guided modestly below the full-year range and margin steps down to mid-23s as tariff refunds lapse. EPS guidance was raised to $7.85-$8.00 on lower below-the-line costs and second-half free cash flow guidance lifted to $1.2-1.4B, alongside a newly declared $0.40 quarterly dividend. Backlog rose 12% to over $19B and book-to-bill was 1.3, but output remains gated by roughly 70 constrained mechanical suppliers, with management explicitly deferring the acceleration to 2027.

negative_highlights: Net charge-offs of $46.3 million required $40.6 million of provision, and NPAs rose 15 bps or $15 million
Fee income of $13.5 million included a $4 million impairment on a third-party fintech investment
Q4 fee income guidance of $17-18 million was characterized as lighter than prior expectations on a weak mortgage gain-on-sale environment
positive_highlights: Net interest margin held at 4.0% with deposit costs up only 1 bp to 1.96% and cost of funds at 2.03%
Loans grew 5% annualized in the quarter (8.1% YTD) with management reiterating 10% full-year 2026 loan growth
Core non-interest expense fell $1.1 million sequentially to $82.6 million excluding one-time items, with Q4 guided to $75-77 million
summary: NBHC reported an elevated-credit quarter: $46.3 million of net charge-offs (driven by two credits, one franchise and one healthcare, totaling ~$65 million of principal) required $40.6 million of provision, and non-performing assets rose 15 bps or $15 million, which management called a 'disappointing quarter.' Net interest margin was a strong 4.0% with deposit costs up only 1 bp to 1.96%, loans grew 5% annualized (8.1% YTD), and core non-interest expense fell $1.1 million sequentially to $82.6 million excluding $15.2 million of acquisition/restructuring items. Fee income of $13.5 million was hit by a $4 million fintech impairment, and Q4 fee guidance of $17-18 million was described as lighter than prior expectations due to a tough mortgage environment. Q4 core expense is guided to $75-77 million, and management reiterated a target of quarterly EPS above $1.00 in Q4 and 10% full-year 2026 loan growth.

negative_highlights: Adjusted operating margin slipped 10 bps year-over-year to 19.3%; full-year margins guided roughly flat
Digital Operations revenue declined 1.7% year-over-year
Banking, Capital Markets & Diversified Industries gross margin fell ~80 bps sequentially on hiring and AI services investment
positive_highlights: Full-year revenue guidance raised to $2.43-$2.44 billion from $2.39-$2.415 billion, a $32 million midpoint increase
Adjusted EPS guidance raised to $2.34-$2.36 from $2.25-$2.29, implying ~20%-21% growth
Data and AI-led revenue grew 36% reported / 31% organic and now represents about two-thirds of total revenue
summary: EXL reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $634 million, up 19.7% year-over-year (17% organic constant currency), and adjusted EPS of $0.62, up 28.5%. Data and AI-led revenue grew 36% reported (31% organic) to nearly two-thirds of total revenue, and all four segments grew double digits, though Digital Operations declined 1.7% by design. Management raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $2.43-$2.44 billion from $2.39-$2.415 billion and adjusted EPS to $2.34-$2.36 from $2.25-$2.29. Adjusted operating margin was 19.3%, down 10 bps year-over-year on investments, and full-year margins are guided roughly flat.

negative_highlights: Gross margin contracted five percentage points to 58% from 63% on new CAL facility overhead and amortization of acquired intangibles
Sales and marketing expense rose 44% YoY to $5.5 million, outpacing the 36% revenue growth on field-team expansion ahead of 2027 launches
First-ever ATM draw of $22 million net signals front-loaded cash needs, with operating burn of $20.1 million through Q3 2026 and additional CAL CapEx expected over the next 12 months
positive_highlights: Total revenue grew 36% YoY to $12.1 million, with neurosurgery navigation up 59% to $5.4 million and capital equipment/software up 68% to $1.7 million, the largest capital sales quarter in company history
Operating expenses of $13.4 million fell from nearly $17 million in the prior quarter, with sales and marketing down more than 15% QoQ on commercial reorganization
Gross margin headwinds notwithstanding, revenue growth of 36% outpaced opex growth of 23%, supporting the operating-leverage trajectory Danilo guided toward over the next four to six quarters
summary: ClearPoint Neuro reported Q3 2026 revenue of $12.1 million, up 36% YoY from $8.9 million, with neurosurgery navigation up 59% to $5.4 million (driven by acquired IRRAflow) and capital equipment/software up 68% to $1.7 million. Gross margin fell to 58% from 63% on CAL overhead and acquired-intangible amortization, R&D rose 16% to $4.0 million and sales/marketing rose 44% to $5.5 million, while total opex of $13.4 million was down from ~$17 million in Q2. Management referenced a ~$49 million full-year midpoint for Q4 step-up and indicated mid-teens base growth for 2027 without formal guidance until January. The company raised $22 million net via its ATM, ending with $46.2 million in cash and $20.1 million year-to-date operating burn.

negative_highlights: Gross margin contracted 100 bps to 81.4% from 82.4% on FX, product mix, and supply chain cost pressure.
Non-GAAP diluted EPS was $0.32, down from $0.33 a year ago, and net income fell 6% to $13.9 million.
Financial income declined to $4.5 million from $5.2 million on lower rates and reduced cash after buybacks, with management flagging a continued modest headwind.
positive_highlights: Revenue of $84.4 million grew 12% YoY, an acceleration and the eighth double-digit growth quarter in the last nine.
Cloud ARR rose 21% YoY to ~$107 million, now 41% of total ARR versus 37% a year earlier.
Operating cash flow swung to $15.5 million from negative $2.1 million in Q3 2025, and $13.7 million of shares were repurchased in the quarter.
summary: Radware reported record Q3 FY2026 revenue of $84.4 million, up 12% YoY, and non-GAAP diluted EPS of $0.32 versus $0.33 a year ago. Cloud ARR reached ~$107 million, up 21%, while total ARR was ~$266 million, up 11%. Gross margin slipped to 81.4% from 82.4% on FX, mix, and supply chain pressure, and non-GAAP net income fell 6% to $13.9 million, with management noting $0.32 EPS would have been $0.41 excluding a $4.6 million shekel impact. Q4 guidance was set at $88-90 million revenue and $0.34-0.35 EPS.

negative_highlights: Total deposits fell to $16.6 billion from $16.8 billion, including a $159 million reduction in brokered time deposits; deposits essentially flat year to date
Net unrealized AFS losses increased $237 million in the quarter, pressuring tangible book value and TBV per share
Management guided Q4 loan growth down to roughly 10% annualized and longer-term to high single digits from 13%, citing higher-rate demand sensitivity and expected pipeline fallout
positive_highlights: Adjusted EPS of $0.66 rose 59% YoY and adjusted pre-tax pre-provision earnings grew 49-58% YoY to $100.3 million
Loans grew $429 million, a 13% annualized rate, with a commercial pipeline of approximately $1.3 billion and NPLs down 15%
Adjusted efficiency ratio improved to 53.9% from 54.5% QoQ and 57.6% a year ago; adjusted ROTE reached 16.9%
summary: Seacoast reported Q3 FY2026 net income of $59.9 million ($0.55 per share), up 1% sequentially and 64% YoY, with adjusted EPS of $0.66 (up 9% QoQ, 59% YoY) and adjusted ROA of 1.34%. Net interest margin held at 3.83% (core up 1 bp to 3.66%), loans grew $429 million or 13% annualized, NPLs fell 15% to $73.3 million (54 bps), and adjusted efficiency improved to 53.9% from 54.5%. 2026 guidance was reiterated with management stating it expects to hit the high end of the range, while flagging ~$2.4 million of discrete Q4 expenses and a step-up to roughly 10% annualized loan growth vs. 13% this quarter. The Villages conversion completed, ending M&A charges, and management pointed to margin expansion into 2027 on back-book repricing plus a ~$300 million seasonal public-funds deposit inflow.

negative_highlights: Recovery characterized by the CFO as a supply-moderation story rather than demand recovery; demand described as 'just steady' with no significant improvement
A new Southern California state-of-emergency order pauses the LA rate normalization after only roughly half of affected customers were moved to market rates, a potential 2027 overhang
Third-party management had elevated attrition this quarter as a 59-property portfolio sale offset 78 additions, though management expects to return net positive in Q4
positive_highlights: Same-store revenue accelerated 290 bps YoY to 2.7%, with 27 of top 30 markets now showing positive growth versus 12 a year ago
Full-year core FFO guidance raised for the second time in 2026 to $8.40-$8.50, a 1.5% midpoint increase, alongside a 150 bps midpoint lift to same-store NOI guidance
Same-store expenses declined 1.8% (payroll -4.6%, marketing -6.8%, insurance -16.5%, R&M -20%), with management describing the R&M savings as a sustainable new run rate
summary: Core FFO of $2.17/share rose 4.3% YoY, ahead of internal projections, driven by same-store NOI, tenant insurance, and lower G&A. Same-store revenue grew 2.7% (fifth consecutive quarter of sequential improvement), same-store expenses fell 1.8%, and same-store NOI rose 4.6%, with occupancy at 94% (up 30 bps YoY). Management raised full-year core FFO guidance for the second time in 2026 to $8.40-$8.50 (from $8.25-$8.40, +1.5% at midpoint), lifted same-store revenue growth by 75 bps, cut expense growth by 125 bps, and raised acquisitions guidance to $400 million from $300 million. The recovery is attributed primarily to moderating new supply rather than a demand rebound, and a new Southern California emergency pricing restriction will pause rate increases there.

negative_highlights: Q4 cRPO growth guided to 18.5% cc, decelerating from 21% in Q3, with early Q3 renewals pulling roughly half the beat forward out of Q4
Only about half of the Q3 revenue beat was passed into the full-year guide, with management citing a ~25 bps Q3 and ~50 bps Q4 carve-out of deployment services into professional services
Higher on-prem/public-sector mix creates a 25 bps Q4 cRPO headwind, reinforcing that cRPO is not tracking revenue momentum
positive_highlights: Subscription revenue, cRPO and operating margin all beat the high end of guidance by 50-150 bps, with 19 deals over $5M net new ACV up 135% YoY
AI net new ACV grew 65% YoY and the AI ACV target was raised for the second time this year, from $1.5B to $1.7B+ by year end
FY free cash flow margin target raised 100 bps to 36% and full-year subscription revenue raised $15M at the midpoint
summary: Q3 subscription revenue of $3.988B grew 20.5% cc, 50 bps above the high end of guidance, with cRPO up 21% cc (100 bps beat) and non-GAAP operating margin of 32.5% (150 bps above guidance); free cash flow margin was 20%. Guidance was raised: full-year subscription revenue midpoint lifted $15M to $15.785B (21% cc growth) and FY free cash flow margin raised 100 bps to 36%, alongside a second AI ACV target raise to $1.7B+ from $1.5B. Q4 cRPO guidance of 18.5% cc embeds headwinds from early Q3 renewals that pulled deals forward, higher on-prem mix, and deployment-expertise carve-outs (~50 bps), which management framed as accounting nuance rather than demand softening. AI net new ACV grew 65% YoY and year-to-date agentic AI consumption in production is up 13x.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined 2.9% YoY and 1.9% QoQ, with direct fee revenue only up very modestly sequentially
Revenue guidance raised to the high end of the prior range is driven by higher pass-through activity rather than core direct-fee growth
Pass-throughs now approach one-third of revenue, adding volatility and skewing the bookings-to-revenue conversion picture
positive_highlights: Record net business wins of $3.15 billion, up 51% YoY, with net book-to-bill of 1.56x — a fourth consecutive quarter above 1.3x
Adjusted gross margin expanded 90 bps sequentially to 24.7% and adjusted EBITDA margin rose 70 bps to 16.6% as mix improved
$302 million of free cash flow, $400 million of shares repurchased at an average of $170, and a new $750 million buyback authorization
summary: Revenue fell 2.9% YoY to just over $2 billion (down 2.5% in constant currency and 1.9% QoQ, partly from the Symphony divestiture), but adjusted EBITDA rose 3% sequentially to $337 million with margin up 70 bps to 16.6%, and adjusted EPS rose 4% sequentially to $2.66. Commercial momentum was strong: gross wins up 27% YoY, record net wins of $3.15 billion (up 51% YoY), net book-to-bill of 1.56x, and free cash flow of $302 million. Management narrowed 2026 guidance, raising the revenue outlook to the high end of the prior range on higher pass-through activity (~low 30s as a percentage of revenue), and declined to give formal 2027 guidance while floating mid-single-digit revenue growth and higher single-digit earnings growth as a reasonable reference point.

negative_highlights: Copper production fell 1% to 232,396 tons, with Peru down 6% on lower ore grades; YTD production down 2.9%
Tía María startup pushed from Q4 2027 to H1 2028, with CapEx under review and no guidance update until January
Operating cash cost before by-product credits rose 10% to $2.46/lb on diesel, power, and labor inflation
positive_highlights: Net sales rose 39% YoY to $4.7 billion and net income jumped 63% to a record $1.8 billion
Adjusted EBITDA hit a record $3.0 billion (+54%) with margin expanding to 65% from 59%
Operating cash flow of $2.2 billion in Q3 (+43%) and $5.9 billion year-to-date (+81%)
summary: Record quarterly results: net sales of $4.7 billion (+39% YoY), adjusted EBITDA of $3.0 billion (+54%) at a 65% margin (vs 59%), and record net income of $1.8 billion (+63%) at a 38% margin. Cash costs net of by-product credits fell 77% to $0.09/lb on a 31% rise in by-product credits, while costs before credits rose 10% ($2.46/lb). Copper production fell 1% to 232,396 tons on lower Peruvian ore grades; 2026 copper guidance is 918,000 tons (+0.7% vs initial plan) and moly 29,000 tons (+12%), but detailed 2027 guidance was deferred to the January call. Tía María slipped from Q4 2027 to H1 2028 and CapEx reviews are pending, while the board declared a $1.30 cash dividend plus a 0.0126 stock dividend.

negative_highlights: Adjusted free cash flow fell to $66 million from $101 million, hit by a $20 million working capital use and $11 million higher capex
Full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance held at ~$825 million due to cost inflation and delayed customer recoveries, with general inflation described as a nine-digit number
GAAP loss from continuing operations of $10 million, including a $29 million foreign income tax audit settlement and $24 million loss on euro note redemption
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA rose $56 million to $218 million with margin expanding 220 bps to 10.7%
Adjusted diluted EPS of $0.41 versus a $0.04 loss in the prior year period
FY2026 sales guidance midpoint raised $50 million to ~$7.8 billion on stronger commercial vehicle demand and commodity recoveries
summary: Dana reported Q3 FY2026 sales of $2.038 billion, up $121 million YoY, and adjusted EBITDA of $218 million at a 10.7% margin, up 220 bps from 10.7% prior year. Adjusted diluted EPS was $0.41 versus a $0.04 loss last year, though GAAP continuing-operations loss was $10 million on a $64 million tax charge including a $29 million foreign audit settlement. Full-year guidance raised sales midpoint by $50 million to ~$7.8 billion while maintaining adjusted EBITDA at ~$825 million (10.6% margin), EPS at ~$2.00, and adjusted free cash flow at ~$325 million, citing cost inflation and recovery timing uncertainty. The Eaton Mobility split-off remains on track for ~Q1 2027 close with $250 million synergy target and leverage of 1.6x.

negative_highlights: Bank segment NIM declined QoQ as full-quarter effect of higher-cost ESP deposits pressured funding costs
Capital Markets fixed-income brokerage revenues fell on municipal securities marks amid rising rates and volatility
FY2027 non-compensation expense guidance of ~$2.5 billion implies about 8% growth, with acquisitions adding ~100 bps
positive_highlights: Record quarterly net revenues of $4.27 billion, up 15% YoY and 9% QoQ, with record adjusted EPS of $3.59
Adjusted pre-tax margin of 21.3% exceeded the approximately 20% guidance
Domestic PCG net new assets rose 88% to a record over $98 billion, 6.4% of beginning-of-year assets
summary: Raymond James reported record quarterly net revenues of $4.27 billion, up 15% year-over-year and 9% sequentially, with record diluted EPS of $3.40 (adjusted $3.59) and record pre-tax income of $862 million, up 18% YoY. Adjusted pre-tax margin of 21.3% came in above the roughly 20% guidance, and PCG client assets hit a record $1.87 trillion with FY net new assets up 88% to over $98 billion. Guidance was constructive but mixed: Q1 FY2027 asset management fees seen up ~1% and combined NII plus RJBDP fees up ~1%, while FY2027 non-comp expenses are guided to ~$2.5 billion (about 8% higher). Buybacks were curtailed to $50 million in the quarter during evaluation of an M&A opportunity that now appears unlikely to progress, with management planning to resume at roughly $400 million per quarter.

negative_highlights: Product gross margins fell a couple of points on higher manufacturing and production costs, prompting Q4 price increases
GAAP opex rose to $18.5 million from $8.8 million, including $6 million in litigation costs and a regulatory provision tied to a BIS export-control fine
Cash declined $2 million to $43 million sequentially despite $0.9 million of operating cash flow
positive_highlights: Record revenue of $20.6 million, up 47% YoY and above the top of guidance
Product revenue up 34% YoY and 11% QoQ; non-product revenue rose to $3.7 million from $1.4 million on the $40 million prime contractor subcontract
Q4 revenue guided to $21.5-$22.5 million (above Q3) with non-GAAP EPS of $0.13-$0.18
summary: Everspin reported record Q3 revenue of $20.6 million, up 47% year-over-year and slightly above the $19.5-$20.5 million guidance range, with MRAM product revenue of $16.9 million up 34% YoY and 11% sequentially. Non-GAAP EPS came in at $0.12, within the $0.10-$0.15 guide and up from $0.06 a year ago. Q4 revenue is guided to $21.5-$22.5 million with non-GAAP EPS of $0.13-$0.18. GAAP gross margin was roughly flat at 51.4% as higher non-product mix offset product margin pressure from manufacturing costs, and GAAP opex jumped to $18.5 million on $6 million of litigation costs plus a BIS export-control provision.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA margin of 15.1% faced mix and inflation pressure; VWR adjusted operating margin fell to 9.7% year-over-year on mix, inflation, and growth investments
BMP Q4 guidance is flat to slightly positive, reflecting ~400 bps of discrete comparison headwinds and a tougher Process Chemicals comparison
Pricing of ~1%-2% in 2026 trails inflation, leaving a cost-price lag management is still working to close
positive_highlights: Organic revenue growth turned positive at 5.2%, with VWR accelerating to 5.8% and BMP returning to growth at 3.6% organic
Full-year 2026 guidance raised on organic revenue (to 0.75%-1.25%), adjusted EPS (to $0.81-$0.83), and free cash flow (to $525-$550M)
Adjusted net leverage reduced to 3.1x from 3.3x last quarter, with net debt cut by $173M and a below-3x target by year-end
summary: Avantor reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $1.698B, up 5.2% organically and 4.6% reported, ahead of expectations, with adjusted EBITDA of $257M (15.1% margin) and adjusted EPS of $0.22. VWR grew 5.8% organically and BMP returned to growth at 3.6% organic despite a ~150 bps serum ordering headwind. Management raised 2026 organic revenue growth guidance to 0.75%-1.25%, adjusted EPS to $0.81-$0.83, and free cash flow to $525-$550M, while leaving adjusted EBITDA margin guidance unchanged. Adjusted net leverage fell to 3.1x from 3.3x, with a target below 3x by year-end.

negative_highlights: Sales were reduced by $87 million of IEEPA tariff refunds, with an additional $50 million expected in Q1
Management sees no relief from inflation in resins, metals, and freight costs entering FY27
Global vehicle production is expected to be down slightly in FY27, with North America still described as challenged
positive_highlights: Q4 sales of $5.3 billion came in ahead of guidance, up 13% organically, with both segments delivering double-digit growth
Orders of $6.1 billion grew 29% year-over-year with book-to-bill of 1.14, and backlog reached a record ~$8 billion, up ~30%
Q1 FY27 guidance calls for 15% organic sales growth to $5.35 billion and EPS of ~$3.30, up 21%, with full-year organic growth expected near 12%
summary: TE delivered Q4 FY26 sales of $5.3 billion, up 13% organically and ahead of guidance, with adjusted EPS of $3.14 (up 21%) and adjusted operating margin of 22.1% (up 100 bps), though sales were reduced by $87 million of IEEPA tariff refunds. Orders grew 29% to $6.1 billion with book-to-bill of 1.14, and the company guided Q1 FY27 sales to $5.35 billion (up 15% organic) and EPS to ~$3.30 (up 21%), while expecting full-year FY27 organic growth similar to the 12% delivered in FY26 and DDN revenue to grow over $1 billion. Record full-year sales of nearly $20 billion (+15% reported, +12% organic) and EPS of $11.52 (+24%) were accompanied by record backlog, but management flagged continued input-cost inflation on resins, metals, and freight with no relief expected.

negative_highlights: Roto-Rooter adjusted EBITDA fell 2.5% and margin contracted 213 bps to 20.6% on paid-lead mix shift ($4.3 million higher marketing) and $1.4 million higher fuel costs
Free internet leads declined 11.8% and paid leads rose to ~60% of total from 56%, a structural cost headwind management expects to persist in Q4
Recently reacquired California franchise territories earn sub-10% EBITDA margins, and management said these acquisitions will mute Roto-Rooter margins in the near term (12-18 months to full model)
positive_highlights: VITAS adjusted EBITDA excluding Medicare Cap rose 31.4% to $92.5 million, with margin at 20.2%
VITAS admissions up 7.2% to 18,995 and average daily census up 9.4% to 24,428; non-hospital Florida admissions rose 11.1%
Full-year 2026 adjusted EPS now expected at or slightly above the high end of prior guidance; Q3 beat guidance by about $0.30
summary: Chemed reported Q3 FY2026 total revenue growth of 10.6% and adjusted diluted EPS growth of 28.1% year over year. VITAS revenue rose 12.2% to $457.4 million on 9.4% days-of-care growth, with adjusted EBITDA ex-Medicare Cap up 31.4% to $92.5 million (20.2% margin), while Roto-Rooter revenue grew 7.5% (same-store +5.5%) but adjusted EBITDA fell 2.5% and margin contracted 213 bps to 20.6% on marketing and fuel costs. Management guided full-year 2026 adjusted EPS to at or slightly above the high end of the prior range, weighted toward VITAS. The key shift versus prior periods is a two-sided mix: VITAS outperformance offset by Roto-Rooter margin pressure and margin-dilutive franchise reacquisitions ($62.5 million California, $96 million year to date).

negative_highlights: Core adjusted operating ratio worsened 120 bps YoY to 61.9% as fuel expense rose 56% on a 53% average price increase
Coal revenue fell 1% on an 11% volume decline from mine production challenges
Personal injury frequency rose to 1.12, 20% higher than last year and below internal standard
positive_highlights: Core adjusted diluted EPS rose 16% YoY to $1.28 on 6% volume growth
Intermodal revenue up 21% with domestic up 7% and international up 11%; SMX volumes up 30% sequentially
Adjusted free cash flow up 59% to CAD 2.4 billion year-to-date with over CAD 4 billion returned via buybacks and dividends
summary: CPKC reported Q3 FY2026 revenues of CAD 4.2 billion with 6% volume growth, a core adjusted operating ratio of 61.9% (up 120 bps YoY), and core adjusted diluted EPS of $1.28, up 16% YoY. Freight revenue rose 15% and cents per RTM increased 9% on disciplined pricing, with record Q3 intermodal and grain volumes. Management reiterated full-year mid-single-digit volume growth guidance, guided Q4 operating ratio to sub-60, and disclosed a new five-year Elk Valley Resources coal contract reclaiming roughly half of interchanged traffic. Fuel was a 190 bps OR headwind from a 53% average price increase, partially offset by $21 million of fuel efficiency savings.

negative_highlights: Provision expense of $14.2M was the highest provisioning quarter management says it has had, including $7.7M of specific reserves on three credits
Non-performing loans increased, concentrated in three credits (a $16M C&I credit newly into non-accrual, a $5M Pittsburgh mixed-use credit, and an $11M mixed-use multifamily loan)
Fee income was flat sequentially and loan growth of 2.6% remains below the mid-single-digit target; management said higher rates would dampen CRE demand
positive_highlights: NIM expanded 10 bps to 4.11%, with guidance to ~4.20% in Q4 and mid-4.20% in 2027 assuming no rate changes
Net interest income increased $3.9M sequentially, an annualized rate of ~13.7%
Loan payoffs slowed for the first time in five quarters, producing 2.6% annualized loan growth; core ROACE rose to 15.90%, up 24 bps
summary: Core EPS was $0.45, with the quarter including $4.7M of one-time energy tax credits offset by $14.2M of provision expense, of which $7.7M was specific reserves on three previously identified credits. NIM expanded 10 bps to 4.11% and net interest income rose $3.9M (13.7% annualized), with management guiding NIM to ~4.20% in Q4 and mid-4.20% in 2027; fee income ($24-25M) and expense ($74-76M) guidance were unchanged. Non-performing loans increased but management characterized it as concentrated rather than broad-based deterioration. The $75M buyback was fully executed with a new $25M authorization announced.

negative_highlights: Operating expenses of $22.5 million remain far above revenue and include $1.2 million of non-recurring finance costs; adjusted EBITDA loss was $11.1 million
Full-year 2026 guidance of $10 million-$15 million implies Q4 revenue of $5.2 million-$10.2 million, heavily dependent on shipment timing rather than demand
Management flagged supply chain as the main risk, citing circuit board, FPGA and memory cost pressure from data center demand and tariffs
positive_highlights: Revenue of $2.4 million in Q3 matched the entire first half of 2026 and was up from $0.2 million in Q3 2025; year-to-date revenue of $4.8 million is nearly 5x the prior-year $1 million
Gross margin reached 50% in the quarter and 46% year-to-date versus -126% in the first nine months of 2025, aided by Luminar-acquired inventory and the Orlando facility
Cash used in operations fell to $13.6 million from $16.5 million a year ago, and 2027 operating cash burn is targeted at ~$40 million, roughly one-third below current levels
summary: Q3 2026 revenue was $2.4 million versus $0.2 million a year ago and equal to the $2.4 million booked in the entire first half of 2026, with gross margin at 50% versus negative $0.7 million gross profit last year. Full-year 2026 revenue guidance of $10 million-$15 million was reaffirmed, supported by about $10 million of purchase orders awaiting shipment, and management guided 2027 revenue to roughly double 2026 with operating cash burn falling to about $40 million from a targeted ~$60 million in 2026. A workforce reduction of about 28% and Q3 opex of $22.5 million mark the first cost actions; GAAP net loss was $12.2 million or $0.45 per share versus $14.2 million or $0.72 per share a year earlier, and the quarter included a $6.3 million German R&D grant.

negative_highlights: Higher bond yields led to pricing adjustments and elongation of decision timelines in select on-market Capital Markets transactions, with pipeline conversion pace slightly moderated
U.S. multifamily most affected by higher rates, and management declined to give granular 2027 guidance citing an uneven macro backdrop
Property Management growth continued to be offset by strategic contract exits in Asia Pacific, with headwinds expected to persist through 2027
positive_highlights: Revenue up 12% with advisory growth accelerating to 22% and adjusted EPS up 52%
Full-year 2026 adjusted EPS target raised to $25.20-$26.30, implying 37% growth at the midpoint
$500 million accelerated share repurchase announced, with $552 million year-to-date buybacks reducing share count over 3%
summary: JLL reported a record third quarter with revenue up 12% in local currency, advisory growth accelerating to 22%, adjusted EBITDA up 33% with margin expansion, and adjusted EPS up 52%. Leasing Advisory revenue rose 27% and Capital Markets investment sales rose 33%, both well above market growth rates. Management raised full-year 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $25.20-$26.30 (37% growth at the midpoint) and lifted the Leasing Advisory full-year revenue target to high teens from mid-to-high teens, while maintaining mid-teens Capital Markets and mid-to-high single-digit REMS targets. The quarter included $142 million of buybacks, a year-to-date total of $552 million, and an imminent $500 million accelerated share repurchase, alongside caution on higher bond yields affecting Capital Markets deal timelines and U.S. multifamily pricing.

negative_highlights: Full-year 2026 deliveries and revenue guidance was lowered, with Q4 incentives guided 200-250 bps above Q3's ~1,300 bps, and management said September weakness continued into October

Adjusted homebuilding gross margin fell 70 bps sequentially to 19.3% (GAAP 15%), driven by higher incentives and $19.6 million of inventory impairments in Bay Area, Houston and Florida South communities
Deliveries fell 2% YoY and orders slowed after a ~75 bp mortgage-rate increase, with starts cut 12% sequentially as buyers moved to the sidelines
positive_highlights: Ending community count rose 7% YoY and 4% sequentially to a record 343 communities, with year-end guidance of 360-370 including 29 from HistoryMaker
Direct construction costs fell 2% sequentially and finished lot costs fell 3%, with cycle times averaging 118 calendar days
Cancellation rate held low at 14.6%, and the company repurchased 1.1 million shares for $71 million YTD at an average 31% discount to record book value of $90.61 per share
summary: Century Communities reported Q3 FY2026 home sales revenue of $842 million with 2,442 deliveries (down 2% YoY and 3% sequentially) and net income of $13 million, or $0.44 per diluted share ($1.01 adjusted). Adjusted homebuilding gross margin of 19.3% fell 70 bps sequentially on higher incentives, and GAAP margin was 15% after $19.6 million in inventory impairments across six underperforming communities. Management lowered full-year 2026 guidance to 9,350-9,650 deliveries and $3.3-3.4 billion in home sales revenue, and guided Q4 incentives 200-250 bps above Q3 levels. Net orders were 2,284 with September and October softening after a ~75 bp rise in mortgage rates, partly offset by a record 343 community count and the October HistoryMaker acquisition adding 29 communities.
